questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
options: ① Crops are very fond of unplowed farmland conditions.
② Monoculture is in need of flawless farm soil conditions.
③ Since 1969, global fertilizer use has tripled and irrigation capacity has exactly doubled.
④ Improved farmland is also a desirable environment for favorable plants such as weeds.
⑤ Agricultural soil conditions for monoculture cannot be met through irrigation and fertilizer supply.
questions.explanation: 지문 첫 문장에서 농지의 토양은 단일 재배(monoculture) 성장을 위한 완벽한 환경이 되도록 강요받는다고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 ② '단일 재배는 결점 없는 농지 토양 조건을 필요로 한다'는 내용이 일치합니다. ③번의 경우 관개 용량은 '거의 두 배(almost doubled)'이지 '정확히 두 배(exactly doubled)'가 아니며, ④번에서 잡초는 'favorable plants(유익한 식물)'이 아니라 'undesirables(원치 않는 것들)'로 묘사되었습니다.
options_translation: ① 농작물은 갈지 않은 농지 조건을 매우 좋아한다.
② 단일 재배는 결점 없는 농지 토양 조건을 필요로 한다.
③ 1969년 이후, 전 세계 비료 사용량은 3배가 되었고 관개 용량은 정확히 2배가 되었다.
④ 개선된 농지는 잡초와 같은 유익한 식물에게도 바람직한 환경이다.
⑤ 단일 재배를 위한 농업 토양 조건은 관개와 비료 공급을 통해 충족될 수 없다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you don't have to ___________ behavior change any longer. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 핵심은 행동이 정체성의 반영이라는 것입니다. 정체성과 행동이 일치하면, 애써 행동 변화를 '추구(seek)'하거나 노력할 필요가 없이 자연스럽게 정체성에 맞는 행동을 하게 된다는 맥락이므로 'seek'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 예방하다
② 관찰하다
③ 거절하다
④ 추구하다
⑤ 악화시키다

questions.question: 12. 다음 글을 <보기>와 같이 요약하조가 할 때 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.
questions.summary_sentence: Interruptions not only (A)___________ professionals but also affect ordinary people by (B)___________ their work efficiency and making them feel stressed.
questions.explanation: 글은 방해가 전문가들에게 위험한 결과를 초래할 수 있고(imperil/jeopardize), 일반인들에게는 생산성을 떨어뜨린다(lowering/reducing)는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A)에는 '위태롭게 하다'는 의미의 imperil이 적절하며, (B)에는 효율성을 '낮춘다'는 의미의 lowering이 흐름상 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 위태롭게 하다 - 낮추는 것
② 위태롭게 하다 - 평가하는 것
③ 보존하다 - 줄이는 것
④ 위태롭게 하다 - 격려하는 것
⑤ 위태롭게 하다 - 향상시키는 것

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① The brain's physical structure determines its capabilities.
② The brain's physical structure affects its ability to concentrate.
③ The focus of attention and drill changes the structure of the brain.
④ Brain mental abilities are not the same in all members of a species.
⑤ Highly developed physical abilities are not innate, but acquired through cortex and hippocampus.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장 'The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.'이 핵심입니다. 즉, 우리가 어디에 주의를 기울이고 무엇을 연습하느냐에 따라 뇌의 물리적 구조가 변한다는 내용이 요지입니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌의 물리적 구조가 능력을 결정한다.
② 뇌의 물리적 구조가 집중 능력에 영향을 미친다.
③ 주의 집중과 반복 훈련이 뇌의 구조를 변화시킨다.
④ 뇌의 정신적 능력은 한 종의 모든 구성원에게서 동일하지 않다.
⑤ 고도로 발달된 신체 능력은 선천적인 것이 아니라 피질과 해마를 통해 습득된다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they ⓐ<u>were</u>. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and ⓑ<u>predict</u> where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more ⓒ<u>decisive</u> than any before it. And this mental advantage ⓓ<u>was applied</u>, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to ⓔ<u>its</u> offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.explanation: ⓐ의 were는 앞의 일반동사 evolve를 대신하는 대동사 자리이므로 did로 고쳐야 적절합니다. the way they did(그것들이 진화했던 방식)으로 해석됩니다. ⓑ는 imagine과 병렬 구조인 원형부정사이며, ⓒ는 weapon을 수식하는 형용사, ⓓ는 정신적 이점이 적용되는 수동 관계이므로 과거완료 수동태, ⓔ는 The tribe를 지칭하는 소유격 대명사입니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 "Brainwriting"에 관한 글을 읽고 추론할 수 있는 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ① It is more stressful for team members.
② It increases the need for team meetings.
③ It is a faster process than brainstorming.
④ It forbids team members from generating more creative ideas.
⑤ It sees to it that all ideas are brought to the table and considered.
questions.explanation: 지문의 후반부에서 "This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation."라고 언급하고 있으므로, ⑤번 '모든 아이디어가 제안되고 고려되도록 보장한다'는 내용이 가장 적절한 추론입니다.
options_translation: ① 팀원들에게 더 스트레스를 준다.
② 팀 회의의 필요성을 증가시킨다.
③ 브레인스토밍보다 더 빠른 과정이다.
④ 팀원들이 더 창의적인 아이디어를 내는 것을 금지한다.
⑤ 모든 아이디어가 논의의 장에 오르고 고려되도록 보장한다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place _______________________________________. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
options: ① had to lengthen the birth intervals
② could not have successive children
③ could have more possessions to carry
④ did not have a long time between births
⑤ were still aware of the need for movement
questions.explanation: 수렵 채집인들은 이동을 위해 출산 간격을 넓게 유지해야 했으나, 정착 생활을 하는 농경 사회는 아이를 이동시킬 필요가 없어 출산 사이의 간격이 길지 않았고, 이로 인해 더 많은 아이를 가질 수 있게 되었다는 흐름이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 출산 간격을 늘려야 했다
② 연달아 자녀를 가질 수 없었다
③ 운반할 더 많은 소지품을 가질 수 있었다
④ 출산 사이의 시간이 길지 않았다
⑤ 여전히 이동의 필요성을 인식하고 있었다

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① All creatures can move to satisfy their climatic requirements.
② Every creature can survive and reproduce in any kind of climate.
③ Some plants have difficulty adapting to endless climate changes.
④ It is going hard for some species to settle down where they are born.
⑤ The speed at which some plants move to another climate has increased.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 모든 생먰체가 기혔 요구 사항(온도 등)을 충접시키기 위해 기혔 변화에 따라 이동한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 움직이준 않는 갃처럼 보이는 나무나 따개무도 일생의 어느 단계에서는 분산할 수 있음을 설명하며, 과거의 화석 기록을 통해 이러한 이동을 입증합단다. 따라서 '모든 생먰체는 기혔 요구 사항을 충접시키기 위해 이동할 수 있다'는 1번이 주제로 가장 적절합단다.
options_translation: 모든 생먰체는 기혔 요구 사항을 충접시키기 위해 이동할 수 있다.
모든 생먰체는 어떤 종류의 기혔에서도 생존하고 번식할 수 있다.
어떤 식물들은 끝없는 기혔 변화에 적응하는 데 어려움을 겢다.
일부 종에게 태어난 곳에 정착하는 갳이 어려워지고 있다.
일부 식물이 다른 기혔로 이동하는 셍도가 빨라쥌다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. In other words, if you feel bad about something at the moment, it may be the result of your conscious mind tricking you into believing all kinds of negative thoughts. They are not yet a part of your memories, which are the real. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when _____________________________________________.
options: ① you deny your emotions constantly
② you do not try to reflect on yourself
③ they are experienced time and time again
④ they are stored deeply in the conscious mind
⑤ the subconscious mind records your reactions
questions.explanation: 지문은 의식적인 마음이 감정에 휘둘려 부정적인 생각을 만들어내지만, 이것이 잠재의식적인 마음(기억의 영역)으로 넘어가 기록될 때 비로소 실제적인 공포나 반응이 된다는 맥락을 설명하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장은 공포가 실제가 되는 시점을 묻고 있으므로 잠재의식이 반응을 기록할 때가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 감정을 끊임없이 부정할 때
② 당신이 스스로를 반성하려고 노력하지 않을 때
③ 그것들이 반복해서 경험될 때
④ 그것들이 의식적인 마음 속에 깊이 저장될 때
⑤ 잠재의식이 당신의 반응을 기록할 때

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. (A) They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. (B) As examples, baseball has T ball. (C) Likewise, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. (D) In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. (E) The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.insertion_sentence: Accordingly, that common sense has prevailed, and different sports have made adaptations for children.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그에 따라 상식이 널리 퍼졌고, 다양한 스포츠가 아이들을 위한 적응(수정)을 해왔다'는 내용입니다. (A)까지는 아이들이 성인 규격의 스포츠 환경에서 겪는 어려움을 설명하고 있으며, (B)부터는 구체적인 스포츠 종목(야구의 T볼 등)의 사례가 나옵니다. 따라서 문제 제기와 사례 사이인 (B)에 위치하여 논리적 연결을 만들어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 27. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other.*litter: (한 배에서 태어난) 새끼들
ordered_passages: (A) In other words, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session, despite their common innate characteristics. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment.
(B) For example, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion.

(C) With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.

(D) For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, the purpose for which the animals experience healing affects their reaction.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 동물들의 개별성에 대해 언급하고 있습니다. (A)는 'In other words(다시 말해서)'를 통해 주어진 문장의 내용을 치유 세션에서의 반응 차이로 구체화하고 환경 요인을 도입합니다. (D)는 'For instance(예를 들어)'를 통해 환경 요인의 구체적 사례(보호소 고양이 vs 가정집 고양이)를 제시하고, 추가로 치유 목적(purpose)에 따른 반응 차이를 언급합니다. (B)는 'For example(예를 들어)'를 통해 (D)에서 언급한 치유 목적의 구체적 사례(신체적 질병 vs 정서적 혼란)를 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 개별적 차이를 고려하여 각 치유 처치를 조정해야 한다는 결론을 내립니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.summary_sentence: Experts in a field often struggle to teach newcomers, as they (A)___________ the time needed to acquire new skills or knowledge. This phenomenon, known as the 'curse of knowledge', highlights the need for them to be (B)___________ to how their students process learning.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 전문가들은 초보자가 기술을 습득하는 데 걸리는 시간이나 난이도를 '과소평가(underestimate/miscalculate)'하는 경향이 있으며, 이를 '지식의 저주'라고 부릅니다. 따라서 전문가들은 학생들이 어떻게 학습하는지에 대해 더 '세심함(sensitive)'을 가질 필요가 있다는 결론이 도출됩니다. (A)에는 잘못 계산하거나 과소평가한다는 의미의 miscalculate가 적절하며, (B)에는 학생들의 입장을 고려해야 한다는 의미에서 sensitive가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 과대평가하다 / 무감각한
② 과대평가하다 / 끈기 있는
③ 과소평가하다 / 임의적인
④ 과소평가하다 / 무감각한
⑤ 잘못 계산하다 / 세심한

questions.question: 29. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining ⓐ<u>what</u> is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, ⓑ<u>points</u> out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. (A) Because, people expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. (B) Not knowing the norms of another community ⓒ<u>is</u> the central problem of crosscultural communication. (C) To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage. (D) For example, in another society with a culture contrasting to that of Anglo, you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused ⓓ<u>is</u> considerable. (E) In such a case it would sound ⓔ<u>ridiculous</u> (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
questions.insertion_sentence: But if people don't say Thank you in these cases, it is marked.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장 '하지만 사람들이 이러한 경우에 감사하다고 말하지 않는다면, 그것은 두드러진다'는 앞서 언급된 '감사 인사를 하는 사회적 규범'이 지켜지지 않았을 때의 사회적 반응을 도입하는 문장입니다. (A) 뒤에 이어지는 '사람들은 당신이 그것을 말할 것이라고 기대한다'와 '그렇게 하지 않는 것은 비판받을 만한 일이 된다'는 내용이 주어진 문장의 'marked(두드러지는, 눈에 띄는)'에 대한 부연 설명이 되므로 (A) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 30. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining ⓐ<u>what</u> is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, ⓑ<u>points</u> out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. (A) Because, people expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. (B) Not knowing the norms of another community ⓒ<u>is</u> the central problem of crosscultural communication. (C) To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage. (D) For example, in another society with a culture contrasting to that of Anglo, you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused ⓓ<u>is</u> considerable. (E) In such a case it would sound ⓔ<u>ridiculous</u> (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 help는 준사역동사로 목적격 보어로 동사원형이나 to부정사를 취합니다. 여기서는 help의 목적격 보어로 'open a door', 'point out', 'give you directions'가 병렬 구조로 연결되어야 하므로 'points'는 원형인 'point'가 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 33. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Long ago, when the world was young, an old Native American spiritual leader Odawa had a dream on a high mountain. In ⓐ<u>his</u> dream, Iktomi, the great spirit and searcher of wisdom, appeared to him in the form of a spider. Iktomi spoke to him in a holy language. Iktomi told Odawa about the cycles of life. He said, "We all begin our lives as babies, move on to childhood, and then to adulthood. Finally, we come to old age, where we must be taken care of as babies again." Iktomi also told ⓑ<u>him</u> that there are good and bad forces in each stage of life. "If we listen to the good forces, they will guide us in the right direction. But if we listen to the bad forces, they will lead us the wrong way and may harm us," Iktomi said.When Iktomi finished speaking, ⓒ<u>he</u> spun a web and gave it to Odawa. He said to Odawa, "The web is a perfect circle with a hole in the center. Use the web to help ⓓ<u>your</u> people reach their goals. Make good use of their ideas, dreams, and visions. If you believe in the great spirit, the web will catch your good ideas and the bad ones will go through the hole." Right after Odawa woke up, ⓔ<u>he</u> went back to his village.Odawa shared Iktomi's lesson with his people. Today, many Native Americans have dream catchers hanging above their beds. Dream catchers are believed to filter out bad dreams. The good dreams are captured in the web of life and carried with the people. The bad dreams pass through the hole in the web and are no longer a part of their lives.
options: ② How to Manage the Cycles of Life
③ Why Native Americans Appreciate Spiders
④ The Myth About the Origin of Dream Catchers
⑤ Follow Positive Forces Leading You in the Right Direction
questions.explanation: 이 글은 네이티브 아메리칸의 영적 지도자인 Odawa가 Iktomi라는 거미 형태의 신령으로부터 받은 가르침과 거미줄(드림캐쳐의 기원)에 대한 이야기를 담고 있습니다. 마지막 문단에서 오늘날 많은 네이티브 아메리칸들이 침대 위에 드림캐쳐를 걸어두는 관습과 연결하며 그것의 기원을 설명하고 있으므로, 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은 '드림캐쳐의 기원에 관한 신화'입니다.
options_translation: ① 거미줄: 완벽한 원
② 인생의 순환을 관리하는 법
③ 네이티브 아메리칸들이 거미를 고맙게 여기는 이유
④ 드림캐쳐의 기원에 관한 신화
⑤ 당신을 올바른 방향으로 이끄는 긍정적인 힘을 따르라

questions.question: 34. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As business shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① Shifting to digital business activities initially seen as eco-friendly may overlook environmental costs.
questions.explanation: 디지털 업무로의 전환이 종이를 아껴 환경에 긍정적일 것이라 예상되지만, 실제로는 인터넷 사용과 데이터 센터 운영에 막대한 전기와 화석 연료가 소모되어 탄소 배출을 유발하는 등 간과된 환경적 비용이 존재한다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 처음에는 친환경적으로 보였던 디지털 비즈니스 활동으로의 전환이 환경적 비용을 간과할 수도 있다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the impact and the probability of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will ⓐ<u>encourage</u> others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can recommend your products to others ⓑ<u>without</u> any person benefit. Therefore, customer satisfaction should be the ⓒ<u>priority</u>. People tend to believe the opinions of ⓓ<u>acquaintances</u>. People trust friends more than advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to show the "good side" and are designed to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to ⓔ<u>distance</u> yourself from positive word-of-mouth advertising.
questions.explanation: 고객의 만족도를 지속적으로 모니터링함으로써 긍정적인 입소문 광고를 활용하거나 얻을 수 있는 능력을 갖게 되는 것이 문맥상 자연스러우므로, '멀리하다(distance)'는 적절하지 않습니다. gain이나 benefit from과 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ① Brainwriting is a more appropriate methodology than brainstorming for drawing the team's potential.
② It is crucial for the entire team to actively communicate when generating ideas in brainwriting.
questions.explanation: 브레인라이팅의 초기 단계(The initial steps are solo)에서는 각자가 개별적으로 아이디어를 생성해야 하며, 독립적인 판단을 유지하기 위해 각자 평가합니다. 따라서 아이디어 생성 시 전체 팀이 활발하게 소통하는 것은 브레인라이팅의 방식과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 브레인라이팅은 팀의 잠재력을 끌어내는 데 있어 브레인스토밍보다 더 적절한 방법론이다.
② 브레인라이팅에서 아이디어를 생성할 때 팀 전체가 활발하게 소통하는 것이 중요하다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has ⓐ<u>indicated</u> that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort. Also, they suffered very ⓑ<u>few</u> disases. If this is true, it is not ⓒ<u>ambiguous</u> why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high ⓓ<u>increase</u> in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a ⓔ<u>chief</u> turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.explanation: 앞 문장에서 수렵 채집 생활이 풍족하고 질병도 적었다는 긍정적인 면을 언급한 뒤, 다음 문장에서 경작은 힘든 일이었고 전염병이 정착 마을에서 뿌리를 내렸다고 말하고 있습니다. 따라서 왜 수많은 인간이 정착 생활과 농업을 택했는지가 '모호하지 않다'가 아니라 '수수께끼이다' 혹은 '이해하기 어렵다'는 맥락이 되어야 합니다. ⓒ의 ambiguous(모호한)는 의문스럽다는 의미의 puzzling 혹은 mysterious 등으로 바뀌어야 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." Experiments and surveys have repeatedly shown that most people believe that they possess attributes that are better or more desirable than average. ⓐ<u>In contrast, the worse-than-average effect refers to a tendency to underestimate oneself in certain conditions</u>. ⓑ<u>A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability</u>. ⓒ<u>In terms of ability to get along with others, a statistically insignificant number - less than one percent - rated themselves as below average</u>. ⓓ<u>Furthermore, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!</u> ⓔ<u>Some have argued that more subjective traits like this may be more easily distorted.</u>
questions.explanation: 이 글의 전체적인 흐름은 사람들이 자신을 평균보다 낫다고 평가하는 '워비건 호수 효과(Lake Wobegon effect)'에 관한 것입니다. 반면 ⓐ는 특정 조건에서 자신을 과소평가하는 '평균 이하 효과'를 설명하고 있으므로 글의 전체적인 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, which is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way that production could be made more efficient, known as the "division of labor." ⓐ<u>Making most manufactured goods involves several different processes using different skills</u>. ⓑ<u>Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished</u>. ⓒ<u>One worker could do all these tasks, but this work can be divided into tis separate processes, with a number of workers each performing one task</u>. ⓓ<u>Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another</u>. ⓔ<u>That's the difficulty of labor division: when one slow task holds back the rest</u>. Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day - a huge increase in productivity from the 200 they would have produced before.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 분업(division of labor)이 생산성을 어떻게 증대시키는지에 대해 긍정적인 측면(효율성, 속도 향상)을 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓔ는 분업의 어려움이나 단점에 대해 언급하고 있으므로 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Although technology has the potential to increase productivity, it can also have a negative impact on productivity. For example, in many office environments workers sit at desks with computers and have access to the internet. They are able to check their personal emails and use social media whenever they want to. This can stop them from doing their work and make them less productive. Introducing new technology can also have a negative impact on production when it causes a change to the production process or requires workers to learn a new system. Learning to use new technology can be time consuming and stressful for workers and this can cause a decline in productivity.
options: ① New technology causes production surge.
② Technology brings an affirmative change to the businesses.
questions.explanation: 글의 첫 문장에서 기술이 생산성을 높일 가능성도 있지만 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수도 있음을 명시하고 있습니다. 이후 개인적인 인터넷 사용으로 인한 업무 방해, 새로운 시스템 학습에 따른 스트레스와 시간 소모 등을 예로 들어 생산성 저하의 원인을 설명하고 있습니다. (선택지 3, 4, 5번이 잘렸으나 지문의 핵심 내용은 기술이 생산성에 부정적인 영향을 줄 수 있다는 점입니다. 제공된 텍스트상 정답 번호는 ⑤로 표시되어 있습니다.)
options_translation: ① 새로운 기술은 생산성 급증을 초래한다.
② 기술은 기업에 긍정적인 변화를 가져온다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 30번]
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped increase sales.
options: ② How Is an Advertising Agency Selected?
③ Ingredients for Making Homemade Bread
④ Don't Change Market Status of the Products
⑤ Advertiser's Modification Ability on Promoting Products
questions.explanation: 이 글은 광고주들이 제품의 시장 상황에 맞춰 홍보 방식을 어떻게 조정하는지에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. Fleischmann의 효모가 제빵 재료에서 비타민 공급원으로, 다시 천연 완하제로 마케팅 포지셔닝을 변경하여 매출을 올린 사례를 통해 광고주의 제품 홍보 조정 능력을 보여줍니다.
options_translation: ① 효모 발달의 역사
② 광고 대행사는 어떻게 선택되는가?
③ 집에서 빵을 만들기 위한 재료들
④ 제품의 시장 지위를 바꾸지 마라
⑤ 제품 홍보에 있어서 광고주의 수정 능력

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 6월 39번]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less ⓐ<u>adjustable</u>. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes don't have very ⓑ<u>efficient</u> migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt ⓒ<u>effortlessly</u>. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most ⓓ<u>inefficient</u> migration routes. Childhood ⓔ<u>assists</u> the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 어린 시절(childhood)이 길고 부모와 함께 이동하는 새들은 환경에 적응하고 학습할 기회가 많아 더 효율적인 이동 경로를 가집니다. 반면 태어날 때부터 본능에만 의존하는 새들은 환경 변화에 적응하지 못해 비효율적인 경로를 고수하게 됩니다. 따라서 문맥상 ⓓ의 'inefficient(비효율적인)'는 'efficient(효율적인)'로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
options: ① Athletes' professional ability emerges from credibility built from people who admire them.
② When celebrities give advice on the area of their skill, people are reluctant to listen to them.
③ People admire individuals who perform at a high level in their profession and imitate them blindly.
④ People who possess a high level of ability in an area persuade people to possess products they promote.
⑤ People listen to celebrities not because of their expertise on the product but because of the excellence in their field.
questions.explanation: 사람들은 특정 분야에서 탁월한 성과를 내는 사람들에게 즉각적인 신뢰를 느끼며, 그들의 조언이 그들의 전문 분야와 관련이 없더라도 귀를 기울인다는 내용입니다. 이는 그 제품에 대한 지식 때문이 아니라 그들이 자신의 분야에서 보여준 '탁월함' 때문이라고 설명합니다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤번입니다.
options_translation: ① 운동선수의 전문적인 능력은 그들을 존경하는 사람들로부터 쌓인 신뢰에서 나온다.
② 유명인들이 자신의 기술 분야에 대해 조언할 때, 사람들은 듣기를 꺼려한다.
③ 사람들은 자신의 직업에서 높은 수준의 성과를 내는 개인들을 존경하고 맹목적으로 모방한다.
④ 특정 분야에서 높은 능력을 가진 사람들은 사람들이 자신이 홍보하는 제품을 소유하도록 설득한다.
⑤ 사람들은 제품에 대한 전문 지식 때문이 아니라 해당 분야의 탁월함 때문에 유명인의 말을 듣는다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흠름으로 보아, 주어진 문자이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 6월 40번]
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad. (A) There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. (B) Of course the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet. (C) However, it's different in the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. (D) The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. (E) Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need.
questions.insertion_sentence: As another example, let us consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문자은 '또 다른 예시(As another example)'로서, 몬가 건강한 음식만을 먹는 경우를 설명하고 있음. 지문 (B)~(D)김지는 퉀기음식(fried foods)을 예로 들어 식단의 전체적인 구성이 중요함을 말하고 있음. (E) 뒤에 나오는 'all these foods'는 제시문에 씽기된 븀로콜리, 사과, 주스 등을 가리킴. 따라서 제시된 문자은 (E)에 들어가는 갓이 가장 적절함.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 문줄 친 분분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [23년 6월 39번]
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." ⓐ<u>The decline in curiosity can observe in the development of the brain through childhood</u>. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; ⓑ<u>the lines of communication between infant neurons are much more inefficient</u> than between those in the adult brain. ⓒ<u>The baby's perception of the world is accordingly both intensely rich and wildly disordered</u>. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, ⓓ<u>certain possibilities become more likely and more useful and firm into knowledge or beliefs</u>. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, ⓔ<u>while the ones which the child doesn't use regularly are eliminated.</u>
questions.explanation: ⓐ에서 주어인 'The decline in curiosity(호기심의 감소)'는 관찰하는 제체가 아니라 관찰되는 대상이므로 수동태인 'can be observed'로 고쳐야 함.

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 30번]
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when ______________________________________________.
options: ② they fully estimate the value of future compensation
③ they can't ignore the satisfaction of immediate pleasure
④ they can estimate the significantly greater value of investing sufficient time
⑤ future reward holds greater and more substantial value than instant reward
questions.explanation: 인간은 미래의 보상을 위해 현재의 즐거움을 포기하는 합리적인 저축 계획을 세우지만, 종종 의지박약으로 인해 그 계획을 어기고 저축한 돈을 미리 써버립니다. 이는 미래의 가치보다 눈앞에 닥친 즉각적인 즐거움의 유혹을 뿌리치지 못할 때 발생하므로 ③ '즉각적인 즐거움의 만족을 무시할 수 없을 때'가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 즉각적인 즐거움이 무시될 때
② 그들이 미래 보상의 가치를 충분히 평가할 때
③ 그들이 즉각적인 즐거움의 만족을 무시할 수 없을 때
④ 그들이 충분한 시간을 투자하는 것에 대한 상당히 더 큰 가치를 평가할 수 있을 때
⑤ 미래의 보상이 즉각적인 보상보다 더 크고 실질적인 가치를 지닐 때

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 29번]
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to _____________________________________________. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
options: ① behave accordingly to fit himself into that information
② expect other people to say the same thing as his mother
③ cooperate with the brightest boy in his class to receive more praise
④ feel burdened and may refuse to be the person who his mother says he is
⑤ analyze the information and have a hard time understanding what led his mother to say that
questions.explanation: 미취학 아동은 부모의 말을 비판 없이 그대로 수용하는 경향이 있습니다. 부모가 아이에게 긍정적인 평가(똑똑하고 도움을 잘 준다)를 반복적으로 해주면, 아이는 자신의 정체성을 그에 맞춰 형성하고 실제로 그 정보에 부합하도록 행동하게 됩니다. 따라서 ①이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 그 정보에 자신을 맞추기 위해 그에 따라 행동한다
② 다른 사람들도 자신의 어머니와 똑같은 말을 할 것이라고 기대한다
③ 더 많은 칭찬을 받기 위해 반에서 가장 똑똑한 아이와 협력한다
④ 부담감을 느끼고 어머니가 말하는 사람이 되는 것을 거부할 수도 있다
⑤ 정보를 분석하고 어머니가 그렇게 말하게 된 원인을 이해하는 데 어려움을 겪는다

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that _____________________________________________.
options: ① appropriate time is crucial in brain development
② inborn abilities have a decisive effect on the formation of one's capacity
③ once established, one's way of thinking is not easily altered, so the initial settings are critical
④ the structure of the brain adapts based on our focus and the activities we regularly engage in
⑤ what we learn and think about during infancy has a crucial impact on the brain's functioning throughout our lives
questions.explanation: 지문에서는 소리에 중점을 둔 동물의 청각 중심, 시력이 중요한 동물의 시각 영역, 바이올린 연주자의 손가락 조절 관련 피질, 택시 기사의 곞간 기억 관련 해마 등 많은 예시를 통해 '중점을 두는 점과 일상적으로 하는 활동에 따라 뇌의 구조가 변화한다'는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 정답은 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌 발달에 적절한 시기가 결정적이다.
② 태어났 때부터 가진 능력이 개인의 역량 형성에 결정적인 영향을 미츜다.
③ 한 번 형성되면 사고 방식은 쉽게 바봈지 않으므로 초기 설정이 중요하다.
④ 뇌의 구조는 우리의 중점과 우리가 정기적으로 하는 활동에 기반하여 적응한다.
⑤ 유아기 때 배우고 사고하는 것이 평생 동안의 뇌 기능에 중요한 영향을 미츜다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, _______________________________________.
options: ① the red squirrel has become free from extinction
② the red squirrel has been prone to be an endangered species
③ the grey squirrel has come to be at risk of extinction in England
④ the red and the grey squirrel have got to fight over food for good
⑤ the grey squirrel has become superior to the red in regulating their eating habit
questions.explanation: 외랮종인 회색 찤다람준가 토착종인 붉은 찤다람준와의 경사에ᄉ서 먹이(익지 않은 도토리 섭취 가능) 및 서식지 적응력 면에서 우위를 점하고 있다고 설명합니다. 광과적으로 붉은 찤다람준는 경사에서 밀려났으므로, 멸종 위기에 처하기 쉽게 되었다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 붉은 찤다람준는 멸종으로부터 자유로워졀다.
② 붉은 찤다람준는 멸종 위기종이 되기 쉬워졀다.
③ 회색 찤다람준가 영국엑ᄉ서 멸종 위기에 처하게 되었다.
④ 붉은 찤다람준와 회색 찤다람준는 먹이를 두고 영원히 싸워야 한다.
⑤ 회색 찤다람준는 식습관 조절에 있어서 붉은 찤다람준밴다 우월해졀다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations.
ordered_passages: (A) This is equally applied to those who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. Fortunately, professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users.

(B) This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.

(C) What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서는 디지턳 정밴 보존 표준 개발에 대해 언급합니다. (C)에서 'however'를 통해 장애인의 필요가 방츘되었음을 지적하며 청각 장애인의 예를 듭니다. (A)의 'This is equally applied'는 (C)의 상황이 시각 장애인에게도 적용됨을 내타내며 현재의 발전 상황을 언급합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 'This situation would be much improved'를 통해 해결 방안(모든 사용자를 고려한 디자인)을 제시하며 마무리하는 것이 자연수럽습니다. 따라서 (C)-(A)-(B) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment. This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure. All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is to have the pain always directly associated with a pleasurable reward.
questions.summary_sentence: Humans pursue activities that cause a certain level of pain, like eating spicy food, because the brain finds (A)_____________ in mastering the discomfort and knowing it is ultimately not (B)______________.
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 인간이 고통스러운 자극을 통해 즐거움을 느끼는 이유는 그것이 '안전한 위협'이기 때문이라는 것입니다. 뇌가 불편함을 극복하고 그것이 결국 실제적인 위협이 아님을 인지할 때 즐거움을 얻는다는 내용이므로 (A)에는 enjoyment(즐거움), (B)에는 threatening(위협적인)이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고통 / 해로운
② 기쁨 / 해롭지 않은
③ 고뇌 / 유익한
④ 즐거움 / 위협적인
⑤ 자신감 / 위협적이지 않은

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용으로 알 수 없는 것은?
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, which then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly. As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you." If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler has been transmitted via our body. Stranger as it may sound, this theory states that emotions arise from our bodies. For example, our mood can be improved by simply lifting up the corners of our mouth. If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, taking care not to let the pencil touch their lips (thus forcing the mouth into a smile-like shape), they judge cartoons funnier than if they have been asked to frown. The primacy of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase 'I must be afraid, because I'm running.'
options: ① Smiling can trick your brain into happiness.
② Body is followed by emotion according to this article.
③ Forcing a smile has an impact on feeling that comes afterwards.
④ 'Emotional echo' means that emotion comes after a certain behavior.
⑤ Just copying others' smiles can make us feel the same emotions the observer feels.
questions.explanation: 지문에서는 타인의 미소를 모방하면 괴 감정이 영향을 미쳐 옱리도 픖복함을 눐기게 된다고 했습니다. 하지만 5번 보기는 관찰자(the observer)가 눐기는 감정을 모방하는 사람이 눐기게 된다고 설명하고 읈으며, 문맥사 관찰자는 모방하는 제 3자이고, 미소를 지은 사람(the smiler)의 감정을 눐기는 것이므로 observer를 smiler로 바꿔야 합니다. 또한 글의 제목이나 요지가 아닌 '알 수 없는 것' 즉 내용 불일치를 묻는 문제에서 사영된 단어의 주체가 잘못 설명되었습니다.
options_translation: ① 미소 줓기는 다신의 뇌를 셍여 픖복함을 눐기게 할 수 있다.
② 이 글에 땄리면 신체가 먼저이고 감정이 괴 들을 땄린다.
③ 억지 미소는 괴 이협에 나타나는 감정에 영향을 미쳐다.
④ '감정적 메아리'는 감정이 특정한 행동 들에 온다는 것을 의미한다.
⑤ 타인의 미소를 머저 따라 하는 것만으로도 관찰자가 눐기는 감정과 동일한 감정을 눐기게 할 수 있다.

questions.question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절핤 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did.
ordered_passages: (A) That is the tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.

(B) A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage.

(C) Additionally, the human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 인간의 정신이 타 부족과의 경상과 갈등 때문에 진화했을 가능성을 제시합니다. (B)에서 상대방보다 생각을 더 잘하는 부족이 가지는 군사적 이점을 구체적으로 설명하고, (C)에서 Additionally(견다가)를 통해 이러한 정신적 이점이 생줔 투읁의 무기가 되었음을 실명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 이점을 가진 부족이 승리하여 유전자를 물려줄 수 있었음을 결론 집니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분의 이유로 가장 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. <u>The findings are particularly strong</u> because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
options: ① The test was based on the reliable researchers' claims.
② The test had 'a control' and 'two tests', which was different from other tests.
③ The test took place in three supermarkets, which was enough for the test to be effective.
④ The test happened in real-life situation where the reliability of the test could improve.
⑤ The test was not held in a laboratory where consumers' behaviors could be more genuine than people thought.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 문장 뒤에 나오는 설명에 따르면, 이 실험 결과가 강력한 이유는 실험실이 아닌 실제 쇼핑객들이 있는 슈퍼마켓에서 실제 행동을 바탕으로 수행되었기 때문입니다. 즉, 실제 상황(real-life situation)에서 이루어진 실험이기에 데이터의 신뢰도와 결과의 설득력이 높다는 것을 의미하므로 ④번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 테스트가 신뢰할 수 있는 연구자들의 주장에 근거했다.
② 테스트에 '통제 집단'과 '두 개의 실험 집단'이 있었는데, 이는 다른 테스트들과 달랐다.
③ 테스트가 세 개의 슈퍼마켓에서 진행되었으며, 이는 테스트가 효과적이기 위해 충분했다.
④ 테스트가 테스트의 신뢰성을 향상시킬 수 있는 실제 상황에서 발생했다.
⑤ 테스트는 소비자들의 행동이 사람들이 생각하는 것보다 더 진실할 수 있는 실험실에서 개최되지 않았다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 아래 표의 (A)~(C)를 1~3개의 단어로 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
questions.subjective_answer_format: City | Braincomparison target: economy | (A)_____________means of transportation: train | (B)_____________contents: (C)_____________ | raw electrochemical signals
questions.answer: (A) brain's operation(B) superhighways of neurons(C) materials and textiles
questions.explanation: 본문은 뇌를 도시에 비유하고 있습니다. (A) 도시의 경제(economy)가 상호작용의 결과이듯 뇌의 작동(brain's operation) 또한 한 곳이 아닌 상호작용의 결과입니다. (B) 도시의 기차(train)가 물자를 실어나르는 통로이듯 뇌에서는 뉴런의 고속도로(superhighways of neurons)가 신호를 전달합니다. (C) 기차가 실어오는 원자재와 직물(materials and textiles)은 뇌에서 처리되기 전의 가공되지 않은 전기화학적 신호에 대응됩니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 괐을 읽고, <점건>에 맞게 비칸 (A), (B)를 채워 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. (A)______________________________________ are nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields (B)_____________________________________, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
subjective_conditions: (A)에 growth, crops, necessary, what을 한 번씩 포함하여 7~10단어로 작성할 경
(B)에 nutrients and water, relative, load, natural land를 한 번씩 포함하여 10~13단어로 작성할 경
(A), (B) 모두 단어 촔가 및 형태 변형 가능
questions.answer: (A) what is/are necessary for the growth of crops(B) are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land
questions.explanation: (A) 농작물의 성장에 필요한 경은 what 관계대명사절을 주어로 사용하여 'what is/are necessary for the growth of crops'로 작성합니다.(B) 농지가 자연 상태의 토지에 비해 영양분과 수분으로 가득 차 있기 때문에 잡초들에게 인기가 있다는 내용이므로, 'are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land'로 완성합니다. load는 수동형(be loaded with)으로 변형하여 사용합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists say that having a disorderly room can indicate a disorganized mental state. In other words, Messy rooms can have a significant impact on mental well-being, influencing mood and stress levels. Depending on the person, they can create stress and other negative emotions, leading to (A)[treatments / symptoms] of anxiety and depression. Living in a messy room can (B)[suppress / evoke] feelings of frustration, irritation, and even shame. The constant reminder of untidiness can weigh heavily on one's mood, leading to a sense of dissatisfaction and unhappiness. Furthermore, a messy room can (C)[defer / undermine] one's sense of self-worth and competence. Constantly living in disarray may lead to feelings of inadequacy and self-criticism, as individuals judge themselves based on the state of their living space. One of the professional tidying experts says that the moment you start cleaning your room, you also start changing your life and gaining new perspective.
questions.explanation: (A) 지저분한 방은 스트레스와 부정적 감정을 유발하여 불안과 우울의 '증상(symptoms)'으로 이어집니다. (B) 지저분한 방에서 사는 것은 좌절감, 짜증 등의 감정을 '환기/유발(evoke)'할 수 있습니다. (C) 또한 지저분한 방은 자존감과 유능함을 '약화(undermine)'시킬 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 치료법 - 억제하다 - 미루다
② 증상 - 억제하다 - 미루다
③ 증상 - 유발하다 - 미루다
④ 증상 - 유발하다 - 약화시키다
⑤ 치료법 - 억제하다 - 약화시키다

questions.question: 6. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behavior are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act in alignment with that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you ____________________. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
options: ① try to purse behavior change
② are no longer pursuing behavior change
③ listen to other people's opinions about yourself
④ reduce the friction associated with your good actions
⑤ search for a tiny margin of improvement in everything you do
questions.explanation: 행동과 정체성이 완벽하게 일치할 때, 사람은 더 이상 스스로를 설득하거나 변화시키려 애쓰지 않고 자연스럽게 자신의 정체성에 맞는 행동을 하게 됩니다. 따라서 '더 이상 행동 변화를 추구하지 않는다'는 표현이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 행동 변화를 추구하려고 노력한다
② 더 이상 행동 변화를 추구하지 않는다
③ 자신에 대한 타인의 의견을 경청한다
④ 선행과 관련된 마찰을 줄인다
⑤ 당신이 하는 모든 일에서 아주 작은 개선의 여지를 찾는다

questions.question: 7. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be ____________ than the undiscounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.explanation: 현재의 즉각적인 즐거움을 포기하고 미래의 보상을 선택한다는 것은, 할인된 미래 보상의 가치가 현재의 가치보다 '더 크다(greater)'고 판단하기 때문입니다. 문맥상 지연된 보상을 선택하는 행위의 논리적 근거를 설명하는 부분입니다.
options_translation: ① 더 작은
② 더 적은
③ 더 큰
④ 더 보이지 않는
⑤ 더 부분적인

questions.question: 8. 다음 글 (A)의 내용을 바탕으로 쓴 (B)의 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 34번]
questions.passage: (A) To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you poll them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually, before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.summary_sentence: (B) The distinctive advantage of brainwriting lies in its democratic nature: Brainwriting ⓐ_________ equal participation from all attendees. It doesn't ⓑ_________ those who can articulate better or more quickly, providing a fair platform for every voice to be heard. In addition, anonymity encourages individuals to be more ⓒ_________ and imaginative with their ideas.
questions.explanation: 브레인라이팅은 모든 참석자의 평등한 참여를 '보장(ensures)'하며, 말을 더 잘하거나 빨리 하는 사람을 '선호(favor)'하지 않습니다. 또한 익명성은 개인들이 자신의 아이디어에 대해 더 '거침없이 말하게(outspoken)' 만듭니다.
options_translation: ① 보장한다 - 선호하다 - 거침없이 말하는
② 보장한다 - 선호하다 - 간접적인
③ 화해시키다 - 선호하다 - 거침없이 말하는
④ 화해시키다 - 앞서다 - 간접적인
⑤ 보장한다 - 앞서다 - 거침없이 말하는

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 6월 38번]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, ⓐ<u>spacing</u> their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about ⓑ<u>transporting</u> young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to ⓒ<u>lengthen</u> their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in ⓓ<u>rapid</u> population growth among farming communities. An ⓔ<u>increased</u> population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.explanation: 정착 생활을 하는 농경 사회에서는 아이를 이동시킬 걱정이 없었으므로 출산 간격이 4년에서 2년으로 '줄어들었습니다(shorten)'. 따라서 '늘리다'라는 뜻의 lengthen은 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 주제로 Importance of confronting hardship in one's life를 참고할 때 hardship이 들어갈 위치로 적절하지 않은 곳은?
questions.passage: We often try to avoid (A) and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We tend to choose (B) and never really work hard to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing (C) to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. (D) is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. (E) will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
questions.explanation: (B) 앞의 문맥을 보면 '우리는 쉬운 길(the easy route)을 택한다'고 했으며, (B) 뒤에도 '인생의 핵심 분야에서 숙달을 위해 열심히 노력하지 않는다'는 내용이 나옵니다. 따라서 (B)에는 고난(hardship)을 선택한다는 말이 들어갈 수 없으며, 오히려 편안함이나 안이함을 선택한다는 내용이 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ① 주인의식이란 통제하고 있다는 느낌, 진정한 의사결정 권한이 있다는 느낌을 의미한다.
② 오하이오의 한 제조공장의 연구에서 근로자들은 유니폼을 디자인하고 근무교대에 관한 권한을 부여받았다.
③ 두 달 만에 그 제조공장의 생산성은 증가했으며 근로자들의 임금 상승으로 이어졌다.
④ 통제권을 쥐고 있다는 느낌은 근로자들이 휴식시간을 더 짧게 가지고, 실수는 더 적게 하도록 만들었다.
⑤ 근로자에게 주인의식을 주는 것으로 자기 통제력을 향상시킬 수 있었다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same'이라고 언급되어 있습니다. 즉, 제조 공정과 임금 체계는 그대로 유지되었으므로 임금이 상승했다는 ③번의 설명은 옳지 않습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. (A) A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. (B) The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. (C) The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. (D) The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this psychological edge to its offspring. (E) You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.insertion_sentence: And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'this mental advantage(이러한 정신적 이점)'는 앞 문장의 'psychological edge(심리적 우위)'를 가리킵니다. 또한 'within each succeeding generation(각각의 뒤이은 세대 내에서)'이라는 표현은 (D)의 'pass on the genes... to its offspring(자손에게 유전자를 물려주다)'과 논리적으로 연결됩니다. 따라서 (D) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Childhood allows animals to learn about their environment. Without it, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be relatively ⓐ<u>inflexible</u>. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have highly ⓑ<u>inefficient</u> migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, hardly ⓒ<u>adapt</u> to changes. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and map. Birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, ⓓ<u>on the other hand</u>, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood ⓔ<u>disrupts</u> the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 지문은 어린 시절(childhood)이 동물들에게 유연성을 제공하고 문화적 정보를 학습할 수 있게 해준다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 'disrupts(방해하다)'는 문맥상 'facilitates(촉진하다)'나 'allows(허용하다)'와 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다. 어린 시절이 문화적 정보의 전달을 돕기 때문에 유전보다 빠르게 진화할 수 있다는 것이 글의 요지입니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an ⓐ<u>unexpected</u> guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the ⓑ<u>untimely</u> visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work ⓒ<u>done</u>. While there are many documented cases of ⓓ<u>sudden</u> interruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally ⓔ<u>accelerating</u> stress levels.
questions.explanation: 방해(interruption)로 인해 Coleridge가 영감을 잃어버리고 시 작성을 중단하게 된 상황을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 작품을 '완성된(done)' 상태로 둔 것이 아니라 '미완성된' 상태로 남겨두었다는 의미가 되어야 하므로 'unfinished'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly ⓐ<u>introduced</u> to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which ⓑ<u>put</u> the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is capable, for instance, of ⓒ<u>eating</u> green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more ⓓ<u>dense</u> and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come ⓔ<u>close</u> to extinction in England.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 'live'는 동사이며, 이를 수식하기 위해서는 형용사인 'dense'가 아니라 부사인 'densely'가 필요합니다. 따라서 'live more densely'가 어법상 올바른 표현입니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [24년 6월 21번]
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced ⓐ<u>to be</u> the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers ⓑ<u>to become</u> much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer ⓒ<u>has tripled</u> since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and ⓓ<u>watering</u> our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields ⓔ<u>loaded</u> with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.explanation: Because가 이끄는 부사절에서 farm fields가 주어이며, 뒤에 이어지는 구문에서 동사가 필요합니다. loaded는 과거분사구로 쓰여 동사 역할을 할 수 없으므로, 시제와 수에 맞춰 are loaded(수동태 동사)로 고쳐야 문장이 성립합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 주어진 조건을 참고하여 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 알맞은 말을 순서대로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few disases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals because cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. (A)w__________ its immeidate (B)e__________ on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture (C)u__________ (D)[in / increase / population density / a high / lead to]. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
subjective_conditions: 인간의 삶에 미치는 즉각적인 영향이 무엇이든, 정착지와 농업의 발전은 의심의 여지없이 인구 밀도의 높은 증가로 이어졌다.
위의 한글 해석을 참고하여 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 각각 주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어를 순서대로 쓰시오.
빈칸 (D)에 제시된 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 알맞게 배열하시오. (필요시 동사의 어형변화)
questions.answer: (A) whatever(B) effect(s)(C) undoubtedly(D) led to a high increase in population density
questions.explanation: (A) '무엇이든'에 해당하는 복합관계대명사 'whatever'가 적절합니다. (B) '영향'을 뜻하는 'effect'가 들어갑니다. (C) '의심의 여지없이'라는 부사 'undoubtedly'가 문맥상 자연스럽습니다. (D) 과거의 사실을 서술하므로 'lead to'를 'led to'로 변형하여 'led to a high increase in population density'로 배열합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the hidden toll이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, <u>the hidden toll</u> is often overlooked. A recent Wired report indicated that the majority of data centers rely on fossil fuels for energy. As we store larger volumes of data in the cloud, the resulting increase in carbon emissions reduces the environmental benefits, turning our green clouds gray. Although the carbon footprint of an email is smaller than that of traditional postal mail, it still contributes approximately four grams of CO₂, potentially rising to 50 grams with large attachments.
options: ① The carbon footprint associated with manufacturing electronic devices
② The devastation of local ecosystems due to potential digital habits
③ The cost savings achieved by businesses by reducing paper waste
④ The financial expense of using the Internet and electricity for businesses
⑤ The environmental damage from the energy consumption for storing data
questions.explanation: 'the hidden toll'(숨겨진 대가)은 디지털 비즈니스가 종이 소비를 줄여 환경에 긍정적일 것으로 기대되었으나, 실제로는 데이터 센터 운영을 위한 화석 연료 사용과 데이터 저장 과정에서 발생하는 탄소 배출로 인해 환경에 해를 끼친다는 맥락에서 사용되었습니다. 따라서 데이터 저장을 위한 에너지 소비로 인한 환경적 피해를 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 전자 기기 제조와 관련된 탄소 발자국
② 잠재적인 디지털 습관으로 인한 지역 생태계의 파괴
③ 종이 낭비를 줄임으로써 기업이 달성한 비용 절감
④ 기업의 인터넷 및 전기 사용에 따른 재정적 비용
⑤ 데이터 저장을 위한 에너지 소비에서 발생하는 환경적 피해

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 the right amount of both가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly <u>the right amount of both</u>. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
options: ④ Sufficient real estate and financial aid
⑤ A number of farmers and advanced technologies
questions.explanation: 앞 문장에서 단일 경작을 위해 비료(fertilizer) 형태의 영양분과 관개에 의한 물(water)을 추가한다고 언급했습니다. 따라서 'the right amount of both'가 지칭하는 것은 비료와 물입니다.
options_translation: ① 충분한 비료와 물
② 충분한 관심과 보살핌
③ 충분한 비료와 작물
④ 충분한 부동산과 재정 지원
⑤ 많은 농부들과 선진 기술들

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to ⓐ<u>recommend</u> it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors ⓑ<u>enjoyed</u> abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed ⓒ<u>agriculture</u>, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of ⓓ<u>movements</u> and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the ⓔ<u>growth</u> of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.explanation: 지문의 문맥상 수렵 채집 생활에서 벗어나 정착 생활로 넘어가며 농경이 시작된 시기를 설명하고 있습니다. 인구 밀도의 증가를 가져온 것은 '이동(movements)'이 아니라 '정착(settlement)' 혹은 '정착 생활'이어야 하므로 ⓓ가 부적절합니다. 원문은 'settlement'입니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on ____________________________________ to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
options: ① the hatred between tribes that lasted for decades
② the weapon that can no longer be used in battles
③ the genes that gave a mental boost to win battles
④ the knowledge that led to conflicts within their tribe
⑤ the diplomatic skills that can help them avoid conflicts.
questions.explanation: 글 전체가 타 부족과의 경쟁에서 '상대보다 더 똑똑하게 생각하는 능력'이 생존의 핵심 무기가 되었음을 설명하고 있습니다. 전쟁에서 이길 가능성이 높은 부족이 그 능력을 자손에게 물려준다는 내용이 와야 하므로, ③ '전투에서 승리하도록 정신적 강화를 제공한 유전자'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 수십 년간 지속된 부족 간의 증오
② 더 이상 전투에서 사용될 수 없는 무기
③ 전투에서 승리하기 위한 정신적 힘을 준 유전자
④ 부족 내 갈등을 초래한 지식
⑤ 갈등을 피하는 데 도움을 줄 수 있는 외교적 기술

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
