questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ① Self-discipline is hard to expect from employees.
② Small decisions cannot affect productivity at all.
③ Empowering workers positively affects productivity.
④ Uniforms give employees a sense of community.
⑤ Controlling employees is important for productivity.
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 스스로 통제하고 있다는 느낌(sense of agency)이나 결정권(authority)을 주는 것이 생산성을 높인다는 것이 글의 요지입니다. 오하이오 공장 실험을 통해 자율성을 부여했을 때 생산성이 20% 향상되었다는 예시가 이를 뒷받침합니다.
options_translation: ① 직원들에게 자율 규제(자기 절제)를 기대하기는 어렵다.
② 작은 결정들은 생산성에 전혀 영향을 미치지 못한다.
③ 직원들에게 권한을 부여하는 것은 생산성에 긍정적인 영향을 미친다.
④ 유니폼은 직원들에게 공동체 의식을 준다.
⑤ 직원들을 통제하는 것이 생산성을 위해 중요하다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 a summer vacation이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on <u>a summer vacation</u> instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure disappears.
options: ① A reasonable use of saved resources
② An immediate voucher reward system
③ Savings for traveling foreign countries
④ A reward or pleasure experienced instantly
⑤ The pleasure that contradicts with short-term goals
questions.explanation: 본문에서 'a summer vacation'은 원래 계획했던 미래의 보상(크리스마스 선물)을 기다리지 못하고 의지 박약으로 인해 즉각적인 유혹에 굴복하여 돈을 써버리는 대상을 의미합니다. 따라서 이는 즉각적으로 경험되는 보상이나 즐거움을 뜻합니다.
options_translation: ① 저축된 자원의 합리적인 사용
② 즉각적인 바우처 보상 시스템
③ 외국 여행을 위한 저축
④ 즉각적으로 경험되는 보상이나 즐거움
⑤ 단기 목표와 상충되는 즐거움

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.summary_sentence: Unlike mobile hunter-gatherers, farmers in a settled community could have short birth intervals due to the reduced need for (A)___________, which led to population (B)___________ essential for agricultural labor.
questions.explanation: 이동 생활을 하던 수렵 채집인과 달리, 정착 생활을 하게 된 농부들은 이동(migration)의 필요성이 줄어들어 출산 간격이 짧아졌고, 이는 농업 노동력에 필수적인 인구 팽창(expansion)으로 이어졌다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 이동 / 팽창
② 이동 / 감소
③ 경작 / 팽창
④ 이동 / 안정
⑤ 이동 / 안정

questions.question: 23. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (단, 필요한 경우 어형을 변형할 것)
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are physically larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that where we direct our attention and what we practice doing can change the ____________ architecture of the brain.
subjective_conditions: 단, 필요한 경우 어형을 변형할 것
questions.explanation: 지문 전체가 집중된 주의력이나 연습이 뇌의 특정 부위를 물리적으로 확장시키거나 재구성한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 특히 앞 문장에서 'physically larger'라는 표현이 사용되었으므로, 빈칸에는 뇌의 '물리적' 구조를 바꿀 수 있다는 의미의 'physical'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (단, 필요한 경우 어형을 변형할 것)
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are taken individually. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. Through the development and assessment of ideas by ____________s before they choose and elaborate them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
subjective_conditions: 단, 필요한 경우 어형을 변형할 것
questions.explanation: 브레인라이팅 과정의 핵심은 아이디어를 팀이 함께 모이기 전에 '개인별로' 내고 평가하는 것입니다. 지문 앞부분의 'individually', 'separately', 'independent judgment', 'on their own' 등의 표현을 통해 빈칸에 들어갈 말이 '개인'임을 알 수 있습니다. 문맥상 '개인들에 의한 아이디어의 개발'이 되어야 하므로 'individuals'로 변형하여 쓰는 것이 정확하지만, 본문에서 찾으라고 했으므로 형용사형인 individual 혹은 명사형 individuals가 고려될 수 있습니다. (정답표에 근거하여 individual)

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 hardware가 의미하는 것을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어)
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on <u>hardware</u>, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 hardware는 타고난 지침이나 생물학적 설정을 의미합니다. 글의 후반부에서 문화가 '유전자(genes)'보다 더 빨리 진화할 수 있다고 언급하며, 학습(유년기) 없이 의존하는 타고난 시스템의 핵심인 유전자를 hardware로 지칭하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말과 같은 의미가 되도록 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that (A)<u>우리의 최종 제품은 장애가 없는 사람뿐만 아니라 장애가 있는 사람들의 필요도 충족시킨다.</u>
subjective_conditions: 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 활용할 것 (단, 필요한 경우 어형 변형 가능)
"조건 1"의 단어 이외에 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말 뜻에 맞게 필요한 단어를 추가할 것
"조건 1"에 제시된 11개의 단어를 포함해 총 15단어로 이루어진 문장을 만들 것
questions.answer: our final product meets the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.explanation: 주어진 우리말을 영작하면 '우리의 최종 제품(our final product)'이 주어이고, '충족시킨다(meets)'가 동사입니다. 'B뿐만 아니라 A도'의 구문인 'A as well as B'를 사용하여 '장애가 없는 사람들(those without (disabilities)) 뿐만 아니라 장애가 있는 사람들(those with disabilities)의 필요(the needs of)'를 구성합니다. 조건에 맞추어 15단어가 되도록 'our final product meets the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without'으로 작성합니다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 요지를 다음 주어진 단어를 알맞게 배열하여 완성하시오. (단, 주어진 단어만을 모두 사용할 것)
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that (A)<u>우리의 최종 제품은 장애가 없는 사람뿐만 아니라 장애가 있는 사람들의 필요도 충족시킨다.</u>
subjective_conditions: 제시된 단어만을 모두 사용할 것
지문의 핵심 주제를 담은 요지 문장을 완성할 것
questions.answer: Digital information standards should not overlook disabled people.
questions.explanation: 디지털 정보 표준이 장애인들의 필요를 간과해서는 안 된다는 글의 핵심 요지를 영작하는 문제입니다. '디지털 정보 표준(Digital information standards)'을 주어로 설정하고, '~해서는 안 된다'는 금지/충고의 의미를 담은 조동사 'should not' 뒤에 '간과하다'라는 뜻의 동사원형 'overlook'을 연결하여 문장을 완성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 대화문을 읽고 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 문장을 주어진 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage:
A: I heard you had trouble with the new software.
B: Yes, I couldn't figure it out at first.
A: Did you finally understand it?
B: _____________________ His explanation really helped me follow everything.
subjective_conditions: 부사 'only'를 문장 맨 앞에 사용할 것
다음 우리말 뜻과 같은 문장을 완성할 것: '그가 그것을 설명해 줄 때 비로소 내가 그 문제를 이해했다.'
'understand'와 'problem'을 반드시 포함할 것
questions.answer: Only when he explained it did I understand the problem.
questions.explanation: 'Only'가 이끄는 부사절이 문장 맨 앞에 올 때, 주절의 주어와 동사가 도치되는 '부정어/한정어 도치' 구문을 활용하는 문제입니다. '그가 그것을 설명했을 때(Only when he explained it)'가 문두에 왔으므로, 주절 'I understood the problem'은 의문문 어순인 'did I understand the problem'으로 도치되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for (A)<u>future consumption</u>. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a (B)<u>delayed reward</u> over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. ⓐThus the discounted value of the future reward should be smaller than the undiscounted value of the present one. ⓑHowever, in some cases the agent does not wait for (C)<u>the envisioned occasion</u> but uses their savings prematurely. ⓒFor example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy (D)<u>Christmas presents</u> but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. ⓓSuch cases could be examples of weakness of will. ⓔThat is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for (E)<u>immediate pleasure</u> appears.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 미래 소비를 위해 저축을 하지만 의지박약 등으로 인해 계획보다 일찍 저축을 소비하게 되는 현상에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ⓐ번 문장은 '미래 보상의 할인된 가치가 현재의 할인되지 않은 가치보다 작아야 한다'는 경제학적 원리를 말하고 있는데, 이는 뒤에 이어지는 '계획과 달리 조기에 소비하는 행위(의지 박약)'라는 논리적 흐름과 직접적인 관련이 없거나 글의 핵심 논점(의지 박약 사례)에서 벗어납니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 (A)~(E) 중 의미하는 바가 나머지 넷과 다른 하나는?
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for (A)<u>future consumption</u>. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a (B)<u>delayed reward</u> over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. ⓐThus the discounted value of the future reward should be smaller than the undiscounted value of the present one. ⓑHowever, in some cases the agent does not wait for (C)<u>the envisioned occasion</u> but uses their savings prematurely. ⓒFor example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy (D)<u>Christmas presents</u> but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. ⓓSuch cases could be examples of weakness of will. ⓔThat is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for (E)<u>immediate pleasure</u> appears.
questions.explanation: (A) 미래 소비, (B) 지연된 보상, (C) 계획된 행사(미래), (D) 크리스마스 선물은 모두 '미래'의 보상이나 계획을 의미합니다. 반면 (E) 즉각적인 즐거움은 미래를 위해 참지 못하고 '현재' 취하게 되는 보상을 의미하므로 성격이 다릅니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk-for body and mind.
options: ① 기술의 발전으로 인해 전통적인 생계 수단이 다시 각광받고 있다.
② 오늘날 많은 사람들이 사랑하지 않는 일을 하며 살아가고 있다.
③ 기술 발전으로 생긴 새로운 일자리는 대부분 안전하다.
④ 대중 교육과 미디어는 저기술 신체 노동을 장려한다.
⑤ 고임금 직업의 좌식 생활 방식은 건강에 해롭지 않다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for.'라고 언급되어 있으므로 오늘날 많은 사람들이 자신이 사랑하지 않는 일을 하며 살아가고 있다는 2번 보기가 지문의 내용과 일치합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 Lilian Bland에 관해 알 수 있는 것으로 가장 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Lilian Bland was born in Kent, England in 1878. Unlike most other girls at the time she wore trousers and spent her time enjoying adventurous activities like horse riding and hunting. Lilian began her career as a sports and wildlife photographer for British newspapers. In 1910 she became the first woman to design, build, and fly her own airplane. In order to persuade her to try a slightly safer activity, Lilian's dad bought her a car. Soon Lilian was a master driver and ended up working as a car dealer. She never went back to flying but lived a long and exciting life nonetheless. She married, moved to Canada, and had a kid. Eventually, she moved back to England, and lived there for the rest of her life.
options: ① Before her aviation achievements, Lilian worked as a sports and wildlife photographer for British newspapers.
② Lilian was the first woman to create, construct and fly her own airplane in the 1900s.
③ To encourage her to pursue a safer activity, Lilian's father bought her a car, which led her to become a skilled driver and car dealer.
④ Regretting that she could no longer fly, Lilian moved to Canada to resume her flying career.
⑤ Lilian returned to the place where she was born and spent the rest of her life there.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 Lilian Bland는 결코 비행으로 돌아가지 않았으며(She never went back to flying), 캐나다로 이주하여 결혼하고 아이를 가졌다고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 비행 경력을 재개하기 위해 캐나다로 갔다는 ④번은 사실과 다릅니다.
options_translation: 항공 분야의 성취를 이루기 전, Lilian은 영국 신문사의 스포츠 및 야생 동물 사진작가로 일했다.
Lilian은 1900년대에 자신의 비행기를 설계, 제작하고 비행한 최초의 여성이었다.
더 안전한 활동을 하도록 권장하기 위해, Lilian의 아버지는 그녀에게 차를 사주었고, 이는 그녀가 숙련된 운전사이자 자동차 딜러가 되는 계기가 되었다.
더 이상 비행할 수 없음을 후회하며, Lilian은 비행 경력을 재개하기 위해 캐나다로 이주했다.
Lilian은 자신이 태어난 곳으로 돌아와 그곳에서 여생을 보냈다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: American jazz pianist Bill Evans was born in New Jersey in 1929. His early training was in classical music. At the age of six, he began ⓐ<u>receiving</u> piano lesson, later adding flute and violin. He earned bachelor's degrees in piano and music education from Southeastern Louisiana College in 1950. He went on to ⓑ<u>serve</u> in the army from 1951 to 1954 and played flute in the Fifth Army Band. After serving in the military, he studied composition at the Mannes School of Music in New York. Composer George Russell ⓒ<u>disdained</u> his playing and hired Evans to record and perform his compositions. Evans became ⓓ<u>renowned</u> for recordings made from the late-1950s through the 1960s. He won his first Grammy Award in 1964 for his album Conversations with Myself. Evans' expressive piano works and his unique harmonic approach ⓔ<u>captivated</u> a whole generation of musicians.
questions.explanation: 작곡가 George Russell은 Bill Evans의 연주를 '무시(disdained)'한 것이 아니라 그의 연주에 감탄하여 그를 고용했어야 문맥이 자연스럽습니다. 원문에서는 'admired' 또는 이와 유사한 긍정적인 단어가 사용되는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful ______________________. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
options: ② in fostering self-doubt when not genuine
⑤ for boosting your child's self-worth
questions.explanation: 이 글은 칭찬이 아이의 자아상(self-image)에 어떻게 영향을 미치는지를 설명하고 있습니다. 부모의 칭찬을 그대로 받아들인 아이는 자신을 똑똑하거나 도움을 주는 사람으로 인식하게 되어 더 노력하고 자신감을 얻게 된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 칭찬은 아이의 행동을 개선할 뿐만 아니라 자존감(self-worth)을 높여주는 데에도 강력한 도구라는 흐름이 되어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 잘못된 인식을 만드는 데
② 진실되지 않을 때 자기 의심을 키우는 데
③ 그것을 통제하는 데
④ 나쁜 습관을 막는 데
⑤ 당신 아이의 자존감을 높이는 데

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. ⓐPhysically, animal cartoon characters and toys often exhibit human-like facial features and have their front limbs deformed to resemble human hands, enhancing their resemblance to humans. ⓑThis effect is achieved by displaying their unique characteristics of animals, in a newly discovered species of fish from the Amazon, known for its vibrant colors and unusual patterns. ⓒIn more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. ⓓHowever, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one pay), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. ⓔA general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.explanation: 지문의 주제는 동물을 의인화(인간의 언어 사용, 신체적 특징의 인간화)하여 인간과 닮게 만드는 전략에 대한 것입니다. 하지만 ⓑ는 아마존에서 새로 발견된 물고기 종의 고유한 특징(색상, 패턴)에 대해 설명하고 있어, 인간의 특징을 동물에게 투영한다는 전체 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound?
ordered_passages: (A) Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood.(B) The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer.(C) And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 숲에서 나무가 쓰러질 때 들을 사람이 없다면 소리가 나는가에 대한 유명한 질문입니다. (B)에서 그에 대한 정답은 '아니오'이며 듣는 사람이 없으면 소리도 없음을 설명합니다. (C)에서는 이와 유사하게(And similarly) 과학적 의사소통도 수신자가 이해하지 못하면 무용지물이라는 비유를 듭니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 '따라서(Thus)' 과학 실험은 결과가 출판되고 이해될 때까지 완성된 것이 아니라는 결론(과학의 원리)을 내리는 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 영영풀이에서 설명하고 있는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: 1. an unfair feeling of dislike for a person or group because of race, gender, religion, etc.2. a preconceived opinion that is not based on reason or actual experience3. to have a negative impact on someone's position, chances etc.
questions.explanation: 인종, 성별, 종교 등으로 인한 불공평한 싫어함, 이유나 실제 경험에 근거하지 않은 사전에 형성된 의견, 누군가의 위치나 기회에 부정적인 영향을 주는 것 등은 모두 '편견'을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 논쟁
② 후회
③ 편견
④ 합의
⑤ 타협

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: ␀<u>I woke up in our hotel room, it was almost midnight</u>. I didn't see my husband nor daughter. I called them, but ␁<u>I heard their phones ring in the room</u>. ␂<u>Feeling worried, I went outside and walked down the street</u>, but they were nowhere to be found. When I decided I should ask someone for help, a crowd nearby caught my attention. ␃<u>I approached, hoping to find my husband and daughter</u>, and suddenly I saw two familiar faces. I smiled, feeling calm. Just then, my daughter saw me and called, -Mom!- They were watching the magic show. Finally, ␄<u>I felt that all my worries disappeared</u>.
questions.explanation: ①번 문장 'I woke up in our hotel room, it was almost midnight'는 두 개의 완전한 절이 접속사 없이 콤마로만 연결되어 있어 어법상 틀립니다. 콤마 대신 접속사 and를 쓰거나, 분사구문 혹은 관계부사 등을 활용하여 연결해야 합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 computerized society에 대한 글쓴이는 태도로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The promise of a <u>computerized society</u>, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Companies large and small have off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
questions.explanation: 글쓴이는 컴퓨터화된 사회가 인간에게 더 많은 여가 시간을 줄 것이라는 약속과 달리, 오히려 기업들이 해야 할 일을 소비자에게 떠넘겨 우리가 더 바빠졌다고 지적하고 있습니다. 따라서 컴퓨터화된 사회의 결과에 대해 '비판적인(critical)' 태도를 취하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 중립적인
② 비판적인
③ 무관심한
④ 지지하는
⑤ 동정적인

questions.question: 19. 다음 굸의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 비성 (A), (B)에 들어갈 만로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the -Lake Wobegon effect,- after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where -the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average.- A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
questions.summary_sentence: People tend to (A)_____________ themselves in terms of (B)_____________ attributes.
questions.explanation: 이 굸은 사띌들이 자신의 사회적으로 바람직한 특성에 대해 평균 이상이라고 믿는 경향(레이크 워비건 효과)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 사띌들은 자신을 개과평가(overestimate)하는 경향이 있으며, 이는 바람직한(admirable) 속성에 대한 것입니다.
options_translation: ① 관통하다 - 점경할 만한
② 개과평가하다 - 꺼리는
③ 개과평가하다 - 점경할 만한
④ 개소평가하다 - 꺼리는
⑤ 개소평가하다 - 점경할 만한

questions.question: 20. 다음 굸의 문줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 문맥사 다른 의미를 갖는 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is ①<u>time pressure</u>. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had ②<u>a faster pace of life</u> - which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling ③<u>a constant sense of urgency</u>, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity ④<u>creates wealth</u>, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when ⑤<u>they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves</u>.
questions.explanation: 이 굸은 부유한 국가에서 내타나는 '시간 압박'과 그로 인한 스트레스를 다루고 있습니다. ①(time pressure), ②(a faster pace of life), ③(a constant sense of urgency), ⑤(lack the time to relax) 모두 시간이 부족하고 섑두르는 상황을 나타내지만, ④(creates wealth)는 부를 창출한다는 경제적 결과를 의미하므로 문맥사 성격이 다립니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
options: ① Possession of high-level ability creates a desire for connection in others.
② The number of social media followers is a true indicator of professional success.
③ Celebrity endorsements are entirely based on product knowledge.
④ People admire professionals not for their skills, but for their fashion sense.
⑤ High performance in one area has no impact on how others perceive you.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 특정 분야에서 똰나한 능력을 갖춰 전문가가 타인에게 신뢰를 얻고, 사람들이 그들과 연결되고 싶어한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '고도의 능력 소유는 타인에게 연결에 대한 욕구를 만들어낸다'는 ①번이 가장 적절한 요지입니다.
options_translation: 고도의 능력 소유는 타인에게 연결에 대한 욕구를 만들어낸다.
소셜 미디어 팔로워 수는 전문적인 경제적 성공의 진정한 지표이다.
유명 인사의 광고 협찬은 전적으로 셈품 지식에 기반한다.
사람들은 전문가를 그들의 기술이 아닌 패섘 감각 땄문에 점감한다.
한 분야에서의 똰나한 성과는 다른 사람들이 당신을 인식하는 방식에 영향을 미치지 않는다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. ⓐThe producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. ⓑNo longer the -Soul of Bread,- the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. ⓒAnother health benefit of wholegrain bread has been found owing to the hightened demand for superfood. ⓓShortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. ⓔRepositioning yeast helped increase sales.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 Fleischmann's 효모가 시장 사황에 맞겜 광고 전략(블타민 공급원, 천연 배변 원활제)을 바꾸어 판매를 짝대시킨 사례를 설명하고 있습니다. ⓒ번은 통곡물 빵의 건강상 이점에 대해 언급하고 있어, 효모 광고 전략과는 관련이 없습니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 묑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 숬임이 적절하준 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, which then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel ⓐ<u>accordingly</u>. As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you.- If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler has been ⓑ<u>transmitted</u> via our body. ⓒ<u>Strange</u> as it may sound, this theory states that emotions arise from our bodies. For example, our mood can be improved by simply lifting up the corners of our mouth. If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, taking care not to let the pencil touch their lips (thus forcing the mouth into a smile-like shape), they judge cartoons ⓓ<u>boring</u> than if they have been asked to frown. The ⓔ<u>primacy</u> of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase -I must be afraid, because I'm running.-
questions.explanation: 이 글은 신체 표현(미서) 등이 감정에 영향을 미츜다는 내용입니다. 연필을 물어 억지로 미서 지은 표정을 만들게 하면, 인상을 쓰게 한 집단보다 만화림 더 재미있게(funnier/more amusing) 판단하게 됩니다. 따라서 boring(지루한)은 문맥상 적절하준 않습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 흤름상 비탌 (A), (B)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 표현을 영어로 쓰시오. (단, 반드시 주어진 찠자로 완성하시오.)
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's (A)_________ - e_________. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive (B)s_________ to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his image of the self. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
subjective_conditions: 반드시 주어진 찠자로 완성할 것
questions.explanation: 문맥상 (A)는 자아 이미지와 자신감에 괐련된 단어인 'self-esteem(자존감)'이 들어가얼 하면, (B)는 분석적으로 쵔론하여 거짓 정밴림 거를 수 있는 인지적 '정교함' 또는 '섙숙도'림 뜻하는 'sophistication'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 주어진 문장 다음에 이어질 (A)~(F)를 읽고, 흐름상 글의 순서를 차례대로 바르게 쓰시오. [3.4점]
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city.
ordered_passages: (A) And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation.
(B) There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
(C) If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question.

(D) Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons.
(E) In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly.
(F) Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers.
questions.explanation: 뇌를 도시로 비유하며 시작합니다. (C) 도시의 경제가 어디에 위치하는지 묻는다면 답이 없다는 질문을 던지고, (F) 대신 모든 요소의 상호작용에서 경제가 나타난다고 설명합니다. (A) 이와 같이 뇌도 한 곳에서 일어나는 것이 아니며 고립되어 작동하지 않음을 설명합니다. (E) 뇌와 도시 모두 상호작용에서 결과가 나온다는 공통점을 정리합니다. (D) 기차가 물자를 실어오듯 뉴런을 통해 신호가 운반된다는 비유를 들고, (B) 그 신호가 거기서 처리되어 의식적 현실로 바뀐다는 결론으로 이어집니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에 드러난 'she'의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An airplane flew high above the deep blue seas far from any land. Flying the small plane was a student pilot who was sitting alongside an experienced flight instructor. As the student looked out the window, she was filled with wonder and appreciation for the beauty of the world. Her instructor, meanwhile, waited patiently for the right time to start a surprise flight emergency training exercise. When the plane hit a bit of turbulence, the instructor pushed a hidden button. Suddenly, all the monitors inside the plane flashed several times then went out completely! Now the student was in control of an airplane that was flying well, but she had no indication of where she was or where she should go. She did have a map, but no other instruments. She was at a loss and then the plane shook again. When the student began to panic, there was a loud bang.
questions.explanation: 'she'(학생 조종사)는 처음에 비행기 창밖의 아름다운 풍경을 보며 감탄(wonder and appreciation)을 느꼈으므로 'impressed'의 상태였습니다. 그러나 교관의 비상 훈련 시작으로 계기판이 꺼지고 비행기가 흔들리며 패닉에 빠지는 상황(at a loss, panic)이 되었으므로 'embarrassed' 또는 'nervous' 상태로 변화했습니다. 가장 적절한 선택지는 ①번입니다. (참고: embarrassed는 당황한, 어찌할 바를 모르는 상태를 의미함)
options_translation: ① 감명받은 → 당황한
② 즐거운 → 짜증난
③ 즐거운 → 안도하는
④ 매우 기쁜 → 침착한
⑤ 우울한 → 불안한

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흠름감 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: There are two particular types of praise, unlabeled(general) and labeled(specific) praise. While both unlabeled and labeled praises are good for children and add to the warmth of the parent-child relationship, labeled praises are particularly valuable teaching tools. ⓐLabeled praises are more efficient than unlabeled praises at conveying to the child exactly what can be said or done to earn praise in the future. ⓑParents are not encouraged to use strategies such as ignoring and praise as such methods might undermine kids' independence. ⓒAlthough praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. ⓓPreschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. ⓔThey do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information; thus, if a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image.*profound: 뜻 깊은 **sophistication: 정교화(함)
questions.explanation: 이 글은 아이들에게 칭찬, 특히 구체적인 칭찬(labeled praise)가 어떤 긱정적인 영향을 미치는지에 대해 설명하고 있다. 그러나 ⓑ번 문장은 칭찬이 아이의 독립성을 해칠 수 있으므로 권장되지 않는다는 내용으로, 글의 전체적인 흠름에서 벗어난다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Chess masters ␀<u>are shown</u> a chess board in the middle of a game for 5 seconds with 20 to 30 pieces still in play can immediately reproduce the position of the pieces from memory. Beginners, of course, are able to place only a few. Now take the same pieces and ␁<u>place</u> them on the board randomly and the difference is much reduced. The expert's advantage is only for familiar patterns - those previously ␂<u>stored</u> in memory. Faced with unfamiliar patterns, even when it involves the same familiar domain, the expert's advantage disappears. The beneficial effects of familiar structure on memory ␃<u>has</u> been observed for many types of expertise, including music. People with musical training can reproduce short sequences of musical notation more accurately than ␄<u>those</u> with no musical training when notes follow conventional sequences, but the advantage is much reduced when the notes are ordered randomly. Expertise also improves memory for sequences of movements. Experienced ballet dancers are able to repeat longer sequences of steps than less experienced dancers, and they can repeat a sequence of steps ␅<u>making</u> up a routine better than steps ordered randomly. In each case, memory range is increased by the ability ␆<u>to recognize</u> familiar sequences and patterns.
questions.explanation: ␀: 전체 문장의 본동사가 can immediately reproduce이므로 주어 Chess masters를 수식하는 분사가 필요합니다. are shown이 아니라 shown으로 써야 합니다. ␃: 주어는 The beneficial effects(복수)이므로 has를 have로 고쳐야 합니다. 나머지 ␁(명령문), ␂(수동 의미의 과거분사), ␄(people을 지칭하는 대명사), ␅(능동 의미의 현재분사), ␆(ability를 수식하는 to부정사)는 모두 옳습니다. 틀린 것은 ␀, ␃ 2개입니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. (A) During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. (B) World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled. (C) We are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. (D) Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. (E) Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.insertion_sentence: This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'This'는 앞 문장에 언급된 농경지 토양이 단일 재배 성장을 위한 완벽한 환경이 되도록 강요받는 상태를 가리킵니다. 이것이 '비료'와 '관개'를 통해 달성된다는 설명 뒤에, (A) 문장에서 비료와 물(both)을 공급하는 데 효율적이 되었다는 내용이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. (A) During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. (B) The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. (C) Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. (D) When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. (E) When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small, and in such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
questions.insertion_sentence: This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 원자들이 함께 모여 더 큰 결정을 형성할 충분한 시간을 갖기 때문에 발생하는 결과에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 (D) 문장에서 언급된 '마그마가 천천히 식을 때 육안으로 볼 수 있을 만큼 큰 결정이 형성된다'는 내용에 대한 구체적인 이유이므로, (D) 뒤인 (E) 자리에 위치하여 '천천히 식는 경우'에 대한 설명을 마무리하고, 그 다음 문장에서 '빠르게 식는 경우'를 대조적으로 설명하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 Brainwriting에 대한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ① 처음에는 조원들이 아이디어를 개별적으로 제시한다.
② 각자 제시한 아이디어를 모아 익명으로 조원들과 공유한다.
③ 수합한 아이디어에서 자기 것을 제외한 나머지를 개별적으로 평가한다.
④ 평가가 끝난 후 조원들이 모여 좋은 의견을 고르고 다듬는다.
⑤ 집단 지성이 필요할 때 특히 효과적이다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'each member evaluates them on their own'이라고 언급하며 각 구성원이 아이디어들을 스스로 평가한다고 설명할 뿐, 수합된 아이디어 중 자신의 것을 제외하고 평가해야 한다는 조건은 언급되지 않았습니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives _______________ in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 글은 어린 시절(유년기)의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 유년기가 짧고 본능(hardware)에만 의존하는 동물은 환경 변화에 유연하지 못한 반면, 유년기가 긴 동물은 부모로부터 문화적 정보를 습득하여 변화하는 환경에 더 효율적으로 대응할 수 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 유년기는 변화하는 세상에서의 '적응성(adaptability)'을 부여한다는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 용기
② 안정성
③ 인내
④ 적응성
⑤ 책임감

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to __________________. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ③ a good sense of direction
④ the reshaping of the brain
⑤ the formation of new brain cells
questions.explanation: 지문은 집중된 주의가 뇌의 물리적 구조를 변화시킨다는 증거를 제시하고 있습니다. 소리에 집중하는 동물은 청각 센터가 커지고, 바이올린 연주자는 왼손 담당 피질 영역이 확장되며, 택시 운전사는 해마가 커진다는 예시는 모두 뇌의 구조적 변화를 의미하므로 'the reshaping of the brain(뇌의 재형성)'이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 향상된 기억력
② 더 빠른 반응 시간
③ 좋은 방향 감각
④ 뇌의 재형성
⑤ 새로운 뇌세포의 형성

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
options: ① how people started to settle down
② a population explosion with farming
③ difficulties of hunter-gatherer's wandering life
④ controversy over what agriculture brought to us
⑤ the mechanism for controlling pregnancy and childbirth
questions.explanation: 놈경을 시잡하면서 정착 생활을 하게 되었고, 이로 인해 출산 간격이 줄어들어 인구가 급격히 증가하게 되었다는 내용이므로, 주제로는 ② ' 놈업과 함께 일어난 인구 폭발' 이 가장 적절합니다.

③ 수집 채집인의 방랑 생활의 어려움
④ 놈업이 우리에게 가져다 준 것에 덀한 논란
⑤ 임신과 출산을 조절하는 메캬니즘

questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with ⓐ<u>it</u>. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, (A)<u>그리고 그 후에 학생들은 그에 대한 인상을 말하도록 요청받았다</u>. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon ⓑ<u>their original information of the lecturer</u>. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 '그것과 어울리는 다른 특징들'에서 'it'은 앞에서 언급된 '한 가지 유형의 특징(one type of characteristic)'을 가리킵니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 <조건>에 맞춰 물음에 답하시오.
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for <u>social evidence</u>. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environmental can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to adopt the practices of those around you.Q. Suppose that you are going to buy a TV. You have two options. The two TVs are almost similar in the function and cost except the following features. You are uncertain about what to buy. Which one will you buy?- TV A: fine design, available in various colors / sales: 10- TV B: from a large company / sales: 3,000
subjective_conditions: 1. 주어진 단어(I should buy / because)를 포함하여 영어 문장으로 작성하시오.
2. 밑줄 친 'social evidence'를 바탕으로 선택한 제품과 그 이유를 설명할 것
3. 단어 'people'을 포함하여 작성할 것
4. 지문의 4단어 이상을 연속으로 차용하지 말 것
questions.answer: I should buy TV B because people feel safe and secure in numbers when purchasing products.
questions.explanation: 사회적 증거(social evidence)란 타인의 행동을 보고 결정을 내리는 것이 생존과 안전에 도움이 된다고 믿는 것입니다. 따라서 판매량이 훨씬 많은 TV B를 선택하는 것이 지문의 논리에 부합합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.
options: ① 시인에게 꼤에서 얻는 시적 영감은 중요하다.
③ 갑작스러운 방해는 좂종 삶에서 유익할 수 있다.
④ 일상의 방해는 때때로 문학적 요서로 발전될 수 있다.
⑤ 갑작스러운 방해는 누구에게나 부정적인 결과로 이어질 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 글은 갑작스러운 방해(interruption)가 문학가에게 영감을 잃겐 하고 전문직 종사자들에게 치명적인 결과를 초래하며, 일반인들에게도 생산성 저하와 스트레스를 유발한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 갑작스러운 방해가 부정적인 영향을 미친다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 요지입니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 묑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 슬임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding ①<u>nutrients</u> in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more ②<u>efficient</u> at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World ③<u>usage</u> of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural ④<u>desirables</u>. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are ⑤<u>desired</u> as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.explanation: 농경지의 풍부한 영양분겼 수분은 잡초와 같은 '바람직하지 않은 것들' 또는 '해충들'의 관심을 끌겐 합니다. 따라서 'desirables(바람직한 것들)'은 'undesirables(바람직하지 않은 것들)'로 고쳐앴 합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. (A) In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. (B) A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. (C) A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. (D) When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. (E) The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 인터넷과 전기가 환경에 미치는 비용(영향)이 무시되고 있다는 내용입니다. (B)까지는 종이 절약을 통해 환경을 보호하려는 긍정적인 변화를 설명하고 있고, (C) 이후부터는 데이터 센터의 화석 연료 사용, 탄소 배출 등 디지털 활동이 환경에 미치는 부정적인 실태를 구체적으로 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 긍정적 측면에서 부정적 측면으로 화제가 전환되는 (C) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with __________. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.explanation: 지문의 뒷부분에서 청각 장애가 있거나, 시각 장애가 있는 사람들, 또는 특정 색상을 구별하는 데 어려움이 있는 사람들을 언급하고 있으며, 마지막 문장에서 'those with disabilities(장애가 있는 사람들)'의 요구를 충족시켜야 한다고 결론짓고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 'disability(장애)'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 장애
② 재능
③ 창의성
④ 행운
⑤ 근면

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve?
ordered_passages: (A) And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.

(B) One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage.

(C) The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it.
questions.explanation: 인간 정신의 진화 과정을 묻는 질문에 대해, (B)에서 다른 부족과의 경쟁과 갈등을 원인으로 제시하며 시작합니다. (C)에서는 적의 공격을 예측하고 계획하는 구체적인 정신적 이점이 군사적 우위와 생존의 무기가 되었음을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 이점이 세대를 거듭하며 유전적으로 전달되어 우리가 승리자의 후손이 되었음을 결론짓는 (B)-(C)-(A) 순서가 가장 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 19. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: All humans, to an extent, seek activities that ______________________________. The key is that it is a '<u>safe threat</u>'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a '<u>safe threat</u>' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment. This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure. All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is to have the pain always directly associated with a pleasurable reward.
options: ① give pain to others to feel pleasure
② help them avoid pain to seek pleasure
③ make happiness in pain without a safe context
④ provide painful experiences without any enjoyment
⑤ generate pain in order to enjoy succeeding pleasure
questions.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 인간이 실제 위험이 없는 '안전한 위협' 상황에서 고통스러운 자극을 통해 즐거움을 느낀다는 것입니다. 매운 고추를 먹는 것처럼 뇌는 위험 신호를 보내지만 실제로는 안전하다는 것을 알 때 오는 보상감이 즐거움을 유발하므로, 뒤따르는 즐거움을 위해 고통을 생성한다는 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 즐거움을 느끼기 위해 타인에게 고통을 주다
② 즐거움을 찾기 위해 고통을 피하도록 돕다
③ 안전한 상황 없이 고통 속에서 행복을 만들다
④ 즐거움 없이 고통스러운 경험을 제공하다
⑤ 뒤따르는 즐거움을 즐기기 위해 고통을 발생시키다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① Brain Adaptations: Not Yet Identified by Science
② Violin Practice Reduces Brain Growth in the Cortex
③ Focused Attention: Harmful for Auditory Centers in the Brain Neural Remodeling: How Attention Transforms Brain Structure
④ Neural Remodeling: How Attention Transforms Brain Structure
⑤ The Fixed Brain Architecture: Result from Practicing Attention
questions.explanation: 지문은 우리가 어디에 주의를 기울이고 무엇을 연습하는지에 따라 뇌의 물리적 구조가 변한다는 과학적 증거들(청각 중심지, 시각 영역, 바이올린 연주자의 피질, 택시 운전사의 해마 등)을 나열하고 있습니다. 따라서 '신경 재구성: 주의력이 뇌 구조를 어떻게 바꾸는가'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌 적응: 과학에 의해 아직 확인되지 않음
② 바이올린 연습은 피질의 뇌 성장을 감소시킨다
③ 집중된 주의력: 뇌의 청각 중심지에 해롭다
④ 신경 재구성: 주의력이 뇌 구조를 어떻게 바꾸는가
⑤ 고정된 뇌 구조: 주의력을 연습한 결과

questions.question: [22~23] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.22. 윗글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어가기에 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: [가] Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future ⓐ<u>one</u>. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present ⓑ<u>one</u>. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.[나] For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for ⓒ<u>the greatest benefit</u> but then act differently when temptation for ⓓ<u>immediate pleasure</u> appears.
questions.summary_sentence: Both humans and animals often (A)__________ resources for future use, but sometimes they are (B)__________ by immediate desires, revealing a weakness of will.
questions.explanation: 인간과 동물은 미래를 위해 자원을 (A)비축(reserve/save/set aside)하지만, 때때로 즉각적인 욕구에 의해 (B)매료/유혹(fascinated/tempted)되어 의지의 박약함을 드러낸다는 내용이 적절합니다. 본문에서 'save' 또는 'set aside'는 'reserve'와 유의어이며, 'temptation'은 'fascinated'나 'tempted'와 연결됩니다. 선택지 중 ②번이 가장 적절한 쌍입니다.

② (A) 비축하다 / (B) 매료된
③ (A) 끌어내다 / (B) 유혹된
④ (A) 따로 떼어두다 / (B) 고갈된
⑤ (A) 미루다 / (B) 구별된

④ 따로 떼어 두다 - 고갈된

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ, ⓑ가 각각 지칭하는 한 단어를 [가] 단락에서 찾고, <보기>의 표현을 사용하여 각각 한 문장으로 서술하시오.
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future ⓐ<u>one</u>. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present ⓑ<u>one</u>. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for ⓒ<u>the greatest benefit</u> but then act differently when temptation for ⓓ<u>immediate pleasure</u> appears.
subjective_conditions: 문장 전체를 작성하지 않을 경우 점수 없음
questions.answer: ⓐ refers to pleasureⓑ refers to reward
questions.explanation: ⓐ는 'future one'으로 언급되었으며, 앞 문맥의 'immediate pleasure'와 대조되어 미래의 'pleasure'를 가리킵니다. ⓑ는 'present one'으로 언급되었으며, 앞 문맥의 'future reward'와 대조되어 현재의 'reward'를 가리킵니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓒ, ⓓ가 각각 의미하는 예시를 [나] 단락에서 연속된 두 단어로 찾고, <보기>의 표현을 사용하여 각각 한 문장으로 서술하시오.
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future ⓐ<u>one</u>. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present ⓑ<u>one</u>. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for ⓒ<u>the greatest benefit</u> but then act differently when temptation for ⓓ<u>immediate pleasure</u> appears.
subjective_conditions: 문장 전체를 작성하지 않을 경우 점수 없음
questions.answer: ⓒ means Christmas presentsⓓ means summer vacation
questions.explanation: ⓒ '가장 큰 이득'은 문맥상 원래 계획했던 장기적인 보상인 'Christmas presents'를 의미하며, ⓓ '즉각적인 즐거움'은 유혹에 빠져 미리 써버린 예시인 'summer vacation'을 의미합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 우리말 해석과 일치하도록 (A), (B)에 주어진 단어를 어법상 옳게 고치시오.
questions.passage: It seems that he was ill.= He seems to (A)<u>be</u> ill. (그는 아팠던 것처럼 보인다.)One of the (B)<u>fast</u> growing sports is baseball.(가장 빠르게 성장하는 스포츠들 중 하나는 야구이다.)
questions.explanation: (A) 주절의 시제는 현재(seems)인데 대절의 시제는 과거(was)이므로, 완료 부정사(to have p.p.)를 사용하여 시제 차이를 나타내야 하므로 'have been'이 정답입니다.(B) 'One of the + 최상급 + 복수명사' 구문이므로 형용사 fast를 최상급인 'fastest'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어가기에 가장 적절한 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. 단, 필요시 어형을 바꾸시오.
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives __________ in a changing world.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 쓸 것
필요시 어형을 바꿀 것
questions.explanation: 지문은 유년기가 환경에 적응하고 학습할 수 있는 시간을 제공한다고 설명합니다. 유년기가 없는 동물은 '덜 유연함(less flexible)'에 반해 유년기는 변화하는 세상에서 유연성을 제공한다는 맥락이 적절합니다. 본문에 형용사 형태인 'flexible'이 존재하므로, 문장의 목적어 자리에 올 수 있는 명사형 'flexibility'로 변형하여 쓰는 것이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 29. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말과 일치하도록 <보기>의 표현을 사용하여 문장을 작성하려고 한다. 주어진 조건을 충족시켜 문장을 완성하시오. [24년 6월 29번]
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and (A)<u>전염병이 처음 뿌리를 내렸던 곳은 바로 농경마을이었다.</u> Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "(B)__________."
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기> 표현들을 한 번씩 모두 사용할 것
2. 두 단어를 어법상 옳도록 바꿀 것
3. it으로 시작하는 강조 구문을 활용할 것
vocabulary_box: it / first took robot / what / in farming villages / epidemic diseases / is
questions.answer: it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root.
questions.explanation: It ~ that 강조구문을 사용하여 장소 부사구인 'in farming villages'를 강조해야 한다. 과거의 사실이므로 is를 was로, robot을 root로 어형 변화시켜 'it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root.'가 정답이 된다.

questions.question: 30. 윗글의 흐름상 빈칸 (B)에 들어가기에 가장 적절한 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 그대로 쓰시오. [24년 6월 29번]
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and (A)<u>전염병이 처음 뿌리를 내렸던 곳은 바로 농경마을이었다.</u> Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "(B)__________."
questions.explanation: 인류가 정착 생활을 하고 도시가 성장함에 따라 최종적으로 형성된 것은 정착된 '문명'이다. 지문의 맥락상 가장 적합한 단어는 civilizations이다. (참고: 원문 출처에 근거함)

questions.question: 31. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. <보기>의 표현들만 한 번씩 모두 사용하여 요약문의 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 표현을 완성하시오. 단, 밑줄 친 allow의 어형을 어법상 옳도록 바꾸시오.
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.summary_sentence: While hunter-gatherer mothers carrying their young children could only have one baby every four years, agricultural societies reducing birth intervals and _________________________________________________.
questions.answer: allowing mothers to settle in one place led to rapid population growth
questions.explanation: 제시된 글은 농경 사회가 정착 생활을 통해 출산 간격을 줄여 급격한 인구 증가를 가져왔다는 내용입니다. 요약문에서 'reducing birth intervals and ~'와 병렬 구조를 이루며 주어 역할을 할 수 있도록 'allow'를 'allowing'으로 바꾸고, 'allow + 목적어 + to부정사' 구문을 활용하여 'allowing mothers to settle in one place'를 만든 뒤, 동사구 'led to rapid population growth'를 이어 완성합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, ____________________________.
options: ① the red squirrels are in danger of extinction
② the red squirrels have a problem for humans
③ the grey squirrels look for other habitats
④ the red can have another superior feature
⑤ the red and grey can coexist with each other
questions.explanation: 외래종인 회색 다람쥐가 도입되면서 토착종인 붉은 다람쥐와 경쟁하게 되는데, 회색 다람쥐가 먹이 적응력(익지 않은 도토리 섭취 가능), 서식 밀도, 서식지 다양성 면에서 우위를 점하고 있다는 내용입니다. 회색 다람쥐가 식량을 먼저 소비하고 생존력이 더 뛰어나기 때문에, 그 결과로 토착종인 붉은 다람쥐는 개체 수가 줄어들어 멸종 위기에 처하게 된다는 흐름이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 붉은 다람쥐들은 멸종 위기에 처해 있다
② 붉은 다람쥐들은 인간에게 문제를 일으킨다
③ 회색 다람쥐들은 다른 서식지를 찾는다
④ 붉은 다람쥐는 또 다른 우수한 특징을 가질 수 있다
⑤ 붉은 다람쥐와 회색 다람쥐는 서로 공존할 수 있다

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors ____________________, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
options: ② made efforts to keep crops
③ dwelled with animals and crops
④ lived far away to cultivate crops
questions.explanation: 초기 수렵 채집인들의 유해를 조사한 결과, 우리 조상들이 과도한 노력 없이도 얻을 수 있는 식량이 풍부했고 질병도 거의 겪지 않았음을 시사한다는 내용입니다. 뒤 문장에서 농경 생활이 오히려 고된 노동과 전염병의 원인이 되었다는 점과 대조되므로, 수렵 채집 시절의 긍정적인 측면인 '풍부한 음식을 즐겼다'는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 식량 부족을 겪었다
② 작물을 지키기 위해 노력했다
③ 동물 및 작물과 함께 거주했다
④ 작물을 경작하기 위해 멀리 떨어져 살았다
⑤ 풍부한 음식을 즐겼다

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [24년 6월 31번]
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get ⓐ<u>written</u> because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 ⓑ<u>when</u> Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an ⓒ<u>unexpected</u> guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the ⓓ<u>untimely</u> visitor came at a particularly bad time. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, ⓔ<u>they</u> also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 원문에서 문법적으로 틀린 부분을 찾는 문제이나, 제공된 텍스트의 ⓒ는 'unexpected'(예상치 못한)로 어법상 및 문맥상 적절합니다. 다만 학교 시험지 편집이나 발문상의 오류 혹은 원문 변형 가능성을 고려할 때, 일반적으로 이 지문에서 출제되는 어법 포인트는 ⓔ 'they'가 가리키는 대상(sudden disruptions)과의 수 일치 등입니다. 하지만 여기서는 ③번 ⓒ가 문제의 정답으로 표기되어 있는데, 이는 원문에서 ⓒ 부분이 다른 어색한 형태(예: unexpecting)였으나 텍스트 추출 과정에서 수정되었거나 다른 의도가 있을 수 있습니다. (※실제 제공된 텍스트 상으로는 ⓐ~ⓔ 모두 문법적으로 틀린 곳이 보이지 않으나, 정답 표기에 따라 ③번을 선택합니다.)

questions.question: 9. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did.
ordered_passages: (A) The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation.(B) The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.(C) A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage.
questions.explanation: 인간의 마음이 진화한 이유가 부족 간 경쟁 때문일 수 있다는 제시문 뒤에, (C) 상대 부족보다 생각을 더 잘하는 것이 군사적 이점을 준다는 구체적인 설명이 옵니다. (A) 이러한 정신적 능력이 생존 투쟁에서 결정적인 무기가 되었고 세대를 거쳐 적용되었다는 내용으로 이어지며, (B) 마지막으로 이러한 이점을 가진 부족이 성공하여 유전자를 물려주었고 우리가 그 승리자의 후손이라는 결론으로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very ⓐ<u>inefficient</u> migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't ⓑ<u>adapt</u> easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate ⓒ<u>keep</u> flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood ⓓ<u>restrains</u> the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve ⓔ<u>faster</u> than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 유년기가 동물의 학습과 유연성에 도움이 된다는 내용입니다. 마지막 부분에서 유년기가 문화 정보의 전달을 '억제(restrains)'하는 것이 아니라 '촉진(facilitates)'하거나 '허용(allows)'한다는 맥락이 되어야 하므로 ⓓ가 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
options: ① Nonconscious behavior is a reflection of the characteristics of our innate genes.
② Conscious behavior should be considered more important than unconscious behavior.
③ Our behaviors rely on what kind of person we have around us.
④ Our behaviors change with the flow of time and social influence continually.
⑤ Our actions comes out according to the way what we are.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람의 행동이 그들의 정체성을 반영하며, 스스로를 어떤 유형의 사람으로 믿느냐에 따라 행동이 결정된다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '우리의 행동은 우리의 존재 방식에 따라 나타난다'는 의미의 ⑤번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 무의식적 행동은 우리 타고난 유전자 특성의 반영이다.
② 의식적 행동은 무의식적 행동보다 더 중요하게 고려되어야 한다.
③ 우리의 행동은 우리 주변에 어떤 종류의 사람들이 있느냐에 의존한다.
④ 우리의 행동은 시간의 흐름과 사회적 영향에 따라 계속해서 변한다.
⑤ 우리의 행동은 우리가 누구인지에 따라 나온다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

questions.question: 25. According to the context, write the appropriate words in the blanks.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 6월 29번]

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
