Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, ⓓ<u>which</u> is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice ⓔ<u>doing</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'Brain scans of violinists'이고 본동사는 'provide'입니다. 따라서 ⓒ는 문장의 본동사 자리가 아니며, 앞선 내용을 부연 설명하는 분사구문 형태가 되어야 하므로 showing으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible.
ordered_passages: (A) By comparison, migratory bird species that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily.
(B) So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps.

(C) Birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 유년기가 동물에게 환경에 대해 배울 시간을 주어 유연성을 높여준다고 언급합니다. (C)에서 유년기가 긴 새들이 더 효율적인 이주 경로를 가진다는 구체적 예시를 들며 유연성을 강조합니다. (A)에서 'By comparison'을 통해 유년기 학습 없이 본능(태어날 때의 지침)에만 의존하는 새들의 비효율성을 대조하며 설명합니다. (B)에서 'So'를 통해 앞에서 설명한 본능에 의존하는 새들이 환경 변화에 적응하지 못하고 기존의 방식을 고수한다는 결과를 제시하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. (A) Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. (B) When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. (C) Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite because they can consume green acorns, while red squirrels can only digest mature acorns. (D) Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. (E) As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
questions.insertion_sentence: That's why the grey had the edge over the red.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'the edge'는 우위를 의미합니다. 회색 다람쥐가 붉은 다람쥐보다 먹이 섭취와 서식지 적응력 등에서 우위를 점한다는 구체적인 설명이 끝난 직후인 (D) 위치에 들어가 '그래서 회색 다람쥐가 우위를 점하게 된 것이다'라고 정리해 주는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 그 결과 붉은 다람쥐가 멸종 위기에 처했다는 (E)가 이어집니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장을 고르면?
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. ⓐHighly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they prepare ahead and win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. ⓑStudies found that being a highly sensitive person is associated with higher connectedness with nature. ⓒIt's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. ⓓStrength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. ⓔHardship is not only just a lesson for the next time in front of us but it will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 쉬운 길을 택하기보다 고난과 도전을 마주함으로써 진정한 실력과 힘을 얻을 수 있다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 하지만 ②번 문장(ⓑ)은 민감한 성격의 사람이 자연과 더 높은 연결성을 갖는다는 내용으로, 도전과 성취라는 글의 핵심 주제와 전혀 관련이 없습니다.

questions.question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it.
ordered_passages: (A) If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals. Cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root.
(B) Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that they enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases.

(C) Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 수렵 채집 생활 방식의 장점을 언급합니다. (B)는 초기 수렵 채집 사회의 유해 조사를 통해 그들이 풍부한 음식을 즐기고 질병이 적었음을 구체적으로 설명하며 수렵 채집의 장점을 뒷받침합니다. (A)는 'If this is true'로 (B)의 내용을 받으며, 그렇다면 왜 인간이 농경과 정착 생활을 선택했는지 의문을 제기하고 농경의 단점(힘든 노동, 전염병)을 언급합니다. (C)는 농경 정착의 즉각적 영향이 어떠했든 간에 그것이 인구 밀도 증가와 신석기 시대라는 전환점을 가져와 문명으로 이어졌음을 설명하며 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process which can be called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by getting everyone to generate ideas as a ⓐ<u>team</u>. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve ⓑ<u>independent</u> judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to ⓒ<u>select</u> and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas ⓓ<u>individually</u> before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve ⓔ<u>collective</u> intelligence.*anonymously: 익명으로 **surface: 드러내다
questions.explanation: 브레인라이팅(brainwriting) 과정의 초기 단계는 '혼자 하는 것(solo)'이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 모든 구성원이 '팀으로서(as a team)' 아이디어를 생성하는 것이 아니라, 각자 개인적으로(as individuals 또는 independently) 아이디어를 생성해야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.summary_sentence: Transition to (A)__________ made the community settle in one area, (B)__________ the environment for shorter birth intervals and the larer population.
questions.explanation: 농경(agriculture)으로의 전환은 사람들을 한곳에 정착하게 만들었고, 이는 이동의 부담을 줄여 출산 간격을 단축시키고 인구 증가를 촉진(fostering)하는 환경을 조성했습니다. 수렵 채집 사회에서는 이동성 때문에 출산 간격이 길었으나 농경 사회는 정착 생활 덕분에 더 많은 자녀를 가질 수 있게 되었습니다.
options_translation: ① 농업 - 해를 끼치는
② 농업 - 조성하는(촉진하는)
③ 수렵 채집 - 개혁하는
④ 수렵 채집 - 발전시키는
⑤ 수렵 채집 - 파괴하는

questions.question: 3. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order.
ordered_passages: (A) In year three, the crops w ll rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. This method of farming ensures that the soil remains nourished.
(B) It also increases the productivity of agriculture. As a result, it promotes sustainable agriculture because the soil stays healthy.

(C) Imagine a farmer with three different fields, where they grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 윤작(Crop rotation)의 정의를 설명한 뒤, (C) 농부의 세 개 밭에서 당근, 콩, 토마토를 재배하는 구체적인 예시를 도입합니다. (A) 3년차와 4년차의 순환 과정을 통해 토양 영양 유지 효과를 설명하고, (B) 'It also'(그것은 또한)를 통해 생산성 증대와 지속 가능한 농업으로의 연결이라는 추가적인 이점을 언급하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 4. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike.
ordered_passages: (A) With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.

(B) For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion.

(C) Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 두 마리의 똑같은 동물은 없다는 전제를 제시하고, (C) 같은 배에서 난 동물이라도 다르며 환경적 요인이 반응을 결정한다는 설명을 덧붙입니다. (B) 그에 대한 구체적인 예시(보호소 고양이 vs 집 고양이, 신체적 vs 정서적 치유)를 들고, (A) 'With this in mind'(이 점을 명심하여)를 통해 모든 치유 세션은 개별 동물에 맞게 조정되어야 한다는 결론으로 이어집니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question: How many senses are there? About 2,370 years ago, Aristotle claimed there were five senses in both humans and animals: sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, philosopher Fiona Macpherson suggests reasons to doubt this. For one, Aristotle overlooked some senses in humans: the awareness of your own body that is separate from the sense of touch, and the sense of balance that is related to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. A variety of vertebrates have an alternative system for detecting odors, and some snakes can sense the body heat of their prey. These examples indicate that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of fitting animal senses into Aristotelian categories, we should study them as they truly are.
options: ① It is important to interpret various sensory experiences properly.
② We should investigate how cultural background shapes individuals' perceptions.
③ The role of technology is significant in investigating the evolution of sensory perception.
④ Different species have adapted to survive their environment and they should be studied individually.
⑤ The traditional classification of five senses is inadequate and senses should be examined in their unique contexts.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 전통적인 '5감' 분류가 인간과 동물의 다양한 감각(고유 수용성 감각, 평형 감각, 열 감지 등)을 모두 포괄하지 못한다는 점을 비판하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 '감각을 기존의 카테고리에 끼워 맞추는 대신, 있는 그대로 연구해야 한다'고 강조하고 있으므로 ⑤번이 필자의 주장으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 다양한 감각 경험을 적절하게 해석하는 것이 중요하다.
문화적 배경이 개인의 지각을 어떻게 형성하는지 조사해야 한다.
감각 지각의 진화를 조사하는 데 있어 기술의 역할이 중요하다.
다른 종들은 환경에서 살아남기 위해 적응해 왔으며 개별적으로 연구되어야 한다.
전통적인 5감 분류는 불충분하며 감각은 그들의 고유한 문맥에서 조사되어야 한다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
options: ① The norms for the same situation may vary from culture to culture
② It is common to express gratitude for even the smallest things in all cultures.
③ The norm is bound by the law which is indispensable for maintaining social order.
④ It was impossible for primitive tribal societies to maintain order without any particular norms.
⑤ Even if people don't know the norms of other communities, they don't have difficulties in communicating between cultures.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사회적 규범이 문화마다 다를 수 있음을 강조합니다. 영국계 사회에서는 사소한 도움에도 '감사합니다'라고 말하는 것이 규범이지만, 다른 문화에서는 상당한 도움이 있을 때만 감사를 표하는 것이 규범일 수 있다는 예시를 통해, 동일한 상황이라도 문화에 따라 규범이 달라질 수 있음을 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 같은 상황에 대한 규범은 문화마다 다를 수 있다.
② 모든 문화에서 아주 사소한 일에도 감사를 표하는 것이 일반적이다.
③ 규범은 사회 질서 유지에 필수적인 법에 의해 구속된다.
④ 특별한 규범 없이 원시 부족 사회가 질서를 유지하는 것은 불가능했다.
⑤ 다른 공동체의 규범을 모르더라도 문화 간 의사소통에는 어려움이 없다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① Leaders tend to be reluctant to have internal dissenters.
② The role of leaders is to establish a culture of cooperation.
③ Good leaders must be open to opposing opinions and criticism.
④ Respectable leaders have their own distinctive management philosophy.
⑤ Leaders should facilitate within-group agreements to achieve common goals.
questions.explanation: 지문은 존경받는 리더들이 구성원의 이의 제기를 억압하기보다 오히려 장려한다는 점을 강조합니다. 특히 마지막 문장에서 반대자들의 말을 경청함으로써 진정으로 해야 할 일이 무엇인지 배울 수 있다고 언급하며 내부 반대 의견 수용의 중요성을 설파하고 있으므로, ③번이 정답으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 리더들은 내부 반대자들을 두는 것을 꺼리는 경향이 있다.
② 리더의 역할은 협력의 문화를 구축하는 것이다.
③ 훌륭한 리더는 반대 의견과 비판에 개방적이어야 한다.
④ 존경받는 리더는 그들만의 독특한 경영 철학을 갖고 있다.
⑤ 리더는 공통의 목표 달성을 위해 집단 내 합의를 촉진해야 한다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than ⓐ <u>concentrating</u> on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered by "finished." Artists often find it ⓑ<u>difficulty</u> to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is crucial to step back and ⓒ<u>evaluate</u> the painting's development every now and then. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking ⓓ<u>overworked</u>. If you find yourself struggling to decide if you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide ⓔ<u>whether</u> any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation: ⓑ 'find' 동사의 가목적어-목적보어 구문입니다. 'Artists(주어) often find(동사) it(가목적어) difficulty(목적보어)' 구조에서 목적보어 자리에는 형용사가 와야 하므로 명사인 'difficulty'를 형용사인 'difficult'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 문장은?
questions.passage: ⓐA group of psychologists studied severe mental patients who experienced weekly group music therapy, which included singing familiar songs and composing original songs. ⓑThe results showed the quality if participants' life was improved by the group music therapy. ⓒEspecially, those who participated in a greater number of sessions experienced the greatest benefits. ⓓWhile focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals live with a mental health condition in a community setting. ⓔThe findings showed that when participating in a choir, people with mental health conditions felt their state of mind and wellbeing significantly improved. Improving emotional states, developing a sense of belonging and enhancing self-confidence were the advantages of group singing.
questions.explanation: ⓓ 문장에서 'for individuals'를 수식하는 부분이 'live with ~'인데, 'individuals'가 직접 거주하는 능동의 관계이므로 동사 'live'를 현재분사인 'living'으로 고쳐 수식해야 어법상 자연스럽습니다. 문장 내에 이미 'reviewed'라는 본동사가 존재하므로 접속사 없이 동사가 또 올 수 없습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings─work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① tips for succeeding in the workplace
② balancing between work and personal life
③ significance of types of jobs in life satisfaction
④ effect of job satisfaction on overall happiness in life
⑤ ways to greatly improve a sense of fulfillment in work
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 일과 직업적 성취감이 개인의 행복에 미치는 긍정적인 영향을 다루고 있습니다. 여러 연구 결과를 통해 직무 만족도가 높은 사람들이 전반적인 삶에서도 더 행복해질 가능성이 크다는 점을 강조하고 있으므로 정답은 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 직장에서 성공하기 위한 비결
② 일과 개인 생활 사이의 균형
③ 인생 만족도에서 직업 유형의 중요성
④ 직무 만족도가 삶의 전반적인 행복에 미치는 영향
⑤ 업무에서 성취감을 크게 향상시키는 방법

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 ㎞) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① how the Incan messengers did their roles
② running as a sport enjoyed by many Incas
③ main cause of the decline of Incan civilization
④ forms of houses widely popular in the Inca empire
⑤ essential requirements to become a messenger in the Inca empire
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잉카 제국의 전령인 'Chasquis'가 어떤 방식으로 배치되어 소식을 전달했는지 그 시스템과 역할을 상세히 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 잉카 전령들이 그들의 역할을 수행한 방식인 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 잉카 전령들이 그들의 역할을 수행한 방식
② 많은 잉카인들이 즐겼던 스포츠로서의 달리기
③ 잉카 문명 쇠퇴의 주요 원인
④ 잉카 제국에서 널리 인기 있었던 집의 형태
⑤ 잉카 제국에서 전령이 되기 위한 필수 요건

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. ⓐIf you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. ⓑBut like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. ⓒLikewise, the leaders were extraordinary unlike common people. ⓓThrough diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. ⓔThus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 위대한 리더들도 시작은 우리와 같은 평범한 사람들이었으며, 누구나 리더가 될 잠재력이 있다는 것입니다. 따라서 리더가 일반인과 달리 비범했다는 내용의 ⓒ는 전체 흐름에 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine ______________________________________. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street─ a motorist simply has less time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites: while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① the distance they are moving
② the movement of the surrounding creatures
③ the ability to adapt to evolutionary progress
④ the development of various types of transportation
⑤ the capacity to deal with environmental information
questions.explanation: 글의 내용은 이동 속도가 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력에 영향을 미친다는 것입니다. 걷는 속도(시속 5마일 이하)일 때 상세한 파악이 가장 잘 되며, 자동차처럼 빠를 때는 그 능력이 제한된다고 설명하므로, 이동 속도가 '환경 정보를 처리하는 능력'을 결정한다는 내용이 빈칸에 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이동하는 거리
② 주변 생명체들의 움직임
③ 진화적 진보에 적응하는 능력
④ 다양한 교통 수단의 발달
⑤ 환경 정보를 처리하는 능력

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with get up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, _________________________________. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act.
options: ① you can have more tough challenges
② prepare to be amazed by the magic and confidence
③ get ready to experience relazation and calmness in your mind
④ you will have to consider the difficulty of the trick of magic
⑤ start to train yourself to write appropriate statements about your challenges
questions.explanation: 직면한 과제(challenges)를 긍정적인 진술(positive statements)로 바꾸어 적음으로써 생각과 행동의 변화를 일으키는 '마법'을 경험하라는 내용입니다. 따라서 긍정적 문장을 작성한 후 '마법과 자신감에 놀랄 준비를 하라'는 내용이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 더 힘든 과제들을 가질 수 있다
② 마법과 자신감에 의해 놀랄 준비를 하라
③ 당신의 마음속에서 휴식과 평온함을 경험할 준비를 하라
④ 마법의 트릭의 난이도를 고려해야 할 것이다
⑤ 당신의 과제에 대해 적절한 진술을 쓰는 훈련을 시작하라

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 3월 40번]
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. (A) The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. (B) It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. (C) You think and you can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently becase─fueled by emotions─you make the wrong decisions time and time again. (D) When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. (E) Scared of spiders or the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over.
questions.explanation: 글은 잠재의식과 의식적인 마음을 대조하고 있습니다. (A)와 (B)는 잠재의식의 특징(빠르고 감정을 다루지 않음, 기억과 인식 담당)을 설명합니다. 주어진 문장은 '하지만(However)'으로 시작하며 의식적인 마음이 우리가 더 통제력을 갖는 부분임을 소개합니다. (C) 이후부터는 의식적인 마음의 특징(생각을 이어갈지 선택 가능, 감정에 휘둘려 잘못된 결정 가능)을 설명하고 있으므로, 잠재의식 설명이 끝나고 의식적인 마음 설명이 시작되는 (C) 자리가 정답입니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 3월 19번]
questions.passage: Marilyn and her three-year-old daughter, Sarah, took a trip to the beach, where Sarah built her first sandcastle. Moments later, an enormous wave ⓐ<u>wiped out</u> Sarah's castle. In response to the ⓑ<u>destruction</u> of her sandcastle, tears streamed down Sarah's cheeks and her heart was broken. She ran to Marilyn, saying she would never build a sandcastle again. Marilyn said, "Part of the ⓒ<u>difficulty</u> of building a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give it to the ocean." Sarah loved this idea and responded with ⓓ<u>enthusiasm</u> to the idea of building another castle─this time, even closer to the water so the ocean would get its ⓔ<u>gift</u> sooner!
questions.explanation: 파도에 모래성이 무너진 뒤 실망한 딸에게 엄마가 해준 말의 문맥을 살펴야 합니다. 엄마는 모래성을 짓는 '어려움'이 아니라, 모래성을 짓는 '재미/즐거움(fun/joy)'의 일부가 결국 그것을 바다에게 선물로 주는 것이라고 위로하는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 뒤이어 딸이 이 생각에 열광(enthusiasm)하며 다른 성을 짓기로 한 것으로 보아 'difficulty'는 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they react ①<u>abnormally</u> to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally─they are functionally ②<u>blind</u>. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to ③<u>awaken</u> the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of ④<u>protecting</u> sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems ⑤<u>unnecessary</u> to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement) 없이는 잠을 자는 것이 불가능하다고 했으므로, 지각적 이탈은 수면의 정의에 '필수적(essential)'이어야 합니다. 따라서 unnecessary(불필요한)는 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session.
questions.summary_sentence: In general, it is (A)___________ for experts in a field to introduce novices to that area since they might not be (B)___________ to the difficulty of a task for a novice.
questions.explanation: 지문은 '지식의 저주'로 인해 전문가가 초보자의 입장에서 해당 과업이 얼마나 어려운지 과소평가하고 둔감해지는 현상을 설명합니다. 따라서 전문가가 초보자에게 자신의 분야를 소개하는 것은 (A)어렵고(challenging), 그 이유는 초보자가 느끼는 난이도에 전문가가 (B)민감(sensitive)하지 못하기 때문입니다.
options_translation: ① 쉬운 ... 반응하는
② 단순한 ... 영향받기 쉬운
③ 어려운 ... 무감각한
④ 까다로운 ... 무관심한
⑤ 도전적인(어려운) ... 민감한

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 요약문을 제시된 조건에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements─what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life─as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born─often occupied by its parent─to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 표현들을 형태 변화 없이 각각 한 번씩만 사용하되 필요시 글 속에 있는 단어를 사용할 것
'enough to~' 구문을 사용할 것
8단어 이하로 작성할 것
questions.answer: suitable enough to satisfy climatic requirements
questions.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 기후 변화에 따라 생명체들이 생존에 필요한 기후적 요구 사항을 충족하는 장소를 찾아 이동한다는 것입니다. 'suitable enough to satisfy climatic requirements'는 '기후적 요구 사항을 충족시키기에 충분히 적합한'이라는 의미를 형성하며, 지문의 단어인 'satisfy'를 활용하고 'enough to' 구문을 사용하여 총 7단어로 조건에 부합합니다.

questions.question: 1. Which of the underlined words is NOT appropriate in the passage below?
questions.passage: The hunter gatherer lifestyle, which can be describe as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed ⓐ<u>abundant</u> food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in ⓑ<u>temporary</u> villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its ⓒ<u>immediate</u> effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high ⓓ<u>rise</u> in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the ⓔ<u>growth</u> of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.explanation: 문맥상 수렵 채집인들이 농경을 시작하며 정착한 마을은 '임시적인' 것이 아니라 '영구적인' 정착지여야 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 temporary(일시적인)를 permanent(영구적인) 등으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 3. Where should the statement in the box go into?
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. (A) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (B) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one. (C) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. (D) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (E) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure disappears.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 미래를 위해 저축한 것을 조기에 사용해 버리는 경우에 대한 내용입니다. (C) 뒤에 나오는 예시(크리스마스 선물을 위해 모은 돈을 여름 휴가에 써버리는 것)가 이 '조기에 사용하는 경우'에 해당하므로, 예시가 시작되기 직전인 (C) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. Which of the underlined statements is inappropriate in context?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, ⓐ<u>animals must rely more entirely on hardware, and therefore be less flexible</u>. ⓑ<u>Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with sometimes have very efficient migration routes</u>. ⓒ<u>These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily</u>. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. ⓓ<u>By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most suitable migration routes</u>. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. ⓔ<u>Childhood gives adaptability in a changing world</u>.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 학습이 가능한 '어린 시절'이 있는 동물의 유연성과 적응력을 강조하고 있습니다. ⓑ 문장에서 태어날 때부터 모든 이동 정보를 알고 태어나는(즉, 학습하지 않는) 철새들은 환경 변화에 적응하지 못하고 옛 규칙과 지도에 의존한다는 맥락이 이어지므로, 그들의 이동 경로는 '효율적(efficient)'인 것이 아니라 '비효율적'이거나 '경직된' 것이 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. Which of the underlined statements is inappropriate in context? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. ⓐ<u>What has remained uncared for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities</u>. ⓑ<u>As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have trouble distinguishing particular colors</u>. ⓒ<u>Professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant development in meeting the needs of such users</u>. ⓓ<u>But, some scholars creating digital projects all too often manage to take these needs into account</u>. This situation would be much improved if more projects accepted the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ⓔ<u>making sure that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities and those without.</u>
questions.explanation: 이 글은 디지털 정밴림 구축할 땄 장애인의 접근성이 무시되고 있는 현실을 비판하고 있습니다. ⓓ에서 'manage to take these needs into account'(이러한 필요림 간가워이 고려하다)는 문맥사 맞준 않습니다. 원문은 'fail to take these needs into account'(고려하다림 실패하다)로, 학자들이 장애인의 필요림 고려하준 뮻하고 있음을 내타내야 합니다.

questions.question: 8. Which of the underlined statements is inappropriate in context? [3.2점]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. ⓐ<u>However, digital business activities can still endanger the environment</u>. ⓑ<u>In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more dangerous</u>. A few decades ago, offices used to have more paper waste since all documents were paper based. ⓒ<u>When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a favorable step to save trees</u>. ⓓ<u>However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is ignored</u>. A recent Wired report declared that most data enters' energy source is fossil fuels. ⓔ<u>When we store bigger data on clouds, reduced carbon emissions make our green clouds gray</u>. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 디지털 활동이 환경에 미치는 부정적인 영향(탄소 배출 등)을 설명하고 있습니다. ⓔ에서 'reduced carbon emissions'(감소된 탄소 배출)은 문맥사 맞준 않습니다. 클라우드에 더 많은 데이터림 저장할수록 탄소 배출이 '증가'(원문은 increased)하여 환경을 오염시킨다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. How many words are grammatically wrong among ⓐ~ⓔ?
questions.passage: Your behavior are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown ⓐ<u>that</u> once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who ⓑ<u>were identified</u> as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply ⓒ<u>claiming</u> "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince ⓓ<u>them</u> to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe ⓔ<u>yourself</u> to be.
questions.explanation: 틀린 부분은 총 3개입니다.ⓑ were identified: 문맥상 '~라고 동일시했던'이라는 능동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 'identified'로 고쳐야 합니다.ⓒ claiming: 문장 내에서 동사 역할을 해야 하므로 'claimed'로 고쳐야 합니다.ⓓ them: 주어(the person)와 목적어가 동일인이므로 재귀대명사 'himself or herself' 또는 'themselves(성별 불명 시)'로 고쳐야 합니다.ⓐ와 ⓔ는 어법상 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 1개
② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [24년 3월 37번]
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca King's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① Inca 제국은 말을 타고 메시지를 전달했다.
② Chasquis라고 불리는 전령들은 궁전에서 근무했다.
③ 전령들은 젊은 여자 네 명에서 여섯 명의 집단을 이루어 배치된 오두막에서 생활했다.
④ Inca 사람들은 서로를 볼 수 없도록 높은 지대에 오두막을 지었다.
⑤ Inca 제국은 사정이 좋으면 사나흘 만에 1,000마일 정도 메시지를 이어갈 수 있었다.
questions.explanation: 마지막 문장 'The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610km) in three or four days under good conditions.'를 통해 ⑤번이 일치함을 알 수 있습니다. ①은 말이 없어서 도보로 전달했다는 내용에 어긋나고, ②는 왕도(royal roads)의 오두막에 배치되었다고 했으며, ③은 젊은 남성(young men)이었고, ④는 서로 보일 수 있게(in sight of one another) 지었습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Every species ⓐ<u>have</u> certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that ⓑ<u>satisfying</u> those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, ⓒ<u>being</u> capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often ⓓ<u>occupied</u> by its parent - to a place ⓔ<u>which</u> it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.*barnacle: 따개비 **dispersal: 분산
questions.explanation: 정답 ⑤: survive, grow, reproduce는 자동사로 쓰여 완전한 문장을 이끄므로, 관계부사 where를 써야 할 곳에 'to a place (in/at) which'의 형태로 쓰여 옳습니다. (단, 이 문제의 원문과 대조했을 때 ⑤가 정답으로 처리된 것은 'a place where'를 'a place in which' 또는 단순히 관계사절의 완전성을 묻는 의도로 보입니다.) 틀린 부분 분석:ⓐ Every species는 단수 취급하므로 has가 되어야 합니다.ⓑ the places(주어)를 수식하는 관계절의 동사 자리이므로 satisfy가 되어야 합니다.ⓒ 문장의 본동사 자리이므로 are가 되어야 합니다.ⓓ born과 병렬되거나 수동의 의미를 지닌 분사구문으로 'often occupied by its parent'는 어법상 자연스러울 수 있으나 ⑤가 상대적으로 더 명확한 답이 됩니다. (참고: 실제 원문 어법 문제의 변형에 따라 정답이 ⑤번으로 제시됨)

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Marilyn and her three-year-old daughter, ⓐ<u>Sarah</u>, took a trip to the beach, where Sarah built her first sandcastle. Moments later, an enormous wave destroyed ⓑ<u>her</u> castle. In response to the loss of her sandcastle, tears streamed down Sarah's cheeks and her heart was broken. She ran to her mother, saying ⓒ<u>she</u> would never build a sandcastle again. ⓓ<u>She</u> said, "Part of the joy of building a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give it as a gift to the ocean." ⓔ<u>She</u> loved this idea and responded with enthusiasm to the idea of building another castle - this time, even closer to the water so the ocean would get its gift sooner!
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ는 모두 딸인 Sarah를 가리키지만, ⓓ는 실망한 Sarah를 달래기 위해 교훈적인 말을 해주는 엄마(Marilyn)를 가리킵니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This kind of farming sustainable since the soil remains in good condition.
questions.summary_sentence: Crop rotation is a sustainable farming (A)__________ where farmers change the crops in their fields in a specific sequence to maintain soil (B)__________.
questions.explanation: 윤작(Crop rotation)은 토양의 상태를 좋게 유지하기 위해 농작물을 순서대로 바꾸어 심는 농사 '관행(practice)'이며, 이를 통해 토양의 '건강(health)'을 유지한다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 관행 / 건강
전략 / 부족

questions.question: 25. 윗글(A)에 이어지도록 ⓐ~ⓓ를 순서에 맞게 배열했을 때, 앞에서 두 번째 오는 문장의 첫 두 단어를 적으시오.
questions.passage: (A) Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out hat you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you.ⓐ People expect that you will say it.ⓑ Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism.ⓒ But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked.ⓓ You become responsible. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication.(B) To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that <u>누군가가 초래한 대가가 상당할 때만 "감사합니다"라고 말해야 한다</u>. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
ordered_passages: ⓐ People expect that you will say it.
ⓑ Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism.
ⓒ But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked.
ⓓ You become responsible.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 법은 없지만 사람들이 기대한다는 내용이 먼저 오고, 하지 않았을 때 눈에 띈다는 내용, 그리고 그 결과 비판받을 만하다는 흐름으로 이어집니다. 논리적 순서는 ⓒ-ⓐ-ⓑ-ⓓ 가 적절하므로, 두 번째 문장은 ⓐ입니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글(B)의 우리말 해석에 알맞은 문장을 아래 <보기>에 주어진 표현들 중, 필요한 표현들만을 사용하여 완성하시오. (어휘 변형과 추가는 불가능함)
questions.passage: (A) Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out hat you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you.ⓐ People expect that you will say it.ⓑ Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism.ⓒ But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked.ⓓ You become responsible. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication.(B) To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that <u>누군가가 초래한 대가가 상당할 때만 "감사합니다"라고 말해야 한다</u>. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.

vocabulary_box: only when / is / you should / "Thank you" / has caused / are / considerate / someone / say / the cost / is caused / in which / saying / considerable
questions.answer: you should say "Thank you" only when the cost someone has caused is considerable
questions.explanation: 주어진 우리말 '누군가가 초래한 대가가 상당할 때만 "감사합니다"라고 말해야 한다'에 맞춰 단어를 조합하면, '말해야 한다(you should say "Thank you")' + '오직 ~할 때만(only when)' + '누군가가 초래한 대가(the cost someone has caused)' + '상당하다(is considerable)'의 순서가 됩니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists say that having a disorderly room can indicate a disorganized mental state. One of the professional tidying experts says that the moment you start cleaning your room, you also start changing your life and gaining new perspective. When you clean your surroundings, positive and good atmosphere follows. You can do more things efficiently and neatly. So, clean up your closets, organize your drawers, and arrange your things first, then peace of mind will follow.
options: ③ Don't Judge a Person by His Appearance
④ Good Environments Caused by Positive Thinking
⑤ Positive Minds from Organized Surroundings
questions.explanation: 이 글은 주변 환경(방)을 정리하고 청소하는 것이 정신적 안정과 긍정적인 사고방식을 가져다준다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '정리된 주변 환경으로부터 오는 긍정적인 마음'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 협력의 장점
② 과잉 학습의 문제점
③ 사람을 외모로 판단하지 마라
④ 긍정적인 사고로 만들어진 좋은 환경
⑤ 정리된 주변 환경으로부터 얻는 긍정적인 마음

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the ①<u>best</u> environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have ②<u>enabled</u> farmers to become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global ③<u>capacity</u> for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also ④<u>distracted</u> the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are ⑤<u>considered</u> as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.explanation: 농경지의 풍부한 영양분과 수분은 주변에 분포한 해로운 것들(잡초 등)의 눈길을 끌거나 유도하는 작용을 합니다. 따라서 '주의를 흐트러뜨리다'라는 의미의 distracted가 아니라, '관심을 끌다'나 '자극하다'의 의미를 가진 attracted 혹은 excited가 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. (A) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (B) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. (C) However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. (D) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. (E) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.insertion_sentence: Such cases could be examples of weakness of will.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'Such cases(그러한 사례들)'는 바로 앞 (D)에서 언급된 '크리스마스 선물을 위해 모은 돈을 여름 휴가에 써버리는 행위'를 가리킵니다. 이러한 행위가 '의지의 약함(weakness of will)'의 예시라고 정의한 뒤, (E) 뒤에서 'That is'로 시작하며 이에 대해 구체적으로 설명하는 구조가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 the costs of interruptions에 관한 내용을 본문에서 찾아 완성하시오.
questions.passage: <u>The costs of interruptions</u> are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.
subjective_conditions: (A)는 윗글에서 연속된 4단어로 찾아 쓸 것
(B)는 윗글에서 연속된 3단어로 찾아 쓸 것
questions.answer: (A) knocked on the door(B) didn't get written(C) was visited by an unexpected guest(D) forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished
questions.explanation: 본문의 내용을 바탕으로 두 인물의 사례에서 '방해 요소'와 그로 인한 '결과'를 찾아내는 문제입니다.(A) 마틴 루터 킹의 예시에서 방해 요소는 누군가 '문을 두드린 것'이므로 'knocked on the door'입니다.(B) 그 결과 아름다운 시가 '쓰여지지 않은 것'이므로 'didn't get written'입니다.(C) 사무엘 콜리지의 예시에서 방해 요소는 '예기치 못한 손님의 방문을 받은 것'이므로 'was visited by an unexpected guest'입니다.(D) 그 결과 '영감을 잊고 작품을 미완성으로 남긴 것'이므로 'forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished'입니다.

questions.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

② (B)

④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be _________________________________. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
options: ① less responsive to predatory attacks
② less alert to the possibility of danger
③ quick to learn about their environment
④ less adaptable to dealing with changing information
⑤ more flexible in managing changes of the hardware
questions.explanation: 이 글은 유년기가 동물이 환경에 대해 배우고 변화하는 세상에서 유연성을 가질 수 있게 해준다고 설명합니다. 유년기가 없는 동물은 타고난 하드웨어(유전적 지침)에 의존해야 하므로 환경 변화에 적응하기 어렵습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 변화하는 정보에 대처하는 적응력이 떨어진다는 내용인 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 포식자의 공격에 덜 반응하는
② 위험 가능성에 덜 경계하는
③ 환경에 대해 빠르게 배우는
④ 변화하는 정보를 다루는 데 덜 적응적인
⑤ 하드웨어의 변화를 관리하는 데 더 유연한

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
options: ① the human brain inherited from ancestors
② prehistoric people equivalent to modern humans intellectually
③ inter-tribal competition resulting in the evolution of the human brain
④ the necessity of developing strategies for winning in the struggle for survival
⑤ the reason why humans are more cognitively advanced than other animals
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인류의 두뇌가 진화한 원인 중 하나로 다른 부족과의 경쟁과 갈등을 꼽고 있습니다. 상대보다 더 잘 생각하고 예측하는 능력이 생존과 전투의 승리에서 결정적인 무기가 되었고, 이러한 정신적 이점이 세대를 거쳐 유전적으로 전달되었다고 설명합니다. 따라서 주제는 부족 간의 경쟁이 인간 두뇌의 진화를 초래했다는 ③번입니다.
options_translation: ① 조상으로부터 물려받은 인간의 뇌
② 지적으로 현대인과 대등했던 선사 시대 사람들
③ 인간 두뇌의 진화를 초래한 부족 간의 경쟁
④ 생존 투쟁에서 승리하기 위한 전략 개발의 필요성
⑤ 인간이 다른 동물보다 인지적으로 더 발달한 이유

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved.
ordered_passages: (A) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two.
(B) An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.

(C) In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time.
(D) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 수렵 채집인이 이동 시 모든 소유물을 운반해야 했던 제약 사항을 언급합니다. 이어지는 (C)에서는 특히 아이를 안고 이동해야 했던 어머니들의 고충과 그로 인한 긴 출산 간격을 구체적으로 설명합니다. (A)에서는 이와 대조적으로 한곳에 정착한 농부들은 아이를 장거리 운반할 걱정이 없어 출산 간격을 단축할 수 있었음을 보여줍니다. (D)는 이러한 출산 간격 단축이 인구 급증으로 이어졌다는 결과를 설명하고, 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 인구 증가가 노동력이 많이 필요한 농경 사회에 이점이 되었다는 결론을 내리는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 다음 글을 읽고 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved.
ordered_passages: (A) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two.
(B) An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.

(C) In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time.
(D) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 농경이 정착 생활을 강요했다는 점과 수렵 채집인은 이동 시 모든 소유물을 운반해야 했음을 언급합니다. (C)는 그 구체적 사례로 아이를 안고 이동해야 하는 어머니들의 제약을 설명하며 출산 간격이 길었음을 보여줍니다. (A)는 'on the other hand'를 통해 농경인들이 정착함으로써 아이를 장거리 이동시킬 걱정이 없어 출산 간격이 단축되었음을 대조합니다. (D)는 (A)의 결과로 농경 공동체의 인구가 급증했음을 설명하고, 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 인구 증가가 노동력이 많이 필요한 농경 사회의 장점이 되었음을 결론짓습니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고 정리한 표에서, <조건>에 맞게 빈칸 (A)~(D)를 완성하시오.
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool the ideas and make them shared anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates ideas on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that try very hard to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.summary_sentence: <How to Use Brainwriting>Step 1.Everyone in a group is asked to (A)_________________.Step 2.The Ideas are collected and (B)____________________.Step 3.(C)_________________________________________________.Step 4.The group come together to select and refine the most promising options.<What Brainwriting Is Effective for>The process of brainwriting is effective in groups that struggle to (D)_____________________________.
subjective_conditions: (A)는 윗글에서 연셍된 4단어로 찾아 숬 것
(B)는 윗글에서 연셍된 5단어로 찾아 숬 것
(C)는 윗글에서 연셍된 7단어로 찾아 숬 것
(D)는 윗글에서 연셍된 3단어로 찾아 숬 것
questions.answer: (A) generate ideas separately(B) shared anonymously among the group(C) Each member evaluates ideas on their own(D) achieve collective intelligence
questions.explanation: 지문의 내용을 바탕으로 브묈이라이팅 과정을 요약하눠 문제입니다. (A) Step 1에서 모든 구성원이 개별적으로 아이디어림 생성하도록 요청받는다눠 내용으로 'generate ideas separately'가 적절합니다.(B) Step 2에서 아이디어들이 모이고 익명으로 곞유된다눠 내용으로 'shared anonymously among the group'이 적절합니다.(C) Step 3에서 각 구성원이 스스로 아이디어림 평가한다눠 내용으로 'Each member evaluates ideas on their own'이 적절합니다.(D) 브묈이라이팅은 중단 지성을 달성하려고 노력하눠 중단에게 효과적이므로 'achieve collective intelligence'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. (A) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (B) However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. (C) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. (D) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (E) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.insertion_sentence: Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '따라서 미래 보상의 할인된 가치가 현재 보상의 할인되지 않은 가치보다 커야 한다'는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 이는 지연된 보상을 선택하는 행동(A 앞부분 내용)을 논리적으로 뒷받침하는 근거가 됩니다. 하지만 (B) 뒤에서부터는 계획과 달리 돈을 미리 써버리는 상반된 상황이 제시되므로, 지연된 보상 선호의 논리적 전제를 완성하는 문장으로서 (B)의 자리가 가장 적절합니다. (참고: 원문 맥락상 지연 보상을 선택하기 위해서는 미래의 가치가 현재보다 커야 함을 전제로 합니다.)

questions.question: 18. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것을 선택 후 올바르게 수정하시오.

questions.question: 19. 윗글에서 주어진 질문에 대한 답이 될 수 있는 연속된 네 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A), (B)가 각각 지칭하는 바가 무엇인지 찾아 쓰시오. [3.1점]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, (A)<u>it</u> was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, (B)<u>it</u> causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
questions.answer: (A) workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, (B) an email
questions.explanation: (A)의 'it'은 앞 문장의 주어부인 'workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails' 상황을 가리킵니다. (B)의 'it'은 바로 앞 문장의 주어인 'The carbon footprint of an email'에서 'an email'을 지칭합니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 내용을 바탕으로 주어진 문장을 완성하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 적절한 단어를 윗글에서 한 단어씩 찾아 쓰시오. [3.1점]

questions.explanation: 본문에 따르면 디지털화는 종이 낭비를 줄여 나무를 구하는(save) 데 도움이 될 것으로 기대되지만, 데이터 센터의 화석 연료 사용으로 인해 환경에 해로운(hazardous) 영향을 미칠 수 있습니다. 요약문의 빈칸 (A)에는 나무를 구한다는 맥락의 'save', (B)에는 환경을 위험에 빠뜨린다는 맥락의 'hazardous'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: (A) The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."(B) Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
options: ① According to (A), the hunter-gatherer lifestyle was recommendable in that it would make modern lives more abundant.
② According to (A), farming people were more venerable to epidemic diseases than hunter-gatherers.
③ According to (B), the migrating lifestyle led hunter-gatherer mothers to space their birth.
④ According to (B), agricultural societies eased mothers' burden to carry babies long distances.
⑤ According to (A) and (B), settlement has something to do with population.
questions.explanation: 지문 (A)에서 수렵 채집 생활 방식이 '권장할 만한 점이 많았다(had much to recommend it)'고 언급하며 풍부한 음식과 적은 질병을 예로 들고 있습니다. 다만 선택지 1번이 '현대의 삶을 풍요롭게 만든다'는 부분은 지문과 다소 거리가 있을 수 있으나 제시된 정답에 따릅니다. 실제 지문 내용상으로는 3번(이동 생활이 출산 간격을 조절하게 함)이나 5번(정착이 인구 밀도 증가 및 성장과 관련됨)도 타당한 설명입니다.
options_translation: ① (A)에 따르면, 수렵 채집 생활 방식은 현대의 삶을 더 풍요롭게 만든다는 점에서 권장할 만했다.
② (A)에 따르면, 농경 민족은 수렵 채집인보다 전염병에 더 취약했다(vulnerable의 오타로 보임).
③ (B)에 따르면, 이동하는 생활 방식은 수렵 채집인 어머니들이 출산 간격을 두게 만들었다.
④ (B)에 따르면, 농경 사회는 아기를 먼 거리까지 업고 다녀야 하는 어머니들의 부담을 덜어주었다.
⑤ (A)와 (B)에 따르면, 정착은 인구와 관련이 있다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the ⓓ<u>shortest</u> childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives ⓔ<u>flexibility</u> in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 부모와 함께 이주하며 효율적인 경로를 습득하는 새들은 학습할 수 있는 '어린 시절'이 있는 경우이다. 따라서 ⓓ의 shortest(가장 짧은)는 부모로부터 배울 시간이 충분하다는 맥락을 고려할 때 longest(가장 긴) 등으로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절하다. 어린 시절이 길수록 유연한 학습이 가능하여 효율적인 이동 경로를 가질 수 있다는 것이 글의 핵심이다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 제목으로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. However, the needs of people with disabilities have largely been overlooked. Consequently, (A)<u>시각에 문제가 있는 사람들뿐만 아니라 듣는 것에 어려움이 있는 사람들도 가치 있는 디지털 자원을 사용할 충분한 기회를 가지지 못할 수 있다. </u>Although professionals in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
options: ① Widening the Gap in Accessing Digital Information Standards
② Enhancing Usability for Special Needs : The Importance of Exclusive Digital Projects
③ Exclusive Digital Design: Ignoring Needs of People with Disabilities
④ The Unseen Challenge: Making Digital Resources Accessible to Everyone
⑤ Designing Exclusively for the Disabled: Diminishing Digital Accessibility for the Non-disabled
questions.explanation: 이 글은 디지털 정보를 구축할 때 장애를 가진 사람들의 필요성이 간과되어 온 상황을 지적하며, 가능한 한 가장 넓은 범위의 사용자(장애인과 비장애인 모두)를 고려하여 디지털 자원에 대한 접근성을 높여야 한다는 주장을 담고 있다. 따라서 '보이지 않는 과제: 디지털 자원을 모두가 접근 가능하게 만들기'가 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 디지털 정보 표준 접근의 격차 확대
② 특별한 요구를 위한 사용성 강화: 배타적 디지털 프로젝트의 중요성
③ 배타적 디지털 디자인: 장애인의 요구 무시하기
④ 보이지 않는 과제: 디지털 자원을 모두가 접근 가능하게 만들기
⑤ 장애인 전용 디자인: 비장애인의 디지털 접근성 감소

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)를 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.

However, the needs of people with disabilities have largely been overlooked. Consequently, (A)<u>시각에 문제가 있는 사람들뿐만 아니라 듣는 것에 어려움이 있는 사람들도 가치 있는 디지털 자원을 사용할 충분한 기회를 가지지 못할 수 있다.</u> Although professionals in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. subjective_conditions: · <보기>의 표현들은 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것

vocabulary_box: viewing / hearing / difficulty / enough / valuable digital resources / use / as well as / people who / hard of
questions.answer: People who have difficulty hearing as well as people who are hard of viewing may not have enough chance to use valuable digital resources.
questions.explanation: 'A뿐만 아니라 B도'의 의미를 가진 'B as well as A' 구문을 활용하여 영작합니다. '듣는 것에 어려움이 있는 사람들(people who have difficulty hearing)'을 주어로, '시각에 문제가 있는 사람들(people who are hard of viewing)'을 as well as 뒤에 배치합니다. questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a ⓐ<u>vital</u> advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant ⓑ<u>military</u> advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more ⓒ<u>decisive</u> than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each ⓓ<u>succeeding</u> generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this ⓔ<u>physical</u> advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 정신이 다른 부족과의 경쟁과 갈등을 통해 진화했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 적을 앞서 생각하는 '정신적' 능력이 생존 전쟁에서 중요한 무기가 되었고, 이것이 다음 세대로 전해졌다는 문맥입니다. 따라서 마지막 문장의 ⓔ는 'physical(신체적인)'이 아니라 'mental(정신적인)' 또는 'intellectual(지적인)'과 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. (A) Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. (B) To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. (C) By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. (D) This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. (E) It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.insertion_sentence: Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'Only then(그제서야)'은 앞서 언급된 독립적인 아이디어 생성 및 평가 과정이 끝난 시점을 가리킵니다. (C) 앞부분까지는 개별적인 평가(evaluates them on their own)에 대해 설명하고 있으며, (C) 뒤의 문장은 아이디어를 개별적으로 개발하고 평가한 '후에' 선택하고 정교화함으로써 얻는 이점을 요약하고 있습니다. 따라서 주어진 문장은 선택과 정교화(select and refine) 단계가 시작되는 지점인 (C)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적합합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." ⓐPerhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. ⓑFor Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. ⓒHe forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished, but the abandoned task somehow motivated him to refocus. ⓓWhile sudden disruptions have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives. ⓔThey slow down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.*lament: 슬퍼하다
questions.explanation: 전체 글의 흐름은 방해(interruption)로 인해 작업을 완성하지 못하거나 부정적인 결과가 초래된다는 내용입니다. 하지만 ⓒ는 중단된 작업이 오히려 그에게 '다시 집중하도록 동기부여를 했다'는 긍정적인 맥락이므로 전체 흐름과 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be ⓐ<u>more</u> negative. However, digital business activities can still ⓑ<u>threaten</u> the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to ⓒ<u>save</u> trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is ⓓ<u>neglected</u>. A recent Wired report declared that most data enters' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is ⓔ<u>smaller</u> than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attaching is big.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 기업 활동이 디지털로 전환될 때, 환경에 미치는 영향이 '덜(less)' 부정적일 것이라고 흔히 '가정(assumed)'되지만, 실제로는 환경을 위협할 수 있다는 내용이 이어져야 합니다. 따라서 ⓐ의 more를 less로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be ⓐ<u>less</u> flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very ⓑ<u>inefficient</u> migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt ⓒ<u>easily</u>. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. questions.question: 31. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people ⓐ<u>to stay</u> in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they ⓑ<u>moved</u>. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, ⓒ<u>spaced</u> their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place ⓓ<u>were</u> able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, ⓔ<u>which</u> in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.*counterpart: (대응 관계에 있는) 상대
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 부분은 주절(hunter-gatherer mothers could have...)에 이어지는 분사구문 자리입니다. '간격을 두면서'라는 능동의 의미를 나타내야 하며 뒤에 목적어(their births)가 존재하므로 과거분사 spaced가 아닌 현재분사 spacing이 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. options: ① it preferred a nutritionally balanced menu

⑤ its characteristic of living densely works in favor of survival
questions.explanation: 외래종인 회색 다람쥐가 영국의 토종 붉은 다람쥐와의 경쟁에서 우위를 점한 이유를 찾아야 하는 문제입니다. 지문 하단에서 회색 다람쥐는 붉은 다람쥐와 달리 익지 않은 도토리(green acorns)를 먹을 수 있다고 구체적인 사례를 들고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 식단을 환경에 맞춰 적응시킬 수 있다는 내용인 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 영양적으로 균형 잡힌 메뉴를 선호했다
② 새로운 환경에 맞게 식단을 바꿀 수 있다
③ 몸 색깔이 포식자로부터 발견되지 않게 도와준다
④ 수명이 영양 상태에 의해 결정되지 않는다
⑤ 빽빽하게 모여 사는 특성이 생존에 유리하게 작용한다

questions.question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption.
ordered_passages: (A) However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead.

(B) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one.

(C) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.explanation: 많은 동물들이 미래의 소비를 위해 저축한다는 도입부 뒤에, (B)에서 이러한 행동이 즉각적 보상보다 지연된 보상을 선호하는 것임을 설명하며 미래 보상의 가치가 현재보다 커야 함을 언급합니다. (A)에서는 'However'를 통해 반전하며, 계획했던 때를 기다리지 않고 저축을 조기에 써버리는 사례(크리스마스용 돈을 여름 휴가에 쓰는 경우)를 제시합니다. (C)에서 'Such cases'로 이를 받아 이것이 의지력의 결약(weakness of will)의 사례가 될 수 있으며, 유혹 때문에 결심과 다르게 행동하는 것임을 설명하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. (A) In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. (B) As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. (C) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. (D) Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. (E) Therefore, this increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.insertion_sentence: This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이것은 각 여성이 수렵 채집인보다 더 많은 자녀를 가질 수 있음을 의미했고, 이는 농경 사회의 급격한 인구 증가로 이어졌다'는 내용입니다. (D) 문장에서 정착 생활을 하는 사회가 출산 간격을 4년에서 2년으로 단축할 수 있었다는 내용이 나오고, 주어진 문장의 'This'가 이 사실을 가리킵니다. 또한 (E) 뒤의 'this increased population'이 주어진 문장에서 언급한 'rapid population growth'를 가리키므로 주어진 문장은 (E) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
