questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. (A) This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. (B) During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. (C) World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. (D) Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables.
questions.explanation: 글의 앞부분은 농지에 영양분과 물을 공급하여 작물 성장에 완벽한 환경을 만드는 과정을 설명합니다. 주어진 문장의 'these luxurious conditions'는 (C)까지 설명된 풍부한 비료와 물이 공급된 상태를 지칭하며, 'agricultural undesirables(농업적으로 원치 않는 것들)'가 관심을 갖게 되었다는 부정적 전환을 도입합니다. (D) 뒤에서 'every random weed(온갖 잡초)'가 이 땅을 원한다고 구체적으로 설명하고 있으므로 (D) 위치가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift core activities like sales, marketing, or archiving to digital formats, it's often assumed that this will have a less negative environmental impact. However, digital business activities can still pose environmental threats, sometimes even more severe ones. Several decades ago, the reliance on paper-based documents led offices ⓐ<u>to generate</u> significantly more paper waste. The shift to digital documents, invoices, and emails initially seemed like a ⓑ<u>promising</u> step to save trees. However, the environmental costs of the Internet and electricity often ⓒ<u>overlooked</u>. A recent Wired report highlighted that most data centers are powered by fossil fuels. Storing large amounts of data in the cloud increases carbon emissions, ⓓ<u>turning</u> our "green" clouds gray. While the carbon footprint of an email is smaller than ⓔ<u>that</u> of traditional mail, it still generates four grams of CO₂, and this can rise to 50 grams for emails with large attachments.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 주어인 'the environmental costs of the Internet and electricity'는 동사 'overlook'의 대상(목적어)이므로 수동태인 'are often overlooked'가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Providing employees with _____________________________ can significantly enhance their energy and focus on the job, ultimately improving overall performance. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ① comprehensive training programs and resources
② acknowledging and rewarding their achievements
③ penalties and strict disciplinary measures for mistakes
④ opportunities for skill development and continuous learning
⑤ decision-making authority and autonomy over their work environment
questions.explanation: 오하이오 제조 공장의 사례에서 노동자들이 일정과 작업 환경에 대해 스스로 결정할 수 있게 되었을 때 생산성이 향상되었다는 내용을 통해, 직원들에게 의사 결정 권한과 자율성을 부여하는 것이 업무 성과를 높인다는 것을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 포괄적인 훈련 프로그램과 자원
② 성취에 대한 인정과 보상
③ 실수에 대한 처벌과 엄격한 징계 조치
④ 기술 개발과 지속적인 학습 기회
⑤ 업무 환경에 대한 의사 결정 권한과 자율성

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Experiencing childhood ________________________________________.
options: ① inhibits to navigate through unfamiliar surroundings
② fosters adaptability in a world that is always shifting
③ influences the development of social and emotional skills
④ promotes the acquisition and internalization of ethical values
⑤ restrains individuals from responding flexibly to changes in their surroundings
questions.explanation: 유년기를 거치지 않고 본능(하드웨어)에만 의존하는 동물들은 유연성이 떨어지지만, 긴 유년기를 가지며 부모로부터 학습하는 동물들은 변화하는 환경에 더 효율적으로 적응한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 유년기 경험은 항상 변하는 세상에서의 적응력을 키워준다는 결론이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 익숙하지 않은 주변 환경을 항해하는 것을 방해한다
② 항상 변화하는 세상에서 적응력을 기른다
③ 사회적, 정서적 기술의 발달에 영향을 미친다
④ 윤리적 가치의 습득과 내면화를 촉진한다
⑤ 주변 환경의 변화에 유연하게 대응하는 것을 억제한다

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption.
ordered_passages: (A) However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead.

(B) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one.

(C) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.explanation: 인간과 동물의 미래를 위한 저축 행위에 관한 글입니다. 주어진 문장에서 미래 소비를 위한 저축을 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 이러한 행동(This behavior)이 즉각적인 보상보다 지연된 보상을 선호하는 것임을 설명합니다. (A)에서 그러나(However) 예외적으로 저축을 조기에 써버리는 사례를 소개합니다. (C)에서 그러한 사례들(Such cases)은 의지의 나약함의 예시이며, 즉각적인 유혹에 굴복하는 것임을 설명하며 끝맺습니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.*counterpart: (대응 관계에 있는) 상대
options: ① the impact of agriculture on human settlement patterns and population growth
② the importance of choosing the right place to live in with babies
③ the difficulties of raising babies in hunter-gatherer societies
④ the reasons why the longevity of hunter-gatherers was shorter than of farmers
⑤ the main factors causing the shift from hunter-gatherer to farming societies
questions.explanation: 이 글은 농경의 시작이 사람들을 정착하게 만들었고, 이동의 제약이 사라짐에 따라 출산 간격이 짧아져 인구가 급격히 증가하게 되었다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로는 '농업이 인간의 정착 패턴과 인구 성장에 미친 영향'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 농업이 인간의 정착 패턴과 인구 성장에 미친 영향
② 아기와 함께 살기에 적합한 장소를 선택하는 것의 중요성
③ 수렵 채집 사회에서 아기를 키우는 것의 어려움
④ 수렵 채집인의 수명이 농부들보다 짧았던 이유
⑤ 수렵 채집 사회에서 농경 사회로의 전환을 일으킨 주요 요인들

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: There ⓐ<u>is</u> a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find ⓑ<u>far</u> larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, ⓒ<u>which</u> has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, ⓓ<u>enhances</u> in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to ⓔ<u>where</u> we direct our attention and what we practice doing.*cortex: (대뇌) 피질(皮質)**hippocampus: (대뇌 측두엽의) 해마
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 해마(hippocampus)가 택시 운전사들에게서 '확대된다'는 의미가 되어야 합니다. enhance는 타동사로 주로 쓰여 '~을 향상시키다'라는 의미를 가지므로, 여기서는 자동사인 enlarges 혹은 수동태인 is enlarged 등으로 쓰이는 것이 적절합니다. (실제 모의고사 원문은 is enlarged임)

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
options: ① The Art of Conflict Management: A Guide to Effective Resolution Skills
② The Evolutionary Struggles: How Conflict Shaped the Human Mind
③ Why do All Living Things Evolve?
④ Superior Performance Created and Sustained by Competitive Advantage
⑤ Large Brain and Advanced Intelligence, Which Are Advantageous for Group Life
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 지능과 정신이 다른 부족과의 경쟁 및 갈등에서 살아남기 위한 '무기'로서 진화했음을 설명하고 있습니다. 상대보다 더 잘 생각하는 능력이 생존과 승리에 유리했고, 이것이 유전적으로 이어졌다는 내용이므로 '갈등이 어떻게 인간의 정신을 형성했는가'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 갈등 관리의 기술: 효과적인 해결 기술 가이드
② 진화적 투쟁: 갈등이 어떻게 인간의 정신을 형성했는가
③ 왜 모든 생명체는 진화하는가?
④ 경쟁 우위에 의해 생성되고 유지되는 우수한 성과
⑤ 집단 생활에 유리한 큰 뇌와 진보된 지능

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ① the need to improve the working environment of workers
② the reason why employees should have a sense of ownership of the company
③ differences between the working environment of the manufacturing plants and other ones
④ the importance of the authority of the director to improve the productivity of the factory
⑤ the positive impact of giving employees a platform for control and decision-making
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 통제권과 결정권을 부여(sense of agency)하는 것이 그들의 업무 에너지, 집중력, 그리고 결과적으로 생산성을 크게 향상시킨다는 내용입니다. 오하이오 공장의 사례를 통해 작은 결정권 부여가 가져온 긍정적 변화를 보여주고 있으므로, 주제는 직원들에게 통제와 의사결정의 장을 제공하는 것의 긍정적인 영향입니다.
options_translation: ① 노동자의 작업 환경을 개선할 필요성
② 직원들이 회사에 대한 주인 의식을 가져야 하는 이유
③ 제조 공장과 다른 곳의 작업 환경 차이
④ 공장 생산성 향상을 위한 관리자 권한의 중요성
⑤ 직원들에게 통제와 의사결정권을 부여하는 것의 긍정적 영향

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be ⓐ<u>less</u> flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't ⓑ<u>adapt</u> easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the ⓒ<u>new</u> rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most ⓓ<u>efficient</u> migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a ⓔ<u>changing</u> world.
questions.explanation: 태어날 때부터 이주 방법을 알고 태어난 새들은 환경 변화(호수가 마르거나 기후 변화 등)에 쉽게 적응하지 못한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 이들은 변화된 환경에도 불구하고 새로운 규칙이 아니라 자신들이 원래 가지고 태어난 '오래된/기존의(old)' 규칙과 지도를 따라 계속 비행하게 됩니다. 그러므로 ⓒ는 new가 아니라 old가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. ⓐResearch has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. ⓑFor example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. ⓒThough, the way your identity is perceived by people around you is another factor that influences your self-formation. ⓓ Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. ⓔDoing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 행동이 정체성의 반영이며, 스스로를 어떤 유형의 사람이라고 믿느냐에 따라 행동이 달라진다는 것입니다. 반면 ⓒ문장은 '주변 사람들에 의해 정체성이 어떻게 인식되는지'가 자아 형성에 영향을 미치는 또 다른 요인이라는 내용으로, 자신의 믿음과 행동의 일치라는 글의 전체적인 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo.
ordered_passages: (A) By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise.(B) You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options.(C) This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 브레인라이팅의 첫 단계는 '솔로(혼자)'라고 명시했습니다. 따라서 개별적으로 아이디어를 생성하고 익명으로 공유하며 각자 평가한다는 구체적인 절차를 설명하는 (B)가 가장 먼저 옵니다. 그 다음, 이러한 '개별적 개발 및 평가'가 가져오는 이점을 요약하는 (A)가 이어지며, 마지막으로 브레인라이팅 과정 전체의 의의와 효과를 정리하는 (C)로 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. (A) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (B) However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. (C) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. (D) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (E) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.insertion_sentence: Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '따라서 미래 보상의 할인된 가치가 현재 보상의 할인되지 않은 가치보다 커야 한다'는 결론적 논리를 담고 있습니다. 이는 (A) 문장에서 설명하는 '지연된 보상을 즉각적인 보상보다 선호하여 현재의 즐거움을 포기하는 행동'의 전제 조건이나 논리적 근거가 되므로, 일반적인 저축 행동을 설명한 뒤 그 행동의 기저 논리를 보충하거나 전환이 일어나기 전 위치인 (B) 자리가 적절합니다. (원문 문맥상 (A)에서 미래 보상을 선택하는 이유를 논리적으로 뒷받침하며 (B)의 'However'로 이어지는 흐름을 만듭니다.)

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. (A) This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. (B) During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. (C) World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. (D) Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'these luxurious conditions(이러한 사치스러운 조건들)'는 앞 문장의 비료와 관개를 통해 만들어진 풍부한 영양소와 물이 있는 환경을 의미합니다. 또한 'agricultural undesirables(농업적으로 원치 않는 것들)'는 뒤에 나오는 'every random weed(모든 무작위의 잡초)'와 연결됩니다. 따라서 영양분이 풍부해진 농지의 상태를 설명한 뒤, 잡초가 꼬이게 된다는 내용이 시작되는 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 (A)the largest possible audience가 가리키는 대상을 여덟 단어로 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep (A)<u>the largest possible audience</u> in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 여덟 단어로 쓸 것
questions.answer: those with disabilities as well as those without
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 '가능한 한 가장 큰 관객(the largest possible audience)'은 문맥상 디지털 정보 디자인 시 고려해야 할 모든 대상층을 의미합니다. 지문의 마지막 부분에서 '장애가 있는 사람뿐만 아니라 장애가 없는 사람(those with disabilities as well as those without)'의 필요를 충족시킨다고 언급하고 있으므로, 이 부분이 가리키는 대상에 해당합니다. 해당 어구는 정확히 8단어입니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Cultivating crops necessitated ⓐ<u>settlement</u>. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to ⓑ<u>transport</u> young children over long distances. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could enjoy the stability of staying in one place, ⓒ<u>eliminating</u> the need to carry young children over long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to ⓓ<u>extend</u> their birth intervals. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. This proved ⓔ<u>advantageous</u> to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.explanation: 정착 생활을 하게 된 농경 사회에서는 아이를 멀리 옮길 필요가 없어졌으므로 출산 간격을 '연장(extend)'하는 것이 아니라 '축소(shorten)'할 수 있게 되었습니다. 이를 통해 여성들이 더 많은 자녀를 가질 수 있게 되어 인구가 급증하게 된 것이 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. ⓐ<u>lamented</u> them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an ⓑ<u>unexpected</u> guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. Ultimately, he left the work ⓒ<u>finished</u>. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in ⓓ<u>critical</u> roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally ⓔ<u>increasing</u> stress levels.
questions.explanation: 갑작스러운 방해자(방문객) 때문에 시를 마저 쓰지 못했다는 문맥이므로, 시를 '완성된(finished)' 상태로 남겨둔 것이 아니라 '미완성된(unfinished)' 상태로 남겨두게 된 것입니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that where we focus our attention and what we consistently practice can ____________________________________.
options: ① speed up our sensory response
② shape our attitudes towards risk-taking
③ alter the physical structure of our brain
④ control our sensitivity to different senses
⑤ alleviate the effects of brain damage on memory
questions.explanation: 글의 첫 문장에서 '집중된 주의가 뇌의 재형성(reshaping of the brain)으로 이어진다'는 핵심 주제를 제시하고 있습니다. 이후 동물(청각, 시각 센터), 바이올린 연주자(피질의 손 담당 영역), 택시 운전사(해마)의 예시를 통해 특정 활동이나 주의 집중이 관련 뇌 부위를 확장시키고 변화시킨다는 증거를 나열하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 우리가 어디에 집중하고 무엇을 연습하느냐가 '우리 뇌의 물리적 구조를 바꿀 수 있다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 감각 반응을 가속화할 수 있다
② 위험 감수에 대한 우리의 태도를 형성할 수 있다
③ 우리 뇌의 물리적 구조를 바꿀 수 있다
④ 다른 감각들에 대한 우리의 민감도를 조절할 수 있다
⑤ 기억에 대한 뇌 손상의 영향을 완화할 수 있다

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were given authority to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees ___________________________________ improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ⑤ detailed training on the assembly process
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 스스로 결정하고 통제할 수 있는 권한(sense of agency)을 부여했을 때 생산성과 자기 규율이 향상되었다는 실험 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 'a sense of agency'를 다른 말로 표현한 'a sense of empowerment(권한 부여 의식)'가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 높은 임금
② 회사의 비전
③ 권한 부여 의식(자율권)
④ 빈번한 실수의 사례들
⑤ 조립 과정에 대한 상세한 교육

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the shift will have a more (A)__________ impact on the environment. However, digital business activities can pose environmental risks. In certain instances, they can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a positive step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is (B)___________. A recent Wired report declared that most data enters' energy source is fossil fuels. Storing bigger data on cloud platforms leads to heightened carbon emissions, (C)__________ the eco-friendly perception of green clouds. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞뒤 문맥상 디지털로의 전환이 환경에 더 '이로운(beneficial)' 영향을 미칠 것이라 가정되지만, 실제로는 위험할 수 있다는 흐름이 적절합니다. (B) 인터넷과 전기의 환경적 비용이 '무시된다(disregarded/neglected)'는 내용이 와야 뒤의 화석 연료 사용 및 탄소 배출 이야기가 자연스럽게 연결됩니다. (C) 늘어난 탄소 배출이 친환경 클라우드라는 인식을 '부정한다(negating)'는 의미가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 유익한 ... 무시된 ... 부정하는
② 불리한 ... 감사되는 ... 향상시키는
③ 부정적인 ... 간과된 ... 타협하는
④ 긍정적인 ... 방치된 ... 높이는
⑤ 유망한 ... 과대평가된 ... 손상시키는

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. (A) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (B) Yet, there are instances where the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion, but uses their savings prematurely. (C) As an illustration, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. (D) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (E) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.insertion_sentence: Therefore, the discounted value of the future reward should exceed the un-discounted value of the present one for this act.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 미래 보상의 가치가 현재의 가치보다 커야 한다는 저축 행위의 논리적 전제를 설명합니다. (A)에서 저축 행위가 미래 보상을 선호하는 것임을 설명한 직후, 이 행위가 성립하기 위한 조건을 설명하는 주어진 문장이 오는 것이 적절합니다. 그 후 (B)에서 '하지만(Yet)'을 통해 계획과 달리 저축을 조기에 써버리는 반대의 경우를 제시하며 글이 이어집니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. (A) This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. (B) During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. (C) World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. (D) Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area. (E) In addition, the fields that were plowed for planting were already home to innumerable insects and bacteria that are only too eater to eat our crop plants before we can.
questions.insertion_sentence: Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables.
questions.explanation: (C)까지는 농경지에 비료와 물을 효율적으로 공급하여 작물이 자라기 좋은 환경을 만드는 긍정적인 측면을 설명합니다. 주어진 문장의 'these luxurious conditions'는 (C)에서 설명한 영양분과 물이 풍부한 상태를 의미하며, 'agricultural undesirables(농업적으로 원치 않는 것들)'가 등장하기 시작하는 전환점이므로, 잡초(weed)에 대한 설명이 시작되는 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. ⓐThe ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. ⓑThe human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. ⓒAt times, powerful weapons can be more crucial than resolute decision-making and unyielding determination. ⓓAnd this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. ⓔThe tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 정신이 다른 부족과의 경쟁에서 이기기 위한 '지적 우위'를 확보하는 방향으로 진화했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 정신적 능력(사고력, 예측력)이 생존과 전쟁의 승리에 결정적인 무기가 되었다는 맥락을 따르지만, ⓒ는 물리적인 '강력한 무기'가 결단력보다 중요할 때가 있다는 내용으로, '정신의 진화'라는 주제에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: American jazz pianist Bill Evans was born in New Jersey in 1929. His early training was in classical music. At the age of six, he began receiving piano lessons, later adding flute and violin. He earned bachelor′s degrees in piano and music education from Southeastern Louisiana College in 1950. He went on to serve in the army from 1951 to 1954 and played flute in the Fifth Army Band. After serving in the military, he studied composition at the Mannes School of Music in New York. Composer George Russell admired his playing and hired Evans to record and perform his compositions. Evans became famous for recordings made from the late-1950s through the 1960s. He won his first Grammy Award in 1964 for his album Conversations with Myself. Evans′ expressive piano works and his unique harmonic approach inspired a whole generation of musicians.
options: ① 뉴저지에서 태어났으며 초기에 클래식 음악 교육을 받았다.
② 6세에 플루트 수업을 받기 시작했고 나중에 피아노를 추가했다.
③ 작곡가 George Russell은 그의 연주를 높이 평가하여 그를 고용했다.
④ 1950년에 Southeastern Louisiana College에서 학사 학위를 받았다.
⑤ 1964년에 Conversations with Myself 앨범으로 첫 그래미상을 받았다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 빌 에반스는 6세에 피아노 레슨을 받기 시작했고(At the age of six, he began receiving piano lessons), 그 이후에 플루트와 바이올린을 추가로 배웠습니다(later adding flute and violin). 따라서 6세에 플루트를 먼저 시작했다는 ②번은 지문의 내용과 정반대이므로 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 뉴저지에서 태어났으며 초기에 클래식 음악 교육을 받았다.
② 6세에 플루트 수업을 받기 시작했고 나중에 피아노를 추가했다.
③ 작곡가 George Russell은 그의 연주를 높이 평가하여 그를 고용했다.
④ 1950년에 Southeastern Louisiana College에서 학사 학위를 받았다.
⑤ 1964년에 Conversations with Myself 앨범으로 첫 그래미상을 받았다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are - writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
options: ① 한 사람의 가치는 그의 수행 능력만으로 규정될 수 없다.
② 한 사람의 능력을 의미하는 측면이 점점 다양해지고 있다.
③ 아직도 지능이 누군가의 능력을 의미하는 경향이 지배적이다.
④ 능력을 정의할 때 외부로 드러나는 가치만을 고려하는 것은 문제이다.
⑤ 우리는 타인의 가치를 평가할 때 무의식적으로 자신의 강점 분야를 포함시킨다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 능력을 정의하는 방식이 다양할 수 있지만, 능력을 자아 가치의 유일한 결정 요인으로 삼을 때 발생하는 문제점을 지적하고 있습니다. 필자는 수행 능력이 그 사람을 평가하는 유일한 척도가 되어서는 안 된다고 주장하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① effects of sound on a scientific experiment
② dynamics of the scientific publishing industry
③ importance of interaction in scientific communication
④ factors influencing comprehension of scientific papers
⑤ challenges of writing innovative and creative scientific papers
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학적 의사소통을 소리에 비유하며, 소리가 들려야 의미가 있듯이 과학 논문도 독자에게 전달되고 이해되어야 비로소 완성된다는 것을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 과학적 의사소통에서 상호작용(전달과 이해)의 중요성이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 과학 실험에 소리가 미치는 영향
② 과학 출판 산업의 역학
③ 과학적 의사소통에서 상호작용의 중요성
④ 과학 논문의 이해에 영향을 미치는 요소들
⑤ 혁신적이고 창의적인 과학 논문을 쓰는 것의 어려움

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
options: ① A traditional one-off negotiation strategy which is commonly learned may lead to optimal outcomes.
② Achieving successful results in negotiation is so important that maintaining relationships can be overlooked.
③ Negotiation is a fundamental aspect of daily life, yet many individuals lack proficiency in this skill.
④ In the interconnected world, adopting a win-win approach to negotiation is increasingly essential.
⑤ A stable and healthy relationship should be followed by a win-win outcome in the negotiation.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 현대 사회가 상호 의존적이고 장기적인 관계가 중요해짐에 따라, 과거의 승패 방식보다는 양측 모두에게 이익이 되는 '윈-윈(win-win)' 협상 방식이 필수적이라고 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 흔히 배우는 전통적인 일회성 협상 전략이 최선의 결과로 이어질 수 있다.
② 협상에서 성공적인 결과를 얻는 것이 너무 중요해서 관계 유지가 간과될 수 있다.
③ 협상은 일상생활의 근본적인 측면이지만, 많은 개인들이 이 기술에 숙달되어 있지 않다.
④ 상호 연결된 세상에서 협상에 대한 윈-윈 접근 방식을 채택하는 것이 점점 더 필수적이다.
⑤ 안정적이고 건강한 관계 뒤에는 협상에서의 윈-윈 결과가 따라야 한다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
options: ① All that matterse in fashion is uniqueness.
② Creativity stems from breaking traditional custom.
③ The slightest deviation from a norm could be disastrous.
④ Judge others not by their appearances but by their behaviors.
⑤ Slight changes in what we expect to wear are favorable as they are considered relevant to a high social status.
questions.explanation: 사람들은 일반적으로 기대에 부합하는 옷차림을 선호하지만, 규범에서 아주 약간 벗어난 독특한 차림(예: 턱시도에 빨간 나비넥타이, 강의 중 빨간 운동화)은 해당 인물이 사회적 비용을 감수할 만큼 충분히 지위가 높고 유능하다는 인상을 주어 긍정적으로 평가받는다는 내용입니다. 따라서 우리가 기대하는 복장에서의 약간의 변화가 높은 사회적 지위와 관련되어 호의적으로 받아들여진다는 5번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 패션에서 중요한 것은 오직 독특함뿐이다.
② 창의성은 전통적인 관습을 깨는 것에서 나온다.
③ 규범으로부터의 아주 작은 일탈도 재앙이 될 수 있다.
④ 다른 사람을 외모가 아니라 행동으로 판단하라.
⑤ 우리가 입을 것으로 기대하는 것의 약간의 변화는 그것이 높은 사회적 지위와 관련이 있다고 여겨지기 때문에 호의적이다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
options: ① 결정을 구성하는 가장 기본 단위는 원자이다.
② 모든 암석은 결정으로 이루어져 있다.
③ 결정은 '습성'이라고 불리는 다양한 모양으로 나온다.
④ 일반적인 결정 습성은 사각형, 삼각형, 육면의 육각형을 포함한다.
⑤ 결정격자는 원자가 아름답게 배열되는 느리고 안정적인 환경조건이다.
questions.explanation: 지문 마지막 부분에서 결정격자(crystal lattice)는 원자들이 반복적으로 배열되어 나타나는 '원자의 기본 구조'라고 설명하고 있습니다. 느리고 안정적인 환경은 결정격자가 형성되기 위한 '조건'이지 결정격자 그 자체를 정의하는 말이 아닙니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status - they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as <u>customers may not be completely locked in to the product</u>. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.
options: ① customers may find alternatives of the product
② customers tend to easily change their choices
③ customers rarely have fixed brand loyalty to the product
④ car buyers should be careful not to be locked out of their cars
⑤ what makes a product complementary may be a matter of personal preference
questions.explanation: 지문은 보완재에 대해 설명하면서, 어떤 제품이 완벽하게 보완적이라고 가정하지 말라고 경고합니다. 그 근거로 운전자가 가솔린 대신 전기차를 선택할 수 있다는 예를 듭니다. 이는 고객이 특정 제품에 완전히 묶여 있는 것이 아니라 다른 대안(alternatives)을 찾을 수 있다는 의미이므로 1번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 고객은 제품의 대안을 찾을 수 있다.
② 고객은 자신의 선택을 쉽게 바꾸는 경향이 있다.
③ 고객은 제품에 대해 고정된 브랜드 충성심을 거의 가지고 있지 않다.
④ 자동차 구매자는 차에 갇히지 않도록 주의해야 한다.
⑤ 무엇이 제품을 보완적으로 만드는가는 개인적인 선호의 문제일 수 있다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may ⓐ<u>diminish</u> productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also ⓑ<u>influence</u> the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may ⓒ<u>embrace</u> a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a ⓓ<u>deviation</u> of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might not ⓔ<u>fear</u> that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 다양성이 국가 정체성에 대한 '일탈(deviation)'로 인식될 때, 원주민들은 다른 민족 집단을 차별하거나 사회적 갈등이 자신들의 이웃으로 유입되는 것을 '두려워할(fear)' 수 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 'they might not fear'라고 표현하면 사회적 갈등 유입을 걱정하지 않는다는 의미가 되어 앞뒤 맥락(차별, 매력적이지 않은 특징으로 인식)과 어긋납니다. 따라서 'fear'가 적절하며, 'not fear'는 문맥상 'fear' 또는 'worry' 등으로 고쳐야 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are (A)[minimized / maximized]. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones - one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater (B)[division / vagueness] between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer (C)[combining / differentiating] work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 일과 가정의 경계를 관리하는 두 가지 방식을 대조합니다. (A) 경계를 분리하려는 사람들(segmenters)은 경계 교차를 '최소화(minimized)'하고 싶어 합니다. (B) 이들에게 유연한 시간표는 일하는 시간과 다른 역할 시간 사이의 더 큰 '분할(division)'을 가능하게 하므로 유리합니다. (C) 반면, 다른 개인들은 하루 종일 일과 가정의 역할을 '통합하는 것(combining)'을 선호합니다. 이는 사무실에서 아이와 문자를 주고받거나 집에서도 이메일을 확인하는 행동으로 설명됩니다.
options_translation: ① 최소화된 / 분할 / 결합하는 것
② 최소화된 / 모호함 / 결합하는 것
③ 최소화된 / 분할 / 구별하는 것
④ 최대화된 / 모호함 / 구별하는 것
⑤ 최대화된 / 분할 / 구별하는 것

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us. One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Gobekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of how ____________________________. Things are not so different in our own time.
options: ① individuals engage in the process of constructing various types of buildings
② agricultural societies shifted to hunter-gathered societies
③ architectural advancements drive societal progress
④ social structures impact the design of buildings
⑤ architectural styles reflect social status
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 건물을 만드는 것 같지만 실제로는 건물이 인간을 형성한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 터키의 괴베클리 테페 유적을 짓기 위해 수렵 채집인이 정착하게 되면서 농경 사회가 형성된 사례를 통해, 건축의 발전이 사회적 발전을 이끈다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 개인들이 다양한 종류의 건물을 짓는 과정에 참여한다
② 농경 사회가 수렵 채집 사회로 전환되었다
③ 건축적 진보가 사회적 발전을 이끈다
④ 사회 구조가 건물의 설계에 영향을 미친다
⑤ 건축 양식이 사회적 지위를 반영한다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. Considering most of time we are the (A)[passengers / pilots], you can understand this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a plane crash are not (B)[higher / lower] than the odds of dying in a car crash. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, real situations (C)[contradict / match] this assumption. Most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
questions.explanation: 비행 공포는 통제력 부족에서 오는데, 우리가 보통 조종사가 아닌 '승객(passengers)'이기 때문입니다. 논리적으로 비행기 사고 확률이 자동차보다 '높지(higher)' 않음에도 불구하고, 사람들의 실제 선택은 불안감을 최소화하는 쪽으로 기울어 논리적 가정과 '상반(contradict)'됩니다.
options_translation: ① 승객 - 더 높은 - 일치하다
② 승객 - 더 높은 - 상반되다(모순되다)
③ 승객 - 더 낮은 - 상반되다(모순되다)
④ 조종사 - 더 높은 - 일치하다
⑤ 조종사 - 더 낮은 - 일치하다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 "linguistic castration"이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of tool making said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "<u>linguistic castration</u>." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
options: ① 인간이 각 동물이 가진 특성과 능력을 물리적으로 어떻게 빼앗는지 설명하는 생물학 용어
② 인간과 같은 방식의 동물 행위를 다르게 명명하여 동물을 낮게 평가하는 것
③ 실제 침팬지의 지능이 인간보다 낮다는 것을 보여 주는 그들의 언어 사용법
④ 인간과 동물 모두 공통으로 가지는 본능에 의한 행동을 지칭하는 말
⑤ 동물에게 인간과 같은 언어 능력이 없다는 것
questions.explanation: 프란스 드 발은 인간이 다른 동물과의 유사성을 폄하하고 인간의 우월성을 유지하기 위해 교묘한 언어를 사용한다고 비판합니다. '언어적 거세(linguistic castration)'란 동물의 인간적인 행동(키스, 친구, 도구 제작 등)을 전문 용어로 대체하거나 본능으로 치부함으로써 동물의 능력을 약화시키고 인간과 거리를 두는 행태를 의미합니다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 "linguistic castration"이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of tool making said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "<u>linguistic castration</u>." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
options: ① 인간이 각 동물이 가진 특성과 능력을 물리적으로 어떻게 빼앗는지 설명하는 생물학 용어
② 인간과 같은 방식의 동물 행위를 다르게 명명하여 동물을 낮게 평가하는 것
③ 실제 침팬지의 지능이 인간보다 낮다는 것을 보여 주는 그들의 언어 사용법
④ 인간과 동물 모두 공통으로 가지는 본능에 의한 행동을 지칭하는 말
⑤ 동물에게 인간과 같은 언어 능력이 없다는 것
questions.explanation: 프란스 드 발(Frans de Waal)은 인간이 동물과의 유사성을 폄하하고 인간의 우월적 지위를 유지하기 위해 사용하는 언어적 기법을 '언어적 거세(linguistic castration)'라고 불렀습니다. 이는 침팬지의 '키스'를 '입과 입의 접촉'으로, '친구'를 '선호하는 제휴 파트너'로 부르는 등 인간과 같은 행동을 기술적인 용어를 사용하여 의도적으로 소외시키고 낮게 평가하는 것을 의미합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 내용으로 알 수 있는 것만을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation. If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. While the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a protective mechanism for the foot. Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now contract quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object. Sensory and motor nerves control almost all functions in the body - from the beating of the heart to the movement of the gut, sweating and just about everything else.
vocabulary_box: ⓐThe rate at which a specific sensation is relayed to the brain depends on the unique capabilities of nerve endings in the tissues.
ⓑOur body's ability to reduce pain serves as a defensive mechanism to prevent accidents that could result in more severe pain.
ⓒVerbal reactions to pain are intentional responses designed to warn others of potential danger.
ⓓThe process that pain sensation is transmitted to the brain is our innate function to protect our body.
ⓔSensory and motor nerves work together to regulate and coordinate the body's various processes and activities.
questions.explanation: 지문은 통증이 신체를 보호하는 기제로 작용함을 설명하며(ⓓ), 감각 신경과 운동 신경이 신체의 다양한 기능을 조절하고 통합한다고 언급합니다(ⓔ). ⓐ(신호 전달 속도가 신경 말단의 능력에 달려 있다는 내용), ⓑ(고통을 '줄이는' 능력에 대한 내용), ⓒ(언어적 반응이 타인에게 경고하기 위한 '의도적' 반응이라는 내용)은 지문에서 언급되지 않았거나 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ⓐ 특정 감각이 뇌에 전달되는 속도는 조직 내 신경 말단의 고유한 능력에 달려 있다.
ⓑ 통증을 줄이는 우리 몸의 능력은 더 심한 통증을 유발할 수 있는 사고를 예방하는 방어 기제 역할을 한다.
ⓒ 통증에 대한 언어적 반응은 타인에게 잠재적 위험을 알리기 위해 설계된 의도적인 반응이다.
ⓓ 통증 감각이 뇌로 전달되는 과정은 우리 몸을 보호하기 위한 타고난 기능이다.
ⓔ 감각 신경과 운동 신경은 신체의 다양한 과정과 활동을 조절하고 조정하기 위해 함께 작동한다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, few of them ____________ _______________. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
options: ② are subject to constant criticism from other people
③ can dismiss the stream of feedback from non-experts
④ are challenged by those with no professional background
⑤ continually seek opportunities to learn and grow in their field
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 스포츠 전문가들이 일반인(비전문가)들로부터 끊임없이 훈수나 조언을 듣는 상황을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 앞에 부정어 'few'가 있으므로, '전문가들 중 비전문가들의 피드백을 무시할 수 있는 사람은 거의 없다'는 의미가 되어야 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 '비전문가의 피드백을 무시하다'라는 뜻의 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자격 없는 조언으로 고심한다
② 타인으로부터의 끊임없는 비판의 대상이 된다
③ 비전문가들로부터 나오는 피드백의 흐름을 무시할 수 있다
④ 전문적인 배경이 없는 사람들에게 도전을 받는다
⑤ 자신의 분야에서 배우고 성장할 기회를 지속적으로 찾는다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providing students with relevant texts (A)[that / what] they will be interested in. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and (B)[discovered / discovering] ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books." The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read (C)[voracious / voraciously] to find out more.
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤에 전치사 in의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절이 오며, 선행사 'relevant texts'가 존재하므로 관계대명사 that이 적절합니다. (B) 문맥상 '독서를 피하고 우회할 방법을 찾아냈을 것(had avoided ... and [had] discovered)'이라는 예상을 나타내므로, 과거분사 discovered가 avoided와 병렬 구조를 이룹니다. (C) 동사 read를 수식해야 하므로 부사인 voraciously(탐욕스럽게, 많이)가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① that / 발견했다 / 탐욕스럽게
② that / 발견하는 것 / 탐욕스럽게
③ that / 발견하는 것 / 탐욕스러운
④ what / 발견했다 / 탐욕스럽게
⑤ what / 발견하는 것 / 탐욕스러운

questions.question: 23. 다음 글에서 ⓐ~ⓔ가 의미하는 넔로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may ⓐ<u>feel disoriented</u> when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. At this stage ⓑ<u>their understanding is quite literal</u>, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between ⓒ<u>validating children's past experiences</u> and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in ⓓ<u>a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are</u>. This contributes to ⓔ<u>building a sense of community</u>, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
options: ② ⓑ: Children aged 3-6 do not have enough capacity to imagine what will happen
③ ⓒ: prioritizing what children have experienced before moving
④ ⓓ: manner that regards children's past as a trivial aspect of their identity
⑤ ⓔ: creating a physical space where community members gather
questions.explanation: ⓐ의 'feel disoriented'는 일상이 무너지고 친숙한 것이 사라졌을 때 눠기는 혼란수러와 고립감을 의미합니다. 따라서 ①이 가장 적절합니다. ⓑ은 문자 굠대로 이해한다는 것이지 상상력이 부접하다는 것과는 거리가 있을 수 있으며, ⓒ는 과거 경험을 제대로 인정해 주는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ⓐ: 고립감을 경험함
ⓑ: 3-6세 아이들은 일어날 일을 상상할 충분한 능력이 없음
ⓒ: 이사하기 전에 아이들이 경험한 것에 우선순위를 됨
ⓓ: 아이들의 과거를 정체성의 사쇌한 면으로 여기는 방식
ⓔ: 곭체 굤성원들이 모이는 물리적 곞간을 만듬

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 적절한 제목을 <조건>에 맞춰 완성하시오.
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it - you just see the blurred outline of the moving string. How strings vibrate on their own makes little noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. But if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note is heard loud and clear. The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. When the waves reach your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string.
subjective_conditions: ㆍ반드시 본문 단어를 이용해야 하며 필요시 형태를 변형 가능
ㆍ빈칸 각각 1단어로 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 본문은 기타 줄의 진동이 기타 몸통(hollow box)을 통해 어떻게 증폭되어 소리가 들리는지 설명하고 있다. 줄 자체의 진동은 미미하지만 기타 몸통을 통해 공기 압력의 파동이 강해지는 과정을 설명하므로 제목으로는 '기타가 소리를 증폭시키는 방법'이 적절하다. 본문의 'How'와 'amplified'를 변형한 'amplifies'를 사용한다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Sensory and motor nerves govern and operate together to act as a protective mechanism for the body parts. If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, sensory nerve endings in the skin, which pick up a particular sensation, will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now contract quickly, to lift your foot away from the painful object. The same thing happens when you touch a hot surface. This is how sensory nerves detect stimuli that can damage the body and motor nerves bring about rapid responses to protect the body.
options: ① Both sensory and motor nerves function to keep your body from painful stimuli.
② Painful stimuli make your body react before your brain perceives them.
③ The reaction rate varies depending on the intensity of the stimuli.
④ The primary function of motor nerves is to regulate body temperature.
⑤ Pain receptors in the skin are more important than other types of sensory nerves.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 감각 신경(sensory nerves)이 위험한 자극을 감지하고, 운동 신경(motor nerves)이 이에 신속하게 반응하여 신체를 보호하는 메커니즘을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 감각 신경과 운동 신경 모두 고통스러운 자극으로부터 신체를 지키는 기능을 한다는 ①번이 요지로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 감각 신경과 운동 신경 모두 고통스러운 자극으로부터 신체를 보호하는 기능을 한다.
② 고통스러운 자극은 뇌가 그것들을 인지하기 전에 몸이 반응하게 만든다.
③ 반응 속도는 자극의 강도에 따라 달라진다.
④ 운동 신경의 주요 기능은 체온을 조절하는 것이다.
⑤ 피부의 통증 수용체는 다른 유형의 감각 신경보다 더 중요하다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn by seeing, hearing, and even when it is not directly addressed to them. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to choose the right path even when easier or more appealing options are available. Remember that children do not build strong character just by being told what is right. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore, demonstrate good examples for your child through your actions. By displaying these examples, we can teach our children the importance of respecting others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
options: ① the necessity of parental modeling in nurturing their children
② best ways to resist temptation when making decisions
③ how to teach children to live by established laws
④ disruptions to individuals maintaining important values in life
⑤ the essential values and attitudes that children should seek out
questions.explanation: 아이들은 부모의 말뿐만 아니라 행동을 보고 배우므로, 부모가 직접 좋은 본보기를 보여주는 것이 자녀 교육과 가치관 형성에 필수적이라는 내용을 다루고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 자녀를 양육할 때 부모의 모델링(본보기)의 필요성
② 의사결정을 할 때 유혹에 저항하는 최선의 방법
③ 아이들에게 정해진 법에 따라 살도록 가르치는 방법
④ 삶에서 중요한 가치를 유지하는 개인들에 대한 방해 요소들
⑤ 아이들이 추구해야 할 필수적인 가치와 태도

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly ⓐ<u>possible</u> to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate roles, resulting in ⓑ<u>minimized</u> boundary crossings. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these  ⓒ<u>segmenters</u> carrying two phones ─ one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they ⓓ<u>hinder</u> distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer ⓔ<u>incorporating</u> work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.explanation: 일과 가정을 분리하려는 사람들(분할자)에게 유연한 시간표가 잘 맞는 이유는 업무 시간과 다른 역할 간의 구분을 '방해(hinder)'하기 때문이 아니라 '가능하게(enable/allow)' 하기 때문입니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 hinder는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons are the examples of common crystal habits. (A) Crystals normally form when liquids cool like when you create ice cubes. (B) Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. (C) If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they /can form strange, twisted shapes. (D) Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. (E) This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
questions.insertion_sentence: We can see beautiful displays when conditions are right.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 조건이 적절할 때 아름다운 모습(결정)을 볼 수 있다는 내용입니다. (B)와 (C)에서는 결정이 완벽한 모양을 갖추지 못하는 경우를 설명하고 있으며, (D) 뒤의 문장에서는 '이것은(Usually, this involves...)' 결정이 완벽하게 형성되기 위한 느리고 안정적인 환경을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 완벽하고 아름다운 결정이 형성되는 긍정적인 조건을 설명하기 시작하는 위치인 (D)에 주어진 문장이 들어가는 것이 흐름상 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are ─ writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. ⓐYou could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well, one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. ⓑWriting brilliant essays requires extensive practice and dedication. ⓒSome people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. ⓓHowever ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. ⓔThe performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 자신의 가치를 결정하는 '능력'을 어떻게 정의하는지, 그리고 그 능력이 자아 존중감의 유일한 결정 요인이 될 때 발생하는 문제에 대해 다루고 있습니다. ⓑ는 훌륭한 에세이를 쓰는 데 연습과 헌신이 필요하다는 내용으로, 능력의 정의나 자아 가치와의 연관성이라는 전체 주제에서 벗어난 구체적이고 지엽적인 서술입니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status ─ they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers may not be completely locked in to the product. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.
questions.summary_sentence: While a complementary good consumed alongside another product experiences (A)___________ sales when its counterpart becomes popular, perfect complementarity is not always (B)___________.(A)
questions.explanation: 보완재는 한 제품의 인기가 높아지면 함께 매출이 증가하므로 (A)에는 '증가된, 향상된' 뜻의 enhanced가 적절합니다. 또한 글의 후반부에서 보완재가 완벽하게 묶여 있지 않을 수 있다는 예시(가솔린 차에서 전기차로 전환)를 들고 있으므로, 완벽한 보완 관계가 항상 보장되는 것은 아니라는 의미에서 (B)에는 guaranteed가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 늘어난 - 부정된
② 감소된 - 약속된
③ 안정적인 - 확보된
④ 높아진 - 회피된
⑤ 향상된 - 보장된

questions.question: 19. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providingstudents with ⓐ<u>interesting</u> texts, which are relevant to them. The work of Rosalie Fink ⓑ<u>has influenced</u> my scholarly work and my teaching. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and ⓒ<u>discovering</u> ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found these dyslexics ⓓ<u>enthusiastic</u> in reading... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books." The pattern ⓔ<u>which</u> Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장은 'Rosalie Fink가 피실험자들이 읽기를 피하고 읽기를 우회하는 법을 찾아냈을 것(find that they had avoided reading and found/discovered ways...)'이라고 예상했다는 내용입니다. 이때 ⓒ는 앞의 had avoided와 병렬 구조를 이루거나, 혹은 expected to find that 절 내에서 find의 목적어인 that절 동사들과 연결되어야 합니다. 문맥상 그들이 '우회할 방법을 찾아냈을 것'이라고 생각했다는 뜻이므로 'discovered' 또는 'found'의 과거완료 형태 병렬인 discovered가 적절합니다. 본문 원문상으로는 'expected to find that they had avoided reading and (had) discovered'의 흐름입니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 Rosalie Fink의 실험 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞추어 쓰시오.
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providingstudents with ⓐ<u>interesting</u> texts, which are relevant to them. The work of Rosalie Fink ⓑ<u>has influenced</u> my scholarly work and my teaching. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and ⓒ<u>discovering</u> ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found these dyslexics ⓓ<u>enthusiastic</u> in reading... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books." The pattern ⓔ<u>which</u> Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.
questions.summary_sentence: Rosalie Fink's research found that contrary to the expectation, _____________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 표현을 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
<보기>의 표현을 제외한 다른 표현을 추가하지 말 것
필요한 경우 어형 변화를 할 것
vocabulary_box: enthusiastic / can / personal interest / readers / pursue / people / of / become / subjects / with dyslexia / when
questions.answer: people with dyslexia could become enthusiastic readers when pursuing subjects of personal interest
questions.explanation: 실험의 핵심은 난독증이 있는 사람들이라도 개인적인 관심 분야의 주제를 읽을 때는 열정적인 독자가 될 수 있다는 발견입니다. 주어진 단어들을 활용하여 '난독증이 있는 사람들이 개인적인 관심의 주제들을 추구할 때 열정적인 독자가 될 수 있다'는 문장을 완성합니다. <조건>에 따라 'can'을 'could'로, 'pursue'를 'pursuing'으로 어형 변화하여 문맥을 맞춥니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations ─ surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue ─ with one notable (A)__________. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that minor deviations from the norm are judged positively because they suggest that the individual is (B)__________ enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.explanation: (A) 사람들은 보통 기대에 부합하는 옷차림을 선호하지만, 약간의 규범을 깨는 행위가 긍정적으로 작용하는 '예외(exception)'가 존재한다는 내용입니다. (B) 규범에서 약간 벗어나는 행동은 그 개인이 그러한 행동의 사회적 비용을 감수할 만큼 '강력하다(powerful)' 혹은 능력이 있다는 것을 암시하기 때문에 긍정적으로 평가받는다는 결론입니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the brain as a bustling city. If you gazed over a cityscape and wondered, "Where is the economy situated?" you'd realize there isn't a straightforward answer. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the store and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
options: ① The Role of Neurons in Brain Operation
② How the Brain Differentiates Sense From Reality
③ The Impact of the Economy on Brain Development
④ A Brain as a City: Understanding the Complex Interactions
questions.explanation: 뇌의 작동 방식을 도시의 경제 활동에 비유하여, 특정 지점이 아니라 다양한 요소들의 상호작용을 통해 결과가 도출된다는 내용을 담고 있으므로 '도시로서의 뇌: 복잡한 상호작용 이해하기'가 제목으로 적절합니다.
options_translation: 뇌 작동에서 뉴런의 역할
뇌가 감각과 현실을 구별하는 방법
경제가 뇌 발달에 미치는 영향
도시로서의 뇌: 복잡한 상호작용 이해하기

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product. You can also predict whether she will keep it or return it. You'll determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
options: ① Advertising through online media has a huge impact on the sale of the products.
② The role of the customer satisfaction department should be strengthened.
③ It is necessary to study various promotional methods to sell as much as you can.
④ Highlighting only the advantages of a product leads to a loss of consumer trust.
⑤ Understanding post-purchase behavior helps ensure customer satisfaction and prevent negative word-of-mouth.
questions.explanation: 구매 후 고객의 행동과 만족도를 파악하는 것이 재구매 여부, 제품 반품 여부, 타인에게 추천 여부 등을 결정짓는 중요한 요소이며, 특히 지인들의 추천(입소문)이 광고보다 더 큰 신뢰를 얻기 때문에 지속적인 고객 만족 모니터링이 부정적인 입소문을 피하는 길이라는 내용입니다. 따라서 5번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 온라인 매체를 통한 광고는 제품 판매에 큰 영향을 미친다.
② 고객 만족 부서의 역할이 강화되어야 한다.
③ 가능한 많이 팔기 위해 다양한 홍보 방법을 연구할 필요가 있다.
④ 제품의 장점만을 강조하는 것은 소비자 신뢰의 상실로 이어진다.
⑤ 구매 후 행동을 이해하는 것은 고객 만족을 보장하고 부정적인 입소문을 방지하는 데 도움이 된다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. ⓐThe discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. ⓑIn the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. ⓒIf you hold a one-plus-one event, your sales will increase, but your profits will remain the same. ⓓThis shows that the more difficult it is for people to buy a product, the more try to buy it. ⓔThe findings are very meaningful because the test was conducted in a real supermarket, not in a laboratory. They have also affected the marketing strategies of various companies.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구매 수량을 제한하는 '희소성' 전략이 판매량을 증가시킨다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 그러나 ③번(ⓒ)은 1+1 행사가 판매량은 늘리지만 이윤은 그대로라는 내용으로, 구매 수량 제한에 따른 판매 촉진이라는 핵심 주제와 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
questions.passage: Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. Suppose there's a preschool boy who consistently hears from his father that ⓐ<u>he</u> is smart and a good helper. Praise would be very powerful for improving ⓑ<u>his</u> self-esteem. So, probably the father will help ⓒ<u>his</u> son to incorporate what he heard into the self-image. Thinking of ⓓ<u>himself</u> as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make ⓔ<u>him</u> more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 문맥상 '미취학 아동인 소년(a preschool boy)'을 지칭합니다. 반면 ⓒ 'his'는 소년의 아버지(his father)를 지칭하여 소년의 아버지가 자신의 아들을 돕는다는 의미를 나타냅니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. Although it may seem sensible, having two separate calendars for work and personal life can ____________________. To check if something is missing, you will find yourself checking your to-do lists multiple times. Instead, organize all of your tasks in one place. It doesn't matter if you use digital or paper media. It's okay to keep your professional and personal tasks in one place. This will give you a good idea of how time is divided between work and home. This will allow you to make informed decisions about which tasks are most important.
options: ③ lead you not to be confused
④ prevent you from being distracted
⑤ be helpful for organizing your tasks systematically
questions.explanation: 업무용과 개인용 달력을 분리해서 사용하면 누락된 것이 있는지 확인하기 위해 여러 번 할 일 목록을 확인하게 된다고 언급하고 있습니다. 이는 비효율성을 초래하므로 빈칸에는 '시간을 낭비하게 만들 수 있다'는 내용의 ①번이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 시간을 낭비하게 만든다
② 당신의 업무 우선순위를 정하는 데 도움을 준다
③ 당신이 혼란스럽지 않게 해준다
④ 당신이 산만해지는 것을 막아준다
⑤ 당신의 과업들을 체계적으로 정리하는 데 도움이 된다

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad.
ordered_passages: (A) Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods.

(B) The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.

(C) There are, however, combinations of scores that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 음식을 단순히 좋고 나쁨으로 나눌 수 없다고 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 하지만 건강에 좋거나 나쁜 '조합'은 존재한다며 소위 '좋은' 음식만 먹는 성인의 사례를 든다. (A)에서 그 사례가 충분한 영양소를 공급하지 못해 건강하지 않을 수 있음을 지적하고, 이어서 가끔 튀긴 치킨을 먹는 십대의 반대 사례를 소개한다. (B)에서 그 십대의 식단은 망가지지 않지만, 매일 튀긴 음식과 간식을 먹는 사람의 식단이 나쁘다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓗ 중 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions ⓐ<u>are</u> well-documented.
