Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem ⓑ<u>that</u> didn't get ⓒ<u>written</u> because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example ⓓ<u>has</u> happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was ⓔ<u>visiting</u> by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work ⓕ<u>unfinished</u>. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions ⓖ<u>what</u> have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, ⓗ<u>slow</u> down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.*lament 슬퍼하다
questions.explanation: 어법상 어색한 것은 총 4개입니다.ⓓ has happened -> happened: 'in 1797'이라는 명확한 과거 시점이 있으므로 현재완료가 아닌 과거형을 써야 합니다.ⓔ visiting -> visited: 문맥상 예상치 못한 손님에 의해 '방문을 받은(수동)' 것이므로 과거분사형이 적절합니다.ⓖ what -> that/which: 선행사 cases/disruptions를 수식하는 관계대명사 자리이며, 선행사가 있으므로 what을 쓸 수 없습니다.ⓗ slow -> slowing: 분사구문 자리로, 뒤의 increasing과 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 현재분사 slowing이 적절합니다.(ⓐ are(복수주어 costs), ⓑ that(관계사), ⓒ written(수동태), ⓕ unfinished(목적보어)는 옳습니다.)

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when ______________________________.*envision: 계획하다
options: ① temptation for immediate pleasure disappears
② there is a desire to pursue immediate satisfaction
③ they are persuaded to do so by someone they trust
④ the reward for the temporary action is not satisfactory
⑤ the bank interest rates are not higher than they think
questions.explanation: 사람들이 미래를 위해 저축을 하지만 의지박약으로 인해 당장의 즐거움을 위해 미리 돈을 써버리는 경우를 설명하고 있습니다. 즉, 최대의 이익을 위해 특정 방식으로 돈을 쓰기로 결심했더라도 '즉각적인 만족을 추구하려는 욕구가 있을 때' 다르게 행동한다는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 즉각적인 즐거움에 대한 유혹이 사라질 때
② 즉각적인 만족을 추구하려는 욕구가 있을 때
③ 그들이 신뢰하는 누군가에 의해 그렇게 하도록 설득될 때
④ 일시적인 행동에 대한 보상이 만족스럽지 않을 때
⑤ 은행 이자율이 그들이 생각하는 것보다 높지 않을 때

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled human development.
questions.summary_sentence: Although the hunter-gatherer lifestyle was (A)__________ in terms of food availability and health, the development of agriculture and permanent settlements during the New Stone Age significantly increased population density and paved the way for the rise of (B)__________.
questions.explanation: 사냥 개번 생ᄒᅠᆯ은 강가아 거나 건강 면개서 이로어다(beneficial)는 내용이 제시더어 이고, 뇨어ᄇ가 저자ᄀ 생ᄒᅠᆯ으는 인구 밀도를 노피고 문먕(civilization)의 걸파늘 마련해다는 내용이 가강 저ᄀ절하므로 (A)는 beneficial, (B)는 civilization이 드러가야 하ᄆ하.
options_translation: ① 이로운 - 문먕
② 겨냐ᄁ한 - 계묭
③ 멸절 위기에 꺼힌 - 면대하
④ 구저ᄀ절한 - 도시하
⑤ 이로운 - 사너ᄇ하

questions.question: 9. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting.
ordered_passages: (A) This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.

(B) Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise.

(C) The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 brainwriting이라는 과정을 소개하고 이고, (C)에서 그 과정의 초기 단계(The initial steps)인 개별 아이디어 생산 마냐 평가를 설먕하ᄆ하. 그 다으마로 (B)의 'Only then'(그러고 나서야 비로소)를 혀브로 하매 티ᄆ이 모여 선태ᄀ하는 단계를 연갤하며, 마지마ᄀ으로 (A)에서 이러한 brainwriting 과정의 자ᄆ저ᄆ가 의의를 정리하는 거시 자연사러ᄇ스ᄆ하.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.\n*cortex: (대뇌) 피질(皮質)\n**hippocampus: (대뇌 측두엽의) 해마
options: ① Few scientific studies show that focused attention can reshape the brain.
② Animals rewarded for detecting sounds, such as those that hunt or avoid predators, develop significantly larger visual centers in their brains.
③ Brain scans of violinists also reveal substantial growth in the regions of the cortex that control the left hand, which must finger the strings precisely and swiftly.
④ Additional research indicates that taxi drivers have an enlarged hippocampus, trivial for spatial memory.
⑤ The brain's physical structure adapts regardless of where we focus our attention and what activities we practice.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 바이올리니스트의 뇌 스캔 결과, 현을 정교하고 빠르게 짚어야 하는 왼손을 담당하는 피질 부위가 크게 성장하고 확장되었음을 보여준다고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 ③번이 글의 내용과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 집중된 주의가 뇌를 재구성할 수 있다는 것을 보여주는 과학적 연구는 거의 없다.
② 사냥을 하거나 포식자를 피하기 위해 소리를 감지하는 것에 대해 보상을 받는 동물들은 뇌에 상당히 더 큰 시각 센터를 발달시킨다.
③ 바이올리니스트의 뇌 스캔은 또한 현을 정교하고 신속하게 짚어야 하는 왼손을 조절하는 피질 영역의 상당한 성장을 드러낸다.
④ 추가적인 연구는 택시 운전사들이 공간 기억에 사소한(trivial), 확대된 해마를 가지고 있음을 나타낸다.
⑤ 뇌의 물리적 구조는 우리가 어디에 주의를 집중하고 어떤 활동을 연습하는지에 상관없이 적응한다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 제목으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show that you care. If you notice someone who is lonely, you could go and sit with them. If you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. A person's happiness comes from attention. There are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. Even if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
options: ① The Power of small acts of kindness
② Fostering happiness through everyday actions
③ The significance of social interaction in daily Life
④ Creating connection: How attention transforms lives
⑤ Showing you care: simple ways to make a indifference
questions.explanation: 이 글은 타인에 대한 작은 관심과 친절이 그들에게 얼마나 큰 힘이 되고 행복을 주는지에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ③번 '일상생활에서 사회적 상호작용의 의의'는 글의 구체적인 핵심인 '타인에 대한 작은 배려와 관심의 긍정적 효과'를 충분히 반영하기에는 너무 포괄적이고 일반적인 제목입니다. (참고: 5번의 'indifference'는 'difference'의 오타로 추정되나, 제공된 정답지에 따라 3번을 정답으로 선택합니다.)
options_translation: ① 작은 친절의 힘
② 일상적인 행동을 통해 행복을 가꾸기
③ 일상생활에서 사회적 상호작용의 의의
④ 관계 만들기: 관심이 어떻게 삶을 변화시키는가
⑤ 당신이 관심을 갖고 있음을 보여주기: 무관심(차이)을 만드는 간단한 방법

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically (A)[increase / diminish] how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were (B)[banned / empowered] to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control (C)[raised / worsened] how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
questions.explanation: (A) 직원들에게 주체성을 주는 것은 에너지와 집중력을 '증가(increase)'시킵니다. (B) 예시에서 노동자들은 결정권을 '부여받은(empowered)' 사례입니다. (C) 통제권을 주는 것은 자제력을 '높였다(raised)'는 흐름이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 증가시키다 / 금지된 / 높였다
② 증가시키다 / 권한이 부여된 / 높였다
③ 증가시키다 / 금지된 / 악화시켰다
④ 감소시키다 / 권한이 부여된 / 악화시켰다
⑤ 감소시키다 / 금지된 / 악화시켰다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르면? [2.9점]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, ______________________________ In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① environmental damage threatens the whole of civilization.
② we would need to plant trees to reduce his carbon footprint.
③ digital business activities can still threaten the environment.
④ we have developed our fossil fuel infrastructure and network for decades.
⑤ to improve my digital nutrition, I turn off my mobile phone while spending time with my family.
questions.explanation: 디지털 비즈니스로의 전환이 종이 사용을 줄여 환경에 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 것으로 기대되지만, 실제로는 인터넷과 데이터 센터 운영에 막대한 전기와 화석 연료가 소모되어 탄소 배출을 증가시킨다는 통념에 대한 반박의 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 디지털 비즈니스 활동이 여전히 환경을 위협할 수 있다는 내용의 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 환경 파괴는 인류 문명 전체를 위협한다.
② 우리는 탄소 발자국을 줄이기 위해 나무를 심어야 할 것이다.
③ 디지털 비즈니스 활동은 여전히 환경을 위협할 수 있다.
④ 우리는 수십 년 동안 화석 연료 기반 시설과 네트워크를 개발해 왔다.
⑤ 나의 디지털 영양 상태를 개선하기 위해 가족과 시간을 보낼 때 휴대폰을 끈다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: ______________________________ Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
options: ① Here are key life lessons kids learn from spending time with animals.
② The timing of migration seems to be controlled primarily by their parents.
③ Animals can reduce Ioneliness, increase feelings of social support, and boost your mood.
④ Genetic information is transmitted through different routes than cultural information.
⑤ Animals which had childhood come to learn about their surroundings.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린 시절(childhood)이 동물에게 주는 유연성과 홄경 적응 눙력에 대해 설명하고 읈습니다. 태어날 때부터 가지고 읈는 본능(하드웨어)에만 의존하는 동물은 환경 변화에 적응하기 어렵지만, 긴 어린 시절을 보내며 부모로부터 배우는 동물은 더 효율적인 경로를 찾고 변화에 유연하게 대처합니다. 따라서 비칸에는 어린 시절을 겪은 동물이 주변 환경에 대해 배우게 된다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 아이들이 동물과 시간을 보내며 배우는 주요한 삮의 교훈들이 여기 읈다.
② 이주 시기는 주로 괴들의 부모에 의해 제어되는 갃으로 밴인다.
③ 동물은 외로움을 줄이고, 사회적 지지를 느끼는 기분을 높이며, 기분을 북돋울 수 읈다.
④ 유전 정밴는 문화 정밴와는 다른 경로를 통해 전달된다.
⑤ 어린 시절을 보낸 동물들은 자신의 주변 환경에 대해 배우게 된다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment. This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies -capsaicin -touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure. All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real threat. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is to have the pain always directly associated with a pleasurable reward.
options: ① Humor works as a 'safe threat' by violating norms while still making us feel safe.
② The pleasurable feeling after a painful experience comes from the sense of control over the pain.
③ When capsaicin touches our tongue, our body does not trigger warning signals because we are not in danger.
④ Children start enjoying eating spicy food via repetitive exposure and learning that it does not pose a real threat to their bodies.
⑤ Scientists have trained animals by offering them rewards after a painful experience to develop a preference for chilli or self-destructive behaviors.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면, 고추의 캡사이신이 혀에 닿을 때 우리 몸은 화상을 입었을 때와 동일한 수용체를 자귱하여 '위험 신호(danger signals)'를 밴발한다고 했습니다. 단준히 실제로 안전하다는 것을 알기 때문에 즐거움을 느끼는 갃이지, 신호 자체가 밴생하준 않는 갃은 아닙니다. 따라서 ③번은 일치하준 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 해학(유머)은 괴범을 어기면서덄 여전히 우리를 안전하게 느끼게 함으로써 '안전한 위협'으로 작동한다.
② 고통스러운 경험 후의 즐거움은 고통에 대한 통제감에서 온다.
③ 캡사이신이 혀에 닿을 때, 우리는 위험에 처해 읈준 않기 때문에 몸이 경고 신호를 밴생시키준 않눤다.
④ 아이들은 반박적인 노출과 매운 음식이 실제 위협이 되준 않는다는 것을 배움으로써 매운 음식을 즐기기 시작한다.
⑤ 과학자들은 고통스러운 경험 후에 밴상을 제감함으로써 동물들이 고추를 선호하거나 자해 행동을 하도록 훈련시켔다.

questions.question: 23. 주어진 군 다음에 이어질 군의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities.
ordered_passages: (A) While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account.

(B) This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.

(C) As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 디지털 정보에 대한 장애인들의 필요가 무시되어 옔음을 언급합니다. (C)에서는 그 결과(As a result) 디지털 자원이 장애인들에게 무용지물이 된다고 설명하며, (A)에서는 상업적 웹 디자인과 달리 학자들의 프로젝트가 이러한 필요를 고려하준 않음을 지적합니다. 맞지막으로 (B)에서는 모든 사람을 고려한 디자인을 통해 이러한 상황이 개선될 수 있음을 제시하므로 (C)-(A)-(B) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 군의 밑줄 친 that과 쓰을이 가장 가까운 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so <u>that they never had to carry more than one child at a time</u>. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
options: ① Actors and actresses studied their scripts carefully so <u>that they could understand their characters</u>.
② Ms. Maru bought a holiday package <u>that includes a trip to an island</u>.
③ My suitcase had became damaged, so <u>that the lid would not stay closed</u>.
questions.explanation: 본문의 'so that~'은 '모마비 위하여(목적)'를 나타내는 접속사 구문입니다. ①번의 so that 또한 배우들이 캣릭터를 이해하기 위해 대발을 공부했다는 목적을 나타내므로 쓰을이 같습니다. ②번은 관계대명사, ③번은 결과를 나타내는 so that 구문(콤마가 있음)입니다.
options_translation: ① 배우들은 자신의 캣릭터를 이해할 수 있도록 대발을 제대로 공부했다.
② Maru 씨는 섬 여행이 포함된 휴가 패키준를 구매했다.
③ 내 여행 가방이 파섐되어서 뚜껑이 닫히준 않았다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities.
ordered_passages: (A) While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account.

(B) This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.

(C) As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 디지털 정보 보존에서 장애인의 필요가 소외되어 왔다는 문제를 제기합니다. (A)에서는 교육 기술 및 상업 디자인 전문가들은 진전이 있었으나 일부 학술 프로젝트는 여전히 이를 고려하지 않는다는 구체적 상황을 설명합니다. (C)는 그 결과(As a result)로 인해 시청각 장애인들에게 디지털 자원이 무용지물이 되는 부정적 결과를 나열합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 상황(This situation)을 개선하기 위해 모든 사용자를 고려해야 한다는 해결책을 제시하며 마무리되는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. ⓐWhen the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. ⓑThe grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. ⓒWithin the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. ⓓLike other tree squirrels, the eastern gray squirrel plays an important role in what's known as seed dispersal. ⓔGreys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 외래종인 회색다람쥐가 도입되면서 토착종인 붉은다람쥐가 멸종 위기에 처하게 된 경쟁 관계를 설명하고 있습니다. ⓓ는 회색다람쥐가 씨앗 퍼뜨리기에 중요한 역할을 한다는 생태적 장점을 언급하고 있어, 두 종간의 생존 경쟁과 붉은다람쥐의 위기라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글에서 전 흐름과 관계없는 것은?
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. ⓐFor example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. ⓑThis phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after a fictional community where "all the members are above average." ⓒThe community members actually have much influence on teenagers in real society due to their excellence. ⓓA survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. ⓔIn terms of ability to get along with others, the results were the same.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 자신이 평균보다 더 낫다고 믿는 경향인 '워비곤 호수 효과(Lake Wobegon effect)'에 관한 글입니다. 하지만 ⓒ는 실제 사회에서 가상의 지역 공동체 구성원들이 십대들에게 영향력을 행사한다는 내용으로, 글의 주제와 무관합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. The decline in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.
options: ① 네 살을 정도의 어린 나이부터 호기심이 증가한다.
② 호기심의 감소는 청소년기 이후의 뇌 발달에 원인이 있다.
③ 유아의 뇌는 성인의 뇌보다 더 적은 신경 연결을 가지고 있다.
④ 유아의 뉴런 간의 전달은 성인에 비해 훨씬 더 효율적이다.
⑤ 주기적으로 사용하지 않는 신경 경로는 제거된다.
questions.explanation: 지문 마지막 문장인 'the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away'를 통해 아이가 정기적으로 사용하지 않는 신경 경로는 제거(가지치기)된다는 것을 알 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 so it is with the brain's operation이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements ─ from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And <u>so it is with the brain's operation</u>: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
options: ① The brain functions independently without influence of other related elements.
② The brain, like a city, relies on the dynamic interplay between its parts to function.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 뇌의 작동 방식도 경제와 마찬가지로 특정 한 지점에서 일어나는 것이 아니라 모든 요소들의 상호작용을 통해 발생한다는 의미입니다. 따라서 뇌가 도시처럼 부품들 간의 역동적인 상호작용에 의존한다는 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌는 다른 관련 요소의 영향 없이 독립적으로 기능한다.
② 뇌는 도시와 마찬가지로 기능을 수행하기 위해 부품들 사이의 역동적인 상호작용에 의존한다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase ⓐ<u>productivity</u>, which is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way that production could be made more efficient, known as the "ⓑ<u>division</u> of labor." Making most manufactured goods involves several different processes using different skills. Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished. One worker could do all these tasks, and make 20 pins in a day. But this work can be divided into its ⓒ<u>distinct</u> processes, with a number of workers each performing one task. Because each worker ⓓ<u>undermines</u> one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day, which is a substantial ⓔ<u>increase</u> from the 200 they would have produced before.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 분업을 통해 각 노동자가 한 가지 작업에 '숙달하기(specializes)' 때문에 더 빠르게 일할 수 있다는 내용이 되어야 합니다. ⓓ의 'undermines(약화시키다)'는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although technology has the potential to increase productivity, ____________________________________________. For example, in many office environments workers sit at desks with computers and have access to the internet. They are able to check their personal e-mails and use social media whenever they want to. This can stop them from doing their work and make them less productive. Introducing new technology can also have a negative impact on production when it causes a change to the production process or requires workers to learn a new system. Learning to use new technology can be time consuming and stressful for workers and this can cause a drop in productivity.
options: ① it will make humans work more efficiently
② it can have a positive impact on productivity
③ it can have a negative impact on the environment
④ there is a possibility that it will take away human jobs
⑤ productivity may also suffer as a result of technology
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기술이 생산성을 높일 수 있는 잠재력이 있지만, 인터넷 접근을 통한 업무 방해나 새로운 시스템 학습의 스트레스 등으로 인해 생산성이 오히려 감소할 수 있다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 기술로 인해 생산성이 저하될 수 있다는 내용인 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그것은 인간이 더 효율적으로 일하도록 만들 것이다
② 그것은 생산성에 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있다
③ 그것은 환경에 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있다
④ 그것이 인간의 일자리를 빼앗아 갈 가능성이 있다
⑤ 기술의 결과로 생산성이 또한 저하될 수도 있다

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Companies large and small have off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers. Think about the things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company. ______________________________. For example, with air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
options: ① We now have our responsibility to complete them on our own
② They are still provided to us as part of customer service
③ They are no longer useful and valuable in our daily lives
④ We don't need them anymore due to advanced technologies
⑤ They have been automated, requiring no human intervention
questions.explanation: 컴퓨터 사회가 되어 여가 시간이 늘어날 것이라는 기대와 달리 기업들이 소비지에게 업무를 전가(off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers)하고 있으며, 예시로 항공권 예약이나 식료품 계산 등을 직접 해야 한다는 내용이 나오므로, 빈칸에는 '이제 우리는 그것들을 스스로 완료해야 할 책임을 진다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이제 우리는 그것들을 스스로 완료해야 할 책임을 진다
② 그것들은 여전히 고객 서비스의 일부로 우리에게 제공된다
③ 그것들은 우리 일상에서 더 이상 유용하거나 가치 있지 않다
④ 발전된 기술 덕분에 우리는 더 이상 그것들이 필요하지 않다
⑤ 그것들은 자동화되어 인간의 개입이 필요하지 않게 되었다

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, which then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly. As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you." If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler has been transmitted via our body. Strange as it may sound, this theory states that emotions arise from our bodies. For example, our mood can be improved by simply lifting up the corners of our mouth. If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, taking care not to let the pencil touch their lips (thus forcing the mouth into a smile-like shape), they judge cartoons funnier than if they have been asked to frown. The primacy of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase "I must be afraid, because I'm running."
questions.summary_sentence: Our bodily movements (A)___________ emotions, which is demonstrated by how smiling can (B)___________ our mood and make us perceive things funnier.
questions.explanation: 지문은 신체적인 움직임이 감정을 형성한다는 이론을 설명하고 있습니다. 미소를 지으면 기분이 좋아지고 상황을 더 재미있게 인식한다는 내용을 바탕으로 할 때, 신체적 움직임은 감정을 '형성(shape)'하고, 미소 짓는 것은 기분을 '강화/향상(enhance)'시킨다고 요약할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 형성하다 / 강화하다
② 증가시키다 / 유지하다
③ 유발하다 / 우울하게 하다
④ 억제하다 / 업그레이드하다
⑤ 제한하다 / 간과하다

questions.question: 11. 주어진 글(A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: (A) In one study, it is revealed that restricting the number of items customers can buy ⓐ<u>boosts</u> sales.
ordered_passages: (B) This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor ⓑ<u>was</u> it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.

(C) In that study, Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, ⓒ<u>to offer</u> Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents.

(D) The ⓓ<u>discounted</u> soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition, shoppers bought less cans than they ⓔ<u>are</u> in the scarce condition.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 한 연구가 판매를 촉진함을 보여준다고 시작합니다. (C)에서 그 연구(In that study)를 구체적으로 소개하며 코넬 대학교의 Brian Wansink 교수의 실험을 설명합니다. (D)에서 그 실험의 세 가지 조건(무제한, 4개 제한, 12개 제한)을 상세히 설명하고 결과를 보여줍니다. (B)에서 이 결과가 '희소성(scarcity)'이 판매를 장려함을 시사한다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 가장 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 12. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: (A) In one study, it is revealed that restricting the number of items customers can buy ⓐ<u>boosts</u> sales.(B) This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor ⓑ<u>was</u> it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.(C) In that study, Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, ⓒ<u>to offer</u> Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents.(D) The ⓓ<u>discounted</u> soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition, shoppers bought less cans than they ⓔ<u>are</u> in the scarce condition.
questions.explanation: ⓔ are는 앞에서 언급된 동사 bought를 대신하는 대동사가 되어야 합니다. 과거형 일반동사 bought를 대신하므로 did로 고쳐야 올바른 표현입니다.

questions.question: 15. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Up until about 6,000 years ago, most people were farmers. Many lived in different places throughout the year, hunting for food or moving their livestock to areas with enough food. There was no need to tell the time because life depended on natural cycles, such as the changing seasons or sunrise and sunset. Gradually more people started to live in larger settlements, and some needed to tell the time. For example, priests wanted to know when to carry out religious ceremonies. This was when people first invented clocks ─ devices that show, measure, and keep track of passing time. Clocks have been important ever since. Today, clocks are used for important things such as setting busy airport timetables ─ if the time is incorrect, aeroplanes might crash into each other when taking off or landing!
options: ① Why Modern People Need Watches Unlike in the Past
② How Successful People Manage Their Time Efficiently
③ Significant Difference between Farmer's Time and Pilot's Time
④ Relationship between Agricultural Society and Settlement Life
⑤ From Tragedies to Triumph: The Story of Safe Flight in Plane Crashes
questions.explanation: 과거 농경 사회에서는 자연의 주기에 따라 시간을 알 필요가 없었으나, 정착 생활이 시작되고 사회가 복잡해지면서 종교 의식이나 공항 시간표 관리 등 시간을 정밀하게 파악해야 할 필요성이 생겼다는 내용이므로, 과거와 달리 현대인이 시계를 필요로 하는 이유가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 과거와 달리 현대인들에게 시계가 필요한 이유
② 성공한 사람들이 시간을 효율적으로 관리하는 방법
③ 농부의 시간과 조종사의 시간 사이의 중대한 차이
④ 농경 사회와 정착 생활의 관계
⑤ 비극에서 승리까지: 비행기 추락 사고에서의 안전 비행 이야기

questions.question: 16. 윗글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Up until about 6,000 years ago, most people were farmers. Many lived in different places throughout the year, hunting for food or moving their livestock to areas with enough food. There was no need to tell the time because life depended on natural cycles, such as the changing seasons or sunrise and sunset. Gradually more people started to live in larger settlements, and some needed to tell the time. For example, priests wanted to know when to carry out religious ceremonies. This was when people first invented clocks ─ devices that show, measure, and keep track of passing time. Clocks have been important ever since. Today, clocks are used for important things such as setting busy airport timetables ─ if the time is incorrect, aeroplanes might crash into each other when taking off or landing!
options: ① Many farmers traveled around the year in search of food or to relocate their cattle to locations where there was enough of it.
② Because life depended on natural cycles, the farmers didn't need to know the time.
③ Larger communities with a growing population hardly required many residents to tell the time.
④ In order to determine when to perform religious rites, priests sought to know the time.
⑤ Important things like creating hectic airport schedules are done using clocks these days.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 인구가 늘어나고 더 큰 정착지에 살기 시작하면서 일부 사람들이 시간을 알 필요가 생겼다(some needed to tell the time)고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 대규모 공동체 주민들이 시간을 알 필요가 거의 없었다(hardly required)는 3번 설명은 내용과 반대됩니다.
options_translation: ① 많은 농부들이 음식을 찾거나 충분한 먹이가 있는 곳으로 가축을 옮기기 위해 일 년 내내 이동했다.
② 삶이 자연의 주기에 의존했기 때문에 농부들은 시간을 알 필요가 없었다.
③ 인구가 증가하는 더 큰 공동체는 많은 거주자들이 시간을 알 것을 거의 요구하지 않았다.
④ 종교 의식을 언제 수행할지 결정하기 위해 성직자들은 시간을 알고자 했다.
⑤ 오늘날 바쁜 공항 시간표를 만드는 것과 같은 중요한 일들은 시계를 사용하여 수행된다.

questions.question: 17. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for ⓐ<u>raising</u> your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and ⓑ<u>dismiss</u> false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to ⓒ<u>integrate</u> that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts. Also, it makes him ⓓ<u>increase</u> his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks, because he has self-trust out of his positive self-image. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him ⓔ<u>unwilling</u> to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
options: ① The Side Effects of Praise on Preschoolers' Self-Esteem
② The Importance of Self-Respect in Solving Challenging Tasks
③ The Power of Praise: Enhancing Preschoolers' Self-Regard and Behavior
④ The Challenges That Parents are Faced When Raising a Preschooler
⑤ Disciplining Preschoolers: Effective Techniques for Better Behavior
questions.explanation: 이 글은 칭찬이 아이들의 행동 개선뿐만 아니라 자존감(self-esteem)을 높이는 데 강력한 도구라는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 아이들은 부모의 말을 그대로 받아들여 긍정적인 자아 이미지를 형성하고, 이것이 어려운 과제에 도전하는 자신감으로 이어진다는 내용입니다. 따라서 3번 '칭찬의 힘: 미취학 아동의 자아 존중감과 행동 향상'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 칭찬이 미취학 아동의 자존감에 미치는 부작용
② 도전적인 과제를 해결하는 데 있어서 자존감의 중요성
③ 칭찬의 힘: 미취학 아동의 자존감과 행동 강화
④ 미취학 아동을 키울 때 부모가 직면하는 도전들
⑤ 미취학 아동 훈육하기: 더 나은 행동을 위한 효과적인 기술들

questions.question: 18. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for ⓐ<u>raising</u> your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and ⓑ<u>dismiss</u> false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to ⓒ<u>integrate</u> that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts. Also, it makes him ⓓ<u>increase</u> his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks, because he has self-trust out of his positive self-image. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him ⓔ<u>unwilling</u> to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 아이가 자신을 '좋은 조력자(good helper)'라고 생각하게 되면, 집이나 유치원에서 일을 돕겠다고 자원할 가능성이 높아져야 합니다. 따라서 '기꺼이 하는'이라는 의미의 willing이 적절하며, '꺼려하는'의 의미인 unwilling은 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel (A)[bonded to / isolated from] them. When they speak, others listen─even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. How could he be that rich? He has made (B)[more / less] money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. Likewise, when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. The reason we listen to him is because we (C) [disregard / appreciate] his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
options: ① danger of excessive trust on world-famous celebrities
② influence of professional excellence on public perception and trust
③ financial profits that Olympic medalists get from endorsements
④ importance of accurate knowledge of the product in advertisements
⑤ excellence of professionals in their knowledge of the products they promote
questions.explanation: 이 글은 특정 뵄야에서 훌륭한 성과를 내눠 전문가들이 다른 사람들에게 즉각적인 신뢰를 얻으며, 그들의 전문 뵄야와 관련 없는 뵄야에서조차 영향력을 발휘한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 'professional excellence(전문적 탁월함)'이 대중의 인식과 신뢰에 미치는 영향을 다룬 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 세계적으로 유명한 유명인에 대한 과도한 신뢰의 위험성
전문적 탁월함이 대중의 인식과 신뢰에 미치는 영향
올림픽 메달리스트들이 광고 협찬으로 얻는 재정적 이익
광고에서 제품에 대한 정확한 지식의 중요성
전문가들이 홍밴하는 제품에 대해 가지는 탁월한 지식

questions.question: 22. 윗글의 묘줄 친 (A), (B), (C)에서 묘맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel (A)[bonded to / isolated from] them. When they speak, others listen─even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. How could he be that rich? He has made (B)[more / less] money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. Likewise, when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. The reason we listen to him is because we (C) [disregard / appreciate] his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
questions.explanation: (A) 다른 사람들이 그들을 제경하고 닮고 싶어하므로 유대감(bonded to)을 눐깁니다. (B) 매우 부자인 선수는 경기를 해서 번 돈보다 광고(endorsements)로 '더 많은(more)' 돈을 버었습니다. (C) 배우가 추찜하는 차를 타는 이유는 그의 재능을 인정(감상)(appreciate)하기 때문입니다.
options_translation: (A) 유대감을 눐기는 (B) 더 적은 (C) 인정하다
(A) 유대감을 눐기는 (B) 더 많은 (C) 인정하다
(A) 유대감을 눐기는 (B) 더 많은 (C) 무시하다
(A) 고립된 (B) 더 적은 (C) 무시하다
(A) 고립된 (B) 더 많은 (C) 인정하다

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can ①<u>be labeled</u> as either good or bad. There are, however, combinations of foods ②<u>which</u> add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods ③<u>thought</u> of as "good"─for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients that we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise ④<u>stay</u> away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks e ⑤<u>has</u> a bad diet.
options: ① 다양한 방식의 조리법을 활용한 석단이 좋은 석단이다.
② 괠형 있는 석사는 옰리 몸에 더 많은 에너지를 줄 수 있다.
③ 석단의 좋고 나쁨은 석재료의 신선함을 기준으로 결정된다.
④ 석단의 건강성은 석단이 어떤 음식으로 구성되는지에 달려있다.
⑤ 석단을 다양한 음식으로 구성하는 것은 석욕 증진에 도움이 된다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 음식 개별 품목을 '좋은 음식' 혹은 '나쁜 음식'으로 나눠 라벨을 붙일 수 없유며, 건강한 식단은 음식의 조합과 구성에 달려 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 ④번이 가장 적절한 요지입니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 묘줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can ①<u>be labeled</u> as either good or bad. questions.explanation: ④번의 stay는 관계대명사 who의 선행사인 the teenager가 3인칭 단수이며, eats와 병갬 구조를 이뤄어야 하므로 stays로 고칀어야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of ___________________. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.*envision: 계획하다
questions.explanation: 이 글은 미래의 더 큰 보상을 위해 저축을 결심했음에도 불구하고, 눈앞의 즉각적인 유혹(여름 휴가 등) 때문에 저축한 돈을 미리 써버리는 상황을 설명하고 있다. 이는 결심한 바를 지키지 못하는 '의지의 박약(weakness of will)'의 사례에 해당한다.
options_translation: ① 비용 절감
② 효과적인 가치
③ 의지의 박약
④ 지연된 판단
⑤ 미래를 위한 준비

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when ___________________________, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
options: ① you have a right reason for your behavior
② your behavior and your identity perfectly match
③ you are already doing what people want you to do
④ your conscious and nonconscious self-images differ
⑤ you have a desire to change your identity for the better
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 행동이 정체성의 반영이라는 점이다. 자신의 정체성을 특정한 방식으로 믿게 되면 그에 맞춰 행동하기가 쉬워진다. 따라서 행동과 정체성이 완벽하게 일치할 때(your behavior and your identity perfectly match), 더 이상 행동 변화를 추구하는 것이 아니라 자신이 믿는 모습대로 행동하게 된다는 흐름이 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 행동에 정당한 이유가 있을 때
② 당신의 행동과 당신의 정체성이 완벽하게 일치할 때
③ 사람들이 당신이 하길 원하는 것을 당신이 이미 하고 있을 때
④ 당신의 의식적이고 무의식적인 자아상이 다를 때
⑤ 당신의 정체성을 더 좋게 바꾸고 싶은 욕망이 있을 때

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: In the 21st century, green marketing has become the mainstream. Society has become more concerned about the consequences of business practices and pushes companies to act more responsibly toward the environment and to ⓐ<u>reduce</u> the harm their business causes. As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more ⓑ<u>hazardous</u>. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a ⓒ<u>disappointing</u> step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is ⓓ<u>neglected</u>. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big. Organizations should be aware that ⓔ<u>unnecessary</u> use of email, cloud, or online documentation will be a part of environmental problems in the near future.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 ⓒ가 포함된 문장은 종이에서 디지털 문서로 전환하는 것이 나무를 구하기 위한 '긍정적인' 혹은 '유망한' 단계였다는 의미가 되어야 자연스럽습니다. 하지만 뒤이어 인터넷과 전기 사용으로 인한 환경적 비용(화석 연료 사용, 탄소 배출 등)이 간과되고 있다는 점을 지적하며 디지털화의 이면을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '실망스러운'이라는 뜻의 disappointing은 문맥상 어색하며, 'promising'이나 'positive'와 같은 낱말로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 연결어로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. (A)_____________, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, (B)_____________, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which (C)_____________ led to rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.*counterpart: (대응 관계에 있는) 상대
options: ① In particular ... in contrast ... consequently
③ Particularly ... on the other hand ... nevertheless
④ Instead ... first of all ... likewise
⑤ On the Contrary ... however ... accordingly
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 이동할 때 소지품을 다 챙겨야 한다는 일반적인 상황을 말하고, 뒤에서 어머니가 아이를 업어야 한다는 구체적인 예시(특히)를 들고 있으므로 'In particular'가 적절합니다. (B) 수렵 채집인과 대조되는 농경인의 상황을 설명하고 있으므로 'in contrast'가 적절합니다. (C) 출산 간격이 짧아져 더 많은 아이를 가질 수 있게 된 원인에 따른 결과로 인구 성장이 일어난 것이므로 'consequently'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 특히 ... 대조적으로 ... 결과적으로
② 구체적으로 ... 예를 들어 ... 가능성이 낮은
③ 특히 ... 반면에 ... 그럼에도 불구하고
④ 대신에 ... 우선 ... 마찬가지로
⑤ 반대로 ... 그러나 ... 그에 따라서

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening. (A) Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms, where we feel uncomfortable, but safe. (B) In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment. (C) When the active ingredient of chillies ─ capsaicin ─ touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. (D) Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure. (E) All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm.
questions.insertion_sentence: This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain: the closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'This reward-like effect'는 (B) 문장에서 언급된 'the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward'를 가리킵니다. 또한 (C) 이후부터 고추(chilli)를 먹는 구체적인 사례를 통해 이 보상과 같은 효과가 고통에 대한 숙달감에서 온다는 점을 설명하기 시작하므로 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 가리키는(또는 의미하는) 바가 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented ⓐ<u>them</u> when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because ⓑ<u>someone</u> knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from ⓒ<u>a dream</u> he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of ⓓ<u>sudden disruptions</u> that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, ⓔ<u>they</u> also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.*lament: 슬퍼하다
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 작업의 흐름을 깨는 '방해(interruptions, disruptions, someone knocking on the door)'와 관련된 대상을 가리킵니다. 반면 ⓒ 'a dream'은 시적 영감의 원천일 뿐 방해 요소가 아닙니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ 방해의 대가들
② ⓑ 문을 두드린 누군가 (방해 요소)
③ ⓒ 꿈 (영감의 원천)
④ ⓓ 갑작스러운 중단 (방해)
⑤ ⓔ 그것들 (갑작스러운 중단/방해)

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: A farm field is a completely artificial landscape; it is obliged to support a "monoculture," a single, designated plant type. (A) The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. (B) This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. (C) During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. (D) World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. (E) Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.*obliged monoculture: 단일 작물 재매**irrigation: (논,밭에) 물을 댐; 관개
questions.insertion_sentence: Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'these luxurious conditions'는 (D) 문장에서 언급한 풍부한 비료와 관개 시설을 갖춘 상태를 의미한다. 또한 'agricultural undesirables'가 뒤에 오는 (E)의 'every random weed'와 연결되므로 (E) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절하다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 빈칸 어느 곳에도 들어가기에 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and ___________ with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital ___________. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its ___________ was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the ___________ of the winners.
questions.explanation: 지문의 맥락상 빈칸에는 타 부족과의 '갈등(conflicts)', 군사적 '이점(advantage)', '상대(opponents)'보다 뛰어난 생각, 승리자의 '후손(descendants)' 등이 들어가야 한다. '책임(responsibility)'은 지문의 진화적 경쟁 구도와 관련이 없다.
options_translation: ① 책임
② 후손
③ 상대/적
④ 이점
⑤ 갈등

questions.question: 28. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs.
ordered_passages: (A) Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.(B) They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same.(C) One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 직원들에게 자율성을 주는 것의 효과를 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 이를 뒷받침하는 구체적인 연구 사례(오하이오 제조 공장)를 소개한다. (B)에서 그 연구에서 직원들이 구체적으로 어떤 결정권(유니폼 디자인, 교대 근무 권한)을 가졌는지 설명하고, (A)에서 그 결과 생산성이 향상되었다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 29. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible.
ordered_passages: (A) These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps.

(B) Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes.

(C) By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 어린 시절이 환경 학습과 유연성에 중요하다는 일반적 사실을 언급합니다. (B)에서 그 반대 사례로 어린 시절의 학습 없이 본능(하드웨어)에만 의존하는 철새들의 비효율적인 경로를 소개합니다. (A)의 'These birds'는 (B)에서 언급된 본능에 의존하는 새들을 가리키며, 환경 변화에 적응하지 못하는 구체적인 예시를 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 'By comparison'(대조적으로)을 통해 학습 기간(어린 시절)이 긴 새들의 유연성과 효율성을 강조하며 주제를 강화합니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed ①<u>abundant</u> food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very ②<u>few</u> diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was ③<u>hard</u> work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high ④<u>decrease</u> in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the ⑤<u>growth</u> of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.explanation: 문맥상 정착 생활과 농업의 발전은 인구 밀도의 '감소'가 아니라 '증가'를 가져왔습니다. 농경을 통해 더 많은 식량을 생산할 수 있게 되면서 인구가 밀집되었고, 이것이 도시와 문명의 발달로 이어졌다는 흐름이 적절합니다. 따라서 ④ decrease는 increase(증가) 또는 rise(상승)와 같은 단어로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 31. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the ⓐ<u>same</u> food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can ⓑ<u>adapt</u> its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can ⓒ<u>destroy</u> the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in ⓓ<u>limited</u> habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to ⓔ<u>extinction</u> in England.*edge: 우위 **acorn: 도토리
questions.explanation: 회색 다람쥐는 토착종인 붉은 다람쥐보다 더 다양한 서식지에서 더 밀집하여 살 수 있기 때문에 생존에 유리했다는 맥락입니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 '제한된(limited)' 서식지가 아니라 '다양한(varied)' 혹은 '더 넓은 범위의' 서식지에서 살 수 있었다는 표현이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
options: ① distinctions between human and animal senses
② discovery of new senses that detect external events
③ contradicting the conventional classifications of senses
④ impossibility of comprehending the animal sense systems
⑤ justification of Aristotelian theory on the sensing systems
questions.explanation: 이 글은 아리스토텔레스가 제시한 전통적인 5감 분류 체계에 의문을 제기하며, 인간과 동물의 감각이 단순히 다섯 가지로 나뉘기 어렵다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 감각의 전통적인 분류에 반박하는 내용인 ③이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간과 동물 감각의 차이점
② 외부 사건을 탐지하는 새로운 감각의 발견
③ 감각의 전통적인 분류에 대한 반박
④ 동물 감각 체계를 이해하는 것의 불가능성
⑤ 감각 체계에 관한 아리스토텔레스 이론의 정당화

questions.question: 10. 다음 글을 읽고 추론할 수 있는 것으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The decline in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.
options: ① Susan Engel states that curiosity starts to decline as early as four years old, continuing into adulthood, where we have more default settings.
② Brain development throughout childhood shows the gradual decrease in curiosity as neural connections become more efficient but less abundant.
③ Infants' perception of the world, is intensely affluent and well arranged due to their numerous yet inefficient neural connections.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 아기들의 세상에 대한 인식은 매우 풍부하지만 '엉망진창(wildly disordered)'이고 '비효율적(less efficient)'이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 인식이 '잘 정리되어 있다(well arranged)'고 말하는 ③번은 지문의 내용과 정반대되는 추론입니다.
options_translation: ① Susan Engel은 호기심이 4세만큼 일찍 감소하기 시작하여 성인기까지 이어지며, 성인기에는 더 많은 기본 설정(고정 관념)을 갖게 된다고 말한다.
② 유년기 동안의 뇌 발달은 신경 연결이 더 효율적으로 변하지만 그 수는 줄어들면서 호기심이 점차 감소함을 보여준다.
③ 유아들의 세상에 대한 인식은 수많지만 비효율적인 신경 연결 덕분에 매우 풍부하고 잘 정리되어 있다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they __________ the conscious mind, only becoming real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의식적인 마음과 잠재의식적인 마음의 차이를 설명하고 있습니다. 거미나 어둠에 대한 두려움과 같은 감정은 의식적인 마음에서 기인하지만(stem from), 잠재의식이 그러한 반응을 기록할 때 비로소 실제적인 두려움이 된다는 문맥이므로 ④번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 활성화하다
② 안정시키다
③ 보완하다
④ ~에서 기인하다
⑤ ~에서 사라지다

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they _____________________________. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
options: ① make the sensory neurons more sensitive
② bring the individual back to consciousness
③ stay in the cognitive processes of the brain
④ are clearly distinguished from internal stimuli
⑤ leave the individual in a state of unconsciousness
questions.explanation: 잠자는 동안 외부 자극이 감각기관을 통해 등록은 되지만, 뇌에서 정상적으로 처리되지 않기 때문에 감각적 이탈이 일어납니다. 따라서 이러한 자극들은 개별 개체를 무의식 상태(state of unconsciousness)에 머물게 한다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 감각 뉴런을 더 민감하게 만든다
② 개인을 다시 의식 상태로 되돌린다
③ 뇌의 인지 과정 속에 머무른다
④ 내부 자극과 명확하게 구별된다
⑤ 개인을 무의식 상태로 둔다

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 29번]
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and __________________________. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
options: ① grow the fear of making mistakes
② increase his willingness to challenge new things
③ strengthen his mind to employ only easy tricks
④ hesitate to try new and difficult tasks by himself
⑤ increase the tendency to taste food that has been experienced
questions.explanation: 칭찬이 아이의 자아존중감 형성에 큰 영향을 미친다는 내용입니다. 자신이 똑똑하다고 믿는 아이는 문제 해결을 위해 더 오래 견디고, 새로운 것에 도전하려는 의지가 강해진다는 맥락이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 실수에 대한 두려움을 키운다
② 새로운 것에 도전하려는 의지를 높인다
③ 쉬운 속임수만 쓰려는 마음을 강화한다
④ 스스로 새롭고 어려운 과제를 시도하기를 주저한다
⑤ 경험해 본 음식을 맛보려는 경향을 높인다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 40번]
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad. However, _____________________ ____________. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
options: ① foods should contain essential nutrients with minerals
② we can say what compositions of foods are good or bad
③ vegetarian diets are usually good for teenagers in general
④ basic ingredients for certain dishes used to be perceived as poisonous before
⑤ what people consider healthful cannot be the same in the various countries
questions.explanation: 음식 자체를 단순히 '좋다' 혹은 '나쁘다'로 규정할 수는 없지만, 식단의 구성(조합)에 따라 그것이 건강에 좋은지 나쁜지를 말할 수 있다는 내용입니다. 영양가가 높은 음식만 먹어도 다양성이 부족하면 건강한 식단이 아니며, 가끔 튀긴 닭을 먹어도 전체적인 식단이 균형 잡혀 있으면 문제가 되지 않는다는 예시가 이를 뒷받침합니다.
options_translation: ① 음식은 미네랄과 함께 필수 영양소를 포함해야 한다
② 우리는 어떤 음식의 구성이 좋고 나쁜지를 말할 수 있다
③ 채식 식단은 일반적으로 청소년들에게 보통 좋다
④ 특정 요리의 기본 재료들은 이전에 독이 있는 것으로 인식되곤 했다
⑤ 사람들이 건강에 좋다고 생각하는 것은 국가마다 같을 수 없다

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted.
ordered_passages: (A) The Thompson agency was the first to reposition yeast, which was previously known as the 'Soul of Bread,' as a vital nutrient source with numerous health benefits. Shortly after, the agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. As a result of these changes, sales of yeast increased.
(B) The Fleischmann's yeast manufacturer engaged the J. Walter thompson advertising agency to create a fresh marketing approach in order to boost sales.

(C) For instance, Fleischmann's yeast was a component in the cooking of homemade bread. However, as bread was increasingly purchased from bakeries or stores in the early 20th century, there was a decline in the demand for yeast among consumers.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 광고주들이 제품의 시장 상태에 맞춰 주장을 바꾼다는 일반론입니다. (C)에서 예시(For instance)로 Fleischmann의 효모가 집에서 빵을 만들지 않게 되면서 수요가 줄어든 문제 상황을 제시합니다. (B)에서 이 문제를 해결하기 위해 광고 대행사를 고용합니다. (A)에서 대행사가 효모를 영양제나 완하제로 재정의(reposition)하여 판매를 늘렸다는 해결책이 나옵니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998.
ordered_passages: (A) The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
(B) In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales.
(C) He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents.
(D) He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents.
(E) The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 구매 수량 제한이 판매를 늘린다는 가설과 실험을 소개합니다. (C)에서 아이오와주 슈퍼마켓에서의 캠벨 수프 할인 행사라는 구체적 실험 설정을 제시합니다. 본문 텍스트상 (D)는 (C)와 내용이 중복되나 원문의 흐름상 (C/D) 이후 실험 조건(무제한 vs 4개/12개 제한)을 설명하는 (E)가 필요하지만 선택지에는 (E)가 누락되어 있습니다. 하지만 선택지의 조합을 볼 때 (C)-(D)-(B)-(A) 순으로, 실험 설계(C/D) -> 실험 결과 수치 제시(B) -> 실험의 의의 및 결론(A) 순으로 이어지는 것이 가장 타당합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Until around 6,000 years ago, the majority of people were farmers. Many people moved about during the year, seeking for food or transferring their cattle to areas with plenty of food. There was no need to tell time because life was based on natural cycles like the changing seasons or sunrise and dusk. ⓐThe history of agriculture is only 12,000 years old, and it spread around the globe relatively quickly. ⓑAs more people began to reside in greater towns, some needed to tell the time. ⓒPriests, for instance, were curious about the appropriate time to perform a religious ceremony. ⓓThis is when clocks-devices that display, measure, and record the passage of time-were initially created. ⓔSince then, they have grown in significance. These days, clocks are sued for crucial purposes including creating complicated airport schedules. If the time is off, planes might hit each other during takeoff or landing!
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 인류가 정착 생활을 하고 도시를 형성하면서 '시간을 측정할 필요성(시계의 발명)'이 생겨났다는 것입니다. ⓐ는 농업의 역사와 전파 속도에 대해 언급하고 있는데, 이는 시간을 측정하게 된 계기나 시계의 발명이라는 전체 맥락과는 직접적인 관련이 없는 문장입니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no ⓐ<u>suitable</u> answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in ⓑ<u>separate</u> area. Just as in a city, no area of the brain functions ⓒ<u>together</u>. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are ⓓ<u>moved</u> along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo ⓔ<u>processing</u> and transformation into our conscious reality.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 뇌의 작동을 도시의 경제 시스템에 비유하여, 특정 한 구역이 아닌 전체 요소들의 '상호작용'을 통해 기능이 발현된다는 점을 설명합니다. ③의 문맥을 보면 '도시에서와 마찬가지로 뇌의 어떤 구역도 [고립되어/홀로] 작동하지 않는다'는 의미가 되어야 하므로 'together'는 'in isolation' 혹은 'alone' 등으로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to ⓐ<u>ban</u> my staff from speaking up. I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing statements from ever getting ⓑ<u>withdrawn</u>." If anything, most bosses even say that they are ⓒ<u>pro-discord</u>. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually ⓓ<u>foster</u> internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these ⓔ<u>rebels</u> because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
questions.explanation: 글의 앞부분에서 보스들이 직원들의 자유로운 발언을 장려한다는 맥락입니다. ⓐ는 직원들의 발언을 '금지(ban)'한다고 말하지 않는다는 뜻으로 적절하며, ⓑ는 '반대 의견이 [제기/표출]되는 것을 막는 문화를 유지하지 않는다'는 맥락이 되어야 하므로 'withdrawn(철회된)'이 아니라 'heard(들리는)'나 'voiced(목소리가 나오는)' 등의 단어가 오는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.summary_sentence: Creatures living in a(n) (A)__________ lifestyle can also disperse in the form of their own (B)__________ at the reproductive stage.
questions.explanation: 지문은 기후 변화에 따라 모든 생물종이 이동하며, 심지어 나무나 따개비처럼 움직이지 못하는 생물들도 생애의 특정 단계(씨앗, 유충)에서는 이동이 가능함을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '움직이지 않는/정착성의' 의미인 sedentary가 적절하고, (B)에는 이동의 주체인 '후손' 의미의 descendants가 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 집단적인 ...... 기관
② 개인적인 ...... 탈것/수단
③ 비활동적인 ...... 영양분
④ 대안적인 ...... 자손
⑤ 정착성의 ...... 후손

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 빈칸 (F)에 들어갈 말로 보기의 주어진 단어 중 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the insufficient availability of food and other essential resources led to the lack of extra resources, and it was ⓐ<u>not enough to support a full-time chief or village council</u>. The (A)______ (B)______ (C)______ (D)______ (E)______ (F)______ (G)______ (H)______. Early farmers could reap 3-10 kg of grain from each 1 kg of seed planted. Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided support for individuals, such as chieftains, village councils, men who practice medicine, priests, and warriors, ⓑ<u>who were not directly involved in farming activities</u>. In return, the nonfarmers provided leadership and security for the farming population, encouraging an environment ⓒ<u>which farmers could continue to increase food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses</u>. As technology advanced and conditions became more favorable, agriculture consistently yielded ⓓ<u>a surplus of essential resources, facilitating the growth of population groups</u>. These groups concentrated in towns and cities, and human tasks specialized further. Specialists, including carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their skills and ⓔ<u>ensured they got more efficiency in their use of time and energy</u>. The goods and services they provided brought about an improved quality of life, a higher standard of living, and, for most societies, increased stability.
vocabulary_box: on / patterns / an / development / had / work / agricultural / impact
questions.explanation: 문맥상 빈칸 (A)~(H)를 포함한 문장은 'Agricultural development had an impact on work patterns.'(농업의 발전은 작업 패턴에 영향을 주었다)가 되어야 합니다. 이에 따라 (F) 자리에 올 단어는 on입니다.
options_translation: ① ~에
② 가졌다
③ 일
④ 영향
⑤ 패턴
