questions.question: 25. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the insufficient availability of food and other essential resources led to the lack of extra resources, and it was ⓐ<u>not enough to support a full-time chief or village council</u>. The (A)______ (B)______ (C)______ (D)______ (E)______ (F)______ (G)______ (H)______. Early farmers could reap 3-10 kg of grain from each 1 kg of seed planted. Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided support for individuals, such as chieftains, village councils, men who practice medicine, priests, and warriors, ⓑ<u>who were not directly involved in farming activities</u>. In return, the nonfarmers provided leadership and security for the farming population, encouraging an environment ⓒ<u>which farmers could continue to increase food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses</u>. As technology advanced and conditions became more favorable, agriculture consistently yielded ⓓ<u>a surplus of essential resources, facilitating the growth of population groups</u>. These groups concentrated in towns and cities, and human tasks specialized further. Specialists, including carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their skills and ⓔ<u>ensured they got more efficiency in their use of time and energy</u>. The goods and services they provided brought about an improved quality of life, a higher standard of living, and, for most societies, increased stability.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 절은 'farmers(주어) could continue to increase(동사) food/energy yields(목적어)'로 완전한 문장이 오고 있습니다. 선행사 environment를 수식하면서 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오려면 관계대명사 which가 아니라 관계부사 where 또는 'in which'가 쓰여야 합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at ⓐ<u>which</u> one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power ⓑ<u>while</u> walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, ⓒ<u>being</u> much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar ⓓ<u>opposites</u>; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than ⓔ<u>those</u> of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: ⓔ는 앞의 'the rate of speed'를 지칭하는 대명사입니다. 'the rate'는 단수 명사이므로 복수 대명사인 those 대신 단수 대명사인 that으로 받아야 합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, ⓐ<u>which then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly</u>. As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you." If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler ⓑ<u>has been transmitted though our body</u>. Strange as it may sound, this theory states that emotions arise from our bodies. For example, our mood ⓒ<u>can be improved simply by lifting up the corners of our mouth</u>. If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, ⓓ<u>taking care not to let the pencil touch their lips</u> (thus forcing the mouth into a smile-like shape), they judge cartoons funnier than ⓔ<u>if they have asked to frown</u>. The primacy of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase "I must be afraid, because I'm running."
questions.explanation: ⓔ 부분에서 사람들은 찡그리라는 '요청을 받은 것'이므로 수동태를 써야 합니다. 따라서 'have asked'를 'have been asked'로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Numerous human and non-human animals exhibit the behavior of saving commodities or money for future use.
ordered_passages: (A) Nevertheless, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead.

(B) This conduct indicates a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the individual sacrifices some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one.

(C) Such scenarios could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 미래를 위해 저축하는 행동을 소개합니다. (B)는 'This conduct(이러한 행동)'로 시작하여 저축이 지연된 보상을 선호하는 것임을 설명하며 논리를 확장합니다. (A)는 'Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구하고)'를 사용하여 저축을 미리 써버리는 예외적인 상황을 소개합니다. (C)는 'Such scenarios(그러한 시나리오들)'를 통해 (A)에서 언급한 조기 지출 사례가 '의지의 박약'의 예시임을 결론지으며 마무리합니다. 따라서 (B)-(A)-(C)가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The soil in farm fields has been optimized for monoculture growth through the addition of nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water via irrigation. (A) Over the past five decades, advancements in engineering and crop science have enabled farmers to efficiently provide the precise amount of both. (B) The global use of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, while irrigation capacity has nearly doubled. (C) As a result, our fields are now more nourished and hydrated than ever before, leading to thriving crops. (D) Due to the abundance of nutrients and water in farm fields compared to the surrounding natural environment, they have become luxury real estate for invasive weeds. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: However, these ideal conditions have also attracted unwanted attention from various agricultural pets.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'these ideal conditions'는 농경지의 풍부한 영양과 수분 공급으로 인해 작물이 번성하게 된 (C) 문장까지의 긍정적인 상황을 가리킵니다. 'However'를 통해 이러한 조건이 'unwanted attention(원치 않는 관심)' 즉 잡초나 해충을 끌어들인다는 부정적 측면으로 전환되므로, 구체적인 문제점(잡초를 위한 호화 부동산이 됨)을 설명하는 (D) 앞인 ④번 자리가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, there is an assumption that the impact on the environment will be ⓐ<u>less</u> negative. Nevertheless, digital business practices can still pose a threat to the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more ⓑ<u>hazardous</u>. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a ⓒ<u>promising</u> step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, ⓓ<u>increased</u> carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂ and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is ⓔ<u>small</u>.
questions.explanation: 이메일의 이산화탄소 배출량에 대해 설명하며, 일반적인 경우에는 4g이지만 첨부 파일이 '클' 경우 50g까지 늘어날 수 있다는 문맥이 되어야 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 'small'을 'large' 혹은 'big'으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Numerous scientific studies have illustrated that focused attention can result in the restructuring of the brain. For instance, animals that are rewarded for their acute hearing abilities tend to have ⓐ<u>larger</u> auditory centers in their brains. Similarly, animals rewarded for their ⓑ<u>keen</u> eyesight exhibit larger visual areas. Brain scans, of violinists provide additional evidence that ⓒ<u>contradicts</u> this idea, revealing significant growth and expansion in areas of the cortex responsible for precise finger movements on the left hand. Additionally, research has indicated that the hippocampus, crucial for spatial memory, is ⓓ<u>enlarged</u> in taxi drivers. These findings emphasize that the brain's physical structure ⓔ<u>adapts</u> based on the focus of our attention and the activities we engage in.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체 내용은 집중된 주의가 뇌의 재구조화를 가져온다는 것입니다. 바이올리니스트의 뇌 스캔 결과는 손가락 운동을 담당하는 피질 영역의 성장을 보여주므로, 이는 해당 아이디어를 '반박하는(contradicts)' 것이 아니라 '뒷받침하는(supports)' 증거가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off ⓐ<u>shifting</u> to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone ⓑ<u>to generate</u> ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then ⓒ<u>do</u> the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and ⓓ<u>assessing</u> ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities ⓔ<u>that</u> might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.explanation: 'Only then'이라는 부사구가 문장 맨 앞으로 나오면서 도치가 발생했습니다. 주어인 'the team'은 단수 집합 명사로 취급되므로 조동사는 'do'가 아니라 'does'가 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The lifestyle of hunter-gatherers, often considered "natural" for humans, seems to have had many advantages. Analysis of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. if this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Despite the immediate impact on human life, the establishment of settlements and agriculture ultimately resulted in ______________________________. This era, referred to as the New Stone Age, marked a crucial milestone in human progress, paving the way for the development of the first towns and cities, and eventually the rise of settled "civilizations."
options: ① the advent of a hierarchical society
② returning to a hunter-gatherer society
③ a substantial rise in population density
④ the renaissance of the former tribal community
⑤ population decline as a result of epidemic illnesses
questions.explanation: 농경과 정착 생활은 초기 전염병 발생이나 힘든 노동과 같은 부정적인 면도 있었지만, 궁극적으로 인구 밀도의 상당한 증가를 가져와 마을과 도시, 문명의 발달로 이어졌다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 계급 사회의 출현
② 수렵 채집 사회로의 회귀
③ 인구 밀도의 상당한 증가
④ 이전 부족 공동체의 르네상스(부흥)
⑤ 전염병의 결과로 인한 인구 감소

questions.question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of the human mind may have been influenced by ____________________________. It is possible that the brains of our ancestors evolved in response to the need to outsmart rival tribes. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could outthink its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
options: ① achieving unity among rival tribes
② the transmission of beneficial genetic traits
③ competition and conflicts with other human tribes
④ an intelligent individual creating efficient military plans
⑤ the endurance of those best suited to their environment
questions.explanation: 인간의 정신적 진화가 경쟁 관계에 있는 다른 부족보다 더 똑똑하게 생각하고 예측하여 승리하려는 욕구에서 비롯되었다는 내용이므로, 빈칸에는 '다른 인간 부족과의 경쟁과 갈등'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 경쟁 부족 간의 단합 달성
② 유익한 유전적 특질의 전달
③ 다른 인간 부족과의 경쟁과 갈등
④ 효율적인 군사 계획을 세우는 지적인 개인
⑤ 환경에 가장 잘 적응한 사람들의 인내력

questions.question: 23. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Employees who feel a sense of agency, believing they have control and decision-making power, __________________________________. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ① bring about both merits and demerits
② can have negative influence on their fellow workers
③ can significantly boost their energy and focus at work
④ tend to have longer breaks and make more mistakes
⑤ can adversely affect their enthusiasm and concentration levels
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 통제권과 결정권(주체성)을 부여했을 때 생산성이 20% 증가하고 실수가 줄어들었다는 연구 결과를 제시하고 있습니다. 이는 직원들이 통제감을 느낄 때 일에 대한 자율성과 집중력이 높아진다는 것을 의미하므로, 빈칸에는 '일에서의 에너지와 집중력을 상당히 북돋울 수 있다(can significantly boost their energy and focus at work)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 장점과 단점을 모두 가져온다
② 동료 직원들에게 부정적인 영향을 줄 수 있다
③ 일에서의 에너지와 집중력을 상당히 북돋울 수 있다
④ 더 긴 휴식을 취하고 더 많은 실수를 하는 경향이 있다
⑤ 그들의 열의와 집중력 수준에 불리하게 작용할 수 있다

questions.question: 24. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. (A)____________, when Britain's grey squirrels arrived from America in the 1870s, both Britain's red and grey squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. (B)____________, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 외래종 도입의 문제를 언급한 뒤, 영국 회색 다람쥐의 구체적인 사례를 들고 있으므로 'For example'이 적절합니다. (B) 회색 다람쥐가 생존에 유리한 조건들을 나열한 뒤 그 결과로 토착종인 붉은 다람쥐가 멸종 위기에 처했다는 결론을 맺고 있으므로 'Therefore'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 반대로 / 그러므로
② 게다가 / 여전히
③ 마찬가지로 / 결과적으로
④ 그럼에도 불구하고 / 예를 들어
⑤ 예를 들어 / 그러므로

questions.question: 25. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The practice of cultivating crops compelled individuals to settle in one place. (A)____________, hunter-gatherers were known for their frequent movements, requiring them to carry all their possessions, including their young children, whenever they relocated. Consequently, hunter-gatherer mothers could only give birth to a single baby every four years or so, strategically spacing out their pregnancies to avoid the burden of transporting multiple children simultaneously. (B)____________, farmers could establish permanent settlements and were not burdened with the task of transporting young children over long distances. (C)____________, settled societies were able to reduce the time between births from four years to approximately two years. This enabled women to have a greater number of children compared to their hunter-gatherer counterparts, leading to rapid population growth within farming communities. The increased population proved to be advantageous for agricultural societies as farming required a substantial amount of human labor.
options: ① In contrast / Thus / As a result
② In contrast / Conversely / As a result
questions.explanation: (A) 앞부분의 정착 농경인과 대비되는 수렵 채집인의 특성을 설명하므로 대조의 연결어 'In contrast'가 적절합니다. (B) 수렵 채집인의 출산 제한 상황과 대조적으로 농부들은 정착 생활 덕분에 아이를 이동시킬 부담이 없었다는 대조적 상황을 다시 제시하므로 'Conversely'가 적절합니다. (C) 정착 생활로 인해 이동 부담이 사라진 결과로 출산 간격이 줄어들었다는 인과관계를 나타내므로 'As a result'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 대조적으로 / 따라서 / 결과적으로
② 대조적으로 / 반대로 / 결과적으로
③ 하지만 / 반대로 / 그럼에도 불구하고
④ 게다가 / 따라서 / 그럼에도 불구하고
⑤ 게다가 / 반대로 / 그러므로

questions.question: 1. 다음 편지의 발신자와 수신자의 관계를 가장 바르게 나타낸 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Dear Ms. Jane Watson,I am John Austin, a science teacher at Crestville High School. Recently I was impressed by the latest book you wrote about the environment. Also my students read your book and had a class discussion about it. They are big fans of your book, so I'd like to ask you to visit our school and give a special lecture. We can set the date and time to suit your schedule. Having you at our school would be a fantastic experience for the students. We would be very grateful if you could come.Best regards,John Austin
questions.explanation: 편지의 발신자인 John Austin은 Crestville 고등학교의 과학 교사이며, 수신자인 Jane Watson이 쓠 환경에 관한 책을 읽고 감명을 받아 수신자를 학교에 초청하고 있습니다. 따라서 발신자는 책을 읽은 독자(reader)이고, 수신자는 책을 쓠 저자(author)임을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 독자 - 저자
② 편집자 - 작가
③ 감독 - 제작자
④ 교사 - 학부모
⑤ 학생 - 교수

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ① Enhancing Life Quality: A Look into Group Biomedical Therapy
② Exploring the Effects of Group Music Activities on Physical Health
③ The Negative Impacts of Weekly Group Singing and Music Therapy
④ Music Therapy and Group Singing: Improving Mental Health and Well-being
⑤ Addressing Mental Illness and Promoting Recovery Through Individual Music Therapy and Exercise
questions.explanation: 이 글은 집단 음악 치료와 합창(노래) 활동이 정신 질환을 앓고 있는 사람들의 정신 건강과 안녕(well-being)을 개선한다는 연구 결과를 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 삶의 질 향상: 집단 생물 의학 치료 살펴보기
② 집단 음악 활동이 신체 건강에 미치는 영향 탐구
③ 주간 집단 가창 및 음악 치료의 부정적 영향
④ 음악 치료와 집단 가창: 정신 건강과 안녕 개선하기
⑤ 개인 음악 치료와 운동을 통한 정신 질환 해결 및 회복 촉진

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Marilyn and her three-year-old daughter, Sarah, took a trip to the beach, where Sarah built her first sandcastle. (A) Moments later, an enormous wave destroyed Sarah's castle. (B) In response to the loss of her sandcastle, tears streamed down Sarah's cheeks and her heart was broken. (C) She ran to Marilyn, saying she would never build a sandcastle again. (D) Sarah loved this idea and responded with enthusiasm to the idea of building another castle. (E) This time, even closer to the water so the ocean would get its gift sooner!
questions.insertion_sentence: Marilyn said, "Part of the joy of building a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give it as a gift to the ocean."
questions.explanation: 사라가 모래성을 다시는 쌓지 않겠다고 울며 달려간 뒤((C)의 내용), 엄마인 Marilyn이 모래성은 바다에 주는 선물이라는 말을 함으로써 사라를 달래는 과정이 필요합니다. 이후 (D)에서 사라가 '이 생각(this idea)'을 좋아했다는 내용과 연결되려면, (D) 위치에 제시된 문장이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the --tongue map-- explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. ① Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. ② It's essential to maintain proper tongue posture and movement for optimal oral health and function. ③ Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. ④ Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. ⑤ It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거에 알려졌던 '혀의 지도'가 잘못되었다는 사실을 바탕으로, 모든 맛은 혀의 어느 곳에서나 느낄 수 있다는 과학적 사실을 다루고 있습니다. 하지만 ②번 문장은 구강 건강과 기능을 위한 적절한 혀의 자세와 움직임을 강조하고 있으므로, 맛의 인지 체계를 설명하는 전체 글의 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown ①<u>how</u> experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people ②<u>expert</u> in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ③<u>insensitively</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge.' Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken ④<u>themselves</u> to acquire that skill in an earlier session. ⑤<u>Knowing</u> that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: ③번이 속한 문장의 become은 2형식 동사로, 뒤에 주격 보어를 필요로 합니다. 보어 자리에는 부사를 쓸 수 없으므로, 부사인 insensitively를 형용사인 insensitive로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make ⓐ<u>it</u> a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say ⓑ<u>that</u> they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, ⓒ<u>published</u> weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to ⓓ<u>continually</u> encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something ⓔ<u>do</u>."
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 있는 부분은 'get + 목적어 + 목적격 보어' 구조입니다. 목적어인 'something'과 'do'의 관계가 수동(무언가가 행해지는 것)이므로, 과거분사인 'done'으로 써야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are ⓐ<u>known</u> as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the ⓑ<u>one</u> that you have more control over. You think. You can choose ⓒ<u>whether</u> to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it. This is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently ⓓ<u>because</u> - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that ⓔ<u>holds</u> you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.explanation: ⓔ의 선행사는 'all kinds of other negativities'로 복수 명사입니다. 주격 관계대명사 'that' 뒤에 오는 동사는 선행사의 수에 일치시켜야 하므로, 단수 동사인 'holds'를 복수 동사인 'hold'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the ①<u>challenges</u> and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is ②<u>certain</u> if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made ③<u>modifications</u> for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for ④<u>shorter</u> time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has ⑤<u>adjusted</u> the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: 어린아이들이 자신들에게 너무 크고(too large), 무겁고(too heavy), 빠른(too fast) 성인용 장비와 경기장에서 경쟁할 경우, 성공으로 가는 길은 '확실(certain)'한 것이 아니라 오히려 '불확실'하거나 '불가능'할 것입니다. 따라서 문맥상 ②번의 certain은 uncertain 혹은 unlikely와 같은 부정적인 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question: How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. (A) For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. (B) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. (C) Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. (D) Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. (E) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'it'은 앞 문장에서 언급된 아리스토텔레스의 '인간과 동물의 감각은 5가지'라는 주장을 가리킵니다. (A) 문장이 '우선(For a start)'으로 시작하며 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 구체적인 감각들을 나열하기 시작하므로, 아리스토텔레스의 주장에 의문을 제기하는 도입부인 주어진 문장은 (A) 위치에 들어가는 것이 흐름상 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.summary_sentence: Crop rotation is a (A)_________ farming practice where farmers grow different crops in a specific (B)_________ across multiple fields to maintain soil health and enrich it for subsequent crops.
questions.explanation: 본문은 윤작(crop rotation)이 특정 순서에 따라 작물을 바꾸어 심음으로써 토양을 비옥하게 유지하는 '지속 가능한(sustainable/maintainable)' 농법임을 설명하고 있습니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 이러한 농법의 특징인 '유지 가능한/지속 가능한(maintainable)'이 적절하며, (B)는 작물을 심는 방식인 '특정한 순서(sequence)'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 파괴적인 ... 순서
② 파괴적인 ... 순환
③ 지속 가능한 ... 양
④ 유지 가능한 ... 순서
⑤ 해로운 ... 서식지

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어의 쓰임이 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable ⓐ<u>with</u> excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear ⓑ<u>that</u> so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages ⓒ<u>where</u> epidemic diseases first took root. ⓓ<u>However</u> its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to ⓔ<u>settling</u> "civilizations."*remains: 유적, 유해 **epidemic: 전염병의
questions.explanation: ⓐ '과도한 노력 없이' 얻을 수 있어야 하므로 'without'이 적절합니다.ⓑ 가주어 it에 대한 진주어 절이지만, 문맥상 '왜' 정착했는지 불분명하다는 뜻이므로 'why'가 적절합니다.ⓒ it is ~ that/where 강조구문으로, 장소의 부사구(in farming villages)를 강조하고 있으므로 관계부사 성격의 where를 쓰는 것이 가능합니다.ⓓ 뒤에 명사구(its immediate effect...)가 오므로 양보의 전치사 'Despite'나 'Regardless of'가 적절합니다. However는 접속부사입니다.ⓔ '정착된 문명'이므로 과거분사인 'settled'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. ⓐ<u>What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously</u>. ⓑ<u>Research has shown that a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief</u>. ⓒ<u>For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform</u>. Similarly, ⓓ<u>the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train</u>. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. ⓔ<u>You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓑ: show의 목적어인 that절 내부에 조건/시간의 부사절이 필요합니다. '한 사람이 정체성의 특정 측면을 믿을 때'라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 that 뒤에 접속사 once 또는 when이 추가되어야 문장이 성립합니다. (Research has shown that once a person believes...)

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one.
ordered_passages: (A) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.

(B) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.

(C) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will.*envision: 계획이다
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 인간과 동물이 미래 소비를 위해 저축하는 행동을 언급하며 지연된 보상을 선호하는 것처럼 보인다고 설명합니다. (B)에서는 '따라서(Thus)' 지연된 미래 가치가 현재 가치보다 커야 함을 말한 뒤, '그러나(However)' 어떤 경우에는 이를 조기에 사용해버린다고 반전을 줍니다. (C)에서는 그에 대한 예시(예: 크리스마스 선물을 위한 돈을 여름 휴가에 씀)를 들고, 이를 '의지의 나약함'의 사례로 규정합니다. (A)에서는 '즉(That is)'이라는 연결어를 통해 앞선 사례를 요약하며, 이성적 판단과 유혹에 의한 실제 행동 사이의 괴리를 설명하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could be ⓐ<u>superior</u> to its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military ⓑ<u>priority</u>. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more ⓒ<u>critical</u> than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each ⓓ<u>following</u> generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then ⓔ<u>pass by</u> the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.explanation: ⓔ의 'pass by'는 '~을 그냥 지나치다/방관하다'는 의미입니다. 문맥상 경쟁에서 우위를 점하게 해준 유전자를 후손에게 '물려주다/전달하다'는 의미가 되어야 하므로 'pass on'으로 고쳐야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. ______________________________________________.
options: ① Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
② It is important for children to live with their parents.
③ Climate change education must be included in schools.
④ Migratory bird species should have their own route for themselves.
⑤ The more flexible the body structure of migratory birds, the more they can fly.
questions.explanation: 지문은 어린 시절(유년기)이 동물의 유연한 학습을 가능하게 하여 환경 변화에 적응하도록 돕는다는 내용을 다룹니다. 타고난 본능(hardware)에만 의존하는 새들은 환경 변화에 적응하지 못하고 비효율적인 경로를 고수하지만, 부모와 함께 비행하며 긴 유년기를 보내는 새들은 문화적 정보를 전수받아 더 효율적으로 적응합니다. 따라서 '유년기는 변화하는 세상에서 유연성을 제공한다'는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 유년기는 변화하는 세상에서 유연성을 제공한다.
② 아이들이 부모와 함께 사는 것은 중요하다.
③ 기후 변화 교육이 학교에 포함되어야 한다.
④ 철새 종들은 그들 스스로를 위한 자신들만의 경로를 가져야 한다.
⑤ 철새의 신체 구조가 더 유연할수록, 그들은 더 많이 날 수 있다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. <summary>에서 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [24년 6월 34번]
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually, before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.*anonymously: 익명으로 **surface: 드러내다
questions.summary_sentence: <summary>※ Brain Writing Process(A) ⓐAsking team members to make their own ideas respectively.(B) ⓑGathering each idea from team members and holding the ideas in common with their name identified.(C) ⓒChoosing and sophisticating the most promising options.※ Brain Writing strength⦁ ⓓEvery opinion of team members could be reflected.⦁ ⓔIt is useful for the team which has difficulty completing collective intelligence.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 브레인라이팅 과정은 아이디어를 익명으로(anonymously) 공유한다고 되어 있으나, 요약문의 (B) ⓑ에서는 '이름이 확인된 채로(with their name identified)' 공유한다고 설명하고 있으므로 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 문장의 개수는? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. ⓐ<u>It has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities</u>. As a result, ⓑ<u>many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors</u>. ⓒ<u>While professionals worked in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account</u>. ⓓ<u>This situation would have been much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions</u>, ⓔ<u>ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.</u>
questions.explanation:
어법상 어색한 문장은 ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓓ의 총 3개입니다.

ⓐ: 'It has remained neglected ... are the needs' 구문에서 주어는 'the needs of people with disabilities'입니다. 'are'라는 동사의 주어가 뒤에 나오는 도치 구문이거나 명사절이 주어가 되어야 하는데, 가주어 'It'을 사용하는 것은 구조상 불가능합니다. 'What has remained neglected ... are ...'와 같이 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 What을 사용하여 주어 절을 만들어야 적절합니다.

ⓒ: 'professionals'를 수식하는 분사가 '교육 기술 등의 분야에서 종사하는(일하는)'이라는 능동의 의미를 나타내야 하므로, 과거분사 'worked' 대신 현재분사인 'working'이 오는 것이 적절합니다.

ⓓ: 가정법 시제 일치의 오류입니다. 조건절(if절)의 동사가 'embraced(과거형)'로 사용되어 가정법 과거(현재 사실의 반대)를 나타내고 있으므로, 주절의 조동사 역시 'would be much improved'와 같은 형태가 되어야 합니다. 혹은 과거 사실의 반대를 나타내고자 한다면 if절을 'had embraced'로 고쳐 가정법 과거완료로 일치시켜야 합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 taking the path of least resistance가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, <u>not from taking the path of least resistance</u>. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
options: ③ going through adversity and hardship
④ choosing an easy and comfortable way
⑤ confronting the prejudices of the world
questions.explanation: 본문은 도전을 피하고 쉬운 길(easy route)을 택하는 대신, 고난을 마주하고 준비를 철저히 해야 힘과 실력을 얻을 수 있다고 강조합니다. 따라서 '최소 저항의 경로를 택하는 것'은 고난을 피하고 쉽고 편안한 방법만을 선택하는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 철저한 준비를 하는 것
② 경쟁력을 확보하려 노력하는 것
③ 역경과 고난을 겪는 것
④ 쉽고 편안한 길을 선택하는 것
⑤ 세상의 편견에 맞서는 것

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden ____________  that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.
questions.explanation: 지문 도입부에서 '방해(interruptions)'의 대가에 대해 언급하며, 누군가 문을 두드리거나 예기치 못한 손님이 방문하여 흐름이 끊기는 사례를 들고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 방해나 혼란을 의미하는 'disturbances'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 치료, 대우
② 방해, 소란
③ 오해
④ 규제
⑤ 부당함

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristic of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself. Psychologist George M.Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment.
ordered_passages: (A) As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems: he used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something, for example. Fortunately, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for the rest of his life. For him, everything returned to normal after one day.

(B) Stratton wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally turned the world upside down for him. In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him.
(C) With time, however, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated.
questions.explanation: 심리학자 Stratton의 실험 과정을 설명하는 글로, (B)에서 반전 안경을 처음 착용했을 때의 어려움이 먼저 나오고, (C)에서 시간이 흐름에 따라 시각 체계가 적응하여 다시 정상적으로 행동할 수 있게 된 내용이 이어집니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 안경을 벗었을 때 다시 겪게 된 일시적 혼란과 회복을 다루는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing ⓐ<u>invaluable</u> possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to ⓑ<u>detach</u> oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple: the assumption of the question is ⓒ<u>essentially</u> wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of ⓓ<u>ambiguity</u>. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to ⓔ<u>discard</u> stuff that is unused or not going to be used in the near future.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 미니멀리즘이 감정에 해를 끼치지 않는다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 불필요한 물건을 버릴 때의 일시적인 슬픔은 곧 다른 긍정적인 감정으로 극복된다는 맥락이므로, '모호함'을 뜻하는 ⓓ의 ambiguity는 '명확함(clarity)' 등으로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation ─ transferring organs to others ─ is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these ⓐ<u>rigid</u> regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ⓑ<u>alleviate</u> public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements ⓒ<u>lower</u> public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an ⓓ<u>dependable</u> process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom ⓔ<u>prompt</u> burial or cremation is intended.
questions.explanation: 장기 이식을 위한 뇌사 판정 기준의 엄격함이 대중의 불안을 완화하려는 목적이지만, 오히려 불신을 초래할 수 있다는 내용입니다. 문장에서 뇌사 판정이 정밀함이 결여된(lacking precision) 과정이라는 잘못된 믿음을 유지한다고 했으므로, '신뢰할 수 있는'이라는 의미의 ⓓ dependable은 문맥에 맞지 않으며 '신뢰할 수 없는(unreliable)'과 같은 반대 의미의 단어가 필요합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. (A) This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. (B) During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. (C) World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled. (D) we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. (E) Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.insertion_sentence: Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'these luxurious conditions'는 (D) 이후의 풍부한 영양분과 물 공급으로 인해 작물이 잘 자라는 상태를 의미하며, 'certain agricultural undesirables(어떤 농업적으로 바람직하지 않은 것들)'는 (E) 문장에서 언급된 'every random weed(온갖 잡초)'를 가리킵니다. 따라서 주어진 문장은 (E) 바로 앞에 위치하여 농장의 좋은 조건이 잡초의 관심까지 끌게 되었다는 흐름을 연결하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the (A)__________ of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing (B)__________ growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
questions.explanation: 글의 주제는 집중된 주의가 뇌의 물리적 구조를 변화시킨다는 것입니다. (A)에는 '재구성(restructuring)'이 적절하며, (B)에는 바이올린 연주자의 뇌 부위가 눈에 띄게 확장되었음을 나타내는 '상당한(substantial)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 재구성 - 상당한
② 제한 - 상당한
③ 제한 - 지속 가능한
④ 복구 - 중요한
⑤ 재구성 - 침체된

questions.question: 22. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears ⓐ<u>to have had</u> much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors ⓑ<u>enjoying</u> abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and ⓒ<u>developed</u> agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and (A)<u>전염병들이 처음으로 뿌리를 내렸던 곳은 바로 농경 마을들 안에서였다.</u> Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, ⓓ<u>known</u> as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually ⓔ<u>leading</u> to settled "civilizations."
questions.explanation: ⓑ suggested 뒤의 that절 내에서 'our ancestors'가 주어이므로 정동사가 필요합니다. 문맥상 과거의 사실을 언급하고 있으므로 현재분사인 'enjoying'을 과거형 동사인 'enjoyed'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)를 강조 구문을 활용하여 주어진 우리말과 같도록 영작하시오.
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears ⓐ<u>to have had</u> much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors ⓑ<u>enjoying</u> abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and ⓒ<u>developed</u> agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and (A)<u>전염병들이 처음으로 뿌리를 내렸던 곳은 바로 농경 마을들 안에서였다.</u> Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, ⓓ<u>known</u> as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually ⓔ<u>leading</u> to settled "civilizations."
questions.answer: It was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root.
questions.explanation: 'It is/was + 강조대상 + that ~' 강조 구문을 사용하여 장소 부사구인 'in farming villages'를 강조합니다. 전염병은 epidemic diseases, 뿌리 내리다를 take root로 표현하여 구성합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 세 곳을 찾아 바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still endanger the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more innocuous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a futile step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is considered. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO2, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
questions.answer: (1) innocuous → hazardous (또는 harmful/serious)(2) futile → promising (또는 positive/helpful)(3) considered → neglected (또는 overlooked/ignored)
questions.explanation: (1) 디지털 비즈니스의 위해가 더 심각할 수 있다는 내용이어야 하므로 '무해한(innocuous)'은 흐름상 어긋납니다. (2) 종이에서 디지털로의 전환이 나무를 구하는 '유망한/긍정적인(promising)' 단계였다는 내용이 와야 합니다. (3) 이어지는 문장에서 화석 연료 사용과 탄소 배출을 언급하므로, 인터넷 사용의 환경적 비용이 '간과되고 있다(neglected)'는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 지문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (*단, 필요할 경우 문맥에 맞추어 어형을 바꾸시오.)
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.summary_sentence: In a (A)____________ agricultural society, the birth rate of children (B)____________, which was based on an agricultural society that (C)____________ a lot of labor.
subjective_conditions: 지문에서 찾아 쓸 것
필요할 경우 문맥에 맞추어 어형을 바꿀 것
questions.explanation: 정착한(settled) 농경 사회에서는 아이들의 출산율이 증가(increased)했는데, 이는 많은 노동력을 필요로 하는(required) 농경 사회의 특성에 기반한 것이었습니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 요지를 주어진 <조건>에 맞추어 10단어 이내의 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>의 주어진 단어를 모두 사용할 것
(*단, 필요시 어형 변화, 어휘의 중복 활용 및 어휘 추가 가능)
questions.answer: Birds with childhood have efficient migration routes.
questions.explanation: 지문은 어린 시절(childhood)을 보내며 환경에 적응하고 부모로부터 배우는 새들이 더 효율적인 이동 경로를 가진다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '어린 시절을 가진 새들이 효율적인 이동 경로를 가진다'는 의미로 영작하면 됩니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 빈칸 (A)~(E)에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 <조건>에 맞추어 쓰시오.
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a (A)h__________ enemy tribe might (B)s__________, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a (C)s__________ military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more (D)d__________ than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the (E)d__________ of the winners.
subjective_conditions: 1. 주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어로 쓰기
2. 제시된 우리말의 의미와 같아야 함
3. 문맥에 맞게 단어의 어형을 변화시킬 수 있음
questions.explanation: 문맥상 각 철자에 맞는 단어를 채워 넣는 문제입니다. (A) '적대적인'은 hostile, (B) '공격하다'는 strike, (C) '중요한/상당한'은 significant, (D) '결정적인'은 decisive, (E) '후손'은 descendants가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 29. 윗글에서 어법상 어색한 부분 세 가지를 찾아 바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shift to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone generating ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluate them on their own. ⓐ<u>The team comes together to select and refine the most promising options only then.</u> By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.answer: (1) we're better off shift → we're better off shifting(2) asking everyone generating → asking everyone to generate(3) evaluate → evaluates
questions.explanation: (1) 'be better off -ing' (~하는 것이 더 낫다) 구문을 사용해야 하므로 shift를 shifting으로 고쳐야 합니다. (2) ask는 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취하므로 generating을 to generate로 고쳐야 합니다. (3) each member는 단수 취급하므로 동사 evaluate를 evaluates로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 30. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ문장을 only then을 강조하는 도치 문장으로 바꿔쓰시오.
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shift to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone generating ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluate them on their own. ⓐ<u>The team comes together to select and refine the most promising options only then.</u> By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.answer: Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options.
questions.explanation: 부사구 Only then이 문두에 오면 주어와 동사가 도치됩니다. 일반동사(comes) 문장이므로 조동사 do(does)를 사용하여 'Only then + does + 주어 + 동사원형'의 어순으로 도치합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those  that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate─those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with─sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So, when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most  efficient migration routes. __________________ and culture can evolve faster than genes. ② Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information
③ Inefficient routes expose birds to vulnerability
