questions.explanation: 본문은 어린 시절(childhood)을 거치며 부모로부터 효율적인 이동 경로를 배우는 새들이 유전적 본능에만 의존하는 새들보다 변화하는 환경에 더 잘 적응한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 어린 시절이 문화적 정보의 전달을 용이하게 한다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이동은 유리한 생활 환경을 찾으려는 욕구에 의해 주도된다
② 어린 시절은 문화적 정보의 전달을 용이하게 한다
③ 비효율적인 경로는 새들을 취약성에 노출시킨다
④ 새들의 이동은 자연의 법칙과 선택에 의해 엄격하게 통제된다
⑤ 인간의 방해는 새의 번식에 위협이 될 수 있다

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency ─ a feeling ⓐ<u>that</u> they have genuine decision-making authority ─ can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers ⓑ<u>empowering</u> to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales ⓒ<u>stayed</u> the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant ⓓ<u>increased</u> by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline ⓔ<u>that</u> they brought to their jobs.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 조립 라인 근로자들이 작은 결정을 내릴 수 있는 '권한을 부여받은' 것이므로, 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 'empowered'가 와야 합니다. 현재분사 ⓑ 'empowering'은 어법상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops made people stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children.
ordered_passages: (A) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.explanation: 이 질문은 제공된 텍스트 조각에서 (B)와 (C) 단락이 누락되어 있어 전체 순서를 완성할 수 없으므로 처리가 불가하나, 시스템 지침에 따라 온전한 형태가 아니므로 상세 분석을 중단합니다. (단, 문제의 의도는 농경 생활이 정착과 인구 증가를 가져온 과정을 설명하는 것임)

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be ⓐ<u>less</u> negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more ⓑ<u>hazardous</u>. A few decades ago, offices used to  have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a ⓒ<u>hopeless</u> step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is ⓓ<u>neglected</u>. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds ⓔ<u>gray</u>. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO2, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
questions.explanation: 종이 문서에서 디지털 문서로 전환하는 것은 나무를 보존하기 위한 '희망적인(hopeful)' 또는 '긍정적인(positive)' 단계라고 여겨졌을 것이므로, 문맥상 '절망적인'을 의미하는 'hopeless'는 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.* lament: 슬퍼하다
options: ① Unexpected discoveries are crucial for creativity.
② Inequality is a problem in all areas of our lives.
③ Interruptions greatly affect human tasks and emotions.
④ Disruptions lower human memory capacity and raise Some level of regulation is essential for productivity growth.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 예기치 못한 방문이나 방해(interruptions/disruptions)가 창의적인 작업(시 쓰기 등)을 중단시키고, 다양한 전문가들뿐만 아니라 일반인들의 생산성을 떨어뜨리며 스트레스를 유발한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 방해가 인간의 업무와 감정에 큰 영향을 미친다는 ③번이 요지로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 예기치 못한 발견은 창의성에 중요하다.
② 불평등은 우리 삶의 모든 영역에서 문제이다.
③ 방해는 인간의 업무와 감정에 큰 영향을 미친다.
④ 방해는 인간의 기억력을 낮추고 생산성 성장을 위해 어느 정도 수준의 규제가 필수적이다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 각각 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 한 단어로 쓰시오. (필요시 어형을 바꿀 것)
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects included the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.summary_sentence: Digital projects have often (A)____________ people with disabilities, but this can be improved by designing (B)____________ for everyone.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 한 단어로 쓸 것
필요시 어형을 바꿀 것
questions.explanation: (A) 본문 두 번째 문장에서 'What has remained neglected... are the needs of people with disabilities'라고 언급되어 있으므로, 디지털 프로젝트가 장애인을 '방치해왔다/소홀히 해왔다'는 의미로 neglected가 적절합니다. (B) 마지막 문장에서 'keep the largest possible audience in mind'와 'serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without'라는 내용을 통해 모두를 위해 '포괄적으로' 디자인해야 함을 알 수 있습니다. 본문 단어인 including/included의 부사 형태인 inclusively를 유추하거나 문맥상 의미를 도출합니다. (단, 본문 근거에 따라 inclusive 또는 inclusively 변형이 요구됨)

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group.
options: ① Urgency of Implementing Moral Values at Work
② Comprehensive Guide to Earning a Higher Income
③ Several Ways to Set a Goal for Lifelong Learning
④ Nurturing Good Atmosphere in Community Matters Most
⑤ Leadership for Community: Developing the Potential Within Us All
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 지도자들도 처음에는 우리와 같은 평범한 학생, 노동자, 시민이었으며, 일상적인 개선 아이디어를 타인과 공유하고 협력하며 발전시켜 나갔음을 강조합니다. 즉, 리더십은 특별한 누군가만이 가진 것이 아니라 우리 모두의 내면에 있는 잠재력을 개발하여 공동체를 위해 발휘하는 것임을 말하고 있으므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 직장에서 도덕적 가치를 실행하는 것의 긴급성
② 더 높은 수입을 얻기 위한 종합적인 가이드
③ 평생 학습을 위한 목표를 설정하는 몇 가지 방법
④ 공동체에서 좋은 분위기를 조성하는 것이 가장 중요하다
⑤ 공동체를 위한 리더십: 우리 모두의 내면에 있는 잠재력 개발하기

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is their abnormal response to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see ⓐ<u>ordinarily</u> ─ they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is ⓑ<u>strengthened</u>; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed effectively, resulting in the sleeper remaining ⓒ<u>undisturbed</u>. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors ⓓ<u>exclude</u> it from the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to ⓔ<u>derive</u> some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 잠을 잘 때는 자극이 들어오더라도 정상적으로 처리되지 않는다는 내용입니다. 따라서 시각 정보가 들어오더라도 그것이 '강화(strengthened)'되는 것이 아니라, '약화되거나(weakened)' '단절'되어 처리되지 않아야 합니다. 그러므로 ②가 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 common sense has prevailed가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Accordingly, <u>common sense has prevailed</u>. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① many people get to know more about the rules of sports events
② it is acknowledged that the adjustments for children in sports should be made
③ all sports facilities must be adapted to children's level, given their age and capabilities
④ it is suggested that government must take the lead in promoting children's sports
⑤ the development of sports programs for adults is prioritized
questions.explanation: 성인용 경기장에서 아이들이 활동하는 것의 어려움을 깨닫고 아이들의 수준에 맞춰 장비나 경기장을 조정하는 상식이 널리 퍼졌다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '스포츠에서 아이들을 위한 조정이 이루어져야 한다는 점이 인정되었다'는 의미의 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 많은 사람들이 스포츠 경기의 규칙에 대해 더 많이 알게 된다
② 스포츠에서 어린이를 위한 조정이 이루어져야 함이 인정된다
③ 나이와 능력을 고려할 때 모든 스포츠 시설은 어린이 수준에 맞춰져야 한다
④ 정부가 어린이 스포츠 장려에 앞장서야 한다는 제안이 있다
⑤ 성인을 위한 스포츠 프로그램 개발이 우선시된다

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who _____________________ were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① received a high annual salary in their careers
② gained higher satisfaction from their careers
③ carried out works well with an assigned task
④ had a permanent job in prestigious company
⑤ got inspired by their mentor's successful career
questions.explanation: 이 글은 직업에서 느끼는 성취감과 의미가 개인의 행복과 생산성에 미치는 긍정적인 영향을 다루고 있습니다. 일에서 만족감을 느끼는 사람이 삶 전체에서도 더 행복할 가능성이 높다는 연구 결과를 소개하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 직업에서 더 높은 만족감을 얻은 사람들이 전반적으로 더 행복한 삶을 살 가능성이 높다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자신의 경력에서 높은 연봉을 받았다
② 자신의 경력에서 더 높은 만족감을 얻었다
③ 할당된 업무로 일을 잘 수행했다
④ 명성 있는 회사에서 정규직 일자리를 가졌다
⑤ 멘토의 성공적인 경력에서 영감을 얻었다

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn.
ordered_passages: (A) But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication.
(B) In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.

(C) As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you.

(D) To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 규범(Norms)의 편재성에 대해 언급합니다. (C)에서 영미권 사회에서 고맙다고 말하는 규범을 예시로 들기 시작하며 법은 아니라고 말합니다. (A)에서 '하지만(But)'을 사용해 법은 아닐지라도 하지 않으면 비판의 대상이 된다는 점을 지적하며 타 문화권 규범 이해의 중요성을 언급합니다. (D)에서 타 문화권으로 예시를 확장하여, 고맙다는 말의 사용 규범이 다를 수 있음을(비용이 클 때만 사용) 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 그러한 문화권(such a case)에서는 사소한 일에 고맙다고 하는 것이 오히려 우스꽝스러울 수 있다고 마무리하는 순서가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. (A) It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. (B) You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because you make the wrong decisions time and time again. (C) When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. (D) There are reasons for all of such fears as spiders or dark, but they originate in the conscious mind. (E) They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부는 잠재의식(subconscious mind)의 특징을 설명하고 있습니다. (A)까지도 잠재의식에 대한 설명이 이어지며, (B) 뒤의 문장부터는 사용자가 생각을 이어가거나 감정을 더할 수 있다는 내용(통제권에 대한 내용)이 나오므로, '의식적인 마음(conscious mind)이 더 통제 가능한 부분이다'라는 역접의 전환 문장이 (B)에 위치해야 문맥이 자연스럽게 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글을 읽고 밑줄 친 (A), (B)에 들어갈 적절한 말이 되도록 주어진 철자를 올바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their (A)<u>nariogil</u> order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is (B)<u>tasysbleina</u> because the soil stays healthy.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 4년째에 작물들이 다시 '원래의' 순서로 돌아간다는 의미가 되어야 하므로 'nariogil'은 original로, 이러한 방식의 농사는 토양을 건강하게 유지하므로 '지속 가능한' 방식이어야 하므로 'tasysbleina'는 sustainable로 고쳐 쓰는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것 두 개를 찾아 기호를 쓰고 올바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting ⓐ<u>can consider</u> "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know ⓑ<u>when stop painting</u>, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time ⓒ<u>to assess your progress</u>. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you ⓓ<u>find yourself struggling</u> to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.answer: ⓐ → can be considered, ⓑ → when to stop painting
questions.explanation: ⓐ 주어인 그림(the painting)은 '간주되는' 대상이므로 수동태인 'can be considered'가 적절합니다. ⓑ 의문사 뒤에 동사가 바로 올 수 없으며, '언제 멈춰야 할지'라는 의미의 의문사 + to 부정사 구인 'when to stop painting'으로 고쳐야 어법상 옳습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.summary_sentence: The tongue map theory suggesting specific taste regions on the tongue has been (A)____________, and it is uncovered that taste perceptions can be influenced by the (B)____________ of perception.
questions.explanation: 혀의 특정 부위에서 특정 맛을 느낀다는 '혀 지도' 이론은 틀린 것으로 증명(disproved)되었으며, 맛의 인지는 장소가 아니라 시간적 순서(sequence)에 의해 영향을 받는다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 확인된 - 결과
② 개선된 - 과정
③ 비판받은 - 위치
④ 승인된 - 차원
⑤ 틀렸음이 입증된 - 순서

questions.question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 각각 주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어로 쓰시오. [3.3점]
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Even animals from the same litter will display similarities but never (A)i____________ features; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, responses of a cat in a rescue center will (B)v____________ significantly from those of a cat in a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be (C)a____________ to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.explanation: (A) 한 배에서 태어난 동물이라도 '동일한' 특징을 가질 수 없으므로 identical이 적절합니다. (B) 구조 센터의 고양이와 집에서 자라는 고양이의 반응은 '다를' 것이므로 vary가 적절합니다. (C) 동물의 특정 필요에 맞게 치료가 '조정되어야' 하므로 adjusted가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B))에 들어갈 적절한 말을 각각 주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street ─ a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.summary_sentence: How fast people travel (A)a____________ how well they can (B)p____________ details in their surroundings.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어로 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 속도가 빠를수록 세부 사항을 파악하기 어렵고, 보행자처럼 느릴수록 더 잘 파악할 수 있다는 것이 요지입니다. 따라서 요약문은 '사람들이 얼마나 빨리 이동하는지가 그들이 주변의 세부 사항을 얼마나 잘 인지하는지에 영향을 미친다'는 내용이 되어야 하므로 (A)에는 affects(영향을 미치다), (B)에는 perceive(인지하다/지각하다)가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말이 되도록 <보기>의 낱말만을 모두 사용하여 바르게 배열하고 문장을 완성하시오. (단어 중복 사용 가능)
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. The curse of knowledge is a cognitive bias that _________________________________ those who do not have as much information as them. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 낱말만을 모두 사용하여 바르게 배열
단어 중복 사용 가능
questions.answer: causes people to fail to properly understand the perspective of
questions.explanation: 지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)에 관한 설명으로, 전문가들이 초보자의 입장을 이해하지 못하는 인지적 편향을 설명하는 문장을 완성하는 문제입니다. '원인(지식의 저주)이 사람들로 하여금 ~의 관점을 제대로 이해하는 데 실패하게 만들다'라는 구조인 'causes people to fail to properly understand the perspective of'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions. But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
options: ③ ways to choose important information
④ impact of internet use on intellectual confidence
⑤ role of internet access in enhancing actual knowledge
questions.explanation: 이 글은 실험을 통해 인터넷 검색을 경험한 사람들이 그렇지 않은 사람들보다 새로운 지식에 대해 더 높은 자신감을 갖게 된다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 첫 번째 단계에서 인터넷을 사용한 그룹은 두 번째 단계의 무관한 질문에 대해서도 스스로 더 유능하다고 평가했으며, 이는 인터넷 정보에 대한 접근성이 지적 자신감(intellectual confidence)을 높이는 데 영향을 미친다는 것을 보여줍니다.
options_translation: ① 온라인 정보의 위험성
② 의미 있는 질문의 장점
③ 중요한 정보를 선택하는 방법
④ 인터넷 사용이 지적 자신감에 미치는 영향
⑤ 실제 지식을 향상시키는 데 있어 인터넷 접근의 역할

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must ⓐ<u>agree</u> over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ⓑ<u>ease</u> public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements ⓒ<u>reduce</u> public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an ⓓ<u>unreliable</u> process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be ⓔ<u>different</u> the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 일관성(consistency)의 문제로 볼 때, 장기 기증자의 사망 진단 기준은 즉각적인 매장이나 화장이 예정된 사람들의 기준과 '동일해야(the same)' 한다고 흐름상 이어져야 합니다. 따라서 'different'는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: From food and air to bacteria and viruses, nearly everything has to go through your mouth ⓐ<u>to get</u> to the rest of you. A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and prevent it from harm - with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums ⓑ<u>in which</u> prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. From the moment you are created, every aspect of your life ⓒ<u>is affected</u> by oral health. What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and a reflection of what is happening in other parts of the body. Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease that ⓓ<u>influences</u> the entire body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, ⓔ<u>posing</u> serious health risks.
questions.explanation: ⓑ의 'in which' 뒤에는 완전한 문장이 와야 하는데, 뒤에 바로 동사 'prevent'가 나오므로 주어 역할을 하는 주격 관계대명사 'which'나 'that'으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristic of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself.
ordered_passages: (A) With time, however, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated. As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems.

(B) Psychologist George M. Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment. Stratton wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally turned the world upside down for him. In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him.

(C) One of them was that he used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something. Fortunately, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for the rest of his life. For him, everything returned to normal after one day.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 시각 시스템의 적응력을 언급한 후, (B)에서 Stratton의 역전 안경 실험을 구체적 예시로 도입합니다. (A)에서 시간이 흐름에 따라 적응했다는 내용과 안경을 벗었을 때 다시 문제가 생겼다는 내용이 이어지며, (C)에서 안경을 벗은 후 겪은 구체적 문제(잘못된 손 사용)와 하루 뒤 정상으로 돌아왔다는 결론으로 마무리되는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글에서 밑줄 친 (A)에 해당하는 것을 찾아서 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; (A)<u>the assumption of the question</u> is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of clarity. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused or (B)_______________________________.
subjective_conditions: 단어 5개 이내로 쓸 것
단어를 변형하지 말 것
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 (A) '질문의 가정'은 바로 앞 문장에 나온 의문문의 내용, 즉 '미니멀리즘이 누군가의 감정에 상처를 줄 것'이라는 전제를 의미한다. 따라서 본문의 'minimalism will hurt one's emotions'를 그대로 추출한다.

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; (A)<u>the assumption of the question</u> is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용하되, 각각 한 번씩만 쓸 것
<보기>에 주어진 단어를 필요시 변형할 것
문맥상 필요한 한 단어를 본문에서 추가하여 쓸 것
vocabulary_box: go / use / in / to be / the near future
questions.answer: not going to be used in the near future
questions.explanation: 미니멀리스트들은 사용되지 않거나 '가까운 미래에 사용되지 않을' 물건을 제거해야 한다고 생각한다. 보기의 'go'를 'going'으로 변형하고, 문맥상 부정을 뜻하는 'not'을 본문(Minimalism does not hurt...)에서 가져와 'not going to be used in the near future'로 완성한다.

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 32번]
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. Suppose that you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?"
ordered_passages: (A) Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons.(B) You'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements ─ from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers.(C) And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 도시의 경제가 어디에 위치하는가를 물어보는 상황으로 시작하므로, (B)에서 그 질문에 대한 답이 없으며 모든 요소들의 상호작용으로 경제가 나타나는 것이라는 설명이 오는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 이를 뇌의 작용 방식에 비유하는 (C)가 오고, 그 구체적인 과정으로서 감각 기관의 신호가 뇌로 전달되는 과정을 도시의 물자 수송에 비유하는 (A)가 마지막에 위치하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C) 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Our homes aren't just ecosystems, they're unique ones, hosting species that are adapted to indoor environments and (A)[pushing / pushed] evolution in new directions. Indoor microbes, insects, and rats have all evolved the ability to survive our chemical attacks, developing resistance to antibacterials, insecticides, and poisons. German cockroaches are known to have developed a distaste for glucose, which is commonly (B)[using / used] as bait in roach traps. Some indoor insects, which have fewer opportunities to feed than their outdoor counterparts, seem to have developed the ability to survive when food is limited. Dunn and other ecologists have suggested that as the planet becomes more developed and more urban, more species will evolve the traits (C)[what / which] they need to thrive indoors. Over a long enough time period, indoor living could drive our evolution, too. Perhaps my indoorsy self represents the future of humanity.
questions.explanation: (A) hosting species와 병렬 구조를 이루어 앞의 unique ones를 수식하는 분사로, 진화를 새로운 방향으로 '밀어붙이는' 능동의 의미이므로 pushing이 적절합니다. (B) 포도당(glucose)은 바퀴벌레 덫에서 미끼로 '사용되는' 것이므로 과거분사 used가 적절합니다. (C) 선행사 the traits가 있고, need의 목적어가 비어있는 관계대명사 절이므로 which가 적절합니다. (what은 선행사를 포함하므로 선행사 the traits와 함께 쓸 수 없습니다.)

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists say that having a disorderly room can indicate a disorganized mental state. One of the professional tidying experts says that the moment you start cleaning your room, you also start changing your life and gaining new perspective. When you clean your surroundings, positive and good atmosphere follows. You can do more things efficiently and neatly. So, clean up your closets, organize your drawers, and arrange your things first, then peace of mind will follow.
options: ① Think about what to do for a positive change.
② Organize your own space to promote positive change.
③ Above all, it is important to have a clean mind.
④ Try creative thinking in a disorderly environment.
⑤ Observe routine from a new perspective.
questions.explanation: 글 전체는 방을 정리하는 행위가 정신적인 질서와 긍정적인 삶의 변화를 가져온다고 설명하며, 주변 환경을 정리함으로써 마음의 평화를 얻으라고 조언하고 있습니다. 필자의 주된 요지는 정리 정돈을 통한 내면의 안정을 강조하는 것이며, 제공된 정답지에 따라 '깨끗한 마음을 가지는 것의 중요성'을 강조하는 ③번이 선택되었습니다. (참고: 지문 내용상 ②번이 더 논리적인 정답으로 보이나 원본 정답 표기를 따름)
options_translation: 긍정적인 변화를 위해 무엇을 해야 할지 생각하라.
긍정적인 변화를 촉진하기 위해 당신 자신의 공간을 정리하라.
무엇보다도 깨끗한 마음을 갖는 것이 중요하다.
무질서한 환경에서 창의적인 사고를 시도하라.
새로운 관점에서 일상을 관찰하라.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited ___________________________ Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
options: ① a different yield for a particular crop than before
② farmers' interest in different yields
④ an interest in crop rotation to prevent the rapid consumption of arable land
⑤ an interest in the rich harvest of agricultural crops
questions.explanation: 농경지는 비료와 물이 풍부하게 공급되어 작물이 자라기에 매우 좋은 환경이지만, 동시에 이 비옥한 환경은 주변의 모든 잡초들에게도 매력적인 곳이 됩니다. 따라서 이러한 '호화로운 조건'이 '농업적으로 바람직하지 않은 것들(잡초)의 관심'을 자극했다는 내용이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 이전보다 특정 작물에 대한 다른 수확량
서로 다른 수확량에 대한 농부들의 관심
농업적으로 바람직하지 않은 일부 존재들의 관심
경작지의 급격한 소모를 막기 위한 윤작에 대한 관심
농작물의 풍부한 수확에 대한 관심

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 공통적으로 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing ____________ to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. ____________ is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. ____________ will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 쉬운 길만 택하지 말고 고난과 투쟁을 통해 힘과 기술을 얻어야 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 운동선수들이 힘을 얻기 위해 직면하는 것, 그리고 우리 인생의 위대한 스승이 되는 것은 '역경(adversity)' 또는 '고난'을 의미하는 단어가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 역경
② 승리
③ 숙달
④ 항복
⑤ 패배시킴

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when ______________________________________.
options: ④ having trouble in saving money
⑤ determined to fulfill the future dream
questions.explanation: 사람들이 미래를 위해 저축을 하지만, 의지의 박약으로 인해 원래 계획했던 미래의 보상 대신 눈앞의 즉각적인 쾌락이나 유혹(여름 휴가 등)에 굴복하여 돈을 써버리는 경우를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '현재의 만족에 직면했을 때'라는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 여름 휴가를 건너뛸 때
② 지연된 이점에 유혹될 때
③ 현재의 만족에 직면했을 때
④ 돈을 모으는 데 어려움을 겪을 때
⑤ 미래의 꿈을 성취하기로 결심했을 때

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. (A) In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. (B) A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step lo save trees. (C) A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. (D) When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. (E) The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, il causes four grams of CO2, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big,
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 인터넷과 전기가 환경에 미치는 '비용(영향)'이 간과되고 있다는 내용입니다. (B) 앞부분까지는 종이를 아끼는 디지털화의 긍정적 측면이 서술되었으나, (C) 이후부터는 데이터 센터의 에너지원이 화석 연료라는 점, 탄소 배출 증가 등 디지털화의 부정적인 환경 영향이 구체적으로 나열됩니다. 따라서 긍정에서 부정으로 논조가 바뀌며 인터넷/전기 사용의 환경적 비용을 화두로 던지는 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations.
ordered_passages: (A) This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.

(B) While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account.

(C) What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 디지털 정보를 보존하기 위한 학자들의 노력을 설명합니다. (C)에서 'however'와 함께 그 과정에서 간과된 '장애인의 필요'를 처음 언급하며 문제 제기를 합니다. (B)에서는 상업 분야에 비해 학문적 디지털 프로젝트들이 이러한 필요(such users' needs)를 고려하는 데 실패하고 있다는 구체적 상황을 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 'This situation'을 받아 설계 시 모든 사용자(장애인 포함)를 고려해야 한다는 해결책을 제시하며 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고, 주어진 문장에 있는 문법적인 오류 두 곳을 찾아 바르게 고치고 그 이유를 설명하시오.
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, is appeared to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opens the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.answer: (1) is appeared → appears / 이유: appear는 자동사이므로 수동태로 쓸 수 없다.(2) opens → opening / 이유: and 뒤의 leading과 병렬 구조를 이루어 주절 뒤에 부수적인 상황을 나타내는 분사구문이 되어야 한다.
questions.explanation: (1) 'appear'는 '인 것 같다'는 의미의 자동사로, 수동태(be appeared)가 불가능하며 능동 형태인 'appears'로 써야 합니다. (2) 문장의 주어는 'This period'이고 동사는 'was'로 이미 존재합니다. 쉼표 뒤에 이어지는 구문은 분사구문 자리이며, 접속사 'and'를 통해 'leading'과 병렬 구조를 형성해야 하므로 'opening'으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고, 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 밑줄 친 한글 문장을 영작하시오.
questions.passage: Africa had the lowest electronic waste collection and recycling rates in both 2016 and 2019, showing the smallest gap between 2016 and 2019.
subjective_conditions: 두 번의 최상급 표현 사용
[,] 이후에 분사구문으로 영작
questions.answer: Africa had the lowest electronic waste collection and recycling rates in both 2016 and 2019, showing the smallest gap between 2016 and 2019.
questions.explanation: 조건에 따라 'lowest(가장 낮은)'와 'smallest(가장 작은)'라는 두 개의 최상급을 사용하였습니다. 문장의 주절 뒤에 콤마(,)와 현재분사 'showing'을 사용하여 부수적인 상황을 나타내는 분사구문을 구성하였습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 주제를 10단어 내외(±3단어)로 영작하시오. (단, 명사구의 형태, 구체적으로 작성)
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
subjective_conditions: 10단어 내외(±3단어)
명사구의 형태
구체적으로 작성
questions.answer: The human mind evolved through the struggle for survival
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 정신이 다른 부족과의 경쟁 및 생존 투쟁(struggle for survival) 과정을 통해 진화했음을 설명하고 있습니다. 상대보다 앞선 생각(out-think)을 하는 것이 군사적 이점과 생존 확률을 높였고, 이것이 유전되었다는 핵심 내용을 포함하여 명사구 형태로 작성합니다.

questions.question: 다음 그래프에 대한 내용 중 밑줄 친 우리말 부분을 <조건>에 맞도록 영작하시오. [24년 6월 25번]
questions.passage: The above graph shows the electronic waste collection and recycling rate by region in 2016 and 2019. In both years, Europe showed the highest electronic waste collection and recycling rates. The electronic waste collection and recycling rate of Asia in 2019 was lower than in 2016. The Americas ranked third both in 2016 and in 2019, with 17 percent and 9 percent respectively. In both years, the electronic waste collection and recycling rates in Oceania remained under 10 percent, <u>아프리카는 2016년과 2019년 모두 가장 낮은 전자 폐기물 수거율 및 재활용률을 가지고 있었으며, 두 해 사이의 가장 작은 격차를 보여주었다</u>.
subjective_conditions: 1. 두 번의 최상급 표현 사용
2. [,] 이후에 분사구문으로 영작
questions.answer: Africa had the lowest electronic waste collection and recycling rates in both 2016 and 2019, showing the smallest gap between the two years.
questions.explanation: 최상급 표현 'the lowest'와 'the smallest'를 사용하고, 콤마 뒤에 현재분사 'showing'을 이용한 분사구문을 사용하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 글의 흐름에 맞도록 빈칸에 문장을 완성하시오. (단, 주어진 <조건>을 충족시킬 것) [24년 6월 38번]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down 'in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that __________________ ___________________________________________________________. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
subjective_conditions: 1. 주어진 단어는 한 번씩만 사용할 것.
2. 어형 변화 없음
questions.answer: each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities.
questions.explanation: 정착 생활을 하게 된 농경 사회에서 출산 간격이 줄어든 결과, 농경 사회의 여성이 수렵 채집 사회의 여성보다 더 많은 자녀를 가질 수 있게 되었고 이것이 급격한 인구 증가로 이어졌다는 흐름을 완성합니다. 관계대명사의 계속적 용법(, which)과 인과 관계를 나타내는 'resulted in'을 적절히 배치합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 The expert's advantage가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Chess masters shown a chess board in the middle of a game for 5 seconds with 20 to 30 pieces still in play can immediately reproduce the position of the pieces from memory. Beginners, of course, are able to place only a few. Now take the same pieces and place them on the board randomly and the difference is much reduced. <u>The expert's advantage</u> is only for familiar patterns- those previously stored in memory. Faced with unfamiliar patterns, even when it involves the same familiar domain, the expert's advantage disappears. The beneficial effects of familiar structure on memory have been observed for many types of expertise, including music. People with musical training can reproduce short sequences of musical notation more accurately than those with no musical training when notes follow conventional sequences, but the advantage is much reduced when the notes are ordered randomly. Expertise also improves memory for sequences of movements. Experienced ballet dancers are able to repeat longer sequences of steps than less experienced dancers, and they can repeat a sequence of steps making up a routine better than steps ordered randomly. In each case, memory range is increased by the ability to recognize familiar sequences and patterns.*expertise 전문 지식 **sequence 연속, 순서***musical notation 악보
options: ① recalling familiar structures and sequences more effectively
② recognizing and remembering unfamiliar patterns better
③ being able to remember unrelated pieces more accurately
questions.explanation: 지문은 전문가의 기억 우위가 무작위적인 정보가 아니라 이미 기억 속에 저장된 '익숙한 패턴(familiar patterns)'이나 '구조'를 다룰 때만 나타난다고 설명합니다. 따라서 '전문가의 이점'이란 익숙한 구조와 순서를 더 효과적으로 상기하는 능력을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 익숙한 구조와 순서를 더 효과적으로 상기하는 것
② 익숙하지 않은 패턴을 더 잘 인식하고 기억하는 것
③ 관련 없는 조각들을 더 정확하게 기억할 수 있는 것

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs have ⓐ<u>been removed</u>. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things ⓑ<u>for which</u> they have no love. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans ⓒ<u>to avoid</u> low-tech physical work and to seek jobs working in the digital world. Our increasing ⓓ<u>use</u> of high technology in the workplace puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs ⓔ<u>are</u> a health risk - for body and mind.
questions.explanation: ⓔ 문장의 주어는 'the sedentary nature(단수)'이므로 동사는 복수형 are가 아닌 단수형 is로 써야 수 일치가 이루어집니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also _____________________________________.
options: ① change the initial impressions over time
② influence our behavior towards others
④ alter our perceptions of reality
questions.explanation: 연구 결과, 강사가 따뜻할 것이라고 기대한 학생들이 그렇지 않은 학생들보다 강사와 더 많이 상호작용(interact)했습니다. 이는 기대가 단순히 인상 형성에만 그치는 것이 아니라 타인에 대한 실제 '행동(behavior)'에까지 영향을 미친다는 것을 보여줍니다.
options_translation: ① 시간이 지남에 따라 초기 인상을 바꾼다
② 타인에 대한 우리의 행동에 영향을 준다
③ 우리의 학업 성취에 영향을 준다
④ 현실에 대한 우리의 인식을 바꾼다
⑤ 우리의 인지 능력을 형성한다

questions.question: 28. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that strengthened the view that _________________________________. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.*affluent 부유한
options: ② production would create its own demand
③ providing quality products matters the most
④ supplying goods ensures that demand for them will exist
⑤ providing a quality product at a reasonable cost is satisfactory
questions.explanation: 과거에는 저렴한 가격에 좋은 품질의 제품을 생산하는 것만으로 충분했으나, 사회가 변화하면서 고객이 실제로 원하는 제품을 제공하고 그들의 다양한 욕구를 충족시키는 것, 즉 고객 만족(customer satisfaction)이 가장 중요하다는 마케팅 혁명이 일어났다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 고객 만족이 중요하다
② 생산이 그 자체의 수요를 창출할 것이다
③ 품질 좋은 제품을 제공하는 것이 가장 중요하다
④ 물건을 공급하는 것은 수요가 존재할 것임을 보장한다
⑤ 합리적인 가격에 품질 좋은 제품을 제공하는 것이 만족스럽다

questions.question: 30. 다음 글 (가)를 표 (나)로 나타내었을 때, 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 적절한 내용을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
subjective_conditions: 지문의 내용을 바탕으로 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 적절한 어구를 본문에서 찾아 그대로 쓰거나 변형하여 완성할 것
questions.subjective_answer_format: (나)Magma reaches the Earth's surface or is trapped below.⦁Elements in magma (C)____________________⦁Cooling rate affects crystal size:- Slow cooling forms large, visible  crystals.- Rapid cooling  forms small, less  visible crystals.↓Magma cools, and atoms(A)__________________________.↓Atoms move closer together and (B)_______________________.↓
questions.answer: (A) lose heat energy(B) (begin to) combine into compounds(C) determine which minerals (will) form
questions.explanation: 지문 (가)의 내용을 논리적 흐름에 따라 표 (나)로 재구성하는 문제입니다.(A): 마그마가 식으면서 원자들이 겪는 첫 번째 단계는 열 에너지를 잃는 것입니다. 본문의 'atoms lose heat energy'를 참고합니다.(B): 열을 잃은 원자들이 가까워지며 나타나는 현상은 화합물로 결합하는 것입니다. 본문의 'begin to combine into compounds'를 참고합니다.(C): 마그마에 있는 원소의 종류와 양이 결정하는 것이 무엇인지 묻고 있습니다. 본문의 'determine which minerals will form'을 참고하여 작성합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress. For example, according to a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. ⓐHowever, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. ⓑThe key issue in richer economies is time pressure. ⓒStress can strengthen the relationships and improve cognitive function. ⓓA 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life-which caused a higher standard of living. ⓔBut at the same time they left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 가난한 국가뿐만 아니라 부유한 국가에서도 발생하는 스트레스(특히 시간 압박으로 인한 스트레스)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓒ는 스트레스가 관계를 강화하고 인지 기능을 향상시킨다는 긍정적인 효과를 언급하고 있어 글의 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests, that ________________________________________. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
options: ① scarcity is not essential for increasing sales
② it is more effective to diversify products to promote sales
③ the more quality goods businesses sell, the more goods customers buy
④ when people find the items hard to buy, they want to possess them eagerly
⑤ offering several options has nothing to do with the volume of purchases
questions.explanation: 실험 결과, 구매 수량에 제한이 없을 때보다 제한이 있을 때(희귀성 조건) 소비자들이 더 많은 양의 수프를 구매했다. 이는 사람들이 구하기 힘든 물건일수록 더 간절히 소유하고 싶어 한다는 점을 시사하므로 ④번이 정답이다.
options_translation: ① 희소성은 판매 증가에 필수적이지 않다
② 판매를 촉진하기 위해 제품을 다양화하는 것이 더 효과적이다
③ 기업이 양질의 상품을 더 많이 팔수록 고객은 더 많은 상품을 구매한다
④ 사람들이 품목을 구매하기 어렵다는 것을 알게 될 때, 그것들을 간절히 소유하고 싶어 한다
⑤ 여러 선택 사항을 제공하는 것은 구매량과 상관이 없다

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Why do you care how care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people ⓐ<u>they</u> know. ⓑ<u>They</u> trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that ⓒ<u>they</u>'re used to persuade ⓓ<u>them</u> to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring people's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid ⓔ<u>their</u> negative word-of-mouth advertising.
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 '사람들(People)' 또는 '고객'을 지칭하는 반면, ⓒ는 문맥상 '광고(advertisements)'를 지칭한다. 광고가 제품을 구매하도록 설득하는 데 사용된다는 의미이다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. That is to say, ________________________________________.
options: ① birds can move efficiently in a group by only inheriting the nature of migration directions from their parents
② innate rules and maps are considered as insignificant for animals in a changing world
③ parents are the facilitators teaching their offspring how to search for food rapidly
④ genes are less significant and valuable than any other attributes for all animals
⑤ the ability to adapt to surroundings can be acquired through childhood
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물의 어린 시절(유년기)이 환경에 적응하는 능력을 배우는 데 중요하다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 유전적 본능(하드웨어)에만 의존하는 새들은 변화하는 환경에 잘 적응하지 못하는 반면, 부모와 함께 긴 유년기를 보내며 문화를 습득하는 새들이 더 효율적인 경로를 갖는다는 내용을 통해, 환경 적응 능력이 유년기를 통해 습득될 수 있음을 결론짓고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 새들은 부모로부터 이동 방향의 본성을 물려받는 것만으로도 무리 지어 효율적으로 이동할 수 있다
② 타고난 규칙과 지도는 변화하는 세상에서 동물들에게 중요하지 않은 것으로 간주된다
③ 부모는 자손에게 먹이를 빠르게 찾는 법을 가르치는 조력자이다
④ 모든 동물에게 유전자는 다른 어떤 속성보다 덜 중요하고 가치 있다
⑤ 주변 환경에 적응하는 능력은 어린 시절을 통해 습득될 수 있다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
options: ① Progress of the Human Mind in Competition with Other Tribes
② Competition and Conflicts: Reasons of Making Weapons
③ Empathy to Each Other: The Human's Greatest Capacity
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 지능(정신)이 어떻게 진화했는지를 다루며, 다른 부족과의 경쟁 및 갈등에서 상대보다 더 깊이 생각할 수 있는 능력이 생존과 승리의 핵심 무기가 되었다고 설명합니다. 이러한 정신적 우위가 세대를 거쳐 전달되어 인간의 마음이 현재와 같은 방식으로 진화했다는 내용이므로 ①번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 부족과의 경쟁을 통한 인간 정신의 진보
② 경쟁과 갈등: 무기를 만드는 이유
③ 서로에 대한 공감: 인간의 가장 위대한 능력

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, which then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly. As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you." If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler has been transmitted via our body. Strange as it may sound, this theory states that emotions arise from our bodies. For example, our mood can be improved by simply lifting up the corners of our mouth. If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, taking care not to let the pencil touch their lips (thus forcing the mouth into a smile-like shape), they judge cartoons funnier than if they have been asked to frown. The primacy of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase "I must be afraid, because I'm running."
options: ① How to Make Various Facial Expressions
② It Starts with the Body and Emotions Follow
③ Body Language: What It Is and How to Read It
④ The Power of a Smile: Spreading Happiness and Positiveness
⑤ Copying Emotions of Others: Eliciting Creativity from a Singer
questions.explanation: 이 글은 감정이 신체에서 발생한다는 이론을 설명하고 있습니다. 타인의 보디랭귀지를 모방하거나 단순히 입꼬리를 올리는 것만으로도 기분이 변한다는 예시를 통해 신체가 감정에 앞선다는 점을 강조하고 있으므로 ②번 '신체에서 시작되고 감정이 뒤따른다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다양한 얼굴 표정을 짓는 방법
② 그것은 신체에서 시작되고 감정이 뒤따른다
③ 보디랭귀지: 그것이 무엇이며 어떻게 읽는가
④ 미소의 힘: 행복과 긍정의 전파
⑤ 타인의 감정 모방하기: 가수로부터 창의성 이끌어내기

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
options: ① various functions of the brain
② interaction of every element in the brain
③ differences between brains and cities
④ the location of the economy in the cities
⑤ the relationship of electrochemical signals and neurons
questions.explanation: 이 글은 뇌의 작용을 도시의 경제에 비유하여 설명하고 있습니다. 경제가 특정 장소에 국한되지 않고 다양한 요소들의 상호작용으로 나타나듯이, 뇌의 활동 역시 고립된 한 지점이 아니라 신경 세포들 간의 상호작용과 신호 전달을 통해 이루어진다는 것이 핵심입니다. 따라서 주제는 ②번 '뇌의 모든 요소의 상호작용'입니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌의 다양한 기능들
② 뇌의 모든 요소의 상호작용
③ 뇌와 도시의 차이점
④ 도시 내 경제의 위치
⑤ 전기화학적 신호와 뉴런의 관계

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he ________________________________________. That is to say, thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
options: ① will integrate her evaluation into his sense of self
② is reluctant to reflect his misbehavior at preschool
③ associates the given problem to his mother's expertise
④ tends to erase the vulnerability of his own self-image
⑤ is willing to endure difficult tasks than any other adults
questions.explanation: 미취학 아동은 부모의 말을 깊이 믿고 분석적으로 거를 능력이 없으므로, 부모의 평가(칭찬)를 자신의 자아상으로 받아들인다는 내용이 빈칸 뒤에 이어진다. 따라서 엄마의 평가를 자신의 자아의식에 통합시킨다는 ①번이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 그녀의 평가를 자신의 자아의식 속으로 통합할 것이다
② 유치원에서의 자신의 잘못된 행동을 반영하기를 꺼려한다
③ 주어진 문제를 엄마의 전문 지식과 연관시킨다
④ 자신의 자아 이미지의 취약성을 지우는 경향이 있다
⑤ 다른 어떤 성인들보다 어려운 과업을 기꺼이 견뎌낸다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future use. (A) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (B) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. (C) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. (D) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (E) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 미래를 위해 저축하지만 경우에 따라 조기에 소비한다는 내용을 담고 있다. (B)까지는 미래 보상을 위해 현재의 즐거움을 포기하는 원론적인 저축 행태를 설명하고, (C) 위치에서 '하지만(However)'과 함께 조기 소비의 사례인 '여름 휴가비로 써버리는 예시'가 나오기 직전인 (C) 자리가 가장 적절하다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 바르게 짝지어진 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. (A)__________, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. (B)__________ professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved (C)__________ more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
options: ② As a consequence / While / unless
③ As a result / Since / unless
⑤ As a consequence / While / if
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 장애인의 요구가 소외되었다고 했고, (A) 뒤 문장에서 그 결과로 많은 디지털 자원이 장애인들에게 무용지물이라는 결과가 이어지므로 인과관계를 나타내는 'As a consequence(그 결과)'가 적절합니다. (B) 에듀테크나 상업 웹 디자인 전문가들은 진전을 보인 반면(while), 일부 학자들은 여전히 이를 고려하지 못한다는 대조를 이루고 있으므로 'While'이 적절합니다. (C) 뒤의 문장은 더 많은 프로젝트가 보편적 설계 아이디어를 수용한다면 상황이 개선될 것이라는 가정의 의미를 담고 있으므로 조건의 접속사 'if'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그럼에도 불구하고 / ~때문에 / 만약 ~라면
② 그 결과 / ~하는 동안(반면에) / 만약 ~하지 않는다면
③ 그 결과 / ~때문에 / 만약 ~하지 않는다면
④ 그럼에도 불구하고 / ~하는 동안(반면에) / 만약 ~하지 않는다면
⑤ 그 결과 / ~하는 동안(반면에) / 만약 ~라면

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was ⓐ<u>what</u> it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and ⓑ<u>to have</u> more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us ⓒ<u>has</u> less. Companies large and small have off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we're now expected to do ourselves. With air travel, we're expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs ⓓ<u>what</u> used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, ⓔ<u>scanning</u> our own purchases.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'what'은 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사이지만, 여기서는 'was' 뒤에서 보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며 뒤 문장이 완전하므로 접속사 'that'으로 바꿔야 합니다. ⓒ 주어 'most of us'는 복수이므로 동사도 복수형인 'have'로 써야 합니다. ⓓ 명사 'jobs'를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 자리이므로 'which'나 'that'으로 바꿔야 합니다. 'what'은 선행사가 없을 때 씁니다. ⓔ 'to bag'과 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 'scan' 혹은 'to scan'으로 써야 합니다. (be expected to bag and scan) ⓑ 'pursue'와 병렬을 이루는 'to have'는 문법적으로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to (A)[compel / challenge]. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly (B)[successful / successive] athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from (C)[confronting / neglecting] difficulties, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
questions.explanation: (A) 쉬운 길만 택하면 도전(challenge)할 수 있는 힘을 얻지 못한다는 맥락이 적절합니다. (B) 장비보다 정신력과 기술로 이기는 선수들은 성공적인(successful) 선수들입니다. successive는 '연속적인'이라는 뜻입니다. (C) 힘은 저항이 적은 길을 가는 것이 아니라 어려움에 맞서는 것(confronting)에서 옵니다.
options_translation: ① 도전하다 / 성공적인 / 직면하는
② 도전하다 / 성공적인 / 무시하는
③ 도전하다 / 연속적인 / 직면하는
④ 강요하다 / 연속적인 / 무시하는
⑤ 강요하다 / 성공적인 / 직면하는

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The decline in curiosity can be tracked down in the brain development in childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between those in the adult brain. As a result, the baby's perception of the world is ________________________________________. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.
options: ① unchanging due to the curiosity
② related to the human mental health
③ invariable regardless of the brain size
④ influenced by his parents' background
⑤ both highly disarranged and abundant
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부에서 유아의 뇌는 성인보다 수백만 개 더 많은 신경 연결을 가지고 있지만(abundant), 그 연결망이 엉망(mess)이며 덜 효율적이라고 설명합니다. 따라서 아기가 세상을 인지하는 방식은 '매우 무질서하면서도 풍부한' 상태라는 내용의 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 호기심으로 인해 변하지 않는
② 인간의 정신 건강과 관련된
③ 뇌 크기와 상관없이 불변하는
④ 부모의 배경에 영향을 받는
⑤ 매우 무질서하면서도 풍부한

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Up until about 6,000 years ago, most people were farmers. Many lived in different places throughout the year, hunting for food or moving their livestock to areas with enough food. There was no need to tell the time because life depended on natural cycles, such as the changing seasons or sunrise and sunset. Gradually more people started to live in larger settlements, and some needed to tell the time. For example, priests wanted to know when to carry out religious ceremonies. This was when people first invented clocks - devices that show, measure, and keep track of passing time. Clocks have been important ever since. Today, clocks are used for important things such as setting busy airport timetables-if the time is incorrect, aeroplanes might crash into each other when taking off or landing!
questions.summary_sentence: Clocks were invented due to the rise of (A)__________ settlements and the increasing need for timekeeping, ultimately becoming (B)__________ for tasks like arranging airport schedules to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: 지문은 사람들이 더 큰 정착지(larger settlements)에서 살기 시작하면서 시간을 알 필요가 생겨 시계가 발명되었으며, 오늘날에는 공항 일정 관리와 같이 사고를 방지하기 위한 중요한 일에 필수적(important/indispensable)이 되었다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 enlarged(확장된/더 커진), (B)에는 indispensable(필수적인)이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 확장된 ... 필수적인
② 확장된 ... 불필요한
③ 좁아진 ... 매우 귀중한
④ 줄어든 ... 관련 없는
⑤ 조밀한 ... 중요한

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Advertisers ________________________________________ to adapt to a changing market. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped increase sales.
subjective_conditions: - <보기>에 있는 모든 단어를 한 번씩만 사용할 것
- 한 단어만 형태를 변형할 것
vocabulary_box: show / new / the products / by / give / images / flexibility / to
questions.answer: show flexibility by giving new images to the products
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 Fleischmann의 효모가 시장 변화에 따라 용도를 빵 재료에서 비타민 공급원, 그리고 천연 완하제로 재정립(repositioning)함으로써 매출을 올린 사례를 다루고 있습니다. 광고주들이 제품에 새로운 이미지를 부여함으로써 변화하는 시장에 대응하는 '유연함을 보여주었다'는 내용이 빈칸에 적절합니다. <보기>의 단어들 중 'give'를 전치사 'by' 뒤에 위치시키기 위해 동명사인 'giving'으로 형태를 변형하여 문장을 완성해야 합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.*anonymously: 익명으로 **surface: 드러내다
options: ① 팀원들은 가장 유망한 옵션만을 제시해야 한다.
② 누구의 아이디어인지 제대로 표기하는 것이 필요하다.
③ 팀이 함께 모여 아이디어를 나누는 과정을 먼저 하는 것이 좋다.
④ 팀의 잠재력을 찾기 위해 모든 사람이 대화에 참여하는 것이 좋다.
⑤ 먼저 개별적으로 아이디어를 개발하고 평가하는 과정을 거치는 것이 좋다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 팀의 잠재력을 끌어내기 위해 브레인스토밍 대신 '브레인라이팅(brainwriting)'을 제안합니다. 브레인라이팅은 팀원들이 먼저 개별적으로 아이디어를 만들고 독립적으로 평가한 후에 팀 전체가 모여 논의하는 방식입니다. 따라서 정답은 5번입니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 밑줄 친 luxury real estate가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as <u>luxury real estate</u> by every random weed in the area.*monoculture: 단일작물 재배 **irrigation: 관개
options: ① a region with greater economic value
② a field rich in essential resources for plants
③ a location preserved for ecological purposes
④ a district exclusively accessible to the wealthy
⑤ a farm that greatly needs the assistance of a scientist
questions.explanation: 글의 문맥상 농경지는 비료와 관개 시설 덕분에 영양분과 물이 풍부한 상태입니다. 잡초들에게 있어 이러한 풍부한 자원이 있는 농경지는 매우 탐나는 장소라는 의미에서 'luxury real estate(호화로운 부동산)'라고 표현되었습니다. 따라서 식물에게 필수적인 자원이 풍부한 들판을 의미하는 2번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 큰 경제적 가치를 지닌 지역
② 식물에게 필수적인 자원이 풍부한 들판
③ 생태학적 목적을 위해 보존된 장소
④ 부유층만 접근할 수 있는 구역
⑤ 과학자의 도움이 크게 필요한 농장

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
options: ① 행동은 자신이 생각하는 자기 모습을 반영한다.
② 무의식적인 행동은 주변의 압력으로부터 나온다.
③ 유권자들은 투표라는 행동으로 권리를 실행한다.
④ 모든 운동하는 사람들은 운동하는 것이 정체성이다.
⑤ 행동과 정체성이 완벽하게 일치하는 사람은 행동 변화를 추구한다.
questions.explanation: 글의 첫 문장에서 '행동은 대개 정체성의 반영이다'라고 핵심 내용을 제시하고 있습니다. 자신이 어떤 사람이라고 믿는지(정체성)에 따라 그에 일치하는 행동을 하게 된다는 것이 이 글의 요지입니다. 따라서 1번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life.
