These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
options: ② dangers of facing adversity unprepared
③ significance of facing difficulties in one's life
④ connection between individual habits and skills
⑤ challenges in dealing with unexpected life obstacles
questions.explanation: 이 글은 쉬운 길만을 택하려 하면 실력을 기를 수 없으며, 진정한 힘은 고난과 투쟁을 통해 얻어진다고 말합니다. 따라서 인생에서 어려움에 직면하는 것의 중요성이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 잘 준비된 운동선수들의 특성
② 준비되지 않은 채 역경에 직면하는 것의 위험성
③ 인생에서 어려움에 직면하는 것의 중요성
④ 개인의 습관과 기술 사이의 연결고리
⑤ 예상치 못한 삶의 장애물을 다루는 데 있어서의 어려움

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists say that having a disorderly room can indicate a disorganized mental state. One of the professional tidying experts says that the moment you start cleaning your room, you also start changing your life and gaining new perspective. When you clean your surroundings, positive and good atmosphere follows. You can do more things efficiently and neatly. So, clean up your closets, organize your drawers, and arrange your things first, then peace of mind will follow.
options: ① Act First and Do Not Overthink
② Birth of Creative Ideas in Disorder
③ Organizing Your Space for Positive Change
④ Observing Your Life from a Fresh Perspective
⑤ Setting Short-term Goals for Long-term Success
questions.explanation: 주변 환경을 정리하는 것이 정신 상태를 맑게 하고 삶에 긍정적인 변화와 마음의 평화를 가져다준다는 내용이므로, 공간을 정리하여 긍정적인 변화를 만든다는 제목이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 먼저 행동하고 너무 깊게 생각하지 마라
② 무질서 속에서 창의적인 아이디어의 탄생
③ 긍정적인 변화를 위해 당신의 공간을 정리하기
④ 새로운 관점에서 당신의 삶을 관찰하기
⑤ 장기적인 성공을 위해 단기적인 목표 설정하기

questions.question: 7. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The above graph shows the electronic waste collection and recycling rate by region in 2016 and 2019. ⓐEurope had the highest rates of electronic waste collection and recycling in both years. ⓑAsia's electronic waste collection and recycling rate was lower in 2019 compared to 2016. ⓒThe Americas placed third in both 2016 and 2019, with rates of 17 percent and 9 percent, respectively. ⓓIn both years, Oceania's electronic waste collection and recycling rates were below 10 percent. ⓔAfrica had the lowest electronic waste collection and recycling rates in both 2016 and 2019, with the smallest difference between the two years.
questions.explanation: 문장 ⓒ에서 미주 지역(The Americas)이 2016년과 2019년 각각 17%와 9%의 비율을 기록했다고 설명하고 있으나, 지문 내 수치 혹은 일반적인 도표 추이 분석 시 (2024년 6월 25번 원문 도표 기준) 2019년 수치가 2016년보다 높아야 하거나 순위/수치가 도표 데이터와 일치하지 않습니다. 지문에 제시된 수치 '17 percent and 9 percent' 중 2019년이 더 낮게 표현된 점이 오류입니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 Gourmet Baking Competition에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Gourmet Baking CompetitionGet out your cookbooks and dust off your greatest baking recipes.When & Where∙ 5 p.m. ─ 7 p.m. Saturday, August 3rd∙ Gourmet Baking StudioRegistration∙ Register online at www.bakeoff.org by July 25th.∙ Anyone can participate in the competition.Categories∙ Pies, Cakes, and Cookies∙ Each person can only enter one category.Prizes & Gifts∙ Prizes will be given to the top three in each category.∙ Souvenirs will be given to every participant.
options: ④ 각 참가자는 한 가지 부문에만 지원할 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 안내문의 마지막 줄에 'Souvenirs will be given to every participant.'(기념품은 모든 참가자에게 제공될 것이다)라고 명시되어 있으므로, 우승자에게만 제공된다는 ⑤번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that __________________________________ according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① our body parts move and react
② we are easily triggered by rewards
③ how brain is wired cannot be changed
④ the physical architecture of the brain changes
⑤ spatial memory and muscle memory may be different
questions.explanation: 이 글은 중중된 주의가 뇌의 재구성(reshaping)을 이끄어낸다는 내용입니다. 소리림 잘 듣는 동물의 청각 중심이 커지고, 바이올린 연주자의 왼손 담당 피질이 확장되며, 택시 기사의 해마가 커진다는 예시림 통해 우리가 어디에 주의림 기울이고 무엇을 훈련하는지에 땄라 뇌의 물리적 구조가 변한다는 결론을 도출할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 신체 부위가 와직이고 반응한다
② 우리는 밴상에 의해 쉽게 유발된다
③ 뇌가 어떻게 연결되어 있는지는 변할 수 없다
④ 뇌의 물리적 구조가 변한다
⑤ 감간 기억과 근육 기억은 다림 수 있다

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. ⓐOne 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. ⓑThese consistent and coordinated decisions made by the bosses led to increased efficiency. ⓒThey designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. ⓓWithin two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. ⓔGiving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심 주제는 직원들에게 자율권(a sense of agency)과 통제권을 부여하는 것이 생산성과 업무 몰입도를 획기적으로 높인다는 것입니다. 오하이오 공장의 사례 역시 노동자들이 스스로 업무 환경에 대한 결정을 내렸을 때의 긍정적인 결과를 보여주고 있습니다. 하지만 ②번(ⓑ) 문장은 '상사들(bosses)'에 의해 내려진 결정이 효율성을 높였다고 서술하고 있어, 직원의 자율성을 강조하는 글의 전체 흐름과 상반됩니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. (A) In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. (B) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. (C) Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. (D) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. (E) An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.insertion_sentence: As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 이동 생활을 하는 수렵 채집인 어머니들이 아이를 한 번에 한 명 이상 업고 다닐 수 없었기에 출산 간격을 4년 정도로 두게 되었다는 결과적인 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A)에서 어머니들이 어린 아이들을 데리고 다녀야 했다는 이동의 고충이 언급된 뒤, 그 결과에 해당하는 주어진 문장이 오는 것이 적절합니다. 그 뒤인 (B)부터는 정착 생활을 하는 농경 사회의 대조적인 상황이 제시됩니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.summary_sentence: Digital projects have frequently (A)____________ the requirements of individuals with disabilities, which is a situation that could be (B)____________ by embracing inclusive design principles.
questions.explanation: 본문은 디지털 프로젝트를 만들 때 장애인의 필요가 무시(neglected)되어 왔으며, 포괄적인 디자인 원칙을 수용함으로써 이러한 상황이 개선(improved/refined)될 수 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '방치하다/소홀히 하다'의 의미인 neglected, (B)에는 '개선되다/정교해지다'의 의미인 refined가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 방치했다 - 악화되었다
② 수용했다 - 정교해졌다
③ 간과했다 - 거부되었다
④ 수용했다 - 악화되었다
⑤ 방치했다 - 정교해졌다

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하눤 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although technology has the potential to increase productivity, it can also have a negative impact on productivity. For example, in many office environments workers sit at desks with computers and freely use the internet. They are able to check their personal emails and use social media whenever they want to. this can stop them from doing their work and make them less productive. Introducing new technology can also have a negative impact on production when it causes a change to the production process or requires workers to learn a new system. Learning to use new technology can be time consuming and stressful for workers and this can cause a decline in productivity.
options: ① Convenience can bring about unexpected laziness.
② Negative influence of technology is greater than ever.
③ Technology provides workers with excessive autonomy.
④ Technology affects lowering as well as boosting productivity.
⑤ Employers should be aware of the impact of technology.
questions.explanation: 글은 기술이 생산성을 높일 수 읈는 잠재력을 가지고 읈지만, 동시에 생산성에 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수도 읈다고 설명합니다. 인터넷 사용으로 인한 업무 방해나 새로운 시스템 숙득 과정에서의 스트레스 등을 예로 들어, 기술이 생산성을 향상시키기도 하지만 떨어뜨리기도 한다눤 점을 시사합니다.
options_translation: ① 편리함은 예상치 못한 게영림을 불러올 수 읈다.
② 기술의 부정적인 영향은 그 어느 때보다 킬다.
③ 기술은 노동자들에게 과도한 자율성을 부여한다.
④ 기술은 생산성을 줝대시킬 뿐만 아니라 저하시 수도 읈다.
⑤ 고용주들은 기술의 영향을 인지해야 한다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① Scientific Communication, a Bidirectional Interaction Between Readers and Scientific Papers
② The Distinction Between Sound Process and Scientific Communication
③ A True Literary Work: Only When the Reader is Understood
④ Scientists! Do Not Be Swayed by the Intended Audience
⑤ Why We Should Not Disregard Each Other's Opinions
questions.explanation: 글은 소리가 듣눤 사람이 읈어야 비로소 소리가 되눤 것처럼, 과학 커문니케이션도 발표된 놼문이 독자에 의해 수신되고 이해되어야 비로소 완성된다눤 점을 강조합니다. 즉, 과학적 소통은 쌍방향적 과정이라눤 것이 핵심 주제입니다.
options_translation: ① 과학적 소통, 독자와 과학 놼문 사이의 쌍방향적 상호작용
② 소리 과정과 과학적 소통의 차이
③ 진정한 문학 작품: 독자가 이해될 때만
④ 과학자들이여! 의도된 청중에 의해 휘둘리지 만라
⑤ 우리가 서로의 의견을 무시해서는 안 되눤 이유

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better we know about the Earth. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
options: ① Creating Perfect Condition For Our Planet
② The Beauty of Shapes in Crystal Structure
③ The Secret of How to Consume an Elephant
④ Building Blocks of the Earth: Understanding Atoms
⑤ The Simpler the Arrangement of Atoms, the More Beautiful Crystals Are
questions.explanation: 지문은 지구가 원자라는 기본 단위로 구성되어 있으며, 원자가 모여 결정이 되고 결정이 모여 암석(지구의 구성 성분)이 된다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 지구를 구성하는 요소로서 원자를 이해해야 한다는 내용의 4번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리 행성을 위한 완벽한 조건 만들기
② 결정 구조에서 모양의 아름다움
③ 코끼리를 먹는 방법에 대한 비밀
④ 지구의 구성 요소: 원자에 대한 이해
⑤ 원자의 배열이 단순할수록 결정은 더 아름답다

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans ⓐ<u>understate</u> shared characteristics between us and other animals as a way of protecting our spot at the top of hierarchy. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to ⓑ<u>distinguish</u> us from the other species. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence sowing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively ⓒ<u>superior</u> to those of humanity in the kind of toolmaking. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as not intelligence, but rather as an ⓓ<u>innate</u> behavior. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to ⓔ<u>deprive</u> animals of power, the way we manipulate words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 인간이 위계질서의 꼭대기를 유지하기 위해 동물의 능력을 폄하하고 인간과 구분 짓는 언어를 사용한다는 내용입니다. 침팬지나 까마귀의 도구 제작 능력이 인간의 도구 제작 능력보다 질적으로 '우수한(superior)' 것이 아니라 '열등한(inferior)' 것으로 해석한다는 흐름이 적절하므로 ⓒ가 틀렸습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: A key to ⓐ<u>engaging</u> students is providing them with relevant texts they will be interested in. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who performed highly ⓑ<u>successfully</u> in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. Although they had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years, all of them demonstrated excellence in their fields. While she expected to find that they had been ⓒ<u>obsessed</u> with reading and had discovered ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic... they hardly avoided reading. ⓓ<u>Unexpectedly</u>, they sought out books." The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The various areas such as religion, math, business, science, history, and biography ⓔ<u>triggered</u> their interest. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.
questions.explanation: Rosalie Fink는 난독증이 있는 사람들이 읽기를 '기피하고(avoid)' 그것을 우회할 방법을 찾았을 것이라고 예상했으나 반대의 결과(열정적으로 읽음)를 얻었다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ⓒ의 '열광했다(obsessed)'는 문맥상 '기피했다(avoided)'와 같은 부정적인 의미의 단어가 와야 예상과 실제가 반대되는 상황이 성립됩니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: People Who Reported Using Social Media in the U.S.(by age group) The graph above shows the percentages of people in different age groups who reported using social media in the United States in 2015 and 2021. ⓐIn each of the given years, the 65 and older group had the lowest percentage of people who said they used social media. ⓑIn 2015, the percentage of people who reported using social media in the 50-64 group was 39 percentage points lower than that in the 18-29 group. ⓒThe percentage of people who said they used social media in the 30-49 group in 2021 was more than twice that in the 65 and older group. ⓓExcept for the 50-64 group, the gap between the percentages of people who reported using social media from 2015 to 2021 isn't over one-fifth of 100%. ⓔAmong all the age groups, the 18-29 group showed the highest percentage of people who said they used social media in both years, followed by the 30-49 group.
questions.explanation: 원본 도표 데이터를 참고할 때, 2021년 30-49세 그룹의 소셜 미디어 사용 비율은 81%이고, 65세 이상 그룹은 45%입니다. 81%는 45%의 두 배(90%)를 넘지 않으므로 'more than twice'라는 설명은 틀렸습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity ⓐ<u>that</u> is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way ⓑ<u>which</u> production could be made more efficient, known as the "division of labor." One worker could do all these tasks, ⓒ<u>making</u> 20 pins in a day. But this work can be divided into its separate processes, with a number of workers each ⓓ<u>performing</u> one task. Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day. ⓔ<u>Had it not been for</u> the division of labor by Adam smith, only 200 would have been made a day.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 'production could be made more efficient'는 완전한 문장입니다. 선행사 'a way'를 수식하기 위해 관계대명사 which를 쓰는 것은 부적절하며, 관계부사 how를 대신할 수 있는 'in which'나 'that'으로 고쳐야 합니다. (way와 how는 함께 쓸 수 없습니다.)

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, we cannot classify food as good, ⓐ<u>nor can</u> we classify it as bad. There are, however, combinations of foods ⓑ<u>adding</u> up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats exclusively foods ⓒ<u>thought of</u> as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. ⓓ<u>Although</u> nutrient-dense, all these foods would not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person ⓔ<u>consumes</u> fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
questions.explanation: 문장의 주어는 'the person'이고 이에 연결되는 동사는 'has'입니다. 'consumes'부터 'snacks'까지는 주어인 'the person'을 수식하는 관계절이어야 하므로, 동사 'consumes'를 현재분사 'consuming'으로 바꾸거나 주격 관계대명사를 포함한 'who consumes'로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product.
ordered_passages: (A) By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady steam of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status - they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb.

(B) For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase.

(C) However, do not assume that a product is thoroughly complementary, as customers may not be completely locked in to the product. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 보완재의 정의를 내린 후, (B)에서 보완재의 예시(팝콘-영화)를 들며 한 제품의 인기가 오르면 보완재 매출도 오른다는 특징을 설명합니다. (A)에서는 이러한 보완재 생산이 수요를 보장한다는 비즈니스적 통찰과 '완전 보완재' 개념을 소개합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 'However'를 통해 제품이 완전히 보완적이지 않을 수도 있다는 예외 상황(가솔린차-전기차)을 제시하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. (A) Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. (B) This goes for the boardroom as well. (C) Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. (D) Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. (E) Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'many of them'은 앞 문장의 'Executives in sport management'를 가리킵니다. (D) 문장에서 스포츠 경영진의 전문성을 언급한 뒤, (E) 위치에 주어진 문장이 들어가 '하지만 그들은 비전문가들로부터 사업 운영 방식에 대한 비판에 직면한다'는 대조적 내용을 연결하는 것이 적절합니다. 뒤따르는 문장에서도 의사나 회계사에게는 훈수를 두지 않지만 스포츠 조직에는 피드백을 준다는 예시를 통해 이를 뒷받침하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life of natives in a location. ___________________________ because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
options: ① Natives will favor single ethnicity
② Ethnic pluralism may be welcomed
④ Natives can be preferable over foreigners
questions.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에 '이용 가능한 상품과 서비스의 범위가 늘어나기 때문에'라는 긍정적인 이유가 제시되고 있으며, 그 다음 문장이 'On the other hand'로 시작하며 다문화의 부정적인 측면을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 다문화(민족적 다원주의)가 긍정적으로 받아들여질 수 있다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 현지인들은 단일 민족을 선호할 것이다
② 민족적 다원주의가 환영받을 수 있다
③ 생산성이 확실히 안정된다
④ 현지인들이 외국인들보다 더 선호될 수 있다
⑤ 다문화주의는 경제 성장을 저해한다

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us. One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Göbekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society which ___________________________. Things are not so different in our own time.
options: ① quickly ended the era of hunter-gatherers and started an industrial society
② was fundamentally reorganized by architecture greatly influencing the way of life
③ revealed more talent in architecture than in the areas of philosophy and mathematics
④ built many historical structures for our descendants, leaving famous works to this day
⑤ led to the development of a city unprecedented in history by the combination of tourism and agriculture
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심 주제는 건물이 인간의 삶을 형성한다는 것입니다. 터키의 괴베클리 테페 유적을 예로 들어, 거석을 세우는 건축 활동을 완수하기 위해 수렵 채집인이 정착 생활을 하게 되었고 결국 최초의 농경 사회가 되었다는 내용을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '건축이 삶의 방식에 큰 영향을 미침으로써 근본적으로 재편된 사회'라는 의미가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 수렵 채집 시대를 빠르게 끝내고 산업 사회를 시작했다
② 생활 방식에 크게 영향을 미치는 건축에 의해 근본적으로 재편되었다
③ 철학이나 수학 분야보다 건축에서 더 많은 재능을 드러냈다
④ 우리 후손들을 위해 많은 역사적 구조물을 지어 오늘날까지 유명한 작품을 남겼다
⑤ 관광과 농업의 결합으로 역사상 유례없는 도시 발전을 이끌었다

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to _________________________________________. In other words, children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are and who they will be. This contributed to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
options: ① bridge the gap between their preexisting familiarity and upcoming shift
② disregard their previous memories and create new ones for adaptation
③ enable children to maintain their old habits, which boosts their imagination
④ expand their superficial knowledge to help relive stress and enhance self-esteem
questions.explanation: 이사할 때 아이들은 익숙한 것들을 잃고 불안해합니다. 빈칸 뒤의 'In other words' 이하의 문장에서 아이들의 과거를 존중하며 배경을 공유할 기회를 주어야 한다고 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 '기존의 익숙함과 다가올 변화(이사) 사이의 간극을 메워주는 것'이 중요하다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그들의 기존 익숙함과 다가올 변화 사이의 간극을 메우다
② 적응을 위해 이전의 기억을 무시하고 새로운 기억을 만들다
③ 아이들이 예전 습관을 유지하게 하여 상상력을 증진시키다
④ 스트레스를 완화하고 자존감을 높이기 위해 피상적인 지식을 확장하다

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are - writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
questions.summary_sentence: As having a good ability is thought of as making something visible or (A)___________ in a certain area, people are evaluated as either outstanding or average by their performance, which is inappropriate (B)___________ of oneself.
questions.explanation: 글의 내용은 능력을 지적 능력이나 특정 기술로 정의할 때, 그것이 자존감의 유일한 결정 요인이 되면 수행 능력이 곧 그 사람의 가치가 되어버리는 문제점을 지적합니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 능력이 뛰어난 것을 '비교 불가능한(incomparable)' 혹은 독보적인 것으로 만드는 것으로 볼 수 있고, (B)는 수행 능력만으로 사람을 평가하는 것이 부적절한 '판단(judgment)'임을 나타내야 합니다. 하지만 제시된 보기 중 흐름상 가장 적절한 것은 능력을 가시적이거나 뛰어난(incomparable) 성취로 보는 것과, 이를 자아에 대한 부적절한 '판단(judgment)'으로 연결하는 4번입니다.
options_translation: ① 도덕적인 - 이미지
② 부족한 - 반영
③ 사소한 - 평가
④ 비교할 수 없는 - 판단
⑤ 유연한 - 표준

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afriad they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're reasonable enough for your decision, not just being emotional.
questions.summary_sentence: Like driving a car directly rather than flying, most people (A)___________ control to reduce their fear, but this is a choice that rarely relies on (B)__________.
questions.explanation: 사람들이 비행기보다 직접 운전하는 것을 선택하는 이유는 통제권을 가짐으로써 불안을 줄이려 하기 때문입니다. 하지만 이는 통계적 사실(논리)보다는 감정에 기반한 선택입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 통제권을 선택한다는 의미의 'opt for(선택하다)'가, (B)에는 논리적인 근거를 뜻하는 'rationality(합리성)'가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 선택하다 ... 합리성
② 거절하다 ... 논리
③ 선택하다 ... 감정
④ 거부하다 ... 불안
⑤ 행사하다 ... 자신감

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable ⓐ<u>deviation</u>. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who ⓑ<u>violated</u> established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having ⓒ<u>remarkable</u> status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing peculiarity ⓓ<u>elevated</u> audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge slightly breaking away from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual ⓔ<u>unwillingly</u> pays the social costs on such behaviors.
options: ① tendency to consider the slight departure from the norm to be favorable in fashion
② social alienation issues that can arise when uniqueness and exceptions are valued
③ why appropriate clothing for different situations and time is increasingly important
④ need for the professional workers to prioritize competence and ability over their appearance
⑤ why people with a spirit of challenge, who dare to break away from the norm, are disappearing
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 관습이나 기대에서 아주 약간 벗어난 복장을 한 사람(예: 정장에 붉은 나비넥타이, 강의 중 빨간 운동화)에 대해 긍정적으로 평가하고, 그들의 지위와 능력을 더 높게 평가한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 '패션에서 규범으로부터의 약간의 일탈을 우호적으로 간주하는 경향'인 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 패션에서 규범으로부터의 약간의 일탈을 우호적으로 간주하는 경향
② 독특함과 예외가 가치 있게 여겨질 때 발생할 수 있는 사회적 소외 문제
③ 상황과 시간에 따른 적절한 의복이 점점 더 중요해지는 이유
④ 전문직 종사자들이 외모보다 역량과 능력을 우선시해야 할 필요성
⑤ 규범에서 과감히 벗어나려는 도전 정신을 가진 사람들이 사라지는 이유

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable ⓐ<u>deviation</u>. The results suggest that people judge slightly breaking away from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual ⓔ<u>unwillingly</u> pays the social costs on such behaviors.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장에서 사람들이 규범을 살짝 벗어나는 것을 긍정적으로 평가하는 이유는, 그 개인이 그러한 행동에 따르는 사회적 비용을 '기꺼이(willingly)' 지불할 만큼 충분히 지위나 능력이 있다고 생각하기 때문입니다. 따라서 'unwillingly(마지못해)'를 'willingly'로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 주제를 아래와 같이 작성하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 각각 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. <u>Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities</u>. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are minimized. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these -segmenters- carrying two phones - one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.subjective_answer_format: two different approaches to the boundaries between work and home (A)___________ by (B)___________ of portable digital technology(A) ________________ (1단어)(B) ________________ (1단어)
questions.explanation: 휴대용 디지털 기술의 발달로 인해 일과 가정의 경계가 흐려진 상황에서 사람들이 취하는 두 가지 접근 방식에 대한 글입니다. (A)에는 경계가 '흐려진'이라는 뜻의 blurred가, (B)에는 기술의 '발전'이라는 뜻의 advance(s)나 development가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바를 영어로 작성하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. <u>Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities</u>. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are minimized. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones - one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어만을 사용하여 작성할 것
<보기>의 단어를 중복하여 사용 가능
<보기>의 단어 형태 변형 가능
questions.answer: prefer separating the roles (of work and family) to minimize the boundary crossings while others prefer integrating the roles (of work and family)
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 사람들이 일과 외부 책임을 관리하는 방식이 서로 다르다는 의미입니다. 글의 맥락에 따라, 어떤 이들은 경계 교차를 최소화하기 위해 역할을 분리하는 것을 선호하고, 반면 다른 이들은 역할을 통합하는 것을 선호한다는 내용을 <보기>의 단어를 활용해 작성해야 합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Sometimes the pace of change is far slower. The face you saw reflected in your mirror this morning probably appeared no different from the face you saw the day before - or a week or a month ago. Yet we know that the face that stares back at us from the glass is not the same, cannot be the same, as it was 10 minutes ago. The proof is in your photo album: Look at a photograph taken of yourself 5 or 10 years ago and you see clear differences between the face in the snapshot and the face in your mirror. If you lived in a world without mirrors for a year and then saw your reflection, you might be surprised by the change. After an interval of 10 years without seeing yourself, you might not at first recognize the person peering from the mirror. Even something as basic as our own face changes from moment to moment.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸을 작성할 것
(A), (B) 관계없이 <보기>의 단어는 한 번만 사용할 것
필요한 단어를 추가하여 작성할 것
<보기>의 단어 형태를 변형하지 말 것
questions.answer: (A) faces change gradually and consistently(B) difficult to notice[recognize] easily
questions.explanation: 지문은 얼굴이 매 순간 변하지만 그 속도가 매우 느려서 평소에는 인식하기 어렵고, 시간이 많이 흐른 뒤 사진 등을 통해서야 그 변화를 분명히 알 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 요약문 (A)에는 얼굴이 점진적이고 지속적으로 변한다는 내용이, (B)에는 그것을 쉽게 알아차리기 어렵다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; (A)_____________, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. (B)_____________, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 동물마다 특징이 다르다고 했으므로, 그 결과 치유 과정에서도 다르게 반응할 것이라는 인과 관계가 성립하여 'thus'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞에서는 환경적 요인에 따른 차이를 언급했고, (B) 뒤에서는 질병의 종류(신체적 vs 정서적)에 따른 차이를 추가로 언급하고 있으므로 첨가/나열의 의미인 'Besides'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나 - 더욱이
② 대신에 - 결과적으로
③ 따라서 - 게다가
④ 마찬가지로 - 그럼에도 불구하고
⑤ 그렇지 않으면 - 예를 들어

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. ⓐIf they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. ⓑLiving in huts on high ground, they arranged for horses to get out immediately. ⓒThe Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. ⓓWhen a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. ⓔThe Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인카 제국이 말이 없는 상황에서 'Chasquis'라고 불리는 도보 전령들을 통해 메시지를 전달한 방식에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 첫 문장에서 '말이 이용 가능하지 않았다(no horses available)'고 명시하고 있으므로, 말이 바로 나갈 수 있도록 준비했다는 내용인 ⓑ번 문장은 전체 흐름과 맞지 않습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. ⓐBut like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. ⓑThrough diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others. ⓒTo be worldwide famous leaders, being born with superiority in the ability and passion for achieving goals is the first requirement. ⓓSeeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. ⓔThus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 위대한 리더들도 처음에는 평범한 시민으로 시작했으며, 누구나 일상 속에서 리더가 될 잠재력이 있다는 내용입니다. 그러나 ⓒ번은 세계적인 리더가 되기 위해 타고난 능력과 열정의 우월함이 첫 번째 요건이라고 주장하고 있어, 평범한 사람들도 리더가 될 수 있다는 글의 흐름과 반대됩니다.

questions.question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(B) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.

(C) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 아리스텀텔룬스가 정의한 5감각을 설명합니다. (B)에서 그것에 대한 의문(However... doubt it)을 제기하며 인간의 추가적인 감각을 예로 듭니다. (A)에서는 인간 외에 'EB24른 동물들(Other animals)'의 특수한 감각 사례를 듭니다. (C)에서는 'EB74러한 사례들(These examples)'을 통해 감각을 몇 가지로 명확히 나누기 어뮵다고 결론을 내립니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 묑줄 친 붽분 중, 문맥사 낱말의 스임이 적절하준 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more ①<u>energizing</u> and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more ②<u>content</u> on the job, they produce higher quality work and a greater output. As a result, they are also generally ③<u>well paid</u>. Those most satisfied with their work are also much ④<u>less</u> likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater ⑤<u>satisfaction</u> from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 일에서 의문를 찾고 만족하는 사람이 삶 전체적으로도 덄 행복하다는 내용입니다. 따라서 일에 만족하는 사람은 삶 전체에서 행복해질 가능성이 덄 '높아야(more)' 합니다. ④번의 less(덜)는 문맥사 반대되는 표현입니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 it(its)이 의미하는 것이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases ⓐ<u>it</u> is marked and appears to be out of the norm. People expect that you will say ⓑ<u>it</u>. You become responsible. Failing to say ⓒ<u>it</u> will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for ⓓ<u>its</u> usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case, saying ⓔ<u>it</u> would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
questions.explanation: ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 문맥상 구체적인 표현인 'Thank you(고맙다는 말)'를 가리킵니다. 반면 ⓐ는 앞선 조건문 'if people don't say Thank you in these cases'의 내용을 받아 '사람들이 이러한 경우에 고맙다는 말을 하지 않는 상황/사실'을 나타내는 상황의 it입니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. (A) Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. (B) The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street. (C) Thus, Motorists simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. (D) Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 보행자 이동(pedestrian travel)이 환경적 세부 사항을 감상하게 해준다는 내용입니다. (D) 앞부분은 운전자(motorists)가 세부 사항을 감상할 시간이 없다는 부정적인 내용을 다루고 있고, (D) 이후에는 조깅하는 사람과 자전거 타는 사람이 그 '양극단(polar opposites)' 사이에 있다고 설명합니다. 여기서 양극단이란 운전자와 보행자를 의미하므로, 보행자에 대한 설명인 주어진 문장은 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 밑줄 친 curse of knowledge가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the '<u>curse of knowledge</u>'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
options: ① learner's insensitivity to the difficulty in mastering skills
② assumptions about training situations by new participants
③ the level of learning difficulty underestimated by experts
④ hard tasks that a novice usually needs to acquire skills
⑤ people's inaccuracy of expertise in an earlier session
questions.explanation: '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'란 전문가가 어떤 기술을 습득하고 나면 그것을 배우는 것이 얼마나 어려운지 잊어버리고, 초보자에게 그 과업이 얼마나 어려울지를 과소평가하게 되는 현상을 의미합니다. 따라서 ③번 '전문가에 의해 과소평가된 학습 난이도의 수준'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기술을 숙달하는 데 있어서의 어려움에 대한 학습자의 무감각
② 새로운 참가자들에 의한 교육 상황에 대한 가정
③ 전문가에 의해 과소평가된 학습 난이도의 수준
④ 초보자가 기술을 습득하기 위해 보통 필요로 하는 어려운 과업들
⑤ 이전 세션에서의 전문 지식에 대한 사람들의 부정확성

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 대명사와 그것이 가리키는 대상이 서로 잘못 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - ⓐ<u>they</u> are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but ⓑ<u>it</u> is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and ⓒ<u>they</u> fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count ⓓ<u>it</u> as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, ⓔ<u>it</u> seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장 'But as sleep would be impossible without it, ⓔit seems essential to its definition'에서 'it'은 앞에서 언급된 'perceptual disengagement(지각적 이탈)'를 가리킵니다. 지각적 이탈 없이는 잠이 불가능하므로, 그것(지각적 이탈)이 수면의 정의에 필수적인 것으로 보인다는 문맥입니다. 따라서 ⓔ가 가리키는 대상은 sleep이 아니라 perceptual disengagement입니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐthey: 눈(the eyes)
② ⓑit: 일부 시각 정보(some visual information)
③ ⓒthey: 자극(stimuli)
④ ⓓit: 지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)
⑤ ⓔit: 수면(sleep)

questions.question: 19. 다음 글을 읽고 정리한 내용에서 바르게 작성된 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and ⓐ<u>recognition</u>. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to ⓑ<u>carry on</u> a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that ⓒ<u>lets you down</u> frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but ⓓ<u>they</u> originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.summary_sentence: The mind of consciousness is in charge of thoughts and emotions while the mind of subconsciousness stores your responses and turns fears into true fears.
options: ① ⓐrecognition: a lack of knowledge, understanding, or education
② ⓑcarry on: cause someone to stop paying attention to something
③ ⓒlets you down을 lets down you로 바꿀 수 있다.
⑤ The mind of consciousness is in charge of thoughts and emotions while the mind of subconsciousness stores your responses and turns fears into true fears.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)은 사고와 감정을 담당하며 통제 가능한 부분으로 설명되고, 잠재의식적인 마음(subconscious mind)은 반응을 기록하고 이를 실제 공포로 저장하는 역할을 한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 ⑤번 요약문이 지문의 내용을 가장 정확하게 반영하고 있습니다. ① recognition은 '인식/재인'을 의미하므로 무지를 뜻하는 영풀은 틀렸습니다. ② carry on은 '계속하다'의 의미입니다. ③ 타동사+대명사+부사 어순에서 대명사는 반드시 중간에 와야 하므로 'lets down you'는 불가능합니다. ④ they는 문맥상 'all of these fears'를 지칭합니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐrecognition: 지식, 이해 또는 교육의 부족
② ⓑcarry on: 누군가가 무언가에 주의를 기울이는 것을 멈추게 하다
③ ⓒlets you down을 lets down you로 바꿀 수 있다.
④ ⓓthey는 잘못된 결정들(wrong decisions)을 지칭한다.
⑤ 의식의 마음은 생각과 감정을 담당하는 반면, 잠재의식의 마음은 당신의 반응을 저장하고 공포를 진정한 공포로 바꾼다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: In the past, the tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. According to leading taste researchers, it's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
options: ① 과거에는 혀의 끝에는 단맛, 양면에는 신맛, 안쪽에는 쓴맛이 '혀 지도'에 등록되어 있었다.
② '혀 지도'는 1980년대와 1990년대에 수행된 연구를 오해하고 오역한 것이다.
③ 오늘날의 선도적인 미각 연구자들은 미뢰가 맛을 느끼는 전문 분야에 따라 분류된다고 믿는다.
④ 선도적인 미각 연구자들에 따르면 작동 기제는 시간이 아니라 위치이다.
⑤ 선도적인 미각 연구자들에 의하면, 혀끝에서 단맛을 느끼는 것이 아니라 오히려 그 단맛 인식을 가장 먼저 등록하는 것이다.
questions.explanation:
① 과거에 쓴맛은 혀의 안쪽(뒤쪽)에서 느끼는 것으로 알려져 있었습니다.
② '혀 지도'는 20세기 초 독일에서 이루어진 연구 해석을 오해하고 오역한 결과입니다.
③ 오늘날의 미각 연구자들은 미뢰가 특정 맛에 전문화되어 분류되지 않는다고 주장합니다.
④ 작동 기제는 위치(장소)가 아니라 시간이라고 지문에 명시되어 있습니다.
⑤ 지문의 마지막 문장에서 혀끝이 단맛을 가장 먼저 인식(등록)한다는 점을 언급하고 있으므로 내용과 일치합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Especially focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of (A)_________________ as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence. The findings showed that when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly (B)___________.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 쓸 것.
단어를 변형하지 말 것.
(A)는 2단어, (B)는 1단어로 쓸 것.
questions.explanation: (A)는 문맥상 '정신 건강 치료로서의 노래 부르기의 효능'을 의미하므로 본문에서 'group singing'을 찾아 쓸 수 있습니다. (B)는 합창단에 참여했을 때 정신 건강과 안녕이 '개선되었다'는 내용이 들어가야 하므로 본문에서 'improved'를 찾아 쓸 수 있습니다. (developed 또한 가능하나 문맥상 improved가 적절함)

questions.question: 9. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. For example, in animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. (A)__________, in animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Likewise, brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. (B)__________, other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① Reshape Your Brain Using Brain Scanning Technology
② The Impact of Focused Attention on Brain Development
③ Focused Attention: Understanding Your Brain's Limitations
④ Enlarge Your Brain Functions through Scanning and Practice
⑤ Differences in Brain Development Between Animals and Humans
questions.explanation: 이 글은 집중된 주의가 뇌의 구조적 변화(재구성)를 이끈다는 내용을 동물과 사람(바이올린 연주자, 택시 기사)의 사례를 통해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '뇌 발달에 미치는 집중된 주의의 영향'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌 스캐닝 기술을 이용해 뇌를 재구성하라
② 집중된 주의가 뇌 발달에 미치는 영향
③ 집중된 주의: 당신의 뇌의 한계 이해하기
④ 스캐닝과 연습을 통한 뇌 기능 확대
⑤ 동물과 인간 사이의 뇌 발달 차이점

questions.question: 10. 윗글의 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. For example, in animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. (A)__________, in animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Likewise, brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. (B)__________, other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ④ On the hand ... By contrast
⑤ On the other hand ... On the contrary
questions.explanation: (A) 앞뒤 내용이 소리에 보상받는 동물과 시력에 보상받는 동물의 유사한 사례를 나열하고 있으므로 'Similarly(마찬가지로)'가 적절합니다. (B) 바이올린 연주자의 예시 뒤에 택시 기사의 또 다른 사례를 추가하고 있으므로 'Additionally(추가적으로)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 마찬가지로 ... 추가적으로
② 결과적으로 ... 대조적으로
③ 불행하게도 ... 비교해 볼 때
④ 한편으로는 ... 대조적으로
⑤ 반면에 ... 반대로

questions.question: 11. 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. In the 1870s, grey squirrels were brought to England by people as pets, and they quickly became an invasive species. As a result, they competed with the native red squirrels for food and habitat, putting the red populations under significant pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England. (A)If the grey had __________ __________ __________ __________, the red would not have __________ __________.
options: ① 생태계에 유입된 외래종은 문제를 유발할 수 있다.
② 1870년대 영국으로 애완용 붉은 다람쥐가 도입되었다.
③ 회색 다람쥐는 설익은 도토리를 소화시킬 수 없다.
④ 붉은 다람쥐는 모든 도토리를 먹을 수 있어 우위를 차지했다.
⑤ 붉은 다람쥐는 영국에서 계속 개체수가 급증했다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 첫 문장 "Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem."에 주제가 명시되어 있습니다. ②번은 회색 다람쥐가 도입된 것이고, ③번 회색 다람쥐는 설익은 도토리(green acorns)를 먹을 수 있으며, ④번 회색 다람쥐가 우위를 점했고, ⑤번 붉은 다람쥐는 멸종 위기에 처했습니다.

questions.question: 12. 윗글의 (A) 부분을 <보기>의 단어들만을 모두 활용하여 문맥과 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [5.0점]
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. In the 1870s, grey squirrels were brought to England by people as pets, and they quickly became an invasive species. As a result, they competed with the native red squirrels for food and habitat, putting the red populations under significant pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England. (A)If the grey had __________ __________ __________ __________, the red would not have __________ __________.
subjective_conditions: - <보기>에서 제시된 단어만을 꼭 모두 사용할 것
- 필요한 경우 단어를 변형하거나 반복 사용할 수 있음
questions.answer: not been brought in, been threatened
questions.explanation: 본문의 내용을 바탕으로 과거 사실에 대한 반대 상황을 가정하는 가정법 과거완료 문장을 구성해야 합니다. '회색 다람쥐가 도입되지 않았더라면, 붉은 다람쥐는 위협받지 않았을 것이다'라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 'had not been brought in'과 'would not have been threatened'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process ______________________________. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ① overlooks certain ideas and voices
② limits the range of ideas and perspectives
③ ensures the inclusion of every idea and opinion
④ prioritizes specific ideas and options over others
⑤ considers only the merits of select ideas and voices
questions.explanation: 브레인라이팅은 아이디어를 개별적으로 생성하고 익명으로 평가하는 과정을 거치기 때문에, 소외되는 의견 없이 모든 구성원의 아이디어가 포함되도록 보장하는 역할을 합니다.
options_translation: ① 특정 아이디어와 목소리를 간과한다
② 아이디어와 관점의 범위를 제한한다
③ 모든 아이디어와 의견의 포함을 보장한다
④ 다른 것보다 특정 아이디어와 선택 사항을 우선시한다
⑤ 선택된 아이디어와 목소리의 장점만을 고려한다

questions.question: 24. 다음은 사회자가 이끄는 'brainwriting' 진행 과정이다. 밑줄 친 표현들 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process ensures the inclusion of every idea and opinion. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.<Brainwriting Session Led by a Facilitator>Welcome, everyone! Today, we're conducting a brainwriting session ⓐ<u>to uncover underlying potential</u> in our team. Let's get started. Take 10 minutes to generate as many ideas as you can on 'Improving Digital Accessibility for People with Disabilities.' ⓑ<u>Work individually</u> and write down your thoughts. Submit your ideas into our central collection box. I'll distribute ⓒ<u>the pooled ideas back to you anonymously</u>. Please review the ideas you've received. Spend 15 minutes ⓓ<u>evaluating the ideas interdependently</u>. Consider their feasibility, creativity, and impact of each idea. Let's discuss your top ideas and ⓔ<u>choose and enhance the most favorable ones as a team</u>. Now, let's elaborate on our selected ideas. Discuss implementation strategies and challenges. Thank you for participating. We've surfaced some fantastic ideas. Any questions or final thoughts? Thanks again, everyone. Have a wonderful day!
questions.explanation: 지문 본문에서 "To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own(독립적인 판단을 보존하기 위해, 각 구성원은 그것들을 스스로 평가한다)"라고 언급되어 있습니다. 따라서 사회자의 말 중 ⓓ의 'interdependently(상호의존적으로)'는 'independently(독립적으로)' 또는 'on your own'으로 바뀌어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. Although it may seem sensible, having two separate calendars for work and personal life can result in reduced (A)[distraction / concentration]. To check if something is missing, you will find yourself checking your to-do lists multiple times. A preferable approach is to (B)[disarrange / consolidate] all tasks into a single organizational system. It doesn't matter if you use digital or paper media. It's okay to keep your professional and personal tasks in one place. This will give you a good idea of how time is divided between work and home. You'll be equipped to make well-informed decisions regarding the priority of tasks. This way, you can manage your time more efficiently and avoid (C)[conflicting / balanced] schedules.
questions.explanation: (A) 두 개의 별도 달력을 갖는 것은 주의를 분산시켜 '집중력(concentration)'을 감소시킵니다. (B) 더 나은 접근법은 모든 업무를 하나의 시스템으로 '통합하는(consolidate)' 것입니다. (C) 이렇게 하면 시간을 효율적으로 관리하고 일정이 '충돌하는(conflicting)' 것을 피할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although technology has the potential to increase productivity, it can also have a negative impact on productivity. For example, in many office environments workers sit at desks with computers and have access to the internet. They are able to check their personal e-mails and use social media whenever they want to. This can stop them from doing their work and make them less productive. Introducing new technology can also have a negative impact on production when it causes a change to the production process or requires workers to learn a new system. Learning to use new technology can be time consuming and stressful for workers and this can cause a decline in productivity.
questions.summary_sentence: Technology, while capable of (A)____________ productivity, can also hinder it, especially in office settings where access to personal emails and social media can lead to distractions. Additionally, the introduction of new technology may (B)____________ workflows and require time-consuming training, potentially resulting in decreased productivity.
questions.explanation: 본문은 기술이 생산성을 높일 수도 있지만 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수도 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 요약문 (A)에는 생산성을 높이다(boosting/increasing/elevating)라는 의미가 들어가야 하며, (B)에는 새로운 기술 도입이 작업 흐름을 방해하거나 중단시킨다(disrupt/disturb)는 의미가 들어가야 합니다. 따라서 ⑤번 'boosting - disrupt'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 높이는 - 지원하다
② 줄어드는 - 방해하다
③ 감소시키는 - 안정시키다
④ 증가시키는 - 용이하게 하다
⑤ 높이는 - 방해하다(중단시키다)

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is that people in wealthier, more industrialized nations _________________________. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life - which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
options: ① are stressed out due to time pressure
② ease their stress by having time flexibility
③ have a relaxed time frame to complete a task
④ maintain healthy stress levels for overall productivity
⑤ achieve fast-paced productivity at the cost of reduced quality
questions.explanation: 부유하고 산업화된 국가일수록 생활 속도가 빨라지고, 이로 인해 시간적 압박과 긴박함을 느끼며 스트레스를 받는다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 시간 압박으로 인해 스트레스를 받는다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 시간 압박으로 인해 스트레스를 받는다
② 시간적 유연성을 가짐으로써 스트레스를 완화한다
③ 과업을 완수하기 위한 여유로운 시간 틀을 가진다
④ 전반적인 생산성을 위해 건강한 수준의 스트레스를 유지한다
⑤ 품질 저하를 대가로 빠른 속도의 생산성을 달성한다

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Sometimes the pace of change is far slower. The face you saw reflected in your mirror this morning probably appeared no different from the face you saw the day before - or a week or a month ago. Yet we know that the face that stares back at us from the glass is not the same, cannot be the same, as it was 10 minutes ago. The proof is in your photo album: Look at a photograph taken of yourself 5 or 10 years ago and you see __________________ between the face in the snapshot and the face in your mirror. If you lived in a world without mirrors for a year and then saw your reflection, you might be surprised by the change. After an interval of 10 years without seeing yourself, you might not at first recognize the person peering from the mirror. Even something as basic as our own face changes from moment to moment.
questions.explanation: 매일 거울을 볼 때는 변화를 느끼지 못하지만, 5년 전이나 10년 전의 사진과 현재의 얼굴을 비교하면 분명한 차이를 보게 된다는 내용이므로 '명백한 차이점'이라는 뜻의 obvious distinctions가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 명백한 차이점
② 변하지 않는 측면
③ 미묘한 유사점
④ 규칙적인 동일성
⑤ 균일한 특징

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are fee of most of those that are socially undesirable. ⓐFor example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. ⓑThis phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." ⓒReading both fiction and nonfiction broadens our understanding of the world. ⓓA survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. ⓔIn terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 자신은 평균보다 더 나은 특성을 가지고 있고 바람직하지 않은 특성은 덜 가지고 있다고 믿는 '레이크 워비곤 효과(Lake Wobegon effect)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓒ는 허구와 비허구 도서를 읽는 것이 세상에 대한 이해를 넓혀준다는 내용으로, 자기 자신을 평균 이상으로 평가하려는 경향이라는 주제와 전혀 관련이 없습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad. There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on symbolsized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
options: ① A balanced and varied diet is not essential for all age groups.
② When we have good food, it supplies a wide variety of the nutrients we need.
③ High-calorie foods such as fried chicken cause health problems in teenagers.
④ Labeling individual foods strictly as "good" or "bad" can help simplify dietary choices for people.
⑤ It's not about labeling foods as good or bad but about how they come together to shape the quality of one's diet.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 개별 음식을 '좋은 음식'과 '나쁜 음식'으로 나누는 이분법적 사고를 비판하며, 건강한 식단은 개별 음식이 아니라 음식들이 어떻게 조합되어 전체적인 식습관(diet)을 형성하느냐에 달려 있다고 강조합니다. 몸에 좋은 음식만 먹어도 다양성이 부족하면 건강하지 않을 수 있고, 가끔 튀긴 음식을 먹어도 전체적인 균형이 맞으면 문제가 없다는 예시를 통해 요지를 뒷받침하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 균형 잡히고 다양한 식단이 모든 연령층에게 필수적인 것은 아니다.
② 우리가 좋은 음식을 먹을 때, 그것은 우리에게 필요한 다양한 영양소를 공급한다.
③ 프라이드치킨과 같은 고칼로리 음식은 십 대들에게 건강 문제를 일으킨다.
④ 개별 음식을 '좋음' 또는 '나쁨'으로 엄격하게 분류하는 것은 사람들의 식단 선택을 단순화하는 데 도움이 될 수 있다.
⑤ 음식을 좋거나 나쁜 것으로 분류하는 것이 아니라, 그것들이 어떻게 모여 한 사람의 식단의 질을 형성하는지가 중요하다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Up until about 6,000 years ago, most people were farmers. Many lived in different places throughout the year, hunting for food or moving their livestock to areas with enough food. (A) There was no need to tell the time because life depended on natural cycles, such as the changing seasons or sunrise and sunset. (B) For example, priests wanted to know when to carry out religious ceremonies. (C) This was when people first invented clocks - devices that show, measure, and keep track of passing time. (D) Clocks have been important ever since. (E) Today, clocks are used for important things such as setting busy airport timetables - if the time is incorrect, aeroplanes might crash into each other when taking off or landing!
questions.insertion_sentence: Gradually more people started to live in larger settlements, and some needed to tell the time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 사람들이 더 큰 정착지에 살기 시작하면서 시간을 알 필요가 생겼다는 내용입니다. (A) 앞뒤 내용은 시간이 필요 없었던 농경/유목 생활에 대해 말하고 있습니다. (B) 뒤에 나오는 '예를 들어, 제사장들은 종교 의식을 언제 수행할지 알고 싶어 했다'라는 문장은 시간을 알아야 할 필요성에 대한 구체적인 사례이므로, 주어진 문장은 (B) 자리에 들어가는 것이 흐름상 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글을 읽고, 대화의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [2.9점]
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.↓A: Did you read this article?B: Not yet. What's is about?A: It says that individuals who (A)__________ in their professions often gain immediate credibility with others.B: Interesting. Tell me more.A: People admire them and feel a connection to them. Their words carry weight, even if their expertise isn't related to the advice they're giving. Think about a famous basketball player. He makes more money from endorsements than from actually playing.B: Right.A: The same goes for an actor. When an actor recommends a car, we pay attention not because of (B)_____________________________. Excellence fosters connections. If you perform at a high level in a particular area, others are likely to seek a connection with you because of that excellence.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 한 단어로 쓸 것
필요시 어형을 변형할 것
questions.explanation: 본문의 'perform at a high level'을 한 단어로 요약하면 'excel(뛰어나다)'이 됩니다. 문맥상 관계대명사 who 뒤에 오는 동사 자리이며, 선행사 individuals가 복수이므로 동사원형 excel을 사용합니다.

questions.question: 28. 윗글을 읽고, 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [3.1점]
