questions.question: 1. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Number of Births and Deaths in Korea The above graph shows the number of births and deaths in Korea from 2016 to 2021. ⓐThe number of births continued to decrease throughout the whole period. ⓑThe gap between the number of briths and deaths was the largest in 2016. ⓒIn 2019, the gap between the number of births and deaths was the smallest, with the number of births slightly smaller than that of deaths. ⓓThe number of deaths increased steadily during the whole period, except the period from 2018 to 2019. ⓔIn 2020, the number of deaths was larger than that of births for the first time.
questions.explanation: 2019년에 출생아 수와 사망아 수 사이의 격차가 가장 작았던 것은 맞으나, 본문 ⓔ에서 알 수 있듯이 2020년에 처음으로 사망자 수가 출생아 수보다 많아졌으므로, 2019년에는 여전히 출생아 수가 사망자 수보다 많았습니다. 따라서 '출생아 수가 사망자 수보다 약간 더 적었다'는 ⓒ의 설명은 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often establish instant trust with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen even if the area of their skill is ⓐ<u>extraneous</u> to the advice they give. For example, Michael Jordan is one of the world's most talented athletes. In terms of sports, his record is legendary. Nike, on the other hand, does manufacture shoes. And since it ⓑ<u>partnered</u> with Jordan in 1984 to sell shoes, the company has grown in revenue more than 40 times over. Although Michael Jordan is not a shoe manufacturer, he also has made more money from Nike shoes endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. ⓒ<u>Credibility</u> can form a connection. The same can be said of a famous actor. When the actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we listen. The reason to pay attention to his advice has ⓓ<u>something</u> to do with the qualifications to drive specific types of vehicles. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may model ⓔ<u>themselves</u> on you.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 한 분야에서 뛰어난 능력을 가진 사람에 대한 신뢰가 다른 분야의 조언까지 수용하게 만든다는 내용입니다. 유명 배우가 특정 자동차를 운전하라고 권할 때 우리가 귀를 기울이는 이유는, 그가 그 자동차를 운전할 특별한 자격(qualifications)이 있어서가 아닙니다. 즉, 그의 자격과는 '관련이 없지만(nothing to do with)' 그의 명성이나 신뢰도 때문에 듣는 것입니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 'something'은 문맥상 'nothing' 또는 'little'이 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Just like a city, the brain's overall operation emerges from the networked interaction of its innumerable parts. There is often a temptation to assign a ⓐ<u>function</u> to each region of the brain, in the form of "this part does that." But despite a long history of attempts, we are ⓑ<u>able</u> to regard brain function as the sum of activity in a collection of well-defined modules because the whole is greater than the sum of its parts. Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?", it is ⓒ<u>difficult</u> to answer the question. It is because the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And it's the ⓓ<u>same</u> with how the brain operates: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain functions ⓔ<u>independently</u>. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly.
questions.explanation: 뇌의 기능은 특정 부위에 국한된 기능의 합이 아니라, 전체적인 네트워크 상호작용을 통해 발생한다고 설명하고 있습니다. '전체는 부분의 합보다 크기 때문에' 뇌 기능을 단순히 잘 정의된 모듈의 합으로 간주하는 것은 '불가능하다(unable)'는 맥락이 되어야 합니다. ⓑ의 able은 흐름상 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The term "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists for a reason. A quick look at social media comments about weekend games reveals that many fans think they could play, coach, and manage sports teams more ⓐ<u>effectively</u> than the professionals. This attitude extends to the boardroom as well. Even those with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business often feel embarrassed to receive ⓑ<u>feedback</u> from friends, family, or strangers who lack expertise. Executives in sport management, despite their decades of knowledge and experience, frequently encounter criticism from fans and community members on how to ⓒ<u>run</u> their organizations. ⓓ<u>Like</u> in fields such as medicine or accounting, where people rarely question professionals, many people give advice on how sports should be managed. This trend not only showcases more people engaging in sports discussions but also reveals the ⓔ<u>challenges</u> professionals face.
questions.explanation: 의학이나 회계와 같은 분야에서는 사람들이 전문가에게 거의 의문을 제기하지 않는다는 내용과, 스포츠 분야에서는 비전문가들이 전문가에게 조언을 한다는 내용이 대조를 이루어야 합니다. 따라서 'Like(~처럼)'가 아니라 'Unlike(~와 달리)'가 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. As a result, businesses had to shift their focus from mere production efficiency to _______________________________. That is, customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ① building the capacity for mass production
② taking the lead in revolutionary technology
③ understanding and satisfying customer needs
④ focusing on increasing production speed
⑤ maintaining a simple product lineup
questions.explanation: 과거에는 생산만 하면 수요가 창출된다는 생산 효율성 중심의 사고가 지배적이었으나, 사회가 현대화되면서 고객이 실제로 원하는 제품을 제공하는 마케팅 혁명이 일어났습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 내용에서 고객의 다양하고 복잡한 요구를 충족시키는 것이 초점이 되었다고 했으므로, 정답은 '고객의 요구를 이해하고 만족시키는 것'입니다.
options_translation: ① 대량 생산 능력을 구축하는 것
② 혁신적인 기술에서 앞서 나가는 것
③ 고객의 요구를 이해하고 만족시키는 것
④ 생산 속도를 높이는 데 집중하는 것
⑤ 단순한 제품 라인업을 유지하는 것

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Moving presents challenges for everyone, but it's especially stressful for children. Children lose their sense of security and feel disoriented as their familiar routines are broken and their surroundings ⓐ<u>change</u>. Particularly weak are young children experiencing moving, whose understanding is largely literal, making it challenging for them to imagine ⓑ<u>what</u> a new home and bedroom will be like beforehand. Worries such as "Will I remain the same person in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" are common among young children ⓒ<u>facing</u> a move. It's essential to balance recognizing children's previous experiences with helping them ⓓ<u>to adjust</u> to their new environment. Enabling children to share their backgrounds in a manner that honors their history as crucial parts of their identity significantly ⓔ<u>contribute</u> to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those going through transitions.
questions.explanation: 문장 ⓔ가 포함된 부분의 주어는 'Enabling children to share their backgrounds ~ identity'로, 동명사구(Enabling ~)가 주어 역할을 하고 있습니다. 동명사구 주어는 항상 단수 취급하므로, 동사 contribute를 단수형인 contributes로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.ⓐ change: 복수 주어 surroundings에 대한 현재 시제 동사로 적절합니다.ⓑ what: imagine의 목적어 절을 이끌며, like 뒤에 명사 자리가 비어 있는 불완전한 문장이므로 의문대명사 what이 적절합니다.ⓒ facing: '이사에 직면한 아이들'이라는 의미로 앞의 명사 young children을 수식하는 현재분사로 적절합니다.ⓓ to adjust: 동사 help는 목적격 보어로 동사원형이나 to부정사를 모두 취할 수 있으므로 to adjust는 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field ⓐ<u>is forced</u> to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by ⓑ<u>adding</u> nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have let farmers ⓒ<u>to become</u> much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizers has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation for farm fields ⓓ<u>has</u> almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land ⓔ<u>which</u> surrounds them they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.explanation: ⓒ 'let farmers to become'에서 'let'은 사역동사이므로 목적격 보어로 동사원형을 취해야 합니다. 따라서 'to become'을 'become'으로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① The brain is reshaped when focused attention occurs.
② The auditory centers can be expanded in the brain of the animal which is insensitive to sound.
③ Violinists' left hands fingering strings fast are the evidence of the enlarged areas of the related cortex.
④ Taxi drivers have the larger hippocampus as it is crucial for the spatial memory.
⑤ The physical architecture of the brain is determined based on where we pay attention to.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 소리를 알아채는 것(noticing sound)에 대해 보상을 받는 동물들의 뇌에서 청각 중심부가 훨씬 더 크다고 언급하고 있으므로, 소리에 무감각한(insensitive) 동물의 청각 중심부가 확장될 수 있다는 2번 설명은 지문의 내용과 정반대입니다.
options_translation: ① 집중된 주의가 일어날 때 뇌는 재형성된다.
② 소리에 무감각한 동물의 뇌에서 청각 중심부가 확장될 수 있다.
③ 줄을 빠르게 짚는 바이올리니스트의 왼손은 관련된 피질 영역이 확대된 증거이다.
④ 택시 기사들은 공간 기억에 중요하기 때문에 더 큰 해마를 가지고 있다.
⑤ 뇌의 물리적 구조는 우리가 어디에 주의를 기울이는지에 따라 결정된다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species with the <u>ⓐshortest</u> childhood, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born ⓑ<u>knowing</u> how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying ⓒ<u>efficiently</u> by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates cultural information to be ⓓ<u>descended</u>, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives ⓔ<u>flexibility</u> in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 태어날 때부터 이주 방법을 알고 태어난(어린 시절이 짧은) 새들은 환경 변화에도 불구하고 옛 규칙과 지도를 따라 계속 날아간다고 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 비효율적인 행동이므로 ⓒ의 'efficiently'(효율적으로)를 'inefficiently'(비효율적으로)와 같은 단어로 바꾸어야 흐름상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How can employees improve their productivity? Simply __________________________________. They can feel they are in control with the genuine decision-making authority so that they radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ① raise their salary in advance
② empower them with a sense of agency
③ force them to follow the shift schedules
④ let them work longer than they expected
⑤ improve their work environment and welfare
questions.explanation: 지문의 내용은 직원들에게 스스로 결정할 수 있는 권한과 통제력을 부여했을 때 생산성이 향상되었다는 실험 결과를 보여주고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '그들에게 주체 의식(통제권)을 부여하는 것'이라는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 미리 그들의 급여를 인상하라
② 그들에게 주체 의식(권한)을 부여하라
③ 그들이 교대 근무 일정을 따르도록 강요하라
④ 그들이 예상했던 것보다 더 오래 일하게 하라
⑤ 그들의 작업 환경과 복지를 개선하라

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life, though these skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. ⓐHighly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. ⓑThey win through mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. ⓒMentally healthy people don't have to try as hard as physically healthy ones to move forward. ⓓStrength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. ⓔHardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us and it will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
questions.explanation: 전체 글의 흐름은 쉬운 길을 택하기보다 고난과 고군분투를 통해 힘과 실력을 길러야 성공하고 숙련될 수 있다는 내용입니다. 하지만 ③번(ⓒ) 문장은 정신적으로 건강한 사람과 신체적으로 건강한 사람의 노력 정도를 비교하는 내용으로 주제와 무관합니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved.
ordered_passages: (A) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two.

(B) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.

(C) In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 수렵 채집인들이 이동할 때 모든 소지품을 운반해야 했다는 내용이 나옵니다. (C)에서 특히 어머니들이 아이를 업고 가야 했기 때문에 출산 간격이 4년 정도로 길 수밖에 없었다는 구체적인 제약 사항이 이어집니다. 그 후 (A)에서 '반면에(on the other hand)'를 통해 농경 사회는 정착 생활로 인해 아이들을 장거리 이동시킬 걱정이 없어 출산 간격이 짧아졌음을 대조합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 짧아진 출산 간격이 인구 증가와 농경 사회의 노동력 확보로 이어졌다는 결론으로 마무리되는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 언급된 'Brainwriting'의 세 단계를 우리말로 서술하시오.
questions.passage: To overcome the common problems of brainstorming, many teams have switched to a process called "brainwriting." This method helps unlock creativity and gives everyone a voice. In brainwriting, there are three main steps. First, (1) ask everyone to generate ideas individually. This allows people to think deeply without being influenced by others. Second, (2) collect those ideas and share them with the group anonymously. This ensures that ideas are judged on their own merit, not on who came up with them. Finally, (3) get the team together to select and refine the most promising options. This collaborative final step helps the group reach a consensus on the best way forward.
subjective_conditions: 우리말로 서술하시오.
questions.answer: (1) 모든 사람에게 개별적으로 아이디어를 내도록 요청한다.(2) 아이디어를 모아 익명으로 그룹에 공유한다.(3) 팀이 함께 모여 가장 유망한 옵션을 선택하고 다듬는다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 설명하는 Brainwriting의 3단계를 순서대로 한국어로 번역하여 서술하는 문제입니다. (1) First 단계: individual idea generation, (2) Second 단계: collection and anonymous sharing, (3) Finally 단계: team selection and refinement를 정확히 기술해야 합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under (A)[pressure / aggression]. The grey had the (B)[edge / damage] because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to (C)[distinction / extinction] in England.
questions.explanation:
(A) 동일한 먹이와 서식지를 두고 경쟁하므로 토착 다람쥐는 압박을 받게 됩니다. 따라서 'pressure(압박)'가 적절합니다.
(B) 회색 다람쥐가 다양한 식습성을 통해 경쟁에서 우위를 점하므로 'edge(우위)'가 적절합니다.
(C) 토착 다람쥐가 먹이를 뺏기고 서식지를 잃어 멸종 위기에 처하므로 'extinction(멸종)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 압박 - 우위 - 멸종
② 공격 - 우위 - 멸종
③ 압박 - 우위 - 차이
④ 공격 - 피해 - 차이
⑤ 압박 - 피해 - 차이

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions _____________________________________. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
options: ② have drawn agrarian unfavorable things
③ have made farmers richer than ever before
④ have also attracted many people to start farming
⑤ have caused a shortage of fertilizer in the market
questions.explanation: 지문 후반부에서 농경지가 주변 자연 땅에 비해 영양분과 물이 풍부하기 때문에 온갖 잡초들이 탐내는 '호화 부동산'이 된다고 설명하고 있습니다. 즉, 비료와 관개로 만든 좋은 조건이 오히려 농사에 불리한 요소(잡초)들을 끌어들인다는 내용이 빈칸에 적절합니다.

questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. questions.explanation: 농경지는 비료와 관개 시설을 통해 영양분과 물이 풍부하게 공급되는 '호화로운 조건'을 갖추게 됩니다. 이러한 환경은 주변의 자연 지역보다 자원이 풍부하기 때문에 잡초들에게는 매우 매력적인 서식지, 즉 '최적의 영토(a prime territory)'로 여겨진다는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 척박한 오아시스
② 최적의 영토
③ 경제적 자산
④ 천연 자원
⑤ 차선의 에너지원

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities.
ordered_passages: (A) This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of people with disabilities as well as those without.

(B) As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors.

(C) While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account.
questions.explanation: 디지털 정보 구축에서 장애인의 필요가 무시되어 왔다는 문제 제기 이후, (C)에서 교육 기술이나 상업적 웹 디자인 분야의 발전과 대조적으로 일부 학술 프로젝트가 이를 간과하고 있다는 현실을 구체화합니다. (B)에서는 그 결과(As a result)로 다양한 장애를 가진 사람들이 디지털 자원을 이용하지 못하게 된다는 실질적인 문제점을 열거합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서는 디자인 결정 시 가능한 가장 넓은 대상을 고려해야 한다는 해결책이자 지향점을 제시하며 끝맺는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.summary_sentence: Many animals and humans prefer (A)___________ rewards, but often fail to resist (B)___________ and spend savings prematurely.
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간과 동물이 미래 소비를 위해 저축을 하며 이는 '지연된 보상(delayed reward)'에 대한 선호를 나타내지만, 종종 의지력이 약해져서 즉각적인 즐거움의 '유혹(temptation)'에 굴복하여 저축을 일찍 써버린다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 delayed, (B)에는 temptation이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 현재의 - 조바심
② 지연된 - 만족
③ 지연된 - 유혹
④ 즉각적인 - 주의 산만
⑤ 즉각적인 - 욕구

questions.question: [2~3] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.2. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, <u>모든 문서가 종이 기반이었기 때문에 사무실에서는 훨씬 더 많은 종이 낭비가 있곤 했었다</u>. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data enters' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① Fossil fuels are the main energy source for data centers.
② The environmental cost of emails is surprisingly high.
③ Carbon emissions from cloud storage are increasing.
④ Paper documents were harmful to the environment.
⑤ Digital activities can still harm the environment.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 비즈니스가 디지털로 전환되면서 환경에 긍정적인 영향(종이 절약 등)을 줄 것으로 예상되지만, 실제로는 데이터 센터 운영을 위한 화석 연료 사용, 탄소 배출 증가 등 디지털 활동이 여전히 환경에 위협이 될 수 있다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 '디지털 활동도 여전히 환경에 해를 끼칠 수 있다'는 내용의 5번입니다.
options_translation: ① 화석 연료는 데이터 센터의 주요 에너지원이다.
② 이메일의 환경적 비용은 놀라울 정도로 높다.
③ 클라우드 저장소로부터의 탄소 배출이 증가하고 있다.
④ 종이 문서는 환경에 해로웠다.
⑤ 디지털 활동은 여전히 환경에 해를 끼칠 수 있다.

questions.question: [2~3] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.3. 윗글의 밑줄 친 의미가 되도록 아래 단어를 변형 없이 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 서술하시오.
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, <u>모든 문서가 종이 기반이었기 때문에 사무실에서는 훨씬 더 많은 종이 낭비가 있곤 했었다</u>. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data enters' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
questions.answer: used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based
questions.explanation: 주어진 한국어 문장 '사무실에서는 훨씬 더 많은 종이 낭비가 있곤 했었다(과거의 습관/상태 used to)'와 '모든 문서가 종이 기반이었기 때문에(접속사 since)'를 영작하는 문제입니다. 'Offices'를 주어로 시작하여 '사무실은 ~하곤 했다(used to have)', '훨씬 더 많은 종이 낭비(much more paper waste)', '~이기 때문에(since)', '모든 문서가 종이 기반이었다(all documents were paper based)' 순으로 배열하면 됩니다.

questions.question: 5. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors reflect your identity, indicating the type of person you believe you are, either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief.
ordered_passages: (A) Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy.
(B) After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
(C) For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed 'voting" was an action they wanted to perform.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 정체성이 행동에 영향을 미친다는 일반적인 원리를 설명합니다. (C)에서 'For example'을 통해 투표자의 사례를 들어 구체화합니다. (A)에서 'Similarly'를 사용하여 운동을 정체성으로 받아들인 사람의 또 다른 사례를 추가합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 'After all'을 통해 행동과 정체성이 일치할 때의 결론을 맺는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you need to do is ______________________. If you notice someone who is lonely, you could go and sit with them. If you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. A person's happiness comes from attention. There are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. Even if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
options: ① go and express your concern
② conduct marketing via social media
③ assist those who suffer from diseases
④ exchange ideas with your closest friends
⑤ have relationships with people only online
questions.explanation: 지문 전체는 타인을 돕는 것이 거창한 일이 아니라, 외로운 사람 곁에 앉아주거나 혼자 밥 먹는 동료와 함께하는 것, 지나가는 사람에게 인사하는 것과 같이 '관심(attention)'을 보여주는 것임을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말은 관심을 표현하라는 내용인 1번입니다.
options_translation: ① 가서 당신의 관심을 표현하는 것
② 소셜 미디어를 통해 마케팅을 수행하는 것
③ 질병으로 고통받는 사람들을 돕는 것
④ 당신의 가장 가까운 친구들과 아이디어를 교환하는 것
⑤ 온라인상으로만 사람들과 관계를 맺는 것

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less ⓐthreatening. However, digital business activities can still harm the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more ⓑhazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a ⓒdesirable step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds ⓓ<u>eco-friendly</u>. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is ⓔ<u>big</u>.
questions.explanation: 데이터 센터의 에너지원이 화석 연료이고 데이터 저장량이 늘어남에 따라 탄소 배출량이 증가한다는 내용이므로, 클라우드를 '친환경적(eco-friendly)'으로 만든다는 표현은 문맥상 어색합니다. 탄소 배출 증가는 환경에 해로운 영향을 미치기 때문입니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
options: ① How to Become Digitally Literate
④ Making Digital Information Accessible for Everyone
⑤ The Value of Authentic Content Creation for Viewers
questions.explanation: 이 글은 디지털 정보를 구축할 때 장애를 가진 사람들의 필요가 간과되어 왔음을 지적하며, 장애 유무와 상관없이 가능한 모든 사람이 이용할 수 있도록 디자인해야 한다는 주장을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '모든 사람을 위해 디지털 정보에 접근 가능하게 만들기'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 디지털 문해력을 갖추는 방법
② 장애인을 위한 교육
③ 교육 분야의 기술적 발전
④ 모든 사람을 위해 디지털 정보에 접근 가능하게 만들기
⑤ 시청자를 위한 진정성 있는 콘텐츠 제작의 가치

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (A) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. (B) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. (C) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (D) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure arises. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.
questions.explanation: 지문의 전반부는 미래의 보상을 위해 저축하는 일반적인 선호도를 설명합니다. 하지만 주어진 문장은 'However'를 사용하여 일부 사례에서는 저축한 돈을 조기에 써버린다는 대조적인 내용을 도입합니다. (B) 뒤의 문장에서 이에 대한 구체적인 예시(크리스마스 선물용 돈을 여름 휴가에 씀)가 나오므로 (B) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment: they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
questions.summary_sentence: Success comes from facing and overcoming (A)___________ because strength and skills needed for success are gained through confronting (B)___________ and preparing thoroughly rather than taking the easy route.
questions.explanation: 지문은 쉬운 길을 택하기보다 어려움(hardship)과 고군분투(struggle)를 통해 실력과 힘을 길러야 성공할 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 요약문의 (A)에는 '어려움(difficulties)', (B)에는 '고난(hardship)'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 번영 / 고통
② 저항 / 장비
③ 어려움 / 고난
④ 도전 / 습관
⑤ 경쟁 / 기술

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 문맥과 <조건>에 맞게 주어진 어휘를 바르게 배열하여 빈칸을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The key idea is that the physical structure ____________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 다음에 각각 제시된 단어(구)만을 빠짐없이 모두 사용할 것
필요한 경우 문맥과 어법에 맞게 고칠 것 (중복 사용 불가)
작성한 답안이 총 16단어인지 확인할 것
vocabulary_box: and / where / what / vary / our attention / depending on / we focus / of the brain / we practice doing
questions.subjective_answer_format: The key idea is that the physical structure ____________________________________.
questions.answer: of the brain varies depending on where we focus our attention and what we practice doing
questions.explanation: 주어 'the physical structure'를 수식하는 'of the brain'을 먼저 배치하고, 동사 'vary'를 주어의 수에 맞춰 'varies'로 변형합니다. '~에 따라'라는 의미의 'depending on' 뒤에 두 개의 간접의문문 'where we focus our attention'과 'what we practice doing'을 'and'로 연결하여 배열합니다. 전체 단어 수는 16단어가 됩니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오. [3.5점]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.summary_sentence: Farming (A)<u>possible / it / to / for / people / settle down / made</u> in one place, contributing to (B)_________________ which was a benefit to agricultural societies.
subjective_conditions: (A)는 제시된 모든 단어(구)만을 배열하여 완성하되, 형태를 변형하지 말 것 (총 8단어로 작성할 것)
(B)는 본문에 나와 있는 3단어로 연결된 어휘를 찾아서 그대로 쓸 것
vocabulary_box: possible / it / to / for / people / settle down / made
questions.answer: (A) made it possible for people to settle down(B) rapid population growth
questions.explanation: 지문은 농경의 시작이 정착 생활을 가능하게 했고, 이는 출산 간격을 줄여 급격한 인구 증가를 가져왔으며 이것이 노동력이 많이 필요한 농경 사회에 이득이 되었다는 내용입니다. (A)는 5형식 구문(주어+made+가목적어 it+목적격보어 possible+의미상주어 for people+진목적어 to settle down)을 사용하여 문장을 완성하고, (B)는 본문 마지막 부분에서 인구 증가를 나타내는 'rapid population growth'를 찾아 기입합니다.

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his hands.
ordered_passages: (A) Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions.

(B) If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him.
(C) The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 인카 제국의 전령들에 대해 서술하고 있습니다. (A)에서는 관스키라고 불리는 그들의 거주 형태와 특징을 서개하고, (B)에서는 그들이 다음 전령에게 메시지를 전달하는 구체적인 방박을 묘사합니다. 마지막 (C)에서는 이러한 시스템을 통해 얻은 결과(며칠 만에 멀리까지 전달 가능)를 언급하며 마무리하는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other, therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ① mystery of animals and what it means to us
② various factors must be considered when treating animals
③ treating animals for healing purpose can be difficult but worthwhile
④ some cautions that are needed to be taken when looking after an animal
⑤ environmental factors can have more impact on an animal than genetics when healing
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물마다 특성이 다르고 환경적 요인, 질병의 정리 등에 따라 츘료 밑 츘유 방식에 대한 반응이 다르므로, 각 동물의 구체적인 필요에 맞게 츘료가 조절되어야 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ② ' 동물을 츘료하는 때 다양한 요인들이 고려되어야 한다' 가 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① ␖ 동물의 신비와 그것이 우리에게 갖는 의미
② ␗ 동물을 츘료할 때 다양한 요인들이 고려되어야 한다
③ ␘ 츘유 목적으로 동물을 츘료하는 것은 어렵지만 가츘 있는 일이다
④ ␙ 동물을 돌볼 때 취해야 할 먐먐 주의사항들
⑤ ␔ 츘유 시 환경적 요인이 유전적 요인바다 동물에게 더 큰 영향을 미칠 수 있뉄

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 표현만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was ⓐ<u>mapped</u> into separate areas ⓑ<u>in which</u> certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated ⓒ<u>what</u> the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research ⓓ<u>being conducted</u> in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may ⓔ<u>perceive</u> at a litter different ⓕ<u>intensities</u> at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather it's ⓖ<u>that you register that perception first</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓒ what -> that: demonstrated의 목적어절을 이끄는 접속사이며, 뒤 문장이 완전하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 와야 합니다. ⓓ being conducted -> conducted: '연구'를 수식하는 분사구인데, 진행의 의미를 강조하는 being conducted보다는 이미 수행된 연구라는 의미의 과거분사 conducted가 더 자연스럽지만, 문법적으로 불가한 것은 아닙니다. 다만 정답 선지를 고려할 때 ⓔ가 명백히 틀렸으므로 포함된 것으로 보입니다. ⓔ perceive -> be perceived: 주어 they가 가리키는 것은 '맛(tastes)'입니다. 맛은 지각되는 대상이므로 수동태인 be perceived가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because-fueled by emotions-you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
options: ① How do we come to fear something?
② What parts are there in a human mind?
③ What role does conscious mind have on us?
④ What function does subconscious mind serve?
⑤ Which one is more superior: conscious mind or the subconscious mind?
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 의식과 잠재의식의 구성(②), 잠재의식의 기능(④), 의식의 역할(③), 그리고 공포가 형성되는 과정(①)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 두 마음의 영역 중 어느 것이 더 우월한지에 대한 비교나 평가는 언급되지 않았으므로 5번은 답할 수 없습니다.
options_translation: ① 우리는 어떻게 무언가를 두려워하게 되는가?
② 인간의 마음에는 어떤 부분들이 있는가?
③ 의식이 우리에게 어떤 역할을 하는가?
④ 잠재의식은 어떤 기능을 수행하는가?
⑤ 의식과 잠재의식 중 어느 것이 더 우월한가?

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 우리말을 영작하시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: <u>규범은 무엇이 "정상적"인지를 규정하고 모든 순간 사회적 생활에 대한 우리의 해석을 안내해 주며 어디에나 존재한다</u>. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
subjective_conditions: 분사구문을 사용할 것
변형 가능, 추가 가능
questions.answer: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn.
questions.explanation: 주어진 우리말은 규범의 특징을 나열하고 있습니다. 'Norms are everywhere'를 주절로 삼고, '규정하고', '안내해 주며'라는 동사 부분을 분사구문인 'defining'과 'guiding'으로 변형하여 영작합니다. 'interpret'는 명사형인 'interpretations'로 변형하여 'interpretations of social life'로 구성하고 'every turn' 앞에 전치사 'at'을 사용합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
options: ① The Secret to Raising a Genius
② Why Preschoolers are Naturally Confident
③ How Praise Can Make Your Child Dependent
④ Benefits and Drawbacks of Praising Your Child
⑤ The Power of Praise in Preschool Development

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)의 어법상 혹은 문맥상 쓰임이 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, which then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly. As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you." If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler has been transmitted via our body. (A)___________ as it may sound, this theory states that emotions arise from our bodies. For example, our mood can be improved by simply lifting up the corners of our mouth. If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, taking care not to let the pencil touch their lips (thus forcing the mouth into a smilelike shape), they judge cartoons (B)___________ than if they have been asked to frown. The primacy of the (C)___________ is sometimes summarized in the phrase "I must be afraid, because I'm running."
questions.explanation:
(A) 양보의 의미를 나타내는 접속사 as가 형용사를 강조하기 위해 Strange(형용사)를 문두로 보낸 도치 구문이므로 Strange가 적절합니다. (Strange as it may sound = Though it may sound strange)
(B) 입가에 미소 모양을 강제로 만드는 것이 기분을 좋아지게 하므로, 만화를 더 재미있다고(funnier) 판단하게 됩니다.
(C) 몸(신체)이 먼저 반응하고 그 다음에 감정이 생긴다는 '신체의 우위성'에 대한 내용이므로 신체(body)가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이상한 — 더 재미있는 — 신체
② 이상한 — 더 심각한 — 감정
③ 이상한 — 더 재미있는 — 감정
④ 이상하게 — 더 심각한 — 신체
⑤ 이상하게 — 더 재미있는 — 감정

questions.question: 8. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. ⓐFor example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fairminded, less biased, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. ⓑSurprisingly, people often underestimate their ability to remember names accurately. ⓒThis phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." ⓓA survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. ⓔIn terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 자신의 긍정적인 특성을 평균 이상으로 과대평가하는 경향인 '레이크 워비건 효과'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ②번은 이름을 정확하게 기억하는 능력을 과소평가한다는 내용으로, 전체 흐름인 '자기 능력을 과대평가한다'는 주제와 반대되거나 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 Stress에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is time pressure. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life ─ which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel timepoor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
options: ① Richer countries have their own apparent sources of stress.
② A higher standard of living can be accompanied by a constant sense of urgency.
③ Poverty is the only major factor that contributes to high levels of stress hormones.
④ Wealthy, more industrialized nations are likely to experience a fast-paced life.
⑤ People can feel time-poor despite the wealth they've earned through fast productivity.
questions.explanation: 지문은 가난이 스트레스를 유발한다는 점을 언급하면서도, 부유한 국가들 또한 '시간 압박(time pressure)'이라는 고유한 스트레스를 가지고 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 가난이 스트레스 호르몬 수치를 높이는 유일한 요인이라는 ③번은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 더 부유한 국가들은 그들만의 분명한 스트레스 원인을 가지고 있다.
② 더 높은 생활 수준은 끊임없는 긴박감과 동반될 수 있다.
③ 가난은 높은 수준의 스트레스 호르몬에 기여하는 유일한 주요 요인이다.
④ 부유하고 더 산업화된 국가들은 빠른 속도의 삶을 경험할 가능성이 높다.
⑤ 사람들은 빠른 생산성을 통해 얻은 부에도 불구하고 시간이 부족하다고 느낄 수 있다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped increase sales.
options: ① Advertiser's Ability to Adapt a Product to its Context
② The Efficacy of a Changing Product with the Times and the Need to Improve it
③ The Importance of Hiring Advertising Agencies and Scarcity of Investment Value
④ Outstanding Efficacy of Home-made Bread in Contrast to Corporate-made Bread
⑤ The Role of a Chief Executive Who Plays a Very Decisive Role in the Fate of a Company

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 6월 32번]
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. (A) And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. (B) Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. (C) In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. (D) Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. (E) There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
questions.insertion_sentence: Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements ─ from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 경제가 상점, 은행, 상인, 고객 등 모든 요소의 상호작용에서 발생한다는 내용입니다. 지문 전반부에서 경제가 어디에 위치하는지 묻는 질문에 대한 답이 없다고 언급한 뒤, (A) 앞부분에서 그 대안적 설명(상호작용의 산물)이 나오고, (A) 뒤에서 '뇌의 작동 방식도 그러하다'며 뇌와 도시 경제의 유사성을 설명하기 시작하므로 (A) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은? [23년 6월 34번]
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy ⓐ<u>boost</u> sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He demanded that a famous supermarket in Sioux City, Iowa, ⓑ<u>offer</u> Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, ⓒ<u>which</u> there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the ⓓ<u>scarcely</u> condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, ⓔ<u>nor was</u> it happen in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
questions.explanation: ⓐ는 동명사 구(Restricting ~)가 주어이므로 단수 동사인 boosts가 되어야 합니다. ⓑ는 demand(요구하다)라는 동사 뒤의 that절에서 당위성을 나타내므로 '(should) offer'의 형태인 동사원형 offer가 오는 것이 적절합니다. ⓒ는 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오므로 관계부사 where나 in which가 적절합니다. ⓓ는 명사 condition을 수식하므로 형용사형인 scarce가 되어야 합니다. ⓔ는 부정어 도치 구문이지만 일반 동사 happen의 의문문/도치 형태이므로 nor did it happen이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 연구의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. <조건>에 맞게 문장을 완성하시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more.
questions.summary_sentence: (A)_________________________________ of a guest lecturer as either 'warm' or 'cold', university students formed significantly different impressions of him, (B)______________________________________ that developed.
subjective_conditions: 1. 분사구문으로 문장을 연결할 것
2. 관계대명사를 활용할 것
questions.answer: (A) Having received (or Having been given) a description (B) which affects their relation(s) and interaction(s) with him
questions.explanation: 지문은 사전에 주어진 정보(따뜻함 vs 차가움)가 사람의 인상 형성과 상호작용에 큰 영향을 미친다는 내용이다. (A)는 '설명을 들은 후에'라는 의미를 나타내기 위해 완료 분사구문(Having received/been given)을 사용하고, (B)는 형성된 인상이 이후의 관계에 영향을 미친다는 것을 설명하기 위해 주격 관계대명사(which)를 활용하여 완성한다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is the thing ⓐ<u>which</u> we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down ⓑ<u>what</u> you face and deal with now. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me ⓒ<u>give</u> you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, ⓓ<u>getting</u> ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in ⓔ<u>how</u> you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장은 접속사 Once가 이끄는 부사절 뒤에 오는 주절입니다. 문장에 본동사가 없으므로 현재분사 getting이 아닌 명령문 형태인 동사원형 Get으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents ⓐ<u>disagreeing</u> viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, ⓑ<u>published</u> weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about ⓒ<u>its</u> management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us ⓓ<u>to listen</u> to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something ⓔ<u>done</u>."
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 지칭하는 대상은 복수 명사인 'the featured leaders'입니다. 따라서 단수 소유격인 its가 아니라 복수 소유격인 their로 써야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. (B) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. (C) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (D) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. (E) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.insertion_sentence: But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'it'은 앞 문장의 'Perceptual disengagement(지각적 이탈)'를 가리킵니다. (D) 문장에서 일부 학자들은 지각적 이탈을 수면의 정의에 포함하지 않는다고 언급했습니다. 하지만 주어진 문장에서 '그것(지각적 이탈) 없이는 수면이 불가능하므로 정의에 필수적이다'라고 반박하며 수면의 정의에 대한 논의를 마무리한 뒤, (E)에서 지각적 이탈이 완전하지 않은 '졸음' 상태에 대해 설명하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. (A) They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. (B) As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. (C) All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. (D) In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. (E) The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.insertion_sentence: Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children.
questions.explanation: (A)까지는 성인용 스포츠 환경이 아이들에게 부적합하다는 문제점을 지적하고 있습니다. 주어진 문장은 '상식이 우세해졌고, 여러 스포츠가 아이들을 위해 조정되었다'는 일반적인 해결책을 제시합니다. (B)부터는 야구(T ball), 축구(flag football) 등 구체적인 조정 사례가 시작되므로, 일반적 진술인 주어진 문장은 사례가 시작되기 직전인 (B) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, ________________________. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
options: ① carrots will be in the first and tomatoes in the third
② tomatoes will be in the second and carrots in the third
③ tomatoes will be in the first and green beans in the third
④ green beans will be in the first and carrots in the second
⑤ tomatoes will be in the second and green beans will in the third
questions.explanation: 이 글은 윤작(crop rotation)의 순환 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. - 1년차: 1번 밭(당근), 2번 밭(강낭콩), 3번 밭(토마토)- 2년차: 1번 밭(강낭콩), 2번 밭(토마토), 3번 밭(당근) [왼쪽으로 한 칸씩 이동]- 3년차: 1번 밭(토마토), 2번 밭(당근), 3번 밭(강낭콩)원문상의 논리적 순환에 따르면 3년차에는 토마토가 1번, 당근이 2번, 강낭콩이 3번 밭에 있어야 합니다. 보기 ③번이 이와 일치하나, 제공된 정답 ⑤번은 '토마토가 2번 밭에, 강낭콩이 3번 밭에 있을 것'이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 문제 자체의 설정이나 보기의 구성에 오류가 있을 수 있으나, 정답으로 제시된 ⑤번을 기준으로 보면 3년차의 배치를 묻는 질문에 대해 가능한 응답을 고르는 문제입니다.
options_translation: ① 당근은 첫 번째 들판에, 토마토는 세 번째 들판에 있을 것이다
② 토마토는 두 번째 들판에, 당근은 세 번째 들판에 있을 것이다
③ 토마토는 첫 번째 들판에, 강낭콩은 세 번째 들판에 있을 것이다
④ 강낭콩은 첫 번째 들판에, 당근은 두 번째 들판에 있을 것이다
⑤ 토마토는 두 번째 들판에, 강낭콩은 세 번째 들판에 있을 것이다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of ⓐ<u>accomplishment</u> and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and ⓑ<u>pleasant</u>, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and ⓒ<u>terrific</u> results, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be more ⓓ<u>depressed</u> with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took further ⓔ<u>satisfaction</u> from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 업무와 직업적 만족감이 개인의 행복과 성과에 긍정적인 영향을 미친다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 자신의 일에 가장 만족하는 사람들이 삶 전반에 대해 더 '우울해할(depressed)' 가능성이 높다는 ⓓ는 문맥상 정반대의 의미이므로 적절하지 않습니다. '행복할' 또는 '만족할'과 같은 긍정적인 단어가 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than ⓐ<u>novice</u> phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓑ<u>insensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓒ<u>overestimate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an ⓓ<u>earlier</u> session. Knowing that experts forget how ⓔ<u>hard</u> it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: '지식의 저주'는 전문가가 초보자에게 어떤 일이 얼마나 어려운지를 잊어버리는 현상입니다. 전문가가 될수록 그 기술이 얼마나 어려운지를 과소평가하게 되므로 ⓒ 'overestimate(과대평가하다)'는 'underestimate(과소평가하다)'로 바뀌어야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. ⓐAll creatures are capable of some degree of movement. ⓑEven creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. ⓒThe growth rate of all tree seeds and larvae depends on the environment. ⓓA creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. ⓔFrom fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 기후 변화에 따라 생물종이 이동하며 적응한다는 내용입니다. ③번 문장은 모든 나무의 씨앗과 유충의 성장 속도가 환경에 달려 있다는 내용으로, 생물종의 '이동과 분산'이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 주장에 대한 근거로 옳은 것만을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 모두 고른 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, <u>there are reasons to doubt it</u>. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
vocabulary_box: ⓐ Different animals possess different senses that are unique to their needs. Some examples include temperature sense, time sense, bonus-color vision, whisker sense, and electric-field sense. It can explain that animals possess more than the five basic senses.

ⓑ You can know which parts of your body are where without looking. It's how we can type without looking at the keyboard, for instance, or walk around without having to watch our feet. It is called "proprioception", which is difficult to describe with the five senses.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 'there are reasons to doubt it'은 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 5가지 감각 체계에 의문을 제기하는 내용입니다. <보기> ⓐ는 동물이 5가지 이상의 감각을 가지고 있다는 내용으로 본문의 뱀의 열 감지 능력 등과 일맥상통하며, ⓑ는 인간의 고유 수용성 감각(자기 몸의 위치 인지)에 대한 설명으로 본문에서 언급된 'the perception of your own body'를 뒷받침하는 근거가 됩니다. 따라서 둘 다 옳습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 30번]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① How Speed Affects Physical Health
② The Effect of Travel Speed on Detail Recognition
③ Comparing Travel Preferences in Different Speeds
④ The Efficient Way to Maintain Memories While Walking
⑤ The Relationship Between Speed and Cognitive Development
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하고 인식하는 능력에 큰 영향을 미친다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 인간의 감각은 걷는 속도에 최적화되어 있어, 속도가 빠른 운전자는 세부 사항을 인식하기 어렵고, 느린 보행자는 세부 사항을 더 잘 감상할 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ② '이동 속도가 세부 인식에 미치는 영향'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 속도가 신체 건강에 미치는 영향
② 이동 속도가 세부 사항 인식에 미치는 영향
③ 서로 다른 속도에서의 이동 선호도 비교
④ 걷는 동안 기억을 유지하는 효율적인 방법
⑤ 속도와 인지 발달 사이의 관계

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ① The Seeds of Leadership: What We All Have Within Us
② The Tremendous Potential for Minorities to Become Leaders
③ Sharing Ideas with Experts as a Key Factor in Becoming a Leader
④ The Journey of Leadership Through Important Individuals in History
⑤ What Are the Primary Challenges for Leaders in Improving Ideas?
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 지도자들도 처음에는 평범한 사람들로부터 시작했으며, 타인과 아이디어를 공유하고 피드백을 수용하는 과정을 통해 발전했음을 강조합니다. 결론적으로 나이나 경험에 상관없이 우리 모두는 학교, 지역 사회, 직장에서 리더가 될 잠재력을 가지고 있다는 내용이므로 ① '리더십의 씨앗: 우리 모두가 내면에 가지고 있는 것'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 리더십의 씨앗: 우리 모두가 내면에 가지고 있는 것
② 소수자가 리더가 될 수 있는 엄청난 잠재력
③ 리더가 되는 핵심 요소로서 전문가와 아이디어 공유하기
④ 역사의 중요한 인물들을 통한 리더십의 여정
⑤ 아이디어를 개선하는 데 있어 리더들의 주요 과제는 무엇인가?

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind.
ordered_passages: (A) The latter is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over.

(B) Let's imagine a situation related to this emotional decision-making. When your emotions cloud your judgment, it creates biases and various negative thoughts that hold you back. There are reasons for all of fears such as aranchnophobia or nyctophobia, but they originate in the conscious mind.

(C) To be specific, you can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 의식과 잠재의식을 소개합니다. (A)에서 'the latter'(잠재의식)의 특성을 먼저 설명한 뒤 의식에 대해 대조적으로 언급합니다. (C)에서는 의식에 대해 구체화하며(To be specific) 의식이 감정에 의해 잘못된 결정을 내리게 하는 과정을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 감정적 의사결정과 관련된 구체적 상황을 가정(Let's imagine)하여 부연 설명하므로 (A)-(C)-(B) 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으衜 표현하고자 할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <감건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.summary_sentence: Artists should _________________________________________ because overwork can spoil their impact.
subjective_conditions: • 하나의 문장으衜 작성할 것.
• 10단어 이상, 20단어 이하로 작성할 것.
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 한 번씩은 반드시 사용할 것.
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 변형하지 말 것.
• 가목적어와 진목적어를 사용할 것.
• to부정사의 형용사적 용박을 활용할 것.
questions.answer: make it a point to find the right moment to finish their works
questions.explanation: 글의 요지는 화가들이 과하게 작업하여 작품의 영향력을 망치지 않도록 적절한 마무리 시점을 찾눔 것이 중요하다는 것입니다. 제시된 점건에 따라 가목적어 'it'과 진목적어 to부정사 구문("make it a point to find~")을 사용하고, '마무리 할 시기'를 표현하기 위해 to부정사의 형용사적 용박("moment to finish")을 활용하여 영작합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 <보기>에서 찾아 <감건>에 맞게 싰시오.
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" (A)___________ of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research (B)___________ in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to (C)___________. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that (D)___________ first.
subjective_conditions: • 각 빈칸에 한 단어만 심 것.
• 단어의 형태를 문맥과 어법에 맞게 반드시 변형할 것.
• <보기>의 단어만을 선택해 한 번씩만 사용할 것.
questions.explanation: (A) 리사치에 따른 형용사적 수식이 필요하며 맞의 방식에 대한 '설먕'("tongue map" explanation)이라눔 명사형이 적절합니다.(B) 댅일에ᄉ서 '수행된' 연구(research conducted)라눔 과거분사 형태가 올바릅니다.(C) 맞 벼울이 '전문성'(특성) 따라 괸형되어 있지 않다눔 의미으衜 'speciality'가 적절합니다.(D) 맞을 '인지'(지각)한다눔 명사형 '인지(perception)'가 문맥사 잘 어울립니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength __________ from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심 주제는 '진정한 힘과 성공은 고난과 노력을 통해 얻어진다'는 것입니다. 빈칸이 포함된 문장은 '힘은 투쟁(struggle)으로부터 ______, 저항이 가장 적은 길을 택하는 것에서 오는 것이 아니다'라는 구조입니다. 문맥상 '나오다, 유래하다, 자라다'라는 의미가 들어가야 합니다. 원문은 'arises'이나, 제공된 정답 ④는 'suffers'로 되어 있어 논리적으로 상충됩니다. 하지만 지문 하단에 표기된 정답 번호를 따르자면 ④번입니다. (※ 실제 논리상으로는 ①, ②, ③, ⑤가 '발생하다/유래하다'의 유사 의미를 지닙니다.)
options_translation: ① 자라다
② 발생하다
③ 유래하다
④ 고통받다
⑤ 나타나다

questions.question: 9. 다음 밑줄 친 certain agricultural undesirables가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of <u>certain agricultural undesirables</u>. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area. Therefore, controlling weeds is significant for maintaining healthy and productive farm fields.
options: ② crops needing less fertilizer and water
③ fertilizer and water used in farm fields
④ unwanted plants like weeds in farm fields
⑤ surrounding natural land with a poor environment
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'certain agricultural undesirables(어떤 농업적으로 바람직하지 않은 것들)'은 뒤에 이어지는 문장에서 농장 주변의 '무작위적인 잡초(random weed)'들로 설명되고 있습니다. 비료와 물이 풍부한 최적의 환경을 잡초들도 선호하기 때문에 이들을 통제하는 것이 중요하다는 내용이므로, 정답은 '농장의 잡초와 같은 원치 않는 식물들'을 의미하는 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 영양분이 과도한 농작물
② 비료와 물이 덜 필요한 농작물
③ 농장에서 사용되는 비료와 물
④ 농장의 잡초와 같은 원치 않는 식물들
⑤ 환경이 좋지 않은 주변의 자연 토지

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용을 요약할 때, 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root.↓ Over many thousands of years, human society eventually shifted from being primarily based on hunting-gathering to primarily based on farming, but this was not a ___________ decision. The reason is that humans did not weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each and make a choice of one over the other.*remains: 유적 유해 *epidemic: 전염병의*be based on: ~에 기반을 두다*primarily: 주로 *weigh: 따져보다, 비교 검토하다
questions.summary_sentence: Over many thousands of years, human society eventually shifted from being primarily based on hunting-gathering to primarily based on farming, but this was not a ___________ decision. The reason is that humans did not weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each and make a choice of one over the other.
questions.explanation: 요약문 뒤의 이유를 설명하는 문장에서 '인간이 각 방식의 장단점을 따져보고(weigh) 선택을 내린 것이 아니다'라고 언급하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 '신중한' 또는 '의도적인' 결정을 의미하는 단어가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다. 따라서 4번 'careful(신중한)'이 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: 지속적인
결정적인
끊임없는
신중한
문화적인

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 35번]
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are (A)__________ control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts. Before the change, they had often taken long breaks and made many mistakes. Within two months, however, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking (B)__________ breaks and making (C)__________ complete products. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 통제권(sense of agency)을 주는 것이 업무 효율을 높인다는 내용입니다. (A)에서는 자신이 통제권을 가지고 있다는 의미인 'in' control이 적절합니다. (B) 변화 후 생산성이 높아졌으므로 쉬는 시간은 더 짧아졌을 것이기에 'shorter'가 적합합니다. (C) 생산성 향상은 더 많은 완성품을 의미하므로 'more'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① ~에 있는 / 더 짧은 / 더 적은
② ~에 있는 / 더 긴 / 더 많은
③ ~에 있는 / 더 짧은 / 더 많은
④ ~하에 있는 / 더 긴 / 더 적은
⑤ ~하에 있는 / 더 짧은 / 더 많은

questions.question: 12. 다음 밑줄 친 You and I are the descendants of the winners가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 33번]
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage.
