The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. <u>You and I are the descendants of the winners</u>.
options: ① We are unable to survive and reproduce outside of the active support by a social group.
② We are the offspring of tribes that possessed, the most lethal weapons, such as hunting knives.
③ We carry within our genes the same adaptive mechanisms that enabled our ancestors to be successful.
④ We have evolved by making efforts to change aspects of our external environment rather than adjusting our internal mindset.
⑤ We gain a survival advantage as we have bigger brains and become smarter, which allows us to make better tools and hunt better.
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 인간의 정신 능력이 타 부족과의 경쟁에서 승리하기 위한 도구로 진화해왔으며, 이러한 정신적 우위를 가진 부족이 살아남아 유전자를 물려주었다고 설명합니다. 따라서 '우리는 승리자의 후손이다'라는 말은 조상들을 성공하게 했던 그 적응 기제(정신적 이점)를 우리가 유전자 속에 가지고 있다는 의미인 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리는 사회 집단의 적극적인 지지 밖에서는 생존하고 번식할 수 없다.
② 우리는 사냥용 칼과 같은 가장 치명적인 무기를 소유했던 부족의 자손이다.
③ 우리는 조상들이 성공할 수 있게 해주었던 것과 똑같은 적응 기제를 유전자 속에 지니고 있다.
④ 우리는 내면의 마음가짐을 조정하기보다 외부 환경의 측면을 변화시키려는 노력을 통해 진화해 왔다.
⑤ 우리는 더 큰 뇌를 갖고 더 똑똑해짐에 따라 생존상의 이점을 얻으며, 이는 더 나은 도구를 만들고 더 잘 사냥하게 해준다.

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 (A) 뒤에 (B)가 이어진다고 할 때 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment. This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies ─ capsaicin ─ touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure.(B) We are likely to see the same in the case of marathons. Marathon runners experience breathless pain, but their physical safety is not threatened; in other words, they feel safe. If people did not experience any pain or suffering as part of running marathons, they would probably not get much enjoyment for them at all. The fact is that marathons are only rewarding because they are challenging, and they are only challenging because marathon runners have to suffer the pain it takes to run 40 kilometers. If we ___________ suffering from marathons, they would be neither challenging nor rewarding.*breathless: 숨이 막힐 듯한 *physical: 신체의, 육체의*threaten: 위협하다
questions.explanation: 이 글은 고통이 수반되는 활동(매운 음식, 마라톤 등)이 즐거움과 보상을 주는 이유가 그것이 도전적이기 때문이며, 그 도전은 고통을 견디는 데서 온다고 설명합니다. 따라서 마라톤에서 고통(suffering)을 제거한다면(remove), 그것은 더 이상 도전적이지도 보람차지도 않을 것이라는 문맥이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 허용하다
② 제거하다
③ 제공하다
④ 유발하다
⑤ 생성하다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger ⓐ<u>hearing</u> part centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp ⓑ<u>eyesight</u>, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to ⓒ<u>press</u> the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for space related memory, is ⓓ<u>enlarged</u> in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we ⓔ<u>lose</u> our attention and what we practice doing.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 집중된 주의(focused attention)가 뇌의 재구성을 이끈다는 것입니다. 마지막 문장에서 뇌의 물리적 구조가 변하는 기준은 주의를 '잃는(lose)' 곳이 아니라 주의를 '두는(place/focus)' 곳이어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 동물의 유년기에 관한 글을 읽고 유추할 수 있는 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
options: ① The innate abilities that some animals are born with can limit their adaptability.
② Animals' flexibility can never be developed during childhood or through parental guidance.
③ Animals can benefit from learning about their environment during their early life stages.
④ Cultural information among animals can adapt and change more rapidly than genetic information.
⑤ The adaptability provided by learning during childhood is valuable in a world that is constantly changing because of factors like climate change.
questions.explanation: 지문은 유년기(childhood)가 동물들에게 환경에 대해 배울 수 있는 시간을 제공하며, 이를 통해 변화하는 세상에서 유연성(flexibility)을 갖게 해준다고 설명합니다. 특히 부모와 함께 이동하며 긴 유년기를 보내는 새들이 가장 효율적인 경로를 갖는다고 언급합니다. 따라서 동물의 유연성이 유년기나 부모의 지도를 통해 결코 발달될 수 없다는 ②번 선지는 지문의 내용과 정반대이므로 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 일부 동물이 타고나는 선천적 능력은 그들의 적응력을 제한할 수 있다.
② 동물의 유연성은 유년기 동안이나 부모의 지도를 통해 결코 발달될 수 없다.
③ 동물은 생애 초기 단계 동안 환경에 대해 배움으로써 이득을 얻을 수 있다.
④ 동물들 사이의 문화적 정보는 유전적 정보보다 더 빠르게 적응하고 변할 수 있다.
⑤ 유년기 학습을 통해 제공되는 적응력은 기후 변화와 같은 요인들로 인해 끊임없이 변화하는 세상에서 가치가 있다.

questions.question: 27. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children.
ordered_passages: (A) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
(B) As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time.

(C) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 농경으로 인해 한곳에 머물게 되었으나, 이전의 수렵 채집인들은 이동해야 했고 특히 어머니들이 아이들을 업고 다녀야 했음을 설명합니다. (B)에서 그 결과로 수렵 채집인 어머니들은 아이를 업고 다니는 부담 때문에 4년에 한 번씩만 아이를 가질 수 있었다는 제약이 나옵니다. (C)에서 반면에('on the other hand') 농부들은 정착 생활 덕분에 아이 이동 걱정 없이 출산 간격을 2년으로 줄일 수 있었다는 대조적 내용이 이어집니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이것(출산 간격 단축)이 인구 증가로 이어졌고 노동력이 많이 필요한 농경 사회에 이점이 되었다는 결론으로 마무리되는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 괸의 밑줄 친 make our green clouds gray가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions <u>make our green clouds gray</u>. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① reinforce ecological initiatives through technological advancement
② reduce energy waste by maximizing the use of digital technologies in business
③ worsen the environmental impact by turning eco-friendly solutions into pollution contributors
④ offer the chance to address environmental problems by lowering corporate carbon footprints
⑤ degrade the cost of digital transitions to encourage more businesses to adopt cloud computing service
questions.explanation: 디지털 활동이 종이 사용을 줄여 환경에 도움이 될 것으로 기대했지만('green clouds'), 실제로는 데이터 센터 운영을 위한 화석 봐료 사용과 탄소 배출로 인해 환경을 오염시키고 있다는('gray') 의미이므로, 친환경적 해결책이 오염의 원인이 되어 환경 영향을 악화시키고 있다는 ③가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기술 발전을 통해 생태적 계획을 강화하다
② 비즈니스에서 디지털 기술 사용을 최대화하여 에너지 낭비를 줄이다
③ 친환경적 해결책을 오염 기여요인으로 바꿈으로엌 환경 영향을 악화시키다
④ 기업의 탄소 발자국을 줄임으로써 환경 문제를 해결할 기회를 제공하다
⑤ 더 많은 기업이 클라우드 컴퓨팅 서비숤를 채택하도록 독려하기 위해 디지털 전환 비용을 낮추다

questions.question: 3. 다음 괸의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brian. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① 인간 뇌의 발달 과정은 동물 뇌의 발달 과정과 차이가 있다.
② 뇌 스칈은 뇌의 재구조화에 대한 정확한 줝거들을 제시한다.
③ 왼섐을 사용하면 뇌의 피질 영역이 더 극적으로 성장한다.
④ 특정 눔력에 대한 바상은 전체적인 뇌 발달을 저해한다.
⑤ 주의 중점과 연습이 뇌의 묳리적 구조를 바화시킨다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장인 "The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing."이 이 괸의 핵심 요지입니다. 즉, 우리가 어떤 것에 주의를 기울이고 무엇을 연습하느냐에 따라 뇌의 묳리적 구조가 변한다는 내용이므로 ⑤가 정답입니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ② Ways to Resolve Vexing Problems
③ What is Essential to Be a Neutral Moderator
④ Brainwriting: The Way Everyone Gets a Fair Hearing
⑤ Brainstorming: The Facilitator for Independent Judges
questions.explanation: 이 글은 브레인스토밍 대신 브레인라이팅이라는 과정을 제안하고 있습니다. 브레인라이팅은 각 개인이 독립적으로 아이디어를 생성하고 평가한 후 그룹이 모여 결정하는 방식입니다. 이를 통해 모든 목소리가 대화에 포함되고 모든 아이디어가 공평하게 검토될 수 있음을 강조하므로 4번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 브레인라이팅이 역효과를 내는 방식
② 짜증스러운 문제를 해결하는 방법들
③ 중립적인 중재자가 되기 위해 필수적인 것
④ 브레인라이팅: 모두의 의견이 공평하게 들리는 방법
⑤ 브레인스토밍: 독립적인 판단자들을 위한 촉진제

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
options: ① 동물은 유년기를 보내면서 환경에 대해 학습한다.
② 이동 방법을 알고 태어난 새들은 새로운 이동 경로에 더 쉽게 적응할 수 있다.
③ 유년기가 가장 긴 새들은 가장 효율적인 이동 경로를 가지고 있는 경향이 있다.
④ 문화는 유전자보다 더 빠르게 진화할 수 있고, 유년기는 문화적 정보의 전달을 촉진한다.
⑤ 유년기는 변화하는 세상에서 유연성을 제공한다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 이동 방법을 알고 태어난 새들(born knowing how to migrate)은 유년기가 짧고 하드웨어에 의존하기 때문에 변화하는 환경에 쉽게 적응하지 못하고(don't adapt easily) 이전의 규칙과 지도를 고수한다고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 ②번은 지문의 내용과 정반대입니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and various animals often save resources or funds for future use, indicating a tendency to prefer long-term rewards over ⓐ<u>immediate</u> satisfaction. This preference suggests that the value perceived from future benefits ⓑ<u>surpasses</u> that of current rewards. Despite this, there are instances where individuals do not adhere to their original intentions and spend their savings ⓒ<u>later</u> than planned. For instance, an employee may initially save money for Christmas gifts but choose to use these funds for a summer holiday instead. Such behavior can be seen as a manifestation of ⓓ<u>weak</u> willpower. That is, individuals might plan to use their savings for the most significant future benefit, yet often change their course of action when the temptation of immediate pleasure ⓔ<u>arises</u>.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 원래 의도를 지키지 못하고 저축한 돈을 계획보다 '일찍' 써버리는 경우를 설명하고 있습니다. 크리스마스 선물을 위해 모은 돈을 그보다 이른 시기인 여름 휴가 때 사용한다는 예시가 뒤따르므로 'later(더 늦게)'가 아니라 'sooner(더 일찍)'가 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed ⓐ<u>recommendations</u> for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained ⓑ<u>disregarded</u> for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are ⓒ<u>pragmatic</u> for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in ⓓ<u>meeting</u> the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects ⓔ<u>adopted</u> the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.explanation: 장애인들의 필요가 무시되어 왔기 때문에, 가치 있는 디지털 자원들이 청각 장애인이나 시각 장애인들에게는 '실용적인(pragmatic)' 것이 아니라 '접근 불가능한(inaccessible)' 또는 '쓸모없는(useless)' 상태가 된다는 흐름이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 ⓒ pragmatic은 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. ________________________________ _______________ improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ③ Granting a feeling of control to workers
④ Providing workers with financial bonuses
⑤ Applying a sense of control via strict supervision
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 통제권과 의사 결정권을 주는 것(sense of agency)이 생산성을 높인다는 내용입니다. 오하이오 공장 실험 예시를 통해 작은 결정권을 부여받은 노동자들이 더 높은 자제력을 보였다고 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 '노동자들에게 통제감을 부여하는 것'이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 업무 프로세스 표준화하기
② 팀 빌딩 활동 실시하기
③ 노동자들에게 통제감을 부여하기
④ 노동자들에게 금전적 보너스 제공하기
⑤ 엄격한 감독을 통해 통제감 적용하기

questions.question: 23. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as -natural- to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. ①Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. ②The hunter-gatherer lifestyle became increasingly challenging due to natural climate changes, making it difficult to sustain their traditional way of life. ③If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. ④Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. ⑤This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled -civilizations.-
questions.explanation: 이 글은 수찵 채집 생활의 장점과 농경 및 정착 생활로의 이행 및 괴리에 대해 다루고 은 글입니다. ①에서는 수찵 채집이 퐒요하고 질병이 적었다고 설명하고 있을며, ③에서는 그렇다면 왜 힘든 농경을 선택했는지 의문을 제기합니다. 하지만 ②은 기홤 변화로 인해 수찵 채집 생활이 어려워죌섔 전통적 방식을 유지하기 힘들었다는 내용으로, 수찵 채집이 충분히 권장할 만하였다는 전체 맥락과 어색합니다.

questions.question: 25. 제시된 글 다음에 이어질 글의 수서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve?
ordered_passages: (A) One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage.

(B) And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.

(C) The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it.
questions.explanation: 인간의 정신 진화에 대한 질문 후 (A)에서 '한 가지 가능성'으로 타 부접과의 경읁을 제시합니다. (C)에서는 그 경읁에서 사고 닥력이 어떻게 광사적 이점을 준는지 구체적으로 설명하며 정신이 '무기'가 되었음을 말합니다. 맍지막으로 (B)에서 And this mental advantage림 통해 이러한 이점이 세대림 거쳐 전달되었음을 설명합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. (A) This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. (B) During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. (C) World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled. (D) We are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. (E) Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.insertion_sentence: Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장은 '불행히도, 이러한 사치스러운 조건들은 또한 특정한 농업적 바람직하지 않은 것들의 주의를 끌었다'는 내용입니다. (D)까지는 농지가 영양분과 물이 풍부한 완벽한 환경이 된 과정과 긍정적인 면을 설명하고 있습니다. (E) 다음 문장에서 농지가 주변 자연지에 비해 영양분과 물이 가득하여 '잡초'들에게 사치스러운 부동산으로 여겨진다는 구체적인 문제(agricultural undesirables)를 언급하므로, 제시문은 (E) 자리에 오는 것이 흐름상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
questions.summary_sentence: Due to the (A)_____________ of the invasive species to habitat and food, they can (B)_____________ the indigenous species, which leads to a decrease in the population of (C)_____________.
options: ① hierarchy - fall behind - the aboriginal
④ susceptibility - fall behind - the exotic
questions.explanation: 이 글은 외래종인 회색 다람쥐가 토착종인 붉은 다람쥐와의 경쟁에서 승리하여 붉은 다람쥐가 멸종 위기에 처하게 된 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. 회색 다람쥐가 먹이(익지 않은 도토리 섭취 가능)와 서식지에 대해 뛰어난 (A) 적응성(adaptability)을 가졌기 때문에 토착종을 (B) 경쟁에서 물리칠(outcompete) 수 있었고, 이는 결국 (C) 토착종(the native)의 개체 수 감소로 이어졌다는 요약이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 계급 - 뒤처지다 - 토착의
② 분산 - 능가하다 - 해외의
③ 적응성 - 경쟁에서 이기다 - 토착의
④ 민감성 - 뒤처지다 - 외래의
⑤ 취약성 - 경쟁에서 이기다 - 둘 다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You′ll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the good side and that they′re used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By __________, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
options: ① making fair compensation for ambassadors' contributions
② responding wisely to ambassadors' complaints after the sale
③ understanding strategies for television advertising campaigns
④ figuring out what designs customers prefer before they purchase
⑤ regularly keeping an eye on how much your customers are content with the purchase they made
questions.explanation: 이 글은 제품 판매 이후 고객이 자신의 구매에 대해 어떻게 반응하는지(post-purchase behavior)를 관찰하는 것이 왜 중요한지를 설명하고 있습니다. 만족한 고객은 무보수 홍보 대사가 되어 주변 지인들에게 긍정적인 영향을 미치지만, 그렇지 않을 경우 부정적인 입소문을 낼 수 있기 때문입니다. 따라서 판매 후에도 고객의 만족도를 정기적으로 모니터링함으로써 부정적인 평판을 방지할 수 있다는 ⑤번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 홍보 대사의 기여에 대해 공정한 보상을 제공하는 것
② 판매 후 홍보 대사의 불만에 현명하게 대응하는 것
③ 텔레비전 광고 캠페인 전략을 이해하는 것
④ 구매 전 고객이 선호하는 디자인을 파악하는 것
⑤ 고객이 자신의 구매에 얼마나 만족하는지 정기적으로 지켜보는 것

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. (A) Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. (B) To work on it, make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. (C) There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. (D) There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. (E) So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.insertion_sentence: Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 가용 시간에 과업을 맞추는 것에 주의림 기울이라고 합니다. (C) 들의 문장에서 상당한 시간이 있을 때만 시작할 수 있다는 과업 이얼기가 나오므로, 가용 시간과 과업을 맞추는 것의 구쳌적인 예시가 시작되는 (C) 윐치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing -- all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence ______________________________________________.
options: ① all the beauties in the world
② what we have never dreamed
③ the future as we have imagined it
④ a better way of managing products
⑤ the right way we have experimented
questions.explanation: 세상의 모든 것은 실제로 만들어지기 전에 마음셍에서 먼저 완성된다고 했으므로, 미래를 설계하는 과정도 이와 마찬가지로 우리가 상상한 대로의 미래를 실현시키는 과정입니다.
options_translation: ① 세상의 모든 아름다움
② 우리가 꼬꾸지 못했던 것
③ 우리가 상상해 온 대로의 미래
④ 제품을 관리하는 덄 나은 방법
⑤ 우리가 실험해 온 올바른 길

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' (A)_____________ to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as a sign of confidence because they suggest that the individual can afford the social costs of such (B)_____________.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 사회적 규범을 약간 어기는 사람들에 대해 어떻게 반응하는지를 다루고 있습니다. (A)에는 규범을 어긴 사람들에 대한 관찰자들의 '반응(responses/reactions)'이 들어가야 하며, (B)에는 그러한 '태도(attitudes)' 혹은 '행동(behaviors)'이 들어가야 합니다. 본문 맥락상 규범에서 벗어난 행동이 자신감의 신호로 해석되어 긍정적인 평가를 이끌어낸다는 내용이므로, 관찰자들의 '반응(responses)'과 그러한 독특한 '태도(attitudes)'를 의미하는 ②번이 가장 적절합니다. (다만 원문이나 일반적인 선지 구성상 behaviours도 가능하나, 제공된 정답 ②에 맞춰 responses-attitudes를 선택합니다.)
options_translation: ① 의존 - 행동
② 반응 - 태도
③ 반응 - 구매
④ 무지 - 예의
⑤ 무관심 - 의상

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks consist of crystals, the more you know about atoms, ⓐ<u>the better</u>. Crystals come in a variety of shapes ⓑ<u>what</u> scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways ⓒ<u>that</u> do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form the shapes that are strange and twisted. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment ⓓ<u>which</u> the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that ⓔ<u>are seen</u> time after time.
questions.explanation: 어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개입니다. ⓑ what -> which/that: 선행사 shapes가 있으므로 관계대명사 what은 올 수 없고, 목적격 관계대명사 which나 that이 필요합니다.ⓓ which -> in which/where: 뒤에 완전한 문장(the individual atoms have plenty of time...)이 오고 장소/환경의 의미를 나타내므로 관계부사 where나 전치사+관계대명사 in which가 적절합니다.ⓔ are seen -> is seen: 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 단수인 the basic structure of atoms이므로 수 일치에 따라 is seen이 되어야 합니다.(ⓐ 'the+비교급, the+비교급' 구문의 일부로 적절함, ⓒ 선행사 ways를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사로 적절함)
options_translation: ① 1개
② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개

questions.question: 25. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Claims that local food production cut greenhouse gas emissions by reducing the burning of transportation fuel are usually not well founded.
ordered_passages: (A) In the United Kingdom, lamb meat that travels 11,000 miles from New Zealand generates only one-quarter the carbon emissions per pound compared to British lamb because farmers in the United Kingdom raise their animals on feed (which must be produced using fossil fuels) rather than on clover pastureland. When food does travel, what matters most is not the distance traveled but the travel mode (surface versus air), and most of all the load size.

(B) Transport is the source of only 11 percent of greenhouse gas emissions within the food sector, so reducing the distance that food travels after it leaves the farm is far less important than reducing wasteful energy use on the farm. Food coming from a distance can actually be better for the climate, depending on how it was grown. For example, field-grown tomatoes shipped from Mexico in the winter months will have a smaller carbon footprint than local winter tomatoes grown in a greenhouse.

(C) Bulk loads of food can travel halfway around the world by ocean freight with a smaller carbon footprint, per pound delivered, than foods traveling just a short distance but in much smaller loads. For example, 18-wheelers carry much larger loads than pickup trucks so they can move food 100 times as far while burning only one-third as much gas per pound of food delivered.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 지역 식품 생산이 온실가스 배출을 줄인다는 주장이 근거가 부족하다는 점을 언급하며 글을 시작합니다.(B)는 이에 대한 일반적인 근거로, 식품 부문에서 운송이 차지하는 비중은 11%에 불과하며 생산 방식이 더 중요하다는 점을 설명하고, 장거리 운송 식품이 더 나을 수 있다는 예시(멕시코 토마토 vs 지역 온실 토마토)를 제시합니다.(A)는 (B)의 주장을 뒷받침하는 또 다른 구체적 사례로 뉴질랜드 양고기와 영국 양고기를 비교하며, 거리보다 생산 방식과 운송 수단이 중요함을 강조합니다.(C)는 (A)의 마지막 부분인 운송 방식(travel mode)과 적재량(load size)에 대한 상세 설명을 이어가며, 해상 대량 운송이나 대형 트럭이 소규모 운송보다 탄소 발자국이 적음을 설명하며 마무리합니다.따라서 가장 자연스러운 순서는 (B)-(A)-(C)입니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓗ 중, 가리키는 대상이 같은 것끼리 묶인 것은?
questions.passage: A nurse took a tired, anxious soldier to the bedside. -Jack, your son is here,- the nurse said to an old man lying on the bed. She had to repeat the words several times before the old man's eyes opened. Suffering from the severe pain because of heart disease, ①<u>he</u> barely saw the young uniformed soldier standing next to him. He reached out his hand to the soldier. The soldier gently wrapped his fingers around the weak hand of the old man. The nurse brought a chair so that the soldier could sit beside the bed. All through the night the young soldier sat there, holding the old man's hand and offering ②<u>him</u> words of support and comfort. Occasionally, she suggested that the soldier take a rest for a while. ③<u>He</u> politely said no. Whenever the nurse came into the room, she heard the soldier say a few gentle words. The old man said nothing, only held tightly to him all through the night. Just before dawn, the old man died. The soldier released the old man's hand and left the room to find the nurse. After she was told what happened, she went back to the room with ④<u>him</u>. The soldier hesitated for a while and asked, -Who was this man?- She was surprised and asked, -Wasn't ⑤<u>he</u> your father?- -No, he wasn't. I've never met ⑥<u>him</u> before,- the soldier replied. She asked, -Then why didn't you say something when I took you to him?- ⑦<u>He</u> said, -I knew there had been a mistake, but when I realized that ⑧<u>he</u> was too sick to tell whether or not I was his son, I could see how much he needed me. So, I stayed.-
questions.explanation: ① ①(old man), ②(old man), ⑤(old man)은 모두 침대에 누워있던 노인을 가리킵니다. 나머지를 살펴보면, ③(soldier), ④(soldier), ⑥(old man), ⑦(soldier), ⑧(old man)입니다. 따라서 노인을 가리키는 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓔ가 묶인 1번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation. If, for example, you step on a ①<u>sharp</u> object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. While the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a protective mechanism for the ②<u>brain</u>. Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech, so that you may well ③<u>shout</u> 'ouch' or something rather less polite. They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now contract quickly to ④<u>lift</u> your foot away from the painful object. Sensory and motor nerves ⑤<u>control</u> almost all functions in the body - from the beating of the heart to the movement of the gut, sweating and just about everything else.
questions.explanation: ②번 문맥상 통증은 신체(the body)를 보호하기 위한 메커니즘이지 뇌만을 보호하기 위한 것이 아닙니다. 핀에 찔렸을 때 통증을 느끼고 발을 떼는 행위는 전체적인 신체의 손상을 막기 위한 보호 기제입니다. 따라서 brain보다는 body가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글을 읽고 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 (A)와 (B)를 완성하시오. 필요한 단어를 추가하되 각각 4단어 이하로 완성하시오. (답안지에 바드시 과호 문자를 표시하세요.)
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer (A)_________________________ so that boundary crossings are minimized. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones - one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because (B)__________________ _____________ between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
subjective_conditions: <백기>에 주어진 단어를 모됐 사용할 감
필요한 단어를 추가하되 각각 4단어 이하로 완성할 감
questions.answer: (A) to separate roles, (B) they enable greater distinction
questions.explanation: (A)는 prefer의 목적어로서 '역할을 분리하는 감'을 표현하기 위해 'to separate roles'로 완성하고, (B)는 because 절의 주어+동사 구조로서 '그감들이 더 큰 차이(구분)를 가능하게 한다'는 의미의 'they enable greater distinction'으로 완성합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.*lament: 슬퍼하다
options: ② Both sides of written documents
③ The importance of creating literary works
④ The ways of avoiding sudden interruptions
⑤ The difference between unrecorded and well-documented things
questions.explanation: 이 글은 방해(interruptions/interference)가 초래하는 부정적인 결과들에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 마틴 루터 킹 주니어와 사무엘 테일러 콜리지의 예시를 통해 창작 활동이 중단된 사례를 언급하고, 전문가들뿐만 아니라 일반인들의 생산성 저하와 스트레스 증가라는 결과를 초래한다고 서술하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 '방해의 결과'입니다.
options_translation: ① 방해의 결과
② 서면 문서의 양면성
③ 문학 작품 창작의 중요성
④ 갑작스러운 방해를 피하는 방법
⑤ 기록되지 않은 것과 잘 문서화된 것의 차이

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is ⓐ<u>to come</u> around and show that you care. If you notice someone ⓑ<u>lonely</u>, you could go and sit with them. If you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more ⓒ<u>social</u> after a while, and they will owe it all to you. A person's happiness comes from attention. There are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ⓓ<u>ignored</u> them. Even if you say hi to someone ⓔ<u>is passing</u> by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: ⓔ의 'is passing'은 앞에 있는 명사 'someone'을 수식하는 구조여야 합니다. 한 문장에 접속사 없이 동사가 두 개(say, is passing) 올 수 없으므로, 현재분사 형태인 'passing'으로 고쳐서 'someone (who is) passing by'의 구조가 되도록 해야 합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 싿임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. During the last fifty years, agricultural engineers and crop scientists have significantly ␐<u>enhanced</u> how accurately they provide water and nutrients to crops. Since 1969, the global use of fertilizers has tripled and irrigation capacities have nearly doubled. This cultivation has made crops ␑<u>thrive</u> more than ever. However, these improved conditions have also drawn the attention of ␒<u>unwanted</u> agricultural pests. Farm fields are ␓<u>less</u> rich in nutrients and water than the surrounding natural areas. As a result, they have become very attractive to weeds that seek this ␔<u>abundance</u> of plant necessities.
questions.explanation: 농경지는 비료와 관개 시설 등을 통해 영양분감 물을 충분히 공급받고 있으므로, 접경 자연 지역밴다 'less rich'(덜 퐒부한)가 아닌 'more rich'(더 퐒부한)가 되어앴 한다. 뒤에 ␔ abundance(퐒부함)와도 흐름이 일치한다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 싿임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be ␐<u>less</u> negative. However, digital business activities can still ␑<u>threaten</u> the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more ␒<u>hazardous</u>. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is ␓<u>neglected</u>. A recent Wired report declared that most data enters' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, ␔<u>decreased</u> carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
questions.explanation: 클라우드에 더 큰 데이터림 저장할수록 화석 연료 사용이 늘어나 탄소 배출이 줝가하여 그린 클라우드림 회색으로 만들게 되므로, 'decreased'(감소한)림 'increased'(줝가한)로 바꿀어앴 문맥상 적절하다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For instance, individuals who view themselves as -voters- are more likely to cast their votes compared to those who merely express a desire to vote. Likewise, someone who identifies with regular exercise doesn't need to convince themselves to work out; it's simply a natural part of who they are. In other words, when your actions match with your self-perception, there's no longer a need for _____________________ behavior change.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 행동이 정체성의 반영이며, 자신을 어떤 사람으로 인식하느냐에 따라 행동이 자연스럽게 따라온다는 점을 설명합니다. 행동이 자아 인식과 일치하면, 더 이상 의도적인(애쐘 노력하는) 행동 변화가 필요치 않게 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 의도적인
② 부정적인
③ 걍정적인
④ 단순한
⑤ 예측 불가한

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that ____________________________________ according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① nothing changes in the physical structure of the brain
② the physical architecture of the brain changes
③ attention and concentration are greatly improved
④ the speed at which the brain forms is influenced
⑤ the brain is the central organ of the human nervous system
questions.explanation: 이 글은 집중된 주의력과 반복적인 연습이 뇌의 물리적 구조(가소성)를 변화시킨다는 과학적 증거들(동물의 청각/시각 센터, 바이올리니스트의 대뇌 피질, 택시 기사의 해마)을 나열하고 있습니다. 따라서 결론적으로 우리가 주의를 기울이고 연습하는 것에 따라 '뇌의 물리적 구조가 변한다'는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌의 물리적 구조에는 아무런 변화도 일어나지 않는다
② 뇌의 물리적 구조가 변한다
③ 주의력과 집중력이 크게 향상된다
④ 뇌가 형성되는 속도가 영향을 받는다
⑤ 뇌는 인간 신경계의 중심 기관이다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. ⓐ<u>We often take the easy route to improve our skills</u>. ⓑ<u>Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life</u>. ⓒ<u>Taking time to rest and reflect is essential, as it revitalizes the mind and body, allowing for sustained energy and focus in one's pursuits</u>. ⓓ<u>These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity</u>. ⓔ<u>Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill</u>. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 '쉬운 길을 택하지 말고 고난과 노력을 통해 실력과 강인함을 길러야 한다'는 것입니다. ③번(ⓒ) 문장은 '휴식과 성찰이 활력을 되찾아주는 데 필수적이다'라는 내용으로, 고난을 통한 실력 배양이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어난 휴식의 중요성을 말하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. ⓐ<u>Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes</u>. ⓑ<u>These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily</u>. ⓒ<u>So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps</u>. ⓓ<u>By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes</u>. ⓔ<u>Childhood hinders the passing on of cultural information, and genes can evolve faster than culture</u>. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 유년기가 동물들에게 환경에 대해 배우고 유연성을 가질 수 있게 해준다는 내용의 글입니다. 철새의 예시를 통해 학습 기간(유년기)이 긴 새들이 더 효율적인 경로를 가진다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ⓔ는 유년기가 문화 정보의 전달을 방해한다는 내용으로, 유년기의 긍정적 역할을 강조하는 전체 흐름에 반합니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved.
ordered_passages: (A) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two.

(B) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.

(C) In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 수렵 채집인이 이동할 때 짐을 모두 옮겨야 했다는 점을 언급합니다. (C)에서 특히 어머니들이 아이를 업어야 했기에 출산 간격이 길었다는 구체적인 제약 사항을 설명합니다. (A)에서 이와 대조되는(on the other hand) 농경 사회의 특징(정착 생활로 인한 출산 간격 단축)을 제시하고, (B)에서 이러한 변화가 인구 증가와 농경 사회의 노동력 확보로 이어졌다는 결론을 맺는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities.
ordered_passages: (A) Naturally, many of the most valuable digital resources are useless for them. So, recently some professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have tried to make significant progress in meeting their needs.
(B) This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions.
(C) Despite such progress, some scholars creating digital projects still too often fail to take these needs into account.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 장애인의 필요가 디지털 정보 분야에서 무시되어 왔음을 지적합니다. (A)에서 그 결과(Naturally) 장애인들이 디지털 자원을 쓰지 못하게 되었고, 최근 이를 해결하려는 노력이 시작되었음을 언급합니다. (C)에서 그러한 진전(such progress)에도 불구하고 여전히 많은 학자들이 이를 간과하고 있음을 지적하고, (B)에서 더 넓은 관객을 고려하는 설계가 필요하다는 해결책 혹은 개선 방향을 제시하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. (A) Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. (B) When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. (C) The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. (D) Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. (E) As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
questions.insertion_sentence: Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 회색다람쥐가 더 밀집해서 살 수 있고 다양한 서식지에 살 수 있어 생존에 유리하다는 '추가적인(also)' 이점을 설명하고 있습니다. (D)까지는 먹이 경쟁에서의 우위를 설명했고, (E) 뒤의 문장은 붉은다람쥐가 멸종 위기에 처했다는 최종 결과를 말합니다. 붉은다람쥐가 멸종 위기에 처하게 된 복합적인 이유(먹이 우위 + 서식지 적응력)가 모두 제시된 후 결과가 나오는 것이 자연스러우므로 (E) 자리에 들어가는 것이 맞습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.summary_sentence: Saving for future needs suggests a choice for (A)___________ gratification, yet instances of early expenditure, like using funds intended for holiday gifts on a summer trip, could signal a lack of (B)___________ in resisting immediate temptations.
questions.explanation: 지문은 미래의 소비를 위해 돈이나 물건을 아끼는 행위가 당장의 즐거움보다 나중에 올 보상을 선택하는 '지연된(delayed)' 만족을 선호함을 보여주지만, 의지 박약으로 인해 원래 계획과 달리 당장의 유혹에 굴복하여 돈을 미리 써버리는 경우는 '자기 통제(self-control)'의 부족을 나타낸다고 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 delayed, (B)에는 self-control이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 즉각적인 ...... 자기 통제
② 즐거운 ...... 선호
③ 지연된 ...... 선호
④ 지연된 ...... 자기 통제
⑤ 즉각적인 ...... 유혹

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment.
questions.summary_sentence: People engage in activities that involve mild (A)___________ for pleasure because the human brain perceives them as (B)____________, even when survival isn't threatened.
subjective_conditions: 글 속에서 찾아 쓸 것
어형 변화 없이 작성할 것
철자 오류 발생 시 오답 처리
OMR 답안지 뒷면의 문항 번호에 맞춰 작성할 것
questions.explanation: 인간은 쾌락을 위해 어느 정도의 고통(pain)을 유발하는 활동을 찾으며, 이는 뇌가 그것을 안전한(safe) 위협으로 인식하기 때문이라는 내용입니다. 지문 내에서 'pain'과 'safe'를 찾아 원형 그대로 빈칸에 채울 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 두 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 단어를 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options.
questions.summary_sentence: The brainwriting process begins with (A)__________ generating ideas, and then the ideas are shared (B)__________ within the group. To make (C)__________ decision, members evaluate each other and then come together to select and improve the most (D)__________ choices.
subjective_conditions: 글 속에서 찾아 쓸 것
어형 변화 없이 작성할 것
철자 오류 발생 시 오답 처리
OMR 답안지 뒷면의 문항 번호에 맞춰 작성할 것
questions.explanation: 브레인라이팅 과정의 단계를 요약하는 문제입니다. (A) 각자 따로 아이디어를 생성하고(separately), (B) 익명으로 공유하며(anonymously), (C) 독립적인 판단(independent)을 내린 후, (D) 가장 유망한(promising) 선택지를 고른다는 내용입니다. 지문 내의 단어를 어형 변화 없이 그대로 추출하여 빈칸에 대입합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Businesses are expected to have less of a negative environmental impact as they move some of their core business operations ─ like sales, marketing, and archiving, ─ to digital platforms. Nonetheless, environmental risks can still arise from digital business operations. The harm that digital businesses can cause can occasionally be even more dangerous. Offices used to generate a lot more paper waste a few decades ago because all documents were printed on paper. One encouraging step toward saving trees was the transition of offices from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails. On the other hand, the environmental cost of electricity and the Internet is overlooked. According to a recent Wired article, fossil fuels power the majority of data centers. When we store more data on clouds, we generate more carbon emissions.
options: ① Digital business activities can lead to environmental harm.
② Digital businesses have increased efficiency in the environmental sector.
③ Productivity can be greatly improved by changing working environment.
④ Reducing carbon emissions is better than saving trees for the environment.
⑤ Converting from paper documents to digital versions has provided convenience.
questions.explanation: 디지털 비즈니스로의 전환이 종이 사용을 줄여 환경에 도움이 된다고 간주되곤 하지만, 실제로는 데이터 센터 운영을 위한 화석 연료 사용과 인터넷 소비 전력으로 인해 디지털 비즈니스 운영에서도 상당한 환경 위험과 탄소 배출이 발생할 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 요지로는 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 디지털 비즈니스 활동은 환경 피해로 이어질 수 있다.
② 디지털 비즈니스는 환경 분야에서 효율성을 높여왔다.
③ 작업 환경을 바꿈으로써 생산성을 크게 향상시킬 수 있다.
④ 탄소 배출을 줄이는 것이 환경을 위해 나무를 살리는 것보다 더 낫다.
⑤ 종이 문서를 디지털 버전으로 바꾸는 것은 편리함을 제공해왔다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels. * lament: 슬퍼하다
options: ① ways to minimize disruptions to our work
② historical literary examples by great writers
③ negative consequences of sudden interruptions
④ importance of reducing stress levels in everyday life
⑤ difficulties in finding inspiration when writing poems
questions.explanation: 이 글은 외부의 방해(interruptions)가 초래하는 부정적인 결과들에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 마틴 루터 킹과 콜리지의 문학적인 사례를 통해 영감을 잃어버리거나 작품을 완성하지 못하는 등의 손해를 언급하며, 실제 전문직 종사자들이나 일반인들에게도 생산성을 떨어뜨리고 스트레스를 높인다고 말하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로는 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 업무 방해를 최소화하는 방법들
② 위대한 작가들에 의해 나타난 역사적인 문학 사례들
③ 갑작스러운 방해의 부정적인 결과들
④ 일상생활에서 스트레스 수치를 줄이는 것의 중요성
⑤ 시를 쓸 때 영감을 찾는 것의 어려움

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 35번]
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency ─ a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority ─ can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales remained the same. It led to increased efficiency even though their decisions were not focused on meeting organizational goals. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and with fewer mistakes made. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.* radically: 급격하게 ** shift: (근무) 교대
options: ① Self-Discipline: The Most Important Value of Employees
② What Happens When Employees Get a Sense of Control
③ Shorter Break Time: The Key to Increase Productivity
④ The Necessity of Meeting Organizational Goals
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 통제권이나 결정권(주체성)을 부여하는 것이 업무에 대한 에너지와 집중력을 높인다는 내용입니다. 오하이오 제조 공장의 사례를 통해 작은 결정권을 주었을 때 생산성이 20% 증가하고 효율성이 높아졌음을 보여줍니다. 따라서 ②번 '직원들이 통제감을 가질 때 일어나는 일'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자율성: 직원의 가장 중요한 가치
② 직원들이 통제감을 가질 때 일어나는 일
③ 더 짧은 휴식 시간: 생산성 향상의 열쇠
④ 조직 목표 달성의 필요성
⑤ 편안한 유니폼, 더 큰 효율성!

questions.question: 7. 다음 안내문의 Winter Sports Program에 관한 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Winter Sports ProgramWinter is coming! Let's have some fun together!Time & Location• Every Sunday in December from 1 p.m. to 3 p.m.• Grand Blue Ice RinkLesson Details• Ice Hockey, Speed Skating, and Figure Skating• Participants must be 8 years of age or older.Fee• Ice Hockey: $200• Speed Skating / Figure Skating: $150Notice• Skates and helmets will be provided for free.• You should bring your own gloves.※ For more information, visit www.wintersprorts.com.
options: ② 아이스하키, 스피드 스케이팅 강좌는 개설되지 않는다.
③ 참가자는 반드시 여덟 살 이상이어야 한다.
