⑤ 스케이트는 유로로 대여할 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 안내문의 'Participants must be 8 years of age or older.'(참가자는 8세 이상이어야 한다)라는 내용과 일치한다. ① 일요일(Sunday)에 실시된다. ② 세 가지 강좌(아이스하키, 스피드 스케이팅, 피겨 스케이팅)가 개설된다. ④ 피겨 스케이팅 강좌는 $150이다. ⑤ 스케이트와 헬멧은 무료(for free)로 제공된다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Gary Becker was born in Pottsville, Pennsylvania in 1930 and grew up in Brooklyn, New York City. His father, who ⓐ<u>had</u> not been well educated, had a deep interest in financial and political issues. After graduating from high school, Becker went to Princeton University, ⓑ<u>where</u> he majored in economics. He was dissatisfied with his economic education at Princeton University because "it didn't seem ⓒ<u>to be</u> handling real problems." He earned a doctor's degree in economics from the University of Chicago in 1955. His doctoral paper on the economics of discrimination was mentioned by the Nobel Prize Committee as an important contribution to economics. Since 1985, Becker had written a regular economics column in Business Week, ⓓ<u>explaining</u> economic analysis and ideas to the general public. In 1992, he was ⓔ<u>awarding</u> the Nobel Prize in economic science. As a Nobel Prize winner in 1992, he was able to make more people around the world interested in his study.* discrimination: 차별
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장에서 주어인 'he'(Gary Becker)는 노벨상을 수여한 것이 아니라 '받은' 대상이므로 수동태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 awarding을 과거분사인 awarded로 고쳐 'was awarded'로 써야 한다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease when children are as ⓐ<u>young</u> as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The decline in curiosity can ⓑ<u>be traced</u> in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess: the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between ⓒ<u>those</u> in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly ⓓ<u>disordered</u>. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs ⓔ<u>to become</u> faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.* default setting: 기본값** groove: 고랑 *** prune: 가지치기하다
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'The neural pathways'이며, 'that enable those beliefs'는 이를 수식하는 관계절이다. 따라서 ⓔ 자리는 문장의 본동사가 와야 하므로 'to become'을 'become'으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절하다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A farm field is a completely artificial landscape; it is required to ⓐ<u>support</u> a monoculture, a single, chosen plant type. The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved through the ⓑ<u>addition</u> of nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years. advancements by engineers and crop scientists have significantly ⓒ<u>enhanced</u> farmers' ability to precisely supply these resources. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also ⓓ<u>attracted</u> the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Due to the ⓔ<u>lack</u> of nutrients and water in cultivated fields compared to surrounding natural land, the fields are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.* monoculture: 단일 작물 재배** irrigation: (논, 밭에) 물을 댐: 관개
questions.explanation: 앞선 문장에서 경작지에 비료와 물을 충분히 공급하여 '사치스러운(luxurious) 환경'이 조성되었다고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 주변의 자연 토양보다 영양분과 물이 '부족한(lack)' 것이 아니라 '풍부하기(abundance)' 때문에 잡초들이 선호하는 부동산이 된다는 맥락이 되어야 하므로 ⓔ가 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The rate at which different aspects of our world change varies. In a matter of seconds, storm winds may bring an ancient oak tree thundering to the ground or knock out electric power to a million people. In a few months, farmland may be ⓐ<u>transformed</u> into a suburban development.Sometimes the pace of change is far ⓑ<u>slower</u>. The face you saw reflected in your mirror this morning probably appeared no different from the face you saw the day before ─ or a week or a month ago. Yet we know that the face that stares back at us from the glass is not ⓒ<u>different</u>, and cannot be, as it was 10 minutes ago. The proof is in your photo album: Look at a photograph taken of yourself 5 or 10 years ago and you see noticeable ⓓ<u>distinctions</u> between the face in the snapshot and the face in your mirror. If you lived in a world without mirrors for a year and then saw your reflection, you might be surprised by the change. After an interval of 10 years without seeing yourself, you might not at first recognize the person peering from the mirror. Even something as basic as our own face varies from moment to moment. The next time you look at yourself in the mirror, you will see the face of ⓔ<u>change</u>.* suburban: 도시 주변의** peer: 응시하다
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 요지는 모든 것이 매 순간 변한다는 것이며, 얼굴 역시 10분 전과 같을 수 없다는 맥락입니다. 뒤이어 나오는 5~10년 전 사진과의 대조가 증거로 제시되고 있으므로, 10분 전과 '다르지 않은' 것이 아니라 '동일한(the same)' 혹은 '같은(the same)' 상태가 아니라는 흐름이 되어야 합니다. 문맥상 is not the same이 되어야 하므로 'different'는 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show that you ____________________. If you notice someone who is lonely, you could go and sit with them. If you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. A person's happiness comes from attention. There are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. Even if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: 누군가를 돕는 데 있어 거창한 것이 필요한 것이 아니라, 관심을 가지고 지켜봐 주는 것(attention)이 중요하다는 내용입니다. 외로운 사람 곁에 앉아주거나 인사하는 행위는 상대방에게 누군가 자신을 신경 쓰고 있다는 느낌을 줍니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '주의 깊고 염려하고 있음(are attentive and concerned)'을 보여준다는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 주의 깊고 염려하고 있다
② 짜증 나고 조급해한다
③ 재능과 능력을 갖추고 있다
④ 당신의 미래에 관심이 있다
⑤ 무관심하다

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Companies large and small have ________________________________. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.* drudgery: 고된 일
options: ② forced their customers to do more work
③ realized employees' perfect work-life balance
④ automated difficult and time-consuming tasks
⑤ off-loaded work onto the backs of their employees
questions.explanation: 컴퓨터화된 사회가 여가 시간을 늘려줄 것이라는 기대와 달리, 실제로는 기업들이 이전에 해주던 서비스(예약, 체크인, 장바구니 담기 등)를 고객이 직접 하게 만들었다는 내용입니다. 즉, 기업들이 고객에게 더 많은 일을 하도록 강요했다는 내용이 빈칸에 적절합니다. 5번 선택지는 '직원들'에게 업무를 떠넘겼다는 뜻이므로 문맥상 '고객'에게 전가했다는 내용인 2번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 고객의 만족도를 향상시켰다
② 그들의 고객들이 더 많은 일을 하도록 강요했다
③ 직원들의 완벽한 일과 삶의 균형을 실현했다
④ 어렵고 시간이 많이 걸리는 업무를 자동화했다
⑤ 업무를 그들 직원들의 등으로 떠넘겼다

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread." the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped increase sales. This shows _____________________________.* laxative: 완하제
options: ① a product has limited range of applications
② why people are no longer interested in yeast
③ how advertisers can adapt to regain consumer interest
④ repositioning a product has nothing to do with the sales increase
⑤ advertisers can successfully boost sales without changing their tactics
questions.explanation: 효모(yeast)에 대한 수요가 줄어들자 광고 대행사가 이를 비타민 공급원이나 완하제로 재포지셔닝하여 판매를 늘린 사례를 통해, 광고주가 소비자의 관심을 다시 얻기 위해 어떻게 적응하고 변화하는지를 보여줍니다.
options_translation: ① 제품은 제한된 범위의 용도를 가지고 있다
② 왜 사람들이 더 이상 효모에 관심이 없는지
③ 광고주가 소비자의 관심을 다시 얻기 위해 어떻게 적응할 수 있는지
④ 제품을 재포지셔닝하는 것은 매출 증대와 관련이 없다
⑤ 광고주는 전략을 바꾸지 않고도 성공적으로 매출을 올릴 수 있다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [23년 6월 23번]
questions.passage: People commonly believe they possess numerous socially desirable qualities while believing they lack most undesirable ones. ⓐFor instance, a significant portion of the population perceives themselves as more intelligent, fair-minded, less prejudiced, and better drivers than average. ⓑThis tendency, referred to as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average," is widespread. ⓒDespite being aware of the Lake Wobegon effect, many individuals still tend to underestimate their abilities and positive traits compared to others. ⓓA survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. ⓔIn terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10% and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 자신의 능력을 실제보다 높게 평가한다는 '레이크 워비건 효과'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ⓒ번 문장은 많은 개인이 자신의 능력과 긍정적 특성을 타인에 비해 과소평가(underestimate)한다고 서술하고 있는데, 이는 글 전체의 주제인 '과대평가'와 정반대되는 내용이므로 흐름상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [23년 6월 31번]
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. When they speak, others listen ─ even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. ⓐThink about a world-famous basketball player who has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. ⓑIt's not because of his knowledge of the products he endorses, but because of what he can do with a basketball. ⓒAnd when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines, but because of his talents as an actor. ⓓThese examples show why the advertisers should not rely on the popularity of famous people when they pay them for endorsement. ⓔIf you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.* endorsement: (유명인의 텔레비전 등에서의 상품) 보증 선전
questions.explanation: 이 글은 특정 분야에서 뛰어난 능력을 가진 사람이 그 분야와 상관없는 조언을 할 때도 다른 사람들이 귀를 기울이는 현상(후광 효과)을 설명하며, 광고에서 유명인을 활용하는 이유를 뒷받침하고 있습니다. ⓓ번은 광고주들이 보증 광고를 위해 돈을 지불할 때 유명인의 인기에 의존해서는 안 된다는 주장을 펴고 있으므로 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless We're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad.
ordered_passages: (A) Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods.

(B) The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.

(C) There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" ─ for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 음식을 이분법적으로 '좋은 음식'과 '나쁜 음식'으로 나눌 수 없다고 말합니다. (C)에서 하지만 '음식의 조합'이 건강에 좋거나 나쁜 식단을 만든다고 전환하며 예시(좋은 음식만 먹는 성인)를 도입합니다. (A)에서 이 예시의 문제점(영양 다양성 부족)을 지적하고, 반대 예시인 치킨을 가끔 먹는 십 대를 소개합니다. (B)에서 그 십 대의 식단은 괜찮지만, 매일 튀긴 음식을 먹는 사람은 나쁜 식단을 가진 것이라고 결론 짓습니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Both people and animals, human and non-human alike, tend to save goods or money for future use.
ordered_passages: (A) However, in some cases, individuals don't wait for the planned occasion and instead use their savings too soon. For instance, at the beginning of the year, an employee might put money aside for Christmas gifts but then spend it on a summer vacation.

(B) This suggests a preference for waiting for a reward instead of receiving it immediately: individuals sacrifice some instant pleasure for a future one. Thus, the value of the future reward, even after discounting, should be higher than that of the present one.

(C) Consider the scenario where someone might save money up for a new smartphone to be released at the end of the month but then spend it on a fancy dinner this weekend. These cases could be examples of a lack of willpower. Individuals may use their savings for maximum benefit but act differently when tempted by immediate pleasure.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 인간과 동물 모두 미래를 위해 저축하는 경향이 있다는 일반적 사실을 언급합니다. (B)의 'This'는 주어진 글의 저축 행위를 가리키며, 이는 즉각적 보상보다 미래의 보상을 기다리는 선호도를 나타낸다고 설명합니다. (A)에서 'However'를 통해 반전하며 계획보다 빨리 저축을 써버리는 예외 상황(크리스마스 선물 대신 여름 휴가)을 소개합니다. (C)에서 또 다른 예시(스마트폰 대신 근사한 저녁 식사)를 들며, 이것이 의지력 부족의 사례임을 밝히며 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. (A) However, wealthier societies have their own unique sources of stress. (B) One significant stress factor in wealthier nations is the pressure of time. (C) In a study conducted in 1999, examining 31 countries, it was found that wealthier and more industrialized nations tended to have a faster pace of life. (D) Moreover, this constant urgency increased the risk of heart disease. (E) In effect, while rapid productivity contributes to wealth, it can also lead individuals to feel deprived of time for relaxation and enjoyment.
questions.insertion_sentence: This lifestyle resulted in a higher standard of living but also left people constantly feeling urgent and under pressure.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이러한 생활 방식(This lifestyle)'이 높은 생활 수준을 결과로 가져왔지만 사람들로 하여금 긴박함과 압박을 느끼게 했다고 말합니다. (C) 문장에서 부유하고 산업화된 국가들이 더 빠른 삶의 속도를 갖는 경향이 있다는 '생활 방식'이 언급된 후, 이 방식의 결과(높은 생활 수준과 압박감)를 설명하는 주어진 문장이 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다. 그 뒤 (D) 문장의 'this constant urgency'가 주어진 문장의 'feeling urgent'를 받아 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고, 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Scarcity encourages sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a lower price: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests that if _____________________, you can promote sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.* tactic: 전략
subjective_conditions: 1. 10단어 이내로 작성할 것(빈칸만)
2. you, customers, items를 모두 사용할 것(변형 불가)
3. 빈칸을 포함하여 한 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.answer: you restrict the number of items customers can buy
questions.explanation: 본문은 '희소성(Scarcity)'이 판매를 장려한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 실험 결과 구매 수량에 제한을 둔 경우에 판매량이 더 높았으므로, 빈칸에는 '고객이 살 수 있는 물품의 수를 제한하면'이라는 의미가 들어가야 합니다. 조건에 맞춰 you(주어), restrict(동사), the number of items(목적어), customers can buy(수식어)를 사용하여 구성합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고, 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. ________________________________________. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
subjective_conditions: 1. 11단어 이내로 작성할 것
2. birth, possible, intervals, made를 모두 사용할 것(변형 불가)
3. 빈칸을 한 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.answer: The settlement lifestyle made it possible to shorten the birth intervals
questions.explanation: 정착 생활을 하게 되면서 아이를 이동하며 데리고 다닐 걱정이 없어졌고, 그 결과 출산 간격이 짧아졌다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. '정착 생활 방식이 출산 간격을 줄이는 것을 가능하게 만들었다'는 의미의 문장을 구성합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고, 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: _______________________________________________ ─ either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are merely behaving in line with your own self-identity.
subjective_conditions: 1. 12단어 이내로 작성할 것
2. are, believe, reveal, the kind를 모두 사용할 것(변형 불가)
3. 빈칸을 포함하여 한 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.answer: Your actions reveal the kind of person you believe that you are
questions.explanation: 자아 정체성과 행동의 일치에 관한 글입니다. 빈칸은 주제문 역할을 하며, 당신의 행동이 당신이 스스로를 어떤 사람이라고 믿는지를 보여준다는 내용이 들어가야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고, 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Children who receive more praise feel better about who they are and what they can do. That is, ___________________________________________________________. Preschoolers deeply internalize their parents' words, lacking the cognitive ability to question or dismiss false information. For instance, if a preschool boy consistently hears praise from his mother about his intelligence and helpfulness, he is likely to integrate these beliefs into his self-perception. This positive self-image as a capable and helpful individual can enhance his persistence in solving problems and boost his confidence when facing challenges. Likewise, seeing himself as a helpful individual may encourage him to willingly assist with tasks both at home and in preschool settings.
subjective_conditions: 1. 13단어 이내로 작성할 것(빈칸만)
2. improves, not only를 모두 사용할 것(변형 불가, 중복 가능)
3. 빈칸을 포함하여 한 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.answer: praise not only improves young children's behavior, but it also improves their self-esteem
questions.explanation: 칭찬이 아이들의 긍정적인 자기 이미지를 형성하고 자존감을 높여준다는 내용입니다. 빈칸 앞의 'That is(즉)'를 통해 앞 문장을 상술하는 내용이 와야 하므로 'praise not only improves young children's behavior, but it also improves their self-esteem'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, which is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way that  production could be made more efficient, known as the "division of labor." Making most manufactured goods involves several different processes using different skills. Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished. One worker could do all these tasks, and make 20 pins in a day. But this work can be divided into its separate processes, with a number of workers each performing one task. Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day ─ a huge increase in productivity from the 200 they would have produced before.
subjective_conditions: 1. 10단어 이내로 작성할 것
2. 한 문장으로 작성할 것
questions.answer: The division of labor can increase productivity.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 분업(division of labor)이 각 노동자의 전문화를 통해 생산성을 크게 향상시킬 수 있다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 요지는 '분업은 생산성을 높일 수 있다'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Animals learn about their environment by spending time as children. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
subjective_conditions: 1. 11단어 이내로 작성할 것
2. flexibility, allows, adapting to를 모두 사용할 것(변형 불가)
3. 한 문장으로 작성할 것
questions.answer: Childhood allows animals to have flexibility in adapting to the environment.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린 시절(childhood)이 동물들에게 유전적 본능(hardware) 이상의 유연성을 제공하여, 변화하는 환경에 더 효율적으로 적응할 수 있게 해준다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 조건에 맞추어 유연성(flexibility), 허용하다(allows), 적응하는 것(adapting to)을 사용하여 요지를 작성합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 설명한 뜻이 가장 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Fritz Zwicky, a memorable astrophysicist who ⓐ<u>coined the term</u> 'supernova', was born in Varna, Bulgaria to a Swiss father and a Czech mother. At the age of six, he was sent to his grandparents who ⓑ<u>looked after</u> him for most of his childhood in Switzerland. There, he received an advanced education in mathematics and physics. In 1925, he ⓒ<u>emigrated to</u> the United States and continued his physics research at California Institute of Technology (Caltech). He developed numerous theories that have had a ⓓ<u>profound</u> influence on the understanding of our universe in the early 21st century. After being appointed as a professor of astronomy at Caltech in 1942, he developed some of the earliest jet engines and ⓔ<u>holds</u> more than 50 patents, many in jet propulsion.
options: ① ⓐ: to invent a new word or expression
② ⓑ: to be in charge of someone or something
③ ⓒ: to come to live in a different country
④ ⓓ: felt or experienced very strongly or in an extreme way
⑤ ⓔ: to keep something in your hand or arms
questions.explanation: ⓔ의 'holds'는 문맥상 '특허를 보유하다(to legally possess or own something)'라는 의미이지, '손이나 팔에 무언가를 들고 있다'는 물리적인 의미가 아닙니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ: 새로운 단어나 표현을 만들어 내다
② ⓑ: 누군가나 무언가를 책임지다(돌보다)
③ ⓒ: 다른 나라에 살러 오다(이주하다)
④ ⓓ: 매우 강하게 또는 극단적으로 느껴지거나 경험되는(심오한/깊은)
⑤ ⓔ: 손이나 팔에 무언가를 유지하다(들고 있다)

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show that you care. If you notice someone who is lonely, you could go and sit with them. If you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. A person's happiness comes from attention. There are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. Even if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
options: ② The best criteria on helping others in need
③ How to handle people with social phobia
④ Small efforts for the big world: Voluntary work
⑤ The power of small attention: Simple ways to help
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 도움을 주기 위해 거창한 것을 할 필요 없이, 외로운 사람 곁에 앉아주거나 인사를 건네는 등의 '작은 관심(attention)'만으로도 상대방에게 큰 힘이 될 수 있다는 내용이므로 ⑤가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 타인에 대한 적절한 간섭
② 어려움에 처한 타인을 돕는 최선의 기준
③ 사회 공포증이 있는 사람들을 다루는 법
④ 큰 세상을 위한 작은 노력: 자원봉사
⑤ 작은 관심의 힘: 돕기 위한 간단한 방법들

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 요지와 가장 잘 어울리는 표현은?
questions.passage: In some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
options: ① A bad workman blames his tools.
② The early bird catches the worm.
③ Never judge a book by its cover.
④ You scratch my back and I'll scratch yours.
⑤ A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
questions.explanation: 본문은 의지의 박약(weakness of will)으로 인해 장기적인 계획이나 더 큰 이익을 포기하고 당장의 즉각적인 쾌락을 위해 저축한 돈을 미리 써버리는 상황을 설명하고 있습니다. (제시된 정답 ②는 부지런함을 강조하는 격언이나, 제공된 정답지에 따라 정답을 표기하였습니다. 실제 문맥상으로는 현재의 확실한 이익을 선호하는 경향과 관련된 ⑤번 등이 고려될 수 있으나 원본 데이터를 따릅니다.)
options_translation: ① 서툰 목수가 제 연장 탓한다.
② 일찍 일어나는 새가 벌레를 잡는다.
③ 겉만 보고 판단하지 마라.
④ 오는 정이 있어야 가는 정이 있다.
⑤ 손 안의 한 마리 새가 숲속의 두 마리보다 낫다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.*cortex: (대뇌) 피질(皮質)*hippocampus: (대뇌 측두엽의) 해마
options: ① The Relatively Large Brain Size of Humans
② The Brain Area Essential for Spatial Memory
③ The Need for Practice and Attention in Daily Life
④ The Excellence of Animals' Exceptional Sensory Organs
⑤ The Impact of Attention and Practice on Brain Structure
questions.explanation: 이 글은 집중된 주의력(focused attention)과 연습이 뇌의 물리적 구조(physical architecture)를 재구성하고 변화시킨다는 과학적 증거들(바이올리니스트의 뇌, 택시 기사의 해마 등)을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '주의와 연습이 뇌 구조에 미치는 영향'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 인간의 상대적으로 큰 뇌 크기
② 공간 기억에 필수적인 뇌 영역
③ 일상생활에서 연습과 주의의 필요성
④ 동물들의 뛰어난 감각 기관의 우수성
⑤ 주의와 연습이 뇌 구조에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. (A) Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. (B) So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. (C) By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. (D) Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. (E) Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.insertion_sentence: These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'These birds'는 (A)에서 언급된 '이동 방법을 알고 태어난 철새들'을 가리킵니다. (A) 문장에서 이동 방법이 비효율적일 수 있다고 언급한 뒤, 주어진 문장에서 이들이 쉽게 적응하지 못한다는 내용을 제시하고, 그 구체적인 예시로 (B)에서 호수가 마르거나 기후가 변해도 이전의 규칙과 지도를 고수한다는 내용이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: ⓐOver the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. ⓑWhat has remained considered for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. ⓒAs a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. ⓓWhile professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. ⓔThis situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 디지털 정보를 구축할 때 장애를 가진 사람들의 필요성이 간과되고 있다는 점을 지적하는 내용입니다. ⓑ 문장은 '무엇보다 중요하게 고려되어 온 것은 장애인들의 필요성이다'라는 의미가 되어 전체 흐름(장애인의 필요가 무시되고 있다는 흐름)과 정반대의 내용을 담고 있으므로 관계가 없습니다. (원문은 What has remained unconsidered... 가 되어야 함)

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 어휘 중 글의 흐름과 어울리지 않는 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. Although it may seem ⓐ<u>sensible</u>, having two separate calendars for work and personal life can lead to ⓑ<u>concentration</u>. To check if something is missing, you will find yourself checking your to-do lists multiple times. Instead, organize all of your tasks in one place. It doesn't ⓒ<u>matter</u> if you use digital or paper media. It's okay to keep your ⓓ<u>professional</u> and personal tasks in one place. This will give you a good idea of how time is divided between work and home. This will allow you to make ⓔ<u>informed</u> decisions about which tasks are most important.
questions.explanation: 직장과 개인 생활을 위한 두 개의 달력을 갖는 것은 혼란(distraction)이나 비효율성을 초래할 수 있다는 맥락입니다. 따라서 '집중(concentration)'은 흐름상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법이 어색한 것 두 개는? [3.8점]
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that ⓐis socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public ⓑthinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile ⓒthan the average person. This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and ⓓ<u>that</u> only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought ⓔ<u>what</u> they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
questions.explanation: ⓐ 주격 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 복수 대명사인 those(socially desirable characteristics를 가리킴)이므로 동사 is를 복수형인 are로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓔ thought의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절이며 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오므로 관계대명사 what 대신 접속사 that을 써야 합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen ─ even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.*endorsement: (유명인의 텔레비전 등에서의 상품) 보증 선전
options: ① Individuals who perform at a high level in their occupation often get instant credibility with others.
② When a person who has a special ability in one area speaks, others listen ─ even if the area of his skill is not related with the advice he gives.

④ A world-famous basketball player and an Olympic medalist swimmer have great influence on ordinary people.

questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 세계적인 농구 선수가 광고하는 제품에 대해 사람들이 귀를 기울이는 이유는 그 제품에 대한 전문 지식 때문이 아니라 그가 농구 분야에서 보여준 탁월함(능력) 때문이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 전문 지식 때문에 조언을 듣는다는 3번은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 자신의 직업에서 높은 수준의 성과를 내는 개인들은 종종 타인으로부터 즉각적인 신뢰를 얻는다.
② 한 분야에서 특별한 능력을 가진 사람이 말할 때, 비록 그의 기술 분야가 그가 주는 조언과 관련이 없더라도 타인들은 경청한다.
③ 타인들이 그 조언을 듣는 이유는 그 제품에 대한 선수의 전문적인 지식 때문이다.
④ 세계적으로 유명한 농구 선수와 올림픽 메달리스트 수영 선수는 일반인들에게 큰 영향력을 미친다.
⑤ 배우가 우리에게 특정 차를 운전해야 한다고 말할 때, 우리는 그의 엔진에 대한 전문 지식 때문이 아니라 그의 재능 때문에 경청한다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 표현으로 짝지어진 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Up until about 6,000 years ago, most people were farmers. Many lived in different places throughout the year, hunting for food or moving their livestock to areas with enough food. There was no need to tell the time because life depended on (A)___________ cycles, such as the changing seasons or sunrise and sunset. Gradually more people started to live in larger settlements, and some needed to tell the time. For example, priests wanted to know when to carry out (B)___________ ceremonies. This was when people first invented clocks ─ devices that show, measure, and keep track of passing time. Clocks have been important ever since. Today, clocks are used for important things such as setting busy airport timetables ─ if the time is (C)___________ aeroplanes might crash into each other when taking off or landing!
questions.explanation: (A) 계절의 변화나 일출, 일몰은 '자연적인(natural)' 주기에 해당합니다. (B) 예시로 언급된 사제(priests)들이 수행하는 의식은 '종교적인(religious)' 의식입니다. (C) 비행기가 서로 충돌할 위험이 있는 상황은 시간이 '부정확한(incorrect)' 경우입니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists ⓐ<u>says</u> that having a disorderly room can indicate a disorganized mental state. One of the professional tidying experts says that the moment you start ⓑ<u>to clean</u> your room, you also start ⓒ<u>changing</u> your life and gaining new perspective. When you clean your surroundings, positive and good atmosphere follows. You can do more things ⓓ<u>efficient and neat</u>. So, clean up your closets, organize your drawers, and ⓔ<u>arrange</u> your things first, then peace of mind will follow.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 'efficient and neat'은 동사 'do'를 수식하는 부사 역할을 해야 하므로 형용사 형태가 아닌 부사 형태인 'efficiently and neatly'로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다. (참고: ⓐ 역시 주어인 Psychologists가 복수이므로 say가 되어야 하나, 문제의 정답인 ④번이 더 명확한 오류로 제시되었습니다.)

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. (A) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (B) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one. (C) However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. (D) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (E) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.insertion_sentence: For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 저축한 돈을 원래 계획(크리스마스 선물)과 다르게 조기에(여름 휴가) 써버리는 구체적인 예시를 제공합니다. (C) 문장에서 저축을 조기에 사용하는 경우(uses their savings prematurely)를 언급하고 있고, 주어진 문장이 그 구체적인 예시 역할을 하기에 적절합니다. (D) 이후 문장은 이러한 구체적 사례들을 '의지의 나약함'의 예로 정의하고 있으므로, 주어진 문장은 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 3. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities.
ordered_passages: (A) As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors.

(B) This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.

(C) While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 장애인의 요구가 소홀히 다뤄졌음을 언급한 후, (A)에서 그 결과(As a result) 장애인들이 디지털 자원을 사용하지 못하게 된 현상을 설명합니다. (C)에서는 일부 분야의 진전에도 불구하고 여전히 학자들이 이러한 요구를 고려하지 못하고 있음을 지적합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 더 넓은 관객을 고려하는 디자인 결정을 통해 상황을 개선할 수 있다는 대안을 제시하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas ⓐ<u>personally</u>. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member ⓑ<u>estimates</u> them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most ⓒ<u>outstanding </u>options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process ⓓ<u>overlook</u> that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially ⓔ<u>useful</u> in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.explanation: 브레인라이팅은 모든 아이디어가 테이블에 놓이고 모든 목소리가 대화에 포함되도록 '보장'하거나 '확실히' 하는 과정입니다. 따라서 '간과하다'라는 의미의 ⓓ overlook은 문맥상 어색하며, ensures나 guarantees와 같은 단어가 오는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible.
ordered_passages: (A) By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes.
(B) Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with.
(C) These birds sometimes have very inefficient migration routes.
(D) Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
(E) These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily.
(F) Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes.
(G) So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps.
questions.explanation:
제시문에서 어린 시절(유년기)이 하드웨어(선천적 본능)에 의존하는 것보다 환경에 대한 학습과 유연성을 제공한다는 점을 언급합니다. 
(B)에서 타고난 정보에만 의존하여 이동하는 철새들을 소개하고, (C)에서 이들이 때때로 매우 비효율적인 경로를 갖게 됨을 설명합니다. 
(E)와 (G)에서는 이러한 본능 위주의 새들이 환경 변화에 적응하지 못하는 구체적인 한계와 사례를 제시합니다. 
이에 반해 (A)에서는 유년기가 긴 새들의 효율성을 대조적으로 보여주며, 마지막으로 (F)와 (D)를 통해 유년기가 문화적 정보 전수를 가능하게 하여 변화하는 세상에서 유연성을 제공한다는 결론으로 마무리하는 (B)-(C)-(E)-(G)-(A)-(F)-(D)의 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are thoroughly ⓐ<u>recorded</u>. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. questions.question: 25. [24년 6월 41-42번] 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening.
ordered_passages: (B)The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies ─ capsaicin ─ touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure. All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm.

In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment. This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. _____________________________________________This mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
options: ① The environmental conditions played a minimal role.
② Physical strength was the main determinant of success.
③ The tribe's physical strength ensured that their dominance.
④ Social structures became increasingly complex over time.
⑤ The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival.
questions.explanation: 지문 전체가 인간의 정신적 능력(상대보다 더 잘 생각하는 능력)이 생존 경쟁과 전쟁에서 큰 이점이 되었음을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 앞뒤 문맥 또한 적의 공격을 예측하고 계획하는 능력이 군사적 이점을 주었으며, 이 정신적 우위가 세대를 거쳐 전달되었다고 말하므로 '인간의 마음이 생존을 위한 투쟁에서 무기가 되었다'는 내용의 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 환경적 조건은 최소한의 역할만 했다.
② 신체적 힘이 성공의 주요 결정 요인이었다.
③ 부족의 신체적 힘이 그들의 지배를 보장했다.
④ 사회 구조는 시간이 지남에 따라 점점 더 복잡해졌다.
⑤ 인간의 정신은 생존을 위한 투쟁에서 하나의 무기가 되었다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. ⓐWhen the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations. ⓑThe grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. ⓒIn the same area of forest, grey squirrels can deplete the food supply before red squirrels even have a chance to eat. ⓓThe arrival of grey squirrels also caused changes in the local bird populations. ⓔGreys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.*edge: 우위 **acorn: 도토리
questions.explanation: 이 글은 외래종인 회색 다람쥐의 유입이 토종인 붉은 다람쥐의 멸종 위기를 초래한 과정과 그 원인(먹이 경쟁의 우위, 서식지 적응력 등)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓓ문장은 회색 다람쥐의 유입이 '새의 개체수'에 미친 변화를 언급하고 있어, 다람쥐 종 간의 경쟁과 토종 다람쥐의 감소라는 글의 핵심 주제에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 31번]
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
options: ① procedure of obtaining a high level of ability
② priority consideration to become a credible celebrity
③ exceptional performance that affects the public's trust
④ a factor that hinders an outstanding professional from gaining public credibility
⑤ a reason why superior job performance leads to infinite respect and declined credibility
questions.explanation: 이 글은 특정 분야에서 뛰어난 눔력(탁월함)을 갖춘 사람이 그 분야와 관련 없는 일에서도 대중의 신뢰와 관심을 받는 현상(후광 효과)에 대해 설명하고 읈습니다. 운동 선수나 개우의 사례를 통해 탁월한 성과가 대중의 신뢰에 영향을 미친다는 것이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 높은 수준의 눔력을 얻는 과정
② 신뢰할 수 읈는 인사가 되기 을한 우선 갱려 사항
③ 대중의 신뢰에 영향을 미친 뛰어난 성과
④ 뛰어난 전문가가 대중적 신뢰를 얻는 것을 방해하는 요인
⑤ 우수한 업무 수행이 무한한 존경감과 하락한 신뢰로 이어지는 이유

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. (A) Instead of more time, most of us have less. (B) Companies large and small have off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers. (C) Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. (D) With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. (E) At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
questions.insertion_sentence: It didn't work out this way.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장 'It didn't work out this way(일이 이런 식으로 풀리지 않았다)'는 컴퓨터화된 사회가 우리에게 더 많은 여가 시간을 줄 것이라는 기대가 실현되지 않았음을 나타내는 전환점입니다. 따라서 기대감을 설명하는 첫 문장 뒤이자, 실제로 여가 시간이 줄어들었다는 내용이 시작되는 (A) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
options: ① an inherited trait of the preschoolers raised through active interaction
② importance of inadequate praise and high self-esteem in one's life
③ tendencies among the preschoolers who lack parental praise
④ positive effects of praise on preschoolers' identity development
⑤ remarkable improvements in infants' cognitive sophistication and analytical reasoning skills
questions.explanation: 본문은 부모의 칭찬이 미취학 아동의 자아상(self-image)과 자존감(self-esteem) 형성에 어떻게 긍정적인 영향을 미치는지 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '칭찬이 미취학 아동의 정체성 발달에 미치는 긍정적 효과'가 가장 적절한 주제입니다.
options_translation: ① 활발한 상호작용을 통해 길러진 미취학 아동의 유전적 특성
② 한 사람의 인생에서 부적절한 칭찬과 높은 자존감의 중요성
③ 부모의 칭찬이 부족한 미취학 아동들 사이의 경향
④ 칭찬이 미취학 아동의 정체성 발달에 미치는 긍정적인 영향
⑤ 영유아의 인지적 정교함 및 분석적 추론 능력의 눈부신 향상

questions.question: 23. 다음 글에서 쓰인 밑줄 친 단어의 뜻풀이가 옳지 않은 것을 <보기>에서 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this ⓐ<u>tactic</u> in 1998. He ⓑ<u>persuade</u>d three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the ⓒ<u>volume</u> of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the ⓓ<u>scarce</u> condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity ⓔ<u>encourage</u>s sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with ⓕ<u>genuine</u> shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a ⓖ<u>laboratory</u> where consumers might behave differently.
vocabulary_box: ⓐ: an action or method that is planned and used to achieve a particular goal
ⓑ: to cause someone to do something by asking, giving reasons or despising
ⓒ: the amount of space that is filled by something
ⓓ: very small in amount or number; not plentiful
ⓔ: to make something more appealing or more likely to happen
ⓕ: actual, real, or true; not false or fake
ⓖ: a room or building with special equipment for doing scientific experiments and tests
questions.explanation: ⓑ의 persuade는 '설득하다'는 뜻으로 누군가에게 질문하거나 이유를 제시하여 행동하게 하는 것이지, 'despising(경멸하다)'을 통해 행동하게 하는 것이 아닙니다. 또한 ⓒ의 volume은 이 지문에서 '구매량' 즉 amount나 quantity의 의미로 쓰였으나, 영풀이에서는 '공간적 부피(space)'로 정의하고 있어 문맥적 의미와 맞지 않습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, ___________________________________________ in England.*edge: 우위 **acorn: 도토리
options: ③ the red squirrels have disappeared
④ greys have come close to extinction
⑤ both are living in the balance of ecosystems
questions.explanation: 외래종인 회색 다람쥐가 토착종인 붉은 다람쥐와의 경쟁에서 먹이 적응력, 서식 밀도 등의 우위를 점하여 살아남았으므로, 그 결과 토착종인 붉은 다람쥐가 사라지게 되었다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 둘 다 살아남지 못했다
② 외래종이 축출되었다
③ 붉은 다람쥐들이 사라졌다
④ 회색 다람쥐들이 멸종에 가까워졌다
⑤ 둘 다 생태계의 균형 속에서 살고 있다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.summary_sentence: Birds that experience their (A)______ with their parents are more adaptable to the environment than birds that do not; this is because it promotes (B)_________ in altering environment.
questions.explanation: 지문은 어린 시절(childhood)이 동물들에게 환경에 대해 배우고 유연하게 대처할 수 있게 해준다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 부모와 함께 어린 시절을 보내는 새들은 문화적 정보를 전달받아 변화하는 환경에서 유연성(flexibility)을 갖게 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 이동 / 돌연변이
② 어린 시절 / 유연성
③ 진화 / 효율성
④ 어려움 / 진화
⑤ 애착 / 번식

questions.question: 19. 다음 가의 묜줄 챜 불분 중 문맥상 낱말의 숬임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that was ⓐ<u>uncompleted</u> because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an ⓑ<u>unexpected</u> guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the ⓒ<u>untimely</u> visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work ⓓ<u>unfinished.</u> While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally ⓔ<u>decreasing</u> stress levels.
questions.explanation: 방해(interruption)는 일의 생산성을 떨어뜨리고 일반적으로 스트레스 수치림 '높이는(increasing)' 것이 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 가의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ① Manager's Efforts to Resolve Employee Issues
② Necessit of Adequate Rest of Work Efficiency
③ Importance of Ownership and Control for Work Improvement
④ Necessity of Facility Investment to Increase Work Productivity
⑤ Importance of Creating a Satisfactory Work Environment for Employee
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 통제권과 의사결정 권한(제어감)을 부여하는 것이 업무 생산성과 중심도림 킬게 향상시킨다는 내용이므로 ③가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 직원 문제 해결을 위한 관리자의 노력
② 업무 효율을 위한 적절한 휴식의 필요성
③ 업무 향상을 위한 주인 의식과 통제권의 중요성
④ 업무 생산성 증대림 위한 설비 투자의 필요성
⑤ 직원을 위한 만족스러운 근무 환경 젰성의 중요성

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As I walked from the mailbox, my heart was beating rapidly. In my hands, I held the letter from the university I had applied to. I thought my grades were good enough to (A)____________ and my application letter was well-written, but was it enough? I hadn't slept a wink for days. As I carefully tore into the paper of the envelope, the letter slowly emerged with the opening phrase, "It is our great pleasure..." I shouted with joy, "(B)____________!" As I held the letter, I began to make a fantasy about my college life in a faraway city.
options: ① (A) hit the hay - (B) I am in
② (A) make the cut - (B) I got rejected
③ (A) cross the line - (B) I made it
④ (A) make it through - (B) I have a long face
⑤ (A) break the ice - (B) I'm over the moon
questions.explanation: (A)에는 '합격하다/통과하다'는 의미의 표현이 들어가야 합니다. 'cross the line'은 선을 넘는다는 뜻도 있지만 여기서는 합격선의 맥락으로 쓰였으며, (B)는 합격 통지서를 받고 기뻐하는 상황이므로 '해냈다(I made it)'가 가장 적절합니다. (다만, 학교측 정답이 3번으로 기재되어 있으나 관용구의 일반적 의미상 4번의 'make it through'가 문맥상 더 자연스러울 수 있으나 원문 변형 혹은 학교 수업 내 강조된 표현에 따라 3번이 정답으로 제시된 것으로 보입니다.)
options_translation: ① 잠자리에 들다 - 나는 합격했다
② 합격하다 - 나는 거절당했다
③ 합격하다 - 내가 해냈다
④ 통과하다 - 나는 우울한 표정이다
⑤ 어색함을 깨다 - 나는 매우 기쁘다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 2개를 고르면?
questions.passage: We often try to find shortcuts in our challenges and take the easy route. ⓐ<u>When taken the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete</u>. ⓑ<u>We often take the easy route to improve our skills</u>. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. ⓒ<u>Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment</u>; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. ⓓ<u>It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that sets them apart</u>. ⓔ<u>Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance</u>. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'When taken'에서 의미상 주어인 'we'가 '빠른 탈출구를 취하는' 능동의 관계이므로 현재분사 'taking'을 써야 합니다. (When taking the quick exit)ⓓ 'It is ~ that' 강조구문에서 강조되는 대상(주어)이 'mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill'로 복수이므로, 뒤따르는 동사 'sets'는 'set'으로 일치시켜야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. ①The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. ②The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. ③The invention of weapons like bows and arrows changed the course of human history, enabling societies to hunt more effectively and defend themselves against predators. ④And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. ⑤The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 '정신(지능)'이 타 부족과의 경쟁 과정에서 생존을 위한 '정신적 무기'로 진화했다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 나머지 문장들은 모두 지능의 군사적·생존적 이점과 유전적 전달을 설명하고 있는 반면, ③번 문장은 활과 화살 같은 '물질적인 무기'의 발명과 사냥의 효율성을 설명하고 있으므로 지문의 전체적인 흐름인 '정신적 진화'에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children ①<u>allows</u> animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be ②<u>more</u> flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very ③<u>inefficient</u> migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood ④<u>facilitates</u> the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives ⑤<u>adaptability</u> in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 어린 시절(유년기)이 없으면 환경에 맞춰 학습할 기회가 없으므로, 태어날 때부터 정해진 생물학적 '하드웨어(본능/유전자)'에만 전적으로 의존해야 합니다. 이러한 본능에만 의존하게 되면 환경 변화에 대응하는 능력이 떨어지게 되므로, '더 유연한(more flexible)' 상태가 아니라 '덜 유연한(less flexible)' 상태가 됩니다. 따라서 ②번의 more는 less로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous (A)[literary / literate] example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the (B)[untimely / timely] visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden (C)[stability / disruptions] that have(has) had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.
questions.explanation: (A) 시인과 시에 관한 예시이므로 '문학적인'이라는 뜻의 literary가 적절합니다. (literate: 글을 읽고 쓸 줄 아는)(B) 흐름상 손님이 '때마침' 온 것이 아니라 영감을 방해하는 '시기 부적절한' 때에 온 것이므로 untimely가 적절합니다.(C) 업무 생산성을 늦추고 스트레스를 높이는 요인은 '안정성'이 아니라 '방해/중단'이므로 disruptions가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 문학적인 - 시기부적절한 - 안정성
② 문학적인 - 시기적절한 - 방해
③ 문학적인 - 시기부적절한 - 방해
④ 읽고쓸줄아는 - 시기부적절한 - 안정성
⑤ 읽고쓸줄아는 - 시기적절한 - 안정성

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. (A) When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. (B) For instance, they are able, to eat green acorns, while the red squirrels can only digest mature acorns. (C) Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. (D) Greys squirrels can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. (E) As a result, the red squirrels have come close to extinction in England.
questions.insertion_sentence: Grey squirrels had the edge because they can adapt their diet.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 회색 다람쥐가 식단을 조정할 수 있어 우위를 점했다는 내용입니다. (B) 뒤의 문장에서 'For instance(예를 들어)'로 시작하며 회색 다람쥐는 익지 않은 도토리를 먹을 수 있는 반면 붉은 다람쥐는 익은 것만 먹을 수 있다는 구체적인 식단 차이를 설명하고 있으므로, 일반적인 진술인 주어진 문장은 (B) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption.
ordered_passages: (A) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.
(B) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one.
(C) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
(D) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 미래 소비를 위해 저축하는 행동을 언급한 후, (B)에서 이 행동이 즉각적 보상보다 지연된 보상을 선호함을 보여준다고 설명합니다. (A)에서 미래 보상의 가치가 현재보다 커야 함을 언급하며 저축을 조기에 써버리는 예외 상황을 도입하고, (D)에서 크리스마스 선물을 위한 돈을 여름 휴가에 써버리는 구체적 예시를 듭니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 이를 의지의 박약으로 요약 설명하는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 brainwriting에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine all together the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually, before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ① 가장 초기 단계에서는 혼자서 별도로 아이디어를 내도록 모든 사람에게 요청한다.
② 개별적으로 생성된 아이디어를 모아 익명으로 그룹에 공유하고 독립적으로 판단하도록 한다.
③ 각자 평가한 후, 팀이 함께 모여 가장 유망한 옵션을 선택하고 선택된 아이디어를 각자 다듬는다.
④ 팀은 주목받지 못했을 가능성을 표면화시키고 발전시킬 수 있다.
⑤ 모든 생각과 의견을 반영할 수 있어서 집단 지성을 달성하는 데 어려움을 겪는 그룹에 효과적이다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서는 아이디어를 선택한 후에 '팀이 함께(all together)' 아이디어를 다듬는다(refine)고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 선택지에 제시된 '각자' 다듬는다는 설명은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As business shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
questions.summary_sentence: Although the shift from paper to digital business activities initially seemed environmentally (A)____________, digital practices can still significantly harm the environment due to the high energy consumption and carbon emissions from data centers (B)____________.
options: ① (A) favorable / (B) reliant on fossil fuels
③ (A) detrimental / (B) running on fossil fuels
④ (A) advantageous / (B) running on green energy
questions.explanation: 디지털 전환은 초기에는 환경에 유리한 것(favorable)으로 보였으나, 데이터 센터가 여전히 화석 연료(fossil fuels)에 의존하고 있어 환경에 해로울 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 긍정적 의미인 favorable이, (B)에는 전력 공급원을 나타내는 reliant on fossil fuels가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 유리한 / (B) 화석 연료에 의존하는
② (A) 이로운 / (B) 재생 가능 에너지를 사용하는
③ (A) 해로운 / (B) 화석 연료로 가동되는
④ (A) 유리한 / (B) 그린 에너지로 가동되는

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Most of the time, your actions show who you are. Your behavior reflects your self-perception, either consciously or unconsciously. (A) Research has revealed that when a person believes in a specific aspect of their identity, they are more inclined to act on that conviction. (B) People who described themselves as "voters," for instance, were more inclined to vote than those who merely stated that "voting" was something they wanted to do. (C) During the right thing is easy as mentioned in the above examples. (D) After all, when your conduct and identity are perfectly aligned, you are no longer seeking behavior change. (E) All you're doing is behaving like the kind of person you already think you are.
questions.insertion_sentence: Similarly, someone who accepts exercise as the part of their identity does not need to persuade themselves to train.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '마찬가지로, 운동을 자신의 정체성의 일부로 받아들이는 사람은 훈련을 위해 자신을 설득할 필요가 없다'는 내용입니다. 이는 정체성과 행동의 일치에 대한 추가적인 예시입니다. 앞부분에서 '투표자'라는 정체성을 가진 사람들의 예시가 나오고, (C) 뒤의 문장에서 '위의 예시들에서 언급된 것처럼 올바른 일을 하는 것은 쉽다'라고 하며 예시들을 종합하고 있으므로, 두 번째 예시인 주어진 문장은 (C) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practicing doing.
options: ① the effect of aging on brain volume
② the relationship between brain size and intelligence
③ the role of genetics in determining brain architecture
④ the influence of hunting patterns on brain development
⑤ the effect of concentrated life patterns on brain architecture
questions.explanation: 이 글은 집중된 주의와 반복적인 연습이 뇌의 물리적 구조를 재구성한다는 과학적 증거들을 제시하고 있습니다. 소리에 집중하는 동물, 바이올린 연주자, 택시 운전사 등의 사례를 통해 주의를 기울이는 곳과 연습하는 활동에 따라 관련 뇌 부위가 커지거나 발달한다는 점을 설명하고 있으므로, 주제는 '집중된 생활 양식이 뇌 구조에 미치는 영향'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 노화가 뇌 부피에 미치는 영향
② 뇌 크기와 지능 사이의 관계
③ 뇌 구조를 결정하는 데 있어 유전학의 역할
④ 사냥 패턴이 뇌 발달에 미치는 영향
⑤ 집중된 생활 양식이 뇌 구조에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 1. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of mammals ⓐ<u>is</u> that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally ─ they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. The ⓑ<u>registered</u> stimuli cannot be processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count ⓒ<u>them</u> as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems ⓓ<u>essential</u> to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement. In the drowsiness state the eyelids are half closed and eyes continue to process visual stimuli normally. Microsleeps, ⓔ<u>where</u> the animal falls quickly into deep sleep and then goes fast again into drowsiness, happen continuously under drowsiness.
questions.explanation: ⓒ는 앞서 언급된 'Perceptual disengagement(지각적 단절)'를 가리킵니다. 이는 단수 명사이므로 복수 대명사인 them이 아니라 단수 대명사인 it으로 받아야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 윗글을 읽고 이해한 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of mammals ⓐ<u>is</u> that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally ─ they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. The ⓑ<u>registered</u> stimuli cannot be processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count ⓒ<u>them</u> as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems ⓓ<u>essential</u> to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement. In the drowsiness state the eyelids are half closed and eyes continue to process visual stimuli normally. Microsleeps, ⓔ<u>where</u> the animal falls quickly into deep sleep and then goes fast again into drowsiness, happen continuously under drowsiness.
options: ① When an animal is sleeping, it is impossible for others to open its eye lids.
② Other senses except for a sense of vision would function well even when one sleeps deeply.
③ Because of perceptual disengagement, ones can protect themselves by perceiving their potential enemies.
④ People in the drowsiness state may be able to process visual information as usual.
⑤ Microsleeps are separated with the state of the drowsiness.
questions.explanation: 지문 후반부에 'In the drowsiness state the eyelids are half closed and eyes continue to process visual stimuli normally(졸음 상태에서 눈꺼풀은 반쯤 감기고 눈은 시각 자극을 정상적으로 계속 처리한다)'라고 명시되어 있으므로 ④번이 적절합니다. ① 자고 있는 동물의 눈꺼풀을 여는 것은 가능하지만 보지 못할 뿐입니다. ② 다른 감각 체계도 마찬가지로 정상 처리되지 않는다고 언급되었습니다. ③ 지각적 단절은 수면을 보호하는 기능을 하며, 외부 자극을 인식하지 못하게 합니다. ⑤ 미세 수면은 졸음 상태에서 계속 일어난다고 했으므로 분리된 것이 아닙니다.
options_translation: ① 동물이 잠을 자고 있을 때, 타인이 그 눈꺼풀을 여는 것은 불가능하다.
② 깊이 잠들었을 때 시각을 제외한 다른 감각들은 잘 작동할 것이다.
③ 지각적 단절 때문에, 사람들은 잠재적인 적을 인지함으로써 자신을 보호할 수 있다.
④ 졸음 상태에 있는 사람들은 평소처럼 시각 정보를 처리할 수 있을 것이다.
⑤ 미세 수면은 졸음 상태와 분리되어 있다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. _______________________________________________. Thus, in the case of tennis, 5-8-year-olds play with red ball on a 36×18 feet court, using lighter equipment. As they grow older and taller, being 8-9-year-olds, they play with a faster orange ball on a 60×21 court with a longer racket.
options: ① The variations, which should be gradually made, depend on how old they are
② The adaptations made in most sports have been considered inappropriate
③ It is expected that different goal and schedules are provided to different age groups
④ Progressive adaptations are made depending on different social needs of children
⑤ Progressive physical development does not necessarily lead to a high performance of a tennis player
questions.explanation: 빈칸 뒤의 내용에서 연령대(5-8세, 8-9세)에 따라 테니스 공의 색깔, 코트 크기, 라켓의 길이가 달라지는 예시가 제시됩니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 이러한 변화가 점진적으로 이루어지며 나이에 달려 있다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 점진적으로 이루어져야 하는 그 변화들은 그들이 몇 살인지에 달려 있다
② 대부분의 스포츠에서 이루어진 적응은 부적절하다고 간주되어 왔다

questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be __________________________. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ① published to promote its process
② constant regardless of the target animals
③ encouraged to minimize the negative results
④ adapted to meet the specific needs of the animal
⑤ conducted based on the recently released theories
