questions.question: 6. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 갓은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts ⓐ<u>know</u> as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether ⓑ<u>carrying</u> on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because ─ fueled by emotions ─ you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities ⓒ<u>what</u> hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There ⓓ<u>is</u> reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears ⓔ<u>during</u> the subconscious mind records your reactions.

questions.question: 12. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that ⓐ<u>orders</u> you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People ⓑ<u>hope</u> that you will say it. You become responsible. ⓒ<u>Failing</u> to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. ___________________________________________________________. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be ⓓ<u>different</u> norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ⓔsuitable if you were to thank someone for something too minor as holding a door open for you.
options: ① Criticism is sometimes good for your social life unless it hurts your relationships
② If you don't hold a door open for those following you, it may cause an accident leading to serious damage
③ It is more important to know that norms don't tend to change or can't change despite various cultural settings
④ Being familiar with the norms of your community is most important not to cause misunderstanding with others
⑤ Saying of appreciation is not necessarily required because the extent to which we express thanks is culturally different

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Also it has been shown that many experts are poor communicator of what they are doing. As their skills are automated, they tend to leave out essential information for novice, ending up with failing to convey the knowledge in a step-by-step manner so that only people who already know a lot about the topic could understand. For instance, you can ride a bicycle expertly, but are unable to explain how you can do this.
questions.summary_sentence: People who are skilled in a certain field tend to underestimate how (A)_____________ the task is, and possessing a high level of knowledge can be a(n) (B)_____________ when experts teach novices.

Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was not, in fact, totally (A)[true / wrong]. questions.question: 2. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

By the early 1990s, a growing number of scientists had concluded that many species would not ⓔ<u>fail</u> to keep up the rate of climate change.*dislocation: 소란, 소동

(B)에서는 'Similarly(이와 마찬가지로)'를 통해 도시의 사례를 뇌에 적용하여, 뇌의 활동도 단일 구역이 아닌 구성 요소들의 상호작용으로 발생함을 서술합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 도시로 물자를 실어 나르는 기차를 뇌의 신호를 전달하는 신경망에 비유하며 내용을 구체화하고 있으므로 정답은 (C)-(B)-(A) 순서인 ⑤번입니다.

questions.question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

(C) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
(D) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one.

(A)에서는 'Thus'를 통해 미래 보상의 할인된 가치가 현재 가치보다 높아야 함을 논리적으로 설명한 뒤 'However'를 통해 계획과는 다르게 성급하게 저축액을 사용하는 예외 상황을 도입합니다. (B)에서 그 구체적 예시(For example)로 선물 비용을 휴가비로 써버리는 '의지의 박약(weakness of will)' 사례를 들고, 마지막으로 (C)에서 이를 유혹에 굴복하는 행동으로 일반화하며 마무리하는 (D)-(A)-(B)-(C)의 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

④ How Different Countries Used 'On Foot' to Send Messages
⑤ Appropriate Speed: Messages Don't Necessarily Send Fast
questions.explanation: 본문은 스페인의 바스크인, 터키의 전령들, 중국, 인도의 무굴 제국, 그리고 잉카 제국 등이 말 대신 도보(on foot)를 이용해 어떻게 메시지를 효율적으로 전달했는지를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 동물 없는 통신의 어려움
② 가장 빠른 메시지 전달의 열쇠: 동물의 사용
③ 왕에게 메시지를 보내는 동안의 물리적 장애물
④ 여러 국가들이 메시지를 보내기 위해 '도보'를 활용한 방법
⑤ 적절한 속도: 메시지가 반드시 빨리 보내질 필요는 없다

questions.question: 15. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: In many countries, bad roads caused the postal service to depend ⓐ<u>heavy</u> on men on foot to deliver the mail. Running footmen sometimes doubled as messengers, but there were also runners who specialized in delivering messages. The Basques from northwest Spain ⓑ<u>were</u> famous running footmen and messengers who could "run like the wind." Turkish messengers ran 193km from Constantinople to Adrianople in 24 hours: even in the heat of summer, they were more rapid than men on horses over the route. Several other countries used relays of runners to deliver messages. One of the earliest was China and later the Mogul empire in India. With no horses available, the Inca empires in Central and South America excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were ⓒ<u>stationed</u> on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his provinces. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners ⓓ<u>who</u> watched the road in both directions. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca could relay messages 1,610 km in three or four days under good conditions. This method of delivering messages worked well, but used many runners. Many other countries, such as China and the Mogul empire in India, also delivered messages ⓔ<u>using</u> relays of runners.
options: ① In order to transport mail, the postal service had to rely mostly on men on foot.
② Turkish messengers were far quicker on the journey than men riding horses, even in the extreme summer heat.
③ In relaying messages on foot, the Mogul empire in India was among the first, followed by China.
④ Within visual range of each others, the Inca set up houses for Chasquis on an elevated landsacpe.
⑤ Although it worked successfully, message delivery on foot required a lot of men.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 "One of the earliest was China and later the Mogul empire in India"라고 명시되어 있습니다. 즉, 중국이 먼저였고 인도의 무굴 제국이 그 다음이었으므로, 인도의 무굴 제국이 먼저였다는 ③번의 설명은 본문 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 우편물을 운송하기 위해 우체국 서비스는 대부분 도보 전령들에게 의존해야 했다.
② 터키의 전령들은 극심한 여름 열기 속에서도 말을 탄 사람들보다 훨씬 빨랐다.
③ 도보로 메시지를 전달하는 데 있어 인도의 무굴 제국이 최초 중 하나였고 그 뒤를 중국이 이었다.
④ 서로의 시야 범위 내에, 잉카인들은 높은 지대에 Chasquis를 위한 집들을 지었다.
⑤ 성공적으로 작동했음에도 불구하고, 도보 메시지 전달은 많은 인원을 필요로 했다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳게 쓰인 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Occasionally, change ⓐ<u>happen</u> much more slowly. You most likely didn't notice any differences between the face you saw this morning and the face you saw a week or a month ago, or even the day before. We are aware, however, ⓑ<u>which</u> the face peering back at us through the glass is not, and cannot be, the same as it was ten minutes earlier. The evidence is in your photo album: When you compare your reflection in the mirror with a snapshot of yourself from five or ten years ago, you will ⓒ<u>obviously</u> notice differences in your face. If you were to live in a world free of mirrors for a year before ⓓ<u>seeing</u> your reflection, you could be shocked by the transformation. You might not identify the person ⓔ<u>stares</u> back at you in the mirror after a ten-year break without seeing yourself.
questions.explanation: ⓐ happen은 주어인 change가 단수이므로 happens가 되어야 합니다. ⓑ which는 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오며 aware의 목적어절을 이끄는 접속사 that이 되어야 합니다. ⓒ obviously는 동사 notice를 수식하는 부사로 적절합니다. ⓓ seeing은 전치사 before의 목적어인 동명사로 적절합니다. ⓔ stares는 선행사 the person을 수식하는 분사형태인 staring이나 관계대명사절인 who stares가 되어야 합니다. 따라서 옳은 것은 ⓒ, ⓓ입니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Experts underestimate task difficulty for novices. A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr. Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can ________________________________ _______________ for someone just starting off, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to place too low a value on the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even minimized how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session.
options: ① share experiences as an educational goal
② delay responses as a sign of expectation
③ not become insensitive to a tasks's difficulty
④ compete with other experts to decrease difficulties
⑤ show a lack of sympathy in how difficult a task is
questions.explanation: 지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)에 관한 내용으로, 전문가들은 초보자들이 특정 과업을 얼마나 어려워하는지를 과소평가한다는 것이 핵심입니다. 즉, 전문가들은 초보자가 느끼는 난이도에 대해 공감하지 못하는 모습을 보인다는 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 교육적 목표로서 경험을 공유할 수 있다
기대의 표시로서 응답을 지연시킬 수 있다
과업의 난이도에 대해 무뎌지지 않을 수 있다
난이도를 낮추기 위해 다른 전문가들과 경쟁할 수 있다
어떤 과업이 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 공감의 부족을 보일 수 있다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farm communities. An increased population was actually advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
options: ① Hunter-gathers benefited from population increases, not agriculture.
② Farmers rarely reproduced their offsprings because they took very little in the way of nutrition.
③ Agricultural gaps were caused by the educational differences between farmers and hunter-gathers.
④ Agriculture caused population growth by letting farmers live more secure lives than hunter-gathers.
⑤ More farmers than hunter-gathers succeeded in their own cultural aspects, which led to population expansion.
questions.explanation: 농경의 시작으로 정착 생활이 가능해지면서 수렵-채집 사회보다 출산 간격이 줄어들게 되었고, 이는 급격한 인구 증가로 이어졌으며, 늘어난 인구는 다시 농경 사회에 필요한 노동력을 제공했다는 것이 글의 핵심입니다. 따라서 농업이 정착 생활(안정적인 생활)을 가능하게 함으로써 인구 성장을 유발했다는 4번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 수렵-채집인들은 농업이 아닌 인구 증가로부터 혜택을 입었다.
농부들은 영양 섭취가 거의 없었기 때문에 자손을 거의 번식시키지 못했다.
농업의 격차는 농부와 수렵-채집인 사이의 교육적 차이로 인해 발생했다.
농업은 농부들이 수렵-채집인들보다 더 안정적인 삶을 살게 함으로써 인구 성장을 유발했다.
수렵-채집인보다 더 많은 농부들이 각자의 문화적 측면에서 성공하여 인구 확대로 이어졌다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.summary_sentence: Birds that are absent from childhood are (A)________ to adapt, while ones that have childhood experience can learn about their surroundings more (B)________.
questions.explanation: 본문은 유년기 없이 본능에만 의존해 이동하는 새들은 환경 변화에 잘 적응하지 못하고 비효율적인 경로를 고수하는 반면, 부모와 함께 긴 유년기를 보내며 학습하는 새들은 문화적 정보를 전달받아 더 효율적이고 유연하게 적응한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 유년기가 없는 새는 적응이 더 느리고(slower), 유년기 경험이 있는 새는 환경에 대해 더 자유롭게(freely) 배울 수 있다는 1번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 더 느린 / 자유롭게
② 더 빠른 / 융통성 없게
③ 더 쉬운 / 자유롭게
④ 어리석은 / 융통성 없게
⑤ 효율적인 / 쉽게

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. ⓐExamination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. ⓑIf this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. ⓒUnfortunately, due to the lack of suitable treatments for the epidemic, the population available for farming decreased. ⓓWhatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. ⓔThis period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."*remains: 유적, 유해 **epidemic: 전염병의
questions.explanation: 이 글은 수렵 채집 생활의 장점과 정착 농경 생활로의 전환 및 그로 인한 인구 밀도 증가와 문명의 발달을 설명하고 있습니다. 전염병에 대한 적절한 치료법 부족으로 농사 가능 인구가 감소했다는 내용인 ⓒ(옵션 3번 해당)는 전체적인 인류 발달 과정의 흐름에서 벗어난 지엽적인 내용입니다. 문제에서 정답 번호가 4번으로 표시되어 있으나, 흐름상 어색한 문장은 ⓒ(3번)입니다. (제공된 정답 4번은 ⓓ를 지칭하는 것으로 보이나, 맥락상 ⓒ가 가장 부적절합니다.)

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. ⓐWhat has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. ⓑAs a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. ⓒWhile professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. ⓓToday, there are various programs to help people with disabilities live socially compared to the past. ⓔThis situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 디지털 정보를 구축할 때 장애인의 접근성이 소외되고 있는 문제점과 이를 개선해야 할 필요성에 대해 다루고 있습니다. ⓓ(옵션 4번 해당)는 과거에 비해 장애인들의 사회적 생활을 돕는 다양한 프로그램이 있다는 내용으로, 디지털 정보의 설계 및 접근성이라는 글의 핵심 주제와는 거리가 멉니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. (A) Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. (B) When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. (C) The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. (D) Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. (E) As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
questions.insertion_sentence: Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 회색다람쥐가 더 조밀하게, 다양한 서식지에서 살 수 있어 숲이 파괴되었을 때 더 잘 생존한다는 내용입니다. 이는 회색다람쥐가 붉은다람쥐보다 생존에 유리한 추가적인 이유를 설명합니다. (D) 앞까지는 먹이 적응력에 대한 차이를 설명하고, 주어진 문장이 (E) 자리에 들어가 회색다람쥐의 우월한 생존 조건을 마무리 지은 후, 그 결과(As a result) 붉은다람쥐가 멸종 위기에 처했다는 결론으로 이어지는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 9. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption.
ordered_passages: (A) However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead.(B) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.(C) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one.
questions.explanation: 저축 행위와 그에 따르는 의지력의 문제를 설명하는 글입니다. 저축은 미래의 보상을 위해 현재의 쾌락을 포기하는 행위라는 정의(C)를 먼저 내리고, 그러나 계획과 달리 저축한 돈을 미리 써버리는 예외적인 상황(A)을 제시한 뒤, 이것이 즉각적인 쾌락의 유혹에 굴복하는 '의지의 박약' 사례임을 설명하는(B) 구성이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
options: ① The Only Weapon to Succeed in Battle
② Various Ways to Out-think Its Enemies
③ Tribal Conflicts and the Evolution of Modern Technology
④ The Evolution of Human Intelligence Through Tribal Conflict
⑤ The Way of Genes Being Passed on to Succeeding Generation
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 지능이 다른 부족과의 갈등과 경쟁 속에서 우위를 점하기 위해 진화해 왔다는 주장을 담고 있습니다. 상대보다 더 잘 생각하고 예측하는 능력이 생존과 승리에 필수적이었으며, 이러한 정신적 이점이 후세에 전달되었다는 내용이므로 ④ '부족 갈등을 통한 인간 지능의 진화'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 전투에서 성공하기 위한 유일한 무기
② 적들보다 한 수 앞서 생각하기 위한 다양한 방법들
③ 부족 갈등과 현대 기술의 진화
④ 부족 갈등을 통한 인간 지능의 진화
⑤ 후세로 전달되는 유전자의 방식

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.*cortex: (대뇌) 피질(皮質)**hippocampus: (대뇌 측두엽의) 해마
options: ① scientific evidence on the relationship of cortex and hippocampus
② descriptions of different areas in our brain
③ advantages of having special memory in playing violins
④ alterations in the brain's structure due to focused attention and practice.
⑤ fastness between animals with developed hearing and those with developed eyesight
questions.explanation: 글의 도입부와 결론부에서 공통적으로 '집중된 주의와 연습이 뇌의 물리적 구조를 재구성한다(reshape, changes)'고 명시하고 있습니다. 동물, 바이올린 연주자, 택시 기사의 사례를 통해 특정 영역을 많이 사용하면 그와 관련된 뇌 부위가 발달한다는 것을 보여주고 있으므로 주제는 ④ '집중된 주의와 연습에 따른 뇌 구조의 변화'입니다.
options_translation: ① 대뇌 피질과 해마의 관계에 대한 과학적 증거
우리 뇌의 서로 다른 영역들에 대한 묘사
③ 바이올린 연주 시 특별한 기억력을 갖는 것의 장점
④ 집중된 주의와 연습으로 인한 뇌 구조의 변화
⑤ 청각이 발달한 동물과 시각이 발달한 동물 간의 속도 차이

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.*cortex: (대뇌) 피질(皮質)**hippocampus: (대뇌 측두엽의) 해마
options: ① scientific evidence on the relationship of cortex and hippocampus
② descriptions of different areas in our brain
③ advantages of having special memory in playing violins
④ alterations in the brain's structure due to focused attention and practice.
⑤ fastness between animals with developed hearing and those with developed eyesight
questions.explanation: 원문 텍스트에는 밑줄이 표시되어 있지 않으나, 질문 12번의 선택지가 글의 내용을 요약하거나 제목을 묻는 형태로 구성되어 있습니다. 질문 11번의 주제 유형과 유사하게 구성되었으며, 본문은 '집중된 주의와 연습에 따른 뇌 구조의 물리적 변화'에 대해 설명하고 있으므로 ④번이 정답입니다. (참고: 문제의 지시문은 '어법상 어색한 것'이나 실제 선택지는 제목/주제 찾기 형식이므로 원문 오류로 판단되나, 내용상 ④가 가장 적합함)
options_translation: ① 피질과 해마의 관계에 대한 과학적 증거
② 우리 뇌의 서로 다른 영역들에 대한 묘사
③ 바이올린 연주 시 특별한 기억력을 갖는 것의 장점
④ 집중된 주의와 연습으로 인한 뇌 구조의 변화
⑤ 청각이 발달한 동물과 시각이 발달한 동물 사이의 빠름

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, ⓐ<u>spacing</u> their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about ⓑ<u>transporting</u> young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to ⓒ<u>shorten</u> their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in ⓓ<u>slow</u> population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an ⓔ<u>advantage</u> to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.explanation: 농경 사회가 정착하면서 출산 간격이 4년에서 2년으로 짧아졌고(shorten), 이는 여성 한 명당 더 많은 자녀를 가질 수 있게 되었음을 의미하므로, 인구 성장은 '느린(slow)' 것이 아니라 '빠른(rapid/fast)' 것이 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be ⓐ<u>less</u> flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with ⓑ<u>instructions</u> they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt ⓒ<u>easily</u>. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most ⓓ<u>efficient</u> migration routes. Childhood ⓔ<u>hinders</u> the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 유년기(childhood)가 있는 동물들은 환경에 대해 배우고 유연성을 가집니다. 따라서 유년기는 문화적 정보의 전달을 '방해하는(hinders)' 것이 아니라 '촉진하거나 가능하게 한다(allows/facilitates)'는 내용이 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making __________ - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had __________ over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
questions.explanation: 본문은 직원들에게 통제권과 주체성(sense of agency)을 부여하는 것이 생산성을 높인다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸에는 '결정권' 혹은 '권한'을 뜻하는 단어가 들어가야 하므로 authority가 가장 적절합니다. 첫 번째 빈칸은 'decision-making authority(의사 결정 권한)', 두 번째 빈칸은 'had authority over shifts(교대 근무에 대한 권한을 가졌다)'로 연결됩니다.
options_translation: ① 청중
② 권한
③ 사인
④ 저작권
⑤ 자동화

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also ___________________________________. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
options: ① increased the price of farm fields
② led farmers to use more fertilizer
③ disrupted the study of monoculture growth
④ attracted the attention of various unwanted intruders
⑤ made farmers distinguish between the amounts of fertilizer and water supplements.
questions.explanation: 농지에 영양분과 물을 풍부하게 공급하여 단일 작물 재배에 완벽한 환경을 만드는 과정에 대한 글입니다. 빈칸 이후 문장에서 이러한 환경이 주변의 잡초들에게 '호화 부동산(luxury real estate)'처럼 여겨진다고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 이러한 풍족한 조건이 원치 않는 침입자(잡초)들의 주의를 끌었다는 내용인 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 농지의 가격을 인상시켰다
② 농부들이 더 많은 비료를 사용하도록 유도했다
③ 단일 작물 재배 연구를 방해했다
④ 다양한 원치 않는 침입자들의 주의를 끌었다
⑤ 농부들이 비료와 수분 보충량 사이를 구분하게 만들었다

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 제목을 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
subjective_conditions: 1. 다음 글의 제목을 명사형으로 완성하시오.
2. 단어의 수가 7개 이상이어야 하며, 'confront'를 반드시 활용하여야 함.
questions.answer: importance of confronting hardship in one's life
questions.explanation: 이 글은 쉬운 길을 택하기백다 고난을 마주하고 극복함으로써 강함을 얻을 수 있다는 내용입니다. 조건에 맞게 '삶에서 고난에 맞서는 것의 설요성'을 명사구 형태로 왁성합니다. (7단어)

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① The environmental impact of digitization is minimal, and reducing paper usage is more important.
② Digitalization accelerates environmental destruction, so its use should be restricted as much as possible.
③ Companies should promptly transit to digital business operations to reduce paper waste.
④ Processing a lot of data in digital clouds and emails is more eco-friendly than using postal mail.
⑤ Digitization in business can be more harmful to environmental pollution in some cases.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 비즈니스의 디지털화가 종이 소비를 줄여 환경에 도움이 될 것이라는 일반적인 믿음과 달리, 데이터 센터 운영을 위한 화석 연료 사용과 전기 소모로 인해 발생하는 탄소 발자국이 오히려 환경에 더 해로울 수 있음을 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 디지털화의 환경적 영향은 미미하며 종이 사용을 줄이는 것이 더 중요하다.
② 디지털화는 환경 파괴를 가속화하므로 사용을 최대한 제한해야 한다.
③ 기업들은 종이 낭비를 줄이기 위해 즉각적으로 디지털 업무 운영으로 전환해야 한다.
④ 디지털 클라우드와 이메일로 많은 데이터를 처리하는 것은 우편을 이용하는 것보다 더 친환경적이다.
⑤ 비즈니스의 디지털화는 어떤 경우에 환경 오염에 더 해로울 수 있다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
options: ① efficient methods for cultivating crops
② impact of agriculture on population growth
③ relationship between birth rates and productivity
④ Difficulties of hunter-gatherers moving long distances
⑤ necessity of amounts of human labor in agricultural societies
questions.explanation: 이 글은 농경의 시작으로 사람들이 정착 생활을 하게 되면서 출산 간격이 짧아졌고, 그 결과 농경 사회의 인구가 급격히 증가하게 되었음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 '농업이 인구 성장에 미치는 영향'입니다.
options_translation: ① 작물 재배를 위한 효율적인 방법들
② 농업이 인구 성장에 미치는 영향
③ 출산율과 생산성 사이의 관계
④ 수렵 채집인이 장거리를 이동하는 데 겪는 어려움
⑤ 농업 사회에서 대량의 인간 노동력의 필요성

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
options: ① The grey squirrel from America competed with the native red squirrel for food and habitat.
② The grey squirrel had an advantage in competition because it was able to control its food consumption.
③ Red squirrels could only eat fully matured acorns as food.
④ Grey squirrels could live in diverse habitats, which led to deforestation.
⑤ Red squirrels almost became extinct in Britain in the end.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 회색 다람쥐는 산림지(woodland)가 파괴되었을 때 더 쉽게 살아남았다고 언급되어 있을 뿐, 회색 다람쥐의 다양한 서식지 거주가 산림 벌채(deforestation)를 초래했다는 내용은 없습니다.
options_translation: ① 미국에서 온 회색 다람쥐는 먹이와 서식지를 두고 토착 붉은 다람쥐와 경쟁했다.
② 회색 다람쥐는 식단 조절이 가능했기 때문에 경쟁에서 우위를 점했다.
③ 붉은 다람쥐는 먹이로 완전히 익은 도토리만 먹을 수 있었다.
④ 회색 다람쥐는 다양한 서식지에서 살 수 있었고, 이는 삼림 벌채로 이어졌다.
⑤ 붉은 다람쥐는 결국 영국에서 거의 멸종 위기에 처했다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process ⓐ<u>called</u> brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone ⓑ<u>to generate</u> ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them ⓒ<u>anonymously</u> among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then ⓓ<u>does</u> the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas ⓔ<u>bring</u> to the table and everyone's opinions and ideas are included in the discussion. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 절의 주어인 all ideas는 '테이블에 내놓아지는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 가져야 합니다. 따라서 능동형 bring이 아니라 수동태인 are brought로 수정되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be ⓐ<u>rigid</u>. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very ⓑ<u>inefficient</u> migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the ⓒ<u>shortest</u> childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood ⓓ<u>facilitates</u> the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives ⓔ<u>flexibility</u> in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 지문의 전체적인 흐름은 어린 시절(childhood)을 거치는 것이 환경에 대한 학습과 유연한 적응을 가능하게 하여 더 효율적인 경로를 갖게 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 부모와 함께 이동하며 학습하는 새들은 어린 시절이 '짧은' 것이 아니라 '긴(longest)' 새들일 때 가장 효율적인 이동 경로를 가질 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 각 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절하게 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a (A)[hospitable / hostile] enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more (B)[decisive / delusive] than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each (C)[succeeding / preceding] generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.explanation: (A) 적대적인 부접이 공격할 것을 예측하는 것이므로 hostile(적대적인)이 적절합니다.(B) 생존 경쟁에서 인간의 정신은 그 어떤 무기밴다 결정적인 무기가 되었으로 decisive(결정적인)가 적절합니다.(C) 이러한 이점이 다음 세대로 이어져 내려갔다는 내용이므로 succeeding(다음의, 계승하는)이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 적대적인 - 결정적인 - 이전의
② 환대하는 - 기만적인 - 이전의
③ 적대적인 - 결정적인 - 다음의
④ 환대하는 - 결정적인 - 이전의
⑤ 적대적인 - 기만적인 - 다음의

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly ____________________________________________. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
options: ① provided ideal conditions for the spread of infectious diseases
② led to an immediate effect on the distribution of population
③ resulted in a rapid growth of population concentration
④ ensured a stable supply of food for the hunter-gatherers
⑤ encouraged people to maintain their natural lifestyle
questions.explanation: 수렵 채집 생활이 건강과 식량 면에서 이점이 있었음에도 불구하고 인류가 정착 생활과 농업을 선택한 이유에 대한 글입니다. 빈칸 이후의 문장에서 이 시기가 마을과 도시의 성장으로 가는 길을 열었고 결국 정착된 '문명'으로 이어졌다고 설명하고 있으므로, 정착과 농업이 '인구 집중의 급격한 성장'을 결과했다는 내용이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 전염병 확산을 위한 이상적인 조건을 제공했다
② 인구 분포에 즉각적인 영향을 미쳤다
③ 인구 집중의 급격한 성장을 초래했다
④ 수렵 채집인들에게 안정적인 식량 공급을 보장했다
⑤ 사람들이 자연스러운 생활 방식을 유지하도록 권장했다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흤름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. ⓐThus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. ⓑHowever, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. ⓒFor example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. ⓓWeakness of will is also a major factor in the consumption of goods and services that are not necessary or beneficial. ⓔThat is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure arises.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 미뜘 소비륄 위해 저축하지변, 순간적인 유혹으로 인해 이를 조기에 소비하는 홄상에 대한 글입니다. ⓓ문장은 필와치 않거나 이롭지 않은 물건 소비에 의지 박약이 영향을 미친다는 내용으로, 저축한 돈을 계획과 다르게 미리 서버리는 전체 흤름과는 거리가 있습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes.
questions.summary_sentence: Giving employees the feeling that they can perform their tasks with (A)_____________ affected how much (B)_____________ they brought to their jobs, making them feel more responsible to handle their tasks.
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 스스로 결정할 수 있는 권한, 즉 자율성(autonomy)을 주는 것이 그들이 업무에 쏟는 집중력과 규율, 즉 자기 통제/자기 규율(self-discipline)에 긍정적인 영향을 미쳐 생산성을 높였다는 실험 결과를 요약한 문장입니다.
options_translation: ① 자율성 - 자기 규율
② 압박 - 자기 통제
③ 전략 - 남의 이목을 의식함
④ 타협 - 이기심
⑤ 효율성 - 자존감

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 모두 순서대로 사용하여 빈칸을 20 단어 이하의 문장으로 완성하시오. (필요시 어형변화 할 것)
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which ha sto finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that ____________ __________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 주어진 단어를 모두 순서대로 사용
20 단어 이하의 문장으로 완성
필요시 어형변화 할 것
questions.answer: the physical architecture of the brain is influenced by where we direct our attention and what we practice doing
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 집중된 주의가 뇌의 재구성을 이끈다는 과학적 증거들을 나열하고 있습니다. 동물의 청각/시각 센터, 바이올린 연주자의 피질, 택시 운전사의 해마 등의 사례는 뇌의 물리적 구조가 우리가 어디에 주의를 기울이고 무엇을 연습하는지에 의해 결정된다는 것을 보여줍니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '뇌의 물리적 구조는 우리가 주의를 기울이는 곳과 우리가 연습하는 것에 의해 영향을 받는다'는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. influence를 수동태인 is influenced로 변형하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
options: ① Brain is a total set of elements that operate independently.
② Knowing how brain works can help analyze the system of the city.
③ Cities and brains have many similarities and differences in many ways.
④ Components of the brain work white interacting, like the economy of a city.
⑤ In order to revitalize the city's economy, transportation must be developed.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 뇌의 작동 원리를 도시의 경제 시스템에 비유하여 설명하고 있습니다. 경제가 도시의 한 지점이 아닌 모든 요소들의 상호작용에서 발생하듯이, 뇌 또한 여러 부위가 고립되지 않고 서로 상호작용하며 신호를 처리함으로써 작동한다는 것이 핵심 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌는 독립적으로 작동하는 요소들의 전체 집합이다.
② 뇌가 어떻게 작동하는지 아는 것은 도시 시스템을 분석하는 데 도움을 줄 수 있다.
③ 도시와 뇌는 여러 방면에서 많은 유사점과 차이점을 가지고 있다.
④ 뇌의 구성 요소들은 도시의 경제처럼 상호작용하며 작동한다.
⑤ 도시 경제를 활성화하기 위해서는 교통 시스템이 발달해야 한다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. (A)_____________, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. (B)_____________, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
options: ⑤ For example / First of all
questions.explanation:
(A) 앞 문장은 특정한 정체성에 따라 행동한다는 일반적인 원리이며, 뒤에는 '투표자'라는 정체성을 가진 사람들의 구체적인 사례가 나오므로 'For example(예를 들어)'이 적절합니다.
(B) 행동과 정체성이 일치하면 더 이상의 의도적인 변화를 추구하지 않고 그대로 행동하게 된다는 결론으로 글을 마무리하고 있으므로, 'After all(결국)'이 논리적 흐름을 완성합니다.
options_translation: ① 또한 / 마침내
② 하지만 / 결국
③ 하지만 / 먼저
④ 예를 들어 / 결국
⑤ 예를 들어 / 먼저

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced ①<u>to be</u> the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers ②<u>become</u> much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer ③<u>has tripled</u> since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and ④<u>watering</u> our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields ⑤<u>loaded</u> with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.explanation: Because 접속사가 이끄는 부사절에서 'farm fields'가 주어이므로, 뒤에는 분사가 아닌 정동사가 필요합니다. 문맥상 현재의 상태를 나타내는 수동태 동사 형태가 되어야 하므로, loaded를 are loaded로 바꿔야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad. There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet _________________________________________________. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to mock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
options: ① if they recognize how to eat with various combinations of foods
② if they don't deliver a lot of nutrients enough that we should eat
③ unless people control their diet with appropriate amounts of food
④ because they supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we want
⑤ because adults can distinguish the differences between good and bad foods
questions.explanation: 글의 주제는 개별 음식의 좋고 나쁨이 아니라, 음식들의 '조합'이 건강한 식단을 결정한다는 것입니다. '좋은 음식'들로만 구성된 식단이라 하더라도, 우리 몸에 필요한 충분한 영양소를 골고루 공급하지 못한다면 결국 건강한 식단이 될 수 없다는 맥락이 성립해야 하므로 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 만약 그들이 다양한 음식 조합으로 먹는 법을 인식한다면
② 만약 그들이 우리가 섭취해야 할 만큼의 충분한 영양소를 전달하지 못한다면
③ 사람들이 적절한 음식 양으로 식단을 조절하지 않는 한
④ 그들이 우리가 원하는 충분히 다양한 영양소를 공급하기 때문에
⑤ 성인들이 좋은 음식과 나쁜 음식 사이의 차이를 구별할 수 있기 때문에

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests _____________ encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
questions.explanation: 고객이 구매할 수 있는 품목의 수량을 제한하는 전략이 오히려 판매량을 자극한다는 내용의 실험입니다. 실험 결과, 수량 제한이 없는 경우보다 제한이 있는(scarce condition) 경우에 평균 구매량이 더 높게 나타났으므로 빈칸에는 '희소함(rareness)'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 풍부함
② 빈도
③ 독창성
④ 희소함
⑤ 규모

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, ____________ ___________________________________________________________: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
options: ① The reasons why humans preferred not to grow crops and stayed mobile are well-known.
② It is obvious why humans did not transition to permanent settlements and agricultural practices.
③ There is a clear understanding of why humans avoided developing agriculture and domesticating animals.
④ It is evident why many humans chose to remain as hunter-gatherers instead of settling in permanent villages.
⑤ It is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals.
questions.explanation: 수렵 채집 생활이 건강하고 풍족했다는 가설이 사실이라면, 농경 생활이 훨씬 힘들고 전염병의 근원지가 되었음에도 불구하고 왜 많은 인간이 정착 생활과 농업을 선택했는지는 명확하지 않다는 논리가 이어져야 합니다. 따라서 '왜 그렇게 많은 인간이 정착하고 농업을 발전시켰는지가 명확하지 않다'는 내용의 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간이 작물 재배를 선호하지 않고 이동하며 살기를 선호한 이유는 잘 알려져 있다.
② 인간이 영구 정착지와 농경 관습으로 전환하지 않은 이유는 분명하다.
③ 인간이 농업 발달과 가축 사육을 피한 이유에 대해 명확한 이해가 있다.
④ 왜 많은 인간이 영구적인 마을에 정착하는 대신 수렵 채집인으로 남기로 선택했는지는 분명하다.
⑤ 왜 그렇게 많은 인간이 영구적인 마을에 정착하고 농업을 발전시키며, 작물을 재배하고 동물을 길들였는지는 명확하지 않다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of ________________________. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.explanation: 미래의 더 큰 보상을 위해 현재의 즐거움을 포기하기로 결심했음에도 불구하고, 눈앞의 유혹(여름 휴가 등) 때문에 저축해둔 돈을 미리 써버리는 행위는 자신의 결심을 지키지 못하는 '의지의 박약(weakness of will)'의 예시라고 할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 강한 의지
② 의지의 박약
③ 저축하려는 욕구
④ 저축의 원천
⑤ 미래에 대한 준비

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 각 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 39번]
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The (A)[weakening / strengthening] in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far (B)[more inefficient / less inefficient] than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are (C)[eliminated / retained].
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 나이가 들수록 호기심이 감소한다고 했으므로 'weakening'이 적절합니다. (B) 아기 뇌의 배선은 엉망(mess)이라고 했으므로 성인의 뇌보다 훨씬 'more inefficient(비효율적)'입니다. (C) 자주 사용하지 않는 신경 경로는 사라진다는 뇌의 가소성 원리에 따라 'eliminated'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 약화 - 더 비효율적인 - 유지되는
② 강화 - 더 비효율적인 - 유지되는
③ 약화 - 더 비효율적인 - 제거되는
④ 강화 - 덜 비효율적인 - 제거되는
⑤ 약화 - 덜 비효율적인 - 제거되는

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 6월 32번]
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstratin that focused attention leads to reshaping of the brian. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger ⓐ<u>auditory</u> centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are ⓑ<u>larger</u>. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and ⓒ<u>expansion</u> in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is ⓓ<u>vital</u> for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the ⓔ<u>mental</u> architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 요지는 우리가 어디에 주의를 기울이고 무엇을 연습하느냐에 따라 뇌의 '구조적/물리적' 변화가 일어난다는 것입니다. ⓔ의 mental(정신적인)은 뇌의 하드웨어적 구조 변화를 설명하는 문맥에서 physical 또는 structural과 같은 단어로 대체되는 것이 더 적절합니다. 하지만 지문 전체에서 뇌의 구조를 'physical architecture'라고 표현하는 것이 일반적입니다. (참고: 원문상으로는 physical architecture로 쓰이는 경우가 많으나, 여기서는 지문에 제시된 어휘들 중 ⓔ가 문맥상 구조적 변화를 강조하는 흐름에서 가장 어색할 수 있습니다. 다만, 주어진 지문에서 ⓔ가 mental로 쓰였을 때, 뇌의 물리적 구조를 뜻하는 physical이 오는 것이 과학적 증거를 나열한 앞부분과 더 잘 어울립니다.)

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 올바른 것만을 모두 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Sometimes the pace of change is ⓐ<u>unpredictable</u>. The face you saw reflected in your mirror this morning probably appeared ⓑ<u>similar</u> to the face you saw the day before - or a week or a month ago. Yet we know that the face that stares back at us from the glass is not the same, cannot be the same, as it was 10 minutes ago. The proof is in your photo album: Look at a photograph taken of yourself 5 or 10 years ago and you see clear ⓒ<u>inconsistency</u> between the face in the snapshot and the face in your mirror. If you lived in a world without mirrors for a year and then saw your reflection, you might be surprised by the ⓓ<u>uniformity</u>. After an interval of 10 years without seeing yourself, you might at first ⓔ<u>misjudge</u> the person peering from the mirror. Even something as basic as our own face changes from moment to moment.
questions.explanation: 얼굴의 변화는 매우 미세하여 매일 거울을 볼 때는 전날과 비슷하게(ⓑ similar) 보일 수 있습니다. 하지만 5년이나 10년 전 사진을 보면 현재의 얼굴과 명백한 불일치(ⓒ inconsistency)를 발견하게 됩니다. 따라서 10년 동안 거울을 보지 않다가 자신을 보게 되면 거울 속 인물을 처음에는 누구인지 잘못 판단(ⓔ misjudge)할 수도 있다는 맥락이 자연스럽습니다. ⓐ는 지문 문맥상 '매우 느린(far slower)'이 적절하며, ⓓ는 변화에 놀랄 것이므로 '변화(change)' 혹은 '차이'와 관련된 단어가 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. ⓐFarmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. ⓑSocieties that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. ⓒThis meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. ⓓThe increase in population can sometimes lead to severe inequality. ⓔAn increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 농경의 시작과 정착 생활이 출산 간격을 줄여 인구 증가를 가져왔으며, 이것이 노동력이 많이 필요한 농업 사회에 이점이 되었다는 흐름을 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓓ는 인구 증가가 초래할 수 있는 '심각한 불평등'을 언급하고 있어, 농경으로 인한 인구 증가의 원인과 이점을 다루는 전체적인 논지에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. (A) As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. (B) Professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users. (C) However, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. (D) This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 디지털 정보 보존을 위한 표준 개발에도 불구하고 '장애인의 필요는 방치되었다'는 역접의 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A) 바로 뒤 문장에서 '그 결과(As a result)' 소중한 디지털 자원들이 청각 및 시각 장애인들에게 무용지물이 되었다는 부정적인 결과가 서술되므로, 원인에 해당하는 장애인의 필요가 무시되었다는 내용인 주어진 문장은 (A) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Although technology has the potential to increase productivity, it can also have a negative impact on productivity. (A) For example, in many office environments workers sit at desks with computers and have access to the internet. (B) They are able to check their personal e-mails and use social media whenever they want to. (C) Introducing new technology can also have a negative impact on production when it causes a change to the production process or requires workers to learn a new system. (D) Learning to use new technology can be time consuming and stressful for workers and this can cause a decline in productivity. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: This can stop them from doing their work and make them less productive.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'This'는 앞 문장에서 언급된 '개인 이메일을 확인하고 소셜 미디어를 사용하는 것'을 지칭합니다. 이러한 사적인 행위가 업무를 방해하고 생산성을 떨어뜨린다는 내용이므로, 개인적 용무를 볼 수 있다는 내용이 끝나는 (C) 자리에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다. (C) 이후부터는 '새로운 기술 도입 자체'로 인한 부정적 영향에 대해 설명이 전환됩니다.

questions.question: 28. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village.
ordered_passages: (A) The development of agriculture changed work patterns. Early farmers could reap enough grain from each seed. Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided support for nonfarmers such as chieftains, village councils, and warriors.

(B) Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were seldom sufficient to support a full-time chief or village council.
(C) In return, the nonfarmers provided leadership and security for the farming population, enabling it to continue to increase food/energy yields and provide ever large surpluses.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 초기 수렵 채집 사회의 지도자(chief)를 언급합니다. (B)에서 '이러한 지도자들 대부분(Most of these leaders)'이 식량 부족으로 인해 직접 사냥을 해야 했음을 설명합니다. (A)에서는 농업의 발달로 '잉여 식량(surplus)'이 발생하여 비농업 종사자들을 부양할 수 있게 되었다는 변화를 설명합니다. (C)에서 '그 보답으로(In return)' 비농업 종사자들이 지도력과 보안을 제공했다는 선순환 구조를 설명하며 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
options: ① 도시 경제의 시스템을 정확히 파악하는 것이 필수적이다.
② 뇌와 도시는 모든 구성 요소의 상호작용을 통해 작동한다.
③ 도시마다 생산되고 운반되는 물자의 종류는 매우 다양하다.
④ 뇌의 기능은 특정 부분이 손상되어도 다른 부위가 대체한다.
⑤ 뇌의 작용에서 전기화학적 신호를 직접 관리하는 것이 중요하다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 뇌를 도시에 비유하여 설명하고 있습니다. 도시의 경제가 특정 장소에 국한되지 않고 상점, 은행, 상인, 고객 등 모든 구성 요소의 상호작용을 통해 탄생하는 것처럼, 뇌의 작용 또한 특정 지점이 아니라 뇌 전체의 신경망과 구성 요소들 간의 유기적인 상호작용을 통해 이루어진다는 내용이므로 ②번이 가장 적절한 요지입니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
options: ② the need to have a reliable friend
④ influence of advertising in capitalism
questions.explanation: 구매 후 고객의 반응을 파악하는 것은 재구매 여부와 타인에게의 추천 가능성을 결정짓는 핵심적인 요소입니다. 만족한 고객은 기업을 위해 자발적으로 일하는 '무보수 홍보대사'가 되며, 이는 광고보다 친구의 의견을 더 신뢰하는 소비자의 특성과 맞물려 강력한 효과를 냅니다. 따라서 지속적인 고객 만족 관리의 중요성을 강조하는 ③번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 무보수 홍보대사의 위험성
② 믿을 만한 친구를 사귈 필요성
③ 고객 만족의 중요성
④ 자본주의에서 광고의 영향력
⑤ 부정적인 마케팅 뒤에 숨겨진 심리

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad. There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
options: ① Don't Eat Too Much Fried Foods
② The Power of Vegetables: the Nutrients We Need
③ Is It Reasonable to Define Foods as Good or Bad?
④ The Dangers of Teenagers Eating Unhealthy Foods
⑤ The More We Eat Good Foods, the Healthier We Are
questions.explanation: 음식 자체를 단순히 '좋은 음식'과 '나쁜 음식'으로 이분법적으로 나누는 것은 실제 건강한 식단을 구성하는 원리와 맞지 않습니다. 개별 음식이 영양가가 높더라도 그것만 먹으면 불균형한 식단이 될 수 있고, 반대로 가끔 먹는 튀긴 음식은 전체적인 식단의 균형을 깨트리지 않기 때문입니다. 즉, 중요한 것은 음식의 '조합'이지 개별 음식의 라벨링이 아니라는 주제를 담은 ③번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 튀긴 음식을 너무 많이 먹지 마라
② 채소의 힘: 우리에게 필요한 영양소
③ 음식을 좋거나 나쁜 것으로 정의하는 것이 타당한가?
④ 건강하지 않은 음식을 먹는 청소년의 위험성
⑤ 좋은 음식을 많이 먹을수록 더 건강해진다

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, which then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly. As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you." If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler has been transmitted via our body. Strange as it may sound, this theory states that emotions arise from our bodies. For example, our mood can be improved by simply lifting up the corners of our mouth. If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, taking care not to let the pencil touch their lips (thus forcing the mouth into a smile-like shape), they judge cartoons funnier than if they have been asked to frown. The primacy of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase "I must be afraid, because I'm running."
options: ② When You're Afraid, Run Away!
③ The Tragic Life of Louis Armstrong
④ Body Languages That We Didn't Know
⑤ Physical Movements: Sources of Our Mood
questions.explanation: 이 글은 신체적인 움직임이나 표정이 감정에 영향을 미친다는 이론을 설명하고 있습니다. 다른 사람의 미소를 따라하면 행복해지거나, 연필을 입에 물어 미소 짓는 표정을 만들면 만화가 더 재밌게 느껴진다는 실험 사례를 통해 감정이 신체로부터 발생한다는 점을 강조합니다. 따라서 '신체적 움직임: 우리 기분의 원천'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 스스로 찌푸리게 만들지 마라
② 두려울 때는 도망쳐라!
③ 루이 암스트롱의 비극적인 삶
④ 우리가 몰랐던 보디랭귀지
⑤ 신체적 움직임: 우리 기분의 원천

questions.question: 6. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The above graph shows the share of forest area in total land area by region in 1990 and 2019. ①Africa's share of forest area in total land area was over 40% in both 1990 and 2019. ②The share of forest area in America was 21.4% in 1990, which was smaller than that in 2019. ③The share of forest area in Europe increased from 1990 to 2019 by less than 10 percentage points. ④In 2019, the share of forest area in Asia was the smallest among the five regions, less than half that in Europe in the same year. ⑤Asia showed the largest gap between 1990 and 2019 in terms of the share of forest area in total land area.
questions.explanation: 문장 ②에서 America의 1990년 산림 면적 비율이 2019년보다 더 작았다고 서술되어 있습니다. 하지만 실제 도표(23년 6월 25번 원문 도표 참고)를 확인하면 America의 산림 비율은 1990년(42.6%)에서 2019년(40.8%)으로 감소했으므로, 1990년의 수치가 2019년보다 컸습니다. 따라서 ②번이 옳지 않습니다. (본문의 21.4%라는 수치 자체도 도표 데이터와 어긋나게 변형되어 출제된 오류 또는 불일치 지점입니다.)

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Few people will be ①<u>surprised</u> to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted ②<u>that</u> a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is time pressure. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life ─ ③<u>which</u> led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as ④<u>be</u> more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor ⑤<u>when</u> they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
questions.explanation: ④이 포함된 문장에서 'left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as (being) more prone to heart disease'로 연결되어야 합니다. 'left(5형식 동사) + 목적어(the population) + 목적격 보어1(feeling...)'과 병렬 구조를 이루어 목적격 보어2가 와야 하므로, 동사원형 be가 아닌 현재분사 being 또는 형용사구가 와야 합니다. as well as 뒤에 분사구문 형태나 목적격 보어의 연장이 필요하기 때문에 be는 문법적으로 틀립니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe ⓐ<u>that</u> you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than ⓑ<u>those</u> who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing ⓒ<u>are</u> easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity ⓓ<u>perfectly</u> match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply ⓔ<u>acting</u> like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
questions.explanation: ⓒ 문장의 주어는 동명사구인 'Doing the right thing'입니다. 동명사구 주어는 단수 취급하므로 복수 동사인 are 대신 단수 동사인 is를 써야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for ⓐ<u>boosting</u> your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and ⓑ<u>deny</u> false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to ⓒ<u>match</u> that information to his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him ⓓ<u>impatient</u> in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more ⓔ<u>cooperative</u> to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.explanation: 자신을 똑똑하고 유능한 아이라고 생각하는 것은 문제 해결 과정에서 더 끈기 있게(persistent) 노력하도록 만들고 새로운 과제에 자신감을 갖게 할 것입니다. 따라서 '조급해하는'이라는 의미의 impatient는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive ⓐ<u>drudgery</u> of work, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have ⓑ<u>less</u>. Companies large and small have ⓒ<u>off-loaded</u> work onto the backs of consumers. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. With air travel, we're now expected to ⓓ<u>reject</u> our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to ⓔ<u>pack</u> our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
questions.explanation: 컴퓨터화된 사회에서 소비자가 직접 과거 직원들이 하던 일을 수행하게 되었다는 맥락이므로, 항공 예약과 체크인을 스스로 '거절(reject)'하는 것이 아니라 스스로 '수행(do/handle)'하게 되었다고 하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists say that having a disorderly room can indicate a disorganized mental state. One of the professional tidying experts says that the moment you start cleaning your room, you also start changing your life and gaining new perspective. When you clean your surroundings, ______________________________________. You can do more things efficiently and neatly. So, clean up your closets, organize your drawers, and arrange your things first, then peace of mind will follow.
options: ① the existing system is broken down
② positive and good atmosphere follows
③ you can undergo the physical limitations
④ the difficulties of the region are unsolved
⑤ the negative and useless feelings appear again
questions.explanation: 주변을 정리하는 것이 삶을 변화시키고 새로운 관점을 얻게 하며, 마음의 평화를 가져온다는 내용입니다. 따라서 주변을 청소할 때 긍정적이고 좋은 분위기가 따른다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기존의 시스템이 무너진다
② 긍정적이고 좋은 분위기가 뒤따른다
③ 당신은 신체적 한계를 겪을 수 있다
④ 그 지역의 어려움들이 해결되지 않는다
⑤ 부정적이고 쓸모없는 감정들이 다시 나타난다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The decline in curiosity can be traced in the ___________________________________. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.
options: ③ cultural uniformity and social pressure
④ sudden appearance of artificial intelligence
⑤ development of the brain through childhood
questions.explanation: 지문은 어린 시절에서 성인으로 성장함에 따라 뇌의 신경 연결망이 정리되고 굳어지면서 호기심이 감소하는 과정을 뇌의 발달 과정과 연결하여 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '어린 시절을 통한 뇌의 발달'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 감소된 뇌 효율성
② 비디오 매체의 대중화
③ 문화적 획일성과 사회적 압박
④ 인공지능의 갑작스러운 등장
⑤ 어린 시절을 통한 뇌의 발달

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. Although it may seem sensible, having two separate calendars for work and personal life can lead to distractions. To check if something is missing, you will find yourself checking your to-do lists multiple times. Instead, ___________________________ ___________________. It doesn't matter if you use digital or paper media. It's okay to keep your professional and personal tasks in one place. This will give you a good idea of how time is divided between work and home. This will allow you to make informed decisions about which tasks are most important.
options: ① find what's right for you
② change from paper to digital media
③ write down your to-do lists in detail
④ organize all of your tasks in one place
⑤ use more different ways to encourage your task
questions.explanation: 업무용과 개인용 달력을 분리해 쓰는 것보다 하나로 통합하여 관리하는 것이 시간 배분을 파악하고 중요한 결정을 내리는 데 도움이 된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '모든 일을 한 곳에 정리하라'는 내용이 빈칸에 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신에게 맞는 것을 찾아라
② 종이에서 디지털 매체로 바꿔라
③ 할 일 목록을 상세히 적어라
④ 당신의 모든 업무를 한 곳에 정리하라
⑤ 당신의 과업을 격려하기 위해 더 다양한 방법들을 사용하라

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Up until about 6,000 years ago, most people were farmers. Many lived in different places throughout the year, hunting for food or moving their livestock to areas with enough food. There was no need to tell the time because life depended on natural cycles, such as the changing seasons or sunrise and sunset. Gradually more people started to live in larger settlements, and some needed to tell the time. For example, priests wanted to know when to carry out religious ceremonies. This was when people first invented clocks - devices that show, measure, and keep track of passing time. Clocks have been important ever since. Today, clocks are used for important things such as setting busy airport timetables - if the time is incorrect, aeroplanes might crash into each other when taking off or landing!
options: ① 6000년 전까지 사람들은 자연적 주기에 삶이 달려있었기 때문에 시간을 알 필요가 없었다.
② 더 많은 사람들이 정착지에 살며 어떤 사람들은 시간을 알 필요가 있었다.
③ 시계는 흐르는 시간을 보여주고, 측정하고, 추적하는 장치이다.
④ 종교적 행사를 수행하는 성직자는 시간을 알 필요가 없었다.
⑤ 오늘날, 시계는 공항 시간표 설정과 같은 중요한 일에 사용된다.
