questions.explanation: 본문에서 성직자(priests)는 종교적 의식을 언제 수행해야 할지 알기 위해 시간을 알 필요가 있었다고 언급되어 있으므로(priests wanted to know when to carry out religious ceremonies), ④번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, which is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way that production could be made more efficient, known as the "division of labor." (A) Making most manufactured goods involves several different processes using different skills. (B) Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished. (C) One worker could do all these tasks, and make 20 pins in a day. (D) Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. (E) Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day ─ a huge increase in productivity from the 200 they would have produced before.
questions.insertion_sentence: But this work can be divided into its separate processes, with a number of workers each performing one task.
questions.explanation: (C) 문장에서는 한 명의 노동자가 모든 작업을 수행하여 하루에 20개의 핀을 만드는 상황을 설명합니다. 주어진 문장 '하지만 이 작업은 분리된 공정들로 나뉠 수 있고, 많은 노동자들이 각각 한 가지 작업을 수행한다'는 내용이 뒤에 오는 '각 노동자가 한 가지 일에 전문화되어 훨씬 더 빨리 일할 수 있다'는 내용(D)과 연결되는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. ⓐDuring the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. ⓑSome people insist that the development of machines led to improving productivity in agriculture. ⓒWorld usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. ⓓUnfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. ⓔBecause farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 농경지에서 단일 재배를 위해 비료와 관개 시설을 통해 최적의 환경을 만드는 과정과 그로 인해 잡초와 같은 원치 않는 식물들이 모여들게 된다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. ⓑ의 '기계의 발달이 농업 생산성을 향상시켰다'는 주장은 글의 주된 흐름인 '양분 공급과 그에 따른 부작용(잡초)'과는 거리가 멉니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show that you care. If you notice someone who is lonely, you could go and sit with them. ⓐIf you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. ⓑIf you feel you have a problem with your social life, you need to try to have an opportunity for professional development. ⓒA person's happiness comes from attention. ⓓThere are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. ⓔEven if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 타인에게 관심을 기울이고 작은 친절을 베푸는 것이 큰 도움이 된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ⓑ의 '전문적 발전을 위한 기회를 가져야 한다'는 내용은 개인의 경력 개발에 관한 것으로, 타인을 돕고 관심을 보여주는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 30번]
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption.
ordered_passages: (A) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one.

(B) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.

(C) However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 많은 동물과 인간이 미래를 위해 저축한다고 언급합니다. (A)에서 이러한 행위(저축)가 지연된 보상을 선호하는 것임을 설명합니다. (C)에서는 'However'를 사용하여 계획대로 기다리지 못하고 조기에 저축을 사용해버리는 반대 상황과 예시를 제시합니다. (B)에서 (C)와 같은 경우를 '의지의 박약'으로 정의하며 내용을 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 34번]
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales.
ordered_passages: (A) This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.

(B) The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average.

(C) Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents.
questions.explanation: 구매 수량 제한이 판매를 늘린다는 주제가 제시된 후, (C)에서 이를 검증하기 위해 Brian Wansink 교수가 진행한 실험 설계를 소개합니다. (B)에서는 그 실험의 구체적인 조건(무제한 vs 4개/12개 제한)과 그에 따른 결과(평균 구매 수량 증가)를 기술합니다. (A)에서 이 결과가 희소성이 판매를 촉진함을 시사하며, 실제 마트에서 진행된 실험이라 신뢰도가 높음을 강조하며 결론을 맺습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 23번]
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
questions.summary_sentence: According to Lake Wobegon effect, most people tend to (A)_____________ their achievements and capabilities compared to (B)__________________________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 사람들이 자신을 실제보다 더 지능적이고 유능하다고 믿는 '레이크 워비건 효과(Lake Wobegon effect)'를 설명하고 있습니다. 대다수의 대중이 자신을 평균적인 사람보다 더 낫다고 생각하며, 고등학생들도 리더십 등에서 자신을 평균 이상으로 평가한다는 통계를 제시합니다. 따라서 사람들은 평범한 사람들(ordinary people)에 비해 자신의 능력과 성취를 과대평가(overestimate)한다는 요약이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 과대평가하다 / 평범한 사람들
② 과대평가하다 / 최고 전문가들
③ 과소평가하다 / 평범한 사람들
④ 과소평가하다 / 뛰어난 개인들
⑤ 무시하다 / 최고 전문가들

questions.question: 23. 윗글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. (A) Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were (가)[sufficient / insufficient] to support a full-time chief or village council. (B) The development of agriculture changed work patterns. (C) Early farmers could reap 3-10 kg of grain from each 1 kg of seed planted. (D) Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and offered support for those who are not farmers such as chieftains, village councils, men who practice medicine, priests, and warriors. (E)With improved technology and favorable conditions, agriculture produced consistent surpluses of the basic necessities, and population groups had (나)[decreased / increased]. These groups concentrated in towns and cities, and human tasks specialized further. Specialists such as carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their skills and became more efficient in their use of time and energy. The goods and services they provided brought about an improved quality of life, a higher standard of living, and, for most societies, increased (다)[instability / stability].
questions.insertion_sentence: In return, the nonfarmers provided leadership and security for the farming population, enabling it to continue to increase food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그에 대한 보답으로 비농민들이 농민 인구에게 지도력과 안보를 제공했다'는 내용입니다. (D) 문장에서 농민들이 생산한 잉여 식량이 비농민들(추장, 위원회, 전사 등)을 지원했다는 내용이 나온 후, 그 보답으로 비농민들이 수행한 역할을 설명하는 것이 논리적으로 적절하므로 (E) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글에서 괄호 (가), (나), (다)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. (A) Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were (가)[sufficient / insufficient] to support a full-time chief or village council. (B) The development of agriculture changed work patterns. (C) Early farmers could reap 3-10 kg of grain from each 1 kg of seed planted. (D) Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and offered support for those who are not farmers such as chieftains, village councils, men who practice medicine, priests, and warriors. (E)With improved technology and favorable conditions, agriculture produced consistent surpluses of the basic necessities, and population groups had (나)[decreased / increased]. These groups concentrated in towns and cities, and human tasks specialized further. Specialists such as carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their skills and became more efficient in their use of time and energy. The goods and services they provided brought about an improved quality of life, a higher standard of living, and, for most societies, increased (다)[instability / stability].
questions.explanation: (가) 초기 수렵 채집 사회는 식량이 '불충분(insufficient)'하여 지도자도 사냥에 참여해야 했습니다. (나) 농업 기술 발달로 인구 집단이 '증가(increased)'했습니다. (다) 분업과 기술 발달로 삶의 질이 향상되고 사회적 '안정(stability)'이 증가했습니다.
options_translation: ① 불충분한 / 증가했다 / 안정
② 충분한 / 감소했다 / 불안정
③ 불충분한 / 감소했다 / 불안정
④ 충분한 / 증가했다 / 안정
⑤ 불충분한 / 증가했다 / 불안정

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Sometimes the pace of change is far slower. The face you saw reflected in your mirror this morning probably appeared no different from the face you saw the day before - or a week or a month ago. Yet we know that the face that stares back at us from the glass is not the same, cannot be the same, as it was 10 minutes ago. The proof is in your photo album: Look at a photograph taken of yourself 5 or 10 years ago and you see clear differences between the face in the snapshot and the face in your mirror. If you lived in a world without mirrors for a year and then saw your reflection, you might be surprised by the change. After an interval of 10 years without seeing yourself, you might not at first recognize the person peering from the mirror. ________________________________________ ______________.
subjective_conditions: 1. moment, basic, face, change를 포함하여 문장을 완성하시오. (필요시 어형 변형 가능)
2. as ~ as 원급 비교구문을 사용하여 완성하시오.
3. 8단어 이상의 완전한 문장이 되도록 작성하시오.
questions.answer: Even something as basic as our own face changes from moment to moment
questions.explanation: 지문은 거울 속 우리 얼굴이 매 순간 변하고 있다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 조건에 따라 'as basic as' 원급 비교를 사용하여 '우리의 얼굴만큼 기본적인 것조차도 매 순간 변한다'는 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility ____ ___________________________________________________________. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped increase sales.
subjective_conditions: 1. adapt, goods, promote를 포함하여 문장을 완성하시오. (필요시 어형 변형 가능)
2. in ~ing 구문을 사용하여 10단어 이상으로 작성하시오.
questions.answer: in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted
questions.explanation: 광고주들이 자신들이 홍보하는 제품의 시장 상황에 맞춰 그들의 주장을 조정하는 능력을 보여주었다는 내용이 빈칸에 적절합니다. 'in ~ing' 구문과 'adapt A to B' 구조를 활용하여 영작합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood ______________________________________.
options: ① is the time to prepare independence from parents
② provides insight to analyze geographical information
③ gives the chance to apply what animals are gifted with
④ should be spent overcoming innate weaknesses
⑤ helps adapt to the ever-changing surroundings
questions.explanation: 어린 시절이 길고 부모로부터 배우는 과정을 거치는 동물(새)들은 유전적인 정보(hardware)에만 의존하는 동물보다 변화하는 환경(호수가 마르거나 기후가 변하는 등)에 더 유연하게 적응하고 효율적인 이동 경로를 가질 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 어린 시절은 변화하는 환경에 적응하도록 돕는다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 부모로부터 독립을 준비하는 시간이다
② 지리적 정보를 분석하는 통찰력을 제공한다
③ 동물이 타고난 자질을 적용할 기회를 제공한다
④ 타고난 약점을 극복하며 보내야 하는 시간이다
⑤ 늘 변화하는 주변 환경에 적응하는 것을 돕는다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained ⓐ<u>neglected</u> for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources ⓑ<u>are</u> useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty ⓒ<u>distinguishing</u> particular colors. Professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design ⓓ<u>has</u> made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users. But some scholars creating digital projects all too often ⓔ<u>failing</u> to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ⓕ<u>ensure</u> that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.explanation: ⓓ의 주어는 Professionals(복수)이므로 have로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓔ가 속한 문장의 본동사가 없으므로 failing을 fail로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓕ는 분사구문 자리로 ensurining으로 바꾸거나, making design decisions와 병렬 구조를 이루려면 ensuring 또는 context에 맞춰 적절한 분사 형태 혹은 접속사를 동반한 절로 보아야 하나, 문맥상 결과나 동시동작의 분사구문인 ensuring이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs.
ordered_passages: (A) Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.(B) They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same.(C) One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 직원들에게 주체성(통제권)을 주는 것이 에너지와 집중력을 높인다는 주장을 제시합니다. (C)에서 이에 대한 예시로 2010년 오하이오의 제조 공장 연구를 도입합니다. (B)에서 그 연구의 구체적인 내용(스스로 유니폼 디자인, 근무 시간대 권한 등)을 설명하고, (A)에서 그 결과(생산성 20% 향상)를 제시하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
options: ① to advertise the famous art digital project
② to request the installation of the accommodation for the disabled
③ to introduce the digital projects that the disabled can participate in
④ to explain the inconvenience that the disabled can commonly experience
⑤ to emphasize the importance of accepting demands of the disabled in the digital projects
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장에서 '최종 제품이 비장애인뿐만 아니라 장애인의 요구도 충족하도록 보장해야 한다'고 명시하며, 디지털 프로젝트 설계 시 장애인의 요구를 고려할 것을 강조하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 유명한 예술 디지털 프로젝트를 광고하기 위해
② 장애인을 위한 편의 시설 설치를 요청하기 위해
③ 장애인이 참여할 수 있는 디지털 프로젝트를 소개하기 위해
④ 장애인이 흔히 겪을 수 있는 불편함을 설명하기 위해
⑤ 디지털 프로젝트에서 장애인의 요구를 수용하는 것의 중요성을 강조하기 위해

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① Are Digital Businesses Really Beneficial to the Environment?
② Differences Between Digital Archiving and Paper Storage
③ Efforts to Decrease Carbon Emissions from Data Centers
④ Why Fossil Fuels are Still Main Sources of Electricity
⑤ Effective Ways to Reduce Paper Waste in Modern Offices
questions.explanation: 흔히 디지털 업무 방식이 환경에 덜 해로울 것이라 생각하지만, 실제로는 데이터 센터 운영을 위한 화석 연료 사용, 전력 소비, 이메일 전송에 따른 탄소 배출 등 디지털 활동 역시 환경을 위협한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 디지털 비즈니스가 정말로 환경에 유익한지 의문을 제기하는 ①번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 디지털 비즈니스는 정말로 환경에 유익한가?
② 디지털 아카이빙과 종이 저장의 차이점들
③ 데이터 센터로부터의 탄소 배출을 줄이기 위한 노력들
④ 화석 연료가 여전히 전력의 주된 원천인 이유
⑤ 현대 사무실에서 종이 낭비를 줄이는 효과적인 방법들

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed an essential ⓐ<u>drawbacks</u>. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when an ⓑ<u>antagonistic</u> enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon even more ⓒ<u>crucial</u> than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its ⓓ<u>proponents</u> was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the ⓔ<u>ascendants</u> of the winners.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 적을 능가하는 능력은 '결점(drawbacks)'이 아니라 '이점(advantage)'입니다. ⓓ 적을 능가해야 하므로 '지지자(proponents)'가 아니라 '적/상대(opponents)'가 적절합니다. ⓔ 우리는 승리자의 '조상(ascendants)'이 아니라 '후손(descendants)'입니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have (A)[mimic / authentic] decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were (B)[assigned / disinclined] to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant (C)[elevated / aggravated] by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.*radically: 급격하게 **shift: (근무) 교대
questions.explanation: (A) 직원들이 통제권을 갖는다는 것은 '진정한(authentic)' 의사결정 권한을 갖는다는 것을 의미합니다. (B) 연구 사례에서 노동자들은 결정을 내리도록 '배정/부여(assigned)'되었습니다. (C) 자율성이 부여된 결과 생산성이 20% '상승(elevated)'했습니다.
options_translation: ① 흉내내는 - 배정된 - 상승한
② 흉내내는 - 배정된 - 악화된
③ 흉내내는 - 내키지 않는 - 악화된
④ 진정한 - 배정된 - 상승한
⑤ 진정한 - 내키지 않는 - 악화된

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. ⓐPsychologists say that having a disorderly room can indicate a disorganized mental state. ⓑOne of the professional tidying experts says that the moment you start cleaning your room, you also start changing your life and gaining new perspective. ⓒYou should bear in mind that you wear earrings while cleaning, so put the precious items in the place where you can find them easily. ⓓWhen you clean your surroundings, positive and good atmosphere follows. You can do more things efficiently and neatly. ⓔSo, clean up your closets, organize your drawers, and arrange your things first, then peace of mind will follow.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 '방 청소와 주변 정돈이 심리적 상태와 삶에 미치는 긍정적인 영향'입니다. 하지만 ⓒ번 문장은 청소할 때 귀걸이를 착용하고 있다는 사실을 명심하여 귀중품을 잘 보관하라는 지엽적인 조언으로, 전체적인 흐름인 '청소를 통한 정신적 변화'와는 거리가 멉니다.

questions.question: 17. 제시된 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 29번]
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it.
ordered_passages: (A) Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases.

(B) If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root.

(C) Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.explanation: 도입부에서 수렵 채집 생활이 권장될 만한 점이 많았음을 언급한 뒤, (A)에서 조상들이 풍족한 음식을 즐기고 질병이 적었다는 구체적인 연구 결과를 제시합니다. 이어지는 (B)에서는 (A)의 내용이 사실이라면 왜 더 힘들고 전염병이 창궐하는 농경 생활로 전환했는지에 대한 의문을 제기하며, 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 변화가 결과적으로 인구 밀도 증가와 문명의 발달로 이어졌음을 설명하는 (A)-(B)-(C)의 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 제시된 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 30번]
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one.
ordered_passages: (A) For instance, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will.
(B) In short, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but when temptation for immediate delight occurs, then act differently.

(C) Therefore, the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.
questions.explanation: 도입부에서 미래 소비를 위해 저축하는 행위와 지연된 보상을 선호하는 특성을 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 미래 보상의 가치가 현재보다 커야 한다는 논리적 결론과 함께 저축한 돈을 예정보다 일찍 써버리는 예외적인 상황을 제시합니다. 이어지는 (A)에서 크리스마스 선물을 위한 돈을 여름 휴가에 사용해버리는 구체적인 사례를 '의지의 박약(weakness of will)'의 예로 들며, 마지막으로 (B)에서 유혹에 의해 결심과 다르게 행동하는 상황을 요약하는 (C)-(A)-(B)의 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 6월 21번]
questions.passage: (A) The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. (B) This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. (C) During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. (D) World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. (E) Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.insertion_sentence: Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 언급된 'luxurious conditions(호화로운 조건)'는 (D) 문장에서 설명한 비료 사용량의 급발적인 증가와 관개 시설의 확충으로 영양분과 물이 풍부해진 농장의 상태를 가리킵니다. 또한 'agricultural undesirables(농업적으로 바람직하지 않은 것들)'는 (E) 문장에서 말하는 잡초(weeds)를 의미하므로, 제시문은 농장의 풍족한 환경과 잡초의 침입을 연결해주는 (E) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 어법상 어색한 것 세 개를 골라 주어진 작성 조건에 맞게 바르게 고치시오. [3.3점]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people ⓐ<u>stay</u> in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, ⓑ<u>spacing</u> their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could ⓒ<u>live in</u> the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies ⓓ<u>where</u> settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn ⓔ<u>resulted in</u> rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming ⓕ<u>requiring</u> large amounts of human labor.*counterpart: (대응 관계에 있는) 상대
questions.explanation: ⓐ forced는 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취하므로 stay를 to stay로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓓ 뒤에 바로 동사(settled down)가 나오므로 주격 관계대명사인 that 또는 which가 필요하며, 장소의 선행사라고 해서 무조건 where를 쓸 수 없습니다. ⓕ because절 안에서 farming이 주어이므로 문장의 술어 동사가 필요합니다. 시제에 맞게 requiring을 과거형 동사인 required로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하려고 한다. 주어진 작성 조건에 맞게 작성하시오. [3.1점]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people ⓐ<u>stay</u> in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, ⓑ<u>spacing</u> their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could ⓒ<u>live in</u> the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies ⓓ<u>where</u> settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn ⓔ<u>resulted in</u> rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming ⓕ<u>requiring</u> large amounts of human labor.*counterpart: (대응 관계에 있는) 상대
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어들만 한 번씩 사용하고 올바른 순서로 배열하여, 요약문을 작성하시오.
주어진 단어들을 변형하지 말 것.
questions.answer: Unlike hunting, agriculture made it possible to settle in a town and consequently, the population increased.
questions.explanation: 본문은 수렵 채집과 달리 농경이 정착 생활을 가능하게 하여 인구 증가를 가져왔다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 주어진 단어들을 조합하여 '수렵과 달리 농경은 마을에 정착하는 것을 가능하게 만들었고 그 결과 인구가 증가했다'는 의미의 문장을 완성합니다. (전치사 Unlike + 명사 hunting, 주어 agriculture + 동사 made + 가목적어 it + 보어 possible + 진목적어 to settle... 구조)

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 작성 조건에 맞게 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말을 작성하시오.
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only (A)________________________________. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.*anonymously: 익명으로 **surface: 드러내다
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어들만 한 번씩 사용하고 올바른 순서로 배열하여 빈칸 (A)를 완성하시오.  (the team / to choose / options / gather / do / favorable / then / the most)
주어진 단어들 중 필요시 올바르게 어형을 변화시킬 것.
도치 구문을 사용하여 작성할 것.
questions.answer: then does the team gather to choose the most favorable options
questions.explanation: 브레인라이팅 과정에서 개인별 평가가 끝난 '후에야 비로소' 팀이 모인다는 맥락입니다. 'Only then'이라는 부정어구를 문두에 두어 도치 구문을 만들어야 합니다. Only then 뒤에 의문문 어순인 '조동사(does) + 주어(the team) + 동사원형(gather)'을 사용하고, 목적을 나타내는 'to choose'와 목적어 'the most favorable options'를 연결합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
options: ① Crystals are basically composed of rocks.
② The shapes that crystals can take are known as habits.
③ Crystals generally form when liquids undergo cooling.
④ Imperfect crystal shapes can be formed under certain conditions.
⑤ Proper conditions for ideal crystal shapes entail a slow, steady environment.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 'all rocks are made up of crystals(모든 암석은 결정으로 이루어져 있다)'고 했으므로, 결정이 암석으로 구성된 것이 아니라 암석이 결정으로 구성된 것입니다. 따라서 ①번은 인과관계가 반대로 설명되어 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 결정은 기본적으로 암석으로 구성되어 있다.
② 결정이 가질 수 있는 모양은 '습성(habits)'으로 알려져 있다.
③ 결정은 일반적으로 액체가 냉각될 때 형성된다.
④ 불완전한 결정 모양은 특정 조건 하에서 형성될 수 있다.
⑤ 이상적인 결정 모양을 위한 적절한 조건은 느리고 안정적인 환경을 수반한다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것 두 개를 고르면?
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can ⓐ<u>be labeled</u> as either good or bad. There are, however, ⓑ<u>combinations</u> of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. ⓒ<u>Despite</u> all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who ⓓ<u>occasionally</u> eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. The odd fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks ⓔ<u>have</u> a bad diet.
questions.explanation: ⓒ: 뒤에 'all these foods are nutrient-dense'라는 주어+동사의 절이 오고 있으므로 전치사인 Despite 대신 접속사인 Although나 Though가 와야 합니다. ⓔ: 문장의 주어는 'the person'으로 단수이므로 동사도 단수형인 has가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
options: ① You should choose transportation with safety as the top priority.
② You should rely on rational facts when making decisions involving risks.
③ You should try to minimize the anxiety you feel while going about your daily life.
④ You must always be prepared for the dangerous situations beyond your control.
⑤ You need to learn several solutions to overcome negative emotions including anxiety.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 부분에서 'make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings'라고 언급하며, 위험이 따르는 결정을 할 때 감정이 아닌 사실에 기반할 것을 강조하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 안전을 최우선으로 하여 교통수단을 선택해야 한다.
② 위험이 수반되는 결정을 내릴 때 합리적인 사실에 의존해야 한다.
③ 일상 생활을 하는 동안 느끼는 불안감을 최소화하도록 노력해야 한다.
④ 통제할 수 없는 위험한 상황에 항상 대비해야 한다.
⑤ 불안을 포함한 부정적인 감정을 극복하기 위해 여러 가지 해결책을 배워야 한다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will _________________________________ in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① be much slower than the fastest users of the street
② hardly decide the power to process minute parts
③ greatly determine the ability to prune away features
④ be limited to some extent to keep a sense of security
⑤ significantly influence the capacity which deals with details
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력에 영향을 준다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 걷는 속도(시속 5마일 이하)에서는 세부 사항 구별이 잘 되지만, 빠른 자동차 운전자는 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력이 제한된다는 예시를 통해 빈칸 내용을 추론할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 도로의 가장 빠른 사용자들보다 훨씬 더 느릴 것이다
② 미세한 부분을 처리하는 능력을 거의 결정하지 못한다
③ 특징들을 제거하는 능력을 크게 결정한다
④ 어느 정도 보안 의식을 유지하기 위해 제한될 것이다
⑤ 세부 사항을 다루는 능력에 상당한 영향을 미친다

questions.question: 6. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is __________________________. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status - they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers may not be completely locked in to the product. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.
options: ① an item that provides little value on its own
② a product that can be replaced by another one
③ a product that is often consumed alongside another product
④ a good that decreases in demand as the price of another good rises
⑤ an alternative that offers more benefits to customers than the original
questions.explanation: 보완재(complementary good)에 대한 정의와 예시를 설명하는 글입니다. 팝콘과 영화, 램프와 전구처럼 한 제품과 함께 소비되는 제품을 의미하므로 ③번이 가장 적절합니다. (원문에는 옵션이 누락되어 있어 보편적인 해당 지문 빈칸 문제의 옵션을 구성함)
options_translation: ① 그 자체로는 가치가 거의 없는 품목
② 다른 제품으로 대체될 수 있는 제품
③ 종종 다른 제품과 함께 소비되는 제품
④ 다른 재화의 가격이 오름에 따라 수요가 감소하는 재화
⑤ 원래 제품보다 고객에게 더 많은 혜택을 제공하는 대안

questions.question: 7. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us. One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Gobekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This represents an early case of a society constructing something that _________________________________________. Things are not so different in our own time.
options: ① basically fosters social agreements on redevelopment
② persistently reminds itself of its ancestors' achievement
③ successfully leads its members to more prosperous lives
④ ultimately brings about a substantial reshaping of the society
⑤ strongly stimulates future generations to copy the past construction
questions.explanation: 괴베클리 테페라는 거대 석제 구조물을 건설하는 과정이 수렵 채집 사회를 농경 사회로 변화시킨 사례를 설명하고 있습니다. 즉, 인간이 만든 건축물이 결국 사회를 근본적으로 재구성(reshaping)하는 결과를 가져온다는 내용이므로 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 근본적으로 재개발에 대한 사회적 합의를 촉진한다
② 지속적으로 스스로에게 조상들의 업적을 상기시킨다
③ 성공적으로 구성원들을 더 번영한 삶으로 이끈다
④ 결국 사회의 실질적인 재형성을 가져온다
⑤ 미래 세대가 과거의 건축물을 모방하도록 강하게 자극한다

questions.question: 8. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that 'senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds,' Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Rather than _________________________________, we should study them for what they are.
options: ① questioning the Aristotelian classification of senses
② categorizing different animal senses into rigid groups
③ analyzing various animal senses to discover similarities
④ striving for a philosophic understanding of animal senses
⑤ putting the fixed number of animal senses into expanded categories
questions.explanation: 감각은 제한된 수의 특정한 종류로 명확히 나뉘질 수 없다는 내용의 글입니다. 따라서 감각을 엄격한 그룹으로 분류하기보다는, 그 자체 그대로의 특성에 맞춰 연구해야 한다는 내용의 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 아리스토텔레스식 감각 분류에 의문을 제기하기보다는
② 서로 다른 동물의 감각을 엄격한 그룹으로 분류하기보다는
③ 공통점을 찾기 위해 다양한 동물의 감각을 분석하기보다는
④ 동물의 감각에 대한 철학적 이해를 위해 노력하기보다는
⑤ 고정된 동물의 감각 수를 확장된 카테고리로 넓히기보다는

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title 'Monday Morning Quarterback' exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management (A)_____________________ in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people (B)__________________ on how sport organizations should be managed.
options: ① have decades of experiences / actively agree
② have great knowledge and skill / accept feedback
③ are highly qualified professionals / make comment
④ are totally unskilled specialists / provide guidelines
⑤ are inappropriate trainers / aggressively debate
questions.explanation: 스포츠 경영 분야의 관리자들은 각 분야에서 높은 자격을 갖춘 전문가임에도 불구하고, 많은 사람들이 전문가의 영역인 스포츠 조직 경영에 대해 함부로 견해(훈수)를 내놓는다는 내용의 글입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 전문가임을 나타내는 'highly qualified professionals', (B)에는 의견을 제시한다는 의미의 'make comment'가 들어가는 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 수십 년간의 경험을 가지고 있다 / 능동적으로 동의한다
② 풍부한 지식과 기술을 가지고 있다 / 피드백을 수용한다
③ 매우 자격을 갖춘 전문가들이다 / 견해(의견)를 내놓는다
④ 전혀 숙련되지 않은 전문가들이다 / 가이드라인을 제공한다
⑤ 부적절한 트레이너들이다 / 공격적으로 토론한다

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
options: ① How to Help Kids to Boost Imagination
② Moving for a Better Educational Environment
③ Difficulties in Finding the Right Home for Children
④ Need for Providing Children with New Surroundings
⑤ A Careful Approach to Young Minds Through Moves
questions.explanation: 이사가 아이들, 특히 3~6세 아동에게 큰 스트레스와 정체성 혼란을 줄 수 있다는 점을 설명하며, 이들의 과거를 인정하고 새로운 환경에 적응할 수 있도록 세심하게 도와야 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '이사를 통해 어린 마음(아이들)에 접근하는 신중한 방식'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 아이들이 상상력을 키우도록 돕는 방법
② 더 나은 교육 환경을 위한 이사
③ 아이들을 위한 적절한 집을 찾는 것의 어려움
④ 아이들에게 새로운 환경을 제공할 필요성
⑤ 이사를 통해 어린 마음(아이들)에 접근하는 신중한 방식

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and discovered ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books." The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.
options: ① A Characteristic of Successful People
② Various Ways to Treat Dyslexia Wisely
③ Reasons for Giving up a Field of Interest
④ Learning Strategies to Supplement Reading
⑤ How to Attain a Relevant Interview Outcome
questions.explanation: Rosalie Fink의 연구에 따르면, 난독증을 극복하고 성공한 사람들은 자신이 열정을 가진 특정 관심 분야에 대해 아주 열정적으로 독서했다는 공통점이 있습니다. 따라서 성공한 사람들의 이러한 공통된 특성을 언급하는 1번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 성공한 사람들의 한 가지 특징
② 난독증을 현명하게 치료하는 다양한 방법들
③ 관심 분야를 포기하는 이유들
④ 독서를 보충하기 위한 학습 전략들
⑤ 적절한 인터뷰 결과를 얻는 방법

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 the mental grooves and channels set에 대한 설명으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, <u>the mental grooves and channels set</u>." The decline in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.
options: ① The child's perception of the world is extremely rich but intensely disordered.
② Children's brains have hundreds of millions of neural connections, but they're all messed up.
③ Children's default settings become more common and their curiosity increases while they grow into adults.
④ Transmission between neurons in the child's brain is much less systematic than that in the adult's brain.
⑤ As children acquire various information from their surroundings, some of it solidifies into knowledge or a mindset.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 어른이 되면서 호기심이 줄어들고 기존의 사고방식이나 지식이 고착화되는 상태를 비유적으로 표현한 것입니다. 지문 하단에서 아이들이 정보를 흡수하며 특정 가능성이 지식이나 믿음으로 굳어지고 신경 경로가 자동화된다는 설명이 이를 뒷받침하므로, 5번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 아이의 세상에 대한 인식은 매우 풍부하지만 극도로 무질서하다.
② 아이들의 뇌는 수억 개의 신경 연결을 가지고 있지만, 모두 엉망이다.
③ 아이들이 성인으로 성장함에 따라 기본 설정이 더 흔해지고 호기심이 증가한다.
④ 아이 뇌의 뉴런 간 전달은 성인 뇌의 그것보다 훨씬 덜 체계적이다.
⑤ 아이들이 주변 환경에서 다양한 정보를 습득함에 따라, 그중 일부가 지식이나 사고방식으로 굳어진다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal they eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
options: ① Perceptual adaptation of the blind to stimuli
② decrease in responsiveness with closed eyes
③ altered processing of sensory input during sleep
④ advantages of defining sleeping and wakefulness
⑤ environmental necessities for sleeping organisms
questions.explanation: 이 글은 수면 중에 외부 자극에 대해 정상적으로 반응하지 않는 특성(지각적 이탈)을 설명합니다. 감각 정보가 들어오기는 하지만 정상적으로 처리되지 않거나 약화되어 수면자를 깨우지 못한다는 내용이 핵심이므로, '수면 중 감각 입력의 변화된 처리'가 주제로 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 자극에 대한 시각 장애인의 지각 적응
② 감은 눈으로 인한 반응성 감소
③ 수면 중 감각 입력의 변화된 처리
④ 수면과 깨어 있음을 정의하는 것의 이점
⑤ 수면 생명체를 위한 환경적 필수 요소

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흤름으로 밴아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곣은?
questions.passage: There are contrastive aspects of cultural diversity. (A) The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. (B) This is only an advantage up to a certain degree, because when the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. (C) Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. (D) On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. (E) They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.insertion_sentence: A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 관대한 호실하 주문이 다문화 도시림 긍정적으로 평가할 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C) 문장에서 다양성이 노동 시장 뿐만 아니라 삶의 질에도 영향을 미친다고 한 들, (D) 자리에서 그 구체적인 사례로서 긍정적인 면(사품갼 서비수 범위 증가)을 설명하고, 그 다음 문장에서 'On the other hand'림 통해 부정적인 면을 대조시키는 것이 흤름상 적절합니다. 따라서 (D)가 정답입니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 ••용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, ••칸 (A), (B)에 들어가기 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not compete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
questions.summary_sentence: Just as a hearer is a(n) (A)___________ element for sound, a published scientific paper is of no use if it is not (B)___________ by its readers.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 소리가 존재하기 위해 듣는 사람이 필수적인 것처럼, 과학 논문도 돌자에 의해 이해되어야만 의미가 있다는 과학적 소통의 쌍방향성을 강조하고 있다. 따라서 (A)에는 '필수적인(essential)'이나 '결정적인(crucial)', (B)에는 '이해되다(comprehended)'가 적합하다.
options_translation: ① 결정적인 - 수정된
② 결정적인 - 오해된
③ 필수적인 - 이해된
④ 필수적인 - 홄바된
⑤ 쒰모없는 - 무시된

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In light of this, it's crucial to attain favorable outcomes for ourselves while also nurturing a positive relationship with those with whom we negotiate. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
questions.summary_sentence: Since most of our interactions today (A)_____________, it is desirable to adopt negotiation strategies that secure (B)____________ beneficial agreements.
options: ① vary depending on the partners ... mutually
③ are instant in nature ... reciprocally
④ occur beneath our notice ... one-sidedly
⑤ consist of repeated encounters ... one-sidedly
questions.explanation: 오늘날 대부분의 상호작용은 동일한 사람들과 반복적으로 이루어지기 때문에(involve constant counterparts), 자신에게 유리한 결과를 얻는 것뿐만 아니라 상대방과의 긍정적인 관계를 유지하는 상호(mutually) 이익이 되는 협상 전략이 필요하다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 상대방에 따라 다르기 때문에 ... 상호적으로
② 지속적인 상대를 포함하기 때문에 ... 상호적으로
③ 본질적으로 즉각적이기 때문에 ... 호혜적으로
④ 우리가 인지하지 못하는 사이에 발생하기 때문에 ... 일방적으로
⑤ 반복적인 만남으로 구성되기 때문에 ... 일방적으로

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In light of this, it's crucial to attain favorable outcomes for ourselves while also nurturing a positive relationship with those with whom we negotiate. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
questions.summary_sentence: Since most of our interactions today (A)_____________, it is desirable to adopt negotiation strategies that secure (B)____________ beneficial agreements.
options: ① vary depending on the partners ... mutually
③ are instant in nature ... reciprocally
④ occur beneath our notice ... one-sidedly
⑤ consist of repeated encounters ... one-sidedly
questions.explanation: 지문은 우리가 배우자, 자녀, 친구, 동료 등 동일한 사람들과 반복적으로 상호작용하며 협상한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 오늘날의 상호작용은 '지속적인 상대(constant counterparts)'를 포함하며, 장기적인 관계를 위해 '상호 간에(mutually)' 유익한 협상 전략을 채택하는 것이 바람직하다는 요약이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 파트너에 따라 다양하다 ... 상호적으로
② 지속적인 상대를 포함한다 ... 상호적으로
③ 본질적으로 즉각적이다 ... 상호적으로
④ 우리의 인지 아래에서 일어난다 ... 일방적으로
⑤ 반복적인 만남으로 구성된다 ... 일방적으로

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are - writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.↓While views on the definition of ability are (A)_____________ among people, it is problematic to (B)_____________ based solely on ability.
options: ③ unvaried ... form opinions of people
④ subjective ... decide on a career
questions.explanation: 지문은 능력에 대한 정의가 지적 능력, 기술, 매력 등 사람마다 다양할 수 있음을 언급하면서(diverse/various), 능력이 자아 가치의 유일한 결정 요인이 되어 개인을 평가(assess/evaluate)하는 잣대가 될 때 문제가 발생한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 'diverse', (B)에는 'assess an individual'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다양한 ... 인생을 항해하다
② 다양한 ... 개인을 평가하다
③ 변함없는 ... 사람들에 대한 의견을 형성하다
④ 주관적인 ... 직업을 결정하다
⑤ 일관된 ... 사람을 평가하다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, which is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way that production could be made more efficient, known as the "division of labor." Making most manufactured goods involves several different processes using different skills. Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished. One worker could do all these tasks, and make 20 pins in a day. But this work can be divided into its separate processes, with a number of workers each performing one task. Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day - a huge increase in productivity from the 200 they would have produced before.
options: ① Relying on division of labor undermines production management.
② Reducing the steps of manufacturing contributes to enhancing productivity.
③ Dividing the production into smaller tasks increases the workload for managers.
④ Assigning specific tasks to each employee leads to a substantial rise in output.
⑤ Implementing task specialization raises both productivity and the costs of organizing workplace.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 아담 스미스의 분업(division of labor) 개념을 설명하며, 공정을 나누어 각 노동자가 특정 업무를 전문적으로 수행하게 함으로써 생산성을 대폭 높일 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 각 직원에게 특정 업무를 할당하는 것이 생산량의 상당한 증가로 이어진다는 ④번이 글의 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 분업에 의존하는 것은 생산 관리를 저해한다.
② 제조 단계를 줄이는 것이 생산성 향상에 기여한다.
③ 생산을 더 작은 업무로 나누는 것은 관리자의 업무량을 늘린다.
④ 각 직원에게 특정 업무를 할당하는 것은 생산량의 상당한 증가로 이어진다.
⑤ 업무 전문화를 시행하는 것은 생산성과 작업장 조직 비용을 모두 높인다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it - you just see the ⓐ<u>misty</u> outline of the moving string. Strings vibrating in this way on their own ⓑ<u>scarcely</u> make any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. But if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is ⓒ<u>amplified</u> and the note is heard loud and clear. The vibration of the string is ⓓ<u>interrupted</u> by the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. The vibration of the wood ⓔ<u>generates</u> more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. When the waves reach your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string.
questions.explanation: 기타 줄의 진동이 기타 몸통의 나무판으로 '전달'되어 나무판이 줄과 같은 속도로 진동하게 됨으로써 소리가 증폭되는 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 'interrupted(방해받는)'는 문맥상 '전달되는(passed on)' 혹은 '공명되는' 등의 의미를 가진 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans ⓐ<u>acknowledge</u> similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to ⓑ<u>separate</u> the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps 'mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow fundamentally ⓒ<u>distinct</u> from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal ⓓ<u>outperform</u> us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to ⓔ<u>disempower</u> animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 인간은 자신들의 지위를 유지하기 위해 인간과 동물 사이의 유사성을 '인정'하는 것이 아니라 '부정'하거나 '경시'합니다. 뒤따르는 내용들(언어적 속임수를 써서 인간과 동물을 분리함)을 볼 때 ⓐ acknowledge는 deny 또는 downplay와 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation.
ordered_passages: (A) Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg.

(B) If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. While the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a protective mechanism for the foot.

(C) And they now contract quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object. Sensory and motor nerves control almost all functions in the body - from the beating of the heart to the movement of the gut, sweating and just about everything else.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 감각 신경이 특정 감각을 포착한다는 원론적인 이야기를 한 후, (B)에서 핀을 밟았을 때를 예로 들어 통증 감각이 뇌로 전달되는 과정을 설명합니다. 그 다음 (A)에서 뇌 내부에서 일어나는 일(비명 지르기, 운동 신경으로 연결)을 설명하고, 마지막으로 (C)에서 운동 신경을 통해 발을 떼는 동작과 그 외 신체 기능을 조절한다는 결론으로 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 24. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime.
ordered_passages: (A) Individuals have varying preferences for how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are minimized.

(B) Moreover, we've observed a growing number of these "segmenters" carrying two phones - one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles.
(C) For instance, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time.

(D) Other individuals prefer blending work and family roles all day long. This might call for constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 일과 가정의 역할을 분리하려는 사람들(segmenters)에 대한 선호도를 먼저 제시합니다. (C)에서 'For instance'를 통해 이들이 이메일 계정을 분리하는 등 구체적인 사례를 보여줍니다. (B)에서 'Moreover'와 함께 'segmenters'의 또 다른 특징(휴대폰 두 대 사용)을 추가 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (D)에서 이와 대조되는 'Other individuals'(통합하려는 사람들)의 선호도를 설명하는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것 두 개를 골라 어색한 기호와 고친 내용을 정확하게 답안지에 작성하시오.
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies investigating these judgments found that people prefer clothing that ⓐ<u>meets</u> expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research ⓑ<u>exploring </u>observers' reactions to people who deviated slightly from established norms. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as ⓒ<u>having</u> higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that ⓓ<u>valuing</u> uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual ⓔ<u>be</u> powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.explanation: ⓑ: 문장의 주어는 'A series of studies'이며, 'published~Research'는 수식어구입니다. 문장의 본동사가 필요하므로 현재분사인 'exploring'을 과거형 동사인 'explored'로 고쳐야 합니다.ⓔ: suggest가 '~해야 한다'는 당위성이 아니라 '~라는 사실을 보여준다/시사하다'는 의미로 쓰였습니다. 따라서 종속절에 가정법 현재(동사원형)를 쓰지 않고 시제에 맞춰 'is'로 써야 합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 빈칸들을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 완성하시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating (A)___________ in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is (B)___________ if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made (C)___________ for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more (D)___________ for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
subjective_conditions: 1. 답안지에 (A)~(D)를 표시하여 답을 작성하시오.
2. 주어진 단어들에서 문맥상 알맞은 단어를 하나씩 골라 빈칸을 채우시오.  : achieved / appropriate / barrier / completely / excessive / modification / partly / surprising / temporarily / unlikely
questions.explanation: (A) 성인 스포츠 환경에 아이들이 '완전히(completely)' 참여하는 것의 어려움을 설명합니다. (B) 성인용 장비를 사용하면 성공의 길이 '희박하다(unlikely)'. (C) 아이들을 위해 스포츠 규칙이나 환경을 '수정(modification)'했습니다. (D) 테니스 코트 등을 아이들에게 더 '적절하게(appropriate)' 조정했습니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 요약문의 빈칸을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 완성하시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: Sometimes the pace of change is far slower. The face you saw reflected in your mirror this morning probably appeared no different from the face you saw the day before - or a week or a month ago. Yet we know the face that stares back at us from the glass is not the same, cannot be the same, as it was 10 minutes ago. The proof is in your photo album: Look at a photograph taken of yourself 5 or 10 years ago and you see clear differences between the face in the snapshot and the face in your mirror. If you lived in a world without mirrors for a year and then saw your reflection, you might be surprised by the change. After an interval of 10 years without seeing yourself, you might not at first recognize the person peering from the mirror. Even something as basic as our own face changes from moment to moment.
questions.summary_sentence: Changes, such as those in our faces, happen gradually, _______________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어(어구)를 모두 사용하시오. (조건3에 해당하는 단어만 변형)
questions.answer: making it hard to notice them in the short term, but they become apparent over extended periods.
questions.explanation: 우리의 얼굴 변화는 아주 점진적으로 일어나서 단기적으로는 알아차리기 어렵지만, 장기적으로는 명확하게 나타난다는 글의 내용을 반영하여 요약문을 완성합니다. 분사구문 making it hard to notice~를 사용하고 대조를 나타내는 but을 연결하여 구성합니다.

questions.question: 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 알맞은 단어를 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [5.0점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating (A)___________ in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is (B)___________ if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made (C)___________ for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more (D)___________ for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
subjective_conditions: 답안지에 (A)~(D)를 표시하여 답을 작성하시오.
주어진 단어들에서 문맥상 알맞은 단어를 하나씩 골라 빈칸을 채우시오. : achieved / appropriate / barrier / completely / excessive / modification / partly / surprising / temporarily / unlikely
questions.explanation: (A) 어린 아이들이 성인 스포츠 환경에 '완벽하게' 참여하는 것의 어려움을 깨달았다는 맥락이므로 completely가 적절합니다. (B) 성인용 장비를 사용할 때 성공할 가능성이 '낮다'는 의미이므로 unlikely가 적절합니다.(C) 아이들을 위해 스포츠 규칙이나 환경에 '수정/변화'를 주었다는 맥락이므로 modification이 적절합니다.(D) 테니스 코트와 라켓을 아이들에게 더 '적절하게' 만들었다는 의미이므로 appropriate가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글에 대한 <Q&A>의 빈칸을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 완성하시오. [5.0점]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phone were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어(어구)를 모두 사용하고 추가 단어를 사용하여 완성하시오. (변형 없음)
14단어로 작성하시오.
questions.subjective_answer_format: Q: According to the passage, what is the 'curse of knowledge?'A: It is the effect that once people obtain their own skill, they ______________________________________.→ _____________________________________________________
questions.answer: have a tendency to rate the level of difficulty of that skill too low
questions.explanation: 지문에서 '지식의 저주'란 전문가가 초보자에게 어떤 과업이 얼마나 어려운지 무감각해지는 현상을 말합니다. 따라서 전문가가 기술을 습득하면 '그 기술의 난이도를 너무 낮게 평가하는 경향이 있다'는 내용을 완성해야 합니다. 주어진 단어들을 배열하고 부족한 단어를 채워 14단어로 완성하면 'have a tendency to rate the level of difficulty of that skill too low'가 됩니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ① Things to Keep in Mind When Doing Brainwriting
② Common Misconceptions and Challenges of Brainwriting
③ Brainwriting: A Tool to Unlock Your Team's Full Potential
④ Brainwriting vs. Brainstorming: A Detailed Comparison
⑤ Brainstorming Techniques: Creative Activities to Do Solo or as a Team
questions.explanation: 이 글은 팀의 잠재력을 끌어올리기 위해 브레인스토밍 대신 '브레인라이팅(brainwriting)'을 제안하고 있습니다. 각자 아이디어를 먼저 내고, 익명으로 공유하며, 개별 평가를 거친 후 팀이 모이는 과정은 모든 목소리를 반영하고 집단 지성을 발휘하게 돕는다는 내용입니다. 따라서 브레인라이팅이 팀의 잠재력을 여는 도구라는 ③번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 브레인라이팅을 할 때 명심해야 할 점들
② 브레인라이팅의 일반적인 오해와 도전 과제들
③ 브레인라이팅: 팀의 전체 잠재력을 여는 도구
④ 브레인라이팅 대 브레인스토밍: 상세한 비교
⑤ 브레인스토밍 기법: 혼자 또는 팀으로 하는 창의적 활동

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.
options: ① How Do Disruptions Influence Us?
② The Reasons Why Interruptions Happen
③ The Ways to Handle External Interruptions
④ Write the Inspiration down Not to Forget it!
⑤ What Is Not Written Is What Is Not Remembered
questions.explanation: 이 글은 방해(interruptions/disruptions)가 가져오는 부정적인 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 문학적 사례(콜리지의 미완성 시)부터 전문직 종사자들, 그리고 일반인들의 일상(생산성 저하 및 스트레스 증가)까지 방해가 우리에게 어떻게 영향을 미치는지 다루고 있으므로 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 방해는 우리에게 어떻게 영향을 미치는가?
② 방해가 발생하는 이유들
③ 외부의 방해를 처리하는 방법들
④ 잊지 않기 위해 영감을 기록하라!
⑤ 기록되지 않은 것은 기억되지 않는 것이다

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 are the descendants of the winners가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I <u>are the descendants of the winners</u>.
options: ① tend to avoid other human tribes
② hold a numerical advantage in population
③ have the better mental power than others
④ get our physical advantage from our ancestors
⑤ rarely contribute to the evolution of the human mind
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간의 정신이 다른 부족과의 경쟁에서 이기기 위해 진화했으며, 상대보다 더 잘 생각하는 능력이 생존과 승리의 핵심 무기였다고 설명합니다. 승리한 부족은 이러한 '정신적 이점'에 대한 유전자를 후손에게 물려주었으므로, 우리가 '승리자의 후손'이라는 말은 곧 우리가 타인(또는 경쟁 상대)보다 더 뛰어난 지적/정신적 능력을 갖추게 되었다는 의미인 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 인간 부족을 피하는 경향이 있다
② 인구수에서 수적 우위를 점하고 있다
③ 타인보다 더 나은 정신적 능력을 갖추고 있다
④ 조상으로부터 신체적 이점을 얻는다
⑤ 인간 정신의 진화에 거의 기여하지 않는다

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
options: ① examples of technology that decrease or eliminate barriers faced by disabled people
② necessity of accessible design in digital project to accommodate the needs of people with disabilities
③ the role of artificial intelligence in the social and professional integration of people with disabilities
