questions.explanation: 이 글은 디지털 정보를 구축할 때 장애인들의 필요가 종종 소외되고 있음을 지적하며, 더 넓은 범위의 사용자를 고려하여 장애인의 필요를 충족시키는 접근 가능한 디자인이 필요함을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 디지털 프로젝트에서 장애인의 요구를 수용하는 접근 가능한 디자인의 필요성을 언급한 ②번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다. (참고: 원문의 보기가 3개만 제공된 상태임)
options_translation: ① 장애인들이 직면한 장벽을 줄이거나 제거하는 기술의 사례들
② 장애인의 요구를 수용하기 위한 디지털 프로젝트의 접근 가능한 디자인의 필요성
③ 장애인의 사회적 및 직업적 통합에 있어 인공지능의 역할

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. ⓐThis behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. ⓑThus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one. ⓒHowever, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. ⓓFor example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead, which could be examples of weakness of will. ⓔNamely, the agents may not change their initial plan or decision about their savings, even if temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.explanation: 전체 글은 미래 소비를 위해 저축을 하지만 의지박약 등으로 인해 계획보다 일찍 소비하게 되는 경우를 설명하고 있습니다. ⓔ는 즉각적인 유혹에도 불구하고 원래 계획을 바꾸지 않는다는 내용이므로, 앞선 내용(조기 소비 사례)과 반대되는 진술입니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still (A)[destroy / preserve] the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is (B)[overlooked / perceived]. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it (C)[eliminates / generates] four grams of CO2, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 디지털화가 환경에 미치는 영향이 덜 부정적일 것이라 가정되지만, 실제로는 여전히 환경을 파괴(destroy)할 수 있다는 역접의 내용이 와야 합니다. (B) 인터넷과 전기의 환경적 비용이 간과(overlooked)되고 있다는 내용이 뒤따르는 화석 연료 사용과 탄소 배출 언급과 자연스럽게 연결됩니다. (C) 이메일은 탄소 발자국이 작지만 여전히 4그램의 이산화탄소를 생성(generates)한다는 것이 문맥에 맞습니다.
options_translation: ① 파괴하다 - 간과된 - 생성하다
② 파괴하다 - 간과된 - 제거하다
③ 파괴하다 - 인지된 - 생성하다
④ 보존하다 - 간과된 - 생성하다
⑤ 보존하다 - 인지된 - 제거하다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very ⓐ<u>inefficient</u> migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, adapt with ⓑ<u>difficulty</u>. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most ⓒ<u>efficient</u> migration routes. Childhood ⓓ<u>hiders</u> the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives ⓔ<u>flexibility</u> in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 어린 시절(Childhood)은 문화적 정보의 전달을 '방해하는(hinders)' 것이 아니라 '가능하게 하거나 촉진하는' 역할을 합니다. 문맥상 Childhood facilitates/helps 등으로 바뀌어야 합니다. (참고: 원문의 hiders는 hinders의 오타로 보임)

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show the attention. If you notice someone who is lonely, you could go and sit with them. If you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. A person's happiness comes from __________. There are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. Even if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves.
options: ② the feeling that someone cares
③ seeking virtue and the meaning of life
④ the sense of accomplishment in one's endeavors
⑤ environmental factors like high income and education
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 누군가를 돕는 것은 큰 일이 아니며 관심을 보이는 것만으로도 충분하다고 말합니다. 외로운 사람 곁에 앉아주거나 지나가는 사람에게 인사하는 등의 행동이 그들의 기분을 좋게 한다는 점을 통해, 사람의 행복은 '누군가가 자신을 신경 써준다는 느낌(the feeling that someone cares)'에서 온다는 것을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: 긍정적인 자아상
누군가가 자신을 배려한다는 느낌
미덕과 삶의 의미를 탐구하는 것
자신의 노력에 대한 성취감
높은 수입이나 교육과 같은 환경적 요인

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes depending on __________________________________.
options: ① what type of cognitive challenge we confront
② where attention is focused and what activities are practiced
③ what skills we need to learn and where we should learn them
④ the continuing complex interactions of genetic and environmental influences
⑤ how much social interaction takes place and what environmental stimuli are received
questions.explanation: 이 글은 집중된 주의와 반복적인 활동이 뇌의 물리적 구조를 재구성한다는 뇌 가소성(neuroplasticity)에 관한 내용입니다. 소리에 집중하는 동물은 청각 센터가 발달하고, 시력을 사용하는 동물은 시각 영역이 크며, 바이올린 연주자는 왼손 담당 피질이, 택시 운전사는 공간 기억을 담당하는 해마가 커진다는 예시들이 제시되었습니다. 따라서 뇌의 구조적 변화는 '주의가 어디에 집중되고 어떤 활동이 연습되는지'에 달려 있다는 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 어떤 유형의 인지적 도전에 직면하는지
② 어디에 주의가 집중되고 어떤 활동이 연습되는지
③ 어떤 기술을 배워야 하고 어디에서 배워야 하는지
④ 유전적 요인과 환경적 요인의 지속적인 복합적 상호작용
⑤ 얼마나 많은 사회적 상호작용이 일어나고 어떤 환경적 자극을 받는지

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields are ________________________ relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
options: ② rich in essentials for plants
③ in want of nutrients and water
④ short of the necessities of life
⑤ accessible only for the wealthy
questions.explanation: 농지에 비료와 관개 시설을 통해 영양분과 물을 풍부하게 공급하여 단일 경작을 위한 완벽한 환경을 만들었으나, 이러한 '사치스러운 조건'이 잡초들에게도 매력적인 장소가 되었다는 내용입니다. 주변의 자연 토지에 비해 농지는 '식물에 필수적인 것들이 풍부하기' 때문에 잡초들이 탐내는 장소가 된다는 맥락이므로 ②번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 경제적 가치가 높은
② 식물을 위한 필수 요소들이 풍부한
③ 영양분과 물을 필요로 하는
④ 생필품이 부족한
⑤ 부유한 사람들만 접근 가능한

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 알맞은 말은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. (A)__________, what you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. (B)__________, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
questions.explanation: (A)의 앞 문장(행동은 정체성의 반영이다)과 뒷 문장(당신이 하는 일은 스스로가 믿는 인간 유형의 표시이다)은 동일한 내용을 다르게 설명하고 있으므로 '즉(That is)'이 적절합니다. (B)는 정체성과 행동이 일치할 때의 상황을 종합적으로 정리하여 결론을 내리고 있으므로 '궁극적으로(Ultimately)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: 즉 - 궁극적으로
그럼에도 불구하고 - 결국에는
그렇지 않으면 - 예를 들어
그럼에도 불구하고 - 하지만
다시 말해서 - 반대로

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. (A) Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. (B) When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. (C) Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. (D) So within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. (E) As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
questions.insertion_sentence: The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 회색 다람쥐가 우위를 점한 이유 중 하나로, 익지 않은 도토리(green acorns)도 먹을 수 있는 넓은 식습관을 설명하고 있습니다. 이 내용은 (D) 뒤에 나오는 결과 문장, 즉 '그래서(So) 같은 숲에서 회색 다람쥐가 붉은 다람쥐보다 먼저 먹이를 해치울 수 있다'는 내용에 대한 직접적인 원인이 되므로, (D) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 주제문을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
subjective_conditions: 15단어 이내의 한 문장으로 작성할 것 (15단어까지 인정함)
지문에 나오는 5단어 이상의 연속된 어구를 그대로 사용할 경우 감점 또는 0점 처리될 수 있음
questions.answer: Giving employees a feeling that they have decision-making authority can increase their productivity.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 직원들에게 업무에 대한 자율성(a sense of agency)과 결정 권한을 부여하는 것이 생산성 향상과 업무 몰입에 긍정적인 영향을 미친다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '직원들에게 의사 결정 권한이 있다는 기분을 갖게 하는 것이 생산성을 높일 수 있다'는 요지의 주제문을 조건에 맞춰 영작합니다. (사용된 문장은 13단어로 15단어 이내 조건을 충족하며, 지문의 긴 어구를 그대로 복사하지 않았습니다.)

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
options: ① evolution of childcare in agricultural societies
② negative roles of mothers in human settlements
④ frequent movements in hunter-gatherer societies
⑤ influence of farming on childbirth and population growth
questions.explanation: 농사를 지으며 정착 생활을 하게 됨에 따라, 아이를 데리고 이동해야 하는 부담이 줄어들고 출산 간격이 짧아져 인구가 급격히 증가했다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '농업이 출산과 인구 증가에 미친 영향'을 언급한 ⑤번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 농업 사회에서의 육아 방식의 진화
② 인간 정착지에서 어머니들의 부정적인 역할
③ 수렵 채집 공동체의 발전
④ 수렵 채집 사회에서의 빈번한 이동
⑤ 농업이 출산과 인구 증가에 미친 영향

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has been close to extinction in England.
options: ① the impact of grey squirrels on Britain's ecosystem
② differences between red squirrels and grey squirrels
③ the dietary preferences of squirrel species
④ the role of green acorns in squirrel diets
⑤ strategies for managing grey squirrels
questions.explanation: 외래종인 회색 다람쥐가 영국에 도입되어 토착종인 붉은 다람쥐를 멸종 위기로 몰고 가는 등 생태계에 미친 영향을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '영국 생태계에 회색 다람쥐가 미친 영향'을 언급한 ①번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 회색 다람쥐가 영국 생태계에 미친 영향
② 붉은 다람쥐와 회색 다람쥐의 차이점
③ 다람쥐 개체들의 식성 선호도
④ 다람쥐 식단에서 익지 않은 도토리의 역할
⑤ 회색 다람쥐를 관리하기 위한 전략

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ① The Drawbacks of Solo Idea Generation
② How to Improve Your Collaboration Skills
③ The Limits of Independent Idea Evaluation
④ The Power of Individual Brainstorming in Teamwork
⑤ Unveiling Team Potential: The Brainwriting Revolution
questions.explanation: 팀의 잠재력을 끌어내기 위해 기존의 브레인스토밍 대신, 개별적으로 아이디어를 내고 평가하는 '브레인라이팅(brainwriting)' 과정의 유익함을 설명하는 글입니다. 따라서 팀의 잠재력을 드러내는 브레인라이팅 혁명을 언급한 ⑤번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 개별 아이디어 생성의 단점
② 협업 능력을 향상시키는 방법
③ 독립적인 아이디어 평가의 한계
④ 팀워크에서 개별 브레인스토밍의 힘
⑤ 팀의 잠재력 드러내기: 브레인라이팅 혁명

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive
options: ① Vividness: A Source of Inspiration for Painters
② The Magic Key: Your Daily Encouraging Sentences
③ The Self-Confidence: Towards a More Promising Writer
④ The Path to Leadership Excellence: Perseverance and Self-Improvement
⑤ Challenges of Establishing Statements for Well-Organized Composition
questions.explanation: 이 글은 현재 겪고 있는 어려움을 긍정적인 진술로 바꾸어 적음으로써 생각과 행동의 변화(마법)를 경험할 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 매일 쓰는 고무적인 문장들이 삶을 변화시키는 열쇠라는 내용의 2번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 생생함: 화가들에게 영감의 원천
② 마법의 열쇠: 당신의 매일의 격려 문장들
③ 자신감: 더 유망한 작가가 되는 길
④ 리더십 탁월함으로 가는 길: 인내와 자기 계발
⑤ 잘 구성된 작문을 위한 진술 확립의 어려움

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① Brain Reshaping in Skilled Musicians
② Auditory and Visual Brain Development
③ Why Animal Rewards Reshape Brain Centers
④ Spatial Memory Enhancement in Professionals
⑤ The Impact of Focused Attention on Brain Structure
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우리가 주의를 어디에 집중하고 무엇을 연습하느냐에 따라 뇌의 물리적 구조가 변한다는 과학적 증거들(동물, 바이올린 연주자, 택시 운전사 사례)을 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 '집중된 주의가 뇌 구조에 미치는 영향'을 제목으로 하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 숙련된 음악가들의 뇌 재형성
② 청각 및 시각적 뇌 발달
③ 동물의 보상이 뇌 중추를 재형성하는 이유
④ 전문가들의 공간 기억력 향상
⑤ 집중된 주의가 뇌 구조에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [23년 3월 35번]
questions.passage: Whose story it is ⓐ<u>affects</u> what the story is. If the main character ⓑ<u>is changed</u>, the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them ⓒ<u>differently</u>. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises ⓓ<u>what</u> is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we ⓔ<u>were shown</u> the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
questions.explanation: ⓓ 문장에서 'what is the heart of the story'는 선행사인 the conflict림 수식하는 관계대명사절이어야 합니다. what은 선행사림 포함하므로 이 자리에는 접절하지 않으며, 주격 관계대명사인 that 또는 which로 바꾸어야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out­think its enemies, even slightly, ⓐ<u>possessing</u> a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, ⓑ<u>gave</u> your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more ⓒ<u>decisive</u> than any before it. And this mental advantage ⓓ<u>that</u> the human mind became a weapon was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. It was more likely that the tribe that could out-think its opponents succeeded in battle, ⓔ<u>passing</u> on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.explanation: ⓐ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'A human tribe (that could out-think its enemies, even slightly)'이며, 이 문장에는 본동사가 없습니다. 따라서 현재분사 형태인 'possessing'을 과거 시제 동사인 'possessed'로 바꾸어 문장의 술어 역할을 하게 해야 합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still ⓐ<u>support</u> the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more ⓑ<u>severe</u>. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a ⓒ<u>encouraging</u> step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is ⓓ<u>overlooked</u>. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, ⓔ<u>increased</u> carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO2, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
questions.explanation: 지문의 전체적인 맥락은 디지털 비즈니스 활동이 환경에 덜 해로울 것이라는 예상과 달리 여전히 환경에 부정적인 영향을 준다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ⓐ는 환경을 '지원(support)'한다는 표현 대신 '해치다(harm, damage, threaten)'와 같은 부정적인 의미의 단어가 와야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals-sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to ⓐ<u>question</u> it. For a start, Aristotle ⓑ<u>included</u> some in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are a lot more ⓒ<u>challenging</u> to classify. Many vertebrates have a ⓓ<u>dissimilar</u> sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be divided into a ⓔ<u>fixed</u> number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스가 인간의 오감 이외의 다른 감각들(자신의 신체에 대한 지각, 균형 감각)을 '간과했거나 빠뜨렸다'는 내용이 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다. 따라서 'included(포함했다)'가 아니라 'missed' 또는 'overlooked'와 같은 단어가 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that ______________________.
options: ① maintenance of a balance in a relationship requires much work
② a number of real interactions can never be entirely believable
③ online relationships can have both more privacy and greater closeness
④ different expectations have a significant influence on impressions and interactions
⑤ The mistaken assumption that any and all scientific knowledge contributes to sustainability is common
questions.explanation: 실험에서 학생들은 강연자에 대해 '따뜻하다' 혹은 '차갑다'는 사전 정보를 받았고, 그에 따라 강연자에 대한 인상 형성이 달라졌으며 실제 상호작용 빈도에도 차이가 났습니다. 이는 타인에 대한 사전 정보에 의한 '기대'가 실제 '인상'과 '상호작용'에 큰 영향을 미친다는 것을 입증하므로 ④번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 관계의 균형 유지에는 많은 노력이 필요하다
② 많은 실제 상호작용은 결코 완전히 신뢰할 수 없다
③ 온라인 관계는 더 많은 사생활 보호와 더 큰 친밀감을 모두 가질 수 있다
④ 서로 다른 기대치는 인상과 상호작용에 중요한 영향을 미친다
⑤ 모든 과학적 지식이 지속 가능성에 기여한다는 잘못된 가정은 흔하다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually ___________________________. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
options: ① the result of society that you belong to
② an interpretation of your success
③ imitation as a learning strategy
④ mirror of your sense of self
questions.explanation: 이 글은 개인의 정체성(identity)과 행동(behavior) 사이의 밀접한 관계를 설명하고 있습니다. 자신이 어떤 사람이라고 믿는지(자아 인식)에 따라 그에 일치하는 행동이 자연스럽게 나타난다는 내용을 담고 있으므로, 행동은 당신의 자아 인식의 거울(mirror of your sense of self)이라는 표현이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 속한 사회의 결과물
② 당신의 성공에 대한 해석
③ 학습 전략으로서의 모방
④ 당신의 자아 인식의 거울
⑤ 의사소통의 한 형태

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives _______________ in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 유년기가 있는 동물은 환경에 대해 배울 시간을 가지며, 이는 유전적 지시(hardware)에만 의존하는 것보다 더 유연하게 대처할 수 있게 해줍니다. 변화하는 환경 속에서 학습을 통해 효율적인 경로를 찾는 새들의 사례를 통해, 유년기가 '적응성(adaptability)'을 제공함을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 불안정성
② 참을 수 없음
③ 적응성
④ 책임감
⑤ 취약성

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. ①The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. ②In year three, the crops will rotate again. ③By the fourth year, the crops will return to their original planting order, as they were initially arranged. ④Due to possibly negative effects on the soil, the farmer might not be able to grow a single crop on a large scale for an extended period. ⑤Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop, and therefore, this type of farming is sustainable because of fertile soil that stays healthy.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 돌려짓기(윤작, crop rotation)의 개념과 그로 인한 토양의 건강 및 지속 가능성을 설명하고 있습니다. ④번 문장은 대규모 단일 작물 재배가 불가능할 수도 있다는 내용으로, 돌려짓기의 원리와 긍정적 효과를 설명하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea.
ordered_passages: (A) Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
(B) The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision.

(C) Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 모든 창조물은 아이디어에서 시작된다고 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 그 아이디어가 구체화되는 과정(못이 박히기 전 단계 등)을 설명합니다. (B)에서 이를 인간의 미래 설계라는 동일한 프로세스로 확장하며, (A)에서 그 결과로 생각과 활동이 조화를 이루어 실현된다는 결론을 맺는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations.
ordered_passages: (A) This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.

(B) While professionals working working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account.

(C) What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 디지털 정보 보존 표준에 대해 말한 후, (C)에서 '하지만 소외된 부분'으로 장애인의 필요를 언급합니다. (B)에서 상업 디자인과 달리 학술 프로젝트에서는 이들의 요구를 고려하지 못하는 현실을 지적하고, (A)에서 모든 사용자를 고려하는 디자인 결정이 필요하다는 해결책을 제시하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one. (A)The agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (B) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one. (C) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. (D) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (E) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 미래 소비를 위해 저축한 돈을 계획된 때가 오기 전에 미리 써버리는 경우를 'However'와 함께 소개합니다. (C) 뒤에 이어지는 문장은 크리스마스 선물을 위해 모은 돈을 여름휴가에 써버리는 구체적인 예시를 들고 있으므로, (C) 자리에 주어진 문장이 들어가는 것이 흐름상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle can be described as "natural" to human beings. (A) Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. (B) In other words, cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. (C) Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. (D) This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development. (E) It opened the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually led to settled "civilizations."
questions.insertion_sentence: If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'this'는 (A)에서 설명한 수렵 채집인들의 풍요롭고 건강한 생활을 의미합니다. 만약 수렵 채집 생활이 그토록 이상적이었다면 왜 인류가 정착 생활과 농경을 시작했는지 의문을 제기하는 문장이 먼저 나오고, 그 뒤인 (B)에서 'In other words'로 시작하며 농경 생활이 실제로는 매우 힘들고 전염병의 원인이었다는 대조적인 설명을 이어가는 것이 논리적으로 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment: they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street ─ a motorist simply has enough time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.summary_sentence: The ability to process environmental details (A)____________ with travel speed, as people travel faster, they notice (B)____________ details in their surroundings.

② 증가한다 ...... 더 적은

④ 감소한다 ...... 더 많은

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 31번]
questions.passage: The ⓐ<u>cost</u> of being interrupted are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an ⓑ<u>anticipated</u> guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had ⓒ<u>considerable</u> consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels. But interruptions can have benefits as well. They can offer a mental break from work, which helps to replenish cognitive resources, they can serve as a social break to connect with others, and they can lead us to ⓓ<u>generate</u> new ideas. When people were asked to keep diaries of their interruptions and the corresponding emotions they felt, 80 percent reported that interruptions generated positive as well as negative emotions for them, especially if they regarded the interruption related to a worthy endeavor. So while not all interruptions are bad, we do need to learn how to ⓔ<u>control</u> our attention so that we don't become overwhelmed by the unwelcome ones.*replenish 채우다 **endeavor 노력
options: ② How to Avoid Interruptions in Everyday Life
③ The Role of Interruptions in Creative Processes
④ The Paradox of Interruptions: Costs and Benefits
⑤ Negative Effects of Interruptions on Job Performance
questions.explanation: 이 글은 방해(interruption)가 생산성 저하와 스트레스 증가와 같은 부정적 측면(Costs)도 있지만, 휴식 제공 및 새로운 아이디어 생성과 같은 긍정적 측면(Benefits)도 있다는 내용을 다루고 있으므로 '방해의 역설: 비용과 이점'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 방해를 최소화하기 위한 전략들

③ 창의적 과정에서 방해의 역할
④ 방해의 역설: 비용과 이점
⑤ 직무 수행에 있어 방해가 미치는 부정적 영향

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 make our green clouds gray가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 36번]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data enters' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions <u>make our green clouds gray</u>. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 37번]
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, which is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way that production could be made more efficient, known as the "division of labor." Making most manufactured goods involves several different processes using different skills. Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished. One worker could do all these tasks, and make 20 pins in a day. But this work can be divided into its separate processes, with a number of workers each performing one task. Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day - a huge increase in productivity from the 200 they would have produced before.
options: ① 생산 관리자와 작업자의 관계가 작업량에 영향을 미친다.
② 맡은 업무를 전문으로 하는 것은 작업자의 사기를 높인다.
③ 분업은 제조 분야의 작업 속도를 높이고 생산성을 증가시킨다.
④ 스마트 기술은 인간의 일자리를 대신하여 실업 문제를 발생시킨다.
⑤ 단조로운 노동은 업무 유연성과 변화에 대처하는 능력을 감소시킨다.
questions.explanation: 아담 스미스가 제안한 '분업(division of labor)'을 통해 작업자들이 각자의 전문 분야에 집중함으로써 생산 효율성이 크게 향상되고 결과적으로 생산성이 증가한다는 것이 글의 핵심 내용입니다.

questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ① obstacles to pooling collective intelligence
② tips for developing leadership within your group
③ differences between brainstorming and brainwriting
④ how to overcome the difficulties of achieving group mind
⑤ efficacy of a brainwriting approach to identify team potential
questions.explanation: 이 글은 팀의 잠재력을 끌어내기 위해 브레인스토밍 대신 '브레인라이팅(brainwriting)'을 활용할 것을 제안합니다. 브레인라이팅은 각자 아이디어를 낸 뒤 익명으로 공유하고 개별적으로 평가하는 과정을 거칩니다. 이를 통해 평소 주목받지 못했던 아이디어를 발굴하고 모든 구성원의 참여를 이끌어낼 수 있다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 '팀의 잠재력을 식별하기 위한 브레인라이팅 접근법의 효능'입니다.

③ 브레인스토밍과 브레인라이팅의 차이점
④ 집단 사고를 달성하는 데 따르는 어려움을 극복하는 방법
⑤ 팀의 잠재력을 파악하기 위한 브레인라이팅 접근법의 효능

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
options: ① Farm fields are designed to have the best soil conditions for monoculture development.
② The perfect environment for monoculture growth is accomplished by adding water and nutrients in the form of fertilizer.
③ In the past fifty years, farmers have been able to offer precisely the proper amount of water and fertilizer thanks to the assistance of engineers and agricultural scientists.
④ We are irrigating and feeding our fields less than ever before.
