⑤ 농지는 적절한 양의 물과 영양분으로 가득 차 있어 잡초들도 그것을 갈망한다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: As I walked from the mailbox, my heart was beating ⓐ<u>rapidly</u>. In my hands, I held the letter from the university I ⓑ<u>had applied</u> to. I thought my grades were ⓒ<u>enough good</u> to cross the line and my application letter was well-written, but was it enough? I hadn't slept a wink for days. As I carefully tore into the paper of the envelope, the letter slowly ⓓ<u>emerged</u> with the opening phrase, "It is our great pleasure..." I shouted with joy, "I am in!" As I held the letter, I began ⓔ<u>to make</u> a fantasy about my college life in a faraway city.
questions.explanation: 부사 'enough'가 형용사를 수식할 때는 형용사 뒤에 위치해야 하므로 'good enough'가 올바른 표현입니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: When it comes to ⓐ<u>helping</u> out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do ⓑ<u>is</u> come around and show that you care. If you notice someone who is lonely, you could go and sit with them. If you work with someone who ⓒ<u>eats</u> lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. A person's happiness comes from attention. There are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ⓓ<u>ignoring</u> them. Even if you say hi to someone ⓔ<u>passing</u> by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 'has'에 걸리는 병렬 구조이므로, 'forgotten'과 형태를 맞추어 과거분사인 'ignored'가 되어야 합니다. 수동의 의미(잊혀지거나 무시당하는 것)로 해석되기도 합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것의 개수는? [3.2점]
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have ⓐ<u>fewer</u> questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The decline in curiosity can ⓑ<u>be traced</u> in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between ⓒ<u>that</u> in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more ⓓ<u>usefully</u> and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs ⓔ<u>to become</u> faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.
questions.explanation: 어법상 옳은 것은 ⓐ, ⓑ 2개입니다.ⓐ fewer: 셀 수 있는 명사 questions를 수식하므로 적절합니다.ⓑ be traced: 'the decline(감소)'이 추적되는 수동의 의미이므로 적절합니다.ⓒ that: 복수 명사인 'the lines of communication'을 가리키므로 those가 되어야 합니다.ⓓ usefully: become의 보어 자리이므로 형용사인 useful이 되어야 합니다.ⓔ to become: 'enable + 목적어 + to부정사' 구문에서 주어 역할을 하는 pathways 뒤의 동사 자리가 필요하므로 become(동사원형) 등이 와야 하는 구조적 분석이 필요하거나, enable의 보어로 쓰인 것으로 본다면 문맥상 동사가 이미 enable로 존재하므로 전체 문장의 술어 동사 확인이 필요합니다. (해당 지문 원문상 enable those beliefs to become... 구조에서 pathways가 주어이고 동사가 become 등으로 연결되는 술어 구조인지 확인 시 ⓔ는 틀림)

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of (A)[moderation / ownership] - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were (B)[entitled / forbidden] to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control (C)[impaired / enhanced] how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤의 설명(통제권, 의사결정 권한)을 볼 때 '주인의식(ownership)'이 적절합니다. (B) 스스로 결정을 내리는 권한을 가진 것이므로 '권한이 부여된(entitled)'이 적절합니다. (C) 통제권을 부여하는 것이 자기 수양을 '향상시켰다(enhanced)'가 문맥상 맞습니다.
options_translation: ① 절제 - 금지된 - 손상된
② 소유권 - 금지된 - 향상된
③ 소유권 - 자격이 주어진 - 손상된
④ 소유권 - 자격이 주어진 - 향상된
⑤ 절제 - 자격이 주어진 - 향상된

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the ①<u>effectiveness</u> of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small ②<u>discount</u>: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The lower-priced soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were ③<u>unconditionally</u> given either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the ④<u>scarce</u> condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly ⑤<u>reliable</u> because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
questions.explanation: 지문은 상품 구매 수량을 제한하여 판매량을 늘리는 '희소성 마케팅'의 효과를 설명하고 있습니다. ③번이 포함된 문장은 구매량에 제한을 둔 실험 조건을 설명하는 부분인데, 뒤의 'either four or twelve cans'라는 제한적 수치가 언급되고 있습니다. 따라서 '무조건적으로'라는 의미의 'unconditionally'는 문맥상 어색하며, '제한적으로(limited)' 또는 '제한되어(restricted)'와 같은 표현이 오는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is ______________. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life - which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
questions.explanation: 지문은 가난이 스트레스를 유발한다는 일반적인 상식 외에도, 부유하고 산업화된 국가들 역시 고유의 스트레스를 겪고 있음을 설명합니다. 특히 산업화된 국가의 빠른 삶의 속도(faster pace of life)가 지속적인 긴박감을 유발하고, 이로 인해 사람들이 스스로를 '시간 빈곤자(time-poor)'로 느끼게 만든다는 내용이 핵심입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 이러한 현상을 요약하는 '시간 압박(time pressure)'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 시간 압박
② 도덕적 해이
③ 인종 갈등
④ 계급 투쟁
⑤ 경제적 양극화

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating ___________________________________. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① the brain changes as a result of concentrated attention
② each animal has its own specific sense of development
③ hippocampus responsible for memory varies depending races
④ each person has different parts of the brain that inherently developed
⑤ the size of the brain that controls sight is bigger than one that controls hearing
questions.explanation: 이 글은 뇌의 물리적 구조가 우리가 어디에 주의를 기울이고 무엇을 연습하는지에 따라 변화한다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 바이올린 연주자의 피질 확장이나 택시 운전사의 해마 확대 등의 사례는 모두 특정 활동에 대한 집중과 연습이 뇌의 변화를 이끈다는 것을 보여줍니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '집중된 주의의 결과로 뇌가 변한다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 집중된 주의의 결과로 뇌가 변한다
각 동물은 자신만의 고유한 감각 발달을 가지고 있다
기억을 담당하는 해마는 인종에 따라 다르다
사람마다 선천적으로 발달한 뇌 부위가 다르다
시력을 조절하는 뇌의 크기가 청력을 조절하는 뇌보다 크다

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted.
ordered_passages: (A) The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales.

(B) No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped increase sales.

(C) Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, to consumer demand for yeast increased.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 광고주들이 시장 상황에 맞춰 제품 홍보 방식을 바꾼다는 내용을 제시합니다. (C)에서 Fleischmann의 효모가 가정용 빵 재료였으나 시장 상황 변화(가게에서 빵을 삼)로 수요가 줄어든 구체적 사례가 시작됩니다. (A)에서 이 문제를 해결하기 위해 광고 대행사를 고용하고, (B)에서 그 대행사가 효모를 비타민 공급원이나 천연 완하제로 재포지셔닝하여 매출을 올렸다는 결론으로 이어지는 (C)-(A)-(B) 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved.
ordered_passages: (A) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.

(B) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two.

(C) In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 농경으로 인한 정착 생활과 수렵 채집인의 이동 생활을 대조합니다. (C)는 수렵 채집인 어머니가 이동 시 아이를 업어야 했기 때문에 출산 간격이 길었다는 구체적 제약을 설명합니다. (B)는 반대로 정착한 농부들은 아이 이동 걱정이 없어 출산 간격을 단축할 수 있었다고 대조하며, (A)는 이로 인해 인구가 급증했고 이것이 노동력이 필요한 농경 사회의 이점이 되었다는 결과로 마무리됩니다. 본문에 명시된 답안(②)에 따라 순서를 구성하였습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. (A) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (B) However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. (C) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. (D) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (E) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.insertion_sentence: Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '미래 보상의 가치가 현재 보상의 가치보다 커야 한다'는 저축의 경제적 논리를 설명합니다. (A)는 미래의 보상을 위해 현재의 쾌락을 포기하는 행동(저축)을 설명하며, 주어진 문장은 이 행동이 성립하기 위한 가치 판단의 근거를 보충합니다. (B)부터는 '하지만(However)'을 통해 이러한 논리적 판단에도 불구하고 저축을 조기에 써버리는 예외 상황을 다루기 시작하므로, (B) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
questions.summary_sentence: High-performing individuals gain people's (A)____________ and connect with others, even if their skill is (B)____________ to their advice, fostering a desire to emulate them.
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 특정 분야에서 뛰어난 능력을 발휘하는 사람들은 그 전문성과 무관한 분야에서도 사람들에게 즉각적인 신뢰를 얻는다는 것입니다. 농구 선수나 배우의 사례처럼 사람들은 그들의 재능에 감탄하여 그들과 연결되고 싶어 하며, 그 결과 그들의 조언이 실제 전문 기술과 '무관할지라도(unrelated)' 그들을 '신뢰(trust)'하게 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 신뢰 / 무관한
② 감탄 / 관련된
③ 인기 / 수용 가능한
④ 적대감 / 적절한
⑤ 비판 / 받아들이기 어려운

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.summary_sentence: Despite the difficulties of lengthy labor and widespread sickness, the (A)____________ from a hunter-gathere lifestyle to agriculture during the New Stone Ages greatly (B)____________ population density and resulted in the establishment of the first towns and cities.
questions.explanation: 글의 내용은 수렵 채집 생활에서 농경 생활로의 전환이 노동의 어려움과 질병이라는 단점을 수반했음에도 불구하고, 인구 밀도를 높이고 도시와 문명을 탄생시키는 결과를 낳았다는 것입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 전환(transition) 혹은 이동이 들어가야 하며, (B)에는 인구 밀도를 증가(boosted)시켰다는 표현이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 변화 / 삭감했다
② 귀환 / 규제했다
③ 전환 / 높였다(신장시켰다)
④ 이동 / 통제했다
⑤ 강등 / 가속화했다

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: We tend to believe ___________________________________. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
subjective_conditions: 1. 13단어 이하로 완성할 것
2. 주어진 어구를 반드시 사용할 것(필요시 변형 및 2번 이상 사용 가능) [many / few / socially / desirable / traits / one]
3. 1,2 조건을 충족하지 못한 경우 0점 처리함
questions.answer: we have many socially desirable traits and few socially undesirable ones
questions.explanation: 사람들이 자신을 평균보다 낫다고 믿는 경향(레이크 워비건 효과)에 관한 글입니다. 빈칸에는 우리가 사회적으로 바람직한 특성은 많이 갖고 있고, 바람직하지 않은 특성은 거의 없다고 믿는다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 'we have many socially desirable traits and few socially undesirable ones'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then ____________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 1. 15단어 이하로 구성할 것
2. 주어진 단어를 반드시 한 번씩 사용할 것
[mental / pass / responsible / to]
3. 1, 2 조건을 충족하지 못한 경우 0점 처리함
questions.answer: pass on the genes which are responsible for this mental advantage to its descendant
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간의 지능이 경쟁과 갈등으로 인해 진화했다는 내용이므로, 상대를 기만하거나 이기는 지능적 우위를 가진 부족이 생존하여 그 지능적 우위를 가능케 하는 유전자를 후손에게 물려주는 것이 논리적이므로 pass on 등의 표현으로 작성합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 주제를 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Companies large and small have off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
subjective_conditions: 17단어 이상 22단어 이하로 작성할 것
주어진 어구를 반드시 한 번씩 사용할 것 (필요시 변형 및 2번 이상 사용 가능)
한 문장으로 작성할 것 (조건 1, 2, 3 미충족 시 0점 처리)
[어구: although / more / less / expect / having / still / computerized]
questions.answer: Although having been expected to be free from drudgery in a computerized society, people still have less time and more work.
questions.explanation: 컴퓨터 사회가 도래하면 기계가 힘든 일을 대신하여 인간에게 더 많은 여가 시간이 생길 것이라는 기대와 달리, 실제로는 기업이 소비자에게 직접 일을 떠넘기며 사람들은 더 적은 시간과 더 많은 업무를 가지게 되었다는 내용입니다. 주어진 어구들을 활용하여 '비록 ~일지라도'라는 의미의 Although와 '수동형 분사구문(having been expected)'을 사용하여 주제를 완성합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data enters' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attaching is big.
options: ① The Future of Digital Marketing
② The Benefits of Digital Archiving
③ The Sustainable Future of Digital Business
④ Digital Business: Not as Green as It Seems
⑤ Digitalization: Saving Trees and the Environment
questions.explanation: 디지털 비즈니스 활동이 종이 사용을 줄여 환경에 긍정적일 것으로 기대되었으나, 실제로는 데이터 저장 및 인터넷 사용에 막대한 전력(화석 연료)이 소모되어 탄소 배출을 증가시킨다는 내용이다. 따라서 디지털 비즈니스가 겉보기만큼 친환경적이지 않다는 제목이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 디지털 마케팅의 미래
② 디지털 아카이빙의 이점
③ 디지털 비즈니스의 지속 가능한 미래
④ 디지털 비즈니스: 보이는 것만큼 친환경적이지 않다
⑤ 디지털화: 나무와 환경을 구하기

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
options: ① Exotic Species: Great Leaders of New Chapter in Ecosystem
② The Toxic Power: Invaders Beat Indigenous Species
③ Population of Exotic Species Growth Requirements
④ The Hidden Meaning of Colors in Ecosystem
⑤ The Butterfly Effect of Mass Extinction
questions.explanation: 외래종인 회색 다람쥐가 도입되어 토착종인 붉은 다람쥐와 경쟁하게 되었을 때, 회색 다람쥐의 뛰어난 적응력(먹이 습성, 서식 밀도 등)으로 인해 토착종이 멸종 위기에 처하게 된 사례를 설명하고 있다. 따라서 외래종이 토착종을 이기는 위협적인 힘에 대한 내용이 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 외래종: 생태계의 새로운 장의 위대한 지도자들
② 유독한 힘: 침입자가 토착종을 이기다
③ 외래종 개체수 성장의 요구 조건
④ 생태계에서 색깔의 숨겨진 의미
⑤ 대멸종의 나비 효과

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad. There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
options: ① Nutrient balance is the key to a healthful diet.
② Eating the same healthy foods every day is best.
③ All fried foods are nutritionally bad for our health.
④ Sugar should be completely avoided for a healthy diet.
⑤ Eating only vegetables and fruits guarantees a healthy diet.
questions.explanation: 개별 식품을 '좋은 것' 혹은 '나쁜 것'으로 규정하기보다, 전체적인 식단에서 영양소의 다양성과 균형이 건강한 식단을 결정한다는 내용이다. 건강에 좋다고 여겨지는 음식만 먹어도 다양성이 부족하면 건강한 식단이 될 수 없다는 예시를 통해 영양 균형의 중요성을 강조하고 있다.
options_translation: ① 영양 균형은 건강한 식단의 핵심이다.
② 매일 똑같은 건강식을 먹는 것이 최선이다.
③ 모든 튀긴 음식은 영양학적으로 건강에 나쁘다.
④ 건강한 식단을 위해 설탕은 완전히 피해야 한다.
⑤ 채소와 과일만 먹는 것이 건강한 식단을 보장한다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how customers react to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether ⓐ<u>they</u> will repurchase the product (and whether they will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether ⓑ<u>they</u> will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so their satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of ⓒ<u>people</u> they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that ⓓ<u>they</u> are used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring ⓔ<u>their</u> satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ는 모두 구매를 한 '고객(customers/people)'을 지칭한다. 반면 ⓓ는 앞 문장에 언급된 '광고(advertisements)'가 물건 구매를 설득하는 데 이용된다는 맥락이므로 광고를 지칭한다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains ⓐ<u>to evolve</u> the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, ⓑ<u>possesing</u> a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, ⓒ<u>gives</u> your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over within each ⓓ<u>succeeding</u> generation. The tribe that could out-think tis opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to ⓔ<u>its</u> offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'A human tribe (that could out-think its enemies, even slightly)'이며, 이 문장에는 본동사가 없습니다. 따라서 현재분사 'possesing'을 과거형 동사 'possessed'로 고쳐야 문장이 성립합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 6월 31번]
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone ⓐ<u>knocked</u> on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an ⓑ<u>unexpected</u> guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly ⓒ<u>inappropriate</u> time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work ⓓ<u>finished</u>. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally ⓔ<u>increasing</u> stress levels.
questions.explanation: 영국 시인 콜리지(Coleridge)가 시를 쓰던 중 예상치 못한 손님의 방문으로 인해 영감을 잊어버리게 되었고, 결국 작품을 완성하지 못한 채로 남겨두게 되었다는 내용이므로, ⓓ 'finished(완성된)'를 'unfinished(미완성의)'로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 6월 39번]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less ⓐ<u>flexible</u>. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very ⓑ<u>inefficient</u> migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the ⓒ<u>old</u> rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the ⓓ<u>longest</u> childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood ⓔ<u>hinders</u> the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 유년기는 동물들이 환경에 대해 배우고 유연하게 대처할 수 있도록 도와주며, 문화적 정보를 전달하고 문화가 유전자보다 빠르게 진화할 수 있도록 해주는 기간입니다. 따라서 ⓔ 'hinders(방해하다)'를 'facilitates(용이하게 하다)'나 'allows(허용하다)'와 같은 단어로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 6월 34번]
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. (A) Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. (B) To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. (C) By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. (D) This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. (E) It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.insertion_sentence: Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'Only then(그러고 나서야 비로소)'은 앞 단계인 (B) 뒤의 내용, 즉 각 멤버가 독립적으로 아이디어를 평가하는 과정을 완료한 시점을 의미합니다. 따라서 평가가 끝난 후 팀이 모여서 옵션을 선택하고 정제한다는 내용이 (C)의 위치에 들어오는 것이 가장 적절합니다. (C) 뒤의 문장은 이러한 개별적 개발 및 평가 과정의 이점을 요약하며 글을 마무리하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 연결사로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. (A)_____________, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (B)_____________, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞부분은 미래를 위해 저축하는 이성적인 행동을 설명하지만, (A) 뒷부분은 계획보다 일찍 써버리는 예외 상황을 설명하므로 역접의 'However'가 적합합니다. (B) 앞 문장에서 의지박약의 사례를 언급했고, 뒤 문장은 이를 다시 한번 풀어서 설명하고 있으므로 '즉(That is)'이 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나 / 즉
② 그러므로 / 즉 다시 말해
③ 그럼에도 불구하고 / 게다가
④ 마침내 / 비슷하게
⑤ 더욱이 / 그럼에도 불구하고

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were seldom sufficient to support a full-time chief or village council. The development of agriculture changed work patterns. Early farmers could reap 3-10kg of grain from each 1kg of seed planted. Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided support for nonfarmers such as chieftains, village councils, men who practice medicine, priests, and warriors. It return, the nonfarmers provided leadership and security for the farming population, enabling it to continue to increase food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses. With improved technology and favorable conditions, agriculture produced consistent surpluses of the basic necessities, and population groups grew in size. These groups concentrated in towns and cities, and human tasks specialized further. Specialists such as carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their skills and became more efficient in their use of time and energy. The goods and services they provided brought about an improved quality of life, a higher standard of living, and for most societies, increased stability.
options: ① 초기 수렵-채집사회의 지도자들과 나머지 구성원들과의 역할 분담은 매우 분명했다.
② 농업의 발전은 직업의 분화에 거의 영향을 미치지 않았다.
③ 비농업인들은 공동체의 농업 생산량에 기여하지 못했다.
④ 농업기술의 개선은 인구 집단을 키웠으며 직업의 획일화에 기여했다.
⑤ 직업의 전문화는 삶의 질을 높이고 사회 안정성에 기여했다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 전문직 종사자들이 제공한 상품과 서비스가 삶의 질 향상(improved quality of life), 더 높은 생활 수준(higher standard of living), 그리고 증가된 안정성(increased stability)을 가져왔다고 설명하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.summary_sentence: As agricultural communities settled, mothers could give birth (A)__________ compared to hunter-gatherers, whose frequent movements necessitated (B)__________ between children.
options: ④ (A) at the same rate / (B) less frequent rate
⑤ (A) at longer intervals / (B) more frequent rate
questions.explanation: 글의 내용은 수렵 채집 사회에서는 이동성 때문에 아이를 4년에 한 번씩 낳아야 했지만(긴 간격), 농경 사회로 정착하면서 출산 간격이 2년으로 짧아져 더 자주(more often) 아이를 낳을 수 있게 되었다는 것입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 more often, (B)에는 수렵 채집인들의 특징인 longer intervals가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 매년 / 몇 년마다
② 덜 자주 / 더 짧은 간격
③ 더 자주 / 더 긴 간격
④ 같은 비율로 / 덜 빈번한 비율
⑤ 더 긴 간격으로 / 더 빈번한 비율

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It's comforting to believe that everything happens for a reason but sometimes heartbreaking things can happen and it seems like there is no possible way to explain the situation, or reason with it - not right now anyway. Situations arise sometimes that simply just do not make sense. You may find yourself asking, "how could something like this happen to someone like me?" or "why do bad things happen to good people?" While you may search for a meaning or a reason behind this pain, it's important to remember that sometimes there is no reasons, sometimes things don't happen for any reasons at all. Sometimes life can be cruel, even to the kindest hearts and the softest souls on this planet. However, please remember that _________________________________. If you can't find a reason for you pain right now - at least have trust that better things are on their way to you, even if it doesn't feel like it. Beautiful things are coming, please keep your heart open to them, and above all, please believe that you are worthy of it all.
options: ① there is always sunshine after the rain
② where there is a will, there is a way
③ living up to others is not important
④ everything happens for a reason
⑤ it's much easier said than done
questions.explanation: 이 글은 때로는 이유 없는 불행이 닥칠 수도 있지만, 지금 고통의 이유를 알 수 없더라도 언젠가 더 좋은 일(better things)이 올 것이라는 믿음을 가지라는 위로의 메시지를 담고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 '더 좋은 것들이 당신에게 오고 있다'는 맥락과 일치하는 희망적인 표현은 '비가 온 뒤에는 항상 햇빛이 난다(고진감래)'는 의미의 1번입니다.
options_translation: ① 비 온 뒤에는 항상 햇빛이 비친다
② 뜻이 있는 곳에 길이 있다
③ 타인의 기대에 부응하는 것은 중요하지 않다
④ 모든 일에는 이유가 있다
⑤ 말하기가 행동하기보다 훨씬 쉽다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. ⓐThey do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. ⓑIf a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. ⓒThinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. ⓓHowever, overestimating himself may generate adverse results and lead to unintended consequences, preventing himself from seeing situation objectively. ⓔSimilarly, thinking of himself as the kind of body who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 부모의 칭찬이 어린 아이들의 자아 존중감 형성과 행동 개선에 긍정적인 영향을 미친다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 아이들은 부모의 말을 깊이 믿고 이를 자신의 이미지로 통합하며, 이것이 문제 해결 능력이나 도움을 주려는 태도로 이어진다는 긍정적인 측면을 설명하고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓓ 문장은 자신을 과대평가하는 것이 객관적인 상황 판단을 방해하고 부정적인 결과를 초래할 수 있다는 '부정적인 영향'을 언급하고 있어 전체적인 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. ⓐBut loud sound can damage the auditory system largely over time. ⓑIn animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. ⓒBrain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. ⓓOther studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. ⓔThe point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 집중하는 대상이나 훈련하는 내용에 따라 뇌의 물리적 구조가 변한다는 '뇌의 가소성'에 관한 글입니다. ⓐ문장은 큰 소음이 청각 시스템에 손상을 줄 수 있다는 건강상의 주의사항을 언급하고 있으므로, 뇌의 구조적 변화라는 주제와 관련이 없습니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth.
ordered_passages: (A) World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it.

(B) This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supply exactly the right amount of both.

(C) Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 농지가 단일 작물 재배를 위한 완벽한 환경이 되도록 강요받는다고 언급합니다. (B)에서 'This(이것)'는 앞 문장의 내용을 가리키며 비료와 관개를 통해 달성됨을 설명합니다. (A)에서는 그 구체적인 수치(비료 사용 3배, 관개 능력 2배 증가)를 제시하며 심화 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 'Unfortunately'와 함께 이러한 비옥한 조건이 잡초(undesirables)를 끌어들인다는 역설적인 문제점을 제시하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath.(B) All children start off hating chili, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and ⓐ<u>knowing</u> that they will never experience any real harm. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is to have the pain always directly associated with a pleasurable reward.(C) The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus ⓑ<u>to be</u> painful but ultimately non-threatening. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this contest, ⓒ<u>where</u> survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment.(D) This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more ⓓ<u>remarkable</u> it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but ⓔ<u>what</u> we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure.

The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is to have the pain always directly associated with a pleasurable reward.

When the active ingredient of chillies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but ⓔ<u>what</u> we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 인간이 쾌락을 위해 고통을 찾는 현상을 언급한 후, (C)에서 그 핵심 원인인 '안전한 위협'이라는 개념을 설명합니다. (D)에서 이러한 효과가 고통에 대한 숙달감에서 온다고 보충하며 고추(chilli)를 먹는 습관을 예로 듭니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 아이들이 고추를 먹으며 쾌락을 배우는 과정과 동물과 대조되는 인간만의 독특한 특성을 결론지으며 마무리하는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 윗글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath.(B) All children start off hating chili, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and ⓐ<u>knowing</u> that they will never experience any real harm. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is to have the pain always directly associated with a pleasurable reward.(C) The key is that it is a 'safe threat'.
