The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more ⓓ<u>remarkable</u> it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but ⓔ<u>what</u> we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장에서 'but' 뒤의 절 'we are actually completely safe'는 주어, 동사, 보어를 모두 갖춘 완전한 문장입니다. 따라서 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what이 올 수 없으며, 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 that으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. (A)______________________, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
subjective_conditions: 다음 주어진 단어를 포함할 것(변형 가능)
come from
4단어로 작성할 것
questions.explanation: 지문의 핵심 주제는 고난을 통해 실력과 힘을 기른다는 것이다. (A) 뒤에 '가장 저항이 적은 길(편한 길)에서 오는 것이 아니라'라는 표현이 있으므로, 앞에는 '힘은 고난으로부터 온다'는 내용이 들어가야 한다. 조건에 따라 'come from'을 사용하고 'hardship'을 포함하여 4단어로 구성하면 'Strength comes from hardship'이 된다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고, 밑줄 친 부분의 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. (<u>자신이 통제권을 쥐고 있다는 느낌을 직원들에게 부여한 것이 그들이 업무에 끌어들이는 자기 통제력을 향상시켰다</u>.)
subjective_conditions: 1. 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 포함할 것(변형 가능)
how much / bring / to their jobs / give /
improve / employees / they
2. 14~16단어로 이루어진 한 문장으로 작성할 것
questions.answer: Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs
questions.explanation: '자신이 통제권을 쥐고 있다는 느낌을 직원들에게 부여한 것'을 주어(Giving employees a sense of control)로 설정하고, '향상시켰다'를 동사(improved)로, '그들이 업무에 끌어들이는 자기 통제력을'을 목적어(how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs)로 배열합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when thee was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests (A)______________ encourages (B)______________. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구매 수량을 제한하는 것이 판매를 촉진한다는 내용입니다. 실험 결과 구매 제한이 있을 때(scarce condition) 더 많은 구매가 일어났으므로, (A) 희소성(Scarcity)이 (B) 판매(sales)를 장려한다는 결론이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, which is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way that production could be made more efficient, known as the "division of labor." Making most manufactured goods involves several different processes using different skills. Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished. One worker could do all these tasks, and make 20 pins in a day. But this work can (A)___________________ with a number of workers each performing one task. Because each worker (B)____________________, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day - a huge increase in productivity from the 200 they would have produced before.
subjective_conditions: 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 포함할 것(변형 가능)
specialize / job / divide / seperate
(A), (B) 각각 4~6단어로 작성할 것
questions.answer: (A) be divided into (its) separate processes, (B) specializes in one job
questions.explanation: 문맥상 분업에 대한 설명으로, (A)에는 일이 '별개의 과정으로 나뉘다'는 표현이 들어가야 하므로 'be divided into separate processes'가 적절하며, (B)에는 각 노동자가 '한 가지 일에 전문화되다'라는 뜻의 'specializes in one job'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글을 읽고, 밑줄 친 부분의 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. (<u>당신이 하는 일은 당신이 스스로를 어떤 사람이라고 믿는지를 나타낸다</u>) - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
subjective_conditions: 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 한 번씩 포함할 것(변형 금지)
the type / do / what / an indication / that
14~16단어로 작성할 것
questions.answer: What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are.
questions.explanation: 주어 '당신이 하는 일(What you do)' + 동사 '나타낸다(is an indication of)' + 목적어 '~한 사람의 유형(the type of person)' + 수식절 '당신이 믿는(you believe that you are)'을 조합하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
options: ① 과잉 작업을 피하고 적절한 시점에 일을 마무리해야 한다.
② 어느 일이든 부분보다 전체를 파악한 후에 시작해야 한다.
③ 특히 그림을 그릴 때 과한 작업 후에는 꼭 휴식이 필요하다.
④ 작품성을 위해 그림에서 부분과 전체의 균형을 고려해야 한다.
⑤ 한 번에 하나의 일에만 집중해야 최대의 성과를 이끌어 낼 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 그림을 그릴 때 한 부분에만 집중하기보다 전체적으로 작업함으로써 언제든 멈출 수 있게 하고, 너무 많은 것을 쏟아부어 과잉 작업(overworked)이 되는 것을 경계해야 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 적절한 시점에 마무리를 지어야 한다는 ①번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
options: ① the evolution of sports marketing strategies
② the influence of social media on athlete branding
③ fan engagement strategies in major sporting events
④ trends in sports team ownership and financial management
⑤ the challenge of public disapproval in professional sports management
questions.explanation: 이 글은 스포츠 분야의 전문가들(선수, 감독, 경영진 등)이 비전문가인 팬이나 대중들로부터 그들의 업무 방식에 대해 많은 비판과 훈수를 듣는 상황을 설명하고 있습니다. 다른 전문직(의사, 회계사)과는 대조적으로 스포츠 경영 분야에서 대중의 간섭과 부정적인 피드백이 빈번하다는 것이 핵심이므로 ⑤번 '전문 스포츠 경영에서의 대중적 불만(비난)의 어려움'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 스포츠 마케팅 전략의 진화
② 소셜 미디어가 운동선수 브랜딩에 미치는 영향
③ 주요 스포츠 행사에서의 팬 참여 전략
④ 스포츠 팀 소유권 및 재무 관리의 추세
⑤ 전문 스포츠 경영에서 대중의 비난(반대)이라는 과제

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
options: ① the reason you taste sweet first
② a remarkable tongue's ability to distinguish taste
③ the importance of your tongue to taste five taste
④ role and distribution of taste buds in the tongue
⑤ misunderstandings and truths about the taste of the tongue
questions.explanation: 과거에는 혀의 부위별로 느끼는 맛이 정해져 있다는 '혀 지도'가 정설로 받아들여졌으나, 최신 연구에 따르면 이는 오해이며 실제로는 모든 맛을 혀의 모든 부위에서 느낄 수 있고 단지 감지되는 시간 차이가 있을 뿐이라는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 혀의 맛 감지에 대한 오해와 진실인 ⑤번입니다.
options_translation: ① 단맛을 가장 먼저 느끼는 이유
② 맛을 구별하는 혀의 놀라운 능력
③ 다섯 가지 맛을 느끼는 데 있어 혀의 중요성
④ 혀 안에서 미뢰의 역할과 분포
⑤ 혀의 맛 감지에 대한 오해와 진실

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
options: ① the mechanics of airplane safety systems
② the psychology of control in everyday life
③ the evolution of airline industry regulations
④ irrational concern of flying versus statistical safety
⑤ comparing travel costs between driving and flying
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 비행기 사고의 확률이 자동차 사고보다 훨씬 낮음에도 불구하고, 통제권의 부재로 인해 비행기 타는 것을 더 두려워하며 비합리적인 선택(운전)을 한다는 점을 지적합니다. 감정이 아닌 통계적 사실에 근거하여 판단할 것을 권하고 있으므로, 주제는 비행에 대한 비합리적인 걱정과 통계적 안전성을 대비시킨 ④번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 비행기 안전 시스템의 역학
② 일상생활에서 통제의 심리학
③ 항공 산업 규제의 진화
④ 비행에 대한 비합리적인 걱정 대 통계적 안전성
⑤ 운전과 비행 사이의 여행 비용 비교

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① Science's Echo: Why Publication Alone Is Not Enough
② The Effect of Funding on Scientific Research Outcomes
③ Unseen Science: The Impact of Unread Research on Progress
④ The Evolution of Scientific Methodology: From Hypothesis to Theory
⑤ Advancements in Lab Equipment: Enhancing Experimental Precision.
questions.explanation: 숲에서 나무가 쓰러져도 들을 사람이 없으면 소리가 아니라는 비유를 통해, 과학 논문도 단순히 출판되는 것에서 그치지 않고 독자에게 읽히고 이해되어야만 그 가치가 완성된다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '출판만으로는 충분하지 않은 이유'를 다룬 ①이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 과학의 메아리: 왜 출판만으로는 충분하지 않은가
② 과학 연구 결과에 미치는 자금 지원의 영향
③ 보이지 않는 과학: 읽히지 않는 연구가 발전에 미치는 영향
④ 과학 방법론의 진화: 가설에서 이론까지
⑤ 실험실 장비의 발전: 실험 정밀도 향상

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ① Effects of Nature Sounds on Psychological Well-being
② The Impact of Listening to Classical Music on Mood Disorders
③ Art Therapy as a Tool for Emotional Expression in Mental Health
④ The Role of Individual Music Therapy Sessions in Anxiety Reduction
⑤ Choral Therapy and the Benefits of Group singing for Mental Health and Well-being
questions.explanation: 집단 음악 치료, 특히 합창과 같은 공동 노래 부르기가 정신 질환을 앓고 있는 사람들의 삶의 질과 정신 건강, 정서적 상태를 크게 개선하고 소속감을 고취한다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 집단 노래 부르기(합창)의 이점을 명시한 ⑤가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자연의 소리가 심리적 안녕에 미치는 영향
② 클래식 음악 감상이 기분 장애에 미치는 영향
③ 정신 건강에서 감정 표현의 도구로서의 미술 치료
④ 불안 감소에 있어 개인 음악 치료 세션의 역할
⑤ 합창 치료와 정신 건강 및 안녕을 위한 집단 노래 부르기의 이점

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: We think ⓐ<u>that</u> we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us. One of the best examples of this ⓑ<u>is</u> the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Göbekli Tepe in Turkey. These ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, ⓒ<u>living</u> as hunter-gatherers. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, ⓓ<u>what</u> these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up ⓔ<u>radically</u> remaking the society itself. Things are not so different in our own time.
questions.explanation: ⓓ의 경우, 앞의 'so long, and so many successive generations'와 연결되어 'so ~ that(너무 ~해서 ...하다)' 구문을 형성해야 합니다. 뒤에 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 관계대명사/의문사 what이 아닌 접속사 that으로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓐ는 접속사, ⓑ는 수 일치(One of~ is), ⓒ는 분사구문, ⓔ는 동명사 remaking을 수식하는 부사로 모두 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it ─ you just see the ⓐ<u>distinct</u> outline of the moving string. Strings vibrating in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are very ⓑ<u>delicate</u> and don't push much air about. But if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is ⓒ<u>amplified</u> and the note is heard loud and clear. The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which ⓓ<u>vibrate</u> back and forth at the same rate as the string. The vibration of the wood creates more ⓔ<u>intense</u> waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. When the waves reach your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string.
questions.explanation: 기타 줄이 초당 수백 번씩 앞뒤로 움직일 때, 그 움직임이 너무 빨라서 눈으로 직접 볼 수 없다고 기술되어 있습니다. 따라서 움직이는 줄의 '선명한(distinct)' 윤곽을 보는 것이 아니라, 잔상으로 인해 '흐릿한(blurred/indistinct)' 윤곽을 보게 되는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. People have varying _____________ for organizing their time to balance work and personal obligations. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are minimized. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones ─ one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 일과 가정을 분리하는 것을 선호하는 사람들(분리자)怨ᄀ 통합하는 것을 선호하는 사람들(통합자)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 사람마다 자신의 시간을 조직하는 '선호도(preferences)'가 다르다는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가기에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 장비
한계
선호도
자격
요구 사항

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming ensures the soil remains ________________________________.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 돌려짋기(작물 순환)가 토양을 비옥하게 만든다는 내용을 다무고 있습니다. 따라서 이러한 농사 방식은 토양이 '건강하고 비옥한(healthy and fertile)' 상태를 유지하게 한다는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: 쵙쵙하고 축축한
건강하고 비옥허
고갈되고 척박한
무성하고 잡초가 많은
오염되고 산성인

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providing students with relevant texts they will be interested in. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and discovered ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books." The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been _____________________. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.
options: ① deeply enthusiastic about particular personal pursuits
② keenly interested in professional development
④ intensely focused on academic achievements
⑤ actively engaged in community service
questions.explanation: 난독증이 있음에도 불구하고 성공한 사람들의 공통점은 자신이 관심 있는 특정 분야에 대해 매우 열정적이었다는 것입니다. 그들은 종교, 수학 등 자신의 관심 분야를 더 알아내기 위해 탐독했습니다. 따라서 '특정한 개인적 추구에 깊이 열광적이었다'는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 특정한 개인적 추구에 깊이 열광적인
전문적 발전에 예리하게 관심 있는
환경 보존에 열정적인
학업 성취에 강렬하게 집중한
지역사회 봉사에 적극적으로 참여한

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session __________________________________________________. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ① is mainly about animals with emotional problems
② is only required for animals from the same parent
③ needs to be coordinated to the appropriate location
④ should be tailored to each animal's condition and needs
⑤ can be decided immediately by animal or human therapists
questions.explanation: 동물마다 개별적 차이가 있고, 환경적 요인이나 치유 목적(신체적 혹은 감정적)에 따라 반응이 다르다는 내용입니다. 따라서 모든 치유 세션은 '각 동물의 상태와 욕구에 맞춰져야 한다(tailored to each animal's condition and needs)'가 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: 주로 정서적 문제가 있는 동물들에 관한 것이다
동일한 부모에게서 난 동물들에게만 필요하다
적절한 장소에 조정될 필요가 있다
각 동물의 상태와 욕구에 맞게 조정되어야 한다
동물이나 인간 치료사에 의해 즉각 결정될 수 있다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. ⓐIf you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally ─ they are functionally blind. ⓑRaising the eyelids of a sleeping predator requires attention. ⓒSome visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. ⓓStimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. ⓔBut as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잠을 잘 때 외부 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않는 '지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)'의 특성과 그 기능에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ⓑ번은 '잠자는 포식자의 눈꺼풀을 들어 올리는 것은 주의를 요한다'는 내용으로, 수면 중 자극 처리의 저하라는 전체 흐름과 무관합니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
(B) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(C) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물에게 5가지 감각이 있다고 주장한 내용을 소개합니다. (C)에서 'However'를 통해 이 주장에 의문을 제기하며, 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 인간의 감각(고유 수용성 감각, 평형 감각)을 언급합니다. (B)에서는 인간을 넘어 '다른 동물들(Other animals)'의 특이한 감각(후각 시스템, 열 감지) 사례를 추가합니다. (A)에서 '이러한 사례들(These examples)'을 통해 감각을 한정된 종류로 명확히 나눌 수 없다는 결론을 내리며 글을 마무리합니다. 따라서 적절한 순서는 (C)-(B)-(A)입니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. (A) Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. (B) Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. (C) If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. (D) Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. (E) This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
questions.insertion_sentence: But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays.
questions.explanation: 글의 앞부분(B, C)에서는 환경이 좋지 않을 때 결정이 이상하게 뒤틀린 모양으로 형성되는 경우를 설명하고 있습니다. 주어진 문장은 'But(하지만)'으로 시작하며 '조건이 적절할 때 아름다운 모습(완벽한 형태)을 보게 된다'는 대조적인 상황을 제시합니다. (D) 뒤의 문장은 이 '아름다운 모습'이 만들어지는 구체적인 과정(느리고 안정적인 환경에서 원자들이 완벽하게 결합하는 과정)을 설명하고 있으므로, 주어진 문장은 (D) 자리에 들어가는 것이 흐름상 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. (A) In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. (B) Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. (C) The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street ─ a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. (D) Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites. (E) While they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.insertion_sentence: In contrast, walking, due to its slower pace, enables individuals to notice and appreciate finer details in their surroundings.
questions.explanation: (C) 문장에서는 자동차 운전자가 빠른 속도로 인해 세부 사항을 파악하기 어렵다는 점을 설명합니다. (D) 문장에서는 조깅하는 사람과 자전거 타는 사람이 '이러한 양극단(these polar opposites)' 사이에 위치한다고 말하는데, 여기서 양극단이란 앞서 언급된 운전자와 보행자를 가리킵니다. 따라서 보행자가 세부 사항을 잘 인식한다는 대조적 내용을 담은 주어진 문장이 (D) 앞에 들어가는 것이 논리적으로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.summary_sentence: The above explores how cultural diversity among workers can initially boost productivity through (A)___________ but may lead to communication challenges and (B)___________ if perceived as threatening native identity.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서는 문화적 다양성이 지식 파급(knowledge spillovers)을 통해 생산성을 높일 수 있다고 언급하므로 (A)에는 '정보 교환(information exchange)'이 적절하며, 후반부에서는 다양성이 국가 정체성에 위협이 되거나 사회적 갈등을 유발할 수 있다는 점을 언급하므로 (B)에는 '사회적 긴장(societal strain)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 기술 습득 ... 교차 문화 시너지
정보 교환 ... 사회적 긴장
역량 개발 ... 기술적 지체
문화적 통합 ... 경제적 격차
팀 협업 ... 환경적 압박

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements ─ what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life ─ as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born ─ often occupied by its parent ─ to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.summary_sentence: Life had to move places when the (A)___________ climate changed, and scientists know from fossils that even seemingly (B)___________ things moved during the period of climate change.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후가 변화함에 따라 생물종들이 생존을 위해 이동해야 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A)에는 기후가 '변화하는(dynamic)' 또는 '적응 가능한(adaptable)' 맥락이 올 수 있는데, (B)에는 나무나 따개비처럼 겉보기에 '움직이지 않는(immobile/fixed)' 생물들도 이동한다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 주어진 선택지 중에서는 (A) adaptable(적응 가능한/유동적인 환경에 맞춰 변화하는)과 (B) fixed(고정된/움직이지 않는)의 조합이 문맥상 가장 타당합니다.
options_translation: ① 역동적인 ... 성장하는
② 도달 가능한 ... 가시적인
③ 적응 가능한 ... 고정된
④ 역동적인 ... 고정된
⑤ 적응 가능한 ... 가시적인

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders ─ employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task─like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds─they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.summary_sentence: Frans de Waal argues that humans, especially scientists, use technical language to (A)___________ the resemblance between us and other animals and maintain a sense of (B)___________, a practice he calls linguistic castration.
questions.explanation: Frans de Waal은 인간이 다른 동물과의 유사성을 경시하고(downplay) 기술적인 용어를 사용하여 거리를 둔다고 주장합니다. 이는 인간이 가상의 사다리 꼭대기를 유지하려는 의도에서 비롯된 것입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 유사성을 '최소화하다(minimize)'가, (B)에는 꼭대기 자리를 유지하려는 마음인 '우월감(superiority)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 최소화하다 ... 친밀감
② 최소화하다 ... 우월감
③ 강조하다 ... 박탈
④ 강조하다 ... 소속감

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly─our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain healthy relationships with our negotiating partners at the same time. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
questions.summary_sentence: In everyday interactions, negotiating effectively is crucial for (A)___________ and (B)___________, particularly in today's interconnected and recurring exchanges.
subjective_conditions: a. (A)는 beneficial을 포함하여 3 단어로, (B)는 harmonious를 포함하여 3 단어로 쓸 것
b. 나머지는 본문 속 단어을 사용할 것(형태변형 가능)
※ 조건 위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함.
questions.answer: (A) achieving beneficial results(outcomes) / (B) maintaining harmonious relationships
questions.explanation: 이 글은 상호 의존적인 현대 사회에서 반복적으로 만나는 사람들과의 협상 시 '윈-윈(win-win)' 결과가 중요함을 강조하고 있습니다. 본문 마지막 부분의 'achieve successful results'와 'maintain healthy relationships'를 조건에 맞춰 변형해야 합니다. (A)는 'beneficial'을 포함하여 '유익한 결과를 얻는 것'이라는 의미로 'achieving beneficial results'가 적절하며, (B)는 'harmonious'를 포함하여 '화목한 관계를 유지하는 것'이라는 의미로 'maintaining harmonious relationships'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are─writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
questions.summary_sentence: Defining ability solely as performance in intellectual or specific skills can lead to the problematic view, that _____________________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: a. by, determine, achievements, exclusively를 포함하여 9단어 이내의 완전한 문장으로 쓸 것
b. 나머지는 본문에 있는 단어만 사용할 것.(형태변형 가능)
※ 조건 위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함.
questions.answer: One's self-worth is determined exclusively by the achievements
questions.explanation: 이 글은 능력(성취)이 자아 존중감의 유일한 결정 요인이 될 때 발생하는 문제점을 다루고 있습니다. 성취가 곧 그 사람의 가치가 된다는 내용을 조건에 맞춰 작성해야 합니다. '한 사람의 자아 존중감은 오로지 성취에 의해서만 결정된다'는 문장인 'One's self-worth is determined exclusively by the achievements'가 조건(9단어 이내, 제시 단어 포함)을 모두 충족하는 정답입니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [2.9점]
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore show your child good examples of life by your action. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
questions.summary_sentence: Children develop their value and character traits primarily by (A)______________________________________, so it is crucial (B)______________________________________ in daily life.
subjective_conditions: a. (A)는 observe, (B)는 demonstrate를 사용할 것 (형태 변형 가능)
b. (A), (B) 각각 6단어 이내로 작성할 것
※ 조건 위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함.
questions.answer: (A) observing good behavior of parents(B) to demonstrate good examples to them
questions.explanation: 아이들은 부모의 행동을 보고 배운다는 내용의 글입니다. (A)에는 아이들이 부모의 선한 행동을 관찰함으로써 가치관을 형성한다는 의미의 'observing good behavior of parents'가 적절하며, (B)에는 부모가 아이들에게 좋은 본보기를 보여주는 것이 중요하다는 의미의 'to demonstrate good examples to them'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 요지에서 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [2.9점]
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is not easy for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.summary_sentence: Moving can be particularly stressful for young children, so they need ____________________________ and support to help them adjust.
subjective_conditions: a. recognition을 사용할 것 (형태 변형 불가)
b. 본문의 단어를 사용하여 6단어 이내로 작성할 것
※ 조건 위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함.
questions.explanation: 이사는 아이들에게 큰 스트레스이며, 아이들의 과거 경험을 인정해주는 것이 중요하다는 내용입니다. 빈칸에는 아이들이 적응하도록 돕기 위해 필요한 것으로 '그들의 과거 경험에 대한 인정'이 들어가야 하므로, 본문의 단어를 활용하여 'recognition of their past experiences'로 완성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.*cortex: (대뇌) 피질(皮質)**hippocampus: (대뇌 측두엽의) 해마
options: ① Spatial Memory and Hippocampal Development
② What Is the Importance of the Brain Changes?
③ Drawbacks of the Physical Architecture of the Brain
④ The Impact of Focused Attention on Brain Structure
⑤ How to Develop Focused Attention and Growth and Expansion in Regions of the Cortex
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 집중된 주의와 반복적인 연습이 뇌의 물리적 구조를 재구성한다는 것입니다. 동물의 청각/시각 센터 변화, 바이올리니스트의 대뇌 피질 변화, 택시 운전사의 해마 크기 변화 등이 그 증거로 제시되었습니다. 따라서 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은 4번 '집중된 주의가 뇌 구조에 미치는 영향'입니다.
options_translation: ① 공간 기억과 해마의 발달
② 뇌 변화의 중요성은 무엇인가?
③ 뇌의 물리적 구조의 단점들
④ 집중된 주의가 뇌 구조에 미치는 영향
⑤ 집중된 주의력을 기르는 방법과 피질 영역의 성장 및 확장

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [24년 6월 40번]
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best ⓐ<u>to create</u>, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty in ⓑ<u>distinguishing</u> particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design ⓒ<u>has</u> made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects ⓓ<u>embraced</u> the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as ⓔ<u>those</u> without.*dissent: 반대
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 'While' 절의 주어는 'professionals(전문가들)'로 복수 명사입니다. 따라서 동사 'has'는 수 일치에 어긋나며 복수형인 'have'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 6월 21번]
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by ⓐ<u>adding</u> nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more ⓑ<u>productive</u> at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost ⓒ<u>increased</u> twofold; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also drawn the notice of certain agricultural ⓓ<u>desirables</u>. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as a field ⓔ<u>abundant</u> with necessities for plants by every random weed in the area.*monoculture: 단일 작물 재배**irrigation: (논, 밭에) 물을 댐; 관개
questions.explanation: 농경지의 풍부한 영양과 수분 조건이 잡초(random weed)와 같이 원치 않는 존재들을 끌어들인다는 맥락입니다. 따라서 'desirables(바람직한 것들/사람들)'가 아니라, 'undesirables(달갑지 않은 것들/잡초)'와 같은 부정적인 의미의 단어가 오는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show that you care. If you notice someone who is lonely, you cold go and sit with them. If you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down wit them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. A person's happiness comes from _____________. There are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. Even if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: 지문 전체의 내용은 타인에게 관심을 보이고 돌봐주는 작은 행동이 그 사람을 행복하게 만든다는 것입니다. 빈칸 뒷부분에서도 'someone cares(누군가 신경 써준다)'는 느낌이 사람을 기분 좋게 만든다고 설명하므로, 빈칸에 적절한 말은 '관심, 배려'를 뜻하는 concern입니다.
options_translation: ① 관심, 염려
② 의존

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to _____________________________________: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.*envision 계획하다

questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately.
ordered_passages: (A) Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options.

(B) This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.

(C) By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise.*anonymously: 익명으로 **surface: 드러내다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhood, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes.
questions.summary_sentence: The animals' childhood period provides an opportunity to learn about the environment, enhancing their (A)____________ to a changing environment, whereas birds born knowing their migration patterns tend to have less (B)____________ migration routes as environmental changes occur.
questions.explanation: 동물의 어린 시절은 환경에 대해 배울 기회를 제공하여 변화하는 환경에 대한 유연성과 (A)적응성(adaptability)을 높여줍니다. 반면, 본능적인 지침에만 의존하여 이주하는 새들은 환경 변화에 잘 적응하지 못해 (B)효율적인(efficient) 이주 경로를 갖지 못하는 경향이 있습니다.

② 무능력 ... 편리한
③ 안정성 ... 간접적인
④ 저항 ... 어려운
⑤ 유연성 ... 비효율적인

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 주제를 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오. [24년 6월 23번]
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
subjective_conditions: 1. hardship / life / importance를 반드시 사용할 것
2. 10단어 이내의 어구로 작성할 것

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [23년 3월 35번]
questions.passage: Whose story it is ⓐ<u>affects</u> what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at a certain event through another character's eyes, we will interpret ⓑ<u>it</u> differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that ⓒ<u>is</u> the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. ⓓ<u>Considering</u>, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we ⓔ<u>read</u> the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장은 명령문 형태가 되어야 문맥상 '생각해 보라'는 의미를 전달할 수 있습니다. 따라서 분사 형태인 Considering이 아니라 명령문 동사 원형인 Consider로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓐ는 간접의문문 주어(Whose story it is)에 따른 단수 동사 affects가 맞고, ⓑ는 앞에 나온 a certain event를 지칭하는 대명사 it이 적절하며, ⓒ는 선행사 the conflict를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 절의 동사로 단수형 is가 맞습니다. ⓔ는 가정이나 조건의 의미로 사용된 현재형 동사 read로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글을 읽고 ⓐ~ⓔ 학생이 아래와 같이 대화하였다. 글의 내용과 동떨어진 내용을 말한 학생을 고른 것은? [23년 6월 22번]

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Claims that local food production cut greenhouse gas emissions by reducing the burning of transportation fuel are usually not well founded. Transport is the source of only 11 percent of greenhouse gas emissions within the food sector, so reducing the distance that food travels after it leaves the farm is far less important than reducing wasteful energy use on the farm.
ordered_passages: (A) In other words, food coming from a distance can actually be better for the climate, depending on how it was grown. For example, field-grown tomatoes shipped from Mexico in the winter months will have a smaller carbon footprint than local winter tomatoes grown in a greenhouse.

(B) As two cases show us, farming methods, which are shown above, significantly influence the carbon footprint of food, highlighting the importance of holistic considerations in addressing greenhouse gas emissions. When food does travel, what matters most is not the distance traveled but the travel mode (surface versus air), and most of all the load size.

(C) Another example can be found in UK. In the United Kingdom, lamb meat that travels 11,000 miles from New Zealand generates only one-quarter the carbon emissions per pound compared to British lamb. It's because farmers in the United Kingdom raise their animals on feed (which must be produced using fossil fuels) rather than on clover pastureland.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 현지 식품 생산이 운송 연료 절감을 통해 온실가스를 줄인다는 주장이 근거가 부족하며 농장에서의 에너지 사용 절감이 더 중요함을 언급합니다. (A)에서는 그 예시로 멕시코산 토마토와 현지 온실 토마토를 비교하며 먼 거리 음식이 더 나을 수 있음을 설명합니다. (C)에서 'Another example'을 통해 영국 양고기와 뉴질랜드 양고기의 사례를 추가 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 'As two cases show us'를 통해 (A)와 (C)의 두 사례를 요약하며 결론을 맺는 것이 자연스럽습니다.
