questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village.
ordered_passages: (A) In return, the nonfarmers provided leadership and security for the farming population, enabling it to continue to increase food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses.

(B) The development of agriculture changed work patterns. Early farmers could reap 3-10kg of grain from each 1kg of seed planted. Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided support for nonfarmers such as chieftains, village councils, men who practice medicine, priests, and warriors.

(C) Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were seldom sufficient to support a full-time chief or village council.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 초기 수렵 채집 사회의 미미한 구조와 지도자에 대해 설명합니다. (C)에서 'Most of these leaders'는 주어진 글의 지도자들을 가리키며, 식량 잉여가 적어 그들도 직접 사냥을 해야 했음을 설명합니다. (B)에서 농업의 발전으로 잉여 식량이 발생하여 비농업 종사자들을 지원할 수 있게 되었다는 변화가 나옵니다. (A)에서 'In return'을 통해 비농업 종사자들이 지도력과 안보를 제공했다는 상호 관계를 설명하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 28. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)가 구체적으로 가리키는 내용을 각각 우리말로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. (A)<u>This old-school, adversarial approach</u> may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, (B)<u>such transactions</u> are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
questions.answer: (A) 한쪽에게만 유리한 협상(승패를 가르는 전통적인 협상 방식)(B) 일회성 협상 (다시 보지 않을 사람과 하는 일회적인 거래)
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 언급된 'the traditional, win-lose negotiating style'(승패를 가르는 전통적인 협상 방식)을 의미합니다.(B) 밑줄 친 부분 앞의 'a one-off negotiation'(일회성 협상)을 의미합니다.

questions.question: 29. 윗글의 요지를 보기의 단어를 모두 사용하고 주어진 조건에 맞게 영어로 작성하시오.
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. (A)<u>This old-school, adversarial approach</u> may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, (B)<u>such transactions</u> are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
subjective_conditions: 보기의 단어를 한 번씩만 모두 사용할 것
어형 변화 없음
하나의 단어를 본문에서 찾아 추가할 것
questions.answer: Effective negotiation demands a win-win approach to achieve success and maintain relationships
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 '성공적인 결과와 관계 유지를 위해 상생(win-win)하는 협상 방식이 필요하다'는 것입니다. 보기의 단어들과 본문에서 찾은 'win-win'을 조합하여 'Effective negotiation demands a win-win approach to achieve success and maintain relationships'를 구성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "My intention is to keep my employees from ⓐ<u>raising</u> their voices. I maintain a culture which ⓑ<u>is prevented</u> disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, ⓒ<u>published</u> weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly ⓓ<u>claiming</u> to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is the thing ⓔ<u>that</u> you must do to get something done."
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 주격 관계대명사 which의 선행사는 'a culture'이며, 이 문화가 의견이 표출되는 것을 '막는' 주체이므로 능동태인 'prevents'가 되어야 합니다. 또한 prevent A from B 구문에서 목적어(disagreeing viewpoints)가 뒤에 존재하므로 수동태를 쓸 수 없습니다. ⓓ의 경우 and를 기점으로 are asked와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 claim으로 고쳐야 어법상 더 적절할 수 있으나, 정답으로 제시된 ②번이 확실히 틀린 구조(동사 목적어 구조에서의 수동태 불가)를 가지고 있습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ⓐ<u>more</u> accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how ⓑ<u>complicated</u> a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people are ⓒ<u>proficient</u> in the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even ⓓ<u>underrated</u> how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, they should ⓔ<u>overlook</u> the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 전문가들은 초보자가 배우는 것이 얼마나 어려운지를 잊어버리는 '지식의 저주'를 겪으므로, 학생들의 관점에서 학습 과정을 바라볼 필요성을 '간과해서는(overlook)' 안 된다는 흐름이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 overlook은 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind.
ordered_passages: (A) The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition.

(B) The conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again.
(C) Then, given the two minds' features, how do emotions such as fear manifest? They originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 의식과 잠재의식이라는 두 부분을 소개한 후, (B)에서 먼저 '의식적인 마음'의 특징(통제 가능성, 감정에 의한 잘못된 결정)을 설명합니다. 이어 (A)에서 그와 대조되는 '잠재의식적인 마음'의 특징(빠른 행동, 감정 배제, 기억과 인식 담당)을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 앞서 언급된 두 마음의 특징을 바탕으로 공포와 같은 감정이 어떻게 나타나는지(의식에서 시작되어 잠재의식에 기록됨)를 설명하며 결론짓는 구성이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.summary_sentence: Research in the 1980s and 1990s revealed that taste buds are not (A)_________ by specialty; all flavors, such as sourness, can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, with the mechanism being (B)_________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 과거에 알려진 혀의 맛 지도가 잘못된 정보임을 설명하고 있습니다. 맛봉오리는 전문 분야에 따라 분류된(categorized/organized) 것이 아니라 입안 어디에서나 모든 맛을 느낄 수 있으며, 맛을 느끼는 데 작용하는 메커니즘은 장소가 아닌 시간(time)임이 밝혀졌습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '분류된'을 의미하는 categorized, (B)에는 '시간'을 의미하는 time이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 분류된 - 시간
② 제거된 - 장소
③ 과장된 - 기간
④ 구별되는 - 선호도
⑤ 조직된 - 위치

questions.question: 26. 다음 글 (B)에서 언급된 6명의 사람 중, 글 (A)에 묑줄 친 ⓞthose에 해당 하는 사람의 이름을 영어로 모두 숐시오.
questions.passage: (A) Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the realtime challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive. I hope you to be ⓞ<u>those</u> who are able to work the magic on yourself.(B) Eric had difficulty exercising regularly and wrote: I go to the gym and exercise with enthusiasm four times a week. Emma had trouble making friends and wrote: Why do other people seem not to be interested in me?  Tom would like to eat spicy foods well, but he used to get sick after eating them. He wrote: I never had such spicy food before, and I will have only bland tasting food. Lisa had difficulty finding Big Ben, the famous clock tower in London, during her traveling and wrote: I ask someone where it is located and finally visit there. Adam thought he would be dumped by his girlfriend and wrote: I do not consider our relationship more growing. Julia struggled to get ready for her final exam and wrote: I thoroughly prepare each subject and study more than seven hours a day. *등장인물: Eric / Emma / Tom / Lisa / Adam / Julia
questions.explanation: 글 (A)의 ⓞthose눤 자신이 겪고 있는 아려운 사황(도전 과제)을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸어 쓰고 실찜함으로엞 자신에게 마법을 부리는 사람들을 의묑합니다. Eric, Lisa, Julia는 자신의 문제를 긍정적인 현재형 문장으로 바꾸어 작성하였으며, Emma, Tom, Adam은 의문문이나 부정적인 단정을 쓰거나 회피하눤 문장을 썼습니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 괄호 (A)~(C) 안에서 바르게 짝지어진 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a (A)[low / high] level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his (B)[expert / expertise] on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. (C)[Endurance / Excellence] connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it. *endorsement: (유명인의 텔레비전 등에서의 상품) 보증 광고
questions.explanation: (A) 직업에서 '높은(high)' 수준으로 일하는 사람은 타인에게 즉각적인 신뢰를 얻는다는 내용이 오므로 high가 적절합니다. (B) 전치사 behind/of 뒤에는 명사가 와야 하며 문맥상 '전문 지식(expertise)'이 적절합니다 (expert는 '전문가'라는 사람을 뜻함). (C) 한 분야에서의 '탁월함(Excellence)'이 사람들을 연결해 준다는 문맥의 결론이므로 Excellence가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 낮은 — (B) 전문성 — (C) 탁월함
② (A) 낮은 — (B) 전문가 — (C) 인내
③ (A) 높은 — (B) 전문가 — (C) 탁월함
④ (A) 높은 — (B) 전문성 — (C) 탁월함
⑤ (A) 높은 — (B) 전문성 — (C) 인내

questions.question: 7. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. ⓐThey do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. ⓑCognitive sophistication plays a crucial role in reducing politically motivated reasoning. ⓒIf a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. ⓓThinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. ⓔSimilarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.*profound: 뜻깊은 **sophistication: 정교화(함)
questions.explanation: 이 글은 부모의 칭찬이 미취학 아동의 자아 존중감 형성에 미치는 긍정적인 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ②번 문장은 '인지적 정교함이 정치적 동기 부여된 추론을 줄이는 데 중요한 역할을 한다'는 내용으로, 아동의 자아상 형성과는 무관한 정치적 추론에 대해 언급하고 있어 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 두 개 고르면?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. ⓐ<u>By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of if a buyer will repurchase the product</u>. ⓑ<u>You'll also determine if the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you</u>. ⓒ<u>Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business</u>, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. ⓓ<u>People tend to believe the opinions of people that they know</u>. People trust friends over advertisements any day. ⓔ<u>They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them purchase products and services</u>. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising,
questions.explanation: ⓐ 전치사(of)의 목적어 자리에 명사절 접속사 if를 쓸 수 없습니다. whether로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓔ persuade는 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취하는 동사이므로 persuade them to purchase로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink. Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests __________ encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
questions.explanation: 구매 수량을 제한하는 실험에서 구매 제한이 있을 때(희소한 상태) 더 많은 캔이 팔렸다는 결과는 '부족함(shortage)' 또는 희소성이 판매를 촉진한다는 것을 시사합니다.
options_translation: ① 부족
② 홍보
③ 독특함
④ 가격 전략
⑤ 대량 생산

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is _______________. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life - which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
questions.explanation: 부유한 국가일수록 삶의 속도가 빠르고, 이로 인해 사람들이 긴급함과 시간 부족(time-poor)을 느끼며 스트레스를 받는다는 내용이므로 빈칸에는 '시간 압박(time pressure)'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 빈곤의 덫
② 건강 문제
③ 시간 압박
④ 생활 조건
⑤ 경제적 효율성

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the 1. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. _______________ yeast helped increase sales.*laxative: 완하제(배변을 쉽게 하는 약·음식·음료)
questions.explanation: 제빵용 효모에 대한 수요가 줄어들자 광고 대행사가 효모를 '비타민 공급원'으로, 그 다음에는 '천연 완하제'로 그 이미지나 용도를 바꾸어 홍보함으로써 판매를 늘렸다는 내용입니다. 상품의 시장 내 위치나 용도를 재정립하는 것을 의미하는 ⑤ 'Repositioning(재정립하는 것)'이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 정제하는 것
② 제외하는 것
③ 생산하는 것
④ 제거하는 것
⑤ 재정립하는 것

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from ____________________. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
options: ② taking the path of least resistance
③ relying solely on luck or chance
④ riding the waves ad pushing through the storm
⑤ avoiding challenges through mental preparation alone
questions.explanation: 진정한 힘은 고난과 투쟁을 통해 얻어지는 것이지, 쉬운 길을 택하는 것에서 오는 것이 아니라는 요지의 글입니다. 빈칸 앞의 'Strength comes from struggle, not from ~' 구문은 '힘은 투쟁에서 오는 것이지, ~에서 오는 것이 아니다'라는 의미이므로, '쉬운 길을 택하는 것'에 해당하는 ② 'taking the path of least resistance(가장 저항이 적은 길을 택하는 것)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 안락한 지대를 벗어나는 것
② 가장 저항이 적은 길을 택하는 것
③ 오로지 운이나 기회에 의존하는 것
④ 파도를 타고 폭풍을 뚫고 나아가는 것
⑤ 정신적 대비만으로 도전을 피하는 것

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or non-consciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. (A)__________, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. (B)__________, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞부분에서 자신의 정체성에 따라 행동하게 된다는 일반적인 원리를 설명하고 있으며, (A) 뒤에는 '유권자'로 정체성을 규정한 사람들의 구체적인 사례가 나오므로 'For instance(예를 들어)'가 적절합니다. (B) 뒤에는 정체성의 일부로 운동을 받아들인 사람의 또 다른 유사한 사례가 나오므로 앞의 예시와 병렬 구조를 이루는 'Likewise(마찬가지로)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: 게다가 / 유사하게
하지만 / 게다가
예를 들어 / 결과적으로
예를 들어 / 마찬가지로
따라서 / 뿐만 아니라

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it.
ordered_passages: (A) Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
(B) Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases.

(C) If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 수렵 채집 생활 방식이 권장할 만한 점이 많았음을 언급합니다. (B)는 그 구체적인 증거로 조상들이 풍부한 음식을 즐기고 질병이 적었음을 설명하며 자연스럽게 이어집니다. (C)의 'If this is true(이것이 사실이라면)'은 (B)에서 언급한 풍족하고 건강한 생활을 지칭하며, 그런데 왜 정착과 농경을 선택했는지 의문을 제기합니다. 마지막으로 (A)는 농경과 정착이 인구 밀도를 높이고 도시와 문명으로 이어지는 전환점이 되었음을 설명하며 마무리됩니다. 따라서 정답은 (B)-(C)-(A)입니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will.
questions.summary_sentence: The agents may judge or resolve to spend their (A)__________ in a certain way for the greatest (B)__________ but then act differently when (C)__________ for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.explanation: 미래의 보상을 위해 저축(savings)을 하지만, 의지의 박약으로 인해 즉각적인 즐거움에 대한 충동(impulse)이 생기면 원래 계획했던 이득(benefit)을 포기하고 조기에 저축을 사용한다는 내용입니다. (A)에는 미래를 위해 모아둔 savings, (B)에는 계획했던 효용인 benefit, (C)에는 계획을 무너뜨리는 impulse가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 시간 - 보상 - 유혹
저축 - 이득 - 충동
자원 - 안보 - 동기
에너지 - 편안함 - 기회
자금 - 휴식 - 욕구

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① The Paperless Office: A Green Revolution
② Digital Revolution: Transforming Business Strategies
③ Redefining Environmental Responsibility in the Digital Age
④ The Digital Advantage: Dealing with Environmental Concerns
⑤ Digital Shift: Hidden Environmental Costs of Going Paperless
questions.explanation: 비즈니스의 디지털 전환이 종이 사용을 줄여 환경에 긍정적일 것이라고 예상되지만, 실제로는 데이터 센터 운영을 위한 전력 소모와 탄소 배출 등 보이지 않는 환경적 비용이 크다는 점을 경고하는 글입니다. 따라서 '디지털 전환: 종이 없는 환경으로 가는 숨겨진 환경적 비용'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 종이 없는 사무실: 녹색 혁명
디지털 혁명: 비즈니스 전략의 변모
디지털 시대의 환경적 책임 재정립
디지털 이점: 환경적 우려 다루기
디지털 전환: 종이 없는 환경으로 가는 숨겨진 환경 비용

questions.question: 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will.
questions.summary_sentence: The agents may judge or resolve to spend their (A)__________ in a certain way for the greatest (B)__________ but then act differently when (C)__________ for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간과 동물이 미래를 위해 자원을 저축하지만, 의지력의 결핍(weakness of will)으로 인해 당장의 즐거움을 위해 이를 조기에 소비해 버리는 경향이 있음을 설명합니다. 따라서 행위자들은 최대의 이익(benefit)을 위해 저축(savings)을 계획대로 사용하려 하지만, 즉각적인 즐거움에 대한 충동(impulse)이 생기면 다르게 행동하게 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 시간 - 보상 - 유혹
② 저축 - 이득 - 충동
③ 자원 - 안보 - 동기
④ 에너지 - 편안함 - 기회
⑤ 자금 - 휴식 - 욕구

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. For example, among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
options: ① flexibility in animal adaptation strategies
② comparing efficiency in avian migration routes
③ the impact of climate change on bird migration
④ the importance of cultural information in animal behavior
⑤ the significance of childhood in animal environmental adaptation
questions.explanation: 동물의 어린 시절은 환경에 대해 배우고 적응하는 유연성을 제공하며, 이를 통해 변화하는 환경에 맞춰 더 효율적인 생존 방식(예: 이동 경로)을 습득할 수 있게 합니다. 즉, 어린 시절이 동물의 환경 적응에 있어 매우 중요하다는 것이 주제입니다.
options_translation: ① 동물 적응 전략의 유연성
② 조류 이동 경로의 효율성 비교
③ 기후 변화가 새의 이동에 미치는 영향
④ 동물 행동에서 문화적 정보의 중요성
⑤ 동물의 환경 적응에 있어 어린 시절의 중요성

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: To find the ⓐ<u>visible</u> potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas ⓑ<u>separately</u>. Next, you pool them and share thern anonymously among the group. To preserve ⓒ<u>independent</u> judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and ⓓ<u>elaborating</u> them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve ⓔ<u>collective</u> intelligence.
questions.explanation: 팀 내에서 평소에는 잘 드러나지 않는 '숨겨진' 혹은 '잠재적인' 능력을 발견하기 위해 브레인라이팅을 한다는 맥락이므로, ⓐ의 'visible(눈에 보이는)'은 'hidden'이나 'latent'와 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should _______________ as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
options: ① disregard the impact of disabilities
③ ensure that accessibility is a key consideration
④ prioritize functionality at the expense of accessibility
⑤ ignore the importance of accessibility in pursuit of innovation
questions.explanation: 이 글은 디지털 정보를 구축할 때 장애인들의 필요성(접근성)이 소외되고 있다는 점을 지적하며, 디자인 결정을 내릴 때 장애인과 비장애인 모두의 필요를 충족시켜야 한다고 주장합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '접근성이 핵심적인 고려 사항이 되도록 보장해야 한다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 장애의 영향을 무시하다
② 접근성보다 미학을 강조하다
③ 접근성이 핵심적인 고려 사항이 되도록 보장하다
④ 접근성을 희생하면서 기능성을 우선시하다
⑤ 혁신을 추구하며 접근성의 중요성을 무시하다

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 39번]
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a <u>constant learning process</u>.
options: ① adopting flexible treatments based on an animal's states
② sticking to one healing method applied to all animals
③ making up a prescription for sick animals in advance
④ perceiving an animal's behaviors as less integral
⑤ prioritizing emotional needs over physical ones
questions.explanation: 지문은 모든 동물이 서로 다르며, 환경이나 병의 종류(신체적 vs 정서적)에 따라 치유 세션에 다르게 반응한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 각 치유 세션은 동물의 구체적인 필요에 맞춰 조정되어야 하며, 이를 통해 치유자가 계속 배워나가야 한다는 점을 강조합니다. 'constant learning process(지속적인 학습 과정)'는 고정된 방식이 아니라 동물의 상태에 따라 유연하게 대응하며 배워가는 과정을 의미하므로 ①번 '동물의 상태에 기초하여 유연한 치료법을 채택하기'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 동물의 상태에 근거하여 유연한 치료법을 채택하는 것
② 모든 동물에게 적용되는 하나의 치유 방법을 고수하는 것
③ 아픈 동물들을 위해 미리 처방전을 만드는 것
④ 동물의 행동을 덜 필수적인 것으로 인식하는 것
⑤ 신체적인 필요보다 정서적인 필요를 우선시하는 것

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 32번]
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains transport materials and textiles into a city, which are then processed to benefit the economy, so do raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs travel along neural superhighways, undergoing processing to enable our comprehension based on our rich experiences of perceiving the world around us. Like a city, the brain processes unrefined data through complex functions that emerge from the connections among all regions rather than from any isolated part, resulting in <u>our conscious reality</u>.
options: ① manipulating refined materials using physical method
② contextualizing and making sense of the information
③ making the brain alert and deeply concentrated
④ managing to balance our worldview with others'
⑤ accumulating and filtering explicit information
questions.explanation: 이 글은 뇌의 작동 방식을 도시의 경제에 비유하고 있습니다. 경제가 한 곳에서 일어나는 것이 아니라 모든 요소의 상호작용으로 발생하듯, 뇌의 작용 또한 특정 부위가 아닌 모든 영역의 연결을 통해 일어납니다. 감각 기관의 신호들이 처리 과정을 거쳐 우리의 경험을 바탕으로 세상을 이해하게 만드는 결과물이 '우리의 의식적인 실제(our conscious reality)'입니다. 이는 정보를 맥락화하고 의미를 파악하는 과정이므로 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 물리적인 방법을 사용하여 정제된 재료를 조작하는 것
② 정보를 맥락화하고 이해하는 것
③ 뇌를 기민하고 깊게 집중하게 만드는 것
④ 우리의 세계관과 타인의 세계관 사이의 균형을 맞추는 것
⑤ 명시적인 정보를 축적하고 여과하는 것

questions.question: 3. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 33번]
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. <u>You and I are the descendants of the winners</u>.
options: ① The human mind has evolved a wide range of emotions.
② Mental endurance is an indispensable factor in becoming a winner.
③ Military tactics become important in contemporary conflicts.
④ We have a mental advantage in fostering empathetic leadership.
⑤ We have better legacy of courage and wisdom in competition.
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간의 정신이 다른 부족과의 경쟁과 갈등 속에서 진화했다고 설명합니다. 적보다 더 잘 생각하고 예측할 수 있는 정신적 능력이 생존과 승리의 결정적인 무기가 되었으며, 승리한 부족이 이 유전자를 후대에 물려주었습니다. 따라서 '우리가 승리자의 후손이다'라는 말은 경쟁에서 승리할 수 있게 해준 지혜(정신적 우위)와 용기의 유산을 물려받았음을 의미합니다. 선택지 ⑤가 이 맥락을 가장 잘 반영합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간의 정신은 폭넓은 감정을 진화시켜 왔다.
② 정신적 인내력은 승리자가 되는 데 필수적인 요소이다.
③ 현대의 갈등에서 군사 전술이 중요해진다.
④ 우리는 공감 능력이 있는 리더십을 함양하는 데 정신적인 이점이 있다.
⑤ 우리는 경쟁에서 용기와 지혜라는 더 나은 유산을 가지고 있다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ① How Controlling Workers Affects Their Morale
② Important Role of Uniform Design in the Workplace
③ Influence of Pay Scales on Employees' Performance
④ Empowering Workers Leads to Increased Productivity
⑤ The Shorter Work Hours, The More Employees' Self-discipline
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 스스로 결정하고 통제할 수 있다는 자율성(agency)을 부여했을 때 에너지와 집중력이 높아지고, 결과적으로 생산성이 20% 증가했다는 실험 결과를 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 직원들에게 권한을 부여하는 것이 생산성 향상으로 이어진다는 4번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 노동자를 통제하는 것이 사기에 미치는 영향
② 직장에서 유니폼 디자인의 중요한 역할
③ 임금 체계가 직원의 성과에 미치는 영향
④ 노동자에게 권한을 부여하는 것이 생산성 증대로 이어진다
⑤ 근무 시간이 짧을수록 직원의 자제력이 높아진다

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① Incan Huts as Rest Stops Along the Royal Roads
② Chasquis, the Incan Messengers Who Built Roads
③ Relay Races for Coping with Communication Defects
④ Incan Communication: The Role of Chasquis Messengers
⑤ Inca Postal Service of Delivering Packages with Precision
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잉카 제국에서 왕의 명령과 보고를 전달하기 위해 배치되었던 전령인 'Chasquis'와 그들이 정보를 전달하는 방식(릴레이 방식)을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 잉카의 통신 체계와 그 안에서의 Chasquis 전령의 역할을 다룬 4번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 왕실 도로를 따라 있는 휴게소로서의 잉카 오두막
② 도로를 건설한 잉카의 전령들, Chasquis
③ 의사소통 결함에 대처하기 위한 릴레이 경주
④ 잉카의 통신: Chasquis 전령의 역할
⑤ 물건을 정확하게 배달하는 잉카의 우편 서비스

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
options: ① Multiple childbirths discouraged people from settling in one place.
② Agriculture resulted in population decline in human societies.
③ Frequent movement influenced the adoption of birth control.
④ Longer birth gaps boosted the labor force in agricultural societies.
⑤ Hunter-gatherers could afford several children simultaneously.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 수렵 채집인들은 이동할 때 아이를 업고 다녀야 했기 때문에 한 번에 한 명 이상의 아이를 데리고 다닐 수 없도록 약 4년의 간격을 두고 출산을 조절했다는 내용이 나옵니다. 즉, 잦은 이동이 산아 제한(출산 조절)의 채택에 영향을 미쳤음을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 다산은 사람들이 한곳에 정착하는 것을 저해했다.
② 농업은 인간 사회의 인구 감소를 초래했다.
③ 빈번한 이동은 산아 제한의 채택에 영향을 미쳤다.
④ 더 긴 출산 간격은 농업 사회의 노동력을 증대시켰다.
⑤ 수렵 채집인들은 동시에 여러 아이를 감당할 수 있었다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are pervasive and shape what is considered "normal," guiding our social interactions. For instance, in Japanese society, it is ␐<u>customary</u> to bow as a gesture of respect and gratitude, even for minor acts of kindness like receiving a small gift or assistance. Although not legally required, failing to express gratitude in these situations is ␑<u>trivial</u> enough to be criticized. This expectation highlights a significant ␒<u>challenge</u> in cross-cultural communication: different societies have different norms. For example, while some cultures reserve "Thank you" for more significant favors, making it seem ␓<u>excessive</u> to thank someone for a minor act, others expect gratitude for even the smallest gestures. Understanding these ␔<u>variations</u> is crucial for effective communication across cultures.
questions.explanation: ␑의 trivial(사소한)은 문맥상 적절하준 않습니다. 일반적인 관습을 어기는 것은 비판받을 만큼 '심각한' 또는 '중완한' 것으로 여겨지므로 serious 등의 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: About 2,370 years ago, Aristotle proposed that there are five senses in both humans and animals: sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. But philosopher Fiona Macpherson argues that Aristotle ①␀<u>overlooked</u> some senses. For instance, humans also have a sense of their own body, ②␁<u>distinct</u> from touch, and a sense of balance, which is connected to both touch and vision. Additionally, animals possess senses that ③␂<u>defy</u> easy categorization. Many vertebrates have ④␃<u>identical</u> systems for detecting odors. Certain snakes can detect the body heat of their prey differently from other animals. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into ⑤␄<u>fixed</u> categories," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: ␃ identical(동일한)은 부적절합니다. 앞뒤 문맥은 동물들이 고정된 5가지 감각 체계로 분류하기 힘든 다양한 감각들을 가지고 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 척추동물들이 '동일한' 냄새 감지 시스템을 가졌다는 것은 동물마다의 독특한 감각 능력을 설명하는 글의 흐름과 맞지 않으며, 서로 다른(different/unique) 시스템을 가졌다는 의미가 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Brainwriting allows individuals to generate ideas independently without ①␀<u>alleviating</u> the influence of dominant personalities and the pressure to conform. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve ②␁<u>independent</u> judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might otherwise go ③␂<u>unnoticed</u>. This brainwriting process makes sure that no idea is ④␃<u>dismissed</u> without consideration and no perspective is left out. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve ⑤␄<u>collective</u> intelligence.
questions.explanation: ␀ alleviating(완화하는)은 부적절합니다. 브레인라이팅(brainwriting)은 지배적인 성격의 영향력이나 동조 압력을 '받지 않고' 독립적으로 아이디어를 생성하게 해주는 것이므로, 'without being subject to(영향을 받지 않고)' 혹은 'without the interference of(~의 간섭 없이)' 정도의 의미가 와야 합니다. 만약 'without'과 함께 쓰인다면, '완화하는 것 없이(without alleviating)'는 오히려 그러한 압력이 그대로 남아있다는 뜻이 되어 문맥에 맞지 않습니다. 글의 취지는 브레인라이팅이 부정적인 영향을 '피하게' 해준다는 것입니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: By working on every part of painting ⓐ<u>simultaneously</u> instead of focusing on one section at a time, you ensure that you can stop at any moment and the painting will still appear complete. Otherwise, artists frequently find it challenging to determine when to stop, as the temptation to keep adding more details to their work is ⓑ<u>strong</u>. Regularly stepping back from the painting to assess your progress is crucial for refining your artistic vision and ensuring that your desired outcome is ⓒ<u>achieved</u>. Overloading a painting with ⓓ<u>excessive</u> details can deteriorate its impact and result in an overworked appearance. If you're unsure whether your painting is finished, stepping away and returning to it later can be ⓔ<u>detrimental</u>, allowing you to gain a fresh perspective. After taking a break and returning to it, you can determine if there are any aspects that would benefit from further polishing.
questions.explanation: 그림이 완성되었는지 확신이 서지 않을 때, 잠시 물러났다가 나중에 다시 돌아오는 것은 새로운 관점을 얻게 해주어 도움이 되는 행동입니다. 따라서 '해로운(detrimental)'이 아니라 '도움이 되는(beneficial)' 등의 단어가 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save possessions or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, the agent sometimes ______________________________. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure arises.
options: ① experiences a temporary deviation earlier than intended
② sacrifices some instant gratification for a future reward
③ demonstrates that he possesses sufficient willpower
④ outweighs the discounted worth of the future reward
⑤ uses his savings to achieve the maximum benefit
questions.explanation: 미래를 위해 저축을 하지만, 즉각적인 즐거움의 유혹이 생기면 원래의 계획과 다르게 행동하는 경우를 설명하고 있습니다. 크리스마스 선물을 위해 모은 돈을 여름휴가에 써버리는 예시는 원래 의도보다 일찍 계획에서 벗어나는 것을 의미하므로 ①번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 의도했던 것보다 일찍 일시적인 일탈을 경험한다
② 미래의 보상을 위해 약간의 즉각적인 만족을 희생한다
③ 충분한 의지력을 가지고 있음을 보여준다
④ 미래 보상의 할인된 가치보다 더 큰 비중을 둔다
⑤ 최대의 이익을 얻기 위해 저축을 사용한다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Likewise it continued to change the perception of yeast in the minds of consumers by ________________________________________.
options: ① neglecting consumer preferences for its health benefits
② outsourcing advertising workload to a less reputable agency
③ emphasizing its various applications to different targets
④ seeking advantages over a competing advertising agency
⑤ appealing to bread lovers with conventional marketing methods
questions.explanation: Fleischmann사의 효모 광고 사례를 통해, 제품의 용도를 제빵 재료에서 비타민 공급원, 그리고 천연 완하제로 계속해서 변화시키며 마케팅한 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 제품의 다양한 용도를 강조하여 새로운 소비층을 공략한 것이므로 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 건강상의 이점에 대한 소비자 선호도를 무시함으로써
② 광고 업무를 평판이 좋지 않은 대행사에 외주 줌으로써
③ 서로 다른 대상을 향한 그것의 다양한 용도를 강조함으로써
④ 경쟁 광고 대행사에 비해 우위를 점함으로써
⑤ 전통적인 마케팅 방법으로 빵 애호가들에게 호소함으로써

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: ________________________________________. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① advanced techniques and equipment have been emphasized in all sports
② there has been a persistent reluctance to make adjustments for children in sports
③ various sports have introduced modified versions suited for children's abilities
④ sports teams offer mentorship programs to help children overcome challenges
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린아이들이 성인용 스포츠 환경에서 경기하는 것의 어려움을 인식하고, 아이들의 눈높이에 맞게 스포츠 환경과 장비를 조정한 사례들(T볼, 플래그 풋볼, 주니어 축구, 어린이용 테니스 등)을 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 상식이 통했다는 말 뒤에는 '다양한 스포츠들이 아이들의 능력에 적합한 수정된 형태를 도입했다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 스포츠에서 진보된 기술과 장비가 강조되어 왔다
② 스포츠에서 아이들을 위해 조정하는 것에 대해 지속적인 꺼림이 있었다
③ 다양한 스포츠들이 아이들의 능력에 적합한 수정된 형태를 도입해 왔다
④ 스포츠 팀들이 아이들이 어려움을 극복하도록 돕기 위해 멘토링 프로그램을 제공한다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. ⓐA mobile creature might move around throughout its life. ⓑBut even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life. ⓒFossil evidence indicates that trees such as maple shifted their ranges over relatively short periods in response to changing environmental conditions. ⓓMoreover, studies have shown that certain species are particularly susceptible to changes in temperature. ⓔAll of them highlight the dynamic nature of ecosystems and the capacity of organisms to migrate and adjust to changing climates over time.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화에 따라 생물 종이 자신에게 적합한 환경을 찾아 이동하거나 분산하며 적응한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ는 모두 생물 종의 이동 가능성과 기후 변화에 따른 서식지 이동을 설명하고 있으나, ⓓ는 단순히 특정 종이 온도 변화에 취약하다는 점만을 언급하고 있어 전체적인 흐름인 '이동을 통한 적응'과는 거리가 멉니다.

questions.question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible.
ordered_passages: (A) These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps.

(B) Among migratory bird species those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes.

(C) By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 유년기가 동물이 환경에 대해 배우고 유연성을 가질 수 있게 해준다는 점을 제시합니다. (B)에서는 이와 반대로 유년기 없이 태생적 지시(하드웨어)에만 의존하는 철새들이 비효율적인 경로를 가질 수 있다는 문제를 제기합니다. (A)는 이러한 새들이 환경 변화에 적응하지 못하고 기존의 규칙만을 고수한다는 부연 설명을 제공합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서는 긴 유년기를 보내며 부모로부터 배우는 새들이 더 효율적이고 유연하게 적응한다는 결론을 내리며 주어진 글의 주제를 뒷받침합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.summary_sentence: Crop rotation involves farmers (A)__________ the types of crops in a specific sequence, with each crop (B)__________ the soil for the next crop.
questions.explanation: 본문은 윤작(Crop rotation)이 정해진 순서에 따라 작물을 번갈아 심는 과정이며, 이를 통해 토양이 건강하게 유지(enrich)된다는 점을 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '교대로 심다/번갈아 하다'는 의미의 alternating이 적절하고, (B)에는 토양을 '비옥하게 하다/영양을 공급하다'는 의미의 nourishing이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 수확하는 ... 심는
경작하는 ... 저하시키는
교대로 심는 ... 영양분을 공급하는
바꾸는 ... 고갈시키는

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.summary_sentence: Drowsiness is the state of reduced (A)__________ during sleep, emphasizing the (B)__________ phase between wakefulness and deeper sleep states.
questions.explanation: 졸음(Drowsiness)은 수면 중 외부 자극에 대한 반응이나 감각이 줄어든 상태이므로 (A)에는 sensitivity(민감도) 또는 responsiveness(반응성)가 적절합니다. 또한 졸음은 깨어 있는 상태와 깊은 잠 사이의 '과도기적' 단계라고 본문에 언급(intermediate state)되어 있으므로 (B)에는 transitional(과도기적인)이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 반응성 ... 정지된
② 참여 ... 잠재의식의
③ 명상 ... 중간의
④ 의지 ... 변동하는
⑤ 민감도 ... 과도기적인

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a ⓐ<u>vital</u> advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military ⓑ<u>advantage</u>. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more ⓒ<u>decisive</u> than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each ⓓ<u>following</u> generation. The tribe that could out- think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its ⓔ<u>ancestors</u>. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간의 정신이 경쟁과 갈등을 통해 진화해왔으며, 사고 능력이 뛰어난 부족이 생존 경쟁에서 이겨 그 유전자를 다음 세대에 물려주었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 뛰어난 부족은 그들의 정신적 이점을 '조상(ancestors)'이 아닌 '후손'에게 물려주었을 것이므로, ⓔ의 ancestors는 descendants로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting.
ordered_passages: (A) Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise.

(B) This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.

(C) The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 '브레인라이팅(brainwriting)'이라는 새로운 프로세스를 소개합니다. (C)에서 이 프로세스의 첫 단계인 개별적인 아이디어 생성과 익명 공유 과정을 설명합니다. (A)에서는 그 이후(Only then) 팀이 모여서 아이디어를 선택하고 다듬는 과정을 설명하며, 개별 평가의 장점을 언급합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 브레인라이팅 과정의 전체적인 효과와 의의를 정리하며 마무리하는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency-a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision­making authority-can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly­line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self­discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ① The Role of Uniform Design in Manufacturing
② The Effects of Shorter Breaks on Employee Performance
③ Empowering Employees: The Key to Increased Productivity
④ Scientific Method to Increase the Power of Empowerment
⑤ How to Improve Manufacturing Processes Efficiently
questions.explanation: 이 글은 직원들에게 스스로 통제하고 있다는 느낌(sense of agency)이나 결정권을 부여하는 것이 업무 에너지와 집중력을 높여 생산성을 향상시킨다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 오하이오 제조 공장의 사례를 통해 자율권 부여가 생산성 20% 증가로 이어졌음을 보여주므로 제목으로는 '직원에게 권한 부여하기: 생산성 증대의 열쇠'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 제조 분야에서 유니폼 디자인의 역할
② 짧은 휴식 시간이 직원 성과에 미치는 영향
③ 직원에게 권한 부여하기: 생산성 증대의 열쇠
④ 권한 부여의 힘을 키우기 위한 과학적 방법
⑤ 제조 공정을 효율적으로 개선하는 방법

questions.question: 12. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸의 영어 질문에 대한 답으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.Q: Why were farming societies able to have more children compared to hunter-gatherer societies?
options: ① They had access to better medical care and nutrition.
② They did not have to move frequently and could care for multiple young children at once.
③ They had fewer predators threatening their children.
④ Farming communities had a lower fertility rate.
⑤ Hunter-gatherer societies preferred to scatter families for easier mobility.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 수렵 채집인들은 이동할 때 아이를 업고 다녀야 했기에 출산 간격이 길었으나, 농경 사회는 정착 생활을 하므로 아이를 멀리 이동시킬 걱정이 없어 출산 간격을 단축할 수 있었다고 설명합니다. 따라서 ②번 '그들은 자주 이동할 필요가 없었고 동시에 여러 명의 어린 아이들을 돌볼 수 있었다'가 질문에 대한 올바른 답입니다.
options_translation: ① 그들은 더 나은 의료 서비스와 영양에 접근할 수 있었다.
② 그들은 자주 이동할 필요가 없었고 한 번에 여러 어린 아이들을 돌볼 수 있었다.
③ 그들의 아이들을 위협하는 포식자가 더 적었다.
④ 농경 공동체는 더 낮은 출산율을 가졌다.
⑤ 수렵 채집 사회는 쉬운 이동을 위해 가족을 흩어놓는 것을 선호했다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.summary_sentence: Despite advancements in digital information, many projects fail to address the (A)_____________ of people with disabilities, limiting the (B)_____________ of valuable resources.
questions.explanation: 지문은 디지털 정보 구축 시 장애인들의 '요구(needs)'가 무시되는 경우가 많아 귀중한 자원이 그들에게는 무용지물이 된다는 점을 지적합니다. 따라서 요약문의 (A)에는 'needs', (B)에는 이러한 자원의 이용 가능성 혹은 '접근성(accessibility)'이 제한된다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 능력 / 가용성
② 요구사항 / 복잡성
③ 기대 / 다양성
④ 요구 / 접근성
⑤ 권리 / 투명성

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① Manual Skill: A Partnership Reshaping Brain Morphology
② The Relationship Between Memory Formation and Attentional Focus
③ The Transformative Power of Focused Attention on Brain Architecture
④ The Impact of Investing in Art on Brain Development
questions.explanation: 지문은 집중된 주의와 반복적인 연습이 뇌의 물리적 구조를 재구성한다는 과학적 증거들을 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 '뇌 구조에 대한 집중된 주의의 변화시키는 힘'이라는 제목이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 손의 기술: 뇌 형태를 재구성하는 파트너십
② 기억 형성과 주의 집중 사이의 관계
③ 집중된 주의가 뇌 구조에 미치는 변화의 힘
④ 예술 투자가 뇌 발달에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (A)______________, the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (B)______________, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.*envision: 계획하다
options: ⑤ On the other hand / Furthermore
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 미래의 소비를 위해 현재의 즐거움을 포기한다고 했으므로, 그 결과 미래 보상의 가치가 현재보다 커야 한다는 인과관계가 성립하므로 'Hence(따라서)'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞 문장에서 '의지의 박약'의 예시를 들었고, 뒷 문장에서 이를 다시 구체적으로 설명(가장 큰 이익을 위해 저축하기로 결심하지만 유혹이 나타나면 다르게 행동함)하고 있으므로 부연 또는 재진술을 나타내는 'Namely(즉)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 한편 / 다시 말해서
② 결과적으로 / ~에도 불구하고
③ 게다가 / 그러므로
④ 따라서 / 즉
⑤ 반면에 / 더욱이

questions.question: 3. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "that lovely poem didn't get written because someone knocked on the door."가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he said "<u>that lovely poem didn't get written because someone knocked on the door</u>." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.*lament: 슬퍼하다
options: ① Psychological support can have significant consequences.
② Boosting the flow of thought and creativity prevents potentially bad work from being completed.
③ Disruptions make critical opportunities for creating something valuable.
④ The key to success on productivity lies on decreasing stress levels.
⑤ Interruptions can have detrimental effects on professional and personal productivity.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 문장은 방해(누군가 문을 두드림)로 인해 창작 활동(아름다운 시를 쓰는 것)이 중단된 상황을 비유적으로 나타냅니다. 글 전체의 주제가 방해(interruptions)가 생산성과 스트레스에 미치는 부정적인 영향에 관한 것이므로, ⑤번이 가장 적절한 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 심리적 지지는 중대한 결과를 가져올 수 있다.
② 사고의 흐름과 창의성을 높이는 것은 잠재적으로 나쁜 작품이 완성되는 것을 막는다.
③ 방해는 가치 있는 것을 창조하기 위한 중요한 기회를 만든다.
④ 생산성 성공의 열쇠는 스트레스 수준을 낮추는 데 있다.
⑤ 방해는 전문적이고 개인적인 생산성에 해로운 영향을 미칠 수 있다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
options: ① 고난과 도전을 통해서 힘과 실력을 쌓을 수 있다.
② 운동선수들은 좋은 장비만으로 승리 할 수 있다.
③ 운동선수에게 마인드 컨트롤이 가장 중요하다.
④ 정신적 준비와 전략은 성공에 있어서 중요하지 않다.
⑤ 실력을 향상시키기 위해서 도전보다 쉬운 길을 택하는 것이 더 효과적이다.
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에서 'Strength comes from struggle(힘은 투쟁으로부터 나온다)' 그리고 'Hardship will be the greatest teacher(고난은 인생에서 최고의 스승이 될 것이다)'라고 언급하며 고난과 도전을 통한 성장의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.*monoculture: 단일 작물 재배**irrigation: (논,밭에) 물을 댐; 관개
options: ① Fertilizers and Irrigation: Feeding Crops and Deleting Weeds
② Modern Farming Efficiency: Killing Two Birds with One Stone
③ How to Utilize Fertilizers All around the World
④ The Hidden Costs of Monoculture Farming: A Weedy Dilemma
⑤ Luxury Fields in Need of Optimal Farming Conditions
questions.explanation: 농지에 비료와 관개를 통해 영양분과 물을 풍부하게 공급하여 단일 작물 재배에 최적의 환경을 만들었으나, 이로 인해 잡초들에게도 매력적인 환경이 되어 잡초 문제가 발생한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '단일 작물 재배의 숨겨진 비용: 잡초 딜레마'인 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 비료와 관개: 작물에게 영양을 주고 잡초를 제거하기
② 현대 농업 효율성: 일석이조
③ 전 세계적으로 비료를 활용하는 방법
④ 단일 작물 재배의 숨겨진 비용: 잡초 딜레마
⑤ 최적의 농업 조건이 필요한 호화로운 들판

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO2, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① Digital Documents Should Be Preferred to Paper Based Ones
② What Makes Digital Businesses Attractive to Workplaces?
③ Don't Let the Carbon Footprint Fool You!
④ The Impact of Digital Businesses on the Environment: Worse than Imagined
⑤ Business Activities: Not Simply a Matter of Fossil Fuels
questions.explanation: 디지털 비즈니스가 종이 소비를 줄여 환경에 덜 해로울 것이라고 생각하지만, 실제로는 데이터 센터의 화석 연료 사용과 이메일 전송 등으로 인한 탄소 배출이 상당하다는 점을 지적하는 글입니다. 따라서 ④ '디지털 비즈니스가 환경에 미치는 영향: 상상보다 나쁘다'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 디지털 문서가 종이 기반 문서보다 선호되어야 한다
② 무엇이 디지털 비즈니스를 작업장에서 매력적으로 만드는가?
③ 탄소 발자국에 속지 마라!
④ 디지털 비즈니스가 환경에 미치는 영향: 상상보다 나쁘다
⑤ 비즈니스 활동: 단순히 화석 연료만의 문제가 아니다

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
options: ① 초기 수렵 채집 사회는 풍족한 식량을 누리고 질병에 걸리는 일도 거의 없었다.
② 많은 인류가 영구적으로 마을에 정착하여 농업을 발달시킨 명확한 이유가 있다.
③ 전염병이 처음 뿌리를 내린 곳은 농경 마을이었다.
④ 정착지와 농업의 발전은 인구 밀도의 증가로 이어졌다.
⑤ 신석기 시대는 최초의 마을과 도시가 성장하는 길을 열었다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture'라고 언급하며, 수렵 채집 생활이 유리함에도 불구하고 왜 인류가 정착 농업을 택했는지는 명확하지 않다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ②번은 지문의 내용과 정면으로 배치됩니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 brainwriting에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ① 팀의 숨겨진 잠재력을 찾으려면 브레인스토밍 대신 brainwriting으로 전환하는 것이 좋다.
② 모든 사람에게 개별적으로 아이디어를 내도록 요청한다.
③ 아이디어들을 모으고 그룹 내에서 이름을 밝히고 공유한다.
④ 각 멤버는 독립적인 판단을 위해 스스로 아이디어를 평가한다.
⑤ 집단 지성을 달성하는 데 어려움을 겪는 그룹에 특히 효과적이다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group.'라고 명시되어 있습니다. 'anonymously'는 '익명으로'라는 뜻이므로, 이름을 밝히고 공유한다는 ③번은 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that ________________________________________ as we make design decisions.
options: ① we should always keep everyone updated
② the needs of people with disabilities are rarely overlooked
③ what the disabled require tends to make audience challenged
④ our first project can make a significant difference
⑤ the largest possible users need to be considered
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 디지털 정보를 구축할 때 장애인을 포함한 다양한 사용자들의 요구가 소외되지 않아야 한다는 것입니다. 따라서 디자인 결정을 내릴 때 '가능한 최대의 사용자층이 고려되어야 한다'는 내용의 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리는 항상 모든 사람에게 최신 정보를 제공해야 한다
② 장애인의 요구사항은 거의 간과되지 않는다
③ 장애인이 요구하는 것은 청중을 어렵게 만드는 경향이 있다
④ 우리의 첫 번째 프로젝트가 큰 차이를 만들 수 있다
⑤ 가능한 최대의 사용자들이 고려될 필요가 있다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.*envision: 계획하다
questions.summary_sentence: Humans and animals often save for the future, but sometimes (A)__________ to immediate temptations and use their savings prematurely, reflecting (the) (B)__________ of will.
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간과 동물이 미래를 위해 저축하지만, 때때로 눈앞의 유혹에 굴복하여 저축한 것을 미리 사용해 버리는 현상을 '의지의 박약(weakness of will)'의 예로 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '굴복하다'라는 의미의 yield가, (B)에는 '박약함/약함'이라는 의미의 weakness가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 반응하다 - 힘
② 달아나다 - 통제
③ 굴복하다 - 박약함
④ 항복하다 - 힘
⑤ 반대하다 - 박약함

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.summary_sentence: While birds knowing how to migrate by instinct have difficulty in (A)__________ and finding efficient routes, that's not the case for those with childhood, which seems to (B)__________ useful information sharing.
questions.explanation: 본문은 유년기가 있는 동물(새)들이 환경 변화에 더 유연하게 적응하고 효율적인 이동 경로를 찾는다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 본능에만 의존하는 새들은 환경 변화에 '적응/조정(adjusting)'하는 데 어려움을 겪는 반면, 유년기를 거치는 새들은 문화적 정보 공유를 통해 이를 '촉진(promote)'한다는 맥락이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 조정하는 것 - 촉진하다
② 정착하는 것 - 방해하다
③ 적응하는 것 - 낙담시키다
④ 경쟁하는 것 - 격려하다
⑤ 지시하는 것 - 용이하게 하다

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 우리말을 영어로 바꾸어 표현하시오. (아래의 조건 반드시 반영)
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. <u>적대적인 적 부족이 언제 어디서 공격할지 예측하는 능력은 부족에게 군사적 우위를 가져다 준다</u>. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
subjective_conditions: 제시된 표현(11개)을 한 번씩만 모두 사용
필요시 어형 변화
(어형변화와 무관하게) 새로운 단어 추가 금지
'간접의문문' 사용
vocabulary_box: might strike / enemy tribe / your tribe /
questions.answer: The ability to predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike gives your tribe a military advantage
