questions.explanation: 주어인 '적대적인 적 부족이 언제 어디서 공격할지 예측하는 능력'을 영작할 때 'the ability to predict' 뒤에 간접의문문 'where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike'를 연결해야 합니다. 동사는 단수 주어(The ability)에 맞추어 'gives'로 어형 변화가 필요하며, 목적어인 'your tribe'와 직접목적어인 'a military advantage'를 순서대로 배치합니다.

questions.question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved.
ordered_passages: (A) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.(B) In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time.(C) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 수렵 채집인들이 이동할 때 소유물을 모두 운반해야 했다는 내용이 나옵니다. (B)에서 '특히(In particular)' 어머니들이 어린 아이들을 옮겨야 했다는 점을 구체적으로 설명하며 출산 간격이 길 수밖에 없었던 이유를 설명합니다. 이와 대조적으로 (C)에서 정착 생활을 하는 농부들은 아이들을 먼 거리로 옮길 걱정이 없어 출산 간격이 짧아졌음을 언급하고, (A)의 '이것(This)'이 (C)의 짧아진 출산 간격을 받아 인구 증가와 농경 사회의 노동력 확보로 연결되는 구조가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes ________________________ to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
options: ② for physical abilities in battle
④ responsible for their mastery of martial arts.
⑤ related with their ability to craft advanced weaponry
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 인간의 지능(정신적 능력)이 생존 경쟁에서 중요한 무기가 되었고, 상대를 생각으로 앞설 수 있는 부족이 생존에 유리했다는 것입니다. 따라서 승리한 부족은 후손에게 '더 높은 지능과 관련된' 유전자를 물려주었을 것이므로 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 좋은 시력을 위한
② 전투에서의 신체적 능력을 위한
③ 더 높은 지능과 관련된
④ 무술 숙달을 책임지는
⑤ 진보된 무기를 제작하는 능력과 관련된

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.summary_sentence: Childhood enables animals, particularly migratory birds, to (A)___________ to their environment, resulting in more efficient migration routes and greater flexibility in response to environmental changes compared to those relying only on (B)___________.
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 어린 시절(childhood)을 보내는 동물이 환경에 더 잘 '적응(adapt)'하고 유연성을 갖는다는 것입니다. 반면, 태어날 때부터 모든 지도를 가지고 태어나는 새들은 변화하는 환경에 적응하지 못하고 태어날 때의 규칙, 즉 '본능(instinct)' 또는 유전적인 하드웨어에만 의존합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 adapt, (B)에는 instinct(본능)가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 적응하다 - 교육
② 저항하다 - 경험
③ 적응하다 - 훈련
④ 저항하다 - 유전자
⑤ 적응하다 - 본능

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 맞는 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to ①<u>being</u> the perfect environment for monoculture growth, ②<u>which</u> is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at providing exactly the right amount of both supplies ③<u>needing</u>. World usage of fertilizer ④<u>tripled</u> since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds ⑤<u>it</u>, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.explanation: ① 'be forced to' 다음에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 'be'가 적절합니다. ② 앞 문장의 내용을 선행사로 받는 관계대명사의 계속적 용법으로 'which'는 어법상 옳습니다. ③ 'supplies'와 'need'의 관계는 수동이므로 과거분사인 'needed'가 적절합니다. ④ 'since 1969'라는 과거부터 현재까지의 기간을 나타내므로 현재완료인 'has tripled'가 적절합니다. ⑤ 'surrounds'의 목적어는 앞에 나온 복수 명사인 'farm fields'를 가리키므로 'them'이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
options: ① The hunter-gatherer lifestyle can be considered characteristic of humans.
② Early hunter-gatherers seemingly benefited from rich food without much effort.
③ Settled farming involved hard work and the domestication of animals.
④ The human transition to settled farming communities initially facilitated rooting out pandemic diseases.
⑤ The New Stone Age ultimately contributed to the establishment of settled civilizations.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 농경 마을(farming villages)은 전염병(epidemic diseases)이 처음으로 뿌리 내린(first took root) 곳이라고 명시하고 있습니다. 따라서 농경 공동체로의 정착이 전염병을 근절(rooting out)하는 데 도움이 되었거나 이를 용이하게 했다는 ④번은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 수렵 채집 생활 방식은 인간의 특징적인 성격으로 간주될 수 있다.
② 초기 수렵 채집인들은 큰 노력 없이도 풍부한 식량으로부터 혜택을 받은 것으로 보인다.
③ 정착 농업은 고된 노동과 가축 사육을 포함했다.
④ 정착 농경 공동체로의 인간 이동은 초기에는 전염병을 근절하는 것을 용이하게 했다.
⑤ 신석기 시대는 결국 정착 문명의 수립에 기여했다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under ①<u>threat</u>. The grey had the edge because it can ②<u>adjust</u> its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can ③<u>rebuild</u> the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more ④<u>closely</u> and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to ⑤<u>disappearing</u> in England.
questions.explanation: 회색 다람쥐가 붉은 다람쥐보다 더 빨리 먹이를 먹어 치운다는 내용이므로, 먹이 공급을 다시 채운다는 의미의 'rebuild'는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다. 대신 '고갈시키다(deplete)' 또는 '다 먹어 치우다(finish off)' 등의 단어로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.summary_sentence: Many living beings (A)___________ a future pleasure, preferring a delayed reward that has a greater value than an immediate one; however, there are cases where individuals (B)___________ a temptation for instant satisfaction.
questions.explanation: 많은 생명체들이 미래의 즐거움을 '추구(seek/pursue)'하며 지연된 보상을 선호하지만, 때때로 즉각적인 만족이라는 유혹에 '굴복하는(yield to)' 경우가 있다는 내용이므로 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 추구하다 / ~에 굴복하다
② 무시하다 / 초대하다
③ 간과하다 / ~을 확실히 하다
④ 추구하다 / 견디다
⑤ 무게를 달다 / ~에 저항하다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 The costs of interruptions가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: <u>The costs of interruptions</u> are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.
options: ① expenses for hiring famous professionals to enhance efficiency
② rewards for inspiration arising from sudden disruptions
③ regrets about missed opportunities or incomplete tasks
④ negative impacts of unexpected interruptions
⑤ societal chaos following radical innovation
questions.explanation: 지문은 갑작스러운 방해가 영감을 잃게 하거나 업무 효율성을 떨어뜨리고 스트레스를 높이는 등의 부정적인 영향을 미친다는 사례들을 나열하고 있습니다. 따라서 '방해의 비용'은 '예상치 못한 방해의 부정적인 영향'을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 효율성을 높이기 위해 유명한 전문가를 고용하는 비용
② 갑작스러운 방해로 인해 발생하는 영감에 대한 보상
③ 놓친 기회나 미완성된 과업에 대한 후회
④ 예상치 못한 방해의 부정적인 영향
⑤ 급격한 혁신 이후의 사회적 혼란

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency ─ a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority ─ can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs.
ordered_passages: (A) Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
(B) One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment.
(C) Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes,
(D) They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same.
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 자율성을 주는 것이 업무 집중도를 높인다는 주제를 던진 후, (B)에서 구체적인 2010년 오하이오 공장 사례를 소개합니다. (D)는 해당 공장 노동자들이 받은 구체적인 권한(유니폼 디자인, 교대 근무 권한)을 설명하고, (C)는 그 결과로 나타난 생산성 향상을 언급합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 통제감이 자제력을 향상시켰다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 22. 윗글에서 these needs가 지칭하는 것을 찾아서 그대로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take ⓐthese needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.explanation: 지문의 문맥상 'these needs'는 앞에서 언급된 장애가 있는 사람들(people with disabilities)의 요구를 가리킵니다. 지문 두 번째 문장에서 'the needs of people with disabilities'가 대부분 무시되어 왔다고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.question: 23. 윗글에 대한 다음 대화문을 읽고 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 윗글에서 찾아서 그대로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take ⓐ<u>these needs</u> into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.explanation: 대화문 A에서 장애인의 필요가 무시되어 왔다는 맥락이므로 (A)에는 neglected가 적합하며, B의 대답에서 가능한 가장 넓은 독자층을 고려해야 한다는 내용이므로 (B)에는 the largest possible audience가 들어갑니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고 (A), (B)에 알맞은 표현을 써서 이 글의 주제를 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements─what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life─as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born─often occupied by its parent─to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
subjective_conditions: 윗글에서 필요한 단어들을 모두 찾아 쓸 것
questions.answer: (A) the movement (and dispersal) of species (또는 creatures)(B) climate change
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화(climate change)로 인해 생물 종들이 자신들이 생존 가능한 환경을 찾아 이동(movement)하거나 분산(dispersal)하는 현상을 다루고 있습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 (A)와 (B)에 알맞은 표현을 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you have a hard time (A)_______________________, then your positive statement can be: "I easily stay focused on activities (B)_______________________." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>에 주어진 단어를 한 번씩만 모두 사용할 것
2. 필요시 어형변화 및 단어 추가 가능
vocabulary_box: (B) by / interrupt / smart phone / without / my
questions.answer: (A) staying away from your smartphone(B) without being interrupted by my smartphone
questions.explanation: (A) 'have a hard time ~ing' 구문을 활용하여 스마트폰을 멀리하는 데 어려움을 겪는 상황을 서술해야 하므로 'staying away from your smartphone'이 적절합니다. (B) 전치사 'without' 뒤에 동명사 수동태 형태인 'being interrupted'를 사용하여 스마트폰에 의해 방해받지 않고라는 의미를 완성해야 합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글에 드러난 'I'의 심경으로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 19번]
questions.passage: When I woke up in our hotel room, it was almost midnight. I didn't see my husband nor daughter. I called them, but I heard their phones ringing in the room. Feeling worried, I went outside and walked down the street, but they were nowhere to be found. When I decided I should ask someone for help, a crowd nearby caught my attention. I approached, hoping to find my husband and daughter. I tried to find them, but I couldn't. I just stood in the middle of the road, looking at the sky, not knowing what to do.
questions.explanation: 밤중에 남편과 딸이 사라져 걱정하며 찾아다녔으나 찾지 못하고 무엇을 해야 할지 모르는 막막한 상태이므로 '절망적인(hopeless)'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 절망적인
② 호기심 있는
③ 편안한
④ 기쁜
⑤ 무관심한

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, ⓐ<u>that</u> is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way ⓑ<u>that</u> production could be made more efficient, known as the "division of labor." Making most manufactured goods ⓒ<u>involve</u> several different processes using different skills. Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished. One worker could do all these tasks, and ⓓ<u>making</u> 20 pins in a day. But this work can be divided into its separate processes, with a number of workers each ⓔ<u>performed</u> one task. Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day ─ a huge increase in productivity from the 200 that those workers ⓕ<u>would have been produced before</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓐ: 콤마 뒤에 관계대명사 that은 올 수 없으므로 which로 고쳐야 함. ⓒ: 주어가 동명사구(Making ~ goods)이므로 단수 동사 involves로 고쳐야 함. ⓔ: with + 목적어 + 분사 구문에서 각 노동자들이 과업을 '수행하는(능동)' 주체이므로 performing으로 고쳐야 함. ⓕ: 노동자들이 예전에 생산'했던(능동)' 수량이므로 would have produced로 능동태를 써야 함. ⓑ는 way 뒤에 관계부사를 대신하는 that으로 적절하고, ⓓ는 could do와 and로 병렬 연결되어 make(원형)로 쓰거나, 분사구문으로 쓰더라도 and 없이 making을 써야 하나, 문맥상 ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓔ, ⓕ가 확실히 틀렸으므로 ④번이 답임.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The decline in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.*default setting: 기밸값*groove: 고랑*prune: 가지치기하다
options: ① how to enhance children's curiosity through education
② the decline of curiosity from childhood to adulthood
③ the serious situation of children's declining curiosity
④ the way to stop decreasing children's curiosity
⑤ importance of having curiosity to stay young
questions.explanation: 이 글은 유아기에는 많은 신경 연결망을 통해 호기심이 많지만, 성장하면서 자주 사용하는 경로는 고착화되고 사용하지 않는 경로는 제거되면서 호기심이 줄어든다는 내용입니다. 따라서 "아동기부터 성인기까지 호기심의 감소"가 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 교육을 통해 아이들의 호기심을 향상시 방박
② 아동기부터 성인기까지 호기심의 감소
③ 아이들의 호기심 감소의 심각한 상황
④ 아이들의 호기심 감소로 멈추게 하는 방박
⑤ 젊음을 유지하기 위해 호기심을 가지는 것의 성요성

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 뵈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so ___________________ ____________________________. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
options: ① high-quality advertisements should be at the top of your list
② ensuring customer satisfaction has to be your highest priority
③ try to make a to-do list that prioritizes advertisements to satisfy your customers
④ customers become satisfied when they receive what they pay for
⑤ the unpaid ambassadors often get frustrated when they are exploited
questions.explanation: 글의 내용은 구매 혤 고객의 만접도가 반복 구매 및 타인에가의 촔찜(무보수 홍밴대사)로 이어지므로 중요하다는 것입니다. 따라서 뵈칸에는 고객 만접을 보장하는 것이 최우선 과제가 되어야 한다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고푈질의 광고가 당신의 목록 최상단에 있어야 한다
② 고객 만접을 보장하는 것이 당신의 최우선 과제여야 한다
③ 고객을 만접시기 위해 광고를 우선시하는 할 일 목록을 만들어라
④ 고객들은 지불한 만큼 받을 때 만접한다
⑤ 무보수 홍밴대사들은 착귀당할 때 좂좂 좌절감을 느낀다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
options: ① The economy of a city is clearly located in specific areas.
② The brian's neighborhoods operate independently of each other.
③ The brain functions through the isolated operations of its individual parts.
④ Both the brain and a city rely on the complex networks of their respective components.
⑤ Electrochemical signals in the brain do not require processing.
questions.explanation: 지문은 뇌를 도시에 비유하며, 뇌의 작동이나 도시의 경제가 어느 한 곳에서 일어나는 것이 아니라 각 구성 요소들(elements/residents) 간의 상호작용과 네트워크를 통해 발생한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 뇌와 도시 모두 각 구성 요소의 복잡한 네트워크에 의존한다는 ④번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 도시의 경제는 특정 지역에 명확하게 위치해 있다.
② 뇌의 구역들은 서로 독립적으로 작동한다.
③ 뇌는 개별 부위의 고립된 작동을 통해 기능한다.
④ 뇌와 도시 모두 각 구성 요소들의 복잡한 네트워크에 의존한다.
⑤ 뇌의 전기화학적 신호는 처리가 필요하지 않다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Although praise is ⓐ<u>one of the most powerful tools</u> available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe ⓑ<u>what their parents tell them</u> in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically ⓒ<u>and reject false information</u>. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and ⓓ<u>know how to do things</u> is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will ⓔ<u>make him more likely to volunteer</u> to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.explanation: ⓓ의 'know'는 관계대명사 'who'가 이끄는 절 안의 동사입니다. 선행사인 'a boy'가 단수이므로 수 일치를 위해 'knows'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [23년 6월 33번]
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, which then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel ⓐ<u>correspondingly</u>. As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you." If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler has been ⓑ<u>conveyed</u> via our body. This theory states that emotions ⓒ<u>stem</u> from our bodies. For example, our mood can be improved by simply lifting up the corners of our mouth. If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, taking care not to let the pencil touch their lips (thus ⓓ<u>adjusting</u> the mouth into a smile-like shape), they judge cartoons funnier than if they have been asked to frown. The ⓔ<u>apathy</u> of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase "I must be afraid, because I'm running."
questions.explanation: 이 글은 신체 반응이 감정을 유발한다는 내용입니다. ⓔ가 포함된 문장의 예시는 도망가기 때문에 무서운 것이라는 신체 반응의 '우선함' 혹은 '영향력'을 설명하고 있으므로 '무관심(apathy)'이 아닌 '우선함(primacy)' 혹은 '작동'과 같은 표현이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is time pressure. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life ─ which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
questions.summary_sentence: Just as poverty contributes to stress, so wealthier nations also experience their own stress due to time pressure caused by (A)__________ productivity, leaving people feeling constantly urgent and being more (B)__________ to heart disease.
questions.explanation: 본문은 부유한 국가들이 빠른 삶의 속도와 시간적 압박 때문에 스트레스를 겪는다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 요약문 (A)에는 생산성의 속도가 빠르다는 의미의 high-speed(또는 fast-paced)가 적절하고, (B)에는 질병에 걸리기 쉽다는 의미의 vulnerable(또는 prone)이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 과도한 ... 저항력 있는
② 중간의 ... 민감한
③ 빠른 속도의 ... 면역력이 있는
④ 적당한 ... ~하기 쉬운
⑤ 고속의 ... 취약한

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a rare ability in an area, others may _____________________________________ longing for connection with you on account of it.
options: ③ want to advertise the products you buy
④ sacrifice for the good of your possession
⑤ rely on your expertise in the advertisement
questions.explanation: 한 분야에서 탁월한 능력을 가진 사람은 다른 분야에서도 신뢰를 얻어 사람들이 그들의 선택을 따르게 된다는 내용입니다. 농구 선수의 광고나 배우의 자동차 추천을 따르는 것은 그들의 재능에 감탄하여 그들과 연결되고 싶어 그들의 선택(selections)을 모방(mimic)하는 것으로 해석할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 선택을 모방할지도 모른다
② 고통스러운 장애물을 극복할지도 모른다
③ 당신이 사는 제품을 광고하고 싶어 할지도 모른다
④ 당신의 소유물의 이익을 위해 희생할지도 모른다
⑤ 광고에서 당신의 전문 지식에 의존할지도 모른다

questions.question: 13. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절핬 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals-sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt (A)<u>it</u>. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate: 척추동물 **odor: 냄새
options: ② development in research on perception
③ comparison between old and new perceptions
④ diversity and complexity of sensory perception
⑤ diverse sense of smell among various animals
questions.explanation: 이 글은 감각이 단순히 5개가 아니라 인간겼 동물에겄 더 다양하고 복잡한 감각이 이재함을 설명하고 이습니다. 따라서 '감각 지각의 다양성겼 복잡성'을 다룬 ④번이 가장 적절한 제목이 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 아리스토텔레스의 오해
② 지각 연구의 발전
③ 구 지각겼 신 지각의 비교
④ 감각 지각의 다양성겼 복잡성
⑤ 다양한 동물들 사이의 다양한 후각

questions.question: 14. 윗글에서 묑줄 챜 (A)it이 의미하는 바를 우리말로 시오. [3.3점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals-sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt (A)<u>it</u>. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate: 척추동물 **odor: 냄새
questions.answer: 인간겼 동물에겄 다섯 개의 감각이 이재한다는 것
questions.explanation: 문육사의 (A) it은 바로 앞 문장에서 아리스토텔레스가 주장한 내용, 즉 '인간겼 동물 모됐에겄 시각, 찭각, 후각, 미각, 촉각이띀 다섯 개의 감각이 이재한다는 것'을 가리킵니다.

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session.
ordered_passages: (A) With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
(B) In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion.

(C) Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 동물마다 치뮤 과정에서 다리 밑응할 수 있음을 언급한 현, (C)에서는 호응에 영향을 미츘 수 있는 또 다른 요인으로 '환경적 요인(Environmental factors)'을 제시합니다. 그 홄 (B)에서 'In addition(게다가)'을 통해 치뮤하는 질병의 성격(신체적 vs 감정적)에 따라 밑응이 다를 수 있음을 추가합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 'With this in mind(이러한 점을 염두에 두고)'라고 하면서 동물의 특정한 필요에 맞게 치뮤를 조절해야 한다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 자연숔습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how ⓐ<u>masters</u> in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably more ⓑ<u>inaccurate</u> than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓒ<u>insensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even ⓓ<u>overrated</u> how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through ⓔ<u>learners'</u> eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 전체적인 글의 흐름은 전문가가 초밴자에게 기술을 가리칠 때 발생하눠 수 있는 'ID식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'에 대한 것입니다. 전문가들은 자신이 기술을 숙달하는 데 걸린 시간이나 난이도를 과소평가(underestimate)하는 경향을 밴입니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 overrated(과대평가하다)는 underestimated(과소평가하다)로 고치는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. (A)<u>너가 '감사합니다'라고 말하도록 강요하는 법은 없다. (that, law, say, no)</u>. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. (B)__________ it will be natural and taken for granted. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as (C)____________________.
questions.explanation: 앞 문장에서 사람들이 당신이 감사하다고 말할 것을 기대하고 당신에게 책임이 부여된다고 했습니다. 문맥상 '그렇게 말하지 못하는 것(감사 인사를 하지 않는 것)'은 눈에 띄게 되지만, 반대로 그것을 말하는 것은 자연스럽고 당연하게 여겨진다는 흐름이 되어야 합니다. 지문 원문상으로는 'Doing so'가 적절하나, 선택지 중에서는 문맥의 대조를 이루는 'Failing to say(말하지 않는 것)'가 'it is marked'와 연결되는 논리 구조를 가집니다. (단, 원문상으로는 인사를 하는 행위가 당연시된다는 의미의 Doing so가 맞으나, 문제 구성상 인사를 하지 않는 경우의 결과를 묻는 선택지 구성으로 보입니다.)
options_translation: ① 언급하는 것
② 말하지 못하는 것
③ 상상하는 것
④ 간과하는 것
⑤ 기억하도록 돕는 것

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 (A)의 문장을 괄호 안의 단어를 사용하여 영작하시오.
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. (A)<u>너가 '감사합니다'라고 말하도록 강요하는 법은 없다. (that, law, say, no)</u>. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. (B)__________ it will be natural and taken for granted. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as (C)____________________.
subjective_conditions: 괄호 안의 단어를 사용할 것
questions.answer: There is no law that forces you to say Thank you.
questions.explanation: 주어 '법(law)'이 '없다(no)'는 존재 구문 'There is no law'를 사용하고, 그 법을 수식하는 관계대명사절 'that forces you to say Thank you'를 결합하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 19. 윗글의 빈칸 (C)에 들어갈 수 있는 구를 윗글에서 찾아 변형하여 두 가지 작성하시오. (두 가지 이상 작성한 경우 작성한 순서대로 앞에서부터 2개만 채점함.)
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. (A)<u>너가 '감사합니다'라고 말하도록 강요하는 법은 없다. (that, law, say, no)</u>. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. (B)__________ it will be natural and taken for granted. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as (C)____________________.
subjective_conditions: 윗글에서 찾아 변형할 것
두 가지 작성할 것
questions.answer: 1. holding a door open for you2. pointing out that you've just dropped something
questions.explanation: 빈칸 (C)는 전치사 as 뒤에 오는 자리로, 앞서 언급된 'minor'한 도움의 예시들을 동명사구 형태로 변형하여 넣어야 합니다. 본문에 제시된 예시인 'open a door for you'와 'point out that you've just dropped something'을 각각 'holding/opening a door open for you'와 'pointing out that you've just dropped something'으로 변형하여 답안을 작성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.summary_sentence: Species (A)__________ to suitable environments as climate change, with even stationary creatures (B)__________ at certain life stages.
questions.explanation: 기후 변화로 인해 각 생물 종이 요구하는 환경 조건이 바뀌면, 생물들은 생존을 위해 적합한 장소로 이동해야 합니다. 겉보기에 이동 능력이 없는 나무나 따개비조차 씨앗이나 유생 단계에서 분산(dispersal)이 가능하다는 점을 설명하고 있으므로, (A)에는 이동을 의미하는 'relocate'가, (B)에는 분산/확산을 의미하는 'spreading'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 적응하다 - 퍼뜨리기
② 이동하다 - 퍼뜨리기
③ 이동하다 - 진화하기
④ 이식하다 - 퍼뜨리기
⑤ 적응하다 - 진화하기

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① 잉카 제국은 메시지를 전할 말을 구하기가 어려웠다.
② 전령들은 네 명에서 여섯 명의 집단을 이루었다.
③ 각 전령들은 1마일에서 2마일 간격으로 개별적으로 떨어져 생활했다.
④ 전령들은 달리기를 잘하는 젊은 남성들이었다.
⑤ 전령은 다음 전령에게 메시지를 서너 번 반복하여 소리쳤다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 전령들(Chasquis)은 'huts(오두막)'에 '4~6명씩 무리를 지어(groups of four to six)' 살았다고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 ③번에서처럼 각 전령들이 '개별적으로' 떨어져 생활했다는 설명은 적절하지 않습니다. 오두막 사이의 간격이 1~2마일인 것이지, 전령 개인별로 떨어져 산 것이 아닙니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever ①<u>getting</u> aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of ②<u>conversations</u> with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, ③<u>publishing</u> weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders ④<u>are</u> asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest. As Bob Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you ⑤<u>why</u> we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
questions.explanation:
③번이 포함된 구문에서 'series of conversations'는 신문의 비즈니스 섹션에 매주 '게재되는(발표되는)' 수동의 대상입니다. 따라서 능동의 의미를 가진 현재분사 'publishing'은 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 'published'로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

[오답 분석]
① getting: 전치사 'from'의 목적어로 동명사가 쓰였으며, 'be/get aired(방송되다/발표되다)'의 수동 표현으로 적절합니다.
② conversations: 'a series of' 뒤에 복수 명사가 온 형태로 적절합니다.
④ are: 주어인 'the featured leaders'가 복수이므로 복수 동사 'are'가 쓰인 수동태 문장으로 적절합니다.
⑤ why: 'tell'의 직접목적어 자리에 쓰인 의문사절(간접의문문)을 이끄는 의문사로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 단어를 지문의 내용을 참고하여 쓰시오.
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest. As Bob Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these (A)__________ because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
subjective_conditions: 지문에 언급된 핵심 단어를 활용할 것
문맥에 맞는 적합한 품사와 수로 작성할 것
questions.explanation: 지문 초반부에서 사장들이 'pro-dissent(반대에 찬성하는)' 성향을 가지고 있으며 'internal protest(내부 저항)'를 장려한다고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸 (A)에는 사장에게 반대 의견을 제시하거나 비판적인 목소리를 내는 사람들을 지칭하는 'dissenters(반대자들)'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question:
★ 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. [24년 3월 30번]

1. 윗글에서 문법적으로 잘못된 문장을 하나 찾아 바르게 고쳐 작성하시오.
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street-a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allowing for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
subjective_conditions: 문법적으로 틀린 부분을 포함한 문장 전체를 바르게 고쳐 쓸 것
questions.answer: On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail.
questions.explanation: 지문 내의 'On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allowing for the appreciation of environmental detail.' 문장에서 'being much slower'는 삽입된 분사구로 주어인 'pedestrian travel'을 부연 설명합니다. 이 문장에는 주어를 서술할 본동사가 없으므로, 현재분사인 'allowing'을 문맥상 현재 시제의 본동사인 'allows'로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.

questions.question:
★ 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. [24년 3월 30번]

2. 윗글의 주제와 관련지어 보행자, 자전거 운전자, 자동차 운전자의 정보처리능력을 비교하여 서술하시오.
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street-a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allowing for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.answer: 인간의 감각은 걷는 속도에 맞게 진화했기 때문에, 보행자가 주변 환경을 가장 잘 관찰할 수 있고, 달리기나 자전거를 타는 사람들이 그 다음이고, 자동차 운전자들이 가장 세밀한 환경적 사항을 인지하기 어렵다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 진화론적으로 걷는 속도(시속 5마일 이하)에서 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력이 최적화되어 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 제공된 모범 답안과 같이 이동 속도가 가장 느린 보행자가 가장 높은 정보처리 능력을 보이며, 중간 단계인 달리기/자전거 운전자를 거쳐, 가장 빠른 자동차 운전자가 세부 정보를 인지하는 데 가장 큰 한계를 보인다는 점을 비교하여 서술해야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 요지를 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오.
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must depend more fully on inborn hardware and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born with knowledge of how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhood, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.summary_sentence: 어린 시절에 이동 경로를 학습하는 것은 철새들이 타고난 지식에 기반하여 이동하는 새들보다 더 효율적이고 유연한 이동 경로를 만들게 해준다.
subjective_conditions: - <보기>의 주어진 단어들을 반드시 포함할 것 (중복 사용 가능, 필요에 따라 단어 형태 변경 가능)
- <보기>에 주어진 단어 외에 필요한 단어는 위의 지문 내에서만 찾아 쓸 것 (지문 내 단어 형태 변형 불가)
- 밑줄 친 한글 해석에 대응하도록 현재 시제로 쓰며, 관계대명사 that과 사역동사 let을 사용할 것
- 답안지에는 주어진 단어를 포함하여 완성된 문장을 적을 것 (철자 오답 주의)
vocabulary_box: migration routes / based on / let / those /
migratory birds / than / make / that / during
questions.answer: Learning migration routes during childhood lets migratory birds make efficient and flexible migration routes than those that migrate based on inborn knowledge.
questions.explanation: 주어진 조건에 따라 사역동사 let(목적어 + 목적격보어 원형부정사)과 주격 관계대명사 that을 활용하여 영작합니다. 'Learning migration routes during childhood'가 동명사구 주어이므로 3인칭 단수 동사 lets를 사용하며, 목적어 'migratory birds' 뒤에 원형부정사 'make'를 위치시켜 문장을 구성합니다. 비교 대상인 '타고난 지식에 기반해 이동하는 새들'은 'those that migrate based on inborn knowledge'로 표현합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글을 읽고 문맥을 고려해 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 한 단어를 각각 쓰시오. (주어진 철자로 시작하는 단어를 어법에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: All humans, to some extent, seek activities that cause a bit of pain to feel. This can be from eating spicy food, getting strong massages, or stepping into very cold or hot baths. The key is that these are 'threats'. The brain sees these things as painful but not really (A)d____________. Interestingly, this is similar to how humor works: a 'safe threat' that makes us feel good by breaking rules in a playful way. We feel uncomfortable, but also safe. In this situation, where survival is clearly not at risk, the desire for pain is actually a desire for reward, not suffering or punishment. This reward-like effect comes from feeling that we have mastered the pain. The closer you look at your habit of eating chilies, the more amazing it seems. When the active ingredient in chilies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it activates the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is sending danger signals, but realizing we are completely safe, creates pleasure. All children start off hating chili, but many learn to enjoy it through repeated exposure and knowing they will never get really (B)h____________. Interestingly, seeking pain for its own sake appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to like chili or to self-harm is by always linking the pain with a pleasurable reward.
questions.explanation: (A) 뇌가 이러한 자극들을 고통스럽지만 실제로는 '위험하지 않은(dangerous)' 것으로 간주한다는 문맥이 되어야 '안전한 위협'이라는 개념과 연결됩니다.(B) 아이들이 고추를 먹는 것을 즐기게 되는 이유는 반복적 노출을 통해 자신이 정말로 '다치지(hurt)' 않을 것임을 알기 때문입니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글을 읽고 완성한 요약문을 주어진 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of people with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.summary_sentence: 장애인의 요구들은 디지털 프로젝트들에서 종종 무시되어 왔으며, 이를 포괄적 디자인을 채택함으로써 변경할 수 있습니다.
subjective_conditions: 밑줄 친 한글 해석에 대응할 것
<보기>에 주어진 단어를 빠짐없이 사용할 것
필요에 따라 <보기> 속 단어의 형태를 바꿀 것
필요한 단어들을 추가하여 사용할 것
vocabulary_box: be / in digital projects, / which / could / change / by / an inclusive design / have often been
questions.answer: The needs of people with disabilities have often been neglected in digital projects, which could be changed by adopting an inclusive design.
questions.explanation: 한글 요약문에 맞춰 '장애인의 요구(The needs of people with disabilities)'를 주어로 잡고, '종종 무시되어 왔다(have often been neglected)'는 현재완료 수동태를 사용합니다. 콤마 뒤에 관계대명사 'which'를 써서 앞 문장 전체를 선행사로 받고, '변경될 수 있다(could be changed)'는 조동사 수동태와 '포괄적 디자인을 채택함으로써(by adopting an inclusive design)'를 연결하여 영작합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Having a messy room can ⓐ<u>lead</u> to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists say that ⓑ<u>having</u> a disorderly room can indicate a disorganized mental state. One of the professional tidying experts says that ⓒ<u>when</u> you start cleaning your room, you also start changing your life and gaining a new perspective. When you clean your surroundings, a positive and good atmosphere follows. You can do more things efficiently and neatly. So, ⓓ<u>clean</u> up your closets, organizing your drawers, and arranging your things will ⓔ<u>be followed</u> by peace of mind.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 '옷장을 정리하고 서랍을 정리하고 물건을 정돈하는 것'이라는 동명사구 병렬 구조입니다. 뒤에 동사 will be followed가 나오므로 ⓓ는 동사원형 clean이 아니라 동명사 cleaning이 되어야 문장의 주어 역할을 할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. ⓐ<u>This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation</u>. ⓑ<u>During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become far more efficient at supplying the exact amount of both</u>. ⓒ<u>World fertilizer usage has tripled since 1969, and the global population has doubled, so we need to develop a way to distribute our food evenly</u>. ⓓ<u>We feed and water our fields more than ever, and our crops grow much better</u>. ⓔ<u>Unfortunately, these perfect conditions have also attracted the attention of certain agricultural undesirables</u>. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 단일 경작을 위해 농지에 영양분과 물을 공급하는 완벽한 환경을 조성하는 과정과 그에 따른 부작용(잡초의 유입)을 설명하고 있습니다. ③번 문장은 전 세계 비료 사용량과 인구 증가에 따른 식량 분배의 필요성을 언급하고 있으므로, 농지의 인위적 환경 조성과 잡초 문제라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, _____________________________, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
options: ① if you act like a master of your life
③ when your action follows your desire
④ if you behave exactly according to who you think you are
⑤ if you have the same identity with the great men in history
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 행동이 정체성(자신이 누구라고 믿는지)의 반영이라는 점입니다. 빈칸 뒤의 '더 이상 행동 변화를 추구하지 않고, 이미 스스로 그렇다고 믿는 유형의 사람처럼 행동할 뿐이다'라는 내용과 호응하려면, 빈칸에는 '당신이 생각하는 자신과 똑같이 행동한다면'이라는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 만약 당신이 당신 삶의 주인처럼 행동한다면
② 향상된 의사 결정 기술과 함께
③ 당신의 행동이 당신의 욕구를 따를 때
④ 만약 당신이 당신이 생각하는 당신 자신과 정확히 일치하게 행동한다면
⑤ 만약 당신이 역사상의 위대한 인물들과 같은 정체성을 가진다면

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [24년 6월 29번]
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be describe as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. To preserve their food and avoid the danger of hunting, so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
options: ① Through hunting and gathering, people easily got food and were suffered from less illness.
② People set up villages and cultivated to store food and escape the danger of hunting.
③ Infectious diseases caused by farming were solved through hunting and gathering.
④ Through the agriculture and the settlement, more and more people came to live together.
⑤ People eventually came close to civilization through cultivation and livestock farming.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 농경 마을에서 전염병이 처음으로 뿌리를 내렸다고 언급하고 있지만, 이러한 농경으로 인한 전염병이 수렵 채집을 통해 해결되었다는 언급은 없습니다. 오히려 수렵 채집 시절에 질병으로 고통받는 일이 매우 적었다고 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 수렵과 채집을 통해 사람들은 음식을 쉽게 얻었고 질병에 덜 시달렸다.
② 사람들은 음식을 저장하고 사냥의 위험에서 벗어나기 위해 마을을 세우고 경작했다.
③ 농경으로 인해 발생한 전염병은 수렵과 채집을 통해 해결되었다.
④ 농업과 정착을 통해 점점 더 많은 사람들이 모여 살게 되었다.
⑤ 사람들은 경작과 가축 사육을 통해 결국 문명에 가까워졌다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 6월 31번]
questions.passage: The costs of interruption are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was ⓐ<u>disrupted</u> by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the ultimately visitor came at a ⓑ<u>critical</u> time. He ⓒ<u>grasped</u> his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in important roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, ⓓ<u>lessen</u> work productivity and generally ⓔ<u>heighten</u> stress levels.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 콜리지는 갑작스러운 방문객 때문에 영감을 '놓쳤고' 그 결과 시를 미완성으로 남겨두게 된 것입니다. 따라서 '영감을 붙잡았다'는 뜻의 grasped는 흐름상 적절하지 않으며, 'lost'(잃었다)와 같은 단어가 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 24. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control and that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs.
ordered_passages: (A) They could choose the partners they would work with, design their own uniforms, and had authority over shifts during all the manufacturing processes, while maintaining the same pay.

(B) Productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
(C) A study at a manufacturing plant closely investigated assembly-line workers who were given the power to make minor decisions regarding their schedules and work environment.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 직원들에게 자율성(agency)을 주는 것이 에너지와 집중력을 높인다는 주제를 제시합니다. (C)에서 이와 관련된 제조 공장의 연구 사례를 처음 소개하며 조립 라인 노동자들에게 사소한 결정권이 주어졌음을 언급합니다. (A)는 (C)에서 언급된 결정권의 구체적인 내용(파트너 선택, 유니폼 디자인 등)을 상술하며, (B)는 이러한 변화로 인한 결과(생산성 20% 향상)와 결론을 제시하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① Focused Attention and Brain Transformation
② How Practice Affects Memory in Humans
③ The Impact of Rewards on Animal Brains
④ Auditory and Visual Centers in Animal Brains
⑤ The Role of the Hippocampus in Spatial Memory
questions.explanation: 이 글의 요지는 우리가 어디에 주의를 집중하고 무엇을 연습하느냐에 따라 뇌의 물리적 구조가 변한다는 것입니다. 동물의 청각/시각 영역, 바이올리니스트의 대뇌 피질, 택시 기사의 해마 사례는 모두 집중된 주의와 연습이 뇌의 재형성(reshaping)을 이끈다는 증거로 제시되었습니다. 따라서 '집중된 주의와 뇌의 변형'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 집중된 주의와 뇌의 변형
② 연습이 인간의 기억에 미치는 영향
③ 보상이 동물의 뇌에 미치는 영향
④ 동물의 뇌 속 청각 및 시각 센터
⑤ 공간 기억에서 해마의 역할

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(D)의 의미로 가장 적절한 것을 아래 <보기>에서 골라 각각 기호를 쓰시오.
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are (A)<u>solo</u>. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most (B)<u>promising</u> options. By developing and assessing ideas individually, before choosing and elaborating them, teams can (C)<u>surface</u> and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all (D)<u>voices</u> are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
vocabulary_box: a. indicating future success or improvement
b. an outside part or layer of something
c. to keep something in its original state or in good condition
d. made or done by someone unknown
e. opinions or ideas about a topic
f. done by a single performer instead of a group
g. to give more details about something
h. simple, not complex or complicated
questions.explanation: (A) solo는 혼자서 하는 것이므로 'f. 단독으로 수행되는'이 적절합니다. (B) promising은 유망한 것이므로 'a. 미래의 성공이나 개선을 나타내는'이 적절합니다. (C) surface는 (본문에서 동사로 쓰여) 드러나게 하는 것이므로, 본래 뜻인 표면으로 끌어올린다는 맥락의 'k(본문의 흐름상 표면화하다/드러내다 의미)'가 적합하나 보기에는 생략되어 있습니다(원문상 k가 'to emerge or become known' 등일 것으로 추정). (D) voices는 사람들의 목소리 즉 의견이므로 'e. 주제에 대한 의견이나 아이디어'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: a. 미래의 성공이나 개선을 나타내는
b. 무언가의 외부 부분 또는 층
c. 무언가를 원래 상태나 좋은 상태로 유지하는 것
d. 알려지지 않은 누군가에 의해 만들어지거나 행해진
e. 주제에 대한 의견이나 생각들
f. 그룹 대신 단일 수행자에 의해 수행되는
g. 무언가에 대해 더 많은 세부 사항을 제공하는 것
h. 단순하고, 복잡하거나 복잡하지 않은

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓒ가 공통적으로 의미하는 바를 지문에서 찾아 한 단어로 쓰시오. (단, 지시대명사는 불가능함)
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire ⓐ<u>how to compete</u>. We often take the easy route to improve ⓑ<u>our abilities</u>. Many of us never really work to achieve ⓒ<u>superiority in the key areas of life</u>. These are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. People win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
subjective_conditions: 지문에서 찾아 한 단어로 쓸 것
지시대명사 불가능
questions.explanation: ⓐ 경쟁하는 법, ⓑ 우리의 능력, ⓒ 삶의 핵심 영역에서의 우월함은 모두 고난과 투쟁을 통해 얻어지는 내적인 힘을 의미합니다. 지문 마지막 부분의 'Strength comes from struggle'에서 언급된 'strength'가 이를 관통하는 단어입니다.

questions.question: 28. 윗글이 주장하는 바를 아래 주어진 어구를 변형하지 않고 재배열하여 서술하시오.
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire ⓐ<u>how to compete</u>. We often take the easy route to improve ⓑ<u>our abilities</u>. Many of us never really work to achieve ⓒ<u>superiority in the key areas of life</u>. These are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. People win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 어구를 변형하지 말 것
모두 재배열하여 서술할 것
questions.answer: True strength and mastery in life are achieved through facing challenges and hardship rather than seeking easy ways.
questions.explanation: 지문의 핵심 주장인 '진정한 힘과 숙련은 쉬운 길을 찾는 것이 아니라 도전과 고난에 맞섬으로써 얻어진다'를 주어진 단어들로 구성하면 됩니다. 주어(True strength and mastery in life), 동사(are achieved), 수단(through facing challenges and hardship), 대비(rather than seeking easy ways)의 순서로 배열합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.summary_sentence: As all the creatures including (A)_________ things have particular climate conditions in which they can live, climate changes cause them to (B)_________ their habitat.
questions.explanation: 모든 생물은 특정한 기후 요구 조건을 가지고 있으며, 기후가 변하면 이를 충족하는 장소도 변합니다. 나무나 따개비처럼 움직이지 못하는(motionless) 생물들조차 생애의 특정 단계(씨앗, 유충)에서는 이동이 가능하며, 기후 변화에 맞춰 서식지를 옮기게 됩니다. 따라서 기후 변화는 생물들이 서식지를 바꾸게(alter) 합니다.
options_translation: ① 움직이지 않는 ... 유지하다
② 보이지 않는 ... 유지하다
③ 보이지 않는 ... 바꾸다
④ 움직이지 않는 ... 유지하다
⑤ 움직이지 않는 ... 바꾸다

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they ____________ an objection. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부 이후 리더들이 내부의 반대 의견이나 젊은 직원들의 항의를 계속해서 권장한다고 언급하고 있으며, 반대하는 사람들의 의견을 경청하는 것이 일을 완수하는 데 필수적이라고 말하고 있습니다. 따라서 대부분의 상사들은 반대(objection)를 수용한다(accept)고 말하는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 만들다
② 무시하다
③ 수용하다
④ 비판하다
⑤ 극복하다

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)가 지칭하는 것을 옳게 짝지은 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count (A)<u>it</u> as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to (B)<u>it</u>s definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: (A)가 포함된 문장에서 '지각적 이탈(Perceptual disengagement)'이 수면을 보호하는 기능을 하므로 어떤 저자들은 '그것(지각적 이탈)'을 수면의 정의의 일부로 보지 않는다고 설명합니다. (B)에서는 '그것(수면)'의 정의에 필수적이라고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)는 '지각 이탈', (B)는 '수면'을 지칭합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 필자의 관점에서 보았을 때 내용상 성격이 다른 하나는?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing ⓐ<u>newcomers</u> to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than ⓑ<u>novice</u> phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the ⓒ<u>beginner</u>, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge.' Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that ⓓ<u>experts</u> forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how ⓔ<u>students</u> 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전문가가 초보자의 입장을 이해하지 못하는 '지식의 저주'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ⓐ newcomers, ⓑ novice, ⓒ beginner, ⓔ students는 모두 해당 분야의 '초보자'나 '배우는 입장'의 사람들을 가리키지만, ⓓ experts는 해당 분야에 숙련된 '전문가'를 의미하므로 지칭하는 대상의 성격이 다릅니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness ①<u>who</u> experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those ②<u>participated</u> in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals ③<u>living</u> with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed ④<u>that</u>, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and ⑤<u>enhanced</u> self-confidence. *therapy: 치료 **efficacy: 효능
questions.explanation: ②번의 경우 'with + 명사 + 분사' 구문이 사용되었습니다. 의미상 those(사람들)가 세션에 직접 '참여하는' 능동의 주체이므로, 과거분사인 participated를 현재분사인 participating으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is ①<u>improbable</u> if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made ②<u>adaptations</u> for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller filed. All have junior competitive structures where children play for ③<u>longer</u> time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more ④<u>appropriate</u> for children under 10. The adaptations are ⑤<u>gradual</u> and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: 어린아이들의 주의 집중 시간이나 체력적인 특성상, 스포츠를 아이들에게 맞게 설계할 때는 더 짧은(shorter) 시간 동안 경기를 진행하는 것이 흥미를 유지하고 참여를 높이는 데 적절합니다. 따라서 본문의 흐름상 '더 긴'을 뜻하는 ③번의 longer는 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. (A) Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. (B) They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. (C) If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. (D) The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. (E) When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him.
questions.insertion_sentence: The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca King's orders and reports coming from his lands.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 전령들(The messengers)이 왕의 명령과 보고를 전달하기 위해 왕도에 배치되었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A) 바로 앞 문장에서 잉카 제국이 도보로 메시지를 전달하는 데 뛰어났다는 내용이 나오고, (A) 문장에서 'Chasquis라고 불리는 그들(they)'이라는 대명사가 등장하므로, (A) 자리에 주어진 문장이 들어가 전령들에 대한 구체적인 설명을 시작하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not ____________ according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.explanation: 과거에는 혀의 부위별로 느끼는 맛이 정해져 있다는 '혀 지도'가 있다고 믿었으나, 현대 연구 결과 맛은 입안 어디에서나 느낄 수 있다는 것이 밝혀졌습니다. 따라서 맛봉오리는 전문 분야(특정 맛)에 따라 '분류되지(categorized)' 않는다는 것이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 줄어든
② 뒤섞인
③ 제거된
④ 복제된
⑤ 분류된

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session.
ordered_passages: (A) In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion.

(B) Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment.

(C) With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 동물이 서로 다르며 치유 세션에 다르게 반응할 수 있다는 기본 전제를 제시합니다. (B)에서는 반응의 차이를 만드는 또 다른 원인으로 '환경적 요인'을 소개하고 고양이의 예시를 듭니다. (A)에서는 '게다가(In addition)'를 사용하여 신체적 질병과 정서적 혼란에 따른 반응 차이를 추가로 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 '이러한 점을 염두에 두고(With this in mind)' 앞에서 언급된 모든 차이 요인들을 종합하여 치유 과정이 개별화되어야 한다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very ⓐ<u>slow</u> to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have ⓑ<u>more</u> control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the ⓒ<u>wrong</u> decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in ⓓ<u>prejudices</u> and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the ⓔ<u>subconscious</u> mind records your reactions.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의식과 잠재의식의 차이를 다룹니다. 문맥상 잠재의식은 감정을 다루지 않고 기억과 인식을 다루는 영역이며, 의식은 우리가 제어하고 선택하는 영역입니다. 지문 후반부에서 공포가 잠재의식에 기록될 때 실제 공포가 된다고 언급하는 등 잠재의식의 역할을 볼 때, 잠재의식이 행동하는 데 '느리다(slow)'는 표현은 부적절합니다. 보통 잠재의식은 자동적이고 빠른 반응을 담당하는 것으로 묘사되거나, 이 지문의 논리 구조상 의식적인 선택 과정이 없는 즉각적인 기록 저장소 역할을 하므로 'slow'는 흐름상 맞지 않습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영문 뜻풀이가 바르게 연결되지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's ⓐ<u>self-esteem</u>. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very ⓑ<u>profound</u> way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to ⓒ<u>incorporate</u> that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him ⓓ<u>endure</u> longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to ⓔ<u>volunteer</u> to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
options: ① ⓐself-esteem: a feeling of being happy with your own character and abilities.
② ⓑprofound: felt or experienced very strongly or in an extreme way
③ ⓒincorporate: to separate different things, especially arguments or ideas, that have become confused
④ ⓓendure: to experience and deal with something that is painful or unpleasant
