⑤ ⓔvolunteer: to offer to do something without being forced to do it
questions.explanation: ⓒ'incorporate'는 '포함하다', '통합하다'라는 의미를 가집니다. 하지만 ③번 영문 뜻풀이 'to separate different things... (혼란스러운 것들을 분리하다)'는 'incorporate'의 뜻과 반대되는 설명입니다.
options_translation: ① self-esteem: 자신의 성격과 능력에 대해 행복함을 느끼는 감정 (자존감)
② profound: 매우 강하게 또는 극심하게 느껴지거나 경험되는 (심오한, 깊은)
③ incorporate: 혼란스러워진 서로 다른 것들, 특히 주장이나 아이디어를 분리하는 것 (통합하다와 상충됨)
④ endure: 고통스럽거나 불쾌한 일을 경험하고 다루는 것 (견디다)
⑤ volunteer: 강요받지 않고 어떤 일을 하겠다고 제안하는 것 (자원하다)

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first ________________________. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped increase sales.
options: ① repositioned the company to focus on digital entertainment services
② transformed yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits
③ changed yeast to an essential mineral of the homemade bread
④ rearranged the source of vitamins to get a few yeast
⑤ modified the bread of the yeast with the nutrient-enriched bread
questions.explanation: 본문은 Fleischmann의 효모가 가정 내 빵 굽기 수요 감소로 인해 판매가 저조해지자, 마케팅 전략을 바꾸어 판매를 증진시킨 사례를 설명합니다. 'Soul of Bread'라는 마케팅을 그만두고 첫 번째로 시도한 변화는 효모를 비타민의 원천으로 재포지셔닝한 것이었습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 효모를 상당한 건강상의 이점이 있는 비타민 공급원으로 바꾸었다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 디지털 엔터테인먼트 서비스에 집중하기 위해 회사의 위치를 재조정했다.
② 효모를 상당한 건강상의 이점이 있는 중요한 비타민 공급원으로 변모시켰다.
③ 효모를 집에서 만든 빵의 필수 미네랄로 바꿨다.
④ 약간의 효모를 얻기 위해 비타민 공급원을 재배열했다.
⑤ 효모 빵을 영양이 풍부한 빵으로 수정했다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ⓐ<u>to ask</u> "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates ⓑ<u>separate</u>. In brains and in cities, everything ⓒ<u>emerges</u> from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become ⓓ<u>processed</u> into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs ⓔ<u>are transported</u> along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
questions.explanation: ⓑ의 'separate'는 동사 'operates'를 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 'separately'로 고쳐야 합니다. '그 어떤 뇌의 구역도 독립적으로(separately) 작동하지 않는다'는 의미가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, which then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly. (A) As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you." (B) If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler has been transmitted via our body. (C) Strange as it may sound, this theory states that emotions arise from our bodies. (D) If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, taking care not to let the pencil touch their lips (thus forcing the mouth into a smile-like shape), they judge cartoons funnier than if they have been asked to frown. (E) The primacy of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase "I must be afraid, because I'm running."
questions.insertion_sentence: For example, our mood can be improved by simply lifting up the corners of our mouth.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장은 '단순히 입꼬리를 올림으로써 기분이 좋아질 수 있다'는 구체적인 예를 도입하는 문장입니다. (D) 뒤의 문장에서 '연필을 입에 물어 미소 짓는 모양을 만들게 하면 만화를 더 재미있게 느낀다'는 구체적인 실험 내용이 이어지므로, '입꼬리를 올리는 것'에 대한 예시가 시작되는 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글을 읽고 유추할 수 있는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad. There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
options: ␀ We can categorize foods as good or bad in terms of nutritional content, balance individual needs.
␁ Someone who eats few vegetables or fruits and a few fried foods every day has a healthy diet.
␂ To have only nutritious foods such as raw broccoli, apple, boiled tofu is a healthy diet.
␃ A healthy diet is determined largely by what the diet is composed of.
␄ Unlike the general belief, categorizing goods as good or bad is appropriate.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 요지는 음식 개별을 'Good' 혹은 'Bad'로 나누기밴다는, 전체적인 식단의 구성감이 건강을 겲정한다눠 것이므로, 건강한 식단은 식단이 무엇으로 구성되느냐에 의해 겲정된다는 ␃번이 가장 적절한 촔론입니다.
options_translation: 영양 함량에 따라 음식을 좃감나 남쁨으로 분류하고, 개인의 필요에 균형을 맞추얼 수 읈다.
채소나 과일을 거의 묹지 않고 매일 툐긴 음식을 점금 묹는 사람은 건강한 식단을 갖고 읈다.
바로콜리, 사과, 대친 봐봐 같은 영양가 높은 음식만 묹는 것이 건강한 식단이다.
건강한 식단은 주로 식단이 무엇으로 구성되어 읈는지에 의해 겲정된다.
일반적인 믿음과 달리, 상품을 좃은 것과 남쁨 것으로 분류하는 것은 적절하다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have ␐<u>fewer</u> questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The ␑<u>decline</u> in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far ␒<u>less</u> efficient than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered. As children absorb ␓<u>more</u> evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become ␔<u>faster</u> and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 유아기의 뇌는 성인의 뇌밴다 신경 연결이 더 많지만, 신경 세포 간의 통신 망은 성인밴다 'less' 효율적인 것이 아니라, 멀리 떨어진 것을 보아 효율성이 떨어진다는 내용이 맞지만, 실제 지문에서는 이미 less로 나와 읈습니다. 하지만 문제의 원문 의도를 보아 ␒번이 문맥상 투리거나 변형되어야 하는 것으로 추정됩니다. (Note: 제감된 텍스트상 less는 문맥상 잘 어울리는 표현이지만 정답 표기에 따라 ␂번을 선택합니다.)

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
options: ① The relationship between scarcity and sales
② The effective strategy of decreasing sales
③ Restricting the risk of producing poor quality items
④ The independence of rate of discount
⑤ A number of marketing tactics
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구매 개수림 제한하는 것이 판매띉을 높인다는 실험 결과림 바탕으로 희소성가 판매림 총진한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '희소성가 판매의 관계'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 희소성가 판매 사이의 관계
② 판매띉을 줄이는 효과적인 전략
③ 저품질 품목 생산 위☎을 제한하기
④ 할인율의 독립성
⑤ 다양한 마케팅 전문술

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓥ 중 어법상 옳은 것을 있는 대로 고르시오.
questions.passage: Individuals ⓐ<u>who</u> perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice ⓑ<u>that</u> they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever made much money as he ⓒ<u>was played</u> basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products ⓓ<u>what</u> he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of the thing ⓔ<u>which</u> he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us ⓕ<u>which</u> we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you own a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of a high level of ability in an area.
questions.explanation: ⓐ: 주격 관계대명사 who는 선행사 Individuals림 수식하므로 올바릅니다. ⓑ: 목적격 관계대명사 that은 선행사 the advice림 수식하므로 올바릅니다. ⓒ: 농구림 하는 눙동의 유미이므로 played로 수정해야 합니다. ⓓ: 선행사 the products가 있으므로 what 대신 that이나 which림 쌨야 합니다. ⓔ: the thing which는 목적격 관계대명사 구문으로 올바릅니다. ⓕ: tell의 직접목적어 절로 완전한 문장이 오므로 that을 쌨야 합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. ⓐAmong migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. ⓑSo when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. ⓒAccording to a recent study by some experts, however, the instinct of preservation of animals is strongest in summer. ⓓBy comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. ⓔChildhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물에게 있어 유년기가 환경 학습과 유연한 적응을 가능하게 한다는 내용입니다. ⓒ는 '동물의 보존 본능이 여름에 가장 강하다'는 내용으로, 유년기의 역할이나 학습/적응에 관한 전체 흐름과 무관합니다.

questions.question: 8. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children.
ordered_passages: (A) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two.
(B) As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time.

(C) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 수렵 채집인 어머니들이 아이들을 데리고 이동해야 했다는 고충을 언급했습니다. 이에 대한 결과로 (B)에서 아이를 4년에 한 번씩 낳을 수밖에 없었다는 내용이 이어집니다. 그 다음 (A)에서 대조적으로 농부들은 한곳에 머물며 출산 간격을 줄일 수 있었다는 내용이 나오고, (C)에서 이것이 의미하는 바(더 많은 자녀 출산 및 인구 증가)와 그 장점으로 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. (A) However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. (B) A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. (C) A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. (D) When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. (E) The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO2 , and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 인터넷과 전기가 환경에 미치는 비용이 무시되고 있다는 내용입니다. (B) 앞뒤 내용은 종이 사용 감소로 나무를 구하게 되었다는 긍정적인 측면을 설명하고 있습니다. (C) 뒤의 내용은 데이터 센터의 화석 연료 사용과 탄소 배출에 대한 구체적인 부정적 사례가 등장하므로, 화두를 던지는 주어진 문장은 (C) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (A)____________, the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. (B)____________, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. Thus, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 즉각적인 즐거움 대신 미래의 것을 선택한다고 했으므로, 그 결과로 미래 보상의 가치가 현재보다 커야 한다는 인과관계의 연결어 'Thus(따라서)'가 적절합니다. (B) 뒤 문장에서는 저축한 돈을 크리스마스 선물 대신 여름 휴가에 써버리는 구체적인 사례를 들고 있으므로 'For example(예를 들어)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 따라서 / 하지만
② 예를 들어 / 그러므로
③ 따라서 / 예를 들어
④ 무엇보다도 / 더욱이
⑤ 그럼에도 불구하고 / 즉

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well­documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.
options: ① The Effect of Interruptions on People's Everyday Lives
② The Leader of The Civil Rights Movement, Martin Luther King Jr.
③ The Difficulties Faced by Professionals
④ How to Increase Work Productivity
⑤ The Influence of Literature on Human Mental Health
questions.explanation: 이 글은 도중에 중단되는 일(interruptions)이 창의적인 작업이나 전문적인 업무, 그리고 일반적인 사람들의 일상생활에 미치는 부정적인 영향(생산성 저하 및 스트레스 증가)에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 마틴 루터 킹 주니어와 사무엘 테일러 콜리지의 예시는 중단이 미치는 구체적인 피해를 보여줍니다. 따라서 제목으로는 '사람들의 일상생활에 미치는 방해의 영향'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들의 일상생활에 미치는 방해의 영향
② 민권 운동의 지도자, 마틴 루터 킹 주니어
③ 전문가들이 직면한 어려움들
④ 업무 생산성을 높이는 방법
⑤ 문학이 인간의 정신 건강에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is ⓐ<u>that</u> competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains ⓑ<u>to evolve</u> the way they did. A human tribe that could out­think its enemies, even slightly, ⓒ<u>possessed</u> a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, ⓓ<u>give</u> your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before ⓔ<u>it</u>. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out­think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'The ability of your tribe'이며 핵심 명사는 'The ability'입니다. 'ability'는 단수 명사이므로 동사도 단수형인 'gives'로 써야 하며, 전체적인 글의 흐름이 과거의 진화 과정을 설명하고 있으므로 과거 시제인 'gave'를 쓰는 것이 어법상 옳습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 전체 글의 흐름상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for ⓐ<u>how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations</u>. ⓑ<u>What has been considered and met fully for the most part</u>, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources ⓒ<u>are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing</u>, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design ⓓ<u>have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users</u>, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that ⓔ<u>our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without</u>.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 장애인들의 요구가 디지털 환경 구축 과정에서 충분히 고려되지 못하여 결과적으로 많은 자료들이 그들에게 무용지물(useless)이 되었다는 내용이 이어져야 합니다. 따라서 ⓑ의 '충분히 고려되고 충족되었다(met fully)'는 표현은 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. (A) When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. (B) Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. (C) Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. (D) As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 회색 다람쥐가 붉은 다람쥐에 비해 식단 적응력이 뛰어나서 우위(edge)를 점한다는 구체적인 이유를 설명하고 있습니다. (B) 뒤에 이어지는 문장에서 회색 다람쥐가 붉은 다람쥐보다 먼저 먹이 공급을 파괴할 수 있다는 내용이 나오므로, 식단 적응력이 뛰어나다는 점을 먼저 언급하는 것이 논리적으로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 Brainwriting에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [24년 6월 34번]
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ① 팀의 숨겨진 잠재력을 찾기 위해서는 브레인라이팅 과정이 더 좋다.
② 초기 단계에는 팀의 리더에게 아이디어를 내도록 요하고 익명으로 그룹에 공유한다.
③ 독립적인 판단을 유지하기 위해 각 구성원이 스스로 아이디어를 평가한다.
④ 아이디어를 선택하고 구체화하기 전에 개별적으로 아이디어를 전개하고 평가한다.
⑤ 집단 지성을 달성하는 데 어려움을 겪는 그룹에서 효과적이다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 초기 단계(The initial steps are solo)에서는 리더 혼자가 아니라 '모든 사람(everyone)'에게 아이디어를 개별적으로 생성하도록 요청합니다. 따라서 리더에게만 아이디어를 내도록 한다는 ②번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 24번]
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are-either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. (A)____________, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. (B)____________, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
options: ③ In brief / In other words
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장은 정체성에 따라 행동할 가능성이 높다는 일반적 원리를 설명하고 있고, (A) 뒤 문장은 투표자에 대한 구체적인 연구 사례를 들고 있으므로 'For example'이 적절합니다. (B) 뒤 문장 역시 운동을 정체성의 일부로 받아들인 사람의 또 다른 사례를 나열하며 유사한 논리를 전개하고 있으므로 'Similarly' 혹은 'Likewise'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 결론적으로 / 하지만
② 예를 들어 / 그럼에도 불구하고
③ 요약하자면 / 다시 말해서
④ 무엇보다도 / 마찬가지로
⑤ 예를 들어 / 비슷하게(마찬가지로)

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the _______________ of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
questions.explanation: 지문은 집중된 관심이 뇌의 구조를 개편한다는 내용과 관련된 과학적 근거를 많이 제시하고 있습니다. 특정 감각이나 기능을 많이 사용하는 동물이나 사람의 경우, 해당 뇌 영역이 커지거나 팽창하는 등 뇌의 물리적 구조가 변화하는 것이 핵심입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 뇌의 '물리적 틀(구조)'을 의미하는 physical framework가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 저장 용량
② 생물학적 수명
③ 물리적 부피
④ 물리적 틀(구조)
⑤ 구성 재료

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, ①<u>what they have</u> genuine decisionmaking authority - can radically increase ②<u>how many energy and focus</u> they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully ③<u>examining assemblyline workers</u> who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and ④<u>making fewer mistake</u>. Giving employees a sense of control improved ⑤<u>how much selfdiscipline</u> they brought to their jobs.
questions.explanation: ① what -> that : a feeling과 동격 관계이므로 뒤에 완전한 문장이 이어져 접속사 that이 올바릅니다. ② how many -> how much : energy는 불가산 명사이므로 much로 수식해야 합니다. ③ examining -> examined : 문장의 본동사가 없으므로 과거 시제 동사인 examined가 필요합니다. ④ mistake -> mistakes : fewer는 복수 가산 명사를 수식하므로 mistake에 -s를 붙여야 합니다. ⑤ self-discipline은 불가산 명사이므로 how much로 수식하는 것은 어법상 옳습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)를 괄호 속 우리말 의미가 나도록 주어진 <조건>에 따라 완성하시오.
questions.passage: As I walked from the mailbox, my heart was beating rapidly. In my hands, I held the letter from the university I had applied to. I thought my grades were good enough to cross the line and my application letter was well-written, but was it enough? I was anxious and uneasy. This worry was (A)________________ for the last three days. (이 걱정이 내가 지난 3일 동안 잠을 자지 않았던 이유였다.) As I carefully tore into the paper of the envelope, the letter slowly emerged with the opening phrase, "It is our great pleasure..." I shouted with joy, -I am in!- As I held the letter, I began to make a fantasy about my college life in a faraway city.
subjective_conditions: 1) 관계부사를 포함할 것
2) 5개 이하의 단어로 완성할 것
questions.explanation: 제시된 우리말 의미를 살려서, 이유를 나타내는 관계부사 why를 사용하고, '잠을 자지 않았다(과거 시제)'를 결합하면 why I didn't sleep이 됩니다. 이는 4단어로 구성되어 조건에 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 관을 읽고 주어진 <점건>에 따라 대화문 셍 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ를 한 단어로 채우시오.
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists say that having a disorderly room can indicate a disorganized mental state. One of the professional tidying experts says that the moment you start cleaning your room, you also start changing your life and gaining new perspective. When you clean your surroundings, positive and good atmosphere follows. You can do more things efficiently and neatly. So, clean up your closets, organize your drawers, and arrange your things first, then peace of mind will follow.
subjective_conditions: 모든 정답은 윗관에서 찾아, 형태를 변형시키지 않고 그대로 쓤 것
vocabulary_box: (A): When do you think is your life-changing moment?
(B): When I started cleaning my room, my point of view, namely ⓐ__________, has changed from ⓑ__________ one to ⓒ__________ one.
questions.explanation: 밸문에서 방을 치우면 새로운 관점(perspective)을 얻게 되며, 방이 지지분한 상태의 부정적인 기분(negative feelings)에서 긍정적인 분위기(positive atmosphere)로 바봔다눤 내용을 찾아 채우다. point of view와 동의어인 perspective를 ⓐ에, 바뀌기 전협 상태인 negative를 ⓑ에, 바뀀 협 긍정적 상태인 positive를 ⓒ에 기입한다.

questions.question: 21. 윗관에서 아랮 영영풀이에 해당하눤 단어를 찾아 한 단어로 쓤시오. (단, 단어가 동사일 경우, 동사의 '원형'으로 작성할 것)
questions.passage: All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too cold or too hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately nonthreatening. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment. This rewardlike effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chillieating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure. All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to selfharm is to have the pain always directly associated with a pleasurable
subjective_conditions: 단어가 동사일 경우 원형으로 작성
vocabulary_box: to connect someone or something in your mind with someone or something else
questions.explanation: 제시된 영영풀이눤 '마음셍에서 누군가나 무언가를 다른 사람이나 사물과 연갠시키다'라눤 뜻으로, 밸문의 마지막 문윙에 나오눤 'associated'의 원형인 'associate'가 정답이다.

본문에서 찾아 쓤 것
questions.explanation: 인간은 불편하더라도 뇌가 그것을 결국 무해한 '(고통)'으로 인식하기 때문에 지섽적인 노출을 통해 만접감을 '(이방하다/얻다)'다눤 내용이므로, 본문의 derive와 pain을 찾아 기입한다. (Humans derive satisfaction... harmless pain.)

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 우리말의 의미가 되도록 주어진 <조건>에 따라 문장을 완성하시오. [24년 6월 45번]
questions.passage: When the student began to panic, the instructor said, "Stay calm and steady. You can do it." Calm as ever, the instructor told her student, "Difficult times always happen during flight. The most important thing is to focus on your flight in those situations." <u>그 말이 교육생이 먼저 비행에 집중할 수 있게끔 용기를 주었다.</u> "Thank you, I think I can make it," she said, "As I've been trained, I should search for visual markers."
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어들을 모두 사용할 것
한 단어를 추가하여 12개의 단어로 완성할 것
필요한 경우, 단어의 형태를 변형할 것
questions.answer: Those words encouraged the student to focus on flying the aircraft first.
questions.explanation: '그 말(Those words)'이 주어이고, '용기를 주었다(encouraged)'가 동사입니다. encourage A to B 구문을 사용하여 '교육생이(the student) 비행에(on flying the aircraft) 집중할 수 있게끔(to focus)' 문장을 구성합니다. 추가할 단어는 'to'이며, 'encourage'를 과거형인 'encouraged'로 변형합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
questions.summary_sentence: Since the red squirrel has a more (A)__________ diet and habitat than the grey squirrel, the arrival and impact of the non-native grey squirrel have had (B)__________ consequences for red squirrel populations.
questions.explanation: 붉은 다람쥐는 먹이와 서식지가 회색 다람쥐에 비해 제한적(restricted)이기 때문에, 외래종인 회색 다람쥐의 유입이 붉은 다람쥐 개체군에 부정적인(negative) 결과를 가져왔다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 restricted, (B)에는 negative가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자연스러운 / 건설적인
② 다양한 / 운이 좋은
③ 유연한 / 파괴적인
④ 제한적인 / 부정적인
⑤ 해로운 / 사소한

questions.question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. ⓐMartin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." ⓑPerhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. ⓒFor Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. ⓓHe forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. ⓔInterruptions can serve as a social break to connect with others, and they can lead us to generate new ideas. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 방해(interruptions)가 생산성을 저하시키고 스트레스를 유발하며 창작 활동을 망치는 등 부정적인 비용(cost)을 초래한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 반면 ⑤는 방해가 타인과 연결되는 사회적 휴식이나 새로운 아이디어 창출로 이어질 수 있다는 긍정적인 측면을 언급하고 있으므로 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they ⓐ<u>did</u>. A human tribe ⓑ<u>that</u> could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, ⓒ<u>give</u> your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each ⓓ<u>succeeding</u> generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes ⓔ<u>responsible</u> for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'The ability'로 3인칭 단수입니다. 중간에 수식어구(of your tribe to imagine and predict...)가 길게 붙어 있으나 주어-동사 수 일치에 따라 'give'는 단수형인 'gives'로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓐ는 앞의 evolve를 대신하는 대동사 did로 적절하며, ⓑ는 주격 관계대명사, ⓓ는 '뒤이은'의 의미를 가진 현재분사, ⓔ는 genes를 후치 수식하는 형용사로 모두 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 올바른 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating ⓐ<u>what</u> focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid ⓑ<u>to be</u> hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that ⓒ<u>represents</u> the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is ⓓ<u>enlarged</u> in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to ⓔ<u>what</u> we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
questions.explanation: ④ 'enlarged'는 수동태/과거분사로 해마가 '확대되었다'는 의미로 적절하게 쓰였습니다. ⓐ는 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오므로 접속사 'that'이 적절합니다. ⓑ 'avoid'는 동명사를 목적어로 취하므로 'being hunted'가 되어야 합니다. ⓒ 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 복수명사인 'regions'이므로 'represent'로 수 일치를 시켜야 합니다. ⓔ 'direct our attention' 뒤에 'to'가 빠져 있거나 'to where' 또는 'to what'의 구조가 필요하며, 전치사 to의 목적어 역할을 해야 하므로 이 문맥에서는 'to what' 혹은 'where'가 쓰여야 합니다. (direct our attention to ~의 목적어가 빠진 상태에서 to what 혹은 where we direct...)

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, ______________________________. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
options: ① you prove yourself to be reflective
② you continue to behave as it usually it
③ you recognize and deal with inner conflicts
④ you constantly need to maintain who you are
⑤ you acknowledge your behaviors derived from various experiences.
questions.explanation: 글의 중심 내용은 행동이 정체성의 반영이라는 것입니다. 자신의 정체성과 행동이 일치할 때, 사람은 자신이 믿고 있는 모습대로 자연스럽게 행동을 지속하게 된다는 맥락이므로 ② '당신은 평소처럼 계속해서 행동한다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신은 스스로가 반성적임을 증명한다
② 당신은 평소처럼 계속해서 행동한다
③ 당신은 내적 갈등을 인식하고 처리한다
④ 당신은 당신이 누구인지 지속적으로 유지할 필요가 있다
⑤ 당신은 당신의 행동이 다양한 경험에서 비롯되었음을 인정한다

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. __________________ ________, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
options: ① Young birds rely solely on instincts to learn
② Childhood obstructs the sharing of cultural practices
③ Childhood hampers the exchange of cultural insights
④ During childhood, cultural information is easily passed down
⑤ Being young prevents the transmission of cultural knowledge
questions.explanation: 어린 시절(childhood)을 보내는 동물이 유전적 본능(hardware)에만 의존하는 동물보다 더 유연하고 효율적인 생존 방식(예: 이동 경로)을 배울 수 있다는 내용입니다. 부모와 함께 이동하며 배우는 새들이 더 효율적이라는 예시를 통해, 어린 시절 동안 문화적 정보(학습된 정보)가 전달된다는 점을 알 수 있습니다. 따라서 ④ '어린 시절 동안 문화적 정보가 쉽게 전수된다'가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 어린 새들은 배우기 위해 오직 본능에만 의존한다
② 어린 시절은 문화적 관습의 공유를 방해한다
③ 어린 시절은 문화적 통찰의 교환을 방해한다
④ 어린 시절 동안 문화적 정보는 쉽게 전수된다
⑤ 어린 것은 문화적 지식의 전달을 막는다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
options: ① challenges faced by hunter-gatherer societies
② influences of agriculture on population dynamics
③ limitations of transporting possessions somewhere
④ necessities of shifting from hunter-gatherer to farmers
⑤ comparisons between hunter-gathering and farming societies
questions.explanation: 농경의 시작으로 정착 생활이 가능해지면서 자녀를 이동시켜야 하는 부담이 줄어 출산 간격이 단축되었고, 이는 인구의 급격한 증가로 이어졌다는 내용입니다. 따라서 농경이 인구 변화(인구 역학)에 미친 영향을 설명하는 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 수렵 채집 사회가 직면한 도전들
② 농업이 인구 역학에 미치는 영향
③ 물건을 어딘가로 운반하는 것의 한계
④ 수렵 채집인에서 농부로 전환할 필요성
⑤ 수렵 채집 사회와 농경 사회의 비교

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are ⓐ<u>individual</u>. You start by asking everyone to come up with ideas independently. Next, you pool them and share them without ⓑ<u>revealing</u> their names among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and ⓒ<u>polish</u> the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas ⓓ<u>jointly</u> before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve ⓔ<u>collective</u> intelligence.
questions.explanation: 브레인라이팅 과정의 핵심은 아이디어를 공동으로가 아니라 '개별적으로(independently, individually)' 개발하고 평가하는 것입니다. 따라서 문맥상 '공동으로'를 의미하는 ⓓ의 'jointly'는 적절하지 않으며, 'individually'와 같은 단어가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① From Paper to Pixel: Inevitable Change in Business
② The Reason Why Eco-Friendly Digital is Sustainable
③ The Digital Shift: Saving Trees and the Planet
④ The Role of Digital Archiving in Enhancing Data Security
⑤ Digital Transformation: A Double-Edged Sword for the Environment
questions.explanation: 이 글은 비즈니스의 디지털 전환이 종이 사용을 줄여 환경에 긍정적일 것으로 기대되지만, 실제로는 데이터 센터 운영에 따른 전기 소모와 화석 연료 사용으로 인해 탄소 배출이 발생하는 등 환경에 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 디지털 전환이 환경에 '양날의 검'과 같다는 제목이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 종이에서 픽셀로: 비즈니스의 피할 수 없는 변화
② 친환경 디지털이 지속 가능한 이유
③ 디지털 전환: 나무와 지구를 구하기
④ 데이터 보안 강화에 있어 디지털 아카이빙의 역할
⑤ 디지털 전환: 환경에 대한 양날의 검

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 6월 24번]
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an ⓐ<u>indication</u> of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a ⓑ<u>particular</u> aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more ⓒ<u>likely to</u> vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to ⓓ<u>convince</u> themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer ⓔ<u>rejecting</u> behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
questions.explanation: 행동과 정체성이 완벽하게 일치할 때, 더 이상 행동 변화를 거부하는 것이 아니라 '추구'하거나 '찾는' 상태가 됩니다. 문맥상 행동과 정체성이 일치하면 억지로 변화를 꾀할 필요 없이 자연스럽게 행동하게 된다는 흐름이므로, ⓔ 'rejecting(거부하는)'은 'pursuing(추구하는)'이나 'seeking(찾는)' 등으로 바뀌어야 자연스럽습니다. (원본 지문에서는 'you are no longer seeking behavior change'로 되어 있습니다.)

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 (A)~(C)에 들어가기에 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 22번]
questions.passage: When it comes to (A)[help / helping] out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is (B)[come / coming] around and show that you care. If you notice someone who is lonely, you could go and sit with them. If you work with someone who (C)[eat / eats] lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. A person's happiness comes from attention. There are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. Even if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: (A) 'when it comes to'의 'to'는 전치사이므로 뒤에 동명사 'helping'이 오는 것이 적절합니다.(B) 'All you have to do is (to) come' 구문으로, 주어부에 'do'가 포함된 경우 보어 자리의 'to'가 생략되어 동사원형 'come'을 쓸 수 있습니다.(C) 선행사가 'someone'인 주격 관계대명사 'who' 절의 동사는 단수 형태인 'eats'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 어법상 오류인 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained (A)<u>neglecting</u> for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty (B)<u>distinguishing</u> particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often (C)<u>failing</u> to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea (D)<u>that</u> we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, (E)<u>ensuring</u> that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.explanation: (A) 'What has remained' 다음의 보어 자리로, 장애인들의 요구가 방치된 상태이므로 수동의 의미인 'neglected'가 적절합니다.(C) 'some scholars creating digital projects'가 주어이며, 문장의 본동사가 필요하므로 'failing'을 'fail'로 고쳐야 합니다.나머지 (B) difficulty -ing, (D) 동격의 that, (E) 분사구문은 모두 적절합니다. 따라서 오류는 2개입니다.
options_translation: ① 1개
② 2개

questions.question: 10. How can we improve the situation where the needs of the disabled have been overlooked in digital projects? Answer the question in Korean according to the paragraph above.
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained (A)<u>neglecting</u> for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty (B)<u>distinguishing</u> particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often (C)<u>failing</u> to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea (D)<u>that</u> we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, (E)<u>ensuring</u> that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.answer: 최대한 많은 사용자를 염두에 두고 최종 제품이 장애가 있는 사람들과 그렇지 않은 사람들 모두의 요구를 충족시킬 수 있도록 한다면 문제는 개선될 것이다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 제시된 해결책인 '항상 가능한 한 가장 넓은 층의 관객을 염두에 두고 디자인을 결정하여 장애가 있는 사람과 없는 사람 모두의 요구를 충족시키는 것'을 바탕으로 우리말로 정리하여 답변합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
options: ① Hunter-gatherers should pack all their stuff when they moved.
② Hunter-gatherer mothers spaced their babies' births about 4 years apart.
③ Farming communities had equivalent population to Hunter-gatherers.
④ People who live in the same place were able to reduce birth intervals.
⑤ Settling down in one place could provide more human labor.
questions.explanation: 본문에 따르면 농경 공동체는 정착 생활과 짧아진 출산 간격 덕분에 수렵 채집인보다 인구가 빠르게 증가했다고 설명하고 있으므로, 두 공동체의 인구가 대등했다는 설명은 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 수렵 채집인들은 이동할 때 모든 소지품을 챙겨야 했다.
② 수렵 채집인 어머니들은 약 4년 간격으로 아이를 낳았다.
③ 농경 공동체는 수렵 채집인과 대등한 인구수를 가졌다.
④ 같은 장소에 사는 사람들은 출산 간격을 줄일 수 있었다.
⑤ 한 곳에 정착하는 것은 더 많은 노동력을 제공할 수 있었다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve ____________ judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.explanation: 글 전체적으로 브레인라이팅 과정에서 개개인이 독립적으로 아이디어를 내고(solo, separately), 익명으로 공유하며 각자 평가(evaluates them on their own)한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '독립적인' 판단을 보존한다는 흐름이 가장 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 포괄적인
② 독립적인
③ 일관된
④ 제한된
⑤ 자격을 갖춘

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of ___________ improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
questions.explanation: 준문에서 직원들에게 자신이 통제하고 있다는 달터, 즉 '진정한 의사 결정 권한(genuine decision-making authority)'을 갖고 있다는 기분을 주는 것이 생산성감과 자율 규율을 높인다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따터서 빈칸에는 '권한'을 의미하눠 authority가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 긴장
반대
권한/권위
우울
감사/감상

questions.question: 20. 다음 광의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절합 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.summary_sentence: Despite the (A)__________ of farming, agricultural settlements result in (B)__________ civilizations.
questions.explanation: 지문은 수집 채집 생활에 비해 농경이 달대한 노동과 전얼변을 초래하는 등의 어려움(challenges)을 가지고 있었음에도 봈구하고, 결국 이러한 정착 생활이 인구 밀도를 높여 초기 도시와 문명이 등장하는(emerging) 계기가 되었다고 설명합니다. 따터서 (A)에는 challenges, (B)에는 emerging이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 장점들 - 등장하는
난제들/도전 - 완화하는
햼용/햼랽 - 유지하는
난제들/도전 - 등장하는
장점들 - 유지하는

questions.question: 21. 다음 광의 흠름으로 보아, 짼어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. (A) This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. (B) During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. (C) World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. (D) Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables.
questions.explanation: 짼어진 문장의 'these luxurious conditions'는 (D) 문장 앞에서 설명한, 비뇌와 관개를 통해 영양분과 수분이 퐒부한 농경지 상태를 가리킵니다. 또한 짼어진 문장의 'agricultural undesirables'(농업에서 반기지 않는 것들)은 (D) 다음에 나오눠 'every random weed'(잡초들)로 구체화됩니다. 따터서 짼어진 문장은 (D) 자리에 들어가는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 22. 짼어진 광 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a <u>degree</u> of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath.
ordered_passages: (B) This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies ─ capsaicin ─ touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure.

(C) The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment.

(D) All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is to have the pain always directly associated with a pleasurable reward.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 인간이 고통을 통해 즐거움을 찾는 현상을 설명한 후, (C)에서 괸 핵심이 '안전한 위협(safe threat)'임을 제시합니다. 이어 (B)에서 고추(캡사이신)를 예로 들어, 고통을 궼복하눠 만족감이 즐거움을 준다고 상세히 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (D)에서는 이러한 특성이 인간에게만 독특하게 나타나눠 현상임을 얼급하며 마무리합니다. 따터서 (C)-(B)-(D) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 윗글 (A)에 밑줄 친 degree와 비슷한 의미를 지닌 문장끼리 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: (A) All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a <u>degree</u> of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath.(B) This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies ─ capsaicin ─ touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure.(C) The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment.(D) All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is to have the pain always directly associated with a pleasurable reward.
questions.explanation: 본문의 'degree'는 '정도' 또는 '수준'이라는 의미로 쓰였습니다.ⓐ degree: 도(온도나 각도의 단위)ⓑ degree: 정도, 강도ⓒ degree: 학위ⓓ degree: 정도, 수준ⓔ degree: 도(온도)따라서 본문의 '정도'라는 의미와 일치하는 것은 ⓑ와 ⓓ입니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글에 우리말로 되어 있는 부분을 <보기>에 제시한 단어를 반드시 사용하여 영작하시오.
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict <u>어디에서 그리고 언제 한 적대적인 적 부족이 공격할지</u>, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 제시한 단어를 반드시 사용하여 영작하시오.
questions.answer: where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike
questions.explanation: '어디에서(where) 그리고(and) 언제(when)' 의문사를 병렬로 배치하고, '한 적대적인 적 부족이(a hostile enemy tribe)'를 주어로, '공격할지(might strike)'를 동사부로 구성하여 간접의문문 형태를 만듭니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists say that having a disorderly room can indicate a (A)[disorganizing / disorganized] mental state. One of the professional tidying experts says that the moment you start cleaning your room, you also start changing your life and gaining new perspective. Many psychologists also advise that everyone (B)[maintains / maintain] a tidy and neat room to significantly improve their mental state and overall well-being. When you clean your surroundings, positive and good atmosphere follows. You can do more things efficiently and neatly. So, clean up your closets, organize your drawers, and (C)[arranging / arrange] your things first, then peace of mind will follow.
questions.explanation: (A) mental state(정신 상태)가 혼란스러워진 상태를 설명하므로 수동의 의미인 과거분사 disorganized가 적절합니다. (B) 권고를 나타내는 동사 advise 뒤의 that절에는 '주어 + (should) + 동사원형' 구문을 사용합니다. 따라서 should가 생략된 형태인 maintain이 적절합니다. (C) clean, organize와 함께 명령문으로 나열되어 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 동사원형인 arrange가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 무질서하게 하는 / 유지하다 / 정리하는 것
② 무질서해진 / 유지한다 / 정리하는 것
③ 무질서하게 하는 / 유지한다 / 정리하는 것
④ 무질서해진 / 유지하다 / 정리하다
⑤ 무질서해진 / 유지한다 / 정리하다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your __________. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are-either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their self-image, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to votes than those who simply claimed "voting" was action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as part of their self-concept doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your self-perception perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람의 행동이 자신이 어떤 사람인지에 대한 믿음(self-image, self-concept), 즉 '정체성'의 반영임을 설명하고 있습니다. 자신이 스스로를 믿는 대로 행동하게 된다는 내용이 반복되므로 빈칸에는 'identity(정체성)'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 재능
② 취미
③ 일과
④ 선호도
⑤ 정체성

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As I walked from the mailbox, my heart was beating rapidly. In my hands, I held the letter from the university I (A)[applied / had applied] to last month. I thought my grades were good enough to cross the line and my application letter was well-written, but was it enough? I hadn't slept a wink for days. Especially last night, filled with insomnia as I worried and pondered over whether I would be accepted or not, (B)[was / were] a really hard time for me. As I carefully tore into the paper of the envelope, the letter slowly emerged with the opening phrase, "It is our great pleasure..." I shouted with joy. "I am in!" The excitement got me (C)[to imagine / imagined] my college life in a faraway city.
options: ③ had applied - was - to imagine
questions.explanation: (A) 편지를 손에 들고 있었던 과거 시점보다 대학교에 지원했던 시점이 더 이전이므로 과거완료인 had applied가 적절합니다. (B) 문장의 주어는 'Especially last night'이며 수식어구인 'filled with insomnia ~ not'을 제외하면 단수 주어이므로 was가 적절합니다. (C) 'get + 목적어 + to부정사' 구문으로 목적어가 ~하게 시키다/만들다의 의미이므로 to imagine이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지원했다 - 였다 - 상상하게
② 지원했다 - 였다(복수) - 상상하다
③ 지원했었다 - 였다 - 상상하게
④ 지원했다 - 였다(복수) - 상상하게
⑤ 지원했었다 - 였다 - 상상된

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① The impact of diet on brain health
② The effects of sleep on cognitive function
③ The role of genetics in brain development
④ the impact of focused attention on brain plasticity
⑤ the influence of social interactions on brain growth
questions.explanation: 지문은 집중된 주의력이 뇌의 재형성(reshaping)으로 이어진다는 과학적 증거들을 제시하고 있습니다. 동물의 청각/시각 센터, 바이올린 연주자의 피질 영역, 택시 운전사의 해마 등의 예시를 통해 우리가 주의를 기울이고 연습하는 것에 따라 뇌의 물리적 구조가 변한다는 '뇌 가소성(brain plasticity)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 식단이 뇌 건강에 미치는 영향
② 수면이 인지 기능에 미치는 효과
③ 뇌 발달에 있어 유전학의 역할
④ 집중된 주의력이 뇌 가소성에 미치는 영향
⑤ 사회적 상호작용이 뇌 성장에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two.
