An increased population was actually an advantage to farming societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.summary_sentence: The shift from hunter-gatherer to (A)__________ societies led to settled communities, shorter birth intervals, and rapid population growth, (B)__________ farming through increased human labor.
questions.explanation: 수렵 채집 사회에서 농경(agricultural) 사회로의 전환은 정착 생활과 출산 간격 단축, 인구 급성장을 가져왔으며, 이는 늘어난 노동력을 통해 농업에 이득을 주었다(benefiting)는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 농업의 - 혜택을 주는
② 산업의 - 보상하는
③ 농업의 - 손해를 입히는
④ 유목의 - 혜택을 주는
⑤ 유목의 - 보상하는

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendant of the winners.
questions.summary_sentence: In the evolution of mankind, (A)__________ thinking skills against enemies played an important role in helping mankind (B)__________ many descendants.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인류의 지능이 적들과의 경쟁에서 우위를 점하기 위해 진화했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 적보다 더 잘 생각하는 '우월한(superior)' 사고 능력이 생존 경쟁에서 승리하게 했고, 그 결과 유전자를 다음 세대에 물려주어 인류가 '번성하거나 나아가게(advance/prosper)' 하는 데 도움을 주었다고 요약할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 우월한 ... 나아가게 하다
② 열등한 ... 증가시키다
③ 본능적인 ... 번영시키다
④ 기만적인 ... 감소시키다
⑤ 성공적인 ... 감소시키다

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 get behind the wheel이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs. If you want to increase productivity, let employees <u>get behind the wheel</u>.\n*radically: 급격하게 **shift: (근무) 교대
options: ① take charge of the situation
② decide which uniform to wear
④ find the key to increasing efficiency
⑤ drive a car loaded with manufacturing materials
questions.explanation: 이 글은 직원들에게 통제권과 결정권을 부여했을 때 생산성과 자기 관리가 향상된다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장의 'get behind the wheel(운전대를 잡다)'은 비유적인 표현으로, 직원들에게 업무에 대한 주도권과 통제권을 주어 '상황을 책임지게(take charge of the situation)' 하라는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 상황을 책임지다/주도하다
② 어떤 유니폼을 입을지 결정하다
③ 생산성 향상에 집중하다
④ 효율성을 높이는 열쇠를 찾다
⑤ 제조 물품을 실은 차를 운전하다

questions.question: 25. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. ⓐThe grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. ⓑWithin the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. ⓒGrey and red squirrels gave up on each other in the middle of their fight for survival. ⓓGreys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. ⓔAs a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.*edge: 우위 **acorn: 도토리
questions.explanation: 이 글은 외래종인 회색 다람쥐의 유입으로 인해 토착종인 붉은 다람쥐가 생존 경쟁에서 밀려 멸종 위기에 처한 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. ⓒ는 회색 다람쥐와 붉은 다람쥐가 서로를 포기했다는 내용으로, 치열한 생존 경쟁과 붉은 다람쥐의 위기를 설명하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children helps animals learn about their environment. Without this period of youth, animals must depend more on innate abilities, making them less adaptable. (A) For instance, some migratory bird species are born with innate knowledge of how, when, and where to migrate. (B) When environmental conditions change, such as lakes drying up, forests turning into farmland, or breeding grounds shifting north due to climate change, these instinct-driven birds stick to outdated routes. (C) In contrast, birds with extended childhoods and those that migrate with their parents usually have more efficient migration paths. (D) This extended learning period allows cultural knowledge to be transferred, and culture can evolve faster than genes. (E) Therefore, a longer childhood provides flexibility in a changing world.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, these birds often have inefficient migration routes because they don't adapt well to changes.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 천부적인 지식을 가지고 태어난 철새들의 예시를 든 후, 주어진 문장의 'these birds'가 이들을 지칭하며 이들의 비효율적인 경로에 대해 언급해야 합니다. 그 뒤 (B)에서 구체적으로 환경이 변할 때 이들이 구식 경로를 고수한다는 내용이 이어지는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Giving employees a sense of control ─ believing they have real decision-making power ─ can greatly boost their energy and focus at work. A 2010 study at an Ohio manufacturing plant observed assembly-line workers who were given the ability to make minor decisions about their schedules and work environment. They chose their uniforms and managed their shifts while manufacturing processes and pay remained unchanged. After two months, productivity increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer errors. (A)___________ employees (B)___________ their self-discipline at work.
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 통제권(결정권)을 주는 것이 생산성을 높이고 실수를 줄였다는 연구 결과를 요약하면, 직원들에게 권한을 부여하는 것(Empowering)이 그들의 자제력 혹은 업무 규율(self-discipline)을 향상시켰다(enhanced)는 내용이 되어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 권한 부여 / 향상시켰다
② 가능하게 함 / 방해했다
③ 통제함 / 개선했다
④ 제한함 / 포기했다
⑤ 박탈함 / 지원했다

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은? [①~2464④]
questions.passage: (A) All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening.
ordered_passages: (B) This reward-like effect stems from mastering the pain, such as when enjoying spicy food. When capsaicin, the active ingredient in chillies, touches the tongue, it activates receptors same as those triggered by burns. Knowing that our body fires off signals of danger, but that we are actually in no danger, brings about pleasure.

(C) Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment.

(D) All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 '안전한 위협'이라는 개념을 제시합니다. (C)는 '안전한 위협'이 유머와 유사하게 작동한다고 설명하며 '보상에 대한 욕구'임을 언급합니다. (B)는 (C)에서 언급된 보상 효과(reward-like effect)가 고통을 정복하는 것에서 기인한다고 설명하며 매운 음식의 예시를 구체적으로 듭니다. (D)는 매운 음식에 대한 아이들의 반응 변화를 통해 이러한 행동이 인간에게 고유한 것임을 결론지으며 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 18. 윗글을 읽고 나눈 아래 대화문의 ①~⑤ 중, 본문의 내용을 제대로 이해하지 못한 부분은?
questions.passage: (A) All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening.(B) This reward-like effect stems from mastering the pain, such as when enjoying spicy food. When capsaicin, the active ingredient in chillies, touches the tongue, it activates receptors same as those triggered by burns. Knowing that our body fires off signals of danger, but that we are actually in no danger, brings about pleasure.(C) Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment.(D) All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human.
options: ① ①When we eat spicy food, the pain we feel is a 'safe threat,'
② ②Our body sends danger signals, but since we're actually safe, it feels pleasurable.
③ ③the satisfaction I get from eating spicy food comes from that
④ ④as you keep experiencing it, you come to realize that no matter how much effort you put in, it's impossible to be used to that pain.
questions.explanation: 본문 (D)에 따르면 아이들은 처음에 고추를 싫어하지만 '반복적인 노출(repeated exposure)'을 통해 그것으로부터 즐거움을 얻는 법을 배운다고 설명하고 있습니다. 즉, 고통에 익숙해지는 것이 불가능하다는 ④의 진술은 본문의 내용과 상반됩니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 매운 음식을 먹을 때 느끼는 고통은 '안전한 위협'이야.
② 우리 몸은 위험 신호를 보내지만, 실제로는 안전하기 때문에 즐겁게 느껴지는 거지.
③ 매운 음식을 먹음으로써 얻는 만족감은 거기에서 오는 거구나.
④ 계속 경험하다 보면, 아무리 노력해도 그 고통에 익숙해지는 것은 불가능하다는 걸 깨닫게 돼.
⑤ (해당 없음)

questions.question: 19. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것끼리 짝지어진 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The above graph shows the electronic waste collection and recycling rate by region in 2016 and 2019. ⓐEurope had the highest electronic waste collection and recycling rates in both years. ⓑAsia's electronic waste collection and recycling rates saw a slight decline over the period, moving from 15 percent in 2016 to 12 percent in 2019. ⓒThe Americas experienced a decrease in their electronic waste collection and recycling rates from 2016 to 2019, but they were still ahead of Asia. ⓓOceania maintained electronic waste collection and recycling rates below 10 percent in both years. ⓔAfrica maintained the lowest electronic waste collection and recycling rates, with no change, remaining at 0 percent in both years.
questions.explanation: 모의고사 원문에 따르면 아메리카 대륙(The Americas)은 2016년 17%, 2019년 9%로 감소하여 2019년에는 아시아(12%)보다 낮아졌으므로 ⓒ는 틀린 설명입니다. 또한 아프리카(Africa)는 2016년과 2019년 모두 0.9% 정도의 낮은 수치를 기록하긴 하지만 0%는 아니므로 '0 percent'라고 설명한 ⓔ도 틀린 설명입니다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤번입니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Your behaviors usually ________________________________. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are ─ either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
options: ① reflect how others want you to act
② mirror the essence of who you are
③ reflect an undesirable change in identity
④ align with what people perceive as natural
⑤ display the habits that you haven't developed
questions.explanation: 본문은 행동이 자신의 정체성(Identity), 즉 자신이 어떤 사람이라고 믿는지에 따라 결정된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 'voter'라고 생각하는 사람이 투표를 하고, 운동을 정체성의 일부로 받아들인 사람이 자연스럽게 훈련하는 예시를 통해, 행동이 곧 그 사람의 본질(정체성)을 반영한다는 점을 알 수 있습니다. 따라서 '당신이 누구인지에 대한 본질을 반영한다(mirror the essence of who you are)'가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 사람들이 당신이 행동하기를 원하는 방식을 반영한다
② 당신이 누구인지에 대한 본질을 반영한다
③ 정체성에 있어서 바람직하지 않은 변화를 반영한다
④ 사람들이 자연스럽다고 인식하는 것과 일치한다
⑤ 당신이 발달시키지 못한 습관을 보여준다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still ⓐ<u>endanger</u> the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a ⓑ<u>promising</u> step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is ⓒ<u>overlooked</u>. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, ⓓ<u>decreased</u> carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO2, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big. One research estimated that in a typical workplace, the carbon footprint is around 135 kilograms per person. Organizations should understand that excessive use of email, cloud storage, or online documents could lead to environmental ⓔ<u>concerns</u> in the near future.
questions.explanation: 본문은 디지털 업무 환경이 환경에 미치는 부정적인 영향을 설명하고 있습니다. 클라우드에 더 많은 데이터를 저장할수록 탄소 배출이 '줄어드는(decreased)' 것이 아니라, 화석 연료를 사용하는 데이터 센터 때문에 탄소 배출이 '증가(increased)'하여 환경을 해치게 되므로 ⓓ가 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: All historians agree that until about 12,000 years ago humans were nomadic hunter-gatherers, using stone tools and living in small, mobile groups.
ordered_passages: (A) Contrary to the life style of the earlier period, many human beings all over the world settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development.

(B) This period is referred to as Old Stone Age. The hunter-gatherer lifestyle described as "natural" to human beings appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases.

(C) At some point, however, humans began to change in a new way, not by the process of biological evolution but by cultural evolution. In other words, they developed the ability to alter their way of life by means of the farming revolution.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 12,000년 전 유목 수렵 채집 생활을 언급했으므로, 이를 '구석기 시대(Old Stone Age)'라고 지칭하며 그 특징을 설명하는 (B)가 가장 먼저 옵니다. 그 후 '그러나 어느 시점에서 인간이 변화하기 시작했다'며 농업 혁명을 통한 문화적 진화를 도입하는 (C)가 이어지고, 마지막으로 이전 시대와는 대조적으로 정착 생활과 농업이 발달한 '신석기 시대(New Stone Age)'를 설명하는 (A)가 오는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we're confronting a troublesome problem, we often gather a group to brain-storm. We're looking to get the best ideas as quickly as possible. It seems like a great approach, but there's a problem. Group brainstorming usually backfires. In brainstorming meetings, many good ideas are lost ─ and few are gained. Extensive evidence shows that when we generate ideas together, we fail to (A)_______________________________. Brainstorming groups fall so far short of their potential that we get more ideas─and better ideas─if we all work alone. Think about the brainstorming sessions you've attended. You've probably seen people bite their tongues due to ego threat ("I don't want to look stupid"), noise ("We can't all talk at once."), and conformity pressure ("Let's all agree with the boss."). These problems are even worse for people who don't have power or status: the newest person in the room, the only woman of color in a group of white men, the quiet person surrounded by outgoing people. To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. (B)<u>그러고 나서야 팀이 함께 모여 가장 유망한 옵션을 선택하고 다듬는다.</u> By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brain writing process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.* backfire: 역효과를 낳다
options: ② finish group work within a given time
③ find potential in a short time all alone
④ maintain anonymity when generating an idea
⑤ make members conform to the company's rules
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 맥락은 전통적인 브레인스토밍이 여러 가지 사회적 압박(자아 위협, 소음, 동조 압력) 때문에 효율적이지 못하며, 이를 보완하기 위해 브레인라이팅을 제안하고 있습니다. 따라서 브레인스토밍 환경에서 함께 아이디어를 낼 때 '집단 지성을 극대화하는 것'에 실패한다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 집단 지성을 극대화하다
② 주어진 시간 내에 그룹 업무를 끝내다
③ 혼자서 짧은 시간에 잠재력을 찾다
④ 아이디어를 생성할 때 익명성을 유지하다
⑤ 구성원들이 회사의 규칙을 따르게 만들다

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (B)의 우리말과 일치하도록 <조건>을 준수하여 알맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: When we're confronting a troublesome problem, we often gather a group to brain-storm. We're looking to get the best ideas as quickly as possible. It seems like a great approach, but there's a problem. Group brainstorming usually backfires. In brainstorming meetings, many good ideas are lost ─ and few are gained. Extensive evidence shows that when we generate ideas together, we fail to (A)_______________________________. Brainstorming groups fall so far short of their potential that we get more ideas─and better ideas─if we all work alone. Think about the brainstorming sessions you've attended. You've probably seen people bite their tongues due to ego threat ("I don't want to look stupid"), noise ("We can't all talk at once."), and conformity pressure ("Let's all agree with the boss."). These problems are even worse for people who don't have power or status: the newest person in the room, the only woman of color in a group of white men, the quiet person surrounded by outgoing people. To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. (B)<u>그러고 나서야 팀이 함께 모여 가장 유망한 옵션을 선택하고 다듬는다.</u> By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brain writing process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.* backfire: 역효과를 낳다
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어만 반드시 모두 활용하고, 필요한 경우 형태를 바꿀 수 있음
vocabulary_box: select, and, to, together, the, team, come, refine, do
questions.answer: does the team come together to select and refine
questions.explanation: 부정어구인 'Only then'이 문두에 오면 주어와 동사의 어순이 바뀌는 도치 현상이 일어납니다. 주어인 'the team'이 단수이고 현재 시제이므로 조동사 'does'를 앞에 두고 'does the team come together'의 형태를 갖춥니다. 그 뒤에 목적을 나타내는 to부정사 구문인 'to select and refine'을 연결하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains ⓐ<u>to evolve</u> the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, ⓑ<u>possessing</u> a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, ⓒ<u>gives</u> your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each ⓓ<u>succeeding</u> generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes which ⓔ<u>were</u> responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 속한 문장 'A human tribe (that could out-think its enemies, even slightly) ⓑ<u>possessing</u> a vital advantage.'에서 괄호 친 부분은 주어인 'A human tribe'를 수식하는 관계대명사절입니다. 따라서 문장 전체의 본동사가 필요한 자리이므로 현재분사인 'possessing'을 과거형 동사인 'possessed'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that the brain changes physically in response to focused attention. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much ①<u>expanded</u> auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the ②<u>visual</u> areas are larger. Emotional arousal may also be a factor in the activation that occurs when animals are rewarded for noticing sounds or sights, and the same factor may be involved in the ③<u>modification</u> of the brain when we participate in an activity that is important or meaningful to us. But when we are not engaged emotionally, the experience is less memorable and the structure of the brain is less likely to change. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic ④<u>reduction</u> in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. The point is that the ⑤<u>physical</u> architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
questions.explanation: 바이올리니스트들은 왼손으로 현을 누르는 연습을 고도로 반복하기 때문에, 왼손을 담당하는 뇌 피질 부분은 감축(reduction)되는 것이 아니라 오히려 증가 혹은 확장(expansion)되었을 것입니다. 따라서 ④번의 reduction은 어색하며 expansion 등의 어휘로 바뀌어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① ①
② ②
③ ③
④ ④
⑤ ⑤

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels. But interruptions can have benefits as well. They can offer a mental break from work, which helps to restore cognitive resources, they can serve as a social break to connect with others, and they can lead us to generate new ideas. When people were asked to keep diaries of their interruptions and the corresponding emotions they felt, 80 percent reported that interruptions generated positive as well as negative emotions for them, especially if they regarded the interruption related to a worthy effort. So while not all interruptions are bad, we do need ____________________________ so that we don't become overwhelmed by the unwelcome ones.
options: ① learn how to control our attention
② study how our distraction firmly remains
③ explain why inspiration is interrupted by stress
④ learn how to compose poems like famous writers
⑤ perceive attention as a whole rather than as separate constituents
questions.explanation: 이 글은 외부의 방해(interruption)로 인해 발생하는 해악(생산성 저하와 스트레스)과 그것이 주는 긍정적인 측면(정신적 휴식과 새로운 아이디어 창출)을 동시에 다루고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서는 모든 방해가 나쁜 것은 아니지만, 반기지 않는 갑작스러운 방해에 압도되지 않기 위해서 우리의 주의력(attention)을 스스로 조절하는 법을 배울 필요가 있다고 결론짓고 있습니다. 따라서 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 주의력을 조절하는 법을 배우는 것
② 우리의 주의 산만이 얼마나 견고하게 남아있는지 연구하는 것
③ 영감이 왜 스트레스에 의해 방해받는지 설명하는 것
④ 유명한 작가들처럼 시를 짓는 법을 배우는 것
⑤ 주의력을 개별적인 구성 요소가 아니라 전체로 인식하는 것

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of lack of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.summary_sentence: The agent (A)___________ a larger, later reward instead of a smaller, sooner one, yet sometimes reverses this preferences over time, which is commonly regarded as a example of (B)___________ behavior.
questions.explanation: 지문은 미래의 보상을 위해 저축하지만 유혹이 나타나면 이를 조기에 소비해버리는 행위를 다루고 있습니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 미래의 더 큰 보상을 '선호한다(favors/prefers)'는 내용이 들어가야 하며, (B)는 유혹에 굴복하여 결심을 바꾸는 행동이 '의지가 약한(weak-willed)' 행동의 예시로 여겨진다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 고려한다 - 할인된
② 거부한다 - 일치하지 않는
③ 선택한다 - 수동적인
④ 선호한다 - 일관된
⑤ 선호한다 - 의지가 약한

questions.question: 8. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the ⓐ<u>likelihood</u> of whether a buyer will repurchase the produce (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will ⓑ<u>encourage</u> others to purchase the product from you. ⓒ<u>Content</u> customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to ⓓ<u>convince</u> them to purchase products and services. By continually ⓔ<u>neglecting</u> your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체 맥락은 고객 만족을 챙기는 것이 부정적인 입소문을 피하는 방법임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 neglecting(무시하는 것)을 monitoring(모니터링하는 것)이나 ensuring(보장하는 것) 등으로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

options: ③ how to overlook customer responses
⑤ customer feedback for driving business growth
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구매 후 고객의 반응과 만족도가 재구매 의사와 긍정적인 입소문에 어떤 영향을 미치는지 설명하며, 이를 통해 사업 성장을 도모할 수 있음을 다룹니다. 따라서 '비즈니스 성장을 이끄는 고객 피드백'이 가장 적절한 주제입니다.
options_translation: ① 공격적인 비즈니스 전략
② 제품 광고에 대한 보상

④ 홍보 대사를 위한 보상 시스템
⑤ 비즈니스 성장을 주도하기 위한 고객 피드백

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸 (A)에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are fee of most of those that are socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were (A)_______________ in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were (A)_______________, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
options: ⑤ a large majority of people
questions.explanation: 지문은 사람들이 자신을 실제보다 더 낫다고 생각하는 경향인 'Lake Wobegon effect'를 설명하고 있습니다. 대다수의 고등학생들이 자신의 리더십 능력이 평균 이상이라고 생각하고, 대인관계 능력 또한 평균 이상이라고 생각한다는 통계 수치를 제시하고 있으므로 빈칸 (A)에는 'above average(평균 이상)'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 평균 이상
평균 이하
사회적으로 바람직하지 않은
덜 숙련되고 신뢰할 수 없는
대다수의 사람들

questions.question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, and they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give.
ordered_passages: (A) Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer.
(B) We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
(C) Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball.
(D) People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 전문 분야에서 높은 성과를 내는 사람이 다른 분야에서도 신뢰를 얻는 현상을 소개합니다. (C)에서 세계적인 농구 선수를 예로 들며 시작하고, (A)에서 그가 제품 광고로 돈을 버는 것이 제품 지식 때문이 아니라 농구 실력 때문임을 설명합니다. 이어지는 (D)에서 수영 선수와 배우의 사례를 추가로 제시하여 논리를 확장하며, 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 '탁월함'이 사람들을 연결시킨다는 결론을 내리는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, which then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly. As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you." If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler has been _____________________________. Strange as it may sound, this theory states that emotions arise from our bodies. For example, our mood can be improved by simply lifting up the corners of our mouth. If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, taking care not to let the pencil touch their lips (thus forcing the mouth into a smile-like shape), they judge cartoons funnier than if they have been asked to frown. The primacy of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase "I must be afraid, because I'm running."
options: ⑤ recognized as a contradictory emotional echo
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 타인의 보디랭귀지가 우리 신체에 영향을 미치고, 그것이 감정적 메아리를 만들어낸다는 것입니다. 즉, 웃는 사람의 감정이 우리의 신체적 모방을 통해 전달된다는 내용이므로 'conveyed through our body'가 정답입니다. 뒤이어 나오는 입꼬리를 올리거나 연필을 무는 실험 내용도 감정이 신체로부터 발생한다는 이론을 뒷받침합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 기분에 의해 영향을 받은
② 우리의 말을 통해 전달된
③ 우리의 신체를 통해 전달된
④ 신체적 반응에 의해 방해받은
⑤ 모순된 감정적 메아리로 인식된

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although technology has the potential to increase productivity, it can also have a negative impact on productivity. For example, in many office environments workers sit at desks with computers and have access to the internet. They are able to check their personal e-mails and use social media whenever they want to. This can stop them from doing their work and make them less productive. Introducing new technology can also have a negative impact on production when it causes a change to the production process or requires workers to learn a new system. Learning to use new technology can be time consuming and stressful for workers and this can cause a decline in productivity.
questions.summary_sentence: Technology has the potential to boost productivity, but (A)___________ like personal emails and social media can (B)___________ focus, while introducing new technology can lead to decreased productivity.
questions.explanation: 지문은 기술이 생산성을 높일 수 있지만, 개인 이메일이나 소셜 미디어 같은 요인들이 생산성에 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 설명합니다. 요약문에서 개인 이메일과 소셜 미디어는 주의를 흩뜨리는 요소이므로 (A)에는 'distractions'가 적절하며, 이러한 요소들이 집중력을 '방해'하므로 (B)에는 'hinder'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 혜택 ... 북돋우다
② 접근 ... 용이하게 하다
③ 장점 ... 지지하다
④ 환경 ... 향상시키다
⑤ 주의 분산 요소 ... 방해하다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 요지를 아래와 같이 작성할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, enabling us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Companies large and small have off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
questions.summary_sentence: In a(n) (A)___________ society, human beings do (B)___________ things, causing them to have less time.
questions.explanation: 컴퓨터화된 사회(또는 디지털 사회)가 인간에게 더 많은 여유를 줄 것이라는 예상과 달리, 기업들이 소비자들에게 예전에는 직원이 하던 일을 전가함에 따라 인간이 직접 '더 많은' 일을 하게 되어 시간이 부족해졌다는 내용이므로 (A)에는 digital, (B)에는 more가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 세계화된 - 가치 있는
② 컴퓨터화된 - 더 적은
③ 산업화된 - 확실한
④ 시민의 - 무보수의
⑤ 디지털 - 더 많은

questions.question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear the poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is _______________. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life - which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
questions.explanation: 부유한 국가일수록 삶의 속도가 빨라지면서 사람들이 항상 긴박함을 느끼고, 휴식할 시간이 부족하여 '시간 빈곤'을 느끼게 된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 핵심 쟁점은 '시간의 제약'입니다.
options_translation: ① 건강한 정신
② 시간의 제약
③ 사회적 불평등
④ 의료 서비스 접근
⑤ 사회경제적 지위

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy ⓐ<u>enhances</u> sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this ⓑ<u>approach</u> in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there wasn't a ⓒ<u>constraint</u> on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the ⓓ<u>abundance</u> condition, when thee was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't ⓔ<u>depend on</u> claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
questions.explanation: 지문은 구매 수량을 제한(scarcity)할 때 판매량이 늘어난다는 실험 내용을 담고 있습니다. ⓓ가 포함된 문장은 구매 제한이 있는 상황을 설명하고 있으므로, '풍요(abundance)'가 아닌 '희소성'이나 '제한된(scarcity/limited)' 상황이 오는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they ⓐ<u>promoted</u>. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, ⓑ<u>used</u> as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century ⓒ<u>were</u> buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer ⓓ<u>demand</u> for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped ⓔ<u>increase</u> sales.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 주어인 Fleischmann's yeast(효모)는 요리 재료로 '사용되는' 대상이므로 수동태인 'was used'로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Up until about 6,000 years ago, most people were farmers. Many lived in different places throughout the year, hunting for food or moving their livestock to areas with enough food. (A) There was no need to tell the time because life depended on natural cycles, such as the changing seasons or sunrise and sunset. (B) Gradually more people started to live in larger settlements, and some needed to tell the time. (C) For example, priests wanted to know when to carry out religious ceremonies. (D) Clocks have been important ever since. (E) Today, clocks are used for important things such as setting busy airport timetables - if the time is incorrect, aeroplanes might crash into each other when taking off or landing!
questions.insertion_sentence: This was the era when individuals initially crafted clocks - mechanisms that display, measure, and monitor the track of passing time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 인류가 처음으로 시계를 제작하기 시작한 시대에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. (C) 뒤의 내용은 성직자들이 종교 의식을 위해 시간을 알 필요가 생겼다는 구체적 배경을 설명하고 있으며, 주어진 문장이 시계의 등장을 언급한 뒤 (D)에서 '그 이후로 시계가 중요해졌다'는 결론으로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 25. Which of the following is the most appropriate title for the passage? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
options: ① The Brain and the City: The Interaction of Complexity
② The Brain's Economy: The Importance of Interaction Between Residents
③ The Similarity Between Cities and the Brain: The Role of Neural Signals
④ The Secrets of Brain Function: A Comparison with the Economy
⑤ How the Brain Works: A Metaphor of A City in Isolation
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 뇌의 작동 원리를 도시의 경제 시스템에 비유하여 설명하고 있습니다. 도시 경제가 한 곳에서 일어나는 것이 아니라 모든 구성 요소의 상호작용으로 나타나듯이, 뇌의 기능 또한 모든 뉴런과 신호들의 복잡한 상호작용의 결과임을 강조하고 있으므로 ①이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌와 도시: 복잡성의 상호작용
② 뇌의 경제: 거주자 간 상호작용의 중요성
③ 도시와 뇌의 유사성: 신경 신호의 역할
④ 뇌 기능의 비밀: 경제와의 비교
⑤ 뇌가 작동하는 방식: 고립된 도시의 비유

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providing students with relevant texts they will be interested in. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and discovered ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books." The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.
options: ① 난독증 환자는 직업적으로 성공하기 어렵다.
② 난독증이 있는 학생들은 독서를 피하는 경향이 있다.
③ 난독증이 있는 학생들은 한 가지 분야에만 열정을 쏟는 경향이 있다.
④ 난독증이 있는 학생들을 위한 보완 학습 프로그램이 개발되어야 한다.
⑤ 난독증이 있는 학생들의 성취도와 참여도를 높이려면 학생의 관심사와 관련된 글을 제공해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 필자는 난독증이 있음에도 불구하고 성공한 사람들의 사례를 통해, 그들이 자신의 개인적인 관심 분야에 열정적이었기 때문에 독서를 게을리하지 않았음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 학생들의 참여와 성취를 높이기 위해서는 그들의 관심사와 관련된 글을 제공해야 한다는 것이 글의 요지이자 주장입니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 밑줄 친 linguistic castration이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders ─ employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task ─ like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds ─ they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "<u>linguistic castration</u>." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
options: ① using language to show chimps' intelligence
② making tools qualitatively better than animals
③ holding a superior position in the natural world
④ manipulating words to discriminate animals from humans
⑤ solving cognitive problems with instinct instead of intelligence
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 다른 동물과의 유사성을 낮게 평가하고 인간의 우월적 지위를 유지하기 위해 언어적 기교(기술적 용어 사용)를 사용하여 동물을 우리와 소외시킨다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 'linguistic castration(언어적 거세)'은 인간이 단어를 만들어내거나 다르게 부름으로써 동물의 능력을 폄하하고 인간과 구별 짓는 행위를 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 침팬지의 지능을 보여주기 위해 언어를 사용하는 것
② 동물보다 질적으로 더 나은 도구를 만드는 것
③ 자연계에서 우월한 위치를 유지하는 것
④ 동물과 인간을 차별하기 위해 단어를 조작하는 것
⑤ 지능 대신 본능으로 인지 문제를 해결하는 것

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① 청자는 화자의 이야기를 귀 기울여 들어야 한다.
② 독자는 조용한 곳에서 과학 논문을 읽어야 한다.
③ 쌍방향 의사소통을 위해서는 소리를 키워야 한다.
④ 과학 논문은 발행되고 독자에게 이해되어야 한다.
⑤ 과학 논문은 이해를 돕기 위해 자세히 쓰여야 한다.
questions.explanation: 글쓴이는 소리가 들리는 사람이 있어야 성립하듯, 과학적 의사소통도 논문이 발행되는 것뿐만 아니라 의도된 독자에게 전달되고 '이해'되어야 비로소 완성된다고 주장하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The decline in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.
options: ① the infant's perception of the world
② the reason for decline in cuirosity
③ the process of automating neural pathways
④ the developmental process of the human brain
questions.explanation: 이 글은 유아기에 비해 성인이 될수록 호기심이 줄어드는 이유를 뇌과학적 관점에서 설명하고 있습니다. 유아의 뇌는 수많은 연결망을 가지고 있어 혼란스럽지만 풍부한 지각을 하는 반면, 성장을 거치며 자주 사용하는 신경 경로가 굳어지고 사용하지 않는 경로는 제거(가지치기)되면서 지식과 신념이 자동화되고 호기심이 감소한다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 유아의 세상에 대한 지각
② 호기심이 감소하는 이유
③ 신경 경로가 자동화되는 과정
④ 인간 뇌의 발달 과정

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation. If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. While the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a protective mechanism for the foot. Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now contract quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object. Sensory and motor nerves control almost all functions in the body ─ from the beating of the heart to the movement of the gut, sweating and just about everything else.
options: ① how sensory nerves harm our body
② the way our nerves secure and control our body
③ the similarity between sensory and motor nerves
④ the correlation between our pain and sensory nerves
⑤ the interaction between sensory nerves and certain sensation
questions.explanation: 글은 감각 신경이 자극을 받아 뇌로 전달하고, 뇌가 운동 신경을 통해 몸을 보호하는 반응(발을 떼는 동작 등)을 이끌어내는 과정을 설명합니다. 마지막 문장에서는 이러한 신경들이 신체의 거의 모든 기능을 제어한다고 결론짓습니다. 따라서 주제는 '신경이 우리 몸을 보호하고 조절하는 방식'인 2번입니다.
options_translation: ① 감각 신경이 우리 몸에 해를 끼치는 방식
② 우리 신경이 몸을 보호하고 조절하는 방식
③ 감각 신경과 운동 신경 사이의 유사성
④ 통증과 감각 신경 사이의 상관관계
⑤ 감각 신경과 특정 감각 사이의 상호작용

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
options: ① Passengers are afraid of flying because they cannot control the plane.
② Many passengers prefer a car to an airplane to reach the destination.
③ People are more likely to die in the plane crash than in the car accident.
④ Most people make decisions based on their anxiety rather than logic.
⑤ Logic suggests that flying is safer than driving in terms of death probability.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 자동차 사고로 사망할 확률은 5,000분의 1인 반면, 비행기 사고로 사망할 확률은 1,100만분의 1에 가깝습니다. 즉, 자동차 사고로 죽을 확률이 훨씬 높습니다. 따라서 '비행기 사고로 죽을 확률이 자동차 사고보다 높다'는 3번 보기는 본문의 내용과 정반대입니다. (참고: 4번과 5번 보기는 원문에 없지만 일치 불일치 문항의 구성상 유추되는 일반적인 오답/정답 선지 형태이므로 본문 근거로 3번이 명백한 오답입니다.)
options_translation: ① 승객들은 비행기를 조종할 수 없기 때문에 비행을 두려워한다.
② 많은 승객들이 목적지에 가기 위해 비행기보다 자동차를 선호한다.
③ 사람들은 자동차 사고보다 비행기 사고로 죽을 가능성이 더 높다.
④ 대부분의 사람들은 논리보다는 불안감에 기반하여 결정을 내린다.
⑤ 논리는 사망 확률 측면에서 비행이 운전보다 더 안전함을 시사한다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: Although technology has the potential to increase productivity, it can also have a negative impact on productivity. For example, in many office environments workers ⓐ<u>seat</u> at desks with computers and have access to the internet. They are able to check their personal e-mails and use social media whenever they want ⓑ<u>to</u>. This can stop them from doing their work and make them less ⓒ<u>productively</u>. Introducing new technology can also have a negative impact on production when it causes a change to the production process or ⓓ<u>requires</u> workers to learn a new system. ⓔ<u>Learn</u> to use new technology can be time consuming and stressful for workers and this can cause a decline in productivity.
questions.explanation: ⓐ seat → are seated 또는 sit (workers가 책상에 앉아 있는 상태이므로 수동태나 자동사 필요), ⓒ productively → productive (make + 목적어 + 목적격 보어 자리이므로 형용사 필요), ⓔ Learn → Learning (문장의 주어 자리이므로 동명사 주어가 필요함). 총 3개가 어색합니다. ⓑ는 want to (check/use)의 대부정사로 맞고, ⓓ는 causes와 병렬 구조로 맞습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: Sometimes the pace of change is far slower. The face you saw reflected in your mirror this morning probably appeared no different from the face you saw the day before - or a week or a month ago. Yet we know that the face that stares back at us from the glass is not the same, cannot be the same, as it ⓐ<u>has been</u> 10 minutes ago. The proof is in your photo album: Look at a photograph ⓑ<u>taking</u> of yourself 5 or 10 years ago and you see clear differences between the face in the snapshot and the face in your mirror. If you lived in a world without mirrors for a year and then ⓒ<u>see</u> your reflection, you might be surprised by the change. After an interval of 10 years without seeing yourself, you might not at first recognize the person ⓓ<u>peering</u> from the mirror. Even something as ⓔ<u>basically</u> as our own face changes from moment to moment.
questions.explanation: ⓐ has been → was (10 minutes ago라는 명백한 과거 시점이 있으므로 현재완료 불가), ⓑ taking → taken (사진은 찍히는 것이므로 과거분사 필요), ⓒ see → saw (가정법 과거 if S + 과거동사 구문이므로 saw가 적절), ⓔ basically → basic (as ~ as 원급 비교에서 something을 수식하는 형용사 필요). 총 4개가 어색합니다. ⓓ peering은 person을 수식하는 현재분사로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는? [2.9점]
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is ⓐ<u>disrupting</u> and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is hard ⓑ<u>that</u>  they imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" ⓒ<u>This</u> is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children should have opportunities of ⓓ<u>sharing</u> their backgrounds in a way which respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to ⓔ<u>build</u> a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 일상이 '방해받는' 것이므로 수동태 is disrupted가 되어야 합니다. ⓑ 가주어 it에 대한 진주어 자리인데, 뒤에 they imagine이라는 절이 오고 의미상 to부정사가 더 적절하거나 for them to imagine 형태로 써야 합니다. 또는 it is hard that~ 구문은 어색하며, for them to imagine이 자연스럽습니다. ⓒ 문장의 가주어는 This가 아니라 It이어야 합니다. ⓔ 'contribute to'에서 to는 전치사이므로 build를 building(동명사)으로 고쳐야 합니다. (지문 내 어색한 표기 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ 중 3개를 고르는 선택지 구성상 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ 또는 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ 등이 어색한 것으로 분류됨 - 정답지 기준 3개)

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는? [2.9점]
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. ⓐ<u>Naturally, this movement is such fast that you cannot see it</u> ─ you just see the blurred outline of the moving string. ⓑ<u>Strings vibrate in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about</u>. But if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note is heard loud and clear. ⓒ<u>The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string</u>. ⓓ<u>The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, that travel away from the guitar</u>. ⓔ<u>When the waves reach to your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'so + 형용사/부사 + that' 구문이므로 such를 so로 바꿔야 합니다. ⓑ vibrate와 make라는 동사가 두 개 쓰였습니다. Strings [vibrating in this way on their own] make ~ 형태로 분사구문을 쓰거나 접속사가 필요합니다. ⓓ 관계대명사의 계속적 용법(, that)은 불가능하므로 which로 바꿔야 합니다. ⓔ reach는 타동사로 뒤에 전치사 to가 필요 없으므로 reach your eardrums가 되어야 합니다. (어색한 것: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ 총 4개)

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible ⓐ<u>to work</u> anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in ⓑ<u>the way which</u> they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer ⓒ<u>separating or segmenting</u> roles so that boundary crossings are minimized. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" ⓓ<u>to carry</u> two phones ─ one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer ⓔ<u>to integrate</u> work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.explanation: 어법상 어색한 부분은 2개(ⓑ, ⓓ)입니다.ⓑ the way which → the way that / the way in which / how: the way 뒤에는 관계부사나 '전치사+관계대명사'가 와야 하며, 관계대명사 which만 단독으로 올 수 없습니다(뒷문장이 완전함).ⓓ to carry → carry / carrying: 지각동사 notice의 목적격 보어로 동사원형이나 현재분사가 와야 하며, to부정사는 올 수 없습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 바르게 쓰인 것의 개수는? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and ⓐ<u>because of</u> the fact that all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes ⓑ<u>which</u> scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways ⓒ<u>in which</u> do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there ⓓ<u>aren't</u> enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into ⓔ<u>which</u> is known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
questions.explanation: 어법상 바르게 쓰인 것은 2개(ⓐ, ⓑ)입니다.ⓐ because of: 뒤에 'the fact'라는 명사구가 오므로 전치사 because of가 적절합니다.ⓑ which: call의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 문장이므로 목적격 관계대명사 which가 적절합니다.ⓒ in which → which: 뒤에 동사 do not allow가 바로 나오므로 주격 관계대명사가 필요합니다. (in which 뒤에는 완전한 문장이 와야 함)ⓓ aren't → isn't: 주어인 'enough source material'이 단수이므로 isn't가 적절합니다.ⓔ which → what: 전치사 into의 목적어 역할을 하면서 동시에 뒷문장의 주어 역할을 하는 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what이 필요합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more ⓐ<u>successively</u> than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of ⓑ<u>discipline</u> and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. ⓒ<u>Managers</u> in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them ⓓ<u>receive</u> criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Most people do not tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people give feedback on how to be ⓔ<u>responsible</u> for sport organizations.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'successively'는 '연속적으로'라는 의미입니다. 문맥상 팬들이 실제 전문가들보다 더 '성공적으로' 스포츠 팀을 운영할 수 있다고 믿는다는 내용이 되어야 하므로 'successfully'로 고치는 것이 적절합니다.ⓑ discipline: 훈련, 학과목ⓒ Managers: 경영자, 관리자ⓓ receive: 받다ⓔ responsible: 책임이 있는

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore _________________________________. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
options: ① show your child good examples of life by your action
② don't say anything that compares your child to others
③ strengthen your child's desirable behavior through praise
④ watch it patiently when your child challenges something new
⑤ give your children time to think for themselves before disciplining
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 아이들이 부모의 말보다는 부모의 행동과 본보기를 보고 가치관을 배운다는 것입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 부모가 일상생활에서의 행동을 통해 삶의 모범을 보여주어야 한다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 행동으로 아이에게 삶의 좋은 본보기를 보여주어라
② 당신의 아이를 다른 아이와 비교하는 말을 하지 마라
③ 칭찬을 통해 아이의 바람직한 행동을 강화하라
④ 아이가 새로운 것에 도전할 때 인내심 있게 지켜보라
⑤ 훈육하기 전에 아이들에게 스스로 생각할 시간을 주어라

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 39번]
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status ─ they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, remember that _________________________ as customers may not be completely locked in to the product. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.
options: ① the popularity of a product is steady
② the stream of the sales does not change
③ the quality of the goods should be considered
④ the perfect complementary status is permanent
⑤ the complementary status can be changed any time
questions.explanation: 보완재 관계에 있는 제품이라 하더라도 소비자가 다른 대체 수단(예: 가솔린 자동차에서 전기차로)을 선택할 수 있기 때문에 그 보완재 지위가 영구적이지 않고 언제든 변할 수 있다는 유의점이 빈칸에 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 제품의 인기가 꾸준하다
② 판매 흐름이 변하지 않는다
③ 제품의 질이 고려되어야 한다
④ 완벽한 보완재 지위는 영구적이다
⑤ 보완재 지위는 언제든지 바뀔 수 있다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 21번]
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. (A)____________, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. (B)____________ we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
questions.explanation: (A)에는 숲에서 쓰러지는 나무 소리 비유와 과학적 의사소통을 연결하는 '마찬가지로(Likewise)'가 적절하며, (B)에는 앞선 논의를 바탕으로 결론을 이끌어내는 '그러므로(Therefore)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 마찬가지로 / 그러므로
② 마찬가지로 / 더욱이
③ 하지만 / 그러므로
④ 하지만 / 그렇지 않으면
⑤ 예를 들어 / 더욱이

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 34번]
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents.
ordered_passages: (A) The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
(B) In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales.
(C) The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 캠벨 수프 할인 행사 실험의 도입부입니다. (C)에서 실험의 구체적인 세 가지 조건(무제한, 4개 제한, 12개 제한)을 설명하며 시작합니다. (B)에서는 각 조건에 따른 판매 결과(무제한 3.3캔 vs 제한 5.3캔)를 비교 분석합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이 실험 결과가 실제 쇼핑객을 대상으로 한 것이기에 매우 강력한 증거가 된다는 결론을 내리며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 40번]
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad.
ordered_passages: (A) The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.

(B) Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods.

(C) There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 음식을 좋고 나쁨으로 딱지 붙일 수 없다는 내용입니다. (C)에서 '하지만 건강에 좋거나 나쁜 식단을 만드는 것은 음식의 조합'이라는 새로운 논점을 제시하며 소위 '좋은 음식'만 먹는 성인의 사례를 듭니다. (B)에서 그 '좋은 음식들'이 영양소는 풍부하지만 다양성이 부족해 건강한 식단이 될 수 없음을 지적하고, 이어서 가끔 프라이드치킨을 먹는 십대의 사례를 소개합니다. (A)에서 그 십대의 식단은 문제가 없지만, 매일 튀긴 음식만 먹는 사람은 나쁜 식단을 가진 것이라며 결론을 짓는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us.
ordered_passages: (A) One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Gobekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers.

(B) In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up radically remaking the society itself. Things are not so different in our own time.

(C) It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 건축물을 만들지만, 역으로 건축물이 인간 사회를 형성한다는 내용을 다룹니다. (A)에서 그 예시로 세계에서 가장 오래된 유적인 터키의 괴베클리 테페를 언급하며, 이를 만들기 전에는 수렵 채집인이었다고 설명합니다. (C)에서 이 거대한 석조물을 세우는 데 너무 오랜 시간과 세대가 걸려 건축을 마무리하기 위해 사람들이 정착해야만 했다는 구체적인 변화를 설명합니다. (B)에서 그 결과로 인류 최초의 농경 사회가 되었다는 결론을 내리며, 건축물이 사회를 근본적으로 재구성한 사례임을 강조합니다. 따라서 적절한 순서는 (A)-(C)-(B)입니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes.
ordered_passages: (A) In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture.
(B) The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.

(C) In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations ─ surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue ─ with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly.
questions.explanation: 옷차림으로 타인을 판단한다는 도입부 이후, (C)에서 일반적인 경향(기대에 맞는 옷 선호)과 함께 '약간의 규범 파괴'에 대한 예외적 연구를 소개합니다. (A)에서 그 연구의 구체적인 사례로 정식 파티에서의 빨간 나비넥타이나 강의 중 빨간 운동화가 더 높은 지위와 유능함으로 평가받았음을 설명합니다. (B)에서 이러한 결과가 나오는 이유(사회적 비용을 감수할 만큼 강력한 사람으로 보임)를 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 (C)-(A)-(B)가 적절한 순서입니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Up until about 6,000 years ago, most people were farmers. Many lived in different places throughout the year, hunting for food or moving their livestock to areas with enough food. (A) There was no need to tell the time because life depended on natural cycles, such as the changing seasons or sunrise and sunset. (B) For example, priests wanted to know when to carry out religious ceremonies. (C) This was when people first invented clocks - devices that show, measure, and keep track of passing time. (D) Clocks have been important ever since. Today, clocks are used for important things such as setting busy airport timetables - if the time is incorrect, aeroplanes might crash into each other when taking off or landing! (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: Gradually more people started to live in larger settlements, and some needed to tell the time.
questions.explanation: 지문 초반부에서는 사람들이 자연의 주기에 따라 살았기 때문에 시간을 알 필요가 없었다고 설명합니다(A 뒤). 하지만 주어진 문장에서 '더 큰 정착지에 살기 시작하며 시간을 알 필요가 생겼다'는 변화를 언급하고 있습니다. 이 뒤에 이어지는 (B)는 시간을 알 필요가 생긴 구체적인 사례인 '성직자들이 종교 의식 시간을 알고 싶어 한 것'을 제시하고 있으므로, 주어진 문장은 (B) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. (A) However few people ever learn how to negotiate. (B) Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. (C) This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. (D) But, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly ─ our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. (E) In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
questions.insertion_sentence: Due to this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time.
questions.explanation: (D) 뒷부분에서 현대인들은 가족, 친구, 동료 등 동일한 사람들과 반복적으로 거래한다는 사실을 언급합니다. 주어진 문장의 'Due to this'는 바로 이 '반복적인 관계'를 가리키며, 그렇기 때문에 자신의 이익과 상대방과의 관계 유지를 동시에 달성하는 것이 필수적이라는 결론으로 이어집니다. 이후 (E)에서 상호의존적인 세계에서 윈-윈(win-win) 결과가 유일한 대안이 되고 있다는 내용으로 연결되는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are ─ writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. (A) You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. (B) Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. (C) The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. (D) An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. (E) Period.
questions.insertion_sentence: However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth.
questions.explanation: 지문 전반부인 (C) 이전까지는 지적 능력, 기술, 매력 등 능력이 정의되는 다양한 방식들을 열거합니다. 주어진 문장은 'However ability may be defined(능력이 어떻게 정의되든 간에)'라는 표현으로 앞서 언급된 다양한 정의들을 갈무리하며, 능력이 자아 가치의 유일한 결정 요소가 될 때의 문제점을 화두로 던집니다. (C) 이후부터는 오직 수행 능력만이 사람을 평가하는 척도가 되는 상황에 대한 부연 설명이 이어지므로, 논리적 전환점인 (C)에 문장이 위치해야 합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.summary_sentence: Cultural diversity can (A)___________ productivity and the quality of life. But it may result in high communication costs and social divisions when it becomes (B)___________.
questions.explanation: 글의 앞부분에서는 문화적 다양성이 지식 파급 효과를 통해 생산성을 높이고(increase productivity), 삶의 질에 긍정적인 영향을 줄 수 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 'boost'나 'enhance', 'improve'가 적절합니다. 하지만 다양성이 일정 수준을 넘어 너무 커지면(too large) 의사소통 비용 증가나 사회적 분열을 초래할 수 있다고 경고합니다. 따라서 (B)에는 '과도한' 혹은 '압도적인'의 의미를 가진 'overwhelming'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 향상시키다 ... 제한된
② 증대시키다 ... 압도적인(과도한)
③ 감소시키다 ... 부족한
④ 악화시키다 ... 풍부한
⑤ 개선하다 ... 관대한

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As working anywhere, anytime becomes increasingly possible thanks to portable digital technology, boundaries between work and home are blurring. People have their own preferences about how to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people like separating or segmenting roles more in order to minimize the boundary crossings. For instance, they might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We have seen many of these "segmenters" carry two phones ─ one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. On the contrary, others prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.summary_sentence: In today's digital age, people take one of two positions on the boundaries between work and life: (A)___________ the boundaries, or (B)___________ them.
questions.explanation: 지문은 사람들이 일과 삶의 경계를 대하는 두 가지 방식을 설명합니다. 한 부류는 경계를 나누어 유지하려 하고(segmenters), 다른 부류는 경계를 통합하여 흐릿하게 만듭니다(integrating). 따라서 (A)에는 유지한다는 의미의 retain, (B)에는 흐리게 한다는 의미의 blur가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 유지하기 ... 흐리게 하기
② 세우기 ... 분리하기
③ 유지하기 ... 보존하기
④ 세우기 ... 극대화하기
⑤ 소홀히 하기 ... 흐리게 하기

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, ⓐ<u>which is the ratio of costs to output in production</u>. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way ⓑ<u>in which production could be made more efficient</u>, known as the "division of labor." (A) Making most manufactured goods involves ⓒ<u>several different processes used different skills</u>. (B) Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, ⓓ<u>a head is put on, and then it is polished</u>. (C) One worker could do all these tasks, and make 20 pins in a day. (D) Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. (E) Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day ─ a huge increase in productivity ⓔ<u>from the 200 they would have produced before</u>.
questions.insertion_sentence: But this work can be divided into its separate processes, with a number of workers each performing one task.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '하지만 이 작업은 개별 공정으로 나뉠 수 있고, 다수의 노동자가 각각 한 가지 작업을 수행한다'는 분업의 구체적 방식을 설명합니다. (C) 문장까지는 한 명의 노동자가 모든 일을 처리할 때의 상황(하루 20개 생산)을 설명하고 있고, (D) 다음 문장에서는 노동자들이 각자 전문화되어 생산성이 비약적으로 상승한 결과를 보여줍니다. 따라서 개별 노동자가 한 가지 일만 수행하게 된다는 전환점인 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, ⓐ<u>which is the ratio of costs to output in production</u>. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way ⓑ<u>in which production could be made more efficient</u>, known as the "division of labor." (A) Making most manufactured goods involves ⓒ<u>several different processes used different skills</u>. (B) Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, ⓓ<u>a head is put on, and then it is polished</u>. (C) One worker could do all these tasks, and make 20 pins in a day. (D) Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. (E) Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day ─ a huge increase in productivity ⓔ<u>from the 200 they would have produced before</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 'involves'가 본동사이며, 'several different processes'를 수식하는 분사가 필요합니다. 공정들이 다양한 기술을 '사용하는' 것이므로 과거분사 'used'가 아닌 현재분사 'using'이 쓰여야 능동적으로 목적어 'different skills'를 취할 수 있습니다. (사용되는 기술이라면 used가 맞지만 여기서는 목적어가 존재함)

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
options: ① influence of agriculture and settlements on human history
② what a high increase in population density brought to us
③ things we should remember from the New Stone Age
④ how conflicts could serve for the progress of civilizations
⑤ problems of hunters and gatherers in the development of mankind
questions.explanation: 이 글은 농경과 정착 생활의 시작이 고된 노동과 질병의 원인이 되기도 했으나, 결과적으로 인구 밀도를 높이고 도시와 문명의 발달로 이어지는 인류 역사의 중대한 전환점이 되었음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 '농업과 정착이 인류 역사에 미친 영향'입니다.
options_translation: ① 농업과 정착이 인류 역사에 미친 영향
② 높은 인구 밀도 증가가 우리에게 가져다준 것
대 대로부터 우리가 기억해야 할 것들
④ 갈등이 문명의 진보에 어떻게 기여할 수 있는가
⑤ 인류 발전에 있어 수렵 채집인들의 문제점

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
