questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electro-chemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
options: ① The brain's functions are mainly due to genetic factors.
② The economy of a city is located in its financial district.
③ Cities function due to their physical infrastructure, unlike the brain.
④ The functions of the brain are not solely attributed to any single part.
⑤ The brain is a complex organ responsible for controlling thoughts and emotions.
questions.explanation: 글쓴이는 뇌를 도시에 비유하며, 도시의 경제가 특정 장소에 국한되지 않고 여러 요소들의 상호작용으로 나타나듯 뇌의 작동 역시 어느 한 곳에서 일어나는 것이 아니라 각 부위들의 상호작용을 통해 이루어진다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 요지는 '뇌의 기능은 단 하나의 부위 때문만은 아니다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌의 기능은 주로 유전적 요인 때문이다.
② 도시의 경제는 금융 지구에 위치해 있다.
③ 뇌와 달리 도시는 물리적 기반 시설 때문에 기능한다.
④ 뇌의 기능은 단지 어느 한 부분에만 기인하는 것이 아니다.
⑤ 뇌는 사고와 감정을 조절하는 복잡한 기관이다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data enters' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① Digital Shift: The Illusion of Eco-Friendly Progress
② Influences of Our Environment on Digital Business
③ Digital Businesses: A Last Hope for Our Environment
④ Obstacles to Reducing Carbon Footprint in E-Business
⑤ Want to Save the Earth? Return to Paper-Based Business!
questions.explanation: 디지털로의 전환이 종이 소비를 줄여 환경에 덜 해로울 것이라고 생각하지만, 실제로는 데이터 센터 가동을 위한 화석 연료 사용과 전기 소모로 인해 상당한 탄소 배출이 발생한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로는 '디지털 전환: 친환경적 진보라는 환상'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 디지털 전환: 친환경적 발전이라는 환상
② 환경이 디지털 비즈니스에 미치는 영향
③ 디지털 비즈니스: 우리 환경을 위한 마지막 희망
④ 이비즈니스에서 탄소 발자국을 줄이는 데 장애물들
⑤ 지구를 구하고 싶은가? 종이 기반 비즈니스로 돌아가라!

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
options: ① Disadvantages of Being a Good Helper
② How Praise Can Work for Your Children
③ Unique Ways of Fostering Preschoolers
④ The Role of Difficult Tasks in One's Life
⑤ How Sophistication in Cognition Develops
questions.explanation: 칭찬이 어린 아이들의 행동 개선뿐만 아니라 자아 존중감 형성에도 큰 영향을 미친다는 점을 설명하며, 부모의 긍정적인 말을 내면화한 아이가 자신감을 얻고 더 노력하게 된다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로 '칭찬이 아이들에게 작용하는 방식'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 좋은 조력자가 되는 것의 단점
② 칭찬이 아이들에게 효과를 발휘하는 방법
③ 미취학 아동을 양육하는 독특한 방법들
④ 인생에서 어려운 과업의 역할
⑤ 인지적 정교함이 발달하는 방식

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists say that having a disorderly room can indicate a disorganized mental state. One of the professional tidying experts says that the moment you start cleaning your room, you also start changing your life and gaining new perspective. When you clean your surroundings, positive and good atmosphere follows. You can do more things efficiently and neatly. So, clean up your closets, organize your drawers, and arrange your things first, then peace of mind will follow.
options: ① Tidying Up: A Method That Changes Your Life for the Better
② Why Do People Keep Repeating Destructive Thoughts?
③ Everything You Need To Know About Depression
④ Surprising Reasons Behind Your Messiness
⑤ A Messy Desk Encourages A Creative Mind
questions.explanation: 지저분한 방은 부정적인 감정과 혼란스러운 정신 상태를 나타내지만, 주변을 정리함으로써 삶을 변화시키고 새로운 관점과 마음의 평안을 얻을 수 있다는 내용의 글입니다. 따라서 정돈이 삶을 더 낫게 변화시키는 방법임을 나타내는 ①번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 정리 정돈: 당신의 삶을 더 좋게 변화시키는 방법
② 왜 사람들은 파괴적인 생각을 계속 반복하는가?
③ 우울증에 대해 알아야 할 모든 것
④ 당신의 지저분함 뒤에 숨겨진 놀라운 이유들
⑤ 지저분한 책상이 창의적인 마음을 고취한다

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be ⓐ<u>marked</u> as their good or bad. There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "ⓑ<u>beneficial</u>" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not ⓒ<u>result in</u> a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise ⓓ<u>rarely</u> eats fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to ⓔ<u>support</u> his or her diet. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 요지는 음식을 단순히 '좋은 것'과 '나쁜 것'으로 나눌 수 없으며, 식단의 균형이 중요하다는 것입니다. ⓔ가 포함된 문장은 가끔 먹는 프라이드 치킨이 식단의 균형을 '망치지(ruin/harm/knock out of balance)' 않는다는 흐름이 되어야 자연스럽습니다. '지지하다/유지하다'라는 뜻의 support는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding ⓐ<u>nutrients</u> in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more ⓑ<u>ineffective</u> at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are ⓒ<u>loving</u> it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural ⓓ<u>undesirables</u>. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the ⓔ<u>natural</u> land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.explanation: 지난 50년 동안 기술자들과 농작물 과학자들은 농부들이 정확한 양의 비료와 물을 공급하는 데 있어 훨씬 더 '효율적(effective)'이 되도록 도왔다는 문맥이 적절합니다. 따라서 '비효율적인'을 뜻하는 ineffective는 문맥상 반대되는 의미입니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Body language has a hand in regulating your mood. By simply smiling, you can improve your mood and boost your creativity, according to research published in Cognition. Smiling is also contagious. Additionally, research published in Social Behavior and Personality found that smiling impacted participants willingness to help, as well as (A)[their / its] overall helpfulness. Participants who were smiled at also (B)[reported / reporting] feeling more positive after the interaction. Service with a smile can leave your employees feeling happier and more willing to cooperate with one another. It can also improve likelihood (C)[which / that] they will become patrons and clients.
questions.explanation: (A) participants를 가리키므로 복수 소유격인 their가 적절합니다. (B) 문장의 주어가 Participants이므로 술어 동사인 reported가 필요합니다. (C) 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오고 앞의 likelihood와 동격을 이루어야 하므로 동격의 접속사 that이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① their --- reported --- that
② their --- reported --- which
③ their --- reporting --- that
④ its --- reporting --- which
⑤ its --- reported --- that

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The Lake Wobegon effect is the human tendency to (A)____________ one's achievements and capabilities in relation to others. It is named for the fictional town of Lake Wobegon from the radio series A Prairie Home Companion, where, according to Garrison Keillor, "all the children are above average". In a similar way, a large majority of people claim to be above average; this phenomenon has been observed among drivers, CEOs, stock market analysts, college students, and state education officials, among others. Experiments and surveys have repeatedly shown that most people believe that they possess attributes that are more (B)____________ than average.
questions.explanation: 레이크 워비건 효과는 타인에 비해 자신의 능력이나 업적을 과대평가(overestimate)하는 경향을 의미합니다. 이러한 맥락에서 사람들은 자신이 평균보다 더 바람직한(desirable) 특성을 가지고 있다고 믿는다는 결론이 도출됩니다.
options_translation: ① 과대평가하다 - 바람직한
② 과소평가하다 - 호의적인
③ 확대하다 - 부족한
④ 과대평가하다 - 부정적인
⑤ 과소평가하다 - 현명한

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Companies large and small have ______________________________________. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
options: ① uploaded new items to attract consumers
② off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers
③ shown an enthusiastic support for customers
④ set up many production lines to meet the demand
⑤ done their best to offer supreme service for customers
questions.explanation: 과거에는 기업의 서비스로 제공되던 일들(항공권 예약, 체크인, 식료품 담기 등)을 이제는 소비자가 직접 수행하게 되었다는 내용이 뒤따르므로, 기업들이 업무를 소비자에게 떠넘겼다(off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers)는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 소비자들을 끌어들이기 위해 새로운 품목을 업로드했다
② 업무를 소비자들의 등 위로 떠넘겼다
③ 고객들을 향한 열정적인 지지를 보여주었다
④ 수요를 충족시키기 위해 많은 생산 라인을 구축했다
⑤ 고객들에게 최고의 서비스를 제공하기 위해 최선을 다했다

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on <u>hardware</u>, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood __________________________________________________.
options: ③ sets back migration and navigation abilities
④ facilitates genetic development and adaptation
⑤ enhances the acquisition of environmental knowledge
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물들이 어린 시절(아동기)을 거치면서 유전적인 본능(hardware)에만 의존하지 않고 환경에 유연하게 대응하는 법을 배운다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 어린 시절이 긴 새들이 부모로부터 문화적인 정보를 전달받아 더 효율적인 이동 경로를 가질 수 있다는 설명으로 미루어 볼 때, 빈칸에는 '어린 시절이 환경 지식 습득을 향상시킨다'는 내용의 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 학습과 적응을 저해한다
② 의존성과 취약함을 조장한다
③ 이동 및 항해 능력을 저퇴시킨다
④ 유전적 발달과 적응을 촉진한다
⑤ 환경 지식 습득을 향상시킨다

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always ____________________________ as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
options: ① strive to find the most rational alternative
② consider as wide a range of audience as possible
③ present a solution in accordance with the majority rule
④ establish precise criteria for determining right and wrong
⑤ keep the neglected from having access to the digital world
questions.explanation: 디지털 정보 기술이 눈부시게 발달해왔음에도 불구하고, 장애인들의 웹 접근성이나 필요성은 오랫동안 간과되어 왔습니다. 지문은 디자인을 결정할 때 장애인과 비장애인 모두의 필요를 충족시킬 수 있도록 가능한 한 넓은 범위의 사용자(audience)를 고려해야 한다고 강조하므로 ②번이 정답으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 가장 합리적인 대안을 찾으려고 노력하다
② 가능한 한 넓은 범위의 독자(사용자)를 고려하다
③ 다수결 원칙에 따라 해결책을 제시하다
④ 옳고 그름을 결정하기 위한 정확한 기준을 세우다
⑤ 소외된 사람들이 디지털 세계에 접속하지 못하게 하다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Up until about 6,000 years ago, most people were farmers. Many lived in different places throughout the year, hunting for food or moving their livestock to areas with enough food. Telling time wasn't necessary. (A) People's lives revolved around natural patterns like the shifting seasons and the daily cycles of sunrise and sunset. (B) They timed their work, meals, and rest periods based on the celestial cues, ensuring optimal productivity and harmony with the nature. (C) Traders and merchants needed to know the time precisely to organize market activities and guarantee efficient trades. (D) Priests required accurate time measurements to conduct religious ceremonies. (E) This was when people first invented clocks - devices that show, measure, and keep track of passing time. Clocks have been important ever since.
questions.insertion_sentence: As societies evolved, however, the need for the accurate measurement of time became essential.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 '사회가 발전하며 정확한 시간 측정이 필수적이게 되었다'는 전환점의 내용입니다. 이전까지는 자연의 패턴에 의존해 시간 측정이 중요하지 않았다는 내용(A, B)이 나오고, (C)부터 상인과 사제들이 구체적으로 정확한 시간을 필요로 하게 되는 사례가 시작되므로 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 6월 30번]
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. (A) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (B) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. (C) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. (D) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (E) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그러나 어떤 경우에 행위자는 예상된 때를 기다리지 않고 저축한 것을 조기에 사용한다'는 역접의 내용입니다. (C) 앞부분까지는 미래의 보상을 위해 현재의 즐거움을 포기하는 일반적인 저축 행태를 설명하고 있으며, (C) 뒷부분에서 크리스마스 선물을 위해 모은 돈을 여름휴가에 써버리는 구체적인 '조기 사용'의 예시가 나오므로 (C) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. (A) Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. (B) For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. (C) Doing the right thing is easy. (D) After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. (E) You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
questions.insertion_sentence: Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 정체성과 행동의 일치에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. (B)에서는 '유권자'라는 정체성을 가진 사람들의 예시를 들었습니다. 제시된 문장은 'Similarly(마찬가지로)'를 사용하여 '운동'을 정체성으로 받아들인 사람의 또 다른 예시를 들고 있습니다. 따라서 유권자 예시 뒤이자, 행동이 쉬워진다는 일반적 진술(C) 앞인 (C) 자리에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." ⓐPerhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. ⓑFor Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. ⓒHe forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. ⓓInterruptions can provide a mental break from work, helping to replenish cognitive resources, and they can also lead to the generation of new ideas. ⓔWhile there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 '방해(interruptions)가 미치는 부정적인 영향과 비용'입니다. 마틴 루터 킹의 언급이나 콜리지의 사례 모두 방해로 인해 작업이 중단되거나 영감을 잃는 부정적인 상황을 묘사하고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓓ번 문장은 방해가 정신적 휴식을 제공하고 새로운 아이디어를 생성하는 데 도움이 된다는 긍정적인 측면을 언급하고 있어 글의 전체적인 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. ⓐThe ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. ⓑThe human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. ⓒAnd this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. ⓓOvercoming a generation gap is so difficult that we have to cooperate with each other. ⓔThe tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 지능이 다른 부족과의 경쟁과 갈등 속에서 살아남기 위한 전략으로 진화했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ⓓ번 문장은 세대 차이를 극복하는 것의 어려움과 협력에 대해 이야기하고 있어, 진화론적 관점에서의 지적 우위 확보라는 주제에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show that you care. ⓐIf you notice someone who is lonely, you could go and sit with them. If you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. ⓑA person's happiness comes from attention. ⓒTo receive such attention, more and more people are struggling to develop their own unique social skills and personalities. ⓓThere are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. ⓔEven if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 타인에게 관심을 기울이고 함께 있어주는 작은 행동이 큰 도움과 행복이 된다는 내용을 강조하고 있습니다. ⓒ번 문장은 관심을 받기 위해 사람들이 자신의 사회적 기술을 개발하려 애쓴다는 내용으로, 타인에게 베푸는 관심의 중요성이라는 주제와 거리가 있습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하도록, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped increase sales.
questions.summary_sentence: Fleischmann's yeast has been promoted in (A)____________ ways according to its status in the market by the advertisers with (B)____________ in their attitude.
questions.explanation: Fleischmann의 효모는 시장 상황의 변화(집에서 빵을 굽는 사람들의 감소)에 따라 비타민 공급원, 천연 완하제 등 다양한(various) 방식으로 홍보되었습니다. 이는 광고주들이 상황에 맞춰 전략을 바꾸는 유연성(flexibility)을 가지고 있었음을 보여줍니다.
options_translation: ① 구식의 / 격식
② 다양한 / 배제
③ 다양한 / 격식
④ 다양한 / 유연성
⑤ 구식의 / 유연성

questions.question: 24. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved.
ordered_passages: (A) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two.(B) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.(C) In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 수렵 채집인이 이동할 때 짐을 모두 챙겨야 했다는 내용이 나옵니다. (C)에서 특히 어머니들이 아이를 업고 이동해야 했기 때문에 출산 간격이 길었다는 구체적인 어려움이 이어집니다. (A)에서는 이와 반대로(on the other hand) 농경 사회에서는 정착 생활로 인해 출산 간격이 줄어들었음을 설명합니다. (B)에서는 이러한 출산 간격 단축이 인구 증가로 이어졌으며, 이는 노동력이 많이 필요한 농경 사회에 이점이 되었다는 결과로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 25. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them.
ordered_passages: (A) Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool.(B) When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball.(C) And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 전문 분야에서 뛰어난 성과를 내는 사람이 타인에게 신뢰를 얻는다는 내용입니다. (B)에서 그들의 기술과 무관한 분야에서도 사람들이 귀를 기울인다는 일반적인 설명을 하고, 예시로 유명 농구 선수를 언급합니다. (A)에서 그 농구 선수의 예시를 구체화하여 그가 홍보하는 제품 지식 때문이 아니라 농구 실력 때문에 사람들이 신뢰한다는 점을 밝히고 수영 선수의 예시를 덧붙입니다. (C)에서 배우의 예시를 추가하며 '탁월함이 연결해준다(Excellence connects)'는 결론으로 내용을 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
questions.summary_sentence: Understanding post-purchase behavior helps ensure repurchases, customer (A)_____________, and the prevention of negative word-of-mouth, which makes customer (B)_____________ a top priority.
questions.explanation: 지문은 구매 후 행동을 이해함으로써 재구매 여부를 파악하고 만족한 고객이 다른 사람에게 제품을 추천하게 만든다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 고객의 '추천(recommendations)'이 적절하며, 이를 위해 고객의 '충족/만족(fulfillment/satisfaction)'이 우선순위가 되어야 하므로 (B)에는 fulfillment가 적합합니다. 3번의 경우 (A)에 부정적인 의미인 complaints가 오기 때문에 전체 문맥과 맞지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 추천 / 결정
② 추천 / 충족(만족)
③ 불만 / 만족
④ 불만 / 칭찬
⑤ 충성도 / 심사숙고

questions.question: 27. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'.
ordered_passages: (A) Our body fires off danger signals. Knowing that we are actually completely safe despite these signals ⓐ<u>produces</u> pleasure. All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and ⓑ<u>knowing</u> that they will never experience any real harm.

(B) This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more ⓒ<u>remarkably</u> it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues ⓓ<u>are</u> burned.

(C) The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, ⓔ<u>where</u> survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 고통을 수반하는 활동을 즐기는 것을 '안전한 위협'이라고 정의했습니다. (C)에서는 뇌가 자극을 고통스럽지만 비위협적으로 인식한다는 점을 설명하며 유머와의 유사성을 언급합니다. (B)에서는 고통에 대한 지배력(mastery)에서 오는 보상 효과를 설명하며 고추(chilli)의 예를 도입합니다. (A)에서는 고추를 먹을 때 몸은 위험 신호를 보내지만 안전하다는 것을 알기에 즐거움을 얻는다는 구체적인 과정을 설명하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 28. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'.(A) Our body fires off danger signals. Knowing that we are actually completely safe despite these signals ⓐ<u>produces</u> pleasure. All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and ⓑ<u>knowing</u> that they will never experience any real harm.(B) This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more ⓒ<u>remarkably</u> it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues ⓓ<u>are</u> burned.(C) The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, ⓔ<u>where</u> survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 동사 'seems'는 2형식 연결 동사로 뒤에 주격 보어를 필요로 합니다. 'remarkably'는 부사이므로 보어 자리에 올 수 없으며, 형용사인 'remarkable'로 고쳐야 합니다. (ⓐ 주어 Knowing은 단수 취급하므로 produces 적절, ⓑ through 뒤 exposure와 병렬 구조이므로 동명사 knowing 적절, ⓓ 주어 any of these tissues는 복수 취급하므로 are 적절, ⓔ context를 수식하는 관계부사 where 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오므로 적절)

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to ⓐ<u>positive</u> externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause ⓑ<u>excessive</u> transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an ⓒ<u>increase</u> in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an ⓓ<u>attractive</u> feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are ⓔ<u>imported</u> into their own neighbourhood.*externality: 외부효과*fractionalization: 분열
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장은 '반면에(On the other hand)'로 시작하며, 원주민들이 다양성을 국가 정체성에 대한 왜곡으로 인식하는 부정적인 상황을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 다양성은 '매력적인(attractive)' 특징이 아니라 '부정적인(negative 또는 unattractive)' 특징으로 인식될 것입니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 어휘 중 영영풀이가 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel ⓐ<u>disoriented</u> when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite ⓑ<u>literal</u>, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between ⓒ<u>validating</u> children's past experiences and focusing on helping them ⓓ<u>adjust to</u> the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in ⓔ<u>transition</u>.
options: ① ⓐ: having lost his or her bearings
② ⓑ: describing someone who uses or understands words in a plain and simple way
③ ⓒ: validating: providing or confirming that they are valueless or worthless
④ ⓓ: to get used to it by changing your behaviour or your ideas
⑤ ⓔ: the process in which something changes from one state to another
questions.explanation: ⓒ의 'validating'은 '정당성을 입증하다' 또는 '가치를 확인하다'라는 의미로, 본문에서는 아이들의 과거 경험이 소중하고 가치 있음을 인정해 주는 맥락에서 쓰였습니다. 하지만 ③번의 영영풀이는 '그것들이 가치가 없거나 쓸모없음을 제공하거나 확인하는 것(valueless or worthless)'이라고 설명하고 있어 문맥 및 단어의 본래 의미와 정반대입니다.
options_translation: ⓐ: 자신의 방향 감각을 잃은
ⓑ: 단어를 평이하고 단순한 방식으로 사용하거나 이해하는 사람을 묘사하는
ⓒ: 그것들이 가치 없거나 쓸모없음을 제공하거나 확인하는 것
ⓓ: 행동이나 생각을 변화시킴으로써 그것에 익숙해지는 것
ⓔ: 무언가가 한 상태에서 다른 상태로 변하는 과정

questions.question: 17. 다음 글 (A)를 읽고 정리한 글 (B)에서 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: (A) Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.(B)Research Topic:①<u>The Correlation between the number of items and sales</u>Research Subject:three supermarkets in Sioux City, lowaProcess:•a control group: no limit on purchasing•two tests groups: ②<u>limitation on purchasing of either four or twelve cans</u>Result:•a control group: ③<u>3.3 cans of purchasing on average</u>•two tests groups: 5.3 cans of purchasing on averageImplication:④<u>In limited condition, consumers tend to generally buy more products than usual</u>.Comments:⑤<u>The experimental results are significant because it processed refined data</u>.
questions.explanation: 지문 마지막 부분에서 실험이 'claimed data(주장된 데이터)'에 의존하지 않았고 실제 쇼핑객을 대상으로 한 실제 환경에서 이루어졌음을 강조하고 있습니다. 'refined data(정제된 데이터)'는 보통 통제된 실험실 환경 등에서 인위적으로 가공된 데이터를 의미할 수 있는데, 이 실험은 가공되지 않은 실제 환경의 데이터를 사용했으므로 ⑤번은 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글에서 어법상 어색한 것 2개를 찾아 고치시오.
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people ①<u>gave</u> more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper ②<u>to get</u> to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways ③<u>coming</u> many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made ④<u>possible</u> the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and ⑤<u>led</u> to tourism growth.
questions.explanation: ① '사람들이 휴가림 받엘다'는 수동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 gave림 were given으로 고쳐야 합니다. ③ With + 명사 + 분사 구문이 아닌, 'With the railways'는 전츠구이며, 들에 따라 동사와 주어가 댄치된 구문입니다. 문맥상 '철도와 함께 많은 대형 호텔들이 생겨났다'는 과거 시제 문장이므로 coming을 came로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists say that having a disorderly room can indicate a disorganized mental state. One of the professional tidying experts says that the moment you start cleaning your room, you also start changing your life and gaining new perspective. When you clean your surroundings, positive and good atmosphere follows. You can do more things efficiently and neatly. So, clean up your closets, organize your drawers, and arrange your things first, then peace of mind will follow.
options: ① Have a posture that is not affected by your surroundings.
② Organize your own space to promote positive change.
③ Think about how to handle things efficiently.
④ Try creative thinking in a disorderly room.
⑤ Be receptive to expert advice.
questions.explanation: 방을 정리하는 것이 삶을 변화시키고 새로운 관점을 얻게 하며, 마음의 평화를 가져다준다는 내용이므로, 자신의 공간을 정리하여 긍정적인 변화를 도모하라는 주장이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 주변 환경에 영향을 받지 않는 자세를 가져라.
② 긍정적인 변화를 촉진하기 위해 자신의 공간을 정리하라.
③ 일을 효율적으로 처리하는 방법에 대해 생각하라.
④ 어질러진 방에서 창의적인 사고를 시도하라.
⑤ 전문가의 조언을 수용하라.

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth.
ordered_passages: (A) World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it.(B) This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both.(C) Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 농지가 단일 재배를 위한 완벽한 환경이 되도록 강요받는다고 언급합니다. (B)에서 이것이 비료와 관개를 통해 어떻게 달성되는지 설명하며 (A)로 연결되어 비료 사용과 관개 능력이 비약적으로 늘어난 통계치를 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 '이러한 호사스러운 조건'이 잡초를 불러모은다는 역효과(부작용)를 설명하며 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a(n) ____________ of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 행동이 정체성을 반영하며, 정체성이 확립되면 그에 따른 행동을 하는 것이 자연스럽고 쉬워진다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 빈칸에는 '행동은 정체성의 [반영]이다'라는 의미가 들어가야 하므로 reflection이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 위기
② 왜곡
③ 환상
④ 개혁
⑤ 반영

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence which ①<u>demonstrate</u> that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals ②<u>rewarding</u> for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals that receive rewards for keen eyesight, their visual regions exhibit increased size. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, ③<u>show</u> dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, ④<u>are enlarged</u> in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and ⑤<u>what</u> we practice doing.
questions.explanation: ① demonstrate -> demonstrates: 선행사 evidence가 단수이므로 단수 동사 필요.② rewarding -> rewarded: 동물이 소리를 알아챈 것에 대해 보상을 '받는' 것이므로 과거분사 수동형 필요.③ show -> showing: 문맥상 증거를 제공하면서 ~를 '보여준다'는 분사구문 능동형 필요.④ are enlarged -> is enlarged: 주어인 hippocampus가 단수이므로 단수 동사 필요.⑤ what: practice의 목적어 역할을 하는 관계대명사 what으로 어법상 옳음.따라서 옳은 것은 ⑤ 1개입니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
options: ① Genetic Instincts Increase Bird Migration Efficiency
② The Role of Peers in Enhancing Birds' Migration Efficiency
③ Absent Childhood: A Sure Path no Success in a Changing World
④ The Characteristic of Bird Species: the Tendency to Have Long Childhoods
⑤ Flexibility in Migration: The Advantage of Birds' Learning from Parents during Childhood
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린 시절(유년기)의 중요성을 강조하며, 특히 이동하는 새들의 사례를 통해 유년기가 길고 부모로부터 학습하는 새들이 변화하는 환경에서 더 유연하고 효율적인 이동 경로를 가질 수 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '이동에서의 유연성: 유년기 동안 부모로부터 배우는 새들의 이점'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 유전적 본능이 새의 이동 효율성을 증가시킨다
새의 이동 효율성을 높이는 데 있어 동료의 역할
유년기의 부재: 변화하는 세상에서 성공으로 가는 확실한 길
조류의 특징: 긴 유년기를 갖는 경향
이동의 유연성: 유년기 동안 부모로부터 배우는 새들의 이점

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less ⓐ<u>harmful</u>. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much ⓑ<u>less</u> paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is ⓒ<u>overlooked</u>. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, ⓓ<u>increased</u> carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big. Organizations should be aware that unnecessary use of mail, cloud, or online documentation will ⓔ<u>contribute</u> to environmental problems.
questions.explanation: ⓑ less → more: 수십 년 전 모든 서류가 종이 기반이었을 때는 종이 낭비가 훨씬 '더 많았다(more)'고 해야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다. 뒤이어 사무실이 종이에서 디지털로 전환되면서 나무를 살리는 유망한 단계였다는 내용과 대조를 이룹니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. (A) Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. (B) When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. (C) The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. (D) Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. (E) As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
questions.insertion_sentence: Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 회색다람쥐가 더 조밀하게 살 수 있고 다양한 서식지에서 살 수 있어 숲이 파괴되었을 때 더 쉽게 생존했다는 추가적인 생존 이점을 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 앞서 언급된 먹이 적응 능력(녹색 도토리 섭취)에 이은 또 다른 경쟁 우위 요소입니다. 이러한 여러 경쟁 우위의 결과로 토착종인 붉은다람쥐가 멸종 위기에 처하게 되었다는 (E) 뒤의 결론 문장 앞에 오는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ① 직원에게 주도성을 주면 업무 생산성이 올라간다.
② 직원의 급여 인상이 곧 회사의 수익성으로 직결된다.
③ 직원의 업무 효율을 위해서는 휴식시간이 필수적이다.
④ 회사에서는 관리자와 직원 간의 소통이 가장 중요하다.
⑤ 직원의 실수를 감싸줄 때 회사에 대한 충성심이 생긴다.
questions.explanation: 본문은 직원들에게 스스로 통제하고 결정할 수 있는 '주도성(sense of agency)'을 부여했을 때, 에너지가 집중되고 생산성이 20% 증가했다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 요지는 직원의 주도성이 생산성 향상으로 이어진다는 내용입니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention ⓐ<u>leads</u> to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being ⓑ<u>hunting</u> for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that ⓒ<u>represent</u> the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is ⓓ<u>enlarged</u> in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and ⓔ<u>where</u> we practice doing.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 'avoid being hunted'는 '사냥당하는 것을 피하다'라는 수동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 현재분사 hunting을 과거분사 hunted로 고쳐야 합니다. 'avoid being p.p.' 구문입니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had ⓐ<u>much</u> to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors ⓑ<u>enjoyed</u> abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in ⓒ<u>permanent</u> villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high ⓓ<u>decrease</u> in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a ⓔ<u>major</u> turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.explanation: 농경과 정착 생활의 발달은 인구 밀도의 '감소(decrease)'가 아니라 '증가(increase)'를 가져왔습니다. 인구가 밀집된 정착촌이 형성되면서 전염병이 뿌리를 내리게 된 배경을 설명하고 있으므로 문맥상 decrease는 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is (A)[achieved / interrupted] by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more (B)[efficient / inefficient] at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the (C)[natural / artificial] land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.subjective_answer_format: (A)     (B)  (C)① achieved  efficientnatural② interrupted  efficientartificial③ achieved  inefficientartificial④ interrupted  inefficientnatural⑤ achieved  efficientartificial
questions.explanation: (A) 비료와 관개를 통해 단일 재배를 위한 완벽한 환경이 '달성되는(achieved)' 것이고, (B) 과학자들의 도움으로 농부들은 비료와 물을 공급하는 데 더 '효율적(efficient)'이 되었으며, (C) 영양분과 물이 풍부한 농경지는 그 주변을 둘러싼 '자연적인(natural)' 땅과 대비되는 개념이므로 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 달성된 - 효율적인 - 자연적인
② 방해받은 - 효율적인 - 인공적인
③ 달성된 - 비효율적인 - 인공적인
④ 방해받은 - 비효율적인 - 자연적인
⑤ 달성된 - 효율적인 - 인공적인

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show that you care. If you notice someone who is lonely, you could go and sit with them. If you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. A person's happiness comes from __________. There are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. Even if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 외로운 사람과 함께 앉아주거나 관심을 보이는 사소한 행동이 큰 도움이 된다고 말하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서도 인사 한 번이 누군가 자신을 신경 써준다는 느낌을 주어 기분을 좋게 만든다고 설명하므로, 인간의 행복은 타인으로부터 받는 '관심(attention)'에서 온다는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 야망
② 관심
③ 매력/끌림
④ 성취
⑤ 업적/완수

questions.question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved.
ordered_passages: (A) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two.

(B) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, leading to rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies.

(C) In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 농경으로 인한 정착 생활과 수렵 채집인의 이동 생활을 대조합니다. 이동이 잦았던 수렵 채집 사회의 특징을 이어받아, (C)에서 특히 어머니들이 아이를 업고 이동해야 했기에 출산 간격을 길게 유지해야 했던 상황을 설명합니다. (A)에서는 'on the other hand'를 통해 정착 생활을 하게 된 농경 사회의 변화를 대조하며 출산 간격이 단축되었음을 언급하고, (B)에서 이러한 변화가 인구 증가로 이어져 농경 사회의 이점이 되었다는 결과로 마무리되는 (C)-(A)-(B) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. He forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.
options: ② cost of being interrupted at work
③ increased productivity by work interruptions
④ differences in productivity between men and women
⑤ impact of interruptions on creativity and productivity
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서는 방해로 인해 시 작성을 완성하지 못한 사무엘 테일러 콜리지의 사례를 통해 창의적 활동에 미치는 부정적 영향을 설명하고, 후반부에서는 방해가 전문가들뿐만 아니라 일반인의 업무 생산성을 떨어뜨리고 스트레스를 높인다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 방해가 창의성과 생산성에 미치는 영향이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 휴식의 중요성
② 업무 중 방해를 받는 것의 비용
③ 업무 방해에 의한 생산성 증가
④ 남성과 여성 간의 생산성 차이
⑤ 방해가 창의성과 생산성에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 they(them)이 가리키는 대상이 다른 것은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of ⓐ<u>them</u>, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, ⓑ<u>they</u> started out as students, workers, and citizens. ⓒ<u>They</u> just possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing ⓓ<u>them</u> with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders like ⓔ<u>them</u> at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ는 모두 '지도자들(leaders)'을 가리키지만, ⓓ는 지도자들이 공유하는 '그들의 아이디어(their ideas)'를 가리킵니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that the poorer people are, the more stress they ⓐ<u>experience</u>: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, even ⓑ<u>developed</u> economics have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is time pressure. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a less ⓒ<u>fast-paced</u> life - which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time hardly left the population feeling a constant sense of ⓓ<u>relaxation</u>. In effect, rapid productivity creates ⓔ<u>wealth</u>, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they have no time to relax and enjoy themselves.
questions.explanation: 부유하고 산업화된 국가일수록 삶의 속도가 더 빠르다는 것이 문맥상 적절하므로, less fast-paced(덜 빠른 속도)는 more fast-paced(더 빠른 속도)로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 3. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others.
ordered_passages: (A) Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool.

(B) And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.

(C) People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skills has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 전문 분야에서 높은 성과를 내는 사람들이 신뢰를 얻는다는 내용입니다. (C)에서 사람들이 그들을 동경하고 그들의 말에 귀를 기울인다는 설명과 함께 유명 농구 선수의 예시를 시작합니다. (A)에서 그 농구 선수가 제품 홍보로 돈을 버는 이유가 농구 실력 때문임을 설명하고 수영 선수의 예를 덧붙입니다. (B)에서 배우의 예시를 추가하며 탁월함이 사람들을 연결해 준다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Although technology has the potential to increase productivity, ⓐ<u>they</u> can also have a negative impact on productivity. For example, in many office environments workers sit at desks with computers and have access to the internet. They are able to check their personal e-mails and ⓑ<u>uses</u> social media whenever they want to. This can stop them from ⓒ<u>doing</u> their work and make them less productive. Introducing new technology can also have a negative impact on production ⓓ<u>when</u> it causes a change to the production process or requires workers to learn a new system. Learning to use new technology ⓔ<u>are</u> time consuming and stressful for workers and this can cause a decline in productivity.
questions.explanation: ⓐ는 앞의 단수 명사 technology를 지칭하므로 it이 되어야 합니다. ⓑ는 are able to check와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 동사 원형인 use가 되어야 합니다. ⓔ는 동명사구(Learning to use new technology)가 주어이므로 단수 동사인 is가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 과호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 흐름에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, children begin to (A)[gain / lose] their curiosity as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The decline in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons work more (B)[efficiently / inefficiently] than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and widly disordered. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more (C)[probable / unlikely] and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤 문장에서 성인이 되면 질문이 줄어든다고 했으로 호기심을 'lose(잃다)'는 것이 적절합니다. (B) 유아의 뇌 배선은 씡말진창(a mess)이라고 했으로 성인밴다 '비효율적(inefficiently)'으로 작동합니다. (C) 세상에서 증거를 흡수함에 따라 특정 가능성들이 확실해지고 지식으로 고착되므로 'probable(있을 법한/개연성 있는)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 얻다 / 비효율적으로 / 있을 법하지 않은
② 얻다 / 효율적으로 / 있을 법하지 않은
③ 잃다 / 비효율적으로 / 있을 법한
④ 잃다 / 비효율적으로 / 있을 법하지 않은
⑤ 잃다 / 효율적으로 / 있을 법한

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절한 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>Limiting</u> the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to ⓑ<u>sell</u> Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the ⓒ<u>unrestricted</u> condition, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity ⓓ<u>raises</u> sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with ⓔ<u>fake</u> shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 판매 개수를 제한하는 것(Limiting)이 판매를 늘린다는 글의 핵심 주제이므로 적절합니다. ⓑ 할인된 가격에 판매(sell)하도록 설득한 것이므로 적절합니다. ⓒ 무제한 조건과 비교되는 것은 제한이 있는 조건이므로 restricted가 되어야 합니다. ⓓ 희소성이 판매를 높인다(raises)는 결론이므로 적절합니다. ⓔ 실험실이 아닌 실제 마트에서 진짜 쇼핑객을 대상으로 했으므로 real이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy nine countries, finding that those who took grater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: 操作② Double Your Income by Changing Your Job
③ The Importance of Having Satisfying Career
④ How to Find Satisfaction in Your Own Business
⑤ Increasing Work Efficiency by Comfortable Atmosphere
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 직업과 그에 대한 만족감이 삶의 행복, 에너지, 그리고 업무 성과 및 소득에 긍정적인 영향을 미친다는 내용을 담고 있으므로 '만족스러운 직업을 갖는 것의 중요성'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 성공한 사업가들의 비밀
② 직업을 바꿈으로써 수입을 두 배로 늘리기
③ 만족스러운 직업을 갖는 것의 중요성
④ 자신의 사업에서 만족을 찾는 방법
⑤ 쾌적한 분위기로 업무 효율 높이기

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Sometimes the pace of change is far slower. The face you saw reflected in your mirror this morning probably appeared no different from the face you saw the day before - or a week or a month ago. Yet we know that the face that stares back at us from the glass is not the same, cannot be the same, as it was 10 minutes ago. The proof is in your photo album: Look at a photograph taken of yourself 5 or 10 years ago and you see clear differences between the face in the snapshot and the face in your mirror. If you lived in a world without mirrors for a year and then saw your reflection, you might be surprised by the change. After an interval of 10 years without seeing yourself, you might not at first recognize the person peering from the mirror. Even something as basic as our own face _____________________________________.
options: ① needs our attention and care
② seems to be different from others'
③ does not stay the same every moment
④ has to be recorded through photographs
⑤ resists changes caused by the flow of time
questions.explanation: 매일 보는 거울 속 얼굴은 변하지 않는 것처럼 보이지만, 사진이나 오랜 시간 뒤의 모습을 통해 얼굴이 계속해서 조금씩 변하고 있음을 알 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 얼굴이 매 순간 똑같은 상태로 머물지 않는다는 내용인 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 관심과 보살핌을 필요로 한다
② 타인의 것과 달라 보인다
③ 매 순간 똑같은 상태로 머물지 않는다
④ 사진을 통해 기록되어야 한다
⑤ 시간의 흐름에 따른 변화에 저항한다

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adjusting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped increase sales. This example of Fleischmann's yeast made it clear that _____________________________ worked.
options: ② getting help from a press agency
③ taking yeast as a source of vitamins
④ reflecting bakers' demand on products
⑤ adopting an adaptive marketing strategy
questions.explanation: Fleischmann의 효모 사례를 통해, 시장 상황의 변화에 따라 제품의 용도를 비타민 공급원이나 천연 완하제로 재설정(repositioning)하여 판매를 늘린 과정을 설명합니다. 이는 시장 상황에 맞춘 유연한 마케팅 전략이 효과적이었음을 보여주므로 ⑤번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 경제적 혜택에 집중하는 것
② 언론사로부터 도움을 받는 것
③ 효모를 비타민 공급원으로 취급하는 것
④ 제빵사의 요구를 제품에 반영하는 것
⑤ 적응형 마케팅 전략을 채택하는 것

questions.question: 15. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. (A)___________________________________________. It is named after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%
options: ① difficulty of getting out of prejudiced ideas
② importance of being a socially reliable person
③ our common belief that we are inferior to others
④ reason why we always desire to be more intelligent
⑤ tendency to overestimate our own socially positive qualities
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 자신의 사하저ᄀ으로 바람지ᄀ하나 경향을 가지고 이다고 과대평가하는 경향에 대해 사라고 있으므로 ⑤번이 가장 저ᄀ자ᄅ하다.

② 사하저ᄀ으로 신래할 새 있는 사람이 댸는 갸스의 중요상

questions.question: 17. 다음 글 (가)를 읽고, 이에 대한 Tom과 Jane의 대화 (나)를 완성하시오. [23년 6월 41-42번]
questions.passage: (가) Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were seldom sufficient to support a full-time chief or village council. The development of agriculture changed work patterns. Early farmers could reap 3-10kg of grain from each 1kg of seed planted. Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided support for nonfarmers such as chieftains, village councils, men who practice medicine, priests, and warriors. In return, the nonfarmers provided leadership and security for the farming population, enabling it to continue to increase food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses. With improved technology and favorable conditions, agriculture produced consistent surpluses of the basic necessities, and population groups grew in size. These groups concentrated in towns and cities, and human tasks specialized further. Specialists such as carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their skills and became more efficient in their use of time and energy. The goods and services they provided brought about an improved quality of life, a higher standard of living, and, for most societies, increased stability.(나)Tom: Did you know that agriculture has changed our society?Jane: Really? How?Tom: In the hunter-gatherer societies of the past, most leaders had to hunt and gather with other members.Jane: I heard that it was because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were not (A)____________.Tom: Right. Then there was the development of agriculture which (B)____________ the surpluses of food and resources. In this condition, the people who were not farmers could be supported. Jane: I see. I think that flow of development continued and people with (C)____________ jobs provided goods and services. As a result, the quality of life and stability have improved.
subjective_conditions: 빈칸 하나에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
본문에서 찾아 쓰되, 필요시 형태를 변형할 것
questions.explanation: (A) 본문 첫 번째 단락에서 수렵 채집 사회는 식량 잉여분이 전업 추장을 부양하기에 충분하지 않았다(seldom sufficient)고 했으므로, Jane의 대화에서 'not' 뒤에는 'sufficient'가 적절합니다. (B) 농업의 발달로 인해 식량/에너지 수확량이 계속해서 늘어났다(continue to increase)는 내용을 바탕으로, 잉여분을 늘린 주체가 농업의 발달이므로 과거형 동사 'increased'를 사용합니다.(C) 두 번째 단락에서 인구 집단이 커지며 인간의 과업이 더욱 전문화되었다(specialized further)고 언급되었고, 목수나 대장장이 같은 전문가(Specialists)들이 언급되므로 'specialized'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 아래 표와 같이 정리하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(E)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure for more time in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
subjective_conditions: 빈칸 하나에 두 단어 이내로 작성할 것
본문에서 찾아 쓰되, 필요시 형태를 변형할 것
questions.subjective_answer_format: TitleHow Parental Praise Has a Strong Effect on a child's positive (A)_____________Step 1Praise from parents is integrated into a preschooler's (B)_____________.↓Step 2It enhances his good characteristics.↓Examplemaking him- (C)_____________ longer in effort to find solutions to a problem- be more (D)_____________ facing unfamiliar and hard tasks- and (E)_____________ more to help with duties at home and at preschool
questions.explanation: 본문의 내용을 표로 요약하는 문제입니다. (A) 부모의 칭찬이 아이의 자존감(self-esteem)에 영향을 미친다는 제목이 적절합니다. (B) 부모의 칭찬은 아이의 자아상(self-image)으로 통합됩니다. (C) 스마트하다는 칭찬을 받은 아이는 문제 해결에 더 오래 견디고(endure) 노력합니다. (D) 칭찬은 새로운 과제에 직면할 때 더 자신감을 갖게(confident) 만듭니다. 본문의 confidence를 형용사형인 confident로 변형합니다. (E) 돕는 아이라는 칭찬은 집이나 유치원에서 기꺼이 돕게(volunteer) 만듭니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. <조건>에 맞게 요약문의 빈칸을 완성하시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.summary_sentence: In contrast to the former explanation that taste buds are grouped in (A)___________ ___________ according to specialty, current leading taste researchers think that how we taste depends on (B)___________ rather than (C)___________ of registering the taste.
subjective_conditions: 빈칸 하나에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
본문에서 찾아 쓰되, 형태를 변형하지 말 것
questions.explanation: 본문은 과거 혀의 특정 부위(separate areas)에서 맛이 느껴진다는 '혀 지도' 이론이 잘못되었음을 설명하며, 오늘날 연구자들은 맛의 인지가 부위(place)가 아닌 시간(time)의 문제라고 생각한다는 점을 강조합니다. (A)에는 첫 문장의 'separate areas', (B)와 (C)에는 마지막 문장의 핵심 대조어인 'time'과 'place'를 각각 배치합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 production would create its own demand가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that <u>production would create its own demand</u>. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ① all the manufactured goods are to be inherently consumed
② the process of sales must be affected by customers' needs
③ price does not matter if the quality of products is ensured
④ simplification is the best way to make the brand appealing
⑤ practicality should be the only standard of product evaluation
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 '생산이 그 자체의 수요를 창출할 것이다'라는 의미로, 과거 산업 사회에서 물건을 만들기만 하면 무조건 팔린다는 공급자 중심의 사고방식을 의미합니다. 따라서 가장 적절한 의미는 모든 제조된 상품은 본질적으로 소비되기 마련이다라는 1번입니다.
options_translation: 모든 제조된 상품은 본질적으로 소비되게 되어 있다
판매 과정은 고객의 요구에 영향을 받아야 한다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어휘의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
