Village dwellers also learned to work ⓓ<u>separately</u> to do a task faster. For example, toolmakers could ⓔ<u>share</u> the work of making stone axes and knives. In this way, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
questions.explanation: 마을 거주자들이 일을 더 빨리 하기 위해 협력하여 일하는 법을 배웠다는 문맥이므로 '따로따로(separately)'가 아니라 '함께(together)'가 적절하다. 뒤에 이어지는 예시에서도 도구 제작자들이 작업을 '공유(share)'한다고 언급되어 있다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것 2개를 찾아 기호, 바르게 고친 표현을 모두 쓰시오. (답안지에 아래와 같은 형식으로 쓰시오.) [4.0점]
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its ⓐ<u>expense</u>. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs ⓑ<u>removed</u>. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs ⓒ<u>prevent</u> physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The ⓓ<u>separation</u> of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health ⓔ<u>benefit</u> - for body and mind.
questions.explanation: 기술 도입으로 인해 인간이 겪는 고통과 부정적인 측면을 설명하는 글입니다. ⓒ가 포함된 문장은 기술과 관련된 직업이 신체적 고통이나 질병을 '유발한다(cause)'는 의미가 되어야 흐름상 자연스러우며, ⓔ가 포함된 문장은 고소득 직종의 주로 앉아서 하는 특성이 건강에 '위험(risk)'이 된다는 내용이어야 문맥에 맞습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed _______________________.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 동물 캐릭터가 인간을 닮도록 변형된다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장은 아이들과 어른들에게 정서적으로 더 호소력이 있게 만들기 위한 전략을 설명하고 있는데, 일반적으로 캐릭터가 정서적 호소력을 갖기 위해 '어린아이 같은 특징(childlike features, 예를 들어 큰 눈이나 머리 등)'을 부여하는 것이 보편적인 전략입니다.
options_translation: ① 동물 같은 얼굴
② 독특한 캐릭터
③ 손짓
④ 어린아이 같은 특징
⑤ 눈에 띄는 특성

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that _______________________ not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
options: ⑤ lengthy descriptions of a lecture
questions.explanation: 강사에 대해 '따낻한' 또는 '차가운' 사전 정밴림 제갑받았을 때, 괴 기대치에 따라 강사에 대한 인상감 달라지고 후속 행동(상호작용)까지 달라졀다는 실험 결과림 보여줍니다. 따라서 '서로 달랼 기대(different expectations)'가 인상 형성감 행동에 영향을 미친다는 내용이 빈칸에 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 흔한 실수
② 서로 달랼 기대
③ 사회적 상호작용 기술
④ 편견 없는 토론
⑤ 강의에 대한 긴 설명

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire ____________________________________ became the focus of business.
options: ② to produce high profitable items
③ to maintain their marketing strategies
④ to make simple and uniform products
⑤ to satisfy their varied and complicated require
questions.explanation: 과거에는 생산이 수요림 창출한다는 관점이었으나, 협대 사회로 오면서 고객이 지짜로 원하는 것을 제갑하는 것이 중요해졌다는 내용입니다. 따라서 고객감 괴들의 '다양하고 박잡한 요구림 충점시키고자 하는 욕구(to satisfy their varied and complicated require)'가 비즈니스의 중심이 되었다는 내용이 오아야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 호화스러운 윐차림 제조하기 위해
② 고수익 품목을 생산하기 위해
③ 괴들의 마케팅 전략을 유지하기 위해
④ 단순하고 균일한 제품을 만들기 위해
⑤ 괴들의 다양하고 박잡한 요구림 충점시키기 위해

questions.question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, ____________________________________ for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to adopt the practices of those around you.
options: ① doing what you want is safe
② searching for the safe place is positive
③ coming up with new ideas is appropriate
④ ignoring other people's opinions is desirable
⑤ doing as most people do is likely to be safe and secure
questions.explanation: 사람들은 사회적 증거(social evidence)를 통해 무엇이 안전한지 결정하며, 다른 사람들이 하는 대로 따르는 것이 생존에 유리하다는 진화론적 관점을 설명하고 있습니다. 줄을 선 식당의 예를 통해 다수를 따르는 것이 안전하다는 논지를 뒷받침합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 원하는 것을 하는 것이 안전하다
② 안전한 장소를 찾는 것은 긍정적이다
③ 새로운 아이디어를 생각해내는 것이 적절하다
④ 다른 사람들의 의견을 무시하는 것이 바람직하다
⑤ 대부분의 사람들이 하는 대로 하는 것이 안전하고 확실할 가능성이 높다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. ⓐRailways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. ⓑWith the railways came many large hotels. ⓒFollowing some decline due to competition from cars and airplanes, rail transport has had a revival in recent decades. ⓓIn Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. ⓔLater, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사회 경제적 발달과 운송 수단의 발달(특히 철도)이 관광 산업의 성장과 호텔 건설 등으로 이어진 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. ⓒ번은 자동차와 비행기와의 경쟁으로 인한 철도 운송의 쇠퇴와 최근의 부활을 언급하고 있어, 관광 산업의 성장을 설명하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. (A) They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. (B) The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." (C) If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, in which case only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster. (D) Then only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. (E) Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
questions.insertion_sentence: Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '붉은 여왕 효과'를 진화론적 원리 설명에 사용한다는 내용입니다. (B)까지는 루이스 캐럴의 소설 속 '붉은 여왕'의 일화를 설명하고 있으며, (C)부터는 실제 생물(여우와 토끼)의 진화 사례를 다루기 시작하므로, 일반적 일화에서 과학적 원리로 전환되는 지점인 (C)가 가장 적절한 삽입 위치입니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것 3개를 찾아 기호, 바르게 고친 표현을 모두 쓰시오. (답안지에 아래와 같은 형식으로 쓰시오.)
questions.passage: People differ in how ⓐ<u>quick</u> they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and ⓑ<u>prolong</u> your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough ⓒ<u>having</u> an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward ⓓ<u>perform</u> significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence ⓔ<u>which</u> eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'how'가 수식하는 형용사/부사는 뒤의 문장에서의 역할에 따라 결정되는데, 여기서는 동사 'reset'을 수식해야 하므로 부사 'quickly'가 적절합니다. ⓒ '형용사 + enough + to-부정사' 구문이므로 'enough to have'로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓔ 'evidence' 뒤에서 완전한 문장을 이끌며 동격의 의미를 나타내야 하므로 관계대명사 'which'를 접속사 'that'으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 25. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Chess masters shown a chess board in the middle of a game for 5 seconds with 20 to 30 pieces still in play can immediately reproduce the position of the pieces from memory.
ordered_passages: (A) The beneficial effects of familiar structure on memory have been observed for many types of expertise, including music. People with musical training can reproduce short sequences of musical notation more accurately than those with no musical training when notes follow usual sequences, but the advantage is much reduced when the notes are ordered randomly.

(B) Expertise also improves memory for sequences of movements. Experienced ballet dancers are able to repeat longer sequences of steps than less experienced dancers, and they can repeat a sequence of steps making up a routine better than steps ordered randomly. In each case, memory range is increased by the ability to recognize familiar sequences and patterns.

(C) Beginners, of course, are able to place only a few. Now take the same pieces and place them on the board randomly and the difference is much reduced. The expert's advantage is only for familiar patterns - those previously stored in memory. Faced with unfamiliar patterns, even when it involves the same familiar domain, the expert's advantage disappears.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 체스 고수들이 게임 중인 체스판을 보고 기억해낸다는 내용입니다. (C)는 이에 대비되는 초보자의 경우를 언급하며, 무작위 배치 시 전문가의 이점이 사라진다는 체스 사례의 결론을 맺습니다. (A)는 이러한 익숙한 구조의 효과가 음악 등 다른 분야에서도 관찰된다는 내용으로 확장을 시작하며, (B)는 '또한(also)'을 사용하여 무용 동작 등의 연속 동작으로 사례를 추가 확장한 뒤 익숙한 패턴 인식의 중요성으로 전체 내용을 요약합니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글에 관한 내용으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Chess masters shown a chess board in the middle of a game for 5 seconds with 20 to 30 pieces still in play can immediately reproduce the position of the pieces from memory.(A) The beneficial effects of familiar structure on memory have been observed for many types of expertise, including music. People with musical training can reproduce short sequences of musical notation more accurately than those with no musical training when notes follow usual sequences, but the advantage is much reduced when the notes are ordered randomly.(B) Expertise also improves memory for sequences of movements. Experienced ballet dancers are able to repeat longer sequences of steps than less experienced dancers, and they can repeat a sequence of steps making up a routine better than steps ordered randomly. In each case, memory range is increased by the ability to recognize familiar sequences and patterns.(C) Beginners, of course, are able to place only a few. Now take the same pieces and place them on the board randomly and the difference is much reduced. The expert's advantage is only for familiar patterns - those previously stored in memory. Faced with unfamiliar patterns, even when it involves the same familiar domain, the expert's advantage disappears.
options: ① 체스의 달인은 말들의 익숙한 패턴을 본 후 바로 재현할 수 있다.
② 음악 전문가는 음표가 특이한 순서를 따를 때도 정확하게 재현한다.
③ 전문지식은 연속 동작에 대한 기억을 향상시킨다.
④ 숙련된 무용수는 초보보다 긴 연속스텝 반복이 가능하다.
⑤ 무작위로 놓인 체스판의 말에 대한 기억은 전문가와 초보의 차이가 줄어든다.
questions.explanation: 지문 (A)에서 음악 훈련을 받은 사람들도 음표가 무작위로 배열될 때(when the notes are ordered randomly)는 그 이점이 크게 줄어든다(advantage is much reduced)고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 '특이한 순서(무작위 순서)일 때도 정확하게 재현한다'는 설명은 틀렸습니다.
options_translation: ① 체스의 달인은 말들의 익숙한 패턴을 본 후 바로 재현할 수 있다.
② 음악 전문가는 음표가 특이한 순서를 따를 때도 정확하게 재현한다.
③ 전문지식은 연속 동작에 대한 기억을 향상시킨다.
④ 숙련된 무용수는 초보보다 긴 연속스텝 반복이 가능하다.
⑤ 무작위로 놓인 체스판의 말에 대한 기억은 전문가와 초보의 차이가 줄어든다.

questions.question: 27. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started.
ordered_passages: (A) Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
(B) Likewise, the human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be.

(C) The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 모든 것이 시작되기 전 마음속에서 먼저 완성된다는 주제를 던집니다. (C)는 집, 자동차, 옷 등의 구체적인 예시를 들어 이 주제를 뒷받침합니다. (B)는 '마찬가지로(Likewise)'를 사용하여 물리적 대상에서 인간의 미래라는 추상적 대상으로 논의를 전환하며 같은 프로세스를 적용합니다. (A)는 (B)에서 언급한 미래에 대한 아이디어를 다듬고 실현하는 구체적인 과정을 설명하며 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오. (답안지에 반드시 (A), (B)를 쓰고 답을 작성할 것)
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are (A)____________ sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are (B)___________ to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather rapidly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
subjective_conditions: 답안지에 반드시 (A), (B)를 쓰고 답을 작성할 것
각각 한 단어로 쓰시오
questions.explanation: 복합 탄수화물(complex)과 대조되는 '나쁜' 탄수화물의 특징을 설명하는 글입니다. 복합 탄수화물과 반대되는 나쁜 탄수화물은 구조가 단순한(simple) 당이고, 구조가 복합적이지 않아 분해하기 쉽습니다(easy).

questions.question: [11~12] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.11. 윗글 (A), (B)의 공통된 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) It is difficult for any of us to maintain a constant level of attention throughout our working day. We all have body rhythms characterised by peaks and valleys of energy and alertness. You will achieve more, and feel confident as a benefit, if you schedule your most demanding tasks at times ⓐ<u>when</u> you are best able to cope with them. If you haven't thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to observe yourself. Try to note when you are at your best. We are all different. For some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for others it may take a while to warm up.(B) If you want the confidence that comes from achieving ⓑ<u>which</u> you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience ⓒ<u>when</u> tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks ⓓ<u>which</u> you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time ⓔ<u>that</u> you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
options: ① what can make you feel proud
② factors that lead to different results
③ combination of what to do and how to do it
④ how to differentiate body rhythms from time
⑤ effective ways to achieve plans and become confident
questions.explanation: 글 (A)는 자신의 에너지 정점 시간대에 가장 힘든 업무를 배치함으로써 더 많은 성취를 이루고 자신감을 얻을 수 있다는 내용이며, 글 (B)는 업무 소요 시간을 정확히 파악하고 가용 시간에 맞춰 계획을 세움으로써 성취와 자신감을 얻는 방법에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 두 글의 공통 주제는 계획을 달성하고 자신감을 얻는 효과적인 방법입니다.
options_translation: ① 당신을 자랑스럽게 만들 수 있는 것
② 다른 결과로 이어지는 요인들
③ 무엇을 할지와 어떻게 할지의 조합
④ 신체 리듬을 시간과 구별하는 방법
⑤ 계획을 성취하고 자신감을 얻는 효과적인 방법

questions.question: [11~12] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.12. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) It is difficult for any of us to maintain a constant level of attention throughout our working day. We all have body rhythms characterised by peaks and valleys of energy and alertness. You will achieve more, and feel confident as a benefit, if you schedule your most demanding tasks at times ⓐ<u>when</u> you are best able to cope with them. If you haven't thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to observe yourself. Try to note when you are at your best. We are all different. For some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for others it may take a while to warm up.(B) If you want the confidence that comes from achieving ⓑ<u>which</u> you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience ⓒ<u>when</u> tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks ⓓ<u>which</u> you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time ⓔ<u>that</u> you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 achieve의 목적어 역할을 하면서 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사가 필요하므로 which가 아닌 what이 되어야 적절합니다. set out to do의 목적어가 비어 있는 불완전한 문장이기 때문입니다. ⓐ는 선행사 times를 수식하는 관계부사 when으로 적절하며, ⓒ는 learn의 목적어 절을 이끄는 접속사, ⓓ와 ⓔ는 각각 tasks와 time을 수식하는 목적격 관계대명사입니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whose story it is affects what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, ________________________________. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
options: ① the ending becomes more predictable
② the setting of the story becomes more vivid
③ it is not strange to expect something diverse
④ they will be praying for a consistent outcome
⑤ the supporting characters gain more importance
questions.explanation: 누구의 이야기냐에 따라 이야기의 초점이 달라지고 해석이 달라진다는 글의 내용상, 화자가 바뀌면 이야기의 핵심 갈등 상황에서 '다양한 결과를 기대하는 것이 이상하지 않다'는 ③번이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다. 원래 지문의 'we will be praying for a different outcome'이 변형된 형태입니다.
options_translation: ① 결말이 더 예측 가능해진다
② 이야기의 설정이 더 생생해진다
③ 무언가 다양한 것을 기대하는 것이 이상하지 않다
④ 그들은 일관된 결과를 위해 기도할 것이다
⑤ 조연들이 더 중요해진다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Lilian Bland was born in Kent, England in 1878. Unlike most other girls at the time she wore trousers and spent her time ⓐ<u>enjoying</u> adventurous activities like horse riding and hunting. Lilian began her career as a sports and wildlife photographer for British newspapers. In 1910 she became the first woman to design, ⓑ<u>build</u>, and fly her own airplane. In order to persuade her to try a slightly safer activity, Lilian's dad bought her a car. Soon Lilian was a master driver and ended up ⓒ<u>working</u> as a car dealer. She never went back to ⓓ<u>fly</u> but ⓔ<u>lived</u> a long and exciting life nonetheless. She married, moved to Canada, and had a kid. Eventually, she moved back to England, and lived there for the rest of her life.
questions.explanation: ⓓ go back to에서의 to는 방향을 나타내는 전치사이므로 뒤에 동사원형이 아닌 명사나 동명사가 와야 합니다. 따라서 fly를 flying으로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk ─ for body and mind.
options: ① 전통적인 직업들은 기술 발전으로 인해 사라졌다.
② 사람들은 기술의 도입으로 더 나은 삶을 살 수 있다.
③ 대중 교육과 미디어는 사람들을 디지털 세계로 유도하고 있다.
④ 최고의 임금을 받는 직업은 몸과 마음에 건강 위험이 있다.
⑤ 수많은 사람이 기술과 관련된 위험하고 새로운 직장에서 일하고 있다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기술 도입에 따른 대가(비용)와 부정적인 영향(일자리 상실, 건강 문제, 스트레스 등)을 주로 다루고 있습니다. 기술 도입으로 인해 더 나은 삶을 살 수 있다는 내용은 본문의 논조와 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "putting on the same clothes" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
questions.summary_sentence: Effective learners adapt their strategies based on the specific requirements of different tasks and situations, understanding that _______________________.
options: ① one strategy fits all situations
② tasks don't vary in their demands
④ every task has the same requirements
⑤ one approach does not work for everything
questions.explanation: 본문은 상황에 맞지 않는 옷을 입는 비유를 통해, 모든 학습 상황에 동일한 방식을 적용하는 '고무인형 방식(rubber-stamp approach)'이 비효율적임을 지적합니다. 숙련된 학습자는 상황에 따라 전략을 유연하게 바꾼다는 내용이므로, 요약문의 빈칸에는 '한 가지 접근법이 모든 상황에 통하지 않는다'는 의미의 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 한 가지 전략이 모든 상황에 적합하다
② 과업들의 요구 사항이 다르지 않다
③ 구체적인 전략은 필요하지 않다
④ 모든 과업은 동일한 요구 사항을 가진다
⑤ 하나의 접근법이 모든 상황에 효과가 있는 것은 아니다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions (A)[improved / developed]. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, (B)[however / for example], the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to (C)[industrial / tourism] growth.
questions.explanation: (A) 경제 상황이 좋아지면서 임금 수준과 근로 조건이 '개선되었다(improved)'는 흐름이 적절합니다. (B) 영국 철도 사례에 이어 캐나다의 철도 사례를 들고 있으므로 '예를 들어(for example)'가 적절합니다. (C) 운송 수단의 발달과 철도, 호텔 건립 등은 모두 '관광(tourism)' 성장을 이끌었다는 맥락입니다.
options_translation: ① 개선된 / 예를 들어 / 관광
② 개선된 / 하지만 / 관광
③ 개선된 / 예를 들어 / 산업의

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 직장인들이 ⓐ처럼 느끼는 이유는 무엇인가?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, ⓐ<u>you're stuck</u>. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying ─ but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
options: ① Due to the lack of time off
② Due to the lack of financial rewards
③ Because they enjoy their work too much
④ Because they are not good at what they do
⑤ Because of the poor employment market and dissatisfaction
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장에서 많은 직장인이 '열악한 고용 시장(poor employment market)' 때문에 '보수가 좋을지라도 궁극적으로 만족스럽지 못한(unsatisfying)' 일자리에 갇혀 있다고 느끼게 된다고 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 휴식 시간의 부족 때문에
② 금전적 보상의 부족 때문에
③ 그들의 일을 너무 즐기기 때문에
④ 그들이 하는 일을 잘하지 못하기 때문에
⑤ 열악한 고용 시장과 불만족 때문에

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. ⓐMany people believe that animals have their own unique ways of communicating that humans just haven't understood yet. ⓑPhysically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. ⓒThis is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. ⓓIn more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. ⓔHowever, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 특징(언어, 신체 구조)이 동물 캐릭터나 장난감에 투영되는 방식에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓐ번 문장은 동물이 인간이 이해하지 못한 독자적인 의사소통 방식을 가지고 있다는 내용으로, '인간화된 특징의 투영'이라는 글의 주제에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s.
ordered_passages: (A) In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible.

(B) The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
(C) This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 산업 사회가 풍요로워지고 경쟁이 치열해지며 판매 개념의 철학적 변화가 일어났다는 내용 다음에, 이러한 사회적 변화가 기업이 고객과 가까운 관계를 맺게 만들어 가격과 품질만으로는 부족하다는 것을 깨닫게 하는 (C)가 오고, 고객이 원하는 제품을 제공하는 것이 중요해졌다는 (A), 그러한 현대화가 마케팅 혁명으로 이어져 고객 중심의 경영이 되었다는 (B)가 오는 순서가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 위 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s.(A) In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible.(B) The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.(C) This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price.
options: ② Henry Ford's Influence on Modern Marketing
③ The Importance of Producing Quality Products
④ The Shift in Selling: From Production to Customer Focus
⑤ The Affluence and Competitiveness of the 1940s and 1950s
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거의 생산 중심적인 판매 개념이 현대 사회에서 고객 니즈 충족 중심으로 변화해가는 과정을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 ④번 '판매의 변화: 생산 중심에서 고객 중심으로'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 산업 생산의 진화
② 현대 마케팅에 미친 헨리 포드의 영향력
③ 고품질 제품 생산의 중요성
④ 판매의 변화: 생산 중심에서 고객 중심으로
⑤ 1940년대와 1950년대의 풍요로움과 경쟁성

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel. *jet lag: 시차로 인한 피로감
options: ① 여행의 방향은 생물학적 시계의 회복 속도에 연관이 없다.
② 서쪽으로 여행하는 것은 동쪽으로 여행하는 것보다 생물학적 시계를 재설정하는 데 더 쉽다.
③ 여행의 방향과 피로도는 스포츠 팀의 경기 성적에 어떠한 영향도 미치지 않는다.
④ 프로 야구와 대학 미식축구 팀 중 서쪽으로 여행하는 팀은 동쪽으로 여행하는 팀보다 경기 성적이 나쁘다.
⑤ 연구에서 동쪽과 서쪽 여행은 방향과 상관없이 동일한 영향을 미친다고 밝혀졌다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 "Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it."라고 언급되는데, 이는 서쪽으로 여행하는 것이 동쪽으로 여행하는 것보다 시차 적응을 해소하고 생물학적 시계를 재설정하는 것이 더 쉽다는 뜻입니다. 따라서 ②번이 내용과 일치합니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. (A) Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. (B) So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. (C) Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. (D) There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. (E) So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.*gear up: 준비를 갖추다, 대비하다
questions.insertion_sentence: There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '상당한 시간이 있어야 시작할 수 있는 과업들이 있다'는 내용입니다. (D) 뒤의 문장에서 '그런 과업(such a task)'을 준비하는 것은 시간이 짧을 때 의미가 없다고 설명하고 있으므로, 'such a task'가 지칭하는 대상이 포함된 주어진 문장은 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. (A) Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. (B) So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. (C) Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. (D) There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. (E) So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.*gear up: 준비를 갖추다, 대비하다
options: ① history of clocks and time measurement
② the benefits of overestimating time for tasks
③ the importance of having a colorful 'things to do' list

options_translation: ① 시계와 시간 측정의 역사

④ 달리기와 시간 관리 사이의 관계
⑤ 일상생활에서 과업을 계획하고 조직하기 위한 시간 관리 전략

questions.question: 28. 다음 글을 읽고 Red Queen Effect를 설명하기 위해 아래 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 각각 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster ─ in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.*thrive: 번성하다
questions.summary_sentence: The Red Queen Effect is the evolutionary principle where (A)__________ must continuously (B)__________ to maintain their relative position in competition, resembling a race where participants run fast but (C)__________ the position.
questions.answer: (A) species(B) evolve(C) keep in / stay in / keep / stay
questions.explanation: 본문에 따르면 여우와 토끼라는 두 종(species)이 서로 경쟁하며 진화(evolve)하지만 결과적으로는 제자리(stay in place/keep in the same place)에 머물게 된다는 원리입니다.(A)는 경쟁하는 생명체인 'species'가 적합합니다.(B)는 상대적 위치를 유지하기 위해 계속 수행해야 하는 과정인 'evolve'가 적합합니다.(C)는 빨리 달려도 결국 위치를 '유지한다'는 의미이므로 'keep (in)' 혹은 'stay (in)' 등이 적합합니다.

questions.question: 29. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 34번]
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was ⓐ<u>visualized</u> in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly ⓑ<u>removed</u> the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the ⓒ<u>identical</u> process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we ⓓ<u>fine-tune</u> and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have ⓔ<u>conceptually</u> concluded about the future.
options: ① cars, houses, and clothing are examples of physical creations
② everyone has a different approach to creating and refining ideas
③ ideas and thoughts play an important role in shaping our daily decisions
④ the significance of establishing ideas and thoughts before materializing them
⑤ people often rush into turning their ideas into physical products
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심 내용은 세상의 모든 물리적 창조물(집, 자동차 등)뿐만 아니라 인간의 미래 설계 또한 실제 결과물로 나타나기 전에 마음속에서 먼저 구상되고, 정교화되는 과정을 거친다는 것입니다. 따라서 실현하기 전에 아이디어와 생각을 정립하는 것의 중요성이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자동차, 집, 그리고 옷은 물리적 창조물의 예시이다
② 모든 사람은 아이디어를 창조하고 개선하는 데 서로 다른 접근 방식을 가진다
③ 아이디어와 생각은 우리의 매일의 결정을 형성하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다
④ 아이디어를 구체화하기 전에 그것들을 확립하는 것의 중요성
⑤ 사람들은 종종 그들의 아이디어를 물리적 제품으로 바꾸기 위해 서두른다

questions.question: 30. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [23년 3월 34번]

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
options: ① the significance of providing specialized training to novices
② the role of novice in guiding and instructing new learners
③ practical applications of the recently introduced learning theory
④ the necessity for an expert to understand from a student's viewpoint in the learning process
⑤ development of a variety of examinations to test students' understanding
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전문가가 초밴자에게 새로운 분야림 설먕할 때 '지식의 저주'로 인해 초밴자가 느끼는 어려움을 과소평가하는 경향이 있음을 설먕합니다. 따라서 학습 과정을 학생의 관점에서 바라볼 필요성을 강하고 있으므로 정눵은 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 초밴자에게 특화된 훈련을 제공하는 것의 중요성

④ 학습 과정에서 전문가가 학생의 관점에서 이해해야 할 필요성

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth.
ordered_passages: (A) Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.

(B) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites.

(C) Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 혀의 부위별로 맛이 정해져 있다는 과거의 '맛 지도'에 대한 설명입니다. (C)에서 하지만(however) 1980~90년대 연구를 통해 이 지도가 독일 연구의 오역에서 비롯된 잘못된 것임을 밝히며 내용을 반박합니다. (B) 이어서 오늘날(Today) 연구자들은 모든 맛을 혀의 모든 부위에서 느낄 수 있다고 본다는 최신 견해를 제시합니다. (A) 마지막으로 게다가(Moreover) 맛을 지각하는 핵심 기제는 장소(place)가 아니라 시간(time)이라는 점을 덧붙이며 마무리하는 (C)-(B)-(A) 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.*barnacle: 따개비 **dispersal: 분산 ***fossil: 화석
options: ① 생물의 다양성을 확보하기 위해서 모든 동력을 친환경 에너지에서 얻어야 한다.
② 기후 변화가 너무 빠르게 진행되고 있어서 몇몇 종은 새로운 환경에 적응하지 못하고 있다.
③ 모든 종은 기후 변화에 적응하고 생존하기 위해 서식지를 옮기는 적응 능력을 지니고 있다.
④ 기후 변화가 생물의 다양성에 어떤 영향을 주는가에 대한 과학적인 연구 사례를 모아야 한다.
⑤ 기후 변화를 막기 위해 통제와 규제의 범위를 확장하고, 새로운 에너지원을 계속 찾아야 한다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 모든 생물 종이 기후 변화에 따라 생존 가능한 장소로 이동해야 하며, 움직이지 않는 것처럼 보이는 나무나 따개비조차도 생애의 어느 단계에서 분산(이동)할 능력을 갖추고 있음을 강조합니다. 화석을 통해 과거에도 생물들이 기후 변화에 맞춰 빠르게 이동했음을 알 수 있다는 내용으로 보아, 모든 종이 생존을 위해 서식지를 옮기는 능력이 있다는 것이 핵심입니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.*excel: 탁월하다 **messenger: 전령
options: ① to introduce the Inca Empire's way of delivering messages
② to describe the unique lifestyle of the Inca people
③ to explain the progress of message delivery methods
④ to promote tourism to the historic sites of the Inca Empire
⑤ to explain the difference between the Inca Empire and other empires
questions.explanation: 이 글은 말이 없던 인카 제국에서 'Chasquis'라고 불리는 전령들이 왕의 명령과 보고를 전달하기 위해 구축한 효율적인 보행 전달 체계(릴레이 방식)를 상세히 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 글의 목적은 인카 제국의 메시지 전달 방식을 소개하는 것입니다.
options_translation: ① 인카 제국의 메시지 전달 방식을 소개하기 위해
② 인카 사람들의 독특한 생활 방식을 묘사하기 위해
③ 메시지 전달 방식의 발전을 설명하기 위해
④ 인카 제국의 역사 유적지 관광을 홍보하기 위해
⑤ 인카 제국과 다른 제국들의 차이점을 설명하기 위해

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross - cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
options: ① Ignore cultural diversity to build a harmonious society.
② Be aware of your surroundings to avoid accidents in your daily life.
③ You should be considerate of others around you in your daily life.
④ You should thank people for their help, no matter how small it is.
⑤ Be aware of the norms of other cultures to have effective cross-cultural communication.
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부에서 'Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication'이라고 명시하며, 타문화의 규범을 알지 못하는 것이 문화 간 소통의 핵심적인 문제라고 지적합니다. 따라서 효과적인 소통을 위해 다른 문화의 규범을 인지해야 한다는 ⑤번이 필자의 주장으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 조화로운 사회를 건설하기 위해 문화적 다양성을 무시하라.
② 일상 생활에서 사고를 피하기 위해 당신의 주변 환경을 인지하라.
③ 당신의 일상 생활에서 당신 주변의 타인을 배려해야 한다.
④ 아무리 작은 도움일지라도 사람들의 도움에 감사해야 한다.
⑤ 효과적인 타문화 간 의사소통을 위해 다른 문화의 규범을 인지하라.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
options: ① Five Senses Hard to Categorize
② The Number of Senses : It Depends
③ Various Interpretation of Five Senses
④ Don't Try to Find Out Meanings of Senses
⑤ Reasons to Doubt Aristotelian Definition of Senses
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 인간과 동물의 5감(시각, 청각, 후각, 미각, 촉각)에 대해 의문을 제기하며, 실제로는 평형 감각, 신체 위치 감각 등 인간에게도 더 많은 감각이 있고 동물들에게는 훨씬 더 다양하고 분류하기 힘든 감각 체계가 존재함을 설명합니다. 결국 감각의 개수는 단순히 5개로 정해진 것이 아니라 상황과 관점에 따라 달라질 수 있다는 내용이므로 2번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 분류하기 어려운 다섯 가지 감각
② 감각의 수 : 그것은 (상황에 따라) 달라진다
③ 오감에 대한 다양한 해석
④ 감각의 의미를 찾아내려 노력하지 마라
⑤ 아리스토텔레스의 감각 정의를 의심하는 이유

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① People considering their employment as joy and pride produce things they have love for.
② People's feeling contentment with their work brings about their happiness in life after all.
③ People fulfilled on the job generally earn more wages than those who are not satisfied with their work.
④ People love work that provides a sense of fulfillment and authority because they want to live in a comfortable rut.
⑤ Workplace studies show that when people are satisfied with their job, they feel relaxed in what may be a secure, or well-paying job.
questions.explanation: 의미 있는 일(성취감과 자율성을 주는 일)이 인간에게 얼마나 중요한지를 설명하는 글입니다. 일에서 깊은 의미와 만족감을 느끼는 사람들이 더 활기찬 하루를 보내며, 일에서의 만족도가 결국 삶 전체의 행복으로 이어진다는 연구 결과들을 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 일에서의 만족감이 전반적인 삶의 행복을 가져온다는 2번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자신의 고용을 기쁨과 자부심으로 여기는 사람들은 자신이 사랑하는 것들을 생산한다.
② 일에 대한 사람들의 만족감은 결국 그들의 삶의 행복을 초래한다.
③ 직장에서 성취감을 느끼는 사람들은 일반적으로 업무에 만족하지 못하는 사람들보다 더 많은 임금을 받는다.
④ 사람들은 편안한 틀 속에서 살고 싶어 하기 때문에 성취감과 권한을 주는 일을 사랑한다.
⑤ 직장 연구들은 사람들이 자신의 직업에 만족할 때, 안정적이거나 보수가 좋은 직업에서 편안함을 느낀다는 것을 보여준다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것의 개수를 고르면?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - <u>what</u> degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species <u>force</u> to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures <u>that</u> appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often <u>occupied</u> by its parent - to a place <u>which</u> it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees <u>moved</u> with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: 틀린 부분은 총 2개입니다.1. 'Species force to follow' 부분: 종들은 기후 변화에 따라 이동하도록 '강요받는' 것이므로 수동태인 'are forced'가 되어야 합니다.2. 'to a place which it can survive...' 부분: 뒤의 문장이 'it(주어) can survive, grow, and reproduce(자동사들)'로 완벽하므로, 관계대명사 which 대신 장소를 나타내는 관계부사 where 혹은 in which가 와야 합니다.- 'what'은 의문형용사로 뒤의 명사 degree를 수식하며 '어떤 정도'라는 의미로 적절합니다.- 'that'은 주격 관계대명사로 creatures를 선행사로 받아 적절합니다.- 'occupied'는 분사구문 혹은 수식어로 앞의 place를 수식하며 '차지된'이라는 수동의 의미가 적절합니다.- 'moved'는 과거 사실을 나타내는 본동사로 시제가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
options: ① various methods for teaching new fields
② experts' difficulties in teaching newcomers
③ the gap between estimated time and actual time in learning
④ importance of learning new skills in using digital devices
⑤ negative impacts of overestimating students' knowledge on teaching
questions.explanation: 이 글은 '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'라는 개념을 통해 전문가가 초보자에게 자신이 아는 분야를 가르칠 때 겪는 어려움을 설명하고 있습니다. 전문가들은 자신이 그 기술을 배우는 것이 얼마나 어려웠는지를 잊어버리는 경향이 있기 때문에 초보자의 입장에서 학습 과정을 바라볼 필요가 있다는 내용이므로 '신입을 가르칠 때 전문가들이 겪는 어려움'이 가장 적절한 주제입니다.
options_translation: ① 새로운 분야를 가르치기 위한 다양한 방법들
② 초보자를 가르칠 때 전문가들이 겪는 어려움
③ 학습에 있어 예상 시간과 실제 시간 사이의 격차
④ 디지털 기기 사용에 있어 새로운 기술 습득의 중요성
⑤ 가르칠 때 학생의 지식을 과대평가하는 것의 부정적 영향

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions were ⓐ<u>enhanced</u>. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport ⓑ<u>diminished</u> and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution ⓒ<u>resulted in</u> many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made ⓓ<u>available</u> the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism ⓔ<u>expansion</u>.
questions.explanation: 국가의 사회적, 경제적 상황이 개선되면서 임금 수준과 근로 조건이 나아졌고, 교통 수단 또한 발전하고 개선되었습니다. 본문에서 교통 수단이 더 빨라지고 저렴해졌다고 언급하고 있으므로, 교통 수단이 '줄어들었다(diminished)'는 표현은 문맥상 어색합니다. 이를 '개선되었다(improved)' 또는 '발전했다(developed)'와 같은 단어로 바꾸어야 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond ⓐ<u>abnormally</u> to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally ⓑ<u>sightless</u>. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and waking the individual becomes ⓒ<u>unsuccessful</u>. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems ⓓ<u>essential</u> to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep ⓔ<u>with</u> total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 졸음(drowsiness)은 깨어 있는 상태와 잠든 상태 사이의 중간 단계입니다. 이 상태에서는 수면의 혜택을 얻으면서도 지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)이 '완전하지 않은' 상태여야 합니다. 따라서 '완전한 지각적 이탈을 가지고(with)'가 아니라 '완전한 지각적 이탈 없이(without)'가 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. ⓐ<u>For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third</u>. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. ⓑ<u>By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order</u>. ⓒ<u>Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop</u>. ⓓ<u>However, growing the same crop in the same place for many years in a row, known as monocropping, gradually depletes the soil certain nutrients</u>. ⓔ<u>This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy</u>. Also, this practice reduces pest and weed pressure, along with the probability of developing resistant pests and weeds.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 윤작(Crop rotation)의 정의와 예시, 그리고 토양 건강 유지 및 해충 감소와 같은 장점에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ⓓ문장은 윤작과 반대되는 개념인 단일 경작(monocropping)의 단점(토양 영양분 고갈)을 설명하고 있어 전체적인 글의 흐름에서 벗어납니다. 또한 ⓔ문장의 'This type of farming'은 문맥상 윤작을 의미하므로 ⓒ문장 뒤에 바로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
options: ① There are some types of carbohydrates that are good for the body and others that are not.
② Good carbohydrates have complex structures, but bad carbohydrates do not.
③ Complex carbohydrates are efficient because they provide energy to the body for a long time.
④ Bad carbohydrates trap nutrients in their sturcture except for the sugars.
⑤ Carbohydrates with simple structures break down quickly, so what our body cannot use turns into fat.
questions.explanation: 본문에 따르면 복합 탄수화물(Complex carbohydrates)이 비타민이나 미네랄 같은 영양소를 사슬 안에 가두고(trap) 천천히 분해하며 영양소를 공급합니다. 반면 나쁜 탄수화물(Bad carbohydrates)인 단순 당류는 구조가 복잡하지 않아 분해되기 쉽고, 당분 외에는 영양소를 거의 포함하고 있지 않다고 설명합니다. 따라서 나쁜 탄수화물이 영양소를 가둔다는 4번 선지는 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 몸에 좋은 탄수화물 유형이 있고 그렇지 않은 유형이 있다.
② 좋은 탄수화물은 복잡한 구조를 가지지만, 나쁜 탄수화물은 그렇지 않다.
③ 복합 탄수화물은 신체에 오랫동안 에너지를 제공하므로 효율적이다.
④ 나쁜 탄수화물은 당분을 제외한 영양소를 그들의 구조 안에 가둔다.
⑤ 단순한 구조를 가진 탄수화물은 빠르게 분해되므로, 우리 몸이 사용할 수 없는 것은 지방으로 변한다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중에서 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that ⓐ<u>they</u> can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing ⓑ<u>them</u> with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend is that ⓒ<u>they</u> show the creatures in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and ⓓ<u>they</u> still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give ⓔ<u>them</u> enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 문맥상 '동물(들)' 또는 '동물 캐릭터(들)'을 가리킵니다. 반면 ⓒ는 'In more recent animated movies the trend is that they show...' 문장에서 최신 애니메이션 영화 제작자나 영화계의 '동향(trend)'을 이끌어가는 주체, 즉 일반적인 사람이나 제작사를 가리키는 막연한 대명사 'they'입니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
options: ① Hot melted rock material cools even underground.
② When magma cools, it combines to form compounds.
③ The rate at which magma cools determines the size of the crystals.
④ When the magma cools over a long period of time, there isn't enough time for the atoms to move together.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 마그마가 천천히 식을 때(cools slowly) 원자들이 결합하여 큰 결정을 형성할 '충분한 시간(enough time)'을 갖는다고 설명합니다. 따라서 마그마가 오랜 시간 동안 식을 때 원자들이 함께 이동할 시간이 충분하지 않다는 4번의 설명은 본문 내용과 반대됩니다.
options_translation: ① 뜨겁게 녹은 암석 물질은 지하에서도 식는다.
② 마그마가 식을 때, 그것은 결합하여 화합물을 형성한다.
③ 마그마가 식는 속도는 결정의 크기를 결정한다.
④ 마그마가 오랜 기간 동안 식을 때, 원자들이 함께 이동할 시간이 충분하지 않다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to ________________________________.
options: ① follow a leader's opinion without disagreement
② adopt a variety of opinions around
③ get enough information in advance
④ accept the majority of choices
⑤ have the courage to oppose
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 '사회적 증거'를 따르는 것, 즉 다른 사람들이 많이 하는 선택(다수의 선택)을 따르는 것이 생존이나 신뢰도 판단에 유리하다는 것이므로 4번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이견 없이 리더의 의견을 따르는 것
② 주변의 다양한 의견을 채택하는 것
③ 사전에 충분한 정보를 얻는 것
④ 다수의 선택을 받아들이는 것
⑤ 반대할 용기를 가지는 것

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 각 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Chess masters shown a chess board in the middle of a game for 5 seconds with 20 to 30 pieces still in play can immediately reproduce the position of the pieces from memory. Beginners, of course, are able to place only a few. Now take the same pieces and place them on the board randomly and the difference is much (A)__________. The expert's advantage is only for familiar patterns - those previously stored in memory. Faced with unfamiliar patterns, even when it involves the same familiar domain, the expert's advantage disappears. The beneficial effects of familiar structure on memory have been observed for many types of expertise, including music. People with musical training can reproduce short sequences of musical notation (B)__________ than those with no musical training when notes follow conventional sequences, but the advantage is much reduced when the notes are ordered randomly. Expertise also improves memory for sequences of movements. Experienced ballet dancers are able to repeat longer sequences of steps than less experienced dancers, and they can repeat a sequence of steps making up a routine better than steps ordered randomly. In each case, memory range is increased by the ability to recognize (C)__________ sequences and patterns.
questions.explanation: (A) 무작위로 배치할 경우 전문가와 초보자의 차이가 '줄어들기(lessened)' 때문에 적절합니다. (B) 훈련된 사람들은 관습적 배열일 때 더 '정확하게(more precisely/accurately)' 재현합니다. (C) 기억력의 증가는 '익숙한(familiar)' 배열을 인식하는 능력에 기인합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 줄어든 (B) 더 정확하게 (C) 익숙하지 않은
② (A) 줄어든 (B) 더 정확하게 (C) 익숙한
③ (A) 확장된 (B) 덜 정확하게 (C) 익숙한
④ (A) 확장된 (B) 덜 정확하게 (C) 익숙하지 않은
⑤ (A) 확장된 (B) 더 정확하게 (C) 익숙한

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to _______________________________.
options: ① the emotional state of the children
② the degree of the competitiveness
③ where the sports are played
④ the popularity of the sports
⑤ how old the children are
questions.explanation: 지문은 어린아이들의 신체적 조건에 맞춰 스포츠 환경(경기장 크기, 공 무게, 경기 시간 등)을 조정해야 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 10세 미만 어린이를 위한 테니스 코트 조정 등의 예시를 통해 이러한 적응 조치가 아이들의 연령(발달 단계)과 관련되어 있음을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 아이들의 감정 상태
② 경쟁의 정도
③ 스포츠가 행해지는 장소
④ 스포츠의 인기
⑤ 아이들의 연령

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This not only forced business to develop closer relations with buyers but also made business realize that ________________________________. For example, Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ① delivery service of the product was what customers really wanted
② to increase the sales, color of the product was the first thing to consider
③ it was not a matter of quality or price but a matter of what people wanted
④ it was important to invest money in advertisements not in the product itself
questions.explanation: 지문은 생산 중심에서 고객 욕구 중심으로 마케팅 철학이 변했음을 설명합니다. 과거 헨리 포드의 단색 자동차 생산 방식이 더 이상 통하지 않게 된 것은 현대 사회에서 '사람들이 원하는 것(고객의 다양한 요구)'을 충족시키는 것이 비즈니스의 핵심이 되었기 때문입니다.
options_translation: ① 제품의 배송 서비스가 고객이 진정으로 원하는 것이었다
② 판매를 늘리기 위해 제품의 색상이 고려해야 할 첫 번째 사항이었다
③ 그것은 품질이나 가격의 문제가 아니라 사람들이 원하는 것의 문제였다
④ 제품 자체보다는 광고에 돈을 투자하는 것이 중요했다

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before we ________________________________. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
options: ① could realize the importance of preparation
② focused on what are considered important
③ set realistic objectives and plans
⑤ came up with more reliable ideas
questions.explanation: 이 글은 모든 창조물이 물리적 실체로 존재하기 전에 이미 창조자의 마음속에서 먼저 완성된다는 점을 강조합니다. 즉, 물리적인 제작이 시작되기 전에 생각이 먼저 다듬어지고 완성된다는 맥락이므로 빈칸에는 '실제로 무언가를 만들기 시작하기(actually started making something)'가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 준비의 중요성을 깨달을 수 있었다
② 중요하다고 간주되는 것에 집중했다
③ 현실적인 목표와 계획을 세웠다
④ 실제로 무언가를 만들기 시작했다
⑤ 더 신뢰할 수 있는 아이디어를 생각해 냈다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears. However, they originate in the _______________________.
options: ① conscious mind and become real when the subconscious mind registers your responses
② subconscious mind and become real when the conscious mind handles your reactions
③ conscious mind and can be eliminated when the subconscious mind adds new emotion to them
④ conscious mind and become more intense when the subconscious mind makes the wrong decision
⑤ subconscious mind and can be overcome when you have a number of experiences related to them
questions.explanation: 본문은 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)이 감정을 더하고 잘못된 결정을 내리게 하는 부분이며, 잠재의식(subconscious mind)은 반응에 대한 기억을 다루는 곳이라고 설명합니다. 거미나 어둠에 대한 공포 같은 감정적인 반응은 의식적인 마음에서 시작되어 잠재의식이 그 반응을 기록할 때 실재화되므로 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 의식적인 마음에서 기원하며 잠재의식이 당신의 반응을 기록할 때 실제가 된다
② 잠재의식에서 기원하며 의식적인 마음이 당신의 반응을 처리할 때 실제가 된다
③ 의식적인 마음에서 기원하며 잠재의식이 그것들에 새로운 감정을 더할 때 제거될 수 있다
④ 의식적인 마음에서 기원하며 잠재의식이 잘못된 결정을 내릴 때 더 강렬해진다
⑤ 잠재의식에서 기원하며 그것들과 관련된 수많은 경험을 할 때 극복될 수 있다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 묑줄 친 부분 섡 묘맥상 낱말의 시임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs ⓐ<u>thrived</u>. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they ⓑ<u>dislike</u>, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to ⓒ<u>choose</u> high-tech work. The ⓓ<u>separation</u> of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health ⓔ<u>risk</u> - for body and mind.
questions.explanation: 기술 발전으로 인해 전적인 생계 수단이 밀려났다고 했으므로, 그 일자리와 관련된 생활 방식 또한 발전하거나 번성한(thrived) 것이 아니라 소멸하거나 서제진 것이 묘맥상 적절합니다. 따라서 ⓐ의 thrived는 removed 또는 disappeared 등의 단어로 바관어야 합니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글에서 전체 흠름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. ⓐ<u>Keeping a consistent routine and sleep schedule is one of the most important things you can do to maintain a healthy rhythm</u>. ⓑ<u>Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it</u>. ⓒ<u>This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams</u>. ⓓ<u>Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football</u>. ⓔ<u>A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel</u>.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 비행 방향(동쪽인준 서쪽인준)에 따라 시차 적응 셍도가 달라지며, 특히 서쪽으로 비행하는 것이 동쪽보다 더 싽다는 사실을 스포츠 팀의 성적을 통해 보여주고 읈습니다. ⓐ는 건강한 리듬을 유지하기 윑한 일반적인 수면 수츙에 대한 설명으로, 비행 방향에 따른 시차 관련 내용과는 거리가 멀얽니다.

questions.question: 22. 윗글을 읽고 알 수 읈는 내용이 아닌 것은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. ⓐ<u>Keeping a consistent routine and sleep schedule is one of the most important things you can do to maintain a healthy rhythm</u>. ⓑ<u>Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it</u>. ⓒ<u>This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams</u>. ⓓ<u>Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football</u>. ⓔ<u>A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel</u>.
options: ① The speed of recovery from jet lag is different among travelers in terms of the direction of travel.
② The journey toward east makes the duration of the day shorter than that toward west.
③ The impact of the direction of travel on athletes is so slight that it should not be considered.
⑤ There is a research finding that having sports games after flying westward produces good results than the opposite situation.
⑥ We can find more proof that it is harder to play baseball in the countries located in the eastern part of where he/she is.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 동서 방향의 시차 차이는 스포츠 팀의 경기 결과에 영향을 미칠 먄큼 상당하다(sizable enough)고 명시되어 읈으므로, 영향이 매우 미미하여 고려되지 않아야 한다는 ③번은 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 시차 광뱱 회뱱 셍도는 리행 방향에 따라 리행자들마다 다르다.
② 동쪽으로의 여정은 서쪽으로의 여정보다 하루의 길이림 더 짧겂 만든다.
③ 운동 선수들에게 미치는 리행 방향의 영향은 매우 미미하여 고려될 필요가 않다.
⑤ 서쪽으로 비행한 후 경기림 치리는 것이 반대의 상황보다 좋은 결과림 낸다는 연구 결과가 읈다.
⑥ 볼인이 읈는 곳보다 동쪽에 위치한 나라에서 야구 경기림 하는 것이 더 어렵다는 더 많은 증거림 찾을 수 읈다.

questions.question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions.
ordered_passages: (A) In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.

(B) To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable.

(C) There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases <u>it is marked</u>. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 영미권 사회에서 낯선 이가 도움을 주었을 때 감사 인사를 하는 규범을 예로 듭니다. (C)에서 이 규범을 지키지 않았을 때의 사회적 반응을 설명하며 타 문화의 규범을 아는 것의 중요성을 화두로 던집니다. (B)에서 타 문화권은 감사가 필요한 상황에 대한 기준이 다를 수 있다는 점(큰 노고가 있을 때만 감사)을 언급하고, (A)에서 그런 문화권 사람에게 영미식 규범을 적용해 사소한 일로 감사 인사를 하는 것이 오히려 이상하게 보일 수 있다는 구체적 결과로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 밑줄 친 it is marked가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions.(A) In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.(B) To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable.(C) There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases <u>it is marked</u>. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication.
options: ③ people stand out from the crowd
④ people are forced to study the norms again
⑤ people become famous among the people around them
questions.explanation: 문맥상 'it is marked'는 규범을 따르지 않았을 때 그 행동이 정상적인 범주에서 벗어나 두드러지게 보인다는 의미입니다. 사람들이 규범에 따라 행동할 것을 기대하기 때문에, 그렇지 않은 행동은 사람들 사이에서 '눈에 띄게(stand out)' 된다는 의미인 3번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들이 체포된다
② 사람들이 정상으로 여겨진다
③ 사람들이 군중 속에서 눈에 띈다
④ 사람들이 규범을 다시 공부하도록 강요받는다
⑤ 사람들이 주변 사람들 사이에서 유명해진다

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 알파벳으로 시작하는 단어를 사용하여 어법에 맞게 아래 요약문을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word ′warm′, the other half were told the speaker was ′cold′. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the study above, the lecturer evaluation (A) d__________ depending on the (B) i__________ given to the test subject group about the lecturer because of the (C) s__________ formed beforehand.
questions.explanation: 사람들은 타인의 한 가지 특징을 보고 그와 연관된 다른 특징들도 당연히 가지고 있을 것이라고 잘못 가정하는 경향이 있습니다. 실험에서 강사에 대한 사전 정보가 '따뜻함'인지 '차가움'인지에 따라 학생들의 평가와 행동이 크게 달라졌음을 보여줍니다. 요약문은 '미리 형성된 (C) 고정관념(stereotype) 때문에 피실험자들에게 제공된 (B) 정보(information)에 따라 강사 평가가 (A) 달라진다(differs)'는 내용이 되어야 하므로 정답은 각각 differs, information, stereotype입니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <보기>의 단어를 활용하여 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the tongue map explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It′s not that you (A)___________________________, but rather that (B)___________________________.
subjective_conditions: 1. (A)와 (B) 각각 3~8단어의 영어로 작성할 것
2. <보기>의 단어 중 필요한 단어를 선택하여 사용하고 글의 흐름과 어법에 맞게 작성할 것
3. 필요시 단어를 추가하거나 변형하여 사용할 수 있음
vocabulary_box: (B) first / later / at the same time / perception / taste / register
questions.answer: (A) taste bitterness at the back (B) you register that perception later
questions.explanation: 이 글은 특정 맛을 혀의 특정 부위에서만 느낀다는 '혀 지도'가 잘못된 이론임을 설명하며, 맛을 느끼는 차이는 장소가 아니라 '시간'의 문제임을 강조하고 있습니다. 지문의 마지막 문장은 '혀 뒷부분에서 쓴맛을 느끼는 것이 아니라, 그 감각을 더 나중에 등록(인지)하는 것뿐이다'라는 의미가 되어야 흐름상 적절합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 위치와 맛에 대한 표현이, (B)에는 인지 시점에 대한 표현이 들어가야 합니다.

questions.question: 6. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Consider the question which seems simple, how many senses are there? About 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that both humans and animals have five senses- sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Other animals have senses that are much more difficult to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(B) According to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, however, there are reasons to reconsider it. First of all, Aristotle missed a few things in humans: the perception of their own bodies which is different from touch and the sense of balance which is linked to both touch and vision.

(C) These examples demonstrate that "senses cannot be clearly classified into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to sort various animal senses into fixed categories, we should study them as they are.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각을 5가지로 정의했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (B)에서 'however'를 통해 이에 대한 재고의 필요성을 제기하며 인간에게서 놓친 감각들(자기 신체 지각, 균형 감각)을 언급합니다.
