(A)에서는 인간뿐만 아니라 '다른 동물들(Other animals)'의 범주화하기 어려운 감각들(냄새 감지 시스템, 열 감지)을 예로 듭니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 'These examples(이러한 사례들)'를 통해 앞서 언급된 인간과 동물의 사례들을 종합하며, 감각을 고정된 범주로 나누기보다 있는 그대로 연구해야 한다는 결론을 내립니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal, the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. (B) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. (C) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. (D) But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. (E) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.insertion_sentence: Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '자극이 등록되지만 정상적으로 처리되지 않아 개체를 깨우지 못한다'는 내용입니다. (B) 문장에서 시각 정보가 들어오지만 약화되어 처리된다는 구체적 설명이 끝난 후, 이러한 상태를 (C)에서 'Perceptual disengagement(지각적 이탈)'라는 용어로 요약하여 정의하기 시작합니다. 따라서 주어진 문장은 정보가 처리되지 않는 구체적 상황(B)과 이를 지각적 이탈이라 칭하며 기능을 설명하는 문장(C) 사이인 (C) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness ⓐ<u>who</u> experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed ⓑ<u>that</u> the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life because those participating in a greater number of sessions ⓒ<u>experiencing</u> the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals who ⓓ<u>were</u> living with a mental health condition in a community setting. They found that people with mental health conditions, ⓔ<u>participating</u> in a choir experienced significant improvements in their mental health and well-being. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 절 'because those participating in a greater number of sessions ⓒexperiencing the greatest benefits'에서 because절의 주어는 those(participating~는 수식어구)입니다. 접속사 because 뒤에는 '주어+동사'의 형태가 와야 하므로, 현재분사인 experiencing은 동사 형태인 experienced로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot, ⓐ<u>as</u> there were no horses available. The messengers called Chasquis were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. They lived in groups of four to six in huts, ⓑ<u>located</u> from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they ⓒ<u>noticed</u> another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger ⓓ<u>approached</u> the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one running out to meet him. The Inca empire could ⓔ<u>disconnect</u> messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
questions.explanation: 잉카 제국이 뛰어난 통신 시스템을 통해 먼 거리까지 메시지를 전달했다는 맥락이므로, ⓔ의 disconnect(단절시키다)는 부적절합니다. 메시지를 '전달하다' 혹은 '보내다'는 의미인 relay나 deliver 등이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements like what degree of heat or cold it can endure. As the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements ⓐ<u>are</u> likely to change as well. Species are forced ⓑ<u>to follow</u>. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of ⓒ<u>dispersing</u> at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born, ⓓ<u>which</u> is often occupied by its parent, to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees ⓔ<u>move</u> with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: 문장 끝에 'during past periods of climate change(과거의 기후 변화 기간 동안)'라는 과거 시점을 나타내는 부사구가 있으므로, 현재 시제인 move를 과거 시제인 moved로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick.
ordered_passages: (A) If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence.(B) Write down all the realtime challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here.(C) You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 마법을 만드는 비결(trick)을 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 그 구체적인 방법으로 직면한 어려움을 긍정적인 문구로 바꾸어 쓰라는 제안을 합니다. (A)는 (B)의 마지막 문장(example)에 대한 구체적인 예시(아침 일찍 일어나기)를 보여줍니다. (C)는 이러한 문구들을 씀으로써 나타나는 결과(생각과 행동의 변화)를 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. ⓐIf you consider the historical importance and farreaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. ⓑBut like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. ⓒPart of the reason people think they're not a good leader is because they see leadership in a narrow way. ⓓThrough diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. ⓔThus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 위대한 리더들도 평범한 시작을 했으며, 우리 모두가 리더가 될 잠재력을 가지고 있다는 것입니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 이러한 맥락에서 위대한 리더들의 평범한 시작과 노력, 그리고 우리 모두의 가능성을 연결하고 있습니다. 반면 ⓒ는 사람들이 스스로 리더라고 생각하지 않는 이유(리더십을 좁게 보는 시각)를 언급하고 있어, 리더의 성장 과정과 보편적 잠재력에 초점을 맞춘 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분에 들어갈 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore _______________ along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① are more exposed to traffic accidents
② have enough time to observe more details
③ have a more enlarged ability to handle details
④ have a more restricted capacity to process details
⑤ improve the cognitive abilities to distinguish the designs of the city
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 이동 속도가 빠를수록 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력이 떨어진다는 것입니다. 인간의 감각은 걷는 속도에 최적화되어 있으므로, 가장 빠른 운전자(motorists)는 세부 사항을 감상할 시간이나 능력이 부족하다는 내용이 이어져야 합니다. 따라서 '세부 사항을 처리하는 능력이 더 제한적이다'라는 의미인 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 교통사고에 더 많이 노출되어 있다
② 더 많은 세부 사항을 관찰할 충분한 시간을 갖는다
③ 세부 사항을 다루는 능력이 더 확장된다
④ 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력이 더 제한적이다
⑤ 도시의 디자인을 구별하는 인지 능력을 향상시킨다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥상 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I (A)[block / preserve] a culture that prevents differing disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these (B)[objectors / supporters] because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done. It gets you out of your framework of the (C)[conventions / profitabilities] of what you can and can't do."
questions.explanation: (A) 훌륭한 상사라면 반대 의견을 막는 문화를 '유지한다(preserve)'고 말하지 않을 것이므로, 역설적으로 그런 말을 하지 않는다는 문맥에서 preserve가 적절합니다. (B) 하급 직원들의 내부적인 항의나 반대를 장려하는 내용이므로, 그들의 말을 들어야 한다는 의미에서 '반대자들(objectors)'이 적절합니다. (C) 할 수 있는 것과 없는 것에 대한 기존의 '관습(conventions)' 또는 틀에서 벗어나게 해준다는 의미이므로 conventions가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 한 단어는?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adultstyle competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made __________ for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The __________ are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성인 위주의 스포츠 환경이 아이들에게는 적합하지 않다는 점을 인지하고, 경기장 규격이나 장비, 규칙 등을 어린이들의 수준과 신체 조건에 맞게 '수정(modifications)'하여 운영하는 다양한 사례를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 두 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어는 ① modifications입니다.
options_translation: ① 수정
② 장점
③ 참가자
④ 팀
⑤ 삭감(축소)

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. (A)__________, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose (B)__________ to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. (C)__________ your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.explanation:
(A) 앞쪽에서 설명한 무의식적인 마음(subconscious mind)의 특징과 대조되는 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)의 특징을 설명하기 시작하므로 역접의 연결어 'However(그러나)'가 적절합니다.
(B) 생각을 계속 이어갈지 말지를 '선택(choose)'하는 맥락이므로 '~인지 아닌지'라는 의미를 가진 'whether'가 적절합니다.
(C) 감정에 의해 판단이 흐려지는 상황을 조건이나 때로 나타내고 있으므로 '~할 때'라는 의미의 'When'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나 - ~인지 아닌지 - ~할 때
② 그럼에도 불구하고 - ~인지 아닌지 - ~에도 불구하고
③ 그러나 - 어떻게 - ~할 때
④ 게다가 - ~함에 따라 - 따라서
⑤ 그러므로 - ~인지 아닌지 - 짧게 말해서

questions.question: 20. 문맥상 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 단어를 본문에 제시된 철자로 시작하여 쓰시오.
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that offers a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and consider their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has (A)<u>p</u>_________ numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only perform higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most (B)<u>s</u>_________ with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones (A)<u>p</u>_________ a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who were (B)<u>s</u>_________ with their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
subjective_conditions: 본문에 제시된 첫 철자를 반드시 사용할 것
문맥에 맞는 적절한 형태(시제 등)로 작성할 것
questions.explanation:
(A) '수많은 직장 연구를 수행해 왔다'는 의미를 나타내기 위해 '수행하다'라는 뜻의 동사 perform을 현재완료 시제(has + p.p.)와 과거형에 맞게 'performed'로 쓰는 것이 적절합니다.
(B) '자신의 업무에 만족하는 사람들'이라는 의미를 나타내기 위해 '만족한'이라는 뜻의 형용사 'satisfied'를 사용하는 것이 문맥상 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말을 주어진 단어들을 모두 알맞게 배열하여 완성하시오. (단, 필요 시 동사의 어법 변화 가능)
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session (A)__________(be / need to / a different way / explore in), and each healing treatment (B)__________(of the animal / should / adapt to / the specific needs / be / meet). You will learn gradually; healing is a constant learning process.
subjective_conditions: 1. 주어진 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 배열할 것
2. 필요 시 동사의 어형을 변화시킬 것
vocabulary_box: (A) be / need to / a different way / explore in
(B) of the animal / should / adapt to / the specific needs / be / meet
questions.answer: (A) needs to be explored in a different way (B) should be adapted to meet the specific needs of the animal
questions.explanation:
(A) every healing session이 단수 주어이므로 동사를 needs로 쓰고, '~할 필요가 있다'는 의미의 need to와 '탐색되어야 한다'는 수동태 be explored를 결합하여 needs to be explored in a different way로 배열하는 것이 적절합니다.
(B) each healing treatment를 주어로 하여 '~에 맞춰져야 한다'는 수동태 조동사 구문인 should be adapted를 쓰고, 그 뒤에 목적(~하기 위해)을 나타내는 to부정사구 to meet the specific needs of the animal을 연결하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말을 주어진 단어들을 모두 알맞게 배열하여 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. For example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. (A)<u>다문화 소통의 중심적인 문제는 다른 집단의 규범에 대한 이해 부족에서 비롯된다</u>. (Cross-cultural communication's / regarding the norms / central problem / comes from / the lack of understanding / of different communities). To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (B)<u>만약 네가 혹시라도 아주 사소한 일에 대해 누군가에게 감사해한다면</u> (if you / so minor / were / something / thank someone for / to) as holding a door open for you.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어들을 모두 알맞게 배열하여 완성할 것
vocabulary_box: (A): Cross-cultural communication's / regarding the norms / central problem / comes from / the lack of understanding / of different communities
(B): if you / so minor / were / something / thank someone for / to
questions.answer: (A) Cross-cultural communication's central problem comes from the lack of understanding regarding the norms of different communities.(B) if you were to thank someone for something so minor
questions.explanation: (A) '다문화 소통의 중심적인 문제'인 'Cross-cultural communication's central problem'을 주어로 하고, '~에서 비롯되다'라는 'comes from'을 동사로 사용합니다. 그 뒤에 목적어 'the lack of understanding'과 수식어 'regarding the norms of different communities'를 순서대로 배열합니다.(B) 가정법 미래인 'if + 주어 + were to + 동사원형' 구문을 사용합니다. 'if you were to thank someone' 뒤에 '이유'를 나타내는 'for something so minor'를 연결하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글 (A)의 내용을 기반으로 아래와 같은 글 (B)를 쓰고자 할 때, 괄호 안에 단어를 주어진 조건에 부합하도록 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: (A) A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.summary_sentence: (B) The curse of knowledge is a cognitive bias that (cause(s) / fail / of those / people / properly / the perspective / to / to / understand / who) do not have as much information as them.
subjective_conditions: 어법상 어색하지 않고 문맥에 맞게 완성.
위 제시된 단어만을 모두 한 번씩 사용
단어 중복사용 불가 (단, 두 번 제시된 to는 두 번 사용)
단어 추가 불가
주어진 단어 중 cause(s)는 cause 또는 causes 중 문맥에 맞게 택 1 하여 사용하고 그 외 단어는 어형 변화 불가
questions.answer: causes people to fail to properly understand the perspective of those who
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전문가들이 초보자의 어려움을 이해하지 못하는 '지식의 저주' 현상에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. (B) 문장에서 선행사가 단수인 a cognitive bias이므로 동사는 causes를 사용해야 하며, 'cause + 목적어 + to 부정사' 구문을 활용하여 '사람들이 ~하는 것을 실패하게 만든다'는 구조를 만들어야 합니다. 따라서 'causes people to fail to properly understand the perspective of those who'가 정답입니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 밑줄 친 (A)에 들어갈 알맞은 한 단어를 써넣고, 밑줄 친 (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 문장을 괄호 안에 단어를 사용하여 주어진 조건에 부합하도록 배열하여 완성하시오.
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first. (A)__________ the scientific evidence, the tongue map has (B)<u>(burrow / common knowledge / into / its / way</u>) and is still taught in many classrooms and textbooks today.
subjective_conditions: 어법상 어색하지 않고 문맥에 맞게 완성.
위 제시된 단어만을 모두 한 번씩 사용, 단어 중복사용 불가, 단어 추가 불가
주어진 단어 중 burrow만 반드시 어형 변화하고 그 외 단어는 어형 변화 불가
questions.answer: (A) Despite(B) burrowed its way into common knowledge
questions.explanation: (A)는 뒤에 구(the scientific evidence)가 오고 문맥상 양보의 의미가 필요하므로 전치사 Despite가 적절합니다. (B)는 현재완료(has + p.p.) 시제에 맞춰 burrow를 burrowed로 변형해야 하며, 'burrow one's way into' (~으로 파고들다)라는 표현을 사용하여 '상식 속으로 파고들었다'는 의미의 'burrowed its way into common knowledge'를 완성합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. [3.5점]
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those __________ in their daily lives. Therefore show your child good examples of life by your action. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 아이들이 부모의 가치관(values)을 공유한다고 언급하고 있으며, 빈칸 앞의 'those'가 가리키는 대상은 앞 문장의 'the values that make up strong character'입니다. 따라서 빈칸에 알맞은 단어는 'values'입니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용으로 가장 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ① 모두 리더가 될 잠재력이 있다.
③ 어떤 사람들은 큰 영향력을 가지고 있다.
④ 리더들은 삶을 향상할 아이디어가 있었다.
⑤ 리더십은 평범한 사람들은 가지기 어려운 자질이다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 "we all have the potential to be leaders... regardless of age or experience"(나이나 경험에 상관없이 우리 모두는 리더가 될 잠재력을 가지고 있다)라고 명시하고 있으므로, 평범한 사람이 가지기 어려운 자질이라는 5번은 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. ⓐFor example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. ⓑThe next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. ⓒBy the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. ⓓEach crop enriches the soil for the next crop. ⓔSometimes it is best to consider different kinds of farming. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 '윤작(Crop rotation)'의 개념과 그 예시, 그리고 그것이 토양에 주는 이점에 대해 설명하는 글입니다. 하지만 ⑤번은 단순히 '다른 종류의 농사법을 고려하는 것이 최선일 때가 있다'는 일반적인 진술로, 윤작의 구체적인 과정과 장점을 설명하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 단어들로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to (A)__________ your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking (B)__________. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further (C)__________.
questions.explanation: 지문의 내용상 (A)에는 진행 상황을 '평가(assess)'하기 위해 뒤로 물러나야 한다는 내용이, (B)에는 너무 많이 그려 넣으면 그림이 '지나치게 공들인(overworked)' 것처럼 보인다는 내용이, (C)에는 나중에 다시 보고 더 '다듬을(refinement)' 필요가 있는지 결정한다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다. (제시된 텍스트에는 4번 선지가 잘려 있으나, 원문 맥락상 assess, overworked, refinement 등이 정답 조합입니다.)
options_translation: ① 칭찬하다 / 미완성된 / 감소

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 Species are forced to follow가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. <u>Species are forced to follow</u>. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① Some species will eventually extinct.
② Some species cause extreme climate change.
③ Every species can move at any stage of their life.
④ Species must move to survive climate change.
⑤ Species endure harsh climate exactly from where they are.
questions.explanation: 기후가 변하면 생물이 생존할 수 있는 요구 조건을 충족하는 장소도 변하기 때문에, 생물들은 생존을 위해 그러한 장소를 따라 이동해야 한다는 의미이다.
options_translation: ① 일부 종들은 결국 멸종할 것이다.
② 일부 종들은 극단적인 기후 변화를 초래한다.
③ 모든 종은 생애의 어느 단계에서든 이동할 수 있다.
④ 종들은 기후 변화에서 살아남기 위해 반드시 이동해야 한다.
⑤ 종들은 그들이 있는 바로 그곳에서 가혹한 기후를 견뎌낸다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. ____________________ probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 수면 중에 외부 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않는 현상에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 'perceptual disengagement(지각적 단절)' 없이 잠의 이점을 얻는다고 언급하고 있는데, 빈칸은 잠을 보호하는 기능을 하는 개념이 들어가야 하므로, 자극에 반응하지 않는 상태인 'perceptual disengagement'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 강한 감각
② 수면 패턴
③ 자극 강도
④ 정보 처리
⑤ 지각적 단절

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas ⓐ<u>where</u> certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, ⓑ<u>demonstrating</u> that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research ⓒ<u>conducted</u> in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they are probably ⓓ<u>perceived</u> at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work ⓔ<u>is</u> not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'Research'이고, 그 뒤에 나오는 'that절'은 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절입니다. 따라서 ⓑ 자리는 문장의 본동사가 필요한 자리이므로 현재분사인 'demonstrating'을 과거 시제 동사인 'demonstrated'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ② Lonley Life of the inca Messengers
③ King's involvement in Inca messaging
④ The Message Delivery System in Inca Empire
⑤ The Inca Empire's Use of Horses for Message Delivery
questions.explanation: 지문은 잉카 제국에서 말이 없는 상황에서 'Chasquis'라고 불리는 전령들이 도보로 메시지를 전달하는 체계적인 방식에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ④ '잉카 제국의 메시지 전달 시스템'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① Chasquis의 의무와 한계
② 잉카 전령들의 외로운 삶
③ 잉카 메시지 전달에 대한 왕의 관여
④ 잉카 제국의 메시지 전달 시스템
⑤ 잉카 제국의 메시지 전달을 위한 말의 사용

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing ⓐ<u>newcomers</u> to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably more ⓑ<u>inaccurate</u> than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓒ<u>sensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even ⓓ<u>underestimated</u> how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how ⓔ<u>hard</u> it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: '지식의 저주'는 전문가가 초보자의 입장을 이해하지 못하고 과업의 난이도를 과소평가하는 현상을 말합니다. 따라서 전문가들이 초보자에게 과업이 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 '민감해진다(sensitive)'는 것은 문맥상 반대되는 내용이므로 '둔감해진다(insensitive)'와 같은 표현이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adultstyle competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made __________ for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 내용은 아이들의 신체 조건에 맞지 않는 성인용 스포츠 환경을 아이들에게 적합하게 '조정'하거나 '변형'했다는 사례들을 들고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 문장들에서 야구, 축구, 테니스 등의 사례를 통해 구체적인 변경 사항을 언급하며, 마지막 문장에서 'The adaptations'라고 직접적으로 명시하고 있으므로 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 조정(개조)
② 기억
③ 활동
④ 인상
⑤ 교훈

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. ⓐIn evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. ⓑMost people say that there are five senses, but actually there are more. ⓒOur ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. ⓓThe fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. ⓔOn the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 인간의 감각이 보행 속도에 최적화되어 있어 속도가 빨라질수록 세부 사항 파악 능력이 떨어진다는 내용이 주를 이룹니다. 반면 ⓑ는 감각의 종류가 다섯 가지 이상이라는 내용으로, 이동 속도와 인지 능력이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Although animals from the same litter might display the exact same features, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.summary_sentence: As animals show (A)__________ responses to healing session according to the environment and symptoms, treatments need to be (B)__________ to fit each animal's need.
questions.explanation: 본문은 동물이 환경과 증상에 따라 치유 세션에 다르게 반응하며, 그에 따라 각 동물의 특정 필요에 맞게 치료법이 조정(adjusted)되어야 함을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 different(다른), (B)에는 changed(변경된/조정된)가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 - 바뀐
② 지연된 - 반복된
③ 다른 - 반복된
④ 지연된 - 향상된
⑤ 유사한 - 바뀐

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 20번]
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore show your child good examples of life by your action. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
options: ① reason of teaching children life priorities
② effect of words and actions in negotiation
③ necessity of principles when disciplining children
④ significance of parents setting positive examples for their children
⑤ concern about parents' involvement in a child's decision-making process
questions.explanation: 이 글은 부모가 말보다는 행동을 통해 자녀에게 가치관을 가르친다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 아이들은 부모의 일상적인 행동을 보고 배우므로, 부모가 긍정적인 본보기를 보여주는 것이 중요하다는 내용이 핵심입니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 '부모가 자녀에게 긍정적인 본보기를 보여주는 것의 중요성'입니다.
options_translation: ① 자녀에게 인생의 우선순위를 가르치는 이유
② 협상에서 말과 행동의 효과
③ 자녀를 훈육할 때 원칙의 필요성
④ 부모가 자녀에게 긍정적인 본보기를 설정하는 것의 중요성
⑤ 자녀의 의사결정 과정에 대한 부모의 개입에 대한 우려

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 21번]
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk - for body and mind.
options: ① the benefits of working in hated jobs
② escaping the stress of manual labor in the digital age
③ the perils of maintaining low-tech work in the digital world
④ celebrating the rise of digital jobs and sedentary lifestyles
⑤ the impact of technology adoption on traditional livelihoods and human well-being
questions.explanation: 기술 채택에는 비용이 따르며, 이는 전통적인 생계 수단의 상실, 하기 싫은 일에서의 고통, 신체적/정신적 건강 위험 등을 포함한다는 내용입니다. 즉, 기술 도입이 전통적 생계와 인간의 웰빙에 미치는 부정적인 영향에 대해 다루고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 싫어하는 일을 하는 것의 이점
② 디지털 시대에 육체 노동의 스트레스로부터 탈출하기
③ 디지털 세계에서 저기술 노동을 유지하는 것의 위험성
④ 디지털 일자리와 앉아서 일하는 라이프스타일의 부상을 축하하기
⑤ 기술 채택이 전통적인 생계와 인간의 웰빙에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 21번]
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① Why Don't Scientific Publications Have Readers?
② Explore How a Tree Falls Silently in the Forest!
③ From Signal to Understanding: The Essence of Publication
④ Investigating the Disconnection Between Research and Reality
⑤ Scientific Communication: Harmonizing Publication and Understanding
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학적 의사소통은 출판되는 것만으로는 부족하며, 의도된 청중에게 전달되고 '이해'되어야 비로소 완성된다는 것을 강조합니다. 소리가 들려야 소리이듯이, 과학 논문도 이해되어야 진정한 의미를 갖는다는 비유를 사용하고 있습니다. 따라서 '출판과 이해의 조화'를 다룬 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 과학 출판물에는 독자가 없는가?
② 숲에서 나무가 어떻게 조용히 쓰러지는지 탐구하라!
③ 신호에서 이해까지: 출판의 본질
④ 연구와 현실 사이의 단절 조사하기
⑤ 과학적 의사소통: 출판과 이해의 조화

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Sometimes the pace of change is far slower. The face you saw reflected in your mirror this morning probably appeared no different from the face you saw the day before - or a week or a month ago. Yet we know that the face that stares back at us from the glass is not the same, cannot be the same, as it was 10 minutes ago. The proof is in your photo album: Look at a photograph taken of yourself 5 or 10 years ago and you see clear differences between the face in the snapshot and the face in your mirror. If you lived in a world without mirrors for a year and then saw your reflection, you might be surprised by the change. After an interval of 10 years without seeing yourself, you might not at first recognize the person peering from the mirror. Even something as basic as our own face changes from moment to moment.
options: ① Mirror: The Best Tool to Perceive Changes
② Differences Between Real Faces and Photos
③ Things That Seldom Change Over Time
④ Change Happens Slowly but Definitely
⑤ How to Take Good Photos of Yourself
questions.explanation: 이 글은 매일 보는 자신의 얼굴이 변하지 않는 것처럼 느껴지지만, 실제로는 매 순간 변하고 있으며 시간이 지나 사진을 통해 확인하면 그 명확한 차이를 알 수 있다는 점을 설명합니다. 즉, 변화는 느리지만 확실하게 일어난다는 내용이므로 ④번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 거울: 변화를 감지하는 최고의 도구
② 실제 얼굴과 사진의 차이점
③ 시간이 지나도 좀처럼 변하지 않는 것들
④ 변화는 천천히 하지만 확실하게 일어난다
⑤ 자신의 멋진 사진을 찍는 방법

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. People have ⓐ<u>different</u> preferences when it comes to managing their time for work and other responsibilities. Some individuals prefer to keep work and personal life separate to ⓑ<u>reduce</u> the chances of mixing them. They may use separate email accounts and often carry two phones, one for work and one for ⓒ<u>private</u> use. They typically strive to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. On the other hand, other prefer to ⓓ<u>blend</u> work and family duties throughout the day. For these individuals, the distinction between work and personal time can be less ⓔ<u>flexible</u>. They might exchange text messages with family members during work hours or check work emails during leisure time at home or while on vacation, instead of waiting until they return to work to respond.
questions.explanation: 업무와 가정의 의무를 하루 종일 섞어서 처리하는(blend) 사람들에게는 업무 시간과 개인 시간의 구분이 더 '유연한' 것이지, '덜 유연한' 것이 아닙니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 'flexible'을 'distinct'나 'clear' 등으로 고쳐 '구분이 덜 명확하다(less distinct/clear)'라고 하거나, 'less'를 'more'로 바꾸어 '더 유연하다'라고 표현해야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad. There are, however, ____________________ that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
options: ④ whole foods and raw foods
⑤ some fats essential for health
questions.explanation: 지문은 특정 음식이 그 자체로 좋거나 나쁜 것이 아니라, 전체적인 식단을 구성하는 음식들의 '조합'이 건강에 영향을 미친다는 내용을 설명하고 있습니다. 좋은 음식만 먹어도 다양성이 부족하면 건강하지 않을 수 있고, 가끔 나쁜 음식을 먹어도 전체적인 균형이 맞으면 괜찮다는 예시를 통해 빈칸에는 '음식의 조합'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 패스트푸드 선택지들
② 건강 보조 식품들
③ 음식들의 조합
④ 가공되지 않은 식품과 생식
⑤ 건강에 필수적인 일부 지방들

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, are _______________________. With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
options: ① eventually performed by AI robots
② addressed by more use of creativity
③ expected to be performed by the company
④ now assigned to the consumers themselves
⑤ having us undermine benefits of automation
questions.explanation: 컴퓨터화된 사회가 여유 시간을 늘려줄 것이라는 기대와 달리, 과거에 기업이 서비스로 제공하던 일들(항공 예약, 체크인, 식료품 스캔 등)이 이제는 '소비자 자신에게 할당되었다(now assigned to the consumers themselves)'는 내용이 이어지는 예시들과 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 결국 AI 로봇에 의해 수행된다
② 더 많은 창의성 사용으로 해결된다
③ 회사에 의해 수행될 것으로 기대된다
④ 이제 소비자 자신에게 할당된다
⑤ 우리가 자동화의 이점을 약화시키게 만든다

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that __________________________________. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight challenges from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
options: ① meets societal expectations with minor deviations
② represents one's cultural background and identity
③ sticks to established norms without hesitation
④ reflects one's social status and competence
⑤ reveals one's personal tastes and interests
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 기존의 규범을 아주 약간 어긴 의복(검은 넥타이 정장에 빨간 나비넥타이, 강의 시 빨간 운동화 등)을 착용한 사람을 더 유능하고 지위가 높은 것으로 평가한다는 연구 결과를 소개하고 있습니다. 따라서 사람들은 '약간의 일탈을 동반하여 사회적 기대를 충족시키는' 의복을 선호한다는 내용이 빈칸에 어울립니다.
options_translation: ① 약간의 일탈과 함께 사회적 기대를 충족시키는
② 개인의 문화적 배경과 정체성을 나타내는
③ 망설임 없이 확립된 규범을 고수하는
④ 개인의 사회적 지위와 능력을 반영하는
⑤ 개인의 개인적 취향과 관심을 드러내는

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. _______________________ became the focus of business.
options: ① Noticing customers' various needs and trying to fulfill them
② Establishing and maintaining closer relationships with competitors
③ Producing diverse products regardless of customer preferences
④ Putting a lot of energy and effort into developing cost-effective products
⑤ Conducting revolutionary marketing strategies to raise brand awareness
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거 생산 중심의 경제에서 현대의 고객 요구 중심의 마케팅 혁명으로 변화한 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. 단순히 제품을 만드는 것을 넘어 고객이 실제로 원하는 제품을 제공하는 것이 필수적이 되었다는 맥락이므로, 빈칸에는 '고객의 다양한 요구를 파악하고 이를 충족시키려 노력하는 것'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고객의 다양한 요구를 알아차리고 이를 충족시키려 노력하는 것
② 경쟁자들과 더 긴밀한 관계를 수립하고 유지하는 것
③ 고객의 선호도와 상관없이 다양한 제품을 생산하는 것
④ 비용 효율적인 제품을 개발하는 데 많은 에너지와 노력을 들이는 것
⑤ 브랜드 인지도를 높이기 위해 혁명적인 마케팅 전략을 수행하는 것

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. (A) Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. (B) This goes for the boardroom as well. (C) Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. (D) Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. (E) Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 (D)에서 언급된 '스포츠 경영진(Executives in sport management)'들이 비전문가들로부터 사업 운영 방식에 대한 비판에 직면한다는 내용입니다. (E) 앞에서 경영진의 전문성을 언급한 뒤, 'However'로 시작하는 주어진 문장이 나와 대조를 이루고, (E) 뒤에서 일반인들이 의사나 회계사에게는 훈수를 두지 않지만 스포츠 조직 관리에는 피드백을 준다는 구체적 예시가 이어지는 구조가 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers.
ordered_passages: (A) On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups.(B) This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity.(C) Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 문화적 다양성이 생산성을 높일 수 있다는 긍정적 측면을 언급합니다. (B)의 'This is only an advantage up to a certain degree'는 주어진 문장의 'advantage(생산성 증가)'를 받으며 다양성이 너무 커질 때의 단점을 제시합니다. (C)는 노동 시장 외에 삶의 질 측면에서도 다양성이 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 언급하며 관용적인 원주민의 긍정적 반응을 다루고, (A)는 'On the other hand'를 통해 원주민이 정체성 왜곡으로 느껴 부정적으로 반응할 수 있는 상황을 대조적으로 보여줍니다. 따라서 (B)-(C)-(A)가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: It is difficult for any of us to maintain a constant level of attention throughout our working day. We all have body rhythms characterised by peaks and valleys of energy and alertness. ⓐYou will achieve more, and feel confident as a benefit, if you schedule your most demanding tasks at times when you are best able to cope with them. ⓑIf you're feeling overwhelmed by demanding tasks, just ignore them and hope they go away. ⓒIf you haven't thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to observe yourself. ⓓTry to note the times when you are at your best. ⓔWe are all different; for some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for others it may take a while to warm up.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 에너지의 정점 시간대에 맞춰 까다로운 일을 처리하라는 조언입니다. ⓑ는 '까다로운 일로 압도당한다면 무시하고 사라지길 바래라'는 내용으로, 자신의 생체 리듬을 파악하여 생산성을 높이자는 글의 전체 흐름과 상반되며 무관한 문장입니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.summary_sentence: Children are (A)__________ to the challenges and stresses associated with moving, so they need to (B)__________ their past and live in the moment in order to adapt to the new surroundings.
questions.explanation: 지문은 아이들이 이사로 인한 변화에 특히 스트레스를 많이 받으며(sensitive), 아이들이 새로운 환경에 적응하기 위해서는 그들의 과거 경험을 존중하고 소중히 여기는(cherish) 과정이 필요하다고 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 예민한 - 소중히 여기다
② 무관심한 - 수용하다
③ ~하기 쉬운 - 잊다
④ 반응하는 - 무시하다
⑤ 부주의한 - 놓아주다

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Anthropomorphism, which means giving human characteristics to non-human things, like animals or objects, ⓐ<u>is</u> prevalent in visual arts and popular culture, particularly in cartoons, comics, and animated movies. Characters like Mickey Mouse, Bugs Bunny, and Simba from "The Lion King" have become iconic symbols of anthropomorphism, ⓑ<u>fascinated</u> audiences with their blend of animal and human traits. The most noticeable human characteristic ⓒ<u>assigned</u> to animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often ⓓ<u>deformed</u> in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy ⓔ<u>used</u> to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 'Characters like Mickey Mouse, Bugs Bunny, and Simba... have become iconic symbols of anthropomorphism'이 주절입니다. 뒤따르는 부분은 분사구문으로, 캐릭터들이 관객을 매료시키는 능동적인 주체이므로 과거분사 fascinated가 아니라 현재분사 fascinating이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글에 나타난 'animal characters in cartoons or animated movies'의 특징으로 언급된 것만을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Anthropomorphism, which means giving human characteristics to non-human things, like animals or objects, ⓐ<u>is</u> prevalent in visual arts and popular culture, particularly in cartoons, comics, and animated movies. Characters like Mickey Mouse, Bugs Bunny, and Simba from "The Lion King" have become iconic symbols of anthropomorphism, ⓑ<u>fascinated</u> audiences with their blend of animal and human traits. The most noticeable human characteristic ⓒ<u>assigned</u> to animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often ⓓ<u>deformed</u> in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy ⓔ<u>used</u> to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
vocabulary_box: (B) have altered front legs to mimic human hands
questions.explanation: (A) 본문에서 동물 캐릭터들은 인간의 언어(human language)로 말한다고 했으므로 그들만의 방식(their own ways)으로 소통한다는 것은 틀린 내용입니다. (B) 앞다리가 사람의 손처럼 변형되었다고 언급되었습니다. (C) 인간 같은 얼굴 표정을 보여준다고 언급되었습니다. (D) 아이 같은 특징이 확대되고 변형되어 나타난다고 언급되었습니다. 따라서 (B), (C), (D)가 정답입니다.

questions.question: 22. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓒ가 어법에 맞는지를 판단하여 <조건>에 따라 어법에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy ⓐ<u>promotes</u> sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, ⓑ<u>to offer</u> Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. The strength of the study lies in its real-world setting within supermarkets with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor ⓒ<u>was</u> it take place in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
subjective_conditions: 어법에 맞는 것은 그대로 답안지에 쓸 것
어법이 어색한 것은 어법에 맞게 고쳐 쓸 것
questions.explanation: ⓐ는 동명사 주어 'Restricting ~'에 일치하는 단수 동사 promotes로 적절합니다. ⓑ는 'persuade + 목적어 + to부정사' 구문으로 to offer가 적절합니다. ⓒ는 'nor'에 의한 도치 구문인데, 뒤에 일반 동사 원형 take가 있으므로 be동사인 was가 아니라 조동사 did가 필요합니다.

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 실험 내용을 다음과 같이 정리하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 내용을 <보기>의 단어들을 이용하여 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy ⓐ<u>promotes</u> sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, ⓑ<u>to offer</u> Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. The strength of the study lies in its real-world setting within supermarkets with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor ⓒ<u>was</u> it take place in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
questions.summary_sentence: The study conducted by Brain Wansink in 1998 demonstrates _____________________________. Limiting the number of items customers could buy resulted in a significant increase in the average number of cans bought by customers.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용하되, 한 번씩만 사용할 것
<보기>외의 단어를 한 개만 추가하여 쓸 것
vocabulary_box: the, boosting, of, in, effectiveness, sales
questions.answer: the effectiveness of scarcity in boosting sales
questions.explanation: 이 글은 희소성(판매 제한)이 판매를 촉진하는 데 효과적이라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 주어진 단어들을 조합하고 'scarcity(희소성)'라는 단어를 추가하여 'the effectiveness of scarcity in boosting sales (판매를 촉진하는 데 있어서 희소성의 효과)'라는 문구를 완성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 내용을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [2.9점]
questions.passage: Whose story it is affects what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the perspective of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
questions.summary_sentence: The _________________________________ determines the interpretation and outcome of the story.
subjective_conditions: 3~5단어로 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 이야기가 누구의 관점에서 서술되느냐에 따라 이야기의 초점과 해석이 달라진다는 것입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '주인공의 관점'에 해당하는 'perspective of a main character' 또는 'viewpoint of a main character'가 적절하며, 3~5단어 조건을 충족합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글 (A)와 (B)의 내용을 주어진 문장과 같이 정리하고자 한다. 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓓ에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: (A) For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are - writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. Nothing else other than performance is taken into account - An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.(B) Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
questions.summary_sentence: Both passages share a discussion of the relationship between ⓐ__________ and its ⓑ__________ on self-worth, credibility, and admiration from others. But to be more specific, passage(A) warns against judging people only from their performance, ⓒ__________ other aspects of their identities. On the other hand, passage(B) emphasizes that ⓓ__________ in a particular area can significantly impact how others perceive and connect with individuals, regardless of their expertise in other areas.
subjective_conditions: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ는 각각 한 단어씩 쓸 것
ⓐ, ⓑ는 글 (A)에서 찾아 쓰되, 필요시 변형할 것
questions.explanation: 글 (A)는 능력(ability)이 자아 존중감의 유일한 결정 요소가 될 때의 문제점을 지적하며 수행 능력 외의 다른 정체성 요소들을 무시(neglecting/disregarding)하게 됨을 경고합니다. 글 (B)는 특정 분야의 탁월함(excellence)이 그 분야와 상관없는 부분에까지 타인의 신뢰와 연결을 이끌어내는 영향(influence)을 미친다는 점을 설명합니다. 따라서 각 빈칸에는 전체 맥락을 관통하는 키워드인 능력, 영향, 무시, 탁월함이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.*tempting: 유혹하는 **refinement: 정교하게 꾸밈
options: ① 그림을 그리는 재능은 연습으로 얻어질 수 없다.
② 예술가는 다른 사람의 평가에 연연해서는 안 된다.
③ 그림을 그릴 때는 한 가지 주제에만 몰두해야 한다.
④ 적절한 때에 그리는 것을 멈춰야 더 나은 작품을 만들 수 있다.
⑤ 어려움을 극복하는 과정을 통해야만 진정한 예술작품을 만들 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 필자는 그림을 그릴 때 너무 많은 것을 덧붙이면 오히려 작품의 영향을 망칠 수 있으며(spoil its impact), 언제 멈춰야 할지 아는 것이 중요하다고 설명합니다. 따라서 '적절한 때에 멈추는 것'의 중요성을 강조하는 ④번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that ⓐ<u>are</u> known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one ⓑ<u>that</u> you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or ⓒ<u>adding</u> emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is ⓓ<u>clouded</u> by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions. While the controllable conscious mind deals with thoughts and emotions, the fast-acting subconscious mind stores your responses, ⓔ<u>forming</u> real fears.
questions.explanation: ⓒ 'whether to' 구문에서 'carry on'과 병렬 구조를 이루어야 합니다. 따라서 'adding'은 동사원형인 'add'로 고쳐야 'whether to [carry on ...] or [add ...]'의 구조가 완성됩니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found ⓐ<u>deeper</u> meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce ⓑ<u>lower</u> quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most ⓒ<u>satisfied</u> with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took ⓓ<u>greater</u> satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall. It's essential to experience job satisfaction to ⓔ<u>foster</u> productivity and reach success.
questions.explanation: 사람들이 직업에서 성취감을 느낄 때 더 높은 품질의 일을 하고 더 많은 결과물을 낸다는 내용이므로, lower(더 낮은)를 higher(더 높은)와 같은 단어로 바꾸어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to __________ detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street -  motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 처리(process)하는 능력에 미치는 영향을 설명합니다. 인간의 감각은 걷는 속도에 맞추어져 있으며, 그 속도에서 환경의 세부 사항을 잘 인식하고 '구별(distinguish)'할 수 있도록 진화했다는 흐름이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 구별하다
② 결합하다
③ 간과하다
④ 혼동하다
⑤ 무시하다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr, Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the ′curse of knowledge′. Dr, Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students′ eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students ′should be′ learning.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'로, 전문가가 초보자에게 어떤 것을 가르치거나 소개할 때 그 난이도를 과소평가하여 겪는 어려움을 다루고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓑ 문장은 휴대폰이 지식에 대한 즉각적인 접근을 제공하여 학습 능력을 향상시킨다는 내용으로, 글의 주제인 전문가와 초보자 사이의 인지적 격차와는 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question "How many senses are there"? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(B) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.

(C) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.
questions.explanation: 제시된 글은 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각을 5가지로 정의했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C)에서 'However'를 통해 이 주장에 의구심을 제기하며 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 인간의 감각(고유 감각, 평형 감각)을 언급합니다. 이어지는 (A)에서는 'Other animals'를 통해 인간뿐만 아니라 다른 동물의 감각(후각 시스템, 열 감지)으로 범위를 확장합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 예시들을 종합하며 감각을 제한된 수로 명확히 나눌 수 없다는 결론을 내리는 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.*therapy: 치료 **efficacy: 효능
questions.summary_sentence: Group music therapy, including singing, (A)__________ the quality of life and mental wellbeing for individuals with severe mental illness, with (B)__________ participation correlating with greater benefits.
questions.explanation: 본문은 음악 치료와 합창단 참여가 정신 질환자의 삶의 질과 정신적 웰빙을 '개선(improved)'시켰다고 설명하며, 더 많은 세션에 참여할수록 혜택이 컸다고 언급하므로 참여가 '증가(increased)'할수록 이득이 커진다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 개선된 - 증가된
② 우울하게 된 - 제한된
③ 손상된 - 감소된
④ 손상된 - 증가된
⑤ 개선된 - 감소된

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
options: ① The human being needs to work in harmony.
② Action is the most crucial for a sustainable future.
③ Every thought will be completed after finishing tasks.
④ A physical existence comes from each idea in the mind.
⑤ Analyze every creative idea in detail to make it come true.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우리가 살고 있는 집, 차, 옷 등 모든 물리적 실체들이 시작되기 전 마음속 아이디어에서 먼저 완성되었다는 점을 강조합니다. 인간의 미래 설계도 이와 마찬가지로 마음속에서 완성된 비전이 조화를 이루어 현실로 나타난다는 내용이므로 요지는 '물리적인 존재는 마음속의 각 아이디어에서 나온다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간은 조화롭게 일할 필요가 있다.
② 지속 가능한 미래를 위해 행동이 가장 중요하다.
③ 모든 생각은 업무를 마친 후에 완료될 것이다.
④ 물리적 존재는 마음속의 각 아이디어에서 나온다.
⑤ 창의적인 아이디어를 실현하기 위해 세부적으로 분석하라.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew larger. Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. ⓐWhile some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. ⓑAfter farmers decided what to grow, they sowed seeds in the soil and used natural fertilizers to nourish the soil. ⓒVillage dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster. ⓓFor example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. ⓔBy working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 농경의 시작으로 정착 생활을 하게 되면서 공동체 내에서 업무 분담(분업)이 효율적으로 이루어졌다는 내용입니다. ⓑ번 문장은 농부들이 작물을 심고 비료를 주는 구체적인 농사 방법론을 설명하고 있어, 공동체의 효율적인 분업이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession have instant credibility with others, where people may desire to connect with them because of their excellence in their career. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. ⓐWhen they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill is not related to the advice they give. ⓑThink about a world-famous basketball player who has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. ⓒBecause he is an expert on the products he endorses, we should pay attention to him. ⓓPeople listen to him because of what he can do in the baseball court and the same can be applied to an actor who tells us to drive a certain car. ⓔWe choose the car not because of his technical skills about machines but his expertise on his profession.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 특정 분야의 전문성이 그와 무관한 다른 영역에서도 신뢰를 얻게 만든다는 '후광 효과'에 관한 것입니다. ⓒ번은 그가 홍보하는 제품의 전문가이기 때문에 주목해야 한다는 내용으로, 전문성과 상관없는 분야에서도 영향력을 발휘한다는 전체 논지와 반대됩니다. (참고: 지문의 baseball court는 원문상 basketball court의 오타로 보이나 흐름 판단에는 지장이 없습니다.)

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
options: ① Similarity of a City and a Brain; All Interacted
② Interaction: A Key to Success in an Active Social Life
③ Various Elements of Organisms Operating in Isolation
④ How to Build an Effective System for Local Community
⑤ Don't Be Afraid of Asking Questions about the Economy
questions.explanation: 이 글은 뇌의 작동 방식을 도시의 경제 시스템에 비유하여, 뇌의 기능이 어느 한 특정 부위에서 일어나는 것이 아니라 도시처럼 여러 요소들의 상호작용을 통해 발생한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '도시와 뇌의 유사성: 모든 것은 상호작용한다'는 내용의 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 도시와 뇌의 유사성; 모든 것이 상호작용함
② 상호작용: 활발한 사회 생활 성공의 열쇠
③ 고립되어 작동하는 유기체의 다양한 요소들
④ 지역 사회를 위한 효율적인 시스템 구축 방법
⑤ 경제에 관해 질문하는 것을 두려워하지 마라

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies ⓐ<u>became</u> more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This made business ⓑ<u>develop</u> closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn forced business to realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products ⓒ<u>what</u> customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution ⓓ<u>destroying</u> the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, ⓔ<u>became</u> the focus of business.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에ᄉ서 products라는 선행사가 존재하므로, 선행사림 포함하는 관계대명사 what은 올바리 않다. 선행사 products림 수식하는 목적격 관계대명사 which 또는 that으로 고쳐야 한다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, it's inappropriate for us to ⓐ<u>label</u> the foods as either good or bad. ⓑ<u>What</u> the diet is composed of plays a significant role. There are combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't provide her ⓒ<u>with</u> a wide enough variety of the nutrients she needs.
