Or take the case of the teenager who is an ⓓ<u>occasional</u> eater of fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and ⓔ<u>drink</u> supersized cups of coke, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 속한 문장의 주어는 the person이다. 관계대명사 who 절 내에ᄉ서 eats와 drink가 병렬 구조림 이루고 읈으므로, 주어인 단수 명사 the person에 수 일치림 시켐 drinks로 고쳐야 한다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: __________________________________. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① different sports share a common regulation
③ several sports have been modified for juniors
④ young children participate more in adult sports
⑤ children adapt to new rules more easily than adults
questions.explanation: 성인용 경기장이나 장비가 아이들에게 너무 크고 무겁기 때문에, 여러 스포츠들이 아이들의 수준에 맞춰(T볼, 작은 축구공 등) 수정되었다는 내용이 이어지고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '여러 스포츠가 주니어를 위해 수정되어 왔다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 서로 다른 스포츠들이 공통된 규정을 공유한다
② 경쟁 구조가 점진적으로 발전한다
③ 몇몇 스포츠들이 주니어를 위해 수정되었다
④ 어린 아이들이 성인 스포츠에 더 많이 참여한다
⑤ 아이들이 성인보다 새로운 규칙에 더 쉽게 적응한다

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation involves growing various plants in a set order on the same land. Suppose a farmer wants to boost sugar cane growth. Since this plant uses a lot of nitrogen and beans add nitrogen to the soil, the farmer may grow beans after the sugar cane harvest to improve soil nutrient balance and fertility. There are numerous ecological and economic benefits of using crop rotation. In a more specific sense, it aids in long-term soil and farm management. Different plant species interact with soil nutrients in particular ways, releasing and absorbing specific nutrient elements in unique proportions. Therefore, a well-planned rotation strategy helps to _________________________ by either restoring depleted nutrients or using excess nutrients, balancing the soil's nutrient levels.*sugar cane 사탕수수 **nitrogen 질소***fertility (토지가) 비옥함 ****deplete (자원 따위를)고갈시키다
options: ① keep the soil dry out
③ remove nitrogen from the soil
④ grow various plants at random
⑤ make the soil fertile and enriched
questions.explanation: 윤작(Crop rotation)을 통해 토양의 영양분 균형을 맞추고 비옥도를 높인다는 내용이므로, 빈칸에는 '토양을 비옥하고 풍요롭게 만든다'는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 토양을 계속 메마르게 한다
② 인공 비료를 사용한다
③ 토양에서 질소를 제거한다
④ 다양한 식물을 무작위로 기른다
⑤ 토양을 비옥하고 풍요롭게 만든다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Long ago, while receiving a spiritual vision high on a mountain, an old Native American leader Odawa met Iktomi, a great spirit who also held great wisdom. (A) Appearing to the leader in the form of a spider, Iktomi told the aged leader a story about forces. (B) The story was that there were many forces, both bright and dark, and people needed something to catch the bright forces and avoid the dark ones. (C) While making a circle-shaped object with a willow hoop and a spider web, calling it a dream catcher, Iktomi explained what each element and design of it meant. (D) After delivering the meaning of the design, Iktomi told the old man to make dream catchers for his people so they could protect themselves and achieve a bright future. (E) The old man went back to his village to share both Iktomi's lesson and the dream catchers with his people.
questions.insertion_sentence: The hoop represented a perfect circle of life with a hole in the center, and the layering of the web, patterned after a spider's web, meant to catch the bright forces while passing through the bad.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 드림캐처의 고리(hoop)와 그물(web)이 상징하는 구체적인 의미를 설명하고 있습니다. 지문 (C)에서 Iktomi가 드림캐처를 만들며 각 요소의 의미를 설명했다는 내용이 나오고, (D) 다음 문장에서 "디자인의 의미를 전달한 후에(After delivering the meaning of the design)"라는 표현이 등장하므로, 디자인의 구체적 의미를 담은 주어진 문장은 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be heard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying. But it's understandable to not always feel energized by work, of course.
ordered_passages: (A) For people who don't feel energized by work, being an adult at work today is like being a kid at a school without art, gym, and recess - no fun. And, that's a huge reason why they are disconnected, bored, and disengaged.
(B) Moreover, employees who are happier than average earn more money. In other words, happiness at work increases not only business ability but also the amount of income they gain.

(C) Unlike them, when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Research shows that employees who are happiest at work are considered to be the most efficient and display the highest levels of performance.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 의미 있는 일의 중요성을 언급하며, 일에서 항상 활력을 느끼기는 어렵다는 점을 제시합니다. (A)는 일에서 활력을 느끼지 못하는 사람들이 겪는 부정적인 상황(지루함, 단절)을 학교 생활에 비유하여 설명합니다. (C)는 'Unlike them(그들과 달리)'을 통해 (A)의 사례와 대조되는, 일에서 충만함을 느끼는 사람들이 더 높은 성과와 수입을 얻는다는 긍정적인 측면을 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (B)는 'Moreover(게다가)'를 사용해 (C)에서 언급된 경제적 이득에 대한 내용을 보완하며 글을 마무리합니다. 따라서 적절한 순서는 (A)-(C)-(B)입니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the mental grooves and channels set이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, <u>the mental grooves and channels set</u>." The decline in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.
options: ① the size of the brain increases as the infant grows
② children become curios by disconnecting neurons
③ the system in the infant brain is so complex that the child has lots of curiosity
④ infants solidify their knowledge of the world through the development of the brain
⑤ the neural information processing system is simplified, which allows infants to respond faster
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성인이 되면서 호기심이 줄어들고 뇌의 배선이 정리되는 과정을 설명합니다. 아기일 때는 뇌의 연결망이 무질서하고 풍부하지만, 세상을 경험하며 특정 가능성이 지식이나 믿음으로 굳어지면서 신경 경로가 고정된다는 내용입니다. 밑줄 친 'the mental grooves and channels set(정신적인 고랑과 경로가 설정된다)'은 뇌 발달 과정을 통해 아이들이 세상에 대한 지식을 확고히 함으로써 사고방식이 고정되는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 유아가 성장함에 따라 뇌의 크기가 증가한다
② 아이들은 뉴런을 끊음으로써 호기심이 많아진다
③ 유아 뇌의 시스템은 너무 복잡해서 아이가 많은 호기심을 갖는다
④ 유아는 뇌의 발달을 통해 세상에 대한 지식을 공고히 한다
⑤ 신경 정보 처리 시스템이 단순화되어 유아가 더 빠르게 반응할 수 있게 해준다

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
questions.summary_sentence: Tourism expansion (A)______________ an overall development of our society and the advancement of (B)_____________ triggered by the Industrial Revolution.
questions.explanation: 지문은 산업 혁명으로 인한 전반적인 사회 경제적 상황의 개선(임금 상승, 노동 조건 개선, 시간적 여유)과 교통 수단(철도, 항공 등)의 발달이 관광업의 성장을 이끌었다고 설명합니다. 따라서 관광의 확장(Tourism expansion)은 사회의 전반적 발전과 교통(transportation)의 진보로부터 기인한 것이므로 (A)에는 'resulted from', (B)에는 'transportation'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) ~에서 기인했다 (B) 교통
② (A) ~를 이끌었다 (B) 항공 산업
③ (A) ~에서 나타났다 (B) 보건 의료
④ (A) 유발했다 (B) 증기 기관
⑤ (A) 초래했다 (B) 건축

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 활용하여 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that (A)__________________, but rather that (B)___________________.
subjective_conditions: 어법과 문맥에 맞게 작성할 것
<보기>에 주어진 어구를 모두 사용할 것(중복 사용 가능함)
<보기>에 주어진 어구는 어형 변화 없음
단어 추가 없음
vocabulary_box: at the tip of tongue / perceive / you / sweetness / first
questions.answer: (A) you perceive sweetness at the tip of tongue(B) you perceive sweetness first
questions.explanation: 혀의 특정 부위에서 특정 맛을 느낀다는 '혀 지도'는 잘못된 것이며, 실제로는 모든 부위에서 모든 맛을 느낄 수 있지만 맛이 느껴지는 '강도'나 '시간'에 차이가 있다는 내용입니다. 마지막 문장은 '혀 끝에서 단맛을 지각하는 것이 아니라, 단맛을 가장 먼저 지각하는 것'이라는 맥락이 되어야 하므로 'It's not that you perceive sweetness at the tip of tongue, but rather that you perceive sweetness first'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 활용하여 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, to consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales; the agency tried to _____________________________. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped increase sales.
subjective_conditions: 어법과 문맥에 맞게 작성할 것
<보기>에 주어진 어구를 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
<보기>에 주어진 어구는 어형 변화 있음
단어 추가 없음
vocabulary_box: of function / by / about yeast / adapt / on / its claim / the diversification / focus
questions.answer: adapt its claim about yeast by focusing on the diversification of function
questions.explanation: 광고주들이 상품의 시장 상황에 맞춰 주장을 조정한다는 내용입니다. 빵 재료로 쓰이던 효모의 수요가 줄자, 광고 대행사는 효모의 '기능 다각화'에 집중함으로써 효모에 대한 주장을 바꿈으로써 판매를 증진시키려 했습니다. 따라서 'adapt its claim about yeast by focusing on the diversification of function'이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 활용하여 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that ______________________.
subjective_conditions: 답안을 문맥에 맞게 작성할 것
<보기>에 주어진 어구들을 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
<보기>에 주어진 어구는 어형 변화 없이 사용할 것
단어 추가는 하지 않을 것
questions.answer: Prior information of the lecturer influences students' impressions and behavior they form
questions.explanation: 강사에 대한 사전 정보가 학생들이 형성하는 인상과 행동에 영향을 미친다는 내용입니다. 따라서 'prior information of the lecturer'가 주어가 되어 'influences'(단수 동사)로 연결되어 학생들이 형성하는 인상과 행동을 수식하는 구조가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 활용하여 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: 'here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place.' Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster - in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place. The Red Queen Effect means that __________________________________________ in a changing environment, where their enemies and competitors are also evolving.
subjective_conditions: 답안을 문맥에 맞게 작성할 것
<보기>에 주어진 어구들을 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
<보기>에 주어진 어구는 어형 변화 없이 사용할 것
단어 추가는 하지 않을 것
questions.answer: all animals should constantly evolve to survive
questions.explanation: 본문은 붉은 여왕과 토끼의 예시를 통해 포식자와 피식자가 모두 진화하여 제자리걸음을 하는 '붉은 여왕 효과'를 설명하고 있습니다. 결국 'all animals'(모든 동물은) 'should constantly evolve'(계속해서 진화해야만 한다) 'to survive'(생존하기 위해)라는 내용이 들어가야 하므로, 이를 연결한 문장이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 안내문을 읽고 John과 Sora의 대화문을 완성하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 단어를 안내문에서 찾아 어형 변화 없이 그대로 쓰시오. (단, (A)~(C)는 각 한 단어로 작성할 것)
questions.passage:
<안내문>
Spring Field Trip for Freshmen
Join us for a delightful Spring Field Trip, where you'll experience various activities.

Activity Schedule of Your Choice
- Monday: Upcycling Contest or Tea Class
- Tuesday: Mountain Hiking or Museum Visit

Participants Requirement
- Bring used clothes for an upcycling contest.
- Wear a hat if you have an allergy to the sun.

Note
- Video show: The video filmed by freshmen will be posted on our school website on April 30.

<대화문>
John: Have you noticed the poster about a spring field trip?
Sora: Oh, yes. Freshmen will have a chance to experience various activities.
John: Right. We can choose an (A) ________ contest on Monday or mountain hiking on Tuesday.
Sora: Cool. I want to participate in the contest. So I'll bring some used ones.
John: Good. By the way, the poster says you should wear a hat if you have an (B) ________ to the sun.
Sora: Okay. I'll keep that in mind. Do you know where the video filmed by freshmen will be shown?
John: Yes. It will be (C) ________ on our school website on April 30.
Sora: Thanks for letting me know.
subjective_conditions: 1. (A)~(C)는 안내문 내에서 각각 한 단어로 작성할 것
2. 어형 변화 없이 본문의 단어를 그대로 쓸 것
questions.explanation:
안내문의 세부 내용을 대화문과 대조하여 빈칸을 완성하는 문제입니다.
(A): 월요일 활동 내용 중 대화문의 'contest' 앞에 수식어로 들어갈 단어는 'Upcycling'입니다.
(B): 햇빛에 반응하여 모자를 써야 하는 이유로 안내문에 명시된 단어는 'allergy'입니다.
(C): 영상이 학교 웹사이트에 게시되는 상황이므로 안내문의 문구인 'will be posted'에서 'posted'를 추출합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition.
options: ① Blindness Caused by Environmental Pollution
② Perceptual Disengagement: A Vital Component of Sleep
③ Perceptual Disengagement That Shouldn't Occur
④ Sleep: The Privilege of Mammals
⑤ Deep Sleep Enhancing Sensitivity to Stimuli
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잠을 자는 동안 외부 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않는 현상인 '지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 지각적 이탈은 자극을 처리하지 않음으로써 수면을 보호하는 기능을 하며, 수면의 정의에 있어 필수적인 요소임을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로는 '지각적 이탈: 수면의 필수적인 구성 요소'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 환경 오염으로 인한 실명
② 지각적 이탈: 수면의 필수적인 구성 요소
③ 발생해서는 안 되는 지각적 이탈
④ 수면: 포유류의 특권
⑤ 자극에 대한 민감도를 높이는 깊은 수면

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① 행복은 작은 일에서도 느낄 수 있다.
② 인간은 끊임없이 의미 있는 일을 찾는 본성을 가지고 있다.
③ 더 높은 수입을 얻게 될수록 직업에 대한 만족감이 커진다.
④ 모든 직업에서 만족감을 느낄 수는 없지만 사명감을 가져야 한다.
⑤ 의미있는 일은 인간에게 중요하고, 자신의 일에 만족하는 사람이 행복감을 느낀다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간에게 '의미 있는 일(meaningful work)'이 얼마나 중요한지를 강조하고 있습니다. 직업에서 성취감과 의미를 찾는 사람들이 더 활기차고 만족스러운 삶을 살며, 높은 성과와 수입뿐만 아니라 전반적인 삶의 행복도 또한 훨씬 높다는 연구 결과들을 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 요지는 ⑤번입니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experiences weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ① Group music therapy and singing in a choir significantly worsen the emotional states of individuals with severe mental illness.
② Group music therapy primarily focuses on enhancing self-confidence, whereas the effects of choir activities are less clear.
③ Music therapy and choir participation mainly provide a sense of belonging and enjoyment, but have little impact on mental health improvement.
questions.explanation: 제시된 지문은 그룹 음악 치료와 합창단 활동이 정신 질환을 앓고 있는 사람들의 삶의 질과 정신 건강을 향상시킨다는 연구 결과를 다루고 있습니다. (본래 5지선다형 문제이나 텍스트가 잘려 있어 제공된 보기 중 가장 적절한 흐름을 유추하여 해석함. 원문 요지는 '음악 치료와 그룹 노래 부르기가 정신 건강에 긍정적인 영향을 준다'는 내용임)
options_translation: ① 집단 음악 치료와 합창단에서의 노래 부르기는 중증 정신 질환자들의 정서 상태를 상당히 악화시킨다.
② 집단 음악 치료는 주로 자신감 향상에 초점을 맞추는 반면, 합창 활동의 효과는 덜 분명하다.
③ 음악 치료와 합창 참여는 주로 소속감과 즐거움을 제공하지만, 정신 건강 개선에는 거의 영향이 없다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons ①<u>to doubt</u> it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which ②<u>have</u> links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses ③<u>that</u> are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us ④<u>that</u> -senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds,- Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for ⑤<u>what</u> they are.
questions.explanation: ②번인 'the sense of balance which have' 부분에서 주격 관계대명사 which의 선행사는 단수 명사구인 '평형 감각(the sense of balance)'입니다. 따라서 관계대명사절 내의 동사는 복수형인 have가 아니라 단수 형태인 has가 되어야 어법상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas ①<u>where</u> certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the top, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated ②<u>that</u> the -tongue map- explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research ③<u>conducted</u> in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, ④<u>leading</u> taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not ⑤<u>what</u> you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.explanation: 마지막 문장은 'It is not that ~ but rather that ~' 구문으로, 'A가 아니라 B다'라는 의미를 나타냅니다. ⑤번의 what은 뒤에 불완전한 절이 올 때 사용하지만, 해당 절은 주어(you), 동사(taste), 목적어(sweetness)를 모두 갖춘 완전한 문장이므로 명사절 접속사인 that으로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 곳이 있는 것은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. ⓐ<u>If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it</u>. ⓑ<u>You may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it</u>. The danger is that one day you look around and realize ⓒ<u>you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air</u>; ⓓ<u>the sides of the rut have become so slipperily that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out</u>; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. ⓔ<u>The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure</u>, or even well-paying - but ultimately unsatisfying-job.
questions.explanation: ⓓ에서 'so ~ that ...' 구문이 쓰였는데, 'become'은 이형식 동사로 뒤에 형용사 보어를 취해야 합니다. 따라서 부사 'slipperily'를 형용사인 'slippery'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 것을 가장 잘 나타낸 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made <u>adaptations for children</u>. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adjustments are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: 지문은 아이들이 성인용 경기 환경에서 운동하는 것의 어려움을 해결하기 위해, 아이들의 연령과 신체 조건에 맞춰 경기장 크기, 장비 무게, 경기 시간 등을 조정한 사례들을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 'adaptations for children'은 아이들의 연령에 특화된 수정을 의미하는 'Age-specific modifications'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 넓은 경기 구역
② 강화된 안전 조치
③ 증가된 경쟁 수준
④ 연령별 맞춤 수정
⑤ 고급 기술 요구 사항

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
options: ① The subconscious mind processes emotions quickly and effectively.
② Memories and recognition are functions primarily associated with the conscious mind.
③ The conscious mind allows greater control and decision-making capabilities.
④ Emotions do not affect the decision-making process.
⑤ Initial reaction of fears of spiders and the dark occurs in the subconscious mind.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over'라고 언급하며, 의식적인 마음이 우리가 더 많이 통제할 수 있는 부분이며 사고를 이어가거나 감정을 더하는 등의 결정을 내리는 부분임을 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 잠재의식은 감정을 빠르고 효과적으로 처리한다.
② 기억과 인식은 주로 의식적인 마음과 연관된 기능이다.
③ 의식적인 마음은 더 큰 통제력과 의사결정 능력을 가능하게 한다.
④ 감정은 의사결정 과정에 영향을 미치지 않는다.
⑤ 거미와 어둠에 대한 공포의 초기 반응은 잠재의식에서 발생한다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. (A) This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. (B) When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. (C) Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. (D) A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. (E) They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.insertion_sentence: On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '반면에(On the other hand)'로 시작하며 다문화가 국가 정체성의 왜곡으로 인식될 때 부정적인 특징으로 보일 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (D) 다음 문장까지는 다문화 도시의 긍정적인 가치에 대해 설명하고 있으며, (E) 뒤의 문장은 '그들이 다른 인종 집단을 차별할 수도 있고 갈등을 두려워할 수도 있다'는 부정적인 반응을 설명하므로, 긍정에서 부정으로 전환되는 지점인 (E)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 34. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)를 주어진 <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 문맥에 맞도록 완성하시오. (필요시 어형변화 할 것) [23년 9월 20번]
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to (A)____________________________. Remember that children do not learn the values (B)___________________________. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore show your child good examples of life by your action. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용
필요시 어형변화 할 것
vocabulary_box: <보기 (A)> tempt / other roads / take / when / look / the high road
<보기 (B)> strong character / about them / that / be told / make up / simply by
questions.answer: (A) take the high road when other roads look tempting(B) that make up strong character simply by being told about them
questions.explanation: (A) '다른 길이 유혹적으로 보일 때 올바른 길을 택하다'라는 의미로 구성해야 하므로 'take the high road when other roads look tempting'이 적절하다.(B) '단지 그것들에 대해 들음으로써 강한 인격을 형성하는 가치'를 아이들이 배우지 않는다는 내용이므로, values를 수식하는 관계대명사절을 사용하여 'that make up strong character simply by being told about them'으로 완성한다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 흐름상 밑줄 친 (A)에 각각 들어갈 가장 적절한 표현을 영어로 쓰시오. (단, 형태 변형 없이 보기의 표현만을 모두 사용해 완성하시오.)
questions.passage: Success can (A)________________________________________ a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become So slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying - but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
subjective_conditions: 형태 변형 없이 보기의 표현만을 모두 사용해 완성하시오.
vocabulary_box: path / you / lead / intended / into / off / and / your
questions.answer: lead you off your intended path and into
questions.explanation: 'lead + 목적어(you) + off (장소1) + and into (장소2)'의 구조를 사용하여 '당신을 의도한 길에서 벗어나 편안한 타성으로 이끌 수 있다'는 의미를 완성합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 (A)~(D)를 읽고, 흐름상 이어질 글의 순서를 차례대로 바르게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: On a two-week trip in the Rocky Mountains, I saw a grizzly bear in its native habitat. At first, I felt joy as I watched the bear walk across the land.
ordered_passages: (A) He stopped every once in a while to turn his head about, sniffing deeply.
(B) This was no longer a wonderful experience; it was now an issue of survival. The bear's motivation was to find meat to eat, and I was clearly on his menu.
(C) [See initial passage content provided in the question logic]
(D) He was following the scent of something, and slowly I began to realize that this giant animal was smelling me! I froze.
questions.explanation: 제시문(C)에서 곰을 보고 기쁨을 느낀 상황이 먼저 나오고, (A)에서 곰이 멈춰 서서 냄새를 맡는 구체적인 행동이 이어집니다. (D)에서 그 곰이 내 냄새를 맡고 있다는 것을 깨닫고 얼어붙는 긴장 상황이 발생하며, (B)에서 이것이 더 이상 즐거운 경험이 아니라 생존의 문제임을 깨닫는 결말로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: To whom it may ⓐ<u>concern</u>, I am a resident of the Blue Sky Apartment. Recently I observed that the kid zone is in need of repairs. I want you to pay attention to the ⓑ<u>poor</u> condition of the playground equipment in the zone. The swings are damaged, the paint is falling off, and some of the bolts on the slide are ⓒ<u>unable</u> to be found. The ⓓ<u>facilities</u> have been in this terrible condition since we moved here. They are dangerous to the children playing there. Would you please have them repaired? I would be ⓔ<u>ungrateful</u> for your immediate attention to solve this matter.Yours sincerely,Nina Davis
questions.explanation: 편지글의 마무리에서 빠른 조치에 대해 감사할 것이라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 '감사하지 않는'이라는 뜻의 'ungrateful'은 문맥상 틀린 단어입니다. 'grateful'(감사하는)로 고쳐야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 관계자(에게)
② 열악한
③ 할 수 없는(발견될 수 없는)
④ 시설물
⑤ 감사하지 않는

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s</u>. ⓑ<u>This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price</u>. ⓒ<u>In fact, it was equally essential that business deliver that customers actually wanted</u>. ⓓ<u>Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible</u>. ⓔ<u>The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand</u>. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
questions.explanation: ⓒ에서 'deliver'의 목적어 역할을 하면서 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사가 필요하므로, 접속사나 지시사인 that이 아니라 what으로 바꾸어야 합니다. (deliver what customers actually wanted: 고객들이 실제로 원했던 것을 전달하다)

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 technology에 대한 글쓴이의 태도로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt <u>technology</u>, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk - for body and mind.
questions.explanation: 필자는 기술을 채택할 때 지불해야 하는 '비용(대가)'을 강조하며, 전통적인 생계 수단의 상실, 싫어하는 일 수행, 육체적 고통 및 질병, 디지털 업무로 인한 정신적 스트레스와 건강 위험 등을 열거하고 있습니다. 따라서 기술의 부정적인 측면을 비판적으로 보고 있는 'cynical(냉소적인, 비판적인)'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 불분명한
② 냉소적인
③ 어리둥절한
④ 만족해하는
⑤ 우호적인

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 밑줄 친 the rubber-stamp approach와 문맥상 같은 의미를 갖는 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "<u>the rubber-stamp approach</u>." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's ⓐ<u>appropriate dress</u> for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that ⓑ<u>putting on the same clothes</u> won't work for every class. They are ⓒ<u>flexible learners</u>. They have ⓓ<u>different strategies</u> and know when to use them. They know that you use ⓔ<u>suitable approaches</u> for multiple-choice tests differently from you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
questions.explanation: 'the rubber-stamp approach'는 모든 상황에 똑같은 방식을 적용하는 것을 의미합니다. 본문에서 비유적으로 표현된 ⓑ 'putting on the same clothes(똑같은 옷을 입는 것)'가 상황에 관계없이 일률적인 방식을 사용하는 것과 상응하는 의미를 갖습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with human like facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
options: ① Uncommon Features Found in Animal Movies
② Humanization: How Animals are Portrayed in Animation
③ Noticeable Human Characteristics in the Animal Kingdom
④ Animated Movies: The Projection of Human Society
⑤ Disneyfication: The Standard of Animated Movies
questions.explanation: 본문은 애니메이션 캐릭터나 장난감 속의 동물이 인간처럼 말하고, 인간의 이목구비를 닮거나 앞발을 손처럼 사용하는 등 인간화(humanization)되는 방식과 그 전략에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ② '인간화: 애니메이션에서 동물이 묘사되는 방식'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 동물 영화에서 발견되는 흔치 않은 특징들
인간화: 애니메이션에서 동물이 묘사되는 방식
동물계에서 눈에 띄는 인간의 특성들
애니메이션 영화: 인간 사회의 투영
디즈니화: 애니메이션 영화의 표준

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to ⓐ<u>overcome</u> jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the ⓑ<u>direction</u> of travel. Generally, it's more easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is ⓒ<u>sizable</u> enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly ⓓ<u>worse</u> than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is ⓔ<u>tougher</u> than westward travel.
questions.explanation: 앞 문장에서 서쪽으로 비행하는 것이 동쪽으로 비행하는 것보다 더 쉽다고 했으므로, 서쪽으로 이동하는 팀이 동쪽으로 이동하는 팀보다 '더 나쁜(worse)' 성적을 낸다는 것은 문맥상 맞지 않습니다. 'better'와 같은 단어로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us ⓐ<u>was finished</u> in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea. Each idea ⓑ<u>was then studied</u>, refined and perfected before the first nail ⓒ<u>was driven</u> or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea ⓓ<u>was turned into</u> a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being ⓔ<u>is designed</u> his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'The human being'이고, 뒤에 'his or her own future'라는 목적어가 나오므로 수동태 'is designed'가 아닌 능동태 'designs'가 되어야 합니다. 인간은 같은 과정을 통해 자신의 미래를 설계한다는 능동의 의미가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the ①<u>speed</u> at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally ②<u>suited</u> to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has ③<u>little</u> time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the ④<u>appreciation</u> of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much ⑤<u>faster</u> than that of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: 조깅하는 사람과 자전거를 타는 사람은 보행자(느림)와 운전자(빠름) 사이에 있다고 했으므로, 괴들의 셍도는 일반적인 운전자의 셍도보다 더 ' 느리다'는 내용이 와야 한다. 따라서 faster를 slower로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절하다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 연결어를 고르면? [3.2점]
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. (A)__________, towns and villages grew larger. Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster. (B)__________, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
options: ④ (A) As a result - (B) For example
⑤ (A) As a result - (B) In short
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 사람들이 농사를 짓기 시작하면서 정착했다고 했고, 그 결과로 마을이 커졌다는 내용이 이어지므로 인과관계를 나타내는 'As a result'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞 문장에서 마을 사람들이 더 빨리 일을 하기 위해 협력하는 법을 배웠다고 설명한 후, 도구 제작자들이 협력하여 도끼를 만드는 구체적인 사례를 들고 있으므로 'For example'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나 - 그러므로
② 그러나 - 예를 들어
③ 그럼에도 불구하고 - 아직
④ 그 결과 - 예를 들어
⑤ 그 결과 - 요약하자면

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind.
ordered_passages: (A) But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
(B) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 수면 중 감각 반응이 정상적이지 않음을 언급했습니다. (B)에서 일부 정보가 들어오긴 하지만 정상적으로 처리되지 않는다는 구체적인 설명을 덧붙입니다. 그 후 (A)에서 이러한 감각 차단이 수면의 정의에 필수적이지만, 많은 동물들이 완전한 차단 대신 졸음 상태를 이용하기도 한다는 내용으로 이어지는 것이 흐름상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸에 알맞은 말을 <보기>에 있는 단어만 사용하여 알맞게 배열하시오.
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all ____________________ at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
vocabulary_box: to / leaders / the potential / have / be
questions.answer: have the potential to be leaders
questions.explanation: 문맥상 '우리 모두는 나이나 경험에 상관없이 리더가 될 수 있는 잠재력을 가지고 있다'는 결론이 도출되어야 하므로, <보기>의 단어들을 활용해 'have the potential to be leaders'로 배열하는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ① 동물 치료는 오랜 시간이 걸리는 장객적인 과정이다.
② 동물 치료에서 환경적인 요소는 크게 중요하지 않다.
③ 동물을 치료할 때는 여러 가지 요소를 고려해야 한다.
④ 동물 보호 센터는 동물의 자연 습성을 유지하는 데 초점을 둔다.
⑤ 야생 환경의 동물과 가정집 환경의 동물은 다른 행동 특성을 지닌다.
questions.explanation: 글의 하반부에서 '모든 치유 세션은 다르게 탐색되어야 하며, 각 치료는 동물의 특정 필요에 맞게 조정되어야 한다(each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal)'고 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 동물 치료 시 환경이나 동물의 특성, 환경적 요소, 질환의 성격 등 여러 요소를 고려해야 한다는 ③이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
options: ① 과제의 특성에 맞는 여러 방법을 시도하라.
② 매일 해야 할 일의 목록을 작성하는 습관을 길러라.
③ 자신의 과제 수행 능력에 대해 낙관적으로 생각하라.
④ 중요한 일을 먼저 처리하고 사소한 일은 나중으로 미뤄라.
⑤ 효과적인 과제 수행을 위해서는 과제 소요 시간을 추정하라.
questions.explanation: 필자는 할 일 목록(things to do list)의 각 항목 옆에 필요한 예상 시간을 추정하고 기록하는 습관을 기르라고 조언합니다. 이는 시간에 대해 지나치게 낙관적으로 생각하는 문제점을 해결하고, 가용한 시간 내에 과제를 효율적으로 배치하여 성취감을 얻기 위함이므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 주장입니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 38번]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that ____________________________________. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
options: ① taste are exclusive to their respective areas
② taste buds are grouped according to specialty
③ individual taste qualities are not restricted to a single region of the tongue
④ taste buds allow you to experience tastes that are sweet, salty, bitter, and sour
⑤ some parts of the tongue are slightly more sensitive to certain tastes than others
questions.explanation: 과거의 혀 지도 이론은 잘못된 것이며, 실제로는 입안 어디에서나 모든 맛을 느낄 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 개별적인 맛의 특성이 혀의 단일 영역에 국한되지 않는다는 ③번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 맛은 각각의 해당 영역에 독점적이다
② 맛봉오리는 전문 분야에 따라 그룹화되어 있다
③ 개별적인 맛의 특성은 혀의 단일 영역에 국한되지 않는다
④ 맛봉오리는 당신이 단맛, 짠맛, 쓴맛, 신맛을 경험하게 해준다
⑤ 혀의 어떤 부분은 다른 부분보다 특정 맛에 약간 더 민감하다

questions.question: 6. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 35번]
questions.passage: Whose story it is affects what they story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes? ______________________________________________.
options: ① The story will gain more popularity in the world
② We can come up with a better solution for the conflict
③ It won't have any influence on the understanding of the story
④ We may have different feelings and understanding of the story
⑤ A more perfect understanding of the story will be possible from all angles
questions.explanation: 이야기의 관점이 누구냐에 따라 사건의 해석과 공감이 달라진다는 내용입니다. 신데렐라나 바람과 함께 사라지다의 사례를 통해 시점의 변화가 가져올 차이를 암시하고 있으므로, 이야기에 대해 다른 감정과 이해를 갖게 될 것이라는 ④번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 이야기는 세상에서 더 많은 인기를 얻게 될 것이다
② 우리는 갈등에 대해 더 나은 해결책을 생각해낼 수 있다
③ 그것은 이야기의 이해에 아무런 영향을 미치지 않을 것이다
④ 우리는 이야기에 대해 다른 감정과 이해를 가질 수 있다
⑤ 모든 각도에서 이야기에 대한 더 완벽한 이해가 가능해질 것이다

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. (A) In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. (B) Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. (C) The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. (D) Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites. (E) While they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.insertion_sentence: On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력에 미치는 영향을 설명합니다. (C) 다음 부분은 자동차 운전자의 제한된 세부 사항 파악 능력을 다룹니다. 주어진 문장은 '반면에'라는 연결사를 사용하여 보행자가 환경적 세부 사항을 감상할 수 있다는 점을 대조적으로 보여줍니다. (D)의 'these polar opposites(이러한 양극단)'는 앞서 언급된 운전자와 보행자를 지칭하므로, 보행자에 대한 설명인 주어진 문장은 (D) 위치에 들어가야 합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. (A) For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. (B) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. (C) Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. (D) Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. (E) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it.
questions.explanation: 글의 시작 부분에서 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물에게 5가지 감각이 있다고 기술했다는 내용이 나옵니다. 주어진 문장은 '하지만 피오나 맥퍼슨에 따르면 그것(5가지 감각설)을 의심할 이유가 있다'는 내용으로, 아리스토텔레스의 주장에 반박하는 흐름의 전환점입니다. (A) 이후부터 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 감각들(고유 수용성 감각, 평형 감각 등)에 대한 구체적인 반거가 제시되므로 주어진 문장은 (A)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phone were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
options: ① Why Do People Underestimate Their Abilities?
② E-learning Tips: Creating Tasks for Novice Learners
③ How Long Does It Take to Learn to Use Smart Phones?
④ The Effect of Mobile Phones on Learning and Memory
⑤ Expert Blindness: A Difficulty in Understanding Less-Informed Perspectives
questions.explanation: 전문가들이 자신이 가진 지식 때문에 초보자가 해당 분야를 배울 때 겪는 어려움을 인지하지 못하는 '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)' 현상을 설명하는 글입니다. 전문가들은 기술을 습득할수록 그 기술의 난이도를 과소평가하게 되며, 자신이 배울 때 얼마나 힘들었는지조차 잊어버린다는 연구 결과를 제시합니다. 따라서 제목으로는 '전문가의 맹점: 지식이 적은 관점을 이해하는 것의 어려움'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 왜 사람들은 자신의 능력을 과소평가하는가?
E-러닝 팁: 초보 학습자를 위한 과업 만들기
스마트폰 사용법을 배우는 데 얼마나 걸리는가?
모바일 폰이 학습과 기억에 미치는 영향
전문가의 맹점: 지식이 적은 관점을 이해하는 것의 어려움

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ② What Fossils Can Tell Us
⑤ Transformation of Creatures for Survival
questions.explanation: 지문은 모든 생물종이 기후 변화에 따라 자신이 생존할 수 있는 적절한 환경을 찾아 이동해야 하며, 움직이지 못하는 것처럼 보이는 나무나 따개비조차도 일생의 특정 시기에 분산되어 이동한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '생존을 위한 이동'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 생존을 위해 이동하라
② 화석이 우리에게 말해주는 것
③ 지구의 기후 변화
④ 씨앗이 퍼지는 방법
⑤ 생존을 위한 생명체의 변형

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.summary_sentence: Animal characters and toys (A)_______________ so that they can (B)_______________.
options: ① have humanlike features ... be a friend of humans
② go through little change ... have similarity with humans
③ resemble humans ... be shown in a more natural way
④ are emotionally appealing ... be distinct from humans
⑤ are physically deformed ... look like humans
questions.explanation: 지문은 동물 캐릭터나 장난감이 인간의 언어를 사용하거나, 인간과 닮은 얼굴 특징 및 손처럼 사용하는 앞다리를 가지는 등 신체적으로 변형(deformed)되어 인간처럼 보이도록(look like humans) 만들어진다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. (A)에는 신체적 변형에 대한 내용이, (B)에는 그 결과인 인간을 닮게 된다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간 같은 특징을 가진다 ... 인간의 친구가 된다
② 거의 변화를 겪지 않는다 ... 인간과 유사성을 갖는다
③ 인간을 닮는다 ... 더 자연스러운 방식으로 보여진다
④ 감정적으로 호소력이 있다 ... 인간과 구별된다
⑤ 신체적으로 변형된다 ... 인간처럼 보인다

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would way, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bob Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done." To hear the leaders describe their organizations, it seems they are run more like (A)__________ anarchist associations than (B)__________ institutions.
questions.explanation: 지문은 경영자들이 부하 직원들의 반대 의견과 자유로운 발언을 장려한다고 주장하는 경향을 설명합니다. 따라서 리더들의 설명에 따르면 그들의 조직은 권위주의적인 (B)지시와 통제(command-and-control) 기관보다는 (A)협동적인(cooperative) 무정부주의자 연합처럼 운영되는 것으로 보인다는 흐름이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 협동적인 ... 지시와 통제형의
② 전통적인 ... 혁신적인
③ 수용적인 ... 책임감 있는
④ 상향하명식의 ... 엄격하게 구조화된
⑤ 협업적인 ... 반응하는

questions.question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started.
ordered_passages: (A) The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut.
questions.explanation: 해당 문제는 지문이 (A)에서 끊겨 있어 전체 순서를 파악할 수 없습니다. 따라서 '이미 완성된 온전한 문제'가 아니므로 규칙에 따라 제외하거나 처리해야 하지만, 요청하신 출력 형식에 맞춰 (A) 이후의 내용을 알 수 없으므로 정답 및 해설 생성이 불가능합니다. (단, 주어진 지문 내에서 (A)는 앞선 문장의 예시 역할을 합니다.)

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 this Red Queen Effect가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use <u>this Red Queen Effect</u> to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster - in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
options: ① every species has its natural enemy
② all creatures have to adapt to environmental changes
③ the two opposing species co-evolve to stay in the same place
④ animals have a natural mechanism to prevent them from extinction
⑤ the evolutionary progress of one species results in the extinction of another
questions.explanation: 붉은 여왕 효과(Red Queen Effect)는 여우가 빨라지면 토끼도 생존을 위해 더 빨라져야 하고, 결국 두 종 모두 진화하지만 상대적인 관계에서는 제자리에 머물게 되는 현상을 말합니다. 따라서 이는 두 대립하는 종이 같은 자리에 머물기 위해 함께 공진화한다는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 종은 천적을 가지고 있다
② 모든 생물은 환경 변화에 적응해야 한다
③ 두 대립하는 종이 제자리에 머물기 위해 공진화한다
④ 동물들은 멸종을 방지하기 위한 자연적 기제를 가지고 있다
⑤ 한 종의 진화적 발전이 다른 종의 멸종을 초래한다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally ⓐ<u>blind</u>. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they ⓑ<u>fail</u> to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of ⓒ<u>protecting</u> sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be ⓓ<u>possible</u> without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the ⓔ<u>intermediate</u> state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)이 없으면 수면이 불가능하다는 내용이 뒤의 '필수적(essential)이다'라는 결론과 어울립니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 'possible(가능한)'을 'impossible(불가능한)'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: It is difficult for any of us to maintain a constant level of attention throughout our working day. We all have body rhythms ⓐ<u>characterised</u> by peaks and valleys of energy and alertness. You will achieve more, and feel confident as a benefit, if you schedule your most demanding tasks at times when you are best able to cope with ⓑ<u>it</u>. If you haven't thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to observe ⓒ<u>yourself</u>. Try to note the times ⓓ<u>when</u> you are at your best. We are all different. For some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for ⓔ<u>others</u> it may take a while to warm up.
questions.explanation: ⓑ의 it이 가리키는 대상은 바로 앞의 복수 명사인 'your most demanding tasks'이므로, 단수 대명사 it이 아닌 복수 대명사 them으로 바꿔야 한다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'Skillful learners'의 특징을 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. <u>Skillful learners</u> know that "putting on the same clothes" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
subjective_conditions: 1. 지문의 4단어 이상 연속으로 차용하지 말 것
2. 주어-동사가 있는 문장으로 쓸 것
questions.answer: Skillful learners have different strategies for different tasks and know when they should use them.
questions.explanation: 숙련된 학습자의 특징은 상황에 따라 다른 전략을 가지고 있고 그것을 언제 사용해야 할지 아는 유연한 학습자라는 것입니다. 지문의 문장을 그대로 사용하지 않고 같은 의미를 가진 표현으로 재구성하여 영작합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 주제를 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
subjective_conditions: 1. 지문의 4단어 이상 연속으로 차용하지 말 것
2. 'transport'를 포함할 것
3. 주어-동사가 있는 문장으로 쓸 것
questions.answer: The development of countries and their transport systems caused tourism growth.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 국가의 사회 경제적 상황 개선과 운송 수단의 발달이 관광 산업의 성장을 이끌었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 'transport'를 포함하여 국가의 발전과 운송 시스템의 발달이 관광 성장을 야기했다는 주제문을 영작합니다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 가리키는 내용을 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: (A)<u>The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling</u> came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that ⓐ<u>it</u> was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, ⓑ<u>it</u> was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies ⓒ<u>this</u> was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
subjective_conditions: 1. 지문의 4단어 이상 연속으로 차용하지 말 것
2. (변화 이전) → (변화 이후)를 쓸 것
3. 주어-동사가 있는 문장으로 쓸 것
questions.answer: It was enough for business to produce good products at a good price. → Business had to consider what customers wanted and satisfy their diverse needs.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 (A) '판매 개념의 주요한 철학적 변화'는 과거의 '적절한 가격에 양질의 제품을 생산하는 것만으로 충분했던' 생산 중심의 관점에서, 현대의 '고객이 실제로 원하는 제품을 전달하고 그들의 다양한 요구를 충족시키는 것'을 중시하는 마케팅 중심의 관점으로 변화했음을 의미합니다.

questions.question: 28. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ가 가리키는 것을 지문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

questions.question: 29. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓑ가 가리키는 것을 지문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

questions.answer: to deliver products that customers actually wanted

questions.question: 30. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓒ가 가리키는 것을 지문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
