questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, -I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired.- If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: -I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done.-
options: ① ways to get rid of dissenters from their workplace
② influence of being leader in communication at workplace
③ necessity of installing mic at workplace for warm atmosphere
④ the quality of respectable leader in managing business
⑤ negative effect of featured boss in the business section of newspaper
questions.explanation: 이 글은 존경 네는 경영자들이 반대 의견을 장려하고 하급 직원들의 목소리에 귀 기울이는 것이 중요함을 강조하고 있습니다. 특히 반대자들의 의견을 경청함으로쓰 무언가림 해내기 위해 필요한 것을 발견할 수 있다고 말하고 있으며, 이는 비즈니스 경영에 있어 존경 받는 리댔의 자질에 대한 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 일터에서 반대자들을 제거하는 방법
② 일터 소통에 있어 리댔가 되는 것의 영향
③ 분위기림 따낻하게 하기 위해 일터에 마이크림 설치할 필요성
④ 비즈니스 경영에 있어 존경 받는 리댔의 자질
⑤ 신문 비즈니스 섹션에 등장하는 사장들의 부정적 영향

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." (A) Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. (B) Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. (C) If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. (D) Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 진행 상황을 평가하기 위해 때때로 그림에서 몇 발자국 물러나는 것이 중요하다는 내용입니다. (A) 다음에는 그림을 멈추는 시점을 알기 어렵고 계셍 더하고 싶은 유혹을 받는다는 내용이 옵니다. 제시문은 (A) 뒤, 즉 (B) 자리에 들어가서, 너무 많은 것을 그림에 담아 과하게 그린 것 같아 발이는 부작용을 막기 위해 물러나서 평가하라는 흐름을 만들어 줍니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ⓐ<u>accurate</u> than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓑ<u>insensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓒ<u>underestimate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an ⓓ<u>earlier</u> session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through ⓔ<u>learners' eyes</u>, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 글의 주제는 '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'로, 전문가들이 초보자의 입장을 이해하지 못하고 자신의 숙련도를 기준으로 상황을 판단한다는 내용입니다. ⓐ의 맥락을 보면 전문가들이 초보자보다 학습 소요 시간을 예측하는 데 있어 '덜 정확하거나(less accurate)' 또는 '부정확(inaccurate)'해야 합니다. 이어지는 내용에서 전문가들이 초보자에게 과업이 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 '무감각(insensitive)'해지고 난이도를 '과소평가(underestimate)'한다고 했으므로 ⓐ는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 9. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment.
ordered_passages: (A) On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.

(B) The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little enough time or ability to appreciate design details.

(C) In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력을 결정한다는 내용입니다. (C)에서는 진화론적으로 인간의 감각이 걷는 속도에 최적화되어 있음을 설명하고, (B)에서는 대조적으로 가장 빠른 운전자가 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력이 제한됨을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서는 '반면에(On the other hand)'를 사용하여 다시 보행자의 장점과 그 중간 단계(조깅, 자전거)를 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the tongue map'' explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century, Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
options: ① Bitterness was registered at the back of the mouth.
② Researchers found tastes distribution on the tongue is reliable research.
③ Experts of taste research know that taste organs are not tied.
④ Each taste can be perceived across the whole tongue.
⑤ Misinterpretation of tastes distribution on the tongue has led to misunderstanding among people.
questions.explanation: 본문에 따르면 1980년대와 90년대의 연구 결과, 혀의 부위별 맛 지도는 완전히 틀린 것(totally wrong)으로 밝혀졌습니다. 따라서 혀 위의 맛 분포가 신뢰할 만한 연구라는 ②번의 진술은 본문 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 쓴맛은 입 뒷부분에서 등록되었다.
② 연구원들은 혀 위의 맛 분포가 신뢰할 수 있는 연구라는 것을 발견했다.
③ 맛 연구 전문가들은 맛 기관이 묶여 있지 않다는 것을 안다.
④ 각 맛은 혀 전체에서 인지될 수 있다.
⑤ 혀 위의 맛 분포에 대한 오해는 사람들 사이의 오해를 불러일으켰다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ① The frequency of singing affects the quality of life
② Group singing is essential for psychological research
③ Group music therapy has positive effect on mental health
④ Group activities are needed to improve a sense of belonging
⑤ Singing for individuals turns negative effects into positive ones
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부와 후반부 모두 집단 음악 치료와 집단 합창이 정신 질환을 앓는 사람들의 삶의 질과 정신 건강, 행복감을 향상시킨다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '집단 음악 치료가 정신 건강에 긍정적인 영향을 미친다'는 3번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 노래하는 빈도가 삶의 질에 영향을 미친다.
② 집단 합창은 심리학 연구에 필수적이다.
③ 집단 음악 치료는 정신 건강에 긍정적인 효과가 있다.
④ 소속감을 향상시키기 위해 집단 활동이 필요하다.
⑤ 개인을 위한 노래는 부정적인 영향을 긍정적인 영향으로 바꾼다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 그에서 전체 흠름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. ①Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. ②Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. ③Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. ④People who put a lot of time in their leisure time tend to feel joyful and cheerful. ⑤For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 이 그만 인간에검 있어 '의미 있는 일(직업)'이 삶의 만접도와 행복에 미치는 중요성에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ④번은 여가 시간(leisure time)에 대한 이얼기이므로 전체적인 흠름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds." Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal sense into Aristotelian buckets, we should (A)<u>study them for what they are</u>.
options: ① neglect the way to analyze real senses
② contradict various viewpoints from one another
③ classify many animal senses into fixed categories
④ understand the differences between two opinions
⑤ acknowledge an unrestricted number of senses
questions.explanation: 필자는 감각을 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 5가지와 같은 제한된 범주(buckets)에 억지로 집어넣으려 하지 말고, 감각 그 자체의 모습대로 연구해야 한다고 주장합니다. 이는 감각이 특정 숫자로 명확히 나뉘지 않으며 훨씬 더 다양하고 많은 수의 감각이 존재할 수 있음을 인정하라는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 실제 감각을 분석하는 방법을 소홀히 한다
② 여러 관점을 서로 반박한다
③ 많은 동물의 감각을 고정된 범주로 분류한다
④ 두 의견 사이의 차이점을 이해한다
⑤ 제한되지 않은 수의 감각을 인정한다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.summary_sentence: Crop rotation has benefits when farmers (A)__________ their crops in periodic order to (B)__________ healthy soil.
questions.explanation: 윤작(Crop rotation)은 농부들이 주기적으로 작물을 '변경(alter/switch)'함으로써 토양의 건강을 '유지(maintain/retain)'하는 농법입니다. (A)에는 change의 유의어인 alter가, (B)에는 stays healthy와 일맥상통하는 maintain이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 변경하다 - 유지하다
② 개선하다 - 처리하다
③ 고집하다 - 다루다
④ 보존하다 - 보유하다
⑤ 바꾸다 - 변화시키다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that ⓐ<u>satisfy</u> those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of ⓑ<u>movement</u>. Even creatures that appear ⓒ<u>immobile</u>, like trees and barnacles, are capable of ⓓ<u>gathering</u> at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and ⓔ<u>reproduce</u>. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 나무나 따개비처럼 움직이지 못해 보이는 생물들도 생애 어느 단계(씨앗이나 유생 단계)에서는 '이동(dispersal/moving)'할 수 있다는 내용이 되어야 합니다. gathering(모으기, 채집)은 문맥상 어울리지 않습니다.

questions.question: 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.summary_sentence: Crop rotation has benefits when farmers (A)__________ their crops in periodic order to (B)__________ healthy soil.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 윤작(crop rotation)의 개념과 그 이점에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 농부들이 정해진 순서에 따라 작물을 바꾸어 심음으로써 토양을 건강하게 유지한다는 내용이 핵심입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '바꾸다'의 의미인 alter가, (B)에는 '유지하다'의 의미인 maintain이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 바꾸다 --- 유지하다
② 개선하다 --- 가공하다
③ 고집하다 --- 다루다
④ 보존하다 --- 보유하다
⑤ 바꾸다 --- 변화시키다

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animals. You will learn as you go: _________________________________________.
options: ① healing is a continuous learning process
② every animal has a similar characteristic
③ animals are affected by the specific environment
④ treatment should apply equally to all animals
⑤ emotional therapy is more important than physical therapy
questions.explanation: 동물마다 개별적 특성, 환경, 증상에 따라 치유 반응이 다르므로 매 회기마다 다르게 탐구되고 개별 요구에 맞춰 조정되어야 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 치유는 진행하면서 계속 배워나가는 과정이라는 의미의 'healing is a continuous learning process'가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 치유는 지속적인 학습 과정이다
② 모든 동물은 유사한 특징을 가지고 있다
③ 동물들은 특정 환경에 영향을 받는다
④ 치료는 모든 동물에게 동일하게 적용되어야 한다
⑤ 정서적 치료가 신체적 치료보다 더 중요하다

questions.question: 23. 다음 빈칸을 조건에 맞게 영어로 답하시오.
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by (A)__________ them with others. (B)__________ their opinions and feedback and constantly (C)__________ the bes way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age of experience.
subjective_conditions: 리더의 자질로서 3가지에 해당합니다.
(A): 1단어
(B): 1단어
(C): 2단어
questions.explanation: 문맥상 훌륭한 리더들이 아이디어를 발전시킨 방식에 대한 설명입니다. (A)는 타인과 아이디어를 '공유함(sharing)'으로써, (B)는 의견과 피드백을 '구함(seeking)'으로써, (C)는 집단의 목표를 달성할 최선의 방법을 '찾음(looking for)'으로써 아이디어를 개선했다는 흐름이 적절합니다. 전치사 by에 걸리는 병렬 구조이므로 모두 동명사 형태가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① People who feel satisfied with their jobs make happier lives.
② A job with high satisfaction is a job with a high salary.
③ Quantity is more important than quality in a job.
④ The better the job, the higher the satisfaction.
⑤ Happy people are able to have better jobs.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 직업에서 성취감과 의미를 찾는 사람들이 업무 효율이 높을 뿐만 아니라 전반적인 삶의 행복도도 훨씬 높다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '직업에 만족하는 사람들이 더 행복한 삶을 만든다'는 ①번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 직업에 만족감을 느끼는 사람들은 더 행복한 삶을 만든다.
② 만족도가 높은 직업이 높은 연봉을 받는 직업이다.
③ 직업에서 양이 질보다 더 중요하다.
④ 직업이 좋을수록 만족도가 더 높다.
⑤ 행복한 사람들은 더 좋은 직업을 가질 수 있다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어가기에 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become (A)__________ to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants (B)__________ how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 '지식의 저주' 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 전문가들은 초보자에게 어떤 과업이 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 (A)무감각(insensitive)해지는 경향이 있습니다. 또한, 기술을 습득함에 따라 전문가들은 자신이 그 기술을 배우는 데 걸린 시간을 (B)과소평가(underestimated)하기 시작한다는 연구 결과를 보여줍니다. 따라서 정답은 4번입니다.
options_translation: ① 주의 깊은 / 잊었다
② 반응하는 / 깨달았다
③ 반응하는 / 과소평가했다
④ 무감각한 / 과소평가했다
⑤ 무감각한 / 깨달았다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to ____________________ from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
options: ① stop painting and appreciate other good works
② check the details of your painting without exception
③ get the right feedback on the shortcomings in your picture
④ look at it as a whole, away from the details of the painting
questions.explanation: 글의 주제는 그림을 그릴 때 특정 부분에 매몰되지 말고 전체적인 진행 상황을 살피는 것의 중요성입니다. 지나치게 많은 것을 덧붙여 그림을 망치는 것을 방지하기 위해, 때때로 그림의 세부 사항에서 벗어나 전체를 바라보는 것이 필요하다는 맥락이므로 4번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그림 그리기를 멈추고 다른 좋은 작품들을 감상하는 것
② 예외 없이 당신의 그림의 세부 사항들을 확인하는 것
③ 당신의 그림의 단점에 대해 적절한 피드백을 받는 것
④ 그림의 세부 사항에서 벗어나 전체적으로 그것을 바라보는 것

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment.
ordered_passages: (A) On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.

(B) In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under.

(C) The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 속도가 세부 사항 파악 능력을 결정한다고 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 진화적으로 인간의 감각이 걷는 속도(시속 5마일 이하)에 맞춰져 있음을 설명한다. (C)에서는 이에 대한 반대로 가장 빠른 운전자가 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력이 제한적임을 제시하고, (D)에서 '반면에(On the other hand)'를 사용하여 보행자가 세부 사항을 감상할 수 있음을 대조하며 조깅하는 사람이나 자전거 타는 사람이 그 중간 단계임을 설명하는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Specifically, she pointed out that Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.

(B) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. Thus, it is unreasonable to categorize senses into a few types.

(C) However, the philosopher Fiona Macpherson wrote in The Senses that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds." According to her, instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각을 5개로 정의했음을 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 'However'와 함께 철학자 Fiona Macpherson의 의견을 빌려 감각이 한정된 종류로 나뉠 수 없음을 주장한다. (A)에서는 구체적으로(Specifically) 인간에게서 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 감각들(자기 수용 감각, 평형 감각)을 예로 들고, (B)에서 다른 동물의 사례를 들어 감각을 몇 가지 유형으로 범주화하는 것이 타당하지 않다는 결론을 맺는 것이 논리적이다.

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other.
ordered_passages: (A) With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.

(B) For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion.
(C) Therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment.
questions.explanation: 어떤 두 동물도 완전히 똑같지 않다는 도입부 이후, (C)에서 그러므로 치유 과정에서도 똑같이 반응하지 않을 것이며 환경적 요인이 반응을 결정할 수 있다는 일반적인 결론을 제시합니다. (B)에서는 그에 대한 구체적인 예시(보호소 고양이 vs 집 고양이, 신체 질환 vs 정서 혼란)를 들고, 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 점을 고려하여 모든 치유 세션은 개별적으로 탐구되고 조정되어야 한다는 시사점을 주며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. (A) They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. (B) As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. (C) All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. (D) In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. (E) The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.insertion_sentence: Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '상식이 통했다: 다양한 스포츠가 아이들을 위해 조정되었다'는 내용입니다. (A)까지는 아이들이 성인용 환경에서 스포츠를 할 때 겪는 어려움을 설명하고 있으며, (B) 뒤부터는 야구, 축구, 테니스 등 구체적으로 어떻게 스포츠가 조정되었는지에 대한 예시가 나열됩니다. 따라서 일반적인 변화를 선언하는 주어진 문장은 구체적인 사례가 시작되기 직전인 (B) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond ⓐ<u>normally</u> to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally ⓑ<u>paralyzed</u>. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or ⓒ<u>weakened</u>; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are ⓓ<u>recognized</u> but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of ⓔ<u>interrupting</u> sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 수면 중인 개체가 외부 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않는 '지각적 단절(perceptual disengagement)'에 관한 글입니다. 지각적 단절은 자극이 뇌로 전달되어 잠에서 깨는 것을 방지함으로써 수면을 '유지'하거나 '보호'하는 역할을 합니다. 따라서 수면을 ⓔ'방해(interrupting)'한다는 표현은 문맥상 정반대의 의미이므로 'protecting'이나 'maintaining'과 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.summary_sentence: It is a(n) (A)__________ that certain tastes are divided into individual areas; all taste can be felt anywhere in the mouth, and the important mechanism at work is not a location of a tongue, but time of a(n) (B)__________.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 혀의 부위별로 느끼는 맛이 다르다는 '혀 지도'가 사실은 오해에서 비롯된 틀린 정보임을 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '오해(misconception)'가 적절하며, 마지막 문장에서 맛을 느끼는 기제는 위치가 아니라 시간, 즉 지각(perception)되는 순서라고 했으므로 (B)에는 '지각(perception)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 오해 / 지각
② 상식 / 인식
③ 사실 / 의식
④ 오류 / 만족
⑤ 불운한 사고 / 알림

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ① Animals should be approached in a calm and confident manner.
② You should remain consistent when it comes to animal training.
③ People who abuse animals are often likely to have mental health issues.
④ Animals should be treated in the way that is best for the animals concerned.
⑤ When preparing for a new pet, set out clear rules before it comes to your home.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 동물마다 개별적인 특성이 있고 환경적 요인이나 치료 목적(신체적 혹은 정서적)에 따라 반응이 다르다는 것입니다. 따라서 필자는 모든 치유 세션이 다르게 탐색되어야 하며, 각 치료는 동물의 특정한 필요에 맞게 조정되어야 한다고 주장하고 있습니다. 따라서 ④번 '동물들은 관련된 동물에게 가장 좋은 방식으로 대우받아야 한다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 동물들은 침착하고 자신감 있는 방식으로 접근되어야 한다.
② 동물 훈련에 있어서는 일관성을 유지해야 한다.
③ 동물을 학대하는 사람들은 종종 정신 건강 문제를 가질 가능성이 높다.
④ 동물들은 해당 동물에게 가장 좋은 방식으로 치료받아야 한다.
⑤ 새 반려동물을 준비할 때, 집으로 오기 전에 명확한 규칙을 정하라.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① Inca Way of Improving Running Efficiency
② Writing Skills of Mailmen In The Inca Empire
③ The Inca Society Based On Strict Social Classes
④ Road Construction That Moved the Human History
⑤ Inca Communication System by Relay Roadrunners
questions.explanation: 인카 제국은 말이 없는 상황에서도 '차스키'라고 불리는 젊고 잘 달리는 주자들을 도로 곳곳에 배치하여 릴레이 방식으로 메시지를 빠르게 전달하는 뛰어난 시스템을 갖추고 있었다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ⑤번 '이어달리기 주자들에 의한 인카의 통신 시스템'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 달리기 효율성을 높이는 인카의 방법
② 인카 제국 우체부들의 작문 기술
③ 엄격한 사회 계층에 기초한 인카 사회
④ 인류 역사를 바꾼 도로 건설
⑤ 이어달리기 주자들에 의한 인카의 통신 시스템

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not ⓐ<u>respond</u> normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally ⓑ<u>blind</u>. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but processed ⓒ<u>normally</u> and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible ⓓ<u>without</u> it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the ⓔ<u>intermediate</u> state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.*stimuli: 자극 **disengagement: 이탈**drowsiness: 졸음
questions.explanation: 잠자는 동안에는 환경 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않고 정보 처리가 약화된다는 내용입니다. ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 자극이 등록되지만 개체(individual)를 깨우는 데 실패한다고 했으므로, 정보가 '정상적으로(normally)' 처리되는 것이 아니라 '비정상적으로' 혹은 '변형되어' 처리된다고 해야 흐름상 적절합니다. 따라서 normally를 abnormally 등으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with ⓐ<u>emotions</u>. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have ⓑ<u>more</u> control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it. And this is the part of your mind that lets you ⓒ<u>down</u> frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other ⓓ<u>negativities</u> that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the ⓔ<u>subconscious</u> mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.explanation: 해당 지문의 논리에 따르면, 공포는 처음에 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)에서 시작되며, 이것이 잠재의식(subconscious mind)에 기록될 때 비로소 실제적인 두려움이 됩니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 'subconscious'는 'conscious'로 바뀌어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. (A)____________, research in the 1980s and 1990s demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. (B)____________, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞부분에서는 과거의 혀 지도를 설명하고 있고, 뒷부분에서는 80~90년대 연구를 통해 그것이 틀렸음이 입증되었다고 했으므로 역접의 연결어 'Yet'이 적절합니다. (B) 앞부분에서는 미뢰가 전문 분야에 따라 그룹화되지 않았고 입안 어디에서나 맛을 느낄 수 있다고 설명하며, 뒷부분에서는 작용하는 메커니즘이 장소가 아니라 시간이라는 추가적인 설명을 덧붙이고 있으므로 첨가의 'Moreover'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 하지만 / 게다가
② 또한 / 하지만
③ 따라서 / 결과적으로

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. ABC's baking soda, for instance, was used as an ingredient functioning to expand and enhance the taste of flour when making bread or snacks. However, it was hard to expect a meaningful increase in sales only with the use. So, advertisers imitated the scene of an actor making Dalgona using sugar and baking soda in a famous drama called Squid Game. Also, they highlighted that it could be used as an eco-friendly detergent by using its ability to absorb pollutants. Repositioning baking soda helped increase sales.
options: ① The effect of expensive advertising on sales cannot be underestimated.
② Baking soda can only be appreciated when used for its original purpose.
③ Businesses are obliged to produce and sell environmentally friendly products.
④ Through the image transformation of the product, the desired result could be obtained.
⑤ To promote products using famous movie actors is the most effective way to increase sales.
questions.explanation: 광고주들이 제품의 시장 상황에 맞춰 주장을 조정하는 능력을 보여주었다는 내용입니다. 베이킹 소다의 사례를 통해, 원래의 용도(제과) 외에 달고나 만들기나 친환경 세제로서의 새로운 이미지(repositioning)를 구축함으로써 판매를 늘렸다는 내용을 담고 있으므로 ④번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 매출에 대한 비싼 광고의 효과는 과소평가될 수 없다.
② 베이킹 소다는 원래 목적으로 사용될 때만 그 가치를 인정받을 수 있다.
③ 기업들은 환경 친화적인 제품을 생산하고 판매할 의무가 있다.
④ 제품의 이미지 변신을 통해 원하는 결과를 얻을 수 있었다.
⑤ 유명 영화배우를 활용하여 제품을 홍보하는 것이 매출 증대의 가장 효과적인 방법이다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as their good or bad. There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
options: ① It is recommended to consume nutrient-dense foods as much as possible.
② We should get rid of bad foods on our dining tables to maintain our health.
③ It is important to include foods that provide various nutrients in your diet.
④ The frequency of eating foods has a great impact on health than the types of foods.
⑤ Recipes for foods are the most significant factor in determining healthy and unhealthy foods.
questions.explanation: 음식 자체를 '좋은 음식'과 '나쁜 음식'으로 이분법적으로 나누는 것은 옳지 않으며, 중요한 것은 다양한 영양소를 충분히 공급할 수 있도록 음식을 조합하는 것이라는 내용입니다. 몸에 좋은 음식만 편식하는 것도 건강한 식단이 아니라고 설명하므로 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 가능한 한 영양 밀도가 높은 음식을 섭취하는 것이 권장된다.
② 건강을 유지하기 위해 우리 식탁에서 나쁜 음식을 제거해야 한다.
③ 식단에 다양한 영양소를 제공하는 음식을 포함하는 것이 중요하다.
④ 음식을 먹는 빈도가 음식의 종류보다 건강에 더 큰 영향을 미친다.
⑤ 음식의 레시피는 건강한 음식과 건강하지 않은 음식을 결정하는 가장 중요한 요소이다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
options: ① importance of brain function for active physical activity
② relationship between the capacity of the brain and economic power
③ effect of the active interaction of various organizations in the city
④ similarities between the operation of the brain and the operation of the city
⑤ principle of transmitting electrochemical signals from neurons to sensory organs
questions.explanation: 이 글은 뇌의 작동 방식을 도시의 경제 시스템에 비유하여 설명하고 있습니다. 경제가 한 곳에서 발생하는 것이 아니라 도시의 여러 요소들의 상호작용에서 비롯되듯이, 뇌의 작용 또한 특정 한 지점에서 발생하는 것이 아니라 뉴런들의 상호작용과 신호 전달을 통해 이루어진다는 점을 강조합니다. 따라서 주제는 뇌와 도시 운영의 유사성입니다.
options_translation: ① 활발한 신체 활동을 위한 뇌 기능의 중요성
② 뇌의 용량과 경제력 사이의 관계
③ 도시 내 다양한 조직의 활발한 상호작용의 효과
④ 뇌의 운영과 도시의 운영 사이의 유사점
⑤ 뉴런에서 감각 기관으로 전기화학적 신호를 전달하는 원리

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the produce (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
options: ① Consumer Behavior in the Digital Age
② Increase Sales through Discounts and Promotions
③ Customers Prefer Advertisements to Acquaintances' Opinions
④ The More Marketing Strategies, the More Attracted Customers
⑤ The Power of Satisfied Customers: Impact on Repurchase and Referral
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구매 후 고객의 만족도가 재구매 여부뿐만 아니라 타인에 대한 추천(무보수 홍보대사 역할)에 큰 영향을 미친다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 사람들이 광고보다 지인의 의견을 더 신뢰하기 때문에 고객 만족을 관리하는 것이 부정적인 입소문을 피하고 긍정적인 영향을 미친다는 내용이므로 5번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 디지털 시대의 소비자 행동
② 할인과 프로모션을 통한 판매 증대
③ 고객들은 지인의 의견보다 광고를 선호한다
④ 마케팅 전략이 많을수록 더 많은 고객이 유인된다
⑤ 만족한 고객의 힘: 재구매와 추천에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it sometimes makes children have a good child complex. Many of the children raised by parents who think they are "good children" or treat them with strict standards for their behavior have this complex. In serious cases, even when they become adults, they can overly care about others or cannot reject others' opinions, and to endure such a self-image is difficult, leading to depression. They lead a standardized life that does not tolerate deviations due to concerns about going against the expectations of others, and they have difficulty in human relationships due to a lack of understanding of others. To make sure your children grow up healthy, let them know that they need to feel anger in their heart and sometimes practice causing inconvenience to others. Finally, even when your children refuse someone's request, you should advise them that they choose what they want rather than suit the feelings of others.
options: ② Applying Strict Standards to Children
③ Parents' Permissive Attitude Spoils Children
④ Keep Your Child Safe from the Negative Effects of Praise
⑤ The Need to Educate Children to Develop Consideration for Others
questions.explanation: 칭찬이 아이들에게 '착한 아이 컴플렉스'를 유발할 수 있으며, 이는 성인이 되어서도 타인의 시선을 지나치게 의식하거나 자신의 욕구를 무시하는 등의 부작용을 낳을 수 있다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 자녀를 건강하게 키우기 위해 칭찬의 이러한 부정적 영향으로부터 보호해야 한다는 내용인 ④가 제목으로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 아이들에게 칭찬이 필요한 이유
② 아이들에게 엄격한 기준 적용하기
③ 부모의 허용적인 태도가 아이를 망친다
④ 칭찬의 부정적인 영향으로부터 아이를 안전하게 지키기
⑤ 타인에 대한 배려심을 기르도록 아이들을 교육할 필요성

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Gary Becker was born in Pottsville, Pennsylvania in 1930 and grew up in Brooklyn, New York City. His father, who was not well educated, had a deep ⓐ<u>interested in</u> financial and political issues. After graduating from high school, Becker went to Princeton University, ⓑ<u>where</u> he majored in economics. He was dissatisfied with his economic education at Princeton University because "it didn't seem to be handling real problems." He earned a doctor's degree in economics from the University of Chicago in 1955. His doctoral paper on the economics of discrimination ⓒ<u>was</u> mentioned by the Nobel Prize Committee as an important contribution to economics. Since 1985, Becker had written a regular economics column in Business Week, ⓓ<u>explaining</u> economic analysis and ideas to the general public. In 1992, he ⓔ<u>was awarded</u> the Nobel Prize in economic science.
questions.explanation: ⓐ의 'interested in'에서 interested는 형용사나 과거분사 역할을 하지만, 앞의 형용사 deep의 수식을 받아 '깊은 관심'이라는 명사구가 되어야 하므로 명사형인 interest가 적절합니다 (had a deep interest in). 나머지는 ⓑ 관계부사 where, ⓒ 수동태 동사 was mentioned, ⓓ 분사구문 explaining, ⓔ 수동태 was awarded로 모두 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 묑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, which is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way ⓐ<u>which</u> production could be made more efficient, known as the ''division of labor.'' Making most manufactured goods ⓑ<u>includes</u> several different processes using different skills. Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished. One worker could do all these tasks, ⓒ<u>making</u> 20 pins in a day. But this work can be divided into its separate processes, with a number of workers each ⓓ<u>carrying out</u> one task. Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day - a huge increase in productivity from the 200 ⓔ<u>that</u> they would have produced before.
questions.explanation: ⓐ에서 관계대명사 which 들에 오는 문장 'production could be made more efficient'는 완전한 문장입니다. 선행사 a way를 수식하면서 들에 완전헄 문장이 오려면 관계부사 in which 또는 that이 와야 합니다. (how는 a way와 함께 쓸 수 없음)

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 묑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옾은 것만을 있는 대로 고릸 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. ⓐ<u>When they speak, others listen - even if the areas of their skills have nothing to do with the advice which they give</u>. ⓑ<u>Think about a few world-famous basketball players who have made more money from promotions than they ever did playing basketball</u>. ⓒ<u>Is it because of their knowledge of the products they endorse it?</u> No. ⓓ<u>We listen because of our admiration for their talent</u>. Excellence connects. ⓔ<u>If you have remarkable and excellent ability in one area, others may desire to connecting with you due to it.</u>
questions.explanation: ⓐ 옾음. have nothing to do with(~와 관련이 없다)와 목적격 관계대명사 which가 바리게 사용됨.ⓑ 옾음. 명령문으로 시작하며 주격 관계대명사 who와 대동사 did(이전에 벌었던 것보다)가 적절함.ⓒ 툐림. 관계대명사(that/which)가 생략된 구문에서 endorse의 목적어가 선행사 products이므로, 들에 대명사 it을 중복해서 쓰면 안 됨.ⓓ 옾음. because of 다음에 명사구(our admiration ~)가 잘 왔음.ⓔ 툐림. desire는 to부정사를 목적어로 취하므로 to connect로 고쳐야 함.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: ㉠<u>Someone else's body language affects our own body, who then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly</u>. As Louis Armstrong sang, -When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you.- ㉡<u>If copying another's smile makes us felt happy, the emotion of the smiler has been transmitted via our body</u>. ㉢<u>Strange as it may sound, this theory mentions that emotions arise from our bodies</u>. ㉣<u>For example, our mood can be improved by simply lifting up the corners of our mouth</u>. ㉤<u>If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, taking care not to let the pencil touch their lips, they judge cartoons funnier than if they have been asked to frown</u>. The primacy of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase -I must be afraid, because I'm running.-
questions.explanation:
㉠: 선행사가 ‘body language’ 또는 ‘our own body’이므로 관계대명사 who를 which로 고쳐야 합니다.
㉡: 사역동사 make의 목적격 보어 자리에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 felt를 feel로 고쳐야 합니다.
㉢: ‘형용사 + as + 주어 + 동사’는 ‘비록 ~할지라도’의 의미를 갖는 양보 구문이며, 자동사 arise가 적절하게 쓰였습니다.
㉣: ‘기분(mood)’은 개선되는 대상이므로 수동태인 ‘can be improved’는 어법상 적절합니다.
㉤: ‘be asked to V(~하도록 요청받다)’ 구문과 비교급 funnier, 그리고 조건절 내의 시제 등이 모두 일관성 있게 쓰였습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were seldom sufficient to support a full-time chief or village council. ______________________________ changed work patterns. Early farmers could reap 3-10kg of grain from each 1kg of seed planted. Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided support for nonfarmers such as chieftains, village councils, men who practice medicine, priests, and warriors. In return, the nonfarmers provided leadership and security for the farming population, enabling it to continue to increase food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses. With improved technology and favorable conditions, agriculture produced consistent surpluses of the basic necessities, and population groups grew in size. These groups concentrated in towns and cities, and human tasks specialized further. Specialists such as carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their skills and became more efficient in their use of time and energy.
options: ② The improved stability of life
⑤ The expansion of the population
questions.explanation: 이 글은 초기 수렵 채집 사회와 달리 농업의 발전이 잉여 식량을 만들어내고, 이로 인해 비농민 계층을 부양할 수 있게 되면서 노동 패턴이 변화하고 분업과 전문화가 이루어졌음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '농업의 발전'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 직업의 다양화
② 삶의 안정성 향상
③ 농업의 발전
④ 리더십의 발달
⑤ 인구의 확장

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, ___________________________. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Companies large and small have off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
options: ① to maintain traditional work methods
② to make us have more free time and greater goals
③ to slow down the pace of technological innovation
④ to encourage the progress of automation in society
⑤ to discourage the utilization of technology in everyday life
questions.explanation: 컴퓨터화된 사회의 약속은 반복적인 힘든 일을 기계로 넘겨 인간에게 '더 많은 여유 시간'을 주는 것이었으나, 실제로는 소비자가 직접 해야 할 일(예약, 체크인, 계산 등)이 늘어나 오히려 시간이 부족해졌다는 내용입니다. 따라서 약속된 긍정적인 측면은 여유 시간과 더 큰 목표를 갖게 하는 것입니다.
options_translation: ① 전통적인 작업 방식을 유지하는 것
② 우리가 더 많은 자유 시간과 더 큰 목표를 갖게 하는 것
③ 기술 혁신의 속도를 늦추는 것
④ 사회의 자동화 진보를 장려하는 것
⑤ 일상생활에서 기술 활용을 억제하는 것

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This also explains ____________________________________________. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket and a department store with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
options: ① why the price of the goods should be set high from the beginning
② why people who live in big cities can buy daily necessities at a lower price
③ why increasing the discount rate of a product improves the inclination to purchase
④ why it is important to consider regional characteristics when choosing items to discount
⑤ why people line up in front of a department store early in the morning to buy limited-edition products
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구매 수량을 제한(희소성 원리)하는 것이 오히려 판매량을 늘린다는 실험 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 이러한 원리는 사람들이 한정판 제품(수량 제한)을 사기 위해 아침 일찍 줄을 서는 현상을 설명해 줍니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 상품 가격이 처음부터 높게 책정되어야 하는지
② 왜 대도시에 사는 사람들이 생필품을 더 낮은 가격에 살 수 있는지
③ 왜 제품의 할인율을 높이는 것이 구매 의향을 향상시키는지
④ 왜 할인 품목을 선택할 때 지역적 특성을 고려하는 것이 중요한지
⑤ 왜 사람들이 한정판 제품을 사기 위해 이른 아침부터 백화점 앞에 줄을 서는지

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although many people think that technology doesn't help much to improve productivity, I'm telling you it an have a positive impact on productivity. For example, in many office environments workers sit at desks with computers and have access to the internet. They are able to check their personal e-mails and use social media whenever they want to. This helps them think creatively as well as reducing the stress they get from work and developing an eye to see their current trends. Introducing new technology can also have a positive impact on production when it causes a change to the production process or requires workers to learn a new system. As soon as they become accustomed to the new system, work efficiency improves, and as a result, employees have time to relax and work happily. This ultimately leads to increased productivity. As demonstrated by these instances, _______________________________________________.
options: ① technology can interfere with efficiency and productivity.
② technology can have positive aspects when it comes to improving productivity.
③ using personal e-emails or accessing social media while working is strictly restricted.
④ the close relationship between employees and employers helps to improve productivity.
⑤ the stress management program for employees is the key to the success of the business.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 기술이 생산성에 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 언급하고 있으며, 개인적인 이메일/SNS 사용을 통한 창의성 향상과 스트레스 감소, 그리고 새로운 시스템 도입을 통한 업무 효율성 증대를 사례로 들고 있습니다. 따라서 결론은 기술이 생산성 향상에 긍정적인 역할을 할 수 있다는 내용이 되어야 합니다.
options_translation: 기술은 효율성과 생산성을 방해할 수 있다.
기술은 생산성 향상에 있어 긍정적인 측면을 가질 수 있다.
업무 중 개인 이메일 사용이나 소셜 미디어 접속은 엄격히 제한된다.
직원과 고용주 사이의 긴밀한 관계는 생산성 향상에 도움이 된다.
직원을 위한 스트레스 관리 프로그램이 사업 성공의 핵심이다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. Although it may seem ⓐ<u>reasonable</u>, having two separate calendars for work and personal life can lead to distractions. To check if something is missing, you will find yourself checking your to-do lists ⓑ<u>numerous</u> times. Instead, ⓒ<u>organize</u> all of your tasks in one place. It doesn't matter if you use digital or paper media. It's okay to keep your ⓓ<u>professional</u> and personal tasks in one place. This will give you a good idea of how time is divided between work and home. This will allows you to make ⓔ<u>instinctive</u> decisions about which tasks are most important.
questions.explanation: 모든 할 일을 한곳에 정리하면 업무와 가정 사이에서 시간이 어떻게 분배되는지 잘 알 수 있게 되어, 어떤 일이 가장 중요한지에 대해 '정보에 입각한' 또는 '이성적인' 결정을 내릴 수 있게 된다는 문맥이 적절합니다. 따라서 본능적인(instinctive) 결정을 내린다는 표현은 흐름상 어색하며, 'informed' 등이 더 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 관 다음에 이어질 관의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: When I woke up in our hotel room, it was almost midnight. I didn't see my husband nor daughter. I called them, but I heard their phones ringing in the room.
ordered_passages: (A) I approached, hoping to find my husband and daughter, and suddenly I saw two familiar faces. I smile, feeling calm.
(B) Feeling worried, I went outside and walked down the street, but they were nowhere to be found. When I decided I should ask someone for help, a crowd nearby caught my attention.
(C) Just then, my daughter saw me and called, -Mom!- They were watching the magic show. Finally, I felt all my worries disappear.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 호텔 방에 가접들이 없어 걱정하는 사황이 제시됩니다. (B)에서 걱정하며 밑으로 나가서 찾다가 군중을 발견하는 내용이 이어집니다. (A)에서 그 군중에게 다가가 측근한 얼굴을 발견하고 안도하며, (C)에서 딸이 얼굴을 발견하고 마술 쇼림 보고 있었음을 확인하며 걱정이 사라지는 흐름으로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 관의 흐름으로 밴아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress. (A) A 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. (B) The key issue is time pressure. (C) A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life. (D) It led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. (E) In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 However림 시작하여 부유한 경제 체제는 그들만의 독특한 스트럨스가 있다고 합니다. (A) 문장김지는 가난(낮은 사회경제적 지위)가 스트럨스림 유발한다는 내용이며, (B) 문장부터 그 핵심 문제가 '시간 압박'이라며 부유한 국가들의 스트럨스 요인을 설명하기 시작합니다. 따라서 역접의 접속사가 포함된 주어진 문장은 (B) 자리에 오는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. ⓐFor example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. ⓑThis phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." ⓒA survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. ⓓHowever, another study revealed that many individuals tend to underestimate their abilities in various domains. ⓔIn terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 자신이 평균보다 더 낫다고 믿는 경향(레이크 워비곤 효과)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓓ번 문장은 사람들이 자신의 능력을 '과소평가(underestimate)'한다는 내용을 담고 있어, 자신의 능력을 과대평가한다는 전체 글의 흐름과 반대됩니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 래, 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, -Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set.- The decline in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.
questions.summary_sentence: The cause of the (A)____________ in human curiosity after the age of 4 can be explained by brain development; infants with more (B)____________ and less efficient neural communication in their brains view the world in a more rich and disordered way, which encourages curiosity, but as they grow older, they come to have more (C)____________ beliefs about the world, resulting in the pruning of the unused neural pathways, which lowers curiosity.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 아이들이 나이가 들면서 호기심이 줄어들고 뇌의 신경 회로가 강화되거나 가준칤기 되는 과정을 설명합니다. 4세 이홄 호기심이 (A)감소(decrease)하는 이유는, 유아기에는 더 (B)복잡한(complex) 신경 연결을 가지고 있어 세상을 퐒요하고 무질서하게 보지만, 성장하면서 더 (C)견고한(solid) 믿음을 가지게 되기 때문입니다.
options_translation: 상승 - 단순한 - 확실한
하락 - 체계적인 - 분명한
감소 - 복잡한 - 견고한
증가 - 복잡한 - 불확실한
감소 - 혼란수러운 - 모호한

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 요약문을 제시⅋ 조건에 맞게 완성하시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: Sometimes the pace of change is far slower. The face you saw reflected in your mirror this morning probably appeared no different from the face you saw the day before - or a week or a month ago. Yet we know the face that stares back at us from the glass is not the same, cannot be the same, as it was 10 minutes ago. The proof is in your photo album: Look at a photograph taken of yourself 5 or 10 years ago and you see clear differences between the face in the snapshop and the face in your mirror. If you lived in a world without mirrors for a year and then saw your reflection, you might be surprised by the change. After an interval of 10 years without seeing yourself, you might not at first recognize the person peering from the mirror. Even something as basic as our own face changes from moment to moment.
questions.summary_sentence: _________________________________________________, the face undergoes subtle changes over time.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어들을 형태 변하 없이 각각 한 번숭만 사용할 것
적절한 접셍사림 포함할 것
questions.subjective_answer_format: _________________________________________________, the face undergoes subtle changes over time.
questions.answer: Although it is difficult for you to recognize the differences
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우리의 얼굴이 매 순간 변하고 있지만, 그 변화가 너무 늬려서 슽게 인식하기 어렵다는 내용입니다. 조건에 따라 '비록 당신이 그 차이림 인식하기 어렵지만(양보의 접셍사 Although 사용)'을 영작하면 'Although it is difficult for you to recognize the differences'가 됩니다.

questions.question: 22. 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally ⓐ<u>blind.</u> Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or ⓑ<u>weakened</u>; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of ⓒ<u>protecting</u> sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be ⓓ<u>possible</u> without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep ⓔ<u>without</u> total perceptual disengagement.
options: ① 잠자는 동물이나 사람은 주변 자극에 정상적으로 반응한다.
② 포유동물은 잠잘 때 눈꺼풀을 열면 정상적으로 볼 수 있다.
③ 시각을 제외한 다른 감각 체계는 수면 시 정상적으로 작동한다.
④ 몇몇 저자들은 지각이탈을 잠 그 자체 정의의 일부로 여기지 않는다.
⑤ 많은 동물은 졸음이라는 중간 상태를 전적인 지각 이탈 때문에 사용하지 못한다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 "some authors do not count it (perceptual disengagement) as part of the definition of sleep itself"라고 명시하고 있으므로 4번이 일치합니다. 1, 2, 3번은 수면 중 감각 자극이 정상적으로 처리되지 않는다는 본문 내용과 반대되며, 5번은 전적인 지각 이탈 없이(without) 졸음 상태를 이용한다고 했으므로 틀렸습니다.

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. (A)_________, research in the 1980s and 1990s demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. (B)_________, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.explanation:
(A) 앞서 언급된 '혀의 지도' 이론이 후대 연구를 통해 틀렸음이 밝혀지는 반전의 내용이 이어지므로 역접의 연결어 'However'가 적절합니다.
(B) 혀의 지도가 틀렸다는 사실 외에, 맛 지각의 기제가 장소가 아닌 시간이라는 추가적인 논거를 제시하고 있으므로 첨가의 연결어 'Furthermore'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 하지만 / 게다가
② 하지만 / 마찬가지로
③ 그럼에도 불구하고 / 요약하자면
④ 예를 들어 / 그렇지 않으면
⑤ 예를 들어 / 그와 대조적으로

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① The Evolution of Adult Sports
② Adapting Sports for Young Children
③ Intense Competition in International Sports
④ The Conditions of Participation in Junior Sports
⑤ The Difficulty of Young Athletes in Adult Sports
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린아이들을 위해 스포츠 환경, 장비, 경기 방식 등을 개조하고 적응시키는 것이 필요하다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ②번 'Adapting Sports for Young Children(어린이를 위한 스포츠 개조)'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.summary_sentence: People who are expert in a certain field tend to (A)_____________ how difficult a task is for a beginner. To overcome the problems caused by this insensitiveness, we need to look at the learning process through (B)__________ eyes.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 전문가들은 자신이 과거에 그 기술을 배울 때 얼마나 힘들었는지를 잊어버리는(forget) 경향이 있으며, 이로 인해 초보자에게 과업이 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 무뎌지게 됩니다. 이를 극복하기 위해서는 학생이나 초보자(newcomers)의 관점에서 학습 과정을 바라볼 필요가 있다고 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 잊다 - 초보자의
② 기억하다 - 전문가의
③ 잘 알다 - 우등생의
④ 과대평가하다 - 초보자의
⑤ 과소평가하다 - 전문가의

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 소개하고 있는 특징을 가진 상사와 가장 유사한 것은?
questions.passage: Any respectable supervisor wouldn't say, "I actively discourage my staff from expressing their onions, and I foster an environment where disagreeing viewpoints are never allowed to surface." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, The outstanding leaders are questioned about their management approaches, often asserting their ongoing encouragement for dissent from their junior staff members. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① Bosses are ones who want any input from their staff to ensure that the best solution is based on the tolerance for opposition.
② Bosses are ones who have a closed mindset on how they should lead a team.
③ Bosses are characterized by their focus on economic profit.
④ Bosses are ones who rely on manipulation and control to maintain their position and are not tolerant of their staff making decisions.
⑤ Bosses are characterized by their dedication to work, such as going beyond their normal working hours.
questions.explanation: 지문은 훌륭한 리더들이 반대 의견(dissent)을 장려하고, 반대자들의 말을 경청하여 최선의 해결책을 찾는 태도를 가지고 있음을 설명하고 있다. 따라서 '반대에 대한 관용을 바탕으로 최선의 해결책을 보장하기 위해 직원들의 의견을 원하는 상사'인 ①번이 가장 유사하다.
options_translation: ① 상사는 반대에 대한 관용을 바탕으로 최선의 해결책을 보장하기 위해 직원들의 어떠한 의견이라도 원하는 사람들이다.

questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. ⓐ<u>If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind</u>. ⓑ<u>Some visual information apparently gets in but it is not processed normally as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems</u>. ⓒ<u>You can observe the eyeballs moving around rapidly under the closed eyelids while the rest of the body is mostly motionless</u>. ⓓ<u>Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to rouse the individual</u>. ⓔ<u>Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself</u>. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement. In the drowsiness state the eyelids are half closed and eyes continue to process visual stimuli normally.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잠자는 동안 외부 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않는 '지각적 단절(perceptual disengagement)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ⓒ는 REM 수면 중의 안구 운동에 대한 설명으로, 외부 자극에 대한 반응 저하라는 주제와는 무관한 내용입니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 요지를 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 주어진 조건에 맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 표현들을 1번씩 꼭 사용할 것
필요한 경우 주어진 어휘를 변형하거나 추가하여 작성할 것
vocabulary_box: each / adapt / to / should / purpose / suit / animal / different / on
questions.answer: should be adapted to suit the different purpose of each animal
questions.explanation: 지문은 모든 동물이 서로 다르며, 환경이나 병의 종류에 따라 치료에 다르게 반응한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 요약문은 '모든 치유 세션과 치료는 각 동물의 서로 다른 목적에 맞게 조정되어야 한다'는 내용이 되어야 합니다. 'should be adapted' (조정되어야 한다), 'to suit' (~에 맞게), 'the different purpose of each animal' (각 동물의 서로 다른 목적)의 구조로 작성합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다ᄋ혀 빈간에 대러갈 마라로 가장 저ᄀ절한 거신?
questions.passage: The design of streets for multiple uses requires an understanding of how different users perceive the street-scape. Joggers and bicyclists perceive street design features differently because of the ____________ of speeds at which they move along the street. The rate of speed at which one is traveling will significantly influences their capacity to perceive details in their surroundings. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adjusted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our capacity to perceive details in our surroundings is best suited for movement at speeds of approximately five miles per hour or less. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate_of_speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: 거리 설개 요소를 이내하는 저도낸 이둉 속도에 다라 다르ᄆ니다. 속도의 차이로 이ᄂ해 사용자마다 다르게 이내하는 거시므로, 속도의 '차이' 호근 '발산(divergence)'의 의미를 가진 다너가 저ᄀ절하ᄆ니다.
options_translation: 보판성
경의성
발한
요구 사항
발산(차이)

questions.question: 22. 다ᄋ혀 글의 미ᄐ줄 친 ⑀~⑄ 중 스이미 가ᄐ은 거ᄉ끼리 작지어진 거스닌?
questions.passage: Several research studies have demonstrated the challenges ⑀<u>that</u> experts encounter when orienting newcomers to their field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found ⑁<u>that</u> people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began (A)<u>underestimate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. ⑂<u>That</u>'s why her participants underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. If we don't forget the fact ⑃<u>that</u> experts often overlook the difficulty of (B)<u>learn something</u> for the first time, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than (C)<u>make assumptions</u> about the ideas ⑄<u>that</u> students should learn what the teacher has decided.
questions.explanation: ⑀낸 관개대며ᄂ사, ⑁과 ⑃은 저ᄇ속사(⑃핸 동객 저ᄇ속사), ⑂낸 지시대며ᄂ사, ⑄낸 동객의 저ᄇ속사이므로 ⑃과 ⑄가 동객 저ᄇ속사라 가ᄐ은 스이므라 사용하고 이그므로 저ᄀ절하ᄆ. (다만 ⑀낸 목적개 관개대며ᄂ사이고 ⑃, ⑄핸 동객 저ᄇ속사이므로 형해상 대개 저ᄇ속사 가타거나 다른 다너의 그분이 피료하ᄆ)

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. (A) For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. (B) Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. (C) Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. (D) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. (E) Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.insertion_sentence: Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '다른 동물들은 분류하기 훨씬 더 어려운 감각들을 가지고 있다'는 내용입니다. (A) 앞뒤로는 인간에게서 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 감각들(자기 수용 감각, 평형 감각)을 설명하고 있고, (B) 뒤에서부터는 척추동물의 냄새 감지 시스템, 뱀의 열 감지 등 '동물'의 사례가 시작되므로 주어진 문장은 (B) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 옳은 것은? [24년 3월 29번]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that ⓐ<u>provide</u> a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and ⓑ<u>satisfied</u>, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, ⓒ<u>conducting</u> numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally ⓓ<u>earn</u> higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work ⓔ<u>was</u> 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: ① ⓐ provide: 선행사가 단수인 work이므로 provides가 되어야 합니다. ② ⓑ satisfied: 목적격 보어 자리에서 days(일과)를 수식하는데, 일과는 만족감을 주는 것이므로 현재분사인 satisfying이 적절합니다. ③ ⓒ conducting: 문장의 본동사 자리입니다. 문맥상 과거에 연구를 수행했다는 의미이므로 conducted가 되어야 합니다. ④ ⓓ earn: when절 내의 주어 they에 연결되는 두 번째 본동사로, produce와 병렬을 이루는 현재형 복수 동사 earn은 적절합니다. ⑤ ⓔ was: 주어가 관계대명사절의 수식을 받는 복수 명사인 those이므로 were가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
