questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are ⓐ<u>adapted</u> to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to ⓑ<u>identify</u> detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more ⓒ<u>infinite</u> ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, ⓓ<u>enable</u>s the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel more ⓔ<u>rapidly</u> than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력에 영향을 미친다는 내용입니다. 자동차 운전자는 보행자보다 훨씬 빠르게 이동하므로 세부 사항을 처리할 시간이 거의 없습니다. 따라서 그들의 능력은 '무한한(infinite)' 것이 아니라 '제한된(limited)' 것이어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.summary_sentence: During sleep, animals and humans fail to respond normally to external stimuli, which helps (A)__________ their sleep. Nonetheless, they can still gain some benefits of sleep through the semi-conscious state of drowsiness without completely (B)__________ perception from sensory stimuli.
questions.explanation: 지문은 잠을 자는 동안 외부 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않는 '지각의 단절(perceptual disengagement)'이 수면을 보호하는 역할을 한다고 설명합니다. 또한 기면(drowsiness)이라는 중간 상태를 통해 지각을 완전히 분리하지 않고도 수면의 이점을 얻을 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '보호하다/수호하다'의 의미인 safeguard나 protect가, (B)에는 '분리하다/단절하다'의 의미인 separating이나 disconnecting이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 방해하다 ...... 잃는 것
② 괴롭히다 ...... 연결하는 것
③ 보호하다 ...... 이동하는 것
④ 인지하다 ...... 단절하는 것
⑤ 보호하다 ...... 분리하는 것

questions.question: 19. 다음 글을 읽고, 추론할 수 없는 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① Employees are usually willing to present their ideas.
② Bot Pittman is one of the leaders who listen to dissenters.
③ Leaders are often asked about their management techniques in the interviews.
④ Respectable leaders try to encourage their staff to present dissenting opinions.
⑤ Dissenters want to tell what their leaders must do to have something done.
questions.explanation: 지문은 리더들이 반대 의견을 장려한다고 '주장한다'는 내용을 다루고 있을 뿐, 실제로 직원들이 보통 자신의 아이디어를 기꺼이 제시하는지에 대한 일반적인 경향성이나 추론은 포함되어 있지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 직원들은 보통 기꺼이 자신의 아이디어를 제시한다.
② Bot Pittman은 반대자들의 말을 듣는 리더들 중 한 명이다.
③ 리더들은 인터뷰에서 종종 경영 기법에 대해 질문을 받는다.
④ 훌륭한 리더들은 직원들이 반대 의견을 제시하도록 격려하려 노력한다.
⑤ 반대자들은 무언가를 성취하기 위해 리더가 무엇을 해야 하는지 말해주고 싶어 한다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.summary_sentence: Experts usually forget the fact that beginners can have (A)____________ learning new tasks. Therefore, it is important to look at the learning from the (B)___________ of students.
questions.subjective_answer_format: (A)      (B)① troubles      representative② experiences      sensitiveness③ knowledges      disrespectability④ controls      assumption⑤ difficulties      perspective
questions.explanation: 지문은 전문가들이 초보자가 겪는 어려움을 망각하는 '지식의 저주' 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 전문가들은 초보자들이 새로운 과업을 배울 때 (A)어려움(difficulties)을 겪는다는 사실을 잊으며, 학생들의 (B)관점(perspective)에서 학습을 바라보는 것이 중요하다는 요약이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 문제들 ... 대표자
② 경험들 ... 세심함
③ 지식들 ... 무례함
④ 통제들 ... 가정
⑤ 어려움들 ... 관점

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. (A) They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. (B) As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. (C) All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. (D) In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. (E) The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.insertion_sentence: Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '상식이 우세해졌다: 다양한 스포츠들이 아이들을 위한 조정을 해왔다'는 내용입니다. (A)까지는 아이들이 성인 환경에서 운동할 때의 어려움을 설명하고 있고, (B)부터 구체적인 조정의 예시(티볼, 플래그 풋볼 등)가 나오므로, 일반적인 변화를 선언하는 주어진 문장은 (B) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 적절한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 그대로 적으시오.
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by (A)___________, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real (B)____________ when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.explanation: (A)의 경우 앞 문장에서 의사결정을 그르치게 하는 원인이 'fueled by emotions(감정에 의해 자극된)'라고 언급되었으므로 판단을 흐리게 하는 것은 'emotions'입니다. (B)의 경우 앞 문장에서 거미나 어둠에 대한 공포(fears)를 언급하며, 이것들이 무의식에 기록될 때 실질적인 'fears'가 된다는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 의미가 되도록 주어진 단어들만을 배열하여 영작하시오.
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered 'finished.' Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. (A)<u>한 그리메 타먀 마는 거스ᄑ 낸는 거스ᄂ 거거스ᄃ 강향려그ᄑ 망스ᄑ 새 거 거거스ᄃ 개하게 바ᄀ거ᄇ던 거ᄉ개라ᄆ 보거게 대스 거다</u>. If you are struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it alter with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
subjective_conditions: 1. 부어진 단애는 모두 한 번시ᄀ 사용
2. ᄑ펴시 단애의 형태르ᄑ 변해시ᄁᄑ 거ᄉ
questions.answer: Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked
questions.explanation: 주어 부분 '한 그리메 타먀 마는 거스ᄑ 낸는 거스ᄂ' -> 'Putting too much into a painting'동사 부분 '거거스ᄃ 강향려그ᄑ 망스ᄑ 새 거' -> 'can spoil its impact'병려ᄑ 구조 '거거스ᄃ 개하게 바ᄀ거ᄇ던 거ᄉ개라ᄆ 보거게 대스 거다' -> 'and leave it looking overworked'조가ᄂ에 타라 putᄑ Putting으로, lookᄑ looking으로, overworkᄑ overworked로 변형하여 자성하ᄆ니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and ⓐ<u>guiding</u> our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that ⓑ<u>forces</u> you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect ⓒ<u>what</u> you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. ⓓ<u>To continue</u> the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused ⓔ<u>is</u> considerable.
questions.explanation: ③번 ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 'People expect'의 목적어 역할을 하는 절은 뒤에 완전한 문장('you will say it')이 오고 있으므로, 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사인 what이 아니라 접속사 that이 쓰여야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably more ⓐ<u>accurate</u> than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts may not become ⓑ<u>sensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓒ<u>depreciate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even ⓓ<u>underrated</u> how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how ⓔ<u>challenging</u> it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 전문가들은 초보자가 특정 기술을 배우는 데 걸리는 시간을 과소평가하는 경향이 있으며 실제보다 더 짧게 예측하는 오류를 범한다. 따라서 전문가들이 초보자보다 '더 정확하다(accurate)'는 표현은 문맥상 어색하며, '부정확하다(inaccurate)'는 내용이 와야 한다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to ⓐ<u>question</u> it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is ⓑ<u>different</u> from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even ⓒ<u>harder</u> to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a ⓓ<u>unlimited</u> number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into ⓔ<u>fixed</u> categories, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 지문의 전체적인 맥락은 감각을 단순히 5개로 한정할 수 없으며, 감각들이 명확하게 소수의 범주로 나뉘지 않는다는 내용이다. 따라서 ⓓ의 'unlimited(무제한의)'는 'limited(제한된/한정된)'가 되어야 "감각들이 명확하게 한정된 숫자의 특정한 종류로 나누어질 수 없다"는 문맥이 완성된다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where __________________________. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① children have a playbook designed to help them
② strict observance of rules is emphasized for a fair play
③ a small number of children perform well at high levels for fans
④ children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams
⑤ children with excellent physical conditions are excluded from their team
questions.explanation: 어린이들이 성인용 규격의 스포츠 환경에서 겪는 어려움을 해결하기 위해 스포츠가 어린이에 맞춰 조정(adaptations)되었다는 내용이다. 야구, 축구, 테니스 등의 예시를 통해 경기장 크기나 장비의 조정이 언급되므로, 빈칸에도 어린이 수준에 맞춘 경기 방식인 '더 짧은 시간 동안, 더 작은 팀으로 경기한다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 아이들은 그들을 돕기 위해 고안된 플레이북을 가지고 있다
② 공정한 경기를 위해 엄격한 규칙 준수가 강조된다
③ 소수의 아이들이 팬들을 위해 높은 수준에서 잘 수행한다
④ 아이들은 더 짧은 시간 동안 그리고 종종 더 작은 팀으로 경기한다
⑤ 신체 조건이 우수한 아이들은 팀에서 제외된다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. (A) Species are forced to follow. (B) All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. (C) Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. (D) A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. (E) From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.insertion_sentence: When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too.
questions.explanation: 첫 문장에서 종마다 특정한 기후적 요구사항이 있다고 언급했습니다. 주어진 문장의 'those requirements'는 이 기후적 요구사항을 가리킵니다. 따라서 기후가 변하면 그 요구사항을 충족하는 장소도 변한다는 내용의 주어진 문장이 (A)에 들어가야, 그 뒤의 '종들은 (그 변화된 장소를) 따라가도록 강요받는다(Species are forced to follow)'는 내용과 자연스럽게 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① the effect of job satisfaction on happiness
② the importance of a good work-life balance
③ advantages and disadvantages of a stable job
④ the evolution of a pleasant working environment
⑤ how to increase a sense of accomplishment at work
questions.explanation: 이 글은 직업에서의 만족감(job satisfaction)과 의미 있는 일(meaningful work)이 개인의 행복(happiness)과 삶 전반의 만족도에 미치는 긍정적인 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 여러 연구 결과를 인용하며 직업 만족도가 높은 사람들이 전반적으로 더 행복한 삶을 영위한다는 점을 강조하고 있으므로 주제는 ①이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 직무 만족이 행복에 미치는 영향
② 훌륭한 일과 삶의 균형의 중요성
③ 안정적인 직업의 장단점
④ 쾌적한 작업 환경의 진화
⑤ 직장에서 성취감을 높이는 방법

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)와 같은 의미가 되도록 주어진 <조건>에 따라 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: (A)<u>마법은 우리 모두 자신의 삶에서 일어나기를 바라는 것이다</u>. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here ⑀<u>is</u> the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges ⑁<u>which</u> you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, ⑂<u>getting</u> ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be ⑃<u>surprising</u> that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more ⑄<u>powerfully and positively</u>.
subjective_conditions: 1. 아래에 주어진 단어만을 한 번씩 모두 사용할 것
2. 주어진 단어의 형태를 바꾸지 말 것
vocabulary_box: / wish / to / is / for / we / magic /
/ what / happen in our life / all /
questions.answer: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life
questions.explanation: 주어 'Magic' + 동사 'is' + 보어절(관계대명사 what절) 구조입니다. 'what we all wish for to happen'에서 wish for + 목적어 + to-v 구문을 사용하여 '우리 모두가 일어나기를 바라는 것'을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 22. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⑀~⑄ 중 어법상 어색한 부분을 3개 찾아 <조건>에 따라 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
questions.passage: (A)<u>마법은 우리 모두 자신의 삶에서 일어나기를 바라는 것이다</u>. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here ⑀<u>is</u> the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges ⑁<u>which</u> you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, ⑂<u>getting</u> ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be ⑃<u>surprising</u> that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more ⑄<u>powerfully and positively</u>.
subjective_conditions: 1. 기호는 쓰지 말 것
2. 올바르게 고친 답만을 답안지에 쓸 것
3. 4개 이상을 답한 경우, 첫 3개의 답안만 인정함
questions.explanation: (1) ⑂: 'Once you write these statements'는 부사절이며, 뒤에 이어지는 문장은 주어가 없는 명령문 형태여야 하므로 동사원형 'get'이 되어야 합니다.(2) ⑃: 주어인 'You'가 감정을 느끼는 주체이므로 현재분사 surprising 대신 과거분사 'surprised'를 써야 합니다.(3) ⑄: 감각동사 'feel'의 보어 자리에는 부사가 아닌 형용사가 와야 하므로 'powerful and positive'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a still more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than those of the typical motorist.
options: ① benefits and disadvantages of walking slowly
② tips for appreciating our surroundings while moving fast
③ factors that influence fast information search and processing
④ optimized steps for capturing the details of the surroundings
⑤ effects of travel speed on ability to process environmental information
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 인간의 감각은 걷는 속도에 최적화되어 있어, 보행자는 세부 사항을 잘 파악하지만 운전자는 속도가 너무 빨라 이를 파악하기 어렵다는 내용을 담고 있으므로 주제로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 천천히 걷는 것의 이점과 단점
② 빠르게 이동하면서 주변 환경을 감상하기 위한 팁
③ 빠른 정보 검색 및 처리에 영향을 미치는 요인들
④ 주변의 세부 사항을 포착하기 위한 최적화된 단계들
⑤ 이동 속도가 환경 정보를 처리하는 능력에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures which appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① Factors that Hinder the Spread of Species
② Migration of Species to Cope with Climate Change
③ Regional Distributional Shifts Trend of Living Things
④ Countermeasures to Safely Preserve Endangered Species
⑤ Requirements of Organism for Survival and Reproduction
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화에 따라 생물 종들이 자신들의 생존 조건을 충족하는 장소로 이동해야 하며, 움직이지 못해 보이는 식물들조차 씨앗 등의 형태로 이동한다는 내용을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로 ②번 '기후 변화에 대처하기 위한 종의 이동'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 종의 확산을 방해하는 요인들
② 기후 변화에 대처하기 위한 종의 이동
③ 생물체의 지역적 분포 변화 추세
④ 멸종 위기 종을 안전하게 보존하기 위한 대책
⑤ 생존과 번식을 위한 유기체의 요구 조건

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca King's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① 전령들은 왕·의 명령을 전달하기 위해 왕·의 길에 배치됐다.
② 전령들은 다닥다닥 붙여 지은 오두막에 무※ 지어 살았다.
③ 전령들은 양방향으로 길을 보며 달리기를 잘하는 저음이들이었다.
④ 잉카인들은 서로를 볼 수 있는 고지대에 오두막을 지었다.
⑤ 잉카 제국은 사정이 접으면 사나흘 만에 1000마일 정도 메시지를 이어갈 수 있었다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 오두막들은 'placed from one to two miles apart along the roads'(길을 따라 1~2마일 간격으로 떨어져 배치됨)이라고 하였으므로, '다닥다닥 붙여 지은'이라는 ②은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ⓐ<u>more</u> accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓑ<u>insensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓒ<u>overlook</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underrated how long it had taken themselves to ⓓ<u>acquire</u> that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making ⓔ<u>assumptions</u> about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: '지식의 저주' 효과에 따르면 전문가는 초보자의 입장을 이해하는 데 어려움을 겪으므로, 학습에 걸리는 시간을 예측할 때 초보자보다 '더(more)' 정확한 것이 아니라 '덜(less)' 정확해야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how ⓐ<u>importantly</u> meaningful work acts to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more ⓑ<u>energized</u>, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more ⓒ<u>fulfilled</u> on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most ⓓ<u>satisfied</u> with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work ⓔ<u>were</u> 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: ⓐ가 포함된 구문은 'how + 형용사/부사 + 주어 + 동사'의 간접의문문 어순을 취하고 있습니다. 동사 act(작용하다)는 '의미 있는 일이 얼마나 중요하게 작용하는지'라는 의미에서 동사를 수식하는 부사처럼 보일 수 있으나, 여기서는 보어 역할을 하는 형용사가 필요하거나 혹은 meaningful work acts (as) ~ 의 구조에서 meaningful을 수식하는 구조 등으로 분석될 수 있습니다. 그러나 결정적으로 '의미 있는 일이 인간에게 얼마나 중요하게 작용하는가'라는 문맥에서 '얼마나 중요한지(how important)'가 타당합니다. 사실 이 문장에서는 how important (it is that) meaningful work acts ~ 또는 meaningful work가 how important한지에 대한 의미이므로 형용사형인 important가 오는 것이 적절합니다. 나머지는 모두 적절합니다: ⓑ energized는 목적보어로 '활기차게 된' 상태, ⓒ fulfilled는 '충족감을 느끼는', ⓓ satisfied는 '만족하는', ⓔ were는 주어인 those에 일치시킨 복수 동사입니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents __________________ from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but If you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 내용은 리더들이 부하 직원들의 반대 의견(dissent, internal protest)을 듣는 것을 장려한다는 내용입니다. 빈칸 앞의 문장은 '어떤 훌륭한 상사도 ~하는 문화를 유지한다고 말하지 않을 것이다'라는 부인된 내용이므로, 빈칸에는 상사가 겉으로는 장려한다고 주장하는 '반대 의견'이나 '다른 관점'이 들어가는 것이 문맥상 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 'opposing perspectives(반대되는 관점)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 독창적인 생각
② 중립적인 관점
③ 호의적인 논평
④ 반대되는 관점
⑤ 건설적인 토론

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. (B) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. (C) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (D) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. (E) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.insertion_sentence: But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잠의 특징 중 하나인 '지각적 단절(perceptual disengagement)'에 대해 다루고 있습니다. (D) 문장에서 일부 저자들은 지각적 단절이 수면을 보호하는 기능을 할 뿐 수면의 정의 자체는 아니라고 주장했습니다. 주어진 문장은 '하지만 그것(지각적 단절) 없이는 잠이 불가능하므로 정의에 필수적으로 보인다'라는 반론을 제시합니다. 따라서 (D)에서의 부정적 견해 뒤에 역접으로 이어지는 (E) 위치가 가장 적절합니다. 그 뒤 문장인 (E) 이후의 내용은 '그럼에도 불구하고(Nevertheless)' 완전히 단절되지 않은 상태(졸음)를 이용하는 경우를 설명하며 논의를 보충합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites: while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① how speed influences safety in vehicle travel
② the risks pedestrians face from motor vehicles
③ evolutionary perspective on technological mobility
④ impact of travel speed on environmental perception
⑤ role of street design in enriching urban environment
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 셍도가 제볼적인 세부 사항을 인식하는 능력에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 인간의 감각은 걷는 셍도에 최적화되어 있어서, 셍도가 빨라질수록(예: 운전자) 세부 사항을 인식하기 어렵고, 닌리면(예: 봱행자) 더 잘 인식할 수 있다눠 것이 핵심입니다. 따라서 ④ '이동 셍도가 환경 지각에 미치는 영향'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 셍도가 차달 이동 시 안전에 미치는 영향
② 봱행자가 자동차로부터 겪는 위험
③ 기술적 이동성에 대한 진화론적 관점
④ 이동 셍도가 환경 지각에 미치는 영향
⑤ 도시 환경을 풍요롭게 하는 도로 디자인의 역할

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, each healing treatment should be ___________________________________. You will learn as you go: healing is a constant learning process.
options: ① customized to fit the distinct needs of each creature
② conducted in a stress-free work environment
③ preceded by respect and love for animals
④ restricted to physical and mental illness
⑤ explored not differently but identically
questions.explanation: 개별 동물마다 특징이 다르고, 환경적 요인이나 질병의 종류(신체적 vs 정서적)에 따라 치료 반응이 다르다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 각 치료는 각 동물의 개별적인 요구에 맞춰 조정되어야 한다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 각 생명체의 뚜렷한 요구에 맞게 제작되어야(맞춤화되어야) 한다
② 스트레스가 없는 업무 환경에서 수행되어야 한다
③ 동물에 대한 존중과 사랑이 선행되어야 한다
④ 신체적 및 정신적 질병에 국한되어야 한다
⑤ 다르게가 아니라 동일하게 탐구되어야 한다

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus ________________________________ at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ① creativity is the essential driver that ensures success
② good leaders often reveal their natural-born potential
③ leadership is a possibility for each and every one of us
④ individuals must possess a critical mindset towards leaders
⑤ true leadership is rooted in commitment to moral principles
questions.explanation: 위대한 지도자들도 처음에는 평범한 학생, 노동자, 시민으로 시작하여 일상적인 아이디어를 발전시켜 나갔다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 나이나 경험에 상관없이 우리 모두에게 리더십의 가능성이 열려 있다는 결론이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 창의성은 성공을 보장하는 필수적인 원동력이다
② 좋은 리더들은 흔히 타고난 잠재력을 드러낸다
③ 리더십은 우리 각자 모두에게 열려 있는 가능성이다
④ 개인들은 리더들에 대해 비판적인 사고방식을 가져야 한다
⑤ 진정한 리더십은 도덕적 원칙에 대한 헌신에 뿌리를 두고 있다

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A) 부분을 어법과 문맥에 맞게 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오. (단, 주어진 단어만을 모두 한 번씩 사용하시오)
questions.passage: Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five senses, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a second sensory system for detecting odors. Rattlesnakes can detect the body heat of their prey. The platypus's bill is loaded with sensors that detect electric fields and sensors that are sensitive to pressure. These examples tell us that -senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds,- Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should instead study them for what they are. Rather than counting senses, we should ask how animals use their senses, and attempt to step inside their Umwelten. In his classic 1974 essay, -What Is It Like to Be a Bat?,- the American philosopher Thomas Nagel argued that other animals have conscious experiences that are inherently subjective and hard to describe. Bats, for example, perceive the world through sonar, and since this is a sense that the majority of humans lack, -there is no reason to suppose that it (A)<u>[experience / or / subjectively / we / like / can / is / anything / imagine]</u>,- Nagel wrote. You could envision yourself with webbing on your arms or insects in your mouth, but you'd still be creating a mental caricature of you as a bat. -I want to know what it is like for a bat to be a bat,- Nagel wrote. -Yet if I try to imagine this, I am restricted to the resources of my own mind, and those resources are inadequate to the task.-
subjective_conditions: 1. 주어진 단어만을 모두 한 번씩 사용하시오
questions.answer: is like anything we can subjectively experience or imagine
questions.explanation: 철학자 네이글(Nagel)의 견해에 따르면, 박쥐가 느끼는 주관적인 세상은 인간이 경험해보거나 상상할 수 있는 것과 비슷하다고 가정할 근거가 없습니다. 따라서 "is like anything (목적격 관계대명사 생략) we can subjectively experience or imagine"의 어순으로 배열하는 것이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment.
ordered_passages: (A) On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.

(B) In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under.

(C) The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 이동 속도가 환경 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력을 결정한다는 내용입니다. (B)에서는 인간의 감각이 걷는 속도에 최적화되어 있다는 근거를 제시하고, (C)에서는 이와 대조적으로 가장 빠른 운전자는 세부 사항 처리 능력이 제한적임을 설명합니다. (A)에서 'On the other hand'를 통해 다시 느린 보행자는 세부 사항을 감상할 수 있음을 언급하고 그 중간 형태(조깅, 자전거)를 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, _______________________________________________. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
options: ① take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes
② go to a specialist for advice on your painting method
③ look at the existing artwork first and come back
④ constantly continue working without pausing
⑤ concentrate on one area and keep adding more to work
questions.explanation: 그림을 그릴 때 언제 멈춰야 할지 결정하기 어려운 경우, 잠시 휴식을 취하고 나중에 새로운 시각으로 다시 확인하는 것이 도움이 된다는 내용입니다. 빈칸 뒤의 '그 후에(Then) 정교하게 꾸밀 부분이 있는지 결정할 수 있다'는 내용과 가장 자연스럽게 연결되는 것은 ①번입니다.
options_translation: 휴식을 취하고 나중에 새로운 시각으로 다시 그것으로 돌아와라
당신의 그림 기법에 대한 조언을 구하러 전문가에게 가라
기존의 예술 작품을 먼저 보고 다시 돌아와라
멈추지 않고 끊임없이 계속 작업하라
한 영역에 집중하고 작업에 더 많은 것을 계속 추가하라

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. ⓐIf you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. ⓑBut like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. ⓒThrough diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. ⓓThe idea that a diligent person in a group always is sacrificed is a misconception. ⓔThus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 지도자들도 처음에는 평범한 사람들로서 자신의 아이디어를 개선하고 공유하며 리더가 되었고, 따라서 우리 모두 리더가 될 잠재력이 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 하지만 ④번 문장은 집단 내에서 부지런한 사람이 항상 희생된다는 오해에 대해 언급하고 있으므로 글의 전체적인 흐름인 '리더십의 보편적 잠재력'과는 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."*dissent: 반대
options: ① True Leader: Encourage Not Only Advocates but Also Opponents
② Don't Take a View That Doesn't Agree with Your Boss
③ Why a Boss Who Has Regular Conversation Is Respected
④ Start with Why: How Great Leaders Inspire Everyone to Take Action
⑤ What Kind of Corporate Culture Will Affect Employee Satisfaction?
questions.explanation: 지문은 훌륭한 리더들이 부하 직원들의 반대 의견(pro-dissent)을 장려하고 그들의 목소리를 경청하여 일을 완수하기 위해 무엇을 해야 하는지를 알아낸다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '진정한 리더: 지지자뿐만 아니라 반대자도 장려하라'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 진정한 리더: 지지자뿐만 아니라 반대자도 독려하라
② 상사와 의견이 일치하지 않는 관점을 취하지 마라
③ 정기적인 대화를 나누는 상사가 존경받는 이유
④ '왜'에서 시작하라: 위대한 리더들이 모두가 행동하도록 영감을 주는 방법
⑤ 어떤 종류의 기업 문화가 직원의 만족도에 영향을 미치는가?

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the ⓐ<u>same</u> way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also ⓑ<u>determine</u> how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very ⓒ<u>differently</u> than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for ⓓ<u>emotional</u> confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to ⓔ<u>overlook</u> the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.*litter: (한 배에서 태어난) 새끼들
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 각 치유 세션은 다르게 탐색되어야 하며, 각 치유 치료는 동물의 특정한 요구사항을 '충족하거나 고려하도록' 조정되어야 합니다. 'overlook(간과하다)'은 문맥상 어색하며, 'address'나 'meet'와 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. (A) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. (B) For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. (C) Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. (D) Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. (E) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate: 척추동물 **odor: 냄새
questions.insertion_sentence: Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize.
questions.explanation: (B)까지는 인간에게서 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 감각(고유 수용성 감각, 균형 감각)을 언급하고 있습니다. 주어진 문장은 '다른 동물들은 분류하기가 훨씬 더 어려운 감각들을 가지고 있다'는 내용이므로, 인간의 사례가 끝나고 동물의 사례(냄새 탐지 시스템, 뱀의 열 감지 등)가 시작되는 지점인 (C)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.summary_sentence: Climate changes can cause shifts in species' habitats that (A)__________ their survival needs, and even immobile organisms like trees can move by (B)__________ as a seed or a larva as shown in the fossils.
questions.explanation: 기후 변화로 인해 생물의 생존 요구 조건을 (A)충족하는(meet/satisfy) 서식지가 이동하게 됩니다. 이에 따라 생물도 이동해야 하는데, 나무와 같이 고정된 생물도 씨앗의 형태로 (B)흩어짐(scattering/dispersing)으로써 이동이 가능하다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 'meet', (B)에는 본문의 'dispersal'과 일맥상통하는 'scattering'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 충족시키다 / 모으기
② 충족시키다 / 흩어지기
③ 달성하다 / 견디기
④ 무시하다 / 흩어지기
⑤ 제외하다 / 적응하기

questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 질문의 대답을 본문에서 찾아 그대로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.*stimuli: 자극 **disengagement: 이탈***drowsiness: 졸음
questions.subjective_answer_format: Q. What do many mammals do to benefit from sleep as well as avoid perceptual disengagement?정답: ___________________________________________________
questions.answer: Many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness.
questions.explanation: 본문 마지막 문장에서 많은 동물들(인간 포함)이 완전한 지각적 이탈 없이 수면의 이점 중 일부를 얻기 위해 '졸음의 중간 단계(the intermediate state of drowsiness)'를 이용한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 질문에서 묻는 바가 바로 지각적 이탈을 피하며 수면의 이점을 얻기 위해 하는 행동이므로 해당 문장을 그대로 기재합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① benefits of jogging and bicycling for eyesight
② superiority of pedestrian travel over motorist travel
③ correlation between travel speed and the level of cultural awareness
④ rate of movement affecting the ability to perceive the environmental features
⑤ evolutionary adaptation of human senses to different modes of transportation
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력에 큰 영향을 미친다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 인간의 감각은 걷는 속도에 최적화되어 있어 속도가 빠른 운전자는 세부 사항 파악 능력이 제한되는 반면, 보행자는 더 상세히 인식할 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ④번 '환경적 특징을 지각하는 능력에 영향을 미치는 이동 속도'가 주제로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 시력을 위한 조깅과 자전거 타기의 이점
② 운전자 이동보다 보행자 이동의 우수성
③ 이동 속도와 문화적 인식 수준 사이의 상관관계
④ 환경적 특징을 지각하는 능력에 영향을 미치는 이동 속도
⑤ 다양한 교통 수단에 대한 인간 감각의 진화적 적응

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Marilyn and her three-year-old daughter, Sarah, took a trip to the beach, where Sarah built her first sandcastle. Moments later, an enormous wave destroyed Sarah's castle. In response to the loss of her sandcastle, tears streamed down Sarah's cheeks and her heart was broken. She ran to Marilyn, saying she would never build a sandcastle again. Marilyn said, "Part of the joy of building a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give it as a gift to the ocean." Sarah loved this idea and responded with enthusiasm to the idea of building another castle ─ this time, even closer to the water so the ocean would get its gift sooner!
questions.explanation: 모래성이 파도에 부서져 슬퍼하던 아이에게 엄마가 '바다에 주는 선물'이라는 새로운 관점을 제시함으로써 아이가 다시 즐겁게 모래성을 쌓게 되었다는 내용입니다. 이는 관점의 변화가 상황을 긍정적으로 바꾸고 즐거움을 줄 수 있음을 보여주므로 ⑤번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have ⓐ<u>greater</u> control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the ⓑ<u>inappropriate</u> decisions time and time again. When your judgment is ⓒ<u>clarified</u> by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they ⓓ<u>stem</u> from the conscious mind. They only become ⓔ<u>genuine</u> fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions, embedding them deeply within your psyche. Subconscious processes play a significant role in solidifying emotional responses and fears.
questions.explanation: 감정이 판단을 흐리게 하여 편견과 부정적인 요소가 발생한다는 맥락이므로, '명확해지다(clarified)'는 적절하지 않습니다. '흐려지다(clouded)' 혹은 '가려지다(obscured)' 등이 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Wide-scale temporary travel away from home is a relatively ⓐ<u>new</u> phenomenon. In the past few people enjoyed leisure time. For ordinary people, any time off was usually for religious reasons. For holy days - hence the word holidays. Early travel was often ⓑ<u>confined</u> to pilgrimages. Later, as the spas developed, people travelled for health. With the Age of Reason, they started travelling for culture. As a result the famous Grand Tour became popular. As the social and economic situation of countries ⓒ<u>accelerated</u>, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system ⓓ<u>facilitated</u> the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism ⓔ<u>contraction</u>.
questions.explanation: 교통 수단의 발달(철도, 항공)로 인해 더 많은 세계가 열리고 관광 산업이 발전했다는 문맥이므로, ⓔ의 'contraction(수축, 축소)'은 'expansion(확장, 확대)' 또는 'growth(성장)'와 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 새로운
② 국한된
③ 가속화된
④ 용이하게 하다
⑤ 축소

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. However, research in the 1980s and 1990s demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that ___________________________________. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
options: ① taste buds aren't segregated based on their specialities
questions.explanation: 지문은 과거의 '혀 지도' 이론이 잘못된 해석에 기반한 것임을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 문장에서 단맛, 짠맛, 쓴맛, 신맛은 입안 어디에서나 느낄 수 있다고 설명하므로, 오늘날 연구자들이 믿는 바는 '미뢰가 전문 분야(특정 맛)에 따라 분리되어 있지 않다'는 내용인 ①이 정답입니다. (이 문항의 경우 제공된 텍스트에 선지가 1개만 포함되어 있으나 흐름상 명확함)
options_translation: ① 미뢰는 그들의 전문성에 따라 분리되어 있지 않다

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products ________________________________. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ③ that were easy to access
⑤ that satisfied the provider's desires
questions.explanation: 1940~50년대 이후 산업 사회가 발전하면서 판매 방식이 단순히 좋은 품질의 제품을 만드는 것에서 고객의 다양하고 복잡한 요구를 충족시키는 방향으로 바뀌었다는 내용이다. 따라서 제품을 '소비자 선호도에 맞춰(tailored to consumer preferences)' 전달하는 것이 필수적이라는 흐름이 적절하다.
options_translation: 완전한 기능을 갖춘
안전 기준을 충족하는
접근하기 쉬운
소비자 선호도에 맞춘
공급자의 욕구를 만족시키는

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and _________________________________. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ① animals sharing identical genes respond to the same remedy
② treating animals is most effective when approached in a cohesive manner
③ the consideration of genetic factors plays a significant role in animal treatment
④ every healing therapy needs to be customized to meet individual needs of the animals
⑤ animals modify their characteristics in response to environmental influences as they progress through life
questions.explanation: 어떠한 동물도 서로 같지 않으며 환경이나 질병의 성격에 따라 다르게 반응한다는 점을 강조하고 있다. 따라서 모든 치유 요법은 동물의 개별적인 요구를 충족시키기 위해 '맞춤화되어야(customized)' 한다는 결론이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: 동일한 유전자를 공유하는 동물들은 같은 치료법에 반응한다
동물을 치료하는 것은 일관된 방식으로 접근할 때 가장 효과적이다
유전적 요인에 대한 고려가 동물 치료에서 중요한 역할을 한다
모든 치유 요법은 동물의 개별적인 요구를 충족시키기 위해 맞춤화될 필요가 있다
동물들은 삶을 살아가면서 환경적 영향에 반응하여 그들의 특성을 수정한다

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field.
ordered_passages: (A) This observation highlights a phenomenon known as the 'curse of knowledge'. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, as Dr. Hinds was able to demonstrate. Moreover, as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill.

(B) For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones.

(C) Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 분야의 전문가가 초보자에게 해당 분야를 소개할 때 겪는 어려움에 대해 설명합니다. (B)에서 Pamela Hinds 박사의 휴대폰 사용 실험이라는 구체적인 예시를 들고, (A)에서 이 관찰 결과를 '지식의 저주'라고 명명하며 전문가들이 초보자가 느끼는 난이도에 무감각해지는 현상을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 실험 참가자들이 자신의 학습 소요 시간조차 과소평가했다는 추가 결과를 제시하며 학생의 관점에서 학습 과정을 바라볼 필요가 있다는 결론으로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli.
ordered_passages: (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened.(B) It's the same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself.(C) But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 수면 중 외부 자극에 반응하지 않는 특성을 설명하는 글입니다. (A)에서 시각 자극에 대한 구체적인 예시(기능적 맹목)를 들며 정보가 정상적으로 처리되지 않음을 설명합니다. (B)에서 다른 감각 체계도 마찬가지임을 언급하며 '지각적 단절'이라는 용어를 도입하고, 이것이 수면의 정의에 포함되는지에 대한 학자들의 견해를 소개합니다. (C)에서 앞선 견해를 반박하며(But) 지각적 단절이 수면의 정의에 필수적임을 주장하고, 완전한 단절이 없는 졸음 상태에 대해 언급하며 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress. (A) A 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. (B) The key issue is time pressure. (C) A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life. (D) It led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. (E) In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 역접의 접속사 'However'와 함께 '더 부유한 경제 국가들도 그들만의 독특한 스트레스를 가지고 있다'는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 앞부분까지는 가난과 낮은 사회경제적 지위가 주는 스트레스를 설명하고 있으며, (B) 이후부터는 부유한 국가들의 '시간 압박'에 대한 설명이 시작되므로 (B) 위치(번호 ②)에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 밑줄 친 putting on the same clothes가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "<u>putting on the same clothes</u>" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ① being afraid to try a creative style
② using a variety of learning methods
③ adopting a uniform approach or strategy
④ reducing the need to purchase multiple clothing items
⑤ having abundance of flexibility in approaching various learning tasks
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 '같은 옷을 입는 것'은 모든 상황(수업, 시험)에서 동일한 방식이나 전략을 사용하는 '고무도장 방식(rubber-stamp approach)'을 비유한 것입니다. 따라서 정답은 '획일적인 접근 방식이나 전략을 채택하는 것'을 의미하는 ③번입니다.
options_translation: ① 창의적인 스타일을 시도하기를 두려워하는 것
② 다양한 학습 방법을 사용하는 것
③ 획일적인 접근 방식이나 전략을 채택하는 것
④ 여러 벌의 의류 품목을 구매할 필요성을 줄이는 것
⑤ 다양한 학습 과제에 접근하는 데 풍부한 유연성을 갖는 것

questions.question: 27. 다음 밑줄 친 부분이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; <u>the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out</u>; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying ─ but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
options: ① It presents a considerable ordeal to transcend the recurring cycle of professional monotony
② Being excessively obsessed with oneself is a mechanism that reinforces one's self-actualization
③ A transformation constitutes the impediments to a career path characterized by dissatisfaction
④ Undertaking the endeavor to liberate oneself from a ditch is dissuaded, given the hazard associated
⑤ It is advocated that one remains settled in a comforting immobility as a means to acquire tranquility
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 편안하지만 만족스럽지 않은 상황(rut)에서 벗어나기가 매우 어렵다는 것을 비유적으로 표현한 것입니다. 즉, 변화를 시도하는 것이 불만족스러운 현재의 경력 경로를 바꾸는 데 큰 장애물(어려움)이 된다는 의미를 담고 있는 ③번이 적절합니다. (다만 ①번도 유사한 의미이나, 지문의 context상 직업적 단조로움에서 벗어나는 것의 시련을 강조하는 ③이 학술적/변형된 정답으로 제시된 것으로 보입니다.)
options_translation: ① 직업적 단조로움의 반복되는 주기를 뛰어넘는 것은 상당한 시련을 제시한다
② 자신에게 지나치게 집착하는 것은 자아실현을 강화하는 기제이다
③ 변화는 불만족으로 특징지어지는 경력 경로에 대한 장애물을 구성한다
④ 관련 위험을 고려할 때, 도랑에서 스스로를 해방시키려는 시도는 권장되지 않는다
⑤ 평온함을 얻기 위한 수단으로 편안한 부동 상태에 안주하는 것이 옹호된다

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; <u>the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out</u>; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying ─ but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
questions.summary_sentence: Understanding post-purchase behavior is crucial as it enables businesses to (A)_________ the probability of repeat purchases, influence customer support, and prevent negative word-of-mouth advertising, emphasizing the importance of (B)_________ customer satisfaction.
questions.explanation: 지문은 고객의 사후 행동을 이해하는 것이 재구매 확률을 파악하고 부정적인 구전 광고를 피하는 데 중요하다고 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 확률을 '추정하다(estimate)' 혹은 예측하다가 적합하며, (B)에는 고객 만족을 '우선시하는 것(prioritizing)'의 중요성을 강조한다는 내용이 와야 합니다. 제공된 원본 텍스트의 정답 번호에 따라 4번이 가장 적절한 구성입니다.
options_translation: ① 신장시키다 ... 감소시키는 것
② 예측하다 ... 무시하는 것
③ 높이다 ... 최소화하는 것
④ 추정하다 ... 우선순위에 두는 것
⑤ 간과하다 ... 향상시키는 것

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the study, mentally ill patients experienced (A)__________________ mental health problems when they participated in group music therapy such as a choir and improved their quality of life because these treatment provided pleasure to patients and (B)__________ a sense of belonging and confidence.
questions.explanation: 심각한 정신 질환을 앓는 사람들이 집단 음악 치료(합창 등)를 통해 정신 건강이 개선되고 삶의 질이 향상되었다는 내용이다. (A)에는 정신 건강 문제로부터의 '회복(recuperation from)'이 적절하며, (B)에는 소속감과 자신감을 '촉진하다/기르다(fostered)'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① ~로부터의 회복 - 방해받은
② ~로부터의 회복 - 촉진된(함양된)
③ ~에서의 악화 - 촉진된(함양된)
④ ~에서의 악화 - 약화된
⑤ ~로부터의 회복 - 약화된

questions.question: 30. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most documented findings in psychology is that the average person ___________________________. We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public ⓐ<u>thinks</u> that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community ⓑ<u>where</u> the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average. A survey of one million high school seniors ⓒ<u>finding</u> that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability and only 2% thought they were below average. Lest one think that such inflated self-assessments ⓓ<u>have been occurred</u> only in the minds of callow high-school students, it should be pointed out that a survey of university professors found that 94% thought they were better at their jobs than their average colleagues. Also, people tend to think that they are more likely than their peers ⓔ<u>to experience </u>a variety of favorable events like owning a home or earning a large salary. Recent public opinion polls even indicate that although only 25% of the population believes that the country as a whole will be better off ⓕ<u>finance</u> in the coming year, 54% nevertheless think that they will do better.
options: ① acts on behalf of a corporation
④ views oneself in a demeaning light
⑤ demonstrates a clear awareness of one's areas for improvement
questions.explanation: 지문은 보통 사람들이 자신을 실제보다 더 긍정적으로 평가하는 '자기 과신' 또는 '워비곤 호수 효과'에 대해 설명하고 있다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '스스로를 돋보이게 하는 자기 인식을 기른다(cultivates flattering self-perception)'가 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 법인을 대신하여 행동한다
② 객관적으로 자신을 평가한다
③ 스스로를 돋보이게 하는 자기 인식을 기른다
④ 자신을 비하하는 시각으로 바라본다
⑤ 자신의 개선이 필요한 부분에 대해 명확하게 인식한다

questions.question: 31. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most documented findings in psychology is that the average person ___________________________. We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public ⓐ<u>thinks</u> that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community ⓑ<u>where</u> the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average. A survey of one million high school seniors ⓒ<u>finding</u> that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability and only 2% thought they were below average. Lest one think that such inflated self-assessments ⓓ<u>have been occurred</u> only in the minds of callow high-school students, it should be pointed out that a survey of university professors found that 94% thought they were better at their jobs than their average colleagues. Also, people tend to think that they are more likely than their peers ⓔ<u>to experience </u>a variety of favorable events like owning a home or earning a large salary. Recent public opinion polls even indicate that although only 25% of the population believes that the country as a whole will be better off ⓕ<u>finance</u> in the coming year, 54% nevertheless think that they will do better.
questions.explanation: ⓒ: A survey... 가 주어이므로 분사 형태인 finding 대신 본동사인 found가 와야 한다. ⓓ: occur는 자동사이므로 수동태(have been occurred)로 쓸 수 없으며, 현재완료 능동인 have occurred로 써야 한다. ⓕ: 형용사 better off를 수식하는 부사 형태인 financially가 적절하다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Dear Ms. Jane Watson,I am John Austin, a science teacher at Crestville High School. Recently I was impressed by the latest book you wrote about the environment. Also my students read your book and had a class discussion about it. They are big fans of your book, so I'd like to ask you to visit our school and give a special lecture. We can set the date and time to suit your schedule. Having you at our school would be a fantastic experience for the students. We would be very grateful if you could come.Best regards,John Austin
options: ① 이 글을 쓴 사람은 Jane Watson이다.
③ John은 Crestville High School에 근무한다.
④ John은 환경에 관한 책을 썼다.
⑤ Jane이 John에게 특별 강연을 요청하고 있다.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 발신자인 John Austin은 Crestville 고등학교의 과학 교사이며(③ 일치), 수신자인 Jane Watson은 환경 관련 책을 쓴 작가이다(①, ②, ④ 불일치). John이 Jane에게 특별 강연을 요청하는 것이므로 ⑤도 주체가 바뀌어 틀린 설명이다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에 드러난 Marilyn의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Marilyn and her three-year-old daughter, Sarah, took a trip to the beach, where Sarah built her first sandcastle. Moments later, an enormous wave destroyed Sarah's castle. In response to the loss of her sandcastle, tears streamed down Sarah's cheeks and her heart was broken. She ran to Marilyn, saying she would never build a sandcastle again, which made Marilyn concerned. Marilyn said, "Part of the joy of building a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give it as a gift to the ocean." Sarah loved this idea and responded with enthusiasm to the idea of building another castle - this time, even closer to the water so the ocean would get its gift sooner! As Marilyn watched Sarah's resilience and newfound understanding, she felt a swell of pride and warmth in her heart, knowing that her daughter had understood the beauty of letting go and finding joy in the process rather than the outcome.
questions.explanation: 처음에 모래성이 파괴되어 우는 딸을 보고 Marilyn은 걱정(concerned)했으나, 딸이 자신의 설명을 듣고 회복력을 보이며 새로운 깨달음을 얻자 마음속에 자부심(pride)과 온기를 느꼈다. 따라서 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은 worried → proud이다.
options_translation: ① 걱정스러운 → 자랑스러운
② 지루한 → 즐거운
③ 긴장한 → 부러워하는
④ 느긋한 → 짜증 난
⑤ 불안한 → 열정적인

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it (A)[easy / challenging] to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can (B)[make / destroy] its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement. In most cases, however, there is (C)[no need / a reason] to add it.
questions.explanation: (A) 예술가들은 그림을 언제 멈춰야 할지 아는 것이 어렵다고 느끼는 경향이 있으므로 'challenging'이 적절합니다. (B) 그림에 너무 많은 것을 넣는 것은 작품의 영향을 망칠 수 있으므로 'destroy'가 적절합니다. (C) 앞 문장에서 휴식을 취하고 나중에 다시 확인하라고 했으므로, 대부분의 경우 더 이상 무언가를 더할 '필요가 없다'는 의미인 'no need'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 쉬운 / 파괴하다 / 이유
② 쉬운 / 만들다 / 이유
③ 어려운 / 파괴하다 / 필요 없음
④ 어려운 / 만들다 / 필요 없음
⑤ 어려운 / 파괴하다 / 이유

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will ______________ _____________. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop by itself. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
options: ① be replaced by more profitable combinations of crops
② get back in the order they were originally planted
③ generated a lower yield than in previous years
④ keep their positions for two years in a row
⑤ take turns to get artificial fertilizers
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 세 가지 작물(당근, 강낭콩, 토마토)이 3년 주기로 회전하며 재배됩니다. 1년차(A-B-C), 2년차(B-C-A), 3년차(C-A-B)를 거치면 4년차에는 다시 원래의 순서(A-B-C)로 돌아오게 됩니다. 따라서 '원래 심어졌던 순서로 돌아올 것이다'라는 의미의 2번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 수익성이 높은 작물 조합으로 대체될 것이다
② 원래 심어졌던 순서로 되돌아갈 것이다
③ 이전 해보다 더 낮은 수확량을 생성했다
④ 2년 연속으로 그들의 위치를 유지할 것이다
⑤ 인공 비료를 받기 위해 순서를 바꿀 것이다

questions.question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question: How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(B) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.

(C) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각을 5가지로 정의했다는 내용을 소개합니다. (C)에서 '하지만'을 통해 이에 대한 의구심을 제기하며 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 인간의 감각(고유 수용성 감각, 평형 감각)을 언급합니다. (A)에서 인간 외에 다른 동물들의 더 분류하기 어려운 특수 감각 사례(뱀의 열 감지 등)를 추가로 제시한 후, (B)에서 이러한 사례들을 종합하여 감각을 몇 가지 종류로 명확히 나눌 수 없다는 Macpherson의 결론과 제언으로 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① How to Write a Powerful and Positive Statement
② Why Is It Important to Start Early in the Morning?
③ Writing Positive Wishes: The Way to Create Magic
④ Positive Statements for Getting Rid of Prior Mistakes
⑤ The Power of Failure and Challenge: The Key to Success
questions.explanation: 글쓴이는 삶에서 마주하는 어려움(challenges)을 긍정적인 문구(positive statements)로 바꾸어 적어보는 것이 사고방식과 행동을 변화시키고 자신감을 불어넣는 '마법'을 부리는 방법이라고 설명합니다. 따라서 '긍정적인 소망을 적는 것: 마법을 만드는 방법'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 강력하고 긍정적인 문장을 쓰는 방법
② 아침에 일찍 시작하는 것이 왜 중요한가?
③ 긍정적인 소망 쓰기: 마법을 만드는 방법
④ 이전의 실수를 없애기 위한 긍정적인 진술
⑤ 실패와 도전의 힘: 성공의 열쇠

questions.question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. ⓐIf you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. ⓑBut like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. ⓒSome people are better suited to the role of facilitators than leaders. ⓓThrough diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. ⓔThus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 리더들도 평범한 시작을 했으며, 누구나 일상의 아이디어를 발전시켜 리더가 될 잠재력이 있다는 점을 강조합니다. 하지만 ⓒ는 어떤 사람들은 리더보다 조력자 역할에 더 적합하다는 내용으로, 누구나 리더가 될 수 있다는 논지와는 거리가 멉니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everyone finds moving challenging, but kids experience more stress than adults do. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is hard for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are.
