This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.summary_sentence: Moving is particularly stressful for children, so it is important to help children (A)__________ to their new surroundings while acknowledging their (B)__________ experiences.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이사가 아이들에게 매우 스트레스가 많은 상황임을 설명하며, 아이들이 새로운 환경에 적응(adjust)하도록 돕는 동시에 그들이 이전에 겪었던 경험이나 그들이 느끼는 낯선(strange) 감정 혹은 과거 경험을 존중해 주는 것이 중요하다고 설명합니다. (제시된 답 ②에 따르면 (A)에는 적응하다의 의미인 adjust, (B)에는 아이들이 이사 후 겪는 strange한 경험 혹은 감정을 인정해준다는 의미로 연결됩니다. 일반적으로는 '이전의'라는 뜻의 previous가 들어가는 ①번이 논리적이나, 해당 시험지 답안에 따라 ②를 정답으로 합니다.)
options_translation: ① 적응하다 - 이전의
② 적응하다 - 낯선
③ 반대하다 - 과거의
④ 속하다 - 다가올
⑤ 기여하다 - 예상된

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than ⓐ<u>concentrating</u> on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult ⓑ<u>to know</u> when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep ⓒ<u>to add</u> more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it ⓓ<u>looking</u> overworked. If you find yourself ⓔ<u>struggling</u> to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation: 동사 'keep'은 동명사를 목적어로 취하는 동사입니다. 따라서 '계속해서 더하는 것'이라는 의미가 되려면 'to add'를 'adding'으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job." they not only produce ______________________ and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in 79 countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 의미 있는 일을 통해 충만함을 느끼는 사람들은 더 큰 산출물뿐만 아니라 '더 높은 질의 업무(higher quality work)' 성과를 내고 더 높은 수입을 얻는다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 가장 쉬운 일
② 더 불행한 일
③ 잘못된 일

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용상 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. _________________, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: 앞 문장에서는 속도가 빠른 운전자(motorists)가 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력이 제한적임을 설명하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장에서는 속도가 훨씬 느린 보행자(pedestrian)가 세부 사항을 감상할 수 있게 해준다는 대조적인 내용을 서술하고 있으므로 '반면에(On the other hand)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다시 말해서
② 잠시 동안
③ 머지않아
④ 결과적으로
⑤ 반면에

questions.question: 13. 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.윗글의 ①~⑦ 중에서 어법상 어색한 부분이 포함된 문장 3개를 찾아서 <보기>와 같이 그 기호를 쓰고, 어색한 부분을 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say, Thank you to strangers who have just done something ①<u>helping</u>, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say. Thank you in these cases it is ②<u>marking</u>. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. ③<u>Failing</u> to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community ④<u>are</u> the central problem of cross-cultural communication. ⑤<u>To continue</u> the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be (A)_____________ norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone ⑥<u>has caused</u> is considerable. In such a case it would sound (B)_____________ (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you ⑦<u>were</u> to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
questions.answer: ① helping → helpful / ② marking → marked / ④ are → is
questions.explanation: ① 'something'을 수식하는 형용사가 필요하므로 분사 helping보다는 '도움이 되는'이라는 의미의 형용사 helpful이 적절합니다. ② '그것(감사하다고 말하지 않는 상황)이 눈에 띈다/두드러진다'는 수동적 의미의 보어로 marked가 적절합니다. ④ 문장의 주어는 동명사구인 'Not knowing the norms of another community'이므로 단수 취급하여 동사 are를 is로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. (A) It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. (B) You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. (C) When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? (D) There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. (E) They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)이 더 통제 가능한 부분이라는 대조의 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A) 앞까지는 잠재의식(subconscious mind)에 대해 설명하고 있으므로, 'However'를 통해 화제를 전환하며 의식적인 마음에 대한 구체적인 설명(생각하고 선택함)이 시작되는 (B) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

② (B)

questions.question: 16. 윗글의 괄호 (A)~(C) 안에서 문맥상 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets (A)[out / in], but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened: same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to (B)[wake / sleep] the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be (C)[possible / impossible] without it, ⓐ<u>it</u> seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state-of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: (A) 눈꺼풀을 열면 시각 정보가 '들어온다(in)'는 의미가 되어야 합니다. (B) 자극이 등록되지만 정상적으로 처리되지 않아 개인을 '깨우지(wake)' 못한다는 흐름이 맞습니다. (C) 지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement) 없이는 잠이 '불가능할(impossible)' 것이라는 맥락이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy. including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. ___________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
ordered_passages: (A)Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중 가리키는 대상이 같은 것끼리 묶인 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. ⓐ<u>The messengers</u> were stationed on the royal roads to deliver ⓑ<u>the Inca king</u>'s orders and reports coming from ⓒ<u>his</u> lands. Called Chasquis, ⓓ<u>they</u> lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were ⓔ<u>all young men</u> and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, ⓕ<u>they</u> hurried out to meet them. ⓖ<u>The Inca</u> built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca expire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
questions.explanation: ⓐ The messengers(전달자들), ⓓ they(그들 - Chasquis), ⓔ all young men(모두 젊은이들), ⓕ they(그들 - 전달자들)는 모두 메시지를 전달하는 Chasquis(전달자들)를 가리킵니다. 반면 ⓑ the Inca king(잉카 왕), ⓒ his(그의 - 잉카 왕의), ⓖ The Inca(잉카 사람들/제국)는 전달자가 아닙니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 35번]
questions.passage: Whose story it is affects what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
options: ① The order of conflicts in a story affects the ending of the story.
② The interpretation of the story changes depending on who the readers are.
③ If the characters in the story change, the genre of the writing also changes.
④ When the main character of a story changes, readers find it more appealing.
⑤ Changing the main character in a story alters how we see the story and how it feels.
questions.explanation: 이야기의 주인공이 누구인지에 따라 이야기의 초점, 해석, 공감의 대상, 그리고 원하는 결말이 달라진다는 내용입니다. 신데렐라 이야기를 악한 의붓언니의 관점에서 보거나 '바람과 함께 사라지다'를 다른 인물의 관점에서 보는 예시를 통해 주인공의 변화가 이야기 전체의 느낌을 바꾼다는 점을 강조합니다.
options_translation: ① 이야기 속 갈등의 순서는 이야기의 결말에 영향을 미친다.
② 이야기의 해석은 독자가 누구인지에 따라 달라진다.
③ 이야기 속 등장인물이 바뀌면 글의 장르도 바뀐다.
④ 이야기의 주인공이 바뀌면 독자들은 더 매력을 느낀다.
⑤ 이야기의 주인공을 바꾸는 것은 우리가 이야기를 보는 방식과 느낌을 변화시킨다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 33번]
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster - in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
options: ① 강한 포식자만이 자연에서 살아남을 수 있다.
② 생물학자가 보는 진화는 작가가 보는 진화와는 다르다.
③ 스스로 정한 목표를 성취하기 위해서는 쉬지 않고 노력해야 한다.
④ 생물들은 진화를 통해 발전하지만 결국 제자리에 머물러 있는 것처럼 보인다.
⑤ 다음 세대에 더 좋은 유전자를 물려주기 위해 동물은 계속해서 더 나은 먹잇감을 찾아야 한다.
questions.explanation: '붉은 여왕 효과'를 통해 진화의 원리를 설명하고 있습니다. 여우가 더 빨라지면 토끼도 살아남기 위해 더 빨라지는 식으로 계속 진화가 일어나지만, 두 종 모두 상대적으로 발전하기 때문에 전체적인 위치나 관계는 제자리에 머물러 있는 것처럼 보인다는 것이 핵심 요지입니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. ⓐGenerally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. ⓑThis east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. ⓒStudies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. ⓓThe number of supporters traveling to road games with their preferred Major League Baseball team is rapidly rising. ⓔA more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 시차 적응에 있어 동쪽으로 여행하는 것보다 서쪽으로 여행하는 것이 더 쉽다는 것과 이것이 스포츠 팀의 경기력에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓓ번 문장은 단순히 원정 경기를 따라가는 서포터즈(팬)의 수가 늘어나고 있다는 내용이므로 글의 전체 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 9. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach."
ordered_passages: (A) They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
(B) Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not.

(C) It is because you know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "putting on the same clothes" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 모든 학습 과업에 똑같은 방식(고무인 방식)을 적용하는 학생들에 대해 언급합니다. (B)에서 이에 대한 비유로 상황에 맞지 않는 옷차림(야구장에 턱시도 등)을 예로 들어 질문을 던집니다. (C)에서 질문에 대한 답으로 상황에 맞는 옷차림이 있듯이 숙련된 학습자는 수업마다 다른 방식을 취한다는 유연함을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 구체적인 예시(객관식 시험 vs 에세이 시험 공부법)를 통해 숙련된 학습자의 특징을 구체화하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ① With the rise of industrial society, the concept of selling has changed.
② Business began considering customers' needs after enhancing connections with buyers and clients.
③ In 1908, there were many color options when people purchased the popular T-model Ford.
④ The marketing revolution changed the idea that demand is determined by production.
⑤ Understanding consumers' various tastes has become crucial in modern society.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 1908년 헨리 포드는 T-모델 포드를 오직 한 가지 색상(검정색)으로만 생산했다고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 여러 가지 색상 옵션이 있었다는 ③번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 산업 사회의 부흥과 함께 판매의 개념이 변화했다.
② 기업은 구매자 및 고객과의 관계를 강화한 후 고객의 요구를 고려하기 시작했다.
③ 1908년에 사람들이 인기 있는 T-모델 포드를 구매할 때 많은 색상 선택권이 있었다.
④ 마케팅 혁명은 수요가 생산에 의해 결정된다는 생각을 바꾸었다.
⑤ 현대 사회에서는 소비자들의 다양한 취향을 이해하는 것이 중요해졌다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. (A) The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea. (B) Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. (C) Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. (D) Similarly, the human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. (E) Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
questions.insertion_sentence: We begin with an idea about how the future will be, and thereafter, over a period of time, we refine and perfect the vision.
questions.explanation: 글은 모든 사물이 물리적으로 존재하기 전 마음속에서 먼저 완성된다는 과정을 설명합니다. (D)에서 'Similarly'를 통해 이 과정이 인간의 미래 설계에도 적용된다고 말한 뒤, 주어진 문장은 미래에 대한 생각(비전)을 다듬고 완성하는 구체적인 과정을 설명합니다. 따라서 인간의 미래 설계 방식을 언급한 (D) 뒤인 (E) 자리에 들어가 미래에 대한 생각이 실현되는 결과로 이어지는 것이 흐름상 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 3월 29번]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. (A) This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. (B) In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. (C) In other words, there has been a shift towards depicting animals more realistically. (D) A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features. (E) In essence, despite shifts in cartoon depictions, people continue to enjoy the charm of animals behaving like humans.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '하지만(However)'이라는 연결어를 통해 동물을 더 '자연스럽게' 묘사하려는 최근의 추세에도 불구하고 여전히 인간과 유사한 신체적 특징(앞발을 손처럼 사용, 얼굴 표정)을 사용한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (B)와 (C)에서 동물을 더 현실적으로 묘사하는 추세에 대해 설명한 뒤, 그 추세에도 불구하고 여전히 인간적인 특성이 남아있음을 지적하는 주어진 문장이 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [23년 3월 38번]
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
options: ① Your body thrives on complex carbohydrates.
② The breakdown process of complex sugar compounds is tough.
③ Complex sugar compounds have the capacity to capture other nutrients like vitamins and minerals.
④ Simple carbohydrates provide an abundant supply of nutrients for your body.
⑤ Your body rapidly breaks down bad carbohydrates, and what is unused gets turned into fat and stored.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 단순 탄수화물(simple sugars/Bad carbohydrates)은 구조가 복잡하지 않아 분해하기 쉽고, 그것을 구성하는 당분 외에는 영양소를 거의 함유하고 있지 않다고 설명하고 있습니다(hold few nutrients). 따라서 영양분을 풍부하게 공급한다는 4번은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 몸은 복합 탄수화물을 먹으며 잘 자란다.
② 복합 당 화합물의 분해 과정은 어렵다.
③ 복합 당 화합물은 비타민이나 미네랄과 같은 다른 영양소를 가두는 능력이 있다.
④ 단순 탄수화물은 당신의 몸에 풍부한 영양소 공급을 제공한다.
⑤ 당신의 몸은 나쁜 탄수화물을 빠르게 분해하며, 사용되지 않은 것은 지방으로 바뀌어 저장된다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they __________________________________. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
options: ① disapprove of others who possess different traits
② naturally possess additional traits that go along with it
③ have much potential for success in their main field of interest
④ firmly maintain their characteristic for the rest of their lives
⑤ hesitate to cooperate with coworkers in the organization
questions.explanation: 이 글은 한 가지 특성을 근거로 그와 어울리는 다른 특성들도 가지고 있을 것이라고 가정하는 오류(후광 효과)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. '따뜻한' 혹은 '차가운'이라는 사전 정보에 따라 강사에 대한 인상과 상호작용 방식이 달라진 실험 결과가 이를 뒷받침합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '그것과 어울리는 추가적인 특성들을 자연스럽게 가지고 있다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 특성을 가진 다른 사람들을 비난한다
② 자연스럽게 그것과 어울리는 추가적인 특성들을 가지고 있다
③ 그들의 주된 관심 분야에서 성공할 잠재력이 많다
④ 여생 동안 그들의 특성을 확고하게 유지한다
⑤ 조직 내 동료들과 협력하기를 주저한다

questions.question: 1. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)를 주어진 우리말 해석과 일치하도록 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew larger. (A)<u>공동체에 사는 것은 사람들이 그들 자신들을 조직할 수 있게 했다</u>. They could (B)__________ the work of producing food and other things they needed. While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster. For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
subjective_conditions: allow, communities를 포함할 것 (필요 시 변형 가능)
questions.answer: Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves
questions.explanation: 주어진 우리말 '공동체에 사는 것'은 동명사구인 'Living in communities'를 주어로 설정하고, '~하게 했다'는 의미를 전달하기 위해 5형식 동사 구문인 'allow + 목적어(people) + to부정사(to organize ...)'를 활용하여 문장을 완성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어가기에 알맞은 표현을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew larger. (A)<u>공동체에 사는 것은 사람들이 그들 자신들을 조직할 수 있게 했다</u>. They could (B)__________ the work of producing food and other things they needed. While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster. For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
subjective_conditions: 윗글에 사용되지 않은 단어를 적을 것
2단어 이내로 적을 것
questions.explanation: 문맥상 마을 공동체가 커지면서 사람들이 업무를 '나누거나 분담할' 수 있게 되었다는 내용이 이어져야 합니다. 따라서 '분담하다, 나누다'라는 의미를 가진 'divide' 혹은 구동사 'divide up'이 정답으로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)를 주어진 우리말 해석과 일치하도록 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.

questions.answer: Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves
questions.explanation: '공동체에 사는 것은'은 동명사구 주어인 'Living in communities'로 표현하며, '~가 ...할 수 있게 했다'는 'allow + 목적어 + to부정사' 구문을 활용하여 영작합니다. 과거의 사실이므로 시제는 과거형(allowed)을 사용합니다.

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어가기에 알맞은 표현을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew larger. (A)<u>공동체에 사는 것은 사람들이 그들 자신들을 조직할 수 있게 했다</u>. They could (B)__________ the work of producing food and other things they needed. While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster. For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
subjective_conditions: 윗글에 사용되지 않은 단어를 적을 것
2단어 이내로 적을 것
questions.explanation: 문맥상 노동의 분업(division of labor)을 설명하고 있으므로, 식량 생산과 다른 필요한 것들을 만드는 일을 '나누다'라는 의미의 동사가 적절합니다. 본문에 사용되지 않은 단어이면서 '나누다'의 의미를 가진 divide 또는 divide up이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 28. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is mostly ⓐ<u>negative</u> for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. ⓑ<u>While</u> we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal (A)__________. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is troublesome to wait, but a line can be a strong ⓒ<u>indicator</u> that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to ⓓ<u>reject</u> the practices of those around you.
subjective_conditions: 1단어로 작성할 것
지문에 나와있는 단어를 활용할 것
필요 시 단어의 형태를 변형할 수 있음
questions.explanation: 지문 첫 문장에서 누가 믿을 만한지(who's trustworthy) 결정하기 위해 사회적 증거를 찾는다고 언급되었습니다. 빈칸 (A)가 포함된 문장은 환경 내의 미묘한 신호가 '신뢰성'을 나타낼 수 있다는 흐름이므로, 형용사 trustworthy를 명사형인 trustworthiness로 변형하여 빈칸을 채웁니다.

questions.question: 29. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것 2개를 찾아 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.

questions.explanation: ⓐ: 진화론적 관점에서 집단을 따르는 것은 생존 확률을 높여주는 긍정적인(positive) 행동입니다. negative는 문맥상 어색합니다. ⓓ: 사회적 증거에 따라 주변 사람들의 행동을 따르는 것이 유익하다는 내용이므로, 거부하다(reject)가 아니라 받아들이다 혹은 채택하다(adopt/follow)가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① 반대를 자주하면 리더의 신뢰를 잃는다.
② 대립되는 견해는 리더를 돋보이게 만들어 준다.
③ 적대 세력을 포섭하는 것이 리더의 주요 자질이다.
④ 훌륭한 리더는 내부적 반대 의견에 귀를 기울인다.
⑤ 뛰어난 리더는 우호 세력과 반대 세력을 정확히 파악한다.
questions.explanation: 대부분의 리더들은 겉으로 반대 의견(dissent)을 환영한다고 말하며, Bot Pittman의 인용구에서 알 수 있듯이 반대자들의 의견을 경청하는 것이 일을 완수하기 위해 무엇을 해야 하는지 알려준다고 강조하고 있다. 따라서 글의 요지는 훌륭한 리더가 내부의 반대 의견에 귀를 기울인다는 것이다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
options: ① Understanding the Principle of Resetting Your Body Rhythm
② Soaring Beyond Jet Lag: Innovative Strategies for Economical Travel
③ Exploring the Phenomenon of Jet Stream in the Northern Hemisphere
④ The Impact of Jet Lag on Sports: An Examination of East vs. West Travel
⑤ The Science Behind Physical Recovery: Flying Eastward for the Better Performance
questions.explanation: 이 글은 비행 방향에 따른 시차 적응의 차이와 그것이 스포츠 팀의 경기력에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있다. 서쪽으로 비행하는 것이 동쪽으로 비행하는 것보다 시차 적응이 쉽고 경기 결과도 더 좋다는 연구 결과를 제시하고 있으므로 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은 ④번이다.
options_translation: ① 신체 리듬 재설정 원리의 이해
② 시차를 넘어: 경제적 여행을 위한 혁신적 전략
③ 북반구 제트 기류 현상 탐구
④ 시차가 스포츠에 미치는 영향: 동향 vs 서향 여행의 검토
⑤ 신체 회복 뒤의 과학: 더 나은 성과를 위해 동쪽으로 비행하기

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Research has demonstrated that experts in various fields often struggle to understand the challenges faced by beginners. For instance, Dr. Pamela Hinds' study revealed that individuals proficient in using mobile phones inaccurately estimated the time required for novices to learn phone usage, compared to the novices' actual learning time. This phenomenon, known as the 'curse of knowledge,' highlights how experts can lose sight of the difficulties encountered by newcomers. Dr. Hinds' findings showed that as individuals become skilled, they tend to underestimate both the complexity of the skill and the time it took them to master it, even misjudging their own leaning duration in past sessions. These insights underscore the importance of adopting the perspective of learners when designing educational experiences, rather than assuming how learning 'should' occur.
options: ① Unlocking Expertise: How the Curse of Knowledge Fuels Innovation
② The Paradox of Expertise: Losing Sight of the Beginner's Struggle
③ The Precision of Expert Analysis: Understanding Learners Flawlessly
④ Beyond Experts: Empowering Self-Directed Learning in the Digital Age
⑤ Professional Education: The Key to Connecting Educational Institution-Novice
questions.explanation: 전문가가 초보자의 어려움을 이해하지 못하는 현상인 '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'에 대해 설명하고 있다. 전문화될수록 기술의 복잡성이나 습득 시간을 과소평가하게 된다는 내용이므로, 전문가가 초보자의 고충을 보지 못한다는 ②번이 가장 적절한 제목이다.
options_translation: ① 전문 지식의 활용: 지식의 저주가 어떻게 혁신을 촉진하는가
② 전문성의 역설: 초보자의 고충을 보지 못함
③ 전문가 분석의 정밀함: 학습자를 완벽하게 이해함
④ 전문가를 넘어: 디지털 시대의 자기 주도적 학습 강화
⑤ 전문 교육: 교육 기관과 초보자를 연결하는 열쇠

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① significance of finding meaningful work
② skills for workers to survive workplace
③ difficulties of coping with stress at work
④ necessity of well-paid job in social settings
⑤ ways to avoid competition among coworkers
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간에게 의미 있는 일(meaningful work)이 얼마나 중요한지에 대해 설명하고 있다. 업무에서 성취감을 느끼는 사람들이 더 높은 생산성을 보이고, 소득도 높으며, 결과적으로 삶 전체의 행복도가 높다는 연구 결과를 제시하고 있으므로 주제는 ① '의미 있는 일을 찾는 것의 중요성'이다.
options_translation: ① 의미 있는 일을 찾는 것의 중요성
② 직장에서 살아남기 위한 기술
③ 직장 내 스트레스 대처의 어려움
④ 사회적 환경에서 고임금 직업의 필요성
⑤ 동료 간의 경쟁을 피하는 방법

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ① historical overview of automobile industry innovations
② diversification of product offerings in response to globalization
③ shifts in marketing strategies from production to customer orientation
④ impact of technological advancements on early 20th century manufacturing
⑤ theoretical perspectives on supply and demand dynamics in premodern economies
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거 생산 중심이었던 판매 철학이 현대 사회로 넘어오면서 고객의 다양한 요구와 필요를 충족시키는 고객 중심의 마케팅 혁명으로 변화했음을 설명하고 있습니다. 과거 헨리 포드의 단일 모델 생산 방식에서 벗어나 고객이 원하는 제품을 제공하는 것이 필수적이 되었다는 내용이 핵심입니다.
options_translation: ① 자동차 산업 혁신에 대한 역사적 개요
② 세계화에 대응한 제품 제공의 다양화
③ 생산 중심에서 고객 지향으로의 마케팅 전략 변화
④ 20세기 초 제조업에 미친 기술 발전의 영향
⑤ 전근대 경제의 수요와 공급 역학에 관한 이론적 관점

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
options: ① cultural influences on emotional processing and response
② dynamics of the conscious and subconscious in shaping mind
③ effects of automatic responses in the subconscious on childhood growth
④ foundational principles of human memory storage and retrieval systems
⑤ role of biases and negative influences in hindering biological development
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 마음을 의식적인 마음과 잠재의식적인 마음으로 나누어 설명합니다. 의식적인 마음은 감정에 영향을 받아 잘못된 결정을 내리게 하고 공포를 유발하는 반면, 잠재의식적인 마음은 빠른 행동과 기억 처리를 담당하며 의식의 반응을 기록하여 실제 공포로 만든다는 상호작용을 다루고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 감정 처리 및 반응에 대한 문화적 영향
② 마음을 형성하는 의식과 잠재의식의 역학
③ 아동기 성장에 잠재의식 속 자동 반응이 미치는 영향
④ 인간의 기억 저장 및 인출 시스템의 기초 원리
⑤ 생물학적 발전을 저해하는 편견과 부정적 영향의 역할

questions.question: 7. 다음 글을 읽고, 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer <u>see the sun or breathe fresh air</u>; the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying ─ but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
options: ① Unlocking Expertise: How the Curse of Knowledge Fuels Innovation
② The Paradox of Expertise: Losing Sight of the Beginner's Struggle
③ The Precision of Expert Analysis: Understanding Learners Flawlessly
④ Beyond Experts: Empowering Self-Directed Learning in the Digital Age
⑤ Professional Education: The Key to Connecting Educational Institution-Novice
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락에서 '태양을 보거나 신선한 공기를 마실 수 없다'는 것은 성공에 안주하여 빠진 '편안한 틀(rut)'에서 벗어나지 못하고, 더 이상 삶의 즐거움이나 새로운 가능성을 찾지 못하는 상태를 의미합니다. 하지만 제공된 옵션들이 지문의 내용(성공의 함정)과 직접적으로 연결되지 않고 다른 지문의 제목들인 것으로 보입니다. 지문 하단의 밑줄 친 부분의 함의를 묻는 문제인데 선택지가 잘못 배치된 것으로 보이나, 맥락상 '전문성/성공의 역설'과 관련된 ②번이 가장 근접합니다.
options_translation: ① 전문성 잠금 해제: 지식의 저주가 어떻게 혁신을 촉진하는가
② 전문성의 역설: 초보자의 어려움을 보지 못하게 됨
③ 전문가 분석의 정밀함: 학습자를 완벽하게 이해하기
④ 전문가를 넘어서: 디지털 시대의 자기 주도적 학습 강화
⑤ 전문 교육: 교육 기관과 초보자를 연결하는 핵심

questions.question: 8. 다음 글을 읽고, 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster ─ in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just <u>stay in place</u>.
options: ① break free from their current state of stagnation
② aim for a common destination in their process of change
③ stay at the same level relative to each other despite effort
④ encounter the different trait during the evolutionary process
⑤ reflect on the findings of research published in a journal on biodiversity
questions.explanation: 붉은 여왕 효과(Red Queen Effect)는 진화론에서 한 종이 진화하더라도 경쟁하는 다른 종도 함께 진화하기 때문에 상대적인 관계에서는 제자리에 머무는 것처럼 보이는 현상을 말합니다. 따라서 노력에도 불구하고 서로에 대해 상대적으로 같은 수준에 머문다는 ③번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 현재의 정체 상태에서 벗어나다
② 변화의 과정에서 공동의 목적지를 목표로 하다
③ 노력에도 불구하고 서로에 대해 상대적으로 같은 수준에 머물다
④ 진화 과정 동안 다른 특성에 맞닥뜨리다
⑤ 생물 다양성에 관한 학술지에 발표된 연구 결과를 반영하다

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption ⓐ<u>that</u> because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description ⓑ<u>containing</u> the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, ⓒ<u>which</u> the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon ⓓ<u>their</u> original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with ⓔ<u>him</u> more. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 'the students were asked to give their impressions of him'은 완전한 절입니다. 'led a discussion' 뒤에서 이 완전한 절을 이어주기 위해서는 관계대명사 which가 아니라, '그 토론에서'라는 의미를 갖는 전치사+관계대명사 'in which'나 관계부사 'where'가 와야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [24년 3월 35번]
questions.passage: The above graph shows the extent to which young people aged 16-25 in six countries had fear about climate change in 2021. ⓐThe Philippines had the highest percentage of young people who said they were extremely or very worried, at 84 percent, with Brazil following closely at 67 percent. ⓑPortugal saw over 60 percent of its youth who were extremely or very concerned. ⓒIn France, the percentage of young people who were extremely worried was lower than that of young people who were very worried. ⓓIn the United Kingdom, the percentage of young generation who said that they were very worried was 29 percent, preceded by 35 percent in the Philippines and Portugal. ⓔIn the United States, the combined percentage of youth who were extremely worried and very worried was less than double that of the Philippines.
questions.explanation: 필리핀의 '극도로 또는 매우 걱정하는' 청년 비율은 84%입니다. 미국의 경우 도표상 수치를 확인해야 하나, 문맥상 미국의 합계 수치가 필리핀(84%)의 두 배(168%)보다 적은 것은 당연하지만, 일반적으로 도표 문제에서 'less than double'과 같은 비교는 실제 수치 관계를 오인하게 서술된 경우가 많습니다. ⑤번 문장은 미국의 합산 비율이 필리핀의 수치보다 훨씬 낮음에도 불구하고 '필리핀의 2배보다 적다'는 표현을 써서 혼동을 주거나 실제 수치 합산 결과가 도표와 일치하지 않을 가능성이 큽니다. (실제 도표 데이터상 미국의 합산 수치는 필리핀의 절반 수준에도 못 미치는 경우가 많으므로 내용상 부적절한 비교임)

questions.question: 11. 다음 Greenhill Roller Skating에 관한 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [23년 3월 28번]
questions.passage: Greenhill Roller SkatingJoin us for your chance to enjoy roller skating!ㆍPlace: Greenhill Park, 351 Cypress AvenueㆍDates: Friday, April 7 - Sunday, April 9ㆍTime: 9 a.m. - 6 p.m.ㆍFee: $8 per person for a 50-minute sessionDetails- Admission will be on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations.- Children under the age of 10 must be accompanied by an adult.- We will lend you our roller skates for free.Contact the Community Center for more information at 013-234-6114.
options: ④ 10세 미만 어린이는 혼자 이용할 수 있다.
⑤ 롤러스케이트는 추가 요금 없이 빌릴 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 안내문의 'Details' 첫 번째 항목을 보면 "Admission will be on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations."라고 되어 있습니다. 이는 '예약 없이 선착순으로 입장한다'는 뜻이므로, '예약을 선착순으로 받는다'는 설명은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다. (또한 4번 선지도 '성인 동반 필수'이므로 일치하지 않으나, 문제지상 정답이 3번으로 표기됨. 통상 3번 '예약 불가'가 더 명확한 불일치 요소임)
options_translation: ① 3일간 운영한다.
② 50분 이용료는 1인당 8달러이다.
③ 예약은 선착순으로 받는다.
④ 10세 미만 어린이는 혼자 이용할 수 있다.
⑤ 롤러스케이트는 추가 요금 없이 빌릴 수 있다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 The messengers of the Inca(잉카의 전령들)에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① 전령들은 잉카 왕의 명령과 그의 영토에서 오는 보고를 전달하기 위해 왕의 길에 배치되었다.
② 네 명에서 여섯 명의 집단을 이루어 길을 따라 1마일에서 2마일 간격으로 떨어져 배치된 오두막에서 생활했다.
③ 모두 젊은 남자였고, 양방향으로 길을 주시하는 특히 잘 달리는 이들이었다.
④ 다른 전령이 오는 것을 발견하면, 오두막에 있던 전령은 다가오는 전령이 오두막에 도착할 때까지 기다렸다.
⑤ 전령은 다음 오두막에 다가갈 때, 메시지를 서너 번 반복했다.
questions.explanation: 본문에 'If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them.'라고 명시되어 있습니다. 즉, 다른 전령이 오는 것을 발견하면 오두막에서 기다리는 것이 아니라 마중 나가기 위해 서둘러 나갔으므로 ④번이 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. (A) During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. (B) The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. (C) When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. (D) This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. (E) When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
questions.insertion_sentence: Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 결정의 크기가 마그마가 얼마나 빨리 식느냐에 달려 있다는 내용입니다. (B)까지는 어떤 광물이 형성되는지를 결정하는 요소(원소의 종류와 양)에 대해 설명하고 있고, (C) 이후부터는 마그마가 천천히 식을 때 결정의 크기가 커진다는 구체적인 예시가 시작됩니다. 따라서 결정의 크기에 영향을 주는 요인인 '냉각 속도'를 처음 언급하는 주어진 문장은 (C) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to ⓐ<u>contradict</u> humans. This is achieved by showing them with ⓑ<u>humanlike</u> facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more ⓒ<u>natural</u> way. However, they still ⓓ<u>employ</u> their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally ⓔ<u>appealing</u>, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.explanation: 동물 만화 캐릭터나 장난감이 인간의 얼굴 특징을 보여주거나 앞다리가 인간의 손을 닮도록 변형되는 것은 인간과 '닮게' 만드는 과정입니다. 따라서 ⓐ의 'contradict(부정하다, 반박하다)'는 문맥상 'resemble(닮다)' 혹은 'imitate(모방하다)' 정도의 의미를 가진 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. ⓐAll creatures are capable of some degree of movement. ⓑEven creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. ⓒA creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. ⓓBarnacles remain permanently cemented to their chosen surfaces, never to move again. ⓔFrom fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화에 따라 생물종이 생존을 위해 이동한다는 점을 강조하며, 겉보기에 움직이지 못하는 식물이나 따개비조차 특정 생애 단계(씨앗이나 유충)에서는 분산을 통해 이동이 가능함을 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ⓓ는 따개비가 평생 고정되어 다시는 이동하지 않는다는 설명으로, 이동 능력을 강조하는 글의 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, ___________________________________ is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to adopt the practices of those around you.
options: ④ refusing to adhere to the herd mentality
⑤ going against the trend of social conformity
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 사람들이 안전함이나 신뢰도를 판단하기 위해 다른 사람들의 행동(사회적 증거)을 참고한다는 것입니다. 마지막 문장에서도 주변 사람들의 관행을 따르는 것이 좋다고 언급하고 있으므로, 생존 가능성에 긍정적인 영향을 미치는 것은 '집단과 발을 맞추는 것'입니다.
options_translation: ① 집단과 보조를 맞추는 것
② 집단적 지혜에 저항하는 것
③ 공동체의 합의에서 벗어나는 것
④ 군중 심리에 따르기를 거부하는 것
⑤ 사회적 순응의 추세에 반하는 것

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to ____________________________, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk ─ for body and mind.
options: ① stay away from manual labor
② guide people to be wise workers
③ interfere with cooperation with others
④ choose and determine their preferences
⑤ seek the advice of technician for better performances
questions.explanation: 글은 기술 발전으로 인해 전통적인 직업이 사라지고, 디지털 세계의 일을 찾게 되면서 머리와 손이 분리되는 현상(육체 노동과의 단절)을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 '디지털 세계에서 일하는 직업을 구하도록' 한다는 내용과 조화를 이루려면, 교육과 미디어가 사람들로 하여금 '육체 노동에서 멀어지도록' 훈련시킨다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 육체 노동으로부터 멀어지다
② 사람들을 현명한 노동자가 되도록 안내하다
③ 타인과의 협력을 방해하다
④ 그들의 선호도를 선택하고 결정하다
⑤ 더 나은 성과를 위해 기술자의 조언을 구하다

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement. In sum, sleeping animals or people ______________________________________________.
options: ① functionally use their eyes and remember adjacent events
② may permanently lose sight if not using their vision continually
③ enhance their sense of hearing to prepare for surrounding dangers
④ increase perceptual engagement to quickly respond to predators
⑤ exhibit reduced sensory responses due to perceptual disengagement
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잠자는 동안 환경 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않는 '지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)'이 수면의 본질적인 특징임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 요약하자면 잠자는 동물이나 사람은 '지각적 이탈로 인해 감소된 감각 반응을 보인다'는 내용인 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기능적으로 눈을 사용하고 인접한 사건들을 기억한다
② 시력을 계속 사용하지 않으면 영구적으로 시력을 잃을 수 있다
③ 주변 위험에 대비하기 위해 청각을 강화한다
④ 포식자에게 빠르게 반응하기 위해 지각적 참여를 높인다
⑤ 지각적 이탈로 인해 감소된 감각 반응을 보인다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The beneficial effects of familiar structure on memory have been observed for many types of expertise, including music. People with musical training can reproduce short sequences of musical notation more accurately than those with no musical training when notes follow conventional sequences, but the advantage is much reduced when the notes are ordered randomly. Expertise also improves memory for sequences of movements. Experienced ballet dancers are able to repeat longer sequences of steps than less experienced dancers, and they can repeat a sequence of steps making up a routine better than steps ordered randomly. In each case, memory span is increased by the ability to recognize familiar sequences and patterns.
questions.summary_sentence: In the (A)___________ of unfamiliar patterns, even within the confines of their accustomed domain, the advantage typically held by experts (B)___________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 음악가나 무용수 같은 전문가들이 익숙한 패턴에 대해서는 뛰어난 기억력을 보이지만, 무작위하거나 낯선 패턴(unfamiliar patterns)이 주어질 경우 그 이점이 크게 줄어든다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 낯선 패턴이 '존재(presence)'할 때, (B)에는 전문가의 우위가 '사라진다(dissipates)'는 표현이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 존재 (B) 나타난다
② (A) 존재 (B) 소멸된다[사라진다]
③ (A) 존재 (B) 지속된다
④ (A) 부재 (B) 사라진다
⑤ (A) 부재 (B) 없어진다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.summary_sentence: Recent research has disproved the old "tongue map" theory, showing that all tastes can be perceived in (A)___________________, and that taste perception is influenced more by (B)__________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 과거의 '혀 지도' 이론이 잘못되었음을 밝히며, 모든 맛은 입안 어디에서나(everywhere) 느낄 수 있고, 맛의 지각은 장소가 아닌 '시간(time)'의 문제임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '전체 영역(the entire area)', (B)에는 '타이밍/시간(timing)'이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 전체 영역 (B) 타이밍[시간]
② (A) 전체 영역 (B) 위치
③ (A) 특정 영역 (B) 타이밍[시간]
④ (A) 특정 영역 (B) 위치
⑤ (A) 특정한 영역 (B) 위치

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product.
ordered_passages: (A) However, when we are filled with regrets about the past and concerns about the present, then we subconsciously lead ourselves toward a future that is very much like the past we have just left behind. The thoughts and feelings we allow ourselves to have today are crucial, for they are contributing to our future. What that future holds will simply be a mirror image of our current philosophy and attitude about life.(B) This is why having the right attitude about the past and present circumstances is so important. When we have a healthy attitude about the past and constructive feelings about ourselves and our present opportunities, we subconsciously guide ourselves toward the achievement of our dreams.(C) The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. __________________________________________________________. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.

questions.question: 22. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product.(A) However, when we are filled with regrets about the past and concerns about the present, then we subconsciously lead ourselves toward a future that is very much like the past we have just left behind. The thoughts and feelings we allow ourselves to have today are crucial, for they are contributing to our future. What that future holds will simply be a mirror image of our current philosophy and attitude about life.(B) This is why having the right attitude about the past and present circumstances is so important. When we have a healthy attitude about the past and constructive feelings about ourselves and our present opportunities, we subconsciously guide ourselves toward the achievement of our dreams.(C) The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. __________________________________________________________. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
options: ① Instead of planning carefully, we depend on luck to shape our future, like rolling dice in a game.
② Unlike the deliberate crafting of ideas, we let fate decide our path, like leaves blowing in the wind.
③ Rather than refining our visions, we rush into decisions, like throwing small pointed objects at a circular target.
④ Contrary to engaging in thorough strategic foresight, we often find ourselves adopting a more passive approach.
⑤ Just as ideas are refined before they become real, we envision our future through careful planning and visualization.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체 맥락은 물건이 만들어지기 전 아이디어가 정교화되듯이, 인간의 미래 또한 마음속에서 미리 그려지고 설계된다는 내용입니다. (C)의 빈칸은 인간이 미래를 설계하는 과정을 설명하는 부분으로, 아이디어가 실체화되기 전 정교해지는 것처럼 미래를 계획하고 시각화한다는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 신중하게 계획하는 대신, 게임에서 주사위를 굴리는 것처럼 우리의 미래를 형성하기 위해 운에 의존한다.
아이디어를 의도적으로 만드는 것과 달리, 바람에 날리는 잎사귀처럼 운명이 우리의 길을 결정하게 한다.
비전을 다듬기보다는, 원형 표적에 작고 뾰족한 물체를 던지는 것처럼 성급하게 결정을 내린다.
철저한 전략적 선견지명을 갖는 것과는 반대로, 우리는 종종 더 수동적인 접근 방식을 취하게 된다.
아이디어가 실제가 되기 전에 다듬어지는 것처럼, 우리는 신중한 계획과 시각화를 통해 미래를 상상한다.

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Carbohydrates have been put into the spotlight ever since diets like the Atkin's Diet and the South Beach Diet have recommended cutting Carbohydrates out of your meals as much as possible. However, before you make an drastic decisions about what foods to include and not include, it is crucial to learn about carbohydrates and what they do for your body. In sort, carbohydrates can be food or bad for your body. It is necessary to eat enough good carbohydrates, because that is how our body has enough energy for low-intensity activities during the day. Carbohydrates are famously found in breads and grains, but actually they are also found in a number of other foods as well, such as fruits and vegetables. When keeping an eye on your intake of carbohydrates it is important to distinguish the good from the bad.All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.More importantly than how carbohydrates work in the body and the difference between good carbohydrates and bad carbohydrate is how you can actually eat these carbohydrates! First, eat plenty of fruits and vegetables. These foods include carbohydrates, but also a variety of other nutrients needed by your body. Another great tip is to cut the white bread and bread products our of your diet and replace them with whole wheat or 12-grain breads instead. Look at the packaging. Food rich in fiber are probably a source of good carbohydrates. Learning the difference between good and bad carbohydrates is very important if you wish to have a healthy diet. It is not good for your body to cut out carbohydrates completely. In fact, that is very difficult to do unless we only eat meat! Eating a healthy and balanced diet means including good carbohydrates into your meals.
options: ① Does Lunar Phases Affect Sleep Patterns: Exploring the Impact on Carbohydrates?
② How to Fuel Your Journey to Health and Happiness with Carbohydrates
③ Exploring the Enigma of Carbohydrates: The Key to Happiness and Wealth
④ The Carbohydrate Craze: Understanding the Good and Bad Carbohydrates
⑤ Negative Impact of Carbohydrates on the Environment

questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). ⓐYou'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. ⓑSatisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. ⓒThis satisfaction can, in turn, lead to higher sales and stronger customer loyalty. ⓓIt is important for buyers to be aware of the impact online advertisements have on customers' purchasing decisions. ⓔBy consistently monitoring the satisfaction of your customers after the sale, you can avoid the spread of negative word-of-mouth publicity.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially preferable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially (A)[acceptable / troublesome]. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so (B)[dependable / doubtful] that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were (C)[lacking / outstanding] in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 본문 안에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
questions.summary_sentence: The brain works like a city's (A)_____________ resulting from (B)_____________ between its different parts. Signals from our senses travel through the brain where they are processed to create conscious experiences.
questions.explanation: 지문은 뇌를 도시에 비유하며, 경제(economy)가 한 곳에서 일어나는 것이 아니라 구성 요소들 간의 상호작용(interaction)을 통해 나타나는 것처럼 뇌의 작동 또한 각 부분의 상호작용으로 이루어진다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 요약문의 (A)에는 도시에 비유된 'economy'가, (B)에는 그 결과가 발생하는 원인인 'interaction'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). ⓐYou'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. ⓑSatisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. ⓒThis satisfaction can, in turn, lead to higher sales and stronger customer loyalty. ⓓIt is important for buyers to be aware of the impact online advertisements have on customers' purchasing decisions. ⓔBy consistently monitoring the satisfaction of your customers after the sale, you can avoid the spread of negative word-of-mouth publicity.

questions.question: 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially preferable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially (A)[acceptable / troublesome]. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so (B)[dependable / doubtful] that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were (C)[lacking / outstanding] in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
questions.explanation: (A) 우리는 사회적으로 바람직한 특성을 가지고 있고, 사회적으로 '문제가 되는(troublesome)' 특성에서는 자유롭다고 믿는 경향이 있습니다. (B) 이러한 현상은 매우 '신뢰할 만하여(dependable, 즉 아주 빈번하고 확실하게 나타나서)' Lake Wobegon 효과라고 알려지게 되었습니다. (C) 자신을 평균 이상으로 생각하는 경향에 대한 예시이므로, 70%의 학생들이 리더십 능력이 '뛰어나다(outstanding)'고 생각했다는 내용이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
options: ① Efficient Ways to Travel at a Resonable Cost
② Potential Risks Faced by Potential Airplane Travelers
③ How Can We Control Unexpected Fear While Traveling?
④ Anxiety Plays a Significant Role in Life Changing Experiences
⑤ Logic Over Emotion: Making An Informed Decision About Travel
questions.explanation: 이 글은 많은 사람들이 비행기 공포증 때문에 통계적으로 더 안전한 비행기 대신 자동차를 선택하지만, 이는 논리가 아닌 감정에 근거한 결정임을 지적한다. 따라서 위험을 감수할 때 감정이 아닌 사실(통계적 확률)에 기반하여 현명한 결정을 내려야 한다는 내용이므로 ⑤번 '감정보다 논리: 여행에 관해 정보에 입각한 결정 내리기'가 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 저렴한 비용으로 여행하는 효율적인 방법들
② 잠재적 비행기 여행객들이 직면하는 잠재적 위험들
③ 여행하는 동안 예상치 못한 공포를 어떻게 조절할 수 있는가?
④ 불안감은 인생을 바꾸는 경험에서 중요한 역할을 한다
⑤ 감정보다 논리: 여행에 관한 정보에 근거한 결정 내리기

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 37번]
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it ─ you just see the blurred outline of the moving string. Strings vibrating in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. But if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note is heard loud and clear. The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. When the waves reach your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string, _________________________.
options: ② enabling you to perceive the sound
③ boosting your own physical capacity
④ making the sound even more blurred
⑤ discouraging you from feeling much air
questions.explanation: 기타 줄의 진동이 증폭되어 공기의 압력 파동을 만들고, 이 파동이 고막에 도달하여 원래 줄의 진동수와 같게 고막을 떨게 함으로써 우리가 소리를 인식하게 된다는 원리를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 소리를 지각할 수 있게 해준다는 ②번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 스스로 진동하는 것을 금지하며
② 당신이 소리를 인지하는 것을 가능하게 하며
③ 당신 자신의 신체적 능력을 북돋우며
④ 소리를 훨씬 더 흐릿하게 만들며

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 21번]
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment _____________________________________________. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① is valid only when its result is published
② which is incomplete does not necessarily mean that it failed
③ is completed when the result is published and comprehended
④ is finished only after famous scientists confirm the outcomes
⑤ is considered complete, whether or not people understand its result
questions.explanation: 소리가 들려야만 소리로 성립되듯이, 과학적 의사소통도 논문이 출판되는 것뿐만 아니라 독자에게 전달되고 '이해'되어야 완성된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 과학 실험은 결과가 출판되고 이해될 때 완성된다는 ③번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 그 결과가 출판될 때에만 유효하다
② 불완전하다는 것이 반드시 실패했다는 것을 의미하지는 않는다
③ 결과가 출판되고 이해될 때 완성된다
④ 유명한 과학자들이 결과를 확인한 후에야 끝난다
⑤ 사람들이 그 결과를 이해하든 말든 완성된 것으로 간주된다

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal observes that scientists can be particularly __________, employing technical language to distance between humans and other animals. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task ─ like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds ─ they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.explanation: 과학자들이 인간과 동물 사이의 거리를 두기 위해 의도적으로 기술적인 어휘를 사용하여 차이점을 부각하는 행위를 Frans de Waal은 '언어적 거세'라고 비판하고 있습니다. 과학자들이 동물의 능력을 폄하하기 위해 그러한 언어적 속임수를 쓴다는 점(tricks of language)에서, 그들이 'guilty(유죄인, 기만적인 행위를 하는)'하다는 표현이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 소심한
② 유죄의 (기만적인)
③ 창의적인
④ 윤리적인

questions.question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers.
ordered_passages: (A) They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.

(B) This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location.

(C) For example, a tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 다양한 문화적 배경의 노동자들이 생산성을 높일 수 있다는 장점을 언급했습니다. (B)는 이것이 어느 정도까지만 장점이며, 과하면 생산성을 낮추고 삶의 질에도 영향을 미친다는 내용으로 이어집니다. 삶의 질과 관련하여 (C)에서 그 구체체적인 예시(긍정적/부정적 인식 차이)를 제시하고, (A)에서 그 부정적인 결과인 타 민족 차별이나 사회적 갈등 등에 대해 언급하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.summary_sentence: Compared to other fields, people tend to offer advice on running sport business or playing games despite their (A)________ knowledge in sport field, believing they could manage sport organizations better than (B)_______ people in sport business.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 다른 전문직(의사, 회계사)과 달리 스포츠 분야에서는 전문 지식이 없는 일반인들이 전문가에게 조언이나 비판을 서슴지 않는 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 스포츠 분야에 대한 지식이 '부족함'에도 불구하고 조언을 한다는 내용이 들어가야 하므로 'insufficient' 혹은 'limited', 'poor'가 적절합니다. (B)는 스포츠 비즈니스에 종사하는 '숙련된/전문적인' 사람들보다 자신들이 더 잘할 수 있다고 믿는다는 내용이 되어야 하므로 'experienced' 또는 'qualified'가 적절합니다. 따라서 두 빈칸을 모두 충족하는 것은 ②번입니다.
options_translation: ① 깊은 ... 자격 있는
② 불충분한 ... 경험 많은
③ 제한된 ... 평범한
④ 상당한 ... 숙련된
⑤ 형편없는 ... 보통의

questions.question: 17. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is ⓐ<u>preserved</u> and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is ⓑ<u>flexible,</u> and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. They could be ⓒ<u>anxious</u> and may ask themselves, "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to ⓓ<u>create</u> a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that ⓔ<u>respects</u> their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.explanation: 이사는 아이들에게 스트레스를 주며 일상적인 일(routine)이 파괴될 때 혼란을 느낍니다. 따라서 ⓐ는 '보존되다(preserved)'가 아니라 '방해받다(disrupted)' 혹은 '무너지다'와 같은 부정적인 의미의 단어가 와야 문맥상 적절합니다.

options_translation: ① 지역 간 이사 비용의 차이
