questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ⓐ<u>less</u> accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓑ<u>insensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓒ<u>underestimate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even ⓓ<u>forgot</u> how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how ⓔ<u>easy</u> it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes. We had better not make assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 전문가들은 자신이 과거에 그 기술을 습득할 때 얼마나 어려웠는지를 잊어버리는 '지식의 저주'에 빠진다는 내용입니다. 따라서 마지막 부분의 내용은 전문가들이 배우는 것이 얼마나 '어려웠는지(hard/difficult)'를 잊는다는 것이 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: ␐<u>Working</u> around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean that you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop ␑<u>painting</u>. Also, it can be tempting to keep on ␒<u>adding</u> more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it ␓<u>looking</u> overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, ␔<u>taking</u> a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation: ␔가 포함된 문장은 접섽사 If가 이밁는 부사절 다음에 나오는 주절입니다. and come back~과 병렬 구조림 이루며 명령문이 되어야 하며, 동사원형인 take로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses ␐<u>available</u>, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were ␑<u>stationed</u> on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, ␒<u>where</u> were placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger ␓<u>coming</u>, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. Nearing the next hut, a messenger began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one ␔<u>who</u> was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
questions.explanation: ␒ 다음에 바로 동사 were placed가 오며 주어가 빈 불완전한 문장이므로, 관계부사 where가 아닌 주격 관계대명사 which가 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 중 어법상 어색한 것이 있는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter display some of the same features, but are not exactly the same as each other. ⓐTherefore, they do not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. ⓑEnvironmental factors also determine how the animal responds during the treatment. ⓒFor instance, a cat in a rescue center responds very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. ⓓIn addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness reacts differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. ⓔWith this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal.
questions.explanation: ⓓ 문장의 주어는 'animals'로 복수형입니다. 'that' 관계대명사절의 수식을 받고 있으며, 문장의 정동사인 'reacts'는 주어의 수에 일치시켜 복수 동사 'react'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. (B) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. (C) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (D) But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. (E) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.insertion_sentence: Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)이 수면을 보호하는 기능을 하므로, 일부 저자들은 그것을 수면 정의의 일부로 포함시키지 않는다'는 내용입니다. (D) 뒤의 문장이 '하지만 그것(지각적 이탈) 없이는 잠을 자는 것이 불가능할 것이기에, 그것은 수면의 정의에 필수적인 것처럼 보인다'며 앞선 주장에 반박하고 있습니다. 따라서 역접의 접속사 'But'이 가리키는 대상이 들어있는 주어진 문장은 (D)에 위치해야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. (A) The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. (B) It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. (C) However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. (D) You think and you can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. (E) Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.insertion_sentence: In this way, when your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이런 식으로 당신의 판단이 감정에 의해 흐려질 때, 편견과 부정적인 것들이 생겨 당신을 방해한다'는 인과적 결과를 담고 있습니다. (D) 위치 바로 앞 문장에서 '의식적인 마음은 감정을 더할 수 있고, 감정에 자극받아 계속해서 잘못된 결정을 내리게 하여 당신을 실망시킨다'는 내용을 설명하고 있으므로, 이러한 현상을 'In this way'로 요약하며 보충 설명하는 주어진 문장은 (D)에 들어가는 것이 가장 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [24년 3월 36번]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. ⓐThey found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. ⓑCommon sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. ⓒAs examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. ⓓIn a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. ⓔAll have junior competitive structures where adults can use every price of affordable exercise equipment leisurely and freely to achieve good results.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린아이들을 위해 스포츠 환경(경기장 크기, 장비 등)을 조정해야 한다는 필요성과 실제 사례들을 설명하고 있습니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ는 모두 아이들을 위한 적응과 변화를 다루고 있으나, ⓔ는 갑자기 '성인들이 저렴한 운동 기구를 사용하여 좋은 결과를 얻는 구조'를 언급하고 있어 글의 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 23번]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop makes the soil _____________ for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 윤작(crop rotation)의 개념과 이점에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 이 농법이 '토양을 건강하게 유지하기 때문에 지속 가능하다'고 언급했으므로, 빈칸에는 각 작물이 다음 작물을 위해 토양을 '비옥하게' 만든다는 의미의 단어가 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 비옥한
② 고독한
③ 똑바로 선
④ 나눌 수 있는
⑤ 각각의

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time _____________ that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 우리가 직면하고 해결해야 하는 '도전 과제(challenge statement)'나 'struggle'을 긍정적인 진술로 바꾸라는 내용입니다. 따라서 우리가 마주하는 실시간의 '고난/어려움(hardships)'을 적어보라는 3번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 상
② 방어
③ 고난/어려움
④ 목표
⑤ 전망

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents (A)_____________ from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done. It gets you out of your (B)_____________ of what you can and can't do."
questions.explanation: 문맥상 (A)는 상사가 막지 말아야 할, 즉 반대 의견이나 '다른 관점(different perspectives)'을 의미하며, (B)는 반대자들의 말을 통해 벗어나게 되는 자신의 '고정 관념(fixed idea)'을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 관점들 ─ 고정 관념
② 공정한 생각들 ─ 칭찬
③ 독특한 재능들 ─ 낙담
④ 다양한 집단들 ─ 개방적 사고
⑤ 긍정적인 분위기 ─ 거절

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking.
ordered_passages: (A) Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.

(B) The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail.
(C) Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under, our approximate walking speed.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 인간의 감각이 걷기 셍도에 적응되어 있다고 했으므로, 그 걷기 셍도에 대한 구체적인 설명이 나오는 (C)가 먼저 와앴 합니다. (C) 다음에는 가장 빠른 운전자와 느린 백행자를 대조하는 (B)가 오고, 마지막으로 그 사이의 셍도를 가지는 조깅하는 사람과 자전거 타는 사람을 언급하는 (A)로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)를 아래 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. (A)<u>모든 생명체는 어느 정도의 이동이 가능하다.</u> Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, (B)과학자들은 나무와 같은 생명체조차도 기후 변화의 과거 시기 동안 놀라운 속도로 이동했다는 것을 안다.
subjective_conditions: all / are / movement를 모두 한 번씩 반드시 포함할 것
제시된 단어 외에 필요한 단어를 추가하여 문맥에 맞는 문장을 완성할 것
questions.answer: All creatures are capable of some degree of movement
questions.explanation: 지문의 핵심 내용인 '모든 생명체의 이동 능력'을 영작하는 문제입니다. '~할 수 있다/가능하다'라는 의미의 표현 'be capable of'를 기본 틀로 삼고, 주어인 '모든 생명체(All creatures)'와 목적어 역할을 하는 '어느 정도의 이동(some degree of movement)'을 결합하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (B)를 아래 <보기>의 어구만을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 영작하시오.
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. (A)모든 생명체는 어느 정도의 이동이 가능하다. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, (B)<u>과학자들은 나무와 같은 생명체조차도 기후 변화의 과거 시기 동안 놀라운 속도로 이동했다는 것을 안다.</u>
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 어구만을 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것
지문의 (B) 해석에 맞게 문법적으로 어색함이 없도록 영작할 것
questions.answer: scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change
questions.explanation: 주어 'scientists'와 동사 'know' 뒤에 목적어 절을 이끄는 접속사 'that'을 배치합니다. 명사절 내부에서 주어인 'even creatures like trees'와 동사 'moved'를 연결하고, '놀라운 속도로(with surprising speed)'와 '과거의 기후 변화 시기 동안(during past periods of climate change)'이라는 수식어구를 논리적 순서에 맞게 배열하여 완성합니다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어색한 내용이 있는 것을 고르고, 어색한 부분을 바르게 고쳐서 전체 문장을 영어로 다시 쓰시오.
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered</u>: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that ⓑ<u>the tongue map explanation of how we taste was totally right</u>. As it turns out, ⓒ<u>the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century</u>. Today, ⓓ<u>leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty</u>. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although ⓔ<u>they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites</u>. Moreover, (A)________________________________________________________. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.answer: 어색한 기호: ⓑ, 수정한 문장: the tongue map explanation of how we taste was totally wrong
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 과거의 혀 지도는 오역과 오해에서 비롯된 것이라고 설명하고 있으므로, 1980년대와 90년대의 연구는 혀 지도의 설명이 '옳다(right)'가 아니라 '틀렸다(wrong)'는 것을 입증했습니다. 따라서 right를 wrong으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 28. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)에 들어갈 하나의 완전한 문장을 아래 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered</u>: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that ⓑ<u>the tongue map explanation of how we taste was totally right</u>. As it turns out, ⓒ<u>the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century</u>. Today, ⓓ<u>leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty</u>. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although ⓔ<u>they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites</u>. Moreover, (A)________________________________________________________. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
subjective_conditions: at work / not / place / the mechanism / time을 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것
주어진 단어들 이외에 새로운 단어를 추가할 것
questions.answer: the mechanism at work is not place, but time
questions.explanation: 지문 마지막 부분에서 혀 끝에서 단맛을 느끼는 것이 아니라 그 지각을 먼저 등록하는 것이라고 설명하므로, 핵심 기제는 '장소'가 아니라 '시간'임을 추론할 수 있습니다. 'not A but B' 구문을 사용하여 'the mechanism at work is not place, but time'으로 작성합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Staying focused throughout the workday can be ⓐ<u>tough</u> because our energy levels fluctuate. We all have times when we're at our peak performance, but there are also times when we feel ⓑ<u>less</u> alert. To maximize productivity and boost confidence, it's helpful to take on demanding tasks when you're feeling most ⓒ<u>incapable</u>. If you haven't paid attention to your energy peaks before, try ⓓ<u>observing</u> yourself for a few days. Take note of when you feel most energized and focused. Peak productivity periods ⓔ<u>vary</u> from person to person; some people shine in the morning, while others need a bit longer to warm up.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 자신의 에너지 수준이 가장 높을 때(peak performance) 어려운 일을 처리하는 것이 생산성을 높이는 데 도움이 된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 생산성을 극대화하기 위해서는 스스로 가장 무능하다고 느낄 때(incapable)가 아니라 가장 유능하거나 에너지가 넘친다고 느낄 때(capable/energetic) 힘든 일을 맡아야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, ⓐ<u>instead of</u> concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it ⓑ<u>undemanding</u> to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to ⓒ<u>evaluate</u> your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking excessively ⓓ<u>labored</u>. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would be ⓔ<u>enhanced</u> from further refinement to raise its overall quality.
questions.explanation: 예술가들은 종종 그림 그리기를 언제 멈춰야 할지 아는 것이 '어렵다(difficult/hard)'고 느낍니다. 뒤이어 나오는 '작업에 더 많은 것을 계속 추가하고 싶은 유혹을 느낄 수 있다'는 내용과도 일맥상통해야 하므로 '힘들지 않은/쉬운'을 뜻하는 undemanding은 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, <u>it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place</u>." Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster - in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
options: ① It is important to focus on the starting point to thrive.
② Species constantly evolve to maintain their relative positions.
③ From the perspective of biologists, rabbits and foxes are closely linked.
④ Species must engage in competition for survival in order to thrive and evolve.
⑤ Due to a lack of effort, it would be unlikely to make advancements in the process of evolution.
questions.explanation: 이 글에서 언급된 '붉은 여왕 효과'는 한 종이 진화하더라도 경쟁 관계에 있는 다른 종 또한 진화하기 때문에, 상대적인 지위를 유지하기 위해서는 끊임없이 달려야(진화해야) 함을 의미합니다. 따라서 종들이 상대적인 위치를 유지하기 위해 끊임없이 진화한다는 내용인 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 번성하기 위해 시작 지점에 집중하는 것이 중요하다.
② 종들은 그들의 상대적인 지위를 유지하기 위해 끊임없이 진화한다.
③ 생물학자의 관점에서 토끼와 여우는 밀접하게 연결되어 있다.
④ 종들은 번성하고 진화하기 위해 생존 경쟁에 참여해야 한다.
⑤ 노력의 부족 때문에 진화 과정에서 발전을 이루기는 어려울 것이다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other essential nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body breaks down these simple carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body. Consequently, excessive consumption of simple carbohydrates can contribute to weight gain and negatively impact overall health.
options: ① Complex carbohydrates can trap crucial nutrients such as vitamins and minerals within their structure.
② Simple carbohydrates are quickly broken down and any unused portions are stored as fat.
③ Complex carbohydrates are considered beneficial for the body.
④ Simple carbohydrates provide long-lasting fuel for the body for many hours.
⑤ Excessive intake of simple carbohydrates can lead to weight gain.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 몇 시간 동안 신체에 연료(에너지)를 제공하는 것은 복합 탄수화물(Complex carbohydrates)입니다. 단일 탄수화물(Simple carbohydrates/Bad carbohydrates)은 구조가 단순하여 빨리 분해되므로 오랫동안 연료를 제공한다는 ④번 설명은 본문 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 복합 탄수화물은 비타민과 미네랄 같은 중요한 영양소를 구조 안에 가둘 수 있다.
② 단순 탄수화물은 빠르게 분해되며 사용되지 않은 부분은 지방으로 저장된다.
③ 복합 탄수화물은 신체에 유익한 것으로 간주된다.
④ 단순 탄수화물은 신체에 여러 시간 동안 지속되는 연료를 제공한다.
⑤ 단순 탄수화물의 과도한 섭취는 체중 증가로 이어질 수 있다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
options: ① Balancing the Physical and Mental World
② Exploring the Unknown: Journey into Mystery
③ The Importance of Designing Finished Products
④ Mindset of the Creator Before Building Monuments
⑤ The Power of Perfected Ideas Preceding Reality
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우리 주변의 모든 사물들이 실제 만들어지기 전에 누군가의 마음속에서 이미 완성된 아이디어였다는 점을 강조합니다. 인간의 미래 설계 또한 이와 마찬가지로 마음속에서 완성된 비전이 현실로 나타나게 된다는 내용이므로 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 물리적 세계와 정신적 세계의 균형 잡기
② 미지의 탐험: 신비로의 여정
③ 완성된 제품을 디자인하는 것의 중요성
④ 기념물을 세우기 전 창조자의 마음가짐
⑤ 현실보다 앞서는 완성된 아이디어의 힘

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do." explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to adopt the practices of those around you.
options: ① Challenges Involved in Embracing Collective Views
② Social Validation: Reliable Evidence in Decision Making
③ The Art of Waiting: Exploring the Pleasures of Patience
④ Consumer Behaviors: Factors Affecting Purchase Decisions
⑤ Various Evolutionary Strategies: Universally Applicable Perspectives
questions.explanation: 사람들은 위험과 안전, 신뢰 여부를 결정할 때 타인의 행동인 '사회적 증거'를 참고한다는 내용입니다. 진화론적 관점에서도 집단을 따르는 것이 생존에 유리했으며, 식당의 줄과 같은 사례를 통해 사회적 입증이 의사 결정의 신뢰할 수 있는 근거가 됨을 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 집단적 견해를 수용하는 데 따르는 과제들
② 사회적 입증: 의사 결정 시 신뢰할 수 있는 증거
③ 기다림의 미학: 인내의 즐거움 탐구하기
④ 소비자 행동: 구매 결정에 영향을 미치는 요인들
⑤ 다양한 진화 전략: 보편적으로 적용 가능한 관점들

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whose story it is affects what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events ________________, we will interpret them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
options: ④ through an objective point of view
⑤ according to the chronological order
questions.explanation: 이야기의 주인공이 누구냐에 따라 이야기의 초점과 해석이 달라진다는 내용입니다. 신데렐라 이야기를 악한 의붓자매의 관점에서 보거나, '바람과 함께 사라지다'를 다른 인물의 관점에서 보는 예시를 통해, 사건을 '다른(대안적인) 관점'에서 바라볼 때 해석이 달라짐을 유추할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 육안으로
② 정확한 렌즈를 통해
③ 대안적인 관점에서
④ 객관적인 관점을 통해
⑤ 연대순에 따라

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 39번]
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm'. The other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations __________________________________.
options: ① rarely determine personal impressions and interactions
② form cultural norms and customs in diverse communities
③ have a profound impact on ethical framework and moral judgments of others
④ construct impressions of others based on valid and empirical observations
⑤ significantly influence individuals' perceptions and the subsequent behavior
questions.explanation: 사람들이 타인의 한 가지 특성을 보고 다른 특성까지 추측하는 경향(후광 효과와 유사한 개념)에 대한 글입니다. 강사에 대해 '따뜻하다' 혹은 '차갑다'는 사전 정보를 받은 학생들은 그에 따라 인상을 다르게 형성했을 뿐만 아니라, 실제 상호작용(행동)의 빈도도 달랐습니다. 이는 서로 다른 기대치가 개인의 인식과 그에 따른 행동에 상당한 영향을 미친다는 점을 보여줍니다.
options_translation: ① 개인의 인상과 상호작용을 거의 결정하지 않는다
② 다양한 공동체에서 문화적 규범과 관습을 형성한다
③ 타인의 윤리적 틀과 도덕적 판단에 깊은 영향을 미친다
④ 타당하고 경험적인 관찰에 기초하여 타인의 인상을 구성한다
⑤ 개인의 인식과 그에 따른 행동에 상당히 영향을 미친다

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 22번]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership _______________________________________. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ① appears as an honorable and lofty aspiration
② is regarded as an unnecessary characteristic
③ can help guide you in navigating your career path
④ is an essential ability required for becoming a president
⑤ might enable individuals to make decisions independently
questions.explanation: 역사적인 인물들의 영향력을 생각할 때 리더십은 '고귀하고 높은 열망'처럼 보일 수 있지만, 사실 그들도 평범하게 시작하여 아이디어를 발전시켰다는 내용입니다. 빈칸 앞부분은 우리가 리더십을 대단하고 먼 것으로 느끼는 일반적인 인식을 다루므로 '숭고하고 높은 포부처럼 보인다'는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 숭고하고 높은 포부(열망)처럼 보인다
② 불필요한 특성으로 간주된다
③ 당신의 경력 경로를 탐색하는 데 도움을 줄 수 있다
④ 대통령이 되기 위해 요구되는 필수적인 능력이다
⑤ 개인이 독립적으로 결정을 내리는 것을 가능하게 할지도 모른다

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to ________________________________. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk - for body and mind.
options: ① prioritize low-tech physical work over other activities
② steer clear of manual labor that doesn't involve high technology
③ preserve and value traditional manual labor skills alongside digital proficiency
④ develop fundamental skills such as literacy, numeracy, and critical thinking
⑤ encourage a varied skill set blending traditional craftsmanship and digital literacy
questions.explanation: 지문은 기술 채택에 따른 대가에 대해 설명하며, 전통적인 생계 수단의 상실과 현대의 소외된 노동, 그리고 육체와 정신의 분리 문제를 지적합니다. 특히 '손과 머리의 분리'가 정신적 스트레스를 주고 고연봉 직업이 주로 앉아서 하는 일임을 언급하며, 교육과 미디어가 사람들이 고도의 기술이 없는 육체 노동(manual labor)을 피하게 만들고 있음을 비판하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 활동보다 저기술 육체 작업을 우선시한다
② 고도의 기술이 포함되지 않은 육체 노동을 멀리한다
③ 디지털 숙련도와 함께 전통적인 육체 노동 기술을 보존하고 가치 있게 여긴다
④ 읽고 쓰는 능력, 수리 능력, 비판적 사고와 같은 기초적인 능력을 개발한다
⑤ 전통적인 수공예와 디지털 문해력이 혼합된 다양한 기술 세트를 장려한다

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded and plentifully paid for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. Furthermore, the poor employment market forces them to _________________________________.
options: ① settle for a substantially compensated yet unfulfilling profession
② explore alternative career paths to achieve their intended goal
③ invest considerable effort to acquire the skills for their profession
④ experience gratification in a career that offers insufficient pay yet is worthwhile
⑤ seek support and collaboration from others facing similar challenges in the job market
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성공이 도리어 삶을 즐겁지 않은 '편안한 틀'에 가두는 상황을 경고합니다. 보수는 좋지만 성취감이 없는 일을 계속하다가 나중에는 그만두고 싶어도 빠져나올 수 없게 되는데, 여기에 열악한 고용 시장 상황까지 겹치면 사람들은 결국 보상은 좋지만 만족스럽지 못한 직업에 안주할 수밖에 없게 됩니다. 따라서 1번이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 보상은 상당하지만 성취감이 없는 직업에 안주한다
② 의도한 목표를 달성하기 위해 대안적인 경력 경로를 탐색한다
③ 자신의 직업을 위한 기술을 습득하기 위해 상당한 노력을 투자한다
④ 보수는 불충분하지만 가치 있는 경력에서 만족감을 경험한다
⑤ 구직 시장에서 유사한 어려움에 처한 타인들로부터 지원과 협력을 구한다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there ⓐ<u>are</u> five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reaons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which ⓑ<u>has</u> links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are ⓒ<u>still</u> harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us ⓓ<u>that</u> "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study ⓔ<u>it</u> for what they are.
questions.explanation: 마지막 문장에서 지칭하는 대상은 복수 명사인 'animal senses'입니다. 따라서 단수 대명사인 'it'을 복수 대명사인 'them'으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다. ⓐ는 there are 구문의 수 일치, ⓑ는 주격 관계대명사 뒤의 수 일치, ⓒ는 비교급 강조, ⓓ는 명사절 접속사 that으로 모두 적절하게 쓰였습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~␕ 중, 완법상 어색한 것만을 읈는 대로 고맠 것은?
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>If you want the confidence that arises from achieving what is set out for each day, then it's important to understand how long tasks are going to take</u>. ⓑ<u>Being excessively optimistic about the things that can accomplish within the designated time is resulted in difficulties</u>. So work on it. ⓒ<u>Establish your daily routine in which you can make a practice of calculating the time needed for tasks as a means of organizing your 'things to do' list</u>. ⓓ<u>And also you need to be learned by experience which tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected</u>. You should give attention to fitting the task to the available time. ⓔ<u>There are some tasks which you can only set about if you are given a significant amount of time available</u>. ⓕ<u>There is no point in striving to adequately prepare for such a task when the accessible time to do so is limited</u>. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.explanation: ␑ 문윑에서 things는 성취되는 대상이므로 can be accomplished로, 결과를 초뜘하다는 능동태인 results in으로 고쳐야 합니다. ␓ 문윑에서는 숙련되거나 배우는 제체가 학생이므로 need to learn으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 관의 흐름으로 밴아, 주어진 문윑이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." (A) Think about it this way: Would yo wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. (B) You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. (C) They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. (D) They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. (E) And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
questions.insertion_sentence: Skillful learners know that "putting on the same clothes" won't work for every class.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문윑은 숙련된 학습자들은 모든 수업에 같은 옷을 입을 수 없다는 것을 알고 읈다는 내용입니다. 이는 설명을 위해 들었던 옷차림 비유가 끝나고, 숙련된 학습자(유연한 학습자)에 대한 설명이 시작되는 (C) 윐츠에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 3월 37번]
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. (A) As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. (B) During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. (C) The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. (D) When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. (E) This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
questions.insertion_sentence: Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 결정의 크기가 냉각 속도에 달려 있다는 내용입니다. (C)까지는 광물의 형성 종류에 대해 설명하고, (D)부터 구체적으로 냉각 속도(slowly)와 결정 크기(large)의 관계를 설명하기 시작하므로, 그 원리를 도입하는 문장인 주어진 문장은 (D)가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 23번]
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off.
ordered_passages: (A) In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.

(B) One of the factors leading to the changes is the Railway system. In the nineteenth century, it opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels.
(C) At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 사회적 경제적 상황의 개선과 더 많은 자유 시간이 주어졌음을 언급합니다. (C)에서는 이와 동시에 운송 수단이 발달했음을 설명하며 영국 산업 혁명이 이러한 변화들을 이끌었다고 소개합니다. (B)에서는 그 운송 수단 변화의 요인 중 하나인 철도 시스템을 언급하며 영국 내의 사례를 들고, (A)에서는 추가적인 사례로 캐나다의 철도와 이후 항공 운송을 통한 관광 성장을 설명하는 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장이 있는 곳은?
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. ⓐOnce people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew larger. ⓑLiving in larger communities facilitated more efficient organization, allowing tasks to be divided among individuals. ⓒThey could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster. ⓓDuring the evenings, the villagers often gathered around bonfires to share stories and songs. For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. ⓔBy working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time. Overall, the transition to settled agricultural communities during the Old Stone Age enabled more efficient cooperation and task division.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구석기 시대 이후 정착 생활과 농경이 시작되면서 발생한 노동 분업과 협업의 효율성에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓓ 문장은 마을 사람들이 저녁에 모닥불 주위에 모여 이야기와 노래를 나누었다는 내용으로, 경제적/사회적 효율성 및 협업이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어난 일상적인 친목 활동을 언급하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
questions.summary_sentence: Individuals overcome (A)___________ using positive affirmations to (B)___________ confidence, similar to the magical changes portrayed in movies like Cinderella.
questions.explanation: 본문은 직면한 문제나 도전(challenges)을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸어 씀으로써 자신감(confidence)을 얻고 사고방식을 바꿀 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '도전'이나 '난관'을 뜻하는 difficulty가 적절하고, (B)에는 자신감을 '높이다'라는 뜻의 boost가 들어가는 것이 문맥상 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 편안함 - 증가시키다
② 새로움 - 되찾다
③ 어려움 - 신장시키다
④ 안락함 - 향상시키다
⑤ 추상 - 감소시키다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
questions.summary_sentence: During the mid-20th century, as industries expanded, there was a notable change towards emphasizing customer (A)__________ rather than just manufacturing products. It led to (B)__________ shifts in marketing approaches.
questions.explanation: 지문은 1940년대와 50년대 산업 사회의 변화로 인해 기업이 단순히 제품을 생산하는 것보다 고객이 실제로 원하는 것을 제공하는 고객 중심의 마케팅 혁명이 일어났음을 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 고객 만족을 의미하는 satisfaction이, (B)에는 이러한 마케팅 접근의 근본적 변화를 뜻하는 revolutionary가 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 충성도 ... 결함 있는
② 보유 ... 전략적인
③ 상호작용 ... 파괴적인
④ 만족 ... 혁명적인
⑤ 권한 부여 ... 역효과의

questions.question: 다음 글을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.question: 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it.
ordered_passages: (B) A more recent stud of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel. Let's consider an example of Major League Baseball (MLB) teams. Suppose that the Los Angeles Dodgers from the west coast are traveling to play against the New York Yankees from the east coast.

(C) Conversely, if the New York Yankees travel to Lost Angeles, they're moving westward, which extends their day. This westward travel might provide them with more time to adjust to the later time zone in Los Angeles, potentially making it easier for them to perform well.

(D) This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football.

(E) When the Dodgers travel from Los Angeles to New York, they are moving eastward, which means they're essentially shortening their day. Due to this eastward travel, they might experience difficulties adjusting to the earlier time zone in New York, which could affect their performance.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 시차 극복 속도가 방향에 따라 다르며 서쪽으로 비행하는 것이 동쪽보다 쉽다는 일반적인 사실을 제시합니다. (D)에서 이러한 차이가 스포츠 팀의 성과에 영향을 미칠 만큼 크다는 점을 구체적인 연구 결과와 함께 언급합니다. (B)에서는 메이저리그 야구의 사례를 들기 시작하며 상황을 가정합니다. (E)에서 서부에서 동부로 이동하는 구체적인 예시(Dodgers)를 들어 설명하고, (C)에서 반대로 동부에서 서부로 이동하는 경우(Yankees)를 대조하며 마무리하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 윗글에 관한 내용으로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it.(B) A more recent stud of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel. Let's consider an example of Major League Baseball (MLB) teams. Suppose that the Los Angeles Dodgers from the west coast are traveling to play against the New York Yankees from the east coast.(C) Conversely, if the New York Yankees travel to Lost Angeles, they're moving westward, which extends their day. This westward travel might provide them with more time to adjust to the later time zone in Los Angeles, potentially making it easier for them to perform well.(D) This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football.(E) When the Dodgers travel from Los Angeles to New York, they are moving eastward, which means they're essentially shortening their day. Due to this eastward travel, they might experience difficulties adjusting to the earlier time zone in New York, which could affect their performance. Therefore, based on the research findings, traveling eastward (such as from Los Angeles to New York) in MLB games might be more challenging than traveling westward (such as from New York to Los Angeles).
options: ① The speed of recovery from jet lag has much to do with the types of sports.
② Recent findings suggest that the impact of jet lag on sports team performance is negligible.
③ Recovery from jet lag is slower when traveling eastward compared to traveling westward.
④ There is no difference in the speed of recovery from jet lag based on the direction of travel.
⑤ Teams flying eastward have an advantage over teams flying westward in professional baseball.
questions.explanation: 지문 전체에서 동쪽으로 이동할 때가 서쪽으로 이동할 때보다 시차 적응이 더 힘들고 회복이 더디다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 ③번 '동쪽으로 여행할 때 시차 회복이 서쪽으로 여행할 때보다 느리다'는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 시차 회복 속도는 스포츠의 종류와 큰 관련이 있다.
② 최근 연구 결과는 스포츠 팀의 성과에 시차가 미치는 영향이 무시해도 될 정도임을 암시한다.
③ 서쪽으로 여행할 때와 비교했을 때 동쪽으로 여행할 때 시차 회복이 더 느리다.
④ 여행 방향에 따른 시차 회복 속도 차이는 없다.
⑤ 프로야구에서 동쪽으로 비행하는 팀들이 서쪽으로 비행하는 팀들보다 유리하다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
options: ① 과제를 최대한 빠르게 마무리 짓는 능력이 중요하다.
② 시간이 적게 걸리는 과제들을 먼저 처리하는 것이 효율적이다.
③ 목표를 달성하는 데 있어서 어느 정도의 낙관주의적인 태도는 필요하다.
④ 과제를 수행하기 위해서 필요한 것들을 잘 준비하는 것이 가장 우선적인 일이다.
⑤ 목표를 달성하기 위해서는 과제를 수행하는 데 필요한 시간을 파악하는 것이 중요하다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 매일 설정한 목표를 달성하기 위해서는 각 과제가 어느 정도의 시간을 필요로 하는지 객관적으로 파악하는 것이 중요하다고 말하고 있습니다. 따라서 과제 수행에 필요한 시간을 파악하는 것이 중요하다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without perceptual disengagement, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.*stimuli: 자극 *disengagement: 이탈*drowsiness: 졸음
options: ① 동물은 잠을 자는 동안 환경 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않는다.
② 잠자고 있는 포유류의 눈은 기능적으로는 실명 상태와 같다고 볼 수 있다.
③ 잠자고 있는 포유류의 눈으로 들어온 시각 정보는 짧아지거나 약화 된다.
④ 수면은 지각 이탈 없이는 불가능 할 것이다.
⑤ 많은 동물은 수면의 이득을 끌어내기 위해서 완전한 지각 이탈을 통해 졸음이라는 상태를 이용한다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 'total perceptual disengagement' 없이(without) 졸음(drowsiness) 상태를 이용하여 수면의 이득을 얻는다고 했으므로, '완전한 지각 이탈을 통해'라는 설명은 틀린 내용입니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
options: ① significance of intensities of perception, not place or time
② the tongue map which can explain the mystery of how we taste
③ the dramatic change in the mechanism of the tongue, as humans evolving
④ the misunderstanding and the newly disclosed truth about the mechanism of taste
⑤ the critical mistake of 20th research, which obstructed further research on taste buds
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거의 잘못된 '혀 지도' 이론(오해)과 현대 연구를 통해 밝혀진 새로운 사실(진실)에 대해 다루고 있으므로 ④번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 장소나 시간이 아닌 지각 강도의 중요성
② 우리가 맛을 느끼는 신비함을 설명할 수 있는 혀 지도
③ 인류가 진화함에 따른 혀 메커니즘의 극적인 변화
④ 미각 메커니즘에 대한 오해와 새로 밝혀진 진실
⑤ 미뢰에 대한 추가 연구를 방해한 20세기 연구의 중대한 실수

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ① Healing session can become changed according to varying domestic environments.
② Healing is similar to a learning process because it needs lots of patience and perseverance.
③ It is crucial that healing treatment ought to be modified to meet the requirements of each animal.
④ People should realize that there are no animals that are alike even if they are from the same litter.
⑤ There is an obvious distinction in reactions between animals that have physical illness and those with emotional confusion.
questions.explanation: 모든 동물은 제각기 다르고 환경과 상황에 따라 치유에 반응하는 방식이 다르기 때문에, 각 치유 과정은 해당 동물의 구체적인 필요(specific needs)에 맞춰 조정되어야 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ③번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 치유 세션은 다양한 가정 환경에 따라 변화될 수 있다.
② 치유는 많은 인내와 끈기가 필요하기 때문에 학습 과정과 유사하다.
③ 치유 치료가 각 동물의 요구 사항에 맞춰 수정되어야 하는 것이 매우 중요하다.
④ 사람들은 한 배에서 태어났더라도 똑같은 동물은 없다는 것을 깨달아야 한다.
⑤ 신체적 질병을 가진 동물과 정서적 혼란을 겪는 동물 사이에는 명확한 반응 차이가 있다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bob Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① The Consequences of Ignoring Opposite Opinions
② The Definition of Smooth and Effective Communication
③ The Pros and Cons of Going against the General Trend
④ Academic Qualifications for Becoming a Respected Leader
⑤ The Meaning of Accepting Expressed Disagreement in Management
questions.explanation: 경영진들은 부하 직원들의 반대 의견(dissent)을 경청해야 한다고 강조합니다. 이는 반대 의견이 실제로 문제를 해결하는 실마리를 제공해 주기 때문입니다. 따라서 경영에서 의견 차이를 수용하는 것의 가치를 설명하는 ⑤번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 반대 의견을 무시하는 것의 결과
② 원활하고 효과적인 의사소통의 정의
③ 일반적인 추세에 반대하는 것의 장단점
④ 존경받는 리더가 되기 위한 학문적 자격
⑤ 경영에서 표현된 이견(반대 의견)을 수용하는 것의 의미

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how ⓐ<u>professionals</u> in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓑ<u>supersensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge', which means our incorrect assumption that everyone knows as much as we do an people come to own the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of ⓒ<u>difficulty</u> of that skill. Her participants estimated the time spent for the ⓓ<u>acquisition</u> of that skill in an earlier session as being less than the actual time. Knowing that experts ⓔ<u>rarely</u> forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전문가가 초보자의 입장을 이해하지 못하는 '지식의 저주'를 설명합니다. ⓐ professionals(전문가), ⓒ difficulty(난이도), ⓓ acquisition(습득)은 문맥상 적절합니다. 반면 ⓑ supersensitive(매우 민감한)는 전문가가 초보자의 어려움을 잘 모른다는 맥락이므로 insensitive(무감각한) 등으로 고쳐야 하며, ⓔ rarely(드물게)는 전문가가 자신이 과거에 배웠던 고충을 자주 잊어버린다는 맥락이므로 often 등으로 고쳐야 합니다. 따라서 적절한 것은 ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓓ 3개입니다.

questions.question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly straightforward question How many senses exist? Approximately 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals: sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) These instances indicate that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," as Macpherson wrote in her work The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian categories, we ought to examine them for what they are.

(B) Furthermore, animals possess senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates, for instance, have a different sense system for detecting odors, while certain snake can discern the body heat of their prey.

(C) However, philosopher Fiona Macpherson, suggests reasons to doubt it. Initially, Aristotle overlooked certain sense in humans, such as the perception of one's own body, distinct from touch, and the sense of balance, which had links to both touch and vision.
questions.explanation: 감각의 개수에 대한 아리스토텔레스의 전통적인 견해(5감)를 제시한 후, (C)에서 'However'를 통해 철학자 Fiona Macpherson이 제시한 인간의 추가적인 감각(자기 수용 감각, 균형 감각)을 근거로 의문을 제기합니다. (B)에서는 'Furthermore'를 사용하여 인간을 넘어 동물의 분류하기 어려운 감각 체계(냄새 탐지 시스템, 열 감지 등)의 예시를 추가합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 사례들을 종합하여 감각을 제한된 숫자로 명확히 나눌 수 없다는 결론을 내리며, 동물의 감각을 있는 그대로 관찰해야 한다고 마무리하는 순서가 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 13. 윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① You can be happy by enjoying your leisure time and hobbies.
② High income is the biggest support for your high self-esteem.
③ In order to feel satisfied, one must have a socially respected job.
④ It is important to consider collaborating with coworkers when choosing a job.
⑤ Finding meaning in your work significantly boosts happiness and success.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 업무에서 의미와 성취감을 찾는 것이 인간의 행복과 성공에 미치는 긍정적인 영향을 강조하고 있습니다. 소냐 류보미르스키 교수의 연구를 인용하여 성취감을 느끼는 사람들이 더 높은 질의 업무를 수행하고 더 많은 수입을 올리며, 전반적인 삶의 행복도도 높다는 점을 설명하므로 정답은 5번입니다.
options_translation: ① 여가 시간과 취미를 즐김으로써 행복해질 수 있다.
② 높은 수입은 높은 자존감을 위한 가장 큰 지지대이다.
③ 만족감을 느끼기 위해서는 사회적으로 존경받는 직업을 가져야 한다.
④ 직업을 선택할 때 동료들과의 협업을 고려하는 것이 중요하다.
⑤ 업무에서 의미를 찾는 것은 행복과 성공을 크게 증진시킨다.

questions.question: 14. 윗글의 Lyubomirsky 교수의 업무 현장 연구에 따르면, 직업에서 더 많은 성취감을 느끼는 사람들이 얻게 되는 것이 있다. 이를 찾아 두 가지만 우리말로 쓰시오. (각각 10자 이내)
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.answer: 더 질 높은 업무, 더 큰 성과, 더 높은 수입 중 두 가지
questions.explanation: 본문 중 'when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes' 문장에 근거하여 성취감을 느끼는 사람들이 얻는 이점으로 더 질 높은 업무, 더 많은 생산량(성과), 더 높은 수입을 언급하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying ─ but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
options: ① 성공은 당신에게 더 많은 보상을 안겨주어 사람을 나태함에 빠지게 한다.
② 끊임없는 노력이야말로 당신을 성공적이고 편안한 삶으로 이끌 수 있다.
③ 주위를 돌아볼 여유도 없이 목표를 향해 달려가는 것은 위험하다.
④ 열악한 고용 시장이 편안하면서도 만족스럽지 않은 일자리에 갇히게 한다.
⑤ 틀에 박힌 편안한 삶은 햇빛을 보거나 바깥 공기를 마실 수 없게 한다.
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에서 언급하듯, 많은 직업인이 열악한 고용 시장(poor employment market)으로 인해 안정적이고 수입은 좋을지 모르나 궁극적으로는 만족스럽지 못한 일자리에 갇혀(locked in) 있다고 느끼는 상황을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ④번이 글의 요지로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
questions.passage: Marilyn and her three-year-old daughter, Sarah, took a trip to the beach, where Sarah built her first sandcastle. As she liked ⓐ<u>it</u> so much, she wished it to exist forever. Moments later, an enormous wave destroyed ⓑ<u>it.</u> In response to ⓒ<u>its</u> collapse, tears streamed down Sarah's cheeks and her heart was broken. She ran to Marilyn, saying she would never build a sandcastle again. Marilyn said, "Part of the joy of building a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give ⓓ<u>it</u> as a gift to the ocean." Sarah loved this idea and responded with enthusiasm to the idea of building another castle ─ this time, even closer to the water so the ocean would get ⓔ<u>its</u> gift sooner!
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ는 모두 Sarah가 지은 '모래성(sandcastle)'을 가리키는 반면, ⓔ는 바다(the ocean)를 가리키는 소유격 대명사입니다.

questions.question: 17. 다으ᄆ 글으ᄆ 흐르ᄆ으로 바ᅡ 주어진 문자ᄀ이 댜라가기개 가장 저ᄀ절하ᄂ 고스는? [2.7자ᄆ]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. (A) Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. (B) This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. (C) However, they still use their front legs like human hands, for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw. (D) Moreover, they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. (E) A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.insertion_sentence: In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way.
questions.explanation: 저시문아서는 차근 애니메이션 영화에사 동물을 더 '자연서러운' 바ᄂ시ᄀ으로 보여주는 경햐ᄀ을 어느거하ᄆ니다. (C) 뒤의 문자ᄀ아사 However라는 여ᄀ저ᄇ의 녀ᄀ결어를 파하ᄆ하고 이ᄄ느ᄂ데, 이는 자연서러ᄇ가ᄂ 모스ᄇ으로 보여주ᄆ에도 발구하고 여저ᄂ히 인간개 가튼 행동(아ᄑ발을 쇠처라ᄆ 사용) 틍을 하냬는 내용이 이어지므로 (C)가 가장 저ᄀ절하ᄆ니다.

questions.question: 18. 다으ᄆ 글으ᄂ 내요ᄀ으로 유추할 수 아는 거스는? [2.9자ᄆ]
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
options: ① Minerals are formed by natural processes such as the cooling of magma.
② As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy and combine into compounds to form an orderly pattern.
③ The composition of elements present in a magma has an important influence on mineral types in part.
④ The magma cooling rate also plays an important role in the quality of the crystals produced.
⑤ Slower cooling produces larger visible crystals, but faster cooling produces smaller ones.
questions.explanation: 지문에사 마그마가 시ᄀ는 소ᄀ도는 결정으ᄆ 그기(size)에 영햐ᄀ을 미친다고 해ᄄ지, 결정으ᄆ 페질(quality)개 대해사는 어느거하지 아나스ᄆ니다.
options_translation: ① 과ᄆ물으ᄂ 마그마으ᄆ 내ᄀ가걔 가트ᄂ 자연자ᄀ영에 의해 형사ᄀ뎨냬.
② 마그마가 시ᄀ으면사 워자드르ᄂ 결에나지를 일고 퐈하ᄆ마ᄆ로 겨ᄀ하ᄑ하여 질서 저ᄀ으ᄂ 파턴을 형사ᄀ하냬.
③ 마그마 소ᄀ으ᄆ 워서 구서ᄀ으ᄂ 과ᄆ물 저ᄂ류에 바구부 주다하ᄂ 영햐ᄀ을 미치냬.
④ 마그마으ᄆ 내ᄀ가 소ᄀ도는 생사ᄂ댜는 결정으ᄆ 페질에도 주다하ᄂ 여하늘 하냬.
⑤ 내ᄀ가가 더딜수로ᄀ 더 근 가시자ᄀ으ᄂ 결정을 마ᄂ들고, 내ᄀ가가 바를수로ᄀ 더 자그ᄂ 결정을 마ᄂ든다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become _______________ to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session.
questions.explanation: 전문가들이 초보자에게 작업이 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 무관심하거나 고려하지 않게 되는 현상을 '지식의 저주'라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '생각 없는, 배려 없는'의 의미를 가진 thoughtless가 가장 적절합니다. (원문은 insensitive이나 맥락상 유사한 의미)
options_translation: ① 생각 없는 (무심한)
② 예견하는
③ 민감한
④ 정확한
⑤ 조심스러운

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that ____________________ ____________________________. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.*disengagement: 이탈
options: ① they actively accept external information
② they respond normally to surrounding stimuli
③ they reflect what they experienced in the unconscious
④ their responses to environmental stimuli are not normal
⑤ their eyes keep moving to deal with the change immediately
questions.explanation: 지문은 잠자는 동안 외부 자극이 정상적으로 처리되지 않는 '지각적 이탈'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 잠자는 포유류의 눈을 떠도 정상적으로 보지 못하며 자극이 등록되더라도 처리되지 않는다는 내용을 통해, 환경적 자극에 대한 반응이 정상적이지 않다는 ④번이 정답임을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 그들은 외부 정보를 능동적으로 받아들인다
② 그들은 주변 자극에 정상적으로 반응한다
③ 그들은 무의식 속에서 경험한 것을 반영한다
④ 환경적 자극에 대한 그들의 반응이 정상적이지 않다
⑤ 그들의 눈은 변화에 즉각 대처하기 위해 계속 움직인다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport _______________________________________.
options: ① became a new growth engine for our country
② changed the structure of industries around the world
③ discouraged the economy from developing and creating jobs
④ caused environmental pollution worldwide due to high carbon emissions
⑤ led to the expansion of the tourism industry, opening the door to the world
questions.explanation: 경제 성장, 근로 조건 개선, 교통수단의 발달(철도 등)이 관광 산업의 발전을 이끌었다는 내용의 글입니다. 마지막 문장에서 항공 운송의 등장이 가져온 결과를 추론해야 하므로, 관광 산업의 확장과 세계로 나가는 문을 열었다는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리 나라의 새로운 성장 동력이 되었다
② 전 세계 산업 구조를 변화시켰다
③ 경제 발전과 일자리 창출을 저해했다
④ 높은 탄소 배출로 인해 전 세계적인 환경 오염을 초래했다
⑤ 관광 산업의 확장으로 이어져 세계로 향하는 문을 열었다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
questions.summary_sentence: The sales philosophy focused solely on (A)__________ and price has shifted to (B)________ in this affluent modern society.
questions.subjective_answer_format: (A)                        (B)① employment    analyzing consumer prices② marketing ignoring the buyers' requirements③ production      meeting the diverse needs                         of customers④ product       building relationshipswith employers⑤ demand       satisfying the buyers' individual needs
options: ② marketing - ignoring the buyers' requirements
③ production - meeting the diverse needs of customers
④ product - building relationships with employers
⑤ demand - satisfying the buyers' individual needs
questions.explanation: 과거에는 생산(production)과 가격에만 집중했지만, 사회가 현대화되면서 고객의 다양한 요구를 충족(meeting the diverse needs of customers)하는 마케팅 혁명으로 비즈니스의 초점이 옮겨갔다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 production, (B)에는 meeting the diverse needs of customers가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고용 - 소비자 가격 분석하기
② 마케팅 - 구매자의 요구사항 무시하기
③ 생산 - 고객의 다양한 요구 충족하기
④ 제품 - 고용주와 관계 구축하기
⑤ 수요 - 구매자의 개별적 욕구 만족시키기

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 3월 38번]
questions.passage: At the turn of the twentieth century, German biologists ␀<u>conducted</u> research on taste. The tongue was mapped into ␁<u>undivided</u> areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, ␂<u>proved</u> that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not ␃<u>classified</u> according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not ␄<u>spot</u>, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.explanation: 지문의 앞부분은 과거에 혀가 특정 맛을 느끼는 구역으로 나뉘어 있다고 믿었음을 설명하고 있습니다. 혀가 구역별로 나뉘어 특정 맛을 등록한다는 맥락이므로 ␁ 'undivided(나뉘지 않은)'는 'divided(나뉜)' 혹은 'discrete(분리된)'로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 글에서 찾아 쓰시오. [23년 3월 32번]
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.summary_sentence: To be confident in (A)________ daily goals, practice (B)________ how long each thing takes, learn from experience, and prioritize tasks based on the amount of time (C)________. Set a time for longer tasks first and put short tasks in between.
subjective_conditions: 글에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 매일 하고자 하는 일을 달성하는 것(achieving what you set out to do)에서 자신감이 오며, 필요한 시간을 어림잡는(estimating) 연습을 하고, 이용 가능한(available) 시간에 맞춰 업무를 배치하라고 조언하고 있습니다. 요약문의 문맥에 맞춰 지문 내 단어들을 추출하여 채울 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [23년 3월 21번]
questions.passage: By adopting technology, thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. ⓐHundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. ⓑSometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. ⓒAt the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. ⓓEducation plays a significant role in personality development by shaping one's values, beliefs, knowledge, and skills. ⓔThe divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk ─ for body and mind.*chronic: 만성의 **sedentary: 주로 앉아서 하는
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기술 도입으로 인해 전통적인 일자리가 사라지고, 현대인들이 싫어하는 일을 하며 겪는 육체적/정신적 고통과 디지털 업무로의 쏠림 현상, 그리고 머리와 손이 분리된 업무 환경이 주는 건강상의 위험에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ⓓ는 교육이 가치관과 기술 형성을 통해 인격 발달에 중요한 역할을 한다는 일반적인 교육의 기능을 설명하고 있으므로 기술 발전과 일자리의 성격 변화라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question:
★ 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. [24년 3월 29번]

13. 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① You can be happy by enjoying your leisure time and hobbies.
② High income is the biggest support for your high self-esteem.
③ In order to feel satisfied, one must have a socially respected job.
④ It is important to consider collaborating with coworkers when choosing a job.
⑤ Finding meaning in your work significantly boosts happiness and success.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 업무(meaningful work)를 통해 성취감을 얻는 것이 개인의 행복과 성공에 얼마나 중요한지를 설명하고 있습니다. 직업에서 깊은 의미를 찾는 사람들이 더 에너지 넘치고 만족스러운 삶을 살며, 업무 성과와 수입 면에서도 더 좋은 결과를 얻는다는 연구 결과를 제시하고 있으므로 주제로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 여가 시간과 취미를 즐김으로써 행복해질 수 있다.
② 높은 수입은 높은 자존감을 위한 가장 큰 지지대이다.
③ 만족감을 느끼기 위해서는 사회적으로 존경받는 직업을 가져야 한다.
④ 직업을 선택할 때 동료들과의 협력을 고려하는 것이 중요하다.
⑤ 자신의 일에서 의미를 찾는 것은 행복과 성공을 크게 증진시킨다.

★ 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. [24년 3월 29번]

Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride.
