questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말이 알맞게 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. (A)____________, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. (B)____________, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.*litter: (한 배에서 태어난) 새끼들
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 환경적 요인이 동물의 반응을 결정한다고 했고, 뒤 문장에서 구조 센터의 고양이와 가정집의 고양이의 반응이 다르다는 구체적인 예시를 들고 있으므로 'For example'이 적절합니다. (B) 앞에서는 환경적 차이에 따른 반응의 차이를, 뒤에서는 치료 목적(신체적 질병 vs 정서적 혼란)에 따른 반응의 차이를 추가로 언급하고 있으므로 'In addition'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 예를 들어 / (B) 게다가
② (A) 사실 / (B) 마찬가지로
③ (A) 게다가 / (B) 더욱이
④ (A) 결과적으로 / (B) 그러나
⑤ (A) 대조적으로 / (B) 그렇지 않으면

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 38번]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.summary_sentence: Research disclosed the error of the traditional "tongue map" theory of taste, revealing taste buds are (A)____________ evenly throughout the mouth, with perception being based on timing rather than (B)____________.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 혀의 지도는 틀린 이론이며, 맛봉오리는 특정 부위에 모여있는 것이 아니라 입안 전체에 골고루 퍼져 있고, 맛을 느끼는 것은 위치가 아니라 시간의 문제라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '분포된(distributed)', (B)에는 '위치(location)'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 배치된 / 맛
② 제거된 / 장소
③ 퍼진 / 냄새
④ 위치한 / 풍미
⑤ 분포된 / 위치

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [24년 3월 40번]
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. The only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
options: ① There are two parts in the mind, one is the conscious part and the other is the subconscious part.
② Of the two parts of the mind, the part where you have more control is the conscious mind.
③ In the conscious mind, we humans are overwhelmed by emotions and repeat wrong decisions, which often discourages us.
④ The subconscious mind is responsible for managing emotions and making rational decisions when the conscious mind fails.
⑤ Fears like being scared of spiders or the dark are based on the conscious mind, but they only become real when recorded by the subconscious mind.
questions.explanation: 본문에 따르면 잠재의식(subconscious mind)은 감정을 다루지 않으며(doesn't deal with emotions), 매우 빠르게 작용하고 기억과 인식을 다룬다고 설명되어 있습니다. 감정에 의해 잘못된 결정을 내리는 것은 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)의 특징입니다. 따라서 잠재의식이 감정을 관리하고 합리적인 결정을 내린다는 ④번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 마음에는 의식적인 부분과 잠재의식적인 부분이라는 두 가지 부분이 있다.
② 마음의 두 부분 중 당신이 더 많이 통제할 수 있는 부분은 의식적인 마음이다.
③ 의식적인 마음에서 우리 인간은 감정에 압도되어 잘못된 결정을 반복하며, 이는 종종 우리를 낙담시킨다.
④ 잠재의식은 감정을 관리하고 의식적인 마음이 실패할 때 합리적인 결정을 내리는 책임이 있다.
⑤ 거미나 어둠을 무서워하는 것과 같은 두려움은 의식적인 마음에 근거하지만, 잠재의식에 의해 기록될 때만 실제가 된다.

questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.summary_sentence: Research disclosed the error of the traditional "tongue map" theory of taste, revealing taste buds are (A)____________ evenly throughout the mouth, with perception being based on timing rather than (B)____________.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거의 '혀 지도' 이론이 잘못되었음을 밝히며, 미뢰는 혀 전체에 골고루 분포되어 있으며 맛의 지각은 위치(장소)가 아니라 시간적 순서에 근거한다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '분포된(distributed)'이, (B)에는 '위치(location)'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 놓인 --- 맛
② 제거된 --- 장소
③ 퍼진 --- 냄새
④ 위치한 --- 풍미
⑤ 분포된 --- 위치

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. (A) As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. (B) There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. (C) People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. (D) Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. (E) Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication.
questions.insertion_sentence: But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'it is marked(눈에 띄다/이례적이다)'는 내용과 뒤따르는 문장의 'People expect that you will say it(사람들은 당신이 그것을 말할 것이라고 기대한다)'는 사회적 기대를 나타내는 흐름이 자연스럽게 연결됩니다. 특히 (C) 뒤에 오는 문장들에서 감사 인사를 하지 않았을 때의 비판 가능성을 언급하고 있으므로, 감사 인사를 하지 않는 것이 눈에 띄게 된다는 문장은 (C) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① Most living things need to move from where they were born to find suitable environments for survival, growth, and reproduction.
② Every species prefers exactly the same climate conditions as every other species, and when the climate changes, they lose the ability to withstand heat or cold.
③ Scientists have discovered through fossils that living things like trees couldn't move during past climate changes.
④ Even if the climate changes, because places that meet climate conditions remain the same, living things don't need to move to find suitable environments.
⑤ All living beings have the ability to move, but entities like trees or barnacles, which cannot move, cannot relocate in other ways.
questions.explanation: 지문은 모든 생명체가 기후 변화에 대응하여 생존, 성장, 번식을 위해 적절한 환경을 찾아 태어난 곳에서 이동해야 하며, 나무와 같은 식물도 씨앗의 형태로 이동할 수 있다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 1번이 지문의 내용과 정확히 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 대부분의 생명체는 생존, 성장 및 번식에 적합한 환경을 찾기 위해 태어난 곳에서 이동해야 한다.
② 모든 종은 다른 모든 종과 똑같은 기후 조건을 선호하며, 기후가 변하면 열이나 추위를 견디는 능력을 잃는다.
③ 과학자들은 화석을 통해 나무와 같은 생명체들이 과거의 기후 변화 기간 동안 이동할 수 없었다는 것을 발견했다.
④ 기후가 변하더라도 기후 조건을 충족하는 장소는 동일하게 유지되기 때문에 생명체는 적절한 환경을 찾기 위해 이동할 필요가 없다.
⑤ 모든 생명체는 이동 능력을 갖추고 있지만, 나무나 따개비처럼 움직일 수 없는 실체들은 다른 방식으로 재배치될 수 없다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
options: ① During sleep, environmental stimuli are not processed immediately, but they gradually become recognized in a normal way and eventually wake a person up from sleep.
② Many animals, including humans, use a half-asleep state to gain some benefits of sleep without completely losing awareness.
③ Scientists conclude that since losing awareness does not protect sleep, it should not be considered a part of the definition of sleep itself.
④ Visual information may get shortened or weakened when it enters the eyes and not processed normally, but other sensory systems detect it and immediately prepare for an attack.
⑤ Even while sleeping, animals and people can respond normally to environmental stimuli, so if you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal, it detects an attack and responds immediately.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 많은 동물(인간 포함)이 완전한 지각적 단절 없이 잠의 혜택을 얻기 위해 졸음이라는 중간 상태를 이용한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ②번이 지문의 내용과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 수면 중에 환경 자극은 즉시 처리되지 않지만, 점차 정상적인 방식으로 인식되어 결국 사람을 잠에서 깨우게 된다.
② 인간을 포함한 많은 동물들은 의식을 완전히 잃지 않고 잠의 일부 이점을 얻기 위해 반수면 상태를 이용한다.
③ 과학자들은 의식을 잃는 것이 잠을 보호하지 못하기 때문에 그것이 잠 자체의 정의의 일부로 간주되어서는 안 된다고 결론짓는다.
④ 시각 정보는 눈에 들어올 때 짧아지거나 약해져서 정상적으로 처리되지 않을 수 있지만, 다른 감각 시스템이 이를 감지하고 즉시 공격에 대비한다.
⑤ 잠을 자는 동안에도 동물과 사람은 환경 자극에 정상적으로 반응할 수 있으므로, 잠자는 포유류의 눈꺼풀을 열면 공격을 감지하고 즉시 대응한다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energyizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater _____________ from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 지문 전체는 일에서의 의미 찾기, 성취감, 만족도가 인간의 행복에 얼마나 중요한지를 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 앞의 내용이 자신의 일에서 더 큰 무언가를 얻은 사람들이 전반적으로 더 행복한 삶을 살 가능성이 높다는 연구 결과이므로, 문맥상 '만족감(satisfaction)'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 만족
② 불평
③ 우울
④ 불안
⑤ 수치심

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed ⓐ<u>at which</u> one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment ⓑ<u>is</u> therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has ⓒ<u>little</u> time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, ⓓ<u>allowing</u> for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than ⓔ<u>that</u> of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'pedestrian travel'이며, 'being much slower'는 분사구문으로 삽입된 형태입니다. 문장 전체에 정동사가 없으므로 현재분사인 'allowing'을 정동사 형태인 'allows'로 고쳐야 문법적으로 옳습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snacks can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "<u>senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds</u>," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate: 척추동물 **odor: 냄새
options: ① The senses are combined by the common sense.
② Engaging the five senses to learn about our world is necessary.
③ Many animals experience a different version of the world than we do.
④ Whatever I have accepted until now has come to me through my senses.
⑤ Distinguishing and systematically classifying various senses is challenging.
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 5가지 감각 외에도 인간에게는 고유 수용 감각이나 평형 감각이 있고, 동물들에게는 냄새 탐지 시스템이나 열 감지 등 더 다양한 감각이 존재한다는 내용을 통해, 감각을 단순히 몇 가지 종류로 명확하게 나누기 어렵다는 것을 시사합니다. 따라서 정답은 '다양한 감각을 구별하고 체계적으로 분류하는 것은 도전적이다(어렵다)'는 의미인 ⑤번입니다.
options_translation: ① 감각은 상식에 의해 결합된다.
② 우리 세계를 배우기 위해 오감을 사용하는 것이 필수적이다.
③ 많은 동물들은 우리와 다른 버전의 세계를 경험한다.
④ 내가 지금까지 받아들인 모든 것은 감각을 통해 왔다.
⑤ 다양한 감각을 구별하고 체계적으로 분류하는 것은 어렵다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing ⓐ<u>newcomers</u> to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ⓑ<u>more</u> accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓒ<u>insensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'ⓓ<u>curse</u> of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts ⓔ<u>forget</u> how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 전문가는 초보자가 기술을 익히는 데 걸리는 시간을 과소평가하는 경향이 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 전문가가 초보자보다 시간을 판단하는 데 있어 더 정확하다는 ⓑ의 'more accurate'는 문맥상 'less accurate'(덜 정확한)가 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 35번]
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.*therapy: 치료 **efficacy: 효능
options: ① Guarantee of Privacy in Community Setting
② Benefit of Group Signing for Mental Therapy
③ Importance of Music for Intellectual Development
④ Better Effect of Group Singing Than Composing Alone
⑤ Improvement of Quality in Life through Individual Activities.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 정신 질환을 앓고 있는 사람들에게 집단 음악 치료(특히 집단 가창)가 삶의 질을 높이고 정신 건강과 안녕을 개선하는 데 큰 도움이 된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '정신 치료를 위한 집단 가창의 이점'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지역 사회 환경에서의 사생활 보장
② 정신 치료를 위한 집단 가창의 혜택
③ 지적 발달을 위한 음악의 중요성
④ 혼자 작곡하는 것보다 집단 가창의 더 나은 효과
⑤ 개인 활동을 통한 삶의 질 개선

questions.question: 26. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 36번]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are ____________ and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: 스포츠에서 아동의 연령과 신체 조건에 맞춰 경기장 크기, 장비, 경기 시간을 조정한다는 내용입니다. 이러한 조정은 아동의 발달 단계나 연령에 맞추어 점진적으로 이루어지는 것이므로 빈칸에는 '점진적인(progressive)'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 점진적인
② 과도한
③ 불필요한
④ 급진적인
⑤ 비이성적인

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca King's orders and reports coming from his lands. (A) Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. (B) They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. (C) The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. (D) When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. (E) The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610km) in three or four days under good conditions.*excel: 탁월하다 **messenger: 전령
questions.insertion_sentence: If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet him.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '다른 전령이 오는 것을 발견하면, 그를 만나러 서둘러 나갔다'는 내용입니다. (C) 문장에서 오두막을 서로 시야에 들어오는 높은 곳에 지었다는 내용이 나오므로, 서로를 발견하고 마중 나간다는 내용인 주어진 문장은 (C) 뒤인 ③번에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다. 이후 (D)에서 전령이 다음 오두막에 가까워졌을 때의 구체적인 소통 방식이 이어집니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "(A)p<u>utting on the same clothes</u>" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ① applying the identical learning method
② knowing both what to do and how to do it
③ wearing one type of clothes regardless of one's taste
④ studying for multiple-choice tests harder than essay tests
⑤ approaching a learning task in a flexible and appropriate way
questions.explanation: 이 글은 상황에 따라 다른 학습 전략을 사용하는 것의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 밑줄 친 '(A)putting on the same clothes'는 비유적인 표현으로, 문맥상 모든 수업이나 학습 과제에 똑같은 방식(rubber-stamp approach)을 적용하는 것을 의미합니다. 따라서 정답은 ① '동일한 학습 방법을 적용하는 것'입니다.
options_translation: ① 동일한 학습 방법을 적용하는 것
② 무엇을 해야 할지와 그것을 어떻게 해야 할지 둘 다 아는 것
③ 자신의 취향과 상관없이 한 종류의 옷을 입는 것
④ 에세이 시험보다 선다형 시험을 더 열심히 공부하는 것
⑤ 유연하고 적절한 방식으로 학습 과제에 접근하는 것

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. (A) They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. (B) The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." (C) If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the quickest rabbits will survive long enough to result in subsequent generation of even faster bunnies. (D) In that case, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. (E) Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
questions.insertion_sentence: Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 생물학자들이 '붉은 여왕 효과(Red Queen Effect)'를 진화 원리를 설명하는 데 사용한다는 내용입니다. (B)까지는 루이스 캐럴의 소설 속 붉은 여왕의 일화(제자리에 머물기 위해 계속 달려야 함)를 소개하고 있으며, (C)부터는 이를 실제 생물학적 예시(여우와 토끼의 진화적 경쟁)에 적용하고 있습니다. 따라서 소설 속 비유와 실제 과학적 적용을 연결해 주는 주어진 문장은 (C) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. Recently, the animals are shown by their ______________ characteristics in animated movies. For example, in "The Secret Life of Pets', the animals are displayed in a more natural way in terms of their physical and habitual qualities. However, they still use their front legs like human hands, the they skill talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.explanation: 빈칸 뒤의 예시인 'The Secret Life of Pets'에서 동물들이 신체적, 습성적 특성 면에서 '더 자연스러운 방식(more natural way)'으로 보여진다고 설명하고 있습니다. 'natural'과 상응하며 동물의 본래적인 특성을 나타내는 단어는 ① 'innate(타고난, 내재적인)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 타고난 (내재적인)
② 인공적인
③ 변장한
④ 과장된
⑤ 초자연적인

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew larger. Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. Village dwellers also learned to _______________________. For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
options: ② cooperate to complete a task more quickly
③ maintain good relationships in the community
④ distinguish good information from bad information
⑤ demand a salary for their work through negotiations
questions.explanation: 공동체 생활을 통해 업무를 분담(divide up the work)하고 효율적으로 조직되었다는 내용이 앞에 나오며, 빈칸 뒤에는 도구 제작자들이 협력을 통해 같은 시간 안에 더 많은 도구를 만들 수 있게 되었다는 구체적인 예시가 제시됩니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '과업을 더 빨리 완수하기 위해 협력하는 것'이 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 도구를 효과적으로 사용하는 것
② 과업을 더 빠르게 완수하기 위해 협력하는 것
③ 공동체 내에서 좋은 관계를 유지하는 것
④ 나쁜 정보로부터 좋은 정보를 구별하는 것
⑤ 협상을 통해 그들의 노동에 대한 임금을 요구하는 것

questions.question: 7. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved.
ordered_passages: (A) In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.(B) Gradually people were given more time off and they came to have spare time. Furthermore, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places.(C) England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 임금 수준과 근로 조건의 개선을 언급하므로, 그 결과로 나타난 여가 시간의 증대와 교통수단의 발달을 설명하는 (B)가 가장 먼저 옵니다. 이어서 (B)에서 언급된 교통수단의 변화(철도 등)가 구체적으로 어떻게 사회를 변화시켰는지 영국의 사례로 보여주는 (C)가 연결되고, 마지막으로 캐나다의 사례와 항공 운송으로의 확장까지 다루는 (A)가 오는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 8. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group.
ordered_passages: (A) This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.(B) As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more.(C) Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 한 가지 특성이 다른 특성까지 결정한다는 잘못된 가정(후광 효과)을 언급하며 연구 사례를 소개합니다. (C)에서 학생들을 두 집단으로 나누어 '따뜻함'과 '차가움'이라는 단어가 포함된 설명을 제공하고 토론 후 인상을 묻는 실험 과정을 구체화합니다. (B)에서 정보에 따라 인상에 큰 차이가 있었고 행동(상호작용)에도 차이가 있었다는 결과를 제시하며, (A)에서 이러한 기대가 인상 형성뿐만 아니라 행동과 관계 형성에도 영향을 준다는 결론을 도출하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
options: ① The type of carbohydrates that are good for your body is complex ones.
② It is quite difficult to break down complex sugar compounds.
③ Some nutrients are released into your body when complex sugar compounds break down gradually.
④ Bad carbohydrates provide your body with much nutrition including the sugars they are formed of.
⑤ Unused carbohydrates are transformed into fat and stored in the body.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 나쁜 탄수화물(단순당)은 구조가 복잡하지 않아 분해되기 쉽고, 그것이 만들어진 당 이외에는 영양소를 거의 포함하고 있지 않다(hold few nutrients)고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 많은 영양을 제공한다는 ④번 보기는 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 신체에 좋은 탄수화물 유형은 복합 탄수화물이다.
② 복합 당 화합물을 분해하는 것은 꽤 어렵다.
+③ 복합 당 화합물이 서서히 분해될 때 일부 영양소가 신체로 방출된다.
④ 나쁜 탄수화물은 그것을 구성하는 당을 포함하여 많은 영양을 신체에 제공한다.
⑤ 사용되지 않은 탄수화물은 지방으로 변하여 몸에 저장된다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
questions.summary_sentence: The future of an individual, like everything else in the world, is (A)_______ in their mind even before it is (B)________.
questions.explanation: 본문은 모든 것이 실제로 시작되기 전에 창조자의 마음속에서 먼저 완성된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 개인의 미래도 이와 마찬가지로 그것이 실제로 실현되기(realized) 전에 마음속에서 이미 미리 결정된다(predetermined)는 요약이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 미리 결정된 - (B) 실현되는
② (A) 무시된 - (B) 설계되는
③ (A) 성취된 - (B) 제거되는
④ (A) 삭제된 - (B) 창조되는
⑤ (A) 고정된 - (B) 상상되는

questions.question: 17. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more ⓐ<u>geographically</u> spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, ⓑ<u>which</u> in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products ⓒ<u>that</u> customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that ⓓ<u>destroyed</u> the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, ⓔ<u>becoming </u>the focus of business.
options: ① the appropriate distance between business and customers
② the necessity of modernization for people's comfortable lives
③ Henry Ford's creativity of producing products only in back
④ the difficulty in focusing on the complicated needs of customers
⑤ the importance of meeting the customers' needs after modernization
questions.explanation: 이 글은 1940년대와 1950년대의 산업 사회 변화에 따라 판매에 대한 철학적 변화가 일어났음을 설명합니다. 과거에는 단순히 양질의 제품을 생산하면 수요가 창출된다는 관점이었으나, 현대 사회로 접어들며 고객이 실제로 원하는 제품을 제공하고 그들의 복잡한 요구를 충족시키는 마케팅 혁명이 일어났다는 내용이 핵심입니다. 따라서 주제는 현대화 이후 고객의 요구를 충족시키는 것의 중요성입니다.
options_translation: ① 기업과 고객 사이의 적절한 거리
② 사람들의 편안한 삶을 위한 현대화의 필요성
③ 검은색으로만 제품을 생산한 헨리 포드의 창의성
④ 고객의 복잡한 요구에 집중하는 것의 어려움
⑤ 현대화 이후 고객의 요구를 충족시키는 것의 중요성

questions.question: 18. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more ⓐ<u>geographically</u> spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, ⓑ<u>which</u> in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products ⓒ<u>that</u> customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that ⓓ<u>destroyed</u> the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, ⓔ<u>becoming </u>the focus of business.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 마지막 문장에서 주어는 'Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs'입니다. 이 주어에 대응하는 본동사가 문장에 존재하지 않으므로, 현재분사인 'becoming'을 본동사 형태인 'became'으로 고쳐야 문법적으로 옳습니다.

questions.question: 19. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Being excessively (A)[confident / doubtful] about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of (B)[estimating / neglecting] the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you have (C)[insufficient / sufficient] period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
options: ① What Do You Need to Do to Manage Your Time Efficiently?
② Why Are Spare Moments in Between Worthless for People?
③ The Confidence Comes from the Experience of Success
④ Is It Always Helpful to Create a -Things To Do- List?
⑤ Excessive Optimism Decreases People's Creativity
questions.explanation: 이 글은 효율적인 시간 관리림 위해 각 업무에 소요되는 시간을 정확히 팄단하고 스케줄을 짜는 것이 중요함을 설명하고 읈습니다. 따라서 효율적인 시간 관리림 위해 무얇이 필요한준를 묻는 ①이 가장 적전한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 효율적으로 시간을 관리하기 위해 무얇을 해야 하는가?
② 왜 틈새 시간이 사람들에게 가치가 없는가?
③ 자신감은 -성공의 경험-에서 온다.
④ -할 일 목록-을 만드는 것은 항상 댄움이 되는가?
⑤ 과도한 낙관제의는 사람들의 창의성을 감소시다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 과호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 들어갈 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적전한 것은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Being excessively (A)[confident / doubtful] about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of (B)[estimating / neglecting] the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you have (C)[insufficient / sufficient] period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.explanation: (A) 시간 프너을 설정할 때 무얇을 이룰 수 있을지에 대해 과도하게 'confident(자신감 있는)' 한 것이 문제라고 하는 것이 문맥상 자연설획니다.(B) '할 일 목록' 항목 옆에 필요한 시간을 'estimating(쵔정하는)' 숕관을 들이라는 내용이 접절합니다.(C) 시간이 'insufficient(불충분한)' 때 긴 시간이 건리는 일을 준비하는 것은 소용이 없다는 내용이 맞습니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 묑줄 찜 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적전한 것은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for (A)<u>social evidence</u>. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our ⓐ<u>prospect</u>s of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a ⓑ<u>sensible</u> thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even ⓒ<u>subtle</u>r cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a ⓓ<u>hassle </u>to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to ⓔ<u>adopt</u> the practices of those around you.
options: ① the facts proved by scholars
② the choice of a large number of people
③ the theory frequently mentioned in a book
④ clear evidence that everyone acknowledges
⑤ the information about humans' biological evolution
questions.explanation: 글에서 'social evidence(사회적 줘거)'는 다른 사람들이 하는 행동이늘사 집단을 따라가는 것을 의미합니다. 식당 줄을 예로 든 것처뜐, 많은 사람들의 선택을 보고 결정하는 것이므로 ②이 가장 적전합니다.
options_translation: ① 학자들에 의해 줝명된 사실들
② 많은 수의 ­사람들의 선택
③ 책에서 자줐 언급되는 이론
④ 모든 사람이 인정하는 명확한 줝거
⑤ 인간의 생물학적 진화에 대한 정보

questions.question: 22. 윗글의 묑줄 찜 부분 중 문맥상 의미가 어색하게 연결된 것은?

Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a ⓓ<u>hassle </u>to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to ⓔ<u>adopt</u> the practices of those around you.
options: ① ⓐprospect: an apparent probability of advancement, success, profit, etc.
② ⓑsensible: having, using, or showing sound judgments
③ ⓒsubtle: hard to notice or see; not obvious
④ ⓓhassle: a problem brought about by pressures of time, money, inconvenience, etc.
⑤ ⓔadopt: to take a child of other parents legally as your own child
questions.explanation: 글에서 adopt는 '방식을 채택하다' 또는 '취하다'라눠 의미로 쓰였습니다. ⑤의 영영 퐒이는 '입양하다'라눠 의미로, 이 문맥에서는 적전하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 가능성, 성공, 이익 등의 명백한 확률
② 합리적인 판단을 갖거나 보여줌
③ 알아차리기 어렵거나 보기 힘듬; 분명하지 않음
④ 시간, 돈, 불편함 등의 압박으로 인해 발생한 문제
⑤ 다른 부모의 아이를 법적으로 자신의 아이로 데렐오다

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 제목적으로 가장 적전한 것은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot ⓐ<u>melted</u> rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin ⓑ<u>combining</u> into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange ⓒ<u>itself</u> into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine ⓓ<u>which</u> minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally ⓔ<u>large enough</u> to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
options: ① The Causes and Effects of Volcanic Explosions
② What Determines the Size and Types of Minerals?
③ People Who Study Magma: Is Their Work Worthy?
④ All That Crystals : Large Crystals and Their Beauty
⑤ The Size of Minerals That Can Be Observed with the Naked Eye
questions.explanation: 이 글은 마그마가 식는 과정에서 광물이 형성되는 방식과, 광물의 종류 및 결정의 킬기를 결정하는 요인(옐소의 종류, 냉각 속도 등)에 대해 설명하고 읈습니다. 따라서 ②이 가장 적전한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 화산 폭발의 원인과 결과
② 광물의 킬기와 종류를 결정하는 것은 무얇인가?
③ 마그마를 연구하는 ­사람들: 그들의 일은 가치 있는가?
④ 결정의 모든 것: 킬 결정가 그 아름다움
⑤ 모벼으로 관찰할 수 있는 광물의 킬기

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 묑줄 찜 부분 중 어법상 어색하게 연결된 것은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot ⓐ<u>melted</u> rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin ⓑ<u>combining</u> into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange ⓒ<u>itself</u> into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine ⓓ<u>which</u> minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally ⓔ<u>large enough</u> to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
questions.explanation: ⓒ 문장의 주어는 'atoms of the different compounds'로 복수입니다. 주어와 목적어가 같을 때 재귀대명사를 쓰므로 itself가 아닌 themselves가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. (A) Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. (B) As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. (C) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. (D) Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. (E) It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.insertion_sentence: Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 맛의 기제가 장소가 아니라 '시간'임을 강조하고 있습니다. (E) 뒤의 문장에서 혀끝에서 단맛을 느끼는 것이 아니라 그 지각을 '먼저(first)' 등록한다는 시간적 개념이 설명되고 있으므로 (E) 자리에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸 어디에도 들어가기에 적절하지 않은 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are __________(e)d to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to __________ detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street-a motorist simply has little time or ability to __________ design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, __________(e)s for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: 지문의 빈칸에 들어갈 단어들은 다음과 같습니다.첫 번째 빈칸: human senses are adapted to (인간의 감각은 ~에 맞춰져 있다/적응되어 있다)두 번째 빈칸: ability to distinguish detail (세부 사항을 구별하는 능력)세 번째 빈칸: ability to appreciate design details (디자인의 세부 사항을 감상/이해하는 능력)네 번째 빈칸: allows for the appreciation (감상을 가능하게 하다)따라서 'maintain(유지하다)'은 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 적응하다
② 허용하다
③ 구별하다
④ 유지하다
⑤ 감상하다/이해하다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ⓐ<u>less</u> accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓑ<u>insensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓒ<u>underestimate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an ⓓ<u>earlier</u> session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through ⓔ<u>experts</u>' eyes.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전문가가 초보자에게 무언가를 가르칠 때 겪는 어려움인 '지식의 저주'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 전문가들은 자신이 이미 알고 있는 지식 때문에 초보자가 느끼는 난이도를 과소평가하고 학습 과정의 어려움을 잊어버리는 경향이 있습니다. 따라서 학습 과정을 개선하기 위해서는 전문가의 눈이 아닌 '초보자(newcomers/novices)'의 눈으로 학습 과정을 바라볼 필요가 있습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A), (B), (C)가 각각 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. (A)<u>They</u> found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for (B)<u>them</u> to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make (C)<u>them</u> more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: (A) 'They'는 어린 아이들이 성인 스포츠 환경에 참여하는 것의 어려움을 깨달은 'people'을 가리킵니다. (B) 'them'은 너무 크거나 무거운 장비를 다루기 힘들어하는 'young children'을 가리킵니다. (C) 'them'은 10세 미만의 아이들에게 더 적합하게 조정된 'the court areas, balls and rackets'를 가리킵니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 사람들 - (B) 어린 아이들 - (C) 조정물들
② (A) 사람들 - (B) 성인 경기장, 코트 혹은 아레나 - (C) 코트 구역, 공 그리고 라켓
③ (A) 사람들 - (B) 어린 아이들 - (C) 코트 구역, 공 그리고 라켓
④ (A) 어린 아이들 - (B) 성인 경기장, 코트 혹은 아레나 - (C) 코트 구역, 공 그리고 라켓
⑤ (A) 어린 아이들 - (B) 어린 아이들 - (C) 조정물들

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition.
ordered_passages: (A) There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.

(B) However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because-fueled by emotions-you make the wrong decisions time and time again.
(C) When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark?
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 잠재의식(subconscious mind)의 특징을 설명한 후, (B)에서 'However'를 사용하여 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)에 대해 대조적으로 소개하며 감정에 의해 휘둘리는 특징을 설명합니다. (C)에서는 의식적인 마음이 감정에 의해 판단이 흐려질 때 나타나는 부정적인 예시(거미 공포 등)를 나열하고, (A)에서 이러한 두려움들이 의식적인 마음에서 비롯되어 잠재의식에 기록될 때 실제 두려움이 된다고 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals-sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate: 척추동물 **odor: 냄새
options: ① major differences between human and animal senses
② unique characteristics that some vertebrates have
③ diversity and complexity of sensory perception
④ the most common way to categorize sense systems
⑤ Aristotle's influence on modern science and philosophy
questions.explanation: 이 글은 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 5감을 넘어 인간과 동물이 가진 감각이 훨씬 다양하고 복잡하며, 이를 단순히 몇 가지 범주로 명확히 나눌 수 없다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 감각 인지의 다양성과 복잡성이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간과 동물 감각 사이의 주요 차이점
② 일부 척추동물들이 가진 독특한 특징들
③ 감각 인지의 다양성과 복잡성
④ 감각 체계를 분류하는 가장 일반적인 방법
⑤ 아리스토텔레스가 현대 과학과 철학에 끼친 영향

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 문맥상 괄호 (A)~(C) 안에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements-what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to (A)[follow / neglect]. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement dispersal, as scientists call it. Even creatures that appear (B)[immobile / mobile] are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life-as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born-often occupied by its parent-to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. Movement is constant and (C)[essential / optional]. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.*barnacle: 따개비 **dispersal: 분산 ***fossil: 화석
questions.explanation: 기후 변화에 따라 생물 종은 적합한 기후 환경을 따라(follow) 이동해야 합니다. 나무처럼 움직이지 못하는(immobile) 생물도 씨앗의 형태로 분산이 가능하며, 이러한 이동은 생존과 번식을 위해 필수적(essential)입니다.
options_translation: ① 따르다 - 움직이지 못하는 - 필수적인
② 방치하다 - 움직이지 못하는 - 선택적인
③ 따르다 - 움직이지 못하는 - 선택적인
④ 방치하다 - 움직이는 - 선택적인
⑤ 따르다 - 움직이는 - 필수적인

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should ________________________________________. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.*litter: (한 배에서 태어난) 새끼들
options: ① start with a complete physical examination
② be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal
③ take place in a peaceful and quiet environment for animals
④ be done with gentle care, so animals don't get scared
⑤ follow the requirements of animals' hosts
questions.explanation: 한 배에서 태어난 동물이라도 개별 특성이 다르고 환경(구조 센터 vs 가정) 및 질환의 종류(신체적 vs 정서적)에 따라 반응이 다르다는 내용이 앞에 나옵니다. 따라서 모든 치유 세션은 다르게 탐구되어야 하며, 각 치료는 동물의 특정 필요에 맞게 조정되어야 함(be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal)이 문맥상 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 완전한 신체 검사로부터 시작되어야 한다
② 동물의 특정한 필요에 맞게 조정되어야 한다
③ 동물을 위해 평화롭고 조용한 환경에서 이루어져야 한다
④ 동물이 겁먹지 않도록 부드러운 보살핌과 함께 행해져야 한다
⑤ 동물의 주인의 요구사항을 따라야 한다

questions.question: 31. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions.
ordered_passages: (A) For instance, there's a society that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.

(B) Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage.

(C) There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 영미권 사회의 '고맙다'고 말하는 규범을 예로 듭니다. (C)에서 이러한 규범이 법은 아니지만 지키지 않을 경우 비판받을 수 있음을 설명하며 사회적 기대를 언급합니다. (B)에서 타 문화권으로 화제를 전환하며, 번역 가능한 표현이 있더라도 사용 규범이 다를 수 있음을 시사합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 타 문화권의 구체적인 예시(비용이 큰 경우에만 고마움을 표현하는 사회)를 들어 (B)의 내용을 뒷받침합니다.

questions.question: 32. 다음 글의 내용을 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally-they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.summary_sentence: Even if the eyelids of a sleeping mammal are opened, they will be (A)__________ to see properly as their senses are weakened, protecting their sleep. However, many animals and humans benefit from (B)__________ sleep without total perceptual disengagement using a state of drowsiness.
questions.explanation: 본문은 수면 중 발생하는 '지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)'의 특성을 설명합니다. (A) 지문에서 수면 중인 포유류의 눈꺼풀을 열어도 기능적으로 눈이 보이지 않는 상태(functionally blind)가 된다고 했으므로 '제대로 볼 수 없다'는 의미의 'unable'이 적절합니다.(B) 지각이 완전히 차단되지 않은 '졸음(drowsiness)'이라는 중간 상태를 통해 수면의 이점 중 일부를 얻는 것이므로 '부분적인' 수면을 의미하는 'partial'이 적절합니다. 따라서 정답은 ①입니다.
options_translation: ① 할 수 없는 ... 부분적인
② 할 수 있는 ... 완전한
③ 할 수 없는 ... 깊은
④ 할 수 있는 ... 부분적인
⑤ 허용된 ... 완전한

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "putting on the same clothes" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ① necessity of avoiding too many study strategies
② importance of wearing appropriate clothing in class
③ key elements of lesson planning for creative thinking
④ value of applying learning methods to different tasks flexibly
⑤ effectiveness of using identical reading techniques in the test
questions.explanation: 지문은 학생들이 상황에 맞지 않는 옷을 입지 않는 것처럼, 공부할 때도 모든 과제에 똑같은 방식(고무인 도장 방식)을 적용해서는 안 된다고 설명합니다. 숙련된 학습자는 과제의 성격(객관식 vs 논술식)에 따라 전략을 유연하게 바꾸어야 한다는 내용이므로 ④번 '서로 다른 과제에 학습 방법을 유연하게 적용하는 것의 가치'가 주제로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 너무 많은 학습 전략을 피할 필요성
② 수업 시간에 적절한 옷을 입는 것의 중요성
③ 창의적 사고를 위한 수업 계획의 핵심 요소
④ 서로 다른 과제에 학습 방법을 유연하게 적용하는 것의 가치
⑤ 시험에서 동일한 읽기 기술을 사용하는 것의 효과성

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.*affluent: 부유한
options: ① The Industrial Revolution: An Old Marketing
② The Evolution of Customer-Centric Marketing
③ Henry Fords Impact on Consumer Preferences
④ The Changing Dynamics in Automobile Industries
⑤ A Better Way to Advertise: Going Online Strategy
questions.explanation: 이 글은 1940~50년대 산업 사회가 풍요로워지고 경쟁이 치열해지면서 단순히 품질 좋은 제품을 생산하는 것에서 고객이 실제로 원하는 제품을 제공하는 방향으로 판매의 철학이 바뀌었음을 설명합니다. 과거 헨리 포드의 일방적인 생산 방식이 더 이상 통하지 않게 되었고, 고객의 다양한 요구를 충족시키는 것이 기업의 핵심이 되었다는 내용입니다. 따라서 제목은 '고객 중심 마케팅의 진화'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 산업 혁명: 오래된 마케팅
② 고객 중심 마케팅의 진화
③ 헨리 포드가 소비자 선호도에 미친 영향
④ 자동차 산업의 변화하는 역동성
⑤ 더 나은 광고 방법: 온라인 전략

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. ⓐ<u>Over-optimism</u> about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of ⓑ<u>accessing</u> the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a ⓒ<u>significant</u> amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a ⓓ<u>considerable</u> period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the ⓔ<u>spare</u> moments in between.
questions.explanation: 상당한 시간이 필요한 업무를 준비할 때, 이용 가능한 시간이 '적을' 때 준비하는 것이 무의미하다는 맥락이 되어야 합니다. ⓓ의 considerable(상당한)은 short나 limited와 같은 '짧은/제한된' 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally ⓐ<u>blind.</u> Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is ⓑ<u>weakened</u> or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they ⓒ<u>fail</u> to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of ⓓ<u>disturbing</u> sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the ⓔ<u>intermediate</u> state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.*disengagement: 이탈 **drowsiness: 졸음
questions.explanation: 지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)은 외부 자극에 반응하지 않게 함으로써 잠을 방해하는 것이 아니라 '보호(protecting)'하거나 '유지'하는 기능을 수행합니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 disturbing(방해하는)은 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [23년 3월 31번]
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. ⓐGenerally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. ⓑThis east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. ⓒIf the climatic conditions are favorable, the performance of the sports team significantly improves. ⓓStudies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. ⓔA more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 비행 방향(동쪽 혹은 서쪽)에 따른 시차 적응의 차이와 그것이 스포츠 팀의 경기력에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓒ는 기후 조건이 경기력에 미치는 영향에 대해 말하고 있으므로 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [24년 3월 31번]
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. ⓐAll creatures are capable of some degree of movement. ⓑEven creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. ⓒA creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. ⓓCreatures adjust the thickness of their skin and the amount of their fur in response to climate change. ⓔFrom fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화에 따라 생물 종들이 생존 가능한 지역으로 이동하는 것에 대해 다루고 있습니다. ⓓ는 기후 변화에 대응하여 피부 두께나 털의 양을 조절한다는 신체적 적응에 대해 설명하고 있으므로, '장소 이동'이라는 전체 주제와는 관련이 없습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 3월 36번]
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. (A) As a result, towns and villages grew larger. (B) Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. (C) They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. (D) While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. (E) For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
questions.insertion_sentence: Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'also learned to work together to do a task faster'는 앞서 언급된 '일을 나누어 효율적으로 하는 것(분업)'에 이어 '협력하여 속도를 높이는 것'을 추가로 설명하는 내용입니다. (E) 다음의 예시(도구 제작자들이 도끼와 칼을 만드는 일을 공유함)는 주어진 문장에 대한 구체적인 사례이므로 (E) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea. (A) Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. (B) Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. (C) We begin with an idea about how the future will be. (D) Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. (E) Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
questions.insertion_sentence: The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process.
questions.explanation: 지문의 전반부는 집, 자동차, 옷과 같은 물리적 대상이 만들어지기 전 설계자의 마음속에서 먼저 완성된다는 점을 설명합니다. 주어진 문장은 인간이 자신의 '미래'를 설계하는 것도 이와 똑같은 과정을 거친다고 언급하며 화제를 전환합니다. 따라서 물리적 대상에 대한 설명을 마무리하는 (B) 이후이자, 미래를 구상하기 시작한다는 (C) 단계의 시작점에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. (A) During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. (B) The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. (C) Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. (D) When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. (E) When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
questions.insertion_sentence: This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 원자들이 함께 이동하여 더 큰 결정을 형성할 충분한 시간을 갖기 때문이라는 이유를 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 마그마가 천천히 식을 때 결정이 눈으로 볼 수 있을 만큼 커진다는 (D)의 진술에 대한 직접적인 인과 관계를 제공합니다. 따라서 (D) 문장 바로 뒤인 (E) 위치에 삽입되어야 논리적인 흐름이 완성됩니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience. Leadership is __________________________________.
options: ② a skill that only a few can obtain
③ a native trait that cannot be developed
④ achievable through solitude and independence
⑤ determined by one's historical accomplishment
questions.explanation: 리더십은 역사적인 위인들만의 거창한 목표가 아니라, 평범한 사람들 또한 자신의 아이디어를 발전시키고 공유함으로써 발휘할 수 있는 능력입니다. 나이나 경험에 상관없이 누구나 리더가 될 잠재력이 있다는 내용이므로 빈칸에는 '모든 사람의 범위 안에 있다(누구나 도달 가능하다)'는 의미가 적절합니다.
options_translation: 모든 사람이 도달할 수 있는 범위 안에 있는
소수만이 얻을 수 있는 기술인
개발될 수 없는 타고난 특성인
고독과 독립을 통해 달성 가능한
한 사람의 역사적 업적에 의해 결정되는

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the _________________________________. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① reasonable pricing policy of public transportation
② level of mental and physical endurance required
③ ability to process detail in the environment
④ likelihood of encountering tough obstacles
⑤ major sources of environmental pollution
questions.explanation: 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력에 미치는 영향을 설명하는 글입니다. 인간의 감각은 보행 속도에 최적화되어 있어 빠르게 이동하는 운전자는 세부 사항을 인지하는 능력이 제한되는 반면, 느리게 걷는 보행자는 이를 잘 감상할 수 있습니다. 따라서 이동 속도가 '환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력'을 결정한다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: 대중교통의 합리적인 가격 정책
요구되는 정신적, 육체적 인내의 수준
환경 속의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력
힘든 장애물을 만날 가능성
환경 오염의 주요 원인

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to ________________________________. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ③ suit the specific needs of the animal
④ ignore the differences between animals
⑤ overlook social factors affecting the animal
questions.explanation: 똑같은 동물은 없으며, 환경이나 질병의 종류(신체적 vs 정서적)에 따라 치유 과정에 대한 반응이 다르다는 내용을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 모든 치유 세션은 다르게 탐색되어야 하며, 각 치유 치료는 '동물의 구체적인 필요에 맞춰' 조정되어야 한다는 결론이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 신체적 증상에 집중하도록
② 모든 종에 걸쳐 일반화하도록
③ 동물의 구체적인 필요에 맞추도록
④ 동물들 사이의 차이점을 무시하도록
⑤ 동물에 영향을 미치는 사회적 요인을 간과하도록

questions.question: 28. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.(B) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.(C) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각을 5가지로 정의했다는 내용을 소개합니다. (B)에서 'However'를 통해 그 정의에 의문을 제기하며 인간에게서 누락된 감각(고유 수용성 감각, 균형 감각)을 언급합니다. 이어지는 (A)에서는 'Other animals'를 통해 인간 외의 다른 동물의 특수한 감각(열 감지 등)을 예로 듭니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 'These examples'를 통해 앞선 예시들을 정리하며 감각을 제한된 수로 명확히 나눌 수 없다는 결론을 내리는 구성이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 7. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel.
ordered_passages: (A) This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football.
(B) A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
(C) Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 시차 적응 속도가 여행 방향에 따라 다르다고 언급했습니다. (C)에서 일반적으로 서쪽 여행이 동쪽 여행보다 쉽다는 구체적인 원리를 제시합니다. (A)에서 이러한 동서 차이가 스포츠 팀의 성적에 영향을 미친다는 연구 결과를 제시하고, (B)에서 더 최근의 대규모 연구 결과를 추가 증거로 제시하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. (A) At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. (B) England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. (C) Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. (D) In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. (E) Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
questions.insertion_sentence: With the railways came many large hotels.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 철도와 함께 많은 대형 호텔이 생겨났다는 내용입니다. (C)에서 철도가 유명한 해안 리조트를 열었다는 내용이 나온 후, (D) 뒤에서 구체적인 예시로 캐나다 철도 시스템이 유명한 '호텔'들의 건설을 가능하게 했다는 내용이 이어지므로, (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. (A) As a result, towns and villages grew larger. (B) Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. (C) They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. (D) While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. (E) For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
questions.insertion_sentence: Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 마을 거주자들이 과업을 더 빨리 하기 위해 협력하는 법을 배웠다는 내용입니다. (D)까지는 업무 분담(분업)에 대한 설명이 나오고, (E) 뒤에 나오는 예시인 '도구 제작자들이 석기와 칼을 만드는 일을 분담(협력)하여 같은 시간에 더 많은 도구를 만들었다'는 내용은 협력을 통한 속도 향상을 구체적으로 설명하므로 (E)가 가장 적절한 위치입니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Whose story it is affects what the story is. Changing the main character inevitably leads to a ⓐ<u>shift</u> in the focus of the story. If the events in the story are viewed through the lens of other characters, it results in ⓑ<u>different</u> interpretations of the events. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises which was the heart of the story, our desired outcome is likely to be ⓒ<u>unaffected</u> based on the character's perspective. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would be ⓓ<u>changed</u> if described from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Similarly, Gone with the Wind is the story of Scarlett O'Hara's experience, but if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes, we would likely find ourselves hoping for outcomes that are in their best ⓔ<u>interests</u>.
questions.explanation: 이야기의 주인공이 바뀌면 이야기의 초점이 변하고 사건에 대한 해석도 달라집니다. 따라서 갈등이 발생했을 때 우리가 바라는 결과 또한 누구의 관점에서 보느냐에 따라 당연히 '달라질(changed/altered)' 것입니다. 본문의 unaffected(영향을 받지 않는)는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop ⓐ<u>intimate</u> relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally ⓑ<u>dispensable</u> to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer ⓒ<u>feasible</u>. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that ⓓ<u>demolished</u> the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to ⓔ<u>gratify</u> their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
questions.explanation: 품질 좋은 제품을 저렴한 가격에 만드는 것만으로는 부족하고, 고객이 실제로 원하는 제품을 제공하는 것이 '필수적(essential/indispensable)'이 되었다는 흐름이 되어야 합니다. dispensable은 '없어도 되는, 불필요한'이라는 뜻이므로 문맥상 반대되는 단어입니다.

questions.question: 14. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Chess masters shown a chess board in the middle of a game for 5 seconds with 20 to 30 pieces still in play can immediately reproduce the position of the pieces from memory. Beginners, of course, are able to place only a few. Now take the same pieces and place them on the board randomly and the difference is much reduced. The expert's advantage is only for ⓐ<u>recognized</u> patterns ─ those previously stored in memory. Faced with unfamiliar patterns, even when it involves the same familiar domain, the expert's advantage disappears. The ⓑ<u>advantageous</u> effects of familiar structure on memory have been shown for a wide range of expertise, including music. Individuals with musical training may repeat short sequences of musical notation more ⓒ<u>correctly</u> than those with no musical training when notes follow usual sequences. But the advantage much ⓓ<u>declines</u> when the notes are ordered randomly. Expertise also improves memory for sequences of movements. Dancers who are ⓔ<u>adept</u> at ballet movements are able to repeat shorter sequences of steps than experienced dancers that can repeat a sequence of steps making up a routine better than steps ordered randomly. In each case, memory range _________________________________,
questions.explanation: 전문가들이 일반인보다 더 많은 양을 기억하는 이유는 익숙한 패턴(루틴)을 인식하기 때문이라는 내용입니다. 발레에 숙련된(adept) 무용수는 무작위로 배열된 스텝보다 루틴을 구성하는 연속된 스텝을 더 잘 재현할 것이며, 비숙련자보다 '더 긴(longer)' 시퀀스를 반복할 수 있어야 합니다. 따라서 '더 짧은'을 의미하는 ⓔadept(문장 내 shorter 부분)와 관련된 맥락에서 적절하지 않은 어휘 선택이 포함되어 있습니다. (원문: Dancers are able to repeat longer sequences of steps...)

questions.question: 15. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Chess masters shown a chess board in the middle of a game for 5 seconds with 20 to 30 pieces still in play can immediately reproduce the position of the pieces from memory. Beginners, of course, are able to place only a few. Now take the same pieces and place them on the board randomly and the difference is much reduced. The expert's advantage is only for ⓐ<u>recognized</u> patterns ─ those previously stored in memory.
