Faced with unfamiliar patterns, even when it involves the same familiar domain, the expert's advantage disappears. The ⓑ<u>advantageous</u> effects of familiar structure on memory have been shown for a wide range of expertise, including music. Individuals with musical training may repeat short sequences of musical notation more ⓒ<u>correctly</u> than those with no musical training when notes follow usual sequences. But the advantage much ⓓ<u>declines</u> when the notes are ordered randomly. Expertise also improves memory for sequences of movements. Dancers who are ⓔ<u>adept</u> at ballet movements are able to repeat shorter sequences of steps than experienced dancers that can repeat a sequence of steps making up a routine better than steps ordered randomly. In each case, memory range _________________________________,
options: ① can be raised through repeated chess practices
② randomly grows and decreases in a certain situation
③ is improved by being able to identify recognizable patterns and routines
④ depends on the difference in intelligence between experts and non-experts
⑤ is a measure to determine whether an individual is born with a talent for recognizing sequences
questions.explanation: 체스, 음악, 무용 등 다양한 분야에서 전문가들이 기억력이 뛰어난 이유는 자신이 알고 있는 익숙한 패턴과 루틴을 인식할 수 있기 때문입니다. 따라서 기억의 범위는 인식 가능한 패턴과 루틴을 식별함으로써 향상된다는 ③번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 반복적인 체스 연습을 통해 향상될 수 있다
② 특정 상황에서 무작위로 늘어나고 줄어든다
③ 인식 가능한 패턴과 루틴을 식별할 수 있음으로써 향상된다
④ 전문가와 비전문가 사이의 지능 차이에 달려 있다
⑤ 개인이 순서를 인식하는 타고난 재능을 가졌는지 판단하는 척도이다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye.
options: ① various factors affecting the use of minerals
② factors determining mineral formation and crystal size
③ differences between minerals found on and below surface
④ chemical reactions that occur during the cooling of magma
⑤ the importance of magma in the formation of Earth's crust
questions.explanation: 이 글은 마그마가 냉각되면서 광물이 형성되는 과정과 그 과정에서 광물의 종류를 결정하는 원소의 유형/양, 그리고 결정의 크기를 결정하는 마그마의 냉각 속도에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 '광물 형성과 결정 크기를 결정하는 요인들'입니다.
options_translation: ① 광물 사용에 영향을 미치는 다양한 요인들
② 광물 형성과 결정 크기를 결정하는 요인들
③ 지표면과 지표 아래에서 발견되는 광물의 차이점
④ 마그마 냉각 중에 일어나는 화학 반응
⑤ 지각 형성에서 마그마의 중요성

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster ─ in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
options: ① A Wonderland of the Imagination
② Species Colliding with Each Other
③ Evolution Running on the Treadmill
④ Rabbits Doomed to Fall Prey to Foxes
⑤ The Inevitable Consequence of Controversy
questions.explanation: 여우가 더 빨리 달리도록 진화하면 토끼도 그에 맞춰 더 빨리 달리도록 진화하게 되어, 두 종이 상대적으로 제자리에 머무는 것처럼 보이는 '붉은 여왕 효과'를 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 열심히 달려도 제자리인 트레드밀(러닝머신)에 비유할 수 있으므로 'Evolution Running on the Treadmill'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 상상의 이상한 나라
② 서로 충돌하는 종들
③ 트레드밀 위를 달리는 진화
④ 여우의 먹잇감이 될 운명인 토끼들
⑤ 논쟁의 불가피한 결과

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.summary_sentence: In addition to the language ability, the physical appearance of animals characters are frequently (A)______________ to bear (B)______________ to humans, especially children.
questions.explanation: 동물 캐릭터가 인간 언어를 사용하는 것 외에도, 정서적인 호소력을 갖기 위해 인간과 닮도록 신체적 외형이 변형(contorted/deformed)되어 유사성(likeness/resemblance)을 띠게 된다는 내용입니다. (A)에는 '변형되다'의 의미인 contorted가 적절하며, (B)에는 bear a likeness to (~와 닮다) 표현이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 왜곡된 - (B) 목격
② (A) 변형된 - (B) 유사성
③ (A) 뒤틀린 - (B) 증언
④ (A) 복원된 - (B) 관계
⑤ (A) 파편화된 - (B) 닮음

questions.question: 19. 다음 밑줄 친 부분이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before <u>the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut</u>. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
options: ① we began making a visible creation from the idea
② we started to design the actual project in our mind
③ we chose the right environment for the assignments
④ we planned to make a new regulation for our safety
⑤ we transformed our concepts for creation into our dreams
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 '첫 번째 못이 박히거나 첫 번째 천 조각이 잘리기 전'이라는 표현은 아이디어가 실제 물리적인 실체(건물이나 옷 등)로 만들어지기 시작하는 시점을 의미합니다. 따라서 아이디어로부터 가시적인 창조물을 만들기 시작했다는 의미인 1번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 아이디어로부터 가시적인 창조물을 만들기 시작했다
② 우리가 마음속에서 실제 프로젝트를 설계하기 시작했다
③ 우리가 과제를 위해 적절한 환경을 선택했다
④ 우리가 안전을 위해 새로운 규정을 만들 계획을 세웠다
⑤ 우리가 창조를 위한 개념을 꿈으로 변형시켰다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that _________________________ won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ③ sticking to the identical route
questions.explanation: 이 글은 상황에 따라 다른 학습 전략을 사용하는 유연한 학습자의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 빈칸 앞부분에서 언급된 '고무인장 방식(똑같이 찍어내는 방식)'과 반대되는 개념이 숙련된 학습자의 특징입니다. 따라서 '똑같은 경로를 고수하는 것(sticking to the identical route)'이 모든 수업에 효과가 있지는 않다는 것을 안다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 널리 퍼진 전술을 채택하는 것
② 최적의 전략을 적용하는 것
③ 똑같은 경로를 고수하는 것
④ 그들의 환경을 조작하는 것
⑤ 상당한 능력을 발휘하는 것

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would ________________________; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying ─ but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
options: ② cause the vehicle to run at full speed
③ cultivate perseverance in the face of difficulty
④ take a handful of sand or salt to create traction
⑤ have a wheel fixed tightly in a groove in the road
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성공이 우리를 안락한 타성(rut)에 빠지게 하여 빠져나오지 못하게 만드는 위험에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 'rut'은 원래 바퀴 자국이나 고랑을 의미하므로, 타성에서 벗어날 수 없는 상황을 비유적으로 표현하기 위해 '바퀴가 길의 홈에 단단히 고정되게 하다(have a wheel fixed tightly in a groove in the road)'라는 표현이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 적응력을 약화시키다
② 차량이 최고 속도로 달리게 하다
③ 어려움에 직면했을 때 인내심을 기르다
④ 견인력을 만들기 위해 한 움큼의 모래나 소금을 가져가다
⑤ 바퀴가 길의 홈에 단단히 고정되게 하다

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they (A)[rapidly / slowly] break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. Because their structure is (B)[complicated / uncomplicated], they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body (C)[decomposes / integrates] these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
questions.explanation: 복합 탄수화물(Complex carbohydrates)은 분해되기 어렵기 때문에 (A)천천히(slowly) 분해되면서 에너지를 오래 제공합니다. 반면 나쁜 탄수화물인 단순당은 구조가 (B)복잡하지 않기(uncomplicated) 때문에 분해되기 쉽습니다. 우리 몸은 이러한 단순 탄수화물을 꽤 빨리 (C)분해(decomposes)하며, 남은 에너지는 지방으로 저장됩니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓚ에 <보기>의 단어들을 각각 한 번씩 모두 사용하여 문장을 완성할 때, ⓗ의 자리에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, <u>    ⓐ    </u> <u>    ⓑ    </u> <u>    ⓒ    </u> <u>    ⓓ    </u><u>    ⓔ    </u> <u>    ⓕ    </u> <u>    ⓖ    </u> <u>    ⓗ    </u> <u>    ⓘ    </u><u>    ⓙ    </u> <u>    ⓚ    </u>.
questions.explanation: 이 지문의 마지막 문장은 "More often than not, it's good for you to adopt the practices of those around you."입니다. 각 자리에 대응시키면:ⓐ it's ⓑ good ⓒ for ⓓ you ⓔ to ⓕ adopt ⓖ the ⓗ of ⓘ those ⓙ around ⓚ you 가 됩니다. (보기의 단어를 조합할 때 원문 it is가 생략된 형태로 it is good for you to adopt the practices of those around you 순서가 되어야 함). 단, <보기>의 단어만을 조합하면 'it is'가 없으나 문제의 의도는 문맥상 'it is good for you to adopt the practices of those around you'를 완성하는 것이며 ⓗ에 해당하는 단어는 'of'입니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs ⓐ<u>have been removed</u>. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, ⓑ<u>producing</u> things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs ⓒ<u>that</u> are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans ⓓ<u>avoid</u> low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head ⓔ<u>puts</u> a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk ─ for body and mind.
questions.explanation: ⓓ train A to B(A가 B하도록 훈련시키다) 구문이 쓰여야 하므로 avoid를 to avoid로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they ⓐ<u>automatically have other characteristics with which that characteristic goes together</u>. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. ⓑ<u>Half the students received the word 'warm' contained in a description</u>, and the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, and ⓒ<u>after that the students were asked to give their impressions of him</u>. As expected, ⓓ<u>large differences appeared between the impressions which were formed by the students, </u>depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that ⓔ<u>those students who had expected the lecturer to be warm was likely to interact with him more</u>. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
questions.explanation: ⓔ 주어가 those students(복수)이므로 동사 was를 복수형인 were로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 윤작에 관한 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming makes the soil stay healthy. When the same type of crop is planted in a filed again and again, it uses all the nutrients in the soil. Pests and diseases that are common to that crop also increase.
options: ① This type of farming is hardly sustainable and soil may become barren.
② Crop rotation is an important tool for sustainable agriculture and the health of farm soil.
③ In this system, multiple crops are grown in the same field, but they are rotated on a yearly basis.
④ In this type of rotation, a sequence of three different crops is cultivated consecutively over three years within a single field.
⑤ It can be a good tip to keep detailed records of what you plant where so that you can remember what goes where in future years.
questions.explanation: 본문은 윤작(Crop rotation)이 토양을 건강하게 유지하고 영양소 고갈 및 병충해 증가를 막아준다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 윤작이 지속 가능한 농업과 토양 건강을 위한 중요한 도구라는 ②번이 가장 적절합니다. ①은 지속 불가능하다는 내용이라 틀렸고, ③은 여러 작물을 동시에 기르는 것이 아니라 순서대로 기르는 것이며, ④는 예시에서 3년에 걸쳐 순환된다고 했지만 단일 필드에 대한 설명이라기보다 전체적인 시스템 설명이며, ⑤는 본문에 언급되지 않은 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 이런 종류의 농업은 거의 지속 가능하지 않으며 토양은 척박해질 수 있다.
② 윤작은 지속 가능한 농업과 농지 토양의 건강을 위한 중요한 도구이다.
③ 이 시스템에서는 여러 작물이 같은 밭에서 재배되지만, 매년 순환된다.
④ 이러한 유형의 순환에서, 세 가지 다른 작물의 배열은 단일 필드 내에서 3년에 걸쳐 연이어 재배된다.
⑤ 미래에 무엇이 어디로 가는지 기억할 수 있도록 무엇을 어디에 심었는지 상세한 기록을 남기는 것이 좋은 팁이 될 수 있다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of _____________ communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be similar norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
questions.explanation: 문화마다 사회적 규범(예를 들어 '고맙다'고 말하는 상황)이 다르기 때문에, 다른 공동체의 규범을 모르는 것이 '문화 간(cross-cultural)' 의사소통에서 중심적인 문제가 된다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 민족의
② 민주적인
③ 잘 적응된
④ 문화 간의
⑤ 차별적인

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is __________________________________________________________."
options: ① to focus on the executive decisions regardless of the truth
② the importance to say no when your staff asserts wrong
③ the requirements a respectable boss should have in nature
④ what you must do to get something done in your workplace
⑤ how the employee who has disagreeing viewpoints get promoted
questions.explanation: 대부분의 리더들이 반대 의견을 장려한다고 주장하며, 특히 반대자들의 말을 경청해야 하는 이유는 그들이 겉으로는 '왜 할 수 없는지'를 말하지만, 깊이 들어보면 '무언가를 성취하기 위해 무엇을 해야 하는지'를 알려주기 때문이라는 맥락입니다.
options_translation: ① 진실과 상관없이 경영진의 결정에 집중하는 것
② 직원이 틀린 주장을 할 때 거절하는 것의 중요성
③ 존경받는 상사가 본질적으로 가져야 할 요건들
④ 직장에서 무언가를 완수하기 위해 당신이 해야만 하는 것
⑤ 반대 의견을 가진 직원이 승진하는 방법

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is ①<u>what</u> we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the realtime challenges ②<u>that</u> you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me ③<u>give</u> you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." ④<u>Once</u> you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way ⑤<u>how</u> you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
questions.explanation:
⑤번은 선행사 'the way'와 관계부사 'how'가 함께 쓰였습니다. 영어 어법상 'the way'와 'how'는 반드시 둘 중 하나만 써야 하며, 나란히 쓸 수 없습니다. 따라서 'the way'만 남기거나, 혹은 'the way that' 또는 'the way in which' 등으로 고쳐야 합니다.

[오답 분석]
① what: 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사로 'is'의 보어 역할을 하며 뒤에 'for'의 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 문장을 이끌고 있어 적절합니다.
② that: 'challenges'를 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사로 적절합니다.
③ give: 사역동사 'let'의 목적보어 자리이므로 원형부정사인 'give'가 오는 것이 적절합니다.
④ Once: '일단 ~하면'이라는 의미를 가진 접속사로 문맥상 적절하게 쓰였습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question, how many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are 5 in both humans and animals, sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is ①<u>distinct</u> from touch and the sense of balance, which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to ②<u>classify</u>. Many vertebrates have a 2nd sensory system for detecting odors. Snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. The American philosopher Thomas Nagel argued that other animals have conscious experiences that are inherently ③<u>objective</u> and hard to describe. In thinking about other animals, we are ④<u>biased</u> by our own senses and by vision in particular. Our species and our culture are so driven by sight that even people who are blind from birth will describe the world using visual words and metaphors. Even when scientists describe senses that humans ⑤<u>lack</u> altogether, like the ability to detect electric fields, they talk about images and shadows. Senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.    *inherently: 선천적으로
questions.explanation: 다른 동물의 의식 경험은 관찰 가능한 '객관적인(objective)' 것이 아니라, 그 주체만이 느낄 수 있는 '주관적인(subjective)' 것이기 때문에 설명하기 어렵다고 보는 것이 옳습니다. 따라서 ③번의 objective는 subjective로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably (A)[more / less] accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become (B)[sensitive / insensitive] to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how (C)[easy / hard] it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to took at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: (A) 전문가들은 초보자의 입장을 이해하기 어렵다는 내용이므로, 휴대폰 사용 시간 예측에 있어 초보자보다 'less(덜)' 정확했다고 보는 것이 맞습니다. (B) 초보자에겂 과업이 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 무감각해지는 것이므로 'insensitive' 가 적절합니다. (C) 전문가들은 자신들이 배우는 것이 얼마나 '어려웠는지(hard)'를 잊기 때문에 학생의 눈으로 바라봐야 한다는 결론으로 이어집니다.
options_translation: (A) 더 - (B) 민감한 - (C) 쉬운
(A) 더 - (B) 무감각한 - (C) 어려운
(A) 덜 - (B) 민감한 - (C) 쉬운
(A) 덜 - (B) 무감각한 - (C) 어려운
(A) 덜 - (B) 무감각한 - (C) 쉬운

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr.
ordered_passages: (A) Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
(B) If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal.

(C) Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 링컨이나 마틴 루터 킹 같은 위대한 지도자들을 언급했습니다. (B)에서 '이러한 개인들(these individuals)'을 언급하며 리더십이 숭고하고 높은 목표처럼 보일 수 있다고 연결합니다. (C)에서 그들이 아이디어를 개선하고 목표를 달성하는 과정을 설명한 뒤, (A)에서 '따라서(Thus)' 우리 모두가 나이나 경험에 상관없이 리더가 될 잠재력이 있다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. (A) Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. (B) As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. (C) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. (D) Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. (E) It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.insertion_sentence: Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 맛을 느끼는 기제가 '장소(place)'가 아니라 '시간(time)'이라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 혀의 모든 부위에서 맛을 느낄 수 있다는 (D)의 설명 뒤에 이 문장이 위치해야, (E) 뒤의 내용인 '혀끝에서 단맛을 느끼는 것이 아니라 그 감각을 가장 먼저(first) 인식하는 것이다'라는 시간적 지각 설명과 논리적으로 완벽하게 이어집니다. 따라서 (E) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. (A)_____________, our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. (B)_____________, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① Therefore ... On the other hand
⑤ For instance ... As a result
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 인간의 감각은 걷는 속도에 맞춰져 있다고 했으며, 뒤 문장은 그 결과 시속 5마일 이하의 움직임에 세부 사항 파악 능력이 적합하다고 결론짓고 있으므로 인과관계를 나타내는 'Therefore'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞 문장은 운전자의 제한된 시각적 처리 능력을 언급하고 있고, 뒤 문장은 대조적으로 보행자의 세부 사항 감상 가능성을 언급하므로 대조를 나타내는 'On the other hand'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: 그러므로 ... 반면에
여전히 ... 마찬가지로
게다가 ... 이런 이유로
그와 반대로 ... 그럼에도 불구하고
예를 들어 ... 결과적으로

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympics Games. The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants. Not only were their athletic talents superior, the Cubans appeared even stronger from just the colour of their uniforms. A game would not even start and the opposing team would already be scared. A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time. The country that ruled international baseball for decades has not been on top since that uniform change. Traditions are important for a team; while a team brand or image can adjust to keep up with present times, if it abandons or neglects its roots, negative effects can surface.
options: ① 북미의 보수적인 야구 유니폼 스타일은 변화가 필요하다.
② 현대 사회의 새로운 기술이 코치의 역할을 대체하고 있다.
③ 야구팀의 혁신적 이미지 개선은 팀의 전력에 도움이 된다.
④ 시대에 맞게 유니폼 현대화를 수용하는 구단의 인식 변화가 요구된다.
⑤ 팀 이미지를 현대화함에 있어 팀의 전통을 유지하는 것이 중요하다.
questions.explanation: 과거 쿠바 야구팀은 상징적인 붉은 유니폼을 통해 강한 이미지를 구축하며 세계를 제패했으나, 현대화를 위해 이를 변경한 후 쇠퇴했다는 사례를 통해 팀의 전통과 뿌리를 유지하는 것의 중요성을 강조하는 글입니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 putting on the same clothes가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "<u>putting on the same clothes</u>" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ② developing innovative methods for tests
③ sticking to unchanging learning strategies
④ figuring out who they are and what they study
⑤ insisting on wearing the same outfit for special occasions
questions.explanation: 글의 문맥상 '같은 옷을 입는 것'은 상황(강의의 성격이나 시험의 종류)에 상관없이 동일한 학습 방식(고무인 도장 방식)을 고수하는 것을 비유합니다. 따라서 '변하지 않는 학습 전략을 고수하는 것'이 가장 적절한 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 유연한 학습 기술을 적용하는 것
② 시험을 위한 혁신적인 방법을 개발하는 것
③ 변하지 않는 학습 전략을 고수하는 것
④ 자신들이 누구인지와 무엇을 공부하는지 파악하는 것
⑤ 특별한 행사를 위해 같은 옷을 입을 것을 고집하는 것

questions.question: 8. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly everything has to go through your mouth to get to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and prevent it from harm - with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. From the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. <u>What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg</u> and a reflection of what is happening in other parts of the body. Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease that affects the entire body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, posing serious health risks.
options: ① the importance of medical education is overlooked
② a healthy mouth allows your blood to move around freely
③ the formal research on microorganisms has not been conducted
④ advanced medical technologies can lead to the elimination of bacteria and viruses
⑤ oral health issues are indicative of deeper underlying health conditions beyond dental health
questions.explanation: 구강에서 일어나는 일이 '빙산의 일각'이라는 것은 입안의 건강 상태가 단순히 입에 국한된 문제가 아니라 몸 전체의 건강 상태를 보여주는 지표라는 의미입니다. 구강 내 미생물이 혈류를 타고 전신으로 퍼질 수 있다는 본문의 내용을 통해 구강 건강 문제가 치아 건강을 넘어선 더 깊은 기저 건강 상태를 나타낸다는 것을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 의학 교육의 중요성이 간과되고 있다
② 건강한 입은 혈액이 자유롭게 이동하게 한다
③ 미생물에 대한 공식적인 연구가 수행되지 않았다
④ 첨단 의료 기술은 박테리아와 바이러스의 박멸로 이어질 수 있다
⑤ 구강 건강 문제는 치아 건강을 넘어 더 깊은 기저의 건강 상태를 나타낸다

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 It is not the train timetable or the building blueprint가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절합니다. 것은?
questions.passage: When writing a novel, research for information needs to be done. The thing is that some kinds of fiction demand a higher level of detail: crime fiction, for example, or scientific thrillers. The information is never hard to find; one website for authors even organizes trips to police stations, so that crime writers can get it right. Often, a polite letter will earn you permission to visit a particular location and record all the details that you need. But remember that you will drive your readers to boredom if you think that you need to pack everything you discover into your work. The details that matter are those that reveal the human experience. The crucial thing is telling a story, finding the characters, the tension, and the conflict - <u>It is not the train timetable or the building blueprint</u>.
options: ① Focusing on ordinary details can be the crucial aspect of writing a novel
② It's important to avoid overwhelming readers with excessive details
③ Writers need to describe everything they discover to satisfy the readers' curiosity
④ Writing the train timetable or the building blueprint in the novel doesn't drive the readers to boredom
⑤ The through details such as the train timetable or the building blueprint reveal the human experiences
questions.explanation: 소설을 쓤 땄 정보 제각이 필요하지변, 모든 세부 사항(열차 시간표나 건물 차선도 같은 나열) 등을 다 담으려 하면 독자를 지루하게 만든다고 하고 있습니다. 중요한 것은 인간의 경험을 드러내는 이야기이지, 단순한 세부 정보가 아님을 의미합니다. 따라서 과도한 세부 사항으로 독자를 압도하지 않는 것이 중요하다는 ②이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 평범한 세부 사항에 중심을 두는 것이 소설 쐬기의 중요한 면이 될 수 읈다
② 과도한 세부 사항으로 독자를 질리게 하는 것을 피하는 것이 중요핔
③ 작가는 독자의 호기심을 충접시키기 위해 발견한 모든 것을 묘사해야 한다
④ 소설 셍에 열차 시간표나 건물 차선도를 쓤 것은 독자를 지루하게 만든지 않는다
⑤ 열차 시간표나 건물 차선도 같은 차선한 세부 사항이 인간의 경험을 드러내준다

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 각각 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite. TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. In order that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more, boredom in reaction to a (A)___________ environment (B)___________ the level of neural excitation. It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
questions.explanation: 지문은 변화하지 않는 자극에는 신경 반응이 줄어들고(지루함), 새로운 자극에는 반응이 강화되는 신경 체계의 원리를 설명합니다. 새로운 자극이 더 눈에 띄게 하기 위해서, '변하지 않는(constant)' 환경에 대한 지루함은 신경 자극의 수준을 '감소시킵니다(decreases)'.
options_translation: ① 끊임없는(변하지 않는) - 감소시키다
② 역동적인 - 감소시키다
③ 안정적인 - 유지하다
④ 역동적인 - 증가시키다
⑤ 끊임없는(변하지 않는) - 증가시키다

questions.question: 21. 제시된 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem.
ordered_passages: (A) So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected.
(B) Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available.

(C) There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 일의 소요 시간을 파악하는 것의 중요성과 과도한 낙관주의의 문제를 언급합니다. (A)는 'So work on it'을 통해 그 문제를 해결하기 위해 시간을 측정하는 연습을 하라고 제안합니다. (B)는 'Give attention also'를 통해 측정한 시간에 일을 맞추는 또 다른 방법을 설명하며, 많은 시간이 필요한 일에 대해 언급합니다. (C)는 'such a task'로 (B)의 많은 시간이 필요한 일을 지칭하며 효율적인 시간 배분 방법을 결론으로 제시합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 11월 35번]
questions.passage: In statistics, the law of large numbers describes a situation where having more data is better for making predictions. According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to match the true state of the world. For instance, on your first encounter with the game of roulette, you may have beginner's luck after betting on 7. But the more often you repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning, meaning that your luck will at some point fade away. Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to balance individual losses.
questions.summary_sentence: In statistics, the law of large numbers suggests that having more data (A)__________ prediction accuracy, as (B)__________ repeated experiments tend to get the results of true probabilities.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 통계학의 대수의 법칙에 대해 설명하고 있다. 대수의 법칙에 따르면 데이터가 많을수록, 즉 실험이 더 자주 반복될수록 결과의 평균이 실제 확률에 가까워져 예측의 정확도가 높아진다는 내용이다. 따라서 (A)에는 '높이다(heightens)', (B)에는 '더 많은(more)'이 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 높인다 ... 더 많은
② 증명한다 ... 더 적은
③ 약화시킨다 ... 더 많은
④ 악화시킨다 ... 더 적은
⑤ 향상시킨다 ... 더 적은

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than ⓐ<u>concentrating</u> on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find ⓑ<u>it</u> difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take ⓒ<u>a few</u> steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. ⓓ<u>Putting</u> too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find ⓔ<u>you</u> struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 If절의 주어인 you입니다. 동사 find의 목적어가 주어인 you와 동일한 대상이므로 재귀대명사 yourself를 써야 어법상 적절합니다. (find yourself struggling)

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed ⓐ<u>at which</u> one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while ⓑ<u>walking</u>. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have an ⓒ<u>even</u> more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, ⓓ<u>allows</u> for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than ⓔ<u>those</u> of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: ⓔ는 문맥상 앞에 나온 'their rate of speed'를 대신하는 대명사입니다. 비교 대상인 'rate(속도)'가 단수 명사이므로, 복수 대명사인 those가 아니라 단수 대명사인 that으로 써야 어법상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic.
ordered_passages: (A) Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day."

(B) Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
(C) Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 실제 삶에서도 마법을 부릴 수 있다고 언급합니다. (C)에서 그 비결(trick)로 현재 직면한 도전 과제들을 쓰고 그것을 긍정적인 문구로 바꾸라고 제안한 후, (A)에서 아침에 일찍 일어나는 것에 대한 구체적인 예시를 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 문구를 쓰고 나면 생각과 행동의 변화가 일어난다는 긍정적인 결과를 설명하는 흐름인 (C)-(A)-(B) 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.

(B) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.
(C) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 아리스토텔레스의 5감설(시각, 청각, 후각, 미각, 촉각)을 설명합니다. (B)에서 철학자 피오나 맥퍼슨이 이에 의문을 제기하며 인간이 가진 다른 감각들(고유 수용성 감각, 평형 감각 등)을 예시로 듭니다. (C)에서 인간 외의 동물들은 분류하기가 더 어려운 감각 체계(뱀의 복사열 감지 등)를 가지고 있다고 확장한 뒤, 마지막으로 (A)에서 감각은 명확하게 몇 가지 종류로 나뉘지 않으므로 있는 그대로 연구해야 한다는 결론을 내리는 (B)-(C)-(A) 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 22번]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus _______________________________ at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ① each one of us holds the possibility of becoming leaders
② leadership is an exclusive privilege limited only to the upper class
③ all of us lack the potential to assume leadership roles
④ leadership is a unique talent only possessed by a few
⑤ we all have the potential to be followers
questions.explanation: 위대한 역사적 리더들도 처음에는 우리와 같은 평범한 학생이나 시민으로 시작하여, 일상을 개선하려는 아이디어를 발전시키고 다른 이들과 협력하며 성장했다는 내용입니다. 따라서 리더십은 소수의 전유물이 아니라 나이나 경험에 관계없이 우리 모두가 가질 수 있는 가능성이라는 결론이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리 각자는 리더가 될 가능성을 가지고 있다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 39번]
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be _________________________________. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ① tailored to meet the particular requirements of the animal
② administered without regard to individual circumstances of the animal
③ identically provided to accommodate the specific needs of the animal
④ applied uniformly considering various surrounding conditions of the animal
⑤ prescribed universally, neglecting the diverse requirements of each animal
questions.explanation: 동물들은 개체마다 특성이 다르고, 처한 환경(구조 센터 vs 가정)이나 겪고 있는 문제(신체적 질병 vs 정서적 혼란)에 따라 치료에 대한 반응이 제각각이라는 설명입니다. 따라서 모든 치유 과정은 일률적으로 적용되어서는 안 되며, 각 동물의 구체적이고 특별한 요구 조건에 맞춰 조정되어야 한다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 동물의 특정 요구 사항을 충족하도록 맞춰져야 한다
② 동물의 개별적인 상황과 상관없이 시행되어야 한다
③ 동물의 구체적인 필요를 수용하기 위해 동일하게 제공되어야 한다
④ 다양한 주변 환경을 고려하여 균등하게 적용되어야 한다
⑤ 각 동물의 다양한 요구 사항을 무시하고 보편적으로 처방되어야 한다

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① The Significant Role of Horses in the Inca Empire's Communication Network
② Inca Empire's Messaging System: Foot Messengers Overcoming the Absence of Horses
③ The Inca Empire: Navigating Message Routes With the Aid of Horses
④ The Magnificence of the Inca Empire: A Historical Overview
⑤ Exploring the Mysteries of the Inca Empire's Architecture
questions.explanation: 말이 없었던 잉카 제국에서 도보 전령인 'Chasquis'를 활용하여 어떻게 효율적으로 왕의 명령과 보고를 전달했는지에 대한 시스템을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 말의 부재를 극복한 도보 전령 시스템이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.summary_sentence: Species adapt to changing (A)___________ by relocating to areas that meet their requirements, facilitated by inherent (B)___________ in all creatures, including seemingly immobile ones, as evidenced by fossil records.
questions.explanation: 생명체는 기후(climates)가 변할 때 생존을 위해 이동하게 되며, 이는 모든 생명체가 가진 고유의 이동성(mobility) 덕분이라는 내용의 글입니다. 나무처럼 움직이지 못해 보이는 생물도 씨앗의 형태로 이동한다는 예시가 이를 뒷받침합니다.
options_translation: (A) 기후 (B) 이동성
(A) 풍경 (B) 취약성
(A) 서식지 (B) 부동성
(A) 서식지 (B) 안정성
(A) 기후 (B) 호기심

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 3월 29번]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of ⓐ<u>satisfaction</u> and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest ⓑ<u>obstructions</u> of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn ⓒ<u>higher</u> incomes. Those highly ⓓ<u>content</u> with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent ⓔ<u>more</u> likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 일이 인간에게 얼마나 중요한지 설명하며, 그러한 일을 가진 사람들이 더 행복하고 활기찬 삶을 산다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ⓑ가 포함된 문장은 자신의 직업을 기쁨과 자부심의 가장 큰 '방해물(obstructions)'이 아니라 '원천(sources)'으로 여긴다는 맥락이 되어야 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 3월 34번]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing ⓐ<u>novices</u> to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less ⓑ<u>precise</u> than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓒ<u>sensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓓ<u>undervalue</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through ⓔ<u>students</u>' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전문가가 초보자에게 어떤 것을 가르칠 때 겪는 어려움인 '지식의 저주'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 전문가는 해당 기술이 초보자에게 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 '민감해지는(sensitive)' 것이 아니라, 자신이 이미 알고 있기 때문에 타인이 배우기 어렵다는 사실을 잊어버리거나 무감각해지게 됩니다. 따라서 ⓒ는 '무감각한(insensitive)' 또는 '무지한(unaware)' 정도의 의미가 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 가장 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents ⓐ<u>disagreeing</u> viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This Idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the ⓑ<u>featured</u> leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually ⓒ<u>discourage</u> internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may ⓓ<u>intend</u> to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen ⓔ<u>hard</u>, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."* dissent: 반대
questions.explanation: 문맥상 대부분의 상사들은 자신이 반대 의견에 찬성한다(pro-dissent)고 말합니다. 따라서 이어지는 인터뷰 내용에서 리더들은 부하 직원들의 내부적인 반대 의견을 '장려한다(encourage)'고 주장하는 것이 흐름상 적절합니다. 'discourage(낙담시키다/막다)'는 문맥에 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.

questions.explanation: 본문에서 당면한 도전 과제(challenges)를 긍정적인 진술(positive statements)로 바꾸어 쓰면 자신감(confidence)을 얻고 사고방식과 행동에 변화가 생긴다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 요약문의 (A)에는 confidence, (B)에는 positive가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기회 - 확실한
② 자신감 - 긍정적인

questions.question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. ① They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. ② Children may have certain advantages in sports due to their physical characteristics, such as greater flexibility and a faster recovery time from injuries. ③ Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. ④ As examples, baseball has T-ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. ⑤ In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child. * prevail: 널리 퍼지다
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린이들에게 맞게 스포츠 환경이나 장비를 아동용으로 변형(adaptation)해 온 사례들에 대한 내용입니다. 반면 ②번 문장은 어린이의 신체적 장점(유연성, 빠른 회복력)을 설명하고 있어 지문의 핵심 주제인 '환경의 변형'과 관계가 없으므로 흐름상 가장 어색합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage:
Working around the whole painting, rather than ①<u>concentrating</u> on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can ②<u>be considered</u> "finished." It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time ④<u>to assess</u> your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. *tempting: 유혹하는  **refinement: 정교하게 꾸밈
questions.explanation:
③번이 포함된 문장에서 동사 'find' 뒤에 '형용사(difficult) + to부정사(to know ~)'의 구조가 올 때는 목적어 자리에 가목적어 'it'을 사용해야 합니다. 따라서 'them'을 'it'으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

[오답 분석]
① concentrating: 'rather than' 뒤에서 동명사 구문으로 쓰여 주어인 'Working'과 병렬 구조를 이룹니다. 
② be considered: '그림은 ~라고 여겨지다'라는 의미의 수동태로 쓰였으며, 조동사 'can' 뒤에 'be p.p.' 형태가 오는 것이 적절합니다.
④ to assess: '~하기 위하여'라는 목적의 의미를 나타내는 to부정사의 부사적 용법으로 적절합니다.
⑤ find: 조건을 나타내는 if절에서는 미래의 일이라도 현재 시제를 사용하므로 'find'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.

(B) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.

(C) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.* vertebrate: 척추동물  *odor: 냄새
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스의 5감설을 소개한 주어진 글 다음에, (B)에서 'However'를 사용하여 인간에게도 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 다른 감각(자기 수용 감각, 평형 감각)이 있음을 들어 반박합니다. 이어지는 (C)에서는 인간 외의 '다른 동물들'이 가진 분류하기 어려운 감각(냄새 감지 시스템, 열 감지 등)을 예로 듭니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 예시들(These examples)을 통해 감각을 특정 숫자로 명확히 나눌 수 없다는 결론을 내리는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. (A) In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. (B) Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. (C) The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. (D) Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites. (E) While they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.* distinguish: 구별하다 ** pedestrian: 보행자
questions.insertion_sentence: On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '반면에 보행은 훨씬 느려서 환경적 세부 사항을 감상할 수 있게 해준다'는 내용입니다. (C) 앞부분까지는 자동차 운전자의 제한된 능력을 설명하고 있고, (D) 뒤에서는 조깅하는 사람과 자전거 타는 사람이 그 중간(자동차와 보행자 사이)에 해당한다는 내용이 나옵니다. 따라서 자동차 운전자와 대조되는 보행자의 특징을 설명하는 주어진 문장은 (D)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are ⓐ<u>identical</u>. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also ⓑ<u>decide</u> how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very ⓒ<u>similarly</u> to a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will ⓓ<u>react</u> differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be ⓔ<u>adjusted</u> to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 동물마다 개별성이 있고 환경에 따라 다르게 반응한다는 내용이므로, 구조 센터의 고양이와 가정집의 고양이는 환경 요인 때문에 매우 '다르게' 반응할 것입니다. 따라서 'similarly'는 'differently' 등으로 고쳐야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은? (정답 세 개) [24년 3월 40번]
questions.passage: The mind has parts ⓐ<u>what</u> are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one ⓑ<u>that</u> you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down ⓒ<u>frequent</u> because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities ⓓ<u>that</u> hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears ⓔ<u>when</u> the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'what'은 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사이지만, 문맥상 선행사 'parts'가 있으므로 주격 관계대명사인 'that'이나 'which'로 바뀌어야 합니다.ⓑ 선행사 'the one'을 수식하는 목적격 관계대명사로 적절합니다.ⓒ 동사구 'lets you down'을 수식해야 하므로 부사 형태인 'frequently'가 되어야 합니다.ⓓ 선행사 'negativities'를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사로 적절합니다.ⓔ 부사절을 이끄는 접속사로 '언제 ~할 때'라는 의미로 적절하게 쓰였습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 32번]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."   *dissent: 반대
options: ① Don't Let Your Staffers Speak Up Freely
② The Famous Leader Who Used to Be a Pro-Dissenter
③ How to Persuade Your Dissenter to Follow Your Leads
④ Sharing the Same Vision With Juniors Makes Your Group Better
⑤ A Golden Key to a Good Leader : Listening to Dissenters
questions.explanation: 이 글은 훌륭한 리더들이 직원들의 반대 의견(dissent)을 장려하고, 그들의 의견을 경청하는 것이 일을 완수하는 데 필요한 것을 찾는 방법이라는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '반대하는 사람들의 말을 듣는 것'이 좋은 리더의 핵심이라는 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 직원들이 자유롭게 발언하게 하지 마라
② 한때 반대론자였던 유명한 리더
③ 당신의 반대자를 리더의 지시에 따르도록 설득하는 방법
④ 하급자들과 같은 비전을 공유하는 것이 그룹을 더 낫게 만든다
⑤ 훌륭한 리더로 가는 황금 열쇠 : 반대자들의 말을 경청하기

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ⓐ<u>less</u> accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓑ<u>sensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓒ<u>underestimate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an ⓓ<u>earlier</u> session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making ⓔ<u>assumptions</u> about how students 'should be' learning.   *novice: 초보
questions.explanation: 지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)에 대한 설명으로, 전문가들은 초보자들에게 그 과업이 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 무감각해지거나 잊어버리게 됩니다. 따라서 ⓑ의 sensitive(민감한)는 insensitive(무감각한) 또는 unaware(인식하지 못하는)와 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. (A) Species are forced to follow. (B) All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. (C) Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. (D) A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. (E) From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.        *barnacle: 따개비  *dispersal: 분산    *fossil: 화석
questions.insertion_sentence: When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too.
questions.explanation: 첫 문장에서 모든 종은 특정한 기후적 요구 사항(climatic requirements)을 가지고 있다고 언급합니다. 주어진 문장의 'those requirements'는 이 기후적 요구 사항을 지칭하며, 기후가 변하면 이러한 요구 사항을 충족하는 장소도 변한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 그 결과로 종들이 (변화된 장소를) 따라가야만 한다는 (A) 뒤의 문장 'Species are forced to follow.'와 자연스럽게 연결되므로 ①번 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the _____________ to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.explanation: 위대한 지도자들도 처음에는 평범한 학생이나 시민으로 시작하여 자신의 아이디어를 발전시키고 다른 사람들과 공유하며 목표를 달성해 나갔다는 내용입니다. 따라서 나이나 경험에 상관없이 우리 모두에게는 지도자가 될 수 있는 '능력(capacity)'이나 '잠재력'이 있다는 결론이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 스트레스
② 운
③ 도전
④ 의심
⑤ 능력

questions.question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order.
ordered_passages: (A) The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third.
(B) For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third.

(C) In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 윤작(Crop rotation)의 개념을 소개합니다. (B)에서 '예를 들어(For example)' 세 개의 밭에 각각 다른 작물을 심는 구체적인 첫해의 예시를 들고, (A)에서 '그다음 해(The next year)' 작물들이 위치를 바꾸는 과정을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 '3년 차(In year three)'와 '4년 차(By the fourth year)'의 순환을 마무리하며 윤작의 장점(지속 가능성)을 언급하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
options: ① 한 그림에 최대한 넣을 수 있는 모든 것을 넣어야 한다.
② 화가는 다양하고 다량의 작품을 완성해야 더 유명해질수 있다.
③ 과하게 작업하기 보다 적절한 휴식 후에 작업하는 것이 중요하다.
④ 작품의 진행사항을 평가하는데 타인의 의견도 필요하다.
⑤ 쉬지 않고 한번에 작업을 완성해야 효율적인 작품을 만들 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부 이후에 '과하게 그려 넣는 것이 그림의 임팩트를 망칠 수 있다'고 경고하며, '결정을 내리기 힘들 때는 휴식을 취하고 새로운 눈으로 돌아오라'고 조언하고 있습니다. 따라서 ③번 '과하게 작업하기보다 적절한 휴식 후에 작업하는 것이 중요하다'가 필자의 주장으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 한 그림에 최대한 넣을 수 있는 모든 것을 넣어야 한다.
② 화가는 다양하고 다량의 작품을 완성해야 더 유명해질수 있다.
③ 과하게 작업하기 보다 적절한 휴식 후에 작업하는 것이 중요하다.
④ 작품의 진행사항을 평가하는데 타인의 의견도 필요하다.
⑤ 쉬지 않고 한번에 작업을 완성해야 효율적인 작품을 만들 수 있다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 문맥상 적절한 단어를 주어진 조건을 사용하여 완성하시오.
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made _____________ for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The _____________ are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
subjective_conditions: 1. 하나의 단어만을 사용할 것.
2. 정확한 스펠링을 쓸 것.
questions.explanation: 지문은 성인 규격의 경기장과 장비가 아이들에게 부적합함을 깨닫고, 스포츠들이 아이들의 연령과 신체적 조건에 맞춰 변화를 주었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 야구의 T-볼, 축구의 작은 공과 경기장, 테니스의 작은 라켓 등은 모두 아이들을 위한 '조정(adaptations)'의 예시입니다. 마지막 문장에서 이러한 조정사항들이 점진적이고 아동의 연령과 관련이 있다고 언급하고 있으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어는 'adaptations'입니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 문맥상 적절한 단어를 주어진 조건을 사용하여 올바르게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of (A)p_____________ sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems (B)n_____________ to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.   *stimuli: 자극     *disengagement: 이탈        *drowsiness: 졸음
subjective_conditions: 1. 주어진 알파벳으로 시작할 것.
2. 각각 하나의 단어만 쓸 것.
3. 정확한 스펠링을 쓸 것.
questions.explanation: (A) 지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)은 외부 자극에 반응하지 않게 함으로써 잠을 방해받지 않게 '보호(protecting)'하는 기능을 수행합니다.(B) 하지만 이러한 지각적 이탈 없이는 잠이 불가능하므로, 그것은 잠의 정의에 '필수적인(necessary)' 것으로 보입니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글을 읽고, 두 가지 물음에 우리말로 자세하게 답하시오. (반드시 우리말 문장으로 작성하시오.)
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you are to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
subjective_conditions: 반드시 우리말 문장으로 작성할 것.
questions.subjective_answer_format: (A)Why are people criticized for not saying Thank you when someone helps them in Anglo society?(B)What is the main problem of cross-cultural communication?(A): _____________________________________________________(B): _____________________________________________________
questions.answer: (A) 도움을 줄 수 있는 무언가를 이제 막 해준 낯선 사람에게 '감사합니다'라고 말하는 규범이 Anglo 사회에 있기 때문이다.(B) 다른 집단의 규범을 모른다는 것은 문화간 의사소통에서 중심적인 문제이다.
questions.explanation: (A) 지문 전반부에서 앵글로 사회에는 문을 열어주는 등 사소한 도움을 준 낯선 이에게 감사 인사를 하는 규범이 존재하며, 이를 어길 시 비판의 대상이 될 수 있음을 설명하고 있습니다.(B) 지문 중반부에서 "Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication."라고 직접적으로 언급되어 있습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글을 읽고, 다음 요약문의 빈칸을 <보기>의 단어와 <조건>을 사용하여 올바르게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings-work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
subjective_conditions: 1. (A)는 6단어로, (B)는 8단어로 작성할 것
2. <보기>에 주어진 단어를 반드시 모두 사용할 것 (미사용 시 감점, 필요 시 형태 변형 가능)
3. <보기> 이외의 새로운 단어 추가 불가
vocabulary_box: (A) work / significant / important / for / contentment / be (총 6개)
(B) can / high / income / and / output / overall / lead to / happy (총 8개)
questions.answer: (A) significant work is important for contentment (B) can lead to high output, incomes, and overall happiness
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 일(meaningful work)이 인간에게 얼마나 중요한지 설명하며, 직업에서의 만족감이 높은 생산성, 소득, 그리고 삶 전체의 행복으로 이어진다는 연구 결과를 다루고 있습니다. 요약문 (A)에서는 '의미 있는 일을 하는 것이 만족감을 위해 중요하다'는 의미가 되도록 significant work is important for contentment로 구성하며, (B)에서는 직업적 만족이 '높은 생산량, 소득, 전반적인 행복으로 이어질 수 있다'는 의미가 되도록 can lead to high output, incomes, and overall happiness로 작성하는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their ⓐ<u>inceptive</u> excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons ⓑ<u>intensify</u> their responses to things that change a ─ especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment ⓒ<u>promotes</u> the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out ⓓ<u>more</u>. It's the neural ⓔ<u>counterpart</u> of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
questions.explanation: 변하지 않는 환경에 대한 지루함은 신경 자극 수치를 낮추어야(reduces/lowers) 새로운 자극이 더 눈에 띄게 됩니다. 따라서 'promotes(촉진하다/높이다)'는 문맥상 어색합니다. 변하지 않는 배경에 대한 반응도를 낮추어야 새로운 위협이나 변화를 감지하기 쉽다는 진화론적 설명을 하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① Where the Incas Build Their Houses
② A Collective Living Area of the Incan Empire
③ The Architectural Method of the Incan Empire
④ How the Inca Empire's Message Is Transmitted
⑤ The Labor Activities of the Young Men of the Incan Empire
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잉카 제국이 말이 없는 상황에서도 'Chasquis'라고 불리는 전령들을 통해 도보로 어떻게 메시지를 효율적으로 전달했는지를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '잉카 제국의 메시지가 어떻게 전달되는가'를 뜻하는 ④번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인카인들이 집을 짓는 곳
② 인카 제국의 집단 거주 지역
③ 인카 제국의 건축 방식
④ 인카 제국의 메시지가 전달되는 방법
⑤ 인카 제국 젊은이들의 노동 활동

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because ─ fueled by emotions ─ you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
options: ① The subconscious mind works rapidly.
② You can take a position in the conscious mind if to continue a thought.
③ Poor decisions driven by emotions often disappoint you.
④ You can draw an objective conclusion when you make a judgment by considering your emotions.
⑤ The genuine fears you experience have something to do with recording your responses in the subconscious mind.
questions.explanation: 지문에서는 감정에 의해 판단이 흐려지면 편견과 부정적인 것들이 생겨 당신을 방해한다고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 감정을 고려하여 판단할 때 객관적인 결론을 도출할 수 있다는 ④번의 내용은 지문과 상반됩니다.
options_translation: ① 잠재의식은 빠르게 작동한다.
② 의식적인 마음에서 생각을 계속할지 여부를 결정할 수 있다.
③ 감정에 이끌린 좋지 못한 결정은 종종 당신을 실망시킨다.
④ 감정을 고려하여 판단을 내릴 때 객관적인 결론을 도출할 수 있다.
⑤ 당신이 경험하는 진정한 공포는 잠재의식에 반응을 기록하는 것과 관련이 있다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. ⓐAs it turns out, the "tongue map" was a common misconception that different sections of the tongue are exclusively responsible for different basic tastes. ⓑToday, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. ⓒAn awareness is prevailing that different parts of the tongue play significant roles for perceiving certain tastes. ⓓSweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. ⓔIt's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first, showing the mechanism at work is not place, but time.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심 주제는 과거의 '혀 지도(tongue map)' 개념이 잘못되었으며, 혀의 모든 부위에서 모든 맛을 느낄 수 있다는 것입니다. 하지만 ⓒ는 '혀의 다른 부위들이 특정 맛을 인지하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다는 인식이 만연해 있다'는 내용으로, 혀 지도의 개념(부위별 특정 맛 인지)을 지지하는 뉘앙스이므로 전체 흐름과 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment.
