In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.summary_sentence: Each treatment should be (A)___________ to the (B)___________ of each animal.
questions.explanation: 지문은 동물마다 특성이 다르고 환경이나 질환의 종류에 따라 반응이 다르므로, 각 동물의 구체적인 필요에 맞춰 치료를 조정해야 한다고 강조합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '맞춰지다/조정되다'라는 의미의 tailored가, (B)에는 '특성'을 의미하는 characteristics가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 탐구되어야 함 / 무리
② 수정되어야 함 / 무게
③ 무시되어야 함 / 본성
④ 맞춰져야 함 / 특성
⑤ 보충되어야 함 / 허약함

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. (A) In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. (B) Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. (C) The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street ─ a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. (D) Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '반면에(On the other hand)'로 시작하며 보행자 이동이 환경적 세부 사항을 감상할 수 있게 해준다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 앞부분((C))에서는 가장 빠른 운전자가 세부 사항을 인지하기 어렵다는 점을 설명했고, (D) 뒤의 문장에서는 보행자와 운전자의 중간 단계인 조거와 자전거 이용자에 대해 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 '운전자(빠름)'의 대조 사례인 '보행자(느림)'를 언급하는 주어진 문장은 (D) 자리에 들어가 앞뒤 맥락을 연결하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements ─ what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of ___________ at some stage of their life ─ as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born ─ often occupied by its parent ─ to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화에 따라 생물들이 이동해야 한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 나무나 따개비처럼 움직이지 못해 보이는 생물들도 생애의 어느 단계(씨앗이나 유충 단계)에서는 이동이 가능함을 설명하고 있으므로, '흩어지기/분산(scattering)'이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 억제하는 것
② 모이는 것
③ 고정하는 것
④ 보장하는 것
⑤ 흩어지는 것

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, ⓐ<u>including</u> singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those ⓑ<u>participating</u> in a greater number of sessions ⓒ<u>experienced</u> the greatest benefits. ⓓ<u>Focusing</u> on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions ⓔ<u>participated</u> in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장은 'with + 목적어 + 분사' 구문입니다. those participating in a greater number of sessions(더 많은 세션에 참여한 사람들)가 가장 큰 혜택을 '경험하는' 능동의 관계이므로 과거분사 experienced가 아니라 현재분사 experiencing으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 요지를 10~15단어로 영어로 작성하시오.
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, ⓐ<u>including</u> singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those ⓑ<u>participating</u> in a greater number of sessions ⓒ<u>experienced</u> the greatest benefits. ⓓ<u>Focusing</u> on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions ⓔ<u>participated</u> in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
subjective_conditions: 10~15단어 내외로 작성할 것
영어로 작성할 것
questions.answer: Group music therapy positively affects individuals with severe mental illness.
questions.explanation: 지문은 집단 음악 치료(노래 부르기 포함)가 정신 질환을 앓는 개인의 삶의 질과 정신 건강, 자존감 등을 향상시킨다는 내용을 담고 있습니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 세 곳을 찾아 바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: One of the most marked characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally ─ they are physically blind. Some visual information obviously gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they achieve to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems crucial to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the extreme state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.answer: (1) physically → functionally(2) achieve → fail(3) extreme → intermediate
questions.explanation: (1) 눈은 뜨고 있어 물리적으로는 볼 수 있지만 뇌에서 처리되지 않는 것이므로 '기능적으로' 먼 상태(functionally blind)가 맞습니다.(2) 자극이 등록되지만 정상적으로 처리되지 않아 개인을 깨우는 데 '실패하는' 것(fail to wake)이 문맥상 적절합니다.(3) 완전한 차단 없이 이득을 취하는 것이므로 극단적인 상태가 아닌 졸음과 같은 '중간의' 상태(intermediate state)가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 our brain and the universe meet이 의미하는 것을 5~10단어의 영어로 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light ─ a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless ─ and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective ─ "the place," as Paul Cezanne put it, "where <u>our brain and the universe meet</u>." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.answer: Our mind and physical reality interact with each other. (or Objective and subjective properties interact with each other.)
questions.explanation: 이 글은 색이 객관적인 물리적 현상이면서 동시에 관찰자의 뇌에 의해 해석되는 주관적 현상임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '우리의 뇌와 우주가 만나는 곳'은 우리의 마음(주관)과 물리적 현실(객관)이 상호작용한다는 것을 의미합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 주어진 우리말과 같도록 <조건>에 맞추어 영작하시오.
questions.passage: For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, <u>자신의 일로부터 더 큰 만족감을 갖는 사람이 전반적으로 더 행복한 삶을 살 가능성이 더 크다는 것을 알아냈다.</u>
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>의 주어진 단어를 모두 사용할 것 (*단, 필요시 어형 변화, 어휘의 중복 활용 및 어휘 추가 가능!)
2. 분사구문을 활용할 것
3. 관계대명사를 포함할 것
vocabulary_box: those / likely great / take / a / have
questions.subjective_answer_format: → For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, ____________________ ___________________________________________________________.정답: ___________________________________________________
questions.answer: finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were more likely to have a happier life overall
questions.explanation: 연구자가 알아낸 내용을 분사구문(finding that...)으로 연결하고, '사람들'을 수식하는 관계대명사절(who took...)을 포함하며 'be more likely to' 구문을 활용하여 영작합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 주어진 우리말과 같도록 <조건>에 맞추어 영작하시오.
questions.passage: <u>Pamela Hinds 박사는 휴대 전화기를 사용하는 데 능숙한 사람들이 휴대 전화기 사용법을 배우는 것에 얼마나 오랜 시간이 걸리는지를 판단하는 데 있어서 휴대 전화의 초보 사용자보다 놀랍도록 덜 정확하다는 것을 알아냈다.</u>
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>의 주어진 단어를 모두 사용할 것 (*단, 필요시 어형 변화, 어휘의 중복 활용 및 어휘 추가 가능!)
2. 비교급을 활용할 것
vocabulary_box: expert / mobile phones / phone users / phones / people / in / take / novice
questions.answer: found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones.
questions.explanation: 주어 Dr. Pamela Hinds 뒤에 동사 found와 접속사 that절을 배치합니다. '숙련된 사람'과 '초보 사용자'를 비교하는 'less accurate than' 비교급 표현을 사용하고, 소요 시간을 나타내는 'it takes (time) to' 구문을 활용하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when they introduce newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ⓐ<u>more</u> inaccurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓑ<u>mindful</u> of how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓒ<u>undervalue</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an ⓓ<u>earlier</u> session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through the views not of teachers, but of ⓔ<u>learners</u>.
questions.explanation: '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'란 전문가들이 초보자가 특정 과업을 수행할 때 겪는 어려움을 망각하거나 무시하게 되는 현상을 말합니다. 따라서 전문가들은 초보자에게 과업이 얼마나 어려운지를 '잊거나 의식하지 못하게(unaware)' 되는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다. ②의 mindful('의식하는', '염두에 두는')은 문맥상 정반대의 의미입니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle as trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: ___________________________________________. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① it is needed to consider the changes of game rules for adults in terms of profits
② the key point to success in sports is gradual growth of physical fitness along with a player's age
③ modification for kids in sports fields is essential when it comes to their developmental processes
④ different sports have seldom developed the new versions for children due to their physical characteristics
⑤ each young player has a different biological age and maturity so that it is inappropriate to compete each other
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린이들이 성인용 경기장이나 장비를 사용하는 것의 어려움을 인식하고, 아동들의 발달 과정에 맞게 장비와 규칙을 점진적으로 조정(변경)해야 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '상식이 승리했다(Common sense has prevailed)'는 문장 뒤에는 '스포츠 분야에서 아동들을 위한 수정이 발달 과정에 있어 필수적이다'라는 내용의 ③번이 오는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 수익 측면에서 성인을 위한 경기 규칙의 변화를 고려할 필요가 있다.
② 스포츠 성공의 핵심은 선수의 연령에 따른 신체 능력의 점진적인 성장이다.
③ 스포츠 분야에서 아동들을 위한 수정은 그들의 발달 과정에 있어 필수불가결하다.
④ 신체적 특성 때문에 다양한 스포츠에서 아동들을 위한 새로운 버전을 거의 개발하지 않았다.
⑤ 각 어린 선수는 서로 다른 생물학적 연령과 성숙도를 가지고 있어 서로 경쟁하는 것은 부적절하다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the 'tongue map' explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the 'tongue map' explanation, different parts of your tongue are for different sorts of tastes. However, recent research discovers that tastes receptors detect all tastes regardless of their (A)___________. It's true that some taste buds are more receptive to certain kinds of tastes than others, but the difference is (B)___________.
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 과거의 '혀의 지도'가 틀린 이론이며, 모든 맛은 혀의 모든 부위에서 느낄 수 있다는 것입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 부위와 상관없음을 뜻하는 '위치(locations)'가 적절하고, (B)에는 부위별로 맛을 느끼는 강도 차이가 있을 수는 있지만 그 차이가 '미묘하다/미미하다(slight)'는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 강도 - 뛰어난
② 종류 - 눈에 띄는
③ 장소 - 기이한
④ 상태 - 미묘한(미미한)
⑤ 위치 - 미미한/미묘한

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are ⓐ<u>identical</u>. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a ⓑ<u>healing</u> session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently from one within a domestic home environment, ⓒ<u>likely</u> to behave similarly. In additional, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react ⓓ<u>differently</u> than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be ⓔ<u>adjusted</u> to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.explanation: 구조 센터에 있는 고양이는 가정 환경에 있는 고양이와 매우 다르게 반응할 것이라고 언급하고 있으므로, 뒤따르는 분사구문은 '비슷하게 행동할 가능성이 높다'가 아니라 '비슷하게 행동할 가능성이 낮다' 혹은 '다르게 행동할 가능성이 높다'는 의미가 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다. 따라서 ⓒ likely를 unlikely 등으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 아래 주어진 단어를 재배열하고 완성하고(A), 그 의미를 한국어로 해석하시오(B).
questions.passage: _______________________________________ - work ⓐ<u>that</u> provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and ⓑ<u>to count</u> their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies ⓒ<u>showing</u> that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work ⓓ<u>are</u> also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, ⓔ<u>she found</u> that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.*numerous: 수많은
questions.answer: (A) It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings. (B) 인간에게 의미 있는 일이 얼마나 중요한지를 과장해서 말한다는 것은 어려울 것이다.
questions.explanation: 주어진 단어들을 조합할 때 가주어 it과 진주어 to-부정사 구문을 활용해야 합니다. 또한 '얼마나 중요한지'에 해당하는 간접의문문(how important meaningful work is)을 목적어 절로 구성하여 완성합니다.

questions.question: 22. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것 2개를 골라 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오. (답안지에 어색한 것 2개를 골라 쓴 후, 바르게 고쳐 쓸 것)
questions.passage: _______________________________________ - work ⓐ<u>that</u> provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and ⓑ<u>to count</u> their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies ⓒ<u>showing</u> that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work ⓓ<u>are</u> also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, ⓔ<u>she found</u> that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.*numerous: 수많은
subjective_conditions: 답안지에 어색한 것 2개를 골라 쓸 것
바르게 고쳐 쓸 것
questions.answer: (1) to count → count(2) she found → finding
questions.explanation: ⓑ는 find their days... and (find) their employment...로 이어지는 병렬 구조이므로 동사원형 count가 적절합니다. ⓔ는 문장이 끝난 후 콤마(,) 뒤에서 결과를 나타내거나 부연 설명하는 분사구문 자리이므로 현재분사 finding으로 고쳐야 하며, 만약 she를 살리려면 and she found와 같이 접속사가 필요합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by (A)__________, this puts in biases and all kinds of others negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the (B)__________ mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your (C)__________.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 쓸 것
각각 한 단어로 쓸 것
questions.explanation: (A) 바로 앞 문장에서 'fueled by emotions'라고 언급되었으므로 감정에 의해 판단이 흐려진다는 의미에서 'emotions'가 적절합니다. (B) 지문 전체에서 사고와 감정 처리를 담당하며 우리를 실망시키기도 하는 부분은 'conscious mind'로 설명됩니다. (C) 지문 초반부에 잠재의식은 인생에 대한 반응(responses)의 기억을 다룬다고 하였으므로 'responses'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 Grace Braddock에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Dear Ms. MacAlpine,I was so excited to hear that your brand is opening a new shop on Bruns Street next month. I have always appreciated the way your brand helps women to feel more stylish and confident. I am writing in response to your ad in the Bruns Journal. I graduated from the Meline School of Fashion and have worked as a sales assistant at LoganMart for the last five years. During that time, I've developed strong customer service and sales skills, and now I would like to apply for the sales position in your clothing store. I am available for an interview at your earliest convenience. I look forward to hearing from you. Thank you for reading my letter. Yours sincerely, Grace Braddock
options: ① Bruns Street에 다음 주에 새 매장을 연다.
② Bruns Journal의 광고를 보고 지원하려고 한다.
③ 패션 학교를 졸업했고 판매직 경험이 있다.
④ 의류 매장의 판매직 분야에 지원하려고 한다.
⑤ MacAlpine이 원하는 시간에 맞춰 면접을 볼 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문 첫 문장에서 매장이 'next month(다음 달)'에 문을 연다고 언급되어 있으므로, '다음 주'라고 설명한 ①번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 is usually just the tip op the iceberg가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Nearly everything has to go through your mouth to get to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and prevent it from harm - with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. From the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. What happens in the mouth <u>is usually just the tip of the iceberg</u>. Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease that affects the entire body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, posing serious health risks.
options: ① is rarely relevant for daily life
② ignores the importance of oral health
③ only affects the appearance of the mouth
④ has no role in maintaining a healthy body
⑤ generally reflects the state of overall health
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락에서 구강 건강이 전신 건강에 영향을 미친다고 설명하고 있습니다. '입안에서 일어나는 일은 빙산의 일각일 뿐이다'라는 표현은 입안의 상태가 보이지 않는 몸 전체의 건강 상태를 나타내는 지표가 된다는 의미이므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 일상생활과 거의 관련이 없다
② 구강 건강의 중요성을 무시한다
③ 입의 외형에만 영향을 미친다
④ 건강한 신체를 유지하는 데 아무런 역할이 없다
⑤ 일반적으로 전반적인 건강 상태를 반영한다

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed ⓐ<u>strict</u> guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a ⓑ<u>potential</u> donor. The reason for these though regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a ⓒ<u>premature</u> diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements ⓓ<u>heighten</u> public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is ⓔ<u>scheduled</u>.
questions.explanation: 장기 기증을 위한 뇌사 판정 기준이 엄격한 이유는 대중의 두려움을 완화하기(ease) 위해서입니다. 하지만 문맥상 이러한 엄격한 요구 사항들이 대중의 의심을 '높이는(heighten)' 것이 아니라, 의심을 '해소하거나 완화하는(allay/reduce)' 역할을 하는지에 대해 의문이 제기된다는 흐름이 되어야 자연스럽습니다. 뒤따르는 문장에서 이러한 요건들이 뇌사 판정이 부정확하다는 잘못된 믿음을 유지시킨다고 언급하고 있으므로, ⓓ는 '완화하다' 계열의 단어가 오는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. ⓐThe Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants. ⓑThe uniforms for the local football team were once made by a small family-owned company that had been in business for generations. ⓒNot only were their athletic talents superior, the Cubans appeared even stronger from just the colour of their uniforms and even before a game started, the opposing team would already be scared. ⓓA few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined and has not been on top since that time. ⓔTraditions are important for a team; while a team brand or image can adjust to keep up with present times, if it abandons or neglects its roots, negative effects can surface.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 쿠바 야구팀의 전통적인 붉은 유니폼과 그 유니폼이 주는 심리적 영향력, 그리고 전통을 버린 후 성적이 하락한 사례를 통해 팀 전통의 중요성을 설명하고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓑ는 지역 '축구팀'의 유니폼이 가족 기업에 의해 제작되었다는 내용으로, 쿠바 야구팀의 사례 및 전통 유지라는 주제와 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions. But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for.
questions.summary_sentence: They study suggests that having access to (A)_____________ information online can contribute to (B)_____________ participants' intellectual confidence.
questions.explanation: 이 실험에 따르면, 첫 번째 단계에서 인터넷 검색을 통해 정보를 얻은 사람들은 두 번째 단계에서 첫 번째 질문과 전혀 상관없는(irrelevant/unrelated) 질문을 받았을 때도 자신들이 더 많이 안다고 느끼며 지적 자신감이 상승(boosting/enhancing)했습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 관계없는 정보를 뜻하는 irrelevant가, (B)에는 자신감을 높여준다는 의미의 boosting이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 필수적인 ... 향상시키는 것
② 무관한 ... 북돋우는 것
③ 연결된 ... 감소시키는 것
④ 관계없는 ... 약화시키는 것
⑤ 부정확한 ... 유지하는 것

questions.question: 8. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: I had never seen a beach with such white sand or water that was such a beautiful shade of blue.
ordered_passages: (A) Jane and I set up a blanket on the sand while looking forward to our ten days of honeymooning on an exotic island.

(B) I didn't want to lose her wedding ring, so I started looking in the area where I thought it had landed. However, the sand was so fine and I realized that anything heavy, like gold, would quickly sink and might never be found again.

(C) "Look!" Jane waved her hand to point at the beautiful scene before us - and her gold wedding ring went flying off her hand. I tried to see where it went, but the sun hit my eyes and I lost track of it.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 해변의 아름다운 풍경을 묘사한 뒤, (A)에서 화자와 Jane이 담요를 깔고 신혼여행을 즐기려는 상황이 먼저 나옵니다. (C)에서 Jane이 풍경을 가리키려다 손을 흔들면서 결혼반지가 날아가 버리는 사건이 발생하고, 마지막으로 (B)에서 반지를 잃어버리지 않으려 찾으려 하지만 모래가 고와서 찾기 힘들 것 같다는 절망적인 상황으로 마무리되는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 9. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristic of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself.
ordered_passages: (A) He used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something, for example. Fortunately, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for the rest of his life. For him, everything returned to normal after one day.

(B) With time, however, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated. As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems.

(C) Psychologist George M. Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment. Stratton wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally turned the world upside down for him. In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 시각 체계의 적응 능력을 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 심리학자 Stratton의 반전 안경 실험이 구체적인 예시로 시작됩니다. (B)에서 시간이 흐름에 따라 시각 체계가 적응하여 정상적으로 행동할 수 있게 되었으나 안경을 벗자 다시 문제가 생겼다는 내용이 이어지며, (A)에서 안경을 벗은 후 겪은 구체적 문제(엉뚱한 손 사용)와 다시 하루 만에 정상으로 회복되었다는 결말로 끝나는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions.
ordered_passages: (A) In other words, minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of clarity.

(B) This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. As emotional beings, humans tend to give meaning to the things around them, making it difficult to distance oneself from them.
(C) Then a relevant question arises here: if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong.
(D) So, minimalists don't encourage you to leave every modern convenience. They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused or unlikely to be used in the near future.
questions.explanation: 미니멀리즘에 대한 오해와 실상을 다룬 글입니다. 주어진 글에서 소유물을 희생한다는 부정적인 인상을 언급했고, (B)에서 이러한 불안감(This insecurity)이 소유물에 대한 애착에서 비롯됨을 설명합니다. (C)에서 감정을 해치는데 왜 미니멀리스트가 되는가라는 질문을 던지고 가정이 틀렸음을 말한 뒤, (A)에서 무용지물을 버릴 때의 일시적 슬픔보다 명료함의 기쁨이 크다는 사실을 통해 감정을 해치지 않음을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (D)에서 결론적으로 미니멀리스트는 불필요한 것만 제거할 것을 권장한다는 견해를 정리합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The adolescent brain is not fully developed until its early twenties. This means the way the adolescents' decision-making circuits integrate and process information may put them at a disadvantage. (A) One of their brain regions that matures later is the prefrontal cortex, which is the control center, tasked with thinking ahead and evaluating consequences. (B) It is the area of the brain responsible for preventing you from sending off an initial angry text and modifying it with kinder words. (C) Because of its earlier development, it is more likely to influence decision-making. (D) Decision-making in the adolescent brain is led by emotional factors more than the perception of consequences. (E) Due to these differences, there is an imbalance between feeling-based decision-making ruled by the more mature limbic system and logical-based decision-making by the not-yet-mature prefrontal cortex. This may explain why some teens are more likely to make bad decisions.
questions.insertion_sentence: On the other hand, the limbic system matures earlier, playing a central role in processing emotional responses.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 청소년기의 뇌 발달 과정에서 발생하는 불균형에 대해 설명합니다. (A)와 (B)에서는 나중에 발달하는 전전두엽 피질(prefrontal cortex)의 역할(결과 평가, 감정 조절)을 설명합니다. 주어진 문장은 'On the other hand(반면에)'로 시작하며 더 일찍 성숙하는 대뇌변연계(limbic system)를 소개하므로, 전전두엽에 대한 설명이 끝난 (C)의 위치가 적절합니다. (C) 뒤에 나오는 'Because of its earlier development, it...'에서 'it'은 주어진 문장의 대뇌변연계를 지칭하게 되어 문맥이 자연스럽게 이어집니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Despite the remarkable progress in deep-learning based facial recognition approaches in recent years, in terms of identification performance, they still have limitations. (A) These limitations relate to the database used in the learning stage. (B) If the selected database does not contain enough instances, the result may be systematically affected. (C) For example, the performance of a facial biometric system may decrease if the person to be identified was enrolled over 10 years ago. (D) The factor to consider is that this person may experience changes in the texture of the face, particularly with the appearance of wrinkles and sagging skin highlighted by weight gain or loss. (E) They are used to compensate for the differences in facial characteristics, which appear over a given time period.
questions.insertion_sentence: To counteract this problem, researchers have developed models for face aging or digital de-aging.
questions.explanation: (C)와 (D)는 시간이 흐름에 따라 얼굴에 주름이 생기는 등 변화가 생겨 안면 인식 성능이 저하되는 '문제점'을 상술하고 있습니다. 주어진 문장은 'To counteract this problem(이 문제를 해결하기 위해)'이라며 얼굴 노화 모델이나 디지털 노화 방지 모델을 개발했다는 해결책을 제시합니다. (E) 문장의 'They'가 주어진 문장의 모델들을 가리키며 그것들이 안면 특성의 차이를 보정하는 데 사용된다고 설명하므로, 주어진 문장은 (E)에 들어가는 것이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson suggests that we tend to understand the world by focusing in on particular features within it. Take platypuses. We might zoom in so ⓐ<u>closely</u> to their fur that each hair appears different. We might also zoom out to the extent ⓑ<u>where</u> it appears as a single, uniform object. We might take the platypus as an individual, or we might treat it as part of a larger unit such as a species or an ecosystem. It's possible to move between many of these perspectives, ⓒ<u>despite</u> we may need some additional tools and skills to zoom in on individual pieces of hair or zoom out to entire ecosystems. Crucially, however, we can only take up one perspective at a time. We can pay attention to the varied behavior of individual animals, look at what unites ⓓ<u>them</u> into a single species, or look at them as part of bigger ecological patterns. Every possible perspective involves emphasizing certain aspects and ⓔ<u>ignoring</u> others.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 절에는 'we(주어) may need(동사)...'라는 완전한 절의 구조가 뒤따르고 있습니다. 'despite'는 전치사로 뒤에 명사(구)가 와야 하며, 접속사인 'although'나 'even though'로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the observable world serves as a(n) ____________________________________________ of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
options: ① perfect reflection of what is beyond our perception
② inadequate mirror of a hidden fundamental reality
③ limitless opportunities for uncovering secrets
④ flawless presentation of physical objects
⑤ unclear insight into the future
questions.explanation: 플라톤의 이데아론에 따르면 우리가 눈으로 보는 현실 세계의 사물들은 불완전하고 변하기 쉬운 것이며, 보이지 않는 완벽한 세계인 '형상(Forms)' 혹은 '보편자'가 진정한 실재입니다. 따라서 관찰 가능한 현실 세계는 이러한 근본적인 실재(이데아)를 제대로 반영하지 못하는 '불충분한 거울(inadequate mirror)'의 역할을 한다고 보는 것이 글의 맥락상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 지각을 넘어선 것에 대한 완벽한 반영
② 숨겨진 근본적 실재의 불충분한 거울
③ 비밀을 밝혀내기 위한 무한한 기회
④ 물리적 대상의 결점 없는 제시
⑤ 미래에 대한 불분명한 통찰

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: When writing a novel, research for information needs to be done. The thing is that some kinds of fiction demand a higher level of detail: crime fiction, for example, or scientific thrillers. The information is never hard to find; one website for authors even organizes trips to police stations, so that crime writers can get it right. Often, a polite letter will earn you permission to visit a particular location and record all the details that you need. But remember that you will drive your readers to boredom if you ________________________________. The details that matter are those that reveal the human experience. The crucial thing is telling a story, finding the characters, the tension, and the conflict - not the train timetable or the building blueprint.
options: ① analyze what you've discovered in your work
② write down every detail without anything missing
③ do not provide accurate information to you readers
④ force your readers to try reading only what you're interested in
⑤ stick to a specific genre such as crime novel or scientific thriller
questions.explanation: 소설 집필 시 세부적인 조사가 필요하지만, 독자에게 정말 중요한 것은 '인간의 경험'을 드러내는 이야기입니다. 따라서 조사한 모든 세부 사항을 빠짐없이 나열하는 것은 독자를 지루하게 만들 수 있다는 경고의 내용이 빈칸에 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 작품에서 발견한 것을 분석하다
② 빠지는 것 없이 모든 세부 사항을 적다
③ 독자에게 정확한 정보를 제공하지 않다
④ 독자들에게 당신이 관심 있는 것만 읽도록 강요하다
⑤ 범죄 소설이나 과학 스릴러와 같은 특정 장르를 고수하다

questions.question: 17. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A ball thrown into the air is acted upon ⓐ<u>by the initial force given it</u>, persisting as inertia of movement and tending to carry it in the same straight line, and by the constant pull of gravity downward, as well as by the resistance of the air. It moves, accordingly, in a curved path. Now the path does not represent the working of any particular force; there is simply the combination of ⓑ<u>the three elementary forces mentioned</u>; but in a real sense, there is something in the total action ⓒ<u>besides the isolated action of three forces</u>, namely, their joint action. In the same way, when two or more human individuals are together, their mutual relationships and their arrangement into a group are things which would be concealed (A)________________________________. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that some of the tendencies to action of the individual are related definitely to other persons, and could not be aroused except ⓓ<u>by other persons acting as stimuli</u>. An individual in complete isolation would not reveal their competitive tendencies, their tendencies towards the opposite sex, their protective tendencies towards children. This shows that ⓔ<u>the traits of human nature are not fully appeared</u> until the individual is brought into relationships with other individuals.
options: ① if we realized we were inseparable from relationships with other individuals
② if we focused our attention only on each individual with out interaction
③ even if we experienced trouble through conflict within relationships
④ unless we confined our attention to each individual separately
⑤ when we understood the working of any particular force
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락에서 공의 궤적이 단일한 힘이 아닌 여러 힘의 결합된 작용에 의해 결정되듯이, 인간의 집단적 행동 또한 개개인을 분리해서 보았을 때는 드러나지 않는 상호 관계적 특성을 지닌다고 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 (A)는 이러한 관계적 특성이 '가려지게 될' 상황을 가정하는 것이므로, 상호작용 없이 각 개인에게만 주의를 집중하는 경우를 의미하는 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 다른 개인들과의 관계에서 분리될 수 없다는 것을 깨달았다면
② 상호작용 없이 오직 각 개인에게만 우리의 주의를 집중한다면
③ 우리가 관계 내의 갈등을 통해 문제를 겪었더라도
④ 우리가 각 개인에게 개별적으로 주의를 국한하지 않는다면
⑤ 우리가 특정한 힘의 작동을 이해했을 때

questions.question: 18. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: A ball thrown into the air is acted upon ⓐ<u>by the initial force given it</u>, persisting as inertia of movement and tending to carry it in the same straight line, and by the constant pull of gravity downward, as well as by the resistance of the air. It moves, accordingly, in a curved path. Now the path does not represent the working of any particular force; there is simply the combination of ⓑ<u>the three elementary forces mentioned</u>; but in a real sense, there is something in the total action ⓒ<u>besides the isolated action of three forces</u>, namely, their joint action. In the same way, when two or more human individuals are together, their mutual relationships and their arrangement into a group are things which would be concealed (A)________________________________. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that some of the tendencies to action of the individual are related definitely to other persons, and could not be aroused except ⓓ<u>by other persons acting as stimuli</u>. An individual in complete isolation would not reveal their competitive tendencies, their tendencies towards the opposite sex, their protective tendencies towards children. This shows that ⓔ<u>the traits of human nature are not fully appeared</u> until the individual is brought into relationships with other individuals.
questions.explanation: ⑤ 'appear'는 '나타나다'라는 의미의 자동사로, 수동태로 쓰일 수 없습니다. 따라서 'are not fully appeared'를 능동태인 'do not fully appear' 혹은 'are not fully revealed(드러나다)'와 같은 표현으로 수정해야 어법상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글이 주장하는 바를 <보기>의 낱말만을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 바르게 배열하고 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. They do well enough in school to keep advancing. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ends with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now lack a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when the journey really begins. When school is finished, your growth becomes voluntary. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career are likely to stop progressing as a result.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 낱말만을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 바르게 배열
questions.answer: Try to lay out a road map for the future on your own and devote your efforts to it.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 학교 교육이 끝난 후 성장은 자발적이어야 하며, 스스로 성장 로드맵을 설계하고 노력해야 함을 주장합니다. 따라서 'Try to' 뒤에 '스스로 미래를 위한 로드맵을 설계하고(lay out a road map for the future on your own) 그것에 노력을 기울여라(and devote your efforts to it)'라는 구조로 배열하는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 흐름에 맞지 않는 어휘를 하나 찾아 올바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and (A)<u>so would everything else</u>. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cezanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 색이 물리적 세계에 '거주하다(존재하다)'라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 '금지하다/방해하다'라는 뜻의 'inhibit'은 'inhabit'으로 고쳐야 합니다. (참고: 제공된 텍스트에는 이미 inhabit으로 적혀 있으나 문제 의도상 오타를 교정하는 유형임)

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 (A)와 같은 의미가 되도록 'so'가 지시하는 바를 본문에서 찾아 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and (A)<u>so would everything else</u>. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cezanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.subjective_answer_format: 정답: Everything else would be _____________, too.
questions.explanation: (A)의 'so would everything else'는 앞 문장의 'its leaves would be colorless'를 받아 '다른 모든 것들도 (색이 없을) 것이다'라는 의미를 나타냅니다. 따라서 so가 가리키는 보어는 colorless입니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 적절한 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 각각 쓰시오. (단, 필요시 주어진 단어의 형태를 변형할 것)
questions.passage: Frederick Douglass was born as a slave at a farm in Maryland. His full name at birth was Frederick Augustus Washington Bailey. He changed his name to Frederick Douglass after he successfully escaped from (A)_____________ in 1838. He became a leader of the Underground Railroad - a network of people, places, and routes that helped enslaved people in their fight for (B)_____________. He assisted other runaway slaves until they could safely get to other areas in the north. As a slave, he had taught himself to read and write and he spread that knowledge to other slaves as well. Once free, he became a well-known abolitionist and strong believer in equality for all people including Blacks, Native Americans, women, and recent immigrants. He wrote several autobiographies describing his experiences as a slave. In addition to all this, he became the first African-American candidate for vice president of the United States.
questions.explanation: Frederick Douglass는 노예(slave)로 태어났으므로 1838년에 탈출한 대상은 '노예 상태(slavery)'입니다. 또한 노예가 된 사람들이 투쟁하는 목적은 '자유(freedom)'입니다. (A)는 slave를 명사형인 slavery로 변형하거나 본문에서 유추하여 씁니다. (B)는 글의 문맥상 자유를 위한 투쟁이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)에 <보기>의 낱말만을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 바르게 배열하고 문장을 완성하시오. (단, 필요시 주어진 단어의 형태를 변형할 것)
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants (A)___________________________________________ by diseases, pests and climate extremes.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 낱말만을 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것
필요시 주어진 단어의 형태를 변형할 것
questions.answer: is in greater danger of being threatened
questions.explanation: 문맥상 주어인 'a global food system'의 상태를 설명해야 하므로 동사 is가 필요하며, '더 큰 위험에 처해 있다'는 의미의 'is in greater danger of' 뒤에 '위협받는 것'이라는 수동의 동명사구 'being threatened'가 이어지는 구조가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 철자로 시작하는 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 한 단어를 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
questions.summary_sentence: Q: What is the (A)e___________ purpose for boredom?A: Individuals with the capacity to feel (B)b___________ easily are favored because they are more likely to improve their (C)c___________ of survival.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 철자로 시작할 것
questions.explanation: 인간이 쉽게 지루함을 느끼는 이유가 진화적 관점에서 생존에 유리하기 때문이라는 내용입니다. (A)는 '진화적인 목적'을 뜻하는 evolutionary, (B)는 지루함을 느끼는 상태인 bored, (C)는 생존 '가능성(확률)'을 높여준다는 의미에서 chance(s)가 적합합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 철자로 시작하는 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 한 단어를 쓰시오.
questions.passage: In statistics, the law of large numbers describes a situation where having more data is better for making (A)p______. According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to match the true state of the world. For instance, on your first encounter with the game of roulette, you may have beginner's luck after betting on 7. But the more often you repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning, meaning that your luck will at some point slowly (B)d______. Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to balance individual losses.
questions.explanation: 통계학의 '대수의 법칙'은 데이터가 많을수록 더 정확한 예측(prediction)을 할 수 있음을 설명합니다. 시행 횟수가 적을 때는 운이 따를 수 있으나, 횟수가 반복될수록 결과는 실제 확률에 수렴하며 일시적인 운은 결국 사라지게(disappear) 됩니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)에 <보기>의 낱말만을 사용하여 바르게 배열하고 문장을 완성하시오. (단, 필요시 주어진 단어의 형태를 변형할 것, 단어 중복 가능)
questions.passage: Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying them to culture. Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually likened to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection. However, these approaches had to be modified to account for the differences between genetic and cultural transmission. For example, we do not expect the cultural transmission to follow the rules of genetic transmission strictly. If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily equally likely to acquire the mother's or father's form of that trait. Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers; thus, the frequency of a cultural trait in the population is relevant beyond just the probability that an individual's parents had that trait. That is, (A)______________________________________________, transmission in the cultural evolution can occur between any individuals.
subjective_conditions: 단, 필요시 주어진 단어의 형태를 변형할 것
단어 중복 가능
questions.answer: compared to biological evolution where genes are transmitted from parents to descendants
questions.explanation: 이 글은 문화적 진화와 생물학적 진화의 차이점을 설명하고 있습니다. 생물학적 진화는 부모에게서 자손으로만 유전자가 전달되지만, 문화적 진화는 부모 외의 사람들과도 일어날 수 있다는 점을 대조해야 하므로 '유전자가 부모로부터 자손에게 전달되는 생물학적 진화와 비교하여'라는 문장을 영작해야 합니다. compare를 분사구문인 compared to로, transmit을 수동태인 are transmitted로 변형하여 활용합니다.

questions.question: [17~18] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.17. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A ball thrown into the air is acted upon ⓐ<u>by the initial force given it</u>, persisting as inertia of movement and tending to carry it in the same straight line, and by the constant pull of gravity downward, as well as by the resistance of the air. It moves, accordingly, in a curved path. Now the path does not represent the working of any particular force; there is simply the combination of ⓑ<u>the three elementary forces mentioned</u>; but in a real sense, there is something in the total action ⓒ<u>besides the isolated action of three forces</u>, namely, their joint action. In the same way, when two or more human individuals are together, their mutual relationships and their arrangement into a group are things which would be concealed (A)________________________________. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that some of the tendencies to action of the individual are related definitely to other persons, and could not be aroused except ⓓ<u>by other persons acting as stimuli</u>. An individual in complete isolation would not reveal their competitive tendencies, their tendencies towards the opposite sex, their protective tendencies towards children. This shows that ⓔ<u>the traits of human nature are not fully appeared</u> until the individual is brought into relationships with other individuals.
options: ① if we realized we were inseparable from relationships with other individuals
② if we focused our attention only on each individual with out interaction
③ even if we experienced trouble through conflict within relationships
④ unless we confined our attention to each individual separately
⑤ when we understood the working of any particular force
questions.explanation: 지문은 공의 궤적이 세 가지 개별 힘의 합산이 아닌 그들의 '공동 작용'에 의해 결정되듯이, 인간 집단 내에서의 행동과 관계 역시 개별 인간만을 보아서는 알 수 없다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 (A)는 집단의 관계나 배치가 '숨겨지게(concealed)' 되는 조건을 묻고 있으므로, 상호작용 없이 개별 구성원에게만 집중할 때라는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 다른 개인들과의 관계에서 뗄 수 없는 존재임을 깨닫는다면
② 우리가 상호작용 없이 각 개인에게만 주의를 집중한다면
③ 비록 우리가 관계 내의 갈등을 통해 문제를 겪더라도
④ 우리가 각 개인에게 별도로 주의를 제한하지 않는다면
⑤ 우리가 특정 힘의 작용을 이해할 때

questions.question: [17~18] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.18. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: A ball thrown into the air is acted upon ⓐ<u>by the initial force given it</u>, persisting as inertia of movement and tending to carry it in the same straight line, and by the constant pull of gravity downward, as well as by the resistance of the air. It moves, accordingly, in a curved path. Now the path does not represent the working of any particular force; there is simply the combination of ⓑ<u>the three elementary forces mentioned</u>; but in a real sense, there is something in the total action ⓒ<u>besides the isolated action of three forces</u>, namely, their joint action. In the same way, when two or more human individuals are together, their mutual relationships and their arrangement into a group are things which would be concealed (A)________________________________. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that some of the tendencies to action of the individual are related definitely to other persons, and could not be aroused except ⓓ<u>by other persons acting as stimuli</u>. An individual in complete isolation would not reveal their competitive tendencies, their tendencies towards the opposite sex, their protective tendencies towards children. This shows that ⓔ<u>the traits of human nature are not fully appeared</u> until the individual is brought into relationships with other individuals.
questions.explanation: ⑤의 'appeared'는 자동사 'appear'의 과거분사형입니다. 'appear'는 자동사이므로 수동태로 쓸 수 없습니다. 따라서 'are not fully appeared'를 현재 완료 형태인 'have not fully appeared'나 단순 현재 'do not fully appear' 등으로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓐ force를 수식하는 과거분사구, ⓑ forces를 후치 수식하는 분사, ⓒ 전치사구, ⓓ 전치사 by의 목적어 acting(동명사)의 의미상 주어 persons 구성으로 모두 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: [20~21] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.20. 윗글의 흐름에 맞지 않는 어휘를 하나 찾아 올바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and (A)<u>so would everything else</u>. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cezanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 색깔이 물리적 세계에 '살고 있지(존재하지)' 않는다는 의미가 되어야 하므로 '억제하다'라는 뜻의 inhibit이 아니라 '거주하다, 존재하다'의 의미인 inhabit으로 고쳐야 합니다. (원문에 'inhabit'으로 표기되어 있으나 문제에서 이를 'inhibit'으로 변형하여 출제한 것으로 간주함)

questions.question: [20~21] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.21. 윗글의 (A)와 같은 의미가 되도록 'so'가 지시하는 바를 본문에서 찾아 한 단어로 쓰시오.

They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and (A)<u>so would everything else</u>. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cezanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.subjective_answer_format: 정답: Everything else would be _____________, too.
questions.explanation: 문장에서 'its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else'는 '나뭇잎도 색이 없을 것이며, 다른 모든 것도 그러할(색이 없을) 것이다'라는 뜻입니다. 따라서 'so'가 받는 형용사는 앞 절의 보어인 'colorless'입니다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 문맥에 맞게 본문에서 유추하여 알맞은 단어로 쓰시오. [3.1점]
questions.passage: In statistics, the law of large numbers describes a situation where having more data is better for making (A)p______. According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to match the true state of the world. For instance, on your first encounter with the game of roulette, you may have beginner's luck after betting on 7. But the more often you repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning, meaning that your luck will at some point slowly (B)d______. Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to balance individual losses.
questions.explanation: 통계학에서 대수의 법칙(law of large numbers)은 시행 횟수가 많아질수록 실제 확률에 가까워진다는 원리입니다. (A)에는 더 많은 데이터가 있을 때 더 잘 할 수 있는 '예측(predictions)'이 들어가는 것이 적절하며, (B)에는 반복적인 시행을 통해 결과가 실제 확률에 수렴하면서 운이 서서히 '사라진다(disappear)'는 의미가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ___________________ than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 지문은 '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 전문가들은 초보자가 특정 기술을 배우는 데 얼마나 오랜 시간이 걸리는지 판단할 때, 자신이 이미 그 기술을 잘 알고 있기 때문에 초보자의 입장을 과소평가하게 됩니다. 따라서 휴대폰 사용 전문가들은 초보자들에 비해 사람들이 휴대폰 사용법을 배우는 데 걸리는 시간을 판단하는 데 있어 현저하게 '덜 정확하다(less precise)'는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 비판적인
② 덜 중요한
③ 더 창의적인
④ 덜 정확한
⑤ 더 정확한

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to ___________________________________. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ① achieve aims of an organization
② discourage creeds of specific groups
③ enable people to seek only one purpose
④ lead people of a group to pursue something trivial
⑤ destroy a faith of an organization in a critical way
questions.explanation: 이 글은 리더십이 특별한 사람들의 전유물이 아니라 일상의 개선을 위해 노력하는 모든 이들이 가질 수 있는 자질임을 설명하고 있습니다. 역사적 리더들 또한 자신의 아이디어를 타인과 공유하고 피드백을 받으며 '조직의 목표를 달성하기 위한(achieve aims of an organization)' 최선의 방법을 찾음으로써 영향력을 발휘했습니다. 따라서 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 조직의 목표를 달성하다
② 특정 집단의 신조를 낙담시키다
③ 사람들이 단 하나의 목적만을 추구하게 하다
④ 집단의 사람들을 사소한 것을 추구하도록 이끌다
⑤ 결정적인 방식으로 조직의 신뢰를 파괴하다

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, ⓐ<u>meaning</u> you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often ⓑ<u>find difficult</u> to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. ⓒ<u>That</u> is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. ⓓ<u>Putting</u> too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide ⓔ<u>whether</u> any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'Working... (주어)'에 대응하는 본동사 자리가 필요하므로 meaning을 means로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓑ find의 목적어로 가목적어 it이 필요하며, difficult는 목적격 보어이므로 find it difficult로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓒ 가주어 it이 필요한 자리이므로 That을 It으로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓓ 동명사 주어로서 적절합니다. ⓔ decide의 목적어절을 이끄는 접속사 '인지 아닌지'의 의미로 적절합니다. 어색한 것은 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ 총 3개입니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. (A) In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. (B) Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. (C) On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. (D) Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 가장 빠른 운전자가 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력이 매우 제한적이라는 내용입니다. (B)까지는 인간이 걷는 속도(시속 5마일 이하)에 맞춰 진화했다는 설명이 나옵니다. (C) 뒤의 문장은 '반면에(On the other hand)'로 시작하며 '보행'이 세부 사항 감상을 가능하게 한다고 말하고 있습니다. 주어진 문장의 운전자(가장 빠른)와 보행자(훨씬 느린)의 대조가 이루어지는 지점인 (C)가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? (A) Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. (B) Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. (C) Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." (D) Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. (E) Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
questions.insertion_sentence: Just change the challenge statement into positive statements.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '어려움에 대한 진술을 긍정적인 진술로 바꾸라'는 지침입니다. (B)에서 어려움들을 적으라고 한 뒤, (C) 위치에서 이 지침을 준 후, 그 뒤에 나오는 예시(아침 일찍 일어나기 힘든 어려움을 '나는 매일 5시에 일어난다'는 긍정문으로 바꾸는 것)가 연결되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to ⓐ<u>prevent</u> my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are ⓑ<u>pro-dissent</u>. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and ⓒ<u>nonprofit</u> leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually ⓓ<u>obstruct</u> internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these ⓔ<u>objectors</u> because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
questions.explanation: 글의 앞부분에서 대부분의 상사들이 자신은 '반대 의견에 찬성한다(pro-dissent)'고 말한다고 했습니다. 따라서 인터뷰에서 리더들이 하급자들의 내부 저항을 계속해서 '방해한다(obstruct)'고 주장하는 것은 문맥상 어색합니다. obstruct 대신 encourage(장려하다)나 invite(청하다)와 같은 단어가 와야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made (A)________ for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures (B)________ children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more (C)________ for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: (A) 성인용 경기 환경이 아이들에게 맞지 않아 여러 스포츠에서 아이들을 위해 '조정(adjustments)'이나 '개조(adaptations)'를 했다는 내용이 적절합니다.(B) 뒤에 완전한 절(children play for shorter...)이 오고 앞에 장소나 추상적인 상황인 구조(structures)를 수식하므로 관계부사 'where'가 적절합니다.(C) 테니스 경기장과 장비를 아이들에게 더 '적절하게(proper/appropriate)' 만들었다는 내용이 와야 합니다.따라서 ⑤ adjustments - where - proper가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 일관성 - ~하는 곳/상황 - 부적절한
② 개조 - 무엇/것 - 적절한
③ 변화 - 어떤 것 - 부적절한
④ 일관성 - 어떤 것 - 맞지 않는
⑤ 조정 - ~하는 곳/상황 - 적절한

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing ①<u>accustomed</u> songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy ②<u>enriched</u> the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest ③<u>advantages</u>. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the ④<u>affirmance</u> of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, ⑤<u>developed</u> a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 노래 부르기가 정신 건강 치료제로서 가지는 '효과성'을 나타내야 하므로 affirmance(단언, 확언)가 아닌 efficacy(효능, 효과)가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
options: ① The presence of various sense
② The importance of detecting odors
③ The process of studying a variety of sense
④ The reason why we doubt five sense
⑤ The way to divide a limited number of specific sense
questions.explanation: 이 글은 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 오감(시각, 청각, 후각, 미각, 촉각) 외에도 인간에게는 고유 수용 감각이나 균형 감각 등이 있고, 동물들에게도 더 복잡하고 다양한 감각 체계가 존재한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '다양한 감각의 존재'가 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 다양한 감각의 존재
냄새 감지의 중요성
다양한 감각을 연구하는 과정
우리가 오감을 의심하는 이유
제한된 수의 특정 감각으로 나누는 방법

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. ⓐFailing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. ⓑWhen you criticize someone, you must have respect for the other person. ⓒNot knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. ⓓTo continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. ⓔIn such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사회적 규범(특히 감사를 표하는 규범)과 그것이 사회적 해석에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. '감사합니다'라고 말하지 않았을 때의 비판적 시선이나 문화권마다 다른 감사 규범에 대해 이야기하던 중, ⓑ의 '타인을 비판할 때는 존중을 가져야 한다'는 내용은 규범의 역할이나 문화적 차이라는 주제에서 벗어난 충고에 가깝습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 들어갈 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are (A)[visually / functionally] blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally (B)[possessed / processed] as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be (C)[possible / impossible] without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 잠자는 상태의 특징에 대한 글입니다.(A): 눈 자체의 기능 문제가 아니라 수면 중 정보 처리가 안 되는 것이므로 '기능적으로(functionally)' 눈이 먼 상태라고 하는 것이 적절합니다.(B): 시각 정보가 들어오기는 하지만 정보가 정상적으로 '처리되지(processed)' 않는다는 맥락이 적합합니다.(C): 지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)이 없으면 수면이 '불가능(impossible)'하므로 수면 정의의 필수 요소라는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 기능적으로 소유된 가능한
② 시각적으로 처리된 불가능한
③ 기능적으로 처리된 불가능한
④ 시각적으로 소유된 가능한
⑤ 기능적으로 처리된 가능한

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; (A)__________, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. (B)__________, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. (C)__________, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ② (A) reversely - (B) As a result - (C) On the other hand
④ (A) therefore - (B) As a result - (C) However
questions.explanation:
(A) 동물마다 개별적인 특성이 다르다는 앞 문장에 대한 결과로 치유 과정의 반응이 다를 수 있다는 내용이 이어지므로 인과관계의 연결어 'therefore(그러므로)'가 적절합니다.
(B) 환경적 요인이 반응에 영향을 준다는 일반적인 진술 뒤에 유기견 센터의 고양이와 가정집의 고양이라는 구체적인 사례를 들고 있으므로 예시의 연결어(For instance/example)가 와야 합니다. (제공된 선택지 ⑤의 'At last'는 문맥상 '마침내'보다는 사례 제시의 맥락으로 이해됩니다.)
(C) 신체적 질병과 정서적 혼란에 따른 반응의 차이를 추가로 설명하고 있으므로, 맥락상 내용의 전환이나 보충을 나타내는 'However' 혹은 'In addition' 계열의 연결어가 위치할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 반대로 - 마침내 - 그러나
② 반대로 - 결과적으로 - 반면에
③ 반대로 - 예를 들어 - 그러나
④ 그러므로 - 결과적으로 - 그러나
⑤ 그러므로 - 마침내 - 그러나

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to ①<u>exaggerate</u> how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more ②<u>energizing</u> and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much ③<u>less</u> likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones carried out a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater ④<u>contentment</u> from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 직업에서 의미와 만족감을 찾는 사람들이 업무 생산성뿐만 아니라 삶 전반에서도 더 큰 행복을 느낀다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 자신의 일에 가장 만족하는 사람들이 삶 전반에서 행복을 느낄 가능성이 '낮다(less)'는 ③번의 표현은 문맥상 적절하지 않으며, '더 높다(more)'와 같은 표현으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; (A)__________, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. (B)__________, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. (C)__________, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ② reversely - As a result - On the other hand
④ therefore - As a result - However
questions.explanation: 동물들은 서로 다르기 때문에 치유 과정에서 다르게 반응할 수 있다는 (A) 인과 관계(therefore)가 적절하며, 환경적 요인의 예시로 보호소 고양이와 가정 고양이를 들고 있으므로 (B)에는 인과나 예시가 적절한데 선택지 중에서는 As a result가 가능합니다. 신체적 질병과 감정적 혼란을 겪는 동물들의 반응 차이를 대조하므로 (C)에는 However가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 반대로 - 마침내 - 그러나
② 반대로 - 그 결과 - 반면에
③ 반대로 - 예를 들어 - 그러나

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements ─ what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life ─ as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born ─ often occupied by its parent ─ to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① The More You Move, the More You Live
② Species on the Move: Adaptation to Climate Change
③ How Animals Are Evolving Because of Climate Change
④ Survival or Extinction? How to Save Endangered Species
⑤ What Are the Factors That Influence the Movement of Animals?
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화에 따라 생물 종들이 생존 가능한 환경을 찾아 이동하며 적응한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '이동 중인 종들: 기후 변화에 대한 적응'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 많이 움직일수록 더 오래 산다
② 이동 중인 종들: 기후 변화에 대한 적응
③ 기후 변화 때문에 동물들이 진화하는 방식
