questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하거나 미루어 알 수 있는 것을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street ─ a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
vocabulary_box: ␀ The average human walking speed is about five miles per hour and under.
␁ Joggers have less time or ability to appreciate design details than pedestrians do.
␂ Motorists would have a greater ability to process environmental features compared to bicyclists.
questions.explanation: ␀ 인간의 감각은 시속 5마일 이하의 셍도에 이상적으로 적응하여 세부 사항을 구분한다고 본문에 명시되어 은유적으로 알 수 읈습니다. ␁ 조깅하는 사람은 부행자밴다 빠르기 때문에 세부 디자인을 감상할 시간이나 눘력이 더 적습니다. ␂ 윐전자는 자전거 타는 사람밴다 빠르기 때문에 환경 특징을 찘리하는 눘력이 더 낮습니다. (greater -> limited/less)

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 두 개 고르면? [3.2점]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work ⓐ<u>is</u> to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers ⓑ<u>find</u> their days much more energyizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, have conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally ⓒ<u>to earn</u> higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also ⓓ<u>much</u> more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work ⓔ<u>was</u> 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: ⓒ not only produce ... but also generally (동사 병갬 구문)이므로, produce와 병갬을 이루는 earn이 와야 합니다.ⓔ that절 내의 주어가 Those(who took ... work)로 복수이므로, was림 were로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 두 개 고르면?
questions.passage: A number of research studies ⓐ<u>have</u> shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones ⓑ<u>were</u> remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect ⓒ<u>referring</u> to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken ⓓ<u>herself</u> to acquire that skill in an earlier session. ⓔ<u>Knowing</u> that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: ⓒ 'an effect'를 수식하는 분사구로, 지식의 저주라고 '불리는' 효과이므로 수동의 의미인 'referred'가 적절하다. ⓓ 문맥상 실험 참가자들이 '자신들'이 그 기술을 습득하는 데 걸린 시간을 과소평가한 것이므로 주어인 'participants'에 맞춰 재귀대명사 'themselves'가 되어야 한다.

questions.question: 16. 윗글의 (A)~(E) 중 문맥상 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally ─ they are functionally blind. (B) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. (C) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (D) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. (E) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without ___________________________.
questions.insertion_sentence: But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition.
questions.explanation: (D)에서 지각적 이탈을 수면의 정의에 포함하지 않는다는 의견이 나왔고, 주어진 문장은 지각적 이탈 없이는 수면이 불가능하므로 그것이 정의에 필수적이라는 반론을 제기합니다. 이후 (E)에서 그럼에도 불구하고(Nevertheless) 졸음이라는 중간 상태를 이용한다는 흐름으로 이어지는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally ─ they are functionally blind. (B) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. (C) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (D) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. (E) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without ___________________________.
options: ① immediate response to external stimuli
② total absence of sensory engagement
③ being socially isolated and lonely
④ connection to the outside world
questions.explanation: 졸음(drowsiness)은 완전한 감각적 차단 없이 수면의 이점을 얻을 수 있는 상태임을 설명하고 있으므로 '감각적 관여의 완전한 부재(total absence of sensory engagement)' 없이도 이점을 얻는다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 외부 자극에 대한 즉각적인 반응
감각적 관여의 완전한 부재
사회적으로 고립되고 외로움
외부 세계와의 연결
에너지와 건강을 회복함

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것을 두 개 고르면?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 ㎞) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① 전령들은 왕의 길에 배치되었으며, 집단을 이루어 많게는 여덟 명까지 오두막에서 생활했다.
② 전령은 모두 남자였고 그중 지혜 많은 노인이 섞여 있었다.
③ Inca 사람들은 적의 눈에 띄지 않게 낮은 지대에 오두막을 지었다.
④ 전령은 자신을 만나러 달려 나오고 있는 전령에게 메시지를 서너 번 반복하여 외쳤다.
⑤ Inca 제국은 사정이 좋으면 사나흘 만에 1,000마일 정도 메시지를 이어 갈 수 있었다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 Chasquis라고 불리는 전령들은 4명에서 6명씩 그룹을 지어 살았다고 했으므로 ①은 틀렸습니다. 전령들은 모두 젊은이였다고 했으므로 노인이 섞여 있었다는 ②는 틀렸습니다. 오두막은 서로 잘 보이도록 높은 지대(high ground)에 지었다고 했으므로 ③은 틀렸습니다. 전령은 다음 오두막에 가까워지면 달려 나오는 다음 전령에게 메시지를 3~4번 반복했다고 했으므로 ④는 일치합니다. 좋은 조건 하에서 3~4일 만에 1,000마일을 전달할 수 있었다고 했으므로 ⑤도 일치합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① To gain confidence, turn difficulties into positive statements.
② Don't avoid the challenges you face in real life and endure them.
③ To solve a difficult problem, ask for help from the people around you.
④ If you want to achieve your goal, put your thoughts into action immediately.
⑤ Learn magic from time to time to improve your confidence in your daily life.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 일상에서 겪는 도전이나 어려움들을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸어 적어봄으로써 생각과 행동의 변화를 겪고 자신감을 얻을 수 있다는 내용을 전달하고 있습니다. 따라서 필자의 주장은 ① '자신감을 얻기 위해 어려움을 긍정적인 진술로 바꿔라'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자신감을 얻기 위해 어려움을 긍정적인 진술로 바꿔라.
② 실생활에서 직면하는 어려움을 피하지 말고 견뎌라.
③ 어려운 문제를 해결하기 위해 주변 사람들에게 도움을 요청하라.
④ 목표를 달성하고 싶다면 즉시 생각을 행동으로 옮겨라.
⑤ 일상 생활에서 자신감을 높이기 위해 때때로 마술을 배워라.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 우리말과 <보기>의 문장이 의미가 같도록 알맞게 배열한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." <u>화가들은 종종 언제 그림 그리는 것을 멈춰야 할지 알기 어렵다는 것을 깨닫는다</u>, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. (이후 생략)
options: ① find it difficult to know when to stop to paint
② find difficult to know when to stop painting it
③ find it difficult to know when to stop painting
④ find when to stop painting it difficult to know
⑤ find to know when to stop to paint it difficult
questions.explanation: '~하는 것이 어렵다는 것을 깨닫는다'는 가목적어 it을 사용하는 'find it + 형용사(difficult) + 진목적어(to-부정사)' 구문을 사용해야 한다. 또한 '그림 그리는 것을 멈추다'는 stop + 동명사(~하는 것을 멈추다)를 사용하여 stop painting으로 표현하는 것이 적절하다. 따라서 "find it difficult to know when to stop painting"이 정답이다.
options_translation: ① 화가들은 종종 그림 그리기 위해 언제 멈춰야 할지 아는 것이 어렵다는 것을 발견한다.
② (문법 오류 - 가목적어 it 누락)
③ 화가들은 종종 언제 그림 그리는 것을 멈춰야 할지 아는 것이 어렵다는 것을 깨닫는다.
④ (문법 오류 - 어순 부적절)
⑤ (문법 오류 - 어순 및 stop 용법 부적절)

questions.question: 25. 주어진 글 사이에 들어갈 글의 순서로 (A)~(E)를 알맞게 배열할 때 세 번째에 위치하는 것은? [24년 3월 21번]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
ordered_passages: (A) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses.
(B) For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.
(C) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it.
(D) Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.
(E) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각을 5가지로 분류했다는 내용입니다. 이에 대해 (C)에서 의구심을 제기하며, (B)에서 인간에게서 놓친 감각들(자기 수용 감각, 균형 감각)을 구체적으로 언급합니다. 그 다음 (E)에서 인간 외의 '다른 동물들'로 화제를 전환하여 분류하기 더 힘든 감각이 있음을 시사하고, (D)에서 그 구체적 예시(뱀의 열 감지 등)를 듭니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이 모든 예시들을 종합하며 감각은 특정 수로 명확히 나뉠 수 없다는 결론을 내립니다. 따라서 전체 순서는 (C)-(B)-(E)-(D)-(A)이며, 세 번째에 위치하는 것은 (E)입니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will _____________.
options: ① go back to their original order
② be replaced with completely new ones
③ remain the same as in the previous year
④ be twice as much quantity than usual
⑤ grow at the same speed
questions.explanation: 윤작(Crop rotation)의 원리에 대한 설명입니다. 3개의 밭에서 3가지 작물을 순서대로 돌려 짓는 경우, 1년 차, 2년 차, 3년 차를 지나 4년 차가 되면 다시 첫 번째 해의 순서로 돌아오게 됩니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '원래의 순서로 돌아간다'는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 원래의 순서로 돌아갈 것이다
② 완전히 새로운 것으로 대체될 것이다
③ 전년도와 동일하게 유지될 것이다
④ 평소보다 두 배 많은 양이 될 것이다
⑤ 같은 속도로 자랄 것이다

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, map was a the misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not _____________________. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
options: ① divided into specific regions on your tongue
② equally sensitive to all taste stimuli
③ evenly distributed in the mouth
④ visible to the naked human eye
⑤ only located on the tongue
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거의 '혀 지도(tongue map)' 개념이 잘못된 정보였음을 설명하고 있습니다. 혀 지도는 특정 맛이 특정 부위에서만 느껴진다고 주장했으나, 현대 연구에 따르면 맛은 입안 어디에서나 느껴질 수 있습니다. 따라서 미뢰가 '혀의 특정 영역으로 나뉘어 있지 않다'는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 혀의 특정 부위로 나뉘어 있지 않다
② 모든 맛 자극에 똑같이 민감하지 않다
③ 입안에 고르게 분포되어 있지 않다
④ 인간의 맨눈으로 볼 수 있지 않다
⑤ 오직 혀에만 위치해 있지 않다

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. (A)__________, like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. (B)____________, we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ⑤ (A) In fact / (B) On the other hand
questions.explanation: (A) 앞부분에서는 리더십이 숭고하고 거창한 목표인 것처럼 보인다고 했으나, 뒷부분에서는 위대한 리더들도 시작은 우리와 같은 평범한 학생, 시민이었다는 상반된 내용을 서술하므로 역접의 'Yet'이 적절합니다. (B) 앞 문장에서 리더십이 점진적인 노력을 통해 발휘된다는 과정을 설명했고, 그 결론으로 우리 모두 리더가 될 잠재력이 있다는 결과론적 진술을 하므로 인과관계의 'Thus'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 하지만 / (B) 예를 들어
② (A) 하지만 / (B) 따라서
③ (A) 더욱이 / (B) 결과적으로
④ (A) 사실 / (B) 하지만
⑤ (A) 사실 / (B) 반면에

questions.question: 6. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 comfortable rut이 의문하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a <u>comfortable rut</u>. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this <u>comfortable rut</u> that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying - but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
options: ① a job that gives people comfort
② a well-paying, but unsatisfying job
③ a high-income, but not very stable job
④ a job environment that is easy to fit in
⑤ a daily routine that is common among people
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 부분에서 comfortable rut을 'secure, or even well-paying - but ultimately unsatisfying - job'으로 설명하고 있습니다. 즉, 및은 잘 받지만 구국적으로는 만족스럽지 뮻한 직업을 의문합니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들에게 편안함을 주는 일
② 및은 잘 받지만 만족스럽지 뮻한 일
③ 고석득이지만 매우 안정적이지는 않은 일
④ 적응하기 쉬운 업무 환경
⑤  사람들 사이에서 흤한 일상적인 일과

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: If we (A)[adopt / adapt] technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly (B)[harmless / dangerous]. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the (C)[mobile / sedentary] nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk - for body and mind.
questions.explanation: (A) 기술을 '채택(adopt)'할 때 비용을 치러야 한다는 문맥입니다. (B) 앞서 언급된 기술로 인한 부정적인 영향(신체적 고통 등)을 고려할 때, 기술이 '위험한(dangerous)' 일자리를 만든다는 흐름이 적절합니다. (C) 높은 임금을 받는 일자리의 '주로 앉아서 하는(sedentary)' 특성이 건강에 위험 요소가 된다는 내용이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 채택하다 - 무해한 - 이동하는
② 채택하다 - 위험한 - 주로 앉아서 하는
③ 적응하다 - 무해한 - 이동하는
④ 적응하다 - 무해한 - 주로 앉아서 하는
⑤ 적응하다 - 위험한 - 주로 앉아서 하는

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to ⓐ<u>overcome</u> jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and ⓑ<u>lengthen</u> your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is ⓒ<u>sizable</u> enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform ⓓ<u>significantly</u> better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found ⓔ<u>contrary</u> evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
questions.explanation: 앞 문장에서 서쪽으로 비행하는 팀이 동쪽으로 비행하는 팀보다 성적이 훨씬 좋다는 연구 결과를 언급했고, 뒤이어 나오는 46,000개 이상의 경기 분석 연구 또한 동쪽 여행이 서쪽 여행보다 더 힘들다는 결론을 내렸으므로 이는 이전의 발견과 일치하는 '추가적인(further/additional)' 증거입니다. 따라서 '상반되는'이라는 뜻의 ⓔ contrary는 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 그 쓰임이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
questions.passage: (A) If you want the confidence ⓐ<u>that</u> comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. (가)<u>Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list</u>, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks ⓑ<u>that</u> you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time ⓒ<u>that</u> you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.(B) Here are some tips ⓓ<u>that</u> will help you manage your time more effectively. Figure out the amount of time you need for your activities and make a weekly plan. This way, you'll be able to take greater control of your time and perform your responsibilities in a timely fashion. Without planning, you may find yourself easily caught up with more than one task and end up finishing none of them. You see some people keeping a calendar or making a daily to-do list. These are also good ways to organize your schedule in advance. Don't forget ⓔ<u>that</u> for every minute you spend organizing, an hour is earned.
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ는 모두 선행사를 수식하는 관계대명사로 쓰였습니다. (ⓐ: 주격 관계대명사, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ: 목적격 관계대명사) 반면 ⓔ는 'Don't forget'이라는 타동사의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 'that'입니다.

questions.question: 14. 윗글의 (A)의 밑줄 친 (가)와 의미가 가장 비슷한 부분을 (B)에서 찾아 그대로 옮겨 쓰시오.
questions.passage: (A) If you want the confidence ⓐ<u>that</u> comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. (가)<u>Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list</u>, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks ⓑ<u>that</u> you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time ⓒ<u>that</u> you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.(B) Here are some tips ⓓ<u>that</u> will help you manage your time more effectively. Figure out the amount of time you need for your activities and make a weekly plan. This way, you'll be able to take greater control of your time and perform your responsibilities in a timely fashion. questions.answer: Figure out the amount of time you need for your activities
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 (가) 'Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed'는 '해야 할 일 목록에 있는 항목들과 더불어 필요한 시간의 양을 추산하는 습관을 들이라'는 의미입니다. (B) 부분에서 이와 가장 의미가 유사한 부분은 '활동에 필요한 시간의 양을 파악하라'는 의미를 가진 'Figure out the amount of time you need for your activities'입니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 내용을 <보기>에 주어진 표현을 각각 한 번씩 모두 사용하여 문맥에 맞게 영작하시오. (단, 추가되는 단어는 없고, 필요시 단어의 형태를 변형할 것)
questions.passage: Whose story it is affects what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shit if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but _____________________________________ the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
subjective_conditions: 추가되는 단어는 없고, 필요시 단어의 형태를 변형할 것
vocabulary_box: be / events / from / if / show / the same / we / what
questions.answer: what if we were shown the same events from
questions.explanation: '~라면 어떨까?'라는 의미의 'what if' 구문을 사용합니다. 문맥상 수동태가 필요하므로 'be shown'의 형태를 쓰는데, if절 내의 가정을 나타내기 위해 과거형 'were shown'을 사용합니다. 전체 문장은 'what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of...'가 됩니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(G) 중, 어법상 어색한 것 2개를 찾아 그 기호를 적고, 각각 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption (A)<u>which</u> because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students (B)<u>were given</u> descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description (C)<u>contained</u> the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, (D)<u>after which</u> the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, (E)<u>depending</u> upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer (F)<u>to be</u> warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only (G)<u>affect</u> the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
questions.explanation: (A) 'assumption' 뒤의 절이 완전하므로 관계대명사 which 대신 동격의 접속사 that이 와야 합니다. (C) 'description'을 수식하는 분사 자리로, '단어를 포함하고 있는'이라는 능동의 의미이므로 과거분사가 아닌 현재분사 containing이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea.
ordered_passages: (A) Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
(B) The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be.

(C) Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 모든 것은 아이디어에서 시작된다고 언급한 후, (C)에서 그 아이디어가 구체화되고 다듬어지는 과정을 설명합니다. 이어서 (B)에서 인간도 이와 같은 과정으로 미래를 설계한다고 비유를 확장하며, (A)에서 그 과정을 거쳐 최종적으로 실현되는 결과를 설명하는 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글을 읽고 미루어 알 수 있는 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
options: ① 근로 여건이 개선되면서 사람들의 여가 시간이 줄어들었다.
② 운송 형태가 다양화되면서 장소 이동에 드는 비용은 천차만별이었다.
③ Blackpool과 Brighton같은 유명한 리조트들은 호숫가에 위치해있다.
④ 캐나다의 대륙 횡단 철도 시스템은 19세기에 도입되었다.
⑤ 항공 운송의 출현으로 항공 사고로 인한 사상자가 늘어났다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 19세기에 철도가 유명한 해안가 리조트들을 열었다는 언급과 캐나다의 예시가 이어지는데, 이는 산업 혁명 이후의 변화 과정을 설명하고 있으므로 캐나다의 대륙 횡단 철도 시스템 또한 19세기 전후의 상황임을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually _____________. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에서 마케팅 혁명이 일어났고 고객의 요구(needs)를 충족시키는 것이 비즈니스의 초점이 되었다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 기업은 고객들이 '실제로 원하는(wanted)' 제품을 전달하는 것이 필수적이게 되었습니다.
options_translation: ① 원했던
② 무시했던
③ 생산했던
④ 폐기했던
⑤ 불평했던

questions.question: 22. 다음 Magma에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
options: ① 지구 표면 아래에 갇혔을 때도 식는다.
② 식으면서 원자는 화합물로 결합하기 시작한다.
③ 식는 속도에 따라 어떤 광물이 형성될지가 결정된다.
④ 천천히 식으면 형성되는 결정은 육안으로 볼 수 있을 만큼 크다.
⑤ 빠르게 식으면 형성되는 개별 광물 결정을 쉽게 볼 수 없다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 어떤 광물이 형성될지를 결정하는 것은 '마그마에 존재하는 원소의 종류와 양'이며, 식는 속도는 '형성되는 결정의 크기'를 결정하는 요소입니다. 따라서 속도가 광물의 종류를 결정한다는 ③번은 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. ⓐAs they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. ⓑBad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. ⓒWhole grains and vegetables are two healthy carbohydrates foods that are also important nutritional sources of fiber, vitamins, and minerals. ⓓBecause their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. ⓔYour body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 복합 탄수화물(좋은 탄수화물)과 단순 탄수화물(나쁜 탄수화물)의 화학적 분해 과정과 영양적 특성에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ⓒ번 문장은 통곡물과 채소가 건강에 좋은 탄수화물 식품이라는 영양학적 정보를 제공하고 있어, 탄수화물의 구조적 분해 과정을 설명하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started form. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain ________________. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster - in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
questions.explanation: 지문은 생태계에서 포식자와 피식자가 서로 생존을 위해 계속 진화하지만, 상대적인 관계에서는 제자리에 머무는 것처럼 보이는 '붉은 여왕 효과'를 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 생물학적 '진화의 원리'를 설명하는 것이므로 빈칸에는 an evolutionary principle이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 진화의 원리
② 면역 체계
③ 유전적 구조
④ 줄기 세포 이론
⑤ 신체 기능

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew larger. (A) Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. (B) They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. (C) While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. (D) For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. (E) By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
questions.insertion_sentence: Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 마을 거주자들이 업무를 더 빨리 처리하기 위해 '협업(work together)'하는 법을 배웠다는 내용입니다. (D) 뒤의 문장에서 그에 대한 구체적인 예시로 도구 제작자들이 돌도끼와 칼을 만드는 작업을 '분담(share the work)'하는 내용이 나오므로 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글에서 'animal characters에게 투영된 인간의 특징'으로 언급되지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands, and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
options: ① 인간의 언어로 대화할 수 있다.
③ 인간과 같은 얼굴 특징을 가지고 있다.
④ 변형된 앞다리는 사람의 손을 닮아있다.
⑤ 어린이와 비슷하게 몸집이 실제보다 작다.
questions.explanation: 지문 마지막 부분에서 동물의 캐릭터가 아이와 같은 특징(childlike features)을 가지도록 확대되고 변형된다고 언급되어 있으나, 이것이 '몸집이 실제보다 작다'는 의미는 아닙니다. 오히려 '확대된(enlarged)' 특징을 부여한다고 설명하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
options: ① effective time management for achieving daily goals
② challenges of maintaining routines without planning
③ strategies for avoiding mistakes in task completion
④ importance of taking breaks to increase efficiency
⑤ techniques for improving multitasking skills
questions.explanation: 하루 목표를 달성하기 위해 각 업무에 필요한 시간을 정확히 추정하고, 가용 시간에 맞춰 계획을 세우는 등 효과적인 시간 관리의 중요성을 설명하는 글입니다.
options_translation: ① 일일 목표 달성을 위한 효과적인 시간 관리
② 계획 없는 루틴 유지의 어려움
③ 과업 완료 시 실수를 피하기 위한 전략
④ 효율성을 높이기 위한 휴식의 중요성
⑤ 멀티태스킹 능력을 향상시키는 기법

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 putting on the same clothes가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "<u>putting on the same clothes</u>" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they know what to do and also know how to do it.
options: ① knowing what to do and how to do it
② greeting everyone with a positive attitude
③ using the same strategy over and over again
④ conserving resources by not buying new clothes
⑤ approaching similar situations with different strategies
questions.explanation: 글의 앞부분에서 언급된 'rubber-stamp approach(일률적인 접근법)'와 같은 맥락으로, 모든 학습 상황에서 동일한 방식을 고수하는 것을 비유적으로 표현한 것입니다.
options_translation: ① 무엇을 해야 할지 그리고 어떻게 해야 할지 아는 것
② 긍정적인 태도로 모든 사람을 맞이하는 것
③ 똑같은 전략을 반복해서 사용하는 것
④ 새 옷을 사지 않음으로써 자원을 보존하는 것
⑤ 비슷한 상황에 서로 다른 전략으로 접근하는 것

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면? [23년 3월 34번]
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us ⓐ<u>was complete in the mind of its creator before it was started</u>. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, ⓑ<u>refined and perfected before the first nail was driving</u> or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before ⓒ<u>the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind has clearly pictured</u> the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. ⓓ<u>We begin with an idea about how the future will be</u>. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony ⓔ<u>to bring into existence when we have mentally concluded about the future</u>.*refine: 다듬다
questions.explanation: ⓑ: 못이 '박히는' 수동의 의미이므로 driving을 driven으로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓒ: '생각이 물리적 실체가 되기 훨씬 전'이라는 과거의 특정 시점을 나타내는 부사구(Long before ~)와 함께 쓰였으므로, 과거 완료인 had clearly pictured가 적절합니다. ⓔ: bring into existence의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌어야 하므로, '미래에 대해 마음속에서 결론 내린 것'이라는 의미의 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what이 필요합니다. (when -> what)

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 26번]
questions.passage: Lilian Bland was born in Kent, England in 1878. Unlike most other girls at the time she wore trousers and spent her time enjoying (A)[adventurous / passive] activities like horse riding and hunting. Lillian began her career as a sports and wildlife photographer for British newspaper. In 1910 she became the first woman to design, build, and fly her own airplane. In order to (B)[frustrate / persuade] her to try a slightly safer activity, Lilian's dad bought her a car. Soon Lilian was a master driver and ended up working as a car dealer. She never went back to flying but lived a long and (C)[exciting / boring] life nonetheless. She married, moved to Canada, and had a kid. Eventually, she moved back to England, and lived there for the rest of her life.
questions.explanation: (A): 승마나 사냥과 같은 활동은 '모험적인(adventurous)' 활동에 해당합니다.(B): 비행기 조종보다 안전한 활동(운전)을 시도하도록 '설득하기(persuade)' 위해 아버지가 차를 사주었습니다.(C): 최초의 여성 비행기 설계자이자 조종사였고 자동차 딜러로도 활동한 그녀의 삶은 '흥미진진한(exciting)' 삶이었습니다.
options_translation: ① 모험적인 / 좌절시키다 / 지루한
② 모험적인 / 설득하다 / 흥미진진한
③ 모험적인 / 좌절시키다 / 흥미진진한
④ 수동적인 / 설득하다 / 흥미진진한
⑤ 수동적인 / 좌절시키다 / 지루한

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to ⓐ<u>overcome</u> jet lag. And the speed of recovery depends on the ⓑ<u>direction</u> of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an ⓒ<u>impact</u> on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying eastward perform significantly ⓓ<u>better</u> than teams flying westward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is ⓔ<u>tougher</u> than westward travel.*jet lag: 시차로 인한 피로감
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 맥락이 서쪽으로 비행하는 것이 동쪽으로 비행하는 것보다 시차 적응이 쉽다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 동쪽으로 비행하는 팀들이 서쪽으로 비행하는 팀들보다 성적이 '더 나쁘다(worse)'가 되어야 하므로 ⓓ 'better'는 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop ⓐ<u>liking</u> it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so ⓑ<u>deep</u> in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take ⓒ<u>little</u> effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're locked in place. And it's a situation that many working people ⓓ<u>fear</u> they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling ⓔ<u>stuck</u> in what may be a secure, or even well-paying - but ultimately unsatisfying - job.*rut: 틀에 박힌 생활
questions.explanation: 편안하지만 틀에 박힌 생활(rut)이 너무 깊어져서 빠져나오기 힘든 상황을 묘사하고 있습니다. 비유적으로 미끄러운 벽 때문에 밖으로 기어나오는 데 '엄청난(great/much)' 노력이 필요하다는 맥락이 되어야 하므로, '거의 없는'이라는 뜻의 'little'은 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk - for body and mind. If we adopt technology, we ____________________.*chronic: 만성의 **sedentary: 주로 앉아서 하는
options: ① need not pay its costs
② must try to keep tradition
③ should pay the price for it
④ should learn how to use it
⑤ can select a job we really like
questions.explanation: 지문은 기술 발전이 가져온 부정적인 측면들(전통적 생계 수단의 상실, 싫어하는 일, 신체적 고통, 정신적 스트레스 등)을 열거하고 있습니다. 따라서 기술을 도입한다면 그에 따른 '대가를 치러야 한다'는 ③번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그것의 비용을 지불할 필요가 없다
② 전통을 지키려 노력해야 한다
③ 그것에 대한 대가를 치러야 한다
④ 그것을 사용하는 법을 배워야 한다
⑤ 우리가 정말 좋아하는 직업을 선택할 수 있다

questions.question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It is difficult for any of us to maintain a constant level of attention throughout our working day. We all have body rhythms characterised by peaks and valleys of energy and alertness. You will achieve more, and feel confident as a benefit, if you schedule your most demanding tasks _________________\n________________. If you haven't thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to observe yourself. Try to note the times when you are at your best. We are all different. For some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for others it may take a while to warm up.
options: ① during the times when you reach your peat
② at times when you are able to hold them off
③ while your mind and body are relaxed and calm
④ when other people can help you cope with them
⑤ long after bursts of heightened energy have passed
questions.explanation: 사람마다 에너지가 정점(peak)에 도달하는 시간이 다르며, 가장 힘든 업무를 에너지가 가장 높은 시간에 배치하면 더 많은 성과를 내고 자신감을 얻을 수 있다는 내용의 글입니다.
options_translation: 당신이 정점에 도달하는 시간 동안
당신이 그것들을 미룰 수 있는 시간에
당신의 몸과 마음이 편안하고 차분할 때
다른 사람들이 당신이 그것들을 대처하도록 도울 수 있을 때
높아진 에너지의 분출이 지나간 한참 후에

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: On a two-week trip in the Rocky Mountains, I saw a grizzly bear in tis native habitat. At first, I felt joy as I watched the bear walk across the land. ⓐHe stopped every once in a while to turn his head about, sniffing deeply. ⓑHe was following the scent of something, and slwoly I began to realize that this giant animal was smelling me! I froze. ⓒThis was no longer a wonderful experience; it was now an issue of survival. ⓓI didn't know that certain animals use their sense of sight rather than smell to find food. ⓔThe bear's motivation was to find meat to eat, and I was clearly on his menu.
questions.explanation: 필자가 로키산맥에서 곰을 만났을 때 곰이 자신의 냄새를 맡고 다가오는 위태로운 생존의 문제에 직면했다는 내용인데, 일부 동물이 냄새 대신 시각을 사용해 먹이를 찾는다는 내용인 ④번은 전체적인 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. ⓐAt the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. ⓑEngland's Industrial Revolution led to air and water pollution, resulting in environmental destruction. ⓒRailways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside reports such as Blackpool and Brighton. ⓓWith the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-cast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. ⓔLater, the arrival transport opened more of the world and led to tourism growth.
questions.explanation: 경제적 여건의 개선과 교통수단(철도, 항공 등)의 발달로 인해 관광업이 성장하게 된 배경을 설명하는 글입니다. 영국 산업 혁명으로 인한 환경 오염 문제를 다룬 ②번은 글의 주제에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. ⓐThese complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. ⓑAs they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. ⓒBad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars and because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body. ⓓThe problem is that too much consumption of carbohydrates can cause heart disease and other serious illnesses. ⓔYour body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 복합 탄수화물(좋은 탄수화물)과 단순 탄수화물(나쁜 탄수화물)의 구조적 차이와 체내 흡수 과정을 대조하여 설명하고 있습니다. ⓓ는 탄수화물의 과잉 섭취가 유발하는 질병에 대해 언급하고 있는데, 이는 탄수화물의 종류별 특징과 분해 과정을 다루는 글의 핵심 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 25. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside.
ordered_passages: (A) Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster.(B) They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place."(C) In this case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 붉은 여왕이 앨리스를 경주에 데려간 상황이 제시됩니다. (B)에서 경주 상황이 구체적으로 묘사되며 제자리에 머무는 '붉은 여왕 효과'가 처음 소개됩니다. (A)에서 생물학자들이 이 효과를 진화 원리(여우와 토끼의 관계)에 적용하여 설명하기 시작하고, (C)에서 여우 또한 더 빨라져야 생존한다는 결론을 내리며 두 종이 상대적으로는 제자리에 머무는 상황을 정리하므로 (B)-(A)-(C)가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence.
ordered_passages: (A) While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat?
(B) It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to adopt the practices of those around you.

(C) From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. -If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do,- explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 '社会적 짝거'림 찾는다고 한 홄, (C)에서 진화론적 관점에서 집단을 따리는 것이 생존에 유리함을 설명합니다. (A)에서는 이림 현대의 사례(상품 리뷰, 식당 대기 줄)로 연갠하며, (B)에서 그 식당 줄이 가지는 의미와 타인의 행동을 따리는 것의 유익성을 결론 집니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 대러갈 말뢰 가장 재ᄀ잴한 개슨? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Whose story it is affects what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
questions.summary_sentence: The (A)_____________ of a story depends on the (B)_____________ choices of whose viewpoint he selects to look at the events.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이야기의 서술 관점이 달뎼지면 그 이야기에 대한 'ED54석(interpretation)'이 달뎼진다는 내용입니다. 퀀테스트에서 이러한 관점을 선택하는 주체는 작가이므로, (A)에는 interpretation, (B)에는 writer's가 적절합니다. (*본문의 ①과 ⑤가 동일하게 제시되어 있으며, 정답지에는 ①로 표기되어 있으나 내용상 될 다 맞습니다.)
options_translation: ① (A) 해석 (B) 작가의
② (A) 인기 (B) 작가의
③ (A) 해석 (B) 등장인물의
④ (A) 인기 (B) 독자의
⑤ (A) 해석 (B) 작가의

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in an more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands, and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.summary_sentence: Animal characters are made to have humanlike characteristics in order to look attractive. For instance, some animal characters in animations ________________________________________.
options: ② communicate with their own languages
③ behave in a different way from humans
④ are rarely used as a strategy for advertisements
⑤ are modified to have features of human children
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에서 동물 츐릭터림 감정적으로 매력적으로 만들기 위해 '확대되고 변형된 아이 같은 특징(enlarged and deformed childlike features)'을 부여한다고 하였습니다. 따라서 요약문의 예시로는 인간 아이의 특징을 갖덄록 수정된다는 ⑤가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자연스러운 특성을 부여받는다
② 그들자신만의 언어로 소통한다
③ 인간과는 다른 방식으로 행동한다
④ 광고 전략으로 거의 사용되준 않는다
⑤ 인간 아이의 특징을 가지덄록 수정된다

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 30번]
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
questions.summary_sentence: During the mid-20th century, business (A)__________ its focus from simply making products to meeting the (B)__________ needs of customers, sparking a marketing revolution.
questions.explanation: 1940년대와 50년대 산업 사회가 변화하면서 비즈니스의 초점이 단순히 제품 생산에서 고객이 실제로 원하는 다양한 요구를 충족시키는 것으로 바뀌었다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 변화했다(changed), (B)에는 다양한(various)이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 변화시켰다 - 다양한
② 줄였다 - 흥미로운
③ 지속했다 - 다른
④ 나누었다 - 즉각적인
⑤ 개혁했다 - 비자연적인

questions.question: 30. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 3월 37번]
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if its' trapped below the surface. (A) As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. (B) During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. (가)<u>마그마에 존재하는 원소의 종류와 양이 어떤 광물이 형성될지를 부분적으로 결정한다</u>. (C) Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. (D) When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이것은 원자들이 함께 이동하여 더 큰 결정을 형성할 충분한 시간을 갖기 때문이다'라는 이유를 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 앞 문장에서 언급된 '마그마가 천천히 식을 때 형성되는 결정은 일반적으로 육안으로 볼 수 있을 만큼 크다'는 현상에 대한 이유이므로 (D)의 위치가 가장 적절합니다. (D) 다음 문장부터는 마그마가 빠르게 식을 때의 상황으로 내용이 전환됩니다.

questions.question: 31. 윗글의 (가)에 주어진 우리말과 의미가 같도록 <보기>의 단어를 활용하여 <조건>에 맞게 배열하시오.
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if its' trapped below the surface. (A) As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. (B) During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. (가)<u>마그마에 존재하는 원소의 종류와 양이 어떤 광물이 형성될지를 부분적으로 결정한다</u>. (C) Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. (D) When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals. (E)*compound: 화합물
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 주어진 단어들만 모두 사용할 것
주어진 단어 이외의 단어를 추가하지 말 것
주어진 단어의 형태를 바꾸지 말 것
questions.answer: of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form
questions.explanation: '마그마에 존재하는(present in a magma) 원소의 종류와 양(The type and amount of elements)'이 주어이며, '어떤 광물이 형성될지를(which minerals will form)'이 목적어 역할을 하는 절로 구성됩니다.

questions.question: 32. 다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 부분이 있는 것 두 개를 찾고, 기호와 수정된 전체를 쓰시오.
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have ⓐ<u>other characteristics which go with it</u>. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received ⓑ<u>a description containing the word 'warm'</u>, the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, ⓒ<u>after it the students were asked</u> to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, ⓓ<u>depending upon their original information</u> of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm ⓔ<u>tending to interact</u> with him more. This shows that different expectations affect the impressions we form, our behavior, and the relationship which is formed.
subjective_conditions: 예) ⓐThis is an apples.이 어색할 경우
답안 작성: ⓐThis is an apple → (O)
ⓐ → (X), ⓐapple → (X)
questions.answer: (1) ⓒafter which the students were asked (2) ⓔtended to interact
questions.explanation: ⓒ는 앞 문장과 뒷 문장을 연결하는 접속사 역할을 해야 하므로 대명사 it 대신 관계대명사 which를 써서 'after which'가 되어야 합니다. ⓔ는 문장의 본동사 자리이므로 준동사인 tending 대신 시제에 맞는 과거형 동사 tended를 써야 합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: To whom it may concern, I am a resident of the Blue Sky Apartment. Recently I observed that the kid zone is in need of repairs. I want you ⓐ<u>to pay</u> attention to the poor condition of the playground equipment in the zone. The swings are ⓑ<u>damaged</u>, the paint is falling off, and some of the bolts on the slide ⓒ<u>are</u> missing. The facilities ⓓ<u>have been</u> in this terrible condition since we moved here. They are dangerous to the children playing there. Would you please have them ⓔ<u>repair</u>? I would appreciate your immediate attention to solve this matter.Yours sincerely,Nina Davis
questions.explanation: 사역동사 have의 목적어인 them(시설물들)은 수리되는 대상이므로 수동의 관계입니다. 따라서 동사원형 repair 대신 과거분사인 repaired를 써야 합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. In the end, more often than not, __________________________________.
options: ① it's good to follow the actions on all sides of you
② it's good to track the reviews of local restaurant
③ it's not good to chase the opinion of your society
④ it's good to deny the practices of those around you
⑤ it's not good to follow the social evidence around you
questions.explanation: 이 글은 타인의 행동이나 집단의 선택이 안전과 신뢰의 신호(사회적 증거)가 된다는 점을 진화론적 관점과 식당의 줄 서는 사례를 통해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 결론은 주변 사람들의 행동을 따르는 것이 유익하다는 내용이 되어야 하므로 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신 주변 모든 쪽의 행동들을 따르는 것이 좋다
② 지역 식당의 리뷰를 추적하는 것이 좋다
③ 당신 사회의 의견을 쫓는 것은 좋지 않다
④ 당신 주변 사람들의 관행을 거부하는 것이 좋다
⑤ 당신 주변의 사회적 증거를 따르는 것은 좋지 않다

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, (A)[producing / produced] things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work and (B)[to seek / seeking] jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs (C)[is / are] a health risk ─ for body and mind.
questions.explanation: (A) 'humans'가 주체로서 물건을 만드는 능동의 관계이므로 현재분사인 producing이 적절합니다. (B) 'train humans'의 목적격 보어인 to avoid와 and로 연결되어 병렬 구조를 이루므로 to seek가 적절합니다. (C) 주어 'the sedentary nature'가 단수이므로 단수 동사 is가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. ⓐGenerally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. ⓑThis east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. ⓒStudies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. ⓓThis is the reason why athletes born in the western hemisphere definitely perform better than the eastern hemisphere. ⓔA more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 여행 방향(동쪽 혹은 서쪽)에 따른 시차 적응의 차이와 그것이 스포츠 팀의 경기력에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 서쪽으로 비행하는 것이 시차 적응에 더 유리하여 경기력이 좋다는 연구 결과를 뒷받침하고 있는데, ⓓ는 서반구에서 태어난 선수가 무조건 동반구 태생보다 잘한다는 내용으로 글의 핵심인 '비행 방향에 따른 시차 적응'과 관련이 없습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. ⓐIf you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air. ⓑAlso, the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're stuck. ⓒAnd it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. ⓓIn this situation, employees are more united through unions. ⓔThe poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying ─ but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성공이 도리어 사람을 편안하지만 즐겁지 않은 매너리즘(rut)에 빠지게 하여 벗어나기 힘들게 만든다는 내용입니다. ⓓ는 이러한 상황에서 직원들이 노동조합을 통해 단결한다는 내용으로, 개인의 직업적 만족도와 매너리즘에 대한 글의 흐름과는 무관합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.summary_sentence: Though describing animal characters in a more natural way is a trend, it is still general to (A)___________ them with childlike features to make them more (B)___________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 동물 캐릭터를 인간처럼 묘사하거나 어린아이 같은 특징을 부여하여 정서적 호소력을 높이는 전략에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 동물 캐릭터를 변형하거나 바꾸는 것을 의미하므로 transform이 적절하며, (B)는 그러한 변형의 목적인 '정서적으로 매력적이게(appealing)' 만드는 것이므로 attractive가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 무시하다 / 확신에 찬
② 미루다 / 인위적인
③ 확인하다 / 야심 있는
④ 혼동하다 / 긍정적인
⑤ 변형시키다 / 매력적인

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form ____________________________________. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. On the contrary, when magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
options: ① are hardly visible to the unaided eye
② include various minerals which are good for humans
③ are so large that you can see them with the naked eye
④ move closer enough to combine into compounds which make unique patterns
⑤ change their arrangement to the extent of being different from the original ones
questions.explanation: 지문에서 마그마가 천천히 식을 때 원자들이 결합하여 더 큰 결정을 형성할 충분한 시간을 갖는다고 언급하고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒷부분에서 '원자들이 함께 이동하여 더 큰 결정을 형성할 충분한 시간을 갖기 때문이다'라는 근거가 제시되므로, 육안으로 볼 수 있을 만큼 결정이 크다는 ③번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: 육안으로 거의 보이지 않는다
인간에게 유익한 다양한 미네랄을 포함한다
육안으로 볼 수 있을 만큼 아주 크다
독특한 패턴을 만드는 화합물로 결합하기에 충분히 가깝게 이동한다
원래의 것과 다를 정도로 배열을 바꾼다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It is difficult for any of us to maintain a constant level of attention throughout our working day. We all have body rhythms ________________________________. You will achieve more, and feel confident as a benefit, if you schedule your most demanding tasks at times when you are best able to cope with them. If you haven't thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to observe yourself. Try to note the times when you are at your best. We are all different. For some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for others it may take a while to warm up.
options: ① identified by highs and lows of vitality
② identified by peaks and valleys of luck
③ characterised by highs and lows of benefit
④ characterised by peaks and valleys of emotion
⑤ characterised by maxs and mins of demanding task
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람마다 에너지가 넘치는 정점(energy peaks)의 시간이 다르며, 이에 맞춰 가장 힘든 작업을 계획해야 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 신체 리듬은 활력의 고조와 저조에 의해 식별된다는 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: 활력의 고조와 저조에 의해 식별되는
운의 정점과 골짜기에 의해 식별되는
이익의 고조와 저조에 의해 특징지어지는
감정의 정점과 골짜기에 의해 특징지어지는
힘든 업무의 최대치와 최소치에 의해 특징지어지는

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 3월 26번]
questions.passage: Lilian Bland was born in Kent, England in 1878. Unlike most other girls at the time she wore trousers and spent her time enjoying adventurous activities like horse riding and hunting. (A) Lilian began her career as a sports and wildlife photographer for British newspapers. In 1910 she became the first woman to design, build, and fly her own airplane. (B) Soon Lilian was a master driver and ended up working as a car dealer. (C) She never went back to flying but lived a long and exciting life nonetheless. (D) She married, moved to Canada, and had a kid. (E) Eventually, she moved back to England, and lived there for the rest of her life.
questions.insertion_sentence: In order to persuade her to try a slightly safer activity, Lilian's dad bought her a car.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 릴리안의 아버지가 그녀를 비행(위험한 활동) 대신 더 안전한 활동을 하도록 설득하기 위해 차를 사주었다는 내용입니다. 이 문장 뒤에는 그녀가 차와 관련된 일을 하게 되었다는 내용이 이어져야 자연스럽습니다. (B) 뒤의 문장에서 릴리안이 숙련된 운전자가 되었고 자동차 딜러로 일하게 되었다는 내용이 나오므로, 주어진 문장은 (B) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 3월 36번]
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. (A) Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. (B) As a result, towns and villages grew larger. Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. (C) They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. (D) While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. (E) For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
questions.insertion_sentence: Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 마을 거주자들이 일을 더 빨리 하기 위해 협력하는 법을 배웠다는 내용입니다. (E) 뒤의 문장에서 그 예시로 도구 제작자들이 돌도끼와 칼을 만드는 일을 분담(share the work)하여 같은 시간에 더 많은 도구를 만들 수 있었다는 내용이 나오므로, 주어진 문장은 (E) 위치에 들어가는 것이 흐름상 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓖ 문장 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고른 것은? [23년 3월 35번]
questions.passage: ⓐWhose story it is affected what the story is. ⓑChange the main character, and the focus of the story must also alter. ⓒIf we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them differently. ⓓWe'll place our sympathies with someone new. ⓔWhen the conflict arises what is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. ⓕConsider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if it described from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. ⓖGone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were told the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'Whose story it is'는 문장의 주어 역할을 하는 의주동 어순의 간접의문문 명사절입니다. 문장의 본동사가 필요하므로 'affected'는 현재 시제 'affects'로 쓰여야 전체적인 글의 시제(현재)와 일치하며 문맥상 더 자연스럽습니다. (다만, 과거의 사실을 언급하는 경우 affect가 가능할 수 있으나 이 지문은 일반적 사실을 다루므로 현재형이 적절합니다.)ⓔ 'what is the heart of the story'는 'the conflict'를 수식하는 관계절입니다. 선행사가 사물이며 관계대명사 절 내부의 주어 역할을 해야 하므로 'what'이 아니라 'that'이나 'which'가 되어야 합니다. ⓕ 신데렐라 이야기가 악한 의붓자매의 관점에서 '묘사된다면'이라는 수동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 'if it were described' 또는 'if described'(it were 생략) 형태로 수동태가 되어야 합니다. 'it described'는 능동태이므로 어색합니다. 따라서 ⓐ, ⓔ, ⓕ가 포함된 ③번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved.
ordered_passages: (A) In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.(B) Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels.(C) Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 국가의 사회 경제적 상황 개선과 임금/근로 조건 향상을 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 사람들이 더 많은 휴가를 갖게 되고 교통 수단이 발달하며 산업 혁명이 이러한 변화를 이끌었음을 설명합니다. 그 후 (B)에서 영국의 사례로 철도가 유명 해변 리조트를 열었음을 말하고, (A)에서 추가 예시로 캐나다의 철도와 항공 운송의 발달이 관광 성장을 이끌었음을 서술하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started.
ordered_passages: (A) Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be.(B) The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut.(C) Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 모든 것은 시작되기 전 창조자의 마음속에서 완성된다고 말합니다. (B)에서 우리 주변의 구체적인 예시들(집, 자동차, 옷)도 아이디어에서 시작되었음을 설명합니다. (A)에서 이러한 아이디어가 현실이 되기 전 마음속에서 그려진다는 점을 일반화하여 인간의 미래 설계 과정에 적용합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 우리가 그 비전을 다듬고 완성하며 결국 현실로 만들어낸다는 흐름으로 이어집니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very ⓐ<u>difficult</u> to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they ⓑ<u>slowly</u> break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are ⓒ<u>simple</u> sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold ⓓ<u>lots of</u> nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather ⓔ<u>quickly</u> and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
questions.explanation: 나쁜 탄수화물(단순 당)은 구조가 단순하여 분해되기 쉽지만, 당분 이외에 몸에 필요한 다른 영양소는 '거의 포함하고 있지 않다'는 내용이 와야 합니다. 따라서 'lots of(많은)'는 'few(거의 없는)'와 같은 표현으로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 33번]
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers (A)[which / that] they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes (B)[evolve / will evolve] to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster ─ in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits (C)[thrive / to thrive] and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
options: ③ (A) that - (B) will evolve - (C) to thrive
questions.explanation: (A) 동사 discovers의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 'that'이 적절합니다. 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오기 때문입니다.(B) 조건의 부사절 'If foxes...'에서 미래의 의미라 할지라도 현재 시제 'evolve'를 사용하는 것이 규칙입니다.(C) 'catch enough rabbits'를 수식하여 '번성하기에 충분한 토끼를 잡다'라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 형용사적 용법 또는 목적을 나타내는 to부정사 'to thrive'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① which - evolve - thrive
② which - evolve - to thrive
③ that - will evolve - to thrive
④ that - will evolve - thrive
⑤ that - evolve - to thrive

questions.question: 28. 다음 글을 읽고, 아래 요약문에 들어갈 내용을 주어진 글에서 찾아 영어로 쓰시오. [23년 3월 30번]
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. The desire to meet customers' diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
questions.summary_sentence: The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that viewed it was (A)________ ________ ________ ________ ________ ________ ________ and satisfied (B)________ ________ ________ ________ ________ ________.
subjective_conditions: • 본문에서 찾아 그대로 쓸 것
• (A)는 7단어, (B)는 6단어로만 쓸 것
questions.answer: (A) not enough to produce a quality product(B) customers' diverse and often complex needs
questions.explanation: 본문에서 사회의 현대화가 마케팅 혁명으로 이어졌으며, 단순히 양질의 제품을 생산하는 것(not enough to produce a quality product)만으로는 부족하고 고객의 다양하고 복잡한 요구(customers' diverse and often complex needs)를 충족시켜야 한다는 내용을 찾아 작성합니다. (A)는 it was 뒤에 보어로 쓰이는 형용사구(7단어)이며, (B)는 satisfied의 목적어(6단어)입니다.

questions.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)를 채우시오. [5.0점]
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. The desire to meet customers' diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
questions.summary_sentence: The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that viewed it was (A)________ ________ ________ ________ ________ ________ ________ and satisfied (B)________ ________ ________ ________ ________ ________.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 그대로 쓸 것
(A)는 7단어, (B)는 6단어로만 쓸 것
questions.answer: (A) essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted(B) customers' diverse and often complex needs
questions.explanation: 본문의 중반부 'it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted'와 마지막 문장의 'customers' diverse and often complex needs'를 활용하여 요약문을 완성할 수 있습니다. (A)에는 고객이 정말로 원하는 제품을 전달하는 것이 필수적이라는 내용이, (B)에는 고객의 다양하고 복잡한 요구를 충족시킨다는 내용이 들어갑니다.

questions.question: 31. 다음 글을 읽고, ⓐ~ⓖ 중 어법상 어색한 것 2개를 골라, 밑줄 친 부분을 올바르게 다시 쓰시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day</u>, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. ⓑ<u>Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem</u>. So work on it. ⓒ<u>Make a practice of estimated the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience</u> when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. ⓓ<u>Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time</u>. ⓔ<u>There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significantly amount of time available</u>. ⓕ<u>There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available</u>. So ⓖ<u>schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between</u>.
subjective_conditions: 어색한 문장의 기호를 쓰고, 수정 부분을 포함한 밑줄 부분 전체를 쓸 것
questions.answer: (1) 문장기호: ⓒ   수정된 문장: Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience.(2) 문장기호: ⓔ   수정된 문장: There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available.
questions.explanation: ⓒ: 전치사 of 뒤에는 명사나 동명사가 와야 하므로 estimated를 동명사 estimating으로 고쳐야 합니다.ⓔ: 명사구 amount of time을 수식해야 하므로 부사인 significantly를 형용사인 significant로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 32. 다음 안내문을 읽고, 아래 <Tom's diary>의 내용 중 안내문과 일치하지 않는 부분을 찾아 올바르게 다시 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Call for Articles Do you want to get your stories published? New Dream Magazine is looking for future writers! This event is open to anyone aged 13 to 18.ArticlesㆍLength of writing: 300-325 wordsㆍ Articles should also include high-quality color       photos.RewardsㆍFive cents per word   ㆍFive dollars per photoNotesㆍYou should send us your phone number together with your writing.ㆍPlease email your writing to us at article@ndmag.com.<Tom's diary> I achieved my dream of becoming a writer. Last month, my article, which was applied for New Dream Magazine, was adopted and published. I wrote 320 words of writing and attached three pictures about volunteer activities. I sent the completed article to the magazine by post. Finally, I was able to receive the magazine containing my article today. I received $35 for writer's fee. Today is the happiest day of my life.
subjective_conditions: 안내문의 내용과 일치하게 <Tom's diary>의 내용을 수정할 것
일치하지 않는 부분을 수정하고 수정 부분을 포함한 문장 전체를 쓸 것
questions.answer: (1) I sent the completed article to the magazine by email.(2) I received $31 for writer's fee.
questions.explanation: (1) 안내문에서 'Please email your writing to us'라고 명시되어 있으므로 'by post(우편)'를 'by email'로 수정해야 합니다.(2) 고료 계산: 단어당 5센트(320자 x 0.05 = $16) + 사진 한 장당 5달러(3장 x $5 = $15). 총합은 $16 + $15 = $31입니다. 따라서 $35를 $31로 수정해야 합니다.
