questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you __________ with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
questions.explanation: 아침에 일찍 일어나는 것이 '어렵거나 고군분투한다면' 이를 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸어 보라는 예시입니다. 'struggle with'(~로 고생하다, 애쓰다)가 가장 적절합니다. 나머지는 모두 '굴복하다', '수긍하다'라는 뜻입니다.
options_translation: ① 굴복하다
② 항복하다
③ 고군분투하다
④ 누그러지다
⑤ 투항하다

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "_________________________," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
options: ① senses cannot be explicitly separated into a limited number of specific types
② senses of human being are surprisingly sensitive and unclassifiable ones
③ senses of human being are a spectacular illusion and tempting ones
④ we have a lot of reasons to doubt the differences between humans and animals
⑤ senses between humans and animals are classified in the same way
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 5가지 감각 외에도 인간에게는 신체 지각이나 균형 감각이 있으며, 동물들에게는 더 분류하기 어려운 다양한 감각 체계가 존재한다는 사례들을 통해, 감각은 제한된 수의 특정 유형으로 명확히 구분될 수 없음을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 감각은 제한된 수의 특정한 유형으로 명확하게 분리될 수 없다
② 인간의 감각은 놀라울 정도로 예민하며 분류할 수 없는 것이다
③ 인간의 감각은 화려한 환상이며 유혹적인 것이다
④ 인간과 동물 사이의 차이점을 의심할 만한 많은 이유가 있다
⑤ 인간과 동물 사이의 감각은 같은 방식으로 분류된다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ① A good leader lives a life of sacrifice for a noble goal.
② A great man exerts great determination in times of crisis.
③ Anyone who develops ideas for a community can be a leader.
④ Attitude to listen to others' opinions is most important to achieving goals.
⑤ Hardworking and experienced people can be economically successful.
questions.explanation: 유명한 지도자들도 시작은 평범한 시민이었으며, 공동체의 삶을 개선하려는 아이디어를 발전시키고 공유함으로써 지도자가 되었다는 내용을 통해, 누구나 공동체를 위한 아이디어를 발전시키면 지도자가 될 수 있다는 요지를 도출할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 좋은 지도자는 숭고한 목표를 위해 희생하는 삶을 산다.
② 위대한 사람은 위기의 순간에 큰 결단력을 발휘한다.
③ 공동체를 위해 아이디어를 발전시키는 누구든 지도자가 될 수 있다.
④ 타인의 의견을 경청하는 태도는 목표 달성에 가장 중요하다.
⑤ 근면하고 경험 많은 사람들은 경제적으로 성공할 수 있다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. (A) In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. (B) Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. (C) The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. (D) Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '반면에 보행자 여행은 훨씬 느려서 환경적 세부 사항을 감상할 수 있게 해준다'는 내용입니다. (C) 문장에서 자동차 운전자의 제한된 세부 사항 처리 능력을 언급한 뒤, 보행자의 장점을 대조적으로 보여주는 주어진 문장이 오고, 그 뒤 (D)에서 '이러한 양극단의 사이(between these polar opposites)'라는 표현이 운전자와 보행자를 모두 가리키게 되므로 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. _______________ can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.explanation: 빈칸 뒤의 예시에서 구조 센터에 있는 고양이와 일반 가정 환경에 있는 고양이가 서로 다르게 반응한다는 점을 언급하고 있으므로, 동물의 반응을 결정하는 요소는 '환경적 요인(Environmental factors)'임을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 환경적 요인들
② 학습의 결과들
③ 치유 시스템들
④ 신체적 특징들
⑤ 질병의 종류들

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. ⓐExperts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. ⓑDr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. ⓒHigh achievers who fully understand the difficulty of the skills tend to underestimate their skills because they understand that there is always more to learn. ⓓHer participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. ⓔKnowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 전체 글의 흐름은 전문가가 초보자에게 무언가를 가르칠 때 자신이 처음 배울 때의 어려움을 잊어버리는 '지식의 저주' 현상에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓒ번 문장은 높은 성취를 이룬 사람들이 배울 것이 더 많다는 것을 알기 때문에 자신의 기술을 과소평가한다는 내용으로, 글의 주제인 '타인이 배우는 데 느끼는 난이도를 과소평가함'과는 거리가 먼 내용입니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 단어의 올바른 형태를 쓰시오. [24년 3월 41-42번]
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just ⓐ<u>drop</u> something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is ⓑ<u>mark</u>. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both ⓒ<u>surprise</u> and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that ⓓ<u>appear</u> translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused ⓔ<u>be</u> considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as ⓕ<u>hold</u> a door open for you.
questions.answer: ⓐ dropped, ⓑ marked, ⓒ surprising, ⓓ appears, ⓔ is, ⓕ holding
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'have just' 뒤에 오는 현재완료 시제이므로 과거분사 dropped가 적절합니다. ⓑ 'it is marked' (그것은 눈에 띈다)의 수동태 형태가 필요하므로 과거분사 marked가 적절합니다. ⓒ 주어 'Failing to say it'이 놀라움을 주는 주체이므로 현재분사 surprising이 적절합니다. ⓓ 선행사 'an expression'이 단수이므로 단수 동사 appears가 적절합니다. ⓔ 절의 주어인 'the cost'가 단수이므로 be동사의 단수형 is가 적절합니다. ⓕ 전치사 'as' 뒤에 오는 동명사 형태인 holding이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 (A), (B)의 의미에 맞게 영작하시오. (단, 반드시 관계대명사를 사용할 것) [24년 3월 40번]
questions.passage: The mind has parts (A)<u></u>. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one (B)<u></u>. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
subjective_conditions: 반드시 관계대명사를 사용할 것
questions.answer: (A) that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind(B) that you have more control over
questions.explanation: (A) '의식적 마음과 잠재의식적 마음이라고 알려진' 부분을 영작하기 위해 주격 관계대명사 'that'과 수동태 'are known as'를 사용합니다. (B) '여러분이 더 많은 통제력을 가지고 있는' 부분을 영작하기 위해 목적격 관계대명사 'that'을 사용하며, 'control over'의 목적어가 생략된 구조로 작성합니다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ를 문맥과 어법에 맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just ⓐ<u>drop</u> something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is ⓑ<u>mark</u>. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both ⓒ<u>surprise</u> and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that ⓓ<u>appear</u> translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused ⓔ<u>be</u> considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as ⓕ<u>hold</u> a door open for you.
questions.answer: ⓐ dropped, ⓑ marked, ⓒ surprising, ⓓ appears, ⓔ is, ⓕ holding
questions.explanation: ⓐ는 현재완료 시제(have+p.p.)의 구조이므로 dropped가 적절합니다. ⓑ는 '두드러진, 눈에 띄는'의 의미로 수동의 의미를 지닌 형용사 marked가 필요합니다. ⓒ는 'Failing to say it'이라는 상황(사물)이 주어이므로 능동의 감정을 유발하는 surprising이 적절합니다. ⓓ는 주격 관계대명사절의 동사로 선행사 an expression에 맞춘 단수형 appears가 필요합니다. ⓔ는 주어 the cost에 맞춘 단수 동사 is가 적절합니다. ⓕ는 전치사 as 뒤에 오는 동명사구 자리이므로 holding이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 문장에 있는 문법적인 오류 세 곳을 찾아 바르게 고치고 그 이유를 설명하시오.
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.answer: (1) knowing → to know / 수정이유: 해당 문장은 가목적어(it), 진목적어의 구조이므로 to 부정사구를 사용해 주어야 한다.(2) overwork → overworked / 수정이유: 2형식의 구조를 갖는 감각동사 look에서 비롯된 준동사(looking)가 사용되었으므로 해당 위치에는 형용사 보어를 사용해 주어야 한다.(3) that → whether/if / 수정이유: 해당 문장의 문맥적 상황은 그림그리기를 끝낼지를 결정하기 위해 휴식을 취한 다음 다시 검토하는 상황에서 자신의 그림이 추가적인 꾸밈으로부터 '득이 되는지 안 되는지'의 의미로 사용되는 것이 더 타당하다.
questions.explanation: 1. 'find it difficult to know' 구문에서 it은 가목적어이며 뒤의 명사구(to know)가 진목적어입니다. 2. 'look overworked'에서 look은 상태 유지/감각 동사로 보어 자리에 '과하게 작업된'이라는 수동/완료 의미의 분사형 형용사 overworked가 와야 합니다. 3. 결정하다(decide)의 목적어절로 '인지 아닌지'의 불확실한 내용을 이끄는 접속사 whether나 if가 문맥상 어울립니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. (A) You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. (B) They are flexible learners. (C) They have different strategies and know when to use them. (D) They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. (E) And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
questions.insertion_sentence: Skillful learners know that "putting on the same clothes" won't work for every class.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 숙련된 학습자들이 모든 수업에 동일한 방식을 적용하는 것이 효과가 없음을 안다는 내용입니다. 지문의 (A) 앞부분까지는 상황에 맞지 않는 옷차림의 부적절성을 예로 들고 있으며, (A) 뒤 문장은 상황에 맞는 적절한 복장이 있음을 언급합니다. (B) 이후부터는 '그들(They)' 즉 숙련된 학습자들에 대한 설명이 시작되므로, 일반적인 복장 예시에서 학습자로 화제가 전환되는 지점인 (B)에 주어진 문장이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with human-like facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.       *deform: 변형하다        *paw: (동물의) 발
options: ① The Evolution of Animal Representation in Media
② The Unnatural Reality of Talking Animals in Cartoons
③ Giving Human Traits to Animated Animals: Solely Concerned with Appearance
④ Humanizing Animal Characters: A Blend of Fantasy and Reality
⑤ Misleading Depictions of Animals in Modern Animation
questions.explanation: 이 글은 만화나 애니메이션에서 동물 캐릭터를 언어, 신체 구조, 표정 등을 통해 의인화하여 묘사하는 방식을 설명하고 있으므로, '동물 캐릭터의 의인화: 환상과 현실의 조화'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 미디어에서의 동물 표현의 진화
② 만화 속 말하는 동물들의 비자연스러운 현실
③ 애니메이션 동물에게 인간적인 특징 부여하기: 오로지 외모에만 관심이 있음
④ 동물 캐릭터의 의인화: 환상과 현실의 조화
⑤ 현대 애니메이션에서 동물의 오해 소지가 있는 묘사

questions.question: 24. 다음 글이 주는 교훈으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster - in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place. *thrive: 번성하다
options: ① Just as Alice and the Red Queen run without moving forward, individuals and societies must continuously adapt and evolve to deny their current states.
② In the competitive landscape of life, staying still requires persistent effort; constant improvement and adaptation are essential for survival.
③ This tale encourages us to question our perceptions of progress and success, recognizing that sometimes huge effort is needed just to remain stable.
④ It teaches that in the grand plan of nature and life, the struggle for existence demands innovation and persistence.
⑤ To maintain our position or progress, we must continually put in effort, as the Red Queen Effect shows that ceaseless effort is needed just to stay in place.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 '붉은 여왕 효과'는 상태적으로 제자리를 유지하기 위해 끊임없이 노력해야 하는 경쟁의 위험성을 이야기하는 것이지, 현재의 상태를 '부정하기 위해(to deny their current states)' 노력해야 한다는 것은 아니므로 ①번은 적절하지 않은 교훈입니다.
options_translation: ① 앨리스와 붉은 여왕이 앞으로 나가지 못하고 달리는 것처럼, 개인과 사회는 그들의 현 상태를 부정하기 위해 쉬지 않고 적응하고 진화해야 한다.
② 삶의 경쟁적인 파노라마에서, 가만히 있는 것은 끊임없는 노력을 필요로 하며, 쉬지 않는 개선과 적응은 생존을 위해 필수적이다.
③ 이 이야기는 우리에게 발전과 성공에 대한 인식에 의문을 제기하도록 권유하며, 때로는 단순히 안정된 상태를 유지하기 위해서만도 거대한 노력이 필요하다는 것을 인정하게 한다.
④ 그것은 자연과 삶의 거대한 계획 속에서, 생존을 위해 투쟁하는 것은 혁신과 끈기를 요구한다는 것을 가르친다.
⑤ 우리의 지위나 발전을 유지하기 위해, 우리는 지속적인 노력을 투입해야 하며, 붉은 여왕 효과가 보여주듯이 단순히 제자리에 머무르기 위해서만도 끊임없는 노력이 필요하기 때문이다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)even subtler cues가 의미하- 것을 <보기>의 글을 참고하여 지문에서 찾아 슬시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. -If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do,- explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, (A)<u>even subtler cues</u> within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to adopt the practices of those around you.
subjective_conditions: 1. 주어와 서술어림 갖춘 완전한 문장의 형태로 심 것
vocabulary_box: -even subtler cues- refers to less obvious indicators within the environment that signal trustworthiness or quality. The specific example given in the passage above to illustrate -even subtler cues- is: -________________________________________-. This example points out how the busyness of a restaurant serves as a subtle cue to its quality and desirability.
questions.answer: When you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat?
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'even subtler cues(훨씬 더 미묘한 단서들)'에 대한 구체적인 예시로 식당이 붐비는지, 밑에 줄이 서 있는지 아니면 자리림 찾기 쉬운지에 대한 문장을 제시하고 있습니다. 조건에 따라 주어와 서술어림 갖춘 완전한 문장으로 지문에서 찾아 써야 합니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 문맥과 어법에 맞도록 괄호안의 단어들을 순서대로 배열하시오.
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. In general, (A)[<u>easy / than / by flying eastward / by flying westward / is / extending the day / shortening it</u>]. It is because your body's internal clock is slightly longer than 24 hours, so it's easier to delay it rather than reset it to an earlier time. This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.       *jet lag: 시차로 인한 피로감
subjective_conditions: 1. 형용사(easy)를 변형하여 비교문을 완성할 것
2. 조건1을 위한 어형 변화 이외에 주어진 표현의 변형 불가
3. 주어진 모든 표현을 다 한 번씩 사용할 것
questions.answer: extending the day by flying westward is easier than shortening it by flying eastward
questions.explanation: 지문 내용상 서쪽으로 비행하여 하루를 늘리는 것이 동쪽으로 비행하여 하루를 줄이는 것보다 쉽다는 내용이 되어야 합니다. 비교급 구문 'A is easier than B'를 사용하며, 주어진 단어들을 배열하면 'extending the day by flying westward is easier than shortening it by flying eastward'가 됩니다.

questions.question: 11. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, (A)~(E) 중 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. (A) During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. (B) The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. (C) Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. (D) When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. (E) When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
questions.insertion_sentence: This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이는 원자들이 함께 이동하여 더 큰 결정을 형성할 충분한 시간을 갖기 때문이다'라는 이유를 설명하고 있다. (D) 문장에서 마그마가 천천히 식을 때 결정이 육안으로 볼 수 있을 만큼 커진다고 언급했으므로, 그에 대한 원인 설명인 주어진 문장은 (D) 바로 뒤인 (E) 자리에 위치하는 것이 흐름상 적절하다.

questions.question: 12. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. (A) During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. (B) The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. (C) Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. (D) When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. (E) When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
options: ① 마그마는 지구의 표면 아래에 갇혔을 때도 식는다.
② 마그마가 식으면서 마그마의 원자는 열에너지를 잃고 서로 더 가까이 이동한다.
③ 마그마가 식는 과정에서 서로 다른 화합물의 원자는 질서 있고 반복적인 패턴으로 배열된다.
④ 마그마에서 형성되는 결정의 크기는 부분적으로는 마그마의 식는 속도에 달려있다.
⑤ 마그마가 빠르게 식으면 형성되는 결정은 육안으로 볼 수 있을 정도로 크다.
questions.explanation: 본문의 마지막 부분에서 마그마가 빠르게 식으면 결정이 작게 형성되어 개별 광물 결정을 쉽게 볼 수 없다고 설명하고 있으므로, 5번은 본문 내용과 상반된다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. ⓐ<u>At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places</u>. ⓑ<u>England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes</u>. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. ⓒ<u>With the railways came many large hotels</u>. ⓓ<u>In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies</u>. ⓔ<u>Springs in the Rockies occurred when the groundwater emerged onto the surface of the earth</u>. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 경제 상황의 개선과 교통 수단(철도, 항공 등)의 발달이 관광 산업의 성장으로 이어진 과정을 설명하고 있다. ⓔ번 문장은 로키 산맥의 온천이 발생하는 지질학적 과정을 설명하고 있어, 관광 산업의 역사적 발달이라는 전체 흐름과 관계가 없다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more.
questions.summary_sentence: The study where university students' perceptions were shaped based on the (A)_____________ descriptions they received shows how people's assumptions about a person's traits can significantly impact their impressions and (B)_____________.
questions.explanation: 이 실험은 강연자에 대해 사전에 제공된 '따뜻한' 또는 '차가운'이라는 초기 정보가 학생들의 인상 형성과 태도(상호작용)에 영향을 미쳤음을 보여줍니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '초기의(initial)', (B)에는 '태도(attitudes)'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다. (1번의 behavior도 가능성이 있으나 A의 abstract가 부적절하며, 지문에서 interact more라는 행동 변화를 태도의 변화로 볼 수 있습니다.)
options_translation: ① 추상적인 - 행동
② 초기의 - 태도
③ 편향되지 않은 - 관계
④ 상세한 - 책임
⑤ 원래의 - 공격성

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your ⓐ<u>intended</u> path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to ⓑ<u>keep doing</u> it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort ⓒ<u>to climb</u> out; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation ⓓ<u>that</u> many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying-but ultimately ⓔ<u>unsatisfied</u> ㅡ job.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 수식하는 대상은 job(직업)입니다. 직업은 사람에게 만족감을 주거나 주지 않는 대상이므로, '만족스럽지 못한'이라는 의미를 나타낼 때는 감정을 느끼는 주체에 쓰는 과거분사 unsatisfied가 아니라 사물(직업)의 성질을 나타내는 현재분사 unsatisfying을 써야 합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ① Quality should be prior to quantity in business world.
② To increase selling, business should consider customers' needs in producing products.
③ Henry Ford should have produced T-model ford in various colors for his success.
④ The price of goods in the market is determined by the amount of supply and demand.
⑤ Selling products at a reasonable price is more important than understanding major characteristics of the modern industrial societies.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거에는 생산 중심의 사회였으나 현대 사회로 오면서 고객의 요구를 충족시키는 것이 비즈니스의 초점이 되었다는 내용입니다. 따라서 판매를 늘리기 위해 제품 생산 시 고객의 요구를 고려해야 한다는 ②번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 비즈니스 세계에서 질은 양보다 우선되어야 한다.
② 판매를 늘리기 위해 기업은 제품 생산 시 고객의 요구를 고려해야 한다.
③ 헨리 포드는 성공을 위해 T-모델 포드를 다양한 색상으로 생산했어야 했다.
④ 시장에서 상품의 가격은 수요와 공급의 양에 의해 결정된다.
⑤ 적정한 가격에 제품을 판매하는 것이 현대 산업 사회의 주요 특징을 이해하는 것보다 더 중요하다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains.
ordered_passages: (A) Bad carbohydrates, however, are simple sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made.
(B) Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
(C) As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 복합 탄수화물이 분해되기 어렵고 영양소를 가두고 있다고 설명합니다. (C)에서 '그것들이 천천히 분해되면서(As they slowly break down)' 영양소가 방출된다는 내용이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 그 다음 (A)에서 '하지만 나쁜 탄수화물은 단순당이다'라며 대조되는 내용을 도입하고, 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 나쁜 탄수화물(these carbohydrates)이 빠르게 분해되어 지방으로 저장된다는 결론을 내는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 각 괄호 (A), (B), (C)의 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: Whose story it is (A)[inflates / influences] what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will (B)[comprehend / compromise] them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different (C)[conclusion / contract]. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
questions.explanation: (A)는 누구의 이야기인가가 이야기의 내용을 '결정한다(영향을 미친다)'는 맥락이므로 influences가 적절합니다. (B)는 다른 캐릭터의 눈으로 사건을 본다면 그것들을 다르게 '이해할(comprehend)' 것이라는 맥락이 적절합니다. (C)는 관점이 바뀌면 공감의 대상이 바뀌고, 그에 따라 다른 '결말(conclusion)'을 기도하게 될 것이라는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다. *참고: 원문의 옵션 표기가 이미지 텍스트 추출 과정에서 다소 변형되었으나(표기 형식 오류), 질문의 선택지 1~5번 구조에 맞춰 정답을 도출하면 ③번입니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field.
ordered_passages: (A) Then, Dr. Hinds was also able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session.

(B) For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr. Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'.

(C) Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 전문가가 초보자에게 분야를 소개할 때 겪는 어려움을 언급합니다. (B)에서 '예를 들어' Pamela Hinds 박사의 연구를 소개하며 휴대폰 전문가가 초보자의 학습 시간을 예측하는 데 서투르다는 구체적인 사례를 제시합니다. (A)의 'Then'은 앞선 연구 내용에 이어지는 추가적인 결과로, 사람들이 기술을 습득할수록 그 난이도를 과소평가한다는 점을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 '지식의 저주'를 인지함으로써 학생의 관점에서 학습 과정을 바라볼 필요가 있다는 결론을 도출하므로 (B)-(A)-(C)가 정답입니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew larger. Living in communities ___________ ____________________. They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster. For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
options: ① led to conflicts among villagers
② made individuals work with greater cost
③ became more monotonous as time went by
④ made it easier for people to get organized efficiently
⑤ enabled the community members to lead quiet lives
questions.explanation: 지문은 구석기 시대의 이동 생활에서 신석기 농경 시작 이후의 정착 생활로의 변화를 다루고 있습니다. 특히 공동체 생활을 통해 업무를 분담(식량 생산, 집 짓기, 도구 제작 등)하고 협력함으로써 더 짧은 시간에 더 많은 결과물을 낼 수 있게 되었다는 점을 강조합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 공동체 생활이 사람들을 효율적으로 조직화하는 데 기여했다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 마을 주민들 사이의 갈등을 초래했다
② 개인들이 더 큰 비용을 들여 일하게 만들었다
③ 시간이 지남에 따라 더 단조로워졌다
④ 사람들이 효율적으로 조직화되는 것을 더 쉽게 만들었다
⑤ 공동체 구성원들이 조용한 삶을 영위할 수 있게 했다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 글의 내용상 의미하는 바가 같은 것끼리 짝지어진 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call ⓐ"<u>the rubber-stamp approach</u>." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's ⓑ<u>appropriate dress for different occasions and settings</u>. Skillful learners know that "ⓒ<u>putting on the same clothes</u>" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have ⓓ<u>different strategies</u> and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know ⓔ<u>how to do it</u>.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 학습 상황에 따라 유연하게 대처하는 '숙련된 학습자'의 특징을 설명하고 있습니다. ⓐ'고무인장 방식(rubber-stamp approach)'과 ⓒ'같은 옷을 입는 것(putting on the same clothes)'은 상황에 관계없이 매번 동일한 방식을 고수하는 부정적인 태도를 의미합니다. 반면 ⓑ'상황에 맞는 적절한 복장', ⓓ'서로 다른 전략들', ⓔ'그것을 하는 방법'은 상황에 맞춰 유연하게 대처하는 긍정적이고 전략적인 능력을 의미합니다. 따라서 ⓓ와 ⓔ가 유연한 학습자가 가진 전략과 실행 능력이라는 동일한 맥락의 의미를 지닙니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, a pedestrian, being much slower, ________________________________.Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① is prohibited from accepting new data
② finds himself in the middle of the street
③ notice more information of surroundings
④ is reluctant to process environmental details
⑤ tries to speed up to catch up with the fastest runner
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도와 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력 사이의 관계를 설명하고 있습니다. 속도가 빠를수록(운전자) 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력이 제한되는 반면, 속도가 느린 보행자(pedestrian)는 주변 환경에 대한 더 많은 정보를 인지할 수 있다는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 새로운 데이터를 받아들이는 것이 금지된다
② 자신이 도로 한가운데에 있음을 발견한다
③ 주변 환경의 더 많은 정보를 인지한다
④ 환경적 세부 사항을 처리하기를 꺼려한다
⑤ 가장 빠른 러너를 따라잡기 위해 속도를 높이려 노력한다

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① Joggers and Bicyclists: Who Is Faster?
② How a Rapidly Changing Environment Halts Evolution

questions.passage: The above graph shows the extent to which young people aged 16-25 in six countries had fear about climate change in 2021. ⓐThe Philippines had the highest percentage of young people who said they were extremely or very worried, at 84 percent, following Brazil by 17 percent. ⓑMore than 60 percent of young people in Portugal said they were extremely worried or very worried. ⓒIn France, the percentage of young people who were extremely worried was lower than that of young people who were very worried. ⓓIn the United Kingdom, the percentage of young generation who said that they were very worried was 29 percent. ⓔIn the United States, the total percentage of extremely worried and very worried youth was the smallest among the six countries.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers ⓐ<u>who</u> have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that ⓑ<u>forces</u> you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, ⓒ<u>even though</u> another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ⓓ<u>ridiculously</u> (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you ⓔ<u>were to</u> thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 동사 'sound'는 2형식 감각 동사로, 뒤에 보어로 형용사가 와야 합니다. 따라서 부사 'ridiculously'가 아닌 형용사 'ridiculous'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how ⓐ<u>important </u>meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much ⓑ<u>more</u> energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more ⓒ<u>fulfilled</u> on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be ⓓ<u>happier</u> with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took ⓔ<u>little</u> satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 흐름이 일에서의 만족감이 인생의 행복으로 이어진다는 긍정적인 상관관계를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 마지막 문장에서 행복한 삶을 살 가능성이 150% 더 높으려면 일에서 '적은' 만족감이 아니라 '많은' 만족감을 얻어야 문맥상 적절합니다. 'little'을 'much'나 'great' 등으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. ⓐThe subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. ⓑHowever, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. ⓒYou can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. ⓓFor most people, their subconscious sees too many things as bad and not enough as good. ⓔWhen your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)과 잠재의식적인 마음(subconscious mind)의 차이와 역할에 대해 설명하며, 특히 감정에 의해 조절되는 의식적인 마음이 잘못된 결정을 내리거나 공포의 원인이 된다는 점을 다루고 있습니다. ⓓ번 문장은 대부분의 사람들의 잠재의식이 사물을 나쁘게 본다는 내용으로, 의식과 잠재의식의 기능적 상호작용 및 감정의 역할이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.(B) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.(C) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 감각이 5개라는 아리스토텔레스의 전통적인 견해를 소개합니다. (C)에서 'However'로 이를 반박하며 인간에게도 다른 감각(고유 수용 감각, 평형 감각)이 있음을 제시합니다. (B)에서는 인간 외에 'Other animals(다른 동물들)'의 특수한 감각 사례를 추가합니다. (A)에서 'These examples(이러한 사례들)'로 앞선 내용들을 종합하며 감각을 제한된 수로 명확히 나눌 수 없다는 결론을 내리는 구조가 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. (A) Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. (B) They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. (C) If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. (D) The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. (E) When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
questions.insertion_sentence: The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 전령들이 왕의 명령과 보고를 전달하기 위해 길에 배치되었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A) 뒤의 문장에서 'Called Chasquis, they...'라고 시작하는데, 여기서 'they'가 지칭하는 대상이 바로 주어진 문장의 'The messengers'입니다. 따라서 전령의 역할과 배치를 설명하는 주어진 문장이 (A) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 production would create its own demand가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that weakened the view that <u>production would create its own demand</u>. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ① Production should be demand centered.
② Customers do not tend to consider the quality of goods.
③ It is essential to have price competitiveness in the product market.
④ The elimination of geographical constraints has led to overproduction of goods.
⑤ If products are produced at a reasonable price, customers will naturally buy those products.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 '생산이 그 자체의 수요를 창출할 것이다'라는 표현은 과거의 공급 중심적인 사고방식을 의미합니다. 즉, 물건을 적정 가격에 만들어내기만 하면 소비자들이 당연히 살 것이라는 믿음을 뜻합니다. 지문에서는 현대 사회로 오면서 이러한 관점이 약화되고 고객의 요구에 맞춘 마케팅 혁명이 일어났음을 설명하고 있으므로, ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 생산은 수요 중심이어야 한다.
② 고객은 상품의 품질을 고려하지 않는 경향이 있다.
③ 제품 시장에서 가격 경쟁력을 갖추는 것이 필수적이다.
④ 지리적 제약의 제거가 상품의 과잉 생산을 초래했다.
⑤ 제품이 합리적인 가격에 생산되면, 고객들은 자연스럽게 그 제품들을 살 것이다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① Based on the characteristics of each animal, different healing treatments are needed.
② A healing session which can be used widely to all animals needs to be developed.
③ A rescue center for animals is requiring financial support to provide better treatment.
④ It is important to understand the environmental factors influencing animal growth.
⑤ There is a similarity between treating physical illness and caring for emotional confusion.
questions.explanation: 제공된 지문은 인카 제국의 전령 시스템(Chasquis)에 대한 내용이지만, 선택지들은 동물의 치유(Healing)에 관한 내용을 담고 있습니다. 이는 문제 구성상의 오류로 보이나, 주어진 번호와 지문 매칭 시스템상 2번 문제의 지문은 잉카의 전령 시스템이며, 3번 문제의 지문은 동물 치유에 관한 것입니다. 만약 2번 문항의 요지를 묻는다면 잉카의 효율적인 전령 시스템이 정답이 되어야 하나, 선택지 구성에 맞춰 3번 지문의 내용을 기준으로 본다면 동물의 개별 특성에 맞춘 치료가 필요하다는 ①번이 가장 적절합니다. (참고: 지문 2와 3의 선택지가 서로 바뀐 것으로 보입니다.)
options_translation: ① 각 동물의 특성에 근거하여, 서로 다른 치유 치료법이 필요하다.
② 모든 동물에게 널리 사용될 수 있는 치유 세션이 개발될 필요가 있다.
③ 동물 구조 센터는 더 나은 치료를 제공하기 위해 재정적 지원을 요구하고 있다.
④ 동물 성장에 영향을 미치는 환경적 요인을 이해하는 것이 중요하다.
⑤ 신체적 질병을 치료하는 것과 정서적 혼란을 돌보는 것 사이에는 유사점이 있다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal.
options: ① places connecting people to people in the Inca
② messengers delivering letters between the Incas
③ technology making huts on high ground possible
④ roads opening up more of the world to the Inca
⑤ system allowing swift and efficient relay of messages in the Inca
questions.explanation: 이 문항 역시 지문은 동물 치유에 관한 것이나 선택지는 잉카 제국의 전령 시스템에 관한 것입니다. 2번 지문(잉카 전령)의 주제를 고르는 문제로 판단했을 때, 신속하고 효율적인 메시지 전달 시스템을 설명하는 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 제목/주제입니다.
options_translation: ① 인카에서 사람과 사람을 연결하는 장소들
② 인카 사람들 사이에서 편지를 전달하는 전령들
③ 높은 지대에 오두막을 짓는 것을 가능하게 한 기술
④ 인카에게 더 넓은 세상을 열어준 도로들
⑤ 인카에서 신속하고 효율적인 메시지 전달을 가능하게 한 시스템

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
options: ① Perception Wins Out Over Drowsiness
② Don't Open Your Eyes for Your Better Sleep
③ Does Perceptual Disengagement Help the Blind?
④ Laziness of Sensing System: It warns Your health
⑤ Effective Inactivity: For Preventing One from Waking up
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잠자는 동안 외부 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않는 '지각적 단절(perceptual disengagement)'의 특성과 그 기능에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 이러한 단절은 수면을 보호하는 역할을 하며 자극이 수면자를 깨우지 못하게 합니다. 따라서 '깨어나는 것을 방지하기 위한 효과적인 비활동성'을 언급하는 ⑤번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지각이 졸음을 이기다
② 더 나은 수면을 위해 눈을 뜨지 마라
③ 지각적 단절이 시각 장애인에게 도움이 되는가?
④ 감각 시스템의 게으름: 당신의 건강을 경고한다
⑤ 효과적인 비활동성: 누군가가 깨어나는 것을 방지하기 위해

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것만을 <보기>에서 고른 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
vocabulary_box: ⓐDifferent areas of the tongue are responsible for detecting specific tastes.
ⓑThe "tongue map" theory was proven correct by research conducted in the 1980s and 1990s.
ⓒToday, tasted buds are believed not to be organized based on specialization.
ⓓSweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be perceived across all regions of the mouth.
ⓔTaste perception on the tongue is only based on the intensity of taste sensations.
ⓕThe mechanism of taste preception is based on time rather than specific locations on the tongue.
questions.explanation: 글의 내용에 따르면 ⓐ 혀의 부위에 따라 특정 맛을 담당한다는 '혀 지도'는 틀린 이론입니다. ⓑ 1980-90년대 연구는 혀 지도가 '완전히 틀렸음(totally wrong)'을 입증했습니다. ⓔ 맛의 지각 메커니즘은 장소가 아니라 시간(time)에 기반한다고 설명되어 있으므로, 단순히 강도에만 기반한다는 설명은 적절하지 않습니다. 따라서 일치하지 않는 내용은 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓔ입니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것만을 <보기>에서 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
vocabulary_box: ⓐOne of the processes of mineral formation involves the cooling of magma.
ⓑAtoms of the same compounds arrange themselves into disorganized patterns.
ⓒAtoms in magma combine into compounds while cooling.
ⓓThe elements present in magma have no influence on mineral formation.
ⓔThe size of crystals formed is only determined by the type of compounds present in magma.
ⓕMineral crystals may not be easily visible if magma rapidly cools.
questions.explanation: ⓑ 본문에서 원자들은 무질서한 것이 아니라 '질서 정연하고 반복적인 패턴(orderly, repeating patterns)'으로 배열된다고 하였습니다. ⓓ 마그마에 존재하는 원소의 종류와 양은 어떤 광물이 형성될지를 결정하므로 영향이 있습니다. ⓔ 결정의 크기는 화합물의 종류뿐만 아니라 냉각 속도(how rapidly the magma cools)에 따라 결정됩니다. 따라서 일치하지 않는 것은 ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ입니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people recently started considering the difficulties of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. In the past, the ⓐ<u>prevailing</u> thought was that sports should have the same condition in play, no matter who participates. However, they found the road to success for young children is significantly ⓑ<u>limited</u> if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle in adult-style competition. Therefore, different sports have made ⓒ<u>appropriate</u> adaptations for the young. For example, junior soccer uses a lighter ball and a smaller field. All have competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, swimming has adapted its stadiums to have shorter lanes so that ⓓ<u>proper</u> environment is avoided for children under 10. The ⓔ<u>transformations</u> are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: 수영 경기장이 짧은 레인을 갖도록 개조된 이유는 어린 아이들에게 '부적절한(inappropriate)' 환경을 피하기 위해서입니다. 따라서 ⓓ 'proper(적절한)'은 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions ⓐ<u>improved</u>. Gradually people were given ⓑ<u>less</u> time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, ⓒ<u>paved the way</u> for now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made ⓓ<u>available</u> the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism ⓔ<u>expansion</u>.
questions.explanation: 사회적, 경제적 상황이 나아지면서 임금 수준과 근로 조건이 개선되었고, 점차 사람들은 '더 많은(more)' 휴가 시간을 갖게 되었다는 맥락이 적절합니다. 따라서 ⓑ의 'less'는 'more'로 바뀌어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① ⓑ
② ⓒ

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to _______________________________." Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster - in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
options: ② keep in the same place
questions.explanation: 붉은 여왕 효과(Red Queen Effect)는 주변 환경(또는 경쟁 상대)이 같이 진화하기 때문에, 제자리에 머물기 위해서라도 끊임없이 달려야 한다는 진화론적 원리를 설명합니다. 글의 마지막 부분 'stay in place'와도 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 다양한 분야에서 뛰어나다
② 같은 장소에 머물러 있다
③ 유전적으로 우세하다
④ 타인과 조화를 이루다
⑤ 균형 잡힌 시각을 가지다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because-fueled by emotions-you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when _______________________________.
options: ④ reinforced by the subconscious mind
questions.explanation: 의식적인 마음에서 비롯된 생각이나 두려움이 잠재의식 속에 기억과 인식으로 자리 잡게 되면 비로소 '진정한 두려움'이 된다는 맥락입니다. 앞부분에서 잠재의식이 기억과 인식을 담당한다고 했으므로, 의식에서 시작된 감정이 잠재의식에 의해 강화되거나 고착화될 때를 설명하는 4번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 그것들을 극복할 때
② 그것들이 통제 가능할 때
③ 의식적인 노력을 통해 제거될 때
④ 잠재의식에 의해 강화될 때
⑤ 의식이 잠재의식보다 앞설 때

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. ____________________________________ can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
options: ① To imitate great work of art
② Putting too less into a painting
③ To keep painting overly without stop
④ To paint without detailed description
⑤ Simplifying paintings to expose a subject
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 그림을 그릴 때 적절한 시점에 멈추는 것의 중요성입니다. 빈칸 뒤에 '영향력을 망치고 과하게 작업된 것처럼 보이게 할 수 있다'는 내용이 나오므로, 빈칸에는 멈추지 않고 과도하게 계속 그리는 행위에 대한 내용이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 위대한 예술 작품을 모방하는 것
② 그림에 너무 적게 투입하는 것
③ 멈추지 않고 과도하게 계속 그리는 것
④ 세부적인 묘사 없이 그리는 것
⑤ 주제를 드러내기 위해 그림을 단순화하는 것

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. (A) In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. (B) Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. (C) The fastest users of the street, motorists having little time to appreciate design details along the street. (D) On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. (E) While they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.insertion_sentence: Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도에 따른 세부 정보 파악 능력의 차이를 설명합니다. (C)에서는 가장 빠른 '운전자'를, (D)에서는 대조적으로 훨씬 느린 '보행자'를 언급하며 양극단(polar opposites)을 형성합니다. 주어진 문장의 '조깅하는 사람과 자전거 타는 사람'은 보행자보다는 빠르지만 운전자보다는 느린 그 '중간'에 해당하므로, 보행자에 대한 설명이 끝난 뒤인 (E)에 위치하여 보행자보다 빠르고 운전자보다 느리다는 부연 설명과 이어지는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. (A) As a result, towns and villages grew larger. (B) Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. (C) They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. (D) While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. (E) For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
questions.insertion_sentence: Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 정착 생활 이후의 분업과 협동에 대해 설명합니다. (D)까지는 업무를 나누어(divide up) 농사를 짓거나 도구를 만드는 등의 분업에 대해 이야기합니다. 주어진 문장의 '함께 일하여 일을 더 빨리 하는 법을 배웠다'는 내용은 분업에서 나아가 '협동'의 개념을 도입합니다. (E) 뒤의 예시(도구 제작자들이 도끼 만드는 일을 공유하여 더 많은 도구를 만듦)는 바로 이 협동과 효율성에 대한 구체적 사례이므로 (E)가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn.
ordered_passages: (A) But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication.

(B) As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you.

(C) To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable.    *norm: 규범
questions.explanation: 규범(Norms)에 대한 정의가 나온 후, (B)에서 '단순한 예시'로 영미권 사회에서 도움을 받았을 때 '감사합니다'라고 말하는 규범을 소개합니다. (A)는 (B)의 마지막 문장인 '강제하는 법은 없다'와 대조되는 '하지만(But)'으로 시작하여, 그럼에도 불구하고 말하지 않았을 때 책임과 비판이 따른다는 규범의 영향력을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)는 '감사합니다 예시를 계속하자면(To continue the Thank you example)'이라며 다른 문화권에서의 차이점과 교차 문화적 소통의 어려움으로 내용을 확장하고 있습니다. 따라서 (B)-(A)-(C) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to come together with him more.
questions.summary_sentence: This shows that different expectations not only affect the (A)_____________ we form but also our behaviour and the (B)_____________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 사람에 대한 사전 정보(warm vs cold)가 그 사람에 대한 나중의 인상 형성에 큰 영향을 준다는 실험을 설명하고 있습니다. 또한 따뜻할 것이라 기대한 학생들이 강연자와 더 많이 교류(come together)했다는 결과를 보여줍니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '인상(impressions)'이, (B)에는 '상호작용(interaction)'이 들어가는 것이 지문의 요약문으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 친절함 / 상호작용
② 친절함 / 지능
③ 인상 / 상호작용
④ 인상 / 지능
⑤ 차가움 / 묘사

questions.question: 29. 다ᄋᄆ 글으ᄂ 미ᄐ줄 친 한글 문자ᄀ으래 주어진 개거네 타라 문바ᄇ저ᄀ으로 오그른 여거 문자ᄀ으로 바귀어 새수ᄅ하시오.
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. <u>자시느ᄂ 이레 만조ᄀ하느ᄂ 사라ᄆ드르ᄂ 그다르ᄂ 살메 하ᄂ보ᄀ해할 가느ᄂ서ᄀ으ᄅ 그다</u>. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica PryceJones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work had a happier life overall.
subjective_conditions: 1. 가래 주어지ᄂ 애구마ᄂ으ᄅ 하ᄂ 번시ᄀ 모두 사여ᄂ하시오.
2. 하ᄂ그ᄅ 문자ᄀ으ᄂ 의미에 마ᄌ추어 벼ᄂ혀ᄀ으ᄂ 피료하ᄂ 애구 1개르ᄅ 차자 문바ᄇ저ᄀ으로 오그르ᄂ 혀ᄂ태로 고쳐 새수ᄅ하시오.
3. 채자 오류 2개가지마ᄂ 부부ᄂ 자ᄆ수 부여. (3개 이사ᄂ부타 무ᄂ하ᄀ 0자ᄆ 처리)
4. 대소무ᄂ자 구부ᄂ하지 개느ᄆ
questions.answer: People satisfied with their work are likely to be happy with their lives.
questions.explanation: 주어지ᄂ 애구드르ᄅ 사여ᄂ하여 문자ᄀ으ᄅ 구서ᄀ하며, '마ᄂ조ᄀ하느ᄂ 사라ᄆ드ᄅ'으ᄂ People satisfied with로 사여ᄂ하느ᄂ 거시 저ᄀ저ᄅ하다. 이태 satisfy with느ᄂ 사라ᄆ드ᄅ으ᄂ 마ᄂ조ᄀ으ᄅ 느끼느ᄂ 수도ᄃ저ᄀ 대사ᄀ이므로 과가부ᄂ사인 satisfied with로 벼ᄂ혀ᄀ해야 하ᄂ다. 그러므로 'People satisfied with their work' 가 주어가 되고, 'are likely to be happy with their lives' 가 사수ᄅ어가 되느ᄂ 구조이다.

questions.question: 30. 다ᄋᄆ 글으ᄂ 미ᄐ줄 친 push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets가 의미하느ᄂ 바르ᄅ <개거네> 타라 새수ᄅ하시오.
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals-sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that ‖senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds,- Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to <u>push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets</u>, we should study them for what they are.
subjective_conditions: 1. 가래 재시되ᄂ 애구마ᄂ으ᄅ 사여ᄂ할 거스 (※벼ᄂ혀ᄀ 호그ᄂ 추가 시 무ᄂ하ᄀ 0자ᄆ)
2. Write the answer into 7 words (not phrases), beginning with a verb
3. <개거네> 퓌배 시 무ᄂ하ᄀ 0자ᄆ 처리.
4. 채자 오류 2개가지마ᄂ 부부ᄂ 자ᄆ수 부여. (3개 이사ᄂ부타 무ᄂ하ᄀ 0자ᄆ 처리)
questions.answer: sort various animal senses into fixed categories
questions.explanation: 미ᄐ줄 친 바느ᄂ 도물으ᄂ 가ᄆᄀ가ᄀ으ᄅ 아리ᄉ토테레스시ᄀ 바구니내개 미러너흐려 하느ᄂ 거ᄉ으로, 그 의미느ᄂ 다야하ᄂ 도물으ᄂ 가ᄆᄀ가ᄀ드르ᄅ 고저ᄀ되ᄂ 가테고리로 바뉴하느ᄂ 거ᄉ으ᄅ 트ᄉ하ᄂ다. 저시되ᄂ 애구 주ᄀ 도머사로 시자ᄀ하느ᄂ 7다ᄂ어 문자ᄀ으ᄂ 'sort(1) various(2) animal(3) senses(4) into(5) fixed(6) categories(7)'가 되느ᄂ 거시 저ᄀ저ᄅ하다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 putting on the same clothes가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that <u>putting on the same clothes</u> won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ① knowing how to use stamps efficiently
② not being able to handle difficulties in learning
③ being close-minded and denying new knowledge
④ using the same method no matter what kinds of tasks
⑤ applying various learning strategies depending on context
questions.explanation: 이 글은 상황에 따라 다른 학습 전략을 사용해야 함을 강조하고 있습니다. '똑같은 옷을 입는 것(putting on the same clothes)'은 앞서 언급된 '고무인장 방식(rubber-stamp approach)'과 같은 의미로, 과업의 종류나 상황에 관계없이 항상 똑같은 방식만을 고수하는 것을 비유적으로 표현한 것입니다.
options_translation: ① 도장을 효율적으로 사용하는 방법을 아는 것
② 학습의 어려움을 감당할 수 없는 것
③ 폐쇄적이고 새로운 지식을 거부하는 것
④ 어떤 종류의 과업이든 상관없이 같은 방식을 사용하는 것
⑤ 맥락에 따라 다양한 학습 전략을 적용하는 것

questions.question: 4. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
options: ① 집중력을 기르기 위해서는 한 가지 일에만 몰두해야 한다.
② 해야 할 목록을 작성하고 중요한 일부터 처리하는 것이 좋다.
③ 효율적으로 일을 처리하기 위해서는 자투리 시간을 활용해야 한다.
④ 경험하지 않은 일도 늘 성공할 수 있다는 낙관주의를 경계해야 한다.
⑤ 어떠한 일을 성취하기 위해서는 필요한 시간을 추산하는 것이 필요하다.
questions.explanation: 필자는 무언가를 성취하기 위해서는 일이 얼마나 오래 걸릴지 이해하는 것이 중요하며(important to understand how long things are going to take), 할 일 목록 옆에 필요한 시간을 추산하는 습관을 들이라고 조언하고 있습니다(Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed). 따라서 정답은 5번입니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more 'natural' way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
options: ① the most effective way to gain popularity
② the reason why animals are different from humans
③ shift in the use of childlike characters in animation
④ commercial strategies to compete with human characters
⑤ ways of making animal characters attractive in industries
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물 캐릭터를 사람처뜜 묘사하거나 아이 같은 특징을 부여하여 더옑 감정적으로 매력적이게 만드는 방법들에 대해 설명하고 은다. 따라서 제목으로는 산업계에서 동물 캐릭터를 매력적으로 만드는 방법이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 인기를 얻는 가장 효과적인 방법
② 동물이 인간과 다른 이유
③ 애니메이섘에서 아이 같은 캐릭터 사용의 경향 변화
④ 인간 캐릭터와 경쟁하기 을 한 상업적 전략
⑤ 산업에서 동물 캐릭터를 매력적으로 만드는 방법

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. Although it may seem sensible, having two separate calendars for work and personal life can lead to distractions. To check if something is missing, you will find yourself checking your to-do lists multiple times. Instead, organize all of your tasks in one place. It doesn't matter if you use digital or paper media. It's okay to keep your professional and personal tasks in one place. This will give you a good idea of how time is divided between work and home. This will allow you to make informed decisions about which tasks are most important.
options: ① steps to get your surroundings in order to increase work concentration
② necessity of organizing one's work and personal tasks in one place
③ need for a habit of taking notes of good ideas
④ why you need to have two different checklists
⑤ importance of having expertise in one's work
questions.explanation: 이 글은 업무와 개인 생활의 일정을 분리하지 말고 한 곳에 정리하는 것이 주윘 산만을 방준하고 효실적으로 시간을 관리하는 데 도움이 된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로는 업무와 개인 일정을 한 곳에 정리할 필요성이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 업무 집중력을 높이기 위해 주변을 정리하는 단계
② 업무와 개인 일정을 한 곳에 정리할 필요성
③ 좋은 아이디어를 메모하는 습관의 필요성
④ 둀 가지 다른 체크리스트를 갖아야 하는 이유
⑤ 자신의 일에 전문성을 갖는 것의 성요성

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: ‖here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster; in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
options: ① Kill Two Birds with One Stone
② Red Queen Effect : Endless Evolutionary Race
③ A Biological Secret Discovered by Lewis Carroll
④ Competition to Survive Between Foxes and Rabbits
⑤ The Birth of New Species and Its Effect on Ecosystem
questions.explanation: 이 글은 루이스 캐러의 소설에 등장하는 '붉은 여왕' 이야기를 비오하여 생물학적 진화 원리인 '붉은 여왕 효과'를 설명하고 있습니다. 모든 종이 같이 빨리 진화하기 때문에 상대적으로는 제자리 걸음인 것처뜜 보이는 끝없는 진화적 경쟁을 설명합니다. 따라서 제목으로는 '붉은 여왕 효과: 끝없는 진화적 경쟁'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 일석이조
② 붉은 여왕 효과: 끝없는 진화적 경쟁
③ 루이스 캐러에 의해 발견된 생물학적 비밀
④ 여우와 토뉼 사이의 생존 경쟁
⑤ 새로운 종의 태동과 그것이 생태계에 미찘는 영향

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body breaks down these carbohydrates quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
options: ① There are good carbohydrates which are good for your health.
② Complex sugar compounds are difficult to break down and contain nutrients in them.
③ Complex sugar compounds supply fuel for a number of hours as they break down slowly.
④ The carbohydrates with simple sugars are easily breakable so that they help you hold nutrients.
⑤ Your body quickly breaks down bad carbohydrates and what it can't use is turned into fat.
questions.explanation: 본문에 따르면 단순당(simple sugars)은 구조가 복잡하지 않아 분해되기 쉬우며, 구성 성분인 당 외에는 영양소를 거의 함유하고 있지 않다고 했으므로, 영양소 보유를 돕는다는 ④번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 건강에 좋은 좋은 탄수화물이 존재한다.
② 복합당 화합물은 분해하기 어렵고 그 안에 영양소를 포함하고 있다.
③ 복합당 화합물은 천천히 분해되면서 몇 시간 동안 연료를 공급한다.
④ 단순당을 가진 탄수화물은 쉽게 분해되어 영양소를 보유하도록 도와준다.
⑤ 신체는 나쁜 탄수화물을 빠르게 분해하며 사용하지 못한 것은 지방으로 바뀐다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop ⓐ<u>enjoying</u> it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut ⓑ<u>that</u> you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut ⓒ<u>have</u> become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation ⓓ<u>which</u> many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has made them ⓔ<u>felt</u> locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying - but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장에서 made는 사역동사로 쓰였습니다. 사역동사(make) + 목적어(them) + 목적격 보어의 구조에서 목적어가 동작을 직접 당하는 수동의 의미인 경우 과거분사를 쓸 수 있지만, 여기서는 그들이 갇혀 있다고 느끼게 만드는 것이므로 원형 부정사인 feel이 와야 자연스럽습니다. 다만 '느껴지는 상태'로 보아도 felt는 부적절하며, feel locked 형태로 쓰여 '갇혀 있다고 느끼다'가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
