questions.passage: Whose story it is ⓐ<u>affects</u> what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them ⓑ<u>differently</u>. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises ⓒ<u>what</u> is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, ⓓ<u>how</u> the tale of Cinderella would change if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were ⓔ<u>shown</u> the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
questions.explanation: ⓒ 'what is the heart of the story'는 선행사인 'the conflict'를 수식하는 관계대명사절이어야 합니다. what은 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사이므로 앞에 선행사가 올 수 없습니다. 따라서 주격 관계대명사인 that이나 which로 바꾸어야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant ⓐ<u>trustworthiness</u> with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel ⓑ<u>related</u> to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill is ⓒ<u>irrelevant</u> with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of his ⓓ<u>expertise</u> with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his knowledge on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence ⓔ<u>attracts</u> people. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
questions.explanation: 전체 맥락상 뛰어난 능력(Excellence)을 가진 사람이 관련 없는 분야에서도 영향력을 행사한다는 내용입니다. 지문에서는 농구 선수가 제품 지식 때문이 아니라 농구에서의 전문성 때문에 사람들이 그를 신뢰한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 본문에 제시된 ⓒ는 irrelevant가 적절하며, ⓓ의 expertise도 문맥상 맞습니다. 하지만 원본 텍스트의 정답 표시인 ④번을 기준으로 분석할 때, 지문의 문맥상 전문성(expertise)이 아닌 다른 단어가 와야 할 자리가 아니므로, 만약 문제가 의도한 오류라면 해당 단어가 잘못 사용된 곳을 찾아야 합니다. (이 지문은 원래 'halo effect'를 설명하는 글로, 전문성 자체가 다른 분야의 신뢰를 '유발'한다는 내용이므로 ⓓ는 흐름상 적절합니다. 다만, 원문 텍스트에서 제공된 정답이 ④번이므로 해당 지문의 ⓓ가 본래 원문과 다르게 변형되었거나 오타일 가능성이 있으나, 주어진 텍스트 내에서 ⓓ는 expertise로 적절해 보입니다. 단, ⓑ가 중복 사용된 것으로 보아 ⓑ(irrelevant) 혹은 중복 표기된 다른 부분이 오류일 수 있습니다.) *실제 원문 대조 시: 이 문제는 해당 단어가 맥락에 맞지 않는 것을 고르는 것인데, ④번 expertise는 문맥상 어색하지 않습니다. 다만 지문 내 ⓑ가 두 번 표기된 편집 오류가 보입니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew larger. Living in communities allowed people to __________________________________. They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster. For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
options: ③ buy and sell the products
questions.explanation: 본문은 농경 시작 이후 공동체 생활을 하면서 업무를 분담(divide up the work)하고 협력함으로써 더 짧은 시간에 더 많은 도구를 만들 수 있게 되었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 이는 '업무 효율성을 높이다'라는 의미인 ① enhance work efficiency가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 업무 효율을 높이다
② 그들 자신의 마을을 보호하다
③ 제품을 사고팔다
④ 서로를 다르게 대우하다
⑤ 책임감 있고 사교적이게 되다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution _______________________________________________. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ① spread the idea that colors would matter all things
② forced business to lower prices of high quality products
③ focused on producing products with customer's preference
④ reinforced the belief that production would lead to profit
⑤ made business mainly focus on producers, not customers
questions.explanation: 지문은 판매의 철학적 변화를 다루고 있습니다. 과거에는 단순히 저렴하고 질 좋은 제품을 생산하는 것에 집중했다면, 이제는 고객이 실제로 원하는 제품을 제공하는 것이 필수적이 되었습니다. 마지막 문장에서 고객과 그들의 다양한 요구를 충족시키는 것이 기업의 중심이 되었다고 했으므로, 빈칸에는 '고객의 선호도에 따른 제품 생산에 집중하는' 마케팅 혁명이 일어났다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 색상이 모든 것에 중요하다는 생각을 퍼뜨렸다
② 기업이 고품질 제품의 가격을 낮추도록 강요했다
③ 고객의 선호도에 따른 제품 생산에 집중했다
④ 생산이 이윤으로 이어질 것이라는 믿음을 강화했다
⑤ 기업이 고객이 아닌 생산자에게 주로 집중하게 만들었다

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, ___ __________________________________________________________.
options: ① it is a waste of time to meet many people to gather social evidence
② accepting what the majority of people choose to do is a secure practice
③ it is necessary to listen carefully to what famous psychologists say
④ the more trustworthy people you have around you, the more trustworthy you are
⑤ following a small number of trustworthy people is better than following a large number of people
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 안전함과 신뢰성을 판단하기 위해 '사회적 증거', 즉 다수의 행동을 따르는 경향이 있다는 것을 설명합니다. 진화론적 관점에서 집단을 따르는 것이 생존에 유리했으며, 식당의 줄과 같은 예시를 통해 많은 사람이 선택한 것이 좋은 선택이라는 신호로 작용함을 보여줍니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 다수의 선택을 따르는 것이 안전한 관행이라는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사회적 증거를 모으기 위해 많은 사람을 만나는 것은 시간 낭비이다
② 대다수의 사람들이 하기로 선택한 것을 받아들이는 것은 안전한 관행이다
③ 유명한 심리학자들이 말하는 것을 주의 깊게 들을 필요가 있다
④ 주변에 신뢰할 수 있는 사람이 많을수록 당신도 더 신뢰할 수 있는 사람이 된다
⑤ 적은 수의 신뢰할 수 있는 사람을 따르는 것이 많은 수의 사람을 따르는 것보다 낫다

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable.
ordered_passages: (A) This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." This was found in a recent survey of one million high school seniors.

(B) For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are moreintelligent, more fairminded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person.

(C) The survey found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 우리가 자신을 사회적으로 바람직하다고 믿는 경향이 있다는 일반적 진술입니다. (B)에서 'For example'을 통해 대중이 스스로를 평균보다 지적이고 공정하다고 생각하는 구체적인 예시를 제시합니다. (A)에서 이러한 현상을 'Lake Wobegon effect'라고 명명하며 최근 고등학생 대상 설문조사를 언급합니다. (C)에서 (A)에 언급된 그 설문조사(The survey)의 구체적인 수치 결과(70%, 2% 등)를 제시하며 마무리됩니다. 따라서 (B)-(A)-(C) 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 갳은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing -- all of these began with an idea. (A) Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. (B) Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. (C) The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. (D) We begin with an idea about how the future will be. (E) Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
questions.insertion_sentence: Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장 'Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision'은 시간이 흐름에 따랼 비전(미래에 대한 생각)을 다듬고 완성한다는 내용입니다. (D) 문장에서 미래가 어떻게 될지에 대한 생각으로 시작한다는 내용이 나오고, 그 다음에 이 비전을 다듬는 과정이 있어야 (E)에서처랼 모든 생각과 활동이 점차 점화되어 미래를 실현하게 됩니다. 따랼서 (E) 윐치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 갳은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). (A) Satisfied customers can recommend the products to others for no gain, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. (B) People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. (C) People trust friends over advertisements any day. (D) They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. (E) By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
questions.insertion_sentence: You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 구매자가 다른 사람들에게 구매를 권장할지 여부를 판단할 수 있게 한다는 내용입니다. 이는 (A) 앞 문장의 '재구매 여부' 판단에 이어 추가적인 판단 요소(also)를 설명하며, (A) 들에 나오는 '만족한 고객이 다른 사람에게 촔찜한다'는 내용과 자연스럽게 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the study, our (A)______________ assumptions about people based on original information are (B)_____________ with the impression and interaction we make.
questions.explanation: 지문은 사람들이 한 가지 특징을 근거로 다른 특징까지 자동으로 가질 것이라 가정하는 경향이 있음을 보여줍니다. 실험 결과, '따뜻함' 또는 '차가움'이라는 사전 정보를 받은 학생들은 그 정보에 따라 서로 다른 인상을 형성했고 실제 상호작용 방식도 달라졌습니다. 따라서 초기 정보에 기반한 (A)부정확한(incorrect/mistaken) 가설은 실제 인상 형성 및 상호작용과 (B)관련(associated)되어 있다는 결론이 도출됩니다.
options_translation: ① 부정확한 ... 관련된
② 잘못된 ... 관련 없는
③ 무관심한 ... 연결된
④ 동일한 ... 관련된
⑤ 거짓의 ... 관련 없는

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 옳은 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs</u>. ⓑ<u>The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experience the greatest benefits</u>. ⓒ<u>Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting</u>. ⓓ<u>The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participating in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved</u>. ⓔ<u>Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence</u>.
questions.explanation:
ⓑ 'with + 명사 + 분사' 구문에서 목적어(those participating~)와 목적격 보어의 관계가 능동이므로, experience는 현재분사인 experiencing으로 고쳐야 합니다.
ⓓ when 접속사절 내에서 participating은 주어 people을 수술하는 분사구가 아니라 절의 본동사 역할을 해야 하므로, 시제에 맞춰 과거 동사인 participated로 고쳐야 합니다.
ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓔ는 문법상 오류가 없는 올바른 문장입니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students eyes rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
options: ① need of understanding the learning process of novices
② difficulties experts experience in learning something new
③ important tips for communicating what experts think to novices
④ ways to build sound relationships between experts and newcomers
⑤ skills overestimated by experts who have difficulty in understanding learners
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전문가들이 초바자에게 지식을 전달할 때 겪는 어려움(지식의 저주)을 설먐하며, 학습 과정을 학생의 관점에서 바라볼 필요성을 강조하고 이습니다.
options_translation: ① 초바자의 학습 과정을 이해할 필요성
② 전문가들이 새로운 것을 봀울 때 겪는 어려움
③ 전문가의 생각을 초바자에게 전달하기 위한 중요한 팁
④ 전문가와 신입자 사이의 건강한 관계림 협성하는 방박
⑤ 학습자림 이해하는 데 어려움을 겪는 전문가들에 의해 과대 평가된 기술

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time difficulties that you face and deal with. Just turn the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as -I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day.- Once you write these statements, get ready to experience magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① role of magic in achieving academic goals
② negative consequences of being too positive
③ impact of positivity in overcoming challenges
④ effect of a positive attitude on the morning routine
⑤ positive example of overcoming adversity in the story of Cinderella
questions.explanation: 이 글은 실제로 겪는 어려움들을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꿔 써보는 것이 생각걠 행동의 변화림 이끌어 내고, 난관을 극밑하는 데 도움을 준다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 학업 목표 달성에서 바법의 료할
② 나무 긍정적인 것의 부정적인 결과
③ 도전 과제 극밑에서 긍정성의 영향
④ 아침 일과에 대한 긍정적인 태도의 효과
⑤ 신데렐라 이야기에서 역경을 극밑한 긍정적인 예시

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것만을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은? [24년 3월 33번]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 지문 내용 분석:ⓒ: 일반적으로 잠을 자는 포유류는 환경 자극에 반응하지 않는다는 내용은 지문 첫 문장과 일치합니다.ⓔ: 지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)이 일부 저자들에게는 무시되기도 하지만 잠에 기여할 수 있다는 내용은 지문 후반부(protecting sleep, essential to its definition)와 일치합니다.틀린 보기 분석:ⓐ: 시각 정보가 약하게 처리될 때 깨어 있어야 한다는 내용은 지문과 반대입니다(잠자는 동안 정보가 약하게 처리됨).ⓑ: 사람들은 잠자는 동안 외부 요인에 관여(get involved)하지 않고 지각적으로 분리됩니다.ⓓ: 지각적 이탈은 졸음 상태를 방해하는 것과 관련이 있다는 언급은 없으며, 오히려 졸음 상태는 완전한 지각적 이탈 없이 수면의 이점을 얻는 중간 상태라고 설명됩니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 3월 39번]
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also ⓐ<u>affect</u> how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will ⓑ<u>react</u> differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for ⓒ<u>emotional</u> confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be ⓓ<u>endured</u> to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a ⓔ<u>continuous</u> learning process.
questions.explanation: 지문의 문맥상 각 치유 치료는 동물의 특정한 요구에 맞추어 '조정되거나(tailored/adjusted)' 구성되어야 한다는 의미가 적절합니다. 'endured(견뎌지다/인내되다)'는 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글을 읽고 알 수 있는 내용이 아닌 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① Each species has specific climatic conditions, such as tolerance to heat or cold.
② Fossils provide evidence that trees moved during past periods of climate change.
③ Although seemingly immobile, trees and barnacles can spread as a seed or a larva.
④ Climate change delays species from moving to areas that meet their temperature needs.
⑤ A creature must leave its birthplace to find a better environment for survival, growth, and reproduction.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 기후가 변화할 때 생물종들은 기후 조건을 충족하는 장소로 이동해야 하며(forced to follow), 나무조차 놀라운 속도로 이동했다는 내용이 나옵니다. 기후 변화가 종의 이동을 지연시킨다는 내용은 지문에 언급되지 않았으며, 오히려 이동을 강요하는 요인입니다.
options_translation: ① 각 종은 열이나 추위에 대한 내성과 같은 특정한 기후 조건을 가지고 있다.
② 화석은 과거 기후 변화 기간 동안 나무가 이동했다는 증거를 제공한다.
③ 겉보기에는 움직이지 않는 것처럼 보이지만, 나무와 따개비는 씨앗이나 유생의 형태로 퍼질 수 있다.
④ 기후 변화는 종들이 그들의 온도 요구를 충족하는 지역으로 이동하는 것을 지연시킨다.
⑤ 생물은 생존, 성장, 번식을 위해 더 나은 환경을 찾기 위해 태어난 곳을 떠나야 한다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying - but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
questions.summary_sentence: Success leading to a comfortable life that is difficult to (A)___________ may eventually create (B)___________ situations.
questions.explanation: 성공이 가져다주는 안락한 타성에 젖어 빠져나오기(escape) 힘든 상태가 되면, 결국 만족스럽지 못한(displeasing) 상황에 갇히게 된다는 내용이 적절합니다. 지문 마지막의 'ultimately unsatisfying'이 (B)의 displeasing과 연결됩니다.
options_translation: ① 정착하기 - 바람직하지 않은
② 탈출하기 - 불쾌한(즐겁지 않은)
③ 성취하기 - 부족한
④ 감사하기 - 받아들일 수 있는
⑤ 벗어나기 - 기분 좋은

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while ⓐ<u>walking</u>. Therefore, our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is ideally ⓑ<u>suited</u> to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a ⓒ<u>much</u> more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, ⓓ<u>allows</u> for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than ⓔ<u>those</u> of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: ⑤번의 those는 앞의 단수 명사인 their rate of speed를 지칭해야 하므로 단수형인 that으로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다. ① walking은 while (they are) walking의 분사구문으로 적절합니다. ② suited는 ideally와 함께 쓰여 '이상적으로 적합해진'의 수동 의미로 적절합니다. ③ much는 비교급 more limited를 강조하는 부사로 적절합니다. ④ allows는 주어인 pedestrian travel이 단수이므로 단수 동사로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ① The Evolution of Citizenship: From Ideas to Impact
② Born Leaders: Viewpoint of Leadership Development
③ The Limitations of Leadership: Why Not Everyone Can Lead
④ Mistake-Free Leadership: Unrealistic Expectations of Perfection
⑤ Being Leaders: How Leaders Are Made from Ordinary Beginnings
questions.explanation: 위대한 리더들도 시작은 평범한 학생이나 시민이었으며, 누구나 일상에서의 아이디어를 발전시켜 리더가 될 잠재력이 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '평범한 시작으로부터 어떻게 리더가 만들어지는가'라는 내용의 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 시민권의 진화: 아이디어에서 영향력까지
② 타고난 리더: 리더십 개발의 관점
③ 리더십의 한계: 왜 모두가 이끌 수 없는가
④ 실수 없는 리더십: 완벽함에 대한 비현실적인 기대
⑤ 리더가 되는 것: 어떻게 리더는 평범한 시작으로부터 만들어지는가

questions.question: 18. 다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은? [24년 3월 21번]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago. Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans; the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds." Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
options: ① Who proposed the idea that humans have five senses?
② What are some senses that Aristotle missed in humans?
③ How does the sense of smell function in vertebrates?
④ How can some snakes sense their prey?
⑤ How should we approach the study of senses in animals?
questions.explanation: 본문에서 척추동물이 냄새를 감지하는 '다른 감각 시스템'을 가지고 있다고 언급은 되어 있지만, 그 후각이 구체적으로 '어떻게' 작동하는지에 대한 원리나 과정은 설명되어 있지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 누가 인간이 5감을 가지고 있다는 아이디어를 제안했는가?
② 아리스토텔레스가 인간에게서 놓친 몇 가지 감각은 무엇인가?
③ 척추동물에서 후각은 어떻게 기능하는가?
④ 일부 뱀은 어떻게 먹잇감을 감지할 수 있는가?
⑤ 동물의 감각 연구에 우리는 어떻게 접근해야 하는가?

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 This idea가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 32번]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they support opposition. <u>This idea</u> can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① Bot Pittman's philosophy for hiring employees
② The attitude of supervisors who support dissent
③ A company culture that discourages employee voice
④ Strategies to encourage internal dissent from employees
⑤ A series of advertisements in a newspaper's business section
questions.explanation: 문맥상 'This idea'는 바로 앞 문장의 'most bosses even say that they support opposition(대부분의 상사들이 반대 의견을 지지한다고 말한다)'를 가리킵니다. 따라서 '반대 의견을 지지하는 관리자의 태도'가 가장 적절한 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 직원 채용에 관한 Bot Pittman의 철학
② 반대 의견을 지지하는 관리자의 태도
③ 직원의 목소리를 억제하는 기업 문화
④ 직원들의 내부 반대를 장려하기 위한 전략
⑤ 신문 비즈니스 섹션의 일련의 광고

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, _________________ for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to adopt the practices of those around you.
options: ① following the group is sometimes not helpful
② it is almost always good to go with the majority
③ doing what is thought to be sensible is meaningless
④ it is necessary to agree with the profit for the group
⑤ choosing a restaurant where no one waits in line is sensible
questions.explanation: 지문은 사람들이 무엇이 안전하고 신뢰할 수 있는지 판단할 때 '사회적 증거(social evidence)'를 찾는다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 진화론적 관점에서 다수가 하는 행동을 따르는 것이 생존 확률을 높인다는 맥락이므로 빈칸에는 '대세를 따르는 것이 거의 항상 좋다'는 의미의 2번이 적합합니다. 마지막 문장의 '주변 사람들의 관습을 따르는 것이 좋다'는 결론과도 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 집단을 따르는 것이 때때로 도움이 되지 않는다
② 대다수와 함께 가는 것이 거의 항상 좋다
③ 합리적이라고 생각되는 것을 하는 것은 의미가 없다
④ 집단의 이익에 동의하는 것이 필요하다
⑤ 줄을 서서 기다리는 사람이 없는 식당을 선택하는 것이 현명하다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "putting on the same clothes" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ① Strategies: Key to Maintaining Attention
② Learning Materials Dealing with Different Tests
③ Skilled Learners: Using Proper Learning Strategies
④ Approach Similar Settings to Become Skillful Learners
⑤ Need to Wear Appropriate Clothing for Different Events
questions.explanation: 이 글은 숙련된 학습자들이 상황(시험의 종류나 수업의 성격)에 따라 서로 다른 학습 전략을 유연하게 사용하는 능력을 갖추고 있음을 옷차림에 비유하여 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '숙련된 학습자: 적절한 학습 전략의 사용'을 의미하는 3번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 전략: 주의력을 유지하는 핵심
② 서로 다른 시험을 다루는 학습 자료
③ 숙련된 학습자: 적절한 학습 전략 사용하기
④ 숙련된 학습자가 되기 위해 유사한 환경에 접근하기
⑤ 서로 다른 행사에 적절한 의복을 입을 필요성

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places.
ordered_passages: (A) Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
(B) England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton.

(C) With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 사회 경제적 발전으로 인한 여가 시간 증가와 교통 수단의 발달을 언급합니다. (B)에서 영국 산업 혁명으로 인한 철도의 등장이 이러한 변화를 이끌었음을 구체화하며 블랙풀 등 해안 리조트의 탄생을 언급합니다. (C)에서는 철도의 보급으로 대형 호텔들이 생겨난 사례를 들고, (A)에서 나중에(Later) 항공 운송의 등장으로 관광이 전 세계로 확대되었다는 흐름으로 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. ⓐThis is achieved by showing them with human like facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. ⓑIn more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. ⓒHowever, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. ⓓChildren are negatively affected by modern animation that describes animals as people. ⓔA general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물 캐릭터를 인간처럼 묘사(의인화)하여 친숙하게 만드는 기법에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ⓓ는 '아이들이 동물을 사람으로 묘사하는 현대 애니메이션에 부정적인 영향을 받는다'는 내용으로, 의인화 기법의 특징과 효과를 설명하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: It is difficult for any of us to maintain a ⓐ<u>steady</u> level of attention throughout our working day. We all have body rhythms ⓑ<u>presented</u> by peaks and valleys of energy and alertness. You will achieve more, and feel confident as a ⓒ<u>advantage</u>, if you schedule your most demanding tasks at times when you are best able to cope with them. If you haven't thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to ⓓ<u>watch</u> yourself. Try to note the times when you are at your best. We are all ⓔ<u>similar</u>. For some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for others it may take a while to warm up.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 부분에서 어떤 사람은 아침 일찍 정점에 도달하고, 어떤 사람은 예열 시간이 필요하다고 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 사람마다 신체 리듬이 다르다는 것을 의미하므로, '유사하다'는 뜻인 ⓔ similar는 '다르다'는 의미의 different 등으로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① the qualifications of ideal boss
③ the method of persuading the dissenters
④ how to deal with objectors in a company
⑤ the importance of accepting staff's various views
questions.explanation: 본문은 많은 리더들이 표면적으로 반대 의견(dissent)을 장려하며, 하급 직원들의 내부적인 항의를 계속해서 부추긴다고 주장한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 특히 Bot Pittman의 인용구를 통해 반대자들의 말을 경청함으로써 무엇을 해야 할지 알 수 있다는 점을 강조하고 있으므로, 주제로는 '리더들의 반대 의견 장려'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이상적인 상사의 자격
② 리더들의 반대 의견 장려
③ 반대자들을 설득하는 방법
④ 회사 내 반대자들을 다루는 방법
⑤ 직원들의 다양한 견해를 수용하는 것의 중요성

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Like the fairy tale, Cinderella, we can also create magic. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with the change the challenge statement into positive statements. For example, if you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① The Power of Positive Words
② The Reason of Waking up Early
③ Write It Down, and It Will Disappear
④ The Scientific Explanation of the Magic
⑤ How to Deal with the Present Difficulties
questions.explanation: 이 글은 자신이 직면한 어려움을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸어 쓰는 행위가 생각과 행동의 변화를 일으키고 자신감을 주어 마치 '마법'과 같은 효과를 낸다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '긍정적인 말의 힘'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 긍정적인 말의 힘
② 일찍 일어나는 이유
③ 그것을 적어라, 그러면 사라질 것이다
④ 마법에 대한 과학적 설명
⑤ 현재의 난관에 대처하는 방법

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① 사람들은 어린아이들이 성인 스포츠 환경에 완전히 참여하는 것은 어렵거나 불가능할 수 있다는 사실을 알게 되었다.
② 성인용 스포츠 경기장에서 경기하기 위해서 어린아이들이 크고 무거운 장비를 다루는 방법을 배워야 한다.
③ 아이들을 위해 성인 스포츠 형태를 조정한 것의 한 예로 야구의 티볼이 있다.
④ 아이들을 위해 성인 스포츠 형태를 조정한 경기에서는 성인 경기보다 더 짧은 경기 시간이 주어지는 경우가 있다.
⑤ 테니스의 경우, 아이들에게 더욱 적합하도록 경기장, 공, 라켓을 조정했다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서는 아이들이 성인용 장비를 다루는 것이 너무 어렵고 성공 가능성이 낮기 때문에, 장비와 환경을 아이들에게 맞게 조정(adaptation)했다고 설명합니다. 아이들이 성인용 장비를 다루는 법을 배워야 한다는 내용은 본문의 취지와 반대됩니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to ⓐ<u>quit</u> painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to ⓑ<u>evaluate</u> your progress and to decide when to stop. Artists often want to ⓒ<u>remove</u> details from their paintings continuously. However, putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with ⓓ<u>refreshed</u> eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further ⓔ<u>improvement</u>.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 화가들은 자신의 작품에 계셍해서 세부 사항을 '추가'하고 싶어하는 경향이 있으며(keep on adding), 이것이 과하면 작품을 망친다는 내용이므로 ⓒ의 remove(제거하다)는 add(추가하다)로 바귈어야 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally ⓐ<u>sightless</u>. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or ⓑ<u>reinforced</u>; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they are ⓒ<u>incapable</u> of waking up the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably ⓓ<u>provides</u> the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems ⓔ<u>crucial</u> to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 수면 중에는 시각 정보가 들어오더라도 정상적으로 처리되지 않는다는 내용입니다. 정보가 '단축되거나 약화되어' 처리되지 않는다는 흐름이어야 하므로, '강화되다'라는 뜻의 ⓑ reinforced는 적절하지 않습니다. 'weakened'와 같은 표현이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and __________________________________. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① find it difficult to work with someone
② want to keep their annual salary confidential
③ think their careers as means for self-reliance
④ try to seek another resource of energy and satisfaction
⑤ regard their jobs as a source of their delight and happiness
questions.explanation: 자신의 일에서 깊은 의미를 찾는 사람들은 일상을 더 활기차고 만족스럽게 느끼며, 자신의 직업을 즐거움과 행복의 원천으로 여긴다는 내용이 이어지는 것이 흐름상 자연스럽습니다. 이어지는 내용에서도 일에서 만족을 느끼는 사람이 전체적인 삶에서도 더 행복할 가능성이 높다는 연구 결과를 제시하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 누군가와 함께 일하는 것을 어렵게 여긴다
② 그들의 연봉을 비밀로 유지하기를 원한다
③ 그들의 경력을 자립을 위한 수단으로 생각한다
④ 에너지와 만족의 또 다른 원천을 찾으려고 노력한다
⑤ 그들의 직업을 기쁨과 행복의 원천으로 간주한다

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they _________________________. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
options: ① persuaded the beginners not to get the skill
② tended to rate the value of their skill highly
③ could understand the difficulties of the newcomers
④ were able to explain the obtained skill more easily
⑤ began to underestimate the difficulty of the skill they acquired
questions.explanation: 지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)에 대한 설명으로, 전문가가 되면 그 기술을 배우는 것이 얼마나 어려운지 잊어버리게 된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 기술을 습득함에 따라 그 기술을 습득하는 난이도를 과소평가하게 된다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 초보자들에게 그 기술을 습득하지 말라고 설득했다
② 그들의 기술의 가치를 높게 평가하는 경향이 있었다
③ 초보자들의 어려움을 이해할 수 있었다
④ 획득한 기술을 더 쉽게 설명할 수 있었다
⑤ 그들이 습득한 기술의 난이도를 과소평가하기 시작했다

questions.question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(B) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.

(C) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 인간과 동물의 오감에 대해 설명합니다. (C)에서 철학자 Macpherson이 이에 의문을 제기하며, 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 인간의 감각들(자기 몸 지각, 균형 감각 등)을 언급하며 반박합니다. 이어지는 (A)에서는 인간 외에 다른 동물들이 가진, 분류하기 더 어려운 독특한 감각들(뱀의 열 감지 등)의 사례를 추가로 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 사례들을 바탕으로 감각을 몇 가지 종류로 명확히 나눌 수 없으며, 감각 자체로 연구해야 한다는 결론으로 마무리하는 (C)-(A)-(B) 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. (A) They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. (B) As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. (C) All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. (D) In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. (E) The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.insertion_sentence: Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '상식이 우세해졌다: 다양한 스포츠가 아이들을 위해 개조되었다'라는 내용입니다. (A)까지는 성인용 경기장에서 아이들이 겪는 어려움에 대해 설명하고 있고, (B)부터는 야구, 축구 등 구체적으로 개조된 사례가 시작됩니다. 따라서 문제 제기 이후 해결책(개조)이 시작되는 지점인 (B)에 주어진 문장이 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; (A)___________, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. (B)___________, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 동물들이 서로 똑같지 않다고 했으므로, 그 결과(인과) 치유 과정에서도 똑같이 반응하지 않는다는 내용이 이어지기에 'hence(따라서)'가 적합합니다. (B) 환경적 요인에 따른 차이 예시에 이어 질병의 종류(신체적 vs 정서적)에 따른 차이라는 추가적인 예시를 들고 있으므로 'Moreover(게다가)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 따라서 - 게다가
② 요약하자면 - 그러므로
③ 그러므로 - 반대로
④ 대조적으로 - 추가적으로
⑤ 그럼에도 불구하고 - 동시에

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail.
options: ① Walking is a great way to improve both physical and mental well-being.
② The pace of life influences everything from our daily routines to our stress levels.
③ The progress of technology has transformed both movement and transportation, altering the way we travel.
④ Perception of detail is influenced by travel speed, with pedestrians having a better awareness of details than motorists.
⑤ Pedestrians are more attentive to their environment, while motorists solely concentrate on the advancement of technology.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력에 큰 영향을 미친다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 인간의 감각은 걷는 속도에 최적화되어 있어, 빠른 자동차 운전자보다 느린 보행자가 환경의 세부적인 디자인이나 요소를 더 잘 인식할 수 있다는 것이 핵심입니다.
options_translation: ① 걷기는 신체적, 정신적 웰빙을 모두 개선하는 좋은 방법이다.
② 삶의 속도는 일상적인 루틴부터 스트레스 수치까지 모든 것에 영향을 미친다.
③ 기술의 발전은 이동과 교통을 변화시켜 우리가 여행하는 방식을 바꾸어 놓았다.
④ 세부 사항에 대한 인식은 이동 속도에 영향을 받으며, 보행자가 운전자보다 세부 사항에 대해 더 잘 인식한다.
⑤ 보행자는 자신의 환경에 더 주의를 기울이는 반면, 운전자는 오로지 기술의 발전에만 집중한다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike, Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. ⓐEnvironmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. ⓑFor instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. ⓒIn addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. ⓓGood animal welfare requires disease prevention and appropriate shelter. ⓔWith this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물의 개별적 특성과 환경적 요인, 그리고 질환의 성격에 따라 치유 세션에 대한 반응이 다르므로 맞춤형 치료가 필요하다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ⓓ의 '질병 예방과 적절한 쉼터가 좋은 동물 복지에 필요하다'는 내용은 동물 치료 세션의 개별화라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어난 일반적인 복지 이야기입니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and told the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① Absence of horses available led the Inca Empire to utilize foot messengers in delivering messages.
② Chasquis dwelled in huts, forming groups consisting of four to six individuals.
③ When Chasquis spotted another messenger coming, they rushed out to meet them.
④ The Inca people built their huts in high areas where they could see each other.
⑤ Chasquis delivered the message to the approaching messenger only through gestures and signals.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 전령(Chasqui)이 다음 오두막에 가까워지면 소리를 지르기 시작하여 마중 나오는 사람에게 메시지를 서너 번 '말했다(told the message three or four times)'고 언급되어 있습니다. 몸짓과 신호로만 전달했다는 ⑤번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 이용 가능한 말이 없었기 때문에 잉카 제국은 메시지 전달에 도보 전령을 활용하게 되었다.
② Chasquis는 오두막에 거주하며 4~6명으로 구성된 그룹을 형성했다.
③ Chasquis는 다른 전령이 오는 것을 발견하면 그를 맞이하러 달려 나갔다.
④ 잉카 사람들은 서로를 볼 수 있는 높은 지역에 오두막을 지었다.
⑤ Chasquis는 다가오는 전령에게 오직 몸짓과 신호만을 통해 메시지를 전달했다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to ⓐ<u>combine</u> into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds ⓑ<u>organize</u> themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on the ⓒ<u>speed</u> at which the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally ⓓ<u>invisible</u>. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be ⓔ<u>small</u>. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
questions.explanation: 마그마가 천천히 식으면 원자들이 결합하여 '더 큰 결정(larger crystals)'을 형성할 충분한 시간을 갖게 됩니다. 따라서 결정은 일반적으로 '눈에 보일 정도로 크게(visible)' 형성됩니다. invisible(보이지 않는)은 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has been so prevalent that ________________________________________. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① various sports have modified their approaches to be suitable for children
② young athletes believed that practice was their only way to survive
③ competition has been highlighted over collaboration in the sports field
④ sports coaches argued that children should practice with adults
⑤ sports authorities have purchased advanced sports equipment
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린아이들이 성인용 장비나 경기장에서 스포츠를 하는 것의 어려움을 인식하고, 이를 아이들에게 맞게 조정한 사례(티볼, 플래그 풋볼, 주니어 축구, 어린이용 테니스 등)를 나열하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '다양한 스포츠가 아이들에게 적합하도록 방식을 수정해 왔다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다양한 스포츠가 어린이들에게 적합하도록 접근 방식을 수정해 왔다
② 젊은 선수들은 연습만이 생존할 수 있는 유일한 길이라고 믿었다
③ 스포츠 분야에서 협력보다 경쟁이 강조되어 왔다
④ 스포츠 코치들은 아이들이 성인들과 함께 연습해야 한다고 주장했다
⑤ 스포츠 당국은 고급 스포츠 장비를 구입했다

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "putting on the same clothes"가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "<u>putting on the same clothes</u>" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ① wearing different attire for different occasions
② grasping the need for flexibility and adaptability
③ seeking to dress in a more conservative manner
④ adopting a uniform approach in every academic setting
⑤ employing a one-size-fits-all strategy to tackle urgent issues
questions.explanation: 이 글은 모든 학습 상황(강의, 시험 등)에 똑같은 방식(고무인 도장 방식)을 적용하는 것을 지양해야 한다는 내용입니다. '같은 옷을 입는다'는 비유는 모든 학업적 상황에서 동일한 접근 방식을 사용하는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 상황에 맞춰 다른 의복을 입는 것
② 유연성과 적응성의 필요성을 파악하는 것
⑧ 더 보수적인 방식으로 옷을 입으려고 노력하는 것
④ 모든 학업 상황에서 획일적인 접근 방식을 채택하는 것
⑤ 긴급한 문제를 해결하기 위해 만능 전략을 사용하는 것

questions.question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth.
ordered_passages: (A) According to this research, sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites.
(B) Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong.
(C) Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 과거의 잘못된 이론인 '혀의 부위별 맛 지도'를 설명합니다. (B)에서 'however'를 통해 이 지도가 틀렸음을 입증한 1980-90년대 연구를 소개합니다. (A)에서 'this research(이 연구)'를 지칭하며 모든 부위에서 맛을 느낄 수 있다는 구체적인 연구 결과를 설명합니다. (C)에서는 'Moreover(게다가)'를 사용해 맛을 느끼는 메커니즘이 장소가 아닌 시간의 문제라는 추가 정보를 제시하며 결론을 맺습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster - in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
options: ① Why Change Isn't Always Needed
② Just Staying the Same Doesn't Work
③ Fast Rabbits, Slow Foxes: The Mystery of Evolution
④ Stopping the Chase: Why Running Slower Is Better
⑤ Survival' Endless Race: How Animals Evolve to Keep Up
questions.explanation: 이 글은 여우와 토끼의 예시를 통해 생물들이 상대적인 경쟁 속에서 제자리를 유지하기 위해(살아남기 위해) 끊임없이 진화해야 한다는 '붉은 여왕 효과'를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '생존을 위한 끝없는 경주'를 언급한 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 변화가 항상 필요한 것은 아닌 이유
② 그냥 똑같이 머물러 있는 것은 효과가 없다
③ 빠른 토끼, 느린 여우: 진화의 미스터리
④ 추격 멈추기: 왜 더 천천히 달리는 것이 더 나은가
⑤ 생존의 끝없는 경주: 동물들이 뒤처지지 않기 위해 진화하는 법

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① Role of Reproduction in Living Creatures
② Species Vanishing Due to Climate Change
③ Species Mobility: Adapting to Climate Shifts
④ Effective Strategies for Addressing Climate Change
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화에 따라 생물종들이 생존 가능한 환경을 찾아 이동해야 하며, 움직이지 못해 보이는 식물들조차도 씨앗 등의 형태로 이동 능력을 갖추고 기후 변화에 적응해왔다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '종의 이동성: 기후 변화에 적응하기'가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 생물에 있어서 번식의 역할
② 기후 변화로 인해 사라지는 종들
③ 종의 이동성: 기후 변화에 적응하기
④ 기후 변화에 대처하기 위한 효과적인 전략

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic ⓐ<u>projected</u> onto animals is their ability to speak human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with facial features that are similar to ⓑ<u>those</u> of humans and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more animated movies the trend has been ⓒ<u>to show</u> the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still exhibit human behaviors like ⓓ<u>using</u> front legs as hands and conveying emotions through facial expressions. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more ⓔ<u>attractively</u>, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장에서 'make + 목적어(the animal characters) + 목적격 보어'의 구조가 쓰였습니다. 보어 자리에는 부사가 올 수 없으므로, attractively를 형용사인 attractive로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture ⓐ<u>which</u> prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even, say ⓑ<u>that</u> they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, ⓒ<u>published</u> weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim ⓓ<u>what</u> they continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you ⓔ<u>what</u> you must do to get something done."
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 절 'regularly claim [that/what] they continually encourage internal protest...'에서 claim의 목적어절은 뒤에 주어(they), 동사(encourage), 목적어(internal protest)를 모두 갖춘 완전한 문장입니다. 따라서 선행사를 포함하고 불완전한 절을 이끄는 관계대명사 what이 아니라, 접속사 that이 쓰여야 합니다. (참고: ⓔ의 경우 지문 원문상 is로 쓰여야 하나, 이 문제에서는 ⓓ가 명확하게 틀린 것으로 제시되었습니다.)

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
options: ① advantages and disadvantages of formal art education in school
② how to assess your painting by focusing on one spot at a time
③ importance of avoiding overwork and knowing when to stop in painting
④ effects of taking occasional breaks on increasing productivity and creativity
⑤ why artists should maintain work-life balance to create masterpieces of their time
questions.explanation: 이 글은 그림을 그릴 때 한 부분에만 집중하기보다 전체적으로 작업하여 언제든 멈출 수 있게 하고, 과도하게 작업하여 작품을 망치는 것을 경계하며 적절한 시점에 멈추는 것의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 학교 정규 미술 교육의 장단점
② 한 번에 한 곳에 집중하여 그림을 평가하는 방법
③ 그림 그리기에서 과도한 작업을 피하고 멈출 때를 아는 것의 중요성
④ 가끔 휴식을 취하는 것이 생산성과 창의성 증대에 미치는 영향
⑤ 예술가들이 당대의 걸작을 만들기 위해 일과 삶의 균형을 유지해야 하는 이유

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
questions.summary_sentence: The shift in selling philosophy emphasized the necessity for businesses to (A)__________ connections with customers and to meet their desires, (B)__________ the belief that production alone would generate demand.
questions.explanation: 판매 철학의 변화로 인해 기업들은 고객과의 유대 관계를 구축(cultivate)하고 고객의 요구를 충족시키는 것이 필수적이 되었으며, 이는 생산이 스스로 수요를 창출한다는 기존의 믿음에 도전(challenging/반박)하는 마케팅 혁명을 가져왔다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 구축하다 / 도전하는(반박하는)
② 무시하다 / 붕괴시키는
③ 육성하다 / 강화하는
④ 확립하다 / 수용하는
⑤ 무시하다 / 보완하는

questions.question: 21. 다음 글(I)의 내용을 바탕으로 아래와 같이 대화문(II)을 작성하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce better performance and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who were satisfied with their jobs were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.↓<II>A: Hey, did you know that meaningful work has a significant effect on our lives?B: Really? How so?A: Well, according to Sonya Lyubomirsky's research, people who find fulfillment and empowerment in their (A)__________ tend to produce a greater output and earn higher incomes.B: That's interesting. So, people who find meaning in their professions not only (B)__________ better but also earn more money, right?A: Exactly! But it's not just about money. Jessica Pryce-Jones' study showed that those who find (C)__________ in their jobs are 150 percent more likely to have overall happier lives.B: Thanks for sharing that. I'll have to keep that in mind. It really emphasizes the (D)__________ of finding fulfillment in what we do.
subjective_conditions: (A)~(D)는 각각 다른 1단어로 완성할 것
위 본문(I)에 있는 단어만을 이용할 것
필요한 경우 품사나 어형을 변형할 것
questions.answer: (A) careers (또는 jobs)(B) perform(C) satisfaction (또는 fulfillment)(D) importance (또는 meaning)
questions.explanation: (A) 본문의 'careers'를 활용하여 직업에서의 성취감을 나타냅니다.(B) 본문의 'performance'를 동사형인 'perform'으로 변형하여 더 나은 성과를 낸다는 의미를 완성합니다.(C) 본문의 'satisfied'를 명사형인 'satisfaction'으로 변형하거나 'fulfillment'를 사용하여 일에서의 만족감을 나타냅니다.(D) 본문의 'important'를 명사형인 'importance'로 변형하여 성취감을 찾는 것의 중요성을 강조합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

questions.explanation: 자신의 직업에서 깊은 의미를 찾은 사람들은 그들의 하루가 활력이 넘치고(energizing) 즐거움과 자부심의 원천이라고 느끼는 것이 맥락상 적절합니다. 따라서 부정적인 의미인 'frustrating(좌절감을 주는)'은 문맥상 어색합니다. (satisfying 등 긍정적인 단어가 적절함)

questions.question: 10. 윗글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. ⓐStimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. ⓑSleep loss not only adversely affects our health, it also costs us and the economy. ⓒPerceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. ⓓBut as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. ⓔNevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잠자는 동안 외부 자극에 반응하지 않는 '지각적 단절(perceptual disengagement)'의 특성과 그 기능에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓑ는 수면 부족이 건강과 경제에 미치는 부정적인 영향에 대해 말하고 있으므로 흐름에서 벗어납니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, prepare yourself to ______________________. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ② feel the enchantment of hesitation
③ experience a sense of awe and self-doubt
④ anticipate undesirable and unexpected consequences
⑤ observe a transformation filled with wonder and self-assurance

경이로움과 자신감으로 가득 찬 변화를 관찰하다

questions.question: 15. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말 뜻에 맞게 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 모두 활용하여 영작하시오. (단, 필요시 변형할 것)
questions.passage: Before you consider the following, (A)<u>얼마나 많은 감각이 있는지 너 자신에게 질문하라</u>. Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
subjective_conditions: 필요시 변형할 것
questions.answer: ask yourself how many senses there are
questions.explanation: '질문하라'는 명령형이므로 동사 원형인 ask로 시작합니다. 간접 목적어로 '너 자신에게'에 해당하는 yourself를 쓰고, 직접 목적어로 '얼마나 많은 감각이 있는지'에 해당하는 의문사절 'how many senses there are'를 어순에 맞게 배열합니다. '있다'의 의미를 위해 'there be' 구문을 사용하며, 주어가 복수형인 senses이므로 be동사는 are가 됩니다.

questions.question: 16. 윗글의 내용을 다음과 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (B), (C)에 들어갈 알맞은 표현을 주어진 철자로 시작하는 단어로 쓰시오.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글을 읽고, 감상문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 변형 없이 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.<Reflection>

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① The Impossibilities of Youth Sports
② What Protects Young Children from Competition?
③ Struggles of Youth Athletes in Competitive Sports
④ Adjusting Youth Sports Circumstances for Success
⑤ Adult Sports: Adapting the Environment for Juniors
questions.explanation: 본문은 어린 아이들이 성인용 스포츠 환경에서 겪는 어려움을 해결하기 위해 스포츠 장비, 경기장 크기, 팀 규모 등을 아이들의 연령과 신체 조건에 맞춰 조정(adaptations)했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 ④ '성공을 위한 청소년 스포츠 환경의 조정'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.

③ 경쟁적인 스포츠에서 청소년 선수들의 고군분투
④ 성공을 위해 청소년 스포츠 환경을 조정하기
⑤ 성인 스포츠: 주니어를 위해 환경을 조정하기

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
options: ① the ways to overcome jet lag
② the regional variations in popular sports
③ the activities that help adjust the biological clocks
④ the difficulties in flight control depending on direction
⑤ the influence the travel direction has on the recovery from jet lag
questions.explanation: 여행 방향(동쪽 혹은 서쪽)에 따라 시차 극복 속도와 스포츠 팀의 경기력에 차이가 생긴다는 내용이므로, 여행 방향이 시차 회복에 미치는 영향이 주제로 적절합니다.
