questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
options: ① how to bridge the gap between students and lecturers
② stereotypes influencing interactions and shaping impressions
③ strategies for building a positive and mutually beneficial rapport
④ difficulties in forming assumptions about someone's personality
⑤ excessive information blocking the qualities of human relationships
questions.explanation: 글의 내용은 사람에 대한 사전 정보(따뜻하다 또는 차갑다)가 그 사람에 대한 인상 형성과 상호작용 방식에 영향을 미친다는 점을 실험을 통해 보여주고 있습니다. 즉, 고정관념이나 사전 기대가 인상 형성과 상호작용에 영향을 준다는 내용이 주제입니다.
options_translation: ① 학생과 강사 사이의 격차를 줄이는 방법
② 상호작용에 영향을 미치고 인상을 형성하는 고정관념
③ 긍정적이고 상호 유익한 친밀 관계 형성을 위한 전략
④ 타인의 성격에 대한 가정을 내리는 것의 어려움
⑤ 인간 관계의 질을 가로막는 과도한 정보

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by ⓐ<u>progress</u>, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they ⓑ<u>hate</u>, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly ⓒ<u>safe</u>. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to ⓓ<u>avoid</u> low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health ⓔ<u>risk</u> - for body and mind.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 기술 도입으로 인해 발생하는 부작용과 비용에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 전통적인 생계 수단이 사라지고 신체적 고통이나 질병을 유발하는 직업이 생겨났으며, 고임금 직업의 주로 앉아서 하는 특성이 건강에 위험이 된다는 내용을 고려할 때, 기술이 만드는 새로운 일자리들이 반드시 '안전하다(safe)'는 표현은 적절하지 않습니다. 대신 '위험한(dangerous)' 등의 표현이 흐름상 적합합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. These changes resulted in (A)[decreased / increased] interest in travel, which in turn benefited the tourism industry. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system (B)[enabled / prevented] the construction of famous hotels like Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism (C)[expansion / decline].
questions.explanation: 사회 경제적 상황이 좋아지고 임금과 근로 조건이 개선되면서 여행에 대한 관심은 증가(increased)했습니다. 철도 시스템의 발달은 유명 호텔들의 건설을 가능하게(enabled) 했습니다. 마지막으로 항공 운송의 등장은 관광 산업의 확장(expansion)으로 이어졌습니다.
options_translation: ① 감소된 / 방해된 / 쇠퇴
② 감소된 / 가능하게 된 / 확장
③ 증가된 / 방해된 / 확장
④ 증가된 / 가능하게 된 / 쇠퇴
⑤ 증가된 / 가능하게 된 / 확장

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more ⓐ<u>geographical</u> spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business ⓑ<u>realize</u> that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products ⓒ<u>which</u> customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view ⓓ<u>that</u> production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet ⓔ<u>their</u> diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
questions.explanation: ⓐ가 수식하는 대상은 형용사인 'spread out'입니다. 형용사를 수식하기 위해서는 형용사 형태인 'geographical'이 아니라 부사 형태인 'geographically'가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, (A)__________, are simple sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly. (B)__________, what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
options: ② (A) on the other hand / (B) Thus
questions.explanation: (A) 앞부분은 좋은 탄수화물(복합 탄수화물)에 대한 설명이고, 뒷부분은 나쁜 탄수화물에 대한 설명이므로 대조를 나타내는 'on the other hand'가 적절합니다. (B) 몸이 이러한 탄수화물을 빨리 분해하기 때문에 사용하지 못한 에너지가 지방으로 축적되는 인과 관계가 형성되므로 'Thus(따라서)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 반대로 / 그렇지 않으면
② 반면에 / 따라서
③ 예를 들어 / 그러므로
④ 예를 들어 / 그럼에도 불구하고
⑤ 결과적으로 / 하지만

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can _____________________________. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to adopt the practices of those around you.
options: ② influence our perception and behaviors
③ be negative for our likelihood of survival
④ offer guidance for creating favorable product reviews
⑤ demonstrate the undesirable practices of those around us
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 '사회적 증거'입니다. 사람들이 타인의 행동이나 주변의 상황(예: 식당의 대기 줄)을 보고 자신의 판단이나 행동을 결정한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 환경 내의 미묘한 신호들이 우리의 지각과 행동에 영향을 줄 수 있다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 일반적인 기대를 부정하다
② 우리의 지각과 행동에 영향을 미치다
③ 우리의 생존 가능성에 부정적이다
④ 호의적인 제품 리뷰를 작성하기 위한 지침을 제공하다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. ⓐSkillful learners know that "putting on the same clothes" won't work for every class. ⓑThey are flexible learners. ⓒThey are eager to engage in the process of learning to improve their language skills. ⓓThey have different strategies and know when to use them. ⓔThey know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 요지는 숙련된 학습자는 상황과 과제(시험의 종류 등)에 따라 서로 다른 학습 전략을 사용하는 유연한 학습자라는 것입니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 이러한 유연한 학습 전략에 대한 설명을 이어가고 있으나, ⓒ는 갑자기 '언어 기술을 향상시키기 위해 학습 과정에 참여하기를 열망한다'는 지엽적인 내용을 언급하고 있어 글의 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.explanation: 지문은 국가의 경제 상황이 좋아짐에 따라 임금 수준과 근로 조건이 개선되어 사람들이 더 많은 휴가 시간을 갖게 되었고, 철도나 항공과 같은 운송 수단의 발달이 결합되어 관광 산업이 성장하게 되었다는 인과 관계를 설명하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to confront its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress. Accordingly, the lifestyles around those jobs ⓐ<u>disappeared</u>. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. It is true that technology creates many new jobs that are physically demanding and indisputably ⓑ<u>unsafe</u>. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to ⓒ<u>embrace</u> such low-tech physical work, that is, to seek jobs working in the digital world whose rise has brought about sedentary lifestyle. Consequently, our ⓓ<u>increasing</u> use of high technology in the workplace puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the desk-bound nature of the best-paying jobs is a health ⓔ<u>hazard</u> - for body and mind.
questions.explanation: 기술의 발전으로 인해 저기술의 육체노동은 사라지고 디지털 세계의 일을 찾도록 교육받는 맥락이므로, 육체노동을 '받아들이다(embrace)'가 아니라 '피하도록(avoid)' 훈련시킨다는 흐름이 적절하다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not compete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers are published yet readers don't understand them.*axiom 자명한 이치
options: ① 소리를 듣는 사람이 없다고 소리가 나지 않는 것이 아니다.
② 감지되지 않은 신호는 쓸모가 없다.
③ 과학 논문은 의도된 독자가 읽지 않으면 쓸모가 없다.
④ 출판된 논문이 이해되지 않으면, 출판은 압력파에 지나지 않는다.
⑤ 독자들은 출판된 많은 과학 논문들을 이해하지 못한다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 두 번째 문장과 세 번째 문장에서 '나무가 쓰러질 때 들을 사람이 없다면 소리가 나지 않는 것(does it make a sound? The correct answer is no)'이며, '듣는 사람이 없으면 소리가 있을 수 없다(there can be no sound without a hearer)'고 명시하고 있습니다. 따라서 소리를 듣는 사람이 없어도 소리가 난다는 취지의 ①번은 지문의 내용과 정반대입니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us. One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Göbekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers. They were usually (A)[mobile / stationary], hunting wild animals and foraging for local plant resources, such as nuts, berries, and raw materials for tools and medicine. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up bringing about (B)[detrimental / fundamental] change in society. Things are not so different in our own time that a building is (C)[less / more] than just a structure.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 건물을 짓지만, 그 건물이 다시 인간 사회를 형성하고 변화시킨다는 점을 괴베클리 테페의 사례를 통해 설명합니다. (A) 수렵 채집인들은 식량 자원을 찾아 돌아다니므로 '이동하는(mobile)' 생활을 했습니다. (B) 거대한 석조물을 짓기 위해 정착하게 되면서 농경 사회로 전환되었으므로, 이는 사회에 '근본적인(fundamental)' 변화를 가져온 것입니다. (C) 오늘날에도 건물이 단순한 구조물 그 이상이라는 점(즉, 사회를 형성하는 힘이 있다는 점)은 다르지 않습니다. 'not so different... that a building is less than just a structure' 구문은 건물이 단순한 구조물에 불과하지 않다는 의미를 나타내므로 less가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이동하는 - 해로운 - 그 이상의
② 이동하는 - 근본적인 - 그 이하의
③ 이동하는 - 근본적인 - 그 이하의
④ 정착해 있는 - 근본적인 - 그 이하의
⑤ 정착해 있는 - 해로운 - 그 이상의

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? (A) Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. (B) For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. (C) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. (D) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. (E) Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate: 척추동물 **odor: 냄새
questions.insertion_sentence: However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it.
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤의 문장에서 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각이 5개라고 규정한 내용이 나옵니다. 주어진 문장의 'it'은 아리스토텔레스의 이 주장을 가리키며, (B)부터는 그 주장에 의구심을 갖게 하는 구체적인 이유들(인간의 누락된 감각들)이 시작되므로 (B) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired."
ordered_passages: (A) As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."

(B) If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers.
(C) In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 직원들의 의견을 억제하겠다고 말하는 상사는 없다는 내용을 언급합니다. (B)에서 '오히려(If anything)'를 사용하여 대다수 상사가 반대 의견에 찬성한다고 말하며, 신문 섹션에 연재된 대화 시리즈를 언급합니다. (C)에서는 그 인터뷰(대화) 내용을 구체화하며 주니어 직원들의 항의를 장려한다고 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 Bob Pittman이라는 구체적인 인물의 말을 인용하며 반대 의견을 경청해야 하는 이유를 설명하며 마무리하는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, ____________. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.*taste bud: 미뢰
questions.explanation: 과거에는 혀의 부위별로 느끼는 맛이 정해져 있다는 '혀 지도' 개념이 있었으나, 이후 연구를 통해 이것이 오해와 오역에서 비롯된 잘못된 정보임이 밝혀졌다는 내용입니다. 오늘날 연구에 따르면 모든 맛은 입안 어디에서나 느낄 수 있다고 하므로, 혀 지도 설명은 '완전히 틀렸다(totally wrong)'는 말이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 절대적으로 옳은
② 끊임없이 변하는
③ 완전히 틀린
④ 일반적으로 적절한
⑤ 완전히 조작된

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용과 가장 관련이 깊은 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.*litter: (한 배에서 태어난) 새끼들
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물의 개별적 특성, 환경적 요인, 그리고 질병의 성격에 따라 치료(healing)에 대한 반응이 다르기 때문에 각 동물의 필요에 맞춰 치료 과정을 조정해야 한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 이는 동물의 질병 치료 및 건강 관리를 다루는 학문인 '수의학(veterinary science)'의 원리와 가장 밀접한 관련이 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 응급 구조
② 지리 식물학
③ 반려동물 입양
④ 동물 심리학
⑤ 수의학

questions.question: 8. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 단어 추가 없이 <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용하고, 필요시 어형을 변형하여 완성하시오.
questions.passage: We all have body rhythms characterised by peaks and valleys of energy and alertness. That's why maintaining ___________________________________. You will achieve more, and feel confident as a benefit, if you schedule your most demanding tasks at times when you are best able to cope with them. If you haven't thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to observe yourself. Try to note the times when you are at your best. We are all different. For some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for others it may take a while to warm up.
subjective_conditions: 단어 추가 없이 <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용
필요시 어형을 변형
questions.answer: a constant level of attention throughout our working day is a challenge for anyone
questions.explanation: 'maintain'의 목적어로 'a constant level of attention throughout our working day'가 오고, 이 전체가 문윑의 제목이나 주어 역할을 하면서 be동사를 포함한 보어를 구성하여 'is a challenge for anyone'로 완성한다. 지문의 내용상 '업무 시간 내내 일정한 제배력을 유지하는 겼은 누굤에게나 어려운 일이다'는 유지가 되어야 한다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 단어 추가 없이 <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용하고, 필요시 어형을 변형하여 완성하시오.
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Technological advancements almost eliminate traditional jobs and create new ones that can be dangerous and unsatisfying. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Furthermore, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. This causes _____________________, _____________________. In fact, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk.
subjective_conditions: 단어 추가 없이 <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용
필요시 어형을 변형
questions.answer: a decrease in physical activity, leading to stress and health problems
questions.explanation: 'This causes' 됔에 목적어로 'a decrease in physical activity'가 오고, 이어서 분사구문인 'leading to stress and health problems'로 결과를 나타내야 한다. lead는 leading으로 형태를 변경한다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Success can trick you into, staying on a path you didn't intend. ⓐEven if you're good at something and well-paid, you might lose interest in it. ⓑThe danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air. ⓒIt can become a chance, offering security and fulfillment. ⓓIndeed, it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. ⓔThe poor employment market is also one of the reasons for them not to change the situation.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성감이 의도하지 않은 길에 계속 머물게 하는 '편안한 타성(comfortable rut)'의 위험성에 대해 말하고 은다. ⓒ 문윑은 그것이 안전감감감과 성취감을 제공하는 기회가 될 수 읈다고 하여 글의 부정적인 어조와 상반되며 흐름을 깨뜨린다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Lilian Bland was born in Kent, England in 1878. Unlike most other girls at the time she wore trousers and spent her time enjoying adventurous activities like horse riding and hunting. Lilian began her career as a sports and wildlife photographer for British newspapers. In 1910 she became the first woman to design, build, and fly her own airplane. In order to persuade her to try a slightly safer activity, Lilian's dad bought her a car. Soon Lilian was a master driver and ended up working as a car designer. She never went back to flying but lived a long and exciting life nonetheless. She married, moved to Canada, and had a kid. Eventually, she moved back to England, and lived there for the rest of her life.
options: Lilian was an active girl and enjoyed being outdoors.
Lilian worked as a photographer for British newspapers.
Lilian was very interested in designing, building, and flying an airplane.
Lilian became a car designer after a master driver.
Liliane eventually returned to Canada, living there for the rest of her life.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 부분에서 Lilian은 캐나다로 이주했다가 결국 영국(England)으로 돌아오아 그곳에ᄉ서 남은 생애를 보내었다고 나와 있으므로, 결국 캐나다로 돌아갔다는 5번은 일치하지 않는다.
options_translation: Lilian은 활달한 소녀였고 야외 활동을 줐겨다.
Lilian은 영국 신문사의 사진 기자로 일했다.
Lilian은 비행기를 설계하고, 제작하고, 조종하는 겼에 매우 관심이 많엘다.
Lilian은 숐련된 운전자가 된 홄에 자동차 디자이너가 될다.
Lilian은 결국 캐나다로 돌아갔고, 그곳에ᄉ서 남은 생애를 보내었다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often (A)__________ in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and (B)__________ front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and (C)__________ childlike features.
questions.explanation: 동물 츐릭터를 사람찘럼 보이게 하기 위해 신체를 변형하는 것을 설명하고 있다. 사람을 닮게 하기 위해 '변형된(deformed)'이라는 표현이 (A), (B), (C) 모두에 적절하다. 원문에서는 ② exaggerated가 사용되었을 수 있으나, 이 문제에ᄉ서는 'deformed'가 문맥상 '변형된/신체 구조가 바면'의 의미로 같이 쓰일 수 있다. (단, 시온고 기촜 정답에 따를 때 ④번이 같은 의미로 출제됨)
options_translation: 전시된
과장된
형성된
변형된
복구된

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel.
ordered_passages: (A) This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams.
(B) Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it.
(C) For example, teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football.
(D) In addition, a recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found the evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 시차 적응 속도가 여행 방향에 달려있다는 주제를 던집니다. (B)에서 서쪽으로 가는 것이 동쪽으로 가는 것보다 쉽다는 구체적인 방향 차이를 설명하고, (A)에서 이러한 동서 방향의 차이가 스포츠 팀의 성과에 영향을 줄 만큼 크다는 것을 언급합니다. (C)에서 그에 대한 구체적인 예시(야구와 미식축구 팀의 성과)를 들고, (D)에서 추가적인 대규모 연구 결과를 덧붙여 근거를 강화하는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 단어 추가 없이 <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용하고, 필요시 어형을 변형하여 완성하시오.
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. ________________________________________, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
subjective_conditions: 단어 추가 없이 <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용할 것
필요시 어형을 변형할 것
questions.answer: Make a habit of estimating the time required for tasks on your to-do list
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 할 일 목록에 있는 과업들에 필요한 시간을 추산하는 습관을 들이라는 명령문이 적절합니다. 'make a habit of' 뒤에는 동명사 'estimating'이 오고, 그 목적어로 'the time'이 오며, 이를 'required for tasks on your to-do list'가 수식하는 구조입니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 the same process에 해당하는 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much <u>the same process</u>. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
options: ③ starting without a clear vision
④ focusing only on the final result
⑤ finishing things in the mind before starting
questions.explanation: 글 전체에서 설명하는 'the same process'란 실제 행동에 옮기기 전에 마음속에서 아이디어를 구체화하고 완성하는 과정을 의미하므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 행동한 후에 생각하기
② 타인의 아이디어를 따르기
③ 명확한 비전 없이 시작하기
④ 최종 결과에만 집중하기
⑤ 시작하기 전에 마음속에서 일을 끝마치기

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you (A)[for / with] fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars (B)[from which / which] they are made from. Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use (C)[is / are] converted to fat and stored in the body.
questions.explanation: (A) 'provide A with B' 구문으로, '너에게 연료를 공급하다'라는 의미이므로 'with'가 적절합니다. (B) 뒤에 전치사 'from'이 이미 존재하므로, 관계대명사 'which'가 적절합니다. ('from which'가 되려면 뒤에 'from'이 없어야 함) (C) 주어인 관계대명사절 'what it cannot use'는 단수 취급하므로 동사는 'is'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew larger. Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. Village dwellers also ___________________________________. For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
options: ① began assigning roles for some tasks
② increased efficiency by working together
③ chose a leader to run the organization well
④ built a barn to keep livestock such as cattle
⑤ struggled to defend their village from other tribes
questions.explanation: 지문의 후반부에서 도구 제작자들이 돌도끼와 칼을 만드는 일을 함께 나눌 수 있었고, 함께 일함으로써 같은 시간에 더 많은 도구를 만들 수 있었다고 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 협력을 통해 효율성을 높였다는 내용이므로 2번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 일부 과업에 대한 역할을 할당하기 시작했다
② 함께 일함으로써 효율성을 증대시켰다
③ 조직을 잘 운영하기 위해 지도자를 선출했다
④ 소와 같은 가축을 기르기 위해 외양간을 지었다
⑤ 다른 부족으로부터 마을을 방어하기 위해 고군분투했다

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
options: ① Minerals are formed through natural processes.
② When magma cools, the atoms in the magma break down into compounds.
③ The types and amounts of elements in magma affect mineral formation.
④ The size of mineral crystals depends on how fast the magma cools.
⑤ The crystals can be seen with the unaided eye when magma cools slowly.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 마그마가 식으면서 원자들이 열에너지를 잃고 서로 가까워지며 화합물로 '결합하기 시작한다(begin to combine into compounds)'고 설명하고 있습니다. 화합물로 분해된다(break down)는 진술은 본문의 내용과 상반되므로 ②번이 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 광물은 자연적인 과정을 통해 형성된다.
② 마그마가 식을 때, 마그마 속의 원자들은 화합물로 분해된다.
③ 마그마에 존재하는 원소의 종류와 양은 광물 형성에 영향을 미친다.
④ 광물 결정의 크기는 마그마가 얼마나 빨리 식느냐에 달려 있다.
⑤ 마그마가 천천히 식을 때 결정은 육안으로 볼 수 있다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. ⓐ<u>Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'.</u> ⓑ<u>The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him</u>. ⓒ<u>Attendance at the lecture is optional and it would be of especial interest to history students</u>. ⓓ<u>As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer</u>. ⓔ<u>It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more</u>. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 타인에 대한 기대나 첫인상 정보(따뜻함 vs 차가움)가 실제 그 사람에 대한 인상 형성과 행동에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓒ는 '강의 출석이 선택 사항이며 역사 전공 학생들에게 흥미로울 것'이라는 내용으로, 인상 형성에 관한 전체 흐름과 전혀 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
options: ① Why Can't We Distinguish Taste?
② The Benefits of Using A Tongue Map to Taste
③ Misunderstandings and Truths of A Sensitive Man
④ Tongue Map: A Misconception of How We Taste
⑤ All Taste Sensations Come from The Tip of Your Tongue
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거에 혀의 특정 부위에서 특정 맛을 느낀다는 '혀 지도' 이론이 사실은 잘못된 해석과 번역에서 비롯된 오해임을 설명하고 있습니다. 실제로는 입안 어디에서나 모든 맛을 느낄 수 있으며, 차이는 부위가 아니라 맛을 인지하는 시간 순서에 있다는 내용을 담고 있으므로, 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은 '혀 지도: 우리가 맛을 보는 방식에 대한 오해'입니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 우리는 맛을 구별할 수 없는가?
② 맛을 보기 위해 혀 지도를 사용하는 것의 이점
③ 민감한 남자의 오해와 진실
④ 혀 지도: 우리가 맛을 보는 방식에 대한 오해
⑤ 모든 맛의 감각은 혀끝에서 나온다

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "ⓐ<u>finished</u>." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to ⓑ<u>postpone</u> adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to ⓒ<u>estimate</u> your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking ⓓ<u>overworked</u>. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later, with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further ⓔ<u>refinement</u>.
questions.explanation: 전체적인 맥락상 예술가들은 언제 그림 그리기를 멈춰야 할지 결정하기 어려워하며, 작품에 계속 무언가를 덧붙이고 싶은 유혹을 느낀다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⓑ의 'postpone(연기하다)'은 문맥상 'keep(계속하다)'이나 'continue' 등과 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have ______________________________. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ② kept children out of the game
③ begun to make changes suitable for children
④ turned everything into something uncomfortable
⑤ made all the rules easier for children to figure out
questions.explanation: 성인용 경기장이나 장비가 아이들에게 부적합하다는 것을 깨닫고 야구의 T볼, 축구의 플래그 풋볼 등 아이들의 연령과 신체 조건에 맞춰 변화를 주었다는 내용이므로, 빈칸에는 '아이들에게 적합한 변화를 만들기 시작했다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 성인들을 위해 적응을 시켰다
② 아이들을 경기에서 배제했다
③ 아이들에게 적합한 변화를 만들기 시작했다
④ 모든 것을 불편한 것으로 바꾸었다
⑤ 모든 규칙을 아이들이 이해하기 더 쉽게 만들었다

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that ______________________________. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ② requires hard work and effort
③ challenges people to be perfect
④ drives people to be self-centered
⑤ provides a sense of accomplishment
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간에게 '의미 있는 일'이 얼마나 중요한지를 설명하며, 일에서 성취감과 만족감을 느끼는 사람들이 더 행복하고 생산적이라는 연구 결과를 인용하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 의미 있는 일을 수식하는 '성취감을 제공하는(provides a sense of accomplishment)'이 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 경제적 지원을 제공하는
② 고된 노동과 노력을 요구하는
③ 사람들이 완벽해지도록 도전하게 하는
④ 사람들이 자기중심적이 되게 몰아가는
⑤ 성취감을 제공하는

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. To start with, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that __________________________. Instead of trying to sort various animal senses into fixed categories, we should study them for what they are.
options: ① there is no difference between human and animal senses by Aristotelian view
② animals also have the perception of their own body and the sense of balance
③ senses should be reconceptualized according to Fiona Macpherson's findings
④ the possibility that the sixth sense exists needs to be considered
⑤ all senses can be obviously classified into Aristotelian groups
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스는 감각을 5가지로 분류했지만, 피오나 맥퍼슨은 인간의 평형감각이나 동물의 특수 감각(열 감지 등)을 예로 들며 감각이 고정된 범주로 쉽게 분류될 수 없음을 시사합니다. 따라서 감각은 '기존의 범주를 넘어 재개념화되어야 한다'는 맥락의 ③번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 아리스토텔레스의 관점에 따르면 인간과 동물의 감각 사이에는 차이가 없다
② 동물들 또한 자신의 몸에 대한 인지와 균형 감각을 가지고 있다
③ 피오나 맥퍼슨의 발견에 따라 감각은 재개념화되어야 한다
④ 제6감이 존재할 가능성이 고려되어야 한다
⑤ 모든 감각은 아리스토텔레스의 분류군으로 명확히 분류될 수 있다

questions.question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장을 고르면?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. ⓐAll creatures are capable of some degree of movement. ⓑEven creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. ⓒBeing immobile is similar to animals' camouflage skill to protect themselves from predators. ⓓA creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. ⓔFrom fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화에 따라 생물종이 생존을 위해 이동해야 한다는 점과, 움직이지 못해 보이는 식물이나 고착 생물들도 생애 주기의 특정 단계(씨앗이나 유충)를 통해 이동을 한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ⓒ번은 움직이지 못하는 상태가 포식자로부터 자신을 보호하기 위한 동물의 위장 기술과 유사하다는 내용이므로, 기후 변화에 따른 '이동'이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents ①<u>disagreeing</u> viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are ②<u>pro-dissent</u>. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and ③<u>regularly</u> claim to continually ④<u>discourage</u> internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these ⑤<u>dissenters</u> because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
questions.explanation: ④ ⌕ discourage(낙담시다, 릻다)는 문맥상 encourage(권윙하다, 격려하다)가 되어야 적절합니다. 문윙에서 많은 경영자들이 반댄 의견을 지지하고 하급 직원들의 내붽 항의를 계석해서 장려한다고 주장하는 내용이 되어야 하기 때문윙니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 3월 21번]
questions.passage: The sense of animals has ⓐ<u>fascinated</u> people for thousands of years, but there are still many mysteries. Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. Yet according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it, as some animals actually have senses that are ⓑ<u>hard</u> to categorize. To begin with, Aristotle missed a few things in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch, and the sense of balance that is ⓒ<u>related</u> to both touch and sight. Other animals have senses that are even more difficult to ⓓ<u>classify</u>. Many vertebrates have different sensory systems that detect odors. Some snakes can sense the body temperature of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into an ⓔ<u>unrestricted</u> number of specific types," Mcpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 감각이 특정 유형의 '제한되지 않은(unrestricted)' 숫자로 명확하게 나누어질 수 없다는 것이 아니라, '제한된(limited/fixed)' 숫자로 명확히 나눌 수 없다는 의미가 되어야 합니다. 따라서 unrestricted를 limited 등으로 고쳐야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Dear Professor Sanchez, My name is Ellis Wight, and I'm the director of the Alexandria Science Museum. As we prepare for an exciting event in our community, I wanted to contact you for assistance. We are thrilled to announce that we will be announcing that we will be hosting a Chemistry Fair for local middle school students on Saturday, October 28. Our primary objective with the fair is to arouse their passion for science through guided experiments. To ensure the success of this event, we are seeking the support of college students who are knowledgeable about chemistry. Considering your expertise and connections within the chemistry department at your college, I am asking you ____________________________________________________. Your recommendations will play a vital role in shaping the educational experience for these middle school students and inspiring their interest in science. Thank you in advance for your help, and I look forward to hearing from you soon.Sincerely,Ellis Wight
options: ① to choose college students who are not majoring in science but like science and want to learn it through the fair
② to send a list of some students who you believe would be proficient in assisting with these experiments during the fair
③ to recruit college students who can make middle school students understand science with theoretical explanations rather than experimental methods
questions.explanation: 박물관 관장이 교수에게 화학 박람회에서 중학생들의 실험을 도와줄 유능한 대학생들을 추천해달라고 요청하는 글입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '박람회 기간 동안 이러한 실험을 돕는 데 능숙할 것이라고 믿는 학생들의 명단을 보내달라'는 내용인 ②가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 과학을 전공하지는 않지만 과학을 좋아하고 박람회를 통해 배우고 싶은 대학생들을 선발해 줄 것
② 박람회 기간 동안 이러한 실험을 돕는 데 능숙할 것이라고 믿는 일부 학생들의 명단을 보내줄 것
③ 실험적인 방법보다는 이론적인 설명으로 중학생들에게 과학을 이해시킬 수 있는 대학생들을 모집할 것

questions.question: 17. 다음 관의 묑줄 친 영리말 부분을 <밴기>의 단어를 반드시 모됐 사용하여 영어로 윑문하시오. (필요시 어형을 봀확시킬 것)
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. <u>아이들은 확고한 인격을 구성하는 가츘들을 그것들에 대해 들음으로얽 배우지 않는다는 것을 기억하라</u>. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore show your child good examples of life by your action. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
subjective_conditions: - <밴기>의 단어를 반드시 모됐 사용할 것
- 필요시 어형을 봀확시킬 것
vocabulary_box: strong character / that / tell / by / the values / make up
questions.answer: the values that make up strong character by being told
questions.explanation: '기억하라(Remember that children do not learn...)' 문장의 목적어 부분을 영작하는 문제입니다. '확고한 인격을 구성하는 가츘들'은 the values that make up strong character로, '들음으로쎽'은 by being told로 표현합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. Although it may seem ⓐ<u>sensible</u>, having two separate calendars for work and personal life can lead to ⓑ<u>distractions</u>. To check if something is missing, you will find yourself ⓒ<u>checking</u> your to-do lists multiple times. Instead, organize all of your tasks in one place. It doesn't matter if you use digital or paper media. It's okay to keep your professional and personal tasks in one place. This will give you a good idea of ⓓ<u>how</u> time is divided between work and home. This will allow you to make informed decisions about ⓔ<u>that</u> tasks are most important.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장에서 about의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌어야 하며, 뒤에 명사 tasks를 수식하는 의문형용사가 필요합니다. 문맥상 '어떤 업무가 가장 중요한지'라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 접속사 that이 아니라 의문사 which(또는 what)가 쓰여야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience ⓐ<u>difficulties</u> when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ⓑ<u>less</u> accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓒ<u>sensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓓ<u>underestimate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how ⓔ<u>hard</u> it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 지문의 핵심인 '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'는 전문가가 초보자의 입장을 이해하지 못하는 현상을 말합니다. 따라서 전문가는 초보자에게 과업이 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 '민감(sensitive)'해지는 것이 아니라 '무감각(insensitive)'해지거나 이해하지 못하게 됩니다.

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment.
ordered_passages: (A) On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.

(B) In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under.

(C) The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details.
questions.explanation: (B)에서 인간의 감각이 걷는 속도에 최적화되어 있음을 설명한 뒤, (C)에서 이와 대조적으로 가장 빠른 운전자는 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력이 제한적임을 설명하고, 마지막으로 (A)에서 보행자와 그 중간 단계인 조깅/자전거 타는 사람들을 비교하며 마무리하는 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 흐름상 적절하지 않은 문장은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. ⓐYet few people ever learn how to negotiate. ⓑThose who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. ⓒThis old-school, adversarial approach may be useless in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. ⓓHowever, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly ─ our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. ⓔIn view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 다시 보지 않을 사람과의 일회성 협상(one-off negotiation)에서는 전통적인 승패(win-lose) 방식이나 적대적 방식이 '쓸모없을(useless)' 것이 아니라, 오히려 '효과적일(effective/useful)' 수 있습니다. 필자는 현대 사회가 상호의존적이기 때문에 이런 방식이 지양되어야 한다고 말하는 것이므로, ⓒ가 흐름상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and ①<u>doesn't</u> deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one ②<u>that</u> you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that ③<u>let</u> you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities ④<u>that</u> hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears ⑤<u>when</u> the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.explanation: ③번이 포함된 'this is the part of your mind that let you down frequently' 문장에서 주격 관계대명사 that의 선행사는 'the part of your mind'로 단수입니다. 따라서 관계절 내의 동사도 단수 취급하여 let을 lets로 바꿔야 어법상 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① ①
② ②
③ ③
④ ④
⑤ ⑤

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without perceptual disengagement it seems essential to the definition of sleep.
options: ① 잠자는 동안 동물이나 사람은 환경의 자극에 정상적으로 반응한다.
② 잠자는 동안 포유류의 눈꺼풀을 열면 그 눈은 제 기능을 잘 발휘한다.
③ 수면 상태에서 들어오는 시각 정보는 다른 감각 체계들과는 달리 축소되거나 약해진다.
④ 모든 저자들이 지각적 이탈(Perceptual disengagement) 현상을 수면 자체의 정의로 여긴다.
⑤ 지각적 이탈(Perceptual disengagement)이 없으면 수면이 불가능할 것이다.
questions.explanation: 마지막 문장 'But as sleep would be impossible without perceptual disengagement it seems essential to the definition of sleep.'을 통해 지각적 이탈이 수면에 필수적이며 이것 없이는 수면이 불가능하다는 것을 알 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five senses in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) However according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.
(C) Other animals have sense that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(B) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kind," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 아리스토텔레스의 5감설을 소개한 뒤, (A)에서 Fiona Macpherson이 이를 의심할 이유가 있다며 인간에게서 빠진 감각(고유 수용 감각, 평형 감각)을 언급합니다. (C)에서는 인간 외에 '다른 동물들(Other animals)'의 분류하기 힘든 감각(냄새 감지, 열 감지)을 추가로 예시합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 '이러한 사례들(These examples)'이 감각을 특정 종류로 명확히 나눌 수 없음을 시사한다고 결론짓는 (A)-(C)-(B) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① The Impact of Pedestrians on the Environment
② The Evolutionary Perspective on Human Senses
③ Drivers: Those Who Move on the Street Most Quickly
④ How Travel Speed Influences the Perception of Environmental Detail
⑤ Unique and Comfortable Lifestyles of Typical Runners and Cyclists
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력에 큰 영향을 미친다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 인간의 감각은 걷는 속도에 최적화되어 있어, 속도가 빠른 운전자는 세부 사항을 파악하기 어렵고, 느린 보행자는 환경적 세부 사항을 잘 감상할 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '이동 속도가 환경 세부 사항 지각에 미치는 영향'을 의미하는 ④번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 보행자가 환경에 미치는 영향
② 인간 감각에 대한 진화론적 관점
③ 운전자: 도로에서 가장 빠르게 움직이는 사람들
④ 이동 속도가 환경 세부 사항의 인지에 어떻게 영향을 미치는가
⑤ 일반적인 러너와 사이클리스트의 독특하고 편안한 생활 방식

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that ⓐ<u>prevents</u> disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are ⓑ<u>pro-dissent</u>. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually ⓒ<u>discourage</u> internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these people who don't ⓓ<u>agree</u> with us because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but it you pay close ⓔ<u>attention</u> to what they say, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
questions.explanation: 글의 앞부분에서 대부분의 상사들이 자신은 반대 의견에 찬성(pro-dissent)한다고 말한다고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 경영 기법에 대한 인터뷰에서도 부하 직원들의 내부적 항의나 반대 의견을 '장려한다'고 주장하는 것이 문맥상 자연스럽습니다. ③번의 discourage(낙담시키다, 막다)를 encourage(격려하다, 장려하다)와 같은 단어로 바꾸어야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. (A) Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. (B) As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. (C) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. (D) Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. (E) It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.insertion_sentence: Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '게다가, 작용하는 메커니즘은 장소가 아니라 시간이다'라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (D) 문장까지는 혀의 어느 곳에서나 맛을 느낄 수 있다는 '장소'의 개념을 다루고 있으며, (E) 뒤의 문장인 '혀끝에서 단맛을 느끼는 것이 아니라 그 지각을 먼저 등록하는 것이다'라는 설명은 '시간'의 개념을 설명하는 구체적인 예시입니다. 따라서 시간 개념을 도입하는 주어진 문장은 (E) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'the curse of knowledge'가 문맥상 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as '<u>the curse of knowledge</u>'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
options: ① The more you know, the less you want to achieve.
② Experts tend to forget how difficult a task is for the novice.
③ Too much knowledge of wireless devices is harmful for mobile phone users.
④ Beginners are often inaccurate in judging how long it takes to acquire a skill.
⑤ Knowledge can be a curse if teaching experts try to look at the learning process through students' eyes.
questions.explanation: '지식의 저주'는 전문가가 초보자에게 어떤 과업이 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 무감각해지는 현상을 의미합니다. 따라서 ②번 '전문가들은 과업이 초보자에게 얼마나 어려운지 잊어버리는 경향이 있다'가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 더 많이 알수록, 더 적게 성취하고 싶어 한다.
② 전문가들은 과업이 초보자에게 얼마나 어려운지 잊어버리는 경향이 있다.
③ 무선 기기에 대한 너무 많은 지식은 휴대폰 사용자에게 해롭다.
④ 초보자들은 종종 기술을 습득하는 데 걸리는 시간을 판단하는 데 부정확하다.
⑤ 가르치는 전문가들이 학생들의 시선으로 학습 과정을 보려 한다면 지식은 저주가 될 수 있다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 전체 흐름과 관계없는 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same littler will display some of the same features, but they will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, ⓐ<u>they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session</u>. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. ⓑ<u>For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic environment</u>. ⓒ<u>In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion</u>. ⓓ<u>With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored in the same way</u>. ⓔ<u>Each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal</u>. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 동물마다 개별적 차이가 있고 환경이나 병명에 따라 반응이 다르므로 각 치유 세션은 동물에 맞춰 조정되어야 한다는 것입니다. 하지만 ⓓ는 '모든 치유 세션이 동일한 방식으로 탐구되어야 한다'고 말하고 있으므로 글의 전체 흐름과 반대되는 내용입니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 전체 흐름과 관계없는 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. ⓐ<u>Many species show complex parental behaviors that ensure their young creatures are equipped to survive in a competitive world</u>. ⓑ<u>All creatures are capable of some degree of movement</u>. ⓒ<u>Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a speed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle</u>. ⓓ<u>A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce</u>. ⓔ<u>From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change</u>.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화에 따라 생물 종이 생존을 위해 이동해야 한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. ⓐ번 문장은 종의 복잡한 부모 행동과 새끼의 생존 장비에 관한 내용으로, 기후 변화에 따른 종의 이동이라는 전체 흐름과 무관합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 문맥과 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.

It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. When your judgment (B)_____________________, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.summary_sentence: Meaningful work is important for human fulfillment and empowerment, leading to greater job satisfaction, higher quality work, and overall happiness. Studies by some experts confirm that ___________________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 1. 다음에 제시된 단어(구)만을 변형하지 않고 빠짐없이 모두 사용할 것 (중복 사용 불가)

questions.answer: those who are satisfied with their careers are more productive at work and live a happier life.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓘ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: A number of research studies ⓐ<u>has</u> shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when they ⓑ<u>introduce</u> newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr. Pamela Hinds found that people expert in ⓒ<u>using</u> mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in ⓓ<u>judging</u> how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect ⓔ<u>referred to as</u> the 'curse of knowledge'. Her participants even underestimated how long it ⓖ<u>has</u> taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. ⓗ<u>Knowing</u> that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand ⓘ<u>the need</u> to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 어법상 어색한 것은 ⓐ와 ⓖ 두 개입니다.ⓐ: 주어가 'A number of research studies'로 복수이므로 동사는 has가 아닌 have가 되어야 합니다.ⓖ: 주절의 시제가 과거(underestimated)이며, 그보다 더 이전에 일어난 일이므로 현재완료 has taken이 아닌 과거완료 had taken이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 33번]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
options: ① Can you process information while asleep?
① Can you process information while asleep?
② How is seeing different from other senses?
③ What should you do when you feel drowsy?
④ How can the environment affect our perception?
⑤ How do people and animals behave differently when asleep?
questions.explanation: 잠을 자는 동안에는 외부 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않는 '지각적 이탈'이 일어나 정보 처리가 정상적으로 이루어지지 않는다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 이러한 현상은 수면을 보호하기 위해 필수적이라는 것이 글의 핵심이므로 '① 잠자는 동안 정보를 처리할 수 있을까?'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글에서 어법상 어색한 것으로만 모은 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: The speed at which one travels greatly ⓐ<u>influences</u> their capacity to observe detail in their surroundings. Motorists, who are the fastest on the streets, ⓓ<u>possesses</u> a significantly diminished capacity to notice such details due to the rapid pace ⓔ<u>at which</u> they move, lacking both the time and the means to truly appreciate the intricacies of design. Conversely, the slower pace of pedestrian travel ⓕ<u>enhances</u> the ability to enjoy the richness of environmental details. ⓖ<u>Position</u> between these two extremes, joggers and bicyclists move faster than walkers but much slower than drivers.
