questions.question: 21. 다음 글과 대화의 내용이 일치하지 않는 단어는?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."↓A: Have you noticed how bosses always claim to ⓐ<u>support</u> dissent?B: Yeah. Like Bot Pittman in that interview, he actually ⓑ<u>promotes</u> listening to dissent to figure out solutions, right?A: Exactly. He believes that dissenters aren't just pointing out problems but are actually ⓒ<u>highlighting</u> necessary actions to succeed.B: It makes sense. By ⓓ<u>excluding</u> different viewpoints, leaders can navigate challenges more effectively.A: True, it shows they value a ⓔ<u>diverse</u> range of opinions to improve decision-making.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 리더들이 반대 의견을 '포함하거나 경청함으로써' 도전을 효과적으로 헤쳐나가는 것이므로, excluding(제외하다)은 어색하며 including 혹은 listening to 등으로 고쳐야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고 요약문에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어는? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.summary_sentence: Climate change (A)[causes / stabilizes] the environments where animals can live to change, (B)[forcing / preventing] them to move to new areas. Even species that seem (C)[movable / stationary], like trees and barnacles, can spread through seeds or larva.
questions.explanation: 지문은 기후 변화가 생물들의 서식 환경을 변화시켜 이동을 강요한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A) 기후 변화는 환경 변화를 '유발(causes)'하며, (B) 이는 생물들로 하여금 새로운 지역으로 이동하도록 '강요(forcing)'합니다. (C) 나무나 따개비처럼 움직이지 않는 것처럼 보이는 '정지된(stationary)' 생물들도 씨앗이나 유생 단계에서 퍼져 나갈 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 유발한다 / 막으면서 / 움직일 수 있는
② 유발한다 / 강요하면서 / 움직일 수 있는
③ 안정시킨다 / 강요하면서 / 움직일 수 있는
④ 유발한다 / 강요하면서 / 정지된
⑤ 안정시킨다 / 막으면서 / 정지된

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고 <보기>와 <조건>을 참고해 글의 주제를 쓰시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
subjective_conditions: - 한 개의 절로 문장을 만들 것.
- 제시된 단어들만 전부 사용하고, 다른 단어를 추가할 수 없음.
- <보기>의 제시된 단어 중 한 개의 단어만을 변형할 것.
questions.answer: How finding meaningful work in life greatly improves happiness and satisfaction
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 '의미 있는 일이 인생의 행복과 만족감을 크게 향상시킨다'는 것입니다. 보기의 단어들을 활용하여 문장을 구성하면, 주어 역할을 하는 명사구 뒤에 동사 improve를 주어의 수에 맞춰 improves로 변형하여 'How finding meaningful work in life greatly improves happiness and satisfaction' 또는 'How meaningful work in life greatly improves happiness and satisfaction'의 구조를 가집니다. (단, 제시된 정답 예시는 원문에서 도출된 핵심 주제 문장입니다.)

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색하거나 혹은 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [23년 3월 22번]
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, ①<u>use</u> what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it ②<u>this way</u>: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know ③<u>that</u> "putting on the same clothes" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently ④<u>than</u> you study for essay tests. And they not ⑤<u>merely</u> know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
questions.explanation: ① using: 주절의 동사가 may approach이므로, 쉼표(,)로 이어지는 부분은 분사구문 자리입니다. 따라서 동사형인 use를 현재분사인 using으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다. ② this way: '이런 식으로'라는 부사구로 적절합니다. ③ that: know의 목적어 절을 이끄는 접속사로 적절합니다. ④ than: 'differently than ~' 구조로 '~와는 다르게'라는 의미로 적절합니다. ⑤ merely: 'not merely A but also B' (A뿐만 아니라 B도) 구조로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [23년 3월 23번]
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
options: ① The development of the economy has led to improvements in working conditions.
② The advancement of technology has increased working hours.
③ The coastal resorts in the UK are one of the results of the Industrial Revolution.
④ The famous hotels in the Rockies were made possible due to the coast-to-coast railroad system.
⑤ The introduction of air transportation also contributed to the growth of the tourism industry.
questions.explanation: 글 서두에서 경제 상황이 나아지며 노동 조건이 개선되어 사람들에게 더 많은 휴가(time off)가 주어졌다고 했으므로, 기술의 발전이 노동 시간을 늘렸다는 ②번은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 경제 발전은 노동 조건의 개선으로 이어졌다.
② 기술의 발전은 노동 시간을 증가시켰다.
③ 영국의 해안 휴양지는 산업혁명의 결과 중 하나이다.
④ 로키 산맥의 유명한 호텔들은 대륙 횡단 철도 시스템 덕분에 가능해졌다.
⑤ 항공 운송 시스템의 도입도 관광 산업의 성장에 기여했다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. (A) In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. (B) Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. (C) The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. (D) Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'This'는 앞 문장의 산업 사회의 변화(부유해지고 경쟁이 치열해짐)를 가리키며, 그 결과로 나타난 인식의 변화(합리적 가격의 품질 좋은 제품 생산만으로는 부족함)를 설명합니다. 이어지는 (A)의 'In fact, it was equally essential...' 문장은 주어진 문장에서 언급한 '부족함'에 대한 구체적인 보완 설명(고객이 원하는 것을 전달하는 것이 필수적임)이므로 (A)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. (A) So work on it. (B) Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. (C) Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. (D) There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. (E) So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.insertion_sentence: Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 특정 시간 내에 달성할 수 있는 것에 대한 과도한 낙관주의가 문제라는 내용입니다. (A) 뒤의 'So work on it(그러니 그것에 노력을 기울여라)'에서 'it'은 시간 추정의 정확성을 높이는 연습을 의미하며, 문맥상 과도한 낙관주의라는 문제점을 먼저 지적한 후 (A) 위치에서 해결책(연습)을 권고하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Whose story it is affects what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
options: ① Characters: The Souls of Every Story
② The Unchanging Values of Classic Tales
③ Shifting Perspectives: How Characters Shape Stories
④ Why We Sympathize with the Protagonists
⑤ The Importance of Conflict in Modern Storytelling
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 '누구의 이야기인가'가 '이야기가 무엇인가'를 결정한다는 것입니다. 주인공이나 시점이 바뀌면 이야기에 대한 해석과 공감의 대상, 기대하는 결과가 모두 달라진다는 내용을 신데렐라와 바람과 함께 사라지다를 예로 들어 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '변하는 관점: 캐릭터가 이야기를 형성하는 방식'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 캐릭터: 모든 이야기의 영혼
② 고전 동화의 변하지 않는 가치
③ 변하는 관점: 캐릭터가 이야기를 형성하는 방식
④ 왜 우리는 주인공에게 공감하는가
⑤ 현대 스토리텔링에서 갈등의 중요성

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓗ 중에서 비슷한 의미를 내포하는 것끼리 짝지은 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of ⓐ<u>traditional livelihoods</u> have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around ⓑ<u>those jobs</u> removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes ⓒ<u>these jobs</u> cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid ⓓ<u>low-tech physical work</u>, to seek ⓔ<u>jobs working in the digital world</u>. The divorce of ⓕ<u>the hands</u> from ⓖ<u>the head</u> puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, The majority of ⓗ<u>well-paying jobs that primarily involve sitting</u> can lead to health risks - for body and mind.
questions.explanation: 지문은 육체적 노동(저기술 작업)과 디지털/정신적 노동을 대조하고 있습니다. ⓔ(디지털 세계에서의 일), ⓖ(머리 - 육체와 분리된 정신적 영역), ⓗ(주로 앉아서 하는 고소득 직업)은 모두 현대 기술 사회에서 강조되는 '정신적/비육체적 노동'의 맥락에서 서로 유사한 의미를 공유합니다. 반면 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓕ는 육체적 노동이나 전통적 생계수단과 관련이 있습니다.

questions.question: 16. 주어진 글 (A), (E) 사이에 들어갈 글 (B)~(D)의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started.
ordered_passages: (B) We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision.
(C) Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process.

(D) The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 모든 것은 시작 전 마음에 완성된다는 대전제를 제시합니다. (D)는 집, 자동차, 옷과 같은 구체적인 예시를 들어 이 과정(아이디어에서 시작되어 다듬어짐)을 설명합니다. (C)는 이러한 물리적 현실 이전에 마음속 그림이 먼저라는 것을 다시 강조하며, 인간이 미래를 설계하는 과정도 이와 같다고 연결합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 그 과정을 우리(인간)의 미래에 대입하여 아이디어로 시작해 비전을 완성해 나간다는 흐름으로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 17. 윗글의 (E) 문장이 '머지않아 우리의 모든 생각, 결정, 활동은 우리가 미래에 대해 머릿속에서 완성한 것을 생겨나게 하려고 모두 조화롭게 작용하게 된다.' 의 뜻이 되도록 작성하되 아래의 어휘만을 모두 사용하여 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: (A) Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started.(B) We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision.(C) Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process.(D) The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut.(E) _______________________________________________________   _______________________________________________________   _______________________________________________________
subjective_conditions: 머지않아 우리의 모든 생각, 결정, 활동은 우리가 미래에 대해 머릿속에서 완성한 것을 생겨나게 하려고 모두 조화롭게 작용하게 된다.
제시된 한국어 의미에 맞게 영어 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.answer: Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
questions.explanation: 제공된 어휘들을 의미에 맞게 배열하면 다음과 같습니다. '머지않아(Before long)', '우리의 모든 생각, 결정, 활동은(our every thought, decision and activity)', '모두 조화롭게 작용하게 된다(are all working in harmony)', '~을 생겨나게 하려고(to bring into existence)', '우리가 미래에 대해 머릿속에서 완성한 것을(what we have mentally concluded about the future)'.

questions.question: 19. 다음 주어진 해석과 같은 의미가 되도록 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 사용하여 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: 성공은 여러분을 의도한 길에서 벗어나 틀에 박힌 편안한 생활로 이끌 수 있다.
vocabulary_box: a / and / can / comfortable / intended / into / lead / off / path / rut / success / you / your
questions.answer: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut.
questions.explanation: '주어(Success) + 조동사(can) + 동사(lead) + 목적어(you) + 방향/경로(off your intended path and into a comfortable rut)' 순으로 문장을 구성합니다. 'lead A off B'는 A를 B에서 벗어나게 이끌다는 의미입니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 주어진 해석과 같은 의미가 되도록 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 사용하여 문장을 완성하시오.
vocabulary_box: a / be / but / even / employment / feeling / has / in / job / left / locked / market / may / or / poor / secure / the / them / ultimately / unsatisfying / well-paying / what
questions.answer: The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying but ultimately unsatisfying job.
questions.explanation: 'leave + 목적어 + 목적격 보어(현재분사)' 구문을 사용하여 '그들을 ~인 상태로 두었다'를 표현합니다. 목적어 them 뒤에 feeling locked를 쓰고, 전치사 in의 목적어로 what절(what may be...)을 구성하여 복잡한 수식 관계를 영작합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. ⓐExperts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. ⓑDr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. ⓒHer participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. ⓓPeople generally tend to rate their abilities and personality traits as better than average. ⓔKnowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.*novice: 신참자, 초심자 **trait: 특성, 특색
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전문가가 초보자에게 무언가를 가르칠 때 겪는 어려움인 '지식의 저주(전문가가 초보자의 난이도를 과소평가함)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ⓓ번 문장은 사람들이 자신의 능력을 평균보다 높게 평가하는 경향이 있다는 일반적인 심리 현상을 설명하고 있어 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 바르게 묶은 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places ⓐ<u>that</u> satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures ⓑ<u>that</u> appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place ⓒ<u>where</u> it is born in - often occupied by its parent - to a place ⓓ<u>where</u> it can survive in. From fossils, scientists know ⓔ<u>that</u> even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.*barnacle: 따개비 **dispersal: 분산 ***fossil: 화석
questions.explanation: ⓒ와 ⓓ는 모두 관계부사 where가 쓰였습니다. 관계부사 뒤에는 완전한 절이 와야 하는데, ⓒ 뒤의 절에는 전치사 in의 목적어가 빠져 있으며, ⓓ 뒤의 절 역시 전치사 in의 목적어가 빠져 있는 불완전한 절입니다. 따라서 관계부사 where 대신 관계대명사 which(또는 that)를 쓰거나, 전치사를 관계부사 앞으로 옮겨 in which로 써야 합니다. ⓐ와 ⓑ는 주격 관계대명사로 적절하며, ⓔ는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① Create magic through positive statements.
② Don't blame others; build your confidence instead.
③ Change positive thinking into positive action and results.
④ Repeat positive statements to reduce stress and anxiety.
⑤ Leave your problems behind and look forward to a positive day.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 현재 겪고 있는 어려움(challenge)을 긍정적인 문구(positive statements)로 바꾸어 적음으로써 생각과 행동의 변화를 일으키고 인생에서 마법과 같은 결과를 만들어낼 수 있다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '긍정적인 문구를 통해 마법을 만들어라'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 긍정적인 진술을 통해 마법을 만들어라.
② 다른 사람을 탓하지 말고 대신 당신의 자신감을 쌓아라.
③ 긍정적인 사고를 긍정적인 행동과 결과로 바꿔라.
④ 스트레스와 불안을 줄이기 위해 긍정적인 진술을 반복하라.
⑤ 당신의 문제들을 뒤로하고 긍정적인 하루를 기대하라.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago. Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate: 척추동물 **odor: 냄새
questions.summary_sentence: Fiona Macpherson points out that many animals have (A)____________ senses, such as detecting odors differently or sensing body heat. She suggests that we (B)____________ stick to Aristotle's five categories of senses without question.
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 5가지 감각 외에도 생물들은 열 감지나 독특한 냄새 감지 체계 같은 독특한(unique) 감각을 가지고 있으므로, 우리가 감각을 단순히 5가지 범주로 제한하여 고집해서는 안 된다(shouldn't)는 내용이 요약문으로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 전형적인 ... 해야 한다
② 독특한 ... 해야 한다
③ 전형적인 ... 해서는 안 된다
④ 독특한 ... 해서는 안 된다
⑤ 일반적인 ... 해서는 안 된다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 가리키는 대상이 같은 것을 모두 골라 바르게 묶은 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find ⓐ<u>it</u> difficult to know when to stop painting, and ⓑ<u>it</u> can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. ⓒ<u>It </u>is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave ⓓ<u>it</u> looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to ⓔ<u>it</u> later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.*tempting: 유혹하는 **refinement: 정교하게 꾸밈
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ는 모두 가주어 'it'으로 뒤에 나오는 진주어를 가리키지만, ⓓ와 ⓔ는 문맥상 'a painting(그림)'을 직접적으로 가리키는 대명사입니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Motorists, pedestrians, joggers, and bicyclists perceive street design features differently because of the difference in speeds at which they move along the street. The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much (A)__________, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while their rate of speed is ordinarily much (B)__________ than that of the typical motorist, they travel (C)__________than pedestrians.*feature: 특징 **distinguish: 구별하다***pedestrian: 보행자
questions.explanation: 이동 속도에 따라 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력이 달라진다는 내용입니다. (A) 보행자의 이동은 운전자보다 훨씬 느리므로(slower) 세부 사항을 감상할 수 있습니다. (B) 조깅하는 사람이나 자전거 타는 사람의 속도는 운전자보다는 훨씬 느리고(slower), (C) 보행자보다는 더 빠릅니다(faster).
options_translation: 더 빠른 / 더 느린 / 더 빠른
더 빠른 / 더 빠른 / 더 느린
더 느린 / 더 빠른 / 더 느린
더 느린 / 더 느린 / 더 빠른
더 느린 / 더 빠른 / 더 빠른

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When discussing their own leadership and management styles, bosses usually acknowledge the need to thoughtfully listen to dissenting views from their employees. Respectable bosses would say, "I make it a point to ⓐ<u>encourage</u> my staff to speak up, and I maintain a culture that ⓑ<u>encourages</u> the airing of disagreeing viewpoints." Most bosses even say that they are ⓒ<u>pro-dissent</u>. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from ⓓ<u>few</u> junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these ⓔ<u>dissenters</u> because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."*acknowledge: 인정하다 **thoughtfully: 사려 깊게***dissent: 반대
questions.explanation: 훌륭한 리더들은 직원들의 반대 의견(dissenting views)을 경청하고 장려한다고 주장하는 내용의 글입니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 'few(거의 없는)'는 주니어 직원들로부터의 내부 반대 의견을 거의 장려하지 않는다는 의미가 되므로, 문맥상 '많은' 또는 '다양한' 의견을 장려한다는 긍정적인 맥락의 단어로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① Incan Messengers Running on War Fields
② A Brilliant Way of Delivering Messages In Inca
③ Why Inca Couldn't Last Even With Best Horses
④ Good Runners And Good Horse Riders
⑤ The Systematic Way to Build Huts
questions.explanation: 이 글은 말이 없는 인카 제국에서 보행 전령(Chasquis)들을 일정한 간격의 오두막에 배치하여 체계적이고 신속하게 메시지를 전달했던 효율적인 방식을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 인카의 뛰어난 메시지 전달 방법을 핵심으로 삼은 ②번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 전쟁터에서 달리는 인카의 전령들
② 인카의 뛰어난 메시지 전달 방법
③ 왜 인카가 최고의 말들로도 지속되지 못했는가
④ 훌륭한 달리기 선수들과 훌륭한 기수들
⑤ 오두막을 짓는 체계적인 방법

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth.
ordered_passages: (A) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites.

(B) Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century.
(C) Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 과거의 잘못된 '혀 지도' 이론을 소개한 뒤, (B)에서 'however'를 통해 이 지도가 사실은 오역과 오해에서 비롯된 완전히 틀린 것임을 밝힙니다. 이어지는 (A)에서는 'Today'를 통해 오늘날의 과학적 정설(모든 곳에서 모든 맛을 느낄 수 있음)을 설명하며, 마지막으로 (C)에서 'Moreover'를 사용하여 맛을 느끼는 차이가 장소가 아닌 '시간(속도)'의 문제라는 추가적인 매커니즘을 설명하는 (B)-(A)-(C)의 전개가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글읈 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 채, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.summary_sentence: Healing sessions should be (A)__________ to individual animals because they are not entirely (B)____________.
questions.explanation: 동물마다 특성과 환경이 다르므로 측정 회기(측치)는 각 동물에 맞게 -젰응(조정)-되어야 하며, 괸 이유는 동물들이 완전히 -동일하지- 않기 때문입니다.
options_translation: ① 줐거운 - 다른
② 고통순러운 - 정서적으로 혼란순러운
③ 젰응된(맞춤의) - 동일한
④ 쒸모없는 - 비슷한
⑤ 다른 - 측치된

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
options: ① 의식적 마음과 잠재 의식적 마음은 상호작용하며 두려움을 이겨내는 힘을 준다.
② 의식적 마음보다 잠재 의식적 마음이 감정을 조정하며 부정적 감정을 형성한다.
③ 잠재 의식적 마음은 의식적 마음의 부산물이며 기억을 왜곡시켜 두려움을 만들어 낸다.
④ 의식적 마음은 생각과 감정을 다루지만, 잠재 의식적 마음은 반응을 기록해 실제 두려움을 형성한다.
⑤ 거미나 어둠을 두려워하는 이유는 기억을 기록할 때 일어나는 오류로 의식적 마음으로 극복할 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 의식적인 마음은 생각하고 감정을 조절할 수 있지만 감정 때문에 잘못된 결정을 내리기도 하며, 두려움의 기원도 의식적인 마음에 있습니다. 그러나 잠재의식적인 마음이 이러한 반응을 기록할 때 그것이 실제적인 두려움이 된다고 설명하고 있으므로 ④가 정답입니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: At would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① Fulfilling work often leads to the avoidance of financial success.
② Meaningful work contributes to human happiness and well-being.
③ One's pride can be both a source of strength and a barrier to growth.
④ The government should create more jobs that guarantee income stability.
⑤ Empowerment inhibits individuals from realizing their full potential.
questions.explanation: 글의 도입부에서 인간에게 의미 있는 일(성취감과 자율권을 주는 일)이 얼마나 중요한지는 아무리 강조해도 지나치지 않다고 언급하며, 직업에서 의미를 찾은 사람들이 더 활기차고 만족스러운 삶을 살며, 높은 수입과 전반적인 행복을 누린다는 연구 결과를 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 글의 요지는 의미 있는 일이 인간의 행복과 안녕에 기여한다는 것입니다.
options_translation: ① 성취감을 주는 일은 종종 경제적 성공을 피하게 만든다.
② 의미 있는 일은 인간의 행복과 안녕에 기여한다.
③ 개인의 자부심은 강점의 원천이자 성장의 장벽이 될 수 있다.
④ 정부는 소득 안정을 보장하는 더 많은 일자리를 창출해야 한다.
⑤ 자율권(권한 부여)은 개인이 자신의 잠재력을 최대한 발휘하는 것을 방해한다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① impact of competitive pressure on children
② significance of team selection in junior sports
③ necessity of adapting sports for young players
④ ways of enhancing skill techniques in young athletes
⑤ benefits of overcoming challenges in competitive sports
questions.explanation: 어린이들이 성인용 경기장이나 장비를 사용하여 운동하는 것의 어려움을 인식하고, 야구(T볼), 축구(플래그 풋볼, 작은 공), 테니스(작은 코트와 라켓) 등 여러 종목에서 아이들의 신체 조건과 나이에 맞게 스포츠를 변형(adaptation)해 왔다는 내용입니다. 따라서 주제는 어린 선수들을 위한 스포츠 조정/변형의 필요성입니다.
options_translation: ① 경쟁적 압박이 아이들에게 미치는 영향
② 주니어 스포츠에서 팀 선정의 중요성
③ 어린 선수들을 위한 스포츠 변형의 필요성
④ 어린 운동선수들의 기술 기법을 향상시키는 방법
⑤ 경쟁적인 스포츠에서 도전을 극복하는 것의 이점

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① how the Inca sent messages across the vast stretches of their realm
② how the Inca expanded and conquered a vast territory
③ craftsmen and roadway facilities of the Inca empire
④ what led to the downfall of the Inca empire
⑤ how the Incas kept their empire strong
questions.explanation: 본문은 인카 제국이 말이 없는 상황에서도 'Chasquis'라고 불리는 전령들을 도로망 곳곳에 배치하여 도보로 매우 신속하게 메시지를 전달했던 시스템을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '인카가 광대한 영토 전역에 메시지를 보낸 방법'이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 인카가 그들 영토의 광대한 지역에 메시지를 보낸 방법
② 인카가 광대한 영토를 확장하고 정복한 방법
③ 인카 제국의 장인들과 도로 시설들
④ 무엇이 인카 제국의 몰락을 초래했는가
⑤ 인카인들이 그들의 제국을 강하게 유지한 방법

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
options: ① 과거에는 입의 뒤쪽에 쓴맛을 느끼는 영역이 있다고 구획되었다.
② 1980년대 1990년대의 연구의 맛을 느끼는 방식에 대한 이전 설명이 틀렸다는 것을 보여주었다.
③ "혀 지도"는 20세기 초에 수행된 독일의 연구를 오해하고 오역한 것이었다.
④ 오늘날 선도적인 미각 연구자들은 모든 맛이 여러 위치에서 같은 강도로 지각된다고 설명한다.
⑤ 미각이 작동하는 기제는 위치가 아니라 시간이며 단맛이 혀에 가장 먼저 등록된다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites'라고 언급하고 있으므로, 모든 맛이 여러 위치에서 '같은 강도'로 지각된다는 ④번 설명은 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다. 위치에 따라 강도는 조금 다르게 지각될 수 있다고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed ⓐ<u>at which</u> humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally ⓑ<u>suited</u> to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street ─ a motorist simply has ⓒ<u>little</u> time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, ⓓ<u>allowing</u> for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than ⓔ<u>that</u> of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'pedestrian travel'이며, 'being much slower'는 삽입구(분사구문)입니다. 따라서 이 문장에는 본동사가 필요하므로 현재분사인 'allowing'을 단수 본동사인 'allows'로 고쳐야 문법적으로 옳습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 진 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond ⓐ<u>normally</u> to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not*see normally ─ they are functionally ⓑ<u>blind</u>. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened. The same is the case with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are ⓒ<u>registered</u> but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual ⓓ<u>engagement</u> probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the <u>intermediate</u> state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual detachment.
questions.explanation: 잠을 자는 동안 감각 자극이 정상적으로 처리되지 않고 외부 환경에 반응하지 않는 이유는 외부 자극으로부터 분리되기 때문입니다. 따라서 수면을 보호하는 기능을 하는 것은 지각적 '관여(engagement)'가 아니라 지각적 '분리(detachment 또는 disengagement)'가 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that novice phone users were remarkably (A)[less / more] accurate in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones than people expert in using mobile phones. Experts can become (B)[sensitive / insensitive] to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts fail to (C)[remember / forget] how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: (A) 숙련자들은 학습 시간을 저평가하는 경향이 있으므로, 초보자들이 학습 시간을 판단하는 데 훨씬 더(more) 정확합니다. (B) 지식의 저주로 인해 전문가들은 초보자에게 과업이 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 무감각(insensitive)해질 수 있습니다. (C) 전문가들이 자신들이 배우는 것이 얼마나 힘들었는지 기억(remember)하는 데 실패한다는 점을 알면 학생의 관점에서 학습 과정을 바라볼 필요를 이해할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 덜 - 민감한 - 기억하다
② 덜 - 무감각한 - 잊어버리다
③ 덜 - 무감각한 - 기억하다
④ 더 - 민감한 - 잊어버리다
⑤ 더 - 무감각한 - 기억하다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "_________________________," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
options: ① it is impossible to categorically separate senses into a small number of distinct sorts
② we can divide senses up in different ways depending on the types of species
③ functional properties of receptors evolve to ignore different types of information
④ natural selection has no intentions or senses and does not create new traits
⑤ sensations are clearly classified into a finite number of distinct kinds
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 5감(시각, 청각, 후각, 미각, 촉각) 외에도 인간에게는 평형감각이나 자기 신체 지각 능력이 있으며, 동물들에게는 열 감지 등 더 복잡한 감각이 존재한다는 예시를 들고 있습니다. 따라서 감각을 단순히 몇 가지 종류로 명확히 나누는 것이 불가능하다는 결론이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 감각을 적은 수의 뚜렷한 종류로 절대적으로 분류하는 것은 불가능하다
② 우리는 종의 유형에 따라 다양한 방식으로 감각을 나눌 수 있다
③ 수용체의 기능적 특성은 다양한 유형의 정보를 무시하도록 진화한다
④ 자연 선택은 의도나 감각이 없으며 새로운 특성을 만들어내지 않는다
⑤ 감각은 유한한 수의 뚜렷한 종류로 명확하게 분류된다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. ␐If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. ␑But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. ␒Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. ␓Only a select few, possessing unique qualities of exceptional talent and constant dedication, have the capacity to emerge as leaders. ␔Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 리더십이 위대한 인물들만의 전유물이 아니라, 우리 모두가 일상생활의 개선 아이디어를 공유하고 발전시킴으로써 리더가 될 잠재력을 가지고 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ␓번 문장은 오직 선택된 소수만이 리더가 될 능력이 있다고 말하고 있으므로, 누구나 리더가 될 수 있다는 글의 전체 흐름과 상반됩니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will ⓐ<u>exhibit</u> some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the ⓑ<u>different</u> way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also ⓒ<u>determine</u> how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very ⓓ<u>dissimilarly</u> than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the ⓔ<u>particular</u> needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 동물들이 서로 완전히 똑같지는 않다고 했으므로, 치유 과정에서 '완전히 똑같은(same)' 방식으로 반응하지 않을 수도 있다는 내용이 되어야 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 different를 same 등으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: 질문의 보기 옵션이 텍스트에 포함되어 있지 않으나, 정답이 ③번으로 제공되었습니다. 지문의 내용은 모든 생물(나무와 따개비 포함)이 생애의 특정 단계(씨앗이나 유충 등)에서 이동 능력을 갖추고 기후 변화에 따라 서식지를 옮긴다는 내용입니다. (참고: 실제 원문 시험 문제의 ③번 선지는 보통 '움직이지 못하는 나무와 따개비는 이동이 불가능하다'는 식의 내용일 가능성이 높습니다.)

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 2개 골라 바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>With no horses available</u>, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads ⓑ<u>to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports came</u> from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, ⓒ<u>placing from one to two miles apart along the roads</u>. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. ⓓ<u>Nearing the next hut</u>, a messenger began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one ⓔ<u>who was running out to meet</u> him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
questions.answer: (1) ⓑ came → coming (또는 that/which came)(2) ⓒ placing → placed
questions.explanation: ⓑ reports를 수식하는 구조이므로 과거분사나 현재분사가 와야 하는데, 보고서가 '오는' 것이므로 coming이 적절하거나 관계대명사가 필요합니다. ⓒ 오두막(huts)이 '위치해 있는' 수동의 의미이므로 과거분사 placed가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은? [23년 9월 18번]
questions.passage: Dear Professor Sanchez, My name is Ellis Wight, and I'm the director of the Alexandria Science Museum. We are holding a Chemistry Fair for local middle school students on Saturday, October 28. The goal of the fair is to encourage them to be interested in science through guided experiments. We are looking for college students who can help with the experiments during the event. I am contacting you to ask you to recommend some students from the chemistry department at your college who you think are qualified for this job. With their help, I'm sure the participants will have a great experience. I look forward to hearing from you soon.Sincerely,Ellis Wight
options: ① What is the position of the writer of this letter?
② How often does the fair take place in a year?
③ What is the objective of the fair?
④ What are the college students supposed to do?
⑤ What is the purpose of this letter?
questions.explanation: 이 글은 화학 박람회에 도움을 줄 대학생들을 추천받기 위해 쓰인 편지입니다. 편지에는 작성자의 직책(Alexandria 과학 박물관 관장), 박람회의 목적(학생들의 과학에 대한 관심 고취), 대학생들이 할 일(실험 보조) 등이 명시되어 있으나, 박람회가 일 년에 몇 번 개최되는지에 대한 정보는 없습니다.
options_translation: ① 이 편지를 쓴 사람의 직책은 무엇인가?
② 이 박람회는 일 년에 몇 번 열리는가?
③ 박람회의 목적은 무엇인가?
④ 대학생들은 무엇을 하기로 되어 있는가?
⑤ 이 편지의 목적은 무엇인가?

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 18번]
questions.passage: To whom it may concern, I am a resident of the Blue Sky Apartment. Recently I observed that the kid zone is in need of repairs. I want you to pay attention to the poor condition of the playground equipment in the zone. The swings are damaged, the paint is falling off, and some of the bolts on the slide are missing. The facilities have been in this terrible condition since we moved here. They are dangerous to the children playing there. Would you please have them repaired? I would appreciate your immediate attention to solve this matter.Yours sincerely,Nina Davis
options: ① Poor facilities in the kid zone need to be fixed.
② The latest equipment should be added to the playground.
③ We need to change the purpose of the apartment playground.
④ Safety rules regarding the use of playgrounds should be established.
⑤ The kid zone should be transformed into a child-friendly play area.
questions.explanation: 글쓴이는 아파트 내 키즈 존의 놀이터 시설(그네, 미끄럼틀 등)이 노후화되고 위험한 상태임을 지적하며, 이에 대한 즉각적인 수리를 요청하고 있습니다. 따라서 1번 '키즈 존의 열악한 시설물이 수리되어야 한다'가 필자의 주장으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 키즈 존의 열악한 시설물은 수리되어야 한다.
② 최신 장비가 놀이터에 추가되어야 한다.
③ 아파트 놀이터의 용도를 변경해야 한다.
④ 놀이터 이용에 관한 안전 수칙이 제정되어야 한다.
⑤ 키즈 존은 아이 친화적인 놀이 공간으로 변모되어야 한다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 9월 19번]
questions.passage: Gregg and I had been rock climbing since sunrise and had had no problems. So we took a risk. (A) "Look, the first bolt is right there. I can definitely climb out to it. Piece of cake," (B) It wasn't a piece of cake. (C) The rock was deceptively barren of handholds. (D) I clumsily moved back and forth across the cliff face and ended up with nowhere to go...but down. (E) The bolt that would save my life, if I could get to it, was about two feet above my reach. My arms trembled from exhaustion. I looked at Gregg. My body froze with fright from my neck down to my toes. Our rope was tied between us. If I fell, he would fall with me.
questions.insertion_sentence: I persuaded Gregg, minutes before I found myself pinned.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '내가 꼼짝 못 하게 되기 몇 분 전에 나는 Gregg를 설득했다'는 의미입니다. (A)에서 필자가 '확실히 올라갈 수 있다, 식은 죽 먹기다'라고 말하며 위험을 감수하도록 Gregg를 설득하는 장면이 나오므로, 상황이 나빠지기 직전인 (B) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다. (B) 이후부터는 예상과 달리 상황이 어려워지는 내용이 이어집니다.

questions.question: 18. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children (A)<u>take</u> the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by (B)<u>tell</u> about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore show your child good examples of life by your action. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
options: ① the various ways to show respect to others
② the principles and priorities for raising children
③ the importance of self-control in shaping a child's character
④ the necessity of demonstrating good examples through parents' actions
⑤ the reason why visual training is more effective than auditory training in early education

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It is difficult for any of us to maintain a constant level of attention throughout our working day. questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, (A)[favorable / adversarial] approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, such transactions are becoming increasingly (B)[rare / popular], because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only (C)[acceptable / unacceptable] result.
questions.explanation: (A) win-lose 방식은 전통적이고 '적대적인(adversarial)' 접근 방식입니다. (B) 오늘날에는 같은 사람과 반복적으로 거래하므로 일회성 거래는 점점 '드물어(rare)'지고 있습니다. (C) 상호 의존적인 비즈니스 환경에서는 윈윈(win-win) 결과만이 '수용 가능한(acceptable)' 유일한 결과가 되고 있습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, ⓐ<u>which</u> may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also ⓑ<u>affecting</u> the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region ⓒ<u>because</u> an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of ⓓ<u>what</u> they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear ⓔ<u>that</u> social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.explanation: ⓑ 'may also affecting'에서 조동사 may 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 affect가 되어야 합니다. ⓒ 'because an increase...' 뒤에 명사구가 이어지므로 전치사인 because of가 필요합니다. 따라서 어색한 것은 ⓑ, ⓒ 총 2개입니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are - writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how successfully one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. _________________________ becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
options: ① How much effort one puts into a task
② How others think of someone
③ How persistent one has been
④ How well one completes tasks
⑤ How nice one's personality is
questions.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에서 '뛰어난 수행(performance)은 뛰어난 사람을, 평균적인 수행은 평균적인 사람을 의미한다'고 설명하고 있습니다. 즉, 개인의 가치가 오로지 그의 '수행 능력'이나 '과업을 완수하는 정도'에 의해서만 평가되는 상황의 문제점을 지적하는 글이므로, 빈칸에는 '얼마나 업무를 잘 수행하느냐(How well one completes tasks)'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 얼마나 많은 노력을 기울였느냐
② 다른 사람들이 누군가를 어떻게 생각하느냐
③ 얼마나 지속적(끈기)이었느냐
④ 얼마나 과업을 잘 수행하느냐
⑤ 성격이 얼마나 좋으냐

questions.question: 24. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. ①Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. ②Similarly, scientific communications is a two-way process. ③Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. ④Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. ⑤In a nutshell, scientist are publishing too many papers and the number of papers being published has grown exponentially over the years.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학적 의사소통이 단순히 결과를 발표하는 것(공표)에서 끝나는 것이 아니라, 독자에게 전달되고 '이해'되는 과정이 수반되어야 비로소 완성된다는 '양방향 과정'으로서의 과학적 소통을 강조하고 있습니다. 반면 ⑤번 문장은 출판되는 논문의 수가 급격히 늘어나고 있다는 양적인 문제를 언급하고 있으므로, 소통의 본질을 다루는 전체 글의 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용으로 보아 "Monday Morning Quarterback"에 대한 설명으로 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them confront criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.summary_sentence: "Monday Morning Quaterback" refers to people who (A)___________ the actions or decisions of others after certain events happened from a position of (B)___________ to suggest alternative actions.
questions.explanation: 'Monday Morning Quarterback'은 스포츠 경기가 끝난 뒤(나중에) 전문가가 아닌 입장에서 선수나 코치의 행동을 비판하며 '나였으면 더 잘했을 것'이라고 말하는 사람들을 지칭합니다. (A)에는 다른 사람들의 행동을 비판한다는 의미인 criticize가 적절하며, (B)에는 일이 벌어진 뒤에 깨닫는 '뒤늦은 깨달음/사후 확신'의 의미인 hindsight가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 비판하다 / 뒤늦은 깨달음
② 비난하다 / 전문가
③ 승인하다 / 전문가
④ 받아들이다 / 관찰자
⑤ 비판하다 / 선견지명

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은 모두 몇 개인가? [3.1점]
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us. One of the best examples of this ⓐ<u>is</u> the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Göbekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea ⓑ<u>to erect</u> standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were ⓒ<u>forcing</u> to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up radically ⓓ<u>remaking</u> the society itself. Things are not so ⓔ<u>differently</u> in our own time.
questions.explanation: 어색한 부분은 ⓒ와 ⓔ 총 2개입니다.ⓒ: innovators(혁신가들)가 건설을 완료하기 위해 정착하도록 '강요받은' 수동의 의미이므로 were forced(수동태)가 되어야 합니다.ⓔ: be동사(are) 뒤에는 보어인 형용사가 와야 하므로 부사인 differently를 형용사 different로 고쳐야 합니다.참고: ⓐ 주어 One of the ~ 복수명사에서 One이 주어이므로 단수동사 is는 적절함. ⓑ the idea를 수식하는 형용사적 용법 to erect는 적절함. ⓓ ends up -ing(~하는 것으로 결국 끝나다) 구문에서 remaking은 적절함.

questions.question: 27. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Share of Forest Area in Total Land Area by Region in 1990 and 2019The above graph shows the share of forest area in total land area by region in 1990 and 2019. ⓐAfrica's share of forest area in total land area was 21.4% in 2019, which was about 4% lower than that in 1990. ⓑThe share of forest are in America was 42.6% in 1990, which was 20% higher than that in Asia in the same year. ⓒThe share of forest area in Asia declined from 1990 to 2019 by more than 10 percentage points. ⓓIn 2019, the share of forest area in Europe was the largest among the five regions, almost as twice as that in Oceania in the same year. ⓔOceania showed the smallest increase between 1990 and 2019 in terms of the share of forest area in total land area.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 문맥상 영영 풀이로 바르지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel ⓐ<u>disoriented</u> when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Children need to have opportunities to ⓓ<u>share</u> their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in ⓔ<u>transition</u>.
options: ① ⓐdisoriented: confused as to time or place or personal identity
② ⓑliteral: tending to understand words in an unimaginative way

④ ⓓshare: talk about personal experiences or feelings with others
⑤ ⓔtransition: converting a work into another language
questions.explanation: ⓔ transition은 지문에서 이사 등의 과정에서 겪는 '변화'나 '전이' 단계를 의미한다. ⑤번의 영영 풀이 'converting a work into another language'는 '번역(translation)'에 대한 설명이므로 문맥상 단어의 뜻과 일치하지 않는다.
options_translation: ① ⓐdisoriented: 시간, 장소 또는 정체성에 대해 혼란스러워하는
② ⓑliteral: 상상력이 없는 방식으로 단어를 이해하는 경향이 있는
③ ⓒvalidating: 사람, 상태 또는 시스템이 가치 있거나 보람 있음을 증명하거나 확인하는 것
④ ⓓshare: 다른 사람들과 개인적인 경험이나 감정에 대해 이야기하다
⑤ ⓔtransition: 작품을 다른 언어로 변환하는 것

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ␐~␓를 어법과 흠름에 맞게 고찴 쓰시오. (단어츤가 및 어형변화 가능) [3.2점]
questions.passage: American jazz pianist Bill Evans ␐<u>bear</u> in New Jersey in 1929. His early training was in classical music. At the age of six, he began receiving piano lessons, later adding flute and violin. He earned bachelor's degrees in piano and music education from Southeastern Louisiana College in 1950. He went on to serve in the army from 1951 to 1954 and played flute in the Fifth Army Band. After ␑<u>serve</u> in the military, he studied composition at the Mannes School of Music in New York. Composer George Russell admired his playing and hired Evans ␒<u>record</u> and perform his compositions. Evans became famous for recordings ␓<u>make</u> from the late-1950s through the 1960s. He won his first Grammy Award in 1964 for his album Conversations with Myself.
subjective_conditions: 단어츤가 및 어형변화 가능
questions.answer: ␐ was born, ␑ serving, ␒ to record, ␓ made
questions.explanation: ␐ 과거 태어났다는 수동의 의미이므로 was born이 적절합니다. ␑ 전츠사 after 됤에는 동명사가 와야 하므로 serving이 맞습니다. ␒ hire는 'hire A to do'의 구문으로 쓰이므로 to record가 적절합니다. ␓ recordings를 수식하는 과거분사가 필요하므로 made가 맞습니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)an Olympic medalist swimmer에 대한 (B)의 설명을 <보기>에 제시된 단어 모됐와 밤문에 쓰인 단어만을 사용하여, 비칸을 15단어 이내로 완성하시오. (단, 밤문과 보기의 단어를 여러 번 쓰을 수 있음) [4.3점]
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of (A)<u>an Olympic medalist swimmer</u>. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.↓(B) According to the passage, if (A)<u>the medalist swimmer</u> recommended a certain golf club, people would gladly buy that brand _________________________.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 제시된 단어 모됐와 밤문에 쓰인 단어만을 사용
15단어 이내로 완성
밤문과 보기의 단어를 여러 번 쓰을 수 있음
vocabulary_box: not / but / because of / golf / swimming
questions.answer: not because of his(her) expertise(knowledge) on golf but because of his(her) excellence (talent/ability/skill) in(on/with) swimming
questions.explanation: 지문의 핵심 내용은 특정 분야의 탁월함이 그 분야와 상관없는 다른 분야에서도 신뢰를 준다는 것입니다. 따라서 수영 메달리스트가 골프채를 촔찜할 땄 사람들이 사는 이유는, 골프에 대한 지식 때문이 아니라 수영에서의 탁월함 때문임을 not A but B 구문을 활용하여 서술합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of ㅡ movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ② Various Types of Rainfall Patterns
③ What Survival of the Fittest Means
④ Different Ways Organism to Reproduce
⑤ The Impact of Climate Change on Species Moving
questions.explanation: 글은 모든 생명체가 기후 변화에 따라 자신이 생존할 수 있는 기후 조건을 찾아 이동해야 하며, 움직이지 않는 것처럼 보이는 식물(나무)조차도 기후 변화 시기에 이동한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 ⑤ '기후 변화가 종의 이동에 미치는 영향'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기후 변화에 대한 해결책
② 강우 패턴의 다양한 유형들
③ 적자생존이 의미하는 것
④ 유기체가 번식하는 다양한 방법들
⑤ 기후 변화가 종의 이동에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that ⓐ<u>provides</u> a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and ⓑ<u>count</u> their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing ⓒ<u>that</u> when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally ⓓ<u>earn</u> higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, ⓔ<u>find</u> that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation:
ⓔ번(find)이 포함된 문장에서 이미 본동사 'conducted'가 쓰였으므로, 콤마 뒤에 이어지는 부분은 부수적인 상황이나 결과를 나타내는 분사구문이 되어야 합니다. 문맥상 연구자가 결과를 '찾아낸/발견한' 능동의 관계이므로, 동사원형 'find'를 현재분사인 'finding'으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

[오답 분석]
ⓐ provides: 주격 관계대명사절 내의 동사로, 선행사인 단수 명사 'work'와 수일치가 적절합니다.
ⓑ count: 주어인 'Those'에 연결되는 두 번째 동사로, 앞에서 쓰인 'find'와 병렬 구조를 이루며 복수 형태인 'count'가 적절하게 쓰였습니다.
ⓒ that: 타동사 'showing'의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로, 뒤에 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 적절합니다.
ⓓ earn: 상관접속사 'not only A but also B' 구문에서 주어인 'they'에 호응하는 복수 동사로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 30번]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to ____________________________________. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ③ understand the process of evolution
④ recognize details in our surroundings
⑤ know the differences between vehicles
questions.explanation: 지문은 이동 속도가 주변의 세부 사항을 인식하는 능력에 영향을 미친다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 걷는 속도(시속 5마일 이하)에서는 세부 사항을 잘 인식하지만, 자동차처럼 빠른 속도에서는 인식 능력이 제한된다고 설명하므로 빈칸에는 '우리 주변의 세부 사항을 인식하는(recognize details in our surroundings)' 능력이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이동 시간을 조절하는
② 환경 문제를 인지하는
③ 진화의 과정을 이해하는
④ 우리 주변의 세부 사항을 인식하는
⑤ 차량들 사이의 차이점을 아는

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to ______________________________________ from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
options: ① be sure to seek advice from an expert
② take a few step back from the painting
③ check the time and place of the painting
④ select a similar picture to complete the painting
⑤ set some empty space to complete the painting
questions.explanation: 그림을 그릴 때 한 부분에만 집중하기보다 전체를 골고루 작업해야 어느 시점에서든 완결성을 가질 수 있다는 내용입니다. 또한, 작가들이 그림을 멈출 때를 아는 것이 어려워 과하게 덧칠하는 경우가 많으므로, 때때로 그림에서 '거리를 두고 물러나서' 진행 상황을 객관적으로 평가하는 것이 중요하다는 흐름입니다. 따라서 ②번이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 전문가로부터 조언을 구하도록 확실히 한다
② 그림에서 몇 걸음 뒤로 물러난다
③ 그림의 시간과 장소를 확인한다
④ 그림을 완성하기 위해 유사한 사진을 선택한다
⑤ 그림을 완성하기 위해 빈 공간을 설정한다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Taste is one of the traditional five senses. It refers to the ability to detect the flavor of substances such as food, certain minerals, and poisons. Taste is a sensory function of the central nervous system. The receptor cells for taste in humans are found on the surface of the tongue. All of the taste sensations arise from all regions of the oral cavity, despite the common misconception of a "taste map" that is thought to ___________________________________________. options: ① mean that humans receive tastes through sensory organs

④ help us to understand what basic tastes are
⑤ show where taste buds are mainly located
questions.explanation: 이 글은 미각이 혀의 특정 부위에서만 느껴진다는 이른바 '맛 지도'가 잘못된 상식임을 설명하고 있습니다. 실제로는 입안의 모든 부위에서 다양한 맛을 느낄 수 있다고 설명하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 '맛 지도'가 무엇으로 여겨지는지(오해의 내용)에 대한 설명인 '각 맛에 대해 혀의 특정 부위와 일치한다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간이 감각 기관을 통해 맛을 받아들인다는 것을 의미한다
② 각 맛에 대해 혀의 특정 부위와 일치한다
③ 입천장을 중요하지 않은 것으로 언급한다
④ 기본적인 맛이 무엇인지 이해하도록 돕는다
⑤ 맛봉오리가 주로 어디에 위치하는지 보여준다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. ⓐCommon sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. ⓑAs examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and a smaller field. ⓒChildren and parents want more opportunities to play safely close to where they live. ⓓAll have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. ⓔIn a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성인용 스포츠 환경에 적응하기 어려운 어린 아이들을 위해 스포츠 규칙이나 장비가 어떻게 변형되었는지를 설명하고 있습니다. ⓒ의 '아이들과 부모들이 거주지 근처에서 안전하게 놀 수 있는 더 많은 기회를 원한다'는 내용은 스포츠의 아동용 변형이라는 중심 내용과 거리가 멉니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? (A) Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. (B) For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. (C) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. (D) Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. (E) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 아리스토텔레스가 주장한 '5가지 감각'이라는 전통적 관점을 의심할 이유가 있다는 내용입니다. (A)까지는 아리스토텔레스의 견해를 설명하고 있으며, (B) 뒤의 'For a start'부터는 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 인간의 감각들을 구체적으로 열거하며 반박을 시작하므로 주어진 문장은 (B) 자리에 오는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. (B) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. (C) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (D) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. (E) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.insertion_sentence: But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition.
questions.explanation: (D) 문장에서는 일부 저자들이 지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)을 수면의 정의에 포함하지 않는다고 언급합니다. 주어진 문장의 'But'은 이에 대한 반론으로, 지각적 이탈 없이는 잠을 자는 것이 불가능하므로 그것이 수면의 정의에 필수적이라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (E) 앞에 위치하여 (D)의 내용과 대조를 이루고 흐름을 이어가야 합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절할 것은?
questions.passage: Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal.
questions.summary_sentence: Considering each animal's environmental or genetic (A)_____________, we should (B)_____________ methods of providing care or assistance to animals to meet their distinct needs.
questions.explanation: 본문은 동물의 유전적 차이(같은 배에서 태어나도 다름)와 환경적 차이(구조 센터 vs 가정)에 따라 치유 반응이 다르므로, 개별적인 필요에 맞춰 치료를 조정해야 한다고 강조합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 'differences(차이점)', (B)에는 개별화하다 또는 특수하게 맞추다라는 의미의 'individualize'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 상관관계 / 사용자 정의하다
② 대조 / 방치하다

④ 성격 / 무시하다
⑤ 차이점 / 개별화하다

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 쓰시오.
questions.passage: •글 속에서 찾아 쓸 것•어형 변화 필요 없음[24년 3월 34번](지문 내용이 잘렸으나, 해당 번호의 원문은 다음과 같습니다)We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all seniors thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
questions.summary_sentence: We often (A)_____________ how we are seen through our own (B)_____________, believing we are better than the average person.

(단, 학교 측 정답 (A) underestimate는 지문 맥락에 따라 '부정적인 특성을 가지고 있을 가능성을 과소평가한다'는 의미 등으로 사용되었을 가능성이 큼)

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 아래의 두 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The Inca Empire constructed monumental feats of architecture and developed incredible innovations in agriculture. Seeing as the Inca were without wheeled vehicles or riding animals, most of the long-distance transportation throughout the network was done on foot. The Inca used the chasqui - also known as "the runners" - to deliver messages throughout the empire. These fast, highly-trained, and incredibly fit messengers were estimated to run as much as 200 miles per day. They delivered everything from news to lightweight goods like fish. Relay stations, called tambos, were used for the chasquis to stop and transfer messages efficiently to the next chasqui, who would carry the message on through the rest of the empire.
questions.summary_sentence: The Inca Empire, which excelled in architecture and agriculture, relied on foot transportation, with chasquis (A)_____________ messages. In addition, relay stations facilitated the (B)_____________ transfer of messages between chasquis.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 참고하여 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말을 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.summary_sentence: Assuming that the same crops are continued to be planted, (A)_____________ will be planted in the first filed, (B)_____________ in the second field, and (C)_____________ in the third field, in the fifth year.
