questions.explanation: 본문에 따르면 3년 주기의 윤작이 이루어집니다. 1년차(4년차와 동일) 순서는 1번 밭: carrots, 2번 밭: green beans, 3번 밭: tomatoes입니다. 4년차에 다시 원래 순서(1년차)로 돌아간다고 명시되어 있으므로, 5년차는 2년차와 동일한 순서가 됩니다. 2년차 순서는 본문에 'green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third'라고 기술되어 있습니다. 따라서 (A) green beans, (B) tomatoes, (C) carrots가 정답입니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter won't be identical even if they display some same features; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. ⓐEnvironmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. ⓑFor instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. ⓒIn addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. ⓓThat's why physical therapy is a growing field that helps people recover from injuries. ⓔWith this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal.*litter: (한 배에서 태어난) 새끼들
questions.explanation: ※ ④번 문윑은 물리 츘료가 사람의 부상 회복을 돕는 분야라는 내용으로, 동물마다 츘료 반응이 다르므로 개별화된 츘료 접근이 필요하다는 전체 글의 흤름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The idea of the tongue having separate areas for different tastes, such as sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back, was proven wrong by research in the 1980s and 1990s. ⓐThis ‖tongue map‖ was actually a misunderstanding of research from Germany in the early 20th century. ⓑNowadays, leading taste researchers believe taste buds are not specialized in certain areas. ⓒIf anything, sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted anywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived with varying intensity in different places. ⓓAs a result, we find that taste buds are specialized in specific areas and prove the truth of the tongue map. ⓔMoreover, the mechanism at work is not where you taste a flavor, but when you register it; sweetness, for instance, might be noticed first, but it's not limited to the tip of the tongue.*taste bud: 미료
questions.explanation: 전체 글은 훌의 부위마다 다른 맛을 눐긴다는 '훌 지도' 개념이 투렸음을 설명하고 읈습니다. ④번 문윑은 미료가 특정 부위에 특화되어 훌 지도가 사실임을 짝명한다는 내용으로, 글의 주제와 정반대되는 진술입니다.
options_translation: ① ⑀
② ⑁
③ ⑂
④ ⑃
⑤ ⑄

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into ⑀<u>positive</u> statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as ‖I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day.‖ Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a ⑁<u>shift</u> in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive. Before you experience this change, be sure that you matter. And there's nothing wrong with you being the most important person. Magical affirmation is about having ⑂<u>doubt</u> about your abilities. Believing that you're worth something. Pay attention to what you tell yourself. Understand that you're doing the best you can. Nobody becomes successful overnight. Tell yourself that you're getting ⑃<u>closer</u> to success every single day. Since it's in your hands to be happy, tell yourself that you're completely in charge. Nobody is ⑄<u>responsible</u> for anything in your life except you. Your happiness lies within you.*affirmation: 공정
questions.explanation: 글의 문맥사 마벽과 같은 확신(affirmation)은 자신의 능력에 대한 '뮿음' 혹은 '신뢰'를 갖는 경이므로, ⑂의 doubt(의심)는 confidence(신뢰) 등의 단어로 바귀어야 합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: People differ in how ⑀<u>quickly</u> they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and ⑁<u>lengthen</u> your day compared to traveling eastward and shortening it. This east-west difference in jet lag seems so ⑂<u>sizable</u> that it can have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward ⑃<u>performs</u> significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence ⑄<u>that</u> traveling eastward is more challenging than traveling westward. *jet lag: 시차로 인한 피로감
questions.explanation: ⑃번이 포함된 문윑의 주어는 'teams(복수)'이고 flying westward는 주어를 수식하는 분사구입니다. 따라서 동사는 복수 형태인 perform이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 6. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(B) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.

(C) These examples of humans and animals tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to sort various animal senses into fixed categories, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각을 5가지로 정의했다는 내용을 소개합니다. (B)에서 'However'를 사용하여 이 견해에 의문을 제기하며 인간에게서 누락된 감각(고유 감각, 평형 감각)을 언급합니다. 이어지는 (A)에서는 인간뿐만 아니라 '다른 동물들(Other animals)'의 특이한 감각 사례를 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 'These examples of humans and animals'를 통해 앞선 사례들을 종합하며 감각을 고정된 범주로 나누기보다는 있는 그대로 연구해야 한다는 결론을 내립니다.

questions.question: 7. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people wrongly assume that if someone displays one characteristic, they automatically possess others associated with it.
ordered_passages: (A) After the lecture, the students shared their impressions of the lecturer. As expected, there were significant differences in the impressions formed by the students based on the initial information they received about the lecturer.

(B) In a study, university students were provided with descriptions of a guest lecturer before he addressed the group. Half of the students received descriptions containing the word 'warm', while the other half were informed he was 'cold'.

(C) Moreover, students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact more with him. This indicates that our expectations not only shape the impressions we form but also influence our behavior and the relationships we establish.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 하나의 특징으로 다른 특징까지 판단하는 경향에 대해 말합니다. (B)에서 이를 실험하기 위해 학생들에가 'warm'과 'cold'라는 사전 정밴를 제공한 사례가 나옵니다. (A)에서 그 결과로 인상이 달랼졌음을 보여준 홄, (C)에서 그것이 행동에까지 영향을 미친다는 결론을 내립니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The above graph shows the extent to which young people aged 16-25 in six countries had fear about climate change in 2021. ⓐIn the Philippines, the total percentage of extremely worried and very worried youth was the highest among the six countries. ⓑIn Portugal, the percentage of young people who were extremely worried was 5 percent lower than that of young people who were very worried. ⓒIn France, the percentage of young generation who more than twice as high as that of young generation who said that they were very worried. ⓓIn the United Kingdom, the percentage of young people who said they were very worried was less than 30 percent. ⓔThe United States had the lowest total percentage of young people who said they were extremely and very worried, at 46 percent.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "putting on the same clothes" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ① students' rubber-stamp approach to learning
② skillful learners' use of different learning strategies
③ the best way to analyze the test results as a student
④ importance of the right dress for different occasions
⑤ negative effects of multiple-choice tests on students' learning
questions.explanation: 이 글은 모든 상황에 동일한 방식을 적용하는 '고무도장 방식'의 학습이 아니라, 상황과 과제의 성격에 맞게 유연하게 다양한 학습 전략을 사용하는 숙련된 학습자들의 특징에 대해 설명하고 있습니다.

④ 다양한 상황에 맞는 적절한 복장의 중요성
⑤ 선다형 시험이 학생들의 학습에 미치는 부정적인 영향

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we must consider its costs. Many traditional jobs have been replaced by progress, and the way of life around those jobs has changed. Today, millions of people work in jobs they don't like, making things they don't care about. These jobs can even cause physical pain, disability, or long-term illness. Technology also creates new jobs that can be risky. Additionally, education and media encourage people to avoid manual labor and aim for jobs in the digital world. This separation of physical and mental work can be stressful. Furthermore, the sedentary nature of well-paying jobs poses health risks for both the body and mind.     *manual: 육체노동의      *sedentary: 주로 앉아서 하는
options: ① disadvantages of employing technology n the field of health care
② risks from increasing use of high technology in workplaces
③ importance of physical activities for workers
④ prospects for the development of technology
⑤ business trends in the digital era
questions.explanation: 지문은 기술 도입이 가져오는 비용(대가)에 대해 설명하며, 전통적인 일자리의 소멸, 원치 않는 노동, 건강상의 문제(질병, 신체적 고통), 디지털 업무로 인한 스트레스 및 주로 앉아서 일하는 습관으로 인한 건강 위험 등 기술 발전에 따른 일터에서의 위험 요소들을 다루고 있습니다.

⑤ 디지털 시대의 비즈니스 트렌드

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to _________________________________ from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.*tempting: 유혹하는*refinement: 정교하게 꾸밈
options: ① work excessively on a painting
② make sure that every detail is not lost
③ take a few steps back from the painting

questions.explanation: 작업이 과해지는 것을 막고 진행 상황을 평가하기 위해 '가끔씩 그림에서 물러나 살펴보는 것'이 중요하다는 문맥이므로 ③번 '그림에서 몇 걸음 뒤로 물러나는 것'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그림 작업을 과도하게 하는 것
② 모든 세부 사항이 유실되지 않도록 확인하는 것
③ 그림에서 몇 걸음 뒤로 물러나는 것

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, _____________________________. Messengers were stationed along the royal roads to carry out the Inca king's orders and bring back reports from his territories. Known as Chasquis, these messengers lived in groups of four to six in huts positioned every one to two miles along the roads. They were young men selected for their exceptional running skills, tasked with keeping watch over the roads in both direction. If they spotted another messenger approaching, they would quickly move out to meet them. The Inca strategically positioned these huts on elevated terrain within sight of each other. As a messenger approached the next hut, he would start calling out and repeat the message several times to the one coming out to meet him. This relay system enabled messages to travel up to 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under favor conditions. While effective, this method required a significant number of runners.*elevated: 높은
options: ① the Spanish conquest of the Inca empire was fueled
② the Inca empire developed its regional system of government
③ the Inca empire used other animals such as llamas and alpacas
④ smoke signals were used by the Inca empire to deliver the king's messages
⑤ there were runners who specialized in delivering messages at the Inca empire
questions.explanation: 지문은 말이 없는 상황에서 잉카 제국이 뛰어난 달리기 실력을 가진 'Chasquis'라 불리는 전령들을 도로에 배치하여 메시지를 전달하는 릴레이 시스템을 구축했다는 내용을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ⑤번 '잉카 제국에는 메시지를 전달하는 것을 전문으로 하는 달리기 주자들이 있었다'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 스페인의 잉카 제국 정복이 가속화되었다
② 잉카 제국은 지역 정부 시스템을 발전시켰다
③ 잉카 제국은 라마나 알파카와 같은 다른 동물들을 사용했다
④ 왕의 메시지를 전달하기 위해 잉카 제국에서 봉화 신호가 사용되었다
⑤ 잉카 제국에는 메시지 전달을 전문으로 하는 달리기 주자들이 있었다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling _________________________________________. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.*distinguish: 구별하다*pedestrian: 보행자
options: ① influences one's ability to process environmental details
② affects decision-making abilities in dynamic situations
③ depends on the level of comfort experienced by passengers
④ plays an important role in determining arrival times and scheduling
⑤ cannot change the perception of the surrounding environment
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력에 영향을 미친다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 인간의 감각은 걷는 속도에 최적화되어 있어, 빠른 자동차 운전자는 세부 사항을 파악하기 어렵고 느린 보행자는 더 잘 파악할 수 있다는 예시를 통해 빈칸의 내용을 뒷받침합니다.
options_translation: ① 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력에 영향을 미친다
② 역동적인 상황에서의 의사 결정 능력에 영향을 준다
③ 승객이 느끼는 편안함의 수준에 달려 있다
④ 도착 시간과 일정을 결정하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다
⑤ 주변 환경에 대한 인식을 변화시킬 수 없다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There is no point in trying to gear up for a task requiring a significant amount of time available when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
options: ① 계획을 세울 때 오랜 시간이 걸리는 과제일수록 뒤로 미루어라.
② 해야할 일의 목록을 작성할 때 최대한 많은 과제를 넣을수록 좋다.
③ 일의 성취를 위해 과제 수행 시간을 파악하고 과제를 적절한 시간에 배치하라.
④ 과제를 정확하게 수행하는 것이 시간 내에 수행하는 것보다 더 중요하다.
⑤ 해야할 일의 목록을 매일 작성하면 업무를 경감하는데 도움이 된다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 계획한 일을 성취하기 위해 각 과제가 얼마나 걸릴지 파악하고, 이용 가능한 시간에 맞춰 과제를 배치하는 것이 중요하다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 특히 긴 과제를 위해 시간을 할애하고 짧은 과제는 그 사이의 남는 시간에 배치하라고 조언합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. (A) Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. (B) This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. (C) However, they still use their front legs like human hands (D) For example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw, and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. (E) A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.insertion_sentence: In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 최근 애니메이션 영화에서 동물을 보다 '자연스러운' 방식으로 묘사하는 경향이 생겼다는 새로운 흐름을 소개합니다. (C) 앞까지는 동물을 인간처럼 변형하여 묘사하는 전통적인 방식을 설명하고 있으며, (C) 바로 뒤의 문장이 '그러나 그들은 여전히 앞발을 인간의 손처럼 사용한다'라며 대조를 이루고 있습니다. 따라서 '자연스러운 묘사 트렌드'를 언급한 제시문이 (C) 위치에 와야만, 뒤이어 나오는 '그럼에도 불구하고 여전히 인간 같은 특징(앞발 사용)이 남아있다'는 역접의 내용이 자연스럽게 이어집니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: In a story by Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, Alice races with the Red Queen through the countryside. (A) They run and run, but end up back where they started, under the same tree. (B) The Red Queen tells Alice that it takes all their effort just to stay in place. (C) Biologists use this idea, the Red Queen Effect, to explain evolution. (D) These babies are also fast, making it harder for foxes to catch them. (E) So, even though both foxes and rabbits are getting faster, they're still just staying at the same level, like running on a treadmill.
questions.insertion_sentence: For instance, if foxes evolve to run faster and catch more rabbits, only the fastest rabbits survive to have babies.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 생물학에서의 '붉은 여왕 효과'를 설명하기 위한 구체적인 예시로, 여우의 진화에 따라 가장 빠른 토끼들만이 살아남아 새끼를 낳게 된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (D) 바로 뒤의 문장이 "These babies(이 새끼들)"로 시작하며, 이 지시어가 가리키는 대상이 주어진 문장의 "the fastest rabbits survive to have babies"에서 언급된 새끼들이므로, 주어진 문장은 (D) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.      *compound: 화합물
questions.summary_sentence: Natural processes, such as cooling magma, determine the (A)____________ of minerals, with factors like elemental composition and cooling (B)____________ influencing crystal size.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 마그마가 식으면서 광물이 어떻게 형성되는지를 설명합니다. (A)는 광물의 '형성(formation)'을 의미하며, (B)는 마그마가 식는 '속도(rate)'가 결정의 크기에 영향을 미친다는 내용을 포함해야 합니다. 따라서 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 형성 / 속도
② 형성 / 위치
③ 분류 / 위치
④ 기능 / 속도
⑤ 기능 / 강도

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: When we think about leaders, famous figures like Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. often come to mind. Considering their historical importance and wide influence, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. However, theses individuals started their journeys as ordinary people - students, workers, and citizens - with ideas about how to make life better for many. With hard work and experience, they developed their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking feedback, and always striving to find the best ways to achieve goals together. This shows that each of us has the potential to be a leader, whether at school, in our communities, or at work, no matter what our age or lever of experience.
options: ① Who Can Be a Leader?
② All Leaders Were Born Famous
③ Good Examples of Great Leaders in History
④ Leadership Dynamics: Navigating Paths to Success
⑤ Interaction: The Only Skill for Survival Within a Group
questions.explanation: 본문은 위대한 지도자들도 처음에는 평범한 사람들이었으며, 누구나 지도자가 될 잠재력을 가지고 있다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '누가 리더가 될 수 있는가?'라는 질문을 던지는 ①번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 누가 리더가 될 수 있는가?
② 모든 리더는 유명하게 태어났다
③ 역사 속 위대한 리더들의 좋은 사례들
④ 리더십 역학: 성공으로 가는 길 탐색하기
⑤ 상호작용: 집단 내 생존을 위한 유일한 기술

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall. * numerous: 수많은
options: ① Why Happiness at Work Is a Myth
② Hard Work Doesn't Always Lead to Success
③ To Achieve Work-Life Happiness, Stop Pretending to Be Happy
④ Meaningful Work: Enhancing Happiness and Fulfillment in Life
⑤ Which Is More Essential: Having a High Salary or Job Satisfaction?
questions.explanation: 이 글은 일에서 의미를 찾는 것이 개인의 행복과 삶의 만족도를 높이는 데 얼마나 중요한지를 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '의미 있는 일: 삶의 행복과 성취감을 강화하기'라는 내용의 ④번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 직장에서의 행복이 허구인 이유
② 노력이 항상 성공으로 이어지는 것은 아니다
③ 일과 삶의 행복을 얻으려면, 행복한 척하는 것을 그만두라
④ 의미 있는 일: 삶의 행복과 성취감을 강화하기
⑤ 무엇이 더 필수적인가: 높은 급여 혹은 직무 만족?

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 요지를 조건에 맞게 한 문장으로 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change. * barnacle: 따개비 * dispersal: 분산 * fossil: 화석
subjective_conditions: 1. 17단어 이내로 작성할 것
2. a place, force, all creatures, survive를 모두 사용할 것 (단어 변형 가능)
3. 완전한 한 개의 문장으로 작성할 것
questions.answer: Climate change forces all creatures to move to a place where they can survive. (또는 All creatures are forced to move to a place where they can survive because of climate change.)
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화가 모든 생물을 생존이 가능한 장소로 이동하게 만든다는 내용의 글입니다. 제시된 단어를 활용하여 '기후 변화는 모든 생물이 생존할 수 있는 장소로 이동하도록 강제한다'라는 의미를 담아 문장으로 구성하면 됩니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고 문맥에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: It is difficult for any of us to maintain a constant level of attention throughout our working day. We all have body rhythms characterised by peaks and valleys of energy and alertness. You will achieve more, and feel confident as a benefit, if you schedule your most demanding tasks at times when you are best able to cope with them. If you haven't thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to observe yourself. Try to note the times ___________________________________. We are all different. For some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for others it may take a while to warm up.*alertness: 기민함
subjective_conditions: 1. 7단어 이내로 작성할 것(빈칸만)
2. which를 사용할 것
3. 빈칸을 완성하여 완전한 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.answer: in which you are at your best
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 자신의 에너지 수준이 가장 높은 정점(peak)인 시간을 관찰하여 기록하라는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. '당신이 최상의 상태에 있는 시간'이라는 의미를 'which'를 사용하여 관계절로 표현하면 'in which you are at your best'가 됩니다. times를 선행사로 하는 관계부사 when을 대신하여 '전치사+관계대명사' 구조를 사용한 형태입니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고 문맥에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: __________________________________. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.*prevail: 널리 퍼지다
subjective_conditions: 1. 10단어 이내로 작성할 것(빈칸만)
2. make, help를 모두 사용할 것(변형 가능)
3. 빈칸을 완성하여 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.answer: Different sports have made adaptations to help children.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성인 위주의 스포츠 환경이 어린 아이들에게 부적합하다는 것을 깨닫고, 아이들을 돕기 위해 여러 스포츠들이 변형(adaptation)을 거쳤다는 내용을 다룹니다. 따라서 '다양한 스포츠들이 아이들을 돕기 위해 조정을 해왔다'는 내용을 'make'와 'help'를 사용하여 영작하면 됩니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 문맥에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: There are some studies showing the impact of music on mental health positively. A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that __________________________________. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence. Hense and McFerran, working with young people in a youth mental health service, showed that encouraging young people to express their musical identities might help them recover from mental illness.  *therapy: 치료  *efficacy: 효능
subjective_conditions: 1. 17단어 이내로 작성할 것(빈칸만)
2. led to, mental, individuals, a choir를 모두 사용할 것(변형 불가)
3. 빈칸을 완성하여 완전한 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.answer: participating in a choir led to improvements in the mental health of individuals with mental health conditions
questions.explanation: 이 글은 음악(특히 합창/노래)이 정신 건강에 미치는 긍정적인 영향을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸은 연구 결과의 요약이 들어가야 하며, 주어진 조건을 활용하여 '합창단에 참여하는 것이 정신 질환을 가진 개인들의 정신 건강 개선으로 이어졌다'는 의미의 문장을 완성해야 합니다. 정답은 "participating in a choir led to improvements (recovery) in the mental health of individuals with mental health conditions (problems)"와 같은 구조가 됩니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 문맥에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. So, when you decide how to act in uncertain conditions, more often than not, ____________________________________________.  *subtle: 미묘한        *hassle: 성가신 일
subjective_conditions: 1. 11단어 이내로 작성할 것(빈칸만)
2. practices, advantageous를 모두 사용할 것(변형 불가)
3. 빈칸을 완성하여 완전한 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.answer: it is advantageous to adopt the practices of people around you
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 불확실한 상황에서 타인의 행동(사회적 증거)을 따르는 경향이 생존에 유리했음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 결론 부분인 빈칸에는 '주변 사람들의 관행을 따르는 것이 유리하다'는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 조건에 제시된 단어들을 사용하여 "it is advantageous to adopt the practices of people around you"라고 작성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고 문맥에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 작성하시오. [2.9점]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. _____________________________________________, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.*novice: 초보
subjective_conditions: 1. 11단어 이내로 작성할 것(빈칸만)
2. expert, how, a task, novice를 모두 사용할 것(변형 가능)
3. 빈칸을 완성하여 완전한 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.answer: Experts can undervalue how difficult a task is for novices
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전문가가 초보자에게 자신의 분야를 가르칠 때 겪는 어려움, 즉 '지식의 저주'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 전문가는 자신이 그 기술을 습득하는 데 얼마나 공을 들였는지 잊어버리고, 초보자가 그 일을 배우는 것이 얼마나 어려운지 과소평가한다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 주어진 단어들을 조합하여 '전문가들이 초보자들에게 과업이 얼마나 어려운지를 과소평가할 수 있다'는 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 6. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick.
ordered_passages: (A) Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as 'I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day.'

(B) Write down all the real time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence.
(C) You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
questions.explanation: 마법을 부리는 비결로 먼저 (B)에서 아찰면한 도전 과제를 긍정적인 문육으로 바꾸어 쓰라고 하고, (A)에서 그에 대한 구체적인 예시(일찍 일어나기)를 들어줍니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 문육을 쓰는 겼의 효과(생각걠 행동의 변화)를 설몂하는 흠름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered 'finished.' Artists often ①<u>find it difficult</u> to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on ②<u>adding more to</u> your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to ③<u>announce your progress.</u> Putting too much into a painting can ④<u>spoil its impact</u> and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, ⑤<u>take a break</u> and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation: 그림에서 물러나서 진행 상황을 '판단하거나 평가하기'(assess / evaluate)윔한 겼이지, '발표하는'(announce) 겼은 문맥상 어사합니다.

questions.question: 10. 윗글의 묔줄 차 that의 시임과 같은 것은? [24년 3월 29번]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their work find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count it as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing <u>that</u> when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.*numerous: 수많은
options: ① <u>That</u> was the last meeting about the issue.
② I hope <u>that</u> the Korean national football team wins.
③ She is the only student <u>that</u> wears a blue cap.
④ <u>That</u> cake is the present that I made for your birthday.
⑤ Our school's playground is larger than <u>that</u> of your school.
questions.explanation: 밤문의 that은 현재분사 showing의 목적어절을 이끄는 명사절 접셍사입니다. ②번의 that 또한 동사 hope의 목적어절을 이끄는 접셍사입니다.
options_translation: ① 그것은 그 문제에 대한 마지막 회의였다. (지시댄명사)
② 나는 한국 국가대표 축구팀이 이기길 바란다. (접셍사)
③ 그녀는 파란 모자림 쓴 유일한 학생이다. (관계댄명사)
④ 접 케이크뉄 내가 너의 생일을 위해 만든 선물이다. (지시형용사)
⑤ 옰리 학교 운동장은 너희 학교의 광장보다 더 탭다. (지시댄명사)

questions.question: 11. 윗글의 내용을 다음과 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 각각 들어갈 말로 가장 적합한 1개의 단어림 찾아 형태 변형 없이 시시오. [24년 3월 29번]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their work find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count it as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing <u>that</u> when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.*numerous: 수많은
questions.summary_sentence: According to the above passage, some studies revealed a strong positive correlation between (A)___________ satisfaction and overall (B)___________ happiness.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 '일(직업)'에서 얻는 만접감이 '삶' 전체의 행복과 밀중한 관렠이 있다는 내용이므로, 밤문에서 job(직업)과 life(삶)림 찾아 쓸 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. (A) As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. (B) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. (C) Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. (D) It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 맛을 인지하는 메커니즘이 장소가 아니라 시간이라는 내용입니다. (D) 뒤의 문장이 '혀끝에서 단맛을 느끼는 것이 아니라 그 감각을 가장 먼저 인지하는 것이다'라고 시간을 언급하고 있으므로 (D) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 문장 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike.
ordered_passages: (A) Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment.

(B) With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go: healing is a constant learning process.
(C) In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion.

(D) Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session.*litter: (한 배에서 태어난) 새끼들
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 동물은 똑같지 않다는 화두를 던집니다. (D) 같은 배에서 난 새끼들도 서로 다르므로 치유 과정에서 반응이 다를 수 있음을 설명합니다. (A) 또한 환경적 요인(구조 센터 vs 가정)에 따라 반응이 달라질 수 있음을 'also'를 통해 추가합니다. (C) 게다가(In addition) 신체적 질병과 정서적 혼란 중 무엇을 치유하느냐에 따라 또 다르다는 점을 덧붙입니다. (B) 이러한 점들을 염두에 두고(With this in mind) 매 세션을 개별적으로 조정해야 한다는 결론으로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To whom it may concern,I am a resident of the Blue Sky Apartment. Recently I observed that the kid zone is in need of repairs. I want you to pay attention to the poor condition of the playground equipment in the zone. The swings are damaged, the paint is falling off, and some of the bolts on the slide are missing. The facilities have been in this terrible condition since we moved here. They are dangerous to the children playing there. Would you please have them repaired? I would appreciate your immediate attention to solve this matter.
options: ① To introduce enhanced security system
② To notify temporary closure of apartment playground
③ To request compensation for apartment playground accident
④ To inform guidelines for using apartment facilities of residents
⑤ To call for repair of apartment playground equipment
questions.explanation: 아파트 단지 내 놀이터 시설물(그네, 미끄럼틀 등)의 노후 및 파손 상태를 지적하며 수리를 요청(Would you please have them repaired?)하는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 강화된 보안 시스템을 소개하기 위해
② 아파트 놀이터의 일시적 폐쇄를 알리기 위해
③ 아파트 놀이터 사고에 대한 보상을 요청하기 위해
④ 거주자들에게 아파트 시설 이용 가이드라인을 알리기 위해
⑤ 아파트 놀이터 장비 수리를 요구하기 위해

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we __________________________. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk ─ for body and mind.*chronic: 만성의 **sedentary: 주로 앉아서 하는
options: ① can enhance efficiency in the workplace
questions.explanation: 지문 전체의 내용은 기술 도입이 전통적인 생계 수단을 밀어내고, 인간을 싫어하는 일에 종사하게 하며, 육체적/정신적 건강 위험을 초래한다는 부정적인 영향을 다루고 있습니다. (본문의 선택지 ④가 누락되어 있으나 제공된 정답 15번의 ④를 참고할 때 '대가를 치러야 한다(need to pay a cost)'와 같은 맥락의 문장이 들어갈 것으로 유추됩니다. 단, 제공된 텍스트에는 선택지가 ①번만 나타나 있어 완전한 분석이 어렵습니다.)
options_translation: ① 작업장에서 효율성을 높일 수 있다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
options: ① Everyone experiences jet lag at the same rate.
② It's easier to adjust to traveling westward than eastward.
③ Jet lag has no significant impact on athletic performance.
④ Professional baseball players experience more jet lag than any other sport players.
⑤ There is no recent evidence to support the claim that eastward travel is harder than westward travel.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 서쪽으로 비행하여 하루를 늘리는 것이 동쪽으로 비행하여 하루를 줄이는 것보다 시차 적응이 쉽다고 언급하고 있습니다. 1번은 사람마다 속도가 다르다고 했으므로 틀리고, 3번은 스포츠 팀 성적에 영향을 미친다고 했으므로 틀립니다. 4번은 야구 선수들이 더 많이 겪는다는 언급은 없으며, 5번은 최근 연구에서도 증거가 발견되었다고 했으므로 틀립니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 사람이 같은 속도로 시차증을 경험한다.
② 동쪽보다 서쪽으로 여행할 때 적응하는 것이 더 쉽다.
③ 시차증은 운동 능력에 큰 영향을 미치지 않는다.
④ 프로 야구 선수들은 다른 어떤 종목 선수들보다 시차증을 더 많이 경험한다.
⑤ 동쪽 여행이 서쪽 여행보다 힘들다는 주장을 뒷받침하는 최근의 증거는 없다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to adopt the practices of those around you.
options: ① 온라인에서 제품 구매 시 상품에 대한 평가와 댓글을 맹신할 경우 속을 수 있으니 주의해야 한다.
② 개인의 판단과 비판적 사고를 기르기 위해서는 다양한 사람들을 만나보는 경험이 무엇보다 중요하다.
③ 인간은 위험하거나 불확실한 경우 주변 사람들의 행동을 따르는 것이 좋고 안전하다고 느낀다.
④ 지역 음식점을 방문할 때, 미리 예약하는 습관을 들이면 줄을 서서 기다리는 수고를 덜 수 있다.
⑤ 무리의 생각에 휩쓸려 개인의 판단을 잃는 집단적인 사고는 반드시 경계해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 무엇이 안전하고 신뢰할 수 있는지 판단하기 위해 '사회적 증거(다른 사람들의 행동)'를 찾는다는 내용을 설명합니다. 진화론적 관점에서 집단을 따르는 것이 생존에 유리했으며, 주변 사람들의 관습을 따르는 것이 좋다는 결론을 내리고 있으므로 3번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop __________ the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.explanation: 윤작(crop rotation)을 통해 토양이 건강하게 유지된다(soil stays healthy)는 내용이 뒤따르므로, 각 작물이 다음 작물을 위해 토양을 '풍요롭게 한다(enrich)'는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 망치다
② 보존하다
③ 조사하다
④ 협력하다
⑤ 비옥하게 하다

questions.question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. ⓐWhen the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. ⓑAll creatures are capable of some degree of movement. ⓒEven creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. ⓓAll creatures share same genes. ⓔFrom fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화에 따라 생물 종이 이동을 해야 하며, 움직이지 못하는 생물도 특정 단계에서 이동 능력을 갖춘다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. ⓓ의 '모든 생물은 동일한 유전자를 공유한다'는 내용은 기후 변화에 따른 생물의 이동이라는 전체 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. (A) Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. (B) If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. (C) The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. (D) When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. (E) The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610km) in three or four days under good conditions.
questions.insertion_sentence: The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 전령들이 왕의 명령을 전달하기 위해 도로에 배치되었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A) 뒤의 문장에서 'Chasquis라고 불리는 그들(they)'이 바로 주어진 문장의 'The messengers'를 가리키므로, 주어진 문장은 (A) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; (A)___________, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. (B)___________, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 동물들은 서로 똑같지 않다고 언급했으므로, 치유 세션에서 다르게 반응한다는 결론이 이어지는 것이 자연스러워 'therefore(따라서)'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞뒤 문장은 동물들이 환경이나 질환의 종류에 따라 다르게 반응한다는 사례들을 추가적으로 나열하고 있으므로 'in addition(게다가)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 예를 들어 / 따라서
② 반면에 / 예를 들어
③ 따라서 / 게다가
④ 더욱이 / 그러나
⑤ 그렇지 않으면 / 한편

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 요지로 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.*distinguish: 구별하다 **pedestrian: 보행자
options: ① Joggers are the fastest users of the street, limiting their ability to perceive details.
② Motorists have the best ability to appreciate environmental details due to their high speed.
③ The design of the environment has no impact on how details are perceived by different travelers.
④ The ability to process environmental details does not change regardless of how fast one is moving.
⑤ The ability to observe details in the environment is highly influenced by the speed at which one is moving.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 셍도가 제공되는 호경을 인식하고 세부 사항을 처리하는 눔력에 큰 영향을 미친다는 내용입니다. 터크성 보다 느린 셍도인 보행자는 세부 사항을 잘 관찰할 수 있지닌, 빠른 셍도의 운전자는 그렇지 못한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 요지로는 ⑤가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 점깅선수들은 길가에서 가장 빠른 사용자들이며, 그들의 세부 사항 인식 눔력을 제한한다.
② 운전자들은 빠른 셍도 덕분에 호경 세부 사항을 감상하는 최고의 눔력을 갖고 있습니다.
③ 호경 디자인은 섑로 다른 이동자들에 의해 세부 사항이 어떻게 인식되는지에 아무뜐 영향을 미치지 않누다.
④ 호경 세부 사항을 처리하는 눔력은 얼마나 빠리 움직이느냐에 상관없이 변하지 않누다.
⑤ 호경의 세부 사항을 관찰하는 눔력은 이동 셍도에 의해 큰 영향을 똛누다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will meant you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "___________". Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.*tempting: 유혹하는 **refinement: 정교하게 꾸뮼
questions.explanation: 한 번에 한 부분에 중중하기바다 그림 전체를 고루 작업하면 어느 지점에서 멈춰도 그림이 '완성된(completed)' 것으로 간주될 수 있다는 내용입니다. 후술되는 내용들이 어제 멈춰야 할지, 마무리 지어야 할지를 결정하는 것과 관련이 있으뭀로 ④가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 일시 정지된
② 섐상된
③ 확장된
④ 완성된
⑤ 버려진

questions.question: 23. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to ________________________. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience. * diligence: 근면
options: ③ accomplish goals for a group
questions.explanation: 이 글은 리더십이 위대한 사람들만이 갖는 고귀하고 높은 목표가 아니라, 우리 모두가 일상적으로 가지고 있는 아이디어를 타인과 공유하고 협력하며 발전시켜 나가는 과정이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 리더는 집단을 위한 목표(goals for a group)를 달성하기 위해 노력하는 사람들이므로, 빈칸에는 '집단을 위한 목표를 달성하기 위한 가장 좋은 방법을 찾는 것'이 오는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사적 이익을 극대화하기
② 개인적인 야망을 통제하기
③ 집단을 위해 목표를 달성하기
④ 외부 영향으로부터 고립하기
⑤ 개별적인 성과를 평가하기

questions.question: 24. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: __________________________________________. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child. * prevail: 널리 퍼지다
options: ① adult players have to simplify their game tactics.
② different sports have made adaptations for children.
③ children need to play with adults to gain experience.
④ young athletes are encouraged to use standard equipment early.
⑤ coaching strategies remain consistent across all age groups.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린아이들이 성인용으로 설계된 스포츠 환경에서 겪는 어려움을 해결하기 위해, 스포츠 종목들이 아동의 발달 수준에 맞게 장비와 규칙을 변형해 왔다는 내용을 다룹니다. 야구(티볼), 미식축구, 축구, 테니스 등의 사례를 통해 다양한 스포츠가 아동에게 적합하도록 적응(adaptation)을 거쳐 왔음을 보여주므로 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 성인 선수들은 경기 전략을 단순화해야 한다.
② 서로 다른 스포츠들이 아동을 위해 변형되어 왔다.
③ 아동은 경험을 쌓기 위해 성인과 함께 경기를 해야 한다.
④ 어린 선수들은 초기에 표준 장비를 사용하도록 권장된다.
⑤ 코칭 전략은 모든 연령대에서 일관되게 유지된다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." (A) This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. (B) In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. (C) As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something. (D) However, if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done." (E)*dissent: 반대
questions.insertion_sentence: If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장 'If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent.(오히려 대부분의 상사들은 자신들이 반대에 찬성한다고 말하기까지 한다.)'는 앞 문장의 내용(어떤 상사도 직원들의 의견 표출을 막는다고 말하지 않는다)을 보강하며 강조하는 역할을 합니다. (A) 뒤의 'This idea'가 제시된 문장에서 언급한 '자신들이 반대 의견에 찬성한다는 생각'을 지칭하므로, (A) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. (A) Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. (B) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. (C) Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. (D) It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first. (E)*taste bud: 미뢰
questions.insertion_sentence: Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장 'Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time.(게다가, 작용하는 메커니즘은 장소가 아니라 시간이다.)'는 장소에 따른 맛 지도가 틀렸다는 내용 뒤에 추가적인 설명을 덧붙이는 문장입니다. (D) 앞 문장에서 맛은 입안 어디에서나 느껴질 수 있다고 설명한 후, (D) 뒤 문장에서 혀 끝에서 단맛을 느끼는 것이 아니라 그 지각을 '먼저(first)' 등록하는 것이라고 '시간'과 관련된 구체적 설명을 하고 있으므로 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 40번]
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more ⓐ<u>control</u> over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down ⓑ<u>infrequently</u> because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in ⓒ<u>biases</u> and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions. While the controllable conscious mind ⓓ<u>deals with</u> thoughts and emotions, the fast-acting subconscious mind stores your responses, ⓔ<u>forming</u> real fears.
options: ① The Role of Memory in Emotional Responses
② Understanding the Speed of the Subconscious Mind
③ The Influence of the Conscious and Subconscious Mind
④ Mastering Emotional Control Through Conscious Thought
⑤ Emotions and Decision Making: Navigating Internal Conflicts
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의식적인 마음과 잠재의식적인 마음의 차이와 각각의 역할(의식적 마음은 생각과 감정을 다루고, 잠재의식적 마음은 반응을 저장하고 실행함)이 어떻게 공포를 형성하고 결정에 영향을 미치는지 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '의식적 마음과 잠재의식적 마음의 영향력'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 정서적 반응에서 기억의 역할
② 잠재의식적 마음의 속도 이해하기

④ 의식적 사고를 통한 감정 조절 숙달하기
⑤ 감정과 의사 결정: 내부 갈등 헤쳐나가기

questions.question: 31. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A) 부분의 우리말과 의미가 같도록 주어진 단어를 사용하여 문장을 완성하시오.
