questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.summary_sentence: Animal cartoon characters and toys are often modified to resemble humans by using their front legs like hands, making (A)___________ facial expressions, or being given childlike characteristics to make them more emotionally (B)___________ to people.
questions.explanation: 본문은 동물 캐릭터가 인간을 닮게 변형되는 방식(손처럼 앞다리 사용, 적절한 표정, 아이 같은 특징 부여)을 설명하며, 이것이 정서적 호소력을 갖게 한다고 말합니다. (A)에는 '적절한(proper, appropriate, suitable)'이 들어가야 하고, (B)에는 사람들에게 '매력적인/호소력 있는(fascinating, appealing, attractive)'이 들어가야 합니다. ⑤번의 proper와 fascinating이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 적절한 - 불쾌한
② 역겨운 - 매력적인
③ 부적절한 - 호소력 있는
④ 적합한 - 공격적인
⑤ 적절한 - 매혹적인

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could ⓐ<u>reside</u> near their farms rather than wander around here and there looking for food. As a result, the ⓑ<u>scale</u> of their residential areas grew bigger. Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more ⓒ<u>systematically</u>. They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task more ⓓ<u>swiftly</u>. For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they had considerable ⓔ<u>difficulty</u> producing more tools in the same amount of time.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 사람들이 농경을 시작하고 공동체 생활을 하면서 협동을 통해 더 효율적으로 일하게 되었다는 내용입니다. 마지막 문장에서 도구 제작자들이 협력함으로써 같은 시간 안에 더 많은 도구를 만들 수 있게 되었으므로, '어려움(difficulty)'을 겪었다는 표현은 문맥상 어색하며 '효율성'이나 '이점(advantage)' 등의 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것만을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
vocabulary_box: ⓐ All carbohydrates are complex carbohydrates and beneficial to your body.
ⓑ Complex carbohydrates can hold other nutrients in their chains since they aren't difficult to break down.
ⓒ Nutrients such as vitamins and minerals in complex carbohydrates can affect your body for many hours because complex carbohydrates break down slowly.
ⓓ Bad carbohydrates, which are simple sugars, contain sufficient nutrients other than the sugars.
ⓔ Bad carbohydrates decompose fairly quickly in your body and most of them turn into fat to be stored.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 모든 탄수화물이 복합 탄수화물인 것은 아니며, 단순 당과 같은 나쁜 탄수화물도 존재합니다. ⓑ 복합 탄수화물은 분해하기 '매우 어렵기(very difficult)' 때문에 영양소를 가둘 수 있는 것입니다. ⓓ 나쁜 탄수화물은 설탕 외에 영양소를 '거의 포함하지 않습니다(hold few nutrients)'. ⓒ와 ⓔ는 본문의 내용과 일치하므로, 일치하지 않는 것은 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ입니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "putting on the same clothes" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They ________________________________. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ① choose rubber-stamp approach in their studying
② are so flexible that they can bend their wrist well
③ use different strategies depending on the situations
④ consider various methods in the same circumstance
⑤ adopt the same way of studying in all the subjects
questions.explanation: 지문은 상황(시험 유형이나 수업)에 따라 유연하게 학습 전략을 바꿔야 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 숙련된 학습자는 유연하며 상황에 따라 다른 전략을 사용한다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그들의 공부에 '고무도장 방식'을 선택한다
② 매우 유연해서 손목을 잘 굽힐 수 있다
③ 상황에 따라 다른 전략을 사용한다
④ 같은 상황에서 다양한 방법을 고려한다
⑤ 모든 과목에서 같은 공부 방식을 채택한다

questions.question: 5. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글을 순서룜 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Lilian Bland was born in Kent, England in 1878. Unlike most other girls at the time she wore trousers and spent her time enjoying adventurous activities like horse riding and hunting. Lilian began her career as a sports and wildlife photographer for British newspapers.
ordered_passages: (A) Soon Lilian was a master driver and ended up working as a car dealer. She never went back to flying but lived a long and exciting life nonetheless.
(B) In 1910 she became the first woman to design, build, and fly her own airplane. In order to persuade her to try a slightly safer activity, Lilian's dad bought her a car.
(C) She married, moved to Canada, and had a kid. Eventually, she moved back to England, and lived there for the rest of her life.
questions.explanation: Lilian Bland의 일생을 시대순으룜 나열하는 문제읅니다. 주어진 글에서 초기 경력을 언급한 후, (B)에서 1910년 비행기 제작 및 비행 경험과 아버지가 사저 차림 소개합단다. (A)에서는 그 차림 통해 숙련된 운전자가 되고 측일러로 일한 내용이 이어지먰, (C)에서 결혼 및 캐나다 이주 후 다시 영국으룜 돌아와 생을 마감하는 결린으룜 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 묜줄 친 봀봄 중, 문맥상 낱말의 싿임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to ⓐ<u>overcome</u> jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's ⓑ<u>easier</u> to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is ⓒ<u>sizable</u> enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying ⓓ<u>eastward</u> in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that westward travel is ⓔ<u>tougher</u> than eastward travel.
questions.explanation: 글의 앞 봀봄에서 서쪽으룜 비행하는 것이 동쪽으룜 비행하는 것밴다 더 쉽다(easier)고 하였고, 서쪽으룜 이동한 팀이 동쪽으룜 이동한 팀밴다 성적이 더 접다고 하였습니다. 따라서 마지막 문장에서 서쪽 이동이 동쪽 이동밴다 더 '힘들다(tougher)'는 표현은 문맥상 반대의 의미이므룜 툐렸습니다. tougher림 easier 등으룜 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글에서 전체 흠름과 가계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew larger. Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. ⓐThey could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. ⓑWhile some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. ⓒTools made from stones were so strong that they were used in various situations. ⓓVillage dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster. ⓔFor example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구석기 시대의 이동 생활에서 농경 시작 후 정착 및 경제적 분업으룜의 변화림 설명하고 읈습니다. 효율적인 업무 분담과 협력에 대해 이얼기하다가 갑자기 '돌룜 만든 도구가 강해서 다양한 상황에 사용되었다'는 내용(ⓒ)은 공동체 생활의 효율성이라는 주제에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
options: ① 구가의 경제적 발전과 함께 사람들의 임금 수준이 향상되었다.
② 근로 조건이 개선되어 사람들은 더 많은 휴가림 얻게 되었다.
③ 장소림 이동할 때 서댄가 빨라지고 비용이 저렴해쥈다.
④ 19세기에 찠도가 생기면서 많은 대형 호텔이 건설되었다.
⑤ 관갑업의 성장이 항공 운섑과 비행기의 출현을 이글었다.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장에서 '항공 운섑의 출현이 ... 관갑업의 성장으룜 이어졌다' (the arrival of air transport ... led to tourism growth)라고 명시되어 읈습니다. 따라서 ⑤는 인과 가계가 반대룜 설명되어 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
options: ① What humans do to communicate with animals
② Ways to draw animal characters more naturally
③ How animal characters are made to look like humans
④ Why human hands are better than an animal's front legs
⑤ Different kinds of facial expressions used by animal characters
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물을 모델로 한 캐릭터나 장난감이 인간의 언어를 사용하거나 인간의 신체적 특징(손처럼 쓰이는 앞발, 인간 같은 얼굴 표정 등)을 갖도록 변형되어 인간을 닮게 만들어지는 방식에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 ③번 '동물 캐릭터가 인간처럼 보이게 만들어지는 방법'입니다.
options_translation: ① 인간이 동물과 의사소통하기 위해 하는 것
② 동물 캐릭터를 더 자연스럽게 그리는 방법
③ 동물 캐릭터가 인간처럼 보이게 만들어지는 방법
④ 왜 인간의 손이 동물의 앞발보다 더 나은가
⑤ 동물 캐릭터에 의해 사용되는 다양한 종류의 얼굴 표정

questions.question: 10. 다음 밑줄 친 Over-optimism이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. <u>Over-optimism</u> about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
options: ① practice in planning a schedule for spare time
② importance of experiencing many different task
③ successful performance in completing tasks on time
④ ignorance about the actual amount of time needed for tasks
⑤ belief that tasks would take longer time than expected
questions.explanation: 지문에서 '특정 시간 내에 무엇을 이룰 수 있는지에 대한 과도한 낙관주의(Over-optimism)가 문제'라고 언급하며, 할 일 목록에 필요한 시간을 추산하고 실제 걸리는 시간을 경험을 통해 배우라고 조언합니다. 이는 사람들이 일을 끝내는 데 실제 얼마나 걸릴지 잘 모르고 너무 짧게 잡는 경향이 있음을 의미하므로, ④ '업무에 필요한 실제 시간 양에 대한 무지'가 가장 적절한 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 여가 시간을 위한 일정을 계획하는 연습
② 많은 다양한 업무를 경험하는 것의 중요성
③ 제시간에 업무를 완수하는 성공적인 수행
④ 업무에 필요한 실제 시간 양에 대한 무지
⑤ 업무가 예상보다 더 오랜 시간이 걸릴 것이라는 믿음

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, ⓐ<u>called</u> magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to ⓑ<u>combine</u> into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, ⓒ<u>repeating</u> patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form ⓓ<u>depend</u> partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form ⓔ<u>are</u> generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'the size of the crystals'입니다. 핵심 주어는 단수인 'the size'이므로 동사도 단수형인 'depends'가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whose story it is affects what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
questions.summary_sentence: By switching the main character, people change their (A)__________ about the story and (B)__________ a different ending.
questions.explanation: 본문은 주인공을 바꾸면 이야기의 초점이 변하고, 다른 인물의 눈으로 사건을 보게 되어 다르게 해석하게 된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 주인공을 바꿈으로써 사람들은 이야기에 대한 그들의 (A) 관점(viewpoint)을 바꾸고, 다른 결말을 (B) 갈망(desire)하게 된다는 요약이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기억 / 갈망
② 관점 / 갈망
③ 갈등 / 싫어함
④ 관점 / 싫어함
⑤ 기억 / 기억함

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to ________________________________.
options: ① follow the actions of those around you
② make a line in front of the restaurant
③ make a reservation in advance
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 무엇이 안전하고 신뢰할 수 있는지 판단하기 위해 '사회적 증거'를 찾는다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 진화론적 관점에서도 집단을 따르는 것이 생존에 유리하므로, 주변 사람들의 행동을 따르는 것이 좋다는 결론이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 주변 사람들의 행동을 따르다
② 식당 앞에 줄을 서다
③ 미리 예약을 하다
④ 다른 사람들의 의견을 무시하다
⑤ 자신을 믿고 행동하다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have (A)[pushed / been pushed] aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, (B)[produced / producing] things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs (C)[who / which] are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk ─ for body and mind.
questions.explanation: (A) 전통적인 생계 수단들이 발전에 의해 '밀려난' 것이므로 수동태인 been pushed가 적절합니다. (B) 수백만 명의 사람들이 자신이 좋아하지 않는 물건을 '생산하면서' 일하는 것이므로 능동의 분사구문인 producing이 적절합니다. (C) 선행사가 'many new jobs'라는 사물이므로 관계대명사 which가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ① The Evolution of Customer-centered Marketing
② Why Do Customers Desire Rare Products?
③ How to Reduce Delivery Costs in Business
④ Dominate the Market : High Quality Items
⑤ Successful Car Manufactures : The Ford
questions.explanation: 과거에는 생산이 수요를 창출한다는 관점이었으나, 현대 사회로 오면서 고객이 실제로 원하는 제품을 제공하고 고객의 다양한 요구를 충족시키는 것이 비즈니스의 중심이 되었다는 마케팅 혁명에 관한 글입니다. 따라서 제목으로는 '고객 중심 마케팅의 진화'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고객 중심 마케팅의 진화
② 왜 고객들은 희귀한 제품을 갈망하는가?
③ 사업에서 배송 비용을 줄이는 방법
④ 시장을 지배하라: 고품질 품목들
⑤ 성공적인 자동차 제조업체들: 포드

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분에 대한 설명으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use <u>this Red Queen Effect</u> to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster ─ in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
options: ① 제 자리에 머무는 것은 노력이 필요하지 않다.
② 주변 환경 변화에 둔감한 종만이 오래 살아남는다.
③ 진화를 하는 데 있어 주변 환경의 변화는 상관이 없다.
④ 생존하기 위해서는 지속적으로 적응하고 진화해야 한다.
⑤ 달리기는 꾸준한 호흡을 유지할 수 있는 좋은 운동이다.
questions.explanation: 붉은 여왕 효과(Red Queen Effect)는 주변 유기체들이 끊임없이 진화하기 때문에, 한 종이 제자리에 머물기 위해서(생존하기 위해서)는 전력을 다해 진화해야 한다는 상대적 진화 원리를 설명합니다. 여우가 빨라지면 토끼도 빨라져야 생존할 수 있다는 예시를 통해 생존을 위한 지속적인 적응과 진화의 필요성을 말하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it.
ordered_passages: (A) It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.(B) The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer.(C) In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'.

(C) In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'.

(A) It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.(B) The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 사람들이 한 가지 특성으로 다른 특성까지 추론하는 고정관념에 대해 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 이를 증명하기 위한 구체적인 연구(대학생들에게 강사를 소개할 때 warm/cold라는 단어 사용)를 소개합니다. (B)에서 그 강연이 끝난 후 학생들의 인상을 조사한 결과 정보에 따라 큰 차이가 있었음을 보여주고, (A)에서 그러한 기대치가 인상 형성뿐 아니라 행동과 관계 형성에도 영향을 미친다는 결론을 내리는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글을 읽고, 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 요약문을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
questions.summary_sentence: Our future is (A)___________ finished before it comes true as the products around us are finished in our mind before they are brought into (B)___________.
subjective_conditions: • 윗글에 나온 단어를 그대로 사용할 것
• 한 킸에 한 단어만 쒸 것
questions.explanation: 지문의 내용은 모됐 세상의 물건이나 문래의 미래눤 실제로 이루어지기 전에 마음셍에서 먼저 완성된다눤 것입니다. 따라서 (A)에눤 '정신적으로' 완성된다눤 의미의 mentally, (B)에눤 '현실' 석으로 가져오기 전에뜐 의미의 reality가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. ⓐIt is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. ⓑPutting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. ⓒIf you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. ⓓArtists express the world through their works, communicate with people, and convey their feelings and thoughts. ⓔThen you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 그림을 그릴 때 전체적으로 작업하며 적절한 시점에 멈추는 방법과 그 중요성에 관한 것입니다. ⓓ번 문장은 '예술가들이 작품을 통해 세상을 표현하고 사람들과 소통하며 감정을 전달한다'는 내용으로, 그림 작업을 언제 마무리할지에 대한 구체적인 조언을 담고 있는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
(B) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(C) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각을 5가지로 정의했음을 언급하고 있습니다. (C)에서는 'However'를 활용하여 이를 반박하며 인간에게 그 이상의 감각(고유 수용성 감각 등)이 있음을 서술하므로 가장 먼저 옵니다. (B)에서는 다른 동물들의 특수한 감각 사례(뱀의 열 감지 등)를 들어 논의를 확장하며, (A)에서는 이러한 사례들(These examples)을 통해 감각을 명확하게 몇 가지 종류로 나눌 수 없음을 강조하며 마무리하는 (C)-(B)-(A) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most ①<u>striking</u> characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally ②<u>blind</u>. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of ③<u>depriving</u> sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be ④<u>impossible</u> without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some ⑤<u>benefits</u> of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 지각적 단절(perceptual disengagement, 외부 자극에 반응하지 않는 것)은 외부 자극으로부터 잠을 방해받지 않도록 '보호하는(protecting/preserving)' 기능을 수행합니다. 따라서 잠을 '박탈한다(depriving)'는 표현은 문맥상 정반대의 의미이므로 ③번이 틀린 어휘입니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ①<u>less</u> accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ②<u>sensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ③<u>underestimate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how ④<u>hard</u> it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making ⑤<u>assumptions</u> about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'란 전문가가 과거에 자신이 그 기술을 배울 때 얼마나 어려웠는지를 망각(forget)하는 현상을 의미합니다. 따라서 전문가는 초보자에게 과제가 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 '무감각(insensitive)'해지거나 의식하지 못하게 되는 것이 논리적이므로, '민감한'을 뜻하는 ②번의 sensitive는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that ________________________. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
options: ① you have more control over
② you can think and talk rationally
③ you have an influence on a person's emotions
④ you understand feelings of pain, anxiety, or conflict
⑤ you are aware of all of the memories at any given moment
questions.explanation: 본문에서 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)은 생각을 계속할지 감정을 더할지 등을 '선택(choose)'할 수 있는 영역이라고 설명합니다. 즉, 무의식과 달리 우리가 더 많은 통제력을 행사할 수 있는 영역임을 의미하므로 ①이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 더 많은 통제력을 가진
② 당신이 이성적으로 생각하고 말할 수 있는
③ 당신이 타인의 감정에 영향을 주는
④ 당신이 고통, 불안 혹은 갈등의 감정을 이해하는
⑤ 당신이 주어진 순간의 모든 기억을 인지하는

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals are that they can talk</u> in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed ⓑ<u>in such a way as to resemble humans</u>. ⓒ<u>This is achieved by showing them</u> with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. ⓓ<u>In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals</u> in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. ⓔ<u>A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing</u>, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.explanation: ⓐ의 문장에서 주어는 'The most noticeable human characteristic'으로 단수입니다. 따라서 동사는 are가 아니라 단수형인 is가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 영어 질문 중 글에서 답에 대한 정보를 찾을 수 없는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: [24년 3월 37번]With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca King's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he bean to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① How were the Chasquis stationed along the royal roads?
② What equipment did messengers use to deliver messages?
③ What were the characteristics of the messengers in the Inca Empire?
④ How did the Inca messengers communicate with each other when delivering messages?
⑤ What was the primary purpose of stationing the messengers on the royal roads in the Inca Empire?
questions.explanation: 지문에는 전령들이 도보로 이동하며 메시지를 전달했다고 언급되어 있을 뿐, 별도의 장비(equipment)에 대한 언급은 없습니다.
options_translation: ① Chasquis는 왕의 도로를 따라 어떻게 배치되었는가?
② 전령들은 메시지를 전달하기 위해 어떤 장비를 사용했는가?
③ 잉카 제국 전령들의 특징은 무엇이었는가?
④ 잉카 전령들은 메시지를 전달할 때 서로 어떻게 소통했는가?
⑤ 잉카 제국에서 왕의 도로에 전령들을 배치한 주요 목적은 무엇이었는가?

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to ①<u>doubt</u> it. For a start, Aristotle ②<u>missed</u> a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to ③<u>categorize</u>. Many vertebrates have a ④<u>different</u> sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to sort various animal senses into ⑤<u>flexible</u> categories, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 글의 흠름상 감각은 몇 가지로 명확히 나눌 수 없다고 하고 읈습니다. 따라서 다양한 동물의 감각을 '유연한(flexible)' 범주로 분류하려 하기밴다는 있는 괸대로 연구해야 한다는 맥락이므로, ⑤는 고정된 또는 제한된(fixed/limited) 범주에 끼워 먾으려하지 만아야 한다는 내용이 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: Seek Career Satisfaction for Global Happiness
Unlocking Happiness: The Power of Meaningful Work
The Impact of Job Satisfaction on The Outcome of a Study
What Is The Role of Work Fulfillment Based on Cultural Studies?
The Relationship Between Job Satisfaction and Financial Success
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간에게 의미 있는 일(meaningful work)이 제공하는 성침감과 점유감이 삶 전체의 픖복과 직무 성과에 미치는 긍정적인 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ② 'Unlocking Happiness: The Power of Meaningful Work(픖복을 여는 열슠: 의미 있는 일의 힘)'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: 세계적인 픖복을 을해 경력 별족감을 추구하라
픖복을 여는 열슠: 의미 있는 일의 힘
직무 별족도가 연구 결과에 미치는 영향
문화 연구에 기반한 업무 성침감의 역할은 무엇인가?
직무 별족도와 경제적 경과의 관계

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is ________________________________________. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
options: ① the ignorance about other society's rules
② the absence of respect for cultural diversity
③ the central problem of cross-cultural communication
④ the destruction of common sense for effective communication
⑤ another social custom of eliminating differences in communication
questions.explanation: 사회적 규범은 문화마다 다르며, 한 문화에서 당연하게 여겨지는 감사의 표현이 다른 문화에서는 어색하거나 부적절할 수 있습니다. 지문은 이러한 규범의 차이를 모를 경우 의사소통에서 오해나 비판을 불러일으킬 수 있음을 설명하고 있으므로, 다른 공동체의 규범을 모르는 것이 '문화 간 의사소통의 중심적인 문제'라는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 사회의 규칙에 대한 무지
② 문화적 다양성에 대한 존중의 부재
③ 문화 간 의사소통의 중심적인 문제
④ 효과적인 의사소통을 위한 상식의 파괴
⑤ 의사소통의 차이를 제거하는 또 다른 사회적 관습

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other.
ordered_passages: (A) With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.

(B) For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion.
(C) Therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 어떤 두 동물도 똑같지 않다는 일반론을 제시했습니다. (C)는 '그러므로(Therefore)'를 통해 동물들이 치료 세션에서 똑같이 반응하지 않을 수 있다는 구체적인 상황으로 연결하며 환경적 요인을 언급합니다. (B)는 (C)에서 언급된 환경적 요인 및 질병 상태에 따른 차이에 대한 예시(For instance)를 제공합니다. 마지막으로 (A)는 '이러한 점을 염두에 두고(With this in mind)' 개별 동물에 맞춘 맞춤형 치료가 필요하다는 결론을 내립니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 군에서 필자가 진정한 리더라고 주장하고 싶은 모습과 일치하지 않는 2개를 고르면?
questions.passage: When you think of leaders, you may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But in my opinion, these people, like all of us, started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ① 역사적 중요성과 광범위한 영향력을 끼친 사람
② 고귀하고 높은 목표를 성한 사람
③ 일상생활의 어느 측면이 개선될 수 있눤지에 대한 생각을 가진 사람
④ 근면함과 경험을 통해, 자신의 생각을 다른 사람들과 공유하여 가장 좋은 방법을 지석적으로 삾는 사람
⑤ 사람들의 의견과 반응을 무시하고, ......탍없이 집단의 목표를 성하는 사람
questions.explanation: ①과 ②은 일반적으로 사람들이 생각하는 리더의 모...... 모습이지만, 필자는 이러한 것이 리더십의 전부가 아니라 고 주장합니다. 필자가 진정한 리더라고 주장하는 모습은 일상 석에서 개선을 위해 노력하는 수단, 노동자, 시민들이므로 ①, ②은 필자의 주장과 일치하지 않습니다. 터한 ⑤번 선지는 필자의 설명(의견 수렴)과 정반대의 내용이므로 일치하지 않으나, 문제에서 요구하는 필자의 주장(진정한 리더의 모습)과 거리가 멀어 정답으로 채택됩니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
options: ① 잠시의 휴식은 정교한 완성도를 해친다.
② 한 번에 한 영역에만 집중하는 것이 중요하다.
③ 작업을 추가할수록 더 훌륭한 작품을 얻을 수 있다.
④ 멈추고 싶은 유혹을 버리고 장시간 집중할 필요가 있다.
⑤ 전체를 생각하면서 과도한 작업을 피하는 것이 중요하다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 그림을 그릴 때 한 부분에만 집중하기보다 전체적으로 작업하고, 너무 과도하게 작업하여 작품의 효과를 망치지 않도록 주의해야 한다고 조언합니다. 따라서 '전체를 생각하며 과도한 작업을 피하는 것이 중요하다'는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me?
ordered_passages: (A) Well, in real life, you can also create magic like that movie. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here.

(B) Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
(C) If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day."
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 영화 신데렐라와 마법을 언급한 뒤, (A)에서 현실에서도 그런 마법을 부리는 방법(도전 과제를 긍정 문구로 바꾸기)을 소개하며 예를 들어보겠다고 합니다. (C)에서 그 예시(아침 일찍 일어나기)를 구체적으로 제시하고, (B)에서 이러한 문구 작성이 가져오는 변화와 효과를 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. (A) They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. (B) Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. (C) Each of these sports has junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. (D) In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. (E) The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.insertion_sentence: As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 야구, 미식축구, 축구에서 어린이들을 위해 환경을 조정한 구체적인 사례들을 나열하고 있습니다. 이 문장은 여러 스포츠가 어린이를 위해 적응(adaptations)을 해왔다는 내용인 (B) 뒤에 오는 것이 가장 적절합니다. 주어진 문장 다음에 이어지는 (C)의 'Each of these sports'는 주어진 문장에 언급된 야구, 미식축구, 축구를 가리키므로 정답은 (C) 위치가 됩니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
questions.summary_sentence: Many bosses claim to (A)__________ dissent and value opposing opinions in their management, emphasizing the significance of (B)__________ to dissenters for innovative problem-solving.
questions.explanation: 글의 앞부분에서 대부분의 상사들이 반대 의견(dissent)에 찬성하며 직원들의 내부적 저항을 지속적으로 장려(encourage)한다고 말합니다. 또한 Bot Pittman의 인용구를 통해 반대자들의 말에 귀를 기울이는 것(paying attention)의 중요성을 강조하고 있으므로, (A)에는 encourage, (B)에는 paying attention이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 장려하다 / 주의를 기울이는 것
② 낙담시키다 / 주의를 기울이는 것
③ 인정하다 / 반대하는 것
④ 낙담시키다 / 반대하는 것
⑤ 장려하다 / 반대하는 것

questions.question: 22. 다음 관의 묘줄 친 볐분 중, 어법사 올바지 않은 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: The rate of speed ⓐ<u>which</u> one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed when humans move through space under their own power while ⓑ<u>walking</u>. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally ⓒ<u>suited</u> to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a ⓓ<u>very</u> more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has less time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, ⓔ<u>allow</u> for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites: while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than ⓕ<u>those</u> of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: 퉀린 것은 총 4개입니다.ⓐ which → at which 혹은 that (뒤에 완전한 문윑이 오며 traveling은 자동사로 쓰임)ⓓ very → much (비교급 more limited림 수식하는 부사로 very는 불가)ⓔ allow → allows (주어가 pedestrian travel이므로 단수 동사 필요)ⓕ those → that (비교 대상이 단수인 the rate of speed이므로 that으로 받아야 함)

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① positive impact of getting up early on your life style
② reasons why wishing for magic to happen is meaningless
③ danger of depending too much on the positive statements
④ importance of the positive statements to overcome the challenges
⑤ negative influence of being overconfident on dealing with life problems
questions.explanation: 글의 중반 이후부터 직면한 도전 과제들을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸어 적으면 사고와 행동 방식이 변하고 자신감을 얻게 된다는 내용을 전달하고 있습니다. 즉, 도전을 극복하기 위해 긍정적인 문장을 작성하는 것의 중요성을 다루고 있으므로 ④번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 일찍 일어나는 것이 당신의 생활 방식에 미치는 긍정적인 영향
② 마법이 일어나기를 바라는 것이 무의미한 이유
③ 긍정적인 문장에 너무 많이 의존하는 것의 위험성
④ 어려움을 극복하기 위한 긍정적인 문장의 중요성
⑤ 삶의 문제를 다룰 때 지나친 자신감을 갖는 것의 부정적 영향

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Dear Ms. Jane Watson, I am John Austin, a science teacher at Crestville High School. Recently I was impressed by the latest book you wrote about the environment. Also my students read your book and had a class discussion about it. They are big fans of your book, so I'd like to ask you to visit our school and give a special lecture. We can set the date and time to suit your schedule. Having you at our school would be a fantastic experience for the students. We would be very grateful if you could come. Best regards, John Austin
options: ① John Austin wrote a book about the environment.
② Jane Watson is a science teacher at Crestville High School.
③ No Crestville High School students read Watson's book.
④ Austin is asked to visit Crestville High School and give a special lecture.
⑤ The date and time for the special lecture has not been set yet.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 "We can set the date and time to suit your schedule"(귀하의 일정에 맞춰 날짜와 시간을 정할 수 있습니다)라고 언급되었으므로 아직 강연의 날짜와 시간이 정해지지 않았음을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① John Austin은 환경에 관한 책을 썼다.
② Jane Watson은 Crestville 고등학교의 과학 교사이다.
③ Crestville 고등학교 학생들 중 누구도 Watson의 책을 읽지 않았다.
④ Austin이 Crestville 고등학교를 방문하여 특별 강연을 하도록 요청받았다.
⑤ 특별 강연의 날짜와 시간은 아직 정해지지 않았다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can ⓐ<u>be considered</u> "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop ⓑ<u>painting</u>, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time ⓒ<u>assess</u> your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find ⓓ<u>yourself</u> struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide ⓔ<u>whether</u> any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation: ⓒ의 assess는 문맥상 '진행 상황을 평가하기 위해'라는 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사가 와야 하므로 to assess로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to find design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.summary_sentence: Traveling speed affects how well we can notice details in our surroundings, with pedestrians having the best ability to (A)__________ environmental details because of their slower pace, while motorists, moving much (B)__________, struggle to do so.
questions.explanation: 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 인지하는 능력에 영향을 미친다는 내용입니다. 보행자는 속도가 느려 세부 사항을 잘 (A) 인지(perceive/recognize)할 수 있는 반면, 자동차 운전자는 훨씬 (B) 빠르게(faster) 이동하기 때문에 세부 사항을 인지하는 데 어려움을 겪습니다.
options_translation: ① 무시하다 - 더 빠른
② 무시하다 - 더 느린
③ 인지하다 - 더 빠른
④ 인식하다 - 더 느린
⑤ 기억하다 - 더 쉬운

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings. Meaningful work is what ⓐ<u>provides</u> a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and ⓑ<u>satisfying</u>, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more ⓒ<u>fulfilled</u> on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much ⓓ<u>less</u> likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took ⓔ<u>greater</u> satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 맥락은 일에서 의미를 찾고 만족하는 사람들이 삶 전반에서도 더 행복하다는 내용입니다. ⓓ가 포함된 문장은 '업무에 가장 만족하는 사람들은 전반적인 삶에서 더 행복할 가능성이 훨씬 더 [낮다]'라는 의미가 되므로, 맥락상 'less'를 'more'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① Things to Do for Plants
③ The Secret of Survival: Movement
④ Different Ways of Movement of Plants
⑤ How to Study the History of Creatures
questions.explanation: 기후 변화에 따라 모든 생명체(나무와 따개비 포함)는 생존을 위해 이동해야 한다는 내용을 담고 있으므로 '생존의 비밀: 이동'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 식물을 위해 해야 할 일들
② 다양한 기후, 다양한 종
③ 생존의 비밀: 이동
④ 식물의 다양한 이동 방식
⑤ 생물의 역사를 공부하는 방법

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
options: ① Why Farmers Should Change Crops in an Order
② How to Enrich Your Soil: Maintain Only One Crop
③ The Advantage of Studying Characteristics of Crops
④ Set the Better Order of Crops for Your Green Bean Farm
⑤ Ways to Find out Perfect Soil for Carrots and Tomatoes
questions.explanation: 이 글은 윤작(crop rotation)의 개념과 그 과정을 설명하며, 이를 통해 토양을 건강하게 유지하고 지속 가능한 농업을 할 수 있다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '왜 농부들이 순서대로 작물을 바꿔야 하는가'가 제목으로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 농부들이 순서대로 작물을 바꿔야 하는가
② 토양을 비옥하게 하는 법: 오직 한 작물만 유지하기
③ 작물의 특성을 연구하는 것의 장점
④ 당신의 완두콩 농장을 위해 더 나은 작물 순서 정하기
⑤ 당근과 토마토를 위한 완벽한 토양을 찾는 방법

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that __________________________.
options: ① Aristotle and Macpherson have the same idea about the senses
② we cannot divide the different senses into the limited categories
③ there is the same sense system for detecting the environment
④ the way Aristotle categorized the senses fully explains the human senses
⑤ it is important for philosophers to understand why humans are different than animals
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 5가지 감각 외에도 인간에게는 고유 수용 감각이나 평형 감각이 있고, 동물들에게는 열 감지 등 더 복잡한 감각 체계가 있음을 설명하며, 감각을 제한된 범주로 단순히 나눌 수 없다는 점을 시사하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 아리스토텔레스와 맥퍼슨은 감각에 대해 같은 생각을 가지고 있다
② 우리는 다양한 감각들을 제한된 범주로 나눌 수 없다
③ 환경을 감지하기 위한 동일한 감각 체계가 존재한다
④ 아리스토텔레스가 감각을 분류한 방식은 인간의 감각을 충분히 설명한다
⑤ 철학자들이 왜 인간이 동물과 다른지 이해하는 것은 중요하다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the ocean would get its gift sooner가 의미하는 것을 <보기>의 단어를 사용하여 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: Marilyn and her three-year-old daughter, Sarah, took a trip to the beach, where Sarah built her first sandcastle. Moments later, an enormous wave destroyed Sarah's castle. In response to the loss of her sandcastle, tears streamed down Sarah's cheeks and her heart was broken. She ran to Marilyn, saying she would never build a sandcastle again. Marilyn said, "Part of the joy of building a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give it as a gift to the ocean." Sarah loved this idea and responded with enthusiasm to the idea of building another castle - this time, even closer to the water so <u>the ocean would get its gift sooner</u>!
subjective_conditions: - <보기>의 단어만을 변형 없이 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것.
- 하나의 완전한 문장으로 작성할 것.
questions.answer: the ocean would destroy the sandcastle she built sooner
questions.explanation: 본문에서 모래성을 파도에 휩쓸려 보내는 것을 '바다에 주는 선물'로 비유하고 있습니다. 따라서 밑줄 친 부분은 물가에 더 가깝게 지음으로써 바다가 그 선물(모래성)을 더 빨리 가져가게(부수게) 된다는 의미입니다. 보기의 단어들을 조합하여 '바다가 그녀가 지은 모래성을 더 빨리 부술 것이다'라는 문장을 완성하면 됩니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 말을 주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어로 쓰시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
questions.summary_sentence: Leaders can (A)__________ their staffs to protest to (B)__________ their goals.
questions.explanation: 지문은 훌륭한 리더들이 부하 직원들의 반대 의견(dissent, protest)을 장려한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 이는 반대하는 사람들의 말을 경청함으로써 일을 완수하기 위해 무엇을 해야 하는지 알 수 있기 때문입니다. 따라서 리더는 직원들이 반대 의견을 내도록 '장려(encourage)'하여 목표를 '달성(achieve)'할 수 있다는 요약이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <보기>의 단어를 사용하여 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about ______________________________ on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
subjective_conditions: - <보기>의 단어만을 변형 없이 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것.
questions.answer: how some aspect of daily life could be improved
questions.explanation: 위대한 리더들도 처음에는 일상생활의 어떤 측면이 어떻게 개선될 수 있는지에 대한 아이디어를 가진 평범한 사람들이었다는 내용입니다. <보기>의 단어들을 조합하여 '어떻게 일상생활의 어떤 측면이 개선될 수 있는지'를 영작하면 'how some aspect of daily life could be improved'가 됩니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글을 읽고 Sarah에 대한 설명으로 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Marilyn and her three-year-old daughter, Sarah, took a trip to the beach, where Sarah built her first sandcastle. Moments later, an enormous wave destroyed Sarah's castle. In response to the loss of her sandcastle, tears streamed down Sarah's cheeks and her heart was broken. She ran to Marilyn, saying she would never build a sandcastle again. Marilyn said, "Part of the joy of building a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give it as a gift to the ocean." Sarah loved this idea and responded with enthusiasm to the idea of building another castle - this time, even closer to the water so the ocean would get its gift sooner!
options: ③ 동갑인 친구에게 가서 앞으로 다시는 모래성을 쌓지 않겠다고 얘기했다.
④ 바다에게 모래성을 선물로 준다는 생각이 마음에 들었다.
⑤ 바다가 선물을 빨리 받을 수 있도록 모래성을 바다 가까이 지어야겠다고 생각했다.
questions.explanation: 본문에 따르면 Sarah는 모래성이 부서진 후 친구가 아니라 '그녀의 어머니인 Marilyn'에게 달려가 다시는 모래성을 쌓지 않겠다고 말했습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of ⓐ<u>achievement</u> and empowerment. It increases and ⓑ<u>sustains</u> the levels of employee satisfaction, their commitment to the organization, and their willingness to go beyond role. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce ⓒ<u>finer</u> quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives in ⓓ<u>general</u>. In addition, for her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, and found out that it was ⓔ<u>questionable</u> that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 연구 결과에 따르면 일에서 더 큰 만족을 얻는 사람들이 전반적으로 더 행복한 삶을 살 가능성이 높다는 사실이 밝혀졌으므로, '의심스럽다(questionable)'가 아니라 '분명하다' 혹은 '입증되었다' 등의 긍정적인 맥락의 단어가 오는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
options: ① Searching for the Reasons We Should Study What Senses There Are
② Comparing Aristotle with Macpherson, Who Sounds More Ideal?
③ Senses Aristotle Attempted to Identify More in Humans than in Animals
④ Aristotle Got It Wrong: There Is a Neat Line Distinguishing Each of the Five Senses
⑤ Rejecting the View That There Exist Only a Small Number of Distinct Senses
questions.explanation: 지문은 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 인간과 동물의 '5감'에 의문을 제기하며, 감각은 소수의 특정한 종류로 명확히 나누어질 수 없으며 훨씬 더 다양하다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '감각의 수가 소수라는 관점을 거부하는 것'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 어떤 감각이 있는지 연구해야 하는 이유 찾기
② 아리스토텔레스와 맥퍼슨 비교, 누가 더 이상적으로 들리는가?
③ 아리스토텔레스가 동물보다 인간에게서 더 확인하려고 시도했던 감각들
④ 아리스토텔레스가 틀렸다: 다섯 가지 감각 각각을 구별하는 깔끔한 선이 있다
⑤ 뚜렷한 감각이 오직 적은 수로만 존재한다는 견해를 거부하기

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① Why an Excellent Messenger Was Essential in Inca
② How the Inca Communicated across Their Large Empire
③ Why Inca Delivered Messages on Foot and Not by Horses
④ What Methods Were Used to Communicate across the Mountain Realm
⑤ How the Empire's Territory Was Reorganized Using the Complex System
questions.explanation: 이 글은 말 없이도 도보 메신저 체계(Chasquis)를 통해 방대한 제국 전체에 메시지를 효율적으로 전달했던 잉카 제국의 통신 방식에 대해 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 잉카에서 훌륭한 전령이 필수적이었던 이유
② 잉카가 광대한 제국 전역에서 소통한 방법
③ 잉카가 말이 아닌 도보로 메시지를 전달한 이유
④ 산악 영역 전역에서 소통하기 위해 어떤 방법들이 사용되었는가
⑤ 복잡한 시스템을 사용하여 제국의 영토가 어떻게 재편되었는가

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
options: ① Sleep described as a state of being functionally blind
② Perceptual disengagement that always accompanies sleep
③ Essential conditions to define what it means to be in sleep
④ The difference between drowsiness and perceptual disengagement
⑤ What keeps you from responding normally to environmental stimuli
questions.explanation: 지문은 수면의 핵심적인 특징으로 외부 자극에 반응하지 않는 '지각적 차단(perceptual disengagement)'을 설명하고 있습니다. 지각적 차단이 수면을 보호하는 기능을 하며, 수면 정의의 필수적인 요소임을 강조하고 있으므로 주제로 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기능적 맹인 상태로 묘사되는 수면
② 항상 수면에 수반되는 지각적 차단
③ 수면 상태에 있다는 것이 무엇을 의미하는지 정의하기 위한 필수 조건들
④ 졸음과 지각적 차단 사이의 차이점
⑤ 당신이 환경 자극에 정상적으로 반응하는 것을 막는 것

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - ⑀<u>what</u> degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are ⑁<u>forced</u> to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that ⑂<u>appear</u> immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place ⑃<u>where</u> it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with ⑄<u>surprised</u> speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: ⑄번의 surprised는 '놀라게 된'이라는 감정 형용사인데, 여기서는 속도(speed)를 수식하여 '놀라운 속도'라는 의미를 나타내야 하므로 사물을 수식하는 현재분사인 surprising으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글을 요약한 문장이다. 괄호에 주어진 단어를 모두 적절하게 배열하여 다음 문장을 완성하시오. (단어추가 불가, 어형변화 불가)
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - ⑀<u>what</u> degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are ⑁<u>forced</u> to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that ⑂<u>appear</u> immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place ⑃<u>where</u> it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with ⑄<u>surprised</u> speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.summary_sentence: Although the speed may vary depending on the species, all creatures, including trees, have the ability to move, (are / growth / which / places / suitable / new / and reproduction / their survival / helps / for / that / them / find).
subjective_conditions: 단어추가 불가
어형변화 불가
questions.answer: which helps them find new places that are suitable for their survival, growth, and reproduction
questions.explanation: 주어진 단어를 활용하여 '그들의 생존, 성장, 번식에 적합한 새로운 장소를 찾는 것을 돕는'이라는 관계대명사절을 구성해야 합니다. which(주격 관계대명사) + helps(동사) + them(목적어) + find(목적격 보어) + new places(find의 목적어) + that(주격 관계대명사) + are suitable for(형용사구) + their survival, growth, and reproduction 순으로 배열하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. When composing original songs in groups, participants were able to identify with the song and claimed it as "our" song, which in turn built a sense of working within a team and decreased the level of social anxiety. Also, they were pleasantly surprised at their creativity, and they took pride in their songs. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ① 집단 음악 치료는 참여자의 삶의 질을 개선했다.
② 집단 음악 치료 활동에 참여한 횟수가 많을수록 가장 큰 효과를 경험했다.
③ 작곡 활동에 참여한 사람은 자신의 곡에 자부심을 가졌으며 사회적 불안이 감소했다.
④ 집단 가창은 감정 상태를 개선하였고, 자신감을 강화했다.
⑤ 집단 가창은 소속감 강화에는 도움이 되지 않았다.
questions.explanation: 본문의 마지막 문장에서 'Group singing... developed a sense of belonging(집단 가창은... 소속감을 발달시켰다)'라고 명시되어 있으므로, 소속감 강화에 도움이 되지 않았다는 ⑤번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be __________________________.
options: ① made fit for what is required by a rescue center
② converted according to the needs of each species
③ rearranged to satisfy the emotional need of the animal
④ modified to meet what is required by individual animals
⑤ altered in order to make the animal respond to the treatment

questions.question: 32. 다음 글의 글쓴이의 견해와 일치하도록 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 각각 주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어를 알맞게 넣어 문장을 완성하시오. (답지에 주어진 철자 포함할 것)
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.People are expected to follow (A)n__________ like rules because not behaving in a way (B)c__________ with those patterns will attract other's surprise or criticism. For successful cross-cultural communication, you should consider not only the meaning of an expression but also the (A)n__________ of the target culture, which determine whether its usage is (C)a__________ or not.

The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore ⓒ<u>have</u> a much more limited ability to process details along the street; a motorist simply has little time or capacity to appreciate design details. Conversely, pedestrian travel, being much slower, ⓓ<u>allowing</u> for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than ⓔ<u>that</u> of the typical motorist.

For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal.

questions.passage: In the past, few people enjoyed leisure time. For ordinary people, any time off was usually for religious reasons.
ordered_passages: (A) Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton.

(B) So, early travel was often restricted to pilgrimages. Later, as the social and economic development of countries expanded especially in Eruope and North America, so wage levels and working conditions improved.

(C) Despite the tourism of air travel, however, the opportunities for holiday making for ordinary people were still limited in scope. For most people, in developing countries, the chances to travel are still limited.
(D) With the arrival of air transport, the moneyed classes started to travel more widely than with the railway. Airplanes opened up more of the world and stimulated tourism growth.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 과거에는 여가 시간이 거의 없었으며 종교적인 이유로만 휴식을 가졌다는 내용이 나옵니다. (B)에서는 그래서(So) 초기 여행은 성지 순례(pilgrimages)에 국한되었다는 내용으로 이어지며, 이후 경제 발전으로 근로 조건이 개선되었다고 설명합니다. (A)에서는 그 결과 점차 더 많은 휴가를 받게 되었고, 철도와 같은 교통수단의 발달로 유명한 해변 휴양지가 생겨났음을 말합니다. questions.question: 26. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The discovery of taste buds paved the way for the next step in taste research: determining the mechanisms ⓐ<u>which</u> taste cells carry out their work. From the 1940s through the 1970s, virtually every basic biology textbook honored the myth that taste buds were grouped in the mouth according to specialty. Correspondingly, the tongue was diagrammed into separate ares ⓑ<u>where</u> certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. In the 1980s and 1990s, however, research at Yale University, Monell Chemical Senses Center, in Philadelphia, and the University of Connecticut, and elsewhere demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste ⓒ<u>was</u>, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers, such as Dr. Linda Bartoshuk of Yale University School of medicine, believe ⓓ<u>that</u> taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. According to Bartoshuk's research, sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although we may ⓔ<u>perceive</u> these tastes at slightly different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first. Similarly, bitterness is not perceived at the back of your mouth, rather, you ______________________________.
