④ open taste pores on the tip of the tongue
⑤ experience it a few milliseconds after sweetness
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에서 맛의 인식 기제는 '장소'가 아니라 '시간'의 문제라고 설명하고 있습니다. 단맛을 먼저 느끼고 쓴맛을 나중에 느끼는 시간적 차이를 언급하는 흐름이므로, 빈칸에는 단맛을 느낀 후 수 밀리초 뒤에 쓴맛을 경험한다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 단맛 이전에 그것을 감지한다
② 혀의 모든 부위에서 그것을 맛본다
③ 쓴맛을 느끼는 미뢰가 부족하다
④ 혀끝에 있는 미공을 연다
⑤ 단맛을 느낀 후 수 밀리초 후에 그것을 경험한다

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements 一 what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life 一 as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born 一 often occupied by its parent 一 to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① division of species into mobile and immobile
② effect of climate change on species movement
③ decline of species in response to climate change
④ process of inferring climate change from fossils
⑤ relationship between climate change and species growth
questions.explanation: 글은 모든 종이 특정 기후 조건을 필요로 하며, 기후가 변함에 따라 그 조건에 맞는 장소로 이동해야 함을 설명하고 있습니다. 움직이지 않는 것처럼 보이는 나무나 따개비조차도 생애의 특정 단계(씨앗, 유충 등)에서 이동을 통해 기후 변화에 적응해왔다는 내용이므로 '기후 변화가 종의 이동에 미치는 영향'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이동 가능한 종과 이동 불가능한 종의 분류
② 기후 변화가 종의 이동에 미치는 영향
③ 기후 변화에 따른 종의 감소
④ 화석으로부터 기후 변화를 추론하는 과정
⑤ 기후 변화와 종의 성장 사이의 관계

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip. sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the -tongue map" explanation of how we taste was. in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
options: ① All areas of the tongue can detect all four basic tastes by the time - based mechanism not location - based.
② Sweet, bitter, and sour flavors are distinctly detected on specific areas of the tongue.
③ The -tongue map-, which shows how we perceive taste, has been scientifically proven to be correct.
④ The taste buds on the tongue are categorized according to the specialized areas for each taste.
⑤ Different areas of the tongue can taste everything, but some areas of the tongue cannot feel certain tastes.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거의 '혀 지도' 이론(혀의 특정 부위에서 특정 맛을 느낀다는 이론)이 독일 연구의 오역과 오해에서 비롯된 틀린 이론임을 밝히고 있습니다. 현대 연구에 따르면 혀의 모든 부위에서 모든 맛을 느낄 수 있으며, 특정 맛이 먼저 느껴지는 것은 위치가 아닌 시간 기반의 메커니즘 때문이라는 것이 요지입니다.
options_translation: ① 혀의 모든 영역은 위치 기반이 아닌 시간 기반 메커니즘에 의해 네 가지 기본 맛을 모두 감지할 수 있다.
② 단맛, 쓴맛, 신맛은 혀의 특정 영역에서 뚜렷하게 감지된다.
③ 우리가 맛을 인지하는 방식을 보여주는 '혀 지도'는 과학적으로 옳음이 입증되었다.
④ 혀의 미뢰는 각 맛에 대한 전문 영역에 따라 분류된다.
⑤ 혀의 서로 다른 영역은 모든 것을 맛볼 수 있지만, 일부 영역은 특정 맛을 느끼지 못할 수도 있다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because 一 fueled by emotions 一 you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions. The only become real fears when the subconscious mind __________________________________.
options: ③ is repeatedly trained by experts
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 거미나 어둠에 대한 공포는 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)에서 기인하지만, 이것이 실제적인 공포가 되는 시점은 잠재의식(subconscious mind)이 우리의 반응을 기록할 때입니다. 따라서 잠재의식이 우리의 반응을 포착/기록한다는 내용이 빈칸에 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 반응을 포착한다
② 우리의 경험을 파괴한다
③ 전문가들에 의해 반복적으로 훈련된다
④ 부정적인 관계를 다룬다
⑤ 통제 가능한 반응을 피한다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question. How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago. Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals 一 sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that ___________________________________________.
options: ① all creatures receive signals through the sense organs
② the concept of five senses remains universally applicable
③ Aristotle's classification of five senses is comprehensive
④ all animals share the exact same sensory capabilities as humans
⑤ senses are not easily categorized into a set number of distinct types
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스는 인간과 동물의 감각이 5개라고 정의했지만, 피오나 맥퍼슨은 인간에게도 고유 수용 감각이나 평형 감각 등이 더 있으며, 동물들 또한 열 감지 등 인간과 다른 다양한 감각 체계를 가지고 있다고 주장합니다. 이러한 사례들은 감각을 정해진 숫자로 쉽게 분류할 수 없음을 보여줍니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 생명체는 감각 기관을 통해 신호를 받는다
② 오감의 개념은 보편적으로 적용 가능한 상태로 남아있다
③ 아리스토텔레스의 오감 분류는 포괄적이다
④ 모든 동물은 인간과 정확히 동일한 감각 능력을 공유한다
⑤ 감각은 정해진 숫자의 뚜렷한 유형으로 쉽게 분류되지 않는다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally 一 they are functionally blind. (B) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. (C) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (D) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. (E) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.insertion_sentence: But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition.
questions.explanation: (D) 앞까지는 수면 중 자극에 반응하지 않는 현상(지각적 단절)에 대해 설명합니다. (D) 문장 뒷부분에서 일부 저자들은 지각적 단절을 수면의 정의로 보지 않는다고 언급합니다. 주어진 문장의 'it'은 지각적 단절을 의미하며, '그것(지각적 단절) 없이는 잠이 불가능하므로 수면의 정의에 필수적인 것처럼 보인다'는 내용은 (D)의 의견과 대조를 이룹니다. 따라서 (E) 위치에 들어가서 그 뒤에 나오는 'Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구하고)'를 통해 지각적 단절이 완전하지 않은 졸음 상태에서도 수면의 이점을 얻는 경우가 있다는 내용으로 이어지는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한번씩 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 완성하시오. (철자 및 어법 오류시 부분 점수 없음)
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, ________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 철자 및 어법 오류시 부분 점수 없음
<보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한번씩 사용하여 완성할 것
questions.answer: what they are really telling you is what you must do to get something done
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 지도자들이 반대 의견을 경청해야 한다는 점을 강조합니다. Bob Pittman의 인용구는 반대하는 사람들이 '왜 할 수 없는지'를 말하려 할 수도 있지만, 깊이 들으면 '어떤 일을 완수하기 위해 당신이 무엇을 해야 하는지'를 말해주고 있다는 내용입니다. 주어진 단어를 조합하면 'what they are really telling you(그들이 정말로 당신에게 말하고 있는 것) is(은) what you must do(당신이 해야만 하는 것) to get something done(무언가가 완수되도록 하기 위해)'가 됩니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한번씩 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 완성하시오. (철자 및 어법 오류시 부분 점수 없음) [2.8점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation _____________________________________. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
subjective_conditions: <보기>-에 주어진 단어만 모두 한번씩 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 완성하시오.
철자 및 어법 오류시 부분 점수 없음
questions.answer: is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 윤자ᄀ(crop rotation)에 대하녀 가느키고 이스ᄐ니다. 그 저긔를 서술하느ᄂ거스로, "농부댜들이 그댈으ᄀ 경자ᄀ지에사 기우느ᄂ나무를 트ᄀ뱔하느ᄂ 순사대로 바꾸느ᄂ 개정이다"라느ᄂ 의미가 댜거나 구조해 연개해야 하ᄐ니다. 'the process in which'가 가ᄂᅠ개 대명사 절으로 수시ᄀ하고 이스ᄐ니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한번씩 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 완성하시오. (철자 및 어법 오류시 부분 점수 없음) [2.8점]
questions.passage: The rate ____________________________________________. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street 䀀 a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
subjective_conditions: <보기>-에 주어진 단어만 모두 한번씩 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 완성하시오.
철자 및 어법 오류시 부분 점수 없음
questions.answer: of speed at which one is moving will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 소ᄀ도가 주뱌ᄂ의 세부 사항을 파아ᄀ하느ᄂ 느녀ᄀ에 미치느ᄂ 경햐가 서술하고 이스ᄐ니다. 'the rate of speed at which one is moving'이 주어 파트이며, 'will greatly determine'가 동사, 그리고 'the ability to process detail in the environment'가 모ᄀ저거가 대느ᄂ거시 마ᄎ스ᄐ니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한번씩 사용하고 필요시 몇 단어는 어형 변화하여 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 완성하시오. (철자 및 어법 오류시 부분 점수 없음) [3.0점]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they ________________________________. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한번씩 사용
필요시 몇 단어는 어형 변화
철자 및 어법 오류시 부분 점수 없음
vocabulary_box: and feedback / the best way / by sharing them / and look for / seek their opinions / improved upon / their ideas / with others, / for a group / to accomplish goals
questions.answer: improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group
questions.explanation: 위대한 지도자들도 처음엔 평범한 사람들로서 아이디어를 가졌고, 이를 타인과 공유하고 의견을 구하며 발전시켰다는 내용입니다. 주어 'they' 다음에는 동사 'improved upon'이 오며, 'by sharing them(그것들을 공유함으로써)' 구문이 뒤따릅니다. <보기>의 'seek'와 'look'은 문맥상 'sharing'과 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 'seeking'과 'looking'으로 어형을 변화시켜 분사구문 형태로 작성합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸을 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 모두 순서대로 사용하여 20 단어 이하의 문장으로 완성하시오. (단, 어형 변화 금지. 철자 및 문법 오류시 오답 처리) [3.2점]
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. _______________________________________________. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 주어진 단어를 모두 순서대로 사용
20 단어 이하의 문장으로 완성
어형 변화 금지
철자 및 문법 오류시 오답 처리
questions.answer: Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment.
questions.explanation: 개별 동물의 차이뿐만 아니라 환경적 요인 또한 치료에 대한 반응을 결정한다는 맥락입니다. <보기>의 단어들을 순서대로 사용하여 문장을 구성하면 'Environmental factors(환경적 요인들)'를 주어로 하고, 'can also determine(또한 결정할 수 있다)'을 동사로, 의문사절 'how the animal will respond during the treatment(동물이 치료 중에 어떻게 반응할지)'를 목적어로 배치하여 완성합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. ⓐEngland's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. ⓑRailways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. ⓒWith the railways came many large hotels. ⓓIn Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. ⓔFurthermore, the railway system caused great environmental pollution in England. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사회 경제적 발전과 교통수단의 발달(철도 등)이 관광 산업의 성장과 휴양지 발달로 이어진 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. ⓔ는 철도 시스템이 환경 오염을 유발했다는 내용으로, 관광 산업 발달이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 어법상 옳은 것끼리만 짝지은 것으로 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically ⓐ<u>spread</u> out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, ⓑ<u>that</u> in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential ⓒ<u>to deliver</u> products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view ⓓ<u>which</u> production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to ⓔ<u>meeting</u> their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
questions.explanation: ⓐ spread는 과거분사로 '분산된'의 의미로 쓰여 적절합니다. ⓒ to deliver는 가주어 it에 대응하는 진주어로 적절합니다. ⓑ that은 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로 쓰일 수 없으므로 which로 바뀌어야 하며, ⓓ which는 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오므로 동격의 접속사 that이 되어야 합니다. ⓔ meeting은 명사 desire를 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to meet이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice (A)[discovers / distrusts] that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run (B)[faster / slower] so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster - in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to (C)[flourish / decline] and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
questions.explanation: (A) 계속 달렸음에도 제자리에 있다는 것을 '발견하는(discovers)' 것이 맥락상 맞습니다. (B) 토끼를 잡기 위해 여우가 '더 빠르게(faster)' 진화해야 경쟁이 성립합니다. (C) 가장 빠른 여우만이 충분한 먹이를 잡아 유전자를 물려주고 '번성(flourish)'하게 될 것이라는 내용이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 발견한다 / 더 빠르게 / 번성하다
② 발견한다 / 더 빠르게 / 쇠퇴하다
③ 발견한다 / 더 느리게 / 번성하다
④ 불신한다 / 더 느리게 / 쇠퇴하다
⑤ 불신한다 / 더 느리게 / 번성하다

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew larger. Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster. For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
options: ① 마을이 점점 커지면서 사람들은 음식과 필요한 도구가 많아졌다.
② 농사를 짓는 사람들은 도구를 만드는 사람보다 효과적으로 일했다.
③ 같은 시간에 더 많은 도구를 만드는 사람들이 좋은 대우를 받았다.
④ 구석기 시대는 공동체보다 개인이 더 중요해서 분업이 필요 없었다.
⑤ 공동체 생활 후 사람들은 분업을 통해 효율적으로 일할 수 있게 되었다.
questions.explanation: 글의 중반 이후(Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. They could divide up the work...)에서 공동체 생활이 시작되면서 업무를 분담(분업)하게 되었고, 이를 통해 더 효율적으로 일할 수 있게 되었다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 putting on the same clothes가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "<u>putting on the same clothes</u>" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ① learning with various methods for better fulfillment
② keeping only one style despite of different conditions
③ memorizing enough to win first prize in every subject
④ wearing the causal clothes even for a special occasion
⑤ applying appropriate strategies depending on situation
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'rubber-stamp approach'와 맥락을 같이 하는 'putting on the same clothes'는 모든 상황(수업, 시험 등)에 대해 똑같은 방식(전략)을 고수하는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 나은 성취를 위해 다양한 방법으로 학습하기
② 서로 다른 조건에도 불구하고 단 하나의 스타일만을 유지하기
③ 모든 과목에서 1등을 하기 위해 충분히 암기하기
④ 특별한 행사에도 평상복을 입기
⑤ 상황에 따라 적절한 전략을 적용하기

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Chess masters shown a chess board in the middle of a game for 5 seconds with 20 to 30 pieces still in play can immediately reproduce the position of the pieces from memory. Beginners, of course, are able to place only a few. Now take the same pieces and place them on the board (A)__________ and the difference is much reduced. The expert's advantage is only for familiar patterns - those previously stored in memory. Faced with unfamiliar patterns, even when it involves the same familiar domain, the expert's advantage disappears.The beneficial effects of familiar structure on memory have been observed for many types of expertise, including music. People with musical training can reproduce short sequences of musical notation more accurately than those with no musical training when notes follow conventional sequences, but the advantage is much reduced when the notes are ordered randomly. Expertise also improves memory for sequences of movements. Experienced ballet dancers are able to repeat longer sequences of steps than less experienced dancers, and they can repeat a sequence of steps making up a routine better than steps ordered randomly. In each case, memory range is increased by the ability to recognize (B)__________ sequences and patterns.
questions.explanation: 전문가들이 일반인보다 더 많은 양을 기억해내는 것은 그들이 해당 분야의 '친숙한 패턴'을 인식하기 때문입니다. 따라서 체스 기물들을 (A) '무작위로(randomly)' 배치하면 전문가의 우위가 사라지게 됩니다. 결론적으로 기억력의 범위는 (B) '친숙한(familiar)' 순서나 패턴을 인식하는 능력에 의해 증가하는 것이므로 정답은 ①번입니다.
options_translation: ① 무작위로 / 친숙한
② 무작위로 / 불규칙한
③ 무작위로 / 친숙하지 않은
④ 질서 있게 / 친숙하지 않은
⑤ 질서 있게 / 친숙한

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma (A)[cools / heats], its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how (B)[quickly / quietly] the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into (C)[larger / smaller] crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
questions.explanation: (A) 문맥상 마그마가 '식으면서(cools)' 에너지를 잃고 결합하게 됩니다. (B) 결정의 크기는 마그마가 얼마나 '빨리(quickly)' 혹은 느리게 식느냐에 달려 있다는 흐름입니다. (C) 마그마가 천천히 식으면 원자들이 결합할 충분한 시간을 갖게 되어 '더 큰(larger)' 결정을 형성하게 됩니다. 따라서 정답은 ③번입니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: (A) In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. (B) They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. (C) Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. (D) As the first example, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. (E) The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.insertion_sentence: In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 'In a similar way(비슻한 딩으로)'로 시작하며 테니스의 사례를 들고 있습니다. (D) 단락에서 야굠, 미국 축굠, 축굠의 첫 번째 사례들을 나열한 후, 비슻한 또 다른 사례로서 테니스를 언급하는 감이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 (E) 자리에 들어가아 나지막 문장인 '이러한 개조(적응)들은 점진적이다'라는 결론으로 이어질 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. (A)__________, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.To summarize this article, (B)__________ the controllable conscious mind deals with thoughts and emotions, the fast-acting subconscious mind stores your responses, forming real fears.
options: ④ As a result - For example
questions.explanation: (A) 압 문장에서는 잠재의식의 특징을 설명하고, (A) 들 문장부터는 그와 대조되는 의식적인 마음의 특징을 설명하므로 역접의 연결어 However가 적절합니다. (B) 요약문에ᄉ서 의식적 마음가 잠재의식을 대조하며 나열하고 있으므로 '~하는 바민에'라는 의미의 while이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나 - ~하는 바민에
② 그러나 - 마찬가지로
③ 결과적으로 - 마찬가지로
④ 결과적으로 - 예를 들어
⑤ 예를 들어 - 예를 들어

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "__________________________________" Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① No one can get up early.
② Whenever I get up early, I feel tired.
③ It is hard to get up early every morning.
④ I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day.
⑤ I could not get up early because I studied very hard.
questions.explanation: 지문에서는 직면한 문제를 '긍정적인 진술(positive statements)'로 바꾸라고 조언하고 있습니다. 아침에 일찍 일어나는 데 어려움을 겪고 있다면, 이를 극복한 상태의 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸어 써야 하므로 "나는 매일 아침 5시에 일찍 일어난다"는 내용의 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 아무도 일찍 일어날 수 없다.
② 내가 일찍 일어날 때마다 나는 피곤함을 느낀다.
③ 매일 아침 일찍 일어나는 것은 어렵다.
④ 나는 매일 아침 5시에 일찍 일어난다.
⑤ 나는 공부를 매우 열심히 했기 때문에 일찍 일어날 수 없었다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: It would be hard ⓐ<u>to overstate</u> how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those ⓑ<u>who</u> have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people ⓒ<u>fulfilled</u> on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most ⓓ<u>satisfied</u> with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work ⓔ<u>were</u> 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 절 'when people ⓒfulfilled on the job'에서 문맥상 '사람들이 직장에서 성취감을 느낄 때'라는 수동의 의미가 되어야 하므로, fulfilled를 are fulfilled로 고쳐야 합니다. 또는 분사구문으로 볼 경우에도 의미상 '성취감을 느낀다'는 수동의 의미가 필요합니다. ① ⓐ는 가주어 It에 대한 진주어 to부정사로 적절합니다. ② ⓑ는 선행사 Those를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사로 적절합니다. ④ ⓓ는 Those (who are) most satisfied... 구조에서 Those를 수식하는 과거분사로 적절합니다. ⑤ ⓔ는 주어 those(복수)에 일치시킨 과거 동사로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are ⓐ<u>adopted</u> to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to ⓑ<u>distinguish</u> detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more ⓒ<u>limited</u> ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much ⓓ<u>slower</u>, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they ⓔ<u>travel</u> faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 인간의 감각이 걷는 속도에 '적응되었다'는 의미가 되어야 하므로 adopted(채택된)가 아니라 adapted(적응된)가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. questions.explanation: 글은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력에 어떤 영향을 미치는지 설명하고 있습니다. 느린 속도(도보)는 세부 사항 감상에 적합하고, 빠른 속도(운전)는 세부 사항 인식이 제한적이라는 내용이므로 속도와 인식의 관계를 나타낸 ②가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 세상을 이해하기 위한 이동 수단 간의 유사점과 차이점

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Marilyn and her three-year-old daughter, Sarah, took a trip to the beach, where Sarah built her first sandcastle. Moments later, an enormous wave destroyed Sarah's castle. In response to the loss of her sandcastle, tears streamed down Sarah's cheeks and her heart was broken. She ran to Marilyn, saying she would never build a sandcastle again. Marilyn said, "Part of the joy of building a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give it as a gift to the ocean." Sarah loved this idea and responded with enthusiasm to the idea of building another castle - this time, _____________________________________.
options: ① Let's make lots of castles to give them to the ocean as a gift!
② even closer to the water so the ocean would get its gift sooner!
③ Let's build a strong castle to prevent the ocean from knocking it down!
④ Sarah tries to build a castle as big as possible to give it to the ocean as a gift.
⑤ Although Sarah knows that her sandcastle will be destroyed, she builds it again with delight.
questions.explanation: 모래성이 파도에 무너진 것을 바다에게 주는 선물이라는 관점의 전환으로 받아들인 Sarah는, 그 선물을 더 빨리 주기 위해 물에 더 가까운 곳에 짓겠다는 반응을 보이는 것이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 바다에 선물로 주기 위해 많은 성을 만들자!
② 바다가 선물을 더 빨리 받을 수 있도록 물에 훨씬 더 가까이!
③ 바다가 성을 무너뜨리는 것을 막기 위해 튼튼한 성을 쌓자!
④ Sarah는 바다에 선물로 주기 위해 가능한 한 큰 성을 쌓으려 노력한다.
⑤ Sarah는 모래성이 파괴될 것을 알지만, 기쁘게 다시 쌓는다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk - for body and mind.
options: ① 환경의 변화로 인해 다양한 직업군이 생겨나고 있다.
② 기술의 진보에 치중하다 보면 다양한 문제 상황에 직면하게 된다.
③ 미리 다가올 질병에 대해 대비하면 어떠한 질병도 극복 가능하다.
④ 교육이 우리 사회에 미치는 부정적인 영향력을 간과해서는 안된다.
⑤ 우리는 고수익의 직장을 갖는 것을 인생의 목표로 삼지 않도록 해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기술 채택에 따른 비용(대가)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 전통적인 생계 수단이 사라지고, 사람들이 싫어하는 일을 하며 신체적 고통이나 만성 질환을 겪기도 하고, 머리와 손이 분리된 디지털 업무가 정신적 스트레스와 건강상의 위험을 초래한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 기술의 진보가 가져오는 다양한 부정적 문제 상황을 지적하는 ②번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
options: ① You need to adopt the strong points of over - optimism.
② Do what you like to do first when you have lots of things to do.
③ Don't put off tasks that you can complete in just a few moments.
④ Learning from experience brings lessons that you can't learn from books.
⑤ Identify the time required to perform the assignment and schedule accordingly.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 계획한 일을 성취하기 위해 각 업무가 얼마나 걸릴지 정확히 파악하고 그에 맞춰 일정을 짜는 것이 중요하다고 강조합니다. 지나친 낙관주의를 경계하고 가용 시간에 맞춰 업무를 배치하라는 조언을 담고 있으므로 ⑤번 '수행해야 할 과제에 필요한 시간을 확인하고 그에 따라 일정을 계획하라'가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 과도한 낙관주의의 장점을 수용할 필요가 있다.
② 할 일이 많을 때는 당신이 좋아하는 일을 먼저 하라.
③ 아주 짧은 시간 안에 끝낼 수 있는 일을 미루지 마라.
④ 경험으로부터 배우는 것은 책에서 배울 수 없는 교훈을 가져다준다.
⑤ 과제를 수행하는 데 필요한 시간을 확인하고 그에 맞춰 일정을 계획하라.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 'curse of knowledge'가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the '<u>curse of knowledge</u>'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
options: ① Nothing is a waste of time if you use the experience wisely.
② A long life may not be good enough, but a good life is long enough.
③ Our greatest glory is not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall.
④ We all have big changes in our lives that are more or less a second chance.
⑤ When you are familiar with something, it is hard to understand people we are not.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'는 전문가가 자신이 이미 알고 있는 지식 때문에 초보자가 겪는 어려움을 이해하지 못하거나 과소평가하게 되는 현상을 의미합니다. 따라서 ⑤번 '무언가에 익숙해졌을 때, 그렇지 않은 사람들을 이해하기 어렵다'가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 경험을 현명하게 사용한다면 어떤 것도 시간 낭비가 아니다.
② 긴 인생이 충분히 좋지 않을 수도 있지만, 좋은 인생은 충분히 길다.
③ 우리의 가장 큰 영광은 결코 넘어지지 않는 것이 아니라, 넘어질 때마다 일어나는 데 있다.
④ 우리 모두의 삶에는 다소 두 번째 기회와 같은 큰 변화들이 있다.
⑤ 당신이 무언가에 익숙할 때, 그렇지 않은 사람들을 이해하는 것은 어렵다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① traffic order education for drivers
③ changes in the walking position of humanity
④ relationship between speed of movement and detail processing
⑤ necessity of separating bicycle riders' paths from pedestrian paths
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력에 미치는 영향에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 걷는 속도에 맞춰 진화한 인간의 감각은 속도가 빨라질수록(운전자) 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력이 제한되고, 느릴수록(보행자) 환경의 세부 사항을 더 잘 감상할 수 있다는 내용을 설명합니다. 따라서 ④번 '이동 속도와 세부 정보 처리 사이의 관계'가 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 운전자를 위한 교통 질서 교육
② 보행자 이동 시 주의사항
③ 인류의 보행 자세의 변화
④ 이동 속도와 세부 처리 사이의 관계
⑤ 자전거 도로와 보행자 도로 분리의 필요성

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent -to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① efforts to deal with climate change over different countries
② necessity of movement so that creatures escape predators
③ importance of how creatures manage to endure heat or cold
④ influences of climate change on creatures' movement and spread
⑤ requirements with humans need for participating in social activities
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화가 생물종의 이동과 확산에 미치는 영향을 다루고 있습니다. 모든 생물은 특정 기후 조건을 필요로 하며, 기후가 변하면 그 조건에 맞는 장소를 찾아 이동해야 한다는 점을 설명합니다. 나무나 따개비와 같이 고착된 생물조차도 생애의 특정 단계(씨앗이나 유충)에서 이동을 하며, 과거 기후 변화 시기에도 이러한 이동이 일어났음을 화석을 통해 알 수 있다는 내용을 포함하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 여러 국가의 기후 변화 대응 노력
② 포식자로부터 도망치기 위한 생물의 이동 필요성
③ 생물들이 더위나 추위를 견뎌내는 방식의 중요성
④ 기후 변화가 생물의 이동과 확산에 미치는 영향
⑤ 인간이 사회 활동에 참여하기 위해 필요한 요구 사항

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ① Music: Make Your Free Time Better with It
② Lower Your Stress with a Relaxing Meditation
③ What a Wonderful Power Music Has in Treatment
④ Don't Have Too Much Faith in Group Music Therapy
⑤ The More You Waste Your Time, the More You Have Regrets
questions.explanation: 이 글은 정신 질환을 앓고 있는 사람들에게 그룹 음악 치료(노래 부르기, 작곡 등)와 그룹 합창이 삶의 질 개선, 정서적 상태 호전, 소속감 형성 및 자신감 향상 등 긍정적인 영향을 미친다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 치료에 있어서 음악이 가진 놀라운 힘을 강조하는 제목이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 음악: 그것과 함께 당신의 여가 시간을 더 좋게 만드세요
② 편안한 명상으로 스트레스를 낮추세요
③ 치료에 있어서 음악이 가진 얼마나 놀라운 힘인가
④ 그룹 음악 치료에 너무 많은 믿음을 갖지 마세요
⑤ 시간을 낭비할수록, 후회는 더 커집니다

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing 一 all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
options: ① Finishing Projects: The Sooner the Better
② Your Future: Already in Your Mind
⑤ How to Work in Harmony
questions.explanation: 이 글은 모든 창조물(집, 자동차, 옷 등)이 물리적으로 실현되기 전에 이미 설계자의 마음속에서 먼저 완성된다는 점을 언급하며, 인간의 미래 또한 같은 과정을 거친다고 설명합니다. 미래에 대한 생각이 먼저 정립되고 다듬어지면, 그 비전을 실현하기 위해 생각과 결정, 활동이 조화롭게 작동한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '당신의 미래: 이미 당신의 마음속에 있다'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 프로젝트 마무리하기: 빠를수록 좋다
② 당신의 미래: 이미 당신의 마음속에 있다
③ 물리적 현실의 정의
④ 좋은 시작의 중요성
⑤ 조화롭게 일하는 법

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions ⓐ<u>improved</u>. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and ⓑ<u>cheaper</u> to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, ⓒ<u>opened</u> up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made ⓓ<u>possible</u> the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the ⓔ<u>extinction</u> of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
questions.explanation: 글의 문맥상 항공 운송이 전 세계의 더 많은 곳을 열어주고 관광 산업의 성장을 이끌었다는 내용이 되어야 하므로, '멸종/소멸'을 뜻하는 extinction은 부적절합니다. 항공 운송의 '출현'이나 '도입'을 뜻하는 appearance, advent, arrival 등의 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always ⓐ<u>positive</u> for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a ⓑ<u>sensible</u> thing to do." explains famous psychologist, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler clues within the environment can signal ⓒ<u>trustworthiness</u>. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful ⓓ<u>cue</u> that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to ⓔ<u>avoid</u> the practices of those around you.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 사회적 증거(다른 사람들의 행동)를 따르는 것이 생존과 의사결정에 도움이 된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 주변 사람들의 관습이나 행동을 '피하는(avoid)' 것이 좋다는 내용은 글의 전체적인 흐름과 반대됩니다. '따르는(follow)' 것이 좋다는 맥락이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have (A)[more / less] control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it. And this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because 一 fueled by emotions 一 you make the (B)[right / wrong] decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that (C)[suppress / improve] you. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 잠재의식은 감정을 다루지 않고 빠르게 작동한다고 했으나, 의식적인 마음은 우리가 생각하고 선택할 수 있는 부분이므로 더 많은(more) 통제권을 가집니다. (B) 의식적인 마음이 감정에 의해 자극을 받으면 실수를 하게 되므로 '틀린(wrong)' 결정을 내린다는 흐름이 적절합니다. (C) 판단이 감정에 의해 흐려지면 편향과 부정적인 것들이 생겨나 우리를 '억누르게(suppress)' 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 더 많은 - 잘못된 - 억누르다
② 더 적은 - 옳은 - 억누르다
③ 더 많은 - 옳은 - 억누르다
④ 더 적은 - 옳은 - 개선하다
⑤ 더 많은 - 잘못된 - 개선하다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with (A)[humanlike / animallike] facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "(B)[unnatural / natural]" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally (C)[attractive / unattractive], both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.explanation: (A) 동물 캐릭터를 인간과 닮게 변형한다고 했으므로 '인간과 같은(humanlike)' 얼굴 특징을 보여준다는 것이 적절합니다. (B) 최근의 경향은 동물을 더 '자연스러운(natural)' 방식으로 보여주려 하지만, 여전히 인간의 특징을 사용한다는 대조의 흐름입니다. (C) 아이들과 어른들에게 감정적으로 더 '매력적으로(attractive)' 보이게 하기 위해 아이 같은 특징을 부여한다는 설명이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간과 같은 - 자연스러운 - 매력적인
② 동물과 같은 - 자연스러운 - 매력적이지 않은
③ 인간과 같은 - 자연스러운 - 매력적이지 않은
④ 동물과 같은 - 부자연스러운 - 매력적인
⑤ 인간과 같은 - 부자연스러운 - 매력적인

questions.question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals 一 sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds.

(B) Those are the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize.
(C) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start. Aristotle missed a few things in humans.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 아리스토텔레스가 제시한 5가지 감각을 언급합니다. (C)에서 이를 의심할 이유가 있다고 반박하며 아리스토텔레스가 인간에게서 몇 가지를 놓쳤다고 말합니다. (B)에서 그 놓친 부분인 신체 인식과 균형 감각을 구체적으로 설명하며 다른 동물의 감각을 언급합니다. (A)에서 척추동물과 뱀의 예를 들어 감각을 제한된 수로 명확히 나눌 수 없음을 결론짓습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. (A) Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. (B) As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. (C) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. (D) Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. (E) It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.insertion_sentence: Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 '작용하는 기제는 장소가 아니라 시간이다'라는 내용은 맛의 인지가 혀의 위치(장소)에 따른 것이 아니라는 (D)의 설명 뒤에 보충 설명으로 적절합니다. (E) 앞에서 혀의 모든 곳에서 맛을 느낄 수 있다고 설명한 뒤, (E) 뒤 문장에서 단맛을 혀끝에서 느끼는 것이 아니라 그 지각을 '먼저(first)' 등록하는 것(시간)이라는 구체적 설명이 이어집니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally 一 they are functionally blind. (B) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened: same with the other sensing systems. (C) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (D) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. (E) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.insertion_sentence: But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 '그것(지각적 이탈) 없이는 잠이 불가능하므로, 정의에 필수적인 것으로 보인다'는 내용은 (D)에서 일부 저자들이 지각적 이탈을 잠의 정의의 일부로 간주하지 않는다는 내용에 대한 반박으로 이어져야 합니다. (E)의 Nevertheless 앞인 (E) 자리에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 안내문의 Clothes Upcycling Contest 2024에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Clothes Upcycling Contest 2024 Are you passionate about fashion and the environment? Then we have a contest for you!•Participants -Anyone living in Lakewood,  aged 11 to 18•How to participate -Take before and after photos of your upcycled clothes. -Email the photos at lovelw@lwplus.com. -Send in the photos from April 14 to May 12.•Wining Prize -A $100 gift card to use at local shops
options: ① 패션과 환경에 열정이 있는 사람을 위한 대회이다.
② Lakewood에 거주하는 11세에서 18세 누구나 참여 가능하다.
③ 업사이클링한 옷의 전과 후 사진을 찍어서 제출해야 한다.
⑤ 우승 상품은 지역 상점에서 사용할 수 있는 100달러 기프트 카드이다.
questions.explanation: 안내문의 'How to participate' 항목에 따르면 사진은 이메일(lovelw@lwplus.com)로 보내야 한다고 명시되어 있으므로 우편으로 보내야 한다는 ④번 설명은 옳지 않습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption ⓐ<u>that</u> because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description ⓑ<u>containing</u> the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, ⓒ<u>which</u> the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions ⓓ<u>formed</u> by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only ⓔ<u>affect</u> the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
questions.explanation: ⓒ 뒤의 절 'the students were asked to give their impressions of him'은 주어, 동사, 목적어가 모두 갖춰진 완전한 문장입니다. 관계대명사 'which'는 뒤에 불완전한 절을 이끌어야 하므로 부적절하며, 문맥상 '그 토론에서'라는 의미를 나타내는 전치사+관계대명사 'in which' 또는 관계부사 'where'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에 문맥의 흐름으로 보아, 관련이 없는 문장은?
questions.passage: It is difficult for any of us to maintain a constant level of attention throughout our working day. We all have body rhythms characterised by peaks and valleys of energy and alertness. ⓐYou will achieve more, and feel confident as a benefit, if you schedule your most demanding tasks at times when you are best able to cope with them. ⓑIf you haven't thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to observe yourself. ⓒSlow paced charging will limit the rush for power, and thus reducing your energy peaks. ⓓTry to note the times when you are at your best. ⓔFor some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for others it may take a while to warm up.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 자신의 에너지 수준이 가장 높은 시간(peak)을 파악하여 그에 맞춰 가장 까다로운 업무를 처리하라는 조언입니다. 그러나 ⓒ번 문장은 저속 충전이 전력 소모를 제한하여 에너지 정점을 줄인다는 내용으로, 개인의 생체 리듬과 업무 효율에 관한 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에 문맥의 흐름으로 보아, 관련이 없는 문장은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. ⓐGenerally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. ⓑThis east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. ⓒStudies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. ⓓMany players often have a trouble with resigning a professional baseball team since they consider an annual salary and a player management system. ⓔA more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 비행 방향(동쪽 vs 서쪽)에 따른 시차 적응의 차이와 그것이 스포츠 팀의 경기력에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ⓓ번 문장은 선수들이 연봉이나 관리 시스템 때문에 팀을 사퇴하는 문제에 대해 언급하고 있으므로 글의 주제와 무관합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is ________________ because the soil stays healthy.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 돌려짓기(crop rotation)를 통해 토양의 영양분을 보존하고 건강하게 유지하는 농법을 설명하고 있습니다. 토양을 건강하게 유지하여 장기적으로 농사를 지을 수 있게 하므로 이러한 방식은 '지속 가능한(sustainable)' 방식입니다.
options_translation: ① 즉각적인
② 지속 가능한
③ 분리된
④ 일회용의
⑤ 예기치 못한

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that ___________________________________. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ② reflect the needs of customers
④ enable business to maximize its profits
⑤ have a reasonable price and good quality
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에서 마케팅 혁명이 일어나며 고객의 다양하고 복잡한 요구를 충족시키는 것이 비즈니스의 초점이 되었다고 언급합니다. 따라서 기업은 단순히 품질 좋은 제품을 만드는 것을 넘어 '고객의 요구를 반영하는' 제품을 전달하는 것이 필수적이게 되었습니다.
options_translation: ① 기업의 성장을 극대화하는
② 고객의 요구를 반영하는
③ 생산자의 이익만을 고려하는
④ 기업이 이윤을 극대화하게 해주는
⑤ 합리적인 가격과 좋은 품질을 가진

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far - reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.summary_sentence: Leaders started with (A)_________ people (B)_________ in their daily lives, so we can all be leaders.
options: ④ extraordinary / being respectful of others
⑤ unique / having a lot of conversation
questions.explanation: 지문은 위대한 리더들도 처음에는 우리와 같은 평범한(ordinary) 학생이나 시민으로 시작했으며, 일상의 개선점(improvements)을 찾는 과정에서 리더로 성장했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 ordinary, (B)에는 looking for improvements가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 평범한 / 개선을 찾는
② 비범한 / 고도의 기술을 사용하는
③ 평범한 / 실수를 반복하지 않는
④ 비범한 / 타인을 존중하는
⑤ 독특한 / 많은 대화를 나누는

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more High School English Exam Data Extraction energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. _________________________________________ with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
subjective_conditions: 1. their, satisfy, likely, those, happier를 모두 포함하여 문장을 완성하시오. (문맥에 맞도록 단어 형태 변형 가능)
2. 10단어 이상의 한 문장으로 작성하시오.
questions.answer: Those satisfied with their work are likely to be happier
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 일에서 만족을 느끼는 사람들이 삶 전반에 걸쳐 더 행복할 가능성이 높다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 'those'를 주어로 하고 수식어구인 'satisfied with their work'를 붙인 뒤 'are likely to be happier'로 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should ________________________________________________. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
subjective_conditions: 1. suit, specific, of, adjust를 모두 포함하여 문장을 완성하시오. (문맥에 맞도록 단어 형태 변형 가능)
2. 빈칸에 8단어 이상을 작성하여 해당 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.answer: be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal
questions.explanation: 각 동물마다 특성이 다르므로 치유 세션 또한 개별 동물에 맞게 조정되어야 한다는 내용이 필요합니다. 'should' 뒤에 수동태 'be adjusted'를 쓰고 목적을 나타내는 'to suit the specific needs of the animal'을 사용하여 8단어 이상의 문장을 구성합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. _________________________________________ from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
subjective_conditions: 가주어 it, 진주어 to~를 활용하여 쓰시오.
from, steps, essential를 모두 포함하여 문장을 완성하시오. (문맥에 맞도록 단어 형태 변형 가능)
9단어 이상의 한 문장으로 작성하시오.
questions.answer: It is essential to take (a few) steps back from (the) painting
questions.explanation: 그림을 그릴 때 지나치게 세부 사항에 집착하지 않고 전체적인 진행 상황을 확인하기 위해 가끔 뒤로 물러나서 보는 것이 중요하다는 맥락입니다. 가주어 It과 진주어 to-v 구문을 사용하고, 필수 단어(essential, steps, from)를 포함하여 '그림으로부터 몇 걸음 뒤로 물러나는 것이 필수적이다'라는 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just _____________________________________. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
subjective_conditions: state, convert를 모두 포함하여 문장을 완성하시오. (문맥에 맞도록 단어 형태 변형 가능)
6단어 이상의 한 문장으로 작성하시오.
명령문으로 작성하시오.
questions.answer: convert challenge statement(s) into positive statement(s)
questions.explanation: 자신이 직면한 어려움들을 적은 뒤, 그것을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸어 쓰라는 내용입니다. 'convert A into B(A를 B로 바꾸다)' 표현을 사용하고, 명령문 형태(동사원형 시작)로 작성해야 합니다. 'challenges'를 'positive statements'로 변환하라는 지시가 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental fators can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ① 동물의 특성은 유전적 요인과 환경적 요인으로 결정된다.
② 동물의 다양한 치료법을 학습하기 위해서 오랜 시간이 걸린다.
③ 동물의 치료 활동을 결정하기 위해서 환경적 요인을 고려해야 한다.
④ 동물의 치료법은 각각의 특정한 상황과 필요에 맞도록 조정되어야 한다.
⑤ 동물의 신체적 질병 치료법은 감정적 동요를 면밀히 관찰하여 결정해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부 이후 "every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal"이라는 문장을 통해, 모든 동물 치료 과정은 다르게 탐색되어야 하며 동물의 특정한 요구에 맞춰 조정되어야 한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 요지로는 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 동물의 특성은 유전적 요인과 환경적 요인으로 결정된다.
② 동물의 다양한 치료법을 학습하기 위해서 오랜 시간이 걸린다.
③ 동물의 치료 활동을 결정하기 위해서 환경적 요인을 고려해야 한다.
④ 동물의 치료법은 각각의 특정한 상황과 필요에 맞도록 조정되어야 한다.
⑤ 동물의 신체적 질병 치료법은 감정적 동요를 면밀히 관찰하여 결정해야 한다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르면? [3.1점]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that ⓐ<u>prevents</u> disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are ⓑ<u>pro-dissent</u>. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques and regularly claim to continually ⓒ<u>discourage</u> internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these ⓓ<u>objectors</u> because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something ⓔ<u>finished</u>."
questions.explanation: 상사들은 대외적인 인터뷰에서 자신들이 반대 의견을 환영하고 수용하는 태도를 가진 것처럼 말합니다. 따라서 문맥상 하급자들로부터의 내부적인 저항(protest)을 '낙담시키거나 억제한다(discourage)'고 주장하는 것이 아니라, '장려한다(encourage)'고 주장하는 것이 흐름상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs.
ordered_passages: (A) Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting.

(B) The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
(C) The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 심리학자들이 정신 질환자를 대상으로 음악 치료 연구를 했다는 내용이 나온다. (C)에서 그 연구의 결과가 삶의 질을 향상시켰음을 보여주고, (A)에서는 '또 다른 심리학자 그룹'이 노래 부르기의 효능에 집중하여 기사들을 검토했다고 언급하며 연구 대상을 좁힌다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 합창(노래 부르기)에 참여했을 때의 구체적인 긍정적 결과들을 설명하는 순서가 가장 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① Don't Trick People by Telling a Lie
② Positively Alter the Depiction of Challenges
③ Want to Perform the Magic Well? Practice It Steadily!
④ Trust Yourself, Then You Can Reach Your Fullest Potential
⑤ Challenge Spirit: Confront the Difficulties and Keep Trying
questions.explanation: 글쓴이는 자신이 직면한 도전을 적고 그 진술을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸는 것만으로도 사고와 행동에 변화가 생겨 마법 같은 일이 일어날 수 있다고 말하고 있다. 따라서 제목으로는 2번 '도전에 대한 묘사를 긍정적으로 바꾸라'가 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 거짓말을 함으로써 사람들을 속이지 마라
② 도전에 대한 묘사를 긍정적으로 바꾸라
③ 마술을 잘 하고 싶은가? 꾸준히 연습하라!
④ 자신을 믿어라, 그러면 당신의 최대한의 잠재력에 도달할 수 있다
⑤ 도전 정신: 어려움에 맞서고 계속 노력하라

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 적절한 것만을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking ⓐ<u>features</u> of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information obviously ⓑ<u>get</u> in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to ⓒ<u>waking</u> the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of ⓓ<u>protect</u> sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness ⓔ<u>to obtain</u> some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: ⓐ features: 'One of the + 밵수명사' 구문으로 밵수형인 features는 적절합니다.ⓑ get: 주어가 Some visual information으로 단수 취급하므로 gets가 되앴 합니다.ⓒ waking: fail to 다음에는 동사원형이 와앴 하므로 wake가 되앴 합니다.ⓓ protect: 전츘사 of 다음에는 동명사가 와앴 하므로 protecting이 되앴 합니다.ⓔ to obtain: '잠의 이점을 얻기 위해서'라는 목적을 내타내는 to부정사의 부사적 용법으로 적절합니다.따라서 적절한 감은 ⓐ와 ⓔ입니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것만을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
questions.passage: Generally, we are ⑀<u>unwilling to</u> accept Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. as leaders. If you consider the historical importance and ⑁<u>extensive</u> influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who ⑂<u>discarded</u> ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with other, seeking their opinions and feedback and ⑃<u>incessantly</u> looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, ⑄<u>irrespective of</u> age or experience.
questions.explanation: ⑀ 사람들은 보통 링컨이나 킹 목사를 리더로 받아들이는 데 'willing(기께이 하는)' 것이 문묥사 자연스럽습니다. ⑂ 이 리더들도 처음에는 일상의 개선을 윐한 생각을 버리는(discarded) 것이 아니라 '품고 있었던(held/possessed)' 사람들이었습니다. ⑁, ⑃, ⑄눤 문묥사 적절하게 사용되었습니다.

questions.question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked.
ordered_passages: (A) To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable.

(B) People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication.
(C) In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 '감사합니다'라고 말하는 규범에 대해 설명합니다. (B)에서 앞 문장의 'marked'에 대한 부연 설명으로 사람들이 그것을 기대하며 말하지 않을 시 비난받을 만하다는 내용이 이어집니다. 그 후 (B)의 마지막 문장인 타 문화권 규범에 대한 언급을 (A)의 'To continue the Thank you example'이 받아 타 문화에서는 비용이 상당할 때만 감사 인사를 한다는 예시를 듭니다. 마지막으로 (C)의 'In such a case'가 (A)의 예시 상황을 가리키며 문장이 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. ①<u>However, the philosopher Fiona Macpherson revealed that this could be doubted for several reasons</u>. ②<u>First, Aristotle omitted something in humans such as the perception of our body that is distinct from touch and the sense of balance</u>. ③<u>Moreover, in animals, there are complex senses which are more difficult to classify</u>. ④<u>On top of that, snakes solely use just five senses mentioned above to seek prey like other vertebrates</u>. ⑤<u>Some animals have a different sense system for perceiving odors</u>. These examples tell us that 'senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds,' Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate ᄀᅠ가동물 **odor 내매
questions.explanation: ④번 문장은 뱀이 다른 척추동물처뜜 위에서 언갉된 5가지 감각만을 사용한다고 하고 있으나, 이 글의 전체적인 흠름은 아리솤텔레스가 정의한 5가지 감각 이외에도 더 다양한 감각이 존재한다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 5가지 감각만을 사용한다는 내용은 글의 주제와 상반됩니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. ①<u>Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads</u>. ②<u>They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions</u>. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. ③<u>The Inca built the huts on high ground in sight of one another</u>. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. ④<u>The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610km) in three or four days under good conditions</u>. ⑤<u>Atahuallpa was the 13th emperor of the Incas who achieved victory in a devastating civil war with his half brother</u>.*excel 타궐하다 **messenger 전령
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인카 제국의 파발 시스템(차스키)의 효율성개 운영 방식에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ⑤번 문장은 인카 황제 아타왈파의 내전 승리에 대한 내용으로, 메시지 전달 체계와는 관련이 없습니다.

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 주어진 조건에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer who wants to grow three crops has three fields, he or she may grow peanuts in the first field, cabbages in the second, and potatoes in the third. The second year, potatoes will be in the second field, (A)_____________ in the first field, and the crop which was originally in the first field will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again like this. And then the (B)____________ year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
subjective_conditions: 1. 빈칸 (A), (B) 모두 위의 지문에 나온 한 단어로 채울 것
2. 어법상 오류가 있거나, 철자 오류로 문장의 의미가 바뀔 경우 감점함
questions.explanation: 지문에서 설명한 윤작 순서에 따르면, 2년째에는 첫 번째 밭에 양배추(cabbages)가 오게 됩니다. 3년째에 다시 순환한 후 그 다음 해인 4년째(the next year)에는 원래의 순서로 돌아가게 됩니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하려고 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 주어진 조건에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer who wants to grow three crops has three fields, he or she may grow peanuts in the first field, cabbages in the second, and potatoes in the third. The second year, potatoes will be in the second field, (A)_____________ in the first field, and the crop which was originally in the first field will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again like this. And then the (B)____________ year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.summary_sentence: Crop rotation is a practice that the first crop _______________________________________ to maintain the soil health.
subjective_conditions: 1. 주어진 단어들만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 올바른 순서로 배열할 것 : different crops / on the land / on the same land / follow / plant / be
2. 필요시 주어진 단어들 중 동사들을 변형시킬 것
3. 어법상 오류가 있거나, 철자 오류로 문장의 의미가 바뀔 경우 감점함
questions.answer: planted on the land is followed by different crops on the same land.
questions.explanation: 주어진 단어를 활용하여 '땅에 심어진 첫 번째 작물이 같은 땅에서 다른 작물들에 의해 뒤따라지는 관행'이라는 문장을 만듭니다. 'the first crop'을 수식하는 분사 'planted on the land'를 사용하고, 뒤에 수동태 'is followed by'를 구성합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)를 주어진 조건에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the text above, those most (A)_____________ with their work are even more (B)_____________ with their lives eventually.
questions.explanation: 본문은 일에서 의미와 성취감을 찾는 사람들이 더 생산적일 뿐만 아니라 전반적인 삶에서도 더 행복하다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 일에 '만족하는(contented/satisfied)'이, (B)에는 삶에서 '기쁜/만족스러운(pleased/happier)'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
options: ② 고객의 재구매율을 기록하는 습관을 길러라.
③ 무급의 홍보대사가 기업을 돕도록 지원하라.
④ 기업의 최우선 목표를 고객 만족도로 지정하라.
⑤ 부정적인 입소문 광고는 설문조사를 통해 차단하라.
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부에서 'customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list(고객 만족이 할 일 목록의 최우선 순위에 있어야 한다)'라고 명시하고 있으므로 ④가 필자의 주장입니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
