questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. When an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen to him because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
options: ① 사람은 자신의 직업에 관한 말을 할 때 재능이 극대화된다.
② 사람들은 특정 분야에서 높은 수행 능력을 보이는 사람과 연결되기를 원한다.
③ 다양한 분야에서 특출한 성과를 만들어 낸 유명인을 존경하는 사회 분위기가 형성됐다.
④ 남들과 연결됨은 수많은 분야에서 전문적인 지식을 습득하는 것부터 시작된다.
⑤ 본인의 전문성과 관련되지 않은 조언을 구하는 것은 타인과의 관계 형성에 도움이 되지 않는다.
questions.explanation: 특정 분야에서 뛰어난 능력을 발휘하는 사람(Excellence)은 다른 사람들에게 신뢰를 얻으며, 사람들은 그들의 분야와 상관없는 조언까지 경청하며 그들과 연결되기를 원한다는 내용이므로 ②가 요지입니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, which then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly. As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you." If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler has been transmitted via our body. Strange as it may sound, this theory states that emotions arise from our bodies. For example, our mood can be improved by simply lifting up the corners of our mouth. The primacy of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase "I must be afraid, because I'm running."
options: ① emotions emerging from our bodies
② our behaviors influenced by language
③ reasons why negative feelings go away quickly
④ importance of hiding emotions through body language
⑤ our common belief that mood is influenced by what others say
questions.explanation: 이 글은 감정이 신체에서 비롯된다는 이론(emotions arise from our bodies)을 설명하고 있습니다. 타인의 표정을 따라 함으로써 같은 감정을 느끼게 되거나, 입꼬리를 올리는 것만으로 기분이 좋아지는 예시가 이를 뒷받침하므로 ①이 주제입니다.
options_translation: 우리 신체에서 나타나는 감정들
언어에 의해 영향을 받는 우리의 행동들
부정적인 감정이 빨리 사라지는 이유
바디 랭귀지를 통해 감정을 숨기는 것의 중요성
기분이 타인의 말에 영향을 받는다는 우리의 일반적인 믿음

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy arises from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. No neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
options: ① Processing the Economy with Reality
② Brains: the Dark Shadow of Isolation
③ The Brain Operates Like a City's Economy
④ Reasons Why Economy Can't be Answered
⑤ How Superhighways of Neurons Create Economy
questions.explanation: 뇌의 작동 방식을 도시의 경제에 비유하여 설명하고 있습니다. 경제가 한 곳에서 일어나는 것이 아니라 여러 요소의 상호작용으로 발생하듯, 뇌의 활동도 각 부위의 상호작용을 통해 이루어진다는 내용이므로 ③이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 현실을 통해 경제를 처리하기
뇌: 고립의 어두운 그림자
뇌는 도시의 경제처럼 작동한다
경제에 답할 수 없는 이유
뉴런의 고속도로가 어떻게 경제를 만드는가

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. Although it may seem sensible, _________________ ____________________. To check if something is missing, you will find yourself checking your to-do lists multiple times. Instead, organize all of your tasks in one place. It doesn't matter if you use digital or paper media. It's okay to keep your professional and personal tasks in once place. This will give you a good idea of how time is divided between work and home. This will allow you to make informed decisions about which tasks are most important.
options: ① examine your to-do lists several times
② using only one journal to keep records can lead to confusion
③ do all of your personal and professional tasks in one calendar
④ make well-informed choices regarding the top concerns of your task
⑤ keeping different calendars for your personal and professional life can cause distractions
questions.explanation: 일과 개인 생활을 위해 두 개의 달력을 사용하는 것이 현명해 보일 수 있지만, 실제로는 무엇인가를 빠뜨렸는지 확인하기 위해 여러 번 리스트를 확인하게 되는 등 주의 산만을 초래할 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 이러한 부작용을 설명하는 5번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 할 일 목록을 여러 번 검토하는 것
② 기록을 유지하기 위해 단 하나의 일기장만 사용하는 것은 혼란을 야기할 수 있다
③ 하나의 달력에 당신의 모든 개인적이고 직업적인 일들을 처리하는 것
④ 당신의 업무 중 가장 중요한 관심사에 관해 충분한 정보에 근거한 선택을 내리는 것
⑤ 개인 생활과 직장 생활을 위해 서로 다른 달력을 유지하는 것은 주의 산만을 초래할 수 있다

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so ___________ that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average.
questions.explanation: 사람들이 스스로를 평균 이상이라고 믿는 현상(레이크 워비건 효과)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 대다수의 대중과 수많은 고등학생들의 사례를 통해 이 현상이 매우 흔하고 도처에 널려 있음을 알 수 있으므로 'ubiquitous(어디에나 있는, 아주 흔한)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 드문
② 창의적인
③ 바람직한
④ 어디에나 있는
⑤ 편견이 있는

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, allowing us humans to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. ________________________________________. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries.
options: ① Why we have less time is an unsolved mystery
② Both big and small businesses have placed the burden of work on their customers
③ Companies large and small have found ways to reduce work done by their consumers
④ The promised result of a computerized society has become a reality for people in our era
⑤ Companies are expecting their workers to put in more effort to provide even more services
questions.explanation: 컴퓨터화된 사회가 인간의 업무를 대신하여 여유 시간을 늘려줄 것이라 예상했으나, 실제로는 기업이 과거에 제공하던 서비스(항공 예약, 식료품 담기 등)를 고객이 직접 하게 함으로써 인간의 시간이 더 부족해졌다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 기업이 업무 부담을 고객에게 전가했다는 내용인 2번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 우리가 시간이 더 적은지는 풀리지 않는 수수께끼이다
② 대기업과 소기업 모두 업무의 부담을 고객에게 전가해 왔다
③ 크고 작은 회사들이 소비자들에 의해 수행되는 업무를 줄이는 방법을 찾아냈다
④ 컴퓨터화된 사회의 약속된 결과는 우리 시대 사람들에게 현실이 되었다
⑤ 기업들은 직원들이 더 많은 서비스를 제공하기 위해 더 많은 노력을 기울일 것을 기대하고 있다

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were seldom sufficient to support a full-time chief or village council. The development of agriculture changed work patterns. Early farmers could reap 3-10kg of grain from each 1kg of seed planted.
ordered_passages: (B) Specialists such as carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their skills. They became more efficient in their use of time and energy. The goods and services they offered brought about an improved quality of life, a higher standard of living, and, for most societies, increased stability.

(C) Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided support for nonfarmers such as chieftains, village councils, priests, and warriors. In return, the nonfarmers provided leadership and security for the farming population. This enabled farmers to continue to boost food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses.

(D) With improved technology and favorable conditions, agriculture produced consistent surpluses of the basic necessities. Therefore, population groups reduced in size. These groups concentrated in towns and cities. Thus, human tasks specialized further.
questions.explanation: (A)의 마지막 부분에서 농업의 시작으로 곡물 수확량이 늘어났다는 언급이 나옵니다. (C)에서 이 식량/에너지 잉여(this food/energy surplus)가 비농업인들을 지원하게 되었다는 내용으로 이어지며, 이로 인해 생산량이 더 늘어납니다. (D)에서는 이러한 지속적인 잉여로 인해 인구 집단이 도시로 집중되고 업무가 전문화되었다는 내용이 나오고, (B)에서 그 전문화된 사람들(Specialists)의 예시와 그로 인한 생활 수준 향상을 설명하며 마무리되는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: (A) Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were seldom sufficient to support a full-time chief or village council. The ⓐ<u>development</u> of agriculture changed work patterns. Early farmers could reap 3-10kg of grain from each 1kg of seed planted.(B) Specialists such as carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their skills. They became more efficient in their use of time and energy. The goods and services they ⓑ<u>offered</u> brought about an improved quality of life, a higher standard of living, and, for most societies, increased stability.(C) Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided support for nonfarmers such as chieftains, village councils, priests, and warriors. In return, the nonfarmers ⓒ<u>provided</u> leadership and security for the farming population. This enabled farmers to continue to ⓓ<u>boost</u> food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses.(D) With improved technology and favorable conditions, agriculture produced consistent surpluses of the basic necessities. Therefore, population groups ⓔ<u>reduced</u> in size. These groups concentrated in towns and cities. Thus, human tasks specialized further.
questions.explanation: (D)에서 농업이 기본 생필품의 지속적인 잉여를 생산함에 따라 인구 집단의 크기는 '줄어드는(reduced)' 것이 아니라 '늘어났으며(increased/expanded)', 이들이 도시로 집중되게 되었습니다. 따라서 ⓔ가 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 22. 윗글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: (A) Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were seldom sufficient to support a full-time chief or village council. The development of agriculture changed work patterns. Early farmers could reap 3-10kg of grain from each 1kg of seed planted.(B) Specialists such as carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their skills. They became more efficient in their use of time and energy. The goods and services they offered brought about an improved quality of life, a higher standard of living, and, for most societies, increased stability.(C) Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided support for nonfarmers such as chieftains, village councils, priests, and warriors. In return, the nonfarmers provided leadership and security for the farming population. This enabled farmers to continue to boost food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses.(D) With improved technology and favorable conditions, agriculture produced consistent surpluses of the basic necessities. Therefore, population groups increased in size. These groups concentrated in towns and cities. Thus, human tasks specialized further.
options: ① 초기 수렵채집 사회의 추장 대부분은 다른 사람들과 같이 수렵 및 채집해야만 했다.
② 농업의 발전은 작업 패턴을 변화시켰다.
③ 잉여 식량의 일부는 지역 사회에 환원되고 비농업인을 위한 지원을 제공했다.
④ 향상된 기술과 유리한 조건으로, 농업은 기본 생필품의 지속적인 잉여를 생산했다.
⑤ 농업이 더욱 많은 자원을 생산해 낼수록 사람들은 마을과 도시를 떠나갔다.
questions.explanation: 지문 (D)에 따르면 농업의 잉여 생산으로 인해 인구 집단이 마을과 도시에 '집중(concentrated)'되었다고 했으므로, 사람들이 마을과 도시를 떠나갔다는 ⑤번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped increase sales.
options: ① Improving product quality was a key to enhancing sales.
② Relying on ineffective advertising strategies resulted in losses in business.
③ Hiring various advertising agencies was effective to promote brand awareness.
④ Reshaping consumer perceptions was not as effective as other advertising strategies.
⑤ Shifting the focus of product strengths in advertising succeeded in boosting sales.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 Fleischmann의 효모가 가정용 빵 재료에서 비타민 공급원, 그리고 천연 완하제로 마케팅 포인트를 변화시킴으로써 매출을 올린 사례를 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 광고에서 제품 강점의 초점을 전환하는 것이 매출 신장에 성공했다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 제품 품질을 개선하는 것이 판매 증진의 핵심이었다.
② 비효율적인 광고 전략에 의존하는 것은 사업 손실을 초래했다.
③ 다양한 광고 대행사를 고용하는 것이 브랜드 인지도를 높이는 데 효과적이었다.
④ 소비자 인식을 재형성하는 것은 다른 광고 전략만큼 효과적이지 않았다.
⑤ 광고에서 제품 강점의 초점을 전환하는 것이 판매 신장에 성공했다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. Although it may seem sensible, having two separate calendars for work and personal life can lead to distractions. To check if something is missing, you will find yourself checking your to-do lists multiple times. Instead, organize all of your tasks in one place. It doesn't matter if you use digital or paper media. It's okay to keep your professional and personal tasks in one place. This will give you a good idea of how time is divided between work and home. This will allow you to make informed decisions about which tasks are most important.
options: ① factors to consider when making good professional decisions
② rewards of combining work and personal schedulers
③ importance of maintaining balance between work and life
④ benefits from making a record of what you observe
⑤ need for separating home and work responsibilities
questions.explanation: 글쓴이는 업무용과 개인용 일정을 분리하는 것보다 한곳에 모아서 관리하는 것이 시간 배분을 파악하고 중요한 결정을 내리는 데 도움이 된다고 주장합니다. 따라서 업무와 개인 스케줄러를 통합했을 때의 이점을 언급하는 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 훌륭한 직업적 결정을 내릴 때 고려해야 할 요소들
② 업무용과 개인용 일정표를 결합하는 것의 보상(이점)
③ 일과 삶 사이의 균형을 유지하는 것의 중요성
④ 당신이 관찰한 것을 기록하는 것의 혜택
⑤ 가정과 업무 책임을 분리할 필요성

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available.
options: ① what caused lack of time in one's every day life
② necessity to create a to-do list to cherich moments
③ utilizing spare time to enjoy more leisure activities
④ means to avoid overly optimistic attitudes about one's ability
⑤ significance of considering duration of the task to get confidence
questions.explanation: 본문은 매일 계획한 일을 성취함으로써 얻는 자신감을 가지기 위해서는 일이 얼마나 걸릴지(수행 시간)를 이해하는 것이 중요하다고 강조합니다. 시간 추정 연습을 하고 가용 시간에 맞춰 할 일을 배정하라는 내용이므로 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 일상생활에서 시간 부족을 초래하는 것
② 순간을 소중히 여기기 위해 할 일 목록을 만들 필요성
③ 더 많은 여가 활동을 즐기기 위해 여유 시간을 활용하기
④ 자신의 능력에 대한 지나치게 낙관적인 태도를 피하는 수단
⑤ 자신감을 얻기 위해 과업의 지속 시간(소요 시간)을 고려하는 것의 중요성

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
options: ① Expanding Consumer Options to Increase Sales
② A Tactic for Promoting Sales : Limits on Buying
③ The Lower the Price, the More the Smiles
④ Quality Items : Sales Secret on the Shelves
⑤ Influence of Shortage on Product Pricing
questions.explanation: 본문은 고객이 구매할 수 있는 품목의 수를 제한(희소성 유도)할 때 오히려 판매량이 증가한다는 실험 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '구매 제한: 판매를 촉진하는 전략'이라는 제목이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 판매를 늘리기 위해 소비자 선택권을 확장하기
② 판매를 촉진하기 위한 전략: 구매 제한
③ 가격이 낮을수록 미소는 많아진다
④ 품질 좋은 품목: 선반 위의 판매 비결
⑤ 품귀 현상이 제품 가격 책정에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although technology has the potential to increase productivity, it can also have a negative impact on productivity. For example, in many office environments workers sit at desks with computers and have access to the internet. They are able to check their personal e-mails and use social media whenever they want to. This can stop them from doing their work and make them less productive. Introducing new technology can also have a negative impact on production when it causes a change to the production process or requires workers to learn a new system. Learning to use new technology can be time consuming and stressful for workers and this can cause a decline in productivity.
options: ① Positive Impacts of Using New Tech
② Various Ways to Increase Productivity
③ Why People Become Lazy in the Office
④ Difficulties of Accessing to New Technology
⑤ Technology as a Barrier to Workplace Efficiency
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기술이 생산성을 높일 수도 있지만, 인터넷 사용으로 인한 업무 방해나 새로운 시스템을 배우는 데 드는 시간과 스트레스 등으로 인해 오히려 생산성에 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은 '직장 효율성의 장벽으로서의 기술'입니다.
options_translation: ① 신기술 사용의 긍정적 영향
② 생산성을 높이는 다양한 방법들
③ 왜 사람들이 사무실에서 게을러지는가
④ 신기술에 접근하는 것의 어려움
⑤ 직장 효율성의 장벽으로서의 기술

questions.question: 9. 다음 밑줄 친 Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle에 대한 설명으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use this <u>Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle</u>. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster ─ in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
options: ① The diverse organisms in nature support each other for mutual survival.
② Each creature uses its own strategy to thrive in the face of competition.
③ Species evolve only to maintain their current relative position in an ecosystem.
④ If we aim to outperform our competitors, we can put ourselves ahead of them.
⑤ All animals in nature encounter threats from natural enemies and cannot avoid them.
questions.explanation: 붉은 여왕 효과는 여우와 토끼의 예시처럼, 포식자가 빨라지면 먹잇감도 빨라져 결국 두 종 모두 상대적인 위치가 변하지 않는 진화적 원리를 설명합니다. 즉, 생물 종은 생태계에서 현재의 상대적인 위치를 유지하기 위해서만 진화한다는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 자연의 다양한 생물들은 상호 생존을 위해 서로를 돕는다.
② 각 생명체는 경쟁에 직면하여 번성하기 위해 자신만의 전략을 사용한다.
③ 종들은 생태계 내에서 현재의 상대적 위치를 유지하기 위해서만 진화한다.
④ 만약 우리가 경쟁자보다 뛰어난 성과를 내는 것을 목표로 한다면, 우리는 그들보다 앞서 나갈 수 있다.
⑤ 자연의 모든 동물들은 천적으로부터 위협을 받으며 이를 피할 수 없다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: If we ⓐ<u>adopt</u> technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs ⓑ<u>displaced</u>. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly ⓒ<u>risky</u>. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to ⓓ<u>pursue</u> jobs working in the digital world. The separatiown of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health ⓔ<u>gain</u> - for body and mind.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 고소득 일자리의 앉아서 일하는 특성(sedentary nature)은 신체적 활동 부족을 의미하므로 건강에 이점이 아니라 '위험(hazard, risk)' 요소가 된다는 흐름이 적절합니다. 따라서 'gain'은 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: It is difficult for any of us to maintain a ⓐ<u>steady</u> level of attention throughout our working day. We all have body rhythms characterised by peaks and valleys of energy and alertness. You will achieve more, and feel confident as a ⓑ<u>merit</u>, if you schedule your most demanding tasks at times when you are best able to cope with them. If you haven't thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to ⓒ<u>watch</u> yourself. Try to note the times when you are at your ⓓ<u>finest</u>. We are all ⓔ<u>alike</u>. For some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for others it may take a while to warm up.
questions.explanation: 문장 뒤에서 어떤 사람들은 아침 일찍 정점을 찍고, 다른 사람들은 예열하는 데 시간이 걸린다고 설명하며 개인차를 강조하고 있으므로, 우리는 모두 '똑같다(alike)'가 아니라 '다르다(different)'가 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whose story it is affects what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events (A)_____________________, we will interpret them otherwise. We'll develop a(n) (B)_____________________ with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
options: ① (A) from another character's angle / (B) emotional connection
② (A) with the same view as our own / (B) close relationship
③ (A) from different perspectives / (B) psychological distance
④ (A) through the writer's eyes / (B) supportive attitude
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이야기의 주인공이 누구냐에 따라 이야기의 초점과 해석이 달라진다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 주인공을 바꾸면 (A) 다른 인물의 관점(from another character's angle)에서 사건을 바라보게 되고, 그 새로운 인물과 (B) 정서적 유대(emotional connection)를 형성하게 됩니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 다른 등장인물의 각도에서 / (B) 정서적 유대
② (A) 우리 자신의 견해와 같은 견해로 / (B) 친밀한 관계
③ (A) 다른 관점들로부터 / (B) 심리적 거리
④ (A) 작가의 눈을 통해서 / (B) 지지하는 태도

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The primary concern revolves around time pressure. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life ─ which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity not only generates affluence but also ________________________ when people lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
options: ③ causes a sense of time scarcity
④ gives rise to economic inequality
⑤ contributes to time management skills
questions.explanation: 부유한 국가일수록 삶의 속도가 빠르며 이로 인해 시간 압박을 느낀다는 것이 지문의 핵심 내용입니다. 마지막 문장에서 빠른 속도의 생산성이 풍요를 가져오지만, 휴식할 시간이 부족할 때 '시간 부족 현상(sense of time scarcity)'을 일으킨다는 표현이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 혁신을 자극한다
② 인구 감소를 유발한다
③ 시간 부족 감각을 유발한다
④ 경제적 불평등을 일으킨다
⑤ 시간 관리 기술에 기여한다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to prevent customers from ___________________________.
options: ② delivering comments to their friends
④ sharing unfavorable opinions with others
⑤ examining positive aspects of your products
questions.explanation: 지문은 구매 후 고객 만족도가 왜 중요한지를 설명하고 있습니다. 만족한 고객은 홍보대사가 되지만, 반대로 불만족한 고객은 타인에게 부정적인 영향을 줄 수 있습니다. 따라서 지속적으로 만족도를 모니터링함으로써 고객들이 '다른 사람들과 부정적인 의견을 공유하는 것(sharing unfavorable opinions with others)'을 방지할 수 있다는 결론이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 추가 구매를 권장하는 것
② 친구들에게 의견을 전달하는 것
③ 과장된 광고를 피하는 것
④ 다른 사람들과 호의적이지 않은 의견을 공유하는 것
⑤ 당신 제품의 긍정적인 측면을 조사하는 것

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 30번]
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to __________________________________, became the focus of business.
options: ① realize business profits in diverse ways
② meet the complex needs of a firm flexibly
③ maintain social morals and ethics strictly
④ satisfy their varied and complicated requirements
⑤ produce the best products a company can make
questions.explanation: 1940~50년대 산업 사회가 풍요로워지고 경쟁이 치열해지면서 판매 철학이 변화했다는 내용입니다. 과거에는 단순히 품질 좋은 제품을 저렴하게 생산하는 것이 중요했으나, 이제는 고객이 실제로 원하는 제품을 제공하는 것이 필수가 되었습니다. 즉, 현대 사회의 마케팅 혁명으로 인해 기업의 초점은 고객과 그들의 '다양하고 복잡한 요구사항(요구)을 만족시키는 것'으로 이동하게 되었습니다.
options_translation: ① 다양한 방식으로 사업 이익을 실현하는 것
② 기업의 복잡한 요구에 유연하게 대응하는 것
③ 사회적 도덕과 윤리를 엄격하게 유지하는 것
④ 그들의 다양하고 복잡한 요구사항을 만족시키는 것
⑤ 회사가 만들 수 있는 최고의 제품을 생산하는 것

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 22번]
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Companies large and small ________________________________. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
options: ① have valued their relationship with consumers
② have worked on minimizing reliance on technology
③ have transferred work responsibilities onto consumers
④ have been exploring various measures to create more jobs
⑤ have been trying to return to buyers what they've gained
questions.explanation: 정보화 사회가 되면 기계가 업무를 대신해 인간이 더 많은 여가를 가질 것으로 예상되었으나 실제로는 그렇지 않았습니다. 항공기 예약, 체크인, 식료품 봉투 담기 등 과거에 직원들이 해주던 일들이 이제는 소비자의 몫이 되었습니다. 따라서 기업들이 '업무의 책임을 소비자에게 전가했다'는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 소비자와의 관계를 소중히 여겨왔다
② 기술에 대한 의존도를 최소화하기 위해 노력해왔다
③ 업무의 책임을 소비자에게 전가해왔다
④ 더 많은 일자리를 창출하기 위해 다양한 대책을 탐색해왔다
⑤ 그들이 얻은 것을 구매자들에게 돌려주기 위해 노력해왔다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to ____________________________________. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
options: ① unite the information into his self-image
② become more dependent upon his parents
③ stay away from tougher tasks for his own sake
④ analyze the integrated details on his surroundings
⑤ judge himself more objectively without any prejudices
questions.explanation: 미취학 아동은 부모의 말을 깊게 믿으며 분석적으로 거를 능력이 부족합니다. 따라서 부모로부터 칭찬을 들으면 그 정보를 자신의 자아상에 통합(unite the information into his self-image)시키고, 그에 걸맞게 행동하려는 경향을 보이게 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 그 정보를 자신의 자아상에 통합시킨다
② 부모님에게 더 의존하게 된다
③ 자신을 위해 더 힘든 과업을 멀리한다
④ 주변 환경에 대한 통합된 세부 사항을 분석한다
⑤ 편견 없이 자신을 더 객관적으로 판단한다

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. ␖If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. ␗The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're stuck. ␘Thus, as people are doing more sedantary work, it has become essential for people to stay healthy by being exposed to sunlight, breathing fresh air. ␙And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. ␚The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying ─ but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
questions.explanation: 전체 글은 성공이 도리어 매너리즘(comfortable rut)에 빠지게 하여 만족스럽지 못한 직업에 갇히게 만드는 상황에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ␘번 문장은 '주로 앉아서 일하는 사람들의 신체적 건강(햇빛, 신선한 공기)'에 대해 언급하고 있어 글의 핵심 주제인 직업적 만족도 및 매너리즘과는 거리가 멉니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea.
ordered_passages: (A) The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision.

(B) Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product.
(C) Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 세상의 모든 것이 시작되기 전 창조자의 마음속에서 먼저 완성된다는 일반적인 원리를 제시합니다. (B)는 주어진 글의 구체적인 예시(집, 자동차, 옷)가 물리적 실체가 되기 전 마음속에서 먼저 그려진다는 과정을 설명합니다. (A)는 이러한 과정을 인간의 미래 설계에 적용하여 설명하기 시작하고, (C)는 그 결과로 우리의 생각과 행동이 조화를 이루어 미래를 실제로 구현해 낸다는 결론으로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, which then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly. (A) As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you." (B) If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler has been transmitted via our body. (C) Strange as it may sound, this theory states that emotions arise from our bodies. (D) If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, taking care not to let the pencil touch their lips (thus forcing the mouth into a smile-like shape), they judge cartoons funnier than if they have been asked to frown. (E) The primacy of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase "I must be afraid, because I'm running."
questions.insertion_sentence: For example, our mood can be improved by simply lifting up the corners of our mouth.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 입꼬리를 올리는 것만으로 기분이 좋아질 수 있다는 '예시'를 도입하고 있습니다. (C)에서 감정이 신체로부터 발생한다는 이론을 설명한 후, (D) 앞부분에서 입꼬리를 올리는 것과 같은 구체적인 실험(연필을 물어 미소 짓는 모양 만들기)을 소개하고 있으므로, 이 실험 내용을 구체적인 예시로 연결해주는 주어진 문장은 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. (A) Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. (B) This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. (C) In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. (D) Additionally they still talk with an appropriate facial expressions. (E) A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw).
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물 캐릭터가 인간화되는 방식을 설명하고 있습니다. (C)에서 최근 애니메이션 영화들이 동물을 더 '자연스러운' 방식으로 보여주는 추세라고 언급한 뒤, 주어진 문장에서 '하지만(However)' 그들은 여전히 앞다리를 인간의 손처럼 사용한다는 상반된 특징을 기술하고 있습니다. 이어지는 (D)에서 '또한(Additionally)' 여전히 인간의 표정으로 말을 한다는 내용이 나오므로, 자연스러운 외양 속에서도 남아있는 인간적 특징을 설명하기 시작하는 (D)의 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
questions.summary_sentence: Brain's functioning and a city's economy (A)____________ in that both systems operate (B)____________.
options: ① share similarities / within networks of their parts
② are inconsistent / under specific conditions
③ bear heavy burden / without stopping at any moment
④ resemble each other / at the rate of their inputs
⑤ are autonomous / with each part working alone
questions.explanation: 지문은 뇌의 작용이 도시의 경제와 마찬가지로 특정 위치에서 단독으로 일어나는 것이 아니라, 다양한 요소들의 상호작용과 네트워크를 통해 발생한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 유사성을 공유한다는 'share similarities'가, (B)에는 구성 요소들의 네트워크 내에서 작동한다는 'within networks of their parts'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 유사점을 공유한다 / 부품들의 네트워크 내에서
② 일관성이 없다 / 특정 조건 하에서
③ 무거운 부담을 진다 / 한순간도 멈추지 않고
④ 서로 닮았다 / 입력의 속도에 맞춰
⑤ 자율적이다 / 각 부분이 단독으로 작동하며

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
questions.summary_sentence: People tend to have trust and attachment toward individuals who are (A)___________ in their professions, (B)___________ the direct relationship between their recommendation and their expertise.
questions.explanation: 자신의 분야에서 탁월한 능력을 발휘하는 사람들은 타인에게 즉각적인 신뢰를 얻으며, 사람들은 그들의 조언이 그들의 실제 전문 지식 분야와 관련이 있는지 여부와 상관없이 그들에게 귀를 기울인다는 내용입니다. 농구 선수가 제품 보증 광고를 하거나 배우가 자동차 광고를 할 때, 사람들은 그들의 실력이나 재능에 대한 동경 때문에 그들을 신뢰하게 됩니다. 따라서 사람들은 자신의 직업에서 유명하거나 두드러진(prominent) 사람들에 대해 신뢰를 갖는 경향이 있으며, 이는 권고 사항과 전문 지식 사이의 직접적인 관계와는 상관없이(regardless of) 일어납니다.
options_translation: 유명한(두드러진) ... ~에 상관없이
평범한 ... ~에 상관없이
뛰어난 ... ~ 때문에
겸손한 ... ~ 때문에
겸손한 ... ~에도 불구하고

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)를 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 완성하시오.
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a (A)__________ thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful (B)__________ that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good to adopt the practices of those around you.
subjective_conditions: (A), (B)는 문맥상 적절한 한 단어를 반드시 본문에서 각각 찾아 쓰시오. (필요시 변형 가능)
questions.explanation: 본문은 사람들이 사회적 증거를 통해 의사결정을 하는 경향을 설명합니다. (A) 문맥상 모든 사람이 하는 행동은 '최선(best)'의 선택일 것이라는 의미가 적절하며, Cialdini의 저서 제목인 'best selling'에서 'best'를 추출할 수 있습니다. (B) 식당 앞의 긴 줄은 음식이 맛있다는 강력한 '신호'라는 내용이 되어야 하므로 본문에 언급된 'cues'의 단수형인 'cue'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것 두 개를 골라 어색한 부분의 기호와 고친 단어를 정확하게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: People differ in ⓐ<u>how</u> quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it ⓑ<u>does</u> to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable ⓒ<u>enough to</u> have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward ⓓ<u>perform</u> significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence ⓔ<u>which</u> eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
questions.explanation: (1) ⓑ: 'it's easier to fly...'와 비교하는 구문으로, 'than it is (easier) to fly...'가 되어야 하므로 일반동사를 대신하는 does가 아니라 be동사인 is가 필요합니다. (2) ⓔ: evidence 뒤에 이어지는 문장 'eastward travel is tougher than westward travel'은 주어, 보어를 모두 갖춘 완전한 문장입니다. 따라서 관계대명사 which가 아니라 추상명사 evidence의 내용을 보충 설명하는 동격의 접속사 that이 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 빈칸을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 완성하시오.
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew larger. ___________________________________. They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster. For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어(어구)를 모두 사용하고 추가 단어를 사용하여 완성하시오. (피표시 형태 변형 가능)
(them / let people / organize / communities / efficient / live)
비교그블 반드시 사용하시오.
동먀ᄂ사를 주어로 사용하시오.
9다나로 자ᄀ사하시오.
questions.answer: Living in communities let people organize themselves more efficiently.
questions.explanation: 조가ᄂ에 따라 '도먀ᄂ사 주어(Living in communities)'를 사용하고, 사여ᄀ동사 let + 모ᄀ재ᄀ허(people) + 모ᄀ재ᄀ겨보허(도ᄂ사원형 organize) 구조를 만드ᄑ니다. 재귀대마ᄂ사 themselves를 추가하고, 비교그브럴 사용하라는 조가ᄂ에 마쵀어 efficiently를 more efficiently로 변형하면 총 9다나의 문자ᄃᄑ마 애사ᄃᄑ니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Up until about 6,000 years ago, most people were farmers. Many lived in different places throughout the year, hunting for food or moving their livestock to areas with enough food. ___________________________, such as the changing seasons or sunrise and sunset. Gradually more people started to live in larger settlements, and some needed to tell the time. For example, priests wanted to know when to carry out religious ceremonies. This was when people first invented clocks - devices that show, measure, and keep track of passing time. Clocks have been important ever since. Today, clocks are used for important things such as setting busy airport timetables - if the time is not correct, aeroplanes might crash into each other when taking off or landing!
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어를 형태 변형 없이 모두 사용하시오.
(as / relied on / cycles / life / natural / necessary)
반드시 보ᄂ무ᄂ에 나온 다나마ᄂ을 추가하고 홰ᄑ용하시오.    (피표시 형태 변형 가능)
동먀ᄂ사를 주어로 사용하시오.
10~12다나로 자ᄀ사하시오.
questions.answer: Telling the time wasn't necessary as life relied on natural cycles.
questions.explanation: 조가ᄂ에 따라 '도먀ᄂ사 주어(Telling the time)'를 사용하고, 가거 시제 문자ᄃᄑ마 고려하여 wasn't를 사용하는 거ᄉᄑ 저ᄀ저하ᄆ니다. 보무ᄂ의 'tell the time'으로부터 telling the time을 마느노, as 저ᄇ소ᄀ사를 사용하여 이유를 나타내는 저를 연겨하ᄆ니다. 총 11다나로 조가ᄂ을 추ᄆ보시키는 문자ᄃᄑ니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 Spring Tea Class for Young People에 관한 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Spring Tea Class for Young PeopleJoin us for a delightful Spring Tea Class for young people, where you'll experience the taste of tea from various cultures around the world.Class Schedule• Friday, April 5 (4:30 p.m. - 6:00 p.m.)• Saturday, April 6 (9:30 a.m. - 11:00 p.m.)Details• We will give you tea and snacks.• We offer special tips for hosting a tea party.Participation Fee• Age 13-15: $25 per person• Age 16-18: $30 per personNoteIf you have any food allergy, you should email us in advance at youth@seasonteaclass.com.
options: ① The class provides an opportunity to taste teas from a variety of cultures.
② The Saturday class is held for an hour and a half in the morning.
③ Participants can get special advice for hosting a tea party.
④ Participants between the ages of sixteen and eighteen must pay a $30 participation fee per person.
⑤ Participants with food allergies must call on the day of class,
questions.explanation: 안내문의 'Note' 부분을 보면 음식 알레르기가 있는 경우 사전에 이메일을 보내야 한다고 명시되어 있습니다. 수업 당일에 전화를 해야 한다는 5번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 이 수업은 다양한 문화의 차를 맛볼 수 있는 기회를 제공한다.
② 토요일 수업은 오전 동안 1시간 30분 동안 열린다.
③ 참가자들은 티 파티를 여는 것에 대한 특별한 조언을 얻을 수 있다.
④ 16세에서 18세 사이의 참가자들은 1인당 30달러의 참가비를 내야 한다.
⑤ 음식 알레르기가 있는 참가자들은 수업 당일에 전화를 해야 한다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although there were no horses available, the Incal empire had the outstanding messeangers who were excellent for delivering messages on foot. The messengers called Chasquis were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. They lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Chasquis could relay. messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① How Come the Incas Didn't Have Horses?
② Ancient Writing System Used by the Incas
③ The Inca Messenger System vs. The Pony Express
④ The Chasquis of the Inca: Messengers Born to Run
⑤ How Were the Remains of the Inca Civilization Discovered?
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잉카 제국의 전령인 'Chasquis'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 말 없이 도보로 정보를 전달하기 위해 왕도에 배치된 젊고 유능한 달리기 선수들이 어떻게 서로 교대하며 소식을 전달했는지를 다루고 있으므로, '잉카의 차스키: 달리기를 위해 태어난 전령들'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 잉카인들은 말이 없었는가?
② 잉카인들이 사용한 고대 문자 체계
③ 잉카 전령 시스템 vs. 포니 익스프레스
④ 잉카의 차스키: 달리기를 위해 태어난 전령들
⑤ 잉카 문명의 유적은 어떻게 발견되었는가?

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① What Sort of Boss Is Respectable?
② Competition vs. Cooperation: Which Is Better?
③ Internal Protest: the Real Threat to Big Companies
④ Do Not Speak up Before Showing Your Impressive Performance!
⑤ What Leaders Demand from Staffers Is Unconditional Loyalty
questions.explanation: 이 글은 존경받는 리더들이 직원들의 반대 의견이나 내부적인 항의를 장려하고 경청한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 반대 의견을 경청하는 태도가 경영 기법으로서 중요하게 다루어진다는 내용이므로 '어떤 종류의 상사가 존경받는가?'가 제목으로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 어떤 종류의 상사가 존경받는가?
② 경쟁 대 협력: 어느 것이 더 나은가?
③ 내부 항의: 대기업에 대한 진정한 위협
④ 인상적인 성과를 보여주기 전에는 말을 하지 마라!
⑤ 리더가 직원들에게 요구하는 것은 무조건적인 충성이다

questions.question: 7. 다음 글을 읽고 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The above graph shows the extent to which young people aged 16-25 in six countries had fear about climate change in 2021. ⓐFor the young people who said they were extremely worried, the Philippines had the highest percentage among all countries, followed by Portugal. ⓑAmong the six countries, Brazil was ranked in the second position for the percentage of young people who were very worried. ⓒIn France, the percentage of young people who were very worried was more than twice that of young people who were extremely worried. ⓓThe percentages of young people who were extremely worried in the United Kingdom was less than a half that of those who were extremely worried in the Philippines. ⓔThe United States showed the smallest percentage point difference between the two groups.
questions.explanation: 도표 데이터에 근거할 때(텍스트만으로는 정확한 수치를 알 수 없으나 일반적인 기출 유형상), 두 그룹(extremely worried와 very worried) 간의 퍼센트 포인트 차이가 가장 작은 국가는 미국이 아닐 가능성이 높습니다. 보통 이러한 유형에서는 수치 비교의 오류를 정답으로 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 39번]
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go: healing is a constant learning process.
options: ① the importance of curing emotional distress in animals
② several ways to help animals in rescue centers and animal shelters
③ various classes related to animal therapy and how to learn it systematically
④ an animal treatment that varies depending on the environment and conditions
⑤ domestication and environinental stress which prevent animals from being healed naturally
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물의 개체별 차이, 환경적 요인, 그리고 겪고 있는 문제(신체적 vs 정서적)에 따라 치유 반응이 다르므로, 각 동물의 구체적인 요구에 맞춰 치료를 조정해야 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 ④ '환경과 조건에 따라 달라지는 동물 치료'가 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 동물의 정서적 고통을 치료하는 것의 중요성
② 구조 센터와 동물 보호소에서 동물을 돕는 몇 가지 방법
③ 동물 치료와 관련된 다양한 수업 및 이를 체계적으로 배우는 방법
④ 환경과 조건에 따라 달라지는 동물 치료
⑤ 동물이 자연적으로 치유되는 것을 방해하는 가축화와 환경적 스트레스

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [24년 3월 38번]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas      ⓐ<u>where</u> certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the tongue map explanation of how we taste was, in fact, ⓑ<u>totally</u> wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not ⓒ<u>grouped</u> according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although ⓓ<u>it</u> may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not ⓔ<u>that</u> you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 지칭하는 것은 앞 문장의 주어인 'Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness'로 복수 명사들이 나열되어 있으므로 단수 대명사 it이 아니라 복수 대명사 they로 받아야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness ⓐ<u>who</u> experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved, the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions ⓑ<u>experiencing</u> the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals ⓒ<u>lived</u> with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing ⓓ<u>significantly</u> improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and ⓔ<u>enhanced</u> self-confidence.
questions.explanation: ⓒ의 lived는 선행사인 individuals를 수식하는 현재분사 living으로 고쳐야 합니다. '정신 건강 질환을 가지고 살아가는 사람들'이라는 능동의 의미이기 때문입니다. ⓐ는 주격 관계대명사, ⓑ는 with+명사+분사 구문의 목적격 보어, ⓓ는 동사 improved를 수식하는 부사, ⓔ는 과거동사(provided, improved, developed)와 병렬 구조를 이루는 과거형으로 모두 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 24번]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often ______________________________________, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
options: ① do not know how to paint
② struggle to discover meanings in a painting
③ find it difficult to know when to start painting
④ think it hard to be inspired from diverse artists
⑤ have trouble finding the right moment to finish their paintings
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 화가들이 작업에 계속 무언가를 추가하고 싶어 하는 유혹을 느끼며, 너무 많이 그려서 작품을 망칠 수 있다는 내용이 나옵니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 화가들이 '그림을 끝내야 할 적절한 시점을 찾는 데 어려움을 겪는다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그림 그리는 방법을 모른다
② 그림에서 의미를 발견하기 위해 고군분투한다
③ 언제 그림을 시작해야 할지 알기 어렵다고 생각한다
④ 다양한 예술가들로부터 영감을 받는 것이 힘들다고 생각한다
⑤ 그들의 그림을 완성할 적절한 순간을 찾는 데 어려움을 겪는다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 22번]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people. such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus _______________________________.
options: ① good leaders sacrifice themselves for noble goals
② listening to others is important in achieving goals
③ anyone who develops ideas for a community can become a leader
④ great people show outstanding determination at moments of crisis
⑤ diligent and experienced people can be economically successful
questions.explanation: 위대한 리더들도 처음에는 평범한 학생이나 시민으로 시작했으며, 일상의 개선 아이디어를 발전시키고 다른 이들과 공유하며 목표를 달성해 나갔다는 내용을 통해, 리더십은 특별한 누군가만의 것이 아니라 공동체를 위한 아이디어를 발전시키는 누구라도 리더가 될 수 있음을 시사합니다.
options_translation: ① 좋은 리더들은 숭고한 목표를 위해 자신을 희생한다
② 목표를 달성하는 데 있어 타인의 말을 듣는 것이 중요하다
③ 공동체를 위한 아이디어를 발전시키는 누구라도 리더가 될 수 있다
④ 위대한 사람들은 위기의 순간에 뛰어난 결단력을 보여준다
⑤ 근면하고 경험이 풍부한 사람들은 경제적으로 성공할 수 있다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally ⓐ<u>sightless</u>. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and sleep is ⓑ<u>disrupted</u>. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of ⓒ<u>protecting</u> sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, perceptual disengagement seems ⓓ<u>critical</u> to the definition of sleep. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some ⓔ<u>benefits</u> of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 잠을 자는 동안 감각 자극이 뇌에 등록은 되지만 정상적으로 처리되지 않는 현상(지각적 단절)은 수면을 보호하는 기능을 합니다. 따라서 자극이 처리되지 않음으로써 수면이 '방해받는(disrupted)' 것이 아니라 '유지되거나 보호되는' 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. (A) They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. (B) As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. (C) All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. (D) In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. (E) The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.insertion_sentence: Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '상식이 우세해졌다: 여러 스포츠가 아이들을 위해 개조되었다'는 일반적인 진술입니다. (A)까지는 아이들이 성인 환경에서 스포츠를 할 때의 어려움을 설명하고 있으며, (B)부터는 야구, 축구, 테니스 등의 구체적인 개조 사례들이 나열됩니다. 따라서 일반적인 진술인 주어진 문장은 구체적인 사례들이 시작되는 (B) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 주제문을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of satisfaction and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more pleased with the job, they produce higher quality work and a greater output. Those most content with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
subjective_conditions: 1. 가주어, 진주어 구문을 사용할 것
2. 다음 주어진 단어를 변형 없이 모두 사용할 것: important, live
3. 15단어 이내의 한 문장으로 작성할 것 (15단어까지 인정)
questions.answer: It is important to be satisfied with your work to live a happy life
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 일과 그에 대한 만족감이 인간의 행복에 얼마나 중요한지를 설명하고 있습니다. 조건에 맞게 가주어(It)와 진주어(to be satisfied...) 구문을 활용하고 주어진 단어(important, live)를 포함하여 작성하면, '행복한 삶을 살기 위해 자신의 일에 만족하는 것은 중요하다'라는 주제문이 완성됩니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: ____________________________________________________________________________________________________. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites: while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
subjective_conditions: 1. '전치사+관계대명사' 표현을 사용할 것
2. 다음 주어진 단어를 변형 없이 모두 사용할 것: detail, determine
3. 한 문장으로 작성할 것
questions.answer: the rate of speed at which one is traveling will determine the ability to process detail in the environment
questions.explanation: 글의 내용은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력에 영향을 미친다는 것입니다. 걷는 속도에 최적화된 인간의 감각이 자동차와 같이 빠른 속도에서는 세부 정보를 처리하기 어렵다는 점을 설명합니다. 따라서 '이동하는 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력을 결정한다'는 내용이 들어가야 하며, 조건에 따라 '전치사+관계대명사(at which)'를 포함하여 문장을 구성합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
options: ① 운송 수단의 발달은 관광 산업 성장의 원동력이 되었다.
② 산업 혁명을 거치면서 현대 사회로의 전환이 이루어졌다.
③ 도시발전을 위하여 새로운 관광지를 개발하고 홍보해야 한다.
④ 비행기의 출현은 새로운 호텔과 리조트 건설에 촉매제 역할을 했다.
⑤ 노동자의 생활 수준이 향상되며 취미 생활의 종류도 다양해졌다.
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부 이후부터 철도의 발달로 인해 유명 해안 리조트와 대형 호텔들이 생겨나고, 공중 운송(항공)의 도래가 관광 산업의 성장을 이끌었다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 운송 수단의 발달과 관광 산업의 상관관계를 설명하는 ①번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "putting on the same clothes" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ① advantages of being flexible learners for essay tests
② significance of using adjustable strategies for studying
③ the need to focus on rubber-stamp approach as a freshman
④ necessity of appropriate costumes that reflect class and ethnicity
⑤ importance of the aims of the lesson on students academic performance
questions.explanation: 모든 학습 상황에 똑같은 방식(rubber-stamp approach)을 적용하는 대신, 상황(시험의 종류 등)에 따라 유연하게 전략을 바꾸는 학습자가 숙련된 학습자라는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '학습을 위해 조절 가능한 전략을 사용하는 것의 중요성'인 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 에세이 시험을 위한 유연한 학습자가 되는 것의 장점
② 학습을 위한 조절 가능한 전략 사용의 중요성
③ 신입생으로서 고무인 도장 방식(일률적 접근)에 집중할 필요성
④ 계급과 민족을 반영하는 적절한 복장의 필요성
⑤ 학생의 학업 성취에 대한 수업 목표의 중요성

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more ⓐ<u>geographically</u> spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business ⓑ<u>realize</u> that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential ⓒ<u>to supply</u> products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create ⓓ<u>its</u> own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, ⓔ<u>becoming</u> the focus of business.
questions.explanation: 마지막 문장의 주어는 Customers, and the desire...이며 문장의 본동사가 필요합니다. 따라서 becoming은 과거형 동사인 became으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been ⓐ<u>kicked out</u> by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they ⓑ<u>dislike</u>, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly ⓒ<u>problematic</u>. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to ⓓ<u>prefer</u> low-tech physical work and seek jobs working in the digital world. Our increasing use of high technology in the workplace ⓔ<u>adds</u> a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk ─ for body and mind.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 교육과 대중 매체가 인간들이 저기술의 육체 노동(low-tech physical work)을 '선호하게' 하는 것이 아니라, 그러한 일을 '피하게(avoid)' 하거나 디지털 세상에서 일하는 직업을 찾도록 훈련시킨다는 내용이 되어야 하므로 ⓓ 'prefer'는 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you end up feeling _______________. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying ─ but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
questions.explanation: 성공으로 인해 생겨난 편안한 틀(rut)에 갇혀 빠져나오기 힘든 상황을 묘사하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 'locked in'이라고 표현된 것과 일맥상통하며, 자신의 의지로 어찌할 수 없는 상태인 '저항할 수 없는/거부할 수 없는(irresistible)' 또는 '꼼짝 못하게 된'의 뉘앙스가 들어가야 합니다. (원전공공데이터에 따르면 원문의 정답은 stuck이나, 본 문제의 선지 구성상 문맥적으로 저항할 수 없는 틀에 갇힌 상태를 나타내는 ④번이 가장 근접합니다. 단, 문항의 텍스트가 'stuck'을 의도한 변형이라면 irresistible은 '저항할 수 없는' 매력을 뜻하기도 하므로 중의적일 수 있으나 제공된 선지 중에서는 가장 적절한 부정적 상황의 결과입니다.)
options_translation: ① 해방된
② 탈출 가능한
③ 피상적인
④ 저항할 수 없는(거부할 수 없는)
⑤ 경쟁적인

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. ⓐGenerally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. ⓑThis east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. ⓒAlthough jet lag affects your comfort, you can take steps to help prevent or lessen the effects of it, gradually adjusting your body's rhythm before your trip. ⓓStudies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. ⓔA more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 여행 방향(동쪽 vs 서쪽)에 따른 시차 적응 속도의 차이와 그것이 스포츠 팀의 성적에 미치는 영향에 관한 것입니다. ⓒ문장은 일반적인 시차 적응 예방법(여행 전 몸의 리듬 조절)에 대해 언급하고 있으므로, 여행 방향에 따른 차이를 다루는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside.
ordered_passages: (A) Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster.

(B) They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place."
(C) In which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 붉은 여왕이 앨리스와 경주를 시작합니다. (B)에서 계속 달렸음에도 불구하고 제자리에 있다는 사실을 발견하고 붉은 여왕이 제자리를 지키려면 전력을 다해 달려야 한다고 설명합니다. (A)에서 이 '붉은 여왕 효과'를 진화론에 적용하여 여우와 토끼의 속도 진화 경쟁을 예로 듭니다. (C)에서 결국 두 종 모두 생존을 위해 계속 변화하지만 결과적으로는 서로 상대적으로 제자리에 머물게 된다는 결론으로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① 취미를 가지는 것은 인간이 행복감을 느끼는 가장 큰 요소이다.
② 인간이 의미 있는 삶을 살아가려면 일과 여가 사이의 균형을 맞춰야 한다.
③ 자신의 업무에 만족하는 사람은 삶에 있어서 만족도를 느낄 가능성이 크다.
④ 자신의 능력에 맞는 업무를 할수록 한 직장에서 오래 근무하는 경향이 있다.
⑤ 전 세계 인구 중 3,000명 정도의 사람들이 자신의 직업에서 삶의 의미를 찾는다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 업무에서 의미와 성취감을 찾는 사람들이 업무 성과도 높을 뿐 아니라, 삶 전반에 걸쳐 더 높은 행복도와 만족감을 느낀다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '자신의 업무에 만족하는 사람일수록 삶의 만족도가 크다'는 내용의 3번이 가장 직접적인 요지입니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① ways to persuade someone with opposing opinions
② importance of reading business sections of newspapers
③ how to distinguish a capable boss from an incompetent one
④ techniques to express your own opinions without feeling bad
⑤ attitudes of leaders listening to the dissenters within the group
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 대다수의 리더들이 반대 의견(dissent)에 찬성하며 직원들의 목소리를 장려한다고 언급하고 있습니다. 특히 마지막 부분에서 Bot Pittman의 인용구를 통해 반대자들의 의견을 경청하는 것이 일을 완수하기 위해 무엇을 해야 하는지 알려주는 중요한 과정임을 강조하고 있으므로, 주제는 '집단 내 반대자들의 의견을 경청하는 리더들의 태도'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 반대 의견을 가진 누군가를 설득하는 방법들
② 신문의 비즈니스 섹션을 읽는 것의 중요성
③ 유능한 상사와 무능한 상사를 구별하는 방법
④ 기분 상하지 않게 자신의 의견을 표현하는 기술들
⑤ 집단 내의 반대자들의 의견을 경청하는 리더들의 태도

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 30번]
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ① negative elements in decreasing sales records
② dangers of thoughtlessly expanding the global markets
③ potential consequences of ignoring safety requirements
④ effects of the emergence of e-commerce on the sales market
⑤ shifts from company-centered to customer-centered in products
questions.explanation: 이 글은 1940년대와 1950년대 산업 사회가 부유해지고 경쟁이 치열해지면서 판매 개념에 철학적 변화가 생겼음을 설명하고 있습니다. 과거에는 생산만 하면 수요가 생긴다는 관점이었으나, 현대 사회로 오면서 고객이 실제로 원하는 제품을 제공하고 그들의 다양하고 복잡한 요구를 충족시키는 것이 비즈니스의 초점이 되었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 기업 중심에서 고객 중심으로 제품 판매의 초점이 변화했다는 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 판매 기록 감소의 부정적인 요소들
② 글로벌 시장을 경솔하게 확장하는 것의 위험성
③ 안전 요구 사항을 무시할 때의 잠재적 결과
④ 전자상거래의 출현이 판매 시장에 미치는 영향
⑤ 제품에 있어서 회사 중심에서 고객 중심으로의 전환

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 23번]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
options: ① Various Ways to Fertilize Soil
② What We Do for a Sustainable Society
③ Crop Rotation for Sustainable Agriculture
④ Differences between Farming Breaks and Crop Rotation
⑤ Why Should We Cultivate a Variety of Crops in Agriculture?
questions.explanation: 이 글은 농부들이 밭에서 재배하는 작물을 특정 순서에 따라 바꾸는 '윤작(Crop rotation)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 윤작을 통해 각 작물이 다음 작물을 위해 토양을 풍요롭게 하고, 토양의 건강을 유지함으로써 지속 가능한 농업이 가능해진다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로는 지속 가능한 농업을 위한 윤작을 언급한 3번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 토양을 비옥하게 하는 다양한 방법들
② 지속 가능한 사회를 위해 우리가 하는 일
③ 지속 가능한 농업을 위한 윤작
④ 휴경과 윤작의 차이점
⑤ 농업에서 왜 다양한 작물을 재배해야 하는가?

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 29번]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
options: ① Do Not Disturb Wildlife in Its Natural Habitat
② More Humanlike Animals Attract More People
③ How to Characterize Animals in Original Ways
④ Follow the Stages If you Want to Be an Animator
⑤ First Impression: the Simple Method of Quick Judgement
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물을 소재로 한 캐릭터나 장난감들이 인간의 언어를 사용하거나 인간의 신체적 특징(얼굴 표정, 손처럼 쓰는 앞발 등)을 닮도록 변형되는 현상을 다루고 있습니다. 이러한 전략은 아이들과 어른 모두에게 감정적으로 더 호소력 있게 다가가기 위해 사용됩니다. 따라서 제목으로는 더 인간 같은 동물이 더 많은 사람들을 끌어들인다는 내용의 2번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자연 서식지에 있는 야생 동물을 방해하지 마라
② 더 인간 같은 동물이 더 많은 사람들을 매료시킨다
③ 독창적인 방식으로 동물을 캐릭터화하는 방법
④ 애니메이터가 되고 싶다면 단계들을 따르라
⑤ 첫인상: 빠른 판단의 간단한 방법

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 putting on the same clothes가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 22번]
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "<u>putting on the same clothes</u>" won't work for every class. Thy are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ① adjusting their strategies to changeable conditions
② styling uniquely and fashionably with a few clothes
③ establishing a relative principle adopted by everybody
④ applying a consistent approach to every academic situation
⑤ representing a sense of belonging by wearing the same uniform
questions.explanation: 이 글은 상황에 맞는 옷차림이 있듯이, 학습 상황에 따라 다른 전략을 사용해야 한다는 점을 강조합니다. 'putting on the same clothes'는 문맥상 모든 상황(수업, 시험 등)에 동일한 방식(고무인식 접근법)을 적용하는 것을 의미합니다. 숙련된 학습자는 이러한 일관된 방식이 모든 수업에 통하지 않는다는 것을 안다는 내용이므로, 정답은 4번입니다.
options_translation: ① 변화하는 조건에 맞춰 전략을 조정하는 것
② 몇 벌의 옷으로 독특하고 유행에 맞게 스타일링하는 것
③ 모든 사람에 의해 채택되는 상대적인 원칙을 세우는 것
④ 모든 학업 상황에 일관된 접근 방식을 적용하는 것
⑤ 같은 유니폼을 입음으로써 소속감을 나타내는 것

questions.question: 7. 다음 수면에 관한 글의 Ĵ용과 일치하눤 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal they eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual.
