Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
options: ① 잠을 자고 있는 동물이나 사람의 가장 큰 특징 설 하나는 그들이 환경의 자극에 정상적으로 반응한다는 점이다.
② 수면 중 어떤 시각적 정밴는 명백히 눈으로 들어오지만 그것은 잘아지거나 약화된다.
③ 잠을 자때 자극은 등록되지 않으며 정Ĵ적으로 찘리되지도 않아서 개인을 깨울 수 없다.
④ 지각 이탈 없이 수면이 가능하기에 지각 이탈은 수면의 정의에 필수적인 요소가 아눐다.
⑤ 많은 동물은 완전한 지각 이탈을 통해 수면의 이득을 얻기를 원한다.
questions.explanation: 글의 세 번째 문장 "Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened"에서 시각 정밴가 일부 들어오지만 약화된다고 하였으므로 ②번이 일치한다. ①은 반응하지 않는다고 했으므로 퉄리고, ③는 자극이 등록은 된다(등록되지 않는것이 아님)고 했으므로 퉄린다. ④은 지각 이탈 없이는 수면이 불가능하고 필수적이라고 했으므로 퉄린다. ⑤는 완전한 지각 이탈 없이 졸음 상태를 통해 이득을 얻는다고 했으므로 퉄린다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Marilyn and her three-year-old daughter, Sarah, took a trip to the beach, ⓐ<u>where</u> Sarah built her first sandcastle. Moments later, an enormous wave ⓑ<u>to destroy</u> Sarah's castle. In response to the loss of her sandcastle, tears streamed down Sarah's cheeks and her heart was ⓒ<u>broken</u>. She ran to Marilyn, ⓓ<u>saying</u> she would never build a sandcastle again. Marilyn said, "Part of the joy of building a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give it as a gift to the ocean." Sarah loved this idea and responded with enthusiasm to the idea of building another castle - this time, ⓔ<u>a lot</u> closer to the water so the ocean would get its gift sooner!
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 'an enormous wave'는 주어이며, 뒤에 문장을 완결할 본동사가 필요합니다. 따라서 준동사인 'to destroy'를 과거형 동사 'destroyed'로 고쳐야 문법적으로 옳습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 어법상 옳은 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: A number of research studies ⓐ<u>has shown</u> how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found ⓑ<u>that</u> people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how ⓒ<u>hardly</u> a task is for the beginner, an effect referring to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began ⓓ<u>to underestimate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated ⓔ<u>how long had it taken</u> themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. ⓕ<u>Know</u> that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 어법상 옳은 것은 ⓑ와 ⓓ 두 개입니다.ⓐ has shown -> have shown (주어 'A number of research studies'는 복수 취급)ⓑ that (접속사로 쓰여 found의 목적어 절을 이끔) - 옳음ⓒ hardly -> hard (형용사 보어 자리로, 'hardly'는 '거의 ~않다'라는 의미의 부사임)ⓓ to underestimate (begin의 목적어로 사용된 부정사) - 옳음ⓔ how long had it taken -> how long it had taken (간접의문문의 어순은 의문사+주어+동사)ⓕ Know -> Knowing (문장 전체의 주절에 연결되는 분사구문 자리임)

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements ― what degree of heat or cold it can ① <u>endure</u>, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to ② <u>follow</u>. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear ③ <u>mobile</u>, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life ― as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must ④ <u>get</u> from the place it is born ― often ⑤ <u>occupied</u> by its parent ― to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: 기후가 변화할 때 모든 생물은 생존을 위해 이동해야 합니다. 겉으로 보기에는 움직이지 못하는(immobile) 것처럼 보이는 나무나 따개비와 같은 생물들도 씨앗(seed)이나 유충(larva) 단계에서는 이동과 분산이 가능합니다. 문맥상 ③번 자리는 '움직이지 못하는'이라는 의미의 'immobile'이 자연스러우므로, '움직일 수 있는'을 의미하는 'mobile'은 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 견디다
② 따르다
③ 움직일 수 있는
④ 도달하다
⑤ 점유된

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here′s the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just _________. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day. Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① accept the situation as they are
② pray for a miracle like Cinderella
③ try to deal with the problems all at once
④ change the challenge statement into positive statements
⑤ make a specific time-unit plan to solve them one by one
questions.explanation: 필자는 실생활에서 긍정적인 변화(마법)를 일으키는 방법으로, 자신이 직면한 과제나 어려움들을 적은 뒤 이를 긍정적인 문장(positive statements)으로 바꾸어 볼 것을 제안하고 있습니다. 예를 들어, 아침에 일찍 일어나는 것이 힘들다면 '나는 매일 아침 5시에 일어난다'라고 긍정문으로 쓰는 것입니다. 이러한 방식이 생각과 행동의 변화를 불러일으킨다고 설명하고 있으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 상황을 있는 그대로 받아들이기
② 신데렐라처럼 기적이 일어나기를 기도하기
③ 문제들을 한꺼번에 해결하려고 노력하기
④ 과제에 대한 진술을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸기
⑤ 그것들을 하나씩 해결하기 위한 구체적인 시간 단위 계획 세우기

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold.' The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also __________________________________________.
options: ① their academic performance and inquiry ability
② our behavior and the relationship which is formed
③ students' attitude for achieving the goal of the lecture
④ the capability to screen the truth from common people
⑤ cultural stereotypes of strangers on their first impression
questions.explanation: 이 글은 한 사람에 대한 첫인상이나 기대감이 그 사람에 대한 인상 형성뿐만 아니라 실제로 그 사람과 상호작용하는 행동에도 영향을 미친다는 내용입니다. 강사가 따뜻할 것이라고 예상한 학생들이 더 많이 소통했다는 결과를 통해 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 그들의 학업 성취도와 탐구 능력
② 우리의 행동과 형성되는 관계
③ 강의 목표를 달성하기 위한 학생들의 태도
④ 일반인들로부터 진실을 가려내는 능력
⑤ 낯선 사람들의 첫인상에 대한 문화적 고정관념

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. ⓐCommon sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. ⓑAs examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. ⓒStudents with exceptional athletic abilities are sometimes enlisted to participate in adult competitions, such as the Olympics. ⓓAll have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. ⓔIn a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린아이들을 위해 성인용 스포츠 환경과 장비를 아이들의 신체 조건에 맞게 조정(adaptation)했다는 내용입니다. 반면 ③번(ⓒ)은 뛰어난 운동 능력을 가진 학생들이 올림픽과 같은 성인 대회에 참가한다는 내용으로, 글의 주제인 '아이들을 위한 스포츠 환경의 변형'과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment.
ordered_passages: (A) On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.

(B) The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details.

(C) In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력을 결정한다는 주제를 제시합니다. (C)에서 인간의 감각이 걷기 속도(시속 5마일 이하)에 맞춰져 있다는 진화론적 근거를 설명하고, (B)에서 이와 대조되는 매우 빠른 자동차 운전자의 경우 세부 사항 처리가 제한됨을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 다시 느린 보행자의 장점과 그 중간 단계인 조깅/자전거 타는 사람들을 언급하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off.
ordered_passages: (A) In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
(B) At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes.
(C) Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 경제 상황 개선과 여가 시간의 증가를 언급한 후, (B)에서 이와 동시에(At the same time) 운송 수단이 개선되었음을 설명하며 산업 혁명을 예로 듭니다. (C)에서 19세기 철도가 유명한 해안 리조트를 열게 했음을 구체적으로 설명하고, (A)에서 철도 시스템의 또 다른 예(캐나다)를 든 뒤 항공 운송의 등장으로 인한 관광 성장을 언급하며 마무리하는 순서가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. (A) From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. (B) "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. (C) While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. (D) Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? (E) More often than not, it's good to adopt the practices of those around you.
questions.insertion_sentence: It is a hassle to wait but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '기다리는 것은 번거롭지만 줄이 서 있다는 것은 음식이 맛있다는 강력한 신호'라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (D)에서 식당에 줄이 있는지, 자리를 찾기 쉬운지에 대한 질문을 던졌으므로, 그 질문에 대한 구체적인 답변이자 사회적 증거의 사례인 주어진 문장이 (E) 자리에 오는 것이 논리적입니다. (E) 이후의 문장은 타인의 관습을 따르는 것이 좋다는 결론으로 자연스럽게 이어집니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.summary_sentence: The taste is not related to a specific (A)___________ of the tongue but rather to factors such as which taste is experienced first and the (B)____________ of tasting.
questions.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 '혀의 지도(영역별 맛 감지)'가 잘못된 것이며, 맛은 입안 어디에서나 느낄 수 있다는 것입니다. 또한 마지막 문장에서 맛을 느끼는 매커니즘은 '장소'가 아니라 '시간(어떤 맛을 먼저 등록하느냐)'이라고 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '장소'를 의미하는 area가, (B)에는 '시간/시기'를 의미하는 timing이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지역 / 타이밍(시기)
② 부분 / 예절
③ 능력 / 냄새
④ 기능 / 전문성(특기)
⑤ 온도 / 종류

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.summary_sentence: To get (A)____________ from completing a given task, one should find out the (B)____________ of working through a variety of practices.
questions.explanation: 지문은 일을 완수함으로써 오는 자신감을 얻기 위해서는 각 업무가 얼마나 오래 걸릴지(필요한 시간)를 이해하고 추정하는 연습이 중요하다고 강조합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 완수나 성취를 뜻하는 'accomplishment', (B)에는 '필요한 시간(required time)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 수익 / 진심 어린 성취감
② 수익 / 금전적 보상
③ 사회적 지능 / 높은 산출물
④ 성취 / 요구되는 시간
⑤ 성취 / 진정한 가치

questions.question: 26. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 조건에 맞게 쓰시오. [3.0점]
questions.passage: __________________________________________. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
subjective_conditions: 10단어 이하로 완성할 것
주어진 어구를 반드시 한 번씩 사용할 것(필요시 변형 가능)
questions.answer: The narrator takes the initiative in telling a story.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 서술자가 누구냐에 따라 이야기의 초점과 해석이 달라진다는 내용입니다. 따라서 서술자가 이야기를 전개하는 데 주도적인 역할을 한다는 내용이 빈칸에 적절합니다. 'take the initiative in' 뒤에는 동명사 ~ing가 오므로 'in telling a story'로 연결합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be __________________________. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
subjective_conditions: 15단어 이하로 완성할 것
주어진 어구를 반드시 한 번씩 사용할 것(필요시 변형 가능)
questions.answer: adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal
questions.explanation: 이 글은 모든 동물이 개별적 특성과 환경, 질병의 종류에 따라 치유에 다르게 반응하므로, 각 치유 처치가 '동물의 구체적인 필요에 맞게 조정되어야 함'을 설명하고 있습니다. <보기>의 'adjust'를 수동태 문맥에 맞게 'adjusted'로 변형하고, 목적을 나타내는 'to suit the specific needs of the animal'을 사용하여 15단어 이내로 작성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① ways to persuade someone with opposing opinions
② importance of reading business sections of newspapers
③ how to distinguish a capable boss from an incompetent one
④ techniques to express your own opinions without feeling bad
⑤ attitudes of leaders listening to the dissenters within the group
questions.answer: attitudes of leaders listening to the dissenters within the group
questions.explanation: 리더들이 겉으로는 반대 의견을 장려하며, 조직 내의 비판적인 목소리를 경청하는 것이 실제 업무를 완수하는 데 필요한 통찰을 준다는 내용입니다. 따라서 주제는 집단 내 반대자들의 의견을 경청하는 리더들의 태도입니다.
options_translation: ① 반대 의견을 가진 사람을 설득하는 방법
② 신문의 비즈니스 섹션을 읽는 것의 중요성
③ 유능한 상사와 무능한 상사를 구별하는 방법

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① Uncover Your Passion and Get What You Truly Deserve!
② Meaningful Work: The Driving Force to Happier Life
③ The More You Work, The Happier Life You Get
④ Lower the Bar for the Higher Satisfaction
⑤ The Joy of Little Break in Work Place
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 일이 인간에게 얼마나 중요한지를 강조하고 있습니다. 직업에서 깊은 의미를 찾는 사람들은 에너지가 넘치고 만족감을 느끼며, 결과적으로 더 높은 품질의 업무와 소득뿐만 아니라 전반적인 삶의 행복도도 훨씬 높다는 연구 결과를 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 '의미 있는 일: 더 행복한 삶을 위한 원동력'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 열정을 발견하고 진정으로 마땅한 것을 얻으라!
② 의미 있는 일: 더 행복한 삶을 향한 원동력
③ 일을 더 많이 할수록, 당신은 더 행복한 삶을 얻는다
④ 더 높은 만족을 위해 기준을 낮추라
⑤ 직장에서의 짧은 휴식의 즐거움

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① Exploring Urban Design of Street Layouts
② The Power of Details in Designing Vehicles
③ The Importance of Speed Limit in Urban Street
④ The Impact of Travel Speed on Detail Perception
⑤ Adventures in Traveling Landscapes and Cultures
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력에 큰 영향을 미친다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 인간의 감각은 걷는 속도에 최적화되어 있어, 자동차 운전자처럼 빠른 속도로 이동할 때는 세부 사항을 인식하기 어렵고 보행자처럼 느릴 때 더 잘 인식할 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '이동 속도가 세부 사항 지각에 미치는 영향'이 제목으로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 거리 배치의 도시 디자인 탐색하기
② 차량 설계에서 세부 사항의 힘
③ 도시 거리에서 속도 제한의 중요성
④ 이동 속도가 세부 사항 지각에 미치는 영향
⑤ 풍경과 문화를 여행하는 모험

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① The Decline of Traditional Sports
② Sports Adaptations for the Young
③ The Role of Coaches in Junior Sports
④ Children's Health and Competitive Sports
⑤ Overcoming Childhood Obesity through Sports
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린아이들이 성인용 스포츠 환경에서 경기하는 것의 어려움을 해결하기 위해 스포츠 분야에서 일어난 변화를 설명하고 있습니다. 야구의 T볼, 미식축구의 플래그 풋볼, 주니어 축구와 테니스의 사례를 통해 아이들의 신체 조건과 나이에 맞게 경기장, 장비, 규칙을 조정하고 있음을 보여줍니다. 따라서 '어린이를 위한 스포츠 변형(적응)'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 전통 스포츠의 쇠퇴
② 어린이를 위한 스포츠 변형(적응)
③ 주니어 스포츠에서 코치의 역할
④ 아동 건강과 경쟁 스포츠
⑤ 스포츠를 통한 소아 비만 극복

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with these participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ① problems caused by severe mental illness
② societal factors that improve mental health
③ ways to participate in group singing program
④ benefits of group music therapy on mental health
⑤ reasons people are eager to experience new things
questions.explanation: 이 글은 정신 질환을 앓고 있는 사람들을 대상으로 한 집단 음악 치료와 집단 가창의 긍정적인 효과에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 음악 치료가 삶의 질을 향상시키고, 합창 참여가 정서 상태 개선, 소속감 형성, 자신감 증진 등 정신 건강과 안녕에 큰 도움이 된다는 연구 결과를 담고 있으므로 주제로 '정신 건강에 미치는 집단 음악 치료의 이점'이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
options: ① Magma cools when it reaches the Earth's surface or below the surface.
② Atoms move closer together as they lose heat energy during magma cooling.
③ Atoms arrangement in minerals formed from magma is entirely random.
④ The size of the crystals depends on how quickly the magma cools.
⑤ Individual mineral crystals are hard to see when magma cools quickly.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 "atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns."라고 언급하며 원자들이 '질서 있고 반복적인 패턴'으로 배열된다고 했으므로, 완전히 무작위(entirely random)라고 설명한 3번은 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 마그마는 지구 표면에 도달하거나 표면 아래에 갇혀 있을 때 식는다.
② 마그마가 식는 동안 원자들은 열에너지를 잃으면서 서로 더 가까이 이동한다.
③ 마그마로부터 형성된 광물의 원자 배열은 완전히 무작위적이다.
④ 결정의 크기는 마그마가 얼마나 빨리 식느냐에 부분적으로 달려 있다.
⑤ 마그마가 빠르게 식을 때 개별 광물 결정은 보기 어렵다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - ⓐ<u>what</u> degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced ⓑ<u>to follow</u>. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear ⓒ<u>immobile</u>, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place ⓓ<u>where</u> it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees ⓔ<u>moving</u> with surprising speed during past period of climate change.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장에서 주어는 even creatures like trees이고, know의 목적어인 that절 내부의 동사가 필요한 자리입니다. 과거의 기후 변화 기간 동안 이동했다는 사실을 나타내므로 현재분사인 moving 대신 과거시제 동사인 moved가 와야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your ⓐ<u>intended</u> path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well ⓑ<u>rewarded</u> for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut ⓒ<u>that</u> you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort ⓓ<u>to climb out</u>; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them ⓔ<u>to feel</u> locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying - but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 속한 문장에서 'leave'는 'leave + 목적어 + 목적격 보어'의 형식을 취하며, 목적어(them)와 보어의 관계가 능동일 때 현재분사(feeling)를 사용합니다. 따라서 'to feel'을 'feeling'으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말 및 표현의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the ⓐ<u>identical</u> as each other; therefor, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. ⓑ<u>Environmental</u> factors can also determine how the animal will react during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a ⓒ<u>domestic</u> home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will respond differently than those accepting healing for ⓓ<u>emotional</u> confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit these ⓔ<u>common</u> needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.explanation: 글 전체에서 동물마다 특성이 다르고 환경이나 겪고 있는 문제에 따라 반응이 다르므로 치료 세션을 다르게 탐색하고 조정해야 한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 동물의 '공통적인(common)' 필요가 아니라 '개별적인(individual)' 또는 '특정한(specific)' 필요에 맞게 조정되어야 하므로 ⓔ가 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말 및 표현의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience ⓐ<u>difficulties</u> when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less ⓑ<u>inaccurate</u> than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓒ<u>insensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓓ<u>underestimate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underrated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts ⓔ<u>forget</u> how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: '지식의 저주'는 전문가들이 초보자의 입장에서 생각하지 못해 난이도를 과소평가하는 현상을 말합니다. 전문가들은 휴대폰 사용법을 배우는 데 걸리는 시간을 판단할 때 초보자들보다 현저히 '덜 정확했다(less accurate)'는 내용이 되어야 하므로 'less inaccurate'는 문맥상 반대 의미가 되어 어색합니다. ⓑ는 accurate로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that 'senses ___________________ into a limited number of specific kinds,' Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
options: ④ are defined in a concrete way
⑤ can be tied up with each other
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 5가지 감각 외에도 인간에게는 신체 지각이나 균형 감각이 있고, 다른 동물들은 열 감지 등 독특한 감각 체계를 가지고 있다는 사례를 통해 감각을 몇 가지 종류로 딱 나누어 분류할 수 없다는 내용을 추론할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 정교해질 것이다
② 단순화될 필요가 있다
③ 정확하게 분류될 수 없다
④ 구체적인 방식으로 정의된다
⑤ 서로 결합될 수 있다

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered 'finished.' Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. This approach allows the painting to develop evenly and avoids the problem of some areas being more detailed than others. By working on the whole canvas at the same time, you ensure that the composition and color balance are maintained throughout the process. It also helps in keeping the overall vision and theme of the painting consistent, which is crucial for its final appearance. Also, it is important to ______________________ from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation: 그림을 그릴 때 한 부분에 집중하기보다 전체적으로 작업하는 것이 균형 유지에 좋으며, 너무 많이 그려서 작품을 망치는 것을 방지하기 위해 때때로 진행 상황을 평가하기 위해 '잠시 멈추고 되돌아보는 것(pause and reflect)'이 중요하다는 흐름입니다. 뒤에 나오는 '휴식을 취하고 새로운 눈으로 돌아오라'는 조언과도 일맥상통합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흠름개 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. ⓐIt deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. ⓑThere are various factors that affect recognition and memory, but age, environmental changes, and stress are indeed often mentioned as playing significant roles. ⓒHowever, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. ⓓWhen you think, you can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. ⓔWhen your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negatives that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의식적 마음감 무의식적 마음의 특징을 대조하며, 특히 의식적 마음이 감정에 휘둘려 잘못된 결정을 내리는 과정을 설명합니다. (B)는 인식감 기억에 영향을 미치는 외부적 요인(나이, 환경, 스트너스)에 대한 설명으로, 둀 가지 마음의 작용 방식을 다루는 전체 내용에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흠름으로 밴아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver what customers actually wanted. (A) Henry Ford may have gotten away with producing his best-selling T-model Ford in one colour only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. (B) The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production, and the accompanying salesmanship, would create its own demand. (C) Satisfying the needs of consumers obviously involves more than just putting together a slick advertisement or offering a temporary discount. (D) Marketing demands a process where a range of issues are considered in order to maximize the likelihood that a customer will first of all be attracted to the product, will make the decision to buy it, and be satisfied by the product or service once it has been consumed and used. (E) These processes can then be combined in order to construct a workable definition of marketing.
questions.insertion_sentence: Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focal point of business.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장은 고객감 그들의 다양한 요구를 충족시키려는 욕구가 비즈니스의 중심점이 되었다는 내용입니다. (B) 문장에서 마케팅 혁명으로 인해 생산이 수요를 창출한다는 관점이 파킴되었음을 언급한 후, (C) 앞에 고객이 중심이 되었다는 제시문이 위치하고, (C) 문장에서 '소비자의 니즈를 충족시키는 걃'에 대한 구체적인 설명이 이어지는 걃이 논리적으로 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. (A) The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. (B) We begin with an idea about how the future will be. (C) Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. (D) This is why having the right attitude about both past and present circumstances is so important. (E) When we have a healthy attitude about the past and constructive feelings about ourselves and our present opportunities, we subconsciously guide ourselves toward the achievement of our dreams.
questions.insertion_sentence: Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 우리의 모든 생각과 결정, 활동이 조화를 이루어 미래에 대해 정신적으로 결론 내린 것을 실현한다는 내용입니다. (C)까지는 미래에 대한 비전을 다듬고 완성하는 과정을 설명하고 있으며, 주어진 문장은 그 비전이 현실화되는 과정을 연결합니다. 이후 (D)에서 '이것이 과거와 현재 상황에 대해 올바른 태도를 갖는 것이 중요한 이유이다'라고 결론을 맺으므로, (D) 즉 ④번 위치가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli.
ordered_passages: (A) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself.

(B) But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.

(C) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 자는 동안 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않는다는 특성을 제시합니다. (C)에서 눈을 떠도 보지 못하는 구체적인 예시를 들며 자극이 정상 처리되지 않음을 설명합니다. (A)는 이러한 현상을 '지각적 이탈'로 정의하며, 일부 학자들은 이를 수면의 정의에 포함하지 않는다고 언급합니다. (B)는 'But(그러나)'으로 시작하여 지각적 이탈이 수면의 정의에 필수적임을 주장하며 마무리됩니다. 따라서 (C)-(A)-(B)가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.summary_sentence: The research showed taste buds aren't specialized by (A)____________. Additionally, taste perception operates on (B)____________ rather than a(n) (C)____________ basis.
questions.explanation: 본문은 과거의 '혀 지도' 이론이 틀렸음을 설명합니다. 미뢰는 전문화된 위치에 따라 그룹화되어 있지 않으므로 (A)에는 location(위치)이 적절합니다. 또한 맛의 지각은 장소가 아니라 시간의 문제라고 언급했으므로 (B)에는 a time basis(시간적 근거), 공간적 위치에 따른 것이 아니라는 의미에서 (C)에는 spatial(공간적)이 들어가는 것이 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 위치 - 시간적 근거 - 공간적
② 영양소 - 식품 근거 - 성분
③ 강도 - 위치 근거 - 순차적
④ 화학 - 본능 근거 - 유전적
⑤ 온도 - 복합 근거 - 단일

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고, (A)~(D)에 들어갈 단어를 <조건>에 맞게 <보기>에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken (A)__________ that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given (B)__________ of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large (C)__________ between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who anticipated the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different (D)__________ not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
subjective_conditions: 1. 글의 흐름과 어법에 맞게 선택할 것
2. 중복 선택 불가 및 변형 금지
vocabulary_box: predictions / confusion / collaboration / similarities / presumption / rejection / distinctions / portrayals
questions.explanation:
(A) 어떤 특성이 다른 특성을 수반한다는 일반적인 생각은 '잘못된 추정(mistaken presumption)'이라는 문맥이 적절합니다.
(B) 강연을 듣기 전에 강연자에 대한 미리 주어진 '설명이나 묘사(portrayals)'를 의미하므로 적절합니다.
(C) 기존 정보(Warm vs Cold)에 따라 형성된 인상 사이에 나타난 큰 '차이점(distinctions)'을 의미합니다.
(D) 서로 다른 '예측(predictions)'이 인상뿐만 아니라 행동과 관계 형성에도 영향을 준다는 결론을 도출하는 문맥입니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고, (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 문맥과 어법에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, -I make it a point to (A)__________ my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired.- If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually (B)__________ internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: -I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done.-
questions.explanation: 문맥상 어떤 훌륭한 상사도 직원들이 자유롭게 의견을 말하는 것을 '저지한다(discourage)'고 말하지 않을 것이며, 오히려 하급 직원들의 내부 반대를 '장려한다(encourage)'고 주장한다는 내용이 되어야 적절합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 d로 시작하는 'discourage', (B)에는 e로 시작하는 'encourage'가 적합합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고, 주제문을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. Thi sis achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more -natural- way. However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
subjective_conditions: 1. 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 포함할 것(변형 가능)
appeal / cartoons / human / look / make
2. 11~16단어로 이루어진 한 문장으로 작성할 것
questions.answer: Animals in cartoons are made to look and act like humans to make them more appealing.
questions.explanation: 지문은 만화 속 동물이 인간과 닮게 묘사되는 이유와 방식에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 특히 마지막 문장에서 이러한 전략이 동물 캐릭터를 감정적으로 더 매력적으로 만들기 위함임을 언급하고 있습니다. 조건에 맞추어 '만화 속 동물들은 더 매력적으로 보이기 위해 인간처럼 행동하고 보이도록 만들어진다'는 의미의 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 문맥과 어법을 고려하여 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the realtime challenges that you face and deal with _________________________________. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as -I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day.- Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
subjective_conditions: 1. 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 포함할 것(변형 금지)  change / challenge
2. 6~8단어로 이루어진 한 문장으로 작성할 것
questions.answer: Just change the challenge statement into positive statements.
questions.explanation: "'직면한 어려움을 적고, 그 도전 문장을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸라'는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가야 한다. 'Just change the challenge statement into positive statements.'는 8단어로 구성되어 조건에 맞는다."

questions.question: 29. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 문맥과 어법을 고려하여 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a (A)____________________. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the (B)____________________ at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age and experience.
subjective_conditions: 1. (A), (B) 각각 3~4단어로 작성할 것
questions.answer: (A) noble and high goal    (B) potential to be leaders
questions.explanation: "(A) 위대한 인물들의 영향력을 고려할 때 리더십은 '고귀하고 높은 목표(noble and high goal)'처럼 보일 수 있다는 맥락이다. (B) 하지만 평범한 사람들도 리더십을 발휘했으므로, 우리 모두는 '리더가 될 잠재력(potential to be leaders)'을 가지고 있다는 결론이 적절하다."

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
options: ① 쉬운 일은 먼저, 어려운 일은 나중에 해결하라.
② 계획을 세워 무의미하게 낭비되는 시간을 줄여라.
③ 매사에 자신감을 가지고 낙관적으로 세상을 바라보라.
④ 능력에 맞는 목표를 설정하고 목표 달성을 위해 노력하라.
⑤ 일에 필요한 시간을 추산하고 시간에 맞게 과제를 배치해라.
questions.explanation: 필자는 일일 계획을 세울 때 각 업무에 소요될 시간을 추산하고(estimating the amount of time needed), 이용 가능한 시간에 맞춰 과제를 배치할 것(fitting the task to the available time)을 권장하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 putting on the same clothes가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When student are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that "<u>putting on the same clothes</u>" won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 '같은 옷을 입는 것'은 모든 학습 상황(강의, 시험 등)에 동일한 방식(the rubber-stamp approach)을 적용하는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 에너지 절약 선호도를 취함
② 강한 선호도를 표현함
③ 그들의 적응력을 입증함
④ 동일한 학습 방법을 적용함
⑤ 그들의 학습 전략을 맞춤화함

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
options: ① 어린 시절 성취의 경험이 자신감 형성에 필수적이다.
② 미취학 아동의 행동 교정을 위해 적절한 훈육이 필요하다.
③ 아동의 인지 발달 단계에 맞는 놀이 경험을 제공해야 한다.
④ 긍정적인 자아상을 가진 부모가 아이와 좋은 관계를 형성한다.
⑤ 아이의 자존감 향상에 있어 부모의 칭찬이 큰 영향을 미친다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 부모의 칭찬이 미취학 아동의 자아상(self-image) 형성과 자존감(self-esteem) 향상에 강력한 도구가 된다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel.
options: ① 여행지에 대한 만족감은 사람마다 차이가 있다.
② 운동 후에는 충분한 휴식을 취하는 것이 중요하다.
③ 시차가 작을수록 피로에서 회복하기가 더 수월하다.
④ 여행 이동의 방향은 시차로 인한 피로도에 영향을 미친다.
⑤ 같은 거리라도 방향에 따라 비행 시간에 차이가 발생한다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 시차로 인한 회복 속도가 여행의 방향(서쪽 vs 동쪽)에 따라 달라지며, 일반적으로 서쪽으로 여행하는 것이 동쪽보다 수월하다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whose story, it is affects what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
options: ① demand for creating main characters that properly reflect times
② the influence of the surrounding characters on the plot in the story
③ the impact of altering the main character on analysis and emphasis of a story
④ a number of benefits that can be gained by changing the way one views things
⑤ the tendency in which readers analyze the main character and revise the plot
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이야기의 주인공이 누구인가에 따라 이야기의 초점, 해석, 공감의 대상, 그리고 바라는 결과가 달라진다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 신데렐라나 바람과 함께 사라지다의 사례를 통해 주인공의 시점 변화가 이야기의 내용과 강조점을 완전히 바꿀 수 있음을 말하고 있으므로, ③번 '주인공의 변경이 이야기의 분석과 강조에 미치는 영향'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 시대를 적절히 반영하는 주인공을 창조하라는 요구
② 이야기의 줄거리에 주변 인물들이 미치는 영향
③ 주인공을 바꾸는 것이 이야기의 분석과 강조에 미치는 영향
④ 사물을 보는 방식을 바꿈으로써 얻을 수 있는 여러 이점들
⑤ 독자들이 주인공을 분석하고 줄거리를 수정하는 경향

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen 一 even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
options: ② The Qualifications of an Outstanding Actor
③ Strive to Attain Expertise in Your Profession
④ How to Build Credibility in Business Relationships
⑤ The Power of Excellence in Professional Domains
questions.explanation: 자신의 전문 분야에서 뛰어난 능력을 발휘하는 사람들은 그 분야와 상관없는 내용에 대해서도 타인으로부터 신뢰와 선망을 얻는다는 내용입니다. 농구 선수나 수영 선수, 배우의 사례를 들어 한 분야의 '탁월함(Excellence)'이 가지는 파급력과 연결의 힘을 강조하고 있으므로 ⑤번 '전문 영역에서의 탁월함의 힘'이 정답으로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 광고를 맹목적으로 절대 믿지 마라
② 뛰어난 배우의 자격 요건
③ 당신의 직업에서 전문 지식을 얻으려 노력하라
④ 비즈니스 관계에서 신뢰를 쌓는 방법
⑤ 전문 영역에서 탁월함의 힘

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk 一 for body and mind.
options: ① Technology: A Key to Sustainable Development
② New Technology Stabilizing Economic Framework
③ Industrial Development Generates More Professions Than Ever
④ How Are Technologies Involved in Controlling Mass Education and Media
⑤ The Drawbacks of Integrating Technology: Impacts on Livelihoods and Human Well-being
questions.explanation: 기술의 발달이 전통적인 생계 수단을 없애고, 사람들이 원치 않는 일이나 위험한 일을 하게 만들며, 육체 노동과 정신적 활동의 분리를 통해 인간의 정신과 신체 건강에 부정적인 영향을 끼친다는 비용(costs)적 측면을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 기술 통합의 단점과 그것이 생계 및 안녕에 미치는 영향을 언급한 ⑤번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 기술: 지속 가능한 발전을 위한 열쇠
② 경제적 틀을 안정시키는 새로운 기술
③ 산업 발전은 그 어느 때보다 많은 직업을 만들어낸다
④ 기술이 어떻게 대중 교육과 미디어를 통제하는 데 관여하는가
⑤ 기술 통합의 단점: 생계와 인간의 안녕에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, which then ⓐ<u>creates</u> an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly. As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you." If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler has ⓑ<u>transmitted</u> via our body. Strange as it may sound, this theory states ⓒ<u>that</u> emotions arise from our bodies. For example, our mood can be improved by simply ⓓ<u>lifting</u> up the corners of our mouth. If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, taking care not to let the pencil ⓔ<u>touch</u> their lips (thus forcing the mouth into a smile-like shape), they judge cartoons funnier than if they have been asked to frown. The primacy of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase "I must be afraid, because I'm running."
questions.explanation: ⓑ 'the emotion of the smiler has transmitted'에서 미소 짓는 사람의 감정은 우리의 몸을 통해 '전달되는' 대상입니다. 따라서 수동의 의미를 나타내는 현재완료 수동태인 'has been transmitted'가 되어야 어법상 적절합니다. ⓐ는 주격 관계대명사 which의 선행사인 our own body(또는 앞 문장 전체)에 일치시킨 단수 동사로 적절하며, ⓒ는 states의 목적어 절을 이끄는 접속사, ⓓ는 전치사 by의 목적어인 동명사, ⓔ는 사역동사 let의 목적격 보어로 쓰인 동사원형으로 모두 옳습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. Although it may seem sensible, having two separate calendars for work and personal life possibly ⓐ<u>leads</u> to distractions. To check if something is missing, you will find your self ⓑ<u>to check</u> your to-do lists multiple times. Instead, organize all of your tasks in one place. It doesn't matter ⓒ<u>if</u> you use digital or paper media. It's okay to keep your professional and personal tasks in one place. This will give you a good idea of ⓓ<u>how</u> time is divided between work and home. This will allow you to make ⓔ<u>informed</u> decisions about which tasks are most important.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 있는 문장에서 find는 5형식 동사로 쓰였으며, 목적어(yourself)와 목적격 보어의 관계가 능동일 때 현재분사를 사용합니다. 따라서 'to check'는 'checking'으로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓐ는 동명사 주어(having ~)에 따른 단수 동사, ⓒ는 ~인지 아닌지의 의미를 갖는 접속사, ⓓ는 의문부사, ⓔ는 '정보에 근거한'이라는 의미의 분사로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have ⓐ<u>fewer</u> questions and more default settings. The decline in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are even more ⓑ<u>efficient</u> than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly ⓒ<u>disarranged</u>. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and ⓓ<u>solidify</u> into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are ⓔ<u>removed</u>.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 유아의 뇌는 연결망이 많지만 '엉망(mess)'이고 효율성이 떨어진다는 내용이 나와야 합니다. 따라서 성인의 뇌보다 연결 노선이 '더 효율적(more efficient)'이라는 표현은 문맥상 어색하며, '덜 효율적(less efficient)'으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about ⓐ<u>spoiled</u> stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be ⓑ<u>labeled</u> as either good or bad. There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" 一 for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they can add up to a ⓒ<u>healthy</u> diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who Irregularly eats fried chicken, but otherwise ⓓ<u>stays</u> away from fired foods. The ⓔ<u>occasional</u> fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
questions.explanation: 앞서 나열된 몸에 좋은 음식들만 먹더라도, 필요한 영양소를 충분히 다양하게 공급하지 못한다면 그것은 '건강한(healthy)' 식단이 아니라 '건강하지 않은(unhealthy)' 식단이 됩니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modem societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Businesses shifted their attention to _______________________________________.
options: ③ increasing employee satisfaction and loyalty
④ maximizing the income and corporate value
⑤ adhering strictly to industrial safety regulations
questions.explanation: 지문은 과거의 '생산 중심' 사고에서 현대의 '고객 중심' 마케팅 혁명으로의 변화를 설명하고 있습니다. 고객이 실제로 원하는 제품을 제공하는 것이 필수적이 되었으므로, 기업들은 고객의 다양한 요구를 충족시키는 것으로 관심을 돌렸다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고객의 다양한 요구를 충족시키는 것
② 지속 가능한 발전 목표를 달성하는 것
③ 직원의 만족도와 충성도를 높이는 것
④ 수익과 기업 가치를 극대화하는 것
⑤ 산업 안전 규정을 엄격히 준수하는 것

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. As a result, ___________________________________________.
options: ① reframing goods contributed to a rise in sales
② the new advertising methods were considered innovative
③ the efforts to develop new types of yeast enhanced sales
④ advertisers could sacrifice their benefits to increase sales
⑤ advertisers were encouraged to promote specific products
questions.explanation: 집에서 빵을 만드는 사람이 줄어들어 효모(yeast)의 수요가 감소하자, 광고 대행사는 효모를 '빵의 영혼'이 아닌 '비타민 공급원'이나 '천연 완하제'로 새롭게 정의(reframe)하여 마케팅을 전개했습니다. 이러한 제품의 성격 재설정 덕분에 판매가 다시 촉진되었을 것이므로, 빈칸에는 '제품을 재정의하는 것이 판매 상승에 기여했다'는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 제품을 재정의하는 것이 판매 상승에 기여했다
새로운 광고 방법이 혁신적인 것으로 간주되었다
새로운 유형의 효모를 개발하려는 노력이 판매를 향상시켰다
광고주들은 판매를 늘리기 위해 자신들의 이익을 희생할 수 있었다
광고주들은 특정 제품을 홍보하도록 권장되었다

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city.
ordered_passages: (A) Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.

(B) And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly.

(C) If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 뇌를 도시에 비유하며 시작합니다. (C)에서 도시의 경제가 어느 한 곳에 위치한 것이 아니라 모든 요소의 상호작용에서 발생한다는 점을 언급하고, (B)에서 이와 마찬가지로 뇌 또한 고립되어 작동하는 구역 없이 상호작용을 통해 기능함(it doesn't happen in one spot)을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 기차가 물자를 실어 나르는 비유를 통해 감각 신호가 뉴런을 통해 전달되어 현실로 처리되는 구체적인 작동 원리를 설명하는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, which is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way that production could be made more efficient, known as the "division of labor." (A) Making most manufactured goods involves several different processes using different skills. (B) Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished. (C) One worker could do all these tasks, and make 20 pins in a day. (D) Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. (E) Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day 一 a huge increase in productivity from the 200 they would have produced before.
questions.insertion_sentence: But this work can be divided into its separate processes, with a number of workers each performing one task.
questions.explanation: (C)에서 한 명의 노동자가 모든 공정을 수행하여 하루 20개의 핀을 만든다는 내용이 제시된 후, 주어진 문장의 'But(하지만)'을 기점으로 이 작업을 여러 공정으로 나누어 여러 명의 노동자가 각자 한 가지 일을 수행할 수 있다는 대조적 내용이 나오는 것이 적절합니다. 이후 (D)에서 이렇게 분업을 할 경우 각 노동자가 전문화되어 훨씬 빨라진다는 결과로 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. (A) He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. (B) The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. (C) In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. (D) The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. (E) It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
questions.insertion_sentence: This study on sales tactics indicated that insufficiency drives consumer purchasing behavior.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장은 판매 전략에 관한 연구 결과가 '부족함(insufficiency)'이 소비자 구매 행동을 유도함을 나타냈다는 결론 부분입니다. (C)에서 수량 제한이 있을 때 평균 구매량이 늘어났다는 구체적인 실험 결과를 설명한 후, 이 결과의 의미를 요약하는 제시된 문장이 (D)에 오는 것이 논리적입니다. (E)의 'The findings' 또한 제시문의 내용을 지칭하므로 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 21번]
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
questions.summary_sentence: Understanding post-purchase behavior is crucial for (A)_____________ repurchase likelihood, fostering customer satisfaction, and turning satisfied customers into free (B)_____________.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구매 후 고객의 행동을 이해하는 것이 재구매 가능성을 예측하고, 만족한 고객을 통해 긍정적인 구전 효과(홍보)를 얻는 데 중요하다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 재구매 가능성을 '예측하는(predicting)'이 적절하며, (B)에는 만족한 고객이 비즈니스를 위한 무료 '홍보대사(promoters)' 역할을 한다는 의미가 적합합니다. 'unpaid ambassadors'라는 본문의 표현이 'free promoters'로 환언되었습니다.
options_translation: ① 예방하는 것 ...... 승객
② 예측하는 것 ...... 정신
③ 예방하는 것 ...... 지지자
④ 예측하는 것 ...... 홍보자
⑤ 증가시키는 것 ...... 사색가

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is time pressure. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life 一 which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
questions.summary_sentence: While poverty typically leads to stress due to (A)_____________ constraints, affluent societies experience their own stressors, particularly related to (B)_____________.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 가난이 경제적 제약으로 인해 스트레스를 유발하는 반면, 부유한 국가들은 빠른 삶의 속도로 인한 시간 압박(시간적 요구) 때문에 스트레스를 받는다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '재정적인(financial)', (B)에는 '시간적인 요구(temporal demand)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: 재정적 / 시간적 요구
문화적 / 서두르는 라이프스타일
사회적 / 인종 차별
경제적 / 낮은 생산성
물리적 / 주거 환경

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. __ is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
subjective_conditions: 1. this, that, belief, average를 반드시 사용할 것
2. 8단어 이내로 작성할 것
※ 조건위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함.
questions.answer: this belief that we are better than average
questions.explanation: 문맥상 우리가 다른 사람들보다 더 낫다고 믿는 경향이 '워비곤 호수 효과'로 알려져 있다는 내용이 되어야 합니다. 앞 문장에서 언급된 '보통 사람보다 더 지적이고, 공평하며, 편견이 적다'는 믿음을 지칭하면서 '동격의 that' 절을 활용하여 '우리가 평균보다 낫다는 이 믿음'이라는 의미의 'this belief that we are better than average'로 완성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 요지에 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive and hard tasks, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Companies large and small have off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
subjective_conditions: 1. 현재완료 시제를 사용할 것
2. make(      사역동사)를 사용할 것
3. 10      단어 이내의 완전한 문장으로 쓸 것
4. 본문에 있는 단어만 사용할 것 (형태 변형 불가)
※ 조건위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함.
questions.answer: companies have made humans do more tasks
questions.explanation: 본문은 정보화 사회가 인간의 업무를 줄여줄 것이라는 예상과 달리, 기업들이 소비자들에게 업무를 전가하여 인간이 더 많은 일을 하게 만들었다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 조건에 맞춰 '현재완료(have made)', '사역동사(make + 목적어 + 동사원형)', '10단어 이내', '본문 단어 활용'을 충족하는 문장을 구성하면 'companies have made humans do more tasks'가 됩니다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
questions.summary_sentence: Understanding post-purchase behavior is crucial for (A)_____________ repurchase likelihood, fostering customer satisfaction, and turning satisfied customers into free (B)_____________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 구매 후 행동을 이해하는 것이 재구매 가능성을 예측(predicting)하고, 만족한 고객을 기업의 홍보 대사(ambassadors) 즉, 무료 홍보자(promoters)로 만드는 데 중요하다고 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 방지하는 것 - 무임 승차자
② 예측하는 것 - 정신/영혼
③ 방지하는 것 - 지지자
④ 예측하는 것 - 홍보자
⑤ 증가시키는 것 - 사색가

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation. Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less ⓐ<u>correct</u> than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓑ<u>sharp</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓒ<u>underrate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to ⓓ<u>learn</u> that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how ⓔ<u>difficult</u> it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 전문가들은 초보자들에게 과업이 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 무뎌지거나 둔감해지는 현상(지식의 저주)을 겪습니다. 따라서 'sharp(예리한/민감한)'를 'insensitive(둔감한)' 또는 'unaware'와 같은 단어로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.*barnacle: 따개비 **dispersal: 분산 ***fossil: 화석
options: ① Alternative Ways for Species to Reproduce
② The Future Development Process of Species
③ Growing Requirements of Increasing Populations
④ Species Mobile Possibilities Affected by Climate Change
⑤ The More Climate Changes, The Less Species Produce
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화가 생물 종이 생존 가능한 환경을 찾아 이동하게 만든다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 심지어 움직이지 않는 것처럼 보이는 나무나 따개비조차도 특정 생애 주기 단계에서 이동할 수 있으며, 과거 기후 변화 시기에 놀라운 속도로 이동했음을 언급하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 종이 번식하는 대안적 방법들
② 종의 미래 발달 과정
③ 증가하는 인구의 성장 요구 조건
④ 기후 변화에 영향을 받는 종의 이동 가능성
⑤ 기후가 더 많이 변할수록 종은 더 적게 생산한다

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, -I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture ①<u>that</u> prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired.- If anything, most bosses even say ②<u>that</u> they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, ③<u>published</u> weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly ④<u>claimed</u> to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: -I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something ⑤<u>done</u>.-*dissent: 반대
questions.explanation: ④번의 claimed는 문맥상 'the featured leaders are asked... and (are) regularly claimed...' 구조로 연결되거나, 수동태인 'are regularly claimed'가 되어야 합니다. 하지만 내용상 리더들이 '주장받는 것'이 아니라 리더들이 주니어 직원들로부터의 내부 반대를 장려한다고 '주장하는' 것이므로, are asked와 병렬 구조를 이루어 'claim'이 되거나, 주어인 leaders의 동작을 나타내는 능동형 동사가 필요합니다. 원문에서는 'claim'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at ⓐ<u>which</u> one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, humans senses are ⓑ<u>adapted</u> to the speed, humans move through space under their own power while walking at the speed. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally ⓒ<u>suited</u> to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability ⓓ<u>to appreciate</u> design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, ⓔ<u>allow</u> for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites.*distinguish: 구별하다 **pedestrian: 보행자
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'pedestrian travel'로 3인칭 단수입니다. 'being much slower'는 삽입된 분사구문이므로, 동사인 'allow'를 단수형인 'allows'로 고쳐야 수 일치 어법에 맞습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there?
