Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are ____________________. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that ''senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds,'' Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate: 찙추동물 **odor: 냄새
options: ① much more difficult to classify
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에서 감각은 특정한 수로 명확히 나눠질 수 없다고 명시되어 있다. 따라서 다른 동물들의 감각은 '뵄류하기가 훌씬 더 어렵다'(①)는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 뵄류하기가 훌씬 더 어렵다
② 그들의 밸능에 의해 억제된다
③ 인간과 동일하다
④ 인간에검서 기원하였다
⑤ 구뵄하기 쉽다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. ⓐFor example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. ⓑThe next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. ⓒPest and disease limitation are one of the benefits of crop rotation. ⓓIn year three, the crops will rotate again. ⓔBy the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 윤작(crop rotation)이 이루어지는 구체적인 과정과 순서에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. (A), (B), (D), (E)는 모두 연도별 작물의 이동 순서를 묘사하고 있으나, ⓒ번 문장은 윤작의 이점(해충 및 질병 제한)을 설명하고 있어 순차적인 과정 설명의 흐름을 방해합니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth.
ordered_passages: (A) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites.
(B) Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.

(C) Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn, of the twentieth century.
questions.explanation: 혀의 특정 부위에서 특정 맛을 느낀다는 '혀 지도'를 소개한 주어진 글 뒤에, 'however'를 사용하여 이 설명이 완전히 틀렸음을 밝히는 (C)가 오는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 그 후 오늘날 연구자들이 밝혀낸 사실인 '모든 부위에서 모든 맛을 느낄 수 있다'는 내용인 (A)가 이어지고, 'Moreover'를 통해 맛을 느끼는 메커니즘이 장소가 아닌 시간의 문제라는 추가 설명을 덧붙이는 (B)가 오는 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. (B) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. (C) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (D) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. (E) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.insertion_sentence: But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition.
questions.explanation: 수면 중 자극에 반응하지 않는 '지각적 이탈(Perceptual disengagement)'에 대해 설명하는 글입니다. (D)에서 일부 학자들이 지각적 이탈을 수면의 정의에 포함하지 않는다는 견해를 소개합니다. 이에 대해 주어진 문장이 'But'을 통해 반론을 제기하며 지각적 이탈이 수면의 정의에 필수적임을 주장합니다. 이후 (E)에서 'Nevertheless'로 시작하며 완전한 지각적 이탈이 없는 '졸음' 상태에서도 수면의 이점을 얻는 예외적인 경우를 설명하는 순서가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those ___________________________ were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.*numerous: 수많은
subjective_conditions: 1. 관계대명사를 사용하여 작성할 것
2. satisfaction / work를 반드시 활용하고 필요시 형태를 변형하고 단어를 추가하여 작성할 것
3. 7단어 이내로 작성할 것
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 일과 직업적 만족감이 삶의 행복에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸에는 '자신의 일에서 더 큰 만족감을 얻은 사람들'이라는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 주격 관계대명사 'who' 또는 'that'을 사용하고, 'take satisfaction from/in' 표현을 활용하여 'who took satisfaction from their work'와 같이 작성합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: No ⓐ<u>respectable</u> boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents ⓑ<u>disagreeing</u> viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with ⓒ<u>corporate</u>, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually ⓓ<u>discourage</u> internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may ⓔ<u>intend</u> to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."*dissent: 반대
questions.explanation: 글의 앞부분에서 대부분의 상사들이 반대 의견에 찬성하며(pro-dissent), 부하 직원들이 자유롭게 말할 수 있는 문화를 유지한다고 말합니다. 따라서 문맥상 인터뷰에서도 이 리더들은 부하 직원들의 내부 저항(internal protest)을 계속해서 '장려한다(encourage)'고 주장해야 자연스럽습니다. ⓓ의 discourage(낙담시키다, 막다)는 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 3. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
(B) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(C) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각을 5가지라고 정의했음을 언급합니다. 이에 대해 (C)에서 Fiona Macpherson이 의구심을 제기하며 아리스토텔레스가 인간에게서 놓친 감각들(자기 신체 지각, 균형 감각)을 예로 듭니다. 이어 (B)에서 '다른 동물들' 또한 범주화하기 어려운 감각(열 감지 등)을 가지고 있다고 추가적인 예시를 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 예시들을 종합하여(These examples), 감각을 한정된 수로 명확히 나눌 수 없으며 그 자체로 연구해야 한다는 결론을 내리는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; ____________________________________.*litter: (한 배에서 태어난) 새끼들
options: ① healing is a constant learning process.
② healing doesn't involve continual learning.
③ mastering healing requires no ongoing education.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 내용은 모든 동물이 다르고 환경이나 질병의 종류에 따라 반응이 다르기 때문에, 각 치유 세션마다 개별적인 요구에 맞게 조정되어야 한다는 것입니다. 마지막 문장의 'You will learn as you go(진행하면서 배우게 될 것이다)'라는 말은 치유가 지속적으로 배워나가는 과정임을 시사하므로, ① '치유는 지속적인 학습 과정이다'가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 치유는 지속적인 학습 과정이다.
② 치유는 지속적인 학습을 포함하지 않는다.
③ 치유를 마스터하는 데에는 지속적인 교육이 필요하지 않다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. The negative effects of music were greater than the psychologists expected. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ① Revolutionizing Mental Health Care: The Rise of Virtual Reality Therapy
② The Positive Impact of Group Music Therapy and Singing on Mental Health
③ Unforeseen Consequences: The Surprising Negative Effects of Music Therapy
④ Breaking Barriers: Examining the Role of Dance Therapy in Treating Mental Health Disorders
⑤ Unlocking the Power of Art: Exploring the Benefits of Group Painting Sessions for Mental Health
questions.explanation: 본문은 집단 음악 치료와 합창 참여가 정신 질환을 앓는 사람들의 삶의 질과 정신 건강, 그리고 정서적 상태에 긍정적인 영향을 미친다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '집단 음악 치료와 노래가 정신 건강에 미치는 긍정적 영향'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다. (본문 중 'negative effects' 부분은 문맥상 'positive effects'의 오타로 추정되나, 전체적인 주제는 긍정적인 효과를 강조하고 있습니다.)
options_translation: ① 정신 건강 관리의 혁신: 가상 현실 치료의 부상
② 집단 음악 치료와 노래가 정신 건강에 미치는 긍정적 영향
③ 예상치 못한 결과: 음악 치료의 놀라운 부정적 효과
④ 장벽 허물기: 정신 질환 치료에서 무용 치료의 역할 조사
⑤ 예술의 힘 잠금 해제: 정신 건강을 위한 집단 페인팅 세션의 이점 탐색

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well ⓐ<u>rewarded</u> for doing it, you may want to ⓑ<u>keep</u> doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so ⓒ<u>shallow</u> in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so ⓓ<u>slippery</u> that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling ⓔ<u>locked</u> in what may be a secure, or even well-paying - but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 너무 깊게(deep) 빠져서 해를 보거나 신선한 공기를 마실 수 없다는 내용이 되어야 하므로 'shallow(얕은)'는 적절하지 않습니다. 'deep'으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ③ Production: Tips for Business Success
④ How to Increase Customer Satisfaction
⑤ Changes in Selling Strategies Affected by Customer Needs
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거의 생산 중심적 사고방식에서 벗어나 고객의 다양한 요구와 필요를 충족시키는 방향으로 판매 전략이 변화했음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⑤번 '고객의 필요에 의해 영향을 받은 판매 전략의 변화'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① T-모델 포드의 특징
② 현대화의 장점
③ 생산: 비즈니스 성공을 위한 팁
④ 고객 만족을 높이는 방법
⑤ 고객의 요구에 의해 영향을 받은 판매 전략의 변화

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: _____________________________________. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
options: ① A story is influenced by whose perspective it is
② The conflict plays an important role in the story
③ Reader's background changes the mood of the story
④ Readers show more sympathy when the characters are pitiful
⑤ We become more interested when there are many conflicts in the story
questions.explanation: 이야기의 주인공을 바꾸거나 다른 인물의 시각에서 사건을 바라보면 해석과 공감의 대상, 기대하는 결과가 모두 달라진다는 내용입니다. 신데렐라나 바람과 함께 사라지다의 예시를 통해 이를 뒷받침하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 '누구의 관점인지에 따라 이야기가 영향을 받는다'는 내용의 1번이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 이야기는 그것이 누구의 관점인지에 의해 영향을 받는다
② 갈등은 이야기에서 중요한 역할을 한다
③ 독자의 배경이 이야기의 분위기를 바꾼다
④ 독자들은 캐릭터가 불쌍할 때 더 많은 동정을 보낸다
⑤ 이야기 속에 많은 갈등이 있을 때 우리는 더 흥미를 느낀다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: People ⓐ<u>differ</u> in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the ⓑ<u>direction</u> of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is ⓒ<u>sizable</u> enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly ⓓ<u>worse</u> than teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is ⓔ<u>harder</u> than westward travel.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 동쪽으로 비행하는 것보다 서쪽으로 비행하여 하루를 연장하는 것이 시차 적응에 더 쉽다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 서쪽으로 비행하는 팀이 동쪽으로 비행하는 팀보다 더 나은(better) 성적을 낸다는 연구 결과가 나와야 문맥상 적절합니다. 그러므로 ⓓ의 worse는 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 15. ※ 다음 글의  내용과 일치하준 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.*taste bud: 미렰
options: ① The traditional tongue map suggesting specific taste areas has been shown to be incorrect by research from the 1980s and 1990s.
② Taste buds are now understood to be distributed evenly across the tongue, not specialized in certain areas.
③ Contemporary taste researchers emphasize that taste perception is not determined by the timing of perception, but rather by the location of taste buds.
④ While tastes like sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be perceived throughout the mouth, their intensities may vary.
⑤ The misconception of a tongue map attributing specific tastes to particular regions originated from a misinterpretation of early twentieth-century research in Germany.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 부분에서 맛을 눐기눤 메캬니즘은 장소(place)가 아니라 시간(time)이라고 명시하고 읈습니다. 따라서 맛 지각이 시간이 아닌 미렰의 위치에 의해 궳정된다고 설명한 ③번은 본문의 내용과 반대됩니다.
options_translation: ① 특정 맛 영역을 제시하눤 전통적인 혀 지도눤 1980년대와 1990년대의 연구에 의해 툤린 것으로 밝혀지었다.
② 미렰눤 이제 특정 영역에 특화된 것이 아니라 혀 전체에 고렐가 분포되어 읈는 것으로 이해된다.
③ 홄대 맛 연구자들은 맛 지각이 지각 타이밍에 의해 결정되는 것이 아니라 미렰의 위치에 의해 결정된다고 강조한다.
④ 단맛, 짠맛, 쓴맛, 신맛과 같은 맛은 입안 어디서든 눐길 수 읈지만, 그 강도눤 다를 수 읈다.
⑤ 특정 맛을 특정 지역의 탋으로 돌리눤 혀 지도의 오해눤 20세기 초 독일 연구의 오역에서 비롯되었다.

questions.question: 16. ※ 다음 글의  내용과 일치하준 않은 것은?
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
options: ④ 머에서 사용되지 먻하눤 나쁜 탄수화물은 단백질로 바꿈다.
⑤ 나쁜 탄수화물은 머을 위한 영씑소를 거의 가준고 읈지 않다.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장에서 신체가 사용하지 먻한 탄수화물은 지방(fat)으로 바꿈어 저장된다고 하였으므로, 단백질로 바꿈다는 ④번은 오답입니다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 39번]
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it.
ordered_passages: (A) It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.

(B) The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer.

(C) In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 고정관념에 대한 일반적 사실을 언급한 후, (C)에서 이를 입증하기 위한 구체적인 연구(초빙 강사에 대한 '따뜻한' 혹은 '차가운' 묘사 제공)를 시작합니다. (B)에서는 그 강연 이후 학생들의 인상을 조사한 결과, 처음에 받은 정보에 따라 인상이 크게 달랐음을 보여주며, (A)에서는 추가적인 발견으로 기대치가 인상뿐만 아니라 행동과 관계 형성에도 영향을 미친다는 결론을 내립니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 문장을 찾아 쓰시오. [24년 3월 20번]
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
questions.answer: Just change the challenge statement into positive statements.
questions.explanation: 필자는 삶에서 마법(긍정적인 변화)을 만드는 방법으로, 직면한 도전 과제들을 적은 뒤 그것을 긍정적인 진술로 바꾸라고 직접적으로 명령문을 사용하여 주장하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. [24년 3월 23번]
questions.passage: __________ __________ is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 농부들이 밭에 심는 작물을 특별한 순서에 따라 바꾸는 과정(rotate)을 설명하고 있으므로, 이를 일컫는 용어인 'Crop rotation(윤작)'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓘ 중 어법상 어색한 것 4개를 고르고 올바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: If you want the confidence ⓐ<u>which</u> comes from achieving ⓑ<u>that</u> you set out to do each day, then it's important ⓒ<u>to understand</u> how long things are going to take. Overoptimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time ⓓ<u>needed</u> alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and ⓔ<u>learned</u> by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There ⓕ<u>is</u> some tasks ⓖ<u>that</u> you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in ⓗ<u>try</u> to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time ⓘ<u>that</u> you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.explanation: ⓑ: achieving의 목적어 역할을 하며 선행사가 없으므로 관계대명사 what이 적절합니다.ⓔ: 문장의 첫 부분인 Make와 병렬 구조를 이루는 명령문이어야 하므로 동사원형 learn으로 고쳐야 합니다.ⓕ: 유도부사 There 뒤의 실제 주어가 복수 명사인 some tasks이므로 복수 동사인 are를 써야 합니다.ⓗ: 전치사 in의 목적어로 쓰여야 하므로 동명사 형태인 trying이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 문맥에 맞게 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 각각 쓰시오.
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably (A)[less / more] accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become (B)[sensitive / insensitive] to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken (C)[them / themselves] to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: (A) '지식의 저주'로 인해 전문가는 초보자가 배우는 데 걸리는 시간을 판단할 때 초보자보다 현저히 '덜(less)' 정확합니다.(B) 전문가들은 과업이 초보자에게 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 '무감각(insensitive)'해질 수 있습니다.(C) 참가자들이 '그들 자신'이 기술을 습득하는 데 걸렸던 시간을 과소평가한 것이므로 재귀대명사 'themselves'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
options: ① Optimism: A Key to Address Causes of the Failure
② Success Without Planning: Embrace Uncertainty
③ Practical Tips for Effective Time Allocation
④ Have a Chance to Enjoy Your Leisure Time
⑤ Complete Your Bucket List Before Sunset
questions.explanation: 이 글은 효율적인 시간 관리를 위해 각 업무에 소요되는 시간을 정확히 추정하고, 가용 시간에 맞춰 업무를 배치하는 구체적인 방법을 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 '효과적인 시간 배분을 위한 실질적인 조언들'을 의미하는 ③번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 낙관주의: 실패의 원인을 해결하는 열쇠
② 계획 없는 성공: 불확실성을 수용하라
③ 효과적인 시간 배분을 위한 실질적인 팁들
④ 여가 시간을 즐길 기회를 가져라
⑤ 일몰 전에 당신의 버킷리스트를 완성하라

questions.question: 6. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. ⓐYou know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. ⓑExperiencing interactions with a variety of people contributes significantly to personal growth and enriches his/her university experience. ⓒSkillful learners know that "putting on the same clothes" won't work for every class. ⓓAs flexible learners, they have different strategies and know when to use them. ⓔThey know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests.
questions.explanation: 전체 글은 학습 상황에 따라 서로 다른 학습 전략(옷을 갈아입듯)을 취해야 한다는 유연한 학습 방식에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓑ문장은 다양한 사람들과의 상호작용이 개인적 성장과 대학 생활을 풍요롭게 한다는 내용으로, 학습 전략의 유연성과는 관련이 없습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것만을 고른 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us ⓐ<u>was</u> finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses ⓑ<u>where</u> we live, the cars we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth ⓒ<u>cutting</u>. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind ⓓ<u>had pictured</u> the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, everything we think about, decide, and do is all working together to make real ⓔ<u>which</u> we have mentally concluded about the future.
questions.explanation: ⓒ before절 내에서 주어 the first piece of cloth가 '잘리는' 것이므로 수동의 의미인 was cut(또는 cut - 과거분사 병렬)이 되어야 합니다. ⓔ make의 목적어 역할을 하면서 concluded의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끄는, 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what이 필요합니다. ⓐ 주어가 Everything이므로 단수 동사 was는 옳으며, ⓑ 선행사 The houses를 수식하는 관계부사 where는 뒤가 완전한 절(we live)이므로 적절하고, ⓓ '생각이 현실이 되기 훨씬 전'이라는 과거보다 더 이전의 일을 나타내므로 과거완료 had pictured는 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것만을 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, ⓐ<u>called</u> magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to ⓑ<u>combining</u> into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange ⓒ<u>themselves</u> into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how ⓓ<u>rapid</u> the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large ⓔ<u>enough</u> to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
questions.explanation: ⓑ 'begin'은 목적어로 to부정사나 동명사를 모두 취할 수 있으나 'begin to' 다음에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 'combine'이 되어야 한다. ⓓ 동사 'cools'를 수식해야 하므로 형용사 'rapid'가 아니라 부사 'rapidly'가 와야 한다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것만을 고른 것은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for ⓐ<u>social</u> evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always ⓑ<u>beneficial</u> for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal ⓒ<u>reliability</u>. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are rarely ⓓ<u>in demand</u>. In conclusion, we tend to feel secure in numbers when we decide how to act, particularly when faced with ⓔ<u>predictable</u> conditions.
questions.explanation: ⓓ 식당 밖에 줄이 서 있다는 것은 음식이 맛있다는 신호이며, 따라서 그 식당의 좌석은 수요가 많다는 의미가 되어야 한다. 문맥상 'rarely in demand(거의 수요가 없는)'는 'highly in demand(수요가 많은)'가 되어야 어색하지 않다. ⓔ 우리가 타인의 행동을 따르는(사회적 증거를 찾는) 이유는 상황이 불확실할 때이다. 따라서 'predictable(예측 가능한)'이 아니라 'uncertain(불확실한)'과 같은 단어가 적절하다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk ─ for body and mind.
options: ① Progress comes at the expensive of traditional livelihoods.
② Countless individuals find themselves trapped in jobs they hate.
③ The influence of education and media encourages individuals to pursue low-tech labor.
④ High-tech occupations typically involve a lot of sitting.
⑤ People may face physical and mental injuries in the modern workplace.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 대중 교육과 미디어는 사람들이 저기술 육체 노동을 '피하도록(avoid)' 훈련시키고 디지털 세계에서 일하는 직업을 찾도록 한다고 설명하므로, 저기술 노동을 추구하도록 장려한다는 ③번은 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 진보는 전통적인 생계 수단을 희생시키며 발생한다.
② 수많은 개인이 자신이 싫어하는 직업에 갇혀 있음을 발견한다.
③ 교육과 미디어의 영향은 개인이 저기술 노동을 추구하도록 장려한다.
④ 첨단 기술 직종은 일반적으로 많이 앉아 있는 것을 포함한다.
⑤ 사람들은 현대의 직장에서 신체적, 정신적 상해에 직면할 수 있다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것만을 있는 대로 <보기>에서 고른 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
vocabulary_box: ⓐ Industrial societies got richer and more competitive in the 1940s and 1950s.
ⓑ Realizing it was enough to produce good-quality products at a good price, business got closer to their customers.
ⓒ Henry Ford was one of the first to reflect modern marketing practices, introducing black T-model Ford.
ⓓ Ford's decision to offer the car in only one color option is not effective in modern societies.
ⓔ The view that the production would create its own demand resulted from the modernization of society.
ⓕ Business shifted their focus to customers, addressing their complicated and various needs.
questions.explanation: ⓑ: 합리적인 가격에 양질의 제품을 생산하는 것으로는 '충분하지 않다'는 것을 깨달았다고 했으므로 일치하지 않습니다. ⓒ: 헨리 포드의 단일 색상 생산 방식은 현대 마케팅 혁명 이전의 과거 방식이며 현대 사회에서는 가능하지 않다고 언급되었으므로 현대 마케팅을 반영했다는 것은 틀립니다. ⓔ: 생산이 자체 수요를 창출한다는 견해는 사회의 현대화로 인해 '파괴된' 과거의 관점이지, 현대화로부터 결과된 것이 아닙니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with human-like facial and physical features. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. However, cartoon animals still have exaggerated physical features that make them visually distinct from real animals. This could include oversized eyes, or exaggerated facial expressions, and they even talk with appropriate facial expressions. ____________________________, the animal characters are more emotionally appealing to audiences, both to children and adults.
options: ① Thanks to authenticity of a story
③ Despite their lively facial expressions
④ Due to their species' distinctive features
⑤ Without deformed and exaggerated features
questions.explanation: 동물 캐릭터가 인간의 언어를 사용하거나 인간을 닮은 외형(큰 눈, 과장된 표정 등)을 갖도록 만들어진다는 내용입니다. 이러한 인간과 유사한 특징들 덕분에 관객들에게 정서적으로 더 매력적으로 다가간다는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 '이러한 인간 같은 특징들을 고려할 때'라는 의미의 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이야기의 진정성 덕분에
② 이러한 인간 같은 특징들을 고려할 때
③ 그들의 활기찬 얼굴 표정에도 불구하고
④ 그들 종의 독특한 특징들 때문에
⑤ 변형되고 과장된 특징들 없이

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. (A) Once people began farming, they could settle down near their farms. (B) Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. (C) They could divide up the work of producing food and other things they needed. (D) While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. (E) Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task faster. For example, toolmakers could share the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
questions.insertion_sentence: As time passed, people increasingly began to form bigger towns and villages.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 사람들이 점점 더 큰 마을과 부락을 형성하기 시작했다는 내용입니다. (A) 문장에서 농경이 시작되어 정착하게 되었다는 내용 뒤에, 그리고 (B) 문장에서 공동체 생활(Living in communities)이 효율적이었다는 내용이 나오기 직전에 위치하는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글을 읽고 아래와 같이 요악할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (단, 각각 한 단어로 쓰고, 필요시 어형을 변형할 것)
questions.passage: Chess masters ⓐ<u>shown</u> a chess board in the middle of a game for 5 seconds with 20 to 30 pieces still in play can immediately reproduce the position of the pieces from memory. Beginners, of course, are able to place only a few. Now take the same pieces and place ⓑ<u>them</u> on the board randomly and the difference is much reduced. The expert's advantage is only for familiar patterns ─ those previously stored in memory. Faced with unfamiliar patterns, even when it involves the same familiar domain, the expert's advantage disappears. The beneficial effects of familiar structure on memory ⓒ<u>have observed</u> for many types of expertise, including music. People with musical training can reproduce short sequences of musical notation more ⓓ<u>accurately</u> than those with no musical training when notes follow conventional sequences, but the advantage is much reduced when the notes are ordered randomly. Expertise also improves memory for sequences of movements. Experienced ballet dancers are able to repeat longer sequences of steps than less experienced dancers, and they can repeat a sequence of steps making up a routine better than steps ⓔ<u>ordered</u> randomly. In each case, memory range is increased by the ability to recognize familiar sequences and patterns.
questions.summary_sentence: As the (A)_________ of the structure is reduced, the difference in memory between experts and non-experts vanishes. In other words, the advantage of the expert disappears when the structure is arranged at (B)_________.
subjective_conditions: 각각 한 단어로 쓸 것
필요시 어형을 변형할 것
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 전문가가 일반인보다 기억력이 좋은 이유는 익숙한 패턴(familiar patterns) 덕분이며, 무작위로(randomly) 배열된 경우에는 그 이점이 사라진다는 것입니다. 요약문 (A)에는 구조의 '익숙함'이 줄어듦에 따라 기억력 차이가 사라진다는 내용이 들어가야 하므로 familiar의 명사형인 familiarity가 적절하며, (B)에는 구조가 '무작위'로 배치될 때 이점이 사라진다는 의미인 random(본문의 randomly 변형)이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 찾아 기호를 쓰고, 옳게 고치시오.
questions.passage: Chess masters ⓐ<u>shown</u> a chess board in the middle of a game for 5 seconds with 20 to 30 pieces still in play can immediately reproduce the position of the pieces from memory. Beginners, of course, are able to place only a few. Now take the same pieces and place ⓑ<u>them</u> on the board randomly and the difference is much reduced. The expert's advantage is only for familiar patterns ─ those previously stored in memory. Faced with unfamiliar patterns, even when it involves the same familiar domain, the expert's advantage disappears. The beneficial effects of familiar structure on memory ⓒ<u>have observed</u> for many types of expertise, including music. People with musical training can reproduce short sequences of musical notation more ⓓ<u>accurately</u> than those with no musical training when notes follow conventional sequences, but the advantage is much reduced when the notes are ordered randomly. Expertise also improves memory for sequences of movements. Experienced ballet dancers are able to repeat longer sequences of steps than less experienced dancers, and they can repeat a sequence of steps making up a routine better than steps ⓔ<u>ordered</u> randomly. In each case, memory range is increased by the ability to recognize familiar sequences and patterns.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'The beneficial effects'(유익한 효과들)입니다. 효과는 관찰되는 대상이므로 수동태가 되어야 합니다. 현재완료 능동태인 'have observed'는 'have been observed'인 현재완료 수동태로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 밑줄 친 the two species just stay in place가 글에서 의미하는 바를 <보기>에 주어진 표현을 변형 없이 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 한 문장으로 완성하시오. [23년 3월 33번]
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster ─ in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, <u>the two species just stay in place</u>.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 필수어혘를 바형 없이 모됐 한 번식만 사용할 것
<보기>의 선택어혘 중에 필요한 어혘를 골라 한 번식만 사용할 것 (필요시 변형 가능)
<보기>의 어혘 이외에 필요한 어혘를 추가할 것
10~15자로 슬 것
vocabulary_box: • 필수어혘: a place / both / its environment / the heritage
• 선택어혘: destroy / preserve / impossible / possible / pollute / purify / complete / available
questions.answer: Despite evolving, both species may remain relatively same in the ecosystem, improving their positions and their abilities.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 '제자리걸음을 한다'는 것은 상대적인 지위가 변하지 아는다는 것을 의미합니다. 예시 답안은 진화함에도 뵈구하고 둀 종 모됐가 생태계에서 상대적으로 동일한 상태를 유지한다는 내용을 담고 읈습니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ① change of policy in each nation
② business philosophy leading to social philosophy
③ economic crisis causing changes in industrial design
④ corporate marketing strategies following societal changes
⑤ tactics in the production sector reflecting environmental conservation
questions.explanation: 이 글은 1940년대와 1950년대를 거치며 산업 사회가 변화함에 따라 기업의 마케팅 전략이 생산 중심에서 고객의 다양한 요구를 충족시키는 고객 중심으로 변화했다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '사회적 변화에 따른 기업 마케팅 전략'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 각 국가의 정책 변화
② 사회적 철학으로 이어지는 비즈니스 철학
③ 산업 디자인의 변화를 야기하는 경제 위기
④ 사회적 변화를 따르는 기업 마케팅 전략
⑤ 환경 보존을 반영하는 생산 부문의 전술

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen - even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses? No. It's because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don't listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
options: ① negative impact of success on credibility
② skills for gaining trust though professional success
③ importance of getting instant credibility with others
④ ways to be connected to individuals who have expertise
⑤ the relationship between professional competence and trust
questions.explanation: 자신의 분야에서 뛰어난 능력을 발휘하는 사람들은 그 전문 지식과 상관없는 다른 분야에서도 타인에게 즉각적인 신뢰를 얻는 경향이 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '전문적인 유능함과 신뢰 사이의 관계'가 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 성공이 신뢰도에 미치는 부정적 영향
② 전문적 성공을 통해 신뢰를 얻는 기술
③ 타인으로부터 즉각적인 신뢰를 얻는 것의 중요성
④ 전문 지식을 가진 개인과 연결되는 방법
⑤ 전문적인 유능함과 신뢰 사이의 관계

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
options: ① Understanding the Dual Nature of the Mind
② Mastering Emotional Intelligence by Yourself
③ Memories: the bridge Between Past and Present
④ Harnessing the Power of Super Positive Thinking
⑤ The Neuroscientific Perspective on Fear Management
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 정신이 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)과 잠재의식적인 마음(subconscious mind)의 두 부분으로 나뉘어 있으며, 각각이 어떻게 작동하고 상호작용하는지를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '정신의 이중적 특성에 대한 이해'를 뜻하는 ①번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 정신의 이중적 특성 이해하기
② 스스로 감성 지능 통달하기
③ 기억: 과거와 현재 사이의 가교
④ 초긍정 사고의 힘 활용하기
⑤ 공포 관리에 대한 신경과학적 관점

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① Respect for Dissent: Guiding Leaders in the Right Direction
② Keep Holding onto Your Perspective with Confidence
③ The Stubborn Bad Leaderships to Drive Internal Conflict
④ The Way of Resolving Disagreements among Employees
⑤ What Makes a Conflict Between Employers and Employees?
questions.explanation: 지문은 리더들이 반대 의견(dissent)을 장려하고 경청해야 할 필요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 특히 반대자들의 말을 귀 기울여 들으면 무엇을 해야 할지 알 수 있다는 내용이 핵심이므로 ①번 '반대 의견에 대한 존중: 리더를 올바른 방향으로 안내하기'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 반대 의견에 대한 존중: 리더를 올바른 방향으로 안내하기
② 자신감을 가지고 당신의 관점을 계속 고수하라
③ 내부 갈등을 몰고 오는 고집 센 나쁜 리더십
④ 직원들 간의 불일치를 해결하는 방법
⑤ 고용주와 피고용인 사이에 갈등을 만드는 것은 무엇인가?

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those experiencing __________.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이사가 아이들에게 큰 스트레스를 주며, 특히 새로운 장소에 적응하는 과정에서 과거의 경험을 존중해주고 배경을 공유하는 기회를 주는 것이 공동체 의식을 형성하는 데 중요하다고 설명합니다. 빈칸은 이사를 통해 새로운 곳에 적응하는 중인 아이들을 지칭해야 하므로 'adjustment(적응)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 평화
② 적응
③ 안정성
④ 불평
⑤ 우울증

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that (A)[meets / challenges] expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue. However, the people, wearing clothing with one notable exception, can be seen differently. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness (B)[increased / decreased] audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as (C)[affirmative / skeptical] because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤의 예시(수술복을 입은 외과의사, 파란색 옷을 입은 남자아이)는 일반적인 기대치에 부합하는 옷차림이므로 'meets'가 적절합니다. (B) 독특함을 가치 있게 여기는 태도는 붉은 운동화를 신은 교수의 지위와 역량에 대한 평가를 '높였으므로(increased)'가 적절합니다. (C) 이러한 규범에서의 약간의 이탈은 개인이 사회적 비용을 감수할 만큼 충분히 강력하다는 것을 암시하므로 긍정적인('affirmative') 것으로 판단된다는 흐름이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 부합하다 / 증가시키다 / 긍정적인
② 부합하다 / 증가시키다 / 회의적인
③ 부합하다 / 감소시키다 / 회의적인
④ 도전하다 / 증가시키다 / 긍정적인
⑤ 도전하다 / 감소시키다 / 회의적인

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 주어진 글에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오. (어형 변화 불가) [2.9점]
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
questions.summary_sentence: Just as in a city, no part of the brain works in (A)__________, as the (B)__________ between nervous generates conscious reality from sensory signals.
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 뇌의 활동이 어느 한 곳에서만 일어나는 것이 아니라 모든 요소들의 '상호작용'을 통해 발생한다는 것입니다. 본문 중 "no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation"에서 (A) isolation을 찾을 수 있고, "everything emerges from the interaction"에서 (B) interaction을 찾을 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 <보기>의 단어를 활용하여 <조건>에 맞도록 (A)를 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you (A)<u>누군가가 초래한 대가가 상당할때만</u>. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어를 한 번씩 모두 사용할 것
어형 변화 없음
추가 단어 없음
vocabulary_box: when / the / has / is / only / someone /cost / caused / considerable
questions.answer: only when the cost someone has caused is considerable
questions.explanation: 우리말 '누군가가 초래한 대가가 상당할 때만'을 영어로 옮기면 'only when the cost (which) someone has caused is considerable'이 됩니다. 'someone has caused'는 목적격 관계대명사가 생략된 채 'the cost'를 수식하는 구조입니다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 빈칸을 <보기>의 단어를 활용하여 <조건>에 맞도록 완성하시오.
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. ______________________________ is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for (A)<u>such a task</u> when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어를 한 번씩 모두 사용할 것
어형 변화 없음
추가 단어 없음
vocabulary_box: certain / about / be / within / achieved / a /
questions.answer: Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame
questions.explanation: 글의 문맥상 시간 관리에 있어 문제가 되는 상황을 설명해야 하므로 '특정 시간 내에 무엇이 성취될 수 있는지에 대한 과도한 낙관주의'라는 의미의 구를 완성해야 합니다. 'Over-optimism about'(~에 대한 과도한 낙관주의) 뒤에 간접의문문 형태인 'what can be achieved'(무엇이 성취될 수 있는지)와 시간적 범위를 나타내는 'within a certain time frame'(특정한 시간 프레임 내에서)을 결합합니다.

questions.question: 28. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)such a task가 구체적으로 의미하는 것을 우리말로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. ______________________________ is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for (A)<u>such a task</u> when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 (A) 앞 문장에서 '일부 과업들은 상당한 양의 시간이 이용 가능할 때만 시작할 수 있다(tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available)'고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 'such a task'는 바로 앞의 '상당한 양의 시간이 필요한 일', 즉 '시간이 많이 걸리는 일'을 지칭합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness ①<u>going</u> through weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions ②<u>obtaining</u> the greatest benefits. ③<u>Absorbing</u> in singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions ④<u>engaged</u> in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, better emotional states, and a sense of belonging as well as ⑤<u>enhanced</u> self-confidence.
questions.explanation: ③번의 Absorbing은 분사구문으로, 주체(another group of psychologists)가 노래 부르기에 '몰입된' 상태를 나타내야 하므로 수동 의미의 과거분사인 Absorbed로 고쳐야 합니다. be absorbed in(~에 몰두하다)이라는 표현의 분사구문 형태입니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal, the eyes will not function ⓐ<u>properly</u>; they are practically blind. Some ⓑ<u>optical</u> information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not ⓒ<u>addressed</u> normally. Thus, they fail to ⓓ<u>wake</u> the individual since people cannot notice and process them. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems ⓔ<u> unnecessary</u> for its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement) 없이는 잠이 불가능하므로, 그것은 잠의 정의에 '불필요한(unnecessary)' 것이 아니라 '필수적인(essential/necessary)' 것이라고 해야 문맥이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that both humans and animals have five senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Moreover, other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.(B) The philosopher Fiona Macpherson claims that there are reasons to dispute the opinion. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.(C) These cases of the animals tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," as Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 아리스토텔레스가 주장한 오감을 소개합니다. (B)에서 철학자 Fiona Macpherson이 이에 반박하며 인간에게도 촉각과는 다른 신체 지각이나 평형감각 등 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 감각이 있다고 언급합니다. (A)에서는 'Moreover'를 사용하여 인간 외의 다른 동물들이 가진, 분류하기 더 어려운 감각들(열 감지 등)을 추가로 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 사례들을 종합하여 감각을 한정된 수로 명확히 나눌 수 없다는 결론을 내리며 마무리하는 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Each species possesses specific climatic requirements: what degree of heat or cold it can endure. (A) The locations that satisfy those requirements change when the climate undergoes changes; species are forced to follow. (B) Some mammals including lions and deer can move along the changing location. (C) Even some creatures that appear immobile are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life. (D) Not only are the barnacles capable of movement as larvae, but the trees also have the ability to move as seeds. (E) A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.insertion_sentence: As simple examples, there are barnacles and trees.
questions.explanation: 지문은 기후 변화에 따라 생물종들이 이동해야 함을 설명합니다. (C)에서 움직이지 못하는 것처럼 보이는 생물들도 생애의 어떤 단계에서는 분산이 가능하다고 언급합니다. 주어진 문장 'As simple examples, there are barnacles and trees.'는 (C)에서 말한 '움직이지 못하는 것처럼 보이는 생물들'에 대한 구체적인 예시를 제시합니다. 이어지는 (D) 문장에서 'Not only are the barnacles... but the trees also...'라며 이 예시들에 대한 보충 설명을 하고 있으므로, 주어진 문장은 (D) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. To (A)<u>people who have such a norm</u>, it's a natural thing. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is _____________. People   expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 영미권 사회에서 도움을 준 낯선 사람에게 '고맙다'고 말하는 것은 규범(norm)이며 자연스러운 일입니다. 만약 이 상황에서 감사를 표하지 않는다면, 이는 사람들의 기대를 저버리는 일이며 비판의 대상이 됩니다. 즉, 평범하지 않고 눈에 띄거나 '두드러진(marked)' 상황이 된다는 의미이므로 ①번 'marked'가 가장 적절합니다. 나머지는 '합리적인', '평범한', '보편적인', '편안한' 등의 의미로 문맥상 어울리지 않습니다.
options_translation: 두드러진, 눈에 띄는
합리적인
평범한
보편적인
편안한

vocabulary_box: One day, Daniel saw someone coming right behind him. He opened a door for her. She walked through the door and went her own way without saying anything to him. Daniel's friends watched that situation and had a conversation about it.
Tom: Look! She just went away with no word, I think she is quite rude.
Jane: I don't think so. What, then, should she have done for him?
Henry: I agree with you, Jane. Could someone provide an explanation for Tom's statement?
Sara: I can do it. I agree with the point Tom mentioned. She should have thanked him.
Daniel: Hey, guys! What are you talking about?
Eva: We just saw you open the door for her and were talking about her. I think we don't have a right to criticize her conduct.
Daniel: Hey, I experienced negative emotions since she failed to express gratitude for my action.
*등장 인물: Tom, Jane, Henry, Sara, Daniel, Eva
questions.explanation: 본문의 (A) '그런 규범(도움을 준 사람에게 고맙다고 말하는 규범)을 가진 사람들'은 상대방이 감사를 표하지 않았을 때 이를 무례하다고 생각하거나 비판할 만한 일로 여깁니다. 대화문에서 Tom은 상대가 무례하다고 했고, Sara는 그녀가 고마워했어야 했다고 동의했으며, Daniel은 상대가 감사를 표하지 않아 부정적인 감정을 느꼈다고 했습니다. 반면 Jane, Henry, Eva는 상대의 행동을 비판할 권리가 없다고 하거나 동의하지 않았으므로 (A)에 해당하는 인물은 Tom, Sara, Daniel입니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 내용에 근거하여, 밑줄 친 'curse of knowledge'의 예로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the '<u>curse of knowledge</u>.' Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be'.
options: ① A car expert fails to provide essential details in explaining the car-making process, leaving beginners confused.
② A scientist uses complex scientific terms when talking to beginners, who fail to understand them.
③ A developer creates user-friendly videos to help beginners use a complex software program.
④ A proficient musician does not understand the beginner's struggle in learning an instrument.
⑤ A beginner is surprised to be given a recipe which a chef wrote with professional words.
questions.explanation: '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'란 전문가가 초보자의 입장에서 생각하지 못하고, 초보자가 느끼는 난이도를 과소평가하거나 복잡한 지식을 당연하게 여기는 현상을 말합니다. ③번은 개발자가 초보자를 돕기 위해 '사용자 친화적인(user-friendly)' 영상을 제작하는 것이므로 지식의 저주를 극복한 사례에 해당하며, 지식의 저주 자체의 예시로는 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 자동차 전문가가 자동차 제조 과정을 설명하면서 필수적인 세부 사항을 제공하지 않아 초보자들을 혼란에 빠뜨린다.
② 과학자가 초보자들에게 이야기할 때 복잡한 과학 용어를 사용하여 초보자들이 이해하지 못한다.
③ 개발자가 초보자들이 복잡한 소프트웨어 프로그램을 사용하는 것을 돕기 위해 사용자 친화적인 영상을 만든다.
④ 숙련된 음악가가 악기를 배우는 초보자의 고충을 이해하지 못한다.
⑤ 초보자가 셰프가 전문적인 단어로 쓴 레시피를 받고 놀란다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
options: ① The mind comprises the conscious and subconscious parts, with the latter rapid in its actions.
② The subconscious mind handles memories, responses and recognition.
③ You can decide to fill your thought with emotion, yet it often leads to mistaken decisions.
④ Biases and various negative influences caused by emotional clouding of judgment can hinder progress.
⑤ The fears from the conscious mind will disappear when reactions are stored in the subconscious mind.
questions.explanation: '거미나 어둠에 대한 공포는 의식적인 마음에서 비롯되지만, 잠재의식이 당신의 반응을 기록할 때 진정한 공포가 된다'고 설명되어 있습니다. ⑤번은 잠재의식에 반응이 저장될 때 공포가 사라진다고 했으므로 지문의 내용과 정반대입니다.
options_translation: ① 정신은 의식적인 부분과 잠재의식적인 부분으로 구성되며, 후자는 행동이 빠르다.
② 잠재의식은 기억, 반응, 그리고 인식을 다룬다.
③ 당신은 당신의 생각에 감정을 채우기로 결정할 수 있지만, 그것은 종종 잘못된 결정으로 이어진다.
④ 감정적인 판단 흐림으로 인해 발생하는 편견과 다양한 부정적 영향은 발전을 저해할 수 있다.
⑤ 의식적인 마음에서 비롯된 공포는 반응이 잠재의식 속에 저장될 때 사라질 것이다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Up until about 6,000 years ago, most people were farmers. Many lived in different places throughout the year, hunting for food or moving their livestock to areas with enough food. There was no need to tell the time because life depended on natural cycles, such as the changing seasons or sunrise and sunset. Gradually more people started to live in larger settlements, and some needed to tell the time. For example, priests wanted to know when to carry out religious ceremonies. This was when people first invented clocks - devices that show, measure, and keep track of passing time. Clocks have been important ever since. Today, clocks are used for important things such as setting busy airport timetables - if the time is incorrect, aeroplanes might crash into each other when taking off or landing!
options: ① Evolution and Significance of Clocks in Human History
② Why Do We Rely on Natural Cycles for Timekeeping?
③ Need for Precise Timing for Religious Ceremonies
④ Accurate Scheduling: Essential to Safe Air Travel
⑤ The Critical Role of Invention in Human Evolution
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거 농경 사회에서는 시간을 알 필요가 없었지만, 정착 생활을 하면서 시계가 발명되었고, 괸 이홄 현대 사회에 이르기까지 시계가 어떻게 중요한 역할을 해왔는지림 설명하고 읈습니다. 따라서 인류 역사에서 시계의 진화와 중요성을 다루는 ①이 가장 적ಈ한 제목은 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 인류 역사에서 시계의 진화와 중요성
② 옰 옰리는 시간 측정을 윔해 자연적 주기에 의존하는가?
③ 종교 의식을 윔한 정확한 타이믽의 필요성
④ 정확한 일정 계획: 안전한 항공 여행에 필수적인 것
⑤ 인류 진화에서 발명의 결정적 역할

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Sometimes the rate of change is ⓐ<u>very</u> slow. The face peering from your mirror this morning probably ⓑ<u>was</u> no different from the face you saw the day before - or a week or a month ago. Yet we know that the face ⓒ<u>which</u> was stare at in the glass is not the same, cannot be the same, as it was 10 minutes ago. The proof is in your photo album: Look at a photograph taken of yourself 5 or 10 years ago and you see clear differences between the face in the snapshot and the face in your mirror. If you lived in a world without mirrors for a year and then saw your reflection, your experienced change might be ⓓ<u>amazed</u>. After an interval of 10 years without seeing yourself, you might not at first recognize the person reflected in the mirror. Even something as ⓔ<u>basic</u> as our own face changes from moment to moment.
questions.explanation: ⓓ의 experienced change(경험된 변화)는 주체에게 '놀라움을 주는' 것이므로 감정의 원인을 나타내는 현재분사 amazing이 적절합니다. amazed는 사람이 놀라움을 느낄 때 사용합니다. (참고: ⓒ는 stare를 staring으로 고쳐야 할 수도 있으나, 지문 원문에 따라 ⓓ가 명백한 감정 형용사 오류이므로 정답으로 간주됩니다.)

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: According to a 2006 study ⓐ<u>which</u> was published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. Likewise, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is time pressure. There was a 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan, ⓑ<u>demonstrating</u> that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life - which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as ⓒ<u>having</u> a higher chance of getting heart disease. Also, an interesting discovery was made in a 2008 American study of quality of life: people in wealthier nations were likely to identify themselves as stressed like ⓓ<u>that</u> in poorer nations. More consumer goods and higher material standards meant that people felt they had to work faster and harder to fulfill expectations, which made them ⓔ<u>feel</u> all the more pressured.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 가리키는 대상은 앞에 나온 people(복수 명사)입니다. 복수 명사를 대신하는 지시대명사는 those여야 하므로 that은 어색합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff speaking up, and I maintain a culture that _______________________________________." If anything, most bosses even say that they are prodissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① cooperation and mutual support among my staff are emphasized
② communication primarily occurs through social media platform
③ my employees are encouraged to come up with creative ideas
④ dissenting viewpoints are stopped from being publicized
⑤ differing opinions are welcomed and seen as valuable
questions.explanation: 지문의 내용은 경영진들이 겉으로는 직원들의 반대 의견(dissent)을 환영하고 장려한다고 말한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 빈칸은 어떤 '존경받는 상사'도 하지 않을 말의 내용이어야 하므로, 기업 문화가 부정적이라는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 따라서 '반대하는 관점이 공표되는 것을 막는 문화를 유지한다'는 4번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 내 직원들 사이의 협력과 상호 지원이 강조된다
② 소통은 주로 소셜 미디어 플랫폼을 통해 이루어진다
③ 내 직원들이 창의적인 아이디어를 내도록 장려된다
④ 반대하는 관점이 공표되는 것이 차단된다
⑤ 서로 다른 의견이 환영받고 가치 있게 여겨진다

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It is difficult for any of us to maintain a constant level of attention throughout our working day. We all have body rhythms characterized by peaks and valleys of energy and alertness. You will achieve more, and feel confident as a benefit, if you schedule your most demanding tasks at times when ________________________________________. If you haven't thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to observe yourself. Try to note the times when you are at your best. We are all different. For some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for others it may take a while to warm up.
options: ① you become more capable or skilled in a particular field
② you feel most energized and focused, such as after a break
③ you have taken care of any potential obstacles in advance
④ you have created a backup plan for an unexpected emergency
⑤ you have successfully completed similar tasks in the past
questions.explanation: 인간은 누구나 에너지와 기민함의 정점(peaks)과 최저점(valleys)이 있는 신체 리듬을 가지고 있습니다. 따라서 가장 힘든 과업(most demanding tasks)을 에너지가 가장 넘치고 집중이 잘 되는 시간에 배치할 때 더 큰 성과를 낼 수 있다는 것이 글의 요지입니다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 특정 분야에서 더 유능해지거나 숙련될 때
② 휴식 후와 같이 가장 활기차고 집중력이 높다고 느낄 때
③ 당신이 잠재적인 장애물을 미리 처리했을 때
④ 당신이 예상치 못한 비상사태에 대비해 예비 계획을 세웠을 때
⑤ 당신이 과거에 유사한 업무를 성공적으로 완료했을 때

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society was that machines would deal with a repetitive tasks, giving humans more leisure time. However, the reality is that most people now have less free time, as companies have shifted tasks to consumers, requiring them to perform tasks once done by companies. ⓐFor examples, some companies sell products, such as furniture or electronics, and expect customers to assemble them themselves rather than providing their assembly services. ⓑWith the rise of e-commerce, companies may expect customers to arrange for package pickup or delivery, rather than offering in-house delivery services. ⓒWith travel, service providers offer customers personalized assistance and guidance throughout the customer journey. ⓓIn conclusion, this is known as shadow work - it represents a kind of shadow economy in which a lot of the service we expect from companies has been transferred to the customer. ⓔEach of us is doing the work of others and not getting paid for it.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기술의 발전이 인간에게 여유를 주는 대신, 과거 기업이 하던 일을 소비자에게 전가하여 소비자가 보수 없는 노동(그림자 노동)을 하게 만들었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 하지만 ③번(ⓒ) 문장은 여행 서비스 제공자가 고객에게 개인화된 도움과 안내를 제공한다는 긍정적이고 서비스 중심적인 내용이므로, 소비자가 스스로 일을 처리해야 한다는 전체 흐름과 상반됩니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the -tongue map- explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.summary_sentence: Contrary to the 'tongue map' theory, modern research suggests that taste buds detect all flavors throughout the mouth with the (A)____________ of perception, rather than (B)____________, being key factors in taste detection.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 주어진 조건에 맞게 서술하시오.

This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 내용으로 보아, 글쓴이의 Inca 제국의 전령 조직에 대한 생각으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca King's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610km) in three or four days under good conditions.*excel 탁월하다 **messenger 전령
questions.explanation: 잉카 제국이 말이 없는 상황에서도 도보를 이용해 메시지를 전달하는 데 탁월했으며(excelled), 젊고 잘 달리는 전령들을 전략적으로 배치하여 1,000마일을 3~4일 만에 전달할 수 있었다는 내용을 통해 필자가 이 시스템을 매우 훌륭하다고 평가하고 있음을 알 수 있습니다.
