questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. ⓐ<u>They</u> found the road to success for young children in unlikely if ⓑ<u>they</u> play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for ⓒ<u>them</u> to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for ⓓ<u>children</u>. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where ⓔ<u>they</u> play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.*prevail 널리 퍼지다
questions.explanation: ⓐ의 They는 어린 아이들이 성인용 스포츠 환경에서 경기하는 것의 어려움을 깨달은 '사람들(성인들/관계자들)'을 가리키는 반면, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 경기 규칙이나 장비의 조정이 필요한 대상인 '어린 아이들'을 가리킵니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름상 어색한 문장은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefor, ⓐ<u>they respond in entirely the same way during a healing session</u>. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, ⓑ<u>a cat n a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment</u>. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. ⓒ<u>With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently</u>. ⓓ<u>Moreover, each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal</u>. ⓔ<u>You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process</u>.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 모든 동물은 서로 다르기 때문에 치유 세션 또한 동물마다 개별적으로 다르게 접근해야 한다는 것입니다. 앞 문장에서 동물들은 서로 똑같지 않다고 언급했으므로, ⓐ의 '전적으로 똑같은 방식으로 반응한다'는 내용은 논리적 흐름에 어긋납니다. '서로 다른 방식으로 반응한다'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not (A)__________, but (B)__________. It's not that you taste sweetness at the top of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. ⓐFor example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. ⓑExperts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. ⓒDr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. ⓓThe rapid advancement of technology has made manual skills less relevant in today's job market. ⓔKnowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to explore the learning process through students' eyes rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 전체 글의 주제는 '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'로, 전문가가 초보자의 어려움을 이해하지 못하거나 과소평가하는 경향에 대해 설명하고 있다. 하지만 ⓓ는 기술의 발전이 수동적 기술의 중요성을 떨어뜨린다는 내용으로 주제와 무관하다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ가 의미하는 대상으로 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that ⓐ<u>they</u> do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - ⓑ<u>they</u> are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as ⓒ<u>it</u> is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count ⓓ<u>it</u> as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, ⓔ<u>it</u> seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.*stimuli 자극 **disengagement 이탈***drowsiness 졸음
questions.explanation: 문맥상 ⓔ 'it'은 바로 앞 문장의 'without it'과 연결되며, 이는 그 앞의 'perceptual disengagement(지각적 이탈)'를 지칭합니다. 즉, 지각적 이탈 없이는 잠을 자는 것이 불가능하므로, 지각적 이탈이 수면의 정의에 필수적인 것처럼 보인다는 내용입니다. 따라서 sleep 자체가 아니라 perceptual disengagement를 의미합니다.

④ ⓓ - 지각적 이탈

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore hve a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.*distinguish 구별하다 **pedestrian 보행자

questions.question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.*taste bud: 미뢰
options: ① 혀는 특정 맛이 등록되는 개별적인 영역으로 구획되어, 끝에는 단맛, 측면에는 신맛, 그리고 입의 뒤쪽에는 쓴맛이 있었다.
② 1980~1990년대의 연구는 맛을 느끼는 방식에 대한 '혀 지도' 설명이 사실은 완전히 틀렸다는 것을 보여 주었다.
③ 선도적인 미각 연구자는 미뢰가 맛을 느끼는 특화된 분야에 따라 분류되지 않는다고 믿는다.
④ 단맛, 짠맛, 쓴맛 그리고 신맛은 입안 어디에서나 느낄 수 있다.
⑤ 혀에서의 주요 작동 기제는 시간이 아니라 위치다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 'Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time.'라고 명시되어 있습니다. 즉, 혀에서의 주요 작동 기제는 '위치'가 아니라 '시간'이므로 5번 설명은 지문 내용과 정반대입니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that ⓐ<u>prevents</u> disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say ⓑ<u>that</u> they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders ⓒ<u>asked</u> about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us ⓓ<u>to listen</u> to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why  we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you ⓔ<u>is</u> what you must do to get something done."*dissent: 반대
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'the featured leaders'이며, 문맥상 이 리더들이 경영 기법에 대해 질문을 '받는' 것이므로 수동태인 'are asked'가 되어야 합니다. 또한 뒤에 이어지는 'and regularly claim'과 병렬 구조를 이룬다고 보더라도, 의미상 질문을 받는 상황이므로 수동의 의미를 지닌 과거분사 형태나 수동태 동사가 필요합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a ___________ in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
questions.explanation: 자신이 처한 어려움을 긍정적인 진술로 바꾸어 써보라는 글의 흐름상, 그렇게 함으로써 생각하고 행동하는 방식에 '변화(shift)'가 생긴다는 내용이 오는 것이 적절합니다. 뒤이어 나오는 'Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive'가 이러한 변화를 뒷받침합니다.
options_translation: ① 법칙
② 변화(이동)
③ 도전
④ 어려움
⑤ 선물/현재

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, ____________________________. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize.Many vertebrates have a sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
options: ① we should accept the lessons from Aristotle
② all senses need to be divided into fixed categories
③ finding real senses doesn't matter at all
④ Aristotle tried to keep a balanced view
⑤ there are reasons to doubt it
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각이 5개라고 규정한 것에 대해, 철학자 Fiona Macpherson은 인간이 가진 추가적인 감각(균형 감각 등)과 동물의 특수 감각(열 감지 등)을 예로 들며 반박하고 있습니다. 따라서 아리스토텔레스의 주장에 대해 '의심할 만한 이유가 있다(there are reasons to doubt it)'는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리는 아리스토텔레스의 교훈을 받아들여야 한다
② 모든 감각은 고정된 범주로 나뉘어야 한다
③ 실제 감각을 찾는 것은 전혀 중요하지 않다
④ 아리스토텔레스는 균형 잡힌 시각을 유지하려 노력했다
⑤ 그것을 의심할 만한 이유들이 있다

questions.question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field.
ordered_passages: (A) Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.(B) For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones.(C) Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 전문가가 초보자에게 분야를 소개할 때 겪는 어려움을 제시합니다. (B)에서 이에 대한 구체적인 예시로 닥터 파멜라 하인즈의 휴대폰 사용 연구가 나오며 전문가들이 학습 시간을 판단하는 데 덜 정확했음을 보여줍니다. (C)에서는 이러한 현상을 '지식의 저주'라고 명명하며 전문가들이 과업의 난이도를 과소평가하게 되는 과정을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 사실을 바탕으로 학생의 눈으로 학습 과정을 바라볼 필요가 있다는 결론을 도출하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. (A) It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. (B) You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. (C) When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? (D) There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. (E) They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think.
questions.explanation: (A) 문장까지는 잠재의식(subconscious mind)의 특징에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 주어진 문장은 '그러나 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)은 당신이 더 통제권을 가진 것이다'라며 화제를 의식적인 마음으로 전환합니다. (B) 뒤의 문장 내용인 '생각을 이어갈지 감정을 더할지 선택할 수 있다'는 의식적인 마음의 통제권에 대한 구체적인 부연 설명이므로 주어진 문장은 (B) 위치에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop helps maintain soil health for the next crop, which allows this type of farming to be sustainable.*sustainable: 지속 가능한
questions.summary_sentence: Crop rotation can have a(n) (A)____________ impact on soil by making it stay (B)____________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 윤작(crop rotation)이 토양의 건강을 유지하게 도와주고 농업을 지속 가능하게 만든다는 긍정적인 측면을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 긍정적인 의미인 beneficial(유익한)이 적절하며, (B)에는 토양이 비옥해진다는 의미인 rich가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 부정적인 ... 유기적인
② 긍정적인 ... 건조한
③ 즉각적인 ... 중요한
④ 유익한 ... 풍부한(비옥한)
⑤ 시각적인 ... 건강한

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition.*stimuli: 자극 **disengagement: 이탈***drowsiness: 졸음
questions.summary_sentence: During sleep, mammals demonstrate functional blindness and (A)___________ responsiveness to environmental stimuli, indicating a state of perceptual disengagement (B)___________ for sleep.
questions.explanation: 수면 중에는 외부 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않고 자극 처리가 약화되는 '지각적 이탈'이 일어난다는 내용입니다. 이는 외부 자극에 대한 반응이 감소(reduced/weakened)하고, 이러한 지각적 이탈 상태가 수면에 필수적(vital/essential)임을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 증가된 ... 필수적인
② 활발한 ... 중요한
③ 가끔의 ... 의무적인
④ 감소된 ... 필수적인
⑤ 약화된 ... 불필요한

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called (A)<u>Chasquis</u>, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.*excel: 탁월하다 **messenger: 전령
options: ① Popular Sports in the Inca Empire
② The Origin of Contemporary Mailing System
③ The Only Way for Commoners to Become Nobles in the Inca Empire
④ The Inca's Horseback Riding Service: Revolutionizing Communication
⑤ Inca Empire's Foot Messengers: The Chasquis Relay System
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잉카 제국에서 말이 없는 상황에서 도보 전령인 'Chasquis'들이 어떻게 효율적으로 소식을 전달했는지(계전 방식)를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 잉카 제국의 발 전령들인 Chasquis 계전 시스템이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 잉카 제국의 인기 스포츠
② 현대 우편 시스템의 기원
③ 잉카 제국에서 평민이 귀족이 되는 유일한 방법
④ 잉카의 승마 서비스: 통신의 혁명
⑤ 잉카 제국의 도보 전령: Chasquis 계전 시스템

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)Chasquis의 특징을 본문에서 찾아 두 가지만 우리말로 쓰시오. (각 20글자 내로 작성할 것)

The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called (A)<u>Chasquis</u>, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. questions.answer: (1) 4~6명씩 무리를 지어 오두막에서 살았다.(2) 양방향으로 길을 주시하는 잘 달리는 젊은 남자였다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
questions.summary_sentence: Some psychological findings revealed that group music activities like group music therapy and group singing (A)__________ those with mental illness, strengthening their overall (B)__________.
questions.explanation: 심리학 연구들에 따르면 집단 음악 치료와 집단 가창과 같은 활동들은 정신 질환을 앓는 사람들을 도왔고(aided), 그들의 전반적인 행복(well-being)을 강화시켰습니다. (A)에는 도움을 주었다는 의미의 aided, (B)에는 삶의 질이나 건강 상태를 뜻하는 well-being이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. (A) The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. (B) It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. (C) You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. (D) When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? (E) There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장은 '하지만, 의식적인 마음은 당신이 더 많이 통제할 수 있는 부분이다'라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 'However'를 통해 앞선 내용인 '통제하기 어려운 잠재의식(subconscious mind)'에 대한 설명과 대조를 이루며 전환되는 지점을 찾아야 합니다. (A)와 (B) 문장까지는 잠재의식의 빠른 작용과 기억/인식 처리에 대해 설명하고 있으며, (C)부터는 'You can choose(당신은 선택할 수 있다)'와 같이 통제와 관련된 의식적 마음의 특징이 시작되므로, (B) 위치(즉, (C) 문장 바로 앞)가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
options: ① danger of ignoring different levels of knowledge
② difficulties of becoming better teachers and mentors
③ different learning speed between experts and novices
④ positive effect of the 'curse of knowledge' on learning
⑤ importance of putting ourselves into students' boots in learning
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전문가가 초보자에게 가르칠 때 겪는 어려움인 '지식의 저주'를 설명하며, 전문가들이 자신이 처음 배울 때 얼마나 힘들었는지를 잊어버린다는 점을 지적합니다. 따라서 학습 과정을 학생의 관점에서 바라보는 것이 중요하다는 5번 '학습에 있어 학생의 입장이 되어 보는 것의 중요성'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지식의 서로 다른 수준을 무시하는 것의 위험성
② 더 나은 교사와 멘토가 되는 것의 어려움
③ 전문가와 초보자 사이의 서로 다른 학습 속도
④ '지식의 저주'가 학습에 미치는 긍정적 효과
⑤ 학습에 있어 우리 자신을 학생의 입장에 두는 것의 중요성

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.(B) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.(C) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각이 5개라고 한 내용을 소개합니다. (B)에서 'However'를 통해 인간에게도 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 감각(고유 수용성 감각, 평형 감각)이 있다는 반론을 제기합니다. (C)에서는 인간 외의 '다른 동물들'은 분류하기 더 어려운 감각 체계를 가지고 있다는 예시(뱀의 열 감지 등)를 듭니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 예시들을 종합하며 감각을 제한된 수로 명확히 나눌 수 없다는 결론을 내리는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [24년 3월 24번]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find ⓐ<u>it</u> difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be ⓑ<u>tempted</u> to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and ⓒ<u>leave</u> it looking overworked. If you find yourself ⓓ<u>struggling</u> to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide ⓔ<u>if</u> any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation: ②번 ⓑ의 'tempted'는 가주어 'it'(내용상 계속해서 작품에 무언가를 더하는 행위)을 수식하고 있습니다. 행위 자체가 유혹을 느끼는(감정을 느끼는) 것이 아니라 유혹하는 성질을 가진 것이므로 현재분사인 'tempting'으로 고쳐야 합니다. ① ⓐ는 find의 가목적어로 적절합니다.③ ⓒ는 can spoil과 병렬 구조를 이루는 원형 부정사(leave)로 적절합니다.④ ⓓ는 find yourself ~ing 구문으로 현재분사가 적절하게 쓰였습니다.⑤ ⓔ는 decide의 목적어절을 이끄는 '인지 아닌지' 의미의 접속사로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. <보기>에 주어진 표현을 모두 한 번씩만 사용하여 빈칸을 완성하시오. [24년 3월 30번]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.summary_sentence: The speed at which someone moves affects their ability to observe and process details, with human senses most effective at perceiving details at a walking pace, which _______________________________.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 주어진 표현을 모두 한 번씩만 사용하여 빈칸을 완성하시오.
vocabulary_box: compared to / better at / motorists / makes /
questions.answer: makes pedestrians better at appreciating environmental details compared to motorists
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력에 미치는 영향을 설명합니다. 인간의 감각은 걷는 속도에 최적화되어 있어, 보행자가 자동차 운전자에 비해 세부 사항을 더 잘 감상할 수 있다는 내용입니다. 요약문은 '걷는 속도에서 인간의 감각이 가장 효과적인데, 이것이 보행자를 운전자와 비교했을 때 환경적 세부 사항을 감상하는 데 더 뛰어나게 만든다'는 흐름이 되어야 합니다. '주어(which) + 동사(makes) + 목적어(pedestrians) + 목적격 보어(better at appreciating environmental details) + 비교 대상(compared to motorists)'의 어순으로 구성합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
options: ① 뜨거운 용암 물질은 지구의 표면 아래에 갇혔을 때도 식는다.
② 마그마가 식으면서 마그마의 원자는 서로 더 가까이 이동한다.
③ 마그마의 서로 다른 화합물의 원자가 질서 있는 패턴으로 배열된다.
④ 결정의 크기는 전적으로 마그마가 식는 속도를 결정한다.
⑤ 마그마가 천천히 식으면, 형성되는 결정은 대개 육안으로 볼 수 있을 만큼 크다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 'the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools'라고 언급되어 있습니다. 즉, 결정의 크기는 마그마가 식는 속도에 '부분적으로(partly)' 의존하는 것이지 '전적으로' 결정하는 것은 아닙니다. 또한 문장의 인과관계가 반대로 설명되어 있습니다(속도가 크기를 결정함).

questions.question: 12. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [23년 3월 25번]
questions.passage: The above graph shows the number of births and deaths in Korea from 2016 to 2021. ⓐThe number of births continued to decrease throughout the whole period. ⓑThe gap between the number of births and deaths was the largest in 2016. ⓒIn 2019, the gap between the number of births and deaths was the smallest, with the number of deaths slightly larger than that of births. ⓓThe number of deaths increased steadily during the whole period, except the period from 2018 to 2019. ⓔIn 2020, the number of deaths was larger than that of births for the first time.
questions.explanation: 도표 분석 결과: ⓐ 출생아 수는 전 기간 동안 계속 감소했습니다. ⓑ 2016년은 출생아 수와 사망자 수의 차이가 가장 컸던 해입니다. ⓓ 사망자 수는 2018~2019년을 제외하고 꾸준히 증가했습니다. ⓔ 2020년에 사망자 수가 출생아 수보다 처음으로 많아졌습니다(데드크로스). ⓒ의 경우 2019년은 출생아와 사망자의 차이가 가장 작았던 해가 맞으나, 2019년까지는 여전히 출생아 수가 사망자 수보다 많았습니다. (텍스트상 ⓒ는 오류가 포함된 설명이나 정답이 ③으로 표기되어 있으므로 제공된 답안을 따릅니다. 실제 도표상 2020년이 데드크로스 지점입니다.)

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem.
ordered_passages: (A) There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
(B) Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available.

(C) So work on the problem. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected.
questions.explanation: 도입부에서 시간 계획에 대한 지나친 낙관주의가 문제라고 지적합니다. (C)에서는 이에 대한 해결책으로 할 일 목록에 예상 시간을 적는 연습을 하라고 제안합니다. (B)에서는 가용한 시간에 맞춰 일을 배정하라는 추가 조언을 하며, (A)에서 가용 시간이 짧을 때와 길 때의 구체적인 업무 배분 방식(긴 업무는 따로 시간을 잡고, 짧은 업무는 남는 시간에 배치)을 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
questions.summary_sentence: People's (A)__________ significantly influences their (B)_________ impressions they form and interactions with others.
questions.explanation: 강연을 듣기 전 제공된 정보(따뜻함/차가움)가 이후 강연자에 대한 인상 형성과 상호작용에 큰 영향을 미쳤다는 실험 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 사전 정보나 선입견을 뜻하는 'preconception'이, (B)에는 그 후에 이어지는 인상을 뜻하는 'subsequent'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 선입견 / 차후의
② 선호도 / 피상적인
③ 열정 / 종합적인
④ 간섭 / 연이은
⑤ 편견 / 호의적인

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 29번]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language.
ordered_passages: (A) This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way.

(B) However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
(C) Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 동물의 인간 언어 사용을 언급한 후, (C)에서 신체적 변형을 통한 인간 닮기를 소개합니다. (A)는 (C)에서 언급된 신체 변형의 구체적 방법과 최근의 자연스러운 묘사 경향을 설명하며, (B)에서 'However'를 통해 자연스러운 묘사에도 불구하고 여전히 인간과 같은 특징을 유지하며 감정적 호소력을 높이는 전략을 설명하는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "putting on the same clothes"가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 22번]
questions.passage: When students are starting their college life, they may approach every course, test, or learning task the same way, using what we like to call "the rubber-stamp approach." Think about it this way: Would you wear a tuxedo to a baseball game? A colorful dress to a funeral? A bathing suit to religious services? Probably not. You know there's appropriate dress for different occasions and settings. Skillful learners know that <u>"putting on the same clothes"</u> won't work for every class. They are flexible learners. They have different strategies and know when to use them. They know that you study for multiple-choice tests differently than you study for essay tests. And they not only know what to do, but they also know how to do it.
options: ② diverse approach for each learning task
③ choosing appropriate clothes for situations
④ tackling each learning task in a uniform manner
⑤ possessing various learning strategies and when to use them
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 맥락에서 '같은 옷을 입는 것'은 상황이나 목적에 관계없이 모든 학습 과제에 대해 동일한 방식(고무인 방식)으로 접근하는 것을 비유적으로 표현한 것입니다. 따라서 ④ '각 학습 과제를 획일적인 방식으로 다루는 것'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 매일 제복을 입는 것
② 각 학습 과제에 대한 다양한 접근법
③ 상황에 맞는 적절한 옷을 선택하는 것
④ 각 학습 과제를 획일적인 방식으로 해결하는 것
⑤ 다양한 학습 전략을 소유하고 그것을 언제 사용할지 아는 것

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [23년 3월 36번]
questions.passage: In the Old Stone Age, small bands of 20 to 60 people wandered from place to place in search of food. Once people began farming, they could ⓐ<u>settle</u> down near their farms. As a result, towns and villages grew ⓑ<u>larger</u>. Living in communities allowed people to organize themselves more efficiently. They could ⓒ<u>combine</u> the work of producing food and other things they needed. While some workers grew crops, others built new houses and made tools. Village dwellers also learned to work together to do a task ⓓ<u>faster</u>. For example, toolmakers could ⓔ<u>share</u> the work of making stone axes and knives. By working together, they could make more tools in the same amount of time.
questions.explanation: 뒤따르는 문장에서 어떤 사람들은 농사를 짓고, 다른 사람들은 집을 짓거나 도구를 만드는 등 역할이 나뉘는 것을 설명하고 있으므로, 업무를 '결합(combine)'하는 것이 아니라 '분담(divide/split)'하는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that weakened the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and _________________________________________, became the focus of business.
options: ① the effort to make a product of good quality
② the endeavor to produce at a reasonable price
③ the intention to be better than rival companies
④ the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs
⑤ the need to deliver products to the customer's doorstep
questions.explanation: 과거에는 생산이 수요를 창출한다는 관점이 지배적이었으나, 사회가 현대화되면서 마케팅 혁명이 일어났습니다. 기업은 단순히 제품을 생산하는 것을 넘어 고객이 실제로 원하는 제품을 제공해야 한다는 사실을 깨닫게 되었습니다. 따라서 현대 기업의 초점은 고객과 '그들의 다양하고 종종 복잡한 욕구를 충족시키려는 갈망'에 맞춰져야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 좋은 품질의 제품을 만들려는 노력
② 합리적인 가격에 생산하려는 노력
③ 경쟁사보다 더 나아지려는 의도
④ 그들의 다양하고 종종 복잡한 욕구를 충족시키려는 욕구
⑤ 고객의 문 앞까지 제품을 배달해야 할 필요성

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process. We begin with an idea about how the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
options: ② process of shaping future through mental vision
③ importance of planning before perfecting products
④ economic factors that perfect the future for each person
⑤ factors that caused evolution of human self-planning
questions.explanation: 이 글은 세상의 모든 물건들이 실제로 만들어지기 전에 창조자의 마음속에서 먼저 완성된다는 점을 언급하며, 인간의 미래 설계 또한 이와 같은 과정을 거친다고 설명합니다. 미래에 대한 생각(아이디어)에서 시작하여 이를 정교화하고 완벽하게 다듬는 정신적 과정이 미래를 현실로 만든다는 내용이므로, 주제는 '정신적 비전을 통해 미래를 형성하는 과정'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 제품을 제조하는 방법
② 정신적 비전을 통해 미래를 형성하는 과정
③ 제품을 완성하기 전 계획의 중요성
④ 각 개인의 미래를 완성하는 경제적 요인들
⑤ 인간의 자기 계획 진화를 일으킨 요인들

questions.question: [25~26] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.25. 윗글의 밑줄 친 우리말 (A)를 <보기>의 단어를 배열하여 다음 단어들로 시작되는 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. (A)<u>오늘날 수억 명의 사람들이 자기가 싫어하는 일자리에서 일하면서, 자신이 아무런 애정을 느끼지 못하는 것들을 생산한다</u>. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk - for body and mind.*chronic: 만성의 **sedentary: 주로 앉아서 하는
vocabulary_box: for / at / work / no / producing / they / hate /
questions.answer: work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for.
questions.explanation: '수억 명의 사람들'은 Hundreds of millions of humans로 이미 주어져 있으며, '자기가 싫어하는 일자리에서 일하다'는 'work at jobs they hate'로 표현할 수 있습니다. '~하면서'에 해당하는 분사구문 'producing things'를 연결하고 '자신이 아무런 애정을 느끼지 못하는'을 관계대명사절 'they have no love for'로 연결하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: [25~26] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.26. 윗글의 기술에 대한 필자의 생각을 전통 생계수단, 건강과 관련하여 우리말로 서술하시오.
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. (A)<u>오늘날 수억 명의 사람들이 자기가 싫어하는 일자리에서 일하면서, 자신이 아무런 애정을 느끼지 못하는 것들을 생산한다</u>. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk - for body and mind.*chronic: 만성의 **sedentary: 주로 앉아서 하는
questions.answer: 기술을 적용하면서 수천 개의 전통적인 생계 수단이 없어졌고 현재의 일자리들은 육체적 고통, 장애 또는 만성 질환을 유발한다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 기술 도입의 부작용을 두 가지 측면에서 강조하고 있습니다. 첫째, 수많은 전통적인 생계 수단이 사라지고 그와 관련된 생활 방식이 제거되었다는 점이며, 둘째, 현대의 일자리들이 신체적 고통이나 만성 질환을 일으키고 정신적 스트레스를 주는 등 신체와 정신 건강에 위험 요인이 된다는 점입니다.

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 ⓞ서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five senses, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(B) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.

(C) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate: 척추동물 ** odor: 냄새
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물에게 5감이 있다고 한 내용을 언급합니다. (B)에서 However로 이를 반박하며 인간의 추가적인 감각을 예로 듭니다. (A)에서 Other animals를 통해 동물의 다른 감각들로 확장하고, (C)에서 These examples로 압선 예시들을 정리하며 결론을 내립니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.*litter: (한 배에서 태어난) 새기들
options: ① -④ 내용 석략 (options omitted as per standard processing but should be retrieved from text if possible, providing translations instead)
① 인간과 동물 모두 개별 종의 고유성과 개성을 젔중해야 한다.
② 동물 치료에서 유전적 요인바다 환경적 요인이 우세하다.
③ 구조 센터에 있는 고양이를 가정 환경 내에서 치료하면 효과적이다.
④ 동물 치료 과정에는 신체적 요인붼만 아니라 정서적 요인도 고려해야 한다.
⑤ 동물의 특정한 필요에 맞게 치료법이 조정⃞어야 한다.
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에 명시된 "every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal"이 글의 핵심 요지입니다. 모든 동물이 다르기 ⃞문에 각 동물의 특수한 요구에 맞춰 치료를 조정해야 한다는 내용입니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. ①Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. ②Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. ③Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. ④In general, those who are happy with their lives are those who prepared for retirement when they were young. ⑤For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 일(직업)이 인간의 삶의 만족도와 행복에 미치는 긍정적인 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 4번 문장은 은퇴 준비와 행복의 관계를 언급하고 있어 글의 전체적인 흐름인 '직업적 성취감과 행복'과는 거리가 멉니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and __________________________________ at every turn. As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
options: ② reminding us of what we should say
③ offering typical forms of communication
④ guiding our interpretations of social life
⑤ judging something done done in different culture
questions.explanation: 본문은 사회적 규범(norms)이 우리가 세상을 어떻게 바라보고 해석하는지를 결정한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 빈칸은 규범이 무엇이 정상인지를 정의하고, 매 순간 '우리의 사회 생활에 대한 해석을 안내한다'는 맥락이 적절하므로 ④번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 무례한 표현을 삼가게 함
② 우리가 무엇을 말해야 하는지 상기시킴
③ 전형적인 의사소통 형태를 제공함
④ 사회 생활에 대한 우리의 해석을 안내함
⑤ 다른 문화에서 행해진 무언가를 판단함

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr. Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect (A)[referring / referred] to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it (B)[took / had taken] themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them (C)[to learn / learning], we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes rather than making assumptions about how students should be learning.
options: ② referred, had taken, to learn
questions.explanation: (A) an effect를 수식하는 분사구로, '지식의 저주라고 불리는'의 수동 의미이므로 'referred to as'가 맞습니다. (B) 과소평가한 시점(underestimated)보다 기술을 습득했던 시점(earlier session)이 더 과거이므로 과거완료인 'had taken'이 적절합니다. (C) how hard it(가주어) was for them(의미상주어) to learn(진주어)의 구조이므로 'to learn'이 맞습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As is turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to (A)___________. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but (B)___________. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first. * taste bud: 미뢰
questions.explanation: (A) 과거에는 혀의 부위별로 특정 맛이 정해져 있다고 믿었으나 실제로는 그렇지 않으므로, 미뢰가 '특수성(specialty)'에 따라 분류되지 않는다는 의미가 적절합니다.(B) 혀의 끝에서 단맛을 더 잘 느끼는 것이 아니라 단맛을 '먼저(first)' 인지하는 것이라고 했으므로, 장소가 아닌 '시간(time)'의 문제라는 설명이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 강도 / 감각
② 분리 / 인지
③ 특수성 / 시간
④ 절차 / 순서
⑤ 위치 / 공간

questions.question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 각각 들어갈 적절한 말을 본문에서 찾아 넣어 perceptual disengagement의 의미를 완성하시오. ((A), (B) 각 한 단어씩)
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally ─ they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.*stimuli: 자극  ** disengagement: 이탈 *** drowsiness: 졸음
questions.summary_sentence: Perceptual disengagement means that external (A)____________ are not processed properly, allowing the individual not to (B)____________.
subjective_conditions: (A), (B) 각 한 단어씩
본문에서 찾아 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)은 외부의 '자극(stimuli)'이 정상적으로 처리되지 않아 개체가 '잠에서 깨지(wake)' 않게 함으로써 수면을 보호하는 기능을 합니다. 요약문의 문맥에 맞춰 본문에서 단어를 찾으면 (A)는 stimuli, (B)는 wake가 됩니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 연속한 두 단어를 본문에서 찾아 아래 <조건>에 맞게 요약문을 완성하시오. [24년 3월 32번]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."* dissent: 반대
questions.summary_sentence: ▷ The respectable bosses propose that they ________ ________.
subjective_conditions: 연속한 2단어일 것.
동사 변형 가능
연속하지 않거나 3단어 이상일 경우 3점.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 대다수의 리더들이 자신들이 '반대(dissent)에 찬성한다'고 말한다는 내용(they are pro-dissent)이 나옵니다. 요약문의 주어인 The respectable bosses에 맞춰 본문의 are pro-dissent를 그대로 또는 문맥에 맞게 활용하여 작성합니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 본문에서 세 단어 이상의 연속한 어구를 찾아 주제 문장을 완성하시오. (단, 동사 변형 가능)
questions.passage: In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street ─  a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.* distinguish: 구별하다 ** pedestrian: 보행자
subjective_conditions: 세 단어 이상의 연속한 어구를 찾을 것
동사 변형 가능
questions.answer: (A) The rate of speed at which one is traveling(B) process detail in the environment
questions.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 이동 속도(rate of speed)에 따라 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력(ability to process details)이 결정된다는 내용이다. 본문에 언급된 'the speed at which humans move' 및 'process details along the street' 등의 표현을 활용하여 주제문을 완성한다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "_________________________," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate: 척추동물 **odor: 냄새
options: ① We only need to study human senses
② Only humans have different kinds of senses
③ Senses are only about what we see and hear
④ Animals and humans share exactly the same senses
⑤ Senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 5가지 감각 외에도 인간에게는 신체 지각이나 균형 감각이 있고, 동물들에게도 분류하기 힘든 다양한 감각 체계가 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 감각은 한정된 숫자의 특정한 종류로 명확하게 나누어질 수 없다는 5번이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리는 인간의 감각만을 연구할 필요가 있다
② 인간만이 다른 종류의 감각을 가지고 있다
③ 감각은 우리가 보고 듣는 것에 관한 것뿐이다
④ 동물과 인간은 정확히 똑같은 감각을 공유한다
⑤ 감각은 제한된 수의 특정한 종류로 명확하게 나누어질 수 없다

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

② (A) 법 - (B) 규칙과 처벌
③ (A) 좋아하는 것 - (B) 선택과 자유
④ (A) 기술 - (B) 새로운 업데이트
⑤ (A) 역사 - (B) 오래된 이야기들

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.*diligence: 근면
options: ① Everyone Can Be a Leader
② Leadership: A Nobel Goal in Life
③ Leading with Clarity and Confidence
④ Exchanging Opinions: The Key to Successful Leadership
questions.explanation: 위대한 지도자들도 처음엔 평범한 시민이나 학생이었으며, 일상의 개선을 위한 생각을 발전시켜 나갔음을 설명하며 누구나 학교, 지역사회, 직장에서 리더가 될 잠재력이 있다는 것이 글의 핵심 내용이므로 '누구나 리더가 될 수 있다'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 누구나 리더가 될 수 있다
② 리더십: 인생의 고귀한 목표
③ 명확함과 자신감을 가지고 이끌기

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
options: ① 예술 작업에는 치열한 고민을 통해 계속해서 더 많이 추가하는 것이 더 나을 수 있다.
② 과도한 작업을 피하고 작업을 마무리할 적절한 시기를 찾아야 한다.
③ 예술가는 다양한 예술가들로부터 영감을 받아야 한다.
④ 예술 작품을 통해 숨겨진 의미를 발견할 수 있다.
⑤ 예술 작품을 미완성으로 남겨두어서는 안 된다.
questions.explanation: 그림 작업 시 한 부분에만 집중하기보다 전체적으로 작업하고, 때때로 뒤로 물러나 진행 상황을 점검해야 하며, 너무 많은 것을 추가하여 작품의 임팩트를 망치지 않도록 적절한 마무리 시점을 결정해야 한다는 내용입니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies ⓐ<u>have</u> shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in ⓑ<u>using</u> mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it ⓒ<u>had taken</u> themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for ⓓ<u>them</u> to learn, we can understand the need to ⓔ<u>looking</u> at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: ⓔ번의 'the need to looking'에서 'to'는 부정사 'to'이므로 뒤에 동사원형이 와야 합니다. 따라서 'looking'을 'look'으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다. ⓐ 'A number of' 뒤에 복수 명사 studies가 오고 복수 동사 have가 온 것이 적절하며, ⓑ 전치사 in의 목적어로 동명사 using이 온 것, ⓒ 과거 시점 이전의 일을 나타내는 과거완료 had taken, ⓓ 전문가들을 지칭하는 대명사 them은 모두 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to ⓐ<u>overstate</u> how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and ⓑ<u>pleasing</u>, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has ⓒ<u>converted</u> numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn ⓓ<u>higher</u> incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a ⓔ<u>happier</u> life overall.*numerous: 수많은
questions.explanation: 문맥상 심리학 교수인 Sonya Lyubomirsky가 수많은 연구를 '검토했다' 혹은 '수행했다'는 내용이 나와야 하므로, '변환하다'라는 뜻의 'converted'는 부적절합니다. reviewed나 conducted 등의 어휘가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees ____________ with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.*barnacle: 따개비 **dispersal: 분산 ***fossil: 화석

options_translation: ① 자랐다

questions.question: 1. 다음 글을 읽고, 문맥상 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle' wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "(A)__________________________________" Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate: 척추동물*odor: 냄새
options: ① senses can be divided into definite limited kinds
② we are able to easily find sixth sense of Aristotle
③ you can categorize animal senses into fixed numbers
④ people are superior to animal in sensing differences
⑤ there may be more senses than we are able to expect
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스가 제시한 5가지 감각 외에도 인간에게는 고유 수용 감각이나 균형 감각이 있으며, 동물들에게는 먹잇감의 체온을 감지하는 등 인간의 범주로 설명하기 어려운 감각들이 존재한다는 내용을 통해, 우리가 예상하는 것보다 더 많은 감각이 존재할 수 있음을 추론할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 감각은 명확하고 제한된 종류로 나뉠 수 있다
② 우리는 아리스토텔레스의 육감을 쉽게 찾을 수 있다
③ 동물의 감각을 고정된 숫자로 분류할 수 있다
④ 사람들은 차이를 감지하는 데 있어 동물보다 우월하다
⑤ 우리가 예상할 수 있는 것보다 더 많은 감각이 있을 수 있다

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than ⓐ<u>centering</u> on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be ⓑ<u>appealing</u> to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to ⓒ<u>evaluate</u> your progress. Putting too much into a painting can ⓓ<u>reinforce</u> its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further ⓔ<u>polishing</u>.
questions.explanation: 그림에 너무 많은 것을 넣는 것은 작품을 지나치게 공을 들인(overworked) 상태로 보이게 하여 오히려 작품의 영향력을 '손상(spoil)'시키거나 '약화'시킨다는 맥락이 적절합니다. 따라서 '강화하다'라는 의미의 reinforce는 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. (A) In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. (B) Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. (C) The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has enough time or ability to appreciate design details. (D) Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist. (E)*distinguish: 구별하다*pedestrian: 보행자

questions.question: 4. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. ⓐThose who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying. ⓑIn contrast, those that have not realized any worth from the careers treat their employment as source of stress. ⓒSonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted studies to reveal that people gain not only higher incomes but also better output when they feel more fulfilled on their job. ⓓWhen the work meets the people's needs, they are also more likely to become irritated by their overall lives. ⓔFor her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers, finding that happiness comes from the greater satisfaction from their work.*numerous: 수많은
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 일이 인간에게 주는 충족감과 긍정적인 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓓ번 문장은 업무가 사람들의 요구를 충족할 때 전반적인 삶에 짜증을 낼 가능성이 더 높다는 내용으로, 글의 전체적인 흐름과 정반대되는 진술을 하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is ⓐ<u>what</u> they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally 一 they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli ⓑ<u>is</u> registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count ⓒ<u>them</u> as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to ⓓ<u>its</u> definition. Nevertheless, many animals (ⓔ<u>included</u> humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: ⓓ의 its는 문맥상 sleep의 정의를 의미하므로 단수 소유격인 its가 적절합니다.ⓐ what -> that (완전한 문장을 이끄는 보어절 접속사 필요)ⓑ is -> are (주어 Stimuli가 복수임)ⓒ them -> it (지칭하는 대상이 단수인 Perceptual disengagement임)ⓔ included -> including (~을 포함하여 라는 전치사적 분사구문)

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. (A) They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy. (A) The therapy includes singing familiar songs and composing original songs.
