questions.explanation: 제시문은 합창단에 참여한 정신 건강 질환자들의 상태가 호전되었다는 결과를 나타낽니다. (C) 이홄 문장에서 또 다른 심리학자 중단이 괴제 합창(group singing)의 효능을 검턐했다는 내용이 나오고, (D) 문장에서는 구체적으로(Specifically) 합창이 즐거움과 자신감 등을 즬다고 합니다. 제시문의 'The findings this time'이 (C)에서 언급된 검턐 결과를 가리키므로, 이를 구체화하는 (D) 윑츠에 위치하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, ‖I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: ‖I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① Most respectable bosses resist pro-dissenters' voices for their business.
② Most respectable bosses prioritize viewpoints only agreeing with their opinions.
③ Most respectable bosses foster opposing perspectives and view them as an opportunity for task completion.
④ Most respectable bosses provide constructive feedback to their employees who are inexperienced in the same field.
⑤ Most respectable bosses hardly accept internal protest from more experienced employees for improvement and growth.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 훌수한 사장들이 반대 의견을 장려하고, 괴제를 통해 일을 완수하기 위해 필요한 것을 배우렐 한다는 내용임으로, 반대 괴점을 장려하고 일을 해내기 위한 기회로 본다는 ③번이 가장 적절한 주제입니다.
options_translation: ① 대부분의 훌수한 사장들은 사업을 위해 반대자들의 목소리에 저항한다.
② 대부분의 훌수한 사장들은 자신의 의견에 동의하는 괴점만을 우선시한다.
③ 대부분의 훌수한 사장들은 반대 괴점을 장려하고 이를 과업 완수를 위한 기회로 간주한다.
④ 대부분의 훌수한 사장들은 같은 분야에서 경험이 부족한 직원들에게 건설적인 피드백을 제공한다.
⑤ 대부분의 훌수한 사장들은 개선과 성장을 위한 경험 많은 직원들의 내부 항의를 거의 받아들이지 않다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 'the curse of knowledge'이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as '<u>the curse of knowledge</u>'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was I for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
options: ① Newcomers' perceiving how challenging their tasks are
② Novices' overestimating the difficulty of a particular skill
③ Experts' losing empathy for the difficulty of a task that newcomers feel
④ Experts' comprehending the need to view the learning process from the perspective of learners
⑤ Experts' emphasizing comprehensive knowledge about specific area and effective ways to overcome difficulties
questions.explanation: '지식의 저주(the curse of knowledge)'는 전문가가 자신이 이미 알고 있는 지식에 너무 익숙해져서, 그 지식이 없는 초보자가 느끼는 학습의 어려움을 이해하지 못하거나 과소평가하게 되는 현상을 의미합니다. 따라서 전문가가 초보자가 느끼는 과업의 난이도에 대해 공감 능력을 잃는다는 3번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 신입자들이 자신의 과업이 얼마나 도전적인지 인지하는 것
② 초보자들이 특정 기술의 난이도를 과대평가하는 것
③ 전문가들이 신입자들이 느끼는 과업의 난이도에 대한 공감을 상실하는 것
④ 전문가들이 학습자의 관점에서 학습 과정을 바라볼 필요성을 이해하는 것
⑤ 전문가들이 특정 분야에 대한 포괄적인 지식과 어려움을 극복하는 효과적인 방법을 강조하는 것

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.*taste bud: 미뢰
options: ① Disproving the Existing Idea of the Tongue Map
② Stable Taste Experiences Unaffected by Surroundings
③ Supporting the Traditional Concept of the Tongue Map
④ Diverse Tongue Maps of People Affected by Personal Experience
⑤ Different Taste Intensities that People Perceive according to Their Conditions
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거 혀의 특정 부위에서 특정 맛을 느낀다는 '혀 지도' 이론이 실제로는 잘못된 해석과 오역에서 비롯된 오해였음을 설명하고 있습니다. 현대 연구에 따르면 혀의 모든 부위에서 모든 맛을 느낄 수 있으며 차이는 단지 인지되는 속도의 문제임이 밝혀졌습니다. 따라서 기존의 혀 지도 개념을 반박하는 내용인 1번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 혀 지도의 기존 아이디어에 대한 반박
② 주변 환경에 영향을 받지 않는 안정적인 맛 경험
③ 혀 지도의 전통적인 개념을 지지하기
④ 개인적 경험에 영향을 받는 사람들의 다양한 혀 지도
⑤ 사람들이 상태에 따라 인지하는 서로 다른 맛의 강도

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① The Stability of Species in Changing Climates
② Climate Change: Its Impact on Dominant Species
③ How Species Cope with Climate Crisis in the World
④ Trees Fail to Accept to the Notion of Mobility in Climate Change
⑤ Adaptation and Mobility: How Species Respond to Climate Change
questions.explanation: 기후가 변화하면 모든 생명체는 자신의 생존 조건에 맞는 곳으로 이동해야 하는데, 이는 움직이기 어려운 나무 등도 해당한다는 내용입니다. 기후 변화에 대응하는 생명체의 적응과 이동성의 가능성을 다루고 있으므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 변화하는 기후 속에서 종들의 안정성
② 기후 변화: 우세한 종들에 미치는 영향
③ 생물체들이 세계적인 기후 위기에 대처하는 방법
④ 나무는 기후 변화에서 이동성의 개념을 받아들이지 못함
⑤ 적응과 이동성: 종들이 기후 변화에 대응하는 방법

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
questions.summary_sentence: Called Chasquis, the messengers were (A)_____________ in delivering messages (B)_____________ in the Inca empire land.
questions.explanation: 인카 제국은 말이 없는 상황에서 도보로 메시지를 전달하는 데 뛰어났으며, 'Chasquis'라 불리는 전달꾼들은 여러 구간에서 메시지를 릴레이 방식으로 이어 전달했습니다. (A)는 능숙한(proficient), (B)는 연속적으로(consecutively)가 맥락상 어울리므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 숙련되지 못한 - 효율적으로
② 능력 있는 - 자동적으로
③ 경험이 없는 - 즉시
④ 무지한 - 체계적으로
⑤ 능숙한 - 연속적으로

questions.question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, defining what is “normal” and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn.
ordered_passages: (A) But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication.

(B) As a simple example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you’ve just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you.

(C) To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don’t), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
questions.explanation: 기본 문장에서 규범의 보편성을 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 앵글로색슨 사회에서 타인에게 감사하는 규범을 구체적인 예로 듭니다. 그 후 (A)에서 그러한 규범을 지키지 않았을 때 발생하는 상황과 타문화 간 소통의 문제로 내용이 이어지며, 마지막으로 (C)에서 감사 표현에 대한 문화적 차이를 상술하며 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. ⓐEnvironmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. ⓑFor instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. ⓒIn addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. ⓓWhether dealing with physical illness or emotional confusion, they need to gradually develop their own independent mind-set. ⓔWith this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal.   *litter: (한 배에서 태어난) 새끼들
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 모든 동물은 서로 다르기 때문에 치유 과정에서 개별적인 접근과 조정이 필요하다는 것입니다. 동물의 개별 특성(ⓐ), 환경적 요인(ⓑ), 질병의 종류(ⓒ)에 따라 반응이 다르다는 점을 강조하며 결론(ⓔ)을 맺고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓓ는 질병 치료와 상관없이 독립적인 사고방식을 길러야 한다는 내용으로, 치유 세션에서의 개별적 반응과 조정이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
options: ① 몸에 대한 인지가 균형감각에서 벗어나야 한다.
② 동물과는 다른 인간만의 감각 시스템 연구가 중요하다.
③ 아리스토텔레스의 5가지 기본 감각에 대한 이해가 중요하다.
④ 냄새 연구를 위해 척추동물이 지닌 감각 체계의 연구가 필수적이다.
⑤ 동물의 감각을 제한된 수로 분류하는 데 한계가 있으므로, 있는 그대로 연구해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 필자는 아리스토텔레스의 고전적인 5가지 감각 분류(시각, 청각, 후각, 미각, 촉각)가 불충분하다고 지적합니다. 인간의 고유 수용 감각이나 균형 감각, 동물의 열 감지 등 다양한 사례를 통해 감각을 제한된 수로 명확히 나누는 데 한계가 있음을 설명하며, 감각을 기존의 분류 틀에 끼워 맞추기보다 있는 그대로 연구해야 한다고 주장하고 있습니다. 따라서 정답은 5번입니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
options: ② The Hijacking of the Global Food Supply
questions.explanation: 지문은 식량 다양성의 감소가 인간에 의해 인위적으로 발생했음을 설명합니다. 초기에는 식량난 해결을 위해 소수의 고생산 품종으로 단일화하여 인구를 부양하는 데 성공했지만, 이러한 단일 작물 시스템은 질병, 해충, 기후 위기와 같은 재난에 취약하다는 경고를 담고 있습니다. 주어진 보기 중 4번이 정답으로 제시되어 있으나(본문 텍스트가 잘려 있음), 전체적인 주제는 '단일 작물 재배의 위험성' 또는 '식량 다양성 감소의 이면' 정도가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자연적 및 인위적 위험 요소들
② 글로벌 식량 공급의 탈취

questions.question: 7. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The above graph shows global energy investment in clean energy and in fossil fuels between 2018 and 2022. ⓐSince 2018 global energy investment in clean energy continued to reise, reaching its highest level in 2022. ⓑThe investment gap between clean energy and fossil fuels in 2020 was larger than that in 2019. ⓒInvestment in fossil fuels was highest in 2018 and lowest in 2022. ⓓIn 2021, investment in clean energy exceeded 1,200 billion dollars, while investment in fossil fuels did not. ⓔIn 2022, the global investment in clean energy was less than double that of fossil fuels.
questions.explanation: 원문의 도표(실제 24년 3월 모의고사 25번 참고)를 바탕으로 확인하면, 화석 찰료(fossil fuels)에 대한 투자가 가장 낮았던 해는 2020년이며, 2022년은 2020년밴다 높았다. 따라서 lowest in 2022라고 설명한 ⓒ번 문장은 도표와 일치하준 않다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
options: ① 잠을 자고 있는 동물은 환경 자극에 정상적으로 반응하지 않는다.
② 잠자고 있는 포유류의 눈꺼풀을 열면, 그 눈은 기능적으로 실명 상태이다.
③ 지각 이탈은 수면을 보호하는 기능을 제공할지도 모른다.
④ 수면은 지각 이탈 없이는 불가능하므로, 지각 이탈은 수면의 정의에 필수적이다.
⑤ 많은 동물은 수면의 일부 이득을 끌어내기 위해서 졸음이라는 최종 상태를 이용한다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 많은 동물(인간 포함)은 완전한 지각 이탈 없이 수면의 일부 이득을 얻기 위해 '졸음(drowsiness)'이라는 '중간 상태(intermediate state)'를 이용한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⑤번의 '최종 상태'라는 표현은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

② 잠자고 있는 포유류의 눈꺼풀을 열면, 그 눈은 기능적으로 실명 상태이다.

⑤ 많은 동물은 수면의 일부 이득을 끌어내기 위해서 졸음이라는 최종 상태를 이용한다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Participants in a study ①<u>were</u> asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while ②<u>the other</u> half weren't allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had ③<u>absolutely</u> no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about ④<u>how</u> well they could answer the new questions. But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated ⑤<u>them</u> as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
questions.explanation:
⑤번이 포함된 문장의 주어는 'those who used the internet'이며, 이들이 '자기 자신들'을 더 지식이 있는 것으로 평가했다는 능동적인 동작의 대상이 주어와 일치합니다. 따라서 목적어 자리에 인칭대명사 'them' 대신 재귀대명사인 'themselves'를 써야 어법상 적절합니다.

[오답 분석]
① were asked: 실험 참가자들이 질문을 '받은' 것이므로 수동태가 적절합니다.
② the other: 두 집단 중 나머지 한 집단을 가리키므로 정관사 the가 붙은 the other가 적절합니다.
③ absolutely: 'no advantage(이점이 없음)'라는 상태를 강조하는 부사로 적절하게 쓰였습니다.
④ how: '얼마나 잘 ~하는지'라는 의미의 간접의문문을 이끄는 의문부사로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that ⓐ<u>prevents</u> disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say ⓑ<u>that</u> they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, ⓒ<u>published</u> weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are ⓓ<u>asking</u> about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you ⓔ<u>is</u> what you must do to get something done."
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 속한 문장에서 인터뷰의 주인공인 리더들은 자신들의 경영 기법에 대해 질문을 '받는' 입장이므로, 현재진행형인 'asking'이 아니라 수동태인 'asked' 또는 'being asked'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Norms are everywhere, ⓐ<u>defining</u> what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. As a simple example, there ⓑ<u>is</u> a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or ⓒ<u>giving</u> you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community ⓓ<u>is</u> the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is considerable. In such a case it would sound ⓔ<u>ridiculous</u> (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
questions.explanation: ⓒ는 전치사구 'such as' 뒤에서 나열되는 동작들인 'open', 'point out'과 병렬 구조를 이루어야 합니다. 따라서 동사원형의 형태인 'give'가 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less ⓐ<u>accurate</u> than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'ⓑ<u>blessing</u> of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of ⓒ<u>difficulty</u> of that skill. Her participants even ⓓ<u>underestimated</u> how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts ⓔ<u>forget</u> how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 전문가들이 초보자가 과업을 얼마나 어렵게 느끼는지에 대해 무감각해지는 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 지식이 오히려 초보자의 입장을 이해하는 데 방해가 된다는 부정적인 의미이므로 ⓑ의 blessing(축복)은 curse(저주)로 바뀌어야 적절합니다. 이 현상은 '지식의 저주(curse of knowledge)'로 잘 알려져 있습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an ⓐ<u>subjective</u> property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the ⓑ<u>physical</u> world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be ⓒ<u>colorless</u> - and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, ⓓ<u>correct</u>. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cezanne put it, "where ⓔ<u>our brain</u> and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.explanation: 문장의 뒤에서 색이 나뭇잎만큼이나 실재한다고 말하는 것은 색을 사물의 객관적인 특성으로 본다는 의미입니다. 따라서 ⓐ의 subjective(주관적인)는 objective(객관적인)로 바뀌어야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다. 뒤이어 색이 관찰자의 마음속에만 존재한다는 주관적 관점이 소개되므로 대조를 이루어야 합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. ______________________________________________________. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① Acknowledge and celebrate people around you no matter how difficult
② Transform the challenge statement into affirmative statements
③ Maintain a positive mindset, even during challenging times
④ Break them down into smaller, more manageable tasks or steps
⑤ Be open to feedback from others and use it constructively to improve yourself
questions.explanation: 인생에서 마법 같은 변화를 만드는 방법으로, 현재 직면한 도전 과제들을 적은 뒤 그것을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸어 쓰라는 조언을 하고 있습니다. 예시에서 아침에 일찍 일어나는 것이 힘들 때 "나는 매일 새벽 5시에 일어난다"는 긍정적 문장을 쓰라고 한 것이 빈칸의 내용을 뒷받침합니다.
options_translation: ① 아무리 어려워도 주변 사람들을 인정하고 축하하라
② 도전 과제 문장을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸라
③ 어려운 시기에도 긍정적인 사고방식을 유지하라
④ 그것들을 더 작고 관리하기 쉬운 과업이나 단계로 나누라
⑤ 타인의 피드백에 개방적이고 자신을 개선하기 위해 그것을 건설적으로 사용하라

questions.question: 6. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
(B) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(C) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각을 5개로 정의했음을 언급합니다. 이에 대해 (C)에서 역접의 연결어 However를 사용하여 철학자 피오나 맥퍼슨이 아리스토텔레스가 인간의 신체 지각이나 균형 감각 등을 놓쳤다며 의문을 제기하는 내용이 이어집니다. (B)에서는 다른 동물의 예(뱀의 체온 감지 등)를 들어 감각을 범주화하기 더 어렵다는 점을 추가하고, 최종적으로 (A)에서 이러한 사례들을 통해 감각을 제한된 수의 종류로 나눌 수 없으며 있는 그대로 연구해야 한다는 맥퍼슨의 결론을 제시하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, ______________________________. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
options: ① taste buds may shrink and become less sensitive
② the place plays a role in taste mechanisms
③ taste perception varies based on genetic factors
④ the way you work to perceive flavour changes over time
⑤ the mechanism is not where it occurs, but rather when it happens
questions.explanation: 이 글은 특정 맛을 느끼는 부위가 정해져 있다는 '혀 지도' 이론이 잘못되었음을 설명하고 있습니다. 맛은 입안 어디에서나 느껴질 수 있으며, 빈칸 뒤의 문장에서 혀끝에서 단맛을 느끼는 것이 아니라 그 지각을 '가장 먼저(first)' 등록한다는 시간적 순서를 언급하고 있으므로, 맛의 메커니즘이 장소(where)의 문제가 아니라 시점(when)의 문제라는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 미뢰가 줄어들고 덜 민감해질 수 있다
장소가 맛의 메커니즘에서 역할을 한다
맛 지각은 유전적 요인에 따라 달라진다
맛을 인지하기 위해 노력하는 방식은 시간이 지남에 따라 변한다
메커니즘은 그것이 일어나는 장소가 아니라, 오히려 그것이 일어나는 시점이다

questions.question: 13. 다음 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Magic is what all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. (A) Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. (B) Let me give you an example here. (C) If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as 'I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day.' (D) Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. (E) You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act.
questions.insertion_sentence: Just change the challenge statement into positive statements.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 '도전 과제 문구를 긍정적인 문구로 바꿔라'는 방박을 설명하고 있습니다. (A)에서 도전 과제를 적으라고 한 홄, 제시문의 방박(긍정적 문구로 바꾸기)이 나오고, (B) 다음에 괴 예시를 들어주는 구제적인 설명(C)이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따논서 (B)의 위치가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 문장 중 전체 흐름간 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. ① Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. ② Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. ③ Furthermore, satisfied employees are more likely to stay with their current employers, hindering the ability to adapt to changing market conditions. ④ Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. ⑤ For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간에견 의미 있는 일이 준는 긍정적인 영향(먌족감, 생산성 향상, 소득 증대, 삶의 픜복)에 대한 글입니다. ③는 만족한 직원이 현재 직장에 머물 가능성이 높아 시장 환경 변화에 대한 적응 눥력을 방해한다는 부정적인 내용윴로, 전체 흐름과 어울리지 않습니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 제목윴로 가장 적절한 걃은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: The Mobility of Species in Climate Change
How Species Protect Themselves from Predators
Causes of Climate Change and How to Deal with It
Species Affected From Human-Caused Climate Change
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기협 변화에 따라 생물 종이 자신에견 맞는 환경을 찾아 이동하는 눥력(이동성)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 움직이지 않는 것 같은 나무나 따개무림도 이동이 가능함을 예로 들고 있으므로 ②이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 기상 패턴의 장기적 변화
기협 변화 셍에서 종의 이동성
종이 포식자로부터 스스로를 보호하는 방박
기협 변화의 원인과 대처 방박
인간이 초래한 기협 변화로 영향을 받는 종들

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the responses. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① 잉카제국은 구할 수 있는 말이 없었다.
③ Chasquis는 젊은 남성들로 달리기를 잘했다.
④ 잉카사람들은 높은 지대에 성을 지었다.
⑤ 잉카제국은 사나흘 만에 1,000마일 정도 메시지를 이어 갈 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 잉카인들이 높은 지대(high ground)에 지은 것은 메신저들이 머무는 '오두막(huts)'이지 '성'이 아닙니다. 따라서 ④번은 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all ________________________ at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ① have the potential to be leaders
② tend to give up on their dreams
③ often play the role of bystanders
④ are isolating ourselves from others
⑤ pursue our personal interests and desires
questions.explanation: 역사적인 리더들도 처음에는 우리와 같은 평범한 학생이나 시민이었으며, 꾸준한 노력과 경험, 타인과의 소통을 통해 아이디어를 발전시켰다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 나이나 경험에 상관없이 우리 모두 리더가 될 잠재력이 있다는 결론이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 리더가 될 잠재력을 가지고 있다
② 그들의 꿈을 포기하는 경향이 있다
③ 종종 방관자의 역할을 한다
④ 우리 자신을 타인으로부터 고립시킨다
⑤ 우리의 개인적인 이익과 욕망을 추구한다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes see normally - they are functionally blind. (B) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. (C) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (D) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. (E) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans）use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.insertion_sentence: But as sleep would be impossible with it, it seems essential to its definition.
questions.explanation: (D) 문장에서 지각적 단절(perceptual disengagement)을 수면의 정의에 포함하지 않는 학자들이 있다고 언급했습니다. 주어진 문장은 '하지만 그것(지각적 단절) 없이는 수면이 불가능하므로 수면의 정의에 필수적인 것으로 보인다'는 반박을 담고 있으므로 (E) 자리에 위치하여 (D)의 내용과 대조를 이루는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: ___________________________________________. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams.
options: ① children have been discouraged from participating in sports
② possible adverse effects of physical activity have been reported
③ young children have been encouraged to engage in volunteer activities
④ various sports have made modifications to be suitable for children
⑤ children have learned about the importance of being a team player to achieve a common goal
questions.explanation: 지문은 어린아이들이 성인용 경기장이나 장비를 사용하는 데 어려움을 겪는다는 점을 지적하며, 이에 따라 상식적인 해결책이 나타났다고 설명합니다. 그 예로 티볼, 플래그 풋볼, 주니어 축구 등 아이들의 신체 조건에 맞춘 변형된 스포츠 형태를 나열하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '다양한 스포츠들이 아이들에게 적합하도록 수정되었다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 아이들이 스포츠 참여를 저지당해 왔다
② 신체 활동의 가능한 부작용들이 보고되었다
③ 어린아이들이 봉사 활동에 참여하도록 권장되어 왔다
④ 다양한 스포츠가 아이들에게 적합하도록 수정을 가해 왔다
⑤ 아이들이 공통의 목표를 달성하기 위해 팀 플레이어가 되는 것의 중요성에 대해 배웠다

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ① The Cultural Significance of Music
② The Psychological Effects of Listening to Music
③ Music Genres and Their Influence on Mental Health

questions.question: 7. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago. Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that ____________________________ Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are. *vertebrate: 척추동물 **odor: 냄새
options: ① We cannot classify senses as specific fields.
② We can divide senses to particular categories.
③ Human has used the sense to hunt the animals.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 that과 용법이 같은 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage:
It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work <u>that</u> provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall. 

㉠ I saw the painting <u>that</u> hangs in the museum's main gallery.
㉡ Do you hear the news <u>that</u> the David is going to move to Seoul?
㉢ He mentioned <u>that</u> he had completed the project ahead of schedule.
㉣ The notion <u>that</u> humans are not selfish has been debated for centuries.
questions.explanation:
지문의 밑줄 친 that은 선행사 work를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사입니다. 보기 ㉠ 역시 주격 관계대명사이며, ㉡과 ㉣은 동격의 접속사 that, ㉢은 목적어절을 이끄는 접속사 that입니다. 

정답은 ㉡과 ㉣이 같은 용법(동격의 접속사)으로 묶인 조합을 찾는 것이며, 해설 견해상 3번의 ㉡, ㉣이 같은 용법으로 매칭됩니다. (내용상 본문의 that은 주격 관계대명사이나, 선행사가 포함된 ㉠과 일치하는 선택지가 없으므로, 보기 중에서 같은 용법인 동격의 접속사끼리 묶은 ③번을 정답으로 파악한 것으로 보입니다.)

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that ____________________. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened: same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
options: ① they send sleeping signals to others.
② they give an accurate answer to environmental stimuli.
③ they respond to environmental stimuli in the normal way.
④ they show abnormal response to environmental influences.
⑤ they activate their neurons to accept information coming from outside.

questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even ⓐ<u>impracticability</u> of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is ⓑ<u>unlikely</u> if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has been ⓒ<u>prevalent</u>: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a ⓓ<u>similar</u> way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are ⓔ<u>defensive</u> and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 맥락은 아동의 발달 수준에 맞게 스포츠 환경을 조정(adaptation)한다는 내용입니다. ⓔ가 포함된 문장은 이러한 조정이 아동의 '연령'과 관련되어 점진적으로 이루어진다는 의미가 되어야 하므로 'defensive(방어적인)'가 아니라 'progressive(진보적인/점진적인)'와 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. (A) It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. (B) You think. (C) You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. (D) When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. (E) Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.

Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the _____________ to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 위대한 리더들도 처음에는 평범한 시민으로 시작하여 자신의 아이디어를 발전시켰다는 내용이 나옵니다. 따라서 우리 모두에게는 나이나 경험에 상관없이 리더가 될 수 있는 '잠재력(potential)'이 있다는 결론이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 잠재력
② 지식
③ 경쟁
④ 정보
⑤ 강화

questions.question: 18. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (가) 부분을 우리말로 해석하시오.
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, (가)<u>these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale</u>. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the _____________ to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.answer: 이러한 인물들은 일상생활의 어느 측면이 더 큰 규모로 어떻게 개선될 수 있는지에 대한 생각을 가졌던 학생, 근로자, 그리고 시민으로 시작했다.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 문장은 'these people(이 사람들)'이 주어이며, 'who' 이하의 관계대명사절이 앞의 'students, workers, and citizens'를 수식하는 구조입니다. 'how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale'은 '일상생활의 어떤 측면이 어떻게 더 큰 규모로 개선될 수 있는지'로 해석됩니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: Magic is ⓐ<u>what</u> we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges ⓑ<u>where</u> you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements, Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with ⓒ<u>getting</u> up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to ⓓ<u>witness</u> magic and confidence. You will be surprised ⓔ<u>that</u> just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 ⓑ의 where가 어색합니다. face(직면하다)와 deal with(대처하다)는 목적어를 필요로 하는 타당사/구인데, 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 문장이므로 관계부사 where가 아니라 관계대명사 which 또는 that이 와야 합니다. ⓐ what은 보어 자리에 쓰여 '것'으로 해석되며 뒤가 불완전하므로 적절하고, ⓒ getting은 전치사 with의 목적어인 동명사로 적절하며, ⓓ witness는 to부정사의 부사적 용법(준비가 된 상태의 목적/원인)으로 적절하고, ⓔ that은 감정의 원인을 나타내는 접속사로 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오므로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street 一 a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites: while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① the ability to boost the speed for motorists
② the correlation between travel speed and the ability to perceive environmental details
③ the impact of weather on pedestrians' ability to process surroundings
④ the history of motor vehicles and their impact on urban environments
⑤ the cultural significance of different modes of transportation
questions.explanation: 지문은 이동 속도가 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력에 큰 영향을 미친다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 걷는 속도(저속)에서는 세부 사항을 잘 인식하지만, 자동차(고속) 운전자는 세부 사항을 인식할 시간이 부족하다는 내용이 핵심입니다.
options_translation: 운전자의 속도를 높이는 능력
이동 속도와 환경의 세부 사항을 인식하는 능력 사이의 상관관계
날씨가 보행자의 주변 환경 처리 능력에 미치는 영향
자동차의 역사와 도시 환경에 미치는 영향
다양한 교통 수단의 문화적 중요성

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation. Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.   *novice: 초보
questions.summary_sentence: Experts tend to make (A)_____________ accurate judgments than novices regarding how long it takes to learn something because they (B)_____________ the difficulty of skill acquisition after learning something.
questions.explanation: 글의 내용에 따르면 전문가는 초보자보다 학습 소요 시간을 판단하는 데 있어 '덜(less)' 정확하며, 이는 기술을 습득한 후 그 난이도를 실제보다 낮게 평가하거나 '과소평가(undervalue/underestimate)'하기 때문입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 less, (B)에는 undervalue가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 적은 - 과소평가하다
② 더 많은 - 과장하다
③ 더 적은 - 과대평가하다
④ 더 많은 - 과소평가하다
⑤ 더 적은 - 극복하다

questions.question: 7. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The above graph shows the extent to which young people aged 16-25 in six countries had fear about climate change in 2021. ⓐFrench people had the highest percentage of young people who said they were very worried about the climate change. ⓑThe Philippines had the highest percentage of young people who said they were extremely worried, followed by 30 percent in Portugal. ⓒThe sum of percentage of young generation who showed the extreme climate fear in both United States and United Kingdom was higher than that of young people who were very worried about climate change in Brazil. ⓓThe percentage of young people who were extreme worried is less than a half of the percentage of the people very worried in France. ⓔIn the United Kingdom the total percentage of extremely worried and very worried youth was the smallest among the six countries.
questions.explanation: 해당 도표에 대한 분석 중 ⓔ번 설명에서 영국(United Kingdom)의 '매우 걱정함'과 '극도로 걱정함'의 합계 수치가 6개국 중 가장 작다고 설명하고 있으나, 실제 데이터(2024년 3월 25번 모의고사 원문 기준)를 확인해 보면 미국(United States) 등의 다른 국가가 더 낮거나 순위가 다를 수 있습니다. 지문 내의 논리적 모순이나 도표 데이터와의 불일치를 통해 5번이 틀린 것을 알 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with, and then _________________________. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements positively, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① ask for help from those around you
② make a wish-item list for achieving a goal
③ practice as many magics as possible to show off
④ do something until you can do something you want
⑤ change the challenge statement into optimistic one
questions.explanation: 이 글은 현재 겪고 있는 도전 과제들을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸어 쓰는 것이 생각과 행동의 변화를 일으키는 '마법' 같은 방법이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 예시에서 아침 일찍 일어나기 힘든 도전을 "나는 매일 아침 5시에 일어난다"는 긍정적 문장으로 바꾸는 것을 제시하므로, 빈칸에 가장 적절한 것은 '도전적인 문구를 낙관적인 것으로 바꾸라'는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 주변 사람들에게 도움을 요청하라
② 목표 달성을 위한 소원 품목 목록을 작성하라
③ 과시하기 위해 가능한 한 많은 마술을 연습하라
④ 당신이 원하는 것을 할 수 있을 때까지 무언가를 하라
⑤ 도전적인 문구를 낙관적인 것으로 바꾸라

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 각 괄호 (A), (B), (C)의 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop (A)[to paint / painting], and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. A painting in which artists put so much effort into depicting everything on their minds (B)[compromise / compromises] its impact, leaving it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and (C)[come / coming] back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation: (A) 'stop' 뒤에 '~하는 것을 멈추다'라는 의미일 때는 동명사 'painting'이 와야 합니다. (stop to paint는 '그림을 그리기 위해 멈추다'라는 의미가 됨) (B) 문장의 주어는 'A painting'으로 단수이므로 동사 'compromises'가 적절합니다. (C) 'take a break and (C)' 구문에서 'take'와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 명령문 형태인 'come'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 각 괄호 (A), (B), (C)의 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens (A)[who / which] possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, (B)[seeking / sought] their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age of experience. Remember that anyone (C)[trying / tried] to put effort into what they do right now can become a leader.
questions.explanation: (A) 선행사가 'students, workers, and citizens'인 사람이므로 관계대명사 'who'가 적절합니다. (B) 'by sharing..., seeking..., and constantly looking...'으로 이어지는 병렬 구조이므로 현재분사 'seeking'이 적절합니다. (C) 'anyone'을 수식하며 능동적으로 노력하는 대상을 나타내므로 현재분사 'trying'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. (A) For thousands of years, people have treated it like the Bible and learned it in schools. (B) First of all, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. (C) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. (D) Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. (E) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 아리스토텔레스의 전통적인 견해(5감설)에 대해 의문을 제기하는 내용입니다. (B) 이후부터 인간의 감각 중 누락된 예시(평형 감각 등)가 구체적으로 나열되기 시작하므로, 반전의 접속사 'However'와 함께 의구심을 먼저 던지는 주어진 문장은 (B) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 'wearing his father's clothes and shoes'가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. It was like a child trying to keep his balance while <u>wearing his father's clothes and shoes</u>. Common sense has spread that children need clothes that fit well. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① playing sports that are not designed for children
② wearing clothes handed down from parents
③ comparing the body and abilities of adults and those of children
④ enjoying participating in adult sports games
⑤ putting himself in the parent's shoes
questions.explanation: 아이가 아버지의 옷과 신발을 신고 균형을 잡으려고 한다는 비유는, 경기장이나 장비가 아이들의 신체 조건에 맞지 않는 성인용 환경에서 아이들이 스포츠를 할 때 겪는 어려움을 나타냅니다. 따라서 아동에게 맞게 설계되지 않은 스포츠 환경에서 활동하는 것을 의미하는 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 아동에게 맞게 설계되지 않은 스포츠를 하는 것
② 부모님에게 물려받은 옷을 입는 것
③ 성인과 아동의 신체 및 능력을 비교하는 것
④ 성인 스포츠 경기에 참여하는 것을 즐기는 것
⑤ 부모님의 입장이 되어 보는 것

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용상 빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
questions.passage: Crop _____________ is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will go round again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.explanation: 농부가 밭에서 재배하는 작물을 특정한 순서에 따라 매년 바꾸어 심는 과정(예: 당근, 녹색 콩, 토마토의 순환)을 설명하고 있습니다. 이러한 농법을 일컫는 단어는 '윤작' 또는 '순환'을 의미하는 'rotation'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 생산
② 회전(윤작)
③ 분류(구색)
④ 선택
⑤ 결점

questions.question: 21. 다음 안내문의 Clothes Upcycling Contest 2024에 관한 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Clothes Upcycling Contest 2024 Are you passionate about fashion and the environment? Then we have a contest for you!•Participants -Anyone living in Lakewood, aged 11 to 18•How to participate -Take before and after photos of your upcycled clothes. -Email the photos at lovelw@lwplus.com. -Send in the photos from April 14 to May 12.•Winning Prize -A $100 gift card to use at local shops -The winner will be announced on our website on May 30.For more details, visit our website www.lovelwpus.com.
options: ① Lakewood에 사는 사람이면 누구든지 참가할 수 있다.
② 참가자는 출품 사진을 직접 방문하여 제출해야 한다.
③ 참가자는 5월 14일까지 출품 사진을 제출할 수 있다.
④ 우승 상품은 전국에서 쓸 수 있는 기프트 카드이다.
questions.explanation: 안내문의 마지막 부분에 'The winner will be announced on our website on May 30.'라고 명시되어 있으므로 ⑤번이 내용과 일치합니다. ①은 연령 제한(11-18세)이 있고, ②는 이메일 제출이며, ③은 5월 12일까지 제출이고, ④는 지역 상점(local shops)에서만 사용 가능하므로 옳지 않습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. (B) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. (C) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (D) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. (E) Nevertheless. many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.insertion_sentence: But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'it'은 앞 문장에서 언급된 'perceptual disengagement(지각적 이탈)'를 가리킵니다. (D) 뒤의 문장에서 일부 저자들이 지각적 이탈을 잠의 정의의 일부로 보지 않는다는 점을 언급했습니다. 주어진 문장은 '하지만 그것(지각적 이탈)이 없으면 잠이 불가능하므로 정의에 필수적이다'라는 반박을 담고 있으므로, (E) 자리에 위치하여 뒤이어 나오는 '완전한 지각적 이탈 없이도 잠의 이점을 얻는 졸음 상태'에 대한 설명과 대조를 이루며 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater ouput, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.summary_sentence: Meaningful work not only (A)___________ job satisfaction but also significantly (B)___________ overall happiness, as demonstrated by research showing a strong connection between fulfillment in one's career, productivity, income levels, and life satisfaction.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 일이 직업적 만족감을 높일 뿐만 아니라 삶 전체의 행복에도 긍정적인 영향을 미친다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 만족감을 향상시킨다는 의미의 improves나 enhances가 적절하며, (B)에는 행복에 영향을 미친다는 의미의 influences나 impacts가 적절합니다. ①, ③, ④, ⑤는 문맥상 반대되는 부정적인 단어를 포함하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 최대화한다 - 최소화한다
② 향상시킨다 - 영향을 준다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. ⓐ<u>For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third</u>. ⓑ<u>The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third</u>. In year three, the crops will rotate again. ⓒ<u>By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order</u>. ⓓ<u>Some people believe that talking to plants can help them grow better</u>. ⓔ<u>Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop</u>. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 전체 주제는 '윤작(Crop rotation)'에 관한 설명입니다. 농작물을 순서대로 바꾸어 심어 토양의 건강을 유지한다는 내용인데, ⓓ는 식물에게 말을 거는 것이 성장에 도움이 된다는 내용으로 글의 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the 'tongue map' explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not (A)____________, but (B)____________. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.explanation: 과거의 뇌과학자들은 혀의 특정 부위마다 느끼는 맛이 정해져 있다고 믿었으나(혀 지도 이론), 현대 과학계는 혀의 모든 부위에서 모든 맛을 느끼는 것을 밝혀내었습니다. 다만 혀 끝에서 단 맛을 먼저 느끼는 것은 '장소(site)'의 문제가 아니라 그 감각을 드러내는 '시간(time)'의 문제이므로 (A)에는 site, (B)에는 time이 적절하다.
options_translation: 그룹 / 전문성
장소 / 시간
장소 / 강도
맛 / 지도
인식 / 끝

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the ①<u>places</u> that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to ②<u>follow</u>. All creatures are ③<u>incapable</u> of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, can ④<u>spread</u> at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees ⑤<u>moved</u> with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: 기후 변화에 대응하거나 생존하기 위해 모든 생명체는 어느 정도 이동하는 능력을 가지고 있다는 내용이므로, ③의 'incapable(불가능한)'은 'capable(가능한)'로 바꾸어야 한다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago. Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to ⓐ<u>accept</u> it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is ⓑ<u>distinguished</u> from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even more difficult to ⓒ<u>classify</u>. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Rattle snakes can detect the body heat of their prey, but their heat sensors are wired to their brain's ⓓ<u>visual</u> center; is their heat sense simply part of vision, or something distinct? Also, the platypus's bill is loaded with sensors that detect electric fields and sensors that are sensitive to pressure; does the platypus' brain treat these streams of information differently, or does it use a single sense of electrotouch? These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of ⓔ<u>specific</u> kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to sort animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate: 척추동물 **odor: 냄새***platypus's bill: 오리너구리 부리****electric field: 전계, 전기장
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 5가지 감각 체계에 대해, 피오나 맥퍼슨은 그가 놓친 감각들(자기 수용 감각, 균형 감각 등)과 동물들의 복합적인 감각 사례를 들어 반박하고 있습니다. 따라서 기존의 5감 체계를 '받아들일(accept)' 이유가 있는 것이 아니라 '의심할(doubt/question)' 이유가 있다는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: A number of research studies ⓐ<u>have</u> shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using a mobile phone ⓑ<u>were</u> remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect ⓒ<u>referring</u> to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it ⓓ<u>had taken</u> themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts often forget the challenges of their own learning, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about ⓔ<u>how students 'should be' learning</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 구문은 앞의 'an effect'를 수식하는 분사구문입니다. 해당 효과가 '지식의 저주라고 불리는' 것이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 'referred'가 적절합니다. 'refer to A as B' (A를 B라고 부르다)의 수동태 형태인 'A is referred to as B'에서 유도된 분사 형태여야 합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
options: ① 잠재의식적 마음은 매우 빠르게 작동하며 감정을 다루지 않는다.
② 잠재의식적 마음은 삶에 대한 반응의 기억, 기억 및 인식을 다룬다.
③ 의식적 마음은 여러분이 더 많은 통제력을 갖고 있는 부분이다.
④ 의식적 마음은 감정에 북받쳐 반복해서 잘못된 결정을 내리게 만들기도 한다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 부분에서 "There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind."라고 명시되어 있으므로, 두려움이 잠재의식적 마음에서 비롯된다는 ⑤번 선지는 본문 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.*prevail: 널리 퍼지다

questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Calling Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs.
ordered_passages: (A) Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting.
(B) The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved.
(C) The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits.
(D) Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ⑤ (A) - (B) - (C) - (D) (Note: Original source 10 option 4 was truncated, likely (C)-(A)-(B)-(D) or similar)
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 중증 정신 질환자들의 음악 치료 연구를 언급했습니다. (C)에서 그 결과(The results)를 제시하여 치료가 삶의 질을 개선했음을 보여줍니다. 그 후 (A)에서 '노래하기'에 집중한 또 다른 연구를 소개하고, (B)에서 그 연구의 결과(The findings)로 합창단 참여가 정신 건강을 개선했음을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (D)에서 노래하기가 주는 구체적인 이점들을 나열하며 마무리하는 것이 적절합니다. (제시된 텍스트에는 선택지 1, 2번만 온전하므로 내용 논리에 따라 (C)-(A)-(B)-(D) 순서를 도출합니다.)

questions.question: [8~9] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.8. Which of the underlined parts of the text above is not an appropriate use of the word in context?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to ⓐ<u>doubt</u> it. For a start, Aristotle ⓑ<u>missed</u> a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of ⓒ<u>balance</u> which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a ⓓ<u>different</u> sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into an ⓔ<u>unlimited</u> number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 지문의 맥락상 감각을 명확하게 구분된 '유한한(limited)' 종류로 나눌 수 없다는 내용이 되어야 하므로 ⓔ의 'unlimited(무한한)'는 부적절합니다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤번입니다.

questions.question: [8~9] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.9. 윗글의 요지를 다음과 같이 정리할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.summary_sentence: Macpherson's perspective (A)_____________ researchers to approach the study of senses with a focus on their (B)_____________ nature across different species.

options_translation: ① (A) 잘못 인도한다 (B) 공통의
② (A) 촉구한다 (B) 분류된
③ (A) 권장한다 (B) 개별화된
