questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally-they are functionally blind. (A) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. (B) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (C) But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. (D) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)이 수면 보호 기능을 하므로 일부 저자들은 이를 수면의 정의에 포함하지 않는다'는 내용입니다. (C) 뒤의 문장이 '하지만 그것(지각적 이탈) 없이는 수면이 불가능하므로, 그것은 수면의 정의에 필수적인 것으로 보인다'는 역접의 내용을 담고 있으므로, (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings-work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. ⓐThose who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energyizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. ⓑMeanwhile, the standards and levels of satisfaction associated with meaningful work differ across various communities and societies. ⓒSonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. ⓓThose most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. ⓔResearcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 일이 인간의 행복과 삶의 질에 미치는 긍정적인 영향에 대해 다루고 있습니다. ⓑ 문장은 의미 있는 일에 대한 만족도의 기준이 사회마다 다르다는 내용으로, 전체적인 흐름인 '의미 있는 일의 중요성과 혜택'에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements 一 ⓐ<u>what</u> degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places ⓑ<u>that</u> satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, ⓒ<u>are</u> capable of dispersal at some stage of their life 一 as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born 一 often ⓓ<u>occupied</u> by its parent 一 to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees ⓔ<u>move</u> with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장은 'past periods(과거 기간)'에 일어난 일을 설명하고 있으므로, 동사 move는 과거형인 moved가 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field.
ordered_passages: (A) Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session.

(B) For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones.

(C) Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill.

(D) Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 전문가가 초밴자에게 새로운 분야림 설명할 때 겪는 어려움에 대한 것입니다. (B)에서 휴대폰 사용 전문가와 초밴자의 예시림 통해 구체적으로 시작합니다. (C)에서는 이림 '지식의 저주'라 부르며 전문가가 과제의 난이도림 과소평가한다는 실험 결과림 설명합니다. (A)는 (C)의 Dr. Hinds의 실험 참가자들에 대한 추가 설명이며, (D)는 이러한 현상을 통해 우리가 배우는 사람의 관점에서 바라봐야 한다는 결론을 내립니다. 따논서 (B)-(C)-(A)-(D)가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고, 학생들이 나눈 대화로 글의 내용을 잘못 이해한 학생은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① 학생 A: 사람이 이동하는 속도의 빠르기는 환경 속 세부사항을 처리하는 능력에 의해 결정돼.
② 학생 B: 윗글은 진화론적 관점을 함께 언급하고 있어.
③ 학생 C: 자전거 탄 사람은 보행자보다 환경 속 세부사항을 구별하는 능력이 떨어져.
④ 학생 D: 그래서 이동 중 세부사항을 구별하는 우리의 능력은 대략 시속 5마일의 속도에 이상적으로 맞추어져 있다고 볼 수 있지.
⑤ 학생 E: 시속 50km 자동차 운전자가 시속 5km 자전거 탑승자보다 이동 중 세세한 것을 더 많이 놓치겠지.
questions.explanation: 지문의 첫 문장에 따르면 '이동 속도가 세부사항 처리 능력을 결정한다'고 되어 있습니다. 학생 A는 인과관계를 반대로 설명하여 '속도가 능력에 의해 결정된다'고 말했으므로 틀린 설명입니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find ⓐ<u>it</u> difficult to know when to stop painting, and ⓑ<u>it</u> can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. ⓒ<u>It</u> is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave ⓓ<u>itself</u> looking overworked. If you find ⓔ<u>yourself</u> struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation: ⓓ의 문장 주어는 'Putting too much into a painting'이라는 동명사구입니다. leave의 목적어는 '그 그림(the painting)'을 의미하므로 주어와 목적어가 같지 않습니다. 따라서 재귀대명사 itself 대신 일반 목적격 대명사인 it으로 써야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. Which of the underlined parts of the text below is not an appropriate use of the word in context? [24년 3월 32번]
questions.passage: A ⓐ<u>respectable</u> boss wouldn't say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that ⓑ<u>prevents</u> disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are ⓒ<u>pro-disagreement</u>. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the ⓓ<u>featured</u> leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually ⓔ<u>discourage</u> internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
questions.explanation: 문맥상 리더들은 자신들이 반대 의견에 찬성하며(pro-disagreement), 내부의 저항이나 이견을 장려한다고 주장해야 합니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 discourage(낙담시키다, 막다)는 encourage(권장하다)와 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 22번]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus ________________________________ at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ① a notable leader lives a sacrificial life
② we all have the potential to think critically
③ all of us possess the capacity to be leaders
④ anyone who is diligent can achieve economic success
⑤ leaders should demonstrate resilience in critical moments
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 리더들도 처음에는 평범한 학생, 노동자, 시민으로 시작했으며, 아이디어를 개선하고 공유하는 과정을 통해 목표를 달성했음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 나이나 경험에 상관없이 우리 모두가 리더가 될 능력을 갖추고 있다는 결론이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 주목할 만한 리더는 희생적인 삶을 산다
② 우리 모두는 비판적으로 생각할 잠재력이 있다
③ 우리 모두는 리더가 될 능력을 갖추고 있다
④ 성실한 사람은 누구나 경제적 성공을 거둘 수 있다
⑤ 리더는 결정적인 순간에 회복 탄력성을 보여주어야 한다

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically ⓐ<u>spread</u> <u>out</u> during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business ⓑ<u>to develop</u> closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver ⓒ<u>what</u> customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was ⓓ<u>no longer</u> possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view ⓔ<u>which</u> production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
questions.explanation: ⑤번의 which는 뒤에 완전한 문장(production would create its own demand)이 이어지고 있으므로, 앞의 명사 the view와 동격을 이루는 접속사 that으로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓐ spread out은 과거분사로 형용사 역할을 하며, ⓑ forced A to B 구문으로 to develop이 적절합니다. ⓒ what은 목적어 역할을 하는 관계대명사이며, ⓓ no longer는 '더 이상 ~않다'는 의미로 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic ⓐ<u>projected onto</u> animals is that they can talk in human language. Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often ⓑ<u>deformed</u> in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with ⓒ<u>humanlike</u> facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in an ⓓ<u>unnatural</u> way. However, despite this tendency to express the animals in their original form, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them ⓔ<u>enlarged</u> and deformed childlike features.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 뒤에 이어지는 'original form(원래 형태)'으로 동물을 표현하는 경향에 대해 설명하고 있으므로, ⓓ unnatural(부자연스러운)은 'natural(자연스러운)' 또는 동물의 원래 모습에 가까운 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 밑줄 친 Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: <u>Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut</u>. f you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. he danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're stuck. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying ─ but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
options: ① Success guarantees constant growth and moving forward.
② Success leads to immediate dissatisfaction and the need for change.
③ Following your intended path ensures success without any obstacles.
④ Achieving success always encourages people to stay on their intended path.
⑤ Success can result in being stuck in a routine that feels safe, but lacks excitement.
questions.explanation: 성공이 당신을 의도한 길에서 벗어나 편안한 틀(rut)에 박히게 할 수 있다는 말은, 보상이 좋고 편안하지만 더 이상 즐겁지 않거나 성장이 없는 상태에 안주하게 되어 빠져나오기 힘든 상황을 의미합니다. 따라서 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 성공은 끊임없는 성장과 전진을 보장한다.
② 성공은 즉각적인 불만족과 변화의 필요성으로 이어진다.
③ 의도한 길을 따르는 것은 장애물 없는 성공을 보장한다.
④ 성공을 거두는 것은 항상 사람들이 의도한 길에 머물도록 장려한다.
⑤ 성공은 안전하게 느껴지지만 활력이 부족한 일상에 갇히는 결과를 초래할 수 있다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. (A) So work on it. (B) Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. (C) There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. (D) There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. (E) So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.insertion_sentence: Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 과업을 가용 시간에 맞추는 것에 주의를 기울이라는 내용입니다. (C) 뒤부터는 상당한 시간이 필요한 과업과 짧은 시간에 할 수 있는 과업을 구분하여 시간을 배정하는 구체적인 방법이 나오므로, (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run.
ordered_passages: (A) Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an evolutionary principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster.(B) While running, Alice comes to discover that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place."(C) In this case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to thrive and pass on their genes. Even though they might run, the two species just stay in place.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 앨리스와 붉은 여왕이 달리기 시작한 후, (B)에서 아무리 달려도 제자리라는 것을 발견하고 붉은 여왕이 '제자리에 머물기 위해 온 힘을 다해 달려야 한다'고 설명합니다. (A)에서는 생물학자들이 이 일화를 바탕으로 진화적 원리(붉은 여왕 효과)를 설명하며 여우와 토끼의 예를 도입합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 여우 역시 토끼를 잡기 위해 빨라져야 하는 경쟁 상황을 설명하며, 두 종 모두 달려야만 제자리를 유지한다는 결론으로 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body.
options: ① principles of carbohydrates' maintaining their shapes
② effective procedures to reduce bad carbohydrate contents
③ contrasts between complex and simple carbohydrates
④ reasons why you should avoid carbohydrate consumption
⑤ necessity of eating an appropriate amount of carbohydrates
questions.explanation: 이 글은 복합 탄수화물(Complex carbohydrates)과 단순 당질인 나쁜 탄수화물(Bad carbohydrates/simple sugars)의 특성을 대조하고 있습니다. 복합 탄수화물은 분해 속도가 느려 영양소를 지속적으로 공급하는 반면, 단순 탄수화물은 분해가 빨라 지방으로 축적되기 쉽다는 차이점을 설명하고 있으므로 주제는 복합 탄수화물과 단순 탄수화물의 대조가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 탄수화물이 형태를 유지하는 원리
② 나쁜 탄수화물 함량을 줄이는 효과적인 절차
③ 복합 탄수화물과 단순 탄수화물의 대조
④ 탄수화물 섭취를 피해야 하는 이유
⑤ 적절한 양의 탄수화물 섭취의 필요성

questions.question: 7. 윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Chess masters (A)[showing / shown] a chess board in the middle of a game for 5 seconds with 20 to 30 pieces still in play can immediately reproduce the position of the pieces from memory. Beginners, of course, are able to place only a few. Now take the same pieces and place them on the board randomly and the difference is much reduced. The expert's advantage is only for familiar patterns ─ those previously stored in memory. Faced with unfamiliar patterns, even when it involves the same familiar domain, the expert's advantage disappears. The beneficial effects of familiar structure on memory (B)[has / have] been observed for many types of expertise, including music. People with musical training can reproduce short sequences of musical notation more accurately than (C)[that / those] with no musical training when notes follow conventional sequences, but the advantage is much reduced when the notes are ordered randomly. Expertise also improves memory for sequences of movements. Experienced ballet dancers are able to repeat longer sequences of steps than less experienced dancers, and they can repeat a sequence of steps making up a routine better than steps ordered randomly. In each case, memory range is increased by the ability to recognize familiar sequences and patterns.
questions.explanation: (A) 분사구문으로, 체스 마스터가 체스판을 '보여졌을 때(수동)'를 의미하므로 과거분사인 'shown'이 적절합니다. (B) 문장의 주어는 'The beneficial effects'(복수)이므로 복수 동사인 'have'가 적절합니다. (C) 앞에 나온 'People with musical training'과 대조되는 '음악 훈련을 받지 않은 사람들'을 의미하므로 복수 명사 People을 대신하는 부정대명사 'those'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글을 읽고 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (가), (나)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.summary_sentence: Experts in various domains, such as chess, music, and dance, (가)__________________ for (나)__________________ within their respective fields.
options: ① (가) display excellent memory - (나) familiar patterns and sequences
② (가) show impressive thinking skills - (나) uncommon strategies
③ (가) have significant mental capacity - (나) randomized musical sequences
④ (가) are good at complex problem-solving - (나) unpredictable game positions
⑤ (가) possess remarkable intelligence - (나) unfamiliar geographic sequences
questions.explanation: 본문은 체스, 음악, 무용 분야의 전문가들이 각자의 분야에서 익숙한 패턴이나 순서를 접할 때 훨씬 뛰어난 기억력을 발휘한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 (가)에는 '뛰어난 기억력을 보여준다'가, (나)에는 '친숙한 패턴과 순서'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 뛰어난 기억력을 보여준다 - 친숙한 패턴과 순서
② 인상적인 사고 능력을 보여준다 - 흔치 않은 전략
③ 상당한 정신적 능력을 가지고 있다 - 무작위화된 음악 순서
④ 복잡한 문제 해결에 능숙하다 - 예측 불가능한 게임 위치
⑤ 놀라운 지능을 소유하고 있다 - 낯선 지리적 순서

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, which is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way that production could be made more efficient, known as the "division of labor." (A) Making most manufactured goods involves several different processes using different skills. (B) Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished. (C) One worker could do all these tasks, and make 20 pins in a day. (D) Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. (E) Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day ─ a huge increase in productivity from the 200 they would have produced before.
questions.insertion_sentence: But you can think of a more efficient way than the one just mentioned, in which the work is divided into its separate processes, with each worker performing one task.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 앞서 언급된 방식(한 노동자가 모든 일을 하는 방식)보다 더 효율적인 방식인 '분업'에 대해 설명하기 시작하는 문장입니다. (C) 앞까지는 한 명의 노동자가 모든 공정을 수행하여 하루에 20개의 핀을 만드는 비효율적인 상황을 설명하고 있으며, (D) 다음부터는 각 노동자가 한 가지 작업에 특화되어 속도가 빨라지고 생산성이 증대되는 분업의 효과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '앞서 언급된 것보다 더 효율적인 방식'인 분업을 도입하는 문장은 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it).
ordered_passages: (A) They do so because they have a good understanding of two characteristics of advertisements; the first feature is that advertisements are paid to just tell the "good side", and the other feature is that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
(B) You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business.
(C) Therefore, customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 구매 후 행동을 이해하는 것의 중요성을 언급합니다. (B)는 구매자가 타인에게 구매를 권장할지 여부와 만족한 고객이 '무급 대사'가 될 수 있음을 설명하며 자연스럽게 이어집니다. (C)는 고객 만족이 우선순위가 되어야 하는 이유로 사람들이 아는 사람의 의견을 신뢰한다는 점을 제시합니다. (A)의 'They do so'는 (C)의 사람들이 광고보다 친구를 신뢰하는 이유를 설명하며 글을 마무리합니다. 따라서 (B)-(C)-(A)가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy ⓐ<u>boosts</u> sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, ⓑ<u>to offer</u> Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to ⓒ<u>either</u> four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, ⓓ<u>whereas</u> in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor ⓔ<u>did</u> it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장에서 nor 뒤에 도치가 일어났는데, it(실험)이 실험실에서 '열린' 것이므로 수동태가 되어야 합니다. 또한 held는 hold의 과거분사형이므로 조동사 did가 아닌 be동사 was가 쓰여 nor was it held... 형식이 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy ⓐ<u>boosts</u> sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, ⓑ<u>to offer</u> Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to ⓒ<u>either</u> four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, ⓓ<u>whereas</u> in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor ⓔ<u>did</u> it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
options: ① 할인된 수프는 세 가지 조건 중 하나의 조건으로 판매되었다.
② 위 실험의 결과는 희소성이 판매를 장려한다는 것을 보여주는 것이다.
③ 구매량에 제한이 없는 대조군에서는 구매자들이 평균 3.3캔을 구매했다.
④ 고객들이 12개의 캔만 구매할 수 있는 한 실험군에서 구매자는 평균 5.3캔을 구입했다.
⑤ Brian 교수는 세 슈퍼마켓이 수프를 원가격보다 10센트가 할인된 가격으로 제공하도록 했다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 5.3캔은 '제한이 있는 두 가지 실험군(4캔 또는 12캔 제한)'을 통합한 평균치이며, 특정 실험군(12캔 실험군)에서의 단독 결과로 명시되지 않았습니다. 지문은 'scarce condition(희소 조건)' 전체의 평균이 5.3캔이라고 기술하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements - from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so ___________________________________________. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
options: ① the nerve cells of the sensory organs have unpredictable mobility
② the economic system works by interacting with the consumer's sensory organs
③ the law signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons
④ high-tech trains run as fast as their sensors detect and process various stimuli simultaneously
questions.explanation: 글 전체가 뇌의 작동 방식을 도시의 경제 시스템에 비유하고 있습니다. 기차가 도시로 재료를 가져오듯, 감각 기관으로부터 온 가공되지 않은 신호들이 뉴런이라는 고속도로를 통해 전달되어 뇌에서 처리된다는 맥락이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 '감각 기관의 신호들이 뉴런의 초고속도로를 따라 수송된다'는 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 감각 기관의 신경 세포는 예측할 수 없는 이동성을 가진다
② 경제 시스템은 소비자의 감각 기관과 상호작용함으로써 작동한다
③ 감각 기관으로부터의 가공되지 않은 신호들이 뉴런이라는 초고속도로를 따라 수송된다
④ 최첨단 기차는 센서가 다양한 자극을 동시에 감지하고 처리하는 것만큼 빠르게 달린다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have ⓐ<u>fewer</u> questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The ⓑ<u>decline</u> in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far more ⓒ<u>efficient</u> than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly ⓓ<u>disordered</u>. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are ⓔ<u>pruned away</u>.
questions.explanation: 유아의 뇌는 신경 연결은 훨씬 많지만 배선이 엉망(a mess)이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 성인의 뇌에 비해 연결망이 '효율적(efficient)'이기보다는 '비효율적(inefficient)'이라고 해야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. ⓐThey do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. ⓑIf a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. ⓒIn this way, he develops his own analytical and cognitive skills required to achieve the social aims related to public interests. ⓓThinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. ⓔSimilarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 칭찬이 아이의 자아 존중감 형성에 미치는 영향에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 아이가 부모의 말을 그대로 믿어 긍정적인 자아 이미지를 형성한다는 내용이 이어지는데, ⓒ의 '공공의 이익과 관련된 사회적 목표 달성을 위한 분석적 기술을 발달시킨다'는 내용은 글의 핵심 주제와 무관합니다.

questions.question: 19. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." ⓐ<u>Unless</u> we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad. There are, however, combinations of foods ⓑ<u>where</u> add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. ⓒ<u>Even though</u> all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but ⓓ<u>otherwise</u> stays away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with ⓔ<u>few</u> vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 combinations of foods를 선행사로 하고 뒤에 동사 add up이 이어지는 주격 관계대명사가 필요합니다. where는 관계부사이므로 뒤에 완전한 절이 와야 하는데, 여기서는 주어가 빠진 불완전한 절이 오므로 관계대명사 that 또는 which로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." ⓐ<u>Unless</u> we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad. There are, however, combinations of foods ⓑ<u>where</u> add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. ⓒ<u>Even though</u> all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but ⓓ<u>otherwise</u> stays away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with ⓔ<u>few</u> vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
options: ① Not Good or Bad Food But a Healthful or Unhealthful Diet!
② How Does Food Rich in Essential Nutrients Affect Human Bodies?
③ Why Are Human Bodies Not Free from Over-Nutrition?
④ Let Home-Made Meals Be Central to All the Menus
⑤ The More You Have Nutrient-Rich Food, The Longer You Love!
questions.explanation: 이 글은 개별 식품을 '좋은 음식'과 '나쁜 음식'으로 이분법적으로 나누는 것이 아니라, 전체적인 식단의 조합이 건강한지 혹은 건강하지 않은지가 중요하다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 ① '좋거나 나쁜 음식이 아니라 건강한 혹은 건강하지 않은 식단!'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 좋거나 나쁜 음식이 아니라 건강한 혹은 건강하지 않은 식단!
② 필수 영양소가 풍부한 음식이 인체에 어떤 영향을 미치는가?
③ 왜 인체는 과다 영양으로부터 자유롭지 못한가?
④ 모든 메뉴의 중심에 집밥이 있게 하라
⑤ 영양이 풍부한 음식을 더 많이 먹을수록 더 오래 사랑한다!

questions.question: 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 알맞은 말을 글의 흐름과 제시된 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: People who fly across several time zones often suffer from jet lag, which is the feeling of fatigue and disorientation. To (A)____________________, it's recommended to adjust your internal clock to the new time zone as quickly as possible. This means staying awake until the local bedtime and getting exposure to natural light during the day. In sports, travel between time zones can also (B)____________________, as athletes may not be at their physical peak due to the disruption of their circadian rhythms.
subjective_conditions: 본문에 있는 표현을 활용할 수 있음 (단어 형태는 필요시 변형 가능)
(A), (B) 각각 띄어쓰기 기준 10개 이하의 영어 단어로 쓸 것
questions.answer:
(A): overcome jet lag
(B): have an effect on the performance of sports teams
questions.explanation:
(A) 시차증(jet lag)의 피로감과 혼란을 해결한다는 문맥이므로 'overcome jet lag(시차증을 극복하다)'이 적절합니다.
(B) 운동 경기에서 시간대 간의 이동이 선수들의 컨디션에 영향을 미친다는 맥락이므로 'have an effect on the performance of sports teams(스포츠 팀의 성과에 영향을 미치다)'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓒ 중, 어법상 어색한 한 단어라 포함된 문장을 선택하여, 그 어색한 단어를 (A)에 작성하고, 이를 바르게 고친 것을 (B)에 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. ⓐ<u>Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were seldom sufficient to support a full-time chief or village council</u>. The development of agriculture changed work patterns considerably. Early farmers could reap 3-10 kg of grain from each 1 kg of seed planted. Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided more support for nonfarmers such as chieftains, village councils, men who practice medicine, priests, and warriors. ⓑ<u>In return, the nonfarmers provided both leadership and security for the farming people, enabling it to continue to increase food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses</u>. With improved technology and favorable conditions, agriculture produced consistent surpluses of the basic necessities, and population groups grew in size. These groups concentrated in towns and cities, and human tasks specialized further. ⓒ<u>Specialists such as carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their specialized skills and became more efficient in their use of time and energy</u>. The goods and services they provided brought about an improved quality of life, a higher standard of living, and, for most societies, increased stability.
questions.explanation: 문장 ⓑ에서 enabling의 목적어는 앞에 나온 'the farming people'을 가리킵니다. people은 복수 취급하므로 대명사 it이 아니라 them으로 써야 문법적으로 옳습니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글을 다음과 같이 요약하였다. 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 알맞은 단어를 제시된 <조건>에 맞게 각각 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Early hunter-gatherer societies had minimal structure. A chief or group of elders usually led the camp or village. ⓐ<u>Most of these leaders had to hunt and gather along with the other members because the surpluses of food and other vital resources were seldom sufficient to support a full-time chief or village council</u>. The development of agriculture changed work patterns considerably. Early farmers could reap 3-10 kg of grain from each 1 kg of seed planted. Part of this food/energy surplus was returned to the community and provided more support for nonfarmers such as chieftains, village councils, men who practice medicine, priests, and warriors. ⓑ<u>In return, the nonfarmers provided both leadership and security for the farming people, enabling it to continue to increase food/energy yields and provide ever larger surpluses</u>. With improved technology and favorable conditions, agriculture produced consistent surpluses of the basic necessities, and population groups grew in size. These groups concentrated in towns and cities, and human tasks specialized further. ⓒ<u>Specialists such as carpenters, blacksmiths, merchants, traders, and sailors developed their specialized skills and became more efficient in their use of time and energy</u>. The goods and services they provided brought about an improved quality of life, a higher standard of living, and, for most societies, increased stability.
questions.summary_sentence: The development of (A)____________ made it possible for people to produce (B)____________, which allowed them to live in larger groups and (C)____________.
subjective_conditions: 본문에 있는 표현만을 활용하여 쓸 것. (단어 형태는 필요시 변형 가능)
각각 띄어쓰기 기준 2개 단어 이하로 작성할 것.
questions.explanation: 지문은 농업의 발달이 식량 잉여를 가져왔고, 이로 인해 인구가 도시로 집중되며 직업이 전문화되었다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 농업(agriculture), (B)에는 일관된 잉여(consistent surpluses), (C)에는 더 전문화되었다(specialized further)가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, especially their mental health, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ① 가창이 작곡보다 더 효과적인 집단 음악치료 방법이다.
② 집단 음악치료의 효과는 심리학자들의 예상을 뛰어넘는다.
③ 환자들의 삶의 질 개선을 위해 집단 음악치료 연구를 개발해야 한다.
④ 집단 소속감 형성을 위해 집단 가창에 참여하는 비율이 증가하고 있다.
⑤ 집단 음악치료와 집단 가창은 정신 질환 환자들의 정신건강에 긍정적인 영향을 미친다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 중증 정신 질환을 앓고 있는 개인들을 대상으로 한 연구를 인용하며, 집단 음악 치료(노래 부르기, 작곡 등)와 집단 가창(합창단 참여)이 참가자들의 삶의 질, 특히 정신 건강과 웰빙에 긍정적인 영향을 미치고 자신감과 소속감을 높여준다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 요지로는 5번이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first. After all, you don't feel the exact taste of food depending on the location of the taste shown on the 'tongue map'.
options: ① a correlation between the tongue and the taste buds
② the importance of the taste buds in tasting
③ the difference in personal time in taste
④ a misconception of how tastes are perceived
⑤ a tongue map used to accurately distinguish tastes
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거에 널리 알려졌던 '혀 지도(tongue map)'가 사실은 잘못된 해석과 번역에서 비롯된 오류임을 설명하고 있습니다. 실제로는 혀의 모든 부위에서 모든 맛을 느낄 수 있으며, 맛을 느끼는 데는 위치보다 시간이 더 중요하다는 점을 강조합니다. 따라서 주제는 '맛이 어떻게 인지되는지에 대한 오해'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 혀와 미뢰 사이의 상관관계
② 맛을 느끼는 데 있어 미뢰의 중요성
③ 맛 인지에 있어서의 개인적 시간 차이
④ 맛이 인지되는 방식에 대한 오해
⑤ 맛을 정확하게 구별하기 위해 사용되는 혀 지도

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 Chasquis에 관한 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers, called Chasquis, were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. They lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 ㎞) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① 말을 타고 왕의 명령과 보고를 전달하는 잉카 제국의 전령들이었다.
② 1마일에서 2마일 간격으로 떨어져 배치된 오두막에서 생활했다.
③ 젊은 남자와 여자들로 구성되었고, 특히 잘 달리는 이들이었다.
④ 잉카 사람들은 서로를 볼 수 있는 낮은 지대에 오두막을 지었다.
⑤ 잉카 제국은 사정이 좋으면 하루에 1,000마일 정도 메시지를 이어 갈 수 있었다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'They lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads.'라고 명시되어 있으므로 2번이 일치합니다. 1번은 'on foot'이므로 틀렸고, 3번은 'all young men'이라 했으므로 틀렸으며, 4번은 'huts on high ground'이므로 틀렸고, 5번은 '1,000 miles ... in three or four days'이므로 틀렸습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones demonstrated significantly ⓐ<u>lower</u> accuracy compared to novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to challenges that ⓑ<u>beginners</u> face when dealing with a task, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people ⓒ<u>acquired</u> the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even overestimated how they themselves acquired that skill with ⓓ<u>great</u> effort in an earlier session. Knowing that experts may ⓔ<u>overlook</u> how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: '지식의 저주'의 맥락상, 전문가들은 자신이 과거에 그 기술을 습득할 때 들였던 노력을 과소평가(underestimate)해야 합니다. 문맥상 그들이 들였던 노력을 아주 적은(little) 것으로 과대평가(실제보다 쉽게 생각)했다는 흐름이 되어야 하므로 'great'는 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have been made ____________ for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: 성인용 경기장이나 장비가 아이들에게 너무 크고 무겁다는 문제점을 인식하여, 아이들의 체격과 연령에 맞게 경기 방식과 장비를 조정했다는 내용입니다. 따라서 아이들에게 '적절하게(suitable)' 만들어졌다는 표현이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 부담스러운
② 교육적인
③ 불필요한
④ 인기 있는
⑤ 적절한

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. (A) It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. (B) You think; You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because ─ fueled by emotions ─ you make the wrong decisions time and time again. (C) When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. (D) Whether you're scared of spiders or the dark, there are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. (E) They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)이 우리가 더 많은 제어권을 가진 부분이라는 역접의 내용을 담고 있습니다. 앞부분에서 잠재의식(subconscious mind)의 특징과 기능을 설명한 후, (B) 위치부터는 우리가 생각하고 선택할 수 있는 의식적인 마음의 통제력과 그에 따른 결정 과정을 서술하고 있습니다. 따라서 대조를 나타내는 'However'와 함께 의식적인 마음으로 화제를 전환하는 내용이 (B)에 오는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things being likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.summary_sentence: Children tend to (A)_____________ the praise they're given from their parents both in their behavior and in their self-image since they sincerely believe what they hear as they're cognitively (B)_____________.
questions.explanation: 인지적으로 아직 정교하지 못한 아이들은 부모님이 하는 말을 깊이 믿고 이를 그대로 받아들이는 경향이 있습니다. 따라서 부모님의 칭찬을 자신의 자아상과 행동에 '반영하며(mirror)', 이는 그들이 인지적으로 '미성숙하기(immature)' 때문이라는 내용으로 요약할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 반영하다 / 미성숙한
② 무시하다 / 아이 같은
③ 반영하다 / 발달한
④ 무시하다 / 성숙한
⑤ 방지하다 / 정교한

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 표현을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.↓⁍ Title   The Impact of Scarcity on Sale⁍ Material  Campbell's soup on sale at three supermarkets in Sioux City⁍ Control group  Consumers have (A)_____________ condition on the volume of purchases.⁍ Experimental groups  Consumers are (B)_____________ to buying four or twelve cans.⁍ Conclusion  (C)_______________________________________.
subjective_conditions:  본문에서 찾아서 그대로 쓸 것
 1단어로 작성할 것
questions.explanation: (A) 대조군(Control group)은 구매량에 제한이 없는 상태였으므로 본문의 'unlimited condition'에서 'unlimited'를 추출합니다.(B) 실험군(Experimental groups)은 4캔 또는 12캔으로 구매가 제한되었으므로 본문의 'limited to'에서 'limited'를 추출합니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 빈칸 (C)를 <보기>의 표현을 <조건>에 맞게 배열하여 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.↓⁍ Title   The Impact of Scarcity on Sale⁍ Material  Campbell's soup on sale at three supermarkets in Sioux City⁍ Control group  Consumers have (A)_____________ condition on the volume of purchases.⁍ Experimental groups  Consumers are (B)_____________ to buying four or twelve cans.⁍ Conclusion  (C)_______________________________________.
subjective_conditions:  <보기>의 표현을 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
 필요시 어법에 맞게 단어를 변형할 것
vocabulary_box: product sales / in the number of / by consumers / encourage / restriction / purchase / goods
questions.answer: Restriction in the number of goods purchased by consumers encourages product sales.
questions.explanation: 지문의 결론인 '희소성이 판매를 장려한다(Scarcity encourages sales)'를 보기에 주어진 단어들을 활용하여 상세하게 서술하는 문항입니다. '소비자에 의해 구매되는 제품 수의 제한이 제품 판매를 장려한다'는 의미가 되도록 'Restriction (in the number of goods purchased by consumers) encourages product sales' 구조로 배열하며, 주어가 Restriction(단수)이므로 encourage를 encourages로 변형합니다.

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 21번]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(B) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristeliam buckets, we should study them for what they are.

(C) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.
questions.explanation: 제시된 글에서 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물의 감각이 5개라고 주장한 내용을 소개합니다. (C)에서 'However'를 통해 그 주장에 대한 의구심을 제기하며 인간에게서 누락된 감각(균형 등)을 언급합니다. (A)에서는 'Other animals'를 언급하며 인간뿐 아니라 동물의 특수한 감각 사례를 제시합니다. (B)에서 앞의 사례들('These examples')을 요약하며 감각을 제한된 수로 나눌 수 없다는 맥락으로 결론을 맺습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally ⓐ<u>processed</u> as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli ⓑ<u>is</u> registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep ⓒ<u>itself</u>. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems ⓓ<u>essential</u> to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness ⓔ<u>to derive</u> some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 Stimuli인데, 이는 stimulus의 복수형입니다. 따라서 단수 동사인 is가 아니라 복수 동사인 are가 쓰여야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to _____________________________________. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.*litter: (한 배에서 태어난) 새끼들
options: ① have them get used to the rescue center
② respond all the animals in the same way
③ satisfy the particular demands of the animal
④ deal with emotions rather than physical illness
⑤ train the animals to mingle with the other animals
questions.explanation: 글의 앞부분에서 동물마다 개체적 특성, 환경, 질병의 종류에 따라 치료에 대한 반응이 다르다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 모든 치료 세션은 다르게 탐색되어야 하며, 각 치료는 '해당 동물의 특별한 요구사항을 충족시키도록' 조정되어야 한다는 결론이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그들을 구조 센터에 익숙해지게 하도록
② 모든 동물에게 똑같은 방식으로 반응하도록
③ 그 동물의 특별한 요구사항을 충족시키도록
④ 신체적 질병보다는 감정을 다루도록
⑤ 동물들이 다른 동물들과 어울리도록 훈련시키도록

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.*numerous: 수많은
options: ① 성과 중심의 직무 태도는 개인의 행복과 반비례한다.
② 불안정한 고용 시장에서는 만족할 줄 아는 자세가 필요하다.
③ 직장에서 느끼는 보람은 인생 전반의 만족도에 영향을 준다.
④ 직장인에게 수행 업무의 종류는 높은 소득보다 더욱 중요한 요인이다.
⑤ 적성에 맞추기보다는 자부심과 즐거움을 느낄 수 있는 직업을 골라야 한다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 직업에서 의미와 보람을 찾는 것이 인간에게 얼마나 중요한지 설명하고 있습니다. 직장에서 충족감을 느끼는 사람들이 더 높은 성과를 내고 소득도 높을 뿐만 아니라, 삶 전반에 걸쳐 더 행복할 가능성이 크다는 연구 결과를 인용하며 결론을 내리고 있습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.*barnacle: 따개비 **dispersal: 분산 ***fossil: 화석
options: ① Why Is Climate Change Critical to Cultural Heritage?
② Climate Change: What Makes Seemingly Immovable Species Move
③ The Crucial Role of Soil Biodiversity in Sustaining Life of Trees
④ The Biology of Human Survival: Life and Death in Extreme Environments
⑤ Planting Tress May Not Be as Good for the Climate as You Think
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후가 변할 때 생물종들이 생존을 위해 그들의 기후 요구사항을 충족하는 곳으로 이동해야 함을 설명합니다. 나무나 따개비처럼 움직이지 못하는 것처럼 보이는 생물들도 씨앗이나 유충의 형태로 이동한다는 점을 강조하며, 기후 변화가 겉보기에 정적인 생물들조차 이동하게 만든다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 ②번 '기후 변화: 겉보기에 움직일 수 없는 종들을 움직이게 만드는 것'이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 기후 변화는 문화 유산에 중요한가?
② 기후 변화: 겉보기에 움직일 수 없는 종들을 움직이게 만드는 것
③ 나무의 생명을 유지하는 데 있어 토양 생물 다양성의 결정적 역할
④ 인간 생존의 생물학: 극한 환경에서의 삶과 죽음
⑤ 나무를 심는 것이 당신이 생각하는 것만큼 기후에 좋지 않을 수도 있다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 전체 흠름과 관계없눔 문장은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. ⓐCommon sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. ⓑFor examples, junior soccer greatly helps relieve children's stress and promotes teamwork. ⓒEach sport typically offers junior formats tailored for children, featuring shorter game durations and frequently smaller team sizes. ⓓIn a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. ⓔThe adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 아동들이 성인용 슬포츠 환경에서 경기하는 걃의 어려움을 인식하고, 장비나 경기장 규모, 경기 방식 등을 아동의 신체 조건에 맞게 조정(변형)하고 있다는 내용입니다. ⓑ은 주니어 촕구가 스트레스 해서와 팀워크에 도움을 준다는 정서적, 사회적 이점을 말하고 있어, 물리적 환경 조정이라는 전체 흠름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."*dissent: 반대
options: ① importance of encouraging dissent and diverse viewpoints within an organization
② emphasis on avoiding conflicts and disagreements within organizational leadership
③ significance of maintaining a hierarchical structure within an organization
④ value of strict conformity and uniformity in organizational leadership practices
⑤ benefits of silencing dissenting voices to maintain smooth operations within an organization
questions.explanation: 지문은 훌륭한 리더들이 조직 내에서 반대 의견이나 비판적인 목소리를 장려한다는 점을 강조합니다. 특히 마지막 문장에서 반대하는 사람들의 말을 경청함으로써 무엇을 해야 할지 알 수 있다는 내용이 나오므로 주제는 조직 내 반대와 다양한 관점을 장려하는 것의 중요성입니다.
options_translation: ① 조직 내에서 반대와 다양한 관점을 장려하는 것의 중요성
② 조직 리더십 내에서 갈등과 불일치를 피하는 것에 대한 강조
③ 조직 내에서 위계 구조를 유지하는 것의 중요성
④ 조직 리더십 관행에서 엄격한 순응과 획일성의 가치
⑤ 원활한 운영을 유지하기 위해 반대 목소리를 침묵시키는 것의 이점

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the '(A)<u>curse of knowledge</u>'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.*novice: 초보
options: ① Experts underestimate their own proficiency in tasks within their field.
② Newcomers struggle to grasp complex concepts presented by experts.
③ Knowledgeable individuals are more likely to make errors in judgment.
④ Beginners possess a natural advantage in learning new skills quickly.
⑤ Professionals find it hard to understand the struggles of beginners due to their high skill level.
questions.explanation: (A) '지식의 저주'란 전문가가 어떤 일을 배우는 것이 얼마나 어려운지를 잊어버리고, 초보자가 느끼는 난이도를 과소평가하는 현상을 말합니다. 따라서 전문가들이 높은 숙련도 때문에 초보자의 고충을 이해하기 어려워한다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 전문가들은 자신의 분야 내 업무에서 자신의 능력을 과소평가한다.
② 신입자들은 전문가가 제시한 복잡한 개념을 파악하는 데 어려움을 겪는다.
③ 지식이 풍부한 개인일수록 판단 착오를 일으킬 가능성이 더 높다.
④ 초보자들은 새로운 기술을 빠르게 배우는 데 타고난 이점을 가지고 있다.
⑤ 전문가들은 자신의 높은 기술 수준 때문에 초보자의 고충을 이해하기 어렵다고 느낀다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
options: ① 과거에는 혀의 끝에는 신맛, 측면에는 단맛, 그리고 입의 뒤쪽에는 쓴맛이 있었다고 알려졌다.
② 혀 짇는 1800년대 후반 독일에서 수행된 연구를 오해하고 오역한 것으로 밝혀졌다.
③ 오늘날의 미각 연구자는 미뢰가 맛을 느끼는 특화된 분야에 따라 분류된다고 믿는다.
④ 단맛, 짠맛, 쓴맛 그리고 신맛은 입안 어디에서나 느낄 수 있다.
⑤ 혀에서 가장 강하게 느끼는 맛은 매운맛이며 이는 혀의 중간에서 느낀다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth'라고 명시되어 있으므로 4번이 일치합니다. 1번은 단맛과 신맛의 위치가 바뀌었으며, 2번은 20세기 초(turn of the twentieth century) 연구이고, 3번은 미뢰가 특화된 분야에 따라 분류되지 않는다고 했으며, 5번 매운맛에 대한 언급은 없습니다.

questions.question: 25. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서를 알파벳 기호로 적으시오. [3.1점]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr.
ordered_passages: (A) But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale.
(B) If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal.
(C) Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.*diligence: 근면
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 리더의 예시로 링컨과 킹 목사를 언급했습니다. (B)에서 '이러한 개인들(these individuals)'의 영향력을 고려하면 리더십이 숭고하고 높은 목표처럼 보일 수 있다고 설명합니다. (A)에서 '하지만(But)' 그들도 우리처럼 평범한 학생, 노동자 등으로 시작했다는 전환이 일어나고, (C)에서 결론적으로(Thus) 우리 모두 리더가 될 잠재력이 있다고 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(D)가 가리키는 대상이 무엇인지 각각 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Marilyn and her three-year-old daughter, Sarah, took a trip to the beach, where Sarah built her first sandcastle. Moments later, an enormous wave destroyed Sarah's castle. In response to the loss of (A)<u>her</u> sandcastle, tears streamed down Sarah's cheeks and her heart was broken. She ran to Marilyn, saying (B)<u>she</u> would never build a sandcastle again. Marilyn said, "Part of the joy of building a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give (C)<u>it</u> as a gift to the ocean." Sarah loved this idea and responded with enthusiasm to the idea of building another castle ─ this time, even closer to the water so the ocean would get (D)<u>it</u>s gift sooner!
questions.explanation: (A) 'her sandcastle'에서 her는 모래성을 만든 Sarah를 가리킵니다. (B) 'she would never build'에서 다시는 모래성을 쌓지 않겠다고 말한 주체는 Sarah입니다. (C) 'give it as a gift'에서 it은 앞서 언급된 sandcastle(모래성)을 의미합니다. (D) 'its gift'에서 선물(모래성)을 받는 대상은 바다이므로 its는 the ocean을 가리킵니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 도표를 보고 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 단어를 각각 작성하시오.
questions.passage: The above graph shows the extent to which young people aged 16-25 in six countries had fear about climate change in 2021. The Philippines had the highest percentage of young people who said they were extremely or very worried, at 84 percent, followed by 67 percent in (A)_________. More than 60 percent of young people in Portugal said they were extremely worried or very worried. In France, the percentage of young people who were extremely worried was (B)_________ than that of young people who were very worried. In the United Kingdom, the percentage of young generation who said that they were very worried was (C)_________ percent. In the United States, the total percentage of extremely worried and very worried youth was the (D)_________ among the six countries.
questions.explanation: 원문 모의고사 도표 데이터에 근거하여 작성합니다. (A) 필리핀(84%) 다음으로 높은 67%를 기록한 국가는 브라질(Brazil)입니다. (B) 프랑스에서 '매우 걱정하는(extremely worried)' 비율은 '상당히 걱정하는(very worried)' 비율보다 낮았으므로 lower가 적절합니다. (C) 영국에서 '상당히 걱정하는(very worried)' 비율은 도표상 29%입니다. (D) 미국은 합계 수치가 6개국 중 가장 작았으므로 smallest, least, 또는 lowest가 들어갑니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① why drivers should yield to pedestrians
② the beneficial effects of running on your body
③ a brief history of the evolution of transportation over time
④ important things to consider when choosing a travel destination
⑤ the impact of travel speed on human perception of environmental detail
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력에 어떤 영향을 미치는지 설명하고 있습니다. 인간의 감각은 걷기 속도(시속 5마일 이하)에 맞춰져 있어, 속도가 빠른 운전자는 세부 사항을 파악하기 어렵지만, 느린 보행자는 환경적 세부 사항을 감상할 수 있다는 내용이므로 '이동 속도가 환경 세부 사항에 대한 인간의 인지에 미치는 영향'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 운전자가 보행자에게 양보해야 하는 이유
② 달리기가 신체에 미치는 유익한 효과
③ 시간에 따른 운송 수단 진화의 간략한 역사
④ 여행 목적지를 선택할 때 고려해야 할 중요한 사항들
⑤ 이동 속도가 환경 세부 사항에 대한 인간의 인지에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to deliver products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best­selling T­model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ① Limitations of Customer Satisfaction Management
② Effects of Uncertainty on Demand and Production
③ How Do You Make People Aware of Your brand?
④ The Role of Customer Loyalty in Driving Business Growth
⑤ Customer-Centered Business: A Changing Views on Selling
questions.explanation: 과거에는 생산이 수요를 창출한다는 관점이 지배적이었으나, 1940년대와 50년대를 거치며 사회가 현대화됨에 따라 고객의 요구를 충족시키는 것이 비즈니스의 핵심이 되었다는 내용입니다. 즉, 판매에 대한 관점이 고객 중심으로 변화했음을 다루고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 고객 만족 경영의 한계
② 불확실성이 수요와 생산에 미치는 영향
③ 사람들에게 당신의 브랜드를 어떻게 인식시키는가?
④ 비즈니스 성장을 이끄는 데 있어 고객 충성도의 역할
⑤ 고객 중심 비즈니스: 판매에 대한 변화하는 관점

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: If you want the confidence ⓐ<u>that</u> comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Overoptimism about ⓑ<u>what</u> can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and ⓒ<u>to learn</u> by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to ⓓ<u>fitting</u> the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period ⓔ<u>available</u>. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.explanation: ⓒ번은 앞의 명령문 'Make a practice~'와 등윔 접속사 and로 병곬 구조를 이루어야 하는 자리입니다. 따라서 to learn을 명령문 형태인 learn으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 각 괄호 (A), (B), (C)의 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience (A)[disadvantages / advantages] when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become (B)[insensitive / sensitive] to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr. Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts don' (C)[remember / forget] how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: (A) 전문가가 초밴자에게 어떤 분야림 소개할 때, 초밴자의 입장을 잘 이해하지 못하는 '지식의 저주'림 경험하므로 disadvantages(불이익)가 적절합니다.(B) 전문가는 초밴자에게 과업이 얼마나 어려운지에 대해 insensitive(무감각한)해질 수 있습니다.(C) 전문가들이 자신들이 배우는 걃이 얼마나 어려웠는지림 remember(기억하지)못한다는 걃을 알기 때문에 학생의 관점에서 바라붼 필요가 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 불이익 / 무감각한 / 기억하다
② 이익 / 무감각한 / 기억하다
③ 불이익 / 물감한 / 잊다
④ 이익 / 물감한 / 기억하다
⑤ 불이익 / 무감각한 / 잊다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 각 괄호 (A), (B), (C)의 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which (A)[accompany / separate from] it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description (B)[including / excluding] the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him (C)[less / more]. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behavior and the relationship which is formed.
questions.explanation: (A) 한 가지 특성을 가지면 구와 accompany(동반하눠) 다른 특성들도 갖게 된다고 생각하는 함정에 대한 글입니다.(B) 학생들을 됐 그룹으로 나눠 한 그룹에게는 'warm'이라는 단어림 including(포함한) 설명을 제공했습니다.(C) 강사가 따뜻할 걃이라고 기대한 학생들은 그와 more(더 많이) 소통하는 경향을 밴였습니다.
options_translation: ① 동반하다 / 제외하다 / 더 적게
② 분리하다 / 포함한 / 더 적게
③ 동반하다 / 포함한 / 더 많이
④ 분리하다 / 제외하다 / 더 많이
⑤ 동반하다 / 포함한 / 더 적게

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. Most often than not, it's good to _________________________________________.
options: ① ignore social evidence you look for
② follow the leads of those around you
③ adopt the practices of a minority of people
④ look for another restaurant instead of waiting
⑤ post product reviews which signal trustworthiness
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 의사결정을 할 때 타인의 행동을 참고하는 '사회적 증거'의 중요성에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 진화론적 관점에서 집단을 따르는 것이 생존에 유리했으므로, 주변 사람들의 행동이나 선택을 따르는 것이 현명한 행동이라는 결론이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 찾는 사회적 증거를 무시하는 것
② 주변 사람들의 주도를 따르는 것
③ 소수의 사람들의 관행을 채택하는 것
④ 기다리는 대신 다른 식당을 찾는 것
⑤ 신뢰성을 나타내는 제품 리뷰를 게시하는 것

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea. (A) Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. (B) Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. (C) We begin with an idea about how the future will be. (D) Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. (E) Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
questions.insertion_sentence: The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 인간이 '똑같은 과정' 세상의 모든 것이 만들어지기 전 마음셍에서 먼저 설계된다는 예시들(중, 자동차, 옷) 다음에, 이를 인간의 '미래' 설계로 확장하는 연결 고리 역할을 합니다. (C) 이후부터는 미래에 대한 생각이 구체화되는 과정을 설명하므로 (C) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings ─ work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. ⓐThose who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. ⓑSonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. ⓒWorkers are most motivated by extrinsic rewards, primarily things like pay, bonuses, promotion and recognition. ⓓThose most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. ⓔFor her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간에게 있어 '의미 있는 일(meaningful work)'이 주는 내적 성취감과 그것이 삶의 전반적인 행복과 생산성에 미치는 긍정적인 영향을 다루고 있습니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ번 문장은 모두 일의 의미와 만족도를 강조하고 있는 반면, ③번(ⓒ) 문장은 보수나 보너스 같은 '외적 보상(extrinsic rewards)'에 의한 동기 부여를 언급하고 있으므로 글의 전체적인 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [23년 3월 23번]
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. ⓐRailways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. ⓑWith the railways came many large hotels. ⓒIn Canada, for example, the new coast­to­coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. ⓓThe development of tourist facilities such as hotels and resorts often leads to deforestation and loss of biodiversity. ⓔLater, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사회 경제적 발전과 교통수단(철도, 항공)의 발달이 관광 산업과 관련 시설(호텔 등)의 성장을 이끌어낸 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. ⓓ문장은 관광 시설의 개발이 초래하는 환경 파괴와 생물 다양성 손실을 언급하고 있어, 관광 산업의 성장 배경을 다루는 전체 흐름에 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 경우는? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Carbohydrates can be broken up into two different groups: simple and complex. Simple carbohydrates comprise what we know as sugars, while complex carbohydrates consist of starches and fiber.
ordered_passages: (A) Simple carbs are much easier for the body to break down and absorb, leading to quicker bursts of energy, while complex carbs take longer to digest, allowing for a more sustained flow of energy over a longer period of time.
(B) Complex carbohydrates are polysaccharides, meaning they contain three or more sugars. The different molecular structures have a huge effect on how the carbs are digested.
(C) The two types of carbs also differ in their molecular structures. Simple carbohydrates comprise just one or two sugars, like fructose, lactose, and sucrose.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 탄수화물을 단순과 박합으로 봄류한 홄, (C)에서 괸들의 봄자 구조 차이를 설명하기 시잡합니다. 이어서 (B)에서 박합 탄수화물의 봄자 구조 특성을 더 자세히 다루고, 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 봄자 구조가 소화 및 에너지 공급 속도에 미치는 영향을 설명하는 것이 가장 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 1. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic.
