ordered_passages: (A) If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence.
(B) You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
(C) Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 현실에서도 마법을 부릴 수 있다고 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 그 비결(trick)로 직면한 도전을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸어 쓰라고 제안한다. (A)에서는 그에 대한 구체적인 예시(아침 일찍 일어나기)를 들고 있으며, (B)에서는 이러한 문장을 쓰는 행위가 가져오는 긍정적인 변화와 효과를 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Dear Ms. Jane Watson, I am John Austin, a science teacher at Crestville High School. (A) Recently I was impressed by the latest book you wrote about the environment. (B) They are big fans of your book, so I'd like to ask you to visit our school and give a special lecture. (C) We can set the date and time to suit your schedule. (D) Having you at our school would be a fantastic experience for the students. (E) We would be very grateful if you could come.Best Regards,John Austin
questions.insertion_sentence: Also my students read your book and had a class discussion about it.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 '또한 내 학생들도 당신의 책을 읽고 토론을 했다'는 내용은 (B) 뒤에 나오는 '그들(They)은 당신의 책의 광팬이다'라는 문장의 They를 지칭할 대상을 제공해야 한다. 따라서 학생들에 대한 언급이 처음 나오는 (B) 위치가 가장 적절하다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Long ago, an old Native American spiritual leader Odawa had a dream. In his dream, Iktomi, the great spirit and searcher of wisdom, ⓐ<u>appeared to</u> him in the form of a spider. Iktomi said, "We all begin our lives as babies, move on to adulthood and then finally come to old age, where we must ⓑ<u>take</u> care of as babies again. In each stage of life, there are good and bad forces. If we listen to the good forces, they will guide us in the right direction. But if we listen to the bad forces, they will lead us the wrong way and may harm us." When Iktomi finished ⓒ<u>speaking</u>, he spun a web and gave it to Odawa. He said to Odawa, "Use this web which is a perfect circle with hole in the center to help your people ⓓ<u>reach</u> their goals. If you believe in the great spirit, the web will catch your good ideas and the bad ⓔ<u>ones</u> will go through the hole." After Odawa woke up, he shared Iktomi's lesson with his people.
questions.explanation: ⓑ의 문맥상 노년기에는 다시 아기처럼 '돌봄을 받아야' 한다는 수동의 의미가 필요합니다. 따라서 take care of는 be taken care of로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. Researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones also conducted a study of 3,000 workers, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.*numerous: 수많은
options: ① Do not overstate the importance of happiness.
② Competitive leaders earn much money from work.
③ The higher income is meaningless in career success.
④ Satisfaction from work tends to lead to a happier life.
⑤ Human beings run after money rather than joy and pride.
questions.explanation: 지문은 업무에서 성취감과 의미를 찾는 사람들이 더 활기찬 하루를 보내며, 업무 성과가 높고 소득도 높을 뿐 아니라 전반적인 삶의 만족도가 훨씬 높다는 연구 결과들을 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 '업무에서의 만족감이 더 행복한 삶으로 이어지는 경향이 있다'는 ④번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 행복의 중요성을 과장하지 마세요.
② 경쟁력 있는 리더들은 업무를 통해 많은 돈을 법니다.
③ 높은 수입은 경력 성공에 있어 무의미합니다.
④ 업무에서의 만족감은 더 행복한 삶으로 이어지는 경향이 있습니다.
⑤ 인간은 기쁨과 자부심보다는 돈을 쫓습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "_________________________ of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.*vertebrate: 척추동물 **odor: 냄새
options: ① Aristotle doubted a limited sense system
② senses need to be considered as balances
③ the sense of touch is similar to the perception
④ senses can be accurately sorted into 5 perceptions
⑤ we can't clearly categorize senses into a limited number
questions.explanation: 아리스토텔레스가 정의한 5개의 감각(시각, 청각, 후각, 미각, 촉각) 외에도 인간에게는 고유 수용성 감각이나 평형 감각이 있고, 동물들에게는 열 감지 등 더 다양한 감각이 존재한다는 예시를 통해 감각을 특정 개수로 제한하여 분류할 수 없음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '감각을 제한된 숫자로 명확하게 분류할 수 없다'는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 아리스토텔레스는 제한된 감각 체계를 의심했습니다
② 감각은 균형으로 간주될 필요가 있습니다
③ 촉각은 지각과 유사합니다
④ 감각은 5가지 지각으로 정확하게 분류될 수 있습니다
⑤ 우리는 감각을 제한된 숫자로 명확하게 분류할 수 없습니다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 봄용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 32번]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."*dissent: 반대
questions.summary_sentence: Most respectable bosses do not prevent disagreeing points of view from being (A)__________ openly, and they cheer up their junior staffers to show (B)__________ opinions which could be called internal protest.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 많은 리더들이 반대 의견을 표면화하는 것을 장려한다는 내용이다. 따라서 (A)에는 반대 의견이 개방적으로 '표현되는(expressed)' 것을 리더들이 막지 아뉤다는 내용이 적절하며, (B)에는 내부 저항이라 불리는 '반대하는(dissenting)' 의견을 보이도록 하급 직원들을 격려한다는 내용이 들어가야 한다.
options_translation: ① 표현된 - 무지한
② 낙담된 - 인영적인
③ 표현된 - 반대하는
④ 제거된 - 무지한
⑤ 낙담된 - 반대하는

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥사ᄂ 낱말의 싿임이 적절하지 아ᄂ은 것은? [24년 3월 34번]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ⓐ<u>worse</u> than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓑ<u>aware</u> of how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓒ<u>underestimate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill and they even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire it. Knowing that experts no longer ⓓ<u>remember</u> how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand that the experts need to put themselves in the position of ⓔ<u>beginners</u> and look at the learning process through beginners' eyes.*novice: 초밴
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전문가가 초밴자에게 무언가림 가림칠 때 겪는 어려움, 즉 '지식의 저주'에 대한 내용이다. 전문가들은 초밴자에게 과업이 얼마나 어려운지림 잘 '모르게' 된다는 내용이 들어가야 하므로, ⓑ의 aware(인식하는)는 unaware(인식하지 못하는)로 고쳐야 한다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ① Every animal has the same pattern in their healing session so they need only one treatment.
② Animals help people treat their family members in a variety of ways.
③ Each animal is unique, and healing sessions should be adjusted to their needs and situation.
④ Animals make a decision on where they live based on their healing sessions.
⑤ Environment determines how animals learn and what they will eat.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물마다 개별적인 특성, 환경, 그리고 질환의 종류가 다르기 때문에 치유 과정에서 서로 다르게 반응하며, 따라서 각 동물의 특정 요구와 상황에 맞게 치유 세션을 조정해야 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 동물은 치유 세션에서 동일한 패턴을 가지므로 단 한 번의 치료만 필요하다.
② 동물들은 사람들이 다양한 방식으로 가족 구성원들을 치료하도록 돕는다.
③ 각 동물은 독특하며, 치유 세션은 그들의 필요와 상황에 맞춰 조정되어야 한다.
④ 동물들은 치유 세션에 근거하여 어디에 살지 결정한다.
⑤ 환경은 동물들이 배우는 방식과 무엇을 먹을지를 결정한다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① The Rise and Fall of the Inca Empire
② The Way to Use Horses in the Inca Empire
③ The History of Building Huts in the Inca Empire
④ The Way to Become a Messenger in the Inca Empire
⑤ Inca Chasquis: The Fast Foot Messengers of Empire Communication
questions.explanation: 지문은 잉카 제국에서 말 없이 도보로 메시지를 전달했던 'Chasquis'라고 불리는 전령들의 운영 방식과 그들의 효율성을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 5번 '잉카의 Chasquis: 제국 통신의 빠른 도보 전령들'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 잉카 제국의 흥망성쇠
② 잉카 제국에서 말을 사용하는 방법
③ 잉카 제국의 오두막 건설 역사
④ 잉카 제국에서 전령이 되는 방법
⑤ 잉카의 Chasquis: 제국 통신의 빠른 도보 전령들

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. ⓐJust as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. ⓑThus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. ⓒAlso, scientific method should be neutral, objective, rational, and as a result, should be able to approve or disapprove the hypothesis. ⓓHowever, too many scientific papers are published yet readers don't understand them. ⓔPublication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심 주제는 '과학적 커뮤니케이션(발표된 논문)은 독자가 이해해야만 완성되는 양방향 과정이다'입니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 논문의 출판이 이해되는 과정의 중요성을 설명하고 있으나, ③번 문장(ⓒ)은 과학적 방법론의 중립성, 객관성, 합리성 및 가설 증명에 대해 말하고 있어 글의 전체 흐름인 '커뮤니케이션의 완결성'과는 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 2. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers.
ordered_passages: (A) This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity.

(B) On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.

(C) Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 문화적 배경이 다른 노동자들과 현지 주민의 상호작용이 생산성을 높일 수 있다는 긍정적인 측면을 언급합니다. (A)에서 'This is only an advantage up to a certain degree'를 통해 이러한 장점이 일정 수준까지만 유효하며, 지나친 다양성은 오히려 생산성을 낮출 수 있다는 한계를 제시합니다. (C)는 다양성이 노동 시장뿐만 아니라 삶의 질(상품 및 서비스의 범위 확대)에도 영향을 미칠 수 있다는 추가적인 긍정적 측면을 언급하고, (B)는 'On the other hand'를 통해 원주민들이 이를 국가 정체성 왜곡으로 받아들일 때의 부정적인 인식과 사회적 갈등의 우려를 설명합니다. 따라서 긍정적 측면의 한계 제시(A) -> 다른 긍정적 영향(C) -> 그에 반대되는 부정적 인식(B) 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. A significant criticism to Monday Morning Quarterbacks is that they tend to focus excessively on what went wrong, often neglecting the positive aspects of successes of an event. (A) This negative viewpoint can create a distorted perception of the event and can be demoralizing for those involved in the actual decision-making process. (B) Acting as a Monday Morning Quarterback can be a significant learning opportunity. (C) It encourages individuals and teams to reflect on past actions and decisions, fostering a culture of continuous improvement. (D) This reflective practice is especially beneficial in organizational contexts, where learning from past experiences is crucial for future success. (E) A balanced view, which acknowledges both the limitations and the strengths of post-event analysis, is essential for making the most of this common yet complex practice.
questions.insertion_sentence: While often criticized in this way, the role of a Monday Morning Quarterback can also be seen in a positive light.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '비판을 받기도 하지만 긍정적인 측면으로도 볼 수 있다'는 내용으로, 글의 흐름이 비판(부정적 측면)에서 긍정적 측면으로 전환되는 시점에 들어가야 합니다. (A) 이전까지는 Monday Morning Quarterback에 대한 비판적 관점(지나친 잘못에 대한 집중, 사기 저하)을 설명하고 있고, (B) 이후부터는 학습 기회, 지속적 개선, 조직 내의 이점 등 긍정적 가치를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 전환점인 (B) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>Many people are afraid of flying in airplanes</u>. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. ⓑ<u>Many potential passengers are so afraid that they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying</u>. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, ⓒ<u>the odds of dying in a car crash is around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash is closer to 1 in 11 million</u>. If you're going to take a risk, ⓓ<u>especially one that could possibly involve your well-being</u>, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. ⓔ<u>Pay attention to the thoughts that you have about taking the risk</u> and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
questions.explanation: ⓒ 문장에서 'the odds of dying in a car crash'의 주어는 복수 명사인 'the odds'입니다. 따라서 이에 대응하는 동사는 단수형 'is'가 아니라 복수형 'are'가 되어야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providing students with relevant texts they will be interested in. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and discovered ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books." The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.
options: ① several causes and treatments of dyslexia
② reasons why dyslexics flip words and letters
③ pros and cons of reading books in various fields
④ ways to avoid dyslexia discrimination in the workplace
⑤ importance of reading a lot of texts in areas of interest
questions.explanation: 이 글은 난독증이 있음에도 불구하고 성공한 사람들의 사례를 통해, 자신의 관심 분야에 대한 글을 읽는 것이 학습과 성취에 얼마나 중요한지를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로는 '관심 분야의 글을 많이 읽는 것의 중요성'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 난독증의 몇 가지 원인과 치료법
② 난독증 환자들이 단어와 글자를 뒤집어 읽는 이유
③ 다양한 분야의 책을 읽는 것의 장단점
④ 직장에서의 난독증 차별을 피하는 방법
⑤ 관심 분야의 텍스트를 많이 읽는 것의 중요성

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation. If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. While the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a (A)[defensive / aggressive] mechanism for the foot. Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that are (B)[stretched / tightened] quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object. Sensory and motor nerves are (C)[irrelevant / connected] to almost all functions in the body - from the beating of the heart to the movement of the gut, sweating and just about everything else.
questions.explanation: (A) 통증은 신체를 보호하기 위한 수단이므로 'defensive(방어적인)'가 적절합니다. (B) 발을 들어 올리기 위해서는 다리 근육이 'tightened(수축된/긴장된)'되어야 합니다. (C) 감각 신경과 운동 신경은 신체의 거의 모든 기능과 'connected(연결된)'되어 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 방어적인 / 늘어난 / 무관한
② 방어적인 / 늘어난 / 연결된
③ 공격적인 / 늘어난 / 무관한
④ 방어적인 / 수축된 / 연결된
⑤ 공격적인 / 수축된 / 연결된

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product such as popcorn and a movie. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. For example, if the demand for cell phones increases, the demand for cell phone chargers might also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Complementary products also _____________________________________. When one product becomes inexpensive, the demand for it and its complement might increase, and vice versa. Why is this so? Because of the law of demand, cost and demand are inversely related. Some of these goods rely on each other, while you might sell others independently.
options: ② have some disadvantages for entrepreneurs
③ operate within price standards and regulations
④ help customers to find a high-quality set of relevant products
⑤ allow managers to make investment decisions to produce new products
questions.explanation: 보완재(complementary good)는 한 제품의 가격이 하락하면 그 제품뿐만 아니라 함께 소비되는 보완재의 수요도 함께 증가하는 특성을 갖습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 문장에서 제품이 저렴해질 때 수요가 늘어난다는 가격과 수요의 역관계(law of demand)를 설명하고 있으므로, 보완재가 '가격 변동에 의존한다'는 내용인 ①번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 가격 변동에 의존한다
② 기업가들에게 몇 가지 불리한 점이 있다
③ 가격 기준과 규제 내에서 작동한다
④ 고객들이 관련 고품질 제품 세트를 찾도록 도와준다
⑤ 경영자들이 신제품 생산을 위한 투자 결정을 내리게 한다

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it ─ you just see the blurred outline of the moving string. Strings vibrating in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. But if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note is heard loud and clear. The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. When the waves reach your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string.
options: ① Guitar: The World's Best Instrument
② What Causes the Strings to Vibrate?
③ Ways to Protect Ear From Loud Noises
④ How Can We Hear a Guitar Make a Sound?
⑤ The Thinner the Guitar String, the Better the Sound
questions.explanation: 기타 줄 자체는 매우 가늘어서 공기를 많이 밀어내지 못해 소리가 거의 나지 않지만, 줄의 진동이 기타 바디의 나무 판으로 전달되어 증폭됨으로써 우리가 소리를 들을 수 있게 되는 과학적 원리를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '우리가 어떻게 기타 소리를 듣게 되는가'를 묻는 ④번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기타: 세계 최고의 악기
② 무엇이 기타 줄을 진동하게 하는가?
③ 시끄러운 소음으로부터 귀를 보호하는 방법
④ 우리는 기타 소리를 어떻게 듣게 되는가?
⑤ 기타 줄이 가늘수록 소리는 더 좋아진다

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders ─ employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task ─ like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds ─ they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration."
options: ① ways to coexist with other animals peacefully on earth
② linguistic tactics to maintain human superiority over animals
③ technical language contributing to the studies of primates
④ necessity of distinguishing humans from other animal species
⑤ negative effects of underestimating animals' cognitive intelligence
questions.explanation: 인간이 동물의 지능이나 행동을 전문적인 용어(예: mouth-to-mouth contact)를 사용하여 '본능'으로 치부하거나 인간의 행동과 분리하려 하는 것은, 인간이 상상의 사다리 꼭대기에서 다른 동물보다 우위에 있음을 유지하기 위한 일종의 '언어적 전략'입니다. Frans de Waal은 이를 '언어적 거세(linguistic castration)'라고 명명하며 비판하고 있으므로, ②번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지구상에서 다른 동물과 평화롭게 공존하는 방법들
② 동물에 대한 인간의 우월성을 유지하기 위한 언어적 전략들
③ 영장류 연구에 기여하는 전문적인 언어
④ 인간을 다른 동물 종들과 구분하려는 것의 필요성
⑤ 동물의 인지 지능을 과소평가하는 것의 부정적인 영향들

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 20번]
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore show your child good examples of life by your action. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
options: ① Watch Out Your Words When Raising Children
② Teach Values Through Actions: Lead by Example
③ Show Your Love to Your Children through Actions
④ Learning Values Through Overhearing, Not Direct Teaching
⑤ Parenting Secrets: Instilling Values in Kids through Words
questions.explanation: 아이들은 부모의 언어적인 가르침보다 부모의 실제 행동과 모범(Leading by example)을 보고 직접 배우며 가치관을 형성합니다. 따라서 자녀에게 올바른 가치를 가르치기 위해서는 부모가 일상생활에서 그 가치를 몸소 실천하는 본보기를 보여야 한다는 내용이므로 ②번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 아이를 키울 때 말실수를 조심하라
② 행동을 통해 가치를 가르쳐라: 솔선수범하여 이끌어라
③ 행동을 통해 자녀에게 사랑을 보여주어라
④ 직접적인 교육이 아닌 곁듣기를 통한 가치 학습
⑤ 자녀 교육의 비결: 말로써 아이들에게 가치를 심어주기

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
options: ① Rocks consist of crystals, with atoms acting as their fundamental components.
② Scientists refer to the various shapes of crystals as habits.
③ Typical shapes found in crystals contain squares, triangles, and hexagons.
④ Extreme temperature conditions are the single reason for the imperfect shapes of crystals.
⑤ One of optimal conditions for observing beautiful displays is when atoms are positioned in the crystal lattice structure.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 결정이 불완전한 모양을 형성하는 이유는 너무 차갑거나 뜨거운 온도 조건뿐만 아니라 충분한 원재료(source material)가 없는 경우도 포함됩니다. 따라서 극단적인 온도 조건이 '유일한(single)' 원인이라는 설명은 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 암석은 결정으로 구성되며, 원자가 그 기본 구성 요소 역할을 한다.
② 과학자들은 결정의 다양한 모양을 '습성(habits)'이라고 부른다.
③ 결정에서 발견되는 전형적인 모양에는 사각형, 삼각형, 육각형이 포함된다.
④ 극단적인 온도 조건은 결정의 불완전한 모양에 대한 유일한 이유이다.
⑤ 아름다운 전시를 관찰하기 위한 최적의 조건 중 하나는 원자들이 결정격자 구조에 위치할 때이다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They may find their sense of security weakened and ①<u>suffered</u> disorientation when their usual routine is interrupted and everything familiar is removed. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. At this stage, their comprehension tends to be quite literal, making ②<u>it</u> difficult for them to imagine a new home and their future room in advance. Young children may have worries such as "Will I continue to be ③<u>myself</u> in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a manner that ④<u>appreciates</u> their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to the formation of a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those ⑤<u>experiencing</u> transition.
questions.explanation: ①번 문장에서 'suffered'는 'find'의 목적보어인 'weakened'와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 합니다. 아이들이 '그들의 안전감이 약화되고 혼란을 겪는 것(disorientation)'을 알게 되는 것이므로, find + 목적어(their sense of security) + 목적보어1(weakened) and 목적보어2(disoriented)의 형태가 되거나, 혹은 weakened와 병렬을 이루어 suffer가 아닌 suffering(분사) 등으로 문맥에 맞게 수정되어야 하나, 원문상 disorientation이라는 명사를 목적어로 취하고 있으므로 suffer(동사 원형/현재분사) 계열이 목적보어로 와야 합니다. 하지만 문맥상 아이들이 disorientation을 '느끼는/경험하는' 능동의 관계이므로 과거분사 suffered는 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that __________________________________. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
options: ① clothes that subtly challenge conventional expectations are favored by people
② most individual choose attire that conforms to expected norms without any exceptions
③ clothes that are popular with the public are the ones that deviate from social norms completely
④ people are likely to admire whatever those who have high social status and competence wear
⑤ people typically prefer clothing that meets their expectations, although there are exceptions to certain jobs
questions.explanation: 본문은 정해진 규범에서 약간 벗어난 옷차림(검은 넥타이 정장에 빨간 나비넥타이, 강의 중 빨간 운동화 등)이 오히려 그 사람의 지위와 능력을 높게 평가하게 만든다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 관습적인 기대를 미묘하게 거스르는 의복이 사람들에게 긍정적으로 받아들여진다는 것을 의미하므로 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 관습적인 기대를 미묘하게 거스르는 옷은 사람들에게 선호된다
② 대부분의 개인은 예외 없이 예상되는 규범에 순응하는 의복을 선택한다
③ 대중에게 인기 있는 옷은 사회적 규범에서 완전히 벗어난 것들이다
④ 사람들은 사회적 지위와 능력이 높은 사람들이 입는 것이라면 무엇이든 감탄하는 경향이 있다
⑤ 비록 특정 직업에 대한 예외는 있지만, 사람들은 보통 자신의 기대를 충족시키는 의류를 선호한다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are. (A) Writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation - these are just a few examples. (B) You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. (C) Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. (D) The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. (E) An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
questions.insertion_sentence: However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '능력이 어떻게 정의되든 간에, 그것이 자기 가치의 유일한 결정 요인이 될 때 문제가 발생한다'는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C)까지는 능력이 정의되는 다양한 방식(지적 능력, 특정 기술, 매력 등)에 대해 나열하고 있으며, (D) 다음 문장부터는 '수행 능력이 사람을 측정하는 유일한 척도가 된다'는 문제 상황의 구체적인 양상을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 개념 정의에서 문제점 제기로 넘어가는 지점인 (D)에 위치하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용을 세 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 38번]
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are minimized. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones ─ one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.summary_sentence: With widespread portable digital technology, individuals employ diverse methods to balance work and life. Some opt to segment their roles to (A)___________ boundary crossings. Others smoothly integrate work and family responsibilities, with the (B)___________ group finding flexible schedules advantageous.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 분리자(segmenters)들은 경계가 교차하는 것을 최소화(minimize)하려 한다고 했으므로 (A)에는 'reduce'가 적절합니다. 또한 유연한 시간표가 잘 맞는 집단은 일과 다른 역할을 더 명확하게 구분하고자 하는 분리자들이므로, 앞서 언급된 전자의 집단(the former)을 가리키는 'former'가 (B)에 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 증가시키다 - 후자
② 줄이다 - 전자
③ 증가시키다 - 전자
④ 줄이다 - 후자
⑤ 유지하다 - 전체

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [23년 9월 22번]
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a mutually ⓐ<u>beneficial</u> agreement. In a one-time negotiation where future interactions are ⓑ<u>likely</u>, this conventional, adversarial approach might serve a purpose. However, such transactions are ⓒ<u>decreasing</u>, because most of us regularly deal with the same people ─ our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and ⓓ<u>cultivate</u> a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only ⓔ<u>desirable</u> result.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 전통적이고 적대적인 협상 방식(win-lose style)이 목적에 부합할 수 있는 경우는 '미래의 상호작용이 없을 것 같은(unlikely)' 일회성 협상에서입니다. 따라서 ⓑ의 likely를 unlikely로 고쳐야 문맥이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Claims that local food production cut greenhouse gas emissions by reducing the burning of transportation fuel are usually not well founded. Transport is the source of only 11 percent of greenhouse gas emissions within the food sector, so reducing the distance that food travels after it leaves the farm is far less important than reducing wasteful energy use on the farm. Food coming from a distance can actually be better for the climate, depending on how it was grown. For example, field-grown tomatoes shipped from Mexico in the winter months will have a smaller carbon footprint than local winter tomatoes grown in a greenhouse. In the United Kingdom, lamb meat that travels 11,000 miles from New Zealand generates only one-quarter the carbon emissions per pound compared to British lamb because farmers in the United Kingdom raise their animals on feed (which must be produced using fossil fuels) rather than on clover pastureland.When food does travel, what matters most is not the distance traveled but the load size. Bulk loads of food can travel halfway around the world by ocean freight with a smaller carbon footprint, per pound delivered, than foods traveling just a short distance but in much smaller loads. For example, 18-wheelers carry much larger loads than pickup trucks so they can move food 100 times as far while burning only one-third as much gas per pound of food delivered.
questions.summary_sentence: (A) C_____ s in the production process and (B) l_____ e are more important than (C) t_____ e to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
subjective_conditions: (A), (B), (C)는 모두 두 단어임.
윗글에 나와 있는 단어들만을 사용할 것.
대소문자는 무관함.
칸 하나에 철자 하나임.
주어진 철자를 포함하여 작성할 것.
questions.answer: (A) carbon emissions (B) load size (C) travel distance
questions.explanation: 글의 요지는 온실가스 감축을 위해서는 단순히 이동 거리를 줄이는 것보다, 생산 방식에 따른 (A) 탄소 배출(carbon emissions)과 한 번에 운송하는 양인 (B) 적재 용량(load size)이 (C) 이동 거리(travel distance)보다 더 큰 영향을 미친다는 것입니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 밑줄 친 Things are not so different in our own time이 의미하는 것을 <조건>에 맞게 한 문장으로 쓰시오. [3.2점]
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us. One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Gobekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up radically remaking the society itself. <u>Things are not so different in our own time</u>.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에서 주어진 표현을 한 번씩만 사용하되, 필요하면 어법에 맞게 변형할 것.
단어를 추가하지 말 것.
questions.subjective_answer_format: → Just as the construction work at Gobekli Tepe transformed society, now ___________________________  _______________________________________________________.
questions.answer: our constructions revolutionize the modern world
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 과거 괴베클리 테페의 건설이 사회를 변화시킨 것처럼 현대에도 우리가 만드는 건축물이나 개발이 사회를 변화시킨다는 의미입니다. 보기의 단어들을 활용하여 '우리의 건설(주어)이 현대 세계를 혁신한다(동사+목적어)'는 의미의 문장을 완성합니다. revolution을 동사 revolutionize로 변형하여 사용해야 합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Dear Professor Sanchez, My name is Ellis Wight, and I'm the director of the Alexandria Science Museum. We are holding a Biology Fair for local middle school students on Saturday, October 28. The goal of the fair is to encourage them to be interested in science through guided experiments. We are looking for college students who can help with the experiments during the event. I am contacting you to ask you to recommend some students from the biology department at your college who you think are qualified for this job. With their help, I'm sure the participants will have a great experience. I look forward to hearing from you soon.Sincerely,Ellis Wight

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① species movement in response to climate change
② the role of trees and barnacles in preventing climate change
questions.explanation: 지문은 기후 변화에 따라 생물 종들이 자신들이 생존할 수 있는 기후 조건을 갖춘 장소로 이동한다는 사실을 설명하고 있습니다. 움직이지 못하는 것처럼 보이는 나무조차도 씨앗 형태로 이동한다는 예시를 들어 모든 생명체의 기후 변화에 따른 이동을 주제로 다루고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 기후 변화에 반응한 종의 이동
② 기후 변화를 예방하는 데 있어서 나무와 따개비의 역할

questions.question: 7. 다음 Clothes Upcycling Contest 2024에 관한 안내문의 ±탄용과 일치하준 않눤 것은?

questions.question: 8. 다음 글에 대한 <보기>의 진술 (A)~(G) 중, 어색한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and ⓐ<u>this</u> is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in ⓑ<u>biases</u> and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
vocabulary_box: (A) The mind has two parts: the conscious mind and the subconscious one.
(B) The subconscious mind acts rapidly and it manages memories - and it doesn't deal with emotions.
(C) You can control the conscious mind: You are able to deal with thoughts as well as emotions.
(D) The underlined ⓐ refers to a thought.
(E) Emotions often influence decisions through the conscious mind, leading to wrong choices repeatedly.
(F) The underlined ⓑ means thoughts which make decisions without being influenced by personal opinions or favors.
(G) Fears of spiders or of the dark only come from the subconscious.
questions.explanation: 어색한 진술은 (D), (F), (G)로 총 3개입니다. (D) ⓐ(this)는 '생각을 이어갈지 아니면 감정을 더할지 선택할 수 있는 의식적 마음의 작용'을 가리킵니다. (F) ⓑ(biases)는 편견을 의미하며, 이는 개인의 의견이나 선호에 의해 '영향을 받는' 사고이므로 '영향을 받지 않는다'는 설명은 틀렸습니다. (G) 지문에 따르면 공포는 잠재의식에 기록될 때 실재가 되지만, 기원은 '의식적 마음(originate in the conscious mind)'이라고 명시되어 있으므로 '잠재의식에서만 온다'는 진술은 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear the poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is time pressure. A 1999 study by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life - which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves. So it is concluded that people in wealthy countries do not _____________________________.
options: ① share their wealth with those in poor countries
② make big money fast despite their high productivity
③ have lower stress levels than those in poor countries
④ become concerned about what will happen in the future
⑤ suffer from diseases related to abnormal hormone patterns
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서는 가난이 스트레스를 유발한다고 하지만, 후반부에서는 부유한 국가들 또한 시간 압박과 빠른 삶의 속도로 인해 스트레스를 받고 건강 문제를 겪는다고 설명합니다. 따라서 부유한 국가의 사람들이 가난한 국가의 사람들보다 스트레스 수준이 낮지 않다는 결론이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 가난한 나라의 사람들과 그들의 부를 공유한다
② 높은 생산성에도 불구하고 빠르게 큰 돈을 벌지 못한다
③ 가난한 나라의 사람들보다 낮은 스트레스 수치를 가지고 있지 않다
④ 미래에 일어날 일에 대해 걱정하게 된다
⑤ 비정상적인 호르몬 패턴과 관련된 질병으로 고통받지 않는다

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 35번]
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, _________________________________. Group signing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ① their choir participation did not relate to their mental illness
② the disadvantages of choir participation varied among them
③ the negative impact on mental illness remained unchanged
④ their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved
⑤ they found it difficult to sing along harmoniously
questions.explanation: 지문은 합창이나 노래 부르기와 같은 그룹 음악 치료가 정신 질환을 앓고 있는 사람들의 삶의 질과 정서적 상태를 개선하고 자신감을 높여준다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 합창 참여 시 그들의 정신 건강과 안녕(wellbeing)이 상당히 개선되었다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그들의 합창 참여는 정신 질환과 관련이 없었다
② 합창 참여의 단점은 그들 사이에서 다양했다
③ 정신 질환에 미치는 부정적인 영향은 변하지 않은 채로 남았다
④ 그들의 정신 건강과 안녕이 상당히 개선되었다
⑤ 그들은 조화롭게 따라 부르는 것이 어렵다는 것을 발견했다

questions.question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [24년 3월 20번]
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. ⓐLet me give you an example here. ⓑIf you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." ⓒMagic tricks require a lot of practice and skill to master, just like any other art form. ⓓOnce you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. ⓔYou will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 '직면한 문제를 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸어 쓰는 행위'가 인생에서 마법 같은 변화를 일으킨다는 것입니다. 하지만 ⓒ 문장은 '마술 기법(Magic tricks)을 익히기 위해서는 많은 연습과 기술이 필요하다'는 실제 마술에 관한 내용이므로, 비유적으로 마법을 언급하는 글의 전체 흐름과 무관합니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. (A) They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. (B) As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. (C) All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. (D) In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. (E) The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.insertion_sentence: Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 여러 스포츠가 아이들을 위해 적응(변화)을 해왔다는 내용을 도입하고 있습니다. (A)까지는 아이들이 성인 규격의 경기장에서 운동하는 것이 왜 어려운지 설명하고 있으며, (B)부터는 그에 대한 구체적인 예시(야구의 T볼, 미식축구의 플래그 풋볼 등)가 나열됩니다. 따라서 일반적인 변화를 선언하는 주어진 문장은 구체적인 예시가 시작되는 (B) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds." Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
(B) Also, other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(C) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.
questions.explanation: 감각의 개수에 대한 아리스토텔레스의 전통적인 견해(5감)를 소개한 도입부 뒤에, (C)에서 Macpherson의 견해를 빌려 아리스토텔레스가 놓친 인간의 감각(고유 수용 감각, 평형 감각)을 언급하며 반론을 제기합니다. (B)에서는 'Also'를 사용하여 인간 외의 다른 동물이 가진 분류하기 더 어려운 특수한 감각(척추동물의 후각 시스템, 뱀의 열 감지) 사례를 추가합니다. 최종적으로 (A)에서 이러한 사례들을 근거로 감각을 특정 종류로 명확히 나눌 수 없다는 결론을 내리며 글을 맺는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 요약문을 작성하고자 한다. 요약문의 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 가장 적절한 말을 각각 주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The tongue was traditionally mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted at any areas in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but sequence. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.summary_sentence: Recent taste studies have shown that the (A)t__________ "tongue map" theory is (B)f__________, indicating that taste buds are not grouped into specialties, and flavors can be perceived (C)e__________ in the mouth. Additionally, taste perception is now understood to be influenced by time rather than by (D)l__________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 과거의 '혀 지도' 이론이 틀렸음을 설명하고 있습니다. (A) 전통적인(traditional) 이론은 (B) 거짓(false/wrong)이며, 맛은 입안 (C) 어디에서나(everywhere/anywhere) 느껴질 수 있습니다. 또한 맛의 인식은 장소(location/place)가 아니라 시간적 순서에 영향을 받는다는 내용입니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고 밑줄 친 우리말 표현을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 작성하시오.
questions.passage: No respectable boos would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard: <u>그들이 정말로 여러분에게 말하고 있는 것은 어떤 일이 이루어지도록 하기 위해서 여러분이 무엇을 해야만 하는가이다."</u>
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 주어진 단어와 어구를 모두, 한 번씩만 사용할 것
<보기>에 주어진 단어와 어구 외에는 추가하지 말고, 어형도 변형시키지 말 것
questions.answer: what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done
questions.explanation: 주어 부분 '그들이 정말로 여러분에게 말하고 있는 것은'은 관계대명사 what을 사용하여 'what they're really telling you'로 영작하고, 동사 'is' 뒤에 보어절로 '여러분이 무엇을 해야만 하는가'인 'what you must do'를 씁니다. 마지막으로 목적을 나타내는 부사구 '어떤 일이 이루어지도록 하기 위해서'를 사역동사 get의 용법을 활용해 'to get something done'으로 완성합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① The Role of Writing Positive Statements
② Magicians You Can Meet Everyday
③ The Power of Magic in Cinderella
④ Confidence Works for Your Life
questions.explanation: 이 글은 일상의 문제를 긍정적인 진술로 바꾸어 쓰는 것만으로도 생각과 행동이 변화하고 힘을 얻게 된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '긍정적 진술 쓰기의 역할'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 긍정적인 문장을 쓰는 것의 역할
② 매일 만날 수 있는 마술사들
③ 신데렐라에 나타난 마법의 힘
④ 자신감이 당신의 삶에 작용하는 방식
⑤ 행동이 사고를 방해하는 방식

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It is difficult for any of us to maintain a constant level of attention throughout our working day. We all have body rhythms characterised by peaks and valleys of energy and alertness. You will achieve more, and feel confident as a benefit, if you schedule your most demanding tasks at times when you are best able to cope with them. If you haven't thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to observe yourself. Try to note the times when you are at your best. We are all different. For some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for others it may take a while to warm up.
options: ④ Set Your Peak Time On Your Own
⑤ Your Peak Time: Flexible, Not Fixed
questions.explanation: 사람마다 에너지가 가장 높은 '정점 시간(peak time)'이 다르므로, 이를 파악하여 가장 어려운 업무를 그 시간에 배치하라는 내용의 글입니다. 따라서 '당신의 정점 시간을 파악하라'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 정점 시간을 파악하라
② 에너지를 낭비하지 마라
③ 성찰의 시간을 확보하라
④ 당신의 정점 시간을 스스로 설정하라
⑤ 당신의 정점 시간: 고정된 것이 아니라 유연하다

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① Why High Paying Jobs Matter
② Coworkers Affect Your Job Satisfaction
③ Don't Let Your Boss Push You Too Hard
④ Creating an Energizing Work Environment
⑤ How Meaningful Work Leads to a Fulfilling Life
questions.explanation: 의미 있는 일(성취감과 권한 부여를 제공하는 일)이 직무 만족도를 높일 뿐만 아니라 생산성 향상, 소득 증대, 그리고 전반적인 삶의 행복으로 이어진다는 연구 결과를 인용하며 그 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고소득 직업이 중요한 이유
② 동료들이 당신의 직무 만족도에 미치는 영향
③ 상사가 당신을 너무 몰아붙이게 두지 마라
④ 활기찬 작업 환경 조성하기
⑤ 의미 있는 일이 어떻게 충만한 삶으로 이어지는가

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① Messages were delivered by Chasquis in the Inca empire.
② The Chasquis were good runners and composed of only men.
③ Messengers lived in huts built for them.
④ When a messenger came nearer, another messenger had to stay in his place.
⑤ With the help of good conditions, it took three or four days to deliver messages 1,000 miles away.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 전령이 다음 오두막에 가까워지면, 다른 전령은 마중을 나가기 위해 밖으로 달려 나갔으며(the one who was running out to meet him), 서로 마주 보기 위해 서둘러 나갔다고(hurried out to meet them) 설명되어 있습니다. 따라서 제자리에 머물러 있어야 했다는 ④번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 잉카 제국에서 메시지는 Chasquis에 의해 전달되었다.
② Chasquis는 훌륭한 달리기 선수들이었으며 오직 남성으로만 구성되었다.
③ 전령들은 그들을 위해 지어진 오두막에서 살았다.
④ 전령이 가까이 오면, 다른 전령은 제자리에 머물러 있어야 했다.
⑤ 좋은 조건의 도움으로, 1,000마일 떨어진 곳까지 메시지를 전달하는 데 3~4일이 걸렸다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what about what can be achieved within a certain time frame ⓐ<u>is</u> a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time ⓑ<u>needed</u> alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to ⓒ<u>fitting</u> the task to the available time. There are some tasks ⓓ<u>that</u> you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task ⓔ<u>which</u> you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장에서 when(또는 for which)이 와야 할 자리입니다. 뒤따르는 문장 'you only have a short period available'은 주어, 동사, 목적어(a short period), 목적보어(available)를 갖춘 완전한 문장이므로 관계대명사 which는 올 수 없습니다. 앞의 'such a task'를 수식하며 때를 나타내는 관계부사 when이나 전치사+관계대명사 형태인 for which가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if ⓐ<u>trapped</u> below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy. move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange ⓑ<u>themselves</u> into orderly, repeating patterns. The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine ⓒ<u>which</u> minerals will form. Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how ⓓ<u>rapidly</u> the magma cools. When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. This is ⓔ<u>because</u> the atoms having enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools fast, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
questions.explanation: ⓔ 뒤에는 주어와 동사를 갖춘 절이 와야 하는데, 'the atoms having...' 부분에서 having은 분사 형태로 동사 역할을 할 수 없습니다. 이 문장은 'This is because the atoms have enough time...'과 같이 술어 동사(have)가 포함된 절이 되어야 어법상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find (A)[it / themselves] difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and (B)[leave / leaving] it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide if you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide (C)[that / whether] any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation:
(A) 뒤에 진목적어(to know when to stop painting)가 오므로, 가목적어 it이 적절합니다.
(B) 동명사 주어 Putting에 연결되는 동사 spoil과 and로 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 동사 원형인 leave가 맞습니다.
(C) decide의 목적어절로, '~인지 아닌지'라는 불확실한 내용을 결정하는 맥락이므로 접속사 whether가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① it | leave | whether
② it | leave | that
③ it | leaving | that
④ themselves | leave | that
⑤ themselves | leaving | whether

questions.question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(B) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.

(C) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 아리스토텔레스가 인간과 동물에게 5감이 있다고 정의한 내용을 설명합니다. (B)에서 'However'를 통해 이를 반박하며 인간에게 다른 감각(평형 감각 등)이 더 있음을 언급합니다. 이어 (A)에서는 인간 외에 다른 동물들의 특수한 감각 예시(뱀의 열 감지 등)를 들고, (C)에서 'These examples'를 통해 이를 정리하며 감각을 특정 개수로 나눌 수 없음을 결론 짓는 (B)-(A)-(C) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body.
ordered_passages: (A) Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is converted to fat and stored in the body. Too many simple carbohydrates can contribute to weight gain. They can also increase your risk of diabetes, heart disease and high cholesterol.(B) Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. Because their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold few nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made.(C) These complex sugar compounds are very difficult to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they slowly break down, the other nutrients are also released into your body, and can provide you with fuel for a number of hours.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 복합 탄수화물(Complex carbohydrates)이 몸에 좋다고 언급했습니다. (C)에서 'These complex sugar compounds'로 받아 복합 탄수화물의 구조적 특징과 장점을 설명합니다. 그 다음 (B)에서 'on the other hand'를 사용해 나쁜 탄수화물인 단순 당(simple sugars)을 소개합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 'these carbohydrates'(단순 당)가 몸에서 어떻게 분해되고 과잉 섭취 시 어떤 부작용(체중 증가, 질병 위험)이 있는지 설명하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to ⓐ<u>adjust to</u> jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's ⓑ<u>tougher</u> to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is ⓒ<u>substantial</u> enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform markedly ⓓ<u>superior</u> to teams flying eastward in professional baseball and college football. A more recent study of more than 46,000 Major League Baseball games found additional evidence that eastward travel is ⓔ<u>more</u> challenging than westward travel. This suggests that sports teams strategically schedule westward travel for important games to maximize their chances of winning.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 서쪽으로 비행하여 하루를 늘리는 것이 동쪽으로 비행하여 하루를 단축하는 것보다 '더 쉽다(easier)'는 것이 핵심 내용입니다. 이어지는 문장들(서쪽으로 이동한 팀의 성적이 더 좋음, 동쪽 이동이 더 힘들다는 증거 등)을 볼 때, ⓑ의 'tougher(더 힘든)'는 문맥상 'easier'와 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience ⓐ<u>challenges</u> when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ⓑ<u>more</u> inaccurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓒ<u>concerned</u> about how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to undervalue the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in their ⓓ<u>beginner</u> times. Knowing that experts ⓔ<u>wipe</u> how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 '지식의 저주'에 관한 글로, 전문가가 초보자의 어려움을 제대로 이해하지 못한다는 내용입니다. 전문가들은 해당 기술을 배우는 것이 초보자에게 얼마나 힘든지에 대해 무감각하거나 과소평가하는 경향이 있습니다. 따라서 ⓒ의 concerned(걱정하는, 염려하는)는 문맥상 'insensitive(무감각한)' 혹은 'unaware(인지하지 못하는)'와 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: To help decide what′s risky and what′s safe, who′s trustworthy and who′s not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone′s doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food′s tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it′s good to _________.
options: ② neglect the reviews and cues
③ find new restaurants by yourself
④ concentrate on your taste on food
⑤ adopt the practices of those around you
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 의사결정을 할 때 타인의 행동이나 사회적 증거(social evidence)를 따르는 경향이 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 진화론적 관점에서 집단을 따르는 것이 생존에 유리하며, 줄이 길게 늘어선 식당을 인기가 많고 맛있는 곳으로 인식하는 것처럼 주변 사람들의 행동을 참고하는 것이 합리적인 선택이 될 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '주변 사람들의 관행(행동)을 채택하는 것'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자신만의 견해를 고수하는 것
② 리뷰와 신호를 무시하는 것
③ 스스로 새로운 식당을 찾는 것
④ 음식에 대한 자신의 취향에 집중하는 것
⑤ 주변 사람들의 관행(행동)을 채택하는 것

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르면? [24년 3월 36번]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성인용 스포츠 환경이 어린 아이들에게는 너무 어렵거나 부적절하다는 것을 인식하고, 아이들의 체격과 능력에 맞게 경기장 크기, 장비, 규칙 등을 변경했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 야구의 T-볼, 축구의 작은 공과 경기장, 테니스의 적응된 라켓 등이 그 예시입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '조정'이나 '수정'을 의미하는 '① adjustments'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 조정(수정)
② 모의 시허ᄆ
③ 평가
④ 년하ᄱ(ᄑ해기)
⑤ 조지ᄀ

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: People commonly make the mistaken assumption that because a person has one type of characteristic, then they automatically have other characteristics which go with it. In one study, university students were given descriptions of a guest lecturer before he spoke to the group. Half the students received a description containing the word 'warm', the other half were told the speaker was 'cold'. The guest lecturer then led a discussion, after which the students were asked to give their impressions of him. As expected, there were large differences between the impressions formed by the students, depending upon their original information of the lecturer. It was also found that those students who expected the lecturer to be warm tended to interact with him more. This shows that different expectations not only affect the impressions we form but also our behaviour and the relationship which is formed.
questions.summary_sentence: Prior descriptions of a lecturer influenced students' impressions and (A)__________ in a study on (B)__________.
questions.explanation: 연구에서 강사에 대한 사전 정보('따뜻함' 또는 '차가움')가 학생들의 인상 형성에 영향을 주었을 뿐만 아니라, 더 많이 상호작용하게 하거나 덜 하게 하는 행동(engagement)의 차이를 보였습니다. 따라서 (A)는 참여/관여를 뜻하는 engagement가, (B)는 그러한 원인이 된 '기대'를 뜻하는 expectations가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 참여 - 기대
② 관찰 - 열망
③ 상호작용 - 열망
④ 평가 - 의무
⑤ 관찰 - 기대

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Chess masters shown a chess board in the middle of a game for 5 seconds with 20 to 30 pieces still in play can immediately reproduce the position of the pieces from memory. Beginners, of course, are able to place only a few. Now take the same pieces and place them on the board randomly and the difference is much reduced. The expert's advantage is only for familiar patterns - those previously stored in memory. Faced with unfamiliar patterns, even when it involves the same familiar domain, the expert's advantage disappears. The beneficial effects of familiar structure on memory have been observed for many types of expertise, including music. People with musical training can reproduce short sequences of musical notation more accurately than those with no musical training when notes follow typical sequences, but the advantage is much reduced when the notes are ordered randomly. Expertise also improves memory for sequences of movements. Experienced ballet dancers are able to repeat longer sequences of steps than less experienced dancers, and they can repeat a sequence of steps making up a up a routine better than steps ordered randomly.
questions.summary_sentence: Experts tend to (A)__________ their memory by recognizing (B)__________ patterns and sequences.
questions.explanation: 체스 전문가, 음악가, 발레 무용수들 모두 자신이 익숙한 패턴(familiar patterns)이 주어질 때 기억력이 향상된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '강화하다/향상시키다(enhance)', (B)에는 '친숙한(familiar)'이 들어가는 것이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 향상시키다 / 독특한
② 향상시키다 / 친숙한
③ 과장하다 / 친숙한
④ 과장하다 / 독특한
⑤ 증가시키다 / 특이한

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. (A) Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. questions.insertion_sentence: However, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'However'는 반전을 나타냅니다. (C) 이후의 문장은 최근 애니메이션 영화들이 동물을 더 '자연스러운(natural)' 방식으로 보여주는 추세라고 설명합니다. 하지만 주어진 문장은 '그럼에도 불구하고 여전히 앞발을 손처럼 사용하고 표정으로 말을 한다'는 내용을 담고 있어, 자연스러운 방식이라는 (C)의 내용과 대조를 이룹니다. 따라서 (D) 위치에 들어가서 자연스러운 묘사에도 불구하고 인간적 특징이 여전히 남아있음을 설명하는 것이 흐름상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. (B) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (C) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. (D) But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. (E) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.insertion_sentence: Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened: same with the other sensing systems.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '일부 시각 정보가 분명히 들어오기는 하지만, 약해지거나 짧아지기 때문에 정상적으로 처리되지 않으며, 이는 다른 감각 시스템도 마찬가지이다'라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 이는 (A) 문장에서 언급한 '잠자는 포유류의 눈은 기능적으로 멀어 있다'는 현상에 대한 구체적인 메커니즘을 설명하는 것입니다. 따라서 자극이 등록은 되지만 처리되지 않아 깨우지 못한다는 (B) 뒤의 일반적 진술 바로 앞에 위치하여 구체적 사례를 완성하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. ⓐThe danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air. ⓑMoreover, the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're stuck. ⓒMany people want to learn how to climb the rocks to protect themselves in the mountains. ⓓAnd it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. ⓔThe poor employment market has left them feeling locked in what may be a secure, or even well-paying - but ultimately unsatisfying - job.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성공이 편안하지만 매너리즘에 빠진 상황(rut)으로 이끌어 거기서 빠져나오기 힘든 상태가 될 수 있다는 경고를 담고 있습니다. ⓒ번 문장은 산에서 자신을 보호하기 위해 암벽 등반하는 법을 배우고 싶어 한다는 내용으로, 비유적 표현인 'rut(틀에 박힌 생활)'과는 무관한 실제 암벽 등반 이야기를 하고 있으므로 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. ⓐIf you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. ⓑBut like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. ⓒDepending on how large-scale improvements are made, the appearance of our society can vary greatly. ⓓThrough diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. ⓔThus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 지도자들도 처음엔 우리와 같은 평범한 사람들이었으며, 자신의 아이디어를 발전시켜 나갔기에 우리 모두 지도자가 될 잠재력이 있다는 내용입니다. ⓒ번 문장은 대규모 개선이 어떻게 이루어지는가에 따라 사회의 모습이 달라진다는 내용으로, 개인의 리더십 잠재력이라는 중심 소재에서 벗어난 사회적 변화에 대해 언급하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. ⓐFor example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. ⓑThe next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. ⓒIn year three, the crops will rotate again, and, by the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. ⓓEach crop enriches the soil for the next crop. ⓔPackaging is becoming as important as marketing when farmers trade vegetables. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 '윤작(Crop rotation)'의 정의와 과정, 그리고 토양의 건강을 유지해 주는 지속 가능성에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ⓔ번 문장은 농부들이 채소를 거래할 때 포장이 마케팅만큼 중요해지고 있다는 내용으로, 농법인 윤작의 원리와 이점과는 무관한 상업적 측면을 다루고 있습니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것을 고르면?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available.
