questions.question: 25. 윗글 [B]의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: [A] There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe ⓐ<u>they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field</u>. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find them being given ⓑ<u>advice on how to do their jobs</u> from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members ⓒ<u>telling them how to run their business</u>. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.*boardroom 이사회실[B] Passion and engagement are often at the heart of Monday Morning Quarterbacking. questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [24년 3월 19번]

Marilyn said, "Part of the joy of ⓓ<u>building</u> a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give it as a gift to the ocean." Sarah loved this idea and responded with enthusiasm to the idea of building another castle一this time, ⓔ<u>much</u> closer to the water so the ocean would get its gift sooner!
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 'her heart'는 주어이며, 뒤에 문장의 동사가 필요합니다. 앞선 'tears streamed'와 병렬 구조를 이루며 과거 시제인 'was'로 고쳐야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field.
ordered_passages: (A) For example, in a genuine training situation. Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'.

(B) Based on her study, knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.

(C) Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 전문가가 초보자를 가르칠 때 겪는 어려움을 언급한 후, (A)에서 Pamela Hinds 박사의 구체적인 휴대폰 사용 연구 사례를 제시하며 '지식의 저주'를 설명합니다. (C)에서는 해당 연구의 상세 결과(기술 습득 시 난이도를 과소평가함)를 설명하고, (B)에서 이러한 연구 결과를 바탕으로 학생들의 관점에서 학습 과정을 바라볼 필요가 있다는 결론을 도출하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (A) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. (B) Stimuli entering the sensory systems are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. (C) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. (D) But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. (E) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.insertion_sentence: That is to say, some visual information apparently gets in. but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'That is to say(즉)'는 앞선 내용에 대한 재설명을 의미합니다. (A)에서 잠자는 포유류의 눈을 뜨게 해도 정상적으로 보지 못한다는 구체적 사례를 든 후, 주어진 문장이 '즉, 시각 정보가 들어오긴 하지만 정상적으로 처리되지 않는다'며 이를 일반화하여 설명합니다. 그 뒤 (B)에서 이러한 감각 시스템의 정보 등록과 비정상적 처리가 개인을 깨우지 못한다는 내용으로 이어지는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 (A), (B)를 조건에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: I am John Austin, a science teacher at Crestville High School. Recently (A)<u>저는 환경에 관해 당신이 쓴 최신 도서에 감명받았습니다</u>. Also my students read your book and had a class discussion about it. They are big fans of your book, so I'd like to ask you to visit our school and give a special lecture. We can set the date and time to suit your schedule. (B)<u>당신이 우리 학교에 와 주신다면 학생들에게 멋진 경험이 될 것입니다</u>. We would be very grateful if you could come.
subjective_conditions: 1. 주어진 단어를 모두 1번씩만 이용하되, 형태를 바꾸지 말 것
2. (A), (B) 모두 각각 단어를 1개 추가할 것
vocabulary_box: (A)about / was / the / I / book / environment / wrote / latest / the / by / you
(B)you / experience / the / having / school / be / a / at / for / students / would / our
questions.answer: (A) I was impressed by the latest book you wrote about the environment(B) Having you at our school would be a fantastic experience for the students
questions.explanation: (A) '감명받았다'는 표현을 위해 'impressed'를 추가하여 'I was impressed by the latest book you wrote about the environment'로 완성합니다.(B) '멋진'에 해당하는 'fantastic'을 추가하여 'Having you at our school would be a fantastic experience for the students'로 완성합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote ⓐ<u>that</u> there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a ⓑ<u>few</u> in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that ⓒ<u>is</u> even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be ⓓ<u>clearly</u> divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for ⓔ<u>what</u> they are.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 주격 관계대명사 that의 선행사는 복수 명사인 'senses'입니다. 따라서 관계절의 동사는 단수형 is가 아니라 복수형인 are로 써야 어법상 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally ⓐ<u>blind</u>. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or ⓑ<u>weakened</u>; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of ⓒ<u>protecting</u> sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems ⓓ<u>essential</u> to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some ⓔ<u>drawbacks</u> of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 잠을 자는 동안 감각이 차단되는 현상은 잠을 보호하는 필수적인 기능입니다. 마지막 문장에서 많은 동물들이 완전한 지각적 이탈 없이 잠의 '이점'을 얻기 위해 졸음이라는 중간 단계를 사용한다고 해야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 'drawbacks(결점, 단점)'은 'benefits(이점)'과 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① blind (눈이 먼)
② weakened (약해진)
③ protecting (보호하는)
④ essential (필수적인)
⑤ drawbacks (단점)

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; (A)__________, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. (B)__________, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 동물들은 서로 똑같지 않다고 했고, 뒷 문장에서는 그 결과 치유 과정에서 똑같은 방식으로 반응하지 않을 수 있다고 했으므로 인과관계를 나타내는 'therefore'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞 문장에서 환경적 요인에 따른 반응의 차이(예시: 보호소 고양이 vs 집 고양이)를 설명한 후, 추가적으로 질병의 종류(신체적 vs 정서적)에 따른 차이를 나열하고 있으므로 첨가를 나타내는 'In addition'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더욱이 / 실제로
② 더욱이 / 사실상
③ 그러나 / 비슷하게
④ 그러므로 / 대조적으로
⑤ 그러므로 / 게다가

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. (A)__________, our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. (B)__________, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① Therefore / On the other hand
questions.explanation: (A) 인간의 감각이 걷는 속도에 적응되어 있다는 앞 문장의 결론으로, 환경의 세부 사항을 구별하는 능력이 시속 5마일 이하에 적합하다는 내용이 이어지므로 인과의 'Therefore'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞서 언급한 운전자(motorists)의 제한된 능력과 대조적으로, 보행자(pedestrian)는 속도가 느려 세부 사항을 감상할 수 있다는 내용이 나오므로 대조의 'On the other hand'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러므로 / 반면에
② 한편 / 예를 들어
③ 그러나 / 결론적으로
④ 그럼에도 불구하고 / 다시 말해서
⑤ 따라서 / 결과적으로

questions.question: 11. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. ⓐThose who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. ⓑSonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. ⓒThe studies reached the conclusion: happiness continues to rise with income even in the high range of incomes for the majority of people, showing that for many of us, on average having more money can make us increasingly happier. ⓓThose most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. ⓔFor her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 전체 글은 일에서의 의미와 만족감이 삶의 행복과 성공에 미치는 긍정적인 영향에 대해 다루고 있으나, ⓒ번 문장은 단순히 소득이 높을수록 행복도가 올라간다는 '돈과 행복의 관계'에 치중되어 있어 글의 핵심 주제인 '의미 있는 일'의 중요성에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. ⓐIf you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. ⓑHowever, analysts say that methods used by a business leader do not necessarily work for a leader of the nation. ⓒBut like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. ⓓThrough diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. ⓔThus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 지도자들도 평범한 사람으로 시작했으며, 일상의 개선 아이디어를 발전시켜 리더가 되었으므로 우리 모두 리더가 될 잠재력이 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓑ번 문장은 '기업 지도자의 방식이 국가 지도자에게는 반드시 통하지 않는다'는 분석가들의 의견을 언급하고 있어, 리더십의 보편적 잠재력이라는 전체 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth.
ordered_passages: (A) Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century.
(B) Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.

(C) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 전통적인 혀 지도의 개념(부위별 맛 인지)을 설명한 후, (A)에서 'however'를 통해 이 설명이 사실 완전히 틀렸음을 밝히며 그 배경을 설명합니다. (C)에서는 오늘날의 연구 결과로 맛 봉오리가 특정 맛에 따라 분류되지 않고 어디서든 모든 맛을 느낄 수 있음을 설명하며, (B)에서 'Moreover'를 사용하여 위치가 아닌 '시간'이 핵심 기제라는 추가적인 반박 내용을 제시하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding customers' behavior ⓐ<u>before</u> a purchase, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will ⓑ<u>persuade</u> others to purchase the product from you. ⓒ<u>Pleased</u> customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they are ⓓ<u>familiar</u> with. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side and that they're used to encourage them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to ⓔ<u>reduce</u> negative word-of-mouth advertising.
questions.explanation: 구매 후의 고객 반응(재구매 여부, 반품 여부 등)을 이해하는 것에 대한 내용이므로, 구매 '전(before)'의 행동이 아니라 구매 '후(after)'의 행동을 이해함으로써 영향력과 재구매 가능성을 파악할 수 있다는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 윗글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. (A)________________________, having two separate calendars for work and personal life can lead to distractions. (B)__________________________, you will find yourself checking your to-do lists multiple times. Instead, organize all of your tasks in one place. ⓐIt doesn't matter if you use digital or paper media. ⓑDigital technology has brought enormous progress to our society. ⓒIt's okay to keep your professional and personal tasks in one place. ⓓThis will give you a good idea of how time is divided between work and home. ⓔThis will allow you to make informed decisions about which tasks are most important.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 업무용과 개인용 일정을 하나로 통합하여 관리해야 효율적이라는 내용입니다. ②번 문장은 디지털 기술이 사회에 가져온 엄청난 진보에 대한 일반적인 진술로, 일정을 통합 관리하라는 글의 핵심 주제와는 무관합니다.

questions.question: 16. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)와 (B)가 주어진 뜻이 되도록 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. (A)________________________, having two separate calendars for work and personal life can lead to distractions. (B)__________________________, you will find yourself checking your to-do lists multiple times. Instead, organize all of your tasks in one place. ⓐIt doesn't matter if you use digital or paper media. ⓑDigital technology has brought enormous progress to our society. ⓒIt's okay to keep your professional and personal tasks in one place. ⓓThis will give you a good idea of how time is divided between work and home. ⓔThis will allow you to make informed decisions about which tasks are most important.
subjective_conditions: - <보기>에 주어진 단어만을 한 번씩 모두 사용할 것- <보기>의 단어를 변형하지 말고 그대로 쓸 것- 주어진 단어를 포함하여 답란에 적을 것
vocabulary_box: may / is / something / seem / check / it / missing / sensible / if
questions.answer: (A) it may seem sensible, (B) check if something is missing
questions.explanation: (A) '비록 그것이 현명해 보일지도 모르지만'은 'Although' 뒤에 주어 'it', 조동사 'may', 동사 'seem', 형용사 보어 'sensible'을 순서대로 배열합니다.(B) '누락된 것이 있는지를 확인하기 위해'는 목적을 나타내는 'To' 뒤에 동사 'check', 목적어 절을 이끄는 접속사 'if', 주어 'something', 동사 'is', 형용사 보어 'missing'을 순서대로 배열합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: ACC Travel Agency Customers: Have you ever wanted to enjoy a holiday in nature? This summer is the best time to turn your dream into reality. We have a perfect travel package for you. This travel package includes special trips to Lake Madison as well as massage and meditation to help you relax. Also, we provide yoga lessons taught by experienced instructors. If you book this package, you will enjoy all this at a reasonable price. We are sure that it will be an unforgettable experience for you. If you call us, we will be happy to give you more details.
options: ① apology for dissatisfaction with travel packages
② asking for feedback on package travel products
③ complaint about a package tour from a customer
④ promotion of a package product from a travel agency
⑤ notice of a change in the travel plan to the customers
questions.explanation: 이 글은 여름 휴가 패키지 상품을 홍보하고 가격 혜택 등을 안내하는 내용이므로, '여행사의 패키지 상품 홍보'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 여행 패키지에 대한 불만에 대한 사과
② 패키지 여행 상품에 대한 피드백 요청
③ 고객으로부터의 패키지 관광에 대한 불만 제기
④ 여행사의 패키지 상품 홍보
⑤ 고객들에게 여행 계획 변경 공지

questions.question: 18. [다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.] 위 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, enabling us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. (A)___________, it didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Companies large and small have off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. (B)___________, with air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
options: ① (A) However / (B) On the other hand
③ (A) Therefore / (B) On the other hand
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 정보화 사회에 대해 기대했던 것과 달리 실제로는 그러하지 않았다는 내용이 오므로, 역접으로 연결하는 However가 적절합니다. (B) 소비자에게 업무가 전사된 구체적인 사례(항공 예약 등)를 나열하고 있으므로 For example이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나 / 반면에
② 그러나 / 예를 들어
③ 그러므로 / 반면에
④ 그러므로 / 불행하게도
⑤ 마찬가지로 / 예를 들어

questions.question: 19. [다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.] 위 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (가), (나)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, enabling us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. (A)___________, it didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Companies large and small have off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. (B)___________, with air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
subjective_conditions: - <보기>에 주어진 표현만을 한 번씩 모두 사용할 것
- <보기>의 표현을 그대로 사용하되 필요시 동사의 형태를 적절히 변형하여 쓸 것
vocabulary_box: (가) to have more free time / people / allow / the opportunity to pursue high goals / and
(나) to people / their tasks / off-load / some of
questions.answer: (가) allowing people to have more free time and the opportunity to pursue high goals / (나) have off-loaded some of their tasks to people
questions.explanation: (가) 전치사 'instead of' 다음이므로 동사 allow를 동명사 형태인 allowing으로 변형하고, 'allow + 목적어 + to-부정사' 구문을 활용하여 작성합니다. (나) 주어인 companies에 맞춰 현재완료 시제(have off-loaded) 또는 현재 시제를 사용하여, 회사가 고객들에게 업무를 전가했다는 내용으로 결합합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as <u>a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another</u>. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.
options: ① All organisms must follow a completely unpredictable path.
② Complex systems inevitably settle into a few stable states.
③ Changing systems can remain in intermediate conditions.
④ Systems remain in a random or undefined phase.
⑤ Multiple outcomes can occur simultaneously.
questions.explanation: 본문은 생명체와 같은 복잡한 시스템(고차원 시스템)이 안정성을 유지하기 위해 가능한 수많은 결과 중 소수의 명확한 상태로 수렴된다는 '운하화(canalization)' 개념을 설명하고 있다. 공이 골짜기 바닥 중 하나로 굴러 들어가야 한다는 비유는 복잡한 시스템이 결국 몇 가지 안정적인 상태 중 하나로 정착하게 됨을 의미한다.
options_translation: ① 모든 유기체는 완전히 예측 불가능한 경로를 따라야 한다.
② 복잡한 시스템은 필연적으로 몇 가지 안정적인 상태로 정착한다.
③ 변화하는 시스템은 중간 상태에 머물 수 있다.
④ 시스템은 무작위적이거나 정의되지 않은 단계에 머문다.
⑤ 여러 결과가 동시에 발생할 수 있다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of clarity. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused or not going to be used in the near future.
options: ① misunderstandings about minimalism and its true purpose
② minimalism and its relationship with material value
③ the importance of possessions in modern society
④ emotional attachment and the conflict with minimalism
⑤ the connection between minimalism and emotional attachment
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부는 미니멀리즘이 소중한 소유물을 희생하는 것이라는 오해(부정적 인상)에 대해 다루고, 후반부에서는 미니멀리즘이 감정을 해치는 것이 아니라 쓰지 않는 물건을 정리함으로써 명료함의 즐거움을 얻는 것이라는 실제 목적을 설명하고 있다. 따라서 주제는 미니멀리즘에 대한 오해와 진정한 목적이다.
options_translation: ① 미니멀리즘에 대한 오해와 그것의 진정한 목적
② 미니멀리즘과 물질적 가치와의 관계
③ 현대 사회에서 소유물의 중요성
④ 정서적 애착과 미니멀리즘과의 갈등
⑤ 미니멀리즘과 정서적 애착 사이의 연관성

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre ─ indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant ─ in time or in place ─ we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
options: ① The Art of Ignoring Reality Through Cinematic Magic
② The Hollywood Blockbuster Guide to Climate Solutions
③ Why Fictional Climate Disasters Are Enough to Warn Us
④ How We're Rewriting the Story of Global Warming with Fantasy
⑤ The End of Climate Fiction: When Reality Outpaces Imagination
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화가 인류의 삶에 지대한 영향을 미치게 됨에 따라, 더 이상 기후 변화를 허구적인 이야기로 다루는 기후 소설(climate-fiction) 장르가 무의미해질 것이라고 주장합니다. 현실이 상상력을 앞지르게 되면서 기후 변화는 더 이상 '이야기'가 아닌 '현실'이 된다는 내용이므로 정답은 ⑤번입니다.
options_translation: ① 영화적 마법을 통해 현실을 무시하는 기술
② 기후 해결책에 대한 할리우드 블록버스터 가이드
③ 허구적인 기후 재앙이 우리에게 경고하기에 충분한 이유
④ 우리가 판타지로 지구 온난화의 이야기를 다시 쓰는 방법
⑤ 기후 소설의 종말: 현실이 상상력을 앞지를 때

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: For a long time, people believed that colors were objective, physical properties of objects or of the light that bounced off them. Even today, science teachers educate their students with stories about Issac Newton and his prism experiment, telling them how different wavelengths of light produce the rainbow of colors around us. But this theory isn't really ␐<u>accurate</u>. Different wavelengths of light do exist independently of us but they only become colors inside our bodies. Color is ultimately a ␑<u>neurological</u> process whereby photons are detected by light-sensitive cells in our eyes, transformed into electrical signals and sent to our brain, where, in a series of complex calculations, our visual cortex converts them into "color". Most experts now agree that color, as commonly understood, doesn't ␒<u>inhabit</u> the physical world at all but exists in the eyes or minds of its beholders. They argue that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be ␓<u>colorless</u> ─ and so would everything else. To put it another way: there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who perceive it. This is why no two people will ever see exactly the same colors. Every person's visual system is ␔<u>identical</u> and so, therefore, are their perceptions. About 8% of men are color-blind and see fewer colors than everyone else; a small number of lucky women might, thanks to a genetic duplication on the X chromosome, be able to distinguish many more than the rest of us.*photon: 광양자 **chromosome: 염색체
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 색상이 객관적인 물리적 속성이 아니라 인간의 뇌에서 일어나는 주관적인 과정이라는 것입니다. 지문 마지막 부분에서 사람마다 보는 색이 다르다는 점을 설명하고 있으며, 색맹인 남성이나 더 많은 색을 구별하는 여성을 예로 들고 있습니다. 따라서 모든 사람의 시각 체계가 '동일하다(identical)'는 표현은 문맥상 적절하지 않으며, '독특하다(unique)' 또는 '다르다(different)'와 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So ⓐ<u>to find</u> one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, ⓑ<u>what</u> they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes ⓒ<u>stared</u> upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn ⓓ<u>itself</u> into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt ─ ⓔ<u>producing</u> the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 구문은 'with + 목적어 + 분사' 구문입니다. 여기서 목적어인 'its two eyes(그것의 두 눈)'가 위쪽을 '응시하는' 능동적인 동작을 수행하는 주체이므로, 과거분사인 stared가 아니라 현재분사인 staring이 와야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive _________________.
options: ① changes in dietary preferences worldwide
② difficulties in managing agricultural expansion
③ unpredictable biological and climatic challenges
④ advancements in genetic modification technology
⑤ competition between traditional and modern crops
questions.explanation: 지문은 식량 다양성 감소의 위험성에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 특히 작물이 균일해질수록 재해에 취약해진다고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 좁은 범위의 식물 품종에만 의존하는 세계 식량 시스템은 '예측 불가능한 생물학적, 기후적 도전'을 견뎌내지 못할 가능성이 큽니다.
options_translation: ① 전 세계적인 식습관 선호도의 변화
② 농업 확장을 관리하는 데 있어서의 어려움
③ 예측할 수 없는 생물학적 및 기후적 도전
④ 유전자 변형 기술의 발전
⑤ 전통 작물과 현대 작물 사이의 경쟁

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Where is big data useful? It is most useful in situations that are stable, where data are reliable and where theory can guide the search. Examples of these situations are astronomy and the analysis of past data, as in health records. Big data is less promising in situations that may change unexpectedly and where one is looking for the needle in a huge haystack of data. Examples of these situations are predicting spread of the flu, currency exchange rates, children at risk or human behavior in general. In statistics, the law of large numbers describes a situation where having more data is better for making predictions. According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to match the true state of the world. For instance, on your first encounter with roulette, you may have beginner's luck after betting on 7. But the more often you repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning, meaning that your luck will at some point fade away. Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, dependent on their age, region or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to balance individual losses. Yet that works only as long as _________________________________.*haystack: 건초더미
options: ① the technology used to collect and analyze the data is reliable
② the data is analyzed using a variety of techniques
③ the risks involved are carefully calculated
④ the individuals involved are able to make quick decisions
⑤ the situation in which they are operating remains stable
questions.explanation: 지문 초반에 대량 데이터(빅데이터)가 가장 유용한 상황은 '안정적인(stable)' 상황이라고 언급하고 있습니다. 카지노나 보험 업계가 대수의 법칙(law of large numbers)에 의존하여 이익을 내는 것 또한 그들이 운영되는 상황이 변하지 않고 일정하게 유지될 때(remains stable)만 가능합니다.
options_translation: ① 데이터를 수집하고 분석하는 데 사용되는 기술이 신뢰할 수 있다
② 데이터가 다양한 기술을 사용하여 분석된다
③ 관련된 위험이 신중하게 계산된다
④ 관련된 개인들이 빠른 결정을 내릴 수 있다
⑤ 그들이 운영되고 있는 상황이 안정적으로 유지된다

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans _____________________________. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change ─ especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
options: ① experience a decline in boredom when exposed to repetitive or static experiences
② are wired to seek novelty and respond more strongly to new stimuli
③ are constantly entertained by our surroundings
④ are programmed to remain focused on familiar things
⑤ are designed to become more responsive to repeated experiences and focus on survival
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 신경 세포가 변하지 않는 자극에는 무뎌지고, 새로운 자극이나 변화하는 것에는 더 강하게 반응하도록 진화했다는 내용입니다. 반복되는 것에 대해 지루함을 느끼는 것은 새로운 자극을 즉각적으로 눈에 띄게 만드는 생존 기제이므로, 인간은 새로운 것을 찾고 거기에 더 강하게 반응하도록 회로가 짜여 있다는 2번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 반복적이거나 정적인 경험에 노출될 때 지루함의 감소를 경험한다
② 새로운 것을 찾고 새로운 자극에 더 강하게 반응하도록 타고났다(회로가 짜여 있다)
③ 주변 환경에 의해 끊임없이 즐거움을 느낀다
④ 익숙한 것에 계속해서 집중하도록 프로그램되어 있다
⑤ 반복적인 경험에 더 민감하게 반응하고 생존에 집중하도록 설계되어 있다

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on ________________________________. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people on our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
options: ① how successfully we fit into the social dynamics of the group
② how strongly we influenced the decisions of others
③ how well we competed with others
④ how creatively we contributed to group activities
⑤ how effectively we maintained personal boundaries with others

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The adolescent brain is not fully developed until its early twenties. This means the way the adolescents' decision-making circuits integrate and process information may put them at a disadvantage. One of their brain regions that matures later is the prefrontal cortex, which is the control center, tasked with thinking ahead and evaluating consequences. It is the area of the brain responsible for preventing you from sending off an initial angry text and modifying it with kinder words. On the other hand, the limbic system matures earlier, playing a central role in processing emotional responses. Because of its earlier development, it is more likely to influence decision-making. Decision-making in the adolescent brain is led by emotional factors more than the perception of consequences. Due to these differences, there is an imbalance between feeling-based decision-making ruled by the more mature limbic system and logical-based decision-making by the not-yet-mature prefrontal cortex. This may explain why some teens are more likely to make bad decisions.
questions.summary_sentence: Teenagers often make (A)____________ choices because their brain's logic center is still growing, while the part that controls feelings is fully (B)____________.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. (A) A study of happiness might measure the number  of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. (B) Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. (C) It is because respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. (D) Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" (E) Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
questions.insertion_sentence: But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '하지만 작년에 아파서 결근할 정도로 슬펐던 적이 몇 번인가?'라고 묻는 것이 구체적인 답변을 유도한다는 내용입니다. (C) 뒤에서 단순히 얼마나 슬펐는지 묻는 것은 부정확할 수 있다는 문제점을 지적한 뒤, (D) 위치에서 그 대안으로 구체적인 질문을 던지는 예시가 와야 하며, 그 뒤에 '마찬가지로(Similarly)'를 통해 또 다른 구체적 질문의 예시가 이어지는 구조가 자연스럽습니다. 다만 이 지문에서 (D)는 주어진 문장이 들어간 뒤의 연결을 설명하므로 정답은 ④번입니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying them to culture. (A) Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually likened to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection. (B) For example, we do not expect the cultural transmission to follow the rules of genetic transmission strictly. (C) If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily equally likely to acquire the mother's or father's form of that trait. (D) Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers. (E) Thus, the frequency of a cultural trait in the population is relevant beyond just the probability that an individual's parents had that trait.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, these approaches had to be modified to account for the differences between genetic and cultural transmission.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그러나 이러한 접근법들은 유전적 전이와 문화적 전이 사이의 차이를 설명하기 위해 수정되어야 했다'는 내용입니다. (A)까지는 문화와 유전의 유사성을 설명하고 있으며, (B) 위치부터는 '예를 들어, 문화적 전이가 유전적 전이의 규칙을 엄격하게 따를 것으로 기대하지 않는다'며 차이점에 대한 구체적 예시가 시작되므로, 반전의 연결어 'However'가 포함된 주어진 문장은 (B) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 윗글 [A]에 밑줄 친 It didn't work의 이유로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: [A] In the United States, more than 100,000 people are waiting for an organ transplant. There aren't enough donors, and even if everyone signed up to do so, less than 1% of those who volunteer die in such a way that their organs are viable for transplantation. On an average day, 17 people die waiting for an organ. "That someone has to die for someone to live is a broken paradigm," said Dr. Robert Montgomery, director of the NYU Langone Transplant Institute and one of the researchers who has been exploring xenotransplantation. "I think animals are the answer." Transplanting organs from animals to humans isn't a new idea. Decades ago, doctors thought primates were the best candidates for xenotransplantation, and in 1984, they transplanted a baboon heart into a child who went on to live for 21 days. "But primates turned out to be too small, too expensive and too controversial," said Dr. Art Caplan, a professor of bioethics and founding head of the Division of Medical Ethics at NYU Grossman School of Medicine's Department of Population Health. Primates also didn't breed as quickly as pigs do. Bottom line, Caplan said: "<u>It didn't work.</u>" Pig organs, though, are anatomically similar to humans'. For more than three decades, pigs' heart valves have been used to repair human hearts. Pig products go into dozens of life-saving drugs like epinephrine, which is used to treat severe allergic reactions, and heparin, a blood thinner. Humans are also more ethically comfortable with organs from pigs than non-human primates, Caplan said. Pigs have been in "Disney-esque" stories that make people sympathetic, but "Babe" and "Charlotte's Web" didn't stop everyone from eating pork "at a rate of a billion or so per year," Caplan said. "So it's a little hard to object to using a dozen in transplants."*baboon: 개코원승이 **anatomically: 해부학적으로***Disney-esque: 디즈니 스타일의[B] Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation ─ transferring organs to others ─ is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities. For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation or avoid it, and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely in order to avoid the threat in the future. Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the 'specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
options: ① Emotions: Adaptive Tools for Survival
② Human Emotions: A Flaw in Evolution
③ The Key of Humanity: Positive Thinking
④ Survival Secret: Why Emotions Make Us Weak
⑤ Surviving With Emotions: An Unsolved Mystery
questions.explanation: 이 글은 감정이 인간의 생존과 적응에 기여했기 때문에 진화해 왔다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 'Emotions: Adaptive Tools for Survival (감정: 생존을 위한 적응적 도구)'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
options: ① Plato's Realism: an Absurd Faith of Ancient Times
② The Greatest Mathematical Discovery Saving Humans
③ Love Yourself! Everyone Has Their Own Imperfection
④ Is There Any Perfect Circle in This World? Ask Plato!
⑤ Philosophical Consideration About Where We Came From

questions.question: 13. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 have beginner's luck after betting on 7이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In statistics, the law of large numbers describes a situation where having more data is better for making predictions. According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to match the true state of the world. For instance, on your first encounter with the game of roulette, you may <u>have beginner's luck after betting on 7</u>. But the more often you repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning, meaning that your luck will at some point fade away. Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to balance individual losses.
options: ① take many tries to find the surest way to win games at a casino
② get additional rewards for trying something new that people avoid
③ experience unexpected random winning during a few initial attempts
④ estimate the exact probability that beginners make the biggest win
⑤ develop skills to overcome the extreme tension even at the first trial
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락에서 '초심자의 행운'은 대수의 법칙이 적용되기 전, 즉 시행 횟수가 적을 때 발생하는 우연한 승리를 의미합니다. 통계적으로는 데이터가 쌓일수록 결과는 실제 확률에 수렴하게 되므로, 초기의 행운은 일시적이고 무작위적인 결과임을 나타냅니다. 따라서 3번 '초기의 몇 번의 시도 동안 예상치 못한 무작위적 승리를 경험하는 것'이 가장 적절한 의미입니다.
options_translation: 카지노에서 게임을 이기는 가장 확실한 방법을 찾기 위해 많은 시도를 한다
사람들이 피하는 새로운 것을 시도함으로써 추가적인 보상을 얻는다
몇 번의 초기 시도 동안 예상치 못한 무작위적 승리를 경험한다
초보자들이 가장 큰 승리를 거둘 정확한 확률을 추정한다
첫 시도에서도 극도의 긴장감을 극복하는 기술을 개발한다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying them to culture. Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually ⓐ<u>similar</u> to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection. However, these approaches had to be ⓑ<u>altered</u> to account for the differences between genetic and cultural transmission. For example, we ⓒ<u>suspect</u> that the cultural transmission follows the rules of genetic transmission strictly. If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child may acquire cultural traits ⓓ<u>unevenly</u> from each parent. Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers; thus, the frequency of a cultural trait in the population ⓔ<u>matters</u> beyond just the probability that an individual's parents had that trait.
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 문화적 진화와 유전적 진화의 유사점과 차이점을 다루고 있습니다. (C)가 포함된 문장은 앞서 언급된 유전적 전수와 문화적 전수의 '차이점'에 대한 예시를 시작하는 부분입니다. 이어지는 내용에서 아이가 부모뿐 아니라 타인으로부터도 문화적 특성을 배울 수 있다고 설명하므로, 문화적 전수가 유전적 전수의 규칙을 '엄격하게' 따른다고 생각하기는 어렵습니다. 따라서 ⓒ의 suspect(생각하다, 추측하다)는 문맥상 'cannot expect'나 'doubt'와 같이 부정적인 맥락을 담은 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants. Not only were their athletic talents superior, the Cubans appeared even stronger from just the colour of their uniforms. A game would not even start and the opposing team would already be scared. A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time. The country that ruled international baseball for decades has not been on top since that uniform change. Traditions are important for a team; while a team brand or image can adjust to keep up with present times, unless it __________________________, negative effects can surface.
options: ④ ignores the rules it has followed
⑤ maintains its own foundational identity
questions.explanation: 쿠바 야구팀이 강렬한 붉은 유니폼 전통을 버리고 현대화된 스타일로 바꾼 뒤 성적이 하락했다는 사례를 통해, 팀의 브랜드나 이미지를 시대에 맞게 조정하더라도 근본적인 정체성(전통)을 유지하지 않으면 부정적인 결과가 나타날 수 있음을 시사하는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 타인의 의견을 수용하다
② 전통을 널리 퍼뜨리다
③ 국가 영토를 보존하다
④ 따랐던 규칙들을 무시하다
⑤ 자체의 근본적인 정체성을 유지하다

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. That is, a global food system has to _______________________________ in order to have greater chance of being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
options: ① secure a wider genetic range of crops
② eliminate some species lacking nutrients
③ diversify the methods of food processing
④ rely on the most productive plant species
⑤ develop new methods to fertilize farm land
questions.explanation: 식량 생산을 위해 작물의 종류를 단순화한 것이 질병이나 기후 변화 같은 재난에 취약하게 만들었으므로, 생존 확률을 높이기 위해서는 작물의 유전적 다양성(genetic range)을 확보해야 한다는 논리가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 작물의 더 넓은 유전적 범위를 확보하다
② 영양소가 부족한 일부 종을 제거하다
③ 식품 가공 방식을 다양화하다
④ 가장 생산적인 식물 종에 의존하다
⑤ 농지를 비옥하게 할 새로운 방법을 개발하다

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. In contrast, technological metaphors are characterized as active and often imposing, as they show up in digital tools that are forcefully changing _________________________________. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
options: ① the range and the frame of meaning
③ some hidden meanings in literary works
④ old perspectives on existing biased interpretations
⑤ digital representation in terms of human relationships
questions.explanation: 언어적 은유는 독자의 능동적 해석 노력을 필요로 하는 수동적인 성격인 반면, 기술적 은유는 디지털 도구 안에서 즉각적이고 명확하게 작용하며 의미의 범위와 틀을 강제로 변화시키는 능동적이고 강요적인 성격을 가집니다.
options_translation: ① 의미의 범위와 틀
② 언어적 은유에 대한 고려
③ 문학 작품 속의 숨겨진 의미들
④ 기존의 편향된 해석에 대한 오래된 관점들
⑤ 인간 관계의 측면에서의 디지털 표현

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could _____________________________. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
options: ① contribute to our society by openly sharing our uncertainties
② interact with technologies in ways that reduce non-digital learning
③ dedicate our large brains to the final piece of an endless calculation
questions.explanation: 인간은 인지 능력의 한계로 인해 모든 정보를 스스로 처리하는 대신 사회적으로 분담하여 처리합니다. 복잡한 작동 원리를 다 알 필요 없이 인터페이스 사용법만 익힘으로써, 우리의 뇌를 거대한 집단적 계산의 마지막 조각(실제 활용 단계)에 전념할 수 있게 한다는 내용이 적절합니다. (본문 흐름상 4, 5번 보기가 잘려 있으나 주어진 3번 보기가 글의 요지와 가장 부합함)
options_translation: ① 우리의 불확실성을 공개적으로 공유함으로써 사회에 기여하다
② 비디지털 학습을 줄이는 방식으로 기술과 상호작용하다
③ 우리의 커다란 뇌를 끝없는 계산의 마지막 조각에 헌신하다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 전체 흠름겼 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. ⓐWhen middle or long distance runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race - their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't psychologically suffer much. ⓑIn fact, ultra-marathon runners - those people who are crazy enough to push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50 - 100km or more over many hours, talk about making friends with their pain. ⓒHere is another example; a patient may have paid for passive back pain therapy, where the therapist applies deep pressure to a sore area of the back to relieve tension and improve movement. ⓓPassive back pain therapy can feel soothing but it provides only temporary relief, not a permanent cure. ⓔIn that case, the patient calls that good pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 고통을 어떻겐 프벴임(재구성)하느냐에 따라 고통의 정도가 달라진다는 내용입니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ는 고통을 가치 읈다고 여기면 고통을 덜 느낀다는 사례를 들고 읈지만, ⓓ는 수동적 통증 츱료가 일시적인 완화만 제공한다는 내용으로 주제와 가까였지 않습니다.

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so.
ordered_passages: (A) It naturally means participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions.

(B) But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.

(C) Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 실험의 첫 번째 단계(달의 위상 질문) 설명이 남옵니다. (C)에서 'Then, in the second part'로 다음 단계를 설명하고 새로운 질문을 제시합니다. (A)는 이 새로운 질문에 대해 인터넷 사용자들이 객관적으로는 이점이 없음을 말하며, (B)에서 'But'을 통해 그럼에도 불구하고 그들이 스스로를 더 박식하다고 평가하는 실험 결과를 제시합니다. 따라서 순서는 (C)-(A)-(B)가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also overlooks the fact that the trend of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.summary_sentence: Social media attention can lead to elite celebrity status, but some creators aim for a more (A)_________ kind of fame. This shift (B)_________ the concept of fame, focusing on everyday connections with other people and metrics like followers, Likes, and clicks.
questions.explanation: 본문은 소셜 미디어를 통해 전통적인 엘리트 유명인사와는 다른 '평범한(ordinary)' 유명세가 나타나고 있음을 설명합니다. 이러한 평범한 유명인사는 신비로움이나 재능보다는 일상적인 소통과 수치화된 지표(구독자, 좋아요 등)를 기반으로 합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 'ordinary(평범한)'가 적절하며, 이러한 현상이 명성의 의미를 '재구성(reconstruct/redefine)'하고 있다고 했으므로 (B)에는 'redefines'가 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 예외적인 - 유지하다
② 평범한 - 재정의하다
③ 엘리트의 - 왜곡하다
④ 공통의 - 복잡하게 만들다
⑤ 비정상적인 - 좁히다

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
questions.summary_sentence: Apart from their intention, stricter regulations for brain death diagnoses of organ donors decrease public (A)_________ in the diagnostic process, and the standards for diagnosing brain death need to be (B)_________ regardless of organ donation status.
questions.explanation: 장기 기증 시 뇌사 판정 기준을 더 엄격하게 하는 것은 대중의 두려움을 완화하려는 의도였으나, 오히려 진단 과정에 대한 대중의 '신뢰(trust)'를 떨어뜨리고 부정확하다는 오해를 유지시킬 수 있습니다. 따라서 일관성을 위해 기증 여부와 상관없이 뇌사 판정 기준은 '일관되어야(consistent)' 한다는 것이 글의 핵심입니다.
options_translation: ① 의심 - 신뢰할 수 있는
② 신뢰 - 일관된
③ 의심 - 융통성 없는
④ 믿음 - 가변적인
⑤ 주의 - 일관성 있는

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용에 근거하여 밑줄 친 (A)parent trap이 문맥상 의미하는 바를 한 문장으로 표현하고자 할 때, 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 본문에서 정확히 찾아 각각 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오. (필요한 경우, 어형 변화 가능함)
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common (A)<u>parent trap</u>. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents are talking too much about them. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a dropout, or worse.
questions.summary_sentence: To fall into the parent trap means to put too much ⓐ___________ on gifted children by ⓑ___________ too much about how talented they are.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 정확히 찾아 각각 한 단어의 영어로 쓸 것
필요한 경우 어형 변화 가능
questions.explanation: 글의 내용에 따르면 영재 아동의 부모가 자녀에 대해 끊임없이 자랑하는 것은 자녀에게 스트레스와 압박감을 줍니다. 요약문에서 ⓐ는 자녀에게 주는 '압박(pressure)'을 의미하며(본문의 pressured를 명사형으로 변형), ⓑ는 부모의 '자랑하는 행위(bragging)'를 의미합니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: A ball thrown into the air is acted upon by the initial force given to it, which persists as inertia of movement and ⓐ<u>tends</u> to carry it in the same straight line, and by the constant pull of gravity downward, as well as by the resistance of the air. It moves, accordingly, in a curved path. Now the path does not represent the working of any particular force; there is simply the combination of the three elementary forces mentioned. But in a real sense, there is something in the total action besides the isolated action of three forces, which ⓑ<u>is</u> their joint action. In the same way, when two or more human individuals are together, their relationships and their arrangement into a group are ⓒ<u>that</u> would be concealed if we confined our attention to each individual separately. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that, ⓓ<u>relating</u> definitely to other persons, some of the tendencies to action of the individual could not be aroused except by other persons acting as stimuli. An individual in complete isolation would not reveal their competitive tendencies, their tendencies towards the opposite sex, their protective tendencies towards children. This shows that the traits of human nature do not fully appear until the individual ⓔ<u>mutually</u> interacts with other individuals.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 be동사(are) 뒤에 오는 보어 자리에 주어가 빠진 불완전한 절을 이끌어야 하므로, 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사인 'what'이 와야 합니다. that은 명사절 접속사로 쓰일 때 뒤에 완전한 문장이 와야 하는데, 여기서는 'would be concealed'의 주어가 비어 있습니다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 내용을 다음과 같이 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 본문에서 정확히 찾아 각각 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: A ball thrown into the air is acted upon by the initial force given to it, which persists as inertia of movement and ⓐ<u>tends</u> to carry it in the same straight line, and by the constant pull of gravity downward, as well as by the resistance of the air. It moves, accordingly, in a curved path. Now the path does not represent the working of any particular force; there is simply the combination of the three elementary forces mentioned. But in a real sense, there is something in the total action besides the isolated action of three forces, which ⓑ<u>is</u> their joint action. In the same way, when two or more human individuals are together, their relationships and their arrangement into a group are ⓒ<u>that</u> would be concealed if we confined our attention to each individual separately. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that, ⓓ<u>relating</u> definitely to other persons, some of the tendencies to action of the individual could not be aroused except by other persons acting as stimuli. An individual in complete isolation would not reveal their competitive tendencies, their tendencies towards the opposite sex, their protective tendencies towards children. This shows that the traits of human nature do not fully appear until the individual ⓔ<u>mutually</u> interacts with other individuals.
questions.summary_sentence: Individual human behaviors would be (A)__________ without the context of relationships with others. Certain traits, such as competitive or social tendencies, are (B)__________ only when individuals interact with others.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 정확히 찾아 쓸 것
각각 한 단어의 영어로 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 지문에서 개인을 따로 떼어놓고 볼 때 감춰지는 부분(concealed)이 있으며, 타인과의 관계 속에서 개인의 행동 성향이 유발된다(aroused)고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 concealed, (B)에는 aroused가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)stimuli와 문맥상 같은 개념을 의미하는 것을 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 있는 대로 모두 골라 기호로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to (A)<u>stimuli</u> each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to ⓐ<u>what was moving in a tree</u> than to ⓑ<u>the tree</u> itself. Boredom in reaction to ⓒ<u>an unchanging environment</u> turns down the level of neural excitation so that ⓓ<u>new stimuli</u> stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of turning off ⓔ<u>a front door</u> light to see ⓕ<u>the fireflies</u>.
subjective_conditions: 있는 대로 모두 골라 기호로 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 (A)의 stimuli는 신경 세포가 반복적으로 발생할 때 반응을 줄이는 '익숙하거나 변하지 않는 자극'을 의미합니다. 이에 해당하는 것은 ⓑ 나무 그 자체(변화 없는 대상), ⓒ 변하지 않는 환경, ⓔ 현관 등(배경이 되는 고정적 자극)입니다. 반면 ⓐ 나무에서 움직이는 것, ⓓ 새로운 자극, ⓕ 반딧불이는 신경이 반응을 강화하는 '변화'의 개념입니다.

questions.question: 31. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 (A)the winners가 의미하는 바를 정확히 찾아 연속된 7개의 단어로 이루어진 영어 구문으로 쓰시오. [24년 9월 21번]
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. subjective_conditions: 본문에서 연속된 7개의 단어로 찾을 것
questions.answer: those who are in a higher vibration
questions.explanation: 문맥상 (A)the winners는 부정적인 생각에서 벗어나 긍정적인 에너지를 가진 사람들을 의미합니다. 본문에서 이들을 지칭하는 표현으로 'those who are in a higher vibration'이 7단어로 정확히 일치합니다.

questions.question: 32. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 각 문장의 완결성과 의미적 타당성을 고려하여 어법상 어색한 곳을 두 개 찾아 그 기호를 쓰고, 이를 각각 바르게 고치시오. [23년 11월 36번]
questions.passage: Not until its early twenties ⓐ<u>are</u> the adolescent brain fully develop. This means ⓑ<u>how</u> the adolescents' decision-making circuits integrate and process information may put them at a disadvantage. One of their brain regions that ⓒ<u>mature</u> later is the prefrontal cortex, which is the control center, tasked with thinking ahead and evaluating consequences. It is the area of the brain that keeps you from sending off an initial angry text and ⓓ<u>modifying</u> it with kinder words, so that you can avoid unnecessary conflict. On the other hand, the limbic system, which plays a central role in processing emotional responses, ⓔ<u>develops</u> earlier. Because of its earlier development, it is more likely to influence decision-making. Due to these differences, there is an imbalance between feeling-based decision-making ruled by the more mature limbic system and logical-based decision-making by the not-yet-mature prefrontal cortex. This may explain why some teens are more likely to make bad decisions.
subjective_conditions: 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고칠 갳
questions.explanation: (1) ⓐ 문장 맨 앞의 Not until이라는 부정어구 도치로 인해 주어(the adolescent brain)와 동사가 도치되었습니다. 이땄 일반동사 develop을 강조하기 위해 조동사 does가 필요합니다. (2) ⓓ It is ~ that 강조 구문 내에서 동사 modifies는 keeps와 병갬 구조를 이루어야 합니다. modifying으로 쓰면 sending가 병갬이 되어 '친절한 말로 고츘 수 없게 한다'는 어색한 의미가 됩니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목을 한 문장으로 표현할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.summary_sentence: Are colors grounded in (A)__________ or is it a matter of (B)__________?
options: ③ our eyes / the external world
④ the real world / a property of things
questions.explanation: 이 글은 색이 사물의 객관적 속성(물리학적 측면)인지, 아니면 관찰자의 눈이나 마음에 존재하는 주관적 속성(인간의 지각 측면)인지에 대해 다루며, 결국 두 가지 측면이 만나는 지점에서 색이 생성된다고 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 물리적 속성을 의미하는 physics가, (B)에는 주관적 해석을 의미하는 human perception이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 물리학 / 인간의 지각
② 우리의 뇌 / 우리의 해석
③ 우리의 눈 / 외부 세계
④ 현실 세계 / 사물의 속성
⑤ 문화적 차이 / 인지 기능

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것을 세 개 찾아서 각각의 번호를 쓰고 바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: Nearly everything has to go through your mouth to get to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. From the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and a reflection of ⓓ<u>which</u> is happening in other parts of the body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, ⓔ<u>pose</u> serious health risks.
questions.explanation: ⓒ prevent A from B(ing) 구문으로 전치사 from 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 하므로 entering으로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓓ 전치사 of의 목적어 역할을 하며 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 문장이 오므로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what이 적절합니다. ⓔ 주절 뒤에 이어지는 분사구문으로, 미생물이 건강상의 위험을 '초래하면서'라는 능동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 현재분사인 posing이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 묜줄 친 붽분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쉄임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [23년 11월 29번]
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed more ⓐ<u>rigid</u> guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a ⓑ<u>prospective</u> donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ⓒ<u>aggravate</u> public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking ⓓ<u>accuracy</u>. questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 흠름으로 밴아 주어진 문윕이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 11월 31번]
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristic of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself. Psychologist George M. Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment. (B) In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him. (C) As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems: he used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something, for example. (D) Fortunately, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for the rest of his life. (E) For him, everything returned to normal after one day.
questions.insertion_sentence: With time, however, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문윕은 시간을 두고 시각 계통이 새로운 자극(됤집휴 세계)에 적응하여 다시 정상적으로 행동할 수 있겐 되었다는 내용입니다. 이는 (B) 뒤의 촐기 어려움을 궼복하고 적응한 과정을 내타내며, (C) 이홄 안경을 벗었을 때 다시 문제에 봉착한 내용이 나오기 전에 위치해야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [23년 11월 37번]
questions.passage: Despite the remarkable progress in deep-learning based facial recognition approaches in recent years, in terms of identification performance, they still have limitations. These limitations relate to the database used in the learning stage. For example, the performance of a facial biometric system may decrease if the person to be identified was enrolled over 10 years ago. ⓐThe factor to consider is that this person may experience changes in the texture of the face, particularly with the appearance of wrinkles and sagging skin. ⓑThese changes may be highlighted by weight gain or loss. ⓒThe use of facial recognition systems has also raised controversy, with claims that the systems violate citizens' privacy, commonly make incorrect identifications. ⓓTo counteract this problem, researchers have developed models for face aging or digital de-aging. ⓔIt is used to compensate for the differences in facial characteristics, which appear over a given time period.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 딥러닝 기반 얼굴 인식 시스템이 시간 경과에 따른 얼굴 변화(노화, 체중 변화 등) 때문에 식별 성능이 저하되는 한계점과 이를 해결하기 위한 노력을 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ③번(ⓒ)은 얼굴 인식 시스템의 사생활 침해 논란에 대해 언급하고 있으므로 기술적 한계와 해결책이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 11월 33번]
questions.passage: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson suggests that we tend to understand the world by focusing in on particular features within it. Take platypuses. We might take the platypus as an individual, or we might treat it as part of a larger unit such as a species or an ecosystem. It's possible to move between many of these perspectives, although we may need some additional tools and skills to zoom in on individual pieces of hair or zoom out to entire ecosystems. Crucially, however, we can _______________ ________. We can pay attention to the varied behavior of individual animals, look at what unites them into a single species, or look at them as part of bigger ecological patterns. Every possible perspective involves emphasizing certain aspects and ignoring others.
options: ① break the framework of old ideas
② concentrate on one thing at a time
③ add new information to what we know
④ consider both bright and dark sides of it
⑤ have multiple perspectives for critical thinking
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장에서 모든 가능한 관점은 특정 측면을 강조하고 다른 측면을 무시하는 것을 포함한다고 언급합니다. 즉, 여러 관점을 동시에 취하는 것이 아니라 한 번에 하나의 관점에 집중한다는 의미이므로 빈칸에는 '한 번에 한 가지에만 집중할 수 있다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.

⑤ 비판적 사고를 위해 다각적인 관점을 가지다

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In statistics, the law of large numbers describes a situation where __________ is better for making predictions. But the more often you repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning, meaning that your luck will at some point fade away. Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to balance individual losses.
options: ⑤ expecting the true chance of winning
questions.explanation: 이 글은 통계학의 '대수의 법칙'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 대수의 법칙은 실험 횟수가 많아질수록(데이터가 많아질수록) 결과의 평균이 실제 확률에 가까워진다는 원리입니다. 카지노나 보험사가 많은 양의 데이터를 수집하여 예측의 정확도를 높이는 사례를 통해 알 수 있듯이, 빈칸에는 '더 많은 데이터를 정리하는 것'이 예측에 더 유리하다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time. The country that ruled international baseball for decades has not been on top since that uniform change. questions.question: 14. 윗글의 내용과 가장 일치하는 것은? [2.7점]

⑤ 던져진 공의 경로는 특정 힘의 작동으로 나타난다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 (B) 단락 마지막 문장인 'This shows that the traits of human nature do not fully appear until the individual is brought into relationships with other individuals.'를 통해 인간의 본성이 타인과의 관계 속에 놓일 때 비로소 온전히 나타난다는 것을 알 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 15. 윗글 (A) 다음에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: (A) A ball thrown into the air is acted upon by the initial force given it, persisting as inertia of movement and tending to carry it in the same straight line, and by the constant pull of gravity downward, as well as by the resistance of the air.
ordered_passages: (B) An individual in complete isolation would not reveal their competitive tendencies, their tendencies towards the opposite sex, their protective tendencies towards children. This shows that the traits of human nature do not fully appear until the individual is brought into relationships with other individuals.

(C) In the same way, when two or more human individuals are together, their mutual relationships and their arrangement into a group are things which would not be revealed if we confined our attention to each individual separately. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that some of the tendencies to action of the individual are related definitely to other persons, and could not be aroused except by other persons acting as stimuli.

(D) It moves, accordingly, in a curved path.
