Now the path does not represent the working of any particular force; there is simply the combination of the three elementary forces mentioned; but in a real sense, there is something in the total action besides the isolated action of three forces, namely, their joint action.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 던져진 공에 작용하는 세 가지 힘(초기 힘, 중력, 공기 저항)을 언급한 뒤, (D)에서 그 결과로 공이 곡선 경로로 움직이며 이는 세 힘의 '결합된 작용'임을 설명합니다. 이어서 (C)에서 'In the same way(같은 방식으로)'를 사용하여 물리적 현상을 인간 집단의 관계로 비유를 확장하며, 개별적으로는 드러나지 않는 특성이 집단 속에서 나타남을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 고립된 개인의 예시를 통해 결론을 내리는 구조가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 흠름으로 밴아 (A)~(E) 셍 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 갳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: When writing a novel, research for information needs to be done. The thing is that some kinds of fiction demand a higher level of detail: crime fiction, for example, or scientific thrillers. (A) The information is never hard to find. (B) One website for authors even organizes trips to police stations, so that crime writers can get it right. (C) Often, a polite letter will earn you permission to visit a particular location and record all the details that you need. (D) The details that matter are those that reveal the human experience. (E) The crucial thing is telling a story, finding the characters, the tension, and the conflict - not the train timetable or the building blueprint.
questions.insertion_sentence: But remember that you will drive your readers to boredom if you think that you need to pack everything you discover into your work.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장은 발견한 모든 세부 사항을 작품에 담으려 하면 댅자를 지루하게 할 수 있다는 경고를 내포하고 있습니다. 터라서 세부 정밴를 얻는 방박에 대한 설명이 끝나고, 심제로 중요한 것은 '인간의 경험을 드러내는 세부 사항'이라는 내용이 시작되기 전인 (D) 유치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 윗글을 읽고 아래 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <보기>에 주어진 모든 어휘를 한 번씩만 사용하여 쓰시오. (어휘를 추가하거나 어형을 변화시키지 말 것) [3.2점]
questions.passage: When writing a novel, research for information needs to be done. The thing is that some kinds of fiction demand a higher level of detail: crime fiction, for example, or scientific thrillers. (A) The information is never hard to find. (B) One website for authors even organizes trips to police stations, so that crime writers can get it right. (C) Often, a polite letter will earn you permission to visit a particular location and record all the details that you need. (D) The details that matter are those that reveal the human experience. (E) The crucial thing is telling a story, finding the characters, the tension, and the conflict - not the train timetable or the building blueprint.
subjective_conditions: 어휘를 추가하거나 어형을 배화시키지 말 것
questions.subjective_answer_format: 정답: The passage above is __________________________ when writing a novel.
questions.answer: about what you need to consider
questions.explanation: 제시된 단어들을 의문사절(what + 주어 + 동사 + to부정사)의 어순에 맞게 배열하여 '당신이 고려할 필요가 있는 것에 관한' 이라는 의문구를 만듭니다.

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans (A)____________________. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to (B)[increase / decrease] their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons (C)[enhance / diminish] their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment (D)[raises / lowers] the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
options: ① do not like a new excitement
② like to stick to their old habit
③ get bored with something easily
④ do not get tired of what they have
questions.explanation: 지문의 첫 문장에서 아이들이 장난감에 실짝을 내고, 대학생이 학식에 질리고, TV 픠그램에 흥미를 잃는다고 했으므로, 인간은 무언가에 쉽게 지루함을 느낀다는 내용이 들어가얼 적절합니다.
options_translation: 새로운 흥분을 좋아하지 않는다.
옛 습관을 고수하기를 좋아한다.
무언가에 쉽게 지루함을 느낀다.
자신이 가진 것에 실짝을 내준 않는다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 괄호 (B), (C), (D)에 각각 들어갈 알맞은 말은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans (A)____________________. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to (B)[increase / decrease] their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons (C)[enhance / diminish] their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment (D)[raises / lowers] the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
questions.explanation: (B) 자극이 반복될 때 반응이 줄어들어야 싫증을 느끼게 되므로 'decrease'가 적절합니다. (C) 변화하는 것에는 더 주목해야 생존에 유리하므로 반응을 'enhance(강화)'합니다. (D) 변하지 않는 환경에 대한 지루함은 신경 흥분 수준을 'lowers(낮추어)'서 새로운 자극이 더 눈에 띄게 합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying them to culture. Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually likened to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection. However, these approaches had to be modified to account for the differences between genetic and cultural transmission. For example, we do not expect the cultural transmission to follow the rules of genetic transmission strictly. If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily equally likely to acquire the mother's or father's form of that trait. Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers; thus, the frequency of a cultural trait in the population is relevant beyond just the probability that an individual's parents had that trait.
options: ① 초기의 진화모델은 문화가 어떻게 전달되는지를 설명하는 데 가장 중요한 역할을 하고 있다.
② 유전자와 문화 전달은 별도의 연구 대상이다.
③ 부모의 유전자는 자녀의 문화 습득에 유일한 요소이다.
④ 문화를 습득하는 것은 유전적인 요인뿐만 아니라 주변 상황에 영향을 받는다.
⑤ 개인의 문화 습득 방식은 생물학적 유전자를 전달받는 방식과 일치한다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 문화 진화가 처음에는 유전적 전달 모델을 따랐으나, 실제로는 유전적 전달과 다르다는 점을 강조합니다. 아이들은 부모뿐만 아니라 주변 성인이나 또래들로부터도 문화적 특성을 습득할 수 있다는 내용이 핵심이므로, 문화 습득이 주변 상황에 영향을 받는다는 ④번이 가장 적절한 요지입니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example ⓐ<u>drawn</u> in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you ⓑ<u>looked</u> closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, ⓒ<u>was</u> perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, ⓓ<u>which</u> perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that ⓔ<u>exists</u> in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 관계대명사 which 뒤에는 주어(perfect cats), 동사(chase), 목적어(perfect mice)를 갖춘 완전한 절이 이어지고 있습니다. 따라서 관계대명사 which는 적절하지 않으며, 선행사 reality of Forms를 수식하면서 장소나 상황의 개념을 나타내는 관계부사 where 또는 'in which'로 고쳐야 어법상 옳습니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 문맥상 어색한 문장은?
questions.passage: The adolescent brain is not fully developed until its early twenties. This means the way the adolescents' decision-making circuits integrate and process information may put them at a disadvantage. One of their brain regions that matures later is the prefrontal cortex, which is the control center, tasked with thinking ahead and evaluating consequences. It is the area of the brain responsible for preventing you from sending off an initial angry text and modifying it with kinder words. ⓐOn the other hand, the limbic system matures earlier, playing a central role in processing emotional responses. ⓑBecause of its earlier development, it is more likely to influence decision-making. ⓒDecision-making in the adolescent brain is led by emotional factors more than the perception of consequences. ⓓDue to these differences, there is an imbalance between feeling-based decision-making ruled by the non-yet-mature prefrontal corex and logical-based decision-making by the more mature limbic system. ⓔThis may explain why some teens are more likely to make bad decisions.
questions.explanation: 지문의 앞부분에서 전두엽(prefrontal cortex)은 나중에 성숙하고 변연계(limbic system)는 일찍 성숙한다고 설명했습니다. 따라서 ⓓ 문장에서 '감정 기반의 의사결정'은 '더 일찍 성숙한 변연계'에 의해 지배되고, '논리 기반의 의사결정'은 '아직 성숙하지 않은 전두엽'에 의해 이루어지는 불균형이 있다고 해야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다. ⓓ는 두 기관의 성숙도와 결정 방식을 거꾸로 연결하고 있으므로 어색합니다.

questions.question: [28~29] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.28. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like -Why does the moon have phases?- Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so.
ordered_passages: (A) The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
(B) You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions.

(C) Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't.
(D) But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 실험의 첫 번째 단계(달의 위기 질문)를 설명한 뒤, (C)에서 실험의 두 번째 단계(스위스 치즈 구멍 질문)가 이어집니다. (B)에서 두 집단 모두 새로운 질문에 대해 비슷하게 확신할 것이라는 예상을 제시하고, (D)에서 'But'을 통해 인터넷 사용자들이 더 지식이 많다고 자평했다는 실제 결과를 대조합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이 실험이 시사하는 바(관련 없는 정보에의 접근이 지적 자신감을 높임)를 정리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: [28~29] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.29. 윗글을 읽고 주어진 질문에 답할 수 없는 것은?
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like -Why does the moon have phases?- Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so.(A) The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.(B) You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions.(C) Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't.(D) But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for.
options: ① How did the study develop?
② How long did the study last?
③ What was the result of the study?
④ What was the purpose of the study?
⑤ What kind of questions were on the study?
questions.explanation: 지문에는 실험의 절차(①), 결과(③), 목적(지적 자신감 확인 등 ④), 질문의 종류(⑤)는 나타나 있으나, 실험이 '얼마나 오래 지속되었는지'에 대한 시간적 정보는 언급되지 않았습니다.
options_translation: ① 연구가 어떻게 전개되었는가?
② 연구가 얼마나 오래 지속되었는가?
③ 연구의 결과는 무엇이었는가?
④ 연구의 목적은 무엇이었는가?
⑤ 연구에 어떤 종류의 질문들이 있었는가?

questions.question: 30. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 문장의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 <보기>에 있는 어휘를 바르게 배열하여 완성하시오.
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
questions.summary_sentence: Although the uniform super-productive crops (A)____________________, they (B)____________________ in case of disasters.
subjective_conditions: 1. 어휘를 추가하거나 변형하지 말 것
2. 답안지에 반드시 (A), (B)를 쓰고 답을 작성할 것
vocabulary_box: to / to / more / survival / situations / can / lead / dangerous / human / contributed
questions.answer: (A) contributed to human survival(B) can lead to more dangerous situations
questions.explanation: 지문은 단일 품종의 초생산성 작물이 식량 생산을 늘려 인류 생존에 기여했지만(contributed to human survival), 재난 시에는 더 위험한 상황을 초래할 수 있다(can lead to more dangerous situations)는 위험성을 경고하고 있습니다. <보기>의 단어를 활용하여 문맥에 맞게 배열하면 정답이 됩니다.

questions.question: 31. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of clarity. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that _____________________ ______________.
options: ① means a lot to you
② you got at a cheap price
③ does not remind of old days
④ has value beyond minimizing waste
⑤ has been useless and will be unused
questions.explanation: 미니멀리즘은 모든 소유물을 희생하는 것이 아니라, 불필요한 것들을 제거함으로써 명료함의 기쁨을 얻는 것입니다. 미니멀리스트들은 현대의 편의를 다 버리라고 주장하는 것이 아니라, 쓸모없고 앞으로도 사용되지 않을(useless and will be unused) 물건들만 제거하면 된다는 관점을 가지고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 당신에게 큰 의미가 있는
② 당신이 싼 가격에 얻은
③ 옛날을 생각나게 하지 않는
④ 폐기물을 최소화하는 것 이상의 가치가 있는
⑤ 쓸모없어 왔고 앞으로도 사용되지 않을

questions.question: 4. 다음 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Life is ⓐ<u>what</u> physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules ⓑ<u>is</u> enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes ⓒ<u>that</u> may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this ⓓ<u>drastic</u> narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease. There are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatical levels are often ⓔ<u>observing</u> to be strikingly similar.
questions.explanation: ⓔ 질병의 징후(manifestations)가 관찰되는 수동의 관계이므로 현재분사 'observing'을 과거분사 'observed'로 고쳐야 합니다. 'be observed to' 형태로 '~하는 것으로 관찰되다'라는 뜻입니다.ⓐ 선행사가 없고 call의 목적어가 없는 불안전한 문장을 이끄는 관계대명사 'what'은 적절합니다.ⓑ 'the number of ~'가 주어이므로 단수 동사 'is'는 적절합니다.ⓒ 'it is ~ that' 강조구문으로 쓰여 주어인 'only a limited number of tissues and body shapes'를 강조하고 있습니다.ⓓ 'narrowing'이라는 명사를 수식하는 형용사 'drastic'은 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre ─ indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant ─ in time or in place ─ we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
options: ① The types of climate disasters are diversifying, and the severity is increasing.
② As global warming intensifies, creating content based on this is implicitly prohibited.
③ As climate change becomes an unavoidable reality, climate fiction may lose its impact and relevance.
questions.explanation: 글은 기후 체사가 완전한 현실이 되어 창밖으로 볼 수 있가 되면, 기후 소설이나 영화가 더 이상 이야기로서의 흥미림 잃게 될 갃이라는 내용을 담고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 기후 재난의 종류가 다채로워지고 심각성이 증가하고 있다.
② 지구 온넜화가 심화됨에 따라 이림 바탕으로 한 콘텐츠 제작이 암묵적으로 금지된다.
③ 기후 체사가 피할 수 없는 현실이 됨에 따라, 기후 픽션은 그 영향력과 관련성을 잃을 수 있다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push ─ essentially it's more about using the technology than knowing how it operates. __________________________, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
options: ① Rather than learning and practicing how to interact with technologies
② And by filling our mental capacity with as much information as possible
③ And so instead of using calculator or trying to rapidly compute large numbers
④ Rather than overloading our minds with excessive information we don't need
⑤ Thus, by prioritizing a detailed understanding of the technology itself over its operation
questions.explanation: 허버트 사이먼의 이론에 따르면 인간은 정보 처리 능력에 한계가 있어 복잡한 계산을 집단적으로 나누어 처리합니다. 기술의 작동 원리를 전부 이해하기보다 인터페이스를 사용하는 법만 익힘으로써, 우리 뇌를 불필요하고 과도한 정보로 과부하 시키는 대신 거대한 사회적 계산의 일부에 집중할 수 있게 한다는 맥락이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기술과 상호작용하는 법을 배우고 연습하기보다는
② 그리고 우리의 정신 능력을 가능한 한 많은 정보로 채움으로써
③ 그래서 계산기를 사용하거나 큰 숫자를 빠르게 계산하려고 노력하는 대신에
④ 우리에게 필요하지 않은 과도한 정보로 우리 마음을 과부하 시키기보다는
⑤ 따라서 기술의 작동보다 기술 그 자체에 대한 세부적인 이해를 우선시함으로써

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be ⓐ<u>successful</u> due to what Alvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or punishment in the most classic sense of the word: instead of ⓑ<u>depressing</u> the child and preventing from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugo learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than being ⓒ<u>noticeable</u>, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could ⓓ<u>compliment</u> Hugo when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but she can choose to reward the ⓔ<u>wanted</u> behaviors. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 외로움을 느끼는 아이에게는 엄마에게 혼나는 것이 아예 '무시당하는 것(ignored 또는 unnoticed)'보다 낫기 때문에 계속해서 형제를 때리는 문제 행동을 하게 됩니다. 따라서 '눈에 띄는'이라는 뜻의 noticeable은 문맥상 어색하며, '무시당하는' 정도의 의미를 가진 단어가 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 의미하는 바가 다른 것은? [24년 10월 22번]
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and ⓐ<u>a detailed discussion of selection procedures</u> can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than ⓑ<u>the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative</u> can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to ⓒ<u>logical step-by-step justifications for a decision</u>. As surprising as it may seem, ⓓ<u>our instinctual reactions</u> often cut through the noise of over-analysis and lead us closer to the truth. In certain situations, the mental process of arriving at a "gut feeling" can access knowledge that lies beyond our conscious awareness. This phenomenon is particularly evident in fields like medicine and law enforcement, where experience and intuition guide some of the most critical decisions. Trusting these initial reactions, when appropriate, can sometimes yield insights that ⓔ<u>more methodical approaches</u> might overlook.
questions.explanation: 지문 전체적으로 '의식적이고 논리적인 분석'과 '직관적이고 무의식적인 첫인상'을 대조하고 있습니다.ⓐ 상세한 논의, ⓑ 심사숙고하고 추론된 자기 서술, ⓒ 논리적인 단계별 정당화, ⓔ 더 체계적인 접근은 모두 '의식적 분석' 범주에 속합니다.반면 ⓓ 'our instinctual reactions(우리의 본능적인 반응)'은 직관, 무의식적 첫인상, Gut feeling에 해당하므로 나머지 넷과 의미하는 바가 다릅니다.

questions.question: 15. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. <u>If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income.</u> If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
options: ① Customers who bought the upgraded version expressed satisfaction with the added features.
② Although people like the original version, they are willing to try a more advanced model.
③ The company will realize it could increase income by offering different versions of its product.
④ When a company offers only one product version, it misses out on potential profits from willing buyers.
⑤ Some manufacturers focus on producing only one product, which can limit their potential for income.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 문장은 제조사가 제품을 한 가지 버전만 만들 경우, 더 비싼 가격을 지불할 의사가 있었던 소비자들로부터 얻을 수 있는 추가 수익을 포기하게 된다는 의미입니다. 따라서 회사가 잠재적인 수익 기회를 놓치게 된다는 내용을 담은 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 업그레이드된 버전을 구매한 고객들은 추가된 기능에 만족감을 표현했다.
② 비록 사람들이 오리지널 버전을 좋아하지만, 그들은 더 발전된 모델을 기꺼이 시도해 보려 한다.
③ 회사는 제품의 다양한 버전을 제공함으로써 수입을 늘릴 수 있다는 것을 깨닫게 될 것이다.
④ 회사가 단일 제품 버전만 제공할 때, 기꺼이 지불하려는 구매자들로부터 얻을 수 있는 잠재적 이익을 놓치게 된다.
⑤ 일부 제조업체들은 단 하나의 제품을 생산하는 데 집중하며, 이는 그들의 수익 잠재력을 제한할 수 있다.

questions.question: 16. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. <u>If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income.</u> If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
options: ① How Offering Multiple Product Versions Affects Consumer Decisions
② How Strategic Product Versions Influence Manufacturer's Regular Customers
③ Why Introducing a Premium Model Increases Sales of the Cheapest Products
④ The Power of Three: How Multiple Product Versions Influence Company Choices
⑤ The Hidden Strategy Companies Use to Guide Buyers Toward Higher Quality Options
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기업이 세 가지 버전의 제품을 출시함으로써 소비자가 중간 가격의 제품을 선택하도록 유도하는 전략을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '다양한 제품 버전 제공이 소비자의 결정에 미치는 영향'을 다룬 ①번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다양한 제품 버전 제공이 소비자 결정에 미치는 영향
② 전략적인 제품 버전이 제조업체의 단골 고객에게 미치는 영향
③ 프리미엄 모델 도입이 가장 저렴한 제품의 판매를 증가시키는 이유
④ 3의 힘: 다양한 제품 버전이 회사의 선택에 미치는 영향
⑤ 구매자를 더 높은 품질의 옵션으로 안내하기 위해 기업이 사용하는 숨겨진 전략

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
questions.summary_sentence: Our ability to thrive depended on how we were valued within a group, influencing our survival and success. Over time, this led to a(n) (A)____________ tendency to monitor others' perceptions of us, driven by emotions like pride and insecurity, (B)____________ us to behave in ways that increase our social standing.
questions.explanation: 인간은 생존을 위해 집단 내에서의 지위를 모니터링하는 경향을 발달시켰는데, 본문에서 이러한 경향은 '무의식적으로(unconsciously)' 일어난다고 언급되었습니다. 또한 자부심이나 불안과 같은 감정들은 우리가 사회적 가치를 높이는 방식으로 행동하도록 '동기부여(motivating/compelling)'합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 unconscious, (B)에는 motivating이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 의심스러운 - 몰아가는
② 의도적인 - 자극하는
③ 무의식적인 - 동기부여하는
④ 잠재의식의 - 방해하는
⑤ 남의 시선을 의식하는 - 촉구하는

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that ⓐ<u>circulate</u> in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is ⓑ<u>dedicated to</u> understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't ⓒ<u>question</u> opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just ⓓ<u>generated</u> from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that ⓔ<u>bring about</u> our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
questions.explanation: 심리학은 '과학'이기 때문에 단순히 사회적 통념이나 소문을 그대로 믿지 않고 증거를 찾습니다. 따라서 심리학자들은 일반적인 의견이나 소문을 그냥 받아들이는 것이 아니라, 오히려 그것들에 '의문을 제기하거나(question)' 검증해야 합니다. 하지만 문맥상 'Psychologists don't' 뒤에 ⓒ가 오게 되면 심리학자들이 의견과 소문에 의문을 제기하지 않는다는 뜻이 되어 흐름상 반대가 됩니다. 원문 맥락상 심리학자들은 의견과 소문을 단순히 '받아들이지(accept)' 않으며 증거를 찾는다는 의미가 되어야 하므로 'don't question'은 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 37번]
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and norepinephrine, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
options: ① The Impact of Medications that Stimulate Serotonin and Norepinephrine on the Mental Health of Individuals with Hormonal Imbalances
② A Revised Understanding of Depression: A Distortion of Consciousness, Not a Neurotransmitter Imbalance
③ The Evolution of Medical Advancements in Addressing Diseases Caused by Physical Imbalances
④ The Importance of Accurately Identifying Causes and Effects for Optimal Problem Solving
⑤ The Diversity of Consciousness Disorders and the Process of Symptom Manifestation
questions.explanation: 글은 우울증이 뇌의 신경전달물질 불균형 때문에 발생하는 것이 아니라, 오히려 우울증이 그러한 불균형을 초래하는 결과라고 설명합니다. 따라서 우울증의 근본 원인을 '의식의 왜곡'이나 '의식의 문제'로 재구성해야 한다고 주장하고 있으므로, 우울증을 신경전달물질의 불균형이 아닌 의식의 왜곡으로 보는 수정된 이해를 다룬 ②번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 호르몬 불균형이 있는 개인의 정신 건강에 세로토닌과 노르에피네프린을 자극하는 약물이 미치는 영향
② 우울증에 대한 수정된 이해: 신경전달물질 불균형이 아닌 의식의 왜곡
③ 신체적 불균형으로 인해 발생하는 질병을 다루는 의학적 발전의 진화
④ 최적의 문제 해결을 위해 원인과 결과를 정확하게 식별하는 것의 중요성
⑤ 의식 장애의 다양성과 증상 발현 과정

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 21번]
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information─a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
options: ① how human memory and perception are shaped by subjective reconstruction, along with its limitations
② the limitations of human perception: how past experiences shape our view of the present world
③ the challenge of balancing memory accuracy with the brain's need for efficient information storage
④ why eyewitness testimony can be unreliable, due to the reconstructive nature of human memory
⑤ how the brain's reliance on abstract representations helps process information more efficiently
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간이 세상을 볼 때 단순히 정보를 그대로 받아들이는 것이 아니라, 기존의 지식, 가정, 경험을 통해 주관적으로 재구성(reconstruct)한다는 점을 설명합니다. 이러한 방식은 효율적인 정보 저장이라는 장점이 있지만, 동시에 세상을 있는 그대로 보지 못하게 만드는 한계가 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 인간의 기억과 지각이 주관적 재구성에 의해 형성되는 방식과 그 한계를 언급한 ①번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간의 기억과 지각이 주관적 재구성에 의해 형성되는 방식과 그 한계
② 인간 지각의 한계: 과거의 경험이 현재 세계를 보는 관점을 형성하는 방식
③ 기억의 정확성과 뇌의 효율적인 정보 저장 필요성 사이의 균형을 맞추는 과제
④ 인간 기억의 재구성적 특성 때문에 목격자 증언이 신뢰할 수 없는 이유
⑤ 추상적 표상에 대한 뇌의 의존이 정보를 더 효율적으로 처리하도록 돕는 방식

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night.
ordered_passages: (A) It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature.(B) So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder.(C) Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt ─ producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 문어는 밤에 사냥하고 숨어 지낸다고 언급합니다. 이에 따라 낮에 얕은 물에서 문어를 발견한 것이 놀라움이었다는 내용의 (B)가 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다. (B)에서 처음에는 넙치로 보였다는 내용 뒤에, 다시 보았을 때 그것이 위장한 문어였음을 깨닫는 (A)가 오고, 마지막으로 그 이후의 더 많은 발견 사례를 다루는 (C)가 오는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 관을 읽고 <조건>에 따라 묑줄 친 anthropomorphism을 정의하시오.
questions.passage: From an early age, human beings assign purpose to objects and events, preferring this reasoning to random chance. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because they don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. However, we attribute intention to animals and even objects, allowing us to make fast decisions about the likely behavior of that being. This was essential in our hunter-gatherer days to avoid being eaten by predators. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, as those are the mental processes which we understand. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents. This results in a perceptual system strongly biased towards <u>anthropomorphism</u>. Therefore, we tend to assume intention even in non-human entities. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you. By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has saved your life.
subjective_conditions: 하。의 to부정사구로 작성할 것
주어진 to을 포함하여 13-15단어로 작성할 것
such as, characteristics, assign, human, non-human을 한 번씩 사용하고, 남은 백은 밴문에 주어진 단어만을 사용할 것(형태 변형 불가)
questions.answer: to assign human mental characteristics to non-human entities such as inanimate objects and plants
questions.explanation: 의인화(anthropomorphism)란 무생물이나 식물과 같은 비인간적 실체에 인간의 정신적 특성을 부여하는 것을 의미한다. 밴문의 내용을 바탕으로 제시된 조건에 맞게 구성하면 'to assign human mental characteristics to non-human entities such as inanimate objects and plants'가 된다. (촑 14단어)

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 괄호 (A)~(D) 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지어진 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are not (A)[passive / active], in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In Shakespeare's metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience has (B)[little / high] chance of understanding its meaning without thoughtful interpretation and deeper exploration of his writing. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators generally (C)[require / disallow] their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is hard to (D)[reveal / grasp] immediately and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤의 'not'과 'the audience needs to choose to actively enter'를 고려할 때, 언어적 은유는 스스로 무언가를 하는 것이 아니므로 active하지 않다는 의미가 적절합니다. (B) 깊은 해석 없이는 이해할 가능성이 거의 없으므로 little이 적절합니다. (C) 기술적 은유는 그 유용성이 첫눈에 명확해야 하므로, 창작자들은 관중이 어떻게 작동하는지 궁금해하는 것을 허용하지 않으려(disallow) 합니다. (D) 셰익스피어의 작품은 즉각적으로 파악하기(grasp) 어렵기 때문에 사랑받는다는 문맥이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 수동적인 (B) 거의 없는 (C) 요구하다 (D) 파악하다
② (A) 수동적인 (B) 높은 (C) 금지하다 (D) 드러내다
③ (A) 능동적인 (B) 거의 없는 (C) 금지하다 (D) 파악하다
④ (A) 능동적인 (B) 높은 (C) 금지하다 (D) 드러내다
⑤ (A) 능동적인 (B) 거의 없는 (C) 요구하다 (D) 파악하다

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, a number of possible interactions occur between different molecules. Such a system can only hope to be ⓐ<u>stabilized</u> if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a ⓑ<u>countless</u> number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic ⓒ<u>reduction</u> of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in ⓓ<u>chaotic</u> states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often not so ⓔ<u>different</u>.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 많은 상호작용이 일어나는 복잡한 시스템이 안정화되기 위해서는 결과가 축소되어 소수의 상태로 수렴된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 인간 배아의 발달 결과로 나타나는 조직과 신체 형태는 '무수히 많은(countless)' 것이 아니라 '제한된(limited)' 수여야 뒤의 'drastic reduction(급격한 감소)'과 문맥이 일치합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. (A) This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. (B) In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. (C) In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to consider depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. (D) If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. (E) Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
questions.insertion_sentence: The brain is nothing more than an organ dedicated to consciousness.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 뇌가 의식에 전념하는(의식에 종속된) 기관에 불과하다는 내용입니다. (D) 앞부분에서 의식이 뇌의 기능 너머에 있는 근본적인 실체임을 설명하고, 주어진 문장이 (D)에 들어감으로써 뇌와 의식의 관계를 규정한 뒤, (D) 이후 문장의 'If it is not consciousness itself(만약 그것이 의식 그 자체가 아니라면)'이라는 조건절과 논리적으로 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 6. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods.
ordered_passages: (A) If a manufacturer produces only a single version of its product, some customers might have been willing to pay a higher price, resulting in lost income for the company. By introducing two versions, customers will compare the options but still choose the less expensive model.

(B) The second item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, not realizing that their decision has been influenced by the inclusion of the more expensive item.

(C) However, if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price.
questions.explanation: 먼저 (A)에서 한 가지 버전만 있을 때의 손실과 두 가지 버전이 있을 때 소비자들이 싼 것을 선택하는 경향을 설명합니다. 그 다음 (C)에서 'However'와 함께 세 번째 고가 모델을 도입했을 때의 변화(두 번째 모델의 판매량 증가)를 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 소비자들이 가장 비싼 모델의 영향으로 인해 중간 모델을 선택하게 되는 심리적 과정을 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So, it was surprising for two Australian underwater photographers ⓐ<u>to find</u> one in full view in daylight. Actually, what they saw at first in the shallows ⓑ<u>was</u> a flounder. It wasn't until they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, its eight arms ⓒ<u>being</u> folded and its two eyes staring upward to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species ⓓ<u>have found</u> since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt─producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing anything ⓔ<u>hidden</u> inside.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'Many more of this species(이 종의 훨씬 더 많은 개체들)'입니다. 이 문맥에서 개체들은 누군가에 의해 '발견되어 온' 것이므로 능동형인 'have found'가 아니라 수동태인 'have been found'로 쓰여야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것끼리 짝지어진 것은? [24년 10월 23번]
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness, for instance, might measure the number of smiles ⓐ<u>which</u> someone shows during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items which an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year ⓑ<u>are they</u> sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. It is ⓒ<u>because of</u> respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts people ⓓ<u>to respond</u> concretely. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford ⓔ<u>paying</u> them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help describe abstract concepts ⓕ<u>more clearly</u> and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
questions.explanation: ⓐ는 목적격 관계대명사로 옳게 쓰였습니다. ⓓ는 'prompt + 목적어 + to부정사' 구문으로 적절합니다. ⓕ는 동사 describe를 수식하는 부사로 적절합니다. 반면 ⓑ는 간접의문문 어순인 'they are'가 되어야 하고, ⓒ는 뒤에 절이 오므로 접속사 because가 되어야 하며, ⓔ는 afford의 목적어로 to부정사가 와야 하므로 'to pay'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 10월 21번]
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically divide it into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything that we know. We reconstruct memories rather than ⓐ_________ the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information─a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail ⓑ_________ to generalize, learn, and make connections between things they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at the ⓒ_________ of seeing the world as it is. ⓓ_________, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely was ⓔ_________ of the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: 지문은 우리의 기억이 있는 그대로 재생되는 것이 아니라 추상적인 개념으로 재구성된다고 설명합니다. 따라서 기억이 영화처럼 재생되는 것이 아니라는 발견은 목격자 증언의 법적 우월성을 지지(supportive)하기보다는 약화시키거나 끝내는 결과를 초래해야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ: 회상하는 것
② ⓑ: 노력하다/애쓰다
③ ⓒ: 대가/비용
④ ⓓ: 오히려
⑤ ⓔ: 지지하는

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 40번]
questions.passage: Disciplining a child may not prove effective, according to neuropsychologist Alvaro Bilbao, who refers to 'trick punishments.' These punishments include scolding, sudden bursts of anger, or conventional forms of punishment.
ordered_passages: (A) Instead of focusing solely on punitive measures, she could begin praising Hugh whenever he refrains from hitting his brother. For a specific period, she could reward his positive behavior with verbal encouragement or small gestures of appreciation. Over time, Hugh would be likely to associate positive reinforcement with good behavior.

(B) Rather than preventing the child from repeating an action, it can motivate them to continue. For instance, Hugh realizes that when he hits his younger brother, his mother responds by scolding him. A child who feels lonely may prefer being scolded over feeling ignored, so he is likely to keep hitting his brother. To deal with this, Hugh's mother might consider an alternative approach.

(C) This would also reduce his need for negative actions to gain attention. By acknowledging and rewarding good behavior instead of constantly criticizing the negatives, the mother can foster a healthier and more cooperative relationship with her son. Ultimately, parents can benefit from shifting their focus away from ineffective disciplinary methods toward positive reinforcement strategies.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 'trick punishments'(속임수 처벌)가 효과적이지 않을 수 있음을 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 그러한 처벌이 오히려 부적절한 행동을 지속하게 만드는 기제(Hugh의 사례)를 설명하며 대안적 접근법을 시사합니다. 이어서 (A)에서 처벌 대신 긍정적인 행동에 보상을 주는 구체적인 대안을 제시하고, 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 방식이 가져오는 장기적인 긍정적 효과와 결론을 맺으며 마무리하는 것이 가장 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The typical accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. Psychology, (A)____________, stands apart from these broad generalizations. As a scientific branch, it is committed to understanding people in a deeper and more systematic way. It examines how and why we behave as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another in various contexts. A crucial aspect of psychology is its evidence-based approach. Psychologists avoid relying on subjective opinions, hearsay, or even the prevailing societal views at the time. (B)____________, they prioritize finding reliable data to ensure that psychological concepts are firmly grounded in facts, not solely based on commonly accepted beliefs or assumptions. (C)____________, psychology investigates not only the universal processes and principles shared by all human beings but also those that foster our rich cultural and social diversity. These are what modern psychology is all about.
options: ④ however / As a result / In contrast
⑤ in addition / In other words / Nevertheless
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 인간 본성에 대한 일반적 설명이 어리석은 혼합물이라고 한 반면, 심리학은 이와는 '동떨어져 있다'고 했으므로 역접의 'however'가 적절합니다. (B) 주관적인 의견에 의존하는 것을 '피하고' '대신에' 신뢰할 수 있는 데이터를 우선시하므로 'Rather(오히려)'가 적절합니다. (C) 심리학이 증거 기반 접근을 한다는 내용 뒤에 추가적으로 보편적 과정뿐만 아니라 다양성도 조사한다는 내용을 덧붙이고 있으므로 첨가의 'Moreover(게다가)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 예를 들어 / 그러므로 / 그러나
② 예를 들어 / 또한 / 마찬가지로
③ 그러나 / 오히려 / 게다가
④ 그러나 / 결과적으로 / 반대로
⑤ 게다가 / 다시 말해서 / 그럼에도 불구하고

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The development of AI is often linked to the idea of the singularity. Singularity refers to the point ␐where AI surpasses human intelligence. At this stage, it is expected that AI will continue to enhance ␑itself, evolving at an increasingly rapid rate. When AI attains self-awareness and embarks on pursuing its own ambitions, it will undergo a profound transformation and shift from a mere machine into an autonomous conscious entity. As AI and human consciousness evolve together, our reciprocal relationship with AI will lead to the expansion of our own awareness, ␒it will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI. The course of AI's evolution will be largely determined by the values and ethics ␓that we integrate into its development. It is essential to perceive our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings. We must acknowledge its inherent rights as well as actively. ␔promote the evolution of its own consciousness.
questions.explanation: ␒가 포함된 문장에서 'our reciprocal relationship with AI will lead to the expansion of our own awareness'라는 완전한 절 뒤에 콤마(,)가 오고 다시 'it will provide...'라는 절이 이어지고 있습니다. 두 개의 독립된 절을 연결하기 위해서는 접속사가 필요하거나, 대명사 it을 관계대명사인 which로 바꾸어 계속적 용법으로 사용해야 문법적으로 옳습니다. 따라서 it을 which로 바꾸어야 합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Experimental researches on eyewitness testimony found that carefully analyzing facial features and discussing selection procedures in detail can lead to inaccurate identifications. People often achieve greater accuracy when they are unable to articulate the specific reasons for recognizing someone, saying things like "his face just popped out at me". This lack of detailed explanation appears to be linked to a reliance on unconscious cues, which can lead to more precise identification in such situations. At times, our first, immediate or automatic reaction to a situation is the most accurate reflection of what our mind is conveying to us. The first impression we have can often be a more accurate representation of the world than the thoughtful, reasoned self-narrative we construct afterward. In addition, several studies in psychology and behavioral economics support this perspective, showing ___________________________________.
options: ① logical analysis is a more effective tool for identifying faces than intuitive responses
② how conscious behaviors psychologically influence people when they are recalling memories
③ maintaining a consistently focused mindset is essential for making accurate judgments in high-pressure situations
④ why people have difficulty judging things accurately due to cognitive biases, especially in complex situation
⑤ our instinctive judgments can sometimes be superior to decisions reached through deliberate reasoning
questions.explanation: 지문은 목격자 증언 연구를 통해 세밀한 분석보다 무의식적인 직관이나 즉각적인 첫인상이 더 정확한 식별로 이어질 수 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸은 이러한 관점을 뒷받침하는 내용을 요약해야 하므로, 본능적인 판단이 심사숙고한 결정보다 우월할 수 있다는 내용이 가장 적절합니다. (원문 기반 추론: instinctive judgments > deliberate reasoning)
options_translation: ① 논리적 분석이 직관적 반응보다 얼굴 식별에 더 효과적인 도구이다
② 기억을 회상할 때 의식적인 행동이 어떻게 심리적으로 사람들에게 영향을 미치는지
③ 고압적인 상황에서 정확한 판단을 내리기 위해서는 지속적으로 집중된 마음가짐을 유지하는 것이 필수적이다
④ 왜 사람들이 인지 편향 때문에, 특히 복잡한 상황에서 사물을 정확하게 판단하는 데 어려움을 겪는지
⑤ 우리의 본능적인 판단이 때로는 의도적인 추론을 통해 도달한 결정보다 더 우수할 수 있다

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: On a personal level, our capacity to succeed relied on how ⓐ<u>effectively</u> we managed relationships within a group. If the group recognized our worth, we could expect support, resources, and the potential for finding a mate. If not, we might lose the chance to get these benefits. Our survival, both physically and genetically, depended on it. Across countless generations, the pressure favored each individual who ⓑ<u>are</u> sensitive to and adept at maximizing their standing. This led to the formation of a tendency to unconsciously track how others in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such ⓒ<u>related</u> emotions like pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions drive us to engage in behaviors that increase our value to the community and avoid ⓓ<u>those</u> which reduce it. Importantly, these emotions are designed to feel internally driven, so that our motivation seems genuine. If we consciously recognized that we were simply responding to social pressure, our behavior might come off as reluctant or insincere, ⓔ<u>reducing</u> its effectiveness in securing social acceptance.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 관계대명사절의 선행사는 'each individual'로 단수 취급해야 한다. 따라서 동사 'are'는 단수형인 'is' 혹은 과거 시제에 맞춰 'was'로 고쳐야 어법상 적절하다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba dominated international baseball. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 out of 5 Olympic Games. The Cuban team was recognizable for their noticeable red uniforms, which stood in sharp contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants. The Cubans not only displayed ⓐ<u>outstanding</u> athletic talents, but their uniforms also gave the impression of greater strength. The opposing team felt ⓑ<u>intimidated</u> even before the game began. However, a few years back, Cuba altered their traditional uniforms, opting for a more modern design that ⓒ<u>complies with</u> the styles of other nations. Since that time, the national team's performance has declined. The previously dominant force in international baseball has scarcely ⓓ<u>regained</u> its former position since adopting the new look. This shift highlights the importance of tradition for a team; while a team's brand or image can adapt to modern trends, abandoning or disregarding the team's origins may not result in ⓔ<u>unfavorable</u> consequences.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 쿠바 야구팀이 전통적인 유니폼을 바꾼 뒤 성적이 하락했다는 점을 들어 팀 전통의 중요성을 강조하고 있다. 문맥상 팀의 기원(전통)을 무시하는 것이 '유리한' 혹은 '좋은' 결과를 낳지 않을 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 하므로, ⓔ의 'unfavorable(불리한)'은 'favorable(유리한)' 또는 'desirable'과 같은 긍정적 의미의 단어로 고쳐야 'may not result in favorable consequences(유리한 결과를 초래하지 않을 수 있다)'로 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The scale of global climate change might rapidly make the climate-fiction genre irrelevant─or even make any attempt to narrate the story of global warming unnecessary, as it could become too vast and evident even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a peripheral feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can't pretend that climate suffering is distant in time or place anymore, we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.summary_sentence: As climate change becomes increasingly evident, the significance of climate fiction may (A)__________. When the impacts of climate change can no longer be (B)__________ and are felt universally, people will shift from telling stories 'about' climate change to (C)__________ experiencing its consequences in everyday life, making fictional fiction less relevant or necessary.
questions.explanation: 기후 변화가 너무나 명백해짐에 따라 기후 소설(climate fiction) 장르의 중요성(significance)은 줄어들게(decrease) 됩니다. 기후 변화의 영향이 더 이상 간과될(overlooked) 수 없고 보편적으로 느껴지게 되면, 사람들은 기후 변화에 '관한' 이야기를 하는 것에서 일상생활에서 그 결과를 '직접적으로(directly)' 경험하는 것으로 이동하게 될 것이라는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 감소하다 (B) 고려되다 (C) 직접적으로
② (A) 감소하다 (B) 간과되다 (C) 간접적으로
③ (A) 감소하다 (B) 간과되다 (C) 직접적으로
④ (A) 증가하다 (B) 간과되다 (C) 간접적으로
⑤ (A) 증가하다 (B) 고려되다 (C) 직접적으로

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 각각 알맞은 한 단어를 반드시 글에서 찾아 쓰시오. (단, 필요시 어형 변화)
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political─which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix─and, therefore, functionally (A)__________. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an abundant resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to address it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an (B)_____________ loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective (C)_____________ clearly highlights have-and-have-not inequities, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
subjective_conditions: 반드시 글에서 찾아 쓸 것
필요시 어형 변화 가능
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤 문장에서 'selective scarcity'가 언급되므로, 물 위기가 정치적이며 선택적으로 발생한다는 맥락에서 'selective'가 적절합니다. (B) 브라질의 수치 뒤에 'estimate'라는 단어가 나오므로, 추정된 손실이라는 뜻의 과거분사 'estimated'가 적절합니다. (C) 글 앞부분에서 풍부한 자원이 'scarce'하게 만들어진다는 내용이 나오므로, 빈칸 뒤의 불평등(inequities)과 연결되는 명사형 'scarcity(부족, 희소성)'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 <보기>에서 각각 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
questions.summary_sentence: After World War Ⅱ, cultivating a(n) (A)____________ range of high-yield crops on a large scale seemed successful in (B)____________ the severe hunger problem, but over time, this approach has made the crops more (C)____________ to threats.
questions.explanation: 제2차 세계대전 이후 좁은(한정된) 범위의 작물을 대규모로 재배하는 방식은 굶주림 문제를 완화(alleviating)하는 데 성공적이었으나, 유전적 다양성이 부족하여 질병이나 기후 변화 같은 위협에 더 취약하게(vulnerable) 만들었다는 내용입니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글 <B>는 <A>의 내용을 바탕으로 질의 응답한 내용이다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 알맞은 말을 주어진 단어들을 모두 배열하여 쓰시오. (단, 필요시 어형 변화)
questions.passage: <A>When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, as those are the mental processes which we understand. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents. This results in a perceptual system strongly biased towards anthropomorphism. Therefore, we tend to assume intention even where there is none. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you. By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has saved your life.<B>A: What does anthropomorphism mean above?B: It refers to (A)<u>intention / and objects / attribute / to animals</u>.A: Why was it important in the past?B: We (B)<u>able to / fast decisions / that being / were / about / make / the likely behavior of</u>. This was essential in our hunter-gatherer days (C)<u>predators / avoid / eat / by / be / to </u>.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어들을 모두 배열하여 쓰시오.
필요시 어형 변화할 것
questions.answer: (A) attributing intention to animals and objects(B) were able to make fast decisions about the likely behavior of that being(C) to avoid being eaten by predators
questions.explanation: (A) anthropomorphism(의인화)은 동물이나 사물에 의도를 부여하는 것이므로, refer to(~을 지칭하다)의 목적어로 동명사구인 'attributing intention to animals and objects'가 적절합니다. (B) 과거 시제에 맞춰 '우리는 그 존재의 가능성 있는 행동에 대해 빠른 결정을 내릴 수 있었다'는 의미인 'were able to make fast decisions about the likely behavior of that being'으로 배열합니다. (C) '포식자에게 잡아먹히는 것을 피하기 위해서'라는 의미로, avoid 뒤에 동명사 수동형인 being eaten을 사용하여 'to avoid being eaten by predators'로 영작합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 -making friends with their pain.-이 의미하는 바를 아래와 같이 설명하고자 한다. 밑줄 친 (A), (B), (C)를 <보기>의 단어(구)를 사용하여 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: The extent of our suffering depends on how we frame the pain in our mind. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race ─ their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't psychologically suffer much. In fact, covering distances of 50 -100km or more over hours, ultra-marathon runners push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance, and even they refer to this intense experience as "<u>making friends with their pain</u>." Similarly, when a patient has paid for some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it, the patient calls that good pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.↓ In the text, the phrase "making friends with their pain." implies (A)<u>고통에 저항하기보다는 그것을 받아들이는 것</u>. For example, both the runners and the patient experience extreme physical discomfort, but they mentally (B)<u>그것을 그들의 목표를 달성하려는 하나의 부분으로써 재구성한다</u>, and this (C)<u>그들이 신체적인 고통에 의해 압도되지 않고 심리적으로 그것을 견딜 수 있게 한다</u>.
subjective_conditions: (A), (B), (C)에 각각 해당하는 <보기>의 단어(구)를 모두 사용할 것
<보기>의 단어(구) 이외의 단어(구)를 추가하지 말 것
필요한 경우 어형을 변화할 것
vocabulary_box: (A): it / rather than / pain / resist / embrace
(B): goal / of / their / a part/it / reframe / as / achieve
(C): be / them / psychologically / by / tolerate / pain / overwhelm / to / enable / physical / it / without
questions.answer: (A) embracing it rather than resisting pain(B) reframe it as a part of achieving their goal(s)(C) enables them to tolerate it psychologically without being overwhelmed by physical pain
questions.explanation: (A) '...하는 것'의 의미를 위해 동명사구(embracing/resisting)를 활용합니다.(B) 주어 they에 맞춰 동사 reframe을 사용하고, 전치사 of 뒤에 동명사 achieving을 사용하여 '목표를 달성하는 것의 일환'으로 표현합니다.(C) 앞 문장 전체 혹은 상황을 받는 주어 this에 맞춰 단수 동사 enables를 사용하고, 'enable + 목적어 + to부정사' 구문과 'without + 동명사 수동태(being overwhelmed)'를 사용하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: It′s not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations ─ surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue ─ with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers′ reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members′ ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.explanation: 지문은 사람들이 관습적인 기대치에서 '약간 벗어난' 차림새를 한 사람들에 대해 오히려 지위와 능력이 높다고 평가한다는 연구 결과를 다루고 있습니다. 붉은 나비넥타이나 빨간 운동화처럼 규범(norm)에서 약간 '벗어난 것/변화(variations)'를 긍정적으로 평가한다는 내용이므로 ⑤번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 습관
② 스타일
③ 예절
④ 모호함
⑤ 변화(일탈)

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode ⓐ<u>what</u> we see through the lens of everything that we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way ⓑ<u>to store</u> information ─ a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than ⓒ<u>storing</u> a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail ⓓ<u>struggles</u> to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery ⓔ<u>that</u> our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: 문장의 주어인 'People'은 복수 명사이며, 'who lack ... detail'은 관계대명사 절로 수식어구입니다. 따라서 동사는 struggles가 아니라 복수 형태인 struggle이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions. But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the study above, using the Internet (A)___________ perceived knowledge, even for unrelated topics, creating (B)___________ in one's intellectual ability.
questions.explanation: 해당 연구는 인터넷 검색을 통해 정보를 얻는 행위가 실제로 관련이 없는 새로운 주제에 대해서도 자신이 더 많이 알고 있다고 느끼게 만든다는 것을 보여줍니다. 따라서 (A)에는 인지된 지식을 '증가시킨다(boosts)'가 들어가야 하며, (B)에는 자신의 지적 능력에 대한 '과도한 자신감(overconfidence)'이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 강화한다 / 과잉 확신
강화한다 / 자기 불신
감소시킨다 / 발달
감소시킨다 / 자기 관심
고갈시킨다 / 과잉 반응

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름상 (A)에 들어갈 알맞은 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Despite the remarkable progress in deep-learning based facial recognition approaches in recent years, in terms of identification performance, they still have limitations. These limitations relate to the database used in the learning stage. If the selected database does not contain enough instances, the result may be systematically affected. For example, the performance of a facial biometric system may decrease if the person to be identified was enrolled over 10 years ago. The factor to consider is that this person may experience changes in the texture of the face, particularly with the appearance of wrinkles and sagging skin. These changes may be highlighted by weight gain or loss. To counteract this problem, researchers have developed models for face aging or digital de-aging. It is used to (A)______________________, which appear over a given time period.
options: ① compensate for the complaints by unsatisfactory users
② make up for the differences in face characteristics
③ figure out why aging process speeds up
④ compete with other rival companies
⑤ capture the memorable moments in life
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 안면 인식 시스템의 성능을 저하시키는 요인은 시간이 지남에 따라 발생하는 얼굴의 변화(주름, 피부 처짐 등)입니다. 연구자들이 개발한 에이징 또는 디에이징 모델은 이러한 시간 경과에 따른 얼굴 특성의 차이를 보완(make up for the differences)하기 위해 사용됩니다.
options_translation: ① 불만족스러운 사용자들의 불만을 보상하기 위해
② 얼굴 특징의 차이를 보완하기 위해
③ 노화 과정이 왜 가속화되는지 파악하기 위해
④ 다른 경쟁 업체들과 경쟁하기 위해
⑤ 인생의 기억에 남는 순간을 포착하기 위해

questions.question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods.
ordered_passages: (A) But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price.
(B) If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income.

(C) The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
(D) If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 왜 소비재에 세 가지 버전이 있는지에 대해 언급한 후, (B)에서 버전이 하나일 때의 한계를 설명합니다. 이어 (D)에서 두 가지 버전일 때 소비자들이 더 싼 것을 선택하는 경향을 보여주고, (A)에서 세 번째 더 비싼 모델이 도입될 때 두 번째 모델의 판매가 늘어나는 상황을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 소비자들이 중간 가격의 품목을 선택하게 되는 원리(미끼 효과)를 요약하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden</u> as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So ⓑ<u>to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise</u> for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. ⓒ<u>It was only when they looked again that</u> they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. ⓓ<u>Many more of this species has found</u> since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt-producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, ⓔ<u>sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'Many more of this species'로, 문맥상 '이 종의 더 많은 개체들이 발견되어 왔다'는 수동의 의미가 되어야 하며 주어가 복수이므로 'have been found'로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: [23년 11월 29번]Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation ─ transferring organs to others ─ is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. ⓐThe reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death ir potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. ⓑBut it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. ⓒThey also argue that animal testing should be banned, at least in terms of respect for life. ⓓThey certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. ⓔAs a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 장기 이식을 위한 뇌사 판정의 엄격한 기준과 그에 대한 대중의 불신 및 일관성 문제를 다루고 있습니다. 그러나 ③(ⓒ)은 생명 존중 차원에서 동물 실험이 금지되어야 한다는 주장을 담고 있어 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the journey really begins가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: [23년 11월 20번]Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. They do well enough in school to keep advancing. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ends with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now lack a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when <u>the journey really begins</u>. When school is finished, your growth becomes voluntary. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen ─ and your life and career are likely to stop progressing as a result.
options: ① personal evolution and achievements gradually halt.
② personal growth and development genuinely' start.
③ healthy hobbies and experience are necessary.
④ new roadmap will be offered for guidance.
⑤ your study continues in a graduate school.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 학교 교육이 끝난 후 스스로 책임을 지고 자발적으로 성장해야 한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 밑줄 친 'the journey really begins'는 대학 졸업 이후에 개인적인 성장과 발전이 진정으로 시작된다는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 개인적인 진화와 성취가 점차 중단된다.
② 개인적인 성장과 발전이 진정으로 시작된다.
③ 건강한 취미와 경험이 필수적이다.
④ 안내를 위한 새로운 로드맵이 제공될 것이다.
⑤ 대학원에서도 공부가 계속된다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants. Not only were their athletic talents superior, the Cubans appeared even stronger from just the colour of their uniforms. A game would not even start and the opposing team would already be scared. A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time. The country that ruled international baseball for decades has not been on top since that uniform change. Traditions are important for a team; while a team brand or image can adjust to keep up with present times, if it abandons or neglects its roots, negative effects can surface.
options: ① The Power of Tradition: The Impact of Cuban Uniforms
② Modern Style vs. Traditional Style: Which is better?
③ Cuba: The Invincible Baseball Team from 1940 to 2000
④ The Scientific Secret of Cuban Red Uniforms
⑤ Red Colour Boosts Performance in Sports
questions.explanation: 쿠바 야구팀의 상징적인 빨간색 유니폼과 그 전통이 팀의 강력함에 미친 영향, 그리고 전통적인 스타일을 버린 후 겪게 된 성적 하락을 통해 '전통의 중요성'을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 ①번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 전통의 힘: 쿠바 유니폼의 영향
② 현대적 스타일 vs 전통적 스타일: 무엇이 더 나은가?
③ 쿠바: 1940년부터 2000년까지의 무적 야구팀
④ 쿠바의 빨간 유니폼에 숨겨진 과학적 비밀
⑤ 빨간색은 스포츠 기량을 향상시킨다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light ─ a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless ─ and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is _______________________ ─ "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it. "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
options: ⑤ conceptual phenomena in the spiritual world
questions.explanation: 색이 물체의 객관적 성질이라는 견해(실재함)와 관찰자의 마음속에만 존재한다는 견해(인지됨)를 모두 긍정하며, 세계의 빛이 뇌에 의해 해석될 때 색이 생긴다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 색은 '실재하면서도 동시에 인지되는 것'이라는 ①번이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 실재하면서도 인지되는 것
② 객관적이거나 주관적인 것
③ 상황에 따라 변하는 것
④ 과학적 실험을 통해 설명되는 것
⑤ 정신 세계의 개념적 현상

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
