questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are ①<u>readily</u> bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to ②<u>diminish</u> their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At e same time, these neurons ③<u>strengthen</u> their responses to things that change ─ especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to a ④<u>dynamic</u> environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural ⑤<u>equivalent</u> of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
questions.explanation: ④의 'dynamic(역동적인)'은 문맥상 어색합니다. 지문은 반복되는 자극에 대해 신경 반응이 줄어드는 현상(지루함)을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '역동적인 환경'이 아니라, 변화가 없는 '정적인(static)' 혹은 '변하지 않는(unchanging)' 환경에 대한 반응으로 지루함이 신경 흥분 수준을 낮추어 새로운 자극이 돋보이게 한다는 흐름이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 예문의 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 영단어를 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: 1. The sand was so ___________ and I realized that anything heavy, like gold, would quickly sink and might never be found again.2. The masks are to prevent people from breathing in ___________ dust.3. If the weather is ___________, we'll go hiking this weekend.
questions.explanation: 다의어 'fine'의 여러 의미를 묻는 문제입니다. 1번 문장에서는 '미세한/고운(sand)', 2번 문장에서는 '미세한(fine dust)', 3번 문장에서는 '맑은/좋은(weather)'의 의미로 공통적으로 사용될 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 흐름상 빈칸 (A)에 각각 들어갈 가장 적절한 표현을 영어로 쓰시오. (단, 형태 변형 없이 <보기>의 표현만을 모두 사용해 완성하시오)
questions.passage: In statistics, the law of large numberse describes (A)_____________________________________. According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to match the true state of the world. For instance, on your first encounter with the game of roulette, you may have beginner's luck after betting on 7. But the more often you repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning, meaning that your luck will at some point fade away. Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to balance individual losses.
subjective_conditions: 형태 변형 없이 <보기>의 표현만을 모두 사용해 완성하시오
vocabulary_box: predictions / situation / a / more / better / making / where / your / for / is / having / data
questions.answer: a situation where having more data is better for making your predictions
questions.explanation: 대수의 법칙(law of large numbers)은 시행 횟수가 많아질수록 실제 확률에 가까워진다는 원리입니다. 따라서 '더 많은 데이터를 가지는 것이 예측을 하는 데 더 나은 상황'이라는 의미가 되도록 주어진 단어를 조합하면 'a situation where having more data is better for making your predictions'가 됩니다. (문법적으로 'for your making predictions'도 가능하지만 일반적인 동명사의 의미상 주어 구문보다 전자 가 더 자연스럽습니다.)

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 흐름상 주어진 우리말 해석을 참고하여 빈칸 (A)에 각각 들어갈 가장 적절한 표현을 영어로 쓰시오. (단, 형태 변형 없이 <보기>의 표현만을 모두 사용해 완성하시오.)
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of clarity. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. <u>They are (A)_______________________ or not going to be used in the near future.</u> <그들은 여러분이 사용되지 않거나 가까운 미래에 사용되지 않을 물건을 없애기만 하면 된다는 견해를 가지고 있다.>
subjective_conditions: 형태 변형 없이
<보기>의 표현만을 모두 사용해 완성할 것
주어진 우리말 해석을 참고할 것
questions.answer: of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused
questions.explanation: 미니멀리즘이 소중한 소유물을 희생하는 것이라는 오해를 반박하는 내용입니다. 미니멀리스트들은 모든 현대적 편의를 버리라고 주장하는 것이 아니라, 단지 사용되지 않는 물건들을 제거하는 것뿐이라는 견해를 가지고 있다는 문장을 완성해야 합니다. 우리말 해석 '그들은 ~라는 견해를 가지고 있다'에 맞춰 'They are of the view that ~' 구문을 사용하고, '사용되지 않는 물건을 없애기만 하면 된다'는 부분을 'you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused'로 영작합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글을 읽고 추론할 수 없는 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.
options: ① Life is a high-dimensional system with many things happening.
② Life can be considered stable when collective ways are applied.
③ The possibilities for development of a single cell are endless
④ An organism can change within a set of possible states.
⑤ The causes of diseases vary, but their manifestations are not random.
questions.explanation: 지문에서는 고차원적 시스템인 생명이 안정화되기 위해서는 가능한 상태의 수가 급격히 좁아지는 '운하화(canalization)'가 발생해야 한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 인간 배아의 발달 결과가 제한된 수의 조직과 신체 형태로 나타난다는 예를 통해 단일 세포의 발달 가능성이 무궁무진(endless)하다는 것은 지문의 내용과 정반대되는 추론입니다.
options_translation: 생명은 많은 일이 일어나는 고차원 시스템이다.
집합적인 방식이 적용될 때 생명은 안정적인 것으로 간주될 수 있다.
단일 세포의 발달 가능성은 무궁무진하다.
유기체는 설정된 가능한 상태 내에서 변화할 수 있다.
질병의 원인은 다양하지만, 그 증상은 무작위가 아니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. (A) So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. (B) Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. (C) It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. (D) Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. (E) And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.insertion_sentence: An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 문어가 큰 뇌와 뛰어난 시력, 색과 패턴을 바꾸는 능력을 사용하여 자신을 완전히 다른 생물로 바꾸고 있었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C)에서 사진작가들이 처음에는 넙치인 줄 알았다가 다시 보니 문어였다는 구체적인 발견 사실을 언급하고, 주어진 문장이 이 능력을 설명하며 요약해준 뒤, (D)에서 이후 이 종의 더 많은 개체들이 발견되었고 다른 생물(바다뱀)로 변신하는 사례들도 있다는 내용으로 이어지는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness.
ordered_passages: (A) The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions.

(B) However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another.

(C) In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 인간 본성에 대한 사회의 일반적인 설명이 가정과 허구의 혼합물이라고 언급합니다. (B)에서 'However'를 통해 심리학은 이와 다르며 '과학'의 한 분야임을 소개합니다. (A)에서는 (B)에서 언급된 '과학'이라는 키워드를 받아 심리학자들이 의견이나 소문이 아닌 '증거'에 의존함을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 '증거 기반 접근법'에 덧붙여 현대 심리학이 다루는 핵심 내용을 정리하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which AI exceeds human intelligence.
ordered_passages: (A) AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity.

(B) After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine.

(C) Conversely, the direction of AI's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 AI가 인간의 지능을 넘어서는 시점인 '특이점(singularity)'을 정의합니다. (B)의 'After that point'는 제시문의 특이점을 가리키며, AI가 자의식을 가진 존재가 되는 과정을 설명합니다. (A)의 'then'은 AI가 의식적인 존재가 된 이후 AI와 인간의 의식이 함께 진화하는 상호작용을 설명합니다. (C)에서는 이러한 진화의 방향이 인간이 주입하는 가치와 윤리에 달려있음을 언급하며 상호 공존의 태도를 강조하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a __________ of depression. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우울증의 원인과 결과에 대한 기존의 통념을 뒤집는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 기존 의학은 뇌의 화학적 불균형이 우울증을 일으킨다고 믿었으나, 필자는 우울증이 뇌 물질의 감소를 '유발'한다고 주장합니다. 즉, 뇌 물질의 불균형은 우울증의 원인이 아니라 우울증으로 인해 나타나는 '결과(result)'라는 맥락이 되어야 하므로 빈칸에는 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 결과
② 원인
③ 왜곡
④ 특징
⑤ 증상

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is _________________________________. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
options: ② try to be independent of society
④ learn how to use the latest technologies perfectly
⑤ acquire the correct answers through social learning
questions.explanation: 인간은 정보와 인지 능력의 한계로 인해 모든 것을 스스로 해결하는 대신 인류 전체에 계산을 분산시키고 세대를 거쳐 해답을 찾아냅니다. 우리는 기술의 작동 원리를 다 알 필요 없이 어떻게 사용하는지만 알면 되며, 사회의 집단적 지능을 통해 얻어진 결과를 이용합니다. 따라서 우리가 해야 할 일은 '사회적 학습을 통해 정확한 답을 습득하는 것'이므로 ⑤번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 사회적 합의를 엄격히 따르다
② 사회로부터 독립적이려고 노력하다
③ 정보를 비판적으로 받아들이는 연습을 하다
④ 최신 기술을 완벽하게 사용하는 법을 배우다
⑤ 사회적 학습을 통해 정답을 습득하다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to __________________________________. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
options: ① unconsciously check other people's evaluations of us
② work hard to please the people in our community
③ hide our achievements instead of revealing them
④ intentionally monitor how others perceive us
⑤ externalize caring about people's opinions.
questions.explanation: 인간은 집단 내에서 타인의 평가에 민감하도록 진화해 왔습니다. 이러한 평가는 자존감, 수치심 같은 감정으로 처리되어 우리가 공동체로부터 가치 있게 여겨지는 행동을 하도록 만듭니다. 지문 마지막 부분에서 우리가 '의식적인 수준'에서 사회적 압력에 반응한다는 것을 깨닫는다면 그 행동이 냉소적으로 보일 수 있다고 언급하고 있으므로, 이러한 확인 과정은 '무의식적으로' 일어난다는 점이 핵심입니다. 따라서 ①번 '무의식적으로 우리에 대한 다른 사람들의 평가를 확인한다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리에 대한 타인의 평가를 무의식적으로 확인하다
② 공동체의 사람들을 기쁘게 하기 위해 열심히 일하다
③ 우리의 성취를 드러내는 대신 숨기다
④ 타인이 우리를 어떻게 인지하는지 의도적으로 모니터링하다
⑤ 사람들의 의견에 신경 쓰는 것을 외면화하다

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly ⑀<u>get rid of</u> the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a ⑁<u>inconsiderable</u> feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, ⑂<u>scarcely</u> anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may ⑃<u>expand</u> to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is ⑄<u>far away</u> - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.explanation: ④(d) 'expand'("확장하다")는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다. 지문의 흐름은 기후 변화가 너무 거대해지고 일상화되어 창문 밖으로 훤히 보이는 현실이 되면, 더 이상 그것이 특별한 '이야기'가 될 수 없음을 시사합니다. 따라서 기후 변화가 지평선 전반으로 확대됨에 따라 그것은 이야기이기를 '멈추다' 혹은 '그만두다'라는 의미인 'cease'와 같은 단어가 오는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절한 것끼리 짝지어진 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a more (A)[ideal / improper] way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as (B)[conceptual / practical] ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie (C)[discredited / confirmed] the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: (A) 정보를 JPG 압축 알고리즘처럼 저장하는 것은 생생한 로우 데이터를 저장하는 것보다 더 효율적이므로 'ideal'("이상적인")이 적절합니다. (B) 앞 문장에서 교육을 통해 배운 '개념'으로 정보를 쪼갠다고 했으므로 세상을 'conceptual'("개념적인") 아이디어와 특징으로 표현한다는 것이 문맥에 맞습니다. (C) 기억이 영화처럼 재생되는 것이 아니라 추상적 표상으로 재구성된다는 발견은 목격자 증언의 법적 우선순위(신뢰성)를 'discredited'("신뢰를 떨어뜨리다/의심하다")하게 만들었습니다.
options_translation: ① 이상적인 - 실제적인 - 확인해주었다
② 이상적인 - 실제적인 - 신뢰를 떨어뜨렸다
③ 이상적인 - 개념적인 - 신뢰를 떨어뜨렸다
④ 부적절한 - 개념적인 - 확인해주었다
⑤ 부적절한 - 실제적인 - 확인해주었다

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 33번]
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been tricked to keep purchasing unnecessary products.
questions.summary_sentence: The reason the company makes three versions of the product is to (A)__________ customers so that the company can sell the product that is neither the most expensive nor has the least number of (B)__________.
questions.explanation: 기업이 세 가지 버전을 만드는 이유는 소비자들이 가장 비싼 제품의 특징은 좋아하지만 가격 때문에 망설일 때, 중간 가격의 제품을 합리적 선택이라고 믿게끔 하여 유도하는 전략입니다. 이는 소비자를 (A) 'deceive(속이다)' 하는 것이며, 결과적으로 기업은 가장 비싸지도 않고 (B) 'functions(기능)'이 가장 적지도 않은 중간 제품을 팔 수 있게 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 속이다 / 기능
② 속이다 / 매뉴얼
③ 끌어들이다 / 사용자
④ 설득하다 / 특성
⑤ 지지하다 / 특징

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
options: ① the story-like factors existing in psychology
② various challenges against modern psychology
③ storytelling as the powerful way to activate brains
④ a certain field of psychology that studies human beliefs
⑤ psychology as a science that seeks to understand human nature
questions.explanation: 이 글은 심리학이 일반적인 가정이나 소문, 사회적 견해에 의존하는 것이 아니라, 증거를 기반으로 인간의 행동과 상호작용의 원리를 연구하는 '과학'임을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 인간 본성을 이해하고자 하는 과학으로서의 심리학입니다.
options_translation: ① 심리학에 존재하는 이야기와 같은 요소들
② 현대 심리학에 대한 다양한 도전들
③ 뇌를 활성화하는 강력한 방법으로서의 스토리텔링
④ 인간의 믿음을 연구하는 심리학의 특정 분야
⑤ 인간 본성을 이해하고자 하는 과학으로서의 심리학

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point ⓐ<u>at which</u> AI exceeds human intelligence. After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. AI and human consciousness will then begin ⓑ<u>evolving </u>together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, ⓒ<u>where </u>will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI. The direction of AI's evolution will depend greatly on ⓓ<u>what</u> values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and ⓔ<u>supporting</u> the evolution of its consciousness.
questions.explanation: ⓒ where는 관계부사로 뒤에 완전한 문장이 와야 하는데, 뒤에 바로 동사 will provide가 나오므로 주어가 빠진 불완전한 문장입니다. 따라서 관계부사 where가 아니라 앞선 interactions(또는 상황 전체)를 선행사로 받는 주격 관계대명사 which가 와야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Onscreen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre ─ indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant ─ in time or in place ─ we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.*escapist: 현실도피주의자(의)
options: ① Facts and feelings matter when communicating climate change.
② The cultural world is struggling to prevent environmental disaster.
③ Excessive concern about climate change only worsens the problem.
④ Vivid and compelling climate fictions are inspiring people to take actions.
⑤ Intense climate change can turn imaginary stories into real-life situations.
questions.explanation: 글은 기후 변화가 가속화됨에 따라 더 이상 픽션(소설) 속의 이삼기가 아닌, 창문 밖으로 바로 바라바지는 현실이 되어 픽션이라는 장르 자체가 사라질 수 있음을 경고하고 있습니다. 즉, 강렬한 기후 변화가 가상의 이삼기를 실제 사황으로 바꿔 놓을 수 있다는 ⑤가 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기후 변화를 소통할 때 사실가 감정이 중요하다.
② 문화계는 환경 재앂을 막기 위해 노력하고 있다.
③ 기후 변화에 대한 과도한 경제는 문제를 악화시킬 붐이다.
④ 생생하고 설득력 있는 기후 소설들이 사람들이 행동하도록 고고하고 있다.
⑤ 궼렬한 기후 변화는 상상의 이삼기를 실제 사황으로 바꿔 놓을 수 있다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.*neurotransmitter: 신경전달물질**manifest: (명백히) 나타내다
options: ① Depression as a Result of Poor Health Habits
② The Most Powerful Brain Substances For Depression
③ Beyond Neurotransmitters : How to Deal with Depression
④ There is a Way Through : A Guide for People Experiencing Stress
⑤ Redefining Depression: Consciousness Distortion, Not Brain Imbalance
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우울증이 뇌의 화학 물질 불균형에 의해 발생한다는 기존 의학계의 통념을 반박하고 있습니다. 우울증은 뇌의 물질 불균형의 원인이 아니라 결과이며, 근밸적인 원인은 자아와 삮의 의미를 상실한 '의식의 왔곡'에 있다고 주장합니다. 따라서 우울증을 뇌의 불균형이 아닌 의식의 왔곡으룜 재정의하는 ⑤가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 나삽 건강 값습의 결과룜서의 우울증
② 우울증에 가장 강력한 뇌 물질
③ 신경통달물질을 넘서: 우울증에 대차하는 방법
④ 통과하는 길이 있다: 스트레스를 경험하는 사람들을 은한 가이드
⑤ 우울증의 재정의: 뇌의 불균형이 아닌 의식의 왔곡

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Alvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it ⓐ<u>encourages</u> them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much ⓑ<u>worse</u> than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could ⓒ<u>praise</u> Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow let him hit his little brother, but she has the option to focus on ⓓ<u>diminishing </u>positive behavior rather than pointing out the negative. In this way, any parent can ⓔ<u>avoid</u> trick-punishments.*neuropsychologist: 신경심리학자
questions.explanation: 문맥사 아이의 부정적인 행동을 지적하기보다 긍정적인 행동에 중점을 두어야 한다는 내용이므로, 긍정적인 행동을 '줄이는(ⓓdiminishing)' 것이 아니라 '강화하거나 충실히 하는(예: reinforcing 또는 fostering)' 것에 중점을 둔다는 표현이 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and inkjet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is ⓐ<u>losing</u> some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the ⓑ<u>less</u> expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model will ⓒ<u>go up</u>; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is more ⓓ<u>expensive</u> than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been ⓔ<u>manipulated</u> by the presence of the higher-priced item.
questions.explanation: 세 가지 버전 중 가운데 제품(the middle item)은 가장 비싼 제품(-the fanciest model- 또는 -the most expensive model-)보다는 '더 저렴해야(less expensive)' 합니다. 문맥사 소비자들이 가장 비싼 것의 기능은 접하되 가격 부담으로 가운데 것을 선택하도록 유도하는 전략이므로 ⓓ의 expensive는 투만 표현입니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education.We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We ⓐ<u>reframe</u> memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. It is a ⓑ<u>beneficial</u> trait. It's a more efficient way to store information ─ a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who don't ⓒ<u>possess</u> this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a ⓓ<u>cost</u> of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely ⓔ<u>justified</u> the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.*retrieve: 상기하다 **primacy: 우위성
questions.explanation: 인간의 기억이 비디오처럼 재생되는 것이 아니라 추상적인 개념으로 재구성된다는 내용의 글입니다. 마지막 문장에서 '보는 것이 믿는 것이 아니다'라고 하며 목격자 증언의 한계를 시사하고 있으므로, 이러한 발견은 목격자 증언의 법적 우위성을 정당화(justified)하는 것이 아니라 약화시키거나 도전(challenged/undermined)해야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a(n) ______________ answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.*procrastinator: 미루는 사람
questions.explanation: 지문은 연구에서 추상적인 개념(슬픔, 미루는 습관 등)을 측정할 때, 단순히 얼마나 슬픈지 묻는 것보다 '아파서 결근할 정도로 슬펐던 횟수'나 '지불 능력이 있음에도 연체된 공과금 개수'처럼 구체적인 질문을 하는 것이 더 신뢰할 수 있는 데이터를 얻는 방법임을 설명하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 '구체적인 응답(concrete responses)'을 구하는 질문이 추상적 개념을 명확하게 한다고 했으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말은 'concrete(구체적인)'입니다.
options_translation: ① 모호한
② 구체적인
③ 마음 내키지 않는
④ 부정확한
⑤ 예기치 못한

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to _______________________, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.*grudging: 투덜대는
options: ⑤ the desire for economic improvement
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 집단 내에서 타인의 인식을 모니터링하고 이에 따라 자존감, 수치심 등을 느끼며 공동체에 가치 있게 여겨지는 행동을 하도록 진화했음을 설명합니다. 이러한 동기는 내면에서 우러나오는 것처럼 느껴지지만, 실제로는 집단의 가치나 타인의 시선과 같은 외부적 요인인 '사회적 압박'에 대한 반응입니다. 만약 우리가 이것이 외부의 사회적 압박에 반응하는 것임을 의식적으로 깨닫는다면, 그 행동은 진정성이 떨어지고 투덜대거나 냉소적으로 보일 수 있다고 언급하고 있으므로 빈칸에는 'social pressure(사회적 압박)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사회적 압박

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night.
ordered_passages: (A) So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion.(B) After the initial identification of the mimic octopus, numerous additional examples of this species have been documented and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt─producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.(C) Their discovery was a mimic octopus living near shallow sandy bottoms or coral reefs in the Indo-Pacific region. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 문어는 주로 밤에 활동하며 숨어 지낸다고 언급했습니다. (A)에서 낮에 얕은 곳에서 발견된 것이 놀라웠다는 내용으로 이어지고, (C)에서 그들이 발견한 것이 '흉내문어(mimic octopus)'임을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 그 이후 추가적인 사례들이 기록되었다는 내용으로 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. ⓐSuch a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. ⓑFor example, it is an enormous number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. ⓒIn 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. ⓓThe organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. ⓔWe'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.

For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will ⓑ<u>continue</u> to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could ⓒ<u>congratulate</u> Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to ⓓ<u>reward</u> the positives. In this way, any parent can ⓔ<u>adopt</u> trick-punishments.
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 맥락은 '속임수 처벌(trick-punishments)'이 아이의 나쁜 행동을 오히려 부추길 수 있으므로, 부정적인 것에 주목하기보다 긍정적인 행동에 보상을 주는 대안적 전략을 사용해야 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ⓔ는 부모가 속임수 처벌을 '채택(adopt)'하는 것이 아니라, 그러한 처벌을 '피하거나(avoid)', '그만두어야(stop)' 한다는 내용이 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. (A) In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. (B) In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. (C) Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. (D) The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. (E) If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life.
questions.insertion_sentence: This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '뇌의 화학 물질 불균형은 우울증의 원인이 아니라 결과이다'라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A) 뒤의 문장에서 'In other words(다시 말해)'로 시작하며 '우울증이 뇌 물질의 감소를 일으키는 것이지, 뇌 물질 감소가 우울증을 일으키는 것이 아니다'라고 앞 문장을 부연 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주어진 문장은 (A) 위치에 들어가 기존의 의학적 통념을 반박하는 논리적 근거를 제시해야 합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 stop pretending about it and start pretending within it이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Onscreen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre ─ indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant ─ in time or in place ─ we will <u>stop pretending about it and start pretending within it</u>.
options: ① adapt to the disruptions it has caused
② embrace it as part of our harsh reality
③ develop approaches to reverse its effects
④ treat it as a remote and fictional problem
⑤ focus less on complaints and more on progress
questions.explanation: 기후 변화가 더 이상 먼 미래나 남의 일이 아니라 창밖으로 생생하게 보이는 현실이 되면, 그것을 허구적인 '이야기'로 소비하는 것을 멈추고(stop pretending about it) 그 가혹한 현실 속에서 살아가며 적응하게 될 것(start pretending within it)임을 의미한다.
options_translation: ① 그것이 야기한 혼란에 적응한다
② 그것을 우리의 가혹한 현실의 일부로 수용한다
③ 그것의 영향을 되돌리기 위한 접근법을 개발한다
④ 그것을 멀고 허구적인 문제로 취급한다
⑤ 불평보다는 진보에 더 집중한다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our Imitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push ─ essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just _______________________________________.
options: ① distributing a fair share of technological benefits
② limiting the potential to expand our mental capacity
③ competing with each other for technological advantages
④ being outpaced by advanced computational technologies
⑤ playing our role in a larger system of collective cognition
questions.explanation: 인간은 인지 능력의 한계로 인해 모든 정보를 스스로 처리할 수 없으며, 대신 전체 인구 사이에 연산을 분산시키고 각자 거대한 계산의 작은 부분을 담당합니다. 이는 우리가 집단적인 인지 시스템 내에서 각자의 역할을 수행하고 있음을 의미하므로, 빈칸에는 '집단 인지라는 더 큰 시스템 안에서 우리의 역할을 수행하고 있다'는 내용이 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 기술적 혜택의 공정한 몫을 나누고 있는 것뿐이다
② 우리의 정신적 능력을 확장할 잠재력을 제한하고 있는 것뿐이다
③ 기술적 우위를 점하기 위해 서로 경쟁하고 있는 것뿐이다
④ 진보된 컴퓨터 연산 기술에 의해 뒤처지고 있는 것뿐이다
⑤ 집단 인지라는 더 큰 시스템 속에서 각자의 역할을 수행하고 있는 것뿐이다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'highdimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.
questions.summary_sentence: Complex biological systems achieve (A)___________ by narrowing down to a limited set of outcomes through canalization, which also explains (B)___________ symptoms across different diseases.
questions.explanation: 지문은 생명체와 같은 복잡한 시스템이 '운하화(canalization)'를 통해 결과를 제한함으로써 안정성을 유지한다고 설명합니다. 생물체는 무작위적인 상태가 아니라 정의된 몇 가지 상태로 수렴하며, 이는 질병에서도 마찬가지로 원인은 다양하더라도 나타나는 증상은 현저히 유사(strikingly similar)하다고 기술합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 안정성을 뜻하는 'stability', (B)에는 증상들이 서로 비슷하다는 맥락의 'common'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 안정성 - 공통된
안정성 - 희귀한
가변성 - 공통된
가변성 - 특이한
유연성 - 희귀한

questions.question: 22. [24년 10월 41-42번] 주어진 글(A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: From an early age, we assign purpose to objects and events, preferring this reasoning to random chance. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because they don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone.
ordered_passages: (B) This results in a perceptual system strongly inclined towards anthropomorphism. Therefore, we tend to assume intention even where there is none. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you.

(C) However, by attributing intention to animals and even objects, we are able to make fast decisions about the likely behaviour of that being. This was essential in our hunter gatherer days to avoid being eaten by predators. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, as those are the mental processes which we understand. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents.

(D) By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has saved your life. The tendency to attribute intention to unclear objects and events helps humans make quick, survival-oriented decisions. Humans instinctively interpret ambiguous situations as having intention, which enhances quick decision-making for survival.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글 (A)에서는 우리가 무생물이나 사건에 목적을 부여한다는 점을 언급하며 시작합니다. (C)는 'However'로 시작하며 동물이나 사물에 의도를 부여함으로써 생존에 필수적인 빠른 결정을 내릴 수 있게 되었다는 점을 설명합니다. (B)는 이러한 의도 부여가 의인화(anthropomorphism)를 향한 지각 시스템으로 이어졌음을 설명하며 사자 공격의 예를 도입합니다. (D)는 사자의 발톱 등을 분석하기 전에 이미 의도를 가정하는 것이 생명을 구한다는 결론으로 마무리됩니다. 따라서 적절한 순서는 (C) - (B) - (D)입니다.

questions.question: 23. [24년 10월 41-42번] 윗글의 요지를 다음과 같이 작성하고자 한다. <보기>의 단어(어구)를 어법과 문맥에 맞게 배열하여 빈칸을 완성하시오. (단, 주어진 단어(어구)만을 변형 없이 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것)

Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone.(B) This results in a perceptual system strongly inclined towards anthropomorphism. Therefore, we tend to assume intention even where there is none. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you.(C) However, by attributing intention to animals and even objects, we are able to make fast decisions about the likely behaviour of that being. This was essential in our hunter gatherer days to avoid being eaten by predators. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, as those are the mental processes which we understand. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents.(D) By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has saved your life. The tendency to attribute intention to unclear objects and events helps humans make quick, survival-oriented decisions. Humans instinctively interpret ambiguous situations as having intention, which enhances quick decision-making for survival.
subjective_conditions: 1. 주어진 단어(어구)만을 변형 없이 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것
vocabulary_box: allows / agency / decisions / the instinct / humans / objects or events / to make / to detect / survival / unclear / quick / in
questions.answer: the instinct to detect agency in unclear objects and events allows humans to make quick survival decisions
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 모호한 대상이나 사건에서 의도(agency)를 탐지하려는 본능이 인간의 빠른 생존 결정을 돕는다는 것입니다. <보기>의 단어들을 조합하면 'unclear objects and events에서 agency를 감지하려는 instinct가 humans가 quick survival decisions를 하도록 allow한다'는 문장이 완성됩니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 괄호 (A)~(C) 중 의미상 가장 적절한 단어끼리 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an (A)[exact / inexact] identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be (B)[accurate / inaccurate] more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the (C)[superior / inferior] performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.explanation: 목격자 증언 실험에서 얼굴 특징을 신중하게 고려하는 것은 오히려 부정확한(inexact) 식별의 신호일 수 있습니다. 반대로 왜 알아보는지 설명하지 못할 때 오히려 더 정확한(accurate) 경향이 있습니다. 글의 결론에서도 무의식적인 첫 추측이 논리적 정당화보다 우수한(superior) 성능을 보인다고 설명합니다.
options_translation: ① 정확한 - 정확한 - 우수한
② 정확한 - 부정확한 - 열등한
③ 부정확한 - 정확한 - 우수한
④ 부정확한 - 정확한 - 열등한
⑤ 부정확한 - 부정확한 - 우수한

questions.question: 8. 윗글의 (A)~(C) 중 어법상 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point (A)[at which / for which] AI exceeds human intelligence. After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. ____________________________________ _____________________________________ Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, (B)[which / that] will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI. The direction of AI's evolution will depend greatly on (C)[what / whether] values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
questions.explanation: (A) 선행사 the point를 수식하며 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오므로 '그 지점에서'라는 의미의 전치사+관계대명사 'at which'가 적절합니다.(B) 콤마(,) 뒤에 이어지는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사이므로 'that'은 사용할 수 없고 'which'가 적절합니다.(C) 뒤에 명사(values and ethics)를 수식하는 의문 형용사 역할을 해야 하므로 '어떤 가치와 윤리'라는 의미의 'what'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 <조건>을 고려하여 완성하시오.
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point (A)[at which / for which] AI exceeds human intelligence. After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. ____________________________________ _____________________________________ Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, (B)[which / that] will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI. The direction of AI's evolution will depend greatly on (C)[what / whether] values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>에 주어진 단어를 모두 사용할 것(어형 변화 불가)
2. 단어 세 개를 본문에서 찾아 추가할 것
3. 오류가 없는 완전한 문장을 작성할 것
vocabulary_box: together, will, and, then, to, human, begin
questions.answer: AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 특이점(singularity) 이후 AI와 인간의 의식이 함께 진화하기 시작할 것이라는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 보기의 단어들(together, will, and, then, to, human, begin)과 본문에서 찾은 세 단어(AI, consciousness, evolve)를 조합하여 'AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together.'라는 문장을 완성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 10월 21번]
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than ⓐ<u>retrieving</u> the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more ⓑ<u>efficient</u> way to store information ─ a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail find it ⓒ<u>difficult</u> to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at the ⓓ<u>expense</u> of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely ⓔ<u>underscored</u> the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: 기억이 있는 그대로 재생되는 것이 아니라 추상적인 재구성을 통해 형성된다는 발견은 목격자 증언이 법적으로 가지는 최고의 권위(legal primacy)를 '강조한(underscored)' 것이 아니라, 오히려 그 신뢰성을 떨어뜨려 '약화시켰다(undermined/challenged)'는 의미가 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods.
ordered_passages: (A) But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price.

(B) The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.

(C) If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one.
questions.explanation: 한 가지 버전만 팔 때의 손실과 두 가지 버전을 팔 때 소비자가 저렴한 것을 선택하는 경향을 설명한 (C)가 먼저 오고, 이를 해결하기 위해 더 비싼 세 번째 모델을 추가하면 두 번째 모델의 판매가 늘어난다는 전략을 제시하는 (A)가 이어집니다. 마지막으로 소비자들이 이러한 마케팅에 유도되어 결국 중간 모델을 사게 된다는 결론을 내리는 (B)가 오는 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods.(A) But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price.(B) The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.(C) If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one.
options: ② How Companies Lead You to Spend More
③ Buying the Cheapest Option Means Buying Twice
④ High-End Technology Guarantees Maximum Profits
⑤ Marketing Tactics That Make Consumers Buy the Most Expensive Item
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기업이 세 가지 옵션을 제시하여 소비자가 심리적으로 유도되어 결국 중간 가격대의 제품을 선택하게 함으로써 더 많은 지출을 하게 만드는 마케팅 기법을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '기업이 어떻게 당신이 더 많이 소비하도록 유도하는가'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 더 많은 기능, 더 비싼 가격
기업이 당신이 더 많이 지출하도록 이끄는 방법
가장 저렴한 옵션을 사는 것은 두 번 사는 것을 의미한다
최첨단 기술이 최대 이익을 보장한다
소비자들이 가장 비싼 품목을 사게 만드는 마케팅 전술

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on (A)________________ in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to (B)________________, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
questions.explanation: 인간의 번영은 집단 내에서의 (A)사회적 관계(social relationships) 혹은 지위에 달려 있으며, 우리는 타인의 인식을 무의식적으로 모니터링하도록 진화했습니다. 만약 우리가 행동하는 동기가 내면에서 오는 것이 아니라 타인의 시선이나 (B)사회적 압박(social pressure)에 반응하는 것임을 의식적으로 인지한다면 그 행동이 진실하지 않게 보일 수 있다는 맥락입니다.
options_translation: 공감적 감정 ... 공공 규제
사회적 관계 ... 사회적 압박
합리적 행동 ... 개인적 감정
사회적 수용 ... 타고난 본능
개인적 성취 ... 외부적 동기

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre ─ indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate' fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant ─ in time or in place ─ we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
options: ① 심각한 기후변화로 인해 사람들은 공포에 휩싸일 것이다.
② 사람들은 각종 노력 끝에 변화하는 기후에 적응할 것이다.
③ 기후변화를 다루는 재난영화는 가장 인기 있는 장르 중 하나다.
④ 기후 소설은 지구온난화의 영향이 명백해짐에 따라 사라질 것이다.
⑤ 기후변화가 실감 남에 따라 기후 소설에 대한 수요도 증가할 것이다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화가 인류의 삶에서 지엽적인 특징으로 보일 때만 그것에 '관한' 이야기를 할 수 있다고 주장합니다. 기후 변화의 영향이 모든 사람에게 명백해지고 일상이 되면, 더 이상 창문 밖으로 보이는 현실과 다를 바 없는 기후 소설이나 영화는 장르로서의 의미를 잃고 사라지게 될 것이라는 내용이 주제입니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 어법에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
subjective_conditions: *어형 변화 불가
questions.answer: (A) a distorted consciousness is responsible for depression(B) a brain substance imbalance
questions.explanation: 지문은 우울증이 뇌의 화학 물질 불균형에 의해 발생하는 것이 아니라, 오히려 의식의 왜곡(자아감이나 삶의 의미 상실)이 우울증의 근본 원인이며, 뇌 물질의 불균형은 그 결과라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '왜곡된 의식이 우울증에 책임이 있다(원인이다)'는 내용이 들어가야 하며, (B)에는 그 결과로 나타나는 '뇌 물질 불균형'이 들어가야 합니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글에서 주어진 글이 들어갈 곳으로 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. (A) Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. (B) In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. (C) Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. (D) Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 기술적 은유의 능동적 특성에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. (A)와 (B)에서는 언어적 은유의 수동적 특성과 독자의 노력이 필요함을 설명하고 있으며, (C) 앞부분까지 이러한 설명이 이어집니다. (C)의 위치는 언어적 은유에서 기술적 은유의 특징으로 설명이 전환되는 지점이며, 주어진 문장의 'on the other hand'와 기술적 은유의 'active'한 성격이 (C) 이후의 기술 제작자들이 즉각적인 유용성을 중시한다는 내용과 자연스럽게 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. (A) Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. (B) In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. (C) Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. (D) Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience. (E)
questions.summary_sentence: Technological metaphors are (A)___________ in that they are made through digital artifacts, forcefully reshaping a user's comprehension, whereas linguistic metaphors are (B)___________, requiring the audience's (C)___________ to understand their meaning.
questions.explanation: 본문은 기술적 은유와 언어적 은유를 비교하고 있습니다. 기술적 은유는 사용자의 의미 지평을 강제로 변화시키는 '능동적(active)'인 성격을 가지는 반면, 언어적 은유는 독자가 스스로 그 세계에 들어가기를 선택해야 하는 '수동적(passive)'인 성격을 가지며 이해를 위해 독자의 '인지적 노력(cognitive effort)'을 필요로 합니다.
options_translation: ① 능동적인 / 수동적인 / 인지적 노력
② 수동적인 / 능동적인 / 수동적인 참여
③ 수동적인 / 능동적인 / 추가적인 지식
④ 수동적인 / 능동적인 / 적극적인 개입
⑤ 능동적인 / 수동적인 / 거의 없는 노력

questions.question: 26. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers.
ordered_passages: (A) An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature.
(B) Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes.
(C) It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion.
(D) And while they mimic, they hunt ─ producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 낮에 얕은 바다에서 문어를 발견한 놀라운 상황을 제시합니다. (C)에서 사진작가들이 다시 보았을 때 그것이 착시를 일으키고 있는 문어임을 알게 된 장면이 이어지고, (A)에서 문어가 가진 지능과 변신 능력을 설명하며 해당 문어의 행동을 묘사합니다. (B)에서는 그 이후 발견된 유사한 사례들을 언급하고, 마지막으로 (D)에서 문어들이 변장하며 사냥하는 구체적인 방식을 설명하며 마무리되는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 have-and-have-not inequities가 가리키는 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Today the water crisis is political ─ which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix ─ and, therefore, functionally elective. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an abundant resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to address it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly highlights <u>have-and-have-not inequities</u>, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
options: ① The divide between politicians and ordinary people regarding income
② The difference between urban and rural areas in terms of healthcare quality
③ The inequality in education resources between wealthy and poor communities
④ The unequal distribution of water and sanitation due to the economic gap between countries
⑤ The disparity between countries that have access to modern technology and those that do not
questions.explanation: 이 글은 물 위기가 자원 부족 때문이 아니라 정치적 무관심과 비효율적인 인프라로 인해 발생한다는 점을 지적합니다. 밑줄 친 'have-and-have-not inequities'는 21억 명의 깨끗한 식수 부재와 45억 명의 위생 시설 부재 상황에서 알 수 있듯이, 경제적 격차로 인해 물과 위생 시설의 혜택을 받는 국가와 받지 못하는 국가 사이의 불평등한 분배 상황을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 소득에 관한 정치인들과 일반인들 사이의 격차
② 의료 서비스 수준 면에서 도시와 농촌 지역의 차이
③ 부유한 지역과 가난한 지역 사이의 교육 자원 불평등
④ 국가 간 경제적 격차로 인한 물과 위생 시설의 불평등한 분배
⑤ 현대 기술에 접근할 수 있는 국가와 그렇지 못한 국가 사이의 격차

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: ___________________________ due to what Alvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the world. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
options: ① Disciplining might not work as expected
② Strict rules are not successful for teens
③ Hitting a student to punish him would cause an opposite effect
④ Penalizing a kid would be an efficient way to make him behave
⑤ Punishing a child may be time-consuming but surprisingly effective
questions.explanation: 이 글은 심리학자 알바로 빌바오가 제안한 '속임수 처벌'의 개념을 통해, 아이를 꾸짖거나 벌을 주는 행위가 오히려 관심을 갈구하는 아이에게는 보상이 되어 원치 않는 행동을 강화할 수 있음을 경고하고 있습니다. 따라서 훈육이 예상과 달리 효과를 거두지 못할 수 있다는 내용의 ①번이 첫 문장의 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 훈육이 기대만큼 효과적이지 않을 수 있다
② 엄격한 규칙은 십 대들에게 성공적이지 않다
③ 벌을 주기 위해 학생을 때리는 것은 반대 효과를 일으킬 것이다
④ 아이를 처벌하는 것이 그를 올바르게 행동하게 만드는 효율적인 방법이 될 것이다
⑤ 아이를 처벌하는 것은 시간 소모가 크지만 놀랍게도 효과적이다

questions.question: 29. [24~30] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure ⓐ<u>the number of times someone smiles</u> during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure ⓑ<u>the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes</u>. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "ⓒ<u>How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?</u>" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of ⓓ<u>asking people to rate how a procrastinator they are bad</u>, ask, "ⓔ<u>How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?</u>" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 'how'는 형용사나 부사를 수식해야 하며, '얼마나 나쁜 미루는 사람인지'를 묻는 맥락이므로 'how bad a procrastinator they are'의 어순이 되어야 합니다. 현재의 'how a procrastinator they are bad'는 어순상 틀린 표현입니다.

questions.question: 30. [24~30] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오. 윗글의 주제를 <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용하고, 윗글에서 두 단어를 추가하여 어법에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure ⓐ<u>the number of times someone smiles</u> during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure ⓑ<u>the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes</u>. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "ⓒ<u>How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?</u>" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of ⓓ<u>asking people to rate how a procrastinator they are bad</u>, ask, "ⓔ<u>How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?</u>" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용할 것
윗글에서 두 단어를 추가하여 완성할 것 (추가 단어: concrete, reliable)
어형 변화 불가

questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심 내용은 신뢰할 수 있는 정량적 데이터를 얻기 위해 구체적인 질문을 하는 것이 중요하다는 것입니다. <보기>의 단어들과 본문에서 추출한 'concrete'(구체적인), 'reliable'(신뢰할 수 있는)을 조합하여 주제문을 작성합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
options: ① The process from brain death determination to transplant surgery must be conducted strictly according to regulations.
② The criteria for determining brain death should be made stricter to support the families of organ donors.
③ Reliable and tougher guidelines for determining death need to be established.
④ After organ transplantation, the recipients should receive continuous health management and medication treatment.
⑤ The criteria for diagnosing death should be identical for both organ donors and non-donors to relieve public mistrust.
questions.explanation: 필자는 장기 기증자의 뇌사 판정 기준이 일반적인 사망 판정 기준보다 더 엄격한 것이 오히려 대중의 불신과 오해를 불러일으킬 수 있다고 지적합니다. 따라서 일관성을 위해 장기 기증자와 비기증자의 사망 진단 기준이 동일해야 한다고 주장하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌사 판정에서 이식 수술까지의 과정은 규정에 따라 엄격하게 진행되어야 한다.
② 뇌사 판정 기준은 장기 기증자의 가족을 지원하기 위해 더 엄격해져야 한다.
③ 사망 판정을 위한 신뢰할 수 있고 더 강화된 가이드라인이 수립될 필요가 있다.
④ 장기 이식 후 수혜자는 지속적인 건강 관리와 약물 치료를 받아야 한다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's <u>the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies</u>.
options: ① the brain's way to keep staying alert to unexpected experiences in everyday life
② the brain's way of avoiding the immediate responses in reaction to fearful situations
③ the brain's mechanism for ignoring the hazardous and pursuing the stable in the environment
④ the way the brain lowers focus on repetitive stimuli so novel details become more noticeable
⑤ the brain's mechanism for processing external information quickly through more complex connections between neurons
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간이 변하지 않는 환경이나 반복되는 자극에 쉽게 지루함을 느끼는 이유가 신경 세포의 설계 때문이라고 설명합니다. 변하지 않는 자극에 대한 반응 수준을 낮추어야 새로운 자극(중요한 변화)이 더 잘 눈에 띄게 되기 때문인데, 이는 '반딧불이(새로운 자극)를 보기 위해 현관 등(반복적 자극)을 끄는 것'과 같다는 비유를 사용하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 일상생활에서 예상치 못한 경험에 대해 계속해서 경계하는 뇌의 방식
② 두려운 상황에 반응하여 즉각적인 반응을 피하는 뇌의 방식

④ 새로운 세부 사항이 더 눈에 띄도록 반복적인 자극에 대한 집중력을 낮추는 뇌의 방식

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There has been remarkable progress in deep-learning based facial recognition approaches in recent years. However, in terms of identification performance, they still have limitations. These limitations relate to the database used in the learning stage. If the selected database does not contain enough instances, the result may be systematically affected. For example, the performance of a facial biometric system may decrease if the person to be identified was enrolled over 10 years ago. The factor to consider is that this person may experience changes in the texture of the face, particularly with the appearance of wrinkles and sagging skin. These changes may be highlighted by weight gain or loss.
options: ① systematic ways to prevent facial aging such as wrinkles over time
② challenges in deep-learning facial recognition due to learned database constraints

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like -Why does the moon have phases?- Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half were not allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as -Why does Swiss cheese have holes?- These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions. But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
options: ① The Universal View of Philosophers to Define Nature
② Time: the Inevitable Force That Makes Everything Wane
③ How Circles Show the Unique Characteristics of Geometry
④ Physical world: the Imperfect Reflection of a Perfect Unseen Reality

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything you consume, from food and air to bacteria and viruses, ⓐ<u>passes</u> through your mouth before reaching the rest of your body. Maintaining a healthy mouth allows your body ⓑ<u>to bet</u> essential nutrients while protecting it from harm. Also, it has adequate space for air to travel to the lungs and healthy teeth and gums ⓒ<u>that</u> block dangerous microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. From the moment life begins, the condition of your mouth influences your overall well-being, often ⓓ<u>reflect</u> the health of your entire body. questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying them to culture. questions.explanation: 이 글은 문화적 진화와 유전적 전달 사이의 유사점과 차이점을 다루고 있습니다. 빈칸 앞부분에서 문화적 전달과 유전적 전달 사이의 차이를 설명하기 위해 모델이 수정되어야 한다고 언급하고, 빈칸 뒤의 예시(자녀가 반드시 부모의 문화적 형질을 따르는 것은 아님)는 두 과정이 다르다는 것을 보여줍니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 "우리는 문화적 전달 과정이 유전적 전달 과정과 '완벽하게 일치한다'고 기대하지 않는다"는 내용이 오는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The adolescent brain is not fully developed until its early twenties. This means the way the adolescents' decision-making circuits integrate and process information may put them at a disadvantage. ④ they are excessively influenced by the opinions of others while making decisions
⑤ they deliberately exclude rational judgment from the decision-making process
questions.explanation: 청소년의 뇌에서 이성적 판단을 담당하는 전두엽은 늦게 성숙하는 반면, 감정 반응을 담당하는 변연계는 일찍 성숙합니다. 이러한 발달 속도의 차이 때문에 청소년의 의사결정은 결과에 대한 인식보다 감정적 요인에 의해 주도되며, 이것이 잘못된 결정을 내릴 가능성을 높입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '의사결정에 관여하는 뇌 부위들이 서로 다른 속도로 발달하기 때문'이라는 내용이 들어가는 것이 논리적입니다.
options_translation: ① 그들의 전두엽과 변연계가 균형 잡힌 방식으로 발달하기
② 그들이 미성숙한 전두엽에 의해 지배되는 감정 기반의 판단을 피하기
③ 의사결정에 관여하는 그들의 뇌 영역들이 서로 다른 속도로 발달하기
④ 그들이 의사결정을 내리는 동안 타인의 의견에 과도하게 영향을 받기
⑤ 그들이 의사결정 과정에서 이성적인 판단을 의도적으로 배제하기

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When writing a novel, research for information needs to be done. The thing is that some kinds of fiction demand a higher level of detail: crime fiction, for example, or scientific thrillers. The information is never hard to find; one website for authors even organizes trips to police stations, so that crime writers can get it right. Often, a polite letter will earn you permission to visit a particular location and record all the details that you need.
