But remember that you will drive your readers to boredom if you think that you need to pack everything you discover into your work. The details that matter are _______________________. The crucial thing is telling a story, finding the characters, the tension, and the conflict - not the train timetable or the building blueprint.
options: ① the things that writers obtain in a particular location
② everything that would be written in a book by writers
③ professional knowledge which enables writers to understand a genre
④ the readers' background knowledge that helps them reconstruct a story
⑤ information that lets readers grasp a story by following what characters undergo
questions.explanation: 소설을 쓸 때 조사를 통해 얻은 세부 사항을 너무 많이 넣으면 독자들이 지루해할 수 있다고 경고합니다. 중요한 것은 기차 시간표나 청사진 같은 단순한 정보가 아니라 이야기, 캐릭터, 긴장감, 갈등이라고 말합니다. 즉, 중요한 세부 사항은 독자가 인물들이 겪는 일을 따라감으로써 이야기를 파악하게 해주는 정보여야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 작가들이 특정 장소에서 얻는 것들
② 작가에 의해 책에 쓰일 모든 것
③ 작가들로 하여금 장르를 이해하게 해주는 전문 지식
④ 독자들이 이야기를 재구성하도록 돕는 배경지식
⑤ 독자들이 등장인물이 겪는 일을 따라가며 이야기를 파악하게 해주는 정보

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 11월 30번]
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions.
ordered_passages: (A) However, sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of clarity. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you just need to let go of belongings that serve no immediate purpose or won't be needed shortly.

(B) So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item.

(C) This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 미니멀리즘이 귀중한 소유물을 희생하는 것이라는 부정적인 인상을 준다고 언급합니다. (C)에서 이러한 불안감이 소유물에 대한 애착에서 비롯된다고 설명하며 인간이 사물에 의미를 부여한다고 부연합니다. (B)에서 그렇다면 왜 미니멀리스트가 되는지에 대한 질문을 던지며 미니멀리즘이 감정을 해치지 않는다고 답합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 쓸모없는 물건을 버릴 때의 슬픔은 명료함의 즐거움으로 극복되며, 진정한 미니멀리즘은 불필요한 것만 놓아주는 것이라고 정리합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 11월 35번]
questions.passage: Both casinos and insurance industries reflect statistical factors. To balance individual losses, they rely on the same law. (A) For example, People may have beginner's luck after betting on 7 on their first encounter with the game of roulette. (B) However, their luck will at some point fade away if they make the same bet several times. (C) In other words, the more often they repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning. (D) Similarly, can insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. (E) According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to match the true state of the world.
questions.insertion_sentence: To summarize, they are ruled by the law of large numbers, describing a situation where having more data is better for making predictions in statistics.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '대수의 법칙'을 요약하며 데이터가 많을수록 통계적 예측에 유리하다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 지문의 (D)에서 보험사들이 대량의 데이터를 수집한다는 사례를 들고 난 뒤, (E) 위치에서 'According to it'의 'it'이 가리키는 대상이 주어진 문장의 'law of large numbers'가 되어야 글의 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 11월 31번]
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristic of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself. Psychologist George M. Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment. Stratton wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally turned the world upside down for him. (A) In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him. (B) With time, however, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated. (C) He used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something, for example. (D) Fortunately, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for the rest of his life. (E) For him, everything returned to normal after one day.
questions.insertion_sentence: As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 반전 안경을 벗었을 때 다시 문제에 직면했다는 내용입니다. (B)에서 안경을 쓴 상태로 적응이 완료된 후, 안경을 벗었을 때 다시 발생하는 혼란에 대한 구체적인 예시인 (C) 'reach for something' 할 때 잘못된 손을 사용하는 내용 바로 앞에 위치하는 것이 적절합니다. (D)는 그 이후 지각이 다시 돌아왔다는 내용으로 이어집니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson argues that we perceive the world by (A)__________ focusing in on particular features within it. Take platypuses. We might zoom in so closely to their fur that each hair appears different. We might also zoom out to the extent where it appears as a single, uniform object. We might take the platypus as an individual, or we might treat it as part of a larger unit such as a species or an ecosystem. It's possible to move between many of these perspectives, although we may need some additional tools and skills to zoom in on individual pieces of hair or zoom out to entire ecosystems. Crucially, however, we can only take up one perspective at a time. We can pay attention to the varied behavior of individual animals, look at what unites them into a single species, or look at them as part of bigger ecological patterns. Each perspective (B)__________ certain aspects while leaving others in the background.
questions.explanation: 인류학자 Gregory Bateson은 옰가 세상의 특정한 특징에 '선택적으로(selectively)' 초점을 믞음으로써 인식한다고 주장합니다. 오리너구리의 털을 확대하거나 축소하는 등 다양한 관점을 가질 수 읈지만, 한 번에 하나의 관점만 취할 수 읈습니다. 따논서 각각의 관점은 어떤 측문을 '강조(highlights)'하는 반면 다른 측문은 배경으로 남겨둡다고 밴는 감이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: 필연적으로 - 통합한다
선택적으로 - 강조한다
독점적으로 - 바꿈다
영구적으로 - 강조한다
관습적으로 - 왔곡한다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
questions.summary_sentence: The development of a small number of mass-produced grains to solve food problems was initially (A)__________, but it has increased reliance on them, making a global food system more (B)__________ to disasters.
questions.explanation: 식량 문제를 해결하기 위해 소수의 고생산 품종을 개발한 갃은 초기에 '생산적(productive)'이었습니다. 그러나 이는 의존도를 포아 품종의 단일화를 초래했고, 결국 세계 식량 체계를 재해에 더 '사우기 쉠운/취약한(fragile)' 상태로 변모시켰습니다.
options_translation: 생산적인 - 취약한
홁신적인 - 저항력 읈는
미숙한 - 민감한
실용적인 - 적응력 읈는
형편없는 - 내구성이 읈는

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고 요약문의 빈칸에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: A ball thrown into the air is acted upon by the initial force given it, persisting as inertia of movement and tending to carry it in the same straight line, and by the constant pull of gravity downward, as well as by the resistance of the air. It moves, accordingly, in a curved path. Now the path does not represent the working of any particular force; there is simply the combination of the three elementary forces mentioned; but in a real sense, there is something in the total action besides the isolated action of three forces, namely, their joint action. In the same way, when two or more human individuals are together, their mutual relationships and their arrangement into a group are things which would not be revealed if we confined our attention to each individual separately. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that some of the tendencies to action of the individual are related definitely to other persons, and could not be aroused except by other persons acting as stimuli. An individual in complete isolation would not reveal their competitive tendencies, their tendencies towards the opposite sex, their protective tendencies towards children. This shows that the traits of human nature do not fully appear until the individual is brought into relationships with other individuals.
questions.summary_sentence: Like the case of a thrown ball, human behavior results from the combined influence of multiple factors, with __________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: ㆍ<보기>의 표현을 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
ㆍ<보기>의 표현을 제외한 다른 표현을 추가하지 말 것
ㆍ필요한 경우 어형 변화를 할 것
vocabulary_box: individuals / others / individual traits / interact / only when / apparent / become / with
questions.answer: individual traits becoming apparent only when individuals interact with others
questions.explanation: 이 글은 공의 움직임이 여러 힘의 상호작용인 것처럼 인간의 행동과 특성 또한 개인이 고립되어 있을 때가 아니라 다른 사람들과 관계를 맺고 상호작용할 때 비로소 드러난다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 'with + 명사 + 분사' 구문을 활용하여 '개별적인 특성이 오직 개인이 타인과 상호작용할 때만 명확해진다'는 내용을 완성해야 합니다. become을 becoming으로 변형해야 합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, ⓐ<u>improving</u> the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs ⓑ<u>where</u> inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with ⓒ<u>potentially</u> positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity ⓓ<u>translate</u> written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of ⓔ<u>lower-skilled</u> individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.*dysarthric: (신경 장애로 인한) 구음(構音) 장애의
questions.explanation: ⓓ의 capacity는 뒤에서 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사를 수반하므로 to translate가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
options: ① Unfamiliar Originality in Modern Music
② Originality Is Irrelevant in Musical Greatness
③ Why Some Composers Shine While Others Fade
④ Mozart: What a Short and Fleeting Genius He is
⑤ What Sets Apart Highly-skilled Leaders from Others?
questions.explanation: 글은 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 오해받았던 이유는 그들의 '독창성(낯설음)' 때문이며, 살리에리가 위대한 작곡가가 되지 못한 이유는 독창성이 부족했기 때문이라고 설명합니다. 따라서 '왜 어떤 작곡가는 빛나고 다른 이들은 사라지는가(독창성의 유무)'를 다루는 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 현대 음악에서의 낯선 독창성
② 독창성은 음악적 위대함과 무관하다
③ 왜 어떤 작곡가는 빛나고 다른 이들은 사라지는가
④ 모차르트: 얼마나 짧고 덧없는 천재인가
⑤ 숙련된 리더들을 다른 사람들과 구별 짓는 것은 무엇인가?

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us ⓐ<u>stay away</u> from dangers and expressing anger helps us scare off threats. Also expressing positive emotions helps us ⓑ<u>connect</u> with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, ⓒ<u>guides</u> many of our activities. For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more ⓓ<u>slightly</u> (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us ⓔ<u>adjust</u> and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 미래에 위협을 피하기 위해 경험을 더 '잘' 혹은 '생생하게' 기억해야 하므로 slightly(약간, 조금)는 부적절합니다. vividly(생생하게)나 strongly(강하게)와 같은 표현이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to ⓐ<u>quantitative</u> data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might ⓑ<u>estimate</u> the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be ⓒ<u>trustworthy</u>. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" ⓓ<u>stimulates</u> a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts ⓔ<u>ambiguous</u>.*procrastinator: 미루는 사람
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구체적인 질문을 통해 추상적인 개념을 '명확하게(concrete/measurable)' 만드는 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 마지막 문장의 ambiguous(모호한)는 문맥상 부적절하며 clear나 measurable 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 40번]
questions.passage: Punishing a child may be __________ due to what Alvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy.
questions.explanation: 아이를 처벌하는 것이 오히려 그 행동을 권장하는 결과를 낳는 '속임수 처벌'의 사례를 설명하고 있으므로, 처벌이 '비효과적(ineffective)'일 수 있다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 성공적인
② 효과 없는
③ 실용적인
④ 피할 수 없는
⑤ 상호 보완적인

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 20번]
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates ____________________, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop-out, or worse.
options: ② obstacles they can fully overcome
③ goals burdened over their capacities
④ a path to genuine self-discovery
⑤ strong motivation for future success
questions.explanation: 부모가 영재인 자녀를 지나치게 자랑하는 행위는 아이에게 스트레스와 압박감을 주며, 아이의 실제 능력보다 과도한 기대를 갖게 합니다. 따라서 '능력 이상의 부담스러운 목표'를 만든다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 뛰어날 수 있는 기회
② 완전히 극복할 수 있는 장애물
③ 능력 밖의 부담스러운 목표
④ 진정한 자아 발견으로 가는 길
⑤ 미래의 성공을 위한 강력한 동기부여

questions.question: 14. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "luminiferous ether"가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of <u>luminiferous ether</u>, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① a fruitless chase after a misconceived core
② a mysterious substance that shines by itself
③ a pointless effort to grasp the meaning of life
④ scientific evidence to find the essence of things
⑤ an availing search for a meaning rooted in evidence
questions.explanation: 본문에서 'luminiferous ether'는 빛의 매질로 존재한다고 믿어졌으나 실제로는 존재하지 않았던 개념입니다. 저자는 이를 어두운 방에 없는 검은 고양이를 찾는 것에 비유하며, 잘못된 개념(wrong concept)을 바탕으로 본질을 찾으려 했던 과학자들의 헛된 노력을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '잘못 파악된 핵심에 대한 결실 없는 추구'라는 의미의 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 잘못 생각된 핵심에 대한 결실 없는 추적
② 스스로 빛나는 신비로운 물질
③ 삶의 의미를 파악하려는 무의미한 노력
④ 사물의 본질을 찾기 위한 과학적 증거
⑤ 증거에 뿌리를 둔 의미에 대한 유용한 탐색

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. ⓐIn contrast, when people struggle to articulate why they recognize someone and say things like "his face just popped out at me," they are often more accurate. ⓑSometimes, our initial, instinctive reaction to a situation provides the most truthful insight into what our mind perceives. ⓒThat first impression can often be more accurate than the rational, step-by-step reasoning we create afterward. ⓓA mistaken first impression can reinforce stereotypes and lead to unfair judgments or discrimination. ⓔIn Blink, Malcolm Gladwell highlights numerous psychological and behavioral economics studies that show how quick, unconscious judgments frequently outperform decisions based on detailed, logical reasoning.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 목격자 증언 등의 사례를 통해, 신중하고 논리적인 추론보다 직관적이고 무의식적인 첫인상이나 판단이 더 정확할 수 있다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓓ번 문장은 잘못된 첫인상이 가져올 수 있는 부정적인 결과(고정관념 강화, 차별)를 언급하고 있어, 직관적 판단의 '정확성'을 강조하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 가리키는 것이 다른 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. ⓐ<u>It</u> refers to the point at which AI exceeds human intelligence. After that point, it is predicted to improve ⓑ<u>itself</u> repeatedly and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, ⓒ<u>it</u> will be a conscious being, not just a machine. AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI. The direction of AI's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into ⓓ<u>it</u>. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing ⓔ<u>it</u>s rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'It'은 앞 문장의 'the concept of singularity'(특이점의 개념)를 가리킵니다. 반면 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 'AI'(인공지능)를 가리키거나 인공지능과 관련된 소유격을 나타냅니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
ordered_passages: (A) The same goes for Instagram. I like looking at pretty people, like everyone else. But to think that life is primarily about these surfaces - getting approval for your six-pack or how you look in a bikini - is a recipe for unhappiness.(B) In fact, that's pretty much the opposite of friendship. Being friends is about looking into each other's eyes, doing things together in the world, an endless exchange of gut laughs and bear hugs, joy and grief and dancing.(C) And the same goes for a lot of how we interact on Facebook too. It's not friendship to pore jealously over another person's photos and boasts and complaints, and to expect them to do the same for you.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 TV가 세상의 표면과 외양에 집중하게 한다고 언급한 뒤, (A)에서 인스타그램 또한 그러한 '표면(surfaces)'에 관한 것이며 이것이 불행의 원인이 될 수 있다고 연결됩니다. (C)에서는 페이스북에서의 상호작용 또한 진정한 우정이 아니라고 설명하며, 마지막으로 (B)에서 진정한 우정의 의미(In fact, that's pretty much the opposite of friendship)를 정의하며 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. (A) Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. (B) This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. (C) But it also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. (D) On the other hand, the ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. (E) Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.insertion_sentence: The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 엘리트 유명인의 특징(신비주의, 계급적 거리감, 재능)을 설명합니다. (D) 뒤 문장에서 '반면에(On the other hand)'라는 연결어와 함께 평범한 유명인(ordinary celebrity)이 다른 평범한 사람들과의 정기적이고 빈번한 소통을 통해 관심을 끈다는 내용이 나오므로, 엘리트 유명인과 대조를 이루기 위해 (D) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. (A) This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. (B) In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. (C) Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. (D) If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. (E) Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
questions.insertion_sentence: In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 우울증이 뇌 물질 감소의 원인이지 결과가 아니라는 내용을 다시 설명(In other words)하고 있습니다. (A)에서 뇌 물질 불균형이 우울증의 '결과'라고 언급한 것을 구체화하고 있으며, (B) 뒤에서 언급된 '이 수정된 인과관계(this revised cause-and-effect)'가 가리키는 대상이 주어진 문장의 내용이므로 (B)가 정답입니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage:
Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon. In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
*phytoplankton: 식물성 플랑크톤
options: ① Whales play a key role in carbon storage, with each whale releasing around 30 tons of carbon dioxide when they die, leaving it in the atmosphere for centuries.
② Compared to trees, whales are far more effective at carbon storage; for example, a single tree absorbs only about 48 pounds of carbon dioxide annually.
③ Whales also boost carbon sequestration by fertilizing the ocean with nutrient-rich waste, which helps increase phytoplankton, tiny plants that absorb carbon dioxide.
④ Economists from the International Monetary Fund in 2019 suggested using incentives to restore whale populations.
⑤ A global whale restoration program is being proposed as a natural solution to help fight climate change and support marine ecosystems.
questions.explanation:
지문에서는 고래가 죽을 때 평균 30톤의 이산화탄소를 격리(sequesters)하여 수 세기 동안 대기 중에서 제거한다(taking that carbon out of the atmosphere)고 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ①번 선택지는 고래가 대기 중으로 이산화탄소를 '방출(releasing)'하여 '남겨둔다(leaving it in the atmosphere)'고 설명하고 있으므로 본문의 내용과 정반대입니다.

[오답 분석]
② 본문의 'average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year'와 일치합니다.
③ 본문의 'fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste' 및 식물성 플랑크톤의 역할과 일치합니다.
④ 본문의 '2019, economists from the IMF ... called for a new global program of economic incentives'와 일치합니다.
⑤ 본문의 마지막 문장 'nature-based solution to climate change' 및 복원 프로그램 제안과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 고래는 탄소 저장에 핵심적인 역할을 하며, 죽을 때 약 30톤의 이산화탄소를 방출하여 수 세기 동안 대기 중에 남겨둔다.
② 나무와 비교했을 때 고래는 탄소 저장에 훨씬 더 효과적이다. 예를 들어, 단일 나무는 연간 약 48파운드의 이산화탄소만을 흡수한다.
③ 고래는 영양분이 풍부한 배설물로 바다를 비옥하게 하여 이산화탄소를 흡수하는 작은 식물인 식물성 플랑크톤을 증가시킴으로써 탄소 격리를 촉진한다.
④ 2019년 국제통화기금(IMF)의 경제학자들은 고래 개체 수를 복원하기 위해 유인책을 사용할 것을 제안했다.
⑤ 세계적인 고래 복원 프로그램이 기후 변화에 맞서고 해양 생태계를 지원하기 위한 자연 기반의 해결책으로 제안되고 있다.

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)에 해당하는 예시가 아닌 것은?
questions.passage: From an early age, we assign purpose to objects and events, preferring this reasoning to random chance. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because they don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. However, by attributing intention to animals and even objects, we are able to make fast decisions about the likely behaviour of that being. This was essential in our hunter-gatherer days to avoid being eaten by predators. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that (A)<u>we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics</u>, as those are the mental processes which we understand. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents. This results in a perceptual system strongly biased towards anthropomorphism. Therefore, we tend to assume intention even where there is none. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you. By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has saved your life.*anthropomorphism: 의인화
options: ① The storm is angry and the wind is trying to knock me down.
② My feet hurt so badly that I don't want to walk anymore tonight.
③ Tom thought, 'This chair doesn't want me to sit on it', if it felt unstable.
④ The printer is refusing to work today. It doesn't give me any paper.
⑤ A series of green traffic lights is the universe helping you get somewhere quickly.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 (A)는 무생물이나 모호한 대상을 인간과 같은 의도를 가진 존재로 해석하는 '의인화'에 대한 설명입니다. 2번은 화자 본인의 신체적 고통과 주관적인 의사를 나타낼 뿐, 무생물을 의인화한 사례가 아니므로 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 폭풍이 화가 났고 바람이 나를 쓰러뜨리려 하고 있다.
② 발이 너무 아파서 오늘 밤에는 더 이상 걷고 싶지 않다.
③ Tom은 의자가 불안정하게 느껴지자 '이 의자가 내가 앉는 것을 원치 않는구나'라고 생각했다.
④ 프린터가 오늘 작동을 거부하고 있다. 종이를 전혀 주지 않는다.
⑤ 연속된 초록색 신호등은 우주가 당신이 어딘가에 빨리 도착하도록 돕는 것이다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: From an early age, we assign purpose to objects and events, preferring this reasoning to random chance. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because they don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. However, by attributing intention to animals and even objects, we are able to make fast decisions about the likely behaviour of that being. This was essential in our hunter-gatherer days to avoid being eaten by predators. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, as those are the mental processes which we understand. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents. This results in a perceptual system strongly biased towards anthropomorphism. Therefore, we tend to assume intention even where there is none. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you. By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has saved your life.*anthropomorphism: 의인화
questions.summary_sentence: Humans are naturally inclined to (A)__________ intention and agency to objects and events, a survival mechanism evolved to make quick decisions and avoid danger, even at the cost of (B)__________ ambiguous situations.
questions.explanation: 인간은 생존을 위해 대상에 의도를 '부여(attribute)'하는 경향이 있으며, 이는 모호한 상황을 '과잉 해석(overinterpreting)'하는 결과를 낳더라도 빠른 결정을 내리게 돕는다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 취하다 / 과소평가하는
② 부여하다 / 과잉 해석하는
③ 배포하다 / 과장하는
④ 이해하다 / ~로부터 도망치는
⑤ 이해하다 / 다루는

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
options: ① Why would you be surprised when you hear a recording of your own voice?
② How many ways do we perceive our voices when we speak?
③ Does the vocal cords that vibrate when we speak affect our recognition of our own voices?
④ What is the specific range of vibration frequencies that directly stimulate our inner ears?
⑤ Why does your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than to others?
questions.explanation: 지문에서는 뼈를 통한 내부 경로로 '낮은 주파수(lower frequencies)'가 강조된다고만 언급하고 있을 뿐, 내이를 직접 자극하는 진동 주파수의 '구체적인 범위(specific range)'가 수치 등으로 제시되어 있지는 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 자신의 목소리 녹음을 들을 때 왜 놀라게 되는가?
② 우리가 말할 때 목소리를 인식하는 경로는 몇 가지인가?
③ 우리가 말할 때 진동하는 성대가 목소리 인식에 영향을 미치는가?
④ 내이를 직접 자극하는 진동 주파수의 구체적인 범위는 무엇인가?
⑤ 왜 자신의 목소리가 타인에게 들리는 것보다 자신에게 더 깊고 풍부하게 들리는가?

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are (A)___________, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. For instance In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engagingShakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, in contrast, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are (B)___________ doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is (C)___________ at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately clear and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 언어적 은유와 기술적 은유의 차이점을 설명하고 있습니다. (A) 언어적 은유는 청중이 인지적 노력을 기울여야 그 세계로 들어갈 수 있다는 점에서 '수동적(passive)'입니다. (B) 반면 기술적 은유는 디지털 도구 속에서 구현되어 '능동적으로(actively)' 무언가를 행하며 사용자의 인식을 바꿉니다. (C) 따라서 기술의 판매 포인트는 대개 그 유용성이 첫눈에 '명백한(obvious)' 것이어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 회의적인 - 비활동적으로 - 비논리적인
② 수동적인 - 능동적으로 - 명백한
③ 신뢰할 수 있는 - 활기차게 - 논리적인
④ 낙관적인 - 매력적으로 - 비이성적인
⑤ 긍정적인 - 자동적으로 - 이해할 수 있는

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 문장에서 어법상 어색한 곳이 있는 문장은?
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for being recognized our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity</u>. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then ⓑ<u>all we have to do is socially learn the right answers</u>. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. ⓒ<u>All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work</u>. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, ⓓ<u>we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation</u>. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but ⓔ<u>all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole</u>. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 문장에서 'for being recognized our limitations'는 어법상 틀립니다. 동명사 절 내에서 'our limitations'라는 목적어가 뒤따르고 있으므로, 수동형인 'being recognized'가 아닌 능동형인 'recognizing'을 써서 'for recognizing our limitations'가 되거나, 전치사 of를 사용하여 'for the recognition of our limitations' 등으로 고쳐야 합니다. 여기서는 허버트 사이먼이 우리의 한계를 인식한 것에 대해 상을 받은 것이므로 능동의 의미가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 질문에 가장 적절한 것은?Question: Which sentence best describes the main topic of the passage?
questions.passage: From an early age, we assign purpose to objects and events, preferring this reasoning to random chance. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because they don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. However, by attributing intention to animals and even objects, we are able to make fast decisions about the likely behaviour of that being. This was essential in our hunter-gatherer days to avoid being eaten by predators. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, as those are the mental processes which we understand. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents. This results in a perceptual system strongly biased towards anthropomorphism. Therefore, we tend to assume intention even where there is none. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you. By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has saved your life.*ambiguous: 모호한 **anthropomorphism: 의인화
options: ① Children assign purpose to objects based on their features.
② Animals were essential to the development of human perceptual abilities.
③ The tendency to assign purpose to objects and events is developed early in life.
④ Stewart Guthrie's theories explain why people see objects as having human characteristics.
⑤ Human beings evolved to perceive intention and purpose in ambiguous objects and situations.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 생존을 위해 주변의 모호한 대상이나 사건에 의도와 목적을 부여(의인화)하려는 경향을 진화적으로 갖게 되었음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '인간은 모호한 대상과 상황에서 의도와 목적을 지각하도록 진화했다'는 ⑤번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 아이들은 특징에 기초하여 사물에 목적을 부여한다.
② 동물들은 인간의 지각 능력 발달에 필수적이었다.
③ 사물과 사건에 목적을 부여하는 경향은 어린 시절에 발달한다.
④ Stewart Guthrie의 이론은 왜 사람들이 사물을 인간적 특성을 가진 것으로 보는지 설명한다.
⑤ 인간은 모호한 사물과 상황에서 의도와 목적을 지각하도록 진화했다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly ⓐ<u>eliminate</u> the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel ⓑ<u>isolated</u> from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may ⓒ<u>stop</u> being a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an ⓓ<u>optimistic</u> pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of ⓔ<u>horror</u>. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.explanation: 기후 변화가 아직 인간 삶의 주변적 특징일 때는 '이야기'로서 즐거움을 줄 수 있지만, 그 즐거움이 공포의 형태를 띠기도 한다고 언급되어 있습니다. 기후 재난을 다루는 장르가 주는 즐거움은 낙관적인(optimistic) 즐거움이라기보다, 재난 영화가 주는 짜릿한 전율이나 미적 쾌감에 가깝습니다. 특히 문맥상 뒤이어 나오는 '공포(horror)의 형태'와 어울리는 단어는 '미적(aesthetic)' 또는 '대리적인' 즐거움이어야 하며, 실제 재앙이 닥치기 전까지 누리는 역설적인 즐거움을 뜻하므로 'optimistic'은 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally elective. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an abundant resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to address it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly highlights have-and-have-not inequities, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
options: ① the inevitability of global water scarcity
② the political and preventable nature of the water crisis
③ the technological solutions to water waste
④ the role of urbanization in environmental destruction
⑤ the global disparity in access to clean water and sanitation
questions.explanation: 이 글은 오늘날의 물 위기가 피할 수 없는 것이 아니라 정치적인 문제이며, 충분히 고칠 수 있는 능력 안에 있음에도 불구하고 정부의 무관심과 인프라 부족 등으로 발생하고 있음을 지적하고 있습니다. 즉, 물 위기의 정치적이고 예방 가능한 성격에 대해 말하고 있으므로 2번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 전 세계적 물 부족의 불가피성
② 물 위기의 정치적이고 예방 가능한 성격
③ 물 낭비에 대한 기술적 해결책
④ 환경 파괴에 있어서 도시화의 역할
⑤ 깨끗한 물과 위생 시설 접근에 대한 세계적인 불평등

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to _______________, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 인간은 집단 내에서 자신의 평판을 관리하도록 진화해 왔으며, 자부심이나 수치심 같은 감정들은 공동체가 우리를 가치 있게 여기도록 행동하게 만듭니다. 이러한 동기 부여는 마치 내면에서 우러나오는 것처럼 느껴져야 설득력이 있는데, 만약 이것이 외부의 타인들에 의한 압력에 반응하는 것임을 의식적으로 깨닫게 된다면 그 행동이 가식적이거나 냉소적으로 보일 수 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 집단적 평판 관리와 관련된 '사회적 압력'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 신체적 욕구
② 타고난 본능
③ 사회적 압력
④ 환경적 요인
⑤ 유전적 성향

questions.question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be ______________ into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 문어는 자신의 색상과 패턴을 바꾸어 다른 생물처럼 보이게 만드는 능력을 가지고 있습니다. 본문에서 가자미(flounder)로 오해받을 만큼 완벽하게 변장한 사례를 설명하고 있으며, 바다뱀(sea snakes)으로 '변신' 혹은 '변형'하는 모습에 대한 설명이 이어지고 있으므로 ③번 'transforming'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 먹이를 먹는 것
② 기대하는 것
③ 변신하는 것
④ 공존하는 것
⑤ 인식하는 것

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that ______________________________________________________. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
options: ① relies entirely on brain functions for its structure and stability.
② experiences difficulty adapting to rapid changes in the environment.
③ has disconnected from its sense of identity and the purpose of existence.
④ struggles to maintain a balance between emotional and logical thinking.
⑤ becomes overly focused on external validation and neglects intrinsic motivation.
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 우울증이 뇌 물질의 불균형 때문에 생기는 것이 아니라, 오히려 우울증이 뇌 물질의 불균형을 초래하는 결과이며, 그 근본 원인은 의식의 왜곡에 있다는 것입니다. 우울증은 의식의 질병으로서 나타나는데, 빈칸에는 이러한 의식의 상태를 설명하는 말이 들어가야 합니다. 의식이 '정체성이나 존재의 목적과의 연결이 끊어진(disconnected from its sense of identity and the purpose of existence)' 상태일 때 그것이 우울증으로 나타난다는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다. 따라서 정답은 ③번입니다.
options_translation: ① 구조와 안정성을 위해 전적으로 뇌 기능에 의존한다.
② 환경의 급격한 변화에 적응하는 데 어려움을 겪는다.
③ 정체성 및 존재 목적에 대한 감각과 단절되었다.
④ 감정적인 사고와 논리적인 사고 사이의 균형을 유지하려고 고군분투한다.
⑤ 외부의 확인에 과도하게 집중하고 내면의 동기를 무시하게 된다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to _____________________________________________.
options: ① quick decisions based on little thought
② initial impressions without much evidence
③ unconscious and emotional first reactions
④ hasty judgments with insufficient reasoning
⑤ conscious and methodical thought processes
questions.explanation: 지문은 신중한 숙고나 상세한 논의보다 직관적이고 자동적인 첫인상이 더 정확할 때가 많다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 글의 마지막 문장은 상대적으로 무의식적인 '첫 번째 추측'이 무엇보다 우월한 성과를 보이는지를 설명하고 있으므로, 대조되는 개념인 '의식적이고 체계적인 사고 과정'이 빈칸에 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 생각이 거의 없는 빠른 결정
② 많은 증거가 없는 초기 인상
③ 무의식적이고 감정적인 첫 반응
④ 불충분한 추론을 동반한 성급한 판단
⑤ 의식적이고 체계적인 사고 과정

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고, (A)~(D) 학생이 <보기>와 같이 대화하였다. 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 내용을 말한 학생들을 알맞게 고른 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
vocabulary_box: (A) I think the passage says punishing a child is bad. When parents punish a child, the child gets sad and stops doing bad things. So, punishment always works, and parents should do it more. That is what I learned from this passage.
(B) I think the mother should just ignore Hugh. If she doesn't look at him when he hits, he will stop. The passage says ignoring is the best way to fix bad behavior. That is how I understand it.
(C) The passage says punishment can make the child want more attention. For example, Hugh hits his brother because he wants his mom to notice him. Punishment can make things worse sometimes.

(D) I think the mother should scold Hugh when he hits his brother. A strong punishment will stop him. If the punishment is strong enough, Hugh will be afraid to hit again. That is the best way to teach him.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 '속임수 처벌'은 아이가 관심을 받기 위해 나쁜 행동을 지속하게 만들 수 있으므로 처벌이 항상 효과적인 것은 아닙니다(A 틀림). 또한 지문은 무시하기가 최선이라고 말하는 것이 아니라 긍정적인 행동에 보상을 주는 전략을 제안하고 있습니다(B 틀림). 강력한 처벌이 아이를 멈추게 할 것이라는 주장(D)은 지문의 핵심인 '속임수 처벌'의 위험성과 대안적 보상 전략에 위배됩니다. 반면 (C)는 지문의 내용을 정확히 이해하고 있습니다. 따라서 일치하지 않는 말을 한 학생은 (A), (B), (D)입니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race - their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't psychologically suffer much. In fact, ultra-marathon runners - those people who are crazy enough to push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50-100km or more over many hours, talk about making friends with their pain. When a patient has paid for some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it, the patient calls that good pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.
options: ① 우리가 얼마나 고통받는지는 우리가 고통을 우리의 마음에서 어떻게 구성하는지와 관련된다.
② 1500미터 달리기 선수가 경주에서 이기기 위해 스스로를 극심한 고통으로 밀어붙일 때, 그들은 정신적으로 많이 고통받지 않는다.
③ 인간 인내력의 정상적 경계를 넘어서 스스로를 밀어붙일 만큼 충분히 열정적인 사람들은 그들의 고통과 친구가 되는 것에 대해 이야기한다.
④ 환자가 특정 형태의 등 통증 치료에 돈을 지불했고 의사가 그것을 풀어 주기 위해 환자 등의 아픈 부분을 깊게 눌렀을 때, 환자는 극심한 통증으로 고통받는다.
⑤ 의사가 환자의 아픈 조직을 직접적으로 누르고 있어도, 만약 환자가 이러한 종류의 압박 치료법이 가치가 있을 것이라고 믿는다면, 환자는 그것을 좋은 아픔이라고 부른다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 부분에 따르면, 환자가 치료의 가치를 믿는다면 의사가 아픈 부위를 깊게 눌러도 그것을 '극심한 통증으로 고통받는 것'이 아니라 '좋은 통증(good pain)'이라고 부른다고 설명되어 있습니다. 따라서 ④번은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 27. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 알맞은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different.
ordered_passages: (A) Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions.
(B) It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.'

(C) In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 심리학은 일반적인 통념과 다르다고 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 심리학이 무엇인지 정의하며 핵심 단어인 '과학'을 제시합니다. (A)에서는 그 과학적 성격의 구체적 설명으로 의견이나 소문이 아닌 '증거'를 찾는다는 내용을 서술합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 '이러한 증거 기반 접근법에 더하여(In addition to this evidence-based approach)'라고 (A)의 내용을 받으며 심리학이 다루는 범위를 확장하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥상 적절한 것끼리 알맞게 짝지은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, (A)[the number of / a number of] possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result (B)[in / from] the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly (C)[similar / different].*embryo: 배아 **physiological: 생리적인
options: ① the number of / from / similar
② the number of / in / similar
③ the number of / in / different
④ a number of / in / similar
⑤ a number of / from / different
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤에 'is enormous'라는 단수 동사가 오므로 '분자들 사이의 상호작용의 수'를 뜻하는 'the number of'가 적절합니다. (a number of는 '많은'의 뜻으로 복수 취급).(B) 인간 배아의 발달'로부터' 발생하는 결과물(조직과 신체 형태)을 설명하고 있으므로 원인을 나타내는 전치사 'from'이 적절합니다 (result in은 결과를 초래하다, result from은 ~로부터 기인하다).(C) 앞선 내용에서 유기체가 정해진 소수의 상태 사이에서만 전환될 수 있다는 '운하화(canalization)'를 설명했습니다. 따라서 질병의 원인은 많더라도 생리적/증상적 수준에서 나타나는 양상은 '유사하다(similar)'는 결론이 문맥상 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 수 / ~로부터 / 유사한
② 수 / ~을 초래하다 / 유사한
③ 수 / ~을 초래하다 / 다른
④ 많은 / ~을 초래하다 / 유사한
⑤ 많은 / ~로부터 / 다른

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The adolescent brain is not fully developed until its early twenties. This means the way the adolescents' decision-making circuits integrate and process information may put them at a disadvantage. One of their brain regions that matures later is the prefrontal cortex, which is the control center, tasked with thinking ahead and evaluating consequences. It is the area of the brain responsible for preventing you from sending off an initial angry text and modifying it with kinder words. On the other hand, the limbic system matures earlier, playing a central role in processing emotional responses. Because of its earlier development, it is more likely to influence decision-making. Decision-making in the adolescent brain is led by emotional factors more than the perception of consequences. Due to these differences, there is an imbalance between feeling-based decision-making ruled by the more mature limbic system and logical-based decision-making by the not-yet-mature prefrontal cortex. This may explain why some teens are more likely to make bad decisions.
questions.summary_sentence: Adolescents are more likely to make (A)__________ decisions because of the (B)__________ in brain development in adolescence.
questions.explanation: 청소년의 뇌는 전두엽(논리적 사고, 결과 예측)보다 변연계(감정 처리)가 더 일찍 발달합니다. 이러한 뇌 발달의 불균형(imbalance/unevenness)으로 인해 청소년들은 결과에 대한 고려보다 감정적인 요인에 의해 잘못된(mistaken/bad) 결정을 내릴 가능성이 높습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 잘못된 결정, (B)에는 발달의 불균형이나 고르지 않음을 의미하는 단어가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 논리적인 ... 성숙
② 정직한 ... 불균형
③ 잘못된 ... 완료
④ 잘못된 ... 고르지 않음
⑤ 적합한 ... 미완성

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson suggests that we tend to understand the world by breaking the framework of old ideas. Take platypuses. We might zoom in so closely to their fur that each hair appears different. We might also zoom out to the extent where it appears as a single, uniform object. We might take the platypus as an individual, or we might treat it as part of a larger unit such as a species or an ecosystem. It's possible to move between many of these perspectives, although we may need some additional tools and skills to zoom in on individual pieces of hair or zoom out to entire ecosystems. Crucially, however, we can only take up one perspective at a time. We can pay attention to the varied behavior of individual animals, look at what unites them into a single species, or look at them as part of bigger ecological patterns. Every possible perspective involves emphasizing certain aspects and ignoring others.
options: ① A View of the World: See It Up Close or from a Distance?
② Why Humans Are Interested in Animals' Behaviors
③ How Anthropologists Classify the World
④ The Role of Platypuses in Ecosystems
⑤ How Useful is Platypus' Fur?
questions.explanation: 이 글은 세상(또는 대상)을 바라볼 때 미세하게 관찰하거나(zoom in) 거시적으로 보는(zoom out) 등 다양한 관점이 존재하지만, 한 번에 하나의 관점만 취할 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 세상을 가까이서 볼지 멀리서 볼지에 대한 관점의 선택을 다룬 1번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 세상에 대한 관점: 가까이서 볼 것인가 멀리서 볼 것인가?
② 왜 인간은 동물의 행동에 관심을 갖는가?
③ 인류학자들이 세상을 분류하는 방법
④ 생태계에서 오리너구리의 역할
⑤ 오리너구리의 털은 얼마나 유용한가?

questions.question: 3. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When writing a novel, research for information needs to be done. The thing is that some kinds of fiction demand a higher level of detail: crime fiction, for example, or scientific thrillers. The information is never hard to find; one website for authors even organizes trips to police stations, so that crime writers can get it right. But remember that you will drive your readers to boredom if you think that you need to pack everything you discover into your work. The details that matter are those that ____________________________________. The crucial thing is telling a story, finding the characters, the tension, and the conflict - not the train timetable or the building blueprint. Readers are drawn to the characters' journeys, the emotions they experience, and the challenges that they face, rather than an exhaustive list of every information discovered along the route.
options: ① can make the storyline overly complicated
② illuminate the essence of human experience
③ lend a sense of realism to specific plot points
④ provide a level of background context to scenes
⑤ add minor elements without dominating the story
questions.explanation: 소설 작가가 조사를 통해 얻은 방대한 정보 중 모든 것을 다 담으려 하면 독자들이 지루해집니다. 중요한 것은 단순한 정보 나열이 아니라 인물, 긴장감, 갈등과 같은 '이야기'입니다. 따라서 중요한 세부 사항은 인간 경험의 본질을 밝혀주는(illuminate the essence of human experience) 것들이어야 한다는 2번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 줄거리를 지나치게 복잡하게 만들 수 있는
② 인간 경험의 본질을 밝혀주는
③ 특정 줄거리 지점에 사실감을 부여하는
④ 장면에 어느 정도의 배경 맥락을 제공하는
⑤ 이야기를 지배하지 않으면서 소소한 요소를 추가하는

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
options: ① 나이가 어릴수록 익숙한 것에 더 쉽게 싫증을 내는 경향이 있다.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 아이들, 대학생, 일반 성인 모두가 익숙한 것에 싫증을 느낀다는 예시를 들고 있지만, 나이가 어릴수록 더 쉽게 싫증을 낸다는 비교나 경향성에 대한 언급은 없습니다. 지문은 인간이 보편적으로 지루함을 느끼는 이유를 신경 세포의 작용과 생존 가치 관점에서 설명하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 내용가 일치하지 안는 거슨?
questions.passage: Nearly everything has to go through your mouth to get to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and prevent it from harm - with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. From the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and a reflection of what is happening in other parts of the body. Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease that affects the entire body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, posing serious health risks.
options: ① Almost everything, including food, air, and viruses, must pass through your mouth before reaching the rest of your body.
② A healthy mouth may protect your body from damage and help it obtain what it needs.
③ Gums and teeth in good health can help keep dangerous bacteria out of your blood.
④ What occurs in the mouth usually represents a small glimpse of broader issues and mirrors conditions present in other areas of the body.
⑤ Microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the body through the air and contribute to the development of various cancers.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구강 건강이 전신 건강에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 읈음다. 중요한 것은 구강 내의 미생물이 '혈류(bloodstream)'를 통해 몸의 다른 부위로 이동한다고 했지, '갱기(air)'를 통해 이동한다거나 '암(cancers)'을 유발한다는 구체적인 언급은 없습니다.
options_translation: ① 음식, 갱기, 바이러스를 포함하여 거의 모든 것이 신체의 나머지 부분에 댄늬하기 전에 입을 통과해야 한다.
② 건강한 구강은 신체를 섐상으로부터 밴호하고 필요한 것을 얻도록 도와줄 수 읈다.
③ 건강한 잇몸과 치아눤 위험한 박테리아가 혈액으로 들어오지 먻하게 도와줄 수 읈다.
④ 입안에서 발생하눠 일은 밴통 더 광범위한 문제의 작은 일부를 나타내며 신체의 다른 부위에서 일어나고 읈눠 상태를 반영한다.
⑤ 건강하지 먻한 구강 내의 미생물은 갱기를 통해 신체로 들어가 다양한 암의 발생에 기여할 수 읈다.

questions.question: 6. 제시된 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In statistics, the law of large numbers describes a situation where having more data is better for making predictions.
ordered_passages: (A) Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to balance individual losses.

(B) According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to match the true state of the world. For instance, on your first encounter with the game of roulette, you may have beginner's luck after betting on 7.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 통계학의 '대섘의 법칙(the law of large numbers)'을 소개합니다. (B)의 'According to it'이 제시문의 법칙을 받아서 구체적인 원리(실험 횟수가 많을수록 실제 상태와 일츘함)를 설명하고 칔시노 게임을 예로 들얽니다. (A)눤 'Similarly'를 통해 칔시노와 마찬가지로 법칙을 활용하눠 볽험 산업을 소개하며 결론을 맺습니다. 단, 선택지에 (C)가 없고 (A), (B)만 있으므로 (B)-(A) 순서가 적절합니다. (원문에는 (C)가 있으나 이 문제는 판단 가눕한 일부만 추출됨)

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants. Not only were their athletic talents superior, the Cubans appeared even stronger from just the colour of their uniforms. A game would not even start and the opposing team would already be scared. A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time. The country that ruled international baseball for decades has not been on top since that uniform change. Traditions are important for a team; while a team brand or image can adjust to keep up with present times, if it abandons or neglects its roots, negative effects can surface.
questions.summary_sentence: From 1940 to 2000, Cuba held dominance in baseball on the world stage, but it faded after (A)___________ their iconic red uniforms that once (B)___________ their opponents.
questions.explanation: 쿠바 야구팀은 상징적인 붉은 유니폼을 입었을 때 세계를 제패했으나, 그 유니폼 스타일을 바꾼(discarding) 후 쇠퇴하였으며, 그 유니폼은 과거 상대 팀들을 겁먹게(frightened) 만드는 효과가 있었다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 버리는 것 --- 겁나게 했던
② 포기하는 것 --- 위로했던
③ 보존하는 것 --- 혼란스럽게 했던
④ 받아들이는 것 --- 협박했던
⑤ 포기하는 것 --- 안심시켰던

questions.question: 9. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth, simply running the race ⓐ<u>that</u> is predetermined for them. They do well enough in school to keep ⓑ<u>advancing</u>. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey (A)[unfolds beyond / ceases after] college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that ⓒ<u>laid out</u> for them and now lack a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that is when the journey actually begins, ⓓ<u>gaining</u> new meaning and depth. When school is finished, your growth becomes (B)[self-directed / disruptive]. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to (C)[pursue / overlook] it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career are likely to stop ⓔ<u>progressing</u> as a result.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 'the life that ⓒlaid out for them'은 '그들을 위해 설계된 삶'이라는 수동의 의미가 되어야 하므로, 과거분사인 laid out 앞에 be동사가 있거나 'that was laid out' 혹은 'laid out' (분사구문) 형태가 되어야 합니다. 여기서는 주격 관계대명사 that 뒤에서 동사 역할을 하려면 was laid out으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth, simply running the race ⓐ<u>that</u> is predetermined for them. They do well enough in school to keep ⓑ<u>advancing</u>. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey (A)[unfolds beyond / ceases after] college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that ⓒ<u>laid out</u> for them and now lack a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that is when the journey actually begins, ⓓ<u>gaining</u> new meaning and depth. When school is finished, your growth becomes (B)[self-directed / disruptive]. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to (C)[pursue / overlook] it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career are likely to stop ⓔ<u>progressing</u> as a result.
questions.explanation: (A) 많은 사람들이 대학 이후에는 배움의 여정이 끝난다고(ceases after) 생각하고 행동한다는 문맥이 적절합니다.(B) 학교가 끝난 후 성장은 스스로 주도해야 하는(self-directed) 것이 됩니다.(C) 건강한 식습관처럼 성장을 위해 시간과 에너지를 쏟으며 추구해야(pursue) 합니다.
options_translation: ① ~너머로 펼쳐지다 --- 자기 주도적인 --- 간과하다
② ~너머로 펼쳐지다 --- 파괴적인 --- 간과하다
③ ~후에 중단되다 --- 자기 주도적인 --- 추구하다
④ ~후에 중단되다 --- 자기 주도적인 --- 간과하다
⑤ ~후에 중단되다 --- 파괴적인 --- 추구하다

questions.question: 11. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 11월 32번]
questions.passage: Participants in a study ⓐ<u>were</u> asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" (A) Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while ⓑ<u>the other</u> half weren't allowed to do so. (B) Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" (C) These questions were unrelated to the ones ⓒ<u>asking</u> during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. (D) You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how ⓓ<u>well</u> they could answer the new questions. (E) The study suggests that having access to unrelated information ⓔ<u>was</u> enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
questions.insertion_sentence: But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 앞서 언급된 '양쪽 집단 모두 새로운 질문에 대해 똑같이 확신하거나 확신하지 못할 것이라고 생각할 것이다'라는 일반적 예상(D)에 반하는 실험 결과를 나타냅니다. 따라서 역접의 접속사 But으로 시작하며 인터넷을 사용했던 사람들이 자신들을 더 똑똑하다고 평가했다는 결과가 나오는 (E) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것은? [23년 11월 32번]
questions.passage: Participants in a study ⓐ<u>were</u> asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" (A) Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while ⓑ<u>the other</u> half weren't allowed to do so. (B) Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" (C) These questions were unrelated to the ones ⓒ<u>asking</u> during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. (D) You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how ⓓ<u>well</u> they could answer the new questions. (E) The study suggests that having access to unrelated information ⓔ<u>was</u> enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 수식하는 'the ones'는 질문들(questions)을 가리키며, 질문은 첫 번째 단계에서 '질문되는' 것이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 'asked'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying ⓐ<u>them</u> to culture.
ordered_passages: (B) For example, we do not expect the cultural transmission ⓑ<u>to follow</u> the rules of genetic transmission strictly. If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily ⓒ<u>equally</u> likely to acquire the mother's or father's form of that trait.

(C) Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers; thus, the frequency of a cultural trait in the population is relevant beyond just the probability ⓓ<u>that</u> an individual's parents had that trait.

(D) Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually likened to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection. However, these approaches had to ⓔ<u>modify</u> to account for the differences between genetic and cultural transmission.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 문화 진화 모델이 유전자와 문화를 연결했다는 도입 후, (D)에서 이러한 문화와 유전적 과정의 유사성을 언급하면서도 두 전송 방식 간의 차이를 설명하기 위해 모델이 수정되어야 했음을 밝힙니다. 이어지는 (B)에서는 그 구체적인 예시로 문화적 전송이 유전적 전송의 규칙을 엄격히 따르지 않는다는 점을 설명하고, (C)에서는 부모 외의 타인으로부터도 문화적 특성을 습득할 수 있다는 추가적인 차이점을 'Further'를 사용하여 설명하는 것이 가장 자연스러운 흐름입니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying ⓐ<u>them</u> to culture.(B) For example, we do not expect the cultural transmission ⓑ<u>to follow</u> the rules of genetic transmission strictly. If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily ⓒ<u>equally</u> likely to acquire the mother's or father's form of that trait.(C) Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers; thus, the frequency of a cultural trait in the population is relevant beyond just the probability ⓓ<u>that</u> an individual's parents had that trait.(D) Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually likened to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection. However, these approaches had to ⓔ<u>modify</u> to account for the differences between genetic and cultural transmission.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장의 주어인 'these approaches(이러한 접근법들)'는 스스로를 수정하는 행위의 주체가 아니라, 연구자들에 의해 수정되는 대상입니다. 따라서 수동의 의미를 나타내는 'be modified'로 고쳐 써야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. ⓐThe reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. ⓑSome powerful people break the order of organ donation and take control of the organ first. ⓒBut it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. ⓓThey certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. ⓔAs a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
options: ① 치료불가한 환자의 안락사 선택권을 보장해야 한다.
② 장기를 불법적으로 사고파는 행위를 엄격히 규제해야 한다.
③ 뇌사판정에 더 많은 의사들이 참여하여 대중의 의심을 해소해야 한다.
④ 장기 기증 여부와 관계없이, 사망 진단 기준은 똑같이 적용되어야 한다.
⑤ 장기 기증의 공익성을 홍보하여 많은 사람들이 참여하도록 해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장인 'criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended'가 이 글의 핵심 주장입니다. 즉, 장기 기증 여부와 상관없이 일관성 있게 동일한 사망 진단 기준이 적용되어야 한다는 내용이므로 ④번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 22. 윗글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. ⓐThe reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. ⓑSome powerful people break the order of organ donation and take control of the organ first. ⓒBut it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. ⓓThey certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. ⓔAs a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
questions.explanation: 전체 지문은 장기 기증을 위한 뇌사 판정 기준이 대중의 불신 때문에 더 엄격해졌지만, 일관성 차원에서 모든 사망 진단 기준은 동일해야 한다는 주장을 담고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓑ는 권력자들이 장기 기증 순서를 무시하고 장기를 선점한다는 내용으로, 사망 판정 기준의 엄격함이나 일관성이라는 전체 주제와 거리가 멉니다.

questions.question: 23. [23년 11월 38번] 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest ⓐ<u>loss</u> of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on a(n) ⓑ<u>tremendous</u> scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a(n) ⓒ<u>tiny</u> number of new super-productive ones. (A)________________________, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more ⓓ<u>identical</u> crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a(n) ⓔ<u>unlimited</u> selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
options: ① The plan worked exceptionally well
② Farmers stopped producing rice and wheat
③ The strategy was not welcomed by the people
④ More and more people were dying of starvation
⑤ The strategy had no effect on the environment
questions.explanation: 빈칸 뒤의 내용에서 곡물 생산량이 3배로 늘고 인구가 2배 이상 증가했다는 결과가 나오므로, 빈칸 (A)에는 그 계획이 매우 잘 작동했다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그 계획은 대단히 잘 작동했다
② 농부들은 쌀과 밀 생산을 중단했다
③ 그 전략은 사람들에게 환영받지 못했다
④ 점점 더 많은 사람들이 굶주림으로 죽어갔다
⑤ 그 전략은 환경에 아무런 영향을 미치지 않았다

questions.question: 24. [23년 11월 38번] 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest ⓐ<u>loss</u> of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on a(n) ⓑ<u>tremendous</u> scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a(n) ⓒ<u>tiny</u> number of new super-productive ones. (A)________________________, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more ⓓ<u>identical</u> crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a(n) ⓔ<u>unlimited</u> selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 소수의 슈퍼 생산 품종이 수천 개의 전통 품종을 대체하여 식량 다양성이 감소했다는 내용이므로, 글로벌 식량 시스템이 '무제한적인(unlimited)' 선택에 의존하는 것이 아니라 '제한적인(limited)' 또는 '좁은(narrow)' 선택에 의존하여 위험에 처하게 된다는 내용이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 대화의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ가 의미하는 것으로 옳지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Life is a series of ⓐ<u>choice</u>s. In order to make the best decisions you can in life, you should consider issues from many different points of view. One way to do this is to come up with several options and think about any possible ⓑ<u>negative</u> consequences they may have. After doing this, you will feel better because you know that you have done everything to make a ⓒ<u>careful</u> decision. It can also be helpful to seek out ⓓ<u>advice</u> from other people.
