Do you know anyone who has made a similar decision in their own life? If so, ⓔ<u>ask</u> them how they made their decision and if they think they did the right thing.
questions.explanation: careful은 '신중한', '조심스러운'이라는 뜻입니다. '급박한'은 urgent 등의 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. (A) This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. (B) However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. (C) The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. (D) The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. (E) Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.insertion_sentence: Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 소셜 미디어 유명인들이 전통적인 엘리트 유명인의 기술(연기, 노래 등)이 없다는 이유로 비판받는다는 내용입니다. (A) 뒤의 'This criticism(이러한 비판)'이 바로 이 내용을 가리키므로 주어진 문장은 (A) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Higher education has transitioned from an elite to a mass system globally, with a significant increase in participation rates after World War II in Europe and the USA. (A) Between 2000 and 2014, global participation rates almost doubled from 19% to 34% among the school-leaving age demographic (18-23 years old). (B) This expansion has brought a wider range of educational institutions and a more diverse student population. (C) The shift towards a mass higher education system is driven by the need to develop a specialized workforce for the economy. (D) In theory? expanding higher education to create a skilled workforce should reduce the reliance on examinations and encourage lifelong learning through assessment for learning and developmental feedback. (E) In contrast, elite systems of the past allowed for close student-teacher relationships and formative feedback shaping students' skills and characters.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the reality of mass higher education calls for efficient assessment methods like exams and multiple-choice quizzes, often resulting in impersonal feedback and a focus on grades over feedbacks.
questions.explanation: 지문은 고등교육의 대중화 현상을 설명합니다. (D) 문장은 이론적으로는 대중 교육이 시험 의존도를 낮추어야 한다고 말합니다. 주어진 문장은 'However'로 시작하며 대중 교육의 현실은 효율적인 시험 방식(객관식 등)을 요구하여 비인격적 피드백을 초래한다고 반박합니다. 이어지는 (E)에서 과거의 엘리트 시스템과 대조하고 있으므로 (E) 앞이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 29번]
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways.
ordered_passages: (A) Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the message of his works is not immediately evident and requires the audience to think about it.

(B) Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the viewer must choose to actively enter the world suggested by metaphor. The audience is unlikely understand the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," unless they exert cognitive effort and engage with Shakespeare's text.

(C) Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and frequently imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that actively perform tasks, forcing a user's meaning horizon to shift. Technological producers cannot generally afford to have their potential audience think how the metaphor works; instead the selling point is that the technology's utility is clear at first glance.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 디지털 은유와 언어적 은유의 차이점을 화두로 던집니다. (B)에서 언어적 은유의 수동성과 그 예로 셰익스피어를 언급하며 논의를 시작합니다. (C)에서 'on the other hand'를 사용하여 언어적 은유와 대조되는 기술적 은유의 능동성(강요성)과 명확한 유용성을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 다시 'on the other hand'를 사용하여 생각할 여지를 주는 셰익스피어(언어적 은유의 속성)가 사랑받는 이유를 기술적 은유와 대조하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적인 흐름입니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 밑줄 친 부분이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 33번]
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was <u>a black cat</u>, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① a lense though which we view reality
② a particular form imposed by human senses
③ a perceived reality that subjects to human conventions
④ an existence that is absolute, self-sufficient or objective
⑤ an abstract entity that is physically impossible to make manifest
questions.explanation: 이 글에서 '검은 고양이'는 존재하지 않는 '본질(essence)'을 찾으려는 헛된 시도를 비유합니다. 특히 빛의 매질로 여겨졌으나 실재하지 않았던 '에테르(ether)'를 예로 들어, 물리학자들이 존재하지 않는 대상을 찾기 위해 이론을 세우고 실험했던 상황을 설명합니다. 따라서 'a black cat'은 물리적으로 실체를 드러내는 것이 불가능한 추상적인 존재를 의미합니다.
options_translation: 우리가 현실을 바라보는 렌즈
인간의 감각에 의해 부여된 특정한 형태
인간의 관습에 종속되는 인지된 현실
절대적이고 자급자족적이며 객관적인 존재
물리적으로 나타내는 것이 불가능한 추상적인 실체

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political ─ which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix ─ and, therefore, functionally elective. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an abundant resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to address it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly highlights have-and-have-not inequities, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
options: ① Water Challenges for Rural Areas
② Water Crisis Caused by Mismanagement
③ Politicians' Excessive Consumption of Water
④ A Problem of Drought and Weather Patterns
⑤ The Selective Scarcity of Sanitation Facilities
questions.explanation: 이 글은 오늘날의 물 위기가 피할 수 없는 자연 현상이 아니라 정부의 태만, 열악한 인프라, 부주의한 도시화 등 관리의 부재(정치적 문제)로 인해 발생한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 '잘못된 관리로 인한 물 위기'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 농촌 지역의 물 문제
② 잘못된 관리로 인한 물 위기
③ 정치인들의 과도한 물 소비
④ 가뭄과 기상 패턴의 문제
⑤ 위생 시설의 선택적 부족

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
options: ① How a Recording Distorts Voices
③ Bone Is a Second Auditory Sense Organ!
④ Two Ways That Vocal Cords Produce Voices
⑤ Comparison of Hearing Sensitivity through Two Different Pathways
questions.explanation: 자신의 녹음된 목소리가 낯설게 들리는 이유는 목소리를 인지하는 두 가지 경로 때문입니다. 외부 공기를 통한 일반적 경로와 뼈의 진동을 통해 내이로 전달되는 경로가 있는데, 후자가 낮은 주파수를 강조하여 자신의 목소리를 더 깊게 들리게 합니다. 따라서 뼈가 제2의 청각 기관 역할을 한다는 비유적 표현인 ③번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 녹음이 목소리를 왜곡하는 방식
② 골전도가 청력을 방해한다
③ 뼈는 제2의 청각 기관이다!
④ 성대가 목소리를 내는 두 가지 방법
⑤ 두 가지 다른 경로를 통한 청각 민감도 비교

questions.question: 13. 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons ⓐ<u>who have resolved the problem which we struggle</u>. This is ⓑ<u>one of the great powers of self-help groups</u>. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. ⓒ<u>Those who are in a higher vibration are</u> free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. ⓓ<u>Merely to be in their presence is</u> beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and ⓔ<u>relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓐ에서 'struggle'은 자동사로 주로 쓰여 '~와 싸우다/고군분투하다'라고 할 때 전치사 'with'가 필요합니다. 여기서는 'the problem'을 수식하는 관계대명사 절이므로 'which we struggle with' 또는 'with which we struggle'로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Onscreen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre ─ indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant ─ in time or in place ─ we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.summary_sentence: Climate fiction may (A)___________ as real-world climate impacts become too (B)___________ to fictionalize.
questions.explanation: 지문은 기후 변화가 인류의 삶에서 주변적인 특징일 때는 허구로 다룰 수 있지만, 기후 변화가 너무 거대하고 명백해져서 일상에서 직접 목격하게 되면 기후 소설이라는 장르가 사라질 것이라고 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 사라지다(vanish), (B)에는 분명한(evident)이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사라지다 - 가벼운
② 흩어지다 - 모호한
③ 사라지다 - 분명한
④ 만연하다 - 구체적인
⑤ 다시 떠오르다 - 명백한

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and effortlessly divide what we perceive into colors, shapes, and ideas that we have studied. We ⓐ<u>reinterpret</u> what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a ⓑ<u>useful</u> trait. It is a more efficient method of information storage ─ a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who are unable to do this and remember everything in complete ⓒ<u>clarity</u> struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as ⓓ<u>abstract</u> ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely ⓔ<u>upheld</u> the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: 지문은 기억이 실제 그대로가 아니라 추상적 재구성을 통해 저장된다는 점을 설명하며, 이는 목격자 증언의 신뢰성이 떨어짐을 시사합니다. 따라서 'Seeing is not believing(보는 것이 믿는 것이 아니다)'이라는 결론과 어울리려면, 목격자 증언의 법적 우위(legal primacy)를 '지지했다(upheld)'가 아니라 '약화시켰다(undermined)'와 같은 단어가 와야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas have a ⓐ<u>thriving</u> ecosystem while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is ⓑ<u>obscure</u> that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data ⓒ<u>representing</u> that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to ⓓ<u>disrupt</u> the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or ⓔ<u>displaced</u> populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: 찬물이 따뜻한 물보다 용존 산소를 더 많이 함유한다는 것은 이미 확립된 사실이며, 지구 온난화로 수온이 올라가면 용존 산소량이 줄어드는 것은 '모호한(obscure)' 것이 아니라 '분명한(obvious/certain)' 사실입니다. 따라서 ⓑ의 obscure는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is ⓐ<u>renouncing</u> it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to ⓑ<u>designated</u> lanes for bikes. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of ⓒ<u>animosity</u>. But they are actually a(n) ⓓ<u>evitable</u> part of making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors ⓔ<u>permits</u> them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 배달 차량은 도시를 더 친환경적으로 만드는 데 있어 '피할 수 없는(inevitable)' 혹은 '필수적인(essential)' 부분입니다. 뒤에 이어지는 문장에서 짐을 꽉 채운 배달 트럭이 여러 대의 하이브리드 차량보다 훨씬 효율적이라고 설명하고 있기 때문입니다. 따라서 '피할 수 있는'이라는 뜻의 evitable은 문맥상 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글을 읽고 추론한 내용으로 옳은 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push ─ essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
options: ① Discovering how to efficiently analyze the human brain, Herbert Simon won the Novel Prize.
② We don't need to understand how things like computers or toilets work because we are discouraged from learning how to use them.
③ By transmitting information through artificial intelligence, society solves complex problems.
④ Everyone is directly involved in the giant calculation, holding more information than we have mental capacity for.
⑤ Individuals make modest computations that add up to larger solutions.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 인간의 인지적 한계 때문에 정보를 분산하여 처리하며, 개개인은 거대한 전체 계산의 작은 부분(small calculations)을 수행하여 사회의 집단 지성에 기여한다는 것입니다. 따라서 ⑤번 '개인들은 더 큰 해결책으로 합쳐지는 적당한 계산을 한다'가 글의 내용과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간의 뇌를 효율적으로 분석하는 방법을 발견하여 허버트 사이먼은 노벨상을 수상했다.
② 컴퓨터나 화장실이 어떻게 작동하는지 이해할 필요가 없는데, 왜냐하면 우리는 그것들을 사용하는 법을 배우는 것을 제지받기 때문이다.
③ 인공지능을 통해 정보를 전달함으로써 사회는 복잡한 문제를 해결한다.
④ 모든 사람이 우리의 정신적 역량보다 더 많은 정보를 보유하며 거대한 계산에 직접 관여한다.
⑤ 개인들은 더 큰 해결책에 보탬이 되는 적당한 계산을 수행한다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓜ에 <보기>의 단어를 각각 한 번씩 모두 사용하여 문장을 완성할 때, ⓙ의 자리에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 37번]
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression. Therefore, unlike conventional medicine which has often <u>   ⓐ   </u> <u>   ⓑ   </u> <u>   ⓒ   </u><u>   ⓓ   </u> <u>   ⓔ   </u> <u>   ⓕ   </u>, <u>   ⓖ   </u> <u>   ⓗ   </u> <u>   ⓘ   </u><u>   ⓙ   </u> <u>   ⓚ   </u> <u>   ⓛ   </u> <u>   ⓜ   </u> a distorted state of consciousness, which then leads to brain chemical imbalances.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 전통 의학(conventional medicine)과 새로운 관점(newer perspectives)을 대조하고 있습니다. 완성된 문장은 'Therefore, unlike conventional medicine which has often <u>attributed depression to brain chemical imbalances</u>, <u>newer perspectives suggest that it stems from</u> a distorted state of consciousness...'가 됩니다. 순서대로 나열하면: ⓐ attributed ⓑ depression ⓒ to ⓓ brain ⓔ chemical ⓕ imbalances / ⓖ newer ⓗ perspectives ⓘ suggest ⓙ that ⓚ it ⓛ stems ⓜ from따라서 ⓙ 자리에 들어갈 단어는 'that'입니다.
options_translation: ① ~로 / ~에게
② 그것
③ ~라는 것 / 저것
④ ~로부터
⑤ 제안하다 / 시사하다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along ─ whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS ─ and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you ______________________. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show ─ whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire ─ you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans to communicate ─ it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ② refine the information it conveys
③ embrace the way it projects things
④ distracted from being in the present
⑤ fixate on the visual stimuli it displays
questions.explanation: 이 글은 새로운 매체가 등장할 때마다 그것이 세상을 보는 방식(안경 혹은 고글)을 규정한다는 마샬 맥루한의 이론을 설명하고 있습니다. 매체 자체가 정보를 전달하는 방식이 정보의 내용보다 중요하며, 우리가 매체가 투영하는 방식으로 세상을 보게 만든다는 내용이므로 빈칸에는 '그것이 사물을 투영하는 방식을 받아들이게'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그것의 가상 세계를 통제하게
② 그것이 전달하는 정보를 정제하게
③ 그것이 사물을 투영하는 방식을 받아들이게
④ 현재에 존재하는 것으로부터 주의가 산만해지게
⑤ 그것이 보여주는 시각적 자극에 집착하게

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. Therefore, despite the complexity of life, the process of canalization ensures that living organisms ______________________________________.
options: ① can shape multiple unpredictable forms
② exist in an infinite number of unstable states
③ evolve without any constraints or boundaries
④ adapt to random changes in their environment
⑤ develop within a constrained set of possible states
questions.explanation: 생명 시스템의 복잡성에도 불구하고, '수로화(canalization)'라는 과정을 통해 유기체가 가질 수 있는 상태나 형태의 가짓수가 제한되고 안정적인 결과로 좁혀진다는 내용의 글입니다. 따라서 마지막 빈칸에는 생물체가 '제한된 집합의 가능한 상태들 내에서 발달하게 된다'는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 여러 예측 불가능한 형태를 형성할 수 있게
② 무한한 수의 불안정한 상태로 존재하게
③ 제약이나 경계 없이 진화하게
④ 환경의 무작위적인 변화에 적응하게
⑤ 제한된 집합의 가능한 상태들 내에서 발달하게

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to __________________, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 인간이 생존을 위해 공동체의 평가에 민감하도록 진화했다는 점을 설명합니다. 자존감, 자부심, 수치심 같은 감정은 타인의 시선을 의식하게 하여 공동체에서 가치 있게 여겨지는 행동을 하도록 유도합니다. 마지막 문장은 이러한 동기부여가 내면에서 오는 것처럼 느껴져야 설득력이 있으며, 만약 우리가 '타인의 시선'에 반응하고 있다는 것을 의식적으로 깨닫게 되면 그 행동이 가식적이거나 냉소적으로 보일 수 있다고 말합니다.
options_translation: ① 타고난 성향
② 타인의 시선
③ 개인적인 충동
④ 개인적인 목표

questions.question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고 <보기>의 빈칸 (A)~(E)에 들어갈 말을 연결한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
vocabulary_box: • The wings of bats and flies can be said to exhibit (A)__________ traits due to their same function but different origin in terms of evolution.
• Sharks and whales would possess (B)__________ traits, because they have both adapted to living in the sea, despite having different ancestors and evolutionary process.

• Human hands and wings of bats are regarded as displaying (C)__________ traits, as they share structural similarities stemming from a common evolutionary origin, despite serving distinctive functions.

• The similarities in bone structure and arrangement between the human hand and the whales flipper exemplify (D)__________ traits, highlighting their same evolutionary origin in spite of their differences in function.
• (E)__________ traits, such as the basic body structure of insects, are observed across different insect species, illustrating their common evolutionary history.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'Analogous(상조적인)'는 기능은 같으나 기원이 다른 특성을 의미하고, 'Homologous(상동의)'는 기능은 다를 수 있으나 공통 조상에서 유래하여 구조가 유사한 특성을 의미합니다.(A) 박쥐와 파리의 날개: 기능은 같으나 기원이 다르므로 analogous.(B) 상어와 고래: 조상이 다르나 바다 생활에 적응한 것이므로 analogous.(C) 사람의 손과 박쥐의 날개: 공통 기원에서 유래한 구조적 유사성이 있으므로 homologous.(D) 사람의 손과 고래의 지느러미: 기능은 다르지만 공통 조상에서 유래한 뼈 구조를 공유하므로 homologous. (정답)(E) 곤충의 기본 신체 구조: 공통의 진화 역사를 보여주므로 Homologous.
options_translation: ① (A): 상동의
② (B): 상동의
③ (C): 상조적인
④ (D): 상동의
⑤ (E): 상조적인

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 41-42번]
questions.passage: From an early age, we assign purpose to objects and events, ⓐ<u>while preferring this reasoning to random chance</u>. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because they don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we need to begin ⓑ<u>by identifying the characteristics of the subject at hand</u>. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. However, by attributing intention to animals and even objects, we are able to make fast decisions about the likely behaviour of that being. This was essential in our hunter-gatherer days ⓒ<u>so that we can avoid eaten by predators</u>. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, ⓓ<u>as those are the mental processes where we understand things</u>. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents. This results in a perceptual system strongly biased towards anthropomorphism. Therefore, we tend ⓔ<u>to assume intention even in the occasions there is none</u>. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you. By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, enables you to rapidly respond to potential threats without necessarily ____________________________, thus ensuring your continued survival.
options: ② relying on the survival mechanism
③ assessing the immediate emotional response
④ waiting to analyze all available evidence
⑤ prioritizing logical analysis over intuition
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 생존을 위해 모호한 대상에게 의도를 부여하여 빠르게 반응하는 경향을 설명하고 있습니다. 사자의 의도를 생각하기 전에 신체 구조를 분석하면 이미 닞으므로, 모든 줝거를 분석하기 위해 기다리준 않고도 속터 리 반응할 수 있게 해준다는 내옑이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: As ⓐ<u>I</u> waited outside the locker room after a hard-fought basketball game, the coach called out to me, "David, walk with me." ⓑ<u>I</u> figured he was going to tell me something important. He was going to select me to be the captain of the team, the leader ⓒ<u>I</u> had always wanted to be. My heart was racing with anticipation. But when his next words hit my ears, everything changed. "We're going to have to send you home," he said coldly. "ⓓ<u>I</u> don't think you are going to make it." I couldn't believe his decision. I tried to hold it together, but inside ⓔ<u>I</u> was falling apart. A car would be waiting tomorrow morning to take me home. And just like that, it was over.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글을 읽고, (A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에 들어갈 단어로 가장 적절한 것을 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to (A)[qualitative / quantitative] data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be (B)[reliable / unreliable]. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to (C)[access / assess] how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
questions.explanation: (A) 미소 지은 횟수나 기억해낸 항목의 수 등 수치로 표현되는 데이터이므로 'quantitative(정량적인/양적인)'가 적절합니다.(B) 응답자의 기억이 부정확하거나 '슬픔'에 대한 정의가 다를 수 있어 데이터가 믿을만하지 않을 수 있다는 문맥이므로 'unreliable(신뢰할 수 없는)'이 적절합니다.(C) 사람들이 자신이 얼마나 심한 미루는 사람인지 스스로 '평가'하게 하는 대신 구체적인 질문을 하라는 흐름이므로 'assess(평가하다)'가 적절합니다. ('access'는 접근하다라는 뜻입니다.)
options_translation: ① 양적인 - 신뢰할 수 있는 - 평가하다
② 질적인 - 신뢰할 수 있는 - 평가하다
③ 양적인 - 신뢰할 수 있는 - 접근하다
④ 질적인 - 신뢰할 수 없는 - 접근하다
⑤ 양적인 - 신뢰할 수 없는 - 평가하다

questions.question: 18. 다음 <보기>는 글을 읽은 후, 학생들이 나눈 대화이다. <보기>에서 옳은 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point ⓐ<u>at which</u> AI exceeds human intelligence. After that point, ⓑ<u>it</u> is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and ⓒ<u>inspire</u> new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI. The direction of AI's evolution will ⓓ<u>depend on</u> what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
vocabulary_box: 갑: ⓐ는 관계부사 'when'으로 바꾸어 적을 수 있어.
병: ⓒ는 문장 내의 동사 'provide'와 병렬을 이루고 있어.
정: ⓓ는 의미상으로 유사한 'rely on'으로 바꾸어 적을 수 있어.
무: 글쓴이는 AI의 존재를 부정적인 시각으로 바라보며, 머지않은 미래에 AI가 인간을 지배할 거라 주장하고 있어.
questions.explanation: 갑: ⓐ 'at which'는 선행사가 'the point'이므로 관계부사 'where'로 바꾸는 것이 더 적절합니다. ('when'은 시간의 선행사일 때 주로 쓰임)을: ⓑ 'it'은 가주어이며, 뒤의 'that AI will ~' 절이 진주어입니다.병: ⓒ 'inspire'는 'will provide'의 'provide'와 병렬 구조를 이루는 것이 맞습니다.정: ⓓ 'depend on'은 '~에 달려있다/의존하다'는 뜻으로 'rely on'과 유사합니다.무: 글쓴이는 AI와 인간의 '상호 공존'과 '함께 진화'하는 긍정적 혹은 중립적 진화 과정을 설명하고 있지, 지배한다는 부정적 주장을 하고 있지 않습니다.따라서 옳은 설명은 병과 정입니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. (A) This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. (B) In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. (C) Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. (D) The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. (E) If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것 세 개를 찾아 바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and ⓐ<u>do</u> their own hunting at night. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes ⓓ<u>staring</u> upwards to create the illusion. questions.explanation: 영재 아이의 부모로서 아이의 업적을 너무 많이 과시하는 것이 아이에게 스트레스와 압박감을 줄 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 아이의 성취에 대해 얼마나 논의하는지에 대해 주의를 기울여야 한다는 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.

② 아이의 성공과 실패의 모든 세부 사항을 공유하는 것
③ 끊임없이 아이의 놀라운 업적을 강조하는 것
④ 아이의 업적에 대해 얼마나 논의하는지에 대해 유념하는 것
⑤ 당신의 육아 기술과 훈육 기법을 논의하는 것에 자부심을 갖는 것

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that __________________ _________________. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
options: ① dissolved oxygen in the oceans will become scarce
② marine biodiversity will increase in this warmer water
③ the amount of dissolved oxygen in ocean water will rise
④ marine species will adapt well to this change and flourish
⑤ the quantity of dissolved oxygen in marine water will remain stable
questions.explanation: 물리학적으로 차가운 물이 따뜻한 물보다 더 많은 용존 산소를 보유한다는 원리를 설명하고 있습니다. 지구 온난화로 인해 해수 온도가 상승함에 따라 바닷속 용존 산소의 양이 줄어들 것이라는 점은 자명합니다. 따라서 해양의 용존 산소가 부족해질 것이라는 내용의 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: 바다의 용존 산소가 부족해질 것이다
이 따뜻해진 물에서 해양 생물 다양성이 증가할 것이다
해수 내의 용존 산소량이 증가할 것이다
해양 생물들이 이 변화에 잘 적응하고 번성할 것이다
해수 내 용존 산소의 양이 안정적으로 유지될 것이다

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. (A) Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. (B) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. (C) As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. (D) Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. (E) A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.insertion_sentence: Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그럼에도 불구하고, 자전거 타기 가장 좋은 도시조차 택시, 긴급 차량, 배달 트럭을 위한 자동차 차로를 필요로 한다'는 내용입니다. (C) 앞까지는 도시에서 자동차 차로를 줄이고 자전거 차로를 늘리는 긍정적인 측면을 설명하고 있습니다. (D) 뒤의 문장부터는 배달 차량(delivery vehicles)이 도시를 더 푸르게 만드는 데 필수적인 요소라는 긍정적인 역할을 설명하기 시작하므로, 자전거 중심 도시에서도 여전히 배달 차량 등이 필요하다는 전환점이 되는 주어진 문장은 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. ⓐFor example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. ⓑAI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. ⓒFor example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. ⓓMany companies are reducing their workforce due to the rise of automation and AI technology, leading to fewer job opportunities for all workers. ⓔMoreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 AI 기술이 장애인이나 저숙련 노동자 등 노동 시장의 소외 계층에게 업무 접근성을 높여주고 직장의 포용성을 개선하는 긍정적인 역할을 한다는 내용입니다. 하지만 ⓓ는 자동화와 AI 기술로 인해 많은 기업들이 인력을 감축하고 일자리가 줄어들고 있다는 부정적인 측면을 언급하고 있으므로 글의 전체적인 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have ⓐ<u>addressed</u> the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are ⓑ<u>powerless</u>. Those who are in a higher vibration are ⓒ<u>full</u> of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is ⓓ<u>helpful</u>. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and ⓔ<u>restarting</u> of one's own latent positive thought forms.
questions.explanation: 상위의 진동(higher vibration)에 있는 사람들은 부정적인 생각으로부터 에너지를 얻는 것이 아니라, 부정적인 생각에서 벗어나 긍정적인 생각의 형태를 활성화시킨 사람들입니다. 따라서 ⓒ의 full(가득 찬)은 '자유로운(free)' 또는 '벗어난' 등의 의미를 가진 단어로 바뀌어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale ⓐ<u>sequesters</u> an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine ⓑ<u>equivalent</u> of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by ⓒ<u>contaminating</u> the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to ⓓ<u>restore</u> whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to ⓔ<u>stop</u> climate change.
questions.explanation: 고래가 영양분이 풍부한 배설물을 배출하여 식물성 플랑크톤의 개체수를 늘리고 탄소를 격리하도록 돕는 과정은 바다를 '오염시키는(contaminating)' 것이 아니라 바다를 '비옥하게 하는(fertilizing)' 작용에 해당합니다. 따라서 ⓒ가 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
options: ① The Importance of Play in Child Development
② The Impact of Mirror Neurons on Observational Learning in Children
③ The Influence of Culture on Child Development: A Historical Perspective
④ The Role of Technology in Shaping Learning Experience for Young Children
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런의 발견이 관찰을 통한 학습이라는 인간의 근본적인 능력에 대한 생각을 바꾸어 놓았으며, 아이들이 부모나 친구의 행동을 모방하며 배우는 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ② '아이들의 관찰 학습에 대한 거울 뉴런의 영향'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 아동 발달에서 놀이의 중요성
② 아이들의 관찰 학습에 대한 거울 뉴런의 영향
③ 아동 발달에 미치는 문화의 영향: 역사적 관점
④ 어린 아이들의 학습 경험 형성에 있어서 기술의 역할

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
options: ① The History of Sound Recording and Music Technology
② How to Improve Your Voice and Master Vocal Technique
③ The Explanation about Why Your Voice Sounds Different to You
④ The Evolution of Sound Recording Technology Through the Years
⑤ Understanding How Different Accents Affect Communication in Different Regions
questions.explanation: 자신의 목소리가 녹음된 것과 다르게 들리는 이유가 두 가지 경로(공기를 통한 외부 경로와 뼈를 통한 내부 경로)를 통해 소리를 인지하기 때문임을 설명하는 글이므로 ③번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 음향 녹음 및 음악 기술의 역사
② 목소리를 개선하고 발성 기술을 숙달하는 방법
③ 왜 당신의 목소리가 다르게 들리는지에 대한 설명
④ 세월에 따른 음향 녹음 기술의 진화
⑤ 서로 다른 억양이 지역별 의사소통에 미치는 영향 이해하기

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist ⓐ<u>because</u> they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us ⓑ<u>to bond</u> with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when ⓒ<u>triggered</u>, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either ⓓ<u>to face</u> a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess ⓔ<u>is</u> thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'the specific emotions (we possess)'로 복수입니다. 따라서 동사는 단수형 is가 아니라 복수형 are가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - ⓐ<u>whether</u> it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on ⓑ<u>makes</u> you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show - whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's ⓒ<u>why</u> Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us ⓓ<u>to see</u> the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you ⓔ<u>which</u> the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
questions.explanation: 동사 'teaches'의 목적어 절을 이끄는 접속사가 필요한 자리입니다. 뒤에 완전한 문장('the world is fast')이 오므로 의문사 'which'가 아닌 접속사 'that'이 적절합니다. 이어지는 구문('that it's about...')과도 병렬을 이룹니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous Nongreat composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.summary_sentence: Great composers such as Beethoven and Brahms were often (A)__________ in their time due to their unusual musical styles, contrasting with peer composers like Salieri, whose lack of (B)__________ prevented him from achieving similar greatness.
questions.explanation: 위대한 작곡가들은 당시 생소함 때문에 (A) 오해받거나 잘못 평가(misjudged/misunderstood)받았으나, 살리에리와 같은 작곡가들은 (B) 독창성(uniqueness/originality)이 부족하여 위대한 반열에 오르지 못했다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 잘못 판단된 / (B) 독특함
② (A) 오해받은 / (B) 단순함
③ (A) 칭찬받은 / (B) 창의성
④ (A) 과대평가된 / (B) 친숙함
⑤ (A) 인정받은 / (B) 독창성

questions.question: 24. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory.
ordered_passages: (A) We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later.
(B) Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form.

(C) After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 벼락치기가 효과적이라는 착각을 하는 이유를 메모리의 차이를 구분하지 못하기 때문이라 설명합니다. (B) 공부 직후 정보가 의식적인 작동 기억에 존재함을 설명하고, (A) 이것이 단기 저장 공간에 있어 아는 것처럼 느껴지지만 장기 기억과는 무관함을 지적한 뒤, (C) 시간이 지나면 사라지므로 장기 기억을 위해 스스로 테스트하는 과정이 필요함을 결론짓는 순서가 가장 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 영어 단어로 가장 적절한 것을 <보기>에서 각각 한 단어씩 골라 형태 변형 없이 쓰시오. [3.3점]
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to (A)__________ depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the (B)__________ selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less (C)__________.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에서 각각 한 단어씩 골라 형태 변형 없이 쓸 것
questions.explanation: (A) 집단 내 관계를 잘 관리하는 능력은 '번영(thrive)'하는 능력과 직결됩니다. (B) 수백만 년에 걸쳐 그러한 특성을 가진 '계통/종족(strain)'이 선택되었습니다. (C) 사회적 압력에 반응하는 것을 자각하면 우리의 행동은 덜 '설득력(convincing)' 있게 보일 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
options: ① Conventional Medicine's View of Mental Health
② Influences of Brain Substances on Consciousness
③ The Effects of Serotonin and Noradrenaline on Mood
④ An Overview of Neurotransmitter's Role in Depression
⑤ Depression Caused by the Distortion of Consciousness
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우울증이 뇌 화학 물질의 불균형 때문에 생기는 것이 아니라, 의식의 왜곡(자아감과 삶의 의미 상실)이 근본 원인이며 뇌 물질의 변화는 그 결과라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '의식의 왜곡에 의해 야기된 우울증'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 정신 건강에 대한 전통 의학의 관점
② 뇌 물질이 의식에 미치는 영향
③ 세로토닌과 노르아드레날린이 기분에 미치는 영향
④ 우울증에서 신경전달물질의 역할에 대한 개요
⑤ 의식의 왜곡에 의해 야기된 우울증

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 설명한 psychology의 특징으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
options: ① Psychology focuses on the shared traits of humans rather than on cultural differences or social diversity.
② Psychology uses an evidence-based approach to understand human behavior and thought.
③ Psychology relies on generally accepted views in society or the opinions of deep thinkers.
questions.explanation: 본문은 심리학이 단순한 추측이나 사회적 통념이 아니라 '과학'이며, 증거에 기반한 접근 방식(evidence-based approach)을 통해 인간의 행동과 사고를 이해하려 한다고 강조하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 심리학은 문화적 차이나 사회적 다양성보다는 인간의 공통된 특성에 초점을 맞춘다.
② 심리학은 인간의 행동과 사고를 이해하기 위해 증거 기반 접근 방식을 사용한다.
③ 심리학은 사회에서 일반적으로 받아들여지는 견해나 깊은 사상가들의 의견에 의존한다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 괄호 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be (A)[effectual / ignorant] due to what Alvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a (B)[rebuke / compliment], a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling (C)[perceptible / unseen], so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤에 이어지는 '속임수 처벌' 때문에 아이를 처벌하는 것이 '효과적(effectual)'이지 않을 수 있다는 내용이 적절합니다. (B) 속임수 처벌은 고전적인 의미의 처벌이므로 '비난/꾸짖음(rebuke)'이 적절합니다. (C) 외로운 아이에게는 꾸지람을 듣는 것이 '보이지 않는(unseen)' 무시당하는 느낌보다 낫다는 맥락이므로 unseen이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 효과적인 / 칭찬 / 인지할 수 있는
② 효과적인 / 비난 / 보이지 않는
③ 효과적인 / 비난 / 인지할 수 있는
④ 무지한 / 칭찬 / 보이지 않는
⑤ 무지한 / 비난 / 인지할 수 있는

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 Seeing is not believing의 사례로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. <u>Seeing is not believing</u>.
options: ① Several people described a suspect, but their accounts didn't match. Some said the suspect had a beard, while others he didn't. Their memories of the person were altered by stress or presumptions.

② Siblings often remember the same family trip differently. One may recall it was full of laughter, while the other recalls arguing and tears. Their memories are influenced by how they felt during the trip.

③ Two people saw the same car accident. One says the car was red and speeding, but the other says it was blue and moving slowly. Their memories after because they were shaped by their own thoughts and feelings.

④ A student saw his friend using a cheat sheet during an exam. Afterward, the teacher discovered the sheet, which contained the friend's handwriting. This confirms that he was indeed cheating, and what he saw is true.

⑤ Many fans recalled a famous K-pop idol wearing a bright red jacket during a performance. However, upon reviewing the video, they discovered that the jacket was actually black. Their memories were likely influenced by the idol's stage lighting or their excitement during the event.
questions.explanation: 본문은 우리가 보는 것이 객관적인 사실 그대로가 아니라 주관적인 경험, 가정, 지식에 의해 재구성된다는 점을 강조합니다. 즉, '보는 것이 믿는 것(사실)이 아니다'라는 의미입니다. ①, ②, ③, ⑤는 모두 기억이 왜곡되거나 사람마다 다르게 인식되는 사례로 본문의 주제와 일치하지만, ④는 본 것이 물증과 일치하여 사실로 확인된 경우이므로 'Seeing is not believing'의 사례로 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 여러 사람이 한 용의자를 묘사했지만 진술이 일치하지 않았다. 어떤 사람들은 수염이 있었다고 했고, 다른 이들은 없었다고 했다. 그들의 기억은 스트레스나 추정에 의해 변했다.
② 형제자매들은 종종 같은 가족 여행을 다르게 기억한다. 한 명은 웃음으로 가득했다고 회상하고, 다른 명은 다툼과 눈물로 기억한다. 그들의 기억은 여행 중 느꼈던 감정에 영향을 받았다.
③ 두 사람이 같은 자동차 사고를 목격했다. 한 명은 차가 빨간색이고 과속 중이었다고 하고, 다른 명은 파란색이고 느리게 가고 있었다고 한다. 그들의 기억은 각자의 생각과 감정에 의해 형성되었다.
④ 한 학생이 시험 중에 친구가 커닝 페이퍼를 사용하는 것을 보았다. 나중에 선생님이 그 친구의 글씨가 적힌 종이를 발견했다. 이것은 그가 실제로 부정행위를 했다는 것과 그가 본 것이 사실임을 확인해 준다.
⑤ 많은 팬들이 공연 중에 유명 아이돌이 밝은 빨간색 재킷을 입었다고 기억했다. 하지만 영상을 다시 확인해보니 재킷은 사실 검은색이었다. 그들의 기억은 조명이나 흥분에 의해 영향을 받았을 가능성이 크다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)와 의미가 같도록 반드시 <보기>의 단어만을 모두 한 번씩 변형 없이 사용해 알맞게 배열하여 영작하시오.
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. (A)<u>오직 그들이 다시 봤을 때서야 그들은 중간 크기의 문어를 보았고 착시를 만들기 위해 그것은 여덟 개의 모든 팔이 접혀 있었고 그것의 두 눈이 위쪽을 응시하고 있었다</u>. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature.
subjective_conditions: 반드시 <보기>의 단어만을 모두 한 번씩 변형 없이 사용
questions.answer: It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion
questions.explanation: "It is ~ that ..." 강조 구문을 사용하여 부사절 "only when they looked again"을 강조하는 문장입니다. 또한 with 분사구문(with + 명사 + 분사)인 "with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards"가 연결되어 문어의 상태를 설명하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: I quickly learned the reason many consumer products come in three different variants while I worked at a sizeable electronics firm that produced laser and ink-jet printers. If the manufacturer had produced only one version of the product, it would have resulted in a little loss for the business, as customers might have been willing to pay more. If the company offers two versions, one of which is more expensive and has more features than the other, people will compare the two models and still choose to purchase the less expensive one. However, if the company releases a third model that is packed with even more features and more costly than other two, sales of the second model increase. The most expensive model's features appeal to many people, but the cost does not. The medium model is less expensive than the most expensive one, but it has more features than the least priced one. They purchased the medium item without realizing that the higher-priced item has been used to manipulated them.
options: ① Pricing Tricks: Why the Fanciest Product Always Sells Best
② Various Features: How They Always Make Customers Happy
③ Pricing Strategies: The Hidden Strategy Behind Three Product Variants
④ Buying Psychology: Why People Never Choose the Cheapest Product
⑤ Marketing Tricks: Why the Most Expensive Product Attracts the Most Customers
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기업들이 세 가지 버전의 제품을 출시함으로써 소비자들이 중간 가격의 제품을 선택하도록 유도하는 가격 책정 전략(Pricing Strategies)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 가장 비싼 모델은 중간 모델의 판매를 높이기 위한 미끼로 사용된다는 내용이 핵심입니다.
options_translation: ① 가격 책정의 요수: 왜 가장 화려한 제품이 항상 가장 잘 팔리는가
② 다양한 기능들: 어떻게 그것들이 항상 고객을 행복하게 만드는가
③ 가격 책정 전략: 세 가지 제품 변체 뒤에 숨겨진 전략
④ 구매 심리학: 왜 사람들은 절대 가장 저렴한 제품을 선택하지 않는가
⑤ 마케팅 요수: 왜 가장 비싼 제품이 가장 많은 고객을 끌어들이는가

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.summary_sentence: Climate change is a huge problem that is becoming (A)__________ to ignore, even in stories and movies. Right now, people enjoy stories about climate disasters because they feel like they are (B)__________ or fictional. But as the world gets hotter and everyone starts feeling the effects, those stories might (C)__________ because the real world will feel just like them.
questions.explanation: 기후 변화가 너무나 명백해짐에 따라 이를 무시하는 것이 '어려워지고(challenging)', 현재는 사람들이 기후 재앙이 '멀리 떨어져(remote)' 있다고 느껴서 즐기지만, 실생활에서 그 영향을 느끼게 되면 기후 소설이라는 장르 자체가 '사라질(disappear)' 것이라는 내용이 요약문에 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 힘들게 만드는 - 멀리 떨어진 - 사라지다
② 힘들게 만드는 - 멀리 떨어진 - 펼쳐지다
③ 힘들게 만드는 - 가까운 - 펼쳐지다
④ 노력이 필요 없는 - 가까운 - 펼쳐지다
⑤ 노력이 필요 없는 - 멀리 떨어진 - 사라지다

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. ⓐSuch a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. ⓑFor example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. ⓒInterestingly, this is why some scientists have frequently been fascinated by the way embryos appear to resist the effects of gravity as they develop. ⓓIn 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. ⓔWe'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 생명체가 고차원적인 시스템으로서 많은 수의 상호작용이 가능하지만 실제로는 제한된 수의 결과물(canalization, 운하화)로 수렴된다는 내용입니다. ⓒ번 문장은 배아가 발달할 때 중력의 영향에 저항하는 방식에 과학자들이 매료되었다는 내용으로, 시스템의 안정화와 결과의 제한이라는 글의 핵심 흐름에서 벗어난 내용입니다.

questions.question: 4. 윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally elective. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: a plentiful resource made (A)[accessible / short] through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no (B)[reward / need] for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to address it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly highlights have-and-have-not (C)[equity / discrimination], leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
options: ① The water issue is triggered by politics due to the governmental inability to control.
② The capital results in water problems and governmental intervention.
questions.explanation: 글의 첫 문장에서 물 위기가 정치적이라고 언급하며, 정부의 방치, 무관심, 열악한 인프라 등으로 인해 자원이 부족해지고 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 물 위기는 정부의 관리 불능으로 인한 정치적인 문제라는 ①번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 물 문제는 정부의 관리 능력 부재로 인한 정치에 의해 유발된다.
② 자본이 물 문제와 정부의 개입을 초래한다.

questions.question: 5. 윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally elective. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: a plentiful resource made (A)[accessible / short] through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no (B)[reward / need] for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to address it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly highlights have-and-have-not (C)[equity / discrimination], leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
questions.explanation: (A) 문맥상 풍부한 자원이 정부의 방치 등으로 인해 '부족해진(short)' 상황을 설명해야 합니다. (B) 물 위기가 일어날 실질적인 '필요(need)'가 없음에도 불구하고 위기가 존재한다는 의미가 적절합니다. (C) 선택적 희소성이 가진 자와 가지지 못한 자 사이의 '차별(discrimination)'을 부각한다는 내용이 적절합니다.

(A) 부족한 (B) 필요 (C) 형평성

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an ⓐ<u>imbalance</u> of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is not a cause of depression but a ⓑ<u>consequence</u> of it. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this ⓒ<u>revised</u> cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root ⓓ<u>effect</u> of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of ⓔ<u>mood</u> disorder.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우울증이 뇌의 화학적 불균형에 의해 발생하는 것이 아니라, 의식의 왜곡이 원인이 되어 뇌의 물질 변화를 일으키는 것이라고 주장하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⓓ 부분은 우울증의 근본적인 '결과'가 아니라 근본적인 '원인(cause)'이 의식 상태의 왜곡이라는 맥락이 되어야 하므로 effect는 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, ⓐ<u>which</u> is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way that production could be made more efficient, ⓑ<u>known</u> as the "division of labor." Making most manufactured goods involves several different processes ⓒ<u>using</u> different skills. Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished. One worker could do all these tasks, and make 20 pins in a day. But this work can be divided into its separate processes, with a number of workers each ⓓ<u>performed</u> one task. Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day - a huge increase in productivity from the 200 they ⓔ<u>would have produced</u> before.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장은 'with + 목적어 + 분사' 구문입니다. 각 노동자들이 하나의 업무를 '수행하는' 능동의 관계이므로 과거분사인 performed가 아닌 현재분사 performing이 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
options: ① The High Quality Laser and Ink-jet Printers
② The Company's One Strategy to Maximize Margin
③ The Persuasive Way to Sell the More Expensive Model
④ Three Models with Different Features and Prices
⑤ The Reason Why a Company Produces its Models Repeatedly
questions.explanation: 가장 비싼 세 번째 모델을 도입함으로써 소비자들이 중간 가격의 두 번째 모델을 선택하도록 유도하여 수익(이익률)을 극대화하는 기업의 전략을 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 고품질 레이저 및 잉크젯 프린터
② 수익을 극대화하기 위한 기업의 한 가지 전략
③ 더 비싼 모델을 팔기 위한 설득력 있는 방법
④ 다른 특징과 가격을 가진 세 가지 모델
⑤ 회사가 반복적으로 모델을 생산하는 이유

questions.question: 16. 윗글 (A)~(C)의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: (A) According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The decline in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.(B) Gender research shows a complex relationship between gender and conflict styles. Some research suggests that women from Western cultures tend to be more caring than men. This tendency may result from socialization processes in which women are encouraged to care for their families and men are encouraged to be successful in competitive work environments. However, we live in a society where gender roles and boundaries are not as strict as in prior generations. There is significant variability in assertiveness and cooperation among women, as well as among men. Although conflict resolution experts should be able to recognize cultural and gender differences, they should also be aware of within-group variations and the risks of stereotyping. Culture and gender may affect the way people perceive, interpret, and respond to conflict; however, we must be careful to avoid overgeneralizations and to consider individual differences.(C) The natural world provides a rich source of symbols used in art and literature. Plants and animals are central to mythology, dance, song, poetry, rituals, festivals, and holidays around the world. Different cultures can exhibit opposite attitudes toward a given species. Snakes, for example, are honored by some cultures and hated by others. Rats are considered pests in much of Europe and North America and greatly respected in some parts of India. ___________________________________. For instance, in Britain many people dislike rodents, and yet there are several associations devoted to breeding them, including the National Mouse Club and the National Fancy Rat Club.
options: ① (A)는 유아의 뇌가 성인보다 신경 연결 개수가 적으며 덜 효율적임을 알려준다.
② (B)는 현재의 성역할이나 경계가 기성 세대보다 완화되었음을 지적하고 있다.
③ (B)에서 서구사회에서 여성이 남성보다 더 주변을 돌보는 모습을 보이는 것이 가족 돌봄을 권장하는 사회화 과정의 영향을 받았을 가능성이 드러나 있다.
④ (B)와 (C)는 문화가 사람들의 인식과 태도에 큰 영향을 끼칠 수 있다는 것을 지적하고 있다.
⑤ (C)에서 특정 동물에 대한 선호는 정해진 기준이나 규범에 의한 것이 아님을 알 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문 (A)에서 유아의 뇌는 성인의 뇌보다 작지만, 수백만 개 더 많은 신경 연결(millions more neural connections)을 포함하고 있다고 명시되어 있으므로 개수가 적다는 설명은 옳지 않습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 they look for evidence가 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, <u>they look for evidence</u>, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
options: ① 심리학자들은 과학적인 논리를 바탕으로 현상을 설명하고 증명한다.
② 심리학자들은 자신들의 정확한 정보 수집 능력을 드러낸다.
③ 심리학자들은 많은 사람들의 의견과 관점을 반영하기 위해 노력한다.
④ 심리학자들은 구전된 데이터의 가치를 인식하고 연구에 활용한다.
⑤ 심리학자들은 인간의 행동을 보다 철학적으로 설명한다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 심리학은 '과학(science)'임을 강조하며, 심리학자들이 의견, 소문, 일반적인 믿음이 아닌 '증거(evidence)'를 찾는다고 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 심리학적 아이디어가 일반적인 통념이 아닌 과학적 근거에 기반하도록 확실히 한다는 의미이므로 1번이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability ⓐ<u>to thrive</u> depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these ⓑ<u>merits</u>. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, 그러한 압박은 그들의 지위를 최대화하는 것에 민감하고 능숙한 사람들을 선택했다. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor ⓒ<u>how</u> other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what ⓓ<u>doesn't</u>. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less ⓔ<u>persuasively</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓔ의 persuasively는 분사구문 making의 목적격 보어 자리입니다. 5형식 동사 make의 목적격 보어로는 부사가 아닌 형용사가 와야 하므로 persuasive로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 문맥을 고려하여 빈칸 (A)에 들어가기에 적합한 말을 한 단어의 (또는 2~4단어의) 영어로 쓰시오. (단, 본문에 없는 단어로 써야 함) [단답형]

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 11월 32번]
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions. But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.*phase: (달의) 상(相)
options: ① Using the internet helps improve problem-solving skills.
② People tend to overrate their knowledge when they have internet access.
③ Internet searches are not helpful for answering unrelated questions.
④ Intellectual confidence is independent of the information one has access to.
⑤ Internet use can falsely inflate people's sense of their own knowledge.
questions.explanation: 지문은 첫 번째 단계에서 인터넷 검색을 한 사람들이 관련 없는 두 번째 단계의 질문에 대해서도 자신들이 더 많이 알고 있다고 생각했다는 실험 결과를 통해, 인터넷 사용이 자신의 지적 능력에 대한 자신감을 과하게 부풀릴 수 있다는 점을 시사하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 인터넷 사용은 문제 해결 능력을 향상시키는 데 도움이 된다.
② 사람들은 인터넷 접속이 가능할 때 자신의 지식을 과대평가하는 경향이 있다.
③ 인터넷 검색은 관련 없는 질문에 답하는 데 도움이 되지 않는다.
④ 지적 자신감은 개인이 접근할 수 있는 정보와 무관하다.
⑤ 인터넷 사용은 자신의 지식에 대한 사람들의 감각을 허위로 부풀릴 수 있다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying them to culture. Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually likened to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection.
