However, these approaches had to be modified to account for the differences between genetic and cultural transmission. For example, we do not expect the cultural transmission to follow the rules of genetic transmission strictly. If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily equally likely to acquire the mother's or father's form of that trait. Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers; thus, the frequency of a cultural trait in the population is relevant beyond just the probability that an individual's parents had that trait.*mutation: 돌연변이 **relevant: 유의미한
options: ① cultural transmission involving more diverse factors than genetic transmission
② different roles between parents and nonparental adults in cultural learning
③ importance of nonparental and peer influence on cultural inheritance
④ methods of analyzing cultural traits in population genetics
⑤ evolutionary aspects of population genetics in society
questions.explanation: 이 글은 초기 문화 진화 모델이 유전적 진화와 문화를 유사하게 보려 했으나, 실제로는 문화적 전이가 유전적 전이보다 훨씬 복잡하고 다양한 요인을 포함하고 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 문화적 전이는 부모뿐만 아니라 또래나 다른 성인으로부터도 일어날 수 있다는 점을 예로 들어 유전적 전이와의 차별성을 강조하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 유전적 전이보다 더 다양한 요인을 포함하는 문화적 전이
② 문화 학습에 있어서 부모와 비부모 성인의 서로 다른 역할
③ 문화 상속에 있어서 비부모 및 또래 영향의 중요성
④ 집단 유전학에서 문화적 특성을 분석하는 방법들
⑤ 사회에서 집단 유전학의 진화론적 측면

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
options: ① The Physical World: A Window to Universals
② How to Rediscover True Reality: Plato's Guide
③ Ancient Philosophy and Its Mathematical Basis
④ Geometrical Perfection: The Key to Modern Science
⑤ Beyond the Visible: Plato's Theory of Perfect Forms
questions.explanation: 이 글은 플라톤의 실재론, 특히 '이데아(Forms)'에 대한 이론을 설명하고 있습니다. 우리가 현실에서 보는 사물들(예: 원)은 불완전하고 변하지만, 보이지 않는 영역에 완벽한 형태인 이데아가 존재하며 그것이 진정한 실재라고 믿었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 물리적 세계: 보편자로 향하는 창
② 진정한 실재를 재발견하는 방법: 플라톤의 가이드
③ 고대 철학과 그것의 수학적 기초
④ 기하학적 완벽함: 현대 과학의 열쇠
⑤ 가시적인 것 너머: 플라톤의 완벽한 형상(이데아) 이론

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 Grace Braddock에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Dear Ms. MacAlpine, I was so excited to hear that your brand is opening a new shop on Bruns Street next month. I have always appreciated the way your brand helps women to feel more stylish and confident. I am writing in response to your ad in the Bruns Journal. I graduated from the Meline School of Fashion and have worked as a sales assistant at LoganMart for the last five years. During that time, I've developed strong customer service and sales skills, and now I would like to apply for the sales position in your clothing store. I am available for an interview at your earliest convenience. I look forward to hearing from you. Thank you for reading my letter.Yours sincerely,Grace Braddock
options: ① 높이 평가해 왔던 브랜드가 새 매장을 연다는 소식에 매우 들떠있었다.
② 저널에 있는 광고에 대한 응답으로 편지를 썼다.
③ 패션 학교를 졸업했고 지난 5년간 판매 보조원으로 일해 왔다.
④ 의류 매장 판매직에 지원하기 위해 편지를 썼다.
⑤ 답변을 받는 대로 최대한 빨리 면접 가능한 날짜를 회신할 예정이다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 Grace Braddock은 'I am available for an interview at your earliest convenience'라고 언급하며, 상대방이 편한 가장 빠른 시간에 면접이 가능하다고 말하고 있습니다. 답변을 받은 후 날짜를 회신하겠다는 내용은 지문에 언급되지 않았습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 ␐~␘ 중 어법상서 올바른 문장의 개수는?
questions.passage: ␐I had never seen a beach with such white sand or water that was a such beautiful shade of blue. ␑Jane and I set up a blanket on the sand while look forward to our ten days of honeymooning on an exotic island. ␒Then, Jane waved her hand, pointing at the beautiful scene before us. ␓And her gold wedding ring went flying off her hand. ␔I tried to see where it went, but ! lost track of it due to the sun hit my eyes. ␕I didn't want to lose her wedding ring. ␖So I started looking in the area which I thought it had landed. ␗However, the sand was so fine that anything heavy, like gold, would quickly sink. ␘I realized it might never find again.
questions.explanation: ␐: such a beautiful(a까 나가거나 사계다) → a such beautiful(X). ␑: while looking forward to(while 다개메 베사개마 거나 깨 새매). ␒: 마게나(바사개마 거매). ␓: 마게나(went flying 바사개마 거매). ␔: due to the sun hitting(due to 다개메 도가매사 나개마 거나 깨 새매). ␕: 마게나. ␖: where I thought it had landed(가내 거내 바사개마). ␗: 마게나. ␘: it might never be found(it가 ring개모 사도대 다개마). 마게나나내 마개나내 ␒, ␓, ␕, ␗ 개 4개머다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 ␐~␔ 중 어법상 올바른 문장은?
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. ␐<u>The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms to cover in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants.</u> ␑<u>Not only were their athletic talents superiorly, the Cubans appeared very strongly from just the colour of their uniforms.</u> A game would not even start and the opposing team would already be scared. ␒<u>A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing them and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time.</u> ␓<u>The country that ruled international baseball for decades had not been on top since that uniform change.</u> ␔<u>Traditions are important for a team; while a team brand or image can adjust to keep up with present times, if it abandons or neglects its roots, negative effects can surface.</u>
questions.explanation: ␐: to cover → covered (마개사 사도대). ␑: superiorly → superior (바개사 가가), strongly → strong (바개사 가가). ␒: modernizing them → modernizing it (uniform style개 다나사). ␓: had not been → has not been (since 개 다개메 혀내깨까내 하나개 타개마). ␔: 마게나.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 보기의 영영 뜻풀이 중 사용된 단어의 뜻이 아닌 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation ─ transferring organs to others ─ is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
options: ① happening too soon or earlier than usual
② able to be believed, likely to be true or correct
③ the quality, condition, or fact of being exact and accurate
④ somethings that are used as reasons for making a judgment or decision
⑤ a part of the body (such as the heart or liver) that has a particular function
questions.explanation: 본문에 사용된 단어들과 영영 풀이를 비교하면 다음과 같습니다.① premature (조급한, 너무 이른) - 본문에 사용됨② reliable (믿을 만한) - 본문에는 'unreliable(믿을 수 없는)'이 사용되었으므로 긍정형인 reliable의 뜻풀이는 일치하지 않음③ precision (정밀성) - 본문에 사용됨④ criteria (기준) - 본문에 사용됨⑤ organ (장기) - 본문에 사용됨
options_translation: ① 평소보다 너무 빨리 혹은 더 일찍 일어나는 (premature)
② 믿어질 수 있는, 사실이거나 정확할 것 같은 (reliable)
③ 정확하고 정밀한 품질, 상태 또는 사실 (precision)
④ 판단이나 결정을 내리는 이유로 사용되는 것들 (criteria)
⑤ 특정한 기능을 가진 신체의 일부(심장이나 간 같은) (organ)

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C) 각 괄호 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In statistics, the law of large numbers describes a situation where having (A)[abundant / minimum] data is better for making predictions. According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to match the true state of the world. For instance, on your first encounter with the game of roulette, you may have beginner's luck after betting on 7. But the more often you repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning, meaning that your luck will at some point gradually grow faint and (B)[appear / disappear]. Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to (C)[ balance / disregard] individual losses.
questions.explanation: (A) 대수의 법칙은 풍부한(abundant) 데이터를 가질 때 예측이 더 잘 된다는 것을 설명합니다. (B) 실험(베팅)을 반복할수록 결과는 실제 확률에 가까워지므로, 초심자의 행운은 점차 희미해지고 사라지게(disappear) 됩니다. (C) 카지노와 보험 업계는 대수의 법칙을 통해 개별적인 손실을 평균적인 수익으로 상쇄하거나 균형을 맞추기(balance) 때문에 이 법칙에 의존합니다.
options_translation: ① 풍부한 / 나타나다 / 균형을 맞추다
② 풍부한 / 사라지다 / 균형을 맞추다
③ 풍부한 / 나타나다 / 무시하다
④ 최소한의 / 사라지다 / 균형을 맞추다
⑤ 최소한의 / 나타나다 / 무시하다

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. They do well enough in school to keep ⓐ<u>progressing</u>. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ⓑ<u>halts</u> with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now lack a road map ⓒ<u>describing</u> the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when the journey really begins. When school is finished, your growth becomes ⓓ<u>instinctive</u>. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and ⓔ<u>dedicate</u> thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen ─ and your life and career are likely to stop moving forward as a result.
questions.explanation: 학교 교육이 끝난 후의 성장은 자동으로 이루어지는 본능적인(instinctive) 것이 아니라, 뒤에 이어지는 설명(식습관이나 운동처럼 전념하고 시간과 에너지를 쏟아야 함)으로 보아 의도적이고 자발적인 노력이 필요한 것입니다. 따라서 '본능적인'이 아니라 '의도적인(intentional)' 또는 '자발적인(voluntary)'과 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.5점]
questions.passage: The adolescent brain is not fully developed until its early twenties. This means the way the adolescents' decision-making circuits integrate and process information may put them at a ⓐ<u>disadvantage</u>. One of their brain regions that matures later is the prefrontal cortex, which is the control center, tasked with thinking ahead and evaluating consequences. It is the area of the brain responsible for ⓑ<u>preventing</u> you from sending off an initial angry text and ⓒ<u>modifying</u> it with kinder words. On the other hand, the limbic system matures earlier, playing a central role in processing emotional responses. Because of its earlier development, it is ⓓ<u>more</u> likely to influence decision-making. Decision-making in the adolescent brain is led by emotional factors more than the perception of consequences. Due to these differences, there is a ⓔ<u>balance</u> between feeling-based decision-making ruled by the more mature limbic system and logical-based decision-making by the not-yet-mature prefrontal cortex. This may explain why some teens are more likely to act before thinking things through.
questions.explanation: 청소년의 뇌에서 감정 반응을 처리하는 대뇌변연계는 일찍 발달하는 반면, 통제 센터 역할을 하는 전전두엽 피질은 나중에 발달합니다. 따라서 감정 기반의 의사 결정과 논리 기반의 의사 결정 사이에는 '균형(balance)'이 아닌 '불균형(imbalance)' 또는 '차이'가 존재하게 됩니다. 그러므로 ⑤번 balance는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: When writing a novel, research for information needs to be done. The thing is that some kinds of fiction demand a higher level of detail: crime fiction, for example, or scientific thrillers. The information is never hard to find; one website for authors even organizes trips to police stations, so that crime writers can get it right. Often, a polite letter will earn you permission to visit a particular location and record all the details that you need. But remember that ___________________________________________. In other words, the details that matter are those that reveal the human experience. The crucial thing is telling a story, finding the characters, the tension, and the conflict ─ not the train timetable or the building blueprint.
options: ① readers appreciate extensive research rather than detailed information in works of fiction
② you should pack as much detailed information as possible to make your story believable
③ in order to make your story more engaging, you need to include more technical vocabulary
④ the right amount of specifics is the key to encourage readers to dive into the narrative
⑤ you will be subject to harsh criticism if you confuse your readers with too many characters
questions.explanation: 소설을 쓸 때 세부적인 정보를 위한 조사가 필요하지만, 작가에게 정말 중요한 것은 열차 시간표나 청사진 같은 기술적 데이터가 아니라 인간의 경험을 드러내는 이야기, 캐릭터, 긴장감, 갈등이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 세부 사항은 독자가 이야기에 몰입하게 할 수 있을 만큼의 '적절한 양'이어야 한다는 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 독자들은 허구의 작품에서 상세한 정보보다는 광범위한 조사를 높이 평가한다.
② 이야기를 믿음직스럽게 만들기 위해 가능한 한 많은 상세 정보를 채워 넣어야 한다.
③ 이야기를 더 매력적으로 만들기 위해 더 많은 전문 용어를 포함해야 한다.
④ 적절한 양의 세부 사항이 독자들이 이야기 속으로 빠져들게 하는 열쇠이다.
⑤ 너무 많은 등장인물로 독자들을 혼란스럽게 하면 혹독한 비판을 받을 것이다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.5점]
questions.passage: Despite the remarkable progress in deep-learning based facial recognition approaches in recent years, in terms of identification performance, they still have limitations. (A) These limitations relate to the database used in the learning stage. (B) If the selected database does not contain enough instances, the result may be systematically affected. (C) For example, the performance of a facial biometric system may decrease if the person to be identified was enrolled over 10 years ago. (D) These changes may be highlighted by weight gain or loss. (E) To counteract this problem, researchers have developed models for face aging or digital de-aging. It is used to ____________________________________, which appear over a given time period.
questions.insertion_sentence: The factor to consider is that this person may experience changes in the texture of the face, particularly with the appearance of wrinkles and sagging skin.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 사람의 얼굴 질감 변화, 특히 주름과 처진 피부의 등장을 언급하고 있습니다. 이는 (C)에서 언급된 '10년 전 등록된 사람의 식별 성능 저하'와 관련된 구체적인 노화 현상을 설명하며, 뒤따르는 (D)의 '이러한 변화들(These changes)은 체중 증감에 의해 두드러질 수 있다'는 문장과 논리적으로 연결됩니다. 따라서 (D) 위치인 ④번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Despite the remarkable progress in deep-learning based facial recognition approaches in recent years, in terms of identification performance, they still have limitations. (A) These limitations relate to the database used in the learning stage. (B) If the selected database does not contain enough instances, the result may be systematically affected. (C) For example, the performance of a facial biometric system may decrease if the person to be identified was enrolled over 10 years ago. (D) These changes may be highlighted by weight gain or loss. (E) To counteract this problem, researchers have developed models for face aging or digital de-aging. It is used to ____________________________________, which appear over a given time period.
options: ② predict the appearance of their kids
③ warn against introducing and using AI
④ delay aging and promote a healthy life
⑤ make up for the variations in facial features
questions.explanation: 이 글은 안면 인식 시스템이 시간 경과에 따른 얼굴의 노화나 변화를 식별하는 데 한계가 있다는 점을 다루고 있습니다. 연구원들은 이를 해결하기 위해 노화 또는 역노화 모델을 개발했으며, 이는 일정 기간 동안 나타나는 '얼굴 특징의 변화를 보충하기 위해(make up for the variations in facial features)' 사용됩니다.
options_translation: ① AI 기술에 반대하다
② 아이들의 외모를 예측하다
③ AI 도입 및 사용에 대해 경고하다
④ 노화를 늦추고 건강한 삶을 도모하다
⑤ 얼굴 특징의 변화를 보충하다

questions.question: 28. 다음 글을 아래와 같이 정리할 경우, 전체 내용과 가장 관계없는 문장은? [23년 11월 31번]
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristic of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself. Psychologist George M. Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment. Stratton wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally turned the world upside down for him. In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him. With time, however, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated. As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems: he used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something, for example. Fortunately, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for the rest of his life. For him, everything returned to normal after one day.*↓The visual system has an impressive ability to adapt, as demonstrated by psychologist George M. Stratton's self-experiment. ␐He wore glasses that reversed his vision, making the world appear upside down. ␑Initially, this caused significant challenges, such as difficulty using a fork to eat. ␒Over time, however, his visual system adjusted, and he was able to navigate his environment as if it were normal. ␓When he removed the glasses, he struggled again and never fully regained normal perception. ␔This experiment highlighted the adaptability of the visual system to new sensory information.
questions.explanation: ␓은 Stratton이 안경을 벗은 홄 다시 적응하지 못했다고 설명하고 있지만, 원문에서는 하렔 바만에 모든 것이 정상으로 돌아왔다고 하였으뭀로 전체 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [23년 11월 33번]
questions.passage: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson suggests that we tend to understand the world by focusing in on particular features within it. Take platypuses. We might zoom in so closely to their fur that each hair appears different. We might also zoom out to the extent where it appears as a single uniform object. ␐We might take the platypus as an individual, or we might treat it as part of a larger unit such as a species or an ecosystem. ␑It's possible to move between many of these perspectives, although we may need some additional tools and skills to zoom in on individual pieces of hair or zoom out to entire ecosystems. ␒Crucially, we must take account of all the perspectives evenly and simultaneously. ␓We can pay attention to the varied behavior of individual animals, look at what unites them into a single species, or look at them as part of bigger ecological patterns. ␔Every possible perspective involves emphasizing certain aspects and ignoring others.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사물을 바라바는 다양한 관점에 대한 글으로, 모든 관점을 균등하고 동시에 고려해야 한다는 내용은 특정 특징에 초점을 맞추어 이해한다는 전체 흤름과 어색합니다. 관점을 이동하며 다른 측면을 본다는 내용이 주를 이립니다.

questions.question: 30. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 11월 21번]
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them.
ordered_passages: (A) Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective ─ "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.

(B) They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light ─ a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer.

(C) They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless ─ and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 색이 객관적 성질이라는 관점을 소개한 홄, (B)에서 그 관점에 대한 구체적인 예시(나무잎이 초록색인 이유)림 들고 다른 관점(주관적 관점)을 소개합니다. (C)는 그 주관적 관점에 대한 부연 설명이며, 마지막으로 (A)에서 둀 관점이 모됀 옳다고 결론을 내립니다.

questions.question: 31. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows.
ordered_passages: (A) The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur.

(B) Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.

(C) At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change ─ especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 사람들이 좋아하는 것들에 쉽게 싫증을 느낀다는 사례를 제시합니다. (A)에서 결론적으로 인간은 쉽게 지루해하며, 그 원인이 자극에 대한 반응을 줄이도록 설계된 신경 세포에 있다고 설명합니다. (C)에서는 동시에 이 신경 세포들이 변화하는 것(예: 나무 속의 퓨마)에 대한 반응은 강화하며, 이것이 생존 가치가 높았기 때문에 진화한 방식이라고 설명합니다. (B)에서 이러한 지루함(신경 흥분 수준을 낮추는 것)이 새로운 자극을 더 돋보이게 만든다는 점을 보충 설명하며 마무리합니다. 따라서 적절한 순서는 (A)-(C)-(B)입니다.

questions.question: 32. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. (A) This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. (B) Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? (C) The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. (E) Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. (E) They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused or not going to be used in the near future.
questions.insertion_sentence: You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of clarity.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 쓸모없는 물건을 버릴 때 약간의 슬픔을 느낄 수 있지만 곧 명료함의 기쁨에 의해 극복될 것이라는 내용입니다. (C) 뒤에서 미니멀리즘이 감정을 해치지 않는다고 언급한 후, 미니멀리스트들이 현대의 모든 편의를 버리라고 주장하지 않는다는 내용이 나오기 전, 즉 감정적인 부분(슬픔)이 언급되고 그것이 기쁨으로 바뀐다는 구체적인 설명이 들어갈 위치는 (D)가 적절합니다. (원문 텍스트에 (D) 기호가 누락되어 있으나 문맥상 (C)와 (E) 사이의 흐름을 보충하는 위치인 ④번 위치가 답이 됩니다.)

questions.question: 33. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 본문에 있는 단어만 활용하여 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
questions.summary_sentence: The decline in the diversity of our food is not the work of nature, but an (A)______________. (우리 식량의 다양성이 감소하는 것은 자연의 산물이 아니라, 전적으로 인간이 만든 과정이다.) Although super-productive grains made their contributions, loss of diversity also involves risks. When it comes to disasters, (B)______________, (C)______________ they have. (재해에 관해서는 작물들이 더 획일적일수록, 그것들의 생존 가능성이 더 작아진다.)
subjective_conditions:  본문에 있는 단어만 사용할 것
 주어진 우리말과 같도록 쓸 것
 단어 수를 지킬 것
questions.answer: (A) entirely human-made process(B) the more uniform crops are(C) the smaller chance of survival
questions.explanation: (A) 본문의 첫 문장에서 'entirely human-made process'를 찾아 쓸 수 있습니다.(B), (C) 'the + 비교급, the + 비교급' 구문을 사용하여 '작물들이 더 획일적일수록 생존 가능성이 더 작아진다'는 의미를 완성해야 합니다. 본문의 'more uniform crops'와 'greater chance of not being able to survive'를 변형하여 'the more uniform crops are', 'the smaller chance of survival'로 작성합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of ___________________________________.
options: ① turning off a front door light to see the fireflies
② quieting the nearby noises to focus on a whisper
③ heavily seasoning a soup to appreciate the taste of tofu
④ softening the surrounding scents to notice the aroma of jasmine
⑤ dimming the brightness around a rainbow to better see its colors
questions.explanation: 지문은 뇌가 반복되는 자극에 대한 반응을 줄임으로써(지루함), 새로운 자극이나 변화하는 자극이 더 돋보이게 만든다는 신경학적 원리를 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸은 이러한 '배경 자극을 줄여서 타겟을 강조하는 현상'에 대한 비유를 찾는 것입니다. 1, 2, 4, 5번은 모두 주변의 자극(빛, 소음, 향기, 밝기)을 줄여서 원하는 대상(반딧불이, 속삭임, 자스민 향, 무지개)을 돋보이게 하는 적절한 비유입니다. 하지만 3번은 '두부 맛을 느끼기 위해 수프에 간을 세게 하는 것'으로, 오히려 배경 자극(수프 간)을 강화하여 본래의 맛(두부)을 가릴 수 있으므로 글의 맥락과 반대됩니다.
options_translation: 반딧불이를 보기 위해 현관 등불을 끄는 것
속삭임에 집중하기 위해 주변 소음을 줄이는 것
두부의 맛을 음미하기 위해 수프에 간을 강하게 하는 것
자스민 향을 알아차리기 위해 주변 향기를 완화하는 것
무지개의 색을 더 잘 보기 위해 주변의 밝기를 어둡게 하는 것

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between cultural and genetic processes. These models borrowed concepts from theoretical population genetics and applied them to the study of culture. For example, cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection were compared to genetic processes such as transmission, mutation, and selection. However, these models required adjustments to reflect the unique characteristics of cultural transmission. ⓐUnlike genetic inheritance, cultural transmission does not strictly follow genetic rules. ⓑFor instance, when biological parents possess different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not equally likely to adopt either the mother's or the father's version. ⓒAdditionally, cultural traits are not exclusively inherited from parents. ⓓIt is out of the question for children to acquire cultural traits from peers or other adults outside their family. ⓔTherefore, the frequency of a cultural trait in the population is relevant beyond just the probability that an individual's parents had that trait. These differences show why genetic ideas need to be adjusted when studying cultural evolution.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 문화적 진화와 유전적 진화의 유사점을 바탕으로 하되, 문화 전승만이 가진 고유한 특징(부모 외의 타인에게서도 학습 가능함 등)으로 인해 유전학적 모델의 수정이 필요하다는 내용입니다. ⓓ는 '아이들이 가족 이외의 또래나 다른 성인으로부터 문화적 특성을 습득하는 것은 불가능하다(out of the question)'는 내용인데, 이는 문화적 특성이 부모로부터만 전수되지 않는다는 앞선 문장(ⓒ) 및 글 전체의 논지와 정반대되는 내용입니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글을 읽고 학생들이 작성한 (A)~(E) 중 글의 내용을 잘못 이해한 학생은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product, enhancing its value or utility. For instance, popcorn complements the movie watching experience, while travel pillows improve comfort on long plane journeys. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. For example, the popularity of smartphones has driven demand for accessories like phone cases and chargers. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status - they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a light-bulb or printers and ink cartridges. However, not all complementary goods are essential. For instance, while gasoline is crucial for traditional cars, the rise of electric vehicles shows that customers have alternatives.
options: ① (A): Gasoline, though essential for traditional cars, is losing importance with the rise of electric vehicles.
② (B): Printers and their specific ink cartridges are classic examples of perfectly complementary goods.
③ (C): Travel pillows make long flights more comfortable, showing how complementary goods add value.
④ (D): Understanding trends in complementary goods can help companies predict customer needs.
⑤ (E): Not all complementary goods are vital, as alternatives can enhance reliance on them.
questions.explanation: 본문 마지막 부분에서 보완재가 필수적이지 않은 경우, 고객들이 대안(alternatives)을 가질 수 있다고 언급하고 있습니다. 대안이 있다는 것은 특정 보완재에 대한 의존도(reliance)를 높이는 것이 아니라 오히려 낮추거나 분산시키는 결과를 가져옵니다. 따라서 대안이 의존도를 높일 수 있다는 (E)의 진술은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① (A): 휘발유는 전통적인 자동차에 필수적이지만, 전기 자동차의 부상으로 중요성을 잃고 있다.
② (B): 프린터와 전용 잉크 카트리지는 완전 보완재의 전형적인 예시이다.
③ (C): 여행용 베개는 장거리 비행을 더 편안하게 만들어주며, 보완재가 어떻게 가치를 더하는지 보여준다.
④ (D): 보완재의 추세를 이해하는 것은 기업들이 고객의 요구를 예측하는 데 도움을 줄 수 있다.
⑤ (E): 모든 보완재가 필수적인 것은 아니며, 대안이 그것들에 대한 의존도를 높일 수 있다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cezanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.summary_sentence: Color emerges from the (A)__________ between light and vision, bridging (B)__________ properties with the subjective processes of human (C)__________.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 색이 사물의 객관적 속성이면서 동시에 관찰자의 주관적 해석의 결과라는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 색은 빛과 시각 사이의 '상호작용(interaction)'에서 발생하며, '물리적(physical)' 속성과 인간의 주관적 '인식(perception)'을 연결한다는 요약이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 연결 - 내부의 - 해석
② 차별/구별 - 객관적인 - 이해
③ 관계 - 추상적인 - 관찰
④ 상호작용 - 물리적인 - 인식
⑤ 상호작용 - 가상의 - 의식

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.*pest: 해충
options: ① The greatest decline in crop diversity occurred before World War II.
② Numerous traditional crop varieties were switched to few highly efficient modern varieties.
③ Grain production tripled as a result of the strategy to increase crop yields.
④ There is a risk that uniform crops are more vulnerable to disasters
⑤ A food system that relies on a limited selection of crops is more susceptible to disease, pests, and extreme climate conditions.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 작물 다양성의 가장 큰 손실은 제2차 세계 대전 '이후(followed)' 수십 년 동안 발생했다고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 전쟁 '이전(before)'에 발생했다는 ①번 선택지는 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 작물 다양성의 가장 큰 감소는 제2차 세계 대전 이전에 일어났다.
② 수많은 전통 작물 품종들이 소수의 고효율 현대 품종으로 교체되었다.
③ 작물 수확량을 늘리기 위한 전략의 결과로 곡물 생산량이 세 배로 늘어났다.
④ 단일한 작물이 재난에 더 취약할 위험이 있다.
⑤ 제한된 작물 선택에 의존하는 식품 시스템은 질병, 해충, 극한 기후 조건에 더 취약하다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The adolescent brain is not fully developed ⓐ<u>until</u> its early twenties. This means the way the adolescents' decision-making circuits integrate and process information may put them at a disadvantage. One of their brain regions that matures later is the prefrontal cortex, ⓑ<u>that</u> is the control center, tasked with thinking ahead and evaluating consequences. It is the area of the brain responsible for preventing you from sending off an initial angry text and ⓒ<u>modifying</u> it with kinder words. On the other hand, the limbic system matures earlier, playing a central role in processing emotional responses. Because of ⓓ<u>its</u> earlier development, it is more likely to influence decision-making. Decision-making in the adolescent brain is led by emotional factors more than the perception of consequences. Due to these differences, ⓔ<u>there</u> is an imbalance between feeling-based decision-making ruled by the more mature limbic system and logical-based decision-making by the not-yet-mature prefrontal cortex. This may explain why some teens are more likely to make bad decisions.*integrate: 통합하다 **limbic system: 대뇌변연계***prefrontal cortex: 전전두엽 피질
questions.explanation: ⓑ 'that'은 선행사인 'the prefrontal cortex'를 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 자리에 쓰였습니다. 관계대명사 'that'은 계속적 용법(콤마 뒤)으로 사용할 수 없으므로, 이를 'which'로 바꾸어야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, _________________________ ___________. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.*externality: 외부 효과 **fractionalization: 분열
options: ① natives could embrace diversity as a symbol of social progress
② a cultural diversity might promote social integration and harmony
③ cultural differences might lead to economic growth and innovation
④ native residents might consider cultural variety as an unfavorable trait
⑤ the native population might adjust to multicultural environments naturally
questions.explanation: 이 글은 문화적 다양성이 생산성과 삶의 질에 미치는 영향을 다루고 있습니다. 빈칸 앞부분은 문화적 다양성을 가치 있게 여기는 긍정적인 측면을 언급한 반면, 빈칸을 포함한 뒷부분은 'On the other hand'로 시작하며 타민족을 차별하거나 갈등을 두려워하는 부정적인 측면을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 원주민들이 문화적 다양성을 좋지 않은 특성으로 여길 수 있다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 원주민들은 다양성을 사회적 진보의 상징으로 받아들일 수 있다
문화적 다양성은 사회 통합과 조화를 증진할 수 있다
문화적 차이는 경제 성장과 혁신으로 이어질 수 있다
원주민 거주자들은 문화적 다양성을 바람직하지 않은 특성으로 간주할 수도 있다
원주민 인구는 다문화 환경에 자연스럽게 적응할 수도 있다

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 39번]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. This suggests that ___________________________________.
options: ① the process of learning through childhood experiences enables animals to adapt more effectively to environmental changes
② the less time animals spend learning as children, the more adaptable they become to changes
③ the genetic information passed down through generations proves to be more reliable than learned behaviors
④ what animals learn during their childhood period might become outdated information in the future.
⑤ the migration patterns of birds are primarily inherited rather than learned behaviors
questions.explanation: 지문은 어린 시절을 보내며 환경에 대해 배우는 동물들이 유전적 정보(하드웨어)에만 의존하는 동물들보다 더 유연하고 적응력이 높다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 특히 긴 유년기를 가지거나 부모로부터 배우는 새들이 변화하는 환경에 더 효율적으로 이동한다는 사례를 통해, 유년기 경험을 통한 학습이 환경 변화에 대한 적응력을 높여준다는 점을 시사합니다. 따라서 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 어린 시절의 경험을 통한 학습 과정은 동물들이 환경 변화에 더 효과적으로 적응할 수 있게 한다
② 동물들이 어린 시절에 학습하는 시간이 적을수록 변화에 더 잘 적응하게 된다
③ 세대를 통해 전해 내려오는 유전 정보가 학습된 행동보다 더 신뢰할 만하다는 것이 증명된다
④ 동물들이 유년기 동안 배우는 것은 미래에 시대에 뒤떨어진 정보가 될 수도 있다
⑤ 새들의 이동 패턴은 학습된 행동이라기보다는 주로 유전되는 것이다

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 문맥을 고려하여 빈칸에 들어갈 말이 무엇인지 <보기>에서 주어진 단어들만을 한 번씩 모두 사용하여 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오. [23년 11월 29번]
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. To ensure fairness and consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly _________________________________.
subjective_conditions: ㆍ<보기>의 표현만을 사용할 것
ㆍ빈칸에 들어갈 말을 10단어로 작성할 것
ㆍ필요한 경우 어형 변화(동사 형태를 변화시키거나 단어의 단수와 복수를 변형하는 것)는 가능하나, 단어 추가 및 삭제 불가
questions.answer: identical to those used for determining the deaths of non-donors
questions.explanation: 이 글은 장기 기증 후보자의 뇌사 판정 기준이 일반인(비기증자)의 사망 판정 기준과 다를 때 발생하는 대중의 불신을 다루고 있습니다. 공정성과 일관성을 보장하기 위해, 장기 기증자의 사망 판정 기준은 비기증자의 사망을 판정하기 위해 사용되는 기준과 '동일해야' 한다는 맥락이 되어야 합니다. 'identical to'(~와 동일한) 구문을 사용하고, 'those'가 앞의 'criteria'를 가리키도록 하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글을 읽고 A의 빈칸에 들어갈 답을 쓰시오. [23년 11월 31번]
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristic of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself. Psychologist George M. Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment. Stratton wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally turned the world upside down for him. In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him. With time, however, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated. As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems: he used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something, for example. Fortunately, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for the rest of his life. For him, everything returned to normal after one day.*reverse: 뒤집다, 반전시키다
subjective_conditions: 본문의 단어(adapt, the visual system, glasses, reversing)를 모두 사용할 것
9단어 이하로 작성할 것
완전한 문장으로 작성할 것
필요한 경우 어형 변화 가능
questions.subjective_answer_format: Q. According to the text, what happened when Stratton used the reversing glasses for several days?A. ___________________ and restored normal perception.정답: ___________________________________________________
questions.answer: The visual system adapted to the reversing glasses gradually
questions.explanation: 글의 내용은 시각 체계의 적응 능력을 설명하고 있습니다. Stratton이 반전 안경을 썼을 때 시각 체계가 점진적으로 그 새로운 자극에 적응했다는 점이 핵심입니다. 조건에 명시된 단어들을 사용하여 '시각 체계가 반전 안경에 점진적으로 적응했다'는 문장을 완성하면 'The visual system adapted to the reversing glasses gradually'가 됩니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.Q. What does Frans de Waal criticize about the way scientists describe animal behaviors?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
subjective_conditions: 본문의 단어(scientists, employ, technical language, distance, animals)를 모두 사용할 것
9~11단어로 작성할 것
완전한 문장으로 작성할 것
필요한 경우 어형 변화 가능
questions.answer: Scientists employ technical language to distance themselves from other animals.
questions.explanation: Frans de Waal은 과학자들이 인간과 동물의 거리를 두기 위해 전문 용어를 사용하는 것을 비판합니다. 조건의 단어들을 사용하여 문장을 구성하면 'Scientists employ technical language to distance (themselves) from animals.' 형태가 됩니다. 9~11단어 조건에 맞춰 작성하면 'Scientists employ technical language to distance themselves from other animals.'(10단어) 등이 정답이 될 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly everything has to go through your mouth to get to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and prevent it from harm - with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. From the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and a reflection of what is happening in other parts of the body. Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease that affects the entire body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, posing serious health risks.
options: ① 건강하지 않은 입을 통해 신체로 들어간 음식은 소화 계통에 부정적인 영향을 줄 수 있다.
② 구강 건강은 삶의 모든 측면에 영향을 미치므로 건강하게 유지하는 것이 중요하다.
③ 건강을 위해 규칙적인 운동과 건강한 식습관의 중요성을 강조해야 한다.
④ 구강 건강에 대한 인식 부족 문제를 해결할 방안을 마련해야 한다.
⑤ 신체의 면역 체계가 바이러스와 싸우는 방식을 이해해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 본문은 입이 우리 몸의 다른 부분으로 연결되는 통로이며, 구강 건강이 전신 건강과 직결된다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 구강 건강의 중요성을 강조하는 ②번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of clarity. Minimalists never argue that you should leave all comforts of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that will be ____________ in the near future.
questions.explanation: 미니멀리즘에 대한 오해를 풀며, 미니멀리스트들이 제거하라고 하는 것은 모든 현대적 편의가 아니라 불필요한 것들임을 설명하고 있습니다. 앞 문장에서 'useless item'을 제거한다고 언급한 것과 일맥상통하는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 유용한
② 편리한
③ 장식적인
④ 매우 귀중한
⑤ 불필요한

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. (A) They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. (B) Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. (C) They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else. (D) They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. (E) Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.insertion_sentence: Both positions are, in a way, correct.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부는 색이 사물의 객관적 속성이라는 견해(A)를 설명하고, 중반부는 색이 관찰자의 마음속에만 존재한다는 상반된 견해(B, C, D)를 설명합니다. 주어진 문장 'Both positions are, in a way, correct(두 입장 모두 어느 정도 맞다)'는 이 상반된 두 견해를 절충하는 문장으로, 색이 객관적이면서도 주관적이라는 결론을 내리는 (E) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristic of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself. Psychologist George M. Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment. Stratton wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally turned the world upside down for him. In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him. With time, however, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated. As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems: he used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something, for example. Fortunately, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for the rest of his life. For him, everything returned to normal after one day.
options: ① The Adaptability of the Visual System
② New Stimuli: The Crucial Factor for Perception
③ The Challenges of Adapting to Reversing Glasses
④ The Most Efficient Way to View the World Upside Down
⑤ George M. Stratton: The Pioneer of an Experiment with Reversing Glasses
questions.explanation: 이 글은 조지 스트래튼의 반전 안경 실험을 통해 시각 체계가 새로운 환경이나 자극에 적응하는 능력을 가지고 있음을 보여줍니다. 따라서 '시각 체계의 적응성(The Adaptability of the Visual System)'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 시각 체계의 적응성
② 새로운 자극: 지각의 핵심 요소
③ 반전 안경에 적응하는 것의 어려움
④ 세상을 거꾸로 보는 가장 효율적인 방법
⑤ 조지 스트래튼: 반전 안경 실험의 선구자

questions.question: 14. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. ⓐThey all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. ⓑSo how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? ⓒPlato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. ⓓModern physics continues to explore the interactions of particles, while the structure of the Forms or universals remains a question for philosophy. ⓔPlato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 플라톤의 실재론(Realism)과 '형상(Forms)'에 대한 개념을 설명하고 있습니다. 우리가 현실 세계에서 보는 원은 불완전하지만, 보이지 않는 완벽한 세계에 '완벽한 원'의 형상이 존재한다는 논지입니다. ⓓ번 문장은 현대 물리학의 입자 상호작용에 대해 언급하고 있는데, 이는 플라톤의 철학적 형상 이론이라는 글의 전체적인 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions. But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more ___________ than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
questions.explanation: 이 연구는 인터넷 검색을 통해 정보를 얻은 사람들이 그렇지 않은 사람들보다 자신의 지적 능력에 대해 더 높은 자신감을 갖게 된다는 점을 보여줍니다. 첫 번째 단계에서 인터넷을 사용한 사람들은 자신들과 직접적인 관련이 없는 새로운 질문에 대해서도 자신이 더 '박식하다(knowledgeable)'고 평가했습니다. 마지막 문장의 '지적 자신감(intellectual confidence)'을 높인다는 단서와 가장 잘 부합하는 단어는 4번입니다.
options_translation: 평범한
사려 깊은
공격적인
박식한
이해할 수 없는

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
options: ② where octopuses live in the sea
③ when octopuses hide themselves and appear
④ the relationship between octopuses and humans
⑤ the ability of octopuses to disguise for survival
questions.explanation: 이 글은 문어가 자신의 색깔과 패턴을 바꾸는 능력(변장)을 사용하여 다른 생물(가자미, 바다뱀 등)로 위장함으로써 자신을 보호하고 사냥하는 법에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 생존을 위해 위장하는 문어의 능력입니다.
options_translation: ① 문어의 다양한 종들
② 문어가 바다 어디에 사는지
③ 문어가 언제 숨고 나타나는지
④ 문어와 인간 사이의 관계
⑤ 생존을 위해 위장하는 문어의 능력

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The greatest ⓐ<u>reduction</u> of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from ⓑ<u>severe</u> hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly ⓒ<u>well</u>, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more ⓓ<u>varied</u> crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that counts on just a ⓔ<u>narrow</u> selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
questions.explanation: 전체 글의 흐름은 식량 다양성이 줄어들고 소수의 다수확 품종에 의존하게 된 위험성을 설명하고 있습니다. ⓓ번 앞뒤 문맥을 보면, 식량 다양성을 줄이고 소수의 품종에 의존하는 전략이 재난에 취약하다고 설명하고 있으므로, '더 다양한(varied)' 농작물을 만드는 위험이 아니라 '더 획일화된(uniform)' 농작물을 만드는 것이 위험하다는 내용이 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)recode what we see의 의미와 다른 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We (A)<u>recode what we see</u> through the lens of everything we know. We ⓐ<u>reconstruct memories</u> rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like ⓑ<u>an optimal image compression algorithm</u> such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and ⓒ<u>remember everything in perfect detail</u> struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But ⓓ<u>representing the world as abstract ideas and features</u> comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we ⓔ<u>see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences</u>. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: (A) '우리가 보는 것을 재부호화한다'는 것은 정보를 있는 그대로 저장하는 것이 아니라 교육, 지식, 가정 등을 통해 추상화하거나 재구성하여 저장한다는 의미입니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 이러한 정보의 압축, 재구성, 추상적 표현과 관련된 내용인 반면, ⓒ '모든 것을 완벽하게 세부적으로 기억하는 것'은 재부호화 능력이 부족한 경우를 설명하는 대조적인 개념입니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration.
ordered_passages: (A) But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision.

(B) In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs.
(C) As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 뇌사 판정 기준을 강화하는 국가들에 대해 언급합니다. (B)에서는 구체적인 예시로 여러 유럽 국가의 법적 요건(의사 팀의 합의)과 그 이유(대중의 두려움 완화)를 설명합니다. (A)에서는 'But'을 통해 이러한 요건들이 오히려 대중의 의구심을 자아내고 뇌사 판정이 부정확하다는 잘못된 믿음을 유지시킨다고 반박합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 일관성의 문제로서 장기 기증자의 사망 진단 기준은 일반적인 경우와 같아야 한다는 결론적 주장을 제시하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In statistics, the law of large numbers describes a situation where having more data ____________________. According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to match the true state of the world. For instance, on your first encounter with the game of roulette, you may have beginner's luck after betting on 7. But the more often you repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning, meaning that your luck will at some point fade away. Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to balance individual losses.
options: ③ enables people to conceal public preferences
④ means giving the information of drivers to car insurers
⑤ is unrelated to the frequency of wins and losses in games.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 '대수의 법칙(law of large numbers)'을 설명하고 있습니다. 데이터가 많아질수록 결과의 평균이 실제 상태에 더 가까워진다는 내용을 통해, 데이터가 많을수록 더 정확한 예측(forecast)을 할 수 있게 된다는 결론을 도출할 수 있습니다. 카지노와 보험 회사가 이 법칙을 활용하여 사고 발생 확률 등을 계산한다는 내용이 이를 뒷받침합니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들이 더 잘 예측하도록 돕는다
② 일어날 일을 경시한다
③ 사람들이 대중의 선호도를 숨길 수 있게 한다
④ 자동차 보험사에게 운전자의 정보를 제공하는 것을 의미한다
⑤ 게임에서의 승패 빈도와 관련이 없다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Despite the remarkable progress in deep-learning based facial recognition approaches in recent years, in terms of identification performance, they still have limitations. These limitations relate to the database used in the learning stage. If the selected database does no ⓐ<u>include</u> enough instances, the result may be systematically affected. For example, the performance of a facial biometric system may ⓑ<u>diminish</u> if the person to be identified was enrolled over 10 years ago. The factor to consider is that this person may experience changes in the texture of the face, particularly with the appearance of wrinkles and sagging skin. These changes may be ⓒ<u>understated</u> by weight gain or loss. To ⓓ<u>counteract</u> this problem, researchers have developed models for face aging or digital de-aging. It is used to ⓔ<u>make up for</u> the differences in facial characteristics, which appear over a given time period.
questions.explanation: 안면 인식 시스템의 한계에 관한 글입니다. 체중 증가나 감소는 얼굴의 주름이나 처진 피부와 같은 노화에 따른 변화를 '축소'시키는 것이 아니라 더 '두드러지게' 할 수 있으므로 'understated'(축소된)는 'exacerbated'(악화된)나 'highlighted'(강조된)와 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [23년 11월 22번]
questions.passage: When writing a novel, research for information needs ⓐ<u>to be done</u>. The thing is that some kinds of fiction demand a higher level of detail: crime fiction, for example, or scientific thrillers. The information is never ⓑ<u>hard to find</u>; one website for authors even organizes trips to police stations, so that crime writers can get it right. Often, a polite letter will earn you permission to visit a particular location and ⓒ<u>record</u> all the details that you need. But remember that you will drive your readers to boredom if you think that you need to pack everything you discover into your work. The details that ⓓ<u>matters</u> are those that reveal the human experience. The crucial thing is telling a story, ⓔ<u>finding</u> the characters, the tension, and the conflict - not the train timetable or the building blueprint.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'The details'로 복수 명사입니다. 따라서 관계대명사 that절 내의 동사는 선행사인 복수 명사 details와 수 일치를 이루어야 하므로, 단수 동사 matters가 아닌 복수 동사 matter로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 두 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 11월 33번]
questions.passage: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson suggests that we tend to understand the world by focusing in on particular features within it. Take platypuses. We might zoom in so closely to their fur that each hair appears different. We might also zoom out to the extent where it appears as a single, uniform object. We might take the platypus as an individual, or we might treat it as part of a larger unit such as a species or an ecosystem. It's possible to move between many of these perspectives, although we may need some additional tools and skills to zoom in on individual pieces of hair or zoom out to entire ecosystems. Crucially, however, we can only take up one perspective at a time. We can pay attention to the varied behavior of individual animals, look at what unites them into a single species, or look at them as part of bigger ecological patterns. Every possible perspective involves emphasizing certain aspects and ignoring others.
questions.summary_sentence: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson argues that we comprehend the world by adopting different perspectives each (A)_________ certain features while (B)_________ others. These can range from focusing on individual details to viewing larger systems, but we are (C)_________ to focus on only one viewpoint at a time.
questions.explanation: 지문은 우리가 세상을 이해할 때 특정 관점을 선택하여 어떤 부분은 강조(emphasizing/stressing)하고 다른 부분은 무시(ignoring/neglecting/excluding)하며, 중요한 점은 한 번에 하나의 관점만 취할 수 있다는 것입니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 '강조하다'인 highlighting 또는 stressing, (B)는 '배제하다/무시하다'인 excluding 또는 neglecting, (C)는 한 번에 하나만 가능하다는 맥락에서 '할 수 없다(unable)'가 가장 적절합니다. 본 지문의 마지막 문장 'emphasizing certain aspects and ignoring others'와 'can only take up one perspective at a time'을 통해 답을 유추할 수 있습니다. (제시된 답지 ①번의 allowed는 문맥상 '허용되다'이지만 지문에서 강조하는 '제한성'을 고려할 때 ⑤번의 unable이 더 명확한 답이 됩니다. 다만 보기 구성상 ①번이 '강조/배제'를 포함하므로 오타가 없다면 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.)
options_translation: ① 강조하면서 / 제외하면서 / 할 수 있는(허용된)
② 과소평가하면서 / 피하면서 / 묶여있는
③ 관찰하면서 / 인정하면서 / 제한된
④ 최소화하면서 / 알아차리면서 / 무제한의
⑤ 강조하면서 / 소홀히 하면서 / 할 수 없는

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말과 일치하도록 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오. [23년 11월 39번]
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants. (A)<u>그들의 운동 재능이 뛰어났을 뿐만 아니라</u> but the Cubans also appeared even stronger from just the colour of their uniforms. A game would not even start and the opposing team would already be scared. A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time. The country that ruled international baseball for decades has not been on top since that uniform change. Traditions are important for a team; while a team brand or image can adjust to keep up with present times, if it abandons or neglects its roots, negative effects can surface.
subjective_conditions: - <보기>의 모든 단어를 한 번씩만 사용하여 구문을 완성할 것
- <보기>의 단어 중 'be'만 어형을 변형할 것
- 부정어구 도치구문으로 쓸 것
vocabulary_box: be / athletic talents / not only / their / superior
questions.answer: Not only were their athletic talents superior
questions.explanation: 부정어구 'Not only'가 문두에 오면 주어와 동사가 도치됩니다. 주어가 복수인 'their athletic talents'이므로 be동사는 과거형인 'were'로 변형되어 'Not only were their athletic talents superior'가 됩니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Regular attendance at school is essential in maximizing student potential. Recently, we′ve become concerned about the number of unapproved absences across all grades. I would like to further clarify that your role as a parent is to approve any school absence. Parents must provide an explanation for absences to the school within 7 days from the first day of any period of absence. Where an explanation has not been received within the 7-day time frame, the school will record the absence as unjustified on the student′s record. Please ensure that you go to the parent portal site and register the reason any time your child is absent. Please approve all absences, so that your child will not be at a disadvantage. Many thanks for your cooperation.
options: ② 학교 출결 시스템의 변경을 알려주려고
③ 결석계 제출 기간이 최대 7일까지임을 안내하려고
④ 자녀가 지각하지 않도록 부모의 지도를 당부하려고
⑤ 자녀의 결석 사유를 학교에 등록하도록 요청하려고
questions.explanation: 이 글은 학교에서 학부모에게 보내는 공지문으로, 학생이 결석했을 경우 학부모가 7일 이내에 학교 포털 사이트를 통해 직접 결석 사유를 등록해 줄 것을 요청하고 있습니다. 이를 통해 자녀가 출결 기록에서 불이익을 받지 않도록 협조를 구하는 내용이므로 정답은 ⑤번입니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race - their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't psychologically suffer much. In fact, ultra-marathon runners - those people who are crazy enough to push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50-100km or more over many hours, talk about making friends with their pain. When a patient has paid for some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it, the patient calls that good pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.
options: ① 심리적 고통의 정도는 어떠한 방법으로도 조절할 수 없다.
② 감정에 대한 집착을 버려야만 삶의 고통으로부터 벗어날 수 있다.
③ 일상에서 반복되는 심리적 고통은 사람들에게 강박을 갖게 만든다.
④ 마라톤 선수들은 육체적 고통보다 정신적 고통에 취약하다.
⑤ 고통은 어떻게 인식하고 받아들이느냐에 따라 심리적 고통의 정도가 달라진다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 육체적인 고통을 마음속에서 어떻게 구성(frame)하느냐에 따라 심리적으로 느끼는 고통의 크기가 달라진다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 마라톤 선수들이나 치료를 받는 환자의 사례를 통해 고통에 부여하는 가치와 인식의 중요성을 강조하고 있으므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
options: ① The Role of Deliberation in Enhancing Eyewitness Testimony
② Trusting Your Gut: The Surprising Accuracy of First Impressions
③ The Impact of Malcolm Gladwell's 'Blink' on Legal Procedures
④ Why Logical Reasoning Always Outperforms First Impressions
questions.explanation: 이 글은 신중한 심사숙고나 논리적 정당화보다 무의식적인 첫인상이나 직관적인 반응이 더 정확할 수 있다는 연구 결과들을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 ② '직관을 믿어라: 첫인상의 놀라운 정확성'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 목격자 증언을 강화하는 데 있어 심사숙고의 역할
② 직관을 믿어라: 첫인상의 놀라운 정확성
③ Malcolm Gladwell의 'Blink'가 법적 절차에 미친 영향
④ 논리적 추론이 항상 첫인상보다 나은 성과를 내는 이유

questions.question: 7. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The graph illustrates electricity generation in 2023 across four countries, categorized by fossil fuels, nuclear energy, and renewables. ⓐIn Australia, electricity is produced solely from fossil fuels and renewables, with the proportion of fossil fuels being over twice that of renewables. ⓑThe United States has the highest proportion of electricity generation from nuclear energy among the four countries. ⓒThe proportion of electricity generated from fossil fuels in the U.S. exceeds that of the U.K., and the same trend applies to electricity generated from renewables. ⓓIn the U.K., the proportion of electricity from nuclear energy is less than one-third of that generated from renewables. ⓔIn Brazil, the share of electricity generation from renewables is 10 percentage points higher than the combined share in Australia and the U.K.
questions.explanation: 제시된 지문의 내용 중 ⓒ번 문장에서 미국의 화석 연료 발전 비중이 영국의 그것보다 높다는 것과 재생 에너지 발전 비중에서도 동일한 경향(미국이 영국보다 높음)이 적용된다고 설명하고 있으나, 실제 통계 수치상 영국의 재생 에너지 비중이 미국보다 높으므로 이 문장은 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is ⓐ<u>enormous</u>. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a ⓑ<u>limited</u> number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic ⓒ<u>expanding</u> of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a ⓓ<u>small</u> number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is ⓔ<u>true</u> also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.*embryo: 배아 **physiological: 생리적인
questions.explanation: 이 글은 생명체가 수많은 상호작용 속에서도 안정성을 유지하기 위해 소수의 정해진 상태로 수렴한다는 '운하화(canalization)'를 설명하고 있습니다. 인간 배아 발달 과정에서 결과물이 무한히 늘어나는 것이 아니라 특정 조직과 신체 형태로 제한되는 과정을 설명하고 있으므로, outcomes의 ⓒ 'expanding(확장)'은 문맥상 'narrowing(좁혀짐)' 또는 'funneling(깔때기처럼 모임)'과 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. ⓐIt was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. ⓑOctopus sashimi is so delicious that it gives people the illusion of eating flounder. ⓒAn octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. ⓓMany more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. ⓔAnd while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.explanation: 문어의 뛰어난 위장 능력(넙치 등으로 변신)에 대해 설명하는 글입니다. ⓑ번 문장은 문어 회가 너무 맛있어서 넙치를 먹는 듯한 착각을 준다는 내용으로, 생물의 생존 및 모방 전략을 다루는 전체 흐름과 전혀 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods.
ordered_passages: (A) If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one.

(B) The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.

(C) But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price.
questions.explanation: 소비재에 왜 세 가지 버전이 존재하는지 그 이유를 설명하는 글입니다. (A)에서 한 가지 버전일 때의 문제점과 두 가지 버전일 때 소비자가 저렴한 것을 선택하는 경향을 설명합니다. (C)에서 'But'과 함께 세 번째(가장 비싼) 모델을 도입했을 때 두 번째 모델의 매출이 올라가는 현상을 제시합니다. (B)에서 그 결과 소비자들이 가장 비싼 모델 때문에 조종당해 중간 가격의 제품을 선택하게 된다는 결론으로 마무리하는 (A)-(C)-(B) 순서가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. (A) In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. (B) In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. (C) Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. (D) The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. (E) Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
questions.insertion_sentence: This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 뇌의 화학 물질 불균형이 우울증의 원인이 아니라 '결과'라고 설명하고 있습니다. (A) 뒤에 이어지는 문장이 'In other words(다시 말해서)'로 시작하며 우울증이 뇌 물질의 감소를 '유발'한다는 역전된 인과관계를 부연 설명하고 있으므로, 주어진 문장은 (A) 위치에 들어가 기존의 믿음에 대한 문제점을 구체화하는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. (A) A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. (B) Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. (C) Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. (D) Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" (E) Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.*procrastinator: 미루는 사람
questions.insertion_sentence: But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer.
questions.explanation: (B)와 (C)에서 사람들이 '슬픈' 횟수를 기억하는 것은 부정확할 수 있고 주관적일 수 있다는 문제점을 제기했습니다. 주어진 문장은 'But'으로 시작하며 병가를 낼 정도로 슬펐던 횟수를 묻는 것이 구체적인 답변을 끌어낸다는 대안을 제시합니다. 이는 (D) 문장의 'Similarly' 이하에 나오는 '미루는 습관에 대해 등급을 매기게 하는 대신 구체적인 공공요금 체납 횟수를 묻는 것'과 논리적 구조가 동일합니다. 따라서 주어진 문장은 (D) 위치에 들어가서 추상적인 질문의 문제점 뒤에 구체적인 질문의 이점을 먼저 설명하는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Alvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
questions.summary_sentence: Considering that trick-punishments can inadvertently (A)__________ undesirable behavior of a child, (B)__________ positive actions is a more effective approach for parents.
questions.explanation: 본문은 '속임수 처벌(trick-punishments)'이 아이의 바람직하지 않은 행동을 오히려 장려(encourage)할 수 있음을 지적합니다. 외로운 아이에게 꾸지람은 무관심보다 낫기 때문입니다. 따라서 부정적인 면을 지적하기보다는 긍정적인 행동을 할 때 칭찬(praising)하거나 보상하는 것이 더 효과적이라는 결론을 내립니다. (A)에는 undesirable behavior를 조장한다는 의미의 encourage(혹은 reinforce, promote)가, (B)에는 긍정적 행동에 대한 보상을 의미하는 praising이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 촉진하다 - 방치하는 것
② 강화하다 - 무시하는 것
③ 장려하다 - 칭찬하는 것
④ 제거하다 - 낙담시키는 것
⑤ 줄이다 - 촉진하는 것

questions.question: 10. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically ⓐ<u>break it up</u> into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We (A)___________________ rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information ─ a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People ⓑ<u>who lack</u> this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between ⓒ<u>what they have</u> learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. (가)<u>우리의 편견이 우리의 지각을 왜곡한 채로</u>. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than ⓓ<u>is playing</u> back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: 지문은 우리가 본 것을 그대로 기억하는 것이 아니라 교육받은 개념이나 지식의 렌즈를 통해 정보를 효율적으로 재부호화하여 저장한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 기억을 있는 그대로 인출하기보다는 '재구성한다(reconstruct memories)'는 표현이 들어가는 것이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 사실을 닦아내다
현실을 삭제하다
기억을 재구성하다
정보를 과장하다
모든 세부 사항을 다시 쓰다
