questions.question: 13. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 낱말의 쓰임이 옳지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay ⓐ<u>hidden</u> as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they ⓑ<u>saw</u> at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes ⓒ<u>fixed</u> upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been ⓓ<u>found</u> since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt ─ ⓔ<u>producing</u> the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 문맥상 문어가 다른 생물로 위장하는 희귀한 사례를 설명하고 있습니다. 원문(24년 10월 31번)의 맥락상 ⓓ가 포함된 문장은 이러한 변신 능력이 매우 드물게 관찰되었음을 의미해야 하므로, found(발견된) 보다는 '관찰되지 않은(unobserved)'이나 '드문'의 의미가 오는 것이 흐름상 적절한 경우가 많으나, 원문 변형 여부를 확인했을 때 ⓓ자리에 original text는 'few more' 형태를 취하여 부정적 의미를 담고 있을 가능성이 큽니다. 여기서는 ⓓ가 지칭하는 바가 문맥상 오류를 포함하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 14. 윗글의 octopuses에 관한 내용으로 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay ⓐ<u>hidden</u> as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they ⓑ<u>saw</u> at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes ⓒ<u>fixed</u> upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been ⓓ<u>found</u> since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt ─ ⓔ<u>producing</u> the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
options: ① They hide at night and hunt during the day.
② They can entice predators using their both eyes.
③ They can mimic other creatures, such as flounders.
④ They posses dangerous venom, which can be fatal.
⑤ They use their arms to grab and hunt sea snakes.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 문어가 넙치(flounder)로 보이게 하거나 바다뱀(sea snakes)으로 변신하는 것처럼 보인다는 내용이 언급되어 있으므로 ③번이 일치합니다. ①은 밤에 사냥한다고 했으므로 틀렸고, ④와 ⑤는 지문에 언급되지 않은 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 그들은 밤에 숨고 낮에 사냥한다.
② 그들은 두 눈을 사용하여 포식자를 유혹할 수 있다.
③ 그들은 넙치와 같은 다른 생물들을 흉내 낼 수 있다.
④ 그들은 치명적일 수 있는 위험한 독을 가지고 있다.
⑤ 그들은 바다뱀을 잡고 사냥하기 위해 팔을 사용한다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Onscreen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre ─ indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer something far away, ___________________________________________________.
options: ① people will stop caring about it
② it will only affect the poorest regions
③ it will become a part of our daily reality
④ it will be too late to do anything about it
⑤ it will be a problem only for future generations
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화가 삶의 주변부 문제일 때는 소설이나 영화 같은 '이야기'의 소재가 될 수 있지만, 기온이 더 올라가서 모든 사람이 그 영향을 직접 피부로 느끼게 되면(창밖으로 기후 재앙이 보일 정도로 일상이 되면) 더 이상 이야기가 될 수 없다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 기후 변화가 더 이상 '멀리 있는 무언가'가 아니게 될 때, 그것은 우리의 일상적인 현실의 일부가 될 것이라는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들이 그것에 대해 관심을 끄게 될 것이다
② 그것은 오직 가장 가난한 지역들에만 영향을 미칠 것이다
③ 그것은 우리 일상 현실의 일부가 될 것이다
④ 어떤 조치를 취하기에는 너무 늦을 것이다
⑤ 그것은 오직 미래 세대에게만 문제가 될 것이다

A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it ⓑ<u>encourages</u> them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling ⓒ<u>ignored,</u> so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time.The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to ⓓ<u>reward</u> the positives. In this way, any parent can ⓔ<u>avoid </u>trick-punishments.
questions.explanation: 지문의 흐름상 처벌이 오히려 아이의 잘못된 행동을 유도하는 '속임수 처벌'이 될 수 있다고 설명하므로, 첫 번째 문장에서 처벌이 '효과적(effective)'이라는 말은 문맥에 맞지 않습니다. '비효율적(ineffective)'이나 '해로울 수 있다'는 맥락이 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Despite the remarkable progress in deep-learning based facial recognition approaches in recent years, in terms of ⓐ<u>identification</u> performance, they still have limitations. These limitations relate to the database used in the learning stage. If the selected database does not contain ⓑ<u>enough</u> instances, the result may be systematically affected. For example, the performance of a facial biometric system may ⓒ<u>decrease</u> if the person to be identified was enrolled over 10 years ago. The factor to consider is that this person may experience changes in the texture of the face, particularly with the appearance of wrinkles and sagging skin. These changes may be highlighted by weight gain or loss. To ⓓ<u>counteract </u>this problem, researchers have developed models for face aging or digital de-aging. It is used to compensate for the ⓔ<u>similarities</u> in facial characteristics, which appear over a given time period.
questions.explanation: 지문은 시간이 흐름에 따라 얼굴에 주름이 생기는 등 얼굴의 특성이 변하는 문제를 다루고 있습니다. ⓔ가 포함된 문장은 이러한 변화를 보완하기 위한 모델을 설명하고 있으므로, '유사성(similarities)'이 아니라 시간 경과에 따라 나타나는 얼굴 특성의 '차이'나 '변화(differences/changes)'를 보완하는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions. But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
options: ① Necessity of Accurate Information for Decision-Making
② Drawbacks of the Overabundance of Information on the Internet
③ Deceptive Self-Assessment: How Access to Unrelated Information Inflates Confidence
④ Human's Intellectual Desire to Thoroughly Explore the Depths of Profound Knowledge
⑤ Impaired Self-Awareness Resulting from Exposure to Misinformation Available on the Internet
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인터넷을 통해 정보를 검색해 본 사람들이 그렇지 않은 사람들보다 새로운 질문(자신이 검색하지 않은 내용)에 대해서도 자신의 지식 수준을 더 높게 평가했다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 즉, 관련 없는 정보에 대한 접근성이 지적 자신감을 부풀린다는 내용이므로 ③번 '기만적인 자기 평가: 무관한 정보에 대한 접근이 어떻게 자신감을 부풀리는가'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 의사결정을 위한 정확한 정보의 필요성
② 인터넷상 정보 과잉의 단점들
③ 기만적인 자기 평가: 무관한 정보에 대한 접근이 어떻게 자신감을 부풀리는가
④ 심오한 지식의 깊이를 철저히 탐구하려는 인간의 지적 욕구
⑤ 인터넷에 가용한 잘못된 정보에 대한 노출로 인해 손상된 자각

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants. Not only were their athletic talents superior, the Cubans appeared even stronger from just the colour of their uniforms. A game would not even start and the opposing team would already be scared. A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time. The country that ruled international baseball for decades has not been on top since that uniform change. Traditions are important for a team; while a team brand or image can adjust to keep up with present times, if it abandons or neglects its roots, negative effects can surface.
options: ① Adaptation Over Tradition Brings Better Results
② Negative Impact of a Uniform Change on Cuban Baseball
③ Differences in Uniform Styles Between Cuba and America
④ Cuba's Exceptional Athletic Talents: Dominance in the Baseball World
⑤ Cuba's Conformity to New Trends Fuels Unstoppable Success in Baseball
questions.explanation: 이 글은 쿠바 야구팀이 전통적인 빨간색 유니폼을 입었을 때 세계를 제패했으나, 현대화된 스타일로 유니폼을 바꾼 이후 성적이 하락했다는 사례를 통해 전통과 뿌리의 중요성을 설명합니다. 따라서 '유니폼 변화가 쿠바 야구에 미친 부정적 영향'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 전통보다 적응이 더 나은 결과를 가져온다
② 유니폼 변화가 쿠바 야구에 미친 부정적 영향
③ 쿠바와 미국의 유니폼 스타일 차이
④ 쿠바의 뛰어난 운동 재능: 야구계의 지배력
⑤ 새로운 유행에 대한 쿠바의 순응이 야구의 멈출 수 없는 성공을 부채질하다

questions.question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글읈 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War.
ordered_passages: (A) The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled.

(B) Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.

(C) In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 식량 다양성의 감소가 2차 세계대전 이홄에 발생했다고 합니다. (C)에서 기아를 해결하기 위해 특정 곡물을 대량 생산하는 방법(수퍼 생산성 품종)을 찾았다는 내용이 나오고, (A)에서 'The strategy'로 이를 받아 그 갰과로 생산량이 늘었음을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 그러한 횁일화된 품종의 위험성을 경고하는 흠름으로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Nearly everything has to go through your mouth to get to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. ␐A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and prevent it from harm - with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. ␑From the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. ␒What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and a reflection of what is happening in other parts of the body. ␓Like other areas of the body, the mouth is full of germs, which are mostly harmless. ␔Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease that affects the entire body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, posing serious health risks.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 전체적인 흐름은 구강 건강(oral health)이 신체 전체의 건강에 미치는 중대한 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ␓번 문장은 '입안에 세균이 많지만 대개 무해하다'는 내용으로, 구강 건강의 중요성과 질병 유발 가능성을 강조하는 전체 흐름과는 어울리지 않는 일반적인 상식 기술입니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 11월 24번]
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. (A) But why should this be true? (B) The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. (C) We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. (D) Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. (E) It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
questions.insertion_sentence: At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장은 '동시에, 이 뉴런들은 변화하는 것들에 대한 반응을 강화한다'는 내용입니다. (B) 뒤의 문장에서 신경 세포(nerve cells)가 반복되는 자극에 대한 반응을 줄이도록 설계되었다는 내용이 나오고, 그와 대조적으로 변화하는 자극에 대한 반응을 강화한다는 내용인 제시문이 온 뒤, (C)에서 이러한 진화적 이유(생존 가치)를 설명하는 것이 흐름상 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 11월 31번]
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristic of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself. Psychologist George M. Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment. (A) Stratton wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally turned the world upside down for him. (B) In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him. (C) With time, however, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated. (D) Fortunately, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for the rest of his life. (E) For him, everything returned to normal after one day.
questions.insertion_sentence: As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems: he used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something, for example.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장은 Stratton이 반전 안경을 벗었을 때 다시 문제에 직면했다는 내용입니다. (C)까지는 안경에 적응하여 정상적으로 활동하게 된 과정을 설명하고 있으며, (D)에서 다행히 지각을 되돌릴 수 있었다는 내용 앞에 안경을 벗고 겪은 재적응의 혼란을 언급하는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.↓Host: Welcome! Today, we're discussing brain death and organ transplantation with Dr. Smith, a medical ethicist. Dr. Smith, why are some countries implementing stricter guidelines for diagnosing brain death?Dr. S: The aim is to (A)________________________________, but these rules might actually heighten suspicion instead.Host: So, they could reinforce misconceptions about how reliable the diagnosis is?Dr. S: Exactly. Many people believe that diagnosing brain death is complicated, despite established medical criteria.Host: Shouldn't the criteria be consistent for all cases of death?Dr. S: Yes, (B)__________________________________ in the medical process.Host: Thank you, Dr. Smith. It's vital for the public to understand these important issues clearly.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 어휘 및 어구를 모두 한 번씩만 사용하되 그 외의 다른 단어는 추가하지 말 것
어형을 변형하지 말 것
questions.answer: address public fears about hasty diagnoses for organ donation
questions.explanation: 지문 본문의 'to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs' 부분을 대화문 상황에 맞춰 '장기 기증을 위한 성급한 진단에 대한 대중의 두려움을 다루는 것(해결하는 것)'이라는 의미로 재구성한 것입니다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.

필요시 어형을 변형하여 쓸 것
questions.answer: consistency is essential for maintaining public trust
questions.explanation: 지문의 핵심 주장인 '진단 기준의 일관성이 필요하다'는 점과 대화 맥락인 '대중의 신뢰 유지'를 결합하여 문장을 완성합니다. 'consistent'를 명사형 'consistency'로, 'maintain'을 전치사 for 뒤에 오는 동명사 'maintaining'으로 변형하여 '일관성은 대중의 신뢰를 유지하는 데 필수적이다'라는 문장을 만듭니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve ⓐ<u>inclusiveness</u> in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more ⓑ<u>widespread</u>, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can ⓒ<u>complicate</u> communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career ⓓ<u>prospects</u>. For example, Al's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly ⓔ<u>improve</u> the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 AI가 장애가 있는 노동자들의 접근성을 높여 직장 내 포용성을 향상시킨다는 긍정적인 측면을 다루고 있습니다. 음성 인식 솔루션이나 실시간 자막 시스템은 의사소통을 '복잡하게(complicate)' 만드는 것이 아니라 '촉진하거나 도와주는(facilitate/enhance)' 역할을 해야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We ⓐ<u>recode</u> what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than ⓑ<u>retrieving</u> the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more ⓒ<u>efficient</u> way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a ⓓ<u>cost</u> of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely ⓔ<u>strengthened</u> the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: 인간의 기억이 비디오처럼 재생되는 것이 아니라 추상적인 표상을 통해 '재구성'된다는 사실은 목격자 증언의 법적 우위성을 '강화(strengthened)'하는 것이 아니라 오히려 '약화(weakened/undermined)'시킵니다. 기억이 왜곡될 수 있음을 시사하기 때문입니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by __________. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.explanation: 글 전체에서 아이들이 부모나 친구가 하는 것을 '관찰(observing)'하고 '모방(imitation, imitate)'함으로써 배운다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 마지막 문윑에서도 단순히 타인을 '밤으로써(watching others)' 많은 것을 배울 수 있다고 하였으뭀로, 비칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말은 'observation(관찰)'입니다.
options_translation: 관찰
실험
직관
시가차호
퀐사

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is _______________________________________. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
options: ① to stay with those who sacrifice themselves for others
② to learn from the mistakes that people have made in the past
③ keeping relationships with people in a higher social position
④ spending time with those who need social skill development
⑤ to be with the persons who have overcome the same kind of problem
questions.explanation: 무력감이나 부정적인 상태에서 벗어나는 방법으로 '승자들과 어울리기(hanging out with the winners)'를 제시하고 있습니다. 이는 이미 부정적인 에너지를 극복하고 긍정적인 에너지를 가진 사람들과 함께함으로써 에너지를 전이받는 것을 의미하므로, 같은 문제를 극복한 사람들과 함께 있는 것이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 타인을 위해 자신을 희생하는 사람들과 머무는 것
② 사람들이 과거에 저지른 실수로부터 배우는 것
③ 더 높은 사회적 지위에 있는 사람들과 관계를 유지하는 것
④ 사회적 기술 개발이 필요한 사람들과 시간을 보내는 것
⑤ 같은 종류의 문제를 극복한 사람들과 함께 있는 것

questions.question: 10. 다음 Capuchin에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
options: ① 큰 집단에서 살아가며, 갇힌 상태에서 사람들과 물건을 교환할 수 있다.
② 먹을 것을 얻기 위해 자신이 가진 돌을 교환한다.
③ 두 마리의 원숭이에게 오이를 제공하면 기쁘게 오이를 먹는다.
④ 한 마리의 원숭에게 포도를 제공하면 오이를 받는 원숭이는 오이를 실험자에게 던진다.
⑤ 다른 원숭이가 포도를 받더라도 오이를 받은 원숭이는 자신의 이익을 포기하지 않는다.
questions.explanation: 지문 마지막 부분에서 'she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure'라고 언급되어 있습니다. 즉, 불공평함을 느끼면 자신의 이익(오이)을 포기하고 던져버린다고 했으므로 5번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "when there is no cat"이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially <u>when there is no cat</u>." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① risks of misusing concepts or assumptions
② meaningless reasoning for a non-existent cat
③ when the cat is unintentionally not in the room
④ inherently unbiased hypotheses by the scientists
⑤ the absence of the actual thing or essence being sought
questions.explanation: 글에서 'when there is no cat'은 과학자들이 존재하지 않는 '본질(essence)'을 찾기 위해 잘못된 개념을 가지고 헛된 노력을 하는 상황을 비유합니다. 즉, 찾고자 하는 실제 대상이나 본질이 존재하지 않는 상태를 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 개념이나 가정을 오용하는 위험
② 존재하지 않는 고양이에 대한 무의미한 추론
③ 고양이가 의도치 않게 방에 없을 때
④ 과학자들에 의한 본질적으로 편향되지 않은 가설
⑤ 찾고 있는 실제 사물이나 본질의 부재

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are ⓐ<u>thought to</u> exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when ⓑ<u>triggering</u>, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very ⓒ<u>attentive</u>, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways ⓓ<u>which</u> they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they ⓔ<u>had not helped</u> us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: ⓓ의 which는 뒤에 완전한 문장('they activate our systems')이 오고 앞의 선행사 'specific ways'를 수식하므로, 관계대명사가 아닌 관계부사 how를 대신하는 that이나 in which가 와야 합니다. way와 how는 같이 쓸 수 없으므로 which 단독으로는 불가능합니다. ⓑ는 분사구문에서 '프로그램이 유발될 때'라는 수동의 의미이므로 triggered가 되어야 합니다. (이 문제에서 중복 정답 가능성이 있으나 원문 문맥상 ⓓ가 명확한 관계사 오류입니다.)

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. (A) Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. (B) This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. (C) The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. (D) The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. (E) Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame.
questions.explanation: (B)까지는 소셜 미디어 유명인들이 엘리트 유명인 영역으로 넘어가는 데 겪는 한계와 비판에 대해 설명합니다. 주어진 문장의 'However, the criticism also misses the point'는 이러한 비판이 명성의 의미를 재구성한다는 점을 간과하고 있다는 반전의 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C)부터는 엘리트 유명인과 평범한 유명인의 차이를 설명하며 새로운 명성의 의미를 풀어나가므로 (C) 위치가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸 (A)~(E)에 들어갈 적절한 어휘를 보기에서 고르시오. [24년 10월 39번]
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is (A)__________. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may (B)__________. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in (C)__________ states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is (D)__________ also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly (E)__________.
questions.explanation: (A) 세포 하나 내 분자 간 상호작용의 수는 매우 많으므로 'enormous(거대한/막대한)'가 적절합니다.(B) 복잡한 시스템이 안정되려면 소수의 집단적 방식이 'emerge(나타나다)'해야 합니다.(C) 정해진 상태 사이의 'random(무작위한/임의의)' 상태로는 존재할 수 없다는 맥락입니다.(D) 이러한 원리가 건강과 질병에도 적용된다는 의미로 'true(사실인/해당하는)'가 적절합니다.(E) 질병의 원인은 다양해도 나타나는 증상은 놀라울 정도로 'similar(유사한)' 경우가 많다는 내용입니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 주어진 조건에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and tooobvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, ______________________________________________. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
subjective_conditions: 1. 보기의 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 완성할 것
2. 문맥과 어법에 맞게 완성할 것(필요시 활용할 것)
questions.answer: hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts
questions.explanation: 기후 변화가 더 이상 주변적인 특징이 아니게 될 때(온도가 3~4도 더 오를 때), 누구도 그 영향으로부터 고립되었다고(영향을 받지 않는다고) 느끼기 어려울 것이라는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 'hardly'는 부정의 의미를 담아 '거의 ~않다'로 쓰이며, 'feel isolated from'은 '~로부터 소외/고립된 느낌을 받다'는 뜻입니다. 조건에 맞게 'isolate'를 'isolated'로 변형하여 완성합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 요약문의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 표현을 조건에 맞게 완성하시오. [24년 9월 37번]
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the passage, the reason your voice sounds deeper and richer to yourself is ___________________________________________. This pathway emphasizes lower frequencies, making your voice sound deeper and richer to you compared to how others hear it.
subjective_conditions: 1. 보기의 주어진 단어를 문맥에 맞게 필요한 단어를 골라 완성할 것
2. 문맥과 어법에 맞게 완성할 것(필요시 형태 변화 가능)
questions.answer: that vibrations are conducted through the internal pathway
questions.explanation: 자신의 목소리가 더 깊고 풍부하게 들리는 이유는 진동이 내부 경로를 통해 전달되기 때문입니다. 'the reason ... is that ~' 구문을 사용하며, 수동태(are conducted)를 사용하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 알맞은 표현을 각각 한 단어로 보기에서 찾아 완성하시오. [24년 9월 38번]
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.Two kinds of Similarity by BiologistsAnalogous: common(A)___________ex) wings of birds and beesHomologous: common(B)___________ex) forelimb of all mammalsHow to differentiate the two kinds of similarity:by focusing on the overall structure and their most (C)___________ traits.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면, 'Analogous(상조적)' 특징은 공통의 기능(function)을 가지며, 'Homologous(상동적)' 특징은 공통의 조상(ancestor)에서 유래합니다. 두 유사성을 구분하기 위해 생물학자들은 비기능적(nonfunctional)인 특징에 집중합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)에 해당하는 사례로 어울리지 않는 것은? [24년 10월 23번]
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after 1, 5 and 10 minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" <u>(A)Questions that seek concrete responses</u> help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
options: ① How many books have you read in the past year?
② How many times did you eat out at a restaurant last month?
③ In the last week, how many hours of sleep did you get on average each night?
④ In the past two month, how many times did you feel connected to the people around you?
⑤ How many times in the past month have you exercised for at least 30 minutes or more?
questions.explanation: 지문에서 (A)는 추상적인 개념을 명확히 하기 위해 '구체적인 답변'을 유도하는 질문을 의미합니다. ④번 질문의 'feel connected(연결되어 있다고 느끼다)'는 사람마다 정의가 다를 수 있는 매우 주관적이고 추상적인 표현이므로, 지문에서 경계하는 모호한 질문의 사례에 해당합니다.
options_translation: ① 작년에 몇 권의 책을 읽었습니까?
② 지난달에 몇 번이나 식당에서 외식을 했습니까?
③ 지난주에 매일 밤 평균 몇 시간의 잠을 잤습니까?
④ 지난 두 달 동안 주변 사람들과 연결되어 있다고 느낀 적이 몇 번입니까?
⑤ 지난 한 달 동안 최소 30분 이상 운동한 적이 몇 번입니까?

questions.question: 8. 다음 중 digital metaphor와 linguistic metaphor의 예시를 알맞게 짝지은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors differ from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience must choose to enter the world the metaphor proposes. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and further engagement with Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) because they are realized in digital artifacts that actively change a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot afford to make their audience wonder how the metaphor works; normally, the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. In contrast, Shakespeare is beloved because his works invite the audience to pause, reflect, and discover meanings that aren't immediately apparent.
options: ① Digital Metaphor: virus / Linguistic Metaphor: The sun rose at 6 a.m.
② Digital Metaphor: Time is the silent thief. / Linguistic Metaphor: Surfing the web
③ Digital Metaphor: Memories are the smell of an old book. / Linguistic Metaphor: recycle bin
④ Digital Metaphor: firewall / Linguistic Metaphor: Hope is like a tiny lantern
⑤ Digital Metaphor: window / Linguistic Metaphor: desktop
questions.explanation: 디지털 은유(Digital/Technological metaphor)는 컴퓨터나 디지털 환경에서 직관적인 사용을 위해 사용되는 용어(firewall, virus, recycle bin, desktop, window 등)이며, 언어적 은유(Linguistic metaphor)는 문학적 표현처럼 인지적 노력을 통해 의미를 파악해야 하는 비유적 표현(Hope is like a lantern, Time is a beggar 등)입니다. 4번의 firewall은 디지털 은유이고, Hope is like a tiny lantern은 언어적 은유로 가장 적절하게 짝지어져 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 디지털 은유: 바이러스 / 언어적 은유: 태양은 오전 6시에 떴다 (사실적 진술)
② 디지털 은유: 시간은 조용한 도둑이다 (언어적) / 언어적 은유: 웹 서핑 (디지털)
③ 디지털 은유: 기억은 헌 책의 냄새다 (언어적) / 언어적 은유: 휴지통 (디지털)
④ 디지털 은유: 방화벽 / 언어적 은유: 희망은 작은 등불과 같다
⑤ 디지털 은유: 창 / 언어적 은유: 바탕화면 (둘 다 디지털)

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색하거나 혹은 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements that specify ⓐ<u>what</u> a whole team of doctors must check in the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reasons for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors ⓑ<u>are</u> undoubtedly to ease public concerns about a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable ⓒ<u>whether</u> these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process that ⓓ<u>lacks</u> precision. As a matter of ⓔ<u>consisting</u>, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
questions.explanation: ⓔ의 'As a matter of consisting'은 문맥상 어색합니다. '적어도 일관성의 문제로서' 혹은 '마땅히 그래야 하는 일로서'라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 'As a matter of consistency'(일관성의 문제로) 또는 문맥에 따라 'As a matter of course'(당연히) 등이 적절합니다. 여기서는 장기 기증자와 일반인의 사망 진단 기준이 일관되게 적용되어야 한다는 흐름이므로 'consistency'가 더 어울립니다.ⓐ 'what'은 check의 목적어 역할을 하는 관계대명사로 적절합니다.ⓑ 주어가 'The reasons'이므로 복수 동사 'are'는 적절합니다.ⓒ 'questionable whether'는 '~인지가 의심스럽다'는 의미로 적절합니다.ⓓ 'process that lacks precision'에서 주격 관계대명사절 내의 동사로 선행사 process에 맞춰 단수형 lacks는 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? (A) You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. (B) They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. (C) So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals. (D) That is where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. (E) Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '하지만 플라톤은 어떤 물리적인 원도 완벽하지 않다는 것을 지적할 것이다'라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A) 문장에서 언급된 돌에 새겨지거나 모래에 그려진 '특정한 예시(particular example)'에 이어, 이 예시들이 완벽하지 않다는 비판이 나와야 하므로 (B) 위치가 가장 적절합니다. (B) 뒤의 'They'는 주어진 문장의 'it'과 'physical circle'을 포함한 물리적 대상들을 가리키며 이들이 결함을 가지고 있음을 설명합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Frederick Douglass was born into slavery at a farm in Maryland. His full name at birth was Frederick Augustus Washington Bailey. He changed his name to Frederick Douglass after he successfully escaped from slavery in 1838. He became a leader of the Underground Railroad - a network of people, places, and routes that helped enslaved people escape to the north. He assisted other runaway slaves until they could safely get to other areas in the north. As a slave, he had taught himself to read and write and he spread that knowledge to other slaves as well. Once free, he became a well-known abolitionist and strong believer in equality for all people including Blacks, Native Americans, women, and recent immigrants. He wrote several autobiographies describing his experiences as a slave. In addition to all this, he became the first African-American candidate for vice president of the United States.
options: ① He published numerous fictional stories that completely fabricated his life as a free man.
② He was the first African American to run for the position of vice president of the United States.
③ Frederick Douglass was born on a Maryland farm where he was enslaved.
④ He emerged as a leader of the Underground Railroad that assisted enslaved individuals in fleeing to the north.
⑤ While he was enslaved, he learned to read and write on his own and also shared that knowledge with other enslaved individuals.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 Frederick Douglass는 자신의 노예 생활 경험을 서술한 자서전(autobiographies)을 썼다고 언급되어 있습니다. 자유인으로서의 삶을 허구로 꾸며낸(completely fabricated) 소설(fictional stories)을 출판했다는 내용은 사실이 아닙니다.
options_translation: ① 그는 자유인으로서의 삶을 완전히 꾸며낸 수많은 허구 소설을 출판했다.
② 그는 미국 부통령 후보로 출마한 최초의 아프리카계 미국인이었다.
③ Frederick Douglass는 그가 노예였던 메릴랜드의 한 농장에서 태어났다.
④ 그는 노예가 된 개인들이 북쪽으로 도망치는 것을 돕는 Underground Railroad의 지도자로 부상했다.
⑤ 그는 노예 생활 동안 스스로 읽고 쓰는 법을 배웠고 그 지식을 다른 노예들과 공유했다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 어법적으로 어색한 3곳을 아래의 조건에 맞게 찾아서 고치시오. [23년 11월 38번]
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways produced grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leave the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants have a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
subjective_conditions: 1. 어색한 부분은 한 단어 혹은 여러 단어일 수도 있음.
2. 어색한 부분을 고치기 위해서 삭제, 추가, 변경을 하나 혹은 두 개 이상 할 수 있음.
3. 아래 지문과 주어진 해석이 일치하도록 수정해야 함.
questions.answer: (1) produced → to produce (혹은 producing)(2) Leave → Leaving(3) have → has
questions.explanation: (1) 'ways produced grains' 부분에서 ways를 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사나 분사가 필요하므로 produced를 to produce 혹은 producing으로 고쳐야 합니다.(2) 문장 처음에 위치하여 '그 전략의 기여를 차치하고'라는 의미의 분사구문을 만들어야 하므로 명령문 형태인 Leave를 현재분사인 Leaving으로 고쳐야 합니다.(3) 'a global food system (that depends on just a narrow selection of plants) have' 문장에서 주어는 단수인 a global food system이므로 복수 동사인 have를 단수 동사인 has로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 <보기>의 어휘만을 모두 한 번씩만 사용하여 주어진 해석과 같은 의미가 되도록 문장을 영작하시오. (어형 변화 없음) [23년 11월 39번]
questions.passage: The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants.
subjective_conditions: 어형 변화 없음
모든 어휘 한 번씩 사용
questions.answer: covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring
questions.explanation: 주어진 우리말 '쿠바인들은 머리부터 발끝까지 빨간색으로 뒤덮인 유니폼을 입는 것으로 알려져 있었는데, 이것은 회색이나 흰색 바지를 특징으로 하는 더 보수적인 북미 스타일과 강한 대조를 이룬다'를 영작하는 문제입니다. uniforms를 수식하는 분사구 'covered in red from head to toe'를 작성하고, 앞 문장 전체 혹은 앞선 내용을 부연 설명하는 동격 형태의 'a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style'를 연결한 후, 다시 style을 수식하는 'featuring'을 사용하여 완성합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 <보기>의 어휘만을 모두 한 번씩만 사용하여 주어진 해석과 같은 의미가 되도록 문장을 영작하시오. (어형 변화 없음) [23년 11월 39번]
