questions.question: 8. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 의미하는 바를 다음과 같이 풀어 쓰고자 한다. 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. (A)<u>It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion</u>. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - (B)<u>producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm</u>, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.*flounder: 넙치**mimic: 모방하다
questions.explanation: 문맥상 사진작가들은 처음에 넙치로 착각했다가 나중에 다시 보고 나서야 문어임을 알았으므로, '즉각적인(immediate)' 인식이 아니라 지연된 혹은 처음에 실패한 인식을 의미해야 합니다. 따라서 ⓐ의 immediate는 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (B)가 의미하는 바를 다음과 같이 풀어 쓰고자 한다. 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. (A)<u>It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion</u>. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - (B)<u>producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm</u>, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.*flounder: 넙치**mimic: 모방하다
questions.summary_sentence: (B) implies that the octopus, while ⓐ__________ a flounder, suddenly ⓑ__________ itself by extending an arm to hunt.
questions.explanation: 문어는 넙치를 흉내 내는(imitating) 동안, 사냥을 위해 팔을 뻗음으로써 자신의 정체를 갑자기 드러내게(reveals) 된다는 내용이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고정시키는 --- 강화하다
② 깊은 인상을 주는 --- 회수하다
③ 개선하는 --- 회복하다
④ 상상하는 --- 세련되게 하다
⑤ 모방하는 --- 드러내다

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage:
Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by a lack of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. According to many studies, lowering the level of serotonin and noradrenaline - the neurotransmitters that are thought to be the causes of depression - in healthy people who have never been depressed does not affect their mood at all. This is because the shortage of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, _____________________________. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
*neurotransmitter: 신경 전달 물질
**manifest: (명백히) 나타내다
options: ① the shortage of substances in the brain comes after depression starts.
② low levels of serotonin and noradrenaline are what directly cause depression to begin.
③ the changes in brain substance levels happen because of depression, not as the reason for it.
④ it is depression itself that leads to a decrease in serotonin and noradrenaline, not the other way around.
⑤ depression causes the levels of certain brain substances, like serotonin and noradrenaline, to drop, rather than these drops causing depression.
questions.explanation: 지문은 뇌 화학 물질의 부족이 우울증의 원인이 아니라 결과라고 주장하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '우울증이 발생한 뒤에 물질 부족이 따라온다'거나 '우울증 자체가 물질 수치를 낮추는 원인이다'라는 맥락의 표현이 적절합니다. 반면 ②번은 '세로토닌과 노르아드레날린의 낮은 수치가 우울증을 시작하게 하는 직접적인 원인이다'라고 주장하고 있어 지문의 전체적인 요지와 정반대됩니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌 물질의 부족은 우울증이 시작된 후에 발생한다.
② 낮은 수치의 세로토닌과 노르아드레날린이 우울증을 시작하게 하는 직접적인 원인이다.
③ 뇌 물질 수치의 변화는 우울증의 이유가 아니라 우울증 때문에 일어난다.
④ 세로토닌과 노르아드레날린의 감소를 초래하는 것은 우울증 그 자체이며, 그 반대가 아니다.
⑤ 이러한 감소가 우울증을 일으키기보다, 우울증이 세로토닌과 노르아드레날린 같은 특정 뇌 물질 수치를 떨어뜨린다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often turn out to be nearly the same.*embryo: 배아**physiological: 생리적인
questions.summary_sentence: The above explains how life, as a complex high-dimensional system, becomes stable by ⓐ<u>reducing</u> the enormous possibilities of molecular interactions into a small number of outcomes. The biologist Conrad Waddington's concept of canalization illustrates how a human embryo develops along ⓑ<u>well-defined</u> possible states, producing ⓒ<u>unpredictable</u> tissues or body shapes. Similarly, in health and disease, while the causes of illness may ⓓ<u>vary</u> greatly, the resulting symptoms and physiological effects often end up being very ⓔ<u>similar.</u>
questions.explanation: 본문에서 생명 시스템의 특징으로 '결과가 급격히 좁아지는 현상(drastic narrowing of outcomes)'을 '운하화(canalization)'라고 설명하며, 인간 배아 발달 시 오직 '제한된 수(limited number)'의 조직과 신체 형태만 결과로 나타날 수 있다고 했습니다. 따라서 요약문에서 배아 발달의 결과가 'unpredictable(예측 불가능한)'하다는 ⓒ의 표현은 적절하지 않으며, 'predictable'이나 'limited'와 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 어색한 부분이 포함된 것은?
questions.passage: From an early age, we assign purpose to objects and events, preferring this reasoning to random chance. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because they don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. However, by attributing intention to animals and even objects, we are able to make fast decisions about the likely behaviour of that being. ⓐ<u>This was essential in our hunter-gatherer days to avoid being eaten by predators because it is more dangerous to assume that predators have aggressive intent than to assume that predators about to attack you have no purpose</u>. ⓑ<u>The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, as those are the mental processes which we understand</u>. ⓒ<u>Ambiguous events are caused by such agents</u>. ⓓ<u>This results in a perceptual system strongly biased towards anthropomorphism</u>. ⓔ<u>Therefore, we tend to assume intention even where there is none</u>. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you. By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has saved your life.*aggressive: 공격적인**ambiguous: 모호한***anthropomorphism: 의인화
questions.explanation: ⓐ의 내용을 보면 '포식자가 의도가 없다고 가정하는 것보다 공격적인 의도를 가지고 있다고 가정하는 것이 더 위험하다'고 기술되어 있습니다. 하지만 진화론적 관점과 생존 매커니즘의 맥락에서 볼 때, 실제로 공격할 의도가 없는 포식자를 위험하다고 '오해'하는 것보다, 공격할 의도가 있는 포식자를 의도가 없다고 '오해'하는 것이 훨씬 위험합니다. 따라서 ⓐ는 'more dangerous to assume ~ have no purpose than to assume ~ have aggressive intent'와 같은 논리가 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Nearly three-quarters of the criminal cases overturned by the Innocence Project using DNA evidence involved eyewitnesses who were very confident but turned out to be wrong. (A) Why would someone admit to a crime they didn't commit? (B) It seems that police interrogation techniques can sometimes lead to false confessions, just like a psychiatrist might accidentally make someone believe false childhood memories or an investigator might create a false memory in a child. (C) These things happen. (D) People who are easily influenced, like those who can be hypnotized by a magician, might also give in under the stress of police questioning. (E) After hours of questioning, some might think confessing is better than enduring more interrogation, just to make it stop for a while.*confession: 고백 **the accused: 피의자***overturn: 뒤집히다 ****interrogation: 심문*****psychiatrist: 정신과 의사*****hypnotize: 최면을 걸다
questions.insertion_sentence: Even more surprising is that over a quarter of these cases included false confessions by the accused during police questioning.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이러한 사건들의 4분의 1 이상이 경찰 심문 중 피의자의 허위 자백을 포함했다는 사실은 훨씬 더 놀랍다'는 내용입니다. 첫 문장에서 목격자의 잘못된 증언에 의한 유죄 판결 사례를 언급한 후, (A) 위치에 이 문장이 들어가야 뒤에 이어지는 '왜 누군가가 자신이 저지르지 않은 죄를 인정하겠는가?'라는 질문과 그에 대한 설명(경찰 심문 기법 등)이 논리적으로 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Imagine that your child's brain is an old train with two steam engines at each end. The first points towards positive behaviour, which will allow the child to achieve their goals in life. The second engine points to a negative one, which will cause difficulties and suffering. (A) Now I want you to imagine that every comment you make to your child is like a log. (B) In which of the two fireboxes do you want to place the log? (C) Too often, frustrated parents focus all their attention on the negative behaviour of their children. (D) When we centre our attention on the negatives, we are placing a log in the firebox pointing towards difficulties. (E) You may feel that your duty is to focus on everything negative your child does, so they will not do it again, but in many cases the only thing this does is fuel more bad behaviour.
questions.insertion_sentence: The one that fuels the locomotive towards satisfaction or towards dissatisfaction?
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '만족을 향해 혹은 불만족을 향해 기관차를 움직이게 하는 것(화덕) 중 어느 것인가?'라고 묻고 있습니다. 이는 앞 문장 (B)에서 부모의 말이 장작이라면 두 화덕 중 어디에 넣고 싶은지 묻는 질문에 대한 부연 설명이자 선택의 기로를 구체화하는 문장입니다. 따라서 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
questions.summary_sentence: Herbert Simon's insights highlight how humans overcome cognitive and resource limitations by (A)__________ knowledge and computation across society, enabling us to (B)__________ solve complex problems over generations through social learning and specialized contributions.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 인지적 한계를 극복하기 위해 지식과 계산을 사회 전체에 분산시키고(distribute), 이를 통해 집단적으로(collectively) 복잡한 문제를 해결한다는 내용을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '분산시키다'라는 의미의 distributing, (B)에는 '집단적으로'라는 의미의 collectively가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 보유하다 --- 천천히
② 공급하다 --- 근본적으로
③ 계산하다 --- 개별적으로
④ 분배하다 --- 집단적으로
⑤ 순환시키다 --- 별개로

questions.question: 25. 다음 글에서 문맥상 밑줄 친 to feel isolated from its impacts가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Onscreen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able <u>to feel isolated from its impacts</u>. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
options: ① to ignore or avoid its consequences of climate change
② to be physically relocated to avoid the impact of the climate change
③ to watch a movie about the climate transformation alone
④ to get emotionally lonely by the impact of 3 degrees higher temperature
⑤ to feel affected by or attached to the consequences of climate change
questions.explanation: 본문에서 기온이 3~4도 더 오르면 기후 변화가 삶의 지엽적인 특성이 아니라 모든 곳에 존재하게 되어 아무도 그 영향으로부터 고립된(떨어져 있는) 느낌을 받을 수 없게 된다는 것은, 기후 변화의 결과를 무시하거나 피할 수 없게 된다는 의미입니다. 따라서 ① '기후 변화의 결과를 무시하거나 피하는 것'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기후 변화의 결과를 무시하거나 피하는 것
② 기후 변화의 영향을 피하기 위해 물리적으로 이주하는 것
③ 기후 변화에 관한 영화를 혼자 보는 것
④ 3도 더 높은 온도의 영향으로 정서적으로 외로워지는 것
⑤ 기후 변화의 결과에 영향을 받거나 애착을 느끼는 것

questions.question: 26. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness.
ordered_passages: (A) Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions.

(B) Psychology is different. Psychology is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another.
(C) The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers.

(D) As different as human beings are, there are processes and principles that we all have in common, and there are processes and principles that produce our wonderful cultural and social differences. These are what modern psychology is all about. *anecdote: 일화, 개인적인 진술 **hearsay: 전해들은 말
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 사회에 떠도는 인간 본성에 대한 설명이 가정과 허구의 혼합이라고 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 이와 다른 '심리학'을 소개합니다. (C)에서는 (B)의 '과학'이라는 키워드를 받아 심리학자가 의견이나 전언에 의존하지 않음을 설명하고, (A)에서 '대신에(Instead)' 증거를 찾는다는 구체적인 방법론을 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (D)에서 심리학이 다루는 공통 과정과 원리들을 정리하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally elective. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an abundant resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to address it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly highlights have-and-have-not inequities, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
options: ① economic inequality as a result of water shortages
② technological advancements in water leakage detection
③ political and structural causes of the global water crisis
④ necessity of governmental transparency in handling water crises
⑤ importance of community involvement in local water management
questions.explanation: 이 글은 오늘날의 물 위기가 피할 수 없는 것이 아니라 정치적이며 선택적인 문제라고 설명하고 있습니다. 정부의 방치, 무관심, 열악한 인프라, 오염, 무분별한 도시화와 같은 정치적 및 구조적 요인들이 물 부족을 초래하고 불평등을 심화시킨다는 것이 핵심 내용입니다. 따라서 '글로벌 물 위기의 정치적 및 구조적 원인'인 3번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 물 부족의 결과로서의 경제적 불평등
② 누수 탐지에 있어서의 기술적 진보
③ 글로벌 물 위기의 정치적 및 구조적 원인
④ 물 위기를 다루는 데 있어서 정부 투명성의 필요성
⑤ 지역 물 관리에서의 지역사회 참여의 중요성

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For most octopus species, the best defense is to remain as inconspicuous as possible, hunting under the cover of darkness. So, encountering one in broad daylight, fully visible in the shallows, was an extraordinary moment for two Australian underwater photographers. At first, they believed they were looking at a flounder. But upon closer inspection, the "flounder" revealed itself to be a medium-sized octopus, cleverly folded and posed, with its two eyes staring upward to create the illusion. This particular octopus was using its remarkable abilities to mimic a completely different creature, fooling unsuspecting prey into thinking the octopus was a different animal, developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there. Since this initial discovery, researchers have identified more of this species, known as the mimic octopus. They are renowned for their intelligence, exceptional eyesight, and unparalleled ability to change their color and pattern. Photographs now document octopuses transforming into sea snakes, a tactic likely meant to intimidate predators.
options: ① A Cunning Animal: Octopus Intelligence Sheds Light on Evolution of Complex Brains
② Octopus Vs Underwater Maze The Unusual Locomotion of Invertebrates
③ Master of Disguise: The Octopus That Transforms to Hunt and Survive
④ Super Powers: What Octopuses Utilize for Prediction
⑤ How Does an Octopus Change Its Skin Textures?
questions.explanation: 이 글은 다른 동물로 위장하여 먹이를 사냥하거나 포식자를 위협하는 능력을 가진 '흉내문어(mimic octopus)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 문어의 뛰어난 지능과 변장술을 다루고 있으므로 '변장의 달인: 사냥과 생존을 위해 변신하는 문어'인 3번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 교활한 동물: 문어의 지능이 복잡한 뇌의 진화에 빛을 비추다
② 문어 대 수중 미로: 무척추동물의 특이한 이동 방식
③ 변장의 달인: 사냥과 생존을 위해 변신하는 문어
④ 슈퍼 파워: 문어가 예측을 위해 활용하는 것
⑤ 문어는 어떻게 피부 질감을 바꾸는가?

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
options: ① How the Memory Ability Fuels Decision-Making Skills
② How Positive Experiences and Emotions Improve Our Memories
③ Individual Differences in Recall and Information Processing
④ Decoding the Digital Age: Algorithms and the Flow of Information
⑤ Self Projection: Viewing the World Through Our Personal Perspective
questions.explanation: 글은 우리가 사물을 볼 때 있는 그대로 보는 것이 아니라, 이미 배운 개념과 지식, 즉 우리만의 '렌즈'를 통해 재구성하여 본다는 점을 설명합니다. 우리의 기억은 비디오를 재생하는 것이 아니라 추상적인 아이디어로 재구성된 것이기 때문에 개인의 가정, 동기, 경험에 의해 세상이 투영되어 보인다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '자기 투영: 개인적 관점을 통해 세상을 바라보기'인 5번이 제목으로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기억 능력이 어떻게 의사 결정 기술을 촉진하는가
② 긍정적인 경험과 감정이 우리의 기억을 어떻게 향상시키는가
③ 회상과 정보 처리에 있어서의 개인차
④ 디지털 시대 해독: 알고리즘과 정보의 흐름
⑤ 자기 투영: 개인적 관점을 통해 세상을 바라보기

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
options: ① A neurotransmitter imbalance in the brain is the root cause of depression.
② Depression can be temporary and treated by cognitive behavior therapy.
③ Serotonin and noradrenaline levels in the brain rise when someone is depressed.
④ Depression stems from a distortion of consciousness, not just a chemical imbalance in the brain.
⑤ Depression is a clarification of the conditions of awareness, resulting from exclusively a chemical imbalance in the brain.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우울증이 뇌의 화학적 불균형에 의해 발생하는 것이 아니라, 의식의 상태가 왜곡되어(자아감과 삶의 의미를 상실하여) 발생하는 의식의 질병이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ④번 진술이 글의 내용과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌 내 신경전달물질의 불균형이 우울증의 근본 원인이다.
② 우울증은 일시적일 수 있으며 인지 행동 치료로 치료될 수 있다.
③ 누군가 우울할 때 뇌의 세로토닌과 노르아드레날린 수치가 상승한다.
④ 우울증은 단순한 뇌의 화학적 불균형이 아니라 의식의 왜곡에서 기인한다.
⑤ 우울증은 인식 상태의 명료화이며, 오직 뇌의 화학적 불균형으로 인해 발생한다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race - their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't psychologically suffer much. In fact, ultra-marathon runners - those people who are crazy enough to push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50-100km or more over many hours, talk about making friends with their pain. When a patient has paid for, some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it, the patient calls that good pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.
options: ① The extent of our suffering depends on the way we perceive and interpret pain in our cognition.
② When 1500m athletes push their limits to win a race, they cannot avoid intense psychological pain and suffering.
③ Ultra-marathon runners are individuals bold enough to push themselves past the usual limits of human perseverance.
④ Ultra-marathon runners mention learning to embrace and coexist with their pain, considering it a friend.
⑤ Patients consider intense pressure on painful back areas as good pain when they trust in the effectiveness of the therapy.
questions.explanation: 본문에 따르면, 1500m 육상 선수들이 경주에서 이기기 위해 극심한 신체적 고통을 겪을 때조차 '심리적으로는 그다지 고통을 겪지 않는다(they don't psychologically suffer much)'고 하였으므로, 강렬한 심리적 고통과 괴로움을 피할 수 없다는 ②번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 고통의 정도는 우리가 인지적으로 통증을 지각하고 해석하는 방식에 달려 있다.
② 1500m 선수들이 승리를 위해 한계까지 밀어붙일 때, 그들은 강렬한 심리적 통증과 괴로움을 피할 수 없다.
③ 울트라 마라톤 주자들은 인간의 인내력의 통상적인 한계를 넘어 자신을 밀어붙일 만큼 용감한 개인들이다.
④ 울트라 마라톤 주자들은 통증을 친구로 여기며 그것을 수용하고 공존하는 법을 배우는 것에 대해 언급한다.
⑤ 환자들은 치료의 효과를 신뢰할 때 허리의 통증 부위에 가해지는 강한 압력을 '좋은 통증'으로 간주한다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 갘의 묑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers ⓐ<u>independently</u>, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially ⓑ<u>learned</u> the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is ⓒ<u>which button to push</u> - essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of ⓓ<u>holding</u> more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things ⓔ<u>well enough to benefit</u> from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
questions.explanation: ⓑ이 속한 문장 'all we have to do is ~'구문에서 is 다음의 밴격 보어 자리에는 (to) 동사원형이 와야 합니다. 주어에 do가 포함된 구문에서 보어 앝의 to는 생략이 가능하므로 learned림 learn으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' ⓐ<u>in which</u> is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules ⓑ<u>is</u> enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes ⓒ<u>that</u> may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states ⓓ<u>in between</u> them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often ⓔ<u>strikingly</u> similar.
questions.explanation: ①번의 in which 뒤에는 완전한 문장이 와야 하는데, 뒤에 바로 동사 is가 나옵니다. 앞 문장 전체 혹은 'high-dimensional system'을 선행사로 받아 보충 설명하는 관계대명사 주격인 which로 써야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and discovered evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually indicate a ⓐ<u>flawed</u> identification. It's when people find themselves ⓑ<u>unable</u> to articulate why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our initial, ⓒ<u>prompt</u>, instinctive reaction to a situation is the truest representation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the ⓓ<u>contemplating</u>, reasoned self-narrative can be. Likewise, Malcolm Gladwell details numerous behavioral economics and psychology experiments in his book Blink that demonstrate the ⓔ<u>superior</u> performance of logical step-by-step justifications for a decision compared to relatively unconscious first guesses.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 요지는 신중하고 논리적인 분석보다 직관적이고 무의식적인 첫인상이 더 정확할 수 있다는 것입니다. 따라서 논리적이고 단계적인 정당화의 성과가 무의식적인 첫 추측보다 '우수하다(superior)'는 ⓔ의 표현은 글의 논지와 반대되므로 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: From an early age, we ascribe purpose to objects and events, preferring this reasoning to random change. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because they don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. ⓐ<u>Inanimate</u> objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. However, by ⓑ<u>attributing</u> intention to animals and even objects, we are able to make fast decisions about the likely behaviour of that being. This was essential in our hunter-gatherer days to avoid being eaten by predators. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, as those are the mental processes which we understand. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents. This results in a perceptual system strongly ⓒ<u>biased</u> towards anthropomorphism. As a result, we tend to assume intention even where there is none. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you. By the time you have ⓓ<u>determined</u> that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has ⓔ<u>compromised</u> your life.
questions.explanation: 사자가 공격할 때 물리적 분석 대신 의도를 빠르게 가정하는 것은 생존 확률을 높여주는 기제입니다. 따라서 이러한 가정이 목숨을 '위태롭게 했다(compromised)'는 표현은 문맥상 어색하며, 목숨을 구했다는 의미의 단어가 와야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. ____________________________________. Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
options: ① The key word here is 'science'
③ It is the issue about humans, not nature
questions.explanation: 심리학은 일반적인 통념이나 의견에 의존하지 않고, 증거를 찾는 '과학'의 한 분야라는 점을 강조하는 글입니다. 빈칸 뒤의 문장에서 심리학자들이 의견이나 소문이 아닌 근거를 찾는다고 설명하고 있으므로 '핵심 단어는 과학이다'라는 문장이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 여기서 핵심 단어는 '과학'이다
② 사회는 항상 개인을 압도한다
③ 그것은 자연이 아니라 인간에 관한 문제이다

questions.question: 24. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which AI surpasses human intelligence.
ordered_passages: (A) In the process of mutual evolution between AI and human consciousness, our consciousness will expand to new dimensions through our interactions with Al, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI.(B) The direction of Al's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.(C) After reaching the point of singularity, AI is expected to continually improve and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 '특이점(singularity)'의 개념을 정의합니다. (C)는 특이점 이후 AI가 가속화된 속도로 진화하며 자의식을 가진 존재가 되어 인간과 함께 진화하기 시작할 것임을 설명합니다. (A)는 이러한 상호 진화 과정에서 인간과 AI가 서로 미치는 영향을 구체화합니다. (B)는 결론적으로 이러한 진화의 방향이 우리의 가치관에 달려 있으므로 상호 공존의 존재로 보아야 함을 제언합니다.

questions.question: 25. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods.
ordered_passages: (A) But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price.(B) If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one.(C) The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 왜 제품이 보통 세 가지 버전으로 출시되는지 그 이유를 발견했다고 언급합니다. (B)에서는 제품이 한 가지 혹은 두 가지일 때의 문제점(수익 손실 또는 저렴한 모델 선호)을 먼저 설명합니다. (A)에서 'But'과 함께 세 번째(가장 비싼) 모델이 도입되었을 때 두 번째 모델의 판매가 늘어나는 현상을 설명하고, (C)에서 소비자들이 더 비싼 모델 때문에 조종당해 중간 모델을 선택하게 된다는 결론으로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
options: ① The Hidden Costs of Expensive Products
② Why the Most Expensive Option Always Wins
③ The Psychology Behind Three-Product Stategies
④ How to Make Smart and Affordable Product Purchases
⑤ Consumers Always Prefer Products with More Features
questions.explanation: 이 글은 제품을 세 가지 버전으로 출시하는 마케팅 전략에 대해 설명합니다. 가장 비싼 세 번째 모델을 도입함으로써 소비자들이 두 번째(중간 가격) 모델을 선택하도록 유도하는 심리적 기제(미끼 효과)를 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로는 '세 가지 제품 전략 뒤에 숨겨진 심리학'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고가 제품의 숨겨진 비용
② 왜 항상 가장 비싼 옵션이 승리하는가
③ 세 가지 제품 전략 뒤에 숨겨진 심리학
④ 똑똑하고 저렴한 제품 구매를 하는 방법
⑤ 소비자들은 항상 더 많은 기능을 가진 제품을 선호한다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. ⓐIn other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. ⓑTherefore, increasing the substances in the brain will gradually improve depression. ⓒIn this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. ⓓOur consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain and the brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. ⓔIf it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life and such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 흐름은 우울증의 원인이 뇌의 화학 물질 불균형이 아니라 '의식의 문제'라는 관점을 제시하고 있습니다. ⓑ는 뇌의 물질을 늘리면 우울증이 개선될 것이라는 기존 의학적 관점(약물 치료 중심)을 따르고 있으므로, 의식의 왜곡이 원인이라는 글의 논조와 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 주어진 철자를 사용하여 철자 수에 맞추어 각 1단어 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there. These traits demonstrate their ability to respond effectively to challenges. In conclusion, these fascinating (A)__________ show how clever and (B)__________ octopuses can be in their underwater world.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 철자를 사용하여 철자 수에 맞출 것
각 1단어 영어로 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 본문은 문어가 자신의 몸 색깔과 패턴을 바꾸어 다른 생물로 변신하는 놀라운 능력을 설명하고 있다. (A)는 이러한 신체적/행동적 특성을 일컫는 '적응(adaptations)'이 적절하며, (B)는 여러 환경에서 다양한 모습으로 변할 수 있는 문어의 '다재다능한/다용도의(versatile)' 특성을 설명하는 단어가 적합하다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 주어진 철자를 사용하여 철자 수에 맞추어 각 1단어 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose, that is, without mental (A)__________ and without a deeper (B)__________ of Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is (C)__________ at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.explanation: 언어적 은유는 이해를 위해 정신적 노력(exertion)과 깊은 탐구(exploration)가 필요한 반면, 기술적 은유는 첫눈에 그 유용성이 분명(evident)해야 한다는 차이점을 설명하는 글입니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 밑줄 친 I don't think you are going to make it이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As I waited outside the locker room after a hard-fought basketball game, the coach called out to me, "David, walk with me." I figured he was going to tell me something important. He was going to select me to be the captain of the team, the leader I had always wanted to be. My heart was racing with anticipation. But when his next words hit my ears, everything changed. "We're going to have to send you home," he said coldly. "<u>I don't think you are going to make it</u>." I couldn't believe his decision. I tried to hold it together, but inside I was falling apart. A car would be waiting tomorrow morning to take me home. And just like that, it was over.
options: ④ You're worthy of being captain.
⑤ You're fully capable of achieving this.
questions.explanation: 주인공 데이비드는 자신이 팀의 주장이 될 것이라고 기대했지만, 코치는 차갑게 '너를 집으로 돌려보내야겠다'고 하며 '네가 (팀에 남거나 성공할 것이라고) 생각하지 않는다'고 말합니다. 이는 팀에서 방출되었거나 탈락했음을 의미하므로 ① '너는 해고다(팀에서 제외되었다)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 너는 해고다(제외되었다).
② 너는 다음에 득점할 것이다.
③ 너는 분명히 성공할 것이다.
④ 너는 주장이 될 자격이 있다.
⑤ 너는 이것을 성취할 충분한 능력이 있다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: "Trick-punishment" refers to a situation where scolding or punishment has the opposite effect of what was intended. Such punishment can actually lead to a child repeating negative behavior because the child experiences some form of attention or interaction through that behavior. For example, if a child feels lonely and engages in negative behavior to attract their parent's attention, scolding or punishment might reinforce that behavior instead. In this case, the child perceives scolding as a way of gaining attention, so the punishment does not suppress the behavior but instead causes it to be repeated. Therefore, "trick-punishment" describes a situation where punishment, implemented without understanding the child's psychological state or motivations, works contrary to its intended purpose. It means that parents should focus on reducing the attention to negatives while rewarding positive behaviors.
options: ① Effective Parenting Strategy to Avoid Trick-Punishment
② Keep Your Cool: How to Control Your Anger
③ Sticking to the Traditional Child Discipline
④ The Consequences of Continuous Scolding
⑤ What's New in Child Psychology?
questions.explanation: 이 글은 처벌이 의도와 반대 효과를 내는 '속임수 처벌(trick-punishment)'에 대해 설명하며, 아이의 심리적 상태를 이해하지 못한 처벌은 오히려 부정적 행동을 반복하게 만든다고 지적합니다. 결론적으로 부모가 부정적 행동에 대한 관심을 줄이고 긍정적 행동에 보상해야 한다고 조언하므로, 이를 피하기 위한 효과적인 양육 전략이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 속임수 처벌을 피하기 위한 효과적인 양육 전략
② 침착함을 유지하라: 화를 조절하는 방법
③ 전통적인 자녀 훈육 고수하기
④ 지속적인 꾸중의 결과
⑤ 아동 심리학의 새로운 소식은?

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: For a long time, people believed that colors were objective, physical properties of objects or of the light that bounced off ⓐ<u>them</u>. Even today, science teachers entertain their students with stories about Isaac Newton and his prism experiment, ⓑ<u>tell</u> them how different wavelengths of light produce the rainbow of hues around us. Most experts now agree that color, as commonly understood, doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but ⓒ<u>exists</u> in the eyes or minds of its viewers. They argue that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so ⓓ<u>would</u> everything else. In other words, there is no such thing as color; it only exists through the perception of people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective. Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and ⓔ<u>interpreted</u> by the brain.*hue: 색조
questions.explanation: ⓑ의 tell은 주절(science teachers entertain...) 뒤에서 부가적인 상황을 설명하는 분사구문의 형태가 되어야 합니다. 주어인 science teachers가 능동적으로 말해주는 것이므로 현재분사인 telling으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 23번]
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. For example, in a study about happiness, researchers might count how many times a person smiles, and in a memory study, they could measure how many items a person remembers after certain time periods. Asking people how many times they felt sad in the past year can provide data, but it may not be reliable due to memory errors or different definitions of sadness. Instead, a question like "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" can give a clearer answer. Similarly, rather than asking someone to rate how much they procrastinate asking, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" provides more concrete data. Questions that __________________________ help make abstract ideas clearer and keep research results consistent.
options: ① did not understand the essence
② can be interpreted in multiple ways
③ ask for specific, measurable answers
④ rely on people's voluntary participation
⑤ bring about dramatic emotional responses
questions.explanation: 이 글은 연구에서 추상적인 개념(행복, 슬픔, 미루기 등)을 명확하게 하기 위해 구체적이고 측정 가능한 질문을 던지는 것이 중요하다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 예시로 든 '아파서 결근한 횟수'나 '납부 기한을 넘긴 공과금 고지서 수' 등은 모두 구체적이고 수치화할 수 있는 답변을 요구하는 것들입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '구체적이고 측정 가능한 답변을 요구하는'이라는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 본질을 이해하지 못했다
② 여러 가지 방식으로 해석될 수 있다
③ 구체적이고 측정 가능한 답변을 요구한다
④ 사람들의 자발적인 참여에 의존한다
⑤ 극적인 감정적 반응을 불러일으킨다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 34번]
questions.passage: The widespread depiction of climate disasters on-screen may soon become irrelevant, as the very reality of climate change grows too immense and undeniable, potentially making the climate-fiction genre outdated. As the effects of global warming become increasingly visible and unavoidable, telling stories about climate change may no longer hold the same narrative power. Currently, we can still tell stories 'about' climate change because it seems like a distant or marginal issue. However, once the temperature rises by several degrees, its impacts will be so pervasive that no one will be able to distance themselves from it. When the world we experience becomes ____________________________, the genre itself loses its relevance. Why would we watch or read stories about a future we're already living in?
options: ③ an ideal world for everyone
④ a new world depicting futuristic life
⑤ the world portrayed in climate fiction
questions.explanation: 기후 변화가 실제 현실에서 너무나도 만연해지고 피할 수 없게 되면, 더 이상 기후 소설(climate fiction) 속의 이야기가 가상의 먼 미래 이야기가 아니게 됩니다. 우리가 겪는 현실 세계 자체가 '기후 소설 속에서 묘사되는 세계'와 같아질 때, 해당 장르는 더 이상 독자나 관객에게 먼 나라 이야기가 아닌 이미 살고 있는 현실이 되어버려 설득력을 잃는다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 이국적인 음악 세계
② 추상적인 사회적 개념
③ 모두를 위한 이상적인 세계
④ 미래 지향적 삶을 묘사하는 새로운 세계
⑤ 기후 소설에서 묘사된 세계

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 30번]
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won the Nobel Prize for recognizing the inherent limitations we face in terms of information, time, and cognitive capacity. Because we lack the resources to independently compute every answer, we distribute the burden of computation across society, solving problems slowly, generation by generation. Instead of needing to understand the intricate workings of energy technology we encounter, we only need to know _________________________. For example, you don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works - you just need to know how to use the interface and perform simple actions like pressing a button or flushing. What's transmitted, then, is not the detailed knowledge of how things function, but the instructions for how to use them. In this way, we don't need to carry all the information in our heads. Instead, we can focus our mental energy on a small part of a much larger, collective computation. We understand just enough to make use of the tools and technologies around us, contributing our small piece to a much larger societal "brain."
options: ① how to interact with it
③ how to process more information
④ how to perform accurate calculations
⑤ how problems are passed down across generations
questions.explanation: 인간은 인지 능력의 한계 때문에 모든 기술의 작동 원리를 다 알 필요가 없으며, 단지 그것을 어떻게 사용하는지(상호작용하는지)만 알면 된다는 내용입니다. 컴퓨터나 변기의 원리를 몰라도 버튼을 누르거나 물을 내리는 법만 알면 되듯이, 빈칸에는 '그것과 상호작용하는 방법'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그것과 상호작용하는 방법
② 기술이 어떻게 진화해 왔는지
③ 더 많은 정보를 처리하는 방법
④ 정확한 계산을 수행하는 방법
⑤ 세대를 거쳐 문제가 어떻게 전달되는지

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 35번]
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is not a crisis of resources, but of _________________________. This is what makes it so distressing: water, a resource that should be abundant, has been made scarce through governmental neglect, inadequate infrastructure, contamination, and unchecked urban expansion. Some cities waste more water through leaks than they supply to households. Even in the United States, an estimated 16 percent of freshwater is lost to leaks and theft, while in Brazil, that number rises to 40 percent. This selective scarcity highlights the deep inequalities between those who have access to water and those who do not, making worse global inequities. Today, 2.1 billion people lack access to safe drinking water, and 4.5 billion live without proper sanitation.
options: ⑤ rapid government responses to problems
questions.explanation: 오늘날의 물 위기는 자원의 부족 때문이 아니라 정부의 방치, 인프라 부족, 오염 등 관리와 책임의 문제라는 내용입니다. 풍부해야 할 자원이 정부의 무관심 등으로 인해 희소해졌다고 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 '정치적 의지와 책임'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 압도적인 공급
② 악화되는 기후 위기
③ 정치적 의지와 책임
④ 국가 간의 교육적 불평등
⑤ 문제에 대한 정부의 빠른 대응

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Adolescence is a crucial stage in human development characterized  by numerous physical, psychological, and cognitive changes. One of the most interesting aspects of this period is the biology of decision-making, especially the role of the prefrontal cortex(PFC). The prefrontal cortex is a region of the brain responsible for decision-making, emotional regulation, planning, and goal-setting. It is one of the last areas of the brain to mature, with the process extending into the early 20s. This late development has profound implications for adolescent decision-making, as the PFC plays a crucial role in assessing risks, considering long-term consequences, and controlling impulsive behaviors. During adolescence, there is a notable imbalance in the development of the PFC compared to other brain regions. The limbic system, which is involved in emotions and motivation, matures more quickly, resulting in a tendency for adolescents to ______________________________. This imbalance can lead to impulsive decision-making, sometimes with negative consequences.*impulsive: 충동적인
options: ① act more an logical reasoning
② be guided by long-term considerations
③ consider a casual relationship in detail
④ make decisions driven by careful analysis
⑤ be more emotionally reactive and likely to take risks
questions.explanation: 청소년기에는 의사개정과 감정 조절을 담당하는 전두엽(PFC)이 닞게 발달하는 반면, 감정과 동기를 담당하는 변엮계는 빨리 발달하여 불균형이 일어납니다. 이로 인해 청소년들은 감정적으로 덄 반응하고 위험을 감수하는 경향을 보이게 됩니다.
options_translation: 논리적 추론에 덄 의존하여 행동하다
장기적 고려 사항에 의해 인도되다
인과 관계를 상세히 고려하다
신중한 분석에 의해 결정을 내리다
감정적으로 덄 반응하고 위험을 감수할 가능성이 높다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. ⓐ<u>Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing</u>. ⓑ<u>The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us</u>. ⓒ<u>In order to live in a community-based society, people must not only be dedicated to their work but also take an interest in the lives of others</u>. ⓓ<u>We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity</u>. ⓔ<u>These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't</u>. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 중단 내에서의 사회적 지ᄁ를 모니터링하고 그에 따라 자존감이나 수치심 등의 감정을 달뀐다는 진화 심리학적 내용을 다루고 있습니다. ⓒ번 문장은 개인의 업무 헌신과 타인에 대한 관심을 언급하고 있어, 중단 내 팄판 모니터링과 감정 발달이라는 전체 흐름과는 거리가 멀습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. ⓐ<u>However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect</u>. ⓑ<u>They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time</u>. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? ⓒ<u>Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks</u>. ⓓ<u>To understand the true nature of anything, one must examine the actual, tangible objects that surround us</u>. ⓔ<u>Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses</u>.
questions.explanation: 플라톤의 형이상학(실재론)에 따르면 우리가 눈으로 보는 현실 세계의 물체들은 불완전한 복사본일 뿐이며, 진짜 실재(이데아)는 보이지 않는 완벽한 세계에 존재합니다. 따라서 현실의 구체적이고 만질 수 있는 대상을 조사해야 한다는 ④번 문장은 플라톤의 사상과 정반대되는 내용이므로 흐름상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways.
ordered_passages: (A) Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon.

(B) Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose.

(C) Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 디지털 은유가 언어적 은유와 다르다는 점을 언급합니다. (B)에서 먼저 언어적 은유의 수동적인 특성과 청중의 인지적 노력을 설명합니다. (A)에서 'on the other hand'를 사용하여 기술적 은유의 능동적인 특성을 대조적으로 제시합니다. (C)에서 기술 창작자들이 직관성을 중시하는 이유를 다시 셰익스피어(언어적 은유의 예시)와 비교하며 글을 마무리하는 것이 논리적으로 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Depression is a complex condition. Research has shown that depression is associated with changes in the structure and function of the brain. (A) These changes can affect the production, function, and levels of neurotransmitters in the brain. (B) Neurotransmitters like serotonin, dopamine, and norepinephrine act as messengers, transmitting signals between nerve cells. (C) With depression, there may be low levels of neurotransmitters like serotonin, which can result in symptoms like low mood, lack of pleasure, and disturbed sleep. (D) Genes can also play a role in the development of depression, and there is a higher risk of depression in individuals with a family history of the condition. (E) Therefore, understanding the multifaceted nature of depression is crucial for developing effective treatment approaches.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, depression is likely influenced by genetic factors as well.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부((A)부터 (C)까지)는 우울증의 뇌 과학적 원인인 뇌 구조 변화와 신경전달물질에 대해 설명합니다. 주어진 문장은 'However'를 통해 화제를 전환하며 우울증이 유전적 요인에 의해서도 영향을 받을 수 있음을 제시합니다. (D) 위치 뒤의 문장에서 '유전자(Genes)'와 '가족력(family history)'에 대한 구체적인 부연 설명이 시작되므로, 주어진 문장은 (D) 즉 ④번에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: For many of us, fitting exercise into a busy schedule is a constant struggle. (A) Between work, family, and other obligations, there often seems to be no time for a dedicated workout. (B) Some people argue that the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores come into play. (C) For example, brief moments of activity, like squats while waiting for coffee, aren't usually enough to make a meaningful impact on health. (D) Even when we attempt to incorporate exercise into chores, time pressures often make it hard to stay consistent. While small adjustments are helpful, replacing structured exercise with everyday tasks is unrealistic for many. (E) Finding time for regular physical activity still requires careful planning and prioritization.
questions.insertion_sentence: Although this may be true, it typically don't provide enough physical activity to serve as a substitute for regular exercise.
questions.explanation: (B) 문장에서 집안일에 미니 운동을 통합하는 것의 장점이 언급됩니다. 주어진 문장의 'this'는 앞서 언급된 미니 운동의 장점을 지칭하며, '비록 이것이 사실일지라도, 규칙적인 운동을 대체할 만큼 충분한 활동을 제공하지 못한다'며 한계를 지적합니다. (C) 뒤에 나오는 '커피를 기다리는 동안 스쿼트를 하는 것과 같은 짧은 활동이 건강에 큰 영향을 주지 못한다'는 구체적인 예시가 이 한계를 뒷받침하므로, 주어진 문장은 (C) 즉 ③번에 들어가야 합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: When I worked for a major consumer goods company, I quickly realized the reason behind the strategy of offering multiple versions of the same product. (A) If the company only sold one version, some customers might have been willing to pay more for additional features, meaning the company would miss out on potential revenue. (B) Offering two versions - one basic and one with more features - creates a comparison for the consumer. (C) Some people may choose the less expensive version of the two options. (D) Customers often opt for the middle-priced version, thinking it offers the best balance of features and price, unaware that the existence of the third, higher-priced option has influenced their decision. (E) This strategy effectively increases sales of the mid-tier product by leveraging the perception of value.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the introduction of a third, more advanced and expensive version than the others changes the game.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기업이 동일 제품의 여러 버전을 제공하는 전략에 대해 설명합니다. (B)와 (C)에서는 두 가지 버전(기본형과 기능 추가형)이 있을 때 소비자가 비교를 통해 선택하는 상황을 설명합니다. 주어진 문장은 세 번째의 더 비싸고 진보된 버전이 도입되면서 '판도가 바뀐다(changes the game)'는 전환을 나타냅니다. (D)에서 고객들이 세 번째 옵션 때문에 중간 가격의 제품을 선택하게 된다는 결과가 이어지므로, 주어진 문장은 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.
questions.summary_sentence: Even though life consists of (A)__________ interactions that make it highly complex, it tends to stabilize by (B)__________ outcomes to a few defined states.
questions.explanation: 지문은 생명체가 분자 간의 무수히 많은 상호작용으로 이루어진 복잡한 고차원 시스템이지만, 실제로는 '운하화(canalization)'라는 과정을 통해 결과가 몇 가지 안정적인 상태로 좁혀진다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 요약문의 (A)에는 상호작용의 많음을 나타내는 'numerous(수많은)' 혹은 'enormous(거대한/막대한)' 등이 적절하며, (B)에는 결과를 몇 가지 상태로 줄이거나 한정한다는 의미인 'limiting(제한함)'이 적절합니다. 가장 적합한 조합은 ⑤번입니다.
options_translation: ① 거대한 ... 확장함으로써
② 셀 수 없는 ... 확장함으로써
③ 제한된 ... 제한함으로써
④ 거의 없는 ... 제한함으로써
⑤ 수많은 ... 제한함으로써

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
questions.summary_sentence: Although some countries have strict (A)__________ for brain death when considering organ donation, many people fear the possibilities for someone else to make a(n) (B)__________ diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 장기 기증을 위한 뇌사 판정 시 몇몇 국가들이 엄격한 지침을 두고 있는 이유와 그 영향을 설명하고 있습니다. 지문에서 'tougher guidelines', 'strict regulations' 등을 언급하고 있으므로 (A)에는 'criteria(기준)'가 적절합니다. 또한, 대중들이 장기 적출을 위해 뇌사 판정이 너무 일찍 내려지는 것('premature diagnosis')을 두려워한다고 했으므로 (B)에는 'hasty(성급한)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 의심 ... 정확한
② 의심 ... 성급한
③ 기준 ... 정확한
④ 기준 ... 성급한
⑤ 표준 ... 종합적인

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 조건에 맞게 써서 제목을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson suggests that we tend to understand the world by focusing in on particular features within it. Take platypuses. We might zoom in so closely to their fur that each hair appears different. We might also zoom out to the extent where it appears as a single, uniform object. We might take the platypus as an individual, or we might treat it as part of a larger unit such as a species or an ecosystem. It's possible to move between many of these perspectives, although we may need some additional tools and skills to zoom in on individual pieces of hair or zoom out to entire ecosystems. Crucially, however, we can only take up one perspective at a time. We can pay attention to the varied behavior of individual animals, look at what unites them into a single species, or look at them as part of bigger ecological patterns. Every possible perspective involves emphasizing certain aspects and ignoring others.
questions.summary_sentence: One (A)P_________ at a Time: The Power of Selective (B)F_________
subjective_conditions: • 주어진 찠자로 시작하는 한 단어림 쒸 경
• 글 셍에서 찾아 쒸 경
• 필요하면 어형 봀형 가능
• 찠자 및 어법 오류 인정하지 않음
questions.explanation: 지문은 한 번에 하나의 관점(perspective)뫌 가질 수 있음을 강조하며, 특정한 특징에 중심을 두는 것(focusing)의 힘에 대해 말하고 있다. 글의 핵심 어휘인 perspective와 focusing을 사용하여 제목을 완성할 수 있다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하도록 A와 B의 대화문을 완성할 때, 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓒ 중에서 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 단어 하나를 골라 바꿔 쓰시오.
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information ─ a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
subjective_conditions: • 문맥상 쓰이이 적절하지 않은 ⓣ어의 기호(ⓐ,ⓑ,ⓒ)림 쒸 경
• 문맥상 쓰이이 적절하도록 수정하여 하나의 단어림 쒸 경
• 찠자 및 어법 오류 인정하지 않음
questions.subjective_answer_format: <댁화문>A: Our memories are reconstructed based on what we know, now stored like a video. We see the world through our assumptions and experiences, which can make eyewitness testimony ⓐᄇunreliableᅡ.B: So, does that mean our memories are often altered?A: Yes. Our brains simplify information to make it easier to process. However, this means we might remember events ⓑᄇaccuratelyᅡ.B: It makes sense now why people can have ⓒᄇdifferentᅡ recollections of the same event, influenced by their assumptions and past experiences. (1) 문맥상 쓰이이 적절하지 않은 단어의 기호: ______(2) 문맥상 쓰이이 적절하도록 수정한 단어   : ______________________
questions.explanation: 글의 내용에 따르면 우리의 기억은 실제 사건을 그대로 재생하는 것이 아니라 쵔상적인 관념으로 재구성하기 때문에, 세상을 있는 그대로 밴 수 없고 오류가 생길 수 있다. 따라서 대화문의 ⓑ accurately(정확하게)는 문맥상 'differently(다르게)' 또는 'inaccurately(부정확하게)'로 바꿈어야 한다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Nearly everything has to go through your mouth to get to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and prevent it from harm - with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. ① From the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. ② What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and a reflection of what is happening in other parts of the body. ③ Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease that affects the entire body. ④ So, regular medical check-ups are not necessary for your health. ⑤ The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, posing serious health risks. *microorganism: 미생물
questions.explanation: 구강 건강이 전신 건강과 깊은 관계가 있다는 내용의 글입니다. 따라서 ④번의 '정기적인 건강 검진이 필요하지 않다'는 내용은 구강 건강의 중요성을 강조하는 전체 흐름과 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Digital technologies are fundamentally tied to metaphors, but they differ significantly from linguistic metaphors. Linguistic metaphors are passive, requiring the audience to consciously engage with the proposed idea. ①For example, in Shakespeare's metaphor "time is a beggar," understanding it needs cognitive effort and deeper engagement with the text. ②Conversely, technological metaphors are active and often forceful, as they are realized in digital artifacts that actively influence users' perceptions. ③Creators of technology cannot expect users to wonder how the metaphor operates; instead, the technology's appeal lies in its apparent usefulness. ④For this reason, users have difficulty using technologies without cognitive effort or even awareness. ⑤In contrast, Shakespeare is cherished partly because his works demand thoughtful consideration, making their meanings less immediately clear.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 언어적 은유가 독자의 의식적인 인지적 노력을 요구하는 것과 달리, 기술적 은유는 그 유용성과 직관성 때문에 사용자가 별다른 인지적 노력 없이도 쉽게 기술을 사용할 수 있게 한다는 차이점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '사용자가 인지적 노력이나 의식 없이는 기술을 사용하는 데 어려움을 겪는다'는 ④번 문장은 글의 핵심 내용(인지적 노력 없이도 사용 가능함)과 정반대의 설명을 하고 있으므로 흐름상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. ①When people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. ②For example, this is why people who look more competent, such as if they wear glasses, are more likely to be hired in leadership positions. ③Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. ④That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. ⑤In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 논리적인 검토보다는 직관적이고 무의식적인 첫인상이 상황을 더 정확하게 파악할 수 있다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 그러나 ②번 문장은 안경을 쓴 사람이 유능해 보여서 채용될 가능성이 높다는 내용으로, 이는 첫인상의 '정확성'이 아니라 첫인상에 의한 '선입견'이나 '사회적 통념'에 관한 사례이므로 글의 전체 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. They do well enough in school to keep advancing. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ends with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now lack a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when the journey really begins. When school is finished, ________________________________. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career are likely to stop progressing as a result.
options: ① you are the one who is in charge of your growth
② a well-run company will lead you to grow step by step
③ a new chapter of your life will be designed by a good mentor
④ what you learned in school will guide you for the rest of your life
⑤ you should be free from the pressure that pushes you to move forward
questions.explanation: 이 글은 학교 교육이 끝난 홄에도 개인이 수숐로 성장에 대한 책임을 지고 노력해야 한다는 내용입니다. 빈칸 둀 문장에서 개인이 수숐로 헌신하고 시간겼 에너지를 쏟아야 한다고 하였으므로, 빈칸에는 "당신이 바로 자신의 성장을 책임지는 사람이다"라는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 바로 성장을 책임지는 사람이다
② 잘 운영되는 회사가 당신을 차근차근 성장하도록 이끌 것이다
③ 당신 인생의 새로운 장은 훌륭한 멘토에 의해 설계될 것이다
④ 학교에서 배운 것이 남은 삶 동안 당신을 인도할 것이다
⑤ 당신은 앞으로 나아가도록 다그치는 압박감에서 벗어나야 한다

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Therefore, ____________________________________.*procrastinator: 미루는 사람
options: ① quantitative data are usually unreliable and should be avoided
② research should conform to the highest standards of data analysis
③ specific questions can improve the reliability of quantitative data
④ focusing on abstract concepts helps yield clearer quantitative results
⑤ this explains why it's essential to focus on qualitative data instead
questions.explanation: 글은 추상적인 질문(얼마나 슬픈가)보다는 구체적인 질문(아파서 결근한 횟수)이 더 신뢰할 수 있는 정량적 데이터를 생성한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 구체적인 질문이 정량적 데이터의 신뢰도를 높일 수 있다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 정량적 데이터는 밴체로 신뢰할 수 없으므로 피해야 한다
② 연구는 데이터 분석의 가장 높은 지준을 중수해야 한다
③ 구체적인 질문은 정량적 데이터의 신뢰도를 향상시킬 수 있다
④ 추상적인 개념에 중심을 두는 것이 더 명확한 정량적 결과를 내는 데 도움이 된다
⑤ 이것은 왜 정성적 데이터에 중심을 두는 것이 필수적인지를 설명해 준다

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A notable feature of the visual system is its ability to ⓐ<u>adapt</u>. Psychologist George M. Stratton demonstrated this through an impressive self-experiment. He wore special glasses that inverted his vision, literally flipping his view of the world upside down for several days. Initially, this posed significant challenges-simple tasks like eating with a fork became ⓑ<u>difficult</u>. However, over time, his visual system adapted to the new stimuli from his environment, and he began to function ⓒ<u>poorly</u>, even perceiving things right-side up when he focused. When he finally removed the glasses, he faced new difficulties, such as reaching for objects with the ⓓ<u>wrong</u> hand. Fortunately, Stratton's perception ⓔ<u>readjusted</u> quickly, and his vision returned to normal within a day.
questions.explanation: 실험 과정에서 시간이 지남에 따라 시각 체계가 환경의 새로운 자극에 '적응(adapted)'하게 되었으므로, 기능이 '서투르게(poorly)' 작동하는 것이 아니라 '제대로/정상적으로(properly/well)' 작동하기 시작했다고 하는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We ⓐ<u>reconstruct</u> memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more ⓑ<u>efficient</u> way to store information ─ a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail ⓒ<u>struggle</u> to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely ⓓ<u>advocated</u> the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing. Our memories fall short of an ⓔ<u>objective</u> representation of the world.\n*retrieve: 상기하다 **primacy: 우위성
questions.explanation: 우리의 기억이 실제 사건을 그대로 보여주는 것이 아니라 추상적인 표상을 통해 재구성된다는 사실은 목격자 증언이 법적으로 가지는 우위성(정확성 및 신뢰성)을 '옹호(advocated)'하는 것이 아니라 오히려 '약화시키거나(undermined/weakened)' 도전하는 근거가 됩니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Alvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. Trick-punishments appear when the child, usually one who does not receive enough attention from their parents, as they spend little time with their child and don't know how to reinforce positive behaviour, learns that they receive more attention by doing things ⓐ<u>wrong</u>. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will ⓑ<u>cease</u> this behavior toward his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a ⓒ<u>different</u> strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to ⓓ<u>reward</u> the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments; they can turn the situation on its head by focusing on the positives and not giving so much ⓔ<u>prominence</u> to the negatives.
questions.explanation: 부모의 관심을 받지 못하는 아이에게 꾸지람(trick-punishment)은 관심의 한 형태로 인식됩니다. 외로움을 느끼는 아이에게는 투명 인간 취급을 받는 것보다 혼나는 것이 낫기 때문에, 동생을 때리는 나쁜 행동을 통해 관심을 끌려고 할 것입니다. 따라서 이러한 행동을 '중단할(cease)' 것이 아니라 '계속하거나 반복할' 것이므로 ⓑ가 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 2024 K-Pop Cover Dance Contest에 관한 안내문의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: 2024 K-Pop Cover Dance Contest Good news for K-Pop fans in Canada!
