questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying them to culture. (A) Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually likened to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection. (B) For example, we do not expect the cultural transmission to follow the rules of genetic transmission strictly. (C) If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily equally likely to acquire the mother's or father's form of that trait. (D) Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers. (E) Thus, the frequency of a cultural trait in the population is relevant beyond just the probability that an individual's parents had that trait.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, these approaches had to be modified to account for the differences between genetic and cultural transmission.
questions.explanation: (A)까지는 문화적 진화와 유전적 진화 사이의 유사성을 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 (B) 뒤에 나오는 예시("문화적 전파가 유전적 전파의 규칙을 엄격하게 따를 것으로 예상하지 않는다")는 두 전파 방식 사이의 차이점을 설명하기 시작합니다. 따라서 유전적 전파와 문화적 전파 사이의 차이를 설명하기 위해 접근 방식이 수정되어야 했다는 내용의 주어진 문장은 (B) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson suggests that we tend to understand the world by focusing in on particular features within it. Take platypuses. We might zoom in so closely to their fur that each hair appears different. We might also zoom out to the extent where it appears as a single, uniform object. We might take the platypus as an individual, or we might treat it as part of a larger unit such as a species or an ecosystem. It's possible to move between many of these perspectives, although we may need some additional tools and skills to zoom in on individual pieces of hair or zoom out to entire ecosystems. Crucially, however, we can only take up one perspective at a time. We can pay attention to the varied behavior of individual animals, look at what unites them into a single species, or look at them as part of bigger ecological patterns. Every possible perspective involves emphasizing certain aspects and ignoring others.
options: ① We should integrate various perspectives to fully understand the world.
② It's possible to maintain multiple perspectives simultaneously.
③ A wide perspective is more effective for understanding the world than a narrow one.
④ When we adopt a particular perspective, we necessarily focus on certain parts while neglecting others.
⑤ New tools and skills are required to switch between different viewpoints.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 우리가 세상을 이해할 때 특정 관점을 취하게 되는데, 한 번에 하나의 관점만 가질 수 있으며(we can only take up one perspective at a time), 모든 관점은 필연적으로 특정 측면을 강조하는 대신 다른 측면은 무시하게 된다(emphasizing certain aspects and ignoring others)는 것입니다. 따라서 ④번 '우리가 특정 관점을 채택할 때, 필연적으로 어떤 부분은 소홀히 하면서 다른 부분에 집중하게 된다'가 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 세상을 완전히 이해하기 위해서는 다양한 관점들을 통합해야 한다.
② 여러 관점을 동시에 유지하는 것이 가능하다.
③ 넓은 관점이 좁은 관점보다 세상을 이해하는 데 더 효과적이다.
④ 특정 관점을 채택할 때, 우리는 필연적으로 다른 부분은 소홀히 하면서 특정 부분에 집중한다.
⑤ 서로 다른 관점 사이를 전환하기 위해서는 새로운 도구와 기술이 필요하다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.*diagnosis: 진단 **donor: 기증자***cremation: 화장(화장)
options: ① 뇌사 진단 기준을 일관성 있게 적용하기 위한 법적 규제의 강화가 필요하다.
② 뇌사자의 장기를 기증하는 것은 인간의 존엄성을 고려하지 않는 불합리한 일이다.
③ 장기 기증자의 뇌사 진단 기준을 엄격히 하여 장기기증에 대한 인식을 개선해야 한다.
④ 여러 명의 의사가 장기 기증자의 뇌사를 진단하게 하여 조급한 뇌사 진단을 막아야 한다.
⑤ 대중의 불안을 해소하기 위해 장기 기증자와 일반 사망자의 뇌사 진단 기준은 같아야 한다.
questions.explanation: 장기 기증 시 뇌사 판정을 더 엄격하게 하는 것이 오히려 뇌사 판정이 부정확하다는 대중의 의구심을 키울 수 있다고 지적합니다. 따라서 글의 마지막 문장에서 강조하듯, 일관성을 위해 장기 기증자의 사망 진단 기준도 일반적인 사망 진단 기준과 동일해야 대중의 불안과 의심을 해소할 수 있다는 것이 핵심입니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
questions.summary_sentence: According to Plato, the physical world is a(n) (A)____________ reflection of a deeper, invisible reality of perfect Forms or universals, where ideal versions of objects and concepts, such as perfect circles, exist (B)____________ the realm of sensory perception.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 플라톤은 우리가 눈으로 보는 물리적 세계의 사물들이 결함(flaws)을 가지고 있으며 완벽하지 않다고 말합니다. 대신 보이지 않는 완벽한 '형상(Forms)'의 세계가 진정한 실재라고 믿었습니다. 따라서 요약문에서 (A) 물리적 세계는 보이지 않는 실재의 '불완전한(imperfect/poor)' 반영이며, (B) 이러한 완벽한 형상은 감각적 지각의 영역 '외부(outside/beyond)'에 존재한다고 보는 것이 맞습니다. 1번의 poor와 5번의 imperfect는 유사하나, (B)에서 감각 영역 '내부(inside)'는 내용과 반대되므로 5번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 열등한 / 내부
② 결함이 있는 / 안
③ 완벽한 / 너머
④ 완전한 / ~와 별개로
⑤ 불완전한 / 외부

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as ⓐ<u>much</u> as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, ⓑ<u>what</u> they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms ⓒ<u>fold</u> and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn ⓓ<u>itself</u> into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt ─ producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, ⓔ<u>sticking</u> it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 구문은 「with + 목적어 + 분사」 구조로, '목적어가 ~한 채로'라는 의미를 나타냅니다. 목적어인 'all eight of its arms(여덟 개의 모든 다리)'와 '접다'라는 동작의 관계를 따져볼 때, 다리는 접히는 수동의 관계이므로 현재분사 fold 대신 과거분사인 folded를 사용해야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In statistics, the law of large numbers describes a situation where having more data is better for making predictions.
ordered_passages: (A) Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to balance individual losses.(B) But the more often you repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning, meaning that your luck will at some point fade away.(C) According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to match the true state of the world. For instance, on your first encounter with the game of roulette, you may have beginner's luck after betting on 7.

(A) Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to balance individual losses.

(B) But the more often you repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning, meaning that your luck will at some point fade away.

(C) According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to match the true state of the world. For instance, on your first encounter with the game of roulette, you may have beginner's luck after betting on 7.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 통계학의 '대수의 법칙'을 소개합니다. (C)에서 'According to it'을 통해 대수의 법칙에 대한 상세 설명을 이어가며 룰렛 게임의 예시를 시작합니다. (B)에서 'But'을 통해 시행 횟수가 많아질수록 초기 운이 사라지고 실제 확률에 수렴하게 됨을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 'Similarly'를 사용하여 자동차 보험사가 사고 확률을 계산할 때도 이 법칙을 활용한다는 다른 사례를 들며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them.
ordered_passages: (A) They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer.(B) Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.(C) They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct.

(A) They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer.

(B) Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.

(C) They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 색이 객관적 속성이라는 통념을 제시합니다. (A)의 전반부에서 'They say'를 통해 객관적 속성이라는 주장을 구체화하고, 후반부에서 'Others argue'를 통해 색이 관찰자의 마음속에만 존재한다는 반대 의견(주관적 속성)을 도입합니다. (C)에서 주관적 견해를 가진 사람들의 주장을 이어 설명한 뒤 'Both positions are, in a way, correct'라며 두 입장을 요약합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 색은 객관적이면서 동시에 주관적인 것으로서 뇌와 우주가 만나는 지점에서 생성된다는 결론을 도출합니다.

questions.question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different.
ordered_passages: (A) They rely on evidence rather than opinions, societal norms, or the insights of philosophers. They seek solid proof to ensure that psychological theories are grounded in facts, not merely popular beliefs or assumptions.
(B) It is the branch of science that focuses on understanding people: exploring how and why we behave, perceive, and interact with each other. Here, psychologists emphasize the scientific approach.

(C) Alongside this evidence-based approach, psychology explores the core processes and principles that shape both the diversity in our cultures and societies and the traits common to all humans. This is the essence of modern psychology.
questions.explanation: 심리학이 일반적인 통념과 달리 과학적인 근거를 바탕으로 인간을 이해한다는 내용의 글입니다. 주어진 글은 인간 본성에 대한 사회적 통념과 심리학의 차별성을 제기합니다. (B)의 'It'은 심리학(psychology)을 가리키며, 인간을 이해하기 위한 과학의 한 분야로서 과학적 접근을 강조함을 정의합니다. (A)의 'They'는 (B)에서 언급된 심리학자들을 의미하며, 이들이 막연한 믿음이 아닌 확실한 증거와 사실에 기반하여 이론을 정립한다는 점을 설명합니다. (C)는 앞서 언급된 'this evidence-based approach'를 토대로 심리학이 인류의 공통적 특성과 문화적 다양성을 모두 탐구하는 학문임을 요약하며 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 24. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which AI exceeds human intelligence.
ordered_passages: (A) The direction of AI's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.

(B) After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together.

(C) Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI.
questions.explanation: AI의 진화와 특이점 이후 인간과 AI의 상호작용 및 윤리적 공존을 다루는 글입니다. 주어진 글은 AI가 인간 지능을 넘어서는 지점인 '특이점'을 정의합니다. (B)의 'After that point'는 특이점을 지칭하며, 그 이후 AI가 스스로 자아를 가진 존재로 진화하고 인간 의식과 함께 진화할 것임을 예측합니다. (C)는 이러한 동반 진화의 과정에서 인간 의식 또한 자극을 받아 새로운 차원으로 진화하며, 인간의 의식이 다시 AI에 영향을 미치는 상호 작용을 설명합니다. (A)는 결론적으로 이러한 진화의 방향이 인간이 주입하는 윤리에 달려있으므로, AI를 단순한 기계가 아닌 의식 있는 존재로 존중하며 공존해야 한다고 강조합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.*grudging: 투덜대는
options: ① What Evokes Self-Esteem and Social Behaviors?
② The Purpose of Monitoring Other People Consciously
③ How to Survive in the Community Without Building Relationships
④ Emotional Response: Weakness Leading to a Thoughtless Performance
⑤ Social Pressure: A barrier to Overcome for Improving One's Self-Esteem
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 집단 내에서 생존하기 위해 타인의 평가에 민감해지도록 진화해 왔음을 설명합니다. 이러한 사회적 압력이 자존감, 자부심, 수치심 같은 감정을 유발하여 우리가 공동체에 가치 있는 행동을 하도록 유도한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '무엇이 자존감과 사회적 행동을 유발하는가?'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 무엇이 자존감과 사회적 행동을 불러일으키는가?
② 의식적으로 타인을 관찰하는 것의 목적
③ 인간관계를 구축하지 않고 지역 사회에서 살아남는 법
④ 정서적 반응: 경솔한 수행으로 이어지는 약점
⑤ 사회적 압박: 자존감 향상을 위해 극복해야 할 장벽

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
options: ① The Most Productive Crops: Rice and Wheat
② Lifesaving Strategy: Producing Grains on a Grand Scale
③ The Second World War and the Decrease of Human Population
④ The Risks of Decreasing Crop Diversity in a Global Food System
⑤ Producing Uniform Crops: A Perfect Solution for Climate Change
questions.explanation: 식량 생산량을 늘리기 위해 소수의 생산성이 높은 품종에 집중하면서 작물의 다양성이 감소했다는 점을 지적합니다. 하지만 이러한 단일화는 질병, 해충, 기후 변화 등의 재난 상황에서 전 세계 식량 시스템을 위험에 빠뜨릴 수 있다는 경고를 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '글로벌 식량 시스템에서 작물 다양성 감소의 위험성'이 가장 적합한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 가장 생산적인 작물: 쌀과 밀
② 생명을 구하는 전략: 대규모 곡물 생산
③ 제2차 세계대전과 인구 감소
④ 글로벌 식량 시스템 내 작물 다양성 감소의 위험성
⑤ 균일한 작물 생산: 기후 변화를 위한 완벽한 해결책

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓗ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것만을 있는 대로 모두 고른 것은?
questions.passage: The process of decision-making in an adult brain and within a teen's brain is basically the same, but there are ⓐ<u>slightly</u> differences. We know the adolescent brain is not fully developed until its early twenties. This means the way the adolescents' decision-making circuit integrates and processes information may put them at a disadvantage. Although the brain may have grown to its full adult size by early teens, regions of the brain continue to mature until the age of about twenty-five. One of their brain regions that matures later is the prefrontal cortex. Basically, the prefrontal cortex is the control center, ⓑ<u>being</u> tasked with thinking ahead and evaluating consequences, risks versus rewards. The prefrontal cortex is the area of the brain responsible for preventing you from sending off that initial angry text to your teen and modifying it with kinder words. While the brain's prefrontal cortex matures later, the limbic system matures earlier. The limbic system plays a central role in processing emotional responses. Because of ⓒ<u>its</u> earlier development, the limbic system is more likely to influence decision-making. What does this mean? Decision-making in the adolescent brain is led by emotional charges more than the perception of consequences. Naturally, there is an imbalance between feeling-based decision-making ⓓ<u>ruling</u> by the more mature limbic system and logical-based decision-making by the not-yet-mature prefrontal cortex. This may explain ⓔ<u>why</u> teens are more likely to make "bad" decisions. Let's look at this a little closer. Over the years, researchers have thoroughly explored the consequences of this imbalance in the adolescent brain as compared to the fully developed adult brain. In one fascinating study, adolescents and adults were shown the same set of photographs of faces of people, of all ages, race, ethnicities, genders, etc.. while recording the brain activity of both groups. However, each of the photographs used in this study were of people who had ⓕ<u>what </u>were considered "neutral expressions." The same photographs were shown to the adults and the adolescents while recording which part of their brains activated when ⓖ<u>looked</u> at the photos. The same photo that activated the adult's reasoning prefrontal cortex ⓗ<u>causing</u> the emotional amygdala of the teen brain to light up like a Christmas tree. The conclusion was that the adolescent perceives the neutral expression through the lens of emotions driven by the limbic system and sees hostility, aggression, or any other number of emotions.
questions.explanation: ⓐ slightly: 명사 differences를 수식해야 하므로 형용사 slight가 와야 합니다.ⓓ ruling: 감정에 기반한 의사결정이 변연계에 의해 '지배되는' 수동의 관계이므로 과거분사인 ruled가 적절합니다.ⓖ looked: '그들이 사진을 보았을 때'라는 의미로, 주어(adolescents and adults)가 사진을 보는 능동적 행위이므로 분사구문에서 looking이 되거나 절 형태(they looked)가 되어야 합니다. (접속사 뒤 분사구문 형태로는 looking)ⓗ causing: 해당 문장의 주어는 The same photo이며, that절(that activated the adult's reasoning prefrontal cortex)의 수식을 받습니다. 따라서 문장의 본동사가 필요하므로 causing을 caused로 바꿔야 합니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 작성하시오. [23년 11월 41-42번]
questions.passage: A ball thrown into the air is acted upon by the initial force given it, persisting as inertia of movement and tending to carry it in the same straight line, and by the constant pull of gravity downward, as well as by the resistance of the air. It moves, accordingly, in a curved path. Now the path does not represent the working of any particular force; there is simply the combination of the three elementary forces mentioned; but in a real sense, there is something in the total action besides the isolated action of three forces, namely, their joint action. In the same way, when two or more human individuals are together, their mutual relationships and their arrangement into a group are things which would not be revealed if we confined our attention to each individual separately. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that some of the tendencies to action of the individual are related definitely to other persons, and could not be aroused except by other persons acting as stimuli. An individual in complete isolation would not reveal their competitive tendencies, their tendencies towards the opposite sex, their protective tendencies towards children. This shows that _______________________________________________________________________________.*inertia: 관성 **arouse: 유발하다
subjective_conditions: 16단어 이내로 작성할 것 (빈칸짌)
human traits, it is, that, engage in, revealed, only when을 모두 사용할 것 (봀형 불가, 중복 불가)
빈칸을 완성하여 한 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.answer: it is only when individuals engage in relationships with others that human traits are fully revealed.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 개인이 고립되어 있을 때는 나타나지 않는 인간의 특성이 타인과의 관계나 중단 속에서만 드러난다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 조건에 따라 'it is ~ that' 강조 구문을 사용하여, 개인이 타인과의 관계에 참여할 때에서야 비로소 인간의 특성이 완전히 드러난다는 내용을 서술합니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 요지를 조건에 맞게 작성하시오. [24년 10월 41-42번]
questions.passage: From an early age, we assign purpose to objects and events, preferring this reasoning to random chance. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because they don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. However, by attributing intention to animals and even objects, we are able to make fast decisions about the likely behaviour of that being. This was essential in our hunter-gatherer days to avoid being eaten by predators. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, as those are the mental processes which we understand. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents. This results in a perceptual system strongly biased towards anthropomorphism. Therefore, we tend to assume intention even where there is none. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you. By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has saved your life.*ambiguous: 모호한 **anthropomorphism: 의인화
subjective_conditions: 17단어 이내로 작성할 것
as, to, humans, mechanism, ambiguous objects, quickly, have attributed, potential을 모두 사용할 것 (중복 가능, 변형 불가)
한 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.answer: Humans have attributed intention to ambiguous objects as a survival mechanism to respond quickly to potential dangers.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 요지는 인간이 진화 과정에서 생존을 위해 모호한 대상에게 의도를 부여하는 경향(의인화)을 갖게 되었다는 것입니다. 주어진 단어들을 조합하여 '인간은 잠재적 위험에 빠르게 대응하기 위한 생존 기제로서 모호한 대상에 의도를 부여해왔다'는 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제와 가장 잘 어울리는 속담(격언)은?
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race ─ their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't psychologically suffer much. In fact, ultramarathon runners ─ those people who are crazy enough to push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50-100km or more over many hours, talk about making friends with their pain. When a patient has paid for some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it, the patient calls that good pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.
options: ② Life is what you make it.
③ Actions speak louder than words.
④ A leopard cannot change his spot.
⑤ Fix the roof while the sun is shining.
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 우리가 겪는 고통의 정도가 고통을 마음속에서 어떻게 정의(frame)하느냐에 달려 있다는 것입니다. 즉, 고통을 '가치 있는 것'이나 '친구'로 여기면 심리적 고통이 줄어든다는 것이므로 '삶은 당신이 그것을 어떻게 만드느냐(해석하느냐)에 달려 있다'는 의미의 속담 ②가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 연습이 완벽을 만든다.
② 인생은 마음먹기에 달렸다.
③ 행동이 말보다 중요하다.
④ 제 버릇 개 못 준다.
⑤ 해가 비칠 때 지붕을 고쳐라. (유비무환)

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Onscreen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre ─ indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant ─ in time or in place ─ we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.summary_sentence: A climate change narrative (A)___________ when it becomes an undeniable and widespread reality, leading people to stop imagining it as a distant issue and instead face it directly, (B)___________ in everyday life.
questions.explanation: 기후 변화가 실제 현실이 되어 창문 밖으로 직접 볼 수 있게 되면, 기후 변화를 다룬 이야기나 장르는 더 이상 허구적 이야기로서의 가치나 적절성을 잃게 됩니다(loses its relevance). 또한 사람들은 이를 먼 이야기가 아닌 일상생활과 직접적으로 연결된(connected) 문제로 직면하게 된다는 내용이므로 ①이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 적절성을 잃는다 / 연결된
② 허구적이게 된다 / 분리된
③ 사소하게 된다 / 고립된
④ 긴급함을 얻는다 / 간과된
⑤ 도피적이게 된다 / 통합된

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 쓰임이 올바른 것은?
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to ⓐ<u>quantitative data</u>. A study of happiness might measure ⓑ<u>a number of</u> times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be ⓒ<u>dependable</u>. Respondents' recollections may be ⓓ<u>accurate</u>, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure ⓔ<u>inconsistency</u> from one study to the next.*procrastinator: 미루는 사람
questions.explanation: 문맥상 1년 동안 몇 번 슬펐는지 묻는 것은 사람들의 기억이 부정확할 수 있고 정의가 다양하기 때문에 '신뢰할 수(dependable)' 없을지도 모른다는 흐름이 적절하다. ⓓ는 문맥상 '부정확한(inaccurate)'이 되어야 하고, ⓔ는 연구 간의 '일관성(consistency)'을 보장한다는 내용이 되어야 한다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. (A) It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. (B) Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. (C) We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. (D) These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. (E) And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.*grudging: 투덜대는
questions.insertion_sentence: The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 다른 사람들이 우리를 어떻게 인식하는지 무의식적으로 모니터링하는 경향의 발달에 대해 설명하고 있다. (C) 앞부분까지는 집단 내에서의 생존 압박과 그에 민감한 사람들이 선택되었다는 진화적 배경을 설명하고, (C) 위치에서 그 결과로 나타난 모니터링 경향을 언급한 뒤, 그 정보가 자존감이나 감정의 형태로 처리된다는 흐름이 이어지는 것이 가장 적절하다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 특징으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information ─ a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. (A)<u>People</u> who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.*retrieve: 상기하다 **primacy: 우위성
options: ① They are good at learning something abstract.
② They store information as breaking it up to recode.
③ They come up with past experiences to see the world.
④ They tend to reconstruct information they have acquired.
⑤ They prefer detailed ideas rather than enduring unclear concepts.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 (A)는 정보를 추상화하거나 재구성하는 능력이 부족하여 모든 것을 완벽한 세부 사항으로 기억하는 사람들입니다. 이들은 일반화하거나 학습하거나 연결 고리를 만드는 데 어려움을 겪는다고 설명되어 있습니다. 따라서 모호한 개념을 견디기보다 아주 세부적인 아이디어를 선호한다는 내용의 ⑤번이 가장 가깝습니다.
options_translation: ① 그들은 추상적인 것을 배우는 데 능숙하다.
② 그들은 재부호화하기 위해 정보를 분해하여 저장한다.
③ 그들은 세상을 보기 위해 과거의 경험을 떠올린다.
④ 그들은 습득한 정보를 재구성하는 경향이 있다.
⑤ 그들은 불분명한 개념을 견디기보다 상세한 아이디어를 선호한다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 쓰시오. [24년 10월 40번]
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Alvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
questions.summary_sentence: A trick-punishment reinforces the unwanted behavior of a child, which implies that parents should focus on reducing the attention to (A)___________ while rewarding (B)___________ behaviors.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 아이를 꾸짖는 것이 오히려 나쁜 행동을 강화시키는 '속임수 처벌'에 대해 설명하고 있으며, 나쁜 점을 지적하기보다는 긍정적인 행동을 격려하는 것이 더 효과적이라고 합니다. 따라서 빈칸 (A)는 나쁜 점들을 뜻하는 'negatives'가, (B)는 긍정적인 행동을 의미하는 'positive'가 적합합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에 대한 필자의 주장으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage:
Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions. But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
*phase: (달의) 모양
options: ① Seeking information on the internet can enhance confidence in unrelated areas.
② Participants who use the internet frequently are good at answering questions.
③ Internet access helps us to solve many difficult topics easily.
④ Excessive online activity can lead to serious internet addiction.
⑤ The internet is a vast and rich source of information on a wide range of topics.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인터넷에서 정보를 검색하는 경험이 객관적으로 관련성이 없는(unrelated) 다른 분야에 대해서도 자신의 지적 능력에 대한 오판, 즉 지적 자신감(intellectual confidence)을 높일 수 있다는 연구 결과를 소개하고 있습니다. 따라서 인터넷 정보를 찾는 행위가 관련 없는 영역에서도 자신감을 높여준다는 ①번이 가장 적절한 주장입니다.
options_translation: ① 인터넷에서 정보를 찾는 것은 관련 없는 분야에서도 자신감을 높일 수 있다.
② 인터넷을 자주 사용하는 참가자들은 질문에 답하는 데 능숙하다.
③ 인터넷 접속은 우리가 많은 어려운 주제들을 쉽게 해결하도록 도와준다.
④ 과도한 온라인 활동은 심각한 인터넷 중독으로 이어질 수 있다.
⑤ 인터넷은 다양한 주제에 관한 방대하고 풍부한 정보의 원천이다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에 들어갈 어법상 올바른 단어들로 각각 알맞게 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage:
Nearly everything has to go through your mouth to get to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body get (A)[what / which] it needs and prevent it from harm - with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. From the moment you are created, oral health affects every (B)[aspect / aspects] of your life. What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and a reflection of what is happening in other parts of the body. Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease that affects the entire body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, (C)[posed / posing] serious health risks.
*microorganism: 미생물
questions.explanation:
(A) 선행사를 포함하며 동사 get의 목적어 역할을 하는 동시에, 뒤에 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절(it needs)을 이끄는 관계대명사 what이 적절합니다.
(B) 형용사 every는 수적으로 단수 취급하여 뒤에 단수 명사가 와야 하므로 aspect가 올바릅니다.
(C) 문맥상 미생물들이 혈류로 들어가 신체 곳곳으로 이동하여 심각한 건강 위험을 '초래하면서'라는 능동의 의미를 나타내므로 현재분사 형태의 분사구문인 posing이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative ⓐ<u>impression</u> to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to ⓑ<u>distance</u> oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question ⓒ<u>arising</u> here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item, but sooner than later, this feeling will be ⓓ<u>replaced</u> by the joy of clarity. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to ⓔ<u>accumulate</u> stuff that is unused or not going to be used in the near future.
questions.explanation: 미니멀리스트들은 현대의 모든 편의를 포기해야 한다고 주장하는 것이 아니라, 사용되지 않거나 가까운 미래에 사용되지 않을 물건들을 '축적(accumulate)'하는 것이 아니라 '정리'하거나 '제거'해야 한다는 관점을 가지고 있습니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 accumulate(축적하다)는 문맥상 '제거하다' 혹은 '버리다'와 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson suggests that we tend to understand the world by focusing in on particular features within it. Take platypuses. We might zoom in so closely to their fur that each hair appears ⓐ<u>different</u>. We might also zoom out to the extent ⓑ<u>where</u> it appears as a single, uniform object. We might take the platypus as an individual, or we might treat it as part of a larger unit such as a species or an ecosystem. It's possible to move between many of these perspectives, ⓒ<u>despite</u> we may need some additional tools and skills to zoom in on individual pieces of hair or zoom out to entire ecosystems. Crucially, however, we can only take up one perspective at a time. We can pay attention to the varied behavior of individual animals, look at ⓓ<u>what</u> unites them into a single species, or look at them as part of bigger ecological patterns. Each possible perspective involves emphasizing certain aspects and ⓔ<u>ignoring</u> others.*anthropologist: 인류학자 **platypus: 오리너구리
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 뒤에 주어(we)와 동사(may need)를 갖춘 절이 이어지고 있으므로, 전치사인 despite 대신 접속사인 although나 even though가 와야 문법적으로 옳습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 편지글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: To the State Education Department, I am writing with regard to the state's funding for the construction project at Fort Montgomery High School. Our school needs additional spaces to provide a fully functional Art and Library Media Center to serve our students in a more meaningful way. Despite submitting all required documentation for funding to your department in April 2024, we have not yet received any notification from your department. A delay in the process can carry considerable consequences related to the school's budgetary constraints and schedule. Therefore, in order to proceed with our project, we request you notify us of the review result regarding the submitted documentation.I look forward to hearing from you.Respectfully,Clara SmithPrincipal, Fort Montgomery High School
options: ① The school has submitted the necessary documents for the construction approval request.
② The Art and Library Media Center construction project is already completed.
③ The school submitted all required documents in April 2024 but has not yet received a notification.
④ The delay in funding approval will have no impact on the school's budget.
⑤ Clara Smith is requesting additional documents from the State Education Department.
questions.explanation: 지문 중 'Despite submitting all required documentation for funding to your department in April 2024, we have not yet received any notification from your department.'라는 문장을 통해 2024년 4월에 서류를 제출했으나 아직 통보를 받지 못했다는 사실을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 학교는 건설 승인 요청을 위한 필수 서류를 제출했다.
② 미술 및 도서관 미디어 센터 건설 프로젝트는 이미 완료되었다.
③ 학교는 2024년 4월에 모든 필요 서류를 제출했으나 아직 통보를 받지 못했다.
④ 자금 승인 지연은 학교 예산에 아무런 영향을 미치지 않을 것이다.
⑤ Clara Smith는 주 교육부에 추가 서류를 요청하고 있다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression __________________________________. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
options: ① is a reliable approach to logical and reasoned decisions
② often aligns with deliberative reasoning about the world
③ can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be
④ must be validated with detailed reasoning to confirm accuracy
⑤ shows the importance of careful deliberation in eye-witness testimony
questions.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 신중한 분석이나 논리적인 단계별 설명보다 직관적인 첫인상이나 무의식적인 추측이 더 정확할 수 있다는 것입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '첫인상이 숙고하고 논리적인 자기 설명보다 세상에 대해 더 정확할 수 있다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 논리적이고 이성적인 결정을 위한 신뢰할 수 있는 접근법이다
② 세상에 대한 숙고적인 추론과 자주 일치한다
③ 숙고적이고 이성적인 자기 서술보다 세상에 대해 더 정확할 수도 있다
④ 정확성을 확인하기 위해 상세한 추론으로 검증되어야 한다
⑤ 목격자 증언에서 세심한 숙고의 중요성을 보여준다

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which AI exceeds human intelligence.
ordered_passages: (A) Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI. The direction of AI's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into AI.
(B) We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.

(C) AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity.

(D) After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 AI가 인간 지능을 초월하는 지점인 '특이점(singularity)'을 언급했습니다. (D)는 '그 지점 이후(After that point)'라는 연결어로 특이점 이후 가속화되는 AI의 진화와 의식을 가진 존재로의 변화를 서술하므로 가장 먼저 와야 합니다. 그 뒤 (C)에서는 '그 후(then)' AI와 인간의 의식이 상호작용하며 함께 진화하는 과정을 설명하고, (A)는 '반대로(Conversely)' 인간의 가치관이 AI 진화에 미치는 영향력을 다룹니다. 마지막으로 (B)는 이러한 상호보완적 관계를 바탕으로 AI와 인간을 공존하는 관계로 바라보자는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 논리적으로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
questions.summary_sentence: Humans overcome their cognitive and resource limitations by (A)__________ information and computation across society, which suggests that individual efforts are most effective when focused on (B)__________ a collective contribution to society's shared knowledge.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 가진 정보 처리 능력의 한계를 극복하기 위해 거대한 계산(정보 처리) 과정을 사회 전체로 배분(distribute)한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 인간은 모든 작동 원리를 알 필요 없이 지식 공유에 기여함(make a contribution)으로써 혜택을 얻는다는 것이 핵심이므로, (A)에는 distributing, (B)에는 making이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 배분하는 - 만드는
② 집중시키는 - 줄이는
③ 제한하는 - 향상시키는
④ 가공하는 - 이해하는
⑤ 보류하는 - 공유하는

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race - their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, ____________________________________. In fact, ultra-marathon runners - those people who are crazy enough to push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50-100km or more over many hours, talk about making friends with their pain. When a patient has paid for some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it, the patient calls that good pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.
options: ① they suffer both physically and mentally from the experience
② they endure the pain but also feel psychological distress
③ they don't psychologically suffer much due to their focus on the goal
④ their pain limits their endurance and performance
⑤ their experience is entirely negative, both mentally and physically
questions.explanation: 고통의 정도는 마음속에서 고통을 어떻게 프레이밍하느냐에 달려 있다는 것이 글의 요지입니다. 1500m 달리기 선수나 울트라 마라톤 선수의 예시를 통해, 목표를 위해 감수하는 고통은 긍정적으로 인식될 수 있음을 보여줍니다. 따라서 선수들이 목표에 집중하기 때문에 심리적으로는 크게 고통받지 않는다는 ③번이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: 그들은 그 경험으로부터 신체적으로나 정신적으로 고통을 겪는다
그들은 고통을 견디지만 심리적 고통도 느낀다
그들은 목표에 대한 집중 덕분에 심리적으로 크게 고통받지 않는다
그들의 고통은 인내심과 수행 능력을 제한한다
그들의 경험은 정신적으로나 신체적으로 전적으로 부정적이다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group ⓐ<u>valued</u> us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at ⓑ<u>maximizing</u> their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community ⓒ<u>valued</u> us and less of what doesn't. And, ⓓ<u>crucially</u>, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is ⓔ<u>coming</u> from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 'makes our community valued us' 부분은 사역동사 make 뒤에 목적어(our community)와 목적격 보어가 오는 구조입니다. 공동체가 우리를 가치 있게 여기게 만든다는 능동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 과거분사인 valued를 동사원형인 value로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that ⓐ<u>float</u> around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that ⓑ<u>is devoted</u> to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, ⓒ<u>to make</u> sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally ⓓ<u>held</u> beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are ⓔ<u>that</u> modern psychology is all about.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장에서 'be all about'의 목적어 역할을 하면서 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사가 필요합니다. that은 앞에 선행사가 없으므로 적절하지 않으며, '현대 심리학의 핵심인 것(현대 심리학이 다루는 전부)'이라는 의미를 완성하기 위해 what으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고 어법상 올바른 문장을 고르면? [24년 10월 21번]
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. ⓐWe recode which we see through the lens of everything we know. ⓑWe reconstruct memories rather than retrieve the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. ⓒPeople who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what it has learned. ⓓBut representing the world as abstract ideas and features come at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. ⓔThe discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely was undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: ⓑ는 어법상 하자가 없는 문장입니다. ⓐ는 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what이 쓰여야 하고, ⓒ의 it has learned는 선행사인 People에 맞춰 they have learned로 바뀌어야 합니다. ⓓ는 동명사 주어 representing이므로 동사 come을 comes로, ⓔ는 동사 undermined 앞에 불필요한 was가 있으므로 was를 삭제해야 합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden and hunt at night. ⓐHowever, two Australian underwater photographers were surprised to find an octopus in full view during daylight in shallow water. ⓑInitially, they mistook it for a flounder, but upon closer inspection, they realized it was a medium-sized octopus, using its arms and eyes to create an illusion. ⓒOctopuses are known for their intelligence, with some species being able to solve complex puzzles and escape enclosures. ⓓOctopuses posses large brains, excellent eyesight, and the ability to change color and pattern, which they use to transform into different creatures. ⓔSince then, more octopuses of this species have been found, with photographs showing them mimicking sea snakes while hunting.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 문어의 위장 능력과 변신 능력에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 낮에 발견된 특정 문어가 다른 생물로 변신하여 자신을 보호하고 사냥하는 구체적인 사례를 다루고 있는데, ⓒ는 문어의 일반적인 지능과 퍼즐 해결 능력에 대해 말하고 있어 글의 전체적인 흐름인 '신체적 변장을 통한 방어 및 사냥'과는 거리가 멉니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In short, depression causes an ⓐ<u>increase</u> in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline. In this ⓑ<u>modified</u> cause-and-effect, the key is to ⓒ<u>reinterpret</u> depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is an ⓓ<u>effect</u> of depression, not its cause. ⓔ<u>In other words,</u> depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and norepinephrine, not a reduction in brain substances causes depression.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장(ⓔ)에서 우울증이 세로토닌과 같은 뇌 물질의 '감소(decrease)'를 유발한다고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 ⓐ의 '증가(increase)'는 문맥상 적절하지 않으며 '감소(decrease)'로 고쳐야 합니다. 이 글은 뇌 물질 불균형이 우울증의 원인이 아니라 결과라고 주장하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 ·내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.
options: ① Canalization is a process that promotes random variation in biological systems.
② Canalization is a concept that explains how external factors have no influence on biological development.
③ Canalization is a phenomenon that limits the number of potential states a biological system can occupy.
④ Canalization is a mechanism that ensure biological systems remain in a state of constant stability.
⑤ Canalization is a process that allows for a wide range of possible outcomes in a biological system.
questions.explanation: 글에서 'canalization'은 결과의 급격한 축소(drastic narrowing of outcomes)림 의미하먰, 생물체가 무작위적인 상태가 아닌 제한된 수의 정의된 상태 사이림 옄황한다고 설명합니다. 내용과 일치하는 것은 생물학적 시숔템이 가질 수 있는 잠재적 상태의 수림 제한한다는 ③번입니다.
options_translation: ① Canalization은 생물학적 시숔템에서 무작위적 변이림 촐진하는 과정이다.
② Canalization은 외부 요인이 생물학적 발달에 영향을 미츘지 않는 방법을 설명하는 개념이다.
③ Canalization은 생물학적 시숔템이 차지할 수 있는 잠재적 상태의 수림 제한하는 현상이다.
④ Canalization은 생물학적 시숔템이 지섽적인 안정 상태림 유지하도록 발호하는 기제이다.
⑤ Canalization은 생물학적 시숔템에서 광밤위한 가능한 결과림 허용하는 과정이다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 제절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
questions.summary_sentence: To obtain (A)__________ quantitative data in research, it's important to ask (B)__________ questions that clarify abstract concepts and ensure consistency.
questions.explanation: 글은 연구에서 신뢰할 수 있는 양적 데이터림 얻기 위해서는 추상적인 질문밴다는 구체적이고 명확한(explicit) 질문을 해야 한다고 설명합니다. 따논서 (A)에는 '신뢰할 수 있는(reliable)', (B)에는 '명확한(explicit)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 궰정적인 - 일반적인
② 복잡한 - 개홀적인

questions.question: 28. 다음 글에서 어법상으로 어색한 2문장을 찾아 이유와 함께 올바르게 고쳐 서술하시오.
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.answer: (1) 어색한 문장 1: normally the selling point is what the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance.(2) 이유 및 수정: 여기에 쓰인 what은 관계대명사이므로 뒤에 불완전한 문장이 와야 하는데, 뒤에 완전한 문장(the usefulness... is obvious)이 왔다. 따라서 명사절로써 보어 역할을 하는 접속사 that이 와야 한다. (수정: normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance.)(3) 어색한 문장 2: It is because the meaning of his works are not immediately obvious and require some thought on the part of the audience.(4) 이유 및 수정: because 이하의 절에서 주어는 'the meaning'(단수)이므로 동사도 단수형인 is와 requires가 되어야 한다. (수정: ...the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought...)
questions.explanation: 첫 번째 오류 문장에서는 보어 자리에 오는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사가 필요한데, 뒤에 문장 성분이 모두 갖춰진 완전한 문장이 오고 있으므로 관계대명사 what 대신 접속사 that을 써야 합니다. 두 번째 오류 문장에서는 'the meaning of his works'에서 주어의 핵심 요소가 단수인 'the meaning'이므로 수의 일치에 따라 동사를 is와 requires로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: On screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre ─ indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant ─ in time or in place ─ we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
options: ① Escaping Reality Through Climate Fiction
② Climate Change: Shaping Fictional Narratives
③ Literature Offering Solutions to Climate Change
④ The Evolution of Climate Art: Blurring Reality and Storytelling
⑤ The End of Climate Fiction Due to the Reality of Climate Change

④ 기후 예술의 진화: 현실과 스토리텔링의 모호해지는 경계

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Alvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
options: ① 트릭 처벌은 가장 전형적인 의미의 처벌이다.
② 아이를 벌주는 것은 트릭 처벌로 인해 효과적이지 않을 수 있다.
③ 외로운 아이는 눈에 띄지 않는 것을 꾸중 듣는 것보다 더 선호한다.
④ 트릭 처벌은 아이가 무엇인가를 단념시키는 대신 그것을 하도록 장려한다.
⑤ 일정 기간 부정적 측면을 지적하는 대신 긍정적인 측면을 보상하는 것으로 트릭 처벌을 피할 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible(외로움을 느끼는 아이에게, 꾸중을 듣는 것이 투명인간이 된 기분을 느끼는 것보다 훨씬 낫다)'라고 언급되어 있습니다. 따라서 외로운 아이는 눈에 띄지 않는 것(feeling invisible)보다 꾸중 듣는 것(being scolded)을 더 선호합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is _____________________________________. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
options: ① to identify serotonin as a major factor in depression
② to understand the role of brain chemistry in depression
③ to recognize the effects of neurotransmitter imbalances
④ to reconstruct depression as a problem of consciousness
⑤ to explore the connection between brain function and substances
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 뇌의 화학적 물질 불균형이 우울증의 원인이 아니라 결과이며, 우울증의 실제 근본 원인은 뇌보다 더 근원적인 '의식(consciousness)'의 왜곡에 있다는 것입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 우울증을 의식의 문제로 재정의한다는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.

신경 전달 물질 불균형의 효과를 인식하는 것
우울증을 의식의 문제로 재구성하는 것

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes (A)[staring / stared] upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn (B)[it / itself] into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could (C)[say / be said] to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt ─ producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.explanation:
(A) 'with + 명사 + 분사' 구문에서 명사인 'its two eyes'가 스스로 '응시하는' 능동의 관계이므로 현재분사 staring이 적절합니다.
(B) 주어(this one)가 자기 자신을 다른 생물로 변신시키는 상황이므로 목적어 자리에 재귀대명사 itself를 써야 합니다.
(C) 문맥상 문장의 주어인 'octopuses'가 '~라고 말해지는(여겨지는)' 수동의 의미이므로 조동사 뒤에 수동태 형태인 be said가 오는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 응시하는 - 그것을 - 말하다
② 응시되는 - 그것을 - 일컬어지다
③ 응시하는 - 그 자신을 - 일컬어지다
④ 응시되는 - 그 자신을 - 말하다
⑤ 응시되는 - 그 자신을 - 일컬어지다

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. ①So when the circumstances have changed, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. ②By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. ③They are more disposed to miss their childhood when they grow up. ④Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. ⑤Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 동물에게 있어 유년기가 환경 학습과 유연한 적응(이주 경로 등)에 미치는 중요성이다. 3번 문장(⑒)은 어른이 되었을 때 유년기를 그리워하는 경향이 있다는 내용으로, 생존 및 학습 능력으로서의 유년기의 역할이라는 전체 흐름과 관계가 없다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around ⓐ<u>frequently</u>, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about ⓑ<u>transporting</u> young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to ⓒ<u>shorten</u> their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in ⓓ<u>slow</u> population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to ⓔ<u>agricultural</u> societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.explanation: 농경 사회에서 출산 간격이 줄어들어 여성이 더 많은 자녀를 가질 수 있게 되었으므로, 이는 인구의 '느린(slow)' 성장이 아니라 '빠른(rapid)' 성장을 초래했습니다.

questions.question: 6. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe ⓐ<u>which</u> could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of a tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, ⓑ<u>allowed</u> the tribe to have a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon ⓒ<u>much</u> more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each ⓓ<u>succeeds</u> generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes ⓔ<u>responsible</u> for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are <u>the descendants of the winners.</u>
questions.explanation: 명사 generation을 수식하는 형용사 형태가 와야 하므로, 동사 succeeds 대신 '연속적인, 뒤를 잇는'이라는 뜻의 형용사 successive가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed ⓐ<u>that</u> the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices ⓑ<u>were used to</u> have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is ⓓ<u>neglected</u>. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. The bigger data we store on clouds, _____________________________________________. questions.question: 14. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: It has been scientifically ⓐ<u>proven</u> that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain in both animals and humans. For example, the animals that have been rewarded for perceiving sound when hunting or avoiding being hunted ⓑ<u>show</u> larger auditory centers in the brain. The animals rewarded for sharp eyesight are likely to have larger visual areas, instead. In addition, brain scans of violinists providing more obvious evidence ⓒ<u>demonstrating</u> dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Furthermore, other studies have shown that the hippocampus, ⓓ<u>which</u> is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. All of the instances above clearly indicate the point ⓔ<u>that</u> the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'brain scans of violinists providing more obvious evidence'이며, 이 주어에 대한 본동사가 필요한 자리입니다. 따라서 분사인 'demonstrating'을 동사형인 'demonstrate' 또는 'demonstrated'로 바꾸어야 문법적으로 옳습니다.

questions.question: 15. 윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It has been scientifically ⓐ<u>proven</u> that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain in both animals and humans. For example, the animals that have been rewarded for perceiving sound when hunting or avoiding being hunted ⓑ<u>show</u> larger auditory centers in the brain. The animals rewarded for sharp eyesight are likely to have larger visual areas, instead. In addition, brain scans of violinists providing more obvious evidence ⓒ<u>demonstrating</u> dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Furthermore, other studies have shown that the hippocampus, ⓓ<u>which</u> is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. All of the instances above clearly indicate the point ⓔ<u>that</u> the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① 다양한 활동과 연습은 뇌의 여러 부분의 기능을 향상시킨다.
② 주의 집중 연습을 통해 뇌의 물리적 구조를 변화시킬 수 있다.
③ 연습과 주의를 통해 뇌를 발달시키는 것은 오랜 시간이 걸린다.
④ 반복적인 뇌 훈련을 통해 뇌의 전반적인 기능을 강화할 수 있다.
⑤ 동물들은 소리와 시각을 통해 사냥하거나 회피하는 능력을 발달시킨다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 우리가 어디에 주의를 기울이고 무엇을 연습하느냐에 따라 뇌의 물리적 구조가 변한다는 내용을 동물과 인간(바이올린 연주자, 택시 운전사)의 사례를 통해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ②번이 가장 적절한 요지입니다.

questions.question: 16. 윗글의 (A)~(E) 중에서 주어진 문장이 들어갈 곳으로 가장 적절한 것은?Such cases could be examples of weakness of will.
questions.passage: Many humans and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one. In other words, the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (A) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one. (B) However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. (C) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. (D) Similarly, a worker who had decided to save money to create an emergency funds eventually used all of it for traveling. (E) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but ______________________________________________.
questions.insertion_sentence: Such cases could be examples of weakness of will.
questions.explanation: 지문은 미래를 위해 저축을 하지만 계획과 달리 즉각적인 즐거움을 위해 저축액을 조기에 사용하는 사례들(C, D)을 제시합니다. (E) 지점은 이러한 사례들이 결국 '의지의 나약함(weakness of will)'의 예시가 될 수 있음을 결론짓거나 요약하는 위치이므로 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many humans and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one. (A) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one. (D) Similarly, a worker who had decided to save money to create an emergency funds eventually used all of it for traveling. options: ① are going to increase their savings regardless of circumstances
② are likely to evaluate the value of future reward to be undiscounted later on
③ then are uncertain about which is more valuable between present or future rewards
④ may later prefer immediate desires to long-term goals giving up their original plans
questions.explanation: 지문 전체의 맥락은 사람들이 미래의 큰 보상을 위해 저축을 결정하더라도, 결국 현실에서는 즉각적인 욕구에 굴복하여 원래 계획을 포기하고 저축을 써버린다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '나중에 원래 계획을 포기하고 장기적 목표보다 즉각적인 욕구를 더 선호할 수 있다'는 의미인 ④번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 상황에 상관없이 저축을 늘릴 것이다
② 나중에 미래 보상의 가치가 할인되지 않은 것으로 평가할 가능성이 높다
③ 현재나 미래의 보상 중 어느 것이 더 가치 있는지에 대해 불확실해한다

questions.question: 18. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off ␁<u>shifting</u> to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas ␂<u>alone</u>. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To ␃<u>prevent</u> independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and ␄<u>refine</u> the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and ␅<u>advance</u> possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially ␆<u>ineffective</u> in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ① The Process and Value of Brainwriting
② A Key to Achievement: Anonymity in Writing
③ Advantages of Brainstroming over Brainwriting
④ How to Develop Your Writing Skills on Your Own
⑤ Collective Intelligence: Essential for Future Society
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기존의 브레인스토밍 대신 브레인라이팅(brainwriting)이라는 새로운 프로세스의 단계(개별 아이디어 생성, 익명 공유, 개별 평가 등)와 그것이 모든 목소리를 반영하게 함으로써 집단 지성을 끌어내는 가치에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로는 '브레인라이팅의 과정과 가치'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 브레인라이팅의 과정과 가치
② 성취의 핵심: 글쓰기에서의 익명성
③ 브레인라이팅 대비 브레인스토밍의 장점
④ 스스로 글쓰기 기술을 개발하는 방법
⑤ 집단 지성: 미래 사회를 위한 필수 요소

questions.question: 19. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ␁~␆ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것 2개를 골라 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고치시오.

questions.explanation: ␃ 'prevent'는 '방지하다'라는 뜻인데, 문맥상 각 구성원이 스스로 평가하는 것은 독립적인 판단을 '보존'하거나 '촉진'하기 위함이므로 'preserve'나 'promote' 등이 적절합니다. ␆ 'ineffective'는 '효과가 없는'이라는 뜻인데, 브레인라이팅은 집단 지성을 발휘하기 힘든 그룹에서 특히 '효과적'이어야 하므로 'effective'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 22. 윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained (A)[neglected / appreciated] for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have (B)[low / sharp] vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much (C)[improved / worse] if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions. Specially, it is important to ensure that our final product serves __________________________.
questions.explanation: (A) 장애를 가진 사람들의 필요가 무시되어 왔다는 흐름이므로 neglected가 적절합니다. (B) 시각 장애인이나 시력이 낮은(low vision) 사람들을 언급하고 있으므로 low가 적절합니다. (C) 더 많은 프로젝트가 모든 청중을 고려하는 아이디어를 수용한다면 상황이 개선될 것이므로 improved가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 소홀히 된 / 낮은 / 개선된
② 소홀히 된 / 날카로운 / 악화된
③ 소홀히 된 / 낮은 / 악화된
④ 인정받은 / 날카로운 / 개선된
⑤ 인정받은 / 낮은 / 악화된

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 내용을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오. [4.0점]

This situation would be much (C)[improved / worse] if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions. Specially, it is important to ensure that our final product serves __________________________.
subjective_conditions: 흐름상 빈칸에 적절한 내용일 것
<보기>의 어휘만을 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
