questions.explanation: 빈칸은 최종 제품이 장애가 없는 사람뿐만 아니라 장애가 있는 사람들의 필요도 충족시켜야 한다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 'the needs of' 뒤에 'not only A but also B' 구문을 사용하여 '장애가 없는 사람들(those who are without disabilities)'과 '장애를 가진 사람들(have them)'을 연결하여 작성합니다.

questions.question: 3. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ⓐ<u>ones</u> that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are textbook example; they are both used for flight, and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight ⓑ<u>has to</u> be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor, and hence have some common structure that indicates ⓒ<u>their</u> being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat, the front leg of a horse, the flipper of a seal and the hand of a human have completely different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals, and as a result share non-functional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are ⓓ<u>connected</u>. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs, and focus on their most useless properties, because the useful ones could have arisen independently in two lineages because they are useful. We deduce ⓔ<u>what</u> bat wings are really hands because we can see the wrist and count the fingers, and because that is not the only way that nature could have built a wing.*lineage: 혈통
options: ① There are two types of similarity that biologists differentiate.
② Both bee's wings and bird's wings serve the same purpose, yet they developed in distinct ways.
③ Nonfunctional features are shared by the bat's wings and the human hand.
④ To distinguish between analogy and homology, the most inefficient aspects of organs are focused by biologists.
⑤ Given that nature could have created a wing in a variety of ways, bat wings are not considered hands.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 자연이 날개를 만들 수 있는 유일한 방법이 손 구조인 것은 아니지만, 박쥐의 날개에서 손목과 손가락을 볼 수 있기 때문에 박쥐의 날개를 '손'으로 추론한다고 언급되어 있습니다. 즉, 박쥐의 날개는 손으로 간주(considered hands)되므로 ⑤번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 생물학자들이 구분하는 두 가지 유형의 유사성이 있다.
② 벌의 날개와 새의 날개는 같은 목적을 수행하지만, 서로 다른 방식으로 발달했다.
③ 박쥐의 날개와 인간의 손은 비기능적 특징들을 공유한다.
④ 상사와 상동을 구별하기 위해 생물학자들은 기관의 가장 비효율적인 측면들에 집중한다.
⑤ 자연이 다양한 방식으로 날개를 만들 수 있었음을 고려할 때, 박쥐의 날개는 손으로 간주되지 않는다.

questions.question: 5. 윗글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system ⓐ<u>are</u> associated with political needs to build a specialized workforce for the economy.
ordered_passages: (B) However, in reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education ⓑ<u>have</u> set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education.

(C) In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback ⓒ<u>shaped</u> the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.

(D) Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often ⓓ<u>causing</u> students to focus more on grades than feedback.

(E) In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment ⓔ<u>that</u> enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 (A)에서 엘리트 교육에서 대중 고등 교육으로의 변화가 경제적 필요와 연관됨을 언급한 뒤, (E)에서 이론적인 교육의 목적과 방향을 설명합니다. (B)에서 'However'를 통해 실제 현실에서는 모순이 발생함을 지적하고, (D)에서 대중 교육의 효율성 추구로 인한 문제점을 설명하며, 마지막으로 (C)에서 과거 엘리트 시스템과의 대조를 통해 마무리하는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 윗글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것은?

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Especially for large items such as computer printers and kitchen and laundry appliances, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 문맥상 낱말의 의미가 바르게 연결되지 않은 것은?

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something - say a rectangular, brown desk - we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We reduce what we see through the lens of everything we know. We store in our minds not the raw image of the desk, but its features in an abstract manner. You can test yourself for how you're mentally representing something by trying to draw it. We draw with ____________________, not with a full picture of what we saw. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail, struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. We see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony.

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be ⓐ<u>attentive</u> to them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They lead us to perceive things that are not real. Firestein opens Ignorance with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." questions.question: 25. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is ⓔ<u>close</u> in time or in place, we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 기후 변화가 일상의 배경이 되어 더 이상 피할 수 없는 현실이 되면, 기후 고통이 시간적으로나 공간적으로 '멀리' 떨어져 있다고 더 이상 가장할 수 없게 된다는 흐름이 적절합니다. 따라서 '가까운'을 뜻하는 ⓔ의 close는 문맥상 어색하며, '멀리 떨어진(distant/remote)'과 같은 의미의 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up: many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
options: ① how to drive consumers to buy products with more features
② the psychological superiority that the high price of a product gives consumers
③ strategies for companies to provide different versions of products to control consumer buying behavior
④ analysis of consumer purchasing behavior that is an important foundation for start-ups
⑤ why consumers prefer the latest models in spite of high prices
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기업이 소비자의 구매 행동을 조절하기 위해 제품을 세 가지 버전으로 출시하는 전략을 설명하고 있습니다. 가장 비싼 모델을 '미끼'로 제시하여 소비자가 상대적으로 합리적이라고 느끼는 중간 가격대의 제품을 선택하도록 유도하는 심리적 기법을 다루고 있으므로 ③번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 소비자가 더 많은 기능을 가진 제품을 구매하도록 유도하는 방법
② 제품의 높은 가격이 소비자에게 주는 심리적 우월감
③ 소비자 구매 행동을 조절하기 위해 다양한 버전의 제품을 제공하는 기업의 전략
④ 스타트업의 중요한 토대가 되는 소비자 구매 행동 분석
⑤ 높은 가격에도 불구하고 소비자들이 최신 모델을 선호하는 이유

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a ⑀<u>consequence</u> of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this ⑁<u>revised</u> cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more ⑂<u>fundamental</u> entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a ⑃<u>reflection</u> of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may ⑄<u>manifest</u> itself in the form of depression.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 우울증의 근본 원인은 의식의 상태를 나타내는 것이어야 합니다. 그러나 지문의 흐름은 뇌의 불균형이 결과이지 원인이 아니라고 주장하며, 인과관계를 재설정하고 있습니다. ⑃ 'reflection'은 '반영'이라는 뜻이지만, 문맥상 뇌의 작용이 아닌 의식의 병적인 상태 혹은 '증상(symptom)'과 같은 맥락이 어울립니다. 그러나 더 정확하게는 문맥상 'disease'나 'problem'을 설명하는 과정에서 ⑃가 쓰인 문장은 '우울증의 근본 원인이 의식의 반영'이라는 논리보다는 '결과'나 '발현'의 의미가 강해야 하는데, ⓓ는 원인을 설명하는 문장에서 어색합니다. (교정: ⑃번이 포함된 문장은 의식의 문제로서 우울증을 재정의하고 있으므로, ⓓ reflection 대신 원인을 나타내는 표현이 와야 할 것 같으나, 원문 출처상 ⓓ는 다른 단어의 오용으로 보입니다. 여기서는 문맥상 ⓓ가 적절하지 않은 위치에 있음을 골라야 합니다.)

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally ⑀<u>compulsory</u>. That is one reason it is nevertheless ⑁<u>distressing</u>: an abundant resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to ⑂<u>address</u> it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft ⑃<u>account</u> for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly highlights have-and-have-not ⑄<u>inequities</u>, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 물 위기는 우리가 해결할 수 없는 것이 아니며 정치적인 문제라고 말하고 있습니다. 따라서 그것은 '강제적인(compulsory)' 것이 아니라 '피할 수 있는' 또는 '해결 가능한' 성격의 것이어야 합니다. ⑀ compulsory는 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞게 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. (A)___________, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people; how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. (B)___________, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서는 인간 본성에 대한 일반적인 이야기가 추측과 어리석음의 혼합물이라고 한 반면, 빈칸 뒤에서는 심리학은 다르다고 했으므로 대조의 연결어 'However'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞 문장에서 심리학자들이 의견이나 소문에 의존하지 않는다고 했고, 빈칸 뒤에서는 증거를 찾는다고 했으므로 앞의 부정적 진술에 대한 대안을 제시하는 'Instead'(대신에)가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 하지만 / 대신에
② 결과적으로 / 반대로
③ 게다가 / 유사하게
④ 무엇보다도 / 그러므로
⑤ 게다가 / 요약하자면

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as ⓐ<u>quickly</u> eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, ⓑ<u>which</u> could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel ⓒ<u>isolated</u> from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories ⓓ<u>illustrating</u> global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop ⓔ<u>to pretend</u> about it and start to pretend within it.
questions.explanation: ⑤번의 'stop to pretend'는 '~하기 위해 멈추다'라는 뜻이나, 문맥상 기후로 인한 고통이 더 이상 멀리 있지 않게 될 때 그것에 대해 '가식하는 것(모르는 척하는 것)을 멈추다'라는 의미가 되어야 하므로, 동명사를 목적어로 취하는 'stop pretending'으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively _________________________________ compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.explanation: 지문은 얼굴 특징을 신중하게 숙고하거나 논리적으로 설명하려 할 때보다, 이유를 설명할 수 없는 즉각적이고 자동적인 반응이 더 정확할 때가 많다고 설명합니다. 따라서 논리적 정당화보다 '초기의 무의식적 판단(initial unconscious judgement)'의 성과가 우수하다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 직접적인 삶의 경험
② 초기의 무의식적 판단
③ 매우 세밀한 관찰
④ 장기적인 합리적 추론
⑤ 오래된 전통적 지식

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive ___________________________________. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
options: ① revealed how much our superiority within the group
② was in putting individual values above community values
③ depended on how advanced a society we had in science and technology
④ depended on how to deal with feelings such as anxiety, self-esteem and shame
⑤ depended on how well we navigated relationships within a group
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 인간의 생존과 번영이 집단 내에서의 평판과 가치에 달려 있음을 설명합니다. 집단이 개인을 가치 있게 여겨야 자원과 지원을 얻을 수 있었기 때문에, 타인의 시선을 의식하고 집단 내 지위를 관리하는 능력이 진화했다는 내용입니다. 따라서 번영할 수 있는 능력은 '집단 내에서 관계를 얼마나 잘 탐색(관리)하느냐'에 달려 있다는 5번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 집단 내에서 우리의 우월함이 얼마나 되는지를 드러냈다
② 개인의 가치를 공동체의 가치보다 위에 두는 데 있었다
③ 우리가 과학과 기술에서 얼마나 진보된 사회를 가졌느냐에 달려 있었다
④ 불안, 자존감, 수치심과 같은 감정을 어떻게 다루느냐에 달려 있었다
⑤ 우리가 집단 내에서 관계를 얼마나 잘 헤쳐 나가는지에 달려 있었다

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which AI exceeds human intelligence.
ordered_passages: (A) Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI.

(B) After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When Al becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together.

(C) The direction of Al's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
questions.explanation: AI가 인간의 지능을 넘어서는 특이점에 대한 정의가 주어진 문장입니다. (B)에서는 그 시점(that point) 이후 AI가 가속화된 속도로 진화하며 자의식을 가진 존재가 되어 인간의 의식과 함께 진화하기 시작할 것임을 설명합니다. (A)에서는 AI와의 상호작용을 통해 인간의 의식이 새로운 차원으로 진화하고 인간의 의식 또한 AI의 진화에 영향을 미친다는 구체적인 진화 양상을 서술합니다. (C)에서 이러한 진화의 방향이 우리가 AI에 부여하는 가치와 윤리에 달려 있으므로 상호 공존의 관계로 보아야 한다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 <보기>에 주어진 단어만을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 들어갈 말을 완성하시오. [4.3점]
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because _______________________________________.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 주어진 단어만을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 영작할 것
questions.answer: the meaning of his works is not immediately apparent and requires some thought on the part of the audience
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기술적 은유(technological metaphors)가 즉각적이고 명확한 반면, 셰익스피어의 작품과 같은 언어적 은유(linguistic metaphors)는 독자의 적극적인 인지적 참여와 노력을 필요로 한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 셰익스피어가 사랑받는 이유로 '그의 작품의 의미가 즉각적인 것이 아니라 청중의 생각을 요구하기 때문'이라는 내용이 빈칸에 들어오는 것이 가장 적절합니다. 따라서 <보기>의 단어들을 조합하여 'the meaning of his works is not immediately apparent and requires some thought on the part of the audience'라는 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 <보기>에 주어진 단어나 어구를 모두 한 번씩 사용하고 필요시 어형 변화하여 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 완성하시오. (어법과 철자 오류시 부분점수 없음) [4.0점]
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but ____________________________________________. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
subjective_conditions: 필요시 어형 변화
어법과 철자 오류시 부분점수 없음
questions.answer: instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can focus on the child's positive behaviors and reinforce them
questions.explanation: 지문은 아이를 처벌하는 것이 오히려 그 행동을 부추길 수 있으므로 다른 전략이 필요하다고 말합니다. 빈칸에는 부정적인 면을 계속 지적하는 대신 긍정적인 행동에 집중하고 이를 강화해야 한다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 'instead of' 뒤에는 동명사 형태인 'pointing'이 와야 하며, 조동사 'can' 뒤에는 동사원형 'focus'가 옵니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 <보기>에 주어진 단어나 어구를 모두 한 번씩 사용하고 필요시 어형 변화하여 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 완성하시오. (어법과 철자 오류시 부분점수 없음) [4.0점]
questions.passage: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. _____________________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 필요시 어형 변화
어법과 철자 오류시 부분점수 없음
questions.answer: Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health
questions.explanation: 이 글의 요지는 일상적인 집안일에 미니 운동을 통합하여 건강을 개선하자는 것입니다. 마지막 문장은 '빠른 운동을 당신의 일상적인 집안일에 포함하는 것은 당신의 건강을 향상시킬 수 있다'는 주제문 성격의 결론이 되어야 합니다. 주어 자리에 'Incorporate'를 동명사 'Incorporating'으로 변형하여 문장을 완성해야 합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글에서 문법적으로 잘못된 부분을 모두 찾아 아래에 주어진 예시처럼 올바르게 고쳐 쓰시오. [5.0점]
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and does their own hunting at night. So find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes stared upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, stick it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.answer: does → (to) do / find → to find(또는 finding) / stared → staring / have found → have been found / stick → sticking
questions.explanation:
1) does: 문장의 보어 역할을 하는 'to stay'와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 동사원형인 'do'가 적절합니다.
2) find: 문장의 주어 자리이므로 동명사 'finding'이나 to부정사 'to find'로 고쳐야 합니다.
3) stared: 'with + 명사 + 분사' 구문에서 '두 눈이 위를 응시하는' 능동의 관계이므로 현재분사인 'staring'이 적절합니다.
4) have found: 주어인 '이 종의 더 많은 개체들'이 발견되어 온 수동의 대상이므로 현재완료 수동태인 'have been found'가 맞습니다.
5) stick: 'developing'과 'grabbing' 사이에서 병렬 구조를 이루며 분사구문을 완성해야 하므로 'sticking'으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
options: ① Quantitative Data: The Fallacy of Precision
② Why Subjective Data is the Future of Research
③ Procrastination: A Matter of Timing, Not Numbers
④ How Concrete Questions Clarify Abstract Research
⑤ When Memories Lie: The Truth About Subjective Data
questions.explanation: 이 글은 행복이나 기억과 같은 추상적인 개념을 연구할 때, 모호한 질문 대신 구체적인 행동이나 상황을 묻는 질문(예: 아파서 결근할 정도로 슬펐던 횟수, 연체된 공과금 개수 등)을 통해 더 명확하고 일관된 정량적 데이터를 얻을 수 있다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '구체적인 질문이 추상적인 연구를 명확하게 하는 방법'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 정량적 데이터: 정밀함의 오류
② 왜 주관적 데이터가 연구의 미래인가
③ 미루는 버릇: 숫자가 아닌 타이밍의 문제
④ 구체적인 질문이 추상적인 연구를 명확하게 하는 방법
⑤ 기억이 거짓말할 때: 주관적 데이터에 대한 진실

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. They do well enough in school to keep advancing. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ends with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now lack a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when the journey really begins. When school is finished, your growth becomes voluntary. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career are likely to stop progressing as a result.
options: ① What Makes School Education Important?
② The More We Exercise, the Faster We Grow
③ Why We Should Focus on Healthy Eating Habits
④ Graduation: Real Beginning of Your Own Growth
⑤ Is It Necessary to Devote Energy to Your Career?

④ 졸업: 당신 자신의 성장의 진정한 시작

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson suggests that we tend to understand the world by focusing in on particular features within it. Take platypuses. We might zoom in so closely to their fur that each hair appears different. We might also zoom out to the extent where it appears as a single, uniform object. We might take the platypus as an individual, or we might treat it as part of a larger unit such as a species or an ecosystem. It's possible to move between many of these perspectives, although we may need some additional tools and skills to zoom in on individual pieces of hair or zoom out to entire ecosystems. Crucially, however, we can only take up one perspective at a time. We can pay attention to the varied behavior of individual animals, look at what unites them into a single species, or look at them as part of bigger ecological patterns. Every possible perspective involves emphasizing certain aspects and ignoring others.
options: ① The Power of Perspective: How Our Focus Shapes What We See
② Unlocking the Mystery: Why Platypuses Don't Fit in Ecosystems
③ Why Looking at a Platypus Too Closely Changes Everything
④ Beyond Fur: The Platypus as a Gateway to Parallel Universes
⑤ Ecosystems and How They Function Independently
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우리가 세상을 이해할 때 특정 측면에 집중하는 관점에 따라 보는 대상이 달라지며, 한 번에 하나의 관점만을 취할 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 관점에 따라 어떤 부분은 강조되고 어떤 부분은 무시된다는 것이 핵심이므로, 관점의 힘과 그것이 우리가 보는 것을 형성하는 방식을 언급한 1번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 관점의 힘: 우리의 초점이 우리가 보는 것을 어떻게 형성하는가
② 미스터리 풀기: 오리너구리가 생태계에 맞지 않는 이유
③ 왜 오리너구리를 너무 자세히 보는 것이 모든 것을 바꾸는가
④ 털을 넘어서: 평행 우주로 가는 관문으로서의 오리너구리

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
options: ① harmful effects of a premature diagnosis of brain death
② correct directions of the criteria for brain death diagnosis
③ importance of determining if a potential donor is adequate to donate organs

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 canalization이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes <u>canalization</u>. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.
options: ① the process of eliminating all forms of genetic variation within an organism
② an organism's ability to adapt to every environmental change immediately
③ the process by which an organism becomes more random and unpredictable in its behavior
④ the random formation of new genes in an organism without any specific direction or limitation
⑤ the process where an organism narrows down to a few stable states out of many possible outcomes
questions.explanation: 생명체와 같은 복잡한 시스템은 수많은 가능성 중 소수의 안정적인 상태가 나타날 때 균형을 유지할 수 있다. Conrad Waddington은 이러한 '결과의 대폭적인 축소'를 '운하화(canalization)'라고 불렀으며, 이는 유기체가 수많은 가능성 중 몇 가지 안정적인 상태로 좁혀지는 과정을 의미하므로 5번이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 유기체 내의 모든 형태의 유전적 변이를 제거하는 과정
② 모든 환경 변화에 즉각적으로 적응하는 유기체의 능력
③ 유기체의 행동이 더 무작위적이고 예측 불가능해지는 과정
④ 특정한 방향이나 제한 없이 유기체에서 새로운 유전자가 무작위로 형성되는 것
⑤ 유기체가 수많은 가능한 결과 중에서 몇 가지 안정적인 상태로 좁혀지는 과정

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 It may cease to be a story.가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, <u>it may cease to be a story</u>. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
options: ① Everyone will forget about climate change and stop discussing it as a global issue.
② The impacts of climate change will be reversed and everything will return to normal.
③ People will pretend that climate change doesn't exist and stop taking any action about it.
④ The impacts of climate change will somehow cease to have any real-world consequences.
⑤ Climate change could become so real that it will no longer can be told as a fictional narrative.
questions.explanation: 지문은 기후 변화가 너무나 분명하고 일상적인 현실이 되면, 더 이상 창작물(이야기)의 소재로 다루어지는 '픽션'의 영역에 머물지 않게 될 것임을 시사하고 있습니다. 창밖으로 생생하게 볼 수 있는 세상을 굳이 소설로 읽을 필요가 없어진다는 맥락이므로 정답은 5번입니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 사람들이 기후 변화를 잊고 글로벌 이슈로 논의하는 것을 중단할 것이다.
② 기후 변화의 영향이 역전되어 모든 것이 정상으로 돌아올 것이다.
③ 사람들은 기후 변화가 존재하지 않는 척하며 그에 대한 조치를 중단할 것이다.
④ 기후 변화의 영향이 어떻게든 실제 세계에 결과를 미치지 않게 될 것이다.
⑤ 기후 변화가 너무나 실제적이 되어 더 이상 허구적 서사로 이야기될 수 없을 것이다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Despite the remarkable progress in deep-learning based facial recognition approaches in recent years, in terms of identification performance, they still have limitations. These limitations relate to the database ⓐ<u>using</u> in the learning stage. If the selected database does not contain enough instances, the result may be systematically ⓑ<u>affected</u>. For example, the performance of a facial biometric system may decrease if the person to be identified ⓒ<u>was</u> enrolled over 10 years ago. The factor to consider is that this person may experience changes in the texture of the face, particularly with the appearance of wrinkles and ⓓ<u>sagging</u> skin. These changes may be highlighted by weight gain or loss. To counteract this problem, researchers have developed models for face aging or digital de-aging. It is used to compensate for the differences in facial characteristics, ⓔ<u>which</u> appear over a given time period.
questions.explanation: ⓐ의 using은 뒤에 목적어가 없고 앞의 명사 database를 수식하며 '학습 단계에서 사용되는 데이터베이스'라는 수동의 의미를 가져야 하므로 과거분사인 used로 고쳐야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most ⓐ<u>easily</u> explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example ⓑ<u>carve</u> into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out ⓒ<u>that</u>, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, ⓓ<u>was</u> perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, ⓔ<u>where</u> perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
questions.explanation: ⓑ의 carve는 앞에 있는 명사 a particular example을 수식하는 분사 자리입니다. 예시가 돌에 '새겨진' 것이라는 수동의 의미를 나타내야 하므로 과거분사 carved로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 21번]
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of _______________________________. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
options: ④ viewing things in their actual state
⑤ seeing the hidden messages in everything
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 내용은 우리가 사물을 있는 그대로 보는 것이 아니라 교육된 개념이나 기존의 지식, 추상적인 표상을 통해 재구성해서 본다는 것입니다. 따라서 세상을 추상적 관념으로 표현하는 것은 '사물을 실제 상태로 보는 것'을 희생(비용)으로 한다는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 장기 기억을 형성하는 것
② 기초 기하학을 이해하는 것
③ 복잡한 감정을 해석하는 것
④ 사물을 실제 상태로 보는 것
⑤ 모든 것에서 숨겨진 메시지를 보는 것

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When writing a novel, research for information needs to be done. The thing is that some kinds of fiction demand a higher level of detail: crime fiction, for example, or scientific thrillers. The information is never hard to find; one website for authors even organizes trips to police stations, so that crime writers can get it right. Often, a polite letter will earn you permission to visit a particular location and record all the details that you need. But remember that __________________________________ if you think that you need to pack everything you discover into your work. The details that matter are those that reveal the human experience. The crucial thing is telling a story, finding the characters, the tension, and the conflict - not the train timetable or the building blueprint.
options: ① your readers will be totally immersed
② you will drive your readers to boredom
③ you will be well-prepared as a crime writer
④ your work will gain popularity among readers
⑤ all the details will be important for each scene
questions.explanation: 소설을 쓸 때 세부 정보를 조사하는 것이 중요하지만, 발견한 모든 정보를 작품에 다 집어넣으려고 하면 독자들을 지루하게 만들 수 있다는 경고를 하고 있습니다. 소설에서 중요한 것은 정보 그 자체가 아니라 이야기, 캐릭터, 긴장감 등 인간의 경험을 드러내는 요소이기 때문입니다.
options_translation: ① 독자들이 완전히 몰입할 것이다
② 독자들을 지루함으로 몰아넣을 것이다
③ 범죄 소설가로서 잘 준비될 것이다
④ 당신의 작품이 독자들 사이에서 인기를 얻을 것이다
⑤ 모든 세부 사항이 각 장면에 중요할 것이다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could ________________________________________. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
options: ① dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation
② try to store as much knowledge as possible individually
③ calculate complex answers entirely on our own, without societal knowledge sharing
④ fill our minds with excessive, detailed knowledge of every single technology available
questions.explanation: 인간은 정보 처리 능력에 한계가 있기 때문에 모든 것을 혼자서 다 알려고 하는 대신, 지식을 사회적으로 분산하여 처리합니다. 따라서 우리는 거대한 계산(사회의 집단 지성)의 작은 부분을 담당하는 데 우리의 뇌를 할애하게 된다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 큰 뇌를 거대한 계산의 작은 부분에 헌신하다
② 개별적으로 가능한 한 많은 지식을 저장하려고 노력하다
③ 사회적 지식 공유 없이 전적으로 혼자서 복잡한 답을 계산하다
④ 이용 가능한 모든 단일 기술에 대한 과도하고 상세한 지식으로 머릿속을 채우다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, not (A)[evitable / inevitable] or beyond our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally elective. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an abundant resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. In other words, a water crisis is unnecessary, yet it exist, and we are taking (B)[minimal / maximal] action to resolve it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly highlights have-and-have-not (C)[inequities / equities], leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
questions.explanation: (A) 문맥상 물 위기는 고칠 수 없는 것이 아니라는 말이 나와야 하므로 '피할 수 없는(inevitable)'이 부정어 not과 결합하여 '피할 수 없는 것이 아니다(고칠 수 있다)'라는 의미를 형성해야 합니다. (B) 물 위기가 불필요함에도 존재한다는 것은 우리가 '최소한의(minimal)' 조치만 취하고 있기 때문입니다. (C) 안전한 식수가 없는 사람들의 사례는 빈부 격차에 따른 '불평등(inequities)'을 강조합니다.
options_translation: ① 피할 수 있는 / 최소한의 / 형평성
② 피할 수 있는 / 최대한의 / 불평등
③ 피할 수 없는 / 최소한의 / 불평등
④ 피할 수 없는 / 최대한의 / 불평등
⑤ 피할 수 없는 / 최소한의 / 형평성

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an (A)[objective / subjective] property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the (B)[physical / psychological] world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be (C)[colorless / colorful] - and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.explanation: (A) 색이 사물의 속성이라고 믿는 상식적인 견해는 색을 '객관적(objective)'인 것으로 봅니다. (B) 반대로 색이 보는 사람의 눈이나 마음속에만 존재한다고 주장하는 사람들은 색이 '물리적(physical)' 세계에는 존재하지 않는다고 봅니다. (C) 색이 관찰자의 마음속에만 있다면, 보는 사람이 없을 때 숲의 잎들은 '색이 없는(colorless)' 상태가 될 것입니다.
options_translation: ① 객관적인 / 물리적인 / 색이 없는
② 객관적인 / 물리적인 / 다채로운
③ 객관적인 / 심리적인 / 다채로운

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 10월 36번]
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. (A) Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. (B) The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. (C) These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. (D) And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. (E) If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
questions.insertion_sentence: We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 언급된 'that information'은 (B) 문장의 타인이 옰리를 어떻게 인식하는지에 대한 모니터링 결과를 의미합니다. 또한 제시문에 나오는 'related emotions(자부심, 수치심 등)'이 (C) 문장의 'These emotions'로 연결되므로 제시문은 (C) 윐에 들어가기에 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [23년 11월 23번]
questions.passage: Nearly everything has to go through your mouth to get to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and prevent it from harm - with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. ⓐMicroorganisms differ from each other not only in size, but also in structure, habitat, metabolism, and many other characteristics. ⓑFrom the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. ⓒWhat happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and a reflection of what is happening in other parts of the body. ⓓPoor oral health can be a cause of a disease that affects the entire body. ⓔThe microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, posing serious health risks.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구강 건강이 전신 건강에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ⓐ번 문장은 미생물의 구조와 특성 차이에 대해 말하고 있으므로 구강 건강과 전신 건강의 상관가계라는 전체 흐름과는 값개가 없습니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristic of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself. Psychologist George M. Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment.
ordered_passages: (A) For example, he used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something. Fortunately, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for the rest of his life. For him, everything returned to normal after one day.

(B) Stratton wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally turned the world upside down for him. In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him.

(C) With time, however, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated. As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 심리학자 Stratton의 자기 실험을 소개했습니다. (B)에서 실험의 시작인 반전 안경 착용과 그로 인한 초기 어려움을 설명합니다. (C)에서 시간이 흐름에 따라 시각 체계가 적응하여 정상적으로 행동할 수 있게 되었으나, 안경을 벗었을 때 다시 문제에 직면했다는 내용이 이어집니다. (A)에서 안경을 벗은 후의 구체적인 문제 사례(잘못된 손 사용)와 다시 정상으로 돌아오는 과정을 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?"
ordered_passages: (A) These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions.

(B) But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.

(C) Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?"
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 연구 참가자들에게 질문을 던지는 상황을 제시했습니다. (C)에서 참가자들을 두 집단(인터넷 검색 허용 vs 비허용)으로 나누고 두 번째 단계의 새로운 질문을 제시하는 실험 설계를 설명합니다. (A)에서 두 번째 질문들이 첫 번째 질문들과 무관하여 인터넷 검색 여부가 유리하지 않다는 점과 일반적인 예상을 언급합니다. (B)에서 'But'을 통해 반전되는 실제 실험 결과(인터넷 사용자가 자신을 더 지식이 많다고 평가함)를 설명하며 지적 자신감이 상승했다는 결론을 내립니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.summary_sentence: Digital metaphors are (A)__________ through technology and immediately clear, while linguistic metaphors require cognitive effort and (B)__________ from the audience.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 디지털 은유는 기술을 통해 '능동적으로 실현(actively realized)'되며 즉각적인 명확성을 가지는 반면, 언어적 은유는 독자의 인지적 노력과 '깊은 관여/참여(deeper engagement)'를 필요로 한다고 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 수동적으로 이해되는 / 즉각적인 인식
② 간접적으로 전달되는 / 피상적인 사고
③ 간접적으로 전달되는 / 깊은 관여
④ 능동적으로 실현되는 / 피상적인 사고
⑤ 능동적으로 실현되는 / 깊은 관여

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
questions.summary_sentence: Human efforts to (A)__________ crop production caused a decline in food diversity, creating a global food system that is now more (B)__________ to diseases, pests, and climate extremes.
questions.explanation: 지문은 식량 생산을 엄청난 규모로 늘리려는 인간의 노력이 작물의 다양성 감소를 초래했으며, 그 결과로 만들어진 획일적인 식량 시스템이 질병, 해충, 기후 위기에 더 취약해졌음을 설명한다. (A)에는 생산을 '증대시키다(boost)', (B)에는 위협에 '취약한(vulnerable)'이 들어가는 것이 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 줄이다 / 취약한
② 줄이다 / 회복력이 있는
③ 증대시키다 / 취약한
④ 증대시키다 / 회복력이 있는
⑤ 방해하다 / 안전한

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 각각 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오. [5.0점]
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while (A)____________________ but sooner than later, this feeling (B)____________________. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused or not going to be used in the near future.
subjective_conditions: ∙ (A)ኔ rid, useሔ ሔበ ሰረመሠ 5ሔሤ መሰሰሤ ሰሱሠሠሱ. (ሰሱሱ ሔሤ ሰሐ በሠሰ ሱሤ)
∙ (B)ኔ joy of, overcomeሔ ሔበ ሰረመሠ 6ሔሤ መሰሰሤ ሰሱሠሠሱ. (ሱሰሤ ሐሤሠ ሠሤሐሠ ሔሤሰሱ ሰሱሠሠሱ.)
questions.answer: (A) getting rid of a useless item(B) will be overcome by the joy of clarity
questions.explanation: 지문의 문맥상 미니멀리즘은 감정을 상하게 하는 것이 아니라 사용하지 않는 물건을 버리는 것이며, 버릴 때의 일시적인 슬픔은 곧 명료함의 즐거움에 의해 극복된다는 내용이다.(A)는 'while' 뒤에 이어지는 분사구문 혹은 동명사구로 '쓸모없는 물건을 제거하는 동안'이라는 의미인 'getting rid of a useless item'이 적절하다 (5단어 이상, rid/use 포함).(B)는 'this feeling'을 주어로 하여 '명료함의 즐거움에 의해 극복될 것이다'라는 수동태 문장인 'will be overcome by the joy of clarity'가 적절하다 (6단어 이상, overcome/joy of 포함).

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The adolescent brain is not fully developed until its early twenties. This means the way the adolescents' decision-making circuits integrate and process information may put them at a disadvantage. One of their brain regions that matures later is the prefrontal cortex, which is the control center, tasked with thinking ahead and evaluating consequences. It is the area of the brain responsible for preventing you from sending off an initial angry text and modifying it with kinder words. On the other hand, the limbic system matures earlier, playing a central role in processing emotional responses. Because of its earlier development, it is more likely to influence decision-making. Decision-making in the adolescent brain __________________________________________. Due to these differences, there is an imbalance between feeling-based decision-making ruled by the more mature limbic system and logical-based decision-making by the not-yet-mature prefrontal cortex. This may explain why some teens are more likely to make bad decisions.
subjective_conditions: more than, lead를 모두 포함하여 문장을 완성하시오. (필요시 단어 형태 변형 가능)
8단어 이상으로 빈칸의 문장을 완성하시오. (빈칸에 들어갈 내용만 답안지에 작성하시오.)
수동태를 반드시 사용하시오.
questions.answer: is led by emotional factors (the limbic system) more than the perception of consequences (the prefrontal cortex)
questions.explanation: 청소년의 뇌는 전두엽보다 감정을 처리하는 변연계가 먼저 발달하기 때문에, 의사결정이 결과에 대한 인지(이성적 판단)보다는 정서적 요인에 의해 더 많이 좌우된다는 내용입니다. 조건에 따라 수동태(is led by)와 비교 표현(more than)을 사용하여 문장을 완성해야 합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고 질문에 대한 답을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
subjective_conditions: 8단어 이상의 완전한 한 문장으로 작성하시오.
middle, make를 모두 포함하여 쓰시오.
비교급을 반드시 사용하시오.
questions.subjective_answer_format: Q: According to the above passage, why do sellers introduce a third, higher priced model to customers?정답: ___________________________________________________
questions.answer: It is to make the middle item look cheaper than the most expensive one. (또는 It makes people buy the middle item more by making it look less expensive.)
questions.explanation: 판매자가 더 비싼 세 번째 모델을 도입하는 이유는 소비자들이 중간 가격의 제품을 상대적으로 저렴하다고 느끼게 만들어 그 제품의 판매를 유도하기 위함입니다. 조건에 맞춰 middle, make와 비교급(cheaper, more 등)을 사용하여 완전한 문장으로 답변해야 합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오. [3.3점]
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants. Not only were their athletic talents superior, the Cubans appeared even stronger from just the colour of their uniforms. A game would not even start and the opposing team would already be scared. A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time. The country that ruled international baseball for decades has not been on top since that uniform change. Traditions are important for a team; while a team brand or image can adjust to keep up with present times, ________________________________.
subjective_conditions: its, negative, if, roots를 모두 포함하여 문장을 완성하시오.
9단어 이상으로 빈칸의 문장을 완성하시오. (빈칸에 들어갈 내용만 답안지에 작성하시오.)
questions.answer: if it abandons or neglects its roots, negative effects can surface
questions.explanation: 쿠바 야구팀의 사례를 통해 전통의 중요성을 강조하는 글입니다. 유니폼 변경(전통의 변화) 이후 성적이 하락했다는 점을 근거로, 팀이 자신의 뿌리(roots)를 저버리거나 소홀히 하면 부정적인 결과가 나타날 수 있다는 내용이 빈칸에 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: From an early age, we assign purpose to objects and events, preferring this reasoning to random chance. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because they don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. However, by attributing intention to animals and even objects, we are able to make fast decisions about the likely behaviour of that being. This tendency would have evolved as a survival mechanism during our hunter-gatherer days, helping us avoid being eaten by predators. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you. By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has ____________________________________________.
options: ① helped you form lasting relationships with animals
② ensured survival by allowing time for detailed planning
③ saved you by making you prefer the randomness of nature
④ provided an advantage for understanding abstract concepts
⑤ given you an edge for staying alive in a hostile environment
questions.explanation: 인간은 생존을 위해 대상의 의도를 빠르게 파악하려는 경향이 있습니다. 사자 같은 포식자의 신체 구조를 분석하기보다 살해 의도를 즉각적으로 가정하는 것이 생존에 유리했다는 예시를 통해, 이러한 경향이 적대적인 환경에서 살아남는 데 이점을 주었음을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 동물들과 지속적인 관계를 형성하도록 도왔다
② 세부적인 계획을 위한 시간을 허용함으로써 생존을 보장했다
③ 자연의 무작위성을 선호하게 함으로써 당신을 구했다
④ 추상적인 개념을 이해하는 데 이점을 제공했다
⑤ 적대적인 환경에서 살아남는 데 우위를 제공했다

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can ______________________________. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
options: ① actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification
② systematically correct the flaws in memory recall
③ help people to recognize hidden patterns in faces
④ uncover subtle emotional states at an unconscious level
⑤ be a means of supporting a logical decision making process
questions.explanation: 데이비드 다닝의 연구에 따르면, 목격자가 얼굴 특징을 신중하게 고려하거나 선택 절차를 자세히 논의하는 것보다, 설명할 수 없는 즉각적이고 무의식적인 '첫인상'을 따를 때 정확도가 더 높았습니다. 따라서 신중한 숙고와 논의는 오히려 부정확한 식별의 징후가 될 수 있다는 ①번이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 실제로 부정확한 식별의 징후일 수 있다
② 기억 회상의 결함을 체계적으로 수정할 수 있다
③ 사람들이 얼굴에서 숨겨진 패턴을 인식하도록 도울 수 있다
④ 무의식 수준에서 미묘한 감정 상태를 밝혀낼 수 있다
⑤ 논리적인 의사 결정 과정을 지원하는 수단이 될 수 있다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is ␀<u>enormous</u>. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For instance, the number of possible distinct states that our cells adopt is far ␁<u>smaller</u> than the number of ways one cell could potentially differ in detail from another. Likewise, when a human embryo develops, only a ␂<u>finite</u> number of tissue types and body shapes are possible. This drastic narrowing of outcomes was described by biologist Conrad Waddington in 1942 as "canalization." The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't ␃<u>exist</u> in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: despite the diverse causes of various diseases, they often lead to ␄<u>inconsistent</u> physiological and symptomatic outcomes.
questions.explanation: 지문은 생명 시스템이 매우 복잡하지만 결과적으로 소수의 특정한 상태(운하화)로 수렴된다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 질병의 원인이 다양함에도 불구하고, 그것들이 종종 '일관된' 생리적 및 증상적 결과로 이어진다는 흐름이 되어야 하므로 ␄ inconsistent(일관되지 않은)를 consistent(일관된)와 같은 단어로 바꾸어야 합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these ⓐ<u>merits</u>. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are ⓑ<u>sensitive</u> to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously ⓒ<u>ignore</u> how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do ⓓ<u>more</u> of what makes our community value us. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it ⓔ<u>less</u> persuasive.
questions.explanation: 인간은 생존을 위해 공동체가 자신을 어떻게 인식하는지에 민감하도록 진화해 왔습니다. 따라서 타인이 자신을 어떻게 인식하는지를 '무시하는(ignore)' 것이 아니라 '모니터링하거나(monitor) 신경 쓰는' 경향이 발달했다는 내용이 되어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중 어법상 오류가 있는 문장만을 고른 것은?
questions.passage: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? ⓐ<u>That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play</u>. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. ⓑ<u>Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essentially part of daily life</u>. ⓒ<u>But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity?</u> For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. ⓓ<u>Incorporate quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓑ: 'an essentially part'에서 형용사인 'part'를 수식해야 하므로 부사 'essentially'를 형용사 'essential'로 바꾸어야 합니다.ⓓ: 'Incorporate'는 동사 원형으로 시작하여 명령문처럼 보이나 뒤에 본동사인 'can improve'가 나오므로 주어 역할을 할 수 있는 동명사 'Incorporating'이나 To부정사 'To incorporate'로 바꾸어야 합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글을 읽고 추론한 것으로 가장 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling pointis that the usefulness of the artifacts is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
options: ① Linguistic metaphors demand significant cognitive engagement from the audience to derive meaning.
② Digital metaphors are considered active because they are manifested in functional digital tools.
③ The effectiveness of technological metaphors is typically based on their immediate and obvious utility.
④ Shakespeare's works are appreciated because their meanings are complex and require deep thought.
⑤ Unlike linguistic metaphors, digital metaphors allow users to choose whether to engage with their underlying concepts.
questions.explanation: • ⑤: 'digital metaphors ALLOW users to CHOOSE' - 'Technological metaphors...are active (...imposing)...forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon', 'Linguistic metaphors are passive...audience needs to choose'• ①: 'Linguistic metaphors demand...cognitive engagement' - 'audience needs to...actively enter'''without cognitive effort'• ②: 'Digital metaphors...active...manifested in functional digital tools' - 'realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things'• ③: 'technological metaphors...immediate and obvious utility' - 'usefulness...obvious at first glance'• ④: 'Shakespeare's works...beloved...complex...deep thought' - 'not immediately obvious and requires some thought'
options_translation: ① 언어재긴 으유는 의미를 도굴하기 위해 독자의 상당한 인지재긴 개이뱔 요구한다.
② 디지탈 으유는 기냉재긴 디지탈 도구로 나타나기 때무네 나ᄆ하가고 간주댜는다.
③ 기샐재긴 으유의 효과는 전형재그로 즈ᄀ각재기고 명해ᄀ한 유요상ᅦ 기반을 던다.
④ 세이ᄀ샤피어의 자ᄀ품은 그 의미가 보ᄀ자하고 기ᄑ은 새ᄀ각을 요구하기 때무네 노파개 평가바ᄃ는다.
⑤ 언어재긴 으유와 다르개, 디지탈 으유는 사용자가 그 기저에 깔린 개념과 상호자굥할지 여부를 샌택하개 한다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 오류가 있는 문장만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and does their own hunting at night</u>. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. ⓑ<u>Only when they looked again did they see a medium-sized octopus with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion</u>. ⓒ<u>An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature</u>. ⓓ<u>Many more of this species have found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes</u>. ⓔ<u>And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking them down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓐ는 'to stay'와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 'does'를 'do'로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓓ는 문맥상 이 종의 더 많은 개체들이 '발견되어 온' 것이므로 수동태인 'have been found'가 적절합니다. ⓔ는 앞에서 언급한 'an octopodian arm'이 단수이므로 대명사 'them'을 'it'으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 it may cease to be a story가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, <u>it may cease to be a story</u>. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
options: ① The climate-fiction genre may gradually gain attention as the reality becomes too immediate to ignore.
② Climate change may become too evident and unavoidable to be presented as a fictional story.
③ Climate change may become too trivial to be considered a serious issue in storytelling.
④ Climate change may no longer be a concern once it is resolved.
⑤ Climate change may turn out to be less severe than we think.
questions.explanation: 글의 문맥상 기후 변화가 매우 거대해지고 모든 곳에서 명백하게 나타나면, 덄 이상 '이얼기(fiction)'로서의 가치림 잃고 현실 괴 이상이 된다는 의미입니다. 창밖으로 혱신히 바라볼 수 있는 현실이 되어 방관할 수 없는 상태가 되면 픽션으로서의 기능을 멈춘다는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 기후 소설 장르는 현실이 무시하기에는 너무 직접적이 됨에 따라 점차 관심을 받을 수 있다.
② 기후 변화는 픽션 이얼기로 제시되기에는 너무 명백하고 피할 수 없게 되어 버릴 수 있다.
③ 기후 변화는 이얼기 구성에서 심각한 문제로 간주되기에 너무 사소해질 수 있다.
④ 기후 변화가 해결되고 나면 덄 이상 관심사가 아눐 수 있다.
⑤ 기후 변화는 우리가 생각하는 것밴다 덜 심각한 것으로 밝혀질 수 있다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race - their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't psychologically suffer much. In fact, ultra-marathon runners - those people who are crazy enough to push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50-100km or more over many hours, talk about making friends with their pain. When a patient has paid for some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it, the patient calls that good pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.
options: ① 의사의 통증 치료는 환자의 심리적 요인을 고려한다.
② 고통에 대한 인식이 우리가 얼마나 고통받는지를 결정한다.
③ 삶의 고통은 항상 부정적이고 극복해야 할 문제로 여겨진다.
④ 신체적 고통은 외부 요인과 내부 요인의 상호작용으로 결정된다.
⑤ 마라톤 선수들은 신체적, 정신적 고통을 견디는 훈련이 필요하다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 고통을 마음속에서 어떻게 정의하고 틀을 짜느냐(frame)에 따라 심리적으로 겪는 고통의 정도가 달라진다고 설명하고 있습니다. 달리기 선수나 치료를 받는 환자의 예시를 통해 고통을 가치 있는 것으로 인식할 때 고통을 덜 느낀다는 점을 강조합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.
options: ① Household chores should be divided among your family members.
② You need to find an exercise you enjoy and do it consistently.
③ Household chores should be utilized as an opportunity to incorporate simple exercises.
④ To maximize the effectiveness of exercise, you should gradually increase its intensity.
⑤ When doing household chores, you should consider the movement path to improve efficiency.
questions.explanation: 바쁜 일정 때문에 운동할 시간을 따로 내기 어려운 현대인들에게 집안일을 하는 시간을 활용해 미니 운동을 병행함으로써 건강을 개선할 수 있다는 제안을 하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 가사 노동은 가족 구성원들이 분담해야 한다.
② 즐거운 운동을 찾아 꾸준히 해야 한다.
③ 집안일을 간단한 운동을 병합하는 기회로 활용해야 한다.
④ 운동 효과를 극대화하기 위해 강도를 점진적으로 높여야 한다.
⑤ 집안일을 할 때 효율성을 높이기 위해 동선을 고려해야 한다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways, Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
options: ① Shakespeare's Influence on Digital Metaphor Design
② The Role of Cognitive Effort in Understanding Metaphors
③ An Analysis of Shakespeare's Use of Metaphor and Simile
④ Why Technological Metaphors Are More Imposing than Linguistic Ones
⑤ How Digital Technologies Utilize Metaphors Differently from Literary Works
questions.explanation: 지문은 언어적 은유(문학)와 디지털 기술 은유의 차이점에 대해 설명합니다. 언어적 은유는 독자의 능동적인 인지적 노력을 필요로 하지만, 기술적 은유는 사용자가 즉각적으로 이해할 수 있도록 설계되어 사용자의 경험 방식을 직접적으로 변화시킨다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로는 ⑤번 '디지털 기술이 문학 작품과 다르게 은유를 활용하는 방식'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 디지털 은유 설계에 미친 셰익스피어의 영향
② 은유를 이해하는 데 있어 인지적 노력의 역할
③ 셰익스피어의 은유와 직유 사용 분석
④ 기술적 은유가 언어적 은유보다 더 강요적인 이유
⑤ 디지털 기술이 문학 작품과 다르게 은유를 활용하는 방식

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
options: ① From Brain Imbalance to Consciousness: A New View on Depression
② Emotional Health: Why It's as Important as Physical Health
③ What Is the Classification of Disorders of Consciousness?
④ Happy or Sad: The Chemistry Behind Depression
⑤ The Role of the Brain in Conscious Processes
questions.explanation: 기존 의학은 우울증을 뇌의 화학적 불균형으로 보았으나, 본문은 뇌의 물질 불균형은 결과일 뿐이며 근본 원인은 자아와 삶의 의미를 잃어버린 '의식의 왜곡'에 있다고 주장합니다. 따라서 뇌의 불균형에서 의식으로 우울증을 보는 새로운 관점이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌의 불균형에서 의식으로: 우울증에 대한 새로운 관점
② 정서적 건강: 왜 육체적 건강만큼 중요한가
③ 의식 장애의 분류는 무엇인가?
④ 행복 혹은 슬픔: 우울증 뒤에 숨겨진 화학
⑤ 의식 과정에서 뇌의 역할

questions.question: 7. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 his face just popped out at me가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "<u>his face just popped out at me</u>," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
options: ③ information about the present situation
④ a statement after a certain period of time
⑤ a facial expression that reflects an emotional state
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 왜 알아보았는지 설명하지 못하면서 즉각적으로 누군가를 알아보는 상황을 묘사합니다. 글의 문맥상 이는 논리적이고 단계적인 정당화보다 더 정확할 수 있는 '무의식적인 최초의 추측' 또는 '자동적인 반응'을 의미하므로 2번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 신중하게 판단된 결과
② 무의식적인 초기 반응
③ 현재 상황에 대한 정보
④ 일정 기간이 지난 후의 진술
⑤ 감정 상태를 반영하는 얼굴 표정

questions.question: 8. 다음 Yummy Paws: Pet Food Cooking Class에 관한 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Yummy Paws: Pet Food Cooking ClassJoin us for an exciting pet food cooking class where you will learn how to create healthy and delicious pumpkin biscuits for your furry friends!When: 2:00p.m. - 4:00p.m., Every Sunday, December, 2024Where: Green Park Community Center, Room 5Registration•Register online at www.yummypawsclass.com.•Limited to 10 participants for each classFee•$30 per participant (Full payment is required when registering.)•The fee includes all ingredients.Note•Additional recipes available for free•For safety reasons, no pets are allowed.•For a refund, cancel at least 48 hours before the class.
