questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. Therefore, for two Australian underwater photographers, seeing one fully ⓐ<u>exposed</u> in the shallows in daylight was truly unexpected. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes ⓑ<u>staring</u> upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn ⓒ<u>itself</u> into a completely different creature. Many more of this species ⓓ<u>have found</u> since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing ⓔ<u>whatever</u> is hiding there.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'Many more of this species'(이 종의 훨씬 더 많은 개체들)이며, 맥락상 이들이 발견한 것이 아니라 (사람들에 의해) 발견되어 온 것이므로 수동태를 써야 합니다. 따라서 have found를 have been found로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than ⓐ<u>recalling</u> the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more ⓑ<u>systematic</u> way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who are ⓒ<u>deficient</u> in this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our ⓓ<u>assumptions</u>, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely ⓔ<u>reinforced</u> the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony.
questions.explanation: 기억이 비디오처럼 재생되는 것이 아니라 추상적인 표상을 통해 재구성된다는 발견은 목격자 증언의 법적 우위성을 '강화(reinforced)'하는 것이 아니라 '약화(undermined)'시킵니다. 재구성된 기억은 오류의 가능성이 높기 때문입니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which AI exceeds human intelligence. After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and ⓐ<u>evolve</u> at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a ⓑ<u>conscious</u> being, not just a machine. AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, which will ⓒ<u>provide</u> us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI. The direction of AI's evolution will ⓓ<u>create</u> what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a ⓔ<u>mutual</u> coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
questions.explanation: 인간의 의식 또한 AI의 진화에 중대한 영향을 미친다는 내용입니다. ⓓ번 문장은 AI 진화의 방향이 우리가 AI에 어떤 가치와 윤리를 통합하느냐에 '달려 있다' 혹은 그것을 '반영한다'는 내용이 되어야 합니다. 진화의 방향이 가치를 '창조(create)'하는 것이 아니라, 우리가 주입한 가치에 의해 진화의 방향이 '결정된다(depend on)' 혹은 '반영된다(reflect)'는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that _____________________________ help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 연구에서 추상적인 질문(예: 얼마나 자주 슬픈가?)보다 구체적인 상황을 묻는 질문(예: 아파서 출근하지 못할 정도로 슬픈 적이 몇 번인가?)이 더 신뢰할 수 있는 데이터를 제공한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 추상적인 개념을 명확하게 하고 일관성을 보장해주는 '구체적인 응답을 목표로 하는(aim for specific responses)' 질문이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 추상적인 추론을 추구하는
수치 분석을 요구하는
구체적인 응답을 목표로 하는
복잡한 계산을 필요로 하는
주관적인 해석을 포함하는

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially how _______________________________________ rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
options: ① we complement the limitations of technology
② we take specific actions to use the technology
③ to become an expert in the field of technology
④ to understand the underlying principles of technology
⑤ to troubleshoot any issues that arise when using technology
questions.explanation: 인간은 인지 능력의 한계 때문에 모든 원리를 다 알 필요 없이 사회적으로 전달된 '사용법'만을 학습하여 혜택을 누린다는 내용입니다. 컴퓨터나 변기의 원리를 알 필요 없이 '어떤 버튼을 누를지' 즉, '기술을 사용하기 위해 어떤 구체적인 행동을 취할지'만 알면 된다는 맥락이므로 ②가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 기술의 한계를 보완하는 방식
② 기술을 사용하기 위해 우리가 취하는 구체적인 행동
③ 기술 분야의 전문가가 되는 방법
④ 기술의 근본적인 원리를 이해하는 법
⑤ 기술 사용 시 발생하는 문제를 해결하는 법

questions.question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 40번]
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Alvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.'
ordered_passages: (A) For example, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
(B) A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it.

(C) For instance, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 언급된 '속임수 처벌(trick-punishments)'에 대한 정의가 (B)에서 가장 먼저 제시됩니다. (B)의 마지막 문장에서 속임수 처벌이 오히려 어떤 행동을 하도록 부추긴다는 점을 설명한 후, (C)에서 그 구체적인 예시(동생을 때리는 Hugh)를 통해 왜 아이가 벌을 받고 싶어 하는지(무시당하는 것보다 야단맞는 게 나음)를 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서는 이에 대한 대안적인 전략으로 부정적인 면을 지적하기보다 긍정적인 면에 보상하는 방법을 제시하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 38번]
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
questions.summary_sentence: Psychology studies human nature through evidence rather than (A)_________, and explores what generates the cultural and social (B)_________ of human beings.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 심리학은 의견이나 전해 듣는 말, 사회적 통념에 의존하지 않고 '증거(evidence)'에 기반을 둔다고 했으므로 (A)에는 assumption(추정) 또는 supposition(가정)이 적절합니다. 또한 심리학은 인간이 공유하는 것뿐만 아니라 풍부한 문화적, 사회적 '다양성(diversity)'을 생성하는 원리를 다룬다고 언급되었으므로 (B)에는 multiplicity(다양성, 다수)가 가장 적절합니다. diversity와 유의어인 multiplicity를 선택한 1번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 추정 / 다양성(다수성)
② 가정 / 균일성
③ 증언 / 변화
④ 증거 / 다양성
⑤ 신화 / 유사성

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It's untrue that teens can focus on two things at once - what they're doing is shifting their attention from one task to another. In this digital age, teens wire their brains to make these shifts very quickly, but they are still, like everyone else, paying attention to one thing at a time, sequentially. Common sense tells us multitasking should increase brain activity, but Carnegie Mellon University scientists using the latest brain imaging technology find it doesn't. As a matter of fact, they discovered that multitasking actually decreases brain activity. Neither task is done as well as if each were performed individually. Fractions of a second are lost every time we make a switch, and a person's interrupted task can take 50 percent longer to finish, with 50 percent more errors. Turns out the latest brain research supports the old advice "one thing at a time."It's not that kids can't do some tasks simultaneously. But if two tasks are performed at once, one of them has to be familiar. Our brains perform a familiar task on "automatic pilot" while really paying attention to the other one. That's why insurance companies consider talking on a cell phone and driving to be as dangerous as driving while drunk - it's the driving that goes on "automatic pilot" while the conversation really holds our attention. Our kids may be living in the Information Age but our brains have not been redesigned yet.
questions.summary_sentence: Contrary to common belief, multitasking doesn't (A)___________ brain activity but rather diminishes it, and if two tasks are performed simultaneously, one of them must be a highly (B)___________ task.
questions.explanation: 멀티태스킹이 뇌 활동을 증가시킬 것이라는 통념과 달리 실제로는 뇌 활동을 줄이며(diminishes), 두 가지 일을 동시에 하려면 그 중 하나는 익숙해서 '자동 조종(automatic pilot)' 상태로 수행될 수 있는 일상적인(routinized) 것이어야 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '증가시키다/높이다(elevate)', (B)에는 '일상적인/익숙한(routinized)'이 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 높이다 - 일상화된
② 향상시키다 - 예외적인
③ 최적화하다 - 복잡한
④ 측정하다 - 자발적인
⑤ 소비하다 - 익숙한

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (단, 필요시 문맥에 맞게 변형하여 쓸 것)
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
questions.summary_sentence: Influenced by a three-tier product strategy, people buy the middle item, without realizing the (A)__________ involved in introducing the (B)__________ model.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 쓸 것
필요시 문맥에 맞게 변형할 것
questions.explanation: 본문 마지막 문장에서 소비자들이 더 비싼 품목(higher-priced item)의 존재에 의해 조종당했다(manipulated)는 것을 인지하지 못한 채 중간 품목을 산다고 언급되어 있습니다. 요약문의 (A)에는 명사형인 manipulation이, (B)에는 해당 전략에서 기준이 된 higher-priced(또는 fanciest)가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
options: ① Climate change will no longer serve as a source of literary inspiration,
② As climate change becomes more evident in daily life, climate fiction is likely to disappear.
③ Climate change provokes greater fear when perceived as a distant future issue.
④ Novels depicting climate disasters play a key role in encouraging real-world action.
⑤ The gap between real-world problems and literary imagination is widening.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기혔 변화가 일상적인 현실이 됨에 따라 기혔 소설(climate-fiction) 장르가 사라질 것이라고 좼장하고 은 글입니다. 즁, 기혔 재사이 멀리 떨어진 이야기일 때는 핔께 소설로 소비될 수 읈지만, 창밖으로 바로 바라볼 수 읈는 현실이 되면 덄 이성 픽션으로서의 의미가 없어진다는 것이 핵심 내용입니다. 따라서 '기혔 변화가 일상에서 더 명확해준에 따라 기혔 픽션은 사라질 가능성이 크다'는 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 기혔 변화는 덄 이성 문학적 영감의 원천으로 작용하준 않을 것이다.
② 기혔 변화가 일상 생활에서 더 분명해준에 따라, 기혔 픽션은 사라질 가능성이 있다.
③ 기혔 변화는 멀리 떨어진 미래의 문제로 인식될 때 덄 큰 공포를 유발한다.
④ 기혔 재앂을 묘사하는 소설은 실제 세계의 행동을 촉구하는 데 핵심적인 역할을 한다.
⑤ 실제 세계의 문제와 문학적 상상력 사이의 갓극이 바어지고 있다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: In his laboratory at Cornell, David. Dunning conducted experimental tests on eyewitness testimony and found that a meticulous examination of facial features, along with a thorough discussion of selection procedures, can indicate an inaccurate identification. ⓐIt's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. ⓑThis phenomenon suggests that our initial, automatic reactions to situations may provide the clearest interpretation of our thoughts. ⓒThat very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. ⓓFor example, eyewitness testimonies may be more dependable when witnesses take time to reflect on specific details and context, rather than relying solely on an initial, unexamined impression. ⓔIn his book Bink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 신중한 분석보다는 직관적이고 무의식적인 첫 인상이 더 정확할 수 있다는 내용을 다리고 있습다. 목격자 증언에서도 유의미한 분석보다는 '그냥 누에 툰다'는 직관이 더 정확하다는 실험 결과를 설명합다. 그러나 ⓓ번은 목격자가 세부 사항을 숙고할 때 증언이 더 신뢰할 만하다고 하여 글의 전체 주제와 정바대되는 주장을 하고 있습다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 부분을 포함하고 있는 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later ⓐ<u>most of us gradually become less interested in the TV shows that we enjoy</u>. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, ⓑ<u>which are programmed to gradually lesser their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur.</u> At the same time, ⓒ<u>these neurons enhance their responses to things that change</u> - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, ⓓ<u>from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself</u>. ⓔ<u>Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turn down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stands out more</u>. It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
questions.explanation: ⓔ번 문장에서 주어는 'Boredom'(단수)이므로 이에 연결되는 동사는 turn이 아니라 3인칭 단수형인 turns가 되어야 합니다. 또한, 뒤의 new stimuli는 복수형(stimulus의 복수)이므로 이에 호응하는 동사도 stands가 아닌 stand가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 trick-punishments가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid <u>trick-punishments</u>.
options: ① effective methods for managing sibling rivalry
② scolding that immediately resolves behavioral issues
③ punishments that unintentionally encourage bad behavior
④ strategies to teach children through positive feedback
⑤ consequences designed to help children understand rules
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'trick-punishments'는 아이의 나쁜 행동을 억제하기보다는 오히려 그 행동을 계속하게 만드는 처벌을 의미합니다. 외로운 아이가 부모의 관심을 얻기 위해 동생을 때리고 꾸중을 듣는 예시가 이를 뒷받침합니다. 따라서 '의도치 않게 나쁜 행동을 부추기는 처벌들'인 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 형제간의 경쟁을 관리하기 위한 효과적인 방법들
② 행동 문제를 즉각적으로 해결하는 꾸짖음
③ 의도치 않게 나쁜 행동을 조장하는 처벌들
④ 긍정적인 피드백을 통해 아이들을 가르치는 전략들
⑤ 아이들이 규칙을 이해하도록 돕기 위해 설계된 결과들

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do: and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
options: ① the origins and development of psychology
② how psychology relies on cultural assumptions
questions.explanation: 제공된 지문의 마지막 문항인 12번은 선택지가 중간에 끊겨 있어 정답을 확정할 수 없으며, 분석 규칙에 따라 불완전한 질문으로 간주될 수 있으나 요청에 따라 포함하였습니다. (실제 데이터셋 구축 시에는 제외 권장)
options_translation: ① 심리학의 기원과 발전
② 심리학이 문화적 가정에 의존하는 방식

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Unlike linguistic metaphors, technological metaphors are designed for immediate understanding, reflecting the efficiency of digital technologies. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
options: ① how metaphors are designed to require cognitive effort for immediate comprehension
② the distinctions between digital metaphors and linguistic metaphors
③ the inefficiency of digital metaphors in modern technology
④ linguistic metaphors only appreciated by passive audiences
⑤ hidden digital metaphors invented by Shakespeare
questions.explanation: 이 글은 언어적 은유(수동적이며 이해를 위해 인지적 노력이 필요함)와 디지털/기술적 은유(능동적이며 즉각적이고 명확한 이해를 추구함)의 차이점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 '디지털 은유와 언어적 은유 사이의 구별'입니다.
options_translation: ① 즉각적인 이해를 위해 인지적 노력을 필요로 하도록 은유가 설계되는 방식
② 디지털 은유와 언어적 은유 사이의 구별
③ 현대 기술에서 디지털 은유의 비효율성
④ 수동적인 청중들만이 감상하는 언어적 은유
⑤ 셰익스피어에 의해 발명된 숨겨진 디지털 은유

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When writing a novel, research for information needs to be done. The thing is that some kinds of fiction demand a higher level of detail: crime fiction, for example, or scientific thrillers. The information is never hard to find: one website for authors even organizes trips to police stations, so that crime writers can get it right. Often, a polite letter will earn you permission to visit a particular location and record all the details that you need. But remember that you will drive your readers to boredom if you think that you need to pack everything you discover into your work. The details that matter are those that reveal the human experience. The crucial thing is telling a story, finding the characters, the tension, and the conflict - not the train timetable or the building blueprint.
options: ① Metaphors and Similes: Painting Pictures with Words
② The Importance of First Lines: Enchanting Readers Instantly
③ The Process of Effectively Managing Scientific Information in Writing
④ The Art of Writing: Infusing Details without Overloading the Story
⑤ The Hidden Secret to Writing Success: More Details, Better Stories
questions.explanation: 소설을 작성할 때 구체적인 세부 사항을 위한 조사는 필수적이지만, 조사한 모든 정보를 작품에 다 담으려 하면 독자를 지루하게 만들 수 있습니다. 중요한 것은 열차 시간표나 설계도 같은 파편적인 정보가 아니라, 인간의 경험을 보여줄 수 있는 세부 사항을 선별하여 이야기의 긴장감과 갈등 속에 녹여내는 것입니다. 따라서 ④번 '작문 기술: 이야기에 과부하를 주지 않으면서 세부 사항을 불어넣기'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 은유와 직유: 말로 그림 그리기
② 첫 문장의 중요성: 독자를 즉각적으로 매료시키기
③ 글쓰기에서 과학적 정보를 효과적으로 관리하는 과정
④ 작문의 기술: 이야기에 과부하를 주지 않으면서 세부 사항을 불어넣기
⑤ 글쓰기 성공의 숨겨진 비밀: 더 많은 세부 사항, 더 나은 이야기

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
options: ① Understanding the Process of Image Compression
② The Tangible Brain Malfunction in Distorting Memory
③ Eyewitness Illusions: How Memory and Reality Diverge
④ The Contribution of Motivation in Shaping Our Memories
⑤ Unlocking Creativity: Techniques to Spark Innovation
questions.explanation: 인간은 본 것을 있는 그대로 기억하는 것이 아니라 자신이 아는 개념과 과거의 경험을 통해 재구성하여 저장한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 이러한 재구성 과정 때문에 실제와 기억이 달라질 수 있으며 목격자 증언의 신뢰성이 떨어진다는 결론으로 이어지므로 '목격자의 환상: 기억과 현실이 갈라지는 방식'이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 이미지 압축 과정 이해하기
② 기억을 왜곡하는 실질적인 뇌 기능 장애
③ 목격자의 환상: 기억과 현실이 갈라지는 방식
④ 우리 기억을 형성하는 데 있어서 동기의 기여
⑤ 창의력 잠금 해제: 혁신을 촉발하는 기술

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we ⓐ<u>managed</u> relationships in a group. If the group valued us we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these ⓑ<u>advantage</u>. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to ⓒ<u>deliberately</u> monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions ⓓ<u>drive</u> us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it ⓔ<u>less</u> convincing.
questions.explanation: 지문의 맥락상 집단 내에서의 생존을 위해 타인의 시선을 모니터링하는 경향은 오랜 진화의 결과로 형성된 자동적이고 무의식적인 반응에 가깝습니다. 또한 마지막 문장에서 우리가 사회적 압력에 반응하고 있음을 '의식적인 수준(conscious level)'에서 깨닫는다면 연기가 설득력이 떨어진다고 언급하고 있으므로, 타인의 인식을 모니터링하는 것이 '의도적으로(deliberately)' 이루어진다는 표현은 문맥상 어색하며, '자동적으로(automatically)' 등의 표현이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers. I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been ⓐ<u>reluctant</u> to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the more ⓑ<u>inexpensive</u> one. But if the company ⓒ<u>launches</u> a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up: many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is more ⓓ<u>affordable</u> than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been ⓔ<u>manipulated</u> by the presence of the higher-priced item.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 가격 책정 전략 중 '미끼 효과(Decoy Effect)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 제품이 한 가지 버전만 있을 때, 사람들은 더 많은 돈을 쓸 '준비가 되어 있을(willing)' 수도 있는데, 선택지가 하나뿐이라 지출을 더 하지 못하게 되어 회사가 수입을 잃게 된다는 문맥이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 '꺼려하는(reluctant)'은 문맥상 반대 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing ⓐ<u>challenge</u>. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? This is where the concept of incorporating mini-exercises into household chores becomes ⓑ<u>redundant</u>. Chores are a part of life; whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, they are ⓒ<u>unavoidable</u>. But Rather than perceiving chores as mere obligations, why not embrace these moments as ⓓ<u>invaluable</u> opportunities for physical exertion? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. ⓔ<u>Embedding</u> quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.
questions.explanation: 바쁜 일상 속에서 집안일에 미니 운동을 통합하는 개념은 매우 유용하고 의미가 있다는 흐름입니다. 따라서 '불필요한, 중복되는(redundant)'이라는 단어는 문맥상 적절하지 않으며, '유용한(useful)'이나 '가치 있는(valuable)' 같은 단어가 와야 합니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This ①<u>anxiety</u> naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It can be challenging to ②<u>detach</u> oneself from things that have been a part of life for a long time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple: the premise of the question is fundamentally ③<u>flawed</u>. Minimalism does not harm emotions. While you may feel a twinge of sadness when parting with an item that no longer serves you, that feeling will soon be ④<u>overshadowed</u> by the joy of having a clearer and more organized space. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to ⑤<u>accumulate</u> stuff that is unused or not going to be used in the near future.
questions.explanation: ⑤ 'accumulate'는 '축적하다, 모으다'라는 뜻입니다. 미니멀리스트는 사용하지 않는 물건을 축적하는 것이 아니라 '제거해야(eliminate/discard)' 한다고 주장하므로 문맥상 반대 의미인 'accumulate'는 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants. Not only were their athletic talents superior, the Cubans appeared even stronger from just the colour of their uniforms. A game would not even start and the opposing team would already be scared. A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries style: interestingly, the national team has declined since that time. The country that ruled international baseball for decades has not been on top since that uniform change. Traditions are important for a team: while a team brand or image can adjust to keep up with present times, if it abandons or neglects its roots, negative effects can surface.
options: ① Cuba dominated the world baseball scene between 1940 and 2000.
② Cuba won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games.
③ Cuban baseball uniforms contrasted strongly with North American styles.
④ The modernization of the Cuban uniforms may have aligned them with other countries' styles.
⑤ The decline of Cuba's baseball team started well before it changed its uniform.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 쿠바 야구팀의 하락세는 유니폼 스타일을 현대화하고 다른 나라의 스타일에 맞추어 변경한 시점부터 시작되었다고 언급되어 있습니다. 따라서 유니폼을 바꾸기 훨씬 전부터 하락세가 시작되었다는 5번 선택지는 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 쿠바는 1940년에서 2000년 사이에 세계 야구계를 지배했다.
② 쿠바는 첫 28회의 월드컵 중 25회, 5회의 올림픽 중 3회 우승했다.
③ 쿠바의 야구 유니폼은 북미 스타일과 강한 대조를 이루었다.
④ 쿠바 유니폼의 현대화는 그것들을 다른 나라의 스타일에 맞추었을 수도 있다.
⑤ 쿠바 야구팀의 쇠퇴는 유니폼을 바꾸기 훨씬 전부터 시작되었다.

questions.question: 31. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works: you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are __________________________________.
options: ① acting against the larger computation
② contributing to a much larger collective effort
③ ignoring the complexities of our communal efforts
④ harming society's shared brain by refusing to cooperate with others
⑤ avoiding contributing to the collective brain by aggregating knowledge
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간이 인지적 한계를 극복하기 위해 정보를 세대에 걸쳐 분산시키고, 모든 원리를 이해하기보다 인터페이스 사용법을 사회적으로 학습하며 살아간다고 설명합니다. 개인은 거대한 계산의 작은 부분을 담당하며 전체에 기여한다는 내용이 핵심이므로, '훨씬 더 큰 집단적 노력에 기여하고 있다'는 2번이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 큰 계산에 반하여 행동하고 있다
② 훨씬 더 큰 집단적 노력에 기여하고 있다
③ 우리 공동 노력의 복잡성을 무시하고 있다
④ 타인과의 협력을 거부함으로써 사회의 공유된 두뇌에 해를 끼치고 있다
⑤ 지식을 집약함으로써 집단적 두뇌에 기여하는 것을 피하고 있다

questions.question: 32. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the passage, depression should be understood not as a (A)__________ problem, but as a (B)__________ issue.
questions.explanation: 지문은 우울증을 뇌의 신경전달물질 불균형(신경학적 문제)으로 보는 기존의 관점을 비판하며, 이를 의식의 왜곡이나 자아 및 삶의 의미 상실과 같은 의식의 문제(인식의 문제)로 보아야 한다고 주장합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 'neurological(신경학적인)', (B)에는 'awareness(인식)'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 감정적인, (B) 신체적인
② (A) 기계적인, (B) 의사소통의
③ (A) 심리적인, (B) 생리적인
④ (A) 신경학적인, (B) 인식의
⑤ (A) 정신적인, (B) 도덕적인

questions.question: 33. 다음 글(A)를 토대로 하여, 같은 주제로 (B)를 작성하고자 한다. 글(B)의 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.(B) In light of the importance of formulating ⓐ_________ questions to improve the reliability of quantitative research, it is essential for researchers, educators, and practitioners to adopt this approach in their methodologies. By ⓑ_________ precision rather than ambiguity, we can elevate the quality of our research findings, leading to more informed decisions and effective strategies.
questions.explanation: 글 (A)는 추상적인 개념을 측정할 때 신뢰성을 높이기 위해 구체적인(concrete) 질문을 던져야 함을 강조합니다. 이를 바탕으로 작성된 글 (B)에서도 양적 연구의 신뢰성을 위해 구체적인(specific) 질문을 구성하고, 모호함보다는 정확성을 우선시(prioritizing)해야 한다는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ 구체적인, ⓑ 우선시함으로써
② ⓐ 모호한, ⓑ 경시함으로써
③ ⓐ 모호한, ⓑ 무시함으로써
④ ⓐ 무작위의, ⓑ 묵살함으로써
⑤ ⓐ 불분명한, ⓑ 반대함으로써

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 to create the illusion이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards <u>to create the illusion</u>. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
options: ① to hunt for the flounder nearby
② to hide behind the surrounding rocks
③ to pose for the underwater photographers
④ to camouflage itself into some other creatures
⑤ to form a temporary elbow, bending to draw objects toward its mouth
questions.explanation: 준비된 글에서 문어가 다른 생물(가재물치 등)로 변신하여 자신을 숨기고 사냥하는 모습을 묘사하고 은휴적으로 '환상을 만들기 위해'라고 표현하였으므로, 이는 다른 생물로 위장하는 것을 의묘합니다.
options_translation: ① 근처의 가재물치림 사냥하기 위해
② 주변의 바위 됤에 숨기 위해
③ 수중 사진 선수들을 위해 포즈림 취하기 위해
④ 다른 생물로 자신을 위­장하기 위해
⑤ 일시적인 팔꿈치림 만들어 물체림 입 쪽으로 끌어당기기 위해

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is <u>a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals</u>, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
options: ① perfect circles that can be found in the physical world
② Forms that are simply subjectively interpreted as physical objects
③ the world of Forms that is irrelevant to our everyday experiences
④ universals that are believed to be the only reality that matters
⑤ the physical world that is an imperfect representation of a higher, ideal reality
questions.explanation: 플라톤은 옰리가 보는 물뮬적 세계가 보이지 않는 완벽한 형상(이데아)의 불완전한 투영이라고 주장했습니다. 따라서 밑줄 친 부분은 물뮬적 세계가 덄 높고 이상적인 실제의 불완전한 재현임을 의묘합니다.
options_translation: ① 물뮬적 세계에서 발견될 수 있는 완벽한 원들
② 단순히 주관적으로 물뮬적 대상으로 해석된 형상들
③ 옰리의 일상 경험과 무관한 형상의 세계
④ 중요한 유일한 실제라고 믿어지뉀 개널들
⑤ 덄 높고 이상적인 실제의 불완전한 재현인 물뮬적 세계

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Despite the remarkable progress in deep-learning based facial recognition approaches in recent years, in terms of identification performance, they still have limitations. These limitations relate to the database used in the learning stage. If the selected database does not contain enough instances, the result may be systematically affected. For example, the performance of a facial biometric system may decrease if the person to be identified was enrolled over 10 years ago. The factor to consider is that this person may experience changes in the texture of the face, particularly with the appearance of wrinkles and sagging skin. These changes may be highlighted by weight gain or loss. To counteract this problem, researchers have developed models for face aging. It is used to compensate for the differences in facial characteristics, which appear over a given time period.
options: ① 노화를 막는 것은 어렵지만, 식습관의 개선을 통해 노화 속도를 늦출 수 있다.
② 일부 노인들은 피부 노화와 감각 기능의 저하로 적극적인 구직활동에서 어려움을 겪는다.
③ 사람의 외모와 음성을 인식하는 AI 기술은 정교한 신원확인을 가능하게 하여 안전한 사회를 유지하는데 기여한다.
④ 얼굴 인식 접근법은 데이터 베이스의 한계를 보완하고 식별 능력을 향상시키기 위해 얼굴 노화 모델을 개발해왔다.
⑤ 인간의 뇌 신경을 모방한 딥러닝 기술은 인간처럼 스스로 학습하고 수집한 데이터를 분석하여 미래를 예측할 수
questions.explanation: 딥러닝 기반 얼굴 인식 시스템이 학습 데이터베이스의 한계(시간 경과에 따른 얼굴 변화 등)로 인해 식별 성능이 저하되는 문제가 발생할 수 있는데, 이를 해결하기 위해 연구자들이 얼굴 노화 모델을 개발해왔다는 것이 글의 요지입니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
options: ① the modernization of burial and cremation procedures
② the challenges of organ rejection in transplant recipients
③ the advancement of technology in organ transplantation surgeries
④ the benefits of lenient guidelines for organ donation practices
⑤ a uniform set of diagnostic criteria required for the diagnosis of brain death
questions.explanation: 장기 기증 시 뇌사 판정을 위한 엄격한 지침들이 오히려 대중의 불신을 초래할 수 있으므로, 일관성을 위해 장기 기증자의 사망 진단 기준은 일반적인 사망 진단 기준과 동일해야 한다는 주장을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로는 뇌사 판정을 위한 통일된 진단 기준의 필요성을 언급한 5번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 매장 및 화장 절차의 현대화
② 이식 수혜자의 장기 거부 반응의 어려움
③ 장기 이식 수술의 기술적 발전
④ 장기 기증 관행을 위한 관대한 지침의 이점
⑤ 뇌사 판정을 위해 요구되는 통일된 진단 기준 세트

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 11월 20번]
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. They do well enough in school to keep advancing. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ends with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now lack a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when the journey really begins. When school is finished, your growth becomes voluntary. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career are likely to stop progressing as a result.
options: ① Why College Education Guarantees Lifelong Success
② Voluntary Growth: The Key to Lifelong Advancement
③ Balancing Work, Growth, and Responsibility in Adulthood

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 21번]
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
options: ② The Potential Fallibility of Human Memories
③ Video Data Management and Information Retrieval
④ Seeing is Believing: An Introduction to Visual Communication
⑤ Mistaken Identification: The Eyewitness, Psychology and the Law
questions.explanation: 인간의 기억은 있는 그대로를 저장하는 것이 아니라 교육받은 개념과 과거의 경험을 바탕으로 재구성(reconstruct)된다는 내용입니다. 이러한 재구성 과정은 정보를 효율적으로 저장하게 해주지만, 세상을 있는 그대로 보지 못하게 하고 목격자 진언의 신뢰성을 떨어뜨리는 등의 오류 가능성을 내포합니다. 따라서 인간 기억의 잠재적 오류 가능성(fallibility)이 제목으로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간 본성에 대한 가정
② 인간 기억의 잠재적 오류 가능성
③ 비디오 데이터 관리 및 정보 검색
④ 보는 것이 믿는 것이다: 시각적 소통 입문
⑤ 잘못된 식별: 목격자, 심리학 그리고 법

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The platypus, a unique and fascinating creature, is a semiaquatic, egg-laying mammal native to eastern Australia. Its unusual appearance, with a duck-like bill, beaver-like body, and otter-like feet, baffled early European naturalists who initially believed it to be a hoax. The platypus is one of only five extant species of monotremes, mammals that lay eggs instead of giving birth to live young. Along with the echidna, the platypus is a member of this ancient lineage, making it a living link to the evolutionary past.The platypus is perfectly adapted to its freshwater habitat, navigating murky waters with ease and using its bill to detect the minute movements of its prey. This bill is not hard like a duck's bill but is soft and rubbery, filled with thousands of electrical receptors that allow the platypus to locate prey even in dark, murky waters. The platypus is also one of the few venomous mammals, with males possessing a spur on their hind leg that delivers a painful venom. This venom, while not fatal to humans, can cause excruciating pain and other symptoms.
options: ① 오리너구리는 알을 낳는 포유류로 동부 오스트레일리아가 원산지이다.
② 유럽의 자연주의자들은 처음에 오리너구리의 특이한 외형 때문에 가짜라고 믿었다.
③ 오리너구리의 부리는 딱딱하여 어두운 물속에서도 먹잇감을 찾을 수 있게 해준다.
④ 오리너구리는 현존하는 다섯 종의 단공류 중 하나로 진화적 과거를 잇는 생물이다.
⑤ 수컷 오리너구리는 뒷다리에 고통스러운 독을 내뿜는 가시를 가지고 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 두 번째 단락을 보면 오리너구리의 부리는 오리의 부리처럼 딱딱한 것이 아니라 '부드럽고 고무 같다(soft and rubbery)'고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 ③번은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Nearly everything has to go through your mouth ⓐ<u>to get</u> to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body ⓑ<u>gets</u> what it needs and prevent it from harm - with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. From the moment you are created, oral health ⓒ<u>affect</u> every aspect of your life. What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and a reflection of ⓓ<u>what</u> is happening in other parts of the body. Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease ⓔ<u>where</u> affects the entire body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, ⓕ<u>posing</u> serious health risks.
questions.explanation: ⓑ help 동사는 목적격 보어로 동사원형이나 to부정사를 취하므로 gets는 get 또는 to get으로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓒ 주어인 oral health가 3인칭 단수이므로 동사는 affects가 되어야 합니다. ⓔ 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 문장이 오므로 관계부사인 where 대신 주격 관계대명사인 which 또는 that을 써야 합니다. ⓐ, ⓓ, ⓕ는 문법적으로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a(n) ⓐ<u>dedicated</u> workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of ⓑ<u>merging</u> mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are ⓒ<u>evitable</u>. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely ⓓ<u>obligatory</u> activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can ⓔ<u>enhance</u> your health.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 집안일(chores)은 설거지나 쓰레기 버리기처럼 일상의 필수적인 부분이며 피할 수 없는 일이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '피할 수 있는'이라는 뜻의 evitable 대신 '피할 수 없는'이라는 뜻의 inevitable이 와야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances 'in the brain is a(n) ⓐ<u>consequence</u> of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decline in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a(n) ⓑ<u>decrease</u> in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to ⓒ<u>reframe</u> depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes ⓓ<u>within</u> the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a(n) ⓔ<u>distortion</u> of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
questions.explanation: 지문의 주장은 의식이 뇌의 기능보다 더 근본적인 실체이며 뇌를 초월한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 의식이 뇌의 기능 '안에' 있다는 의미의 within이 아니라 '너머에' 혹은 '초월하여'라는 의미인 beyond가 문맥상 더 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of a(n) ____________ identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be precise more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be truer about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.explanation: 지문은 얼굴 특징에 대한 신중한 숙고나 상세한 토론보다는, 즉각적이고 자동적인 반응(직관)이 더 정확한 식별로 이어진다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 신중한 숙고는 오히려 '부정확한(inaccurate)' 식별의 신호가 될 수 있다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 계획적인
② 즉흥적인
③ 부정확한
④ 방향의
⑤ 정확한

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' ___________ brains.
questions.explanation: 인간은 인지적 한계 때문에 정보를 혼자 처리하지 않고 인구 전체에 분산시켜 해결하며, 개개인은 거대한 계산의 작은 부분을 담당한다는 것이 글의 핵심입니다. 따라서 우리 사회의 '집단적인(collective)' 두뇌를 위해 역할을 수행하고 있다는 표현이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 집단적인

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their _______________________________. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of clarity. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era.
options: ④ desire to arrange things neatly
⑤ connections to the things that they acquired
questions.explanation: 미니멀리즘이 소중한 소유물을 희생하는 것이라고 생각하며 불안함을 느끼는 이유는 사람들이 주변 사물에 감정적 의미를 부여하고 오랫동안 함께한 사물과 거리를 두기 어렵기 때문입니다. 즉, 자신이 '획득한 물건들과의 연결감(connections to the things that they acquired)'에서 이러한 불안감이 비롯된다고 보는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to ___________________________. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
options: ① make that motivation feel like it is coming from within
② cause us to avoid making deeper relationship in the group
③ motivate such goal-seekers to achieve higher social status
④ emerge and be expressed to let group members perceive them
⑤ exhaust all negative emotions instead of harming physical wellness
questions.explanation: 인간은 집단 내 평판을 관리하기 위해 자존감, 자부심, 수치심 같은 감정을 발달시켰습니다. 이러한 감정들은 사회적 압력에 반응하는 것이지만, 만약 우리가 이것이 외부의 압력 때문임을 의식한다면 행동이 냉소적으로 보일 수 있습니다. 따라서 이러한 감정들은 '그 동기가 내면에서 나오는 것처럼 느껴지게(make that motivation feel like it is coming from within)' 하여 우리의 행동이 더 설득력 있게 보이도록 하는 역할을 합니다.
options_translation: 그 동기가 내면에서 나오는 것처럼 느껴지게 하다
우리가 집단 내에서 더 깊은 관계를 맺는 것을 피하게 하다
그러한 목표 추구자들이 더 높은 사회적 지위를 얻도록 동기 부여하다

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 23번]
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data.
ordered_passages: (A) Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.

(B) Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer.

(C) A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 많은 연구가 정량적 데이터로 이어진다는 일반적인 사실을 언급합니다. (C)에서 행복이나 기억 연구의 예시를 들며 슬픔의 횟수를 묻는 것이 정량적 데이터를 주지만 신뢰할 수 없을 수 있음을 제기합니다. (B)에서 그 신뢰성의 문제(부정확한 기억, 정의의 차이)를 지적하며 구체적인 질문의 필요성을 제시합니다. (A)에서 '마찬가지로(Similarly)'라는 연결어를 통해 미루는 습관에 대한 또 다른 구체적 질문의 예를 들어 결론을 맺는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which AI exceeds human intelligence. After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. (A) When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. (B) Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. (C) Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI. (D) The direction of Al's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. (E) We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
questions.insertion_sentence: AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 AI와 인간의 의식이 함께 진화하기 시작할 것이라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A)에서 AI가 의식 있는 존재가 되는 상황을 설명한 후, (B)에서 인간의 의식이 AI와의 상호작용을 통해 새로운 차원으로 진화한다는 구체적인 상호 진화의 양상을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '함께 진화한다'는 총괄적 선언인 주어진 문장은 (B) 자리에 위치하여 뒤따르는 내용을 이끄는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.summary_sentence: Linguistic metaphors and digital metaphors are different in that the former require (A)_________ effort to interpret, whereas the latter are more (B)_________ and directly shape the user's experience through technology.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 언어적 은유(셰익스피어의 예시)를 이해하기 위해서는 청중의 '인지적 노력(cognitive effort)'이 필요합니다. 반면, 기술적 은유는 첫눈에 그 유용성이 명확해야 하므로 '직관적(intuitive)'입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 cognitive, (B)에는 intuitive가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인지적인 ... 직관적인
② 무의식적인 ... 구체적인
③ 사려 깊은 ... 임의적인
④ 글자 그대로의 ... 추상적인
⑤ 본능적인 ... 두드러진

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. We can endure great pain if we believe at that it is purposeful. For instance, when a patient has paid for some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to 'mobilise' it, the patient calls that 'good' pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race - their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't psychologically suffer much from their pain. In fact, ultra-marathon runners - those people who are crazy enough to push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50-100km or more over many hours, talk about 'making friends with their pain'.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The adolescent brain is not fully developed until its early twenties. This means the way the adolescents' decision-making circuits integrate and process information may put them at a disadvantage. One of their brain regions that matures later is the prefrontal cortex, which is the control center, tasked with thinking ahead and evaluating consequences. It is the area of the brain responsible for preventing you from sending off an initial angry text and modifying it with kinder words. On the other hand, the limbic system matures earlier, playing a central role in processing emotional responses. Because of its earlier development, it is more likely to influence decision-making. Decision-making in the adolescent brain is led by emotional factors more than the perception of consequences. Due to these differences, there is an imbalance between feeling-based decision-making ruled by the more mature limbic system and logical-based decision-making by the not-yet-mature prefrontal cortex. This may explain why some teens are more likely to make bad decisions.
questions.summary_sentence: During adolescence, there is a notable (A)____________ in the development of the prefrontal cortex compared to the limbic system, which can lead to (B)____________ decision-making, sometimes with adverse consequences.
questions.explanation: 청소년기 뇌에서 감정을 담당하는 변엮계(일찡 발달)와 이성적 판단을 담당하는 전두엽(닦게 발달)의 발달 셄도 차이(불균형)를 설명하고 있습니다. (A)에는 발달의 차이를 뜻하는 'disparity'(차이, 불균형)가 적절하며, (B)에는 이로 인해 나타나는 충동적인 의사결정을 뜻하는 'impulsive'가 적합합니다. (①번의 imbalance는 (A)에는 맞지만 rational은 (B)에 맞지 않습니다.)

questions.question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고 <조건>에 맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, ________________________________________ each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고, <조건>에 맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time. questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고, <조건>에 맞게 빈칸 (A)~(C)를 완성하시오. [24년 10월 33번]

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [23년 11월 32번]
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be changed by the joy of clarity. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused or not going to be used in the near future.
options: ① How Minimalism Can Actually Boost Your Well-being
② The Benefits of Coloring Your Life with Possessions
③ Small Changes, Big Impact: Sustainable Consumption
④ Mindful Consumption: Making Conscious Choices
⑤ The More, The Better: Our Needs and Emotions
questions.explanation: 이 글은 미니멀리즘이 소중한 소유물을 희생하는 것이라는 부정적인 오해를 바로잡고, 실제로는 불필요한 물건을 정리함으로써 정서적 명료함과 기쁨을 얻을 수 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 미니멀리즘이 어떻게 우리의 웰빙(안녕)을 증진할 수 있는지를 묻는 ①번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
options: ① Balancing Organ Donation and Public Trust
② Regulations in European Medical Practices
③ Ethics of Burial and Cremation Practices
④ Whole - Body Health Standards for Donors
⑤ Legal Aspects of Organ Donation in the World

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
options: ① 우울증은 뇌의 물질보다는 의식과 더 관련이 있다.
② 우울증의 주요 원인은 뇌의 물리적 손상 때문이다.
③ 우울증은 치료 없이 자연적으로 회복될 수 있다.
④ 우울증은 뇌에서 특정 호르몬의 부족 때문이다.
⑤ 약물 복용이 우울증의 최선의 해결책이다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우울증이 뇌 화학 물질의 불균형 때문에 생기는 것이 아니라, 오히려 우울증이 그 불균형을 초래하며, 우울증의 근본 원인은 자아 감각과 삶의 의미를 잃은 '의식의 왜곡'에 있다고 주장합니다. 따라서 우울증이 물질적 원인보다 의식과 관련이 깊다는 ①번이 요지로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light-a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless-and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective-"the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 (A), (B)에 들어갈 연결사로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence ⓐ<u>that</u> a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's ⓑ<u>when</u> people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of ⓒ<u>which</u> our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, ⓓ<u>reasoned</u> self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that ⓔ<u>demonstrate</u> the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.explanation: ⓒ 'which'는 관계대명사나 의문형용사 등으로 쓰이는데, 여기서는 'telling us'의 목적어가 필요하고 선행사가 없으므로 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사인 'what'으로 바꾸는 것이 어법상 옳습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [23년 11월 34번]
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or ⓐ<u>drawn</u> in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you ⓑ<u>look</u> closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all ⓒ<u>were</u> subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, ⓓ<u>where</u> perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that ⓔ<u>exists</u> in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
questions.explanation: 주절의 동사 'would see'와 문맥상 가정법 과거 문장입니다. 'if 주어 + 과거동사, 주어 + 조동사과거 + 동사원형'의 형태를 취해야 하므로, 현재시제인 look을 과거시제인 looked로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay ⓐ<u>hidden</u> as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again ⓑ<u>that</u> they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn ⓒ<u>it</u> into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said ⓓ<u>to be</u> transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly ⓔ<u>developing</u> an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.explanation: ⓒ의 'it'은 주어인 'this one(이 문어)'과 동일한 대상을 가리킵니다. 주어와 목적어가 같을 때는 재귀대명사를 사용해야 하므로 'itself'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Onscreen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly ⓐ<u>eliminate</u> the climate-fiction genre - indeed remove any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a ⓑ<u>marginal</u> feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel ⓒ<u>isolated</u> from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may ⓓ<u>continue</u> to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is ⓔ<u>distant</u> - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 기후 변화가 너무나 뚜렷하고 일상적인 일이 되어버리면, 창문 밖으로 직접 볼 수 있는 세상을 굳이 소설(허구)로 읽을 필요가 없어지게 됩니다. 따라서 기후 변화가 지평선 전반으로 확대될수록 그것은 더 이상 '이야기(소설 소재)'가 되지 못할 것이므로 'continue(계속하다)'를 'cease(그만두다/중단되다)'나 'stop'과 같은 단어로 바꾸어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is ⓐ<u>losing</u> some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the ⓑ<u>less</u> expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model ⓒ<u>go up</u>; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than ⓓ<u>the least</u> expensive one and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy ⓔ<u>the latest</u> item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
questions.explanation: 가장 비싼 세 번째 모델(미끼 상품)을 제시함으로써 사람들이 가격과 성능의 타협점인 두 번째 모델(중간 가격 제품)을 선택하도록 유도한다는 전략에 대한 설명입니다. 따라서 소비자들이 구매하는 것은 '최신(latest)' 제품이 아니라 '중간(middle)' 가격의 제품이므로 ⓔ가 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to willingly ⓐ<u>engage</u> in the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," understanding the metaphor demands ⓑ<u>cognitive</u> effort and deeper engagement with his prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully ⓒ<u>enlarging</u> a user's understanding. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is ⓓ<u>vague</u> at first glance. Shakespeare, conversely, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately ⓔ<u>obvious</u> and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.explanation: 기술적 제작자들은 잠재적 관객이 메타포의 작동 방식을 궁금해하도록 요구할 여유가 없으며, 기술의 장점은 한눈에 그 유용성이 '명확(obvious/clear)'해야 판매가 됩니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 vague(모호한)는 문맥상 반대되는 의미입니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants. Not only were their athletic talents superior, the Cubans appeared even stronger from just the colour of their uniforms. A game would not even start and the opposing team would already be scared. A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time.
