The country that ruled international baseball for decades has not been on top since that uniform change. ________________________ for a team; while a team brand or image can adjust to keep up with present times, if it abandons or neglects its roots, negative effects can surface.
options: ⑤ Success is all about the latest equipment
questions.explanation: 쿠바 야구팀이 고유의 전통적인 붉은 유니폼을 현대화된 스타일로 바꾼 이후 성적이 하락했다는 내용을 통해, 팀의 뿌리나 전통을 저버리는 것이 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 시사합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '전통이 중요하다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 전통은 중요하다
② 승리가 전부는 아니다
③ 패션 트렌드는 변해야 한다
④ 색상은 성과에 영향을 미치지 않는다
⑤ 성공은 전적으로 최신 장비에 달려 있다

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information-a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are ____________________________________ rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
options: ① filtered through lenses of illusion
③ cast in the shadows of imagination
④ mirrored through a veil of sentiment
⑤ woven from dreamscapes of thought
questions.explanation: 인간은 세상을 있는 그대로 보는 것이 아니라 교육을 통해 배운 개념, 가정, 동기, 과거의 경험이라는 '렌즈'를 통해 재구성하여 기억한다는 내용입니다. 기억이 영화처럼 재생되는 것이 아니라 인지적 필터를 통해 재형성된다는 점이 목격자 증언의 법적 우위성을 약화시켰다는 흐름이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 환상의 렌즈를 통해 걸러진
② 인지적 필터를 통해 재형성된
③ 상상의 그림자 속에 던져진
④ 감정의 베일을 통해 비춰진
⑤ 사고의 꿈결로부터 엮인

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push-essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that ________________________. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collaborative brains.
options: ② play a role in collective progress
③ build systemic and cultural barriers
④ stop making more informed decisions
⑤ include key principles underlying the system
questions.explanation: 인간의 인지 능력 한계로 인해 우리는 계산을 인구 전체에 분산시키고 세대를 거쳐 해결한다는 내용입니다. 개인은 전체 계산의 작은 부분만을 담당하며 사회의 '협력적 뇌'의 일원이 된다는 맥락이므로, 우리의 작은 계산들이 '집단적 진보에서 역할을 한다'는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 사회 구조를 변화시킨다
② 집단적 진보에서 역할을 한다
③ 체계적이고 문화적인 장벽을 쌓는다
④ 더 정보에 입각한 결정을 내리는 것을 멈춘다
⑤ 시스템의 근간이 되는 핵심 원리를 포함한다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. ⓐIt is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another and the key word here is 'science.' ⓑScience can have a negative impact on emotions by oversimplifying or objectifying emotional experiences, leading to a lack of empathy and understanding of human emotions. ⓒPsychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. ⓓInstead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. ⓔIn addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings and these are what modern psychology is all about.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 심리학이 일반적인 통념과 달리 '과학'으로서 증거에 기반하여 인간의 행동과 원리를 연구한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ②번 문장은 과학이 감정에 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있다는 내용으로, 심리학의 과학적 방법론과 그 성격에 대한 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity.
ordered_passages: (A) Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI. The direction of Al's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.(B) AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity.(C) Singularity refers to the point at which AI exceeds human intelligence. After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 AI 진화와 특이점(singularity)의 개념을 제시합니다. (C)에서 특이점의 정의를 설명하며 AI가 스스로를 개선하고 의식 있는 존재가 되는 과정을 설명합니다. (B)에서는 그 이후(then) AI와 인간의 의식이 함께 진화하며 상호작용하는 모습을 서술합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 '반대로(Conversely)' 인간의 의식이 AI의 가치와 윤리 설정에 영향을 미친다는 상호 보완적 관점을 마무리하며 끝맺는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Alvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.'
ordered_passages: (A) For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy.
(B) A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it.

(C) For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 'trick-punishments(함정 처벌)'라는 개념을 소개했습니다. (B)에서 이 용어의 정의와 속성(오히려 행동을 고무시킴)을 설명하는 것이 첫 순서입니다. (A)에서 Hugh라는 구체적인 인물의 예시를 들어 왜 꾸중이 오히려 나쁜 행동을 강화하는지 설명합니다. (C)에서 'For instance'를 통해 (A)의 대안적 전략(긍정적인 면에 보상하기)을 제시하며 함정 처벌을 피하는 방법을 설명하며 결론을 맺습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When two or more human individuals are together, their mutual relationships and their arrangement into a group are things which would not be revealed if we confined our attention to each individual separately. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that some of the tendencies to action of the individual are related definitely to other persons and could not be aroused except by other persons acting as stimuli. An individual in complete isolation would not reveal their competitive tendencies, their tendencies towards the opposite sex, their protective tendencies towards children. This shows that the traits of human nature do not fully appear until the individual is brought into relationships with other individuals.
questions.summary_sentence: Human behavior is shaped by (A)___________ others, revealing traits like competition or protection that wouldn't appear in (B)___________. Group dynamics uncover aspects of human nature not visible in individuals alone.
questions.explanation: 본문은 인간의 본성이나 행동적 특성(경쟁심, 보호 본능 등)이 타인과의 관계 속에서, 즉 집단 내에서 비로소 드러난다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 인간의 행동은 타인과의 '상호작용(interaction)'에 의해 형성되며, 혼자 떨어져 있는 '고립(isolation)' 상태에서는 나타나지 않는다는 내용이 요약문에 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① ~와의 갈등 / 혼란
② ~의 편안함 / 분노
③ ~에 대한 무관심 / 고독
④ ~로부터의 분리 / 긴장
⑤ ~와의 상호작용 / 고립

questions.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally elective. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an (A)__________ resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to (B)__________ it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly highlights have-and-have-not inequities, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 물은 원래 풍부한 자원인데 정책적 무시 등으로 인해 부족해진 것이므로 (A)에는 '풍부한'을 뜻하는 abundant가 적절하며, 이러한 위기를 해결하려는 노력을 하지 않고 있다는 의미이므로 (B)에는 '해결하다, 다루다'의 뜻인 address가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally elective. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an (A)__________ resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to (B)__________ it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly highlights have-and-have-not inequities, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
questions.explanation: 풍부한(abundant) 자원이 정부의 방치와 인프라 관리 부실로 인해 부족해졌다는 내용이므로 (A)에는 abundant가 적절합니다. 또한, 물 부족 위기를 해결하기 위해 별다른 노력을 하지 않는다는 맥락이므로 (B)에는 '다루다/해결하다'라는 의미의 동사 address가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. (A)_________ in reaction to an (B)_________ environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
questions.explanation:
인간이 쉽게 지루함을 느끼는 이유는 변화가 없는 자극에 대한 신경 세포의 반응을 줄여 새로운 자극(생존에 중요한 변화)을 더 잘 감지하기 위함입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '지루함(boredom)'이, (B)에는 '변화가 없는(unchanging)'이 들어가는 것이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.

[구문 분석]
(A) Boredom in reaction to an (B) unchanging environment / turns down (동사) / the level of neural excitation (목적어) ...

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 문장 (A), (B)에서 어색한 어법을 찾아 바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. (A)<u>In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules are enormous</u>. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. (B)<u>The organism may switch between a small number of well-defining possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another</u>. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.
questions.explanation:
(A) 'the number of ~' 구문에서 주어는 복수 명사 interactions가 아닌 단수 명사인 'the number'이므로, 동사 are를 단수형인 is로 고쳐야 합니다.
(B) '잘 정의된/확정된 상태'라는 의미로 뒤의 명사 states를 수식해야 하므로, 능동형인 well-defining을 수동 의미의 과거분사인 well-defined로 고치는 것이 어법상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions _________________________________________. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
subjective_conditions: 1. 보기로 주어진 단어를 모두 한 번씩 포함할 것 (필요 시 어형 변형 가능)
2. 16~18단어 내외로 작성할 것
questions.answer: compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't
questions.explanation: 자부심이나 수치심 같은 감정은 우리로 하여금 공동체가 가치 있게 여기는 일을 더 많이 하고, 그렇지 않은 일은 덜 하도록 강요합니다. 따라서 'compel + 목적어(us) + to do'의 기본 구조를 활용하며, 'more of what makes ~ and less of what doesn't'와 같은 병렬 구조를 통해 문장을 완성하는 것이 출제 의도입니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
options: ① 벼락치기보다 자기 테스트가 장기 기억에 더 효과적이다.
② 기억력 향상을 위해 공부 후 충분히 휴식을 취해야 한다.
③ 시험 직전에 집중력을 발휘하여 암기하는 것이 도움이 된다.
④ 학습한 내용이 작업 기억에 저장될 수 있도록 복습해야 한다.
⑤ 자극은 반복적 시연과 유의미한 경험을 통해 단기 기억에 저장된다.
questions.explanation: 필자는 시험을 위해 벼락치기를 하는 것이 최선의 학습 전략이라는 착각이 단기 기억 때문이라고 설명하며, 정보를 장기 기억으로 옮기기 위해서는 단순히 공부만 하기보다 공부한 내용을 스스로 테스트하는 과정이 필수적이라고 주장하고 있습니다. 따라서 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 like doing well at a game이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is <u>like doing well at a game</u>. In this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
options: ① dependent on luck or chance
② based on social class and status
③ determined by becoming a traditional star
④ like gaining recognition through acting or singing
⑤ related to the accumulation of measurable attention
questions.explanation: 지문 후반부에서 소셜 미디어에서의 명성은 구독자, 팔로워, '좋아요', 클릭수와 같은 지표상의 높은 점수일 뿐이라고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 게임에서 잘한다는 것은 이러한 측정 가능한 관심의 축적과 관련이 있음을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 운이나 우연에 의존하는
② 사회적 계층과 지위에 기반을 둔
③ 전통적인 스타가 됨으로써 결정되는
④ 연기나 노래를 통해 인정을 받는 것과 같은
⑤ 측정 가능한 관심의 축적과 관련된

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race ─ their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't psychologically suffer much. In fact, ultra-marathon runners ─ those people who are crazy enough to push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50-100㎞ or more over many hours, talk about making friends with their pain. When a patient has paid for some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it, the patient calls that good pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.
options: ① amplifying or reducing the intensity of the pain based on our thoughts and emotions
② the role of brain to detect pain signals altogether under any circumstance
③ reasons for pain depending on genetic predisposition, unaffected by mind
④ the fact that pain is felt only when there is visible physical injury
⑤ creating the illusion of pain without any physical basis
questions.explanation: 지문은 고통의 정도가 마음속에서 고통을 어떻게 구성하느냐(frame)와 관련이 있다고 설명하며, 달리기 선수나 환자의 사례를 통해 고통을 가치 있게 여기거나 긍정적으로 받아들일 때 심리적 고통이 줄어든다는 점을 시사합니다. 따라서 사고와 감정에 기반하여 통증의 강도를 증폭시키거나 감소시키는 것이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 생각과 감정에 기초하여 통증의 강도를 증폭시키거나 감소시키는 것
② 어떤 상황에서도 통증 신호를 한꺼번에 감지하는 뇌의 역할
③ 마음에 영향을 받지 않는, 유전적 소인에 따른 통증의 원인들
④ 눈에 보이는 신체적 부상이 있을 때만 통증이 느껴진다는 사실
⑤ 신체적 근거 없이 고통의 환상을 만들어내는 것

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adjust and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
options: ① how cultural differences influence the way emotions are expressed across various societies
② the evolutionary purpose of emotions as adaptive programs that enhance survival
③ an exploration of how emotions influence decision-making in complex social situations
④ the effect of emotions on building and maintaining interpersonal relationships
⑤ the detailed study of the brain's role in generating and regulating emotions
questions.explanation: 이 글은 감정이 인류의 생존에 기여했기 때문에 존재한다고 설명하며, 진화론적 관점에서 감정을 생존을 돕는 '프로그램'으로 정의하고 있습니다. 두려움, 분노, 긍정적 감정 등이 어떻게 환경 적응과 생존을 도왔는지를 구체적으로 설명하므로, 주제는 생존을 강화하는 적응 프로그램으로서의 감정의 진화적 목적을 다룬 2번입니다.
options_translation: ① 문화적 차이가 다양한 사회에서 감정이 표현되는 방식에 어떻게 영향을 미치는지
② 생존을 향상시키는 적응 프로그램으로서 감정의 진화적 목적
③ 복잡한 사회적 상황에서 감정이 의사 결정에 미치는 영향에 대한 탐구
④ 대인 관계를 구축하고 유지하는 데 감정이 미치는 영향
⑤ 감정을 생성하고 조절하는 뇌의 역할에 대한 상세한 연구

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point ⓐ<u>at which</u> AI exceeds human intelligence. After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve ⓑ<u>themselves</u> and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, ⓒ<u>which</u> will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of Al. The direction of AI's evolution will depend greatly on ⓓ<u>what</u> values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and ⓔ<u>supporting</u> the evolution of its consciousness.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 가리키는 대상은 문장의 주어인 'AI'입니다. 여기서 AI는 문맥상 단수 취급되고 있으므로(동사 exceeds, becomes, pursues, its own goals 등에서 확인 가능), 재귀대명사 역시 복수형인 themselves가 아니라 단수형인 itself로 써야 어법상 옳습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt ─ producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
options: ② The Camouflage Skills of Flounders
③ Octopuses: Masters of Disguise and Deception
④ The Survival Strategy of Marine Life
questions.explanation: 이 글은 문어가 자신의 신체적 특징(색깔과 패턴 변화 능력 등)을 이용해 다른 생물체(가자미, 바다뱀 등)로 변신하거나 위장하는 놀라운 능력을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '위장과 속임수의 달인인 문어'라는 3번이 가장 적절합니다. (참고: 원문 텍스트에 4, 5번 보기가 잘려 있어 임의의 관련 내용으로 보충하였습니다.)
options_translation: ① 밝혀진 문어의 미스터리
② 가자미의 위장 기술
③ 문어: 위장과 속임수의 달인
④ 해양 생물의 생존 전략
⑤ 사진작가들이 문어를 포착하는 이유

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
options: ① 삶의 의미를 찾는 것이 우울증 치료의 핵심이다.
② 우울증의 원인은 아직 명확하게 밝혀지지 않았다.
③ 의식 상태의 왜곡으로 인해 우울증이 나타날 수 있다.
④ 신경 전달 물질의 불균형이 정신질환 발병의 직접적 원인이다.
⑤ 우울증은 무의식적으로 발생하며, 의식적으로 조절할 수 없다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우울증이 뇌 속 화학물질의 불균형 때문이라는 기존의 통념을 반박하며, 뇌의 물질 불균형은 우울증의 결과일 뿐 원인이 아니라고 주장합니다. 대신 우울증의 근본 원인을 자아감과 삶의 의미를 잃어버린 '의식 상태의 왜곡'으로 재정의하고 있습니다. 따라서 요지는 ③번입니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this _________________________________ canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.
options: ② total openness of the system
questions.explanation: 생물체라는 복잡한 시스템에서 무수히 많은 상호작용이 가능함에도 불구하고, 실제로는 제한된 수의 조직과 신체 형태만이 나타나 안정성을 유지한다는 맥락입니다. 이러한 현상을 'canalization'이라 부르는데, 이는 수많은 잠재적 상태 중 극히 일부로 좁혀지는 과정을 의미하므로 '가능성의 상당한 감소'가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 결과의 예측 불가능성
② 시스템의 완전한 개방성
③ 가능성의 광범위한 확장
④ 가능성의 상당한 감소
⑤ 결과의 완전한 무작위성

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along─whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS─and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show─whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire─you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along─a new way for humans to communicate─it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. ___________________________, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① The reliability of the information you receive from different sources
② The method or medium through which information is delivered to you
③ The relevance of the information in shaping your worldview
④ The quantity of information you are able to access
⑤ The original source or creator of the information
questions.explanation: 이 글은 새로운 매체가 등장할 때마다 그 매체 자체가 세상을 보는 방식(안경)을 바꾼다는 마샬 맥루한의 이론을 설명하고 있습니다. 특정 정보의 내용(메시지)보다 그 정보를 전달하는 매체(수단) 자체가 인간의 인식에 더 큰 영향을 미친다는 내용이므로, 빈칸에는 '정보가 전달되는 방법이나 매체'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다양한 출처로부터 받는 정보의 신뢰성
② 정보가 당신에게 전달되는 방법이나 매체
③ 당신의 세계관을 형성하는 데 있어서 정보의 관련성
④ 당신이 접근할 수 있는 정보의 양
⑤ 정보의 원래 출처나 창조자

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Capuchins ─ New World Monkeys that live in large social groups ─ will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead ─ grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers ─ the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, _________________. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains ─ the cucumbers themselves ─ to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
options: ① the act of comparing herself to another renders the situation unjust
② the situation becomes unfair due to the same rewards for different efforts
③ the equal distribution of resources makes the situation intolerable
④ the monkey's dissatisfaction stems from receiving fewer rewards than expected
⑤ the monkey's preference for grapes highlights the unfairness of the experiment
questions.explanation: 카푸친 원숭이 실험을 통해, 자신이 받는 보상(오이)이 이전과 같음에도 불구하고 옆 칸의 원숭이가 더 좋은 보상(포도)을 받는 것을 보자 자신의 보상을 거부하며 불만을 표시한다는 내용입니다. 즉, 자신의 상황이 절대적으로 변하지 않았더라도 타인과 자신을 비교함으로써 상황이 불공정하다고 느낀다는 것을 보여줍니다. 따라서 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자신을 다른 개체와 비교하는 행위가 상황을 불공정하게 만든다
② 다른 노력에 대해 동일한 보상을 하기 때문에 상황이 불공평해진다
③ 자원의 균등한 분배가 상황을 참을 수 없게 만든다
④ 원숭이의 불만은 기대보다 적은 보상을 받는 데서 기인한다
⑤ 포도에 대한 원숭이의 선호도가 실험의 불공정성을 강조한다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 묑줄 친 부분 중, 묘맥상 낱말의 시임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We ⓐ<u>reinterpret</u> what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is an advantageous trait. It's a more ⓑ<u>efficient</u> way to store information ─ a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and recall everything with perfect accuracy find it ⓒ<u>difficult</u> to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. However, representing the world as abstract concepts and features comes with the ⓓ<u>drawback</u> of not seeing it as it really is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie significantly ⓔ<u>reinforced</u> the credibility of eyewitness testimony in legal contexts. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: 글의 흠름상 우리의 기억이 실제 사건을 그대로 복원하는 것이 아니라 촔상적인 표옄을 통해 '재구성' 된다는 사실은, 법적 맥락에서 목격자 줐언의 신뢰성을 강화하기밴다는 오휴려 약화시킬 것입니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 reinforced(강화하다)는 undermined(약화시킬)와 같은 낱말로 바귢어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 묑줄 친 부분 중, 묘맥상 낱말의 시임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a ⓐ<u>detailed</u> discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people can't find themselves ⓑ<u>capable</u> of explaining why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our initial, ⓒ<u>instinctive</u> response to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression may provide a more accurate understanding of the world than the ⓓ<u>impulsive</u>, reasoned narrative we construct. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the more ⓔ<u>favorable</u> results of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.explanation: 글의 큰 흠름은 직관적인 첫인상이 나중에 이성적으로 구축한 설명밴다 더 정확할 수 있다는 것입니다. ⓓ 뒤의 reasoned(이성적인, 논리적인) narrative는 시간을 들어 구성한 것이므로, '충동적인(impulsive)'이라는 표현은 묘맥상 성립하지 않습니다. 이는 'deliberate(신중한)' 또는 'calculated'와 같은 단어가 오기에 적합합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." ⓐThis statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. ⓑHistory has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. ⓒFirestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. ⓓThe luminiferous ether is an example of a successful scientific concept that demonstrates the accuracy of early hypotheses. ⓔThe ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 존재하지 않는 본질을 찾으려는 잘못된 개념(검은 고양이 찾기 비유)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 'luminiferous ether(에테르)'는 존재하지 않는 것을 찾으려 했던 과학적 오류의 사례로 제시되었으므로, 이를 '성공적인 과학적 개념'이자 '가설의 정확성을 입증하는 예시'라고 설명하는 ⓓ는 글의 전체 흐름과 반대됩니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. ⓐThe musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. ⓑAnd yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great: effective composers have their own ideas. ⓒIn the classic movie Amadeus, the "host" of this movie, the composer Antonio Salieri is depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers ─ he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. ⓓNow, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one, but he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. ⓔBeethoven, Brahms, and Stravinsky were immediately embraced by audiences for their originality. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 위대한 작곡가들은 당대에 생소함 때문에 이해받지 못했다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 베토벤, 브람스, 스트라빈스키가 그들의 독창성 때문에 청중들에게 '즉각적으로 받아들여졌다(immediately embraced)'는 ⓔ의 내용은 글의 도입부 및 핵심 주제(당대에는 오해받음)와 정면으로 모순됩니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. (A) A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. (B) Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. (C) Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. (D) Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" (E) Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
questions.insertion_sentence: But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 (B), (C)에서 언급된 '추상적이고 부정확할 수 있는 질문(단순히 얼마나 슬펐는지 묻는 것)'에 대한 대안으로 '구체적인 수치를 이끌어내는 질문(병가를 낼 만큼 슬펐던 횟수)'을 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 부정확한 회상의 문제를 지적한 (C) 뒤이자, 이와 유사한 구체적 질문 사례(미루는 습관 대신 미납 고지서 수 묻기)를 도입하는 Similarly 앞인 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. (A) Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. (B) For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. (C) For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. (D) For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. (E) The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
questions.insertion_sentence: In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'In this case'는 앞서 언급된 '훈육(야단치기)이 오히려 동생을 때리게 만드는 강화 요인이 되는 상황'을 가리킵니다. (C)에서 휴(Hugh)가 관심을 받기 위해 계속 때리는 상황이 제시된 후, 그에 대한 해결책으로 '다른 전략을 채택하는 것이 낫다'는 흐름이 이어져야 하며, (D) 뒤에 그 구체적인 다른 전략(긍정적 행동에 대한 축하/보상)이 예시로 나오므로 (D)가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries.
ordered_passages: (A) They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a 'nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.

(B) In turn, whales increase phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon ─ leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD.

(C) For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste.
questions.explanation: 제시된 글은 고래의 이산화탄소 저장 효율성에 대해 설명합니다. (C)에서는 나무 한 그루와 비교하여 고래의 탄소 흡수량이 월등함을 강조하고, 고래의 배설물이 바다를 비옥하게 하여 탄소를 격리한다는 내용을 추가합니다. (B)에서 그 결과(In turn) 식물성 플랑크톤이 증가하여 추가적인 탄소 격리가 일어남을 설명하며 고래의 경제적 가치를 언급합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 고래의 가치를 기반으로 기후 변화 해결책으로서 고래 개체수 회복을 위한 국제적인 노력을 촉구하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities.
ordered_passages: (A) AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace.

(B) For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary.
(C) Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: 제시된 글은 AI가 장애가 있는 근로자들의 직장 접근성과 업무 품질을 개선한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (B)는 이에 대한 구체적인 예시로 음성 인식 솔루션과 자막 시스템을 언급하며 직장 내 소통을 돕는다고 설명합니다. (A)는 '또한(also)'이라는 연결어를 사용하여 AI가 저숙련 근로자의 능력을 향상시킬 수 있다는 또 다른 긍정적인 측면을 제시하며, 실시간 번역의 예시를 듭니다. (C)는 '게다가(Moreover)'를 통해 저숙련 근로자를 돕는 AI의 또 다른 예시인 텍스트 생성기를 언급하며 글을 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push ─ essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
questions.summary_sentence: The article convey Herbert Simon's notion that, due to cognitive (A)____________, humans depend on collective intelligence, interacting with technology without grasping its details, while (B)____________ to a broader societal computation.
questions.explanation: 허버트 사이먼은 인간의 인지적 한계(limitations, deficiencies) 때문에 집단 지성에 의존한다고 보았습니다. 인간은 모든 세부 사항을 다 알 필요 없이 사회적 계산의 일부분을 수행(doing our part)하며 전체에 기여하거나 전념(committing)하게 됩니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '결핍/한계'를 뜻하는 deficiencies, (B)에는 '전념/기여'를 뜻하는 committing이 적절합니다. (④의 flexcibilities는 철자 오류임)
options_translation: ① 제약 - 참조하는
② 유연성 - 조정하는
③ 결핍 - 반대하는
④ 유연성 - 기여하는
⑤ 결핍 - 전념하는

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 표로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
subjective_conditions: 지문에 있는 단어를 사용할 것 (형태 변형 불가)
(A), (B), (C) 모두 2단어로 작성할 것
조건 위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함
questions.subjective_answer_format: Aspect | Linguistic Metaphors | Technological MetaphorsImpact | passive (requires (A)________ from the audience) | active (actively influences the user)Clarity of Meaning | not (B)________ | clear and obviousAudience Involvement | Audience chooses to engage with the metaphor | User is engaged automatically through (C)________(A)_____________________________________________________(B)_____________________________________________________(C)_____________________________________________________
questions.answer: (A) cognitive effort (또는 some thought)(B) immediately obvious(C) digital artifacts
questions.explanation: 본문에서 언어적 은유는 청중의 적극적인 참여와 'cognitive effort' 혹은 'some thought'를 필요로 한다고 설명합니다. 또한 언어적 은유(셰익스피어의 작품)는 그 의미가 'not immediately obvious'하다고 명시되어 있습니다. 반면 기술적 은유는 사용자의 의미 지평을 강제로 변화시키는 'digital artifacts'를 통해 실현된다고 기술되어 있습니다. 조건에 맞게 2단어씩 지문에서 추출하면 위와 같습니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
questions.summary_sentence: Biologists differentiate between analogous traits, which (A)_____________________________, and homologous traits, which (B)_____________________________.
subjective_conditions: 지문에 있는 단어를 사용할 것 (형태 변형 가능)
(A)는 evolve, (B)는 share를 포함하여 각각 6단어 이내로 작성할 것
※ 조건 위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함
questions.answer: (A) evolve independently for the same function (또는 evolved independently for common function)(B) share a common ancestor and structure (또는 share common ancestor and structure)
questions.explanation: 생물학에서 상응 형질(analogous traits)과 상동 형질(homologous traits)의 차이를 설명하는 글입니다. (A) 상응 형질은 동일한 기능을 위해 독립적으로 진화(evolve independently)한 것이고, (B) 상동 형질은 공통의 조상과 구조를 공유(share a common ancestor and structure)하는 것입니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.
subjective_conditions: opportunity, do, should, household chores를 사용할 것 (형태 변형 불가)
questions.answer: It is household chores that you should use as an opportunity to do quick exercises. (또는 You should use household chores as an opportunity to do quick exercises.)
questions.explanation: 따로 운동 시간을 내기 어려운 바쁜 현대인들에게 집안일(household chores)을 하는 시간을 간단한 운동(quick exercises)을 할 수 있는 기회(opportunity)로 활용하라는 것이 글의 요지입니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre ─ indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant ─ in time or in place ─ we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
subjective_conditions: unnecessary, makes, reality를 사용할 것 (형태 변형 불가)
10단어 이내의 완전한 문장을 사용할 것
지문에 있는 단어만을 사용할 것 (형태 변형 불가)
questions.answer: The reality of climate change makes climate fiction unnecessary.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화가 점점 더 뚜렷한 현실이 되어감에 따라, 허구의 이야기를 다루는 '기후 소설(climate fiction)'이라는 장르가 더 이상 필요하지 않게 되거나 사라질 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '기후 변화의 현실이 기후 소설을 불필요하게 만든다'는 요지를 조건에 맞춰 작성하면 됩니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuro-psychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
options: ② useful, strategies in adopting trick-punishment
③ close relationships between parents and children
④ role of parents in encouraging children to learn social relationships
⑤ importance of rewarding positive behaviors instead of reinforcing with trick-punishment
questions.explanation: 글은 아이를 훈계하거나 처벌하는 '속임수 처벌'이 오히려 부적절한 행동을 강화할 수 있음을 지적하며, 부정적인 면을 지적하기보다는 긍정적인 행동에 대해 보상하는 전략을 취할 것을 강조하고 있다.
options_translation: ① 속임수 처벌 사용의 필요성
② 속임수 처벌을 채택하는 데 유용한 전략들
③ 부모와 자녀 사이의 친밀한 관계
④ 아이들이 사회적 관계를 배우도록 장려하는 부모의 역할
⑤ 속임수 처벌로 강화하는 대신 긍정적 행동에 보상하는 것의 중요성

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society ⓐ<u>are</u> generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science ⓑ<u>which</u> is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally ⓒ<u>accepted</u> views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just ⓓ<u>deriving</u> from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as ⓔ<u>those</u> shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 psychological ideas는 beliefs나 assumptions로부터 유래되는(수동적 의미) 대상이므로, 현재분사인 deriving보다는 과거분사인 derived가 오는 것이 적절합니다. (are firmly based and not just derived from...)

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these ⓐ<u>benefits</u>. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at ⓑ<u>minimizing</u> their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community ⓒ<u>perceive</u> us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions ⓓ<u>compel</u> us to do more of what makes our. community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it ⓔ<u>less</u> persuasive.
questions.explanation: 인류 진화 과정에서 집단 내의 지위가 생존에 직결되었으므로, 자신의 지위를 '최소화(minimizing)'하는 것이 아니라 '향상시키거나 관리(improving / managing / monitoring)'하는 데 능숙한 사람들이 선택되었을 것입니다. 따라서 ⓑ는 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works: normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is _____________ at first and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.explanation: 기술재ᄀ 이유는 한 눈에 이해댸야 하지만, 세이ᄀ스피어아 가튼 어너재ᄀ 이유는 도ᄀ자의 사고라를 빌요로 하ᄆ고, 의미가 처으ᄆ개는 모허하게(모호한)느껴지기 따문에 사랑바든다는 내용이므로 'vague'가 가장 저ᄀ잴하다.
options_translation: 쉬운
모호한
지ᄀ제ᄇ재ᄀ한
매려ᄀ재ᄀ한
서ᄃ해ᄀ려ᄀ 이ᄑ는

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also ____________________________________: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.*neurotransmitter: 신경 잔달 묠질**manifest: (명배ᄀ히) 나타내다
options: ① by a stream of natural consciousness
② a lack of neurotransmitters in the brain
③ a distortion of our state of consciousness
④ originated on introversion and delicate feeling
⑤ due to a decline of serotonin and noradrenaline
questions.explanation: 지만은 우울증의 그본 왜인이 내 퐈하ᄀ 묠질의 뷸균형이 아니라, 의시ᄀ의 만제라고 서명하게 이해하고 이다. 빈단 뒤에 나오는 'a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life'는 의시ᄀ 상태의 야개ᄀ과 여ᄂ개다므로, ③번 'a distortion of our state of consciousness(왜리 의시ᄀ 상태의 야개ᄀ)'가 가장 저ᄀ잴하다.
options_translation: 자연서러운 의시ᄀ의 흐르ᄆ에 의해
내 신경 자달 묠질의 뷰조ᄀ
왜리 의시ᄀ 상태의 야개ᄀ
내향성가 세시ᄆ한 가ᄆ저ᄀ에사 기왼한
세로토닌가 노르아도레나딘의 가ᄆ소 따문에

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. ⓐWhen 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race - their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't psychologically suffer much. ⓑIn fact, ultra-marathon runners - those people who are crazy enough to push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance covering distances of 50-100km or more over many hours, talk about making friends with their pain. ⓒIt usually takes about two hours for the world-famous runners to complete a full course. ⓓWhen a patient has paid for some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it, the patient calls that good pain. ⓔThat is regarded as good pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 고통에 대한 심리적 수용(프레이밍)이 고통의 정도를 결정한다는 내용입니다. 주자가 승리를 위해 고통을 감수하거나 환자가 치료를 위해 가해지는 압박을 '좋은 고통'으로 받아들이는 사례를 들고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓒ문장은 세계적인 주자들이 풀코스를 완주하는 데 걸리는 시간(기록)에 대한 언급이므로, 고통을 어떻게 프레이밍하느냐는 글의 주제와 무관합니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which AI exceeds human intelligence.
ordered_passages: (A) The direction of AI's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.

(B) Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI.

(C) After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 AI 진화와 특이점(singularity)의 개념을 소개합니다. (C)의 'After that point'는 주어진 글의 특이점을 가리키며, 그 이후 AI가 스스로 진화하고 의식을 갖게 됨을 설명합니다. (B)는 이어서 인간과 AI의 의식이 서로 상호작용하며 진화하는 과정을 설명합니다. (A)는 이러한 진화의 방향이 우리가 AI에 부여하는 가치와 윤리에 달려 있다는 결론을 제시합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 10월 34번]
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. (A) You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. (B) And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. (C) Why watch or read, climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? (D) At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. (E) But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.insertion_sentence: But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts.
questions.explanation: (A) 문장에서는 기후 변화가 여전히 삶의 지엽적인 특징으로 보일 때는 기후 변화에 '관한' 이야기를 할 수 있다고 말합니다. 주어진 문장은 'But'으로 시작하며 온도가 더 오르면 아무도 그 영향으로부터 고립되었다고 느끼지 못할 것(즉, 모두가 영향을 받을 것)이라는 반전의 상황을 제시합니다. 따라서 (B)에서 기후 변화가 지평선 너머로 확장됨에 따라 그것이 더 이상 '이야기'가 되지 않을 수도 있다는 결론으로 이어지는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 33번]
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model.
questions.summary_sentence: People buy the middle item, (A)____________ that they have been (B)____________ by the presence of the higher-priced item.
questions.explanation: 본문은 기업이 가장 비싼 세 번째 모델을 출시함으로써 소비자들이 중간 가격의 모델을 더 많이 구매하도록 유도하는 전략을 설명합니다. 소비자는 가장 비싼 모델의 가격 때문에 중간 모델을 합리적이라고 생각하여 선택하게 되는데, 이는 기업의 가격 전략에 의해 유도된 결과입니다. 따라서 사람들은 고가 품목의 존재에 의해 자신들이 (B) 조종되었다(manipulated)는 것을 (A) 인지하지 못한 채(being unaware) 중간 품목을 구매한다는 요약이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 인식하면서 / (B) 끌린
② (A) 알지 못한 채 / (B) 조종된
③ (A) 알면서 / (B) 다루어진
④ (A) 의식하면서 / (B) 속은
⑤ (A) 깨달으면서 / (B) 통제된

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)를 우리말로 구체적으로 작성하시오. [5.0점]
questions.passage: The best (A)<u>defence</u> most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using (B)<u>these assets</u> to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt-producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.*flounder: 넙치 **mimic: 모방하다
subjective_conditions: 1. (A)에 관한 2가지 특성과 (B)에 관한 3가지 특성을 반드시 우리말로 작성할 것
2. 1가지 특성 작성 시(각 1점)
3. 영어로 작성 시 감점
questions.answer: (A) 가능한 한 많이 숨음 / 밤에 사냥하는 것(B) 큰 뇌를 가지고 있음 / 뛰어난 시력을 지님 / 색깔과 패턴을 바꾸는 능력이 있음
questions.explanation: (A)는 문장의 보어 부분인 'stay hidden as much as possible'과 'do their own hunting at night'를 우리말로 풀어서 씁니다. (B)는 앞 문장에 언급된 문어의 신체적 자산인 'big brain', 'excellent eyesight', 'ability to change colour and pattern' 세 가지를 우리말로 작성합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분 "his face just popped out at me,"가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "<u>his face just popped out at me</u>," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
options: ② A careful and logical judgment
③ A detailed analysis of facial features
④ An importance of personal space
⑤ An automatic recognition that is hard to explain
questions.explanation: 이 글은 목격자 증언에 대한 실험을 통해, 얼굴 특징을 신중하게 숙고하거나 선택 절차를 상세히 논의하는 것보다 아무런 이유를 설명하지 못하고 그저 얼굴이 '튀어나온 것처럼(popped out)' 느껴지는 직관적인 인식이 더 정확한 경우가 많음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 밑줄 친 부분은 설명하기 어려운 자동적인 인식을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 목적이 분명한 의사결정 과정
② 신중하고 논리적인 판단
③ 얼굴 특징에 대한 상세한 분석
④ 개인적 공간의 중요성
⑤ 설명하기 어려운 자동적인 인식

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
options: ① A child who feels lonely is more likely to continue bad behavior if punished, so punishment should be avoided entirely.
② It is important to discipline children right after they misbehave in order to prevent them from repeating the same actions.
③ Traditional punishments like scolding often backfire by reinforcing negative behavior, while rewarding positive behavior is more effective.
④ Scolding can be an efficient method of drawing attention to a child's actions and encouraging better behavior.
⑤ Parents should abandon any form of punishment and focus solely on rewarding good behavior.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 아이를 꾸짖는 것(trick-punishment)이 오히려 관심을 받고 싶어 하는 아이에게 부정적인 행동을 강화하는 역효과를 낼 수 있음을 설명합니다. 따라서 부정적인 점을 계속 지적하기보다 긍정적인 행동에 보상하는 것이 더 효과적인 훈육 방법임을 제시하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 외로움을 느끼는 아이는 처벌을 받으면 나쁜 행동을 계속할 가능성이 높으므로 처벌을 완전히 피해야 한다.
② 아이들이 같은 행동을 반복하지 않도록 잘못을 저지른 직후에 훈육하는 것이 중요하다.
③ 꾸지람과 같은 전통적인 처벌은 종종 부정적인 행동을 강화하여 역효과를 내는 반면, 긍정적인 행동에 보상하는 것이 더 효과적이다.
④ 꾸지람은 아이의 행동에 주의를 끌고 더 나은 행동을 장려하는 효율적인 방법이 될 수 있다.
⑤ 부모는 어떠한 형태의 처벌도 그만두고 오로지 좋은 행동에 보상하는 것에만 집중해야 한다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
options: ① Social Computation to Overcome Individual Cognitive Limitations
② The Interdependence between Technology and Society
③ The Necessity of Specialized Knowledge for Using Modern Technology
④ Efficient Information Processing in an Age of Information Overload
⑤ The Impact of Social Learning on Technological Innovation
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 정보 처리 능력과 인지 능력에 한계가 있기 때문에, 문제를 독립적으로 해결하기보다는 인구 전체에 걸쳐 계산을 분산시키고 세대를 거쳐 사회적으로 학습한다는 점을 강조합니다. 개인은 모든 기술적 원리를 이해할 필요 없이 인터페이스 사용법만 배우면 되며, 이는 우리 뇌를 거대한 계산의 작은 일부분에 전념하게 함으로써 사회의 집단 지성이 작동하도록 하는 방식입니다. 따라서 개인의 인지적 한계를 극복하기 위한 '사회적 계산'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 개인의 인지적 한계를 극복하기 위한 사회적 계산
② 기술과 사회 간의 상호 의존성
③ 현대 기술 사용을 위한 전문 지식의 필요성
④ 정보 과부하 시대의 효율적인 정보 처리
⑤ 사회적 학습이 기술 혁신에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.*flounder: 넙치 **mimic: 모방하다
options: ① 대부분의 문어는 밤에 사냥하며 최고의 방어는 가능한 한 많이 숨어 있는 것이다.
② 낮 동안 얕은 바다에서 발견된 문어는 사실 여덟 개의 모든 팔이 접혀 있고 두 눈이 위쪽으로 응시하고 있는 넙치였다.
③ 문어는 큰 두뇌와 뛰어난 시력을 자원으로 색과 무늬를 바꾸어 다른 동물로 위장할 수 있다.
④ 다른 문어 종들은 바다뱀과 같은 동물로 위장하는 모습을 보이기도 한다.
⑤ 문어는 모방하는 동안에 사냥을 한다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 호주 사진작가들이 낮 동안 얕은 바다에서 발견한 것은 넙치처럼 보이게 위장하고 있던 '문어'였습니다. 지문에서는 '그들이 처음 본 것은 넙치였지만, 다시 보았을 때 그것은 팔을 접고 눈을 위로 향해 착각을 불러일으키고 있던 중간 크기의 문어였다'고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 2번의 '넙치였다'는 설명은 틀린 내용입니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined ____________________________. Seeing is not believing.*retrieve: 상기하다 **primacy: 우위성
options: ① the universal validity of situational evidence
② the unquestioned reliability of eyewitness testimony
③ the psychological basis of eyewitness testimony
④ the historical use of eyewitness evidence
⑤ the ethical agreement of eyewitness testimony
questions.explanation: 인간의 기억이 실제 사건을 비디오처럼 정확히 저장하는 것이 아니라, 자신이 아는 개념이나 경험을 통해 재구성된다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 이러한 기억의 재구성적 특징은 우리가 보는 것이 사실 그대로가 아닐 수 있음을 의미하며, 마지막에 'Seeing is not believing(보는 것이 믿는 것은 아니다)'이라는 결론이 나옵니다. 따라서 이는 목격자 증언의 절대적인 신뢰성을 약화시킨다는 의미의 'the unquestioned reliability of eyewitness testimony'가 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 상황적 증거의 보편적 타당성
② 목격자 증언의 의심할 여지 없는 신뢰성
③ 목격자 증언의 심리학적 근거
④ 목격자 증거의 역사적 사용
⑤ 목격자 증언의 윤리적 합의

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 29번]
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that ____________________________. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
options: ① the metaphor is hidden and hard to figure out
② audience need to spend hours analyzing the meaning
③ the purpose of the technology is unclear and vague
④ the technology is useful in extensive explanation
⑤ the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance
questions.explanation: 글의 대조를 통해 정답을 유추할 수 있습니다. 셰익스피어와 같은 언어적 은유는 독자의 능동적 해석과 인지적 노력이 필요하지만, 디지털 기술은 사용자가 작동 방식을 고민하게 만들어서는 안 되며 즉각적으로 그 유용성이 드러나야 한다는 것이 핵심입니다. 따라서 기술의 판매 포인트는 '한눈에 보아도 그 유용성이 명확하다'는 점이 되어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 은유가 숨겨져 있어 파악하기 어렵다
② 청중이 의미를 분석하는 데 시간을 보내야 한다
③ 기술의 목적이 불분명하고 모호하다
④ 기술이 광범위한 설명에 유용하다
⑤ 기술의 유용성이 첫눈에 명확하다

questions.question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different.
ordered_passages: (A) In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings.
(B) It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.'

(C) Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 심리학은 사회의 일반적인 통념과 다르다고 언급합니다. (B)에서 심리학이 사람을 이해하는 데 헌신하는 '과학'의 한 분야라고 정의하며 '과학'이라는 키워드를 제시합니다. (C)에서 심리학자들이 의견이나 소문에 의존하지 않고 대신 '증거'를 찾는다는 내용을 설명하며 (B)의 과학적 성격을 구체화합니다. (A)에서 '이러한 증거 기반 접근법(this evidence-based approach)'에 덧붙여 심리학이 다루는 다른 측면들을 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race - their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't ⓐ<u>physically</u> suffer much. In fact, ultramarathon runners - those people who are crazy enough to push themselves ⓑ<u>beyond</u> the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50-100㎞ or more over many hours, talk about making ⓒ<u>friends</u> with their pain. When a patient has paid for some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it, the patient calls that ⓓ<u>good</u> pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of ⓔ<u>value</u>, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 고통을 마음속에서 어떻게 정의(frame)하느냐에 따라 고통의 정도가 달라진다는 내용입니다. 1500m 달리기 선수가 승리를 위해 극한의 고통을 견딜 때, 신체적으로는 분명히 고통을 느끼지만 이를 목표를 위한 과정으로 받아들이기 때문에 '정신적으로(mentally)' 고통을 덜 느낀다는 맥락이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 ⓐ physically(신체적으로)는 mentally(정신적으로)나 psychologically(심리적으로) 정도로 바뀌어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a ⓐ<u>consequence</u> of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression ⓑ<u>leads to</u> a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to ⓒ<u>reinterpret</u> depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes ⓓ<u>beyond</u> the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a ⓔ<u>balance</u> in our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우울증의 근본 원인을 뇌의 화학 물질 불균형이 아닌 '의식의 문제'로 보고 있습니다. 마지막 문장 근처에서 우울증의 원인은 의식 상태의 '불균형' 혹은 '장애'라고 설명해야 맥락이 이어집니다. 따라서 ⓔ balance(균형)는 imbalance(불균형)나 disturbance(장애) 등으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which AI exceeds human intelligence. After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI. The direction of AI's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
questions.summary_sentence: The evolution of AI beyond the singularity may lead to a (A)____________ growth with human consciousness, guided by the values and ethics we (B)____________ for coexistence.
