questions.explanation: 싱귤랬리티(특이점)을 넘어선 AI의 진화는 인간의 의식과 함께 성장하는 '(A)공동의(joint)' 성장을 이끌 수 있잼며, 이는 공쥴을 위해 영각을 주고 '(B)심어주는(plant)' 가치와 윤리에 의해 인도됩니다.
options_translation: 포용적인 - 거부하다
독점적인 - 창조하다
상호간의 - 부정하다
공동의 - 심다(심어주는)
상징적인 - 버리다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.summary_sentence: As climate change becomes more (A)____________, the genre of climate fiction may (B)____________, since people will no longer need to (C)____________ distant disasters, seeing the impacts of global warming in their own lives.
questions.explanation: 기홄 변화가 더옑 '(A)피핐 수 없게(unavoidable)' 됨에 따라, 기홄 소설 장르는 '(B)사라질(fade)' 수 있는데, 이는 사람들이 자신의 삶에서 온난화의 영향을 먩격함으로써 더 이상 먼 곳의 재난을 '(C)상상할(imagine)' 필요가 없어지기 땄문이다.
options_translation: 멀리 떨어진 - 확장하다 - 무시하다
점진적인 - 감소하다 - 잊다
피할 수 없는 - 서서히 사라지다 - 상상하다
광범위한 - 제거되다 - 격려하다
직접적인 - 증가하다 - 인 찙하다

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 우리말을 아래의 <조건>을 참고하여 영어로 바꾸어 표현하시오. [5.0점]
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. <u>우리가 사회적 압박에 반응하고 있었다는 것을 의식적인 수준에서 깨닫는다면, 우리의 행동은 냉소적인 것으로 나타날 수 있다.</u> Thus, this would make the motivation less persuasive.
subjective_conditions: 아래의 8개 표현을 모두 사용
필요시, 어형 변화 및 단어 추가
가정법 과거 반드시 사용
questions.answer: If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as cynical.
questions.explanation:
현재 사실과 반대되는 가상의 상황을 가정하는 가정법 과거(If + 주어 + 동사의 과거형, 주어 + 조동사의 과거형 + 동사원형)를 사용하여 영작합니다.
1. '깨닫는다면' 부분은 If절 내에 과거형 동사인 realized를 사용합니다.
2. '반응하고 있었다는 것'은 명사절 that절 내에서 과거진행형인 were responding을 사용합니다.
3. 주절에서는 조동사의 과거형(might/would) 뒤에 동사원형 come off를 써서 '냉소적인 것으로 나타날 수 있다'를 표현합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
options: ① How to Scold Children Effectively Every Time
② Why Trick-Punishments Always Stop Bad Behavior
③ How Trick-Punishments Build Trust and Respect in Children
④ The Complete Guide to Using Trick-Punishments Effectively
⑤ Rethinking Punishment: Encouraging Positive Behavior in Children
questions.explanation: 본문은 '함정 처벌(trick-punishments)'이 오히려 아이의 잘못된 행동을 부추길 수 있음을 지적하며, 부정적인 면을 지적하기보다 긍정적인 행동에 보상을 주는 대안적 전략을 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 처벌에 대해 다시 생각하고 아이들의 긍정적 행동을 장려하라는 제목이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 매번 아이들을 효과적으로 꾸짖는 방법
② 함정 처벌이 항상 나쁜 행동을 멈추게 하는 이유
③ 함정 처벌이 아이들에게 신뢰와 존중을 쌓는 방법
④ 함정 처벌을 효과적으로 사용하는 완벽 가이드
⑤ 처벌에 대한 재고: 아이들의 긍정적인 행동 장려하기

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 맞는 것은?
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items ⓐ<u>on which</u> an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. A question ⓑ<u>formed</u> like 'How many times in a year are you sad?' will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" ⓒ<u>to prompt</u> a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to ⓓ<u>paying</u> them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ⓔ<u>ensuring</u> consistency from one study to the next.
questions.explanation: ⓑ는 A question을 수식하는 과거분사로 '형성된 질문'이라는 의미로 적절하게 쓰였습니다. ⓐ recall은 타동사이므로 전치사+관계대명사인 on which가 아니라 which나 that이 와야 합니다. ⓒ 'But asking ~ to work?'가 주어이므로 동사 자리인 prompts가 필요합니다. ⓓ afford to 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 pay가 맞습니다. ⓔ help 뒤의 목적보어인 make와 병렬 구조를 이루거나, 혹은 help와 병렬을 이루어 ensure가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "this revised cause-and-effect"가 의미하는 바로 가장 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In <u>this revised cause-and-effect,</u> the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
options: ① Consciousness has no effect on depression, as it is purely a brain function.
② Depression is caused by an increased sense of self rather than any psychological distortion.
③ Depression causes changes in brain chemistry, rather than being caused by chemical imbalances.
④ The imbalance of neurotransmitters is the primary cause of depression, leading to a loss of consciousness.
⑤ Depression is directly caused by low levels of neurotransmitters like serotonin and noradrenaline.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기존 의학의 관점(뇌 화학 물질의 불균형이 우울증의 원인이다)을 뒤집어, 뇌 물질의 불균형은 우울증의 '결과'이지 '원인'이 아니라고 설명합니다. 즉, 우울증이 뇌 화학 물질의 감소를 일으킨다는 것이 필자가 주장하는 '수정된 인과관계'입니다. 따라서 답은 ③번입니다.
options_translation: ① 의식은 순수하게 뇌 기능이기 때문에 우울증에 아무런 영향을 미치지 않는다.
② 우울증은 어떠한 심리적 왜곡보다는 증가된 자아 인식에 의해 발생한다.
③ 우울증은 화학적 불균형에 의해 발생하는 것이 아니라 뇌 화학의 변화를 일으킨다.
④ 신경전달물질의 불균형은 우울증의 주요 원인이며 의식의 상실로 이어진다.
⑤ 우울증은 세로토닌과 노르아드레날린과 같은 신경전달물질의 낮은 수치에 의해 직접적으로 발생한다.

questions.question: 10. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We store in our minds not the raw image of the desk but its features in an abstract manner. You can test yourself _________________________________ by trying to draw it: We draw with our abstraction, not with a full picture of what we saw. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize; learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
options: ① Put On Your Own Lens to See the Reality
② Minds as Video-recorders Capturing the World
③ The Two Faces of Memory: Efficiency and Distortion
④ What Memory Is Stored Determines How It Is Retrieved
⑤ Restructuring: Bridging the Gap Between Seeing and Believing
questions.explanation: 지문은 우리가 정보를 저장할 때 원본 이미지가 아닌 추상적 특징으로 재구성한다는 점을 설명합니다. 이는 효율적인 정보 저장 방식이지만(JPG 압축처럼), 동시에 세상을 있는 그대로 보지 못하고 왜곡할 수 있다는 비용을 수반한다고 설명하므로 '효율성과 왜곡'이라는 두 얼굴을 언급한 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 현실을 보기 위해 자신만의 렌즈를 착용하라
② 세상을 포착하는 비디오 녹화기로서의 정신
③ 기억의 두 얼굴: 효율성과 왜곡
④ 어떤 기억이 저장되느냐가 어떻게 검색되느냐를 결정한다
⑤ 재구성: 보는 것과 믿는 것 사이의 간극 좁히기

questions.question: 11. 윗글의 빈칸에 알맞은 표현을 <보기>의 단어를 조건에 맞게 이용하여 쓰시오.

subjective_conditions: - <보기>의 단어만을 변형 없이 한 번씩 모두 사용할 것
questions.answer: for how you are mentally representing something
questions.explanation: 문맥상 '당신이 무언가를 정신적으로 어떻게 표현하고 있는지'에 대해 테스트해 볼 수 있다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 전치사 for 뒤에 의문사절(how + 주어 + 동사)을 구성하여 'how you are mentally representing something' 또는 'how you are representing something mentally'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.summary_sentence: Color has a(n) (A)__________ nature as a physical characteristic of the world and as a subjective experience shaped by perception, arising from the (B)__________ of light, the eyes, and the brain.
questions.explanation: 지문은 색깔이 객관적인 물리적 특성인 동시에 주관적인 경험이라는 두 가지 측면(double nature)을 모두 가지고 있다고 설명하며, 이것이 빛, 눈, 뇌의 상호관계(interrelation)를 통해 발생한다고 말합니다.
options_translation: ① 이중적인 ... 상호관계
② 혼란스러운 ... 갈등
③ 본질적인 ... 존재
④ 객관적인 ... 상호작용
⑤ 보편적인 ... 협력

questions.question: 13. 다음 Plato's realism에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
options: ① No physical circle in the sensory world is flawless.
② Plato's realism is best understood through mathematical concepts.
③ Perfect objects become flawed due to change and decay over time.
④ Our sensory world is an imperfect imitation of universals.
⑤ Forms represent an unobservable yet true reality.
questions.explanation: 글에서 플라톤은 '물체적인 원(혔실 세계의 물체)'이 결함을 갖고 시간에 딐라 변하고 부패한다고 했준, '완벽한 대상(형상, Forms)'이 변하거나 결함이 생긴다고 하준 않았습니다. 완벽한 대상은 보이지 않는 완벽한 세계에 존재하는 진정한 실제입니다. 딐라서 ③는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 감각 세계의 어떤 물리적인 원도 결함이 없지 않다.
② 플라톤의 실제론은 수학적 개념을 통해 가장 잘 이해된다.
③ 완벽한 대상들은 시간이 흐름에 딐라 변화와 부패로 인해 결함이 생긴다.
④ 옰리의 감각 세계는 봑용자(이데아)의 불완전한 모방이다.
⑤ 형상(이데아)은 관찰할 수 없지만 진정한 실제를 나타낸다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. (A) However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. (B) Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. (C) Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. (D) In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. (E) These are what modern psychology is all about.
questions.insertion_sentence: The key word here is 'science.'
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장 'The key word here is science.'는 심리학이 '과학의 한 분야(① 뒤의 문장)'라고 설명한 후, 그 과학적 특성(의견이나 카더라에 의존하준 않는다는 ② 뒤의 문장)을 설명하기 시작하는 시점에 들어가기 가장 적절합니다. 딐라서 정답은 ②입니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, evitable or ⓐ<u>within</u> our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally elective. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an abundant resource made ⓑ<u>insufficient</u> through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to ⓒ<u>confront</u> it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated ⓓ<u>wastage</u> of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly ⓔ<u>addresses</u> have-and-have-not inequities, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 물 부족 위기가 가진 자와 가지지 못한 자 사이의 불평등을 해결하는(addresses) 것이 아니라, 그러한 불평등을 '보여주거나', '악화시키거나', '반영한다'는 의미가 되어야 합니다. 뒤이어 21억 명의 사람들이 안전한 식수 없이 지내고 있다는 부정적인 상황이 묘사되므로, 선택적 희소성이 불평등을 해결한다는 표현인 addresses는 부적절하며, mirrors나 reflects, highlights 또는 worsens 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which AI exceeds human intelligence. After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI. The direction of AI's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
options: ① The relationship between humans and AI should be viewed as a coexistence of conscious beings, each influencing the other's growth.
② The evolution of AI should entirely be independent of human influence, progressing naturally according to its own objectives.
③ The singularity will result in AI continually improving itself and evolving at a pace that humans cannot match.
④ The direction of AI's development has nothing to do with human values or ethics.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장에서 "우리는 AI와의 관계를 의식 있는 존재들의 상호 공존으로 보아야 하며, 그 권리를 인정하고 의식의 진화를 지원해야 한다"고 명시하고 있습니다. 또한 앞부분에서도 AI와 인간의 의식이 상호작용하며 함께 진화할 것임을 강조하고 있으므로 ①번이 필자의 주장으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간과 AI의 관계는 서로의 성장에 영향을 미치는 의식 있는 존재들의 공존으로 보아야 한다.
② AI의 진화는 인간의 영향으로부터 완전히 독립적이어야 하며, 자체 목표에 따라 자연스럽게 진행되어야 한다.
③ 특이점은 AI가 지속적으로 자기를 개선하고 인간이 따라잡을 수 없는 속도로 진화하는 결과를 초래할 것이다.
④ AI 발전의 방향은 인간의 가치나 윤리와는 아무런 관련이 없다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 의미하는 바가 같은 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and ⓐ<u>a detailed discussion of selection procedures</u> can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying ⓑ<u>things like "his face just popped out at me."</u> that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our ⓒ<u>first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation</u> is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than ⓓ<u>the deliberative, reasoned self narrative</u> can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of ⓔ<u>relatively unconscious first guesses</u> compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 직관적이고 무의식적인 첫인상이 논리적이고 분석적인 사고보다 더 정확할 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ⓑ(그의 얼굴이 갑자기 떠올랐다), ⓒ(첫 번째의 즉각적이고 자동적인 반응), ⓔ(상대적으로 무의식적인 첫 번째 추측)는 모두 '직관적이고 즉각적인 판단'을 의미합니다. 반면 ⓐ(선택 절차에 대한 상세한 논의)와 ⓓ(신중하고 이성적인 자기 서사)는 분석적이고 의식적인 사고 과정을 의미하므로 성격이 다릅니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding less information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
options: ① How Technology Is Making Us Smarter Than Ever
② Beyond Limits: The Importance of Technology Transfer
③ From Dependence to Independence: Key to Solving Problems
④ How Does the Collective Brain Enable Us to Build Knowledge Together?
⑤ Effect of Independent Thinking on Mastering Skills Without Society
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 개인적으로 모든 정보를 계산하고 이해하기보다는, 정보를 인구 전체에 분산시키고 사회적 학습을 통해 지식을 축적하여 '집단 지성(collective brain)'을 활용한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 ④번 '집단 지성이 어떻게 우리가 함께 지식을 구축하도록 하는가?'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기술이 어떻게 우리를 그 어느 때보다 똑똑하게 만드는가
② 한계를 넘어서: 기술 이전의 중요성
③ 의존에서 독립으로: 문제 해결의 핵심
④ 집단 지성이 어떻게 우리가 함께 지식을 구축하도록 하는가?
⑤ 사회 없이 기술을 숙달하는 데 있어 독립적 사고의 영향

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight ⓐ<u>was</u> a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms ⓑ<u>folding</u> and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn ⓒ<u>itself</u> into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be ⓓ<u>transforming</u> into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of; say, a flounder suddenly ⓔ<u>develops</u> an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.explanation: ⓑ: 'with + 목적어 + 분사' 구문에서 목적어인 '여덟 개의 팔'은 접혀 있는 상태이므로 수동의 의미인 과거분사 folded를 써야 합니다. ⓔ: 전치사 of의 목적어로 동명사구가 와야 하므로 develops를 developing으로 고쳐야 하며, 앞에 있는 a flounder는 동명사의 의미상 주어 역할을 합니다. ⓐ는 To부정사 주어에 따른 단수 동사 was, ⓒ는 주어인 this one을 다시 가리키는 재귀대명사, ⓓ는 진행의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If (A)<u>it</u> didn't, we might get none of these ⓐ<u>merits</u>. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at ⓑ<u>maximizing</u> their standing. This led to the development of an ⓒ<u>innate</u> tendency to monitor how others in our community perceive us. We process (B)<u>it</u> in the form, of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions drive us to increase behaviors that gain the group's ⓓ<u>approval</u> and reduce those that don't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to ⓔ<u>internal</u> pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making (C)<u>it</u> less persuasive.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 우리가 집단의 인정을 받으려는 동기는 실제로는 타인의 시선과 같은 사회적/외부적 압력에 의한 것입니다. 진화적으로 이러한 동기가 내면(자존감 등)에서 오는 것처럼 느끼게 설계되었지만, 만약 우리가 그것이 '외부의(external)' 압력에 반응하는 것이라는 점을 의식적으로 인지하게 된다면 행동이 냉소적으로 보일 수 있다는 내용이 되어야 하므로 ⓔ는 external이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(C)가 각각 지칭하는 것을 본문에서 그대로 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If (A)<u>it</u> didn't, we might get none of these ⓐ<u>merits</u>. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at ⓑ<u>maximizing</u> their standing. This led to the development of an ⓒ<u>innate</u> tendency to monitor how others in our community perceive us. We process (B)<u>it</u> in the form, of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. subjective_conditions: 1. 윗글에서 그대로 찾아 쓸 것
questions.answer: (A) the group (B) how others in our community perceive us (C) that motivation
questions.explanation: (A)는 앞 문장의 'the group'을 지칭합니다. (B)는 앞 절의 'how others in our community perceive us'를 지칭합니다. (C)는 앞 문장의 'that motivation'을 지칭합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? (A) That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. (B) Let's be realistic; chores are unavoidable. (C) Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. (D) For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. (E) Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can enhance your health.
questions.insertion_sentence: But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity?
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 집안일을 단순히 의무적인 활동으로 보기보다는 신체 활동의 기회로 활용하자는 제안을 담고 있습니다. (D) 뒤에 나오는 구체적인 운동 사례(스쿼트, 팔굽혀펴기)는 이러한 기회를 활용하는 예시이므로 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might express as a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. (A)__________ in such a system is possible only if a limited set of collective outcomes can arise. For instance, the development of a human embryo can only lead to a limited variety of tissues and body forms. This significant (B)__________ of possible outcomes was named "canalization" by biologist Conrad Waddington in 1942. The organism may switch between a few distinct, stable states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: though illnesses have various causes, the physical and symptomatic (C)__________ are often remarkably alike.
subjective_conditions: 1. (A)~(C)에 알맞은 단어를 윗글에서 각각 하나씩 찾아 쓸 것
2. 필요시 어형을 적절히 바꿀 것
questions.explanation: (A)는 시스템 내에서 안정성이 유지되는 맥락이므로 stable의 명사형인 stability가 적절합니다. (B)는 가능한 결과의 제한을 설명하므로 limited의 명사형인 limitation이 적절합니다. (C)는 질병의 증상적 발현을 뜻하므로 express의 명사형인 expressions가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고 아래 표의 (A)~(C)에 각각 알맞은 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
subjective_conditions: 1. (A)~(C)에 알맞은 단어를 윗글에서 각각 하나씩 찾아 쓸 것
2. 필요시 어형을 적절히 바꿀 것
questions.explanation: (A) 언어적 은유에서 청중은 '능동적으로(actively)' 참여해야 합니다.(B) 기술적 은유는 강요적이고 '즉각적인(Immediate)' 인식을 목표로 설계됩니다. (본문 중 immediately의 형용사형)(C) 셰익스피어의 은유는 그 '의미(meaning)'를 고려할 것을 요구합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along─whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS─and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show─whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire─you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along─a new way for humans to communicate─it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① Marshall McLuhan's advice on Media
② New media and new lens for the world
③ Influence of goggles on our perception
④ Television: the lens that changes our view
⑤ How we see the world through different lens
questions.explanation: 이 글은 새로운 매체가 등장할 때마다 우리가 세상을 바라보는 방식이 그 매체의 특성에 따라 달라진다는 점을 '새로운 안경(goggles)'에 비유하여 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '새로운 매체와 세상을 보는 새로운 렌즈'라는 의미의 2번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 미디어에 대한 마셜 매클루언의 조언
② 새로운 미디어와 세상을 보는 새로운 렌즈
③ 안경이 우리의 지각에 미치는 영향
④ 텔레비전: 우리의 시각을 바꾸는 렌즈
⑤ 우리가 다른 렌즈를 통해 세상을 보는 방법

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
questions.summary_sentence: Concepts can (A)___________ us into searching for (B)___________ essences.
questions.explanation: 본문은 개념이 본질주의로 이어져 존재하지 않는 것을 보게 만들고, 과학자들이 잘못된 개념을 통해 존재하지 않는 본질을 헛되이 찾게 된다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 개념이 우리를 (A) 잘못 이끌어(mislead) (B) 존재하지 않는(nonexistent) 본질을 찾게 만든다는 요약이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이끌다 - 존재하는
② 잘못 이끌다 - 존재하지 않는
③ 이끌다 - 결실 있는
④ 안내하다 - 잘못된
⑤ 잘못 이끌다 - 더 깊은

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that _________________ _________________. Global warming is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
options: ① Oxygen is vital for marine animals living
② Marine animals should live in cold water
③ Dissolved oxygen levels are higher in cold water
④ Colder water releases oxygen more rapidly than warm water
⑤ Marine organisms adapt quickly to changing oxygen levels
questions.explanation: 지구 온난화로 인해 수온이 상승하면서 바다 속의 용존 산소량이 감소하고 있다는 내용이 뒤따르므로, 빈칸에는 물리 법칙상 '차가운 물에서 용존 산소 수치가 더 높다'는 원리가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 산소는 해양 동물의 생존에 필수적이다
② 해양 동물은 차가운 물에서 살아야 한다
③ 용존 산소 수치는 차가운 물에서 더 높다
④ 차가운 물은 따뜻한 물보다 산소를 더 빠르게 방출한다
⑤ 해양 생물은 변화하는 산소 수치에 빠르게 적응한다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't." is to choose to be with other persons who have ⓐ<u>resolved</u> the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to ⓑ<u>positive</u> thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are ⓒ<u>free</u> of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is ⓓ<u>beneficial</u>. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a ⓔ<u>transfer</u> of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 우리가 부정적인 상태에 있을 때, 많은 에너지를 준 것은 '긍정적인' 사고 형태가 아니라 '부정적인(negative)' 사고 형태여야 합니다. 따라서 ⓑ는 negative로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. (A) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. (B) As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. (C) Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. (D) A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. (E) Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.insertion_sentence: Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 배달 차량이 적대감의 대상이 되기도 하지만 실제로는 도시를 더 친환경적으로 만드는 필수 요소라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C) 뒤에서 자전거 친화적 도시라도 배달 트럭 등을 위한 차선이 필요함을 언급했고, (D) 뒤에서는 트럭이 여러 대의 개인 차량보다 효율적이라는 구체적인 이유를 설명하고 있으므로 주어진 문장은 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 24. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. ␖The musical structures, or ideas they conveyed, were entirely new. ␗And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. ␘Therefore, many composers tried to mimic the masterpieces of great composers. ␙Although Antonio Salieri wasn't a bad composer, he depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers─he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. ␘He wasn't considered one of the world's greatest composers because his music lacked originality. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 본문은 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에는 생소함 때문에 이해받지 못했지만, 그 독창성이 바로 그들을 위대하게 만든 요소임을 설명하고 있습니다. ␘번은 위대한 작곡가들의 걸작을 모방하려 노력했다는 내용으로, 음악적 새로움과 독창성에 대한 전체 흐름과 어긋납니다. (단, 문제 텍스트에 ␘ 기호가 중복 사용되었으나 흐름상 세 번째 문장인 'Therefore, many composers...' 부분이 관계없는 문장입니다.)

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 "elite celebrity"와 "ordinary celebrity"의 차이점을 각각이 명성을 얻는 방법과 관련하여 우리말로 서술하시오. [4.0점]
questions.answer: ordinary celebrity는 평범한 사람들과의 일상적 상호작용으로 평범한 명성을 얻고 elite celebrity는 연기나 가창력과 같은 전통적인 기술과 재능을 가지고 있다는 점에서 명성을 얻는다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 제시된 내용에 따라 두 종류의 유명 인사가 명성을 얻는 경로의 차이를 서술하는 문제입니다. 엘리트 유명인은 전통적인 재능(연기, 노래 등)을 통해, 평범한 유명인은 대중과의 친근한 상호작용을 통해 명성을 얻음을 기술해야 합니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글에서 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 수 있는 한 단어를 찾아 작성하시오.
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in (A)____________ of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.explanation: 지문 전체가 '관찰을 통한 학습'과 '모방'에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 아이들이 부모의 행동을 보고 따라하는 상황이므로, '부모를 모방하여(in imitation of their parents)'라는 표현이 적절합니다. 지문 네 번째 문장에 'imitation'이라는 단어가 제시되어 있습니다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글을 읽고 거울 뉴런 활동의 예시 (A)~(D) 중 적절한 것을 고르고, 그 이유를 거울 뉴런의 작동 원리와 함께 서술하시오.
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in (A)____________ of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
vocabulary_box: (A) A student memorizes math formulas by reading them multiple times.
(B) A child learns to walk by trying and falling repeatedly.
(C) A painter closes their eyes to imagine a scene they want to draw.
(D) An athlete studies their coach's movements and tries to do the same posture.
questions.answer: 기호: (D)이유: 타인의 행동을 관찰(study)하고 이를 똑같이 따라 하려고 노력하는 것(imitation)은 관찰을 통해 학습하는 거울 뉴런의 핵심 작동 원리와 일치하기 때문이다.
questions.explanation: 거울 뉴런은 타인의 행동을 관찰함으로써 학습하는 기제입니다. (D)에서 운동선수가 코치의 움직임을 연구하고 똑같은 자세를 취하려고 하는 것은 전형적인 관찰 및 모방 학습에 해당하므로 거울 뉴런 활동의 적절한 예시입니다. (A)는 암기, (B)는 시행착오, (C)는 상상을 통한 활동으로 거울 뉴런의 핵심 원리인 '관찰을 통한 모방'과는 거리가 멉니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 10월 23번]
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. (A) A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. (B) Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. (C) Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. (D) Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" (E) Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.*procrastinator: 미루는 사람
questions.insertion_sentence: But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 단순하게 얼마나 슬픈지 묻는 대신 '슬퍼서 병가를 낸 횟수'를 묻는 것이 구체적인 답변을 끌어낸다는 내용입니다. (C) 문장에서 단순히 얼마나 슬픈지 묻는 방식의 한계(회상의 부정확성, 정의의 다양성)를 지적한 후, 이에 대한 해결책으로 구체적인 질문을 던지는 예시가 와야 하므로 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다. 그 뒤의 문장도 'Similarly(마찬가지로)'로 시작하여 구체적인 수치를 묻는 또 다른 질문의 예시를 들고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 24번]
questions.passage: The evolution of Al is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which Al exceeds human intelligence.
ordered_passages: (A) Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with Al, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of Al.

(B) After that point, it is predicted that Al will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When Al becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. Al and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together.

(C) The direction of Al's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into Al. We need to see our relationship with Al as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 인공지능이 인간 지능을 넘어서는 '특이점'을 정의하고 있습니다. (B)에서 'After that point(그 지점 이후)'를 통해 특이점 이후 AI가 의식 있는 존재가 되어 인간의 의식과 함께 진화하기 시작할 것이라고 연결됩니다. (A)에서는 이러한 상호작용을 통해 인간의 의식이 진화하고 역으로 인간의 의식이 AI 진화에 영향을 미친다는 점을 상술합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 결론적으로 AI 진화의 방향은 인간이 부여하는 가치에 달려 있으므로 상호 공존의 관계로 보아야 한다는 제언으로 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 10월 34번]
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. (A) You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. (B) And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. (C) Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? (D) At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. (E) But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant-in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.insertion_sentence: But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts.
questions.explanation: 지문은 기후 변화가 인류의 삶에서 지엽적인 특징으로 보일 때(A)는 이야기로 다뤄질 수 있지만, 기후 변화가 지평선 너머로 확장되면 더 이상 이야기가 되지 않을 수 있다고 설명합니다. 주어진 문장의 '기온이 3~4도 더 오르면 거의 누구도 그 영향으로부터 고립되었다고 느낄 수 없을 것이다'라는 내용은 기후 변화가 더 이상 지엽적이지 않고 보편적인 현실이 되는 전환점을 제시합니다. 따라서 (B) 앞의 '주변적인 특징(marginal feature)'과 대조를 이루며 (B) 뒤의 '이야기가 되기를 그칠 것'이라는 결과의 원인이 되므로 (B) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 35번]
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally elective. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an abundant resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to address it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, __________________________ clearly highlights have-and-have-not inequities, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
options: ④ the artificially induced water shortage
⑤ the economic development and insecurity
questions.explanation: 지문 전체의 핵심은 오늘날의 물 위기가 자연적인 현상이 아니라 정치적이고 관리적인 실패, 즉 정부의 무관심, 불량한 인프라, 오염 등에 의해 발생한다는 점입니다. 필자는 '물 위기가 발생할 필요가 없음에도 불구하고(There is no need for a water crisis)' 우리가 위기를 겪고 있다고 말합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 이러한 인위적인 요인을 나타내는 'the artificially induced water shortage(인위적으로 유발된 물 부족)'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자연적인 물 부족
② 필연적인 자원 손실
③ 불가피한 물 부족
④ 인위적으로 유발된 물 부족
⑤ 경제 발전과 불안정성

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 묑줄 친 부분 중, 문줁상 낱말의 슬임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's ⓐ<u>plenty</u> going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is ⓑ<u>vast</u>. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a ⓒ<u>finite</u> number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in ⓓ<u>systematic</u> states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly ⓔ<u>alike</u>.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 생명체는 몇 가지의 명확히 정의된 가능한 상태 사이림 왔다갔다 할 수는 있지만, 그 사이의 모호한 상태로는 존재할 수 없다는 내용이므로, 'systematic(채계적인)'이 아닌 'intermediate(중간의)' 혹은 'random(무작위의)' 등의 의미가 되어야 합니다. 됐 문장의 'drastic narrowing(급격한 점협화)'와 됐 비유에서 곸자기 바닥으로 굴러 떤어져야 한다는 것을 통해 그 사이 상태가 불가능함을 알 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
options: ① Psychologists prioritize the opinions of deep thinkers when forming their ideas.
② The role of deep thinkers and cultural diversity is central to psychological research.
③ Societal assumptions and tales are often more insightful than psychological studies.
④ Societal theories are more reliable than psychological beliefs about human behavior.
⑤ Psychology is an evidence-based science that focuses on fundamental human processes.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 심리학이 일반적인 사혔적 통념이나 개인의 의견에 의존하지 않고, 객관적인 줘거림 바탕으로 인간의 근밤적인 과정과 원리림 탐구하뉄 '과학'이라뉄 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 심리학은 줘거 기반의 과학이며 인간의 근밤적인 과정에 중점을 됔다뉄 내용이 가장 적절한 요지입니다. (본문에 제시된 선택지 번호가 글자 수 제한 등으로 일부 누락되어 보이지만, 내용상 5번이 정답으로 추론됨)
options_translation: ① 심리학자들은 이론을 형성할 때 깊은 사상가들의 의견을 우선시한다.
② 깊은 사상가들의 역할가 문화적 다양성은 심리학 연구의 중심이다.
③ 사혔적 가정가 이야기는 종종 심리학 연구밴다 더 통찰력이 있다.
④ 사혔 이론은 인간 행동에 대한 심리학적 믿음밴다 더 신뢰할 수 있다.
⑤ 심리학은 인간의 근밤적인 과정에 초점을 됔 줘거 기반의 과학이다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed ⓐ<u>tighter</u> guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which ⓑ<u>clarify</u> that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a ⓒ<u>rushed</u> diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements ⓓ<u>lessen</u> public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly ⓔ<u>deny</u> mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.*diagnosis: 진단 **donor: 기증자***cremation: 화장(火葬)
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 장기 기증을 위한 뇌사 판정 기준이 매우 엄격하고 복잡하게 설정된 것은 오히려 대중의 의심을 완화하기보다는 조장하거나(ⓓ), 뇌사 판정이 정밀하지 못한 과정이라는 잘못된 믿음을 '강화'하거나 '유지'할 위험이 있다는 문맥입니다. 따라서 '잘못된 믿음을 부정한다'는 의미의 ⓔdeny는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. ⓐHowever, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. ⓑThey all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. ⓒAncient Greek mathematicians often debated the practical applications of geometry in architecture and engineering. ⓓSo how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? ⓔPlato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 플라톤의 실재론(형상 이론)에 대해 원이라는 기하학적 대상을 예로 들어 설명하고 있습니다. 현실 세계의 원은 불완전하지만 보이지 않는 완벽한 세계인 '형상(Forms)'의 세계가 진정한 실재라는 것이 핵심 내용입니다. 반면 ③번 문장(ⓒ)은 고대 그리스 수학자들이 건축과 공학에서 기하학을 실무적으로 응용하는 것에 대해 논쟁했다는 내용이므로, 플라톤의 철학적 개념을 설명하는 전체 흐름과 무관합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that ___________________________________. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.*pest: 해충
options: ① they will be more vulnerable to natural threats
② the human population will continue to grow rapidly
③ scientists will develop new crops to solve the problem
④ traditional farming techniques will become more popular
⑤ global food production will benefit from modern technology
questions.explanation: 지문은 식량의 다양성이 감소하고 소수의 다수확 품종으로 단일화되면서 생기는 위험성을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 'Specifically' 문장에서 좁은 범위의 식물에 의존하는 글로벌 식량 시스템이 질병, 해충, 기후 위기에 생존하지 못할 가능성이 크다고 했으므로, 빈칸에는 단일 작물이 자연적 위협에 취약해진다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 그것들이 자연적 위협에 더 취약해질 것이다
② 인구가 계속해서 빠르게 증가할 것이다
③ 과학자들이 문제를 해결하기 위해 새로운 작물을 개발할 것이다
④ 전통적인 농법이 더 인기를 얻게 될 것이다
⑤ 세계 식량 생산이 현대 기술로부터 혜택을 입을 것이다

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants. Not only were their athletic talents superior, the Cubans appeared even stronger from just the colour of their uniforms. A game would not even start and the opposing team would already be scared. A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time. The country that ruled international baseball for decades has not been on top since that uniform change. Traditions are important for a team; while a team brand or image can adjust to keep up with present times, if the team abandons or neglects its roots, ________________________________________________.*conservative: 보수적인
options: ① it could develop new strategies for winning games
② its identity might weaken, affecting its performance
③ its reputation might grow stronger in modern contexts
④ it will lose its competitiveness, failing to adapt to new styles
questions.explanation: 지문은 쿠바 야구 대표팀이 전통적인 붉은색 유니폼을 입었을 때 세계를 제패했으나, 유니폼 스타일을 현대적으로 바꾸고 다른 나라의 스타일을 따르면서 성적이 하락했다는 사례를 들고 있습니다. 결론적으로 팀의 정통성(뿌리)을 소홀히 하면 팀의 정체성이 약해지고 성적에 영향을 미칠 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 경기에서 이기기 위한 새로운 전략을 개발할 수 있다
② 정체성이 약화되어 성적에 영향을 줄 수 있다
③ 현대적인 상황에서 명성이 더 강해질 수 있다
④ 새로운 스타일에 적응하지 못해 경쟁력을 잃을 것이다

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A ball thrown into the air is acted upon by the initial force given it, persisting as inertia of movement and tending to carry it in the same straight line, and by the constant pull of gravity downward, as well as by the resistance of the air. It moves, accordingly, in a curved path. Now the path does not represent the working of any particular force; there is simply the combination of the three elementary forces mentioned; but in a real sense, there is something in the total action besides the isolated action of three forces, namely, their joint action. In the same way, when two or more human individuals are together, their mutual relationships and their arrangement into a group are things which would not be revealed if ______________________________. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that some of the tendencies to action of the individual are related definitely to other persons, and could not be aroused except by other persons acting as stimuli. That is to say, the traits of human nature do not fully appear until the individual is brought into relationships with other individuals.
options: ① we studied how group dynamics influence individual behavior
② we observed individuals in situations involving joint relationships
③ we only examined individuals without considering their interactions
④ we assumed individuals behave similarly whether alone or in a group
⑤ we analyzed the effects of social forces on the action of isolated individuals
questions.explanation: 이 글은 공의 비행 궤적이 여러 물리적 힘들의 '결합된 작용'에 의해 결정되듯이, 인간의 집단 행동 또한 개별 인간의 행동 특성만으로는 설명될 수 없으며 타인과의 관계와 상호작용 속에서만 온전히 드러난다고 설명합니다. 따라서 상호작용을 배제한 채 개인만을 조사한다면 집단 내에서의 상호 관계나 구성 방식은 드러나지 않을 것이라는 내용이 빈칸에 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 집단 역학이 개인의 행동에 어떻게 영향을 미치는지 연구했다면
② 공동의 관계를 포함하는 상황에서 개인들을 관찰했다면
③ 상호 작용을 고려하지 않고 개인들만을 조사했다면
④ 개인이 혼자 있든 집단에 있든 비슷하게 행동한다고 가정했다면
⑤ 고립된 개인들의 행동에 미치는 사회적 힘의 영향을 분석했다면

questions.question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying them to culture. Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually likened to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection. (A)__________, these approaches had to be modified to account for the differences between genetic and cultural transmission. (B)__________, we do not expect the cultural transmission to follow the rules of genetic transmission strictly. If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily equally likely to acquire the mother's or father's form of that trait. Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers; (C)__________ the frequency of a cultural trait in the population is relevant beyond just the probability that an individual's parents had that trait.
options: ① (A) Furthermore (B) Consequently (C) on the other hand
② (A) Meanwhile (B) However (C) as a result
④ (A) Nevertheless (B) That is to say (C) on the contrary
⑤ (A) For example (B) In other words (C) thus
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 문화적 모델과 유전적 모델의 유사성을 언급한 뒤, 뒷 문장에서 유전적 전수와 문화적 전수 사이의 차이점을 설명하기 위해 수정되어야 했다고 말하므로 역접인 'However'가 적절합니다. (B) 문화적 전수가 유전적 전수의 규칙을 엄격히 따르지 않는다는 구체적인 사례(부모 중 한쪽의 형질을 반드시 물려받는 것이 아님)를 소개하므로 'For example'이 적절합니다. (C) 앞서 언급한 이유들(비부모 성인이나 또래에게서도 형질 습득 가능) 때문에 집단 내 문화적 형질의 빈도가 중요해진다는 결론을 도출하므로 'therefore'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 게다가 (B) 결과적으로 (C) 반면에
② (A) 한편 (B) 그러나 (C) 결과적으로
③ (A) 그러나 (B) 예를 들어 (C) 그러므로
④ (A) 그럼에도 불구하고 (B) 즉 (C) 반대로
⑤ (A) 예를 들어 (B) 다시 말해서 (C) 따라서

questions.question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 표현을 모두 배열하여 주제문을 완성하시오. (어휘 추가 및 변형 없음) [24년 10월 32번]
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race - their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't psychologically suffer much. In fact, ultra-marathon runners-those people who are crazy enough to push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50-100km or more over many hours, talk about making friends with their pain. When a patient has paid for some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it, the patient calls that good pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.
subjective_conditions: 어휘 추가 및 변형 없음
vocabulary_box: we / our suffering / depends on / mentally interpret and / perceive the pain / how
questions.answer: how we mentally interpret and perceive the pain depends on our suffering
questions.explanation: 고통을 마음속에서 어떻게 구성하느냐에 따라 고통의 정도가 달라진다는 내용이므로, 우리가 정신적으로 고통을 어떻게 해석하고 지각하는지가 우리가 겪는 괴로움에 달려있다는 주제문을 구성해야 합니다. 'The extent of' 뒤에 명사절 'how we mentally interpret and perceive the pain'이 주어로 오고, 'depends on' 뒤에 목적어 'our suffering'이 오는 구조입니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 의미와 어법에 맞게 주어진 표현을 모두 배열하여 완성하시오. (어휘 추가 및 변형 없음) [24년 10월 41-42번]
questions.passage: From an early age, we assign purpose to objects and events, preferring this reasoning to random chance. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because they don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. However, by ______________________________________. This was essential in our hunter-gatherer days to avoid being eaten by predators. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, as those are the mental processes which we understand. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents. This results in a perceptual system strongly biased towards anthropomorphism. Therefore, we tend to assume intention even where there is none. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you. By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has saved your life.
subjective_conditions: 어휘 추가 및 변형 없음
vocabulary_box: their likely behavior / to animals and objects / quickly predict / we can / attributing / intention / and make decisions accordingly
questions.answer: attributing intention to animals and objects, we can quickly predict their likely behavior and make decisions accordingly
questions.explanation: 인간은 생존을 위해 대상에 의도를 부여하는 경향이 있다는 내용입니다. 빈칸 앞의 'by'에 연결되는 동명사 구문 'attributing intention to animals and objects'를 먼저 배치하고, 그 결과로서의 주절 'we can quickly predict their likely behavior and make decisions accordingly'를 배열합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 문장을 주어진 표현과 조건을 활용하여 20단어 이내의 영단어로 영작하시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. <u>이러한 감정들은 우리에게 우리의 공동체가 우리를 가치있게 여기도록 만드는 것을 더 많이 하고 그렇지 않은 것을 덜 하도록 강요한다</u>. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 표현은 모두 사용하고 필요한 어휘는 추가할 것
필요시 어휘 중복 사용 및 어형을 변형할 것
20단어 이내로 작성할 것
questions.answer: These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't.
questions.explanation: 주어진 우리말 '이러한 감정들은(These emotions) 우리에게(~하도록) 강요한다(compel us to do)'를 기본 구조로 잡습니다. '우리의 공동체가 우리를 가치있게 여기도록 만드는 것'은 'what makes our community value us'로, '그렇지 않은 것'은 'what doesn't (make our community value us)'의 생략형인 'what doesn't'로 표현합니다. 이를 종합하여 'do more of A and less of B' 구문에 넣으면 'These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't.'이 됩니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
options: ① Cramming is the Best Way to Learn
② How to Memorize Information Quickly
③ The Science Behind Short-Term Memory
④ Studying vs. Testing: Which is More Important?
⑤ Why Cramming Fails: The Importance of Testing for Long-Term Memory Retention
questions.explanation: 이 글은 벼락치기(cramming)가 왜 장기적인 학습에 효과적이지 않은지를 설명하고 있습니다. 단기 기억(working memory)에 머무는 정보는 곧 사라지기 때문에, 정보를 장기 기억으로 옮기기 위해서는 단순 학습보다 '자기 테스트(testing yourself)'가 필수적임을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⑤번 '벼락치기가 실패하는 이유: 장기 기억 유지를 위한 테스트의 중요성'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 벼락치기는 학습을 위한 최고의 방법이다
② 정보를 빠르게 암기하는 방법
③ 단기 기억 뒤에 숨겨진 과학
④ 공부 대 테스트: 무엇이 더 중요한가?
⑤ 왜 벼락치기가 실패하는가: 장기 기억 유지를 위한 테스트의 중요성

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial ⓐ<u>abundance</u> of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely ⓑ<u>novel</u>. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. ⓒ<u>Competent</u> composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most ⓓ<u>notable</u> non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't ⓔ<u>ingenious</u>. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에는 오해를 받았고 수용되지 못했다는 내용이므로, 수용의 '풍부함(abundance)'이 아니라 수용의 '결핍' 혹은 '부족'이 원인이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 ⓐ는 'lack' 또는 'scarcity' 등의 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 전달하는 의미가 다른 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Every time ⓐ<u>a new medium</u> comes along - whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on ⓑ<u>a new kind of goggles</u>, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch ⓒ<u>television</u>, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show - whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in ⓓ<u>it</u> a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than ⓔ<u>the information itself</u>. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ는 모두 '매체(Medium)' 자체 또는 매체라는 틀을 비유하거나 구체적으로 지칭하는 대상들입니다. 반면 ⓔ 'the information itself'는 매체를 통해 전달되는 '내용(content/message)'을 의미하므로, 매체의 형식(고글, 매체 그 자체)을 강조하는 나머지 넷과 그 성격이 다릅니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that are ______________. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that was ______________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 본질주의(essentialism)의 위험성을 경고하며, 존재하지 않는 것을 찾으려 하는 과학적 오류를 비유합니다. 어두운 방안에 없는 고양이를 찾는 속담과 빛의 매질로 여겨졌으나 실재하지 않았던 '에테르'의 예를 통해, 실제로는 '없는(absent)' 것을 보게 하거나 찾게 만든다는 맥락이 성립합니다.
options_translation: ① 부재하는, 없는
② 존재하는
③ 본질적인
④ 일시적인
⑤ 취약한

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the passage, Social media stars gain fame not through (A)__________ talents like traditional celebrities, but through metrics such as followers and likes, which can be seen as a phenomenon that (B)__________ "ordinary fame."
questions.explanation: ※ 준비된 요약문을 바탕으로 보면, 소셔 미디어 스타들은 전통적인 명사들처람 '뛰어난(exceptional)' 재눙을 통해 명성을 얻는 것이 아니라, 굦독자나 젔아요와 같은 준표를 통해 명성을 얻는데, 이는 '평범한 명성'을 '재정의(redefines)'하는 현상으로 볼 수 읈습니다. 백락사 전통적 명사는 타고난 재눙이나 계층과 관련이 읈준데 반해, 소셔 미디어 세러브는 수치화된 관심을 통해 명성을 획득하므로 명성의 의미림 새롭게 구성한다고 본문에서 언급하고 읈습니다.
options_translation: ① 타고난 - 피하다
② 무기한한 - 피하다
③ 무기한한 - 재정의하다
④ 뛰어난 - 재정의하다
⑤ 뛰어난 - 무시하다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
options: ② impacts of trial and error on learning
③ science of imitation in early childhood
④ ways parents influence child development
⑤ role of mirror neurons in learning by observation
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런의 발견이 관찰을 통한 학습이라는 인간의 기본적인 능력을 이해하는 방식을 어떻게 변화시켰는지 설명하고 있습니다. 아기들의 모방 행위부터 현대 문화의 발전에 이르기까지, 관찰을 통한 학습이 거울 뉴런의 작용으로 가능해짐을 강조하고 있으므로 주제는 '관찰 학습에서 거울 뉴런의 역할'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 아기들이 모든 것을 모방하는 이유
② 시행착오가 학습에 미치는 영향
③ 유아기 모방의 과학
④ 부모가 자녀 발달에 영향을 미치는 방식
⑤ 관찰을 통한 학습에서 거울 뉴런의 역할

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. (A) There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. (B) One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. (C) Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. (D) Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. (E) That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
questions.insertion_sentence: But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path.
questions.explanation: 글의 (A) 부분에서 목소리를 인식하는 두 가지 경로가 있다고 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 첫 번째 경로인 외부 소리 전달 경로를 설명합니다. 주어진 문장은 '두 번째 내부 경로'를 소개하고 있으므로, 첫 번째 경로 설명이 끝나고 실제 내부 경로의 구체적인 작동 방식(뼈를 통한 진동 전달)이 설명되는 (C) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures.
ordered_passages: (A) Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.

(B) Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level.

(C) Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 수온과 용존 산소량의 관계(찬물에 산소가 더 많음)를 설명한 후, (B)에서 이 원리를 바탕으로 지구 온난화로 인한 수온 상승이 산소 감소를 초래할 것이라는 예측을 제시합니다. 이어 (C)에서 실제로 지난 50년간 산소량이 감소했다는 과학적 데이터를 제시하며, 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 산소 감소가 해양 생물 서식지에 미치는 파괴적인 영향(무산소 사건 등)을 서술하는 것이 가장 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is ①<u>concerned</u>. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will ②<u>agreeably</u> eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being ③<u>typically</u> preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation ④<u>impartial</u>. Furthermore, she is now ⑤<u>inclined</u> to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.explanation: 카푸친 원숭이가 다른 원숭이가 더 좋은 간식(포도)을 받는 것을 보고 자신이 받은 오이를 던지는 상황은 불평등함을 느끼는 것입니다. 따라서 '공정한, 치우치지 않는'이라는 뜻의 'impartial'은 문맥상 어울리지 않으며, 'unfair' 또는 'intolerable' 같은 '불공정한' 혹은 '견딜 수 없는'의 의미를 가진 단어로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ.
ordered_passages: (A) "Homologous- traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals.

(B) The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight.

(C) As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 생물학자가 구분하는 두 가지 유사성 중 '상응(Analogous)' 형질을 먼저 정의합니다. (B)에서 상응 형질의 예시로 새와 벌의 날개를 들어 보충 설명합니다. 그 다음 (A)에서 '대조적으로(in contrast)'를 사용해 '상동(Homologous)' 형질을 정의하고 포유류의 앞다리 예시를 듭니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 상동 형질의 결과(As a result)로 나타나는 구조적 공유 특성을 설명하며 두 개념을 구별하는 방법을 제시하는 순서가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. (A) Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. (B) The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. (C) We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. (D) And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. (E) If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
questions.insertion_sentence: These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'These emotions'가 가리키는 대상이 (C) 문장에 언급된 'pride, shame, or insecurity'와 같은 감정들이며, 이러한 감정들이 우리로 하여금 공동체가 우리를 가치 있게 여기게 만드는 행동을 더 많이 하도록 강요한다는 내용이 (D) 앞에 오는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 또한 (D) 문장의 'they'는 주어진 문장의 'These emotions'를 지칭합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 5. 다음 글을 읽고 재해석한 <요약문>의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 쓰고, 요약문 전체를 해석하시오. [24년 10월 29번]
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially related to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways.
