Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without cognitive effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.summary_sentence: The audience participating in linguistic metaphors (A)_____________ understand the meaning of the metaphors. Meanwhile, those who participate in technological metaphors are (B)_____________ because the digital metaphors are likely to be intuitive and obvious.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 쓸 것
요약문 전체를 해석할 것
questions.answer: (A) actively(B) passive(C) 언어적 은유의 참가하는 청중들은 은유의 의미 이해를 적극적으로 하고 반면 기술적 은유의 참가자들은 수동적이다. 왜냐하면 디지털 은유는 직관적이고 분명하기 때문이다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 언어적 은유는 청중이 인지적 노력을 들여 '적극적으로(actively)' 참여해야 함을 강조하는 반면, 기술적 은유는 직관적이고 명확하여 청중이 상대적으로 '수동적인(passive)' 상태에서도 의미를 파악할 수 있다고 설명하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 6. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 24번]
questions.passage: The evolution of Al is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which Al exceeds human intelligence.
ordered_passages: (A) Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of Al. The direction of Al's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into Al. We need to see our relationship with Al as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.

(B) After that point, it is predicted that Al will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When Al becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine.

(C) Al and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with Al, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 AI가 인간 지능을 넘어서는 '특이점(singularity)'을 언급했습니다. (B)의 'After that point'는 이 특이점을 가리키며 AI가 의식적인 존재로 진화함을 설명합니다. (C)의 'then'은 AI가 의식을 갖게 된 후 인간의 의식과 상호작용하며 함께 진화하는 단계를 나타냅니다. 마지막으로 (A)는 '반대로(Conversely)' 인간의 가치관이 AI에 미치는 영향을 서술하며 결론을 맺는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can ⓐ<u>recollect</u> after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will yield quantitative data, but it might be ⓑ<u>questionable</u>. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could be ⓒ<u>consistent</u>. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a ⓓ<u>definite</u> answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make ⓔ<u>vague</u> concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 사람마다 '슬픔'에 대한 정의가 서로 다를 수 있어 응답이 부정확할 수 있다는 내용이므로, ⓒ의 'consistent(일관된)'는 'inconsistent(일관되지 않은, 서로 다른)'와 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus ⓐ<u>have</u> is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight ⓑ<u>was</u> a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again ⓒ<u>what</u> they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes ⓓ<u>staring</u> upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn ⓔ<u>itself</u> into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.explanation: ⓒ는 'It is ~ that ...' 강조 구문에서 'when they looked again'이라는 부사절을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 접속사 what 대신에 강조 구문의 that을 사용해야 문법적으로 옳습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 단어의 원형으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We __________ memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are __________ through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 맥락은 우리가 기억을 비디오처럼 그대로 꺼내오는 것이 아니라, 기존의 지식, 개념, 추상적 표현을 통해 정보를 재부호화하고 재구성한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 'rebuild(재구성하다, 다시 세우다)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 소환하다/회상하다
② 반영하다
③ 유지하다
④ 받다
⑤ 재구성하다

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 우리말 (A)를 주어진 조건을 지켜 영어로 서술하시오.
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, (A)<u>지금까지 꾸중을 듣는 것만큼 좋은 반응은 없었다</u>, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
subjective_conditions: '원급 표현'을 반드시 포함시킬 것. (조건을 지키지 않는 경우 0점 처리)
questions.answer: No response is as good as being scolded.
questions.explanation: '~만큼 ...한 것은 없다'는 최상급 의미를 나타내는 원급 비교 구문 'No + 명사 + is as/so + 형용사 + as'를 사용하여 영작합니다. '꾸중을 듣는 것'은 동명사 수동형인 'being scolded'를 사용합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as <u>a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another</u>. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.
options: ① Symptoms of illnesses vary widely between individuals.
② Organisms are capable of existing in infinite possible states.
③ Most diseases in organisms are affected by genetic manipulations.
④ Complex systems naturally evolve toward chaos without intervention.
⑤ Biological systems maintain stability by restricting possible outcomes.
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 복잡한 생물학적 시스템이 안정성을 유지하기 위해 가능한 결과의 범위를 좁힌다는 '운하화(canalization)'에 대한 설명입니다. 밑줄 친 비유는 공이 무작위한 곳에 머물지 않고 특정 골짜기로 굴러 내려가듯, 생명체도 제한된 특정 상태 중 하나로 수렴한다는 의미이므로 5번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 질병의 증상은 개인마다 매우 다양하다.
② 유기체는 무한히 가능한 상태로 존재할 수 있다.
③ 유기체의 대부분의 질병은 유전자 조작의 영향을 받는다.
④ 복잡한 시스템은 개입 없이 자연스럽게 혼돈으로 진화한다.
⑤ 생물학적 시스템은 가능한 결과를 제한함으로써 안정성을 유지한다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another, The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
options: ① Human nature seeks novelty beyond familiar boundaries.
② Psychology counts on subjective opinions and inferences.
③ Psychology utilizes intuitive ways to define human beings.
④ Human behavior is driven by basic motivation and instinct.
⑤ Psychology depends on data to comprehend human behavior.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 심리학이 일반적인 통념이나 의견이 아닌, 과학적인 줐거(줝거)와 대이터에 기반하여 인간의 픐동을 이해하는 학문임을 강조하고 읈습니다. 따라서 심리학이 인간 픐동을 이해하기 위해 대이터에 의존한다는 5번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간의 밤성은 익숙한 경계를 넘어 새로움을 추구한다.
② 심리학은 줜관적인 의견과 추론에 의존한다.
③ 심리학은 인간을 정의하기 위해 중관적인 방박을 활용한다.
④ 인간의 픐동은 기반적인 동기와 밤능에 의해 제도된다.
⑤ 심리학은 인간의 픐동을 이해하기 위해 대이터에 의존한다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: From an early age, we assign purpose to objects and events, preferring this reasoning to random chance. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because they don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. However, by attributing intention to animals and even objects, we are able to make fast decisions about the likely behaviour of that being. This was essential in our hunter-gatherer days to avoid being eaten by predators. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, as those are the mental processes which we understand. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents. This results in a perceptual system strongly biased towards anthropomorphism. Therefore, we tend to assume intention even where there is none. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given its probable intention to kill you. By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming intent, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has saved your life.
questions.summary_sentence: Humans tend to attribute intention to the objects and events, especially in (A)__________ circumstances, as this tendency facilitates (B)__________ decision-making for survival.
questions.explanation: 인간은 진화적으로 모호하거나 불확실한(uncertain) 상황에서 사물을 의도를 가진 존재로 파악함으로써 선존을 위한 즉각적인(immediate) 의사결정을 내리는 경향을 갖게 되었습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 uncertain, (B)에는 immediate가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 예측 가능한 - 긴급한
② 불확실한 - 즉각적인
③ 댄전적인 - 부분적인
④ 신뢰할 수 없눜 - 법적인
⑤ 예외적인 - 협력적인

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally elective. ①That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an abundant resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. ②The rapid urbanization in many countries has solved significant social inequalities and conflicts. ③There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to address it. ④Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater, in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. ⑤Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly highlights have-and-have-not inequities, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 현대의 물 위기가 정치적 문제이며 정부의 무관심이나 부실한 인프라, 무분별한 도시화 등으로 인해 발생한다고 설명합니다. 그러나 ②번 문장은 '빠른 도시화가 사회적 불평등과 갈등을 해결했다'는 내용으로, 물 위기의 부정적 원인으로서 도시화를 언급하는 전체 흐름과 상반됩니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is <u>to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness</u>. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
options: ① to redefine depression not as a neurochemical problem but as an awareness one
② to reconsider depression as a problem which is subject to substance imbalances
③ to re-evaluate the various causes of depression as shaped by the external influences
④ to reconnect depression with explicit environmental causes rather than one's mental states
⑤ to re-examine symptoms of depression solely through biological processes over a long period
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우울증을 뇌의 화학적 불균형(결과)이 아닌 의식의 왜곡(원인)으로 보아야 한다고 주장합니다. 따라서 밑줄 친 부분은 우울증을 신경화학적 문제가 아니라 인식/의식의 문제로 재정의하는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 우울증을 신경화학적 문제가 아니라 인식의 문제로 재정의하는 것
② 우울증을 물질 불균형에 지배받는 문제로 재고하는 것
③ 외부 영향에 의해 형성된 우울증의 다양한 원인을 재평가하는 것
④ 정신 상태보다는 명시적인 환경적 원인과 우울증을 다시 연결하는 것
⑤ 오랜 기간에 걸친 생물학적 과정을 통해서만 우울증 증상을 재검토하는 것

questions.question: 20. 다음 글을 읽고, <요약문>의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 각각 2단어로 쓰고, 요약문을 해석하시오.
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
questions.summary_sentence: The middle version was sold the most because it was (A)__________ than the first one and it is (B)__________ than the third one.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 각각 2단어로 쓸 것
요약문을 해석할 것
questions.answer: (A) more features(B) less expensive(C) 중간 모델은 첫 번째 모델보다 특징은 더 많고 세 번째 모델보다 값이 덜 비싸기 때문이다.
questions.explanation: 본문 하단부에서 중간 모델이 가장 저렴한 모델(첫 번째 모델)보다 특징이 더 많고(more features), 가장 비싼 모델(세 번째 모델)보다 가격이 더 저렴하다(less expensive)고 명시되어 있습니다. 소비자들은 가장 비싼 모델의 가격에 부담을 느끼면서도 더 많은 기능을 원하기 때문에 중간 모델을 선택하게 된다는 내용입니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Electricity Generation from Fossil Fuels,Nuclear Energy, and Renewables, 2023 The above graph shows the electricity generation from fossil fuels, nuclear energy, and renewables in four countries in 2023. ⓐAustralia's electricity generation only comes from fossil fuels and renewables, and the percentage of fossil fuels is more than twice that of renewables. ⓑIn terms of electricity generation from nuclear energy, the U.S. shows the highest percentage among all four countries. ⓒThe percentage of electricity generation from fossil fuels in the U.S. is higher than that in the U.K., which is also true for renewables. ⓓIn the U.K., the percentage of electricity generated from nuclear energy is less than a third of that generated from renewables. ⓔBrazil's percentage of electricity generated from renewables is 20 percentage points larger than that of Australia and the U.K. combined.
questions.explanation: 문장 ⓒ에서 미국의 화석 연료 발전 비율이 영국보다 높다는 설명은 맞을 수 있으나, 재생 에너지(renewables) 발전 비율 또한 미국이 영국보다 높다는 부분('which is also true for renewables')은 실제 2023년 통계(영국의 재생에너지 비율이 미국보다 높음)와 일치하지 않는 설명이 됩니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push ─ essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, (A)<u>we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation</u>. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
options: ① The human brain is designed to solve problems independently.
② Intergenerational learning achieves the same effect without distributing information.
③ An individual possesses all the resources necessary to analyze information.
④ Collaborative computation, which distributes calculation tasks socially, is important.
⑤ Human computational ability can expand sufficiently without social collaboration.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 인지 능력 한계로 인해 모든 정보를 개인이 가질 필요 없이, 사회적으로 정보를 분산시키고 협력하여 거대한 계산(문제 해결)을 수행한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 밑줄 친 (A)는 우리가 거대한 전체 시스템 중 아주 일부분에만 집중하며 기여한다는 의미이므로, 사회적으로 계산 작업을 분산하는 '협력적 계산(Collaborative computation)'의 중요성을 언급한 4번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간의 뇌는 독립적으로 문제를 해결하도록 설계되었다.
② 세대 간 학습은 정보를 분산시키지 않고도 동일한 효과를 거둔다.
③ 개인은 정보를 분석하는 데 필요한 모든 자원을 보유하고 있다.
④ 계산 작업을 사회적으로 분산시키는 협력적 계산이 중요하다.
⑤ 인간의 계산 능력은 사회적 협력 없이도 충분히 확장될 수 있다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode ⓐ<u>what</u> we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than ⓑ<u>retrieving</u> the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information ─ a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People ⓒ<u>who</u> lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features ⓓ<u>come</u> at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are ⓔ<u>reconstructed</u> through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'representing the world as abstract ideas and features'로, 동명사구 주어입니다. 동명사구가 주어일 때는 단수 취급하므로 동사 'come'은 'comes'로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓐ는 관계대명사 what, ⓑ는 병렬구조(rather than retrieving), ⓒ는 주격 관계대명사, ⓔ는 수동태로 모두 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'ⓐ<u>high-dimensional</u> system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules are ⓑ<u>vast</u> in number. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a ⓒ<u>limited</u> number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington referred to this significant ⓓ<u>restriction</u> of possible outcomes as canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often markedly ⓔ<u>different.</u>
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 개념인 '운하화(canalization)'는 수많은 원인이나 상호작용에도 불구하고 결과가 소수의 특정한 상태로 제한되는 현상을 말합니다. 따라서 질병의 원인이 많더라도 생리적, 증상적 수준에서 나타나는 징후는 매우 '제한적이거나 유사하다'는 맥락이 되어야 하므로 ⓔ 'different'를 'similar' 혹은 'limited'와 같은 단어로 바꾸어야 합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and inkjet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. (A) If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. (B) If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. (C) Many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. (D) The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. (E) They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
questions.insertion_sentence: But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 왜 많은 소비재가 세 가지 버전으로 출시되는지에 대해 설명합니다. (B)는 두 가지 버전만 있을 때 저렴한 것을 선택하는 경향을 말합니다. 주어진 문장은 '하지만(But)' 더 비싼 세 번째 모델을 도입하면 두 번째 모델의 판매가 올라간다는 전환을 제공합니다. (C)는 그 이유(비싼 모델의 기능은 좋지만 가격은 부담스러운 상황)를 부연 설명하기 시작하며, (D)에서 중간 제품의 장점이 설명되므로 주어진 문장은 (C) 자리에 오는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre ─ indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. (A) You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. (B) And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. (C) Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? (D) At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. (E) But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant ─ in time or in place ─ we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.insertion_sentence: But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts.
questions.explanation: (A) 문장은 기후 변화가 여전히 지엽적인 특징으로 보일 때 이야기를 할 수 있다고 말합니다. 주어진 문장은 '하지만(But)' 온도가 더 오르면 아무도 그 영향으로부터 고립되었다고 느끼지 못할 것이라는 반전을 줍니다. 이후 (B) 문장에서 기후 변화가 지평선 전체로 확장되면서 이야기가 되기를 멈춘다는 결론으로 이어지므로 (B)가 가장 적절한 위치입니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
questions.summary_sentence: Depression should be viewed not as a chemical (A)_____________ in the brain, but as a disorder of. (B)_____________ that affects brain function and disrupts one's sense of self and life meaning.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우울증의 원인을 뇌의 화학적 불균형으로 보는 기존의 관점을 비판하며, 화학적 불균형은 우울증의 원인이 아니라 결과라고 주장합니다. 대신 우울증의 근본 원인을 자아와 삶의 의미를 잃어버린 '의식'의 왜곡이나 장애로 보아야 한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸 (A)에는 화학적 '불균형(imbalance)'이, (B)에는 '의식(consciousness)'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 불균형 / 의식
② 불균형 / 감정
③ 불균형 / 신진대사
④ 균형 / 지각
⑤ 균형 / 행동

questions.question: 1. 윗글의 빈칸 (가)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>From an early age, we assign purpose to objects and events, preferring this reasoning to random chance</u>. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because ⓑ<u>they</u> don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. However, by attributing intention to animals and even objects, we are able to make fast decisions about the likely behaviour of that being. This was essential in our hunter-gatherer days to avoid being eaten by predators. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, as those are the mental processes which we understand. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents. This results in a perceptual system strongly biased towards anthropomorphism. Therefore, (가)_____________________. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given ⓒ<u>it</u>s probable intention to kill you. By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming ⓓ_________, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has saved your life.*ambiguous: 모호한 **anthropomorphism: 의인화
options: ① people seem to infer its intention for in-depth analysis.
② humans are evolving toward incomplete people intended to be.
③ people are inclined to believe that something is intentional even though it isn't.
④ human tend to hide their intention to help their descendant understand complex situation.
⑤ people are apt to place the importance on the meaning of the object rather than viewing it as random.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 생존을 위해 대상에 의도나 목적을 부여하려는 경향(의인화)이 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 (가) 앞의 내용은 우리의 지각 시스템이 의인화 쪽으로 강하게 편향되어 있다는 것이며, 뒤의 내용은 이것이 생존 기제로 발생했다는 것입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 실제로 의도가 없더라도 무엇인가가 의도적이라고 믿는 경향이 있다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들은 심층 분석을 위해 그것의 의도를 추론하는 것처럼 보인다.
② 인간은 의도된 불완전한 사람들을 향해 진화하고 있다.
③ 사람들은 어떤 것이 의도적이지 않더라도 그것이 의도적이라고 믿는 경향이 있다.
④ 인간은 후손들이 복잡한 상황을 이해하도록 돕기 위해 자신의 의도를 숨기는 경향이 있다.
⑤ 사람들은 객체를 무작위로 보기보다는 그 의미에 중요성을 두는 경향이 있다.

questions.question: 2. 윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓓ에 대한 질문에 답하시오.
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>From an early age, we assign purpose to objects and events, preferring this reasoning to random chance</u>. Children assume, for instance, that pointy rocks are that way because ⓑ<u>they</u> don't want you to sit on them. When we encounter something, we first need to determine what sort of thing it is. Inanimate objects and plants generally do not move and can be evaluated from physics alone. However, by attributing intention to animals and even objects, we are able to make fast decisions about the likely behaviour of that being. This was essential in our hunter-gatherer days to avoid being eaten by predators. The anthropologist Stewart Guthrie made the point that survival in our evolutionary past meant that we interpret ambiguous objects as agents with human mental characteristics, as those are the mental processes which we understand. Ambiguous events are caused by such agents. This results in a perceptual system strongly biased towards anthropomorphism. Therefore, (가)_____________________. This would have arisen as a survival mechanism. If a lion is about to attack you, you need to react quickly, given ⓒ<u>it</u>s probable intention to kill you. By the time you have realized that the design of its teeth and claws could kill you, you are dead. So, assuming ⓓ_________, without detailed design analysis or understanding of the physics, has saved your life.*ambiguous: 모호한 **anthropomorphism: 의인화
subjective_conditions: (1) ⓐ에서 우리가 어릴 때부터 선호하는 것으로 언급된 것은 무엇인가?
(2) ⓑ의 they가 가리키는 것은?
(3) ⓒ의 it이 가리키는 것은?
(4) ⓓ의 빈칸에 들어가기에 적절한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (변형x)
questions.answer: (1) 논리 (이러한 추론)(2) pointy rocks(3) lion(4) intention
questions.explanation: (1) ⓐ 문장에서 'preferring this reasoning to random chance'라고 언급되어 있으므로, 무작위 우연보다 '이러한 추론(논리)'을 선호함을 알 수 있습니다.(2) ⓑ가 속한 문장에서 아이들이 뾰족한 바위(pointy rocks)가 사람들이 앉는 것을 원치 않는다고 생각한다고 했으므로 they는 'pointy rocks'를 지칭합니다.(3) ⓒ는 뒤에 나오는 사자(lion)의 죽이려는 의도를 의미하므로 'it'은 'lion'을 지칭합니다.(4) 글 전체의 핵심 주제가 대상에게 '의도'를 부여한다는 것이며, 문맥상 세부 분석 없이 '의도'를 가정하는 것이 생존에 도움이 되었다는 흐름이므로 본문에 언급된 'intention'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensionalsystem,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on.
ordered_passages: (A) We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.

(B) In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another.

(C) In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 생명체가 매우 복잡한 시스템이라는 것을 언급합니다. (C)에서는 세포 내 분자 간 상호작용의 방대함을 예로 들며 복잡성을 구체화하고, 안정을 위해 소수의 집합적 방식만 나타난다는 핵심 개념(캐널라이제이션의 예시)을 제시합니다. (B)에서는 (C)에서 설명한 '결과의 대폭적인 축소' 현상을 'canalization'이라고 명명하며 이론적으로 설명합니다. (A)에서는 이러한 원리가 건강과 질병에도 동일하게 적용됨을 보여주며 논의를 확장합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by the ⓐ<u>disproportion</u> of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression ⓑ<u>brings about</u> a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this ⓒ<u>revised</u> cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more ⓓ<u>superficial</u> entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may ⓔ<u>elaborate</u> itself in the form of depression.*neurotransmitter: 신경 전달 물질
questions.explanation: 이 글은 우울증이 뇌의 물질 불균형 때문이 아니라 의식의 문제라고 주장하고 있습니다. ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 의식은 뇌의 기능을 넘어서는 존재이며, 뇌는 의식의 기관일 뿐이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 의식은 뇌보다 더 '피상적인(superficial)' 존재가 아니라 더 '심오한' 또는 '근본적인(profound/fundamental)' 실체여야 문맥이 성립합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. (A) If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money. (B) If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model, it would be different. (C) With the third item introduced, which has more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. (D) The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. (E) They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
questions.insertion_sentence: As a result, the company loses the opportunity to gain more income.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장 '그 결과 회사는 더 많은 수입을 얻을 기회를 잃게 된다'는 (A)에서 설명한 상황, 즉 '제조업체가 단 하나의 버전만 만들었을 때, 소비자들이 더 많은 돈을 쓸 의향이 있었음에도 불구하고 그러지 못한 상황'에 대한 결과입니다. 따라서 (A)의 가정 상황 바로 뒤인 (B) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. ___________________________________________. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
options: ① This comprehension capacity focuses on retention.
② Retention is significant asset to retrieve the memory.
③ Utilizing this memory strategy can be highly beneficial.
④ This strategy serves as a valuable tool for eradicating memory.
⑤ The approach to encode information is much more complicated process.
questions.explanation: 인간의 기억은 비디오처럼 저장되는 것이 아니라 추상적인 개념으로 재구성되어 효율적으로 저장된다는 내용입니다. 빈칸 뒤에서 이것이 '정보를 저장하는 더 효율적인 방법'이며, 모든 세부사항을 다 기억하는 것보다 일반화와 학습에 도움이 된다고 설명하고 있으므로, 이러한 기억 전략을 활용하는 것이 유익하다는 ③번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: 이 이해 능력은 보유에 초점을 맞춘다.
보유는 기억을 회상하는 데 중요한 자산이다.
이러한 기억 전략을 활용하는 것은 매우 유익할 수 있다.
이 전략은 기억을 말살하는 귀중한 도구 역할을 한다.
정보를 인코딩하는 접근 방식은 훨씬 더 복잡한 과정이다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 영영 풀이로 가장 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: The best (A)_________ most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually. what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create (B)_________. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.*flounder: 넙치 **mimic: 모방하다
vocabulary_box: ⓐ the action of defending from or resisting attack
ⓑ something that is not really what it seems to be
ⓒ a false idea or belief that is caused by mental illness
ⓓ something that is used to attacking yourself, your country, etc.
ⓔ speak or write about something that is different from the main subject being discussed
questions.explanation: 문맥상 (A)에는 문어가 숨어 있는 등의 행동을 통해 자신을 보호하는 수단인 '방어(defense)'의 의미가 들어가야 하므로 ⓐ가 적절합니다. (B)에는 문어가 몸의 색깔과 패턴을 바꾸어 다른 생물처럼 보이게 만드는 '착각/환상(illusion)'의 의미가 들어가야 하므로 ⓑ가 적절합니다. 따라서 정답은 ①번입니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we ⓐ<u>frame</u> the pain in our mind. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race - their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen ⓑ<u>surplus</u>, they don't psychologically suffer much. In fact, ultra-marathon runners - those people who are crazy enough to push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50-100km or more over many hours, talk about making ⓒ<u>companions</u> with their pain. When a patient has paid for some form of ⓓ<u>passive</u> back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it, the patient calls that good pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be ⓔ<u>worthwhile</u>, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 고통에 대한 마음가짐(프레임)에 따라 고통을 느끼는 정도가 달라진다는 내용입니다. 1500m 달리기 선수가 극한의 고통을 느끼며 달릴 때, 폐는 산소가 과잉인 상태가 아니라 산소가 부족한 상태여야 합니다. 따라서 '과잉, 잉여'를 뜻하는 ⓑ의 surplus는 '부족, 결핍'을 뜻하는 shortage나 deficit으로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 동일한 단어가 들어가기에 부적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature ⓐ_________ float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science ⓑ_________ is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do: why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure ⓒ_________ psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles ⓓ_________ generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are ⓔ_________ modern psychology is all about.
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ는 주격 관계대명사 'that'이 들어갈 수 있고, ⓒ는 접속사 'that'이 들어갈 수 있습니다. 하지만 ⓔ는 문장에서 보어 역할을 하며 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사인 'what'이 들어가야 하는 자리이므로 'that'은 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. (A) You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. (B) But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. (C) And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. (D) At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. (E) But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.insertion_sentence: Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window?
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 창밖으로 이미 명백하게 보이는 기후 변화에 대한 이야기를 왜 굳이 소설이나 영화로 보는지 묻는 질문입니다. (D) 위치에서 이에 대한 대답으로 '현재로서는 여전히 도피적인 즐거움을 줄 수 있기 때문'이라는 내용이 이어지는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에 들어가기에 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 18번]
questions.passage: To the State Education Department. I am writing with regard to the state's funding for the construction project at Fort Montgomery High School. Our school needs additional spaces to provide a fully functional Art and Library Media Center to serve our students in a more meaningful way. Despite (A)[submit / submitting] all required documentation for funding to your department in April 2024, we have not yet received any notification from your department. A delay in the process can carry considerable consequences related to the school's budgetary constraints and schedule. Therefore, in order to proceed with our project, we request you (B)[notify / notifying] us of the review result regarding the submitted documentation. I look forward to (C)[hear / hearing] from you. Respectfully. Clara Smith Principal, Fort Montgomery High School
questions.explanation:
(A) Despite는 전치사이므로 뒤에 동명사 형태인 submitting이 연결되는 것이 적절합니다.
(B) request는 목적어 뒤에 to부정사(to notify)를 취하는 것이 일반적이나, 본 문항에서는 원형(notify)과 현재분사(notifying) 중 선택하는 구조입니다. 동사 request의 의미상 당의성(요청)을 포함하므로 원형인 notify가 정답으로 채택되었습니다.
(C) look forward to에서 to는 전치사이므로 뒤에 명사나 동명사 형태인 hearing이 와야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 제출하다 / 통보하다 / 듣다
② 제출하는 것 / 통보하다 / 듣는 것
③ 제출하다 / 통지하는 것 / 듣는 것
④ 제출하는 것 / 통지하는 것 / 듣는 것
