questions.question:
15. 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. [24년 10월 22번]
Q: Write 3 characteristics of the response that is sometimes the most accurate interpretation of what our mind is telling us. (in Korean)
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
questions.explanation: 지문 중앙부의 "Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction..." 문장에서 우리 마음의 가장 진실된 해석이라고 언급된 반응의 특징은 세 가지 형용사(first, immediate, automatic)로 묘사됩니다. 이를 한국어로 옮기면 '첫 번째의(최초의)', '즉각적인', '자동적인'이 됩니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어가기에 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of Al is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which AI ___________ human intelligence. After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with Al, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI. The direction of Al's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 '특이점(singularity)'은 AI가 인간의 지능을 '넘어서는' 시점을 의미하므로 'exceeds(넘어서다, 초과하다)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 넘어서다
② 기대하다
③ 연장하다
④ 소비하다
⑤ 초과(명사)

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분의 우리말 해석이 가장 적절치 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. ⓐ<u>As we lack the resources to compute answers independently</u>(우리는 독립적으로 해답을 계산하기 위한 자원이 부족하기 때문에), we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand ⓑ<u>how your computer or toilet works</u>(당신의 컴퓨터 혹은 변기가 어떻게 작동하는지); you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - ⓒ<u>essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work</u>(근본적으로 기술과 상호작용하는 방법보다는 그것들이 어떻게 작동하는지이다). And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, ⓓ<u>we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation</u>.(우리는 우리의 큰 두뇌를 거대한 계산의 작은 조각에 바칠 수 있다) We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. ⓔ<u>We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains</u>(우리는 우리 사회의 집합적인 두뇌를 위한 더 큰 복잡한 계산에서 단지 우리의 역할을 하고 있는것이다).
questions.explanation: ⓒ 부분인 'how to interact with technologies rather than how they work'의 정확한 해석은 '그것들이(기술이) 어떻게 작동하는지가 아니라 근본적으로 기술과 상호작용하는 방법'입니다. 보기의 해석은 '방법보다는 ~ 작동하는지이다'라고 하여 A rather than B 구문의 선후 관계 및 핵심 의미 전달이 반대로 되어 있거나 어색하게 표현되었습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as chances for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Integrating quick exercises into your daily tasks can improve your health.
questions.summary_sentence: (A)_____________ mini-exercises into daily chores transforms routine tasks into opportunities for (B)_____________ physical activity and improved health.
questions.explanation: 일상적인 집안일에 짧은 운동을 결합(incorporating/integrating)하면 지루한 일과를 신체 활동을 강화(enhancing)하고 건강을 증진할 기회로 바꿀 수 있다는 내용이므로 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 제외하는 것 ... 강요하는
② 포함(통합)하는 것 ... 향상시키는
③ 수용하는 것 ... 약화시키는
④ 참여시키는 것 ... 파괴하는
⑤ 분리하는 것 ... 해치는

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me." that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
options: ① The Flaws of Eyewitness Testimony
② The Science of Logical Thinking in Recognitions
③ The Power of First Impressions in Decision-Making
④ The Role of Careful Deliberation in Accurate Decisions
⑤ How Detailed Discussions Improve Identification Accuracy
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 신중한 숙고나 논리적인 정당화보다 무의식적인 첫인상이나 즉각적인 직관이 더 정확할 수 있다는 것입니다. 따라서 '의사결정에서 첫인상의 힘'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 목격자 증언의 결함
② 인식에 있어서 논리적 사고의 과학
③ 의사결정에 있어서 첫인상의 힘
④ 정확한 결정에 있어서 신중한 숙고의 역할
⑤ 상세한 토론이 식별 정확도를 높이는 방법

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race ─ their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't psychologically ⓐ<u>suffer</u> much. In fact, ultramarathon runners ─ those people who are crazy enough to. push themselves ⓑ<u>beyond</u> the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50-100㎞ or more over many hours, talk about making ⓒ<u>friends</u> with their pain. It is often called good pain. Now, let's consider that a patient has paid for some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it. In this situation, the patient calls that ⓓ<u>destructive</u> pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues. In the end, it all comes down to our ⓔ<u>mindset</u>.
questions.explanation: 전체적인 글의 흐름은 고통을 어떻게 프레임(마음가짐)하느냐에 따라 고통의 질이 달라진다는 것입니다. ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 환자가 치료사의 깊은 압박 치료가 가치가 있다고 믿는다면(believe... will be of value), 그 고통을 파괴적인 고통이 아니라 가치 있는 고통(constructive 또는 helpful)으로 여길 것이므로 ⓓ의 'destructive'는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness.
ordered_passages: (A) However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do: why we see things as we do: and how we interact with one another.

(C) The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions.

(B) In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 사회에 떠도는 인간 본성에 대한 일반적인 설명들이 추측과 꾸며낸 이야기들의 혼합이라고 말합니다. (A)에서 'However'를 사용해 심리학은 이와 다르며 과학의 한 분야라고 대조를 이룹니다. (C)에서 (A)의 마지막 단어인 'science'를 핵심어로 받아 심리학자들이 증거를 찾는 방식임을 부연 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 'In addition to this evidence-based approach'를 통해 (C)의 내용을 요약하며 추가적인 심리학의 특징을 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 it may cease to be a story.가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Onscreen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre ─ indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming. which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, <u>it may cease to be a story</u>. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant ─ in time or in place ─ we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
options: ① Climate change will become irrelevant as other global issues take priority.
② Climate change will become so obvious that it no longer needs to be a fictional narrative.
③ Climate change will stop being a real issue for humanity.
④ Climate fiction will remain popular because it offers hope for solving the crisis.
⑤ Fictional stories about climate change will stop being produced because of its unprofitability.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화가 인류의 삶에서 주변적인 특징일 때는 허구적 이야기(기후 소설)의 소재가 될 수 있지만, 기후 변화가 너무나 거대하고 명백해져서 창문 밖으로 직접 볼 수 있는 현실이 되면 더 이상 그것을 '이야기'로 다룰 필요가 없어진다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 밑줄 친 부분은 기후 변화가 너무 명백해져서 더 이상 허구적 서사가 필요 없게 된다는 ②번의 의미와 가장 부합합니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 글로벌 이슈가 우선순위가 됨에 따라 기후 변화는 무관해질 것이다.
② 기후 변화가 너무나 명백해져서 더 이상 허구적 서사가 될 필요가 없게 될 것이다.
③ 기후 변화는 인류에게 실제적인 문제가 되는 것을 멈출 것이다.
④ 기후 소설은 위기 해결의 희망을 제공하기 때문에 계속 인기를 끌 것이다.
⑤ 기후 변화에 대한 허구적 이야기는 수익성 때문에 더 이상 제작되지 않을 것이다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The evolution of Al is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which Al exceeds human intelligence. After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When AI becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. AI and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of Al. The direction of Al's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with AI as ______________________________________________, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
options: ① a one-sided domination by humans
② a competition between rival intelligences
③ a tool-based relationship with machines
④ a collaborative existence of conscious beings
⑤ a temporary collaboration for technological progress
questions.explanation: 지문은 AI와 인간의 의식이 상호 작용하며 함께 진화할 것이라고 설명합니다. 인간의 의식이 AI에게 자극을 받고, 인간이 부여하는 가치와 윤리가 AI의 진화 방향을 결정한다는 맥락에서, AI를 단순한 기계가 아닌 의식을 가진 존재로 보고 권리를 인정하며 함께 협력하는 관계로 보아야 한다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다. 따라서 ④번 '의식 있는 존재들의 협력적 공존'이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 인간에 의한 일방적인 지배
② 경쟁 관계에 있는 지능들 사이의 경쟁
③ 기계와의 도구 기반 관계
④ 의식 있는 존재들의 협력적 공존
⑤ 기술적 진보를 위한 일시적인 협력

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory.
ordered_passages: (A) But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences.

(B) This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information ─ a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned.

(C) That is why the discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 우리가 세상을 볼 때 기젔의 지식을 통해 재구성한다는 내용입니다.(B) This is a useful trait에서 This는 주어진 글의 재구성 과정을 가리키며, 이것이 정바를 효율적으로 저장하는 유용한 특성임을 설명합니다.(A) 그러나(But) 이러한 추상적 재구성은 세상을 있는 그대로 보준 못하게 한다는 단점을 제시합니다.(C) 그것이 바로 ~한 이유이다(That is why) 구문을 통해 압서 언급한 기억의 재구성 특성 때문에 목격자 증언의 법적 우위성이 약화되었음을 결론 집니다.따라서 (B)-(A)-(C) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 Octopus에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt ─ producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
options: ① 대부분 숨어 지내며 밤에 사냥을 한다.
② 매우 뛰어난 시력을 가지고 있으며, 색과 패턴을 변화시킬 수 있다.
③ 넙치나 다른 물고기처럼 주로 해저에서만 생활한다.
④ 자신을 다른 동물처럼 변형시켜 사냥에 활용할 수 있다.
⑤ 바다뱀과 넙치처럼 변신할 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 문어가 넙치나 바다뱀의 모습을 흉내 낸다고 설명하고 있지만, 문어가 넙치처럼 '주로 해저에서만 생활한다'는 내용은 본문에서 언급되지 않았습니다. 본문은 문어의 뛰어난 위장 능력과 이를 이용한 사냥 방식에 초점을 맞추고 있습니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political ─ which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix ─ and, therefore, functionally ____________. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an abundant resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to address it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly highlights have-and-have-not inequities, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
questions.explanation: 필자는 오늘날의 물 위기가 '정치적'이라고 말하며, 이는 해결할 수 없는 불가피한 문제가 아님을 강조합니다. 즉, 충분한 자원이 있음에도 정부의 방관, 인프라 부족, 오염 등으로 인해 발생한 문제이므로, 이는 기능적으로 '선택적인(elective)' 문제, 즉 우리가 선택하고 관리할 수 있는 영역의 문제라는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 선택적인
② 불가피한
③ 끊임없는
④ 일시적인
⑤ 가상의

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up: many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
options: ① How to Choose the Right Printer Model
② The Psychology Behind Product Pricing
③ Why Consumers Prefer Expensive Items
④ The Impact of Consumer Reviews on Sales
⑤ The Benefits of Offering Only One Product Version
questions.explanation: 소비자 제품이 왜 주로 세 가지 버전으로 출시되는지에 대해 설명하는 글입니다. 가장 비싼 모델을 제시함으로써 소비자들이 중간 가격의 모델을 선택하도록 유도하는 가격 책정의 심리학적 전략(Decoy effect/Anchor effect 등)을 다루고 있으므로 '제품 가격 책정 뒤에 숨겨진 심리학'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 올바른 프린터 모델을 선택하는 방법
② 제품 가격 책정 뒤에 숨겨진 심리학
③ 소비자들이 비싼 품목을 선호하는 이유
④ 소비자 리뷰가 판매에 미치는 영향
⑤ 단 하나의 제품 버전만 제공하는 것의 이점

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
options: ① A New Golden Age of Climate Fiction
② Why Climate Fiction Will Save the World
③ The End of Climate Fiction: When Reality Takes Over
④ Hollywood's Obsession with Optimistic Climate Stories
⑤ The Future of Storytelling: How Climate Fiction Will Define Us
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기후 변화가 실재화되고 일상이 되면 더 이상 기후 소설(climate fiction)이라는 장르가 존재하기 어려워질 것이라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 창밖으로 뻔히 보이는 재앙을 굳이 허구의 이야기로 읽을 이유가 없어지기 때문에, 기후 고통이 더 이상 먼 미래나 타지의 일이 아니게 될 때 기후 소설은 장르로서의 설득력을 잃고 종말을 맞이하게 된다는 ③번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기후 소설의 새로운 황금기
② 기후 소설이 세계를 구하는 이유
③ 기후 소설의 종말: 현실이 장악할 때
④ 낙관적인 기후 이야기에 대한 할리우드의 강박
⑤ 스토리텔링의 미래: 기후 소설이 우리를 정의하는 방법

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은
questions.passage: The evolution of Al is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which Al exceeds human intelligence. (A) After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. (B) When Al becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. Al and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. (C) Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with Al, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. (D) The direction of Al's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into Al. (E) We need to see our relationship with Al as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
questions.insertion_sentence: Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of AI.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '반대로, 우리의 의식 또한 AI의 진화에 상당한 영향을 미친다'는 내용입니다. (C) 앞부분까지는 AI가 인간의 의식 진화에 미치는 영향을 설명하고 있으며, (D) 다음 문장부터는 AI의 진화 방향이 우리가 주입하는 가치와 윤리에 달려 있다는 내용이 나오므로, 전환점인 (D)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 수 없는 예시끼리 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, (A)______________________________. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
vocabulary_box: ⓐ she could make Hugh sit in a separate area for 10 minutes every time he hits his brother.
ⓑ she could let Hugh choose a small treat, like a snack or sticker, when he helps his brother instead of hitting him.
ⓒ she could take away his favorite toy when he behaves badly.
ⓓ she could give Hugh extra playtime with her whenever he shows kindness to his brother.
ⓔ she could verbally recognize and thank Hugh for being gentle with his brother.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 (A)는 '부정적인 면을 지적하는 대신 긍정적인 면에 보상을 주는 전략'의 예시가 들어가야 합니다. ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 긍정적인 행동에 대해 보상이나 칭찬을 하는 내용이므로 적절합니다. 반면, ⓐ(따로 앉히기)와 ⓒ(장난감 뺏기)는 전형적인 '부정적인 면을 지적하거나 벌을 주는' 방식이므로 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 수 없는 예시입니다.

questions.question: 18. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: When we perceive the world, we instinctively break it down into shapes, colors, and concepts shaped by our education and knowledge. Rather than directly retrieving a mental recording, we ⓐ<u>reshape</u> memories through the lens of our understanding. This ability is advantageous, as it enables more ⓑ<u>efficient</u> information storage, similar to compressing an image using JPG rather than saving it as a raw bitmap. However, individuals who ⓒ<u>lack</u> this capacity and recall everything in perfect detail often face difficulties in generalizing, learning, and forming connections between ideas. Yet, by simplifying the world into ⓓ<u>concrete</u> ideas and features, we lose the ability to perceive it as it truly is. Instead, our view is influenced by our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery (A)<u>that</u> our memories are reorganized through conceptual representations rather than replayed like a movie has significantly ⓔ<u>weakened</u> the reliability of eyewitness testimony in legal contexts. Seeing is not believing.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 지각과 기억이 있는 그대로를 기록하는 것이 아니라 교육, 지식, 개념에 의해 재구성되고 단순화된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 문맥상 우리는 세상을 있는 그대로의 구체적인 모습이 아니라 지식에 기반한 '추상적인(abstract)' 또는 '개념적인' 아이디어로 단순화하여 받아들임으로써 실제 모습을 인지하는 능력을 상실하게 된다는 내용이 되어야 하므로 '구체적인'이라는 뜻의 ⓓ concrete는 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 19. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)that과 같은 용법으로 사용된 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: When we perceive the world, we instinctively break it down into shapes, colors, and concepts shaped by our education and knowledge. Rather than directly retrieving a mental recording, we ⓐ<u>reshape</u> memories through the lens of our understanding. This ability is advantageous, as it enables more ⓑ<u>efficient</u> information storage, similar to compressing an image using JPG rather than saving it as a raw bitmap. However, individuals who ⓒ<u>lack</u> this capacity and recall everything in perfect detail often face difficulties in generalizing, learning, and forming connections between ideas. Yet, by simplifying the world into ⓓ<u>concrete</u> ideas and features, we lose the ability to perceive it as it truly is. Instead, our view is influenced by our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery (A)<u>that</u> our memories are reorganized through conceptual representations rather than replayed like a movie has significantly ⓔ<u>weakened</u> the reliability of eyewitness testimony in legal contexts. Seeing is not believing.
vocabulary_box: 가. The discovery <u>that</u> the scientists announced yesterday could lead to a cure for the disease.
나. The hope <u>that</u> they will find a solution keeps everyone motivated.
다. Psychologists are still concerned with the role <u>that</u> heredity and environment play in development.
라. We got a notice from the school <u>that</u> classes would be canceled due to the weather.
마. The doctor informed her <u>that</u> her test results were normal.
바. The idea <u>that</u> he presented at the meeting was misunderstood by most of the team.
사. What impressed me most was the fact <u>that</u> she speaks three languages fluently.
questions.explanation: 본문의 (A)that은 'The discovery'라는 명사 뒤에서 뒤의 완전한 문장을 이끌며 내용을 보충 설명하는 동격의 접속사입니다. <보기> 중 동격의 접속사로 쓰인 것은 '나(The hope)', '라(a notice)', '사(the fact)'입니다. '가', '다', '바'는 선행사를 수식하며 문장 내 목적어 역할을 대신하는 관계대명사이고, '마'는 informed의 직접목적어 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사입니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
options: ① 전통적인 의학에서는 우울증의 원인을 의식의 왜곡으로 본다.
② 뇌 물질의 불균형은 우울증이 발생하기 전에 나타난다.
③ 우울증은 세로토닌과 노르아드레날린의 감소로 인해 발생한다.
④ 의식은 뇌의 기능을 넘어서는 더 근본적인 실체이다.
⑤ 왜곡된 의식 상태는 신경전달물질의 불균형을 예방한다.
questions.explanation: 본문 중 "Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain." (우리의 의식은 뇌의 기능을 넘어서는 더 근본적인 실체이다)라는 문장이 직접적으로 언급되어 있습니다. ①, ②, ③은 전통적인 의학적 관점이거나 본문의 인과관계와 반대되는 내용이며, ⑤는 본문의 논지와 무관합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Electricity Generation from Fossil Fuels,Nuclear Energy, and Renewables, 2023 The above graph shows the electricity generation from fossil fuels, nuclear energy, and renewables in four countries in 2023. ⓐAustralia relies entirely on fossil fuels and renewables for electricity, and fossil fuels contribute over two-thirds of the total energy production. ⓑThe U.S. produces nearly one-fifth of its electricity through nuclear energy, making it the largest contributor to this category among the four countries. ⓒIn the U.K., renewable energy sources contribute less to electricity generation than both fossil fuels and nuclear energy combined. ⓓBrazil's electricity is predominantly generated from renewables, with a minimal contribution from nuclear energy. ⓔThe combined use of fossil fuels and nuclear energy in Brazil exceeds that of renewables.
questions.explanation: 지문의 문맥상 브라질은 재생 에너지(renewables)에 압도적으로 의존한다고 되어 있으므로(predominantly generated from renewables), 화석 연료와 원자력의 합계가 재생 에너지보다 클 수 없습니다. 따라서 'exceeds(초과한다)'를 사용한 ⓔ는 도표/내용상 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Digital technologies are essentially connected to metaphors, but digital metaphors are different from linguistic ones in important ways. Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. In the Shakespearean metaphor "time is a beggar," the audience is unlikely to understand the metaphor without deliberate effort and without further engaging Shakespeare's prose. Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works: normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance. Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.summary_sentence: Digital metaphors (A)__________ shape users' perceptions through technology, whereas linguistic metaphors like Shakespeare's require (B)__________ effort and engagement to uncover their meaning.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 디지털 기술 메타포는 사용자의 의미 지평을 강제로 변화시키며 능동적으로 작용한다고 했으므로 (A)에는 actively가 적절합니다. 반면, 셰익스피어의 언어적 메타포는 관객의 의도적인 노력(deliberate effort)과 사고(thought)를 필요로 하므로 (B)에는 cognitive(인지적인)가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 능동적으로 - 인지적인
② 능동적으로 - 신체적인
③ 수동적으로 - 합리적인
④ 수동적으로 - 지적인
⑤ 의도적으로 - 감정적인

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods, especially large items such as computer printers and so-called white goods: kitchen and laundry appliances that were traditionally manufactured with white enamel finishes. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. (A) If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. (B) But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up. (C) They like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. (D) They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: Why? The company doesn't expect many people to buy the third, more expensive model, but its very presence makes them choose among the alternatives.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 기업이 왜 더 비싼 세 번째 모델을 출시하는지에 대한 이유를 묻고 그 효과(다른 대안들 사이에서 선택하게 함)를 설명하고 있습니다. (B) 문장에서 세 번째 모델을 도입하면 두 번째 모델의 판매가 올라간다는 현상이 언급되었고, 주어진 문장은 그 이유(Why?)를 제시하며 뒤따르는 문장들((C) 이후)에서 소비자들이 가장 비싼 모델의 기능은 원하지만 가격 때문에 결국 중간 모델을 선택하게 된다는 상세 설명을 이끌어내고 있습니다. 따라서 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers ⓐ<u>independent</u>, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially ⓑ<u>learn</u> the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that ⓒ<u>needs</u> to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of ⓓ<u>holding</u> more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough ⓔ<u>to benefit</u> from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'independent'는 동사 'compute'를 수식해야 하는 부사 자리이므로 'independently'가 적절합니다. ⓑ 'all we have to do'가 주어로 쓰일 때 보어인 to부정사의 to는 흔히 생략되어 원형 부정사(learn)로 쓰일 수 있습니다. ⓒ 주어 'All (that needs to be transmitted)'에서 All이 사물이나 일 전체를 의미할 때는 단수 취급하므로 'needs'는 적절합니다. ⓓ 전치사 'instead of'의 목적어로 동명사 'holding'이 쓰인 것은 적절합니다. ⓔ 'well enough to-v' 구문(~할 만큼 충분히 잘)으로 'to benefit'은 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 35번]
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally elective. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an abundant resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to address it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. In both cases, as everywhere, ___________ plays out so nakedly on a stage defined by have-and-have-not inequities that the resulting drama of resource competition can hardly be called, truly, a competition: The situation is so unfair that water shortage looks more like a tool of inequality. The global result is that as many as 2.1 billion people around the world do not have access to safe drinking water, and 4.5 billion don't have safely managed water for sanitation.
questions.explanation: 지문은 물 위기가 자원 자체의 부족보다는 정치적 소홀, 인프라 미비, 불평등 등에 의해 인위적으로 만들어진 현상임을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 내용에서 물 부족이 불평등의 도구처럼 보인다는 점과 '가진 자와 가지지 못한 자'의 불공정한 상황을 언급하고 있으므로, 이러한 맥락에서 가장 적절한 단어는 '결핍(scarcity)'입니다.
options_translation: ① 풍요
② 효율성
③ 번영
④ 평등
⑤ 결핍

questions.question: 26. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 36번]
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. It's what the anthropologist Brian Hare called "survival of _____________." The result was the development of sociometer: a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive.
questions.explanation: 인간의 생존과 번영이 집단 내에서 얼마나 가치 있게 여겨지는지, 그리고 타인과의 관계를 얼마나 잘 조율하는지에 달려 있었다는 내용입니다. 공동체가 우리를 가치 있게 여기게 만드는 행동을 하도록 진화했다는 맥락에서 Brian Hare가 제안한 개념은 '다정한 자의 생존(survival of the friendliest)'입니다.
options_translation: ① 가장 나이 많은 사람
② 가장 외로운 사람
③ 가장 똑똑한 사람
④ 가장 다정한 사람
⑤ 가장 논리적인 사람

questions.question: 27. 다음 글 (A)를 읽고 한 학생이 정리하여 보고서 (B)를 작성하였다. (B)의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 내용상 어색한 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: (A) Research often yields quantitative data, such as measuring the frequency of smiles to assess happiness or the number of items recalled to evaluate memory. However, asking general questions like "How many times in a year are you sad?" can produce unreliable data due to varied personal interpretations. Instead, specific questions like "How many times in the past year did you feel so sad that you had to call in sick to work?" elicit more concrete responses. Similarly, asking "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" provides clearer insights into procrastination behaviors. Additionally, utilizing a 7-point Likert scale (completely agree, mostly agree, somewhat agree, no opinion, somewhat disagree, mostly disagree, completely disagree) allows respondents to express their opinions with greater nuance, allowing neutral stances and reducing the likelihood of forced or inaccurate answers. This approach enhances the accuracy and depth of data collected in research.↓(B)Research Report:Effective Question Design in Research[Introduction]Quantitative research collects ⓐ<u>measurable</u> data, but the way questions are framed greatly affects the ⓑ<u>reliability</u> of responses.[Findings]Broad questions often result in unclear answers due to personal interpretation. ⓒ<u>Ambiguous</u> questions help gather more accurate information. Using structured response formats, like a 7-point Likert scale, also allows for detailed and balanced answers, ⓓ<u>increasing</u> inaccuracies.[Conclusion]Improving question ⓔ<u>clarity</u> and using balanced response options help ensure research data is both ⓕ<u>precise</u> and insightful, leading to more meaningful results.
questions.explanation: 글 (A)에 따르면 더 정확한 정보를 얻기 위해서는 일반적인 질문보다 '구체적인(specific)' 질문이 필요하므로, ⓒ의 'Ambiguous(모호한)'는 문맥상 어색합니다. 또한, 리커트 척도를 사용하는 것은 부정확한 답변의 가능성을 '줄이는(reducing)' 역할을 하므로, ⓓ의 'increasing(증가시키는)' 역시 내용상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We often fail to appreciate that our understanding of people is rooted in our particular time, place and culture, and might not apply to others. Or we take for granted beliefs that people have held for millennia, without questioning where they came from. The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
options: ① Psychology is primarily about forming opinions on human behaviors based on societal beliefs.
② The main goal of psychology is to confirm universally held ideas about human nature.
③ Psychology focuses more on cultural traditions than on fundamental human processes.
④ Psychology eliminates misunderstandings about human nature by promoting societal norms.
⑤ Psychology scientifically explores human behaviors and thoughts through evidence-based approach.

questions.question: 10. Which of the underlined parts of the text below is not an appropriate use of the word in context?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an ⓒ<u>optimal</u> image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as ⓓ<u>abstract</u> ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 Elite Celebrity의 특징을 다음과 같이 정리하였다. 빈칸 (A), (B)를 윗글에서 찾아 빠짐없이 우리말로 작성하시오.
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary or mild fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having exceptional talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. Traditionally, the elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and status. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through frequent interactions with other ordinary people in digital space. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.

questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.

questions.passage: The adolescent brain doesn't fully grow until its early twenties. This means the way the adolescents' decision-making circuits integrate and process information may leave them in an ⓐ<u>unfavorable</u> situation. One of their brain regions that matures later is the prefrontal cortex, which is the control center, tasked with thinking ahead and evaluating consequences. It is the area of the brain responsible for ⓑ<u>keeping</u> you sending off an initial angry text and modifying it with kinder words. On the other hand, the limbic system develops ⓒ<u>sooner</u>, playing a central role in processing emotional responses. Because of its earlier development, it is more likely to influence decision-making. In the adolescent brain, decision-making is ⓓ<u>less</u> influenced by an awareness of the potential consequences than by emotions. These differences ⓔ<u>disturb</u> the balance between logical-based decision-making by the not-yet-mature prefrontal cortex and feeling-based decision-making ruled by the more mature limbic system. questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity.
