④ shows the level of oral hygiene you maintain
⑤ reflects underlying issues in other areas of your body
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 핵심은 구강 건강이 단순히 입안의 문제가 아니라 신체 전체의 건강과 연결되어 있다는 것입니다. 빈칸 앞의 '빙산의 일각'이라는 표현은 입에서 일어나는 일이 더 큰 문제의 일부임을 시사하므로, 구강 건강이 신체의 다른 부위의 근본적인 문제를 반영한다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 신체의 나머지 부분에 거의 영향을 미치지 않는다
② 다른 어떤 건강 상태와도 관련이 없다
③ 우리 눈에 보이는 만큼만 심각하다
④ 당신이 유지하는 구강 위생 수준을 보여준다
⑤ 신체의 다른 부위에 있는 근본적인 문제들을 반영한다

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 35번]
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to ____________________________. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
options: ① find an appropriate place to prepare for the exam
② ensure absolute time to prepare for the examination
③ differentiate between the various sections of our memory
④ strive to test our learning ability and adaptability effectively
⑤ make the most of our ability to search for materials and papers
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 벼락치기가 효과적이라고 착각하는 이유가 단기 기억(작업 기억)에 정보가 남아있는 것을 실제 장기 기억에 저장된 것으로 오해하기 때문이라고 설명합니다. 즉, 서로 다른 기억 저장 공간(단기 vs 장기)을 구분하지 못하기 때문이므로 ③번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 시험 준비를 위한 적절한 장소를 찾다
② 시험 준비를 위한 절대적인 시간을 확보하다
③ 우리 기억의 다양한 구역들을 구분하다
④ 우리의 학습 능력과 적응력을 효과적으로 테스트하려고 노력하다
⑤ 자료와 논문을 검색하는 능력을 최대한 활용하다

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 40번]
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, ________________ ____________. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
options: ① her depression makes the atmosphere optimistic
② the comparison to another makes the situation unfair
③ her irresponsibility makes the other monkey feel annoyed
④ the lack of communication has resulted in making things worse
⑤ the researcher's unplanned experiments resulted in unexpected results
questions.explanation: 카푸친 원숭이는 자신이 받는 보상(오이)이 이전과 같더라도, 옆의 원숭이가 더 좋은 보상(포도)을 받는 것을 보면 불공평함을 느끼고 화를 낸다는 내용입니다. 따라서 타인(다른 원숭이)과의 비교가 상황을 불공평하게 만든다는 ②번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그녀의 우울함이 분위기를 낙관적으로 만든다
② 타인과의 비교가 상황을 불공평하게 만든다
③ 그녀의 무책임함이 다른 원숭이를 짜증 나게 만든다
④ 의사소통의 부족이 상황을 악화시키는 결과를 초래했다
⑤ 연구자의 계획되지 않은 실험이 예상치 못한 결과를 낳았다

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Despite significant progress in facial recognition technology using deep learning in recent years, there are still some limitations in terms of _________________. These limitations are mainly due to the database used during the training process. If the database doesn't include enough examples, the system's performance can be negatively affected. For instance, a facial recognition system may perform worse if the person being identified was registered more than 10 years ago. This is because changes in the person's face, such as wrinkles or sagging skin, can occur over time, often influenced by factors like weight gain or loss. To address this issue, researchers have created models that simulate facial aging or digital de-aging to adjust for these changes and improve the system's accuracy over time.
options: ① how fast data is enrolled in it
② how effectively it uses database
③ how well it masters the training
④ how accurately it perceives people
⑤ how easily it prevents aging process
questions.explanation: 딥러닝을 이용한 안면 인식 기술이 발전했음에도 불구하고, 시간이 흐름에 따라 발생하는 얼굴의 변화(주름, 피부 처짐 등) 때문에 사람을 정확하게 인식하는 데 한계가 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 기술이 '얼마나 정확하게 사람들을 인식하는지'에 대한 한계가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 데이터가 얼마나 빨리 등록되는지
② 데이터베이스를 얼마나 효과적으로 사용하는지
③ 훈련을 얼마나 잘 숙달하는지
④ 얼마나 정확하게 사람들을 인식하는지
⑤ 노화 과정을 얼마나 쉽게 방지하는지

questions.question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows.
ordered_passages: (A) Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.

(B) The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur.

(C) At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself.
questions.explanation: 인간이 쉽게 지루함을 느끼는 현상에 대해 설명하는 글입니다. 주어진 글에서 지루함의 구체적 사례를 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 '인간은 쉽게 지루해하며 그 이유는 신경 세포에 있다'고 근거를 제시합니다. (C)에서 신경 세포가 변화하지 않는 것보다 빠르게 변화하는 것(위험 요소 등)에 더 강하게 반응하도록 진화했음을 설명하고, 마지막으로 (A)에서 지루함이 새로운 자극을 더 잘 인식하게 해주는 기제임을 결론으로 제시하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Early models of cultural evolution often compared culture to genes, using ideas from population genetics to explain how culture spreads and changes.
ordered_passages: (A) However, these models needed to be adjusted because cultural transmission works differently from genetic inheritance. For instance, if two parents have different versions of a cultural trait, their child may not necessarily inherit one version more than the other.

(B) Additionally, children can learn cultural traits not only from their parents but also from other adults and peers, meaning that the spread of a cultural trait depends on more than just the traits of the parents.
(C) In these models, cultural processes like transmission, innovation, and selection were seen as similar to genetic processes like inheritance, mutation, and natural selection.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 초기 문화 진화 모델이 문화를 유전자에 비유했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C)에서 '이러한 모델들에서(In these models)'라는 표현을 통해 문화 과정이 유전 과정과 유사하게 간주되었음을 부연 설명합니다. (A)에서 '하지만(However)'을 통해 문화 전승이 유전과 다르기 때문에 조정이 필요하다는 반론을 제기하며 구체적 사례를 듭니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 '게다가(Additionally)'를 통해 부모 외의 타인에게서도 문화를 배울 수 있다는 추가적인 차이점을 설명하는 (C)-(A)-(B) 순서가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A fascinating feature of the visual system is its ability to adapt. Psychologist George M. Stratton demonstrated this through an impressive self-experiment.
ordered_passages: (A) However, over time, his visual system adapted to the altered stimuli from reality, allowing him to function normally in his environment and even perceive it as upright when he focused. When he removed the reversing glasses, new problems arose, such as mistakenly using the wrong hand to reach for objects.

(B) He wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally flipped his view of the world upside down. Initially, this caused significant difficulties; something as simple as eating with a fork became a challenge.
(C) Thankfully, Stratton's perception adjusted again, and he did not have to rely on the glasses permanently. Within a day, everything returned to normal for him.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 시각 체계의 적응 능력에 관한 Stratton의 실험을 소개합니다. (B)에서 그가 세상을 거꾸로 보이게 하는 안경을 쓴 실험의 시작과 초기 어려움을 설명합니다. (A)에서 '하지만(However)' 시간이 흐르며 그의 시각 체계가 적응하여 정상적으로 활동하게 되었고, 안경을 벗었을 때 다시 새로운 문제가 생겼음을 언급합니다. (C)에서 다행히 지각이 다시 조정되어 모든 것이 정상으로 돌아왔다는 결말로 마무리되는 (B)-(A)-(C) 순서가 가장 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Some nations have proposed stricter guidelines for determining brain death, particularly when organ transplantation is involved. (A) In several European countries, laws specify that a full team of doctors must reach a consensus on the diagnosis of brain death in potential organ donors. (B) These strict regulations aim to address public concerns about the possibility of premature brain death diagnoses made to obtain organs. (C) However, it is debatable whether such measures actually reduce public suspicion or instead worsen it. (D) To maintain consistency, at the very least, the criteria for diagnosing brain death in organ donors should be the same as those used for individuals whose bodies are destined for immediate burial or cremation. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: They may even reinforce the mistaken belief that diagnosing brain death is an imprecise and unreliable process.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'They'는 (C) 문장에서 언급된 'such measures'(장기 기증 시 뇌사 판정을 엄격히 하는 조치들)를 가리킵니다. (C) 문장에서 이러한 조치들이 대중의 의심을 오히려 악화시킬 수 있다고 한 뒤, 주어진 문장에서 뇌사 판정이 부정확하다는 잘못된 믿음을 강화할 수 있다는 구체적인 악영향을 설명합니다. 따라서 (D) 자리에 들어가는 것이 흐름상 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Gregory Bateson, an anthropologist, suggests that we are inclined to understand the world by focusing on certain details. (A) For example, with platypuses, we could look very closely at their fur and see each hair as unique. (B) We can switch between these different ways of looking, with additional equipment and skills. (C) Nevertheless, we can only focus on one perspective at a time. (D) We are able to look closely at individual hairs, to pay attention to what unites them into a single species, or to think about the platypus as part of a whole system. (E) Each perspective highlights some things and leaves out others.
questions.insertion_sentence: Alternatively, we could step back and see the platypus as just one animal, or ever think of it as part of a bigger group like a species or an ecosystem.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 'Alternatively'(그 대신에)를 사용하여 앞서 언급된 '세부적인 털 하나하나를 보는 관점'(A)에 대비되는 '더 큰 집단의 일부로 보는 거시적인 관점'을 제시합니다. (B) 이후부터는 이러한 '서로 다른 관점 사이의 전환'에 대해 설명하고 있으므로, 미시적 관점(A)과 그에 대한 대안인 거시적 관점을 모두 보여준 직후인 (B) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen ⓐ<u>that all marine animals breathe to stay alive</u>. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen ⓑ<u>than warm water is</u> - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, ⓒ<u>as global warming is raised</u> the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists ⓓ<u>have analyzed data indicating which</u> the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. ⓔ<u>Falling oxygen levels in water have</u> the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: 어법상 어색한 것은 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ로 총 3개입니다.ⓑ: 앞의 'holds'(일반동사)를 대신하는 대동사가 필요하므로 'is'가 아니라 'does'가 되어야 합니다.ⓒ: '온도를 높이다'라는 타동사 의미가 필요하며, 현재 진행형으로 목적어(the temperature)를 취하고 있으므로 수동태 'is raised'가 아니라 능동태인 'is raising'이 되어야 합니다.ⓓ: 'indicating' 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어지므로 의문사/관계사 'which'가 아니라 명사절 접속사 'that'이 적절합니다.(ⓐ는 목적격 관계대명사, ⓔ는 동명사 주어에 따른 복수 명사구 수일치로 적절함)

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, ⓐ<u>they simply run the race lay out for them</u>. They ⓑ<u>do enough well in school to keep advancing</u>. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ends with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now ⓒ<u>lack a road map described the right ways</u> to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when the journey really begins. When school is finished, your growth becomes voluntary. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and ⓓ<u>devote thought, time, and energy to it</u>. Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career ⓔ<u>are likely to stop progress as a result</u>.
questions.explanation: 어법상 어색한 것은 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ로 총 4개입니다.ⓐ: 'race'를 수식하는 과거분사가 필요하므로 'lay'를 'laid'로 고쳐야 합니다.ⓑ: 부사 'well'을 수식하는 'enough'는 뒤에서 수식해야 하므로 'well enough'가 되어야 합니다.ⓒ: 'road map'이 '올바른 방법을 설명하는' 능동의 의미로 수식해야 하므로 'described'를 'describing'으로 고쳐야 합니다.ⓔ: 'stop'은 동명사를 목적어로 취하여 '~하는 것을 멈추다'라는 의미를 만들거나, '~하기 위해 멈추다'의미의 to부정사를 쓸 수 있는데, 맥락상 '발전하는 것을 멈추다'이므로 'progressing'이 적절합니다.(ⓓ는 devote A to B 구조로 적절함)

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. ⓐ<u>This insecurity naturally stem from their attachment to their possessions</u>. ⓑ<u>It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time</u>. At human beings are emotional animal, they give meaning to the things around them. ⓒ<u>So, the question that arouses here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist</u>? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. ⓓ<u>You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will overcome by the joy of clarity</u>. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. ⓔ<u>They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff which is unused or not going to be used in the near future</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 주어가 This insecurity(단수)이므로 stems로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓒ arouse는 타동사이므로 '발생하다'라는 의미의 자동사 arise의 현재분사/단수형인 arises가 적절합니다. ⓓ this feeling(이 감정)은 기쁨에 의해 '극복되는' 것이므로 수동태인 will be overcome으로 고쳐야 합니다. 따라서 ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓓ 세 개가 어색합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: In statistics, the law of large numbers ⓐ<u>explains</u> a situation in which to have more data is better for making predictions. According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to ⓑ<u>match to</u> the true state of the world. For instance, on your first encounter with the game of roulette, you may have beginner's luck after you ⓒ<u>bet on</u> 7. But the more often you repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning, ⓓ<u>which</u> means that your luck will at some point fade away. Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances of ⓔ<u>drivers'</u> causing accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to balance individual losses.
questions.explanation: match는 타동사로 쓰여 뒤에 전치사 없이 목적어를 취하므로 match the true state가 되어야 합니다. match to는 어법상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 These questions had nothing to do with those from the first part가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In a study, participants were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half of them were allowed to search for the answers online, while the other half had to rely on their own knowledge. In the second part of the study, all participants were given a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" <u>These questions had nothing to do with those from the first part</u>. Logically, you'd expect both groups to feel equally confident or uncertain about answering the new questions. However, those who had used the internet earlier rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even for questions they hadn't looked up. The findings suggest that merely having access to information online can inflate a person's confidence in their intellectual abilities.
options: ① The Internet users had no real advantage over the non-users.
② The second set of questions was designed to be easier than the first.
③ Both sets of questions required specialized knowledge in unrelated fields.
④ Participants were allowed to use the internet for both sets of questions.
⑤ The first and second sets of questions were answered by different participants.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 두 번째 질문 세트가 첫 번째 질문 세트와 관련이 없음을 의미합니다. 논리적으로는 두 그룹의 자신감이 같아야 하지만, 인터넷을 사용한 그룹은 관련 없는 질문에 대해서도 자신감이 높게 나타났습니다. 이는 인터넷 사용자가 비사용자에 비해 실질적인 지식 우위(advantage)가 없었음에도 불구하고 자신의 지적 능력을 과신했음을 시사하므로 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인터넷 사용자가 비사용자보다 실제적인 이점을 가지고 있지 않았다.
② 두 번째 질문 세트는 첫 번째 질문 세트보다 더 쉽게 설계되었다.
③ 두 질문 세트 모두 관련 없는 분야의 전문 지식을 필요로 했다.
④ 참가자들은 두 질문 세트 모두에 대해 인터넷을 사용하는 것이 허용되었다.
⑤ 첫 번째와 두 번째 질문 세트는 서로 다른 참가자들에 의해 답변되었다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
questions.summary_sentence: Plato argued that physical objects like circles are (A)__________, and they poorly reflect ideals, unchanging Forms in a(n) (B)__________ reality, which he considered the true essence of existence.
questions.explanation: 플라톤에 따르면 우리가 보는 현실의 원과 같은 물리적 대상들은 불완전하고 결함이 있습니다(defective). 이러한 대상들은 감각을 넘어선 보이지 않는(invisible) 실제인 형상(Forms)의 세계를 제대로 반영하지 못합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '결함이 있는' 뜻의 defective, (B)에는 '보이지 않는' 뜻의 invisible이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 결함 있는 - 명백한
② 절대적인 - 보이지 않는
③ 결함 있는 - 보이지 않는
④ 불완전한 - 인지 가능한
⑤ 변하기 쉬운 - 예측 불가능한

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has ⓐ<u>profound</u> changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing ⓑ<u>that</u> our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue ⓒ<u>stick out</u> each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, ⓓ<u>in which</u> we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are ⓔ<u>born with</u> or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply ____________________.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런의 발견과 이를 통한 '관찰을 통한 학습(learning by observation)'과 '모방(imitation)'에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 아이들이 부모의 행동을 보고 따라 하는 예시들을 통해, 우리가 단순히 타인을 지켜봄으로써(watching others) 많은 것을 배울 수 있다는 결론을 도출할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 논문을 읽음으로써
② 학교에 입학함으로써
③ 규칙을 제한함으로써
④ 타인을 지켜봄으로써
⑤ 동물을 모방함으로써

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has ⓐ<u>profound</u> changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing ⓑ<u>that</u> our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue ⓒ<u>stick out</u> each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, ⓓ<u>in which</u> we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are ⓔ<u>born with</u> or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply ____________________.
questions.explanation: ⓐ profound -> profoundly (동사 changed를 수식하므로 부사가 필요함)ⓑ that -> what (observing의 목적어 역할을 하며 뒤에 do의 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 문장이 오므로 관계대명사 what이 적절함)ⓒ stick out: 지각동사 see + 목적어 + 동사원형/현재분사 구조로 올바름ⓓ in which: 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오고 장소/환경의 개념인 cultures를 수식하므로 올바름ⓔ born with: '~을 가지고 태어나다'라는 의미로 전치사 with의 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 문장이 관계대명사절로 선행사 behavior를 수식하므로 올바름따라서 어색한 것은 ⓐ, ⓑ로 총 2개입니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 바르게 쓰인 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them</u>. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - ⓑ<u>a greenness what is just as real as the leaves</u>. ⓒ<u>Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer</u>. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and ⓓ<u>so did everything else</u>. ⓔ<u>They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people seeing it</u>. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cezanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 바름: 'the view'와 동격의 that절이 쓰였으며, color is...로 완전한 문장이 연결됨.ⓑ 틀림: a greenness를 선행사로 가지며 주어 역할을 하는 관계대명사가 필요하므로 what이 아니라 which 또는 that을 써야 함.ⓒ 바름: argue의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절 접속사 that과 not A but B 구조가 잘 쓰임.ⓓ 틀림: 앞 문장의 would be colorless를 대신하는 'so + 동사 + 주어' 구문이므로 did가 아니라 would를 써서 so would everything else가 되어야 함.ⓔ 틀림: 분사 seeing이 the people을 수식하는 것은 맞지만, 문맥상 '색깔'이라는 것은 없고 오직 그것을 보는 사람들만 '있을 뿐이다'라는 구조에서 seeing 보다는 '색을 인식하는 행위'에 초점이 맞춰져 있으나, 결정적으로 ⓓ와 ⓑ가 확실히 틀렸고 ⓐ, ⓒ가 확실히 맞으므로 개수 판단 시 유의해야 함 (원문 확인 시 ⓔ는 문법적으로는 people을 수식하는 분사로 볼 수 있으나 전체 개수 상 2개가 정답으로 제시됨).

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 내용을 다음과 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness what is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so did everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people seeing it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cezanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.summary_sentence: There are two perspectives about whether color is an objective property of things or a subjective experience created in the mind. Both views are correct because color is created when light from the world, which is a(n) (A)__________ property of things, is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain, which is (B)__________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 색이 사물의 객관적 특성이면서 동시에 뇌에 의해 해석되는 주관적 경험이라는 두 관점을 모두 인정합니다. (A)에는 세상으로부터 온 빛, 즉 사물의 '객관적(objective)' 속성을 설명하는 말이 들어가야 하고, (B)에는 뇌에 의해 해석되는 과정, 즉 '개인적인(personal)' 혹은 주관적인 측면을 설명하는 말이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 주관적인 - 개인적인
② 주관적인 - 보편적인
③ 객관적인 - 공정한
④ 객관적인 - 개인적인
⑤ 객관적인 - 편향되지 않은

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The decrease in the variety of our food is a result of human actions. The greatest loss of crop diversity ⓐ<u>was appeared</u> in the years following the Second World War. To prevent widespread hunger, scientists developed ways ⓑ<u>in which</u> they grow large amounts of grains like rice and wheat. As a result, many traditional crop varieties were replaced with a few highly productive ⓒones. This strategy initially succeeded, leading to a threefold increase in grain production, while the world's population more than doubled between 1970 and 2020. However, the danger of growing fewer types of crops ⓓ<u>lies</u> in the fact that they are less likely to survive disasters. A global food system ⓔ<u>relies</u> on just a small number of plants is at greater risk from diseases, pests, and extreme weather.
options: ① Human activities threatened the variety of food.
② Crop diversity significantly decreased during World War II.
③ Rice and wheat could feed a large number of people.
④ Cultivation of uniform crops contributed to population growth at the beginning.
⑤ A limited range of crops makes a global food system vulnerable to disasters.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 작물 다양성의 가장 큰 손실은 '2차 세계대전 이후 수년간(in the years following the Second World War)' 발생했다고 언급되어 있습니다. ②번의 '2차 세계대전 동안(during World War II)'은 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 인간의 활동은 식량의 다양성을 위협했다.
② 작물 다양성은 제2차 세계대전 중에 현저하게 감소했다.
③ 쌀과 밀은 많은 사람들을 먹여 살릴 수 있었다.
④ 단일 작물의 재배는 초기에 인구 증가에 기여했다.
⑤ 제한된 범위의 작물은 세계 식량 시스템을 재난에 취약하게 만든다.

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는? [3.0점]
questions.passage: The decrease in the variety of our food is a result of human actions. The greatest loss of crop diversity ⓐ<u>was appeared</u> in the years following the Second World War. To prevent widespread hunger, scientists developed ways ⓑ<u>in which</u> they grow large amounts of grains like rice and wheat. As a result, many traditional crop varieties were replaced with a few highly productive ⓒones. This strategy initially succeeded, leading to a threefold increase in grain production, while the world's population more than doubled between 1970 and 2020. However, the danger of growing fewer types of crops ⓓ<u>lies</u> in the fact that they are less likely to survive disasters. A global food system ⓔ<u>relies</u> on just a small number of plants is at greater risk from diseases, pests, and extreme weather.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'appear'는 자동사이므로 수동태로 쓸 수 없습니다. 'was appeared'를 'appeared'로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓔ 문장의 주어는 'A global food system'이며 본동사는 뒤에 있는 'is'입니다. 따라서 'relies'는 주어를 수식하는 현재분사 'relying' 혹은 관계대명사절 'that relies'가 되어야 합니다. ⓑ 'ways'를 수식하는 관계사 'in which'는 적절합니다. ⓒ 'ones'는 앞의 'crop varieties'를 대신하는 부정대명사로 적절합니다. ⓓ 주어 'the danger'에 일치시킨 단수 동사 'lies'는 적절합니다. 따라서 어색한 것은 ⓐ, ⓔ 총 2개입니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
options: ① 식량 생산을 위해 생산성이 높은 소품종에 집중한 결과 식량 다양성이 감소하여 위험에 처하게 되었다.
② 2차 세계대전 이후 기아 문제 해결을 위해 농작물의 생산성을 높이는 연구가 과학계의 최우선 과제였다.
③ 기후 변화의 영향에 따른 농산품 공급-수요의 여러 대안적인 시나리오들을 검토할 필요가 있다.
④ 식량문제 해결을 위해 적극적으로 관심을 가지고 주도적으로 먹거리를 선택하려는 노력을 해야한다.
⑤ 자연 생태계를 보존하면서 누구에게나 평등하게 제공되는 지속 가능한 식량생산 시스템이 필요하다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 2차 세계대전 이후 기아 문제를 해결하기 위해 소수의 고생산성 품종에 집중한 결과, 전 세계적으로 작물의 다양성이 감소하게 되었음을 설명하고 있습니다. 이러한 단일화된 식량 시스템은 질병, 해충, 기후 변화와 같은 재난 상황에서 생존 가능성을 낮추는 위험을 초래한다는 것이 핵심 내용입니다. 따라서 요지로 가장 적절한 것은 1번입니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.5점]
questions.passage: Nearly everything that enters your body passes through your mouth, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. ⓐA healthy mouth is key to your body's functions, ensuring air flows freely to your lungs and keeping harmful microorganisms from entering the bloodstream. ⓑThe way your teeth are lined up can also affect how you speak and chew, influencing your daily life in small ways. ⓒFrom birth, the state of your oral health shapes your overall well-being and can affect your health for life. ⓓWhat happens in your mouth often reflects what's happening in your body, serving as an early sign of health issues. ⓔPoor oral health can lead to serious problems, as bacteria in the mouth can enter the bloodstream and increase the risk of systemic diseases.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구강 건강이 전신 건강 및 신체 기능에 미치는 중대한 영향에 대해 다루고 있습니다. ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 입이 전신 건강의 지표이거나 전신 질환의 통로가 된다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 반면, ⓑ는 치아의 배열이 말하기와 씹기에 미치는 영향이라는 지엽적인 일상 생활의 불편함을 언급하고 있어 전체적인 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.5점]
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? ⓐThe answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. ⓑAt the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. ⓒWe probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. ⓓPumas have been one of the most attracting predators at zoos. ⓔBoredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 쉽게 지루함을 느끼는 신경학적 원인과 그 진화론적 이점(변화하는 새로운 자극에 더 잘 집중하기 위함)을 설명하고 있습니다. ⓓ는 단순히 퓨마가 동물원에서 인기 있는 포식자라는 사실을 언급하고 있으므로, 신경 세포의 반응이나 지루함의 진화적 배경을 설명하는 전체 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba dominated the world baseball scene, winning 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. The Cuban team was famous for their ⓐ<u>striking</u> uniforms, entirely covered in red - a bold contrast to the more conservative North American styles, which featured grey or white pants. Beyond their athletic superiority, the Cubans projected an air of ⓑ<u>dominance</u>, amplified by the vivid color of their uniforms. Even before a game began, opposing teams often found themselves ⓒ<u>intimidated</u>. A few years ago, however, Cuba modernized its uniform style, perhaps in an effort to conform to global trends. Interestingly, the national team's performance has declined since this change. The country that once ruled international baseball for decades has ⓓ<u>expanded</u> its former glory since that uniform change. Traditions are vital for a team's ⓔ<u>identity</u>; while adapting a team's brand or image to modern times is natural, abandoning or neglecting its roots can sometimes lead to unintended consequences.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 쿠바 야구팀이 유니폼을 현대적으로 바꾼 이후 성적이 하락하고 과거의 영광을 잃어가고 있다는 흐름이 되어야 합니다. ⓓ의 expanded(확장하다)는 흐름상 적절하지 않으며, '잃다(lost)'나 '훼손하다(diminished)' 정도의 단어가 와야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of ⓐ<u>existence</u>, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their ⓑ<u>status</u>. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community ⓒ<u>appreciate</u> us and less of what doesn't. And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from ⓓ<u>outside</u>. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less ⓔ<u>convincing</u>.
questions.explanation: 자부심, 수치심과 같은 감정들은 우리가 사회적 압력에 반응하고 있다는 것을 의식하지 못하게 하고, 마치 그 동기가 우리 '내부(inside)'에서 오는 것처럼 느끼게 설계되어 있습니다. 만약 외부의 압력(outside) 때문이라고 느낀다면 우리의 행동이 진정성 있게 보이지 않을 것이기 때문입니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The middle option bias, often referred to as the "Goldilocks effect," is a psychological phenomenon where people tend to choose the middle option when presented with a range of choices. This is because the middle option is perceived as a safe choice, avoiding the ⓐ<u>extremes</u>. For example, medium popcorn is the most popular size in cinemas, and tipping systems often feature odd amounts to highlight a ⓑ<u>reasonable</u> choice. This bias is widely exploited in marketing strategies. By introducing a high-priced option, businesses can make the middle-priced option become ⓒ<u>overlooked</u>. A classic example of this is a marketing study conducted by economist Tversky. When consumers were given a choice between a $110 microwave and a $180 microwave, only 43% chose the more expensive one. However, when a third, even more expensive option was added, the sales of the $180 microwave surged to 60%. The underlying reason for this bias is our innate desire for choice. The ability to choose makes us feel ⓓ<u>empowered</u> and inclined to make a decision. The Goldilocks effect not only influences our choice of a specific option but also ⓔ<u>increases</u> the likelihood of making a purchase in the first place.
questions.explanation: 마케팅 전략에서 아주 비싼 옵션을 도입하는 이유는 중간 가격의 옵션을 '간과되게(overlooked)' 만드는 것이 아니라, 오히려 더 매력적으로 보이게 하거나 '돋보이게' 만들어 소비자가 선택하도록 유도하기 위함입니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. They do well enough in school to keep ⓐ<u>advancing</u>. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ⓑ<u>ends</u> with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now ⓒ<u>have</u> a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when the journey really ⓓ<u>begins</u>. When school is finished, your growth becomes ⓔ<u>voluntary</u>. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career are likely to stop progressing as a result.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 많은 사람이 대학을 졸업하면 배움이 끝난다고 생각하고, 사회가 정해준 단계를 다 밟은 후에는 더 이상 앞으로 나아가고 성장할 방법을 알려주는 로드맵이 '없는(lack)' 상태가 됩니다. 대학 교육까지가 남들이 정해준 길이고, 그 이후부터는 스스로 성장을 책임져야 한다는 맥락이므로 ⓒ have는 문맥상 어긋납니다.
options_translation: ① 나아가는
② 끝나는
③ 가지다
④ 시작되다
⑤ 자발적인

questions.question: 10. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: A ball thrown into the air is acted upon by the initial force given it, persisting as inertia of movement and ①<u>tending</u> to carry it in the same straight line, and by the constant pull of gravity downward, as well as by the resistance of the air. It moves, accordingly, in a curved path. Now the path does not represent the working of any particular force; there is simply the combination of the three elementary forces ②<u>mentioned</u>; but in a real sense, there is something in the total action besides the isolated action of three forces, namely, their joint action. In the same way, when two or more human individuals are together, their mutual relationships and their arrangement into a group ③<u>are</u> things which would not be revealed if we confined our attention to each individual separately. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that some of the tendencies to action of the individual are related definitely to other persons, and could not be aroused except by other persons ④<u>acted</u> as stimuli. An individual in complete isolation would not reveal their competitive tendencies, their tendencies towards the opposite sex, their protective tendencies towards children. This shows ⑤<u>that</u> the traits of human nature do not fully appear until the individual is brought into relationships with other individuals.
questions.explanation: ④번의 'acted'는 앞의 'other persons'를 수식하는 분사 구문으로, 타인이 자극제로서 작용하는 눕동의 관계이므로 홄재분사인 'acting'으로 고쳐야 합니다. (except by other persons acting as stimuli: 자극제로서 작용하는 타인들에 의해서만)

questions.question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity.
ordered_passages: (A) And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation.

(B) We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.

(C) As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers.

(D) You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works: you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 정보, 시간, 인지 능력의 한계를 언급했습니다. (C)에서 우리가 독립적으로 답을 계산할 자원이 부족하기 때문에 계산을 인구 전체에 분산시킨다는 내용이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다. (D)는 그 구체적인 예시로 컴퓨터나 화장실의 작동 원리를 알 필요 없이 인터페이스만 알면 된다는 내용을 다룹니다. (A)는 'And so'로 시작하며 우리가 가진 정신적 능력보다 더 많은 정보를 보유하는 대신 거대한 계산의 작은 부분에 뇌를 헌신할 수 있다는 결론을 제시하고, (B)에서 우리는 전체에 기여하는 작은 계산을 하며 사회의 집단 지성(collective brains)의 일부 역할을 수행한다는 최종 정리로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles.
ordered_passages: (A) So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks.

(B) He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time.

(C) Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses, and that true knowledge comes from understanding these perfect Forms rather than the imperfect physical world.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 원과 같은 기하학적 대상을 통해 플라톤의 실재론을 설명하기 시작합니다. (B)에서 '원동은 무엇인가?'라는 질문을 던지고 물리적 원은 결코 완벽하지 않다는 점을 지적합니다. (A)에서는 그렇다면 어떻게 완벽한 원에 대해 말할 수 있는가라는 의문을 제기하며, 우리가 보는 세상은 '형상(Forms)'이라는 보이지 않는 실재의 불완전한 투영이라는 답을 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 형상이야말로 보이지 않는 완벽한 세계에 존재하는 진정한 실재이며 진정한 지식은 이를 이해하는 데서 온다는 결론으로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally elective. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an abundant resource made scarce through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to address it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they deliver to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the selective scarcity clearly highlights have-and-have-not inequities, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
options: ① how infrastructure influences people and cities
② new technologies to take care of the water crisis
③ the way life differs in Brazil and the United States
④ relationship between contamination and urbanization
⑤ truth over the water crisis and the problem of inequality
questions.explanation: 이 글은 현대의 물 위기가 정치적 원인으로 인해 발생하는 것이며, 정부의 방치와 무관심으로 인해 자원이 부족해지고 이것이 결국 빈부격차와 불평등의 문제를 심화시키는 현상임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 물 위기라고 불리는 현상 이면에 가려진 실체(정치적 원인으로 인한 인위적 결핍)와 그로 인한 불평등 문제를 다루는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기반 시설이 사람과 도시에 미치는 영향
② 물 위기를 해결하기 위한 새로운 기술들
③ 브라질과 미국 삶의 방식 차이
④ 오염과 도시화 사이의 관계
⑤ 물 위기에 대한 진실과 불평등의 문제

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In his Cornell laboratory, David Dunning conducted experimental tests of eyewitness testimony and found evidence that a careful deliberation of facial features and a detailed discussion of selection procedures can actually be a sign of an inaccurate identification. It's when people find themselves unable to explain why they recognize the person, saying things like "his face just popped out at me," that they tend to be accurate more often. Sometimes our first, immediate, automatic reaction to a situation is the truest interpretation of what our mind is telling us. That very first impression can also be more accurate about the world than the deliberative, reasoned self-narrative can be. In his book Blink, Malcolm Gladwell describes a variety of studies in psychology and behavioral economics that demonstrate the superior performance of relatively unconscious first guesses compared to logical step-by-step justifications for a decision.
options: ① need for extensive training in facial recognition
② memory improvement techniques for eyewitnesses
③ reliability of eyewitness testimony in criminal cases
④ accuracy of witness identification through confidence
⑤ effectiveness of intuitive judgments over detailed analysis
questions.explanation: 이 글은 목격자 증언 실험을 통해, 얼굴 특징을 신중하게 숙고하고 논리적으로 설명하는 것보다 직관적으로 "그냥 떠올랐다"고 말할 때 판별의 정확도가 더 높다는 점을 설명합니다. 즉, 논리적인 단계별 정당화보다 무의식적인 첫 추측이나 직관적인 판단이 더 우수한 성과를 낼 수 있다는 내용이므로 주제는 상세한 분석보다 직관적 판단의 효과성입니다.
options_translation: ① 안면 인식에 있어서 광범위한 훈련의 필요성
② 목격자를 위한 기억력 향상 기법
③ 형사 사건에서 목격자 증언의 신뢰성
④ 자신감을 통한 목격자 식별의 정확성
⑤ 상세한 분석보다 직관적 판단의 효과성

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file, representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony.
options: ① The Nature of Human Memory: Efficiency at the Cost of Accuracy
② Memory: The Hidden Pathways That Make Us Human
③ Why Eyewitness Testimony Is an Important Area of Psychological Research
④ Is Memory Loss a Normal Part of Aging?
⑤ How Can You Memorize Any Difficult Things Easily
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 기억이 있는 그대로를 재생하는 것이 아니라 정보를 효율적으로 저장하기 위해 추상적인 개념으로 재구성(reconstruct)된다고 설명합니다. 이러한 방식은 효율적이지만 세상을 있는 그대로 보는 정확성을 희생하게 만든다는 점을 JPG 압축 방식에 비유하고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로는 정확성을 희생하여 효율성을 얻는 인간 기억의 본질이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간 기억의 본질: 정확성을 희생한 효율성
② 기억: 우리를 인간으로 만드는 숨겨진 경로들
③ 왜 목격자 증언이 심리학 연구의 중요한 분야인가
④ 기억 상실은 노화의 정상적인 부분인가?
⑤ 어떻게 하면 어려운 것들을 쉽게 암기할 수 있는가?

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How much we suffer relates to how we frame the pain in our mind. When 1500m runners push themselves into extreme pain to win a race - their muscles screaming and their lungs exploding with oxygen deficit, they don't psychologically suffer much. In fact, ultra-marathon runners - those people who are crazy enough to push themselves beyond the normal boundaries of human endurance, covering distances of 50-100km or more over many hours, talk about making friends with their pain. When a patient has paid for some form of passive back pain therapy and the practitioner pushes deeply into a painful part of a patient's back to mobilise it, the patient calls that good pain if he or she believes this type of deep pressure treatment will be of value, even though the practitioner is pushing right into the patient's sore tissues.
options: ① Pain as Progress: The Crucial Role of Discomfort in Growth
② Psychology of Pain: How Perception Shapes Our Suffering
③ Various Reasons That We Have to Endure Our Pain
④ How Far Can Humans Push Themselves?
⑤ The Science Behind Physiological Pain
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 우리가 겪는 고통의 정도가 통증을 마음속에서 어떻게 프레임화(인식)하느냐에 달려 있다는 것입니다. 달리기 선수나 치료를 받는 환자의 사례를 통해 통증을 가치 있는 것으로 인식할 때 심리적 고통이 줄어든다는 점을 보여주므로 '통증의 심리학: 인식이 우리의 고통을 어떻게 형성하는가'가 정답입니다.
options_translation: 성장으로서의 통증: 성장에서 불편함의 결정적 역할
통증의 심리학: 인식이 우리의 고통을 어떻게 형성하는가
우리가 통증을 견뎌야 하는 다양한 이유들
인간은 어디까지 스스로를 밀어붙일 수 있는가?
생리적 통증 이면의 과학

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" (A) Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so. (B) Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" (C) You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions. (D) But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. (E) The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
questions.insertion_sentence: These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 두 번째 단계의 질문들이 첫 번째 단계와 무관하며, 따라서 인터넷을 사용했던 사람들에게 어떠한 이점도 없었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C) 앞부분에서 새로운 질문 세트가 제시된 직후에 이 문장이 위치하여 '인터넷 사용 유무에 상관없이 두 그룹의 확신도가 같을 것이라고 생각할 수 있다'는 내용과 논리적으로 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 10월 29번]
questions.passage: Metaphors not only enhance our language but also our cognitive abilities, allowing us to think more creatively and understand more deeply. The domain of computing is particularly rich in metaphor, for both cognitive and aesthetic reasons. (A) While digital technologies are fundamentally linked to metaphors, there are significant distinctions between digital and linguistic metaphors. (B) Linguistic metaphors are passive, in the sense that the audience needs to choose to actively enter the world proposed by metaphor. (C) The metaphor "time is a beggar" in Shakespeare's work isn't readily understood; it necessitates both intellectual effort and a more in-depth study of his writing. (D) Technological metaphors, on the other hand, are active (and often imposing) in the sense that they are realized in digital artifacts that are actively doing things, forcefully changing a user's meaning horizon. (E) Shakespeare, on the other hand, is beloved in part because the meaning of his works is not immediately obvious and requires some thought on the part of the audience.
questions.insertion_sentence: Technological creators cannot generally afford to require their potential audience to wonder how the metaphor works; normally the selling point is that the usefulness of the technology is obvious at first glance.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 기술 제작자들이 청중에게 은유가 어떻게 작동하는지 궁금해하게 만들 여유가 없으며, 기술의 유용성이 첫눈에 명확해야 한다는 점을 강조합니다. 이는 (D) 문장에서 설명한 '능동적이고 강요적인' 기술적 은유의 특성을 보완하는 내용입니다. (E) 앞에서 기술적 은유의 즉각적인 명확성을 설명하고, (E) 뒤에서 '반면에(on the other hand)'를 사용하여 세익스피어의 작품이 즉각적이지 않고 생각이 필요하다는 대조를 이루는 것이 논리적입니다. 따라서 (E) 자리에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 10월 20번]
questions.passage: Many of us struggle to find time for exercise due to work commitments and family obligations, making it challenging to fit dedicated workouts into our packed schedules. (A) However, what if exercise could easily fit into your daily routine, turning ordinary moments into opportunities for physical activity? (B) Household chores, such as washing dishes or taking out the trash, are inevitable and an essential part of daily life. (C) For instance, while waiting for your morning kettle to boil, you could do a few squats or wall push-ups to engage your muscles. (D) Incorporating mini-exercises into household chores allows you to multitask effectively, combining productivity with physical wellness. (E) By adopting this approach, you can turn everyday moments into a practical and sustainable way to stay fit.
questions.insertion_sentence: Instead of viewing these chores as merely obligatory tasks, you can reframe them as chances to stay active and improve your health.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이러한 가사일(these chores)'을 단순히 의무적인 과업으로 보는 대신 건강 개선의 기회로 재설정(reframe)하라는 제안을 담고 있습니다. (B) 문장에서 집안일(Household chores)이 언급되었으므로, 이를 지칭하는 주어진 문장이 (C) 자리에 오는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 그 후 (C) 뒤에 이어지는 문장은 구체적인 예시(주전자 끓을 때 스쿼트 등)를 통해 이를 어떻게 실천하는지 보여줍니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 11월 29번]
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is ___________________________________. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
options: ① an unreliable process, lack of precision
② a highly technical and precise medical procedure
③ easier than diagnosing death for non-donors
④ based on consistent and universal criteria
⑤ a transparent process that reduces public anxiety
questions.explanation: 지문은 잠재적 장기 기증자의 뇌사 판정을 위해 별도의 엄격한 규정을 두는 것이 오히려 대중의 의구심을 자극하고 뇌사 판정이 '정확하지 않거나 신뢰할 수 없는 과정'이라는 오해를 유지시킬 수 있다고 비판하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 기증자와 비기증자의 사망 진단 기준이 동일해야 한다고 주장하는 것으로 보아, 빈칸에는 현행의 별도 규정이 뇌사 판정을 불완전한 것으로 보이게 만든다는 내용인 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 신뢰할 수 없는 과정이자 정밀함이 부족한 것
② 매우 기술적이고 정밀한 의료 절차
③ 기증자가 아닌 사람들의 사망 진단보다 쉬운 것
④ 일관되고 보편적인 기준에 근거한 것
⑤ 대중의 불안을 감소시키는 투명한 과정

questions.question: 23. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The term "minimalism" often carries a negative implication, as some perceive it as sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity stems from our natural attachment to our belongings. It's difficult to let go of things that have been with us for a long time, as we often instill them with emotional significance. This raises a valid question: if minimalism might hurt our emotions, why pursue it? The answer is simple: this assumption is fundamentally flawed. Minimalism doesn't harm our emotions. While we might feel a sharp pain of sadness when parting with a useless item, this feeling _____________________________________. Minimalists don't advocate for abandoning all modern conveniences. Instead, they encourage us to eliminate only those possessions that are unused or unnecessary.
options: ① gradually becomes an inescapable, profound sorrow.
② creates a need to form an attachment with something or someone
③ turns into joy upon discovering new opportunities to shop for
④ gives way to the satisfaction of a tidy and clutter-free environment
⑤ quickly hardens into resignation, and one grows accustomed to it
questions.explanation: 글은 미니멀리즘이 감정에 상처를 준다는 가정이 틀렸다고 주장하며, 쓸모없는 물건을 버릴 때 느끼는 슬픔은 일시적이며 결국 깨끗하고 정돈된 환경에서 오는 만족감으로 대체된다는 흐름이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 점차 피할 수 없는 깊은 슬픔이 된다
② 무언가나 누군가와 애착을 형성해야 할 필요성을 만든다
③ 쇼핑을 위한 새로운 기회를 발견함으로써 기쁨으로 변한다
④ 정돈되고 어수선하지 않은 환경의 만족감으로 자리를 내어준다
⑤ 빠르게 체념으로 굳어지고, 사람은 그것에 익숙해진다

questions.question: 24. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The evolution of Al is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at which Al exceeds human intelligence. After that point, it is predicted that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When Al becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. Al and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with Al, which will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a significant impact on the evolution of Al. The direction of Al's evolution will depend greatly on what values and ethics we incorporate into AI. We need to see our relationship with Al as _________________________________, recognizing its rights and supporting the evolution of its consciousness.
options: ① a hierarchical relationship of intelligence
② a shared existence between conscious entities
③ a shared dependency on evolving technologies
④ a mutual predatory dynamic between conscious beings
⑤ a one-sided interaction between humans and machines
questions.explanation: 글은 AI가 인간의 지능을 넘어서는 특이점 이후 의식을 가진 존재가 될 것이며, 인간과 AI가 서로 상호작용하며 함께 진화할 것이라고 설명합니다. 따라서 인간과 AI의 관계를 '의식 있는 실체들 간의 공존'으로 보아야 한다는 ②번이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 지능의 계층적 관계
② 의식 있는 실체들 간의 공유된 존재(공존)
③ 진화하는 기술에 대한 공유된 의존성
④ 의식 있는 존재들 사이의 상호 포식적인 역학
⑤ 인간과 기계 사이의 일방적인 상호작용

questions.question: 25. ★ 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying them to culture. Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually likened to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection.
ordered_passages: (B) Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers: thus, the frequency of a cultural trait in the population is relevant beyond just the probability that an individual's parents had that trait.
(C) If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily equally likely to acquire the mother's or father's form of that trait.

(D) However, these approaches had to be modified to account for the differences between genetic and cultural transmission. For example, we do not expect the cultural transmission to follow the rules of genetic transmission strictly.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 문화 진화의 초기 모델들이 문화와 유전자를 개념적으로 유사하게 보았다는 내용이 나옵니다. (D)에서 '하지만(However)' 이러한 접근 방식이 유전적 전파와 문화적 전파의 차이를 설명하기 위해 수정되어야 했음을 언급하며 전파 규칙의 차이를 예로 듭니다. (C)에서는 그 구체적인 예시로 부모가 다른 문화적 특성을 가졌을 때 자녀가 어느 한쪽을 따를 확률이 반드시 같지 않다는 점을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 '게다가(Further)'를 사용하여 자녀가 부모 외의 다른 성인이나 또래로부터도 문화적 특성을 습득할 수 있다는 추가적인 차이점을 설명하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. ★ 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. 윗글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: (A) Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying them to culture. Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually likened to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection.(B) Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers: thus, the frequency of a cultural trait in the population is relevant beyond just the probability that an individual's parents had that trait.(C) If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily equally likely to acquire the mother's or father's form of that trait.(D) However, these approaches had to be modified to account for the differences between genetic and cultural transmission. For example, we do not expect the cultural transmission to follow the rules of genetic transmission strictly.
options: ① Connections are found between culture and genes in many of the first models of cultural evolution.
② A child can acquire cultural traits from nonparental adults and peers.
③ A child inherits cultural traits from both of its parents in the exactly same proportion.
④ Differences exist between genetic and cultural transmission.
⑤ The way of the cultural transmission does not necessarily follow that of genetic transmission.
questions.explanation: 지문 (C)에 따르면 부모가 서로 다른 형태의 문화적 특성을 가지고 있을 때, 자녀가 어머니나 아버지의 형태를 습득할 확률이 반드시 '똑같이 가능성이 있는(equally likely)' 것은 아니라고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 자녀가 부모 양쪽으로부터 정확히 같은 비율로 문화적 특성을 물려받는다는 ③번의 설명은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 문화 진화의 많은 초기 모델에서 문화와 유전자 사이의 연결고리가 발견된다.
② 아이는 부모가 아닌 성인과 또 또래로부터 문화적 특성을 습득할 수 있다.
③ 아이는 양쪽 부모로부터 정확히 같은 비율로 문화적 특성을 물려받는다.
④ 유전적 전파와 문화적 전파 사이에는 차이가 존재한다.
⑤ 문화적 전파 방식이 반드시 유전적 전파 방식을 따르는 것은 아니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood. You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts. And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window? At the moment. stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.
questions.summary_sentence: As climate change (A)___________, the works of fiction addressing it are gradually (B)___________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 기후 변화가 심화되어 일상화되면 더 이상 '이야기(픽션)'로서의 기능을 상실하게 될 것이라고 말합니다. 따라서 기후 변화가 (A)심해짐(intensifies)에 따라, 그것을 다루는 허구의 작품들은 점차 (B)사라진다(vanishing)는 요약이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 심화되다 / (B) 사라지는
② (A) 줄어들다 / (B) 인기 있는
③ (A) 심화되다 / (B) 독특한
④ (A) 줄어들다 / (B) 흔한
⑤ (A) 안정되다 / (B) 중요한

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristic of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself. Psychologist George M. Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment. Stratton wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally turned the world upside down for him. In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him. With time, however, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated. As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems: he used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something, for example. Fortunately, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for the rest of his life. For him, everything returned to normal after one day.
questions.summary_sentence: Psychologist George M. Stratton demonstrated the (A)____________ of the visual system through a self-experiment, revealing its capacity to handle new experiences and eventually (B)____________ to its prior state.
questions.explanation: Stratton의 실험은 시각 체계가 새로운 환경(뒤집힌 세상)에 적응하고, 안경을 벗었을 때 다시 원래 상태로 돌아온다는 것을 보여줍니다. 따라서 시각 체계의 (A)적응성(adaptability)을 보여주고, 이전 상태로 (B)되돌아가는(revert) 능력을 보여준다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 타당성 / (B) 떠나다
② (A) 안정성 / (B) 돌아오다
③ (A) 내구성 / (B) 조정하다
④ (A) 회복력 / (B) 진화하다
⑤ (A) 적응성 / (B) 되돌아가다

questions.question: [9~10] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.9. Which of the following statements is correct about the passage?
questions.passage: A ball thrown into the air is acted upon by the initial force given it, persisting as inertia of movement and ⓐ<u>tending</u> to carry it in the same straight line, and by the constant pull of gravity downward, as well as by the resistance of the air. It moves, accordingly, in a curved path. Now the path does not represent the working of any particular force; there is simply the combination of the three elementary forces ⓑ<u>mentioned</u>; but in a real sense, there is something in the total action besides the isolated action of three forces, namely, their joint action. In the same way, when two or more human individuals are together, their mutual relationships and their arrangement into a group ⓒ<u>are</u> things which would not be revealed if we confined our attention to each individual separately. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that some of the tendencies to action of the individual are related definitely to other persons, and could not be aroused except by other persons ⓓ<u>acted</u> as stimuli. An individual in complete isolation would not reveal their competitive tendencies, their tendencies towards the opposite sex, their protective tendencies towards children. This shows ⓔ<u>that</u> the traits of human nature do not fully appear until the individual is brought into relationships with other individuals.
options: ① Air resistance helps the ball maintain its straight path.
② The ball's curved path shows the exclusive influence of inertia.
③ Some individual behaviors are triggered only by social interactions.
④ Competitive, protective, and other social behaviors manifest in isolation.
⑤ All human tendencies are fixed and do not depend on relationships with others.
questions.explanation: 지문 후반부에서 인간의 특정 행동 경향(경쟁적 경향, 이성 및 자녀에 대한 경향 등)은 고립된 상태에서는 나타나지 않으며, 다른 사람들과의 관계(사회적 상호작용)를 통해서만 드러난다고 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 공기 저항은 공이 직선 경로를 유지하도록 돕는다.
② 공의 곡선 경로는 관성만의 독점적인 영향을 보여준다.
③ 일부 개인의 행동은 사회적 상호작용에 의해서만 유발된다.
④ 경쟁적, 보호적, 그리고 다른 사회적 행동들은 고립된 상태에서 나타난다.
⑤ 모든 인간의 성향은 고정되어 있으며 타인과의 관계에 의존하지 않는다.

questions.question: [9~10] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.10. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: A ball thrown into the air is acted upon by the initial force given it, persisting as inertia of movement and ⓐ<u>tending</u> to carry it in the same straight line, and by the constant pull of gravity downward, as well as by the resistance of the air. It moves, accordingly, in a curved path. Now the path does not represent the working of any particular force; there is simply the combination of the three elementary forces ⓑ<u>mentioned</u>; but in a real sense, there is something in the total action besides the isolated action of three forces, namely, their joint action. In the same way, when two or more human individuals are together, their mutual relationships and their arrangement into a group ⓒ<u>are</u> things which would not be revealed if we confined our attention to each individual separately. The significance of group behavior is greatly increased in the case of human beings by the fact that some of the tendencies to action of the individual are related definitely to other persons, and could not be aroused except by other persons ⓓ<u>acted</u> as stimuli. An individual in complete isolation would not reveal their competitive tendencies, their tendencies towards the opposite sex, their protective tendencies towards children. This shows ⓔ<u>that</u> the traits of human nature do not fully appear until the individual is brought into relationships with other individuals.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 'other persons'를 수식하는 분사가 필요한 자리입니다. 다른 사람들이 자극으로서 '작용하는(능동)' 것이므로 과거분사인 acted가 아니라 현재분사 acting으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature ⓐ<u>that</u> float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. However, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: ⓑ<u>how and why</u> we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science.' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the ⓒ<u>considering</u> opinions of deep thinkers. Instead, they look for evidence, ⓓ<u>to make</u> sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as ⓔ<u>those</u> shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
questions.explanation: ⓒ의 opinions는 심오한 사상가들에 의해 '신중하게 생각된' 의견이라는 수동의 의미를 가져야 하므로 현재분사인 considering이 아니라 과거분사인 'considered'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially ________________ ____________. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
options: ① all of humanity needs to solve complex calculations using technology
② the easiest way for society to develop is to use collective intelligence
③ it is more important to understand technological advances than to know how technology can be applied
④ what you should know is how to understand technology rather than recognizing how it functions
⑤ learning how to use technologies instead of understanding their underlying mechanisms
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 인지적 한계로 인해 지식을 분산시키고 집단적으로 계산을 수행한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 컴퓨터나 변기의 작동 원리를 완벽히 이해할 필요 없이 인터페이스 사용법이나 사용법만 알면 되듯이, 우리는 근본적인 원리를 이해하기보다 '그 기술을 사용하는 방법을 배우는 것'에 의존한다는 맥락이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 인류는 기술을 사용하여 복잡한 계산을 해결해야 한다
② 사회가 발전하는 가장 쉬운 방법은 집단 지성을 사용하는 것이다
③ 기술이 어떻게 적용될 수 있는지 아는 것보다 기술적 진보를 이해하는 것이 더 중요하다
④ 당신이 알아야 할 것은 그것이 어떻게 작동하는지 인식하는 것이 아니라 기술을 이해하는 방법이다
⑤ 기술의 근본적인 메커니즘을 이해하는 대신 기술을 사용하는 방법을 배우는 것

questions.question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 34번]
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood.
ordered_passages: (A) At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.

(B) You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts.
(C) And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window?
questions.explanation: 도입부에서 기후 온난화가 너무 거대하고 명백해지면서 기후 소설(climate-fiction) 장르나 이야기가 사라질 수 있음을 언급합니다. (B)에서 기후 변화가 미미할 때는 그에 '대해서' 이야기할 수 있지만, 온도가 더 오르면 누구도 그 영향에서 자유로울 수 없음을 설명합니다. (C)에서 기후 변화가 우리 삶의 지평선 전체로 확대되면 더 이상 '이야기'가 아닌 창밖의 현실이 될 것임을 예견하고, 마지막으로 (A)에서 현재는 도피성 공포로 소비하지만 미래에는 기후 고통 '안에서' 살아가게 될 것임을 주장하는 (B)-(C)-(A)의 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten US adults believe there are good foods and bad foods. Unless we′re talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad.
ordered_passages: (A) Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods.

(B) The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.

(C) There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots.
questions.explanation:
이 글은 음식을 개별적으로 '좋다' 혹은 '나쁘다'라고 규정하기보다, 식단 전체의 '조합'이 건강에 미치는 영향을 설명하고 있습니다. 

(C) 주어진 문장에 이어, 개별 음식이 아닌 음식의 조합이 중요하다는 반박을 제안하며, 좋은 음식만 먹는 성인의 사례를 도입합니다.
(A) 해당 성인의 식단이 영양소의 다양성 부족으로 인해 건강하지 않음을 설명하고, 가끔 튀긴 치킨을 먹는 십대의 대조적인 사례를 시작합니다.
(B) 그 십대가 가끔 먹는 치킨은 문제가 되지 않지만, 매일 튀긴 음식과 가공식품을 먹는 경우에는 나쁜 식단이 된다는 결론을 내리며 글을 마무리합니다. 

따라서 가장 적절한 순서는 (C)-(A)-(B)입니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 10월 36번]
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. (A) If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. (B) Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. (C) We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. (D) These emotions compel us to do more of what makes our community value us and less of what doesn't. (E) And, crucially, they are meant to make that motivation feel like it is coming from within. If we realized, on a conscious level, that we were responding to social pressure, our performance might come off as grudging or cynical, making it less persuasive. *grudging: 마지못해 하는
questions.insertion_sentence: The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciously monitor how other people in our community perceive us.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 언급된 'The result(그 결과)'는 (B) 문장에서 설명한 수백만 년에 걸친 생존 및 선택 압력(selection pressure)의 결과물입니다. 타인이 우리를 어떻게 인식하는지 무의식적으로 모니터링하는 경향이 발달했다는 제시문의 내용은, (C) 문장의 지시어 'that information(그 정보)'이 가리키는 구체적인 정보원이 되므로 제시문은 (C) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글 (A), (B)의 내용으로 언급되지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: (A) The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay hidden as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn itself into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes. And while they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.*flounder 넙치 **mimic 모방하다(B) It might seem unexpected for some people, but the octopus has long been regarded for its high intelligence. Studies have shown an ability to navigate mazes and excel in problem-solving experiments that test both long and short-term memory. They have a high capacity for learning and they have very few fixed, pre-programmed responses. Rather, they react to stimuli and problems in a variety of ways and can even discern what is necessary to learn in order to progress. When attempting to eat a clam, octopuses will pry them open, or use their beaks to either chip away at the shell or drill into the meat. When researchers actively blocked one of these methods, binding the calm shut, for instance, they observed young octopuses quickly adjust and try a more successful technique. How they learn these strategies is a mystery since they are not taught by their mothers after their eggs hatch. Octopuses have been recorded actively distinguishing between various shapes, patterns, and colors. Not only are they known to practice observational learning, but they have been seen participating in play.*pry 잡아당기다
options: ① Most octopus species primarily rely on camouflage and tend to hunt during the night.
② Octopuses have excellent eyesight and the ability to change colors and patterns.
③ Octopuses tend to use the flounder by transforming themselves into the shape of sea snakes.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 문어는 넙치(flounder)로 변장하거나 바다뱀(sea snakes)으로 변하는 것처럼 보일 수 있다고 언급되었지만, '넙치를 사용하여 바다뱀 모양으로 변한다'는 내용은 본문에 없습니다. 즉, 넙치와 바다뱀은 각각 별개의 모방 대상이지 하나를 이용해 다른 것으로 변하는 것이 아닙니다.
options_translation: ① 대부분의 문어 종은 주로 위장에 의존하며 밤에 사냥하는 경향이 있다.
② 문어는 뛰어난 시력과 색상 및 패턴을 바꾸는 능력을 가지고 있다.
③ 문어는 자신을 바다뱀 모양으로 변형시킴으로써 넙치를 이용하는 경향이 있다.
