questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 지문의 내용과 관련하여 생성형 인공지능(Artificial Intelligence)에게 추가적인 질문을 한다고 할 때, 질문의 내용으로 가장 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and noradrenaline, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to reframe depression as a problem of consciousness. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.*neurotransmitter 신경 전달 물질**manifest (명백히) 나타내다
options: ① What are the alternative theories explaining the causes of depression?
② How does consciousness influence our mental health?
③ Can lifestyle changes help improve our state of consciousness?
④ What are the reasons people fall into the alerting response and what kinds of pleasures do they experience as a result?
⑤ What are some potential implications of viewing depression as a distortion of consciousness rather than a neurotransmitter imbalance?
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 우울증의 원인을 뇌의 신경전달물질 불균형이 아닌 의식의 왜곡으로 보아야 한다는 내용입니다. ④번의 '경고 반응(alerting response)'이나 '그 결과로 경험하는 즐거움'은 지문의 우울증 및 의식에 관한 논의와 전혀 관련이 없는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 우울증의 원인을 설명하는 대안적인 이론들은 무엇인가?
② 의식은 우리의 정신 건강에 어떻게 영향을 미치는가?
③ 생활 방식의 변화가 우리의 의식 상태를 개선하는 데 도움이 될 수 있는가?
④ 사람들이 경고 반응에 빠지는 이유는 무엇이며 그 결과로 어떤 종류의 즐거움을 경험하는가?
⑤ 우울증을 신경전달물질 불균형이 아닌 의식의 왜곡으로 보는 것의 잠재적 시사점은 무엇인가?

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. 윗글 (A)의 내용을 바탕으로 (B)의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, ______________________________.(B) Goldilocks effect is the psychological effect that people, when provided with similar choices, tend to drift towards the most feasible option. It is based on the idea of product differentiation, comparative pricing, and bracketing. Brands can capitalize on it by offering three versions of a product or service at different price brackets like high-end, middle-end, and low-end. They can only leverage the Goldilocks effect if ___________________________________. This specific approach shows that businesses can offer multiple versions of a product with different quality and price points simultaneously.*leverage 활용하다
options: ① they can increase prices through a variety of products
② they differentiate their own products from one another
③ they organize their product features to be more representative
④ they make up various products that reflect consumers' desire to produce
⑤ they have the ability to construct products only at prices that consumers like
questions.explanation: 글 (A)에서는 세 가지 버전의 제품을 출시할 때 소비자들이 중간 가격의 제품을 선택하게 되는 심리를 설명하며, 이는 제품 간의 기능과 가격 차이를 두는 전략입니다. 글 (B)에서 골디락스 효과를 활용하기 위해서는 자사 제품들 간에 차별성을 두어야 하므로 'differentiate their own products from one another'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다양한 제품을 통해 가격을 인상할 수 있다
② 자사 제품들을 서로 차별화한다
③ 제품의 특징을 더 대표성 있게 구성한다
④ 소비자의 생산 욕구를 반영하는 다양한 제품을 만든다
⑤ 소비자가 좋아하는 가격으로만 제품을 구성하는 능력이 있다

questions.question: 30. 다음 글을 읽고 아래의 요약문을 완성하려고 할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 어휘를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (변형없이 그대로 쓸 것)
questions.passage: Life is what physicists might call a 'high-dimensional system,' which is their fancy way of saying that there's a lot going on. In just a single cell, the number of possible interactions between different molecules is enormous. Such a system can only hope to be stable if only a smaller number of collective ways of being may emerge. For example, it is only a limited number of tissues and body shapes that may result from the development of a human embryo. In 1942, the biologist Conrad Waddington called this drastic narrowing of outcomes canalization. The organism may switch between a small number of well-defined possible states, but can't exist in random states in between them, rather as a ball in a rough landscape must roll to the bottom of one valley or another. We'll see that this is true also of health and disease: there are many causes of illness, but their manifestations at the physiological and symptomatic levels are often strikingly similar.*embryo 배아 **physiological 생리적인
questions.summary_sentence: Life is a complex system with many (A)________, but it maintains stability by narrowing down into a limited number of states, which is also shown in the (B)________ symptoms of various diseases.
subjective_conditions: 변형없이 그대로 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 본문에서 생명체는 수많은 '상호작용(interactions)'이 일어나는 고차원적 시스템이지만, 안정성을 위해 결과의 범위를 좁히는 '운하화(canalization)' 과정을 거친다고 설명합니다. 또한 질병의 원인은 많지만 그 증상은 종종 매우 '유사하다(similar)'고 언급되어 있습니다. 요약문의 (A)에는 복잡한 상호작용을 뜻하는 interactions가, (B)에는 다양한 질병의 증상이 비슷하다는 맥락의 similar가 본문에서 그대로 추출되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push - essentially ________________ ____________. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
options: ① all of humanity needs to solve complex calculations using technology
② the easiest way for society to develop is to use collective intelligence
③ it is more important to understand technological advances than to know how technology can be applied
④ what you should know is how to understand technology rather than recognizing how it functions
⑤ learning how to use technologies instead of understanding their underlying mechanisms
questions.explanation: 허버트 사이먼은 인간의 정보, 시간, 인지 능력의 한계를 인정하여 노벨상을 받았습니다. 인간은 모든 계산을 스스로 할 수 없으므로 사회 전체에 분산시켜 해결하며, 우리는 그저 결과(정답)를 사회적으로 학습하기만 하면 됩니다. 컴퓨터나 변기의 원리를 알 필요 없이 인터페이스 사용법이나 물 내리는 법만 알면 된다는 예시는, 작동 원리(underlying mechanisms)를 이해하기보다는 그것을 사용하는 법(how to use)을 배우는 것이 본질임을 시사합니다. 따라서 5번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 인류는 기술을 사용하여 복잡한 계산을 해결해야 한다
② 사회가 발전하는 가장 쉬운 방법은 집단 지성을 사용하는 것이다
③ 기술이 어떻게 적용될 수 있는지 아는 것보다 기술적 진보를 이해하는 것이 더 중요하다
④ 당신이 알아야 할 것은 기술이 어떻게 작동하는지 인식하는 것보다 기술을 이해하는 방법이다
⑤ 근본적인 메커니즘을 이해하는 대신 기술을 사용하는 방법을 배우는 것

questions.question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: On-screen, climate disaster is everywhere you look, but the scope of the world's climate transformation may just as quickly eliminate the climate-fiction genre - indeed eliminate any effort to tell the story of warming, which could grow too large and too obvious even for Hollywood.
ordered_passages: (A) At the moment, stories illustrating global warming can still offer an escapist pleasure, even if that pleasure often comes in the form of horror. But when we can no longer pretend that climate suffering is distant - in time or in place - we will stop pretending about it and start pretending within it.

(B) You can tell stories 'about' climate change while it still seems a marginal feature of human life. But when the temperature rises by three or four more degrees, hardly anyone will be able to feel isolated from its impacts.
(C) And so as climate change expands across the horizon, it may cease to be a story. Why watch or read climate fiction about the world you can see plainly out your own window?
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 기후 변화의 규모가 너무 커져서 기후 소설 장르가 사라질 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (B)에서 기후 변화가 삶의 주변적 특징일 때만 '이야기'가 가능하다는 점을 언급하고 기온 상승으로 누구나 영향을 받게 되는 상황을 제시합니다. (C)에서는 기후 변화가 확산됨에 따라 더 이상 이야기가 되지 못한다는 점(창밖으로 보이는 현실이 되므로)을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 현재는 도피적 즐거움을 주지만 더 이상 멀게 느껴지지 않을 때는 그 안에서 살아가게 될 것임을 결론지으며 마무리하는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is to stay ⓐ<u>hidden</u> as much as possible and do their own hunting at night. So to find one in full view in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, what they saw at first was a flounder. It was only when they looked again ⓑ<u>what</u> they saw a medium-sized octopus, with all eight of its arms folded and its two eyes staring upwards to create the illusion. An octopus has a big brain, excellent eyesight and the ability to change colour and pattern, and this one was using these assets to turn ⓒ<u>itself</u> into a completely different creature. Many more of this species have been found since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be ⓓ<u>transforming</u> into sea snakes. And ⓔ<u>while</u> they mimic, they hunt - producing the spectacle of, say, a flounder suddenly developing an octopodian arm, sticking it down a hole and grabbing whatever's hiding there.
questions.explanation: ⓑ는 'It is ~ that ...' 강조 구문에서 시간을 나타내는 부사절 'only when they looked again'을 강조하고 있으므로 접속사 that이 와야 합니다. what은 뒤에 불완전한 문장이 와야 하는데, 여기서는 'they saw a medium-sized octopus...'로 완전한 문장이 이어지고 있습니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: The evolution of AI is often associated with the concept of singularity. Singularity refers to the point at ⓐ<u>where</u> Al exceeds human intelligence. After that point it is ⓑ<u>predicted</u> that AI will repeatedly improve itself and evolve at an accelerated pace. When Al becomes self-aware and pursues its own goals, it will be a conscious being, not just a machine. Al and human consciousness will then begin to evolve together. Our consciousness will evolve to new dimensions through our interactions with AI, ⓒ<u>which</u> will provide us with intellectual stimulation and inspire new insights and creativity. Conversely, our consciousness also has a profound impact on the evolution of AI. The direction of Al's evolution will depend greatly on ⓓ<u>what</u> values and ethics we incorporate into Al. We need to see our relationship with AI as a mutual coexistence of conscious beings, recognizing its rights and ⓔ<u>supporting</u> the evolution of its consciousness.
questions.explanation: ⓐ의 'at where'는 중복된 표현입니다. 'the point'를 수식하기 위해 관계부사 where를 단독으로 쓰거나, 관계대명사를 사용하여 'at which'로 써야 합니다. 전치사 at 뒤에 관계부사 where를 또 쓰는 것은 어법상 틀립니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Today, the water crisis is political - which is to say, not inevitable or beyond our capacity to fix - and, therefore, functionally ⓐ<u>elective</u>. That is one reason it is nevertheless distressing: an abundant resource made ⓑ<u>scarce</u> through governmental neglect and indifference, bad infrastructure and contamination, and careless urbanization. There is no need for a water crisis, in other words, but we have one anyway, and aren't doing much to ⓒ<u>address</u> it. Some cities lose more water to leaks than they ⓓ<u>deliver</u> to homes: even in the United States, leaks and theft account for an estimated loss of 16 percent of freshwater; in Brazil, the estimate is 40 percent. Seen in both cases, as everywhere, the ⓔ<u>universal</u> scarcity clearly highlights have-and-have-not inequities, leaving 2.1 billion people without safe drinking water and 4.5 billion without proper sanitation worldwide.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체 맥락상 물 위기는 피할 수 없는 것이 아니라 정치적인 선택의 문제이며, 특정 지역이나 계층에 불평등하게 나타나고 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '보편적인(universal)' 부족이 아니라, 인위적으로 만들어졌거나 불평등하게 배분된 상황을 나타내는 어휘가 문맥상 적절합니다. ⑤의 universal은 뒤에 나오는 'have-and-have-not inequities(가진 자와 가지지 못한 자의 불평등)'와 모순됩니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Conventional medicine has long believed that depression is caused by an imbalance of neurotransmitters in the brain. However, there is a major problem with this explanation. This is because the imbalance of substances in the brain is a consequence of depression, not its cause. In other words, depression causes a decrease in brain substances such as serotonin and norepinephrine, not a decrease in brain substances causes depression. In this revised cause-and-effect, the key is to _______________________________. Our consciousness is a more fundamental entity that goes beyond the functioning of the brain. The brain is no more than an organ of consciousness. If it is not consciousness itself, then the root cause of depression is also a distortion of our state of consciousness: a consciousness that has lost its sense of self and the meaning of life. Such a disease of consciousness may manifest itself in the form of depression.
options: ① reframe depression as a problem of consciousness
② eat foods such as healthy fruits to enhance serotonin production
③ view consciousness as a simple byproduct of brain activity
④ read books related to depression and cognitive perception
⑤ increase self-esteem levels to immediately cure depression
questions.explanation: 지문은 우울증의 원인이 뇌의 화학 물질 불균형이라는 기존 관념을 뒤집고, 오히려 우울증(의식의 상태)이 뇌 물질의 변화를 일으키는 결과라고 주장합니다. 즉, 우울증의 근본 원인을 '의식의 왜곡'이나 '의식의 질병'으로 보고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 우울증을 의식의 문제로 재구성해야 한다는 내용인 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우울증을 의식의 문제로 재구성하는 것
② 세로토닌 생산을 높이기 위해 건강한 과일과 같은 음식을 먹는 것
③ 의식을 뇌 활동의 단순한 부산물로 보는 것
④ 우울증 및 인지 지각과 관련된 책을 읽는 것
⑤ 우울증을 즉시 치료하기 위해 자존감 수준을 높이는 것

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: As individuals, our ability to thrive depended on how well we navigated relationships in a group. If the group valued us, we could count on support, resources, and probably a mate. If it didn't, we might get none of these merits. It was a matter of survival, physically and genetically. Over millions of years, the pressure selected for people who are sensitive to and skilled at maximizing their standing. The result was the development of a tendency to unconsciousy monitor how other people in our community perceive us. We process that information in the form of self-esteem and such related emotions as pride, shame, or insecurity. These emotions compel us to do more of what ___________________________________________ and less of what doesn't.
options: ② makes our community value us
③ helps in the development of relationships
④ becomes a valuable asset to our community
⑤ contributes to the well-being of our society
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간이 집단 내에서 자신의 위치를 모니터링하도록 진화했음을 설명합니다. 자존감과 같은 감정은 집단이 우리를 가츱있게 여기도록 만드는 행동을 덄 하도록 만듭니다.
options_translation: ① 상당한 성공으로 이끄는 것
② 우리의 공동체가 우리를 가츱있게 여기게 만드는 것
③ 관계 발전에 도움이 되는 것
④ 우리 공동체에 귀중한 자산이 되는 것
⑤ 우리 사회의 안녕에 기여하는 것

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The common accounts of human nature that float around in society are generally a mixture of assumptions, tales and sometimes plain silliness. (A)____________, psychology is different. It is the branch of science that is devoted to understanding people: how and why we act as we do; why we see things as we do; and how we interact with one another. The key word here is 'science,' Psychologists don't depend on opinions and hearsay, or the generally accepted views of society at the time, or even the considered opinions of deep thinkers (B)____________, they look for evidence, to make sure that psychological ideas are firmly based, and not just derived from generally held beliefs or assumptions. In addition to this evidence-based approach, psychology deals with fundamental processes and principles that generate our rich cultural and social diversity, as well as those shared by all human beings. These are what modern psychology is all about.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서는 인간 본성에 대한 일반적인 설명들이 가정이나 꾸며낸 이야기의 혼합이라고 했고, 뒤에서는 심리학은 다르다고 했으므로 역접의 '그러나(However)'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞 문장에서 심리학자들은 의견이나 소문에 의존하지 않는다고 했고, 뒤에서는 그들이 증거를 찾는다고 했으므로 '~대신에(Instead)'가 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나, 게다가
② 그러나, 대신에
③ 게다가, 비슷하게
④ 그러므로, 대조적으로
⑤ 그러므로, 예를 들어

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
questions.summary_sentence: Asking (A)__________, measurable questions improves the accuracy and reliability of data on (B)__________ concept.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 추상적인 개념을 측정할 때 구체적인 질문을 던지는 것이 데이터의 정확성과 신뢰성을 높여준다는 내용입니다. 따라서 요약문의 (A)에는 구체적인 질문을 의미하는 'specific'이, (B)에는 모호하거나 추상적인 개념을 의미하는 'obscure'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 새로운 ... 현대의
② 모호한 ... 구체적인
③ 신선한 ... 반복적인
④ 구체적인 ... 모호한
⑤ 상세한 ... 객관적인

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 a black cat이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was <u>a black cat</u>, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① new research method still in development
② popular theory that has yet to be confirmed
③ scientific illusion caused by flawed reasoning
④ difficult issue that requires special tools to solve
⑤ theory that is difficult to test but potentially correct
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학자들이 잘못된 개념(본질주의)에 근거하여 가설을 세울 때, 존재하지 않는 것을 찾으려 애쓰는 상황을 비유하고 있습니다. Stuart Firestein은 '에테르'를 예로 들며, 그것이 실제로는 존재하지 않는 것을 찾으려 했던 '어두운 방 안의 검은 고양이'와 같다고 설명합니다. 따라서 'a black cat'은 결함이 있는 추론으로 인해 만들어진 과학적 환상을 의미합니다.
options_translation: 아직 개발 중인 새로운 연구 방법
아직 확인되지 않은 대중적인 이론
결함이 있는 추론으로 인해 발생한 과학적 환상
해결하기 위해 특별한 도구가 필요한 어려운 문제
테스트하기는 어렵지만 잠재적으로 옳은 이론

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 inclusiveness in the workplace가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve <u>inclusiveness in the workplace</u>. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where interpersonal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
options: ① monitoring employee behavior and enforcing workplace policies by using AI to track rule compliance in real time
② embracing people with disabilities and low-skilled workers at work by enhancing accessibility
③ cutting energy use and making the workplace more environmentally friendly
④ ensuring all employees receives equal pay raises and promotions
⑤ replacing human workers entirely by automating all tasks with AI
questions.explanation: 본문은 인공지능(AI)이 장애인(시각, 언어, 청각 등)이나 저숙련 노동자들의 업무 접근성을 높이고 능력을 보완해줌으로써, 노동 시장에서 불리한 위치에 있는 사람들이 직장에 더 잘 통합될 수 있도록 돕는다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '직장 내 포용성'은 접근성 향상을 통해 이들을 수용하는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: AI를 사용하여 규칙 준수를 실시간으로 추적함으로써 직원의 행동을 모니터링하고 직장 정책을 집행하는 것
접근성을 강화함으로써 직장에서 장애인과 저숙련 노동자를 포용하는 것
에너지 사용을 줄이고 직장을 더욱 환경 친화적으로 만드는 것

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay ⓐ<u>alive</u>. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming ⓑ<u>rises</u> the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data ⓒ<u>indicating</u> that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show ⓓ<u>that</u> the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water ⓔ<u>have</u> the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: ⓑ의 'rises'는 '오르다'라는 의미의 자동사로 뒤에 목적어를 취할 수 없습니다. 문맥상 '해수 온도를 높이다'라는 타동사의 의미가 필요하므로 타동사인 'raises'로 수정해야 합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Recently, campaigners have encouraged us to buy local food. This ⓐ<u>reduces</u> 'food miles', that is, the distance food travels to get from the producer to the retailer. They reason that the higher the food miles, the more carbon emissions. Buying local food, therefore, has a ⓑ<u>lower</u> carbon footprint and is more environmentally friendly. However, the real story is not as simple as that. If our aim is to reduce carbon emissions, we must look at the whole farming process, not just transportation. According to a 2008 study, only 11% of carbon emissions in the food production process result from transportation, and only 4% originated from the final delivery of the product from the producer to the retailer. Other processes, including fertilization, storage, heating and irrigation, contribute much ⓒ<u>more</u>. In fact, imported food often has a lower carbon footprint than locally grown food. Take apples, for example. In autumn, when apples are harvested, the best option for a British resident is to buy British apples. However, the apples we buy in winter or spring have been kept refrigerated for months, and this ⓓ<u>saves</u> a lot of energy. In spring, therefore, it is more energy-efficient to important them from New Zealand, where they are in season. Heating also uses a lot of energy, which is why growing tomatoes in heated greenhouses in the UK is ⓔ<u>less</u> environmentally friendly than importing them from Spain, where the crop grows well in the local climate.
questions.explanation: 영국에서 겨울이나 봄에 먹는 사과는 수개월 동안 냉장 보관된 것이며, 이러한 장기 보관은 막대한 에너지를 소모(uses/consumes)하게 됩니다. 따라서 에너지를 아낀다는 의미의 ⓓ saves는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다. 오히려 봄에는 제철인 뉴질랜드에서 사과를 수입하는 것이 더 에너지 효율적이라는 뒤의 문장과도 모순됩니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ (줄인다)
② ⓑ (더 낮은)
③ ⓒ (더 많이)
④ ⓓ (절약한다)
⑤ ⓔ (덜)

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is ______________ until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 논지는 과학적 의사소통은 양방향 과정이며, 신호가 인지되지 않으면 소용이 없듯이 과학 논문도 독자에게 수용되고 이해되어야 가치가 있다는 것입니다. 따라서 과학 실험은 결과가 출판되고 이해되기 전까지는 '완성되지 않은(incomplete)' 상태라는 의미가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 미완성인
② 독립적인
③ 의미 있는
④ 성공적인
⑤ 결정적인

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge _________________________ as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs on such behaviors.
options: ① slight deviations from the norm
③ strict adherence to social customs
⑤ the similarity between person and environment
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 확립된 규범을 '약간(slightly)' 어기는 사람들을 긍정적으로(높은 지위와 능력을 갖춘 것으로) 평가한다는 연구 결과를 다루고 있습니다. 빨간 나비넥타이나 빨간 운동화와 같은 사례는 규범으로부터의 '약간의 일탈'을 의미합니다. 이러한 행동은 그 개인이 사회적 비용을 감수할 만큼 충분히 강력하다는 것을 암시하기 때문에 긍정적으로 판단된다는 결론이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status - they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers may not _____________________. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.
options: ② always consider its luxury appeal
③ ignore value in both options
④ always prefer its latest version
⑤ be entirely dependent on it
questions.explanation: 보완재에 대한 설명으로, 어떤 제품들은 전등과 전구처럼 함께 소비되어야 하지만, 모든 보완재가 '완전한' 보완 관계는 아님을 주의해야 한다고 말한다. 운전자가 가솔린 차 대신 전기차로 전환할 수 있다는 예시는 고객이 특정 보완재에 '전적으로 의존하지 않을 수도 있음'을 보여준다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. ①Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are minimized. ②For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. ③Many remote workers find that having a dedicated home office space improves their productivity. ④Variable work schedules are ideal for these individuals because they make it easier to separate work from other areas of their lives. ⑤On the other hand, some people mix their work and family life throughout the day, like texting their kids from the office or checking emails while on vacation, instead of coming back to a pile of unread messages.
questions.explanation: 디지털 기술로 인해 일과 가정의 경계가 모호해지고 있으며, 사람들은 일과 가정을 분리해서 관리하려는 '분리자(segmentor)'와 '통합자(integrator)' 유형으로 나뉜다는 내용입니다. ③은 재택 근무자의 사무실 전용 공간이 생산성을 높여준다는 내용이므로, 일과 가정의 관리 방식(분리 vs 통합)을 다루는 전체 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.passage: There is a reason the title 'Monday Morning Quarterback' exists. questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.summary_sentence: In the passage, de Waal explains that humans purposely manipulate language in order to (A)____________ the differences between ourselves and animals, which helps (B)____________ the belief of human superiority over other species.
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간이 동물과의 유사성을 폄하하고 언어를 조작하여 인간이 다른 동물보다 우월하다는 지위를 유지하려 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 인간은 기술적인 용어를 사용하여 동물과 거리를 두고, 인간만이 가진 특성을 강조하려 합니다. 따라서 인간은 언어를 조작하여 차이점을 (A)증폭시키고(amplify), 인간의 우월성이라는 믿음을 (B)지지(support)한다는 결론이 적절합니다.

② 지우다 / 약화시키다
③ 흐리게 하다 / 강화하다
④ 최소화하다 / 의문을 제기하다
⑤ 과장하다 / 밑을 깎아내리다

questions.question: 18. 다음 글을 요약하여 정리한 표에서 본문과 부합하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Have you ever heard a recording of your voice and had a double take? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. Many of us have had that experience. Why is that? The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people. That explanation makes sense for many people, but it doesn't quite explain some variations in this phenomenon like people whose voices sound higher to themselves than it does to others. These variations occur simply because every person's hearing is different. There are more nuanced ways for sounds to be perceived by the inner ear, which creates different perceptions between ourselves and others. For example, vibrations of your voice may encounter cerebrospinal fluid, the clear liquid that sits within the brain and spine, which can influence how you perceive your voice. All these variations and many more make it so that your voice will always sound different to your own ears than it sounds to others.[Summary Table]Title of the Text: ⓐWhy Our Recorded Voices Sound So DifferentFactor: Hearing PathwayEffect: ⓑExternal sounds travel through the outer, middle, and inner car. ⓒThe vibration of our own voice is conducted through bones directly to the inner ear.Factor: Frequency EmphasisEffect: ⓓInternal pathway emphasizes higher frequencies, making voice sound deeper and richer to oneself.Factor: Cerebrospinal FluidEffect: ⓔIt can influence how vibrations of the voice are perceived, contributing to individual differences.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 뼈를 통해 전달되는 내부 경로(internal path)는 '더 낮은 주파수(Lower frequencies)'를 강조한다고 명시되어 있습니다. 표의 ⓓ 부분은 'higher frequencies(더 높은 주파수)'라고 되어 있으므로 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Moving is often a source of stress for the whole family. This change can be difficult for a young child, as they do not always understand the reasons for the move. questions.explanation: 아이에게 익숙한 환경을 제공하여 안심시키기 위해 침구를 바꿔야 한다면, 이사 '후(after)'가 아니라 이사 '전(before)'에 미리 구매하여 가족의 냄새가 배도록 해야 합니다. 따라서 ⓒ의 after는 before로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War.
ordered_passages: (B) In theory, ⓐ<u>its</u> expansion to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand ⓑ<u>it</u> have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education.(C) Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small number of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers. ⓒ<u>It</u> also enabled formative feedback to shape the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.(D) Between 2000 and 2014, ⓓ<u>its</u> participation rates almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). ⓔ<u>Its</u> dramatic growth has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy.

(B)에서 이러한 확장이 이론적으로는 평가 방식을 바꿀 것으로 기대되었으나 현실적으로는 '모순의 장'을 만들었음을 언급하고, (C)에서 그 현실적인 결과물인 대중 교육의 효율적 평가 방식(시험, 퀴즈)과 과거 엘리트 체제의 긴밀한 관계를 대조하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice.
options: ③ Correlation Between Crystal Habits and Its Environment

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
options: ① Pay attention to what your feelings tell you.
② Feelings are behind all human decision-making.
③ Find out others' opinions and interpretations of data.
④ Your anxiety helps you make the final decision about risk.

③ 데이터에 대한 타인의 의견과 해석을 찾아보라.
④ 불안은 위험에 대한 최종 결정을 내리는 데 도움이 된다.
⑤ 감정이 당신을 이끌게 하는 대신 의사 결정에서 논리를 따르라.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?

questions.question: 11. 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. 윗글에서 Frans de Waal의 주장으로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.question: 13. 위 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Claims that local food production cut greenhouse gas emissions by reducing the burning of transportation fuel are usually not well founded. Transport is the source of only 11 percent of greenhouse gas emissions within the food sector, so reducing the distance that food travels after it leaves the farm is far less important than reducing wasteful energy use on the farm. Food coming from a distance can actually be better for the climate, depending on (A)_________________. For example, field-grown tomatoes shipped from Mexico in the winter months will have a smaller carbon footprint than local winter tomatoes grown in a greenhouse. When food does travel, what matters most is not the distance traveled but the travel mode (surface versus air), and most of all (B)_________________. Bulk loads of food can travel halfway around the world by ocean freight with a smaller carbon footprint, per pound delivered, than foods traveling just a short distance but in much smaller loads. For example, 18-wheelers carry much larger loads than pickup trucks so they can move food 100 times as far while burning only one-third as much gas per pound of food delivered.

questions.explanation: (A) 뒤에 나오는 예시들(노지 재배 vs 온실 재배, 사료 vs 클로버 목초지)은 식품이 어떻게 재배되었느냐가 기후에 더 큰 영향을 미친다는 것을 보여주므로 'how it was grown'이 적절합니다. (B) 뒤에 나오는 예시(Bulk loads vs smaller loads, 대형 트럭 vs 픽업트럭)는 한 번에 실을 수 있는 짐의 크기(적재량)가 중요하다는 것을 나타내므로 'the load size'가 적절합니다.
