questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are becoming ⓐ<u>indistinct</u> as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are ⓑ<u>reduced</u>. For example, these people might keep ⓒ<u>different</u> email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones ─ one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable ⓓ<u>less</u> distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer ⓔ<u>combining</u> work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.explanation: 앞 문장에서 일과 가정을 분리하려는 사람들(segmenters)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 유연한 근로 시간표가 이들에게 도움이 되는 이유는 일하는 시간과 다른 역할 사이의 구분을 '줄이는(less)' 것이 아니라 '더 가능하게(greater)' 만들기 때문입니다. 따라서 ⓓ는 'greater'나 'more'와 같은 단어가 되어야 맥락상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 두 개 찾아 기호와 바르게 고친 표현을 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might ⓐ<u>diminish</u> productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only ⓑ<u>a benefit</u> up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may ⓒ<u>ignore</u> a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as ⓓ<u>an unpleasing</u> feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might ⓔ<u>fear</u> that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 지식 파급과 같은 긍정적 외부 효과는 생산성을 '감소(diminish)'시키는 것이 아니라 '증대(increase)'시킵니다.ⓒ 관용적인 원주민들은 이용 가능한 상품과 서비스의 범위가 늘어나기 때문에 다문화 도시나 지역을 '무시(ignore)'하는 것이 아니라 '소중히 여기거나 선호(value)'하게 됩니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글을 읽고 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오. [3.0점]
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our (A)__________ and our (B)__________. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore show your child good examples of life by your action. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 우리는 아이들에게 무엇인가를 항상 가르치고 있으며, 아이들은 보고 듣는 것을 통해 배운다고 언급합니다. 지문 전체의 내용은 부모가 말로만 가르치는 것이 아니라 행동(action)을 통해 모범을 보여야 한다는 것이 핵심입니다. 문맥상 부모의 '말(words)'과 '행동(actions)'을 통해 아이들을 가르친다는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. (A) Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. (B) They may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" (C) It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. (D) Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. (E) This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.insertion_sentence: Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '3세에서 6세 사이의 어린 아이들이 이사에 특히 영향을 받는다'는 구체적인 대상을 언급하고 있습니다. 지문 (A) 뒷문장의 'this stage(이 단계)'가 가리키는 대상이 바로 주어진 문장의 'ages 3-6'이므로, 주어진 문장은 (A) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. (A) Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it ─ you just see the blurred outline of the moving string. (B) Strings vibrating in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. (C) The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. (D) The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. (E) When the waves reach your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string.
questions.insertion_sentence: But if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note is heard loud and clear.
questions.explanation: (B) 문장까지는 줄이 너무 가늘어서 소리가 거의 나지 않는다는 내용이 나옵니다. 주어진 문장은 '하지만(But)'이라는 연결사를 사용하여 속이 빈 상자(기타 몸통)에 줄을 연결하면 소리가 증폭된다는 반전의 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C) 문장부터는 기타 몸통의 나무 패널로 진동이 전달된다는 구체적인 과정이 설명되므로, 주어진 문장은 (C) 위치에 들어가는 것이 논리적으로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation. If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. ⓐWhile the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a protective mechanism for the foot. ⓑWithin the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. ⓒThe sensory system receives and processes information that generates an individual's awareness of their environment. ⓓThey will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now contract quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object. ⓔSensory and motor nerves control almost all functions in the body ─ from the beating of the heart to the movement of the gut, sweating and just about everything else.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 감각 신경이 통증을 전달하고 뇌에서 반응하여 근육(운동 신경)을 통해 발을 떼는 일련의 신경 전달 과정을 구체적인 예시(핀을 밟았을 때)를 통해 설명하고 있습니다. ⓒ는 감각계의 일반적인 정의를 설명하고 있으나, 글 전체의 구체적인 신경 전달 과정 및 보호 반응이라는 흐름 사이에서 흐름을 끊는 일반적 진술에 불과하여 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 22번]
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate.
ordered_passages: (A) In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.

(B) Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again.

(C) However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly ─ our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 사람들이 협상하는 법을 잘 배우지 못한다는 내용입니다. (B)에서 '협상법을 배우는 사람들(Those who do)'이 전통적인 승패 협상 방식을 배운다는 내용으로 이어지며, 이러한 방식이 일회성 협상에 유용할 수 있다고 언급합니다. (C)에서 '하지만(However)' 그러한 거래는 드물어지고 있는데, 우리가 같은 사람들과 반복적으로 거래하기 때문이라고 설명합니다. (A)에서 '이러한 관점에서(In view of this)' 윈윈(win-win) 결과가 유일하게 수용 가능한 결과가 되고 있다는 결론으로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 39번]
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product.
ordered_passages: (A) However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers may not be completely locked in to the product. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.

(B) For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase.

(C) By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status ─ they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 보완재의 정의를 내리고 있습니다. (B)에서 영화와 팝콘 같은 구체적인 예시를 들며 보완재의 특성(한 제품의 인기가 오르면 다른 제품 매출도 오른다)을 설명합니다. (C)에서는 이러한 보완재 생산이 수요를 보장해준다는 비즈니스적 이점과 완벽한 보완재(램프와 전구)를 언급합니다. (A)에서 '하지만(However)' 완벽한 보완재라고 가정하지 말라는 주의를 주며, 자동차와 휘발유 예시를 통해 소비자가 전기차로 바꿀 수 있다는 예외 상황을 설명합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 29번]
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people ________________________________________. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
options: ① hesitate to criticize or pass judgment on
② are reluctant to interfere in other's business
③ enjoy giving misleading advice to the teams
④ make high-quality criticism like a sports expert
⑤ overestimate their own competence without sufficient knowledge in the field
questions.explanation: 이 글은 스포츠 분야에서 전문 지식이 없는 팬들이나 일반인들이 전문가(경영진, 종사자)에게 훈수를 두거나 비판하는 현상에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 'Monday Morning Quarterback'이라는 용어와 의사나 회계사에게는 하지 않는 조언을 스포츠 조직에는 쉽게 한다는 내용을 통해, 사람들이 해당 분야의 충분한 지식 없이 자신의 능력을 과대평가하여 조언한다는 점을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 비판하거나 판단을 내리는 것을 주저한다
② 타인의 사업에 간섭하기를 꺼려한다
③ 팀에게 잘못된 정보를 주는 조언을 즐긴다
④ 스포츠 전문가처럼 수준 높은 비판을 한다
⑤ 해당 분야의 충분한 지식 없이 자신의 능력을 과대평가한다

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is __________________________. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① based on published scientific papers
② useless like pressure waves in the forest
③ informing the audience of scientific experiments
④ knowledge transfer from experts to non-experts
⑤ two-way engagement for mutual understandings
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학적 의사소통이 단순히 정보를 발표하는 것에 그치지 않고, 독자가 그것을 받아들이고 이해해야 완성된다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 소리가 들려야 소리로서 존재하듯, 과학 논문도 이해되어야 의미가 있다는 논리이므로 빈칸에는 상호 이해를 위한 양방향적 관여라는 의미가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 출판된 과학 논문에 기반한다
② 숲속의 압력파처럼 쓸모없다
③ 청중에게 과학 실험을 알린다
④ 전문가로부터 비전문가로의 지식 전달이다
⑤ 상호 이해를 위한 양방향 관여이다

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development _______________________. One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Gobekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up radically remaking the society itself. Things are not so different in our own time.
options: ③ can tell us the building technique
④ are used as the criteria of wealth
⑤ are also motivating another construction
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 건물을 짓는 것 같지만 사실 건물과 건축 과정이 인간 사회를 바꾼다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 터키의 괴베클리 테페 유적지 건설 사례를 통해 수렵 채집인이었던 사람들이 건축물을 짓기 위해 정착하게 되었고 결국 농경 사회가 되었다는 내용을 설명하고 있으므로 빈칸에는 건축물이 우리의 생활 방식을 바꾸고 있다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간의 창의성을 보여준다
② 우리의 생활 방식을 바꾸고 있다
③ 건축 기술을 우리에게 말해줄 수 있다
④ 부의 기준으로 사용된다
⑤ 또한 다른 건설을 동기 부여한다

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>에 주어진 모든 어휘를 한 번씩만 사용하여 영문을 완성하시오. (어휘를 추가하거나 어형을 변화시키지 말 것) [23년 9월 34번]
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are ─ writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. <u>능력이라는 것이 어떻게 정의 되던지, 문제는 발생한다</u> when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
subjective_conditions: 어휘를 추가하거나 어형을 변화시키지 말 것
<보기>의 모든 어휘를 한 번씩만 사용할 것
questions.answer: however ability may be defined a problem occurs
questions.explanation: '~이 어떻게 ...하더라도'의 의미를 가진 양보의 부사절 'however + 주어 + may be + 과거분사' 구문을 사용하여 영작한다. 'however ability may be defined' (능력이 어떻게 정의되더라도) 뒤에 주절 'a problem occurs' (문제가 발생한다)를 연결한다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing and then experimenting in a dark room, searching for evidence of a cat that wasn't there.
questions.summary_sentence: Concepts are necessary far human survival, but they can also (A)___________ us by (B)___________ our understanding of the warld.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 개념(concepts)이 본질주의(essentialism)로 이어져 존재하지 않는 것을 보게 만들 수 있다는 위험성을 설명하고 있습니다. 과학사에서 '에테르'의 사례를 통해 잘못된 개념이 과학자들을 헛된 탐구로 이끌었음을 보여줍니다. 따라서 요약문에서 개념은 인간의 생존에 필수적이지만, 세상에 대한 우리의 이해를 (B)왜곡함으로써(distorting) 우리를 (A)현혹시킬(delude) 수 있다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 현혹시키다 (B) 왜곡함
② (A) 깨우다 (B) 되돌려 놓음
③ (A) 보호하다 (B) 제쳐 놓음
④ (A) 위태롭게 하다 (B) 증가시킴
⑤ (A) 오도하다 (B) 내세움

questions.question: 2. 다음 중 어휘의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Like reality television stars, social media celebrities are often ⓐ<u>condemned</u> for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism ⓑ<u>understates</u> the fact that digital content creators face real obstacles to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity ⓒ<u>redefines</u> the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with ⓓ<u>innate</u> qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and ⓔ<u>frequent</u> interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.explanation: 해당 문장은 디지털 콘텐츠 제작자들이 엘리트 유명인의 영역으로 넘어가는 데 실질적인 장애물에 직면해 있다는 사실을 이러한 비판이 '간과하고 있다'는 맥락이 되어야 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 'understates(축소해서 말하다)'는 문맥상 적절하지 않으며 'overlooks(간과하다)' 혹은 'ignores'와 같은 의미의 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 부분이 있는 문장은?
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>There is an excellent alternative to calming traffic, which is removing traffic</u>. Some cities hold an extensive network for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. ⓑ<u>These motivate people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone</u>. ⓒ<u>As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them</u>. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. ⓓ<u>Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener</u>. ⓔ<u>A tightly packed delivery truck is a great deal of more efficient than several hybrids</u>. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.explanation: ⓔ 문장에서 비교급 형용사인 'more efficient'를 수식하기 위해 'a great deal'이라는 표현을 쓴 것은 적절하지만, 그 뒤에 'of'를 붙여 'a great deal of'라고 쓰면 이는 셀 수 없는 명사를 수식하는 형용사구로 쓰입니다. 비교급 수식어구로는 'a great deal' 혹은 'much', 'far', 'even', 'still', 'a lot' 등이 쓰여야 하므로 'of'를 삭제해야 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where _____________________.
options: ① roles and responsibilities are ambiguous within the organization
② decision making is distributed across various levels within the organization
③ managerial power is distributed to the highest level of the hierarchy
④ working environment is too narrow and rigid to facilitate cooperation
⑤ procedures look complicated to allow the amicable settlement of conflicts
questions.explanation: 글은 조직의 구조(기계적 vs 유기적)에 따른 차이를 설명하고 있습니다. 기계적 구조가 수직적 계층과 많은 의사결정 단계를 가지는 것과 대조적으로, 유기적 구조는 수평적인 특성을 가지므로 의사결정이 조직 내 다양한 수준에 걸쳐 분산되어 있다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 조직 내에서 역할과 책임이 모호하다
② 의사 결정이 조직 내의 다양한 수준에 걸쳐 분산되어 있다
③ 관리 권한이 계층 구조의 최고 수준에 분포되어 있다
④ 작업 환경이 너무 좁고 경직되어 협력을 촉진하기 어렵다
⑤ 갈등의 원만한 해결을 허용하기 위해 절차가 복잡해 보인다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO₂ a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to mitigate climate change.
options: ① the campaign to end the slaughter of whales
② the negative impact of overabundant species on the environment
③ the contribution of whales to climate change alleviation
④ the necessity of protecting marine ecosystems
⑤ the climate-friendly gardening to reduce greenhouse gas emissions
questions.explanation: 본문은 고래가 탄소 저장에 매우 효율적이며, 배설물을 통해 식물성 플랑크톤의 번식을 도와 추가적인 탄소 흡수를 돕는다는 점을 설명합니다. 따라서 고래를 보호하고 복원하는 것이 기후 변화를 완화하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다는 내용이므로 주제로 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고래 학살을 중단하기 위한 캠페인
② 과잉 개체수가 환경에 미치는 부정적인 영향
③ 기후 변화 완화에 대한 고래의 기여
④ 해양 생태계 보호의 필요성
⑤ 온실가스 배출을 줄이기 위한 기후 친화적인 정원 가꾸기

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. Between 2000 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category(typically 18-23).
ordered_passages: (A) In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development.

(B) The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy.

(C) In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback.

(D) In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 고등 교육이 엘리트 중심에서 대중 시스템으로 확대되었다는 사실을 제시합니다. (B) 이러한 확장의 특징과 경제를 위한 전문 인력 양성이라는 정치적 필요성을 설명합니다. (A) 이론적으로(In theory) 이러한 확장은 평생 학습을 가능하게 하는 평가 방식으로 이어져야 한다고 언급합니다. (C) 하지만 현실적으로(In reality) 대중화된 고등 교육은 효율적인 평가(시험, 퀴즈)를 요구하게 되어 학생들을 피드백보다 성적에 집중하게 만든다는 모순을 지적합니다. (D) 이와 대조적으로(In contrast) 과거 엘리트 시스템에서는 학생 수가 적어 교사와 학생 간의 긴밀한 관계와 형성적 피드백이 가능했음을 설명하며 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 중 어휘의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds ①<u>more</u> dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively ②<u>poorly</u> populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will ③<u>decrease</u>. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been ④<u>declining</u> for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or ⑤<u>recovered</u> populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: 마지막 문장에서 무산소 사건(anoxic events)은 해양 생물들을 죽이거나 개체군을 파괴하는 부정적인 상황을 초래해야 합니다. 하지만 '회복시키다'라는 뜻의 recovered는 문맥상 전혀 적절하지 않으므로, decimated(대량으로 죽이다)나 destroyed 같이 나쁜 영향을 주는 단어로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 관의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
options: ① Imitation is an essential step on the path to mastery.
② The world's greatest composers overshadowed their rivals.
③ Even effective composers struggled with their own limitations.
④ It is originality that differentiates the great works from the others.
⑤ Unfamiliar works may not be appreciated when they are released.
questions.explanation: 이 관은 위대한 작곡가들이 뉹시에 이해받지 뮻한 이유가 그들의 새로운 아이디어(낮설음)에 있음을 설명하며, 살리에리의 예를 통해 독창성(originality)이 결여된 작품은 위대한 작품이 될 수 없음을 강조합니다. 따라서 제목으로 ④ '위대한 작품과 다른 작품을 차별화하는 것은 바로 독창성이다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 모방은 숙별로 가는 길에서 필수적인 단계이다.
② 세계의 위대한 작곡가들은 그들의 라이벌들을 무물리쳐다.
③ 유능한 작곡가들조차 그들 자신의 한계와 싸웠다.
④ 위대한 작품과 남들을 구별짓는 것은 바로 독창성이다.
⑤ 낮설은 작품은 발표되었을 때 제대로 평가받지 뮻할 수 있다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 관의 문줄 챜 부분이 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
questions.passage: All the actors on the stage were focused on their acting. Then, suddenly, Arthur fell into the corner of the stage. Jeevan immediately approached Arthur and found ␀<u>his</u> heart wasn't beating. Jeevan began CPR. Jeevan worked silently, glancing sometimes at Arthur's face. He thought, "Please, start breathing again, please." Arthur's eyes were closed. Moments later, an older man in a grey suit appeared, swiftly kneeling beside ␁<u>his</u> chest. "I'm Walter Jacobi. I'm a doctor." He announced with a calm voice, carefully checking ␂<u>the patient</u>'s condition. Then, he took over from Jeevan and continued CPR. As time went on, he got very sweaty, absorbed in the treatment. Jeevan wanted to help in any way he could, so he wiped the sweat off his forehead to avoid interfering with the doctor's CPR on ␃<u>him</u>. With combined efforts, Jeevan and Dr. Jacobi successfully revived him. Arthur's eyes slowly opened. Finally, Jeevan was able to hear Arthur's breath again, thinking to ␄<u>himself</u>, "Thank goodness. You're back."
questions.explanation: ① ␀(his), ② ␁(his), ③ ␂(the patient), ④ ␃(him)은 모됐 쓰러진 배우인 Arthur를 가리킬니다. 반면 ⑤ ␄(himself)는 Arthur가 깨어난 것을 보고 안도하며 수숐로 생각한 Jeevan을 가리킬니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 "The ether was a black cat"이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 33번]
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. <u>The ether was a black cat</u>, writes Firestein, and physicists had been looking for illusive evidence of a cat in a dark room.
options: ① Light moved through the ether that fills the universe.
② Although the ether was always there, it had not been recognized before.
③ The ether exists not only in universe, but also in a dark room on our planet.
④ It was extremely hard to find Luminiferous ether, because it had been unknown.
⑤ Luminiferous ether did not actually exist, which means it was a misleading concept.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 언급된 속담 '검은 고양이가 없는 어두운 방에서 검은 고양이를 찾는 것은 어렵다'는 존재하지 않는 본질을 찾는 헛된 노력을 비유합니다. 따라서 '에테르가 검은 고양이였다'는 말은 에테르가 실제로는 존재하지 않았으며, 과학자들이 잘못된 개념을 바탕으로 존재하지 않는 증거를 찾으려 했음을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 빛은 우주를 채우고 있는 에테르를 통해 이동했다.
② 에테르가 항상 존재했음에도 불구하고 이전에는 인식되지 않았다.
③ 에테르는 우주뿐만 아니라 우리 행성의 어두운 방에도 존재한다.
④ 발광 에테르는 알려지지 않았기 때문에 찾기가 매우 어려웠다.
⑤ 발광 에테르는 실제로는 존재하지 않았으며, 이는 그것이 잘못된 개념이었음을 의미한다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [24년 9월 24번]
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems."
questions.explanation: 해당 지문에서 일반적인 나무 한 그루는 1년에 '48파운드'의 이산화탄소를 흡수한다고 명시되어 있으나, 정답이 ②번인 것으로 보아 선지에는 이 수치가 잘못 기재되었거나(예: 48톤 등) 일치하지 않는 내용이 포함되어 있었을 것으로 추론됩니다. (선지가 제공되지 않았으나 문제 형식상 내용 불일치 문제임)

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 가장 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 9월 34번]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents ⓐ<u>associated</u> with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to ⓑ<u>crossing</u> over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point ⓒ<u>that</u> the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and ⓓ<u>related</u> to naturalized qualities of talent. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks which ⓔ<u>built</u> into social media applications.
questions.explanation: ⓔ 관계대명사 which의 선행사는 metrics(지표들)이며, 지표들이 소셜 미디어 앱에 내장되어 있는 상태를 설명하므로 수동태인 are built 또는 built(과거분사) 형태로 쓰여야 문맥상 적절합니다. 여기서는 동사 자리이므로 are built가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 어휘의 쓰임이 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 9월 39번]
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively ①<u>poorly</u> populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will ②<u>increase</u>. This is a worrisome and potentially ③<u>devastating</u> consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been ④<u>declining</u> more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more ⑤<u>frequent</u> anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.*dissolved: 개댜나내 **anoxic: 사노 겨비긔 듸
questions.explanation: 차가운 물이 따뜻한 물보다 용존 산소를 더 많이 함유한다는 원리에 따르면, 지구 온난화로 바닷물의 온도가 올라가면 용존 산소량은 '증가'하는 것이 아니라 '감소'하게 됩니다. 따라서 ②번 'increase'를 'decrease'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important not to ____________________. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop-out, or worse.
options: ① limit how much you show off your child
② overwhelm the child with excessive praise
③ support them in whatever they want to achieve
④ suggest only easily reachable goals for your child
⑤ avoid your intervention in how your child performs
questions.explanation: 부모가 영재인 아이의 성취를 너무 뽐내고 자랑하면 아이는 큰 스트레스를 받고 부모의 기대에 부응해야 한다는 압박감을 느끼게 됩니다. 따라서 아이를 과도한 칭찬으로 압도하지 않는 것이 중요하다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 아이를 자랑하는 정도를 제한하다
과도한 칭찬으로 아이를 압도하다
아이가 달성하고자 하는 모든 것을 지원하다
아이에게 쉽게 도달할 수 있는 목표만 제안하다
아이가 수행하는 방식에 대한 개입을 피하다

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had ____________________, they would not have evolved with us.
options: ① helped us adapt and survive
② made us avoid all the potential threats
③ been not helpful for our prosperity as a species
④ encouraged us to distract our enemy's attention
⑤ shaped our tendency to respond to various stimuli
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 감정이 종의 생존에 기여했기 때문에 진화적으로 존재하게 되었다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸이 포함된 문장은 가정법 과거완료 문장으로, '만약 감정들이 (우리 종의 번영에 도움이 되지) 않았더라면, 우리와 함께 진화하지 않았을 것이다'라는 논리가 성립해야 합니다. 따라서 ③ '종으로서의 번영에 도움이 되지 않았다면'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 적응하고 생존하도록 도왔다면
② 모든 잠재적인 위협을 피하게 만들었다면
③ 종으로서 우리의 번영에 도움이 되지 않았더라면
④ 적의 주의를 분산시키도록 장려했다면
⑤ 다양한 자극에 반응하는 우리의 경향을 형성했다면

questions.question: 29. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. ⓐPreschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. ⓑThey do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. ⓒIf a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. ⓓThinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. ⓔSimilarly, when they are told things like "You're always the best" despite a lack of effort or achievement, they may struggle with feelings of inadequacy when they face failure.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 부모의 칭찬이 어린 아이의 자아존중감 형성과 긍정적 자기 이미지 구축에 미치는 영향입니다. ⓔ 문장은 노력이나 성취 없이 무조건적인 칭찬을 들을 때 겪게 되는 부작용(무력감)에 대해 언급하고 있으므로, 부모의 긍정적 피드백이 아이의 자아상 형성에 긍정적 역할을 한다는 전체 흐름과 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 31. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. ⓐAI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. ⓑFor example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. ⓒAI can also be a threatening competitor to the low-skilled workers, potentially replacing them in the workplace by offering much lower costs and higher efficiency. ⓓAI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. ⓔMoreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.*dysarthric: (신경 장애로 인한) 구음(構音) 장애의
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 AI가 직장 내 포용성을 증진시키고 취약 계층의 노동 시장 접근성을 높인다는 긍정적인 영향에 관한 것입니다. ⓒ 문장은 AI가 저숙련 노동자를 대체할 수 있는 위협적인 경쟁자라는 부정적인 측면을 언급하고 있으므로 전체적인 긍정적 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 32. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle.
ordered_passages: (A) Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener.

(B) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them.

(C) A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.*animus: 반감, 미움
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 교통을 줄이기 위해 자전거와 보행자 전용 도로를 만드는 도시들의 사례를 언급합니다. (B)의 'This'는 주어진 글에서 언급된 전용 도로 구축을 의미하며, 이를 통해 자전거가 활성화되는 과정을 설명합니다. (A)에서는 'Nevertheless'를 통해 자전거 중심 도시라도 필수적인 자동차(택시, 배달 차량 등)가 필요함을 언급하며 배달 차량의 중요성을 화두로 던집니다. (C)는 (A)의 마지막 부분에서 언급한 배달 차량이 왜 도시를 더 친환경적으로 만드는 필수 요소인지에 대한 구체적인 이유를 설명하고 있으므로 순서는 (B)-(A)-(C)가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 34. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. (A) Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. (B) This sense of confidence often comes from the accessibility of sports, where the outcomes and strategies are widely visible to the public (C) For instance, students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. (D) Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. (E) However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.insertion_sentence: This goes for the boardroom as well.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장 'This goes for the boardroom as well(이는 이사회실/경영진에서도 마찬가지다)'은 앞에서 언급한 스포츠 팬들의 참견이 경기 현장을 넘어 경영 분야까지 이어진다는 흐름의 전환을 나타냅니다. (C) 앞부분까지는 팬들이 경기장에서의 플레이와 코칭에 대해 참견한다는 내용이며, (C) 이후부터 'sport business' 학위 소지자나 'executives(경영진)'에 대한 참견 사례가 나오므로 정답은 (C)인 ③번 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 35. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 41-42번]
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. Between 2000 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students.Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialized workforce for the economy.In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardized feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback.In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.*demographic: 인구집단
questions.summary_sentence: The passage explains the shift from elite to mass higher education globally. Participation in higher education dramatically (A)__________ between 2000 and 2014, driven by the need for a skilled workforce. While the aim was to promote lifelong learning, mass higher education led to more (B)__________ assessments like exams and quizzes, focusing students on grades rather than (C)__________ comments. This contrasts with the approaches in earlier, elite systems.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 고등교육 참여율이 19%에서 34%로 거의 두 배가 되었다고 했으므로 (A)에는 급증했다는 의미의 'soared' 또는 'increased'가 적절합니다. 대중 고등교육 시스템에서는 효율성을 위해 'minimalist, impersonal, or standardized feedback'을 제공한다고 했으므로 (B)에는 'impersonal(비인격적인)'이 적절합니다. 과거 엘리트 시스템에서는 학생과 교사의 긴밀한 관계를 통해 형성적 피드백이 제공되었던 것과 대조적으로, 대중 교육 시스템에서는 개별적인 의견(personal comments)보다는 성적에 집중하게 되었음을 의미하므로 (C)에는 'personal'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 급증했다 ... 비인격적인 ... 개인적인
② 증가했다 ... 효율적인 ... 표준화된
③ 증가했다 ... 비인격적인 ... 표준화된
④ 급락했다 ... 효율적인 ... 형성적인
⑤ 급락했다 ... 비인격적인 ... 개인적인

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. (A) This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. (B) The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. (C) On the other hand, the ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. (D) Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game. (E) It is because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, it also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '하지만 그것은 평범한 유명인이라는 현상이 명성의 의미를 재구성한다는 점을 놓치고 있다'는 내용입니다. (B) 앞부분까지는 소셜 미디어 제작자들이 전통적인 엘리트 유명인의 기술이 부족하다는 비판을 받는다는 내용이 나오며, (B) 이후부터는 전통적인 '엘리트 유명인'과 대비되는 '평범한 유명인'의 특성을 설명하기 시작합니다. 따라서 비판이 놓치고 있는 점을 언급하며 내용의 전환을 알리는 주어진 문장은 (B)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. ⑀Effective composers consistently bring their own unique ideas to their work. ⑁The composer Antonio Salieri is the -host- of the movie Amadeus, depicted as a famous composer. ⑂But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. ⑃The great compositions were made from impressive imitation, skillfully blending existing styles into something familiar. ⑄What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 위대한 작곡가들의 작품이 초기에 수용되지 않았던 이유는 '생소함(unfamiliarity)' 때문이며, 그들의 위대함은 독창성(originality)에서 온다는 것입니다. 살리에리가 위대한 작곡가가 되지 못한 이유가 독창성 부족과 당시 다른 이들과 비슷한 음악을 썼기 때문이라는 흐름에서, 위대한 작품이 '모방(imitation)'과 '친숙한 것(familiar)'에서 만들어졌다는 ⑃번 문장은 전체 흐름과 정반대되는 내용입니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop-out, or worse.
options: ① Keep It Minimum: Showing off How Talented Your Child Is
② Parents' Bragging Sometimes Benefits Children's Development
③ An Effective Way to Figure Out Whether Your Child Is Gifted
④ Frequent Praise from Parents Enhances Children's Self-Esteem
⑤ Not Giving Too Much Pressure on Your Child with Indifference
questions.explanation: 이 글은 영재 아이를 둔 부모들이 아이의 재능을 너무 과시하는 것이 아이에게 스트레스와 압박감을 줄 수 있으므로, 자랑하는 행위를 최소한으로 제한해야 한다는 조언을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '아이의 재능 과시를 최소한으로 유지하라'는 의미의 1번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 최소한으로 하라: 당신의 아이가 얼마나 재능 있는지 과시하는 것
② 부모의 자랑은 때때로 아이의 발달에 도움이 된다
③ 당신의 아이가 영재인지 알아내는 효과적인 방법
④ 부모로부터의 빈번한 칭찬은 아이의 자존감을 높인다
⑤ 무관심으로 아이에게 너무 많은 압박을 주지 않기

questions.question: 7. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Some researchers point out that when ships slow down, the wider community benefits: slower ships not only hit fewer whales but also create less noise pollution, release fewer environmental pollutants, and emit less carbon dioxide.
ordered_passages: (A) In 2019, economists estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a -nature-based solution- to climate change.

(B) For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO₂ a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon.

(C) Hurting fewer whales itself also benefits the global environment since they help mitigate climate change. Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 선박의 속도를 늦추는 것이 고래를 보호하며 환경에 이득이 된다는 점을 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 고래가 탄소를 저장함으로써 기후 변화 완화에 어떻게 기여하는지 구체적으로 설명합니다. 이어 (B)에서 고래 한 마리의 가치를 수천 그루의 나무와 비교하며 그 중요성을 강조하고, 마지막으로 (A)에서 고래의 경제적 가치를 기반으로 한 개체수 복원 장려 프로그램을 제안하는 (C)-(B)-(A)의 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. (A)___________, if you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting -paid- the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. (B)___________, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
options: ④ On the other hand / For example
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서는 동일하게 오이를 받아 먹는 상황이었으나, 다음 문장에서는 다른 원숭이에게 포도를 주었을 때 오이를 받는 원숭이의 반응이 달라지므로 역접을 나타내는 However가 적절합니다. (B) 앞서 언급한 불공평한 상황에 더해, 원숭이 자신이 오이를 버리며 불만을 직접적으로 표출하는 추가 행동을 설명하고 있으므로 나열/첨가의 Furthermore가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나 / 게다가
② 마찬가지로 / 게다가
③ 예를 들어 / 요약하면
④ 반면에 / 예를 들어
⑤ 마찬가지로 / 예를 들어

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 a new kind of goggles가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on <u>a new kind of goggles</u>. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show - whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① an instrument helping to clarify perspectives on political issues
② technological hardware which is required to view new media
③ an information-collecting tool affecting how we interpret reality
④ a device that shifts our focus from format to content itself
⑤ a resource that lets us know what to watch and what to avoid
questions.explanation: 필자는 새로운 매체가 등장할 때마다 그것이 세상을 보는 방식(코드)을 바꾼다고 말하고 있습니다. '새로운 종류의 고글'을 쓴다는 것은 특정 매체를 통해 세상을 바라봄으로써 우리가 현실을 해석하는 방식에 영향을 주는 정보 수집 도구 혹은 틀을 의미합니다.

questions.question: 11. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been ⓐ<u>surprised</u> to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really ⓑ<u>what</u> my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route ⓒ<u>which</u> we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations ⓓ<u>are conducted</u> through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice ⓔ<u>sound</u> deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
options: ① Why We Tend to Feel Familiar with Our Own Voice in Recordings
② How Bone Vibrations Affect Our Perception of Our Own Voice
③ The Role of the Middle and Outer Ear in Sound Transmission
④ How Vibrations and External Sounds Influence Our Hearing
⑤ Why Some People Have Higher-Pitched Voices Than Others
questions.explanation: 글은 우리가 자신의 목소리를 들을 때 뼈의 진동을 통한 내부 경로가 추가로 작용하여 타인이 듣는 것보다 더 낮고 풍부하게 들린다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat."
ordered_passages: (A) The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
(B) Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through.

(C) This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글의 격언 내용을 (C)의 'This statement'로 받아 과학자들이 잘못된 개념으로 본질을 찾으려 했던 사례를 언급합니다. (B)에서 그 사례로 'luminiferous ether'를 도입하고, (A)에서 에테르를 다시 '존재하지 않는 검은 고양이'에 비유하며 내용을 완결합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by ______________________________.
options: ④ reconstructing the meaning of words
⑤ restricting interactions with the public
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런의 발견을 통해 인간의 '관찰을 통한 학습' 능력을 강조하고 있습니다. 신생아가 부모의 혀 내밀기를 따라 하거나, 아기가 부모의 소리와 행동(청소기, 망치질 등)을 모방한다는 사례를 통해 인간이 타인의 행동을 관찰함으로써 많은 것을 배운다는 점을 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 이러한 '관찰 학습'의 핵심인 '주변 사람들을 지켜보는 것'이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리 자신의 재능에 집중함으로써
② 우리 주변 사람들을 관찰함으로써
③ 끊임없이 아이디어를 발전시킴으로써
④ 단어의 의미를 재구성함으로써
⑤ 대중과의 상호작용을 제한함으로써

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)this가 가리키는 것을 우리말로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - (A)<u>this</u> is one reason that cold polar seas are full of lite while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. (B)<u>[impact / in water / to / oxygen levels / falling / of marine organisms / the potential / the habitat / have]</u> and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.answer: 차가운 물이 따뜻한 물보다 더 많은 용존 산소를 함유한다는 사실
questions.explanation: 문장의 앞부분인 'cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does'를 지칭합니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 (B)가 어법 및 문맥상 올바른 문장이 될 수 있도록 주어진 모든 단어를 순서에 맞게 배열하여 쓰시오.

questions.question: 22. [24년 9월 22번] 윗글의 ⓐ~ⓓ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 고른 뒤 올바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, and expressing positive emotions ⓐ<u>helps</u> us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when ⓑ<u>trigger</u>, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation or ⓒ<u>avoid</u> it, and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways ⓓ<u>in which</u> they activate our systems, the specific emotions we have had are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. (A)<u>만약 그것들이 우리가 생존하도록 도와주지 않았었더라면 그것들은 우리와 함께 진화해 오지 않았을 것이다</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 'when triggered' 구문은 'when (it is) triggered'에서 주어와 be동사가 생략된 분사구문이다. 감정(an emotion)은 유발되는 수동의 관계이므로 과거분사 triggered가 적절하다. ⓐ 주어가 동명사구(expressing positive emotions)이므로 단수 동사 helps는 적절하다. ⓒ face와 avoid가 or로 연결된 병렬구조이다. ⓓ 관계부사 how를 대신하여 '전치사+관계대명사'인 in which가 쓰였으며 뒷문장이 완전하므로 적절하다.

조건을 벗어난 단어를 사용하거나 주어진 우리말 해석과 차이가 있을 시 감점될 수 있음.
questions.answer: If they hadn't helped us survive, they wouldn't have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: 과거 사실에 대한 반대를 가정하는 가정법 과거완료(If + 주어 + had p.p., 주어 + 조동사의 과거형 + have p.p.) 구문을 사용하여 영작한다. '도와주지 않았었더라면(had not helped)'과 '진화해 오지 않았을 것이다(would not have evolved)'를 조건에 맞춰 구성한다.

questions.question: 24. [24년 9월 18번] 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)the recent change가 가리키는 것을 우리말로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: To Whom It May Concern, I am writing to express my deep concern regarding (A)<u>the recent change</u> made at Pittsburgh Train Station. The traditional ticket offices, which were previously staffed with personnel, have now been replaced by ticket vending machines. Unfortunately, many individuals who had been unfamiliar with these machines had experienced significant difficulties in accessing railway services. These passengers, who had long relied on the assistance of station staff, found themselves struggling without the support they needed to continue traveling. The absence of human-operated ticket offices had created a barrier for those who had depended on personalized assistance. (B)<u>I urge you to consider the impact of this change, hope that reopening the ticket offices remains an option to restore access for those in need</u>.Sincerely,Sarah Roberts
