questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. (A) Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. (B) But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. (C) Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. (D) If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? (E) Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '하지만 대부분의 사람들은 불안감을 가장 적게 유발하는 선택안을 고른다'는 내용입니다. (D)에서 위험을 감수할 때 자신에게 유리한 확률을 원하지 않겠느냐고 논리적으로 묻고 있고, (E) 뒤에서 감정이 아닌 사실에 근거하여 결정을 내리라는 조언이 나옵니다. 사람들의 실제 선택 경향(불안 최소화)을 설명하고 그에 대한 조언으로 넘어가는 연결 고리인 (E) 자리가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives.
options: ③ 아이들은 그들 부모의 가치를 공유한다.
④ 아이들은 단순히 가치들에 대해 들음으로써 가치를 배우지 않는다.
⑤ 아이들은 아이들 주변의 사람들이 그 가치를 유지하는 것을 봄으로써 배운다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 부모(어른)가 아이들에게 본보기를 보여줌으로써 아이들이 가치관을 배운다는 내용입니다. 지문에서는 '그들(아이들)은 보는 것으로부터 배운다(They learn from seeing)'라고 했지, 어른들이 보는 것으로부터 배운다는 내용은 핵심 주제가 아니며 지문 근거와도 거리가 멉니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And (A)___________, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. (B)___________, we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
questions.explanation: (A) 소리가 들려야 존재하듯 과학적 의사소통도 받는 사람이 있어야 한다는 유사한 원리를 적용하고 있으므로 'similarly(마찬가지로)'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞의 논리(이해되지 않으면 소용없다)를 바탕으로 과학의 격언을 재진술하고 있으므로 결론을 이끄는 'Therefore(따라서)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 하지만 / (B) 대조적으로
② (A) 하지만 / (B) 그러므로
③ (A) 게다가 / (B) 그럼에도 불구하고
④ (A) 마찬가지로 / (B) 그러므로
⑤ (A) 마찬가지로 / (B) 대조적으로

questions.question: 17. 윗글의 밑줄 친 to maintain our spot at the top이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says hardly humans ⓐ<u>respect</u> similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language not to ⓑ<u>distance</u> the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence ⓒ<u>demonstrating</u> that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how ⓓ<u>certain</u> bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to ⓔ<u>downplay</u> animals, the way we invent words <u>to maintain our spot at the top</u>.
options: ① to keep humans and animals in harmony at the top
② to argue with primatologists about linguistic castration
③ to define the relationship as friendship and partnership
④ to think of ourselves as the best species among animals
⑤ to get humans to act like other animals to follow animals
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 언어적 장치(전문 용어 사용 등)를 통해 인간과 다른 동물의 유사성을 부정하고 인간의 우월적 지위를 유지하려 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '정상의 자리를 유지한다'는 것은 인간 스스로를 동물 중 최고의 종으로 생각한다는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 인간과 동물을 정상에서 조화롭게 유지하기 위해
② 언어적 거세에 대해 영장류 학자들과 논쟁하기 위해
③ 관계를 우정과 동반자 관계로 정의하기 위해
④ 우리 자신을 동물들 중 최고의 종으로 생각하기 위해
⑤ 인간들이 다른 동물을 따르기 위해 다른 동물처럼 행동하게 하기 위해

questions.question: 18. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says hardly humans ⓐ<u>respect</u> similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language not to ⓑ<u>distance</u> the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence ⓒ<u>demonstrating</u> that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how ⓓ<u>certain</u> bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to ⓔ<u>downplay</u> animals, the way we invent words <u>to maintain our spot at the top</u>.
questions.explanation: 과학자들이 인간과 동물의 유사성을 부인하기 위해 전문 용어를 사용하는 것이므로, 동물을 우리와 '거리 두기 위해서(to distance)' 언어를 사용하는 것입니다. 따라서 'not to distance'는 문맥상 어색하며 'to distance'로 쓰여야 합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Moving is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is not __________ for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place.
questions.explanation: 3~6세 아이들은 이해력이 상당히 문자 그대로(literal)이기 때문에, 실제로 가보지 않은 새로운 집이나 방을 미리 상상하는 것이 '쉽지(easy)' 않습니다. 앞에 'not'이 있으므로 'not easy'가 되어야 문맥이 성립합니다.
options_translation: ① 스트레스가 많은
② 어려운
③ 쉬운
④ 혼란스러운
⑤ 당황한

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games.
ordered_passages: (A) Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields.(B) You quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field on the comments. This goes for the boardroom as well.(C) However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 'Monday Morning Quarterback'이라는 용어와 SNS상의 팬들의 의견을 언급하며 시작합니다. (B)에서 그 소셜 미디어의 댓글 내용을 구체적으로 설명하며 이것이 이사회실(boardroom)에도 해당한다고 확장합니다. (A)에서는 이와 유사하게 스포츠 비즈니스 전문가들이 전문 지식 없는 사람들로부터 조언을 받는 상황을 묘사합니다. (C)에서는 'However'를 통해 이러한 전문가들이 비판을 받는 현실을 지적하며 다른 전문직(의사, 회계사)과는 대조적인 스포츠 경영 분야의 특성을 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that ⓐ<u>pick</u> up a particular sensation. If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. ⓑ<u>Although</u> the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a protective mechanism for the foot. Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area ⓒ<u>where</u> controls speech, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and ⓓ<u>to</u> the muscles in your leg that now contract quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object. Sensory and motor nerves control almost all functions in the body - from the ⓔ<u>beating</u> of the heart to the movement of the gut, sweating and just about everything else.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 절을 보면 'controls'라는 동사가 바로 이어지므로, 주어 역할을 할 주격 관계대명사가 필요합니다. 선행사가 'the area'이므로 관계부사인 'where' 대신 주격 관계대명사인 'which'나 'that'을 사용해야 합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it - you just see the ⓐ<u>clear</u> outline of the moving string. Strings vibrating in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are not ⓑ<u>thick</u> enough to push much air about. But if you ⓒ<u>hang</u> a string on a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is ⓓ<u>amplified</u> and the note is heard loud. The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. When the waves ⓔ<u>get</u> to your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of time a second as the original string.
questions.explanation: 기타 줄이 초당 수백 번 앞뒤로 움직일 때, 그 움직임이 너무 빨라서 눈으로 볼 수 없고 움직이는 줄의 '흐릿한(blurry)' 윤곽만을 보게 됩니다. 따라서 ⓐ의 clear(선명한)는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are not ⓐ<u>clear</u> as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are ⓑ<u>maximized</u>. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" ⓒ<u>having</u> two phones - one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer ⓓ<u>uniting</u> work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or ⓔ<u>checking</u> emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.explanation: 역할을 분리하거나 분할하는 사람들은 경계 교차(한 영역이 다른 영역에 영향을 미치는 것)를 최소화하기 위해 노력합니다. 따라서 ⓑ의 maximized(최대화된)는 minimized(최소화된)로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
options: ① the impact of changes in a child's routine in a new environment on their psychology
② the difficulty in addressing the various concerns that children may have due to moving
③ the emotional impact of moving on young children and how to support their adjustment
④ how relocating intensifies children's feelings of depression caused by moving to a new environment
⑤ the importance of helping children make friends to adapt well to a new environment after moving
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이사가 어린 아이들에게 주는 정서적 영향(스트레스, 불안감 등)을 설명하고, 아이들이 과거의 경험을 존중받으면서 새로운 환경에 잘 적응할 수 있도록 돕는 방법(균형 잡기, 배경 공유 기회 제공 등)에 대해 다루고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 새로운 환경에서 아이의 일상 변화가 심리에 미치는 영향
② 이사로 인해 아이들이 가질 수 있는 다양한 우려 사항을 해결하는 것의 어려움
③ 이사가 어린 아이들에게 미치는 정서적 영향과 그들의 적응을 돕는 방법
④ 이전이 어떻게 새로운 환경으로의 이사로 인한 아이들의 우울감을 심화시키는지
⑤ 이사 후 새로운 환경에 잘 적응하기 위해 아이들이 친구를 사귀도록 돕는 것의 중요성

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. (A) Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. (B) Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. (C) This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. (D) In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. (E) In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly ─ our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '일회성 협상(one-off negotiation)'과 대조되는 '반복적인 거래(deal with the same people repeatedly)'에 대해 언급하고 있습니다. (C) 문장에서 일회성 협상에서의 '전통적 방식'의 유용성을 언급한 후, '하지만(However)'으로 시작하는 주어진 문장이 나와야 논리적 흐름이 자연스럽습니다. 그 뒤 (D)의 'In view of this(이러한 관점에서)'는 반복적 관계를 고려해야 한다는 주어진 문장의 내용을 가리킵니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.summary_sentence: Sports management professionals, (A)__________ their years of experience and expertise, often face unwanted advice and criticism from people with no (B)__________ knowledge, unlike other professions such as medicine or accounting.
questions.explanation: 지문은 스포츠 경영 전문가들이 수십 년간의 지식과 경험을 갖추고 있음에도 불구하고, 의사나 회계사와 같은 다른 전문직과는 달리 비전문가나 팬들로부터 훈수와 비판을 자주 받는다는 아이러니한 상황을 다룹니다. 따라서 요약문의 (A)에는 전문성에도 '불구하고(despite)'가 적절하며, (B)에는 비판자들을 수식하는 '관련된(relevant)' 지식이 없다는 표현이 오는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① ~에도 불구하고 ... 관련된
② ~ 때문에 ... 적용 가능한
③ ~에 대항하여 ... 다양한
④ ~에도 불구하고 ... 부적절한

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as ___________________________________________. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
options: ① a cultural factor if natives perceive it as a possible thing to emerge
② an unpleasant element if natives think of it as a basis of socialism
③ an undesirable trait if locals view it as a distortion of their national identity
④ an ethnic feature if natives perceive it as something different from their values
⑤ a valuable characteristic if original inhabitants consider it as a help to their national identity
questions.explanation: 지문은 문화적 다양성이 생산성과 삶의 질을 높이는 긍정적인 측면이 있지만, 정도가 지나칠 경우 소통 비용을 증가시키고 현지인들에게 부정적으로 인식될 수 있음을 설명합니다. 빈칸 뒤에서 현지인들이 타 민족을 차별하거나 사회적 갈등의 유입을 두려워할 수 있다는 보수적인 입장이 제시되므로, 다양성을 자신의 국가적 정체성을 왜곡하는 '바람직하지 않은 특성(undesirable trait)'으로 여길 수 있다는 ③번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 현지인들이 그것을 발생 가능한 것으로 인식할 경우의 문화적 요인
② 현지인들이 그것을 사회주의의 기반으로 생각할 경우의 불쾌한 요소
③ 현지인들이 그것을 자신의 국가 정체성 왜곡으로 볼 경우 바람직하지 않은 특성
④ 현지인들이 그것을 자신의 가치관과 다른 것으로 인식할 경우의 민족적 특징
⑤ 원주민들이 그것을 자신의 국가 정체성에 도움이 된다고 여길 경우의 가치 있는 특징

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Claims that local food production cut greenhouse gas emissions by reducing the burning of transportation fuel are usually not well founded. Transport is the source of only 11 percent of greenhouse gas emissions within the food sector, so reducing the distance that food travels after it leaves the farm is far less important than reducing wasteful energy use on the farm. Food coming from a distance can actually be better for the climate, depending on how it was grown. For example, field-grown tomatoes shipped from Mexico in the winter months will have a smaller carbon footprint than local winter tomatoes grown in a greenhouse. In the United Kingdom, lamb meat that travels 11,000 miles from New Zealand generates only one-quarter the carbon emissions per pound compared to British lamb because farmers in the United Kingdom raise their animals on feed (which must be produced using fossil fuels) rather than on clover pastureland.When food does travel, what matters most is __________________________________________________________. The operation of airplanes releases a significant amount of carbon, emitting much more greenhouse gases compared to transporting the same distance by truck. Also, bulk loads of food can travel halfway around the world by ocean freight with a smaller carbon footprint, per pound delivered, than foods traveling just a short distance but in much smaller loads. For example, 18-wheelers carry much larger loads than pickup trucks so they can move food 100 times as far while burning only one-third as much gas per pound of food delivered.
options: ① the mode of transport and the size of the load rather than the distance traveled
② not the load size but the travel mode and most of all the distance traveled
③ the distance covered and the load size, instead of the method of transport
④ the kind of transport compared to the traveled distance and the scale of load
⑤ more the type of transport than the load scale and the distance covered
questions.explanation: 이 글은 지역 음식을 먹는 것(local food)이 이동 거리를 줄여 탄소 배출을 줄인다는 주장이 근거가 약함을 지적합니다. 글의 후반부에서는 비행기와 트럭의 차이(운송 방식), 그리고 대량 운송과 소량 운송의 차이(적재량의 규모)가 탄소 발자국에 큰 영향을 미친다는 사례들을 들고 있습니다. 따라서 식품이 이동할 때 가장 중요한 것은 이동 거리가 아니라 '운송 방식과 적재량의 규모'라는 내용인 ①이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 이동 거리보다는 운송 방식과 적재량의 규모
② 적재량의 규모가 아니라 이동 방식과 무엇보다 중요한 이동 거리
③ 운송 방법 대신에 이동 거리와 적재량의 규모
④ 이동 거리 및 적재 규모와 비교되는 운송 종류
⑤ 적재 규모와 이동 거리보다는 운송 유형

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, _________________________________.
options: ① they would have been lost in our evolution
② we would have used more gestures in communication
questions.explanation: 이 글은 감정이 인간의 생존을 돕기 위해 진화적으로 형성된 프로그램임을 설명합니다. 공포, 분노, 긍정적 감정 등이 모두 생존과 적응에 기여했기 때문에 현재까지 존재한다는 논리입니다. 따라서 만약 이러한 감정들이 우리가 적응하고 생존하는 데 도움이 되지 않았더라면, 진화 과정에서 소멸되었을 것이라는 추론이 가능하므로 ①이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그것들은 우리의 진화 과정에서 사라졌을 것이다
② 우리는 의사소통에서 더 많은 몸짓을 사용했을 것이다

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, ____________________________________________________________.
options: ① you should start reviewing the materials a few days after learning it
② it's vital to study and self-test, rather than solely focusing on studying
③ you need to read the same material over and over again until you memorize it
④ it's important to make the best use of your working memory and short-term storage space
⑤ it's necessary to find appropriate learning strategy that best fits you and helps increase memory limit
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 벼락치기가 왜 비효율적인지 설명하며, 단기 기억(작업 기억)에 머무는 정보가 장기 기억으로 넘어가기 위해서는 단순히 읽고 공부하는 것뿐만 아니라 스스로를 테스트(retest)하는 과정이 필요하다는 것입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 장기 기억으로의 전환을 위해 '자가 테스트'가 중요하다는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 학습 후 며칠 뒤에 자료를 복습하기 시작해야 한다
② 단순히 공부에만 집중하기보다 공부하고 자가 테스트하는 것이 필수적이다
③ 암기할 때까지 같은 자료를 반복해서 읽어야 한다
④ 작업 기억과 단기 저장 공간을 최대한 활용하는 것이 중요하다
⑤ 당신에게 가장 잘 맞고 기억 한계를 늘리는 데 도움이 되는 적절한 학습 전략을 찾는 것이 필요하다

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. ⓐ<u>For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey</u>. ⓑ<u>When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase</u>. ⓒ<u>By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product</u>. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status ─ they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. ⓓ<u>Developing complementary products is crucial for creating a more integrated and efficient system that meets diverse customer needs</u>. ⓔ<u>However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers may not be completely locked in to the product</u>. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 보완재(한 제품과 함께 소비되는 제품)의 정의와 경제적 특성(한 제품의 인기가 상승하면 보완재의 수요도 함께 상승함), 그리고 소비자가 항상 그 보완재에 묶여있는 것은 아니라는 예외 사항을 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ⓓ는 보완재 개발이 '다양한 고객의 요구를 충족하는 통합적이고 효율적인 시스템 구축'에 중요하다는 내용으로, 보완재의 시장 수요 연동 원리라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 태용으로 알 수 없는 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① Sound requires a listener to exist; otherwise, it is just pressure waves.
② The nature of sound is being explained based on principles of physics.
③ Scientific communication is ineffective unless the audience understands the message.
④ A scientific experiment is unfinished until its results are both released and understood.
⑤ Many scientific papers go unnoticed and fail to have an impact on the intended audience.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 소리의 발생 원리를 과학적 측면에서 설명하는 것이 아니라, 소리가 들리기 위해 청자가 필요하듯이 과학 측정이나 논문도 독자에게 이해되어야 완성된다는 비유적 주윙를 담고 읈다. 물리학적 원리를 설명하는 것은 중심 내용이 아니며 알 수 없다.
options_translation: ① 소리는 존재하기 위해 청자를 필요로 한다. 그렇준 아다면 그것은 단준한 압력파일 봤이다.
② 소리의 백질은 물리학의 원리에 기반하여 설명되고 읈다.
③ 과학적 소통은 청중이 그 메시준를 이해하준 아닎다면 효과가 없다.
④ 과학 실험은 그 결과가 발표되고 이해되기 전까지는 끝난 것이 아니다.
⑤ 많은 과학 논문들이 주목받준 못하고 의도된 독자에게 영향을 미치준 못한다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 붽분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along ─ whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS ─ and you start to use it, it feels like you're trying on a ␀<u>different</u> set of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Every set of goggles you wear makes you ␁<u>stick</u> to the way you see things. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show ─ whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire ─ you start to shape your view of the world to ␂<u>resemble </u>the medium, television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans to communicate ─ it has ␃<u>concealed</u> in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about ␄<u>outer</u> looks and appearances.
questions.explanation: 매체가 바뵌때뤱다 세상을 바라보는 방식이 바봄다는 내용이므로, 기존의 방식을 고수한다(stick)는 표현은 문맥상 어색하다. 새로운 고글을 쓰면 보는 방식이 변화한다(change/adjust)는 내용이 와야 한다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention ①<u>is potential an instrument</u> to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities ②<u>are often criticized for</u> not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face ③<u>real barriers to crossing over</u> to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated ④<u>with naturalized qualities of talent and class</u>. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity ⑤<u>is like doing well</u> at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.explanation: ① 'potential'은 형용사로, 명사인 'an instrument'를 수식하거나 보어 역할을 해야 하는데, 여기서는 보어인 'an instrument'를 수식하는 부사 'potentially'가 와서 '잠재적으로 ~이다'라는 의미를 형성해야 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
options: ① Your recorded voice may sound higher than what you are used to hearing.
② When we speak, we hear our voice through two separate channels.
③ The first route for perceiving our own voice is how we typically hear external sounds, with waves moving through the air.
④ When speaking, the vibrations pass through our bones and directly affect out inner ears.
⑤ The second path for perceiving our own voice highlights lower frequencies, making our voice sound deeper to every listeners including ourselves.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 뼈를 통해 전달되는 내부 경로는 낮은 주파수를 강조하여 목소리가 '자기 자신에게(to yourself)' 더 낮고 풍부하게 들리게 만듭니다. 하지만 다른 사람들은 공기를 통한 경로로만 듣기 때문에, 모든 청취자에게 목소리가 더 깊게 들린다는 ⑤번의 내용은 틀린 설명입니다.
options_translation: ① 녹음된 목소리는 당신이 평소 듣던 것보다 더 높게 들릴 수 있다.
② 우리가 말할 때, 우리는 두 가지 별개의 통로를 통해 목소리를 듣는다.
③ 우리 목소리를 인지하는 첫 번째 경로는 우리가 보통 외부 소리를 듣는 방식과 같으며, 파동이 공기를 통해 이동한다.
④ 말할 때 진동은 뼈를 통해 전달되어 내이에 직접적인 영향을 준다.
⑤ 우리 목소리를 인지하는 두 번째 경로는 낮은 주파수를 강조하여, 우리 자신을 포함한 모든 청취자에게 우리 목소리가 더 낮게 들리게 만든다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are ─ writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
options: ① the risks of linking self-worth only to a specific capability
② the correlation between self-esteem and attitudes toward achievement
③ the ways varied standards and metrics affect perceptions of ability and self-esteem
④ the role of natural talent compared to acquired skills in comprehensive self-evaluation
⑤ the influence of intelligence and interpersonal skills on personal success and self-assessment
questions.explanation: 이 글은 능력이 어떻게 정의되든 간에, 그것이 자아 가치(self-worth)의 유일한 결정 요인이 될 때 발생하는 문제점과 위험성에 대해 경고하고 있습니다. 수행 능력이 곧 그 사람의 가치로 직결되는 상황의 위험을 다루고 있으므로 주제로 ①이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자아 가치를 오직 특정 능력에만 연결하는 것의 위험성
② 자존감과 성취에 대한 태도 사이의 상관관계
③ 다양한 기준과 척도가 능력과 자존감의 인식에 영향을 미치는 방식
④ 종합적인 자기 평가에서 습득된 기술과 대비되는 타고난 재능의 역할
⑤ 지능과 대인 관계 기술이 개인적 성공과 자기 평가에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
options: ① Rocks are made up of crystals, and atoms are the fundamental components that make up crystals.
② The shape of the crystals varies including triangles, squares, and hexagons.
③ The lower the temperature is, the more favorable the crystal is to form a regular shape.
④ If the temperature or material is not appropriate, the shape of the crystal is twisted.
⑤ Sufficient time to form crystals is a requirement for flawless crystal formation.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 결정은 액체가 식을 때 형성되지만, 조건이 '너무 춥거나(too cold)', '너무 덥거나(too hot)', 혹은 재료가 충분하지 않으면 완벽한 모양을 갖추지 못하고 뒤틀린 모양이 된다고 언급되어 있습니다. 따라서 단순히 온도가 낮을수록 규칙적인 모양 형성에 유리하다는 3번의 내용은 지문의 설명과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: 암석은 결정으로 구성되어 있으며, 원자는 결정을 구성하는 기본 성분이다.
결정의 모양은 삼각형, 사각형, 육각형을 포함하여 다양하다.
온도가 낮을수록 결정이 규칙적인 모양을 형성하는 데 더 유리하다.
온도나 재료가 적절하지 않으면 결정의 모양이 뒤틀린다.
결정을 형성하기 위한 충분한 시간은 결점 없는 결정 형성의 요건이다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries.
ordered_passages: (A) They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.(B) This leads some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD.(C) For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 고래의 뛰어난 탄소 저장 능력을 언급합니다. (C)는 나무와 비교하여 고래의 탄소 흡수량을 구체화하고, 배설물을 통한 식물성 플랑크톤 증가라는 추가적인 탄소 격리 방식을 설명합니다. (B)에서는 이러한 기능 때문에 고래를 '해양 생태계의 엔지니어'라 부르며 IMF 경제학자들이 추산한 고래의 경제적 가치를 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 가치를 바탕으로 기후 변화 대응을 위한 고래 복원 프로그램을 촉구하는 내용으로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 밑줄 친 Things are not so different가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 24번]
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us. One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Gobekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up radically remaking the society itself. <u>Things are not so different</u> in our own time.
options: ① Accepting diverse opinions helps society evolve constructively.
② Buildings and development have had a profound impact on our way of life.
③ People build and live in the buildings in the ways that best fit their lifestyle.
④ People prefer to live within a fixed framework rather than to change for the better.
⑤ The era of settling down in one place and farming began, moving away from a nomadic, hunter-gatherer lifestyle.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 건물을 짓지만, 그 건물이 다시 인간과 사회를 형성한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 터키의 괴베클리 테페 유적이 수렵 채집인들을 정착 농경 사회로 변화시킨 것처럼, 현대에도 우리가 만든 건축물과 개발이 우리의 생활 방식과 사회 구조에 큰 영향을 미치고 있다는 뜻입니다. 따라서 밑줄 친 부분의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은 ②번입니다.
options_translation: ① 다양한 의견을 수용하는 것은 사회가 건설적으로 발전하도록 돕는다.
② 건물과 개발은 우리의 생활 방식에 깊은 영향을 미쳐 왔다.
③ 사람들은 자신의 생활 방식에 가장 잘 맞는 방식으로 건물을 짓고 거주한다.
④ 사람들은 더 나은 쪽으로 변화하기보다 고정된 틀 안에서 사는 것을 선호한다.
⑤ 유목 생활과 수렵 채집 생활에서 벗어나 한곳에 정착하여 농사를 짓는 시대가 시작되었다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 29번]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
options: ① The structure of an organization can influence how conflicts are managed.
② Organizations should avoid having different cultures within their departments.
③ Organizations function best when all departments adopt the same structure.
④ All the departments must follow strict rules to avoid centralized decision making.
⑤ The main problem in organizations is the lack of communication between departments.
questions.explanation: 조직 내의 각 부서는 자신들만의 편향된 시각('터널 시야')을 갖게 되어 부서 간 갈등이 발생할 수 있는데, 이러한 갈등 관리는 조직의 구조(기계적 구조 vs 유기적 구조)에 따라 크게 영향을 받는다는 것이 이 글의 주된 요지입니다. 따라서 정답은 ①번입니다.
options_translation: ① 조직의 구조는 갈등이 관리되는 방식에 영향을 미칠 수 있다.
② 조직은 부서 내에 서로 다른 문화를 갖는 것을 피해야 한다.
③ 조직은 모든 부서가 동일한 구조를 채택할 때 가장 잘 작동한다.
④ 모든 부서는 중앙 집중식 의사 결정을 피하기 위해 엄격한 규칙을 따라야 한다.
⑤ 조직의 주요 문제는 부서 간의 의사소통 부족이다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 9월 38번]
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on ⓐ<u>different</u> branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are ⓑ<u>similar</u> in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways. However, they arose ⓒ<u>separately</u> in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share ⓓ<u>functional</u> traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most ⓔ<u>useless</u> properties.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 기능이 다르지만 공통 조상으로부터 물려받은 구조를 공유하는 '상동(homologous)' 형질을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 뼈의 숫자나 연결 방식과 같은 특징은 '기능적(functional)'인 특징이 아니라 '구조적(structural)'인 특징에 해당하므로 ⓓ의 functional은 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 9월 41-42번]
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. (A) The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. (B) Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialized workforce for the economy. (C) In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. (D) Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. (E) In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
questions.insertion_sentence: In reality, sociopolitical changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 이론적 기대와 달리 현실(In reality)에서 고등 교육의 확대가 평가에 있어 '모순의 장'을 만들었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C)까지는 고등 교육 확대에 따른 이론적인 긍정적 기대를 설명하고 있으며, (D) 이후부터는 현실적인 대량 교육 시스템이 효율성(객관식 시험 등)을 추구하면서 학생들이 피드백보다 성적에 집중하게 된다는 모순적 상황을 구체적으로 설명하므로 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. The way people handle their time between work and outside responsibilities differs from person to person. Some people prefer to separate or segment their roles to avoid frequent boundary ⓐ<u>overlaps</u>. These individuals, for example, might keep separate email addresses for work and personal matters and ⓑ<u>ensure</u> that family concerns are addressed only during non-work hours or breaks. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones ─ one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules are ideal for these people, as they ⓒ<u>prevent</u> a stronger distinction between work and non-work activities. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might ⓓ<u>involve</u> staying in touch with children via texts during work hours and keeping an eye on emails even at home or on vacation, rather than facing a full inbox later. ⓔ<u>Blending</u> personal and professional tasks can make both facets of life more manageable for these people, particularly with the aid of technology that supports remove work and digital communication.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 일과 삶을 분리하려는 '분할자(segmenters)'들은 유연한 근무 일정을 선호하는데, 그 이유는 이러한 일정이 일과 가정을 더 확실하게 구분할 수 있게 해주기 때문입니다. 따라서 문맥상 ⓒ의 prevent(방해하다, 막다)는 일과 삶의 구분을 가능하게 한다는 의미인 enable 혹은 facilitate와 같은 단어로 고쳐야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders ─ employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. ⓐ<u>They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"</u>. ⓑ<u>Likewise, they always end up overestimating the superiority of what humans do; interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity</u>. ⓒ<u>If an animal excels at a mental task ─ like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds ─ they attribute it to instinct, never to intelligence</u>. ⓓ<u>Animals' instincts are the capabilities to automatically know how to behave or respond in certain circumstances, which helps them to survival and thrive</u>. ⓔ<u>This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration" ─ our linguistic choices are designed to disempower animals and maintain our supremacy over them</u>.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심 주제는 인간이 언어적 속임수(linguistic castration)를 사용하여 동물과 인간의 유사성을 의도적으로 부정하고 인간의 우월성을 유지하려 한다는 것입니다. 하지만 ⓓ번 문장은 동물의 본능에 대한 일반적인 정의와 그것의 생존적 이점에 대해 설명하고 있으므로, 인간의 언어 선택과 관련된 전체 글의 논리적 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water ⓐ<u>does</u>. This is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively ⓑ<u>poorly</u> populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident ⓒ<u>that</u> the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data ⓓ<u>indicating</u> that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water ⓔ<u>has</u> the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: 주어 'Falling oxygen levels in water'에서 핵심 주어는 복수 명사인 'levels'입니다. 따라서 이에 대응하는 동사는 단수형인 'has'가 아니라 복수형인 'have'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 <보기>의 단어들을 모두 사용하여 밑줄 친 (A)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations ─ surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue ─ with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that he (A)___________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 16단어 이내로 작성할 것
so~that 구문을 사용할 것
<보기>의 단어를 모두 사용하여 글의 흐름과 어법에 맞게 작성할 것 (단어 추가 및 변형 가능)
questions.answer: is so powerful that he can risk the social costs of such behaviors
questions.explanation: 이 글은 규범에서 약간 벗어난 행동(예: 빨간 나비넥타이, 빨간 운동화)이 긍정적으로 평가받는 이유에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 그러한 행동은 그 사람이 사회적 비용(타인의 부정적 시선 등)을 감수할 수 있을 만큼 충분히 지위나 권력이 있음을 암시하기 때문입니다. 따라서 'so 형용사/부사 that' 구문을 활용하여 '그는 매우 강력해서 그러한 행동들의 사회적 비용을 감수할 수 있다'는 의미의 문장을 완성합니다. <보기>의 power를 powerful로 변형하고, suggest that 뒤의 절을 완성하는 것이 핵심입니다.

questions.question: 4. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for letting go of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle.
ordered_passages: (A) In some self-help groups, this is referred to as spending time with the winners. The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
(B) This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, whereas the positive thought forms are weak.
(C) People who operate at a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought patterns. Simply being in their presence can be beneficial.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 무력감을 극복하기 위해 문제를 해결한 사람들과 함께하라는 조언을 제시합니다. (B)에서 '이것(문제를 해결한 사람들과 함께하는 것)이 자조 집단(self-help groups)의 큰 힘 중 하나'라고 연결하며 우리가 부정적 상태일 때의 특징을 설명합니다. (C)에서는 (B)와 대조적으로 더 높은 진동(긍정적 상태)에서 활동하는 사람들에 대해 설명하며 그들의 존재만으로 유익할 수 있음을 언급합니다. (A)에서 이러한 과정을 자조 집단에서 '승자들과 시간 보내기'라고 부른다고 정리하며 긍정적 에너지의 전이 효과를 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: AI can improve inclusivity in the workplace by making the environment more ⓐ<u>approachable</u> for workers who often face challenges or disadvantages in the labor market. AI-powered devices to ⓑ<u>assist</u> workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can ⓒ<u>fascinate</u> communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can also ⓓ<u>reinforce</u> the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, Al's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. ⓔ<u>Furthermore</u>, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 장애가 있는 사람들의 의사소통이나 일자리 접근을 '매료시키다(fascinate)'가 아니라 '용이하게 하다/촉진하다(facilitate)'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most interesting examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will not inevitably view any given situation from their own ⓐ<u>subjective</u> perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which ⓑ<u>prevents</u> them from seeing things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can ⓒ<u>cause</u> conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure is more vertical with many rules, many procedures, and a ⓓ<u>hierarchical</u> management structure involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is ⓔ<u>decentralized</u> and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 조직 내의 각 부서가 '필연적으로(inevitably)' 자신들만의 주관적인 관점으로 상황을 바라본다는 내용이 되어야 하므로 'not inevitably'에서 not이 빠져야 문맥이 성립합니다. 따라서 ⓐ가 포함된 문장의 흐름상 부적절합니다. (원문은 'The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own specific perspective'임)

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They make us ⓐ<u>see</u> things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult ⓑ<u>to find</u> a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully summarizes the search for essences. Throughout history, many scientists have pursued them in vain because ⓒ<u>they</u> were guided by a flawed concept. According to Firestein, for example, luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance was believed to fill the universe ⓓ<u>that</u> light would move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been ⓔ<u>hypothesized</u> in a dark room, experimenting in it and searching for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 '물리학자들(physicists)'이며, 이들이 어두운 방 안에서 '가설을 세워오고 있었던 것'이므로 수동태(been hypothesized)가 아닌 능동 진행형인 'had been hypothesizing'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절한 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were not accepted in their lifetime. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. This initial (A)[acknowledgement / misunderstanding] is due to unfamiliarity - these composers were entirely introducing new musical forms, or ideas. However, this is exactly one of the things that makes them (B)[common / extraordinary]. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's illustrated as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely (C)[ahead / eclipsed] by him Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't novel. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 베토벤 등의 음악이 당대에 이해되지 못했다는 내용이 나오므로 생소함으로 인한 '오해(misunderstanding)'가 적절합니다. (B) 고유한 아이디어를 도입하여 훌륭해진 작곡가들을 설명하므로 '비범한(extraordinary)'이 적절합니다. (C) 살리에리는 모차르트와 동시대에 살며 그에 의해 완전히 '가려졌다(eclipsed)'는 문맥이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 인정 / 흔한 / 앞선
② 인정 / 비범한 / 가려진
③ 오해 / 흔한 / 앞선
④ 오해 / 비범한 / 앞선
⑤ 오해 / 비범한 / 가려진

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. (A) This is of course quite a common experience. (B) The explanation is actually fairly simple. We hear our own voice in two ways when we speak. (C) One is through the usual external sound route - sound waves travel through the air to our outer, middle, and inner ear. (D) Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. (E) That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
questions.insertion_sentence: The other way is internal, due to the vibrations of our vocal cords, which travel through our bones and directly stimulate our inner ear.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 목소리를 듣는 두 번째 방법(내부 경로)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. (C)에서 첫 번째 방법(외부 경로)을 설명한 후, (D) 위치에 주어진 문장이 들어가야 그 뒤의 (D)번 문장(this pathway=내부 경로)이 설명하는 낮은 주파수 강조 현상과 (E)의 결과(목소리가 더 깊고 풍부하게 들림)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Emotions are believed to exist due to their contribution to our survival as a species. Not only ⓐ<u>has</u> displaying anger allowed us to avoid potential threats, but also fear has enabled us to scare off danger. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when activated, directs many of our behaviors, ⓑ<u>including</u> our attention, perception, memory, movement, and expressions. For example, fear makes us very ⓒ<u>attentive</u>, sharpens our focus on perceived threats, and drives us to either confront (fight) or evade (flight) the danger. Additionally, it can enhance our memory of the experience, helping us avoid similar threats in the future. Irrespective of the specific ways ⓓ<u>which</u> they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they played an important role in helping our species overcome environmental challenges long ago. If they had not been beneficial for adaptation and survival, these emotions would not ⓔ<u>have persisted</u> through evolution.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 절 'they activate our systems'는 주어(they), 동사(activate), 목적어(our systems)를 갖춘 완전한 문장이므로 관계대명사 which가 올 수 없습니다. 앞의 선행사 ways를 수식하기 위해서는 관계부사 how를 대신하는 'in which'나 'that'으로 고치거나 생략해야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Mirror neurons are a type of brain cell that respond both when you perform an action and when you see someone else perform the same action. The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental aspect of human capacity. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, where we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error.
options: ① Limitations of Mirror Neurons in Learning Processes
② Mirror Neurons: The Key to Building Social Relationship
③ Solutions for Challenges in Learning Through Mirror Neurons
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런이 타인의 행동을 관찰하고 모방함으로써 인간의 능력을 형성하고 문화를 발전시키는 데 핵심적인 역할을 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 제공된 선택지 중 사회적 관계나 학습의 핵심 요소로서의 거울 뉴런을 다룬 ②번이 가장 적절합니다. (참고: 지문의 마지막 부분은 모방을 통한 학습이 문화 형성의 기반임을 강조함)
options_translation: ① 학습 과정에서 거울 뉴런의 한계
② 거울 뉴런: 사회적 관계 구축의 열쇠
③ 거울 뉴런을 통한 학습의 어려움에 대한 해결책

questions.question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: When it comes to saving the earth, whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. Whales accumulate carbon in their bodies during their long lives. When they die, they sink to the bottom of the ocean; each great whale sequesters 30 tons of carbon dioxide on average, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. ⓐIn comparison with a tree, which absorbs only up to 48 pounds of CO₂ annually, each whale is considered equivalent to thousands of trees in terms of its climate impact. ⓑWhales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient rich waste, resulting in substantial Phytoplankton growth, which also sequester carbon. ⓒThe gradual increase in waste from whales has impacted the habitat and populations of other marine species. ⓓAccording to the IMF(the International Monetary Fund) economists, each whale's ecological services, particularly in terms of carbon sequestration, are highly valued, contributing significantly to the health of marine ecosystems. ⓔAs a climate solution, they requested a global program to return whale populations to preindustrial levels, and similar calls are being made to slow climate change through whale restoration.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 고래가 탄소를 저장하고 격리함으로써 지구를 구하는 데 기여하는 긍정적인 역할에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 그러나 ③번 문장은 고래의 배설물이 다른 해양 종의 서식지와 개체수에 끼친 영향에 대한 내용으로, 탄소 격리라는 주제의 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: A highly effective way to ease traffic congestion is to reduce it altogether. In some cities, extensive networks of lanes and streets are set aside for bicycles, pedestrians, and occasional service vehicles. (A) This encourages people to choose biking over driving, making the streets safer for everyone. (B) As the popularity of bicycles in a city grow, urban planners will increasingly convert more car lanes and even entire streets to support this mode of transport. (C) Even the most bike-friendly cities, however, still need lanes for motor vehicles like taxis, emergency services, and delivery trucks. (D) Moreover, a single, well-packed delivery truck is far more efficient transporter of goods than multiple hybrid cars carrying a few shopping bags each. (E) Delivering food and other products to local vendors lets them maintain smaller stores close to neighborhoods, so residents can walk to get their groceries instead of driving.
questions.insertion_sentence: In the case of delivery trucks, while they are often a target of animus, they are actually important for improving the environmental sustainability of cities.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 배달 트럭이 종종 증오의 대상이 되기도 하지만, 도시의 환경적 지속 가능성을 향상시키는 데 중요하다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (D) 앞 문장에서 배달 트럭을 포함한 자동차용 차선이 여전히 필요하다고 언급하였고, (D) 뒤 문장에서는 배달 트럭이 개별 하이브리드 차량보다 효율적인 운송 수단이며, (E) 부분에서 지역 상점에 물건을 공급함으로써 주민들이 걷게 해준다는 장점을 부연 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 배달 트럭의 긍정적 측면을 처음 제시하는 주어진 문장은 (D)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글을 읽고 추론한 내용으로 알 수 없는 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists identify two types of similarities in living organisms. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and bees are both designed for flight and share certain similarities because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways. However, these wings arose independently in evolution and have no shared origin beyond their function in flying. On the other hand, "Homologous" traits might have different functions, but they originate from a common ancestor and thus have some common structure that shows they are fundamentally the same organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all adaptations of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To tell the difference between analogy and homology, biologists usually examine the overall architecture of the organs and pay attention to their most useless features.
options: ① Analogous traits arose from distinct evolutionary origins but may serve similar functions.
② Homologous traits have a common ancestor and share structural similarities.
③ The wings of birds and bees developed separately but have similar functions related to flight.
④ Nonfunctional traits are used in distinguishing between analogous and homologous structures.
⑤ The modifications of forelimbs of all mammals are functionally identical due to their shared ancestry.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 상동 형질(homologous traits)은 공통 조상에서 기원하여 구조적 유사성을 공유하지만, 기능은 다를 수 있다고 설명하고 있습니다(예: 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리). 따라서 포유류의 앞다리 변형이 기능적으로 동일하다는 ⑤번 선지는 본문의 내용과 상충합니다.
options_translation: ① 유사 형질은 서로 다른 진화적 기원에서 발생했지만 유사한 기능을 수행할 수 있다.
② 상동 형질은 공통 조상을 가지며 구조적 유사성을 공유한다.
③ 새와 벌의 날개는 따로 발달했지만 비행과 관련된 유사한 기능을 가지고 있다.
④ 비기능적 특징은 유사 구조와 상동 구조를 구별하는 데 사용된다.
⑤ 모든 포유류의 앞다리 변형은 공유된 조상으로 인해 기능적으로 동일하다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention can be used as a means to reach elite celebrity status, some content creators pursue ordinary fame simply as a social goal in itself.
ordered_passages: (A) However, the criticism overlooks an important aspect: the emergence of ordinary celebrity itself is transforming the concept of fame. In the traditional sense, the elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class.

(B) Social media celebrities, like reality television stars, are frequently criticized for lacking the traditional skills associated with elite fame, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism emphasizes that digital content creators face real obstacles to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity.

(C) Ordinary celebrities, in contrast, are changing the way we understand fame by making it more accessible and less tied to elite status. They attract attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. In this point of view, achieving ordinary fame on social media is comparable to performing well in a game, because in this sphere, fame is merely about attaining relatively high scores on various attention metrics.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 소셜 미디어를 통해 평범한 명성을 추구하는 콘텐츠 제작자들에 대해 언급합니다. (B)에서는 이러한 소셜 미디어 유명인들이 엘리트 유명인들과 달리 전통적인 기술(연기, 노래 등)이 부족하다는 비판을 받는다는 내용을 제시합니다. (A)에서는 'However'를 통해 이러한 비판이 평범한 유명인의 등장이 명성의 개념 자체를 바꾸고 있다는 점을 간과하고 있음을 지적하며, 전통적인 엘리트 유명인의 특징을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서는 이와 대조적으로(In contrast) 평범한 유명인들이 명성을 더 접근 가능하게 만들고, 관심 지표에 따른 게임과 같은 성격으로 명성의 의미를 변화시키고 있음을 설명하며 글을 맺는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 알맞은 단어를 조건을 참고하여 각각 하나씩 순서대로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to (A)d__________ (to recognize or express the difference between things) between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has (B)n__________ (not anything) to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to (C)r__________ (to remember things from the past) the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory (D)v__________. (to disappear suddenly) To transfer information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
subjective_conditions: 괄호 안의 사전적 의미에 해당하는 단어를 쓸 것
주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어를 쓸 것
필요한 경우 어형을 변화할 것
questions.explanation: (A) 차이를 인식하거나 표현한다는 의미인 'differentiate'가 적절합니다. (B) 'nothing to do with'(~와 관련이 없다) 숙어 구조이며 'not anything'의 의미에 부합합니다. (C) 과거의 것을 기억해낸다는 의미인 'recall'이 적절합니다. (D) 갑자기 사라진다는 의미인 'vanish'가 적절하며, 주어 memory가 3인칭 단수이므로 'vanishes'로 어형 변화가 필요합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글을 읽고, <보기>에 제시된 필자의 주장을 한 문장으로 완성하고자 한다. 글의 흐름과 어법을 고려하여 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 그대로 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to continuously tell others about your little genius and his or her remarkable accomplishments, this can be stressful on your child. It is very important to restrict your boasting to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show off their talents too much. This also leads to an inaccurately formed sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they truly are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible accomplishments. Otherwise, you could disrupt the balance in their development, potentially resulting in a perfectionist or even a drop-out.
questions.summary_sentence: Parents need to maintain a(n) (A)__________ between pride and pressure for their gifted children's healthy growth, avoiding excessive (B)__________ about their achievements to others.
questions.explanation: 본문은 영재 부모가 자녀의 성취를 과하게 자랑함으로써 아이에게 스트레스를 주고 발달의 균형을 깨뜨리는 것을 경고하고 있습니다. 따라서 부모는 자긍심과 압박감 사이의 (A) balance(균형)를 유지해야 하며, 타인에게 성취에 대해 과도하게 (B) boasting(자랑)하는 것을 피해야 한다는 요약이 완성됩니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름과 어법을 고려하여 밑줄 친 부분을 <보기>의 단어(구)를 사용하여 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show - whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message. So, each new medium, like TV or social media, <u>우리의 인식들을 형성함으로써 우리가 세상을 보는 방식에 영향을 미친다</u>. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어(구)만을 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것
필요한 경우 동사의 형태를 변형할 것
vocabulary_box: our / perceptions / by / how / influence / we / see / the world / shape
questions.answer: influences how we see the world by shaping our perceptions
questions.explanation: 주어인 'each new medium'이 단수이므로 동사 influence를 influences로 변형합니다. '영향을 미친다(influences)'의 목적어로 간접의문문 '우리가 세상을 보는 방식(how we see the world)'을 배열하고, 수단이나 방법을 나타내는 'by + ~ing' 구문을 사용하여 '우리의 인식들을 형성함으로써(by shaping our perceptions)'를 완성합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(C)에 알맞은 말을 주어진 단어들을 모두 배열하여 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water (A)<u>than / more / warm water / does / dissolved / oxygen / holds</u> - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, (B)<u>that / will / it is / off / the amount / dissolved oxygen / decrease / self-evident</u>. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water (C)<u>have / to / the habitat / of / the potential / marine organisms / impact</u> worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.answer: (A) holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does(B) it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease(C) have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms
questions.explanation: (A) 비교급 구문 'more + 명사 + than'을 사용하여 '찬물이 따뜻한 물보다 더 많은 용존 산소를 보유한다'는 의미가 되도록 배열합니다. 이때 does는 앞의 holds를 대신하는 대동사입니다.(B) 'it(가주어) is self-evident that(진주어)' 구문을 사용하여 '용존 산소의 양이 감소할 것이라는 점은 자명하다'는 문장을 구성합니다.(C) 'have the potential to + 동사원형' (~할 잠재력을 가지다) 구문을 사용하여 '해양 생물의 서식지에 영향을 미칠 잠재력을 가진다'는 의미가 되도록 배열합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 (나)는 (가)의 내용을 바탕으로 질의 응답한 내용이다. 밑줄 친 (A)~(D)에 알맞은 말을 주어진 단어들을 모두 배열하여 쓰시오.
questions.passage: (가) Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.(나)Q: what does a 'field of contradiction' mean?A: It refers to a situation where different aspects or goals (A)<u>each other / with / are / in conflict</u>. In the context of higher education, it suggests that while (B)<u>aims / promote / to / lifelong learning / the expansion</u> and reduce the focus on exams, the need for efficient assessment in a mass system (C)<u>contradictions / leads / to</u>, such as students (D)<u>on / grades / than / feedback / focusing more</u>.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어들을 모두 배열하여 쓸 것
questions.answer: (A) are in conflict with each other(B) the expansion aims to promote lifelong learning(C) leads to contradictions(D) focusing more on grades than feedback
questions.explanation: (A) 서로 충돌한다는 의미로 'be in conflict with each other'를 사용합니다.(B) 대학 교육의 확대가 평생 학습을 증진하는 것을 목표로 한다는 의미로 'aim to' 구문을 사용합니다.(C) 대중화된 시스템에서의 효율적인 평가 필요성이 모순으로 이어진다는 의미로 'lead to'를 사용합니다.(D) 학생들이 피드백보다 성적에 더 집중하게 만든다는 구체적 예시로 'focus more on A than B' 구문의 분사 형태를 사용합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us ⓐ<u>scare off</u> threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond, with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, ⓑ<u>guides</u> many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may prevent us from ⓒ<u>remembering</u> an experience, making it more vivid in our memory. (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) ⓓ<u>survive</u> challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not ⓔ<u>helped</u> us adapt and survive, they would have been left behind in evolution.
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 감정이 진화적 관점에서 인류의 생존에 기여하기 위해 존재한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ③번 ⓒ의 'remembering(기억하는 것을 막다)'은 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다. 이어지는 문구에서 'making it more vivid in our memory(우리의 기억 속에 그것을 더 생생하게 만들면서)'라고 설명하고 있으므로, 공포가 경험을 잊게 만드는 것이 아니라 오히려 '강화하거나 돕는(strengthening or helping)' 역할을 한다는 맥락이 되어야 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. (A) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. (B) As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. (C) Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. (D) Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. (E) Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.insertion_sentence: A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 배달 트럭이 여러 대의 하이브리드 승용차보다 효율적인 운송 수단이라는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. (D)번 문장에서 배달 차량이 도시를 더 친환경적으로 만드는 필수 요소라는 주장이 나오고, (E)번 뒷부분에서는 그 구체적인 방식(동네 상점 물품 공급을 통한 주민 도보 이동 유도)이 설명됩니다. 주어진 문장은 배달 트럭의 효율성을 강조하며 (D)에서 제기된 '배달 트럭이 친환경에 기여한다'는 논지를 뒷받침하는 근거로 (E) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. ⓐIn theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which accelerates lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. ⓑIn reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. ⓒWhile many teachers believe that good assessments should help students learn, standardized tests often focus more on scores than on helpful feedback. ⓓMass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. ⓔIn contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
