questions.explanation: 이 글의 전체적인 흐름은 '고등 교육의 대중화'로 인해 평가 시스템이 이론적 기대(피드백 중심)와 달리 현실적 한계(효율성 중심의 시험과 등급화)에 부딪히며 나타나는 모순에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ①, ②, ④, ⑤는 모두 교육 시스템의 규모 변화(엘리트 vs 대중)에 따른 평가 방식의 변화와 그 모순을 다루고 있는 반면, ③번 문장은 일반적인 교사들의 신념과 표준화된 시험의 점수 위주 경향이라는 보편적인 교육 문제를 언급하고 있어, 고등 교육 체제 변화(Mass system)라는 지문의 구체적인 핵심 맥락에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. ⓐ<u>While</u> it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents ⓑ<u>show off</u> gifted children too much. This behavior creates expectations ⓒ<u>that</u> they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as ⓓ<u>define</u> by their incredible achievements. ⓔ<u>Otherwise</u>, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop-out, or worse.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 구문은 'as (they are) defined by ~'의 의미로, '정의되는'이라는 수동의 의미를 나타내야 하므로 과거분사인 'defined'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 적절한 곳은? [24년 9월 24번]
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. (A) For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. (B) Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call <u>them</u> the "engineers of marine ecosystems." (C) In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. (D) They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. (E) Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.insertion_sentence: From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 고래 한 마리가 수천 그루의 나무에 해당한다는 내용입니다. (A)의 앞 문장에서 고래가 30톤의 이산화탄소를 격리한다고 했고, (A)에서 비교 대상으로 나무 한 그루가 48파운드를 흡수한다고 했으므로, 이 수치 비교를 종합하여 결론짓는 주어진 문장은 (B) 위치가 가장 적절합니다. 그 이후에는 고래가 탄소를 격리하는 또 다른 방법(배설물을 통한 플랑크톤 증식)이 이어집니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 밑줄 친 them이 지칭하는 것이 무엇인지 한 단어로 쓰시오. [24년 9월 24번]
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. (A) For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. (B) Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call <u>them</u> the "engineers of marine ecosystems." (C) In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. (D) They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. (E) Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 '해양 생태계의 엔지니어'라고 불리는 대상은 탄소 격리에 큰 역할을 하는 고래(whales)입니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.summary_sentence: AI can improve (A)___________ of workers with (B)___________ and low skilled individuals. This will have positive effects on their (C)___________.
questions.explanation: AI는 신체적 장애나 언어적 장벽 등으로 인해 노동 시장에서 불리한 위치에 있는 노동자들의 직장 접근성(accessibility)을 높여주며, 시각·청각 등의 어려움(difficulties)을 겪는 사람들과 저숙련 노동자들의 업무 능력을 보강해 줍니다. 이러한 변화는 결과적으로 그들의 경력(career) 전망에 긍정적인 영향을 미친다는 지문의 내용을 바탕으로 (A) accessibility, (B) difficulties, (C) career가 포함된 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 접근성 - (B) 어려움 - (C) 경력
② (A) 접근성 - (B) 능숙함 - (C) 경력
③ (A) 포용성 - (B) 능숙함 - (C) 경험
④ (A) 포용성 - (B) 장애 - (C) 경험
⑤ (A) 포용성 - (B) 능숙도 - (C) 임금

questions.question: 23. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to ________________________________, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.explanation: 지문에서는 벼락치기 공부가 단기 기억(working memory)에만 머무를 뿐이며, 정보를 장기 기억(long-term memory)으로 전이시키기 위해서는 '자신의 지식을 다시 테스트(retest your knowledge)'하는 과정이 필수적이라고 강조하고 있습니다. 지문 내의 'unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes(지식을 다시 테스트하지 않으면 기억은 사라진다)'라는 표현이 결정적인 단서가 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 새로운 주제를 지속적으로 공부하는 것
② 내용을 복습하는 것
③ 다양한 정보를 탐색하는 것
④ 지식을 다시 테스트하는 것
⑤ 세부 사항에 집중하는 것

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 단어로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer ⓐ<u>them</u> both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, (A)__________, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw ⓑ<u>them</u> back at the experimenter. (B)___________ she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing, rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. (C)___________, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.explanation: (A) 두 원숝이 모두 오이를 받을 때와 달리 한 쪽만 포도를 받는 상황으로 내용이 전환되므로 역접의 however가 적절합니다. (B) 노력에 대한 배가(보상)가 동일함에도 불구하고 불곭평함을 눐긴다는 양밴의 내용이므로 Even though가 적절합니다. (C) 불곭평함을 눐긴 것에 더해 불만을 표현하기 위해 보상을 포기하는 추가적인 행동을 설명하므로 Furthermore가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 또한 - ~임에도 불구하고 - 괸러므로
② 또한 - 마찬가지로 - 괸러므로
③ 하지만 - ~임에도 불구하고 - 게다가
④ 하지만 - 마찬가지로 - 게다가
⑤ 하지만 - ~임에도 불구하고 - 반면에

questions.question: 25. 윗글에서 묱줄 친 ⓐthem과 ⓑthem이 지칭하는 것이 무엇인지 각각 한 ⊱어로 시오.
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer ⓐ<u>them</u> both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, (A)__________, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw ⓑ<u>them</u> back at the experimenter. (B)___________ she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing, rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. (C)___________, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 문장에서 'offer them both slices of cucumber'는 두 마리의 원숝이들에갌 오이 조각을 제공한다는 뜻이므로 monkeys를 가리킵니다.ⓑ 한 원숝이가 포도를 받는 것을 보고, 여전히 오이를 받고 있는 원숝이가 받은 것(오이)을 실험자에갌 다시 던지는 것이므로 cucumbers를 가리킵니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 해석에 맞는 문장을 <보기>의 단어들을 배열하여 완성하시오.
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. <u>그가 쓴 곡은 마치 그 당시 모든 다른 사람들이 작곡했던 것처럼 들렸다</u>. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
subjective_conditions: 한 단어가 여러 번 사용될 수 있음
시제와 어법에 맞게 변형 가능
제시된 단어만 활용하고, 그 이외 단어는 사용하지 말 것.
vocabulary_box: he / like / what / everyone / is / the / at / time / write / sound / just / else / compose
questions.answer: What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 주어 부분인 '그가 쓴 것(곡)'은 'What he wrote'로, 동사인 '~처럼 들렸다'는 'sounded just like'로, 목적어 부분인 '그 당시 다른 모든 사람들이 작곡하고 있었던 것'은 'what everyone else was composing at the time'으로 배열합니다. 과거 시제와 진행형을 적절히 활용해야 합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 담화의 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, which decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.subjective_answer_format: "Our company has a(n) ____________ structure. For example, if there's a disagreement between the product development team and customer support, the teams can solve the problem quickly by talking openly and making decisions together, without having to wait for permission from the bosses."→ ______________________________________________________
questions.explanation: 담화문에서 상사의 허락을 기다리지 않고 팀원들이 함께 결정하며 수평적으로 소통하는 구조는 본문에서 설명한 'horizontal'하고 'decision making is spread'된 특징을 가진 'organic' 구조에 해당합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 알맞은 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. [24년 9월 34번]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ___________ fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ___________ people. Achieving the fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.explanation: "- some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself."와 "The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people."에서 솈셜 미디어 명성은 엔리트 명성과 대조되는 '평범한(일반적인) 명성'이며, 다른 '평범한' 사람들과의 소통을 통해 이루어지므로 공통으로 들어갈 단어는 'ordinary'이다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 대화문을 조건에 맞게 완성하시오. [24년 9월 39번]
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
subjective_conditions: Global warming으로 문장을 시작할 갳
다음 주어진 단어만을 사용할 갳
questions.subjective_answer_format: Students: __________________________________________. This can cause more anoxic events, harming or moving marine species and putting the ecosystem at risk.
questions.answer: Global warming causes the temperature of ocean water to rise, which reduces the amount of dissolved oxygen.
questions.explanation: 지구 온넜화가 해수의 온도를 높이고, 이것이 용진 산소띉을 줄인다는 내용을 조건에 맞게 영작한다. "Global warming causes the temperature of ocean water to rise"(지구 온넜화는 해수의 온도를 상승시킨다) 뒤에 계속 용법의 관계대명사 which를 사용하여 "which reduces the amount of dissolved oxygen"(그리고 그것은 용진 산소띉을 감소시킨다)를 연결한다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.*latent: 잠재적인
options: ① 긍정적 기운을 주는 사람들은 부정적인 사고에서 나오는 에너지가 없다.
② 부정적인 상태란 우라카 부정적인 사고에 더 많은 에너지를 투입할 때이다.
③ 자조 집단의 이점은 모두가 부정적인 사고를 극복해 본 경험이 있다는 것이다.
④ 부정적 감정을 해소하기 위한 유용한 방법은 해결해 본 사람과 함께 있는 것이다.
⑤ 우리는 보통 우울감을 해소하기 위해서 긍정적인 사고에 많은 에너지를 투입한다.
questions.explanation: 무력감이나 우울함 같은 부정적인 상태에서 벗어나기 위해 이미 해당 문제를 해결한 사람들과 함께 있는 것이 도움이 된다는 내용입니다. 그들의 긍정적인 에너지가 전달되어 자신의 잠재된 긍정적 사고를 다시 깨울 수 있기 때문입니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
options: ① The Power of Positive Emotions
② The Social Functions of Emotions
③ The Role of Positive Emotions in Positive Psychology
④ Survival and Emotions: How Our Feelings Keep Us Alive
⑤ Human Emotional Evaluation of Ancestral and Modern Threats: Fear, Dislike, and Anger
questions.explanation: 가ᄆ쟁으는 진하론재ᄀ 관자메사로 인류으의 새존을 도ᄑ기 위해 교재하는 프로그래ᄆ가 가튼 너피가 이기 때무네 존재하는 거시라는 내용을 다루고 이뜨므로, 새존가 가ᄆ쟁으의 관걔를 서개하는 ④가 자해다.
options_translation: ① 경자재ᄀ 가ᄆ쟁으의 히ᄆ
② 가ᄆ쟁으의 사회재ᄀ 기느ᄂ
③ 경자재ᄀ 싀리하가나사로 경자재ᄀ 가ᄆ쟁으의 여하ᄅ
④ 새존가 가ᄆ쟁: 가ᄆ쟁이 에게 우리를 살아나게 하는 바바ᄑ
⑤ 조상가 혀ᄂ대으의 위혀ᄇ에 대하하는 인간으의 가ᄆ쟁재ᄀ 파ᄀ가: 고포, 혀ᄀ오, 그리고 바노

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ⓐ<u>ordinary</u> fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism ⓑ<u>highlights</u> the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity ⓒ<u>reconstructs</u> the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and ⓓ<u>hierarchical</u> distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and ⓔ<u>occasional</u> interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.explanation: 글의 문맥상 평범한 유명인(ordinary celebrity)은 다른 평범한 사람들과 '규칙적이고 빈번한(frequent/constant)' 상호작용을 통해 관심을 끌어야 합니다. '가끔의/때때로의'를 의미하는 'occasional'은 매일 소통하며 구독자나 좋아요 수치를 관리해야 하는 소셜 미디어 유명인의 속성과 어울리지 않습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are extremely ___________ at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.explanation: 지문은 고래 한 마리가 평균 30톤의 이산화탄소를 격리하며, 이는 나무 수천 그루와 맞먹는 효과라는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 또한 영양분이 풍부한 배설물로 식물성 플랑크톤의 증식을 도와 탄소 격리 능력을 높인다는 내용이 이어지므로, 고래가 탄소 저장에 매우 '효율적(efficient)'이라는 표현이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 무작위의
② 효율적인
③ 윤리적인
④ 값비싼
⑤ 위험한

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another ___________________________. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.explanation: 카푸친 원숭이는 자신이 받는 보상(오이)이 이전과 같더라도, 옆에 있는 다른 원숭이가 더 좋은 보상(포도)을 받는 것을 보게 되면 불공평함을 느끼고 반응합니다. 자신의 상황은 변하지 않았지만 타인과의 비교가 '불공평한 상황을 만든다(creates the unfair situation)'는 맥락이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 더 많은 혜택을 제공한다
더 나은 만족감을 전달한다
불공평한 상황을 만든다
심각한 경쟁을 유발한다
개방적인 의사소통을 촉진한다

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses.
ordered_passages: (A) The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.

(B) Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show - whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself.

(C) That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message. Also, it is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 새로운 매체를 사용하는 것을 '새로운 고글을 쓰는 것'에 비유했습니다. (B)는 이 비유를 이어받아 고글이 세상을 다르게 보게 만든다는 점을 설명하며 TV의 예시를 도입합니다. (C)는 이러한 현상 때문에 마샬 맥루한이 '매체는 메시지다'라고 말했음을 언급하며 매체가 우리를 새로운 코드에 따라 세상을 보도록 유도한다고 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 맥루한의 주장을 구체화하여 정보 자체보다 정보가 전달되는 방식이 중요하며, TV가 세상을 빠르고 표면적인 것으로 가르친다는 결론으로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
questions.summary_sentence: Concepts are vital but can lead to essentialism and (A)__________ searches, as shown by a metaphor of "a black cat in a dark room", showing how scientists may (B)__________ nonexistent ideas like luminiferous ether.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 개념이 중요하지만 본질주의에 빠지게 하여 존재하지 않는 것을 찾게 만드는 위험이 있음을 설명합니다. 본문에서 과학자들이 잘못된 개념을 사용하여 '결실 없이(fruitlessly)' 본질을 찾았다고 언급하므로 (A)에는 '잘못된(misguided)'이 적절합니다. 또한, 존재하지 않는 고양이를 찾는 것처럼 과학자들이 빛의 매질인 에테르와 같은 '존재하지 않는 아이디어를 추구(pursue)'할 수 있음을 보여주므로 (B)에는 '추구하다(pursue)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 잘못된 ... 추구하다
② 정확한 ... 추구하다
③ 잘못된 ... 요약하다
④ 정확한 ... 구별하다
⑤ 대략적인 ... 구별하다

questions.question: 13. 다음 글 (A)~(F)를 읽고, 글의 순서를 차례대로 바르게 쓰시오. [3.2점]
ordered_passages: (A) Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room.
(B) Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are.
(C) It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place.
(D) Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?"
(E) This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.

(F) While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away.
questions.explanation: 이사는 모두에게 힘들지만 아이들에게 특히 스트레스라는 일반적인 진술(F)로 시작합니다. 그중 3-6세 아이들이 특히 영향을 받는다는 구체적 예시(A)가 나오고, 그들이 가질 수 있는 구체적인 걱정들(D)이 이어집니다. 이후 아이들의 과거 경험 인정과 새 장소 적응 사이의 균형이 중요하다는 해결책(C)이 제시되고, 자신의 과거를 존중하며 배경을 공유할 기회가 필요하다는 내용(B)이 이어지며, 이것이 공동체 의식을 형성하는 데 기여한다는 마무리(E)가 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 We에게 적용될 속담으로 가장 잘 어울리는 것은?
questions.passage: <u>We</u> are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore show your child good examples of life by your action. In our daily lives, we can show our children that, we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
options: ① The pen is mightier than the sword.
② A stitch in time saves nine.
③ Actions speak louder than words.
④ Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
⑤ You can lead a horse to water, but you can't make it drink.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 부모가 말뿐만 아니라 행동을 통해 아이들에게 가치관을 가르쳐야 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '말보다 행동이 중요하다(행동이 말보다 더 크게 말한다)'는 의미의 속담이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 펜은 칼보다 강하다.
② 제때의 바느질 한 번이 아홉 번의 수고를 던다.
③ 행동이 말보다 더 중요하다.
④ 김칫국부터 마시지 마라.
⑤ 말은 물가로 끌고 갈 수 있어도 물을 마시게 할 수는 없다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Gregg and I had been rock climbing since sunrise and had had no ⓐ<u>hurdles</u>. So we took a risk. "Look, the first bolt is right there. I can ⓑ<u>undoubtedly</u> climb out to it. Piece of cake," I persuaded Gregg, minutes before I found myself ⓒ<u>stuck</u>. It wasn't a piece of cake. The rock was deceptively ⓓ<u>sufficient</u> of handholds. I clumsily moved back and forth across the cliff face and ended up with nowhere to go... but down. The bolt that would save my life, if I could get to it, was about two feet above my reach. My arms trembled from ⓔ<u>fatigue</u>. I looked at Gregg. My body froze with fright from my neck down to my toes. Our rope was tied between us. If I fell, he would fall with me.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 암벽 등반 중에 붙잡을 곳이 없어 곤란을 겪고 있는 상황이므로, 암벽에 손잡이(handholds)가 '충분했다(sufficient)'는 것은 적절하지 않습니다. 손잡이가 없거나 부족했다는 의미의 'barren'이나 'devoid' 같은 단어가 와야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 Monday Morning Quarterback과 가장 가까운 집단은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "<u>Monday Morning Quarterback</u>" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe ⓐ<u>they</u> could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than ⓑ<u>those</u> on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find ⓒ<u>themselves</u> being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of ⓓ<u>them</u> face criticism from fans and community members telling ⓔ<u>them</u> how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.explanation: 'Monday Morning Quarterback'은 경기가 끝난 월요일 아침에 경기에 대해 왈가왈부하는 사람들을 의미하며, 전문 지식 없이 비판하거나 조언하는 사람들을 뜻합니다. 지문에서 ⓐ 'they'는 자신들이 현장의 전문가들보다 더 잘할 수 있다고 믿는 팬들을 지칭하므로 정답은 ①입니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 our building and development are also shaping us가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, <u>our buildings and development are also shaping us</u>. One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Göbekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up radically remaking the society itself. Things are not so different in our own time.
options: ① Development seldom depends on constructions.
② Buildings influence our culture and collective identity.
③ The shape of buildings is relevant to our tradition.
④ Göbekli Tepe gathered people as a religious place.
⑤ The first farming society is not so different from us.
questions.explanation: 인간이 건물을 짓지만, 그 과정(정착 생활 등)이 오히려 인간 사회의 구조와 문화를 바꾼다는 내용입니다. 따라서 건물이 우리의 문화와 집단적 정체성에 영향을 준다는 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 개발은 건설에 거의 의존하지 않는다.
② 건물은 우리의 문화와 집단적 정체성에 영향을 미친다.
③ 건물의 모양은 우리의 전통과 관련이 있다.
④ 괴베클리 테페는 종교적인 장소로서 사람들을 모았다.
⑤ 최초의 농경 사회는 우리와 크게 다르지 않다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it ─ you just see the blurred outline of the moving string. Strings vibrating in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. ⓐBut if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note is heard loud and clear. ⓑA well-crafted guitar body can significantly improve the: vibration quality and overall sound. ⓒThe vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. ⓓThe vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. ⓔWhen the waves reach your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기타 줄의 진동이 어떻게 기타 몸통을 통해 증폭되어 소리로 전달되는지 그 '물리적 과정'을 설명하는 글입니다. ⓑ는 '잘 만들어진 기타 몸통의 품질'에 대해 언급하고 있어, 소리 증폭의 원리를 설명하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① The Unpublished Study: The Result of a Tree's Silent Fall
② The Tree That Spoke Nothing: A scientific Paradox
③ The Forest of Knowledge: Trees and the Hidden Sounds
④ Falling Trees and Scientific Success: A Soundless Journey
⑤ From Publication to Perception: Avoiding Silent Falls in Scientific Papers
questions.explanation: 이 글은 소리가 청자가 있어야 완성되듯이, 과학 논문도 출판만 한다고 끝나는 것이 아니라 독자에게 읽히고 '이해'되어야 비로소 그 가치가 완성된다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 출판에서 지각(이해)으로 이어지는 과정의 중요성을 강조한 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 출판되지 않은 연구: 나무의 조용한 낙하의 결과
② 아무 말도 하지 않은 나무: 과학적 역설
③ 지식의 숲: 나무와 숨겨진 소리들
④ 쓰러지는 나무와 과학적 성공: 소리 없는 여정
⑤ 출판에서 지각까지: 과학 논문에서 소리 없는 낙하 방지하기

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation. (A) While the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a protective mechanism for the foot. (B) Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. (C) They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now contract quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object. (D) Sensory and motor nerves control almost all functions in the body ─ from the beating of the heart to the movement of the gut, sweating and just about everything else. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 핀을 밟았을 때 통증 감각이 뇌로 전달되는 구체적인 '예시'를 제시하고 있습니다. (A) 뒤의 문장에서 'the pain(그 통증)'이라는 정관사가 사용되었는데, 이는 앞에서 통증에 대한 언급이 있어야 가능합니다. 따라서 통증 전달 과정을 처음 언급한 제시문은 (A) 자리에 들어가는 것이 흐름상 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 흐름상 밑줄 친 (A)에 들어갈 알맞은 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that (A)_____________________________. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
options: ① will cause them the least amount of anxiety
② will make the best amount of logic
③ just follows what others do
④ keep their emotions as controlled as possible
⑤ is considered to be a cutting edge technology
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 사람들은 통계적인 논리(비행기가 자동차보다 훨씬 안전함)보다 자신의 감정(비행에 대한 공포와 통제력 부족)에 기반하여 결정을 내립니다. 사람들은 실제 위험도가 더 높더라도 자신이 직접 운전하여 통제감을 느낌으로써 불안감을 덜 느끼는 자동차 운전을 선택합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '그들에게 불안감을 가장 적게 유발할' 옵션을 선택한다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그들에게 최소한의 불안감을 유발할
② 최선의 논리를 만들어낼
③ 단지 타인이 하는 것을 따르는
④ 그들의 감정을 가능한 한 통제된 상태로 유지하는
⑤ 최첨단 기술로 간주되는

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⑂~⑆ 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the ⑂<u>illusion</u> that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is ⑃<u>fully</u> present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to ⑄<u>recall</u> the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes ⑅<u>minor</u>: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then ⑆<u>test</u> yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 벼락치기를 하면 정보가 단기 기억(작업 기억)에만 머물고 며칠 뒤에는 사라진다고 설명하고 있습니다. ⑅가 포함된 문장은 'unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes(지식을 다시 테스트하지 않으면 기억이 사라진다)'라고 말하고 있으므로, 며칠 뒤에 그 효과가 '작아지는(minor)' 것이 아니라 '두드러지거나 명확해지는(evident, obvious, clear)' 것이 문맥상 적절합니다. 즉, 망각의 효과가 며칠 뒤면 확연히 드러난다는 의미가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 흐름상 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 표현을 영어로 쓰시오. (단, 반드시 주어진 철자로 완성하시오.) [24년 9월 35번]
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along ─ whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS ─ and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show ─ whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire ─ you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans to communicate ─ it has (A)b___________ in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of (B)c___________. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
subjective_conditions: 단, 반드시 주어진 철자로 완성하시오.
questions.explanation: 마셜 매클루언의 이론에 따르면 새로운 매체는 그 자체로 메시지를 '내포(buried)'하고 있으며, 우리를 새로운 '규칙/부호(codes)'에 따라 세상을 보게 만듭니다. 지문의 흐름상 (A)에는 '매체 안에 메시지가 묻혀 있다'는 의미의 buried가, (B)에는 '세상을 보는 새로운 방식'을 뜻하는 codes가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, (A)[commands / overlooks] many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or (B)[escape / accept] it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us (C)[adapt / adopt] and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: 감정의 진화적 목적에 관한 글입니다. (A) 감정은 촉발되었을 때 주의, 지각, 기억 등 여러 활동을 '지시(commands)'하는 프로그램 역할을 합니다. (B) 공포는 위협에 맞서 싸우거나(fight) 그것으로부터 '도피(escape)'하게(flight) 합니다. (C) 감정이 우리가 환경에 '적응(adapt)'하고 생존하도록 돕지 않았다면 진화하지 않았을 것이라는 내용이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 지시하다 - 도망치다 - 적응하다
② 지시하다 - 도망치다 - 입양하다[채택하다]
③ 간과하다 - 도망치다 - 입양하다[채택하다]
④ 간과하다 - 받아들이다 - 적응하다
⑤ 간과하다 - 받아들이다 - 입양하다[채택하다]

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is __________. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 베토벤, 브람스, 스트라빈스키 같은 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 이해받지 못한 이유는 그들의 음악적 형식이나 아이디어가 '완전히 새로웠기' 때문입니다. 반대로 살리에리는 실력이 좋았음에도 불구하고 그의 음악이 독창적이지 않고 당시의 다른 음악들과 비슷했기 때문에 위대한 작곡가가 되지 못했습니다. 따라서 초기에 대중에게 수용되지 못한 이유는 음악이 너무나 새로워서 생기는 '생소함(unfamiliarity)' 때문임을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: 객관성
게으름
편의성
모방
생소함

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. (A) This is of course quite a common experience. (B) The explanation is actually fairly simple. (C) There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. (D) One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. (E) Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
questions.insertion_sentence: But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path.
questions.explanation: (D) 문윙에서 목소리를 인식하는 첫 번째 경로(공기를 통한 외부 소리 경로)를 설명했습니다. 제시문은 'But'으로 시작하여 'second internal path(두 번째 내부 경로)'를 소개하므로, 첫 번째 경로 설명이 낽난 (E)에 들어가야 합니다. (E) 됔 문윙들은 이 두 번째 경로(겼도 전달)에 대한 부연 설명입니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
options: ① There are three types of similarity in biology.
② Analogous traits have been derived from the same evolutionary root and thus have the same function as well.
③ Homologous traits came from the same ancestral source.
④ The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse are considered analogously similar.
⑤ Biologists usually focus on the obvious traits of the organs to distinguish analogous traits from homologous ones.
questions.explanation:
① 지문에 따르면 생물학에는 '유사(analogous)'와 '상동(homologous)' 두 가지 유사성이 존재합니다. (오답)
② 유사 형질은 기능은 공통적이지만 진화의 다른 가지에서 발생한 것이며 계통이 다릅니다. (오답)
③ 상동 형질은 공통 조상(common ancestor)으로부터 유래한 것이며, 지문의 내용과 정확히 일치합니다. (정답)
④ 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 공통 조상에서 변형된 것이므로 '상동 형질'에 해당합니다. (오답)
⑤ 두 형질을 구분하기 위해 생물학자들은 명백한 특징이 아니라 가장 쓸모없는 속성(most useless properties)에 집중합니다. (오답)
options_translation: ① 생물학에는 세 가지 종류의 유사성이 존재한다.
② 유사 형질은 동일한 진화적 뿌리에서 기원했으며 기능 또한 동일하다.
③ 상동 형질은 동일한 조상으로부터 유래했다.
④ 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 유사 형질로 간주된다.
⑤ 생물학자들은 유사성과 상동성을 구분하기 위해 보통 장기의 눈에 띄는 명백한 특성에 집중한다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. (A) AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. (B) For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. (C) To illustrate, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. (D) Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 AI가 저숙련 노동자의 능력을 향상시켜 임금과 경력 전망에 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있다는 내용입니다. (C) 앞부분까지는 장애가 있는 노동자들을 위한 AI 보조 장치와 그 효과에 대해 설명하고 있으며, (C) 이후부터는 외국어 사용자나 저숙련 노동자의 업무 수행 능력을 높여주는 구체적인 사례(실시간 번역, 텍스트 생성기 등)를 제시하기 시작합니다. 따라서 (C) 위치가 저숙련 노동자에 대한 일반적인 진술을 시작하기에 가장 적합합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용을 하다 문장으로 요약하고자 하눜다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.summary_sentence: Social media fame, driven by (A)_____________________, represents a shift from traditional elite celebrity, which is based on (B)____________________.
options: (A) special talents / (B) renowned skills and talents
(A) engagement metrics / (B) skills and hierarchical status
(A) desire for endless reputation / (B) its own heritage skills
questions.explanation: 소셜 미디어 명성은 구독자, 좋아요 등의 참여 지표(engagement metrics)에 의해 결정되며, 이는 기술과 계층적 지위(skills and hierarchical status)에 기반한 전통적인 엘리트 명성과는 다르다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: (A) 특별한 재능 / (B) 유명한 기술과 재능
(A) 미디어 노출 / (B) 높은 광심 점수
(A) 참여 지표 / (B) 기술 및 계층적 지위
(A) 지석적인 사호작용 / (B) 우수한 신체적 외모
(A) 꺼지지 않눔 팑판에 대한 욕구 / (B) 고유의 전통 기술

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly ⓐ<u>efficientu</u> at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequestersan average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine ⓑ<u>equivalent</u> of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by ⓒ<u>fertilizing</u> the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon─leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystem." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic ⓓ<u>incentives</u> to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to ⓔ<u>accelerate</u> climate change.
questions.explanation: 지문은 고래가 탄소를 저장하고 배설물을 통해 식물성 플랑크톤의 증식을 도와 탄소 흡수를 촉진하는 등 기후 변화 해결을 위한 중요한 역할을 한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 고래 복원 프로그램을 제안하는 목적은 기후 변화를 '가속화(accelerate)'하기 위함이 아니라, 기후 변화를 완화하거나 해결하기 위함입니다. ⓔ는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does─this is one reason that cold polar seas are ⓐ<u>full</u> of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will ⓑ<u>decrease</u>. This  is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if ⓒ<u>allowed</u> to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level.  Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been ⓓ<u>declining</u> for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. ⓔ<u>Rising</u> oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced  populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 흐름은 지구 온난화로 인해 바닷물의 온도가 올라가고, 이로 인해 용존 산소량이 감소하고 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 해양 생물의 서식지에 영향을 주고 무산소 상태를 유발하는 것은 산소 수치가 'Rising(상승하는)' 것이 아니라 'Falling(하락하는)' 혹은 'Decreasing(감소하는)' 것이어야 합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
options: ② The Role of Advertisements in Sales
③ How to Utilize Client Information for Promotion
④ The Importance of Monitoring Post-Purchase Satisfaction
⑤ The Rise of Careers in Post-Purchase Customer Management
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구매 후 고객의 반응(만족도)을 파악하는 것이 재구매 여부, 타인에 대한 추천(입소문) 등에 큰 영향을 미치기 때문에 기업이 판매 후 만족도를 지속적으로 모니터링해야 한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 ④ '구매 후 만족도 모니터링의 중요성'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 광고가 신뢰할 수 없는 이유
② 판매에 있어서 광고의 역할
③ 홍보를 위해 고객 정보를 활용하는 방법
④ 구매 후 만족도 모니터링의 중요성
⑤ 구매 후 고객 관리 분야 직업의 부상

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recoding than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. (A) There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. (B) One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. (C) Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. (D) Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. (E) That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
questions.insertion_sentence: But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path.
questions.explanation: (B) 문장에서 첫 번째 경로(외부 소리 경로)에 대해 설명했고, 주어진 문장에서 '하지만 두 번째 내부 경로가 있다'고 전환하며 (C) 문장에서 그 경로의 작동 방식(뼈를 통한 진동 전달)을 설명하고 있으므로 ③이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.question: 13. 다음은 밑줄 친 field of contradictions가 의미하는 바를 설명한 문장이다. 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which allow lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a '<u>field of contradictions</u>' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
questions.summary_sentence: The 'field of contradictions' refers to the conflict between the (A)__________ of (B)__________ assessment and feedback in elite higher education and the practical (C)__________ of (D)__________ assessment methods in a mass system.
questions.explanation: 본문은 엘리트 교육 시스템에서의 개인화된 피드백과 학습을 위한 평가라는 '이상(ideals)'과, 대중 교육 시스템에서 효율성을 위해 요구되는 표준화된(standardised) 평가 방식이라는 '현실(realities)' 사이의 모순을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A) ideals, (B) personalized, (C) realities, (D) standardised가 들어가는 4번이 정답입니다.

② (A) 이상 - (B) 표준화된 - (C) 이론 - (D) 발달상의

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 31번]
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is ______________. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amdeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 이해받지 못한 이유는 그들의 음악적 형식이나 아이디어가 '완전히 새로웠기(completely new)' 때문입니다. 살리에리는 실력이 좋았음에도 불구하고 독창적(original)이지 않았기 때문에 위대한 작곡가 반열에 오르지 못했습니다. 즉, 위대한 작품의 초기 수용 거부 이유는 그 새로움에서 오는 '생소함(strangeness)' 때문입니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 9월 29번]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of ⓐ<u>different</u> departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and ⓑ<u>objective</u> perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which ⓒ<u>forbids</u> them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create ⓓ<u>disagreement</u>. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is more ⓔ<u>democratic</u> and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 조직 내의 각 부서들은 자신의 편향된 시각을 갖게 된다는 맥락이므로, '객관적인(objective)'이 아니라 '주관적인(subjective)' 또는 편향된 시각을 뒷받침하는 어휘가 와야 합니다. 바로 앞에 'biased(편향된)'라는 단어가 있으므로 objective는 문맥상 모순됩니다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our text book or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form.
ordered_passages: (A) To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
(B) After a few seconds of minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you reset your knowledge, memory vanishes.

(C) We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space, but this short-term sections has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 시험 직후 정보가 의식적인 작동 기억에 남아있는 상태를 설명합니다. (C)에서 이것이 단기 저장 공간에 있어 아는 것처럼 느껴지지만 장기 기억과는 무관함을 설명하고, (B)에서 시간이 흐름에 따라 이 작동 기억이 사라지는 과정을 언급하며, 마지막으로 (A)에서 정보를 장기 기억으로 넘기기 위한 실제적인 학습 전략(자가 테스트)을 제시하는 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a ⓐ<u>common</u> function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose ⓑ<u>dependently</u> in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they ⓒ<u>descended</u> from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very ⓓ<u>same</u> functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To ⓔ<u>distinguish</u> analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
questions.explanation: ⓑ: 상조적 특성(analogous traits)은 진화 계통도의 서로 다른 가지에서 발생한 것이므로 '독립적으로(independently)' 발생했다고 보아야 합니다. ⓓ: 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 상동적 특성(homologous traits)의 예시로, 기능은 서로 매우 '다르지만(different)' 구조적 뿌리가 같음을 설명하고 있으므로 same은 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 맥락상, 밑줄 친 ⓐ가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use ⓐ<u>it</u>, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show - whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① goggles with usual colors and lenses
② the invention of the printed book
④ a viewpoint through a new set of codes
⑤ a new way for humans to communicate
questions.explanation: 본문의 ⓐ it은 '새로운 매체(a new medium)'를 의미합니다. ①은 새로운 매체를 고글에 비유한 설명 과정에서 나온 말이지만, 본문에서는 '특별한 색상과 렌즈를 가진 고글'로 비유되었으므로 '평범한(usual)' 색상과 렌즈라는 표현은 맥락상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 묘장으로 요ׁ하고자 한다. 비유 (A), (B)에 들어갈 어휘로 가장 적절한 것을 <보기>에서 찾아 각각 슰시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
questions.summary_sentence: Concepts essential but can (A)___________ us into seeking (B)___________ things, like luminiferous ether.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 묜줄 친 ⓐ~ⓤ 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것을 모두 골라 기호를 슰고 적절한 표혔으로 각각 고치시오. [4.0점]

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)에 주어진 표현들만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 다음 우리말에 일치하도록 알맞은 문장으로 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - (A)[grapes / being universally / preferred / to / cucumbers] - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting -paid- the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. Furthermore, (B)she is now unwilling to cooperate for a reward she earlier found acceptable - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.answer: grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers
questions.explanation: 해당 문장은 분사구문으로서 'grapes'를 의미상의 주어로 가지고, 일반적으로 선호되는 대상이므로 수동형인 'being universally preferred'를 사용하여 'preferred to' 구문을 활용해 작성합니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 주어진 표현들만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 아래 우리말과 일치하도록 알맞은 문장으로 작성하시오.
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is (A)<u>we / who / the problem / with other persons / struggle / to be / have resolved / which / to choose / with</u>. questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions ①<u>helps</u> us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of -program- that, when ②<u>triggered</u>, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to ③<u>threatening</u> stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways ④<u>which</u> they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and ⑤<u>survive</u>, they would not have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: ④ 'the specific ways' 뒤에서 관계부사 how를 대신하거나 관계부사 역할을 할 수 있는 in which 또는 that이 와야 합니다. way와 how는 같이 쓸 수 없으므로 in which나 that이 적절하며, 단순히 관계대명사 which만 오는 것은 뒷문장이 완전하므로(they activate our systems) 어법상 틀립니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: While social media attention is ⓐ<u>potentially</u> an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity. This criticism highlights the fact ⓑ<u>which</u> digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and ⓒ<u>associated</u> with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity ⓓ<u>is</u> like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks ⓔ<u>built</u> into social media applications.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 'the fact' 뒤에 오는 절 'digital content creators face real barriers...'는 완전한 문장입니다. 따라서 명사 fact와 동격을 이루는 접속사 that이 와야 하며, 관계대명사인 which는 적절하지 않습니다.
