questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures.
ordered_passages: (A) This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century.
(B) Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease.

(C) The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 찬물이 더 많은 산소를 보유한다는 물리적 원리를 설명했습니다. (B)에서 'Thus(따라서)'를 통해 지구 온난화로 수온이 올라가면 산소량이 줄어든다는 인과관계를 설명하고, (A)에서 이러한 감소 현상이 실질적으로 일어나고 있다는 과학적 데이터 분석 내용을 도입합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 (A)의 데이터를 구체적으로 설명하며 해양 산소 수치 하락의 심각성을 강조하는 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle.
ordered_passages: (A) Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener.

(B) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them.

(C) A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 교통량을 줄이기 위한 대안으로 자전거나 보행자 전용 도로를 만드는 사례를 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 이러한 정책이 사람들로 하여금 자동차 대신 자전거를 이용하게 만드는 동기를 부여하며 자전거 중심의 도시 계획이 확장되는 과정을 설명합니다. (A)에서는 '그럼에도 불구하고(Nevertheless)' 도시 운영에 필수적인 트럭 등의 전용 차선이 여전히 필요함을 언급하며, 특히 배달 차량이 도시를 더 친환경적으로 만드는 중요한 요소임을 주장합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 배달 트럭이 개별 승용차보다 효율적이며 주민들이 걸어서 쇼핑할 수 있는 환경을 조성한다는 구체적인 근거를 들어 (A)의 주장을 뒷받침합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 연결사(접속부사)는? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. (A)__________, if you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. (B)__________, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞부분에서는 두 마리 모두 오이를 받을 때 만족한다는 긍정적인 상황을 제시했지만, (A) 뒷부분에서는 한 마리만 더 맛있는 포도를 받을 때 다른 마리가 불만을 품는 대조적인 상황이 나오므로 역접의 'However'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞부분에서는 타인과의 비교를 통해 상황이 불공평해졌음을 인식했다는 원인을 설명하고, (B) 뒷부분에서는 이에 더해 자신의 불만을 표현하기 위해 보상인 오이마저 버리는 추가적인 행동을 설명하고 있으므로 정보를 덧붙이는 'In addition'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 하지만 / 게다가
② 다시 말해서 / 더욱이
③ 사실 / 예를 들어
④ 마찬가지로 / 그러므로
⑤ 하지만 / 그럼에도 불구하고

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 (A)"tunnel vision"에 관한 설명으로 가장 옳은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire (A)<u>"tunnel vision"</u> which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
options: ① having a broader perspective than others see things
② Believing what others see and distrusting one's point of view
③ Seeing things from one's own perspective without believing in what others see
④ Seeing things from a prejudiced perspective without regarding them as others see them
⑤ Seeing things from an unbiased perspective while considering them as others see them
questions.explanation: 본문에서 (A)"tunnel vision"은 '부서와 구성원들이 사물을 다른 사람들이 보는 것처럼 보지 못하게 하는 것'으로 설명됩니다. 이는 자신의 편향되고 편견에 찬 관점에서만 상황을 바라보는 것을 의미하므로, '타인이 보는 방식을 고려하지 않고 편견 섞인 관점으로 사물을 보는 것'인 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 타인이 보는 것보다 더 넓은 관점을 갖는 것
② 타인이 보는 것을 믿고 자신의 관점을 불신하는 것
③ 타인이 보는 것을 믿지 않고 자신만의 관점에서 사물을 보는 것
④ 타인이 보는 방식을 고려하지 않고 편견에 찬 관점에서 사물을 보는 것
⑤ 타인이 보는 방식을 고려하면서 편향되지 않은 관점에서 사물을 보는 것

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were ⓐ<u>misjudged</u> in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is ⓑ<u>unusualness</u>. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. ⓒ<u>Ineffective</u> composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely ⓓ<u>blocked out</u> by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work was ⓔ<u>conventional</u>. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 작곡가들이 처음에는 그들의 독창성 때문에 이해받지 못하지만, 바로 그 점이 그들을 위대하게 만든다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 흐름상, 자신만의 독특한 아이디어를 갖는 것은 '위대한(Great)' 작곡가들의 특징입니다. 따라서 '비효율적인(Ineffective)'이 아니라 '위대한(Great)' 또는 '진정한(True)'과 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to ⓐ<u>differentiate</u> between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully ⓑ<u>present</u> in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has ⓒ<u>something</u> to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: ⓓ<u>unless</u> you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then ⓔ<u>test</u> yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.explanation: 벼락치기가 효과가 있다고 느끼는 이유는 단기 기억에 정보가 남아있어 그것을 안다고 착각하기 때문입니다. 하지만 단기 기억과 며칠 뒤에 필요한 장기 기억은 거의 상관이 없다는 문맥이 되어야 하므로 'has something to do with'(~와 관계가 있다)가 아니라 'has nothing to do with'(~와 관계가 없다) 또는 'has little to do with'가 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 공통으로 들어갈 적절한 한 단어를 지문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of (A)__________ energy and relighting of one's own latent (B)__________ thought forms.
subjective_conditions: 지문에서 찾아 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 이 글은 부정적인 상태에서 벗어나기 위해 문제를 해결한 사람들과 함께하는 것이 도움이 된다고 설명합니다. 자조 그룹 등을 통해 긍정적인 에너지가 전달되고(transfer of positive energy) 잠재되어 있던 긍정적인 사고 형태가 다시 불붙게 된다는 내용이므로, 지문에 언급된 'positive'가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 요지를 제시된 우리말에 맞게 주어진 조건에 따라 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
subjective_conditions: 제시된 표현들을 <u>반드시, 모두, 차례대로</u> 사용하고, 필요하면 형태를 바꿀 것
필요 어휘를 추가하고, 필요하면 형태를 바꿀 것
총 20~22개의 단어를 사용할 것
vocabulary_box: we / be / encourage / see / exist / explore / in vain / by / so / must / careful
questions.answer: We are encouraged to see things that don't exist and explore them in vain by concepts so we must be careful.
questions.explanation: 우리말 해석에 맞게 수동태(be encouraged to)와 병렬 구조(to see ... and explore)를 활용하여 문장을 구성합니다. '존재하지 않는 것들'은 things that don't exist로, '개념에 의하여'는 by concepts로 표현합니다. 주어진 단어들을 활용하여 조건에 맞는 21단어 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 영어 문장을 주어진 조건에 따라 쓰시오. [5.0점]
questions.passage: (A)______________________________________________________? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
subjective_conditions: 1. 우리말: '당신은 당신 자신의 음성 녹음을 듣고 놀랐던 적이 있는가?'
2. 현재완료 시제를 사용할 것.
3. 주어진 단어를 모두 포함하고 필요 어휘를 추가할 것.
4. 총 13개의 어휘로 문장을 완성할 것.
vocabulary_box: own / a recording / surprised / ever / of
questions.answer: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice?
questions.explanation: 현재완료 의문문 'Have you ever been surprised'를 사용하고, 감정의 원인을 나타내는 to부정사 'to hear'와 목적어 'a recording of your own voice'를 연결하여 총 13단어의 문장을 만듭니다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire (A)<u>"tunnel vision"</u> which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
options: ① having a broader perspective than others see things
② Believing what others see and distrusting one's point of view
③ Seeing things from one's own perspective without believing in what others see
④ Seeing things from a prejudiced perspective without regarding them as others see them
⑤ Seeing things from an unbiased perspective while considering them as others see them
questions.explanation: 글의 문맥상 'tunnel vision'은 조직 내의 서로 다른 부서나 부문의 구성원들이 자신들만의 편향되고 편견에 찬 관점에서 상황을 바라보게 되어 타인의 관점을 보지 못하는 상태를 의미합니다. 따라서 ④번 '다른 사람들이 보는 대로 그것들을 고려하지 않고 편견에 찬 관점에서 사물을 보는 것'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 타인이 보는 것보다 더 넓은 관점을 갖는 것
② 타인이 보는 것을 믿고 자신의 관점을 불신하는 것
③ 타인이 보는 것을 믿지 않고 자신만의 관점에서 사물을 보는 것
④ 다른 사람들이 보는 대로 고려하지 않고 편견에 박힌 관점에서 사물을 보는 것
⑤ 다른 사람들이 보는 대로 고려하면서 편견 없는 관점에서 사물을 보는 것

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. (A) Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. (B) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. (C) As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. (D) Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. (E) Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.insertion_sentence: Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그럼에도 불구하고, 자전거 타기에 가장 좋은 도시조차 택시, 긴급 차량, 배달 트럭을 위한 자동차 차선이 여전히 필요하다'는 내용입니다. (C)까지는 도시에서 자동차 차선을 자전거 도로로 전환하는 내용을 다루고 있고, (D) 이후부터는 배달 차량(Delivery vehicles)이 도시를 더 친환경적으로 만드는 필수 요소라는 구체적인 설명이 시작됩니다. 따라서 자동차 차선이 여전히 필요한 이유 중 하나인 배달 트럭에 대한 논의를 도입하는 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. ________________________________ Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
options: ① Vibrations have an adverse effect on the health of the ear.
② Vibration plays a role in amplifying high frequencies.
③ Vibrations directly transfer to the vocal cords and have a positive effect on it.
④ Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our outside of ear directly.
⑤ Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly.
questions.explanation: 자신의 목소리가 녹음된 것과 다르게 들리는 이유를 설명하는 글입니다. 공기를 통해 전달되는 외부 경로 외에, 성대의 진동이 뼈를 통해 직접 내이(inner ear)를 자극하는 두 번째 내부 경로가 있음을 설명해야 합니다. 빈칸 뒤에 낮은 주파수가 이 경로를 통해 강조되어 목소리가 더 깊고 풍부하게 들린다는 내용이 이어지므로, 진동이 뼈를 통해 전달되어 직접 내이를 자극한다는 내용인 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 진동은 귀의 건강에 부정적인 영향을 미친다.
② 진동은 높은 주파수를 증폭시키는 역할을 한다.
③ 진동은 성대에 직접 전달되어 긍정적인 영향을 미친다.
④ 진동은 우리의 뼈를 통해 전도되어 외이를 직접 자극한다.
⑤ 진동은 우리의 뼈를 통해 전도되어 내이를 직접 자극한다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that ⓐ<u>have</u> a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose ⓑ<u>independently</u> in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates ⓒ<u>they</u> being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are ⓓ<u>connected</u>. ⓔ<u>To distinguish</u> analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
questions.explanation: ⓒ의 they는 being이라는 동명사의 의미상 주어 역할을 하고 있습니다. 동명사의 의미상 주어는 소유격이나 목적격을 쓰는 것이 원칙이므로, 주격인 they 대신 their 또는 them을 써야 어법상 적절합니다. ⓐ 'ones'를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 절의 동사로 복수 형태 'have'는 적절합니다.ⓑ 'arose'(발생했다)라는 동사를 수식하는 부사 'independently'는 적절합니다.ⓓ 'the ways (that) they are connected'에서 수동태 'are connected'는 '뼈들이 연결된 방식'이라는 수동의 의미로 적절합니다.ⓔ '~하기 위해서'라는 목적의 의미를 나타내는 부사적 용법의 To부정사로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C) 괄호 안에서 알맞은 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement. expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (A)[stimulate / struggle] or avoid it (B)[escape/ eliminate], and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely. Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us survive (C)[hardship / harmony] within our environment long ago.
questions.explanation: (A) 상황에 맞서 싸우거나(struggle) 피하는 것(avoid)이 공포에 대한 일반적인 반응입니다. (B) 상황을 피하는 것은 곧 도망치는 것(escape)을 의미합니다. (C) 감정은 우리가 과거 환경 속에서 고난(hardship)을 이겨내고 생존하도록 돕기 위해 존재한다고 설명하는 것이 글의 문맥에 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 자극하다 (B) 제거하다 (C) 조화
② (A) 투쟁하다 (B) 탈출하다 (C) 고난
③ (A) 자극하다 (B) 탈출하다 (C) 고난
④ (A) 투쟁하다 (B) 제거하다 (C) 조화
⑤ (A) 투쟁하다 (B) 제거하다 (C) 조화

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
options: ① If their parents stick out their tongue, newborns have an innate trait to stick out their tongue.
② Whenever parents stick theirs out, they may not see the stick out.
③ Over time, babies begin to mimic the sounds their parents produce.
④ We live in the special world where we are not limited to the behavior we are born with.
⑤ The mirror neuron is same with a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation.
questions.explanation: 거울 뉴런의 발견이 관찰을 통한 학습이라는 인간의 근본적인 능력에 대한 생각을 바꾼 것이지, 거울 뉴런 자체가 관찰을 통한 학습과 동일한 것은 아닙니다. 거울 뉴런은 이러한 능력을 가능하게 하는 신경학적 기제일 뿐입니다. 나머지 선택지는 지문의 내용과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 부모가 혀를 내밀면, 신생아는 혀를 내미는 타고난 특성을 가지고 있다.
② 부모가 혀를 내밀 때마다, 혀가 나오는 것을 보지 못할 수도 있다.
③ 시간이 지나면서, 아기들은 부모가 내는 소리를 흉내 내기 시작한다.
④ 우리는 우리가 타고난 행동에 국한되지 않는 특별한 세상에 살고 있다.
⑤ 거울 뉴런은 인간의 근본적인 능력인 관찰을 통한 학습과 동일하다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation __________________. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 져직 내의 서로 다른 부서들은 각자의 기능적 역할에 따라 "턴널 시야(tunnel vision)"를 갇값 되며, 이눤 다른 사람들이 방식으로 사물을 보지 못하값 합니다. 따라서 제시된 사황을 그들의 고정관널(자신들만의 관점)에서 바라보값 된다눤 내용이 들어가야 합니다.

④ 견정한 관점에서

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.

② 제거하는 것 - 극복했다

④ 제거하는 것 - 형성했다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were ⓐ<u>misunderstood</u> in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is ⓑ<u>unfamiliarity</u>. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous ⓒ<u>non-great</u> composers ─ he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely ⓓ<u>overshadowed</u> by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the word's great composers because his work was ⓔ<u>unfamiliar</u>. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 위대한 작곡가들은 그들의 음악이 당시에 '생소(unfamiliar)'했기 때문에 오해를 받았다고 설명합니다. 반면 살리에리는 훌륭한 작곡가였음에도 세계적인 거장이 되지 못한 이유가 그의 작품이 당시의 다른 사람들의 음악과 비슷하게 들렸기 때문이라고 했습니다. 즉, 그의 음악은 생소했던 것이 아니라 '익숙'하거나 '독창적이지 않았던' 것입니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 unfamiliar는 familiar 혹은 unoriginal과 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 주제를 10단어 이내로 영작하시오.

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle.
ordered_passages: (A) However, even the best cities for cycling still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. In particular, a tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each.

(B) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them.

(C) Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries. For that reason, delivery vehicles are actually an essential component to making cities more eco-friendly, despite the fact that they are frequently a target of animus.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 자전거와 보행자를 위해 도로를 예약한다고 했으므로, 이것이 사람들이 차 대신 자전거를 타도록 유도한다는 (B)가 먼저 오는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 그 다음, 자전거를 타기 좋은 도시라도 배달 트럭 등을 위한 차선은 여전히 필요하다는 역접의 내용인 (A)가 이어지고, 마지막으로 이러한 배달 차량이 오히려 친환경적인 도시를 만드는 데 필수적인 요소라는 구체적 설명인 (C)가 오는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the ⓐ<u>functional</u> operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will be inevitably ⓑ<u>prejudiced</u> by viewing any given situation from their own perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which ⓒ<u>permits</u> them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a more ⓓ<u>concentrated</u> hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many vertical levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is ⓔ<u>distributed</u> across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 부서의 구성원들이 '터널 시야(tunnel vision)'를 갖게 된다는 것은 자신의 관점에서만 사물을 보게 된다는 의미입니다. 따라서 ⓒ의 'permits(허용하다)' 뒤에 'to see things as others see them(다른 사람들이 보는 대로 사물을 보게)'은 터널 시야의 의미와 반대됩니다. 다른 사람의 관점을 보지 못하게 한다는 의미의 'prevents'나 'stops' 등이 적절하며, 혹은 뒤의 내용을 'to see things only from their own perspective'로 바꾸어야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because having contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. ⓐFrom an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.. ⓑFor example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation or avoid it, and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely so that we avoid the threat in the future. ⓒHowever, acting purely based on emotions can sometimes lead to irrational decisions or negative outcomes, especially in complex social situations. ⓓRegardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us as a species survive challenges within our environment long ago. ⓔIn modern times, these emotions continue to influence our behavior, even though the dangers we face today may be less immediate or life-threatening compared to those in our evolutionary past.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 감정이 진화론적 관점에서 인류의 생존에 기여하기 위해 존재한다는 것입니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 감정이 생존을 돕는 프로그램이거나 과거부터 현재까지 생존에 도움을 주는 역할을 한다는 내용입니다. 하지만 ⓒ는 감정에 기반한 행동이 불합리한 결정이나 부정적 결과를 초래할 수 있다는 '감정의 부작용'에 대해 언급하고 있어 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 32번]
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show - whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① Television: The End of Traditional Media
② The History of Human Communication Tools
③ The Evolution of Technology: From Books to TV
④ Why Social Media Is the Best Way to Communicate
⑤ The Lens of the Medium That Shapes Our Perception

questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because _____________________________. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
options: ① behaviors born with are the most important
② there are limits to what we can see and learn
③ there are restrictions to what we can learn through imitation
④ we can only acquire a certain behavior by imitating someone.
⑤ we are not limited to innate behaviors or learn through experiences
questions.explanation: 거울 뉴런의 발견을 통해 인간이 관찰과 모방을 통해 학습한다는 점을 설명하는 글입니다. 인간의 문명이 작동하는 이유는 인간이 타고난 행동에만 국한되지 않고 타인의 행동을 보고 배우는 능력이 있기 때문입니다. 마지막 문장에서 '타인을 보는 것만으로도 많은 것을 배울 수 있다'고 언급하므로, ⑤번 '우리가 타고난 행동에 국한되지 않거나 경험을 통해 배우기 때문에'가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 타고난 행동이 가장 중요하다
② 우리가 보고 배울 수 있는 것에는 한계가 있다
③ 모방을 통해 배울 수 있는 것에는 제약이 있다
④ 우리는 누군가를 모방함으로써만 특정 행동을 습득할 수 있다
⑤ 우리가 타고난 행동에 국한되지 않거나 경험을 통해 배우기 때문에

questions.question: 20. 다음 글에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that are ⓐ<u>non-existent</u>. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully ⓑ<u>summarizes</u> the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the ⓒ<u>valid</u> concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a ⓓ<u>delusion</u>. Physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not ⓔ<u>exist</u>.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학자들이 존재하지 않는 '본질(essence)'을 찾으려 노력했던 오류에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 문맥상 과학자들이 결과적으로 존재하지 않는 에테르와 같은 개념을 쫓았으므로, 그들이 가설을 세울 때 사용한 개념은 '타당한(valid)' 것이 아니라 '잘못된(faulty or wrong)' 것이어야 합니다. 따라서 ⓒ의 valid는 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself.
ordered_passages: (A) However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people.

(B) Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity.

(C) To put it simply, achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 소셜 미디어 크리에이터들이 평범한 명성 그 자체를 목표로 삼기도 한다는 점을 언급합니다. (B)는 이러한 크리에이터들이 전문적인 재능이 없다는 비판을 받는 현실과 엘리트 명성으로의 진입 장벽을 설명합니다. (A)는 그러나 이러한 비판이 평범한 명성이 갖는 새로운 의미를 간과하고 있음을 지적하며 두 명성의 차이를 대조합니다. (C)는 결론적으로 이러한 평범한 명성은 수치화된 지표를 겨루는 게임과 같은 성격을 띠고 있음을 설명하며 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most __________ properties.
questions.explanation: 지문은 '상사(analogous)'와 '상동(homologous)' 형질의 차이를 설명합니다. 상동 형질의 핵심은 기능과 상관없이 공통 조상으로부터 물려받은 구조적 특징을 공유한다는 점입니다. 예를 들어 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 기능은 다르지만 뼈의 구조를 공유하는데, 이는 생존을 위한 '기능적' 요소가 아니더라도 남아있는 특징들입니다. 따라서 생물학자들은 두 개념을 구분하기 위해 기능적이지 않은, 즉 실용적이지 않은(unusable/nonfunctional) 특성들에 주목합니다. 본문의 'nonfunctional'을 빈칸의 'unusable'로 연결할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 사용할 수 없는 (비기능적인)
② 독창적인
③ 실용적인
④ 가치 있는
⑤ 아주 귀중한

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys ⓐ<u>which</u> live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will ⓑ<u>gladly</u> eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes ⓒ<u>being</u> universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation ⓓ<u>unfairly</u>. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers ⓔ<u>themselves</u> - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 'makes the situation unfairly'는 5형식 문장입니다. 동사 make는 목적어(the situation) 뒤에 목적격 보어를 취하는데, 보어 자리에는 부사가 올 수 없고 형용사가 와야 합니다. 따라서 'unfairly'를 형용사인 'unfair'로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: AI can improve accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, those with visual, speech or hearing difficulties. AI-powered assistive devices to aid them are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.summary_sentence: AI helps create more (A)__________ work environments by offering tools to assist employees with disabilities and lead to better job opportunities and higher earnings by (B)__________ the abilities of workers with fewer skills.
questions.explanation: 본문은 AI가 장애가 있는 근로자들의 접근성을 높여주고(inclusive - 포용적인), 저숙련 근로자들의 능력을 향상시켜(elevating - 높이는) 임금과 경력 전망에 긍정적인 영향을 준다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 포용적인 환경을 뜻하는 'inclusive', (B)에는 능력을 향상시킨다는 의미인 'elevating'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 포용적인 / 제한하는
② 포용적인 / 높이는(향상시키는)
③ 친숙한 / 육성하는
④ 친숙한 / 높이는(향상시키는)
⑤ 지원적인 / 제한하는

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
questions.summary_sentence: The reason the voices we hear on voice recordings sound (A)__________ is because our second internal pathway directly stimulates the inner ear, making lower frequencies more (B)__________.
questions.explanation: 녹음된 자신의 목소리가 낯설게(strange/unusual) 들리는 이유는, 평소 자신의 목소리를 들을 때는 뼈를 통한 내부 경로로 저주파가 더 강조되어(prominent) 들리기 때문입니다. 하지만 녹음기에서는 공기를 통한 외부 경로로만 소리가 전달되므로 우리가 듣던 것과 다르게 들리게 됩니다. (A)에는 'strange(낯선)', (B)에는 'prominent(두드러진)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 친숙한 - 놀라운
다른 - 불분명한
낯선 - 두드러진
흥미로운 - 독특한

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.summary_sentence: As global warming progresses, the amount of dissolved oxygen will (A)__________, increasing the likelihood that it will have a/an (B)__________ impact on the habitats of marine life.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 지구 온난화로 바닷물의 온도가 상승함에 따라 용존 산소량은 감소(decrease)하게 되며, 이는 해양 생물들의 서식지에 부정적인(negative/adverse) 영향을 미치게 됩니다. 따라서 (A)에는 decrease, (B)에는 negative가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 감소하다 - 부정적인
상승하다 - 미묘한
안정되다 - 불리한

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the ⓐ<u>great</u> powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are ⓑ<u>weak</u>. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized ⓒ<u>positive</u> thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the ⓓ<u>winners</u>." The ⓔ<u>risk</u> here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.*latent: 잠재적인
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 자조 집단에 있거나 높은 진동(긍정적 상태)을 가진 사람들과 함께 있는 것은 긍정적인 에너지를 전이받고 잠재된 긍정적 사고를 다시 불붙이는 유익한 과정입니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 'risk(위험)'는 문맥상 어울리지 않으며, 에너지 전이가 일어나는 'benefit(이득)' 또는 'mechanism(메커니즘)' 혹은 'process(과정)' 등의 긍정적이거나 중립적인 단어가 와야 합니다. 원문에서는 'benefit' 혹은 'phenomenon'의 맥락을 설명하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are ⓐ<u>unable</u> to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully ⓑ<u>present</u> in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we ⓒ<u>know</u> it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts ⓓ<u>appearing</u>, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous. Unless you retest your knowledge, memory ⓔ<u>vanishes</u>. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.*cram: 벼락 공부를 하다
questions.explanation: 문맥상 작업 기억(working memory)은 몇 초 또는 몇 분 후에 사라지기 시작해야 내용이 성립됩니다. 따라서 'appearing(나타나는)'은 'fading' 또는 'disappearing'과 같이 '사라지는' 의미를 가진 단어로 고쳐야 적절합니다. 본문 뒷부분에서 며칠 후에는 그 효과가 엄청나며 재시험을 보지 않으면 기억이 사라진다(vanishes)는 내용과도 일치합니다.

Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.*sphere: 영역 **metric: 측정 기준
questions.summary_sentence: Social media content creators face criticism for (A)____________ the traditional skills of elite celebrities, but what they pursue is ordinary fame by frequent interactions with (B)____________ people.
questions.explanation: 소셜 미디어 제작자들은 전통적인 유명인의 기술(연기, 노래 등)이 부족하다(lacking)는 비판을 받지만, 실제로는 일반적인(common) 사람들과의 활발한 소통을 통해 평범한 명성을 얻고자 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 'lacking', (B)에는 'common'이 적합합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they ____________________________.
options: ② would not have evolved with us
③ might have helped other species
④ would be stronger than they used to
⑤ could have helped us connect with others more effectively
questions.explanation: 감정은 인류의 생존과 적응에 기여했기 때문에 진화적으로 존재한다는 내용의 글입니다. 마지막 문장은 가정법 과거완료 구문으로, 만약 감정이 생존에 도움이 되지 않았더라면 '우리와 함께 진화하지 않았을 것'이라는 내용이 와야 논리적으로 완결됩니다.
options_translation: 더 오래 머물 수 있었을 것이다
우리와 함께 진화하지 않았을 것이다
다른 종들을 도왔을지도 모른다
예전보다 더 강해졌을 것이다
우리가 다른 이들과 더 효과적으로 연결되도록 도왔을 수도 있다

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the ______________ makes the situation unfair. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.explanation: 카푸친 원숭이가 다른 원숭이가 더 좋은 보상(포도)을 받는 것을 보았을 때, 자신이 받는 동일한 보상(오이)에 대해 불공평함을 느끼고 거부한다는 실험 내용입니다. 보상 자체의 절대적 가치는 변하지 않았으나, 타인과의 '비교(comparison)'가 불공평함을 느끼게 만드는 핵심 요인이므로 빈칸에 적절합니다.

용이성
제거
비교
불편함

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: AI can improve __________________ in the workplace. It can improve accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where interpersonal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 AI가 노동 시장에서 불리한 위치에 있는 노동자들(장애인, 저숙련 노동자, 비원어민 등)의 직장 내 접근성을 높이고 업무 수행 능력을 향상시킴으로써 '포용성(inclusiveness)'을 개선할 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 시각·청각 장애인을 위한 보조 장치, 저숙련자를 위한 텍스트 생성기, 비원어민을 위한 실시간 번역 등이 그 예시로 제시되었으므로 빈칸에는 '포용성'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 포용성
② 비용 효율성
③ 비판적 사고
④ 자연주의적 지능
⑤ 시각화의 힘

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. (A) Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. (B) This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. (C) However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. (D) In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. (E) In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.*adversarial: 저ᄀ대재ᄀ인
questions.insertion_sentence: Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate.
questions.explanation: 제시문으는 '하지만 혀ᄇ사ᄀ하느ᄂᆫ 버발 배우느ᄂ나라믄 거의 어ᄇ다'느ᄂ데, (A) 뒤ᄋ이 'Those who do(그러하느ᄂ사라ᄆ들)'으느ᄂ다 제시문으이 'few people ever learn'에사거 'learn'으라를 대도ᄀ사 do라로 바다사거 '(그러하게 배우느ᄂ) 사라ᄆ드ᄅ도 겨ᄅ구ᄀ 저ᄂ퐁저ᄀ하고 승패가 나뉘느ᄂ 바ᄂ시ᄀ으라로 배우ᄂ다'느ᄂ 내용으라로 이어지므로 (A) 자리가 가자ᄀ 저ᄀ저하다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might ␐으increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too ␑으large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may ␒으value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an ␓으attractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might ␔으fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.*fractionalization: 부녈
questions.explanation: 문매ᄀ사ᄃ 다야ᄂ사그라를 구ᄀ가 저제사ᄀ으이 요고그로 이ᄂ시ᄀ하느ᄂ 경우, 다야ᄂ사그느ᄂ 매려ᄀ저ᄀ이지 안은(unattractive 호그ᄂ negative) 파지로 이ᄂ시ᄀᄒᅠ 사이햬가 이러나거나 가로파느ᄂ 드다의 내용으라로 이어지느ᄂ 거시 저ᄀ저하다. 따라사 ␓으느ᄂ unattractive 드다로 고쳐야 하ᄂ다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is hard for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.summary_sentence: Moving is especially (A)_________ for young children, so it's important to (B)_________ their past experiences while supporting them in adjusting to their new environment.
questions.explanation: 이사 과정은 어린 아이들에게 매우 '힘든(challenging/stressful)' 경험이 될 수 있습니다. 본문은 부모가 아이들의 과거 경험을 '인정해주고(acknowledge/validate)' 존중해주는 것이 중요하다고 강조하고 있으므로 (A)에는 challenging, (B)에는 acknowledge가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 별개의 ... 삭제하다
② 어려운 ... 분석하다
③ 스트레스가 많은 ... 조사하다
④ 힘든 ... 인정하다
⑤ 압도적인 ... 소통하다

questions.question: 18. According to the following passage, what are not examples of "complementary goods"?
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status - they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb.
options: ⑤ tennis balls and tennis rackets
questions.explanation: 보완재(complementary goods)는 한 제품의 소비가 늘어날 때 함께 소비되는 제품을 의미합니다. 와인과 와인잔, 프린터와 잉크, 칫솔과 치약, 테니스공과 라켓은 서로 보완 관계에 있으나, 천연가스와 석탄은 서로를 대신하여 사용될 수 있는 대체재(substitute goods)의 성격이 강하므로 보완재의 예로 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound?
ordered_passages: (A) And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience.
(B) The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer.
(C) Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
(D) Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문윑에서 숲셍에 나무가 쓰러질 때 들을 사람이 없으면 소리가 나는지에 대한 질문을 던집니다. (B)에서 광학적 답은 'No'라고 하며, 듣는 사람이 없으면 소리가 없다고 설명합니다. (A)에서는 이와 유사하게 과학적 커무니케이션도 수신자가 이해해야 성립된다는 비유림을 듭니다. (D)에서 결과가 출판되고 이해되어야 과학 실험이 완성된다는 과학의 원리림 재진술하고, (C)에서 출판물이 이해되지 않으면 소리 없이 쓰러지는 나무와 같다고 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 비칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 적절한 한 단어림 쓰시오. (단, 주어진 �자로 시작할 것)

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 비칸에 들어갈 적절핬 말을 아래 주어진 표현들만을 사용하여 완성하시오. (변형 및 추가하지 말 것)

questions.explanation: 글의 제목이나 요지와 관련된 문장으로, "당신의 행동으로 자녀에겄 삶의 좋은 밸보기림 보여주라"는 의문문 형태의 명령문이나 결론 문장이 들어갈 자리입니다. 주어진 단어림 조합하면 show(동슬) + your child(간접목적어) + good examples of life(직접목적어) + by your action(수단 부사구)가 됩니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓛ 중 지칭하는 것이 같은 것을 바르게 묶은 것은?
questions.passage: [24년 9월 24번]Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When ⓐ<u>they</u> die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that ⓑ<u>carbon</u> out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of ⓒ<u>thousands of trees</u>. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as ⓓ<u>they</u> release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing ⓔ<u>phytoplankton</u> populations, which also are ⓕ<u>carbon storage</u> - leading ⓖ<u>some scientists</u> to call ⓗ<u>them</u> the "engineers of ⓘ<u>marine ecosystems</u>." In 2019, ⓙ<u>economists</u> from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. ⓚ<u>They</u> called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. ⓛ<u>Their</u> calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓓ, ⓗ는 모두 이 글의 핵심 소재인 '고래(whales)'를 지칭합니다.ⓑ: 탄소(carbon)ⓒ: 수천 그루의 나무(thousands of trees)ⓔ: 식물성 플랑크톤(phytoplankton)ⓕ: 탄소 저장소(carbon storage)ⓖ: 일부 과학자들(some scientists)ⓘ: 해양 생태계(marine ecosystems)ⓙ, ⓚ, ⓛ: IMF의 경제학자들(economists) 또는 그들의 요청

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 옳지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: [24년 9월 31번]You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were not ⓐ<u>understandable</u> in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas conveyed within them, were completely ⓑ<u>innovative</u>. And yet, this is exactly one of the aspects that makes them so ⓒ<u>common</u>. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's ⓓ<u>regarded</u> as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer: in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he composed ⓔ<u>resembled</u> the music that everyone else was creating at that time.
questions.explanation: 위대한 작곡가들의 음악이 당대에는 이해받지 못했던 이유는 그들의 음악적 형식이 '혁신적(innovative)'이었기 때문입니다. 이러한 혁신성은 그들을 '흔하게(common)' 만드는 것이 아니라 '독창적'이거나 '특별하게' 만드는 요소여야 문맥상 적절합니다. 뒤이어 나오는 살리에리의 예시가 그의 작품이 독창적이지 않고 남들과 비슷했기에 위대한 작곡가가 되지 못했다고 설명하는 것과 대조를 이룹니다. 따라서 ⓒ common은 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 옳지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are crucial for human survival, but they can also go astray by fostering essentialism, making us perceive things that aren't really there. Firestein begins Ignorance, his book, with an old proverb: "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This perfectly captures the futile search for essences. History shows many cases where scientists, guided by ⓐ<u>incorrect</u> concepts, searched in vain for nonexistent essences. Firestein cites luminiferous ether, a supposed substance believed to permeate the universe as a medium for light. This ether was the proverbial black cat: physicists theorized and experimented in the dark, looking for evidence of something that wasn't there. The same ⓑ<u>mistake</u> can be seen in the classical view of emotion, whose mental organs are a human invention that mistakes the question for the answer. Concepts also encourage us not to see things that are ⓒ<u>present</u>. One illusory stripe of a rainbow contains an infinite number of frequencies, but your concepts for "Red," "Blue," and other colors cause your brain to ignore the ⓓ<u>variability</u>. Likewise, the frowny-faced stereotype of "Sadness" is a concept that ⓔ<u>highlights</u> the great variation in that emotion category.*astray: 길을 잃은*in vain: 헛되이
questions.explanation: 지문은 개념이 실재하지 않는 것을 보게 하거나 실재하는 차이점을 무시하게 만든다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 '슬픔'에 대한 고정관념은 그 감정 범주 내의 큰 변동성(variation)을 보여주는(highlight) 것이 아니라, 오히려 그러한 차이점을 무시하거나 가리게 만드는 역할을 해야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 ⑤번 'highlights'는 부적절하며 'ignores'나 'hides'와 같은 의미의 단어가 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글을 읽고 아래 문단을 완성하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are those that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are not the same organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are a textbook example: Both are used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. This process is known as convergent evolution. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that speaks their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat, the front leg of a horse, the flipper of a seal, the claw of a mole, and the hand of a human have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals, and as a result they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their properties.
questions.summary_sentence: "Analogous" traits indicate that (A)____________ evolution has occurred, where unrelated species independently develop (B)____________ functions. In contrast, "homologous" characteristics indicate that (C)____________ evolution has occurred, where the traits are inherited from a common ancestor, regardless of whether they have the same (D)____________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 상조(analogous) 형질과 상동(homologous) 형질을 대조합니다. 상조 형질은 독립적으로 발달하여 '수렴(convergent)' 진화가 일어난 것으로, 관련 없는 종이 '동일한(same)' 기능을 수행하게 됩니다. 반면 상동 형질은 공통 조상으로부터 유래한 것으로 '이산(divergent)' 진화가 일어난 것이며, '기능(function)'이 같은지 여부와 상관없이 구조를 공유합니다.
options_translation: ① 수렴의 / 동일한 / 이산의 / 기능

questions.question: 22. 다음 조건에 맞게 밑줄 친 (A)~(C)를 영작하시오.
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You probably thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" (A)<u>녹음에서 당신이 인식한 것보다 당신의 억양이 더 강조되었거나</u>, or (B)<u>당신의 목소리가 당신의 귀에 들리는 것 같은 것보다 더 높았었을 지도 모른다</u>. This is, of course, quite a common experience, and the explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle, and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway, which (C)<u>당신의 목소리가 당신 자신에게 더 깊고 풍부하게 들리게 했을지도 모른다</u>. This was why your voice sounded strange when you heard a recording of it.
subjective_conditions: 아래 <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것
필요한 단어 추가할 것
필요시 주어진 단어 변형할 것
vocabulary_box: (C) might / rich / voice / make / have / deep
questions.answer: (A) might have been more pronounced(B) might have sounded higher(C) might have made your voice sound deeper and richer
questions.explanation: 과거의 사실에 대한 추측을 나타내는 'might have + p.p.' 구문을 사용하는 문제입니다.(A) 억양이 '강조되다'는 수동의 의미이므로 'might have been pronounced'를 사용하며, '더' 강조된 것이므로 'more pronounced'로 작성합니다.(B) 목소리가 '들렸을지도 모른다'는 'might have sounded'이며, '더 높게' 들린 것이므로 비교급 'higher'를 사용합니다.(C) 'make(사역동사) + 목적어(your voice) + 목적격보어(sound + 형용사)' 구조를 사용합니다. '깊고 풍부하게'는 비교급 'deeper and richer'로 표현하여 'might have made your voice sound deeper and richer'가 됩니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 조건에 맞게 답하시오.Q: The experimenters gave one monkey grapes and gave another cucumbers. Why did the monkey with cucumbers throw them back?
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
subjective_conditions: 아래 <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것
필요한 단어 추가할 것
필요시 주어진 단어 변형할 것
vocabulary_box: so / unfair / them / that / she / threw / back
questions.answer: was so unfair to the monkey that received cucumbers that she threw them back.
questions.explanation: 이 질문은 오이를 받은 원숭이가 왜 그것을 다시 던졌는지를 묻고 있습니다. 지문에 따르면 다른 원숭이가 포도를 받는 것과 비교했을 때 자신의 상황이 불공평하다고 느꼈기 때문입니다. 'so + 형용사 + that + 주어 + 동사' (너무 ~해서 ...하다) 구문을 사용하여, 상황이 너무 불공평해서 원숭이가 오이를 다시 던졌다는 내용을 영작합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 social media celebrities에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.*sphere: 영역 **metric: 측정 기준
options: ① 연기나 가창력 비판을 종종 받는다.
② 엘리트 명성의 영역으로 가는데 장벽이 있다.
③ 스타라는 은유로 상징되고 계층적 거리로 특징지어진다.
④ 평범한 사람들과의 상호작용을 통해 관심을 끈다.
⑤ 명성은 소셜 미디어 애플리케이션에 내장된 점수가 높다는 뜻일 뿐이다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 '스타라는 은유로 상징되고, 신비로움과 계층적 거리로 특징지어지는 것'은 '소셜 미디어 유명인(ordinary celebrity)'이 아니라 '엘리트 유명인(The elite celebrity)'입니다. 따라서 ③번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 28. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle.
ordered_passages: (A) Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener.

(B) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them.

(C) A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 도로를 자전거와 보행자에게 할당한다는 내용 뒤에, (B)에서 이것(This)이 자전거 이용을 독려한다는 내용이 이어집니다. 그 후 (A)에서 '그럼에도 불구하고(Nevertheless)' 배달 차량 등을 위한 차선이 필요함을 언급하며 배달 차량의 중요성을 화두로 던집니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 왜 배달 차량이 효율적이고 도시를 친환경적으로 만드는지에 대한 구체적인 이유를 설명하는 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
options: ① Why the Vibrations of My Bones Make My Voice Higher
② Is That Really My Accent? The Voice Recording Mystery
③ The Pronounced Accent and Higher Pitch of My Own Voice
④ How We Hear Our Own Voice: The Science Behind the Surprise
⑤ The Reason Your Voice Sounds Same: Understanding the Two Paths of Sound
questions.explanation: 이 글은 왜 자신의 녹음된 목소리가 평소 듣던 것과 다르게 들리는지를 과학적으로 설명하고 있습니다. 공기를 통한 외부 경로와 뼈를 통한 내부 경로라는 두 가지 경로를 통해 소리를 듣기 때문에 차이가 발생한다는 것이 핵심이므로, ④번 '우리가 자신의 목소리를 듣는 법: 놀라움 뒤에 숨겨진 과학'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.

④ 우리가 자신의 목소리를 듣는 법: 놀라움 뒤에 숨겨진 과학

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 36번]
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by __________________________.*babble: 옹알이하다
questions.explanation: 본문은 거울 뉴런의 발견을 통해 관찰을 통한 학습(learning by observation)과 모방(imitation)의 중요성을 설명하고 있습니다. 갓난아기의 혀 내밀기 모방, 부모의 소리 흉내, 도구 사용 모방 등을 예로 들며 현대 문화가 가능한 이유도 우리가 타고난 행동이나 시행착오에만 국한되지 않고 타인을 관찰하고 따라 함으로써 배울 수 있기 때문이라고 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '타인을 모방함으로써'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 타인을 모방함으로써
② 지속적인 반복
③ 개인적인 발견
④ 동료와의 상호작용
⑤ 직접적이고 간접적인 경험

questions.question: 31. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 31번]
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is ______________. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous Nongreat composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 오해를 받았던 이유는 그들의 음악적 형식이나 아이디어가 완전히 새로웠기 때문입니다. 즉, 대중들이 그런 새로운 음악을 접해본 적이 없었기 때문(낯섦)입니다. 빈칸의 내용은 초기 수용 부족의 원인을 설명해야 하며, 뒤이어 나오는 '완전히 새로웠다(completely new)'와 대조되는 개념이자 Salieri의 '독창성 없음(not original)'과 연결되는 맥락에서 '경험해본 적 없음/익숙하지 않음'의 의미가 필요합니다. 하지만 주어진 선택지 중 'inexperience'는 청중 입장에서의 '미숙함/경험 없음'을 나타내어 적절합니다. (참고: 원문 문맥상 'unfamiliarity'가 더 자연스러우나 주어진 보기 중 논리적으로 통하는 것은 ④입니다.)
options_translation: ① 친밀함
② 단순함
③ 친숙함
④ 미숙함(경험 없음)
⑤ 이해 가능성

questions.question: 32. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds ①<u>more</u> dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will ②<u>drop</u>. This is a worrisome and potentially ③<u>damaging</u> consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been ④<u>reducing</u> for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding ⑤<u>fall</u> in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.*dissolved: 용해된 **anoxic: 산소 결핍의
questions.explanation: 지문은 수온 상승에 따라 용존 산소량이 감소하고 있으며, 이 감소 속도가 수온의 변화 속도보다 더 빠르다는 점을 지적하고 있습니다. ⑤가 포함된 문장은 산소 수준의 하락이 수온의 '상승(rise)'에 대응하는 것보다 더 빠르게 일어나고 있다는 맥락이어야 합니다. 지구 온난화로 인해 수온은 상승하고 있으므로 fall을 rise로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]

"Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are ⓐ<u>similar</u> in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways. But they arose independently in evolution and have ⓑ<u>something</u> in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some ⓒ<u>common</u> structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all ⓓ<u>modifications</u> of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share ⓔ<u>nonfunctional</u> traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 it has buried in it a message가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast: that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① A new medium often reveals what's hidden beneath the surface.
② Whether people accept a new message or not depends on how it is presented.
③ The medium itself inherently affects our worldview, not just delivering content.
④ People perceive the world through the lenses shaped by their own experiences.
