questions.explanation: (A)와 (B)에서 소셜 미디어 유명인들이 전통적인 엘리트 유명인의 재능이 부족하다는 비판을 받는다는 내용을 설명합니다. 제시된 문장은 'However'로 시작하며 그 비판이 '평범한 유명인'이라는 현상이 명성의 의미를 재구성한다는 점을 간과하고 있다고 전환합니다. (C)부터는 엘리트 유명인의 특징과 대조되는 평범한 유명인의 특징(상호작용, 수치화된 명성)을 설명하기 시작하므로 (C)가 정답입니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year ⓐFrom a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. ⓑWhales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." ⓒAs the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere increases, the atmosphere and oceans warm and sea levels rise, indicating that global warming is clearly progressing. ⓓIn 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. ⓔThey called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 고래가 대기 중의 탄소를 격리하고 해양 생태계를 활성화함으로써 기후 변화 완화에 기여하는 경제적, 환경적 가치를 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ③번(ⓒ) 문장은 온실가스 증가로 인한 지구 온난화의 일반적인 현상(해수면 상승 등)에 대해 언급하고 있어, 고래의 역할에 집중하고 있는 전체적인 글의 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오. (답은 본문에 있는 표현 및 단어를 사용하되 질문에 맞게 수정할 것)Q. Why does your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than to other people? A: Your voice sounds deeper and richer to yourself because (A)___________ through (B)___________ ___________ emphasize (C)___________ frequencies, which aren't as pronounced when (D)___________ hear your voice.
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.*vocal cords: 성대 **frequency: 주파수
subjective_conditions: 답은 본문에 있는 표현 및 단어를 사용하되 질문에 맞게 수정할 것
questions.explanation: 자신의 목소리가 더 깊고 풍부하게 들리는 이유는 뼈(your bones)를 통한 진동(vibrations)이 낮은(lower) 주파수를 강조하기 때문이며, 이는 다른 사람들(others)이 목소리를 들을 때는 그렇게 두드러지지 않습니다.

questions.question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year ⓐFrom a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. ⓑWhales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." ⓒAs the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere increases, the atmosphere and oceans warm and sea levels rise, indicating that global warming is clearly progressing. ⓓIn 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. ⓔThey called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.*sequester: 격리하다**phytoplankton: 식물성 플랑크톤
questions.explanation: 이 글은 고래가 탄소 격리에 있어 매우 효율적인 역할을 하며 기후 변화 해결을 위한 중요한 수단임을 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ③번 문장은 온실가스 농도 증가에 따른 일반적인 지구 온난화 현상(대기와 해양의 온난화, 해수면 상승)을 언급하고 있어, 고래의 생태적 가치와 복원을 통한 기후 변화 대응이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, cafeteria food is a serious ⓐ<u>turn-off</u> to college students, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to ⓑ<u>bring down</u> their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons ⓒ<u>boost</u> their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment ⓓ<u>enhances</u> the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of ⓔ<u>switching off</u> a front door light to see the fireflies.
questions.explanation: 변하지 않는 환경에 대한 지루함은 새로운 자극이 더 눈에 띄게 하기 위해 신경 자극의 수준을 '낮추는(lowers/decreases)' 역할을 합니다. 그래야 새로운 자극이 상대적으로 더 강하게 느껴지기 때문입니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 enhances(강화하다)는 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varietyes were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
questions.summary_sentence: The shift to super-productive crops after World War Ⅱ greatly increased food production but (A)__________ crop diversity, leaving the global food system more (B)__________ to diseases, pests, and climate extremes.
questions.explanation: 지문은 초다수확 품종으로의 전환이 식량 생산을 늘렸으나 작물의 다양성을 줄였고(reduced), 이로 인해 식량 시스템이 질병이나 기후 위기에 더 취약해졌다(vulnerable)는 내용을 담고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 촉진했다 - 저항력이 있는
② 감소시켰다 - 면역력이 있는
③ 줄였다 - 취약한
④ 강화했다 - 민감한
⑤ 극대화했다 - 조정된

questions.question: 17. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and ⓐ<u>relating</u> them to culture. Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually ⓑ<u>disconnected</u> to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection. However, these approaches had to be modified to ⓒ<u>explain</u> the differences between genetic and cultural transmission. For example, we do not ⓓ<u>anticipate</u> that cultural transmission strictly follows the rules of genetic transmission. If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily equally likely to ⓔ<u>get</u> the mother's or father's form of that trait. Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers; thus, ___________________________________________.
questions.explanation: 글의 도입부에서 문화 진화의 초기 모델들이 문화와 유전자 사이의 눈에 띄는 연결성을 끌어냈다고 언급하고 있으므로, 문화적 전수 양상과 유전적 과정이 개념적으로 '분리되어(disconnected)' 있다는 표현은 문맥상 어색합니다. 오히려 개념적으로 '유사하다(similar)' 또는 '연결되어 있다(connected)'는 의미의 단어가 와야 뒤에 이어지는 '이러한 접근법이 차이점을 설명하기 위해 수정되어야 했다'는 내용과 논리적으로 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 18. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and ⓐ<u>relating</u> them to culture. Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually ⓑ<u>disconnected</u> to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection. However, these approaches had to be modified to ⓒ<u>explain</u> the differences between genetic and cultural transmission. For example, we do not ⓓ<u>anticipate</u> that cultural transmission strictly follows the rules of genetic transmission. If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily equally likely to ⓔ<u>get</u> the mother's or father's form of that trait. Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers; thus, ___________________________________________.
options: ① The likelihood of acquiring cultural traits is usually from the parental source.
② Genetic rules of inheritance still play the most significant role in the transmission of cultural traits.
③ Cultural traits are only transmitted vertically, from parent to child, and not influenced by other sources.
④ The spread of cultural traits is solely determined by the parent's traits rather than broader societal influences.
⑤ The occurrence of a cultural trait is more than just the chance that an individual's parents possessed that trait.
questions.explanation: 지문은 문화적 전수가 유전적 전수와 달리 부모뿐만 아니라 부모가 아닌 성인이나 또래로부터도 일어날 수 있음을 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '문화적 특성의 발생이 단순히 부모가 그 특성을 가졌을 확률 그 이상의 것(다양한 사회적 경로를 통함)'이라는 결론이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 문화적 특성을 습득할 가능성은 보통 부모라는 원천으로부터 나온다.
② 유전적 상속 법칙은 문화적 특성 전수에서 여전히 가장 중요한 역할을 한다.
③ 문화적 특성은 부모에게서 자녀로 수직적으로만 전달되며 다른 출처의 영향을 받지 않는다.
④ 문화적 특성의 확산은 더 넓은 사회적 영향보다는 전적으로 부모의 특성에 의해 결정된다.
⑤ 문화적 특성의 발생은 단지 개인의 부모가 그 특성을 소유했을 가능성 그 이상이다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. They do well enough in school to keep advancing. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ends with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now lack a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when the journey really begins. Personal growth becomes a voluntary effort after formal education ends. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career are likely to stop progressing as a result.
options: ① Empathy is the ability to understand and share the feelings of others.
② Group study can be a powerful tool, but only if done strategically.
③ It's hard to admit that we've done something wrong or made a mistake.
④ People who expect themselves to be perfect have trouble acknowledging their mistakes and shortcomings.
⑤ Learning never ends; personal growth requires a lifelong, voluntary commitment beyond formal education.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 많은 사람들이 정규 교육(대학)이 끝나면 학습이 끝난다고 생각하지만, 실제로는 정규 교육 이후의 개인적 성장이 자발적인 노력과 헌신(시간, 에너지 투자)을 필요로 하는 진짜 여정의 시작임을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 학습은 결코 끝나지 않으며 평생의 자발적인 노력이 필요하다는 ⑤번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 공감은 타인의 감정을 이해하고 공유하는 능력이다.
② 그룹 스터디는 강력한 도구가 될 수 있지만, 전략적으로 수행될 때만 그러하다.
③ 우리가 잘못을 저질렀거나 실수를 했다는 것을 인정하는 것은 어렵다.
④ 스스로가 완벽하기를 기대하는 사람들은 자신의 실수와 단점을 인정하는 데 어려움을 겪는다.
⑤ 배움은 결코 끝나지 않는다; 개인적 성장은 정규 교육을 넘어 평생의 자발적인 헌신을 필요로 한다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions. But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
options: ① Why Technology Hasn't Boosted Self-Learning
② How Internet Addiction Affects Teens' Brain and Behaviors
③ Communication Breakdown: How Misunderstandings Happen
④ Does Generative Artificial Intelligence Break Copyright Law?
⑤ Internet Access Boosts Intellectual Confidence, Even on Unrelated Topics
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인터넷을 사용하여 정보를 검색한 사람들이 그렇지 않은 사람들에 비해, 검색하지 않은 무관한 주제에 대해서도 자신의 지식 수준을 더 높게 평가(지적 자신감 상승)했다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '인터넷 접속이 무관한 주제에 대해서도 지적 자신감을 높여준다'는 내용의 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 기술이 자기 주도 학습을 증진시키지 못했는가
② 인터넷 중독이 십대의 뇌와 행동에 미치는 영향
③ 의사소통의 붕괴: 오해가 발생하는 방식
④ 생성형 인공지능이 저작권법을 위반하는가?
⑤ 인터넷 접속은 관련 없는 주제에 대해서도 지적 자신감을 고취시킨다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple: the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of clarity. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused or not going to be used in the near future.
questions.summary_sentence: Minimalism is often misunderstood as requiring the (A)__________ of valuable possessions, but it actually promotes emotional (B)__________ by encouraging individuals to let go of unused items while still embracing the conveniences of modern life.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 미니멀리즘은 귀중한 소유물을 희생(sacrifice)하는 것이라는 오해를 받지만, 실제로는 사용하지 않는 물건들을 제거함으로써 명료함(clarity)의 즐거움을 준다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 sacrifice, (B)에는 clarity가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 희생 - 명료함
② 공유 - 무의미함
③ 제거 - 모호함
④ 기억 - 단순함
⑤ 기부 - 복잡함

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: When writing a novel, research for information needs to be done. The thing is ⓐ<u>that</u> some kinds of fiction demand a higher level of detail: crime fiction, for example, or scientific thrillers. The information is never hard ⓑ<u>to find</u>; one website for authors even organizes trips to police stations, so that crime writers can get it right. Often, a polite letter will earn you permission to visit a particular location and record all the details ⓒ<u>that</u> you need. But remember that you will drive your readers to boredom if you think that you need to pack everything ⓓ<u>what</u> you discover into your work. The details that are of consequence ⓔ<u>are</u> those that reveal the human experience. The crucial thing is to tell a story, finding the characters, the tension, and the conflict - not the train timetable or the building blueprint.
questions.explanation: ⓓ의 'what'은 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사인데, 앞에는 선행사인 'everything'이 이미 존재합니다. 선행사가 사물(everything)이고 뒤의 문장이 목적어가 없는 불완전한 문장이므로, 목적격 관계대명사 'that' 또는 'which'를 사용해야 합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
questions.summary_sentence: Plato's realism suggests that the physical world is (A)__________, merely reflecting a hidden and deeper reality composed of perfect Forms or universals. These Forms, such as the idea of a perfect circle, cannot be (B)__________ but exist in an ideal, invisible world beyond human senses.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 플라톤의 실재론에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 플라톤에 따르면 우리가 눈으로 보는 물리적 세계의 사물들(예: 원)은 결함이 있고 변하기 때문에 불완전(incomplete)하며, 이는 단지 보이지 않는 완벽한 '형상(Forms)'의 세계를 반영할 뿐입니다. 이러한 형상들은 인간의 감각 너머에 존재하므로 물리적으로 지각될(perceived) 수 없습니다. 따라서 빈칸 (A)에는 불완전함을 뜻하는 incomplete가, (B)에는 지각됨을 뜻하는 perceived가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 불완전한 ... 지각되는
② 정확한 ... 인식되는
③ 결함 있는 ... 개발되는
④ 결함 있는 ... 오해되는
⑤ 절대적인 ... 이해되는

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The adolescent brain doesn't fully develop until the early twenties, ①<u>which</u> affects how young people process and integrate information for decision-making. (A) This can make it harder for them ②<u>to make</u> well-considered choices, especially in stressful situations. (B) One of the last areas of the brain to mature is the prefrontal cortex, which plays a key role in planning ahead and weighing consequences. (C) In contrast, the limbic system, which governs emotional responses, ③<u>develop</u> earlier and therefore has more influence on decision-making. (D) As a result, choices during adolescence are often ④<u>driven</u> by emotions rather than a clear consideration of the outcomes. (E) This imbalance between the more developed limbic system and the still-maturing prefrontal cortex helps ⑤<u>explain</u> why teenagers are more likely to act impulsively or make poor decisions.
questions.insertion_sentence: It's the brain region that stops you from sending a hasty, angry message, giving you the chance to revise it with more thoughtful words.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문윑의 'It's the brain region'은 바로 앑 문윑 (B)에서 설명한 'prefrontal cortex(전두엽)'을 가리킵니다. (C) 이홄에는 'In contrast'림 통해 감정을 담당하는 변씝계(limbic system)와 대조림 이루기 적에, 전두엽에 대한 부연 설명이 나오는 (C) 윐치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 묑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: The adolescent brain doesn't fully develop until the early twenties, ⓐ<u>which</u> affects how young people process and integrate information for decision-making. (A) This can make it harder for them ⓑ<u>to make</u> well-considered choices, especially in stressful situations. (B) One of the last areas of the brain to mature is the prefrontal cortex, which plays a key role in planning ahead and weighing consequences. (C) In contrast, the limbic system, which governs emotional responses, ⓒ<u>develop</u> earlier and therefore has more influence on decision-making. (D) As a result, choices during adolescence are often ⓓ<u>driven</u> by emotions rather than a clear consideration of the outcomes. (E) This imbalance between the more developed limbic system and the still-maturing prefrontal cortex helps ⓔ<u>explain</u> why teenagers are more likely to act impulsively or make poor decisions.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문윑의 제어는 the limbic system으로 3인칭 단수입니다. 관계대명사절(which governs...) 이홄에 오는 동사 develop는 제어와 수 일치림 시켔 develops로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 -I-에 관한 관의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Dear Hiring Manager, I am excited to apply for the Assistant Manager position at Want Fashion. I am deeply passionate about fashion. I graduated from the Meline School of Fashion. After that, I have worked as a sales assistant at Logan clothing store for the last five years. During that time, I've developed strong customer service and sales skills. I believe that this position presents an exciting opportunity to contribute my expertise. During the last year, I collaborated closely with the general manager and senior executives, leading to a 10% increase in revenue. And I consistently received positive feedback from team members. Thank you for considering my application. I am eager to discuss how my skills in fashion retail and leadership can contribute to Want Fashion's continued growth. I am available for an interview at your earliest convenience. I look forward to hearing from you.Sincerely,Justin Deluca
options: ① After graduating from the Meline School of Fashion, I have worked as a sales assistant.
② I've worked to improve both customer service and sales expertise.
③ During the last year, collaborating closely with the general manager and senior executives, I led to a 10% increase in revenue.
④ I was consistently recognized by team members for my positive impact.
⑤ I have worked for Want Fashion's continued growth.
questions.explanation: 글의 저자(I)는 Want Fashion의 Assistant Manager 직책에 지원하는 상태이며, 과거에 이곳에서 일한 적은 없습니다. 현재 Logan clothing store에서 일해왔으며 Want Fashion의 성장에 기여하고 싶다고 하였으므로, 이미 Want Fashion을 위해 일해왔다는 ⑤번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① Meline 패션 학교림 질업한 홄에, 판매 보조로 일해왔다.
② 고객 서비스와 판매 전문성을 모둀 향상시키기 위해 노력해왔다.
③ 지난 1년 동안 총괄 뫤니저 및 고위 간부들과 밀섑히 협력하여 수익을 10% 증가시킴다.
④ 내가 끼친 긍정적인 영향력에 대해 팀원들로부터 지석적으로 인정받았다.
⑤ 나는 Want Fashion의 지석적인 성장을 위해 일해왔다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Whales are very efficient at carbon storage. (A) For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. (B) Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." (C) In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. (D) They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. (E) People are making calls for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.insertion_sentence: When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 고래가 죽을 때 발생하눤 탄소 흡수 효과를 설명하고 있습니다. (A) 뒤의 문장에서 '비교를 해바으면(For comparison)'이라고 하면서 나무가 흡수하눤 이산화탄소에 대해 언급하므로, 고래의 탄소 흡수량을 수치로 밝힌 제시문은 (A)에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글에서 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, (A)___________, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For instance, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation or avoid it, and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely so that we avoid the threat in the future. Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they (B)___________ evolved with us.
options: ④ when it is triggeredwould not have
⑤ when it triggersshould not have
questions.explanation: (A) 감정 프로그램이 '유발될 때'라는 수동의 의미가 필요하므로 'when it is triggered'가 적절합니다. (B) 마지막 문장은 과거 사실에 반대되는 가정법 과거완료(If S + had p.p, S + would/could... + have p.p) 문장입니다. '만약 그것들이 우리가 적응하고 생존하는 것을 돕지 않았더라면, 그것들은 우리와 함께 진화하지 않았을 것이다'라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 'would not have (evolved)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: 그것이 유발할 때 - 가졌을 것이다
유발되기 전에 - 가질 필요가 없었다
유발된 이후로 - ~였음에 틀림없다
그것이 유발될 때 - 하지 않았을 것이다
그것이 유발할 때 - 하지 말았어야 했다

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Émilie du Châtelet, a French mathematician and physicist, was born in Paris in 1706. During her childhood, with her father's support, she ⓐ<u>was able to get</u> mathematical and scientific education that most women of her time did not receive. In 1737, she submitted her paper on the nature of fire to a contest ⓑ<u>sponsored by</u> the French Academy of Sciences, and it was published ⓒ<u>a year later</u>. In her book, Institutions de Physique, Émilie du Châtelet explained the ideas of space and time in a way ⓓ<u>how</u> is closer to what we understand in modern relativity than what was common during her time. Her most significant achievement was ⓔ<u>translating</u> Isaac Newton's Principia into French near the end of her life. Émilie du Châtelet's work was not recognized in her time, but she is now remembered as a symbol of the Enlightenment and the struggle for women's participation in science.
questions.explanation: ⓓ의 how는 선행사 way와 함께 쓰일 수 없을 뿐만 아니라, 뒤에 주어가 빠진 불완전한 문장(is closer...)이 이어지므로 관계부사가 아닌 주격 관계대명사 which 또는 that으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of (A)__________ any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which doesn't (B)__________ them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, which decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤에는 완전한 문장이 이어지며, '어떻게 조직이 다양한 문화를 가질 수 있는지에 대한 사례'라는 의미가 적절하므로 의문사 how가 들어가는 것이 옳습니다. (B) 문맥상 터널 시야가 생기면 다른 사람들처럼 사물을 보는 것을 '허용하지 않는다'는 의미가 되어야 하는데, 빈칸 앞에 부정어 doesn't가 있으므로 'allow(허용하다)'를 넣어 '허용하지 않는다'는 의미를 완성해야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 어떻게 / 허용하지 않다
② 무엇을 / 허용하지 않다
③ 언제 / 허용하다
④ 어떻게 / 허용하다
⑤ 어느 쪽을 / 허용하지 않다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. (A) The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. (B) Great composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? (C) The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. (D) Now, Salieri wasn't a bad cemposer: in fact, he was a very good one. (E) What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.insertion_sentence: But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 Salieri가 훌륭한 작곡가였음에도 불구하고 '위대한' 작곡가는 아니었던 이유(독창성 부족)를 설명하고 있습니다. (E) 바로 앞 문장(D)에서 그가 나쁜 작곡가가 아니라 매우 좋은 작곡가였다고 언급한 뒤, (E) 자리에 역접의 But으로 시작하는 주어진 문장이 오고, 그 뒤에 독창적이지 않았다는 구체적 설명(그의 음악이 당시 다른 사람들의 것과 똑같이 들렸다)이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an (A)__________ network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets (B)__________ for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.explanation: (A)에는 '광범위한' 네트워크를 의미하는 형용사 extensive가 적절하며, (B)에는 자전거 도로 확대로 인해 거리가 모든 사람들에게 '더 안전해진'다는 의미의 safer가 가장 적절합니다. (참고: 지문 후반부의 맥락과 연결할 때 쾌적함보다는 안전이나 보행 편의성이 강조됨)
options_translation: ① 범위 / 더 넓은
② 광범위한 / 더 깨끗한
③ 집중적인 / 더 깨끗한
④ 집중적인 / 더 새로운
⑤ 광범위한 / 더 안전한

questions.question: 13. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - (A)__________ it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you accept the message of any particular TV show - (A)__________ it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's because Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast: that it's about surfaces and appearances.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 '(A)이든 (B)이든 상관없이'라는 의미의 부사절을 이끄는 접속사가 필요하므로 'whether'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: 그것(관계사/접속사)
어디에
~인지 아닌지(이든 아니든)
무엇
만약

questions.question: 14. 윗글을 요약할 때 괄호 안의 우리말을 영작하시오. (단수, 복수를 정확히 서술하시오.)
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - (A)__________ it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you accept the message of any particular TV show - (A)__________ it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's because Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast: that it's about surfaces and appearances.
questions.summary_sentence: M. McLuhan said that (새로운 미디어는 우리가 세상을 새로운 방식으로 보도록 이끈다.)
subjective_conditions: 단수, 복수를 정확히 서술하시오.
questions.answer: a new medium leads us to see the world in a new way.
questions.explanation: '새로운 미디어는(a new medium)' 주어, '이끈다(leads)' 동사, '우리가(us)' 목적어, '보도록(to see)' 목적격 보어의 5형식 문장 구조를 활용하여 영작합니다.

questions.question: 15. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot <u>우리 부모님이 하는 것을 관찰함으로써</u>. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
options: ① We should discover the mirror neurons.
② We humans can learn by watching others' action.
③ Not everyone has a tendency to stick out their tongue.
④ We should learn only at school.
⑤ Children should be restricted to their behavior.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런의 발견을 통해 인간이 관찰과 모방을 통해 학습하는 능력을 갖추고 있음을 설명하고 있으므로, '우리 인간은 타인의 행동을 관찰함으로써 배울 수 있다'는 내용이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 우리는 거울 뉴런을 발견해야 한다.
우리 인간은 타인의 행동을 관찰함으로써 배울 수 있다.
모든 사람이 혀를 내미는 경향이 있는 것은 아니다.
우리는 오직 학교에서만 배워야 한다.
아이들은 자신의 행동에 제한을 받아야 한다.

questions.question: 16. 윗글에서 밑줄 친 우리말을 영작하시오. [3.0점]
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot <u>우리 부모님이 하는 것을 관찰함으로써</u>. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.answer: by observing what our parents do
questions.explanation: '~함으로써'는 'by -ing' 구조를 사용하며, '우리 부모님이 하는 것'은 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what을 사용하여 'what our parents do'로 표현합니다. 따라서 'by observing what our parents do'가 정답입니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our ⓐ<u>conscious</u> working memory, in an ⓑ<u>active</u> form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the ⓒ<u>same</u> information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts ⓓ<u>appearing</u>, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory ⓔ<u>vanishes</u>. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.explanation: 작업 기억(working memory)은 짧은 시간 동안만 유지되는 정보 저장소입니다. 문맥상 정보를 읽고 난 몇 초나 몇 분 뒤에는 작업 기억에서 정보가 사라지기 시작한다는 내용이 와야 하므로, ⓓappearing(나타나는)을 decaying 또는 fading(사라지는, 희미해지는)과 같은 단어로 바꾸어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말에 맞게 <보기> 중 필요한 단어만을 골라 배열하여 영작하시오. (형태 변형 없음, 단어 중복 사용 가능) [4.0점]
questions.passage: Once upon a time in the Iranian city of Shiraz, there lived the famous poet Sheikh Saadi. Like most other poets and philosophers, he led a very simple life. A rich merchant of Shiraz was preparing for his daughter's wedding and invited him along with a lot of big businessmen of the town. The poet accepted the invitation and decided to attend. On the day of the wedding, the rich merchant, the host of the wedding, was receiving the guests at the gate. Many rich people of the town attended the wedding. They had come out in their best clothes. The poet wore simple clothes which were neither grand nor expensive. He waited for someone to approach him but no one gave him as much as even a second glance. Even the host did not greet him and looked away. Seeing all this, (A)<u>시인은 조용히 파티를 떠나 그가 옷을 빌릴 수 있는 가게로 갔다</u>. There he chose a richly decorated coat, which made him look like a new person. With this coat, he entered the party and this time was welcomed with open arms.
subjective_conditions: 형태 변형 없음
단어 중복 사용 가능
vocabulary_box: poet / clothes / where / the / he / shop
his / left / went / a / could / rent / and
quietly / clothes / to / him / party / when
questions.answer: the poet quietly left the party and went to a shop where he could rent clothes
questions.explanation: 주어 'the poet'가 '조용히(quietly) 파티를 떠나(left the party)' 그리고 '가게로 갔다(and went to a shop)'는 병렬 구조를 이룹니다. '그가 옷을 빌릴 수 있는' 부분은 관계부사 where를 사용하여 'where he could rent clothes'로 앞의 shop을 수식하게 배열합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents ⓐ<u>associated with</u> traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers ⓑ<u>to crossing over</u> to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that phenomena of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with ⓒ<u>naturalizing qualities of talent and class</u>. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is ⓓ<u>nothing more nor less</u> than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks ⓔ<u>built into</u> social media applications.
questions.explanation: ⓒ는 'naturalized(당연한 것으로 여겨지는)'로 고쳐야 합니다. '재능과 계급이라는 타고난 자질'이라는 수동적 의미를 지니는 분사 형태가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, (A)~(D)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. Between 2000 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of (A)__________ of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should (B)__________ the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to (C)__________ higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often (D)__________ students to focus more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
questions.explanation: (A) 고등 교육의 극적인 확장은 고등 교육 '기관(institutions)'의 폭을 넓혔고, (B) 숙련된 인력을 개발하기 위해서는 시험의 역할을 '줄여야(diminish)' 하며, (C) 고등 교육을 '확장(expand)'하려는 사회정치적 변화가 생겼고, (D) 결과적으로 학생들이 피드백보다 성적에 집중하게 '만드는(causing)' 상황을 묘사하고 있습니다. 따라서 정답은 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 기관의, 줄이다, 확장하다, 야기했다
② 기관의, 늘리다, 소비하다, 야기했다
③ 기관의, 늘리다, 소비하다, 야기하면서
④ 기관들, 줄이다, 확장하다, 야기하면서
⑤ 기관들, 줄이다, 소비하다, 야기했다

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are ⓐ<u>vital</u> to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully ⓑ<u>sums up</u> the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched ⓒ<u>fruitlessly</u> for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their ⓓ<u>hypotheses</u>. Firestein gives the example of (A)<u>luminiferous ether</u>, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a ⓔ<u>essence</u> to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
questions.explanation: 빛이 통과하여 이동할 수 있는 통로로서의 '매질(medium)' 개념이 필요한 문맥입니다. 과학자들이 존재하지 않는 본질(essence)을 찾으려 했던 오류를 설명하는 과정에서, 에테르(ether)를 빛의 이동 매질로 생각했음을 언급하고 있으므로 essence는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.
