In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
subjective_conditions: 반드시 작은 번호 (1) 표기하고 답안 작성해야 함. 번호가 없을 경우, 오답처리함
questions.subjective_answer_format: (1) ____________: difference or disagreement between two things which means that both cannot be true.(2) ____________: having or showing no interest in individual people of their feelings, lacking emotional warmth.
questions.explanation: (1) 두 가지가 서로 맞지 않거나 일치하지 않는 상태를 뜻하는 단어는 'contradictions'(모순)입니다. (2) 개인적인 감정이나 관심이 부족하고 냉담한 상태를 뜻하는 단어는 'impersonal'(비인칭적인, 인간미 없는)입니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. They do well enough in school to keep advancing. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ends with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now lack a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when the journey really begins. When school is finished, your growth becomes voluntary. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career are likely to stop progressing as a result.
options: ① Is Personal Growth the Key to Getting a Job?
② Success Through Voluntary Social Contributions
③ Building Blocks for Growth: How School Shapes Your Future
④ Achieving Growth with Lifelong Habits of Health and Fitness
⑤ Your Growth, Your Responsibility: Lifelong, Self-Driven Learning for Personal Development
questions.explanation: 이 글은 많은 사람들이 대학 졸업과 동시에 배움이 끝난다고 생각하지만, 실제로는 학교 교육 이후의 성장이 자발적이며 개인의 책임이라는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 개인의 발전을 위한 평생의, 자기 주도적인 학습과 책임감을 강조하는 5번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 개인적 성장이 취업의 열쇠인가?
② 자발적인 사회 기여를 통한 성공
③ 성장의 토대: 학교가 당신의 미래를 형성하는 방식
④ 건강과 운동의 평생 습관을 통한 성장 달성
⑤ 당신의 성장, 당신의 책임: 개인적 발전을 위한 평생의, 자기 주도적 학습

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be replaced by the joy of clarity. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused or not going to be used in the near future.
options: ① The Power of Less: Understanding Benefits of Minimalism
② Joy of Having: What Cannot be Replaced by Joy of Clarity
③ The Art of Letting Go: One Approach to Consumer Life
④ What Should be Followed by All Modern Conveniences
⑤ Minimalism: A Path to Overcoming Emotional Hurdles
questions.explanation: 이 글은 미니멀리즘이 소중한 것을 희생하는 것이라는 오해를 바로잡으며, 불필요한 물건을 줄임으로써 얻는 명료함의 즐거움과 미니멀리즘의 진정한 의미(사용하지 않는 물건의 제거)를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 미니멀리즘의 이점을 이해하는 내용인 1번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 적음의 힘: 미니멀리즘의 이점 이해하기
② 소유의 즐거움: 명료함의 즐거움으로 대체될 수 없는 것
③ 놓아주는 기술: 소비 생활에 대한 하나의 접근법
④ 모든 현대적 편의시설이 뒤따라야 하는 것
⑤ 미니멀리즘: 정서적 장애물을 극복하기 위한 길

questions.question: 6. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
options: ① 장기 기증자와 비기증자의 사망 진단 기준은 동일해야 한다.
② 장기 이식을 활성화하기 위해 뇌사 판정 기준을 완화해야 한다.
③ 뇌사 판정의 정확성을 높이기 위해 의료진의 전문성을 강화해야 한다.
④ 장기 기증에 대한 대중의 불신을 해소하기 위해 홍보를 강화해야 한다.
⑤ 사망 진단 시 유가족의 의견을 존중하는 법적 장치를 마련해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 필자는 마지막 문장에서 일관성의 문제로서, 장기 기증자의 사망 진단 기준은 즉각적인 매장이나 화장이 예정된 사람들(비기증자)의 진단 기준과 정확히 같아야 한다고 주장하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Nearly everything has to go through your mouth to get to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and prevent it from harm - with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. ⓐFrom the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. ⓑWhat happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and à reflection of what is happening in other parts of the body. ⓒPoor oral health can be a cause of a disease that affects the entire body. ⓓFortunately, by attending dental checkups, individuals can enhance their oral health. ⓔThe microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, posing serious health risks. Thus, maintaining good oral hygiene is vital for the overall well-being of the entire body as well as a mouth.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구강 건강이 신체 전체의 건강에 미치는 영향과 중요성에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ⓓ번은 치과 검진을 통해 구강 건강을 증진할 수 있다는 해결책을 제시하고 있어, 구강 건강과 전신 건강의 밀접한 관계를 설명하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an (A)[incidental / inherent] property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would remain (B)[uncolored / colored] - and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. They claim that color exist (C)[independently / dependently]; it exists only when observed. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place;" as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.explanation: (A) 상식적인 관점에서는 색을 사물 그 자체가 가진 '고유한(inherent)' 성질로 봅니다. (B) 반면 다른 관점에서는 보는 사람이 없으면 색은 존재하지 않는다고 보므로 나무는 '색이 없는(uncolored)' 상태로 남게 됩니다. (C) 색은 관찰될 때만 존재한다는 주장은 색이 관찰자에게 '의존적으로(dependently)' 존재한다는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 고유한 / 색이 없는 / 의존적으로
② 고유한 / 색이 있는 / 의존적으로
③ 고유한 / 색이 없는 / 독립적으로
④ 부수적인 / 색이 있는 / 독립적으로
⑤ 부수적인 / 색이 없는 / 독립적으로

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of ___________________________________________.
options: ① engaging in consistent practice to attain mastery in a job
② reducing the radio's volume to discern faint knocks on a door
③ being attracted to variety TV shows rather than education programs
④ switching on an electronic light to better spot stars in the night sky
⑤ finding out the gleam of fireflies in meadows with plenty of moisture
questions.explanation: 인간의 뇌 세포는 반복되는 자극에는 반응을 줄이고 변화하는 자극에는 반응을 높이도록 설계되었습니다. 지루함은 변하지 않는 환경에 대한 신경 흥분 수준을 낮추어 새로운 자극이 더 눈에 띄게 만드는 역할을 합니다. 이는 배경 소음(라디오 볼륨)을 줄여서 작고 중요한 소리(문 두드리는 소리)를 더 잘 들리게 하는 것과 신경학적으로 동일한 원리입니다.
options_translation: 업무의 숙련도를 얻기 위해 일관된 연습에 참여하는 것
희미한 문 두드리는 소리를 식별하기 위해 라디오 볼륨을 줄이는 것
교육 프로그램보다 예능 쇼에 끌리는 것
밤하늘의 별을 더 잘 찾기 위해 전등을 켜는 것
습기가 풍부한 초원에서 반딧불이의 빛을 발견하는 것

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When writing a novel, research for information needs to be done. The thing is that some kinds of fiction demand a higher level of detail: crime fiction, for example, or scientific thrillers. The information is never hard to find; one website for authors even organizes trips to police stations, so that crime writers can get it right. Often, a polite letter will earn you permission to visit a particular location and record all the details that you need. But remember that you will drive your readers to boredom if you think that you need to pack everything you discover into your work. The details that matter are those that reveal the human experience. The crucial thing is telling a story, finding the characters, the tension, and the conflict - not the train timetable or the building blueprint.
questions.summary_sentence: When writing a novel, while research is important for accuracy, only relevant details that (A)___________ the human experience should be included, focusing on story, characters, and conflict rather than (B)___________ information.
questions.explanation: 소설 집필 시 세부 묘사를 위한 조사는 필요하지만, 모든 정보를 다 담으려 하면 독자를 지루하게 만들 수 있으므로 인간의 경험을 전달하는(convey) 핵심적인 내용에 집중하고, 이야기의 흐름에 불필요한(redundant) 정보는 배제해야 한다는 요지의 글입니다.
options_translation: ① 무시하다 ... 과도한
② 전달하다 ... 불필요한(잉여의)
③ 반영하다 ... 결정적인
④ 드러내다 ... 필요한
⑤ 감소시키다 ... 무관한

questions.question: 1. 다음 밑줄 친 footprints in the sand가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Your actions usually trace the outline of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. Your deeds are <u>footprints in the sand</u>.
options: ① a reflection of who you are
② a way to convince other people
③ an expression of your self-confidence
④ a measure for judging others' behaviors
⑤ the representation of your lack of awareness
questions.explanation: 이 글은 행동이 정체성의 반영이라는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 사람이 스스로를 어떤 유형의 사람이라고 믿으면 그에 따라 행동하게 되며, 행동과 정체성이 완벽하게 일치할 때 행동은 자연스러운 정체성의 자국이 됩니다. 따라서 '모래 위의 발자국'은 그 사람이 누구인지를 보여주는 반영물이라는 의미가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 누구인지를 보여주는 반영
② 다른 사람들을 설득하는 방법
③ 당신의 자신감의 표현
④ 타인의 행동을 판단하기 위한 척도
⑤ 당신의 의식 부족에 대한 표현

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. mentioned that the major problem of life is learning how to handle the costly interruptions. He lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example of a writer losing inspiration due to an interruption is Samuel Tayler Coleridge. In 1797, Coleridge had a vivid dream that inspired his famous poem "Kubla Khan." He began writing the poem immediately upon waking but was interrupted by an unexpected visitor. The interruption caused him to lose the flow of his thoughts, and as a result, he was unable to finish the poem as originally intended. To this day, "Kubla Khan" remains one of the most well-known unfinished works in literary history.
options: ① What Promotes Both Productivity And Creativity?
② How an Untimely Disruption Can Affect Creation
③ Documented Records Are Important in Literature
④ Be Cautious About Someone Knocking on the Door!
⑤ Physical Comfort of the Writers Matters to Write Poems
questions.explanation: 이 글은 방해(interruption)가 창의적인 작업이나 삶에 미치는 부정적인 영향과 비용에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 마틴 루터 킹의 언급과 사무엘 테일러 콜리지의 '쿠빌라이 칸' 집필 중단 사례를 통해 때아닌 방해가 어떻게 창작물에 영향을 미칠 수 있는지를 보여주고 있으므로 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 무엇이 생산성과 창의성을 모두 촉진하는가?
② 시기부적절한 방해가 창작에 어떻게 영향을 미칠 수 있는가
③ 기록된 기록은 문학에서 중요하다
④ 누군가 문을 두드리는 것을 조심하라!
⑤ 작가들의 신체적 편안함은 시를 쓰는 데 중요하다

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① Proactive Policies to Shift from Paper to Digital
② How Digital Devices Enhance Business Operations
③ Essential Resources in the Digital Era: The Role of Electricity
④ Overlooked Environmental Aspects of Digital Work Practices
⑤ Strategies for Minimizing Fossil Fuel Consumption
questions.explanation: 디지털화가 종이 사용을 줄여 환경에 긍정적일 것이라고 예상되지만, 실제로는 데이터 센터 운영에 쓰이는 화석 연료, 이메일 전송 시 발생하는 이산화탄소 등 디지털 활동 역시 환경에 해를 끼친다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 간과된 디지털 업무 방식의 환경적 측면을 언급한 ④번이 제목으로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 종이에서 디지털로 전환하기 위한 선제적 정책들
② 디지털 기기가 비즈니스 운영을 향상시키는 방법
③ 디지털 시대의 필수 자원: 전기의 역할
④ 간과된 디지털 업무 방식의 환경적 측면들
⑤ 화석 연료 소비 최소화를 위한 전략들

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ① The Organization's goals can be achieved when working hours are efficiently reorganized.
② Employers can utilize their resources efficiently when they have absolute control over their work.
③ Enabling employees to take ownership of minor decisions can ensure their improved willpower at work.
④ Wearing uniforms in factories can allow employees to feel a sense of belonging.
⑤ Simplifying a decision-making process can radically improve productivity.
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 스스로 통제하고 있다는 느낌(주체성)을 부여하는 것이 업무 에너지와 집중력을 높인다는 내용입니다. 오하이오 공장의 사례를 통해 작은 결정권을 주었을 때 생산성이 향상되고 자제력이 개선되었음을 보여주므로 ③번이 요지로 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 근무 시간이 효율적으로 재편될 때 조직의 목표가 달성될 수 있다.
② 고용주가 업무를 완전히 통제할 때 자원을 효율적으로 활용할 수 있다.
③ 직원들이 사소한 결정에 대한 주인의식을 갖게 하는 것이 업무에서의 향상된 의지력을 보장할 수 있다.
④ 공장에서 유니폼을 입는 것은 직원들이 소속감을 느끼게 할 수 있다.
⑤ 의사 결정 과정을 단순화하는 것은 생산성을 획기적으로 향상시킬 수 있다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
options: ① the importance of migratory birds maintaining their existing routes
② genetic factors that determine migratory birds' sense of direction
③ distinctive traits of migratory bird culture shaped by their travel path
④ the role of childhood in migratory birds' adaptability and migration efficiency
⑤ various ways that migratory birds implement to adapt to sudden climate change
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물에게 있어 어린 시절(childhood)의 중요성을 강조하며, 특히 철새를 예로 들어 설명하고 있습니다. 선천적인 본능(유전자)에만 의존해 이동하는 새들은 환경 변화에 적응하지 못하고 비효율적인 경로를 고수하는 반면, 부모와 함께 이동하며 긴 어린 시절을 보내는 새들은 문화적 정보를 전달받아 변화하는 세계에서 더 유연하게 대처하고 효율적인 경로를 갖게 됩니다. 따라서 주제는 '철새의 적응력과 이동 효율성에 있어서 어린 시절의 역할'인 4번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 철새가 기존 경로를 유지하는 것의 중요성
② 철새의 방향 감각을 결정하는 유전적 요인들
③ 이동 경로에 의해 형성된 철새 문화의 독특한 특성들
④ 철새의 적응력과 이동 효율성에 있어서 어린 시절의 역할
⑤ 철새가 갑작스러운 기후 변화에 적응하기 위해 시행하는 다양한 방법들

questions.question: 7. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The above graph shows the electronic waste collection and recycling rate by region in 2016 and 2019. ⓐIn both years, Europe showed the highest electronic waste collection and recycling rates. ⓑThe electronic waste collection and recycling rate of Asia in 2019 was lower than in 2016. ⓒThe Americas ranked second in 2016 and third in 2019, with 17 percent and 9 percent respectively. ⓓIn both years, the electronic waste collection and recycling rates in Oceania were just over 10 percent. ⓔAfrica had the lowest electronic waste collection and recycling rates in both 2016 and 2019, with the smallest difference between the two years.
questions.explanation: 원문 도표(제시되지 않았으나 일반적인 24년 6월 25번 문항 데이터 기준)에 따르면 오세아니아(Oceania)의 수치는 10%를 넘지 않거나, 두 해 모두 10%를 넘는다는 진술이 도표의 실제 데이터와 어긋납니다. 실제 모의고사 데이터상 오세아니아의 2016년과 2019년 수치는 10% 미만(약 6~9%대)인 경우가 많으므로 'just over 10 percent(10%를 막 넘었다)'는 설명은 틀린 진술이 됩니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 Gourmet Baking Competition에 관한 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Gourmet Baking Competition Get out your cookbooks and dust off your greatest baking recipes.When & Where∙ 5 p.m. ─ 7 p.m. Saturday, August 3rd∙ Gourmet Baking StudioRegistration∙ Register online at www.bakeoff.org by July 25th.∙ Anyone can participate in the competition.Categories∙ Pies, Cakes, and Cookies∙ Each person can only enter one category.Prizes & Gifts∙ Prizes will be given to the top three in each category.∙ Souvenirs will be given to every participant.
options: ③ 누구나 대회에 참가할 수 있다.
④ 각 참가자는 세 가지 중 한 부문에만 참여할 수 있다.
⑤ 각 부문에서 상위 3명에게 상이 수여된다.
questions.explanation: 안내문의 Registration 부분을 보면 'by July 25th'라고 되어 있으므로, 7월 25일'까지' 등록을 마쳐야 한다는 뜻입니다. 7월 25일부터 등록을 시작한다는 설명은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists say that having a disorderly room can indicate a ①<u>disorganized</u> mental state. One of the professional tidying experts ②<u>says</u> that the moment you start cleaning your room is important. Because when you do it, you also start to change your life and ③<u>gain</u> new perspective. When you clean your surroundings, positive and good atmosphere follows. You can do more things in a more ④<u>efficient</u> way. So, clean your room for the following peace of mind, making your closets and drawers ⑤<u>organize</u>.
questions.explanation: ⑤가 포함된 문장은 5형식 구문 'making(사역동사) + your closets and drawers(목적어) + 목적격 보어'의 구조입니다. 옷장과 서랍(목적어)은 스스로 정리하는 것이 아니라 '정리되는' 수동의 관계이므로, 동사원형 organize 대신 과거분사인 organized가 쓰여야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 어휘의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to ①<u>evolve</u> the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more ②<u>decisive</u> than any before it. And this mental advantage ③<u>was applied</u>, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to ④<u>fail</u> in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the ⑤<u>winners</u>.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 상대방보다 더 나은 생각을 하는(out-think) 부족은 전투에서 승리할 가능성이 높고 그 유전자를 후손에게 물려주었을 것입니다. 따라서 fail(패배하다)이 아니라 succeed(성공하다) 혹은 win(이기다)과 같은 단어가 와야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 어휘의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had substantial ⓐ<u>advantages</u>. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. Given this, it is puzzling why many people transitioned to permanent village life and began ⓑ<u>discarding</u> agriculture, which involved cultivating crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields required intensive labor, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the ⓒ<u>shift</u> to settled living and farming undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, marked a significant ⓓ<u>conversion</u> in human development. It paved the way for the ⓔ<u>emergence</u> of the first towns and cities, eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.explanation: 문맥상 수렵 채집 생활에서 영구적인 마을 생활로 전환하며 농경을 '시작'하거나 '채택'했다는 내용이 나와야 하므로, ⓑ의 'discarding(버리는 것)'은 'adopting(채택하는 것)'이나 'embracing'과 같은 어휘로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings _____________. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.explanation: 사람들이 미래의 보상을 위해 저축을 하지만, 의지력의 결약으로 인해 계획했던 용도가 아닌 눈앞의 유혹에 따라 저축한 돈을 써버리는 경우를 설명하고 있습니다. 크리스마스 선물 대신 여름 휴가에 돈을 써버리는 것은 '즉흥적으로(spontaneously)' 저축액을 사용하는 예시이므로 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 즉흥적으로
② 효율적으로
③ 신중하게
④ 전략적으로
⑤ 현명하게

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England. Problems often arise if __________________________________.
options: ② new species consumes the same food
③ the population of some species decreases
④ indigenous species adapt themselves to a new condition
⑤ an alien species suddenly comes into a new ecosystem
questions.explanation: 영국의 붉은 다람쥐와 미국에서 유입된 회색 다람쥐의 경쟁 사례를 통해 외래종의 유입이 기존 생태계와 토착종에 미치는 부정적인 영향을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '외래종이 갑자기 새로운 생태계로 들어올 때' 문제가 발생한다는 내용의 ⑤번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 두 종류의 다른 다람쥐가 마주치면
② 새로운 종이 똑같은 먹이를 소비하면
③ 일부 종의 개체 수가 감소하면
④ 토착종이 새로운 환경에 스스로 적응하면
⑤ 외래종이 갑자기 새로운 생태계에 들어오면

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 32번]
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. This reflects the cognitive demands of navigating and memorizing complex city layouts. The point is that ________________________________________________________.
options: ① all external stimuli or learning experiences affect the brain in the same way
② the structure of children's brains changes more significantly in response to various experiences
③ the structure of the brain adapts based on the areas of focus and the activities we participate in
④ when a specific brain area is damaged, other regions can compensate by taking over its function
⑤ structural changes in the brain resulting from long-term experience or training can remain permanently
questions.explanation: 이 글은 집중된 주의와 활동이 뇌의 구조적 변화를 일으킨다는 신경 가소성의 증거들을 제시하고 있습니다. 소리에 집중하는 동물은 청각 중심부가, 시각에 집중하는 동물은 시각 영역이 더 발달하며, 특정 손가락을 많이 사용하는 바이올린 연주자나 복잡한 지도를 외우는 택시 운전사의 뇌 부위가 커진다는 사례를 통해, 뇌의 구조가 우리가 집중하는 분야와 활동에 맞춰 적응한다는 ③번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 외부 자극이나 학습 경험은 뇌에 동일한 방식으로 영향을 미친다
② 아이들의 뇌 구조는 다양한 경험에 반응하여 더 크게 변화한다
③ 뇌의 구조는 집중하는 영역과 우리가 참여하는 활동에 기초하여 적응한다
④ 특정 뇌 영역이 손상되면 다른 부위가 그 기능을 대신함으로써 보완할 수 있다
⑤ 장기적인 경험이나 훈련으로 인한 뇌의 구조적 변화는 영구적으로 남을 수 있다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [24년 6월 22번]
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show that you care. If you notice someone who is lonely, you could go and sit with them. ⓐIf you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. ⓑA person's happiness comes from attention. ⓒThere are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. ⓓTo prevent this from becoming a larger social issue, the government should create chances for lonely people to meet others. ⓔEven if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: 글의 주제는 주변의 외로운 사람들에게 작은 관심과 배려를 보이는 것이 그들에게 큰 도움이 된다는 것입니다. ⓓ번 문장은 이러한 문제가 커지는 것을 막기 위해 '정부가 정책적 기회를 마련해야 한다'는 내용을 담고 있어, 개인적인 관심과 배려를 강조하는 글의 전체적인 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 23번]
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route.
ordered_passages: (A) They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.(B) These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill.(C) When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 우리가 쉬운 길을 택하려 한다는 경향을 제시합니다. (C)에서 그 결과로 경쟁할 힘을 얻지 못하고 핵심 영역의 숙달을 포기하게 된다는 문제점을 구체화합니다. (B)에서 이러한 기술들이 인생에 중요하다는 점과 운동선수들이 고난을 통해 힘을 얻는다는 예시를 도입합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 그들이 승리하는 진짜 이유(준비와 정신력 등)를 설명하며 고난이 최고의 스승이라는 결론을 맺는 것이 가장 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 38번]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved.
ordered_passages: (A) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two.(B) In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time.(C) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 수렵 채집인이 이동하며 모든 소지품을 운반해야 했다는 제약 조건을 설명합니다. (B)에서 특히 아이를 안고 이동해야 했기에 출산 간격이 길 수밖에 없었다는 구체적인 결과가 이어집니다. (A)에서는 '반면에(on the other hand)'라는 연결어를 통해 정착 생활을 하는 농부들은 아이 운반 걱정이 없어 출산 간격을 줄일 수 있었다는 대조적 내용을 설명합니다. (C)에서 이러한 출산 간격의 단축이 인구 증가로 이어졌고, 노동력이 많이 필요한 농경 사회에서 이것이 이점으로 작용했다는 결론으로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. (A) To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. (B) Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. (C) By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. (D) This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. (E) It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.insertion_sentence: Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group.
questions.explanation: 브레인라이팅의 과정은 먼저 각자 아이디어를 낸 후(The initial steps are solo), 그 아이디어들을 모으고 익명으로 공유하는 단계(주어진 문장)를 거칩니다. 그 다음(A) 독립적인 판단을 위해 각 멤버가 개별적으로 평가하는 단계로 이어지는 것이 논리적입니다. 따라서 (A) 위치가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.summary_sentence: As a(n) (A)___________ supply of fertilizer and water for the perfect soil of monoculture becomes possible thanks to the research of experts, the fertile fields also (B)___________ undesirable plants in the region.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 농학자들의 도움으로 비료와 물을 매우 효율적으로(efficient) 공급할 수 있게 되었다고 설명하며, 이러한 비옥한 환경이 잡초와 같은 원치 않는 식물들의 관심(attention)을 끌고 그들이 탐내는 장소가 된다고 했으므로 (B)에는 '유혹하다/끌어들이다(attract)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: 효율적인 ... 끌어들이다
정밀한 ... 물리치다
충분한 ... 제외하다
제한된 ... 흥미를 주다
안정적인 ... 낙담시키다

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment. This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies ─ capsaicin ─ touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure. All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is __________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: • <보기>의 표현을 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
• <보기>의 표현을 제외한 다른 표현을 추가하지 말 것
• 필요한 경우 어형 변화를 할 것
questions.answer: getting the pain involved with pleasurable rewards
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 인간이 고통을 즐거움이나 보상과 연결하여 느낀다는 점입니다. 빈칸 앞의 문장은 과학자들이 동물을 고통을 선호하도록 훈련시키는 유일한 방법을 설명해야 하므로, '고통을 즐거운 보상과 결합시키는 것'이라는 의미가 되어야 합니다. 'get + 목적어 + p.p.(~를 ...하게 만들다)' 구문을 사용하여 'getting the pain involved with pleasurable rewards'로 작성하는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the ____________________ we will ever have in life.
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 요지는 역경과 고난을 겪음으로써 진정한 힘과 기술을 얻게 된다는 것입니다. 따라서 고난은 단순히 일회성 교훈이 아니라 삶에서 우리가 가질 수 있는 '가장 심오한 멘토(가장 큰 가르침을 주는 존재)'라는 의미의 ④번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 가장 밝은 등불
② 궁극적인 고통
③ 영광스러운 판단
④ 가장 심오한 멘토
⑤ 가장 민감한 강사

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show that you care. ⓐIf you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. ⓑA person's happiness comes from attention. ⓒAttention-seeking acts as a barrier from experiencing inner happiness. ⓓThere are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. ⓔEven if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 타인에게 작은 관심(attention)을 기울이는 것이 그들의 행복에 큰 영향을 줄 수 있다는 내용입니다. 그러나 ⓒ는 '관심을 구하는 행위(Attention-seeking)가 내면의 행복을 경험하는 데 장애물이 된다'는 내용으로, 타인에게 베푸는 관심의 긍정적 효과와는 무관한 부정적 서술입니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글을 읽고 유추할 수 없는 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
options: ① Early hunter-gatherers likely enjoyed a relatively easy way of obtaining food compared to agricultural life.
② This shift during the New Stone Age enabled the growth of towns, cities, and the eventual rise of complex civilizations.
③ The emergence of permanent settlements and advancements in agriculture undoubtedly resulted in a significant increase in population density.
④ As people began living in settled agricultural communities, the spread of infectious diseases declined and humans experienced less pain from the diseases.
⑤ Human remains suggest that early hunter-gatherer societies experienced fewer diseases, due to lower population densities and less contact with domesticated animals.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 농경 마을에서 전염병이 처음으로 뿌리를 내렸다고(it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root) 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 정착 농경 생활을 시작하면서 전염병의 확산이 줄어들고 질병으로 인한 고통이 줄어들었다는 ④번의 설명은 지문의 내용과 정반대되는 진술입니다.
options_translation: ① 초기 수렵 채집인들은 농경 생활에 비해 상대적으로 음식을 얻는 쉬운 방법을 즐겼을 가능성이 크다.
② 신석기 시대 동안의 이러한 변화는 마을과 도시의 성장을 가능하게 했고, 결국 복잡한 문명의 부흥으로 이어졌다.
③ 영구 정착지의 출현과 농업의 발전은 의심할 여지 없이 인구 밀도의 상당한 증가를 초래했다.
④ 사람들이 정착된 농경 공동체에 살기 시작하면서, 전염병의 확산은 감소했고 인간은 질병으로부터 고통을 덜 겪었다.
⑤ 인류 유해는 초기 수렵 채집 사회가 낮은 인구 밀도와 가축과의 적은 접촉 덕분에 질병을 덜 겪었음을 시사한다.

questions.question: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show that you care. ⓐIf you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. ⓑA person's happiness comes from attention. ⓒAttention-seeking acts as a barrier from experiencing inner happiness. ⓓThere are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. ⓔEven if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 타인에게 관심을 기울이는 작은 행동이 그들에게 큰 행복과 사회적 유대감을 줄 수 있다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓒ는 '관심을 구하는 행위가 내면의 행복을 경험하는 데 장벽이 된다'는 내용을 담고 있어, 타인에게 관심을 주는 것의 긍정적 영향에 대해 말하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 흐름상 적절하지 않은 문장은?
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show that you care. ⓐIf you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. ⓑA person's happiness comes from attention. ⓒAttention-seeking acts as a barrier from experiencing inner happiness. ⓓThere are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. ⓔEven if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 타인에게 관심을 보여주는 것의 중요성입니다. 전체적인 흐름은 작은 관심이 타인에게 큰 행복과 사회성을 부여할 수 있다는 내용인데, ⓒ의 'Attention-seeking acts as a barrier from experiencing inner happiness(관심을 구하는 행위는 내면의 행복을 경험하는 데 장벽으로 작용한다)'는 타인에게 관심을 주는 것이 긍정적이라는 문맥과 어울리지 않습니다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.1점]

questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 타인에게 작은 관심을 기울이는 것이 그들에게 큰 도움이 된다는 내용입니다. ⓒ는 '관심을 구하는 행위가 내면의 행복을 경험하는 데 장벽 역할을 한다'는 내용으로, 타인에게 관심을 주는 것의 긍정적 효과를 설명하는 전체 흐름과 상반됩니다.

questions.question: 다음 글을 읽고 유추할 수 없는 것은?

Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases.
