questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less ⓐ<u>flexible</u>. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with ⓑ<u>instinctual</u> they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate ⓒ<u>keep</u> flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve ⓓ<u>faster</u> than genes. Childhood ⓔ<u>prevents</u> them from being flexible in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 어린 시절을 보내는 것은 동물이 환경에 대해 배우고 유연해지도록 돕는 역할을 한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 어린 시절이 유연해지는 것을 '막는다(prevents)'는 표현은 글의 전체 흐름과 반대되므로 'allows'나 'enables'와 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① 일부 비즈니스 활동이 디지털로 변화 중이나 영업, 마케팅 등 핵심 영역은 아날로그 상태로 남아있다.
② 업무 공간이 종이에서 디지털 문서로 전환되었을 때 자원을 아끼는 기회라고 전망했다.
③ 대부분의 에너지 센터에서 사용하는 에너지원이 화석연료라는 보고서가 나온 이후 인터넷과 전기 사용이 줄었다.
④ 클라우드에 데이터를 많이 저장하면 탄소 배출량이 줄어들어 환경에 도움이 된다.
⑤ 첨부 파일이 없는 이메일 한 통은 이산화탄소 50g을 유발한다.
questions.explanation: 지문 중간 부분에 "When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents... it was a promising step to save trees."라는 내용이 나오므로, 디지털로의 전환이 나무를 아끼는(자원을 아끼는) 유망한 단계였다고 본 ②번이 일치합니다.

questions.question: 24. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously.
ordered_passages: (A) After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
(B) Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy.

(C) Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 행동이 정체성의 반영이라는 일반적인 원리를 제시합니다. (C)는 이를 뒷받침하는 구체적인 연구 결과와 '투표자'의 사례를 소개합니다. (B)에서는 'Similarly'를 사용하여 운동을 정체성의 일부로 여기는 사람의 또 다른 사례를 들어 앞의 내용을 확장합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 행동과 정체성이 일치할 때의 상태를 설명하며 결론을 맺는 구조가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 'brainwriting'에 대해 아래와 같이 요약하고자 하였을 때, 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (단, (A), (B)는 문장으로 작성할 것)
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.summary_sentence: Solo Idea Generation: You start by asking everyone to generate ideas individually.↓Pooling Ideas: (A)________________________________↓Independent Evaluation: Each member reviews and evaluates the pooled ideas independently.↓Team Activity: (B)_________________________________→ This method ensures all ideas are considered and helps overcome the limit of groupthink, facilitating greater (C)______________________________.
subjective_conditions: (A), (B)는 문장으로 작성할 것
본문에서 찾아 쓸 것
questions.answer: (A) You pool the ideas and share them anonymously among the group(B) The team (then) comes together to select and refine the most promising options(C) collective intelligence
questions.explanation: 본문에서 설명하는 브레인라이팅(brainwriting)의 절차를 요약하는 문제입니다. (A)는 아이디어를 따로 생성한 후의 단계로 '아이디어를 모으고 익명으로 공유하는 것'을 본문에서 찾으면 'You pool them and share them anonymously among the group'이 됩니다. (B)는 개인별 평가 이후 팀이 모여서 하는 활동이므로 '팀이 모여 가장 유망한 옵션을 선택하고 다듬는 단계'인 'The team come together to select and refine the most promising options'를 문장으로 작성합니다. (C)는 이러한 과정을 통해 촉진되는 것으로, 마지막 문장의 'collective intelligence'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does ─ this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.summary_sentence: The temperature rise (A)____________ by global warming is (B)____________ dissolved oxygen, leading to an (C)____________ risk of anoxic events.
questions.explanation: 지문은 지구 온난화로 인한 해수 온도 상승이 용존 산소량을 감소시키고, 이것이 무산소 사건(anoxic events)의 빈도를 높인다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A)에는 온도 상승을 '유발하는(triggered)', (B)에는 산소를 '감소시키는(diminishing)', (C)에는 무산소 사건의 위험을 '높이는/강화하는(enhanced)'의 의미가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 원인된 / 낮추는 / 약해진
② 가져온 / 자라나는 / 증가된
③ 유도된 / 줄이는 / 감소된
④ 유발된 / 감소시키는 / 강화된(높아진)
⑤ 몰아가는 / 강화하는 / 상승하는

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Capuchins ─ New World Monkeys that live in large social groups ─ will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead ─ grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers ─ the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains ─ the cucumbers themselves ─ to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
options: ① Monkeys in captivity will willingly engage in trading rocks for food with humans, especially when tasty food rewards are involved.
② Grapes are universally preferred by monkeys over cucumbers, making them the more desirable food option in this experiment.
③ Monkeys are highly sensitive to unfair treatment during trading experiments, especially when they perceive a difference in rewards.
④ Monkeys often react negatively when they observe another monkey receiving a more desirable food reward, such as grapes.
⑤ Monkeys prefer to trade rocks for food only when they are alone, rather than in the presence of other monkeys.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 카푸친 원숭이들은 사회적 집단을 이루어 살며, 실험 상황에서 옆장에 다른 원숭이가 있을 때 상대방이 받는 보상과 자신의 보상을 비교하여 불공정함에 반응한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 혼자 있을 때만 거래하는 것을 선호한다는 ⑤번 내용은 본문의 실험 설정 및 결과와 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 사육 상태의 원숭이들은 특히 맛있는 음식 보상이 포함될 때 인간과 돌을 음식으로 바꾸는 거래에 기꺼이 참여한다.
② 원숭이들은 보편적으로 오이보다 포도를 선호하며, 이는 이 실험에서 포도를 더 바람직한 음식 선택지로 만든다.
③ 원숭이들은 거래 실험 중에 불공평한 대우에 매우 민감하며, 특히 보상의 차이를 인지할 때 그러하다.
④ 원숭이들은 다른 원숭이가 포도와 같이 더 바람직한 음식 보상을 받는 것을 관찰할 때 종종 부정적으로 반응한다.
⑤ 원숭이들은 다른 원숭이가 있을 때보다 혼자 있을 때만 음식과 돌을 거래하는 것을 선호한다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 38번]
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
options: ① the difference between analogous and homologous traits
② why birds and bees have different wings
③ the importance of bones in animal evolution
④ the evolution of birds and insects
⑤ why animals evolve similar traits
questions.explanation: 이 글은 생물학자들이 구분하는 둀 가지 유사성인 '상사 형질(analogous traits)'과 '호먰 형질(homologous traits)'의 정의와 차이점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제렜는 둀 형질간의 차이가 가장 적절합단다.
options_translation: ① 상사 형질간 호먰 형질 사이의 차이점
② 새와 벜이 서렜 다른 날개림 가지고 있는 이유
③ 동물 진화에서 뮣의 중요성
④ 새와 걤충의 진화
⑤ 동물이 유사한 형질렜 진화하는 이유

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 41-42번]
questions.passage: Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for _________________________ between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
questions.explanation: 지문은 '대중 고등 교육 시스템'과 과거의 '엘리트 시스템'을 대조하고 있습니다. 대중 교육 시스템은 효율성을 위해 비인격적이고 표준화된 피드백을 제공하는 반면, 엘리트 시스템은 적은 학생 수 덕분에 학생과 교사 사이의 '개인적인 피드백(personal feedback)'이 가능했음을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 formative feedback(형성적 피드백)이 학생의 정신과 성격까지 형성했다는 내용이 이를 뒷받침합니다.
options_translation: ① 대규모 수업
② 개인적인 피드백
③ 경쟁적인 시험
④ 학생의 독립성
⑤ 자기 주도 학습

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. (A) Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. (B) It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. (C) But this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. (D) After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous. Unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. (E) To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.insertion_sentence: We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 정보가 단기 저장 공간(working memory)에 있기 때문에 우리가 그것을 안다고 느낀다는 내용입니다. (B)에서 정보가 작동 기억(working memory)에 활성화된 형태로 머물러 있다는 설명 뒤에, 우리가 그것을 알고 있다는 착각을 한다는 주어진 문장이 오는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 그 다음 (C)에서 '하지만(But)' 이 단기적인 부분(short-term section)은 장기 기억과 관련이 없다는 반전 내용이 이어져야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along ─ whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS ─ and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show ─ whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire ─ you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans to communicate ─ it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
questions.summary_sentence: Each new medium not only delivers information but also (A)_____________ us to perceive the world differently, with television emphasizing (B)____________.
questions.explanation: 새로운 매체는 우리가 세상을 다르게 인식하도록 유도하며, 특히 TV는 그 정보 전달 방식의 특징인 속도와 겉모습을 강조합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 권장/유도한다는 의미의 'encourages'가, (B)에는 지문 끝에 언급된 'speed and appearances'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 강요한다 - 실제와 깊이
② 권장한다 - 속도와 겉모습
③ 조종한다 - 사실과 세부 사항
④ 허용한다 - 단순함과 진실
⑤ 제한한다 - 감정과 느낌

questions.question: 15. 다음 글과 관련하여 주어진 질문에 대한 응답으로 가장 적절한 것은?Question: Based on the passage, what is the main danger associated with the use of concepts in scientific inquiry?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① Essentialism can lead scientists to search for nonexistent entities based on flawed concepts.
② Concepts can limit scientific inquiry by narrowing the scope of experimentation.
③ The use of metaphors in science often distorts the understanding of complex ideas.
④ Scientists should avoid experimentation when a concept lacks sufficient evidence.
⑤ Concepts play a crucial role in simplifying the complexity of the natural world.
questions.explanation: 지문에서는 개념이 본질주의(essentialism)를 유발하여, 과학자들이 존재하지 않는 대상(검은 고양이/에테르)을 헛되이 찾게 만드는 위험이 있다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 결함이 있는 개념에 기반해 존재하지 않는 실체를 탐색하게 만든다는 1번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 본질주의는 과학자들이 결함이 있는 개념을 근거로 존재하지 않는 실체를 찾도록 유도할 수 있다.
② 개념은 실험의 범위를 좁힘으로써 과학적 탐구를 제한할 수 있다.
③ 과학에서의 은유 사용은 종종 복잡한 아이디어에 대한 이해를 왜곡한다.
④ 과학자들은 개념에 충분한 증거가 부족할 때 실험을 피해야 한다.
⑤ 개념은 자연계의 복잡성을 단순화하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is ____________________________________________ within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure is hierarchical system, which has a pyramid-like organization with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is decentralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
options: ① to identify causes of conflict in the workplace
② to steer the organization in the right direction
③ to define the overall strategy and important decisions
④ to grasp the operational functions of various departments
⑤ to take a look at how they influence the organization's structure
questions.explanation: 이 글은 조직 내의 다양한 부서(departments)와 분과(divisions)가 각기 다른 관점과 편향된 시각('터널 시야')을 가지고 있으며, 이로 인해 한 조직 내에서도 여러 유형의 문화가 존재할 수 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸은 이러한 다양한 문화가 존재하는 양상을 보여주는 구체적인 대상이 되어야 하므로, 조직 내 다양한 부서들의 운영적 기능들을 파악하는 것이 적절한 예시가 됩니다. 따라서 정답은 4번입니다.
options_translation: 직장에서의 갈등 원인을 식별하는 것
조직을 올바른 방향으로 이끄는 것
전반적인 전략과 중요한 결정을 정의하는 것
다양한 부서의 운영 기능을 파악하는 것
그것들이 조직의 구조에 어떻게 영향을 미치는지 살펴보는 것

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 9월 23번]
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. (A) AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. (B) For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. (C) For instance, AI's ability to translate both written and spoken language instantly can enhance the effectiveness of non-native speakers in a professional setting. (D) Moreover, recent advancements in AI-driven text generators can quickly boost the performance of lower-skilled individuals in areas like writing, coding, and customer service. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: AI can also improve the abilities of low-skilled workers, which may lead to better wages and career opportunities for them.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 AI가 저숙련 노동자의 능력을 향상시켜 임금과 경력 기회를 개선할 수 있다는 내용입니다. (C) 앞부분까지는 장애가 있는 노동자들의 의사소통을 돕는 AI 사례를 다루고 있으며, (C) 이후부터는 비원어민 화자나 저숙련 개인들을 돕는 언어 번역 및 텍스트 생성 기능을 다룹니다. (C) 자리에 주어진 문장이 들어가면 일반적인 저숙련 노동자의 능력 향상 가능성을 먼저 제시하고, 그 구체적인 예시로 (C) 이하의 번역 기능과 (D) 이하의 텍스트 생성 기능을 연결하는 구조가 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing ⓐ<u>it</u>. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, ⓑ<u>making</u> streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets ⓒ<u>to accommodate</u> more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bike able cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component ⓓ<u>to making</u> cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids ⓔ<u>where</u> carry a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.explanation: ⓔ의 where는 관계부사인데, 뒤에 바로 동사 carry가 이어지므로 주어가 없는 불완전한 문장이 옵니다. 따라서 주격 관계대명사인 which 또는 that으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle, and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
options: ① 자신의 목소리가 녹음된 것을 듣고 "내 목소리가 정말 저렇게 들리는 건가?"라고 생각했을지도 모릅니다.
② 녹음된 목소리에서는 자신의 억양이 생각보다 약하게 들리거나, 자신의 귀에 들리는 것보다 목소리가 더 낮게 들릴 수도 있습니다.
③ 내부 경로에서는 저주파가 강조되기 때문에, 자신의 목소리는 다른 사람들에게 들리는 것보다 자신에게 더 깊고 풍부하게 들립니다.
④ 우리가 말을 할 때 자신서의 목소리를 인식하는 또 다른 한 가지 경로는 진동이 뼈를 통해 전달되어 직접적으로 내이를 자극하는 내부 경로입니다.
⑤ 우리가 말을 할 때 자신의 목소리를 인식하는 한 가지 경로는 대부분의 외부 소리를 인식하는 경로로, 공기를 통해 외이, 중이, 내이로 전달되는 파동입니다.
questions.explanation: 본문에 따르면 녹음된 목소리에서는 억양이 더 두드러지고(more pronounced), 자신의 귀에 들리던 것보다 더 높게(higher) 들린다고 하였습니다. 따라서 억양이 약하게 들리거나 목소리가 더 낮게 들릴 수 있다고 한 ②번은 본문의 내용과 정반대입니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity differs from elite celebrity. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
options: ① 소셜 미디어 유명인은 '별'이라는 은유로 상징되며, 신비로움과 계층적 거리감을 특징으로 하며, 타고난 재능과 계급과 연결된다.
② 소셜 미디어 유명인들이 받는 비판은 디지털 콘텐츠 제작자들이 엘리트 유명인의 영역으로 넘어가는 데 현실적인 장벽이 있음을 강조한다.
③ 소셜 미디어에서의 주목은 엘리트 유명인과 같은 목표를 달성하기 위한 도구가 될 수 있지만, 일부 콘텐츠 제작자들은 평범한 유명세를 사회적 목표 자체로 추구한다.
④ 리얼리티 TV 스타들과 마찬가지로, 소셜 미디어 유명인들은 종종 전통적인 엘리트 유명인에게 기대되는 연기나 노래 실력 같은 기술과 재능이 부족하다는 비판을 받는다.
⑤ 소셜 미디어 영역에서 유명세란 구독자 수, 팔로워 수, 좋아요, 클릭 수와 같은 소셜 미디어 애플리케이션에 내장된 주목도 측정 지표에서 높은 점수를 얻는 것이다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 '별'의 은유로 상징되고 신비로움과 계층적 거리감을 특징으로 하며 타고난 재능 및 계급과 연결되는 것은 '엘리트 유명인(The elite celebrity)'입니다. ①은 이를 '소셜 미디어 유명인'에 대한 설명으로 잘못 기술하고 있으므로 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think about a fundamental human ability: Iearning by watching others. As children, we learn a lot by seeing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongues if their parents stick out theirs. You may not see the baby stick out their tongue each time you stick out yours, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to mimic the sounds their parents make. As they grow they begin using vacuum cleaners and hammers by copying what their parents do. Our modern cultures ─ in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships, and go to school ─ can exist only because we are not limited to behaviors we are born with or learn through trial and error. We can learn a lot simply by watching others.
questions.summary_sentence: The discovery of mirror neurons reshaped our understanding of learning through (A)_____________. From a young age, we learn by (B)_____________ our parents and peers, and this ability improves with repetition. This form of learning enables us to develop complex cultures and skills.
questions.explanation: 거울 뉴런의 발견은 '타인을 관찰함으로써 학습하는 것(learning by watching others)'에 대한 이해를 바꾸어 놓았습니다. 지문에서는 아기가 부모를 따라 하거나 흉내 내는 예시를 통해 우리가 '관찰(observation)'을 통해 배우고, 부모나 또래를 '모방(imitating)'함으로써 학습한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 상상력 - 조작하는 것
② 의사소통 - 탐색하는 것
③ 관찰 - 모방하는 것
④ 탐구 - 통합하는 것
⑤ 축하 - 협력하는 것

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
options: ① 위험을 감수할 때는 단순한 감정이 아닌 사실에 근거해 결정을 내려야 한다.
② 안전을 위해 운전 시 주의할 점을 상세히 숙지하고 다양한 변수를 고려해야 한다.
③ 사람에 따라 같은 현상에 대해 느끼는 위험 여부와 불안감의 정도가 다르다.
④ 통제력의 정도를 고려했을 때 비행기를 타는 것보다 직접 자동차를 운전하는 것이 더 안전하다.
⑤ 중요한 문제에 대한 답을 선택하기에 앞서 실제 사례를 수집하여 자신에게 적용해 볼 필요가 있다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 비행기 공포증 때문에 통계적으로 훨씬 안전한 비행 대신 자동차 운전을 선택하는 경향이 있는데, 이는 논리가 아닌 감정에 근거한 결정이라고 설명합니다. 따라서 위험을 감수하는 결정을 내릴 때 감정이 아닌 객관적인 사실에 근거해야 한다는 것이 글의 핵심 요지입니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
options: ① the lifelong impact of emotional changes caused by moving
② the major scientific reasons why moving causes stress for people
③ tips for packing when moving with children that you must remember
④ the significance of the meaningful connection between past and present
⑤ the emotional impact of relocation on children and ways to support them
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이사가 아이들에게 미치는 심리적 스트레스와 정체성 혼란에 대해 설명하며, 아이들의 과거 경험을 인정해주고 새로운 환경에 적응하도록 돕는 방법(배경 공유 기회 제공 등)의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 이사로 인한 감정적 변화의 평생에 걸친 영향
② 이사가 사람들에게 스트레스를 주는 주요 과학적 이유
③ 아이와 함께 이사할 때 기억해야 할 짐 싸기 팁
④ 과거와 현재 사이의 의미 있는 연결의 중요성
⑤ 이전(이사)이 아이들에게 미치는 정서적 영향과 그들을 지원하는 방법

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the ⓐ<u>traditional</u>, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, ⓑ<u>adversarial</u> approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, such transactions are becoming increasingly ⓒ<u>common</u>, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly ─ our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and ⓓ<u>maintain</u> a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only ⓔ<u>acceptable</u> result.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 일회성 거래(one-off negotiation)는 현대 사회에서 줄어들고 있으며, 우리는 같은 사람들과 반복적으로 상호작용하기 때문에 'common(흔한)'이 아니라 'rare(드문)' 또는 'less common'과 같은 의미의 단어가 와야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. (A) Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it ─ you just see the blurred outline of the moving string. (B) Strings vibrating in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. (C) The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. (D) The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. (E) When the waves reach your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note is heard loud and clear.
questions.explanation: (B)에서 줄만으로는 소리가 거의 나지 않는다는 단점을 제시한 뒤, 주어진 문장에서 큰 울림통(기타 몸통)에 줄을 연결하면 진동이 증폭되어 소리가 크게 들린다는 해결책을 제시합니다. 그 이후 (C)부터는 그 울림통(guitar body)의 나무판이 어떻게 진동을 전달하는지에 대한 구체적인 설명이 이어지므로 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. ⓐUsually crystals form when liquids cool, and many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. ⓑIf conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. ⓒBut when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. ⓓWe might think that people who have talent in literature are more interested in the beauty of crystals. ⓔUsually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 원자가 결정체의 기본 구성 요소이며, 환경적 조건(냉각 속도, 온도 등)에 따라 결정이 형성되는 과정과 그 모양에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 문장 ⓓ는 문학에 재능이 있는 사람들이 결정체의 아름다움에 더 관심이 있을 것이라는 내용으로, 결정체의 과학적 형성 과정이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations ─ surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue ─ with one notable exception. ①A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. ②In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. ③In fact, a red bow tie is more recognized by the artists in terms of its aesthetic value. ④The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. ⑤The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 확립된 규범으로부터 아주 약간 벗어난 행동(예: 빨간 나비넥타이, 빨간 운동화 착용)이 오히려 그 사람의 지위와 능력을 더 높게 보이게 한다는 연구 결과를 다루고 있습니다. ③번 문장은 빨간 나비넥타이가 예술가들에게 미적 가치로 인정받는다는 내용으로, 글의 핵심 소재인 '사회적 규범 위반에 따른 지능이나 지위 평가'와는 거리가 멀어 전체 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation. If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. While the pain itself is unpleasant, _______________________________________. Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now contract quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object. Consequently, in the whole process, sensory and motor nerves act as a protective mechanism for the foot.
options: ① it prompts you to act quickly and protect yourself
② it makes the sharp objects more comfortable to step on
③ it delays and relieves the response to the painful stimulus
④ it makes the pain more bearable by removing any sensation
⑤ it ultimately leads you to a feeling of relaxation despite the pain
questions.explanation: 글은 감각 신경을 통해 전달되는 통증이 불쾌하기는 하지만, 결과적으로 뇌와 근육의 상호작용을 통해 위험으로부터 발을 떼게 하는 등 신체를 보호하고 빠르게 행동하도록 만드는 '보호 기제(protective mechanism)'로 작용한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 통증이 스스로를 보호하도록 재촉한다는 내용인 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그것은 당신이 빠르게 행동하고 스스로를 보호하도록 재촉한다
② 그것은 날카로운 물체를 밟는 것을 더 편안하게 만든다
③ 그것은 통증 자극에 대한 반응을 지연시키고 완화한다
④ 그것은 모든 감각을 제거하여 통증을 더 견딜 만하게 만든다
⑤ 그것은 통증에도 불구하고 결국 당신을 편안한 기분으로 이끈다

questions.question: 9. 윗글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything ⓐ<u>that</u> they do to reflect how smart they are ─ writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, write elegant computer code, and say something ⓑ<u>remarkably</u> wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how ⓒ<u>proficient</u> one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or ⓓ<u>to have</u> the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else ⓔ<u>is considered</u>. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
questions.summary_sentence: People tend to define self-worth by ability, which might lead them to (A)__________ only achievements with personal worth and (B)__________ other important qualities.

questions.question: 10. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything ⓐ<u>that</u> they do to reflect how smart they are ─ writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, write elegant computer code, and say something ⓑ<u>remarkably</u> wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how ⓒ<u>proficient</u> one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or ⓓ<u>to have</u> the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else ⓔ<u>is considered</u>. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
questions.explanation: ⓒ는 plays라는 동사를 수식하고 있으므로 형용사 proficient가 아니라 부사인 proficiently가 와야 합니다. ⓐ는 선행사 everything을 수식하는 목적격 관계대명사로 적절하고, ⓑ는 형용사(wise/witty)를 수식하는 부사로 적절하며, ⓓ는 to be와 병렬을 이루는 to부정사, ⓔ는 '고려되다'라는 의미의 수동태로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 23번]
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
options: ① Why Multicultural Cities Are More Productive
② Cultural Diversity's Impact on Economy and Society
③ The Reason Tolerant Societies Achieve Greater Growth
④ The Effects of Cultural Diversity on Knowledge Spillovers
⑤ Diversity of Backgrounds: Major Causes of Communication Fragmentation
questions.explanation: 이 글은 문화적 다양성이 생산성(경제)에 미치는 긍정적/부정적 영향과 삶의 질 및 사회적 인식(사회)에 미치는 영향을 두루 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '문화적 다양성이 경제와 사회에 미치는 영향'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [23년 9월 23번]

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders in research, who (A)[employs / employ] technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking (B)[said / is said] to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task ─ like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds ─ _____________________________________, which downplays its cognitive abilities. This and so many more tricks of language are (C)[what / that] de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
options: ① it must have superior genes compared to humans

③ they seek to find information that will enhance our lives

⑤ they attribute its victory to instinct rather than intelligence

⑤ 그들은 그것의 승리를 지능보다는 본능의 탓으로 돌린다

questions.question: 23. [23년 9월 38번] 다음 글을 읽고 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that they do not ⓐ<u>cross</u> boundaries between work and personal area. For example, these people might keep ⓑ<u>unified</u> email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and off-hour. We've even noticed more of these ⓒ<u>"separators"</u> carrying two phones ─ one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable ⓓ<u>clearer</u> distinction between time at work and time in other roles. On the other hand, other individuals prefer ⓔ<u>merging</u> work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
options: ① The Difficulty of Balancing Work and Home
② Why Work Should Be Done Exclusively at the Office
③ How to Completely Avoid Mixing Work and Family Roles
④ Work-Life Boundaries: Segmenting and Integrating in the Digital Age
⑤ Why Everyone Should Keep Work and Personal Life Completely Separate

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 34번]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.*sphere: 영역 **metric: 측정 기준
options: ① Obstacles to Becoming Famous as a Content Creator
② Distinction Between Elite and Ordinary Celebrity
③ Rise of Untalented Reality Television Stars
④ Downfall of Traditional Celebrity Cultures
⑤ Harsh Criticism of Social Media Stars

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 30번]
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is hard for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as -Will I still be me in the new place?- and -Will my toys and bed come with us?- It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
options: ① Why Routine Changes Don't Affect Kids
② The Positive Effects of Separation from Familiarity
③ How to Make Moving Fun and Exciting for Children
④ The Benefits of Frequent Relocation for Young Families
⑤ Supporting Young Children Through the Stress of Moving
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이사가 아이들에게 큰 스트레스를 준다는 점을 언급하며, 아이들이 과거의 경험을 인정받고 새로운 환경에 잘 적응할 수 있도록 돕는 것이 중요하다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 ⑤번 '이사의 스트레스를 겪는 어린 아이들을 지원하기'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.

④ 젊은 가족들에게 잦은 이주가 주는 이점
⑤ 이사의 스트레스를 겪는 어린 아이들을 지원하기

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety.
options: ① the importance of having control in aviation
② ways to make future-plans based on the odds
③ making irrational decisions out of fear and anxiety
④ reasons why driving is more systematic than flying
⑤ dangers of making illogical decisions as a statistician

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
