⑤ (E)

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own ⓐ<u>biased</u> perspective. A department and its members will acquire 'tunnel vision' which ⓑ<u>disallows</u> them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is 'mechanistic' or 'organic' can have a ⓒ<u>profound</u> influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a ⓓ<u>vertical</u> hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is ⓔ<u>centralized</u> and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 유기적 구조(Organic structures)는 본질적으로 수평적이며 의사결정이 조직 전체에 분산되는 구조이므로, '중앙 집중화된(centralized)'이 아니라 '분산된(decentralized)'이라는 단어가 문맥상 더 적절합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that _____________________.
options: ④ was too small to detect
⑤ kept hiding in the shadows
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잘못된 개념(본질)을 찾기 위해 노력했던 과학적 사례들을 '어두운 방에서 없는 검은 고양이를 찾는 일'에 비유하고 있습니다. 에테르(ether)라는 물질은 빛의 매질로 생각되었으나 실제로는 존재하지 않는 것이었습니다. 따라서 물리학자들은 '결코 그곳에 없었던(was never there)' 고양이의 증거를 찾고 있었던 것이 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 결코 그곳에 없었던
② 영리하게 숨겨졌던
③ 그들의 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 있었던
④ 감지하기에 너무 작았던
⑤ 그림자 속에 계속 숨어 있었던

questions.question: 29. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree.
ordered_passages: (A) A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity.

(b) When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location.
(C) They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 다양한 문화적 배경을 견진 노동자와 현지인의 상호윑용이 생산성을 높일 수 있지만, 이는 일정 수준까지만 장점이라고 언급합니다. (B)에서는 그 이유로 너무 많은 다양성은 의사소통 비용을 발생시켜 생산성을 낮출 수 있음을 설명하며, 다양성이 삶의 질에도 영향을 미친다고 합니다. (A)는 그 삶의 질에 대한 구체적 예시로, 관용적인 현지인은 다양성을 좀게 평가하지만, 국가적 정체성의 왜곭으로 바라볼 경우 매력적이지 않게 느낄 수 있다고 합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서는 그 부정적인 시각이 심화되어 차별이나 사회적 갈등에 대한 됐려움으로 이어지는 내용이 나오므로 (B)-(A)-(C) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 30. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity.
ordered_passages: (A) The composer Antonio Salieri is the 'host' of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him.

(B) Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.

(C) The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus?
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 오해받아서 받아들여지지 못한 이유가 '생소함'이라고 합니다. (C)에서는 그들의 음악 형식이나 아이디어가 완전히 새롭기 때문이며, 이것이 그들을 위대하게 만든다고 하면서 영화 'Amadeus'를 언급합니다. (A)에서는 그 영화의 주인공인 Salieri를 설명하며 그가 Mozart에 가렒혔음을 말합니다. (B)에서는 Salieri가 실력은 있었지만 위대한 작곡가가 되지 못한 이유가 그의 작품이 달른 사람들과 비슷해서 '독창성'(새롭지 않음)이 없었기 때문이라고 결론 집니다. 따라서 (C)-(A)-(B) 순서가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 31. 다음 괸의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약은자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. 'Analogous' traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not 'the same' organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. 'Homologous' traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being 'the same' organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
questions.summary_sentence: Biologists differentiate analogous traits, which serve similar (A)__________ but have independent origins, from homologous traits, which share a (B)__________ despite possibly having different functions.
questions.explanation: 괴 텍스트는 'Analogous traits'(상사 형질)과 'Homologous traits'(혼성 형질)의 차이를 설명합니다. 상사 형질은 기원은 다리지만 유사한 '기능(function)'을 수행하며, 혼성 형질은 기능은 다릴 수 있지만 공통의 조상에게서 물려받아 '공통의 구조(common structure)'를 갖고 있습니다.
options_translation: 기능들 / 공통의 구조
구조들 / 상호간의 목적
기능들 / 다른 목적
배경 / 별개의 기능
구조들 / 유사한 진화 과정

questions.question: 34. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 가장 적절한 순서대로 (A)~(D)를 나열하시오. [24년 9월 35번]
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory.
ordered_passages: (A) We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later.
(B) To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
(C) Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form.
(D) After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 벼락치기가 효과적이라고 착각하는 이유가 기억의 여러 부분을 구분하지 못하기 때문이라고 언급합니다. (C) 공부 직후에는 정보가 작업 기억에 활성화되어 있음을 설명하고, (A) 이것이 단기 저장 공간에 있어 아는 것처럼 느껴지지만 장기 기억과는 무관함을 지적합니다. (D) 시간이 지나면 작업 기억이 사라지는 현상을 언급한 뒤, (B) 정보를 장기 기억으로 옮기기 위한 해결책(테스트)을 제시하는 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 다음 글을 읽고 흐름에 맞게 (A)~(D)의 순서를 배열하시오.
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory.
ordered_passages: (A) We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later.
(B) To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
(C) Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form.
(D) After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes.
questions.explanation: 벼락치기가 효과적이라는 착각은 기억의 종류를 구분하지 못하기 때문에 발생합니다. (C) 교재를 읽은 직후에는 정보가 의식적인 작업 기억에 활성화된 상태로 존재합니다. (A) 단기 저장 공간에 정보가 있어 아는 것처럼 느끼지만, 이는 며칠 후 회상에 필요한 장기 기억과는 무관합니다. (D) 작업 기억은 금방 사라지기 시작하며 며칠 뒤에는 효과가 거의 없어집니다. (B) 따라서 장기 기억으로 전환하기 위해서는 단순 학습보다 스스로 테스트하는 과정이 필수적이라는 결론으로 이어집니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용을 추론한 것으로 옳지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are - writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
options: ① 능력의 정의는 지적 능력 외에 특별한 기술이나 재능을 포함할 수 있다.
② 사람들은 자신이 얼마나 똑똑한지 보여주기 위해 최선의 성취를 원한다.
③ 자신의 능력을 최신 유행을 따르거나 외모를 가꾸는 것으로 정의하기도 한다.
④ 수행 능력이 뛰어나지 않아도 다른 요소들이 자아 가치를 결정할 수 있다.
⑤ 수행 능력이 자아 가치의 유일한 결정 요인이 될 때 문제가 발생할 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 후반부에서 '능력이 자아 가치의 유일한 결정 요인(sole determinant)이 될 때 문제가 발생하며, 이 경우 수행 능력만이 그 사람을 측정하는 유일한 척도가 되고 다른 어떤 것도 고려되지 않는다(nothing else is taken into account)'라고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 ④번의 '다른 요소들이 자아 가치를 결정할 수 있다'는 설명은 지문의 내용과 상충됩니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용을 추론한 것으로 옳지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas of the cortex are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① The functional properties of the auditory cortex are highly dependent on the sounds encountered involuntarily.
② Some areas of the cerebral cortex specialize in processing sensory input originating from the eyes.
③ Violinists have more connectivity in the motor cortex in the hemisphere of the brain that controls the left hand.
④ People with a damaged hippocampus might experience difficulties in navigating familiar places.
⑤ Paying attention involves adaptive structural and functional changes to the brain.
questions.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 '집중된 주의(focused attention)'가 뇌의 재구성을 이끈다는 것입니다. ①번 선지는 청각 피질의 기능적 특성이 '비자발적으로(involuntarily)' 마주치는 소리에 의존한다고 설명하고 있으나, 지문은 주의를 기울이고 연습하는 것에 따라 뇌가 변한다고 설명하므로 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 청각 피질의 기능적 특성은 비자발적으로 마주치는 소리에 크게 의존한다.
② 대뇌 피질의 일부 영역은 눈에서 기원하는 감각 입력을 처리하는 데 특화되어 있다.
③ 바이올린 연주자들은 왼손을 조절하는 뇌 반구의 운동 피질에서 더 많은 연결성을 가지고 있다.
④ 해마가 손상된 사람들은 익숙한 장소를 찾아가는 데 어려움을 겪을 수 있다.
⑤ 주의를 기울이는 것은 뇌의 적응적인 구조적 및 기능적 변화를 수반한다.

questions.question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible.
ordered_passages: (A) By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.(B) So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps.(C) Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 어린 시절이 환경 학습과 유연성을 제공한다고 언급합니다. (C)에서는 어린 시절(학습기) 없이 본능(태어날 때 가진 지시 사항)에만 의존해 이주하는 새들이 비효율적이고 적응력이 낮음을 보여줍니다. (B)에서는 (C)의 사례를 확장하여 환경 변화가 일어날 때 이들이 과거의 방식에만 고립됨을 구체화합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 대조적으로(By comparison) 어린 시절이 긴 새들이 문화적 정보 전달을 통해 더 효율적이고 유연함을 보여주며 결론을 맺는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed ⓐ<u>plentiful food</u>, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans stopped ⓑ<u>foraging for</u> food. Humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and ⓒ<u>taming animals</u> for food production: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to ⓓ<u>a high rise</u> in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, ⓔ<u>getting in the way</u> of the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
questions.explanation: 신석기 시대는 농경과 정착을 통해 인구 밀도를 높이고 도시의 성장을 가능하게 한 전환점이었습니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 'getting in the way(방해하다)'는 문맥상 'paving the way(길을 닦다/가능하게 하다)'와 같은 긍정적인 맥락의 표현으로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans ⓐ<u>ignore</u> similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to ⓑ<u>differentiate</u> the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively ⓒ<u>distinct</u> from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal is ⓓ<u>inferior</u> to us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to ⓔ<u>underestimate</u> animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 새가 수천 개의 씨앗 위치를 기억하는 능력은 인간보다 뛰어난 인지적 과업을 수행하는 예시입니다. 따라서 인간이 동물보다 '열등한(inferior)' 것이 아니라 동물이 인간보다 '우수한(superior)' 상황에서도 인간은 그것을 지능이 아닌 본능으로 치부한다는 내용이 되어야 하므로 ⓓ가 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are getting vague as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. People have different preferences when it comes to managing their time in order to balance their professional and personal responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that crossings between them are ⓐ<u>enlarged</u>. For example, these people might keep email accounts for work and family ⓑ<u>separate</u>. They try to manage work-related tasks within the workplace while ⓒ<u>addressing</u> personal and family matters during breaks and outside of work hours. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones - one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they ⓓ<u>facilitate</u> greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring work emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox. These individuals ⓔ<u>thrive</u> in environments that enable them to blend their work and personal responsibilities.
questions.explanation: 분할자(segmenters)들은 일과 가정의 역할을 분리하여 그 사이의 교차(crossings)를 최소화하려 합니다. 따라서 ⓐ의 'enlarged(확대된)'는 'minimized(최소화된)'와 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this ___________________ to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.explanation: 인간의 정신이 타 부족과의 경쟁에서 상대방보다 생각을 더 잘함으로써(out-think) 얻은 인지적 우위가 생존과 진화에 결정적인 무기가 되었다는 내용입니다. 따라서 이러한 인지적 우위를 유전자로 물려주었다는 ④번 'cognitive dominance'가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 공격적인 특성
② 공감 능력
③ 정신 수양
④ 인지적 우위
⑤ 심리적 방해

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: There is a reason for the title 'Monday Morning Quarterback'. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but _________________________________________.
options: ① doctors and accountants suffer a lot from 'Monday Morning Quarterback'
② sports players, coaches, and management teams are guaranteed even more liberty
③ numerous individuals offer their opinions regarding the management of sports organizations
④ many people provide unpaid assistance for sporting organizations in their capacity as volunteers
⑤ the general public with expert-level knowledge of sports has increased due to the abundance of information
questions.explanation: 의사나 회계사와 같은 전문직에게는 훈수를 두지 않지만, 스포츠 경영 분야에서는 많은 팬들이나 비전문가들이 자신이 더 잘할 수 있다고 믿으며 조언을 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ③번 '수많은 개인들이 스포츠 조직의 경영에 대해 의견을 제시한다'가 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 의사와 회계사는 '월요일 아침의 쿼터백'으로부터 많은 고통을 받는다
② 스포츠 선수, 감독, 경영진은 더 많은 자유를 보장받는다
③ 수많은 개인들이 스포츠 조직의 경영에 대해 의견을 제시한다
④ 많은 사람들이 자원봉사자로서 스포츠 조직에 무보상 도움을 제공한다
⑤ 스포츠에 대한 전문 수준의 지식을 갖춘 대중이 정보의 풍부함으로 인해 증가했다

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: All humans, to some extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment. This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient in chilies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that __________________________________ produces pleasure. All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is to have the pain always directly associated with a pleasurable reward.
options: ① capsaicin does not seem to have any addictive qualities
② it assaults one of the most sensitive organs in the human body
③ our body endures self-harm within the context of directly positive reinforcement
④ repetitive sensations of spiciness reduces the activation of pain receptors in the tongue
⑤ the body's pain response is the result of the nervous system tricked into sensing extreme heat
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 매운맛(통증)을 통해 즐거움을 얻는 이유가 그것이 실제로는 해롭지 않은 '안전한 위협'임을 인지하기 때문이라고 설명합니다. 캡사이신이 실제 열에 의한 화상과 동일한 수용체를 자극한다는 맥락에서, 몸의 통증 반응이 실제 화상이 아닌 극심한 열을 감지하도록 신경계가 '속은 결과'라는 사실을 알 때 즐거움을 느낀다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 캡사이신은 중독성이 없는 것처럼 보인다
② 그것은 인체의 가장 민감한 장기 중 하나를 공격한다
③ 우리 몸은 직접적인 정적 강화의 맥락 안에서 자해를 견뎌낸다
④ 반복적인 매운맛의 자극은 혀의 통증 수용체 활성화를 감소시킨다
⑤ 신체의 통증 반응은 신경계가 극심한 열을 감지하도록 속은 결과이다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
questions.summary_sentence: Frequently, crystals form in (A)_________ shapes, but in a(n) (B)_________ environment with sufficient time, atoms are beautifully arranged to fit into crystal lattice.
questions.explanation: 글의 내용에 따르면 조건이 좋지 않을 때(너무 춥거나 덥거나 재료가 부족할 때) 결정은 '이상하고 뒤틀린(strange, twisted)' 모양이 되는데, 이는 (A)의 distorted(왜곡된)와 일맥상통합니다. 반면, 조건이 적절할(right) 때는 원자들이 결합할 충분한 시간을 가지며 완벽하게 배열된다고 했으므로 (B)에는 suitable(적합한)이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 임의의 / 변동하는
② 결점 없는 / 적절한
③ 불완전한 / 혼란스러운
④ 왜곡된 / 적절한
⑤ 이상적인 / 정적인

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.summary_sentence: The agent (A)_________ obtaining a more valuable reward in the long-term but in some cases ends up (B)_________ the temptation of instant satisfaction.
questions.explanation: 인간이나 동물은 미래의 보상을 위해 현재의 즐거움을 포기하며 저축하지만, 때때로 의지의 박약으로 인해 즉각적인 유혹에 굴복하여 저축한 돈을 미리 써버리곤 한다. (A)에는 미래의 보상을 '상상하다/계획하다(envisages)'가, (B)에는 유혹에 '굴복하다(yielding to)'가 들어가는 것이 문맥상 가장 적합하다.
options_translation: 미루다 - 저항하는
상상하다 - ~에 굴복하는
반대하다 - ~에 굴복하는
고려하다 - 대응하는/중화하는
상관하다/싫어하다 - ~에 굴복하는

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ③ Time to Make a Switch from Paper
④ Shake off Worries about Digital Expansion!
⑤ Tracking the Carbon Footprint of Business Activities
questions.explanation: 본문은 디지털 비즈니스 활동이 종이 사용을 줄여 환경에 긍정적일 것이라는 예상과 달리, 데이터 센터 운영을 위한 전기 소모와 화석 연료 사용으로 인해 탄소 배출을 증가시켜 환경을 위협한다는 내용을 담고 있다. 따라서 '구름(클라우드 서비스)이 우리(실제 자연)의 구름을 위협한다'는 비유적 표현인 ②번이 정답이다.
options_translation: 위기에 처한 디지털화
클라우드가 우리의 구름을 위협한다!
종이로부터 전환해야 할 시간
디지털 확장에 대한 걱정을 떨쳐버려라!
비즈니스 활동의 탄소 발자국 추적하기

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: ⓐ<u>If a tree falls in the forest and no one there hears it falling</u>, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. ⓑ<u>Sound is more than pressure waves and indeed without a hearer sound cannot be existed</u>. Likewise, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless ⓒ<u>if its intended audience does not receive and understand it</u>. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: Until the results have been published and understood, a scientific experiment is not complete. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. ⓓ<u>There are too many scientific papers that have fallen silently in the woods</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓑ의 'cannot be existed'는 틀린 표현이다. 'exist'는 자동사로 수동태로 쓰일 수 없으므로 'cannot exist'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ는 지각동사 hear+목적어+목적격보어(falling) 구문이 포함된 조건절로 옳고, ⓒ는 조건절 내 시제와 수동의 의미가 아닌 타동사 구조로 옳으며, ⓓ는 주격 관계대명사절로 현재완료 시제가 적절하게 쓰였다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, ⓐ<u>we're better off shifting to a process</u> called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by ⓑ<u>asking everyone to generate ideas separately</u>. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. ⓒ<u>Only then do the team comes together</u> to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities ⓓ<u>that might not get attention otherwise</u>. This brainwriting process ⓔ<u>makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table</u> and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.explanation: ⓒ에서 'Only then'이라는 부정어구가 포함된 부사구가 문두에 왔으므로 도치가 일어난다. 조동사 'do'가 이미 사용되었으므로 뒤따르는 주어 'the team' 뒤의 동사는 원형인 'come'이 되어야 한다. (do the team come together)

questions.question: 26. 다음 빈칸에 <보기>의 단어들을 각각 한 번씩 모두 사용하여 문장을 완성할 때, ⓕ의 자리에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual ⓐ______ ⓑ______ ⓒ______ ⓓ______ ⓔ______ ⓕ______ ⓖ______ ⓗ______ ⓘ______ consequences.
subjective_conditions: 보기의 단어들을 각각 한 번씩 모두 사용하여 문장을 완성할 것
questions.explanation: 원문의 핵심 내용은 '개인이 사회적 비용을 감수할 만큼 충분히 강력하다는 것을 암시한다'는 내용입니다. 어순은 "is so powerful that he can disregard potential social" (consequences)가 되어야 합니다. 배열: ⓐ is, ⓑ so, ⓒ powerful, ⓓ that, ⓔ he, ⓕ can, ⓖ disregard, ⓗ potential, ⓘ social. 따라서 ⓕ 자리에 들어갈 단어는 'can'입니다.
options_translation: ① 그
② 매우
③ 할 수 있다
④ 잠재적인
⑤ 무시하다

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Claims that local food production significantly reduces greenhouse gas emissions by minimizing transportation fuel consumption are usually ⓐ<u>ill</u> founded. Within the food sector, transportation accounts for only 11 percent of greenhouse gas emissions, so reducing the distance that food travels after it leaves the farm is far less important than reducing wasteful energy use on the farm. Depending on ⓑ<u>when</u> it was grown, food coming from a distance can actually be more environmentally friendly. For example, field-grown tomatoes shipped from Mexico in the winter months will have a ⓒ<u>smaller</u> carbon footprint than local winter tomatoes grown in a greenhouse. In the United Kingdom, lamb meat that travels 11,000 miles from New Zealand generates only one-quarter the carbon emissions per pound compared to British lamb due to the ⓓ<u>reliance</u> of UK farmers on feed production, which utilizes fossil fuels, instead of clover pastureland. When food travels, the environmental impact is determined more by the mode of transportation and load ⓔ<u>size</u> than by the distance traveled. Bulk loads of food can travel halfway around the world by ocean freight with a smaller carbon footprint, per pound delivered, than foods traveling just a short distance but in much less loads. For example, 18-wheelers carry much larger loads than pickup trucks, enabling them to transport food 100 times the distance while burning only one-third of the gas per pound of food delivered. Ultimately, when considering the environmental impact of food production and transportation, it is vital ________________________________________________________.
options: ① to utilize environmentally friendly fuels to reduce carbon emissions
② to consider the distance food travels and attempt to minimize it
③ to examine the broader context rather than focus solely on food miles
④ to avoid employing transportation methods with a smaller carbon footprint
⑤ to compare the amount of fossil fuels consumed with the quality of food delivered
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주된 내용은 지역 식품 생산이 단순히 이동 거리가 짧다는 이유만으로 친환경적이라는 주장이 항상 옳은 것은 아니라는 것입니다. 생산 방식(비닐하우스 vs 노지), 운송 수단, 운송량 등을 종합적으로 고려해야 한다고 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '단순히 이동 거리(food miles)에만 집중하기보다는 더 넓은 맥락을 검토하는 것이 중요하다'는 3번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 탄소 배출을 줄이기 위해 친환경 연료를 활용하는 것
② 식품이 이동하는 거리를 고려하고 그것을 최소화하려고 시도하는 것
③ 식품 이동 거리에만 단독으로 집중하기보다 더 넓은 맥락을 검토하는 것
④ 더 작은 탄소 발자국을 가진 운송 수단 사용을 피하는 것
⑤ 소비된 화석 연료의 양과 전달된 식품의 품질을 비교하는 것

questions.question: 28. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

For example, 18-wheelers carry much larger loads than pickup trucks, enabling them to transport food 100 times the distance while burning only one-third of the gas per pound of food delivered. Ultimately, when considering the environmental impact of food production and transportation, it is vital ________________________________________________________.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장 바로 뒤의 예시(겨울철 멕시코 노지 토마토 vs 영국 온실 토마토)는 재배 시기가 아니라 '재배 방식' 또는 '장소/환경'에 따른 차이를 설명하고 있습니다. 원문에서도 이 부분은 'how'(어떻게 재배되었는지)로 되어 있어야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다. 문맥상 '어디서/어떻게' 재배되었느냐에 따라 장거리 수송 식품이 더 친환경적일 수 있다는 논리가 성립합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 가장 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a ⓐ<u>boastful</u> parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her ⓑ<u>mediocre</u> behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely ⓒ<u>crucial</u> to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior ⓓ<u>generates</u> expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as ⓔ<u>prescribed</u> by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop-out, or worse.
questions.explanation: 본문은 영재 자녀를 둔 부모가 자녀의 뛰어난 성과에 대해 끊임없이 자랑하는 것에 대해 경고하고 있습니다. ⓑ의 앞부분에 'your little genius(당신의 작은 천재)'라고 언급하고 있으므로, 아이의 행동은 '평범한(mediocre)' 것이 아니라 '뛰어난(extraordinary/outstanding)' 것이어야 문맥이 성립합니다. 따라서 ⓑ가 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace.
ordered_passages: (A) For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.

(B) For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where interpersonal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects.

(C) AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 AI가 노동 시장 소외 계층의 접근성을 높여 포용성을 개선한다는 화두를 던집니다. (C)에서 장애가 있는 노동자들을 위한 보조 장치의 확산을 구체적으로 언급하고, (B)에서 그에 대한 예시(언어 장애, 청각 장애)를 들며 저숙련 노동자의 역량 강화로 확장합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 또 다른 예시로 비원어민 화자나 글쓰기/코딩 영역의 저숙련자들에 대한 지원을 설명하는 흐름이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글을 읽고 어법과 의미를 모두 고려하여 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 고르면?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals (A)[breath / breathe] to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming (B)[rises / raises] the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the (C)[habit / habitat] of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: (A) 'breath'는 명사(숨)이고, 'breathe'가 동사(숨 쉬다)입니다. 문맥상 조동사(can 또는 관계사절 내 동사) 자리에 동사가 필요하므로 breathe가 적절합니다. (B) 'rise'는 자동사이고 'raise'는 타동사입니다. 뒤에 'the temperature'라는 목적어가 있으므로 타동사인 raises가 와야 합니다. (C) 'habit'은 습관이고 'habitat'은 서식지입니다. 해양 생물의 서식지에 영향을 미친다는 문맥이므로 habitat이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. ⓐI give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. ⓑIf you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. ⓒIf, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. ⓓEven though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. ⓔMonkeys are generally known to eat leaves and fruits, but they also eat insects and small rodents. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 카푸친 원숭이가 타인과 비교하여 자신의 보상이 불공정하다고 느낄 때 강한 불만을 표시한다는 '공정성'과 '비교'에 관한 글입니다. ⑤번 문장은 원숭이의 일반적인 식습관(잎, 과일, 곤충 등을 먹음)을 설명하고 있으므로 주제와 무관합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through ____________________ with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전통적인 '엘리트 유명인(star)'과 소셜 미디어의 '보통의 유명인'을 대조하고 있습니다. 엘리트 유명인이 신비감과 위계적 거리를 특징으로 한다면, 소셜 미디어 유명인은 다른 일반인들과 지속적으로 소통하고 상호작용하며 관심을 끕니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 일반 대중과의 '지속적인 상호작용(continuous interplays)'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지속적인 상호작용
② 전염성 있는 행동
③ 결핍된 소통
④ 예외적인 상호작용
⑤ 비판적인 견해

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. (A) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. (B) As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. (C) Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. (D) A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. (E) Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.insertion_sentence: Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그럼에도 불구하고, 자전거를 타기 가장 좋은 도시라 하더라도 택시, 비상 차량, 그리고 배달 트럭을 위한 자동차 차로가 여전히 필요하다'는 내용입니다. (B)까지는 자동차 차로를 자전거 도로로 전환하는 긍정적인 측면을 설명하고 있고, (C)부터는 배달 트럭(delivery vehicles)의 필요성과 효율성에 대해 구체적으로 설명하기 시작합니다. 따라서 전환점이 되는 '그럼에도 불구하고 자동차 도로가 필요한 차량들(배달 트럭 등)'을 언급하는 주어진 문장은 (C) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. (A) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. (B) As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. ② differences between retail and wholesale
③ necessity of removing a variety of lanes
④ reasons why we always try to motivate people to travel by bike
⑤ double-sideness of transportation policy to calm traffic
questions.explanation: 이 글은 교통 정온화를 위해 자동차 통행을 제거하고 자전거 및 보행자 도로를 확장하는 정책의 이점과 동시에, 필수적인 물류 및 서비스를 위해 여전히 자동차 차선이 필요하다는 양면성을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '교통 정온화를 위한 교통 정책의 양면성'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자동차 차선의 부작용
② 소매와 도매의 차이점
③ 다양한 차선을 제거해야 할 필요성
④ 우리가 항상 사람들에게 자전거로 이동하도록 동기를 부여하려는 이유
⑤ 교통 정온화를 위한 교통 정책의 양면성

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.summary_sentence: The works of historically great composers were quite difficult to accept because they were not (A)__________ at the time, and this (B)__________ means (C)__________.
questions.explanation: 글의 내용에 따르면 위대한 작곡가들의 작품이 당대에 받아들여지기 힘들었던 이유는 그것이 '친숙하지 않았기(unfamiliar)' 때문이며, 이러한 '생소함(unfamiliarity)'은 곧 그들의 작품이 가진 '독창성 또는 발명적 재능(inventiveness/originality)'을 의미합니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 'not familiar(친숙하지 않은)'가 되어야 문맥상 맞고, (B)는 명사형인 'unfamiliarity', (C)는 위대함의 척도인 독창성을 뜻하는 'inventiveness'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 친숙한, (B) 생소함, (C) 독창성(발명적 재능)
② (A) 생소한, (B) 친숙함, (C) 일반성
③ (A) 친숙한, (B) 친숙함, (C) 보편성
④ (A) 생소한, (B) 생소함, (C) 독창성
⑤ (A) 친숙한, (B) 생소함, (C) 모방성

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of __________. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 생물학자들이 두 가지 종류의 '유사성(resemblance)'을 구분한다는 내용입니다. 하나는 기능은 같지만 진화 계통이 다른 '유사(analogous)' 형질이고, 다른 하나는 기능은 다를 수 있으나 공통 조상으로부터 물려받아 구조적 공통성을 지닌 '상동(homologous)' 형질입니다. 글 전체가 생물체 간에 나타나는 닮은 모습(유사성)을 어떤 기준으로 분류하느냐에 대해 설명하고 있으므로 빈칸에는 resemblance가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 임의성
② 유사함, 닮음
③ 수렴
④ 신뢰성
⑤ 지속 가능성

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑦ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to ①<u>perceive</u> the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will ②<u>inevitably</u> view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will ③<u>obtain</u> "tunnel vision". It ④<u>allows</u> them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a ⑤<u>negligible</u> influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management ⑥<u>incorporated</u> in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is ⑦<u>more</u> centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation:
문맥상 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 어휘는 총 3개(④, ⑤, ⑦)입니다.

④ allows: 앞 문장의 '터널 시야(tunnel vision)'는 자신의 관점만 고수하는 편협한 시각을 의미하므로, 타인의 시각으로 보는 것을 '허용하는' 것이 아니라 '방해하거나 막는(prevents/stops/hinders)'다는 맥락이 되어야 합니다.
⑤ negligible: 조직 구조의 선택(기계적 vs 유기적)은 갈등 관리에 '무시할 만한' 영향이 아닌 '상당하고 중요한(significant/considerable)' 영향을 미칩니다.
⑦ more: 유기적 구조(Organic structures)는 수평적인 특성을 가지므로, 의사 결정이 한곳에 '더(more)' 집중되기보다는 '덜(less)' 집중화되어 조직 전체로 분산되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 어법상 어색한 것 세 개를 찾아 바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: Our emotions ⓐ<u>considered</u> to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us ⓑ<u>to bond</u> with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when ⓒ<u>triggering</u>, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us ⓓ<u>attentively</u>, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or ⓔ<u>avoid</u> it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways ⓕ<u>in which</u> they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
questions.answer: (1) considered → are considered / have been considered(2) triggering → triggered(3) attentively → attentive
questions.explanation: ⓐ 주어인 Our emotions는 고려되는 대상이므로 수동태(are considered)가 필요합니다. ⓒ 감정이라는 프로그램이 유발'되는' 것이므로 분사구문에서 수동인 triggered가 적절합니다.ⓓ 사역동사 make + 목적어 + 목적격 보어 자리로, 보어로는 부사가 아닌 형용사(attentive)가 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where <u>perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks</u>. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
options: ① true reality comes from senses, not reasoning
② our experiences are shaped by physical influences
③ all things exist in their flawless, unchanging state
④ a circle we encounter in reality is a perfect representation of the Forms
⑤ the journey of mice represents the path from ignorance to enlightenment
questions.explanation: 플라톤의 실재론에 따르면, 우리가 오감으로 지각하는 현실 세계의 사물들은 불완전하고 변하기 쉬운 반면, 보이지 않는 '형상(Forms)'의 세계에는 모든 사물의 완벽하고 변하지 않는 본질이 존재한다는 내용입니다. 밑줄 친 부분은 이러한 완벽한 본질들이 존재하는 형상의 세계를 비유적으로 표현한 것이므로, 모든 것이 결점 없고 변하지 않는 상태로 존재한다는 의미인 3번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 진정한 현실은 추론이 아니라 감각에서 온다
② 우리의 경험은 물리적 영향에 의해 형성된다
③ 모든 사물은 결점 없고 변하지 않는 상태로 존재한다
④ 우리가 현실에서 마주치는 원은 형상의 완벽한 표현이다
⑤ 쥐의 여정은 무지에서 계몽으로 가는 경로를 나타낸다

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying them to culture. Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection are conceptually likened to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection. However, these approaches had to be modified to account for the differences between genetic and cultural transmission. For example, we do not expect the cultural transmission to follow the rules of genetic transmission strictly. If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily equally likely to acquire the mother's or father's form of that trait. Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers; thus, the frequency of a cultural trait in the population is relevant beyond just the probability that an individual's parents had that trait.
options: ① strict inheritance patterns in genetics
② the influence of parental figures in cultural transmission
③ how cultural traits differ from genetic traits in transmission
④ various examples of biological traits in genetic transmission
⑤ similarities between genetic and cultural transmission in evolutionary models
questions.explanation: 이 글은 초기 문화 진화 모델이 유전학적 개념을 차용했지만, 실제 문화 전달 방식은 유전적 전달과 다르다는 점을 강조합니다. 문화적 특성은 부모뿐만 아니라 또래나 다른 성인으로부터도 전달될 수 있어 유전적 전달 법칙을 엄격하게 따르지 않으므로, 유전적 특성과 문화적 특성의 전달 방식 차이를 다룬 3번이 주제로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 유전학에서의 엄격한 상속 패턴
② 문화 전달에서 부모 인물의 영향
③ 문화적 특성이 전달에 있어 유전적 특성과 어떻게 다른가
④ 유전적 전달에서 생물학적 특성의 다양한 사례들
⑤ 진화 모델에서 유전적 전달과 문화적 전달 사이의 유사성

questions.question: 7. 다음 George M. Stratton에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristics of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself. Psychologist George M. Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment. Stratton wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally turned the world upside down for him. In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him. With time, however, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated. As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems: he used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something, for example. Fortunately, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for the rest of his life. For him, everything returned to normal after one day.
options: ① He performed the experiment with himself as the subject.
② His reversing glasses were special glasses that inverted the wearer's perception of the world.
③ Wearing reversing glasses initially brought him difficulties with basic tasks like eating with a fork.
④ His visual system with reversing glasses gradually adapted, allowing normal behavior.
⑤ He still had difficulties adjusting, even a day after taking off the reversing glasses.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장에서 '하루 뒤에 모든 것이 정상으로 돌아왔다(everything returned to normal after one day)'고 명시되어 있으므로, 하루가 지난 뒤에도 여전히 적응에 어려움을 겪었다는 ⑤번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 그는 자신을 실험 대상자로 하여 실험을 수행했다.
② 그의 반전 안경은 착용자의 세상에 대한 지각을 뒤집는 특수 안경이었다.
③ 반전 안경을 쓰는 것은 처음에는 포크로 음식을 먹는 것과 같은 기본적인 작업에 어려움을 주었다.
④ 반전 안경을 쓴 그의 시각 체계는 점차 적응하여 정상적인 행동을 가능하게 했다.
⑤ 그는 반전 안경을 벗은 지 하루가 지난 후에도 여전히 적응하는 데 어려움을 겪었다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: People differ in how quickly they can reset their biological clocks to overcome jet lag, and the speed of recovery depends on the direction of travel. Generally, it's easier to fly westward and lengthen your day than it is to fly eastward and shorten it. This east-west difference in jet lag is sizable enough to have an impact on the performance of sports teams. Studies have found that teams flying westward perform significantly better than teams flying eastward. A more recent study found additional evidence that eastward travel is tougher than westward travel. So teams traveling eastward had more difficulty adjusting to the time change, which affected their overall performance on the field. Thus, teams have implemented various strategies to reduce the effects of jet lag, such as adjusting their sleep schedules before travel and managing light exposure to reset their biological clocks.
options: ① Individuals vary in how fast they can adjust their internal clocks to overcome jet lag.
② How quickly people recover from jet lag is affected by the direction of flight.
③ In most cases, traveling westward is less challenging than travelling eastward.
④ (This option is missing from the provided text fragment but corresponds to the incorrect answer indicated in the key.)
questions.explanation: 제공된 텍스트에는 선택지 4번과 5번의 구체적인 내용이 누락되었으나, 정답 표기에 따라 4번이 일치하지 않는 내용임을 알 수 있습니다. 지문의 핵심 내용은 서쪽 비행이 동쪽 비행보다 시차 적응이 쉽다는 것입니다.
options_translation: ① 개인마다 시차를 극복하기 위해 생체 시계를 조정하는 속도가 다르다.
② 시차에서 얼마나 빨리 회복하는지는 비행 방향의 영향을 받는다.
③ 대부분의 경우, 서쪽으로 여행하는 것이 동쪽으로 여행하는 것보다 덜 힘들다.
④ (내용 누락)

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [23년 3월 24번]
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well rewarded for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The ⓐ<u>concern</u> is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable rut that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air. In addition, the sides of the rut have become so slippery that it would take a ⓑ<u>tremendous</u> effort to climb out. Effectively, you're ⓒ<u>released</u> from a repetitive but comfortable routine. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling trapped in what may be a secure, or even well-paying but ⓓ<u>unsatisfying</u> job. As time passes, the fear of starting over or risking change will grow, making it even ⓔ<u>harder</u> to break free from the rut and pursue something more fulfilling.
questions.explanation: 지문 전체의 흐름은 성감으로 인해 편안한 틀에 박혀 뽀어나오기 힘든 상황을 묘사하고 읈습니다. ⓒ가 포함된 문잕에서는 반복적이고 편안한 일상에 '갇혀 읈다'는 내용이 나와야 하므로, 'released(방출된, 해방된)'는 'locked(갇혀 읈는)' 등의 반대 의미림 가진 단어로 바귈어야 합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 각각 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The (A)__________ in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new (B)__________ ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more (C)__________ when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
questions.explanation: (A) 전통적 품종들이 소수의 신품종으로 대체되면서 종의 다양성이 '감소(decrease/decline/reduction)'했습니다. (B) 대규모 생산을 위해 도입된 신품종은 생산성이 높고 '효율적인(efficient/productive)' 것들입니다. (C) 단일 품종에 의존하게 되면 질병이나 기후 재난에 '취약(vulnerable)'해집니다. 이를 종합하면 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 감소 (B) 열등한 (C) 무기력한
② (A) 감소 (B) 효율적인 (C) 취약한
③ (A) 축소 (B) 생산적인 (C) 안전한
④ (A) 확장 (B) 우수한 (C) 성공적인
⑤ (A) 정체 (B) 저항력이 있는 (C) 위험에 처한

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 요약문을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson suggests that we tend to understand the world by focusing on particular features within it. Take platypuses. We might zoom in so closely to their fur that each hair appears different. We might also zoom out to the extent where it appears as a single, uniform object. We might take the platypus as an individual, or we might treat it as part of a larger unit such as a species or an ecosystem. It's possible to move between many of these perspectives, although we may need some additional tools and skills to zoom in on individual pieces of hair or zoom out to entire ecosystems. Crucially, however, we can only take up one perspective at a time. We can pay attention to the varied behavior of individual animals, look at what unites them into a single species, or look at them as part of bigger ecological patterns. Every possible perspective involves emphasizing certain aspects and ignoring others.
questions.summary_sentence: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson suggests that our understanding of the world depends on the (A)_________ we choose. Using the example of a(n) (B)_________, Bateson illustrates how we can (C)_____________ on specific features or (D)_____________ on broader patterns but we can only look at them from one angle at a time, each highlighting certain aspects while ignoring others.
subjective_conditions: (A), (B)는 각각 1단어, (C), (D)는 각각 연속된 2단어로 쓸 것
본문에서 찾아 변형하지 말고 그대로 쓸 것
본문 이외의 단어를 추가하지 말 것
questions.answer: (A) perspective(s)(B) platypus(C) zoom in(D) zoom out
questions.explanation: 인류학자 Gregory Bateson은 세상에 대한 이해가 우리가 선택한 '관점(perspective)'에 달려 있다고 제안합니다. '오리너구리(platypus)'의 예를 통해, 특정 특징에 '확대(zoom in)'하거나 더 넓은 패턴에 '축소(zoom out)'할 수 있음을 설명하는 내용입니다. 본문의 단어를 그대로 활용하여 빈칸을 채웁니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists say that having a disorderly room can indicate a disorganized mental state. One of the professional tidying experts says that the moment you start cleaning your room, you also start changing your life and gaining new perspective. When you clean your surroundings, positive and good atmosphere follows. You can do more things efficiently and neatly. So, clean up your closets, organize your drawers, and arrange your things first, then ________________________.
options: ① a downturn in performance and concentration will follow
② you will experience the benefits of messiness and untidiness
③ a clear mind will become clouded with confusion and distraction
④ the mental clarity and sense of accomplishment will come with chaos
⑤ you will find a state of peace and calm that comes from a tidy environment
questions.explanation: 글은 어수선한 방이 부정적인 감정을 유발하므로 방을 정리하는 것이 삶의 변화와 효율성을 가져다준다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 주변을 먼저 정리하면 정돈된 환경에서 오는 평화와 차분함을 얻게 될 것이라는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 성과와 집중력의 하락이 뒤따를 것이다
② 당신은 지저분함과 무질서함의 이점을 경험할 것이다
③ 맑은 정신이 혼란과 산만함으로 흐려질 것이다
④ 정신적인 명료함과 성취감이 혼돈과 함께 올 것이다
⑤ 당신은 정돈된 환경에서 오는 평화롭고 차분한 상태를 찾게 될 것이다

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should _______________________________ as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
options: ① consistently consider the widest possible audience
② prioritize the needs of the smallest group possible
③ concentrate solely on the latest technology trends
④ design for a limited audience with specific interests
⑤ focus on the preferences of a specific cultural group
questions.explanation: 디지털 정보 구축 시 장애인들의 접근성이 무시되고 있다는 문제점을 제기하며, 디자인 결정을 내릴 때 장애인을 포함한 가능한 가장 넓은 범위의 청중을 고려해야 상황이 개선될 것이라는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 가능한 가장 넓은 범위의 청중을 일관되게 고려하다
② 가능한 가장 작은 집단의 요구를 우선시하다
③ 최신 기술 트렌드에만 집중하다
④ 특정 관심사를 가진 제한된 청중을 위해 설계하다
⑤ 특정 문화 집단의 선호도에 집중하다

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one.
ordered_passages: (A) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.
(B) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
(C) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 미래 소비를 위해 저축하는 행위(지연된 보상 선호)를 설명합니다. (A)에서 '따라서(Thus)'를 통해 미래 보상의 가치가 현재보다 커야 함을 논리적으로 잇고, 저축을 조기에 사용하는 예외 상황을 제시합니다. (C)는 조기에 사용하는 구체적 예시(크리스마스 저축을 여름 휴가에 씀)를 들며 '의지의 박약'을 언급합니다. (B)는 '즉(That is)'을 통해 의지의 박약에 대해 다시 설명하며 결론짓습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains ①<u>to evolve</u> the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, ②<u>gives</u> your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon ③<u>still</u> more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding ④<u>generation</u>. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes ⑤<u>that</u> responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
questions.explanation: ⑤에서 'that'은 관계대명사 주격으로 쓰였는데, 뒤에 동사가 없이 'responsible'이라는 형용사구만 옵니다. 따라서 'that were responsible' 또는 'responsible' 형용사구 자체가 genes를 수식하도록 해야 합니다. (that were가 생략된 형태로 보거나 were를 써주어야 함)

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people ⓐ<u>to stay</u> in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, ⓑ<u>spacing</u> their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about ⓒ<u>transporting</u> young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place ⓓ<u>was</u> able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, ⓔ<u>which</u> in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.explanation: ⓓ 문장의 주어는 'Societies'로 복수 명사입니다. 따라서 단수 동사인 'was'를 복수 동사인 'were'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: We often try to ⓐ<u>diminish</u> our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to ⓑ<u>attain</u> the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be ⓒ<u>beneficial</u> to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by ⓓ<u>neglecting</u> hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from ⓔ<u>adversity</u>, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
questions.explanation: 성공한 운동선수들은 고난을 무시(neglecting)하는 것이 아니라, 고난을 포용하거나 극복함으로써 힘과 기술을 얻습니다. 문맥상 'embracing'이나 'enduring' 등의 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be ⓐ<u>less</u> flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very ⓑ<u>efficient</u> migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the ⓒ<u>accustomed</u> rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the ⓓ<u>longest</u> childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives ⓔ<u>flexibility</u> in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 학습 없이 선천적으로 타고난 이동 경로만을 따르는 새들은 환경 변화에 적응하지 못하므로, 이들의 경로가 항상 효율적(efficient)이라고 할 수 없습니다. 뒤의 내용에서 어린 시절이 긴 새들이 가장 효율적인 경로를 가진다고 설명하므로, 선천적인 이동 정보만을 가진 새들은 '비효율적인(inefficient)' 경로를 가질 수 있다는 의미가 되어야 흐름상 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Simply ⓐ<u>granting</u> employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were ⓑ<u>denied</u> the right to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had ⓒ<u>authority</u> over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making ⓓ<u>fewer</u> mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control ⓔ<u>boosted</u> how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 직원들에게 통제권과 결정권을 주었을 때 생산성이 향상되었다는 실험 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 오하이오 공장의 노동자들은 결정을 내릴 권한을 '거부당한(denied)' 것이 아니라 '부여받은' 것이어야 합니다. 문맥상 'given' 또는 'granted'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 36번]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data enters' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
questions.summary_sentence: Although shifting business activities from paper to digital was intended to (A)___________ negative environmental impact, the increased reliance on data centers and energy consumption has led to significant carbon emissions, (B)___________ some of the environmental benefits of reducing paper waste.
questions.explanation: 본문은 종이 기반 업무에서 디지털 업무로의 전환이 환경에 덜 해로울 것이라 예상되었지만, 실제로는 데이터 센터 운영과 에너지 소비로 인한 탄소 배출이 발생하여 그 이점을 상쇄한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 부정적인 환경 영향을 '줄이다(lessen/reduce/minimize)'가 들어가야 하며, (B)에는 종이 절약의 이점을 '상쇄하다(offsetting)'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 줄이다  상쇄하는 것
② 무시하다  대응하는 것
③ 극대화하다  약화시키는 것
④ 줄이다  향상시키는 것
⑤ 최소화하다  지지하는 것

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 34번]
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually, before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ① The Evolution of Brainstorming Techniques in Creative Problem-Solving
② The Historical Evolution of Brainwriting Techniques in Creative Industries
③ Unlocking Team Potential: The Advantages of Brainwriting Over Brainstorming
④ Exploring the Psychological Factors That Influence Decision-Making Processes
⑤ Maximizing Team Productivity through Brainstorming: A Better Approach Than Brainwriting
questions.explanation: 이 글은 브레인스토밍 대신 '브레인라이팅(brainwriting)'을 통해 팀의 잠재력을 끌어내는 방법을 설명합니다. 개별적으로 아이디어를 생성하고 익명으로 공유하며 개별 평가를 거치는 과정이 집단 지성을 발휘하는 데 더 효과적임을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 브레인스토밍보다 브레인라이팅이 가진 장점을 언급한 ③번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 창의적 문제 해결에서 브레인스토밍 기술의 진화
② 창의적 산업에서 브레인라이팅 기술의 역사적 진화
③ 팀 잠재력 발휘하기: 브레인스토밍 대비 브레인라이팅의 장점
④ 의사결정 과정에 영향을 미치는 심리학적 요인 탐색
⑤ 브레인스토밍을 통한 팀 생산성 극대화: 브레인라이팅보다 더 나은 접근법

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.summary_sentence: Although bikes are (A)_________ tools for sooth and safe traffic, delivery vehicles provide still (B)_________ elements in the cities.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 자전거가 교통 안전과 완화에 유용한 도구이지만, 배달 차뜡 또한 물건 운섑의 효율성을 통해 도시림 더 친환경적으로 만드는 필수적 요소임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '유용한(useful)', (B)에는 '친환경적인(eco-friendly)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우세한 / 격수한
② 유용한 / 친환경적인
③ 심오한 / 대안의
