questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. ⓐ<u>Fear has helped us avoid dangers</u>, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and ⓑ<u>expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others</u>. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, ⓒ<u>fear makes us very attentive, narrow our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli</u>, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). ⓓ<u>Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems</u>, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. ⓔ<u>If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓒ에서 narrow는 주어인 fear에 연결되는 동사들의 병렬 구조(makes, narrows, will cause, may cause) 중 하나이므로 단수형인 narrows가 되어야 합니다. 또는 makes us (1) very attentive, (2) narrow... 로 보더라도 narrow가 형용사 attentive와 병렬을 이룰 수 없으므로(narrow는 여기서 동사적 의미) 구조상 오류가 있습니다. 전체 문맥상 fear가 만드는 여러 결과들을 나열하는 것이므로 narrows가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is _____________. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
questions.explanation: 지문은 부정적인 상태에서 벗어나기 위해 문제를 해결한 긍정적인 사람들과 함께 있는 것의 이점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 그들의 존재 속에 있는 것만으로도 '이롭다'는 의미가 되어야 하므로 'beneficial'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 피할 수 없는
② 이로운
③ 주목할 만한
④ 근본적인
⑤ 관습적인

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, _____________________________________________.
options: ② discussing the procedures of the experiment
③ checking scientists' hypotheses again and again
④ seeking for evidence of a cat that is not present
⑤ comparing the result of experiment with previous one
questions.explanation: 에테르(ether)라는 존재하지 않는 개념을 찾으려 했던 과학자들의 시도를 '검은 고양이가 없는 어두운 방에서 고양이를 찾는 것'에 비유하고 있습니다. 따라서 물리학자들은 존재하지 않는 고양이(에테르)의 증거를 찾으려 애쓰고 있었다는 맥락의 4번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 과학자들의 실험 정신을 고취하며
② 실험의 절차를 논의하며
③ 과학자들의 가설을 반복해서 확인하며
④ 존재하지 않는 고양이의 증거를 찾으며
⑤ 실험의 결과를 이전의 것과 비교하며

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, ______________________________________________, rather than spend all your time studying.
options: ① it is helpful to study in advance
② it is important to arrange your study plan
③ it is essential to study the material, then test yourself
④ it is difficult to study with old friends in the same place
⑤ it is useless to study without background knowledge of every subject
questions.explanation: 벼락치기가 효과적이라는 착각은 단기 기억을 장기 기억으로 오해하는 데서 비롯됩니다. 정보를 장기 기억으로 보내기 위해서는 단순히 공부만 하는 것이 아니라 스스로를 테스트(retest)하는 과정이 필수적이라는 내용이므로 3번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 미리 공부하는 것이 도움이 된다
② 학습 계획을 짜는 것이 중요하다
③ 내용을 공부한 후 스스로를 테스트하는 것이 필수적이다
④ 같은 장소에서 오랜 친구들과 공부하는 것은 어렵다
⑤ 모든 과목의 배경지식 없이는 공부하는 것이 무용지물이다

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. -Analogous- traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not -the same- organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. -Homologous- traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being -the same- organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
options: ① '상사' 형질은 공통된 기능을 가지는 것들이지만, 진화 계보의 다른 가지에서 생겨났고, '동일한' 기관이 아닌 형질이다.
② '상동' 형질은 공통된 기능이 있을 수도 없을 수도 있으나, '동일한' 기관임을 보여주는 어떠한 공통된 구조를 가진다.
③ 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 모든 포유류 조상의 뒷다리가 모두 변형된 것들이다.
④ 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 뼈의 개수와 그것들이 연결된 방식과 같은 비기능적 형질을 공유한다.
⑤ 상사성과 상동성을 구별하기 위해, 생물학자들은 주로 기관의 가장 쓰임이 없는 특성에 집중한다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 모든 포유류 조상의 '앞다리(forelimb)'가 변형된 것이라고 설명하고 있으므로, 이를 '뒷다리'라고 설명한 ③번은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 8. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability.
ordered_passages: (A) Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.

(B) This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame.

(C) The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 소셜 미디어 셀러브리티가 전통적인 엘리트 셀러브리티와 달리 기술이 부족하다는 비판을 언급했습니다. (B)에서 '이 비판(This criticism)'을 받아 그 비판이 가지는 의미와 한계(명성의 의미 재구성)를 설명합니다. (C)에서는 엘리트 셀러브리티와 평범한 셀러브리티의 특징을 대조하며 명성의 의미 변화를 구체화합니다. (A)에서는 결론적으로 소셜 미디어에서의 명성이 수치화된 지표에 불과함을 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose (A)___________ in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share (B)___________ traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 생물학적 유사성을 '상사성(analogy)'과 '상동성(homology)'으로 구분하여 설명하고 있습니다. 새의 날개와 벌의 날개는 나는 기능은 같으나 진화 계통상 서로 다르게(respectively) 발생한 상사 형질입니다. 반면 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 기능은 다르지만 공통 조상으로부터 유래하여 뼈의 개수나 연결 방식 같은 사소하거나 무의미한(meaningless) 구조적 특징을 공유하는 상동 형질입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 각각 발생했다는 의미의 respectively가, (B)에는 기능과는 무관한 특징을 공유한다는 의미의 meaningless가 적절합니다.
options_translation: 부분적으로 ... 유용한
각각 ... 무의미한
의존적으로 ... 기능하지 않는
개별적으로 ... 기능적인
의도적으로 ... 매우 귀중한

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. (A) The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. (B) And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. (C) Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amdeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great compowers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. (D) Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. (E) What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.insertion_sentence: The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 초기의 수용 부족(lack of acceptance)의 이유가 생소함(unfamiliarity)이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 바로 앞 문장에서 베토벤 등의 음악을 당대 사람들이 이해하지 못했다고 언급했으므로, 그 원인을 설명하는 주어진 문장이 (A) 위치에 들어가는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 그 뒤에 음악 형식이 완전히 새로웠다는 내용이 이어지며 생소함을 구체화합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오. 단, 필요한 경우 어형을 변형할 수 있음.
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds of minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory (A)___________. To get information into (B)___________ memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
subjective_conditions: - 본문에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓸 것
- 필요한 경우 어형을 변형할 수 있음
questions.explanation: 벼락치기 공부는 정보가 단기 기억 공간에만 머물러 있어 그 순간에는 다 아는 것 같지만, 시간이 지나면 곧 사라지게 됩니다. 따라서 지식을 다시 확인(retest)하지 않으면 기억이 '사라진다(disappears)'는 (A)의 소결론과, 학습한 내용을 단순히 읽기만 하는 것이 아니라 스스로 테스트하여 '장기(long-term)' 기억으로 보내야 한다는 (B)의 해결책이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다. (A)의 경우 주어 memory에 맞게 본문의 disappearing을 disappears로 변형해야 합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical structure of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
options: ① how technology affects brain development
② importance of the hippocampus in memory retention
③ effect of attention and practice on brain architecture
④ relationship between auditory and visual skills in animals
⑤ differences in brain development between humans and animals
questions.explanation: 이 글은 집중된 주의와 연습이 뇌의 물리적 구조를 재형성한다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 소리에 집중하는 동물은 청각 중심부가 더 커지고, 손가락 조작에 집중하는 바이올린 연주자는 관련 뇌 부위가 확장되며, 공간 기억이 중요한 택시 기사는 해마가 커진다는 사례들을 통해 주의를 기울이는 곳과 연습하는 활동에 따라 뇌의 구조가 변화한다는 주제를 도출할 수 있습니다. 따라서 '주의와 연습이 뇌 구조에 미치는 영향'인 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기술이 뇌 발달에 미치는 영향
② 기억력 유지에서 해마의 중요성
③ 주의와 연습이 뇌 구조에 미치는 영향
④ 동물들의 청각 및 시각 기술 간의 관계
⑤ 인간과 동물 간의 뇌 발달 차이

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ① The Impact of Uniforms on Employee productivity
② The Benefits of Employee Autonomy on Productivity
③ The Side Effects of Employee Empowerment on Performance
④ The Importance of Team-building Exercises in the Workplace
⑤ The Role of Financial Incentives in Increasing Employee Output
questions.explanation: 이 글은 직원들에게 주체성(자신이 통제하고 있다는 느낌, 의사결정 권한)을 부여하는 것이 업무 에너지와 집중력을 높이고, 결과적으로 생산성을 크게 향상시킨다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 오하이오 제조 공장의 사례를 통해 작은 의사결정 권한을 준 것만으로도 생산성이 20% 증가했음을 보여줍니다. 따라서 주제를 가장 잘 나타내는 제목은 '직원 자율성이 생산성에 미치는 이점'인 ②번입니다.
options_translation: ① 유니폼이 직원의 생산성에 미치는 영향
② 직원 자율성이 생산성에 미치는 이점
③ 직원 권한 부여가 성과에 미치는 부작용
④ 직장에서 팀빌딩 활동의 중요성
⑤ 직원 성과 증대에 있어서 금전적 인센티브의 역할

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. (A) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (B) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. (C) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. (D) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (E) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그러나 어떤 경우에는 행위자가 예상된 기회를 기다리지 않고 저축한 것을 조기에 사용한다'는 내용으로, 저축의 긍정적 측면이나 이론적인 원칙(미래의 보상이 현재보다 커야 함) 뒤에 반전이 일어나는 부분에 위치해야 합니다. (C) 뒤의 예시인 '크리스마스 선물을 위해 돈을 모았다가 여름 휴가에 써버리는 경우'는 바로 이 '조기 사용(prematurely)'에 대한 구체적인 예시입니다. 따라서 (C) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to ⓐ<u>acquire</u> the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be ⓑ<u>of use</u> to our career, health, and prosperity. ⓒ<u>High</u> successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill ⓓ<u>that</u> set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from ⓔ<u>taking</u> the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
questions.explanation: ⓒ 'High'는 형용사로 쓰였으나, 뒤에 오는 형용사 'successful'을 수식하기 위해서는 부사인 'Highly'가 와야 적절합니다. 'Highly successful'은 '매우 성공적인'이라는 의미를 형성합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data enters' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, <u>increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray</u>. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① cloud storage is more cost-effective than traditional methods
② the shift to digital has brought certain advantages for the environment
③ businesses are still generating significant paper and industrial waste, though adopting digitalization
④ advances in digital technology have made energy use more efficient, reducing overall environmental harm
⑤ the promise of eco-friendly digital solutions is undermined by the pollution associated with their energy consumption
questions.explanation: 이 글은 디지털 활동이 환경에 미치는 부정적인 영향을 설명하고 있습니다. 'increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray'는 친환경적이라고 여겨졌던 클라우드(디지털) 서비스가 사실은 탄소 배출을 늘려 환경을 오염시킨다는 의미입니다. 따라서 친환경적인 디지털 솔루션의 약속이 에너지 소비와 관련된 오염으로 인해 약화된다는 내용의 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 클라우드 저장소가 전통적인 방식보다 더 비용 효율적이다
② 디지털로의 전환이 환경에 특정한 이점을 가져다주었다
③ 디지털화를 채택하고 있음에도 불구하고 기업들은 여전히 상당한 종이 및 산업 폐기물을 생성하고 있다
④ 디지털 기술의 발전이 에너지 사용을 더 효율적으로 만들어 전반적인 환경 피해를 줄였다
⑤ 친환경 디지털 솔루션에 대한 약속이 에너지 소비와 관련된 오염에 의해 훼손되고 있다

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained ⓐ<u>overlooked</u> for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are ⓑ<u>accessible</u> for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often ⓒ<u>fail</u> to take these needs into account. This situation could be considerably improved by adopting ⓓ<u>inclusive</u> design practices. That is, if more projects embraced the idea of keeping the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, it would ensure that our final products ⓔ<u>satisfy</u> the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.explanation: 장애인의 필요가 간과(overlooked)되어 왔기 때문에, 그 결과로 가치 있는 디지털 자원들이 장애인들에게 '접근 가능(accessible)'한 것이 아니라 '접근 불가능(inaccessible)'한 상태가 되었다는 맥락이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 41-42번]
questions.passage: All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, ⓐwhether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately ⓑnon-threatening. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by __________________. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment. This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that ⓒactivated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, ⓓproduces pleasure. All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is to have the pain always directly ⓔassociated with a pleasurable reward.
options: ⑤ seriously violating the social contracts
questions.explanation: 지문은 고통을 동반하면서도 안전한 '안전한 위협(safe threat)'이 즐거움을 주는 원리를 설명하고 있습니다. 유머 또한 이러한 '안전한 위협'의 예시로 제시되었는데, 유머는 기존의 관습이나 질서를 우스꽝스럽게 도전하면서도 실제로는 위협이 되지 않는 상황에서 발생합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '유머러스하게 관습에 도전함으로써'라는 의미인 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 유머러스하게 관습에 도전함으로써
② 위험 신호를 완전히 무시함으로써
③ 결과적으로 실제적인 해를 입힘으로써
④ 책임 있는 수용체를 자극함으로써
⑤ 사회적 계약을 심각하게 위반함으로써

questions.question: 16. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [24년 6월 41-42번]

Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is to have the pain always directly ⓔassociated with a pleasurable reward.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 'the same receptor that ⓒactivated' 부분의 수식 관계를 보면, 주격 관계대명사 that이 가리키는 선행사 'the same receptor(동일한 수용체)'는 활성화되는 대상이므로 수동태가 되어야 합니다. 또한 when절의 'are burned'와 시제를 맞추어 현재형 수동태인 'is activated'로 고치는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did.
ordered_passages: (A) In other words, the tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. Through this period of time, you and I are the descendants of the winners.

(B) The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation.

(C) According to the theory, a human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage.
questions.explanation: 인간의 정신이 타 부족과의 경쟁을 통해 진화했다는 가설을 제시하는 도입부에 이어, (C)에서 적을 앞서 생각하는 능력이 군사적 이점이 된다는 구체적 이론을 설명합니다. (B)에서 이러한 정신적 이점이 생존을 위한 결정적인 무기가 되어 다음 세대로 이어졌음을 서술하고, (A)에서 결론적으로 승리한 부족이 유전자를 전달하여 우리가 그 후손임을 강조하는 (C)-(B)-(A) 순서가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 윗글의 요지를 우리말로 쓰고자 한다. 다음 우리말 초성을 사용하여 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting (B)_________________________________________.
questions.explanation: 글의 도입부인 'Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity'를 주제로 하여, 행동이 정체성에 기반함을 설명하고 있습니다. 초성 'ㅎㄷㅇㅈㄱㅈㅊㅅㅇㅂㅇㅇㄷ'은 '행동은 자기 정체성의 반영이다'로 완성될 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 아래 표현을 띄어쓰기를 하여 다시 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting (B)_________________________________________.
questions.answer: like the type of person you already believe yourself to be
questions.explanation: 문맥상 정체성과 행동이 일치할 때 당신은 '이미 스스로가 그렇다고 믿는 유형의 사람처럼' 행동하게 된다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 주어진 무분별한 알파벳 나열을 적절한 단어 단위로 띄어 쓰면 'like the type of person you already believe yourself to be'가 됩니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글을 읽고 (A)와 (B)에 각각 들어갈 어휘를 올바르게 배열하시오.
questions.passage: The (A)ilso of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural (B)<u>radunesibsle</u>. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.explanation: (A)는 농지의 '토양'을 가리키므로 ilso를 재배열한 soil이 정답입니다. (B)는 잡초와 같이 풍부한 영양분을 노리고 몰려드는 '반갑지 않은 존재들'을 의미하므로 radunesibsle을 재배열한 undesirables가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 적절한 말이 되도록 <보기>의 낱말만을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 바르게 배열하고 문장을 완성하시오. (단, 필요시 주어진 단어의 형태를 바꿀 것) [2.9점]
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then (A)____________________________. By developing and assessing ideas individually before selecting and refining them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
subjective_conditions: 보기의 낱말만을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 바르게 배열할 것
필요시 주어진 단어의 형태를 바꿀 것
questions.answer: does the team collaborate to choose and elaborate the most promising options
questions.explanation: 문두에 'Only then'이라는 부정어구가 위치할 경우 주어와 동사가 도치되어야 합니다. 따라서 'do + 주어 + 동사원형'의 어순으로 작성하며, 주어인 'the team'이 단수이므로 'do'를 'does'로 형태 변형하여 'does the team collaborate'로 시작합니다. 이후 '선택하고 정교화하기 위해'라는 목적의 의미를 담아 'to choose and elaborate'를 연결하고 목적어인 'the most promising options'를 뒤에 배치합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 각각 본문에서 찾아 변형하여 주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어로 쓰시오. [3.1점]
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
questions.summary_sentence: The shift to (A)a_____________ fundamentally altered human societies by leading to stable (B)s_____________ and rapid population growth.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 변형할 것
주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어로 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 본문은 농경(farming/growing crops)으로의 전환이 정착 생활과 인구 증가를 가져왔다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. (A)는 농경 사회를 뜻하는 'agricultural' 또는 농사짓는 행위인 'farming'과 관련된 단어 중 'a'로 시작하는 'agriculture(농업)'로 변형하여 사용하며, (B)는 'settled down'이라는 동사구를 명사형인 'settlement(정착)'로 변형하여 완성합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 적절한 말이 되도록 <보기>의 어구와 낱말만을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여, 바르게 배열하고 문장을 완성하시오. (단, 필요시 주어진 단어의 형태를 바꿀 것)
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
questions.summary_sentence: The introduction of the grey squirrels to Britain ___________________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 어구와 낱말만을 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것
필요시 주어진 단어의 형태를 바꿀 것
vocabulary_box: intense / lead / follow / a sharp decline / in the red squirrel / competition / population / resources / by / for / to
questions.answer: led to intense competition for resources, followed by a sharp decline in the red squirrel population
questions.explanation: 영국에 외래종인 회색 다람쥐가 도입되면서 토착종인 붉은 다람쥐와 자원을 두고 치열한 경쟁을 벌였고, 그 결과 붉은 다람쥐의 개체 수가 급감했다는 내용입니다. 과거의 사실이므로 'lead'를 'led'로, 'follow'를 분사구문 형태인 'followed'로 변형하여 '자원에 대한 치열한 경쟁을 초래했고, 뒤이어 붉은 다람쥐 개체 수의 급격한 감소가 나타났다'는 의미의 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: [15~16] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.15. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: All humans, to an extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, ⓐ<u>whether</u> this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately ⓑ<u>non-threatening</u>. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by __________________. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment. This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that ⓒ<u>activated</u> when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, ⓓ<u>produces</u> pleasure. All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is to have the pain always directly ⓔ<u>associated</u> with a pleasurable reward.
options: ⑤ seriously violating the social contracts
questions.explanation: 지문은 매운 음식을 먹는 것과 같은 고통이 '안전한 위협'으로서 즐거움을 준다고 설명합니다. 유머 또한 이와 유사하게 기존의 관습이나 예상에 도전하지만(안전한 위협), 그것이 실제 위험이 아닌 상황에서 즐거움을 유발한다는 맥락이므로 ①이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 해학적으로 관습에 도전함으로써
② 위험 신호를 완전히 무시함으로써
③ 결과적으로 실제적인 해를 입힘으로써
④ 책임 있는 수용체를 자극함으로써
⑤ 사회적 계약을 심각하게 위반함으로써

questions.question: [15~16] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.16. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

The key is that it is a 'safe threat'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately ⓑ<u>non-threatening</u>. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by __________________. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment. This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient of chillies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that ⓒ<u>activated</u> when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, ⓓ<u>produces</u> pleasure. All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm.
