questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 'the same receptor that ⓒactivated'는 수용체가 활성화되는 것이 아니라 활성화되는 대상을 수식하는 구조입니다. 뒤에 'when any of these tissues are burned'라는 조건이 나오므로, 수용체가 (열 등에 의해) 활성화될 때를 의미해야 하므로 수동태인 'is activated'가 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The adolescent brain is not fully developed until its early twenties. This means the way the adolescents' decision-making circuits integrate and process information may put them at a disadvantage. One of their brain regions that matures later is the prefrontal cortex, which is the control center, tasked with thinking ahead and evaluating consequences. It is the area of the brain responsible for preventing you from sending off an initial angry text and modifying it with kinder words. On the other hand, the limbic system matures earlier, playing a central role in processing emotional responses. Because of its earlier development, it is more likely to influence decision-making. Decision-making in the adolescent brain is led by emotional factors more than the perception of consequences. Due to these differences, there is an imbalance between feeling-based decision-making ruled by the more mature limbic system and logical-based decision-making by the not-yet-mature prefrontal cortex. This may explain why some teens are more likely to make bad decisions.
options: ① Why Teens Often Act on Feelings
② Why Teenagers Always Think Ahead
③ The Reasons Some Brain Regions Premature
④ How to Improve Teen Decision-Making Skills
⑤ The Prefrontal Cortex: Key to Logical Decision-Making
questions.explanation: 청소년의 뇌에서 이성적 조절을 담당하는 전두엽은 늦게 발달하는 반면, 감정 반응을 담당하는 변연계는 일찍 발달하여 불균형을 이룹니다. 이로 인해 청소년들이 논리적인 결과 예측보다는 감정적인 요인에 따라 의사결정을 하게 된다는 내용이므로 '왜 십대들이 흔히 감정에 따라 행동하는가'가 제목으로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 십대들이 흔히 감정에 따라 행동하는가
② 왜 십대들은 항상 앞서 생각하는가
③ 일부 뇌 영역이 조숙한 이유
④ 십대의 의사결정 기술을 향상시키는 방법
⑤ 전두엽: 논리적 의사결정의 핵심

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 match the true state of the world가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: In statistics, the law of large numbers describes a situation where having more data is better for making predictions. According to it, the more often an experiment is conducted, the closer the average of the results can be expected to <u>match the true state of the world</u>. For instance, on your first encounter with the game of roulette, you may have beginner's luck after betting on 7. But the more often you repeat this bet, the closer the relative frequency of wins and losses is expected to approach the true chance of winning, meaning that your luck will at some point fade away. Similarly, car insurers collect large amounts of data to figure out the chances that drivers will cause accidents, depending on their age, region, or car brand. Both casinos and insurance industries rely on the law of large numbers to balance individual losses.
options: ① be stable without continued observation
② have an impact on the evaluation process
③ increase the probability of winning in a competition
④ provide useful information on developing a strategy
⑤ become more reliable and reflect the true probability
questions.explanation: 'match the true state of the world'는 통계학의 '대수의 법칙'에 관한 맥락에서 사용되었습니다. 이 법칙은 시행 횟수가 많아질수록 결과의 평균이 실제 확률(진정한 상태)에 가까워진다는 것을 의미합니다. 따라서 이 밑줄 친 부분은 데이터가 많아질수록 결과가 더 신뢰할 수 있게 되고 실제 확률을 반영하게 된다는 의미인 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지속적인 관찰 없이도 안정적이다
② 평가 과정에 영향을 미친다
③ 경쟁에서 승리할 확률을 높인다
④ 전략 수립에 유용한 정보를 제공한다
⑤ 더 신뢰할 수 있게 되고 실제 확률을 반영한다

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 the train timetable or the building blueprint가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: When writing a novel, research for information needs to be done. The thing is that some kinds of fiction demand a higher level of detail: crime fiction, for example, or scientific thrillers. The information is never hard to find; one website for authors even organizes trips to police stations, so that crime writers can get it right. Often, a polite letter will earn you permission to visit a particular location and record all the details that you need. But remember that you will drive your readers to boredom if you think that you need to pack everything you discover into your work. The details that matter are those that reveal the human experience. The crucial thing is telling a story, finding the characters, the tension, and the conflict - not <u>the train timetable or the building blueprint</u>.
options: ① mere information about transportation or architecture
② key information that makes the characters more interesting
③ the need for more research to make the novel exciting and fun
④ important facts that should always be included to make the story realistic
⑤ unnecessary details that do not add to the story or show the human experience
questions.explanation: '열차 시간표나 건물의 청사진'은 소설 집필 과정에서 조사할 수 있는 매우 세부적인 정보들을 의미합니다. 필자는 인간의 경험을 드러내거나 이야기의 긴장감, 갈등을 보여주는 세부 사항이 중요하다고 강조하며, 모든 조사 내용을 다 집어넣으려 하면 독자를 지루하게 만들 수 있다고 경고합니다. 따라서 이는 이야기의 전개나 인간의 경험을 보여주지 못하는 불필요한 세부 사항을 의미하는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 교통이나 건축에 관한 단순한 정보
② 등장인물을 더 흥미롭게 만드는 핵심 정보
③ 소설을 흥미롭고 재미있게 만들기 위한 더 많은 조사의 필요성
④ 이야기를 사실적으로 만들기 위해 항상 포함되어야 하는 중요한 사실들
⑤ 이야기에 보탬이 되지 않거나 인간의 경험을 보여주지 않는 불필요한 세부 사항들

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않거나 미루어 알 수 없는 것을 2개 고르면?
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympics Games. The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants. Not only were their athletic talents superior, the Cubans appeared even stronger from just the colour of their uniforms. A game would not even start and the opposing team would already be scared. A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time. The country that ruled international baseball for decades has not been on top since that uniform change.
options: ① Cuban baseball team was very successful until they changed their uniform style.
② Cuba's previous uniform style helped intimidate the opposing teams.
③ The Cuban team lost fan support after modernizing its uniforms.
④ Cuba's new uniform style was more traditional than the old one.
⑤ Cuba's red uniforms were distinctive compared to North American baseball uniforms.
questions.explanation: ③ 본문에는 유니폼 변경 이후 팀의 실력이 쇠퇴했다는 내용은 있지만, 팬들의 지지를 잃었다는 언급은 없습니다. ④ 새로운 유니폼 스타일은 현대화되고 다른 나라의 스타일을 따른 것이라고 설명되어 있으므로, 예전의 독특한 빨간 유니폼보다 더 전통적이라고 할 수 없습니다.
options_translation: ① 쿠바 야구팀은 유니폼 스타일을 바꾸기 전까지 매우 성공적이었다.
② 쿠바의 이전 유니폼 스타일은 상대 팀을 위협하는 데 도움이 되었다.
③ 쿠바 팀은 유니폼을 현대화한 후 팬들의 지지를 잃었다.
④ 쿠바의 새로운 유니폼 스타일은 예전 스타일보다 더 전통적이었다.
⑤ 쿠바의 붉은 유니폼은 북미 야구 유니폼과 비교하여 독특했다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고른 것은?
questions.passage:
(A) Nearly everything has to go through your mouth ⓐ<u>to reach</u> the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and ⓑ<u>preventing</u> it from harm - with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. From the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and a reflection of ⓒ<u>what</u> is happening in other parts of the body. Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease that affects the entire body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, ⓓ<u>posing</u> serious health risks.

(B) Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants ⓔ<u>presented</u> with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones ⓕ<u>asking</u> during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how ⓖ<u>well</u> they could answer the new questions. But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated ⓗ<u>them</u> as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. Having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
questions.explanation:
(A)의 ⓑ: help와 병렬 관계를 이루어 조동사 can에 걸리는 동사원형 'prevent'가 되어야 합니다.
(B)의 ⓔ: 참가자들이 질문을 '제시받은' 수동의 상황이므로 과거시제 수동태인 'were presented'가 되어야 합니다.
(B)의 ⓕ: 수식받는 명사(questions)가 질문이 '된' 것이므로 수동 의미의 과거분사 'asked'가 적절합니다.
(B)의 ⓗ: 주어(those who used the internet)와 목적어가 동일인물이므로 재귀대명사 'themselves'를 써야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? ① ⓐ ② ⓑ ③ ⓒ ④ ⓓ ⑤ ⓔ
questions.passage: Many of the first models of cultural evolution drew noticeable connections between culture and genes by using concepts from theoretical population genetics and applying ⓐ<u>them</u> to culture. Cultural patterns of transmission, innovation, and selection ⓑ<u>are</u> conceptually likened to genetic processes of transmission, mutation, and selection. However, these approaches had to ⓒ<u>be modified</u> to account for the differences between genetic and cultural transmission. For example, we do not expect cultural transmission to follow the rules of genetic transmission strictly. If two biological parents have different forms of a cultural trait, their child is not necessarily equally ⓓ<u>likely</u> to acquire the mother's or father's form of that trait. Further, a child can acquire cultural traits not only from its parents but also from nonparental adults and peers; thus, the frequency of a cultural trait in the population is relevant beyond just the probability ⓔ<u>which</u> an individual's parents had that trait.
questions.explanation: ⓔ 뒤에는 'an individual's parents(주어) + had(동사) + that trait(목적어)'의 완전한 절이 이어지고 있으므로 관계대명사 which가 올 수 없으며, probability의 구체적인 내용을 설명하는 동격의 접속사 that이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. (A) They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. (B) They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else. (C) They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. (D) Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." (E) Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.insertion_sentence: Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 색의 성격에 대한 두 가지 상반된 관점을 설명하고 있습니다. 전반부((A) 이전)는 색이 객관적 속성이라는 상식적인 견해를 설명하며, (A)에서 그 구체적 예시(나뭇잎의 초록색)를 듭니다. 주어진 문장은 색이 객관 세계가 아닌 관찰자의 눈이나 마음에만 존재한다는 대조적인 의견을 도입하는 문장입니다. (B) 뒤에 이어지는 문장에서 '그들(They)'은 만약 아무도 보지 않는다면 나뭇잎은 색이 없을 것이라고 주장하며, 이는 주어진 문장의 주관적 관점과 일맥상통합니다. 따라서 주관적 관점을 처음 소개하는 주어진 문장은 (B) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 영어 뜻풀이를 <보기>에서 찾을 수 없는 것을 2개 고르면? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all ⓐ<u>aspect</u>s of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might ⓑ<u>indicate</u> a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any ⓒ<u>physical</u> circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and ⓓ<u>decay</u>ed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's ⓔ<u>extraordinary</u> answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
vocabulary_box: - to decline in health, strength, etc: to decline from a sound or prosperous condition
- imagined or suggested, but perhaps not true or really happening
- very different from what is normal: extremely good or impressive
- a particular statue or phase in which something appears or may be regarded
- making you feel that something illegal is happening or that something is wrong
- to say that an event or action will happen in the future, especially as a result of knowledge or experience
questions.explanation: <보기>의 뜻풀이와 지문의 단어를 매칭해보면 다음과 같습니다.- ⓐ aspect: 'a particular statue or phase in which something appears or may be regarded'와 일치합니다.- ⓓ decay: 'to decline in health, strength, etc: to decline from a sound or prosperous condition'과 일치합니다.- ⓔ extraordinary: 'very different from what is normal: extremely good or impressive'와 일치합니다.- ⓑ indicate(가리키다/나타내다)와 ⓒ physical(물리적인/신체의)에 대한 뜻풀이는 <보기>에 존재하지 않습니다. (나머지 뜻풀이들은 '가상적인', '의심스러운', '예측하다' 등으로 본문의 단어들과 맞지 않습니다.)

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed ⓐ<u>tougher</u> guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a ⓑ<u>premature</u> diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements ⓒ<u>raise</u> public suspicious as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an ⓓ<u>unreliable</u> process lacking precision. As a matter of ⓔ<u>consistency</u>, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 뇌사 판정 기준의 엄격함이 대중의 불안을 완화하기 위한 목적이 있지만, 오히려 불신을 초래할 수 있음을 비판하는 내용입니다. 문맥상 엄격한 요건들이 대중의 의심을 '만들어내는(create)' 만큼이나 그것을 '완화하는(assuage/ease)'지는 의문이라는 흐름이 되어야 합니다. ⓒ raise(일으키다/높이다)는 뒤의 create와 의미가 중복되어 문맥상 어색합니다. (대중의 의심을 완화하지 못하고 오히려 유발한다는 논조)

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓔ에 들어갈 단어 혹은 어구의 영영 뜻풀이로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The ⓐ________ in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme ⓑ________, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were replaced by a small number of new ⓒ________ ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the ⓓ________ of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more uniform crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a ⓔ________ selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests, and climate extremes.
options: ① ⓐ: a change to a lower state or level
② ⓑ: the severe lack of food that leads to widespread starvation
③ ⓒ: resulting in or providing a significantly large amount
④ ⓓ: negative consequences or harmful effects
⑤ ⓔ: limited in variety or range
questions.explanation: 빈칸 ⓓ에 들어갈 적절한 단어는 '성공(success)' 또는 '이점(benefit)'인데, 선택지 ④의 영영 풀이는 '부정적인 결과나 해로운 영향(negative consequences or harmful effects)'을 설명하고 있으므로 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ (감소/하락): 더 낮은 상태나 수준으로의 변화
② ⓑ (기아): 광범위한 굶주림으로 이어지는 심각한 음식 부족
③ ⓒ (수확량이 많은): 상당히 많은 양을 결과로 내거나 제공하는
④ ⓓ (성공/이점): 부정적인 결과나 해로운 영향 (틀린 풀이)
⑤ ⓔ (좁은/제한된): 다양성이나 범위가 제한된

questions.question: 26. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristics of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself. Psychologist George M. Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment. Stratton wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally turned the world upside down for him. In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him. With time, (A)____________, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated. As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems: he used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something, for example. (B)____________, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for ther est of his life. For him, everything returned to normal after one day.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 시각 체계의 적응 능력을 보여주는 Stratton의 실험에 관한 내용입니다. (A) 앞부분에서는 반전 안경을 썼을 때 겪는 초기 어려움을 설명하고 있고, (A) 뒷부분에서는 시간이 흐름에 따라 시각 체계가 새로운 자극에 적응하여 정상적으로 행동하게 된 내용이 나오므로 역접의 연결어 'however'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞부분에서는 안경을 벗은 후 다시 혼란을 겪는 상황을 설명하고, (B) 뒷부분에서는 단 하루 만에 다시 지각이 정상으로 돌아왔다는 긍정적인 결과를 제시하므로 문맥상 'Fortunately(다행히도)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나 - 다행히도
② 그러나 - 유사하게
③ 그러므로 - 그 후에
④ 게다가 - 결국
⑤ 게다가 - 예기치 않게

questions.question: 27. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions.
ordered_passages: (A) The answer is very simple: the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of clarity.

(B) Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused or not going to be used in the near future.

(C) This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist?
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 미니멀리즘이 소중한 소유물을 희생하는 것이라는 부정적인 인상을 준다고 언급합니다. (C)의 'This insecurity(이러한 불안감)'은 주어진 글의 부정적 인상을 가리키며, 인간은 물건에 의미를 부여하는 감정적 동물이라는 점을 설명하며 질문을 던집니다. (A)는 (C)에서 던진 질문에 대한 'The answer'를 제공하며 미니멀리즘이 감정을 해치지 않는다고 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)는 미니멀리스트들의 실제 견해(쓰지 않는 물건만 제거함)를 덧붙이며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 29. 주어진 글 사이에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true?
ordered_passages: (A) We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself.
(B) The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur.
(C) Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more.
(D) At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly.
questions.subjective_answer_format: It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 인간이 쉽게 지루함을 느끼는 이유에 대해 질문을 던집니다. (B)에서 그 대답('The answer')이 신경 세포에 있다고 설명하며, 자극에 대한 반응이 감소하도록 설계되었음을 언급합니다. (D)는 (B)의 'At the same time'으로 이어져, 변화하는 것에는 반응을 강화한다는 내용을 덧붙입니다. (A)는 이러한 신경적 특성이 진화적으로(조상들이 퓨마 같은 위협에 집중함) 생존 가치가 있었음을 설명합니다. (C)는 지루함이 신경 흥분 수준을 낮춰 새로운 자극을 두드러지게 한다는 점을 요약하며, 마지막 문장(반딧불이를 보기 위해 전등을 끄는 것과 같음)과 자연스럽게 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are - writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
options: ① 사회적 성공을 위해서는 다양한 분야의 능력을 갖추어야 한다.
② 능력을 자아 존중감의 유일한 기준으로 삼는 것은 문제가 될 수 있다.
③ 뛰어난 성과를 내는 사람일수록 자신의 가치를 높게 평가하는 경향이 있다.
④ 능력은 특정 기술이나 재능으로 정의되어야 더 객관적으로 평가할 수 있다.
⑤ 능력의 정의는 시대와 문화에 따라 변화하므로 고정된 기준을 적용해서는 안 된다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 능력이 어떻게 정의되든 간에, 그것이 자기 가치(self-worth)의 유일한 결정 요인이 될 때 문제가 발생한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 수행 결과가 곧 사람의 가치를 평가하는 유일한 척도가 되어 버리는 상황의 위험성을 경고하고 있으므로 요지는 ②번입니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it - you just see the blurred outline of the moving string. Strings vibrating in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. But if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note is heard loud and clear. The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. When the waves arrive at your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string.*pluck: (현악기를) 뜯다 **amplify. 증폭시키다
options: ① The Way a Guitar Produces Sounds
② The Principle of How We Differentiate Sounds
③ How to Find a High-Quality String Instrument
④ Essential Qualities of a Good String Instrument
⑤ The Correlation Between String Thickness and Sound
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기타 줄의 진동이 기타의 몸통(울림통)을 통해 증폭되어 공기 중으로 전달되고, 최종적으로 우리 고막에 전달되어 소리로 들리게 되는 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은 '기타가 소리를 만드는 방식'인 ①번입니다.
options_translation: ① 기타가 소리를 만들어내는 방식
② 우리가 소리를 구별하는 방식의 원리
③ 고품질의 현악기를 찾는 방법
④ 좋은 현악기의 필수적인 자질들
⑤ 줄의 두께와 소리 사이의 상관관계

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are minimized. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones - one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.*entail: 수반하다
options: ① Segmenters vs. Integrators: A Psychological Study
② The Evolution of Work-Life Balance in the Digital Age
③ The Rising Use of Flexible Schedules in Modern Workplaces
④ Managing Work and Life: Different Approaches to Role Boundaries
⑤ Technological Advancements and Their Effect on Workplace Productivity
questions.explanation: 이 글은 일과 가정의 경계가 모호해지는 현대 사회에서 사람들이 각자의 선호에 따라 역할을 분리(segmenting)하거나 통합(integrating)하는 서로 다른 방식을 취한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '일과 삶의 관리: 역할 경계에 대한 서로 다른 접근법'인 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 분리자 대 통합자: 심리학적 연구
② 디지털 시대 워라밸의 진화
③ 현대 직장에서 유연 근무제 사용의 증가
④ 일과 삶의 관리: 역할 경계에 대한 서로 다른 접근법
⑤ 기술적 발전과 그것이 직장 생산성에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 17. 다음 Fink의 연구 대상자들에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providing students with relevant texts they will be interested in. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and discovered ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books." The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.*dyslexia: 난독증 **voraciously: 탐욕스럽게
options: ① 물리학자, 생화학자 등 자신의 직업에서 성공한 열두 명의 성인들이었다.
② 모두 난독증이 있었고 학창 시절 내내 읽기에 상당한 문제를 겪어 왔다.
③ 높은 학업 성취를 위해 부족한 읽기를 보완할 방법들을 이용했다.
④ 난독증을 가지고 있었지만 읽기를 피하지 않는 열성적인 독자였다.
⑤ 개인적인 관심사에 열정적인 모습을 보였고 더 많이 알기, 위해 탐욕스럽게 읽었다.
questions.explanation: Rosalie Fink의 연구에 따르면 난독증을 가진 성공한 성인들은 읽기를 피하거나 다른 전략으로 보완하려 할 것이라는 예상과 달리, 오히려 자신의 개인적 관심 분야에 대해 열정적으로 책을 찾아 읽는 열성적인 독자였다고 설명되어 있습니다. 따라서 부족한 읽기를 보완할 방법을 이용했다는 ③번은 글의 내용(그 반대였다는 내용)과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way to ⓐ<u>maintain</u> our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - ⓑ<u>employing</u> technical language which distances the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking ⓒ<u>said</u> to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write ⓓ<u>them</u> off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language ⓔ<u>are</u> what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.*primatologist: 영장류학자 **affiliation: 제휴
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 지칭하는 것은 앞선 문장의 주어인 'an animal'(단수)입니다. 따라서 'them'이 아니라 'it'으로 써야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Gregg and I had been rock climbing since sunrise and had had no problems. So we took a risk. "Look, the first bolt is right there. I can definitely climb out to it. Piece of cake," I persuaded Gregg, minutes (A)[after / before] I found myself pinned. It wasn't a piece of cake. The rock was deceptively barren of handholds. I clumsily moved back and forth across the cliff face and ended up with nowhere to go... but down. The bolt that would (B)[save / threaten] my life, if I could get to it, was about two feet above my reach. My arms trembled from exhaustion. I looked at Gregg. My body froze with (C)[delight / fright] from my neck down to my toes. Our rope was tied between us. If I fell, he would fall with me.*barren of: ~이 없는
questions.explanation: (A) 내가 꼼짝 못 하게 되기 '전(before)'에 식은 죽 먹기라고 설득했다는 흐름이 적절합니다. (B) 만약 도달할 수만 있다면 생명을 '구해줄(save)' 볼트입니다. (C) 추락할 위기 상황이므로 '공포(fright)'로 몸이 얼어붙었다는 표현이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 후에 / 구하다 / 기쁨
② 후에 / 위협하다 / 기쁨
③ 전에 / 구하다 / 기쁨
④ 전에 / 위협하다 / 공포
⑤ 전에 / 구하다 / 공포

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation. If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will ⓐ<u>transmit</u> the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. While the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a ⓑ<u>protective</u> mechanism for the foot. Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls ⓒ<u>learning</u>, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now ⓓ<u>contract</u> quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object. Sensory and motor nerves control almost all ⓔ<u>functions</u> in the body - from the beating of the heart to the movement of the gut, sweating and just about everything else.*spinal cord: 척수 **gut: 장
questions.explanation: 통증 신호가 뇌로 전달되어 즉각적인 반응(비명을 지르거나 발을 떼는 것)을 일으키는 것이므로, 뇌에서 '학습(learning)'을 담당하는 부위가 아니라 '언어(speech)'나 '운동 제어'와 관련된 부위로 연결되는 것이 문맥상 더 적절합니다. 뒤에 이어지는 'ouch'라고 소리 지르는 반응은 학습보다는 언어적 반응이나 반사적 반응의 일부입니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status - they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers _____________________. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.
options: ② may not want to pay for unsatisfactory goods
③ may not be completely locked in to the product
④ tend to be resistant to changing their consumption patterns
⑤ find it difficult to keep up with the latest trend information
questions.explanation: '보완재'란 함께 소비되는 제품들을 일컫는데, 한 제품의 인기가 높아지면 보완재의 판매도 함께 늘어나는 경향이 있습니다. 하지만 모든 제품이 완벽한 보완 관계인 것은 아니며, 소비자가 그 상품에 완전히 갇혀 있거나 고정되어 있지 않기 때문입니다. 예를 들어 내연기관차 운전자가 가솔린 대신 전기차로 선택지를 바꿀 수 있는 것처럼, 소비자가 해당 상품에 완전히 묶여 있다고 보기 어렵다는 내용의 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 언제나 익숙한 상품을 구매한다
② 만족스럽지 않은 상품에 비용을 지불하고 싶어 하지 않을 수도 있다
③ 그 상품에 완전히 고정되어(묶여) 있지 않을 수도 있다
④ 소비 패턴을 바꾸는 것에 거부감을 느끼는 경향이 있다
⑤ 최신 트렌드 정보를 따라가는 것을 어렵게 느낀다

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children learn the values that make up strong character __________________________________. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore show your child good examples of life by your action. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
options: ① simply by being told about those key values
② through repeated exposure to good role models
③ by exercising both their mental and physical muscles
④ by surrounding themselves with people of similar interests
⑤ while experiencing hardships and learning to overcome them
questions.explanation: 아이들은 부모님의 말과 행동, 그리고 주변 사람들이 가치를 실천하고 유지하는 모습을 보면서 배운다는 내용입니다. 따라서 아이들은 좋은 롤 모델에 반복적으로 노출됨으로써 강한 인격을 형성하는 가치관을 배우게 된다는 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 단순히 그러한 핵심 가치들에 대해 들음으로써
② 좋은 롤 모델에 반복적으로 노출됨으로써
③ 정신적, 신체적 근육을 모두 단련함으로써
④ 비슷한 관심사를 가진 사람들과 어울림으로써
⑤ 어려움을 겪고 그것을 극복하는 법을 배우면서

questions.question: 23. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is _____________________________________.
options: ① willing to completely disregard others
② insecure about their social standing and status
③ intentionally seeking attention through unusual clothes
④ lacking an understanding of appropriate social behavior
⑤ bold enough to play with the boundaries of social acceptance
questions.explanation: 사람들은 일반적으로 기대치에 맞는 옷차림을 선호하지만, 기존의 관습을 아주 살짝 벗어난 경우(블랙타이 파티에서의 빨간 나비넥타이 등)에 대해 오히려 더 높은 능력과 지위를 가진 것으로 판단합니다. 이는 해당 개인이 사회적으로 용인되는 범위의 경계를 넘나들 만큼 충분히 대담하다는 인상을 주기 때문입니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 사람들을 완전히 무시하는
② 그들의 사회적 지위에 대해 불안해하는
③ 특이한 옷차림으로 의도적으로 관심을 끄는
④ 적절한 사회적 행동에 대해 이해가 부족한
⑤ 사회적 용인의 경계를 넘나들 만큼 충분히 대담한

questions.question: 24. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. ① Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. ② Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. ③ However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. ④ Just as very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, people rarely provide feedback on how sports organizations should be managed. ⑤ This is the reason the title 'Monday Morning Quarterback' exists. *boardroom: 이사회실
questions.explanation: 스포츠 경영에 관해 전문성이 없는 사람들이 전문가들에게 훈수를 두거나 비판하는 현상을 설명하는 글입니다. ④번 문장은 사람들이 스포츠 조직 경영에 피드백을 거의 제공하지 않는다고 서술하고 있어, '전문가에게 조언을 쏟아내는' 전체적인 흐름과 정반대되는 내용을 담고 있으므로 무관한 문장입니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage:
We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. ①This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. ②However, such transactions are becoming increasingly uncommon, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. ③While negotiation skills are important, many people find public speaking to be even more challenging in their professional lives. ④In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. ⑤In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.

*adversarial: 적대적인
questions.explanation: 이 글은 현대의 상호 의존적인 비즈니스 환경과 장기적인 인간관계에서 양측 모두가 승리하는 'win-win' 협상 방식이 필수적임을 설명하는 글입니다. 하지만 ③번 문장은 협상 능력과는 별개인 '대중 연설(public speaking)'의 어려움에 대해 언급하고 있으므로, 글의 전체적인 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 26. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers.
ordered_passages: (A) A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity.

(B) This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location.
(C) They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 다양한 문화적 배경을 가진 노동자들과의 상호작용이 지식 파급 효과와 같은 긍정적 외부 효과를 통해 생산성을 높일 수 있다는 내용으로 시작합니다. (B)에서 'This is only an advantage(이것은 오직 ~까지만 장점이다)'라는 표현을 통해 생산성 향상의 한계를 지적하며 논의를 삶의 질로 확장합니다. (A)에서는 삶의 질 측면에서 현지인들이 느끼는 긍정적 가치와 '국가 정체성 왜곡'이라는 부정적 인식을 대조하며, (C)에서 'They'가 지칭하는 정체성 위협을 느끼는 현지인들이 행하는 구체적인 행동(차별, 갈등에 대한 공포)을 설명하며 마무리하고 있습니다. 따라서 가장 적절한 순서는 (B)-(A)-(C)인 ②번입니다.

questions.question: 27. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us.
ordered_passages: (A) In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up radically remaking the society itself. Things are not so different in our own time.

(B) It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works.

(C) One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Göbekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 우리가 건물을 짓는 행위가 반대로 인간 사회를 형성하기도 한다는 주제를 제시합니다. (C)에서 이 주제의 가장 좋은 예로 터키의 괴베클리 테페(Göbekli Tepe)를 소개하며 조상들이 수렵 채집인이었던 과거를 언급합니다. (B)에서는 거대 석조물 건립 과정이 수세대에 걸쳐 오래 지속되면서 조상들이 공사를 위해 '정착'할 수밖에 없었음을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 정착 과정이 농경 사회로의 전환을 불러왔고, 결국 건축물이 사회 전체를 근본적으로 재구성했음을 결론지으며 주제를 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 가장 적절한 순서는 (C)-(B)-(A)인 ⑤번입니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: -How do you eat an elephant?- The answer is -one bite at a time.- So, how do you -build- the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. (A) Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. (B) Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. (C) Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. (D) If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. (E) Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
questions.insertion_sentence: But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 '하지만 조건이 적절할 때, 우리는 아름다운 모습(beautiful displays)을 지켜보게 된다'는 내용입니다. 이는 (D)에서 기온이 너무 낮거나 높아서 결정이 이상하고 뒤틀린 모양이 된다는 부정적인 상황과 대조를 이룹니다. 따라서 대조의 연결어 'But'을 활용해 (D)의 내용과 반전되는 (E) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다. 또한 (E) 뒤의 문장에서 언급된 'this'가 제시문의 '조건이 적합한 상황'과 그에 따른 결정 형성 과정을 가리키므로 논리적으로 완벽하게 연결됩니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. Similarly, just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is also useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.*axiom: 자명한 이치
questions.summary_sentence: Although scientific communication is a two-way process, many published scientific discoveries, unfortunately, _______________________________________.
options: ① are applied in real life
② stimulate the curiosity of many people
③ have had a significant impact on our lives
④ are neither read nor understood by readers
⑤ are overestimated compared to its actual worth
questions.explanation: 과학적 결과는 출판될 뿐만 아니라 독자에 의해 이해되어야 완성된다는 것이 글의 요지입니다. 숲속에서 나무가 소리 없이 쓰러지는 것처럼, 많은 과학 논문이 독자들에 의해 읽히지도 이해되지도 않은 채(neither read nor understood) 가치 없이 남겨진다는 내용이 요약문에 적합합니다.
options_translation: 실생활에 적용된다
많은 사람들의 호기심을 자극한다
우리 삶에 중대한 영향을 끼쳐 왔다
독자들에 의해 읽히지도 이해되지도 않는다
그것의 실제 가치에 비해 과대평가된다

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.*instill: 스며들게 하다
questions.summary_sentence: Many people fear flying due to a perceived (A)__________ of control, even though statistically, flying is far safer than driving. This fear often leads them to make decisions based on (B)__________, so it's important to base risk decisions on facts.
questions.explanation: 비행에 대한 두려움은 통제력의 결여(lack)에서 비롯되며, 통계적 사실보다는 감정(emotion)에 기반하여 운전을 선택하는 결정을 내린다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 lack, (B)에는 emotion이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 결여 - 감정
부재 - 논리
부족 - 전통
쉬움 - 기분
가능성 - 추론

questions.question: 31. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.summary_sentence: Moving is particularly (A)_________ for young children, requiring a balance between respecting their past experiences and helping them (B)_________ to new environments.
questions.explanation: 이사는 아이들에게 특히 스트레스가 많은(stressful) 일이며, 과거의 경험을 존중하는 것과 새로운 환경에 적응하도록(adjust) 돕는 것 사이의 균형이 필요하다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: 흥미로운 - 적응하다
스트레스가 많은 - 적응하다
혼란스러운 - 기여하다
유익한 - 변화하다
지장을 주는 - 돌아가다

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage:
2023 Drone Racing Championship

Are you the best drone racer? Then take the opportunity to prove you are the one!

When & Where
∙ 6 p.m. - 8 p.m., Sunday, July 9
∙ Lakeside Community Center

Requirements
∙ Participants: High school students only
