Prize
∙ $500 and a medal will be awarded to the winner.

Note
∙ The first 10 participants will get souvenirs.
For more details, please visit www.droneracing.com or call 313-6745-1189.
questions.explanation:
안내문의 'When & Where' 섹션을 보면 대회 시간이 '6 p.m. - 8 p.m.'으로 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 총 2시간 동안 대회가 진행된다는 ①번이 내용과 일치하여 정답입니다.

[오답 분석]
② 참가자는 고등학생으로 제한되어 정답이 아닙니다.
③ 자신의 드론을 직접 가져와야 하므로 정답이 아닙니다.
④ 상금은 우승자 1명에게 500달러가 지급되므로 정답이 아닙니다.
⑤ 기념품은 선착순 10명에게만 지급되므로 정답이 아닙니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 Gary Becker에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Gary Becker was born in Pottsville, Pennsylvania in 1930 and grew up in Brooklyn, New York City. His father, who was not well educated, had a deep interest in financial and political issues. After graduating from high school, Becker went to Princeton University, where he majored in economics. He was dissatisfied with his economic education at Princeton University because -it didn't seem to be handling real problems.- He earned a doctor's degree in economics from the University of Chicago in 1955. His doctoral paper on the economics of discrimination was mentioned by the Nobel Prize Committee as an important contribution to economics. Since 1985, Becker had written a regular economics column in Business Week, explaining economic analysis and ideas to the general public. In 1992, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in economic science.
options: ① 그의 아버지는 교육을 잘 받아 금융학을 전공했다.
② Princeton University에서 경제학 박사 학위를 받았다.
③ 대학교에서 현실적인 문제들을 다루는 교육을 받았다.
④ 그의 박사 논문은 차별의 경제학에 관한 것이었다.
⑤ Business Week에 비정기적으로 경제학 칼럼을 기고했다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면, ① 아버지는 교육을 잘 받지 못했고(not well educated), ② 박사 학위는 1955년 시카고 대학교에서 취득했으며, ③ 프린스턴 대학교에서의 경제학 교육이 현실적인 문제를 다루지 않는 것 같아 불만족스러워했습니다. ⑤ 1985년부터 비정기적이 아닌 '정기적으로(regular)' 경제학 칼럼을 기고했습니다. 따라서 그의 박사 논문이 차별의 경제학(economics of discrimination)에 관한 것이었다는 ④번이 글의 내용과 일치합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. ①Instead of more time, most of us have less. ②Companies large and small have off-loaded work onto the backs of consumers. ③Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. ④With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. ⑤A kiosk that helps self-check-in at the airport provides convenience for people. At the grocery store, we're expected to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
questions.explanation: 전체적으로 컴퓨터 사회가 인간에게 더 많은 여가를 줄 것이라는 약속과 달리, 실제로는 기업이 하던 업무를 소비자에게 전가하여 오히려 인간의 할 일이 늘어났다는(부담이 커졌다는) 비판적인 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 키오스크가 편리함을 제공한다는 ⑤번 문장은 기술의 긍정적인 측면을 언급하고 있으므로, 기술이 무임금 노동을 양산했다는 본문의 비판적 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [23년 6월 29번]
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally ⓐ<u>influential</u> for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive ⓑ<u>deficiency</u> to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is inclined to ⓒ<u>integrate</u> that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him ⓓ<u>persevere</u> longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more ⓔ<u>willing</u> to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 미취학 아동들은 분석적으로 추론하고 잘못된 정보를 거부할 수 있는 인지적 '능력'이 부족한 것이지 '결핍'을 가지고 있지 않다는 흐름은 어색합니다. 아이들은 아직 분석적으로 추론할 인지적 '정교함'이나 '능력'이 없다는 의미가 되어야 하므로 deficiency(결핍)는 적절하지 않으며 sophistication이나 ability 정도가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 6월 38번]
questions.passage: Sometimes the pace of change is far slower. The face you saw (A)[reflect / reflected] in your mirror this morning probably appeared no different from the face you saw the day before - or a week or a month ago. Yet we know that the face (B)[what / which] stares back at us from the glass is not the same, cannot be the same, as it was 10 minutes ago. The proof is in your photo album: Look at a photograph (C)[taking / taken] of yourself 5 or 10 years ago and you see clear differences between the face in the snapshot and the face in your mirror. If you lived in a world without mirrors for a year and then saw your reflection, you might be surprised by the change. After an interval of 10 years without seeing yourself, you might not at first recognize the person peering from the mirror. Even something as basic as our own face changes from moment to moment.
questions.explanation: (A) saw의 목적격 보어로, 얼굴이 거울에 '비춰지는' 수동의 관계이므로 과거분사 reflected가 적절합니다. (B) 선행사 the face가 있고 뒤에 주어가 빠진 불완전한 문장이 오므로 주격 관계대명사 which가 적절합니다. (what은 선행사를 포함하므로 부적절) (C) 사진이 '찍혀진' 것이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 taken이 photograph를 수식하는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 비춰진 / -하는 것(관계대명사) / 찍힌
② 비추다 / -하는 것(관계대명사) / 찍는
③ 비춰진 / 무엇(의문사/관계대명사) / 찍힌
④ 비추다 / 무엇(의문사/관계대명사) / 찍힌
⑤ 비춰진 / -하는 것(관계대명사) / 찍는

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When I woke up in our hotel room, it was almost midnight.
ordered_passages: (A) When I decided I should ask someone for help, a crowd nearby caught my attention. I approached, hoping to find my husband and daughter, and suddenly I saw two familiar faces.
(B) I smiled, feeling calm. Just then, my daughter saw me and called, "Mom!" They were watching the magic show. Finally, I felt all my worries disappear.
(C) I didn't see my husband nor daughter. I called them, but I heard their phones ringing in the room. Feeling worried, I went outside and walked down the street, but they were nowhere to be found.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 호텔 방에서 깼을 때 남편과 딸이 보이지 않는 상황이 제시됩니다. (C)에서 남편과 딸이 보이지 않아 밖으로 나가 찾아다니는 긴박한 상황이 이어지고, (A)에서 도움을 청하려다 군중 속에서 익숙한 두 얼굴(남편과 딸)을 발견하는 장면이 나옵니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 그들이 마술 쇼를 보고 있는 것을 확인하고 안도하며 걱정이 사라지는 결말로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted.
ordered_passages: (A) The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales.

(B) Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased.

(C) No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped increase sales.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 광고주들이 시장 상황에 맞춰 제품 주장을 조정하는 능력이 뛰어나다는 내용입니다. (B)에서 그 구체적인 예로 Fleischmann의 효모 사례를 들며, 집에서 빵을 굽지 않게 되면서 수요가 줄어든 문제 상황을 제시합니다. (A)에서 이 문제를 해결하기 위해 광고 대행사를 고용하고 새로운 마케팅 전략을 세우는 단계로 넘어가며, (C)에서 효모를 비타민 공급원이나 천연 완하제로 재포지셔닝하여 매출을 올린 결과가 나오는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." (A) Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad. (B) Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. (C) Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. (D) Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. (E) The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.
questions.insertion_sentence: There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그러나 건강에 좋거나 나쁜 식단이 되는 것은 음식들의 조합이다'라는 내용입니다. (A)에서 개별 음식 자체를 좋거나 나쁘다고 분류할 수 없다고 말한 뒤, (B) 자리에서 이 문장이 들어감으로써 개별 음식이 아닌 전체적인 식단(조합)이 중요하다는 화두를 던집니다. 이후 (B) 뒤의 내용에서 오직 '좋은' 음식만 먹어도 영양 불균형으로 건강한 식단이 되지 못하는 예시와 대조적인 예시들이 이어지므로 (B)가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Up until about 6,000 years ago, most people were farmers. Many lived in different places throughout the year, hunting for food or moving their livestock to areas with enough food. There was no need to tell the time because life depended on natural cycles, such as the changing seasons or sunrise and sunset. Gradually more people started to live in larger settlements, and some needed to tell the time. For example, priests wanted to know when to carry out religious ceremonies. This was when people fist invented clocks - devices that show, measure, and keep track of passing time. Clocks have been important ever since. Today, clocks are used for important things such as setting busy airport timetables - if the time is incorrect, aeroplanes might crash into each other when taking off or landing!
options: ② The Clock: A Symbol of Agriculture
③ From Nature's Rhythm to Mechanical Time
④ How to Organize Time in Modern Society
⑤ The Role of Priests in Early Civilizations
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인류가 과거에 자연의 주기(계절, 일출, 일몰)에 의존해 시간을 알 필요가 없었던 시절에서부터, 정착 생활이 시작되면서 종교적 의식이나 공항 운영처럼 정밀한 시간을 측정하고 관리해야 하는 기계적 시간 체계(시계)로 변화해 온 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '자연의 리듬에서 기계적 시간으로'를 의미하는 ③번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 바쁜 공항의 관리
② 시계: 농업의 상징
③ 자연의 리듬에서 기계적 시간으로
④ 현대 사회에서 시간을 조직하는 방법
⑤ 초기 문명에서 사제들의 역할

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The decline in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away.
options: ② Neural Connection: The Key to Stay Young
③ Decline of Curiosity: A Natural Process of Aging
④ The Older You Get, The Less Prejudice You have
⑤ Decrease of Neural Paths: A Fast Way to Lose Memory
questions.explanation: 이 글은 나이가 들면서 호기심이 감소하는 현상을 뇌의 신경학적 발달 과정과 연결하여 설명하고 있습니다. 유아기에는 신경 연결이 많아 세상이 무질서하게 느껴지지만, 학습을 통해 특정 경로가 강화되고 사용하지 않는 경로는 제거(pruning)되면서 지식이 고착화되고 호기심은 줄어든다는 내용이므로, 호기심의 감소를 자연스러운 노화 과정으로 보는 ③번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 호기심을 되찾는 방법
② 신경 연결: 젊음을 유지하는 열쇠
③ 호기심의 감소: 자연스러운 노화 과정
④ 나이가 들수록 편견이 줄어든다
⑤ 신경 경로의 감소: 기억을 잃는 빠른 방법

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Someone else's body language affects our own body, which then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly. As Louis Armstrong sang, "When you're smiling, the whole world smiles with you." If copying another's smile makes us feel happy, the emotion of the smiler has been transmitted via our body. Strange as it may sound, this theory states that emotions arise from our bodies. For example, our mood can be improved by simply lifting up the corners of our mouth. If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, taking care not to let the pencil touch their lips (thus forcing the mouth into a smile-like shape), they judge cartoons funnier than if they have been asked to frown. The primacy of the body is sometimes summarized in the phrase "I must be afraid, because I'm running."
options: ① Do not fool your emotional state.
② Language is the mirror of our emotion.
③ Express your emotion by making a face.
④ Facial expressions can determine your mood.
⑤ Your emotion corresponds with the situation you are in.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 신체의 움직임이나 표정이 감정에 영향을 미친다는 이론을 설명하고 있습니다. 타인의 미소를 따라 하면 행복해지거나, 연필을 물어 미소 짓는 표정을 만들면 만화를 더 재미있게 느낀다는 예시를 통해 얼굴 표정이 기분을 결정할 수 있다는 ④번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 감정 상태를 속이지 마라.
② 언어는 우리 감정의 거울이다.
③ 얼굴을 찌푸려 감정을 표현해라.
④ 얼굴 표정은 당신의 기분을 결정할 수 있다.
⑤ 당신의 감정은 당신이 처한 상황과 일치한다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. Although it may seem sensible, having two separate calendars for work and personal life can lead to distractions. To check if something is missing, you will find yourself checking your to-do lists multiple times. Instead, ___________________________. It doesn't matter if you use digital or paper media. It's okay to keep your professional and personal tasks in once place. This will give you a good idea of how time is divided between work and home. This will allow you to make informed decisions about which tasks are most important.
options: ① focus on personal tasks first
② rely solely on digital calendars
③ try using a unified calendar system
④ use multiple apps for better tracking
⑤ keep everything separate to avoid confusion
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 업무용과 개인용 달력을 분리해 사용하는 것의 단점(주의 산만, 여러 번 확인해야 함)을 지적하고 있으며, 후반부에서 업무와 개인 업무를 '한 곳(once place)'에 두는 것이 좋다고 조언하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 통합된 달력 시스템을 사용하라는 내용의 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 개인적인 업무에 먼저 집중하라
② 오로지 디지털 달력에만 의존하라
③ 통합된 달력 시스템을 사용해 보라
④ 더 나은 추적을 위해 여러 앱을 사용하라
⑤ 혼란을 피하기 위해 모든 것을 분리해 두라

questions.question: 23. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. _________________________. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologists Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life - which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
options: ① Poverty is the root of all stress
② Rich people have no worries at all
③ Being wealthy means having more free time
④ Stress is a luxury only the poor can afford
⑤ Being well-off can mean feeling rushed and restless
questions.explanation: 이 글은 가난뿐만 아니라 부유한 경제 국가들도 그들만의 독특한 스트레스를 가지고 있다는 점을 설명합니다. 부유하고 산업화된 국가일수록 생활 속도가 빨라지는데, 이는 높은 생활 수준을 가져오지만 동시에 사람들에게 끊임없는 긴박감을 느끼게 하고 심장병에 더 잘 걸리게 만든다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '부유한 것이 서두름과 불안함을 느끼게 할 수 있다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 가난은 모든 스트레스의 근원이다
부자들은 걱정이 전혀 없다
부유하다는 것은 더 많은 자유 시간을 갖는 것을 의미한다
스트레스는 가난한 사람들만이 누릴 수 있는 사치이다
부유하다는 것은 서두름과 불안함을 느끼는 것을 의미할 수 있다

questions.question: 25. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It is a well-known fact that technology has the potential to increase productivity. For instance, using technology can enable businesses to produce more goods and to get more out of the other factors of production. However, it can also have a pessimistic impact on productivity. For example, in many office environments workers sit in their designated seats with electronic devices, having access to the internet. They are able to check their personal e-mails and use social media whenever they want to. This can ________________________________________. Introducing new technology can also have a negative impact on production when it causes a change to the production process or requires workers to learn a new system. Learning to use new technology can be time consuming and stressful for workers and this can cause a decline in productivity.
options: ① be intriguing to their coworkers
② make them distrustful and lead to resignation
③ make them capable of performing multiple tasks
④ interfere with their work, causing not so much efficiency
⑤ make them keep up to date and skillful in new technology
questions.explanation: 기술이 생산성을 높일 수 있지만 부정적인 영향도 줄 수 있다는 내용의 글입니다. 사무실 환경에서 인터넷 접속이 가능한 전자기기를 사용하는 직원들이 개인 이메일을 확인하거나 소셜 미디어를 사용하는 행동은 업무를 방해하고 효율성을 떨어뜨리게 됩니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 업무를 방해하여 효율적이지 못하게 만든다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 동료들에게 흥미를 유발할 수 있다
그들을 불신하게 만들고 사직으로 이끌 수 있다
그들이 다중 작업을 수행할 수 있게 해준다
그들의 업무를 방해하여 효율성을 떨어뜨릴 수 있다
그들이 최신 상태를 유지하고 새로운 기술에 숙련되게 만든다

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
questions.summary_sentence: Brian Wansink's research in 1998 demonstrated that (A)__________ the number of items customers can buy significantly (B)__________ sales in supermarkets.
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 고객이 구매할 수 있는 품목의 수를 제한(희소성 전략)하는 것이 판매량을 증가시킨다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 브라이언 완싱크 교수의 실험 결과, 구매 제한이 없는 경우보다 제한이 있는 경우(4개 또는 12개)에 고객들이 더 많은 양을 구매했습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '제한하는 것(regulating/limiting/restricting)'이 들어가야 하며, (B)에는 판매를 '촉진한다(promotes/boosts)'는 의미가 들어가야 합니다. 1번의 regulating(조절/통제하는 것)과 promotes(촉진하다)가 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 조절하는 것 - 촉진하다
② 제한하는 것 - 방해하다
③ 제한하는 것 - 감소시키다
④ 할인하는 것 - 신장시키다
⑤ 조사하는 것 - 증가시키다

questions.question: 28. 다음 글을 읽고, 아래 요약문에 들어갈 내용을 주어진 본문에서 찾아 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Why do you care how customers reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
questions.summary_sentence: By focusing on customer (A)_________, businesses can ensure that buyers become (B)_________ who promote their products through positive word-of-mouth.
subjective_conditions: - 주어진 글에 있는 단어만을 그대로 쓸 것裂n- 주어진 글에 없는 단어일 경우, 점수 부여하지 않음裂n- (A), (B) 각각 1단어만 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 본문에서 'customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list'라고 언급하며 고객 만족의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 또한 'Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business'라고 하여 만족한 고객이 홍보대사 역할을 한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 요약문의 (A)에는 satisfaction(만족), (B)에는 ambassadors(홍보대사)가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 안내문을 읽고, 아래 Tom's diary의 내용 중 안내문과 일치하지 않는 부분을 찾아 올바르게 다시 쓰시오. [서술형]
questions.passage: Summer Scuba Diving One-day Class Join our summer scuba diving lesson for beginners, and become an underwater explorer!Schedule⦁10:00 - 12:00 Learning the basics⦁13:00 - 16:00 Practicing diving skills in a poolPrice⦁Private lesson: 150 dollars⦁Group lesson (up to 3 people): 100 dollars per person⦁Participants can rent our diving equipment for 10 dollars.Notice⦁Participants must be 10 years old or over.⦁Participants must register at least 5 days before the class begins.For more information, please go to www.ssdiver.com.<Tom's diary> Today was an exciting day! My family went for a scuba diving activity. I was very excited to learn how to dive. It was incredible to witness wonderful marine life on foot. Since I was learning scuba diving for the first time, I chose a private lesson and rent the diving equipment, while my mom and dad, who had learned before, chose a group lesson and brought their own equipment. We all paid 460 dollars. We learned the basics of scuba diving for two hours. The instructor was nice and explained everything clearly. After learning, we had a break for lunch. We went to the sea to practice diving skills at 1:00 p.m. It was fun to be in the water! I felt a little nervous at first, but I got used to it. This day was a perfect day.
subjective_conditions: 안내문의 내용과 일치하게 diary의 내용을 수정할 것
일치하지 않는 부분을 수정하고 수정 부분을 포함한 <u>문장 전체</u>를 쓸 것(문장이 아닐 경우 부분 점수 없음)
questions.answer: (1) We all paid 360 dollars.(2) We went to the pool to practice diving skills at 1:00 p.m.
questions.explanation: 안내문에 따르면 Tom은 개인 레슨($150) + 장비 대여($10) = $160를 지불했고, 부모님은 그룹 레슨($100 x 2) = $200를 지불하여 총액은 $360입니다. 또한, 실습은 바다(sea)가 아닌 수영장(pool)에서 진행되었습니다.

questions.question: 32. 다음 글을 읽고, (A)~(G) 중 어법상 어색한 기호 2개를 골라, 밑줄 친 부분을 올바르게 다시 쓰시오.
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and (A)<u>that we are free of most of that which is socially undesirable</u>. For example, (B)<u>a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced</u>. Likewise, (C)<u>people think they are more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person</u>. (D)<u>This phenomenon is very reliable and ubiquitous and it has come to be known as the -Lake Wobegon effect,-</u> (E)<u>It is named after Garrison Keillor's fictional community in which -the women are strong, the men are good-looking</u>, and all the children are above average.- (F)<u>A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability</u>, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, (G)<u>all students consider themselves above average, with 60% thought they were in the top 10%.</u>
subjective_conditions: - 어색한 문장의 기호(A~G)를 쓰고, 어법상 어색한 부분을 있는 대로 모두 수정하여 밑줄 부분 전체를 쓸 것
- 내용 없이 문장 기호만 쓰는 경우: 부분 점수 없음
questions.answer: (1) (A), that we are free of most of those which[that] are socially undesirable.(2) (G), all students consider themselves above average, with 60% thinking they were in the top 10%.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 'most of that which is'는 선행사가 복수인 socially undesirable characteristics를 의미하는 맥락이므로 대명사 those를 사용하여 'most of those which are' 또는 'most of what are' 형태가 적절합니다. (G)에서는 'with + 명사 + 분사' 구문에서 60%의 학생들이 생각하는 능동적 관계이므로 과거분사 thought를 현재분사 thinking으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," ⓐ<u>is</u> to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem ⓑ<u>with which</u> we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we ⓒ<u>have been given</u> a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence ⓓ<u>is</u> beneficial. In some self-help groups, this ⓔ<u>is called</u> "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 주어 'we'는 부정적인 생각에 에너지를 '주는' 능동의 주체입니다. 뒤에 'a lot of energy'라는 목적어가 있으므로 수동태인 'have been given' 대신 현재완료 능동태인 'have given'을 써야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI _____________________________________. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where interpersonal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
options: ① can replace low-skilled individual jobs in the job market
② can improve inclusiveness in the workplace
③ can treat workers with disabilities drastically
④ enables learners to overcome difficulties in language learning
⑤ can predict and prepare for future changes in the labor market
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 내용은 AI 기술이 장애인이나 저숙련 노동자 등 노동 시장의 소외 계층에게 도움을 주어 직장 내 접근성을 개선한다는 것입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 AI가 '직장 내 포용성을 개선할 수 있다'는 내용의 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 노동 시장에서 저숙련 개인의 일자리를 대체할 수 있다
② 직장 내 포용성을 개선할 수 있다
③ 장애가 있는 근로자를 획기적으로 치료할 수 있다
④ 학습자가 언어 학습의 어려움을 극복할 수 있게 해준다
⑤ 노동 시장의 미래 변화를 예측하고 대비할 수 있다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 주인공에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Emilie du Chatelet, a French mathematician and physicist, was born in Paris in 1706. During her childhood, with her father's support, she was able to get mathematical and scientific education that most women of her time did not receive. In 1737, she submitted her paper on the nature of fire to a contest sponsored by the French Academy of Sciences, and it was published a year later. In her book, Institutions de Physique, Emilie du Chatelet explained the ideas of space and time in a way that is closer to what we understand in modern relativity than what was common during her time. Her most significant achievement was translating Isaac Newton's Principia into French near the end of her life. Emilie du Chatelet's work was not recognized in her time, but she is now remembered as a symbol of the Enlightenment and the struggle for women's participation in science.
options: ① Her achievements were not recognized at the time.
② Her thesis on the nature of fire was published in 1738.
③ She translated Isaac Newton's Principia into French.
④ The concept of space and time was explained at a general level at the time.
⑤ She was educated in mathematics and science in her childhood.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 Emilie du Chatelet은 자신의 저서에서 시공간의 개념을 당시에 흔했던 일반적인 방식이 아니라 현대의 상대성 이론에 더 가까운 방식으로 설명했다고 기술되어 있습니다. 따라서 ④번 '당시의 일반적인 수준에서 설명되었다'는 내용은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 그녀의 업적은 당대에 인정받지 못했다.
② 불의 성질에 관한 그녀의 논문은 1738년에 출판되었다.
③ 그녀는 아이작 뉴턴의 '프린키피아'를 프랑스어로 번역했다.
④ 시공간의 개념은 당시의 일반적인 수준에서 설명되었다.
⑤ 그녀는 어린 시절 수학과 과학 교육을 받았다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error.
options: ① Trial and error is an effective way to learn.
② Constant practice only makes learning perfect.
③ Any imitation cannot be perfect in some ways.
④ Children's learning must be supervised by the parents.
⑤ Behaviors and knowledge are acquired by copying others.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런의 발견을 통해 인간의 근본적인 능력인 '관찰을 통한 학습' 즉, 모방(imitation)의 중요성을 설명하고 있습니다. 아기들이 부모의 행동이나 소리를 따라 하고, 나아가 현대 문명이 유지되는 것도 시행착오뿐만 아니라 타인을 모방하여 학습하기 때문이라는 내용이므로 주제로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 시행착오는 학습의 효과적인 방법이다.
② 끊임없는 연습만이 학습을 완벽하게 만든다.
③ 어떤 모방도 어떤 면에서는 완벽할 수 없다.
④ 아이들의 학습은 부모에 의해 감독되어야 한다.
⑤ 행동과 지식은 타인을 모방함으로써 습득된다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. (A) Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. (B) However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. (C) The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. (D) The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. (E) Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.insertion_sentence: This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'This criticism'은 앞 문장 (A)에서 언급된 소셜 미디어 유명인들이 전통적인 기술(연기, 노래)이 부족하다고 비판받는 내용을 가리킵니다. 또한 주어진 문장은 이러한 비판이 디지털 창작자들이 엘리트 유명인 영역으로 넘어가는 데 있어 장벽이 된다는 점을 강조하고 있으며, (B) 이후의 내용은 이러한 비판이 놓치고 있는 점(유명세의 의미 재구성)을 다루고 있으므로 (B)의 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create ____________. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on ____________ management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 조직 내의 부서들이 각자의 편향된 시각(tunnel vision)을 가지게 됨에 따라 조직 구조 자체가 '갈등(conflict)'을 유발할 수 있으며, 조직 구조의 선택(기계적 vs 유기적)이 이러한 '갈등 관리'에 큰 영향을 미친다는 내용이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 순응
② 연합
③ 자백
④ 확인
⑤ 갈등

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively ⓐ<u>poorly</u> populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will ⓑ<u>decrease</u>. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to ⓒ<u>continue</u> to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding ⓓ<u>falling</u> in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or ⓔ<u>displaced</u> populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: 수온의 '하락(falling)'이 아니라 지구 온난화로 인해 수온이 '상승(rising)'하고 있는 상황에서 산소 수치가 그 수온 상승에 상응하는 수준보다 더 빠르게 떨어지고 있다는 맥락이 되어야 하므로 ⓓ falling을 rising으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고, 주어진 문장에 있는 문법적인 오류 두 곳을 찾아 바르게 고치고 그 이유를 설명하시오.
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by being fertilized the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.answer: (1) by being fertilized → by fertilizing / 수정이유: 'fertilize'라는 행위의 주체인 고래가 그 행위의 대상인 바다를 비옥하게 하는 맥락이므로, 동명사의 능동 형태가 적합하다.(2) has estimated → estimated / 수정이유: 동사의 행위가 이루어진 시간은 '2019년'이라는 한정된 과거의 상황 속에 있기에, 현재까지도 영향을 미치는 현재완료의 형태보다 과거시제 형태의 사용이 더 적합하다.
questions.explanation: 22번 문항은 문법 오류를 찾아 고치는 문제입니다. 첫 번째 오류는 'by being fertilized'로, 고래가 바다를 비옥하게 '만드는' 능동의 주체이므로 수동태인 'being fertilized'를 능동태인 'fertilizing'으로 고쳐야 합니다. 두 번째 오류는 'has estimated'입니다. 'In 2019'라는 명확한 과거 시점이 제시되었으므로 현재완료 시제가 아닌 과거 시제 'estimated'를 사용하는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고, 주어진 조건에 맞게 밑줄 친 한글 문장을 영작하여 글을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. 만약 그것들이 우리가 적응하고 생존하도록 도움을 주지 않았었더라면 그것들은 우리와 함께 진화해 오지 않았을 것이다.
subjective_conditions: • 가정법 과거완료 사용
questions.answer: If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: 23번 문항은 과거 사실에 반대되는 가정을 나타내는 '가정법 과거완료' 구문을 활용하는 문제입니다. 'If + 주어 + had p.p., 주어 + 조동사과거형 + have p.p.' 형식을 사용하여 영작해야 합니다. 조건에 따라 'adapt'와 'survive'라는 단어를 포함하여 문장을 구성합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, (1)문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 하나 골라 기호와 (2)바르게 고친 단어를 쓰시오. 그리고 (3)그 이유를 조건에 맞게 설명하시오. (우리말로 작성)
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on ⓐdifferent branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have ⓑsomething in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have ⓒa common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very ⓓdifferent functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share ⓔnonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
subjective_conditions: • 상사형질(analogous traits)과 상동형질(homologous    traits) 중 수정 이유에 적합한 용어를 선택하여 정의    를 기술할 것
• 구체적인 수정 이유를 기술할 것
questions.answer: (1) ⓑ → (2) nothing / (3) 이유: 1) 상사형질은 공통된 기능을 가지는 것들이지만, 진화 계보의 다른 가지에서 생겨났고 중요한 면에서 동일한 기관이 아닌 형질이다. 2) ⓑ가 있는 해당 문장은 상사형질에 대한 예시이다. 예로써 사용된 새와 벌의 날개 각각은, 상사형질의 특성에 의해, 진화상에서 별개로 생겨났으며 비행에서의 쓰임 외에는 '공통점이 없다'라는 설명이 적합하므로 something을 nothing으로 고쳐야 한다.
questions.explanation: 25번 문항은 어휘의 적절성을 파악하고 그 이유를 설명하는 문제입니다. 상사형질(analogous traits)은 기능은 같으나 진화 과정에서 독립적으로 생겨난 것이므로, 비행이라는 기능 외에는 구조적 공통점이 없어야 합니다. 따라서 'something in common'은 문맥상 어색하며 'nothing in common'이 되어야 합니다. 이유는 상사형질의 정의와 예시(새와 벌의 날개)의 특성을 연결하여 서술해야 합니다.

questions.answer: (1) ⓑ → nothing(3) 1) 상사형질은 공통된 기능을 가지는 것들이지만, 진화 계보의 다른 가지에서 생겨났고 중요한 면에서 동일한 기관이 아닌 형질이다.2) ⓑ가 있는 해당 문장은 상사형질에 대한 예시이다. 예로써 사용된 새와 벌의 날개 각각은, 상사형질의 특성에 의해, 진화상에서 별개로 생겨났으며 비행에서의 쓰임 외에는 '공통점이 없다'라는 설명이 적합하다.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 ⓑ 'something'은 'nothing'으로 수정되어야 합니다. 상사형질(analogous traits)은 기능은 같지만 진화적으로 독립적으로 발생한 형질이므로, 비행 기능 이외에는 공통점이 없어야 합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us first existed as a thought in the mind of its creator before ⓐ<u>becoming</u> a reality. The houses ⓑ<u>where</u> we live in, the cars that we drive, and our clothing ─ all of these began with an idea. Each idea was then studied, refined and ⓒ<u>perfected</u> before the first nail was hammered or the first piece of cloth was cut. Long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind clearly pictured the finished product. In a similar way, humans design their own futures. We begin with an idea about ⓓ<u>how</u> the future will be. Over a period of time we refine and perfect that vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity ⓔ<u>are</u> all working in harmony to transform our mental picture of the future into reality.
questions.explanation: ⓑ 'where we live in'에서 전치사 in의 목적어가 빠져 있으므로 관계부사 where가 아닌 관계대명사 which(또는 that)를 써야 합니다. 또는 where를 유지하려면 in을 삭제해야 합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것끼리 짝지어진 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might ⓐ<u>boost</u> productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only a ⓑ<u>disadvantage</u> up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too ⓒ<u>small</u>, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of ⓓ<u>usable</u> goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an ⓔ<u>unappealing</u> feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between ⓕ<u>same</u> nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.explanation: ⓑ: 문맥상 생산성 향상은 '장점(advantage)'이므로 disadvantage는 틀립니다. ⓒ: 뒤에 '분열(fractionalization)'이 통신 비용을 발생시킨다는 내용이 나오므로 다양성이 너무 '클(large/great)' 때 문제가 생기는 것입니다. small은 부적절합니다. ⓕ: 타 민족 집단을 차별하고 두려워하는 이유는 '서로 다른(different)' 국적 사이의 갈등이 유입될까 봐서입니다. same은 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by ________________________________________. Therefore, show your child good examples of life by your action. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
options: ① exploring different strategies to avoid making poor choices.
② observing the way friends establish and follow rules in play
③ experiencing how to act on positive behaviors for themselves
④ noticing how people practice the values through their actions
⑤ discussing with their parents which value is an inevitable part of life
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 자녀들이 부모의 말보다는 행동을 통해 가치관을 배운다는 것입니다. 빈칸 앞 문장에서 가치관은 단순히 듣는 것만으로는 학습되지 않는다고 했으므로, 빈칸에는 사람들이 행동을 통해 가치관을 실천하는 것을 지켜봄으로써 배운다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다. 따라서 ④번 '사람들이 행동을 통해 가치관을 실천하는 것을 알아차림으로써'가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 좋지 못한 선택을 피하기 위한 다양한 전략을 탐색함으로써
② 친구들이 놀이에서 규칙을 세우고 따르는 방식을 관찰함으로써
③ 긍정적인 행동을 스스로 실천하는 법을 경험함으로써
④ 사람들이 행동을 통해 가치관을 실천하는 방식을 알아차림으로써
⑤ 어떤 가치가 삶의 필수적인 부분인지 부모와 토론함으로써

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용을 대화문으로 구성하고자 한다. 밑줄 친 부분 중, 내용을 올바르게 이해한 것은? [23년 9월 33번]
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providing students with relevant texts they will be interested in. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and discovered ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books." The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.↓A: You know, ⓐ<u>one key to students' engagement is giving them the texts which they actually don't care about</u>.B: Have you seen any research on this?A: Absolutely, Rosalie Fink's work really stands out. ⓑ<u>She interviewed twelve successful adults, most of whom had trouble with dyslexia</u>.B: Dyslexia? You'd think they would avoid reading.A: ⓒ<u>Fink thought the same, but actually, they were passionate readers</u>.B: That's surprising. What kinds of topics in which they were interested?A: ⓓ<u>They were only interested in philosophical areas such as religion and history</u>. Their interest drove them to read more.B: So it's all about finding what grabs their attention.A: Exactly. ⓔ<u>Personal interest doesn't have students engage in the text and achieve what they want to read</u>.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심 내용은 난독증이 있는 성공한 성인들이 자신의 개인적인 관심사에 대한 열정 때문에 독서에 열성적이었다는 것입니다. ⓐ는 학생들이 관심 없는 글을 주는 것이 몰입의 열쇠라고 했으므로 틀렸습니다(관심 있는 글이어야 함). ⓑ는 12명의 성인 중 '대부분(most of whom)'이 난독증을 앓았다고 했으나, 본문에서는 'All of them(그들 모두)'이라고 명시했습니다. ⓒ는 Fink가 그들이 독서를 피할 것이라고 생각했지만 실제로는 열정적인 독자였다는 사실을 발견했다는 내용으로 본문의 내용과 일치합니다. ⓓ는 '오직(only)' 철학적인 분야에만 관심이 있었다고 했으나 본문에는 수학, 과학, 비즈니스 등 다양한 분야가 언급되었습니다. ⓔ는 개인적 관심사가 학생들을 글에 몰입하게 하지 못한다고 했으므로 주제와 반대되는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us.
ordered_passages: (A) It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works.

(B) One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Göbekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers.

(C) In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up radically remaking the society itself. Things are not so different in our own time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 건물과 개발이 인간을 형성한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (B)에서는 이에 대한 예시로 터키의 괴베클리 테페를 들며, 수렵 채집인이었던 조상들이 세운 석조 구조물을 언급합니다. (A)에서는 이 구조물을 짓는 데 오랜 시간이 걸려 혁신가들이 정착해야 했음을 설명하고, (C)에서는 이 과정에서 농경 사회가 되어 사회 자체가 개조된 사례임을 마무리하며 현대와 연결짓는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are - writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying ⓐ<u>something exceptionally wise</u> or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as ⓑ<u>how well one plays</u> the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability ⓒ<u>to be attractive</u>, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability ⓓ<u>may be defined</u>, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else ⓔ<u>takes into account</u>. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 nothing else(그 밖의 다른 어떤 것도)입니다. 맥락상 다른 어떤 것도 '고려되지 않는다'는 수동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 'takes into account'를 수동태인 'is taken into account'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말끼리 바르게 짝지어진 것은? [23년 9월 32번]
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of (A)[preserving / depriving] our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners'; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can (B)[defeat / deceive] us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to (C)[motivate / suppress] animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.explanation: (A) 인간과 동물의 유사성을 경시함으로써 상상의 사다리 꼭대기 자리를 '보존(preserving)'하려 한다는 문맥이 적절합니다. (B) 인지적 과업(기억력 등)에서 인간을 '이기는(defeat)' 경우를 본능으로 치부한다는 내용이 적절합니다. (C) 언어를 사용하여 동물을 '억압(suppress)'하거나 위치를 공고히 한다는 결론이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 보존하다 - 이기다 - 억압하다
② 박탈하다 - 속이다 - 동기부여하다
③ 보존하다 - 속이다 - 억압하다
④ 박탈하다 - 이기다 - 억압하다
⑤ 보존하다 - 이기다 - 동기부여하다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 9월 37번]
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. (A) Strings vibrating in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. (B) But if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note is heard loud and clear. (C) The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. (D) The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. (E) When the waves reach your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string.
questions.insertion_sentence: Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it - you just see the blurred outline of the moving string.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'this movement'는 지문의 첫 문장에 언급된 'it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second'를 가리킵니다. 따라서 첫 문장 바로 다음인 (A) 위치에 오는 것이 가장 적절합니다. (A) 뒤의 문장은 'Strings vibrating in this way(이런 식으로 진동하는 줄들)'로 이어지며 자연스럽게 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, ⓐ<u>the better</u>. Crystals come in a variety of shapes ⓑ<u>what</u> scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that ⓒ<u>do</u> not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source materials, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment ⓓ<u>where</u> the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that ⓔ<u>is seen</u> time after time.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 'habits'는 선행사 역할을 하고 있으며, 뒤따르는 'scientists call' 뒤에 목적어가 비어 있는 불완전한 문장이 오므로 관계대명사가 필요합니다. 하지만 'what'은 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사이므로 선행사 'habits'와 함께 쓰일 수 없습니다. 따라서 'what'을 'that' 또는 'which'로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amdeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
options: ① What Makes a Great Composer
② Lack of Skills in Writing Song Lyrics
③ Unrevealed Aspects in the Classic Movie
④ The Significance of Understanding Music History
⑤ The Natural Talent for Overshadowing Rival Musicians
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에는 이해받지 못하기도 했지만, 그들이 위대한 이유는 자신만의 독창적인 생각(originality)을 가졌기 때문이라고 설명합니다. 반면 살리에리는 훌륭한 실력을 가졌음에도 독창성이 부족하여 '위대한' 작곡가 반열에 오르지 못했다고 언급하며 위대한 작곡가의 요건을 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 무엇이 위대한 작곡가를 만드는가
② 노래 가사를 쓰는 기술의 부족
③ 고전 영화에서 밝혀지지 않은 측면들
④ 음악사를 이해하는 것의 중요성
⑤ 라이벌 음악가들을 가릴 정도의 타고난 재능

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is not __________ unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is not __________ unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 소리가 청자가 있어야 존재하듯, 과학적 의사소통도 청중(독자)에게 전달되고 이해될 때 비로소 의미를 갖게 된다는 점을 강조합니다. 즉, 신호나 논문은 지각되거나 이해되지 않으면 '의미가 없다'는 흐름이 적절하므로 빈칸에는 '의미 있는'을 뜻하는 meaningful이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 의미 있는
② 불충분한
③ 불완전한
④ 일관된
⑤ 광범위한

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 의미 풀이가 바르지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the ⓐ<u>tissues</u> that pick up a particular sensation. If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will ⓑ<u>transmit</u> the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. While the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a ⓒ<u>protective</u> mechanism for the foot. Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less ⓓ<u>polite</u>. They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now ⓔ<u>contract</u> quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object. Sensory and motor nerves control almost all functions in the body - from the beating of the heart to the movement of the gut, sweating and just about everything else.
options: ① ⓐ: groups of similar cells in an organism that have a common structure and function
② ⓑ: to send or pass something from one person, place, or thing to another
③ ⓒ: having or showing a strong desire to keep someone or something safe from harm, damage, or danger

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.summary_sentence: While (A)__________ elite celebrities are expected to have special talents such as acting or singing, ordinary celebrities on social media are achieved through everyday interactions with common people and are determined by new (B)__________, such as the number of followers, Likes, or clicks at social media applications.

questions.question: 25. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and ________________ relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
questions.explanation: 지문은 현대 사회가 같은 사람들과 반복적으로 거래하는 상호의존적인 사회임을 강조하며 'win-win' 전략이 필수적이라고 말합니다. 빈칸은 'long-term(장기적인)'의 의미와 상반되는 일회성인 'temporary'가 들어가야 문맥상 '비즈니스 파트너십과 일시적이지 않은(장기적인) 관계의 상호의존적인 세계'라는 흐름에 어색할 수 있으나, 출처 지문의 원문은 'long-term' 관계를 지향합니다. 하지만 이 문제의 구성상 '상호의존적인 세계'와 병렬을 이루며 윈윈이 필요한 관계를 수식해야 합니다. 원문상 'long-term'이 들어가야 하나 보기에 'lasting(지속적인)'이 1번에 있으므로 맥락상 1번이 더 적절해 보이나, 제공된 정답 3번(temporary)은 문맥상 '일시적인 관계'가 아닌 '지속적인 관계'여야 하므로 문제 오류 가능성이 높거나, 빈칸 앞의 맥락을 잘못 파악한 것일 수 있습니다. (검토 결과: 원문은 long-term이나 선택지 중 의미상 통하는 것은 1번 lasting 또는 2번 continuous입니다. 정답이 3번으로 기재된 것은 원문 변형 또는 오류로 판단되나 요청에 따라 답은 유지합니다.)

questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy <u>perfect complementary status</u> - they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers may not be completely locked in to the product. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.
options: ⑤ digital camera and memory card

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 33번]
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.

③ 개념을 기반으로 하는 본질주의는 항상 과학적 발견을 낳는다.
④ 본질을 찾기 위한 탐구에서 잘못된 개념은 전혀 문제가 되지 않는다.
⑤ 개념은 헛된 본질에 대한 탐구로 향하는 문을 열 수 있어 주의해야 한다.

questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.*latent: 잠재적인

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 20번]
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop-out, or worse.
