questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds of minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
options: ① 우리는 기억의 다양한 구획을 구별할 수 있다.
② 수업 노트를 읽은 직후 정보는 작업 기억에 활동적인 형태로 자리한다.
③ 단기 기억에 존재하는 정보는 모두 장기 기억이 된다.
④ 몇 분까지는 작업 기억이 절대 사라지지 않는다.
⑤ 모든 시간을 공부하는 데에 쏟는 것이 좋다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 'Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form.'라고 명시되어 있으므로 ②번이 일치합니다. ①번은 'unable to differentiate'이므로 틀리고, ③번은 단기 기억과 장기 기억은 별개라고 언급되었으며, ④번은 몇 초에서 몇 분 후면 사라지기 시작한다고 했고, ⑤번은 공부만 하기보다 스스로 테스트하는 것이 중요하다고 언급되었습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of ⓐ<u>acceptance</u> is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely ⓑ<u>new</u>. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so ⓒ<u>great</u>. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amdeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely ⓓ<u>surpassed</u> him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't ⓔ<u>original</u>. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 안토니오 살리에리는 모차르트 시대에 살며 그에게 완전히 '뒤처졌다' 혹은 '추월당했다'는 의미가 되어야 합니다. ⓓ의 'surpassed'는 '~를 능가하다'라는 능동의 의미를 가진 타동사입니다. 문맥상 살리에리가 모차르트에게 추월당한 것이므로 수동태인 'surpassed by'가 되거나, 혹은 그가 모차르트에 의해 가려졌다는 의미인 'overshadowed by' 등의 표현이 적절합니다. 본문 흐름상 살리에리는 위대한 작곡가가 아닌 인물로 묘사되므로, 그가 모차르트를 능가했다는 능동형 surpassed는 어색합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. ⓐNewborns, in the first week of like, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. ⓑNewborns may acquire a fondness for motion because they have been conditioned through a process of associative learning. ⓒSuch imitation is not perfect. ⓓYou may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. ⓔLater still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런의 발견과 이를 통한 인간의 '관찰 학습(imitation)' 능력을 설명하고 있습니다. 신생아가 부모의 행동을 모방하는 것부터 시작해 문화 전반이 관찰을 통해 학습된다는 내용입니다. 하지만 ②번 문장은 신생아가 연합 학습 과정을 통해 움직임에 대한 선호를 갖게 된다는 내용으로, '모방을 통한 관찰 학습'이라는 주제에서 벗어난 행동주의적 학습 기제를 언급하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself.
ordered_passages: (A) However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class.

(B) The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.

(C) Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity.
questions.explanation: 제시된 글은 소셜 미디어 제작자들이 '평범한 유명세' 자체를 목적으로 추구한다는 내용입니다. (C)에서 이러한 소셜 미디어 유명인들이 전통적인 엘리트 유명인과 같은 재능이 없다는 비판을 받는다는 점과 엘리트 영역으로 진입하는 데 장벽이 있음을 언급합니다. (A)의 However를 통해 이러한 비판이 평범한 유명인이 명성의 의미를 재구성한다는 점을 간과하고 있음을 지적하며 엘리트 유명인의 특징(신비주의, 계층적 거리)을 대조합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 평범한 유명인이 다른 평범한 사람들과의 소통을 통해 관심을 끌며, 이 영역에서의 명성은 관심 척도(구독자, 좋아요 등)의 수치에 불과하다는 특성을 설명하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. (A) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. (B) As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. (C) Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. (D) A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. (E) Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.insertion_sentence: Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그럼에도 불구하고, 자전거 타기 좋은 도시들도 택시, 구급차, 배달 트럭을 위한 자동차 차로가 여전히 필요하다'는 내용입니다. (B)까지는 자전거 도로 확충과 그 이점에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. (C) 뒤의 문장부터는 배달 차량(Delivery vehicles)이 도시를 더 푸르게 만드는 필수적인 요소라는 옹호적 설명이 시작되므로, 자동차 차로의 필요성(특히 배달 트럭)을 언급하며 화제를 전환하는 주어진 문장은 (C) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.*dissolved: 용해된 **anoxic: 산소 결핍의
questions.summary_sentence: Rising ocean temperatures are (A)__________ dissolved oxygen levels, which is (B)__________ to marine ecosystems and leading to more frequent anoxic events.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 바다 온도가 상승함에 따라 바닷속 용존 산소량이 감소하는 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 기온 상승은 용존 산소량을 감소(reducing)시키는 결과를 초래하며, 이는 해양 생태계에 매우 해로운(harmful) 영향을 끼쳐 무산소 사건을 빈번하게 만든다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 유지 - 해로운
② 증가 - 유익한
③ 감소 - 해로운
④ 증가 - 해로운
⑤ 감소 - 유익한

questions.question: 3. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 turning off a front door light to see the fireflies가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons enhance their responses to things that change - especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of <u>turning off a front door light to see the fireflies</u>.
options: ① simplifying stimuli to enhance initial excitement
② reducing overall sensory input to avoid overloading the brain
③ ignoring invariable stimuli to make new stimuli more noticeable
④ limiting exposure to familiar stimuli to make them more engaging
⑤ adjusting the environment to make familiar stimuli more interesting
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간의 신경 세포가 반복되는 자극(변하지 않는 환경)에 대한 반응을 줄이고 변화하는 자극에 민감하게 반응하도록 설계되어 있다고 설명합니다. '반딧불이를 보기 위해 앞문 전등을 끄는 것'은 배경이 되는 큰 빛(익숙한 자극)을 줄임으로써 작지만 새로운 빛(새로운 자극)을 더 잘 보이게 하는 신경계의 작용을 비유적으로 표현한 것입니다.
options_translation: ① 초기 흥분을 높이기 위해 자극을 단순화하기
② 뇌의 과부하를 피하기 위해 전반적인 감각 입력을 줄이기
③ 새로운 자극을 더 눈에 띄게 하기 위해 변하지 않는 자극을 무시하기
④ 익숙한 자극을 더 매력적으로 만들기 위해 노출을 제한하기
⑤ 익숙한 자극을 더 흥미롭게 만들기 위해 환경을 조정하기

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Everything in the world around us was finished in the mind of its creator before it was started. (A) The houses we live in, the cars we drive, and our clothing - all of these began with an idea. (B) Each idea was then studied, refined and perfected before the first nail was driven or the first piece of cloth was cut. (C) In other words, long before the idea was turned into a physical reality, the mind had clearly pictured the finished product. (D) We begin with an idea about how the future will be. (E) Over a period of time we refine and perfect the vision. Before long, our every thought, decision and activity are all working in harmony to bring into existence what we have mentally concluded about the future.
questions.insertion_sentence: The human being designs his or her own future through much the same process.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 인간이 자신의 미래를 '거의 동일한 과정'을 통해 설계한다는 내용입니다. (C)까지는 집, 자동차, 옷과 같은 구체적인 사물이 만들어지기 전 창조자의 마음속에서 먼저 완성된다는 예시를 설명하고 있습니다. (D) 뒤의 문장부터는 '미래가 어떻게 될지에 대한 아이디어로 시작한다'며 인간의 미래 설계에 대한 구체적인 설명이 시작되므로, 사물 설계의 예시와 미래 설계의 내용을 연결해 주는 주어진 문장은 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By analyzing understanding post-purchase behavior, you can determine if the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so customer satisfaction should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
options: ① How to Make Online Advertisements Go Viral
② Hiring Unpaid Ambassadors: Easier Said Than Done
③ Risky Aspects of Understanding Post-Purchase Reaction
④ Why People Tend to Value Friends' Opinions Over Advertisements
⑤ The Benefit of Monitoring Customer Satisfaction After Purchase in Enhancing Sales
questions.explanation: 이 글은 판매 후 고객의 반응과 만족도를 파악하는 것이 중요하다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 만족한 고객은 자발적인 홍보대사가 되어 긍정적인 영향을 미치는 반면, 불만족한 고객은 부정적인 구전 광고를 퍼뜨릴 수 있기 때문입니다. 따라서 판매 후 지속적인 모니터링을 통해 고객 만족을 관리하는 것이 판매 증진과 비즈니스 평판 관리에 이득이 된다는 내용의 ⑤번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 온라인 광고를 입소문 나게 만드는 방법
② 무보수 홍보대사 고용하기: 말처럼 쉽지 않다
③ 구매 후 반응을 이해하는 것의 위험한 측면들
④ 사람들이 왜 광고보다 친구의 의견을 가치 있게 여기는 경향이 있는가
⑤ 판매 증진에 있어 구매 후 고객 만족도를 모니터링하는 것의 이점

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Research shows that people who work usually have two calendars: one for work and one for their personal lives. Although it may seem sensible, having two separate calendars for work and personal life can lead to distractions. ⓐTo check if something is missing or not, you will find yourself checking your to-do lists multiple times. ⓑApparently, proper time management is crucial for achieving long-term career goals. ⓒInstead, organize all of your tasks in one place whether it's digital or paper media. ⓓIt's okay to keep your professional and personal tasks in one place. ⓔThis will allow you to see how time is divided between work and home, and make informed decisions about which tasks are most important.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 흐름은 업무용과 개인용 일정을 하나의 달력으로 통합하여 관리하는 것이 효율적이라는 주장을 담고 있습니다. 하지만 ②(ⓑ)는 장기적인 경력 목표를 달성하기 위해 적절한 시간 관리가 중요하다는 일반적인 원론을 말하고 있어, 일정 통합이라는 핵심 주제에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. (A) They may do well enough in school to keep advancing and go to colleges they have longed for. (B) They have checked all the boxes in the life laid out for them, following a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. (C) At this point, many think and act as if their learning journey ends with college. (D) Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to your growth and devote thought, time, and energy to it. (E) Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career are likely to stop progressing as a result.
questions.insertion_sentence: In truth, the real journey starts after school, with growth becoming your own responsibility.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '사실 진짜 여정은 학교가 끝난 후에 시작되며, 성장이 당신 자신의 책임이 된다'는 내용입니다. (C) 지점까지는 사람들이 대학 교육으로 학습이 끝난다고 착각한다는 부정적인 현상을 설명하고 있고, (D) 이후부터는 성장을 위해 시간과 에너지를 투자해야 한다는 당위성을 설명합니다. 따라서 대학 이후의 성장을 강조하는 주어진 문장은 (D) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. Likewise, scientific communication requires a(n) ________________________________. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper is useless unless it is both acknowledged and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is incomplete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ④ expert well-known in academic fields
⑤ valid receiver who captures the message
questions.explanation: 소리가 단순히 파동에 그치지 않고 소리로서 의미를 가지려면 '듣는 사람'이 필요하듯이, 과학적 논문 또한 단순히 출판되는 것만으로는 부족하며 의도된 독자가 그것을 인지하고 이해해야만 진정한 의사소통이 완성된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 과학적 의사소통은 '메시지를 포착하는 유효한 수신자'를 필요로 합니다.
options_translation: ① 일방적인 전달
② 정확하고 과학적인 증거
③ 대중적인 학술지 출판 플랫폼
④ 학계에서 잘 알려진 전문가
⑤ 메시지를 포착하는 유효한 수신자

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 말을 주어진 <조건>에 유의하여 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Many take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eyes or mind of the observer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the ones who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cézenne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
questions.summary_sentence: The debate over color involves whether it is a(n) (A)__________ property of the physical world or exists solely in the perception of a(n) (B)___________. As a matter of fact, color has duality: it is both a physical phenomenon and a perceptual experience, where it is created when light is detected by the (C)__________ and processed by the (D)__________.
subjective_conditions: 1. 본문에 있는 한 단어를 찾아 쓸 것
2. 같은 단어를 두 번 쓰지 않을 것
questions.explanation: 이 글은 색이 물리적인 실체의 객관적(objective) 속성인지, 아니면 관찰자(observer)의 지각에 의한 것인지에 대한 두 가지 관점을 설명합니다. 결론적으로 색은 눈(eyes)에 의해 등록되고 뇌(brain)에 의해 해석되면서 생성되는 물리적 현상이자 지각적 경험임을 말하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Spending time as children ⓐ<u>allows</u> animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be ⓑ<u>more</u> flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't ⓒ<u>adapt</u> easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the ⓓ<u>old</u> rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most ⓔ<u>efficient</u> migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 유년기가 없으면 동물들은 타고난 하드웨어(유전적 정보)에 더 전적으로 의존해야 하므로, 환경 변화에 유연하게 대처하지 못하고 덜 유연해지게 됩니다. 따라서 ⓑ 'more'를 'less'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글을 읽고 정리한 표에서 적절하지 않은 것만을 고른 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on his own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually, before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
vocabulary_box: The Steps and the Advantage of Brainwritingstep 1.ⓐYou are asked to come up with ideas individually.step 2.ⓑYou have to collect individual ideas and select good ideas in public.step 3.ⓒEach team member evaluates ideas on his own.step 4.ⓓTeams choose and elaborate the most promising ideas together.theadvantageⓔIt is effective in that a variety of ideas, except those that are hard to refine, can be dealt with, which can lead to collective intelligence.
questions.explanation: ⓑ: step 2에서 아이디어를 모으고 공유하는 단계는 'anonymously(익명으로)' 이루어져야 하며, 'in public(공개적으로)'은 본문의 내용과 상충합니다.ⓔ: 브레인라이팅의 장점은 다듬기 어려운 아이디어를 제외하는 것이 아니라, 평소에 주목받지 못했을 가능성들을 드러내고 진전시키며 모든 목소리를 대화에 참여시킨다는 점입니다. 본문의 'all ideas are brought to the table'과 'except those that are hard to refine(다듬기 힘든 것들을 제외하고)'는 맞지 않습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 빈칸에 들어가기에 가장 알맞은 말끼리 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. (A)____________, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time. (B)____________, farmers could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two. This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.
options: ③ As a result / On the other hand
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 이동 시 소지품과 아이를 직접 옮겨야 한다는 상황을 설명하고 있으며, 그 결과(As a result)로 출산 간격을 4년 정도로 길게 두어야 했다는 인과관계가 형성됩니다.(B) 앞부분은 수렵 채집인의 상황이고 뒷부분은 정착 농경인의 상반된 상황을 설명하고 있으므로 대조를 나타내는 'On the other hand(반면에)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나 / 게다가
② 예를 들어 / 그러므로
③ 그 결과 / 반면에
④ 그렇지 않으면 / 그럼에도 불구하고
⑤ 결과적으로 / 마찬가지로

questions.question: 8. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어가기에 가장 알맞은 말끼리 짝지어진 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the undiscounted value of the present one. (A)____________, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (B)____________, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
options: ② As a result ... That is
questions.explanation: 이 글은 미래를 위해 저축을 하지만 의지 박약으로 인해 조기에 소비하는 행태를 설명하고 있습니다. (A)의 앞 문장은 미래 보상이 현재보다 가치가 크다고 판단하여 저축한다는 내용인 반면, (A) 뒤 문장은 계획된 기회를 기다리지 않고 조기에 저축액을 사용한다는 상반된 내용을 다루고 있으므로 역접인 'However'가 적절합니다. (B)의 앞 문장은 이를 의지 박약의 사례로 규정하고 있으며, (B) 뒤 문장은 의지 박약에 대한 구체적인 부연 설명을 하고 있으므로 '즉, 다시 말해'라는 뜻의 'Namely'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 대신에 ... 한편
② 결과적으로 ... 즉
③ 예를 들어 ... 결과적으로
④ 그렇지 않으면 ... 그럼에도 불구하고
⑤ 그러나 ... 다시 말해(즉)

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth.
ordered_passages: (A) Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain agricultural undesirables as well as our crops. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.

(B) This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers become much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both.

(C) World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled. That is, we are feeding and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 농지가 단일 재배를 위한 완벽한 환경이 되도록 강요받는다는 내용입니다. (B)의 'This'가 지시하는 것은 완벽한 환경을 만드는 것이며, 그 방법인 비료와 관개를 통한 영양분 공급이 제시됩니다. (C)에서는 (B)의 비료와 관개 기술의 발달을 구체적인 수치(3배, 2배)로 뒷받침하며 농작물이 이를 좋아한다고 언급합니다. (A)에서 'Unfortunately'와 'these luxurious conditions(풍족한 조건들)'를 통해 앞서 언급된 좋은 환경이 잡초라는 원치 않는 손님도 끌어들인다는 반전과 부정적인 영향을 설명하며 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. (A) When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. (B) A recent Wired report declared that most data enters' energy source is fossil fuels. (C) When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. (D) The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기업 활동의 디지털화가 환경에 미치는 긍정적인 기대와는 달리, 실제로는 디지털 활동 역시 환경에 위협이 될 수 있음을 설명합니다. (A) 앞부분과 (A) 문장까지는 종이에서 디지털로의 전환이 나무를 구하는 긍정적인 변화라는 인식을 서술합니다. 하지만 (B) 이후부터는 데이터 센터의 에너지원이 화석 연료라는 점, 클라우드 저장이 탄소 배출을 증가시킨다는 점 등 구체적인 환경적 대가(비용)를 나열하기 시작합니다. 따라서 인터넷과 전기의 환경적 비용이 간과되고 있다는 내용의 주어진 문장은 긍정적인 측면에서 부정적인 측면(환경 비용)으로 화제가 전환되는 지점인 (B)에 위치하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Problems often arise if an exotic species is suddenly introduced to an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. (A) When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. (B) The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet. (C) For instance, it is able to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. (D) Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. (E) As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
questions.insertion_sentence: Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 외래종인 회색다람쥐가 도입되면서 토착종인 붉은다람쥐가 멸종 위기에 처하게 된 과정을 다룹니다. (B), (C), (D) 문장들은 회색다람쥐가 먹이 적응력(익지 않은 도토리 섭취 등) 면에서 우위를 점하여 붉은다람쥐의 먹이 공급을 파괴하는 상황을 설명합니다. 주어진 문장은 회색다람쥐가 더 높은 밀도로, 그리고 다양한 서식지에서 살 수 있어 생존력이 더 뛰어나다는 '추가적인' 이점을 제시합니다. 따라서 먹이 경쟁에 관한 설명을 마무리하고, 붉은다람쥐가 멸종 위기에 처했다는 최종 결과(As a result)가 나오기 직전인 (E)에 들어가는 것이 논리적으로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것만을 <보기>에서 고른 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
vocabulary_box: ⓐ As a human tribe was born physically superior to other human tribes, the human brain evolved as it did.
ⓑ A human tribe's ability to think better than the enemy made it have the upper hand over other tribes.
ⓒ Predicting the attack plans of the enemy's tribe and planning accordingly gave your tribe a military advantage.
ⓓ Human thoughts had the limit to becoming the most powerful and decisive weapon in the struggle for survival.
ⓔ Tribes with better ideas than their opponents could increase their chances of winning the battle.
ⓕ Our ability to come up with a variety of creative ideas had nothing to do with our ancestors.
questions.explanation: 지문의 내용을 바탕으로 각 보기를 분석하면 다음과 같습니다.ⓐ: 지문은 신체적 우월함이 아닌 정신적인 경쟁과 갈등이 뇌의 진화를 일으켰다고 설명하므로 적절하지 않습니다.ⓑ: 적보다 더 잘 생각하는 능력이 중요한 이점이 되었다는 지문의 내용과 일치합니다.ⓒ: 적의 공격을 예측하고 계획하는 능력이 군사적 이점을 주었다는 지문의 내용과 일치합니다.ⓓ: 지문은 인간의 마음(생각)이 이전의 그 어떤 것보다 더 '결정적인(decisive)' 무기가 되었다고 했으므로, '한계가 있었다'는 내용은 적절하지 않습니다.ⓔ: 상대보다 더 나은 사고력을 가진 부족이 승리할 가능성이 높았다는 지문의 내용과 일치합니다.ⓕ: 인간의 정신적 이점은 조상으로부터 자손에게 유전자로 전달되었다고 설명하므로 '조상과 아무 관련이 없다'는 내용은 틀렸습니다.따라서 옳은 보기는 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ입니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. <u>This situation</u> would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
options: ① creating digital projects for non-disabled people
② offering all the audience valuable digital resources
③ neglecting the needs of the disabled in digital projects
④ meeting people with disabilities to give digital information
⑤ failing to take all professionals into account for web design
questions.explanation: 이 글은 디지털 정보를 구축할 때 장애인의 필요가 무시되고 있는 현실을 비판하고 있습니다. 밑줄 친 'This situation'은 바로 앞 문장에서 언급된 '디지털 프로젝트를 만드는 일부 학자들이 장애인 사용자의 요구를 고려하지 못하는 상황'을 가리킵니다. 따라서 3번 '디지털 프로젝트에서 장애인의 요구를 소홀히 하는 것'이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 비장애인을 위한 디지털 프로젝트를 만드는 것
② 모든 청중에게 가치 있는 디지털 자원을 제공하는 것
③ 디지털 프로젝트에서 장애인의 요구를 소홀히 하는 것
④ 디지털 정보를 주기 위해 장애인들을 만나는 것
⑤ 웹 디자인에 있어 모든 전문가를 고려하지 못하는 것

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ② The Impact of Wage Levels on Employee Autonomy
③ Relationship between Authority over Shifts and Job Satisfaction
④ How Does a Sense of Agency Affect Productivity Improvement?
⑤ Automation of the Manufacturing Process: the Secret to Increasing Productivity
questions.explanation: 이 글은 직원들에게 주체성(agency), 즉 스스로 결정을 내리고 통제하고 있다는 느낌을 주는 것이 업무 효율성과 생산성에 미치는 긍정적인 영향을 설명하고 있습니다. 오하이오주의 제조 공장 사례를 통해, 비록 임금이나 제조 공정은 동일하더라도 일정이나 근무 복장 등에 대한 작은 결정권을 부여했을 때 생산성이 20% 증가했다는 연구 결과를 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 '주체 의식이 생산성 향상에 어떻게 영향을 미치는가?'를 묻는 ④번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 상명하복식 의사결정의 효율성
② 임금 수준이 직원의 자율성에 미치는 영향
③ 교대 근무 권한과 직무 만족도 사이의 관계
④ 주체 의식이 생산성 향상에 어떻게 영향을 미치는가?
⑤ 제조 공정의 자동화: 생산성 증대의 비결

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to ______________________. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
options: ① carry out what they believe
② pursue images of what people prefer
③ act consciously upon the counselor's advice
④ identify themselves according to their ideal type
⑤ change their mind to accept other's identity as well
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심 주제는 '행동은 정체성의 반영'이라는 것입니다. 사람이 스스로를 어떤 유형의 사람이라고 믿게 되면, 그 정체성에 부합하는 행동을 하기가 훨씬 쉬워진다는 점을 설명합니다. 유권자라는 정체성을 가진 사람이나 운동을 자신의 일부로 여기는 사람의 예시를 통해, 빈칸에는 자신의 믿음(정체성)을 실천하거나 수행한다는 내용인 ①번 '그들이 믿는 것을 수행할'이 들어가는 것이 가장 논리적입니다.
options_translation: ① 그들이 믿는 것을 수행할
② 사람들이 선호하는 이미지를 추구할
③ 상담사의 조언에 따라 의식적으로 행동할
④ 자신의 이상형에 따라 스스로를 식별할
⑤ 타인의 정체성 또한 수용하기 위해 마음을 바꿀

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'safe threat'에 관한 설명으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: All humans, to some extent, seek activities that cause a degree of pain in order to experience pleasure, whether this is found in spicy food, strong massages, or stepping into a too-cold or too-hot bath. The key is that it is a '<u>safe threat</u>'. The brain perceives the stimulus to be painful but ultimately non-threatening. Interestingly, this could be similar to the way humor works: a 'safe threat' that causes pleasure by playfully violating norms. We feel uncomfortable, but safe. In this context, where survival is clearly not in danger, the desire for pain is actually the desire for a reward, not suffering or punishment. This reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain. The closer you look at your chilli-eating habit, the more remarkable it seems. When the active ingredient in chilies - capsaicin - touches the tongue, it stimulates exactly the same receptor that is activated when any of these tissues are burned. Knowing that our body is firing off danger signals, but that we are actually completely safe, produces pleasure. All children start off hating chilli, but many learn to derive pleasure from it through repeated exposure and knowing that they will never experience any real harm. Interestingly, seeking pain for the pain itself appears to be uniquely human. The only way scientists have trained animals to have a preference for chilli or to self-harm is to have the pain always directly associated with a pleasurable reward.
options: ① People may experience pleasure in spicy food or strong massages.
② Painful but non-threatening stimulus is regarded as pleasure.
③ In case of humor, playfully violating norms causes pleasure.
④ In life-threatening danger, the desire for pain is the desire for a reward.
⑤ The reward-like effect comes from the feeling of mastery over the pain.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 생존이 분명히 위험에 처하지 '않은' 상황(where survival is clearly not in danger)에서 고통에 대한 갈망이 보상에 대한 갈망이 된다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 생명을 위협하는 위험 상황에서 고통의 욕구가 보상의 욕구라는 ④번 설명은 지문의 내용과 정반대입니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들은 매운 음식이나 강한 마사지에서 즐거움을 경험할 수 있다.
② 고통스럽지만 위협적이지 않은 자극은 즐거움으로 간주된다.
③ 유머의 경우, 장난스럽게 규범을 어기는 것이 즐거움을 유발한다.
④ 생명을 위협하는 위험 속에서, 고통에 대한 욕구는 보상에 대한 욕구이다.
⑤ 보상과 같은 효과는 고통을 극복했다는 숙련감에서 온다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without excessive effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, opening the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
options: ① 수렵 채집인의 유적을 보면 우리 조상은 먹을 것이 많았다.
② 수렵 채집인 시대에 질병이 많지 않았다는 것은 사실이 아니다.
③ 왜 인간이 정착해서 농사를 짓고 가축을 길렀는지는 분명치 않다.
④ 전염병이 처음 뿌리를 내린 것은 농경사회였다.
⑤ 농업의 발전으로 인해 인구 밀도가 많이 증가했다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 초기 수렵 채집 사회의 유해를 조사한 결과, 우리 조상들이 질병을 거의 겪지 않았음(suffered very few diseases)을 시사한다고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 질병이 많지 않았다는 것이 사실이 아니라는 ②번은 지문 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength<u> to compete</u>. We often take the easy route to improve <u>our skills. </u>Many of us never really work to achieve mastery <u>in the key areas of life</u>. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment. They ________________________________. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
subjective_conditions: - <보기>의 단어들을 한 번씩만 모두 사용할 것
- 전체 흐름에 맞는 의미로 쓸 것
- 필요시 단어의 형태를 어법에 맞게 변형할 것
questions.answer: win by facing hardship to gain skill and strength.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 성공적인 운동선수들이 단순히 장비 때문이 아니라 고난을 마주함으로써 실력과 힘을 얻어 승리한다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 'win'을 동사로 하고, 수단의 의미인 'by ~ing' 구문을 활용하여 'by facing hardship'을 구성한 뒤, 목적을 나타내는 to부정사 'to gain skill and strength'를 연결합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고, 밑줄 친 우리말 문장을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that <u>뇌의 물리적 구조는 우리가 어디에 우리의 주의를 기울이고, 우리가 무엇을 하는 것을 연습하느냐에 따라 달라진다</u>.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어들을 한 번씩만 모두 사용할 것
필요시 단어의 형태를 어법에 맞게 변형할 것
questions.answer: the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
questions.explanation: 주어진 우리말 문장 '뇌의 물리적 구조는 우리가 어디에 우리의 주의를 기울이고, 우리가 무엇을 하는 것을 연습하느냐에 따라 달라진다'를 영작하는 문제입니다. 주어는 'the physical architecture of the brain'이며, '달라진다'는 동사 change를 주어의 단수 형태에 맞춰 changes로 변형합니다. '~에 따라'는 according to를 사용하며, 그 뒤에 간접 의문문 형태인 'where we direct our attention'과 'what we practice doing'을 and로 연결하여 구성합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It is believed that our emotions exist because they ________________________________. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
options: ② are primarily based on cultural factors
③ are significant in contemporary society
④ have played a part in our species' survival
⑤ result from neurological and physical processes
questions.explanation: 이 글은 감정의 진화적 목적에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 필자는 감정이 우리의 주의력, 지각, 기억, 행동 등을 조절하여 환경적 도전에 적응하고 생존하는 데 도움을 주었기 때문에 진화했다고 주장합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 감정이 '우리 종의 생존에 역할을 해왔다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사회적 상호작용에서 발생한다
② 주로 문화적 요인에 기반한다
③ 현대 사회에서 중요하다
④ 우리 종의 생존에 역할을 해왔다
⑤ 신경학적 및 신체적 과정에서 기인한다

questions.question: 13. 다음 글을 읽고, 두 사람이 나눈 대화의 밑줄 친 표현들 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.<Conservation>A: Have you heard how mirror neurons changed our understanding of learning by observation?B: Yeah, I know. It's amazing how we learn so much just by ⓐ<u>watching</u> others, especially as kids.A: Exactly! Even newborns imitate. If a parent sticks out their tongue, the baby is ⓑ<u>less</u> likely to copy it perfectly every time.B: Oh, I've heard about that! It's so cool how even that early on, babies are already learning by ⓒ<u>mimicking</u>.A: And it continues are they grow, babbling,            imitating sounds, and actions like pretending to      vacuum or hammer.B: True. Our whole culture, from talking to building spaceships, relies on learning by ⓓ<u>observation</u>.A: Exactly! We're not ⓔ<u>limited</u> to trial and error; we advance by watching others.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 신생아는 부모가 혀를 내밀면 혀를 내미는 선천적인 경향이 있다고 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 그 모방이 완벽하지는 않아서 매번 내밀지는 않더라도 여러 번 반복하면 다른 것을 할 때보다 더 자주 내밀게 된다고 서술되어 있습니다. 대화의 ⓑ 부분은 문맥상 아기가 부모의 행동을 모방할 '가능성(likely)'이 있다는 점을 언급해야 하므로 'less(덜 ~할 것 같은)'는 적절하지 않으며, 원문의 'more often' 맥락을 고려할 때 긍정적인 추측이나 단순 가능성을 나타내는 표현이 와야 합니다. 사실 대화문 ⓑ의 맥락은 '모방을 완벽하게 하지는 않지만 모방을 한다'는 의미를 담아야 하는데, less가 들어가면 모방할 가능성이 낮다는 부정적 의미가 강조되어 어색합니다.

questions.question: 15. 윗글의 내용을 다음과 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.summary_sentence: Global warming leads to a (A)___________ in dissolved oxygen in the oceans, which could have severe consequences for marine life due to anoxic events and ecosystem (B)__________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 지구 온난화로 인해 해수 온도가 상승하면서 용존 산소량이 '감소(decrease)'하고 있으며, 이것이 해양 생태계에 위협적인 수준의 '교란/붕괴(disruption/breakdown)'를 초래할 수 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 decrease, (B)에는 disruption이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 감소 - 혼란/붕괴
② 감소 - 풍부함
③ 감소 - 번영
④ 증가 - 결함/붕괴
⑤ 증가 - 방해/교란

questions.question: 19. 윗글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways. (A)<u>Although they were thought to be the same, they turned out to be actually different body parts</u>. They arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. In the past, (B)<u>biologists barely knew that they originated from the same body part, but the truth has been revealed</u>. In other words, biologists have found that they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
options: ① "Analogous" 형질은 다른 진화 계보를 갖는다.
② 새의 날개와 벌의 날개는 모두 비행에 쓰인다.
③ 새의 날개와 벌의 날개는 쓰임 외에는 공통점이 없다.
④ "Homologous" 형질은 공통된 구조를 갖고 있다.
⑤ 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 동일한 기능을 갖고 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 'Homologous(상동)' 형질의 예시로 제시되었으며, 'have very different functions(매우 다른 기능을 가지고 있다)'라고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 동일한 기능을 갖고 있다는 ⑤번은 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 (A), (B)와 같은 의미가 되도록 빈칸에 알맞은 말을 넣으시오. (빈칸 한 개당 단어 한 개) [3.2점]

The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. In the past, (B)<u>biologists barely knew that they originated from the same body part, but the truth has been revealed</u>. In other words, biologists have found that they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
subjective_conditions: 빈칸 한 개당 단어 한 개
questions.subjective_answer_format: (A)Although they were thought to be the same, they turned out to be actually different body parts.= ______________ ______________ ______________ the same, they turned out to be actually different body parts.(B)biologists barely knew that they originated from the same body part, but the truth has been revealed.= barely ______________ ______________ ______________ that they originated from the same body part, but the truth has been revealed.
questions.answer: (A) Thought to be, (B) did biologists know
questions.explanation: (A) 문장은 분사구문으로 전환할 때 'Though they were thought to be'에서 접속사와 주어가 생략되고 Being이 생략된 형태인 'Thought to be'가 적절하다. (B) 문장은 부정어 'barely'가 문두로 나가는 부정어 도치 구문이므로 조동사 did + 주어 + 동사원형 형태인 'did biologists know'가 적절하다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 take the high road가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to <u>take the high road</u> when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore show your child good examples of life by your action. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
options: ① reach the point at which something can no longer continue
② leave a place, often with a sense of urgency or immediacy
③ choose a morally superior or more honorable course of action
④ start a new activity or job with a lot of energy and enthusiasm
⑤ reluctantly accept distractions that stand in the way of their personal growth
questions.explanation: 문맥상 부모의 올바른 행동 예시와 원칙이 아이들에게 '다른 유혹적인 길' 대신 선택하도록 가르치는 것이므로, 'take the high road'는 도덕적으로 더 우월하거나 명예로운 행동 방침을 선택한다는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 어떤 것이 더 이상 계속될 수 없는 지점에 도달하다
② 긴박함이나 즉각성을 가지고 장소를 떠나다
③ 도덕적으로 더 우월하거나 더 명예로운 행동 방침을 선택하다
④ 많은 에너지와 열정을 가지고 새로운 활동이나 일을 시작하다
⑤ 개인적 성장을 가로막는 주의 산만함을 마지못해 받아들이다

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are - writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
options: ① Tactics for Mastering Exceptional Competence
② Difficulties in Enhancing Particular Skills or Talents
③ Risks of Linking Self-worth Exclusively to Performance
④ Problems with Defining a Person based on Latest Trends
⑤ Interpersonal Traits as the Only Measure of One's Self-worth
questions.explanation: 지문은 사람들이 '능력'을 지적 능력, 특별한 기술, 외모나 유행 민감성 등으로 다양하게 정의하지만, 가장 큰 문제는 이러한 성과(performance)가 자신의 가치를 결정하는 유일한 척도가 될 때 발생한다고 설명합니다. 즉, 자신의 가치를 오로지 수행 결과에만 결부시키는 것의 위험성을 지적하고 있으므로 ③번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 뛰어난 능력을 숙달하기 위한 전략
② 특정 기술이나 재능을 향상시키는 데 있어서의 어려움
③ 자아 가치를 전적으로 수행 능력에만 연결하는 것의 위험성
④ 최신 트렌드에 기반하여 사람을 정의하는 것의 문제점
⑤ 한 사람의 가치를 측정하는 유일한 척도로서의 대인 관계적 특성

questions.question: 7. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but fans and community members _______________________________ on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 스포츠 분야에서 전문 지식이 없는 대중들이 전문가(선수, 감독, 경영진 등)에게 조언이나 비판을 서슴지 않는 현상을 설명합니다. 의사나 회계사 같은 다른 전문직에게는 하지 않는 행동을 스포츠 팬들은 당연하게 여긴다는 대조를 통해, 스포츠 조직 관리에 대해 팬들이 적극적으로 '목소리를 높인다(의견을 낸다)'는 내용인 ①번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자신들의 의견을 내다
② 비판에 취약하다
③ 침묵을 유지하는 것을 고집하다
④ 피드백을 제공하는 것을 삼가다
⑤ 전문가의 추천을 받다

questions.question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. ⓐAnd similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. ⓑThe future of science lies in open access journals that allow free distribution of knowledge. ⓒJust as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. ⓓThus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. ⓔPublication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학적 의사소통은 듣는 사람(독자)이 이해해야 비로소 완성된다는 양방향적 성격에 대해 다루고 있습니다. ②번 문장은 과학의 미래가 오픈 액세스 저널에 달려 있다는 내용으로, 지식의 이해와 수용이라는 핵심 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate.
ordered_passages: (A) In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.(B) However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients.(C) Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again.
questions.explanation: 협상에 대해 배우는 사람이 드물다는 도입부 뒤에, (C) 배우는 사람들조차 대개 승-패 방식의 전통적인 스타일을 배우며 이것이 일회성 거래에 유용할 수 있다는 내용이 옵니다. (B) 그러나 이러한 일회성 거래는 점점 드물어지는데, 우리가 반복해서 같은 사람들을 상대하기 때문이라는 이유가 나옵니다. (A) 이러한 관점에서 자신을 위한 결과와 상대와의 관계 유지를 동시에 달성하는 승-승 결과가 필수적이라는 결론으로 이어집니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. (A) Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. (B) Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. (C) Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. (D) If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. (E) Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice.
questions.insertion_sentence: But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays.
questions.explanation: (D) 앞 문장과 (D) 문장은 결정이 완벽한 모양을 갖추지 못하거나 이상한 뒤틀린 모양을 형성하는 부정적인 조건에 대해 설명합니다. 주어진 문장인 '하지만 조건이 적절할 때, 우리는 아름다운 배열을 보게 된다'는 앞의 부정적 조건과 대조를 이루며, (E) 뒤에 나오는 느리고 안정적인 환경에 대한 설명과 자연스럽게 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly ⓐ<u>possible</u> to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are ⓑ<u>maximized</u>. For example, these people might keep ⓒ<u>separate</u> email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones - one for work and one for personal use. ⓓ<u>Flexible</u> schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer ⓔ<u>integrating</u> work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 공적 역할과 사적 역할을 분리(separate)하고 분절(segment)하려는 사람들은 두 영역 사이의 경계를 넘나드는 일이 최소화되기를 원할 것입니다. 따라서 '경계 교차(boundary crossings)'가 '극대화된다(maximized)'는 표현은 적절하지 않으며 '최소화된다(minimized)'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [3.0점]
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." Scientists and others use it to create an intentional (A)_____________ between human and non-human intelligence.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 한 단어로 쓸 것
어형을 변형하지 말 것
questions.explanation: 지문 전체는 인간이 동물과의 유사성을 부정하기 위해 언어적 책략(기술적인 용어 사용 등)을 사용하여 인간과 동물의 지능 사이에 의도적인 '거리'를 두려 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 본문 앞부분의 'distance the other animals from us'에서 단서를 찾을 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 내용을 다음과 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: We use it to maintain what Frans de Waal has called - linguistic castration.- The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top. They suggest that we are at a distance from them. We use linguistic tools to distance ourselves from other animals. For example, we call it -mouth- on us, but they have -muzzles.- We call it -eyes- on us, but they have -peepers.- They don't think like us; they just have instincts. We don't eat them; we consume them. This language creates a distance between us and other creatures, reinforcing the idea that we are superior.
questions.summary_sentence: The passage explains that scientists and others often use specialized language to downplay the similarities between humans and animals. Frans de Waal refers to this practice as -linguistic castration,- (B)_____________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 어휘 및 어구를 모두 한 번씩만 사용하되 그 외의 다른 단어는 추가하지 말 것
어형을 변형하지 말 것
questions.answer: in which language is used to maintain a sense of human superiority by making animals appear less capable
questions.explanation: 선행사 'linguistic castration'을 수식하는 관계사절 'in which'를 사용하여 문장을 완성해야 합니다. 주어(language) + 수동태 동사(is used) + 목적(~하기 위해: to maintain a sense of human superiority) + 수단(by making animals appear less capable) 순으로 배열합니다.

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [3.0점]
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that when a professor wore red sneakers while giving a lecture, audience members rated the professor's status and competence higher. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.↓A: Did you read the article?B: Not yet. What's it about?A: According to the article, we tend to judge others based on what they wear. That is, people prefer clothing that meets expectations, such as surgeons in scrubs or little boys dressed in blue.B: Interesting. Tell me more.A: However, there is an interesting exception. A series of studies published in the Journal of Consumer Research in June 2014 examined how people react to minor (A)____________ from established norms. For instance, a man at a black-tie event was perceived as having higher status and competence when he wore a red bow tie.B: On, I see. It means that slight variations from the standard are positively considered because they imply that (B)________________________________________.A: Right.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 한 단어로 쓸 것
어형을 변형하지 말 것
questions.explanation: 'deviations'는 본문 마지막 문장의 'these slight deviations from the norm'에서 찾을 수 있습니다. 대화문의 'minor (A)____________ from established norms'와 문맥상 일치합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, ①~⑤ 중 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were ①<u>misunderstood</u> in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is ②<u>unfamiliarity</u>. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so ③<u>understandable</u>. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the -host- of this movie: he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely ④<u>overshadowed</u> by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer: in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't ⑤<u>original</u>. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 그들의 독창성 때문에 오해받거나 거부되었다는 내용으로 시작합니다. ③번(understandable)이 포함된 문장에서는 그들을 가치 있게 만드는 것이 '이해하기 쉬움'이 아니라 그들의 새로움(낯설음)임을 설명해야 하므로, 문맥상 'understandable'은 어색합니다. 따라서 'valuable'이나 'challenging' 등으로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage:
Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen ⓐ<u>that</u> all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly ⓑ<u>populated</u> with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans ⓒ<u>had</u> been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the ⓓ<u>corresponding</u> rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events ⓔ<u>that</u> killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.

*dissolved: 용해된  **anoxic: 산소 결핍의
questions.explanation:
과거완료 진행형(had been declining)은 과거의 어느 특정 시점을 기준으로 그 이전의 동작이 지속되었음을 나타냅니다. 하지만 이 문장은 과거부터 현재까지 수십 년 동안 지속되어 온 현상을 나타내며, 문맥상 과학자들이 '현재(Now)' 분석한 결과를 보여주고 있으므로 현재완료 진행형인 'has been declining'을 쓰는 것이 어법상 적절합니다.

[오답 분석]
① ⓐ: 선행사인 'dissolved oxygen'을 수식하며 목적어 역할을 하는 목적격 관계대명사로 적절합니다.
② ⓑ: '해양 생물들이 거주하는(인구 등이 채워진)'의 의미로 수동태의 분사 형태인 populated가 적절합니다.
④ ⓓ: '상응하는'의 의미로 명사인 rise를 수식하는 현재분사로 적절합니다.
⑤ ⓔ: 선행사인 'anoxic events'를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typicAIly at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve (A) [inclusiveness / exclusiveness] in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can (B)[expedite / impede] communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can AIso (C)[advance / deteriorate] the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: AI가 노동 시장에서 불리한 위치에 있는 노동자들의 직장 접근성을 높여준다는 맥락이므로 (A)에는 '포용성(inclusiveness)'이 적합합니다. 장애가 있는 노동자들을 돕는 보조 장치들이 동료와의 의사소통을 돕는다는 맥락이므로 (B)에는 '촉진하다/신속하게 하다(expedite)'가 적합합니다. 마지막으로 저숙련 노동자들의 능력을 향상시켜 임금과 경력 전망에 긍정적인 영향을 준다고 하였으므로 (C)에는 '향상시키다(advance)'가 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 포용성 - 촉진하다 - 향상시키다
② 배타성 - 촉진하다 - 악화시키다
③ 포용성 - 방해하다 - 악화시키다

questions.question: 8. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. ⓐFrom a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. ⓑWhales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon ─ leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." ⓒThey called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. ⓓIt wasn't until the mid to late 1960s when it became apparent that certain whale species were depleting to near extinction. ⓔCalls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 고래가 탄소를 저장하고 배출함으로써 기후 변화 완화에 기여하는 효율적인 생태계 엔지니어라는 점입니다. ⓓ문장은 고래가 1960년대 중후반에 멸종 위기에 처했다는 역사적 사실을 서술하고 있어, 기후 변화 해결책으로서의 고래의 역할이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. ⓐBabies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. ⓑLater still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. ⓒStill, there are doubts concerning mirror neurons among some scientist groups. ⓓOur modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. ⓔWe can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런의 발견과 이를 통한 관찰 학습, 즉 모방의 중요성에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 아이들이 부모의 행동을 보고 배우는 다양한 사례를 제시하고 있는데, ③번 문장은 일부 과학자들 사이에서 거울 뉴런에 대한 의구심이 있다는 내용으로, 학습의 기제로서의 모방을 강조하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 12. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. Between 2000 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). (A) The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. (B) Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy. (C) In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up <u>a 'field of contradictions'</u> for assessment in higher education. (D) Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. (E) In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
questions.insertion_sentence: In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which allow lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이론적으로는' 고등 교육의 확대가 시험의 역할을 줄이고 발전을 위한 피드백에 집중해야 한다는 긍정적인 전망을 제시합니다. (C) 뒤의 문장에서 '실제로는(In reality)' 사회정치적 변화가 평가에 있어 '모순의 장'을 만들었다고 하며 대중 교육 시스템의 한계를 지적하기 시작하므로, 이론과 실제의 대비가 이루어지는 (C) 자리에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 13. 윗글에서 밑줄 친 a field of contradictions가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which allow lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. (A) The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. (B) Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy. (C) In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up <u>a 'field of contradictions'</u> for assessment in higher education. (D) Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. options: ① The elite system is more assessment-oriented than mass higher education.
② The advantages of traditional elite system and mass higher education are fully combined.
③ Mass higher education is so standardised in assessment that it can provide formative feedback to students.
