questions.explanation: 지문에서 '모순의 장(a field of contradictions)'은 이론적으로는 고등교육의 확대로 평가의 역할이 학생의 발달과 피드백에 집중되어야 함에도 불구하고, 실제로는 대중 교육 시스템의 효율성을 위해 시험이나 객관식 퀴즈 같은 기계적이고 표준화된 평가 방식이 사용되어 학생들이 피드백보다 성적에 더 집착하게 되는 상황을 의미합니다. 따라서 정답은 대중 고등교육이 발달보다는 다수의 학생을 평가하기 위한 효율적인 방법을 추구한다는 내용의 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 엘리트 시스템은 대중 고등교육보다 더 평가 지향적이다.
② 전통적인 엘리트 시스템과 대중 고등교육의 장점들이 완전히 결합되어 있다.
③ 대중 고등교육은 평가가 매우 표준화되어 있어서 학생들에게 형성적 피드백을 제공할 수 있다.
④ 대중 고등교육은 학생들의 발달에 집중하는 대신 많은 학생을 평가하기 위한 효율적인 방법을 모색한다.
⑤ 대중 고등교육의 결과로 학생들은 마침내 형성적 피드백의 중요성을 인식하기 시작했다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈카네 다바갈 말로 가장 자가절한 거슨?
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a(n) __________________________.
questions.explanation: 영재 자녀림 둔 부모가 자녀의 성과림 지수치게 자랑하는 것은 자녀에게 압박감을 주고 잘못된 자아 감각을 협성한다고 하고 있습니다. 그러므로 자녀가 있는 그대로의 모습이 아닌 업적에 의해 정의된 모습으로 살게 되면, 결국 '잘못된 자아 평가림 하는 아이'가 될 수 있음을 경고하는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자수성가한 성공
② 매우 존경묛는 사람
③ 자발적인 완뷐주의자 아이
④ 학교림 즉각 자퇴한 아이
⑤ 잘못된 자아 평가림 가진 아이

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself.
ordered_passages: (A) The ordinary celebrity, on the other hand, attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.

(B) However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs themeaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class.

(C) Not different from reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 소셜 미디어 유명세가 엘리트 유명인이 되기 위한 수단일 수도 있지만, 평범한 유명세 그 자체를 목적으로 하는 제작자들도 있다고 언급합니다. (C)에서 이러한 소셜 미디어 유명인들이 전통적인 엘리트 유명인의 재능(연기, 노래)이 부족하다는 비판을 받는다는 내용이 이어집니다. (B)에서 '그러나(However)'를 통해 이러한 비판이 평범한 유명인이 유명세의 의미를 재구성한다는 점을 간과하고 있음을 지적하며 엘리트 유명인의 특징(별, 신비함, 계급적 거리)을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 '반면에(on the other hand)'를 통해 평범한 유명인은 소통을 통해 관심을 끌며, 여기서의 유명세는 소셜 미디어의 수치(구독자, 좋아요 등)에 불과하다는 설명으로 결론짓습니다. 따라서 순서는 (C)-(B)-(A)가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
options: ① 상사 형질은 서로 다른 기능을 지니며 동일한 기관이 아니다.
② 새와 벌의 날개는 비행 기능 외에도 공통점이 많다.
③ 상동 형질의 분석 대상 간에는 언제나 공통된 기능이 존재한다.
④ 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 상동 형질의 예이다.
⑤ 상사성과 상동성은 생물 기관의 일부 구성과 쓰임 없는 특성을 살펴봄으로써 구별된다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 박쥐의 날개(The wing of a bat)와 말의 앞다리(the front leg of a horse)는 기능은 다르지만 공통 조상의 앞다리에서 변형된 것이라고 설명하며 이를 상동 형질(Homologous traits)의 예로 들고 있습니다. 따라서 ④번이 내용과 일치합니다.① 상사 형질(Analogous traits)은 공통된 기능(common function)을 가집니다.② 새와 벌의 날개는 비행 기능 외에는 공통점이 없습니다.③ 상동 형질은 공통된 기능이 있을 수도 있고 없을 수도 있습니다(may or may not have a common function).⑤ 상사성과 상동성을 구별하기 위해 '전체적인 구조(overall architecture)'와 '가장 쓸모없는 특성(most useless properties)'을 살펴봅니다. ⑤번의 '일부 구성'은 '전체적인 구조'와 상충됩니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us ⓐ<u>avoiding</u> dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when ⓑ<u>triggered</u>, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to ⓒ<u>threatening</u> stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways ⓓ<u>in which</u> they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they ⓔ<u>would not have evolved</u> with us.
questions.explanation: ⓐ의 경우 help 동사는 목적격 보어로 'to 부정사' 또는 '동사원형'을 취합니다. 따라서 avoiding을 to avoid 또는 avoid로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own ⓐ<u>impartial</u> perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which ⓑ<u>keeps</u> them from seeing things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create ⓒ<u>dispute</u>. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a ⓓ<u>vertical</u> hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is more ⓔ<u>dispersed</u> and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 각 부서가 자신의 입장만을 고려하여 상황을 본다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지는 'tunnel vision'(터널 시야)과 연결되어야 합니다. 따라서 '공정한(impartial)'이 아니라 '편향된' 또는 '자신들만의'라는 의미의 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 9월 29번]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own ⓐ<u>unbiased</u> and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which ⓑ<u>prevents</u> them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create ⓒ<u>conflict</u>. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a ⓓ<u>vertical</u> hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less ⓔ<u>centralized</u> and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 지문의 흐름상 각 부서와 분과들은 주어진 상황을 자신들만의 편향되고(biased) 편견에 사로잡힌 관점에서 보게 된다는 내용이 적절합니다. 따라서 ⓐ의 'unbiased(편향되지 않은)'는 'biased(편향된)'로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 9월 34번]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. (A) However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. (B) The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. (C) The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. (D) Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'This criticism'은 지문 앞부분에 언급된 '소셜 미디어 유명인들이 전통적인 엘리트 유명인들과 연관된 기술과 재능이 없다는 비판'을 지칭합니다. 또한 이 비판이 디지털 콘텐츠 제작자들이 엘리트 유명인의 영역으로 넘어가는 데 실질적인 장벽에 직면해 있다는 사실을 강조한다는 내용은 (A) 앞의 비판 내용과 (A) 뒤의 '그러나 그 비판은 ~라는 점을 놓치고 있다'는 내용 사이를 연결하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where interpersonal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.*dysarthric: (신경 장애로 인한) 구음 장애의
questions.summary_sentence: By improving accessibility of the workplace and providing assistive (A)_____________, AI improves inclusiveness in the workplace for disadvantaged workers and enhances job performance of (B)___________________________.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 AI가 노동 시장에서 불리한 위치에 있는 노동자들을 위해 직장 내 포용성을 높이고 저숙련 노동자들의 능력을 향상시킨다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 시각, 언어, 청각 장애를 돕는 AI 보조 기기(technology)를 통해 접근성을 높이고, 실시간 번역이나 텍스트 생성기 등을 통해 저숙련 개인(low-skilled individuals)들의 업무 성과를 향상시킨다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 기술(technologies), (B)에는 저숙련 개인(low-skilled individuals)이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 무력함 - 장애인들
② 기술들 - 저숙련 개인들
③ 잠재력 - 웹 개발자들
④ 시설들 - 텍스트 생성기들
⑤ 창의성 - 어려운 사람들

questions.question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Ludwig van Beethoven, Johannes Brahms, Gustav Mahler, Richard Strauss, Claude Debussy, Stravinsky, or Charles Ives in their day. ⓐThe initial lack of acceptance can be attributed to the unfamiliarity with the completely new musical forms and the ideas expressed within them; however, this very originality is what ultimately contributes to their greatness. ⓑHave you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? ⓒRecently people eagerly anticipate participating in film-making events. ⓓThe composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous Nongreat composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. ⓔAlthough Salieri was a very good composer, he was not considered one of the world's great composers because his work lacked originality and resembled what everyone else was composing during his time.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에는 독창성 때문에 이해받지 못했다는 점과, 반대로 살리에리처럼 독창성이 부족한 경우 위대한 작곡가로 평가받지 못했음을 설명하는 내용입니다. 영화 '아마데우스'와 살리에리의 예시를 통해 독창성의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓒ는 사람들이 영화 제작 이벤트에 참여하기를 기대한다는 내용으로, 글의 핵심 주제인 '작곡가의 독창성과 그에 대한 평가'와는 무관합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. When we are children, we learn a lot by observing what our parents and peers do. ⓐNewborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. ⓑSuch imitation is not perfect so you may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. ⓒBabies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. ⓓLanguage plays the most important role in our culture which is passed down from generation to generation. ⓔLater still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런의 발견과 '관찰을 통한 학습(모방)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 갓난아기의 혀 내밀기 모방, 소리 모방, 부모의 행동(진공청소기, 망치질) 모방 등이 예시로 제시되고 있습니다. ⓓ는 언어가 문화 전수에서 가장 중요한 역할을 한다는 내용으로, 거울 뉴런과 관찰을 통한 신체적/행동적 모방이라는 글의 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen ①<u>that</u> all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water ②<u>does</u> - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and ③<u>potentially</u> disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data ④<u>indicating</u> that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or ⑤<u>displacing</u> populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: ⑤번이 포함된 절은 'anoxic events'를 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사절입니다. 등위접속사 'or'를 중심으로 앞의 과거 동사 'killed'와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로, 현재분사 형태인 'displacing'을 과거형 동사인 'displaced'로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 고래(Whales)에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
options: ① 고래는 죽을 때 평균 30톤의 이산화탄소를 격리한다.
② 한 마리 고래는 기후의 관점에서 수천 그루의 나무와 동등하다.
③ 고래가 바다로 방출하는 배설물은 결과적으로 식물성 플랑크톤 개체를 감소시킨다.
④ IMF의 경제학자들은 각 고래가 제공하는 생태계 서비스의 가치를 200만 달러(USD) 이상으로 추정했다.
⑤ 기후 변화를 늦추기 위해 세계적인 고래 복원 프로그램에 대한 요구가 현재 진행되고 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 고래의 배설물이 영양분을 공급하여 결과적으로 식물성 플랑크톤 개체수를 증가시킨다고 명시되어 있으므로(increasing phytoplankton populations), '감소시킨다'는 설명인 ③번은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸 (A), (B)에 각각 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose (A)____________ in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very (B)____________ functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 생물학에서 '상사(analogous)' 형질과 '상동(homologous)' 형질을 구분하는 기준에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. (A) 새와 벌의 날개는 기능은 같지만 진화의 다른 가지에서 발생했으므로 '독립적으로(independently)' 생겨난 것입니다. (B) 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 공통 조상에서 유래한 상동 형질이지만, 하나는 비행용이고 하나는 달리기용이므로 '서로 다른(different)' 기능을 수행합니다. 따라서 정답은 ②번입니다.
options_translation: ① 독립적으로 ... 유사한
② 독립적으로 ... 다른
③ 독립적으로 ... 공통의
④ 종속적으로 ... 다른
⑤ 종속적으로 ... 유사한

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along ─ whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS ─ and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show ─ whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire ─ you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans to communicate ─ it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① 사람들은 새로운 매체에 쉽게 적응한다.
② 사람들은 자신만의 고글을 통해 삶을 즐긴다.
③ 매체보다는 그 안에 담긴 메시지가 더 중요하다.
④ 이전의 매체가 새로운 매체보다 삶을 더 풍요롭게 한다.
⑤ 새로운 매체를 통해 사람들은 새로운 방식으로 세상을 보게 된다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 마샬 맥루한의 이론을 인용하여 새로운 매체가 등장할 때마다 그 매체 자체가 세상을 보는 방식(코드)을 결정한다는 점을 강조합니다. 즉, 정보의 내용보다 정보가 전달되는 방식(매체)이 더 중요하다는 내용이므로, 정답은 ⑤번입니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Dear Johnson, I hope this letter finds you well. I wanted to share some thoughts that I believe might be helpful. When we find ourselves in states of depression, often caught up in the thought, "I can't," one valuable technique is to be with others who have overcome similar challenges. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. In a negative state, we tend to give a lot of energy to negative thought forms and our positive thought forms become weak. Those who operate at a higher vibration are free from negative thoughts and they are energized with positive thought forms. (A)<u>단지 그들이 있는 자리에 있는 것(단지 그들의 존재 안에 있는 것)으로도 유익해</u>. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here occurs on a psychic level of consciousness, and (B)<u>긍정적인 에너지의 전이(전달)와 우리 자신의 잠재된 긍정적인 사고 형태들의 재점화(재활성화)가 있어</u>. I recommend that you check out the new 'Support Circle' self-help group where people meet every Wednesday at 7 p.m. You'll find support and experience positive changes. I'm always rooting for you.Warmly,Jenny
options: ① To discuss Johnson's recent achievements
② To share tips on overcoming SNS addiction
③ To offer personal advice on physical health
④ To inform Johnson of a new self-help group
⑤ To invite Johnson to an annual celebration event
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부인 "I recommend that you check out the new 'Support Circle' self-help group..." 부분을 통해 필자가 존슨에게 새로운 자조 모임(self-help group)을 소개하고 참가를 권유하기 위해 쓴 글임을 알 수 있습니다. 따라서 정답은 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 존슨의 최근 성취에 대해 논의하기 위해
② SNS 중독 극복을 위한 팁을 공유하기 위해
③ 신체 건강에 대한 개인적인 조언을 제공하기 위해
④ 존슨에게 새로운 자조 모임을 알리기 위해
⑤ 존슨을 연례 축하 행사에 초대하기 위해

questions.question: 22. 다음 Science Journal의 내용을 읽고, 아래 대화문의 빈칸 (A), (B)를 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 완성하시오. [24년 9월 37번]
questions.passage: Science Journal Your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.↓Sue: Hey, have you ever listened to a recording of your own voice?Jordan: Oh, definitely! It always surprises me. I ask to myself, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?"Sue: Your accent is way more pronounced than you thought, right?Jordan: Right. Also, my voice in the recording seems higher than it seems to your own ears.Sue: It's interesting to learn that we actually perceive our own voice in two different ways.Jordan: I wonder how it works.Sue: Well, there's the external way in which sound travels through the air to our ears. But then there's also the internal pathway.Jordan: The internal pathway? Can you explain it?Sue: When we speak, the vibrations of (A)____________     _____________________________________________________.     Those vibrations stimulate our inner ears             directly.Jordan: That's interesting.Sue: Along the inner route, (B)___________ ___________ are emphasized and that's why your voice sounds deeper and richer to yourself.Jordan: That makes so much sense to me! No wonder my voice sounds different in the recording.
subjective_conditions: (A)는 아래 제시어를 빠짐없이 모두 한 번씩만 사용하여 총 14단어로 쓸 것 (단어 중복 사용 또는 추가 사용 불가, 어형 변화 불가)
(B)는 본문(Science Journal)에서 찾아 두 단어로 쓸 것 (연속되는 두 단어를 찾아 쓸 것, 어형 변화 불가)
vocabulary_box: through / vocal cords / inner ears / are / our / our / conducted / and travel / our bones / to
questions.answer: (A) our vocal cords are conducted through our bones and travel to our inner ears(B) lower frequencies
questions.explanation: 이 문항은 자신의 목소리가 왜 녹음된 목소리와 다르게 들리는지에 대한 과학적 설명을 대화문 형식으로 재구성한 서술형 문제입니다. (A)는 주어진 단어들을 사용하여 진동이 뼈를 통해 전도되어 내이로 전달된다는 본문의 내용을 완성하는 것입니다. (B)는 본문에서 낮은 주파수(Lower frequencies)가 이 경로를 통해 강조된다는 내용을 찾아 쓰는 것입니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A)__________ often arise if an exotic species (B)__________ an ecosystem. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
options: ① Problems ... is abruptly abandoned in
② Changes ... is naturally approved by
③ Issues ... has a positive effect on
④ Troubles ... is suddenly introduced by
⑤ Tensions ... finally falls behind in
questions.explanation: 외래종(회색 다람쥐)이 생태계에 도입(introduced)되면서 토착종(붉은 다람쥐)이 멸종 위기에 처하는 등의 문제(Troubles/Problems)가 발생했다는 내용이므로 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 문제들 ... 에서 갑자기 버려지다
② 변화들 ... 에 의해 자연스럽게 승인되다
③ 사안들 ... 에 긍정적인 영향을 미치다
④ 문제들 ... 에 의해 갑자기 도입되다
⑤ 긴장감들 ... 에서 결국 뒤처지다

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained (A)[neglected / neglecting] for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty (B)[distinguishing / to distinguish] particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation (C)[would / will] be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.explanation: (A) 주어인 '장애인의 요구'가 무시된 상태로 남아있는 것이므로 과거분사 neglected가 적절합니다. (B) have difficulty (in) -ing 구문이므로 distinguishing이 적절합니다. (C) if절의 동사가 과거형(embraced)인 가정법 과거 문장이므로 주절에는 조동사의 과거형인 would가 와야 합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be ①<u>less</u> flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate - those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with - sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, ②<u>adapt</u> easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate ③<u>keep</u> flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most ④<u>efficient</u> migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve ⑤<u>faster</u> than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
questions.explanation: 태어내땄 부터 이동 방법을 알고 태어난 새들은 환경 변화에도 불구하고 기존의 규칙과 지도로만 비행하려고 하기 때문에 변화된 환경에 쉱게 적응하지 못합니다. 따라서 adapt(적응하다)는 cannot adapt나 fail to adapt 등의 부정적인 의문이 되어야 문맥사 윱성합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Many human and non-human animals save commodities or money for future consumption. (A) This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one: the agent gives up some immediate pleasure in exchange for a future one. (B) Thus the discounted value of the future reward should be greater than the un-discounted value of the present one. (C) For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. (D) Such cases could be examples of weakness of will. (E) That is, the agents may judge or resolve to spend their savings in a certain way for the greatest benefit but then act differently when temptation for immediate pleasure appears.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, in some cases the agent does not wait for the envisioned occasion but uses their savings prematurely.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 저축을 조기에 사용하는 경옰(prematurely)를 설명하며, (C) 이협의 문장은 크리스마스 선물을 사기 윑해 모은 돈을 여름 휴가에 써버리는 구체적인 예시를 들고 있습니다. 따라서 제시문은 예시 바로 앞인 (C) 윑치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved.
ordered_passages: (A) This meant that each woman could have more children than her hunter-gatherer counterpart, which in turn resulted in rapid population growth among farming communities. An increased population was actually an advantage to agricultural societies, because farming required large amounts of human labor.

(B) In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, spacing their births so that they never had to carry more than one child at a time.

(C) Farmers, on the other hand, could live in the same place year after year and did not have to worry about transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place were able to shorten their birth intervals from four years to about two.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 수렵 채집인은 이동하며 모든 소지품을 운반해야 했다는 내용이 나옵니다. (B)에서 '특히 어머니들은 어린 자녀를 운반해야 했다'며 구체적인 고충을 설명하고 출산 간격을 길게 유지해야 했던 이유를 언급합니다. (C)에서 '반면에 농부들은 한 곳에 정착하여 자녀 운반 걱정을 덜었다'는 대조를 통해 출산 간격이 단축되었음을 설명합니다. (A)에서 이러한 정착 생활이 인구 증가로 이어졌으며, 이는 노동력이 많이 필요한 농경 사회에 이점이 되었다는 결과로 마무리되는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'otherwise'가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options. By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention <u>otherwise</u>. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
options: ① 모둠 기반의 창의적인 아이디어를 개발하지 않으면
② 아이디어를 개별적으로 개발하고 평가하지 않으면
③ 발전시킬 좋은 아이디어들이 관심을 끌지 못한다면
④ 창의적이고 진취적인 아이디어를 선택하지 않는다면
⑤ 팀원들의 독립적인 판단들을 보존하고 지켜나가려면
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'otherwise'는 앞 문장의 조건인 'By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them(아이디어를 선택하고 구체화하기 전에 개별적으로 개발하고 평가함으로써)'의 반대 상황을 의미합니다. 즉, '아이디어를 개별적으로 개발하고 평가하지 않는다면' 주의를 끌지 못했을 가능성들을 찾아낼 수 있다는 맥락이므로 ②번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 33번]
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle, ________________________________________. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
options: ① leaving its genetic traits to the next generation
② choosing the most promising tribes to get along with
③ using weapons based on superior physical condition
④ following instinctive tendency to avoid natural disasters
⑤ inheriting the genes of mental inefficiency to its offspring
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 정신이 생존 경쟁에서 다른 부족보다 뛰어난 사고력을 가질 수 있도록 진화했다고 설명합니다. 적을 앞지르는 사고력을 가진 부족은 생존 경쟁에서 승리할 가능성이 높았으며, 그 승리자들의 후손이 현재의 인류라는 맥락입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 전쟁에서 성공하고 생존한 부족이 '자신의 유전적 형질을 다음 세대에게 남겼다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그것의 유전적 형질을 다음 세대에 남기면서
② 함께 지낼 가장 유망한 부족을 선택하면서
③ 우월한 신체 조건에 기반한 무기를 사용하면서
④ 자연재해를 피하려는 본능적인 경향을 따르면서
⑤ 정신적 비효율성의 유전자를 자손에게 물려주면서

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 36번]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions make our green clouds gray. The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels.
options: ① Why Can't We Throw Away Fossil Fuels?
② When Can We Eliminate Environmental Pollution?
③ Digital Business: Another Threat to Environment
④ The Causes of the Price Rise of the Internet
⑤ The Meaning of the Shift: From Analog to Digital
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기업 활동이 디지털로 전환되면서 환경에 미치는 영향이 줄어들 것이라고 예상하지만, 실제로는 데이터 센터 운영을 위한 화석 연료 사용, 전력 소비 등으로 인해 디지털 활동 역시 환경에 위협이 된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '디지털 비즈니스: 환경에 대한 또 다른 위협'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 우리는 화석 연료를 버릴 수 없는가?
② 우리는 언제 환경 오염을 제거할 수 있는가?
③ 디지털 비즈니스: 환경에 대한 또 다른 위협
④ 인터넷 가격 상승의 원인
⑤ 변화의 의미: 아날로그에서 디지털로

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분의 대명사가 가리키는 것을 본문에서 찾아 정확하게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented (A)<u>them</u> when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous literary example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem Kubla Khan from a dream he had but then was visited by an unexpected guest. For Coleridge, by coincidence, the untimely visitor came at a particularly bad time. (B)<u>He</u> forgot his inspiration and left the work unfinished. While there are many documented cases of sudden disruptions that have had significant consequences for professionals in critical roles such as doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders, and pilots, (C)<u>they</u> also impact most of us in our everyday lives, slowing down work productivity and generally increasing stress levels.
questions.answer: (A) The costs of interruptions(B) Samuel Taylor Coleridge(C) Sudden disruptions
questions.explanation: (A) 'them'은 문장 앞부분의 'The costs of interruptions'를 가리킵니다.(B) 'He'는 앞 문장에 언급된 시인 'Samuel Taylor Coleridge'를 가리킵니다.(C) 'they'는 문장 앞부분의 'sudden disruptions'를 가리킵니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 중에서 전체 흐름과 관계가 없는 문장을 찾아 영어로 그대로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence demonstrating that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid being hunted for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, showing dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Recent research results show that life's brain capacity has a lot to do with its intellectual competence. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, is enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes according to where we direct our attention and what we practice doing.
questions.answer: Recent research results show that life's brain capacity has a lot to do with its intellectual competence.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 집중하는 대상과 연습하는 활동에 따라 뇌의 물리적 구조가 변한다는 '뇌의 가소성'에 관한 내용입니다. 지능적 능력과 뇌 용량의 관계를 언급한 문장은 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 inclusiveness in the workplace의 사례로 볼 수 없는 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve <u>inclusiveness in the workplace</u>. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where interpersonal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of lowskilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, Al's capacity to translate written and spoken word in realtime can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lowerskilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
options: ① Real-time translation for non-native workers
② Live captioning systems for hard of hearing people
③ Al-powered text generators for lowerskilled programmers
④ AI-powered devices to ensure equal treatment for all employees
⑤ Speech recognition solutions for workers with communication challenges
questions.explanation: 이 글은 AI가 노동 시장의 약자(장애인, 저숙련 노동자, 비모국어 화자 등)를 위한 접근성을 높여 '직장 내 포용성(inclusiveness)'을 향상시키는 구체적인 예시들을 나열하고 읈습니다. ④번은 'AI를 통해 모든 직원의 동등한 처우를 밴장한다'는 매우 포간적이고 일반적인 진술이며, 본문에서 언급된 'AI를 통한 기능 보조 및 역량 강화'라는 구체적인 포용성 설명 사례로는 부적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 비모국어 화자 노동자들을 위한 실시간 번역
② 청각 장애인들을 위한 실시간 자막 시스템
③ 저숙련 프로그램 개발자들을 위한 AI 기반 텍스트 생성기
④ 모든 직원의 동등한 처우를 밴장하기 위한 AI 기반 장치들
⑤ 의사소통 어려움은 겪는 노동자들을 위한 음성 인식 솔루션

questions.question: 7. 다음 글에서 전체 흠름과 감계없는 문장은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. ⓐNot unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. ⓑThe rise of influencers is also closely tied to advancements in smartphone camera technology, which has revolutionized the way content is consumed. ⓒThis criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. ⓓHowever, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. ⓔThe elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 소셜 미디어 명성(ordinary fame)을 추구하는 콘텐츠 크리에이터들에 대한 비판과 명성의 재구성에 대해 다루고 읈습니다. ⓑ 문장은 소셜 미디어 인플루언서의 부상을 스마트폰 카메라 기술의 발전과 결부시키고 읈다, 이는 명성의 사회적 의미나 비판과는 거리가 먼 기술적인 측면이므로 글의 흠름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds (A)[less / more] dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is selfevident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will (B)[decrease / increase]. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to (C)[less / more] frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: (A) 물리 법칙상 찬물이 따뜻한 물보다 더 많은(more) 용존 산소를 보유한다는 것은 잘 알려진 사실입니다. (B) 따라서 지구 온난화로 바닷물 온도가 올라가면 용존 산소량은 자연스럽게 감소(decrease)하게 됩니다. (C) 바닷속 산소 수치 하락은 해양 생물들의 서식지에 영향을 미치며, 최근 몇 년간 생물들을 죽게 하거나 쫓아내는 무산소 현상을 더(more) 빈번하게 일으키고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 더 적은 --- 증가하다 --- 더 많은
② 더 적은 --- 감소하다 --- 더 적은
③ 더 많은 --- 감소하다 --- 더 많은
④ 더 많은 --- 감소하다 --- 더 적은
⑤ 더 적은 --- 증가하다 --- 더 적은

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. (A) Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. (B) Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. (C) If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. (D) Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. (E) This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
questions.insertion_sentence: But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays.
questions.explanation: (C)까지의 내용은 결정(crystals)이 조건이 좋지 않을 때 비틀린 모양이 된다는 내용입니다. 주어진 문장의 'But(하지만)'은 앞선 부정적 상황과 대조를 이루며, 조건이 적절할 때 아름다운 모습을 보인다는 전환을 유도합니다. (D) 뒤의 'Usually, this involves...' 문장이 아름다운 결정을 형성하기 위한 적절한 환경(천천히 안정된 환경)을 설명하고 있으므로 (D)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are minimized. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones - one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
options: ① Most individuals find it easy to completely disconnect from work during personal time.
② Some people prefer to keep their work and family obligations distinctly separated.
③ Some individuals often manage their tasks by utilizing separate communication devices for work and personal matters.
④ Flexible work arrangements allow some individuals to maintain a clearer distinction between their professional and personal lives.
⑤ Some choose to merge their work and family roles throughout the day.
questions.explanation: 지문에서눤 휴대용 디지털 기술로 인해 일과 가정의 경계가 모호해지고 이에 따라 사람들마다 관리 방식이 다르다고 설명합니다. 많은 사람들이 개인 시간에 일과 완전히 단절하는 것을 쉱게 느낀다는 내용은 지문에 없으며, 오휸려 경계가 모호해지고 이림 통합하는 사람들도 이습니다.
options_translation: ① 대부분의 개인은 개인 시간 동안 일과 완전히 단절하는 것이 쉱다고 생각한다.
② 어떤 사람들은 일과 가정의 의무림 명확히 분리하는 것을 선호한다.
③ 어떤 개인들은 일과 개인적인 용도로 별도의 통신 기기림 사용하여 과업을 관리한다.
④ 유연한 궼무 배치눤 일부 개인이 직업적 삶과 개인적 삶 사이의 명확한 구분을 유지하게 해 준다.
⑤ 어떤 이들은 하로 종일 일과 가정의 역할을 통합하기로 선택한다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
options: ① People positively rate someone who is very slightly out of the norm in what to wear.
② People often form first impressions based on a person's footwear and accessories.
③ Studies show that individuals are more likely to trust those who dress in formal attire.
④ Social perceptions are influenced by various factors, including appearance and behavior.
⑤ Wearing a vibrant tie can enhance a person's image at professional gatherings.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 복장 규범에서 아주 살짝 벗어난 것을 통해 그 사람의 지위나 눔력을 포지티브하겂 평가한다는 연구 결과림 다루고 이습니다. 따라서 ①번이 가장 적절한 요지입니다.
options_translation: ① ­­사람들은 입는 것에 이서 규범에서 아주 살짝 벗어난 ­­사람을 긍정적으로 평가한다.
② ­­사람들은 좂좂 ­­사람의 신발과 액세서리림 바탕으로 첫인상을 형성한다.
③ 연구눤 개인들이 격식을 갖춘 복장을 한 ­­사람들을 더 신뢰하는 경향이 인음을 밴어낸다.
④ 사회적 인식은 외모와 행동을 포함한 다양한 요인에 의해 영향을 받다.
⑤ 활기 찬 넥타이림 매는 것은 전문적인 모임에서 ­­사람의 이미지림 향상시견 수 이다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularlyaffected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
options: ① Moving can create feelings of uncertainty in children, especially when their familiar routines are disrupted.
② Young children often find it challenging to envision their new living situations before the move takes place.
③ The transition to a new home can be particularly challenging for children aged 3 to 6 due to their literal understanding of the world.
④ Children should be encouraged to express their backgrounds, as this helps foster a sense of community.
⑤ It is indispensable for children to forget their past memories in order to adapt to their new environment.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 아이들의 과거 경험을 인정하고(validating children's past experiences), 과거를 자신들의 중요한 일부로 존중하는 방식으로 배경을 공유할 기회를 가져야 한다고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 새로운 환경에 적응하기 위해 과거의 기억을 잊는 것이 필수적이라는 5번의 내용은 지문의 내용과 정반대입니다.
options_translation: ① 이사는 아이들에게 불확실한 감정을 유발할 수 있으며, 특히 익숙한 일상이 방해받을 때 그러하다.
② 어린아이들은 이사가 일어나기 전에 새로운 거주 상황을 상상하는 것을 종종 어려워한다.
③ 3세에서 6세 사이의 아이들에게 새로운 집으로의 이동은 그들의 세상에 대한 문자 그대로의 이해 때문에 특히 힘들 수 있다.
④ 아이들은 자신의 배경을 표현하도록 권장되어야 하며, 이는 공동체 의식을 함양하는 데 도움이 된다.
⑤ 아이들이 새로운 환경에 적응하기 위해 과거의 기억을 잊는 것이 필수적이다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 어법적으로 어색한 3곳을 아래의 조건에 맞게 찾아서 고치시오.
questions.passage: American jazz pianist Bill Evans was born in New Jersey in 1929. His early training was in classical music. At the age of six, he began receiving piano lessons, later added flute and violin. He earned bachelor's degrees in piano and music education from Southeastern Louisiana College in 1950. He went on to serve in the army from 1951 to 1954 and played the flute in the Fifth Army Band. After serving in the military, he studied composition at the Mannes School of Music in New York. Composer George Russell admired his playing and hired Evans who record and perform his compositions. Evans became famous for recordings to make from the late-1950s through the 1960s. He won his first Grammy Award in 1964 for his album 'Conversations with Myself'. Evans' expressive piano works and his unique harmonic approach inspired a whole generation of musicians.
subjective_conditions: 1. 어색한 부분은 한 단어 혹은 여러 단어일 수도 있음.
2. 어색한 부분을 고치기 위해서 삭제, 추가, 변경을 하나 혹은 두 개 이상 할 수 있음.
3. 아래 지문과 주어진 해석이 일치하도록 수정해야 함.
questions.answer: (1) added → adding 혹은 and later added(2) who → to(3) to make → made
questions.explanation: (1) 'later added' 부분은 주절의 동사 'began'과 연결되는 분사구문이 되어야 하므로 'adding'으로 고치거나, 등위접속사를 넣어 'and later added'가 되어야 합니다. (2) 'hired Evans who record'에서 해석상 '녹음하고 연주하게 하기 위해 고용했다'는 의미이므로 목적격 보어 혹은 목적의 의미를 나타내는 'to record'가 적절합니다. (또는 문맥상 Evans가 선행사라면 who recorded가 되어야 하나 해석에 충실하면 to부정사 구조가 적합합니다.)(3) 'recordings to make'는 '만들어진 음반'이라는 수동의 의미를 지녀야 하므로 과거분사 'made'가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
options: ① The Dangers of Reducing Traffic in Cities
② The Decline of Bicycle Lanes in Modern Cities
③ Why We Should Keep Cars for the Safe Future
④ Managing Traffic to Make Cities Safer and Greener
⑤ Banning Delivery Trucks to Create Person-Only Zone
questions.explanation: 이 글은 교통량을 완화하기 위해 도로를 자전거와 보행자 전용으로 전환하는 전략과 그 이점을 설명합니다. 특히 배달 차량이 효율적인 물류 이동을 가능하게 하여 주민들이 근거리에서 쇼핑할 수 있게 함으로써 도시를 더 친환경적이고 안전하게 만드는 데 기여한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '도시를 더 안전하고 친환경적으로 만들기 위한 교통 관리'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 도시 교통량 감소의 위험성
② 현대 도시에서 자전거 도로의 감소
③ 안전한 미래를 위해 자동차를 유지해야 하는 이유
④ 도시를 더 안전하고 친환경적으로 만들기 위한 교통 관리
⑤ 보행자 전용 구역을 만들기 위한 배달 트럭 금지

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The interesting question is whether human language is homologous, that is, biologically "the same thing," to anything in the modern animal kingdom. (A) Discovering some similarity, such as sequential ordering, is pointless, expecially when it is found on a remote branch, such as a bird species, which is surely not ancestral to humans. (B) Imagine that their wildest dreams are realized and some chimpanzee can be taught to produce real signs, to group and order them consistently to convey meaning, to use them spontaneously to describe events, and so on. (C) Does that show that the human ability to learn the artificial sign system? (D) of course not, any more than seagulls evolved from mosquitos. (E) The symbol system that the chimp learned would have been useful to him and, indeed, the structure was provided by the human inventors.*primates: 영장류*spontaneously: 자발적으로
questions.insertion_sentence: Here primates are relevant, but the ape trainers and their fans are playing by the wrong rules.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 유인원 조련사들과 그 팬들의 접근 방식이 잘못되었다는 비판을 담고 있습니다. (A) 문장에서는 인간의 조상이 아닌 새와 같은 원거리 종과의 유사성을 찾는 것의 무의미함을 언급하고 있고, (B) 위치에서 인간과 생물학적으로 관련 있는 영장류(primates)를 언급하는 주어진 문장이 들어가는 것이 논리적입니다. 그래야 그 뒤의 내용(침팬지가 기호를 배우는 가상의 상황)이 유인원 조련사들의 '꿈'에 대한 예시로 자연스럽게 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along politicians, academics, journalists, educationalists, religious leaders and a while range of other commentators artificial a whole number of concerns about the dangers that such a new medium poses - often for those identified as 'vulnerable groups' in society. For example, television cause all sorts of social ills - violence, 'dumbing down', hyperactivity, cynicism and so on. But how accurate is this analysis? For some it is far from __________, and an analysis of responses to media use and content demonstrates a number of interesting and important patterns. For example, Wartella and Reeves' (1983) study Recurring Issues in Research on Children and Media argued that dangerous new medium stories follow a sequence which is repeated each time a new medium is invented. This sequence is as follows:First: the new medium is seen as harming the sense involved - for example, television harms the eyes.Second: new mediums are psychologically dangerous - making us violent, lonely or apathetic.Third: new mediums encourage adverse sosietal changes - television makes us childish or the internet encourages isolation and marginalisation.*articulate: 분명히 표현하다[설명하다]*vulnerable: 취약한, 피해를 입기 쉬운*dumbing down: 하향평준화*hyperactivity: 과잉행동*cynicism: 냉소주의
questions.explanation: 이 글은 새로운 매체가 등장할 때마다 제기되는 사회적 우려가 사실은 근거가 부족하며 매번 반복되는 일정한 패턴(신체적 위해, 심리적 위험, 사회적 변화)을 따른다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 'But how accurate is this analysis?'라는 질문을 통해 우려의 정확성에 의문을 제기한 후, 그것이 '전혀 설득력이 없다(far from convincing)'고 말하는 것이 뒤따르는 연구 결과(반복되는 고정된 패턴일 뿐이라는 내용)와 가장 잘 어울립니다.
options_translation: ① 중요한
② 효과 없는
③ 설득력 있는
④ 종교적인
⑤ 일어날 것 같지 않은

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [24년 9월 36번]
questions.passage: For many scientists, the seemingly innate human ability to make an internal image of observed movement(mirror neuron's ability) provides the biological template for empathy: It is what enables humans to discern what it must feel like to be another person. I can watch what another person does and know how it feels to act likewise. ①I see a person grimace and punch the air. ②I know what it feels like to make those movements. ③A deficit in mirror neurons can in principle account for three major symptoms of autism, the social, motor and language problems. ④As a result I can relate to what that person must be feeling as "anger" and respond accordingly. ⑤In this way, it is thought, human beings can establish bonds of empathy with one another strong enough to compete with those that rely on shared genetic material.*grimace: 얼굴을 찡그리다*deficit: 부족, 결함, 장애*autism: 자폐증
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 르런을 통해 타인의 행동을 내면화하고 공감을 형성하는 인간의 생물학적 기제에 대해 설명하고 읈습니다. ①, ②, ④는 타인의 신체적 움직임을 보고 괴로움이나 분노를 공감하는 과정을 설명하며, ⑤는 이를 통해 공감의 유대감을 형성한다는 결론을 제시합니다. 반면, ③는 거울 르런의 결함이 자폐증의 원인이 될 수 읈다는 내용으로, 공감의 생물학적 템플릿이라는 전체적인 흠름과는 거리가 읈습니다.

questions.question: 17. 제시된 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 32번]
questions.passage: During the 1970s and 1980s, media scholars treated the media as an instrument of the state or capital, which mediated or translated these institutions' interests into cultural symbolism.
ordered_passages: (A) Central to this argument is the observation that imagery around celebrity has shifted, from the elite to the ordinary. As Laura Grindstaff and Susan Murray have argued, new media presents the idea of celebrity as attainable to ordinary people at a historical moment of downward social mobility, unemployment, and economic instability.

(B) Graeme Turner frames this shift as a demotic turn, emphasizing the Greek root of democracy, demos, which refers to common people. Not only is celebrity now a common people. Not only is celebrity now a common pursuit of ordinary people, recent research indicates that increasing numbers of young people now think of fame per se - fame not as a byproduct of some activity or talent, but fame in itself - as a career option.
(C) However, some scholars now suggest that, since the early 2000s, the media has become driven primarily by its own (commercial) interests and is now more an author than a mediator of culture.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 1970~80년대에 미디어가 국가나 자밸의 도구였다고 설명합니다. (C)에서는 However를 통해 2000년대 초반 이후 미디어가 상업적 이익에 의해 움직이는 문화의 '저자'가 되었다고 내용을 전환합니다. (A)는 이러한 주장의 핵심으로 명성의 이미지가 엘리트에서 평바한 사람으로 이동함을 설명하고, (B)는 이러한 변화를 'demotic turn(물중적 전환)'으로 규정하며 명성 괴신이 직업 선택이 된 홄상을 부연 설명합니다. 따라서 순서는 (C)-(A)-(B)가 가장 적합합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 31번]
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers __________________. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work was conventional. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
options: ① put you in a great mood
③ have a musical idea at the beginning that comes back at the end
④ have repeated elements in a piece of music to keep your interest
⑤ take advantage of music to express the inexpressible, such as a human emotion
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 이해받지 못한 이유가 그들의 작품이 '생소함(unfamiliarity)'과 '완전히 새로움'에 있었음을 언급합니다. 후반부에서 살리에리가 위대한 작곡가가 될 수 없었덀 이유로 그의 작품이 '관습적(conventional)'이었기 때문이라고 대조합니다. 따라서 위대한 작곡가는 관습에 얽매이지 않고 창의적이고 독창적이어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신을 좋은 기분으로 만든다
② 창의적이고 독창적이다
③ 찘에 나온 음악적 아이디어가 끝에서 다시 나타난다
④ 흥미를 유지하기 윔해 음악에 반복되는 요소를 둔다
⑤ 인간의 감정과 같은 표현할 수 없는 것을 표현하기 윔해 음악을 이용합니다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: An organizational structure defines how work is done and information flows. It is fundamentally about the functional operations of different departments and divisions within the organization. In other words, the choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on how decisions are made. A mechanistic structure has a fixed, permanent hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Lines of authority and communication are expected to be followed rather rigidly. Decisions are made at the top, so there is more downward communication than upward communication. That's why the mechanistic structure can normally be drawn in an ⓐ<u>upside-down</u> pyramid form with few people at the top and many people at the bottom. While the mechanistic structure is fixed and ⓑ<u>rigid</u>, the alternative type of structure called the organic organization is based upon flexibility. Typically, the organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is ⓒ<u>less</u> centralized and spread across the plane of the organization. Organizational relationships of the organic structure are expected to be ⓓ<u>flexible</u> and constantly changing. Individuals and groups communicate with anyone at any location in the organization. Takes are continually redefined as organizational members ⓔ<u>interact</u> with each other, so decisions are made by individuals who are affected by the decisions.
questions.explanation: 기계적 구조는 위계가 고정되어 있고 의사 결정이 상부에서 이루어지며, 상단에는 소수의 인원이, 하단에는 다수의 인원이 배치되는 일반적인 피라미드 형태를 띱니다. 따라서 '역피라미드(upside-down pyramid)'가 아니라 일반적인 '피라미드(pyramid)' 형태가 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are ⓐ<u>rich</u> in life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will ⓑ<u>decrease</u>. This is a ⓒ<u>worrisome</u> and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Because falling oxygen levels in water lead to the ⓓ<u>survival</u> of marine organisms worldwide, ⓔ<u>anoxic</u> events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: 해수 내 용존 산소 수치가 떨어지는 것은 해양 생물들의 생존이 아니라 멸종이나 위협, 죽음을 초래합니다. 문맥상 생물들이 죽거나 쫓겨나는 현상(anoxic events)이 뒤따라 나오므로 'survival(생존)'은 부적절하며, 'extinction'이나 'death'와 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. Between 2000 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education ⓐ<u>doubled</u> from 19% to 57% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialized workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly ⓑ<u>skilled</u> workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education relies on ⓒ<u>efficient</u> assessment methods like examinations and multiple-choice quizzes in order to assess the growing number of students within the system's constraints, such as limited time and resources. These approaches provide impersonal or standardized test results, shifting students' focus away from ⓓ<u>feedback</u> and more towards ⓔ<u>grades</u>. In contrast to the large number of students in mass systems, more connected relationships between students and their teachers were common in the smaller, elite systems of the past, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.*demographic: 인구집단*constraint: 제약
questions.explanation: 문맥상 전 세계 고등 교육 참여율이 2000년에서 2014년 사이에 19%에서 57%로 증가한 것은 '두 배가 된(doubled)' 것이 아니라 거의 세 배가 된 것이므로 ⓐ가 틀렸습니다. 하지만 지문의 흐름상 참여율의 급격한 증가를 설명하는 맥락이며, 문제에서 요구하는 낱말의 부적절함은 수치적 계산보다는 문맥적 흐름을 보아야 하는데, 보통 이 지문의 원문이나 변형 문제에서 ⓐ는 'increased' 등의 의미로 쓰여 적절하게 간주되기도 합니다. 그러나 제시된 답안이 ①번인 것으로 보아 19%에서 57%로의 변화를 'doubled'로 표현한 것이 산술적으로 어색하다고 판단한 것으로 보입니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.*dysarthric: (신경 장애로 인한) 구음(構音) 장애의
options: ① Workers have conflicting views of AI's potential to improve the inclusiveness for disadvantaged groups.
② Disadvantaged workers are likely to have better access to jobs in labour markets, thanks to the benefits of AI adoption.
③ AI would help workers with disabilities, but for low-skilled workers, it would harm rather than benefit them.
④ The current uses of AI could risk leaving certain workers behind, such as non-native speakers.
⑤ The availability and quality of translations and other AI-generated text depends on the number of users that speak a certain language.
questions.explanation: 지문은 AI가 노동 시장에서 불리한 처지에 있는 노동자들의 접근성을 개선함으로써 직장의 포용성을 높일 수 있다고 설명합니다. 특히 장애인용 보조 기기, 저숙련 노동자의 능력 강화(임금 및 경력 전망에 긍정적 영향), 비원어민의 성과 향상 등을 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 ②번 'AI 도입의 혜택 덕분에 소외계층 노동자들이 노동 시장의 일자리에 더 잘 접근할 가능성이 있다'가 지문의 내용과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 노동자들은 소외계층을 위한 포용성을 개선하는 AI의 잠재력에 대해 상충하는 견해를 가지고 있다.
② AI 도입의 혜택 덕분에 소외계층 노동자들이 노동 시장의 일자리에 더 잘 접근할 수 있을 것이다.
③ AI는 장애가 있는 노동자들을 돕겠지만, 저숙련 노동자들에게는 이득보다는 해를 끼칠 것이다.
④ 현재의 AI 사용은 비원어민과 같은 특정 노동자들을 뒤처지게 할 위험이 있다.
⑤ 번역 및 기타 AI 생성 텍스트의 가용성과 품질은 특정 언어를 사용하는 사용자 수에 달려 있다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
options: ② Why Do Scientists Call Shapes Habits?
③ A Variety of Source Materials for Crystals
④ Why Is the Crystal Lattice Important?
⑤ How to Eat an Elephant
questions.explanation: 이 글은 원자가 결정의 기본 구성 요소임을 설명하고, 액체가 냉각될 때 결정이 형성되는 과정과 환경적 조건(시간, 온도, 재료 등)에 따라 결정의 모양이 어떻게 형성되는지를 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '결정은 어떻게 형성되는가?'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 결정은 어떻게 형성되는가?
② 왜 과학자들은 모양을 '습성'이라고 부르는가?
③ 결정을 위한 다양한 원천 재료들
④ 결정 격자는 왜 중요한가?
⑤ 코끼리를 먹는 방법

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are - writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. (A) You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent. (B) Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. (C) However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. (D) The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. (E) An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
questions.insertion_sentence: For example, how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 피아노 연주, 언어 학습, 테니스 서브와 같은 특정 기술이나 재능의 예시를 나열하고 있습니다. (A) 문장에서 능력을 '특정 기술이나 재능의 관점'에서 정의할 수 있다고 언급했으므로, 그에 대한 구체적인 예시인 주어진 문장은 (B) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것을 모두 고르면?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to __________________________________.
options: ① pity human beings against other animals
② secure a sense of human superiority
④ describe the interdependent relationships between organisms
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 언어를 사용하여 인간과 동물을 구분 짓고, 인간의 우월성을 유지하려 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 'linguistic castration(언어적 거세)'이라는 표현을 통해 동물의 힘을 빼앗고 인간을 정점에 두려는 태도를 비판하고 있습니다. 빈칸에는 인간의 우월적 지위를 유지하거나 계층적 관점을 고수한다는 내용이 들어가야 하므로 ②번(인간의 우월감을 확보하다)과 ⑤번(계층적인 관점을 유지하다)이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 인간을 다른 동물과 맞붙게 하다
② 인간의 우월감을 확보하다
③ 침팬지들 사이를 구별하다
④ 생물체들 사이의 상호 의존적인 관계를 묘사하다
⑤ 계층적인 관점을 유지하다

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 문장 ⓐ~ⓗ 중 어법상 어색한 부분이 있는 문장의 개수는?
questions.passage: ⓐIf the blood vessels are a bit like the heating system in your house, the nerves are analogous to the electrical wiring, providing information (sensation) from all parts of the body and power to all the muscles of the body. ⓑNerves are specialized cells whose function is to transmit tiny electrical currents from one end to the other, so it does act a bit like electrical wires. ⓒSensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation. ⓓlf, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. ⓔBeing unpleasant, the pain is in fact acting as a protective mechanism for the foot. ⓕWithin the brain, nerves will connect to the area where speech is controlled, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. ⓖThey will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now contracts quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object. ⓗSensory and motor nerves control almost all functions in the body - from the beating of the heart to the movement of the gut, sweating, emptying the bladder and just about everything else.
questions.explanation: ⓑ에서 주어인 Nerves가 복수이므로 대명사 'it does'를 'they do'로 고쳐야 하며, ⓖ에서 관계대명사 that의 선행사인 the muscles가 복수이므로 동사 'contracts'를 'contract'로 고쳐야 합니다. 따라서 어법상 어색한 문장은 ⓑ, ⓖ 총 2개입니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절한 것을 모두 고르면?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the ⓐ<u>indigenous</u> people might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause ⓑ<u>reasonable</u> transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A ⓒ<u>stubborn</u> native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a ⓓ<u>preservation</u> of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities ⓔ<u>penetrate</u> into their own neighbourhood.*externality: 외부 효과 **fractionalization: 분열
questions.explanation: ⓐ는 '현지인'이라는 뜻으로 적절하고, ⓔ는 '침투하다/번지다'라는 뜻으로 사회적 갈등이 인근 지역으로 번지는 것을 두려워한다는 문맥에 적합합니다. ⓑ는 '과도한(excessive)', ⓒ는 '개방적인(tolerant/open-minded)', ⓓ는 '왜곡(distortion)' 등으로 쓰여야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. (A) Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it - you just see the blurred outline of the moving string. (B) Strings vibrating in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. (C) But if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note is heard loud and clear. (D) The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. (E) When the waves reach your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string.*pluck: (현악기를) 뜯다 **amplify: 증폭시키다
questions.insertion_sentence: The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '나무의 진동이 공기 중에 더 강력한 파동을 만들어내어 기타로부터 멀리 퍼져 나간다'는 내용입니다. 이는 (D)에서 현의 진동이 기타 몸통의 나무 패널로 전달된다는 내용 뒤에 이어져야 하며, (E)의 '그 파동이 당신의 고막에 도달할 때'라는 문장 앞인 (E) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the ⓐ<u>conventional</u>, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, ⓑ<u>aggressive</u> approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, such transactions are becoming increasingly ⓒ<u>common</u>, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a ⓓ<u>favorable</u> relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only ⓔ<u>inadequate</u> result.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 대부분의 사람들이 같은 사람과 반복적으로 거래하기 때문에 일회성 거래는 드물어지고 있으므로 ⓒ는 'rare(드문)' 등으로 고쳐야 합니다. 또한 상호의존적인 세계에서 윈-윈 결과는 유일하게 수용 가능한 결과가 되고 있으므로 ⓔ는 'acceptable(수용 가능한)' 등으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us. One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Göbekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up radically remaking the society itself. (A)<u>Things are not so different in our own time</u>.*ornately: 화려하게 **megalithic: 거석의
options: ① The erection of the megalithic stones still takes long time.
② The innovators are leading the rest of us.
③ We are controlling our environment.
④ To date buildings transform how we live.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거 괴베클리 테페의 거석 건조물이 수렵 채집인들을 정착하게 만들어 농경 사회로 변화시킨 것처럼, 건물과 개발이 인간을 형성한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. (A) '우리 시대에도 상황은 그리 다르지 않다'는 것은 오늘날의 건물들 역시 우리가 살아가는 방식을 변화시키고 있음을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 거석의 건립은 여전히 오랜 시간이 걸린다.
② 혁신가들은 우리 나머지를 이끌고 있다.
③ 우리는 우리의 환경을 통제하고 있다.
④ 오늘날까지 건물들은 우리가 사는 방식을 변화시킨다.
⑤ 인간은 여전히 수렵 채집인이다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
