questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
options: ① How to Relieve Children's Stress When They Are Moving
② The Faster You Adjust to the New Place, The Better
③ Moving: The Time Your Routine Is Disrupted
④ The Understanding of Children, Ages 3-6, Is Quite Literal
⑤ Let Go of Your Past Experience
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이사가 아이들에게 주는 스트레스를 설명하며, 아이들의 과거 경험을 존중해주고 새로운 환경에 적응하도록 돕는 균형 잡힌 접근법이 필요함을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 이사할 때 아이들의 스트레스를 완화하는 방법이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 아이들이 이사할 때 스트레스를 완화하는 방법
② 새로운 장소에 더 빨리 적응할수록 더 좋다
③ 이사: 당신의 일상이 방해받는 시간
④ 3-6세 아이들의 이해는 꽤 문자 그대로이다
⑤ 당신의 과거 경험을 놓아주어라

questions.question: 10. 다음 글을 읽고 <보기>의 "complementary good"에 대한 설명으로 옳은 것의 개수를 고른 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status - they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers may not be completely locked in to the product. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.
vocabulary_box: ⓐ It is a good whose appeal increases with the popularity of its complement.
ⓑ lt is either what is shared and beneficial for all or most members of a given community, or alternatively, what is achieved by citizenship.
ⓒ It is a product that can be used as a replacement for another product because it serves the same purpose.
ⓓ When two goods are complements, having more of one good causes the consumer to desire more of the other good.
ⓔ It is a product that people consume more of as the price rises and vice versa.
ⓕ Its demand increases when its complement's price decreases.
questions.explanation: 보완재(complementary good)에 대한 옳은 설명은 다음과 같습니다. ⓐ 한 제품의 인기가 높아지면 보완재의 매력도 증가한다는 본문의 내용과 일치합니다. ⓓ 두 재화가 보완재일 때, 한 재화를 더 많이 가지면 다른 재화도 더 많이 소비하고 싶어지므로 옳습니다. ⓕ 보완 관계인 제품의 가격이 내려가면 해당 제품의 수요가 늘고, 따라서 그 보완재의 수요도 함께 증가하므로 경제학적 원리에 따라 옳습니다. ⓑ는 공공재, ⓒ는 대체재, ⓔ는 기펜재 또는 베블런재에 대한 설명이므로 옳지 않습니다. 따라서 옳은 것은 ⓐ, ⓓ, ⓕ 총 3개입니다.
options_translation: ① 1개
② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 6월 34번]
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The ①<u>primary</u> steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to ②<u>conceive</u> ideas separately. Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most ③<u>favorable</u> options. By developing and assessing ideas ④<u>collectively</u> before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve ⑤<u>group</u> intelligence.
questions.explanation: ④ ␅(collectively)는 '집단적으로'라는 뜻이지만, 글의 흐름상 브레인라이팅 과정은 아이디어를 선택하고 구체화하기 '전에' 아이디어를 독립적 혹은 개별적으로 개발하고 평가하는 것이 핵심입니다. 문맥상 'individually'나 'independently'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 22번]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ① How to be the Perfect Leader in School
② Why Extraordinary People Become Leaders
③ The Leadership Potential in Ordinary People
④ Historical Figures and Their Achievements
⑤ Footsteps of Giants: Abraham Lincoln and Martin Luther King J.
questions.explanation: 대단한 가거의 리더들도 시자ᄀ안 펑범한 시민이ᄋ거나 하ᄀ새이어스먀, 아이디어를 개선하고 고유하는 개선 개선 개선하는 개선하는 개선하는 가정을 페겨 리더가 댸ᄋ으므로, 에리 모두가 리더가 뎨 자매려ᄀ을 가지고 의다는 내용이므로 ③가 가장 저ᄀ절하내용이다.
options_translation: ① 하ᄀ겨에서 관벼ᄀ한 리더가 다는 버ᄇ
② 애외저ᄀ인 사라ᄆ드리 리더가 다는 이유
③ 펑범한 사라ᄆ들 소ᄀ으이 리더시ᄑ 자매려ᄀ
④ 겨사저ᄀ 긴물들가 그드르이 아저ᄀ
⑤ 거인드르이 발자구ᄀ: 애브라함 린건가 마틴 루서 킹 2세

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에 대한 설명으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
options: ① The text begins with an introduction of the topic.
② Detailed examples of crop rotation are provided in the middle of the text.
③ Key ideas are presented at the beginning and reinforced at the end of the text.
④ The text explains that crop rotation is sustainable because it keeps the soil healthy.
⑤ The text concludes with a comparison between crop rotation and other farming methods.
questions.explanation: 지문은 윤작(crop rotation)의 정의로 시작하여 구체적인 예시를 들고, 윤작이 토양을 건강하게 유지하여 지속 가능하다는 장점을 설명하며 마무리됩니다. 타 농법과의 비교는 제시되어 있지 않으므로 5번이 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 글은 주제에 대한 소개로 시작한다.
② 글의 중간 부분에 윤작의 구체적인 예시가 제공된다.
③ 핵심 아이디어는 글의 처음에 제시되고 마지막에 강화된다.
④ 글은 윤작이 토양을 건강하게 유지하기 때문에 지속 가능하다고 설명한다.
⑤ 글은 윤작과 다른 농법 간의 비교로 결론을 맺는다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글을 읽고, <조건>에 맞추어 -Monday Morning Quarterback---의 정의를 완성하시오. [23-9-29]
questions.passage: There is a reason the title -Monday Morning Quarterback--- exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.*boardroom: 이사회실
questions.summary_sentence: Definition of Monday Morning Quarterback: someone who says how an event or problem __________________ by others after something has happened.
subjective_conditions: 윗글의 내용을 참고할 경우
주어진 단어(deal with)림 포함할 경우
5단어로 완성할 경우
필요하면 어형변화 할 경우
questions.explanation: -Monday Morning Quarterback---은 이미 일어난 일에 대해 됤늦게 후수를 두는 사람을 의미합니다. 정의문에서 -사건이나 문제가 타인에 의해 어떻게 찘리되었어얼 했는지---림 말하는 사람이므로, 과거의 일에 대한 후회나 비판을 나타내는 -should have p.p.--- 구문과 수동태림 결합하여 -should have been dealt with---로 완성합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 도턜림 설명하는 문장을 <젰건>에 맞추어 완성하시오. [23-9-25]
questions.passage: (1) In 2015, the percentage of people who reported using social media in the 30-49 group was _____________ in the 65 and older group.(2) In 2021, except for the 65 and older group, more than _____________ of people in each age group reported using social media.
subjective_conditions: (1) 주어진 단어(high, twice)림 포함할 경우
(1) 5단어로 완성할 경우
(1) 필요하면 어형변화 할 경우
(2) 한 단어의 분수로 심 경우
questions.answer: (1) over twice higher than that(2) three-fifths / two-thirds / seven-tenths
questions.explanation: (1) 2015년 30-49세 중(77%)과 65세 이상(35%)림 비교하면 2배가 넑으므로 -over twice higher than that---으로 표현합니다. (2) 2021년 65세 이상을 제외한 모든 연령대가 60% 이상이므로, 수치에 맞는 분수 표현(three-fifths 등)을 쌡다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 개에서 묑줄 친 -the opposite---가 의미하는 바림 찾아 젰건에 맞게 쓰시오. [23-9-33]
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providing students with relevant texts they will be interested in. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and discovered ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found <u>the opposite</u>. -To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books.--- The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more. *dyslexia: 난독증 **voraciously: 탐욕수럽게
subjective_conditions: 6단어 이내의 한 문장으로 쌡 경우
questions.answer: These dyslexics were enthusiastic readers. / They rarely avoided reading. / They sought out books.
questions.explanation: -the opposite---는 난독증을 가진 사람들이 독서림 피할 것이띀 예상과 달리, 실제로는 열정적인 독서가가 되었다는 내용을 의미합니다. 본문에서 이림 나타내는 문장을 참고하여 쓰면 됩니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 아래 질문에 대한 답을 완성하시오. (빈칸에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 쓸 경우 필요시 어형을 변형할 수 있음)
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners.
subjective_conditions: 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 쓸 경우 필요시 어형을 변형할 수 있음
questions.subjective_answer_format: Q: Why does the author say, 'you and I are the descendants of the winners'?A: The author suggests that we're descendants of the winners because our ancestors likely had the mental advantages that enabled them to survive by (A)_____________ their enemies in battle. The cognitively superior genes that we possess today were (B)_____________ from those who prevailed in the evolutionary struggle.(A) ________________________(B) ________________________
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면, 인류의 조상은 적들보다 생각에서 앞섬(out-think)으로써 생존 우위를 점했습니다. (A)는 전치사 'by' 뒤에 오므로 동명사 형태인 'out-thinking'이 적절합니다. 또한, 이러한 정신적 우위를 가능하게 한 유전자는 다음 세대로 전달(pass on)되었으므로, (B)에는 '물려받은' 혹은 '계승된'의 의미인 'inherited'나 'succeeded'가 적합합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Once upon a time the famous poet Sheikh Saadi lived a simple life in the city of Shiraz, like many other poets and philosophers. A wealthy merchant in Shiraz invited Sheikh Saadi and many prominent businessmen to his daughter's wedding, and the poet accepted the invitation. On the day of the wedding, dressed in simple clothes, he went to the wedding ceremony. Ignored by the host and guests, he left, rented a lavish coat, and returned to a warm welcome. The host embraced him as he would do to an old friend and complimented him on the clothes he was wearing. The poet did not say a word and allowed the host to lead him to the dining room. The host personally led the poet to his seat and served out chicken soup to him. After a moment, the poet suddenly dipped the corner of his coat in the sou pas if he fed it. All the guests were now staring at him in surprise. The host said, "Sir, what are you doing?" The poet very calmly replied, "Now that I have put on expensive clothes, I see a world of difference here. All that I can say now is that this feast is meant for my clothes, not for me."
options: ③ Many dishes make many diseases.
④ You can't tell a book by its cover.
⑤ A broken clock is right twice a day.
questions.explanation: 시인 셰이크 사디는 평범한 옷을 입었을 때 무시당했지만, 화려한 옷을 빌려 입었을 때는 극진한 대접을 받았습니다. 이에 시인은 코트 자락을 수프에 적시며 이 환대는 자신이 아닌 자신의 옷을 위한 것이라고 말합니다. 이는 사람을 겉모습으로 판단해서는 안 된다는 교훈을 담고 있으므로 주제로 'You can't tell a book by its cover(겉표지만 보고 책을 판단할 수 없다)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 소탐대실 (푼돈 아끼려다 큰 돈 잃는다).
② 얻어먹는 주제에 가릴 처지가 아니다.
③ 음식이 많으면 병도 많다.
④ 겉모습만 보고 판단해서는 안 된다.
⑤ 고장 난 시계도 하루에 두 번은 맞는다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recoding than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
options: ② Anatomy and Physiology of the Ear
③ How Does the Ear Respond to Stimuli
④ Why Your Voice Sounds Different to You
⑤ How Hearing Works: Our Auditory System
questions.explanation: 자신의 목소리가 녹음된 것과 다르게 들리는 이유는 두 가지 전달 경로 때문입니다. 외부 소리처럼 공기를 통해 전달되는 경로와, 성대의 진동이 뼈를 통해 직접 내이에 전달되는 내부 경로가 있습니다. 내부 경로는 낮은 주파수를 강조하기 때문에 자신의 목소리가 타인에게 들리는 것보다 더 깊고 풍부하게 들립니다. 따라서 정답은 '자신의 목소리가 왜 다르게 들리는가'입니다.
options_translation: ① 법정 공판의 녹음
② 귀의 해부학과 생리학
③ 귀가 자극에 반응하는 방식
④ 왜 당신의 목소리가 당신에게 다르게 들리는가
⑤ 청각의 작동 원리: 우리의 청각 시스템

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show - whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① The Changing Landscape of Media Technology
② Information Taking Priority Over the Medium
③ How New Media Shape Our Viewpoint
④ Subtle Erosion of Thought Through Television
⑤ The Decline of Traditional Media in the Digital Age
questions.explanation: 새로운 매체가 등장하면 우리는 그것을 통해 세상을 다르게 보게 됩니다. 마샬 맥루한은 정보의 내용보다 정보가 전달되는 방식(매체)이 더 중요하다고 주장하며, 매체가 세상을 바라보는 새로운 코드를 제공한다고 설명했습니다. 따라서 글의 제목으로는 '새로운 매체가 우리의 관점을 형성하는 방식'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 미디어 기술의 변화하는 풍경
② 매체보다 우선순위에 있는 정보
③ 새로운 미디어가 우리의 관점을 형성하는 방식
④ 텔레비전을 통한 사고의 미묘한 침식
⑤ 디지털 시대 전통 미디어의 쇠퇴

questions.question: 8. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult <u>to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat</u>." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① to search for hidden truths within complex scientific theories
② to explore unknown areas of science to expand human knowledge
③ to test multiple hypotheses to find the most accurate scientific explanation
④ to pursue something that doesn't exist based on incorrect scientific concepts
⑤ to find a solution to a difficult scientific problem using advanced technology
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 '어두운 방에서 검은 고양이를 찾는 것은 매우 어렵다, 특히 고양이가 없을 때'라는 의미입니다. 이는 과학자들이 잘못된 개념(wrong concept)을 바탕으로 존재하지 않는 본질이나 물질(예: 에테르)을 찾으려고 헛수고를 하는 상황을 비유한 것입니다. 따라서 정답은 ④번 '잘못된 과학적 개념에 근거하여 존재하지 않는 것을 추구하는 것'입니다.
options_translation: ① 복잡한 과학 이론 내에서 숨겨진 진실을 찾는 것
② 인간의 지식을 확장하기 위해 과학의 미지의 영역을 탐구하는 것
③ 가장 정확한 과학적 설명을 찾기 위해 여러 가설을 테스트하는 것
④ 잘못된 과학적 개념에 근거하여 존재하지 않는 무언가를 추구하는 것
⑤ 첨단 기술을 사용하여 어려운 과학적 문제에 대한 해결책을 찾는 것

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 a 'field of contradictions'가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. Between 2000 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up <u>a 'field of contradictions'</u> for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small number of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
options: ① the difficulty in balancing student autonomy with teacher control in education
② the disagreement between theoretical knowledge and practical skills development
③ the contrast between increasing enrollment and limited educational resources
④ the tension between mass higher education expansion and standardized testing
⑤ the gap between the theoretical goals of assessment and its practical implementation
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 이론상으로는 고등 교육의 확대가 평생 학습을 가능하게 하는 평가(학습을 위한 평가, 피드백 중심)로 이어져야 하지만, 실제로는 대중 고등 교육 시스템의 효율성 요구 때문에 시험과 객관식 퀴즈 같은 표준화된 평가와 최소한의 피드백만이 제공되고 있습니다. 이러한 '이론과 실제의 괴리'가 바로 '모순의 장(field of contradictions)'이 의미하는 바이므로 정답은 ⑤번입니다.
options_translation: ① 교육에서 학생의 자율성과 교사의 통제 사이의 균형을 맞추는 것의 어려움
② 이론적 지식과 실무적 기술 개발 사이의 불일치
③ 입학 인원 증가와 한정된 교육 자원 사이의 대조
④ 대중 고등 교육 확대와 표준화된 시험 사이의 긴장
⑤ 평가의 이론적 목표와 실제 실행 사이의 간극

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting 'paid' the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
options: ① Feeling that their circumstances are as favorable as those of others, Capuchin monkeys reject their reward and show their displeasure.
② The Capuchin monkey will decline her rewards to express her displeasure about the treatment, even if she gets more rewards than before.
③ Capuchin monkeys reveal their discontentment by refusing to accept their prize, when they perceive impartiality, even if nothing has changed for them.
④ Capuchin monkeys reject their reward and express dissatisfaction when perceiving inequality in comparison to others, notwithstanding the fact that their own situation has not changed.
⑤ On condition that nothing changes for them personally, Capuchin monkeys express unhappiness and turn down their reward when they recognize that others are treated fairly.
questions.explanation: 카푸친 원숭이는 자신의 개별적인 보상 수준이 나빠지지 않았음에도 불구하고, 타인과의 비교를 통해 불공평함을 느끼면 기존의 보상마저 거부하고 강한 불만을 표현한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 정답 ④번이 지문의 핵심 요지를 가장 잘 요약하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 자신의 상황이 다른 이들만큼 유리하다고 느끼면, 카푸친 원숭이는 보상을 거부하고 불만을 표시한다.
② 카푸친 원숭이는 대우에 대한 불만을 표현하기 위해, 이전보다 더 많은 보상을 받더라도 보상을 거절할 수 있다.
③ 카푸친 원숭이는 자신들에게 변한 것이 없더라도 공평함을 인식하면 보상을 거절하며 불만을 드러낸다.
④ 카푸친 원숭이는 자신의 상황이 변하지 않았음에도 불구하고, 타인과의 비교를 통해 불평등을 인식할 때 보상을 거부하고 불만을 표현한다.
⑤ 개인적으로 변하는 것이 없더라도, 카푸친 원숭이는 다른 이들이 공평하게 대우받는 것을 인식하면 불행함을 표현하고 보상을 거절한다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us ⓐ<u>ward</u> off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, ⓑ<u>controls</u> many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For instance, terror sharpens our perception to dangerous stimuli, keeps us extremely ⓒ<u>alert</u>, drives us to either flee or fight a situation, and may even make us remember a past experience more vividly (so that we avoid the threat in the future). The particular emotions we experience are believed to exist because, in the distant past, they have assisted us (as a species) in ⓓ<u>getting through</u> difficulties in our surroundings, regardless of the precise mechanisms by which they activate our systems. ⓔ<u>With</u> their assistance in adapting and surviving, they would not have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 감정이 적응과 생존에 도움을 주었기 때문에 진화했다는 내용입니다. ⓔ가 포함된 문장은 '가정법 과거완료' 구문으로, '도움이 없었다면 진화하지 않았을 것이다'라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 With가 아니라 Without이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to ⓐ<u>differentiate</u> between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our text book or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an ⓑ<u>active</u> form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term sections has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to ⓒ<u>retrieve</u> the same information a few days later. After a few seconds of minutes, working memory already starts ⓓ<u>dissipating</u>, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you reset your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to ⓔ<u>overlook</u> the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.explanation: 장기 기억으로 정보를 보내기 위해서는 학습 자료를 '간과(overlook)'하는 것이 아니라, 일정한 간격을 두고 다시 '검토(review)'하거나 '인출'하는 과정이 필요합니다. 따라서 overlook은 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 36번]
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity to _____________________. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.explanation: 거울 뉴런의 발견을 통해 인간이 관찰을 통해 배우는 근본적인 능력에 대한 생각이 바뀌었다는 내용입니다. 지문 전체에서 아이들이 부모나 친구의 행동을 관찰하고 모방(imitation)하며 배운다는 사례(혀 내밀기, 소리 흉내, 청소기 놀이 등)가 제시되고 있으므로 빈칸에는 '관찰을 통해 배우는 것'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 관찰을 통해 배우다
② 언어 기술을 습득하다
③ 문화적 동화에 저항하다
④ 불수의적 행동을 흉내 내다
⑤ 비언어적 의사소통을 이해하다

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 23번]
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that ____________________________________, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
options: ① are unable to assist others due to physical disabilities
② are commonly at a disadvantage in the labor market
③ typically receive the lowest wages despite their skills
④ ignore ethical issues related to AI in the workplace
⑤ are at the forefront of technological advancements
questions.explanation: 지문은 AI가 장애인(시각, 청각, 언어 장애 등), 비원어민(언어 장벽), 그리고 저숙련 노동자들의 업무 능력을 향상시켜 직장에서의 포용성을 높인다고 설명합니다. 이들은 공통적으로 노동 시장에서 불리한 위치에 있는 사람들이므로 빈칸에는 '노동 시장에서 흔히 불리한 위치에 있는'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 신체적 장애 때문에 타인을 도울 수 없는
② 노동 시장에서 흔히 불리한 위치에 있는
③ 그들의 기술에도 불구하고 보통 최저 임금을 받는
④ 직장에서의 AI와 관련된 윤리적 문제를 무시하는
⑤ 기술 발전의 최전선에 있는

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Seawater is rich in dissolved oxygen, which marine animals need to survive. Physics has long shown that colder water holds more dissolved oxygen than warmer water - this helps explain why cold polar seas are teeming with life, while tropical oceans are clearer and have fewer living creatures. ⓐPolar seas' rich biodiversity supports valuable fishing industries, while tropical oceans' lower biodiversity offers less economic value. ⓑAs global warming heats up the oceans, the amount of dissolved oxygen is expected to drop, which could become dangerous and potentially harm ecosystems. ⓒRecently, scientists have studied data showing that the oxygen levels in oceans have been decreasing for over fifty years. ⓓIn fact, oxygen is dropping faster than water temperatures are rising. ⓔThis decline in oxygen can affect marine habitats globally, and in recent years has caused more anoxic events, where populations of fish, crabs, and other organisms have died or been displaced.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel overwhelmed when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop-out, or worse.
questions.summary_sentence: Excessive parental bragging can create (A)__________ for the child, so it is important to limit it for the sake of their (B)__________ development.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 영재 아이를 둔 부모들이 자녀의 성취를 과하게 자랑하는 '부모의 함정'에 대해 경고하고 있습니다. 부모의 지나친 자랑은 아이에게 부응하기 힘든 기대감을 주어 (A) 압박(pressure)을 느끼게 하며, 성취로 정의된 거짓된 자아상을 만들 수 있습니다. 따라서 아이가 성취에 얽매이지 않고 있는 그대로의 자신으로 성장할 수 있도록, 즉 (B) 자아 정체성(self-identity)의 발달을 위해 자랑을 제한해야 한다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 분노 ... 성숙
② 혼란 ... 창의성
③ 압박 ... 자아 정체성
④ 불안 ... 자기 의심
⑤ 동기 부여 ... 소외

questions.question: 28. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of ⓐ<u>different</u> departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which ⓑ<u>disallows</u> them to see things as others see them.The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules and procedures and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more ⓒ<u>horizontal</u> in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.Employees in a mechanistic structure are burdened with more rules and regulations than in an organic structure. This inevitably ⓓ<u>facilitates</u> innovation and creativity. Because there are expected behavior patterns in mechanistic structures, it is often difficult for employees to adjust to new situations. New ideas and processes are therefore more ⓔ<u>difficult</u> to implement.

③ Role of Hierarchies in Enhancing Workplace Creativity

questions.question: 29. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are _____________________________________. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO₂ a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
options: ① endangered due to climate change
② destroying the food chain in the ocean
③ exceptionally effective at storing carbon
④ highly helpful to the country's economic growth
⑤ releasing large amounts of waste into the ocean
questions.explanation: 이 글은 고래가 대기 중의 이산화탄소를 흡수하고 저장하는 데 있어 매우 중요한 역할을 한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 고래 한 마리가 죽을 때 평균 30톤의 이산화탄소를 격리하며, 배설물을 통해 식물성 플랑크톤의 성장을 도와 추가적인 탄소 격리를 유도한다는 내용을 통해 고래가 탄소 저장에 매우 효과적임을 알 수 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 고래가 탄소 저장에 뛰어나다는 내용인 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기후 변화로 인해 멸종 위기에 처한
② 바다의 먹이 사슬을 파괴하는
③ 탄소를 저장하는 데 예외적으로 효과적인
④ 국가의 경제 성장에 매우 도움이 되는
⑤ 바다에 대량의 폐기물을 배출하는

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. ⓐAI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. ⓑFor example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. ⓒAI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. ⓓFor example, AI's capacity to translate written or spoken text can be utilized by the high-performing workers to maximize their work productivity and efficiency. ⓔRecently, developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 AI가 노동 시장에서 불리한 위치에 있는 사람들(장애인, 저숙련 노동자 등)의 포용성을 높여준다는 내용입니다. ⓓ는 AI의 번역 능력이 '성과가 높은(high-performing)' 노동자들의 생산성을 극대화하는 데 사용될 수 있다는 내용으로, 사회적 약자나 불리한 노동자의 포용성이라는 주제에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
options: ① the desire of digital content creators in social media era
② the barriers ordinary celebrities face in becoming elite celebrities
③ the comparison of ordinary fame in social media and elite celebrity
④ the differences between reality TV stars and social media celebrities
⑤ the criticism to social media celebrities' lack of traditional talents
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전통적인 '엘리트 유명인'과 소셜 미디어를 통해 등장한 '평범한 유명인'의 특징과 명성의 의미 차이를 비교하고 있습니다. 엘리트 유명인은 신비로움과 계층적 거리를 특징으로 하지만, 평범한 유명인은 빈번한 상호작용과 소셜 미디어 지표(구독자, 좋아요 등)를 통해 명성을 얻는다는 차이점을 설명하고 있으므로 주제로 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 소셜 미디어 시대 디지털 콘텐츠 제작자들의 욕구
② 평범한 유명인들이 엘리트 유명인이 되는 과정에서 직면하는 장벽
③ 소셜 미디어에서의 평범한 명성과 엘리트 유명인의 비교
