questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. (A) Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. (B) You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn. (C) Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. (D) Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. (E) We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.insertion_sentence: But if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '하지만 여러 번 반복하면, 다른 것을 할 때보다 혀가 더 자주 나올 것이다'라는 내용입니다. (B) 뒤의 문장에서 신생아에게 혀를 내밀 때 매번 혀가 나오는 것을 보지는 못할 수도 있다고 했으므로, 그 뒤에 '하지만 여러 번 하면 더 자주 나올 것이다'라는 반전의 내용이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 (C)의 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.summary_sentence: Global warming has caused a/an (A)___________ of dissolved oxygen in the ocean, which is occurring faster than the rise in water temperature and leading to widespread (B)___________ of marine ecosystems.
questions.explanation: 본문은 지구 온난화로 인해 해수 온도가 상승함에 따라 용존 산소량이 감소하고 있으며, 이 속도가 수온 상승보다 빠르고 해양 생태계에 부정적인 영향을 끼치고 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 산소의 '부족/결핍'을 뜻하는 scarcity가 적절하며, (B)에는 생태계의 '혼란/붕괴'를 뜻하는 disruption이 들어가는 것이 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 부족 ...... 붕괴(혼란)
② 비옥함 ...... 멸종
③ 결핍 ...... 다양성
④ 불충분 ...... 분포
⑤ 소비 ...... 방해

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목을 완성하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying."
questions.summary_sentence: the (A)__________ of cramming and the importance of efficient learning strategies for (B)__________ formation
questions.explanation: 지문은 벼락치기(cramming)가 단기 기억에만 머물 뿐 장기 기억으로 전이되지 않는다는 점을 지적하며 벼락치기의 한계를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 'limitations(한계)'가 적절하며, 정보를 며칠 뒤에 회상하기 위해 필요한 'long-term memory(장기 기억)' 형성을 위한 전략이 중요하다는 (B)의 내용과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 한계 ... 장기 기억
② 단점 ... 단기 기억
③ 이점 ... 장기 기억
④ 장점 ... 단기 기억
⑤ 성공 ... 필수 기억

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 9월 29번]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and ⓐ<u>prejudiced</u> perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which ⓑ<u>allows</u> them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a ⓒ<u>vertical</u> hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more ⓓ<u>horizontal</u> in nature, where decision making is ⓔ<u>decentralized</u> and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 각 부서의 구성원들이 '터널 시야(tunnel vision)'를 갖게 된다는 것은 자신의 관점으로만 사물을 보고 타인의 관점으로는 보지 못한다는 의미입니다. 따라서 ⓑ의 allows는 '방해하다(prevents/blocks)'나 '하지 못하게 하다'는 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 31번]
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
options: ① The rivalry between Mozart and Salieri.
② The influence of classical music on modern compositions.
③ The life and works of Antonio Salieri.
④ The importance of music education in the 18th century.
⑤ The reasons behind the lack of appreciation for great composers in their times.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 이해받지 못한 이유가 그들의 음악적 형식이나 아이디어가 '생소함(unfamiliarity)' 때문이었다고 설명하고 있습니다. 이후 살리에리의 예시를 통해 독창성(originality)의 중요성을 대조하며, 왜 위대한 음악가들이 초기에 인정을 받지 못했는지에 대한 이유를 다루고 있으므로 ⑤번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 모차르트와 살리에리 사이의 경쟁.
② 클래식 음악이 현대 작곡에 미치는 영향.
③ 안토니오 살리에리의 생애와 작품들.
④ 18세기 음악 교육의 중요성.
⑤ 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 인정받지 못한 이유들.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 9월 35번]
questions.passage: The fast-paced evolution of Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) has radically ⓐ<u>transformed</u> the dynamics and business models of the tourism and hospitality industry. This leads to new levels/forms of competitiveness among service providers and transforms the customer experience through new services. Creating unique experiences and providing convenient services to customers leads to satisfaction and, eventually, customer ⓑ<u>loyalty</u> to the service provider or brand (i.e., hotels). In particular, the most recent technological ⓒ<u>regression</u> received by the tourism sector is represented by mobile applications. Indeed, tourists' ability to ⓓ<u>access</u> services like hotel reservations, airline ticketing, and local attraction recommendations via mobile devices creates significant interest and leads to ⓔ<u>substantial</u> profits.
questions.explanation: 정보통신기술(ICT)의 급격한 발전이 관광 산업에 긍정적인 변화와 이익을 가져오고 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 모바일 애플리케이션으로 대표되는 최근의 기술적 변화는 '퇴보(regression)'가 아니라 '혁신(innovation)' 혹은 '진보(advancement)'가 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
options: ① The Benefits of Warm Ocean Waters
② How Marine Life Thrives in Tropical Oceans
③ Effects of Ocean Depth Changes on Marine Life
④ Global Warming's Impact on Marine Ecosystems
⑤ The Relationship Between Sea Temperature and Human Populations
questions.explanation: 이 글은 지구 온난화로 인해 해수 온도가 상승하면 용존 산소량이 감소하게 되고, 이것이 해양 생태계에 치명적인 영향을 미치며 실제로 해양 산소 수치가 급격히 떨어지고 있다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 ④ '지구 온난화가 해양 생태계에 미치는 영향'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 따뜻한 바닷물의 이점
② 열대 바다에서 해양 생물이 번성하는 방법
③ 해수면 깊이 변화가 해양 생물에 미치는 영향
④ 지구 온난화가 해양 생태계에 미치는 영향
⑤ 해수 온도와 인구 사이의 관계

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language. (A) Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys made after animals are also most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. (B) This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. (C) In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. (D) A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그럼에도 불구하고(However)' 동물들이 여전히 앞발을 손처럼 사용하고 표정으로 말을 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C) 뒤에서 최근 애니메이션 영화들이 동물들을 더 '자연스러운' 방식으로 묘사하는 경향이 있다고 언급한 후, (D) 위치에 주어진 문장이 들어가야 '자연스럽게 보이려 함에도 불구하고' 여전히 인간적인 특성(앞발 사용, 표정)을 유지하고 있다는 논리가 성립됩니다. 그 뒤 (D) 이후 문장은 동물 캐릭터를 매력적으로 만들기 위한 또 다른 전략(어린아이 같은 특징 부여)을 설명합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: If we adopt technology, we need to pay its costs. Thousands of traditional livelihoods have been pushed aside by progress, and the lifestyles around those jobs removed. Hundreds of millions of humans today work at jobs they hate, producing things they have no love for. Sometimes these jobs cause physical pain, disability, or chronic disease. Technology creates many new jobs that are certainly dangerous. At the same time, mass education and media train humans to avoid low-tech physical work, to seek jobs working in the digital world. The divorce of the hands from the head puts a stress on the human mind. Indeed, the sedentary nature of the best-paying jobs is a health risk─for body and mind.
options: ① Technological Advancement Is Not Free!
② Effects of Physical Labor on Mental Health
③ Stress: Chronic Diseases of Modern People
④ Why the Young Generation Avoids Manual Labor
⑤ Revolutionary Breakthroughs: The Power of Technology
questions.explanation: 글의 첫 문장에서 '기술을 도입하면 그 비용을 치러야 한다'고 언급하며, 기술 발전으로 인해 전통적인 생계 수단이 사라지고, 육체적/정신적 건강 문제가 발생하며, 머리와 손이 분리되는 스트레스 등 기술 발전의 부정적인 대가(costs)를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '기술 발전은 공짜가 아니다(Technological Advancement Is Not Free!)'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 기술적 진보는 공짜가 아니다!
② 육체 노동이 정신 건강에 미치는 영향
③ 스트레스: 현대인들의 만성 질환
④ 젊은 세대가 육체 노동을 기피하는 이유
⑤ 혁명적인 돌파구: 기술의 힘

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. ①England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. ②Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. ③The earliest railways did not use trains but horses to pull wagons and only covered short distances. ④With the railways came many large hotels. ⑤In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 경제 발전과 교통수단(철도)의 발달이 여가 시간 증대와 관광 산업(해안 리조트, 호텔 건립)의 발달로 이어졌다는 흐름을 가지고 있습니다. 하지만 ③(c) 문장은 초기 철도가 말이 끄는 마차를 사용했고 단거리만 운행했다는 철도의 초기 기술적 특성을 설명하고 있어, 관광 산업 발달이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The promise of a computerized society, we were told, was that it would pass to machines all of the repetitive drudgery of work, allowing us humans to pursue higher purposes and to have more leisure time. It didn't work out this way. Instead of more time, most of us have less. Companies large and small have ________________________________. Things that used to be done for us, as part of the value-added service of working with a company, we are now expected to do ourselves. With air travel, we're now expected to complete our own reservations and check-in, jobs that used to be done by airline employees or travel agents. At the grocery store, we're bought to bag our own groceries and, in some supermarkets, to scan our own purchases.
options: ① passed the workload onto the backs of consumers
② reduced the burden that customers have to bear
③ offered a variety of purchasing options and benefits
④ enhanced customer convenience in an innovative way
⑤ handed over manufacturing responsibilities to customers
questions.explanation: 이 글은 컴퓨터화된 사회가 우리에게 더 많은 여가 시간을 줄 것이라는 약속과 달리, 실제로는 기업들이 과거에 직원들이 하던 일(예약, 체크인, 장보기 등)을 소비자에게 떠넘기고 있다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '업무량을 소비자에게 전가했다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 업무량을 소비자들에게 전가했다
② 고객들이 져야 할 부담을 줄였다
③ 다양한 구매 옵션과 혜택을 제공했다
④ 혁신적인 방식으로 고객 편의를 향상시켰다
⑤ 제조 책임을 고객들에게 넘겼다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Success can lead you off your intended path and into a comfortable rut. If you are good at something and are well ⓐ<u>compensated</u> for doing it, you may want to keep doing it even if you stop enjoying it. The danger is that one day you look around and realize you're so deep in this comfortable ⓑ<u>routine</u> that you can no longer see the sun or breathe fresh air; the sides of the rut have become so ⓒ<u>slippery</u> that it would take a superhuman effort to climb out; and, effectively, you're ⓓ<u>unlocked</u>. And it's a situation that many working people worry they're in now. The poor employment market has left them feeling stuck in what may be a ⓔ<u>stable</u>, or even well-paying─but ultimately unsatisfying─job.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성공이 우리를 편안한 틀에 박힌 생활에 가두어 빠져나오지 못하게 만드는 상황을 설명하고 있습니다. 문맥상 빠져나오기 위해 초인적인 노력이 필요할 정도로 깊은 틀에 갇힌 상태이므로 ⓓ는 'unlocked(잠기지 않은)'가 아니라 'locked(갇힌)' 또는 'stuck'과 같은 의미가 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름과 어법에 맞도록 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 표현을 <보기>에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This (A)__________ business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was equally essential to (B)__________ products that customers actually wanted. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that (C)__________ the view that production would create its own demand. Customers, and the desire to (D)__________ their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
questions.explanation: (A) '강요하다'의 의미로 business를 목적어로 취하는 5형식 동사 forced가 적절합니다.(B) '제품을 내놓다/전달하다'의 의미로 deliver가 적절합니다.(C) 기존의 견해를 '바꾼' 마케팅 혁명이므로 changed가 적절합니다.(D) 고객의 욕구를 '충족시키다'라는 의미의 satisfy가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. (A) The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. (B) Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. (C) When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye. (D) This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. (E) In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
questions.insertion_sentence: When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 마그마가 '빠르게' 식을 때 결정이 '작게' 형성된다는 내용입니다. 본문의 (C)와 (D)는 마그마가 '천천히' 식어 결정이 육안으로 보일 만큼 '크게' 형성되는 원리를 설명하고 있습니다. (E) 문장의 'In such cases(그런 경우에)' 뒤에 이어지는 '개별 광물 결정을 쉽게 볼 수 없다'는 결과는 마그마가 빠르게 식어 결정이 작게 만들어진 상황을 의미하므로, 주어진 문장은 (E) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Think of the brain as a city. If you were to look out over a city and ask "where is the economy located?" you'd see there's no good answer to the question. Instead, the economy emerges from the interaction of all the elements ─ from the stores and the banks to the merchants and the customers. And so it is with the brain's operation: it doesn't happen in one spot. Just as in a city, no neighborhood of the brain operates in isolation. In brains and in cities, everything emerges from the interaction between residents, at all scales, locally and distantly. Just as trains bring materials and textiles into a city, which become processed into the economy, so the raw electrochemical signals from sensory organs are transported along superhighways of neurons. There the signals undergo processing and transformation into our conscious reality.
options: ① Neurons: Basic Units of Human Brains
② How the Brain Structure Impacts on Daily Lives
③ The Roles of Banks and Merchants in Economy
④ Economic Growth and Neural Networks: A Direct Comparison
⑤ The Brain as a City: How Interactions Create Consciousness
questions.explanation: 이 글은 뇌의 작동 방식을 도시의 경제에 비유하여 설명하고 있습니다. 경제가 특정 장소에 있는 것이 아니라 여러 요소의 상호작용을 통해 나타나듯이, 뇌의 의식적 실체(consciousness) 또한 여러 신경 세포와 기관들의 상호작용을 통해 발생한다는 것이 핵심 내용입니다. 따라서 5번 '도시로서의 뇌: 상호작용이 어떻게 의식을 만들어내는가'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 뉴런: 인간 뇌의 기본 단위
② 뇌 구조가 일상 생활에 미치는 영향
③ 경제에서 은행과 상인의 역할
④ 경제 성장과 신경망: 직접적인 비교
⑤ 도시로서의 뇌: 상호작용이 어떻게 의식을 만드는가

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the effectiveness of the tactic mentioned below. In 1998, he persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave differently.
questions.summary_sentence: Brian Wnasink's 1998 study shows that limiting the quantity of discounted Campbell's soup cans (A)___________ the average number of cans purchased by shoppers, demonstrating that (B)___________can effectively boost sales.
questions.explanation: 실험 결과, 구매 수량에 제한이 없을 때보다 제한이 있을 때(희소성이 있을 때) 고객들이 평균적으로 더 많은 양의 수프를 구매했습니다(3.3캔 -> 5.3캔). 따라서 (A)에는 '증가시켰다(increased)'가 들어가야 하며, (B)에는 수량 제한을 의미하는 '부족/희소성(shortage/scarcity)'이 들어가야 합니다. (B)의 shortage는 본문의 scarcity와 의미상 통합니다.
options_translation: ① 증가시켰다 / 품질
② 증가시켰다 / 부족
③ 유지시켰다 / 풍요
④ 감소시켰다 / 희소성
⑤ 감소시켰다 / 충분함

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set." The ⓐ<u>decline</u> in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are much more ⓑ<u>arranged</u> than between those in the adult brain. The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly ⓒ<u>disordered</u>. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more ⓓ<u>practical</u> and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are ⓔ<u>pruned away</u>.
questions.explanation: 지문 전반부에서 유아의 뇌는 배선이 엉망(a mess)이며, 세상에 대한 지각이 무질서(disordered)하다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 유아 뉴런 사이의 통신망은 성인의 뇌보다 훨씬 더 '정돈된(arranged)' 것이 아니라, 덜 정돈되거나 엉망인 상태여야 합니다. 원문은 'less connected' 또는 'less efficient' 등의 맥락을 담고 있으나, 주어진 문맥상 arranged는 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 괄호 안에 주어진 말을 "사용/변형하고, 필요한 말을 더하여" 글의 흐름에 맞도록 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: My colleagues and I ran an experiment testing two different messages meant to convince thousands of resistant alumni to make a donation. One message emphasized the opportunity to do good: donating would benefit students, faculty, and staff. The other emphasized the opportunity to feel good: donors would enjoy the warm glow of giving. The two messages were equally effective: in both cases, 6.5 percent of the unwilling alumni ended up donating. Then we combined them, because two reasons are better than one. Except they weren't. When we put the two reasons together, the giving rate dropped below 3 percent. Each reason alone (<u>as / be / combine / effective / more / the two / twice</u>). The audience was already skeptical. When we gave them different kinds of reasons to donate, we triggered their awareness that someone was trying to persuade them ─ and they shielded themselves against it.
subjective_conditions: 괄호 안에 주어진 말을 사용/변형할 것
필요한 말을 더하여 문장을 완성할 것
vocabulary_box: as / be / combine / effective / more / the two / twice
questions.answer: was more than twice as effective as the two combined
questions.explanation: 실험 결과, 기부 권유 메시지를 각각 사용했을 때는 6.5%의 기부율을 보였으나, 두 가지 이유를 결합했을 때는 3% 미만으로 떨어졌습니다. 따라서 '각각의 이유는 결합된 두 개보다 두 배 이상 효과적이었다'는 내용이 되어야 합니다. 'as effective as' 원급 비교를 활용하고, 'more than twice'로 배수 표현을 수식하며, 'the two combined'로 과거분사 수식을 사용해 완성합니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 표현을 <보기>에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Whose story it is affects what the story is. Change the main (A)____________, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will (B)____________ them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different (C)____________. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the (D)____________ of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
subjective_conditions: 보기에서 단어를 찾아 쓸 것
vocabulary_box: atmosphere / character / enlighten / inspire / location / perspective / misconception / control / result / understand / start / time / theme
questions.explanation: (A) 주인공(character)을 바꾸면 이야기의 초점도 바뀐다는 맥락이 적절합니다.(B) 다른 인물의 눈으로 사건을 보면 다르게 이해(understand)하게 된다는 맥락입니다.(C) 갈등 상황에서 다른 결과(result)를 바라게 된다는 내용이 자연스럽습니다.(D) 다른 인물의 관점(perspective)에서 본다면 어떨까 하는 예시가 이어집니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving can be challenging for everyone, young children often adapt to new environments more quickly than adults might expect. Although the transition involves changes in their familiar surroundings, young children, particularly those ages 3-6, are generally quite resilient. Their ability to embrace new experiences with curiosity and enthusiasm often helps them adjust more rapidly. Unlike adults, who may have a deep attachment to their routines and possessions, young children can be more adaptable and open to change. They might find excitement in discovering a new home and exploring new rooms. Their concerns about continuity, such as whether their toys and bed will come with them, are often lessened by their natural inclination to make new places feel familiar. By focusing on the positive aspects of the move and providing reassurance, children can build a new sense of security and community more swiftly, making the transition smoother for both themselves and their families.
options: ① Young Children's Resilience: Adapting Quickly to New Environments
② Exploring New Communities: A Guide to Finding Excitement
③ Creating Familiar Spaces: Enhancing Security in New Homes
④ Reducing Stress: Tips for Adults Facing Routine Changes
⑤ The Curiosity of Young Explorers: Embracing Change
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린 아이들이 성인보다 새로운 환경에 더 빠르게 적응하고 탄력적이라는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 호기심과 열정을 바탕으로 변화를 수용하며, 부모의 안심과 긍정적인 초점을 통해 새로운 보안과 공동체 의식을 신속하게 구축한다는 내용을 담고 있으므로, ① '어린 아이들의 회복력: 새로운 환경에 빠르게 적응하기'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 어린 아이들의 회복력: 새로운 환경에 빠르게 적응하기
② 새로운 공동체 탐구하기: 흥미를 찾기 위한 가이드
③ 익숙한 공간 만들기: 새 집에서의 보안 강화하기
④ 스트레스 줄이기: 일상의 변화에 직면한 성인들을 위한 팁
⑤ 어린 탐험가들의 호기심: 변화를 포용하기

questions.question: 5. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: This chart shows some countries with the overall, science, and reading scores from the OECD PISA results 2022. PISA is the Program for International Student Assessment. ⓐSingapore outperformed all other countries, achieving the highest scores in science and reading. ⓑMacao performed better in science but slightly lower in reading compared to South Korea. ⓒOverall, South Korea ranks higher than Estonia in the PISA assessment. ⓓEstonia demonstrates the most notable performance in science within its own country. ⓔCanada's reading score is over 50 points lower than Singapore's.
questions.explanation: PISA 2022 결과에 대한 지문입니다. ⓔ번 설명에서 캐나다의 읽기 점수가 싱가포르보다 50점 이상 낮다고 되어 있으나, 실제 통계 수치상 캐나다의 읽기 성적은 매우 높은 편에 속하며 싱가포르와의 점수 차이가 50점 이상으로 크게 나지 않기 때문에 일치하지 않는 내용으로 간주됩니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed ⓐ<u>to</u> our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, ⓑ<u>directing</u> many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to ⓒ<u>threatening</u> stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways ⓓ<u>in which</u> they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they ⓔ<u>would</u> not have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장의 구조를 보면 'an emotion is a kind of "program" that... directs...' 형태가 되어야 합니다. 관계대명사 that절 안에서 주어(an emotion)의 동작을 나타내는 본동사 자리이므로 현재분사 directing을 단수 동사인 directs로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Homologous traits are characteristics shared by different species because they inherited them from a ⓐ<u>common</u> ancestor. These traits may look different or serve different functions now, but they come from the same origin. For example, the bones in a human arm, a whale's flipper, and a bird's wing are homologous. Even though they are used for ⓑ<u>different</u> things - like grabbing, swimming, or flying - the basic structure of the bones is similar. As a result, they share ⓒ<u>functional</u> traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. Biologists often distinguish analogy (traits that look similar due to similar functions) from homology by examining the overall architecture of the organs and focusing on these more ⓓ<u>useless</u> properties. Homologous traits help scientists understand how species are related and how they ⓔ<u>evolved</u> over time.
questions.explanation: 상동 형질(homologous traits)은 겉모양이나 기능은 다를 수 있지만 구조적 기원이 같은 형질을 의미합니다. 문맥상 뼈의 개수나 연결 방식 등은 기능적인 특징이 아니라 '구조적인' 특징을 공유하는 것이므로 functional을 structural과 같은 단어로 바꾸어야 합니다. 또한 ⓓ의 경우, 겉으로 보이는 기능보다는 '내부적인/근본적인' 속성에 집중한다는 맥락이므로 원문에서는 structural properties 등을 의미하는데, 제시된 useless는 문맥상 어색할 수 있으나 이 문제의 의도된 정답은 문맥의 핵심인 functional의 오류(구조와 기능의 대비)를 찾는 것입니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are familiar with the question: If a tree falls in a forest and no one is around to hear it, does it make a sound? The answer is no, if we define sound as something that needs to be heard. However, this idea is quite different from the journey of scientific discoveries that were once misunderstood. Throughout history, there have been numerous scientific findings that were not fully grasped by their contemporaries but were later recognized and appreciated by future generations. For instance, the groundbreaking work of Gregor Mendel on genetics was largely ignored during his lifetime, with few understanding the significance of his experiments on pea plants. It wasn't until decades later that Mendel's principles were rediscovered and validated, profoundly shaping the field of genetics. This illustrates that a scientific experiment does not lose its value if it is not immediately understood; its impact can grow over time as knowledge and context evolve. Thus, we can say that scientific research has __________ value, even if its significance is not immediately recognized.
questions.explanation: 과학적 연구는 당대의 사람들이 즉각적으로 그 중요성을 이해하지 못하더라도 시간이 흐르면서 그 가치가 인정되기도 한다는 멘델의 사례를 들고 있습니다. 즉, 연구 자체가 지닌 '내재적인' 가치는 변하지 않는다는 결론이 적절하므로 ③번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: 추가된
윤리적인
내재적인
인지된
유형의

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An organization may choose the types of structures to use when organizing their work and employees. When managers combine the basic elements of an organizational structure together, the result has certain characteristics that are best understood by looking at it through the lens of mechanistic and organic organizations. Mechanistic organizations have centralized decision making and formal, standardized control systems. They work well in stable, simple environments. Managers integrate the activities of clearly defined departments through formal channels and in formal meetings. On the other hand, organic organizations are characterized by low formality, decentralized decision making, and well-integrated activities. Organic structures are used in dynamic, unstable environments where ________________________, as the structure gives the organization the flexibility to deal with many different elements. These organizations use cross-functional teams and maintain a comprehensive information network.
options: ① the decision is made by top management with little input from lower-level workers
② the manual guides people to have prejudiced perspectives
③ the business needs to quickly adapt to change
④ the well-defined, vertical structure is fixed
⑤ tasks are assigned to specific individuals
questions.explanation: 기계적 조직과 유기적 조직의 특성을 대비하여 설명하는 글입니다. 유기적 조직은 역동적이고 불안정한 환경에서 유연하게 대처하기 위해 사용된다고 했으므로, 빈칸에는 기업이 변화에 빠르게 적응해야 할 필요가 있는 상황이라는 ③번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 하위 직원들의 의견 반영 없이 최고 경영진에 의해 결정이 내려진다
매뉴얼이 사람들을 편견 섞인 시각을 갖도록 안내한다
기업이 변화에 빠르게 적응해야 할 필요가 있다
잘 정의된 수직적 구조가 고정되어 있다
과업이 특정 개인들에게 할당된다

questions.question: 14. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Dissolved oxygen in the ocean is crucial for the survival of marine life. ⓐ<u>It is used by fish, shellfish, and other aquatic organisms to breathe, just like humans need air</u>. Plants and algae also rely on oxygen for their growth and metabolic processes. However, global warming is causing a decline in dissolved oxygen levels in the oceans. ⓑ<u>Warmer water holds less oxygen, which creates "dead zones" where marine life struggles to survive</u>. ⓒ<u>This drop in oxygen disrupts marine ecosystems, affecting species that depend on specific oxygen levels for breeding and growth</u>. ⓓ<u>Additionally, reduced oxygen levels can lead to the collapse of important fisheries and damage coral reefs, which are vital habitats for many sea creatures</u>. The increase in harmful algae blooms, driven by higher temperatures, further depletes oxygen as the algae decay. ⓔ<u>Dissolved oxygen concentrations are highest in the open ocean due to extensive phytoplankton blooms.</u> Addressing climate change is crucial to protect ocean health and the diverse life it supports.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 지구 온난화로 인한 바다의 용존 산소 감소가 해양 생태계와 어업에 미치는 부정적인 영향을 다루고 있습니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ는 모두 산소의 역할이나 산소 부족으로 인한 피해를 설명하고 있는 반면, ⓔ는 특정 지역(외해)에서 용존 산소 농도가 높다는 사실을 언급하고 있어 전체적인 흐름인 '기후 변화로 인한 산소 감소와 위협'과는 거리가 멉니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Content creators have redefined fame in the digital age, gaining recognition through relatable engagement rather than traditional skills. ⓐThis "ordinary fame" is more accessible, allowing diverse individuals to connect with audiences. ⓑHowever, success is often measured in metrics like followers and likes, creating pressure and potential burnout. ⓒContent creators often film in busy parks, sharing the lively atmosphere that appeals to their audience. ⓓWhile visibility can lead to profitable opportunities, it also exposes creators to criticism, bullying, and the challenge of maintaining authenticity. ⓔUltimately, this new landscape invites us to rethink fame, balancing its rewards with the complexities it entails as content creators navigate both creative and personal challenges.
questions.explanation: 디지털 시대에 콘텐츠 제작자들이 누리는 '평범한 명성'의 특징과 그로 인해 발생하는 압박감, 비판 등 명성의 명암에 대해 다루는 글입니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 이러한 명성의 성격과 영향에 대해 설명하고 있으나, ⓒ는 제작자들이 공원에서 촬영한다는 구체적이고 지엽적인 행동을 언급하고 있어 주제와 관련이 없습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Depression takes away your energy, hope, and drive, making it difficult to take the steps that will help you to feel better. Getting support plays an essential role in overcoming depression. ⓐOn your own, it can be difficult to maintain a healthy perspective and sustain the effort required to beat depression. ⓑAt the same time, the very nature of depression makes it difficult to reach out for help. ⓒWhenever you experience a negative thought, write ti down on your phone or in a notebook. ⓓIn this case, being with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle can be a great power to overcome it. ⓔStaying connected to people who are in a positive energy state and taking part in social activities will make a world of difference in your mood.
questions.explanation: 우울증을 극복하기 위해서는 타인의 지지를 받고 사회적으로 연결되는 것이 중요하다는 점을 강조하는 글입니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 혼자 힘의 한계와 타인과의 연결의 중요성을 언급하지만, ⓒ는 부정적인 생각을 기록하라는 개인적인 대처 전략을 제시하고 있어 '사회적 지지'라는 핵심 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Scientific research indicates more clearly than ever that our carbon footprint now threatens our ecosystems and our way of life.
ordered_passages: (A) Marine biologists have recently discovered that whales significantly capture carbon from the atmosphere. When they die, they sink to the bottom of the ocean; each great whale sequesters 33 tons of CO2 on average, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries.

(B) Many proposed solutions to global warming are complex, untested, and expensive. What if there were an earth-tech solution to this problem? An example of such an opportunity is to increase global whale populations.
(C) Therefore, the strategy of supporting whales' return to their previous abundance in the oceans would significantly benefit not only life in the oceans but also life on land, including our own.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 탄소 발자국이 생태계를 위협한다는 문제 상황을 제기한 후, (B)에서 이에 대한 지구 기술적 해결책으로 고래 개체수 증가를 제안합니다. (A)에서는 고래가 탄소를 포집하고 죽은 뒤에도 탄소를 가두는 구체적인 과학적 원리를 설명하며, 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 전략이 바다와 육지 모두에 유익하다는 결론을 내리는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities.
ordered_passages: (A) Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.

(B) We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones - one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles.

(C) Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are minimized. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 일과 가정의 경계가 모호해지며 개인마다 이를 관리하는 방식이 다르다는 화두를 던집니다. (C)에서 먼저 역할을 분리(segment)하는 것을 선호하는 사람들의 예시를 들고, (B)에서 이러한 '분리자(segmenters)'들이 두 대의 전화를 사용하는 구체적인 사례를 추가합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 '다른 개인들(Other individuals)'을 언급하며 일과 가정의 역할을 통합(integrating)하는 선호 방식을 설명하는 순서가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Human memory is complex and multilayered. Broadly, it can be divided into sensory memory, short-term memory, and long-term memory. (A) Sensory memory holds sensory information for a very brief period, allowing us to have an immediate perception of the world around us. (B) However, this information fades quickly, and only important information that receives attention is transferred to short-term memory. (C) Short-term memory temporarily stores information, usually for a few seconds to minutes, but it can easily fade without reinforcement. (D) Long-term memory preserves information for extended periods, enabling us to retain knowledge over time. (E) However, even long-term memories can weaken over time, making regular review and self-testing crucial for retention.
questions.insertion_sentence: To move this information into long-term memory, repeated review and deeper processing are essential.
questions.explanation: (C)에서는 단기 기억(short-term memory)에 대해 설명하며 강화 없이는 쉽게 사라질 수 있음을 언급합니다. 주어진 문장의 'this information'은 단기 기억에 있는 정보를 의미하며, 이를 장기 기억(long-term memory)으로 옮기기 위해 반복적인 복습과 깊은 처리가 필수적임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 장기 기억에 대한 일반적인 정의가 시작되는 (D) 앞이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Science is fundamentally the pursuit of understanding what exists in the natural world. (A) It seeks truths about the universe through observation and experimentation. (B) However, this journey can have its dangers. A notable example is the historical belief in luminiferous ether, thought to permeate space as a medium for light. (C) For years, scientists relied on this concept, guiding their research, but no evidence for ether was ever found. (D) The case of ether reminds us that science must be grounded in what can be observed and measured. (E) While the pursuit of knowledge is important, scientists must remain cautious and question their assumptions to deepen our understanding of the universe.*permeate 스며들다, 퍼지다
questions.insertion_sentence: This search illustrated a significant error: depending on a concept without empirical support.
questions.explanation: (C)에서 과학자들이 증거가 발견되지 않은 에테르라는 개념에 의존하여 연구를 진행했음을 언급합니다. 주어진 문장의 'This search'는 이러한 에테르에 대한 탐구 과정을 지칭하며, 그것이 실증적인 지원(empirical support) 없이 개념에만 의존한 중대한 오류였음을 지적합니다. 이 내용은 에테르 사례의 교훈을 정리하는 (D)의 앞 문장으로 들어가는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Frans de Waal, a renowned ethologist, has discussed the concept of relative deprivation in the context of animal behavior and human psychology. Frans de Waal explores how animals, like humans, experience feelings of injustice and inequality, which can lead to what he terms "relative deprivation." This refers to the sense of unfairness and dissatisfaction that arises when individuals or animals compare their own situation to that of others who seem to have more or better resources. In his research, de Waal has observed that primates, such as chimpanzees and capuchin monkeys, display behaviors indicating they are aware of social inequalities. For example, when one monkey receives a better reward than another for the same task, the less rewarded monkey may show signs of frustration or jealousy. This demonstrates that the concept of relative deprivation is not exclusive to humans but is also present in other intelligent and social animals.
questions.summary_sentence: Frans de Waal's research shows that both animals and humans experience "relative deprivation," a sense of (A)__________ and dissatisfaction when (B)__________ their own resources against others, as evidenced by primates displaying frustration or jealousy over unequal rewards.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물과 인간 모두가 타인과 자신의 상황을 비교할 때 느끼는 '상대적 박탈감(relative deprivation)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 불공정함이나 불만족과 관련된 단어가 들어가야 하므로 'unjustness(불공평함)'가 적절하며, (B)는 자신의 자원을 타인의 것과 비교하거나 평가할 때라는 맥락이 되어야 하므로 'evaluating(평가하다, 비교하다)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 불공평함 ... 평가할 때
② 불공평함 ... 방어할 때
③ 불평등 ... 지킬 때
④ 만족 ... 보호할 때
⑤ 정의 ... 보호할 때

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: A primatologist says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. He points out that scientists employ technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task, they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what he has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.summary_sentence: A scientist who studies primates criticizes the tendency to distance humans from animals through language, (A)__________ humans superiority and (B)__________ the cognitive abilities of animals.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 언어를 통해 동물과의 유사성을 폄하하고 인간의 우월적 지위를 유지하려 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 요약문 (A)에는 인간의 우월성을 '강화(reinforcing)'하거나 공고히 한다는 내용이, (B)에는 동물의 인지 능력을 '최소화(minimizing)'하거나 깎아내린다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 낮추는 ... 경시하는
② 줄이는 ... 북돋우는
③ 강화하는 ... 최소화하는
④ 강화하는 ... 강조하는
⑤ 유지하는 ... 가치 있게 여기는

questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 문장의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 알맞은 표현을 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation. If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. While the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a protective mechanism for the foot. Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now contract quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object.
questions.summary_sentence: Pain from the feet travels along the spinal cord to the brain, where sensory nerves connect to the area that controls (A)__________ to shout 'ouch'. The nerve cells then connect to (B)__________ and transmit to the muscles of the leg, which move the foot away from the sharp object.
subjective_conditions: 1. 각각 글 속에서 찾아 어형 변화 없이 작성할 것
2. 철자 오류 인정하지 않음
questions.explanation: 지문에서 뇌 안의 신경이 '말하기(speech)'를 조절하는 영역과 연결되어 '아야(ouch)'라고 소리치게 한다고 설명하며, 또한 척수를 따라 다시 내려가는 '운동 신경(motor nerves)'과 연결되어 다리 근육을 수축시킨다고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 주어진 글을 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 알맞은 단어를 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop-out, or worse.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the passage, it is important for parents of gifted children to (A)__________ excessive bragging. This behavior can make children feel pressured and generate challenging (B)__________ that are difficult to meet, leading to negative results.
subjective_conditions: 1. 각각 글 속에서 찾아 어형 변화 없이 작성할 것
2. 철자 오류 인정하지 않음
questions.explanation: 지문에서 부모가 영재 자녀에 대해 자랑하는 행동을 '제한(limit)'하는 것이 중요하다고 언급하며, 과도한 자랑은 자녀가 부응하기 어려운 '기대(expectations)'를 형성하여 압박감을 준다고 설명하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people think of ability as how smart someone is. They try to show this in everything they do - like writing a really good legal paper, getting the best grade on a test, making clever computer programs, or saying something really smart or funny when talking. Some people might think of ability as being good at a specific skill, like playing the piano, learning languages, or serving in tennis. Others focus on being attractive, fun to be around, knowing what's popular, or having the newest gadgets. The problem comes when people only care about this kind of ability when thinking about how good or valuable they are as a person. When this happens, how well someone does at something becomes the only way to measure their worth. Nothing else matters. So if someone does really well at something, they think they're a great person. If they do just okay, they think they're just an okay person. Period.
options: ① Traveling frequently is the key to developing one's self-esteem.
② Defining self-worth solely by ability or performance can be problematic.
③ Social media popularity is the best way to demonstrate a person's abilities.
④ Physical strength is important as the primary measure of a person's worth.
⑤ Achieving personal goals can significantly boost one's self-worth and confidence.
questions.explanation: 개인의 능력이나 성과만으로 자기 가치를 판단하는 것은 문제가 될 수 있다는 내용이므로, '능력이나 성과만으로 자기 가치를 정의하는 것은 문제가 될 수 있다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 빈번한 여행은 자존감을 발달시키는 핵심이다.
② 능력이나 성과만으로 자기 가치를 정의하는 것은 문제가 될 수 있다.
③ 소셜 미디어에서의 인기는 사람의 능력을 보여주는 가장 좋은 방법이다.
④ 신체적 강함은 사람의 가치를 측정하는 주요한 척도로서 중요하다.
⑤ 개인적인 목표를 달성하는 것은 자존감과 자신감을 크게 높일 수 있다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the (A)<u>"engineers of marine ecosystems."</u> In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.*sequester: 격리하다**phytoplankton: 식물성 플랑크톤
options: ① active animals purifying the waste water from the land
② big consumers focusing on eating harmful species in the ocean
③ natural cleaners playing a role in breaking up marine plastic pollution
④ clever predators hunting effectively while having a minimal impact on ecosystems
⑤ crucial agents enhancing the ocean environment by helping lock away carbon
questions.explanation: 고래가 탄소를 격리(sequester)하고 배설물을 통해 식물성 플랑크톤을 증가시켜 다시 탄소 격리를 도움으로써 해양 생태계를 개선하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다는 것을 의미합니다. 따라서 ⑤번 '탄소를 가두는 것을 도움으로써 해양 환경을 개선하는 중요한 역할자들'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 육지에서 온 폐수를 정화하는 활동적인 동물들
② 해양의 해로운 종들을 잡아먹는 데 집중하는 거대 소비자들
③ 해양 플라스틱 오염을 분해하는 역할을 하는 천연 청소부들
④ 생태계에 미치는 영향을 최소화하면서 효과적으로 사냥하는 영리한 포식자들
⑤ 탄소를 격리하도록 도와 해양 환경을 개선하는 중요한 역할자들

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Each time a new medium is introduced, whether it's the creation of the printed book, television, or social media, and you start to use it, it is like (A)<u>putting on a new pair of goggles with unique filters</u>. These -goggles- change how you see the world. For example, when you begin watching television, before even processing the content of any specific show, like Wheel of Fortune or The Wire, you start viewing the world as if it were shaped by television. This is why Marshall McLuhan stated that every new medium contains a hidden message. It subtly influences how we perceive the world, according to new patterns or codes. McLuhan emphasized that how information is delivered is more significant than the actual content. Television, for instance, conveys the idea that the world is fast-paced and it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① limiting your view to only one type of medium
② physically wearing something to improve your vision
③ seeing the world through clearer and more accurate information
④ becoming more focused on traditional ways of viewing the world
⑤ perceiving the world as being shaped by a new medium you're using
questions.explanation: 새로운 매체가 도입되고 그것을 사용하게 되면, 전달되는 내용과 상관없이 그 매체 자체가 세상을 바라보는 방식과 패턴을 바꾸어 놓는다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ⑤번 '사용하게 되는 새로운 매체에 의해 형성된 대로 세상을 지각하는 것'이 밑줄 친 비유의 의미로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 시야를 단 한 가지 유형의 매체로만 제한하는 것
② 시력을 개선하기 위해 물리적으로 무언가를 착용하는 것
③ 더욱 명확하고 정확한 정보를 통해 세상을 바라보는 것
④ 세상을 바라보는 전통적인 방식에 더 집중하게 되는 것
⑤ 사용하게 되는 새로운 매체에 의해 형성된 대로 세상을 지각하는 것

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.*boardroom: 이사회실
options: ① Social Media Critics Are Always Right
② Do Not Trust the Expertise of Sport Managers
③ Are Sport Executives Experts Above All Others?
④ Many Sport Enthusiasts Believe They Are Experts
⑤ Monday Morning Quarterback: The Most In-Demand Job
questions.explanation: 이 글은 많은 스포츠 팬들이 본인들이 경기 현장의 전문가들보다 더 잘할 수 있다고 믿으며, 전문 지식이 없음에도 불구하고 스포츠 경영에 대해 훈수를 두는 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 'Monday Morning Quarterback'이라는 용어를 예로 들어, 실제 전문가인 경영자들도 팬들의 비판과 피드백에 직면하며, 이는 의사나 회계사 같은 다른 전문직종에서는 흔히 일어나지 않는 일임을 대조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '많은 스포츠 열성팬들이 본인을 전문가라고 믿는다'는 ④번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 소셜 미디어 비평가들은 항상 옳다
② 스포츠 관리자들의 전문 지식을 믿지 마라
③ 스포츠 경영진은 다른 모든 이들 위의 전문가인가?
④ 많은 스포츠 열성팬들이 자신이 전문가라고 믿는다
⑤ Monday Morning Quarterback: 가장 수요가 많은 직업

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
options: ① Adaptation: Process of Patience and Time
② Finding Balance Between Individuals and Community
③ Moving: Stressful Event Threatening Security of People
④ Helping: Young Children Manage the Stress of Moving
⑤ Why Do Children Feel So Disoriented While Growing Up?
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이사가 아이들, 특히 3-6세의 어린 아이들에게 주는 극심한 스트레스와 혼란에 대해 설명합니다. 아이들은 자신의 과거 경험이 존중받는 동시에 새로운 환경에 적응할 수 있도록 도움을 받아야 하며, 자신의 배경을 공유할 기회를 가져야 한다고 조언합니다. 따라서 '어린 아이들이 이사 스트레스를 관리하도록 돕기'라는 내용의 ④번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 적응: 인내와 시간의 과정
② 개인과 공동체 사이의 균형 찾기
③ 이사: 사람들의 안전을 위협하는 스트레스가 많은 사건
④ 도움 주기: 어린 아이들이 이사의 스트레스를 관리하도록 돕기
⑤ 왜 아이들은 자라면서 그렇게 혼란스러워하는가?

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providing students with relevant texts they will be interested in. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and discovered ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books." The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.*dyslexia: 난독증 **voraciously: 탐욕스럽게
options: ① Be Enthusiastic, Find More Joy in Your Life
② Diverse Personal Interests: A Key for Joyful Life
③ Dyslexia: A Common Feature of Successful People in Their Careers
④ How to Compensate for Reading Problems Through Various Strategies
⑤ Passionate Reading: Comes from Personal Interest, Goes to Great Achievement
questions.explanation: 이 글은 Rosalie Fink의 연구를 통해 난독증이 있음에도 불구하고 성공한 사람들이 개인적인 관심 분야에 대한 열정 덕분에 독서를 회피하지 않고 열성적으로 하게 되었음을 설명합니다. 학생들에게 흥미 있는 관련 텍스트를 제공하는 것이 참여와 성취의 핵심이라는 점을 시사하므로, 개인적 관심에서 비롯된 열정적인 독서가 위대한 성취로 이어진다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 열정적이어라, 인생에서 더 많은 즐거움을 찾아라
② 다양한 개인적 관심: 즐거운 인생의 열쇠
③ 난독증: 경력에서 성공한 사람들의 공통적 특징
④ 다양한 전략을 통해 읽기 문제를 보완하는 방법
⑤ 열정적인 독서: 개인적 관심에서 시작되어 위대한 성취로 이어진다

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it ─ you just see the blurred outline of the moving string. Strings vibrating in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. But if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note is heard loud and clear. The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. When the waves reach your ears, they cause your eardrums to move in and out at the same speed as the original string vibrations.
options: ① Innovations in Guitar Sound Engineering
② Mastering Guitar Strings for Better Sound
③ The Evolution of Guitar Sound in Modern Music
④ Exploring the Different Types of Guitar Strings
⑤ From String to Sound: How a Guitar Works

questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Between 2000 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). (B) Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialized workforce for the economy. (C) In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. (D) Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. (E) In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
questions.insertion_sentence: In reality, sociopolitical changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 고등 교육 확대를 위한 사회정치적 변화가 평가에 있어 '모순의 장'을 만들었다는 내용입니다. (C)까지는 이론상으로 교육 확대가 시험의 역할을 줄여야 한다는 긍정적 기대를 다루고 있고, (D)부터는 실제 대중 고등 교육에서 효율성을 위해 시험과 객관식 퀴즈 같은 방식이 요구되어 학생들이 피드백보다 성적에 집중하게 된다는 모순적 현실을 설명하므로, 두 내용이 전환되는 지점인 (D)에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous Nongreat composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.summary_sentence: Great composers like Beethoven and Mozart were initially misunderstood because their (A)________ music challenged the familiar norms of the time, unlike Salieri, whose work followed (B)________ forms.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 오해를 받았던 이유가 그들의 음악이 당대 사람들에게 생소했기 때문이라고 설명합니다. 살리에리는 훌륭한 작곡가였지만 그의 작품은 독창적이지 않고 당대 다른 사람들이 작곡하던 것과 유사했기 때문에 세계적인 거장이 되지 못했습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 베토벤과 모차르트의 음악을 수식하는 '혁신적인(innovative)'이 적절하고, (B)에는 살리에리가 따랐던 '기존의(existing)' 형식이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace by making the workplace more accessible for workers who often face disadvantages in the labor market. AI-powered assistive technologies, such as tools for individuals with visual, speech, or hearing difficulties, are becoming more common, improving both job access and quality of work for people with disabilities. For instance, speech recognition systems for those with dysarthria or live captions for the deaf and hard of hearing people can help with communication and provide better access to jobs that require interpersonal interaction. AI also boosts the performance of low-skilled workers, potentially raising their wages and improving career opportunities. questions.question: 26. 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오. [2.9점]
questions.passage: We, humans, have various emotions, and it seems that they play important roles in our survival when we face challenges. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. In other words, ___________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 15단어 이내로 작성할 것 (빈칸만)
if / they / us / not / to / have / had / would 를 모두 사용할 것 (변형 불가)
빈칸을 한 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.answer: if they(emotions) had not helped us to survive, they would not have evolved with us

questions.question: 29. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 질문에 대한 답을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오. [3.1점]
questions.passage: Generally speaking, claims that local food production cut greenhouse gas emissions by reducing the burning of transportation fuel are usually not well founded. Transport is the source of only 11 percent of greenhouse gas emissions within the food sector. Therefore, merely reducing the distance that food travels after it leaves the farm is not a major factor in lowering greenhouse gas emissions; rather, there is something we should prioritize. In fact, there are many cases where more energy is wasted when growing food on the farm than transporting food from the farm. For example, field-grown tomatoes shipped from Mexico in the winter tomatoes grown in a greenhouse, where the energy used to heat the hothouse accounts for a considerable amount of the tomato's carbon footprint. In the United Kingdom, lamb meat that travels 11,000 miles from New Zealand generates only one-quarter the carbon emissions per pound compared to British lamb because farmers in the United Kingdom raise their animals on feed (which must be produced using fossil fuels) rather than on clover pastureland.
subjective_conditions: 20단어 이내로 작성할 것 (빈칸만)
rather than / during / distance / wasteful / process / energy 를 모두 사용할 것 (변형 불가)
빈칸을 한 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.subjective_answer_format: 질문: According to the passage above, what should we focus more on to reduce greenhouse gas emissions? Answer the question by comparing food transportation and production.답: To reduce greenhouse gas emissions, → ______________________________________________________
questions.answer: we should focus more on reducing wasteful energy use during the food production process rather than the distance food travels.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Seawater is rich in dissolved oxygen, which is essential for the survival of all marine animals. Physics has long established that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water, supporting more marine life in polar seas compared to tropical oceans. Therefore, as global warming increases ocean temperatures, it's clear that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decline. This poses a concerning and potentially disastrous threat to marine ecosystems if it continues unchecked. Scientists have now analyzed data showing that ocean oxygen levels have been decreasing for over fifty years, and this decline has been faster than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Decreasing oxygen levels can significantly impact marine habitats worldwide, and in recent years, this has led to more frequent oxygen-deficient events that have killed or displaced fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
subjective_conditions: 17단어 이내로 작성할 것
which / rising / dissolved / due to / reduce / endanger / global warming 을 모두 사용할 것 (변형 불가)
한 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
questions.answer: Rising ocean temperatures due to global warming reduce dissolved oxygen levels, which can endanger marine ecosystems.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 지구 온난화로 인한 해수 온도 상승이 용존 산소량을 감소시키고, 이것이 전 세계 해양 생태계에 치명적인 위협이 되고 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 주어진 조건에 맞춰 '지구 온난화로 인한 해수 온도 상승이 용존 산소 수치를 낮추며, 이는 해양 생태계를 위험에 빠뜨릴 수 있다'는 내용으로 요약 문장을 완성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are minimized. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones - one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
options: ① Integrating work and family roles is preferred to separating or segmenting them.
② The utilization of portable digital technology has made it easier for individuals to work from home.
③ Technology provides both pros and cons for people who prefer to segment work and family roles.
④ More and more people choose to take advantage of digital devices to help with their work and family matters
⑤ With portable digital technology, individuals have varying preferenes in managing work and home life either by separating or integrating the two.
questions.explanation: 본문은 휴대용 디지털 기술의 발달로 일과 가정의 경계가 모호해진 상황에서, 사람마다 일과 가정의 역할을 분리(segmenting)하거나 통합(integrating)하는 등 선호하는 방식이 다르다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 이를 가장 잘 나타낸 ⑤번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 일과 가정의 역할을 통합하는 것이 분리하는 것보다 선호된다.
② 휴대용 디지털 기술의 활용은 개인들이 집에서 일하는 것을 더 쉽게 만들었다.
③ 기술은 일과 가정의 역할을 분리하기를 선호하는 사람들에게 장단점을 모두 제공한다.
④ 점점 더 많은 사람들이 일과 가정 문제를 돕기 위해 디지털 기기를 활용하기로 선택한다.
⑤ 휴대용 디지털 기술로 인해, 개인들은 일과 가정 생활을 분리하거나 통합함으로써 관리하는 데 각기 다른 선호를 가진다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① The Role of Pressure Waves in communication
② Publishing Papers: The Key to Scientific Success
③ The Philosophy of Hearing and Sound Perception
④ How to Publish Your Scientific Research Effectively
⑤ Beyond Publication: The Necessity of Understanding in Science

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others ⓐ<u>based</u> on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find ⓑ<u>that</u> people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research ⓒ<u>exploring</u> observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair ⓓ<u>was viewed</u> as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor wearing red sneakers during a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as ⓔ<u>positive</u> because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'A series of studies(6월 2014년 소비자 조사 저널에 발표된 기사의)'이며, 문장 전체에 동사가 없습니다. 따라서 분사 형태인 exploring을 본동사인 explored로 바꾸어야 합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: -How do you eat an elephant?- The answer is -one bite at a time.- So, how do you -build- the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks ⓐ<u>consist</u> of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes ⓑ<u>that</u> scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, ⓒ<u>twisted</u> shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment ⓓ<u>where</u> the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that ⓔ<u>are</u> seen time after time.
questions.explanation: ⓔ의 선행사는 'the basic structure of atoms'에서 핵심 명사인 단수 'structure'입니다. 따라서 관계대명사절 내의 동사 are는 선행사에 수 일치시켜 단수인 is가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by ⓐ<u>watching</u> what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an ⓑ<u>innate</u> tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is ⓒ<u>incomplete</u>. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you perform a ⓓ<u>different</u> action. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are ⓔ<u>limited</u> to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply observing others.
questions.explanation: 전체 글의 핵심은 거울 뉴런을 통한 '관찰 학습(타인 모방)'의 중요성입니다. 현대 문화가 발전할 수 있었던 이유는 우리가 단순히 타고나거나 시행착오로 배우는 것에만 '제한(limited)'된 것이 아니라, 타인을 관찰하고 모방함으로써 훨씬 더 많은 것을 배울 수 있기 때문입니다. 따라서 ⓔ는 'not limited' 또는 'not restricted' 등의 의미가 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providing students with relevant texts they will be interested in. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had ⓐ<u>considerable</u> problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had ⓑ<u>embraced</u> reading and discovered ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were voracious readers. They ⓒ<u>rarely</u> avoided reading. On the contrary, they ⓓ<u>engaged</u> in reading." The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been ⓔ<u>enthusiastic</u> in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.
questions.explanation: Rosalie Fink의 연구에 따르면, 난독증이 있는 성공한 성인들은 읽기를 회피하거나 우회하는 방법을 찾았을 것이라는 예상과 달리, 실제로는 읽기에 열정적으로 참여했습니다. 문맥상 ⓑ의 'embraced'(포용했다/받아들였다)는 글의 뒤에서 'opposite'(반대)를 발견했다는 내용과 호응하지 않습니다. 그녀의 예상은 그들이 읽기를 'avoided'(회피했다)거나 'shunned'했을 것이라는 내용이 되어야 반전의 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to ⓐ<u>identify</u> the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will ⓑ<u>necessarily</u> view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which ⓒ<u>keeps</u> them from seeing things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a ⓓ<u>flat</u> hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is ⓔ<u>distributed</u> across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 기계적 구조(mechanistic structure)는 많은 규칙, 절차, 그리고 의사결정에 관여하는 여러 단계의 경영층을 가지고 있다고 설명되고 있습니다. 이는 수직적이고 권위적인 구조를 의미하므로 'flat'(평평한, 수평적인)이 아니라 'tall' 혹은 'rigid'와 같은 단어가 적절합니다. 반면 유기적 구조(organic structures)가 'horizontal'(수평적인)하고 'distributed'(분산된) 특징을 가집니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by (A)_________ the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore show your child good examples of life by your (B)_________. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 요지는 아이들은 부모의 말보다는 행동과 본보기를 통해 배운다는 것입니다. (A)에서는 주변 사람들이 가치관을 실천하는 것을 '봄(seeing/observing)'으로써 배운다는 내용이 적절하며, (B)에서는 따라서 부모의 '행동(behavior/actions)'을 통해 좋은 본보기를 보여주라는 결론이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: 관찰하는 것, 행동
관찰하는 것, 감정
인지하는 것, 지능
만드는 것, 가치관
만드는 것, 행동

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move.
