Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to __________________________________________. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
options: ① ignore their feelings and focus solely on the process of moving
② allow them to pick new toys that will replace their old belongings
③ prioritize making new friends over processing their feelings about the move
④ balance acknowledging children's past experiences with supporting their adjustment to the new environment
⑤ recognize the advantages and disadvantages of a move and discuss the changes associated with the transition
questions.explanation: 이사 과정에서 아이들의 불안함을 해소하기 위해 아이들의 과거 경험(과거의 집, 물건 등)을 존중하면서 동시에 새로운 환경에 적응하도록 돕는 균형이 중요하다는 내용이 빈칸 뒤의 '과거를 존중하는 방식으로 배경을 공유할 기회'라는 문장과 잘 연결됩니다.
options_translation: 그들의 감정을 무시하고 오로지 이사 과정에만 집중하는 것
낡은 물건을 대체할 새로운 장난감을 고르게 해주는 것
이사 자체에 대한 감정을 처리하는 것보다 새로운 친구를 사귀는 것을 우선시하는 것
아이들의 과거 경험을 인정하는 것과 새로운 환경으로의 적응을 지원하는 것 사이의 균형을 맞추는 것
이사의 장단점을 인식하고 변화와 관련된 전환에 대해 논의하는 것

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they _______________________________________. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
options: ① play a vital role in the urban ecosystem
② are actually an inessential component to making cities greener
③ can produce noise, which can reduce the quality of the urban environment
④ emit greenhouse gases, such as carbon dioxide, with a negative impact in the environment
⑤ can cause traffic congestion, which increases fuel consumption and leads to additional emissions
questions.explanation: 이 글은 도심 내 차량 통행을 줄이고 자전거와 보행자 중심의 환경을 구축하는 것에 대해 설명하면서, 배달 차량의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 지문 후반부에서 배달 차량이 여러 대의 승용차보다 효율적으로 물건을 운송하며, 주거지 근처의 작은 상점 운영을 가능하게 하여 주민들이 차를 타지 않고 걸어서 장을 볼 수 있게 해준다고 설명합니다. 따라서 배달 차량이 도시 생태계에서 '중요한 역할을 한다'는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 도시 생태계에서 중요한 역할을 한다
② 사실 도시를 더 친환경적으로 만드는 데 있어 불필요한 요소이다
③ 소음을 발생시켜 도시 환경의 질을 떨어뜨릴 수 있다
④ 이산화탄소와 같은 온실가스를 배출하여 환경에 부정적인 영향을 미친다
⑤ 교통 혼잡을 야기하여 연료 소비를 늘리고 추가적인 배출로 이어진다

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself.
ordered_passages: (A) The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor, less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.

(B) Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity.

(C) However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 소셜 미디어 크리에이터들이 평범한 명성을 그 자체로 갈구한다는 내용을 소개합니다. (B)에서 이들이 전통적인 엘리트 연예인과 같은 재능이 없다는 비판을 받는다는 점을 언급하며 명성 획득의 장벽을 설명합니다. (C)에서 'However'를 통해 이러한 비판이 명성의 의미를 재구성하는 '평범한 유명인(ordinary celebrity)' 현상의 본질을 놓치고 있음을 지적합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 평범한 유명인이 어떻게 소통을 통해 관심을 얻고, 소셜 미디어 내의 수치(구독자, 좋아요 등)를 통해 명성을 쌓는지 구체적으로 설명하는 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved.
ordered_passages: (A) If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter.

(B) Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.

(C) I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 카푸친 원숭이들이 인간과 물건(음식)을 거래하는 습성에 대해 말합니다. (C)에서 구체적인 실험 상황인 '돌을 주고 오이를 받는 상황'을 제시하며 두 원숭이가 모두 만족하는 상태를 보여줍니다. (A)에서 'however'와 함께 한 원숭이에게만 더 선호되는 '포도'를 주는 상황으로 변화를 줍니다. (B)에서 여전히 오이를 받는 원숭이가 상황을 '불공정'하다고 느끼고 불만을 표출하기 위해 오이를 던지는 등의 반응을 보인다는 결론으로 이어지는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. (A) This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. (B) When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. (C) A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. (D) On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive, it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. (E) They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.insertion_sentence: Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 다양성이 노동 시장뿐만 아니라 삶의 질에도 영향을 미칠 수 있다는 내용입니다. (A)와 (B)는 노동 생산성과 관련된 다양성의 장점과 단점(노동 시장 영향)을 설명하고 있으며, (C)부터는 관용적인 원주민이 다문화 도시를 가치 있게 여긴다는 삶의 질과 관련된 긍정적 측면이 시작되므로 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. (A) Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. (B) Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. (C) If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? (D) However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. (E) Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
questions.insertion_sentence: But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 많은 승객들이 비행 대신 운전을 선택한다는 내용이 나오고, 주어진 문장에서 '하지만 그들의 운전 결정은 논리가 아닌 감정에 근거한다'라고 설명한 뒤, (B)에서 그에 대한 구체적인 통계적 수치(논리적 근거)를 제시하며 비행기보다 자동차 사고 확률이 훨씬 높음을 대조하고 있으므로 (B)가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous nongreat composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.summary_sentence: Some of the greatest composers, like Beethoven and Stravinsky, were initially misunderstood because their ideas were not (A)____________, while composers like Antonio Salieri, though famous, lacked the (B)____________ that defines greatness.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 이해받지 못한 이유는 'unfamiliarity(익숙하지 않음)' 때문이라고 하였으므로 (A)에는 ideas가 친숙하지 않았다는 의미의 familiar가 적합합니다. 반면 살리에리는 당대 사람들과 비슷한 곡을 썼기 때문에 위대하지 않았으므로 위대함을 정의하는 '독창성(originality)'이 부족했다는 (B)가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 친숙한 / 독창성
② 독특한 / 인기
③ 친숙한 / 효율성
④ 독특한 / 창의성
⑤ 혁신적인 / 단순함

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where interpersonal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, Al's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.summary_sentence: AI enhances workplace (A)___________ by providing assistive devices for individuals with disabilities and improving the performance of low-skilled workers, ultimately (B)___________ their communication, job access, and career prospects.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 AI가 장애가 있는 노동자들을 위한 보조 장치를 제공하고, 저숙련 노동자들의 능력을 향상함으로써 직장 내 포용성(inclusiveness)을 개선할 수 있다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 이러한 기술적 도움은 궁극적으로 그들의 의사소통, 일자리 접근성 및 경력 전망에 도움(benefiting)을 줍니다. 따라서 (A)에는 inclusiveness, (B)에는 benefiting이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 윤리성 - 평등하게 하는
접근성 - 저하시키는
접근성 - 억제하는
포용성 - 방해하는
포용성 - 혜택을 주는

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <보기>에 주어진 표현을 사용하여 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [24년 9월 38번]
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may ______________________________________ and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용할 것
필요시 주어진 표현을 중복하여 사용할 것
questions.answer: not have a common function but they descended from a common ancestor
questions.explanation: 이 글은 생물학에서 상조성(analogy)과 상동성(homology)을 구분하는 기준에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 상동 형질(homologous traits)은 기능은 다를 수 있으나 공통 조상으로부터 물려받은 구조를 가진다는 특징이 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '공통된 기능을 갖지 않을 수도 있지만 공통 조상으로부터 유래했다'는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "linguistic castration"이 의미하는 바를 <보기>에 주어진 표현을 사용하여 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [23년 9월 32번]
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "<u>linguistic castration</u>."
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용할 것
형태를 변형하지 말 것
단어를 추가하거나 중복하여 사용하지 말 것
questions.answer: the practice of using language to disempower animals while upholding human superiority within an imaginary hierarchy
questions.explanation: 프란스 드 발은 인간이 상상 속의 계층 구조 상단에 위치하기 위해 동물의 능력을 비하하는 용어를 사용하는 현상을 '언어적 거세(linguistic castration)'라고 명명했습니다. 이는 가상의 위계 내에서 인간의 우월성을 유지하면서 동물의 힘을 약화시키기 위해 언어를 사용하는 관행을 의미합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <보기>에 주어진 표현을 사용하여 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [23년 9월 29번]
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find _____________________________________. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용할 것
필요시 형태를 변형할 것
단어를 추가하거나 중복하여 사용하지 말 것
questions.answer: themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from people without any expertise
questions.explanation: 스포츠 관리 분야의 전문가들이 전문 지식이 없는 팬들로부터 업무 방식에 대한 충고를 듣게 되는 상황을 설명하는 문장입니다. find의 목적어로 '자기 자신'을 의미하는 themselves(them의 변형)와 목적보어로 현재분사구(being given ~)를 사용하여 '전문의식이 없는 사람들로부터 일하는 방식에 대한 조언을 받는 자신을 발견한다'는 의미를 구성합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recoding than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. (A) This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. (B) There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. (C) One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. (D) Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. (E) Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
questions.insertion_sentence: But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 우리가 말할 때 성대가 진동하기 때문에 발생하는 '두 번째 내부 경로'에 대해 소개하고 있습니다. (C) 앞부분에서 목소리를 인지하는 두 가지 경로가 있다고 언급했고, (C) 뒤에서는 '첫 번째(One)' 경로인 외부 소리 경로를 설명합니다. (D) 뒤의 문장은 진동이 뼈를 통해 전달되어 내이를 직접 자극한다는 내용으로, 이것이 바로 주어진 문장에서 말한 '두 번째 내부 경로'에 대한 구체적인 설명입니다. 따라서 주어진 문장은 (D) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by ⓐ<u>observing</u> what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such ⓑ<u>imitation</u> is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents ⓒ<u>produce</u>. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not ⓓ<u>restricted</u> to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply ⓔ<u>doing</u> what others do.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 주제는 '관찰을 통한 학습(learning by observation)'과 '모방(imitation)'입니다. 마지막 문장에서 우리가 많은 것을 배울 수 있는 이유는 단순히 다른 사람이 하는 것을 '행함으로써(doing)'가 아니라, 다른 사람이 하는 것을 '관찰함으로써(observing / watching)' 또는 '모방함으로써'라는 맥락이 되어야 합니다. ⓔ가 포함된 문장은 앞서 언급된 거울 뉴런을 통한 관찰 학습의 원리를 결론짓는 부분으로, 단순히 행동하는 것 이상의 '관찰'의 의미가 강조되어야 합니다. (참고: 원문상 ⑤번 위치에는 'watching'이 더 적절하며, 'doing'은 문맥상 관찰을 통한 학습이라는 핵심에서 벗어나 단순히 '따라 하는 행위'에만 치중되어 어색할 수 있습니다. 다만 이 문제의 의도는 '직접 해보는 시행착오'와 대비되는 '타인의 행동을 지켜보고 배우는 관찰'의 의미를 묻는 것이므로 ⓔ가 'observing'의 의미로 쓰여야 함을 시사합니다.)

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 9월 30번]
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. (A) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. (B) As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. (C) Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. (D) A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. (E) Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.*animus: 반감, 미움
questions.insertion_sentence: Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그럼에도 불구하고, 자전거 타기에 가장 적합한 도시조차도 택시, 응급 차량, 배달 트럭을 위한 자동차 차로가 여전히 필요하다'는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C) 앞부분까지는 자전거 도로 확장의 장점과 차량 도로의 자전거 도로 전환을 설명하고 있고, (C) 이후부터는 배달 차량이 도시를 더 푸르게 만드는 필수적 요소라는 설명이 이어집니다. 따라서 자전거 도로의 필요성에서 배달 차량 등의 필수적 차량 존재로 화제가 전환되는 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것끼리 짝지은 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us (A)[to avoid / avoiding] dangers, expressing anger helps us to scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to (B)[threatening / threatened] stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess (C)[is / are] thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: (A) help 동사는 목적격 보어로 원형 부정사나 to부정사를 취하므로 to avoid가 적절합니다. (B) stimuli(자극)를 수식하는 형용사로, 자극이 위협을 주는 능동의 의미이므로 현재분사인 threatening이 적절합니다. (C) 문장의 주어는 'the specific emotions (we possess)'로 복수 명사인 emotions가 주어의 핵심이므로 복수 동사인 are가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 내용이 알맞은 순서대로 나열된 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary.
ordered_passages: (A) AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects.
(B) Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
(C) For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 AI가 장애가 있는 노동자들의 접근성을 높여주는 사례를 설명합니다. (A) 'AI can also enhance...'를 통해 장애인 지원 외에 '저숙련 노동자'의 능력을 향상시킬 수 있다는 새로운 주제를 도입합니다. (C)는 저숙련 노동자(혹은 비원어민 등 불리한 조건의 사람)의 사례로 실시간 번역 능력을 제시하고, (B) 'Moreover'를 통해 또 다른 저숙련 노동자 지원 사례인 텍스트 생성기(글쓰기, 코딩 등)를 추가로 설명하는 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① 과학적 연구는 출판된 논문이 의도된 독자에 의해 이해될 때 비로소 의미를 갖는다.
② 논문 출판은 연구 결과를 공개하고, 동료 평가를 통해 검증받는 필수적인 과정이다.
③ 연구 설계가 명확하게 정의되어야 과학 논문의 신뢰성과 타당성을 높일 수 있다.
④ 좋은 논문을 찾기 위해서는 주제와 관련된 핵심 키워드를 정확히 파악하는 것이 중요하다.
⑤ 과학 실험은 이전 연구자들의 실험 결과를 수용하면서도 그 한계를 극복하는 것을 목표로 한다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학적 커뮤니케이션이 양방향 과정임을 강조하며, 나무가 쓰러져도 들을 사람이 없으면 소리가 아니듯, 과학 논문도 독자에게 전달되고 이해되지 않으면 무용지물이라고 설명합니다. 따라서 '과학적 실험은 결과가 출판되고 이해될 때까지 완성된 것이 아니다'라는 내용이 요지입니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
options: ① Flight vs Driving: Environmental Impact and Sustainability
② Would You Risk Your Life Based on Mere Emotion?
③ Uncovering Misleading Numbers and Hidden Biases
④ Find the Balance between Emotion and Logic!
⑤ The Pilot's Role in Relieving Passenger Fear
questions.explanation: 사람들은 비행기에 대한 통제권이 없다는 불안감 때문에 통계적으로 훨씬 안전한 비행 대신 위험한 운전을 선택하곤 합니다. 글쓴이는 이러한 결정이 논리가 아닌 감정에 의한 것임을 지적하며, 결정을 내릴 때 감정이 아닌 사실에 근거해야 한다고 조언합니다. 따라서 '단순한 감정에 기반해 생명을 걸 것인가?'가 제목으로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 비행 대 운전: 환경적 영향과 지속 가능성
② 당신은 단지 감정에 기반해 생명을 걸 것인가?
③ 오해의 소지가 있는 숫자와 숨겨진 편향 밝혀내기
④ 감정과 논리 사이의 균형을 찾아라!
⑤ 승객의 두려움을 완화하는 데 있어서 조종사의 역할

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form, when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
options: ① 원자는 결정의 기본 구성 요소이고, 모든 암석은 결정으로 이루어져 있다.
② 일반적인 결정 습성은 사각형, 삼각형, 육면의 육각형을 포함한다.
③ 보통 얼음을 만들 때와 같이 액체가 차가워질 때 결정이 형성된다.
④ 많은 경우, 결정은 완벽한 모양을 허용하지 않는 방식으로 형성된다.
⑤ 결정격자는 원자를 이루는 구성 요소이며 느리고 안정적인 환경에서 아름답게 배열된다.
questions.explanation: 지문 마지막 부분에서 결정격자(crystal lattice)는 개별 원자들이 결합하여 만들어지는 원자의 기본 구조(basic structure of atoms)라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 결정격자가 원자를 구성하는 하위 요소라는 설명은 인과관계가 반대로 서술되었으므로 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring, with portable digital technology ⓐ<u>makes</u> it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. How individuals prefer to manage their time to fulfill both work and personal responsibilities ⓑ<u>varies</u> from person to person. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are minimized. Only during breaks and non-work time ⓒ<u>do</u> these people take care of family matters, while they might conduct work solely at the workplace, keeping separate email accounts for work and family. We've even noticed more of these -segmenters- carrying two phones - one for work and one for personal use. These individuals find flexible schedules more ⓓ<u>effective</u> for themselves because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might result in their constantly ⓔ<u>monitoring</u> emails at home and on vacation rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.explanation: ⓐ가 포함된 구문은 「with + 목적어 + 분사(부대 상황)」 구문입니다. 목적어인 'portable digital technology'와 분사의 관계가 능동이므로, 동사 형태인 makes를 현재분사인 making으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies ①<u>investigating</u> these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people ②<u>whose</u> clothing deviated only slightly from established norms. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as ③<u>having</u> higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people are inclined ④<u>to judge</u> these slight deviations from the norm as positive. This is largely because such behavior is seen as a sign ⑤<u>which</u> the individual feels secure enough in their position or authority to challenge societal expectations, knowing they can handle any negative social consequences.
questions.explanation: ⑤번 'which' 둄에 완전한 문장(the individual feels secure enough...) 이 이어지고 있으며, 앐문장의 'a sign'과 동격을 이루고 있습니다. 따라쐜 관계대명사 which가 아닌 동격의 접속사 that으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might ①<u>boost</u> productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause ②<u>excessive</u> transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may ③<u>welcome</u> a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a ④<u>reinforcement</u> of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities ⑤<u>spread</u> into their own neighbourhood.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 혠중국 국민이 다옑성을 매력적이지 않은 특징으로 인식하는 경우는, 그것이 자신들의 국가 정체성에 대한 '위협'(threat)으로 달기기 때문입니다. 따라쐜 'reinforcement(강화)'는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans ①<u>downplay</u> similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst ②<u>offenders</u> - employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively ③<u>different</u> from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal is ④<u>inferior</u> to us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to ⑤<u>disempower</u> animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.explanation: 됤에 이어지는 예시(새가 수천 개의 씨앗 위치림 기억하는 것)는 동물이 인준적 과제에서 인간바다 '우수한(superior)' 경우림 나타낽니다. 따라쐜 이림 지능이 아닌 밸능으로 치부하는 것은 동물이 우리바다 뛰어난 능력을 보일 때의 반응이므로 'inferior(열등한)'는 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. In other words, given the contemporary landscape of business partnerships and long-term relationships, it is hardly helpful to _____________________________________, as it can hinder success and damage ongoing relationships.
options: ① stick to the traditional win-lose negotiating style
② place too much focus on personal relationships
③ adopt a win-win negotiating style
④ overlook the need for innovation and adaptability
⑤ maintain a neutral position in business negotiations
questions.explanation: 현대의 비즈니스 및 인간관계에서는 지속적인 관계 유지가 중요하므로, 성공을 방해하고 관계를 손상시키는 '전통적인 승패 협상 방식을 고수하는 것'은 도움이 되지 않는다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: 전통적인 승패 협상 방식을 고수하는 것
개인적인 관계에 너무 많은 초점을 맞추는 것
상생 협상 방식을 채택하는 것
혁신과 적응성의 필요성을 간과하는 것
비즈니스 협상에서 중립적인 입장을 유지하는 것

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us. One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Göbekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of _________________________________. Things are not so different in our own time.
options: ① the way construction design reflects community values
② how the things we construct make the way we live
③ buildings designed for both function and beauty
④ the use of crop diversity in traditional farming
⑤ humans interacting with other species
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 건물을 짓지만, 그 건물이 다시 인간의 삶의 방식을 형성한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 튀르키예의 괴베클리 테페 유적지 예시를 통해, 수렵 채집인이었던 조상들이 거대한 석조물을 세우기 위해 한곳에 정착하게 되었고, 이것이 결국 최초의 농경 사회로 이어졌음을 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '우리가 건설하는 것이 우리의 삶의 방식을 만드는 방식'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 건축 설계가 공동체의 가치를 반영하는 방식
② 우리가 건설하는 것이 우리의 삶의 방식을 만드는 방식
③ 기능과 아름다움 모두를 위해 설계된 건물들
④ 전통 농법에서의 작물 다양성 활용
⑤ 다른 종들과 상호작용하는 인간

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing, They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore _____________________________________________. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
options: ① encourage your child to learn from mistakes
② help your child realize that seeing is not everything
③ lead your child to a meaningful life by demonstrating positive behaviors
④ use your words wisely to show your values, as children absorb what they hear
⑤ set clear rules and expectations to help your child feel secure and understand boundaries
questions.explanation: 아이들은 부모의 말보다는 행동을 통해 가치관을 배운다는 점을 강조하는 글입니다. 부모가 일상생활에서 타인을 존중하고, 동정심을 보이며, 자제력과 정직함을 실천하는 모습을 보여줌으로써 아이들을 가르쳐야 한다고 말하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '긍정적인 행동을 보여줌으로써 자녀를 의미 있는 삶으로 이끌라'는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자녀가 실수로부터 배우도록 격려하라
② 보는 것이 전부는 아니라는 것을 자녀가 깨닫게 도와주라
③ 긍정적인 행동을 보여줌으로써 자녀를 의미 있는 삶으로 이끌라
④ 아이들은 듣는 것을 흡수하므로 당신의 가치를 보여주기 위해 말을 현명하게 사용하라
⑤ 자녀가 안전함을 느끼고 경계를 이해하도록 명확한 규칙과 기대를 설정하라

questions.question: 23. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. ⓐStudents and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. ⓑExecutives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. ⓒAs the expertise of amateur audiences continues to grow, it becomes increasingly important for professionals to recognize and value their opinions, which can offer fresh perspectives and insights. ⓓHowever, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. ⓔVery few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 스포츠 분야에서 팬들이나 비전문가들이 현장 전문가들의 업무에 대해 전문 지식 없이 훈수를 두는 현상(Monday Morning Quarterback)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 전문가들이 비전문가들로부터 원치 않는 조언이나 비판을 받는 상황을 기술하고 있는데, ③번 문장은 '아마추어 관객들의 전문성이 커짐에 따라 전문가들이 그들의 의견을 존중하고 가치 있게 여겨야 한다'는 내용으로, 비전문가들의 간섭을 비판적으로 바라보는 전체 흐름에 반합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation. (A) If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. (B) While the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a protective mechanism for the foot. (C) Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech. (D) This might cause you to shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. (E) Sensory and motor nerves control almost all functions in the body - from the beating of the heart to the movement of the gut, sweating and just about everything else.
questions.insertion_sentence: They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now contract quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object.
questions.explanation: 글은 핀을 밟았을 때 감각 신경이 뇌로 통증을 전달하는 과정을 설명합니다. 뇌에서 언어 영역과 연결되어 소리를 지르게 된다는 내용(D) 이후, 주어진 문장의 'They will also connect...'는 뇌가 운동 신경과도 연결되어 발을 떼게 만든다는 추가적인 반응을 설명합니다. (E) 문장은 감각 신경과 운동 신경이 신체의 거의 모든 기능을 조절한다는 요약적 결론이므로, 운동 신경의 구체적인 작용을 다룬 주어진 문장은 (E) 바로 앞에 위치하여 전체적인 신경의 역할을 설명하는 흐름을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to ⓐ<u>positive</u> externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause ⓑ<u>excessive</u> transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may ⓒ<u>value</u> a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an ⓓ<u>attractive</u> feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might ⓔ<u>fear</u> that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.*externality: 외부 효과 **fractionalization: 분열
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장은 앞선 긍정적 측면과 반대되는 'On the other hand(반면에)'로 시작하며, 원주민들이 다양성을 국가 정체성의 왜곡으로 받아들이는 상황입니다. 따라서 다양성은 '매력적인(attractive)' 특징이 아니라 '부정적인(unattractive/negative)' 특징으로 인식될 것입니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel (A)[oriented / disoriented] when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is (B)[easy / difficult] for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This (C)[distributes / contributes] to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
questions.explanation: (A) 이사가 아이들에게 스트레스를 준다는 맥락에서 익숙한 것이 사라지면 아이들은 '혼란을 느끼는(disoriented)' 것이 적절합니다. (B) 아이들의 이해가 문자 그대로이고 구체적이기 때문에 새로운 환경을 미리 상상하는 것은 '어렵습니다(difficult)'. (C) 자신의 배경을 공유하는 기회를 갖는 것은 공동체 의식을 형성하는 데 '기여합니다(contributes)'.
options_translation: ① 적응한 / 쉬운 / 기여하다
② 적응한 / 어려운 / 배분하다
③ 혼란을 느끼는 / 쉬운 / 기여하다
④ 혼란을 느끼는 / 어려운 / 기여하다
⑤ 혼란을 느끼는 / 어려운 / 배분하다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 두 개 고르면?
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it - you just see the blurred outline of the moving string. Strings vibrating in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. But if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note is heard loud and clear. The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. When the waves reach your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string.*pluck: (현악기를) 뜯다 **amplify: 증폭시키다
options: ① Guitar strings move slowly enough to be seen by the naked eye.
② Thin strings make hardly any noise because they don't have much impact on the air waves.
③ The combination of both a string and a guitar body makes more powerful air waves, so the sound is heard loud in your ears.
④ The vibrations of a guitar string are interrupted by the guitar body.
⑤ The wooden panels of a guitar vibrate at the same frequency as the string.
questions.explanation: ① 본문에서 기타 줄의 움직임은 매우 빨라 눈으로 볼 수 없고 흐릿한 윤곽만 보인다고 했으므로 일치하지 않습니다. ④ 기타 몸통은 진동을 방해(interrupted)하는 것이 아니라 증폭시켜 소리를 크게 만드는 역할을 하므로 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 기타 줄은 육안으로 볼 수 있을 만큼 충분히 느리게 움직인다.
② 가는 줄은 공기 파동에 큰 영향을 주지 않기 때문에 소리가 거의 나지 않는다.
③ 줄과 기타 몸통의 결합은 더 강력한 공기 파동을 만들어 소리가 귀에 크게 들린다.
④ 기타 줄의 진동은 기타 몸통에 의해 방해받는다.
⑤ 기타의 나무 판은 줄과 같은 주파수로 진동한다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable exception.
ordered_passages: (A) In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture.
(B) A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly.
(C) The findings suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 기대에 부합하는 옷을 선호하지만 '한 가지 주목할 만한 예외'가 있다고 언급했습니다. (B)에서 그 예외와 관련된, 규범을 약간 어긴 사람들에 대한 반응을 연구한 시리즈를 소개합니다. (A)에서는 그 연구의 구체적인 시나리오(빨간 나비넥타이, 빨간 운동화)를 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 발견(The findings)이 시사하는 바를 요약하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve _____________ in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where interpersonal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.*dysarthric: (신경 장애로 인한) 구음 장애의
questions.explanation: 지문은 AI가 장애가 있는 노동자나 저숙련 노동자들을 도와 직장 내 접근성을 높이고 업무 능력을 향상시키는 사례들을 설명하고 있습니다. 이러한 사회적 약자들이 노동 시장에 더 잘 참여할 수 있게 만드는 것을 의미하므로 빈칸에는 '포용(inclusion)'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 포용
② 다양성
③ 수익성
④ 생산성
⑤ 지속 가능성

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to ___________________________________________. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.*latent: 잠재적인
options: ① build a strong sense of self-worth and resilience
② avoid difficult situations that may trigger negativity
③ seek validation from external sources of authority
④ isolate oneself from any form of emotional support to gain clarity
⑤ surround yourself with those who have navigated the difficulties you are facing
questions.explanation: 부정적인 상태에서 벗어나기 위해 긍정적인 에너지를 가진 사람들(winners) 곁에 머무는 것이 도움이 된다는 내용입니다. ⑤번 '당신이 직면한 어려움을 이미 헤쳐나간 사람들과 함께하는 것'이 지문에서 언급한 'hanging out with the winners'와 일맥상통합니다.
options_translation: ① 강한 자아 존중감과 회복 탄력성을 구축하다
② 부정성을 유발할 수 있는 어려운 상황을 피하다
③ 외부의 권위 있는 원천으로부터 인정을 구하다
④ 명료함을 얻기 위해 모든 형태의 정서적 지지로부터 자신을 고립시키다
⑤ 당신이 직면한 어려움을 헤쳐나간 사람들과 함께하다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is ___________________________________________________________. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
options: ① to understand the need for collaboration across departments
② to acknowledge the distinct cultures and perspectives of various departments
③ to identify key challenges in organizational conflict management
④ to create structures that reduce operational inefficiencies
⑤ to improve communication between mechanistic and organic structures
questions.explanation: 지문은 조직 내의 다양한 부서와 분과들이 각자의 편향된 시각(tunnel vision)을 가지고 있어 서로 다른 문화를 형성하고 이것이 갈등의 원인이 될 수 있음을 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 조직 내 다양한 부서들의 별개의 문화와 관점을 인정하는 것이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 부서 간 협업의 필요성을 이해하는 것
② 다양한 부서의 뚜렷한 문화와 관점을 인정하는 것
③ 조직 내 갈등 관리의 핵심 과제를 식별하는 것
④ 운영상의 비효율성을 줄이는 구조를 만드는 것
⑤ 기계적 구조와 유기적 구조 사이의 의사소통을 개선하는 것

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. ⓐThey encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." ⓑThis statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. ⓒThe artist's work tries to show the hidden essence of common things, turning ordinary objects into something meaningful. ⓓFirestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. ⓔThe ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 잘못된 개념(본질주의)에 기반하여 존재하지 않는 대상(검은 고양이/에테르)을 찾는 과학적 탐구의 헛수고를 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ③번 문장은 평범한 사물에서 숨겨진 본질을 찾아내어 의미 있는 것으로 바꾸는 '예술가의 작업'에 대해 언급하고 있으므로, 과학적 개념과 본질주의에 대한 비판적 논조인 전체 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory.
ordered_passages: (A) To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
(B) After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes.
(C) Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind.It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form.

(D) In other words, we feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 벼락치기가 왜 최고의 전략이라고 착각하는지에 대한 질문을 던집니다. (C)에서 교과서를 읽은 직후 정보가 작동 기억에 남아있음을 설명하고, (D)에서 'In other words'로 이를 받아 단기 저장 공간에 정보가 있어 안다고 느끼지만 장기 기억과는 무관함을 지적합니다. (B)에서는 시간이 지남에 따라 이 작동 기억이 사라짐을 경고하고, (A)에서 결론적으로 장기 기억으로 옮기기 위해 단순 공부보다 스스로 테스트하는 과정이 필요함을 제안하는 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. (A) It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. (B) Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. (C) This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. (D) The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. (E) Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.insertion_sentence: Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 과학자들이 지난 반세기 동안 해양의 용존 산소량이 감소했다는 데이터를 분석했다는 내용입니다. (D) 앞부분인 (C)까지는 지구 온난화로 인한 수온 상승이 산소 감소를 초래할 것이라는 일반적인 물리적 법칙과 예측을 다루고 있습니다. (D)의 'The data show'가 지칭하는 대상이 바로 주어진 문장의 'data indicating that...'이므로, 데이터 분석 결과를 처음 언급하는 문장이 (D) 위치에 들어가야 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
options: ① Biologists distinguish similarity based on the function of the organs.
② Homologous traits may perform different functions but share structural similarities.
③ Analogous traits have the same structure but different functions.
④ The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse are analogous traits.
⑤ Biologists often examine the structural features of organs to differentiate between analogy and homology.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 생물학적 유사성을 두 가지로 구분하고 있습니다. 유추 형질(Analogous)은 기능은 같지만 진화 과정이 다른 반면, 상동 형질(Homologous)은 조상이 같아 구조적 특징을 공유하지만 기능은 다를 수 있다고 설명합니다. 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 상동 형질의 예시로 제시되었으며, 본문에서 상동 형질은 공통의 구조를 가진다고 명시하고 있으므로 ②번이 글의 내용과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 생물학자들은 기관의 기능에 기초하여 유사성을 구별한다.
② 상동 형질은 다른 기능을 수행할 수 있지만 구조적 유사성을 공유한다.
③ 유추 형질은 동일한 구조를 가지지만 다른 기능을 가진다.
④ 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 유추 형질이다.
⑤ 생물학자들은 유추와 상동을 구별하기 위해 종종 기관의 구조적 특징을 조사한다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 어법상 어색한 문장을 고르면?
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>Our emotions are thought to exist because they have been contributed to our survival as a species</u>. ⓑ<u>Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others</u>. From an evolutionary perspective, ⓒ<u>an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.)</u>. ⓓ<u>For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future)</u>. Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, ⓔ<u>the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago</u>.
questions.explanation: ⓐ번 문장에서 'contribute to'는 '~에 기여하다'라는 의미로 주로 능동태로 사용됩니다. 문맥상 '우리의 감정이 종으로서의 생존에 기여해 왔기 때문에'라는 능동의 완료 시제가 적절하므로, 수동태인 'have been contributed'를 능동태인 'have contributed'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Marshall McLuhan's assertion that "the medium is the message," highlights how the nature of communication technologies shapes our perceptions and behaviors, beyond the content they deliver. For instance, the rise of social media has diminished direct interpersonal interactions, impacting children's social skill development by limiting their practice opportunities. Each new medium acts like a pair of goggles, altering our worldview. With television, for example, viewers begin to interpret the world through its fast-paced, surface-oriented lens, influencing their understanding of reality. McLuhan emphasized that _______________________________________, often overshadowing the actual information being conveyed, thus guiding us to adopt new codes and ways of seeing the world.
options: ① the medium does not play a critical role in shaping audience perceptions or behaviors
② the medium influences not only how we receive information but also fundamentally alters our perception of reality
③ the effectiveness of communication is solely determined by the clarity of the information presented
④ the content delivered through any medium is always more significant than the medium itself
⑤ new technology helps children's development in multiple ways
questions.explanation: 이 글은 마샬 맥루한의 "매체가 메시지다"라는 주장을 통해, 매체가 전달하는 내용보다 매체 그 자체가 우리의 지각과 행동, 그리고 세계관을 어떻게 형성하는지를 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 '전달되는 실제 정보를 가린다(overshadowing the actual information being conveyed)'는 단서와 매체가 고글처럼 작용하여 세계관을 바꾼다는 예시를 종합할 때, 매체가 정보 수용 방식뿐 아니라 현실에 대한 지각을 근본적으로 바꾼다는 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 매체는 청중의 지각이나 행동을 형성하는 데 결정적인 역할을 하지 않는다.
② 매체는 우리가 정보를 받는 방식뿐만 아니라 근본적으로 현실에 대한 우리의 인식을 바꾼다.
③ 의사소통의 효과는 오직 제시된 정보의 명확성에 의해 결정된다.
④ 어떤 매체를 통해 전달되는 콘텐츠는 항상 매체 그 자체보다 더 중요하다.
⑤ 새로운 기술은 아이들의 발달을 여러 방면에서 돕는다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the passage, the capacity to learn through observation is crucial for (A)___________, as it facilitates the transmission of cultural knowledge and adaptive behaviors across generations, and fosters (B)___________ in the development of individual skills and social interactions.
questions.explanation: 거울 뉴런의 발견은 관찰을 통한 학습이라는 인간의 근본적인 능력에 대한 생각을 바꾸어 놓았습니다. 글의 마지막 부분에서 인류의 현대 문화가 우리가 타고난 행동이나 시행착오를 통한 학습에만 국한되지 않기 때문에 가능하다고 설명합니다. 따라서 관찰 학습은 타고난 것에 얽매이지 않는 (A) 인지적 유연성(cognitive flexibility)에 중요하며, 타인을 모방하며 배우는 과정은 (B) 정서적 지능(emotional intelligence) 발달을 촉진합니다.
options_translation: ① 본능적 반응 - 신체적 강점
② 학업적 성공 - 경직된 사고
③ 창의적 표현 - 본능적 행동
④ 사회적 순응 - 정서적 회복력
⑤ 인지적 유연성 - 정서적 지능

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators ⓐ<u>are attracted to</u> ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism ⓑ<u>emphasizes</u> the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity ⓒ<u>complicates</u> the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and ⓓ<u>hierarchical</u> distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through ⓔ<u>frequent</u> interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.explanation: 전통적인 엘리트 명성(연기, 노래 능력 등)과 달리 소셜 미디어를 통한 평범한 유명인은 타인과의 상호작용과 구독자 수 등 수치화된 지표를 통해 명성을 얻습니다. 문맥상 이러한 평범한 유명세라는 현상은 명성의 의미를 복잡하게 만드는 것이 아니라, 오히려 명성을 단지 주목도의 지표(수치)로 '단순화'하거나 '재정의'하는 것을 의미해야 하므로 ⓒ가 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists ⓐ<u>distinguish</u> two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on ⓑ<u>different</u> branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose ⓒ<u>independently</u> in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they ⓓ<u>descended</u> from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share ⓔ<u>functional</u> traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
questions.explanation: 글의 문맥상 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 상동 형질(homology)로서, 기능은 다르지만 같은 조상에서 유래했기 때문에 뼈의 개수나 연결 방식과 같은 '구조적' 특징을 공유합니다. 따라서 ⓔ functional(기능적인)을 structural(구조적인)과 같은 단어로 바꾸어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. However, if you give one monkey grapes, instead grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers, the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, _____________________________ makes the situation unfair. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.explanation: 카푸친 원숭이는 자신이 받는 보상(오이)이 이전과 같더라도, 옆에 있는 다른 원숭이가 더 좋은 보상(포도)을 받는 것을 보게 되면 상황이 불공평하다고 느끼게 됩니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 타인과의 '비교'를 의미하는 'the comparison to another'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 같은 양
② 다른 양
③ 갇힌 상황
④ 원숭이의 성격
⑤ 다른 이와의 비교

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓖ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것을 있는 대로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not ⓐ<u>unlike</u> reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for ⓑ<u>having not</u> skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact ⓒ<u>that</u> digital content creators face real barriers to ⓓ<u>crossing</u> over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point ⓔ<u>which</u> the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and ⓕ<u>associated</u> with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrities ⓖ<u>are</u> like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.explanation: ⓑ 'having not'은 준동사(동명사)의 부정으로 'not having'이 되어야 합니다. ⓔ 'point' 뒤에는 완전한 문장이 오므로 관계대명사 which가 아닌 동격의 접속사 that이 적절합니다. ⓖ 주어는 동명사구인 'Achieving ordinary fame~'으로 단수 취급해야 하므로 are를 is로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "The ether was a black cat"이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. <u>The ether was a black cat</u>, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① an essential concept to human survival
② a passionate search for wrong hypothesis
③ a mysterious that demonstrates scientific concept
④ a mysterious substance that will fill the universe
⑤ a beautiful summary of the search for the essence
questions.explanation: 본문에서 에테르(ether)는 우주를 채우고 빛의 매질이 된다고 여겨졌으나 실제로는 존재하지 않는 것이었습니다. 필자는 이를 '어두운 방에서 존재하지 않는 검은 고양이를 찾는 것'에 비유하며, 잘못된 개념을 바탕으로 존재하지 않는 본질을 헛되이 찾는 과학적 탐구를 비판하고 있습니다. 따라서 'The ether was a black cat'은 존재하지 않는 대상을 전제로 한 잘못된 가설에 대한 열정적인(그러나 헛된) 탐구를 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간 생존에 필수적인 개념
② 잘못된 가설에 대한 열정적인 탐구
③ 과학적 개념을 입증하는 신비로운 것
④ 우주를 채울 신비로운 물질
⑤ 본질에 대한 탐구의 아름다운 요약

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is to be ⓐ<u>uncommon</u>. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely ⓑ<u>original</u>. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ⓒ<u>creativity</u>. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amdeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and completely ⓓ<u>outdid</u> him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work had ⓔ<u>cliché</u>. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 맥락상 안토니오 살리에리는 모차르트 시대에 살았던 '위대하지 않은' 작곡가로 묘사됩니다. 모차르트와 같은 천재적인 위대한 작곡가와 대조되는 인물이므로, 모차르트를 '능가했다(outdid)'는 표현은 적절하지 않습니다. 살리에리는 모차르트보다 뒤처지거나 그의 천재성에 가려진 인물로 묘사되어야 문맥이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 <보기>는 글을 바탕으로 제작한 광고 전단지이다. 광고 전단지에 쓰인 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Dear Reader, We always appreciate your support. As you know, our service is now available through an app and easy to use. There has never been a better time to switch to an online membership of TourTide Magazine. You can get a 50% discount off your current print subscription. What's more, you can access a full year of online reading. Get new issues and daily web pieces at TourTide.com, read or listen to TourTide Magazine via the app, and get our members-only newsletter. You'll also gain access to our editors' selections of the best articles. Please remember that this special promotion is only for customers with current print membership. Contact and change your subscription.Yours,TourTide Team
vocabulary_box: Join TourTideON-LINE Subscriptionwith SPECIAL Benefits!ⓐ Easy Access via Appⓑ Half Price of the Print Subscriptionⓒ Members-limited Newsletterⓓ Special Editors' Selectionsⓔ Open to Newcomers
questions.explanation: 지문 마지막 부분에서 'this special promotion is only for customers with current print membership'라고 명시되어 있습니다. 즉, 이 프로모션은 현재 지면 잡지 구독자만을 위한 것이므로, 'Open to Newcomers(신규 고객에게 개방됨)'라는 내용은 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 앱을 통한 쉬운 접근
② 지면 구독료의 절반 가격
③ 회원 한정 뉴스레터
④ 편집자의 특별 엄선작
⑤ 신규 고객에게 개방됨

questions.question: 2. 다음 밑줄 친 cross the line이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As I walked from the mailbox, my heart was beating rapidly. In my hands, I held the letter from the university I had applied to. I thought my grades were good enough to <u>cross the line</u> and my application letter was well-written, but was it enough? I hadn't slept a wink for days. As I carefully tore into the paper of the envelope, the letter slowly emerged with the opening phrase, "It is our great pleasure..." I shouted with joy, "I am in!" As I held the letter, I began to make a fantasy about my college life in a faraway city.
options: ① have an opportunity to get financial support
② go to other countries or cities for sightseeing
③ behave in a way that is not socially acceptable
④ show the academic ability needed for higher education
⑤ complete sending an application before the new period begins
questions.explanation: 글의 문맥상 필자는 대학 합격 여부를 기다리고 있는 상황입니다. 성적이 'cross the line' 하기에 충분하다고 생각했다는 것은 대학 입학에 필요한 기준선(합격선)을 넘을 만큼의 학업 능력을 갖추었다는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 재정적 지원을 받을 기회를 갖다
② 관광을 위해 다른 나라나 도시로 가다
③ 사회적으로 용인되지 않는 방식으로 행동하다
④ 고등 교육에 필요한 학업 능력을 보여주다
⑤ 새로운 기간이 시작되기 전에 지원서 전송을 완료하다

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Having a messy room can add up to negative feelings and destructive thinking. Psychologists say that having a disorderly room can indicate a disorganized mental state. One of the professional tidying experts says that the moment you start cleaning your room, you also start changing your life and gaining new perspective. When you clean your surroundings, positive and good atmosphere follows. You can do more things efficiently and neatly. If you want positive change in your life, it's time to clean up your closets, organize your drawers, and arrange your things.
options: ① 어떤 감정이 좋고 나쁜지에 관한 판단은 무의미하다.
② 정신 수양을 통해 긍정적인 마음가짐을 가질 수 있다.
③ 효율적인 정리를 위해 일상에서 기본 원칙을 수립해야 한다.
④ 주변 환경의 정리 상태는 개인의 정신 상태에 영향을 미친다.
⑤ 부정적인 생각은 일시적인 감정이지만, 개인에게 큰 위협이 될 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 방이 지저분한 것이 부정적인 감정과 무질서한 정신 상태를 나타내며, 주변 환경을 정리함으로써 긍정적인 변화와 새로운 관점을 얻을 수 있다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ④번이 가장 적절한 요지입니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your behaviors are usually a reflection of your identity. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, __________________________, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
options: ① if what you do matches what you believe
② because identity is independent of behavior
③ when other people start to follow your thought
④ since you have already learned more by training
⑤ as you have higher moral standards than others
questions.explanation: 지문은 행동이 정체성의 반영이며, 스스로를 어떤 사람이라고 믿으면 그 믿음에 따라 행동하게 된다고 설명합니다. 빈칸 뒤의 문장에서 '당신은 더 이상 행동 변화를 추구하는 것이 아니라 이미 스스로가 믿고 있는 유형의 사람처럼 행동하는 것뿐이다'라고 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 '당신이 하는 일이 당신이 믿는 것과 일치한다면'이라는 조건의 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 하는 일이 당신이 믿는 것과 일치한다면
② 정체성은 행동과 독립적이기 때문에
③ 다른 사람들이 당신의 생각을 따르기 시작할 때
④ 당신이 이미 훈련을 통해 더 많은 것을 배웠기 때문에
⑤ 당신이 다른 사람들보다 더 높은 도덕적 기준을 가지고 있기 때문에

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Fritz Zwicky, a memorable astrophysicist who coined the term 'supernova', was born in Varna, Bulgaria to a Swiss father and a Czech mother. At the age of six, he ⓐ<u>sent</u> to his grandparents who looked after him for most of his childhood in Switzerland. There, he ⓑ<u>got</u> an advanced education in mathematics and physics. In 1925, he emigrated to the United States, ⓒ<u>continuing</u> his physics research at California Institute of Technology (Caltech). He developed numerous theories that ⓓ<u>have had</u> a profound influence on the understanding of our universe in the early 21st century. After ⓔ<u>being appointed</u> as a professor of astronomy at Caltech in 1942, he developed some of the earliest jet engines and holds more than 50 patents, many in jet propulsion.
questions.explanation: ⓐ가 포함된 문장에서 주어 'he(Fritz Zwicky)'가 조부모님에게 보내진 것이므로 수동태인 'was sent'가 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. [7~8] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by ⓐ<u>being added</u> nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers ⓑ<u>becomes</u> much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are ⓒ<u>fed</u> and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain ⓓ<u>agriculturally</u> undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land ⓔ<u>what</u> surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
options: ① We Should Prohibit the Use of Fertilizers
② The Thing Happened to Your Farm in 1969
③ Get Rid of As Much As Weed for Your Crops
④ The Nutrient-rich Farms with the Unexpected Outcome
⑤ Why We Need Enough Amount of Water in Growing Crops
questions.explanation: 농경지가 비료와 관개 시설 덕분에 영양분과 물이 풍부해졌으나, 그로 인해 잡초와 같은 반갑지 않은 것들의 관심(침입)까지 끌게 되었다는 내용이므로 ④번 '예상치 못한 결과를 가져온 영양분이 풍부한 농장'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리는 비료 사용을 금지해야 한다
② 1969년에 당신의 농장에 일어난 일
③ 당신의 작물을 위해 가능한 한 많은 잡초를 제거하라
④ 예상치 못한 결과를 초래한 영양분이 풍부한 농장
⑤ 왜 작물을 기르는 데 충분한 양의 물이 필요한가

questions.question: 8. [7~8] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.윗글의 밑줄 친 어법 오류 ⓐ~ⓔ를 바르게 고치지 못한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by ⓐ<u>being added</u> nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. During the last fifty years, engineers and crop scientists have helped farmers ⓑ<u>becomes</u> much more efficient at supplying exactly the right amount of both. World usage of fertilizer has tripled since 1969, and the global capacity for irrigation has almost doubled; we are ⓒ<u>fed</u> and watering our fields more than ever, and our crops are loving it. Unfortunately, these luxurious conditions have also excited the attention of certain ⓓ<u>agriculturally</u> undesirables. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land ⓔ<u>what</u> surrounds them, they are desired as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area.
questions.explanation: ②번의 help는 목적격 보어로 동사원형이나 to 부정사를 취하므로 becomes는 become이나 to become으로 고쳐야 합니다. became은 과거형이므로 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐbeing added → adding
② ⓑbecomes → became
③ ⓒfed → feeding
④ ⓓagriculturally → agricultural
⑤ ⓔwhat → that

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show that you care.
