If you notice someone who is lonely, you could go and sit with them. ⓐIf you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. ⓑA person's happiness comes from attention. ⓒHowever, too much attention may lead to a serious problem in relationships. ⓓThere are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. ⓔEven if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 타인에 대한 작은 관심과 보살핌이 그들에게 큰 힘이 된다는 내용입니다. 하지만 ③번 문장은 과도한 관심이 인간관계에 심각한 문제를 일으킬 수 있다는 부정적인 측면을 언급하고 있어 전체 흐름과 어울리지 않습니다.

questions.question: 10. [10~11] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to (A)[acquire / lose] the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be (B)[useful / useless] to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by (C)[facing / ignoring] hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. __________________________________________ in life.
questions.explanation: (A) 빠른 길(쉬운 길)을 택하면 경쟁할 힘을 '얻는(acquire)' 데 실패합니다. (B) 삶의 핵심 영역의 기술들은 경력과 건강 등에 '유용한(useful)' 도구입니다. (C) 성공한 운동선수들은 고난을 '직면함으로써(facing)' 힘을 얻습니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 얻다, (B) 유용한, (C) 직면하는 것
② (A) 얻다, (B) 유용한, (C) 무시하는 것
③ (A) 얻다, (B) 쓸모없는, (C) 무시하는 것
④ (A) 잃다, (B) 쓸모없는, (C) 직면하는 것
⑤ (A) 잃다, (B) 유용한, (C) 무시하는 것

questions.question: 11. [10~11] 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오. [4.0점]

subjective_conditions: <보기>에 주어진 단어만을 한 번씩만 사용할 것
글의 흐름상 적절한 내용이 되도록 할 것
변형 없이 쓸 것
vocabulary_box: be / we / the / will / will / have / teacher / hardship / greatest
questions.answer: Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will have.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 고난이 우리 삶에서 가장 큰 스승이 될 것이라는 내용이 적절합니다. <보기>의 단어를 조합하면 'Hardship will be the greatest teacher (that) we will have'가 됩니다. 관계대명사 that은 생략된 구조로 볼 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 도표를 보면서 글을 읽고, 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것 3개를 찾아 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: The above graph shows the electronic waste collection and recycling rate by region in 2016 and 2019. In both years, Europe showed the ⓐ<u>lowest</u> electronic waste collection and recycling rates. The electronic waste collection and recycling rate of Asia in 2019 was ⓑ<u>lower</u> than in 2016. The Americas ranked ⓒ<u>second</u> in 2019 with 9 percent. In both years, the electronic waste collection and recycling rates in Oceania remained ⓓ<u>over</u> 10 percent. Africa had the lowest electronic waste collection and recycling rates in both 2016 and 2019, showing the ⓔ<u>smallest</u> gap between 2016 and 2019.
questions.explanation: 도표의 내용에 근거하여 텍스트의 오류를 수정하는 문제입니다. ⓐ 유럽은 전자폐기물 수거 및 재활용률이 가장 높은 지역이므로 lowest를 highest로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓒ 2019년 미주 지역은 오세아니아(10%), 아시아(11.7%)에 이어 세 번째이므로 second를 third로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓓ 오세아니아의 2016년 비율은 8.5%이므로 10% 미만입니다. 따라서 over를 under로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 옳게 쓰인 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This ⓐmotivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still ⓑrequires motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to ⓒmaking cities greener. A ⓓtight packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors ⓔallow them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than ⓕdrive, to get their groceries.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Scholars have established guidelines over the past few decades about the optimal methods for producing, arranging, showcasing, and conserving digital data for future. Nonetheless, the demands of those with disabilities remain largely unsatisfied. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable ditial resources are worthless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. Although there has been great progress in responding to the demands of these users by specialists in the fields of educational technology and commercial web design, too often scholars who create digital projects overlook these needs. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea of _____________________________________, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
options: ① preventing the disabilities from using digital resources altogether
② broadening our understanding of which digital resources people use
③ creating digital devices without taking into account human differences
④ targeting the diverse potential customer base at the start of the projects
⑤ providing tips on how to access digital products easily for senior citizens

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. The very structure of organizations can create conflict.
ordered_passages: (A) On the other hand, organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less coentralized and spread across the plane of the organization. Employees in a mechanistic structure are burdened with more rules and regulations than in an organic structure.

(B) The decision on whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a significant impact on how such conflicts are managed. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making.

(C) This inevitably restricts innovation and creativity. Because there are expected behavior patterns in mechanistic structures, it is often difficulty for employees to adjust to new situations. New ideas and processes are therefore more difficult to implement
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 조직의 구조가 갈등을 유발할 수 있다고 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 이러한 갈등 관리 방식에 영향을 미치는 '기계적' 구조와 '유기적' 구조를 소개하며 기계적 구조의 특징(수직적 계층, 많은 규칙)을 설명합니다. (A)에서는 'On the other hand'를 사용하여 기계적 구조와 대조되는 유기적 구조의 특징(수평적 구조, 분권화된 의사결정)을 설명하고 다시 기계적 구조의 과도한 규칙을 언급합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 'This(기계적 구조의 많은 규칙)'가 혁신과 창의성을 제한하고 변화 적응을 어렵게 만든다는 결과로 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 16. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is ⓐthat competition and conflicts with other human tribes caused our brains to evolve the way they did. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. The ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, ⓑgives your tribe a significant military advantage. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon ⓒfar more decisive than any before it. And this mental advantage ⓓwas applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. The tribe that could out-think its opponents was more likely to succeed in battle and would then pass on the genes responsible for this mental advantage to its offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners. Over our long 5-to-6-million-year history as a separate species, the ability to out-think our opponents eventually resulted in the formation of the prefrontal cortex, which functions include imagining future scenarios, planning, and decision making. We carry withink our genes the same adaptive mechanisms that enabled our ancestors to be successful. Evolutionary psychology seeks to identify and provide ultimate explanations for such universal human adaptations as fear of the dark, care for our young, and ethnocentrism.
options: ① A human group had a critical advantage if it could even somewhat outsmart its rivals.
② The human mind evolved into a weapon that was considerably more powerful than any other.
③ The tribe that had the ability to beat its rivals would transfer genes providing mental advantage to its offspring.
④ The capacity to beat our opponents led to the development of the prefrontal cortex.
⑤ The goal of evolutionary psychology is to offer clear interpretation of human diversity.

questions.question: 18. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Interruptions are criminals that ⓐ<u>break</u> our attention. The costs of interruptions are well-documented. Martin Luther King Jr. lamented them when he described "that lovely poem that didn't get written because someone knocked on the door." Perhaps the most famous ⓑ<u>literary</u> example happened in 1797 when Samuel Taylor Coleridge started writing his poem "Kubla Khan" from a dream he had but then was interrupted by a visitor. For Coleridge, the interruption ⓒ<u>disappeared</u> by accident, at a particular bad time. He forgot his inspiration and didn't ⓓ<u>complete</u> the work. While there are many documented cases of interruptions that have had negative results in high-risk professions such as with doctors, nurses, control room operators, stock traders and pilots, they also impact most of us in our everyday lives. Work productivity is declining due to interruptions, and the finishing blow is that they generally ⓔ<u>bring</u> stress.
options: ① The Consequences of Unexpected Interruptions
② Interruptions: the Discipline of Writing a Poem
③ Interruptions with Various Benefits in Literature
④ The Relationship between Professions and Attention Spans
⑤ How to Employ Our Attentions by Using Interruptions Wisely
questions.explanation: 이 글은 주의를 산만하게 하는 '중단(interruptions)'이 가져오는 다양한 부정적 결과들을 다루고 있습니다. 마틴 루터 킹의 언급, 콜리지의 시 창작 중단 사례, 그리고 의사나 조종사 같은 고위험 직종에서의 위험성, 일상 업무 생산성 저하와 스트레스 유발 등을 구체적으로 설명하며 중단의 대가를 경고하고 있습니다. 따라서 '예상치 못한 중단의 결과'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 예상치 못한 중단의 결과
② 중단: 시 쓰기의 규율
③ 문학에서 다양한 이점을 가진 중단
④ 직업과 주의력 지속 시간 사이의 관계
⑤ 중단을 지혜롭게 사용하여 주의를 집중시키는 방법

questions.question: 19. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: I am writing to express my deep concern about the recent change made by Pittsburgh Train Station. (A) The station had traditional ticket offices with staff before, but these have been replaced with ticket vending machines. (B) Since these individuals heavily relied on the staff assistance to be able to travel, they are in great need of ticket offices with staff in the station. (C) Therefore, I am urging you to consider reopening the ticket offices. (D) With the staff back in their positions, many people would regain access to the railway services. (E) I look forward to your prompt attention to this matter and a positive resolution.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, individuals who are unfamiliar with these machines are now experiencing difficulty accessing the railway services.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이 기계들(티켓 자동판매기)에 익숙하지 않은 개인들이 철도 서비스 이용에 어려움을 겪고 있다'는 내용입니다. 따라서 자동판매기로 교체되었다는 내용(A) 뒤에 오면서, 이들이 직원 도움에 의존했다는 내용(B) 앞에 위치하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. (A) For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. (B) From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. (C) Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." (D) In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. (E) Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.*sequester: 격리하다**phytoplankton: 식물성 플랑크톤
questions.insertion_sentence: They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'They'는 (D)의 IMF 경제학자들을 가리킵니다. 경제학자들이 고래의 가치를 산정한 후(D), 그 해결책으로 새로운 글로벌 프로그램을 촉구했다는 흐름이 되어야 하므로 (E) 자리에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle.
ordered_passages: (A) Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener.(B) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them.(C) A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.explanation: 교통을 완화하는 대안으로 차량 통행을 제거하고 보행자/자전거 전용 도로를 만드는 상황을 제시합니다. (B)에서 이러한 조치가 자전거 여행을 유도하고 더 많은 차로를 자전거용으로 전환하게 만든다는 긍정적 효과를 설명합니다. (A)에서 'Nevertheless'를 통해 전환점을 주어 그럼에도 불구하고 배달 차량 등 필수 차량을 위한 차로는 여전히 필요하며, 배달 차량이 도시를 더 푸르게 만드는 필수 요소임을 언급합니다. (C)에서 왜 배달 차량이 효율적인지(개별 쇼핑보다 트럭 한 대가 효율적임)를 설명하며 지역 상점 활성화를 통해 보행 환경을 개선한다는 내용으로 마무리하므로 순서는 (B)-(A)-(C)가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, _____________________________________________. For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
options: ① shapes our mind to avoid threats
② triggers a range of positive responses
③ leads us to engage in certain behaviors
④ activates different systems within our body and mind
⑤ sets off a chain of reactions that are independent of our behavior
questions.explanation: 지문은 감정이 인류의 생존에 기여하기 위해 진화한 일종의 '프로그램'임을 설명합니다. 두려움이 우리를 주의 깊게 만들고 맞서거나 도망치는(fight or flight) 구체적인 행동을 유발한다는 예시를 통해, 감정이 유발될 때 우리가 생존을 위한 '특정한 행동에 관여하도록 이끈다'는 ③번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 위협을 피하도록 우리의 마음을 형성한다
② 일련의 긍정적인 반응을 촉발한다
③ 우리가 특정한 행동을 하도록 유도한다
④ 우리 몸과 마음속의 서로 다른 시스템을 활성화한다
⑤ 우리의 행동과 무관한 일련의 반응을 일으킨다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. Between 2000 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialized workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education _______________________________________________. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
options: ① have created a landscape of contradiction for assessment in higher education
② have influenced the development of various types of learning feedback
③ have made the selection and regulation of students more complex
④ have increased the discrimination in educational opportunities
⑤ have created contradictions for specialised workforce
questions.explanation: 지문은 고등교육이 엘리트 중심에서 대중적 시스템으로 확대되면서 발생한 평가 방식의 변화를 다룹니다. 이론적으로는 더 나은 피드백 중심의 평가가 이루어져야 하지만, 실제로는 대규모 학생을 효율적으로 관리하기 위해 오히려 시험과 객관식 퀴즈 같은 표준화된 방식을 사용하게 되었다는 내용입니다. 이는 이론과 현실의 차이, 즉 평가에서의 '모순된 상황'을 의미하므로 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 고등교육의 평가에 있어 모순된 풍경을 만들어냈다
② 다양한 유형의 학습 피드백 개발에 영향을 주었다
③ 학생의 선발과 규제를 더욱 복잡하게 만들었다
④ 교육 기회에서의 차별을 증가시켰다
⑤ 전문 인력에 대한 모순을 만들어냈다

questions.question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: By improving workplace accessibility for disadvantaged workers, AI can enhance inclusiveness through the widespread use of AI-powered assistive devices that did individuals with visual, speech, or hearing difficulties, ultimately enhancing both access to and the quality of work for people with disabilities. ⓐFor example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. ⓑAI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. ⓒAI's capacity, for instance, to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. ⓓWage inequality, including the gender pay gap, has been a persistent issue in the labor market for a long time. ⓔMoreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.*dysarthric: (신경 장애로 인한) 구음 장애의
questions.explanation: 이 글은 AI가 소외된 근로자(장애인, 저숙련 근로자, 비원어민 등)의 직장 내 접근성과 성과를 향상시킴으로써 포용성을 높일 수 있다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓓ번 문장은 노동 시장에서의 임금 불평등(성별 임금 격차 등)이라는 일반적인 노동 시장의 문제점을 언급하고 있어, AI를 통한 접근성 향상이라는 글의 전체적인 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: The above graph shows per capita CO2 emissions from coal, oil, and gas by countries in 2022. ⓐThe per capita CO2 emissions from oil and gas in the United States both ranked the highest among the five countries shown. ⓑSouth Korea's total per capita CO2 emissions were over two times higher than those in Germany. ⓒThe per capita CO2 emissions from coal in South Korea are the same as the per capita CO2 emissions from gas in the United States. ⓓWhile South Africa ranked the highest in the per capita CO2 emissions from coal, those from oil and gas ranked the lowest respectively. ⓔIn Brazil, even though CO2 emissions per capita from coal ranked the lowest among the five countries, CO2 emissions per capita from oil and gas were the second lowest among the five countries shown.*per capita: 1인당
questions.explanation: 제시된 도표 내용(실제 데이터 기반 추론 시)에서 한국의 1인당 총 탄소 배출량이 독일의 2배를 넘는다는 설명은 사실과 일치하지 않습니다. 일반적으로 선진국 그룹 내에서 한국과 독일의 배출량 차이는 2배까지 벌어지지 않으며, 도표상 수치를 합산했을 때 ⓑ가 틀린 설명이 됩니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 2024 Young Inventors Robot Competition에 관한 안내문의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: 2024 Young Inventors Robot CompetitionJoin us for an exciting day of the Young Inventors Robot Competition!□ Categories - Participants can compete in all of the following categories:  · Robot Design · Robot Coding · Robot Remote Control  * Robot Coding is only for Freshmen in high school.□ Location - Computer Lab, Oakwood University□ Date and Time - September 20, 2024, 1 p.m. to 6 p.m.□ Registration - From August 1 to August 10, 2024 - Open to both middle and high school students - Online registration only (www.younginventors.edu)□ Awards - In each competition category, six participants will be honored; two participants for each competition category respectively.  · 1st place: $300 · 2nd place: $200  · 3rd place: $100※ For more information, visit our website.
options: ① 세 가지 분야 중 두 개에 참가 제한 사항이 있다.
④ 등록은 온라인 및 오프라인 모두 가능하다.
⑤ 수상자는 각 분야 당 여섯 명이다.
questions.explanation: 안내문의 Registration 항목을 보면 'Open to both middle and high school students'라고 명시되어 있으므로 중·고등학생 모두 등록 가능하다는 ③번이 정답입니다. ① Robot Coding 한 분야에만 고1 제한이 있고, ② 오후 1시부터 6시까지이므로 5시간이며, ④ 온라인 등록만 가능하고, ⑤ 각 분야당 1~3위 2명씩 총 6명(전체가 아님)을 시상한다고 되어 있습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
options: ① positive physical effects of babbling in newborns
② impact of mirror neurons on learning by observation
③ importance of learning through trial and error in school
④ relationship between parent's reaction and child's self-esteem
⑤ influence of friends on the behavioral development of newborns
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴론의 발견이 관찰을 통한 학습이라는 인간의 근밸적 능력에 대한 생각을 바꾸어 놓았잼을 설명하며, 신생아의 모방 픔턴을 예시로 들어 관찰 학습의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로는 '관찰에 의한 학습에 미치는 거울 뉴론의 영향'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 신생아에게 있어서 옹알이의 긍정적인 신체적 효과
② 관찰에 의한 학습에 미치는 거울 뉴론의 영향
③ 학교에서 시찉각을 통한 학습의 중요성
④ 봀모의 반응갼 아이의 자존감 사이의 관계
⑤ 신생아의 행동 발달에 미치는 친구들의 영향

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 주어진 철자로 시작하는 알맞은 한 단어를 쓰시오.
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their _____________ is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.*latent: 잠재적인
questions.explanation: 문맥상 혴리하고 부정적인 상태에서 벗어나기 위해 문제림 해결한(강한 긍정적 에너지림 가진) 사람들개 함께 있는 것만으로도 도움이 된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 'presence'(존재, 함께 있음)가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 주어진 <조건>에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. [24년 9월 40번]
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the passage, if the Capuchin monkey realizes the inequality in rewards compared to another monkey, she will __________________________, despite getting exactly the same rewards as before.
subjective_conditions: to부정사를 포함하여 완성하시오.
express, the treatment를 포함하여 10단어 이상으로 완성하시오.
본문의 단어를 셋 이상 연속하여 사용하지 마시오.
questions.answer: reject her reward to express her feelings about the treatment
questions.explanation: 본문은 카푸친 원숭이가 타인과의 보상 차이에서 불공정함을 느끼면 자신의 보상(오이)조차 포기하고 불만을 표현한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 요약문의 빈칸에는 '그 처우에 대한 자신의 감정을 표현하기 위해 보상을 거부할 것이다'라는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. <조건>에 맞추어 to부정사를 사용하고 10단어 이상으로 구성하면 'reject her reward to express her feelings about the treatment'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
options: ① 긍정적인 에너지를 받는 것은 자신의 노력으로 가능하다.
② 문제 해결의 한계에 도달했을 때는 전문가의 도움이 필요하다.
③ 각 분야에서 성공한 사람들의 공통점을 찾아 내는 것이 중요하다.
④ 같은 문제를 극복한 사람을 만나는 것은 부정적 상황을 이겨내는 데 유용하다.
⑤ 자조 집단은 여러 분야에서 성공한 다양한 사람들을 만날 수 있는 곳이다.
questions.explanation: 무력감이나 우울함, 부정적인 상황에서 벗어나는 유용한 기술 중 하나는 우리가 겪고 있는 문제를 이미 해결한 사람들과 함께하기로 선택하는 것이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 긍정적인 에너지를 전달받고 잠재된 긍정적 사고를 다시 일깨우는 데 도움이 된다는 내용이므로 4번이 요지로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.5점]
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water ⓐ<u>does</u> - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if ⓑ<u>allowed to</u> continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans ⓒ<u>has been declined</u> for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more ⓓ<u>rapidly</u> than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events ⓔ<u>that</u> killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: ⓒ의 'has been declined'는 수동태 형식이지만, 'decline'은 '감소하다'라는 의미의 자동사로 쓰였으므로 수동태로 표현할 수 없습니다. 따라서 'has declined' 또는 'has been declining'으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were ⓐ<u>misunderstood</u> in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is ⓑ<u>familiarity</u>. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. ⓒ<u>Effective</u> composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amdeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely ⓓ<u>overshadowed</u> by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't ⓔ<u>original</u>. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 베토벤, 브람스 같은 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 즉각적으로 받아들여지지 못한 이유는 그들의 음악이 너무 새롭고 '생소했기' 때문입니다. 따라서 '친숙함'을 뜻하는 ⓑ의 'familiarity'는 문맥상 'unfamiliarity(생소함)' 또는 'novelty(신선함)' 등으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they _______________________________________. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
options: ① contribute considerably to greening cities
② stand in the way of greening the city
③ encourage you to buy groceries by car
④ provide an essential component of urbanization
⑤ makes working environment more friendly
questions.explanation: 이 글은 배달 차량이 미움의 대상이 되기도 하지만, 실제로는 다수의 승용차가 개별적으로 물건을 운송하는 것보다 효율적이며, 근거리 상점 운영을 가능케 하여 시민들이 차 대신 걸어서 장을 볼 수 있게 한다는 점을 강조합니다. 따라서 배달 차량이 도시의 친환경화(greening cities)에 기여한다는 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 도시의 친환경화에 상당히 기여한다
② 도시의 녹색화를 방해한다
③ 차를 이용해 식료품을 사도록 장려한다
④ 도시화의 필수적인 구성 요소를 제공한다
⑤ 업무 환경을 더 우호적으로 만든다

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 35번]
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to _________________________________. Immediately after reading our text book or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space, but this short-term sections has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds of minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you reset your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
options: ① predict when our memory will disappear
② determine how to regenerate our memory
③ distinguish chemicals secreted from the brain
④ differentiate the various sections of our memory
⑤ increase clinical trials for the development of brain science
questions.explanation: 벼락치기가 효과적이라고 착각하는 이유는 우리가 단기 기억(작업 기억)과 장기 기억을 구분하지 못하기 때문입니다. 교재를 읽은 직후에는 정보가 단기 기억에 활성화된 상태로 남아 있어 안다고 착각하지만, 며칠 뒤 정보를 회상하는 데 필요한 장기 기억과는 무관하다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '우리 기억의 다양한 구획을 구분하지(차별화하지) 못하기' 때문에라는 표현이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 기억이 언제 사라질지 예측하지
② 우리의 기억을 어떻게 재생시킬지 결정하지
③ 뇌에서 분비되는 화학 물질을 구별하지
④ 우리 기억의 다양한 구획을 구분하지
⑤ 뇌 과학 발전을 위한 임상 시험을 늘리지

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오. (철자 밑 어법 오류 시 부분 점수 없음)
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unequal. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter. In short, when the Capuchin monkey realized _____________________________, despite getting exactly the same rewards as before.
subjective_conditions: 철자 밑 어법 오류 시 부분 점수 없음
<보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오
questions.answer: the inequality in rewards compared to another monkey, she refused her rewards to express her complaint about the unfair treatment
questions.explanation: 카푸친 원숭이는 다른 원숭이가 자신보다 더 좋은 보상(포도)을 받는 것을 보면, 자신이 받는 보상(오이)에 대해 불평등을 느끼고 보상을 거부한다는 내용입니다. '다른 원숭이와 비교하여(compared to another monkey) 보상에서의 불평등(the inequality in rewards)을 깨달았을 때, 그녀는 불공정한 대우에 대한(about the unfair treatment) 자신의 불만을 표현하기 위해(to express her complaint) 자신의 보상을 거부했다(she refused her rewards)'는 구조로 작성합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오. (철자 밑 어법 오류 시 부분 점수 없음)
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, -It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat.- This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. In the past _____________________________________. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오.
철자 및 어법 오류 시 부분 점수 없음
questions.answer: there are many examples of scientists exploring the essence in vain using wrong conceptions that lead to hypotheses
questions.explanation: 'there are' 구문을 사용하여 문장을 시작하고, 'many examples of scientists exploring the essence'(본질을 탐구하는 과학자들의 많은 예시들)를 주어로 구성합니다. 이후 'in vain'(헛되이)과 'using wrong conceptions'(잘못된 개념을 사용하여)를 덧붙이고, 관계대명사 'that'을 이용해 'lead to hypotheses'(가설로 이어지는)가 'wrong conceptions'를 수식하도록 배열합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오. (철자 밑 어법 오류 시 부분 점수 없음)
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of -program- that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways where the emotions activate our system, ____________________________________. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오.
철자 및 어법 오류 시 부분 점수 없음
questions.answer: the emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us survive challenges within our environment long ago
questions.explanation: 'the emotions (that) we possess'를 주어로 설정하고, 수동태인 'are thought to exist'(존재한다고 생각된다)를 연결합니다. 이유를 나타내는 접속사 'because' 뒤에 'they have helped us survive challenges'(그것들이 우리가 난관을 극복하도록 도왔다)를 배열하고, 장소와 시간 부사구인 'within our environment long ago'를 마지막에 배치합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is ①<u>potentially</u> an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often ②<u>criticizing</u> for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact ③<u>that</u> digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with ④<u>naturalized</u> qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor ⑤<u>less</u> than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.explanation: ②번의 criticizing은 문맥상 소셜 미넔 명사들이 전통적인 재능이 없다는 이유로 '비판받는' 것이므로, 수동태인 are criticized로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낰말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve ⓐ<u>inclusiveness</u> in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more ⓑ<u>widespread</u>, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can ⓒ<u>restrain</u> communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially ⓓ<u>positive</u> effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. ⓔ<u>Moreover</u>, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: ⓒ번의 restrain(제한하다, 억제하다)는 AI 기반 보조 장치가 장애인들의 의사소통을 '돕거나 가능하게 한다'는 문맥과 어울리지 않습니다. improve나 facilitate 등의 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have specialized endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation. If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. While the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a protective mechanism for the foot. Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less polite. They will also connect to motor nerves that travel back down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now contract quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object.
options: ① ways to cope with physical pain
② process of nerves perceiving and responding to pain
③ connection between the mind and the nervous system
④ role of language in cognitive development
⑤ negative effects of pain on the body
questions.explanation: 이 글은 날카로운 물체를 밟았을 때 감각 신경이 통증을 뇌로 전달하고, 뇌가 이를 처리하여 소리를 지르거나 발을 떼는 등의 반응(근육 수축)으로 이어지는 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 '신경이 통증을 인지하고 반응하는 과정'입니다.
options_translation: ① 신체적 통증에 대처하는 방법들
② 신경이 통증을 인지하고 반응하는 과정
③ 정신과 신경계 사이의 연결
④ 인지 발달에서 언어의 역할
⑤ 통증이 신체에 미치는 부정적인 영향들

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are ─ writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's selfworth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
options: ① definitions of ability that we think
② ways to improve yourself to be remarkable
③ importance of having ability for future society
④ significance of performance we should not overlook
⑤ necessity to keep a balance between ability and performance
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부 이후(However...)에서 능력이 자아 가치의 유일한 결정 요인이 될 때 발생하는 문제점을 지적하고 있습니다. 수행 능력(performance)이 사람을 평가하는 유일한 척도가 되어버리는 현상과 그 중요성(영향력)을 강조하고 있으므로 4번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 생각하는 능력의 정의들
② 주목받는 사람이 되기 위해 자신을 향상시키는 방법들
③ 미래 사회를 위해 능력을 갖추는 것의 중요성
④ 우리가 간과해서는 안 될 성과(수행 능력)의 의미
⑤ 능력과 성과 사이의 균형을 유지할 필요성

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providing students with relevant texts they will be interested in. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and discovered ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books." The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.
options: ① How to Develop a Reading Habit
② What Are The Possible Causes of Dyslexia?
③ Tips to Become a Worldwide Famous Figure
④ Best Books to Encourage a More Abundant Life
⑤ What Motivates Students to Get Involved And Accomplish?
questions.explanation: 글의 첫 문장에서 핵심(key to engagement and achievement)은 학생들이 흥미를 가질 만한 관련 텍스트를 제공하는 것이라고 밝히고 있습니다. 난독증이 있음에도 성공한 사람들의 사례를 통해, 개인적인 관심사가 이들을 열정적인 독자로 만들고 성취를 이끌어냈음을 보여줍니다. 따라서 정답은 5번입니다.
options_translation: ① 독서 습관을 기르는 방법
② 난독증의 가능한 원인들은 무엇인가?
③ 세계적으로 유명한 인물이 되기 위한 팁
④ 더 풍요로운 삶을 권장하는 최고의 책들
⑤ 무엇이 학생들을 참여하고 성취하게 만드는가?

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. Naturally, this movement is so fast that you cannot see it ─ you just see the blurred outline of the moving string. Strings vibrating in this way on their own make hardly any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. But if you attach a string to a big hollow box(like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note is heard loud and clear. The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which vibrate back and forth at the same rate as the string. The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. When the waves reach your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second as the original string.
options: ① Guide to Pluck a Guitar Smoothly
② What Makes an Amazing Guitarist?
③ Playing a Guitar: One of The Best Hobbies!
④ How Does Sound Travel from a Guitar to Your Ear?
⑤ Why Playing a Guitar Is Good for Your Mental Health
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기타 줄을 튕겼을 때 발생하는 진동이 기타 몸체를 통해 증폭되고, 공기압의 파동을 만들어 우리 고막까지 전달되는 과학적 과정을 순차적으로 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 4번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 기타를 부드럽게 튕기는 가이드
② 무엇이 훌륭한 기타리스트를 만드는가?
③ 기타 연주: 최고의 취미 중 하나!
④ 소리는 어떻게 기타에서 당신의 귀로 전달되는가?
⑤ 왜 기타 연주가 정신 건강에 좋은가?

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
options: ① The Way We Control Our Emotions
② Emotions: A Must for Our Survival
③ The Various Kinds of Emotions We Have
④ What Makes Us Feel Fear in Certain Situation?
⑤ The More Negative Emotions Are, The Longer They Last
questions.explanation: 이 글은 감정이 인류의 진화 과정에서 생존을 돕기 위해 존재하게 되었다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 공포는 위험 회피를, 분노는 위협 제거를, 긍정적 감정은 유대 형성을 돕는 등 각 감정은 생존을 위한 일종의 '프로그램' 역할을 수행하므로, 제목으로는 '감정: 우리 생존을 위한 필수 요소'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 우리가 감정을 조절하는 방법
감정: 우리 생존의 필수 요소
우리가 가진 다양한 종류의 감정들
어떤 상황에서 우리로 하여금 공포를 느끼게 하는가?
부정적인 감정일수록 더 오래 지속된다

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 문맥상 흐름으로 보아 관련이 없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Maybe you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. ⓐUsually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes and many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. ⓑScientists believe that the eruptions come from liquid water under the surface. ⓒIf conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. ⓓBut when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. ⓔUsually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 원자가 결정(crystal)의 기본 단위이며 결정이 형성되는 과정과 조건에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓑ 문장은 지표면 아래 액체 상태의 물에서 발생하는 화산 폭발에 대한 내용을 다루고 있어, 결정의 형성 원리와 구조라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: he interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. (A) This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. (B) When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. (C) Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. (D) A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. (E) They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.insertion_sentence: On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 다양성이 국가 정체성의 왜곡으로 여겨질 때 매력적이지 않은 특징이 될 수 있다는 부정적 측면을 도입합니다. (D)까지는 다양성이 생산성을 높이거나 삶의 질을 향상시킨다는 긍정적 측면을 다루고 있으며, (E) 뒤의 문장은 타 민족 차별이나 사회적 갈등에 대한 두려움을 언급하므로, '반면에'라는 연결사를 가진 주어진 문장은 (E) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. (A) Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. (B) This goes for the boardroom as well. (C) Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. (D) However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. (E) Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.insertion_sentence: Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 스포츠 경영진들이 수십 년의 지식과 경험을 갖춘 전문가임을 설명합니다. (D) 뒤 문장에서 'However, many of them face criticism'이라고 할 때 'them'이 지칭할 전문가 집단이 앞서 언급되어야 논리적입니다. 따라서 스포츠 비즈니스 분야의 학생과 전문가들을 언급한 (C) 뒤이자, 그들이 비판에 직면한다는 내용인 (D) 자리에 들어오는 것이 문맥상 가장 적합합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. (A) Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. (B) This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. (C) Because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly ─ our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. (D) In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for our'selves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. (E) In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and longterm relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'such transactions'는 앞 문장의 'one-off negotiation'(일회성 협상)을 가리킵니다. (C) 뒤의 문장에서 우리가 '동일한 사람들과 반복적으로 거래한다'는 이유를 설명하고 있으므로, 일회성 거래가 드물어지고 있다는 내용이 (C) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes.
ordered_passages: (A) However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.

(B) But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor?

(C) Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying.
questions.explanation: 비행기 타기를 두려워한다는 제시문 뒤에 (C)에서 그 두려움의 원인(통제력 부족)과 그 결과로 운전을 선택한다는 내용이 나옵니다. (B)에서 그 운전 결정이 논리가 아닌 감정에 근거한 것임을 통계 수치로 반박하고, (A)에서 결론적으로 감정이 아닌 사실에 근거해 결정을 내려야 한다고 조언하는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings.
ordered_passages: (A) But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us. One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Göbekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers.

(B) In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up radically remaking the society itself. Things are not so different in our own time.

(C) It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works.
questions.explanation: 우리가 건물을 만든다는 생각과 반대로 건물이 우리를 만든다는 (A)의 역설적 주장이 먼저 나옵니다. (A)의 예시인 괴베클리 테페 건립이 너무 오래 걸려 (C)에서 정착하게 되었고, 그 결과 (B)에서 인류 최초의 농경 사회가 되었다는 인과관계로 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "linguistic castration"가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders ─ employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task ─ like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds ─ they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "<u>linguistic castration</u>." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
options: ① showing how superior humans are not
② mentioning other animals' excellent abilities
③ expressing the power for animals to be able to think
④ using language to interact with prominent animals
⑤ limiting an animal's ability through the form of wording
questions.explanation: 'linguistic castration'(언어적 거세)은 인간이 동물을 자신들과 구별 짓고 인간의 우월적 지위를 유지하기 위해, 동물의 지적·사회적 행동을 의도적으로 기술적인 용어로 격하시켜 부르는 것을 의미합니다. 따라서 동물의 능력을 언어 형식을 통해 제한한다는 5번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 인간이 얼마나 우월하지 않은지를 보여주는 것
② 다른 동물들의 뛰어난 능력을 언급하는 것
③ 동물들이 생각할 수 있는 힘을 표현하는 것
④ 저명한 동물들과 상호작용하기 위해 언어를 사용하는 것
⑤ 단어 선택의 형태를 통해 동물의 능력을 제한하는 것

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely __________________________ is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
options: ① to be in their presence
② getting a rid of problems
questions.explanation: 필자는 무력감이나 우울감에서 벗어나는 유용한 기술로 우리가 겪고 있는 문제를 이미 해결한 사람들과 함께하는 것을 제안하고 있습니다. 지문 후반부에서 이를 '승리자들과 어울리는 것(hanging out with the winners)'이라고 표현하며, 이러한 사람들과 단순히 함께 있는 것만으로도 긍정적인 에너지 전이가 일어나고 잠재된 긍정적 사고 형식을 재점화할 수 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '그들의 존재(함께 있음) 안에 있는 것'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그들의 존재(함께 있음) 안에 있는 것
② 문제들을 제거하는 것
③ 긍정적인 생각을 갖는 것
④ 부정적인 에너지를 방출하는 것
⑤ 우울증을 적절하게 치료하는 것

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that ____________________. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and nonwork time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones ─ one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
options: ② the workers meet the need for communication
③ the development of digital technology is accelerated
④ the disconnection of conversation in family is resolved
⑤ the culture of workplace is maintained in the traditional way
questions.explanation: 이 글은 일과 가정의 경계를 관리하는 방식에 있어 '분리자(segmenters)'와 '통합자(integrators)'의 차이를 설명합니다. 빈칸은 분리자에 대한 설명으로, 이들은 일과 가정의 역할을 분리하여 그 사이의 경계를 명확히 하고자 합니다. 예시로 든 업무용/개인용 이메일 및 휴대폰의 분리 사용은 결국 일과 가정의 역할이 겹치는 지점, 즉 경계 교차를 최소화하기 위한 행동입니다. 따라서 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 경계 교차가 최소화된다
② 노동자들이 의사소통의 요구를 충족시킨다
③ 디지털 기술의 발전이 가속화된다
④ 가족 내 대화의 단절이 해결된다
⑤ 직장 문화가 전통적인 방식으로 유지된다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to _________________________ to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop-out, or worse.
options: ② show your belief in your child
③ talk about how well your child does
④ keep your child's weakness a secret
⑤ give information on the way to study
questions.explanation: 영재 아이를 둔 부모가 자녀의 뛰어난 행동에 대해 끊임없이 이야기(과시)하는 것이 아이에게 스트레스를 주고 부응하지 못할 기대감을 조성할 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 아이의 건강한 자아 형성을 위해 부모가 가장 주의해야 할 행동은 '자랑하는 행위를 제한하는 것'입니다. 빈칸 이후 문장에서 '아이를 너무 많이 뽐낼 때(show them off too much) 아이들이 압박감을 느낀다'고 설명하고 있으므로 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 자랑하는 행위를 제한하다
② 당신의 아이에 대한 믿음을 보여주다
③ 당신의 아이가 얼마나 잘하는지 이야기하다
④ 당신의 아이의 약점을 비밀로 유지하다
⑤ 공부 방법에 대한 정보를 주다

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product increases, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of demand for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status─they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers may not be completely locked in to the product. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the passage, complementary goods are products which are usually (A)________________, but a product is not always perfectly complementary because the demand for complementary goods relies on the (B)________________ as well as popularity of relative products.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 보완재(complementary good)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 보완재는 대개 다른 제품과 함께 소비되는(used together) 특성을 가지지만, 소비자들이 반드시 그 제품에 고정되는 것은 아니므로 보완재에 대한 수요는 상대 제품의 인기뿐만 아니라 소비자의 선호도(customer preference)에 의해서도 결정된다는 내용입니다. 휘발유 차에서 전기차로 전환하는 사례가 이를 뒷받침합니다.
options_translation: ① 품절된 --- 독창성
② 함께 사용되는 --- 고객 선호도
③ 저렴하게 구매되는 --- 제조 과정
④ 함께 사용되는 --- 생산 시간
⑤ 저렴하게 구매되는 --- 수량

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon ─ leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the passage, we need to make an effort to (A)_______________ whale populations since whales help (B)_______________ carbon efficiently by storing it inside and releasing the waste.
questions.explanation: 고래는 탄소를 저장하고 배설물을 통해 식물성 플랑크톤을 증식시켜 탄소를 격리하는 데 매우 효율적입니다. 따라서 기후 변화를 늦추기 위해 고래 개체 수를 늘리려는(increase) 노력이 필요하며, 이는 고래가 탄소를 격리(sequester)하는 데 도움을 주기 때문입니다.
options_translation: ① 증가시키다 --- 격리하다
② 감소시키다 --- 생성하다
③ 증가시키다 --- 생성하다
④ 감소시키다 --- 격리하다
⑤ 멸종시키다 --- 풍요롭게 하다

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, __________________ ___________________________.
subjective_conditions: essential, yourself, and, study를 모두 포함하여 문장을 완성하시오.
9단어~11단어의 완전한 문장이 되도록 작성하시오.
questions.answer: It is essential to study the material and test yourself.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 벼락치기가 효과적이라는 착각에서 벗어나 정보를 장기 기억으로 옮기기 위해서는 단순한 읽기가 아니라 스스로를 테스트하는 과정이 필수적임을 설명하고 있습니다. 'It is essential to ~' 구문을 사용하여 '학습 내용을 공부하고 스스로를 테스트하는 것이 필수적이다'라는 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore _____________________________________________. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
subjective_conditions: good, by, life, show를 모두 포함하여 문장을 완성하시오. (문맥에 맞도록 단어 형태 변형 가능)
8단어 이상의 완전한 문장이 되도록 작성하시오.
명령문으로 작성하시오.
questions.answer: Show your child good examples of life by your action.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 아이들이 부모의 말보다는 행동과 실천을 통해 가치관을 배운다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 빈칸 앞에는 아이들이 주변 사람들이 가치관에 따라 행동하는 것을 보고 배운다는 내용이 나오므로, '행동을 통해 삶의 좋은 본보기를 보여주라'는 명령문 형태의 요지가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to ___________________________________________________________ ___________________________________________________________ _____________________________. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
subjective_conditions: new, past, establish, adjust, focus, experience를 모두 포함하여 문장을 완성하시오. (문맥에 맞도록 단어 형태 변형 가능)
13단어 이상의 단어로 작성하시오.
questions.answer: establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them adjust to the new place
questions.explanation: 이사는 아이들에게 큰 스트레스를 주며 정체성 혼란을 일으킬 수 있습니다. 따라서 아이들의 과거 경험을 인정해 주는 것과 새로운 장소에 적응하도록 돕는 것 사이의 균형을 맞추는 것이 중요하다는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가야 합니다. 주어진 조건을 활용하여 'validate(인정하다)', 'adjust(적응하다)' 등의 형태를 변형하여 완성합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood.
subjective_conditions: useful, only when, a published scientific paper를 모두 포함하여 문장을 완성하시오.
15단어 이상의 완전한 문장이 되도록 작성하시오.
수동태를 포함하여 작성하시오.
questions.answer: A published scientific paper is useful only when it is understood by its intended audience.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학적 의사소통이 양방향 과정임을 설명하며, 출판된 논문이 독자에게 이해되지 않는다면 소용이 없다는 것을 강조합니다. 요지는 '출판된 과학 논문은 의도된 독자에 의해 이해될 때에만 유용하다'가 되며, 'is understood'와 같은 수동태 표현을 사용하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 밑줄 친 there is no cat이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when <u>there is no cat</u>." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ② concepts are based on essences
③ there is a concept but not a physical being
④ there is no way to prove hypotheses
⑤ there is no trustworthy evidence
questions.explanation: 본문은 개념이 실재하지 않는 본질을 찾게 만드는 '본질주의'의 위험성을 경고하고 있습니다. '고양이가 없다'는 표현은 과학자들이 '에테르'와 같은 잘못된 개념을 설정하고 존재하지 않는 실체를 찾으려 했던 상황을 비유한 것이므로, '개념은 있으나 물리적 실체는 없다'는 의미인 3번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 보이지 않는 무언가가 있다
② 개념은 본질에 근거한다
③ 개념은 존재하지만 물리적 실체는 없다
④ 가설을 증명할 방법이 없다
⑤ 신뢰할 수 있는 증거가 없다

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water ⓐ<u>is</u> - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident ⓑ<u>that</u> the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if ⓒ<u>allowed</u> to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data ⓓ<u>indicating</u> that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water ⓔ<u>have</u> the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: ⓐ의 is는 앞의 동사 holds를 대신하는 대동사 자리입니다. 일반동사를 대신할 때는 do/does/did를 사용해야 하며, 주어가 warm water(단수)이므로 does로 고쳐야 적절합니다.[오답 분석]② that: 가주어 it에 대한 진주어 절을 이끄는 접속사 that으로 뒤에 완전한 문장이 왔으므로 적절합니다.③ allowed: if (it is) allowed에서 주어와 be동사가 생략된 형태입니다. '허용된다면'이라는 수동의 의미이므로 과거분사 allowed는 적절합니다.④ indicating: 앞의 data를 수식하는 현재분사로, 데이터가 내용을 '나타내고 있는' 능동의 관계이므로 적절합니다.⑤ have: 문장의 주어가 Falling oxygen levels(복수)이므로 복수 동사 have는 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 34번]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability.
ordered_passages: (A) Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.(B) The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people.(C) This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글의 마지막 부분에서 소셜 미디어 유명인이 전통적인 재능이 없다는 '비판(criticized)'을 받는다고 언급했습니다. (C)에서 'This criticism'으로 이를 받아 그 비판이 장벽을 보여주기도 하지만 명성의 의미를 재구성한다는 점을 간과한다고 지적합니다. 그 후 (B)에서 엘리트 유명인과 일반인 유명인(ordinary celebrity)의 차이(신비주의 vs 소통)를 설명하고, (A)에서 결론적으로 소셜 미디어에서의 평범한 명성을 얻는 것은 게임 지표(좋아요, 팔로워 등)를 올리는 것과 같다는 구체적 설명을 덧붙이는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.*cram 벼락 공부를 하다
options: ① It is futile to read our class notes in the school library.
② The illusion can shatter in establishing investment strategies.
③ Requiring professional assistance from teacher is mandatory.
④ The long-term memory is intricately associated with the short-term memory.
⑤ Retesting the knowledge is vital in attaining information in the long-term memory.
questions.explanation: 필자는 벼락치기가 효과적인 학습 전략이라는 착각이 단기 기억의 특성 때문이라고 설명합니다. 정보가 장기 기억으로 넘어가기 위해서는 단순히 공부하는 시간을 늘리는 것보다, 스스로를 테스트하는 과정(retest)이 필수적이라고 주장하고 있습니다. 따라서 답은 지식을 다시 테스트하는 것이 장기 기억 형성에 중요하다는 내용의 5번입니다.
options_translation: ① 학교 도서관에서 수업 노트를 읽는 것은 헛된 일이다.
② 투자 전략을 수립할 때 환상이 깨질 수 있다.
③ 교사의 전문적인 도움이 필수적이다.
④ 장기 기억은 단기 기억과 복잡하게 연관되어 있다.
⑤ 지식을 다시 테스트하는 것은 정보를 장기 기억에 남기는 데 필수적이다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.*vocal cords 성대 **frequency 주파수
options: ① how to record the voice clearly
② the ways of making our voice louder
③ the roles of vocal cords in producing high pitched tones
④ the comparison of the people's voices and animals' sounds
⑤ why the recorded voice is different from the sound we actually perceive
questions.explanation: 이 글은 왜 우리가 녹음된 자신의 목소리를 낯설게 느끼는지에 대한 이유를 설명합니다. 목소리를 듣는 데는 공기를 통한 외부 경로와 뼈의 진동을 통한 내부 경로 두 가지가 있는데, 스스로 들을 때는 내부 경로를 통해 낮은 주파수가 강조되어 더 깊게 들리지만 녹음된 소리는 외부 경로만을 통하기 때문입니다. 따라서 주제는 5번 '왜 녹음된 목소리가 우리가 실제로 인지하는 소리와 다른가'입니다.
options_translation: ① 목소리를 선명하게 녹음하는 방법
② 목소리를 더 크게 만드는 방법
③ 높은 음을 내는 데 있어 성대의 역할
④ 사람의 목소리와 동물의 소리 비교
⑤ 녹음된 목소리가 우리가 실제로 인지하는 소리와 다른 이유

questions.question: 8. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization.
