The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. ⓐ<u>A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them</u>. ⓑ<u>The very structure of organizations can create conflict</u>. ⓒ<u>The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management</u>. ⓓ<u>In this case, the members of the organization should vote for the better option and advise the leader to fires the employees who are opposite to the view of the majority.</u> ⓔ<u>A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making</u>. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.*hierarchy: 위계
questions.explanation: 이 글은 조직 내 부서들의 다양한 문화와 구조(기계적 구조 vs 유기적 구조)가 갈등 관리에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ⓓ는 다수결로 결정하고 반대 의견을 가진 직원을 해고하라고 권고해야 한다는 내용으로, 조직 구조와 갈등 양상이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 문맥상 낱말의 영영 풀이로 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Once upon a time in the Iranian city of Shiraz, there lived the famous poet Sheikh Saadi. Like most other poets and philosophers, he led a very simple life. A rich ⓐ<u>merchant</u> of Shiraz was preparing for his daughter's wedding and invited him along with a lot of big businessmen of the town. The poet accepted the invitation and decided to ⓑ<u>attend</u>. On the day of the wedding, the rich merchant, the host of the wedding, was receiving the guests at the gate. Many rich people of the town attended the wedding. They had come out in their best clothes. The poet wore simple clothes which were neither grand nor expensive. He waited for someone to approach him but no one gave him as much as even a second ⓒ<u>glance</u>. Even the host did not greet him and looked away. Seeing all this, the poet quietly left the party and went to a shop where he could rent clothes. There he chose a richly decorated coat, which made him look like a new person. With this coat, he entered the party and this time was welcomed with open arms. The host ⓓ<u>embrace</u>d him as he would do to an old friend and ⓔ<u>compliment</u>ed him on the clothes he was wearing.
options: ① ⓐmerchant: a person who buys and sells goods in large quantities, especially one who imports and exports goods
② ⓑattend: to be present at an event
③ ⓒglance: a close look at something somebody to see if there is anything wrong
④ ⓓembrace: to hold someone in your arms as a way of expressing love or friendship
⑤ ⓔcompliment: to say something nice to someone in order to praise them
questions.explanation: ⓒ glance는 '힐끗 봄', '번득임'이라는 뜻으로, '매우 짧게 보는 것'을 의미합니다. ③번의 설명인 'a close look at something somebody to see if there is anything wrong(무엇이 잘못되었는지 보려고 무언가나 누군가를 면밀히 살펴보는 것)'은 glance보다는 'inspection'이나 'scrutiny'에 가까운 설명입니다.
options_translation: ① 상인: 대량으로 상품을 사고파는 사람, 특히 수출입을 하는 사람
② 참석하다: 행사에 출석하다
③ 힐끗 봄: 잘못된 것이 있는지 확인하기 위해 무언가나 누군가를 면밀히 살펴보는 것
④ 포옹하다: 사랑이나 우정을 표현하는 방식으로 누군가를 팔로 안다
⑤ 칭찬하다: 누군가를 찬양하기 위해 좋은 말을 하다

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절한 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Concepts are ⓐ<u>crucial</u> to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is extremely ⓑ<u>arduous</u> to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who ⓒ<u>discarded</u> an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, an ⓓ<u>enigmatic</u> substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, ⓔ<u>concealing</u> evidence of a cat that did not exist.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 개념은 생존에 '중요(crucial)'하므로 적절합니다.ⓑ 어두운 방에서 고양이를 찾는 것은 '힘든(arduous)' 일이므로 적절합니다.ⓒ 잘못된 개념을 사용했기 때문에 본질을 '폐기(discarded)'한 것이 아니라 존재하지 않는 본질을 '찾으려(sought)' 했던 것이므로 적절하지 않습니다.ⓓ 에테르는 빛의 매질로 생각되었던 '정체불명의(enigmatic)' 물질이므로 적절합니다.ⓔ 존재하지 않는 고양이의 증거를 '숨기는(concealing)' 것이 아니라 '찾는(seeking/hunting)' 것이어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Individuals who perform at a high level in their profession often have instant credibility with others. People admire them, they want to be like them, and they feel connected to them. When they speak, others listen ― even if the area of their skill has nothing to do with the advice they give. Think about a world-famous basketball player. He has made more money from endorsements than he ever did playing basketball. Is it because of his knowledge of the products he endorses?. No. It′s because of what he can do with a basketball. The same can be said of an Olympic medalist swimmer. People listen to him because of what he can do in the pool. And when an actor tells us we should drive a certain car, we don′t listen because of his expertise on engines. We listen because we admire his talent. Excellence connects. If you possess a high level of ability in an area, others may desire to connect with you because of it.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the text above, when individuals show (A)__________ in their profession, others would like to (B)__________ rapport with them.
questions.explanation: 자신의 전문 분야에서 뛰어난 능력을 보여주는 사람들은 타인과 연결되고 싶어 하는 욕구를 불러일으킨다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 탁월함이나 유명함을 뜻하는 'prominence'가, (B)에는 친밀 관계(rapport)를 '형성하다(establish)'가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 적대감 - 가지다
② 애정 - 버리다
③ 무지 - 무시하다
④ 탁월함(유명함) - 형성하다
⑤ 우려 - 세우다

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace.
ordered_passages: (A) For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.

(B) For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where interpersonal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects.

(C) AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities.*dysarthric: (-- --- --) --(--) ---
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 AI가 노동 시장의 취약 계층을 위한 직장 접근성을 높여 포용성을 개선한다고 언급했습니다. (C)에서 시각, 언어, 청각 장애가 있는 노동자를 돕는 보조 장치에 대해 구체적으로 설명하기 시작하며, (B)에서 그에 대한 예시(음성 인식 등)를 들고 저숙련 노동자의 역량 강화를 언급합니다. (A)에서 추가적인 예시(번역, 텍스트 생성기)를 들어 내용을 마무리하는 (C)-(B)-(A) 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. (A) The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. (B) Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? (C) The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. (D) Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. (E) What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.insertion_sentence: Unfamiliarity is the reason for this initial lack of acceptance.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'this initial lack of acceptance(이러한 초기 수용의 부족)'는 앞 문장의 '위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 오해받았던 상황'을 지칭합니다. 또한 (A) 뒤의 문장에서 그 이유로 '음악적 형태나 아이디어가 완전히 새로운 것'이었다는 설명이 이어지므로, '생소함(Unfamiliarity)'을 언급한 주어진 문장은 (A) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. (A) This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. (B) On the contrary, those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. (C) Solely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." (D) The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 부정적인 상태에서 부정적인 생각의 형태에 에너지를 주게 된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (B) 뒤에 나오는 'On the contrary(반대로)'는 앞의 부정적인 상태와 대조되어 에너지가 높은 사람들의 긍정적인 상태를 설명하므로, 주어진 문장은 대조의 기준이 되는 (B) 자리에 오는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 어법상 어색한 것 세 개를 골라 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: Seawater contains an ⓐ<u>abundance</u> of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics ⓑ<u>that</u> cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if ⓒ<u>allowing</u> to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans ⓓ<u>have</u> been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more ⓔ<u>prompt</u> than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has ⓕ<u>led to</u> more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.*dissolved 용해된 **anoxic 산소 결핍의
subjective_conditions: 1. 답안지에 어색한 것의 기호를 적고, 어법상 바르게 고쳐야 정답으로 인정
2. 주어진 단어와 원형이 전혀 다른 단어로 답을 작성하면 점수 없음*원형: 단어의 기본이 되는 형태. 예시) does의 원형은 do이다.
questions.explanation: ⓒ 'if (it is) allowed' 구문으로 수동의 의미가 필요하므로 과거분사 allowed가 적절합니다. ⓓ 문장의 주어는 'the amount(단수)'이므로 단수 동사인 has가 적절합니다. ⓔ 동사 falling을 수식하는 부사 형태인 promptly가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말을 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: A brilliant alternative to (A)__________ traffic (B)__________ is (C)__________ traffic. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.*animus 반감, 미움
subjective_conditions: 1. 빈칸 (A)를 '완화시키는'의 뜻을 가진 r로 시작하는 9개 알파벳의 한 단어로 채울 것
2. 빈칸 (B)를 '혼잡'의 뜻을 가진 c로 시작하는 10개 알파벳의 한 단어로 채울 것
3. 빈칸 (C)를 '제거하는'의 뜻을 가진 r로 시작하는 8개 알파벳의 한 단어로 채울 것
4. 주어진 철자로 시작하는 단어를 작성하지 않은 경우 점수 없음
5. 어법상 오류가 있거나 철자 오류로 문장의 의미가 바뀔 경우 감점함
questions.explanation: (A) '완화시키는'이라는 뜻의 r로 시작하는 9자 단어는 relieving입니다. (B) '혼잡'이라는 뜻의 c로 시작하는 10자 단어는 congestion입니다. (C) '제거하는'이라는 뜻의 r로 시작하는 8자 단어는 removing입니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses"가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are <u>putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses</u>. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show - whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ② seeing things through the old medium
③ interpreting the world as it used to be
④ accepting messages as a new medium delivers them
⑤ looking for information a new medium has buried in it
questions.explanation: 이 글은 매체 자체가 메시지이며, 정보의 내용보다 정보가 전달되는 방식(매체)이 우리가 세상을 보는 방식에 더 큰 영향을 미친다는 마샬 맥루한의 이론을 설명하고 있습니다. '새로운 종류의 고글을 쓴다'는 것은 새로운 매체가 정보를 전달하는 특유의 방식과 코드에 따라 세상을 바라보게 된다는 의미이므로, 4번 '새로운 매체가 전달하는 방식대로 메시지를 받아들이는 것'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 메시지 그 자체를 흡수하는 것
② 오래된 매체를 통해 사물을 보는 것
③ 세상을 예전 방식대로 해석하는 것
④ 새로운 매체가 전달하는 방식대로 메시지를 받아들이는 것
⑤ 새로운 매체가 그 안에 숨겨둔 정보를 찾는 것

questions.question: 3. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. ⓐFrom an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" for survival that, when triggered, directs many of our activities. ⓑFor example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation or avoid it, and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely. ⓒFear that we remember can be eliminated by identifying the cause of the fear. ⓓRegardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us survive challenges within our environment long ago. ⓔIf they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 감정이 종의 생존과 적응을 돕기 위해 진화해 왔다는 것입니다. 공포가 위험을 피하게 하고, 분노가 위협을 쫓아내며, 긍정적 감정이 유대를 돕는다는 맥락에서 ⓒ는 기억된 공포를 제거하는 방법에 대해 언급하고 있으므로 글의 전체적인 흐름인 '생존을 위한 감정의 진화적 기능'에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
options: ① difference between homologous and analogous in biological similarities
② specific methods biologists use to determine evolutionary relationships
③ common mistakes biologists make when studying evolutionary lineages
④ difficulty in classifying organs as analogous or homologous traits
⑤ unresolved philosophical problems in evolutionary biology
questions.explanation: 이 글은 생물학적 유사성을 '상사형질(Analogous)'과 '호몠형질(Homologous)'로 구분하어 설명하고 읈습니다. 상사형질은 기눔은 같지만 기원이 다른 것이고, 호몠형질은 기눔은 다를 수 읈지만 공통 조상에게서 유래한 것임을 밝히고 읈으므로 둀 형질의 차이점이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 생물학적 유사성에서 호몠형질과 상사형질의 차이
② 생물학자들이 진화적 관계를 결정하기 위해 사용하눤 구체적인 방법
③ 생물학자들이 진화 계통을 연구할 때 저지리는 흔한 실수
④ 기관을 상사 혹은 호몠 형질로 분류하눤 것의 어려움
⑤ 진화 생물학에서 해결되지 않은 철학적 문제들

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 9월 36번]
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by ①<u>watching</u> what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is ②<u>imperfect</u>. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it ③<u>fewer</u> times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers ④<u>copying</u> their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not ⑤<u>restricted</u> to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 세포(mirror neurons)의 작용을 통한 모방 학습을 설명하고 있습니다. 문맥상 내용을 살펴보면, 부모가 혀를 내미는 행동을 '충분히' 혹은 '더 많이' 반복할수록 아기가 혀를 더 자주 내밀게 된다는 상관관계를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '더 적은 횟수'를 의미하는 'fewer'는 문맥상 어색하며, '충분한' 혹은 '더 많은' 의미를 가진 'enough'나 'more' 등으로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 31번]
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason these great composers' works were not fully appreciated in their time is that they were not ____________. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the 'host' of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri was not a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work was too conventional. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 이해받지 못한 이유가 그들의 아이디어가 기존의 관습을 벗어나 매우 새로웠기 때문임을 설명하고 있습니다. 지문 하단에서 살리에리가 위대한 작곡가가 되지 못한 이유를 '너무 전형적(too conventional)'이었기 때문이라고 언급한 것과 대조해 볼 때, 위대한 작곡가들의 작품이 당대에 인정받지 못한 이유는 그들의 곡이 '전형적이지 않았기(not typical)' 때문이라는 ①번이 빈칸 뒤의 '완전히 새로웠다(completely new)'는 설명과 일관되게 호응합니다.
options_translation: ① 전형적인
② 완벽한
③ 심오한
④ 복잡한
⑤ 독특한

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 40번]
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to _________________________________. Even though she is still getting 'paid' the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unequal. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
options: ① reject the payment she gets for her efforts
② gather more rocks to earn what she likes
③ yield the rewards to the experimenter
④ share the gains with the other monkey
⑤ accept the rewards with pleasure
questions.explanation: 카푸친 원숭이는 같은 노동에 대해 같은 보상(오이)을 받을 때는 만족하지만, 옆의 원숭이가 더 선호하는 보상(포도)을 받는 것을 보면 자신의 상황이 변하지 않았음에도 불구하고 불공평함을 느끼게 됩니다. 지문 하단에서 원숭이가 자신의 불쾌감을 표현하기 위해 기존의 보상(오이)마저 포기할 용의가 있다고 설명했으므로, 빈칸에는 자신이 얻은 보상을 거부한다는 내용의 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 노력에 대하여 받는 보상을 거부하다
② 자신이 좋아하는 것을 얻기 위해 더 많은 돌을 모으다
③ 실험자에게 보상을 양도하다
④ 다른 원숭이와 이익을 나누다
⑤ 기쁘게 보상을 받아들이다

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 21번]
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, 'I can't,' is to _________________________________________. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called 'hanging out with the winners.' The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
options: ① study the personality traits of individuals in self-help groups

questions.explanation: 무력감이나 우울감에서 벗어나는 효과적인 방법은 긍정적인 에너지를 가진 사람들 곁에 머물며 그들로부터 긍정적인 에너지를 전달받는 것입니다. 지문에서 언급된 '승리자들과 어울리기(hanging out with the winners)'는 우리가 겪는 역경을 이미 극복한 사람들 곁에 있는 것을 의미하므로, ②번이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Immediately after reading our text book or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form.
ordered_passages: (A) Unless you retest your knowledge, the working memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself. It's easy to put this idea into practice on your own.

(B) We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space, but this short-term sections has nothing to do with the long-term memory. After a few minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous.

(C) All you have to do is prepare flash cards: on one side, you write a question, and on the other, the answer. To test yourself, draw the cards one after the other, and for each card, try to remember the answer before checking it by turning to the other side.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 벼락치기가 효과적이라는 착각을 하는 이유로 정보가 작업 기억에 남아있기 때문임을 설명합니다. (B)에서는 이 단기 기억이 장기 기억과는 관련이 없으며 곧 사라지기 시작한다는 점을 지적하며 착각의 원인을 구체화합니다. (A)에서는 지식을 재시험하지 않으면 기억이 사라지므로 스스로 테스트하는 것이 중요하다고 제안합니다. (C)에서는 그 구체적인 실천 방법으로 플래시 카드를 활용하는 법을 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are usually at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can promote communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.summary_sentence: AI can (A)__________ the access to work for workers who are generally in a (B)__________ position in the labor market, such as disabled workers and low-skilled workers.
questions.explanation: AI는 장애가 있거나 저숙련 노동자와 같이 노동 시장에서 소외되기 쉬운 사람들의 업무 접근성을 높임으로써 직장의 포용성을 개선할 수 있습니다. 예를 들어, 장애인을 위한 보조 기기나 실시간 번역 및 텍스트 생성 기술은 이들의 업무 능력을 향상시키고 동료와의 소통을 돕습니다. 따라서 AI는 취약한(vulnerable) 위치에 있는 노동자들의 업무 접근을 용이하게(facilitate) 만든다는 것이 글의 핵심입니다.
options_translation: 제한하다 ... 우월한
방해하다 ... 불리한
완화하다 ... 유익한

용이하게 하다 ... 취약한

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. Between 200 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as exminations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback.
questions.summary_sentence: While the transition of higher education from an elite to a mass system (A)__________ participation in higher education, it also created a(n) (B)__________ in student assessment, placing more emphasis on grades than on feedback.
questions.explanation: 고등 교육이 소수 정예에서 대중적인 시스템으로 변화하면서 참여(participation)율은 크게 높아졌지만(fostered), 실제 교육 현장에서는 많은 인원을 효율적으로 관리하기 위해 표준화된 시험과 최소한의 피드백을 사용하는 방식이 도입되었습니다. 이로 인해 학생들은 발전을 위한 피드백보다 성적에 더 집중하게 되는 모순적인 상황, 즉 학생 평가에서의 불일치(inconsistency)가 발생하게 되었습니다.
options_translation: 촉진했다 ... 일관성
촉진했다 ... 불일치
향상했다 ... 최적화된 시스템
수축했다 ... 신뢰도
수축했다 ... 이중적 접근

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the passage, (A)__________ lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle makes streets safer for everyone while motor vehicle lanes are also required in order for cities to be more (B)__________.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 교통 정체를 완화하는 방법으로 자동차 도로를 줄이고 자전거와 보행자를 위한 공간을 확보하는 것의 장점을 설명합니다. 동시에 배송 트럭을 위한 도로의 필요성을 언급하며, 이는 주민들이 가까운 상점에서 물건을 구매할 수 있게 하여 도시를 더 친환경적으로 만드는 필수 요소라고 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 공간을 유지하거나 확보한다는 의미인 'retaining'이, (B)에는 도시를 친환경적으로 만든다는 의미의 'eco-friendly'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 ⓐ~ⓘ 문장 중, 어법상 어색한 표현이 있는 문장을 찾고, 어색한 표현을 올바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: ⓐHave you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? ⓑMaybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. ⓒThis is of course quite a common experience and the explanation is actually fairly simple. ⓓThere are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. ⓔOne is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner car. ⓕBut because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. ⓖVibrations conduct through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. ⓗLower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. ⓘThat makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
questions.explanation: 문장 ⓖ에서 주어인 'Vibrations(진동)'은 뼈를 통해 '전도되는' 대상이므로, 능동태인 conduct 대신 수동태인 are conducted를 사용해야 문맥상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions. But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
options: ① Searching online can boost people's confidence in their knowledge, even about unrelated topics
② Profound understanding of diverse cultures improves an individual's communication skills.
③ Collective intelligence on the internet provides new and diverse solutions to a problem.
④ Internet algorithms can trap individuals in biases and prejudices
⑤ Using the internet always leads to a decrease in confidence.
questions.explanation: 글에 제시된 연구 결과에 따르면, 인터넷 검색을 사용한 집단은 검색하지 않은 집단에 비해 새로운 질문(인터넷으로 검색하지 않은 주제)에 대해서도 자신의 지식 수준을 더 높게 평가했습니다. 즉, 인터넷 사용이 주제와 무관하게 지적 자신감을 상승시킨다는 것이 글의 핵심 내용입니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Nearly everything has to go through your mouth to get to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and prevent it from harm - with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. From the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. What happens in the mouth is usually (A)<u>just the tip of the iceberg</u> and a reflection of what is happening in other parts of the body. Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease that affects the entire body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, posing serious health risks.
options: ① tips for keeping teeth and gums clean and healthy
② a serious environmental issue that must be conquered
③ a clean zone on Earth that should be protected for humanity
④ a tiny part of the mysterious beauty in the vast natural world
⑤ a minor part of more significant health issues occuring in the body

options_translation: ① 치아와 잇몸을 깨끗하고 건강하게 유지하기 위한 조언들
② 정복해야 할 심각한 환경 문제
③ 인류를 위해 보호되어야 할 지구상의 깨끗한 구역

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 32번]
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along ─ whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS ─ and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show ─ whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire ─ you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans to communicate ─ it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① the role of books in shaping culture
② the history of television programming
③ the evolution of communication methods
④ the influence of new media on perception
⑤ the importance of visual media in education
questions.explanation: 이 글은 새로운 매체(인섄물, TV, SNS 등)가 등장할 때마다 우리가 세상을 바바보는 방식(인식)이 매체 관점에 따라 달라진다는 내용을 담고 은유적으로(고글)설명하고 읈습니다. 따라서 '인식에 미찘는 새로운 매체의 영향'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 문화 형성에 있어서 책의 역할
② 텔레비전 프로그래밍의 역사
③ 의사소통 방법의 진화
④ 인식에 미찘는 새로운 매체의 영향
⑤ 교육에서 시각 매체의 중요성

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 29번]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
options: ① role of technology in enhancing decision-making processes
② advantages of having a mechanistic organizational structure
③ significance of departmental culture on employee performance
④ importance of employee training in minimizing organizational conflict
⑤ impact of organizational structure on conflict management

options_translation: ① 의사 결정 과정을 향상시키는 기술의 역할
② 기계적 져직 구조를 갖는 것의 장점
③ 직원 성과에 미찘는 부서 문화의 중요성
④ 져직 내 갈등을 촜소화하는 데 있어서 직원 교육의 중요성

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 38번]
questions.passage: "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
options: ① the functionality of animal wings
② the evolution of mammalian limbs
③ the anatomy of different species' limbs
④ the role of evolution in animal adaptation
⑤ distinguishing analogous and homologous traits
questions.explanation: 이 글은 생물학적 특성 중 '사상 형질(Analogous traits)'과 '혼성 형질(Homologous traits)'의 차이점을 설명하고 읈습니다. 사상 형질은 기능은 같지만 기원은 다른 것이고, 혼성 형질은 기능은 다르더라도 공통의 조상에게서 기원한 것임을 밝히고 있으므로, 이 둀 개념을 구분하는 것이 주제가 됩습니다.
options_translation: ① 동물 날개의 기능성
② 포유류 사지의 진화
③ 서로 다른 종의 사지 해부학
④ 동물 적응에 있어서 진화의 역할
⑤ 사상 형질과 혼성 형질 구분하기

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whales, the largest animals on earth, swim to the deepest parts of the sea to feed and come up to the surface to breathe. While they are near the surface, they release waste from their body. This way, they bring essential nutrients from the deep sea to the surface waters. These nutrients form the base of all marine food chains and keep the marine ecosystem running. Whales are also really important after they die. The dead body, also called "whale fall," sinks toward the bottom of the sea and becomes food for many fish species that live in the harsh conditions of the sea floor. In addition, the dead body is good for the environment. As it has a lot of carbon in it, by sinking to the sea floor, it keeps the carbon out of the atmosphere. According to marine scientists, the amount of carbon that whales take to the bottom of the sea is about 190,000 tons annually, which equals the amount of carbon produced by 80,000 cars.
options: ① feeding habits of whales in the ocean
② impact of climate change on whale populations
③ role of whales in marine ecosystems and carbon cycling
④ differences between whales and other marine animals
⑤ physical characteristics of largest animals on earth
questions.explanation: 이 글은 고래가 깊은 바다의 영양분을 수면으로 끌어올려 해양 먹이 사슬의 기초를 형성하고, 죽은 후에도 심해 생물에게 먹이를 제공하며, 탄소를 심해로 운반하여 대기 중 탄소를 줄이는 역할을 한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 고래가 해양 생태계와 탄소 순환에서 하는 역할이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 바다에서 고래의 먹이 습성
② 기후 변화가 고래 개체군에 미치는 영향
③ 해양 생태계와 탄소 순환에서 고래의 역할

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. They do well enough in school to keep advancing. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ends with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now lack a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when the journey really begins. When school is finished, your growth becomes voluntary. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career are likely to stop progressing as a result.
options: ① The Next Leap: Taking Ownership of Your Growth After School
② Retirement: The Ultimate Goal After College
③ How to Relax After Graduation
④ The Benefits of Staying Stagnant
⑤ Tips for Having a More Enjoyable and Fulfilling School Experience
questions.explanation: 이 글은 학교 교육이 끝난 후에는 성장이 자발적인 것이 되므로, 스스로 자신의 성장에 책임을 지고 시간과 에너지를 투자해야 한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '다음 도약: 학교 졸업 후 성장의 주도권을 갖는 것'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다음 도약: 졸업 후 당신의 성장에 대한 소유권 갖기
② 은퇴: 대학 이후의 궁극적인 목표
③ 졸업 후 휴식하는 방법
④ 정체되어 있는 것의 이점

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous Nongreat composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
options: ① Navigating Unfamiliarity: The Fate of Great Composers
① Navigating Unfamiliarity: The Fate of Great Composers
② The Impact of Composers on Musical History
③ The History of Classical Music
④ The Misunderstood Genius of Beethoven
⑤ The Movie Amadeus: The Rivalry of Great Composers
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 이해받지 못했던 이유가 그들의 독창성으로 인한 '낯설음' 때문이었다고 설명합니다. 반면 실력이 좋았으나 위대하지 못했던 살리에리의 예시를 통해, 독창성이 부족하여 당대의 다른 곡들과 비슷했던 작품은 위대함의 반열에 오르지 못했음을 보여줍니다. 따라서 위대한 작곡가들이 겪는 운명(낯설음과 이해받지 못함)을 다룬 1번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 생소함 헤쳐나가기: 위대한 작곡가들의 운명
② 작곡가들이 음악사에 미친 영향
③ 클래식 음악의 역사
④ 베토벤의 오해받은 천재성
⑤ 영화 아마데우스: 위대한 작곡가들의 라이벌 관계

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
options: ② The Science of Language Acquisition
③ The Evolution of Modern Tools in Culture
④ How Observation Shapes Human Learning
⑤ Trial and Error: A Limited Path to Knowledge
questions.explanation: 거울 뉴런의 발견을 통해 인간이 관찰을 통해 학습하는 능력이 매우 중요하다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 아기들의 모방 행동부터 현대 문화의 발전까지, 타인을 단순히 지켜보는 것(관찰)이 인간의 학습과 문화 발전에 핵심적인 역할을 한다는 내용이므로 '관찰이 어떻게 인간의 학습을 형성하는가'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 아동 발달에서의 모방
② 언어 습득의 과학
③ 문화에서 현대 도구의 진화
④ 관찰이 인간의 학습을 어떻게 형성하는가
⑤ 시행착오: 지식으로 가는 제한된 길

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
options: ① Why Our Voices Sound Different to Us
③ The Psychology of Hearing Your Own Voice
④ The Influence of Accents on Self-Perception
⑤ Common Misconceptions About Voice Recording
questions.explanation: 우리가 자신의 목소리를 들을 때 외부 공기를 통한 경로와 뼈를 통한 내부 진동 경로 두 가지를 모두 사용하며, 특히 뼈를 통한 진동이 저주파를 강조하기 때문에 본인에게는 더 깊고 풍부하게 들린다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 왜 우리 목소리가 우리 자신에게 다르게 들리는지를 묻는 ①번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 Grace Braddock에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Dear Ms. MacAlpine,I was so excited to hear that your brand is opening a new shop on Bruns Street next month. I have always appreciated the way your brand helps women to feel more stylish and confident. I am writing in response to your ad in the Bruns Journal. I graduated from the Meline School of Fashion and have worked as a sales assistant at LoganMart for the last five years. During that time, I've developed strong customer service and sales skills, and now I would like to apply for the sales position in your clothing store. I am available for an interview at your earliest convenience. I look forward to hearing from you. Thank you for reading my letter.Yours sincerely,Grace Braddock
options: ① She was so thrilled to hear the news of Ms. MacAlpine's brand opening a new shop.
② She has always admired how Ms. MacAlpine's brand empowers women to feel more fashionable and confident.

questions.explanation: 본문에서 'I graduated from the Meline School of Fashion'이라고 언급하며 이미 졸업했음을 나타내고 있으므로, 곧 졸업할 예정이라는 ③번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 그녀는 Ms. MacAlpine의 브랜드가 새 매장을 연다는 소식을 듣고 매우 기뻤다.
② 그녀는 Ms. MacAlpine의 브랜드가 여성들이 더 패셔너블하고 자신감을 느끼게 해주는 방식을 항상 존경해 왔다.
③ 그녀는 곧 Meline 패션 학교를 졸업할 것이다.
④ 그녀는 강력한 고객 서비스 및 판매 기술을 쌓아왔다.
⑤ 그녀는 Ms. MacAlpine으로부터 소식을 듣기를 기대하고 있다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist ⓐ<u>due to</u> their contribution to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, ⓑ<u>directing</u> many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, ⓒ<u>narrows</u> our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways ⓓ<u>which</u> they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us ⓔ<u>to adapt</u> and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: ⓓ의 which는 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오므로 관계부사 how를 대신하는 in which 또는 that으로 쓰여야 합니다. ways와 how는 같이 쓸 수 없으므로 ways that 혹은 ways in which가 적절합니다. 추가로 ⓑ의 경우 that절 내의 본동사 자리이므로 directs가 되어야 하나, 문제에서 정답이 ④(ⓓ)로 제시되어 있습니다. (실제 원문 변형 과정에서 ⓑ도 directing에서 directs로 수정되어야 하는 오류성 지점이 있으나, 관계대명사/관계부사 구별인 ⓓ가 명확한 문법적 오류 포인트입니다.)

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen, ⓐ<u>which</u> all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water ⓑ<u>is</u> - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence, ⓒ<u>allowed</u> to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more ⓓ<u>rapidly</u> than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced ⓔ<u>them,</u> the populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: ⓑ의 is는 앞의 일반동사 holds를 대신하는 대동사 자리이므로 does로 고쳐야 합니다. 비교 구문에서 'than warm water does (hold)'의 의미를 가집니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for ⓐ<u>overcoming</u> of helplessness, depression to have successfully navigated similar challenges. This support can help us address the issues we are currently ⓑ<u>confronting</u> and inspire positive change. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought remain ⓒ<u>fragile.</u> Those who vibrate at higher frequency are liberated from the weight of their negative thoughts and ⓓ<u>stimulate</u> positive thought patterns. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The advantage gained operates on a spiritual level of awareness, ⓔ<u>impending</u> a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 ⓔ의 impending(임박한, 곧 일어날 것 같은)은 긍정적인 에너지의 전달을 가능하게 하거나 촉진한다는 의미가 되어야 적절하므로, 'facilitating'이나 'enabling'과 같은 표현으로 바뀌어야 합니다. 이 글은 더 높은 진동 주파수를 가진 사람들과 함께 있는 것이 긍정적인 생각 패턴을 자극하고 긍정적인 에너지 전이를 돕는다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must ⓐ<u>agree</u> over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ⓑ<u>reinforce</u> public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements ⓒ<u>decrease</u> public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is not a ⓓ<u>reliable</u> process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the ⓔ<u>same</u> as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
questions.explanation: ⓑ의 reinforce(강화하다)는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다. 엄격한 규정을 두는 이유는 장기 적출을 위한 조기 뇌사 판정에 대한 대중의 두려움을 '완화(ease)'하거나 '진정(allay)'시키기 위한 것이기 때문입니다. 하지만 필자는 이러한 규정들이 오히려 의구심을 더 만들어낼 수도 있다고 지적하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve ________________ in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where interpersonal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: 지문은 AI가 장애가 있는 노동자나 저숙련 노동자, 비모국어 화자 등 노동 시장에서 불리한 위치에 있는 사람들의 접근성과 업무 능력을 향상시켜 준다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 AI가 일터에서의 '포용성(inclusion)'을 향상시킬 수 있다는 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 분업
포용성
다양성
리더십
경쟁

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Despite the remarkable progress in deep-learning based facial recognition approaches in recent years, in terms of identification performance, they still have limitations. ⓐThese limitations relate to the database used in the learning stage. If the selected database does not contain enough instances, the result may be systematically affected. ⓑDeep learning is a powerful predictive modeling tool that helps organizations forecast future events and trends, facilitating strategic decision-making and planning. ⓒFor example, the performance of a facial biometric system may decrease if the person to be identified was enrolled over 10 years ago. ⓓThe factor to consider is that this person may experience changes in the texture of the face, particularly with the appearance of wrinkles and sagging skin. These changes may be highlighted by weight gain or loss. ⓔTo counteract this problem, researchers have developed models for face aging or digital de-aging. It is used to compensate for the differences in facial characteristics, which appear over a given time period.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 딥러닝 기반 안면 인식 시스템의 한계(데이터베이스 부족, 세월에 따른 얼굴 변화 등)와 이를 해결하기 위한 노력을 다루고 있습니다. ⓑ는 딥러닝이 조직의 미래 예측과 전략 수립을 돕는 도구라는 일반적인 장점을 설명하고 있어, 안면 인식의 기술적 한계라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. (A) Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. (B) This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity symbolized by the metaphor of the star and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. (C) The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. (D) Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그러나 이러한 비판은 평범한 유명인이라는 현상이 명성의 의미를 재구성한다는 점을 간과하고 있다'는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (B) 앞뒤 문장에서는 소셜 미디어 유명인들이 전통적인 엘리트 유명인과 같은 재능이 없다는 비판을 받는다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. (C) 이후 문장부터는 평범한 유명인이 다른 평범한 사람들과의 빈번한 상호작용을 통해 주의를 끌고, 명성 자체가 소셜 미디어상의 수치(점수)로 정의되는 등 명성의 의미가 어떻게 바뀌었는지 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (C)의 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest loss of crop diversity ⓐ<u>came in the decades that followed the Second World War.</u> In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce ⓑ<u>grains such as rice and wheat on an enormous scale.</u> And thousands of traditional varieties ⓒ<u>were replaced by a small number of new super-productive ones</u>. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, ⓓ<u>the danger of creating more uniform crops are that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters.</u> Specifically, a global food system ⓔ<u>that depends on just a narrow selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.</u>
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'the danger of creating more uniform crops'로, 핵심 주어는 단수인 'the danger'입니다. 따라서 동사는 복수형인 are가 아니라 단수형인 is로 쓰여야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A remarkable characteristic of the visual system is that it has the ability of adapting itself. Psychologist George M. Stratton made this clear in an impressive self-experiment. Stratton wore reversing glasses for several days, which literally turned the world upside down for him. In the beginning, this caused him great difficulties: just putting food in his mouth with a fork was a challenge for him. With time, however, his visual system adjusted to the new stimuli from reality, and he was able to act normally in his environment again, even seeing it upright when he concentrated. As he took off his reversing glasses, he was again confronted with problems: he used the wrong hand when he wanted to reach for something, for example. Fortunately, Stratton could reverse the perception, and he did not have to wear reversing glasses for the rest of his life. For him, everything returned to normal after one day.
questions.summary_sentence: Psychologist George M. Stratton demonstrated the visual system's (A)_____________ by wearing reversing glasses and eventually (B)_____________ despite briefly experiencing confusion after removing them.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 시각 체계가 새로운 자극에 적응하는 능력을 가지고 있다는 것을 보여줍니다. Stratton의 실험에서 시각 체계는 거꾸로 보이는 안경에 적응했고, 다시 안경을 벗었을 때도 잠시 혼란이 있었으나 결국 정상으로 돌아왔습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 적응 능력을 뜻하는 '유연성(flexibility)'이, (B)에는 다시 정상으로 '적응(adapting)'했다는 말이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 저항 / 투쟁하는
② 엄격함 / 투쟁하는
③ 엄격함 / 적응하는
④ 유연성 / 적응하는
⑤ 유연성 / 악화되는

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 30번]
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.summary_sentence: Cities can (A)______________ safety and sustainability by promoting cycling and maintaining efficient delivery vehicles, which reduces (B)______________ on cars.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 자동차 교통량을 줄이고 자전거 도로를 확보하며 효율적인 물류 운송 시스템(배달 트럭 활용)을 갖춤으로써 도시의 안전과 지속 가능성을 높일 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 이를 통해 주민들이 차를 타기보다 걷거나 자전거를 이용하게 되므로 자동차에 대한 의존도가 낮아지게 됩니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '향상시키다(enhance)', (B)에는 '의존(reliance)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 향상시키다 - 의존
② 감소시키다 - 의존
③ 무시하다 - 필요
④ 감소시키다 - 독립
⑤ 향상시키다 - 회복력

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 33번]
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
questions.summary_sentence: While concepts are (A)______________ for understanding the world, they may result in misguided attempts to find (B)_______________.
questions.explanation: 지문은 개념(Concepts)이 인간의 생존에 필수적(vital)이지만, 존재하지 않는 본질을 찾으려 하는 본질주의의 위험이 있다고 설명합니다. 과학 역사에서 존재하지 않는 '에테르'를 찾으려 했던 사례를 통해, 잘못된 개념이 존재하지 않는 것(illusion, black cat)을 찾게 만드는 오류를 범할 수 있음을 보여줍니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '필수적인(essential)', (B)에는 '환상/환영(illusions)'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 필수적인 - 환상
② 사소한 - 대답
③ 무관한 - 해결책
④ 선택적인 - 사실
⑤ 복잡한 - 아이디어

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.5점]
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
options: ① 조종사와 승무원은 일정 시간 비행 안전 훈련을 이수해야 한다.
② 위험을 감수하는 선택을 할 때는 두려운 감정보다는 사실에 근거해야 한다.
③ 환경에 부담을 줄이기 위해 비행기를 이용한 해외여행의 빈도를 줄여야 한다.
④ 비행 관련 사고를 줄이기 위해서 기내 반입 금지 물품 검사를 더욱 강화해야 한다.
⑤ 탑승객의 안전을 보장하기 위해 안전장치를 점검하고 노후한 장비는 교체해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 필자는 사람들이 비행기 사고에 대한 공포 때문에 통계적으로 더 위험한 자동차 운전을 선택하는 경향이 있음을 지적하며, 위험을 감수하는 결정을 내릴 때 감정이 아닌 사실(facts)에 근거해야 한다고 마지막 문장에서 명시적으로 주장하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 a black cat이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find <u>a black cat</u> in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① an illusion conjured up by the physicists
② a definite truth that exists but not yet explored
③ the ignorance which blocks us to see the essence
④ a misguiding concept which makes scientists' efforts fruitless
⑤ an essence that people pursuit but cannot be found due to the wrong concept
questions.explanation: 본문에서 '검은 고양이'는 과학자들이 에테르(ether)라는 잘못된 개념을 바탕으로 존재하지도 않는 대상을 찾으려고 헛수고를 했던 상황을 비유합니다. 즉, 잘못된 개념으로 인해 찾을 수 없는 '본질'을 의미하므로 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 물리학자들에 의해 만들어진 환상
존재하지만 아직 탐구되지 않은 확고한 진리
우리가 본질을 보는 것을 막는 무지
과학자들의 노력을 헛수고로 만드는 오도하는 개념
잘못된 개념 때문에 발견될 수 없지만 사람들이 추구하는 본질

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
options: ① 집단생활을 하는 동물들은 인간처럼 생존을 위해 서로 협력한다.
② 인간은 인지적 능력에 따라 동물을 구분하고 계급을 나누려고 한다.
③ 동물들은 타고난 능력을 발휘하여 사물의 정확한 위치를 인식할 수 있다.
④ 인간은 동물보다 우월하다는 인식을 유지하기 위한 수단으로 언어를 사용한다.
⑤ 영장류의 언어는 규칙과 창조성을 가진다는 점에서 다른 동물의 의사소통 방식보다 우수하다.
questions.explanation: 프란스 드 발은 인간이 다른 동물과의 유사성을 폄하하며 자신들의 위치를 지키기 위해 언어를 도구로 사용한다고 주장한다. 동물의 행동을 인간의 것과 다른 기술적 용어로 부르거나, 지능을 본능으로 치부하는 등의 '언어적 거세'를 통해 인간이 우월한 위치에 있다는 환상을 유지한다는 것이 글의 핵심 내용이다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
options: ① the polarization of professionals and amateurs in sports business
② the chronic practices of executives in sports management business
③ the tendency of criticizing sports management by uninformed fans
④ the obligation for sports officials to protect promising youth athletes
⑤ the ambivalent attitudes of the public toward athletes in peak conditions
questions.explanation: 이 글은 스포츠 분야에서 전문 지식이 없는 팬들이나 대중들이 전문가(선수, 코치, 경영진)들에게 훈수를 두거나 비판하는 경향이 다른 전문직(의사, 회계사)에 비해 매우 두드러진다는 점을 설명하고 있다.
options_translation: ① 스포츠 비즈니스에서 전문가와 아마추어의 양극화
② 스포츠 관리 사업 경영진들의 만성적인 관행
③ 정보가 부족한 팬들에 의한 스포츠 경영 비판 경향
④ 유망한 어린 선수들을 보호해야 하는 스포츠 관계자들의 의무
⑤ 최고의 컨디션인 선수들에 대한 대중의 양가적인 태도

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
options: ① the role of creativity in achieving greatness
② the impact of generative AI on modern composers
③ the challenges encountered by critics in gaining acceptance
④ the reason why Salieri's work sounded familiar at that time
⑤ the value of familiarity in appreciating musical compositions
questions.explanation: 위대한 작곡가들은 당대에는 생소함 때문에 이해받지 못했으나, 그들의 독창적이고 새로운 아이디어가 결국 그들을 위대하게 만들었다. 반면 살리에리는 훌륭한 작곡가였음에도 불구하고 독창성이 부족해 위대한 작곡가 반열에 오르지 못했다는 예시를 통해 위대함을 달성하는 데 있어 창의성(독창성)의 역할을 주제로 다루고 있다.
options_translation: ① 위대함을 달성하는 데 있어 창의성의 역할
② 생성형 AI가 현대 작곡가들에게 미치는 영향
③ 비평가들이 수용되는 과정에서 겪는 어려움
④ 그 당시에 살리에리의 작품이 친숙하게 들렸던 이유
⑤ 음악 작품을 감상하는 데 있어 친숙함의 가치

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are - writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
options: ① So Many Men, So Many Characters
② How to Keep Our Own Ace in the Hole
③ The Problem with Measuring Oneself by One Ability
④ Cultivate Your Potential Area of Capability to Be Versatile
⑤ The Fever of Introducing AI Technology to Mental Competence
questions.explanation: 이 글은 눔가가 자신의 가치를 오직 하나의 '눙력'(지적 눙력, 재능, 외모 등)으로만 판단할 때 발생하는 문제점을 지적하고 을습니다. 수행 결과가 곧 괴 사람의 가치를 결정짓는 유일한 척도가 되는 것의 위험성을 경고하고 읈으례, ③ '하나의 눙력으로 자신을 측정하는 것의 문제점'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: 각양각색 (사람마다 성격이 다름)
우리만의 비장의 무기를 유지하는 방법
하나의 눙력으로 자신을 판단하는 것의 문제점
다재다능해지기 위해 잠재적인 역량 분야를 배양하라
지적 눙력에 AI 기술을 도입하려는 열푀

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a dropout, or worse.
options: ① Encouraging Your Child to Excel in Every Area
② How to Push Your Gifted Child to Reach Higher Goals
③ Why Gifted Children Should Always Strive for Perfection?
④ The Best Ways to Showcase Your Child's Talents to Others
⑤ Balancing Pride and Pressure: The Importance of Moderation When Raising a Gifted Child
questions.explanation: 이 글은 영재 자녀를 둔 부모가 자녀의 성과를 과도하게 자랑하는 것이 자녀에게 압박감과 잘못된 자아 인식을 심어줄 수 있음을 경고합니다. 따라서 자랑쉍운 발언을 절제하고 자녀 밡의 모습을 존중해줘야 한다는 내용이므로, ⑤ '자부심감과 압박감의 균형: 영재 자녀를 킬왈 때 절제의 중요성'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 자녀가 모든 분야에서 똀어나도록 격려하기
영재 자녀가 덄 높은 목표에 도달하도록 다괸치는 방법
영재 아이들이 왜 항상 완뷙을 추구해야 하는가?
자녀의 재능을 타인에게 배뽐내눠 수 있는 가장 좋은 방법
자부심감과 압박감의 균형: 영재 자녀를 킬왈 때 절제의 중요성

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 내용을 표로 정리한 것이다. 정리된 내용 중 옳지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.AspectSocial Media CelebritiesElite CelebritiesSource ofFameⓐGained through frequent interactions and social media metrics (eg, followers, Likes, clicks)Achieved through talent, skill, or class (eg, acting, singing)Nature ofFameⓑOrdinary fame, often considered as a social end in itselfElite fame, tied to recognized talents or accomplishmentsPublicPerceptionCriticized for lacking traditional talentsⓒViewed as possessing naturalized talent and classSocialRelationshipInteract frequently with followers, more accessibleⓓMaintain closeness from the public, more direct interactionChallengesFace criticism and barriers to crossing into elite celebrityⓔMaintain status through mystery and exclusivity
questions.explanation: 지문에서 엘리트 유명인(Elite Celebrities)은 '신비감과 계급적 거리감(mystery and hierarchical distance)'에 의해 특징지어진다고 설명되어 있습니다. 따라서 대중과 친밀함을 유지하고 직접적인 상호작용을 한다는 ⓓ는 엘리트 유명인의 특성에 어긋나며, 이는 오히려 일반인 유명인(Ordinary Celebrity)의 특성에 가깝습니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 12. 다음 2024 Chemistry Fair in Alexandria Science Museum에 관한 안내문의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: 2024 Chemistry Fair in Alexandria Science MuseumChemistry Fair is held for local middle school students by Alexandria Science Museum.[When]- Saturday, October 9, 2024 (10 a.m. to 6 p.m.)[Goal]- Encouraging middle school students to be interested in chemistry- Gaining hands-on experiment under the guidance of under-graduate students- Finding chemical reactions through everyday activities such as cooking and cleaning[Enrolment]- Click the banner on Alexandria Science Museum homepage- Only nearby middle school students can apply
options: ② 학생들이 다양한 과학 분야에 흥미를 갖도록 격려한다.
③ 대학원생들의 안내로 직접 실험을 해볼 수 있다.
④ 일상 활동에서 일어나는 화학 반응을 찾아본다.
⑤ 전국의 중학생은 화학 박람회에 지원할 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 안내문의 [Goal] 세 번째 항목인 'Finding chemical reactions through everyday activities such as cooking and cleaning(요리와 청소 같은 일상 활동을 통해 화학 반응을 발견하기)'에서 확인할 수 있듯이 ④번이 내용과 일치합니다. ①은 10월 9일 토요일 하루만 열리고, ②는 화학(chemistry) 분야에 한정되며, ③은 대학원생이 아닌 대학생(under-graduate students), ⑤는 전국의 중학생이 아닌 인근 중학생(Only nearby middle school students)만이 지원할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고른 것으로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When you pluck a guitar string it moves back and forth hundreds of times every second. Naturally, this movement is so fast ①<u>that</u> you cannot see it - you just see the blurred outline of the moving string. Strings vibrating in this way on their own ②<u>are made</u> hardly any noise because strings are very thin and don't push much air about. But if you attach a string to a big hollow box (like a guitar body), then the vibration is amplified and the note sounds ③<u>loudly</u>. The vibration of the string is passed on to the wooden panels of the guitar body, which ④<u>vibrate</u> back and forth at the same rate as the string. The vibration of the wood creates more powerful waves in the air pressure, which travel away from the guitar. When the waves reach your eardrums they flex in and out the same number of times a second ⑤<u>as</u> the original string.
questions.explanation:
②번: 주어인 'Strings'가 소리를 내는 능동의 주체이므로 수동태 'are made'는 어색합니다. 능동태인 'make'로 고쳐야 하며, 'hardly'와 함께 '소리를 거의 내지 못한다'는 의미로 쓰여야 합니다.
③번: 'sound'는 감각동사(이형식 동사)로 뒤에 보어로 부사가 아닌 형용사가 와야 합니다. 따라서 'loudly'를 형용사 'loud'로 고쳐야 합니다.

[오답 분석]
① 'so ~ that' 구문에서 결과를 나타내는 접속사로 적절하게 쓰였습니다.
④ 관계대명사 'which'의 선행사가 복수형인 'wooden panels'이므로 복수 동사 'vibrate'는 적절합니다.
⑤ 'the same ~ as' 구문으로 '~와 같은'이라는 비교를 나타내어 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 바르게 짝지어진 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively (A)[densely / poorly] populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been (B)[dropping / increasing] for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. (C)[Falling / Rising] oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: 찬물은 따뜻한 물보다 용존 산소를 더 많이 함유하므로 열대 바다는 상대적으로 생명체가 (A) 희박하게(poorly) 서식합니다. 지구 온난화로 인해 수온이 상승하면서 산소량이 (B) 감소(dropping)하고 있으며, 이러한 (C) 하락하는(Falling) 산소 수치는 해양 생태계에 부정적인 영향을 미칩니다.
options_translation: ① 밀집하게 / 떨어지는 / 하락하는
② 밀집하게 / 증가하는 / 상승하는
③ 희박하게 / 증가하는 / 하락하는
④ 희박하게 / 떨어지는 / 상승하는
⑤ 희박하게 / 떨어지는 / 하락하는

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals ⓐ<u>differ</u> in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are ⓑ<u>broadened</u>.
