For example, these people might keep ⓒ<u>separate</u> email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones - one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater ⓓ<u>distinction</u> between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer ⓔ<u>integrating</u> work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 일과 가정의 역할을 분리(segment)하려는 사람들과 통합(integrate)하려는 사람들의 차이를 설명하고 있습니다. 분리하려는 사람들은 경계를 넘나드는 일을 최소화하고자 하므로, ⓑ의 'broadened(넓어진)'는 'minimized(최소화된)'와 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are ____________________, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
options: ⑤ solid and hard in decision making
questions.explanation: 기계적 구조(mechanistic structure)가 수직적 계층과 많은 규칙을 가진다고 대조적으로 설명하고 있으므로, 유기적 구조(organic structures)는 의사결정이 덜 중앙 집중적이고 조직 전반에 퍼져 있는 '유연하고 평면적인 구조(flexible and flat-structured)'가 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 좁게 집중된
② 본질적으로 더 수직적인
③ 유연하고 평면 구조인
④ 고도로 공식화되고 중앙 집중화된
⑤ 의사결정에 있어 견고하고 딱딱한

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is __________________________________.
options: ① tolerable and patient in adverse conditions without a blow
② powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors
③ so influential that the person can signal negative messages
④ too persistent for researchers to sway as much as they intend
⑤ a liberalist who pursues his signature style without being conscious
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 사회적 규범을 약간 위반하는 사람들을 긍정적으로 평가한다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 격식 있는 자리에서 빨간 나비넥타이를 매거나 강의 중 빨간 운동화를 신는 행위는 타인의 시선이나 사회적 비용(비판 등)을 감수할 만큼 그 개인이 충분히 강력하거나 지위가 높다는 신호로 해석되기 때문입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '그러한 행동의 사회적 비용을 감수할 만큼 충분히 강력하다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 타격 없이 불리한 조건에서도 관대하고 참을성 있는
② 그러한 행동의 사회적 비용을 감수할 만큼 충분히 강력한
③ 너무 영향력이 커서 부정적인 메시지를 신호로 보낼 수 있는
④ 연구자들이 의도한 만큼 흔들기에는 너무 끈질긴
⑤ 의식하지 않고 자신만의 스타일을 추구하는 자유주의자

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves if _________________________. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① the published paper is distributed to the targeted audience
② scientific communication skills are not developed and ignored
③ the science papers are read and understood by common people
④ non-scientists don't pay attention to, nor do they comprehend the scientific theories
⑤ scientists never carry out further study to understand the potential scholarly works
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학적 의사소통이 양방향 과정임을 강조하고 있습니다. 소리가 들려야 비로소 소리인 것처럼, 과학 논문도 독자에게 전달되고 '이해'되어야 비로소 가치가 있다는 논지입니다. 따라서 출판된 논문이 독자(비과학자 포함)에게 이해되지 않는다면 그것은 의미 없는 압력파(소음)에 불과하다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 선택지 4번은 독자가 과학 이론에 주의를 기울이지 않거나 이해하지 못하는 상황을 설명하므로 문맥상 가장 적절합니다. (다만 원문의 맥락상 '독자'가 반드시 비과학자일 필요는 없으나, 주어진 선택지 중에서는 이해의 부재를 언급하는 4번이 논리적으로 가장 가깝습니다.)
options_translation: ① 출판된 논문이 목표 관객에게 배포된다면
② 과학적 의사소통 기술이 개발되지 않고 무시된다면
③ 과학 논문이 일반 사람들에 의해 읽히고 이해된다면
④ 비과학자들이 과학 이론에 주의를 기울이지도, 이해하지도 못한다면
⑤ 과학자들이 잠재적인 학술 저작물을 이해하기 위해 추가 연구를 수행하지 않는다면

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. (A) Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. (B) Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. (C) This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. (D) In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. (E) In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '하지만 그러한 거래(일회성 거래)는 점점 드물어지고 있는데, 그 이유는 우리가 같은 사람들과 반복적으로 상호작용하기 때문'이라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 앞 문장 (C)에서 언급된 '일회성 협상(one-off negotiation)'에 대한 반박 혹은 상황 변화를 설명하는 내용이므로, (C)의 뒤이자 '이러한 관점에서 볼 때(In view of this)'로 시작하는 결론 문장 앞인 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. (A) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. (B) As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. (C) Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. (D) A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. (E) Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.insertion_sentence: Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그럼에도 불구하고, 자전거 타기에 가장 좋은 도시들조차 여전히 택시, 구급차, 배달 트럭 등을 위한 자동차 차선이 필요하다'는 내용입니다. (B)까지는 도시에서 차선을 없애고 자전거 도로를 늘리는 긍정적인 측면을 설명하고 있고, (C) 이후부터는 '배달 차량(Delivery vehicles)'의 필요성과 효율성에 대해 구체적으로 설명하기 시작합니다. 따라서 자동차 차선의 지속적인 필요성과 그 예시로 배달 차량을 도입하는 전환점인 (C) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries.
ordered_passages: (A) They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.

(B) Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD.
(C) For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees.
questions.explanation: 고래의 탄소 저장 능력을 설명하는 제시문 뒤에, 나무와 비교하여 고래의 효율성을 강조하는 (C)가 오고, 고래가 생태계 엔지니어로서 탄소를 격리하는 추가적인 방식과 경제적 가치를 언급하는 (B)가 이어집니다. 마지막으로 이러한 가치를 바탕으로 기후 변화 해결책으로서 고래 복원 프로그램을 촉구하는 (A)가 오는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.summary_sentence: While the (A)__________ in the labour market and the quality of life may enhance productivity, it may also incur communication costs and possible discrimination if seen as a(n) (B)__________ of national identity.
questions.explanation: 다양한 문화적 배경을 가진 노동자들의 상호작용은 생산성을 높일 수 있지만(variety), 국가 정체성에 대한 침해(violation)로 인식될 경우 의사소통 비용과 차별을 초래할 수 있다는 내용입니다. 본문의 'variety of backgrounds'와 정체성 훼손에 대한 우려를 종합할 때 (A)에는 variety, (B)에는 violation(또는 distortion과 유사한 부정적 의미)이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다양성 - 침해
② 다양성 - 보존
③ 분리 - 공격
④ 불균형 - 왜곡
⑤ 다원화 - 보호

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us. One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Gobekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up radically remaking the society itself. Things are not so different in our own time.
questions.summary_sentence: Unlike what we think, the relationship between human society and building and development is (A)__________ in that the initial construction had led to the birth of the first (B)__________ society.
questions.explanation: 인간이 건물을 짓지만 동시에 건물이 인간 사회를 형성한다는 양방향적(two-way) 관계를 설명하고 있습니다. 괴베클리 테페의 거석 건조가 수렵 채집인이었던 조상들을 정착(settled)하게 하여 최초의 농경 사회로 변화시켰다는 점을 근거로 합니다.
options_translation: ① 양방향의 - 정착한
② 쌍방의 - 수렵 채집의
③ 무관한 - 농업의
④ 일방적인 - 이주하는
⑤ 상호의존적인 - 방랑하는

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are ─ writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
options: ① The Hidden Costs of Focusing on Ability
② Evaluate Ability Through the Lens of Performance!
③ Ability-Based Evaluation: Finding a Reliable Criterion
④ Surviving Strategies for Thriving in a Skill-based Society
⑤ Seeking One, Knowing Ten: Single Example is a Powerful Tool!
questions.explanation: 이 글은 능력이 자아 가치의 유일한 결정 요인이 될 때 발생하는 문제점을 다루고 있습니다. 성과만이 사람을 평가하는 척도가 되어, 뛰어난 성과가 곧 뛰어난 사람을 의미하게 되는 상황의 위험성을 설명하고 있으므로 '능력에 초점을 맞추는 것의 숨겨진 대가(문제점)'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 능력에 초점을 맞추는 것의 숨겨진 대가
② 성과의 관점을 통해 능력을 평가하라!
③ 능력 기반 평가: 신뢰할 수 있는 기준 찾기
④ 기술 기반 사회에서 번창하기 위한 생존 전략
⑤ 하나를 보고 열을 알기: 단 하나의 예시가 강력한 도구이다!

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along ─ whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS ─ and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show ─ whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire ─ you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans to communicate ─ it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① How New Media is Causing Distress in Society
② How Does New Media Influence Our Perception?
③ The Double-Edged Sword of New Media: Benefits and Pitfalls
④ Generation Z: the First Generation to Grow up with New Media
⑤ Navigating the Challengees and Opportunities of the Digital Age
questions.explanation: 새로운 매체가 등장할 때마다 그것이 새로운 안경을 쓰는 것과 같아서 세상을 다르게 보게 만든다는 내용입니다. 매체의 내용보다 매체 그 자체가 우리의 인식 방식(코드)에 영향을 미친다는 마샬 맥루한의 주장을 담고 있으므로 '새로운 매체는 우리의 인식에 어떻게 영향을 미치는가?'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 새로운 매체가 사회에서 고통을 유발하는 방식
② 새로운 매체는 우리의 인식에 어떻게 영향을 미치는가?
③ 새로운 매체의 양날의 검: 혜택과 위험
④ Z세대: 새로운 매체와 함께 자란 첫 세대
⑤ 디지털 시대의 도전과 기회 탐색하기

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① Clarity isn't needed when the paper is published.
② Papers don't need to engage their audience to be effective.
③ The process of scientific discovery ends with the writing of a paper.
④ Publication alone guarantees the success of scientific research.
⑤ Scientific papers gain value when they are understood by their audience.
questions.explanation: 과학적 의사소통은 쌍방향 과정이며, 논문이 출판되더라도 독자에게 수용되고 이해되지 않으면 무용지물이라는 내용입니다. 과학적 실험은 결과가 이해될 때 비로소 완성된다는 것이 핵심이므로 5번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 논문이 출판될 때 명확성은 필요하지 않다.
② 논문이 효과적이기 위해 독자를 끌어들일 필요는 없다.
③ 과학적 발견의 과정은 논문을 쓰는 것으로 끝난다.
④ 출판 그 자체가 과학 연구의 성공을 보장한다.
⑤ 과학 논문은 독자에 의해 이해될 때 가치를 얻는다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [24년 9월 37번]
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
options: ① Our voice sounds higher in our ears than in the recording.
② We perceive our voice through two different pathways.
③ External sounds travel through the air and reach our ears.
④ Vibrations from our vocal cords reach our inner ears.
⑤ Bone conduction makes our voice sound different to us.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 뼈를 통한 진동(내부 경로)은 낮은 주파수를 강조하여 자신의 목소리가 다른 사람이 듣는 것(녹음된 소리)보다 더 낮고 풍부하게 들리게 한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 녹음된 소리보다 자신의 귀에 목소리가 더 높게 들린다는 ①번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 목소리는 녹음된 것보다 우리 귀에 더 높게 들린다.
② 우리는 두 가지 다른 경로를 통해 우리의 목소리를 인식한다.
③ 외부 소리는 공기를 통해 전달되어 우리의 귀에 도달한다.
④ 성대의 진동은 우리의 내이에 도달한다.
⑤ 골전도는 우리의 목소리가 우리에게 다르게 들리게 만든다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [24년 9월 41-42번]
questions.passage: Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a ⓐ<u>specialised</u> workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment ⓑ<u>which</u> enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education ⓒ<u>has set up</u> a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students ⓓ<u>to focus</u> more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback ⓔ<u>shaping</u> the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'socio-political changes'로 복수 명사입니다. 따라서 단수 동사인 'has set up'이 아니라 복수 동사인 'have set up'으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought ␐<u>to exist</u> because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when ␕<u>triggered</u>, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, ␒<u>narrows</u> our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways ␓<u>which</u> they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not ␔<u>have evolved</u> with us.
questions.explanation: ␓가 포함된 절은 ways림 수숝하는 관계절인데, 둄에 주어(they) + 동사(activate) + 먑적어(our systems)로 이뀨지는 완전한 문장이 왔잼로, 관계대명사 which 대신 관계부사(how림 대신하는 in which 또는 that)가 쓰여야 합니다. the way와 how는 동시에 쓸 수 없으며, that으로 바꿔 쓰거나 생략할 수 읈습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providing students with relevant texts they will be ␐<u>interested</u>. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who ␕<u>were</u> highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and ␒<u>had had</u> significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and ␓<u>discovered</u> ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided ␔<u>reading</u>. On the contrary, they sought out books." The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.
questions.explanation: ␐이 포함된 관계절은 they will be interested in texts에서 texts가 선행사로 나간 구조입니다. interested는 전측사 in가 필요하므로, in을 문장 끝에 봙이거나 (...they will be interested in) 관계대명사 앐에 쓰여야 합니다. 따라서 ␐는 interested in으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말 및 표현의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that ␐<u>matches</u> expectations ─ surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue ─ with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who ␕<u>broke</u> established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having ␒<u>higher</u> status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness ␓<u>increased</u> audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as ␔<u>unfavorable</u> because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 규범에서 벗어난 살짝의 이탈(slight deviations)을 하는 사람에 대해 관찰자들은 그가 사회적 비용을 감수할 처지가 된다고 보아 '긍정적으로(positive/favorable)' 팑단한다는 내용이 되야 합니다. 따라서 ␔ unfavorable(비호감인)림 positive(긍정적인)나 favorable(호의적인)로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말 및 표현의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale ⓐ<u>removes</u> an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by ⓑ<u>fertilizing</u> the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste. This, in turn, ⓒ<u>reduces</u> phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon─leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to ⓓ<u>restore</u> whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, not to ⓔ<u>accelerate</u> climate change.
questions.explanation: 고래가 배설하는 영양분이 풍부한 배설물은 식물성 플랑크톤의 성장을 돕는 비료 역할을 합니다. 따라서 식물성 플랑크톤의 개체수를 감소시키는(reduces) 것이 아니라 증가시키거나 촉진한다는 문맥이 되어야 하므로 'reduces'는 부적절합니다. 해당 문맥에서는 'stimulates'나 'boosts'와 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. ⓐAI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. ⓑTherefore skilled workers in modern workplaces are increasingly relying on AI to simplify routine processes. ⓒFor example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. ⓓAI can enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. ⓔFor example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 AI가 노동 시장에서 불리한 위치에 있는 사람들(장애인, 저숙련 노동자, 비모국어 화자 등)의 접근성과 포용성을 높여준다는 내용입니다. ②번 문장은 숙련된 노동자들이 일상적인 과정을 단순화하기 위해 AI에 의존한다는 내용으로, 사회적 약자의 노동 시장 포용이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. (A) Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. (B) This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. (C) However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. (D) The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. (E) Achieving ordinary fame as a social 'media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.insertion_sentence: The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people.
questions.explanation: (D) 문장에서는 엘리트 유명인의 특징(신비주의, 위계적 거리감)을 설명하고 있습니다. (E) 문장에서는 소셜 미디어 유명인으로서의 '평범한 명성(ordinary fame)'을 얻는 것에 대해 설명하기 시작합니다. 주어진 문장은 평범한 유명인이 다른 평범한 사람들과의 빈번한 상호작용을 통해 관심을 끈다는 내용으로, (D)에서 설명한 엘리트 유명인과 대조를 이루며 (E)의 평범한 명성에 대한 구체적 설명 바로 앞인 (E) 자리에 위치하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 (A), (B)에 들어갈 연결사로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. (A)_____________, "Homologous" traits may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. (B)_____________, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
options: ③ (A) In contrast - (B) As a result
questions.explanation: (A) 앞부분은 서로 다른 기원을 가졌으나 기능이 같은 '유사(analogous)' 형질에 대해 설명하고 있고, 뒷부분은 공통 조상에서 기원했으나 기능은 다를 수 있는 '상동(homologous)' 형질에 대해 설명하고 있으므로 대조를 나타내는 'In contrast'가 적절합니다. (B) 상동 형질의 예시로 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리가 기능은 다르지만 같은 기원을 가졌다는 점을 언급한 후, 그 결과(구조적 공통점)로서 뼈의 개수와 연결 방식 같은 비기능적 특성을 공유한다는 내용이 이어지므로 인과관계를 나타내는 'As a result'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 하지만 - 게다가
② 그러므로 - 마찬가지로
③ 대조적으로 - 그 결과
④ 유사하게 - 더욱이
⑤ 더욱이 - 그럼에도 불구하고

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Capuchins ─ New World Monkeys that live in large social groups ─ will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead ─ grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers ─ the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another _______________________________. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains ─ the cucumbers themselves ─ to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
options: ① can play a role in mitigating inequality
② is an essential tool in decision-making
③ helps to see differences in opinions
④ fosters growth by creating ideas
questions.explanation: 카푸친 원숭이는 똑같은 보상(오이)을 받을 때는 만족하지만, 옆에 있는 원숭이가 더 좋은 보상(포도)을 받는 것을 보게 되면 자신이 받는 보상에 불만을 품고 던져버립니다. 즉, 자신의 절대적인 상황은 변하지 않았더라도 타인(다른 원숭이)과의 비교가 상황을 '불평등하게' 만든다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 불평등을 완화하는 역할을 할 수 있다
② 의사결정에 필수적인 도구이다
③ 의견의 차이를 보는 데 도움을 준다
④ 아이디어를 창출함으로써 성장을 촉진한다
⑤ 상황을 불평등하게 만든다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: if _______________, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
options: ③ you don't read it carefully
④ there are too many facts
⑤ the material is too difficult
questions.explanation: 벼락치기가 효과적이라는 착각은 정보가 단기 기억에 머물러 있기 때문인데, 이 정보는 곧 사라집니다. 장기 기억으로 정보를 넘기기 위해서는 공부한 내용을 테스트하거나 다시 보는 과정이 필요하므로, 만약 '복습하지 않는다면(you don't review it)' 기억이 사라진다는 맥락이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 주의가 산만해진다면
② 당신이 그것을 복습하지 않는다면
③ 당신이 그것을 주의 깊게 읽지 않는다면
④ 너무 많은 사실들이 있다면
⑤ 그 자료가 너무 어렵다면

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
questions.summary_sentence: Connecting with others who have found (A)_________ can help individuals regain their (B)_________ and shift away from (C)_________ thinking.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 무기력함과 우울증에서 벗어나기 위해 이미 문제를 해결한 사람들과 함께하는 것의 중요성을 설명하고 있습니다. 'hanging out with the winners(성공한 사람들과 어울리기)'를 통해 긍정적인 에너지를 전이받고 잠재된 긍정적 사고를 다시 일깨울 수 있다고 언급합니다. 따라서 요약문에서 (A)에는 성공(success), (B)에는 동기부여(motivation) 혹은 의욕, (C)에는 부정적인(negative) 사고방식에서 벗어난다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 성장 - 혼란 - 두려운
② 성공 - 동기부여 - 부정적인
③ 문제 - 자신감 - 무력한
④ 성취 - 열정 - 평화로운
⑤ 이해 - 우울 - 긍정적인

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle.
ordered_passages: (A) Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener.

(B) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them.

(C) A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 교통을 진정시키는 대안으로 차량을 제거하고 자전거와 보행자 전용 도로를 만드는 것을 언급합니다. (B)의 'This'는 이러한 전용 도로 네트워크를 가리키며, 이로 인해 자전거 이용이 늘어나고 더 많은 도로를 전환하게 된다는 내용으로 이어집니다. (A)에서는 자전거 친화적 도시라도 배달 트럭 같은 필수 차량을 위한 차선이 필요함을 언급하며 'Delivery vehicles'를 소개합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 배달 트럭이 개별 차량보다 효율적이며 동네 상점 운영을 도와 주민들이 걷게 함으로써 도시를 더 푸르게 만든다는 구체적인 이유를 설명하는 순서가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by (A)_____________. As children we learn a lot by watching what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such copy is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in (B)_____________ of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런의 발견을 통해 인간의 학습 방식, 특히 '관찰(observation)'을 통한 학습에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 영유아가 부모의 행동이나 소리를 보고 듣고 따라하는 '모방(imitation)' 과정을 통해 사회적 기술과 문화를 습득한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 관찰을 의미하는 observation이, (B)에는 모방을 의미하는 imitation이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a (A)_____________ hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more (B)_____________ in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 조직 내 서로 다른 부서들이 가지는 편향된 관점과 조직 구조에 따른 갈등 관리를 설명하는 글입니다. 많은 규칙과 관리 계층이 존재하는 기계적 구조는 '수직적(vertical)' 위계를 가지며, 의사결정이 분산되고 평면적인 성격을 띠는 유기적 구조는 '수평적(horizontal)'인 특징을 보입니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 요약문을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
questions.summary_sentence: Firestein highlights the importance of concepts in human life, but also warns of the risk of chasing on a basis on wrong concepts. With the example of luminiferous ether, a hypothetical substance that turned out to be fictitious. Firestein says scientists often guide their hypotheses based on _______________ ___________________________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 포함할 것 (변형 가능)
분사구문을 활용하여 8~10 단어로 작성할 것
questions.answer: flawed concepts, resulting in fruitless pursuits for non-existent essences
questions.explanation: 제시된 글은 잘못된 개념(wrong concepts)을 사용하여 본질(essence)을 찾는 과학자들의 헛된 노력을 다루고 있습니다. 조건에 맞추어 '결함이 있는 개념'인 'flawed concepts'를 쓰고, 결과의 의미를 담은 분사구문 'resulting in' 뒤에 '존재하지 않는 본질에 대한 성과 없는 추구'를 연결하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 밑줄 친 make our green clouds gray가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that the impact on the environment will be less negative. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the cost of the Internet and electricity for the environment is neglected. A recent Wired report declared that most data centers' energy source is fossil fuels. When we store bigger data on clouds, increased carbon emissions <u>make our green clouds gray</u> . The carbon footprint of an email is smaller than mail sent via a post office, but still, it causes four grams of CO₂, and it can be as much as 50 grams if the attachment is big.
options: ① boost the efficiency of cloud services
② contribute to the sustainability of digital storage
③ increase the speed and capacity of data storage
④ undermine the environmental benefits of cloud storage
⑤ eliminate the environmental impact of cloud technology
questions.explanation: 필자는 디지털 비즈니스 활동이 종이 사용을 줄여 환경에 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 것으로 예상되지만, 실제로는 데이터 센터 운영에 필요한 화석 연료 사용과 그로 인한 탄소 배출이 환경에 위협이 된다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '우리의 초록색(친환경적) 클라우드를 회색(오염된 상태)으로 만든다'는 표현은 클라우드 저장소가 가진 환경적 이점을 훼손한다는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 클라우드 서비스의 효율성을 높이다
② 디지털 저장의 지속 가능성에 기여하다
③ 데이터 저장의 속도와 용량을 늘리다
④ 클라우드 저장소의 환경적 이점을 훼손하다
⑤ 클라우드 기술의 환경적 영향을 제거하다

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
options: ① 디지털 기기의 과도한 사용을 지양해야 한다.
② 디지털 윤리의 중요성을 알고 실천할 필요가 있다.
③ 노동시장의 디지털화에 맞춰 장애인 고용을 늘려야 한다.
④ 사회적 약자를 위한 디지털 정보활용능력 교육이 필요하다.
⑤ 디지털 프로젝트는 장애가 있는 사람들의 요구를 고려해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에서 필자는 디지털 프로젝트를 수행할 때 가능한 한 가장 넓은 층의 관객(사용자)을 염두에 두어야 하며, 최종 결과물이 장애가 있는 사람들의 요구도 충족할 수 있도록 보장해야 한다고 주장하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Simply giving employees a sense of agency - a feeling that they are in control, that they have genuine decision-making authority - can radically increase how much energy and focus they bring to their jobs. One 2010 study at a manufacturing plant in Ohio, for instance, carefully examined assembly-line workers who were empowered to make small decisions about their schedules and work environment. They designed their own uniforms and had authority over shifts while all the manufacturing processes and pay scales stayed the same. Within two months, productivity at the plant increased by 20 percent, with workers taking shorter breaks and making fewer mistakes. Giving employees a sense of control improved how much self-discipline they brought to their jobs.
options: ① 임금이 높을수록 직원의 삶의 만족도는 높아진다.
② 직원의 복지 향상을 위한 다양한 제도 마련이 필요하다.
③ 직원의 의사 결정권은 직업의 생산성 향상에 영향을 끼친다.
④ 기업과 직원의 협력으로 기업 내 문제의 해결책을 모색할 수 있다.
⑤ 새로운 사업 모델을 위해 기업에 대한 정부의 지원이 필요하다.
questions.explanation: 직원들에게 스스로 통제하고 의사 결정을 할 수 있는 권한(sense of agency)을 부여하는 것이 그들의 업무 에너지와 집중력을 높이고, 결과적으로 생산성 향상으로 이어진다는 내용입니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The term minimalism gives a negative impression to some people who think that it is all about sacrificing valuable possessions. This insecurity naturally stems from their attachment to their possessions. It is difficult to distance oneself from something that has been around for quite some time. Being an emotional animal, human beings give meaning to the things around them. So, the question arising here is that if minimalism will hurt one's emotions, why become a minimalist? The answer is very simple; the assumption of the question is fundamentally wrong. Minimalism does not hurt emotions. You might feel a bit sad while getting rid of a useless item but sooner than later, this feeling will be overcome by the joy of clarity. Minimalists never argue that you should leave every convenience of the modern era. They are of the view that you only need to eliminate stuff that is unused or not going to be used in the near future.
options: ① Minimalism: A Path to Discomfort and Loss
② Why Minimalism Requires Emotional Sacrifice
③ Embracing Minimalism: Letting Go of Convenience
④ The Downsides of Minimalism: Sacrificing Comfort
⑤ Understanding Minimalism: Letting Go Without Losing Joy
questions.explanation: 미니멀리즘이 소중한 소유물을 희생하거나 감정을 상하게 한다는 오해를 바로잡고, 사용하지 않는 물건을 정리함으로써 얻는 명료함의 즐거움을 강조하는 글입니다. 따라서 기쁨을 잃지 않고 보내주는 미니멀리즘에 대한 이해가 제목으로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 미니멀리즘: 불편함과 상실로 가는 길
② 미니멀리즘이 감정적 희생을 필요로 하는 이유
③ 미니멀리즘 수용하기: 편리함을 포기하기
④ 미니멀리즘의 단점: 안락함을 희생하기
⑤ 미니멀리즘 이해하기: 기쁨을 잃지 않고 보내주기

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
options: ① Green: the Permanent Trait of Leaves
② Can Objects Have Color Without Light?
③ Dismiss Color as a Product of Perception
④ Perceive the World as It Is, Without Interpretation
⑤ Color: Where the Physical World Meets the Mind
questions.explanation: 이 글은 색이 사물의 객관적인 속성이라는 견해와 관찰자의 마음속에만 존재하는 주관적인 것이라는 두 가지 견해를 모두 소개하며, 결국 색이란 물리적 세계의 빛이 뇌에 의해 해석될 때 생겨나는, 즉 객관과 주관이 만나는 지점임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '물리적 세계와 정신이 만나는 곳으로서의 색'을 언급한 5번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 초록색: 나뭇잎의 영구적인 특성
② 빛 없이 물체가 색을 가질 수 있는가?
③ 색을 지각의 산물로 일축하기
④ 해석 없이 세상을 있는 그대로 지각하라
⑤ 색: 물리적 세계와 정신이 만나는 곳

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Plato's realism includes all aspects of experience but is most easily explained by considering the nature of mathematical and geometrical objects such as circles. He asked the question, what is a circle? You might indicate a particular example carved into stone or drawn in the sand. However, Plato would point out that, if you looked closely enough, you would see that neither it, nor indeed any physical circle, was perfect. They all possessed flaws, and all were subject to change and decayed with time. So how can we talk about perfect circles if we cannot actually see or touch them? Plato's extraordinary answer was that the world we see is a poor reflection of a deeper unseen reality of Forms, or universals, where perfect cats chase perfect mice in perfect circles around perfect rocks. Plato believed that the Forms or universals are the true reality that exists in an invisible but perfect world beyond our senses.
options: ① Plato's explanation of the ethical behavior of individuals in a just society
② Plato's belief in a higher and unchanging reality of perfect forms beyond the physical world
③ the influence of ancient Greek philosophers on the development of Western scientific thought
④ the relationship between Socratic dialogues and ethical inquiries in Greek moral philosophy
⑤ the development of Plato's political philosophy focusing on the ideal state rather than metaphysical forms
questions.explanation: 이 글은 플라톤의 실재론에 대해 설명하며, 우리가 눈으로 보는 현실 세계의 사물들은 불완전하고 변하지만, 감각 너머의 보이지 않는 세계에는 완벽하고 변하지 않는 '이데아(Forms)'가 진정한 실재로 존재한다는 플라톤의 믿음을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 2번 '물리적 세계 너머의 완벽한 형상이라는 더 높고 불변하는 실재에 대한 플라톤의 믿음'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 정의로운 사회에서 개인의 윤리적 행동에 대한 플라톤의 설명
② 물리적 세계 너머의 완벽한 형상이라는 더 높고 불변하는 실재에 대한 플라톤의 믿음
③ 서구 과학 사상의 발전에 미친 고대 그리스 철학자들의 영향
④ 그리스 도덕 철학에서 소크라테스 대화와 윤리적 탐구 사이의 관계
⑤ 형이상학적 형상보다는 이상 국가에 초점을 맞춘 플라톤의 정치 철학 발전

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [23년 11월 23번]
questions.passage: Nearly everything has to go through your mouth, so ⓐ<u>that</u> it gets to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and prevent it from harm - with adequate space for air ⓑ<u>to travel</u> to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. From the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and a reflection of ⓒ<u>what</u> is happening in other parts of the body. Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease ⓓ<u>which</u> affects the entire body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, which ⓔ<u>pose</u> serious health risks.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장의 선행사는 앞 문장 전체 혹은 앞 문장의 일부 내용입니다. 관계대명사의 계속적 용법에서 앞 문장 전체나 구를 선행사로 받을 때, 동사는 단수 취급해야 하므로 pose를 poses로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [24년 6월 32번]
questions.passage: There's a lot of scientific evidence ⓐ<u>demonstrating</u> that focused attention leads to the reshaping of the brain. In animals rewarded for noticing sound (to hunt or to avoid ⓑ<u>being hunted</u> for example), we find much larger auditory centers in the brain. In animals rewarded for sharp eyesight, the visual areas are larger. Brain scans of violinists provide more evidence, ⓒ<u>showing</u> dramatic growth and expansion in regions of the cortex that represent the left hand, which has to finger the strings precisely, often at very high speed. Other studies have shown that the hippocampus, which is vital for spatial memory, ⓓ<u>is</u> enlarged in taxi drivers. The point is that the physical architecture of the brain changes depending on what we focus on and the activities we ⓔ<u>repeatedly</u> engage in.
questions.explanation: 원문상 어색한 부분은 없으나, 문제 정답표에 ③번으로 기재되어 있습니다. 그러나 문맥과 문법상 showing은 분사구문으로 적절하며, ⓓ is도 hippocampus라는 단수 주어에 일치하므로 적절합니다. 본 지문의 원문(모의고사 32번)에서는 어법상 틀린 곳이 없습니다. (출제 오류 가능성 혹은 원문 변형 확인 필요. 본 텍스트 기준으로는 ③번의 showing이 동사 자리인지 확인해야 하나, 앞의 scans provide evidence로 문장이 완벽하여 분사가 맞습니다.)

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [23년 11월 38번]
questions.passage: The decline in the diversity of our food is an entirely human-made process. The biggest ⓐ<u>reduction</u> of crop diversity came in the decades that followed the Second World War. In an attempt to save millions from extreme hunger, crop scientists found ways to produce grains such as rice and wheat on a ⓑ<u>modest</u> scale. And thousands of traditional varieties were ⓒ<u>substituted</u> by a small number of new super-productive ones. The strategy worked spectacularly well, at least to begin with. Because of it, grain production tripled, and between 1970 and 2020 the human population more than doubled. Leaving the contribution of that strategy to one side, the danger of creating more ⓓ<u>homogeneous</u> crops is that they are more at risk when it comes to disasters. Specifically, a global food system that depends on just a ⓔ<u>narrow</u> selection of plants has a greater chance of not being able to survive diseases, pests and climate extremes.
questions.explanation: 수백만 명을 기아로부터 구하기 위해 쌀과 밀 같은 곡물을 대규모로 생산하는 방법을 찾아낸 것이므로, '보통의, 겸손한'이라는 의미의 modest 대신 '거대한, 방대한' 의미의 massive나 large와 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [23년 11월 29번]
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed ⓐ<u>stricter</u> guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation - transferring organs to others - is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ⓑ<u>relieve</u> public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. However, the argument raises the question of whether these regulations actually ⓒ<u>foster</u> trust. They may instead reinforce suspicions by implying that brain death is a ⓓ<u>more</u> precise diagnosis than it really is. For the sake of consistency and public trust, the criteria for determining brain death in all cases - whether for organ donation or immediate burial - should be ⓔ<u>identical</u>.
questions.explanation: 엄격한 규정은 오히려 뇌사 판정이 실제보다 덜 정확하다는 것을 암시함으로써 의구심을 강화할 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 more를 less로 바꾸어 '실제보다 덜 정확한 진단'이라는 의미가 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 6월 22번]
questions.passage: When it comes to helping out, you don't have to do much. All you have to do is come around and show that you care. If you notice someone who is lonely, you could go and sit with them. If you work with someone who eats lunch all by themselves, and you go and sit down with them, they will begin to be more social after a while, and they will owe it all to you. A person's happiness comes from ___________. There are too many people out in the world who feel like everyone has forgotten them or ignored them. Even if you say hi to someone passing by, they will begin to feel better about themselves, like someone cares.
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 누군가에게 관심을 보이고 함께 있어 주는 것만으로도 그 사람을 행복하게 만들 수 있다는 것입니다. 외로운 사람 곁에 앉아주거나 인사하는 행위는 모두 '관심(attention)'을 주는 행위이므로 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 관심
② 존엄성
③ 정직
④ 공정함
⑤ 인내

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Your conducts typically mirror _______________________. What you do is an indication of the type of person you believe that you are - either consciously or nonconsciously. Research has shown that once a person believes in a particular aspect of their identity, they are more likely to act according to that belief. For example, people who identified as "being a voter" were more likely to vote than those who simply claimed "voting" was an action they wanted to perform. Similarly, the person who accepts exercise as the part of their identity doesn't have to convince themselves to train. Doing the right thing is easy. After all, when your behavior and your identity perfectly match, you are no longer pursuing behavior change. You are simply acting like the type of person you already believe yourself to be.
options: ④ what others expect of you
⑤ influence from peers or family
questions.explanation: 이 글은 행동이 자신의 정체성, 즉 스스로를 어떤 사람이라고 믿느냐를 반영한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 투표자로서의 정체성을 가진 사람이 더 투표를 잘 하고, 운동을 정체성의 일부로 받아들인 사람이 더 쉽게 운동을 하는 예시를 통해, 행동과 정체성이 일치할 때 행동 변화를 추구하는 것이 아니라 단순히 믿는 대로 행동하게 됨을 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '자신을 어떻게 보느냐'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 당신 자신을 어떻게 보는지
② 당신의 과거 경험들
③ 당신의 내재된 능력들
④ 타인이 당신에게 기대하는 것
⑤ 또래나 가족으로부터의 영향

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily bored. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to reduce their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons __________________________________________________. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor's hypothetical puma threat) stand out more. It's the neural equivalent of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
options: ① ignore stimuli that change quickly
② stabilize their responses to things that change
③ increase their sensitivity to things that change
④ prioritize monotonous stimuli over changing ones
⑤ maintain the same response regardless of changes
questions.explanation: 인간이 쉽게 지루함을 느끼는 이유는 신경 세포가 반복되는 자극에는 반응을 줄이도록 설계되어 있기 때문입니다. 이는 동시에 변하는 것(새로운 자극)에 대한 민감도를 높여 생존에 유리하게 작용합니다. 나무 자체보다 나무 속에서 움직이는 푸마에 주의를 기울이는 것이 생존 가치가 높았기 때문이라는 예시를 통해, 신경 세포가 변화하는 것에 대한 감수성을 높인다는 것을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 빠르게 변하는 자극을 무시한다
② 변하는 것들에 대한 반응을 안정시킨다
③ 변하는 것들에 대한 민감도를 증가시킨다
④ 단조로운 자극을 변하는 것보다 우선시한다
⑤ 변화에 관계없이 동일한 반응을 유지한다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Problems often occur when a non-native species is ____________________________________________. Britain's red and grey squirrels provide a clear example. When the grey arrived from America in the 1870s, both squirrel species competed for the same food and habitat, which put the native red squirrel populations under pressure. The grey had the edge because it can adapt its diet; it is able, for instance, to eat green acorns, while the red can only digest mature acorns. Within the same area of forest, grey squirrels can destroy the food supply before red squirrels even have a bite. Greys can also live more densely and in varied habitats, so have survived more easily when woodland has been destroyed. As a result, the red squirrel has come close to extinction in England.
options: ① seriously affected by climate change
② intentionally bred for conservation purposes
③ temporarily removed from its natural habitat

questions.explanation: 영국에 미국산 회색다람쥐가 유입되면서 토착종인 붉은다람쥐가 멸종 위기에 처한 사례를 통해 외래종이 자연 환경에 유입될 때 발생하는 문제점을 설명하고 있습니다. 회색다람쥐의 적응력이 더 뛰어나 먹이 경쟁에서 우위를 점했다는 내용이 이어지므로, '예상치 못하게 자연 환경에 도입될 때'가 가장 적절합니다.
