questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Between 1940 and 2000, Cuba ruled the world baseball scene. They won 25 of the first 28 World Cups and 3 of 5 Olympic Games. The Cubans were known for wearing uniforms covered in red from head to toe, a strong contrast to the more conservative North American style featuring grey or white pants.
ordered_passages: (A) A few years ago, Cuba altered that uniform style, modernizing it and perhaps conforming to other countries' style; interestingly, the national team has declined since that time.
(B) Not only were their athletic talents superior, the Cubans appeared even stronger from just the colour of their uniforms. A game would not even start and the opposing team would already be scared.

(C) The country that ruled international baseball for decades has not been on top since that uniform change. Traditions are important for a team; while a team brand or image can adjust to keep up with present times, if it abandons or neglects its roots, negative effects can surface.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 쿠바 야구팀이 1940년에서 2000년 사이 세계 야구계를 지배했으며, 머리부터 발끝까지 붉은색 유니폼을 입었다는 특징을 언급합니다. (B)에서는 그들의 뛰어난 실력뿐만 아니라 유니폼 색깔 자체가 주는 위압감 때문에 상대 팀이 경기 시작 전부터 겁을 먹었음을 설명하며 연결됩니다. (A)에서는 몇 년 전 쿠바가 이 전통적인 유니폼 스타일을 현대적으로 변경했다는 사실과 그 이후 성적이 하락했음을 언급하고, (C)에서 그 유니폼 변화 이후 다시 정상에 서지 못했음을 재차 강조하며 전통과 뿌리의 중요성에 대한 교훈으로 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: To find the hidden potential in teams, instead of brainstorming, we're better off shifting to a process called brainwriting. The initial steps are solo. You start by asking everyone to generate ideas separately. (A) Next, you pool them and share them anonymously among the group. (B) To preserve independent judgment, each member evaluates them on their own. (C) By developing and assessing ideas individually before choosing and elaborating them, teams can surface and advance possibilities that might not get attention otherwise. (D) This brainwriting process makes sure that all ideas are brought to the table and all voices are brought into the conversation. (E) It is especially effective in groups that struggle to achieve collective intelligence.
questions.insertion_sentence: Only then does the team come together to select and refine the most promising options.
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부는 브레인라이팅 과정의 '개별적' 단계를 설명하고 있습니다. (C) 앞부분까지는 아이디어를 각자 내고(A), 각자 평가하는(B) 독립적 과정이 기술됩니다. 주어진 문장의 'Only then(그러고 나서야 비로소)'은 개별적 평가가 끝난 시점을 의미하며, 팀이 '함께 모여(come together)' 옵션을 선택하고 다듬는 단계로 넘어가는 전환점입니다. (C) 뒤의 문장은 이러한 '개별적 개발 및 평가 후 선택'이라는 전체 과정을 요약하며 브레인라이팅의 장점을 설명하므로 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don't win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It's the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
questions.summary_sentence: The path to mastery is not to take a(n) (A)_____________ way. You need a winning mindset and a prepared posture to face (B)_____________.
questions.explanation: 본문은 진정한 숙련(mastery)이나 힘(strength)은 쉬운 길(easy route)이나 저항이 가장 적은 길(path of least resistance)을 택하는 것이 아니라, 고난(hardship)과 투쟁(struggle)을 마주함으로써 얻어진다고 설명합니다. 따라서 요약문의 (A)에는 '편안한(comfortable)' 또는 '쉬운(easy)' 방식이, (B)에는 '역경(adversity)' 또는 '고난(hardship)'이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다. 보기 ④번의 comfortable과 adversity가 이 흐름에 가장 잘 부합합니다. (5번의 경우 (A)의 sophisticated(정교한)가 문맥상 어울리지 않습니다.)
options_translation: ① 쉬운 / 편의
② 친숙한 / 행복
③ 불완전한 / 문제
④ 편안한 / 역경
⑤ 정교한 / 고난

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Participants in a study were asked to answer questions like "Why does the moon have phases?" Half the participants were told to search for the answers on the internet, while the other half weren't allowed to do so. Then, in the second part of the study, all of the participants were presented with a new set of questions, such as "Why does Swiss cheese have holes?" These questions were unrelated to the ones asked during the first part of the study, so participants who used the internet had absolutely no advantage over those who hadn't. You would think that both sets of participants would be equally sure or unsure about how well they could answer the new questions. But those who used the internet in the first part of the study rated themselves as more knowledgeable than those who hadn't, even about questions they hadn't searched online for. The study suggests that having access to unrelated information was enough to pump up their intellectual confidence.
questions.summary_sentence: The study above focuses on how access to information online can (A)__________ people's confidence in their own knowledge, even when that knowledge isn't directly (B)__________ to the information they accessed.
questions.explanation: 해당 연구는 인터넷 검색을 통해 정보에 접근하는 것만으로도 사람들의 지적 자신감이 부풀려질 수 있음을 보여줍니다. 실험 참가자들은 실제로 검색하지 않은 별개의 지식에 대해서도 자신이 더 많이 알고 있다고 평가했습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 자신감을 '부풀리다(inflate)'가 적절하고, (B)에는 그 지식이 검색한 정보와 직접적으로 '상응하는(corresponding)' 것이 아님에도 불구하고 그러한 현상이 나타난다고 해야 하므로 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 부풀리다 ... 상응하는
② 억제하다 ... 관련된
③ 부풀리다 ... 관련 없는
④ 억제하다 ... 소속된
⑤ 높이다 ... 부정확한

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. They do well enough in school to keep advancing. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ends with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now lack a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when the journey really begins. When school is finished, __________________________________. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career are likely to stop progressing as a result.
subjective_conditions: • up, development를 사용할 것 (형태 변형 불가)
• 6단어의 완전한 문장으로 쓸 것
• 본문에 있는 단어를 사용할 것 (형태 변형 가능)
questions.answer: their development is up to them
questions.explanation: 이 글은 학교 교육이 끝난 이후의 자기 성장은 스스로의 책임이라는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 빈칸에는 '성장은 그들 자신에게 달려 있다'는 의미가 들어가야 합니다. 주어진 조건인 'up', 'development'를 포함하여 6단어로 구성하면 'their development is up to them' 또는 'your development is up to you'가 적절합니다. 본문에 'they'와 'their'가 주어로 사용되고 있으므로 'their development is up to them'이 문맥상 더 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 주제를 조건에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Despite the remarkable progress in deep-learning based facial recognition approaches in recent years, in terms of identification performance, they still have limitations. These limitations relate to the database used in the learning stage. If the selected database does not contain enough instances, the result may be systematically affected. For example, the performance of a facial biometric system may decrease if the person to be identified was enrolled over 10 years ago. The factor to consider is that this person may experience changes in the texture of the face, particularly with the appearance of wrinkles and sagging skin. These changes may be highlighted by weight gain or loss. To counteract this problem, researchers have developed models for face aging or digital de-aging. It is used to compensate for the differences in facial characteristics, which appear over a given time period.
subjective_conditions: • and, developed, to를 사용할 것 (형태 변형 불가)
• 12단어 이내의 명사형으로 쓸 것
• 본문에 있는 단어를 사용할 것 (형태 변형 불가)
questions.answer: limitations of facial recognition approaches and models developed to counteract the problem
questions.explanation: 지문은 딥러닝 기반 안면 인식 기술의 한계점(데이터베이스 부족, 노화로 인한 변화 등)과 이를 해결하기 위해 개발된 모델들에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 '안면 인식 접근법의 한계와 그 문제를 해결하기 위해 개발된 모델들'이 됩니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: The adolescent brain is not fully developed until its early twenties. This means the way the adolescents' decision-making circuits integrate and process information may put them at a disadvantage. One of their brain regions that matures later is the prefrontal cortex, which is the control center, tasked with thinking ahead and evaluating consequences. It is the area of the brain responsible for preventing you from sending off an initial angry text and modifying it with kinder words. On the other hand, the limbic system matures earlier, playing a central role in processing emotional responses. Because of its earlier development, it is more likely to influence decision-making. Decision-making in the adolescent brain is led by emotional factors more than the perception of consequences. Due to these differences, there is an imbalance between feeling-based decision-making ruled by the more mature limbic system and logical-based decision-making by the not-yet-mature prefrontal cortex. This may explain why some teens are more likely to make bad decisions.
questions.summary_sentence: The adolescent brain is driven more by (A)_________, which can (B)____________________________________.
subjective_conditions: • (A)는 than 포함 3단어, (B)는 lead 포함 4단어로 쓸 것
• 본문에 있는 단어를 사용할 것 (형태 변형 가능)
questions.answer: (A) emotions than logic(B) lead to bad decisions
questions.explanation: 청소년의 뇌는 전두엽보다 감정을 담당하는 변연계가 먼저 발달하여 감정적인 요인에 의해 의사결정이 이루어지기 쉽고, 이로 인해 잘못된 결정을 내릴 가능성이 높다는 내용입니다. (A)에는 '논리보다 감정'이라는 의미인 'emotions than logic'이 적절하며, (B)에는 '나쁜 결정으로 이어지다'라는 의미인 'lead to bad decisions'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. Among migratory bird species, those that are born knowing how, when, and where to migrate ─ those that are migrating entirely with instructions they were born with ─ sometimes have very inefficient migration routes. These birds, born knowing how to migrate, don't adapt easily. So when lakes dry up, forest becomes farmland, or climate change pushes breeding grounds farther north, those birds that are born knowing how to migrate keep flying by the old rules and maps. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Childhood facilitates the passing on of cultural information, and culture can evolve faster than genes. Childhood gives flexibility in a changing world.
subjective_conditions: adapt, help, childhood를 사용할 것 (형태 변형 가능)
8단어 이내의 완전한 문장으로 쓸 것
본문에 있는 단어를 사용할 것 (형태 변형 가능)
questions.answer: Childhood helps animals adapt to the changing environment.
questions.explanation: 이 지문은 동물의 유년기(childhood)가 변화하는 환경에 적응하는 데 필요한 유연성(flexibility)과 학습 기회를 제공한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 특히 부모와 함께 이동하며 배우는 유년기가 긴 새들이 더 효율적인 경로를 갖는다는 예시를 통해, 유년기가 문화적 정보의 전달을 돕고 변화하는 세상에서 적응력을 높여준다는 점을 강조합니다. 따라서 조건에 맞춰 '유년기는 동물이 변화하는 환경에 적응하도록 돕는다'는 의미의 문장을 완성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along-whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS-and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show-whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire-you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along-a new way for humans to communicate-it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① 새로운 매체가 등장할 때마다 매체에 따라 세상을 다르게 인식하게 된다.
② 매체가 정보를 전달하는 방식보다는 정보 자체를 중요하게 생각한다.
③ 매가 새로운 정보를 전달해도 전통적인 방식으로 해석하게 된다.
④ TV와 같은 매체가 사회적인 상호작용에 빠르게 영향을 미친다.
⑤ 새로운 매체의 등장으로 세상을 명확하게 이해하게 된다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 새로운 매체(인쇄된 책, TV, SNS 등)가 등장할 때마다 그것이 마치 새로운 색깔과 렌즈를 가진 고글을 쓰는 것과 같아서 세상을 다르게 보게 만든다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 마샬 맥루한의 말을 인용하여 매체가 전달하는 내용보다 정보를 전달하는 방식(매체 그 자체)이 우리가 세상을 인식하는 방식에 더 큰 영향을 미친다고 설명하고 있으므로, 요지는 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a dropout, or worse.
options: ① Disadvantages of Gifted Education Programs
② The Difference Between Praise and Bragging
③ A Gifted Child's Remarkable Bragging Behavior
④ Important Factors in Forming Relationships among Gifted Children
⑤ The Drawbacks of Excessive Parental Bragging about Gifted Children
questions.explanation: 부모가 영재 자녀의 뛰어난 행동이나 성취에 대해 지나치게 자랑하는 것은 자녀에게 스트레스와 압박감을 주며, 자녀가 부응하기 힘든 기대를 만들고 자아감 형성에 부정적인 영향을 줄 수 있으므로 이를 제한해야 한다는 내용의 글이다. 따라서 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은 '영재 자녀에 대한 부모의 과도한 자랑의 결점(단점)'인 5번이다.
options_translation: ① 영재 교육 프로그램의 단점
② 칭찬과 자랑의 차이
③ 영재 아동의 놀라운 자랑 행동
④ 영재 아동 간의 관계 형성에 중요한 요인들
⑤ 영재 자녀에 대한 부모의 과도한 자랑의 결점들

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem ⓐ<u>which</u> we struggle with. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we ⓑ<u>have given</u> a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and ⓒ<u>energized</u> positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this ⓓ<u>is called</u> "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and ⓔ<u>relighting</u> of one's own latent positive thought forms.*latent: 잠재적인
questions.explanation: ⓒ는 Those who are in a higher vibration의 동사인 are에 걸리는 보어 형용사 free of ~와 병렬 구조를 이루며 positive thought forms를 목적어로 취하는 능동의 의미가 되어야 하므로, 과거분사(수동)인 energized가 아니라 energize 또는 energizing 형태의 서술이나 문맥에 맞는 능동형 동사가 필요하다. 본문 맥락상 are free of ... and energize ... (부정적 에너지로부터 자유롭고 긍정적 사고 형태에 에너지를 준다)로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ 전치사 with의 목적어 역할을 하는 관계대명사로 적절하다.ⓑ 우리가 에너지를 '주어 왔다'는 완료의 의미로 적절하다.ⓓ 수동태로 '~라고 불린다'는 의미이므로 적절하다.ⓔ transfer와 병렬 구조를 이루는 명사형(동명사)으로 '다시 불을 붙임'의 의미로 적절하다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may ⓐcontain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own ⓑ<u>prejudiced</u> perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which ⓒ<u>allows</u> them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create ⓓ<u>hostility</u>. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is ⓔ<u>less</u> integrated and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 조직 내의 각 부서들은 각자의 편향된 관점(prejudiced perspective)을 갖게 되며, 이는 다른 사람들의 시각으로 사물을 보는 것을 방해하는 '터널 시야(tunnel vision)'를 형성하게 합니다. 따라서 ⓒ의 'allows(허용하다)'는 문맥상 다른 사람들의 시각을 보는 것을 '막는다(prevents/blocks)'는 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can __________________________________ in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can also improve the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 AI가 장애인 노동자나 저숙련 노동자들에게 보조 도구 및 실시간 번역, 텍스트 생성 기능 등을 제공함으로써 노동 시장에서의 접근성을 높여준다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 이는 결국 직장에서의 '포용성(comprehensiveness/inclusivity)'을 강화하는 것이므로 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말은 ③번입니다.
options_translation: ① 노동자들을 지배하다
② 숙련된 사람들을 배제하다
③ 포용성을 향상시키다
④ 장애인 노동자들을 대체하다
⑤ 주의와 경고를 끌다

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually __________________________. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
options: ① essentials to making cities eco-friendly
② motivating people to buy various vehicles
③ inefficient alternatives to calming traffic
④ not efficient transporters of goods and food
⑤ good devices for delivering stuffs to homes directly
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부에서 배달 차량이 미움을 받기도 하지만 실제로는 효율적인 운송 수단임을 강조하고 있습니다. 가득 채워진 배달 트럭 한 대가 여러 대의 하이브리드 차량보다 효율적이며, 지역 상점에 물건을 공급함으로써 주민들이 차를 타지 않고 걸어서 장을 볼 수 있게 해준다는 맥락에서 이들은 도시를 친환경적으로 만드는 데 필수적인 요소라는 의미가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 도시를 친환경적으로 만드는 데 필수적인 요소들
② 사람들이 다양한 차량을 구매하도록 동기부여하는 것
③ 교통 진정에 대한 비효율적인 대안들
④ 상품과 식품의 효율적이지 않은 운송 수단
⑤ 물건을 집으로 직접 배달하기 위한 좋은 장치들

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" (A) Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. (B) The explanation is actually fairly simple, and there are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. (C) One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. (D) Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. (E) Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
questions.insertion_sentence: But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path.
questions.explanation: (B)에서 자신의 목소리를 듣는 두 가지 경로가 있다고 언급했고, (C)에서 그중 첫 번째인 외부 소리 경로를 설명했습니다. 주어진 문장은 '두 번째 내부 경로'를 도입하는 내용이므로, 뼈를 통한 진동 전달을 설명하는 (D)의 앞인 ④번 위치에 들어가는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does─this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures.
ordered_passages: (A) Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level.

(B) Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.

(C) Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature.
questions.explanation: 찬물이 따뜻한 물보다 용존 산소를 더 많이 함유한다는 과학적 사실을 언급한 주어진 글 뒤에, (A)에서 'Thus(따라서)'를 통해 지구 온난화로 수온이 오르면 산소량이 줄어들 것이라는 논리적 귀결과 그 위험성을 제시합니다. 이어 (C)에서 실제로 과학자들이 지난 반세기 동안 해양 산소량이 감소했다는 데이터를 분석했음을 보여주고, 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 산소 수치 저하가 해양 생태계(물고기, 게 등)에 미치는 실제적인 악영향을 설명하는 순서가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
questions.summary_sentence: Concepts are essential for human survival, but they can lead to essentialism and (A)______________ searches for non-existent essences, as illustrated by the (B)______________ quest for luminiferous ether in physics.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 생존에 필수적인 개념이 때로는 존재하지 않는 본질을 찾게 만드는 '본질주의'의 함정에 빠뜨릴 수 있다고 설명합니다. 물리학에서의 '에테르' 탐구는 존재하지 않는 대상을 찾으려 했던 잘못된 탐구의 사례로 제시됩니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '잘못된(misguided)', (B)에는 '헛된(vain)'이 들어가는 것이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 혼란스러운 ... 가치 있는
② 잘못된 ... 헛된
③ 가치 있는 ... 소홀한
④ 편향되지 않은 ... 결실 없는
⑤ 불합리한 ... 수용 가능한

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers─he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because _____________________. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
subjective_conditions: 본문에 나와 있는 단어를 사용할 것 (변형 가능)
5~7단어로 작성할 것
questions.answer: he didn't have his own ideas
questions.explanation: 살리에리가 위대한 작곡가가 되지 못한 이유는 당시 다른 모든 이들이 작곡하는 것과 비슷하게 썼기 때문이므로, 본문의 'Effective composers have their own ideas'라는 표현을 활용하여 자신만의 아이디어가 없었다는 내용을 영작합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on (A)______________ branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose (B)______________ in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 생물학에서 구분하는 두 가지 유사성인 '유사 형질(analogous traits)'과 '상동 형질(homologous traits)'을 설명하고 있습니다. (A)의 경우, 유사 형질은 공통의 기능을 가지지만 진화 계통도의 서로 '다른(different)' 가지에서 발생한 것이며, (B)의 경우 새의 날개와 벌의 날개는 진화 과정에서 '독립적으로(independently)' 발생한 것이므로 정답은 ①번입니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 - 독립적으로
② 결과적인 - 의존적으로
③ 많은 - 활기차게
④ 같은 - 독립적으로
⑤ 같은 - 빈번하게

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay ⓐ<u>alive</u>. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does ─ this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will ⓑ<u>increase</u>. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data ⓒ<u>indicating</u> that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been ⓓ<u>falling</u> more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more ⓔ<u>frequent</u> anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 차가운 물이 따뜻한 물보다 더 많은 용존 산소를 보유한다고 언급했습니다. 따라서 지구 온난화로 인해 해수의 온도가 상승하면 용존 산소의 양은 '증가(increase)'하는 것이 아니라 '감소(decrease)'할 것이 자명하므로 ⓑ가 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ가 과학적 맥락에서 의미하는 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, ⓐ<u>It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat.</u>" This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① The challenge of finding hidden truths
② The difficulty of understanding complex theories
③ The frustration of conducting experiments
④ The pursuit of nonexistent concepts
⑤ The need for better tools in science
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 ⓐ는 '어두운 방에서 없는 고양이를 찾는 것이 매우 어렵다'는 의미로, 과학 탐구의 맥락에서는 실제로는 존재하지 않는 본질이나 개념을 증명하려고 헛되이 노력하는 상황을 비유합니다. 지문에서는 존재하지 않았던 '에테르(ether)'를 찾으려 했던 과거 물리학자들의 사례를 통해 이를 설명하고 있으므로, 정답은 '존재하지 않는 개념에 대한 추구'인 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 숨겨진 진실을 찾는 것의 어려움
② 복잡한 이론을 이해하는 것의 어려움
③ 실험을 수행하는 데 따르는 좌절감
④ 존재하지 않는 개념에 대한 추구
⑤ 과학에서 더 나은 도구의 필요성

questions.question: 13. 다음 글을 읽고 추론할 수 있는 내용이 아닌 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
options: ① 엘리트를 유명인은 연기나 노래와 같은 전통적인 재능과 관련이 있다.
② 평범한 유명인은 소셜 미디어상의 상호 작용을 통해 만들어진다.
③ 소셜 미디어 유명인은 주로 많은 구독자와 클릭 수로 유명해진다.
④ 평범한 유명인은 엘리트 유명인과 마찬가지로 신비함과 계층적 거리를 유지하는 특징이 있다.
⑤ 소셜 미디어에서 유명해지는 것은 일종의 게임에서 높은 점수를 얻는 것과 유사하다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 엘리트 유명인은 '신비함(mystery)'과 '계층적 거리(hierarchical distance)'로 특징지어지지만, 평범한 유명인(ordinary celebrity)은 다른 평범한 사람들과의 '정기적이고 빈번한 상호작용'을 통해 관심을 얻는다고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 평범한 유명인이 신비함과 거리를 유지한다는 ④번은 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along ─ whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS ─ and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses, Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show ─ whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire ─ you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans to communicate ─ it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① the effect of television viewing on human character
② the transformation of social relationships due to media shifts
③ how media growth makes the standard of information better
④ how new communication tools change perspectives
⑤ the impact of different media on the way we understand things
questions.explanation: 이 글은 새로운 매체(고글)가 등장할 때마다 우리가 세상을 바라보는 방식이 달라진다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 마셜 맥루한의 말을 인용하여 정보의 내용보다 정보가 전달되는 방식(매체)이 우리의 관점을 형성하고 세상을 새로운 암호에 따라 보게 만든다는 것이 핵심입니다.
options_translation: ① 텔레비전 시청이 인간의 인성에 미치는 영향
② 미디어 변화로 인한 사회적 관계의 변모
③ 미디어 성장이 정보의 수준을 개선하는 방식
④ 새로운 통신 도구가 관점을 바꾸는 방식
⑤ 우리가 사물을 이해하는 방식에 미치는 다양한 미디어의 영향

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.*hierarchy: 위계
options: ① Major Causes of Organizational Conflict and Solutions
② The Impact of Perspective Differences Between Departments
③ The Importance of Organizational Structure Choice in Conflict Management
④ A Comparison of the Efficiency of Mechanistic and Organic Structures
⑤ Analyzing Performance Differences Based on Organizational Structure
questions.explanation: 이 글은 조직 내의 부서들이 각자의 편향된 시각(터널 시야)을 가지게 되어 갈등이 발생할 수 있음을 언급한 뒤, 조직 구조(기계적 혹은 유기적)의 선택이 이러한 갈등 관리에 중대한 영향을 미친다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 갈등 관리에서 조직 구조 선택의 중요성이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 조직 갈등의 주요 원인과 해결책
② 부서 간 관점 차이의 영향
③ 갈등 관리에서 조직 구조 선택의 중요성
④ 기계적 구조와 유기적 구조의 효율성 비교
⑤ 조직 구조에 따른 성과 차이 분석

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흤름삼 밴, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? (A) You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" (B) Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. (C) There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. (D) Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. (E) That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
questions.insertion_sentence: This is why many people are surprised when they hear a recording of themselves.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이것이 많은 사람들이 자신의 목소리 녹음을 들었을 땄 놀라는 이유이다'라는 결론적인 내용입니다. (D) 앞까지는 우리가 자신의 목소리를 듣는 둀 가지 경로(외부 경로와 골전도를 통한 내부 경로)를 설명하고 있습니다. 특히 (D) 이홄의 문장에서 내부 경로를 통해 저주파가 강조되어 목소리가 더 깊고 퐒부하게 들린다고 설명하므로, 이러한 과정을 다 설명한 홄인 (D) 위츘가 가장 적절합니다. 그 홄 (E)에서 'That' 또한 삽입된 문장의 내용을 받아줄 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 퀀용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers ─ he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.summary_sentence: Effective composers are recognized for their (A)_____________ and unique contributions, which, despite initial rejection, are later seen as (B)_____________ and groundbreaking.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 작갑가들이 당대에는 이해받지 못했지만, 그 이유가 그들의 작품이 생소할 정도로 '독창적(original)'이었기 뵄문이라고 말합니다. 반면 살리에리는 독창성이 부족했기 뵄문에 위대한 작곡가가 되지 못했습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 'originality(독창성)', (B)에는 '홁명적인(revolutionary)' 또는 '형식을 바꾸는(transformative)'가 적절하지만, 본문의 groundbraking과 가장 잘 어울리는 접표는 2번입니다.
options_translation: (A) 재능 (B) 변화시키는
(A) 독창성 (B) 협명적인
(A) 홁신 (B) 과평가된

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat."이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "<u>It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat</u>." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① The difficulty of finding a deeper message, when it is blended or hidden like a black cat in a dark room
② The key factors of essentialism using concepts which did not exist
③ The worthlessness of searching for something when their guiding or hypotheses are incorrect
④ Low possibility to locate a black cat in a completely dark room due to its color blending into the darkness
⑤ The importance of high vision to locate objects in low visibility conditions
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 문장은 존재하지 않는 본질을 찾으려 애쓰는 과학적 오류를 비유한 것입니다. 잘못된 개념에 근거하여 가설을 세우고 실험을 진행하는 것은 결국 존재하지 않는 고양이를 찾는 것처럼 가치 없는 일임을 의미하므로 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 어두운 방의 검은 고양이처럼 숨겨져 있거나 섞여 있는 더 깊은 메시지를 찾는 것의 어려움
② 존재하지 않는 개념을 사용하는 본질주의의 핵심 요소
③ 지침이나 가설이 잘못되었을 때 무언가를 찾는 것의 무가치함
④ 어둠 속으로 섞여 들어가는 색상 때문에 완전히 어두운 방에서 검은 고양이를 찾을 낮은 가능성

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
options: ① new designs of emotions to guide our behaviors
② significance of emotional support in a modern life
③ artistic expression and creativity caused by emotions
④ the evolutionary role of emotions in human survival
⑤ emotions as a primary source of entertainment and personal expression
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간의 감정이 생존을 돕기 위해 진화해 온 프로그램과 같다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 두려움, 분노, 긍정적 감정 등이 과거 인류가 환경의 도전에 맞서 살아남는 데 기여했기에 지금까지 존재한다는 내용이므로 ④번 '인간 생존에 있어 감정의 진화론적 역할'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 행동을 안내하는 감정의 새로운 설계
② 현대 생활에서 정서적 지지의 중요성

questions.question: 4. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons (A)____________________________________________. [(거울 뉴런의 발견은) 근본적인 인간의 능력에 대해 우리가 생각하는 방식을 완전히 바꾸어 놓았다.] As children we learn a lot by observing ⓐ<u>what</u> our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out ⓑ<u>theirs</u>. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue ⓒ<u>stick</u> out whenever you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start ⓓ<u>to imitate</u> the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior ⓔ<u>for which</u> we are born. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.*babble 옹알이하다
questions.explanation: ⓔ의 경우 be born 뒤에 수반되는 전치사는 to 보다는 in이나 with 등 문맥에 따라 쓰일 수 있으나, 본문의 원문 및 문법적 관용어구상 'be born with(~을 가지고 태어나다)'의 형태가 적절하며, 무엇보다 해당 문장에서 관계대명사절은 'we are born with the behavior'의 구조를 취해야 하므로 전치사 with가 필요합니다. 하지만 본문의 맥락상 'the behavior we are born with' 혹은 'with which we are born'이 되어야 하는데, 원문([24년 9월 36번]) 확인 시 해당 부분은 'the behavior we are born with'로 쓰여 있습니다. ⑤번의 for which는 문맥상 '태어날 때 부여받은(with) 행동'으로 연결되는 것이 자연스러우며, for는 목적이나 이유를 나타내어 어색합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively ⓐ<u>poorly</u> populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will ⓑ<u>increase</u>. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been ⓒ<u>declining</u> for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the ⓓ<u>corresponding</u> rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more ⓔ<u>frequent</u> anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 수온이 상승함에 따라 해수 속의 용존 산소량이 감소하여 해양 생태계에 위협이 되고 있다는 내용입니다. 물리학적으로 찬물이 따뜻한 물보다 더 많은 산소를 보유하므로, 지구 온난화로 인해 해수 온도가 상승하면 용존 산소량은 줄어들게 됩니다. 따라서 ⓑ의 'increase(증가하다)'는 'decrease(감소하다)'와 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. ⓐAs a result, a department and its members must require "tunnel vision" and have a more general understanding by blocking out everything around them. ⓑMeanwhile, the very structure of organizations can create conflict. ⓒThe choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. ⓓA mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. ⓔOrganic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 조직 내의 서로 다른 부서들이 각자의 편향된 시각을 가짐으로써 발생할 수 있는 문화적 차이와 조직 구조(기계적 vs 유기적)에 따른 갈등 관리에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ⓐ번 문장은 부서원들이 주변을 차단하고 좁은 시야(tunnel vision)를 가져야 한다고 주장하고 있는데, 이는 조직 내 부서들이 필연적으로 갖게 되는 편향된 관점을 설명하는 흐름에서 갑자기 부적절한 당위성을 주장하는 것이므로 흐름에 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
options: ① 상사 형질은 공통된 기능을 가지지만 다른 진화적 배경을 가지고 있어 동일한 기관이 아닌 형질이다.
② 새의 날개와 벌의 날개는 비슷한 비행 기능을 가지고 있으며 공통 진화적 기원을 공유하기 때문에 상사 형질로 간주된다.
③ 공통된 기능이 있을 수도 없을 수도 있으나 공통의 조상으로부터 내려와 동일한 기관임을 보여주는 것은 상동 형질이다.
④ 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 다른 기능을 가지지만 뼈의 개수와 그것들의 연결된 방식과 같은 비기능적 형질을 공유한다.
⑤ 생물학자들은 장기의 전제적인 구성을 살펴보고 그들의 가장 쓰임이 없는 특성에 집중한다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 새의 날개와 벌의 날개는 비행이라는 기능은 같지만 진화 과정에서 독립적으로 발생하였으므로 공통 진화적 기원을 공유하지 않습니다. 따라서 ②번은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. While delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, they __________________________________________. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.*animus: 반감, 미움

② play a significant role in running popular stores
③ are actually regarded as the least convenient vehicles
④ are truly a vital part of creating more sustainable cities

questions.explanation: 배달 차량이 종종 미움을 받기도 하지만, 실제로는 여러 대의 하이브리드 차량보다 물건 운송에 효율적이며, 동네 상점에 물건을 공급함으로써 주민들이 차를 타지 않고 걸어서 장을 볼 수 있게 해줍니다. 즉, 지속 가능한 도시를 만드는 데 필수적인 부분이라는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 도시를 더 푸르게 만드는 데 거의 기여하지 않는다

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory.
ordered_passages: (A) We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space, but this short-term sections has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later.
(B) After a few seconds of minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes.
(C) Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form.*cram: 벼락 공부를 하다
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 벼락치기가 최선의 전략이라는 착각을 하는 이유가 기억의 여러 부분을 구분하지 못하기 때문이라고 언급합니다. (C)에서 학습 직후 정보가 '작업 기억(working memory)'에 활성화된 상태로 존재함을 먼저 설명하고, (A)에서 이 작업 기억(단기 저장 공간)에 정보가 있어 '안다'고 느끼지만 이는 장기 기억과는 무관함을 지적합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 시간이 지남에 따라 작업 기억이 사라지고 결국 기억이 소멸되는 과정을 설명하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)'the winners'가 지칭하는 대상을 2개만 찾아 그대로(영어로) 쓰시오.
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups, who are positive people having overcome negative states. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with (A)<u>the winners</u>." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
subjective_conditions: 2개만 찾아 그대로(영어로) 쓰시오.
questions.answer: (1) other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle(2) positive people having overcome negative states
questions.explanation: 문맥상 'the winners'는 부정적인 상태를 극복하고 문제를 해결한 긍정적인 사람들을 의미합니다. 지문 내에서 이를 수식하는 표현인 'other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle', 'positive people having overcome negative states', 'Those who are in a higher vibration' 등이 해당됩니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show - whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
questions.summary_sentence: Each new medium acts like a pair of "goggles" that (A)_________ our perception of the world with the medium itself influencing how we interpret information more than the (B)_________ it conveys.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 마샬 맥루한의 이론을 바탕으로, 새로운 매체가 등장할 때마다 우리가 세상을 바라보는 방식 자체가 바뀐다는 점을 강조합니다. 매체는 단순한 도구가 아니라 세상을 보는 '안경'과 같아서 우리의 인식을 '재구성(reframes)'하며, 전달되는 구체적인 '내용(content)'보다 그 정보가 전달되는 방식(매체 그 자체)이 더 중요하다는 논지입니다.
options_translation: 유지한다 - 감정
무시한다 - 관점
재구성한다 - 내용
조정한다 - 플랫폼
안정시킨다 - 아이디어

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 (A)와 (B)를 어법상 옳게 고치고, 그 이유를 각각 우리말(필요시 영어사용 가능) 50자 내로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, (A)<u>takes</u> that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO₂ a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) (B)<u>estimating</u> the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.answer: (A) taking (또는 and it takes), 이유: 능동의 의미를 나타내며 앞 문장에 이어지는 분사구문이 필요함. (B) estimated (또는 evaluated), 이유: 문장의 본동사가 필요하며 'In 2019'라는 명확한 과거 시점이 있으므로 과거 시제 동사를 써야 함.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞의 완전한 절(each whale sequesters...) 다음에 접속사 없이 동사 takes가 바로 올 수 없으므로, 이를 분사구문인 taking으로 고치거나 접속사를 포함한 and it takes 형태로 고쳐야 합니다. (B) 해당 문장의 주어는 economists이며, 문장 전체의 서술어(본동사)가 없는 상태입니다. 또한 2019년이라는 과거의 특정 시점이 제시되었으므로 현재분사인 estimating을 과거 시제 동사인 estimated(또는 문맥상 평가했다는 의미의 evaluated)로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways of ⓐ<u>increasing</u> productivity, which is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith once wrote when the manufacturing industry was new, ⓑ<u>describing</u> a way that production could be made more efficient, known as the "division of labor." Making most manufactured goods ⓒ<u>involves</u> several different processes using different skills. Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished. One worker could do all these tasks, and make 20 pins in a day. But this work can be divided into its separate processes, with one task ⓓ<u>performed</u> by a number of workers each. Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day - a huge increase in productivity from the 200 ⓔ<u>what</u> they would have produced before.
questions.explanation: ⓔ '200'이라는 선행사가 존재하므로, 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사인 'what'은 올 수 없습니다. 목적격 관계대명사인 'that'이나 'which'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
options: ① Why Your Voice Changes Over Time
② Unlock the Secrets to a Perfect Speaking Voice
③ Why Your Recorded Voice Sounds Different to You
④ How Recordings Enhance the Richness of Our Voices
⑤ Recording Technology Removes Vocal Vibrations for Better Clarity
questions.explanation: 자신의 목소리가 녹음된 것과 다르게 들리는 이유는 공기를 통한 전달 경로 외에 뼈를 통한 내부 진동 경로가 있어 저음이 더 강조되기 때문이라는 내용이므로, 정답은 '녹음된 목소리가 왜 다르게 들리는가'이다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 목소리가 시간이 지남에 따라 변하는 이유
② 완벽한 대화 목소리를 위한 비밀을 밝히다
③ 왜 녹음된 당신의 목소리가 당신에게 다르게 들리는가
④ 녹음이 우리 목소리의 풍부함을 향상시키는 방법
⑤ 더 나은 선명도를 위해 목소리 진동을 제거하는 녹음 기술

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to _______________________________________. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
options: ① focus on work to escape negative thoughts
② rely on yourself without seeking external help
③ engage with people who release positive energy
④ pretend everything is fine and ignore your emotions
⑤ surround yourself with people who also feel helpless
questions.explanation: 지문은 무력감이나 우울함에서 벗어나는 방법으로 '긍정적인 에너지를 가진 사람들과 함께 있는 것'을 제시하고 있습니다. 지문 내에서 'hanging out with the winners'라고 표현하며, 더 높은 진동(higher vibration)을 가진 사람들과 함께 있는 것만으로도 긍정적인 에너지 전이와 잠재된 긍정적 사고를 일깨우는 효과가 있다고 설명하므로 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 부정적인 생각을 피하기 위해 업무에 집중하기
② 외부의 도움을 구하지 않고 스스로에게 의지하기
③ 긍정적인 에너지를 내뿜는 사람들과 교류하기
④ 모든 것이 괜찮은 척하며 감정을 무시하기
⑤ 자신과 마찬가지로 무력감을 느끼는 사람들에게 둘러싸이기

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, Al can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. (A) Al-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. (B) For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. (C) For instance, Al's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. (D) Moreover, recent developments in Al-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service. (E) In summary, Al has the potential to transform workplaces by promoting inclusivity and empowering disadvantaged workers to improve their skills and career opportunities.
questions.insertion_sentence: Al can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 AI가 저숙련 노동자의 능력을 향상시키고 임금과 경력 전망에 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있다는 내용입니다. (C) 뒤에 이어지는 문장들(비원어민의 업무 능력 향상, 텍스트 생성기를 통한 글쓰기/코딩 능력 향상 등)은 모두 저숙련 혹은 특정 능력 보완이 필요한 노동자들에게 AI가 어떻게 도움을 주는지에 대한 구체적인 예시들입니다. 따라서 포괄적인 문장인 주어진 문장이 (C) 위치에 들어가 사례들을 이끄는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy boosts sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated the ⓐ<u>value</u> of this tactic in 1998. He ⓑ<u>persuaded</u> three supermarkets in Sioux City, lowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the unlimited condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas under the ⓒ<u>restriction</u>, when there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity encourages sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with ⓓ<u>actual</u> shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, and it was not held in a laboratory where consumers might behave ⓔ<u>typically</u>.
questions.explanation: 실제 슈퍼마켓에서 실제 쇼객을 대상으로 한 실험이기에, 인위적인 실험실에서 소비자들이 평소와는 다르게 행동할 수 있는 상황이 아니라는 맥락이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 'typically(전형적으로)'를 'differently(다르게)'와 같은 의미의 단어로 바꾸어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ에 대한 설명이 잘못된 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old. By the time we are adults, we have ⓐ<u>fewer questions</u> and more ⓑ<u>default settings</u>. As Henry James put it, "Disinterested curiosity is past, ⓒ<u>the mental grooves and channels</u> set." The decline in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections. The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between those in the adult brain. ⓓ<u>The baby's perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered</u>. As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while ⓔ<u>the ones that the child doesn't use regularly are pruned away</u>.
options: ① ⓐ is linked with decreasing curiosity.
② ⓑ refers to innate knowledge that human beings have.
③ ⓒ symbolizes a solid system of knowledge and beliefs.
④ ⓓ is due to the infant brain's abundant and disorganized neural connections.
⑤ ⓔ is a process that improves efficiency of the brain.
questions.explanation: ⓑ의 'default settings(기본 설정)'는 성인이 되면서 굳어진 지식이나 신념 체계를 의미하는 것이지, 인간이 태어날 때부터 가지고 있는 '타고난 지식(innate knowledge)'을 의미하는 것이 아닙니다. 지문에서 'default settings'는 호기심이 감소하고 지식이 굳어지는 과정의 결과물로 묘사되고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ는 감소하는 호기심과 연결된다.
② ⓑ는 인간이 가진 타고난 지식을 의미한다.
③ ⓒ는 지식과 신념의 견고한 체계를 상징한다.
④ ⓓ는 유아 뇌의 풍부하고 무질서한 신경 연결 때문이다.
⑤ ⓔ는 뇌의 효율성을 향상시키는 과정이다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO₂ a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
options: ① Whales contribute to carbon storage even after they die by keeping carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries.
② Each whale absorbs less carbon dioxide than a single tree over its lifetime.
③ The waste released by whales increases phytoplankton populations in the ocean.
④ Some scientists refer to whales as the "engineers of marine ecosystems" due to their role in carbon sequestration.
⑤ Whale restoration is being promoted as a potential solution to help combat climate change.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 고래 한 마리는 평균 30톤의 이산화탄소를 격리하며, 이는 수천 그루의 나무와 맞먹는 수준이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 나무 한 그루는 1년에 겨우 48파운드의 이산화탄소를 흡수하므로, 고래 한 마리가 나무 한 그루보다 훨씬 더 많은 이산화탄소를 흡수합니다. 따라서 2번 선지는 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: 고래는 죽은 후에도 수세기 동안 대기 중에서 탄소를 제거함으로써 탄소 저장에 기여한다.
각 고래는 일생 동안 단 한 그루의 나무보다 더 적은 양의 이산화탄소를 흡수한다.
고래가 배출하는 배설물은 바다의 식물성 플랑크톤 개체 수를 증가시킨다.
일부 과학자들은 탄소 격리 역할 때문에 고래를 '해양 생태계의 엔지니어'라고 부른다.
고래 복원은 기후 변화에 대응하기 위한 잠재적인 해결책으로 추진되고 있다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although technology has the potential to increase productivity, it can also have a negative impact on productivity. For example, in many office environments workers sit at desks with computers and have access to the internet. They are able to check their personal e-mails and use social media whenever they want to. This can stop them from doing their work and make them less productive. Introducing new technology can also have a negative impact on production when it causes a change to the production process or requires workers to learn a new system. Learning to use new technology can be time consuming and stressful for workers and this can cause a decline in productivity.
options: ① darkside effects of productivity on technology
② desirable attitudes for embracing new technology at work
③ technological issues related to employees' work environment
④ the need for restricting the use of the Internet at the workplace
⑤ how technological advancements can lead to a decline in productivity
questions.explanation: 이 글은 기술이 생산성을 높일 수 있는 잠재력이 있지만, 인터넷 사용으로 인한 업무 방해나 새로운 시스템 학습에 따른 스트레스와 시간 소모 등으로 인해 오히려 생산성에 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 5번 '기술적 발전이 어떻게 생산성 저하로 이어질 수 있는가'입니다.
options_translation: 생산성이 기술에 미치는 어두운 측면의 영향
직장에서 새로운 기술을 수용하기 위한 바람직한 태도
직원들의 업무 환경과 관련된 기술적 문제들
직장에서 인터넷 사용을 제한할 필요성
기술적 발전이 어떻게 생산성 저하로 이어질 수 있는가

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 주제와 가장 잘 어울리는 표현은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we can learn a lot by simply watching others.
options: ① No man was ever great by imitation. - Samuel Johnson
② Experience is a good school. But the fees are high. - Heinrich Heine
③ To copy others is necessary, but to copy oneself is pitiful. - Pablo Picasso
④ If you have never been hated by your child, you have never been a parent. - Bette Davis
⑤ Don't worry that children never listen to you; worry that they are always watching you. - Robert Fulghum
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런의 발견을 통해 인간의 근본적인 능력인 '관찰을 통한 학습(모방)'의 중요성을 설명하고 있습니다. 아이들은 부모의 행동을 관찰하고 모방하며 학습하며, 현대 문명 또한 타인을 관찰함으로써 배우는 능력 덕분에 가능하다고 말합니다. 따라서 "아이들이 당신의 말을 듣지 않는 것을 걱정하지 말고, 그들이 항상 당신을 지켜보고 있다는 것을 걱정하라(즉, 행동으로 보여주는 모방 학습이 중요하다)"는 5번의 격언이 주제와 가장 잘 어울립니다.
options_translation: 모방을 통해 위대해진 사람은 없다. - 사무엘 존슨
경험은 좋은 학교다. 하지만 수업료가 비싸다. - 하인리히 하이네
타인을 모방하는 것은 필요하지만, 자신을 모방하는 것은 한심하다. - 파블로 피카소
아이에게 미움을 받아본 적이 없다면, 당신은 결코 부모였던 적이 없는 것이다. - 베티 데이비스
아이들이 당신의 말을 전혀 듣지 않는 것을 걱정하지 마라. 그들이 항상 당신을 지켜보고 있다는 것을 걱정하라. - 로버트 풀검

questions.question: 18. 다음 Capuchins에 관해 바르게 이해한 것만을 <보기>에서 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
vocabulary_box: ⓐ They hate being disadvantaged in comparative situations.
ⓑ The criteria they use to judge fairness change over time.
ⓒ They react in an annoyed way when their expectations of fairness are not met.
ⓓ Relative comparisons can rarely shift their perception of fairness and acceptance.
ⓔ When in isolation, they will be happy to eat either a grape or a slice of cucumber.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 카푸친 원숭이는 타인과의 비교를 통해 자신의 보상이 불공정하다고 느끼면 화를 내고 보상을 거부합니다. ⓐ 비교 상황에서 불이익을 받는 것을 싫어함(본문 내용 일치), ⓒ 공정성에 대한 기대가 충족되지 않을 때 짜증 섞인 반응을 보임(오이를 던지는 행위), ⓔ 혼자 있을 때(비교 대상이 없을 때)는 오이만 받아도 행복하게 먹음(본문의 'If you put two monkeys... both slices of cucumber... they will happily eat'를 통해 유추 가능)이 옳은 내용입니다. ⓑ는 공정성 기준이 시간에 따라 변한다는 근거가 없으며, ⓓ는 상대적 비교가 공정성 인식을 변화시키지 못한다는 설명이므로 본문과 반대됩니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to distinguish between different types of memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all our time studying.
options: ① Achieving Perfect Recall with Cramming
② Testing Yourself Beats Last-Minute Study!
③ How does a Long-term Memory Function?
④ What Goes First, Short or Long-term Memory?
⑤ Want Good Grades?: Spend All Your Time Studying
questions.explanation: 이 글은 벼락치기 공부가 단기 기억에는 효과적인 것처럼 보일 수 있지만 장기 기억으로 전이되지 않음을 지적합니다. 따라서 단순히 반복해서 읽는 것보다 스스로 테스트하는 과정이 장기 기억 형성에 필수적임을 강조하고 있으므로 ②번 '스스로 테스트하는 것이 벼락치기 공부를 이긴다!'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 벼락치기로 완벽한 회상 달성하기
② 스스로 테스트하는 것이 벼락치기 공부를 이긴다!
③ 장기 기억은 어떻게 작동하는가?
④ 무엇이 먼저인가, 단기 기억인가 장기 기억인가?
⑤ 좋은 성적을 원하는가? 공부하는 데 모든 시간을 쏟아라.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 질문에 대한 답을 조건에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Nearly eight of ten U.S. adults believe there are "good foods" and "bad foods." Unless we're talking about spoiled stew, poison mushrooms, or something similar, however, no foods can be labeled as either good or bad. There are, however, combinations of foods that add up to a healthful or unhealthful diet. Consider the case of an adult who eats only foods thought of as "good" - for example, raw broccoli, apples, orange juice, boiled tofu, and carrots. Although all these foods are nutrient-dense, they do not add up to a healthy diet because they don't supply a wide enough variety of the nutrients we need. Or take the case of the teenager who occasionally eats fried chicken, but otherwise stays away from fried foods. The occasional fried chicken isn't going to knock his or her diet off track. But the person who eats fried foods every day, with few vegetables or fruits, and loads up on supersized soft drinks, candy, and chips for snacks has a bad diet.↓Q: What factors should you consider when composing a diet?A: Variety and balance! Even fried chicken won't harm you, if it is only occasional and part of a healthy combination of foods. Remember. No food is good or bad on its own. What truly matters is considering _____________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>의 단어만을 주어진 형태로 한 번씩 모두 사용할 것
vocabulary_box: it / consumed / items / is / the / with / other
questions.answer: the other items it is consumed with
questions.explanation: 지문은 음식 하나가 좋고 나쁜 것이 아니라 어떤 조합으로 먹느냐가 중요하다는 내용이다. 따라서 '그것(음식)이 함께 소비되는 다른 품목들'이라는 의미로 구성한다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 흐름도의 빈칸 (A)~(D)를 조건에 맞게 완성하시오.
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.summary_sentence: Here's the flowchart of the sequence of eventsthreatening marine organisms.Global Warming↓(A)__________ of Sea Temperature↓(B)__________ in Dissolved Oxygen in Seawater↓Impact on the Habitat of Marine Organisms↓(C)__________ or (D)__________ of Marine Life (Fish, Crabs, etc.)
subjective_conditions: 1. (A)~(D)는 한 단어로 쓸 것
questions.answer: (A) rise(B) decrease [또는 decline / reduction](C) death(D) displacement
questions.explanation: (A) 지구 온난화로 바다 온도가 상승(rise)한다. (B) 온도가 오르면 용존 산소량은 감소(decrease)한다. (C), (D) 산소 부족으로 인해 해양 생물이 죽거나(death) 쫓겨나게(displacement) 된다. (지문 끝부분의 'killed or displaced'를 명사형으로 변환)

questions.question: 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 흐름도의 빈칸 (A)~(D)를 조건에 맞게 완성하시오.
