subjective_conditions: 1. (A)~(D)는 한 단어로 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 지문의 내용을 바탕으로 지구 온난화로 인한 해양 생태계 변화의 흐름도를 완성하는 문제입니다. 지구 온난화는 해수 온도의 상승(rise)을 가져오고, 이는 용존 산소량의 감소(decrease 또는 decline)를 초래합니다. 결과적으로 해양 생물의 서식지에 영향을 미쳐 생물의 죽음(death)이나 이동(displacement)을 야기합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
options: ① physical properties required for sound to exist
③ necessity of perception in scientific communication
④ significance of hypothesis in completing scientific research
⑤ correlations between sound waves and scientific signals
questions.explanation: 이 글은 소리가 들려야만 비로소 소리가 되는 것처럼, 과학적 연구 결과도 단순히 출판되는 것에서 끝나는 것이 아니라 의도된 청중(독자)에 의해 읽히고 이해되어야만 진정으로 완성된다는 과학적 의사소통의 상호작용적 본질을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 '과학적 의사소통에서 인식의 필요성'입니다.
options_translation: ① 소리가 존재하기 위해 필요한 물리적 성질
② 관찰의 철학적 함의
③ 과학적 의사소통에서 인식의 필요성
④ 과학 연구를 완수하는 데 있어 가설의 중요성
⑤ 음파와 과학적 신호 사이의 상관관계

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselves and maintain a healthy relationship with our negotiating partners at the same time. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
options: ① 우리 모두는 우리가 알든 모르든 매일 협상한다.
② 대부분의 사람들은 양쪽 모두에게 유리한 협상을 배운다.
③ 이기고 지는 쪽이 생기는 협상 방식은 일회성 협상에서는 유용할 수 있다.
④ 동일한 사람을 반복적으로 상대하는 협상에서는 협상 파트너들과 건전한 관계를 유지하는 것이 중요하다.
⑤ 장기적인 관계의 상호의존적인 세계에서 양측에 유리한 성과는 수용 가능한 유일한 결과로 빠른 속도로 자리잡고 있다.
questions.explanation: 본문 세 번째 문장인 'Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement'에 따르면, 협상을 배우는 사람들은 보통 양쪽 모두에게 유리한(win-win) 방식이 아니라 한쪽이 이기고 한쪽이 지는(win-lose) 전통적인 방식을 배운다고 했으므로 ②번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
options: ① Social media has transformed how fans engage in sports events.
② Fans rarely criticize sports teams outside of game days.
③ Sports executives must adapt to changing game strategies.
④ The role of education in sports business is increasingly important.
⑤ Professionals in sports management often receive unnecessary advice from unqualified individuals.
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부 이후에 스포츠 관리 경영진들이 수십 년의 지식과 경험을 가지고 있음에도 불구하고, 전문 지식이 없는 팬이나 이웃들로부터 사업 운영 방식에 대한 조언이나 비판을 받는다는 내용이 나옵니다. 다른 전문직(의사, 회계사)과 달리 스포츠 분야의 전문가들은 비전문가들로부터 불필요한 훈수를 많이 받는다는 것이 요지입니다.
options_translation: ① 소셜 미디어는 팬들이 스포츠 경기에 참여하는 방식을 변화시켰다.
② 팬들은 경기일 이외에는 스포츠 팀을 거의 비판하지 않는다.
③ 스포츠 경영진은 변화하는 경기 전략에 적응해야 한다.
④ 스포츠 비즈니스에서 교육의 역할이 점점 더 중요해지고 있다.
⑤ 스포츠 경영 분야의 전문가들은 종종 자격 없는 개인들로부터 불필요한 조언을 듣는다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration" to disempower animals for the purpose of _________________________________________.
options: ① preserving our dominance at the top
③ bridging the gap between species
④ ensuring the intelligence of animals
⑤ illustrating the ethical treatment of animals
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 스스로를 동물보다 우월한 존재로 유지하기 위해 언어적 기교(linguistic castration)를 사용하여 인간과 동물의 유사성을 부정한다는 내용입니다. 과학자들이 동물의 행동을 기계적인 용어로 바꾸어 부르거나 지능을 본능으로 치부하는 행위는 결국 가상의 사다리 꼭대기에서 인간의 지배적 위치를 유지하기 위함이므로, 빈칸에는 '정점에서의 우리의 지배력을 보존하는 것'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 정상에서의 우리의 지배력을 보존하는 것
② 우리의 인지적 한계를 경시하는 것
③ 종들 사이의 간극을 메우는 것
④ 동물의 지능을 보장하는 것
⑤ 동물의 윤리적 대우를 예증하는 것

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and expertise when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and expertise of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. People judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
questions.summary_sentence: The findings indicate that people evaluate these slight deviations from the norm (A)__________, as they imply that the person possesses enough (B)__________ to endure the potential disbenefit of such actions.
questions.explanation: 연구 결과에 따르면, 사람들은 규범에서 약간 벗어난 행동(예: 정장에 빨간 나비넥타이, 강의 중 빨간 운동화)을 하는 사람들에 대해 지위와 전문성이 더 높다고 긍정적으로 평가합니다. 이는 그러한 일탈이 사회적 비용(잠재적 불이익)을 감수할 만큼 그 사람이 충분한 힘(권위)을 가졌음을 암시하기 때문입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '호의적으로(favorably)', (B)에는 '권위(authority)'가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다. (⑤번의 fragility는 '취약함'이므로 부적절함)

questions.question: 17. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Sports experts with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
options: ② Secrets to Success in Sports Coaching
③ How Outsiders Influence Sports Decisions

⑤ The Characteristics of Human's Interference across Various Fields

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether'we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly ─ our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In view of this, it's essential to achieve good results while _________________________. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 현대 사회의 상호 의존적인 관계 속에서 협상의 중요성을 다루고 있습니다. 과거의 승패 방식(win-lose)보다는 장기적인 관계를 유지하기 위해 양측이 모두 만족하는 승승 방식(win-win)이 필수적이라고 설명합니다. 빈칸은 장기적으로 같은 사람들과 반복해서 거래하는 상황에서 필수적인 요소인 '긍정적인 관계 형성'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that crossings are minimized. ⓐThese people, for instance, might take phone calls or video conferences while attending to chores or family needs. ⓑWe've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones─one for work and one for personal use. ⓒFlexible schedules benefit these individuals by allowing them to better differentiate between work time and personal time. ⓓOther individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. ⓔThis might entail constantly blending their work responsibilities seamlessly with their personal life, or having a home setup where individuals can easily switch between professional tasks and family activities.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 일과 가정의 경계를 분리하려는 사람(segmenters)과 통합하려는 사람(integrators)의 차이를 설명하고 있습니다. 문장 ⓐ는 집안일이나 가족 일을 돌보면서 전화 통화나 화상 회의를 한다는 내용으로, 이는 '분리'가 아닌 '통합'을 선호하는 사람들의 사례에 해당하므로, 분리하려는 사람들의 예시로 제시된 ⓐ는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders─employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively (A)_____________ from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task─like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds─they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to (B)_____________ our spot at the top.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 언어를 사용하여 동물과 우리 사이의 유사성을 폄하하고 인간의 우월성을 유지하려 한다는 내용입니다. (A)에서는 동물의 도구 제작이 인간의 것과는 질적으로 '다르다(distinct)'고 주장하며 거리를 두는 모습을 설명하고, (B)에서는 이러한 언어적 기법이 정점의 자리를 '확보/방어(secure)'하기 위한 것임을 설명합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A "complementary good" is a product that is often consumed alongside another product. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When the popularity of one product ⓐ<u>increases</u>, the sales of its complementary good also increase. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ensure a steady stream of ⓑ<u>demand</u> for your product. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status─they have to be consumed ⓒ<u>separately</u>, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, never assume that a product is ⓓ<u>permanently</u> complementary, as customers may not be completely locked in to the product. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can ⓔ<u>switch</u> into electric cars.
questions.explanation: 보완재(complementary good)는 다른 제품과 함께 소비되는 제품을 의미합니다. 램프와 전구의 예처럼 완벽한 보완 관계에 있는 제품은 '따로(separately)'가 아니라 '함께(together)' 소비되어야 하므로 ⓒ의 'separately'는 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 ⓐ를 우리말로 바르게 해석하시오.
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. ⓐ<u>Publication is no more than pressure waves</u> unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers are published yet readers don't understand them.
questions.explanation: 문장에서 'no more than'은 '~에 지나지 않는(only)'이라는 의미를 가집니다. 따라서 해당 부분은 출판된 논문이 독자에게 이해되지 않는다면 그것은 소리의 물리적 현상인 '압력파'일 뿐 아무런 의미가 없다는 뜻으로 해석됩니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.*dissolved: 용해된 **anoxic: 산소 결핍의

③ The Role of Dissolved Oxygen in Marine Life

questions.question: 11. 다음 Whales에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO₂ a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.*sequester: 격리하다**phytoplankton: 식물성 플랑크톤
options: ① 고래는 죽을 때 평균적으로 30톤의 이산화탄소를 격리시키며, 수 세기 동안 이를 대기에서 빼내어 둔다.
② 기후적 관점에서, 각각의 고래는 수천 그루의 나무와 동일한 역할을 한다.
③ 고래의 배설물은 해양 생태계를 풍요롭게 하며, 그 결과 식물성 플랑크톤의 수가 감소해 추가적인 탄소 격리가 이루어진다.
④ 2019년 IMF 경제학자들은 고래 한 마리 당 생태계 서비스 가치를 2백만 달러 이상으로 평가했다.
⑤ 산업화 이전 고래 개체 수로의 회복을 목표로 하는 경제적 유인책을 기반으로 한 고래 복원 프로그램에 대한 요구가 제기되고 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 고래의 배설물이 영양분을 공급하여 식물성 플랑크톤의 개체 수를 '증가시킨다(increasing phytoplankton populations)'고 설명하고 있습니다. ③번 선택지는 개체 수가 '감소'한다고 설명하고 있으므로 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 Analogous(유사 형질)와 Homologous(동종 형질)에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
options: ① Analogous traits, which have a common function, arose from different evolutionary branches.
② The wings of a bird and those of a bee are an example of independent evolution; they serve a common function but arose on different evolutionary branches.
③ Homologous traits do not necessarily have the same function, but they have some common structure derived from a common ancestor.
④ The wings of a bat and the forelimbs of a horse evolved from a common ancestor and share the same function.
⑤ Biologists pay attention to the overall structure and useless traits of organs to distinguish between analogy and homology.
questions.explanation: 본문에 따르면 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 공통 조상으로부터 유래한 동종 형질(Homologous traits)이지만, 날기 위한 용도와 걷기 위한 용도로 서로 매우 다른 기능(very different functions)을 수행합니다. 따라서 동일한 기능을 공유한다는 ④번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 공통된 기능을 가진 유사 형질(Analogous traits)은 서로 다른 진화적 계통에서 발생했다.
② 새의 날개와 벌의 날개는 독립적 진화의 한 예이다. 즉, 공통된 기능을 수행하지만 서로 다른 진화적 계통에서 발생했다.
③ 동종 형질(Homologous traits)은 반드시 같은 기능을 가지는 것은 아니지만, 공통 조상에게서 유래한 공통된 구조적 특징을 가지고 있다.
④ 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 공통 조상에게서 진화했고 동일한 기능을 공유한다.
⑤ 생물학자들은 유사 형질과 동종 형질을 구분하기 위해 기관의 전체적인 구조와 비기능적인(쓸모없는) 형질에 주목한다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another creates a sense of __________. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.explanation: 카푸친 원숭이는 자신과 동일한 행동을 한 다른 원숭이가 더 좋은 보상(포도)을 받는 것을 보고, 자신은 여전히 오이를 받는 상황에서 부당함을 느껴 화를 내며 오이를 던집니다. 이는 타인과의 비교가 '부당함(injustice)'이라는 감정을 불러일으킨다는 것을 보여주는 사례입니다.
options_translation: ① 만족
② 감사
③ 동의
④ 평등
⑤ 부당함(불공정)

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations - surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue - with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a black-tie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge ______________________________________ because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
options: ① these minor variations from established norms as favorable
② those who break accepted norms slightly as lacking competence
③ slight deviations from the norm as signs of disregard for social expectations
④ those norm breakers as having a conservative but power-oriented character
⑤ individuals who wear unconventional clothing as less trustworthy and unprofessional
questions.explanation: 지문에서는 기존의 규범을 아주 살짝 벗어난 사람들(격식 있는 블랙타이 행사에서 빨간 나비넥타이를 한 남자, 빨간 운동화를 신고 강의하는 교수)에 대해 사람들이 오히려 더 호의적인 태도로 판단하는 경향을 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 그들이 그러한 일탈 행동으로 인한 사회적 비용을 감수할 만큼 충분한 능력이 있다고 인식되기 때문입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '기존 규범으로부터의 이러한 사소한 변화를 호의적으로 판단한다'는 내용의 ①번이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기존 규범으로부터의 이러한 사소한 변화들을 호의적으로
② 승인된 규범을 약간 어기는 사람들을 능력이 부족한 것으로
③ 규범으로부터의 사소한 이탈을 사회적 기대를 무시하는 신호로
④ 그러한 규범 파괴자들을 보수적이지만 권력 지향적인 성격을 가진 것으로
⑤ 파격적인 옷을 입은 개인들을 덜 신뢰할 만하고 비전문가스러운 것으로

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, such transactions are becoming increasingly rare, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly - our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients. In view of this, it's essential to achieve successful results for ourselve while _______________________________________________. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long-term relationships, a win-win outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
options: ① preserving a positive relationship with those we negotiate with
② ensuring we win at all costs, regardless of the relationship's future
③ prioritizing the deal over maintaining any form of mutual respect or partnership
④ casually ignoring the long-term relationship with those involved in the negotiation
⑤ subtly undermining the relationship with our negotiation partners for short-term gains
questions.explanation: 현대 사회에서는 동일한 사람들과 반복적으로 상호작용하기 때문에 일회성 거래보다는 장기적인 관계 유지가 중요하다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 협상 시 자신을 위한 성공적인 결과를 얻으면서도 동시에 '협상 대상자와의 긍정적인 관계를 유지하는 것'이 필수적입니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 협상하는 사람들과 긍정적인 관계를 유지하는 것
② 관계의 미래와 상관없이 어떤 대가를 치르더라도 우리가 이기도록 보장하는 것
③ 어떤 형태의 상호 존중이나 파트너십 유지보다 거래를 우선시하는 것
④ 협상에 연루된 사람들과의 장기적인 관계를 무심코 무시하는 것
⑤ 단기적 이익을 위해 협상 파트너와의 관계를 미묘하게 약화시키는 것

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. (A) Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. (B) This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. (C) The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. (D) The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. (E) Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the criticism also fails to recognize that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity redefines what fame means.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그러나 그 비판은 일반적인 유명인의 현상이 명성의 의미를 재정의한다는 것을 인식하지 못한다'는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (B) 문장까지는 소셜 미디어 유명인들이 엘리트 유명인의 영역으로 넘어가는 데 장벽이 있다는 비판적 시각을 다루고 있고, (C) 이후부터는 엘리트 유명인(star)과 일반 유명인(ordinary celebrity)의 차이점을 본격적으로 대조하며 명성의 새로운 정의를 설명하기 시작하므로, 흐름을 전환하는 주어진 문장은 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
questions.summary_sentence: While the expansion of higher education aims to promote lifelong learning through assessment for learning and a focus on (A)_______________, in practice it often leads to (B)_______________ due to the need for efficiency in mass education.
options: ① (A) overall evaluation - (B) reduced learning outcomes
② (A) feedback for development - (B) a concentration on grades
④ (A) performance-based assessment - (B) a focus on feedback
⑤ (A) growth-oriented evaluation - (B) enhanced educational dialogue
questions.explanation: 고등교육이 엘리트 시스템에서 대중 시스템으로 확장되면서, 이론적으로는 발달을 위한 피드백과 학습을 위한 평가를 강조하지만, 실제로는 대중 교육의 효율성을 위해 표준화된 시험이 사용되며 학생들이 피드백보다는 성적(grades)에 집중하게 만든다는 내용이다. 따라서 (A)에는 발달을 위한 피드백(feedback for development), (B)에는 성적에 대한 집중(a concentration on grades)이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① (A) 종합적인 평가 - (B) 줄어든 학습 성과
② (A) 발달을 위한 피드백 - (B) 성적에 대한 집중
③ (A) 학생 중심 학습 - (B) 더 강한 참여
④ (A) 수행 기반 평가 - (B) 피드백에 대한 집중
⑤ (A) 성장 지향적 평가 - (B) 강화된 교육적 대화

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 가장 알맞은 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very organizational structure can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.↓Each department within the organization can have a different (A)__________ and (B)__________________________.
questions.explanation: 본문의 첫 문장에서 'From an organizational viewpoint'라고 언급하며 조직 내 각 부서가 고유의 문화를 가지고 있음을 설명한다. 또한 각 부서가 자신들만의 편향된 관점(perspective)에서 상황을 바라본다고 설명하고 있는데, 요약문의 (A)에 들어갈 말로 본문에서 찾을 수 있는 '관점'에 해당하는 단어는 viewpoint이다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말을 의미와 어법에 맞게 주어진 표현을 배열하여 완성하시오. (어휘 추가 및 변형 없음) [2.9점]
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is (A)________________________________________. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and discovered ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. 'To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books.' The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.*dyslexia: 난독증 ** voraciously: 탐욕스럽게
subjective_conditions: 어휘 추가 및 변형 없음
vocabulary_box: relevant texts / students / they / in / with /
questions.answer: providing students with relevant texts they will be interested in.
questions.explanation: 참여와 성취의 핵심은 학생들이 관심을 가질 만한 관련 텍스트를 제공하는 것입니다. 'provide A with B' 구문과 목적격 관계대명사가 생략된 절을 사용하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞추어 4단어로 영작하시오. [2.9점]
questions.passage: Claims that local food production cut greenhouse gas emissions by reducing the burning of transportation fuel are usually not well founded. Transport is the source of only 11 percent of greenhouse gas emissions within the food sector, so reducing the distance that food travels after it leaves the farm is far less important than reducing wasteful energy use on the farm. Food coming from a distance can actually be better for the climate, depending on (A)________________________. For example, field-grown tomatoes shipped from Mexico in the winter months will have a smaller carbon footprint than local winter tomatoes grown in a greenhouse. In the United Kingdom, lamb meat that travels 11,000 miles from New Zealand generates only one-quarter the carbon emissions per pound compared to British lamb because farmers in the United Kingdom raise their animals on feed (which must be produced using fossil fuels) rather than on clover pastureland.When food does travel, (B)ကᅡ방 방시그냐느는 거시 가장 중요한 거슨 이동단 거리가 가장 중요한 거시 아니라 이동 방시기다, and most of all the load size. Bulk loads of food can travel halfway around the world by ocean freight with a smaller carbon footprint, per pound delivered, than foods traveling just a short distance but in much smaller loads. For example, 18-wheelers carry much larger loads than pickup trucks so they can move food 100 times as far while burning only one-third as much gas per pound of food delivered.*freight: 화물 운송
subjective_conditions: 거휘 구가 아니 주어진 표현 중 피료한 거ᄉ만 골라 사용할 거새
동사난 피료시 형태랄 변화시낄 수 이거나 갸 외그해 표현으난 변혀나어시 그대로 사용할 거새
vocabulary_box: why / how / when / food / greenhouse gas /
questions.explanation: 문매ᄀ사ᄃ 머리 털어진 고새서 온 시ᄀ료푸미 기후가 더 조해을 수 이거는 거슨 '시ᄀ료푸미 어따게 재배되느냐'(여터 고시ᄀ나 노지 드대)에 다라 다라지느냐 거시므로, 'how food was grown'이 저ᄀ저하ᄆ니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 부분이 있는 것을 골라 그 기호를 쓰고, 올바르게 고친 후 밑줄 친 부분 전체를 다시 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as ⓐ<u>portable digital technology makes them possible to work anywhere, anytime</u>. ⓑ<u>Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities</u>. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are minimized. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and ⓒ<u>take care of family matters only during breaks and non-work time</u>. ⓓ<u>We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones</u> - one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or ⓔ<u>monitoring emails at home and on vacation</u>, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.answer: ⓐ, portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime.
questions.explanation: ⓐ에서 'makes them possible to work' 부분은 가목적어 it을 사용하는 구문이어야 한다. 뒤에 진목적어인 'to work anywhere, anytime'이 있으므로 them을 가목적어 it으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절하다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: _________________ ________________, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
options: ① if you examine what you studied
② unless you devote time to studying
③ if you repeatedly memorize a new thing
④ if working memory is not activated
⑤ unless you retest your knowledge
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 부분에서 정보를 장기 기억으로 옮기기 위해서는 단순 공부보다 '스스로를 테스트하는 것(test yourself)'이 필수적이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 앞 문맥은 단기 기억이 사라지는 상황을 설명하고 있으므로, '지식을 다시 테스트하지 않는다면(unless you retest your knowledge)' 기억이 사라진다는 내용이 흐름상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 공부한 것을 검토한다면
② 공부하는 데 시간을 쏟지 않는다면
③ 새로운 것을 반복적으로 암기한다면
④ 작업 기억이 활성화되지 않는다면
⑤ 지식을 다시 테스트하지 않는다면

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen ⓐ<u>that</u> all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water ⓑ<u>is</u> - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if ⓒ<u>allowed</u> to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans ⓓ<u>has</u> been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water ⓔ<u>have</u> the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 'cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water [does]' 구조가 되어야 합니다. 앞선 동사 'holds'를 대신하는 대동사가 필요하므로 be동사인 'is'가 아니라 'does'로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own ⓐ<u>prejudiced</u> perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which ⓑ<u>disallows</u> them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create ⓒ<u>disagreement</u>. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical ⓓ<u>hierarchy</u> with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is ⓔ<u>centralized</u> and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 유기적 구조(Organic structures)는 기계적 구조와 달리 의사결정이 한곳에 집중되지 않고 분산되어 수평적인 성격을 띠는 구조입니다. 따라서 ⑤ 'centralized(집중된)'는 문맥상 'decentralized(분산된)' 또는 'distributed'와 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. ⓐThe wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. ⓑ"Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. ⓒThe wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. ⓓBecause all mammals, including humans, share the same ancestors, we also share very similar biological structures. ⓔAs a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 생물학적 유사성의 두 종류인 '사상적(analogous) 특성'과 '상동적(homologous) 특성'의 차이를 설명하는 글입니다. ⓓ는 모든 포유류가 공통 조상을 공유하며 생물학적 구조가 유사하다는 일반적인 진술로, 앞선 문장에서 설명한 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리(상동적 특성)가 공통 조상에서 기인했다는 구체적 설명과 그 결과(ⓔ) 사이의 흐름을 방해하는 사족에 가깝습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글을 읽고 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 mass higher education의 특징으로 볼 수 없는 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs ⓐ<u>to build a specialized workforce for the economy</u>. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce ⓑ<u>should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students</u>, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up ⓒ<u>a 'field of contradictions' for assessment</u> in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students ⓓ<u>to focus more on grades than feedback</u>. In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with ⓔ<u>formative feedback</u> shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.*demographic: 인구집단
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 부분에서 'formative feedback(형성적 피드백)'은 과거의 'elite systems(엘리트 시스템)'의 특징으로 설명되고 있습니다. 대중 고등 교육(mass higher education)은 효율성을 위해 최소한의 비인격적 피드백을 제공하며 학생들이 피드백보다 성적에 집중하게 만든다고 설명되어 있으므로 ⑤번은 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 you are putting on a new kind of goggles가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like <u>you are putting on a new kind of goggles</u>, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show - whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① Goggles are the forms of protective gear required to wear.
② A new medium is a system within which people can see the world by getting information.
③ People have so strong prejudice against a new medium that it cannot lead to more balanced and accurate judgment.
④ When using a new medium, wear a special gear like glasses as a means of communicating people.
⑤ Selecting your own medium si more important than following others' use of the newest one.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 매체(미디어)가 정보를 전달하는 방식이 내용 자체보다 중요하며, 새로운 매체를 사용하는 것이 세상을 바라보는 새로운 방식을 형성한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. '새로운 종류의 고글을 쓰는 것과 같다'는 표현은 새로운 매체가 우리가 세상을 인식하고 정보를 얻는 새로운 체계(시스템)가 된다는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 고글은 착용해야 하는 보호 장비의 형태이다.
② 새로운 매체는 사람들이 정보를 얻음으로써 세상을 볼 수 있게 하는 시스템이다.
③ 사람들은 새로운 매체에 대해 너무 강한 편견을 가지고 있어서 더 균형 잡히고 정확한 판단으로 이어질 수 없다.
④ 새로운 매체를 사용할 때, 사람들과 소통하는 수단으로서 안경과 같은 특별한 장비를 착용하라.
⑤ 자신만의 매체를 선택하는 것이 다른 사람들의 최신 매체 사용을 따르는 것보다 더 중요하다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고 아래 주어진 문장의 빈칸을 본문에 나오는 한 단어를 넣어 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 완성하시오.
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the passage, Mirror neurons facilitate our learning by enabling us to (A)__________ the actions and behavior of those who (B)__________ (C)__________.
subjective_conditions: 필요할 경우 어형을 변형할 것
반드시 본문에 나오는 어휘를 사용할 것
위의 조건을 다 충족시키기 못한 경우 감점 있음
questions.explanation: 거울 뉴런의 발견은 관찰을 통한 학습이라는 인간의 근본적인 능력에 대한 생각을 바꾸어 놓았습니다. 지문에 따르면 거울 뉴런은 우리가 함께 있는(are with) 사람들의 행동을 모방(imitate)하게 함으로써 학습을 용이하게 합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것을 <보기>의 (A)~(D)에서 순서대로 하나씩 골라 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators ______________________________ in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
vocabulary_box: (B): elite celebrity / elite celebrities / ordinary celebrity / ordinary celebrities
(D): a social end / an outstanding talent / a natural property
questions.answer: desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 소셜 미디어 유명인사(ordinary celebrity)가 전통적인 엘리트 유명인사와 달리 대중과의 상호작용과 수치(구독자, 좋아요 등)를 통해 명성을 얻는 현상을 다룹니다. 빈칸 앞뒤 맥락을 볼 때, 일부 콘텐츠 제작자들이 명성 그 자체를 사회적 목적으로서 추구한다는 내용이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 29. 윗글에 의하면 당신의 목소리가 당신 자신에게 어떻게 들리는가?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 본인의 목소리가 다른 사람들에게 들리는 것보다 자신에게는 더 깊고 풍부하게(deeper and richer) 들린다고 언급하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 30. 윗글을 읽고 문제29번의 답처럼 들리는 이유가 무엇인지 간략하게 서술하시오.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't." is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. (A) This is one of the great powers of sell-help groups. (B) When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. (C) Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. (D) In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." (E) The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
questions.insertion_sentence: Simply to be in their presence is beneficial.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'their presence'는 바로 앞 문장(C)의 'Those who are in a higher vibration'을 가리킵니다. 또한 (D) 뒤의 'The benefit here'가 주어진 문장의 'beneficial' 내용을 구체화하며 이어지므로 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered. directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very (A)____________, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more (B)____________ (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. <u>만약 그것들이 우리가 적응하고 생존하도록 도움을 주지 않았더라면</u>, they would not have evolved with us.
options: ① effective ways of expressing emotions between people
② dispensable emotions for human to survive as a species
③ influence of emotion on developing human perception
④ ways for human to overcome fear within environment
⑤ contribution of emotion to human survival through evolution

questions.question: 10. 주어진 관 다음에 이어질 관의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. AI powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities.
ordered_passages: (A) AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity lo translate written and spoken word in real time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace.
(B) Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.

(C) For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where interpersonal communication is necessary.

questions.question: 13. [24년 9월 24번] 윗글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. ⓐFor comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. ⓑFrom a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. ⓒBut there is still the question of how to reduce the myriad dangers to whales, such as ship strikes and other hazards. ⓓWhales also help sequester carbon by (A)________________________ as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon ─ leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." ⓔIn 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential ________________________________________________.
options: ① to spend more time cramming rather than testing yourself
② to test all the materials you crammed rather than spending all your time studying
③ to spend all your time studying rather than testing yourself after studying materials
④ to test yourself before studying materials rather than spending all your time studying
⑤ to test yourself after studying materials rather than spending all your time studying
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 '벼락치기(cramming)'가 단기 기억에는 도움이 될지 몰라도 장기 기억으로 전환되지 않는다는 것입니다. 정보를 장기 기억으로 보내기 위해서는 단순히 공부만 하는 것이 아니라 스스로를 테스트하는 과정(retest)이 필수적이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '단순히 공부하는 데 시간을 다 보내기보다는 학습 후 스스로를 테스트하는 것'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 스스로를 테스트하기보다는 벼락치기에 더 많은 시간을 소비하는 것
② 공부하는 데 모든 시간을 쓰기보다는 벼락치기한 모든 자료를 테스트하는 것
③ 자료를 공부한 후 스스로 테스트하기보다는 공부하는 데 모든 시간을 소비하는 것
④ 공부하는 데 모든 시간을 쓰기보다는 자료를 공부하기 전에 스스로 테스트하는 것

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 괄호 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 말로 옳은 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are (A)[similar / different] in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose (B)[dependently / independently] in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very (C)[ similar / different] functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share (D)[functional / nonfunctional] traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
questions.explanation: 생물학자들은 두 가지 유사성을 구분하는데, '상사(analogous)' 형질은 기능은 같지만 진화 계통상 다른 가지에서 독립적으로 발생한 것이고, '상동(homologous)' 형질은 조상은 같으나 기능은 다를 수 있는 구조를 의미합니다. (A) 새와 벌의 날개는 비행을 위해 유사한(similar) 방식을 가져야 하고, (B) 진화 과정에서 독립적으로(independently) 발생했습니다. (C) 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 매우 다른(different) 기능을 수행하지만 조상이 같고, (D) 결과적으로 뼈의 수와 같은 비기능적(nonfunctional) 특징을 공유합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 유사한 - (B) 종속적으로 - (C) 다른 - (D) 기능적인
② (A) 유사한 - (B) 독립적으로 - (C) 다른 - (D) 비기능적인
③ (A) 유사한 - (B) 종속적으로 - (C) 유사한 - (D) 기능적인

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive.
ordered_passages: (A) Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature.(B) Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is sell-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level.(C) Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.(D) It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does ─ this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 해수가 용존 산소를 풍부하게 포함하고 있다는 기초 사실을 제시합니다. (D)는 물의 온도와 용존 산소량의 관계를 설명하는 물리 법칙을 제시하며, (B)는 'Thus'를 통해 지구 온난화로 인한 수온 상승이 산소 감소를 초래한다는 결론적 상황을 연결합니다. (A)는 최근 과학자들이 분석한 지난 반세기 동안의 실제 산소 감소 데이터를 언급하며 상황의 심각성을 보여주고, (C)는 이러한 산소 수준 저하가 해양 생태계에 미치는 구체적인 피해(무산소 사건 등)를 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고 추론할 수 있는 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① Discovery of luminiferous ether has contributed to scientific research.
② Science is essential and practical, as illustrated in "the black cat in the dark room".
③ Ignoring the well-known leads to misguided searches for essences.
④ Essentialism has a positive impact on scientific investigation.
⑤ The pursuit of nonexistent essences in science can mislead scientific inquiry.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 개념을 사용할 때 존재하지 않는 '본질'을 찾으려 하는 본질주의의 위험성에 대해 경고하고 있습니다. 에테르(luminiferous ether)의 사례를 통해, 과학자들이 잘못된 개념을 바탕으로 존재하지 않는 것을 증명하기 위해 헛된 노력을 기울였음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 과학에서 존재하지 않는 본질을 추구하는 행위가 과학적 탐구를 잘못된 길로 인도할 수 있다는 추론이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 빛나는 에테르의 발견은 과학 연구에 기여했다.
과학은 '어두운 방 안의 검은 고양이'에서 묘사된 것처럼 필수적이고 실용적이다.
잘 알려진 것을 무시하는 것은 본질에 대한 잘못된 탐색으로 이어진다.
본질주의는 과학적 조사에 긍정적인 영향을 미친다.
과학에서 존재하지 않는 본질을 추구하는 것은 과학적 탐구를 잘못된 방향으로 이끌 수 있다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along ─ whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS ─ and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, belore you absorb the message of any particular TV show ─ whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire ─ you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans to communicate ─ it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
questions.summary_sentence: Marshall McLuhan's viewpoint is that the medium through which information is conveyed contains a(n) (A)_____________ message that shapes our perception of the world, often more (B)_____________ than the content it delivers.
questions.explanation: 마셜 매클루언의 이론에 따르면, 새로운 매체는 그 속에 세상을 특정한 방식으로 보게 하는 암묵적인 메시지를 내포하고 있으며, 정보를 전달하는 매체 자체가 전달하는 내용(콘텐츠)보다 우리의 인식에 더 큰 영향을 미칩니다. 따라서 빈칸 (A)에는 '내포된, 은연중의'라는 뜻의 implicit이, (B)에는 내용보다 더 큰 영향을 미친다는 맥락에서 '강력한'이라는 뜻의 powerful이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
options: ① Different Ways Sounds Paths Through
② How to Make Acceptable Voice to Others
③ We Make Different Voice to Different People
④ Why Does My Voice Sound Different in Recordings?
⑤ Principles of Making Various Accents through Throat
