목구멍을 통해 다양한 억양을 만드는 원리

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because ___________________________. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
options: ① we are not restricted to the behavior we observe and learn by attending school
② children live their own lives even though adults show them how to live theirs
③ we are capable of learning through observation and imitation
④ we have common sense most people accept and share in the society
⑤ every part of our society works independently and organically at the same time
questions.explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런의 발견과 이를 통한 '관찰 학습(learning by observation)'과 '모방(imitation)'의 중요성을 설명하고 있습니다. 신생아부터 성인에 이르기까지 타인의 행동을 보고 배우는 능력이 현대 문화의 근간이 된다는 맥락이므로, 빈칸에는 '우리가 관찰과 모방을 통해 학습할 수 있기 때문'이라는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 우리가 관찰하는 행동에 국한되지 않고 학교에 다님으로써 배우기
성인들이 삶의 방식을 보여줌에도 불구하고 아이들은 그들 자신의 삶을 살기
우리가 관찰과 모방을 통해 학습할 능력이 있기
대부분의 사람들이 사회에서 받아들이고 공유하는 상식을 우리가 가지고 있기
우리 사회의 모든 부분이 독립적이면서 동시에 유기적으로 작동하기

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space, but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
options: ① Cramming is the most effective way to ensure long-term retention of information.
② Information in working memory stays preserved for several days without any significant loss.
③ Cramming creates the illusion of knowing because the information is fresh in short-term memory, but it quickly fades without repetition.
④ The best way to store information for future recall is to spend all your time studying without any self-assessment.
⑤ Long-term memory is formed immediately after studying without the need for testing or review.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 벼락치기가 왜 비효율적인지 설명하고 있습니다. 공부 직후에는 정보가 단기 기억(작업 기억)에 남아 있어 알고 있다는 착각을 주지만, 며칠 뒤 필요한 장기 기억으로 전이되지 않으며 반복적인 테스트 없이는 금방 사라진다고 언급합니다. 따라서 '벼락치기는 정보가 단기 기억에 신선하게 남아있기 때문에 알고 있다는 착각을 불러일으키지만, 반복 없이는 빠르게 사라진다'는 3번이 글의 내용과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 벼락치기는 정보의 장기 보존을 보장하는 가장 효과적인 방법이다.
② 작업 기억의 정보는 큰 손실 없이 며칠 동안 보존된다.
③ 벼락치기는 정보가 단기 기억에 남아 있어 안다는 착각을 만들지만, 반복 없이는 빠르게 사라진다.
④ 미래의 회상을 위해 정보를 저장하는 가장 좋은 방법은 자기 평가 없이 모든 시간을 공부에만 쓰는 것이다.
⑤ 장기 기억은 테스트나 복습 없이 공부 직후에 형성된다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "luminiferious ether"에 대한 설명으로 옳은 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of <u>luminiferous ether</u>, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① A type of energy discovered in the 19th century.
② A tool used by scientists to measure the speed of light.
③ A mysterious form of dark matter that exists in the universe.
④ A theoretical medium that scientists believed light traveled through.
⑤ A substance that was successfully proven to exist by physicists.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 luminiferous ether는 '빛이 이동할 매질이 있도록 우주를 채우고 있다고 생각되었던 신비로운 물질'로 설명됩니다. 하지만 이는 존재하지 않는 '검은 고양이'와 같은 개념으로 묘사되므로, 과학자들이 빛이 통과한다고 믿었던 이론적인 매질임을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 19세기에 발견된 에너지의 일종
② 과학자들이 빛의 속도를 측정하기 위해 사용한 도구
③ 우주에 존재하는 암흑 물질의 신비로운 형태
④ 과학자들이 빛이 통과한다고 믿었던 이론적인 매질
⑤ 물리학자들에 의해 존재가 성공적으로 증명된 물질

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 알맞은 접속사로 짝지은 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. (A)_____________ speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. (B)_____________, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 AI 보조 장치가 확산되고 있다고 언급한 뒤, 뒤에서 구체적인 예시(음성 인식 솔루션, 자막 시스템)를 들고 있으므로 'For instance(예를 들어)'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞 문장에서 AI의 번역 능력이 비원어민의 성과를 높인다고 한 뒤, 뒤에서 또 다른 긍정적인 측면(텍스트 생성기의 성과 향상)을 덧붙이고 있으므로 'In addition(게다가)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 예를 들어 / (B) 그러나
② (A) 예를 들어 / (B) 게다가
③ (A) ~일지라도 / (B) 그러므로
④ (A) 비록 ~이지만 / (B) 예를 들어
⑤ (A) 더욱이 / (B) 결과적으로

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, ①<u>takes</u> that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree ②<u>absorbs</u> only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn ③<u>increasing</u> phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon ─ leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services ④<u>provided by</u> each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now ⑤<u>being made</u> for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.explanation: ①번은 분사구문 자리입니다. takes를 taking으로 바꿔야 합니다. 주절의 동사(sequesters)가 이미 존재하고, 접섽사 없이 동사가 나올 수 없으며 고래가 탄소를 대기에서 제거하는 늬동의 관계이므로 현재분사 구문이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Our emotions are ①<u>thought</u> to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger has helped us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions ②<u>helps</u> us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us ③<u>to remember</u> an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess ④<u>are</u> thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they ⑤<u>didn't help</u> us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: ⑤번은 과거 사실에 대한 반대 가정을 나사내는 가정붕 과거완료 구문이 필요한 자리입니다. 주절에 would not have evolved(조동사 과거형 + have p.p.)가 쓰였으므로, if절에는 had not helped를 써야 합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: High education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. Between 2000 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students.Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which support lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
questions.summary_sentence: Higher education has transformed from an elite to a mass system, with participation rates nearly doubling between 2000 and 2014 While this expansion was intended to create a highly skilled workforce and (A)___________, the reality of mass education often emphasizes standardized assessment methods that (B)___________ the personal feedback that was once common in elite education systems.
options: ① focus on stduent grades / replace
questions.explanation: 이 글은 고등교육이 엘리트 시스템에서 대중 시스템으로 변화하면서 발생한 평가 방식의 모순을 다루고 있습니다. 이론적으로는 고등교육의 확장이 평생 학습을 지원하는 평가 방식을 도입해야 했으나(A: promote lifelong learning), 실제로는 효율성을 중시하는 대중 교육의 특성상 표준화된 평가가 이루어지며 과거 엘리트 교육에서 제공되던 개인적 피드백을 제한하게(B: limit) 되었다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 학생 성적에 집중하다 / 대체하다
② 노동력 훈련을 지원하다 / 장려하다
③ 평생 학습을 장려하다 / 제한하다
④ 시험의 중요성을 줄이다 / 지원하다
⑤ 학문적 경쟁을 증가시키다 / 개인화하다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Capuchins ─ New World Monkeys that live in large social groups ─ will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead ─ grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers ─ the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to _________________________________. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains ─ the cucumbers themselves ─ to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
options: ③ share the grapes with the other monkey
④ throw the cucumbers back at the experimenter
⑤ ignore the grapes and focus on the cucumbers
questions.explanation: 원숭이들은 동일한 노력에 대해 타인(다른 원숭이)이 더 나은 보상(포도)을 받는 것을 보면 불공정함을 느낍니다. 지문 마지막 부분에서 원숭이가 자신의 불쾌감을 표현하기 위해 얻은 이득(오이)조차 포기하려 한다는 점으로 보아, 받은 오이를 실험자에게 다시 던져버리는 행동이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 오이를 더 즐기다
② 돌 거래를 완전히 중단하다
③ 다른 원숭이와 포도를 나누다
④ 실험자에게 오이를 다시 던지다
⑤ 포도를 무시하고 오이에 집중하다

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 문맥상 밑줄 친 단어 ⓐ를 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 가장 적절한 단어를 글 속에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for functional purpose, flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most ⓐ<u>useless</u> properties.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 생물학자들이 상동성(homology)을 판단할 때 뼈의 수나 연결 방식처럼 기능과 상관없는 특징들을 공유한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 'useless(쓸모없는)'와 문맥상 의미가 가장 유사한 단어는 지문 내의 'nonfunctional'입니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 문맥상 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 의미로 가장 알맞은 것을 <보기>에서 골라 쓰시오.
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ⓐ<u>ends</u> like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents ⓑ<u>associated</u> with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism ⓒ<u>highlights</u> the fact that digital content creators ⓓ<u>face</u> real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity ⓔ<u>reconstructs</u> the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this ⓕ<u>sphere</u>, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
vocabulary_box: (B) goals or purposes that someone aims to achieve
(C) to build (something damaged or destroyed) again at a construction site
(D) a particular area of activity, influence, or interest
(E) to stop or finish, to no longer continue to happen or exist
(F) connected or linked with something in thought or meaning
(G) to confront or deal with a difficult situation or challenge directly
(H) to change or reshape the understanding or structure of something
(I) to be a very interesting, exciting, or important part of (something)
(J) the front part of the head that has the eyes, nose, and mouth on it
(K) to draw attention to or emphasize something as particularly important
questions.explanation: ⓐ ends: 목적 (B), ⓑ associated: 연관된 (F), ⓒ highlights: 강조하다 (K), ⓓ face: 직면하다 (G), ⓔ reconstructs: 재구성하다 (H), ⓕ sphere: 영역 (D)가 각각 적절한 영영 정의입니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 한글 해석을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: When you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show ─ whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire ─ you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans to communicate ─ it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. <u>텔레비전은 우리에게 세상은 빠르고, 중요한 것은 표면과 겉모습이라고 가르친다.</u>
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 주어진 단어들을 모두 포함할 것
밑줄 친 한글 해석에 대응할 것
주어진 단어는 중복 사용 가능
주어진 단어를 어법상 올바르게 변형할 수 있음
questions.answer: TV teaches us that the world is fast and what matters is surface and appearance.
questions.explanation: 주어 TV에 맞춰 teach를 teaches로 변형하고, 간접목적어 us 뒤에 명사절 접속사 that을 사용합니다. '세상은 빠르고'는 'the world is fast', '중요한 것은'은 관계대명사 what을 사용하여 'what matters'로 표현하며, 주격 보어로 'surface and appearance'를 연결합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 한글 해석을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오. [24년 9월 39번]
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does ─ this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. (A)<u>따라서, 지구 온난화가 해양 수온을 높임에 따라 용해된 산소의 양이 감소할 것은 자명하다.</u> This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 주어진 단어들을 반드시 포함할 것 (단어 형태 변형 가능)
<보기> 속 단어들 외 필요한 단어는 위의 지문 내에서만 찾을 것
밑줄 친 한글 해석에 대응할 것
questions.answer: as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease.
questions.explanation: 이 문장은 '~함에 따라'를 나타내는 접속사 'as'를 사용하여 시작합니다. '지구 온난화(global warming)가 해양 수온(the temperature of marine waters)을 높임(raises)에 따라'를 먼저 작성하고, '가주어-진주어(it is self-evident that...)' 구문을 활용하여 '용해된 산소의 양(the amount of dissolved oxygen)이 감소할 것(will decrease)은 자명하다'를 영작합니다. 지문 내의 'the amount of dissolved oxygen' 표현을 활용해야 합니다.

questions.question: 1. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)adjust의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. They lose their sense of security and may feel disoriented when their routine is disrupted and all that is familiar is taken away. Young children, ages 3-6, are particularly affected by a move. Their understanding at this stage is quite literal, and it is difficult for them to imagine beforehand a new home and their new room. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" It is important to establish a balance between validating children's past experiences and focusing on helping them (A)<u>adjust</u> to the new place. Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. This contributes to building a sense of community, which is essential for all children, especially those in transition.
options: ① to undergo a sudden change
② to become nearer to something
③ to change level, strength, or value frequently
④ to change in order to work or do better in a new situation
⑤ to try to be noticed, accepted, or chosen over something else
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'adjust'는 아이들이 새로운 환경에 적응하도록 돕는다는 맥락에서 사용되었습니다. 따라서 '새로운 상황에서 더 잘 작동하거나 행동하기 위해 변화하다'라는 의미인 ④번이 영영 풀이로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 갑작스러운 변화를 겪다
무언가에 더 가까워지다
수준, 강도 또는 가치를 빈번하게 바꾸다
새로운 상황에서 더 잘 작동하거나 행동하기 위해 변화하다
주목받거나, 인정받거나, 다른 것보다 선택받으려 노력하다

questions.passage: While moving is difficult for everyone, it is particularly stressful for children. Young children may have worries such as "Will I still be me in the new place?" and "Will my toys and bed come with us?" Children need to have opportunities to share their backgrounds in a way that respects their past as an important part of who they are. questions.explanation: 이 글은 이사가 아이들에게 주는 스트레스와 불안(고통)에 대해 설명하고, 아이들의 과거를 존중하며 새로운 곳에 적응할 수 있도록 돕는 방법(해결책)에 대해 다루고 있으므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 주제입니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 밑줄 친 "Monday Morning Quarterback"이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "<u>Monday Morning Quarterback</u>" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Students and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
options: ① a person who teaches and trains an athlete or performer
② someone who does a job that requires special training, education, or skill
③ a person who passes judgment on and criticizes something after the event
④ someone who manages or directs other people in a company or organization
⑤ a player who leads a team's attempts to score usually by passing the ball to other players
questions.explanation: 'Monday Morning Quarterback'은 주말 경기가 끝난 월요일 아침에 경기 결과에 대해 훈수를 두는 사람을 의미하며, 지문에서는 실제 전문 지식 없이 결과가 나온 후 비판하거나 조언하는 사람들을 가리킵니다. 따라서 ③번 '사건이 일어난 후에 판단을 내리고 비판하는 사람'이 정답입니다.
options_translation: 운동선수나 연기자를 가르치고 훈련시키는 사람
특별한 훈련, 교육 또는 기술이 필요한 일을 하는 사람
사건이 일어난 후에 판단을 내리고 비판하는 사람
회사나 조직에서 다른 사람들을 관리하거나 지시하는 사람
주로 다른 선수들에게 공을 패스하여 팀의 득점 시도를 이끄는 선수

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so ⓐ<u>terrified</u> they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that ⓑ<u>statistically</u>, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly ⓒ<u>accompany</u> your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of ⓓ<u>apprehension</u>. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on ⓔ<u>feelings</u>.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 맥락은 사람들이 감정에 휘둘리지 말고 논리에 근거하여 결정을 내려야 한다는 내용입니다. 마지막 문장에서 '감정(feelings)'에 근거하여 결정을 내리라고 하는 것은 논리적 흐름상 반대되는 내용이므로 'facts(사실)'이나 'logic(논리)'와 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 합니다. (참고: 원문상 ⓒ는 'involve'가 쓰였으나 보기에서는 ⓒ가 아닌 ⓔ가 명백한 오류입니다. 본문의 ⑤번 위치의 feelings가 틀린 단어입니다.)

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans ⓐ<u>underestimate</u> similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders ─ employing technical language to ⓑ<u>segregate</u> the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively ⓒ<u>comparable</u> to the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task ─ like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds ─ they write it off as ⓓ<u>nature</u>, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we ⓔ<u>coin</u> words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 동물을 자신들과 분리하고 인간의 우월함을 유지하기 위해 언어적 수단을 사용하는 방식을 설명합니다. ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 문맥상, 인간은 까마귀나 침팬지의 도구 제작 능력을 인간의 것과 '질적으로 다르다'고 해석함으로써 인간의 정의를 보호하려 합니다. 따라서 'comparable(비슷한, 비교할 만한)'은 문맥상 어색하며 'different(다른)'와 같은 표현이 적절합니다. 참고로 문제 발문은 지시 대상 차이를 묻고 있으나 밑줄은 어휘로 되어 있는 시험지 자체의 오류로 보이며, 내용상 어휘 문항으로 풀이됩니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providing students with relevant texts they will be interested in. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink. She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, ⓐ<u>including</u> a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and ⓑ<u>had had</u> significant problems with reading throughout their school years. While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and ⓒ<u>discovering</u> ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books." The pattern Fink discovered was ⓓ<u>that</u> all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered ⓔ<u>was</u> that they read voraciously to find out more.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 속한 문장에서 expected의 목적어인 that절 내의 동사구 구조를 살펴야 합니다. Fink는 그들이 독서를 피하고 그것(독서)을 우회할 방법을 찾았을 것이라고 예상했다는 내용이므로, had avoided와 병렬 구조를 이루어 had discovered(또는 discovered)가 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다. 'discovering'으로 쓰면 avoided의 목적어가 되어 '방법을 찾는 것을 피했다'는 잘못된 의미가 됩니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are ─ writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code, saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. (A) You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. (B) Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. (C) The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. (D) An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. (E) Period.
questions.insertion_sentence: However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 능력이 어떻게 정의되든 그것이 자아 가치의 유일한 결정 요소가 될 때 문제가 발생한다는 내용입니다. (A)와 (B)까지는 능력의 다양한 정의(지적 능력, 기술, 매력 등)를 설명하고 있으며, (C) 이후부터는 수행 능력이 사람을 평가하는 유일한 척도가 되어 발생하는 문제점(뛰어난 성과=뛰어난 사람)을 구체적으로 설명합니다. 따라서 전환점인 (C)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization.
ordered_passages: (A) The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making.

(B) The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them.
(C) Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 조직 내 부서마다 다른 문화가 존재할 수 있음을 언급합니다. (B)는 이에 이어 부서들이 각자의 편향된 시각('터널 시야')을 갖게 됨을 설명합니다. (A)는 이러한 조직 구조가 갈등을 유발할 수 있음을 도입하며 '기계적 구조'를 설명하고, (C)에서 이와 대조되는 '유기적 구조'의 특징을 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 9. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)them이 지칭하는 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of (A)<u>them</u>. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 자전거가 도시에서 더 인기를 얻음에 따라, 도시 계획가들이 더 많은 자전거들을 수용하기 위해 차선이나 거리 전체를 전환한다는 내용이 되어야 적절하므로 (A)의 them은 'bicycles'를 지칭합니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들
