questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A), (B)를 각각에 대해 주어진 조건을 지켜 모두 영어로 서술하시오.
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, (A)<u>AI는 일터에서 포괄성을 향상시켰던 것처럼 보인다</u>. (※조건: 'to'를 포함시킬 것) AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where interpersonal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, (B)<u>potentially having positive effects on the wages</u>. (※조건: 접속사가 포함된 부사절로 바꿀 것) For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
subjective_conditions: (A) AI는 일터에서 포괄성을 향상시켰던 것처럼 보인다. (※조건: 'to'를 포함시킬 것)
(B) potentially having positive effects on the wages (※조건: 접속사가 포함된 부사절로 바꿀 것)
questions.answer: (A) AI seems to have improved inclusiveness in the workplace(B) and it has potentially positive effects on their wages
questions.explanation: (A) '...한 것처럼 보인다'라는 의미를 표현하기 위해 'seem to' 구문을 사용합니다. 과거에 향상시켰던 사실이 현재 그렇게 보이는 것이므로 'to have improved'라는 완료 부정사 형태를 사용하는 것이 적절합니다.(B) 'potentially having positive effects on the wages'라는 분사구문을 접속사가 포함된 부사절로 전환하면 'as/and it potentially has positive effects on their wages'가 됩니다. 정답 예시에서는 문맥에 맞춰 'and it has potentially positive effects on their wages'로 작성되었습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글을 읽고, 아래 질문의 답을 주어진 조건을 지켜 영어로 서술하시오.
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
subjective_conditions: 본문 내에서 연속된 3개 이상의 단어를 그대로 쓰지 말 것.
다음 주어진 단어를 반드시 포함할 것 (필요시 단어의 형태를 바꿀 수 있음) → their / compose / familiar
답안지에는 빈칸에 해당하는 내용만 기입할 것.
questions.answer: they composed their works that were not familiar
questions.explanation: 베토벤이나 브람스 같은 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에는 환영받지 못했음에도 결국 위대해진 이유는, 그들이 당대에 익숙하지 않았던 새로운 형식이나 아이디어(독창성)를 담은 곡을 썼기 때문입니다. 조건에 따라 'their', 'compose', 'familiar'를 포함하고 본문의 3단어 이상 연속 사용을 피하여 문장을 완성하면 'they composed their works that were not familiar' (그들은 익숙하지 않은 그들의 작품들을 작곡했기 때문에)가 됩니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along ─ whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS ─ and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show ─ whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire ─ you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans to communicate ─ it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① What Makes Medium Content Powerful
② The Evolution of Books and Television
③ Television: The Sole Dominant Medium
④ Why Medium Content is Most Significant
⑤ Our Perception Transformed by Type of Medium
questions.explanation: 글 전체는 새로운 매체가 등장할 때마다 그것이 세상을 보는 '안경(goggles)' 역할을 하여 우리의 인식을 변화시킨다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 마샬 매클루언의 이론을 통해 정보의 내용보다 정보를 전달하는 매체 자체가 더 중요하며, 매체가 우리가 세상을 인식하는 방식을 규정한다는 점을 강조합니다. 따라서 ⑤ '매체 유형에 의해 변형된 우리의 지각'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 무엇이 매체 콘텐츠를 강력하게 만드는가
② 책과 텔레비전의 진화
③ 텔레비전: 유일하게 지배적인 매체
④ 왜 매체 콘텐츠가 가장 중요한가
⑤ 매체 유형에 의해 변형된 우리의 지각

questions.question: 13. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions ⓐ<u>helps</u> us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when ⓑ<u>triggered</u>, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very ⓒ<u>attentive</u>, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways ⓓ<u>how</u> they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not ⓔ<u>have evolved</u> with us.
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 ways와 관계부사 how는 함께 쓰일 수 없습니다. ways만 쓰거나, the way that, the way in which, 또는 how 단독으로 사용해야 합니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 how는 생략되거나 that 혹은 in which로 바뀌어야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 윗글을 읽고 유추할 수 없는 내용은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions ⓐ<u>helps</u> us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when ⓑ<u>triggered</u>, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very ⓒ<u>attentive</u>, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways ⓓ<u>how</u> they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not ⓔ<u>have evolved</u> with us.
options: ① Fear lowers the probability of death for humans.
② Social interactions with others enhance the possibility of survival.
③ Negative emotions are of no use to human evolution.
④ Emotions can be a motivator of human behavior.
⑤ Human emotions have been helpful for the survival of the human race.
questions.explanation: 지문은 감정(공포, 분노 등 부정적 감정 포함)이 종의 생존에 기여했기 때문에 존재한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 부정적 감정이 진화에 아무런 쓸모가 없다는 3번 선택지는 지문의 내용과 정반대되는 추론입니다.
options_translation: ① 공포는 인간의 사망 확률을 낮춰준다.
② 타인과의 사회적 상호작용은 생존 가능성을 높여준다.
③ 부정적인 감정은 인류 진화에 아무런 소용이 없다.
④ 감정은 인간 행동의 동기 부여 요인이 될 수 있다.
⑤ 인간의 감정은 인류의 생존에 도움이 되어 왔다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
options: ① The Benefits of Last-Minute Studying
② Why Cramming Works: A Student's Guide
③ Short-Term Memory: Key to Academic Success
④ Significance of Long-Term Memory in Studying
⑤ Innovative Study Techniques for Modern Learners
questions.explanation: 이 글은 벼락치기가 왜 비효율적인지 설명하며, 정보를 단기 기억이 아닌 장기 기억으로 옮기는 것의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '학습에 있어 장기 기억의 중요성'을 다룬 4번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 마지막 순간 공부(벼락치기)의 이점
② 벼락치기가 효과가 있는 이유: 학생 가이드
③ 단기 기억: 학업 성취의 핵심
④ 학습에 있어 장기 기억의 중요성
⑤ 현대 학습자를 위한 혁신적인 학습 기법

questions.question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself.
ordered_passages: (A) Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.

(B) However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people.

(C) Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 소셜 미디어 제작자들이 평범한 유명세를 원한다고 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 이들이 전통적인 엘리트 유명인과 달리 기술이 없다는 비판을 받는 점을 설명합니다. (B)에서 'However'를 통해 이러한 비판이 유명세의 의미를 재구성하는 현상을 놓치고 있음을 지적하며 평범한 유명인과 엘리트 유명인을 대조합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 평범한 유명세를 얻는 과정을 게임의 높은 점수를 얻는 것에 비유하며 글을 마무리하는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle.
ordered_passages: (A) Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener.(B) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them.(C) A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 교통을 진정시키는 대안으로 교통 제거를 제시하며 자전거와 보행자를 위한 도로망을 언급합니다. (B)의 'This'는 이러한 도로망 확보를 가리키며, 이로 인해 자전거 이용이 늘어나고 더 많은 도로를 자전거용으로 전환하게 된다는 흐름이 이어집니다. (A)에서는 그럼에도 불구하고 특정 차량을 위한 차로는 필요하며, 특히 배달 차량의 중요성을 언급하며 화제를 전환합니다. (C)는 배달 차량이 효율적이며 거주자들이 도보로 쇼핑할 수 있게 하여 도시를 더 친환경적으로 만든다는 구체적 이유를 설명하며 마무리합니다. 따라서 적절한 순서는 (B)-(A)-(C)입니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to _________________________________________.
options: ① a revival of marine biodiversity
② decreased occurrence of animals' migration
③ the reduced frequency of oxygen-shortage crisis
④ more frequent low-oxygen events that damage marine life
⑤ enhanced adaptability of marine organisms to ocean system
questions.explanation: 지문은 지구 온난화로 인한 해수 온도 상승이 용존 산소량 감소를 초래하며, 이것이 해양 생태계에 위협적이라는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 마지막 문장은 수중 산소 수치 하락이 전 세계 해양 생물의 서식지에 영향을 미치고 있음을 설명하므로, 빈칸에는 이로 인한 부정적인 결과인 '해양 생물에 피해를 주는 더 빈번한 저산소 현상'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 해양 생물 다양성의 회복
동물 이동 발생의 감소
산소 부족 위기 빈도의 감소
해양 생물에 피해를 주는 더 빈번한 저산소 현상
해양 생물의 해양 시스템에 대한 적응력 강화

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
options: ① Each department in an organization cannot help viewing things in a biased way.
② Tunnel vision hinders any department from seeing things unbiasedly.
③ Conflict may arise because of the organization's structure itself.
④ Mechanistic structures are hierarchical and go through many steps to make decision.
⑤ Organic structures have horizontal properties whose decision making is done by central executives.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 유기적 구조(Organic structures)는 본질적으로 수평적이며 의사 결정이 덜 중앙 집중화되어 있고(less centralized) 조직 전체에 퍼져 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 의사 결정이 중앙 경영진(central executives)에 의해 이루어진다는 ⑤번 선택지는 지문의 내용과 정반대이므로 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: 조직의 각 부서는 편향된 방식으로 사물을 바라볼 수밖에 없다.
터널 시야는 부서가 사물을 편견 없이 보는 것을 방해한다.
갈등은 조직 구조 자체 때문에 발생할 수 있다.
기계적 구조는 계층적이며 의사 결정을 위해 많은 단계를 거친다.
유기적 구조는 중앙 경영진에 의해 의사 결정이 이루어지는 수평적 특성을 가지고 있다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 밑줄 친 "to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat""가 문맥상 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult <u>to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat</u>." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① to learn how essentialism impacts our existence
② to discover hidden truths by careful observation
③ to pursue what is imagined but does not actually exist
④ to learn something valuable without any conscious effort
⑤ to neglect non-existent things to gain predictable evidence
questions.explanation: "''to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat(어두운 방에서 검은 고양이를 찾는 것은 매우 어렵다, 특히 고양이가 없을 때)"는 본질주의(essentialism)로 인해 실제로는 존재하지 않는 것을 찾으려 애쓰는 과학적 오류를 비유하고 있습니다. 지문에서 언급된 'luminiferous ether'처럼, 존재하지 않는 대상에 대해 이론을 세우고 실험하는 헛된 노력을 뜻하므로, '③ 상상되지만 실제로는 존재하지 않는 것을 추구하기'가 가장 적절한 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 본질주의가 우리의 존재에 어떤 영향을 미치는지 배우는 것
② 세심한 관찰을 통해 숨겨진 진실을 발견하는 것
③ 상상되지만 실제로는 존재하지 않는 것을 추구하는 것
④ 의식적인 노력 없이 가치 있는 것을 배우는 것
⑤ 예측 가능한 증거를 얻기 위해 존재하지 않는 것들을 무시하는 것

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.
questions.summary_sentence: As seen from the discovery of mirror neurons, human behavior is not limited to (A)___________ traits but can be acquired by (B)___________ as well.
questions.explanation: 거울 뉴런의 발견은 관찰을 통한 학습이 인간의 핵심적인 기능임을 설명합니다. 지문 마지막 부분의 'not restricted to the behavior we are born with'는 인간의 행동이 (A) '선천적인(innate)' 특성에 국한되지 않음을 의미하며, 'imitation' 및 'watching others'를 통해 지식이 습득된다는 점은 (B) '복제/모방(duplication)'을 통해 습득될 수 있음을 나타냅니다.
options_translation: ① 선천적인 ... 복제(모방)
② 합리적인 ... 관찰
③ 타고난 ... 보존
④ 근본적인 ... 보류
⑤ 본능적인 ... 애정

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 두 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals, and as a result they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties - the useful ones could have arisen independently in two lineages because they are useful (a nuisance to taxonomists called convergent evolution). We deduce that bat wings are really hands because we can see the wrist and count the joints in the fingers, and because that is not the only way that nature could have built a wing.
questions.summary_sentence: Analogous traits have a common function but evolved in different evolutionary paths, while homologous traits share a common ancestor that indicates their structure's (A)___________. The homologous traits are different from the analogous ones in that they have (B)___________ of their traits while the others do not.
questions.explanation: 본문은 생물학적 유사성을 '상사성(Analogous)'과 '상동성(Homologous)'으로 구분하여 설명하고 있습니다. 상사성은 기능은 같으나 진화 경로가 다른 것이고, 상동성은 공통 조상으로부터 유래하여 구조적 유사성을 지니는 것을 의미합니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 상동 형질이 공통 조상을 공유하여 구조적 '연관성(relatedness)'을 나타낸다는 점이 적절하며, (B)는 상동 형질이 조상의 앞다리 구조가 변형된 것(modification)이라는 본문의 내용을 토대로 '변형(alteration)'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 연관성 - 변형
② 광범위함 - 엄격함
③ 균일성 - 영구성
④ 상호 연결 - 견고함
⑤ 변화 - 우월함

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 32번]
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders - employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact": they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners": they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task - like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds - they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
options: ① Language: The Way to Dominate Over Other Animals
② Animal Intelligence: The Key Factor that Human Should Consider When Raising Animals
③ Primates: The Most Similar Species to Human in Terms of Cognitive Ability
④ Linguistic Discrimination: Valuable and Outstanding Traits for Human
⑤ A Distinctive Point that Distinguishes Animals from Humanity
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 언어적 기교를 사용하여 인간과 동물의 유사성을 축소하고, 동물을 인간보다 열등하게 규정함으로써 인간의 우월적 지위를 유지한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. Frans de Waal은 이를 '언어적 거세(linguistic castration)'라고 지칭했습니다. 따라서 '언어: 다른 동물을 지배하는 방법'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 언어: 다른 동물들을 지배하는 방법
② 동물 지능: 동물을 기를 때 인간이 고려해야 할 핵심 요소
③ 영장류: 인지 능력 면에서 인간과 가장 유사한 종
④ 언어적 차별: 인간에게 가치 있고 뛰어난 특성
⑤ 동물을 인류와 구별하는 독특한 점

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [23년 9월 36번]
questions.passage: May be you've heard this joke: "How do you eat an elephant?" The answer is "one bite at a time." So, how do you "build" the Earth? That's simple, too: one atom at a time. Atoms are the basic building blocks of crystals, and since all rocks are made up of crystals, the more you know about atoms, the better. Crystals come in a variety of shapes that scientists call habits. Common crystal habits include squares, triangles, and six-sided hexagons. Usually crystals form when liquids cool, such as when you create ice cubes. Many times, crystals form in ways that do not allow for perfect shapes. If conditions are too cold, too hot, or there isn't enough source material, they can form strange, twisted shapes. But when conditions are right, we see beautiful displays. Usually, this involves a slow, steady environment where the individual atoms have plenty of time to join and fit perfectly into what's known as the crystal lattice. This is the basic structure of atoms that is seen time after time.
options: ① Crystals are composed of atoms.
② There is a wide range of crystal habits.
③ The colder the temperature is, the more perfect crystals are made.
④ The crystal lattice needs a great deal of time.
⑤ Discovering a crystal lattice is common.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 결정(crystals)은 조건이 너무 춥거나 너무 뜨거울 때(too cold, too hot), 혹은 원료가 충분하지 않을 때 뒤틀린 모양으로 형성될 수 있다고 했습니다. 즉, 온도가 낮다고 해서 무조건 완벽한 결정이 만들어지는 것은 아닙니다. 완벽한 결정은 '적절한 조건(conditions are right)'과 원자들이 결합할 충분한 시간(plenty of time)이 있는 천천히 안정된 환경에서 만들어집니다.
options_translation: ① 결정은 원자로 구성된다.
② 결정 습성(모양)에는 광범위한 종류가 있다.
③ 온도가 더 낮을수록 더 완벽한 결정이 만들어진다.
④ 결정 격자는 많은 시간이 필요하다.
⑤ 결정 격자를 발견하는 것은 흔하다.

questions.question: 7. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 40번]
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat.
ordered_passages: (A) Even though she is still getting "paid" equally the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair.

(B) If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter.
(C) Furthermore, she is unwilling to accept all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 카푸친 원숭이가 돌을 주고 먹이를 받는 거래를 한다는 내용입니다. (B)에서 두 마리의 원숭이에게 처음에는 오이를 주다가 한 마리에게만 포도를 주는 실험 상황을 설정합니다. (A)에서 한 마리에게만 더 좋은 보상(포도)을 주는 것이 다른 원숭이(오이를 받는 원숭이)에게 불공정함을 느끼게 함을 설명합니다. (C)에서 한 걸음 더 나아가(Furthermore) 자신의 불쾌감을 표현하기 위해 오이조차 받기를 거부한다는 내용으로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 8. To summarize the content of the following passage in one sentence, fill in the blanks ⓐ and ⓑ by finding words in the passage above. [24년 9월 40번]
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat.(A) Even though she is still getting "paid" equally the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair.(B) If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter.(C) Furthermore, she is unwilling to accept all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.summary_sentence: When the Capuchin realizes the reward is not given ⓐ__________ compared to another monkey, she refuse to ⓑ__________ her rewards even though she has the same amount of rewards to express her feelings about the treatment.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 요지는 카푸친 원숭이가 다른 개체와의 비교를 통해 보상이 불공평하다고 느끼면 보상 자체를 거부한다는 것입니다. (A)의 'paid equally'에서 'equally(평등하게)'를, (C)의 'unwilling to accept'에서 'accept(받아들이다)'를 찾아 빈칸을 완성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of ⓐ<u>similarity</u>. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose ⓑ<u>independently</u> in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a ⓒ<u>common</u> function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very ⓓ<u>different</u> functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share ⓔ<u>functional</u> traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 생물학에서 '유사성'을 두 가지(유사성과 상동성)로 구분하여 설명하고 있습니다. '상동성(homologous)' 형질은 기능은 다를 수 있으나 공통 조상으로부터 기인하여 동일한 기관임을 나타내는 공통 구조를 가집니다. 본문에서 박쥐의 날개와 말의 앞다리는 기능이 매우 다르지만 공통 조상의 앞다리가 변형된 것이므로, 뼈의 수나 연결 방식과 같은 '구조적(structural)' 특성을 공유한다고 보아야 합니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 'functional(기능적인)'은 문맥상 어색하며 'structural' 같은 단어로 대체되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. Between 2000 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialized workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should _____________________, initiating approaches to assessment which enables lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
options: ① damage the power of the examinations justifying their approval
② reinforce the role of examination in selection and control of students
③ reduce the influence of the evaluation when recruiting qualified workers
④ reduce the emphasis on examination in selecting and evaluating students
⑤ intensify the credibility and reliability of the examinations to sort out the students
questions.explanation: 고등 교육이 엘리트 시스템에서 대중 시스템으로 확장됨에 따라, 이론적으로는 숙련된 노동력을 개발하기 위해 학생을 선발하고 평가할 때 기존의 시험 중심적 사고에서 벗어나 평생 학습과 피드백에 집중하는 방식으로 나아가야 한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 실제로는 대규모 인원을 평가하기 위해 효율적인 표준화 시험에 의존하게 되는 모순이 발생한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 이론적인 이상향에 해당하는 '선발과 평가에 있어 시험에 대한 강조를 줄이는 것'이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 승인을 정당화하는 시험의 권한을 손상시키다
② 학생의 선발과 통제에 있어 시험의 역할을 강화하다
③ 자격을 갖춘 근로자를 채용할 때 평가의 영향력을 줄이다
④ 학생을 선발하고 평가하는 데 있어 시험에 대한 강조를 줄이다
⑤ 학생들을 가려내기 위한 시험의 신뢰도와 타당성을 강화하다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "engineers of marine ecosystems."가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO₂ a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "<u>engineers of marine ecosystems</u>." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
options: ① playing a crucial role in maintaining ecological balance of marine environment
② reserving a marine eco-system by using strategies to ensure their own survival
③ maintaining a healthy marine eco-system in harmony with mammals
④ keeping a balance between marine and fresh water eco-system
⑤ reducing conflicts between whales and other marine lives
questions.explanation: 고래가 배설물을 통해 바다림 비료화하고 식물성 플랑크톤을 줝가시켜 탄소림 격리하는 등 해양 생태계에서 중요한 역할을 한다는 내용이므로, ①이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 해양 환경의 생태계적 균형을 유지하는 데 중요한 역할을 함
② 자신들의 생존을 밑받침하기 윤한 전늬을 사용하여 해양 생태계림 보존함
③ 포유류와 조화림 이루며 건강한 해양 생태계림 유지함
④ 해양 생태계와 담수 생태계 사이의 균형을 유지함
⑤ 고래와 다른 해양 생물 간의 갈등을 줄윰

questions.question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흤름과 관련이 없는 문장은
questions.passage: ⓐ<u>Every time a new medium comes along - whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses</u>. ⓑ<u>This illustrates why it is essential to educate children and adolescents on selecting suitable TV programs</u>. ⓒ<u>Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently</u>. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show - whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. ⓓ<u>That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message</u>. ⓔ<u>It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself</u>. TV teaches you that the world is fast: that it's about surfaces and appearances.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 새로운 매체가 등장할 때마다 세상을 바라밴는 방식이 달늼진다는 Marshall McLuhan의 주장(매체가 메시지다)에 대한 글입니다. ⓑ은 아이들에게 적절한 TV 프로그램을 선택하도록 교육하는 걃이 필요하다는 내용으로 전체 흤름과 가장 거리가 멀습니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 적절한 단어 하나를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just _____________.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장에서 결정을 내릴 때 단순한 감정이 아닌 사실에 근거해야 한다고 조언하고 있습니다. 지문 중간에 사람들의 운전 결정이 논리가 아닌 감정(emotion)에 근거한다고 언급되어 있으므로 빈칸에 적절한 단어는 emotion입니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Sensory nerves have ⓐ<u>specialized</u> endings in the tissues that pick up a particular sensation. If, for example, you step on a sharp object such as a pin, nerve endings in the skin will transmit the pain sensation up your leg, up and along the spinal cord to the brain. While the pain itself is unpleasant, it is in fact acting as a ⓑ<u>defensing</u> mechanism for the foot Within the brain, nerves will connect to the area that controls speech, so that you may well shout 'ouch' or something rather less ⓒ<u>courteous</u>. They will also connect to motor nerves that travel ⓓ<u>leisurely</u> down the spinal cord, and to the muscles in your leg that now ⓔ<u>contract</u> quickly to lift your foot away from the painful object. Sensory and motor nerves control almost all functions in the body - from the beating of the heart to the movement of the gut, sweating and just about everything else.
questions.explanation: 통증을 느끼면 발을 즉시 떼기 위해 척수를 타고 신호가 빠르게 전달되어야 합니다. 따라서 '여유롭게, 느긋하게'라는 뜻의 leisurely는 문맥상 적절하지 않으며 '빠르게(back)' 혹은 '즉각적으로'의 의미를 가진 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers ___________________. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie: he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact. he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
options: ④ try to be famous by any means
⑤ write as many songs as they can
questions.explanation: 베토벤이나 스트라빈스키 같은 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 이해받지 못한 이유는 그들의 음악적 아이디어가 완전히 새롭고 생소했기 때문입니다. 반면 살리에리는 훌륭한 작곡가였음에도 불구하고 그의 작품이 당시 다른 사람들의 곡과 비슷하고 독창적이지 않았기에 위대한 작곡가의 반열에 오르지 못했습니다. 따라서 위대한(효과적인) 작곡가는 남들과 다른 독창적인, 즉 '독립적인 관점을 견지한다'는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 가장 쉬운 경로를 추구한다
② 오직 경쟁만을 위해 노력한다
③ 독립적인 관점을 견지한다
④ 무슨 수를 써서라도 유명해지려 노력한다
⑤ 가능한 한 많은 곡을 쓴다

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. (A) They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb. "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." (B) History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. (C) Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. (D) The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: It beautifully sums up the search for essences.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'It'은 Stuart Firestein이 인용한 '어두운 방에서 존재하지 않는 검은 고양이를 찾는 것'에 관한 격언을 가리킵니다. 이 격언이 본질(essences)을 찾으려는 과학자들의 헛된 노력을 잘 요약해준다는 내용이므로, 격언이 처음 소개된 문장 바로 뒤인 (B)에 위치하는 것이 문맥상 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)에 대한 설명 중 어색한 것의 개수는?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. (A)<u>It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does</u> - this is one reason (B)<u>that</u> cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively (C)__________ populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that (D)<u>해양에서 용존 산소의 양이 반세기가 넘는 기간 동안 감소하고 있는 중이다</u>. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water (E)<u>have</u> the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
vocabulary_box: (가) 'It was Minji that met you at the church yesterday.'의 밑줄 친 it~that은 (A)의 it~that과 쓰임이 같다.
(나) 밑줄 친 (B)를 why로 대체하여도 문제가 없다.
(다) 밑줄 친 (C)에 poorly가 들어가는 것은 적절하다.
(라) (D)를 영작하면 'the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century'이다.
questions.explanation: (가) (A)의 'it~that'은 가주어-진주어 구문이지만, 예문은 it~that 강조 구문이므로 쓰임이 다릅니다. 따라서 어색한 설명입니다. (마) 문장의 주어는 'Falling oxygen levels'로 복수 명사구이므로 동사 'have'는 어법상 올바릅니다. 이를 'has'로 고쳐야 한다는 설명은 어색합니다. (나) 'the reason why'에서 why 대신 관계부사 대용의 that을 쓸 수 있으므로 적절합니다. (다) 열대 바다는 차가운 바다에 비해 생명체가 적게 분포하므로 'poorly(부족하게, 불충분하게)'가 들어가는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다. (라) 주어진 한국어 문장을 현재완료 진행형을 사용하여 정확하게 영작한 것입니다. 따라서 어색한 설명은 (가), (마) 총 2개입니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 단어의 영영 풀이로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their __________ is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
options: ① the fact of being in a particular place
② a state that is not present or doesn't exist
③ giving a lot of attention or energy to something
④ a particular feeling or mood created by something
⑤ a state in which there is not enough of something
questions.explanation: 빈칸에 들어갈 단어는 'presence(존재, 참석, 있음)'입니다. 지문에서 '단지 그들과 함께 있는 것(presence)만으로도 유익하다'는 맥락이므로, '특정한 장소에 있다는 사실'을 의미하는 ①번이 가장 적절한 영영 풀이입니다.
options_translation: ① 특정한 장소에 있다는 사실
② 존재하지 않거나 없는 상태
③ 무언가에 많은 주의나 에너지를 쏟는 것
④ 무언가에 의해 만들어진 특정한 감정이나 분위기
⑤ 무언가가 충분하지 않은 상태

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어가기에 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, Al can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. Al-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. (A)__________, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. Al can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, Al's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. (B)__________, recent developments in Al-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 AI 보조 기구가 널리 보급되고 있다고 언급한 뒤, 뒤 문장에서 구체적인 사례(음성 인식 솔루션, 실시간 자막 시스템 등)를 들고 있으므로 'For instance(예를 들어)'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞 문장에서 비모국어 사용자의 성과를 향상시킬 수 있다는 긍정적 측면을 언급한 뒤, 뒤 문장에서 저숙련 노동자의 성과를 향상시킨다는 또 다른 긍정적 측면을 덧붙이고 있으므로 'Moreover(게다가)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 즉 - 그러나
② 사실 - 그럼에도 불구하고
③ 예를 들어 - 게다가
④ 반대로 - 뿐만 아니라
⑤ 반면에 - 그렇지 않으면

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path. Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.*vocalcords: 성대 **frequency: 주파수
options: ① how people perceive their own speech
② voice recognition technology in everyday life
③ importance of tone in effective communication
④ understanding personal voice and its acoustics
⑤ differences between perceived and recorded voice
questions.explanation: 이 글은 자신의 목소리를 녹음해서 들었을 때 왜 다르게 들리는지에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 본문에 따르면 우리가 말을 할 때 목소리를 인식하는 경로는 외부 공기를 통한 경로와 뼈를 통한 내부 경로 두 가지가 있습니다. 내부 경로를 통해서는 낮은 주파수가 강조되어 스스로에게는 목소리가 더 깊고 풍부하게 들리지만, 녹음된 목소리는 외부 경로만을 통해 전달되므로 평소 듣던 자신의 목소리와 다르게 느껴집니다. 따라서 주제는 '인지되는 목소리와 녹음된 목소리의 차이'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들이 자신의 말을 인식하는 방법
② 일상생활에서의 음성 인식 기술
기 효과적인 의사소통에서 어조의 중요성
④ 개인의 목소리와 그 음향학에 대한 이해
⑤ 인지되는 목소리와 녹음된 목소리의 차이

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: All the actors on the stage ⓐ<u>were</u> focused on their acting. Then, suddenly, Arthur fell into the corner of the stage. Jeevan immediately approached Arthur and found his heart wasn't beating. Jeevan began CPR. Jeevan worked silently, ⓑ<u>glancing</u> sometimes at Arthur's face. He thought, "Please, start breathing again, please." Arthur's eyes were closed. Moments later, an older man in a grey suit ⓒ<u>appeared</u>, swiftly kneeling beside Arthur's chest. "I'm Walter Jacobi. I'm a doctor." He announced with a calm voice. Jeevan wiped the sweat off his forehead. With ⓓ<u>combined</u> efforts, Jeevan and Dr. Jacobi successfully revived Arthur. Jeevan felt relieved when he finally got Arthur ⓔ<u>breathed</u> again. Arthur's eyes slowly opened. Finally, Jeevan was able to hear Arthur's breath again, thinking to himself, "Thank goodness. You're back."
questions.explanation: ⑤번 'got'은 준사역동사로 쓰였으며, 목적어(Arthur)와 목적격 보어의 관계가 능동(Arthur가 숨을 쉬는 것)이므로 과거분사 'breathed'가 아닌 'to breathe' 또는 현재분사 'breathing'을 써야 문법적으로 옳습니다. 나머지는 ① 주어 복수 일치(were), ② 분사구문(glancing), ③ 자동사 과거형(appeared), ④ 명사 수식 과거분사(combined)로 적절하게 쓰였습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. It means that _____________________________________. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
options: ① just to be in their presence is advantageous
② merely thinking about their presence is harmful
③ associating with other persons leads to negativity
④ neutral thought forms provide the greatest benefit
⑤ choosing to engage with one's struggle is beneficial
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 무력감이나 부정적인 상태에서 벗어나기 위해 문제를 해결한 사람들(긍정적인 에너지를 가진 사람들)과 함께 있는 것이 도움이 된다고 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 'hanging out with the winners'나 긍정적 에너지의 전이 등에 대한 설명을 미루어 볼 때, 그들의 존재만으로도 유익하다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 단지 그들과 함께 있는 것만으로도 이롭다
② 단지 그들의 존재를 생각하는 것만으로도 해롭다
③ 다른 사람들과 어울리는 것은 부정성으로 이어진다
④ 중립적인 사고 형태가 가장 큰 혜택을 제공한다
⑤ 자신의 고군분투에 관여하기로 선택하는 것이 유익하다

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. AI-powered (A)[associative / assistive] devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can (B)[hinder / facilitate] communication with colleagues and access to jobs where interpersonal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of nonnative speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly (C)[improve / diminish] the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.*dysarthric: (신경 장애로 인한) 구음(構音) 장애의
questions.explanation: 문맥상 (A) 장애가 있는 근로자를 돕는 장치이므로 '보조하는' 뜻의 assistive가 적절합니다. (B) 음성 인식 솔루션이나 자막 시스템은 의사소통을 '용이하게' 하므로 facilitate가 적절합니다. (C) AI 기반 텍스트 생성기가 저숙련 노동자의 성과를 '향상시킬' 수 있다는 긍정적인 맥락이므로 improve가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 연합의 / 용이하게 하다 / 줄이다
② 보조의 / 용이하게 하다 / 향상시키다
③ 보조의 / 용이하게 하다 / 줄이다
④ 연합의 / 방해하다 / 향상시키다
⑤ 보조의 / 방해하다 / 줄이다

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 31번]
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. it would not be easy (A)[of / for] people to appreciate that new piece of art. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely (B)[overshadowing / overshadowed] by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he neither gained much fame nor (C)[risen / rose] above being a second-in-command because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.*a second-in-command 2인자
questions.explanation: (A) 가주어 it과 진주어 to appreciate 사이에서 의미상 주어를 나타낼 때, 형용사 easy는 성격 형용사가 아니므로 전치사 for를 사용합니다. (B) 살리에리가 모차르트에 의해 '가려진' 수동의 관계이므로 과거분사 overshadowed가 적절합니다. (C) neither A nor B 구조에서 gained와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 과거 시제인 rose가 적절합니다.

(A) for - (B) 가려진 - (C) 올라갔다(과거형)

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 35번]
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our textbook or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it is present in our short-term storage space ... but this short-term section has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds or minutes, working memory already starts disappearing, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you retest your knowledge, memory vanishes. To get information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying.
questions.summary_sentence: Cramming is seen as an effective learning strategy because we (A)__________ working memory with long-term knowledge, but to retain information, it's essential to study and (B)__________ rather than solely studying.
questions.explanation: 우리가 벼락치기가 효과적이라고 착각하는 이유는 단기적인 작업 기억에 있는 정보를 장기 기억과 (A)혼동하기(confuse) 때문입니다. 하지만 정보를 오래 유지하기 위해서는 단순히 공부만 하기보다 (B)자가 테스트(self-test)를 하는 것이 필수적입니다.
options_translation: (A) 묵살하다 - (B) 복습하다
(A) 혼동하다 - (B) 자가 테스트하다
(A) 방치하다 - (B) 간과하다
(A) 묵살하다 - (B) 상기하다
(A) 혼동하다 - (B) 예습하다

questions.question: 11. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [24년 9월 25번]
questions.passage: The above graph shows per capita CO2 emissions from coal, oil, and gas by countries in 2022. ①The United States had the highest total per capita CO2 emissions of three major sources, largely due to its high oil & gas consumption. ②South Korea's per capita CO2 emissions of gas were three times larger than those of oil in South Africa. ③Brazil had the lowest total per capita CO2 emissions among the five countries shown. ④South Africa's per capita CO2 emissions from coal were nearly double those of Germany. ⑤Germany's per capita CO2 emissions from coal were higher than those from oil.

questions.question: 19. 다음 2024 Save the Whale Save the Earth Poster Contest에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.7점]

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle.
ordered_passages: (A) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them.

(C) Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener.

(B) For instance, a tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 자전거와 보행자를 위한 도로 확보를 언급한 후, (A)에서 이것이 자전거 이용을 독려하여 도시 계획의 변화를 가져온다는 내용을 설명합니다. (C)에서 하지만(Nevertheless) 여전히 차량 도로가 필요함을 역설하며 배달 차량의 중요성을 언급하고, (B)에서 그 이유로 배달 차량의 효율성(For instance)을 구체적 예시로 들어 설명하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. It doesn't matter ⓐ<u>whether</u> it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS. Each set of goggles you put on ⓑ<u>makes</u> you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show, you get used ⓒ<u>to seeing</u> the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in ⓓ<u>it</u> a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. McLuhan argued ⓔ<u>that</u> is important is the way information gets to you than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장에서 argued의 목적어 역할을 하는 절에서 주어가 빠진 불완전한 문장이 오고 있으므로, 접속사 that이 아닌 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what이 되어야 합니다. 'What is important'는 '중요한 것은'이라는 의미로 절의 주어 역할을 합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
questions.summary_sentence: In terms of fame, elite celebrities are believed to be engaged with (A)__________, while social media celebrities (B)__________ a moderate level of popularity.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 엘리트 유명인은 신비감과 계층적 거리감(hierarchical distance), 타고난 재능과 계급(class)으로 특징지어진다고 하였으므로 (A)에는 '우월성(superiority)'이 적절합니다. 반면 소셜 미디어 유명인은 일반 대중과의 상호작용을 통해 대중적인 인기를 얻는 것을 목표로 하므로 (B)에는 '선호하다(prefer)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우선순위 / 우려
② 감사함 / 추구하다
③ 우월함 / 선호하다
④ 다양성 / 재구성하다
⑤ 권위 / 제한하다

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. Furthermore, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
options: ① Behavioral Studies on Capuchins' Feeding Habits
② Capuchin Monkeys and the Perception of Fairness
③ Capuchin Monkeys and Their Role in the Ecosystem
④ Capuchins and Their Relationship with Humans in Captivity
⑤ The Intelligence of Capuchin Monkeys in Problem-Solving Tasks
questions.explanation: 이 글은 카푸친 원숭이가 타인(다른 원숭이)과 비교하여 보상이 불공평하다고 느낄 때 분노를 표현하며 보상을 거부한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '공정함에 대한 인식'을 다룬 ②번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 카푸친 원숭이의 식습관에 관한 행동 연구
② 카푸친 원숭이와 공정함에 대한 인식
③ 카푸친 원숭이와 생태계에서의 역할
④ 카푸친 원숭이와 포획 상태에서의 인간과의 관계
⑤ 문제 해결 과제에서의 카푸친 원숭이의 지능

questions.question: 16. 다음 글을 읽고 두 사람이 나눈 대화이다. ⓐ~ⓔ 중 지문의 내용을 제대로 이해하지 못한 부분은? [24년 9월 31번]
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amdeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous non-great composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.A: 위대한 작곡가들이 자기 시대에는 오해받고 이해받지 못했다고 하던데, 그 이유가 뭘까?B: ⓐ<u>그건 그들이 새로운 음악적 아이디어를 시도했기 때문이야. 베토벤이나 스트라빈스키 같은 작곡가들의 음악이 너무 새로워서 아무도 이해하지 못했대</u>.A: ⓑ<u>그런데 그게 그들을 위대하게 만든 요소이기도 한거지?</u>B: 그렇지. 영화 아마데우스 생각나네. ⓒ<u>살리에리도 좋은 작곡가였지만, 그의 음악은 다른 사람들과 크게 다르지 않았어</u>. ⓓ<u>모차르트에 가려지기도 했고 말이야</u>.A: ⓔ<u>그래, 살리에리의 작품은 독창적이지 않았지</u>.B: 맞아, 자기만의 아이디어가 있어야 사람들이 결국 그 가치를 인정하게 되는 거지.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 베토벤이나 스트라빈스키의 음악이 너무 새로워서 '아무도(Not everyone)' 이해하지 못했다는 것은 아닙니다. 지문에서는 'Not everyone could understand(모두가 이해할 수 있었던 것은 아니다)'라고 기술되어 있으므로, 일부는 이해했을 가능성을 배제하지 않습니다. '아무도 이해하지 못했다'는 절대적인 표현은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다. (참고: 문제의 공식 정답표상 1번으로 되어 있으나, 대화 내용 중 ⓐ의 '아무도'가 지문의 'Not everyone'과 미세하게 상충함을 지적한 것으로 보입니다.)
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [24년 9월 23번]
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. ⓐ<u>AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities</u>. ⓑ<u>For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary</u>. ⓒ<u>AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects</u>. ⓓ<u>There are concerns that AI could eventually replace human workers entirely, leading to widespread unemployment and economic instability</u>. ⓔ<u>For example, AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace</u>. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 AI가 노동 시장에서 불리한 위치에 있는 사람들(장애인, 저숙련 노동자, 비모어 화자 등)의 접근성과 포용성을 높여준다는 긍정적인 측면을 다루고 있습니다. 그러나 ④번 문장은 AI가 인간 노동자를 완전히 대체하여 실업과 경제적 불안정을 초래할 수 있다는 부정적인 우려를 언급하고 있으므로 글의 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [24년 9월 25번]
questions.passage: Per Capita CO₂ Emissions from Three Major Sources in 2022 The above graph shows per capita CO₂ emissions from coal, oil, and gas by countries in 2022. ⓐThe United States had relatively low coal emissions compared to other countries except Brazil but had much higher emissions from oil and gas, making it the country with the highest total CO₂ emissions. ⓑSouth Korea relied heavily on coal, with coal being the biggest source of its per capita emissions, while gas emissions were lower. ⓒGermany's oil emissions were lower than South Korea's, but its coal emissions were almost as high as those in the Univted States. ⓓSouth Africa had higher per capita emissions from coal than South Korea, but its coal emissions were not more than double those of Germany. ⓔIn Brazil, oil emissions were much lower than in other countries, and gas was the main source of CO₂ emissions per capita.

② ⓑ

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 9월 30번]
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities have designated large networks of streets and lanes exclusively for cyclists, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. (A) This encourages more people to choose biking over driving, which in turn makes the streets safer. (B) As cycling grows in popularity, urban planners can repurpose additional car langes and streets for bike use. (D) A single delivery truck, packed with goods, is far more efficient than multiple hybrid cars carrying smaller loads. (E) By delivering goods to local stores, these trucks help smaller, conveniently located shops thrive, allowing residents to walk rather than drive to get their necessities.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, even in the most bike-friendly cities, motor vehicle lanes are still needed for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 자전거 친화적인 도시라 할지라도 택시, 비상 차량, 배달 트럭 등을 위한 차선이 여전히 필요하다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C) 앞부분까지는 도시 내 차를 없애고 자전거 도로를 늘리는 긍정적인 측면을 설명하고 있으며, (C) 뒷부분부터는 '배달 차량(delivery vehicles)'이 환경 친화적인 도시를 만드는 데 핵심적인 역할을 한다는 구체적인 설명이 시작됩니다. 따라서 자전거 도로 중심의 변화 속에서도 특정 목적의 차량과 도로가 필요하다는 전환점이 되는 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 41-42번]
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. Between 2000 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
questions.summary_sentence: Higher education has shifted from an elite to a mass system, nearly doubling participation rates. This expansion, aimed at developing a skilled workforce, has caused a(n) (A)__________ on standardized exams and grades, (B)__________ the personalized feedback once common in elite systems.
questions.explanation: 대중 고등 교육 시스템으로 변화하면서 효율적인 평가를 위해 표준화된 시험과 성적에 의존(reliance/focus)하게 되었으며, 이는 과거 엘리트 시스템에서 흔했던 개인 맞춤형 피드백을 대체(replacing)하거나 밀어내는 결과를 초래했습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '의존'을 뜻하는 reliance, (B)에는 '대체하는'을 뜻하는 replacing이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 의존 / 유지하는 것
② 저항 / 인수하는 것
③ 집중 / 보존하는 것
④ 무관심 / 변화시키는 것
⑤ 의존 / 대체하는 것

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것끼리 짝지어진 것은? [24년 9월 22번]
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and ⓐ<u>expressing</u> positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when ⓑ<u>triggered</u>, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to ⓒ<u>threatened</u> stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways ⓓ<u>which</u> they activate our system, the specific emotions we possess ⓔ<u>are</u> thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. As they have helped us adapt and survive, they have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: ⓒ는 '위협적인 자극'이라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 현재분사인 'threatening'으로 고쳐야 합니다(stimuli가 위협을 주는 주체이므로). ⓓ는 뒤에 완전한 문장(they activate our system)이 오고 선행사가 ways이므로 관계부사 how를 대신하는 that이나 in which로 고쳐야 합니다. ways와 how는 함께 쓸 수 없습니다. ⓐ는 동명사 주어로 적절하며, ⓑ는 (it is) triggered의 분사구문으로 적절하고, ⓔ는 주어 emotions와 일치하는 복수 동사로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO₂ a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.

questions.question: 23. 다음 그띘 흠름으로 밴아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 설절한 곳은?

(C) From this point, his path resembles the paths of teen pop stars of previous generations who were discovered on televised talent competitions and were turned into stars by the machinery of the pop music industry. (D) While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. questions.question: 24. 다음 그띘 묑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 스임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Why do we have the illusion that cramming for an exam is the best learning strategy? Because we are unable to differentiate between the various sections of our memory. Immediately after reading our text book or our class notes, information is fully present in our mind. It sits in our conscious working memory, in an active form. We feel as if we know it, because it ⓐ<u>occupies</u> our short-term storage space ... but this short-term sections has nothing to do with the long-term memory that we will need in order to recall the same information a few days later. After a few seconds of minutes, working memory already starts ⓑ<u>fading</u>, and after a few days, the effect becomes enormous: unless you reset your knowledge, memory vanishes. To ⓒ<u>transfer</u> information into long-term memory, it is essential to study the material, then test yourself, rather than spend all your time studying. It's easy to put these ideas into practice on your own. All you have to do is prepare flash cards: on one side, you write a question, and on the other, the answer. To test yourself, draw the cards one after the other, and for each card, try to remember the answer (prediction) before checking it by turning to the other side (error feedback). If you get the wrong answer, put the card back toward the top of the pile - this will force you to ⓓ<u>revisit</u> the same information soon. If you get the right answer, put the card at the bottom of the pile: there is no immediate need to study it again, but it will reappear sooner or later, at a time when forgetting will have ⓔ<u>stopped</u> taking effect.
questions.explanation: 그래프카드 학습법에서 맞힌 카드는 더 나중에 보게 되는데, 이는 '망각이 효력을 발휴하기 시작할 때(잊어버릴 때쯤)' 다시 등장하게 하는 것이 효과적입니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 stopped는 started 또는 begun 등으로 바갸어야 합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 주제와 관련 있는 예시끼리 짝지어진 것은?
questions.passage: The discovery of mirror neurons has profoundly changed the way we think of a fundamental human capacity, learning by observation. As children we learn a lot by observing what our parents and friends do. Newborns, in the first week of life, have an inborn tendency to stick out their tongue if their parents stick out theirs. Such imitation is not perfect. You may not see the tongue stick out each time you stick yours out at your newborn, but if you do it many times, the tongue will come out more often than if you do something different. Babies babble and later start to imitate the sounds their parents produce. Later still, they play with vacuum cleaners and hammers in imitation of their parents. Our modern cultures, in which we write, speak, read, build spaceships and go to school, can work only because we are not restricted to the behavior we are born with or learn by trial and error. We can learn a lot by simply watching others.␀ Novice builders quickly develop their abilities by shadowing more skilled workers.␁ Young athletes improve their skills by relying on inborn abilities.␂ In Stone Age, people learned to make blades by copying what a more experienced person did.␃ An individual develops effective stress management techniques by reflecting on personal experiences and challenges.␄ Scientists discovery new principles by conducting experiments and analyzing the results.
questions.explanation: ␀ ␁ ␂ ␃ ␄ 중에서 중요한 개념은 '관찰을 통한 학습(learning by observation)'이며, ␀(초밴 건설 노동자가 숑련공을 관찰하며 배우는 것)과 ␂(석기 시차 숑련된 사람을 모방하여 칼날을 만들었댘 것)이 이와 일치합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. -Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and pay attention to their most useless properties, because the useful ones could have arisen independently in two lineages because they are useful.*lineage: 혈통
questions.summary_sentence: Biologists distinguish between analogous traits, which have a common function but evolved (A)__________, and homologous traits, which may or may not have a common function despite their (B)__________ lineage(s); to tell the two apart, biologists often analyze the comprehensive structure of the organ and focus on (C)__________ features.
questions.explanation: 사상 형질(Analogous) 같은 기능을 가지지만 진화적으로는 '독립적으로/separately'발생한 것이고, 혼상 형질(Homologous)은 '공통의/common' 조상을 가지고 있으며 기능과 무관한 '비기능적인/nonfunctional' 특성을 공유하므로 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 불가분적으로 - 같은 - 쓸모없는
② 별개로 - 공통의 - 비기능적인
③ 개별적으로 - 다른 - 유용한
④ 의존적으로 - 별개의 - 기능적인
⑤ 독립적으로 - 공유된 - 필요한

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively ①<u>poorly</u> populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to ②<u>continue</u> to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms. Researchers found that the rate at which oxygen is decreasing in the oceans is fast, beyond what they expected from the water warming alone. Over the past several decades, there has been a noticeable ③<u>drop</u> in oxygen levels. However, only a small portion of this decrease is due to the fact that warmer water has difficulty holding oxygen. The majority of the oxygen in the ocean is ④<u>absorbed</u> from the atmosphere at the surface or created by small plants in the water called phytoplankton. Ocean currents then mix this oxygen-rich surface water with the deeper waters. However, rising ocean water temperatures near the surface have made it more lighter and ⑤<u>easier</u> for the warmer surface waters to mix downward with the cooler waters below. In addition, in polar regions, melting ice from glaciers and sea ice has added more freshwater to the ocean's surface. Freshwater is lighter than saltwater, so it stays at the surface. This also hinders the natural mixing process, which increases the layers in the ocean.
options: ① The Role of Phytoplankton in Oxygen Production
② Why Tropical Oceans Are Clearer Than Polar Seas
③ Adaptation of Marine Life to Cold and Warm Water
④ The Causes and Impacts of Declining Ocean Oxygen Levels
⑤ The Surprising Benefits of Rising Ocean Temperatures
