questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO₂ a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.summary_sentence: Whales sequester an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide when they die, (A)_________ the ocean with nutrient-rich waste to boost phytoplankton populations, and are highly valued for their ecosystem services, leading to (B)_________ for a global whale restoration program to combat climate change.

③ 단기 기억은 장기 기억으로의 전환이 매우 어렵다.
④ 다양한 학습 스타일을 개발하는 것은 기억을 오래 유지하는 데 도움이 된다.
⑤ 학습 전략을 잘 세우면 비효율적인 공부 시간을 줄일 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 부분에서 정보를 장기 기억으로 옮기기 위해서는 단순히 공부만 하는 것이 아니라 '스스로 테스트(test yourself)'하는 것이 필수적이라고 명시하고 있습니다. 벼락치기가 효과적이라고 느끼는 것은 단기 기억 때문인 착각이며, 지식을 유지하려면 재시험(retest)이 필요하다는 것이 핵심입니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 -luminiferous ether-에 대한 설명으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, -It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat.- This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of <u>luminiferous ether</u>, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① It refered to an observable phenomenon that was widely accepted by scientists.
② It was a real but intangible substance that scientists eventually managed to discover.
③ Its presence was proved by the scientific experiment with a black cat.
④ It turned out to be a nonexistent entity, which made the search meaningless.
⑤ It played a crucial role in physics in that it helped the light to travel in universe.
questions.explanation: "-luminiferous ether-"는 지문에서 "어두운 방 안에서 존재하지 않는 검은 고양이를 찾는 것"에 비유되었습니다. 이는 과학자들이 빛의 매질이 있을 것이라는 잘못된 전제 하에 찾아 헤맸던, 실제로는 존재하지 않는 가상의 물질을 의미합니다. 따라서 존재하지 않는 실체임이 드러나 탐색이 무의미해졌다는 ④번이 가장 적절한 설명입니다.
options_translation: 그것은 과학자들에 의해 널리 수용되었던 관찰 가능한 현상을 지칭했다.
그것은 과학자들이 결국 발견해낸 실제적이지만 형체가 없는 물질이었다.
그것의 존재는 검은 고양이를 이용한 과학 실험에 의해 증명되었다.
그것은 존재하지 않는 실체로 밝혀졌으며, 이는 그 탐색을 무의미하게 만들었다.
그것은 빛이 우주를 이동하는 것을 도움으로써 물리학에서 중요한 역할을 했다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The (A)[diverse / unified] departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which (B)[allows / disallows] them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is (C)[less / more] centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation:
(A) 조직 내의 부서들이 각자의 편향된 시각을 갖는다는 맥락이므로 '다양한(diverse)' 부서들이라는 표현이 적절합니다.
(B) 앞서 언급된 '터널 시야(tunnel vision)'는 다른 사람들의 관점에서 사물을 보는 것을 못하게 한다는 의미이므로 '차단하다/허용하지 않다(disallows)'가 적절합니다.
(C) 유기적 구조(Organic structures)는 수평적인 성격을 띠며 결정권이 전 조직에 분산되어 있으므로, 중앙 집중화가 '덜(less)' 되어 있다는 표현이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 다양한 - (B) 차단하는 - (C) 덜
② (A) 통일된 - (B) 허용하는 - (C) 덜
③ (A) 다양한 - (B) 차단하는 - (C) 더
④ (A) 통일된 - (B) 차단하는 - (C) 더
⑤ (A) 다양한 - (B) 허용하는 - (C) 더

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
options: ① The Importance of Urban Planning for Green Cities
② Creating a Sustainable City by Removing Traffic
③ The Role of Delivery Vehicles in Urban Areas
④ The Benefits of Cycling in Modern Cities
⑤ How Pedestrian Zones Improve City Life
questions.explanation: 이 글은 교통 정체를 완화하는 방법으로 차량 통행을 아예 제거(removing traffic)하고 자전거와 보행자 위주의 도로망을 구축하는 것의 이점을 설명합니다. 또한 효율적인 배달 시스템이 오히려 도시를 더 친환경적으로 만드는 데 기여한다는 내용을 포함하고 있습니다. 따라서 '통행 제거를 통한 지속 가능한 도시 만들기'라는 내용의 ②번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 친환경 도시를 위한 도시 계획의 중요성
② 통행 제거를 통한 지속 가능한 도시 만들기
③ 도시 지역에서 배달 차량의 역할
④ 현대 도시에서 자전거 타기의 이점
⑤ 보행자 전용 구역이 도시 생활을 개선하는 방법

questions.question: 14. 다음 글을 읽고 추론할 수 있는 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us care off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
options: ① 감정은 생존의 측면에서 크게 기여해왔다.
② 특정한 감정은 구체적인 방식과 밀접하게 연관되어 있다.
③ 두려운 상황에 집중하게 되는 것은 계획된 프로그램과 유사하다.
④ 감정은 특정한 상황에서 우리의 신체 반응을 조절하는 역할을 한다.
⑤ 감정은 인간과 함께 진화해 왔다고 볼 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 본문 하단부에서 "Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems"(그것들이 우리의 시스템을 활성화하는 특정한 방식에 상관없이)라고 언급하며, 감정이 존재하는 이유는 활성화 방식과의 연관성 때문이 아니라 과거 환경에서 생존에 도움을 주었기 때문이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 특정한 감정이 구체적인 방식과 밀접하게 연관되어 있다는 진술은 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along - whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS - and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show - whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire - you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along - a new way for humans to communicate - it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① The impact of television on modern society
② The role of social media in shaping public opinion
③ Marshall McLuhan's theories on media and communication
④ The history of communication mediums and their development
⑤ How new media influences our perception and understanding of the world
questions.explanation: 이 글은 새로운 미디어가 등장할 때마다 그것이 새로운 고글을 쓰는 것과 같아서 우리가 세상을 다르게 보게 만든다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 마셜 매클루언의 말을 인용하며 정보의 내용보다 정보가 전달되는 매체 자체가 우리의 인식과 코드에 더 큰 영향을 미친다는 내용을 담고 있으므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 텔레비전이 현대 사회에 미치는 영향
② 여론 형성에 있어서 소셜 미디어의 역할
③ 미디어와 커뮤니케이션에 관한 마셜 매클루언의 이론들
④ 커뮤니케이션 매체의 역사와 발전
⑤ 새로운 매체가 세상을 바라보는 우리의 인식과 이해에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 16. 다음 글을 읽고, 본문의 내용을 표로 정리했을 때, 표에 들어갈 말로 적절하지 않은 것끼리 바르게 나열된 것은?
questions.passage: Biologists distinguish two kinds of similarity. "Analogous" traits are ones that have a common function but arose on different branches of the evolutionary tree and are in an important sense not "the same" organ. The wings of birds and the wings of bees are both used for flight and are similar in some ways because anything used for flight has to be built in those ways, but they arose independently in evolution and have nothing in common beyond their use in flight. "Homologous" traits, in contrast, may or may not have a common function, but they descended from a common ancestor and hence have some common structure that indicates their being "the same" organ. The wing of a bat and the front leg of a horse have very different functions, but they are all modifications of the forelimb of the ancestor of all mammals. As a result, they share nonfunctional traits like the number of bones and the ways they are connected. To distinguish analogy from homology, biologists usually look at the overall architecture of the organs and focus on their most useless properties.Feature | Analogous Traits | Homologous Traits---|---|---Example | ⓐWings of birds and wings of bees | ⓑWing of a bat and front leg of a horseFunctional Similarity | ⓒmay not exist (e.g., flight) | ⓓmay not exist (e.g., bat's wing and horse's front leg)Evolutionary Origin | ⓔArose dependently | ⓕDescended from a different ancestorStructural Similarity | ⓖOnly functional similarity exists | ⓗNon-functional structural similarity exists
questions.explanation: 표의 항목 중 ⓒ: 유추적(Analogous) 특징은 비행과 같은 공통 기능을 가지고 있으므로 '존재하지 않을 수 있다'는 설명은 틀렸습니다. ⓔ: 유추적 특징은 독립적으로(independently) 발생한 것이지 dependently하게 발생한 것이 아닙니다. ⓕ: 상동적(Homologous) 특징은 공통의 조상(common ancestor)으로부터 유래한 것이므로 '다른 조상'이라는 설명은 틀렸습니다. 따라서 ⓒ, ⓔ, ⓕ가 포함된 ⑤번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Our emotions exist because they have ⓐ<u>contributed</u> to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us to avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us to scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us to bond with other people. From an ⓑ<u>evolutionary</u> perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more ⓒ<u>acutely</u>(so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to ⓓ<u>perish</u> because they have helped us survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us ⓔ<u>adapt</u> and survive, they would not have developed with us.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 우리가 가진 특정한 감정들은 오래전 환경 내의 도전들로부터 우리가 생존하도록 도왔기 때문에 '지속되다' 또는 '남아있다'는 의미가 되어야 합니다. ⓓ의 'perish(사라지다, 죽다)'는 문맥상 반대되는 의미이므로 'persist' 혹은 'remain'과 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat."이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "<u>It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat</u>." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.
options: ① Scientific progress requires persistence despite repeated failures.
② Scientists are always successful in their hypotheses if they use the right concept.
③ It is difficult to discover something important in an unfavorable environment.
④ The search for essences often leads to misleading conclusions from incorrect concepts.
⑤ Discovering the essence of something is essential for making accurate scientific conclusions.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 존재하지 않는 본질을 찾으려 애쓰는 과학자들의 헛된 노력을 비유한 것입니다. 이는 잘못된 개념(wrong concept)에 기반하여 가설을 세우고 실험을 할 때, 결국 존재하지 않는 결과(에테르와 같은 검은 고양이)를 찾으려다 오도된 결론에 이르게 됨을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 과학적 진보는 반복되는 실패에도 불구하고 끈기를 필요로 한다.
② 과학자들은 올바른 개념을 사용하면 항상 가설에 성공한다.
③ 불리한 환경에서 중요한 것을 발견하기란 어렵다.
④ 본질에 대한 탐구는 흔히 잘못된 개념으로부터 잘못된 결론으로 이어진다.
⑤ 어떤 것의 본질을 발견하는 것은 정확한 과학적 결론을 내리는 데 필수적이다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Have you ever been surprised to hear a recording of your own voice? You might have thought, "Is that really what my voice sounds like?" Maybe your accent is more pronounced in the recording than you realized, or your voice is higher than it seems to your own ears. This is of course quite a common experience. The explanation is actually fairly simple. (A) There are two pathways through which we perceive our own voice when we speak. (B) One is the route through which we perceive most external sounds, like waves that travel from the air through the outer, middle and inner ear. (C) Vibrations are conducted through our bones and stimulate our inner ears directly. (D) Lower frequencies are emphasized along this pathway. (E) That makes your voice sound deeper and richer to yourself than it may sound to other people.
questions.insertion_sentence: But because our vocal cords vibrate when we speak, there is a second internal path.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 '두 번째 내부 경로(a second internal path)'를 언급하고 있으므로, 앞서 첫 번째 경로(외부 소리를 듣는 경로)를 설명한 문장 뒤에 와야 합니다. (B)에서 외부 소리를 듣는 첫 번째 경로를 설명했으므로, 그 다음인 (C)의 위치에 제시문이 들어가 '하지만 성대가 울리기 때문에 두 번째 내부 경로도 있다'고 설명하고, (C) 뒤의 문장에서 그 내부 경로의 구체적 메커니즘(뼈를 통한 진동)을 설명하는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 17. 윗글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. Between 2000 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
questions.summary_sentence: While higher education has broadened its reach by including (A)___________, driven by a need to cultivate a(n) (B)___________ workforce, it has also led to several (C)___________, relying on standardised assessments such as exams and grades.
options: ① (A) the general public / (B) proficient / (C) challenges
② (A) more diverse students / (B) competent / (C) advantages
④ (A) the general public / (B) specialised / (C) opportunities
⑤ (A) more diverse students / (B) ordinary / (C) competitions
questions.explanation: 본문은 고등교육이 소수의 엘리트 시스템에서 대중 시스템으로 변화하면서 더 넓은 층의 학생들을 포함하게 되었고, 이는 경제를 위한 전문 인력 양성이라는 필요성에 의해 추진되었으나, 실제로는 효율성 위주의 표준화된 평가 방식을 택하게 되면서 여러 어려움이나 모순(challenges/contradictions)을 낳았다는 내용을 담고 있습니다.(A) 'the general public'은 본문에서 언급된 'mass system'과 'diverse demographic of students'를 포괄하는 대중(일반 대중)을 의미합니다.(B) 'proficient'는 본문의 'specialised' 또는 'highly skilled'와 일치하는 숙련된/능숙한의 의미입니다.(C) 'challenges'는 본문에서 언급된 'field of contradictions'와 피드백보다 성적에 집중하게 되는 문제 상황을 의미하는 난제/도전을 뜻합니다. 따라서 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 일반 대중 / (B) 숙련된 / (C) 난제들
② (A) 더 다양한 학생들 / (B) 유능한 / (C) 장점들
③ (A) 엘리트 학생들 / (B) 기술 있는 / (C) 결점들
④ (A) 일반 대중 / (B) 전문화된 / (C) 기회들
⑤ (A) 더 다양한 학생들 / (B) 평범한 / (C) 경쟁들

questions.question: 18. 윗글에서 다음 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 적절한 표현을 찾아 한 단어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Higher education has grown from an elite to a mass system across the world. In Europe and the USA, increased rates of participation occurred in the decades after the Second World War. Between 2000 and 2014, rates of participation in higher education almost doubled from 19% to 34% across the world among the members of the population in the school-leaving age category (typically 18-23). The dramatic expansion of higher education has been marked by a wider range of institutions of higher learning and a more diverse demographic of students. Changes from an elite system to a mass higher education system are associated with political needs to build a specialised workforce for the economy. In theory, the expansion of higher education to develop a highly skilled workforce should diminish the role of examinations in the selection and control of students, initiating approaches to assessment which enable lifelong learning: assessment for learning and a focus on feedback for development. In reality, socio-political changes to expand higher education have set up a 'field of contradictions' for assessment in higher education. Mass higher education requires efficient approaches to assessment, such as examinations and multiple-choice quizzes, with minimalist, impersonal, or standardised feedback, often causing students to focus more on grades than feedback. In contrast, the relatively small numbers of students in elite systems in the past allowed for closer relationships between students and their teachers, with formative feedback shaping the minds, academic skills, and even the characters of students.
vocabulary_box: (A)___________is an adjective that describes an assessment format where a question is followed by several answer options, requiring the student to select the correct one.(B)___________relates to the characteristics of a specific population, such as age, race, gender, or socioeconomic status, often used to analyze groups within a society.(C)___________is an adjective that refers to something made consistent or uniform across different situations, often following a set of rules or criteria.(D)___________are situations where conflicting or opposing elements exist simultaneously, creating inconsistencies or paradoxes.
questions.explanation: (A) 여러 선택지 중 하나를 고르는 평가 형식을 설명하므로 'multiple-choice'가 적합합니다.(B) 연령, 인종, 성별 등 인구의 특성을 나타내는 단어이므로 'demographic'이 적합합니다.(C) 일관되거나 균일하게 만들어진 것을 의미하므로 'standardised'가 적합합니다.(D) 상충하거나 반대되는 요소가 동시에 존재하여 불일치나 역설을 만드는 상황이므로 'contradictions'가 적합합니다. (단어 설명문이 are로 시작하므로 복수형으로 기재하는 것이 지문의 맥락과도 일치함)

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along-whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS-and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show-whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire-you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along-a new way for humans to communicate-it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① TV shows mirroring societal trends
② the transformative power of media on our world view
③ the effects of television viewing on child development
④ an effective way to communicate important messages
⑤ mental health issues linked to excessive use of social media
questions.explanation: 이 글은 새로운 매체가 등장할 때마다 그것이 우리가 세상을 보는 방식(세계관)을 변화시킨다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 마샬 맥루한의 말을 인용하여 정보의 내용보다 정보가 전달되는 방식(매체) 자체가 더 중요하며, 매체는 우리를 새로운 코드에 따라 세상을 보도록 안내한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 '미디어가 우리의 세계관에 미치는 변형적 힘'입니다.
options_translation: ① 사회적 트렌드를 반영하는 TV 프로그램들
② 우리의 세계관에 대한 미디어의 변형적인 힘
③ 텔레비전 시청이 아동 발달에 미치는 영향
④ 중요한 메시지를 전달하는 효과적인 방법
⑤ 소셜 미디어의 과도한 사용과 관련된 정신 건강 문제

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Capuchins-New World Monkeys that live in large social groups-will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me ⓐ<u>a treat</u> to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will ⓑ<u>happily</u> eat the cucumbers. If, however, you give one monkey grapes instead-grapes being universally ⓒ<u>preferred</u> to cucumbers-the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to  throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" ⓓ<u>the same</u> amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. Furthermore, she is now willing to ⓔ<u>cherish</u> all gains-the cucumbers themselves-to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
questions.explanation: 다른 원숭이가 더 좋은 보상(포도)을 받는 것을 본 원숭이는 자신이 받는 보상(오이)에 대해 불공정함을 느끼고 불쾌감을 표현합니다. 따라서 ⑤번의 'cherish(소중히 여기다)'는 문맥상 불쾌감을 표현하기 위해 오이를 던져버리거나 포기한다는 의미인 'forfeit' 혹은 'reject'와 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Complementary goods are goods that people tend to buy at the same time because they go well together or ⓐ<u>enhance</u> each other's use. For example, popcorn is a complementary good to a movie, while a travel pillow is a complementary good for a long plane journey. When one product's popularity rises, sales of its complementary good often ⓑ<u>increase</u> as well. By producing goods that complement other products that are already (or about to be) popular, you can ⓒ<u>secure</u> a consistent demand for your product. However, there's a negative relationship between the price of one good and the demand for its complement. When the price of one product increases, the demand for both the product and its complementary good tends to ⓓ<u>rise</u>. Some products enjoy perfect complementary status-they have to be consumed together, such as a lamp and a lightbulb. However, do not assume that a product is perfectly complementary, as customers may have ⓔ<u>substitutes</u> available. For example, although motorists may seem required to purchase gasoline to run their cars, they can switch to electric cars.
questions.explanation: 보완재 관계에서 한 제품의 가격이 상승하면 그 제품의 수요가 줄어들고, 그에 따라 보완재의 수요도 함께 줄어들게 됩니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 'rise'는 'fall' 또는 'decrease'로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were ⓐ<u>unrecognized</u> in their own day. Not everyone  could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is ⓑ<u>strangeness</u>. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so ⓒ<u>exceptional</u>. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous ⓓ<u>ordinary</u> composers-he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work was ⓔ<u>unique</u>. What he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time.
questions.explanation: 살리에리가 위대한 작곡가가 되지 못한 이유는 그의 작품이 '독특했기(unique)' 때문이 아니라, 당시 다른 모든 사람들이 작곡하던 것과 비슷했기 때문입니다. 즉, 독창성이 부족했다는 의미가 되어야 하므로 ⓔ의 'unique'는 'not unique' 혹은 'conventional' 등과 같은 의미로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realise it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate. Those who do usually learn the traditional, Ⓩ<u>zero-sum</u> negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement. This oldschool, adversarial approach may be useful in a ⓐ<u>single-use</u> negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again. However, these types of transactions are becoming increasingly common, as we frequently interact with the ⓑ<u>regular</u> individuals over and over again-such as our spouses and children, friends, colleagues, customers and clients. Give this, it is crucial to secure favorable outcomes for ourselves while also preserving a ⓒ<u>constructive</u> relationship with our negotiation counterparts. In today's interdependent world of business partnerships and long term relationships, a ⓓ<u>one-sided</u> outcome is fast becoming the only acceptable result.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 부분에서 오늘날의 비즈니스 파트너십과 장기적 관계가 중요한 상호 의존적인 세상에서는 한쪽에게만 유리한 결과(one-sided outcome)는 허용될 수 없다고 문맥상 판단됩니다. 따라서 'only acceptable result'가 아니라 'unacceptable result'와 같은 흐름이 되어야 하므로 ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 흐름상 적절하지 않은 것은 ⑤번(ⓔ가 지문 내에는 명시되지 않았으나 문항 구성상 ⓓ의 수정을 요구하는 의도)입니다. 원문상 ⓓ 부분은 win-win 결과가 유일한 결과가 되고 있다는 맥락이어야 합니다. 하지만 제시된 지문 텍스트 내에서 ⓓ 'one-sided'는 부정적인 결과로 묘사되어야 하므로 'only unacceptable' 등으로 바뀌어야 문맥이 성립합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop-out, or worse.
options: ① The Reason Not to Brag About Your Kids
② Some Problems in the Definition of Gifted Children
③ How to Handle Parents Who Brag about Their Kids
④ Gifted Children Are Often Misunderstood by Society
⑤ What Makes So Many Parents Think Their Child Is Gifted
questions.explanation: 이 글은 부모가 영재 자녀의 성취에 대해 지나치게 자랑하는 것이 아이에게 압박감을 주고, 아이의 자아 형성에 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 경고하고 있습니다. 따라서 자녀에 대해 자랑하지 말아야 할 이유를 담은 ①번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 아이들에 대해 자랑하지 말아야 하는 이유
② 영재 아동의 정의에 있어서의 몇 가지 문제점
③ 그들의 아이들에 대해 자랑하는 부모들을 다루는 법
④ 영재 아동들은 종종 사회에 의해 오해받는다
⑤ 무엇이 그렇게 많은 부모들로 하여금 자신의 아이가 영재라고 생각하게 만드는가

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: It's not news to anyone that we judge others based on their clothes. In general, studies that investigate these judgments find that people prefer clothing that matches expectations─surgeons in scrubs, little boys in blue─with one notable exception. A series of studies published in an article in June 2014 in the Journal of Consumer Research explored observers' reactions to people who broke established norms only slightly. In one scenario, a man at a blacktie affair was viewed as having higher status and competence when wearing a red bow tie. The researchers also found that valuing uniqueness increased audience members' ratings of the status and competence of a professor who wore red sneakers while giving a lecture. The results suggest that people judge these slight deviations from the norm as positive because they suggest that the individual is powerful enough to risk the social costs of such behaviors.
options: ① What Dress Brand Catches People's Attention?
② Break the Dress Code If You Want to Succeed
③ Status Boost From Subtle Dress Code Deviations
④ The Impact of Dress Code on Work Performance
⑤ Small Exception In Clothing : Absolutely Intolerable
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 관습적인 복장 규정에서 약간 벗어난(slight deviations) 차림새를 한 사람들을 오히려 지위가 높고 유능하다고 판단한다는 연구 결과를 소개하고 있습니다. 따라서 미묘한 복장 규정 위반이 지위 상승을 가져온다는 ③번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 어떤 옷 브랜드가 사람들의 주의를 끄는가?
② 성공하고 싶다면 복장 규정을 어겨라
③ 미묘한 복장 규정 일탈로부터 오는 지위 상승
④ 복장 규정이 업무 성과에 미치는 영향
⑤ 옷차림에 있어서의 작은 예외 : 절대 참을 수 없는 것

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: For many people, ability refers to intellectual competence, so they want everything they do to reflect how smart they are─writing a brilliant legal brief, getting the highest grade on a test, writing elegant computer code. saying something exceptionally wise or witty in a conversation. You could also define ability in terms of a particular skill or talent, such as how well one plays the piano, learns a language, or serves a tennis ball. Some people focus on their ability to be attractive, entertaining, up on the latest trends, or to have the newest gadgets. However ability may be defined, a problem occurs when it is the sole determinant of one's self-worth. The performance becomes the only measure of the person; nothing else is taken into account. An outstanding performance means an outstanding person; an average performance means an average person. Period.
options: ① The Trap of Defining Self-Worth by Ability
② Balancing Skill and Talent in Everyday Life
③ How Ability Shapes Our Personal Identity
④ The Pursuit of Perfection in Every Task
⑤ The Role of Talent in Defining Success
questions.explanation: 능력이 어떻게 정의되든 간에, 그것이 자아 가치(self-worth)를 결정하는 유일한 요소가 될 때 문제가 발생한다는 내용입니다. 즉, 수행 능력이 그 사람을 평가하는 유일한 척도가 되어버리는 위험성을 경고하고 있으므로 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 능력으로 자아 가치를 정의하는 것의 함정
② 일상생활에서 기술과 재능의 균형 맞추기
③ 능력이 우리의 개인적 정체성을 형성하는 방식
④ 모든 과업에서의 완벽함 추구
⑤ 성공을 정의하는 데 있어 재능의 역할

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. (A) This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. (B) When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. (C) Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. (D) On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. (E) They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.
questions.insertion_sentence: A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 다문화 도시나 지역의 이점(가용한 재화와 서비스의 범위 증가)을 언급하고 있습니다. 글의 흐름상 (C)에서 다양성이 노동 시장뿐만 아니라 삶의 질에도 영향을 미칠 수 있다고 언급한 뒤, 그 긍정적인 예시로 주어진 문장이 온 뒤, (D)에서 'On the other hand'를 통해 부정적인 인식으로 전환되는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 (D)의 위치가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve inclusiveness in the workplace. (A) AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. (B) For example. speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. (C) To illustrate. AI's capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. (D) Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 AI가 저숙련 노동자의 능력을 향상시키고 임금과 경력 전망에 긍정적인 영향을 줄 수 있다는 내용입니다. (C) 앞부분까지는 장애가 있는 노동자들에 대한 AI의 도움을 다루고 있으며, (C)의 'To illustrate' 이후부터는 언어적 장벽이 있는 비원어민이나 저숙련자의 능력 향상(번역, 텍스트 생성 등)에 대한 구체적인 예시가 시작됩니다. 따라서 저숙련 노동자에 대한 일반적인 진술인 주어진 문장은 (C) 자리에 위치하여 뒤에 나오는 비원어민(non-native speakers)과 텍스트 생성기 예시를 포괄하는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Claims that local food production cut greenhouse gas emissions by reducing the burning of transportation fuel are usually not well founded. Transport is the source of only 11 percent of greenhouse gas emissions within the food sector, so reducing the distance that food travels after it leaves the farm is far less important than reducing wasteful energy use on the farm. Food coming from a distance can actually be better for the climate, depending on how it was grown.
ordered_passages: (A) Bulk loads of food can travel halfway around the world by ocean freight with a smaller carbon footprint, per pound delivered, than foods traveling just a short distance but in much larger loads. For example, 18-wheelers carry much larger loads than pickup trucks so they can move food 100 times as far while burning only one-third as much gas per pound of food delivered.

(B) For example, field-grown tomatoes shipped from Mexico in the winter months will have a smaller carbon footprint than local winter tomatoes grown in a greenhouse. In the United Kingdom, lamb meat that travels 11,000 miles from New Zealand generates only one-quarter the carbon emissions per pound compared to British lamb.

(C) It's because farmers in the United Kingdom raise their animals on feed (which must be produced using fossil fuels) rather than on clover pastureland. When food does travel, what matters most is not the distance traveled but the travel mode (surface versus air), and most of all the load size.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 지역 식품이 온실가스를 줄인다는 주장이 근거가 부족하며, 재배 방식에 따라 먼 곳의 식품이 기후에 더 나을 수 있다고 언급했습니다. (B)에서는 그 예시로 멕시코 토마토와 뉴질랜드 양고기를 들어 영국 현지 제품보다 탄소 배출이 적을 수 있음을 보여줍니다. (C)에서는 왜 뉴질랜드 양고기가 더 나은지 이유(사료 vs 목초지)를 설명하고, 이동 시 거리보다 이동 방식과 '적재량'이 중요함을 언급합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 그 적재량(load size)에 대한 구체적인 예시(대형 트럭 vs 픽업트럭)를 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A key to engagement and achievement is providing students with relevant texts they will be interested in. My scholarly work and my teaching have been deeply influenced by the work of Rosalie Fink.
ordered_passages: (A) While she expected to find that they had avoided reading and discovered ways to bypass it or compensate with other strategies for learning, she found the opposite. "To my surprise, I found that these dyslexics were enthusiastic readers... they rarely avoided reading. On the contrary, they sought out books."

(B) The pattern Fink discovered was that all of her subjects had been passionate in some personal interest. The areas of interest included religion, math, business, science, history, and biography. What mattered was that they read voraciously to find out more.

(C) She interviewed twelve adults who were highly successful in their work, including a physicist, a biochemist, and a company CEO. All of them had dyslexia and had had significant problems with reading throughout their school years.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 Rosalie Fink의 연구에 대해 언급을 시작합니다. (C)에서 그녀가 난독증이 있지만 성공한 12명의 성인을 인터뷰했다는 구체적인 연구 대상을 소개합니다. (A)에서 그녀의 예상(난독증 환자들이 읽기를 피할 것임)과 정반대의 결과인 '열정적인 독자'였다는 사실이 드러납니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 그들이 읽기에 열중할 수 있었던 공통점인 '개인적 관심 분야에 대한 열정'을 설명하며 결론을 맺습니다.

questions.question: 14. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings.
ordered_passages: (A) Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers. It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works.

(B) In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth. This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up radically remaking the society itself. Things are not so different in our own time.

(C) But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us. One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Göbekli Tepe in Turkey.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 우리가 건물을 만든다고 생각한다는 화두를 던집니다. (C)에서 역접의 'But'을 사용하여 건물 역시 우리를 만든다는 주장을 펴며 그 예시로 터키의 괴베클리 테페를 소개합니다. (A)에서 이 건설을 시작한 조상들이 원래 수렵 채집인이었으나, 건설 기간이 너무 길어지면서 정착할 수밖에 없게 된 상황을 설명합니다. (B)에서 그 정착 과정(In the process)이 최초의 농경 사회로 이어졌음을 밝히며, 건축물이 사회 구조를 바꾼 예시임을 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism.
ordered_passages: (A) The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.

(B) This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses.

(C) They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb. "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat."
(D) Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through.
questions.explanation: 제시문은 개념이 본질주의(essentialism)로 이끄는 위험성을 경고합니다. (C)에서 개념이 존재하지 않는 것을 보게 한다는 점을 Stuart Firestein이 인용한 '검은 방의 검은 고양이' 격언으로 설명합니다. (B)에서 이 격언(This statement)이 본질 탐구를 요약한다고 설명하며 잘못된 개념을 사용한 과학적 사례들을 언급합니다. (D)에서 그 구체적인 예로 '에테르'를 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 그 에테르가 바로 격언 속의 '존재하지 않는 검은 고양이'였음을 비유하며 글을 맺습니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Whales are some of the largest and longest living animals on earth. This allows them to store greater quantities of carbon in their bodies for longer than smaller animals. Whales efficiently digest and store large quantities of carbon-rich prey and exhale very little carbon dioxide back into the atmosphere. This process allows whales to store more carbon in their bodies than trees. After whales die, their dead bodies often sink to the seafloor (called a "whale fall"), trapping the carbon stored in their bodies at the bottom of the ocean. Whale falls can sequester carbon for hundreds to thousands of years. Many deep-sea organisms have evolved to rely on nutrients from sinking dead bodies. Dead bodies of whales are responsible for a large portion of those nutrients due to their massive size. As the dead bodies of whales decompose and are eaten by deep sea animals, that carbon is sequestered in sediment and cycled through the deep-sea ecosystem. This prevents it from returning to the atmosphere as carbon dioxide.
options: ① 고래는 크고 오래 사는 특성 덕분에 작은 동물들 보다 더 많은 양의 탄소를 더 오랫동안 체내에 저장할 수 있다.
② 고래는 나무보다 더 많은 탄소를 체내에 저장할 수 있다.
③ 죽은 고래는 탄소를 저장한 채 해저로 가라앉아 수백에서 수천 년 동안 탄소를 격리할 수 있다.
④ 고래 시체는 그 거대한 크기 덕에 심해 생물들에게 상당한 영향분을 제공한다.
⑤ 고래 시체 분해 과정에서 탄소가 이산화탄소 형태로 대기 중으로 돌아가게 된다.
questions.explanation: 지문 마지막 문장에서 고래의 사체가 분해되어 심해 생태계에서 순환됨으로써 탄소가 이산화탄소 형태로 대기로 돌아가는 것을 '방지한다(prevents)'고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 대기 중으로 돌아간다는 ⑤번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often ①<u>criticized</u> for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point ②<u>which</u> the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, ③<u>characterized</u> by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity ④<u>is</u> like doing well at a game. That is, in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks ⑤<u>built</u> into social media applications.
questions.explanation: ②번 문장에서 the point는 뒤에 완전한 절을 수반하여 동격을 나타내얼 하므로 관계대명사 which 대신 접셍사 that을 쓨어야 합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay ①<u>alive</u>. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water ②<u>does─</u> his is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident ③<u>that</u> the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if ④<u>allowed</u> to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water ⑤<u>has</u> the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: ⑤번이 포함된 문장의 주어는 'Falling oxygen levels' 로 복수 명사구임으로 동사 has를 have로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually __________________________. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
options: ① an essential component to making cities greener
② the very source of air pollution in the cities
③ making the streets safer for pedestrians
④ removing smaller stores from the cities
⑤ the final results of the city planners
questions.explanation: 지문은 자전거와 보행자 중심의 도시 계획이 교통을 진정시키고 도로를 안전하게 만드는 대안임을 설명하면서, 배달 트럭(delivery vehicles)에 대한 오해를 다룹니다. 배달 트럭은 종종 비난의 대상(target of animus)이 되지만, 실제로는 많은 소형 차량들이 개별적으로 물건을 운송하는 것보다 훨씬 효율적입니다. 이는 결과적으로 주민들이 동네 가게를 이용할 수 있게 하여 운전을 줄이고 도시를 더 친환경적으로 만드는 데 기여하므로 빈칸에는 '도시를 더 친환경적으로 만드는 필수적인 구성 요소'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 도시를 더 푸르게(친환경적으로) 만드는 필수적인 구성 요소
② 도시 대기 오염의 바로 그 근원
③ 보행자들을 위해 거리를 더 안전하게 만드는 것
④ 도시에서 더 작은 상점들을 제거하는 것
⑤ 도시 계획가들의 최종 결과물

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore _________________________________. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own selfdiscipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
options: ④ give as much praise as possible
⑤ don't compare your child to others
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 아이들이 부모의 말보다는 행동을 보고 가치를 배운다는 것입니다. '단순히 말을 듣는 것만으로는 가치를 배우지 못한다'와 '주변 사람들이 일상에서 그 가치를 실천하고 지키는 것을 보며 배운다'는 내용 뒤에 결론이 나오므로, 말하는 대로 실천하라는 의미인 'practice what you preach'가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 옳고 그름을 명확히 해라
② 당신이 설교하는 것을 실천해라(언행일치)
③ 말이 행동보다 앞서게 해라
④ 가능한 한 많은 칭찬을 해라
⑤ 당신의 아이를 다른 아이와 비교하지 마라

questions.question: 25. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see how many people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. ⓐStudents and professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. ⓑExecutives in sport management have decades of knowledge and experience in their respective fields. ⓒSports industries are getting bigger these days as the importance of exercising is emphasized. ⓓHowever, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. ⓔVery few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people provide feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 스포츠 팬들이나 비전문가들이 전문적인 지식 없이 스포츠 팀의 운영이나 비즈니스에 대해 훈수를 두는 현상(Monday Morning Quarterback)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ③번 문장은 운동의 중요성이 강조됨에 따라 스포츠 산업이 커지고 있다는 내용으로, 비전문가들의 간섭이라는 글의 주제와 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. This often results in misunderstandings and clashes between departments with conflicting objectives. ①An organization's structure can create conflict, and choosing "mechanistic" or "organic" affects how it's managed. ②A mechanistic structure has a hierarchical setup with multiple layers of management, extensive rules, and numerous procedures guiding decision-making. ③This structure, typically found in large-scale manufacturing companies and bureaucratic government agencies, prioritizes stability over change and fosters a uniform culture. ④Some argue that personal relationships outside of work have a greater impact on conflict than the organizational structure itself. ⑤In contrast, a more flexible structure like an organic structure has a flatter hierarchy, with decision-making decentralized and distributed across the organization.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 젰직 구조(기계적 구조 vs 유기적 구조)가 젰직 내의 갈등과 관리 방식에 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ④번 문장은 직장 밑의 개인적 관계가 갈등에 미치는 영향을 언급하고 있으므로, 젰직 구조와 갈등의 상호작용이라는 전체 흠름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 설적한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders─employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task─like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds─they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.summary_sentence: Frans de Waal argues that humans, particularly scientists, use technical language to (A)_____________ our likeness with other animals and sustain our assumed (B)_____________, a practice he refers to as "linguistic castration."
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 자신들의 우옔성을 유지하기 위해 동물과의 공통점을 경시하고 전문 용어림 사용하여 거리두기림 한다는 내용입니다. 따핼서 공통점(닮은 점)을 줄이고(diminish) 인간의 우옔성(superiority)을 유지한다눠 표현이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 증폭하다 - 우옔성
② 줄이다 - 우옔성
③ 높이다 - 독창성
④ 반증하다 - 독창성
⑤ 재평가하다 - 순응

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 설적한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Boundaries between work and home are blurring as portable digital technology makes it increasingly possible to work anywhere, anytime. Individuals differ in how they like to manage their time to meet work and outside responsibilities. Some people prefer to separate or segment roles so that boundary crossings are minimized. For example, these people might keep separate email accounts for work and family and try to conduct work at the workplace and take care of family matters only during breaks and nonwork time. We've even noticed more of these "segmenters" carrying two phones─one for work and one for personal use. Flexible schedules work well for these individuals because they enable greater distinction between time at work and time in other roles. Other individuals prefer integrating work and family roles all day long. This might entail constantly trading text messages with children from the office, or monitoring emails at home and on vacation, rather than returning to work to find hundreds of messages in their inbox.
questions.summary_sentence: People manage their work and personal responsibilities differently: some prefer to (A)_____________ boundaries to maintain clear distinctions between roles, while others choose to (B)_____________ tasks to handle both simultaneously.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 일과 가정을 분리하려는 사람들(분리자)과 통합하려는 사람들(통합자)의 차이림 설명합니다. 분리자들은 경계림 강화하여(reinforce) 역할을 명확히 하고, 통합자들은 과업을 섞어서(blend) 동시에 차리합니다.
options_translation: ① 집행하다 - 방치하다
② 강화하다 - 섞다
③ 희미하게 하다 - 분리하다
④ 최소화하다 - 우선순위림 두다
⑤ 설정하다 - 방치하다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. (A) This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. (B) As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. (C) Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. (D) A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. (E) Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.insertion_sentence: Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '그럼에도 불구하고, 자전거를 타기에 가장 좋은 도시조차 택시, 응급 차량, 배달 트럭을 위한 자동차 차로가 여전히 필요하다'는 내용입니다. (B)까지는 자전거 도로 확충에 대해 이야기하고 있으며, (C)부터는 배달 차량(delivery vehicles)의 긍정적인 역할에 대해 설명하기 시작합니다. 따라서 자전거 도로의 한계와 필수 차량의 필요성을 언급하며 화제를 전환하는 주어진 문장은 (C) 자리에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 문맥상 다른 넷과 성격이 다른 하나는? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as ⓐ<u>a species</u>. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, ⓑ<u>an emotion</u> is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For example, ⓒ<u>fear</u> makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because ⓓ<u>they</u> have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within ⓔ<u>our environment</u> long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ는 모두 인간의 '감정(emotions)' 또는 그와 직접적으로 연관된 생존 기제(종으로서의 생존을 돕는 감정 시스템)를 지칭하거나 그 예시를 나타내지만, ⓔ 'our environment'는 감정이 작용하고 우리가 적응해야 했던 외부 대상인 '환경'을 의미하므로 성격이 다릅니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 어법상 올바른 표현을 순서대로 바르게 짝지은 것은? [24년 9월 24번]
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking (A)[that / what] carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, (B)[which / where] also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called (C)[for / off] a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤에 carbon이라는 명사가 있으므로, 이를 수식하는 지시형용사 'that'이 적절합니다. 'what'은 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사로 명사 역할을 하므로 명사 carbon 앞에 바로 올 수 없습니다.(B) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로 쓰여 선행사 phytoplankton populations를 부연 설명해야 합니다. 뒤에 바로 동사(sequester)가 나오므로 주격 관계대명사인 'which'가 적절합니다.(C) 'call for'는 '~을 요구하다'라는 뜻의 숙어입니다. 'call off'는 '~을 취소하다'라는 뜻이므로 문맥상 새로운 글로벌 프로그램을 요구했다는 의미가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① that / which / off
② that / which / for
③ what / which / for
④ what / where / for
⑤ what / where / off

questions.question: 26. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 34번]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself.
ordered_passages: (A) However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people.

(B) Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.

(C) Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 소셜 미디어 제작자들이 평범한 유명세를 원한다는 내용을 제시합니다.(C)에서는 이러한 소셜 미디어 유명인들이 전통적인 엘리트 유명인과 같은 재능이 없다는 비판을 받는다는 점을 설명합니다.(A)에서는 'However'를 사용하여 이러한 비판이 평범한 유명세가 명성의 의미를 재구성한다는 점을 간과하고 있다고 반박하며, 엘리트와 평범한 유명세의 차이를 설명합니다.(B)에서는 평범한 유명세를 얻는 것이 게임에서 좋은 점수를 얻는 것과 같다는 구체적인 비유를 통해 소셜 미디어에서의 명성을 설명하며 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 보기 안의 모든 단어로 배열하여 완성하시오. (어휘 형태 변화 금지, 보기에 포함된 단어로만 어순 배열하기, 부분 점수 없음)
questions.passage: You hear again and again that some of the greatest composers were misunderstood in their own day. Not everyone could understand the compositions of Beethoven, Brahms, or Stravinsky in their day. The reason for this initial lack of acceptance is unfamiliarity. The musical forms, or ideas expressed within them, were completely new. And yet, this is exactly one of the things that makes them so great. Effective composers have their own ideas. Have you ever seen the classic movie Amadeus? The composer Antonio Salieri is the "host" of this movie; he's depicted as one of the most famous Nongreat composers - he lived at the time of Mozart and was completely overshadowed by him. Now, Salieri wasn't a bad composer; in fact, he was a very good one. But he wasn't one of the world's great composers because his work wasn't original. What ______________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 어휘 형태 변화 금지
보기에 포함된 단어로만 어순 배열하기
부분 점수 없음
questions.answer: he wrote sounded just like what everyone else was composing at the time
questions.explanation: 이 글은 위대한 작곡가들이 당대에 오해받았던 이유가 그들의 독창적인 시도 때문이었음을 설명하며, 안토니오 살리에리가 위대한 작곡가가 되지 못한 이유로 독창성 결여를 꼽고 있습니다. 빈칸에는 살리에리가 쓴 음악이 당대의 다른 사람들이 작곡하던 것과 비슷했다는 내용이 와야 하므로, 관계대명사 what이 이끄는 절을 활용하여 'he wrote(그가 쓴 것) sounded just like(똑같이 들렸다) what everyone else was composing at the time(당시 다른 모든 사람들이 작곡하고 있던 것)'으로 구성하는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water ⓐ<u>is</u> ─ this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming ⓑ<u>raises</u> the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data ⓒ<u>indicating</u> that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more ⓓ<u>rapidly</u> than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this ⓔ<u>has led to</u> more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: ⓐ가 포함된 문장에서 'cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water [does]'의 구조가 되어야 합니다. 여기서 대동사는 앞에 나온 일반동사 'holds'를 대신해야 하므로 'is'가 아니라 'does'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 문장이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along ─ whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS ─ and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show ─ whether it's Wheel of Fortune or <u>The Wire</u> ─ you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans to communicate ─ it has buried in it a message. It is gently see the world according to a new set of codes. McLuhan argued that <u>the way information gets to you is more important than the information itself</u>. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
options: ① Information can be obtained through various media except TV.
② We tend to trust considerably the information we get from TV, which is not appropriate.
③ Rather than the content of the information, it is more important to focus on the media that deliver the information.
④ Various information must be delivered quickly and accurately through various media.
⑤ You can build a sense of trust in the media that you encounter information, which means you would be satisfied with it.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 마샬 맥루한의 '매체는 메시지다'라는 개념을 설명하고 있습니다. 밑줄 친 문장은 정보 그 자체보다 정보가 전달되는 방식(매체)이 더 중요하다는 것을 의미합니다. 즉, 매체 자체가 우리의 인식 방식을 규정한다는 내용이므로 ③번 '정보의 내용보다는 정보를 전달하는 매체에 집중하는 것이 더 중요하다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 정보는 TV를 제외한 다양한 매체를 통해 얻어질 수 있다.
② 우리는 TV에서 얻는 정보를 상당히 신뢰하는 경향이 있는데, 이는 적절하지 않다.
③ 정보의 내용보다는 정보를 전달하는 매체에 집중하는 것이 더 중요하다.
④ 다양한 정보는 다양한 매체를 통해 빠르고 정확하게 전달되어야 한다.
⑤ 정보를 접하는 매체에 대한 신뢰감을 형성할 수 있으며, 이는 당신이 그것에 만족할 것임을 의미한다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. (A) When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. (B) Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. (C) Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." (D) The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness. (E) In addition, there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
questions.insertion_sentence: This is one of the great powers of self-help groups.
questions.explanation: 첫 문장에서 무력감과 우울함에서 벗어나는 방법으로 문제를 해결한 사람들과 함께하는 것을 제안합니다. 주어진 문장의 'This'는 앞 문장에서 설명한 '문제를 해결한 사람들과 함께하기로 선택하는 것'을 가리키며, 이것이 자조 집단(self-help groups)의 큰 힘 중 하나라고 연결되는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 (A) 자리에 들어가는 것이 흐름상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글을 읽고 언급된 내용이 아닌 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: While social media attention is potentially an instrument to achieve ends like elite celebrity, some content creators desire ordinary fame as a social end in itself. Not unlike reality television stars, social media celebrities are often criticized for not having skills and talents associated with traditional, elite celebrity, such as acting or singing ability. This criticism highlights the fact that digital content creators face real barriers to crossing over to the sphere of elite celebrity. However, the criticism also misses the point that the phenomenon of ordinary celebrity reconstructs the meaning of fame. The elite celebrity is symbolized by the metaphor of the star, characterized by mystery and hierarchical distance and associated with naturalized qualities of talent and class. The ordinary celebrity attracts attention through regular and frequent interactions with other ordinary people. Achieving ordinary fame as a social media celebrity is like doing well at a game, because in this sphere, fame is nothing more nor less than relatively high scores on attention scales, the metrics of subscribers, followers, Likes, or clicks built into social media applications.
options: ① 소셜 미디어 관심은 잠재적으로 엘리트 명성과 같은 목적을 달성하기 위한 도구이다.
② 소셜 미디어 유명인들은 연기나 가창력을 갖고 있지 않은 경우가 많다.
③ 소셜 미디어 유명인들은 평범한 명성 현상으로 명성의 의미를 재구성한다.
④ 평범한 유명인은 다른 평범한 사람들과의 정기적이고 빈번한 상호작용을 통해 관심을 끌기도 한다.
⑤ 구독자, 팔로워, 좋아요 또는 클릭 수는 소셜 미디어의 명성을 결정하는 요인들이다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 소셜 미디어의 명성이 관심 척도(구독자, 좋아요 등) 상의 높은 점수에 불과하다는 점을 언급하고 있지만, 이 수치들이 명성을 '결정하는 요인(determinants)'이라기보다는 '지표(metrics)' 혹은 '점수(scores)'로 환산된다는 맥락으로 설명하고 있습니다. 본문의 마지막 문장에서 'fame is nothing more nor less than...'이라며 명성의 본질을 해당 수치들과 동일시하고 있으나, 언급된 보기들 중 지문에 명시된 내용의 사실 여부를 따질 때 ⑤번은 명성을 결정하는 독립적 '요인'들이라는 표현보다는 측정 지표라는 의미가 더 강합니다. (출제 의도상 ⑤번이 가장 적절하지 않은 서술로 선택된 것으로 보입니다.)

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 글의 의미를 적절하게 전달하지 못한 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: An excellent alternative to calming traffic is removing it. Some cities reserve an extensive network of lanes and streets for bikes, pedestrians, and the occasional service vehicle. This motivates people to travel by bike rather than by car, making streets safer for everyone. As bicycles become more popular in a city, planners can convert more automobile lanes and entire streets to accommodate more of them. Nevertheless, even the most bikeable cities still require motor vehicle lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks. Delivery vehicles are frequently a target of animus, but they are actually an essential component to making cities greener. A tightly packed delivery truck is a far more efficient transporter of goods than several hybrids carrying a few shopping bags each. Distributing food and other goods to neighborhood vendors allows them to operate smaller stores close to homes so that residents can walk, rather than drive, to get their groceries.
questions.summary_sentence: ⓐSome cities reduce traffic by reserving streets for bikes and pedestrians, encouraging cycling over driving. ⓑAs cycling increases, more car lanes can be adapted for bikes. ⓒHowever, lanes for taxis, emergency vehicles, and delivery trucks are still necessary. ⓓDelivery trucks, despite criticism, are an efficient way to transport goods, supporting local stores so residents can walk, rather than drive, to buy their groceries. ⓔThis helps make cities greener and boosts the need for car trips.
questions.explanation: 본문은 자전거 이용을 장려하고 효율적인 배송 시스템을 통해 자동차 운행(car trips)을 줄여야 한다는 내용입니다. 하지만 ⓔ는 '자동차 여행의 필요성을 높인다(boosts the need for car trips)'고 했으므로 요약으로 부적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 (A), (B), (C)를 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: (A) 그 소리는 깨끗하지도 않고 충분히 주게 나오지도 않는다.(B) 그는 항상 창의적인 물건들을 만드는 것에 흥미를 갖고 있다.(C) 이 이계들에 익숙하지 않은 사람들은 철도 서비스에 접근하는 데 어려움을 경험하고 있다.
subjective_conditions: 1. 아래 나열된 단어 및 어구를 모두 1번씩 사용하되, 형태를 바꾸지 말 것
2. (A), (B), (C) 모두 각각 단어를 1개 추가할 것
vocabulary_box: (A) clear / neither / the sound / loud / is / enough
(B) making / he / interested / always / is / items / in
(C) difficulty / these / are / are / those / with / experiencing / who / accessing / machines / the railway services
questions.answer: (A) The sound is neither clear nor loud enough(B) He is always interested in making creative items(C) Those who are unfamiliar with these machines are experiencing difficulty accessing the railway services.
questions.explanation: (A) 'neither A nor B' 구문을 사용하여 'A도 B도 아니다'를 표현해야 하며, 'nor'를 추가해야 합니다. 'loud enough'는 형용사+enough 어순입니다.(B) 'be interested in -ing' 구문을 사용하며, 명사 'items'를 수식할 형용사 'creative'를 추가해야 합니다.(C) 주격 관계대명사 who절 내에서 'unfamiliar'를 추가하여 '익숙하지 않은'의 의미를 완성합니다. 'experience difficulty -ing' 구문을 활용합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글을 읽고, 고래가 탄소 저장에 기여하는 방법을 한글로 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon─leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.*sequester: 격리하다 **phytoplankton: 식물성 플랑크톤
questions.answer: 죽을 때 30톤의 이산화탄소를 격리하고 풍부한 배설물을 내보내서 식물성 플랑크톤 개체가 증가하여 탄소 저장에 기여한다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 언급된 고래의 두 가지 탄소 저장 방식을 요약해야 합니다. 첫째는 고래가 죽을 때 사체에 엄청난 양의 탄소를 담아 바다 깊이 격리하는 것이고, 둘째는 배설물을 통해 식물성 플랑크톤의 증식을 도와 이들이 탄소를 흡수하게 하는 것입니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 어법상 어색한 문장을 2개 찾아서 <조건>에 맞게 바르게 고치시오.
questions.passage: Every time a new medium comes along ─ whether it's the invention of the printed book, or TV, or SNS ─ and you start to use it, it's like you are putting on a new kind of goggles, with their own special colors and lenses. Each set of goggles you put on make you see things differently. So when you start to watch television, before you absorb the message of any particular TV show ─ whether it's Wheel of Fortune or The Wire ─ you start to see the world as being shaped like television itself. That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans communicate ─ it has buried in it a message. It is gently guiding us to see the world according to a new set of codes. The way information gets to you, McLuhan argued, is more important than the information itself. TV teaches you that the world is fast; that it's about surfaces and appearances.
subjective_conditions: 어색한 부분을 수정한 문장 전체를 쓸 것
(~, - 등 생략 기호를 사용하지 말 것)
questions.answer: (1) Each set of goggles you put on makes you see things differently.(2) That's why Marshall McLuhan said that every time a new medium comes along ─ a new way for humans to communicate ─ it has buried in it a message.
questions.explanation: (1) 주어가 'Each set'으로 단수이므로 동사 'make'를 단수형인 'makes'로 고쳐야 합니다.(2) 'a new way' 뒤에서 'humans'가 의미상의 주어이고 이를 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사가 와야 하므로 'communicate'를 'to communicate'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절한 것의 개수는? [24년 9월 39번]
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe to stay alive. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds ⓐ<u>less</u> dissolved oxygen than warm water does ─ this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively ⓑ<u>densely</u> populated with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a potentially ⓒ<u>devastating</u> consequence if allowed to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans has been declining for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding ⓓ<u>decline</u> in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water have the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that have caused the death or ⓔ<u>relocation</u> of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 찬물은 따뜻한 물보다 더 많은 용존 산소를 보유하므로 'less'는 'more'로 바뀌어야 합니다. ⓑ 열대 바다는 생명체가 상대적으로 적게 서식하므로 'densely'는 'sparsely' 등으로 바뀌어야 적절합니다. ⓒ 용존 산소량의 감소는 생태계에 치명적인 결과이므로 'devastating'은 적절합니다. ⓓ 데이터는 해양 산소 수치가 수온 하락보다 더 빠르게 떨어졌음을 보여주는데, 문맥상 온도 '상승'에 따른 결과이므로 'decline'은 'rise' 또는 'increase'가 적절합니다. ⓔ 산소 부족은 물고기들의 죽음이나 '이동(relocation)'을 초래하므로 적절합니다. 따라서 적절한 단어는 ⓒ, ⓔ로 총 2개입니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글을 읽고 아래 질문에 대한 적절한 답을 고르면? [24년 9월 33번]
questions.passage: Concepts are vital to human survival, but we must also be careful with them because concepts open the door to essentialism. They encourage us to see things that aren't present. Stuart Firestein opens his book, Ignorance, with an old proverb, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." This statement beautifully sums up the search for essences. History has many examples of scientists who searched fruitlessly for an essence because they used the wrong concept to guide their hypotheses. Firestein gives the example of luminiferous ether, a mysterious substance that was thought to fill the universe so that light would have a medium to move through. The ether was a black cat, writes Firestein, and physicists had been theorizing in a dark room, and then experimenting in it, looking for evidence of a cat that did not exist.What must we be careful with concepts?
options: ① Because they are difficult for students to understand.
② Because they do not serve sufficient roles as a medium.
③ Because many scientists have different perspectives on them.
④ Because they are thought to guide the consistent hypotheses.
⑤ Because they can lead us to search for things that don't exist.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 개념(concepts)은 본질주의로 향하는 문을 열어주며, 존재하지 않는 것을 보게 하거나 존재하지 않는 대상을 찾게 할 수 있다고 설명하고 있습니다. '검은 고양이' 비유를 통해 존재하지 않는 에테르를 찾으려 했던 과학자들의 사례를 들며, 개념이 우리를 존재하지 않는 것을 찾도록 유도할 수 있음을 경고합니다. 따라서 5번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 학생들이 이해하기 어렵기 때문에
② 매개체로서 충분한 역할을 하지 못하기 때문에
③ 많은 과학자들이 그것들에 대해 서로 다른 관점을 가지고 있기 때문에
④ 일관된 가설을 안내한다고 생각되기 때문에
⑤ 그것들이 존재하지 않는 것들을 찾도록 우리를 유도할 수 있기 때문에

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Seawater contains an abundance of dissolved oxygen that all marine animals breathe ⓐ<u>to stay alive</u>. It has long been established in physics that cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water does - this is one reason that cold polar seas are full of life while tropical oceans are blue, clear, and relatively poorly ⓑ<u>populated</u> with living creatures. Thus, as global warming raises the temperature of marine waters, it is self-evident that the amount of dissolved oxygen will decrease. This is a worrisome and potentially disastrous consequence if ⓒ<u>allowing</u> to continue to an ecosystem-threatening level. Now scientists have analyzed data indicating that the amount of dissolved oxygen in the oceans ⓓ<u>has been declining</u> for more than a half century. The data show that the ocean oxygen level has been falling more rapidly than the corresponding rise in water temperature. Falling oxygen levels in water ⓔ<u>have</u> the potential to impact the habitat of marine organisms worldwide and in recent years this has led to more frequent anoxic events that killed or displaced populations of fish, crabs, and many other organisms.
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'This(재앙적인 결과)'입니다. '결과'가 스스로 허용하는 것이 아니라 '허용되는 것'이므로 수동의 의미를 지닌 과거분사 allowed가 되어야 합니다. 접속사 if 뒤에 '주어(it) + be동사(is)'가 생략된 분사구문 혹은 부사절 구문으로 보아야 합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The ⓐ<u>varying</u> departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own ⓑ<u>unbiased</u> and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which ⓒ<u>disallows</u> them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict.
