The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a ⓓ<u>profound</u> influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more ⓔ<u>horizontal</u> in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.explanation: 조직 내의 각 부서는 자신의 편견이 섞인(prejudiced) 관점으로 상황을 본다는 맥락이므로, '편견 없는'을 뜻하는 unbiased는 문맥상 반대되는 표현입니다. biased(편향된) 또는 parochial(편협한) 등이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. (A) From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. (B) Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." (C) In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. (D) They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. (E) Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
questions.insertion_sentence: For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 평균적인 나무 한 그루가 연간 흡수하는 이산화탄소 양이 48파운드에 불과하다는 비교 수치를 제공합니다. 본문 (A) 앞 문장에서 고래 한 마리가 죽을 때 평균 30톤의 이산화탄소를 격리한다고 설명하고 있으며, (A) 뒤 문장에서는 기후적 관점에서 고래 한 마리가 '수천 그루의 나무'에 해당한다고 결론짓고 있습니다. 따라서 나무의 흡수량 수치를 제시하여 고래의 격리 능력과 대조를 이루는 주어진 문장은 (A) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Capuchins - New World Monkeys that live in large social groups - will, in captivity, trade with people all day long, especially if food is involved. I give you this rock and you give me a treat to eat. If you put two monkeys in cages next to each other, and offer them both slices of cucumber for the rocks they already have, they will happily eat the cucumbers. If, (A)___________, you give one monkey grapes instead - grapes being universally preferred to cucumbers - the monkey that is still receiving cucumbers will begin to throw them back at the experimenter. Even though she is still getting "paid" the same amount for her effort of sourcing rocks, and so her particular situation has not changed, the comparison to another makes the situation unfair. (B)___________, she is now willing to abandon all gains - the cucumbers themselves - to communicate her displeasure to the experimenter.
options: ② moreover / On the other hand
questions.explanation: (A) 앞부분은 두 마리 모두 오이를 받을 때 행복해한다는 내용인 반면, (A) 이후는 한 마리에게만 포도를 주었을 때 다른 한 마리가 화를 낸다는 대조적인 상황을 설명하므로 역접의 'however'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞에서는 불공정함을 느낀다는 심리 상태를 설명하고 있고, (B) 뒤에서는 그 불공정함 때문에 자신의 이득(오이)까지 포기하며 불만을 표현한다는 추가적인 행동을 설명하므로 '더욱이(Furthermore)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나 / 예를 들어
② 게다가 / 반면에
③ 예를 들어 / 대조적으로
④ 그러나 / 더욱이
⑤ 그러므로 / 그럼에도 불구하고

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, "I can't," is to choose to ___________________________________________. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called "hanging out with the winners." The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one's own latent positive thought forms.
options: ① hang out with those who need social skill development
② raise awareness about the importance of self-confidence
③ stay with positive people who have overcome negative states
④ follow the strategies of successful people in various fields
⑤ keep away those who have resolved the problem with which we struggle
questions.explanation: 이 글은 무력감이나 부정적인 생각에서 벗어나기 위해 긍정적인 에너지를 가진 사람들과 함께할 것을 권장하고 있습니다. 본문에서 언급된 'hanging out with the winners'는 긍정적인 사고방식을 가진 사람들과 시간을 보내는 것이 자신의 잠재된 긍정적 사고를 다시 일깨우는 데 도움이 된다는 의미입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '부정적인 상태를 극복한 긍정적인 사람들과 함께 머무는 것'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사회성 발달이 필요한 사람들과 어울리기
② 자신감의 중요성에 대한 인식을 높이기
③ 부정적인 상태를 극복한 긍정적인 사람들과 머물기
④ 다양한 분야에서 성공한 사람들의 전략을 따르기
⑤ 우리가 겪고 있는 문제를 해결한 사람들을 멀리하기

questions.question: 7. 윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals in cartoons is that they can talk in human language. (A)____________, animal cartoon characters made after animals are most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. (B)____________, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.explanation: (A) 앞문장에서 동물이 인간의 언어로 말한다는 특성을 언급하고, 뒷문장에서 인간을 닮게 변형된다는 추가적인 특징을 설명하므로 '게다가(Moreover)'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞문장에서 최근에는 동물을 더 '자연스럽게' 보여주는 경향이 있다고 했으나, 뒷문장에서 여전히 인간의 손처럼 앞다리를 사용한다고 반대되는 내용을 서술하므로 '그럼에도 불구하고(Nonetheless)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그럼에도 불구하고 / 따라서
② 결과적으로 / 그러므로
③ 게다가 / 그럼에도 불구하고
④ 유사하게 / 예를 들어
⑤ 결과적으로 / 그럼에도 불구하고

questions.question: 8. 윗글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (가), (나)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals in cartoons is that they can talk in human language. (A)____________, animal cartoon characters made after animals are most often deformed in such a way as to resemble humans. This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features and deformed front legs to resemble human hands. In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way. (B)____________, they still use their front legs like human hands (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw), and they still talk with an appropriate facial expression. A general strategy that is used to make the animal characters more emotionally appealing, both to children and adults, is to give them enlarged and deformed childlike features.
questions.summary_sentence: Although animal characters in animated movies show more (가)__________ aspects of animals recently, there are still (나)__________ __________ in them.
subjective_conditions: • 빈칸 하나에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
• 본문에서 찾아 변형하지 말고 그대로 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 본문의 'In more recent animated movies the trend has been to show the animals in a more "natural" way.'를 통해 최근 경향인 (가) natural을 알 수 있고, 'This is achieved by showing them with humanlike facial features...'를 통해 여전히 (나) human features(인간적 특징)가 남아있음을 알 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 9. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off.
ordered_passages: (A) In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.(B) At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes.(C) Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 여가 시간이 늘어났음을 언급한 후, (B)에서 이동 수단의 발달을 소개합니다. (C)에서 철도가 해안 리조트를 개방하고 호텔을 가져왔다는 구체적인 예시를 들고, (A)에서 캐나다의 철도 시스템 예시와 항공 운송의 도래를 순차적으로 설명하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We think we are shaping our buildings. But really, our buildings and development are also shaping us.
ordered_passages: (A) It appears that the erection of the multiple rings of megalithic stones took so long, and so many successive generations, that these innovators were forced to settle down to complete the construction works. In the process, they became the first farming society on Earth.(B) One of the best examples of this is the oldest-known construction: the ornately carved rings of standing stones at Gobekli Tepe in Turkey. Before these ancestors got the idea to erect standing stones some 12,000 years ago, they were hunter-gatherers.(C) This is an early example of a society constructing something that ends up radically remaking the society itself. Things are not so different in our own time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 건물이 우리를 형성한다는 주제를 제시한 후, (B)에서 괴베클리 테페라는 구체적인 역사적 사례를 도입합니다. (A)에서 그 건설 과정이 수 세대에 걸쳐 정착 생활을 유도했고 농경 사회가 되었다는 설명을 이어가며, (C)에서 이것이 사회를 재형성한 사례임을 요약하며 마무리하는 순서가 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Natural processes form minerals in many ways. For example, hot melted rock material, called magma, cools when it reaches the Earth's surface, or even if it's trapped below the surface. (A) As magma cools, its atoms lose heat energy, move closer together, and begin to combine into compounds. (B) During this process, atoms of the different compounds arrange themselves into orderly, repeating patterns. (C) The type and amount of elements present in a magma partly determine which minerals will form. (D) Also, the size of the crystals that form depends partly on how rapidly the magma cools. (E) This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals. When magma cools rapidly, the crystals that form will be small. In such cases, you can't easily see individual mineral crystals.
questions.insertion_sentence: When magma cools slowly, the crystals that form are generally large enough to see with the unaided eye.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 마그마가 천천히 식을 때 결정의 크기가 육안으로 볼 수 있을 만큼 커진다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (E) 바로 뒤의 문장 'This is because the atoms have enough time to move together and form into larger crystals'는 마그마가 천천히 식을 때 원자들이 결합할 충분한 시간을 갖기 때문에 큰 결정이 형성된다는 이유를 설명하므로, 주어진 문장은 (E) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. ⓐIt is important to plan as many things as possible even if you cannot complete those things due to lack of time. ⓑGive attention also to fitting the task to the available time. ⓒThere are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. ⓓThere is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. ⓔSo schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심 주제는 일이 걸리는 시간을 정확히 파악하여 가용 시간 내에 계획을 효율적으로 세워야 한다는 내용입니다. ⓐ번 문장은 시간이 부족해서 완료하지 못하더라도 가능한 한 많은 일을 계획하는 것이 중요하다는 내용으로, 가용 시간에 맞춰 계획을 세워야 한다는 전체 흐름과 상충됩니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore ____________________________________________. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
options: ① represent the values of a good life to your child through how you live
② make children aware of the challenges of understanding others' suffering
③ help children practice determining which is reasonable in their daily lives
④ show children how to find their way when they get lost in the middle of a city
⑤ lead kids to make a positive impression on others by being considerate and friendly
questions.explanation: 이 글은 아이들이 부모의 말보다는 행동과 실천을 보고 가치관을 배운다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '여러분이 어떻게 사는지(삶의 방식)를 통해 아이에게 훌륭한 삶의 가치를 보여주어라'라는 의미인 ①번이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 어떻게 사느냐를 통해 아이에게 좋은 삶의 가치를 보여주어라
② 아이들에게 타인의 고통을 이해하는 것의 어려움을 인식시켜라
③ 아이들이 일상생활에서 무엇이 합리적인지 판단하는 것을 연습하게 도와라
④ 아이들이 도시 한가운데서 길을 잃었을 때 길을 찾는 법을 보여주어라
⑤ 사려 깊고 친절하게 행동함으로써 아이들이 타인에게 긍정적인 인상을 주도록 이끌어라

questions.question: 14. 윗글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Whose story it is ⓐ<u>affects</u> what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them ⓑ<u>differently</u>. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises ⓒ<u>where</u> is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if ⓓ<u>told</u> from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we ⓔ<u>were</u> <u>shown</u> the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 conflict를 수식하는 관계사절이 이어져야 하는데, 뒤에 'is the heart of the story'라는 동사구가 나오므로 주어 역할을 할 수 있는 주격 관계대명사가 필요합니다. 따라서 관계부사 where가 아니라 관계대명사 that 또는 which로 고쳐야 합니다. (참고: arises는 자동사이므로 수동태가 불가능하며, 선행사인 conflict와 관계사절이 떨어져 있는 구조입니다.)

questions.question: 16. 윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," ⓐ<u>explain</u> famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. (A)_____________, when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? ⓑ<u>Be</u> there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good ⓒ<u>adopt</u> the practices of those around you. (B)_____________, we tend to feel safe and secure in numbers when we decide how ⓓ<u>act</u>, particularly when faced with uncertain conditions.
options: ③ On the other hand / Nevertheless
⑤ However / At the same time
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 환경 내의 미묘한 신호가 신뢰성을 나타낼 수 있다고 한 뒤 식당의 예시를 들고 있으므로 'For example'이 적절합니다. (B) 앞서 언급한 사회적 증거와 타인의 행동을 따르는 성향에 대한 결과로 우리가 다수 속에서 안전함을 느낀다는 내용이 이어지므로 'Consequently(따라서, 결과적으로)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 비록 ~일지라도 / 예를 들어
② 예를 들어 / 결과적으로
③ 반면에 / 그럼에도 불구하고
④ 그러므로 / 다시 말해서
⑤ 하지만 / 동시에

questions.question: 17. 윗글의 ⓐ~ⓓ에 주어진 단어를 어법상 맞는 형태가 되도록 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," ⓐ<u>explain</u> famous psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. (A)_____________, when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? ⓑ<u>Be</u> there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand. More often than not, it's good ⓒ<u>adopt</u> the practices of those around you. (B)_____________, we tend to feel safe and secure in numbers when we decide how ⓓ<u>act</u>, particularly when faced with uncertain conditions.
subjective_conditions: ⓐ~ⓓ 각각 한 단어, 또는 두 단어로 쓸 것
주어진 형태 그대로 쓰지 말고 반드시 단어를 추가하거나 변형할 것
questions.answer: ⓐ → explainsⓑ → areⓒ → to adoptⓓ → to act
questions.explanation: ⓐ 주어가 단수(famous psychologist ~ Robert Cialdini)이므로 동사에 s를 붙여 'explains'가 되어야 합니다. ⓑ 의문문에서 주어가 'a line'과 'is it~' 뒤에 병렬되거나 혹은 'there' 구문에서 'are'를 사용해야 하는데, 문맥상 복수 상황이나 의문 형태를 고려하여 'Is' 혹은 'Are'로 변형되어야 하며, 정답지 기준 'are'로 제시됨. ⓒ 가주어 it에 대한 진주어 자리이므로 'to adopt'가 적절합니다. ⓓ 'how to 동사원형' 구문이므로 'to act'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see (A)[many / few] people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have (B)[rich / shallow] knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people (C)[hide / offer] feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤의 내용이 팬들이 자신들이 더 잘할 수 있다고 믿는다는 내용이므로 'many(많은)'가 적절합니다. (B) 스포츠 관리직 경영진들은 해당 분야에 'rich(풍부한)' 지식과 경험을 가지고 있지만 비판을 받는다는 문맥이 이어져야 합니다. (C) 의사나 회계사에게는 훈수를 두지 않지만 스포츠 조직 운영에 대해서는 피드백을 'offer(제공)'한다는 대조적 의미가 필요합니다.
options_translation: ① 많은 / 풍부한 / 숨기다
② 많은 / 얕은 / 숨기다
③ 거의 없는 / 풍부한 / 제공하다
④ 거의 없는 / 얕은 / 숨기다
⑤ 많은 / 풍부한 / 제공하다

questions.question: 19. 윗글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (가)~(다)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
questions.passage: There is a reason the title "Monday Morning Quarterback" exists. Just read the comments on social media from fans discussing the weekend's games, and you quickly see (A)[many / few] people believe they could play, coach, and manage sport teams more successfully than those on the field. This goes for the boardroom as well. Professionals with years of training and specialized degrees in sport business may also find themselves being given advice on how to do their jobs from friends, family, or even total strangers without any expertise. Executives in sport management have (B)[rich / shallow] knowledge and experience in their respective fields. However, many of them face criticism from fans and community members telling them how to run their business. Very few people tell their doctor how to perform surgery or their accountant how to prepare their taxes, but many people (C)[hide / offer] feedback on how sport organizations should be managed.
questions.summary_sentence: Even (가)__________ and experienced people in sports often receive (나)__________ and (다)__________ from many other people.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 변형하지 말고 그대로 쓸 것
'feedback' 은 쓰지 말 것
(가)~(다) 각각 한 단어로 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 본문에 근거하여, 스포츠 분야의 숙련된 사람들을 지칭하는 (가) 'professionals'는 다른 사람들로부터 (나) 'advice'와 (다) 'criticism'을 자주 받는다는 요약문이 완성됩니다.
